## Reported by, not investigated by, an adjacent session

Surfaced while confirming the fix for bug 8070 (external-integration canary). Per operator instruction this was NOT investigated — epic e369 is actively held by another session and owns this subject matter. Filing it here so the owning session sees it. **The root cause below is a candidate, not a finding.**

## Observed (live CI, reproducible)

Run 30651750699 — `workflow_dispatch` of `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` on `main` at commit `b7e6ac963`, 2026-07-31. Job **"jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)"**:

```
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:319
AssertionError: no local ticket was created from DC issue RBJNAZV-1;
  stdout='invariants: scanned=1 filed=0 (cap=5)\nOK: applied 1 of 1 mutations\n'
assert []
FAILED test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance
```

The failing test is `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance`.

## Why this is newly visible

This failure was previously MASKED. Until `b7e6ac963` the whole external tier died at `SnapshotRefError` on an unborn `HEAD` before reaching any behaviour under test (bug 8070). With snapshot resolution fixed, the tier now reaches its subject and this assertion fails on its merits. So this is very likely a pre-existing defect that the canary could not previously report, not a new regression from `b7e6ac963` — which touched only `tests/external/conftest.py` (adds an empty root commit) and added a unit test.

## Candidate cause — UNCONFIRMED, do not treat as diagnosed

`scanned=1 filed=0` says the inbound record was seen and then not filed. That shape is consistent with OPEN bug **5f48-244c-7063-42d0** — "DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel" — where a silent mint failure would drop the record between scan and file. Linked `relates_to`. If that is the cause, this ticket is a duplicate and should be closed as such rather than worked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism behind `scanned=1 filed=0` is identified and cited (`path:line`), and it is
      determined whether this is the same defect as 5f48 (close as duplicate) or distinct.
- [ ] `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` passes against the live DC
      harness, or the failure is guarded by a credential-free test in the default suite.
baseline.summary: DC inbound filing is a no-op in live CI: reconcile reports scanned=1 filed=0, no local ticket created from DC issue

baseline.description:
# `rebar comment <id> --body-file <path>` stores the literal string \`--body-file\` and exits 0

## Observed twice, by two different sessions

`rebar comment` takes its body POSITIONALLY (`Usage: rebar comment <ticket_id> <body>`). It has no `--body`/`--body-file` option. When invoked with one anyway, the flag token is accepted AS the body: the stored comment is the 11-byte string \`--body-file\` (or the 6-byte \`--body\`), the intended content is silently discarded, and **the command exits 0** so nothing signals the loss.

Evidence in the live store right now:
- ticket b690 comments 5-9: five stubs of length 11, 11, 11, 11, 6 — an entire session's root-cause
  analysis, fix rationale, blast-radius audit and live evidence, all lost.
- session log 55a9 comment 5: also \`--body-file\`, written by an EARLIER session. So this is not a
  one-off slip; the same footgun has now cost two independent sessions their durable record.

## Why this is worse than a normal CLI usage error

rebar's own guidance (AGENTS.md) is emphatic that the ticket store — not scratch notes — is the durable, shared trail, and that agents should write progress and findings back as comments. This failure mode silently defeats exactly that instruction, and it does so in the least detectable way:
- exit code 0
- no stderr
- a comment DOES appear, so a \`len(comments)\` check (which is the natural way to confirm "did my
  write land?") passes while the content is gone
- the loss is only discovered later by something that READS the content — in this case the completion
  verifier, which correctly failed a ticket for having "no concrete attestation recorded" because the
  attestation genuinely was not there.

The cost is not the retyping. It is that work believed to be recorded is not, and downstream gates make correct-but-confusing decisions on the missing evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a body argument that begins with \`-\` is REJECTED with a non-zero exit and a message naming the
      correct form, rather than stored — unless the user clearly meant it (see below)
- [ ] the escape hatch exists and is documented: a body that legitimately starts with \`-\` can still be
      written (conventionally via \`--\`, e.g. \`rebar comment <id> -- "-starts with a dash"\`)
- [ ] the same guard covers every positional-body command with this shape, not just \`comment\`
      (audit at least \`create\`/\`edit\`/\`session-log\` for the same footgun and fix or document each)
- [ ] a test asserts the REJECTION for \`--body-file <path>\` and \`--body <text>\` specifically, since
      those are the two forms that have actually occurred
- [ ] consider (and decide explicitly, either way) whether to ADD a real \`--body-file\` option: the
      fact that two independent sessions reached for it suggests it is the expected interface for
      long bodies, and shell quoting of multi-KB markdown through a positional arg is awkward
- [ ] no silent truncation or coercion anywhere in the fix: a body that cannot be stored as given must
      fail loudly

## Notes

Filed OUTSIDE epic 061c — unrelated to the LLM provider seam; this is a CLI/store-durability concern. Found when the completion verifier failed story b690 for missing attestations that had in fact been written five times over.
baseline.summary: rebar comment silently stores a flag-looking argument as the comment body, destroying the record (has now hit two sessions)

baseline.description:
## Why
Serial wall-clock is ~N×CI for N ready stacks; batching collapses it to ~1 CI cycle, which is the wall-clock-optimal option under the Free-tier GHA concurrency cap where speculation would just queue (the exact concurrent-run count isn't the limiter — `gerrit-verify.yaml` uses a per-change concurrency group).

## What
Assemble the queued `Autosubmit` changes/stacks into ONE combined relation chain on current `main`, and trigger CI ONCE on the combined tip. The batching **algorithm** — combine N non-conflicting changes → one CI pass → atomic land — has precedent in bors/Graphite, **adapted** to Gerrit relation chains (those tools are GitHub-PR-native, not usable on Gerrit).

## Dependencies
Depends on **S2** (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`, 0ee8-08de-bf0f-45ec) — the Phase-1 core loop: batching reuses its selection, rebase, and `is:submittable` machinery, and Phase 2 is a fast-follow on the serial lander.

## Verified-satisfaction (cross-reference, no blocking link)
Per-member `Verified` is satisfied by the single combined-tip run, but **casting** that `Verified +1` per member is owned by **S8** (bot-casts-Verified). This story delivers **assembly + the single CI trigger only**; on green it hands off to S8's cast-Verified + submit. **The handoff is an explicit record** — S7 writes `{member_change_ids[], combined_tip_change_id, tested_sha, run_id}` to the batch state that S8 reads before casting any vote (so S8 binds each vote to a SHA S7 actually assembled + tested). (Prose cross-reference — S7 does not `depends_on` S8, to avoid a cycle.)

## Scope
Phase 2. The batching assembly + single-run trigger. Verified-casting, atomic submit, and batch-failure handling are separate stories (S8, S9).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Assembles queued changes/stacks into one combined linear chain on the current `main` tip, reusing S2's `/rebase:chain` as the building block for cross-stack chain assembly.
- [ ] Triggers exactly ONE CI run on the combined tip (not one per change), dispatching `gerrit-verify.yaml` against the **real combined-tip change's** actual Change-Id / change-number / patchset (not a synthetic ref); records that run's `run_id` on the batch for S8's confirmation.
- [ ] **FFO TOCTOU re-check:** immediately before the batch is handed off for submit, re-check the combined chain is still on the current `main` tip; if `main` advanced, re-assemble + re-batch — **bounded to `N=5` re-batch attempts**, after which the batch is dropped to the Phase-1 serial path (never hand off a stale tree, never loop unbounded). NOTE: the Phase-1 single-`wipChain` invariant does NOT hold in Phase 2 — this bounded re-batch loop is the mitigation.
- [ ] On green, **hand off to S8** (cast-Verified-per-member → ancestor-atomic submit) via the handoff record `{member_change_ids[], combined_tip_change_id, tested_sha, run_id}`. This story does **not** cast `Verified` and does **not** itself submit.
- [ ] Batch size bounded by a concrete numeric cap **`BATCH_MAX=8`** members per combined-tip CI run (sized to one run's job budget under the GHA concurrency cap); the cap is documented and enforced at assembly (excess changes wait for the next batch).
baseline.summary: S7 Cross-stack batching: combined-chain CI on tip, land together (Phase 2)

content.text: ## Why
The DET floor is the ONLY blocking tier (every LLM criterion is advisory in v1). It must be a frozen,
deterministic, polyglot floor that fails open on any unsupported stack.
## What
- P1 readiness-shape; P2 file/symbol/import resolution (universal-ctags via the 8f6c oracle — LSP/solidlsp is the T2 follow-on `850f`, NOT v1); P3 package existence
(deps.dev registry + optional syft SBOM); P4 oversize (scc/lizard metrics); P5 task-DAG validity + interference;

P6 AC/DD quality; P7 destructive/irreversible sniff (escalates T4). The polyglot resolution/dependency/size tooling (P2/P3/P4) is CONSUMED — via the SHIPPED `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan` facade — from the now-CLOSED prerequisite epic 8f6c-6008-33f3-4f82 (code-grounding oracle, `src/rebar/grounding/`) — this child does NOT re-build it; it owns the rebar-specific checks (P1/P5/P6/P7) + wiring P2/P3/P4 into the DET floor.
## Scope

- Call the 8f6c grounding-oracle facade (refute_absence/applies/scan); its three-valued abstain-by-default contract IS the fail-open guarantee — unsupported lang / no tool / parse-error / timeout -> abstain (recorded reason) -> skipped = PASS (ironclad).
- The shared oracle SHIPPED as prerequisite epic 8f6c (CLOSED; also consumed by code-review `9da1`); this child depends_on it and consumes it as a library, not as new integrations.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] P1-P7 implemented in Python, polyglot, fail-open (skipped=pass) tested per tool.
- [ ] Coverage recorded on the attestation.

- [ ] DET floor is the only tier that blocks BY DEFAULT in v1 (every LLM criterion is advisory; per-criterion LLM-tier blocking is OPT-IN via its `block_threshold` — 'DET-only' is the v1 default posture, not an architectural limit).
## (Added) P8 — reviewability / context-budget (DET)
A meta-finding, not tied to any one criterion, so it lives in the deterministic floor as P8: a DET check that
PASSES unless the ticket content (or a parent+child pairing for container criteria) EXCEEDS — or is
anticipated (token-estimate) to exceed — the largest configured context window even at one-criterion-per-call.
In that case it FAILS with 'ticket too big to review in full; reduce/decompose it' (the extreme of P4 oversize
/ G5 decomposition). Deterministic (a size/estimate check, no LLM); the orchestrator emits it during the
size-handling ladder.
## Acceptance Criteria (added)

- [ ] P8 reviewability DET check: passes unless content (or a parent+child pairing) exceeds — or is anticipated to exceed — the largest context window at one-criterion-per-call; else a 'ticket too big, reduce it' failure finding.
## Acceptance Criteria (added — T8 DET execution path)
- [ ] P1–P8 run as the deterministic `exec=DET` tier the orchestrator dispatches via its code executor (no LLM) — an explicit, first-class execution path, not merely a named tier.

baseline.summary: Layer-1 deterministic floor (P1-P7) + fail-open polyglot tool wrappers

baseline.description:
## Summary

`rebar init` (auto-init / `rebar init --silent`) created a **fresh, empty** local tracker on a new `tickets` branch even though an authoritative `tickets` branch with real ticket history already existed on the configured sync remote (`origin`). The local tracker (`.tickets-tracker`) diverged from `origin/tickets`, so every read command (`rebar list`, `rebar show`, `search`, …) returns an EMPTY store, hiding all existing tickets. Any writes made now land on the divergent local branch and cannot be fast-forward-pushed back to `origin/tickets`.

Root contributing factor: fetching the remote `tickets` branch times out (>100s) through the agent git proxy, so init silently fell back to bootstrapping a fresh store instead of failing loudly or retrying.

## Impact

- `rebar list --status=open --type=bug` (and all other reads) return `[]` — existing
  work is invisible.
- New ticket events are written to a divergent local `tickets` history that will not
  fast-forward onto `origin/tickets`, risking lost or conflicting events.
- Silent data-hiding: no error is surfaced to the operator; the store simply looks empty.

## Environment

- Remote execution environment (Claude Code on the web), ephemeral container.
- Primary working directory: `/home/user/rebar`
- Platform: Linux 6.18.5
- Checked-out code branch: `claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76`
- rebar version: `nava-rebar 0.10.1`
- `origin` remote: `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/navapbc/rebar`
- Outbound git/HTTPS goes through the pre-configured agent proxy.
- No `.venv` was present at session start; `rebar` was not on `PATH`. Bootstrapped with
  `python3 -m venv .venv && make install`.
- Config (relevant): `sync.remote = origin`, `sync.pull = on`, `sync.push = always`.

## Reproduction — exact commands and observed output

1. rebar not installed / not on PATH:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   /bin/bash: line 1: rebar: command not found
   $ python3 -m rebar list ...
   /usr/local/bin/python3: No module named rebar
   $ ls .venv
   ls: cannot access '.venv': No such file or directory
   ```

2. Bootstrap env:

   ```
   $ python3 -m venv .venv && make install
   Successfully installed ... nava-rebar-0.10.1 ...
   ```

3. Store reports not initialized, then init produced an EMPTY store:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'rebar init' first (auto-init requires an interactive terminal).
   $ rebar init --silent
   (no output)
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   []
   $ rebar list                       # all statuses
   []
   ```

4. But a real `tickets` branch exists on `origin`, and it is actively moving (other
   agents writing to it) — two `ls-remote` reads minutes apart returned different tips:

   ```
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   aa498170daa39767eab3282f505700e30bbed1ea  refs/heads/tickets   # first check
   ...
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   4b51478a14c150a1032a8b2988d1524bfda1da54  refs/heads/tickets   # minutes later
   ```

5. The local tracker worktree is a FRESH divergent branch (bootstrap commits only, none
   of the remote history):

   ```
   $ git worktree list
   /home/user/rebar               ... claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76
   /home/user/rebar/.tickets-tracker ... tickets

   $ git -C .tickets-tracker log --oneline -n 6
   37e8b02 chore: add .store-compat.json store-compatibility record (story 21dd)
   ed99e08 chore: add .gitignore for env-id, state-cache, scratch, and reducer cache
   936ec76 chore: add .gitattributes merge=ours for shared mutable root files (epic 97e7)
   a7ad28d chore: add no-op .pre-commit-config.yaml (bug 27d8-b230)
   94e48da chore: initialize ticket tracker
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets
   37e8b026cf61e04b651f29b849294f6d549c8210
   ```

   Local tip `37e8b02` shares no history with remote tip `4b51478a` → divergent.

6. Fetching the remote `tickets` branch to reconverge TIMES OUT (reproduced multiple
   times, both from the main checkout and from inside `.tickets-tracker`):

   ```
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker fetch origin tickets      # 100s timeout
   Terminated   (exit 143)
   $ git fetch origin tickets                          # 120s tool timeout
   Command timed out after 2m 0s
   ```

   `rebar fsck` reports the (empty) local store as healthy, so nothing flags the problem:

   ```
   $ rebar fsck
   ensures: 6/6 applied
   authorship: 0 signed, 0 unsigned event(s)
   fsck complete: no issues found
   ```

## Confirmed divergence and fetch-latency (observed this session)

A full (unbounded-timeout) background fetch of `origin/tickets` eventually SUCCEEDED, which let me quantify both the divergence and the latency that caused the fallback:

- The remote `tickets` branch is large and event-sourced — **49,301 commits**:

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-list --count origin/tickets
  49301
  ```

- The local auto-initialized tracker and `origin/tickets` share **NO common ancestor**
  (definitively a fresh, divergent store — not a fast-forwardable lag):

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker merge-base tickets origin/tickets
  (no output; exit 1) -> NO COMMON ANCESTOR (divergent)
  $ git rev-parse origin/tickets      # authoritative
  80ec6ba00f4ce4daef8dada62c8056e003e8ef92
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets   # local fresh-init
  dcb0b1ac7ff39999016a7aa73eeef9644b1e0247
  ```

- The branch is **actively written by other agents** — its tip moved four times across
  this single session: `aa498170…` → `4b51478a…` → `80ec6ba…`, etc.

- **Fetch latency is the trigger:** `git fetch origin tickets` was killed at 100s and at
  the 120s tool limit, but the same fetch run WITHOUT a kill-timeout (in the background)
  completed successfully in several minutes. So the branch is reachable; init simply gave
  up (or its bounded fetch timed out) and fell back to a fresh empty store rather than
  waiting/retrying. A bounded init fetch against a 49k-commit branch over the proxy is not
  enough headroom.

## Expected behavior

`rebar init` MUST NOT silently bootstrap a fresh empty store when the configured sync remote already has a `tickets` branch. It should either:

- fetch/adopt `origin/tickets` as the local tracker's base (the store is non-empty), or
- fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear message) when it cannot reach/fetch the existing
  remote `tickets` branch, instead of falling back to a divergent empty store.

Additionally, the remote-`tickets` fetch through the agent proxy should be made resilient (retry/backoff, longer timeout) rather than silently abandoned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar init` / auto-init detects an existing `tickets` branch on `sync.remote`
      before creating a new one, and bases the local tracker on it (reads return the
      existing tickets, not `[]`).
- [ ] When the existing remote `tickets` branch cannot be fetched, init fails loudly
      (clear error + non-zero exit) instead of silently bootstrapping a divergent empty
      store.
- [ ] A health check (`fsck`/`validate`) detects and reports a local `tickets` tracker
      that has diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared history / cannot fast-forward),
      rather than reporting "no issues found".
- [ ] Regression coverage: a test simulates a reachable, non-empty remote `tickets`
      branch and asserts init does not produce an empty divergent store.

## Notes

- Filed per operator request while investigating "show me a list of open bugs" returning
  an empty list.
- Because the local store is currently divergent and the remote fetch times out, this
  ticket may itself be written to the divergent local `tickets` history and may not sync
  to `origin/tickets` until the underlying fetch/reconverge issue is resolved.
baseline.summary: rebar init bootstrapped a fresh empty tracker while origin/tickets already existed (divergent store, reads return [])

baseline.description:
## Problem
The `[rebar:<id>]` citation section in `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` (shipped by 266e-c8b6-0cb0-44ae) states the edge requirement (this ticket `depends_on -> <id>`, OR `<id> blocks -> this ticket`) but never says the edge must be DIRECT. The shipped verifier `det_citation._edge_verified` checks only the plan ticket's OWN direct deps plus the cited ticket's direct `blocks` (no recursion), so a transitive/indirect dependency does NOT satisfy it — the citation then reads as edge-unbacked and grounds as normal (fails closed) with no warning in the doc. This footgun was hit in practice (a ticket transitively depending on a config ticket still needed a direct edge).

## Approach (docs-only; no behavior change)
Add one clause to the EXISTING citation section stating the edge must be DIRECT and that a transitive/indirect dependency does not count. Rationale for docs-only scope: the verifier ALREADY implements direct-edge-only checks correctly (`det_citation._edge_verified` has no recursion) — the code is right and only the documentation lags, so the sound fix is to align the doc, not change any behavior.

## Grounding (verified via Read)
- CONFIRMED `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` contains the "## Citing a prerequisite's symbol (`[rebar:<id>]`)" section with the edge-requirement paragraph.
- CONFIRMED `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py` `_edge_verified` checks only direct edges (the plan ticket's own `deps` for `depends_on -> C`, and `resolve_deps(C)` for `blocks -> P`) — no recursive closure — so "direct" is accurate to the shipped behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The citation section explicitly states the upstream edge must be DIRECT and that a transitive/indirect dependency does not satisfy it. PROVE: `grep -Eiqw "direct" docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md && grep -Eiq "transitive|indirect" docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` (the first grep is word-anchored so it does not match "indirect").
- [ ] The change is confined to the single doc file. PROVE: `[ "$(git diff --name-only origin/main | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] && git diff --name-only origin/main | grep -qxE "docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md"`.

## Files likely touched
- docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md

## Estimated scope: XS
baseline.summary: writing-a-passing-plan: [rebar:<id>] citations require a DIRECT edge (transitive deps do not count)

content.text: ## What
Make union recovery (epic minor-haste-ogle WU-2/WU-3) unconditionally
conflict-free by removing the only mutable, non-disjoint shared paths from the
`tickets` branch. Today `.bridge_state/bindings.json` and the reconciler
lock/gate files are committed at the branch root and are rewritten each reconcile
pass, so two clones produce divergent edits to the same path -> merge conflict
(WU-3 mitigates with `merge=ours`; this ticket removes the conflict class
entirely). uuid-named ticket dirs are already disjoint and always merge cleanly;
once these root files are gitignored off the shared history, EVERY path on the
branch is append-only-disjoint and union merge can never wedge.
## Files
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (the committed `.gitignore` / scaffold on the tickets branch)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` (writes lock/gate + bindings to the shared branch)
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` (the existing `.bridge_state` stash/merge dance can be simplified once they leave the branch)
## Scope / risk

baseline.description:
## Summary
An agent-executed epic cannot be represented in the store as certified/**signed**-closed when
one of its child stories carries an `[operator-attested]` acceptance criterion whose evidence
lives outside the codebase and outside the executing agent's access — even when every
engineering acceptance criterion across the whole epic is demonstrably complete and landed on
`main`. This is a process/tooling gap surfaced while executing epic `bf50-2131-271b-4fdc`
(graceless-hominine-jerboa); it is NOT a defect in any of that epic's code changes.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Decompose an epic into stories and execute it with an agent (claim → implement → land each
   child through the Gerrit gate).
2. Include among the children a story whose acceptance criteria contain an `[operator-attested]`
   item whose admissible evidence is inherently out-of-band — e.g. 5f39-cb52-9355-492f AC3:
   configured GitHub repo VARIABLES (`JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_PROJECT`,
   `ACLI_VERSION`/`ACLI_SHA256`), a configured SECRET (`JIRA_API_TOKEN`), a provisioned
   dedicated Jira test project, and the URL of a green `workflow_dispatch` run in which the live
   Jira test EXECUTED (not all-skip).
3. Have the agent complete and LAND every code change (all children `Verified +1` AND
   `LLM-Review +1`, merged to `main`).
4. Attempt to close that child, then the epic.

## Expected
With all engineering acceptance criteria met and landed, the epic — and every child — can be
closed with a completion-verifier **signature** (certified), such that the store durably
records the epic as fully certified when the work is in fact complete.

## Actual
- The child's completion verifier passes every CODE criterion but FAILS the single
  `[operator-attested]` criterion, because the agent has neither the access nor the
  authorization to produce the required out-of-band evidence (repo secrets/variables, a live
  Jira project, an observed green canary run), and no concrete attestation (run URL/id/timestamp)
  therefore exists to record.
- The child can only be **force-closed UNSIGNED**.
- The epic's own acceptance criterion requires "all child stories closed (**signed**)", so the
  epic's completion verifier fails on that criterion and the epic can only be **force-closed
  UNSIGNED** as well.
- Net: an epic whose entire engineering scope is complete and landed cannot be represented as
  certified/signed, purely because one child's evidence is out-of-band from the agent's reach.

## Evidence / Impact
- Concretely observed on epic `bf50-2131-271b-4fdc`: 19/19 stories implemented and merged to
  `main` (Gerrit changes 537–555 + 559); 18/19 children closed SIGNED (plan-review +
  completion-verifier); child `5f39-cb52-9355-492f` and the epic closed UNSIGNED via force-close.
- Full trail (per-story claims, RED/teeth evidence, landing, the force-close reasoning, and a
  dedicated PROBLEM RECORD entry) is in session log `25f1-5000-760d-4c2b`
  (plump-kitschy-meadowlark), linked to this bug.
- Impact: the "signed = fully certified" invariant cannot be earned for any epic that contains
  an operator-attested criterion the agent cannot attest; such epics are indistinguishable in
  the store (both unsigned) from epics whose OWN engineering work genuinely failed verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The problem is reproducible and characterized: an agent-executed epic with all
      engineering ACs complete + landed, plus one child bearing an out-of-band
      `[operator-attested]` criterion the agent cannot attest, results in unsigned closure of
      both the child and the epic.
- [ ] The gap is documented with the concrete instance (epic bf50, child 5f39) and its evidence
      (the specific out-of-band items required, and why the agent could not produce them).
- [ ] This bug links to the full session log capturing the run and the problem record.
baseline.summary: Agent-executed epic cannot close SIGNED when a child has an operator-attested criterion the agent cannot attest

## Problem
`src/rebar/config.py` is 869 LOC — over the 800-LOC module-size soft cap — and is grandfathered in `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` + `.github/module-size-ceilings.txt` (pinned 869), with a remedy row in `docs/architecture.md`.

## arch.md remedy row is STALE / already-shipped
The `docs/architecture.md` offenders row for `config.py` reads "split the dataclass/schema from the env/CLI-override + cache machinery along the existing seam". That seam ALREADY SHIPPED: the typed dataclass/schema layer now lives in the sibling `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (config.py already imports `_SECTIONS`, `Config`, `ConfigError`, `_as_bool`, `coerce_sparse`, `merge_sparse` from it). So the recorded remedy no longer describes an available seam — it is superseded. This ticket DELETES that stale row rather than claiming it records the seam below.

## New seam (on the CURRENT code): raw-input source layer
Extract the raw-input resolution layer — filesystem config discovery + TOML file parsing (with the mtime-keyed parse cache) + `REBAR_*` env & legacy-alias override collection — into a NEW leaf `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`. This cluster is cohesive (it turns files+env into raw sparse mappings) and sits strictly BELOW the typed-merge/cache/precedence machinery that stays in config.py (`load_config`, `_ordered_layers`, `_resolve`, the resolved-Config cache, the public writers/readers).

MOVE (by name): `repo_root`, `config_file`, `tracker_dir_override`, `_TOML_CACHE`, `_parse_toml`, `_read_toml_table`, `_pyproject_rebar_state`, `_discover_project_config`, `user_config_path`, `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES`, `_canonical_env_name`, `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`, `_map_legacy_env`, `env_overrides`, `_strict_unknown_keys`.

The leaf imports ONLY stdlib + `rebar._config_schema` + `rebar._deprecations` (no import of `rebar.config`), so it is a true leaf with no back-edge.

## Back-compat (public surface preserved)
config.py RE-EXPORTS the full moved set (`from rebar._config_sources import X as X`), so `rebar.config.<name>` attribute access and `from rebar.config import <name>` keep resolving unchanged (~90 importers; externally-used include `repo_root`, `tracker_dir_override`, `_canonical_env_name`, `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`, `user_config_path`, `_read_toml_table`, `_discover_project_config`, `env_overrides`). Two invariants preserved:
- `_TOML_CACHE` shared-object identity: `reset_config_cache` stays in config.py and mutates the imported dict via `.clear()` (never rebinds) — test_config_perf.py depends on this.
- Monkeypatch seam: retained callers (`_ordered_layers` etc.) call the BARE re-exported names (`_discover_project_config(...)`), so `monkeypatch.setattr(cfg, "_discover_project_config", ...)` still intercepts resolution.

## Scope note
This is a pure/mechanical refactor: NO signature or logic changes. E5 testing-plan is not-applicable — the existing config test suite (test_config_perf, test_config_loader, test_config_surface_golden, test_config_backcompat, test_config_tracker_dir, test_config_show) is the behavioral oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New leaf `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` exists with a line count in [100, 800]; verify: `n=$(wc -l < src/rebar/_config_sources.py); [ "$n" -ge 100 ] && [ "$n" -le 800 ]`
- [ ] `src/rebar/config.py` is at most 800 lines; verify: `[ "$(wc -l < src/rebar/config.py)" -le 800 ]`
- [ ] config.py removed from the allowlist; verify: `grep -qv "src/rebar/config.py" .github/module-size-allowlist.txt && ! grep -q "src/rebar/config.py" .github/module-size-allowlist.txt`
- [ ] config.py removed from the ceilings file; verify: `! grep -q "src/rebar/config.py" .github/module-size-ceilings.txt`
- [ ] The stale config.py remedy row is gone from docs/architecture.md; verify: `! grep -q "config.py.*split the dataclass/schema" docs/architecture.md`
- [ ] Module-size contract test passes (allowlist == over-cap set == ceilings keys); verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py -q`
- [ ] Config test suite passes; verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit -k config -q`
- [ ] Lint clean; verify: `make lint` reports "All checks passed!"
baseline.summary: Split config.py: extract raw-input source layer into _config_sources.py

content.text: ## Why

Audit Reliability finding #6 (MEDIUM): REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT / timeout_s is a dead knob — it is defined, documented, and env-resolved (src/rebar/llm/config.py: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=600 @L280, field @L447, resolved @L519) but never passed to the runner (src/rebar/llm/runner.py), so every LLM call rides the Anthropic SDK's built-in default (~600 s) regardless of the operator's setting. An operator who sets a tighter timeout believes hangs are bounded when they are not; the knob silently lies.
## What
Thread the resolved `cfg.timeout_s` into the runner so it actually bounds each LLM call.
## API surface (grounded — resolves the plan-review T1/T8 mechanism question)

Verified by introspecting the installed **pydantic-ai 1.107.0**: the per-request wall-clock timeout is the `timeout` key on `ModelSettings` / `AnthropicModelSettings` (maps to the underlying httpx/Anthropic client request timeout). There is **no** `inactivity_timeout` kwarg on `Agent.run_sync` in this version (run_sync params: user_prompt, output_type, ..., model_settings, usage_limits, ...). So the correct wiring is to set `model_settings["timeout"]` where runner.py already assembles the `AnthropicModelSettings` (alongside max_tokens / cache flags), which flows to both the string-model path and the explicit AnthropicModel branch.

Default semantics: `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 600` equals the Anthropic SDK default (600 s / 10 min), so when the knob is unset the resolved `timeout_s` is already 600 → passing it is never lower than the SDK default. An explicit operator value is honored verbatim (including a higher value); we do not silently raise/lower an explicit value.
## Scope

In: src/rebar/llm/runner.py (set model_settings["timeout"] = cfg.timeout_s), tests (assert the value reaches the passed model_settings), a config-reference/docs note (docs/llm-framework.md) stating the default semantics. Out: retry/backoff on 429/529 (separate audit finding 6.4); workflow-engine step budgets (already enforced); the "fail closed on unreadable config" idea (parked as sluggish-moistful-chital).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cfg.timeout_s` / REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT demonstrably reaches the pydantic-ai model settings (test asserts `model_settings["timeout"] == cfg.timeout_s`, via inspection or a monkeypatched Agent capturing the settings)
- [ ] Unset knob ⇒ effective timeout is the SDK default (600 s) or higher — asserted in the test (no hardcoded lower value); explicit operator value honored verbatim
- [ ] docs/llm-framework.md states the default wiring/semantics
- [ ] `make test` green

baseline.summary: Wire REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT into the LLM runner; default no lower than the SDK default

content.text: ## What

The centralized resolver `rebar._engine_support.resolver.resolve_ticket_id` is the single seam used by the library (`__init__.py`), `signing.py`, all `_commands`, `_engine_support` reads, the reducer link-resolution path, and plan-review. It contains a DEAD Jira-resolution path: `_scan_alias_jira` matches `data.jira_key` on CREATE/SNAPSHOT events, but that field is never written (the reconciler stores the mapping in the binding store; `jira_key` only ever appears as a top-level field on SYNC events, which the resolver does not read). The lookups.py docstring already documents `data.jira_key` as "intentionally not reflected". The authoritative Jira<->rebar mapping is the binding store reverse index at `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json` (`reverse: {jira_key -> local_id}`).
## Why

`rebar show REB-310` (and claim/transition/link/library) cannot resolve a Jira key today even though the binding exists. Per user direction: REPLACE the unused `data.jira_key` resolution path with binding-store-backed resolution, rather than adding a second mechanism beside dead code — to avoid future confusion.
## Approach (replace, not add)
In `src/rebar/_engine_support/resolver.py`:

- REMOVE the `data.jira_key` matching from `_scan_alias_jira` (it becomes alias-only; rename to `_scan_alias`, return `list[str] | None`). Drop the ambiguous-jira_key error branch in `resolve_ticket_id`.

- ADD `_JIRA_KEY_RE = ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+-[0-9]+$` (disjoint from lowercase-hex IDs/short-IDs and lowercase-word aliases) and a best-effort `_resolve_via_binding_store(target, tracker_dir)` that reads `<tracker_dir>/.bridge_state/bindings.json`, looks up `reverse[target]` (and `target.upper()`), and returns the local ticket-dir name iff it exists on disk; missing/corrupt store or non-dict reverse -> None (never raises).

- In `resolve_ticket_id`, for Jira-key-shaped input consult the binding store (after the short-id block, before the alias scan). Update the module + function docstrings to describe binding-store resolution.
## Scope

Resolution only (input -> ticket). The `lookups.py::_auto` DISPLAY path also reads the dead `data.jira_key`; left as-is (documented fallback chain, not resolution) — capture as follow-up if we want auto-display of Jira keys.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_ticket_id("REB-310", tracker)` returns the bound local ticket dir when `.bridge_state/bindings.json` reverse-maps it and the dir exists.
- [ ] The dead `data.jira_key` scan is removed: `_scan_alias` no longer reads/returns jira matches; no `data.jira_key` resolution remains in resolver.py.
- [ ] Jira-shaped input with no binding (or missing/corrupt bindings.json, or binding to a non-existent dir) returns None without raising and without false alias/prefix match.
- [ ] Existing alias / short-id / full-id / prefix resolution unchanged (no regression); hard tracker-listing failure still returns None + a stderr diagnostic.

- [ ] Tests updated: replace the old jira_key-collision test with binding-store coverage (bound -> resolves; unbound -> None; missing/corrupt store -> None; binding -> non-existent dir -> None) and keep alias coverage green.
- [ ] `rebar show REB-310` resolves end-to-end (manual check noted on the ticket).
- [ ] make lint + the resolver test module pass.

baseline.summary: Resolve Jira issue keys (REB-NNN) in the centralized ID resolver via the binding store

baseline.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in **bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json` (1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x), and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git. An earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and dropped re-homing it off-branch because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift. The levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included under an operator-approved quiescence protocol. Its mechanics are proven: a length-aware `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` pipeline on the real branch produced 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges. The dynamic re-add restores the current `.bridge_state` files, so the rewritten HEAD tree is **exactly byte-identical** to the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree; only historical versions of the target paths are removed. Stock git plumbing is used because it is already available and proven for this repository, avoiding a new third-party core dependency. `git-filter-repo` could preserve empty commits with `--prune-empty=never`; DAG preservation is therefore not a reason to reject it.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` and add the write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`.
2. **A4-1** fence `bridge_fsck` before `prev_snapshot.json` is narrowed (independent of A1).
3. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; write both formats and
   read `max(new, legacy)`.
4. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority, deliberately excluding assignee.
5. **A2-2** delete the legacy inline `last_get_pass` field only after its rollout gate clears.
6. **A4-2** narrow `prev_snapshot.json` to a key-set after A4-1; record forward and reverse corpus
   mutation diffs before merge.
7. **A4-3** suppress branch-3 mutations whose effective Jira payload is empty.
8. **A5** record all committed-format changes, mixed-version rules, and rollback boundaries in
   an ADR after A3 and A4-2 establish the final shapes.
9. **A6-0a** add the fail-closed store-epoch guard at both union sites after A2-2 and A4-3.
10. **A6-0b** make the persistent review-bot clone self-converge and fix its deploy trigger; it
    ships with A6-0a so an `src/rebar/` change activates the deploy path.
11. **A6-0c** build and dry-run the stock-git history-strip tooling after A2-2 and A4-3.
12. **A6-0d** enumerate/delete ref pins and create/verify the off-repo backup bundle after A6-0c.
13. **A6-1** execute the reclaim last, only after A1-A5 and A6-0a..0d are closed and Epic B's B6
    is closed.

### Observable rollout gates

**A2-2 has no fixed-delay gate.** A completed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run must execute at a SHA descending from the A2-1 merge, and the host probe binary must be explicitly refreshed from a descendant build with its executable/version and absence of older reconcile processes recorded. A2-2 retains `max(sidecar, legacy)` read compatibility: any legacy writer output is migrated into the sidecar and scrubbed on the next new pass, so direct evidence plus self-healing replaces the former 24-hour proxy.

**A6-1 has no fixed-delay gate.** Before publication, every writer is quiesced; the completed reconciler workflow SHA must descend from A6-0a; the deployed review-bot runtime and the explicitly refreshed host runtime must each refuse an epoch mismatch in real-clone probes; and A6-0b must record the review-bot deployment receipt and persistent-clone convergence. Older binaries ignore the epoch, so direct behavioral proof from each deployed runtime is mandatory. The operator-attested zero-session/MCP-stop and bundle requirements remain additional gates.

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes share one store file. A2-1 is reversible because it continues writing the legacy field. A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes idempotently. A2-2 stops legacy writes and scrubs the field but retains the mixed-version read seam: a later inline stamp is promoted into `get_rotation.json` before removal. Its direct workflow/host deployment evidence and old/new-writer integration oracle replace elapsed time. A4-2 requires both the forward full->key-set corpus diff and the reverse key-set->full rollback diff before merge. The epoch value is introduced only by the reclaim commit, after the descendant workflow and both live writer runtimes have directly demonstrated fail-closed epoch behavior under quiescence.

Post-publish rollback

Post-publish rollback is an explicit second quiesced window, not an application-level union:

1. Disable both reconciler workflows, pause the review-bot/autodeploy writers, poll for no in-flight
   runs and an empty Gerrit review queue, and obtain the operator's zero-session/stopped-MCP
   confirmation again.
2. Verify the off-repo bundle, unbundle it into a fresh unfiltered scratch clone, and verify that
   the recorded old tip and deleted tag tips resolve exactly.
3. Restore the old `tickets` tip with `--force-with-lease=<rewritten-tip>:<old-tip>`. This direct,
   operator-controlled ref replacement does not run the application merge guards. Never bypass
   an epoch mismatch inside `sync._union_merge` or `push.py`.
4. Reset/reclone every writer (shared local tracker, review-bot EBS clone, and ephemeral workflow
   worktrees) to the restored tip before re-enabling writes. New-epoch clones must be replaced;
   their mismatch refusal is the safety signal, not a condition to override.
5. Re-run tree/count/identity checks, then re-enable writers in the same order as the forward path.

This makes the bundle executable as recovery while preserving fail-closed behavior in ordinary clients. A6 remains intentionally non-resumable; all graph assertions run on the scratch clone before either forward or rollback publication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Before A2-2 closes, its descendant workflow evidence, explicit host refresh, and
      mixed-version self-healing oracle are recorded. **[operator-attested rollout evidence]**
- [ ] Before reclaim publication, the descendant workflow ancestry result plus live review-bot and
      exact host-runtime epoch-refusal probes are recorded. **[operator-attested rollout evidence]**

- [ ] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline: 12.79 KB.
- [ ] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce byte-identical
      `bindings.json` and create no commit. Tier: stateful integration asserting bytes and commits.
- [ ] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference remains.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical.
- [ ] A dict-shaped baseline through live `compute_update_fields` matches its normalized-string
      equivalent, and stored description/status/priority are scalars while assignee stays raw.
- [ ] Full-prev versus key-set-prev corpus mutation diff over >=4 real snapshot pairs has zero
      delta in non-empty effects reaching Jira; the reverse-direction diff is recorded too.

content.text: ## Summary
The reconciler is not 1-pass idempotent for INBOUND-created (Jira->local) tickets.
`_apply_inbound_create` materialises a local ticket and writes the Jira-side
`rebar-id:<local_id>` label, but it never records the local<->jira binding in
the binding store. The outbound differ decides "bound" SOLELY from the binding
store (`compute_outbound_mutations`: "unbound local tickets emit create"), so on
the next pass the freshly-imported ticket looks unbound and an outbound CREATE is
re-emitted for it. It only converges later, when the outbound applier's
dedup-skip path (`_apply_outbound_create` -> bind_confirm) finally binds it.
Net effect: an imported ticket costs an extra outbound create + per-ticket Jira
dedup search on the following pass — non-idempotent churn (no data corruption,
because dedup-skip prevents duplicate Jira issues).
## How it surfaced (and the earlier RED herring)
Discovered via the 3 `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_once.py`
failures. The originally-filed hypothesis here (mutation_count=2 driven by the
`git add .bridge_state/bindings.json` exit-128) was WRONG — that git error is a
benign symptom (the unit test's tmp tracker isn't a git repo; bindings still
persist to the filesystem). The real driver is the missing binding above.
## Verified mechanism (bisect + instrumentation)
- Bisected the TEST breakage to commit 2840679 (the 23d2 read-path collapse):
6e58f4e -> 862 passed; 2840679 -> 3 failed.
- Instrumented `reconcile_once` across both engine versions:
pass-2 `_read_local_tickets` returns | pass-2 mutation_count
pre-23d2 : 0 tickets | 0   (GREEN)
post-23d2: 2 tickets | 2   (RED)
- Root of the TEST flip: pre-23d2 `rebar list` errored on the non-git tmp repo
(the test passes repo_root=<non-git tmp>), so `_read_local_tickets` returned
[] and the outbound differ saw no local tickets -> 0 mutations. That was a
FALSE GREEN: it never exercised the outbound dedup path. 23d2 made `rebar list`
read a REBAR_ROOT tracker without git validation, so the inbound-created
working-tree tickets became visible -> outbound differ re-pushed them.
- PRODUCTION is git-backed, so `rebar list` returns those tickets both before and
after 23d2 — i.e. production has ALWAYS had this 2-to-3-pass convergence; 23d2
only made the unit-test environment production-like enough to expose it.
## Experiments run
1. Faithful Jira fake that REFLECTS the `rebar-id:` label write-back across
passes (production-equivalent) + a real `git init` repo: pass-2 still
re-emitted outbound creates (mutation_count 4). => the label round-trip alone
does NOT make the outbound side idempotent; the outbound differ never consults
the snapshot label (outbound_differ.py:78 uses binding_store.get_jira_key only).
2. Proof the outbound binding signal is binding-store-only: read of
compute_outbound_mutations confirmed get_jira_key/is_bound is the sole source;
the differ.py:404 `rebar-id:` label stand-down governs only the INBOUND differ.
3. Trial fix (binding_store.bind_confirm(local_id, jira_key) in
_apply_inbound_create): broke the contract test
test_inbound_create_dedups_against_binding_store (its _FakeBindingStore has no
bind_confirm) AND mutation_count went 2->3 (binding the ticket made the
outbound differ emit an UPDATE for the import's field/label divergence, e.g.
the local-only `imported:reconciler-bootstrap` tag). => binding alone is
insufficient; the imported ticket must also net ZERO outbound divergence.
## Proposed solution (product-level, deferred)
Make `_apply_inbound_create` bind the ticket at creation time (it already holds
both ids; `bind_confirm` supports a direct confirm), AND ensure a freshly
imported ticket nets zero outbound mutations on the next pass:
- record the confirmed binding so the outbound differ sees it as bound;
- reconcile the import-only divergence (e.g. exclude/handle the
`imported:reconciler-bootstrap` tag and the status mapping) so no spurious
outbound UPDATE is emitted;
- update the unit fakes to be faithful:
* test_reconcile_once's acli stub must reflect label/property write-back
(and created issues) across passes;
* test_inbound_create_dedups_against_binding_store's _FakeBindingStore must
gain bind_confirm.
This removes the wasteful pass-2 push-then-dedup-skip round-trip and makes
reconcile genuinely 1-pass idempotent. Blast radius: inbound-reconcile semantics
for every imported ticket + several reconciler tests — do under its own change
with full reconciler-suite verification.
## Interim mitigation (LANDED, commit d747448)
Restored the pre-23d2 read precondition in `ticket_reads.tracker_dir()`: when the
tracker is resolved via repo-root (arg / PROJECT_ROOT / REBAR_ROOT), require root
to be a git work tree, else exit 1 ("not inside a git repository"). Explicit
TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR still reads directly (dispatcher fixtures unaffected);
library/MCP reads via config.tracker_dir unchanged. This makes the 3 tests pass
again (rebar list -> [] in the minimal env, as _read_local_tickets documents) and
restores the correct git-backed contract — but it RESTORES THE FALSE GREEN; it
does not fix the underlying non-idempotency. Full suite green after: pytest 1295
passed / 0 failed, bash 94/94, probe 141/141.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] inbound_create records the local<->jira binding at creation (bind_confirm)
- [ ] A freshly imported ticket produces ZERO outbound mutations on the next pass
(no spurious update from import-only tag/status divergence)
- [ ] reconcile_once is idempotent on pass 2 over an unchanged remote, verified
with a FAITHFUL acli fake (reflects label/property write-back + created
issues) on a git-backed repo — not by `rebar list` returning []
- [ ] test_inbound_create_dedups_against_binding_store updated (fake gains
bind_confirm) and still green
- [ ] Full reconciler suite + interface/schema suites green
- [ ] Consider relocating reconcile_once idempotency coverage to the integration
tier (it needs a faithful Jira round-trip, not a unit stub)

baseline.summary: reconcile not 1-pass idempotent: inbound_create never records its binding (imported tickets re-pushed outbound until dedup-skip converges)

baseline.description:
# Stop auto-deploy killing live code reviews: quiesce via a full-review drain window, and fail-NO-VOTE for retryable conditions

## Problem

The continuous auto-deploy restarts the review-bot container while a code review is in flight, and the interrupted review casts a fail-closed `LLM-Review -1`. That vote then BLOCKS the automatic recovery which already exists, so every occurrence costs a human re-trigger. Observed FOUR times in one session (changes 1132/1189/1193/1208; three of four had a `main` commit land mid-review; measured review durations 260-911s against a 45s drain).

### What the code actually does today (verified against source)

* `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` ALREADY deploys only on change: `changed()` diffs
  deployed-sha..target per path-class and rebuilds the bot only when `BOT_PATHS` /
  `SECRETS_PATHS` changed (autodeploy.sh:219-230). "Deploy only when the image changes" is
  already true — the unexplained 1193 collision needs a different explanation (candidates:
  a SECRETS_PATHS-only refresh, or a backoff retry of a previously-failed target;
  investigate during implementation and record on this ticket).
* The shutdown drain ALREADY waits for the in-flight review: the lifespan does
  `await queue.join()` bounded by `shutdown_drain_seconds()` (app.py:117) and the worker
  marks the queue item done only after `review_and_vote` returns. The defect is purely the
  CONSTANT: `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS = 45` (config.py:42) versus
  `DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1200` (config.py:30). A deploy landing mid-review
  times out the drain at 45s, cancels the worker, and the teardown-corrupted review
  fail-closes a `-1`.
* The backfill reconciler (`reconcile.py`) re-drives any CURRENT revision with NO
  `LLM-Review` vote, on startup and every 300s. Casting the fail-closed `-1` makes the
  change invisible to it — the veto disables the recovery designed for this failure.

## Change 1 — quiesce: size the drain to a full review (operator-approved 20 min)

Raise `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` from 45 to 1200 (= the per-review timeout — the principled bound: the drain exists to let the in-flight review finish, and the review is already wall-clock-bounded by `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). Resize `stop_grace_period` in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` per its existing derivation (drain + store write-lock budget + push reconcile lock): 1200 + 60 + 45 -> 1320s, updating the derivation comment. `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_reviewbot_stop_grace_period_covers_an_in_flight_store_write` reads both values from source and enforces the relationship — it must pass unmodified.

Cost when no review is in flight: none (`queue.join()` returns immediately on an empty queue). Cost when one is in flight: the deploy waits for it — that is the point (the Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds/preStop pattern). The 2-minute timer cadence stays: a deploy that quiesces is safe at any cadence, and autodeploy already no-ops on an unchanged target.

## Change 2 — fail-NO-VOTE for retryable coverage gaps, with a bounded escalation

Matches how Zuul (jobs interrupted by an executor restart are retried without reporting) and Prow (evicted jobs are rescheduled) behave; the bounded retry mirrors Zuul's RETRY_LIMIT.

* `adapter.code_review_decision` already classifies every non-PASS outcome
  (`_TAG_SUFFIXES` / `_coverage_gap_reason`). Thread the machine-readable sub-reason out
  of `_block` as a new `gap_reason` key on the decision dict (None for PASS/finding).
* In `voter.review_and_vote`, when the decision is a coverage-gap BLOCK with a RETRYABLE
  `gap_reason` — `review-error`, `llm-unavailable`, `scanner`, `gate-disabled` — do NOT
  post the vote. Record the attempt in a new `review_attempts` table beside the dedup
  ledger (`dedup.py` SQLite, keyed `(change_id, revision)`), emit a distinct greppable
  `REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED` marker, and return. The change stays vote-less, so the EXISTING
  backfill reconciler re-drives it within `RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` — no reconciler
  change needed.
* `indeterminate` is TERMINAL (vote the `-1`): by CI-system semantics a review that RAN TO
  COMPLETION and concluded "cannot establish coverage" is a result, not an interruption.
  `finding` is unchanged. The merge-path `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` keeps its current
  fail-closed vote in this ticket: it deliberately gets NO `gap_reason` key (its REST
  failures are pre-review setup; revisit separately if it recurs), and the voter's
  deferral protocol keys strictly on `gap_reason` being present and retryable.
* Bounded escalation: when `review_attempts` reaches the cap (new
  `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, default 3, env-overridable via `ReceiverConfig`), cast the
  fail-closed `-1` with the original reason's tag plus an appended "automatic retries
  exhausted" note (tag VOCABULARY unchanged — the tag test keeps passing), and emit the
  existing `VOTER_ERROR` marker so the `rebar/host:voter_errors` alarm surface fires.
  The attempts store is deliberately shaped for ticket bb9b's contributor re-trigger to
  RESET (shared retry budget). Reset semantics: `reset_attempts(change_id, revision)`
  DELETES the row (no status flags, no zeroed counters left behind) — after a reset the
  store is indistinguishable from "never attempted". The attempt is recorded (INSERT/
  increment) BEFORE the deferral `return`; a SQLite failure on that write is caught and
  logged as `VOTER_ERROR` and the deferral still returns vote-less (an uncounted attempt
  only delays escalation by one cycle — fail-open on the counter, never on the vote).
* Teardown mid-review needs no separate discriminator: the deferral decision happens
  before any vote POST, so a teardown-corrupted review that fail-closes as `review-error`
  is deferred vote-less, and with Change 1 the cancel almost never lands mid-review at
  all.

### Constraints (both verified as part of implementation)

1. **No silent-pass hole.** Vote-less stays unsubmittable (submit REQUIRES `LLM-Review +1`);
   assert no reconciler degraded mode turns "no vote" into "submittable".
2. **Genuinely vote-less.** The deferral posts NOTHING to the change (no provisional
   comment), or the reconciler's no-vote pre-filter would be re-suppressed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py` — drain default 45 -> 1200; new
  `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`.
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — `stop_grace_period` 150s -> 1320s + derivation
  comment.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` — `gap_reason` on the decision dict.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` — defer-not-vote for retryable gaps + bounded
  escalation.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/dedup.py` — the `review_attempts` table: `record_attempt` /
  `attempt_count` keyed `(change_id, revision)`, and `reset_attempts` = DELETE the row.
  This table is SEPARATE from the existing `voted` table; the deferred path writes ONLY
  to `review_attempts`, never to `voted`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerate for the new env var (the committed registry is drift-
  gated by `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py::test_check_mode_clean_against_committed_tree`).
- `docs/review-policy.md` — document the retryable/terminal split and the escalation.
- Tests in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` (see below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` is 1200 and compose `stop_grace_period` is
      1320s; `test_reviewbot_stop_grace_period_covers_an_in_flight_store_write` passes
      unmodified.
- [ ] AC2: a coverage-gap decision with `gap_reason` in {review-error, llm-unavailable,
      scanner, gate-disabled} casts NO vote, records an attempt, and posts nothing to the
      change, and emits the greppable `REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED` marker — asserted by a
      unit test per reason.
- [ ] AC3: `indeterminate` and `finding` still cast the `-1`, and PASS still casts the
      `+1` — asserted by tests (no behaviour change for terminal outcomes).
- [ ] AC4: the Nth (default 3rd) consecutive retryable failure on the same
      `(change_id, revision)` casts the fail-closed `-1` with the "retries exhausted" note
      and emits `VOTER_ERROR` — asserted by a test; the cap is env-overridable.
- [ ] AC5: the deferred path leaves the change eligible for the backfill reconciler — no
      row in the `voted` table and no Gerrit vote (the `review_attempts` row from AC2 is
      expected and does NOT suppress re-drive) — asserted by a test driving the
      reconciler over a deferred change.
- [ ] AC6: `docs/review-policy.md` documents the retryable/terminal split, the bound, and
      the escalation surface.
- [ ] AC7: `docs/env-vars.md` is regenerated and committed (its drift-gate test passes),
      and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the review-bot test module pass.

## Testing / Verification

From the worktree venv:
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Relationship to bb9b

`bb9b-608f-0183-4ca5` (lands second) gives contributors a manual re-trigger for any remaining `-1` that is not a real finding — including this ticket's escalated `-1` — implemented as "reset the shared `review_attempts` budget + force re-review". This ticket deliberately shapes the attempts store for that reuse.
baseline.summary: Stop auto-deploy killing live reviews: full-review drain quiesce + fail-NO-VOTE for retryable coverage gaps

## Reproduction Steps

Run `rebar bridge-fsck` — the offline binding-drift arm (epic 3006-e198,
the convergence parity oracle) reports a non-empty `binding_drift` section.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** `binding_drift` is empty (every bound pair converged).
- **Actual:** dangling=4
- **Detected at:** 2026-07-12T18:26:01Z
- **Canary run:** https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/29203803389

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each reported drift is triaged (would_terminal → local archive/delete
      to propagate; dangling → confirmed 404 GC; unbound_jira → adopt or
      archive the Jira-native issue; local_gone → investigate).
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` reports an empty `binding_drift` section.

This ticket auto-closes when bridge-fsck next reports zero binding drift.
