baseline.description:
Cut CI tickets-store transfer cost across both checkout mechanisms. Measured evidence in session_log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 and epic comments: recurring actions/checkout full checkout 1.04 GiB / 59 s versus blob:none 68.7 MiB / 14.3 s; Gerrit verify-identity full tickets fetch 6.73 minutes, with local full 1.4 GB / 66.2 s versus blob:none 22 MB / 3.6 s and 83 MB / 8.6 s after worktree materialization. These recorded baselines do not replace runtime guards.

## Scope and mechanisms
Add the published actions/checkout v7 filter input while retaining fetch-depth: 0 and existing credential/ref settings in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml, .github/workflows/verify-identity.yml, and .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml. These all-history checkouts currently fetch tickets before the mount step.

A later plain git fetch origin +tickets must inherit the named remote filter. Config presence is insufficient because Git records partialclonefilter even when a server ignores it. Prove actual protocol negotiation and missing-object behavior.

In .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml both tickets fetches use a direct URL, so named-remote inheritance does not apply. Add --filter=blob:none explicitly to the depth-1 require-ticket fetch and the full-history verify-identity fetch, preserving their different depth semantics. blob:none retains the complete commit graph needed by merge-base and era scoping; depth remains forbidden on the identity fetch.

## Real-Git fixture and protocol oracle
Start git daemon on localhost with --export-all and --enable=upload-pack. Point GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at a temporary global config containing uploadpack.allowFilter=true and set GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 in the daemon environment, so daemon/upload-pack inherit filter support. Repository-local uploadpack.allowFilter is forbidden because git daemon ignores it for security. Do not use a file URL. Reserve a loopback port, then retry a socket connection every 100 ms for at most 30 seconds; startup failure raises immediately. The module-scoped pytest fixture uses yield/finally and always terminate()+wait(timeout=5), then kill()+wait() if necessary, so failures cannot leak the daemon.

Set GIT_TRACE_PACKET=<unique tmp trace file> in each git subprocess environment. A Git 2.55 probe observed packet: fetch> filter blob:none for fetch and packet: clone> filter blob:none for clone. Tests must not hard-code the actor label. Require a server capability packet advertising filter plus a client-to-server packet matching packet:\s+\S+>\s+filter blob:none$. Also assert the known tickets blob is reported missing before materialization.

The fixture commits an incompressible historical blob larger than 140 MiB, removes it, and leaves a tip whose total files are below 1 MiB. After server-side gc:
- standalone pre-materialization contrast: unfiltered all-history size-pack exceeds REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=102400; blobless size-pack is below 102400;
- Gerrit post-materialization contrast: unfiltered all-history size-pack exceeds REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=131072; blobless plus small-tip materialization stays below 131072.
Execute the actual workflow guard blocks against these repos so broken parsing, units, or comparisons fail.

Capture separate packet traces for plain named-origin inheritance, direct URL with --depth=1 --filter=blob:none, and direct URL full-history with --filter=blob:none. Each must satisfy the capability/request regex and missing-blob oracle.

Never use filter: tree:0: measured 3.57 GiB across 2,255 promisor packs. git worktree add uses unpack-trees -u/check_updates and batch-prefetches missing promisor blobs, unlike the read-tree plus checkout-index footgun in tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py. A real-Git E2E materializes tickets, creates independent local and remote changes, fetches/merges with the B3 ours driver, retains all expected events, and pushes successfully.

## Production guardrails
- Standalone verify-identity declares REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=102400. Immediately after actions/checkout, parse size-pack from git count-objects -v and fail above that limit.
- Gerrit verify-identity declares REBAR_TICKETS_PACK_LIMIT_KIB=131072. After filtered fetch and worktree materialization, fail above that limit; this patchset run proves GitHub honored the direct filter.
- In both identity jobs, snapshot exact git count-objects -v after materialization, run rebar verify-identity, snapshot again, and fail if any line differs. Materialization may fetch tip blobs; identity scanning must add no objects.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each target actions/checkout@v7 step sets filter: blob:none. Tier: parsed workflow. Proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k checkout_filter -v.
- [ ] Each target checkout retains fetch-depth: 0 and prior credential/ref inputs. Tier: parsed workflow. Proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k checkout_preserves_inputs -v.
- [ ] Gerrit require-ticket passes --filter=blob:none and retains --depth=1. Tier: parsed workflow. Proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k require_ticket_fetch -v.
- [ ] Gerrit verify-identity passes --filter=blob:none and has no depth option. Tier: parsed workflow. Proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k identity_fetch -v.
- [ ] Production guards parse size-pack and use the declared 102400 KiB and 131072 KiB limits. Tier: executable workflow. Proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k pack_guard_contract -v.
- [ ] The actual standalone guard rejects unfiltered all-history size-pack above 102400 KiB. Tier: real-Git contrast. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k standalone_guard_rejects_full -v.
- [ ] The actual standalone guard accepts blobless pre-materialization size-pack below 102400 KiB. Tier: real-Git contrast. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k standalone_guard_accepts_blobless -v.
- [ ] The actual Gerrit guard rejects unfiltered all-history size-pack above 131072 KiB. Tier: real-Git contrast. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k gerrit_guard_rejects_full -v.
- [ ] The actual Gerrit guard accepts blobless materialized-tip size-pack below 131072 KiB. Tier: real-Git boundary. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k gerrit_guard_accepts_materialized -v.
- [ ] Plain named-origin fetch advertises filter capability, sends filter blob:none, and leaves the known blob missing. Tier: real Git protocol. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k named_origin_filter -v.
- [ ] Depth-1 direct URL fetch advertises filter capability, sends filter blob:none, and leaves the known blob missing. Tier: real Git protocol. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k direct_depth_filter -v.
- [ ] Full-history direct URL fetch advertises filter capability, sends filter blob:none, and leaves the known blob missing. Tier: real Git protocol. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k direct_full_filter -v.
- [ ] Blobless tickets reconverge independent local/remote changes with the ours driver, retain expected events, and push the merge. Tier: real-Git E2E. Proving command: pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k reconverges -v.
- [ ] Standalone identity leaves exact git count-objects -v unchanged. Tier: workflow plus real Git. Proving commands: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k standalone_no_promisor -v and pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k standalone_identity_no_promisor -v.
- [ ] Gerrit identity leaves exact git count-objects -v unchanged. Tier: workflow plus real Git. Proving commands: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k gerrit_no_promisor -v and pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k gerrit_identity_no_promisor -v.

## Files and rollback
Files: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml; .github/workflows/verify-identity.yml; .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml; .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py; tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py.

Rollback is one Gerrit revert restoring prior full fetches and removing paired guards. Do not disable only a failing guard: a threshold trip means the cost regression is real until the filter/server path is repaired or the whole optimization is reverted.

Scope: M. Depends on closed B3 040e-3f0c-ae86-4212 and closed B6 3036-cb14-86b5-44a3.
baseline.summary: B1: apply filter: blob:none to every CI tickets-branch fetch path

baseline.description:
## Why

FixedBench's 35-65% over-action result has no plan-review counterpart: no criterion asks
whether a proposed change is actually *needed*. Separately, bug tickets are gate-exempt — the
plan-review gate short-circuits every `bug` to a bare exempt-PASS
(`workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck` src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:150-160 →
`orchestrator._exempt_verdict` src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:676), so a bug gets no
substantive review at all (verified on bug 5886: its persisted REVIEW_RESULT was
`{"runner":"exempt","verdict":"PASS","llm_calls":0}`).

This story ships two coupled ADVISORY pieces. Prior art: T1's FixedBench over-action finding
(the over-action gap this probe closes) and the R1/R3 advisory-criterion pattern
(`asserted-capability`, `decomp-shape`) — registered advisory, calibrated by
`rebar criteria eval`, auto-monitored by the standing recorder (d8a5).

## Advisory-first strategy (re-plan — supersedes the stub)

The stub gated R4 on "retrospective eval on E2's class-4 (unnecessary-mechanism) mutant
corpus". That corpus does NOT exist on main and E2/E3 batch evals are PERMANENTLY REJECTED on
cost, so this re-plan DROPS the E2 dependency (`depends_on d125` removed) and validates with
BOUNDED, HAND-AUTHORED fixtures run through `rebar criteria eval` (<=~8 live single-criterion
runs, NOT a batch). Both pieces ship ADVISORY (never block). Post-ship effectiveness is dogfood
monitoring via the standing recorder + the advisory->blocking promotion gate — recorded as an
`[operator-attested]` observation, not a config flag.

## What — piece (a): necessity / no-op probe (pass-1 advisory)

A new pass-1 advisory criterion `necessity` that flags a plan which does NOT demonstrate the
change is needed — current behavior neither reproduced nor motivated (the FixedBench over-action
gap: a plan that adds a mechanism without establishing the need). It ACCEPTS justified no-op /
docs-test-only / well-motivated outcomes (a plan with reproduction + motivation PASSES). It is a
single-turn (1-TURN) plan-text judgment, DISTINCT from R1's `asserted-capability` (which greps
for an already-existing implementation): `necessity` asks whether the plan MOTIVATES the change
at all, not whether a named module already provides it.

- `criteria_routing.json`: new `necessity` entry — `exec:"1-TURN"`, `facet:"scope-intent"`,
  `default_posture:"advisory"`, `block_threshold:0.95`, `applies_at.scope:["leaf"]`, and
  deliberately NO `suppress_types` (so it applies to `bug` — required by piece (b); contrast
  F1/F4/A1/G7 which all `suppress_types:["bug"]`).
- `registry.py`: register `necessity` in `CANONICAL_LLM` (so
  `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` does NOT flag it ORPHAN and fail CI).
- `reviewers/plan_review_necessity.md`: the rubric prompt (gate sub-answer + grounded
  sub-answer), and regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`.
- Wire it into the production Pass-1 finder batch (`workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` `criteria:`
  list, gated by `when: include_necessity`) so it actually runs on leaf plan reviews.

## What — piece (b): lightweight bug review tier

Bugs stop short-circuiting to bare exempt-PASS; instead the plan-review gate runs a LIGHT
ADVISORY tier = the DET floor + the `necessity` probe, never blocking a bug.

- `workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck`: for `ticket_type == "bug"`, run the DET floor, DOWNGRADE
  all DET findings to advisory (`det_blocking:[]` — a bug is never blocked), set `run_llm:True`,
  and stamp `coverage.bug_tier`. (`session_log`/`code_review`/`identity` stay exempt.)
- `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria`: for `ticket_type == "bug"`, restrict the
  included LLM criteria to `registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA` (= `("necessity",)`) so a bug gets the
  DET floor + necessity only (the light tier), not the full suite.
- `registry.py`: add `BUG_TIER_CRITERIA = ("necessity",)`.
- The CLI claim-time bug exemption (`_commands/gates.py:93`) is UNCHANGED — a bug still needs no
  signed attestation to be claimed; this tier only makes an explicit `rebar review-plan <bug>`
  (and the gate run) produce a substantive advisory review instead of exempt-PASS.

## Approach rationale

Reuse the R1/R3 advisory-criterion seam wholesale (routing entry + `CANONICAL_LLM` + rubric +
`rebar criteria eval` fixture + auto-monitoring) rather than a bespoke path — it is the proven,
lint-clean, non-orphan pattern. The bug tier reuses the existing `probe_criteria`-style
criteria restriction (route_criteria/assemble) rather than a new engine branch: bugs flow the
SAME find->verify->decide passes, just with a one-criterion included set and DET downgraded to
advisory, so the "never block a bug" invariant is structural (advisory posture + empty
det_blocking), not a special-case in the decision kernel.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`: `criteria_routing.json` (necessity entry), `registry.py`
  (CANONICAL_LLM + BUG_TIER_CRITERIA), `workflow_ops.py` (bug-tier precheck + assemble),
  `reviewers/plan_review_necessity.md`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (finder batch slot).
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-necessity.eval.yaml` (bounded sanity fixtures).
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (regenerated), `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (bug tier +
  necessity probe + promotion gate).
- `tests/unit/` deterministic unit tests; `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/` sanity
  artifacts.
- Module-size: hard 800-LOC absolute cap on any `src/rebar` file (no allowlist); if a touched
  file would exceed 800, extract a new module. Sequenced AFTER the floor-split (dep 7d91).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both pieces are registered ADVISORY and non-orphan:
  `python -c "import json,rebar.llm.plan_review.registry as r; d=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json')); assert d['necessity']['default_posture']=='advisory'; assert 'bug' not in d['necessity'].get('applies_at',{}).get('suppress_types',[]); assert 'necessity' in r.CANONICAL_LLM; assert r.validate_packaged_routing()==[]; assert r.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA==('necessity',)"`
  exits 0.
- [ ] Deterministic (no-LLM) unit tests pin the non-LLM logic and pass:
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_necessity_criterion.py tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py -q`
  green — registration/routing/prompt-contract/fixture-shape/guide-section/effectiveness
  auto-inclusion for necessity, AND the bug-tier lifecycle (precheck emits `run_llm=True` +
  `det_blocking==[]` + `coverage.bug_tier` for a bug; assemble restricts a bug's included set to
  `necessity`; the tier never yields a blocking verdict for a bug).
- [ ] Bounded live sanity committed (<=~8 live single-criterion runs, NOT an E2/E3 batch): the
  necessity probe FIRES on an over-action positive (adds a mechanism it does not motivate) and is
  CLEAN on a well-motivated negative — `rebar criteria eval necessity --output json` recall 1.0
  over the positives / false-accept 0.0 over the negatives, committed to
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/necessity_sanity.json`. AND the bug tier gives bug 5886
  a light advisory review instead of a bare exempt-PASS (verdict `runner != "exempt"`, the
  necessity probe ran, no blocking), committed to
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/bug_tier_sanity.json`.
  (5886 is NOT a necessity-probe fixture — it is a well-motivated absent-capability bug, so it is
  the bug-tier lifecycle fixture, not an over-action positive.)
- [ ] Both criteria auto-flow into the standing recorder with zero wiring:
  `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/criterion_effectiveness.py --report`
  includes `necessity` when a REVIEW_RESULT cites it (pinned by the effectiveness unit test).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the bug review tier and the necessity probe, and the
  advisory->blocking promotion gate for both (citing the standing per-criterion effectiveness
  recorder protocol, epic d8a5).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The advisory->blocking promotion decision is dogfood-gated on the
  standing recorder's trailing metrics (high detection_proxy, low blocking_fp_proxy, sufficient
  sample) — recorded as an observation expectation on this ticket, met by the Gerrit change
  landing MERGED with both gate votes green (change id / Verified+1 / LLM-Review+1 recorded on
  the ticket), not by an in-session command.
baseline.summary: R4: necessity/no-op probe + lightweight bug review tier (gated retrospective)

# `_resolve_target`'s "already provider-qualified" test is `":" in model`, and real Bedrock ids contain a colon

## Impact, stated first

**Any model class configured with `provider = "bedrock"` and a CANONICAL versioned Bedrock model id is broken, and it fails with an error that names the wrong thing.** Canonical Bedrock ids carry a version suffix containing a colon — `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` — which is the majority form of the ids AWS publishes. Only the unversioned aliases (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`) happen to work. This is in the middle of what epic 061c ships ("first-class AWS Bedrock provider").

## Mechanism, confirmed by experiment (no LLM spend)

`model_classes._resolve_target` decides whether to prefix the configured provider by asking whether the model string already contains a colon:

    def _resolve_target(model: str, provider: str | None) -> str:
        # Already provider-qualified -- return as-is, never double-prefix.
        if ":" in model:
            return model
        resolved_provider = provider or infer_provider(model)
        return f"{resolved_provider}:{model}" if resolved_provider else model

A versioned Bedrock id satisfies `":" in model` for the WRONG reason — the colon is inside its version suffix, not a provider separator — so the function returns the bare model and the operator's explicit `provider = "bedrock"` is silently discarded:

    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",              "bedrock")
      -> "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"                      # correct
    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", "bedrock")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"                 # provider LOST
    _resolve_target("anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0",     "bedrock")
      -> "anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0"                     # provider LOST

Downstream that unqualified string is read back as `provider:model` on the FIRST colon, so:

    infer_provider("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1"

…and the provider factory rejects it. Reproduced end-to-end through the real class table:

    parse_class_slots({"standard": {"model": "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
                                    "provider": "bedrock"}})
    resolve_class("standard", slots) -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"

## Observed live (this is how it was found)

A real `rebar review-code` run with `standard` pointed at the versioned Bedrock haiku id produced:

    verdict: INDETERMINATE, llm_ran: False
    llm_error: "step 'verify' failed: unknown provider
                'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1';
                registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']"

The whole gate degraded to INDETERMINATE. Note how misleading the message is: the operator configured `provider = "bedrock"` — which IS registered — and the error blames a "provider" that is actually most of their model id.

## Why the current test cannot simply be tightened to "split on the last colon"

The two forms are genuinely ambiguous on a naive scan: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains TWO colons, and `us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains one. Splitting on the first colon mis-reads the second form; splitting on the last mis-reads the first. The distinguishing fact is not colon position but whether the prefix names a REGISTERED PROVIDER — the same set the error message already prints.

## Acceptance criteria

**Delivered in TWO STAGES.** This ticket's change fixed the reported failure and the guard order; the alignment with prevailing practice is delivered by child `7b22` and this ticket does not close until it does. The split is recorded here rather than left implicit, because the original AC below asked for the registry in one step and the implementation shipped a shape test instead — an OSS survey then found the registry is the norm and that the reason for deviating was answerable. See the comments.

### This ticket's change (done)

- [x] a configured `provider` is honoured for a model id containing a colon: a class configured
      `{model: "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", provider: "bedrock"}` resolves to
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
- [x] an ALREADY-qualified string is still not double-prefixed: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` stays
      unchanged (this is the property the original test was protecting and it must not regress)
- [x] the qualified/unqualified decision is NO LONGER made by the presence of a colon, and both
      deciders (`_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`) route through ONE shared function
      (`split_provider_qualifier`) so they cannot drift apart — the original defect was two
      independent implementations of one question
- [x] **GUARD ORDER: an explicitly configured `provider` is checked FIRST, before the model string is
      scanned at all**, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule or discard it. Added after the
      OSS survey showed this is the actual fix for the bug CLASS: LangChain uses `:` as its separator
      and is immune purely because `not model_provider` is the first condition it tests. Without this,
      `_resolve_target("openai:gpt-4o", provider="bedrock")` still silently dropped the configured
      provider — the same defect reached by a different input
- [x] a conflicting configured-provider / inline-qualifier pair RAISES rather than silently picking a
      winner, since either choice discards an explicit instruction
- [x] a bare id with no configured provider still infers as it does today (back-compat: every
      existing unversioned value resolves byte-for-byte unchanged)
- [x] tests cover BOTH Bedrock id shapes — unversioned alias and canonical `...-v1:0` — because
      the unversioned form passes even against the bug and is what hid it
- [x] `infer_provider` agrees with the qualifier on every shape the tests cover
- [x] the reported failure mode is gone: no diagnostic reports a fragment of a model id as though it
      were a configured provider

### Delegated to child `7b22` (this ticket stays open until it closes)

- [ ] the qualified/unqualified decision is made against the REGISTERED PROVIDER SET rather than by
      prefix shape, so a future provider name needs no second edit here — the mechanism every
      comparable project uses (LangChain, LiteLLM, pydantic-ai, Vercel AI SDK, simonw/llm)
- [ ] a provider name that is not registered produces a diagnostic naming the invalid provider and
      listing the valid ones. This is the capability a shape test CANNOT provide, and it is why the
      rework is required rather than optional: a typo'd provider
      (`_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")`) currently passes silently
- [ ] back-compat is enumerated and tested against the runtime registries, since a stricter test
      risks breaking provider names that work today but are absent from a static list

## Notes

Found while gathering ticket 3768's non-default-provider evidence, which the bug BLOCKS for any versioned id; that evidence was obtained with unversioned aliases as a workaround. Not folded into b690 (whose change is already `LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1`) because it is an unrelated seam with its own back-compat surface. Filed under epic 061c per the operator's standing ruling that provider- seam wiring is epic work; the epic's mandate is to ship without bugs, so flagging rather than deferring silently.
baseline.summary: Bedrock: a configured provider is silently DROPPED for any model id containing a colon (the canonical '...-v1:0' form)

The B5 cutover defaulted verify.gate_engine to workflow, but the workflow PLAN-REVIEW verify/coach prompt steps fail on the LIVE path: the generic RunnerAgentStep supplies only {ticket_id, ticket_context, repo_path}, not the {{plan}} variable (nor the findings/surviving listing in instructions) the plan-review verifier/coach prompts require — the way bespoke pass2_verify/pass4_coach (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py) construct them via resolve_prompt({'plan': plan}) + a findings listing. So review-plan via the workflow engine degrades to INDETERMINATE. PR #42 flipped the default back to bespoke as a hotfix; this story completes the plumbing so workflow becomes a correct default again.
## What

- Supply {{plan}} to the workflow verify + coach prompt steps. Likely: make RunnerAgentStep (src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py) merge the step's with: string inputs into the resolve_prompt template variables, and have an op emit the plan text (extend plan_review_assemble_criteria or add an op) + the findings/surviving listing as instructions (reuse the bespoke listing builders from passes.py:pass2_verify/pass4_coach, extracted to a shared helper — no duplication).
- Wire the plan + instructions into BOTH dynamic-verify arms (agentic + single-turn) and into coach_notes, in gates/plan-review.yaml.
- Consider whether verify should batch (bespoke batches findings by 12) — document or implement.

- ADD a LIVE smoke test (REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM) that runs review-plan via the workflow engine on a real ticket and asserts a non-INDETERMINATE verdict — the offline parity harness can't catch this (canned agents bypass prompt resolution).
- Once live-correct, re-default verify.gate_engine to workflow.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The workflow plan-review verify + coach steps resolve {{plan}} and receive the findings/surviving listing on the LIVE path (no 'undefined variable' failure).
- [ ] A live review-plan via the workflow engine returns a real PASS/BLOCK verdict (not INDETERMINATE) and signs a byte-compatible attestation.
- [ ] A live (gated) smoke test guards this so the offline blind spot can't recur.
- [ ] verify.gate_engine default is flipped back to workflow.
- [ ] make lint + full test suite pass.

Set `merge.ours.driver=true` in the reconciler workflow so the tickets branch's `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` attribute actually resolves on GHA. Latent bug today; hard prerequisite for B1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`init.py:508-511` sets `merge.ours.driver` **per clone**, and it is never committed; `reconcile-bridge.yml` never sets it. So on the runner the `merge=ours` attribute names an **undefined driver** and git silently falls back to a 3-way text merge of an **18,231,660-byte** JSON file — the opposite of the local-wins behaviour the design assumes.

**Scope correction (plan-review G6 remediation): the canary is NOT in scope.** `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` does a bare `git worktree add` at `:88` but then calls **`rebar init` at `:146`**, and its own comment at `:138-140` explains why ("a bare `git worktree add` of the tickets branch does NOT create ... and the write seam refuses every rebar write without it"). So the canary already gets `merge.ours.driver` via `_merge_ours_unit`. `reconcile-bridge.yml` does the bare worktree add at `:117` and **never** calls `rebar init`, which is why only it is affected. An earlier draft listed both workflows; that was wrong.

This must land before B1: `blob:none` keeps commits but removes merge-base **blobs**, which the reconverge path materializes, so filtering while the driver is undefined makes an already-fragile path lazily fault large blobs mid-merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `reconcile-bridge.yml` sets `merge.ours.driver=true` for the tickets worktree before any merge
      step. Tier: **unit** workflow-lint assertion.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py -v`.
- [ ] The canary is asserted to obtain the driver via its existing `rebar init` call, so it needs no
      edit — a regression guard against re-adding the change there. Tier: **unit** workflow-lint.
- [ ] A reconverge against a **diverged** remote in a fresh runner-shaped checkout resolves
      `.bridge_state/*` **local-wins** (not a text merge) and produces no conflict markers. Tier:
      **integration** in a real temporary git repo mimicking the runner setup.
- [ ] The same scenario **without** the config produces the text-merge behaviour — the negative
      control proving the test detects the defect. Tier: **integration**.

## Files
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`, tests (the canary is deliberately untouched)

Scope: XS-S. No dependencies.
baseline.summary: B3: define merge.ours.driver on the reconciler runner (prerequisite for the CI clone filter)

## Context

rebar's test suite drives the tool largely by SUBPROCESS — the CLI adapter shells out to `python -m rebar.cli`, and many exit-code/CLI tests do the same (≈245 test files use subprocess / spec_from_file_location). coverage.py's in-process tracer never sees that child-process execution, so the measured in-process coverage (**77%** on 2026-06-27, see docs/coverage.md) UNDERSTATES the true exercised fraction. Because of this, `fail_under` is held at a deliberately conservative 70 — it cannot honestly track real coverage while subprocess work is invisible.

Research (peers + coverage.py docs) summary:
- **Modern recipe is ~3 lines**: `[tool.coverage.run] patch = ["subprocess"]` (coverage.py >= 7.10; auto-enables `parallel = true`) plus a `coverage combine` step before the report. pytest-cov >= 7.0 removed its own subprocess support and defers to coverage.py.
- **rebar is the easy case**: its subprocesses run in the SAME environment as the tests (no throwaway venvs), so NO `[tool.coverage.paths]` remapping is needed (unlike pip/tox/virtualenv).
- **Not universal practice**: process-spawning tools (pip, tox, nox, virtualenv, coverage.py itself) measure subprocess coverage; many mature CLIs (pdm, hatch, pipx, pre-commit) accept the in-process undercount with a conservative floor — the current documented stance here.
- **Real gotchas for us**: the `coverage combine` step becomes mandatory (erase -> test -> combine -> report); per-process tracing overhead (mitigate with `core = "sysmon"` on 3.12+); and crucially, rebar has many CLI EXIT-CODE tests — a child that calls `os._exit()` or is SIGTERM-killed never flushes coverage data, so we likely need `patch = ["subprocess", "_exit"]` and/or `sigterm = true`, and should expect to chase some flakiness.

Priority P4: optional, forward-looking. docs/coverage.md already documents this under "Future: subprocess coverage". Pick up when raising the real coverage number becomes worth the combine-step + exit-code-flush complexity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[tool.coverage.run] patch = ["subprocess"]` (or the classic COVERAGE_PROCESS_START + parallel recipe if needed) is enabled and instruments `python -m rebar.cli` children.
- [ ] The exit-code-test flush problem is handled (`patch` includes `_exit` and/or `sigterm = true`); the CLI exit-code suite stays green with no flakiness.
- [ ] The Makefile + CI coverage step run erase -> test -> `coverage combine` -> report in order (the combine step is wired so the report reads the merged parallel data).
- [ ] The reported coverage number measurably rises above the 77% in-process figure (subprocess work now counted); the delta is recorded in docs/coverage.md.
- [ ] `fail_under` is raised to a real guard under the new measured number; docs/coverage.md baseline + 'Future' section updated to reflect that subprocess coverage is now ON.
- [ ] Perf overhead is acceptable (consider `core = "sysmon"` on 3.12+); CI wall-clock regression is noted.
- [ ] CI measures the TRUE exercised coverage (subprocess child processes counted), and `fail_under` is raised to track that real number instead of the in-process undercount — with no new test flakiness.
baseline.summary: Subprocess coverage: measure CLI child-process execution so the floor tracks true coverage

## What

Add a CI job that **drift-proofs the README quickstart's command TEXT** by extracting the
CLI fenced command block from `README.md` and executing those exact lines end-to-end
(init → create → ready → claim → close) in a throwaway git repo against a clean install.
This is the core maintenance-burden reducer for the P0 defects: a wrong command *printed*
in the README (e.g. `session-log` missing its `append` verb, or a hard-coded id) then
exits non-zero and FAILS the build.

**Why extract-and-execute (not `probe-rebar.sh` alone, and not a static `--help` check).**
`scripts/probe-rebar.sh` already exercises the golden path, but it uses its own
internally-correct syntax — it can NOT catch wrong text printed in the README. A static
"parse the block and check each command name against `rebar --help`" would catch a bad
command *name* but NOT a wrong *subcommand/argument* (the actual P0 defect: `session-log`
is a real command, but `session-log "<entry>"` is a wrong invocation) nor a stale
hard-coded id, nor ordering/state errors. Only running the literal README lines against
the live engine catches all of these. So this ticket adds a small **extractor** that pulls
the fenced block(s) from the README and runs them; `probe-rebar.sh` is retained as the
COMPLEMENTARY broader end-to-end smoke (kept wired, or invoked alongside) so it does not
become stranded/stale.

- Add `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.sh` (or a small Python extractor) that parses the
  ```bash fenced quickstart block from `README.md` and executes those exact lines in an
  isolated temp `REBAR_ROOT` / throwaway git repo. No network, no shared state.
- Wire it as a gating job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, running against an INSTALLED
  rebar (clean `pipx`/`pip install`), so it also catches packaging/entry-point regressions.
- Keep `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` as the broader golden-path smoke (either invoked by the
  same job or left as-is) so its coverage is not lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A CI job extracts the README quickstart's CLI fenced block and runs those exact
      lines end-to-end; it FAILS the build if any of init/create/ready/claim/close changes
      exit code or the extracted commands error.
- [ ] The job runs against a CLEAN, non-editable install — the new `golden-path`
      job in `test.yml` AND `gerrit-verify.yaml` does `pip install .` (a built wheel,
      not editable) and runs `check_readme_quickstart.py` against it, so
      packaging/entry-point regressions (MANIFEST, package data, console-script
      registration) — which an editable install cannot catch — fail the build.
      Verify (prints nothing): `for f in .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; do grep -qF 'golden-path' "$f" && grep -qF 'pip install .' "$f" || echo "NO CLEAN-INSTALL JOB: $f"; done`
- [ ] The README *text* itself is what executes: a wrong command *printed* in the README
      — e.g. `session-log` missing its `append` verb, or a disconnected hard-coded id —
      is demonstrably caught (note the manual verification in a comment). Executability of
      an independent probe is NOT sufficient (closes epic finding G6/F4).
- [ ] The CI golden-path is the trimmed init->create->ready->claim->close subset the
      ticket explicitly permits — `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` (which runs
      `rebar init` explicitly and passes non-interactively) — NOT the full
      `probe-rebar.sh`. The broader probe was found to have PRE-EXISTING rot (relies
      on TTY-only auto-init + 10 stale assertions) that is out of this docs epic's
      scope; its fix-and-wire is tracked as discovered follow-up bug
      `slushy-commonlaw-drongo` (linked `discovered_from` this ticket). So T7 is
      addressed by tracking the rot honestly rather than wiring a red probe.

Depends on `a41f` (session-log fix) and `b55f` (quickstart repaired to a runnable
single-ticket block) — this gate extracts and runs the README quickstart, so it must land
AFTER those fix the text, or it would extract currently-broken commands and fail for the
wrong reason. (Dependency edges declared.)

Files: `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.sh` (new extractor), `scripts/probe-rebar.sh`
(retained/complementary), `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A ticket directory containing NO events — created by a write that never emitted its CREATE event — makes the plan-relation reducer error out, and that error surfaces as an INDETERMINATE verdict on plan reviews of OTHER, UNRELATED tickets. The blast radius is every ticket whose relation graph the snapshot walks, which in practice means an entire epic.

## Reproduced, then fixed, by removing the directory and nothing else

Running `rebar review-plan 5267-f026-0f2b-4c02`:

    verdict INDETERMINATE, exit 2, llm_ran: FALSE
    indeterminate[0] = {id: plan-relation-snapshot-error, reason: reducer-error,
                        canonical_id: None, reference: 0de5-6db1-8058-4e80}
    ERROR rebar.llm.plan_review: plan relation snapshot failed

`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` was an EMPTY DIRECTORY in `.tickets-tracker` — `ls -A` returned 0 entries, `rebar show` reported `has no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event`. A second one, `4ab3-411d-9736-4a41`, was in the same state.

CRITICALLY, 5267 DOES NOT REFERENCE 0de5. Its only dep is `relates_to 208f-6e90-1326-403a`; the broken directory was reached by walking the epic's relation graph. A grep across the whole store for `0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` returned ZERO references from any ticket — nothing points at it at all.

After removing the two empty directories and changing nothing else, the SAME command on the SAME tree returned `verdict: PASS`, exit 0, attestation certified at ff295b9cf87. That is the causal proof: one variable changed.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than sweeping

* It is NOT transient. An earlier agent on this epic hit the same signature and recorded it as
  "transient store churn from a half-written ticket, retried clean". It is not churn — it persists
  until someone removes the directory, and a retry only appears to work if the racing writer happens
  to complete in the interim.
* The error names the BROKEN ticket, not the one being reviewed, so the failure looks like a problem
  with an unrelated ticket. That is a strong wrong-direction signal for anyone debugging it.
* It is invisible to git. Git cannot track empty directories, so the artifact never appears in
  `git status`, never reaches the tickets branch, and cannot be spotted by inspecting the shared
  history — it exists only in a local clone.
* The LLM never runs (`llm_ran: false`), so the gate fails closed with no spend. That is correct
  behaviour, but it means the whole epic's claims and closes stall on a filesystem artifact.

## Approach (not yet decided)

The reducer should tolerate a ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event rather than failing the whole snapshot — most plausibly by skipping it with a warning naming the path, since a directory with no events carries no information that a relation snapshot needs. Consider also whether the writer can avoid creating the directory before it has an event to put in it, which would remove the artifact at source.

Both directions should be weighed; tolerating the artifact is the smaller, safer change and fixes existing broken clones, while fixing the writer prevents new ones and does nothing for clones already carrying one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event does not fail the plan-relation snapshot; the
      review proceeds and the artifact is reported as a warning naming the offending path.
- [x] A test constructs an event-less ticket directory and asserts `review-plan` on an UNRELATED
      ticket still reaches a verdict; it fails before the fix.
- [x] It is decided and recorded whether the writer should also stop creating the directory before it
      has an event to write, with the reasoning either way.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: An event-less ticket directory fails the plan-relation reducer, turning unrelated plan reviews INDETERMINATE

baseline.description:
Make the commit-trailer format + all CLI-served guides resolve for repo-less clients

## Context / Problem

Clients using the `rebar` CLI **without a rebar checkout** hit dead ends in CLI-served prose.
Today's commit `c2bfbe217` packaged the two author guides into `src/rebar/_guides/` so
`rebar explain plan|review` serves them from any install — but it left the guides' **internal
cross-references** as consumer-relative paths (`review-policy.md`, `review-kernel.md`,
`../CONTRIBUTING.md`, `plan-review-gate.md`, `plan-review-criteria-guide.md`,
`docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md`, `AGENTS.md`), which dangle for a consumer with no such tree —
the same class of dead-consumer-link bug that `62933ff62` fixed for plan-review deep-links
("client report §5"). Separately, the required `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit-trailer format
(`EXPECTED_FORMAT` in `verify_commit.py`) has **no** CLI-discoverable home at all: only
`rebar verify-commit-ticket --help` prints it, and nothing points there. The remediation was
not comprehensive.

## Approach

Two moves, both grounded in conventions already in this repo:

1. **Give the trailer a first-class CLI home.** Add a third packaged author guide,
   `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md`, registered as the `commit-trailer` topic in
   `AUTHOR_GUIDES` (`registry.py`) — served offline by `rebar explain commit-trailer` and the
   MCP `explain_guide` tool, exactly like `plan`/`review`. It quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim
   (drift-pinned by test) plus how-to-self-check prose (`rebar verify-commit-ticket`).

2. **Repoint every dangling reference in the packaged guides** so it resolves for a repo-less
   consumer, using the established two-way convention: sibling packaged guides →
   `rebar explain <topic>`; repo-only docs → the canonical hosted base
   `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/blob/main/…` (the same base `62933ff62`'s
   `_DEFAULT_DOCS_URL` and pyproject `[project.urls] Documentation` already use).

Then lock it with a guard test asserting no packaged `_guides/*.md` link target is a
consumer-relative path (only `https://`, intra-doc `#anchor`, or `rebar explain` are allowed) —
so the remediation stays comprehensive. Rejected: a bespoke `rebar trailer-format` subcommand
(`explain` is already the on-ramp for `plan`/`review`; a third topic needs no new wiring);
rejected shipping the whole `docs/` tree in the wheel (heavy; hosted URLs already resolve).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_guides/commit-ticket-trailer.md` — NEW packaged guide; quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT`
  verbatim + `rebar verify-commit-ticket` self-check prose; links only via `https://`/`rebar explain`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `"commit-trailer"` → the new file in `AUTHOR_GUIDES`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — the MCP `explain_criterion` tool docstring hardcodes the guide
  list (`plan`/`review`); add `commit-trailer` so MCP clients discover it (the tool dispatch at
  L63 already reads `AUTHOR_GUIDES` dynamically — only the human-facing docstring lags).
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — repoint L5 review-policy/review-kernel + L6/L39
  CONTRIBUTING to hosted URLs; L8 sibling → `rebar explain plan`; L35 trailer →
  `rebar explain commit-trailer` + `rebar verify-commit-ticket --help`.
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` — repoint L6 criteria-guide + L7
  plan-review-gate to hosted URLs; L8 sibling → `rebar explain review`.
- `tests/unit/test_verify_commit_ticket.py` — drift assertion (packaged guide quotes
  `EXPECTED_FORMAT`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py` — `rebar explain commit-trailer` returns the format;
  unknown-guide error lists it; LINK-RESOLUTION guard test (below); a guard asserting every
  `AUTHOR_GUIDES` key is named in the MCP `explain_criterion` docstring (so the MCP guide list
  can't silently drift from the registry again).
- `tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py` — make the existing `test_wheel_ships_author_guides` iterate
  `AUTHOR_GUIDES` (not a hardcoded pair) so the new guide — and any future one — is packaging-
  guarded automatically.
- `AGENTS.md` — one-line pointer to `rebar explain commit-trailer` in the trailer bullet.
- `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` — note the CLI discovery paths.

## Testing

- Happy: `registry.explain_guide("commit-trailer")` and CLI `rebar explain commit-trailer` both
  return text containing `EXPECTED_FORMAT` (exit 0).
- Edge: unknown guide name raises `ExplainError("unknown-id", …)` whose message now lists
  `commit-trailer`.
- Drift: the packaged guide contains `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim.
- Link-resolution guard (the core regression-proofing): a single test enumerates ALL
  in-command help prose a repo-less client can see — every registered `AUTHOR_GUIDES` guide
  body AND every `explain_criterion(<id>)` rendering — extracts every markdown link `](target)`,
  and asserts each target RESOLVES for a non-rebar client. The one canonical allow-list, used
  everywhere: a target is OK iff it starts with `https://`, `http://`, `#` (intra-doc anchor),
  or `mailto:`. Any consumer-relative path (`](*.md)`, `](docs/…)`, `](../…)`) FAILS. A second
  axis scans the packaged guide bodies (only) for bare parenthetical/inline repo paths
  (`docs/…`, `../…`) not part of a hosted `…/blob/main/…` URL — catching non-hyperlink dead
  references the `](…)` regex misses. It also validates every `rebar explain <topic>` mentioned
  in that prose names a real registered guide/criterion, so the reachable-pointer claim can't
  rot. Driven by the registries (not a hardcoded file list) so new guides/criteria are covered
  automatically.
- Full `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar explain commit-trailer` exits 0 and prints the canonical trailer format (run it;
      CLI unit test asserts `EXPECTED_FORMAT` in stdout).
- [ ] `commit-trailer` is listed among known guides in `rebar explain` help and the
      `unknown-id` error (unit test).
- [ ] The packaged `commit-ticket-trailer.md` quotes `EXPECTED_FORMAT` verbatim (drift test).
- [ ] The link-resolution guard passes: across every `AUTHOR_GUIDES` guide body and every
      `explain_criterion(<id>)` rendering, no markdown link target is consumer-relative (allowed
      set is exactly `https://`/`http://`/`#anchor`/`mailto:`), no packaged guide has a bare
      `docs/…`/`../…` path, and every `rebar explain <topic>` cited names a real registered
      guide/criterion (test passes; verified by grep too).
- [ ] `rebar explain review` and `rebar explain plan` no longer reference repo-relative files;
      sibling guides read as `rebar explain <topic>`, repo docs as `https://github.com/navapbc/…`
      — confirmed by the link-resolution guard passing (a manual read may spot-check readability).
- [ ] `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` names `rebar explain commit-trailer` and
      `rebar verify-commit-ticket` as CLI discovery paths (grep the file).
- [ ] The MCP `explain_criterion` tool docstring names `commit-trailer`, and a guard test
      asserts every `AUTHOR_GUIDES` key appears in that docstring (test passes).
- [ ] AGENTS.md's trailer bullet names `rebar explain commit-trailer` (grep).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` all pass (run them).
baseline.summary: Make commit-trailer format + CLI-served guides resolve for repo-less clients

# DC's comment ceiling is admin-configurable and rebar hardcodes the default

## The defect

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` `sanitize_comment` truncates comment bodies at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), a compile-time constant. On Jira Data Center that ceiling is the default of the admin-settable property `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose documented range is `0` (unlimited) to `2147483647`.

So on an instance where an administrator has RAISED the limit or set it to `0`, rebar truncates comments that Jira would have accepted in full. **That is data loss, and it is silent to the author of the comment** — the operator sees a truncation warning (`jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148`), which is why this is low-severity rather than invisible, but the text is still gone from the remote and the local/remote bodies then differ permanently.

This is NOT the "32767 is the wrong number" defect that was originally suspected and is now refuted (see below). It is narrower: the number is right for a STOCK instance and wrong for a CONFIGURED one.

## Established provenance (so nobody re-litigates the number)

`jira.text.field.character.limit`, from Jira's own `jpm.xml`:

    description: "The maximum number of characters to be entered for a single field.
                  Affects Description, Environment, Comments and Text custom fields.
                  0 means unlimited."
    default-value: 32767

Corroborated by JRASERVER-28519 (Resolved/Fixed, fix versions 6.4.1 / 7.0.0): "starting with JIRA 7.0 and Cloud, `jira.text.field.character.limit` will be set to 32767 by default." The DC admin page "Configuring advanced settings" confirms the property, its field scope, `0` = unlimited and the 2147483647 maximum, but does NOT state the default.

Comments and text custom fields share ONE property and therefore one number, by design — so binding DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is structurally faithful to DC, and must not be "fixed" by inventing a separate comment number.

Evidence the ceiling bites people in practice: JRASERVER-64351 has 86 votes from users hitting it, which is also the population most likely to have raised the limit.

## Why the fix is not simply "read the limit"

`/rest/api/2/application-properties` plausibly exposes the key, but **whether it is readable by a non-admin PAT is NOT established and must be tested, not assumed.** rebar authenticates as an ordinary user on DC. If the property is admin-only, discovery is unavailable and the remedy is configuration only.

## Proposed remediation, cheapest first

1. Make the DC comment ceiling CONFIGURABLE, defaulting to 32767. This alone closes the data-loss
   window for any operator who knows their instance's setting.
2. OPTIONALLY probe `application-properties` at connect time and log a warning when the instance's
   value disagrees with the configured one. Gate this on actually confirming the endpoint is readable
   by rebar's credential.
3. Do NOT change the default. It is correct for stock Jira >= 7.0 and matches every independent
   implementation surveyed (carrier-io/dusty annotates its own 32767 as "the
   jira.text.field.character.limit default value").

No surveyed OSS integration queries the live limit — all hardcode — so (1) brings rebar to parity with the field and (2) would make it more correct than the field.

## Two latent traps worth fixing in the same area (not themselves data loss today)

* The constant is named `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` and the comment at `jira_family/rich_text.py:56-60`
  attributes the number to Cloud comment limits, which REVERSES the actual causality. Renaming it
  and citing the property would stop the code asserting a false provenance.
* `sanitize_comment` reuses `fit_outbound`, the DESCRIPTION fitter. Harmless today (plain character
  truncation) but Cloud shows why the coupling is dangerous: Cloud's description fitter is
  ADF-SIZE-based (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000 ADF chars, fitted empirically because
  `text_to_adf` inflates — a 32767-char description was observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars)
  and would be catastrophically wrong applied to comments. Any future change to the DC description
  fitter silently retargets comments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the DC comment ceiling is settable by configuration, defaulting to 32767, with the default's
      provenance (`jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519) cited at the binding
- [x] a comment longer than the configured ceiling but shorter than a raised one is NOT truncated
      when the ceiling is configured upward, proven by a RED-first unit test
- [x] the readability of `/rest/api/2/application-properties` by rebar's non-admin PAT is RECORDED
      WITH ITS EVIDENTIARY STATUS LABELLED, discovery is dropped, and that is stated at the binding.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required an EMPIRICAL determination and the answer obtained is
      DOCUMENTARY** (Atlassian's permission documentation for the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource,
      where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed). No 403 was captured, because the
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and never became usable on the
      arm64 host in three measured attempts. The amendment is justified on two grounds recorded in
      full in this ticket's AC-verification comment: (1) the remedy is INDEPENDENT of the answer — a
      readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery layer ON TOP of the config key, never
      a replacement, so the outstanding measurement cannot invalidate what landed; (2) the
      measurement is DEFERRED, not dropped — it is runnable on the amd64 `jira-dc-harness` CI job and
      is filed as [rebar:275e-81a4-f11a-4b5b] (linked `discovered_from` here), which writes its
      outcome back onto this ticket
- [x] `sanitize_comment` no longer depends on the description fitter, so a change to description
      fitting cannot retarget comments
- [x] mutation-checked: reverting the configurability turns the new test red for the right reason
baseline.summary: DC comment ceiling is admin-configurable; rebar hardcodes the default

baseline.description:
## Why
On failure the bot must NEVER land a partial/inconsistent stack and NEVER evict a change from within a stack (that would orphan its descendants). The whole stack returns to its owning agent to remediate — this is the one Goal-2 exception (agent pulled in only when code must change).

## What
Handle the two failure modes in the auto-lander loop: CI-fail (post-rebase `Verified -1`) and rebase-conflict (`POST /rebase` `409`). The recorded outcome is the single source of truth consumed by the agent contract.

## Dependencies
Depends on **S2** (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`, 0ee8-08de-bf0f-45ec) — the core loop: this story adds the failure/edge branches to S2's loop and consumes its `wipChain` + stack-selection, so the happy-path loop must exist first.

## Outcome record
**Gerrit is the source of truth; the persisted store is a reconstruct-from-Gerrit cache, not an authoritative record.** The bot persists ONLY `needs_rebase` markers in the auto-lander state dir (project-infra state, NOT a rebar event), keyed by `change_id + patchset_SHA` and **self-invalidating**: a marker whose SHA no longer matches the change's current patchset in Gerrit is IGNORED (a new patchset means the rebase was resolved). `merged` / `ci_failed` / `review_failed` are NOT persisted — they are derived LIVE from Gerrit at read time (S4 already does this). Marker shape: `{change_id, patchset_SHA, stack_id, change_ids[], failing_change_id?, tested_sha, recorded_at, acknowledged}`. A re-run overwrites the prior marker for the same `change_id + patchset_SHA`. `stack_id` = the Gerrit topic the auto-lander assigns to a stack at selection time (falling back to the tip change-id for a single-change stack); it is the shared key across S2/S3/S4/S9. `acknowledged`: the writer sets `acknowledged=false` when recording and `true` after `Autosubmit`-removal for every change in the stack completes; on restart, any `acknowledged=false` marker re-drives the removal to completion (idempotent). A rolling per-transition **log line** is kept for debugging even though the authoritative record is single-slot. S4 (land command) and S9 (batch failure) consume this cache + live Gerrit state as the outcome.

## Scope
Failure/edge paths of the core-loop service; the recorded outcome feeds the agent contract story.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **CI-flake auto-recheck (before hand-back):** on a post-rebase `Verified -1`, do a **bounded auto-`recheck`** — 1 retry on the SAME patchset — BEFORE recording `ci_failed` and stripping `Autosubmit`; only hand the stack back if it fails again. (The `gerrit-verify` workflow casts a single **undifferentiated** `Verified -1` for all failure modes — there is NO machine-readable infra-vs-test signal in the vote/label/REST API to branch on — so the auto-`recheck` applies to ANY post-rebase `-1`; the single bounded retry is itself what absorbs a transient flake, and a real test-failure that reproduces on the recheck correctly hands back.) **Recheck trigger + state machine (concrete):** the bot triggers CI re-execution by **posting the exact Gerrit comment `recheck`** — which the gerrit-to-platform ChatOps maps to the `verify` workflow (`gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`: `recheck = verify`), re-running `gerrit-verify.yaml` (the bot posts comments as its own Gerrit user; no extra grant needed). It then enters a **`rechecking` in-flight sub-state** (an S3-owned flag on the `wipChain`, NOT a new S2 phase) and reads the vote sequence correctly: `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `clear-vote` job first **resets `Verified→0`** at run start (GerriScary-safe) — the bot MUST treat this transient `0` as *recheck-running*, NOT as "no result," and MUST NOT re-post `recheck`; it then waits for the terminal vote — `+1` → clear the flag and proceed to submit; `-1` → record `ci_failed` and hand back. The recheck is bounded to **one** post per patchset (the flag prevents a re-post loop). A single flake must not poison an otherwise-green stack (the epic's "zero babysitting" goal).
- [ ] CI-fail: after the auto-recheck still shows `Verified -1`, record a `ci_failed` outcome (derived live from Gerrit), then remove `Autosubmit` from **all changes in the affected stack** (not just the failing change), and stop driving the stack; post NO bot comment (the native `-1` + run logs are the signal — no redundant channel).
- [ ] **Persisted state is a reconstruct-from-Gerrit cache:** persist ONLY `needs_rebase` markers keyed by `change_id + patchset_SHA`; a persisted marker is IGNORED if its patchset SHA no longer matches the change's current patchset in Gerrit. `merged`/`ci_failed`/`review_failed` are NEVER persisted — they are derived live from Gerrit at read time. Keep a rolling per-transition log line for debugging.
- [ ] Rebase-conflict: on `POST /rebase` `409`, record a `needs_rebase` outcome event-driven on that change/stack (NOT a continuously-maintained up-to-date vote — that would churn O(open) per landing), then remove `Autosubmit` from all changes in the stack.
- [ ] **Stack → owner:** the owning agent is the stack's uploader/owner (`owner._account_id` on the tip change); "hand back" = record ONE outcome for the stack + remove `Autosubmit` from every change in it. Never partial-land; never evict a change from within a stack.
- [ ] Never `allow_conflicts` — a `409` from `POST /rebase` routes to the `needs_rebase` path; no conflict-marker patchset is ever created or submitted.
- [ ] **Idempotent ordering under retries/restart:** the outcome is recorded **before** `Autosubmit` removal; label-removal treats `404`/`409` as a no-op; the `stack_id` upsert key makes re-runs overwrite rather than duplicate; on restart an unacknowledged record re-drives the label removal to completion.
baseline.summary: S3 Failure handling & stack-atomic hand-back (409 / CI-fail; never partial-land)

# Sweep: reconciler (_engine/rebar_reconciler/) — LATE, test-heavy (HTTP-classification sensitive)

The highest-behavior-change-risk batch — do it LAST. Many broad-excepts feed exception-type-dependent
bodies (`is_not_found(exc)`, `http_status(exc)`, `getattr(exc, "status_code", ...)` at
`apply_outbound.py:416,441`, `batch_dispatch.py:77,307`). Narrowing these changes which exceptions reach
the body and thus HTTP 404/error classification — so add characterization tests FIRST, then remediate.

## What
- Add characterization tests around `is_not_found`/`http_status` error classification before touching the
  catches (the `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py` helpers already exist).
- Bring broad-excepts in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` to the observability floor. Body-inspecting
  catches stay broad-but-logged unless a narrow is proven safe by a test.
- Rollback/cleanup swallows (e.g. `batch_dispatch.py` "rollback must not mask original error";
  `reconcile.py:1155` `except BaseException ... raise`) stay intentionally broad with a justification —
  do not narrow.
- Migrate stderr-diagnostic prints (`reconcile.py`, `__main__.py`, etc.) to the named logger; keep any
  acli/jira data output semantics intact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Characterization tests cover `is_not_found`/`http_status` classification before remediation.
- [ ] Broad-excepts in `_engine/rebar_reconciler/` meet the observability floor; body-inspecting ones are
      kept-broad-and-logged or narrowed only with a passing test.
- [ ] Rollback/cleanup swallows remain broad with a one-line justification; none silently masks an error.
- [ ] This package removed from the allowlist; `make lint` + full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Sweep: reconciler (_engine/rebar_reconciler) — LATE, test-heavy (HTTP-classification sensitive)

## Summary

The `optionality` GitHub Actions workflow fails on every push to `main` (job
"clean core wheel (no extras → heavy deps absent)"). `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`
imports `httpx` and `pydantic_ai.exceptions` at **module scope**, so importing
the module in a no-extras (core-only) install raises
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_ai'` — breaking the lean-runtime
optionality contract (extras may only ADD deps; core must import with none).

It reached `main` because the Gerrit `Verified` gate (gerrit-verify.yaml) installs
`.[dev]` -> `[agents]` (heavy stack present), so the module-scope import succeeds
there; and the static AST guard that SHOULD catch it
(`tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py::test_no_core_module_imports_heavy_stack_at_module_scope`,
which DOES run inside `make test` = the Verified suite) has a stale `_HEAVY` list
from the LangChain era — it is missing `pydantic_ai` and `httpx`, the actual
runtime heavy deps after the pydantic-ai cutover.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Build the core wheel with no extras, install into a clean venv
   (`python -m build --wheel && pip install dist/*.whl`).
2. `python -c "import rebar.llm.failure"`.

- Expected: import succeeds (core stays lean; heavy imports are lazy).
- Actual: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_ai'` at
  `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:27`; optionality clean-core-wheel job reports
  `8 failed, 11 passed`.

## Root Cause

- `failure.py` module-scope `import httpx` + `from pydantic_ai.exceptions import (...)`.
- `_HEAVY` in `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` omits `pydantic_ai`/`httpx`,
  so the in-Verified static guard never flagged the offender.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` performs NO module-scope import of `httpx` or
      `pydantic_ai`; those imports are lazy (function-local), matching the
      established pattern in `runner.py`. Type annotations remain valid under
      `from __future__ import annotations`.
- [ ] `classify_llm_failure(...)` still classifies correctly WITH the agents
      extra present, and degrades safely (returns NEEDS_INVESTIGATION, never
      raises ModuleNotFoundError) when the heavy stack is ABSENT.
- [ ] `_HEAVY` in `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` includes `pydantic_ai`
      and `httpx`, so the static module-scope guard catches this regression class.
- [ ] The AST guard fails on the unfixed code (RED) and passes after the fix (GREEN).
- [ ] The optionality workflow clean-core-wheel job passes (module imports under
      a no-extras install).
- [ ] Decision recorded on the Gerrit Verified path: the module-scope-heavy-import
      guard is confirmed to run inside the Verified suite via the AST test; the
      residual clean-wheel/packaging jobs are justified as post-merge (or wired in).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass locally.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar show <id>` renders only the edges STORED ON THAT TICKET'S RECORD. For a `blocks` relation that is the OUTGOING side. So a ticket that is blocked BY something shows NOTHING about it, and the reader has to already know which other ticket to inspect in order to discover the blocker.

MEASURED on the live store:

    rebar show eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a  ->  deps [('blocks', '8625-7bea-67db-4cdc')]
    rebar show 0d76-ebbf-ee3a-48ac  ->  deps [('blocks', 'eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a')]

The real chain is `0d76 --blocks--> eb6e --blocks--> 8625`. But reading eb6e alone, the only visible edge points DOWNSTREAM, and eb6e looks unblocked.

## The failure this actually caused, today

An agent inspected eb6e, saw only the outgoing edge, and concluded "nothing blocks eb6e — its only dep is outgoing." On that basis it told the operator the ticket could be planned in parallel, and dispatched a subagent to decompose and plan-review it. The subagent could never have succeeded: per AGENTS.md, `review-plan` on a ticket "open but still blocked by an unclosed dependency" FAST-FAILS with no LLM (unsigned INDETERMINATE, exit 2), and `claim` refuses too. The dispatch was caught and stood down before it spent anything, but only because a human asked a follow-up question about dependency edges.

The reasoning error was reading one side of a bidirectional relation and concluding from it. The tool made that the DEFAULT reading: the information needed to answer "is this ticket blocked?" is definitionally not on the ticket you are looking at.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than learning around

* "Is this blocked?" is one of the most common questions asked of `rebar show`, and it is the one
  question the current output cannot answer.
* It fails toward FALSE CONFIDENCE. The reader does not see an empty or ambiguous field; they see a
  populated `deps` list that looks complete, and reasonably conclude the picture is whole.
* `ready` and `next-batch` know the truth — they correctly withhold a blocked ticket — so the data is
  available; it is only the per-ticket view that omits it. That inconsistency between two tools in the
  same CLI is itself a trap: an agent that cross-checks `show` against `ready` gets contradictory
  impressions and has no obvious reason to trust `ready`.
* Agents are the primary consumers of `rebar show` in this workflow, and they cannot ask a colleague.

## Approach

Render INCOMING edges alongside outgoing ones in the ticket view, clearly labelled by direction — e.g. a `blocked_by` list derived from the reverse index, so "is this blocked?" is answerable from a single `rebar show`. Whether that is a new field, a decorated `deps` list, or a derived summary is a design call; the requirement is that the blocked-ness of a ticket is visible on the ticket.

Consider whether the same asymmetry affects other relations rendered in `deps` (parent/child are already handled separately via `parent_id`, but `discovered_from`, `duplicates` and `relates_to` have the same one-sided storage), and whether the fix should be general rather than special-cased to `blocks`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar show <id>` on a ticket blocked by an unclosed dependency makes that blocker visible without
      the reader needing to inspect the blocking ticket.
- [ ] A test constructs `A --blocks--> B` and asserts the blocker is discoverable from `show B`, failing
      before the fix.
- [ ] The direction of every rendered relation is unambiguous — a reader can tell "blocks" from
      "blocked by" without knowing which record the edge is stored on.
- [ ] It is decided and recorded whether the fix generalises to the other one-sided relations
      (`discovered_from`, `duplicates`, `relates_to`) or is scoped to `blocks`, with the reasoning.
- [ ] `rebar show` and `ready`/`next-batch` cannot disagree about whether a ticket is blocked; a test
      pins the two against the same fixture.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: rebar show renders only outgoing edges, so blocked-by is invisible on the blocked ticket
