# Pin the release supply chain to immutable references

Make every executable the release depends on identifiable by an immutable reference: full-SHA action pins, a hash-locked build environment, an exact-versioned + digest-verified MCP publisher, and non-persisted checkout credentials. (Readiness Finding 4 — verified VALID against `release.yml` lines 31/32/43/60/65/85/124/129 and `pyproject.toml:1-3`.)

## Why

Two release runs of the same rebar SHA can execute different build/upload/publish code today. `release.yml` references first-party actions by moving major-version tags (`actions/checkout@v7` at :31/:124, `actions/setup-python@v6` at :32, `actions/upload-artifact@v7` at :43, `actions/download-artifact@v8` at :60/:85); installs build tools with unrestricted upgrades (`pip install --upgrade build` :37, `--upgrade twine` :41); publishes via the branch-like `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` (:65); declares the build backend as bare `hatchling` (`pyproject.toml:1-3`); and in the `mcp_registry` job downloads its publisher from a mutable `releases/latest` URL and executes it **without a digest/signature check** (:129) in a job that holds `id-token: write` (used for GitHub OIDC login + registry publication). None of the checkouts set `persist-credentials: false`, so the token persists in local git config by default. The repo SHA-pins **some** third-party actions in `gerrit-verify.yaml` (its header claims comprehensive pinning, but e.g. `gerrit-verify.yaml:75` still has an unpinned `actions/setup-python@v6`), so the generic action-security checks are not yet enforced on `release.yml`. Rather than hand-roll regex checks, this story adopts the **proven, maintained tools** — `zizmor` (GitHub-Actions security auditor: unpinned actions, credential persistence, over-broad/dangerous permissions incl. OIDC) and `actionlint` — run under `make lint` **scoped to `release.yml`**, plus a thin project-specific test for the rebar-only invariants zizmor doesn't know about. (Fixing `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s own unpinned `setup-python` and repo-wide zizmor adoption are a separate follow-up; path-scoping the invocation to `release.yml` keeps this story bounded and avoids breaking `make lint` on out-of-scope pre-existing findings.)

## What

Adopt the uv / pip pinning pattern (uv: full-SHA action pins, `persist-credentials: false`, a pinned release tool with a verified SHA-256; pip: SHA-pinned actions + a hash-locked build environment installed with `--require-hashes --no-deps`):

- Replace each action tag with a full commit SHA, keeping the human-readable
  version in a trailing comment.
- Set `persist-credentials: false` on every release checkout unless a later git
  operation demonstrably needs the persisted credential.
- **Enforce the generic action-security checks with `zizmor` + `actionlint` (proven
  tools, not hand-rolled).** Add `zizmor` (itself version+hash-pinned in the release
  lock) and `actionlint` to `make lint`, **invoked with `release.yml` as an explicit
  path argument** (not repo-wide), so they run under the Gerrit `Verified` gate.
  `zizmor` enforces full-SHA pinning of `uses:`, `persist-credentials: false`, and
  over-broad/dangerous permissions (including OIDC) on `release.yml`. **One annotated
  exception:** `mcp_registry`'s `id-token: write` is consumed by the opaque shell command
  `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`, which zizmor cannot introspect, so it false-positives
  as excessive — suppressed with a single scoped
  `# zizmor:ignore[excessive-permissions] -- …` on that job's `permissions:` block (the
  only suppression allowed; the test asserts it verbatim and forbids any other). A thin
  `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` (also under `make test`) then asserts
  only the **rebar-specific** invariants `zizmor` cannot know: the `--no-isolation`
  build flag, the `mcp_verify`(no `id-token`)/`mcp_registry`(has it) split, the
  `chmod +x mcp-publisher` step, the evidence-fragment wiring, and the
  `docs/releasing.md` "Pinning" section substrings.
- Create a reviewed release lock/constraints file covering `build`, Hatchling,
  Twine, any artifact-validation tools, and their transitive deps, generated and
  maintained with an established tool — **`pip-compile --generate-hashes` (pip-tools)**
  (or `uv pip compile --generate-hashes`) — checked into the repo.
- **Hatchling enforcement — decision.** pip's default `python -m build` resolves the
  `[build-system]` requires in a *fresh isolated env*, so the lock only governs
  Hatchling's version if the build uses the pre-installed locked env. **This story
  uses `--no-isolation`**: pre-install the hash-locked env (including Hatchling)
  with `pip install --require-hashes -r .github/release-requirements.txt`, then `python -m build
  --no-isolation`. This keeps enforcement entirely in the workflow and avoids
  editing `pyproject.toml` `[build-system]`. **Close the ambient-package hole with a
  parsed comparison (not a raw diff).** Because `ubuntu-latest` ships
  `pip`/`setuptools`/`wheel`/`packaging` and the `--no-isolation` build runs in the
  ambient env, build in a **fresh venv** containing only the hash-locked packages,
  then run a small guard script (`scripts/check_build_env_locked.py`) that: parses the
  installed set from `pip freeze` (lowercased `name`→`version`), parses the expected
  `name==version` entries from `.github/release-requirements.txt` (skipping `--hash`
  and comment lines — the two files are NOT raw-diff-comparable), and **fails if any
  installed package is absent from the lock or version-mismatched**, modulo a small
  documented base allowlist (`pip`, `setuptools`, `wheel`). This is a deterministic
  parsed check, not a text diff of the two file formats. The `test_release_workflow_pins.py` test (run by `make test`) fails if
  `--no-isolation` is absent (so no free-resolution path can silently return).
- **MCP publisher — download → verify → execute (never stream into tar).** Replace
  the `releases/latest` URL with an exact version, and split the current
  `curl … | tar xz` one-liner into three ordered steps so an unverified archive is
  never extracted or executed:
  1. `curl -fsSL "<exact-version-url>" -o mcp-publisher.tar.gz`
  2. `echo "<pinned-sha256>  mcp-publisher.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c --strict`
  3. `tar xzf mcp-publisher.tar.gz mcp-publisher`
  Prefer an upstream `checksums.txt` if `modelcontextprotocol/registry` ships one;
  otherwise hard-code the SHA-256 computed at pin time with a rationale comment.
  **Arch note:** the current download URL is built from `uname -s`/`uname -m`, so the
  `<url, sha256>` pair is arch-specific. `release.yml` runs on `ubuntu-latest`
  (linux/amd64), so pin the `linux_amd64` URL + its SHA-256 as a single deliberate
  pair (documented, with a revisit note if the runner arch changes); store one pair
  per supported OS/arch tuple if the matrix ever expands.
  **Security contract — structural job split (not step ordering).** This follows
  GitHub's own *Security hardening for GitHub Actions* guidance (least-privilege
  permissions; isolate privileged operations into their own job) and the PyPA
  Trusted-Publishing model of minimizing what runs under the OIDC token. In GitHub
  Actions `id-token: write` is a *job-level* permission: the OIDC token endpoint
  (`$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`) is reachable from the job's **first** step, so
  step ordering within one job does NOT prevent a compromised archive from minting a
  token during the download step. Enforce co-residency structurally by **splitting
  the job in two**: `mcp_verify` (no `id-token: write`; runs curl download +
  `sha256sum -c` and uploads the verified binary as an artifact / sets a `verified`
  output) and `mcp_registry` (`needs: mcp_verify`; holds `id-token: write`; consumes
  the already-verified artifact and runs `mcp-publisher login`/`publish`). Fail on an
  unexpected filename/size/digest/version. So the OIDC-privileged job never downloads
  or holds an unverified binary. **Restore the executable bit after the handoff:**
  `actions/upload-artifact` (v3+) does not preserve POSIX permissions, so
  `mcp_registry` must `chmod +x mcp-publisher` after `download-artifact` or the
  `./mcp-publisher login` call fails "Permission denied" at runtime.
- Print and retain release evidence. GitHub Actions artifacts are **job-scoped** and
  cannot be appended to across jobs, so each job uploads its **own distinctly-named**
  fragment (`evidence-shapin`, `evidence-build`, `evidence-mcp`; Finding 3 later adds
  `evidence-artifacts` for the wheel/sdist sums), and a final aggregation step downloads all fragments and concatenates them into one
  `release-evidence.txt` — recording every action SHA, the Python build-tool versions,
  the MCP publisher version + verified digest, and the wheel/sdist digests.
- Update pins through reviewed dependency-update changes, not implicit resolution
  during a production release.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — SHA-pin all `uses:`; `persist-credentials:
  false`; `--no-isolation` hash-locked build install; split the MCP publisher
  into an unprivileged `mcp_verify` job + an OIDC-privileged `mcp_registry` job that
  consumes the verified artifact (coordinate with Findings 1 and 3, which also edit
  this file).
- `.github/release-requirements.txt` (new, the hash-locked constraints file) compiled
  from `.github/release-requirements.in` via
  `pip-compile --generate-hashes --output-file=.github/release-requirements.txt .github/release-requirements.in`.
- `scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` (new) — the parsed installed-vs-lock guard
  (lowercased `name==version` comparison, base allowlist), with a unit test over a
  fixture lock+freeze pair.
- `scripts/verify_mcp_publisher_pin.py` (new) + a `make verify-mcp-pin` target — parses the
  pinned mcp-publisher URL + embedded SHA-256 out of `release.yml`, downloads the URL,
  computes its SHA-256, and asserts equality (non-zero on mismatch). The implementer runs it
  once in-session to confirm the embedded hash is self-consistent with the pinned URL and
  records the passing output on the ticket (the `[operator-attested]` AC above); its
  *existence + wiring* is asserted by `test_release_workflow_pins.py`.
- `Makefile` + `pyproject.toml [dev]` — add `zizmor` and `actionlint` to `make lint`,
  **invoked scoped to `release.yml` specifically** (`zizmor .github/workflows/release.yml`
  and `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml`), NOT repo-wide — otherwise they would
  flag pre-existing out-of-scope issues in other workflows (e.g. `gerrit-verify.yaml:75`'s
  unpinned `setup-python@v6`) and break the very Gerrit `Verified` gate that runs
  `make lint`. (Repo-wide `zizmor`/`actionlint` adoption is a separate follow-up
  ticket.) **Concrete install paths** (the gate installs via `pip install -e '.[dev]'`,
  so an unfound tool would fail `command not found`): `zizmor` is pip-installable — pin
  it in `pyproject.toml [dev]` (and hash-pin it in the release lock for the release-lint
  usage); `actionlint` is a Go binary — install it via a **pinned-version GitHub release
  download + SHA-256 verification** in a `Makefile` prerequisite (dogfooding the same
  digest-verify discipline this story establishes for `mcp-publisher`). Scoped to
  `release.yml`, `zizmor` enforces the **generic** checks:
  full-SHA pinning of every `uses:`, `persist-credentials: false`, and
  over-broad/dangerous permissions (incl. OIDC). A standalone PR-triggered GitHub
  workflow would NOT run pre-merge in this repo's Gerrit flow, which is why the lint
  runs under `make lint`, not a `pull_request` trigger.
- `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` (new) — a thin test under `make test`
  for only the **rebar-specific** invariants `zizmor` can't know, parsing
  `release.yml` + `docs/releasing.md`: (c) the build invocation includes
  `--no-isolation`; (d) the `docs/releasing.md` "Pinning" section contains the three
  required substrings (see the docs AC); (e) the job-permission split —
  `mcp_verify` declares no `id-token: write`, `mcp_registry` does (fail if
  `mcp_verify` gains it); (f) the release-evidence wiring — the three fragment names
  this story delivers (`evidence-shapin|evidence-build|evidence-mcp`) appear in
  `release.yml` and a consolidation job downloads + concatenates them
  (`evidence-artifacts` is asserted by Finding 3's story after it lands); (g) a
  `chmod +x mcp-publisher` step is present in the `mcp_registry` job; (h) the
  ambient-package guard step (`scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` — a parsed
  name→version comparison, NOT a raw text diff) is present.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_publisher_pin.py` (new) — run by `make test`; writes a test
  copy of the pinned archive, corrupts one byte, runs the `mcp_verify` `sha256sum -c`
  logic, and asserts a non-zero exit.
- `pyproject.toml` — **no change** to `[build-system]` requires: with the chosen
  `--no-isolation` strategy the Hatchling version is governed by the
  pre-installed hash-locked env, not by `pyproject.toml` (this is deliberate; if the
  isolated-build path were kept instead, a `[build-system]` pin would be required —
  but it is not kept).
- `docs/releasing.md` — document the pinning policy and the pin-update process.
  **Section ownership:** this story owns the "Pinning" section only (Finding 1 owns
  "Release-source authorization", Finding 3 owns "Build-once"), avoiding overlap
  across the three concurrent release stories.
- Out of scope: pinning non-release workflows already SHA-pinned; full reproducible
  builds (covered adjacent to Finding 3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `uses:` in `release.yml` references a full 40-char commit SHA with a
  trailing version comment — enforced by `zizmor` (via `make lint`), which fails on
  any unpinned `uses:`.
- [ ] Every release checkout sets `persist-credentials: false` — enforced by `zizmor`
  (via `make lint`), which flags credential persistence.
- [ ] `zizmor` + `actionlint` run under `make lint` **scoped to `release.yml`** (explicit
  path argument, not repo-wide — so pre-existing out-of-scope findings like
  `gerrit-verify.yaml:75` don't break the gate), with concrete install paths: `zizmor`
  pinned in `pyproject.toml [dev]` (+ hash-pinned in the release lock) and `actionlint`
  installed via a pinned-version release download with SHA-256 verification in a
  `Makefile` prerequisite; `make lint` finds both in CI (no `command not found`).
  `zizmor` reports **no findings on `release.yml` except a single annotated suppression**
  for `mcp_registry`'s `id-token: write` (SHA-pins, persist-credentials, and all other
  over-broad/OIDC permissions clean). The one suppression is unavoidable and legitimate:
  `mcp_registry` genuinely needs `id-token: write` for `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`,
  but because that is an **opaque shell command** (not a `uses:` step zizmor can
  introspect), zizmor's `excessive-permissions` audit cannot see the token being consumed
  and reports a false positive. It is suppressed with an inline
  `# zizmor:ignore[excessive-permissions] -- id-token: write is consumed by
  mcp-publisher login github-oidc (runtime OIDC token request; zizmor cannot introspect
  shell commands)` on the `mcp_registry` `permissions:` block. `test_release_workflow_pins.py`
  asserts this exact suppression comment is present (so it cannot be silently broadened to
  suppress other findings), and that no OTHER `zizmor:ignore` appears in `release.yml`.
- [ ] Release build tools (`build`, Hatchling, Twine, validation tools) install from
  `.github/release-requirements.txt` (generated by `pip-compile --generate-hashes
  --output-file=.github/release-requirements.txt .github/release-requirements.in`)
  with `--require-hashes` — the install itself is the verification: `pip install
  --require-hashes --no-deps -r .github/release-requirements.txt` re-hashes every artifact against the lock and
  **fails the build** if any package was replaced or its hash doesn't match (a
  `--dry-run` would not, since pip skips digest-checking for already-satisfied
  packages). The install step emits `pip list --format=freeze > tool-versions.txt`
  into the release evidence artifact.
- [ ] After the hash-locked install, `scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` performs a
  **parsed** comparison — installed packages (from `pip freeze`, lowercased
  name→version) vs the lock's `name==version` entries (skipping `--hash`/comment
  lines) — and fails on any installed package absent from the lock or version-
  mismatched, modulo the documented `pip`/`setuptools`/`wheel` base allowlist (closing
  the ambient-package hole under `--no-isolation --no-deps`; a raw text diff of the two
  formats would be meaningless). `test_release_workflow_pins.py` check (h) asserts this
  guard step is wired into `release.yml`, and a unit test feeds the script a
  lock+freeze fixture pair to confirm it passes on a clean env and fails on an extra
  package.
- [ ] Hatchling's version is enforced end-to-end via `--no-isolation` against
  the pre-installed hash-locked env (not via a `pyproject.toml` pin), with
  `test_release_workflow_pins.py` failing if `--no-isolation` is removed from the build
  invocation (no free-resolution path remains).
- [ ] The MCP publisher is pinned to an exact version and its archive digest is
  verified in a separate `mcp_verify` job that has **no** `id-token: write`; the
  OIDC-privileged `mcp_registry` job `needs: mcp_verify` and consumes only the
  verified artifact — so the OIDC scope is never co-resident with an unverified
  binary; `mcp_registry` runs `chmod +x mcp-publisher` after `download-artifact`
  (upload-artifact drops the exec bit). `test_release_workflow_pins.py` additionally
  asserts the permission structure (`mcp_verify` has no `id-token: write`,
  `mcp_registry` does) and that the `chmod +x mcp-publisher` step is present. Verified by `test_mcp_publisher_pin.py`, which
  corrupts one byte of the pinned archive, runs the verify step, and asserts it exits
  non-zero. If upstream ships no checksums, the pinned SHA-256 is hard-coded in
  the workflow with a rationale comment.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The embedded SHA-256 is **correct for the pinned URL** (not just
  that the verify *mechanism* works): a new `scripts/verify_mcp_publisher_pin.py` (invokable
  as `make verify-mcp-pin`) parses the exact pinned download URL and the embedded SHA-256 out
  of `release.yml`, downloads that URL, computes its SHA-256, and asserts byte-for-byte
  equality with the embedded value — exiting non-zero on any mismatch. `test_release_workflow_pins.py`
  asserts the script exists and that `make verify-mcp-pin` is wired (codebase-verifiable); the
  actual network download + hash match is `[operator-attested]` — the implementer runs
  `make verify-mcp-pin` once in-session and records its passing output (the computed digest ==
  the embedded digest) as a comment on this ticket, so a typoed / wrong-arch / stale hash is
  caught before the change lands rather than at release runtime.
- [ ] The release-evidence pipeline is **wired** so each job writes its data to a
  distinctly-named fragment (`evidence-shapin`/`evidence-build`/`evidence-mcp`) and a
  consolidation job concatenates them into `release-evidence.txt` (job-scoped
  artifacts cannot be appended across jobs). `test_release_workflow_pins.py` check (f)
  asserts the *wiring* statically — the fragment names **and** the write commands that
  populate them (e.g. the mcp step redirecting version+digest into `evidence-mcp`), so … [truncated by reconciler]

content.text: ## Why
Per-criterion **blocking is already done** (`code_review/registry.threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3 +
detector fail-closed). What is missing is **attestation integration**: a project criterion's
verdict/coverage must fold into the signed (kind-keyed) attestation, and activating/editing/
disabling a criterion must invalidate a prior attestation — but `claim_gate_check` never
re-compares the routing version, and `registry_version()` hashes only the PACKAGED routing
(`attest.py:44`), so an overlay change produces an identical version and does NOT invalidate.
## What
- `registry_version(repo_root=None)` additionally hashes the `.rebar/` overlay when `repo_root` is
given; thread `repo_root` through **every** caller: `claim_gate_check` → `compute_validity`, and
also `drift_refresh_candidate` and `remediation_mode_candidate` (which call `registry_version()`
without it today). So activating/editing/disabling a criterion invalidates a prior attestation at
claim time.
- A disabled built-in is recorded in a `disabled_builtins: [ids]` field in the verdict `coverage`
dict (folded into the signed manifest) so the cert reflects reduced coverage; additive/
expand-contract (absent on old certs → treated as stale → re-review, never a crash).
- Cross-gate: this applies to **any** gate attestation backed by the shared registry — plan-review
now; code-review once it signs (code-review signs nothing today; the `attest.py` port to
code-review rides with story `#6`).
## Scope
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (registry_version(repo_root), coverage field,
threading), the claim-gate path.
- Depends on story `#1` (the overlay must exist to hash) and story `#2` (DET blocking).
- Blocking itself is NOT in scope (already shipped via `threshold_for` + kernel Pass-3).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the `.rebar/` overlay; threaded through
`claim_gate_check`/`compute_validity`/`drift_refresh_candidate`/`remediation_mode_candidate`.
- [ ] Activating/editing/disabling a project criterion invalidates a prior plan-review attestation
at claim time; an unchanged overlay does not churn (regver == today when overlay absent).
- [ ] A disabled built-in appears in `coverage.disabled_builtins` in the signed manifest.
- [ ] Expand-contract: an old attestation lacking the new basis is treated as stale (re-review),
never a crash.
- [ ] A project criterion's verdict + coverage fold into the signed attestation; it can never
rebind a built-in.
## compute_validity regver check + disabled_builtins manifest line (remediation, run 1)
### `compute_validity` gains a regver staleness check (clears G6 blocker 1)
Threading `repo_root` into `compute_validity` is necessary but NOT sufficient — its plan-review
branch must ALSO compare the attestation's recorded regver against the current one:
`manifest_regver(manifest) != registry_version(repo_root)` → the record reads as **not valid**
with reason `"stale-regver"` (a new invalidation reason alongside the existing
material/head-sha/reopen checks). So activating/editing/disabling a project criterion (which
changes `registry_version(repo_root)` because it now hashes the `.rebar/` overlay) makes a prior
attestation read stale at claim time. `manifest_regver(manifest)` is a small helper that extracts
the `regver:` line from the signed manifest (mirroring the existing `manifest_material`). An
attestation with NO regver line (pre-this-change) → treated as stale → re-review (expand-contract,
never a crash).
### `disabled_builtins` is a dedicated signed manifest line (clears G6 blocker 2)
`build_manifest()` emits a NEW `disabled_builtins: [id,id,...]` line (sorted, deterministic) WHEN
the verdict `coverage` carries disabled built-ins (from the overlay disabling a built-in via ef7e's
merge) — so the cert reflects reduced coverage rather than silent omission. A `manifest_disabled_builtins(manifest)`
parser reads it back (like `manifest_material`). The line is ADDITIVE/expand-contract: absent on old
certs (parsed as `[]`), present only when non-empty, so a clean run's manifest is byte-identical to
today (attestation-safe). `verify_signature` re-derives the same manifest and checks the HMAC as usual.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)
- [ ] `compute_validity` (plan-review branch) adds a `manifest_regver != registry_version(repo_root)`
staleness check returning reason `stale-regver`; a missing regver line → stale (re-review).
A test proves activating/editing a project criterion invalidates a prior attestation.
- [ ] `build_manifest` emits a deterministic `disabled_builtins: [ids]` line when the verdict
coverage has disabled built-ins; a `manifest_disabled_builtins` parser reads it; absent/empty
on a clean run (byte-identical manifest). A test asserts the round-trip + HMAC re-verify.
## No mass re-review + the built-in-disable mechanism (remediation, run 2)
### The regver line ALREADY exists — no mass invalidation (clears T4)
Current signed manifests ALREADY carry a `regver:` line (verified: e.g. `regver: 83e5f63ad06d893a`).
This story adds the CHECK in `compute_validity`, NOT the line. The `registry_version` basis change is
ADDITIVE: for an OVERLAY-ABSENT repo, `registry_version(repo_root)` hashes the same packaged routing
it does today ⇒ the SAME regver value ⇒ existing certs stay valid (zero churn). A repo that has an
overlay is BY DEFINITION new (the overlay feature shipped in ef7e), so it has NO pre-existing certs to
invalidate. The truly-ancient "no regver line at all" case → stale → one re-review, which is the
correct expand-contract behaviour (never a crash). So there is no deployment-wide mandatory re-review.
### The built-in-disable mechanism is part of THIS story (clears G6)
ef7e's MVP implemented overlay RE-TUNE of a built-in (per-key routing merge) but NOT disable. This
story adds disable: an overlay `plan_review` entry for a BUILT-IN id carrying `"disabled": true`
REMOVES that built-in from `effective_criteria(repo_root)` (so its finder never runs) — implemented
in `registry.effective_criteria` (a disabled built-in is excluded from the returned set) +
`effective_routing` (the entry is retained but flagged). The set of disabled built-in ids is exposed
via a small `disabled_builtins(repo_root) -> list[str]` helper. The gate records them in the verdict
`coverage["disabled_builtins"]`, which `build_manifest` folds into the `disabled_builtins:` manifest
line. `_validate_routing_entry` accepts `disabled: bool` only on an un-prefixed (built-in) id (a
`project.` id cannot be "disabled" — it is simply not activated). This keeps the epic's "the overlay
may re-tune OR disable a built-in; a disable is recorded in coverage" AC coherent within this story.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions, run 2)
- [ ] Overlay-absent repos see NO regver change (existing attestations stay valid); the regver line
already exists, so this adds only the staleness CHECK. A test asserts overlay-absent parity.
- [ ] An overlay `disabled: true` on a built-in id removes it from `effective_criteria`; a
`disabled_builtins(repo_root)` helper lists them; they flow into `coverage` + the manifest line.

baseline.summary: Blocking policy + attestation integration (registry_version(repo_root), disabled_builtins, invalidation)

content.text: # scripts/probe-rebar.sh has 3 stale assertions vs the current engine
## What
The release smoke probe reports 3 failures that are NOT engine defects — the probe
script tests behavior the engine intentionally changed. Surfaced during the 0.6.0

## Reproduction Steps

2. `REBAR_ROOT=<store> PROBE_LIVE=1 bash scripts/probe-rebar.sh`.
3. Observe 3 failures unrelated to engine correctness.

`--set-tags`/`--add-tag`/`--remove-tag` (per CLAUDE.md tag-delta surface).

## Why
Package the auto-lander loop service and wire it into the existing compose stack on the Gerrit box, single-instance. Split out of S5 (`perpetual-ultrasonic-raccoon`) to keep each unit loadable whole.

## Files
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.autolander` — NEW: service image (installs the stdlib loop; `HEALTHCHECK` added by S5d).
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — EDIT: add the `autolander` service (labeled `autoheal=true`, per S5d) + the `willfarrell/autoheal` sidecar (Docker socket mounted **read-write** — autoheal issues `docker restart`, a daemon WRITE, so `:ro` would silently fail; the socket-write privilege is the accepted, inherent cost of autoheal) + declare the named state volume `gerrit_autolander` as `external: true`.
- `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` — EDIT: add `autolander` to `SITE_SUBDIRS` (the `volume_for_subdir()` helper prefixes `gerrit_` + maps `-`→`_`, so the subdir `autolander` yields the docker volume `gerrit_autolander` — the exact name used in `docker-compose.yml`). Incident-2731 drift gate: `config-check.sh` check 5 hard-fails CI when an `external: true` volume is missing from `SITE_SUBDIRS`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `infra/compose/Dockerfile.autolander` (new) + the `autolander` compose service added to the existing `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`.
- [ ] **Single-instance guard:** the container acquires a POSIX advisory **file lock** (`flock` on the concrete lockfile **`autolander.lock`** at the root of its mounted state volume) on start; a second copy fails to acquire it and exits non-zero. This `flock` is the **sole** single-instance mechanism — do NOT rely on `deploy.replicas: 1` (a Swarm-only key silently ignored by plain `docker compose`).
- [ ] **State volume:** the named volume **`gerrit_autolander`** is declared `external: true` and its subdir `autolander` added to `SITE_SUBDIRS` in `compose-up.sh`; it holds `autolander.lock`, the heartbeat file (S5d), the emergency-stop sentinel (S5d), and `recovery.json` (S5d), so all survive container recreation.
- [ ] **Autoheal sidecar wired:** the `willfarrell/autoheal` service is present in `docker-compose.yml` with the Docker socket mounted **read-write** (required for its `docker restart` action), and the `autolander` service carries the `autoheal=true` label so the sidecar manages it (the restart behaviour itself is exercised by S5d's hang test).
- [ ] **Tests:** `docker compose config` validates (autolander + autoheal services, `gerrit_autolander` external volume, `autoheal=true` label, read-write socket mount present); **flock proof (concrete):** `docker compose up -d autolander` then a second `docker run` on the same image + volume asserts exit code ≠ 0 within 10 s (the second instance fails the `flock`); `config-check.sh` check 5 passes (`autolander` in `SITE_SUBDIRS`).
baseline.summary: S5a Container + compose service + flock single-instance + external state volume

content.text: ## Why
Provenance an auditor can't see isn't useful. The gate-code version+SHA stamp
(stories 1-2) must be visible where attestations are inspected (epic
jira-reb-596).
## What
- Surface `manifest_rebar_version()` output in the `show` attestation rendering
(attestation data rides in the ticket state dict; render it in the show path in
`src/rebar/_reads.py` / `src/rebar/__init__.py` alongside the certified/verdict
block, HMAC still stripped).

the `VerifySignatureResultOut` model in `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` and the JSON
schema `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` (new **nullable

content.text: ## Why
Claim (open->in_progress) is the enforcement point and must be fast (no LLM, no network round-trip).
## What
- Claim requires a valid, non-stale signed attestation; a FAST signature-verify only (target p95 < ~50ms);
absence/stale signature blocks; --force + justification override (recorded).
## Scope
- The heavy review runs OUT-OF-BAND (rebar review-plan / an MCP run_workflow), triggered on a claim-block or by CI.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Claim blocks on absent/material-edit-invalidated signature; the fast check meets the latency target.
- [ ] --force override is available and logged with justification.
- [ ] No LLM/network on the claim path.
## Acceptance Criteria (added — close G3 coverage)

- [ ] End-to-end proving check: claim-block (absent/stale signature) → run review-plan → earn a signature → claim succeeds, PLUS edge cases (--force + logging; material-edit invalidation; fail-open on unsupported stack; cap-hit INDETERMINATE; gate-off preference leaves claim at today's behavior).

- [ ] ENFORCE the config preference (defaults OFF): off → claim/transition-to-in_progress unchanged; on → the fast signature check gates them. (The config TOOL/UX is the separate F5 epic; the claim path ENFORCES the preference.)
## Acceptance Criteria (added — T9 claim atomicity)

- [ ] The signature-verify + the open→in_progress transition are ONE atomic operation (reuse rebar's atomic `claim`: re-read under lock + optimistic concurrency), with no check-then-act gap — concurrently, exactly one claim wins; cross-clone double-claims converge per rebar's replay semantics.
## Acceptance Criteria (added — signing-infra unavailability)

- [ ] When the gate is ENABLED and the signing/verification machinery is UNAVAILABLE (missing MCP environment key / signing subsystem error), claim FAILS CLOSED (blocks — consistent with the completion-verifier close gate's fail-closed posture), with the recorded `--force`+justification as the escape. When the gate is DISABLED (default OFF), claim is unchanged regardless. (A missing signing KEY is an INTEGRITY dependency — distinct from review-TIME polyglot tool fail-open, which is about coverage.)

baseline.summary: Claim integration: fast signature check + --force override

baseline.description:
## Why
THE security-critical divergence. e165 (change 563, commit 2efdae38f) implemented key
validity as an **HLC-epoch** window (ordinal position in the reducer's canonical replay).
The APPROVED epic design requires **git-commit-ancestry** validity (tickets-branch commit
SHAs). HLC ordering is partly author-assigned, so a malicious clone holding a
later-revoked key can write an event with a backdated HLC that sorts BEFORE the revocation
and verifies as valid — defeating the feature's "not attacker-controllable" promise. The
immutable commit DAG closes that hole. (User rejected the delivered design; see d7c0.)

## Why the DAG is stronger
Commit SHAs chain content+parents, so an event's position in history is a tamper-proof
fact — you cannot make a new event an ancestor of an existing revocation commit without
forging SHAs. HLC ordering trusts the author-assigned timestamp component; commit ancestry
trusts only the DAG.

## Architecture decision — pure reducer + git-aware resolver (READ FIRST)
The reducer (`_processors.py`) is **pure-filesystem** today (no git/subprocess) and MUST
stay so (its output is cache-keyed; it runs on plain event-file directories). Commit SHAs
are git metadata not in event JSON, so we do NOT store SHAs in reduced state. Instead:

- **Reducer keyring fold (pure):** records each key's lifecycle by **event position** (the
  `{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` filename prefix the reducer already parses) — record shape
  `{public_key, added_at: <position>, revoked_at: <position|None>}`. Drop `added_epoch` /
  `revoked_epoch` / `keyring_epoch`. `state["keys"]` = keys with `revoked_at is None`.
- **Git-aware resolver (new, in `authorship.py`, the attest layer — NOT the reducer):**
  - `resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir, *, repo_root) -> str | None`: maps a
    position prefix to the tickets-branch commit SHA that introduced that event file.
    **TYPE is NOT an input** to the resolver, so it globs the position prefix:
    `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json"` run in the
    tracker dir, taking the (single) introducing commit. Returns `None` on any git failure
    or no match (fail-closed).
  - `verify_authorship_at_commit(envelope, identity_id, event_commit, event_position, *,
    repo_root) -> Verdict`: builds the trust root from exactly the keys valid at
    `event_commit`. A key K is valid iff **`merge-base --is-ancestor(K.added_commit,
    event_commit)` AND NOT `merge-base --is-ancestor(K.revoked_commit, event_commit)`**,
    where `K.added_commit`/`K.revoked_commit` come from resolving K's `added_at`/`revoked_at`
    positions. This is where the AC's commit-anchored record
    `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit}` materializes (resolver output). ANY git
    subprocess failure (`git log` / `merge-base` non-zero, timeout, missing repo) resolves
    to a **non-verified** Verdict — the resolver/verifier NEVER raises (fail-closed, mirrors
    `resolve_trust_root`).
- **Intra-commit refinement (N-events-per-commit):** `batch_stage_and_commit` puts N event
  files in ONE commit, and `merge-base --is-ancestor(C, C)` is true, so when a key's
  add/revoke shares the event's commit the DAG cannot order them — refine with the
  **intra-commit position** (`{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` prefix ordering, which is a total order
  within that commit): a KEY_ADD in the same commit counts as added iff its position ≤ the
  event position; a KEY_REVOKE in the same commit counts as revoked iff its position ≤ the
  event position. NOTE this HLC tiebreak is NOT the rejected inter-commit weakness: events
  in one commit were written by ONE author in ONE atomic batch, so an attacker cannot
  insert an event into someone else's already-sealed commit — intra-commit ordering is not
  attacker-exploitable the way cross-commit backdating was.

## What
- Reducer `process_key_event` folds position-based records (no epoch); `make_initial_state`
  seeds `keyring: []` (no `keyring_epoch`); `_rederive_keyring_keys` → keys with
  `revoked_at is None`; remove `keys_valid_at_epoch`.
- **Genesis / bootstrap:** keys carried on a CREATE (`_bootstrap_genesis_keyring`) get
  `added_at` = **the CREATE event's position** (`{ts}-{uuid}` of the CREATE), so their
  added-commit resolves to the CREATE commit (an ancestor of every later event). There is
  NO separate ambiguous sentinel. TOFU genesis (first `KEY_ADD` on a keyless identity)
  records `added_at` = that KEY_ADD's position.
- **Snapshot restore + v4 migration:** `process_snapshot` restores the position-based
  keyring verbatim. A pre-position (e165 v4) SNAPSHOT whose keyring records carry
  `added_epoch`/`revoked_epoch` (no `added_at`) is MIGRATED by re-seeding from the
  identity's static `keys` via `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (treated as genesis at the
  CREATE position) rather than trusting the stale epoch fields. Because the stack is
  UNLANDED and lands atomically, no real store holds a v4 epoch snapshot; this migration is
  a defensive floor, not a live path.
- `authorship.py`: add `resolve_event_commit` + `verify_authorship_at_commit` +
  commit-ancestry trust root; **REMOVE `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`,
  `keys_valid_at_epoch`, `_position_prefix`'s epoch use** (the HLC-epoch API).
- `identity.py` key add/revoke seam is unchanged in shape (TOFU genesis self-signed;
  unsigned non-genesis refused; signed add/rotate/revoke); only epoch wording in docstrings
  becomes commit wording.
- Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` v4→v5 and `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` v5→v6 (both preserve-and-ignore).
- Consumes TS1's in-toto authorship (verify the event's Statement against keys valid at the
  event's commit).

## Stack scoping (why TS2 and TS3 land together)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 563 = commit 2efdae38f (e165), which touches ONLY
`authorship.py`, `reducer/{_processors,_state,_version,_cache}.py`, and `identity.py`. The
**consumers** of the era model — `verify_authorship.py` (`_verify_signed` → `epoch_for_position`
/ `verify_authorship_at_epoch`) and `compact.py` (`_build_authorship_ledger` → `epoch`) —
live in commit 721702e91 (3183), so they are rewired to `resolve_event_commit` /
`verify_authorship_at_commit` in **TS3 (117b, change 580)**. Because TS2 removes the epoch
API from `authorship.py` while TS3 updates its commit-7 consumers, the two are pushed
together and land atomically with the whole stack; each is internally green at its own
patchset (at commit 563 the verify-gate/compact code does not yet exist). TS2 REPLACES
e165's OWN tests (`test_identity_e165*`, which assert the epoch model) with
commit-ancestry tests.

## Scope
In: position-based key records, `resolve_event_commit`, DAG-ancestry validity
(`verify_authorship_at_commit`) with intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git handling,
TOFU/write-gate, reducer fold + snapshot + v4 migration + version bumps, removal of the
epoch API, transitioning e165's tests. Out: authorship payload format (TS1); the SNAPSHOT
ledger schema + `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict + the verify-gate/compact rewiring (TS3 /
3183, commit 7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The resolved key record binds `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit?}`
  (tickets-branch commit SHAs); a test using TWO real fixture commits asserts the resolved
  shape (add key in commit A, revoke in a later commit B; resolver yields A and B).
- [ ] Genesis key-add is accepted ONLY when self-signed (TOFU base case); an unsigned
  NON-genesis key-add is refused (test).
- [ ] Commit-ancestry validity across the revocation boundary: with key K added in commit
  C1 and revoked in a later commit C3, an event signed by K whose commit descends C1 but
  NOT C3 PASSES, and one whose commit descends C3 FAILS (test, both sides of boundary).
- [ ] Validity derives from commit ancestry, NOT event timestamps: an event written AFTER
  the revocation but carrying a BACKDATED `data`/filename timestamp still FAILS, because its
  introducing commit descends the revocation commit regardless of the timestamp (the
  killer test that commit-ancestry beats HLC backdating).
- [ ] Intra-commit refinement: with a KEY_ADD and an event in the SAME commit, a KEY_ADD at
  an earlier intra-commit position → event PASSES; a KEY_ADD at a later position → event
  FAILS; symmetrically a KEY_REVOKE at an earlier position in the same commit → event FAILS
  (test using a batched multi-event commit).
- [ ] Fail-closed git handling: when the position→commit resolution cannot run (git
  failure / no matching commit), verification returns a non-verified Verdict and never
  raises (test, e.g. an unresolvable position).
- [ ] Replay never rejects: a not-yet-valid-key / bad-signature event still folds into
  state (test); the delivered HLC-epoch surface is gone — a grep-assert confirms
  `verify_authorship_at_epoch`, `epoch_for_position`, `keys_valid_at_epoch`,
  `keyring_epoch`, `added_epoch`, `revoked_epoch` are ABSENT from `src/rebar`.
- [ ] The reducer stays pure: a grep-assert confirms `src/rebar/reducer/` imports no
  `subprocess` and runs no git (the resolver lives in `authorship.py`).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (resolve_event_commit + verify_authorship_at_commit + commit-ancestry trust root + intra-commit refinement + fail-closed git; remove epoch API)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (position-based keyring fold; genesis added_at = CREATE position; remove keys_valid_at_epoch/epoch cursor)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py` (seed keyring, no keyring_epoch)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` (SCHEMA_VERSION v4->v5)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py` (reducer cache v5->v6)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (docstring epoch->commit wording; seam shape unchanged)
baseline.summary: transition: key validity -> git-commit-ancestry (tickets-branch SHAs, replaces HLC-epoch)

baseline.description:
## Why

108 tickets in the store carry `## Success Criteria`. Their criteria are conventionally plain
`- ` bullets, and `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`
(resetting at the next `##`). So those criteria are invisible to the P1 blocking floor, cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag the completion verifier matches on checkbox text, and are
not individually checkable. Migrating them is the substantive half of this epic — the heading
rename is cosmetic by comparison.

## What

Migrate the store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` so their criteria live under
`## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items.

## Scope

The ticket descriptions in the `tickets` branch that match `## Success Criteria` (108 distinct
tickets at time of writing; the migration recomputes the set rather than hard-coding it).

A migration script under `scripts/` performing the rewrite via the rebar library
(`rebar.edit_ticket`) so every change is a normal, auditable ticket event — NOT a direct
rewrite of the git-backed store.

OUT OF SCOPE: closed tickets' historical accuracy is not preserved by rewriting; see Approach
for why closed tickets are migrated too and what that costs.

## Approach

For each matching ticket: locate the `## Success Criteria` block (bounded by the next `## `
heading), convert its `- ` bullets to `- [ ]` items, and merge them into the ticket's existing
`## Acceptance Criteria` block, appending if one exists and creating it if not. Tickets already
carrying both headings merge; the SC heading is then removed.

Editing a ticket's description changes its MATERIAL FINGERPRINT, which invalidates any
plan-review attestation as `stale-material`. That is correct and unavoidable — the plan text
genuinely changed — but it means the migration must not be run blindly across claimed work.
The script therefore processes CLOSED tickets by default and requires an explicit flag to touch
open/in_progress ones, so no in-flight claim is silently invalidated. The count of skipped
in-flight tickets is reported so the remainder can be migrated deliberately.

Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the block-rewriting function over fixtures: SC-only, both-headings, SC with
  mixed `- ` and `- [ ]` items, SC as the LAST section (no following `##`), and a ticket with
  no SC block (must be a no-op).
- Dry-run over the real store, with the resulting diff attached as a ticket comment.
- Post-migration assertion that `_count_ac_items` returns >=1 for every migrated ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A script under `scripts/` performs the migration through `rebar.edit_ticket`, with
      `--dry-run` as the default mode and a required explicit flag to modify non-closed tickets.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all five block-shape cases listed under Testing, including the no-op case.
- [ ] After the live run, `git grep -l "## Success Criteria" tickets` matches no ticket
      description outside the skipped in-flight set.
- [ ] Every migrated ticket returns `_count_ac_items >= 1`, verified by a script pass over the
      migrated set.
- [ ] The dry-run diff and the list of skipped in-flight tickets are recorded as comments on
      this ticket.
baseline.summary: Migrate store tickets from Success Criteria bullets to Acceptance Criteria checkboxes

baseline.description:
# J4 — Pin a `UserIdentityModel` contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

User identity is the second real Cloud/DC difference. Jira Cloud identifies users by opaque `accountId`
(username and userkey were removed for GDPR); Data Center identifies them by `name`. This leaks into two places
in the Cloud adapter: `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`, which returns
`(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` and encodes the 3-state account-resolution fast-path the core diff
consults (ADR 0035 §(d) canonical-comparison corollary), and the transport's create/update assignee payload
shape.

PR #120 handled this by copying `resolve_assignee` and hardcoding `is_account_id=False`, and its copy consulted
`getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` — an attribute nothing ever sets, so its entire authoritative
branch was unreachable and DC would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. That is not a
cosmetic bug: a permanently non-authoritative assignee resolution makes the outbound diff re-emit assignee
changes it can never converge, which is the churn class epic `ace2` was created to fix.

## Approach

Define a `UserIdentityModel` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `resolve(local_value,
remote_identity)` returning the existing `(value, authoritative, is_account_id)` tuple, and
`to_payload(value)` returning the deployment's assignee field shape. Two implementations: `AccountIdIdentity`
(Cloud — the current behavior verbatim, `{"accountId": …}`) and `NameIdentity` (DC — resolves through the DC
user-search endpoint, `{"name": …}`).

`NameIdentity` performs a **real** lookup against DC's user-search endpoint rather than echoing the local
value, so it can return `authoritative=True` and the diff converges. Its resolver is injected at construction
from the DC transport [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], not discovered via `getattr`, so there is no unreachable branch.

**Alternative rejected:** DC returns the local value with `authoritative=False` always (PR #120's effective
behavior). It compiles and passes shallow tests while guaranteeing assignee-diff churn on every pass.

**Alternative rejected:** normalizing both to a single "user reference" string. The core diff's 3-state
fast-path genuinely needs to know whether the value is an accountId, so flattening it would push the branch
back into core.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — Cloud constructed with `AccountIdIdentity`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_user_identity_model.py` (new).

## Testing

Unit tier with a stateful fake resolver for the lookup (the irreducible external boundary), plus a shared
contract test over both implementations, since the 3-state contract must hold identically for each.

- shared contract, parameterized over both models: an empty local value yields
  `("", False, <model default>)`; a value that resolves to the SAME identity the remote already has yields
  `(None, True, …)` (converged, nothing to emit); a value resolving to a different identity yields that
  identity with `authoritative=True`.
- Cloud-specific: the resolved value is an accountId and `is_account_id is True`; payload is `{"accountId": …}`.
- DC-specific: the resolved value is a username and `is_account_id is False`; payload is `{"name": …}`.
- failure path: an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (the neutral base at
  `_backend.py:48`) rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value.
- regression oracle for PR #120's defect: a test asserts that for a resolvable assignee, DC returns
  `authoritative=True` — this test fails against the `getattr`-based implementation.
- contrast case: an unassigned local value yields the documented desired-unassigned state, not a lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test covers all three resolution states for both identity models
- [ ] a test asserts DC returns `authoritative=True` for a resolvable assignee (the anti-churn oracle)
- [ ] a test asserts an unresolvable assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for both models
- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` returns nothing — no `getattr`-discovered collaborator anywhere
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud assignee behavior is unchanged (`make test` green with those assertions unmodified)
baseline.summary: J4 — pin a UserIdentityModel contract (accountId for Cloud, name for Data Center)

content.text: ## What

baseline.description:
## Context
Container plan-review attestations inherit direct live children file-impact declarations. The current binary rule treats every child with an empty path list as undeclared, so a truthful `none` child poisons sibling path declarations and forces whole-HEAD invalidation. Stories 1934, 749c, and 1fd4 established authenticated tri-state scope and the manifest classifier. This story makes container inheritance and P9 consume that contract.

## Behavioral contract
- Closed children are ignored.
- A live `paths` child contributes its declared paths.
- A live `none` child is neutral: it contributes no paths and does not poison siblings.
- Any live `undeclared` child poisons child inheritance: no child paths are inherited and the container is not classified all-none.
- `all_none` is true only when at least one live child exists and every live child is authenticated `none`; no live children yields false.
- Scope precedence is exact: any own, cited, or inherited dependency path yields `paths`; otherwise explicit parent `none` yields `none`; otherwise all-live-children-none promotes only an `undeclared` parent to `none`; otherwise the result is `unscoped`. A parent declared `paths` is never promoted to `none`.
- P9 passes a leaf declared `none`; for containers it ignores closed children and counts only live `undeclared` children as poisoners. Its advisory names poisoners and offers both path declaration and `--none` as truthful remedies.

## Implementation plan
1. In `manifest.py`, replace the set-only child helper with a frozen private result containing `paths: frozenset[str]` and `all_none: bool`. No `effective` field is needed because consumers distinguish every required state with those two values. Preserve the poison rule above.
2. Let `dependency_hashes` accept an optional precomputed child-impact result while preserving its `dict[str, str]` return contract. If absent it computes the result for existing callers; if supplied it adds only the supplied child paths.
3. In `attest.py::sign_plan_review`, compute child impact once from the supplied full child states. Use the same result for dependency hashing and `container_all_none` classification, with the precedence above. The normal review path already supplies `ctx.children`; `orchestrator.py` needs no edit because `_reads.show_ticket` already returns `file_impact_scope`.
4. In `resign.py`, preserve the same behavior without network reads: build the full direct-child list from `initial_generation.relation_snapshot.child_ids` and `ticket_states_by_id`, then pass it to `sign_plan_review` inside the existing attested read session. Missing or inconsistent snapshot child state remains a structured refusal, never a broader or falsely narrow signature.
5. In `det_lint.py`, derive leaf and container P9 outcomes from authenticated `file_impact_scope`, using the same live/closed and neutral/poison rules.

## Behavior-first test design
Tests assert signed manifest dependencies and scope, validity after real file changes, public resign results, and P9 result contracts. They do not inspect source text, private dataclass shape, helper call counts, or implementation names.

- Extend `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` with signed-manifest/validity cases: paths+none inherits only path files and survives unrelated drift; a declared child-file change invalidates it; all-none plus undeclared parent signs `none`; explicit parent `none` remains `none`; own parent paths plus all-none remains `paths`; no live children does not synthesize `none`; a live undeclared child keeps child inheritance poisoned/unscoped.
- Extend `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` through `resign_plan_review` to prove cheap resign signs the same child-derived dependency scope as normal signing without a fetch.
- Extend `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` P9 cases for a `none` leaf, mixed paths+none container, all-none container, closed undeclared child, and live undeclared poisoner with the `--none` remedy.
- RED command: `pytest tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -q`. Confirm failures are missing tri-state behavior, not imports or source-text checks.
- Mutation proof: temporarily restore the legacy behavior that treats live `none` as undeclared, run `pytest tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -q`, and require the mixed-scope manifest/validity, resign, and P9 cases to fail; restore production behavior afterward.
- Refactoring litmus: a rename or extraction of the private child-impact helper must leave all assertions unchanged because they observe only manifest, validity, resign, and P9 contracts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Mixed live `paths` and `none` children sign only the path child dependencies.
- [x] Mixed-scope signatures survive unrelated file drift.
- [x] Mixed-scope signatures become stale when a declared child path changes.
- [x] All live children declared `none` promote an undeclared parent to signed scope `none`.
- [x] Explicit parent `none` remains signed scope `none`.
- [x] Parent-owned paths take precedence over all-none children: the manifest signs parent path dependencies and does not synthesize a file-scope:none marker.
- [x] No live children do not synthesize all-none scope.
- [x] Any live undeclared child poisons child inheritance and preserves conservative unscoped fallback when no parent or citation paths exist.
- [x] Cheap resign preserves the same child-derived signed scope using its immutable relation snapshot.
- [x] P9 passes declared-none leaves and containers whose live children are all declared.
- [x] P9 advises only live undeclared children and names both path and `--none` remedies.
- [x] The focused contract suite (pytest -q tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py) passes while asserting only observable manifest dependency/scope, validity, resign-result, and P9 verdict/coaching contracts; it contains no source-text searches or assertions on private object shape.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Container roll-up: a declared-none child is neutral in drift-scope inheritance and P9

content.text: ## Why
This is the dependency root of the oracle. The three-valued evidence contract, the fail-open execution harness,
and the optional-extra scaffolding are shared by every engine — they must exist and be stable before Engine A,
T0, or Engine B are built. Getting the contract right here is what makes "one implementation, not two" real.
## What
- The normalized **evidence model**: `resolved | abstained(reason)` with a CLOSED structured reason enum
(`unsupported_lang | no_tool | parse_error | timeout | ambiguous | private_or_internal_suspected |
network_error | rate_limited | version_skew | invalid_detector | other`), provenance/tier, and a coverage
record. `version_skew` (the #1 real failure) and `invalid_detector` (a project detector failing validation)
are first-class; `other` is the explicit catch-all (no open `…`). Resolution-lane resolved value is `refuted`
(never an asserted absence). One internal finding shape; SARIF 2.1.0 map at the edges (superset).
- The **fail-open recover/timeout harness** every backend runs inside. OUT-OF-PROCESS tools (ctags, ast-grep,
OpenGrep, scc/lizard, registry HTTP) use the subprocess reaper (mirror `acli_subprocess`: process-group,
SIGTERM→SIGKILL, structured timeout). IN-PROCESS bindings (tree-sitter) CANNOT be bounded by a thread/signal
timeout (it can't interrupt a hung C-extension call, and a segfault would kill the host) — so prefer the CLI
form of every matcher, and run any unavoidable in-process binding inside a WORKER SUBPROCESS so the same reaper
applies. A crash/timeout/missing-tool/version-skew becomes a recorded `abstain`, never raises; the visible skip
IS the coverage record — never a silent no-op. Each backend's version is pinned/recorded.
- **Optional-extra scaffolding**: a new extra in `pyproject.toml`, `_optional.py` guard + `guard_import`, core
stays import-clean (the existing optionality CI gate), non-adopting clients import nothing.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/` (new package) — contract + harness + extra wiring only; no backend logic.
- Polyglot/optional by construction; no Python-specific assumptions in the contract.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Evidence model + CLOSED structured reason enum (incl. version_skew, invalid_detector, other) + coverage implemented; `refute`/`abstain` representable; SARIF map both directions.

- [ ] Fail-open harness covers OUT-OF-PROCESS (subprocess reaper) AND IN-PROCESS (worker-subprocess) backends: crash / hang / timeout / missing tool / version-skew → recorded `abstain`, never raises — incl. a segfaulting C-extension parse.
- [ ] Optional extra added; core import-clean (optionality CI gate passes); non-adopting client imports nothing.
- [ ] Unit-tested: harness converts each failure mode to the correct `abstain(reason)` + coverage entry.

baseline.summary: Evidence contract + fail-open execution harness + optional-extra scaffolding (dependency root)

# P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

**Prerequisite for P2.1, P2.2, P2.3.** Every later item that adds, reorders, or
signs event content depends on there being exactly ONE canonical byte format.

## Context (problem + research)

Event serialization is scattered across many writers and only **one** is
canonical — `_store/event_append.py:56-61` emits
`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)`. Seven
other LIVE writers emit plain `json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False)` (unsorted):
reconciler `_engine/event_append.py:123`, `ticket_txn.py:219/351/372`,
`graph/_links.py:145`, `ticket-delete-unlink-scan.py:149`,
`batch_dispatch.py:222`; plus bash heredocs in `ticket-comment.sh:90-91`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:439` force-close), `ticket-revert.sh:170-174`
(live via `ticket-transition.sh:179` un-archive), `ticket-lib-api.sh:994/1017`
(delete), `ticket-compact.sh:274` (SNAPSHOT). There is **no** byte-parity test —
the one cited in `_store/event_append.py:15`'s docstring does not exist.

**Research / proven art.** The "`json.dumps == jq -S -c`" assumption is unsafe:
`jq` parses numbers as IEEE-754 float64, and rebar's ns `timestamp` is a 19-digit
integer **> 2^53** — jq <=1.6 (default macOS) rounds it on parse, and even jq-1.7
rounds it under arithmetic. The TUF/sigstore ecosystem's hard-won lesson is
"canonicalization across implementations is a footgun; standardize on one / sign
the literal bytes" (RFC 8785 JCS; python-tuf#457; sigstore DSSE). So: collapse to
ONE Python serializer, keep jq out of the event path entirely.

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP2: `json.dumps(...ensure_ascii=False)` == `jq -S -c` ONLY with
  `ensure_ascii=False` (`世界` diverges otherwise).
- EXP-jq: jq rounds the >2^53 timestamp (`.t+0` -> `...655000`); confirmed.
- EXP-R3 (real code): real `_canonical_bytes` != plain dumps, but parsed dicts are
  identical -> **re-serialization is replay-safe** (reducer reads keys, not bytes).
- EXP-R7 (real code): `python3 -m rebar._store.<submodule>` works and emits
  canonical sorted output -> bash heredocs can call the helper.
- EXP-R9/R9b (real code): the committed stdlib guard
  `docs/experiments/event_write_guard.py` flags **exactly 7 Python + 7 bash** event writers
  with **0 false positives** across 73 read/output `json.dumps` sites.

## What / Implementation detail

1. Factor a **lock-free** `canonical_bytes(event) -> bytes` helper (out of
   `_store/event_append.py:56-61`) importable without the write lock (the txn/LINK
   paths rename+commit inline, e.g. `ticket_txn.py:236-243`).
2. Route every live writer through it: the 5 Python sites import it; the 4 bash
   heredocs call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (pass the event(s) on stdin;
   **batch** multi-event paths — delete writes STATUS+ARCHIVED+N*UNLINK — in ONE
   invocation to avoid per-event subprocess cost).
3. Delete the dead leaf writers (`ticket-create.sh`, `ticket-edit.sh`) and leave
   `ticket-link.sh` (still serves `link --dry-run`, writes no event) /
   `ticket-migrate-*.sh` (one-shot) exempt. Fix the false docstring at
   `_store/event_append.py:15`.
4. Ship the **stdlib** structural guard as a CI test (semgrep/ast-grep/pre-commit
   are ABSENT here — EXP-R9). Python prong = AST (json.dump(s) on a dict carrying
   `event_type`); bash prong = regex scoped to `json.dump` co-occurring with an
   `'event_type'` dict (a bare grep false-positives on ~10 read/output `.sh`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `canonical_bytes()` extracted as a lock-free helper and imported by the 5 Python writers
- [ ] 4 bash heredoc writers call `python3 -m rebar._store.canonical` (multi-event paths batched)
- [ ] dead leaf writers deleted; `_store/event_append.py:15` docstring corrected
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test-ticket-write-commit-event.sh` added (parity + >2^53/non-ASCII fuzz)
- [ ] stdlib structural guard wired into CI (Python AST + scoped bash regex), expected writer set empty
- [ ] reconciler + compaction suites still green (no replay change)

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.0) for the full write-up and `docs/experiments/` for the prototypes.
- [ ] All event files (every type) are byte-identical regardless of writer, pinned by
- [ ] The structural guard fails CI on any new raw event serializer; after this epic
- [ ] No reducer/replay behavior change (existing committed data unaffected;
baseline.summary: P1.0 — Unify canonical event-byte serialization + zero-dep structural guard

content.text: ## Why
Pass-2 (validate each finding) is the strongest reuse candidate: the binary sub-questions
(`is_verifiable`, `evidence_entails_finding`, `path_reachable`, `impact_follows_necessarily`,
`no_viable_alternative_explanation`, `no_existing_mitigation`, `severity_claim_justified` + the
cited-reference veto) and the severity-attribute enums are properties of *a finding*, not of
plans-vs-diffs — so a code-review finding and a plan finding answer the SAME questions. Extracting
it gives one binary vocabulary + one `verification` contract that every gate shares, eliminating
the silent-drift class. The verify orchestration already built for plan-review (token-budget
chunking, merge-by-global-index, the non-frontier verifier-model default) is likewise general and
moves with it.
## What
- Move the Pass-2 verifier into the kernel as `verify_findings(findings, *, context, model,
headroom) -> verifications`, carrying the chunking + merge-by-index + verifier-model resolution.
- Make the `verification` pydantic/JSON contract the SINGLE registered source of the binary
vocabulary + severity-attribute enums (one schema, small/flat).
- Reliability: validate with the existing tolerant stack (json-repair + bounded retry +
pydantic-ai native outputs) and DEGRADE to INDETERMINATE on an unparseable turn — never
hard-crash a gate. (Reuse `gate_dispatch`'s degrade path; do not add stricter validation.)
- Rewire the plan-review verify step to consume the kernel (the per-gate verify-prompt preamble +
the plan context are passed in). No behavior change.
## Scope
In scope: the Pass-2 verify function + the `verification` contract + the tolerant-validation
reliability behavior, moved to the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-3 (WS1, on
which this depends), the coach (WS3), the seam doc + behavioral evals (WS4). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (verify builders), `sizing.py` (chunker), `workflow_ops.py`
(verify-inputs op), the verify prompt(s), and the kernel module.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The kernel exposes a `verify_findings` Pass-2 entry that takes a findings list + a domain
context and returns the per-finding `{severity_attributes, binary}` verifications, with the
token-budget chunking + merge-by-global-index + verifier-model default carried over.
- [ ] The `verification` contract is the single registered source of the binary-question
vocabulary + severity-attribute enums (one schema; no second copy).
- [ ] Validation uses json-repair + bounded retry and degrades to INDETERMINATE (never crashes a
gate) on an unparseable structured turn; a test exercises the degrade path.
- [ ] The plan-review verify step consumes the kernel; an offline (FakeRunner) test asserts the
verifications + downstream verdict are unchanged vs before.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS2: Extract Pass-2 finding-verifier + the verification contract into the kernel
