## What
Add a 7th link relation `caused_by` (directional, non-blocking, non-cycle-inducing, Jira-unmapped) expressing "this bug was caused by that ticket/change", making bug provenance a first-class graph edge so "source of bugs" is a real traversal.

## Files
- `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` — add `caused_by` to the `relation` enum (canonical source).
- `src/rebar/types.py` — regenerate the `Relation` Literal via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`.
- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — add `caused_by` to `CANONICAL_RELATIONS`.
- `src/rebar/graph/_graph.py` — CRITICAL: line ~204 has a hardcoded tuple `("relates_to","duplicates","supersedes","discovered_from")` that returns False (non-blocking / non-cycle); `caused_by` MUST be added there or it falls to the else-branch and gets block-cycle semantics.
- `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` — verify the non-blocking relation set includes `caused_by` (promotion applies only to `blocks`/`depends_on`).
- `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py` — update the `_USAGE` relation string (line ~28) and the directional-relations note (line ~30) to include `caused_by`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt` — update the enumerated relation list (overview line ~16).
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — update the relation list in the MCP write surface.
- `tests/golden/cli_help/*.out` — regenerate the ~8 golden CLI-help snapshots that enumerate the relation set (e.g. `link__help.out`, `__overview_help.out`, `__overview_dashhelp.out`).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_graph.py`, `outbound_links.py` — leave `caused_by` intentionally Jira-unmapped (like `discovered_from`/`duplicates`/`supersedes`); add it to the unmapped set if that set is explicit.
- `docs/ticket-model.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md` — document the relation.
- `tests/unit/graph/test_caused_by_relation.py` — new.

## Approach
Follow the `discovered_from` precedent exactly (directional, non-blocking, non-cycle, Jira-unmapped) so the change is purely additive: old LINK events and the reducer stay valid, no persisted data is rewritten, and back-out is simply ceasing to emit the value. The relation string is duplicated across several enforcement/help/golden sites (schema, generated types, `_links.py`, the block-cycle tuple in `_graph.py`, `unlink.py`, `overview.txt`, and the `tests/golden/cli_help/*.out` snapshots), so the edit set spans all of them; the single behavioral gotcha is `_graph.py`'s hardcoded non-blocking tuple, which must list `caused_by` or the relation wrongly gets blocking-cycle semantics. A dedicated relation (not reusing `discovered_from`, whose semantics are temporal not causal) is required so recovery-time and source-of-bugs can traverse causation directly.

## Tests
- Unit (real temp store): `link a b caused_by` round-trips and appears in reduced links with relation `caused_by`; a `caused_by` edge is NOT treated as a blocking dependency and a `caused_by` two-cycle is allowed (asserts the `_graph.py` semantics); an old LINK event without the relation still reduces.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/graph/test_caused_by_relation.py` passes: `rebar link <a> <b> caused_by` exits 0 and `rebar show <a> --output json | jq -e '.links[]|select(.relation==\"caused_by\")'` matches.
- [ ] the generated `Relation` literal in `src/rebar/types.py` includes `caused_by` and the schema enum has 7 values — unit test asserts membership.
- [ ] `caused_by` is non-blocking and non-cycle-inducing: a unit test asserts a `caused_by` edge does not appear as a blocker in `ready`/graph traversal and a `caused_by` two-node cycle does not raise.
- [ ] the golden CLI-help snapshots are regenerated and the `tests/golden/cli_help` suite passes with `caused_by` listed — asserted by the golden test going green.
- [ ] a pre-existing LINK event with a legacy relation still reduces without error (back-compat) — unit test asserts unchanged reducer output for a fixture of old links.
baseline.summary: Add caused_by as a 7th link relation (additive, discovered_from precedent)

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. Configure local signing (`[identity] signing_key` set; git email resolves to an identity — e.g. 594c).
2. `rebar create task "t"` -> the CREATE event is SIGNED (`author_sig` present).
3. `rebar transition <t> open idea` (or any claim/transition/close) -> the STATUS event is written with `author_id` stamped but **NO `author_sig`** (UNSIGNED).
4. `rebar verify-identity --all --format json` lists that STATUS event as `unsigned` (in-scope, enforceable).

**Expected:** transition/claim/close STATUS (and claim EDIT) events sign like CREATE/COMMENT do.
**Actual:** they are attributed but unsigned.

## Root cause

CREATE/COMMENT are written via `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.append_event`, which calls
`_apply_authorship` (the signing seam + write-gate). But transitions/claims/closes are written
via `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (`transition_core` ~L249-268, `claim_core` ~L341-372): these
build the STATUS/EDIT event dicts, merge `attribution` (author_email/author_id) but write them
directly via `fsutil.atomic_write` + git commit, **never calling `_apply_authorship`**. So the
transactional path signs nothing AND bypasses the require_authenticated write-gate.

## Why this blocks the flip (dc09 / pristine-horrible-whapuku)

The CI merge-gate `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` runs `rebar verify-identity` over the
whole tickets store with posture/boundary from `rebar.toml`. After `require_authenticated=true`
lands, every NEW status transition (post-enforce_since) writes an unsigned in-scope STATUS event
that the gate flags -> the gate FAILS -> blocks landing. So enforcement is unsafe across the
txn writer until this is fixed. This is a foundational signing gap the epic's 5 stories did not
anticipate (they assumed signing worked for all writers).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `transition_core` and `claim_core` in `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` sign their STATUS (and
      claim EDIT) events via the same signing seam CREATE/COMMENT use (`_apply_authorship` or an
      equivalent), so a transition/claim/close under a configured signing key produces
      `author_sig`.
- [ ] Under `identity.require_authenticated`, an unsignable transition of a non-exempt ticket is
      refused by the write-gate (parity with `append_event`), while gate-exempt types
      (session_log/code_review/identity) are unaffected.
- [ ] A held-out regression test asserts: with a signing key configured, a transition/claim
      STATUS event has `author_sig` and `rebar verify-identity` reports it `verified`; without a
      key + enforcement on, the transition is refused. Proving command: `make test`.
- [ ] No regression to txn atomicity/locking (claim writes STATUS+EDIT in one commit).
baseline.summary: txn.py transitions/claims/closes write UNSIGNED in-scope STATUS/EDIT events (bypass the signing seam) — blocks safe require_authenticated flip

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` lines 235-242 describe the close's completion precheck inaccurately, and agents reason from the stated mechanism. The current text:

> **After the change MERGES, fast-forward YOUR worktree before you close.** The close's
> completion precheck reads your worktree's git history and requires the merged
> `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit reachable from HEAD (else it fails with "cannot confirm the work
> landed").

Verified against the implementation on this tree (HEAD `1052bc856f`):

1. **"the MERGED commit" is wrong.** `_referencing_commit_exists`
   (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:149`) runs
   `["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "log", "--format=%B%x00"]` (`:159-163`) with **no ref
   argument**, so it scans the whole history reachable from the current HEAD and returns True for
   ANY commit whose message carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or a leading `<id>:` subject that
   `resolve_ticket_id` maps into `accepted_ids` (`:170-176`). Merge status is never consulted. An
   unlanded local commit on your own branch satisfies it.
2. **The precheck is conditional; the doc presents it as unconditional.** It is guarded by
   `if field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker) and not _referencing_commit_exists(...)`
   (`transition_close.py:283-284`), so a ticket with no recorded `file_impact` never reaches it.
   It is also inside `_completion_precheck` (`:195`), which returns early when the
   `require_completion_verification_for_close` gate is off (`:228-236`), on `--force-close`
   (`:237`), and on a live duplicate/supersedes replacement link (`:256`).
3. **`accepted_ids` is a subtree, not one id.** `:277-286` adds every transitive descendant
   returned by `list_descendants` across the `epics`/`stories`/`tasks`/`bugs` buckets, so a
   parent is satisfied by a commit referencing any child.
4. **`--ref` is absent from AGENTS.md.** `rebar transition --ref=<ref>` is documented at
   `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt:7` ("verify (and sign) against the committed tree at <ref>
   instead of HEAD. Use it to close a stacked story against its own commit while your worktree
   stays at the epic tip; default HEAD") and at `docs/plan-review-gate.md:899-916`, whose
   "Stacked-epic recipe" is exactly the workflow this repo runs. AGENTS.md never mentions it —
   `grep -n -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` returns nothing.

The fast-forward advice is a safe superset, so nobody following it is broken. The harm is the false mechanism: believing the precheck ENFORCES land-then-close leads agents to skip `--ref` when closing a stacked story, and to tell operators that a pre-land close is impossible. This happened live — a session told the operator that seven in-progress epic bugs could not be closed before landing; the operator corrected it. The rule that actually orders land-before-close is the POLICY line one bullet above, at `AGENTS.md:233-234`: "Do **not** close a ticket until its change is `Verified +1` — a passing completion-verifier is **not** a substitute for green CI."

## Approach

Rewrite the bullet to state the real mechanism and cite the real ordering rule, keeping the fast-forward guidance for the case it genuinely addresses.

The corrected bullet will:

- lead with the POLICY (`Verified +1`, already stated at `AGENTS.md:233-234`) as the reason to
  wait, instead of implying the precheck enforces it;
- state the precheck accurately: when the ticket records `file_impact` and the
  completion-verification close gate is on, the close requires a commit **reachable from your
  current HEAD** carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer for the ticket **or any transitive
  descendant** — merge status is not checked, so a local unlanded commit satisfies it;
- keep the fast-forward recipe (`git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main`) as the
  remedy for the case it actually fixes: a worktree whose history does NOT contain the commit —
  a fresh worktree, or closing from a checkout that never had it;
- name `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the sanctioned way to close a
  stacked story against its own commit while the worktree stays at the epic tip, and link
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Which commit the completion gate verifies — `--ref`" for the
  detail, per this file's stated "keep this file lean … one-line pointers into `docs/`" rule
  (`AGENTS.md:9-11`);
- state precisely what `--ref` does and does not do: it retargets the completion **verification
  and signature** to that ref's tree; it does **not** narrow the referencing-commit scan, which
  runs `git log` with no ref regardless (`transition_close.py:159-163`);
- preserve the existing NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning **verbatim**, as the
  final sentences of the bullet (`AGENTS.md:239-242`).

**Why a rewrite in place rather than a pointer to `docs/`.** AGENTS.md is loaded at launch by every harness, so a wrong mechanism there is the default belief for every agent in the repo; a pointer alone would leave the false statement resident in context. The corrected text stays short and defers the `--ref` detail to `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, which already documents it correctly at lines 899-916 — no new doc is created and no existing doc is duplicated.

**The whole population, not one sample.** The same misstatement exists in a second place: `CONTRIBUTING.md:219-230` (§2f "After merge — fast-forward your worktree, THEN close the ticket") says the precheck "requires the merged `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit to be reachable from HEAD; without the fast-forward it fails with 'cannot confirm the work landed.'" `AGENTS.md:203` sends readers to CONTRIBUTING.md for "the full recipe", so fixing only AGENTS.md would leave the authoritative long-form copy wrong. `grep -rn "cannot confirm the work landed" . --exclude-dir=.git` returns exactly one Markdown hit, `CONTRIBUTING.md:226`, alongside the source string it quotes at `transition_close.py:291` — so those two Markdown passages ARE the population, and both are in scope. `templates/rebar-usage.md` and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not carry the claim (the `test_client_template_sync.py` drift gate covers only the marked rebar-usage region and forbids Gerrit content in it), so they are untouched.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md` — the single bullet at lines 235-242, rewritten as described above. No other line of
  the file changes.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §2f, lines 219-230: the same three corrections (not-merged, conditional,
  `--ref`), with the blockquote warning at lines 228-230 preserved verbatim.

No file under `src/` and no test file is edited. This is a documentation-accuracy change with no behaviour change, so there is no new testable behaviour to cover with a new test; the verification is that the existing doc-consistency tests still pass and that the corrected text matches the implementation, checked by the greps in the acceptance criteria below.

Assumption checked, not assumed: no test pins the wording being replaced. `tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py:11-13` slices AGENTS.md between `"**Codex Gerrit workflow rule:"` and `"\n\n## Record your work"`, which ends well before line 235; `tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py` and `tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py:166-167` assert only on the "Navigating the codebase" table; `tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` asserts only the DCO placeholder pattern. None reads the Git-workflow bullet or CONTRIBUTING.md §2f.

## Testing

No new test: nothing executable changes, and the module-size / doc-drift gates that do read these files are already in the suite. Verification is by targeted grep assertions (each exits non-zero on failure) plus the existing suite:

- `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` — the false claim is gone from both.
- `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` — the stacked-close tool is now named.
- `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md && grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md`
  — the shared-main-checkout warning survives in both (the phrase is on `AGENTS.md:241` and
  `CONTRIBUTING.md:229` today).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
  tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
  tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` — the doc-reading tests still pass.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — unaffected, run to confirm exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet no longer claims the precheck requires a MERGED commit; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md §2f no longer makes the same claim; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" CONTRIBUTING.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet states that the precheck runs only when the ticket records
      `file_impact`; verified by `grep -q "file_impact" AGENTS.md` exiting 0.
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet states that a referencing commit for the ticket OR any transitive
      descendant satisfies the check; verified by `grep -q "descendant" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 and
      by reading the bullet against `transition_close.py:277-286`.
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet documents `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the
      way to close a stacked story against its own commit without moving the worktree; verified by
      `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (it matches nothing today).
- [ ] The land-before-close ordering is attributed to the `Verified +1` policy rule rather than to
      the precheck; verified by the rewritten bullet naming `Verified +1` — `grep -c "Verified +1"
      AGENTS.md` is one greater than its current value of 3.
- [ ] The NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning is preserved verbatim in both files;
      verified by `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md` and
      `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md` both exiting 0, and by
      `git diff AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` showing those warning sentences unchanged.
- [ ] No source or test file is modified; verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main` listing
      exactly `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] The doc-reading tests still pass; verified by `pytest
      tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
      tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
      tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0 and `make typecheck` exits 0.
baseline.summary: AGENTS.md misstates the close precheck: it requires a referencing commit in HEAD's history, not a MERGED one, and omits --ref

# `main` is RED on the comment-hygiene gate: three rot-prone run-id references

## Symptom

`python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` fails on current `gerrit/main`:

    comment-hygiene: 3 rot-prone reference(s) found
      tests/external/test_provider_matrix_live.py:56  [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:1         [run-id]  30836378745
      tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py:152       [run-id]  30836378745

The gate runs in the `lint + type-check` job, which is one of the six gating jobs behind the `Verified` vote. **So every change pushed for review right now inherits a `Verified -1` it did not cause.** Observed on Gerrit change 1311, whose own (unrelated) hygiene violations were fixed and which still failed on these three.

## Cause

The references landed with story f124 (`9af278b01f` "live external suite covers many providers" and `1d75850974` "close the ambient-default provider leak"), which cite CI run `30836378745` in docstrings as the evidence for why each test exists.

They were presumably clean when written; the gate itself is recent (`f2b2d0b410` added it, and `d4095763e3` "Fix comment-hygiene acceptor path false-accept" TIGHTENED it). A gate that gets stricter after content lands will surface exactly this shape — pre-existing prose that was acceptable under the looser rule.

## Why the content is worth keeping, and what to do instead

These are not padding. Each docstring explains that the test exists **because a real leak shipped**, and the run id is the evidence. The gate's own message names the accepted alternatives: cite a resolvable ticket id, drop the token for durable prose, or mark it `context: external`.

Story f124 is the durable home for the run id. The fix is to keep the reasoning and cite f124 rather than the run number — the same edit ticket 39c1's cells took.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` exits 0 on `main`
- [x] the three docstrings KEEP their explanation of why each test exists — this is a citation
      change, not a deletion; a fix that removes the reasoning is a regression in a different
      direction
- [x] the run id is replaced by a reference a reader can still resolve (the f124 ticket)
- [x] no test behaviour changes: the suites that cover these files pass unchanged

## Note on ordering

Worth landing AHEAD of other in-flight changes, since it unblocks the `Verified` vote for everything currently in review.

baseline.description:
## Summary
Reported by a session using the new auto-lander (epic f1fa). When the serial auto-lander rebases a change to the current `main` tip (because `main` advanced under it — the common concurrent case), the rebase mints a NEW patchset. S1 deliberately made the `Autosubmit` label **non-sticky** (empty `copyCondition`) so `addPatchSet` cannot forge a stale land intent (security). But that same non-stickiness means the **bot's own rebase DROPS `Autosubmit`** — so the change no longer matches the selection query `status:open label:Autosubmit+1 is:submittable` and falls out of the lander's pool mid-flight. Under concurrent traffic this stalls the automatic land and forces a manual rebase — defeating the 'set it and walk away' goal.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Set `Autosubmit+1` on a submittable change while other sessions are landing (so `main` advances).
2. The bot selects it, then `main` advances → the bot rebases to the new tip (new patchset).
3. The new patchset has NO `Autosubmit` (empty copyCondition drops it).
4. On the next poll / a re-drive / a bot restart, the change is not `label:Autosubmit+1` → NOT re-selected → the land stalls; the agent must rebase + re-apply Autosubmit manually.

Expected: the bot's own rebase preserves the land intent, so the change keeps being driven to terminal (merged / handed back) without human intervention.
Actual: the bot's rebase drops Autosubmit; the in-flight land is orphaned across re-drive/restart under concurrent traffic.

## Root cause (design tension)
S1's non-sticky `Autosubmit` (anti-forgery: addPatchSet must not carry a land intent) collides with S2's rebase drive (which mints a new patchset). Within a single in-memory drive the wipChain still holds the change so my dogfood (#618) landed; the gap bites across a re-drive / hand-back / bot restart, where selection re-queries and the dropped label orphans the change.

## Fix options (to design)
- **Bot re-applies `Autosubmit` after its own rebase** (it holds the change in wipChain and the requester's intent is known/authorized): re-set `Autosubmit+1` (under the bot's or the original requester's identity) immediately after a successful rebase, so the change stays selectable. Must preserve the anti-forgery property (only the LANDER re-applies, keyed to an in-flight wipChain — a random addPatchSet still cannot forge it).
- OR the lander tracks in-flight intent durably in its own state (wipChain persisted) so selection does not rely on the live label surviving the rebase — re-drive/restart reads the durable intent, not `label:Autosubmit+1`.
- Either way: preserve the S1 security invariant (a forged addPatchSet cannot self-request a land).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The bot's own rebase does NOT orphan an in-flight land: after a lander rebase, the change remains driven to a terminal outcome without a human re-applying Autosubmit — verified by a test simulating main-advances-then-rebase across a re-drive, and a live check under concurrent traffic.
- [ ] The S1 anti-forgery invariant is preserved (a third-party `addPatchSet` still cannot carry/forge `Autosubmit`); documented + a config-check or test asserting it.
- [ ] ADR-0042 / land-contract updated with the chosen intent-persistence design.

## Notes
Discovered while dogfooding f1fa (a separate session hit the manual-rebase stall). Related: S1 (843b) non-sticky label; S2b (a9e3) rebase drive; the FFO rebase-treadmill (ADR-0040).
baseline.summary: Auto-lander: non-sticky Autosubmit dropped by the bot's OWN rebase stalls automatic landing under concurrent traffic

baseline.description:
# S6 — Clear the parity bar for Bedrock before it becomes a first-class provider

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py` defines rebar's non-inferiority bar — structured-output validity, per-criterion verdict agreement with zero decision-level flips on the gold set, recall and false-accept within 2pp, runtime error rate, and a gold-coverage floor. It was required before the last LLM substrate swap (LangGraph → pydantic-ai). Routing gate traffic through Bedrock is a substrate change of the same kind: a different API surface (Converse), different capability flags, and a different structured-output path. S8 (eb6e) cuts the production review bot over to Bedrock; without a measured bar, that cutover and the epic's "first-class provider" tier label are unearned assertions. This story produces the measurement S8 consumes.

## Approach

Add an opt-in, operator-run provider-parity harness modeled directly on the landed spot-eval precedent `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` — same parity bar, same epoch-majority aggregation, same committed-results-plus-offline-recheck shape. That precedent is the positive reason for the choice: it is the one pattern in this repo that has already run a paired, live, billable two-arm comparison through `parity.parity_report` and left reviewable evidence behind (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/fidelity_spot_eval_results.json`, re-scored offline by `tests/unit/test_fidelity_spot_eval.py::test_recorded_live_results_are_within_tolerance`). Copying a proven harness shape is cheaper and lower-risk than inventing a second one.

**Correcting an earlier claim in this plan.** A previous draft said "no new gate logic is written; wiring only". That is FALSE and nothing here relies on it. `parity_report` itself is pure and needs no change, but it has ZERO production callers — under `src/` the only references are its own definition and two internal reuses, `container_fidelity_report` and `prerequisite_fidelity_report` — and `run_eval` returns `{prompt, epochs, gate, passed, coverage, epoch_pass, junit}`, i.e. per-EPOCH pass/fail, not per-item decision + gold label (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:622-649`). The corpus→`ItemRecord` adapter, the repeat aggregation, the two-arm driver, the CLI and the results serializer are all NET-NEW and load-bearing, because criterion (b) "zero decision-level flips" is scored entirely on that mapping.

### Step 1 — the probe, before any corpus spend

The assumption most likely to sink the run is that the Bedrock inference-profile ids are invokable at all in THIS project's AWS account. Ticket 2932's operator correction records that every earlier Bedrock measurement was taken in a different account and region and assigns the re-measurement to this story; `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:26-28` records a real `AccessDeniedException` on `bedrock:InvokeModel`, and a plain on-demand id was refused with `ValidationException`. So step 1 is a probe, not the corpus: for EACH candidate inference-profile id, one ~8-token `aws bedrock-runtime converse` call in account 896586841071 / us-east-1 — the account of the terraform backend bucket `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` (`infra/terraform/versions.tf:14`) and the `aws_region` default `us-east-1` (`infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5`). Each id is probed TWICE: once with no sampling parameters, and once with `temperature=0`, the value the verifier path sends.

The probe is PER SLOT and its outcome is per slot — the two class slots ride independent profile ids, so "invokable" is not all-or-nothing:

- Both slots invokable → run both slots.
- Only one slot invokable → run that slot, record the other slot's EXACT refusal string as its finding, and
  record `frontier_measured: false` (or `standard_measured: false`) in the results file. A one-slot run is
  explicitly NOT a pass for the unmeasured slot; the unmeasured slot becomes an open question the epic's
  first-class claim must settle before S8.
- Neither slot invokable → no corpus spend at all; the refusals are the entire deliverable.

Worked example of the partial case: if `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` returns a normal completion but `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` returns `ValidationException: Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported`, then the run proceeds with the `standard` slot only; `provider_parity_results.json` contains a `standard` block with a real `ParityReport` and a `frontier` block of `{"measured": false, "refusal": "<the exact error string>"}`; and the ticket comment states that Bedrock cleared the bar at `standard` and is UNMEASURED at `frontier`.

If a `temperature=0` probe 400s where the bare probe succeeded, that id must carry `supports_temperature: False` in `capabilities._MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` before the corpus run. Both current opus candidates are ALREADY enrolled — `capabilities.py:126-129` lists `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (and their `global.` forms) with `supports_temperature: False`, and `runner.py:421-427` withdraws the parameter from the request on that basis — so the probe is expected to confirm an existing mechanism rather than discover new work. It is still run, because an id NOT on that list would 400 on every temperature-bearing case and silently convert a configuration defect into a validity / error-rate parity failure.

### Exactly one variable between the arms

Both arms run the SAME cases through the SAME `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.run_case` path; only the model string differs. The mechanism is `rebar.llm.config.gate_config(cfg)` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:93-101`): inside that scope `resolve_gate_config` returns the arm's config. This is load-bearing rather than incidental, because `runner._effective_config` substitutes `req.config.model` OVER the runner's own base config (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:182,209-212`) — passing a differently-configured runner alone would NOT flip the model. Wrapping each arm in `gate_config` makes the request config and the runner agree, so provider is the only variable and any criterion failure is attributable.

That mechanism reaches only the arms of `run_case` that resolve through `resolve_gate_config` — the plan-review criterion arm, the novelty arm and the code-review arm (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:103,155,229`). It does NOT reach the three agentic disposable-store arms: `completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality` and `spec-alignment` are dispatched to ops that resolve `config or LLMConfig.from_env(...)` directly — `operations.py:136`, `completion.py:331`, `spec_scan.py:68` — and `run_case` passes them no `config=`, so `gate_config` does not apply and both arms would read the same ambient model. **Those three specs are therefore excluded from the corpus**, so the provider split cannot silently collapse on any corpus item. (That divergence contradicts `resolve_gate_config`'s own documented invariant that "the ops call THIS, never `from_env` directly"; it is an existing defect in those three ops, out of scope here, and this story routes around it rather than fixing it.)

The gate's per-pass model ladder is likewise not in play: `RunRequest` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:70-118`) carries no model-class field, so a single-prompt eval case resolves `cfg.model` and nothing else. That is why this harness — rather than a paired `rebar review-plan` run — is the right instrument: the split-brain risk recorded earlier on this ticket (a bare `claude-*` ladder rung silently routing a "Bedrock" arm to direct Anthropic) cannot arise on this path.

### Arms and pairing

Same underlying model on both sides of each pair, named by class slot:

- `standard`: v1 `claude-sonnet-4-6` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:73`) ↔ v2
  `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:38`).
- `frontier`: v1 `claude-opus-4-8` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:67`) ↔ v2
  `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, subject to step 1 confirming it invokable.

Both slots are attempted because production uses both — frontier is the Pass-1 finder, standard is Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach. Certifying only sonnet would leave the frontier path, which does most of the gate's work, unmeasured, which is why an unmeasurable frontier slot is recorded as unmeasured rather than skipped silently.

### Corpus and the gold floor

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:88` sets `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20` and `parity_report` FAILS below it; no single eval spec's gold set reaches 20 (largest: `plan-review-container.eval.yaml`, 12). So the corpus POOLS gold-labelled dataset cases across specs. A case is eligible when its `expect` is in `{finding, fail, pass}` AND its solver id — the case's own `criterion` field when it has one, else the spec's prompt id — resolves to a non-agentic `run_case` arm. That yields a pool of 142 eligible cases across 15 specs. `finding` and `fail` map to the parity decision `block`, `pass` maps to `advisory` — the same two-bucket mapping `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` already uses.

The run takes a deterministic stratified sample: the first `finding`/`fail` case and the first `pass` case per spec, ordered by spec id then case id — **30 items, 15 gold-block and 15 gold-advisory** — with a recorded corpus digest in the shape of `fidelity_spot_eval.prerequisite_corpus_digest`. 30 clears the floor of 20, so **`min_gold` is NOT lowered**: `parity_report` is called with its default. The CI cost rail `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES` is deliberately not used: it truncates `dataset[:12]` per spec (`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:654-655`) and would decapitate the largest gold sources.

Worked example of one corpus item, so the adapter's contract is unambiguous: dataset case `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` in `plan-review-container.eval.yaml` carries `expect: finding` and `criterion: G3`, so it dispatches to the `G3` criterion arm and its gold `label` is `"block"`. Its three v2 epochs return findings / findings / no-findings, so `_verdict_decision` yields `block, block, advisory`, the majority is `block`, and the arm's record is `ItemRecord(valid=True, decision="block", label="block")` — a recall hit, not a flip. Had the v1 arm's majority been `advisory` on the same item, `parity_report` would emit `1 decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)` and `passed=False`.

### Repeats

`parity.ItemRecord`'s "averaged over the N repeats" is prose, not behaviour: `parallel_run_and_diff` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:286-302`) runs each item exactly once per runner with no repeat loop and no averaging. So this harness does NOT use `parallel_run_and_diff`. It runs its own N=3 epoch loop per case per arm and reduces to a majority decision (ties broken toward the cautious `block`), exactly as `fidelity_spot_eval.relocation_spot_eval(epochs=…)` and `_majority_decision` already do, then feeds the averaged paired `ItemRecord` lists straight to `parity_report`.

### Error classification

An epoch that raises is recorded as an errored `ItemRecord` and the comparison completes rather than aborting — but the serializer classifies the cause, so a configuration defect is never recorded as a parity verdict. A sampling-parameter rejection (a 400 naming `temperature`) and an authorization / validation refusal are counted and reported in their own fields, distinct from `decision_flips`. Any non-zero count of either makes the run INVALID for that slot rather than a Bedrock failure: it is fixed and re-run, not written up as non-inferiority evidence.

### Budget

At the both-slots ceiling: 30 cases × 2 arms × 3 epochs × 2 class slots = 360 case-runs, and every eligible arm is single-prompt (the agentic multi-call arms are excluded above), so at most 360 model calls — halved when only one slot is invokable, zero when neither is. Actual per-call model usage is still measured rather than assumed, via `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` — the rig `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml:83,110-112` already uses — and summarized into the recorded report.

### Not a GitHub Actions job

The harness is an operator-run module CLI, like `fidelity_spot_eval.main()`, which no workflow invokes. A CI job was the earlier plan and is rejected on grounded terms: the Bedrock grant in `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:57-72` is attached to the Gerrit **instance** role, and the only GitHub-OIDC role, `rebar-terraform-plan` (`infra/terraform/iam.tf:166-178`, assumed at `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:34-39`), is `ReadOnlyAccess` — so a CI arm would first require a new Bedrock-capable OIDC role, which is unfunded work outside this story. Auth is therefore the ambient AWS credential chain (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:10,55-88`) with `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1` set explicitly (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:569-571`), plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the v1 arm. Region is set explicitly because an unresolvable region otherwise surfaces as a bare boto3 `NoRegionError` from deep inside client construction (`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:67-87`).

### Decision-bearing

If Bedrock fails any criterion, or a slot cannot be measured, this ticket records that outcome and the epic's first-class claim for Bedrock is revisited before the S8 cutover proceeds, rather than shipping a tier label the evidence does not support.

### Out of scope — cited, not absorbed

The sub-4096-token "caching had NO effect" warning is miscalibrated on BOTH providers (bug 7a79-a920-afe7-40cf); it must not be read as a Bedrock caching regression when this run emits it. `MODEL_LADDER`'s equal sonnet/opus context limits (1157) and the mis-located escalation START rung for a non-Anthropic-family primary (48b3) affect ladder escalation, which this harness does not exercise. `infer_provider`'s `gemini` → `google_genai` mapping (5267) is unrelated to the `bedrock:` prefix. The three agentic ops' bypass of `resolve_gate_config` is worked around by corpus exclusion, not fixed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py` (new) — the corpus selector and digest, the two-arm `gate_config`
  driver, the epoch-majority `ItemRecord` adapter, the `parity_report` call, the error classifier, the results
  serializer, and the `main()` CLI including the per-slot step-1 invokability and temperature probes.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` (new) — the committed recorded run: per class slot
  either a `ParityReport` block or a `{"measured": false, "refusal": …}` block, plus each arm's resolved model
  id, the corpus digest, the epoch count, the error-classification counts and the per-arm call/latency summary.
- `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` (new) — the offline tests below, using `FakeRunner`.
- This ticket's comments — the quoted probe outcomes and `ParityReport` verdict.

## Testing

Offline, in `make test`, no model and no credentials:

- Happy path: two agreeing arms over a fixture corpus produce `passed=True` with zero decision flips.
- Failure path: a candidate arm that flips one gold decision produces `passed=False` and the emitted
  `gating_failures` names `decision-level flip(s) on the gold set`.
- Edge: a corpus below the gold floor fails on the coverage guard alone, mirroring
  `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py::test_goldless_run_fails_coverage_guard`.
- Edge: an arm whose runner raises records an `errored` `ItemRecord` and the comparison completes rather than
  aborting.
- Edge: a raised 400 naming `temperature` is counted as a sampling-parameter rejection and marks the slot
  INVALID, not as a decision flip.
- Edge: the corpus selector excludes every case dispatching to `completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality` or
  `spec-alignment`, and returns at least 20 gold items from the remaining specs.
- Recheck: the committed `provider_parity_results.json` is re-scored against the same parity bar with no model
  call, mirroring `test_recorded_live_results_are_within_tolerance`.

Live, opt-in, operator-run, never in default CI:

- Step 1, the per-slot probe: each candidate inference-profile id is invoked once bare and once with
  `temperature=0`, and both outcomes recorded, before any corpus spend.
- Step 2: the paired corpus run at N=3 per arm for each invokable slot, with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` used to assert
  the v2 arm made ZERO calls resolving to a non-Bedrock provider. Extract per-call model only from log lines
  carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`; a whole-log grep for the model id over-counts, because
  verdict-JSON fields match the same string.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The offline test module is green: `pytest tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` passes, covering the
      agreeing-arms, flipped-decision, below-gold-floor, errored-arm, temperature-rejection and
      corpus-exclusion cases.
- [x] The committed recorded-results recheck test passes with no model call, re-scoring
      `provider_parity_results.json` against `parity_report`.
- [x] `make test` passes with no AWS and no Anthropic credentials present.
- [x] The harness has no CI invocation: `grep -rnE '\bprovider_parity\b' .github/workflows/` returns no match
      (exit status 1).
- [x] The corpus selector returns zero cases dispatching to `completion-verifier`, `ticket-quality` or
      `spec-alignment`; verified by the corpus-exclusion offline test asserting an empty intersection.
- [x] `parity_report` is called with its default `min_gold` — the floor is never lowered — and the recorded
      `metrics["n_gold"] >= 20` for every measured slot; verified by the offline recheck test.
- [x] `provider_parity_results.json` carries, for EACH class slot, either a measured block with `passed`,
      `gating_failures`, the full `metrics`, both arms' resolved model ids, the corpus digest, an epoch count
      `>= 3` and the error-classification counts, or an unmeasured block with `"measured": false` and a
      non-empty `refusal`; verified by the offline recheck test, which fails if a slot has neither shape.
- [x] [operator-attested] Step 1's per-slot probe result for account 896586841071 / us-east-1 is recorded as a
      comment on this ticket: for each candidate inference-profile id, the bare-call outcome and the
      `temperature=0` outcome, each either a completion or the exact API error string. Evidence: the pasted
      `aws bedrock-runtime converse` outcomes.
- [x] [operator-attested] For each MEASURED slot, the live paired run's `ParityReport` is attached as a
      comment on this ticket as INFORMATIONAL EVIDENCE — the measured numbers for every `parity.py`
      criterion, plus per-arm latency. It is recorded, NOT gated on: verdict agreement, decision flips,
      recall and false-accept compare two DIFFERENT MODELS' judgements, which is out of this epic's
      scope. Non-determinism between models is expected and is not an S6 failure.
- [x] [operator-attested] PAYLOAD PARITY is proven: for the same logical call, the request that reaches
      the provider is equivalent across providers — same messages, same system prompt, same tool
      definitions — modulo provider-required envelope differences, which are enumerated. Evidence is a
      captured outbound request per provider, compared field by field, not a claim from reading code.
- [x] [operator-attested] TOOL PARITY is proven: the tool set offered to the model is identical across
      providers for the same call, evidenced from the captured requests.
- [x] [operator-attested] Every capability difference that legitimately alters the payload is EXPLICIT
      and recorded rather than silent — e.g. `temperature` being refused on opus and handled by the
      `supports_temperature: False` override. Any such difference found is named with its evidence.
- [x] [operator-attested] For each UNMEASURED slot, the comment states the slot is unmeasured and quotes the
      refusal, and explicitly does NOT claim parity for it.
- [x] [operator-attested] The v2 arm is proven provider-clean: the same comment records the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`
      per-call model tally showing zero non-Bedrock calls on the v2 arm of every measured slot.
- [x] [operator-attested] If PAYLOAD PARITY, TOOL PARITY or provider-cleanliness fails, or any slot is
      unmeasured, a comment on this ticket records the decision taken — remediate, or drop Bedrock's
      first-class claim. A model-judgement difference alone is NOT such a failure and does not trigger
      this criterion.
- [x] [operator-attested] The decision is carried to epic 061c-ecd1-8967-4a76 as a COMMENT, not a description
      edit. Tagged because a ticket field is not a repository file and the completion verifier reads repository
      files only. SEQUENCING HAZARD, and the reason this is spelled out rather than merely tagged: editing the
      epic's DESCRIPTION is a material edit that invalidates its plan-review attestation, and the epic closes
      last, after every child — so an edit made when this criterion naturally lands would force a fresh review
      of a very large plan at the worst moment. A comment is not material and carries the same information. If
      a description edit is later judged necessary anyway, make it BEFORE the epic's final review.
baseline.summary: S6 — clear the parity bar for Bedrock before it becomes a first-class provider

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan review certified epic `1386-5e7c-391d-4a74` and two of its children with zero blocking findings even though acceptance criteria across them were mutually unsatisfiable. Every contradiction surfaced later — mid-implementation or at the completion-verifier close gate — and each correction forced a full LLM re-review because amending a description invalidates the attestation as `stale-material`. Bug `creamy-cocksure-elkhound` records the evidence (seven instances in four failure classes). Until this lands, every plan author and every agent claiming a ticket keeps paying that late-detection cost.

## Approach

Two defects with two separate causes. They ship as one story because the second one's proving tests instantiate the container pass that the first one's registration also touches, so splitting them would duplicate that fixture and force one of the two to re-review against the other's change to `pass1.py`.

**(1) A new 1-TURN criterion `ac-satisfiability` (facet `coherence`).** It owns a concern no criterion owns today: whether a ticket's own acceptance criteria and its Scope / Out-of-Scope declarations can all hold at once. `COH` covers contradictions BETWEEN sections and explicitly disclaims within-section ones ("not within-section nitpicks (those belong to E1/E2)"); `E1` covers criterion-to-description mapping, terminology and duplicates; `F1` covers measurability. None asks whether the commitments are jointly satisfiable.

The rubric is written on a generic primitive rather than the motivating epic's subject matter: *an acceptance criterion quantifies over a set — universally ("no file under X matches P") or by cardinality ("the N items are migrated") — and something else in the same description places a member inside the excepted region.* It names three shapes of that primitive: universal-vs-carve-out (a Scope or Out-of-Scope clause exempts a member of the set an AC quantifies over); derived-artifact closure (an AC asserts a property of an artifact the plan says is regenerated from a source that keeps carrying the negation); and snapshot cardinality (an AC pins a count measured at authoring time for a set the plan says is discovered or recomputed at execution time).

Pass-2 already grades exactly this defect: `internal_conflict` is a live verifier axis (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py:255`) and a member of `_PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES` (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:309`). So the gap is confined to Pass-1 finding, and no verifier or impact-model change is part of this work. The criterion ships `advisory` at the `0.95` default; choosing a blocking posture needs replay data this change does not have yet.

Rejected: widening `COH` instead. It needs no new routing entry, but it puts two concerns in one single-turn scan and erases the boundary the rubrics police out loud. A separate routed criterion is also close to free: `registry.chunk_by_facet` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:434`) facet-sorts the single-turn tier then slices it into fixed-size chunks, so chunk count is `ceil(total / n)` and one added criterion changes the call count only when the applicable population is already an exact multiple of `n`. Single-turn chunks are never shed by the per-plan budget cap, so it cannot be starved on a large ticket the way an AGENT-tier alternative could.

**(2) Make `G3`'s child-coverage audit able to fire.** `G3` asks whether the union of children covers each parent acceptance criterion, and `plan_review_container.md` instructs it to flag an absence "only if NO sibling in the roster covers it". But the roster it is handed carries ids and titles only, which cannot discharge that burden, so the anti-false-positive rule correctly silences the finding every time. Give the roster each child's acceptance-criteria items, extracted with `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` (`src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py:96`) — the same helper the DET floor uses — and say so in `G3`'s rubric.

*Single-source the builder.* That roster is currently built by three independent copies of the same expression — every caller of `passes.pass1_container` that is not a test rolls its own:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:154` — the production path;
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:219` — the spot-eval harness, feeding it in
  at lines 251 and 260;
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:117-119` — the eval-fixture solver, where the expression
  is the fallback behind a `case.get("sibling_roster")` fixture override.

Changing only the production copy would leave the two eval paths sending title-only rosters while production sends AC-bearing ones. That matters beyond tidiness: those harnesses are what would generate the dogfooding data for `G3`'s deferred posture decision, so the divergence would corrupt the evidence for the next step. Extract one `build_sibling_roster(children)` helper and call it from all three.

It goes in `pass1.py`: that module already owns roster construction, it has ample room under the 800-LOC cap, and both other callers can reach it with no new import edge — `eval_solver.py:98` already does `from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA`, so the helper joins an import that exists. Rejected putting it in `passes.py`, which at 781 lines is too close to the cap to absorb a new helper. `eval_solver`'s `case.get("sibling_roster")` override stays ahead of the helper, so a fixture can still pin a roster verbatim.

*The rendered format.* `build_sibling_roster` emits one block per child: the existing `- <ticket_id>: <title>` line, followed by that child's `evaluate_plan_clarity(...).ac_items` entries each on its own line indented two spaces under it. A child with no parseable acceptance criteria keeps its `- <id>: <title>` line alone, so the roster degrades to today's shape rather than dropping the child. `G3`'s rubric refers to these indented items as the child's acceptance criteria.

*Where the roster is sent.* The roster is byte-identical across every pairing of one review, but it currently sits in `instructions` AFTER the per-pairing `children_block`, so it can never be part of a stable prefix. Fattening it in place would re-send the whole child acceptance-criteria corpus once per pairing, growing with the square of the child count. Instead send it once in the byte-stable prefix: in `passes.pass1_container`, build the system prompt as `_resolve_system(PASS_CONTAINER, parent_plan, cfg)` concatenated with a rendered roster block, and delete the roster from `instructions`. This is plain string concatenation on the already resolved system prompt — `_resolve_system` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:276`) keeps its current `(prompt_id, plan, cfg)` signature, `plan_review_container.md` gains no new template variable, and the roster stays a runtime value. In `passes.py` this is a move, not an addition: the roster leaves `instructions` as it joins the system prompt, holding that file flat against the cap.

*Count the roster in the prefix budget.* `parent_tokens` (`pass1.py:156`) is estimated from the parent plan alone, and it feeds three decisions: container bin-packing (`sizing.pack_container_bins`, `pass1.py:166`), the per-pairing size estimate (`pass1.py:168`), and the warm-then-fan-out gate `parent_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (`pass1.py:48`, `:187`). Once the roster is part of the prefix, it must be included in that estimate or bins can be packed over the window budget. Add it to the estimate.

Note the honest limit of the caching claim: sending the roster once in a byte-stable prefix makes it *cacheable* and stops it being re-sent per pairing, but whether a cache is actually written still depends on the prefix clearing `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (4096) and on there being at least two pairings. A larger prefix makes that gate more likely to pass, not less. The acceptance criteria below therefore assert the structural property (the roster is sent in the prefix, once, not repeated in per-pairing instructions), which is deterministic and testable, rather than a cache-hit rate.

Rejected for (2): making the new criterion agentic so it fetches siblings itself. Cross-child contradiction is already `G4`'s declared concern, so that would duplicate an owned concern and force AGENT cost onto the cheap check. `G3`'s posture and threshold are deliberately left untouched — revisiting them needs dogfooding data from this change.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_ac_satisfiability.md` — new: the criterion rubric
  (prompt id `plan-review-ac-satisfiability`, per the stem-underscores-to-dashes convention in
  `prompts._packaged_prompt_files`).
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` — rubric: discharge the sibling test against the
  roster's acceptance criteria.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `ac-satisfiability` routing entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `ac-satisfiability` to `CANONICAL_LLM`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the shared `build_sibling_roster` helper; include the
  roster in the `parent_tokens` prefix estimate.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` — call the shared helper instead of its own
  copy of the roster expression.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` — call the shared helper as the fallback behind its
  existing `sibling_roster` fixture override.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — move the roster from `instructions` into the system
  prompt.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated from the registry.
- `tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py` — new.
- `tests/unit/test_container_roster.py` — new.

## Testing

- Happy path: with `ac-satisfiability` registered, `validate_packaged_routing()` returns an
  empty list and `chunk_by_facet` places it in the facet-sorted `coherence` group alongside
  `COH` and `E1`.
- Happy path: the roster built for a parent whose children carry `## Acceptance Criteria`
  sections contains each child's criterion text.
- Wiring, end to end through Pass-1: drive the single-turn chunk path with a `FakeRunner`
  (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:111`) and assert the new criterion reaches the finder rubric and that
  a finding it emits survives criterion-attribution validation. This proves the criterion is
  actually wired into a review rather than only registered; judging its LLM accuracy is what the
  deferred dogfooding pass is for.
- Edge: a child whose description has no `## Acceptance Criteria` section yields a roster entry
  without raising.
- Empty: a parent with no children yields an empty roster without raising.
- Contract: all three non-test callers of `pass1_container` obtain their roster from the one
  shared builder, so they cannot diverge.
- Contract: `eval_solver`'s `sibling_roster` fixture override still wins over the builder.
- Happy path: the rendered roster puts each child's acceptance-criteria items indented under its
  `- <id>: <title>` line.
- Contract: the container pass sends the roster in its system prompt and not in its per-pairing
  instructions.
- Regression: the existing plan-review unit suite stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ac-satisfiability` is a registered plan-review criterion routed as `exec: "1-TURN"`,
      `facet: "coherence"`, `default_posture: "advisory"`; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_routing_entry` and by
      `validate_packaged_routing()` returning an empty list.
- [ ] Its rubric states the set-quantification primitive and names all three contradiction
      shapes (universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, snapshot cardinality), and does
      not reference the `Success Criteria` migration that motivated it; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_rubric_is_generic`.
- [ ] The criterion is exercised end to end through the Pass-1 single-turn chunk path against a
      `FakeRunner`, and a finding it emits survives attribution validation; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_reaches_pass1_and_attributes`.
- [ ] `explain_criterion("ac-satisfiability")` returns the criterion's non-empty guide section
      rather than raising `ExplainError`; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_ac_satisfiability_criterion.py::test_explain_returns_section`.
- [ ] Nothing under `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/` changes, because Pass-2's
      `internal_conflict` axis already grades this defect; verified by
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/` exiting 0.
- [ ] The sibling roster carries each child's acceptance-criteria items, not only ids and titles;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_carries_child_ac`.
- [ ] All three non-test callers of `pass1_container` (`pass1.py`, `fidelity_spot_eval.py`,
      `eval_solver.py`) obtain the roster from the single shared `build_sibling_roster` helper,
      and none retains its own roster-building expression; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_builder_single_sourced`.
- [ ] `eval_solver`'s `sibling_roster` fixture override still takes precedence over the shared
      builder; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_eval_fixture_roster_override_wins`.
- [ ] The rendered roster places each child's acceptance-criteria items indented beneath that
      child's `- <id>: <title>` line, and a child with no parseable criteria keeps its line
      alone; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_render_format`.
- [ ] A child description with no `## Acceptance Criteria` section, and a parent with no
      children, each produce a roster without raising; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_degrades_gracefully`.
- [ ] `G3`'s rubric instructs the reviewer to test "no sibling covers it" against the roster's
      acceptance criteria; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_g3_rubric_cites_roster_ac`.
- [ ] The container pass sends the roster inside its system prompt and not inside its
      per-pairing instructions; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_rides_prefix_not_instructions`.
- [ ] The roster's token cost is included in the `parent_tokens` prefix estimate that feeds
      container bin-packing and the warm gate; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_roster_counted_in_prefix_estimate`.
- [ ] `G3`'s `default_posture` and `block_threshold` are unchanged from their pre-change values;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_container_roster.py::test_g3_posture_unchanged`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` parity-checks clean against the registry; verified by
      `validate_criteria_guide()` returning an empty list.
- [ ] No `src/rebar/**/*.py` file exceeds the 800-LOC cap; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/unit` all pass.
baseline.summary: Plan review: own AC joint-satisfiability, and let G3's child-coverage audit fire

baseline.description:
# P2.3 — Tag convergence via delta events (TAG_DELTA)

## Context

`process_edit` applies tags as a **whole-field last-writer-wins** assignment
(`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:323` — `state["tags"] = new_value`). Every
current tag writer emits a whole-field `EDIT{fields.tags=[...]}`: `leaf.tag`/
`leaf.untag` (`_commands/leaf.py:85-92,107-114`), `composer.edit_core`
(`_commands/composer.py:314`, `tags` ∈ `_EDIT_FIELDS` :254), and the Jira
**inbound** applier (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py:426-431`). Two
clones concurrently adding different tags → one silently clobbers the other
(reproduced: EXP-R1). This is the bug the epic kills.

The dependency substrate is already in place: **P2.1 (HLC total order)** and
**P1.0 (canonical bytes)** are closed. Replay order is a deterministic total
order `(HLC-int, event-type-order, basename-incl-UUID)` (`reducer/_sort.py`), so
delta events resolve identically on every clone.

### Design (decided via brainstorm + 3 adversarial reviews; full trail in comments)

Replace tag mutation with **add/remove deltas** carried by ONE combined event
`TAG_DELTA {added:[...], removed:[...]}` — mirroring git-bug's
`LabelChangeOperation` (Added[]+Removed[] in one atomic op). After this change
**no upgraded interface emits a whole-field `EDIT.tags` ever again**; all four
writers above are rerouted to `TAG_DELTA`. Because no live `EDIT.tags` writer
remains, there is **no EDIT-vs-DELTA cross-type ordering** to reason about — so
**no first-delta boundary, no `tags_delta_owned` flag, and no
`process_snapshot`/compaction change** are needed. Legacy `EDIT.tags` survive
only as historical log entries (written before upgrade) and from un-upgraded old
clones during rollout; `process_edit`'s wholesale tags handling is left
UNCHANGED to serve them as the replay base.

**Deliberately NOT doing:** no dual-write (advisory tags self-heal on upgrade);
no OR-Set/tombstones; no case-folding (case-sensitive, git-bug parity); no
sort-on-apply (replay order already deterministic ⇒ cross-clone order already
identical). Outbound reconciler is unchanged — `_diff_labels` diffs REDUCED
state (`outbound_differ.py:825`), event-type-agnostic.

Prior-art grounding: git-bug (combined idempotent delta op, no-op suppression,
no set-op), notmuch/Taskwarrior (`+/-` delta grammar), GitLab/notmuch (explicit
separate set-op; GitLab filed clobber-set as a destructive bug twice),
Automerge/Akka (compile set→delta, add-wins).

## Implementation plan

1. **Event type + reducer core.** Define `TAG_DELTA = "TAG_DELTA"` in
   `reducer/_version.py` and reference it INSIDE both `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`
   (`_version.py`) and `EVENT_TYPES` (`_store/event_append.py` imports it) so the
   string cannot drift; update the human-readable type list in the
   `event_append` validation error string. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3
   (documentation only — forward-compat is governed by `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`, not
   the integer). Add `process_tag_delta(state, data)` beside `process_commits`:
   `isinstance(list)` guards on `added`/`removed`; remove-then-add so **add wins
   on intra-event conflict** (first-class, tested reducer invariant); idempotent
   on replay. Wire into the replay dispatch.

2. **Write surface (CLI / library / MCP).** Reroute `leaf.tag`/`leaf.untag` to
   emit `TAG_DELTA` (keep existing command-time no-op suppression). `edit_core`:
   add `--add-tag`/`--remove-tag`/`--set-tags`; `--set-tags=x,y` compiles to a
   delta vs locally-observed reduced state (`removed=observed−{x,y}`,
   `added={x,y}−observed`; convergent add-wins; `--set-tags=""` clears OBSERVED
   only). Mutual-exclusion errors (`--set-tags` with add/remove; same tag in both
   add+remove). Command-time no-op suppression; reject empty/whitespace/
   control-char tag names. **DROP `--tags` from CLI `edit`**; keep library/MCP
   `edit(tags=)` as a DEPRECATED alias for `set_tags` — extracted as a **pre-pass
   in `edit_core` BEFORE the `_EDIT_FIELDS` validation loop** (else the alias is
   rejected as an unknown field; `__init__.py:428` list→CSV and `mcp_server.py`
   both route through `edit_core`). MCP `edit_ticket` gains
   `add_tags`/`remove_tags`/`set_tags`; `tag_ticket`/`untag_ticket` rerouted.
   `create` keeps simple `--tags` (genesis CREATE base).

3. **Jira reconciler (inbound + intent set).** Reroute `apply_inbound`
   (`apply_inbound.py:359-432`) to emit a `TAG_DELTA` built from the add/remove
   ops it already computes (~404-416), carrying `source="inbound"` at `data.source`
   level; dedup `added∩removed`. Extend
   `local_label_intent._extract_tags_from_event` to handle `TAG_DELTA`: check
   `data.source=="inbound"` FIRST (return None), else fold ONLY `data.added` into
   the ever-seen union — NOT `removed` (subtracting would resurrect the a06c
   spurious-REMOVE bug). Removes the last live whole-field `EDIT.tags` writer.

4. **Forward-compat detection + docs.** Add a generic `fsck`/`bridge_fsck`
   warning when the store contains event-type files newer than the running binary
   understands ("upgrade required") — turns the silent old-clone rollout window
   into a visible signal. Docs: `docs/event-schema.md` (TAG_DELTA row,
   `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3, first body-changing type addition); `CLAUDE.md` tool set
   + CLI help (`--set-tags` clear-semantics warning); release note elevating
   "upgrade reconciler-running clones FIRST" to an enforced operational gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `TAG_DELTA` event type + constant registered (KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES,
      EVENT_TYPES, error string); SCHEMA_VERSION 3; `process_tag_delta` with
      defensive guards + tested add-wins invariant + idempotent replay
- [ ] CLI/library/MCP write surface emits `TAG_DELTA`; `--add-tag`/`--remove-tag`/
      `--set-tags` (compile-to-delta) + mutual-exclusion + no-op suppression +
      name validation; `--tags` dropped from edit, `edit(tags=)` deprecated alias
      via pre-pass
- [ ] Jira inbound applier emits `TAG_DELTA` (source=inbound, dedup); intent
      extractor folds only `added` for non-inbound deltas
- [ ] `fsck` flags unknown-newer event types; docs + CLI help + reconciler-first
      deployment gate updated
- [ ] Two-clone convergence + set-table + witnessed/unwitnessed-base +
      forward-compat (old reducer ignores TAG_DELTA) + reconciler tests pass
- [ ] Two clones concurrently `--add-tag x` ‖ `--add-tag y` → BOTH survive on both
- [ ] No upgraded interface (CLI, library, MCP, Jira inbound) emits a whole-field
- [ ] `--set-tags` is convergent (add-wins) and never silently eats a concurrent add;
- [ ] Jira round-trip works through deltas; a user-added (delta) tag is pushed
- [ ] Old clones never corrupt the store (preserve-and-ignore + compaction keeps
- [ ] Each child leaves the repo green (tests pass) on its own.

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` runs (cron hourly). Its "Install rebar" step runs `pip install .` — plain rebar, NO `[agents]` extra, and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the job env.

2. When the reconciler is healthy (`stale=false`) and an open `heartbeat-alert` ticket exists, the "Close alert ticket on recovery" step runs `rebar transition <id> open closed --reason "Fixed: ..."` under `set -euo pipefail`.
3. That close triggers the completion-verification close gate (`verify.require_completion_verification_for_close=true`), which requires the `[agents]` extra + a model API key.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the canary closes its own recovery/alert ticket and the job stays green; the heartbeat self-heals.

- Actual: the gate cannot run (no [agents]/key) -> fail-closed -> `rebar transition` exits non-zero -> the step (under set -e) fails -> canary job RED on every recovery, and the alert ticket (aa7b / luxe-adder-faith, P1) is stuck OPEN. The same defect affects the "Close binding-drift alert on recovery" step.
- A permanently-red canary defeats staleness alerting: a real outage becomes indistinguishable from the constant red.
## Root Cause

The canary manages bot-generated alert tickets, which are not work tickets with verifiable acceptance criteria; subjecting their auto-close to the completion-verification gate is wrong. The install also omits [agents].
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The canary recovery-close steps (heartbeat + binding-drift) close their alert tickets without tripping the completion-verification gate (e.g. `--force-close="Fixed: ..."`).
- [ ] The canary job is green when the reconciler is healthy and an alert ticket is being closed.
- [ ] Verified (dry-run / reasoning) that the recovery-close path no longer invokes the LLM gate.
- [ ] luxe-adder-faith (aa7b) is closed and does not recur on the next healthy cycle.

content.text: ## Why

Audit Reliability finding #4 (MEDIUM). In `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` `stage_and_commit`, `git add` (~L127-131) and `git commit` (~L132-136) run back-to-back and the failure paths only `_silent_unlink(final_path)` (the worktree file) — they never unstage the blob. So a failed write leaves its event **staged in the index**, and the next successful write (which commits the whole index) durably commits that phantom event. The claim/transition path already fixed this exact bug in `_commands/txn.py::_unstage` (~L98-114, `git reset -q -- <rels>`), called from its failure handlers (~L259, ~L441); the general append path never got the fix. Related (audit 2.2): `git commit` currently runs even when `git add` failed, because the add return code isn't checked before commit.
## What / files

- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: (1) check `add.returncode` and raise BEFORE running `git commit` (so a failed add can't let commit sweep unrelated staged residue under this write's message); (2) in both failure branches (add-failed ~L138 and unhealed commit-failed ~L157), run `git reset -q -- <relative_path>` (mirroring `txn._unstage`) in addition to `_silent_unlink(final_path)`, so the blob leaves the index as well as disk.

- Regression test in `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` (or a focused unit test): monkeypatch/inject a `git commit` failure on write A, then perform a successful write B, and assert (a) `git diff --cached` is empty after A fails and (b) replay/fsck contains only B's event, not A's phantom.
## Scope
In: event_append.py failure path + the add-rc-before-commit ordering; one regression test. Out: txn.py (already correct); any broader fsck redesign.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a stage/commit failure the event is removed from the index (`git reset`) as well as from disk (`_silent_unlink`) — asserted by `git diff --cached` being empty after an injected failure
- [ ] `git add`'s return code is checked and raises before `git commit` is invoked (verified by a test where add fails and commit is never reached / no commit is produced)
- [ ] Regression test: injected commit failure on write A followed by successful write B ⇒ store replay contains only B; fsck is clean
- [ ] `make test` green

baseline.summary: event_append: unstage the staged event on stage_and_commit failure (and check git add before commit)
