content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Pick a bound ticket with 0 comments on both sides (e.g. REB-5 / local
2. Add a LOCAL comment: `rebar comment <local_id> "local-origin"`.
3. Add a JIRA comment to the same issue: `acli jira workitem comment create
--key <REB-N> --body "jira-origin"`.
4. Run a reconcile pass (`rebar reconcile --mode live`).
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** bidirectional, additive comment sync — both sides end with BOTH
comments (2 in Jira, 2 in local).
- **Actual:** **Jira = 2 (outbound works), local = 1 (inbound BROKEN).** The
Jira-origin comment is never mirrored to local. `RECON: inbound_differ total=N
with_comments=0` — zero inbound comment imports, fleet-wide (not just this ticket).
## Root cause (confirmed in code)
- `inbound_differ.compute_inbound_mutations(jira_snapshot, binding_store,
local_by_id, outbound_mutations)` takes **no client**.
- `inbound_differ._diff_comments_inbound(jira_fields, local_ticket)` reads comments
from `jira_fields["comment"]` — but the live **search snapshot does NOT include
comment data** (Jira search omits comments; documented in `outbound_differ`). So the
inbound differ sees 0 Jira comments and imports none.
- The OUTBOUND differ DOES fetch comments (`client.get_comments`, for dedup) but that
fetched data is not shared with the inbound path. So outbound comment sync works and
inbound does not.
## Fix approach
Give the inbound comment path the Jira comments — e.g. (a) thread the outbound
differ's already-fetched comments into the inbound snapshot/`compute_inbound_mutations`,
or (b) pass a client to `compute_inbound_mutations` so `_diff_comments_inbound` can
fetch via `get_comments` (bounded, mirroring the outbound path), or (c) include comment
data on the snapshot entries the inbound differ sees (reuse the absent-alive GET path).
Outbound comments carry the `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` marker and dedup is by
`jira_comment_id`, so our own echoes are already filtered — the fix must not re-import
locally-originated comments.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A comment created directly in Jira (no reconciler marker, not already in local)
is mirrored inbound as a local comment on the next pass.
- [ ] The simultaneous case converges: 1 local + 1 Jira comment on the same ticket ->
2 comments in local AND 2 in Jira (no duplicates, no echo re-import).
- [ ] Locally-originated comments (carrying the echo marker / matching jira_comment_id)
are NOT re-imported.
- [ ] `inbound_differ ... with_comments` reflects real Jira-side comments (no longer
structurally 0 when Jira-side comments exist).
- [ ] RED->GREEN test: a Jira-origin comment yields an inbound add; an echo does not.

baseline.summary: Inbound comment sync broken: Jira-side comments never mirror to local (inbound differ has no comment data)

baseline.description:
## Why
Automate the FFO rebase-to-tip-then-submit so parallel agent sessions stop hand-rolling it and racing; serialize so the tested tree is always the merged tree with no thrash. **This racing is a live, active pain on this repo.**

## What
A single-instance project service (Python, project infra — NOT `src/rebar` core; `infra/autolander/loop.py` + a thin stdlib `infra/autolander/gerrit.py` helper) that, for the front `Autosubmit`+submittable change/chain: rebases to the current tip, awaits a fresh `Verified +1`, and ancestor-atomic submits the exact tested SHA. Holds a single in-flight `wipChain`.

**Poll cadence (design-fixed):** a fixed **15 s poll interval** (the "bot poll interval" S4/S5 reference) — picks up a new `Autosubmit` within ~15 s while staying gentle on the Gerrit REST API; distinct from `land`'s 30 s client poll. The bot writes its liveness heartbeat once per poll (S5 AC5).

**`submittable` under FFO (design-fixed):** under ADR-0040, Gerrit's `submittable` already requires descendant-of-tip, so a behind-tip change is *non-submittable* (`submittable=false`); a native `submittable=false` doesn't say *why* (behind-tip vs a failing vote) — the distinction S4's `needs_rebase` needs.

## Dependencies
Depends on **S1** (`sterilized-papery-horse`, 843b-801f-9ef9-442d) — the `Autosubmit` label + its **requester-votable ACL** (granted to group `Contributors`; the loop casts no votes, only *selects on* `label:Autosubmit+1`). **Runtime-provisioning relationship with S5** (`perpetual-ultrasonic-raccoon`, 3c55-2af3-0c9c-4b11): S5 provisions the bot's live credentials + Gerrit capabilities (Submit ACL, `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader`, SSM token) at deploy time. This is NOT a build-order `depends_on` (that would be circular — S5 depends on S2 to have a loop to containerize); the grants are runtime preconditions satisfied by S5's deploy.

## Scope
The core serial loop — decomposed into child tasks so each is loadable whole. **Failure paths** (CI-fail / rebase-conflict hand-back) are S3; deploy is S5; the agent command is S4.

## Acceptance Criteria (story-level; children carry the implementation detail)
- [ ] **Selection + rebase-routing** — child **S2a** (`89f9-b381-60e2-4802`): FIFO selection, RelatedChanges detection, rebase vs `rebase:chain` vs single-change routing, `rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader`, and the stdlib Gerrit helper.
- [ ] **Serialization + safety** — child **S2b** (`a9e3-580c-409c-4eee`): the single `wipChain` state machine, the FFO TOCTOU guard, the bounded `N=5` re-drive, and the CQ-style stack hand-back.
- [ ] **Land the tested tree** — child **S2c** (`1ccf-ca1e-f832-452e`): fresh `Verified` on every rebased chain member's own SHA, and the ancestor-atomic `POST /submit` on the tip.
- [ ] The bot reads existing `Verified` votes only and casts NO votes (no gate-semantics change in Phase 1) — the R5 invariant (tested tree = merged tree) holds across all three children.
baseline.summary: S2 Serial auto-lander core loop (rebase:chain -> await Verified -> ancestor-atomic submit)

content.text: RISK 2 (over-cap growth). `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` crossed the soft cap this window (745 -> 827) and was ADDED to the allowlist rather than split. Split along the front-matter seam so it drops back off the allowlist.
## What / files — careful split along the front-matter seam

- Extract the front-matter I/O cluster to a NEW `src/rebar/llm/prompts_frontmatter.py` (per `docs/architecture.md:219`): `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, plus the constants `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, the module-private regex `_FRONT_MATTER`, and the exception classes `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`. `PromptVersionError` subclasses `PromptError`, so both MUST move together (leaving the base behind would make the new module import `prompts.py` and cycle).

- The new module depends ONLY on the stdlib (`re`, `warnings`, lazy `yaml`) + `rebar.llm.errors` (for `LLMConfigError`, the base of `PromptError`). It MUST NOT import `prompts.py`, so there is no import cycle.
## Symbol disposition (explicit, to avoid implementer ambiguity)

- MOVE to `prompts_frontmatter.py`: `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `_FRONT_MATTER`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`.

- STAY in `prompts.py` (they cannot move — they call `resolve_prompt`/`get_prompt`/`load_prompt` or are only used there): `PromptNotFound` (subclass of the now-imported `PromptError`), `ReviewerError`, `EXECUTION_MODES`, `VOLATILE_MARKER`/`_BASE_MARKER`, the cache-split helpers (`split_volatile`/`strip_volatile_marker`/`resolve_prompt_cached`), `get_prompt`, `load_prompt`, `resolve_prompt`, `prompt_override_drift`, the index/catalog helpers, etc.

- `prompts.py` imports the moved cluster back from `prompts_frontmatter.py` (so its own functions — `get_prompt`, `load_prompt`, `prompt_override_drift` raise/parse via the imported names) AND re-exports them for back-compat.
## Re-export shim (preferred over editing call-sites)

Re-export is preferred over rewriting the ~6 call-sites because several callers use lazy/inline `from rebar.llm.prompts import ...` and updating them would scatter the diff across unrelated modules for no correctness gain. The shim MUST cover EVERY name imported elsewhere from `rebar.llm.prompts`, INCLUDING the private `_split_front_matter_raw` (imported cross-module by `prompt_library.py`). Re-export list: `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`, `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`. F401 is satisfied via an `__all__` entry (the repo's facade convention).
## External import sites that must keep working (verified by grep)

`src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py` (`PromptError`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` (`parse_front_matter`, `write_front_matter`, `PromptError`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/prompt_authoring.py` (`PromptError`, `write_front_matter`); `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` (`PromptError`); `tests/unit/test_prompt_front_matter.py` (`FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `parse_front_matter`, `write_front_matter`); `tests/unit/test_execution_mode.py` (`PromptError`). All keep importing from `rebar.llm.prompts` unchanged.
## Docs to update (no stale references after the split)

- `docs/architecture.md` (~line 219): update the `llm/prompts.py` offenders-table remedy row to state the front-matter I/O now lives in `prompts_frontmatter.py` and `prompts.py` re-exports it, and drop `prompts.py` from the "over-cap" set. Remove `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`.
- Grep the tree for any other reference describing `prompts.py` as holding the front-matter cluster and fix it.
## Rollback / expand-contract sequencing (reversible)

1. Create `prompts_frontmatter.py` with the cluster and add the re-export imports to `prompts.py` WITHOUT yet deleting the originals; run the full suite. 2. Then remove the original definitions from `prompts.py` (now provided by the re-exports); run the suite again. If step 2 surfaces a runtime ImportError, revert ONLY the deletion — `prompts.py` with re-exports still behaves as before. The whole change is one commit, revertible wholesale.
## Scope
In: front-matter cluster extraction + re-export shim + the doc/allowlist updates above. Out: changing the prompt schema or resolution logic (byte-for-byte behavior preserved).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `prompts_frontmatter.py` created (>=100 LOC) holding `parse_front_matter`, `_split_front_matter_raw`, `write_front_matter`, `_refuse_newer_schema_version`, `FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `PROMPT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `_FRONT_MATTER`, `PromptError`, `PromptVersionError` — and NONE of these definitions remain in `prompts.py` (only re-export aliases).
- [ ] `prompts.py` drops BELOW 800 LOC and is REMOVED from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`.

- [ ] Public AND cross-module-private symbols (incl. `_split_front_matter_raw`) remain importable from `prompts.py` (re-export) — every external import site above still imports unchanged; no caller breakage.
- [ ] `prompts_frontmatter.py` does not import `prompts.py` (no import cycle); `prompts.py` imports the cluster from it.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` offenders table updated to the post-split two-file layout; no stale reference to `prompts.py` holding the front-matter cluster survives a grep.
- [ ] The prompt front-matter / drift-gate tests pass (`make lint` + `make test`).

baseline.summary: Risk 2: split prompts.py front-matter cluster (drop off allowlist)

content.text: ## Why

Audit Maintainability finding #3 (MEDIUM). Many `REBAR_*` env vars are read across ~133 sites; only ~42 sit in the intended config modules — the rest scattered (worst in the reconciler), with no single artifact enumerating them. The repo already solved this shape (the derived prompt-index + its regenerate-and-diff CI drift gate).
## What / files

- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` with a `scan(root: Path) -> Registry` core (root defaulting to `src/rebar`, parametrized so tests can point it at a temp dir) and a `--check` mode. It resolves env reads through an EXPLICIT, FACTUALLY-PINNED set of patterns; completeness is defined RELATIVE to this set, which the generated doc header lists verbatim (no unqualified "captures everything" claim):
1. **Direct stdlib literals** — `os.environ["X"]`, `os.environ.get("X", …)`, `os.getenv("X", …)` with a string-literal key.

2. **Project env-read helpers** — a `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` table mapping helper name → (0-indexed position of the env-name argument, name prefix), resolving the string-literal name arg at each CALL SITE. Signatures verified against the current tree:
- `_rebar_env(name, default=None)` — arg 0, prefix `REBAR_` (outbound_differ, outbound_fields, inbound_translate, rebar_id_audit, apply_inbound, apply_handlers)
- `_env_int(name, default, *, minimum=None)` — arg 0, no prefix (outbound_differ, binding_store)
- `_str_pref(env_name, file_key, default, repo_root)` — arg 0, no prefix (llm/gate_source.py)
- `_int_pref(table, env_name, file_key, default)` — arg 1, no prefix (_snapshot/janitor.py)
- `_llm_str(table, cli, env_name, file_key, default)` / `_llm_int(table, cli, env_name, file_key, default)` — arg 2, no prefix (llm/config.py)

- `_int_env(name, default)` / `_severities_env(name, default)` — arg 0, no prefix (review_bot/config.py; the Gerrit review-bot's operator env vars, e.g. LLM_REVIEW_MAX_VALUE, BLOCKING_SEVERITIES, RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS, BOT_USER — GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN is a direct os.environ read, covered by pattern 1)

(These are the bespoke env-read wrappers in the tree, including review_bot's; `_llm_bool`/`_env_str` do NOT exist and are NOT listed.) A helper call whose env-name arg is not a string literal is emitted in a "dynamic/unresolved (see source)" section rather than dropped.

3. **Alias/deprecation status** — from `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` REGISTRY (`via="env"` entries: `REBAR_NO_SYNC`→`REBAR_SYNC_PULL`, `COMPACT_THRESHOLD`→`REBAR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD`). `REBAR_PUSH` / `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` were removed pre-1.0 and are NOT emitted.
The doc header enumerates exactly the scanned patterns/helpers (honest scope). Extending coverage = adding a helper row to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` (one line).
- `docs/env-vars.md`: the committed generated artifact.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`: an "Env-var registry drift gate" step modeled on the "Prompt-index drift gate" (~L224-240): `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check`, failing on drift.
- A pointer to `docs/env-vars.md` in the `docs/README.md` index (Operator section).
## Scope

In: the generator (parametrized `scan(root)` + the pinned `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` resolver + `--check`), the committed doc, the CI drift-gate step, the docs/README.md pointer, a unit test. Out: consolidating scattered reads into config modules; adding/removing any env var; capturing reads through helpers NOT in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` (documented in the header as the scanned scope; extend by adding a row).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` is committed; `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` regenerates it with NO diff (`git diff --exit-code` clean); its header enumerates the scanned patterns/helpers

- [ ] POSITIVE capture (unit test `tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py`): the registry produced by `scan(src/rebar)` contains a known direct read (`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` or similar), the `_rebar_env("RECONCILER_VERBOSE")` read resolved to `REBAR_RECONCILER_VERBOSE`, and the `_llm_int(..., "REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT", …)` read
- [ ] ALIAS assertions (same test): `REBAR_NO_SYNC` appears with its `_deprecations` alias annotation; `REBAR_PUSH` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` are ABSENT (no phantom rows)

- [ ] DRIFT (same test): `scan()` over a TEMP dir containing a synthetic `.py` with `os.environ["REBAR_FAKE_NEW"]` includes `REBAR_FAKE_NEW` (so drift is genuinely detectable), and `--check` against the committed tree exits 0
- [ ] A drift-gate step exists in test.yml; `docs/README.md` links `docs/env-vars.md`; `make lint` green

# Wire store-wide overlap step into _run_plan_review (LLM-gated, graceful skip, advisory) + ADR

## Why
The overlap check fires in the tolerant window before claim — during plan review — folding results into the output as advisory coaching, WITHOUT ever blocking the claim or altering the claim-gate verdict. This is the integration seam tying enrichment + retrieval + judge into the workflow, and it delivers the epic's ADR.

## What
- Integrate in `_run_plan_review` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:401` — the real post-pass site where rising-floor/completion-floor/sidecar/signing run; NOT the wrapper `review_plan` at :352). Overlap findings go in a SEPARATE `overlap[]` verdict key, EXCLUDED from the advisory cap and from the signed `coverage['counts']` — so the ≤3 overlap items never displace real plan-review advisories and the attestation is byte-identical whether overlap is on or off. (This resolves the earlier "inject before counts are baked" tension: we do NOT touch the baked counts at all.)
- Steps: synchronously extract the query ticket's digest by calling S1's `enrich` on the plan-review orchestrator's already-assembled ticket context (the same whole-ticket text `_run_plan_review` passed to its own passes — title+description+comments), so no extra store read is needed, run `retrieve` (S5), run the pairwise `judge` (S6) — the no-embeddings retrieval is justified by the epic's recall experiment (digest-BM25F recall@20 = 1.0), so no embedding index is needed; attach ≤3 results to `overlap[]`. This injection happens AFTER `sidecar.emit()` and the attestation signing, so `overlap[]` is never part of the signed sidecar/coverage (reinforcing verdict-unchanged). Each item is exactly S6's surfaced-finding shape: `{counterpart_id: str, relation: "duplicates"|"supersedes"|"depends_on", shared_artifact: str, confidence: number, link_command: str}`. Whether a candidate is 'overlapping enough' to appear is decided ENTIRELY by S6's aggregation rule (both orderings agree + cited artifact + ≥overlap_conf_threshold); S7 does no thresholding of its own.
- **CLI:** update `_render_plan_review_text` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:386`) to print the `overlap[]` section.
- **MCP:** the `review_plan` MCP tool is `NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT` (returns a plain dict, no `outputSchema`, per `_mcp_llm.py:174` / `schemas/__init__.py:110`) — so there is NO output schema to update; `overlap[]` simply rides in the returned dict. (Corrects the earlier plan text.)
- **Gate/skip:** if `[agents]`, plan-review, or the API key is absent → silent no-op (no `overlap[]`, no error, claim proceeds). Runtime failure in S1/S5/S6 (exception, timeout, empty candidates) → caught, empty `overlap[]`, logged, never blocks.
- **Config flag:** `overlap_enabled` (default OFF) — a BOOL on the `VerifyConfig` dataclass (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `[tool.rebar][verify]`, alongside `require_plan_review_for_claim`) WITH its companion entry in `_SECTIONS["verify"]` (`= _as_bool`) — omitting the `_SECTIONS` entry silently drops the key. (`overlap_enabled` is the ONLY overlap key in `VerifyConfig`; all tunables live on `LLMConfig` per the other stories.)
- **ADR:** write `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md` capturing Cupid-digest-without-embeddings (+ the recall/latency/cost experiment evidence), event-store-as-enrichment-queue, digest-as-REVIEW_RESULT-sidecar, and overlap-at-review-time-not-as-a-5fd2-criterion. This is the epic's ADR deliverable.

## Dependencies
S1 (enrich), S5 (retrieve), S6 (judge). Sequenced LAST. NOTE: S3 also edits `plan_review/__init__.py` (the certification/enqueue path); this story edits `_run_plan_review` (a different function) — S7 lands after S3 to avoid a merge conflict (depends_on S3).

## Scope
- Edits: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (`_run_plan_review` injection), `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` (`_render_plan_review_text`), `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (`VerifyConfig.overlap_enabled` + `_SECTIONS["verify"]` entry), `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md`.
- **NO schema edit** (resolves the earlier contradiction): `overlap[]` rides in the returned plan-review dict WITHOUT touching `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json`, which already declares `"additionalProperties": true` (verified) — so the extra `overlap` key validates without a schema change, and the MCP tool is `NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT` anyway. Do NOT add `overlap[]` to the schema file; `test_verdict_schema_accepts_overlap` asserts a verdict dict carrying `overlap[]` still validates against the UNCHANGED `plan_review_verdict` schema.
- OUT: component ops (S1/S5/S6), async enrichment (S2/S3/S4).

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py` (FakeRunner + fixture corpus): `test_surfaced` (≤3 in `overlap[]` with link commands); `test_verdict_unchanged` (signed coverage/attestation byte-identical vs overlap-off); `test_query_digest_at_review_time` (digest built from current full text, corpus-independent); `test_graceful_skip` ([agents]/key absent → no `overlap[]`, verdict identical); `test_runtime_error` (judge raises → empty `overlap[]`, no block); `test_flag_off` (`overlap_enabled=off` → skipped); `test_render` (`overlap[]` in CLI text + MCP dict).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `review_plan` returns ≤3 findings in a dedicated `overlap[]` key (each with a `rebar link` command); claim NEVER blocked; signed coverage/attestation byte-identical to overlap-off; `pytest ...::{test_surfaced,test_verdict_unchanged}`.
- [ ] Query digest generated at review time from current full text, independent of the enriched corpus; `::test_query_digest_at_review_time`.
- [ ] `[agents]`/plan-review/key absent → silent no-op, verdict identical; runtime S1/S5/S6 failure → empty `overlap[]`, logged, never blocks; `::{test_graceful_skip,test_runtime_error}`.
- [ ] `overlap_enabled` (bool, default OFF) on `VerifyConfig` WITH its `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer gates the step; `::test_flag_off`. `overlap[]` rendered in CLI text and present in the MCP dict (no schema change — tool is NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT); `::test_render`.
- [ ] The ADR `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md` is written (epic's ADR deliverable), citing the concrete experiment figures (recall@20 = 1.0, single-query 0.69 ms @ 800 digests, ~$1.90 one-time enrichment for 793 tickets) from the epic's experiment comment.
baseline.summary: Wire store-wide overlap step into review_plan (LLM-gated, graceful skip, advisory surfacing)

content.text: ## What
Enrich the tests overlay prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`) with the full
behavioral-testing standard ported from DSO: BOTH halves — the recall patterns to flag AND the
FP-discrimination guards — per the locked principle that the domain rubric lives in the OVERLAY,
never in the generic Pass-2 verifier (`code-review-verify.md` stays domain-blind). Base NOT-flag
auto-downgrade rules do not apply to test-correctness findings (a test overlay must still judge test
quality). DO THIS FIRST to prove the overlay-authoring + eval pattern before the other five
specialists (all six are children of da8a).
### Mechanism (resolves plan-review block)
These are NOT new code protocols — they are REVIEW-GUIDANCE PROSE authored into the overlay prompt
body (the `<!--volatile-->`-preceding instructions of `code-review-tests.md`), the same way the base
+ existing overlays carry their rubric. The overlay LLM applies them when emitting/withholding
findings; the generic Pass-2 verifier receives NONE of this. The eval (recall + no-fire) is the
enforcement: a no-fire case per FP-guard proves the overlay does not over-suppress-or-over-fire.
### RECALL patterns the overlay must flag (test antipatterns)
- change-detector: asserts an internal name/structure/state; would break on a behavior-preserving
refactor (Rule-4 litmus: "would this break if internals were renamed without a behavior change?").
- tautological: asserts the mock's OWN configured return value (verifies the mock framework, not the
code). BEFORE flagging, apply the INVERTED-TRACE disproof: mentally invert the condition under
test; if the assertion would then fail, the test IS catching real behavior — drop the claim.
- over-mocking: mocks a module INTERNAL to the unit under test (asserts internal structure).
- under-mocking: does NOT mock an external boundary (DB/network/clock/third-party) → nondeterministic.
- source-grepping: greps/reads the SOURCE UNDER TEST as an assertion (tests text, not behavior).
- existence-only: a standalone `test -f <file>` with no structural-contract purpose (change-detector).
### FP-GUARDS the overlay must honor (the three named protocols, defined)
1. **Four-Criterion Test** — a test-coupling finding may be raised (as more than a `minor` style
nit) ONLY when at least ONE defect criterion holds: (a) Refactoring violation — breaks on a
safe refactor that preserves observable behavior; (b) Tautological assertion — asserts a
test-configured mock return (subject to the inverted-trace disproof above); (c) Isolation failure
— cross-test state / fixture pollution / order dependency / network/wall-clock leak; (d)
Regression blindness — cannot detect a regression in the specific behavior this diff introduces.
When NONE hold (the assertion targets observable output, exercises real code, survives refactor,
no isolation issue), it is a philosophy disagreement → suggestion at most, not a defect.
2. **Rule-5 structural-artifact exception** — `grep`/`awk` over a NON-executable INSTRUCTION artifact
(a `.md` skill/agent/contract/prompt, a workflow YAML, project config, a manifest/index) for a
required heading, canonical identifier, or section is a STRUCTURAL-BOUNDARY assertion and is
VALID — it is NOT the source-grepping antipattern (which applies ONLY to grepping SOURCE CODE
UNDER TEST). Litmus: the grepped token is a contract iff a NON-HUMAN consumer (a parser/validator/
downstream grep/registry/CI-runner that branches on the exact value) reads it; an LLM is NOT a
non-human consumer, so prose/heading greps guarding wording ARE change-detectors.
3. **VALID-patterns-not-to-flag** — do NOT raise a finding on any of these (they are valid by the
standard): (i) observable post-condition assertions (incl. when the unit is the sole producer of
the post-condition); (ii) Rule-5 structural greps on instruction artifacts; (iii) greps of
COMMAND OUTPUT (stdout/stderr/exit code of the executed unit); (iv) table-driven / equivalence /
classifier tests, incl. exact-value assertions on a pure function's output that "look
tautological"; (v) exit-code / emitted-signal assertions; (vi) mocks at the EXTERNAL boundary;
(vii) coverage-gap demands (not blocking findings on their own).
## Files
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md (enrich the overlay prompt body — recall + FP-guards)
- src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml (already exists from f93a; ADD recall cases
for change-detector / over-mocking / source-grepping / existence-only, and no-fire cases for the
Four-Criterion philosophy-disagreement, a Rule-5 instruction-artifact grep, a table-driven exact-
value test, and a boundary mock — each a valid pattern the overlay must NOT flag).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `code-review-tests.md` overlay carries BOTH the recall patterns (change-detector, tautological
w/ inverted-trace, over/under-mocking, source-grepping, existence-only) AND the three named
FP-guards (Four-Criterion Test, Rule-5 structural-artifact exception, VALID-patterns-not-to-flag).
- [ ] `code-review-tests.eval.yaml` gains recall cases (new antipatterns) AND no-fire cases (one per
FP-guard family) and validates offline (`rebar prompt eval code-review-tests` parses/loads);
the overlay does not over-suppress valid patterns nor over-fire on them.
- [ ] The overlay remains ADVISORY; NO domain test-rubric leaks into `code-review-verify.md` (the
generic Pass-2 verifier prompt is unchanged by this story).

baseline.summary: tests overlay: full behavioral-testing standard

# Cloud's three whole-project readers have NO multi-page test — the same class fixed three times on DC

## Claim

`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`'s `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map` and `get_issuelinks_map` each paginate a whole project through an opaque `nextPageToken` cursor at `page_size = 100`. **No test exercises more than ONE page.** The only coverage, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200`, feeds payloads carrying `"isLast": True` — a single page, terminating immediately.

This is the SAME defect class that shipped three times on the DC/shared side and was fixed each time only after it was found in production-shaped code:
  * change 1105 — `get_parent_map` advanced by the REQUESTED page size and stopped on a short page;
  * [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map`, the same bug;
  * [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] — `fetcher._iter_pages`, which lost 92% of a snapshot when measured.
The Cloud copies of these three readers have never been tested past their first page.

## Why the risk is real rather than theoretical

* The cursor contract is genuinely stateful: `acli_graph.py:271-272` terminates on `isLast` OR on a
  null/absent `nextPageToken`, and the request echoes the token back at `:225`. Nothing asserts the
  cursor ADVANCES, that a second page is fetched and merged, that a null token stops the loop, or
  that a repeated token cannot spin forever.
* A silent truncation here is invisible: these are whole-project READS feeding the differ, so the
  symptom is missing parents / comments / links, not an error.
* DC now has exactly these tests (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:66-128`, recovering 250
  items from a 20-cap client) plus a structural AST guard at `:166`. **That guard scans the DC
  transport source only**, so a fourth unpaginated caller cannot be added silently on DC and CAN be
  on Cloud.
* Live coverage does not compensate: the live Cloud tier exercises a real project, but nothing pins
  the working set above 100 issues, so a passing live run is not evidence the cursor loops.

NOTE the fetcher-level guard is NOT this. `fetch/test_fetcher_truncation_gate.py` covers the FETCHER's search loop (same-token-twice / offset-stall). These three `acli_graph` readers are a separate code path with a separate cursor.

## Provenance

Found by a Cloud-vs-DC test-parity audit commissioned while closing epic e369, not by a failure. The audit's framing is worth keeping: the DC side has been heavily tested recently, so the parity gap runs in BOTH directions — this is the largest instance of Cloud lacking what DC now has.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a test drives each of `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map` against a
      fake ACLI client whose working set EXCEEDS one page, and asserts EVERY item is recovered —
      a count comparison against the seeded set, not a `> 0` floor
- [x] the cursor is asserted to ADVANCE: the second request carries the token the first response
      returned, asserted on the recorded request bodies
- [x] termination is asserted on BOTH documented conditions independently — `isLast: True`, and a
      null/absent `nextPageToken`
- [x] a repeated cursor token does NOT loop forever (mirrors the fetcher's same-token-twice guard);
      it either raises or stops, and the test pins which
- [x] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED: breaking the loop after the first page must turn it RED,
      recorded on this ticket with the verdicts
- [x] the structural anti-regression guard is extended to cover `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`, so a
      fourth unpaginated whole-project reader cannot be added silently on EITHER deployment
baseline.summary: Cloud whole-project readers (parent/comment/issuelinks maps) have no multi-page test

content.text: ## Summary
set-file-impact / set-verify-commands accept arbitrary array elements — only array-ness is validated, so junk violating the documented element contract is stored and flows downstream.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar set-file-impact <id> '[42, "string"]' -> exit 0; get-file-impact -> [42, "string"]
2. rebar set-file-impact <id> '[{"reason":"no path"}]' -> exit 0
3. rebar set-verify-commands <id> '[{"x":1}]' -> exit 0
4. Control: non-JSON and non-array inputs ARE rejected.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected (help text): "JSON array of {path,reason} objects" / "{dd_id,dd_text,command}".
- Actual: any array contents accepted; junk reaches show/list/--output llm payloads and (once bug vamp-floor-mica is fixed) the scheduler's conflict detection.
## Source
src/rebar/_engine/ticket-lib-api.sh:1027-1036 (file_impact), :1194-1201 (verify_commands) — validation stops at jq type == array.
## Fix direction

Per-element jq validation: every element an object containing the required string keys; reject with exit 1 naming the first offending index. Preserve current empty-array semantics. Validated jq expression + [] behavior in the implementation-notes comment. Sequence with/after vamp-floor-mica (relates_to link exists).
## Suggested RED test
Each malformed shape above -> exit 1 with index in message; valid arrays and [] -> accepted; round-trip via get-* unchanged for valid input.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Element-level validation on both setters (RED tests per malformed shape first)
- [ ] Error names the offending index and the required keys
- [ ] [] semantics preserved; valid-input round-trip unchanged
- [ ] MCP set_file_impact/set_verify_commands surface the same rejection cleanly

# The completion-verifier close gate FAILS OPEN on an LLM provider error: the ticket closes with no attestation

A close whose completion verifier dies mid-run **succeeds anyway**, leaving the ticket `closed` with no `completion-verifier` attestation. The same gate FAILS CLOSED when the provider package is merely absent. Two failure modes of one dependency, opposite outcomes, and the one that lets work through unverified is the one that fires when the provider is reachable but unhappy.

## Observed

Closing epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb`:

    rebar.llm.errors.LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed: status_code: 400,
    model_name: us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0,
    'The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 64000.
     Try again with a maximum tokens value that is lower than 64000.' (ValidationException)

    ...and then:  UNBLOCKED: none          exit code 0

Result:

    rebar show e369-a449-4773-48fb  ->  status: closed
    attestation kinds present:          ['plan-review']
    completion-verifier:                ABSENT

## Contrast — the same gate fails CLOSED for a neighbouring cause

Earlier in the same session, with the bedrock provider package not installed, three closes were correctly REFUSED:

    Error: cannot close 1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda: completion verification could not run
    (... a bedrock model/provider is configured but the optional bedrock provider package is not
    installed ...). Override with --force-close="<reason>".

So the gate KNOWS how to refuse. A missing package refuses; a 400 from the provider does not.

## Why this is worse than a flaky gate

The whole point of the completion verifier is that a human or agent cannot mark work done without an independent check. A gate that disappears exactly when the provider is degraded is a gate that is absent precisely when nobody is watching closely — and it leaves NO signal on the ticket. The ticket reads `closed`; only the absent attestation and a stack trace scrolled past in the terminal distinguish it from a verified close.

This is the same silent-success shape epic e369 spent its life removing from the Jira bridge, now in the gate that is supposed to certify that removal.

## Two defects, and they are separable

1. **Fail-open on provider error.** `LLMUnavailableError` during completion verification must
   refuse the close, exactly as the missing-package path does, and say so.
2. **The 400 itself.** A `max_tokens` above 64000 is requested against
   `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, whose ceiling is 64000. Bedrock rejects it
   outright, so the trivial-class model is unusable for this step as configured. Likely fallout
   from defaulting local dev to Bedrock — the direct-Anthropic path evidently tolerated the same
   request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a completion verifier that raises `LLMUnavailableError` REFUSES the close, with the same
      remedy text and `--force-close` escape hatch the missing-package path already prints
- [ ] a test pins the refusal, driving the verifier to raise rather than asserting on a mock's
      call count
- [ ] the `max_tokens` request is clamped to the configured model's ceiling, or the step is not
      routed to a model whose ceiling it exceeds
- [ ] epic e369's close is re-verified once the gate works, or its close is explicitly accepted
      without a completion attestation and that decision is recorded on the ticket
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier close gate fails OPEN on an LLM provider error: the ticket closes with no attestation

## Why

The migration must be validated WITHOUT trusting LLM output equivalence (the review is
LLM-dependent and variable). Epic A shipped a `PlannedTraceRunner` (`workflow/trace.py`) that
records each call's INTENDED shape offline. Epic B uses it to prove the workflow and the bespoke
implementations issue the SAME plan — the safety net that lets B5 cut over with confidence.

## What

Build a planned-trace parity harness that runs BOTH the bespoke gate and the new engine workflow
(B2 plan-review, B3 completion-verification) OFFLINE via the Fake runner over a DIVERSE scenario
corpus, and asserts PLANNED-TRACE parity — NOT result parity. The planned trace is the ordered set
of intended execution events: `[DET-check-id | (criterion/prompt-id, INTENDED model, call-mode
agent|1-shot) | deterministic-step-id]`. Parity is asserted on the PRE-ESCALATION planned trace
(tolerating runtime size-ladder escalation divergence), capturing the INTENDED/selected model (not
the fake's echoed `model=None`). The harness runs in CI (no live calls, no credentials).

## Scope

- A parity harness + a diverse OFFLINE scenario corpus (varied ticket shapes: container vs leaf,
  with/without overlays, code-grounded criteria, oversize, missing AC, etc.).
- Trace normalization that ignores ordering noise from concurrency but pins prompt-id + intended
  model + call-mode + deterministic step ids, pre-escalation.
- A CI-run test asserting parity for both gates across the corpus.
- Depends on B2 + B3 (both implementations must exist to diff).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A parity harness runs the bespoke and workflow implementations of BOTH gates offline
      (FakeRunner) over a diverse scenario corpus and asserts identical PRE-ESCALATION planned
      traces (prompt-id + intended model + call-mode + deterministic step ids).
- [ ] The harness captures the INTENDED/selected model (not the fake's echoed field) and tolerates
      runtime size-ladder escalation divergence by asserting pre-escalation only.
- [ ] The parity test runs in CI with no live calls / no credentials; the scenario corpus covers
      container/leaf, overlays on/off, code-grounded, oversize, and missing-AC cases.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: B4: Planned-trace parity harness (bespoke vs workflow, offline corpus, CI)

baseline.description:
## Problem

GitHub code scanning reports TWO OPEN high-severity alerts — the only open alerts on the repository:

    81  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:249  high
    82  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:250  high

Both are this pattern in `test_a_fallback_entry_endpoint_is_built_against_that_endpoint`:

    assert str(model.models[1].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")
    assert not str(model.models[0].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")

`startswith` on a URL is not a host check. `https://fallback.test.evil.example/` satisfies it, because the attacker-controlled part sits AFTER the prefix the assertion pins. The rule is right about the pattern.

## Honest severity assessment

CodeQL rates these high because the rule cannot distinguish test code from production code. In context the exploitability is nil: the string is a hard-coded constant in a unit test, no untrusted input reaches it, and nothing branches on the result except the assertion itself. So the real defect is not a vulnerability — it is a WEAK ASSERTION. The test means "this model was built against that endpoint" but checks "the base_url starts with these bytes", which would also pass for a different host sharing the prefix. Fixing it makes the test say what it means AND clears the alert, so the two goals coincide and there is no reason to dismiss instead.

Do NOT resolve this by dismissing the alerts, and do NOT add a suppression comment: the assertion genuinely is weaker than intended.

## Approach

Compare the URL ORIGIN exactly rather than by prefix. Parse both sides with `urllib.parse.urlsplit` and compare `(scheme, netloc)` as a tuple — exact equality has no substring semantics for CodeQL to flag and no prefix ambiguity for a reader. `startswith` was presumably chosen because the client normalises the configured endpoint (e.g. appends a trailing slash), which whole-string equality would break; comparing the parsed origin keeps that tolerance without keeping the weakness.

Single-source the endpoint constant so the configured value and the asserted value cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both assertions compare the parsed URL ORIGIN (scheme + host) by exact equality, and no
      `startswith`/`in` substring check against a URL remains anywhere in the file.
- [x] The test still FAILS if the fallback entry is built against the provider default instead of the
      configured endpoint — the property the test protects is preserved, verified by running it.
- [x] A host that merely shares the configured endpoint as a prefix
      (e.g. `https://fallback.test.evil.example`) does NOT satisfy the assertion, pinned by a test or by
      the construction of the comparison itself.
- [x] After the fix lands and CodeQL re-runs, `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` reports
      ZERO open `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` alerts.
- [x] No alert is dismissed and no suppression comment is added — the code is changed.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: CodeQL high: incomplete URL substring sanitization in the fallback-endpoint test

baseline.description:
Integrate mandatory security declarations into brainstorm, preplanning, and implementation-plan so security concerns are addressed at planning time — not discovered at code review.

## Mandatory Declarations

Every planning workflow must verify the following security declarations exist before implementation begins:

### 1. Endpoint Access Level Declaration
Every endpoint must explicitly declare its access level: **public**, **authenticated**, or **internal**. Ambiguity (not intentional public) is a planning failure, not a code review finding.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan task generation — every task creating an API endpoint must include an access_level field in its acceptance criteria
- **Preplanning check:** Security reviewer flags stories involving new endpoints without access classification

### 2. PII Encryption-at-Rest Plan
Every data field touching PII must have an encryption-at-rest plan before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during gap analysis, any epic involving user data collection must identify PII fields and their encryption strategy
- **Implementation-plan check:** Tasks creating database models or data stores with PII fields must include encryption acceptance criteria
- **What to declare:** Field name, PII category (name, SSN, DOB, address, etc.), encryption method (column-level, volume-level, application-level), key management approach

### 3. External Integration Threat Model
Every external integration must have a threat model entry before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Brainstorm — during the scrutiny pipeline, any epic involving external APIs, third-party services, or data exchange must produce a threat model entry
- **What to declare:** Integration name, data exchanged, trust boundary, authentication method, failure mode (fail-open vs fail-closed), data residency implications

### 4. Agent/Sub-Agent Permission Scope
Every agent or sub-agent must have a declared permission scope.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks dispatching sub-agents must declare permitted tools, file access scope, and network access
- **Preplanning check:** Stories involving multi-agent orchestration must include permission boundaries in done definitions
- **What to declare:** Permitted tools list, file/directory access scope, network access (none/internal/external), credential access (none/scoped/inherited)

### 5. User Input Validation Strategy
Every user input path must identify its validation strategy before implementation.
- **Where enforced:** Implementation-plan — tasks accepting user input must declare validation approach in acceptance criteria
- **What to declare:** Input type, validation method (allowlist/denylist/regex/schema), server-side enforcement (mandatory), max length, encoding/escaping strategy for output contexts (HTML, SQL, shell, etc.)

## Integration Approach

### Brainstorm
- Gap analysis phase should check for PII fields and external integrations in the epic scope
- Scrutiny pipeline should flag epics touching user data or external services that lack security declarations
- Success criteria should include security declarations when applicable

### Preplanning
- Security concern area scan (Phase C) should verify each story has the required declarations based on its scope
- Stories without required declarations should be flagged as incomplete

### Implementation-Plan
- Task acceptance criteria library should include composable security declaration blocks
- The 5 parallel reviewers should include a check: "Does every task with [endpoint/PII/integration/agent/input] have the corresponding security declaration?"
- Tasks missing declarations should fail the plan review gate

## Government Context
These declarations map to federal compliance requirements:
- Access levels → NIST 800-53 AC (Access Control) family
- PII encryption → NIST 800-53 SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest), NIST 800-122
- Threat models → NIST 800-53 RA-3 (Risk Assessment), FedRAMP requirements
- Permission scopes → NIST 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege)
- Input validation → NIST 800-53 SI-10 (Information Input Validation), OWASP Top 10
baseline.summary: improve security criteria used during plan review

baseline.description:
## Idea: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gate the agent cannot self-satisfy

### Problem

rebar's start-work and completion gates are enforced in-process by the same runtime the agent drives, and their escape hatches are reachable by the agent itself. In particular, `rebar review-plan --force` bypasses the plan-review claim gate, and it is CLI-invocable by an autonomous agent. Recent real-world drift (session `5eb0` / epic `708d`): an agent, acting on a vague human instruction, rationalized repeated `--force` plan reviews of blocked tickets rather than deferring — each individually plausible, collectively defeating the gate's intent (mint no signed attestation against not-yet-final dependencies). 2026 research frames this precisely:

- *Ambig-DS* (arXiv 2605.09698) — under-specified tasks produce **silent commitments** to
  plausible-but-unintended framings; the bottleneck is recognizing underspecification.
- *Bayesian and Motivated Reasoning in AI Agents* (arXiv 2608.00339) — framing/priors
  "neither specified in the task nor visible in the decision record" silently drive conclusions.
- *Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance* (arXiv 2608.01558) —
  "sequences of individually permissible actions may collectively violate system-level
  constraints"; safety must be a **verifiable property of the runtime**, not "an optional
  layer of guidance."

The common thread: any approval an agent can *produce* it can *rationalize producing*. A robust HITL gate must be one the agent structurally **cannot replicate**, only *request*.

### Proposed direction (to be designed via the brainstorm protocol before any build)

Add a HITL approval primitive to rebar that gates a configurable set of consequential / policy-overriding operations (initial candidates: `review-plan --force`, force-close, limit changes to `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, and any future `--force` escape hatch) behind an approval token that:

1. **Is unforgeable by the agent** — the approval is bound to a secret/authority the agent has
   no access to. Sketches to evaluate (prior-art review required, per the brainstorm skill's
   "interrogate novelty" step): a detached signature over the request payload made with a key
   held only by a human/CI identity (mirroring the existing plan-review attestation signing but
   with a *separate, agent-inaccessible* key); a Gerrit-style out-of-band vote by a
   non-agent account; a one-time approval nonce minted by a human-operated command.
2. **Is request/grant-separated** — the agent can only emit a *request* (payload = operation,
   target ticket(s), reason, base SHA). Granting happens in a channel the agent cannot drive;
   the agent then presents the returned token, which rebar verifies against the
   agent-inaccessible authority before allowing the operation.
3. **Is bound and non-replayable** — the token is scoped to the exact operation + target +
   content hash + a short expiry, so a grant for one action cannot be reused for another
   (defeats the "series of individually-plausible forces" pattern; cf. trajectory assurance).
4. **Fails closed and is auditable** — absent/invalid/expired/stale token → operation refused;
   every request and grant is recorded as ticket/session-log events for the decision record
   (directly answering the "not visible in the decision record" finding).

### Explicitly OUT of scope for the primitive itself
- Replacing the existing signing/attestation machinery (this *complements* it with an authority
  the agent cannot hold).
- Deciding *which* operations require HITL — that policy surface is a follow-on decision; this
  idea establishes the mechanism and a minimal initial op set.

### Why an idea, not an open ticket
This needs a full brainstorm pass (purpose / problem / edge cases / implementation) and a prior-art review (existing human-approval / four-eyes / signing-authority patterns, and why OSS agent frameworks do or don't gate self-escalation) before it is claimable work. Promote `idea -> open` and author child stories once the design is settled and the plan-review gate can be satisfied.

### Acceptance criteria (for the eventual design, not this idea)
- A documented threat model showing the agent cannot mint a valid approval token by any
  in-process or CLI path available to it.
- The gated operation set is config-driven and fails closed.
- Request + grant + verification are recorded as durable, queryable events.
baseline.summary: HITL approval gate the agent cannot self-satisfy (unforgeable human approval for --force / policy-overriding ops)

Graduate src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py (867 LOC, over the 800 soft cap) off the module-size allowlist by extracting the cryptographic-identity & signed-attestation fold cluster into a NEW pure, stdlib-free leaf src/rebar/reducer/_processors_identity.py.

MOVE (by name): _fold_author_attribution, _rederive_keyring_keys, process_key_event, _bootstrap_genesis_keyring, attestation_kind, process_signature. These reference only each other (a true leaf): process_key_event calls _rederive_keyring_keys; process_signature calls attestation_kind and _fold_author_attribution. _processors.py imports them back and re-exports them (# noqa: F401) so rebar.reducer._processors.<symbol> keeps resolving for the reducer dispatch table (_replay.py imports process_key_event + process_signature from ._processors) and for attestation_kind's importers (signing.py, _commands/verify_opcert.py, _opcert_signing.py, and tests). reducer/__init__.py needs no change.

DEVIATION from the docs/architecture.md offenders row: that row names the seam _processors_keys.py with ONLY the 4-function keys cluster and explicitly flags it SUB-FLOOR (~84 LOC, below the 100-LOC leaf floor). This ticket WIDENS the seam to also move the attestation pair (attestation_kind + process_signature) so the new leaf clears the 100-LOC floor, and names it _processors_identity.py. _fold_author_attribution MUST travel with process_signature (its caller) into the leaf, else a back-edge cycle forms. The sub-floor _processors_keys.py row is stale/superseded and is DELETED by this ticket.

This is a pure/mechanical refactor: no signature or logic changes; E5 testing-plan is not-applicable — the existing reducer/attestation/signing test suites are the oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New leaf src/rebar/reducer/_processors_identity.py is in [100,800] LOC. Verified by: `lines=$(wc -l < src/rebar/reducer/_processors_identity.py) && [ "$lines" -ge 100 ] && [ "$lines" -le 800 ] && echo "ok ($lines lines)"`.
- [ ] src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py is <=800 LOC (down from 867). Verified by: `lines=$(wc -l < src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py) && [ "$lines" -le 800 ] && echo "ok ($lines lines)"`.
- [ ] The 6 named symbols live in the leaf and are re-exported (# noqa: F401) from _processors.py so back-compat holds. Verified by: `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors import process_key_event, process_signature, attestation_kind, _fold_author_attribution, _rederive_keyring_keys, _bootstrap_genesis_keyring; print('ok')"`.
- [ ] _processors.py removed from .github/module-size-allowlist.txt and .github/module-size-ceilings.txt. Verified by: `! grep -q '_processors.py' .github/module-size-allowlist.txt && ! grep -q 'reducer/_processors.py ' .github/module-size-ceilings.txt`.
- [ ] The stale offenders-table row is deleted from docs/architecture.md. Verified by: `! grep -q _processors_keys docs/architecture.md`.
- [ ] make lint passes (ruff check + ruff format --check). Verified by: `make lint`.
- [ ] tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py passes (allowlist == over-cap set == ceilings keys). Verified by: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py -q`.
- [ ] The reducer/attestation/signing suites pass. Verified by: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py tests/unit/test_signing.py tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py -q` and `python -m pytest tests/unit -k 'reducer or attestation or signing' -q`.

content.text: ## Why
The single `state["signature"]` slot is last-writer-wins, so one kind clobbers another.
This is the root-cause fix and the riskiest slice (back-compat + compaction), done first.
It is ADDITIVE and behavior-preserving: it introduces the `attestations` map without
changing any existing signature/mirror semantics, so it is safe to ship before the gate
migration (929e).
## What
Add `state["attestations"]`, a kind-keyed map (per-key LWW, like `process_workflow_run`).
`process_signature`:
- MIRROR (unchanged semantics): `state["signature"] = record` for EVERY SIGNATURE event,
EXACTLY as today — including a blank/retired event (manifest=[], retired=True), which
still clears the mirror. This preserves 100% of current behavior for the four existing
`state.get("signature")` consumers and for `retire_attested_pin` (which stays in this
slice; it is removed only in 929e, together with the reopen-aware validity that replaces
it — so there is NO window where reopen-invalidation is missing).
- MAP (new, additive): if the event is kindable (non-empty manifest with a derivable kind),
also set `attestations[kind] = record`. Kind = SIGNED `manifest[0]` substring before the
first ":" (authoritative); `data["kind"]` is used only as a hint iff it matches, else
ignored. A blank/retired/unkindable event is SKIPPED for the map (it stays out of the
map; it does not and cannot clear a kind). Nothing in this slice READS the map yet, so the
map's presence is inert until cc1b/929e wire consumers to it.
Also add `state["last_reopened_at"]` (in `process_status`): the timestamp of the most recent
`closed -> open` transition (pre-update status == "closed" and target == "open"); null if
never. (Consumed by compute_validity in 929e; recorded here so the data exists.)
Read fold-in: an OLD SNAPSHOT whose compiled_state carries only `signature` (no
`attestations`) is folded into the map on restore, under the kind derived from that
record's own `manifest[0]` (dropped if blank/unkindable). New SNAPSHOTs carry BOTH
`attestations` and the `signature` mirror automatically (the reducer maintains both).
`_present.py` `public_state()`: add a DEDICATED `attestations` branch stripping the
`signature` (HMAC hex) subkey from each per-kind record (the flat `_INTERNAL_SUBKEYS`
cannot express a wildcard kind level); retain the legacy single-`signature` strip.
114f owns the canonical per-record shape.
## Scope
`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (`process_signature`, `process_status`,
`process_snapshot`), `src/rebar/reducer/_present.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`,
`ticket_state.schema.json`. No change to the signed payload; no change to retirement /
mirror semantics; `retire_attested_pin` untouched here.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `attestations` map added; `process_signature` sets the mirror for EVERY event (old semantics preserved, incl. blank/retired clearing the mirror) AND additively sets `attestations[kind]` only for kindable events.
- [ ] Kind from authoritative `manifest[0]`; `data["kind"]` only a validated hint; blank/unkindable events skipped for the map (never clobber a kind).
- [ ] `state["last_reopened_at"]` records the most recent closed->open timestamp (null if never).
- [ ] Old-snapshot fold-in files the legacy record under its manifest-derived kind (dropped if blank/unkindable); new SNAPSHOTs carry both map and mirror.
- [ ] `public_state()` dedicated `attestations` branch strips HMAC hex from every per-kind record; legacy strip retained; no hex in show/MCP.
- [ ] Compaction/SNAPSHOT round-trips all kinds; empty `attestations` omitted; `retire_attested_pin`/mirror semantics unchanged in this slice.

baseline.summary: Reducer + state model: attestations{} kind-keyed map

baseline.description:
## Problem

`MODEL_LADDER` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`) is the context-limit escalation ladder. Two of its three rungs declare the SAME window:

    ("claude-haiku-4-5",   200_000),
    ("claude-sonnet-4-6", 1_000_000),
    ("claude-opus-4-8",   1_000_000),

Escalation exists to retry on a LARGER context window after a context-limit failure. A sonnet -> opus escalation gains **zero** additional context. The retry that follows is therefore guaranteed to hit the same limit and fail again — but at opus pricing, and after a second full round-trip.

Reproduced by running the code (not by reading the table):

    models_at_or_above('claude-sonnet-4-6') = ['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-8']
    window at sonnet rung = 1,000,000; window at opus rung = 1,000,000; gain = 0

## Why it is not merely wasteful

The failure is silent and self-confirming. The escalation reports that it moved to a larger model, the second attempt fails with the same context-limit error, and nothing in the trace says the two rungs were the same size. An operator reads it as "even opus could not fit it", which is a different and more alarming conclusion than the true one: "we never actually escalated".

The wasted spend is the smaller harm. The misleading diagnosis is the larger one.

## The numbers are CORRECT — the design is wrong

The ticket's option 3 ("correct the numbers if either figure is simply wrong") is **ruled out by measurement**, not by assumption. Both figures were verified against the provider's own live Models API (`client.models.retrieve(...)`, field `max_input_tokens`), which is the authoritative per-model capability source:

| rung                | declared | `max_input_tokens` (live API) | verdict  |
|---------------------|----------|-------------------------------|----------|
| `claude-haiku-4-5`  | 200_000  | 200,000                       | correct  |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6` | 1_000_000| 1,000,000                     | correct  |
| `claude-opus-4-8`   | 1_000_000| 1,000,000                     | correct  |

Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 genuinely share a 1M window. The table is honest; the ladder's *use* of it is not. So the fix is option 2 — escalation must SKIP a rung that is not a real capacity increase — and **not** option 1 (dropping the opus rung), because the rung is a truthful ladder entry that `largest_window_tokens` and the model-class vocabulary (task 7761) both legitimately read.

This also means the originally-drafted AC2 ("`MODEL_LADDER` windows are strictly increasing") would assert a falsehood about the real world and would force option 1. It is replaced below by the two guards that are actually true and actually prevent the defect.

## Scope — distinct from its neighbours

* **48b3** (merged) owns rung LOCATION (which rung the walk starts from for a non-Anthropic
  primary).
* **7de4** owns rung TARGET (resolving a rung through the model-class vocabulary).
* THIS ticket owns the ladder's CONSUMPTION — whether consecutive proposed rungs represent a real
  capacity increase at all. Independent of both; can land in any order.
* **e3cd** owns `capabilities.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`. Different constant, not touched here.

## Approach

Two functions, because there are genuinely two questions and today one function answers both:

* `models_at_or_above(model)` — "which ladder rungs sit at or above this one?" Contract and
  return value **unchanged**. Task 7761's regression suite observes escalation-target resolution
  through exactly this function (provider stickiness on Bedrock, byte-for-byte bare ids with no
  classes configured, cheapest-first / frontier-last ordering). Narrowing it in place would delete
  the frontier rung from all three of those observables and gut coverage that is not this ticket's
  to weaken.
* `escalation_rungs(model)` — **new**: `models_at_or_above(model)` with rungs that buy no
  additional context removed. This is what a context-limit retry loop should consume, and the name
  says so at the call site.

The filter rule: the START rung is always kept (it is the operator's own model, not an escalation); every rung above it is kept only if its declared window is **strictly greater than the last KEPT rung's**. Comparing against the last kept rung rather than the immediate predecessor keeps the filter correct for a future ladder with several equal-window rungs in a row.

Both context-limit escalation loops switch to the new function, so the defect is fixed in both places rather than one:

* `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` — the Pass-1 size ladder.
* `prerequisites.run_focused_finder` — a one-line change; its existing `ladder.index(model) + 1`
  and `IndexError` handler already yield the correct input-too-large indeterminate when the
  filtered ladder runs out.

Resulting escalation rungs (declared-window filter; targets still resolved through the model-class vocabulary exactly as today, so provider stickiness is unaffected):

| primary               | `models_at_or_above` (unchanged) | `escalation_rungs` (new) |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `claude-haiku-4-5`    | haiku, sonnet, opus              | haiku, sonnet            |
| `claude-sonnet-4-6`   | sonnet, opus                     | sonnet                   |
| `claude-opus-4-8`     | opus                             | opus                     |
| `None` (absent)       | haiku, sonnet, opus              | haiku, sonnet            |
| unlocatable primary   | [that model] (48b3)              | [that model]             |

Dropping the opus rung from *escalation* is safe and correct: the rung is only ever reached after `is_context_limit_error`, and a retry at an identical input window (1M) and identical max-output (128K) cannot succeed where the previous attempt failed. It is a guaranteed-failing paid call. `largest_window_tokens` still reads the FULL ladder and is deliberately left unchanged — its job is "the largest window reachable", which is still 1M, so P8's size budget does not move.

Because `models_at_or_above` is untouched, **no existing test changes its expected values.** The change is additive.

## Implementation

1. `sizing.escalation_rungs(model)` — new; wraps `models_at_or_above` and drops any rung whose
   MODEL_LADDER-declared window is not strictly greater than the last kept rung's. Rung windows are
   looked up by the same bare-name substring match `largest_window_tokens` already uses, so a
   class-retargeted (e.g. Bedrock-qualified) target resolves to its rung's window. A target whose
   rung window cannot be determined is KEPT, never silently dropped — escalation is a recovery path
   and must not become a new failure mode (the same principle `_rung_target` already applies).
2. `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` — iterate `escalation_rungs(cfg.model)` instead of
   `models_at_or_above(cfg.model)`.
3. `prerequisites.run_focused_finder` — one line: `ladder = sizing.escalation_rungs(model)`.
4. Export `escalation_rungs` in `sizing.__all__` alongside `models_at_or_above`.
5. No change to `MODEL_LADDER`'s contents, to `largest_window_tokens`, or to
   `models_at_or_above`'s behaviour.

## Test plan (RED first)

New tests in `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py`:

* **The discriminating escalation test.** Asserting `window == 1_000_000` does NOT distinguish
  sonnet from opus and would pass for the wrong reason. The tests therefore assert on rung
  IDENTITY and on the observed per-attempt model sequence, never on a bare window number:
  - `escalation_rungs("claude-sonnet-4-6") == ["claude-sonnet-4-6"]` — opus, by name, absent,
    while `models_at_or_above("claude-sonnet-4-6")` still returns both rungs.
  - Driven through `pass1_with_ladder` with a runner that records `req.config.model` per attempt
    and always raises a context-limit error: the recorded sequence for a sonnet primary is
    exactly `[sonnet, sonnet]` (batch + one single-criterion retry) and contains no opus id —
    i.e. the paid no-op call is not made.
* **Structural guards** (replacing the drafted AC2):
  - MODEL_LADDER declared windows are **non-decreasing** across consecutive entries — a future
    edit cannot introduce a rung that offers *less* context than the rung below it.
  - For every rung, the windows of `escalation_rungs`'s returned sequence are **strictly
    increasing** — a future edit cannot reintroduce a no-op escalation, whatever the table says.
    This is the guard that actually enforces the fix, and it holds even though the table itself
    has two equal-window rungs.
* **Haiku control (AC4).** The real increase is preserved: `escalation_rungs("claude-haiku-4-5")`
  == `["claude-haiku-4-5", "claude-sonnet-4-6"]`, and a haiku-primary run still escalates onto
  sonnet (observed via the recorded per-attempt model sequence, not just the returned list).
* **Non-regression control.** `models_at_or_above` is unchanged, pinned by re-running
  `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` (task 7761's suite) untouched and green.

MUTATION CHECK both directions: with the filter reverted the new escalation/guard tests must FAIL; with the filter in place the full pre-existing selection must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A context-limit escalation never proposes a rung whose declared window is equal to or
  smaller than the current rung's. Enforced by `sizing.escalation_rungs`, which BOTH context-limit
  escalation loops (`pass1_with_ladder`, `prerequisites.run_focused_finder`) consume.
- AC2: Two structural guards are asserted by test: (a) `MODEL_LADDER` declared windows are
  non-decreasing across consecutive entries, and (b) the windows of the rung sequence returned by
  `escalation_rungs` are strictly increasing from every start rung. Adding a no-op rung fails (b).
- AC3: Both window figures are verified against the provider's published limits, the plan states
  which figure was confirmed and how (live Models API `max_input_tokens`), and the resulting
  decision — numbers correct, filter the consumption — is recorded above.
- AC4: Escalation for a haiku primary (a rung that IS a real increase) still climbs onto sonnet,
  pinned by test; `models_at_or_above`'s own contract is unchanged, pinned by task 7761's existing
  suite passing untouched.
- AC5: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default selection is green, each
  judged by exit code on a clean working tree.
baseline.summary: MODEL_LADDER's sonnet and opus rungs share a 1,000,000 window, so context-limit escalation buys nothing at opus pricing
