## Context

Band-A (A3) auto-remediation drove SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT to zero on the shared store but, by
design, LEFT the order-sensitive, human-triage faults for manual reconciliation. As of
2026-07-11 `rebar fsck` reports **17** such faults: **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** (pre-snapshot EDIT
events absent from the snapshot's `source_event_uuids`) + **4 MISSING_CREATE** (110e, 957d,
9fa4, cf5d). Auto-repair is unsafe here: `rebar fsck --repair-snapshots` rebuilds from the full
log and previously CORRUPTED 11/13 statuses, and `--repair` routes EDIT orphans to human triage
(won't fix them). The store has been backed up (188MB git bundle + 967-ticket NDJSON export at
HEAD 8c3c26f72) before any mutation.

## Forensic classification (recorded in detail as a comment on this ticket)

- **13 ORPHAN_EVENT** — benign snapshot-staleness from a distributed compaction-vs-reconciler
  write race; live status/assignee verified correct for all 13 (each orphan's effect is a
  redundant duplicate of an identical post-snapshot reconciler EDIT).
- **4 MISSING_CREATE** — local-only phantom dirs (0 tracked files, not in HEAD, no structural
  references). 957d/9fa4/cf5d are empty; 110e's `.cache.json` holds an epic that is a duplicate
  of the already-tracked open epic 6d0d (content not lost).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Per-orphan disposition applied: retire each of the 13 orphan EDIT files (`.json` ->
  `.json.retired`, which fsck's `is_active_event()` skips) — lossless, touches no status.
- [ ] [operator-attested] MISSING_CREATE disposition applied: delete the 4 local phantom dirs (110e resolved as a
  duplicate of tracked epic 6d0d; 957d/9fa4/cf5d are empty residue).
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar fsck` reports zero ORPHAN_EVENT + zero MISSING_CREATE, and no ticket's displayed
  status/assignee changed (verified via a before/after diff of all 13 orphan tickets — all
  `closed`; assignees `""` except cc5b and f112 = "Joe Oakhart").
- [ ] [operator-attested] Decisions recorded on the ticket (done — see the forensic comment) and the store change
  committed to the `tickets` branch and pushed.

## Notes

- Root cause (compaction snapshotting before observing a remote reconciler write) is a recurring
  race; a durable fix is separate follow-up work, out of scope for this remediate-to-zero ticket.
baseline.summary: Human-triage the 14 residual fsck orphans (13 EDIT ORPHAN_EVENT + 1 MISSING_CREATE)

baseline.description:
## Why
3183 (change 580, commit da27c5f30) delivered the merge-gate + snapshot ledger with a
divergent schema and verdict set vs. the APPROVED epic design (AC8/AC9 — the two ACs the
epic completion-verifier correctly FAILED on). This story reworks commit 7 to the approved
design AND performs the consumer cutover deferred from TS1 (in-toto payload) and TS2
(commit-ancestry era) — the write-seam signing, the merge-gate, and the ledger all live in
THIS commit. Depends on TS1 and TS2. (User rejected the delivered design; see d7c0.)

## Stack scoping (why the cutover is here + why TS2+TS3 land together)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 580 = commit da27c5f30 (3183): `_seam.py`'s write-time
signing, `verify_authorship.py` (merge-gate), `compact.py`'s ledger, and `_state.py`'s
authorship summary. At this commit those consumers currently still call the epoch API that
TS2 REMOVED (`epoch_for_position`, `verify_authorship_at_epoch`), so the commit-7 patchset
is RED until this story rewires them — TS2+TS3 land together. `ensure_identity_for` (aliased
by `create_placeholder`) lives in commit 6, so `create_placeholder` lands here too.

## What

### 1. Write-seam in-toto cutover (`_seam.py::_apply_authorship`)
Stamp `author_sig` by calling `authorship.sign_event_authorship(event, signing_key,
principal=author_id)` (the in-toto Statement envelope) instead of
`sign_authorship(canonical_bytes, ...)`.

### 2. Merge-gate rewire (`verify_authorship.py`)
- Refactor `_ScopedEvent`: REPLACE the `epoch: int | None` field with `commit_sha: str |
  None` and `position: str | None` (the `{timestamp}-{uuid}` string). Live events populate
  `position` from the filename and resolve `commit_sha` lazily; ledger entries populate both
  from the ledger record (below).
- LIVE-event content binding: parse the DSSE payload as an in-toto Statement and check
  `subject[0].name == ev['uuid']` AND `subject[0].digest.sha256 ==
  authorship.authorship_content_hash(ev)` (replacing the raw-bytes `envelope.payload !=
  ev.payload` compare). Resolve the event's commit via
  `authorship.resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir, repo_root)`.
- Verify via `authorship.verify_authorship_at_commit(envelope, author_id, commit_sha,
  position, repo_root=...)` (replacing `epoch_for_position` + `verify_authorship_at_epoch`).
- **Four-way classification (the AC9 distinction):**
  - `unsigned` — no `author_sig`.
  - `unknown-author` — no `author_id` / not an identity ticket.
  - `verified` — content binds AND `verify_authorship_at_commit` verified (key valid at the
    event's commit).
  - `key_not_valid_at_era` — content binds AND the signature is cryptographically valid
    against SOME key in the identity's keyring (any era) BUT not one valid at the event's
    commit. Decided by a NEW helper `authorship.verify_authorship_any_key(envelope,
    identity_id, *, repo_root) -> registry.Verdict` that builds the trust root from ALL
    keyring public keys (regardless of validity window) and runs ONE `registry.verify`
    (boolean). valid-any-key AND NOT valid-at-commit ⇒ `key_not_valid_at_era`.
  - `bad-signature` — content mismatch, malformed envelope, or verifies against NO key the
    identity ever held (forged).
- Add the verdict constant `KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA = "key_not_valid_at_era"` and extend the
  CLI `counts` dict (currently hardcoded `{VERIFIED, UNSIGNED, UNKNOWN_AUTHOR,
  BAD_SIGNATURE}`) with the new key so it is tallied and printed. Document the display
  grouping in the module docstring: `verified` / `unverified` (= `bad-signature` |
  `key_not_valid_at_era` | `unknown-author`) / `unsigned`. When `resolve_event_commit` fails
  for a LIVE event (unresolvable commit), the fail-closed verify yields non-`verified` and
  the event is reported like any other non-verified event.

## Migration note (unlanded + atomic)
The `authorship_ledger` wire format changes from `{event_uuid, author_id, author_sig,
epoch}` to `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position}`. The stack is
UNLANDED and lands atomically, so no real store holds an old-format ledger; there is no
in-place snapshot migration to write (a pre-feature snapshot with no ledger is unaffected;
the reducer cache version bump from TS2 already invalidates stale reductions).

### 3. Ledger (`compact.py::_build_authorship_ledger`)
Record `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position}` per signed folded
event, where:
- `content_hash` = `authorship.authorship_content_hash(ev)` (TS1 digest).
- `signature` = the event's `author_sig` (the DSSE Statement envelope).
- `signer_pubkey` = the actual public key that verified the signature. Because SSHSIG verify
  (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`) returns only pass/fail (NOT which key matched), determine it via a
  new `authorship.identify_signer(envelope, identity_id, *, repo_root) -> str | None` that
  iterates the identity's FULL keyring — ALL public keys, including REVOKED ones (so a valid
  signature by a since-revoked key is still identified, enabling the later
  `key_not_valid_at_era` classification) — verifying the envelope against each single-key
  trust root and returning the first that passes. **Single None-policy:** if `identify_signer`
  returns `None` (the signature verifies against NO key the identity ever held — a forged /
  foreign signature), STILL record a ledger entry (never omit — omitting would hide a forged
  event from the post-compaction merge-gate) with `signer_pubkey: null`; ledger verification
  (Section 4) classifies a null-`signer_pubkey` entry as `bad-signature`. The record always
  has exactly the five keys; `signer_pubkey` is a string or `null`.
- `position` = `{"commit_sha": <resolve_event_commit(...)>, "position": "<{ts}-{uuid}>"}` —
  the `position` string is the SAME `{timestamp}-{uuid}` value `verify_authorship_at_commit`
  already consumes for intra-commit ordering (NO separate integer index; the string ordering
  is the intra-commit index). `commit_sha` is resolved at compaction time.

### 4. Ledger verification (`verify_authorship.py::_ledger_events` + `_verify_signed`)
Rewrite `_ledger_events` to read the NEW fields (`content_hash`, `signature`,
`signer_pubkey`, `position.commit_sha`, `position.position`) — not the old
`author_id`/`author_sig`/`epoch`. For a ledger entry, verification is self-contained:
crypto-verify the `signature` envelope against a ONE-key trust root built from
`signer_pubkey`, check the Statement binds `content_hash`, and decide era from
`position.commit_sha` against the SURVIVING snapshot keyring (retired KEY files folded into
the same snapshot; `resolve_event_commit` still finds a retired file's ADD commit via `git
log --diff-filter=A` across history) via `verify_authorship_at_commit`'s ancestry logic —
emitting the same four-way verdict. A ledger entry with `signer_pubkey: null` is classified
`bad-signature` directly (no key ever verified it). No raw event file needed.

### 5. Verdict vocabulary (NOT the verify-signature schema)
`verify_signature_result.schema.json` is the schema for the SEPARATE `rebar verify-signature`
command (HMAC attestations: `unsigned|foreign_key|certified|mismatch`) — it is NOT touched.
The `verify-authorship` verdicts are its own vocabulary (string constants in
`verify_authorship.py`): `verified`, `unsigned`, `unknown-author`, `bad-signature`, and the
NEW `key_not_valid_at_era`, with the display grouping documented in that module. (The epic
AC's phrase "existing verify_signature_result verdicts" is read as the verdict-vocabulary
style, not a literal edit to that unrelated command's schema — reconciled per plan-review.)

### 6. `create_placeholder`
Add `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name, *, repo_root=None)` to
`identity.py` as a thin idempotent alias over the delivered `ensure_identity_for`, and
re-export it through the library facade chain so `rebar.create_placeholder(...)` is
importable: add it to `_lib_writes.py` and to `rebar/__init__.py`'s `__all__`/exports
alongside `ensure_identity_for`.

## Scope
In: the write-seam in-toto cutover, the merge-gate rewire to commit-ancestry + in-toto
content-binding + the four-way `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict, the approved ledger schema +
self-contained ledger verification, the `signer_pubkey`/`identify_signer` +
`verify_authorship_any_key` helpers, and the `create_placeholder` alias + re-export. Out:
authorship payload machinery (TS1, done); era model machinery (TS2, done); docs/ADR (TS4).
NOTE: `verify_signature_result.schema.json` is deliberately NOT modified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A live signed event round-trips: with `identity.signing_key` set and a current
  identity holding a valid key, an event written through the seam is classified `verified`
  by `rebar verify-authorship` (proves the in-toto `_seam` stamping + the merge-gate in-toto
  content-binding + commit-ancestry verify are wired end-to-end).
- [ ] The SNAPSHOT authorship ledger records `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature,
  signer_pubkey, position}` (position = `{commit_sha, position:"<{ts}-{uuid}>"}`) per signed
  folded event; a round-trip test signs events, compacts (horizon=0, threshold=1), and
  asserts `verify-authorship --all` returns `verified` from the ledger ALONE (raw event
  files retired). A test also asserts the ledger record has exactly those five keys and that
  `signer_pubkey` equals the actual signing key.
- [ ] `verify-authorship` emits a distinct `key_not_valid_at_era` for an event whose
  signature is cryptographically valid by a key the identity holds but which was NOT valid at
  the event's commit (e.g. an event signed by a since-revoked key), distinct from
  `bad-signature` and `unknown-author` (test drives the CLI and asserts the verdict string).
- [ ] `bad-signature` is still emitted for a forged signature (verifies against no key the
  identity ever held) and for a content-binding mismatch (test).
- [ ] The `verify-authorship` verdict vocabulary exposes `key_not_valid_at_era` (a test
  asserts the constant / that the CLI can print it) and the module documents the
  `verified/unverified/unsigned` display grouping; `verify_signature_result.schema.json` is
  unchanged (a test asserts its enum is still `unsigned|foreign_key|certified|mismatch`).
- [ ] `rebar.create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)` mints a keyless
  placeholder identity, is idempotent on repeat (returns the same identity), and is
  importable from the top-level `rebar` package (test).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (in-toto cutover: stamp author_sig via sign_event_authorship)
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (_ScopedEvent epoch->commit_sha/position; in-toto content-binding; verify_authorship_at_commit; key_not_valid_at_era four-way verdict; read new ledger)
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` (approved ledger schema + signer_pubkey via per-key identify)
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (verify_authorship_any_key + identify_signer helpers)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (create_placeholder alias over ensure_identity_for)
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (re-export create_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` (export create_placeholder for rebar.create_placeholder)
baseline.summary: transition: snapshot ledger schema + key_not_valid_at_era verdict (approved AC8/AC9)

## Context / Problem

rebar's four-pass code-review system supports packaged criteria, while project criteria are declared in a repository overlay. Before this epic, a net-new project code-review criterion could be discovered by configuration but was dropped at the criterion-id resolver, Round-A fan-in, Pass-3 routing, eval/calibration surface, and CLI admission. The extension contract was also unproven in the deployed Gerrit review bot.

This epic repairs those seams, documents the contract, authors the first project criterion, and dogfoods it in advisory-only live Gerrit reviews. It supersedes the former umbrella `jira-reb-1001`, generic story `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, and bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`.

## Delivered decomposition

The eight child tickets are dependency-ordered and closed:

1. `fc72-bf7e-7652-4228` — gate-key criterion-id resolver in
   `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py`.
2. `761e-5af2-ed57-408a` — Round-A fan-in and logical-id attribution in
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` and `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`.
3. `58ef-91fa-20c1-4f29` — repository-effective Pass-3 routing in
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py`.
4. `8153-e9b5-5706-49c8` — eval/calibration admission in
   `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py` and `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`.
5. `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847` — CLI admission in
   `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`.
6. `19dd-7d89-972b-4274` — runtime contract in `docs/llm-framework.md`.
7. `225a-323c-a9f6-436b` — `project.review-phase-boundaries`, routing, and balanced eval corpus.
8. `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d` — advisory live-Gerrit dogfood, including the repaired
   repository-root seam and the cleaned final prompt revision.

Each seam child owns a disjoint production-file set. The shared `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` grows the end-to-end RED→GREEN proof across the stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar list --parent 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96` returns exactly the eight children above, each
  `closed` with a completion-verifier attestation.
- [ ] The five original drop-point categories are each owned by exactly one seam child: resolver
  (`fc72`), fan-in/attribution (`761e`), effective routing (`58ef`), eval/calibration (`8153`), and
  CLI admission (`41e2`); their production file-impact sets do not overlap.
- [ ] The no-overlay runtime preserves the ordered 13 built-ins, packaged Pass-3 dispositions, and
  default plan-review resolver mapping. Verify with
  `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k "resolver or fan_in or parity or routing"`.
- [ ] An active project code-review criterion runs once in Round A, retains its logical
  `criteria` id and physical `reviewer_id`, and uses repository-effective Pass-3 routing. Verify
  with the project-criteria unit tests and the live artifact cited on child `9447`.
- [ ] The eval/calibration API and CLI admit an active code-review-only project criterion while
  rejecting inactive or ambiguous project ids; the balanced
  `project.review-phase-boundaries` corpus and its prompt are present.
- [ ] The project-criterion runtime contract is documented in `docs/llm-framework.md`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Child `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d` is closed with a signed completion PASS;
  its final Gerrit change is merged, its live artifact has `coverage.llm_ran: true`, the FIRE
  directive is absent from the submitted revision, and routing remains threshold `0.90` with
  blocking disabled.
- [ ] The epic has `supersedes` edges to `jira-reb-1001`, `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, and
  `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`, and all three tickets are `closed`.

baseline.description:
Add a `make worktree name=<branch>` target that creates a fresh git worktree
branched from current `origin/main` and fully provisions its local env in one
step — so agents and humans stop hand-running the multi-command worktree setup
the repo's CLAUDE.md / docs/local-dev-env.md prescribe.

## Why
The repo mandates working in a fresh worktree branched from `origin/main` with its
own local venv (never the main checkout, never a stale global build). Today that is
a documented but manual sequence (`git fetch` → `git worktree add` → create venv →
`make install`), which is error-prone and easy to shortcut. A single target makes
the canonical setup one command, matches the repo's existing Makefile idiom, and
needs no new per-developer dependency (git + python + the existing `make install`).
This is the wrapper-command approach chosen over direnv: it matches "provision on
creation" semantics, works identically for humans, agents, and non-interactive CI,
and reuses the ONE canonical `make install` path rather than forking it.

## What
Add a `worktree` target to `Makefile` that:
- Requires a `name=<branch>` argument; prints usage and exits non-zero if absent.
- Creates the worktree at `../<name>` (overridable via `dir=<path>`), branched from
  freshly-fetched `origin/main` (`git fetch origin` then
  `git worktree add <dir> -b <name> origin/main`).
- Provisions the venv via the SAME sequence the docs bless and this change dogfoods:
  `python3 -m venv .venv` (seeds pip so the canonical installer works) then, with the
  venv active, `$(MAKE) install` (editable `.[dev]` install + `make hooks` wiring the
  pre-commit gate). No bespoke pip line — it delegates to the existing canonical path.
- Prints a final "activate with: cd <dir> && source .venv/bin/activate" hint.
- Is added to `.PHONY` and carries a `## ` help string so `make help` lists it.

The Gerrit `commit-msg` hook is inherited automatically (worktrees share the common
git dir's hooks), so the target does not re-fetch it — a note in the recipe records
why. Register the new target's purpose with a one-line mention in
`docs/local-dev-env.md` so it is discoverable next to the manual sequence it replaces.

## Scope
- `Makefile`: new `worktree` target + `.PHONY` entry.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`: one line pointing at `make worktree name=<branch>` as the
  one-command form of the documented manual setup.
- Non-goal: direnv / auto-activation on `cd` (a different concern — ongoing activation,
  not creation-time provisioning); non-goal: a `post-checkout` hook; non-goal: removing
  the manual instructions (kept as the explanation of what the target automates).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make worktree` with NO `name=` prints a usage message and exits non-zero.
      Proving command: `make worktree 2>&1; test $? -ne 0 && echo USAGE-OK`
- [ ] `make worktree name=<tmp>` creates a worktree at `../<tmp>` on a new branch
      `<tmp>` whose HEAD equals current `origin/main`, containing a populated `.venv`
      with a working `rebar` on its path.
      Proving command (run against a throwaway name, then clean up):
      `make worktree name=__wt_probe && test -x ../__wt_probe/.venv/bin/rebar && ( cd ../__wt_probe && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD | grep -qx __wt_probe ) && echo CREATE-OK`
      Cleanup: `git worktree remove --force ../__wt_probe && git branch -D __wt_probe`
- [ ] The target is listed by `make help` (has a `## ` description) and is in `.PHONY`.
      Proving command: `make help | grep -q 'worktree' && grep -q '^\.PHONY:.*worktree' Makefile && echo HELP-OK`
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` references `make worktree name=` as the one-command setup.
      Proving command: `grep -q 'make worktree' docs/local-dev-env.md && echo DOC-OK`
- [ ] Existing gates stay green (Makefile is not Python, but the repo's checks must pass).
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck` both exit 0.
baseline.summary: Add 'make worktree name=<branch>' one-command worktree+venv bootstrap target

baseline.description:
## What
Make the `rebar metrics` surface (this epic's registry + `rebar metrics` command) **usable by the tools that do code-health work, and discoverable in project docs** — so the metrics are not a dead-end artifact. Two deliverables: (1) teach the **rebar-janitor** skill to consult `rebar metrics` as durable, historical code-health evidence during Discovery; (2) reference the metrics surface from the project's canonical documentation so any agent/contributor can find it.

## Why
The janitor's Discovery phase already quantifies "size & growth" and "temporal decay" with one-shot tools (`cloc`/`tokei`/`ast-grep`, `git log`). `rebar metrics` adds the **trend** dimension those miss — the code-health-lens metrics the registry actually ships: the registered code-health-lens metrics — module-size distribution, oversized-module count and the module-size trend against the locked 800-line cap, short-term churn, the refactor-to-addition ratio, and cap-change events — as a single durable source. (Complexity/clone/coverage snapshots exist in the store but are not yet surfaced by a registered metric, so they do not appear in `rebar metrics` output — do not cite them.) A janitor that cites `rebar metrics` values as evidence produces findings grounded in measured decay over time, not just a single snapshot. And metrics no agent knows to read provide no value, so discoverability (docs) is part of "done".

## Files
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md` — in the "Size & growth" / temporal-decay guidance, add that a subagent should run `rebar metrics --since <date> --until <date> --output json` (when the repo is a rebar store) and cite the registered code-health-lens metric values (module-size distribution, oversized-module count and module-size trend vs the 800 cap, churn, refactor-to-addition ratio, cap-change events) as evidence; a metric whose signal has not accrued reads `unavailable` — as the historical/trend complement to the one-shot `cloc`/`tokei`/`ast-grep` pass, not a replacement. Note the `unavailable` state (a metric whose signal has not accrued yet) so the agent does not treat absence as zero.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — add a short, hand-written **"Metrics"** section: what `rebar metrics --since/--until [--output json]` surfaces (the four lenses — `agent_process`, `code_health`, `delivery`, `gate_economics`), the `source`/`confidence` labels and the `unavailable{reason,accruing_since}` state, and that backfilled/classified values are segregated from authoritative structural series. This is the human-discoverable home (the CLI-reference is auto-generated syntax; this is the "what/why/when").
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — reference the reusable `rebar.metrics` subsystem (the `MetricSpec`/`REGISTRY` declarative registry + `is_authoritative` segregation helper) so library consumers discover it.
- `AGENTS.md` — add ONE line to the "Where to read" pointer list: **Metrics** → `docs/user-guide.md` (command + lenses) and `docs/reuse-surface.md` (the registry), keeping the file lean per its own convention.

## Approach
Documentation- and skill-only; no `src/rebar` change and no new behavior — it makes the already-shipped `rebar metrics` command and registry usable and findable. It stacks on the metrics command (9a5a) so it references the command's real, landed interface (and so `docs/cli-reference.md` already lists the subcommand). Additive and reversible (revert = remove the references).

## Tests

## Context / Problem
At current origin/main commit 0f5dbc88b, the pinned Ruff 0.15.19 command `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 --statistics src/rebar tests` reports 142 actionable diagnostics: 49 RUF059, 36 RUF022, 18 RUF005, 18 RUF012, 10 RUF043, 6 RUF023, 2 RUF028, and one each of RUF019, RUF046, and RUF102. The same narrow RUF census without ignoring RUF100 reports an additional 771 RUF100 diagnostics; those are narrow-selection artifacts because the currently valid `noqa` codes are outside that command's selected rules. They are not counted as remediation debt.

This story clears the 142 non-ambiguous RUF diagnostics before selecting the family. RUF001, RUF002, and RUF003 remain deferred because many flagged Unicode symbols are intentional prose or UI content. True RUF100 findings are evaluated only with the final full configured rule set after RUF is selected; any suppression that is stale under that full configuration is removed.

## Dependencies and Ownership
This story depends on `28cd-d8f8-4456-482c`. The dependency is both ordering and shared-file ownership: the predecessor lands the ASYNC/DTZ `pyproject.toml` configuration and creates `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`; this story then edits the resulting configuration and extends that test. It does not create a competing version of the file.

## Approach
1. Extend `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` to require `RUF` in `[tool.ruff.lint].select`.
2. Add `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore = ["RUF001", "RUF002", "RUF003"]` in `pyproject.toml`. The global deferral lives only in this exact key; do not introduce `extend-ignore` or RUF entries in `per-file-ignores`.
3. In the shared test, assert that the parsed `ignore` value is exactly the three-item deferral set and that `extend-ignore` is absent. Parse `tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores` and assert that no configured code equals `RUF` or starts with `RUF`. This deterministically prohibits broad or code-specific RUF per-file exemptions.
4. Use the pinned Ruff fixer only for safe mechanical edits, review every diff, then manually resolve remaining enabled RUF diagnostics across `src/rebar` and `tests`. The 142-finding census is the starting inventory; the implementation records the post-fix per-code census on the ticket.
5. After RUF is in the global selection, run `ruff check src tests` and remove only RUF100 suppressions that are stale under that full configured rule set. Do not use the narrow-selection 771 count to drive removals.

Ruff security-family expansion and Semgrep expansion remain deferred and are already guarded by the predecessor's shared ratchet test; this story does not duplicate those orthogonal acceptance criteria.

Rejected: RUF per-file ignores, `extend-ignore`, Ruff S-family expansion, Semgrep expansion, and treating narrow-selection RUF100 output as actionable debt.

## Scope
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` (extend the file landed by 28cd)
- source and test files among the 142 diagnostics reported by the baseline command, limited to safe mechanical or behavior-preserving changes

## Testing / Verification
- Baseline reproduction: `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 --statistics src/rebar tests`
- Configuration and deferrals: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`
- Enabled RUF diagnostics: `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 src/rebar tests`
- Full configured rule set including authoritative RUF100 evaluation: `ruff check src tests`
- Canonical lint: `make lint`
- Default tier: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The implementation begins from the empirically measured 142-diagnostic inventory in Context and changes only files reported by that census.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].select` contains the exact selector `RUF`.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint].ignore` is exactly `RUF001`, `RUF002`, and `RUF003`.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `[tool.ruff.lint]` has no `extend-ignore` key.
- [ ] `ruff check --select RUF --ignore RUF001,RUF002,RUF003,RUF100 src/rebar tests` exits 0.
- [ ] `ruff check src tests` exits 0, proving RUF100 reports no stale `noqa` under the final full configured rule set.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` iterates every `tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores` code and fails if the code equals `RUF` or starts with `RUF`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The implementation records the post-remediation per-code RUF census on this ticket, including the authoritative RUF100 result from `ruff check src tests`.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` exits 0.
baseline.summary: Enable Ruff RUF hygiene ratchet

content.text: ## Why
Workflow LLM output feeds DETERMINISTIC steps, so schema-conformance reliability is load-bearing. Agents
frequently return non-conforming output; the current second-LLM-interpreter workaround is a recognized
anti-pattern. Replace it with a deterministic-where-possible layered stack (research:
docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/structured-output-research.md).
## What
Layered reliability stack: (1) provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported (OpenAI
strict, Gemini responseSchema, Anthropic native structured outputs now GA) via Pydantic AI NativeOutput;
PromptedOutput cross-provider; NOT forced-tool ToolOutput. (2) Deterministic tolerant parse of near-miss output
via json-repair (no LLM). (3) Pydantic validation + normalizing validators, with numeric/length bounds in
VALIDATORS not the JSON Schema (to stay inside Anthropic's strict-grammar subset). (4) Bounded SAME-model retry
feeding the validation error back (retries={'output': 2}; default budget is 1). Handle Anthropic stop_reason in
{refusal, max_tokens}; for steps needing extended thinking, SPLIT reasoning and structured extraction into two
steps. Keep schemas LEAN (native constraint degrades on deeply-nested/hard schemas).
## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py, contracts.py, findings.py
- pyproject.toml (add json-repair)
Out: the runtime adapter itself (separate story).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Output via NativeOutput where supported, PromptedOutput cross-provider; forced-tool ToolOutput NOT used with extended thinking.
- [ ] json-repair tolerant parse + Pydantic validators (bounds in validators, not the schema); bounded retry feeds the validation error back.
- [ ] Anthropic stop_reason {refusal, max_tokens} handled; thinking steps split reasoning vs extraction; schemas kept lean.
- [ ] The second-interpreter LLM is removed; a structured-output validity eval (recall/false-accept) gates the change.

baseline.summary: Structured-output reliability stack (retire the second-interpreter LLM)

baseline.description:
# The cutover withdrew a BLOCKING criterion's grounding tool, by prefix match, with no signal

## Context / Problem

Plan-review criterion **T1** (`facet: overlay-priorart`, `exec: AGENT`, `default_posture: **blocking**`) declares `"web": true` in the packaged routing registry (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`). Its reviewer prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T1.md`) instructs the model: *"when the web-search tool is offered, USE it to ground prior-art claims in real, current sources."* T1 is the bright-line overlay — it fires on external integration, unfamiliar dependency, security/auth, a novel architectural pattern, a perf/scalability target, or a migration.

The tool is attached only by this gate (`src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`):

    if not web or not resolved.startswith("anthropic"):
        return None

**Since the production review bot was cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], `resolved` is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, which does not start with `anthropic`. So T1 now runs WITHOUT its grounding tool on every production plan review.** The live chain, each link verified: `criteria_routing.json` `"web": true` -> `criteria/model.py` `"web": bool(routing_entry.get("web", False))` -> `plan_review/passes.py` `web=agentic and any(bool(c.get("web")) for c in chunk)` -> `runner.py` `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities(resolved, web=req.web)` -> the prefix gate above.

## Why this matters

1. **It is a BLOCKING criterion.** T1 can block a plan. It now does so on weaker evidence — codebase
   and model knowledge instead of current sources — for exactly the plans that cross a bright-line.
2. **It is decided by PREFIX SHAPE, not capability.** The epic's standing rule is provider
   qualification by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, never prefix matching, with zero exceptions — enforced for the
   capabilities module by an attested guard. This site is the same anti-pattern in a different module,
   and the cutover is what made it bite: the identical MODEL (Claude) reached through a different
   PROVIDER loses a capability because of how its name is spelled.
3. **It is SILENT.** No warning is logged and the signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities`
   records `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style`, `supports_temperature` and
   `supports_thinking` — but nothing about web search. So a reader of the verdict cannot tell that a
   declared grounding tool was withheld. This is the failure shape the epic kept hitting: the guard
   shares the bug's assumption.
4. **It contradicts the epic's own premise.** Epic 061c asserts `first_class = full fidelity`, and
   both Anthropic and Bedrock are first-class. This is a measurable fidelity difference between them
   that no acceptance criterion covers.

**Not a hallucination risk** — and this is the one piece of good news. T1's prompt handles absence explicitly: *"when it is not available, fall back to codebase and plan-text reasoning ... and do NOT fabricate web citations."* So the degradation is quiet quality loss, not invented sources.

## OPERATOR DECISION: web access is REQUIRED for T1 regardless of provider or model

This supersedes the branch this ticket was originally filed with. I had written that if Bedrock does not support Anthropic's server-side `web_search`, then returning `None` is CORRECT and the defect is merely that it is silent. **That is wrong.** The operator's requirement is that **T1 needs web access on EVERY provider and model.** A provider that cannot offer it is a capability gap rebar must CLOSE, not a difference rebar may document.

Two consequences follow, and the second is the harder one:

1. **The prefix gate goes regardless.** `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` cannot decide this, both
   because it is prefix matching (the epic's zero-exceptions rule) and because the answer it computes
   is no longer the question being asked.

2. **Provider-side-only is no longer a sufficient design.** The current implementation is deliberately
   provider-side: `plan_review_T1.md` and `anthropic_model.py` both state the tool is Anthropic's
   SERVER-SIDE `web_search`, "executed provider-side, no homegrown HTTP fetch tool" — an explicit
   decision to avoid rebar owning a fetch tool. If web access must hold for every provider, that
   decision must be REVISITED rather than worked around: where a provider offers a server-side tool,
   prefer it; where it does not, rebar must supply the access some other way. Whatever is chosen, it
   must satisfy the constraint the original design was protecting — the reviewer must not be handed an
   unbounded homegrown HTTP fetch capability without thinking about egress, caching and prompt-injection
   from fetched content. That tradeoff is the real work in this ticket and should not be skipped past.

STILL MEASURE BEDROCK FIRST — the measurement now selects the MECHANISM rather than deciding whether there is a bug: if Bedrock's Converse API can carry the server-side tool, that is the cheapest correct path for the current production provider and no rebar-side fetch tool is needed yet. If it cannot, the rebar-side path is required. Either way T1 ends up with web access.

ALSO REVISIT T1's PROMPT. It currently tells the reviewer the tool "MAY be offered on this run (it is provider-dependent...)" and to fall back to codebase reasoning when absent. Under this decision that conditional framing is wrong: web access is a guarantee for T1, so the prompt should assert it rather than hedge. The graceful-degradation clause protected against fabricated citations and should not be deleted carelessly — but it must stop describing absence as an expected state.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities`, the prefix gate.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — most likely home for a profile-derived `supports_server_web_search`
  capability, alongside the existing `prompt_cache_style` / `native_structured_output` decisions.
- the `provider_provenance.capabilities` payload, so the outcome is observable in a signed verdict.

## Testing

- a test that with a `bedrock:`-qualified Claude model and `web=True`, the outcome matches the MEASURED
  Bedrock capability — and that the decision does not consult the provider-name string. Verify RED by
  reinstating a prefix match.
- a test that the signed verdict's provenance records whether server-side web search was attached, so
  the silent case cannot return. Verify RED by removing the field.
- record the Bedrock measurement itself (a real call with the capability requested) as the evidence for
  whichever branch the fix takes; "not supported" is an acceptable answer, an unmeasured assumption is
  not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] whether Bedrock's Converse API can carry Anthropic's server-side `web_search` is MEASURED and
      recorded, with the call and its outcome. This selects the mechanism; it does not decide whether
      there is a bug.
- [ ] T1 has WEB ACCESS ON EVERY PROVIDER rebar can route it to, including Bedrock — verified by a run
      on each configured provider, not by inspection of the gate condition.
- [ ] the web-access decision no longer consults a provider-name prefix; it derives from the model
      profile / capability registry, consistent with the epic's zero-exceptions rule. The attested
      guard `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` is NOT weakened.
- [ ] if a rebar-side mechanism is required for any provider, the egress / caching /
      prompt-injection-from-fetched-content tradeoff that the original provider-side-only design was
      protecting is addressed explicitly, not bypassed.
- [ ] a signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities` records that web access WAS attached, so a
      future silent withdrawal is impossible to miss.
- [ ] `plan_review_T1.md` no longer describes web access as provider-dependent or optional, while still
      forbidding fabricated citations.
- [ ] tests pin the above and are each verified RED by mutation, including one that fails if the
      capability is withheld on a `bedrock:`-qualified model.
baseline.summary: Bedrock cutover silently removed server-side web search from blocking criterion T1, gated by provider-name prefix

# Abort a stalled review-bot `git fetch` in seconds instead of burning the 300s budget

## Context / Problem

Bug `df2c-e4b8-496d-4698` proved the review bot's per-review `git fetch` of the GitHub mirror intermittently hangs: 25 consecutive runs in `compose-review-bot-1` produced 2 hangs past 320s (rc=124) against a 1-3s median on an 80 MB / 54k-object repo.

Root cause (confirmed by experiment, see below): `_fetch_origin` in `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` builds its git argv with no `http.lowSpeedLimit` / `http.lowSpeedTime`, so git's curl handle has **no throughput-keyed abort**. A byte-starved connection is bounded only by the wall-clock `subprocess.run(timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` at 300s.

Change `0347` already removed the DURABLE damage (a retryable coverage gap now defers the vote instead of casting `LLM-Review -1`, escalating only after a 3-attempt budget). It does **not** shorten the stall: each stalled review still costs 5 minutes, and three unlucky stalls in a row still lose the review. This ticket makes the stall abort in seconds. It does **not** touch `voter.py`'s retryable-gap logic.

## Measured evidence

Against a local listener that accepts the connection, sends HTTP headers, then sends zero body bytes (a true stall), and a second listener that dribbles 2000 B/s continuously (legitimately slow but progressing):

| scenario | git config | result |
|---|---|---|
| stall (0 B/s) | none (today) | still running at the 45s harness cap; would burn 300s |
| stall (0 B/s) | `lowSpeedLimit=1000`, `lowSpeedTime=5` | aborts at **5.1s**, rc=128, "Operation too slow" |
| dribble 2000 B/s for 60s | `lowSpeedLimit=1000`, `lowSpeedTime=5` | **not aborted** — runs to the harness cap, still transferring |

Real-world safety check against the actual GitHub mirror with `lowSpeedLimit=1000`, `lowSpeedTime=10`: 5 warm fetches (0.4-0.6s) and 3 **cold full clones of the whole 80 MB repo (87.8s / 88.4s / 101.4s)** all completed — a legitimately slow 90-second transfer is not aborted.

## Approach

1. Pass `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=<bytes/s> -c http.lowSpeedTime=<seconds>` on the snapshot fetch,
   so a byte-starved connection aborts on **throughput**, not wall time. Defaults 1000 B/s over
   10s (evidence above); both overridable by env for operators on pathological links.
2. Retry the fetch in-process a bounded number of times when — and only when — it failed with a
   low-speed abort, so a transient stall self-heals inside the same review instead of deferring
   to a backfill pass. Worst case becomes ~3x10s rather than 300s.

### Module-size constraint (why this change also moves code)

`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` is **788 LOC against the hard 800 cap** (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), leaving no room. Per the module-size policy the fix splits along a call-graph seam that already exists: the git-subprocess + fetch-locking cluster (`_interprocess_lock`, `_fetch_lock_for`, `_git`, `_has_remote`, `_rev_parse`, `_is_auth_failure`, `_fetch_origin`, the `Snapshot*Error` vocabulary they raise, and the `_AUTH_STDERR_MARKERS` they classify with) moves whole into a new sibling `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py`. The dependency becomes one-directional (`repo_snapshot` -> `git_fetch`); no behaviour moves with it, and `_snapshot/__init__.py`'s public surface is unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py` (new — extracted plumbing + the stall abort and retry)
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` (extraction; call sites re-pointed)
- `tests/unit/` — new test module for the stall-abort behaviour

Explicitly out of scope: `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` (0347's retryable-gap logic), `src/rebar/llm/*`, and the 300s `_GIT_TIMEOUT` ceiling itself, which stays as the outer bound.

## Testing

RED-first, and deliberately **not** asserting on wall-clock durations (they flake in CI):

- A test that spawns a real local listener which accepts and then sends **zero bytes**, points
  a fetch at it, and asserts the fetch fails with a low-speed abort well inside a short bound —
  RED today (the fetch is only bounded by the 300s ceiling).
- A test that spawns a listener **dribbling bytes continuously below normal speed but above the
  configured floor**, and asserts the fetch is **not** aborted — this is the discriminator that
  stops the fix from killing healthy slow clones, and it fails if the threshold is keyed on wall
  time rather than throughput.
- A test asserting the emitted git argv carries the low-speed options (cheap contract guard).
- A test asserting a low-speed abort is retried the configured number of times and a
  non-low-speed failure (e.g. auth) is **not** retried.

Mutation check both directions: removing the low-speed args must return the stall test to RED, and a behaviour-preserving rename must not break any of them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A stalled fetch (a remote that accepts the connection and sends no bytes) aborts in ~10
      seconds rather than at the 300s ceiling, demonstrated by a reproduction against an
      unresponsive local remote.
- [x] A genuinely slow-but-progressing fetch is **not** aborted; the threshold is keyed on
      throughput, not wall time, and is proven so by a dribbling-remote test.
- [x] A transient low-speed abort is retried in-process a bounded number of times, so the common
      case still produces a real review; a non-low-speed failure (auth, bad ref) is not retried.
- [x] `voter.py`'s retryable-gap logic from change 0347 is untouched.
- [x] `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` and the new `git_fetch.py` are each under the 800
      LOC module-size cap.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default test selection all pass (exit 0).
baseline.summary: review-bot: abort a stalled git fetch in seconds instead of burning the 300s timeout

Ensure `session_log` tickets are never synced to Jira and never surface in bridge
audits.

## Why

Session logs are local, verbose, agent-facing artifacts with no place in a Jira
project. The reconciler currently maps every type to a Jira issue type; we must
exclude `session_log` so reconcile never emits it.

## What

- Add an `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` set (containing `session_log`) in
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`.
- Filter it in `compute_outbound_mutations()` in
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py`, alongside the existing
  excluded-status check.
- Deliberately do NOT add `session_log` to `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`, so any leak
  fails loudly rather than syncing silently.
- Confirm `bridge_fsck` is unaffected (session logs are never bound, so they never
  appear in its reports).

## Scope

Outbound reconcile exclusion only. No inbound/bridge schema changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dry-run `reconcile` over a store containing `session_log` tickets produces
      zero mutations for them.
- [ ] `session_log` is absent from `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`.
- [ ] `bridge_fsck` output contains no `session_log` entries.
- [ ] Tests assert the outbound exclusion with a `session_log` fixture.
baseline.summary: Exclude session_log from Jira reconcile

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar's plan vocabulary carries two headings for one concept. `## Acceptance Criteria` is the
universal blocking floor: P1 (`det_floor.py`) and the standalone `check-ac` gate require a
`- [ ]` checklist with >=1 item on EVERY ticket type. `## Success Criteria` is a second heading
that the author guide asks container/epic tickets to add on top.

Investigation showed the split is vestigial vocabulary, not a live semantic axis. Every
criterion that touches them POOLS them and applies ONE bar:

- F1 opens "Examine each acceptance/success criterion for measurability and whether an agent
  can complete it within ONE working session", and its routing is
  `applies_at: {"suppress_types": ["bug"]}` — no scope restriction, so it binds containers
  exactly as it binds leaves. There is no SC carve-out.
- G3's checklist reads "The union of children covers each parent acceptance/success criterion".
- G7 fetches the parent's "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract.
- The completion verifier lists both as completion requirements.

Not one criterion applies a different bar to SC. Altitude is already carried by ROUTING — G3 is
`applies_at: {"scope": ["container"]}`, firing on whether a ticket has children — so the heading
name carries no load. The only divergence is the author guide's prose, which implies a split the
gates never implemented.

The split is also actively harmful. `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under
`## Acceptance Criteria`, resetting at the next `##`. SC is conventionally written as plain
bullets, so criteria living under SC (a) do not count toward the P1 blocking floor, (b) cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — the completion verifier matches that token only on
checkbox text, so an SC item is silently judged by the codebase bar — and (c) are not
individually checkable. Collapsing the vocabulary therefore TIGHTENS the gate.

## Why now

Renaming criteria text rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp. Until ticket
`1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` that invalidated every outstanding plan-review attestation repo-wide
(632 tickets, ~40 open/in_progress), which made this migration prohibitively expensive. ADR 0053
grandfathers registry drift at the claim gate, so the rename is now affordable.

## Scope

Collapse `## Success Criteria` into `## Acceptance Criteria` across the live vocabulary:
detector regexes, reviewer prompts, the criteria routing index, author-facing guides, the
generated criteria guide, eval specs and gold-set expectations, the test corpus, and the 108
tickets in the store that carry the old heading.

Sequenced expand-contract: detectors accept BOTH headings first, the vocabulary and data move
under that umbrella, and the alias is removed last. No window in which a ticket is
un-reviewable because its heading is in transit.

IN SCOPE: the `## Success Criteria` -> `## Acceptance Criteria` collapse and the SC -> AC
vocabulary in prompts/docs/tests, plus migrating store tickets' SC bullets to AC checkboxes.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- The `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" vocabulary — a related but SEPARATE concept
  (may be picked up as discovered work). Three live sites carry it and are excluded:
  `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`, `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`,
  and the `dod_uncertifiable` field description in `llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`.
  (AMENDED: originally written as "in the verifier prompts", which did not name the
  `verify_models.py` field carrying the identical wording.)
- `llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` — "a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria for a
  trial". Generic English about whether an EXPERIMENT succeeded, NOT the ticket heading;
  renaming it would change T2's meaning. Same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`.
  (ADDED during implementation; established by story 2aa6, whose AC6 requires it to survive.)
- Removing `clarity-check` (independently planned for removal; this epic only stops it keying
  on the SC heading).
- Frozen test fixtures that RECORD historical text (`tests/fixtures/jira/*`) and historical
  citations to a past ticket's numbered criterion.
- Anything matching `O-RAN-SC` (a Linux Foundation telecom consortium) in ADRs 0021/0022/0023
  and `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, and the minified vendor bundle
  `llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/` returns matches ONLY at the sites
      Scope excludes — `plan_review_T2.md` (trial metrics), `plan_review_verifier.md`,
      `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` and `review_kernel/verify_models.py` (all
      `dod_uncertifiable`), plus the minified vendor bundle — and NO others. Verify with
      `... | grep -v -e plan_review_T2.md -e plan_review_verifier.md
      -e plan_review_verifier_agentic.md -e verify_models.py -e editor_assets/dist/`
      returning empty.
      AMENDED: as originally written ("No live source file ... matches") this was
      UNSATISFIABLE — it contradicted this epic's own Scope, which defers the
      `dod_uncertifiable` vocabulary, and it contradicted story 2aa6's AC6, which REQUIRES
      T2's phrase to survive. The intent — no file still uses SC as the CRITERIA HEADING
      vocabulary — is unchanged and fully preserved; only the false-positive carve-outs are
      now stated, exactly as `O-RAN-SC` and the vendor bundle already were.
- [ ] Both bare-`SC` tokens meaning Success Criteria — `plan_review_G3.md:12`
      ("THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches...'") — read AC, and the
      four `O-RAN-SC` ADR/workflow occurrences are byte-identical to their pre-migration state.
- [ ] A ticket whose plan uses only `## Acceptance Criteria` passes plan review at container
      level: G3's child-coverage audit runs against the parent's AC with no criteria lost.
- [ ] EVERY store ticket carrying a `## Success Criteria` heading is migrated so its criteria
      sit under `## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items counted by
      `_count_ac_items`, proven by a post-run scan finding zero remaining SC HEADINGS (a
      backticked prose mention of the heading is not a heading and must be left intact).
      AMENDED: the set is recomputed at run time, not hard-coded — "108" was a
      point-in-time estimate. DONE: 106 tickets migrated (104 + 2 whose headings carried a
      parenthetical qualifier); 0 SC headings remain; 8 prose mentions correctly untouched.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is REGENERATED (not hand-edited) from the updated
      registry and contains EXACTLY ONE SC match — the T2 criterion's embedded prompt
      ("...stated success criteria for a trial").
      AMENDED: "contains no SC vocabulary" was unsatisfiable. The guide is a GENERATED
      snapshot of the criteria registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim, so the
      excluded T2 phrase necessarily echoes into it. Asserting exactly one match is STRICTER
      than a bare exclusion: it also proves the phrase was carried through, not dropped.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass, and every landed change
      carries `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Collapse Success Criteria into Acceptance Criteria across rebar's plan vocabulary

content.text: ## Summary

A `confirmed` binding whose Jira issue was deleted AND whose local ticket was archived is never garbage-collected — it persists in `bindings.json` forever. Proven: `f8b5-2f30 -> REB-530` is `confirmed`, but REB-530 no longer exists in Jira and f8b5 is locally archived.
## Root Cause (binding GC gated on the local ticket being live)

- The only path that retires a binding for a vanished Jira issue is the "bound-but-absent" direct-GET probe in `outbound_differ.py:598-611` -> `binding_store.note_absent` -> retire after GRACE consecutive 404s (`binding_store.py:292-337`).

- That probe only runs for NON-excluded local tickets: archived/deleted are skipped at `outbound_differ.py:471` (candidate pre-selection) and `:539` (main loop), `excluded_statuses={archived,deleted}`. So an archived-local binding is never probed -> REB-530 is never GET'd -> never `note_absent` -> never retired.
- `recover_pending_bindings` scans only `pending` bindings (`binding_store.py:384`), never `confirmed`. There is no other path that validates a confirmed binding's Jira side still exists.
- Runtime proof: `reconcile --mode dry-run` plans nothing for f8b5/REB-530.
## In plain language

A ticket was synced to a Jira issue (a link record: f8b5 <-> REB-530). Later BOTH sides disappeared — the ticket was archived locally and the Jira issue was deleted — but the link record stays, marked "confirmed", forever. It lingers because the code that retires a stale link works by fetching the Jira issue and waiting for repeated 404s, and that fetch only runs for links whose local ticket is still active. Since the ticket is archived, the reconciler skips it, never fetches REB-530, never sees the 404, never retires the link. The separate "recover" routine only cleans up half-created (pending) links, never confirmed ones.
## Implications
- Unbounded leak: `bindings.json` accumulates dead entries; invisible because `bridge_fsck` cannot see them either (class-D ticket).

- Latent correctness hazard: a stale binding still claims a Jira key. If the ticket is un-archived, or the key is reused, outbound updates target a nonexistent issue (404s) or a clean re-create is blocked.
- Current real impact is low (one test ticket), but the leak grows and carries a resurrection hazard.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Sync a local ticket to Jira (confirmed binding).
2. Delete the Jira issue AND archive the local ticket.
3. Run reconcile passes; observe the binding stays `confirmed` in `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json`.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: a confirmed binding whose Jira issue no longer exists is retired (unbound), even when the local ticket is archived/deleted.
- Actual: the binding persists indefinitely.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A confirmed binding whose Jira issue is gone is retired within a bounded number of passes even when the local ticket is archived/deleted.
- [ ] Binding GC is driven from the binding store (bounded by #bindings), unified with the class-A terminal-transition detection.
- [ ] A RED test: confirmed binding to a nonexistent Jira key + archived local ticket -> asserts retirement; RED before fix.
- [ ] f8b5-2f30 -> REB-530 is retired after the fix.
## Notes
Discovered comparing Jira REB vs local. Files: `outbound_differ.py`, `binding_store.py`, `reconcile.py`.
## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)

- [ ] GC a confirmed binding ONLY from a bounded direct-GET 404 counted to `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` consecutive misses (L13/L14) — NEVER from snapshot-absence (L17: Done-beyond-`_DONE_RECENT_CAP` issues are alive-but-absent; absence-keyed GC would mass-retire the whole Done backlog).
- [ ] Retirement stays REVERSIBLE (soft-delete to `bindings-retired.json`); a 200 GET resets the counter; interacts safely with `recover_pending_bindings` (L15).

- [ ] Extend the existing archived-gated probe so an archived/deleted local ticket's binding IS probed (the current skip at `outbound_differ.py:471,539` is the root cause) — unified with class A's binding-store loop.
- [ ] Circuit breaker backstops a mass-retire from any transient fetch/JQL-scope regression [prior art: Argo `allowEmpty`].
## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)

DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): this bug is the `PROBE_GET` -> `RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE` Decision chain of `classify()`, driven from the binding-store walk — the SAME walk as bug 444d (class A); implement them against one shared iteration, not two loops.

1. The classifier routes bound+ABSENT_IN_WINDOW to PROBE_GET regardless of local state — the fix is precisely that an archived/deleted local no longer exempts its binding from the probe (today's skip at the excluded_statuses candidate filter in outbound_differ.py is the root cause).

2. REUSE the existing probe machinery UNCHANGED: `_safe_get_issue` sentinels (_DELETED/_TRANSPORT_ERROR), bounded GET budget with oldest-first rotation, `note_absent`/`clear_absent` grace counting (RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE, default 3), reversible retirement to bindings-retired.json. Your change is WHICH pairs enter the probe set, not HOW probing works.

3. ADR 0028 #1 is absolute: ABSENT_IN_WINDOW never retires directly (the Done-beyond-_DONE_RECENT_CAP backlog is alive-but-absent — a naive absent==gone would mass-retire it; that is the exact regression cell test to write). Only CONFIRMED_404 counted to grace yields RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE.

4. RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE is an acting kind counted by the circuit breaker; a fetch/JQL regression that empties the window must trip the breaker BEFORE mass-retire (test this cell: snapshot={} -> breaker refuses).

RED test: confirmed binding to a nonexistent key + archived local -> probe fires -> grace counts across 3 simulated passes -> retirement (reversible; entry lands in bindings-retired.json). Regression cells: Done-beyond-cap NOT retired; transport-error defers without incrementing grace.

Live acceptance cell: f8b5-2f30 -> REB-530 retired after grace (REB-530 confirmed absent from the 2026-07-03 snapshot; bindings-retired.json has NEVER existed on prod — its first-ever write is itself a verification point for the commit path in _commit_binding_store_snapshot).
Files: classify.py (cells), outbound_differ.py (probe-set selection), binding_store.py (consume grace/retire as-is), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + state/.

baseline.summary: Confirmed binding to a deleted Jira issue is never GC'd when the local ticket is archived

# Dogfood the completed lifecycle in rebar

## Goal
Prove the integrated behavior through public surfaces and enable both optional policies for this project without requiring migration or backfill.

## Implementation
- Enable verify.enforce_plan_material_pins and verify.require_plan_review_for_close in rebar.toml; retain false defaults in the reusable configuration schema.
- Add public-surface lifecycle scenarios for: legacy unpinned attestations; emission while enforcement is off; enable/disable/re-enable; direct child drift; depends_on and blocks normalization; natural A-to-B-to-C transitivity; successful unchanged re-review stopping propagation; execution-time self-edit; in_progress-to-open reset; code-only drift at close; deleted and archived pinned targets; concurrent review/close changes; and audited force-close.
- Verify no eager backfill, graph-wide invalidation event, new pin command, list-output change, or stored relation migration occurs.
- Treat the sibling stories as the sole owners of adding each configuration key to the reusable schema and `tests/golden/config_surface.json`. This story verifies both keys are already present together, enables them only in `rebar.toml`, and updates `CHANGELOG.md` plus `docs/release-notes.md` for the rebar-project policy cutover; it does not re-register either golden key.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rebar enables both policies while library defaults remain off, and a pre-feature unpinned attestation continues to pass both gates.
- [ ] End-to-end tests prove direct and natural-transitive invalidation only after actual narrow material changes.
- [ ] An unchanged successful re-review produces no further propagation.
- [ ] Outgoing `depends_on` and inbound `blocks` references to one canonical prerequisite normalize to one prerequisite pin/evaluation.
- [ ] Execution adaptation, return-to-open reset, and code-only close freshness are proven through public lifecycle surfaces.
- [ ] Enable, disable, and re-enable behavior is proven through public lifecycle surfaces.
- [ ] Deleted and archived target handling, concurrency rechecks, and audited force-close are proven through public lifecycle surfaces.
- [ ] No eager backfill, graph-wide invalidation event, new pin command, ordinary-list output change, or stored relation migration is introduced.

## Verification
- Run the complete lifecycle interface suite with both rebar policies enabled.
- Run make check and the full non-integration test suite.
- In an isolated fixture tracker, invoke the real checkout CLI with no `--dry-run` bypass and both policies loaded as `true`. Exercise four cases: (1) a legacy unpinned attestation claims successfully with exit 0 and `open -> in_progress`; (2) current pins plus compatible execution-phase plan and completion attestations close successfully with exit 0 and `in_progress -> closed`; (3) stale material-pin drift rejects claim or close with exit 1, leaves status unchanged, and names the canonical stale target plus `stale-pin-drift`; (4) missing or phase-incompatible close-plan review rejects close with exit 1, leaves `in_progress` unchanged, and instructs the operator to run `review-plan`. Do not use force-close in these four gate-health cases.
- Record one JSON object in a ticket comment with `config.enforce_plan_material_pins`, `config.require_plan_review_for_close`, and a `cases` array. Each case contains `name`, `command`, `expected_exit`, `observed_exit`, `before_status`, `expected_after_status`, `observed_after_status`, `expected_reason_tokens`, `observed_reason`, and `passed`. Gate health passes only when both config fields are `true`, every observed exit/status exactly equals its expected value, every required reason token is present, and all four `passed` values are true. Any mismatch fails verification and blocks closing this story.
baseline.summary: Enable material-pin and close-review enforcement for rebar with lifecycle acceptance coverage

## Context

Placeholder epic to brainstorm G-1 from the DSO gap analysis (~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md, §3). rebar's plan-review evaluates each finding independently through Pass 2/3, so it can emit advisory findings that pull the author in opposite directions (e.g. G5 'split this unit' vs G3 'children under-cover parent, add work here'; T4 'add a compat path' vs A1/T4 'gratuitous compat'). Because the protocol is remediate-and-re-run, contradictory coaching can waste review cycles and induce oscillation (fix A -> re-trigger B -> forever).

DSO's answer: a review-protocol Stage-2 that groups findings by target, classifies opposing-direction pairs with a typed taxonomy (add_vs_remove / more_vs_less / strict_vs_flexible / expand_vs_reduce), and resolves via a ladder (critical beats minor; two blocking-tier conflicts escalate to a human; minor never conflicts).

## Open design question (why this is its own epic)

The report proposes a NEW single-turn LLM conflict pass between Pass 3 and Pass 4. That cuts against rebar's grain (minimise LLM calls; keep decisions deterministic/arithmetic). A lower-level alternative: detect opposing pairs DETERMINISTICALLY over the Pass-4 coach's already-chosen (move, subject) tuples -- two findings naming the same subject with opposing moves are a detectable conflict with no extra LLM call. Which level is right, how to render the conflict in the verdict, and how it interacts with the block/advisory posture + the rising-floor re-review are the design questions to resolve in a dedicated brainstorming session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] This epic holds the design rationale and links to the G-1 section of the gap report
- [ ] A brainstorming session produces a concrete implementation plan (child stories) before any code is written
- [ ] Placeholder only: NOT to be claimed/implemented until the design session concludes
- [ ] A decision on the detection level (deterministic-over-coach-tuples vs new LLM pass vs hybrid)
- [ ] A defined conflict taxonomy + resolution ladder mapped onto rebar's block/advisory posture
- [ ] Interaction with rising-floor re-review + oscillation signal (G-2) worked out
- [ ] Evidence (sidecar) that contradictory coaching actually occurs before building
baseline.summary: Plan-review: cross-finding conflict detection (G-1)

baseline.description:
# The 800-LOC cap is saturated: nine modules within 20 lines, three exactly at it

## Measured (this worktree, rebased on current origin/main)

| file | LOC | headroom |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` | 799 | 1 |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` | 796 | 4 |
| `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` | 793 | 7 |
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` | 791 | 9 |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` | 787 | 13 |
| `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` | 782 | 18 |

## Why this is a blocker, not an observation

It is already blocking real work. Story 343b's remaining gap (the gate verdict must carry `provider_provenance`; see that ticket's "gap 5") requires threading one value through `orchestrator.finalize_verdict` and its FIVE call sites, which live in `orchestrator.py` (4 lines of headroom), `workflow_ops.py` (13) and `gate_dispatch.py` (**1 line**, with THREE of the five call sites). The minimal possible change — one helper, one defaulted parameter, one added key, one argument per call site — cannot fit. Even folding the helper into a roomy module leaves `gate_dispatch.py` needing +3 lines against 1 line of headroom, and the kwarg cannot be appended to the existing lines without breaching the 100-char E501 limit.

So a correct, minimal, well-tested change is physically unlandable until something is split.

## This is the third instance in one epic

- `runner.py` hit 800 during story dc0d -> task 2682 split it.
- `runner.py` hit it AGAIN after main grew it to 798 -> ticket 3a98 split it further.
- `attest.py` was at 799 and a two-call-site kwarg change only fit by importing a function directly
  to dodge an E501 wrap, landing at EXACTLY 800 -> ticket c6c9 filed to split it, still open.
Each was treated as a one-off. Nine modules at the edge says it is not.

## The cost is not only structural

The cap is now shaping documentation and design quality, not just file layout:
- In `attest.py` the explanatory comments for a security-relevant change had to be cut to a pointer
  purely to save lines.
- Here, the natural home for the cfg->record helper is beside its consumer; it has to go elsewhere
  purely for space, which is the "split mechanically to hit a number" the module-size policy itself
  forbids.
- The next person to fix a one-line bug in any of the nine pays an unrelated refactor first, under
  whatever time pressure that bug carries.

## Approach (candidate, deliberately not a decision)

Do NOT raise the limit — it is locked, and an administrator override is the documented path for a limit change precisely so this stays deliberate. Instead, treat the saturated set as a queue and split along seams that ALREADY exist in the call graph, one module at a time, as 2682 and 3a98 did. Both of those are worked precedents: 2682 extracted the structured-run cluster with ZERO test edits; 3a98 moved the pai preflight cluster into it, also with zero test edits, by re-importing the moved names so existing monkeypatch seams kept resolving.

Priority should follow what is BLOCKING rather than what is largest: `gate_dispatch.py` (1 line, blocking 343b today), then `orchestrator.py` (4), then the three at exactly 800.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` is under 700 LOC, split along an existing call-graph
      seam, with zero test edits or each edit justified in the commit message
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` is under 700 LOC on the same terms
- [ ] no extracted module is under 100 LOC (the anti-fragmentation floor)
- [ ] after the split, `gate_dispatch.py` has at least 100 lines of headroom under the 800-LOC cap,
      reported as the before/after LOC in the commit message. This is the ticket's PURPOSE stated
      observably: 343b must add one argument at each of the three `finalize_verdict` call sites that
      live in that file, which is unlandable against the 1 line of headroom it has today. This ticket
      does NOT perform that wiring — it only makes it landable, and the wiring is asserted by 343b.
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus
      any new seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines in a comment
baseline.summary: Split the modules saturating the 800-LOC cap, starting with gate_dispatch
