content.text: Mirror how validity is produced, but enforce independence STRUCTURALLY: score novelty in a
SEPARATE Pass-2 structured sub-call that ALONE receives the prior findings and answers a
small novelty sub-answer set ("does this finding correspond to a prior finding?"). The
existing verification sub-call (severity attributes + binary/validity) receives NO prior
findings, so the `verify.py:64` independence invariant (VERIFIER_RULES[0]) holds by
construction. Pass-1 stays unanchored.
This is NEW behavior (pure creation): `discriminates_novelty`, `NOVELTY_EXPECTS`, the
`novelty` contract, the novelty prompt, and the dedicated novelty eval spec do not exist
yet — none are edits to existing symbols.
## Why an LLM sub-call and not the deterministic `sidecar.norm_id` fingerprint
`sidecar.norm_id` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:119`) is an EXACT-match key (a
significant-token set + criteria): it collapses reordering/punctuation but a carryover
finding RE-PHRASED across a plan edit (different significant tokens) mints a different
`norm_id` and would slip through as "novel". The whole point of novelty is to catch the
SUBSTANTIVELY-same finding reworded between reviews, so an LLM matches-prior sub-call is the
right tool. `norm_id` remains the offline join key; novelty is the runtime carryover signal.
Independence is still enforced STRUCTURALLY (the separate sub-call), not by prompt assertion.
## Novelty sub-answer set + scoring arithmetic (canonical)
Novelty is the INVERSE of "matches a prior finding". The sub-call answers a small set of
factual **matches-prior** questions (yes / insufficient / no), each scored on the same
ordinal map Pass-3 uses for validity (`yes=1.0, insufficient=0.5, no=0.0`):
- Q1 `restates_prior_defect` — Does this finding restate the same underlying defect as a
specific prior-review finding?
- Q2 `cites_prior_location` — Does it cite the same plan location/section as that prior finding?
- Q3 `matches_prior_fix` — Is its suggested remediation substantively the same as that prior
finding's?
A named constant `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS = ("restates_prior_defect", "cites_prior_location",
"matches_prior_fix")` in `decide.py` (the analogue of `GRADED_BINARY`) anchors the
`novelty_model` fields to the scoring arithmetic so they can never name different questions.
`carryover_match = mean(answerable matches-prior sub-answers)` (a sub-answer is "answerable"
when it is one of yes/insufficient/no; a missing/blank one is skipped); **`novelty = 1 −
carryover_match`** ∈ [0,1]. High novelty (≈1.0) = no prior match (genuinely new); low novelty
(≈0.0) = carryover. If NO sub-answer is answerable, novelty defaults to **0.0** (carryover →
never dropped — the safe direction). The questions are FACTUAL (match-prior), never normative
("should I downrank"). Pass-3 maps novelty deterministically in task cc5b.
## The `novelty` contract (registered alongside `verification`)
A distinct registered structured-output contract — `novelty_model` in `verify.py`, registered
under the kernel name `novelty`, with `plan_review_novelty` registered as the plan-review
alias in `passes.py` (mirroring how `verification`/`plan_review_verification` pair). Per-item
fields: `index: int`, the three matches-prior sub-answers (default `"insufficient"`, mirroring
the verification Binary defaults), and `matched_prior_id: str` (default `""` — the prior
finding id this matched, or empty when there is no match). The existing `verification`
contract is NOT reused (it has no prior-findings input). There is no schema "prompt id" field —
the prompt is identified by its prompt-library id (`plan-review-novelty`), not a payload field.
## The sub-call mechanism + data-flow contract
`verify.py` gains `score_novelty(findings, *, prior_findings, run_chunk, …) -> {index:
novelty_float}` mirroring `verify_findings`: it injects the prior findings as context to the
SEPARATE novelty sub-call (the only call that sees them), reshapes by global index, and maps
each finding's sub-answers to a novelty via `decide.novelty(...)`. The returned
`{index: novelty}` map is what cc5b's Pass-3 consumes; an index absent from the map (the
finding had no novelty produced) is treated by cc5b as carryover (novelty 0.0). The
severity/validity sub-call and Pass-1 are NOT given the prior findings.
## Fallback (fail-safe — never silently suppress)
If the novelty sub-call errors, times out, or returns malformed/unparseable output, novelty
defaults to **0.0** for the affected findings (treated as carryover → enforced at the normal
threshold, NEVER dropped). A broken novelty signal can only make the gate STRICTER, never
suppress a finding. The fallback emits a WARN log (so an elevated fallback rate is observable)
and is covered by a FakeRunner test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py` (a sub-call
that raises / returns junk → every novelty is 0.0).
## `discriminates_novelty` eval gate — in a DEDICATED spec (the bar; resolves the BLOCK)
The novelty sub-call uses its OWN prompt + contract, NOT the `plan-review-verifier` prompt — so
its eval cases and scorer go in a **dedicated** `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml`
keyed to `prompt: plan-review-novelty` (appending them to the verifier spec would score the
verifier prompt's output, which never carries novelty — the wrong artifact). Add a
`discriminates_novelty` deterministic scorer mirroring `discriminates_true_from_false` /
`discriminates_impact_levels` (`eval_scorers.py`): a PER-CASE boolean at the **0.5 midpoint** —
a `kind: novel` (`expect: high_novelty`) case must score novelty **≥ 0.5**; a `kind: carryover`
(`expect: low_novelty`) case **< 0.5**. The scorer reads the novelty score via a dedicated
`_novelty(out)` extractor (numeric `novelty`, else computed from the matches-prior sub-answers
via the shared `decide.novelty` arithmetic, so the scorer and the gate can never diverge).
Register `discriminates_novelty` in the `eval_scorers.REGISTRY` and add ≥ 3 labeled
(prior-finding, new-finding) carryover/novel pairs (both directions) to the dedicated spec.
`eval_scorers.ALLOWED_EXPECTS` is extended with `NOVELTY_EXPECTS = {high_novelty, low_novelty}`
AND `validate_dataset_and_gold` in `eval.py` gains a novelty-axis balance check analogous to
the validity/impact ones (if any `NOVELTY_EXPECTS` value is used, BOTH `high_novelty` and
`low_novelty` must be present), so `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` both accepts the cases and
still enforces a balanced discrimination set.
**The bar (numeric target):** the scorer is GATED by the spec-level convention already used by
the sibling discriminators — `gate: at_least(2)` over `epochs: 3` with `coverage_threshold: 0.8`
(i.e. every labeled novelty pair discriminated correctly at the 0.5 midpoint in ≥ 2 of 3
epochs). There is no separate AUC/F1 number: house style for deterministic discriminators is
the per-case 0.5 midpoint + the spec gate (the llm-judge `threshold:` field does NOT apply to
deterministic scorers). This eval bar is DISTINCT from the runtime drop threshold
`T_novel = 0.7` (task cc5b): 0.5 is "did the scorer separate novel from carryover at all"; 0.7
is "how novel must a finding be to be eligible for the Pass-3 drop".
## The evidence gate (enforcement lives in cc5b)
"cc5b must not activate the drop rule until this bar is met" is enforced in cc5b, not here: the
Pass-3 drop rule ships behind a config key that is **default-OFF** for v1 (expand-contract), so
the deterministic floor is inert until the novelty discriminator has cleared the bar and the
key is flipped. 150b's responsibility is to make the scorer + labeled set + the dedicated spec
exist and validate; cc5b consumes them.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Novelty scored in a separate Pass-2 sub-call that alone sees prior findings (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` `score_novelty`, re-exported in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py`)
- [ ] The severity/validity sub-call receives NO prior findings; Pass-1 receives none

- [ ] Novelty sub-answers are factual (match-prior), not "should I downrank"; a `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` constant in `decide.py` anchors the fields; `novelty = 1 − mean(answerable matches-prior sub-answers)` on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0` map; no answerable sub-answers → novelty 0.0
- [ ] Fail-safe fallback: novelty sub-call error/timeout/malformed → novelty = 0.0 (carryover; never dropped) + a WARN log; covered by a FakeRunner test in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py`

- [ ] A distinct registered `novelty` contract (`novelty_model` in `verify.py`; `plan_review_novelty` alias in `passes.py`): `index`, the three matches-prior sub-answers (default `insufficient`), `matched_prior_id` (default `""`). The `verification` contract is NOT reused

- [ ] `discriminates_novelty` scorer (per-case, 0.5 midpoint) + a dedicated `_novelty(out)` extractor + ≥ 3 carryover/novel labeled pairs in a DEDICATED `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml` (`prompt: plan-review-novelty`) + registered in `eval_scorers.REGISTRY` (NOT appended to `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml`)

- [ ] `ALLOWED_EXPECTS` extended with `NOVELTY_EXPECTS = {high_novelty, low_novelty}` AND `validate_dataset_and_gold` in `eval.py` extended with a novelty-axis balance check (both poles required), so `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` accepts AND balances the new cases
- [ ] The bar is `gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8` on the novelty pairs (the framework idiom; NOT an AUC literal), distinct from the runtime `T_novel=0.7`

- [ ] The novelty scorer + dedicated spec exist and validate (`rebar prompt eval plan-review-novelty`); the drop rule remains inert (default-OFF, enforced in cc5b) until the bar is cleared — the evidence gate
## Data flow to downstream (cc5b)
`score_novelty` returns `{finding_index: novelty}` (∈ [0,1]); cc5b's Pass-3 reads it, treats an
absent index as carryover (0.0), and applies the deterministic floor. Novelty never re-enters
the severity/validity sub-call (independence). The structural-independence design decision is
recorded in the ADR + docs delivered by task 4cb9.

baseline.summary: Pass-2: emit a structured novelty sub-answer set (prior-findings grounded)

content.text: ## Why
Job 1: refute an asserted absence. When a reviewer (plan or code) claims an import/symbol is hallucinated, this
lane tries to DISPROVE it by resolving the reference against the repo — the highest-value false-positive reducer
for hallucinated-symbol findings. It is confirm-only: `refuted` (found it) or `abstain`, never asserts absence.
## What
- A **deterministic T1 resolver** over a full repo checkout = a **universal-ctags** repo-wide tags index (164
langs, no server, no build) + plain file-path existence. (grep-ast is NOT a repo-wide indexer — per-file
AST-context grep only; spike `docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/` confirmed this — so it is at most an
optional context-display helper, NOT the index.)
- **`refuted` is SCOPED to name-existence WITH AN AMBIGUITY+MEMBER GUARD** (spike E2: naive bare name-existence
false-refutes a collision; the guard restores 0 false-refute). The resolution rule: a **dotted/member** reference
(`foo.bar`) → `abstain` (member binding is T2); a name with **>1 definition** (collision/common name) →
`abstain(ambiguous)`; a **unique, bare** symbol name (or an existing file path) → `refuted`. So "scope to
name-existence" is necessary but NOT sufficient — refute only a *unique, bare, non-member* name; everything else
abstains. Never asserts `absent`.
- **Language support (R-7):** ctags' 164 + tree-sitter-language-pack's ~306 grammars cover the common case (a
COBOL repo resolves out of the box). For a truly unsupported language the PROJECT supplies a ctags optlib
(`--langdef`/`--regex-<LANG>` / `--optlib-dir`, no recompile) or a tree-sitter custom grammar via a `.rebar/`
config slot the resolver reads; an unconfigured language → `abstain(unsupported_lang)`.
- The **explicit reference-in schema** the review agent must emit: `{kind, name, in_file?, container?}` where the
**closed set `kind ∈ {symbol, import, dependency, file, member}`** — `symbol`/`import`/`file` are refute-eligible
by name/path existence, `dependency` routes to the T0 deps lane (S3), and `member` (a dotted `recv.attr`) is
T1-abstain (T2 territory). The closed `kind` set is the integration contract; S5 EXPOSES it (does not redefine).
Optional deterministic extraction FROM a diff/file is in scope; prose extraction is NOT.
- Tiered design: universal-ctags is the always-available floor. LSP/SCIP semantic resolution is **T2 — out of
scope here**, deferred to `850f` (servers/builds, non-deterministic).
## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/resolve.py` (+ helpers); reuse `universal-ctags` (repo-wide tags) + tree-sitter for
structural needs; build on S1's contract + harness. grep-ast optional (context display only).
- Avoid stack-graphs (archived). No language servers, no builds (those are T2).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `refute_absence(reference)` returns `refuted` ONLY for a unique bare non-member name/path, else `abstain` (dotted→member-T2; >1 def→`ambiguous`); never asserts absence. Guard validated by spike E2 (naive=1 false-refute → guarded=0).
- [ ] Polyglot repo-wide symbol/file index via **universal-ctags**; per-language coverage recorded; unsupported lang → abstain.
- [ ] Project language-extensibility slot honored (ctags optlib / tree-sitter custom grammar from `.rebar/`); unconfigured language fails open.
- [ ] Reference-in schema with the closed `kind` set {symbol,import,dependency,file,member} defined + validated; optional deterministic code/diff reference extractor.

- [ ] Refutation yield + false-refute measured on a REAL multi-repo corpus (NOT a self-planted fixture; spike E3 = 88% yield / 0 false-refute on rebar's own source), collision + member cases asserting `abstain`; fail-open tested (no tool / parse error / timeout / unsupported lang → abstain).

baseline.summary: Engine A — refutation resolver (universal-ctags T1 floor) + reference-in schema

content.text: Library `ready()` invokes `ready --json`, but the engine `ready` has no `--json`
(only `--format {ids,llm}` and `--epic`), so `rebar.ready()` raises and the MCP
`ready_tickets` tool errors on EVERY call. Reproduced empirically.
- Engine: src/rebar/_engine/ticket-ready.py:168-179 — argparse choices `ids`/`llm`, `--epic`; no `--json`.
- Library: src/rebar/__init__.py:316-318 — builds `["ready","--json"]`.
- Repro: `rebar ready --json` -> argparse exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --json"; `rebar.ready()` -> RebarError(exit 2); MCP `ready_tickets` -> ToolError every call.
## Fix (engine-side — makes the already-written library call correct, and advances the --json epic)

- Add a `--json` mode to ticket-ready.py emitting a JSON ARRAY (decide + document: array of compiled ticket-state objects [consistent with list/search] vs array of ticket ids [matches the default `ids` semantics]). Reuse the existing reducer the `--format llm` path uses.
- Ensure `rebar ready --json`, library `ready()` (already passes --json), and MCP `ready_tickets` all return the structured list. Keep default (no flag) = id-list, and `--format llm` unchanged.
- Prefer NOT to change src/rebar/__init__.py or mcp_server.py (another fix owns those). If the library can't parse the engine output without an __init__.py change, note it.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar ready --json` emits a valid JSON array (shape decided + documented)
- [ ] `rebar.ready()` returns the list (no longer raises); MCP `ready_tickets` returns it
- [ ] default id-list and `--format llm` outputs unchanged
- [ ] Tests cover `ready --json` (bash dispatcher tier) and library/MCP ready

## Summary

Observed LIVE on the deployed bot (2026-07-13): another agent set Autosubmit+1 on a 2-change stack (#644,#645, 'speed up gerrit-verify'). Both were LLM+1/Verified+1/submittable at selection, but main advanced before the bot's submit, so ancestor-atomic submit hit Gerrit 409 'requires fast-forward'. The bot then **emitted AUTOLANDER_ERROR every poll cycle in an infinite loop** (dozens of identical errors), never converging: it did NOT successfully rebase-on-behalf, and it did NOT clear the stack's Autosubmit (both changes STILL show Autosubmit=+1), so it re-selected the same stale stack forever. This floods the rebar-autolander-errors alarm and starves the serial queue (nothing else lands). Mitigated by engaging the S5d emergency-stop sentinel (bot paused).

## Likely root cause(s)
1. The SUBMIT-first design expects a submit-409 (not-ff) to trigger a rebase-onto-tip (drive_to_submit). For this stale STACK, that rebase path did not run (or failed) and fell through to a loud AUTOLANDER_ERROR + re-select.
2. The hand-back that should remove Autosubmit on a failed drive did not clear the votes — plausibly because the votes were cast by ANOTHER account and RebarBotNava lacks permission to remove another user's label vote (Gerrit label-removal perms), so the 'hand back = remove Autosubmit' step silently fails and the change stays selectable. (Related to but distinct from 0d3e, which is about Autosubmit being dropped across the bot's OWN rebase.)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create a 2+ change stack, get it submittable (LLM+1/Verified+1).
2. Advance main so the stack is no longer a fast-forward.
3. Set Autosubmit+1 on the stack (as a non-bot account).
4. Observe the bot select it, submit → 409, and loop on AUTOLANDER_ERROR without rebasing or clearing Autosubmit.

Expected: on a submit-409 the bot rebases-on-behalf + re-CIs + submits; if it cannot (conflict / can't clear Autosubmit), it hands back ONCE (removes its selectability) and moves on — never an infinite error loop.
Actual: infinite AUTOLANDER_ERROR loop; stack stuck; queue starved.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A submit-409 (not-ff) on a selected stack deterministically routes to rebase-onto-tip (rebase-on-behalf) + fresh-Verified await + re-submit, OR a single clean hand-back — never a repeating error loop.
- [ ] The hand-back reliably makes the change non-selectable even when the Autosubmit vote was cast by another account (handle the label-removal permission case, or exclude a just-failed change from re-selection via the S3 marker/backoff).
- [ ] A regression test simulates the stale-stack submit-409 and asserts bounded outcomes (rebase-and-reland OR one hand-back), asserting NO unbounded AUTOLANDER_ERROR repetition.
- [ ] [operator-attested] After the fix deploys, a stale Autosubmit'd stack lands (or hands back once) without looping, and the alarm stays OK.
baseline.summary: Auto-lander loops on AUTOLANDER_ERROR for a stale submittable stack (submit-409 not rebased; hand-back doesn't clear others' Autosubmit)

## Why

The `optionality` workflow (lean-runtime / clean-core-wheel / per-extra / union checks)
casts NO Gerrit `Verified` vote — only `gerrit-verify.yaml` does, and it installs
`.[dev]` (heavy stack present), so the no-extras clean-wheel RUNTIME check never runs
pre-merge. A module-scope heavy-import regression (pydantic_ai/httpx) recently reached
main this way. The static AST guard already runs in Verified via `make test`; the
runtime/packaging jobs do not. Cost to add: ~0 critical-path latency (32s parallel vs
~1235s macOS long pole), ~145 cheap Linux machine-seconds/run.

## What

Extract optionality's jobs into a `workflow_call` reusable workflow and invoke it from
both the push/PR lane and the Verified lane, so a clean-wheel/packaging failure blocks
the Verified vote. Incorporate the critical-review findings (mandatory items below).

## Scope

- New `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` (`on: workflow_call`, inputs for the checkout
  mode), `.github/actions/smart-checkout` composite, thin `optionality.yml` caller,
  `gerrit-verify.yaml` gains an `optionality` job + it is added to `vote`'s `needs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `optionality`'s jobs live in a reusable `workflow_call` workflow, invoked by both
      `optionality.yml` (push/PR, branch-head checkout) and `gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The gerrit lane checks out the EXACT patchset via `checkout-gerrit-change-action`
      (never plain `actions/checkout`, which would resolve to `main` and false-PASS).
- [ ] The `optionality` job is added to `vote`'s `needs` so the run-level conclusion
      aggregation sees a terminal optionality result before Verified is cast.
- [ ] NO `secrets: inherit` on the reusable workflow; Gerrit values passed as plain
      inputs only (prevents fork-PR exposure of GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY via the PR trigger).
- [ ] The third-party `checkout-gerrit-change-action` is SHA-pinned to the same v1.0.2
      commit gerrit-verify uses.
- [ ] `_optionality.yml` declares `permissions: contents: read`; the optionality caller
      job is pure `uses:` (no `steps:`) and independent of clear-vote/require-ticket.
- [ ] Workflows parse/lint clean (actionlint if available) and the push-triggered
      optionality run passes on the change; gerrit-verify runs the optionality job and
      the Verified vote reflects it.
baseline.summary: Add optionality checks to the Gerrit Verified path via a workflow_call reusable workflow

content.text: # S8 — Client walkthrough: self-host Gerrit + rebar review-bot on AWS to gate GitHub
## Why
A client wants the same setup we built in d251 — a self-hosted Gerrit server combined
with the rebar review-bot (which imports the rebar review kernel / `rebar.llm`, the
same library the `rebar-mcp` server exposes) — used to GATE commits to a GitHub repo:
GitHub `main` becomes a read-only mirror that only advances via Gerrit after the
deterministic `LLM-Review` vote passes. We need a reproducible, **secret-free**
walkthrough that lets a client replicate this code-review-enforcement topology on
their own AWS account + GitHub repo, distilled from the d251 artifacts (Terraform,
docker-compose, the Gerrit config scripts, and ADRs 0007-0014).
## What
- A new client-facing guide `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` that walks through, end to end:
1. **Prerequisites** — AWS account + creds, a GitHub repo + an `Administration: write`
token, a domain/DNS zone, Terraform >= 1.10, Anthropic API key.
2. **Provision the AWS base** (Terraform `infra/`) — EC2 + EBS + EIP + DNS + IAM +
the SSM SecureString parameter contract (`/rebar/prod/*`) — referencing ADR-0012.
3. **Deploy Gerrit + the review-bot** (docker-compose behind nginx/TLS) — referencing
ADR-0007 (receiver-not-MCP-over-HTTP) + ADR-0008 (SSM->.env secrets).
4. **Configure the Gerrit project + `LLM-Review` label + submit requirement** —
referencing ADR-0013.
5. **Wire the review-bot identity + webhooks + events-log** — referencing ADR-0014
(inbound auth) + ADR-0009 (the verdict->label pipe / `code_review_decision` seam).
6. **Gerrit -> GitHub replication** (deploy key, non-force) — referencing ADR-0010.
7. **Lock the GitHub repo** to the replication identity — referencing ADR-0011 + S6-pre.
8. **Verify + operate** — the e2e check, the manual `/rerun`, the kill-switch, rollback.
The guide uses the committed `infra/` scripts/config as the source of truth and shows
the operator commands; it does NOT duplicate large config inline.
- **No secrets in committed docs.** All credentials are PLACEHOLDERS sourced from SSM /
CI secrets (never literal). The guide explicitly calls out the secret-handling model.
- **Link from the existing install docs.** Add a link to `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`
from the project's install documentation (README / docs index) as an OPTIONAL /
ADVANCED step titled for "code-review enforcement (self-hosted Gerrit gating GitHub)".
## Scope
In: the `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` walkthrough, the link from the install docs, and a
no-secrets verification of all committed documentation. Out: any NEW infrastructure or
code (S8 reuses and references the d251 artifacts produced by S1-S7); per-client
customization beyond the walkthrough.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` exists and is a complete, ordered client walkthrough
covering all eight steps above (provision -> deploy -> project/label/submit-req ->
bot/webhooks/events-log -> replication -> GitHub lock -> verify/operate), each step
referencing the relevant `infra/` artifact(s) and ADR(s).
- [ ] The new guide and ALL committed documentation in the repo contain NO secrets —
only placeholders; credentials are sourced from SSM Parameter Store / CI secrets.
Verified by a secret scan over the committed docs (and `infra/`).
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` is linked from the existing install docs (README and/or
the docs index) as an explicitly OPTIONAL / ADVANCED step for code-review
enforcement (self-hosted Gerrit gating GitHub) — discoverable from the normal
install path but not required for standard rebar use.
- [ ] The walkthrough's secret-handling section documents the SSM-SecureString -> ephemeral
`.env` model (ADR-0008) and that no credential is ever committed.

baseline.summary: Client walkthrough: self-host Gerrit + rebar review-bot on AWS to gate GitHub

## Summary

Gerrit's outbound email has never worked on the production box (`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`). `/var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` contains **no `[sendemail]` section at all**, so Gerrit falls back to its built-in default SMTP target of `localhost:25`. The official Gerrit container ships no MTA, nothing listens on that port, and every outbound notification therefore fails.

This is the single largest error signature in the Gerrit logs by an order of magnitude — **4,119 occurrences** across the retained history — and it is still firing today.

## Reproduction Steps

1. SSM onto `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (us-east-1).
2. `grep -A6 -iE '\[sendemail\]' /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config` — no
   `[sendemail]` section exists.
3. Comment on, merge, abandon, or push a new patchset to any Gerrit change.
4. `grep 'Cannot email' /var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** either outbound mail is configured and succeeds, or it is
  explicitly disabled (`sendemail.enable = false`) so Gerrit does not attempt it
  and does not log an error.
- **Actual:** Gerrit attempts SMTP on every notification and fails with
  `Connection refused`, emitting a multi-line ERROR + stack trace each time.

## Evidence

Counts over the retained Gerrit logs (`/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log*`, 2026-06-30 → 2026-07-30):

```
Mail Error: Connection refused ....................... 4119
"Cannot email ..." error lines ....................... 3713
  ERROR EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments for N,N ......... 2812
  ERROR EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification for N .........  840
  ERROR EmailNewPatchSet : Cannot send email for new patch set N,N ..  385
  ERROR AbandonOp : Cannot email update for change N ................   40
in the CURRENT (live) error_log alone ................  135
```

Verbatim, most recent occurrences observed 2026-07-30:

```
[2026-07-30T20:49:16.668Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email merged]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.submit.EmailMerge : Cannot email merged notification
  for 1057 [CONTEXT SUBMISSION_ID="1057-1785444..."]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)

[2026-07-30T20:54:05.506Z] [SendEmail-1[send-email comments]] ERROR
  com.google.gerrit.server.change.EmailReviewComments : Cannot email comments
  for 1048,4 [CONTEXT SSH_SESSION="6e14303c" ...]
com.google.gerrit.exceptions.EmailException: Mail Error: Connection refused
    at com.google.gerrit.server.mail.send.SmtpEmailSender.open(SmtpEmailSender.java:457)
```

Daily spread (non-exhaustive sample of rotations) shows it is continuous, not a burst: 06-30 → 2, 07-05 → 108, 07-10 → 230, 07-15 → 117, 07-20 → 17, 07-25 → 58, 07-28 → 56, 07-29 → 21, live log → 135.

## Why this was never caught

- No CloudWatch alarm covers Gerrit SMTP. The host probe publishes
  `voter_errors`, `deploy_errors`, `g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`
  and `review_bot_merge_change_errors` to namespace `rebar/host`, but nothing
  counts email-send failures, so the `rebar-gerrit-*` alarm set stayed green
  throughout.
- The condition was noticed exactly once, in passing, and set aside without a
  ticket: a comment on story `9249` records "the gerrit log also carries a
  pre-existing SmtpEmailSender connect failure. That is unrelated to this story
  (no SMTP change here)". Correct in that narrow context, but no bug was filed.
- A search of all 1,584 tickets for `smtp` / `sendemail` / `Cannot email`
  returns that single `9249` comment and nothing else.

## Impact

- Reviewers and change owners receive **no** Gerrit notification of comments,
  merges, new patchsets, or abandons. Our flow is heavily bot-driven, so the
  functional impact may be small in practice — but that tradeoff has never been
  recorded as a decision anywhere.
- ~4,000 multi-line ERROR + stack-trace entries actively bury genuine errors in
  `error_log`, which measurably raised the cost of this very audit.
- Contrast with `c943`, where the decision *not* to ship voter logs to
  CloudWatch was deliberately recorded in `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`.
  Here there is no configuration and no recorded decision — only silent failure.

## Decision required

Two legitimate resolutions; this bug should pick one explicitly rather than leave the current silent-failure state:

- **(A) Wire up outbound mail** — configure `[sendemail]` against Amazon SES
  (secrets via SSM SecureString + the existing instance role, consistent with
  how `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat` are handled).
- **(B) Disable cleanly** — set `sendemail.enable = false` so Gerrit stops
  attempting delivery, and record the rationale in the runbook.

Research into how actively-maintained Gerrit deployments configure AWS mail is attached as a comment on this ticket to ground that choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision between (A) configure SES and (B) disable cleanly is made and
      recorded in `infra/runbooks/` (not only in this ticket).
- [ ] `gerrit.config` carries an explicit `[sendemail]` section reflecting that
      decision; the config is materialized by the deploy path so it survives a
      compose-up and an autodeploy roll-forward.
- [ ] After the change, a fresh comment/merge/patchset on a Gerrit change
      produces **zero** `Cannot email` / `Mail Error: Connection refused` lines
      in `/var/gerrit/site/logs/error_log`.
- [ ] If (A): a test message is demonstrably delivered end-to-end, and the SES
      sandbox/production-access state is recorded.
- [ ] If (B): the lost functionality is enumerated in the runbook so the choice
      is reversible with full information.
- [ ] Observability gap closed: either the host probe counts email-send failures
      into `rebar/host` with an alarm, or the runbook states why not (mirroring
      the `c943` precedent).
- [ ] File paths: `infra/gerrit/` (gerrit.config materialization),
      `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, `infra/runbooks/`.
baseline.summary: Gerrit outbound email has never been configured: no [sendemail] section, 4119 'Mail Error: Connection refused' since 2026-06-30 and still firing

content.text: ## Why
Three lightweight, ADVISORY/observational reliability additions from the dso gap report (#7 FP
ledger, #10 grounding-health telemetry, #12 approach-viability note). None ever changes the
deterministic verdict or adds a BLOCK source; all are coverage/coaching signals for agent consumers.
## What
Concrete decisions (resolving the plan-review advisories — thresholds named, data-flow specified):
### #7 — fp:code-review ledger + compile step
- Convention doc `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` (the concrete artifact): a confirmed false
positive / invalid finding from the code-review gate is recorded as a `bug`-typed rebar ticket
tagged `fp:code-review`, whose body carries REQUIRED fields — the finding (criterion + finding
text), the diff/context that triggered it, and a `root-cause` drawn from a CLOSED enum:
`false-evidence`, `rubric-overapplication`, `hallucinated-gap`, `scope-mismatch`, `stale-baseline`.
- Light compile tooling `src/rebar/llm/code_review/fp_ledger.py`:
`compile_fp_ledger(repo_root) -> list[dict]` reads open `fp:code-review`-tagged tickets and DRAFTS
no-fire eval cases in the EXISTING eval-spec dataset shape (`{id, corpus: "fp-ledger",
expect: "pass", mode: <root-cause>, diff: <context>}`, matching code-review-*.eval.yaml). It is
IDEMPOTENT: a drafted ticket gets a `compiled` tag and is skipped on re-run (processed-cursor via
tag). Per-ticket ERROR ISOLATION: a malformed/unparseable ticket is skipped + logged, never aborts
the batch, and a rebar-store error surfaces as an empty draft-list (never raises into a caller).
MANUAL to start (Rule-of-Three: the corpus feeds evals once ≥1 ticket exists; no auto-schedule).
### #10 — grounding-health telemetry + low-grounding note
- Named constant `NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES = 20` (module-level in `fp_ledger.py`'s sibling telemetry
home / gate_dispatch): a diff is NON-TRIVIAL iff `changed_lines > NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES` OR
`changed_files > 1`. Single decided value — not two open options.
- Extend `_attach_code_review_metrics` (gate_dispatch.py) `coverage["metrics"]` with:
`findings_per_run` (len(blocking)+len(advisory)), `verify_requests` (sum of the agentic Pass-2
verify step's `_usage.requests` — the SAME mechanism plan-review's `verify_requests` already uses,
so per-agentic-pass request/tool-call counts ARE available), and `grounding_health` band
- LOW-GROUNDING NOTE: when the diff is NON-TRIVIAL and the agentic verify pass made ZERO requests
(`verify_requests == 0`), set `grounding_health = "low"` and emit an advisory
`coverage["grounding_note"]` naming the named threshold. NEVER blocks.
### #12 — approach-viability advisory note
- Named constants `MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY = 3`, `MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE = 0.5`.
- Deterministic post-Pass-3 signal (computed in `_attach_code_review_metrics` from the assembled
verdict + recorder, so it is verdict-independent): if the surviving high-priority advisory count
`>= MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY` OR the Pass-2 drop rate `>= MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE`
(dropped / (dropped+surfaced+blocking), 0 when denominator 0), emit an advisory
`coverage["approach_viability_note"]` for agent consumers. NEVER changes the verdict.
## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/fp_ledger.py` (new: constants + compile step),
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (`_attach_code_review_metrics` enrichment + the two notes),
`docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` (new). Unit tests for each. All advisory/observational — no
verdict-path change, no new BLOCK source.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/code-review-fp-ledger.md` exists documenting: the `fp:code-review` tag, the required
body fields, and the CLOSED `root-cause` enum (five values above).
- [ ] `compile_fp_ledger` drafts no-fire eval cases (existing fixture shape) from `fp:code-review`
tickets, is idempotent (skips `compiled`-tagged), and isolates per-ticket errors — a unit test
pins draft-shape, idempotency, and that a malformed ticket is skipped not raised.
- [ ] `coverage["metrics"]` carries `findings_per_run`, `verify_requests`, and `grounding_health`;
the low-grounding note fires ONLY on a non-trivial diff with zero verify requests, using the
named `NON_TRIVIAL_DIFF_LINES` constant; it never blocks (unit test).
- [ ] The approach-viability note fires on the named `MIN_SURVIVING_HIGH_PRIORITY` /
`MAX_PASS2_DROP_RATE` thresholds and never changes the verdict (unit test asserts verdict
unchanged with/without the note).

baseline.summary: Reliability & process: FP ledger, telemetry, approach-viability note

# Publish the review policy: what the LLM-Review and Verified gates mean for contributors

## Why

rebar's blocking `LLM-Review` Gerrit label appears to be first-of-kind in public OSS: research (2024–2026) found no project documenting a blocking LLM merge vote — the Kubernetes AI-review policy (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/github-management/ai-code-review-tools.md) makes AI review advisory-only. Novelty raises the documentation bar. The document's SHAPE is convergent: Chromium's CQ doc (https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/infra/cq.md) and Zuul's gating doc (https://zuul-ci.org/docs/zuul/latest/gating.html) both name the labels, define each vote value, state bot-vs-human authority, and document escape hatches.

Why a separate doc rather than expanding CONTRIBUTING §2c: §2c is the in-flow quick reference; the policy doc carries the normative content (authority, dispute, bypass, responsibility) that outlives workflow edits and is linkable from every surface. Authority rule (the epic's single-source protocol, clarified): `docs/review-policy.md` is the sole authoritative DOCUMENT for vote semantics; its table's CONTENT is transcribed from the code (the enums below) — document-of-record and source-of-truth are different things and both are named here.

Sequencing note (resolves the file-existence review findings): `docs/your-first-change.md` does not exist at plan time — it is created by story **fat-leaflike-canary**, which this story `depends_on` (edge recorded in the store). The retarget edit to that file executes only after that story lands.

## What

New `docs/review-policy.md` (contributor-facing):

- The two required labels, described accurately:
  - `Verified` — CI on GitHub Actions via `gerrit-verify.yaml`. NOT described as just three make targets: the workflow additionally runs the rebar-ticket trailer check, module-size gate, prompt-index/env-registry drift gates, security-rules freshness, criteria-routing parity, public-types drift, `make config-check`, pip-audit, and unit + integration pytest tiers. The doc states: "locally approximate with `make lint && make typecheck && make test`; the authoritative list is the workflow file (linked)."
  - `LLM-Review` — what the bot reviews; only bots/admins vote either label (no self-approval, no self-verification).
- Vote-semantics table (Chromium style) transcribed from BOTH code sources: the five `_TAG_SUFFIXES` coverage-gap sub-reasons in `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` (gate-disabled, llm-unavailable, scanner, review-error, indeterminate), PLUS the merge-path tags emitted by `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`: the distinct `coverage-gap (merge-review)` veto (~line 160) and the `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix variant. Each row: what it means + the productive response (`finding` → fix and re-push; any `coverage-gap (…)` → infra veto, not your code, maintainer re-triggers; `Verified −1` → open the linked run; `recheck` for flakes). Drift-guard line in the doc: "if you see a tag not listed here, treat it as coverage-gap-class and ping the maintainer" (a CI drift gate tying doc to enums is out of scope, noted as future work).
- Bot vs human authority (Zuul's mechanical-enforcement framing): (a) the lead maintainer sets the rubric and can waive/override any finding; (b) dispute path — resolve the comment thread with written justification or raise to the maintainer, best-effort response within 5 business days (matching SECURITY.md's ack window); if unresolved, the maintainer's decision is final (solo-maintainer reality, stated plainly); (c) the gate supplements maintainer judgment; (d) bypasses are admin-only and auditable.
- Responsibility clause (Kubernetes norm, cited): the submitter must be able to personally explain their change, AI-assisted or not.
- One clarifying paragraph distinguishing THIS (code-review merge gate) from the plan-review ticket gate, linking docs/plan-review-gate.md.
- Framing recorded in the doc itself: the gate is "required-with-human-override"; the dispute path is v1 and will iterate with the first external contributor.

Links this story owns (ownership-inversion rule): add the review-policy link into CONTRIBUTING.md §2c (slimmed to summary + pointer; the full sub-reason enumeration moves out of §2c) and — after the dependency lands — retarget `docs/your-first-change.md`'s vote-semantics link from §2c to the new doc.

## Scope

IN: `docs/review-policy.md` (new), CONTRIBUTING §2c slim-down + pointer, tutorial link retarget (executes post fat-leaflike-canary).
OUT: changing gate behavior/thresholds/criteria; a CI drift gate tying the doc to the enums (future work); the plan-review gate's own docs; Gerrit ACL changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/review-policy.md` present — prove, each as its own grep against the file: "LLM-Review"; "Verified"; "gate-disabled"; "llm-unavailable"; "scanner"; "review-error"; "indeterminate"; "merge-review"; "merge-change"; "recheck"; "5 business days"; "plan-review"; "override"; "dispute"; "bypass".
- [ ] Verified described via the workflow — prove: `grep -q "gerrit-verify" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "approximat" docs/review-policy.md` (the make targets labeled as local approximation).
- [ ] No-self-approval + maintainer-override stated — prove: `grep -qi "self-approv" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "waive\|override" docs/review-policy.md`.
- [ ] Single-source enforced — prove: `grep -q "review-policy" CONTRIBUTING.md` (pointer added) and `grep -c "llm-unavailable\|gate-disabled" CONTRIBUTING.md` = 0 after the slim-down (enumeration lives only in the policy doc); post-dependency, `grep -q "review-policy" docs/your-first-change.md`.
- [ ] Framing + iteration caveat in the doc — prove: `grep -qi "human-override" docs/review-policy.md` and `grep -qi "will iterate\|v1 of this policy" docs/review-policy.md`.
baseline.summary: Publish the review policy: what the LLM-Review and Verified gates mean for contributors

# Exemplar remediation: llm/plan_review/ end-to-end + enable BLE001/T201 with shrinking allowlist

The reference PR. Its diff IS the convention — every other batch copies it. Do NOT parallelize this with
the sweeps; it must land (and lock the lint) before they start. Depends on the logging substrate.

## What
- Remediate every broad-except in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` to the observability floor: log with
  `exc_info` OR carry a justified `# noqa: BLE001` (reason string required). Opportunistic narrowing only
  where a specific type is genuinely expected, with a test.

- Enable ruff **BLE001** and **T201** (scoped) in `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff.lint]`, gated behind a

  pattern from `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`); `llm/plan_review/` is NOT in the allowlist.

  for the legitimate-`print` surfaces — BOTH (a) the CLI presentation layer (`_cli`, `_commands`), where
  `print(json.dumps(...))` stdout output is the machine contract, AND (b) the reconciler subprocess
  (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/`), which legitimately prints operational `RECON:`/`ERROR:` lines to its OWN
  stderr (all 42 existing `# noqa: T201` sites live there, NOT in the CLI).

- [ ] `llm/plan_review/` is excluded from the allowlist (it is fully conformant).
- [ ] `make lint` + full test suite pass.

## Context (parking lot — undesigned; do NOT dispatch)

The project auto-lander (epic f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af) is deliberately **Gerrit-specific, project-owned
infrastructure** — its agent-facing landing command lives in project tooling, NOT `rebar` core,
because landing/merge-queueing is platform-specific and not part of rebar's platform-agnostic
mission.

rebar's roadmap includes **code-review support on broader platforms** (GitHub without Gerrit,
GitLab, …). IF/when a **second** platform needs to land changes, generalize the *portable* part of
the auto-lander into a **provider-abstracted landing seam in `rebar` core**:

- A platform-neutral **`land → typed outcome` interface**, where the outcome enum
  (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed | review_failed`) is the platform-agnostic core.
- **Adapters** per platform own the status-reading + land-request specifics: Gerrit
  (votes/labels/`POST rebase`+submit), GitHub (checks + `mergeable_state` + merge queue), GitLab
  (`detailed_merge_status` + merge trains).
- The project auto-lander (f1fa) would refactor onto the Gerrit adapter with no behaviour change.

This is consistent with rebar's existing **provider-neutral direction** (identity + reconciler:
jira-accountId now, GitHub node-id later).

## Why this is an `idea`, not `open`

**YAGNI / de-frankenstein discipline.** There is **no second platform that needs to land yet**, so
building the abstraction now would be a speculative seam abstracted from a single implementation —
exactly the premature-generalization rebar avoids (cf. the identity epic cutting the keyless/Sigstore
seam until a real need existed). A Gerrit-shaped `rebar land` in core *today* is the premature
version of this. **Promote to `open` only when a concrete non-Gerrit landing requirement appears**
(likely alongside a broader-platform code-review/sync epic), at which point the two real
implementations justify the abstraction.

## Rough acceptance (when promoted — to be designed then)

- [ ] A provider-neutral landing interface in rebar defining the portable typed-outcome contract.
- [ ] At least two adapters (Gerrit + one of GitHub/GitLab) implementing land-request + status-read.
- [ ] The project auto-lander (f1fa) refactored onto the Gerrit adapter with no behaviour change.
- [ ] Driven by a real second-platform need — not built speculatively.
baseline.summary: Platform-agnostic landing provider-seam in rebar core (Gerrit/GitHub/GitLab adapters + portable outcome enum)

# Verifier paths resolve the standard class

## Context / Problem
Three separate code paths pick the verifier model, and all three break off the default provider:
- `review_kernel/verify.py:269` — `verifier_default if model == default_model else (model or
  verifier_default)`. Any non-default model (every Bedrock id) reads as an explicit operator choice,
  so the downgrade silently stops applying.
- `completion.py:332` — `if cfg.model == DEFAULT_MODEL: cfg = replace(cfg, model=...)`. Same inversion,
  separate path.
- `workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — declares no `model:` on any step, so all four code-review passes
  take `cfg.model` and it never downgrades at all. Its Pass-2 pins `temperature: 0` for greedy
  verification, so running it on the frontier model also loses determinism.

## Approach
Replace all three with a single resolution of the `standard` class. The equality test DISAPPEARS rather than being repaired: "the operator chose a verifier" is now expressed by configuring the `standard` slot, not by comparing `cfg.model` to a constant. One mechanism fixes three gates.

**Alternative rejected — fixing the equality rule in place.** It would need a new way to distinguish "operator override" from "provider change" when both arrive as `cfg.model`, and it would have to be repeated on all three paths.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — add `resolve_model_string(value)`: the ONE place that knows the
  reserved class vocabulary. Returns the resolved id for `trivial`/`standard`/`frontier`, and any
  other string UNCHANGED.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `resolve_model` calls it via a LAZY, function-level import. A
  module-level import is IMPOSSIBLE here: `model_classes` imports from `config`, and its docstring
  forbids the reverse. Function-level is the established pattern in this file already
  (`config.py:108`, `:566`, `:768`).
- `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py` — `resolve_verifier_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — `_verifier_cfg` (line 46). A consumer the plan had NOT
  enumerated, with two further call sites at `xcheck.py:198` and `xcheck.py:336`.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — the parallel equality test at line 332.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — express the per-pass class as `model: standard`.
- `tests/unit/` — per-path resolution tests.

NOT in scope, and deliberately: the ladder path (`production_batch_runner.py:93`, `code_review/batch_runner.py:55`) is sibling task 7761. Both tickets call the SAME `resolve_model_string`, which is why the vocabulary lives in one function.

## Testing
Contract tier: the observable is which model id each pass resolves to under a given class config.
- each of the FOUR verifier paths resolves the `standard` class: `resolve_verifier_model`,
  `_verifier_cfg`, `completion.py`'s equality test, and code-review.yaml's verify step.
- with classes configured for a non-default provider, none of them falls back to the framework
  default (the regression this ticket exists for).
- code review's Pass-2 resolves `standard`, not `frontier`.
- a literal model id passed to `resolve_model_string` comes back UNCHANGED (the back-compat
  guarantee that keeps every existing workflow YAML working).

## MECHANISM (decided on parent eb58 — corrected; do not re-derive)

**A workflow step names a class by using the class name as its `model:` value.** The three class names are RESERVED VALUES in the EXISTING model-string space — no new `class:` key, no schema change. In YAML: `model: standard`.

**There is NO single interception point.** An earlier version of this plan claimed `config.resolve_model` was "the ONE funnel every step model passes through". That was wrong three ways, all verified in source:

1. `config.py` cannot import `model_classes` at module level — the dependency runs the other way and
   `model_classes`'s own docstring forbids the reverse.
2. `model_ladder` never reaches `resolve_model`: `production_batch_runner.py:93` does
   `dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=req.model_ladder[0])`.
3. The verifier paths never reach it either — `resolve_verifier_model` is its own path, as is
   `_verifier_cfg`.

So the shape is ONE FUNCTION, several CALL SITES:

    model_classes.resolve_model_string(value: str) -> str
        "trivial" | "standard" | "frontier"  ->  resolve via load_class_slots()
        anything else                        ->  return unchanged

This ticket wires the VERIFIER call sites; sibling 7761 wires the LADDER ones. Keeping the vocabulary in one function is what stops those two tickets from drifting apart.

REJECTED — a new `class:` key: forks a step schema `runs.py` documents as closed, and makes `model: standard` vs `class: standard` a silent ambiguity.

REJECTED — resolving at YAML load time: the mapping depends on process-scoped env/CLI layers, so it would freeze the wrong value in a long-lived process and be invisible to `provider_provenance`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts plan-review Pass-2/Pass-4 resolve the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts the completion verifier resolves the `standard` class
- [ ] a test asserts code-review's verify step resolves the `standard` class rather than `cfg.model`
- [ ] a test asserts that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves
      a model belonging to a different provider
- [ ] `grep -rn "== DEFAULT_MODEL" src/rebar/llm/` returns no verifier-selection site

- [ ] a test asserts a workflow step whose `model:` is the literal string `standard` resolves to the
      configured standard class's model id, and that a step whose `model:` is a literal model id
      resolves to that id UNCHANGED (the byte-for-byte back-compat guarantee)
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier resolves the `standard` class REGARDLESS of what
      `cfg.model` is — including when `cfg.model` is a Bedrock id. MEASURED today:
      `resolve_verifier_model` downgrades ONLY on an exact match against the bare `claude-opus-4-8`,
      so even `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (the SAME model, merely provider-qualified) silently keeps
      Pass-2 on opus. This criterion fails against the current implementation, so it cannot pass
      vacuously
- [ ] a test enumerates the consumers of `resolve_verifier_model` and asserts each resolves the
      standard class — `plan_review/__init__.py:_verifier_cfg` is one the plan had not enumerated
- [ ] a test asserts `resolve_model_string` returns a literal model id UNCHANGED, so existing
      workflow YAML keeps resolving byte-for-byte

# Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

## Why
After merge, the container still makes one call per child. Many children are small — multiple WHOLE children fit
in one call. Packing them reduces calls further, and because G3/G4 are CROSS-CHILD criteria, seeing children
together can IMPROVE consistency detection. Large (parent+child) pairings must keep the single-child path
(ca03 window-fit guarantee).

## What
- Bin-pack whole children into one call up to a token budget = model-window x P8_HEADROOM - output reserve
  (reuse the existing `pair_tokens`/`budget` + P8 machinery). Each child stays WHOLE (never chunked — ca03).
- PRESERVE the single-child path when parent+child strains the window; a child that alone exceeds budget stays
  the existing "too-big -> reduce the ticket" failure finding.
- Structured per-child sections in the prompt + REQUIRED per-child output so per-child attention isn't lost.
- Gate behind an OFFLINE EVAL confirming no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-child-per-call.

## Scope
- In: the bin-packer; multi-child container prompt + required per-child output; single-child fallback; the eval.
- Out: merge (S4, dependency); the caching/parallel substrate (S1/S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Small children are packed into one call up to the window budget; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] A child whose (parent+child) strains the window keeps its own call; a single child exceeding budget yields
      the too-big failure finding.
- [ ] The prompt requires per-child output; an offline eval shows no per-child attention/accuracy loss vs one-per-call.
- [ ] Container call count drops below N for epics with small children; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 5, MINOR 10, BLOCKER 3)
- Bin budget reuses `int(largest_window_tokens * P8_HEADROOM) - P8_OUTPUT_RESERVE_TOKENS` (pass1.py:57-59), summed
  over `parent + ALL packed children`; the single-child fallback (`pair_tokens > budget`) still fires for a lone
  oversized child -> the existing too-big failure finding, unchanged.
- Update the sizing.py container-cost projection for <N calls after packing.
- Fidelity gate = the S6 semantic eval harness (DEPENDS ON S6).
- [ ] Bin budget = parent + all packed children <= P8 window budget; a lone child exceeding it yields the existing
      too-big failure finding; each child whole (never chunked).
- [ ] sizing.py projection reflects the reduced (<N) call count after packing.
- [ ] The S6 fidelity harness shows packed-call findings within tolerance of one-child-per-call.

## CI/eval posture (S6)
- The S6 semantic fidelity eval is a HUMAN-REVIEWED development gate run before merge (live, opt-in), NOT a required/blocking CI check (non-deterministic). The offline eval-spec discipline check still runs on every PR.
baseline.summary: Child bin-packing for container criteria (pack small children, preserve single-child fallback)

## Summary
Creating a cross-level sibling `depends_on` link escalates the source up the hierarchy and can make an epic block itself (a parent gains a `depends_on` on its own child), which is nonsensical and can wedge `ready`/claim-cascade logic.

## Repro
1. Epic E with children: a `story` S (foundational) and several `task`s T1..Tn (all direct children of E).
2. Attempt to record the real dependency `rebar link T1 S depends_on` (a task depending on a higher-level story sibling).
3. Because "blocking deps (blocks/depends_on) are promoted to a comparable hierarchy level", the link source is REDIRECTED from T1 up to the parent epic E. Observed tool output:
   `{"redirected": true, "original": {"source": "T1", "target": "S"}, "resolved": {"source": "E", "target": "S"}}`
4. Net effect: the epic E now has `depends_on -> S`, i.e. E depends on its own child. The intended per-child dependency (T1 -> S) is NOT recorded.

## Expected
Either (a) record the dependency at the level requested (T1 depends_on S) without escalating past a shared ancestor, or (b) reject the link with a clear error, but NEVER produce a parent -> own-descendant blocking edge. A ticket must not end up blocking itself or its own subtree.

## Impact
- Silent: the user believes T1->S was recorded; it was not (the child is left unblocked; the parent is spuriously blocked).
- The epic becomes blocked by its own child, which can distort `ready`, `next-batch`, and the parent-first claim/transition cascade.
- Workaround used on epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864: retype the lower-level children to the SAME type as the foundational ticket (all `story`) so same-level `depends_on` links persist without escalation, then `rebar unlink` the spurious epic->child edge.

## Notes
Discovered while wiring the dependency graph for the T15 plan-review-criterion epic. The escalation/promotion rule is documented in `rebar link` help ("blocking deps are promoted to a comparable hierarchy level"); the defect is that promotion can cross the parent boundary and self-reference the ancestor rather than being clamped below the nearest common ancestor.
baseline.summary: depends_on escalation makes an epic block its own child (parent<-child self-block)

# Outbound CREATE against DC produces no binding: `get_jira_key` returns None after the pass

## Provenance

Surfaced live by harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`) by story 5200's NEW row-1-outbound cell (`test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers`, landed in change 1283). Its author flagged the create-and-bind SETUP as the likeliest first failure precisely because no prior live cell exercises an outbound CREATE against DC — every other outbound cell mutates an issue that already exists and is already bound. The prediction was correct.

## Evidence — verbatim from the run

> the outbound pass did not create-and-bind '654e-8c11-d632-4a01' (get_jira_key returned None), so
> there is no DC issue to read the provenance markers off. Row 1's markers are written INSIDE the
> create (`dispatch_one.py:306-307`), so a missing binding is upstream of this oracle, not a marker
> finding.

The cell localises the failure itself: this is **not** a provenance-marker defect. The pass did not produce a bound DC issue for the local ticket at all, so the oracle never got as far as reading markers.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into 5200

5200's remaining work was "run the harness and read the verdicts"; this is a product finding the run produced, and burying an unexplained outbound-create failure in a story's comment thread is how a defect of this class survives. It is also the SIXTH instance of the epic's recurring shape — "Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half", every instance a SILENT success where the pass reports OK.

## What is NOT yet established, stated plainly

Whether the create was never PLANNED (the differ emitted nothing for an unbound local ticket), was planned but not DISPATCHED, or was dispatched and the binding write failed. Those are three different defects. The harness output does not separate them, and `dispatch_one.py:571-578`-style warn-and-continue swallowing means a dispatch failure would look identical to a planning gap from the outside.

Note also that this cell is the ONLY live coverage of an outbound create against DC, so there is no prior green run to bisect against — the path may never have worked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the failing STAGE is identified — planned / dispatched / bound — with the evidence that
      distinguishes it from the other two
- [x] the root cause is proven, not inferred, and recorded here
- [x] the fix makes `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` GREEN on a live harness
      run, with the run id recorded
- [x] an outbound create that fails to bind surfaces an operator-visible signal rather than a pass
      that reports OK (consistent with [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] AC4)
baseline.summary: Outbound CREATE against DC produces no binding: get_jira_key returns None after the pass

baseline.description:
## Problem

rebar has several independent read-only diagnostic surfaces today — `validate` (repo-wide tracker health), `fsck` (event/store integrity), `bridge-fsck` (Jira bridge mapping audit), and the local-dev-env docs manual checks (stale global build, missing pre-commit hook, unset commit-msg hook, mixed-build reducer cache staleness). Each catches a different failure class, but there is no single entry point that runs them all, explains what is wrong in plain language, and — where safe — fixes it automatically. A user hitting a symptom (a claim silently not gated, a stale cache serving old state, a missing venv) has to already know which of these tools to reach for.

## Scope

Add a `rebar doctor` command that aggregates diagnostics across four areas and offers automatic repair where it is safe to do so:

1. **Configuration** — detect config keys unrecognized by the running build (the "unknown key ignored" symptom), missing/misconfigured `rebar.toml` values, conflicting gate settings (e.g. both `require_signature_for_close` and `require_completion_verification_for_close` enabled).
2. **Environment** — detect a global/stale `rebar` shadowing the repo checkouts venv build, a missing or unwired pre-commit hook (`make hooks` not run), a missing `commit-msg` hook in a fresh worktree, missing `[agents]` extra when LLM ops are configured on, missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` when their features are enabled.
3. **Ticket data** — wrap/extend `validate` and `fsck` findings (orphaned tickets, cycles, unknown event types from a newer store, stale reducer caches from a mixed-build checkout, malformed attestations) into one report.
4. **Sync artifacts** — wrap `bridge-fsck` (orphaned/duplicate/stale Jira bindings) and surface `PUSH_PENDING` (local `tickets` branch ahead of `sync.remote`) and any bridge probe failures.

For each finding, `doctor` should report: what is wrong, why it matters, and whether it can auto-repair or only advise. Auto-repair should be opt-in per run (e.g. `--fix`) and restricted to unambiguous, reversible actions (e.g. re-running `make hooks`, clearing a stale reducer cache, pushing a `PUSH_PENDING` branch) — never destructive or ambiguous ones (never silently rewrite ticket events, resolve bridge duplicates, or change `rebar.toml` values without confirmation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar doctor` runs and reports on configuration, environment, ticket data, and sync artifacts in one pass
- [ ] Findings are categorized by severity and each includes a plain-language explanation and remediation hint
- [ ] `rebar doctor --fix` applies only safe, reversible auto-repairs and reports what it changed
- [ ] `rebar doctor --output json` produces a machine-readable report suitable for CI or scripting
- [ ] Existing diagnostic surfaces (`validate`, `fsck`, `bridge-fsck`) continue to work standalone; `doctor` composes them rather than replacing them
- [ ] Documented in the appropriate docs (README/local-dev-env.md) with examples of common findings and fixes
baseline.summary: rebar doctor command

baseline.description:
## What
Read-only derivations over the durable ticket event store (including compaction-retired `.retired` events) for the agent-process metrics that have a **clean, verifiable event signature today**: attempts-per-ticket, first-pass verification rate, rework at 7/30 days, reopen-recovery, and revert-linked recovery. Metrics whose signal has no reliable event vocabulary yet (escalation, cross-agent handoff/handoff-failure) are explicitly **out of scope for this ticket** and report `Unavailable` from the registry until a later ticket adds their instrumentation — this ticket does not claim them.

## Data-access ground truth (HYBRID — compiled state where one terminal value suffices; raw events where per-event data is needed)
`reduce_ticket(..., include_retired=True)` returns a **single collapsed terminal-state dict, NOT an ordered event sequence** (`src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:127`), and there is **no** public ordered-event API. So this reader is a deliberate **hybrid**, and each metric states which source it uses:
- **Metrics needing per-event or multi-occurrence data (attempts, rework windows, reopen counts)** read the **raw event files**, because compiled state keeps only the *current* value (e.g. one `claimed_session`, one `last_reopened_at`). To read them, **reuse the existing reducer helpers — do NOT reinvent file-listing/sorting/retired-handling**: sort with `rebar.reducer._sort.event_sort_key` (the authoritative chronological key — plain `sorted()` is NOT relied upon), include/exclude compaction-retired events via `rebar.reducer._cache.is_active_event` / `RETIRED_SUFFIX`, and skip `*-SNAPSHOT.json`. Resolve the ticket dir via `rebar.config.tracker_dir(repo_root)` + `rebar._engine_support.resolver.resolve_ticket_dir_name`.
- **Metrics for which a single terminal value is sufficient (first_pass_rate via `last_reopened_at`-absent, revert_recovery via `reverts[]`)** read **compiled state** from `reduce_ticket` — simpler and correct, since only the terminal fact ("was it ever reopened", "does it carry a substantive revert") is needed.

`Verified -1` does **not** exist anywhere in the event schema and is not used (the store's verdict vocabulary is PASS/FAIL/BLOCK plus the `gate_error_v1` ERROR).

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py` — new: read-only functions taking `(repo_root, since, until)`, registered into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py`. Each returns `None` (→ c085 `Unavailable`) when the range yields no qualifying tickets; a genuine measured zero returns `0`.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics.py` — new.

## Metric definitions (each names its source: RAW = raw event files via the reused helpers; STATE = compiled `reduce_ticket`)
- **attempts_per_ticket** [RAW] — distinct claim sessions: read the ticket's event files (sorted via `event_sort_key`, retired included via `is_active_event`), filter to `*-STATUS.json` on the `open→in_progress` edge (`data.current_status=="open" and data.status=="in_progress"`), collect distinct `data.session` (stamped by `_stamp_session`, `txn.py:56-76`). Compiled state keeps only the *current* `claimed_session`, so raw events are required to count multiple attempts.
- **first_pass_rate** [STATE] — fraction of closed tickets in range that were never reopened: `state["last_reopened_at"]` absent (it is set only on a `closed→open` edge, `_processors.py:304-310`, so its absence is a sufficient terminal signal).
- **rework_within_days(n)** for n∈{7,30} [RAW] — tickets with a `closed→open` STATUS edge followed by a later `→closed` edge within n days, measured from raw STATUS event `timestamp`s (multiple edges → raw required).
- **reopen_recovery** [RAW] — count of tickets with ≥1 `closed→open` STATUS edge in range (raw scan; a full count needs every edge, not just the terminal `last_reopened_at`).
- **revert_recovery** [STATE] — tickets whose reduced `state["reverts"]` (records `{target_event_uuid, target_event_type, timestamp, ...}`, `_processors.py:452-462`) contains a revert whose `target_event_type` is `STATUS` or `COMMITS` — a substantive revert, not a revert of a COMMENT/LINK. The terminal `reverts[]` list is sufficient, so compiled state is used.

## Approach
Everything is structurally witnessed and read-only — no new emission. HLC filename timestamps are real wall-clock ns, so date-range bucketing is exact. `source="structural"`, `confidence="high"` (authoritative). Compaction-retired events are included so history survives compaction.

## Tests
- Unit (real temp store; craft raw event files directly with known timestamps/sessions): a ticket with two distinct `open→in_progress` sessions yields `attempts_per_ticket==2`; a `closed→open→closed` 3 days apart counts in `rework_within_days(7)` but not a 10-day gap; a ticket closed and never reopened counts toward `first_pass_rate`; a ticket with a REVERT of a STATUS event is counted by `revert_recovery` while a ticket with only a COMMENT-revert is not; retired (`*.retired`) events are still counted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_event_metrics.py` passes: a fixture ticket claimed by two distinct sessions yields `attempts_per_ticket == 2` (exact), and a single-session ticket yields `1`.
- [ ] a `closed→open→closed` transition 3 days apart is counted in `rework_within_days(7)` and NOT in a variant 10 days apart — both asserted.
- [ ] `revert_recovery` counts a ticket whose `reverts` targets a STATUS event and does NOT count one whose only revert targets a COMMENT — asserted (proves the target_event_type filter).
- [ ] a metric over an empty range returns `None` so `evaluate()` reports `Unavailable`; a populated range with zero qualifying events returns `0` (measured zero) — both asserted.
- [ ] the metrics register into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` with `source="structural"` and are authoritative — asserted.
baseline.summary: Event-derivation readers (agent-process metrics over the durable event store)

baseline.description:
## Problem
The scc LOC/size analyzer for the code_health lens: produces the `loc` payload of `AnalyzerResult [rebar:3b30-2168-ba16-41fc]` from `scc --format json`, fails closed (Unavailable) when scc is unavailable, and never fabricates zeros.

## Approach & rationale (G6/T1/A1 — self-contained, no cross-layer coupling)
`scc_loc.py` is SELF-CONTAINED: it invokes scc via its own `subprocess` and parses the JSON itself (a trivial, stable read of per-file `Code`+`Location`). It does NOT import from `rebar.grounding` — the `analyzers` package stays independent of the grounding layer (clean layering; avoids a metrics<->grounding dependency). Rationale (A1 ANTI-FP): the scc JSON extraction is ~10 lines of field access, NOT a shared abstraction worth cross-layer coupling; grounding's own `_scc_files` serves a different consumer (Engine-B detectors). If a third consumer ever appears (Rule-of-Three), extraction to a shared module is deferred to then (YAGNI now). New analyzers live in `analyzers/` (NOT the quarantined `adapters/`).

## Concrete contracts (single source of truth — 0734 reads these)
- ENTRY POINT: `scc_loc.analyze(repo_root, scan_roots=None, *, run=_run_scc) -> AnalyzerResult | Unavailable`. `run` is an injectable runner (default shells `["scc","--format","json", <root>]` via `subprocess.run`) so tests need no live scc.
- LOC PAYLOAD: `AnalyzerResult.loc = {"files": {<relpath:str>: <loc:int>}, "max_loc": <int>}`. scc JSON is TWO-LEVEL: `data` is a list of language-group objects, each with a `"Files"` array of per-file entries `{"Code": int, "Location": str}`. The parser flattens BOTH levels (`for group in data: for entry in group.get("Files", []): ...`) — the same flattening grounding's `_scc_files` does; iterating `data` directly would yield nothing. Each `Location` is made repo-relative and POSIX-normalized before use as a key: `files[PurePath(os.path.relpath(entry["Location"], repo_root)).as_posix()] = entry["Code"]`. `max_loc = max(files.values(), default=0)`.
- `_ACCRUING_SINCE = "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"` — the SAME module-level ISO-8601 constant value used by the existing metrics reader modules (git_metrics.py / event_metrics.py both define `_ACCRUING_SINCE = "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"`).
- FAIL-CLOSED (returns `Unavailable(reason, _ACCRUING_SINCE)` AND emits `logger.warning("scc unavailable: %s", reason)`): scc binary missing (`FileNotFoundError` from `subprocess`), non-zero exit, empty stdout, or unparseable JSON. A SUCCESSFUL empty result (`[]`, e.g. all-ignored tree) is NOT unavailable -> `AnalyzerResult(loc={"files": {}, "max_loc": 0})`.

## Grounding (E4 — verified via Read)
- CONFIRMED scc emits per-file LOC as JSON (`scc --format json`); each file entry has `Code`/`Location` (engine_b_backends.py:376,412 read exactly these, independently).
- `AnalyzerResult` / `Unavailable(reason, accruing_since)` from prerequisite `[rebar:3b30-2168-ba16-41fc]`; `[metrics]` extra `[rebar:9597-1b85-d2ab-4eed]`; `[code_health]` config `[rebar:e7a0-acef-ec67-42bb]` (all depends_on edges recorded). This adapter does NOT use `resolve_analyzer` (it IS an analyzer implementation).

## Acceptance criteria (observable + proving command; tests use the injectable `run`, no live scc)
- [ ] parse: `run` returns canned scc JSON for files at 100 & 850 LOC -> `analyze` returns `AnalyzerResult` with `loc["files"]` keyed by repo-relative POSIX paths and `loc["max_loc"] == 850`. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc.py::test_parse`.
- [ ] missing binary: `run` raises `FileNotFoundError` -> `Unavailable(reason, _ACCRUING_SINCE)`, no crash, no zeros. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc.py::test_missing_binary`.
- [ ] non-zero exit AND unparseable/empty stdout each -> `Unavailable`. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc.py::test_bad_output`.
- [ ] successful empty output (`[]`) -> `AnalyzerResult(loc={"files":{},"max_loc":0})`, not Unavailable. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc.py::test_empty_tree`.
- [ ] (supplementary) live scc smoke, skipif scc absent. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc.py::test_live -m integration`.

## Rollback: revert is a clean delete of the two new files (no existing file is modified).

- src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/__init__.py (new; package marker)
- src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py (new; self-contained scc invoke + parse -> AnalyzerResult.loc)

# The `supports_temperature` override table is incomplete — the default model is unguarded

## Context / Problem

Story 2932 landed a MEASURED override so Bedrock models that reject `temperature` have it withdrawn rather than hard-failing (`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:95`, consumed at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:399`). The table has exactly ONE entry:

```python
_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES = {
    "us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7": {"supports_temperature": False},
}
```

A fresh measurement sweep shows the behaviour is **family-wide across the opus line and both profile prefixes**, so the single entry leaves rebar's own DEFAULT model unguarded.

## MEASURED — account 896586841071, us-east-1, boto3 `bedrock-runtime.converse`, maxTokens 8

| model id | temp unset | temp=0.0 | temp=0.5 | temp=1.0 | topP=0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | OK | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | OK | OK | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | **400** | OK | **400** |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | OK | **400** | — | — | — |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` | — | **400** | — | — | — |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |
| `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` | ValidationException: invalid model identifier | | | | |

Error text: `ValidationException: \`temperature\` is deprecated for this model.` (and `\`top_p\` is deprecated for this model.`)

## What the data actually says (three corrections to the current model)

1. **`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` is affected, and it is rebar's `DEFAULT_MODEL`** (`config.py:39` = `claude-opus-4-8`). The table does not list it, so the guard does not fire. This is the single most likely Bedrock Pass-1 model — especially under the operator requirement that Pass-1 run opus (see eb6e) — and it would hard-fail the moment any temperature is configured.
2. **The `global.` prefix is affected too.** The table keys on the full model id, so `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` are both unguarded even if the `us.` twins are listed. Any fix keyed literally per-id must cover both prefixes, or be matched on the family portion.
3. **It is NOT 'temperature unsupported' — it is 'explicit non-default sampling rejected'.** `temp=1.0` (the API default) SUCCEEDS on opus-4-8 while 0.0 and 0.5 fail. So the deprecation is of the parameter's *tunability*. `supports_temperature=False` still produces correct behaviour (withdraw the parameter → the model uses its default), but the field NAME misdescribes the mechanism, which matters for the next person extending it.

**`top_p` is deprecated on opus-4-8 as well, and there is no `supports_top_p` on the capability record.** This is currently LATENT, not live: rebar never sets `top_p` anywhere in `src/rebar`. But `failure.py:367` already lists `top_p`/`top_k` as sampling parameters rebar 'can send', so the gap becomes live the day anything sets one.

## Why this matters now

- The Pass-2 verifiers deliberately pin `temperature=0` (`code-review.yaml:155`). That is safe ONLY while Pass-2 stays on sonnet, which accepts it. It is the per-pass model split (eb6e) that keeps this from being an outage.
- The production cutover ships with **no fallback**, so an unguarded 400 here is a stuck gate, not a degraded one.
- `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5` and `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` are NOT invokable in this account at all — worth noting because an earlier note in this epic recorded cache measurements for opus-4-5, and that model id does not resolve here now. Any conclusion resting on it should be re-measured rather than trusted.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — extend the override table (or match on the family portion of the id so both `us.` and `global.` prefixes are covered by one entry).
- `tests/unit/` — a test per newly-covered id asserting the parameter is withdrawn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `capabilities_for("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8").supports_temperature`
      is False. NOTE the PROVIDER-QUALIFIED form: `_model_id_of` returns None for a bare id with no
      colon, so a bare-string assertion passes VACUOUSLY against the conservative record without ever
      exercising the override table. Production always passes `provider:model` or a model object.
- [ ] a test asserts the same for `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and for both `opus-4-7` prefixes
- [ ] a test asserts `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` retains `supports_temperature is True` (the guard must not over-apply and silently drop determinism from the model that supports it)
- [ ] the table's comment records the measured matrix above, including that temp=1.0 succeeds, so the next reader does not re-derive it
baseline.summary: Bedrock temperature override table misses claude-opus-4-8 (the DEFAULT model) and the global.* variants

(precision is Pass-2's job).
## What
