## Reproduction Steps
1. Mount the tickets store and run `rebar verify-identity` against the real store (~3504 events, ~29,575 tracker commits).
2. Observe the command does not complete within 280s (locally exit 124 / timeout).

**Expected:** the merge-gate completes in seconds.

**Actual:** the report loop calls `rebar.attest.authorship.resolve_event_commit` once per non-verified event, and that function runs `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- <pathspec>` — a full-history traversal — per event. With N events and H commits it is O(N x H): 3504 x 29575 here. A bounded `--base HEAD~200` scan also exceeded 180s.

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` cli() loop: for every non-`verified` event it calls `_resolve_commit` -> `authorship.resolve_event_commit` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`), one `git log` subprocess over the whole tracker history each. Enforced-vs-grandfathered adds a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` subprocess per event on top.

## Fix Sketch
Resolve introducing commits in a SINGLE pass: one `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only --format=%H` over the tracker, build a {event-file-path -> commit} map, and look up per event (O(N + H)). Keep the per-event path as fail-closed fallback. Add a perf regression test at representative scale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Introducing-commit resolution for a full-store scan is single-pass (not one git-log per event).
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity` over a store of ~3.5k events / ~30k commits completes in well under a minute.
- [ ] A test asserts the batched resolver returns the same commit SHAs as the per-event resolver on a seeded store.
- [ ] Fail-closed behaviour (unresolvable commit -> enforced) is preserved.
baseline.summary: verify-identity gate is O(events x history): one git-log per event makes CI multi-minute

baseline.description:
## Why
The landing action itself: wait for CI to re-verify the rebased tree (every chain member) and submit the tip atomically so the tested tree is exactly the merged tree (the R5 gate invariant). Split out of S2 (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`).

## Files
- `infra/autolander/loop.py` — fresh-Verified await + ancestor-atomic submit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Fresh Verified (per member):** a `Verified +1` on the exact rebased patchset SHA (not a copied/carried vote). **For a multi-member chain, `rebase:chain` mints a NEW patchset (distinct SHA) per member, so ALL members must carry a fresh `Verified +1` on their own post-rebase SHAs before submit** — submitting while any member lacks a fresh Verified would land an untested tree (violates R5).
- [ ] **Bounded await:** await fresh Verified up to a bounded timeout (default 30 min, configurable, matching `land`'s timeout); on timeout (CI hung), hand the stack back (S2b mechanism) rather than blocking forever. (`LLM-Review` carries `TRIVIAL_REBASE`/`MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE` per ADR-0041; `Verified` re-runs on each new patchset.)
- [ ] **Ancestor-atomic submit** = a single `POST /changes/{tip-id}/submit` on the chain tip. Gerrit submits the chain's members **"Submitted Together"** by relation-chain ancestry (all-or-nothing), reinforced by the **shared topic S3 assigns to the stack** (`stack_id` = the Gerrit topic) with `change.submitWholeTopic` active on this instance. **Partial-land safety (mandatory):** after the submit call, the loop MUST verify **every** stack member reached `MERGED`; if any member is left `open` (a partial land — e.g. members not grouped as expected), it fails LOUDLY (`AUTOLANDER_ERROR` + metric) and hands the stack back rather than proceeding, upholding R3/R5. On full-merge success, close/annotate the associated ticket(s) via `import rebar` ticket ops.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit-test the all-members-fresh rule (submit blocked if any member's SHA lacks a fresh Verified), the bounded-await timeout → hand-back, the **partial-land detection** (a member left `open` after submit → loud error + hand-back), and the **ticket close/annotate on merge** (`import rebar` called with the right ids).
- [ ] [operator-attested] a live check lands one real single-change stack end-to-end (a live run against the deployed Gerrit auto-lander, not a unit test).
baseline.summary: S2c Fresh-Verified-per-member await + ancestor-atomic submit

## Reproduction Steps
1. Merge a change to infra/scripts/observability.sh (e.g. change 491's root_disk_used_percent section) and let autodeploy roll /opt/rebar forward.
2. autodeploy materialises compose/config but never re-runs infra/scripts/install-observability.sh, which is the only thing that copies observability.sh to /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh (the path the systemd timer executes).
3. The timer keeps running the stale copy.

**Expected:** landing an observability change on main reaches the box's running probe on the next deploy. **Actual:** /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh was a Jun 30 copy (7,196 bytes) while /opt/rebar held 16,275 bytes — the deploy_errors (4d), merge-change (4c) and root-disk (2b) metric sections silently never ran in prod. Found 2026-07-10 verifying ac14; remediated one-off by re-running install-observability.sh via SSM. This is the same drift class as incident 2731 (provisioning script not extended with the artifact it must manage), one layer up: the deploy loop does not own installer-materialized artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] autodeploy's materialise step refreshes /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh when infra/scripts/observability.sh changes (re-run install-observability.sh, or install the file directly like other materialised artifacts).
- [ ] A drift check (config-check or a test) fails when the materialised copy can go stale — i.e. the install path is derived from one source of truth, mirroring the b005 --print-volumes pattern.

# Spike: verify Claude Code loads AGENTS.md via a `@AGENTS.md` import

## What

De-risk the whole migration by confirming, hands-on, that a `CLAUDE.md` whose body is a
single `@AGENTS.md` line actually pulls `AGENTS.md` into Claude Code's context at launch
(the mechanism the research identified, but whose live doc page had a fetch bug). Document
the observed precedence/nesting behavior. If the import does NOT work in the installed Claude
Code version, record the fallback decision (symlink `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`, accepting its
Windows/tool-clobber tradeoffs) so downstream stories build on a proven mechanism.

## Scope

A throwaway spike in a scratch dir or worktree — no durable code change. Files touched:
a temporary `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md`. Output is a written finding recorded as a comment on
this ticket (and, if needed, a correction to the approach in the parent epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Confirmed whether `@AGENTS.md` in `CLAUDE.md` loads `AGENTS.md` into context in the
  installed Claude Code build; result recorded as a comment on this ticket with the exact
  version tested.
  - Proving: comment on this ticket stating PASS/FAIL + `claude --version`.
- [ ] If FAIL, the fallback mechanism (symlink vs. content-copy-with-sync-test) is chosen and
  noted so the AGENTS.md story uses it.
- [ ] No stray spike files left in the repo working tree.
  - Proving: `git status --porcelain` clean after the spike.

## De-risking results — SPIKE EXECUTED (PASS, definitive)

Ran headless Claude Code **v2.1.211** in an isolated temp dir: `CLAUDE.md` = `@AGENTS.md`,
`AGENTS.md` held a canary token. The model returned the canary **verbatim** and with **no
approval prompt** → a project-level `@AGENTS.md` import expands into context. Official docs
(`code.claude.com/docs/en/memory`) confirm and recommend exactly this: "Claude Code reads
CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md … create CLAUDE.md [that] imports [it] … add Claude-specific
instructions below the import" (literal example: `@AGENTS.md` then `## Claude Code`). Import
recursion max depth = 4 hops; same-repo imports need no approval (only imports OUTSIDE the
project tree prompt once). **Decision: use the `@AGENTS.md` import — no symlink fallback needed.**
KEY NUANCE: imports "load at launch" and do NOT reduce context, so AGENTS.md must itself be
lean; the token win comes from de-dup into docs (drives S2). This spike is resolved;
implementation is a no-op adopt-the-proven-pattern.
baseline.summary: Spike: verify Claude Code loads AGENTS.md via a `@AGENTS.md` import

content.text: ## Summary
Reducer cache key is filename+size only, so a same-size in-place rewrite of an event file serves stale state.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar comment <id> "AAAA".
2. Overwrite that event file's body so the comment reads "BBBB" (same byte length).
3. rebar show <id> -> still "AAAA" until any other event lands.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: reads reflect on-disk events.
- Actual: compute_dir_hash (ticket_reducer/_cache.py:38-57) hashes name:size (+ .archived marker) only; the docstring even scopes detection to "same filename, different size".
## Impact
git checkout/rebase of the tickets branch, fsck-recover cherry-picks, or any equal-length rewrite serves stale reads through show/list/search (library, CLI, MCP).
## Source
src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_cache.py:38-57.
## Fix direction

Include st_mtime_ns in the hash parts (stat is already performed for size; expect ~zero overhead — see validation notes comment for measurement). Content hash is the stronger alternative if mtime granularity worries arise.
## Suggested RED test
Same-size overwrite -> fresh state on next read; cache still hits when nothing changed.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Same-size in-place rewrite invalidates the cache (RED test first)
- [ ] No measurable read-path regression (cache still effective on unchanged dirs)
- [ ] Docstring updated to the new invariant

baseline.summary: Reducer cache serves stale state after same-size in-place event rewrite

baseline.description:
## Symptom
Under `verify.enforce_plan_material_pins=true`, the plan-review CLOSE gate rejects a valid,
unchanged **planning-phase** attestation with `incompatible-phase` (`planning -> execution`),
even though the plan material never drifted. Closing then requires a fresh execution-phase
review that cannot be minted after code drift (the drift-refresh path re-signs the prior
planning manifest), so the ticket cannot be closed.

## Root cause — an undocumented override that contradicts the design
The phase mechanism (ticket 5967, "Add planning and execution phases") and the close gate
(ticket 2bbd, "Require a separately attested current plan review at close") deliberately make a
planning attestation COMPATIBLE with an execution-phase ticket at close. `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
§"phase_status compatibility" documents exactly this: `execution | planning or legacy planning |
compatible`. 2bbd's stated purpose is to catch a plan that CHANGED during execution — via
own-material + pin drift — "without invalidating every implementation because implementation
files changed." It never required a fresh execution-phase review.

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py::compute_validity` contains a later override (added by
ticket 145e, "enable ... enforcement for rebar", gated on `enforced`) that forces
`phase_status = "incompatible"` when `profile is CLOSE and signed_phase == "planning"`. This
directly contradicts the documented table and 2bbd/5967's design, and is documented nowhere.
The one concern cited in 145e's trail ("an in-progress self-edit must invalidate close until a
fresh execution review") is already covered by own-material-drift invalidation, so the override
is broader than any real requirement.

## Fix
Remove the `enforced`-gated CLOSE override (and the paired CLOSE-only `current_phase` promotion
to "execution") so the CLOSE profile uses the same documented `review_phase_status` table as
DEFAULT/DRIFT_REFRESH. A planning attestation certifies close iff the plan material/pins have not
drifted; a drifted plan still invalidates and forces a re-review. The implementation is validated
independently by the completion-verifier close gate. (Secondary, out of scope here: the drift-refresh
path is reached even under `--force`, contradicting the `__init__.py` comment that `force` bypasses
it; noted for a follow-up but not required once the gate accepts either phase.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Under `enforce_plan_material_pins=true`, `close_plan_review_gate_check` returns
      `ok=true, verdict="certified"` for an unchanged planning-phase attestation.
- [ ] A plan/pin change during execution still invalidates at close (material/pin drift), forcing
      a re-review — unchanged.
- [ ] The `planning`-current + `execution`-signed row stays `incompatible` (base table unchanged).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states the CLOSE profile uses the same compatibility table.
- [ ] Tests that encoded the undocumented override are inverted to the documented behavior.

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_validity.py
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py
- docs/plan-review-gate.md
baseline.summary: plan-review CLOSE gate rejects a valid unchanged planning-phase attestation (undocumented override contradicts 5967/2bbd design + docs)

baseline.description:
# Prompt caching writes on every gate call and is never read across calls: the marked prefix is not stable

## Observed — measured, with a control

Two `rebar review-plan` runs executed BACK TO BACK, seconds apart, well inside the ~5-minute cache TTL, on two DIFFERENT tickets (1c39 then 9baf), with REBAR_USAGE_LOG capturing every call. All calls on Bedrock via the project default. Per-call figures:

    pass                                RUN A in / write        RUN B in / write        RUN B read
    plan-reviewer (frontier/opus)        5286 / 2800             5394 / 2908             0
    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier    3809 / 1545             3872 / 1608             0
    plan-review-verifier                 7136 / 4871             7199 / 4934             0
    plan-review-coach                    1999 / 0                2062 / 0                0
    ticket-digest (trivial/haiku)        2131 / 0                2816 / 0                0
    TOTALS                               write 9216, read 0      write 9450, read 0

RUN B WROTE THE CACHE AGAIN INSTEAD OF READING IT. Every read is zero in both runs.

## The mechanism this points at

Each pass's cache-WRITE size tracks its input size almost exactly across the two runs (plan-reviewer 5286 -> 5394 input, 2800 -> 2908 write; verifier 7136 -> 7199 input, 4871 -> 4934 write). A cache prefix that were genuinely stable would produce the SAME marked prefix and therefore a hit on the second run. That the write grows in step with per-ticket input says the MARKED PREFIX ITSELF VARIES PER CALL — i.e. per-ticket content is landing ahead of the cache breakpoint, so the cache key is unique every time and can never be reused.

`capabilities.cache_settings_for` marks the INSTRUCTIONS plus tool definitions, and `structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` derives the marked size from the SYSTEM PROMPT. So the hypothesis to test first is that the rendered system prompt/instructions embed per-ticket material (the plan text, the ticket digest, or similar) rather than being invariant across runs.

## What is NOT the explanation — ruled out by evidence

* NOT "caching is off on Bedrock". Three of five passes write thousands of tokens per run, so the
  settings are emitted and the provider accepts them.
* NOT "the read path is broken". Intra-CALL reuse demonstrably works: the production review bot's
  multi-step agentic records read large caches within a single call — e.g. a code-review pass with
  steps=9/125 logged cache_read=386204 against in=430479, and another with steps=17/125 logged
  cache_read=493547. Those are steps 2..N reusing what step 1 wrote inside one conversation.
* NOT the sub-minimum-prefix condition for the three writing passes. That condition explains the
  two passes that write ZERO — coach (whole prompt small) and ticket-digest, where the diagnostic
  fired verbatim: "only 477 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
  4096-token minimum, while 8634 of the 9111 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked". It does
  not explain a pass that writes 4871 tokens and then never reads them.

## Why it costs money rather than being merely untidy

A cache write is billed at a PREMIUM over ordinary input; a read is billed at a steep discount. The current behaviour pays the premium on every gate call and collects the discount only within a single multi-step call. For single-step passes — which is every pass in a plan review, all five records show requests=1 — the write is pure loss: nothing ever reads it. Every plan review on this project pays roughly 9,000-11,000 premium-rate cache-write tokens for zero benefit.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` `cache_settings_for` — where the breakpoints are placed.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` `estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` and the ineffective-cache
  diagnostic — the estimate is the instrument that would have caught this and did not.
- whatever renders the plan-review system prompt / instructions, if that is where per-ticket
  content is crossing the breakpoint.

## Approach — investigate before changing anything

The first task is NOT a fix, it is to identify precisely which bytes sit ahead of the breakpoint and whether they vary per run. Capture the rendered system prompt for the same pass on two different tickets and diff them; the varying region is the defect's location. Only then decide whether the fix is to move per-ticket content behind the breakpoint (into the user message) or to split the instructions into an invariant prefix and a per-run suffix.

Do NOT "fix" this by disabling caching on single-step passes: that trades a real, measurable premium for giving up the cross-call discount entirely, and the cross-call discount is the larger prize once the prefix is stable. Note also that the existing diagnostic's advice — "the changeable thing is where the breakpoint sits, not the size of the prompt" — is exactly right here and was never triggered for the writing passes, so consider whether the predicate should also flag "wrote every call, never read".

## Testing

- an oracle that renders the same pass's marked prefix for two different tickets and asserts they
  are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is the RED test: it should fail today. Verify RED before any fix.
- a live two-run oracle (the experiment above) asserting cache_read > 0 on the second run for at
  least the frontier pass, run inside the TTL.
- a guard that the ineffective-cache diagnostic fires when a pass writes on every call and never
  reads, so this class cannot recur silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the bytes that vary ahead of the cache breakpoint are identified and cited, with a diff of
      the rendered marked prefix for one pass across two different tickets.
- [ ] the marked prefix for a given pass is byte-identical across tickets, pinned by a test
      verified RED against today's behaviour.
- [ ] a second run of the same pass inside the cache TTL records cache_read > 0, evidenced by an
      actual usage-log capture rather than by inspection.
- [ ] the diagnostic in `structured_run` also flags the write-every-call-never-read shape, so a
      regression is loud.
- [ ] the cost change is stated with figures — premium-rate write tokens per review before and
      after — so the benefit is measured rather than asserted.
baseline.summary: Prompt cache is written on every call and never read across calls: the marked prefix varies per ticket

content.text: RISK 3 (worst single unit). `reconcile_once()` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:556-1315` is a ~760-LOC monolith coupling snapshot-load -> diff -> apply -> persist -> log plus corrupt-snapshot abort + OM->Mutation conversion. It is stable (not actively breaking) but untestable per-phase and the highest-touch reconciler file. Decompose IN-PLACE (the natural sub-blocks are below the 100-LOC file floor, so the module-size policy prescribes in-file helpers, NOT a new module).
## Why

No sub-phase can be tested or reused without invoking the whole orchestrator; 5-deep nested error handling lives in the spine. `_apply_batch` in applier.py (handled in the sibling Risk-2b ticket) is the related deep function.
## What — in-place helper extraction along existing seams
- Extract `_load_snapshots()`, `_run_differs()`, `_apply_mutations()`, `_persist_and_log()` as module-level (in-file) helpers; keep `reconcile_once()` as a thin sequencer that calls them in order.
- Lift `_handle_corrupt_snapshot()` out of the spine into its own helper.
- Preserve the single-pass IDEMPOTENT contract and the corrupt-snapshot abort semantics exactly.
## Scope

In: behavior-preserving in-place decomposition + per-phase unit tests now made possible. Out: creating a new file (sub-blocks are <100 LOC), changing the reconcile contract, touching the acli subprocess boundary.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `reconcile_once()` body is a thin sequencer; the four phases + corrupt-snapshot handler are separate in-file helpers.
- [ ] At least the load/persist phases gain direct unit tests (previously impossible).
- [ ] reconcile.py stays in the allowlist if still >800, but `reconcile_once` itself is materially shorter and max nesting drops.
- [ ] Full reconcile idempotency + corrupt-snapshot-abort tests pass byte-for-byte.

# Land dependabot PRs #123 (actions bumps) and #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1) through Gerrit

## Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot still opens PRs there (#123, #124), but they can never merge — the updates have to be re-landed as Gerrit changes and the PRs closed by hand. Two are open now:

* **PR #123 — github-actions group**: `actions/setup-python` 6 -> 7 (new pinned SHA
  `5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97`) across 13 workflow files, plus a re-pin of
  `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` v1.14.0 to SHA `dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33`
  (upstream re-tag; version unchanged). The change also updates the two `echo` allowlist
  lines (the pinned-action identity allowlist) that mirror those SHAs.
* **PR #124 — uv-lock group**: `mcp` 1.29.0 -> **2.0.0 (major)** — pyproject constraint
  loosened `>=1.28.1,<2` -> `<3` in both the `mcp` extra and the dev group, new transitive
  `mcp-types` package in `uv.lock` — and `ruff` `0.15.22` -> `0.16.1` (pinned in the dev
  group; ruff is what `make lint` and the pre-commit hook run).

The mcp major is the risk: `rebar-mcp` imports v1 API paths — `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` (mcp_server.py:570, scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:72), `mcp.server.auth.settings` / `mcp.server.auth.provider` (mcp_server.py:590, _mcp_auth.py:38), `mcp.server.transport_security` (mcp_server.py:512), `mcp.types.ToolAnnotations` (_mcp_models.py:287). Whether 2.0 keeps these paths as compat shims is exactly what the test suite must decide; the upstream migration guide lists every breaking change.

**P0 escalation (2026-08-02):** CI's gating `pip-audit` scan (\`_build-and-test.yml\` `pip-audit` job — part of every `Verified` run) now fails on **click 8.2.1 → PYSEC-2026-2132** (command injection in `click.edit()`; fix 8.3.3), which neither dependabot PR covers (click is a transitive-only dependency — not constrained in pyproject.toml, pinned only in `uv.lock`). Because the scan gates every Verified run, EVERY change is blocked until the fixed lock lands — so this ticket gains a Change 0 that must land FIRST. Change 0's own Verified run scans Change 0's own committed lock, so it can pass while everything else cannot; there is no circular block.

## What — three independently reviewable Gerrit changes

### Change 0 (P0, lands first) — click 8.3.3 lock bump

In the worktree: `uv lock --upgrade-package click` (expect click 8.2.1 -> >=8.3.3 in `uv.lock` only; pyproject.toml is untouched since click is transitive), `uv sync --all-extras`, then `pip-audit --desc` locally (must report no known vulnerabilities) and the targeted suite for the CLI surface that consumes click plus `make lint` / `make typecheck`. Push, wait for both votes (its Verified run proves the unblock), Submit.

All changes carry this ticket's trailer and land through the normal gate (`LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, then Submit). Apply each PR's diff verbatim (`gh pr diff N | git apply`), never retyped by hand, so the landed content is byte-identical to what dependabot proposed (SHA pins included).

### Change A — PR #123 (workflows)

Apply `/tmp`-fetched `gh pr diff 123` onto a fresh worktree at current main. 13 workflow files + the allowlist echo lines. No source code is touched; the `Verified` CI run on the Gerrit change itself exercises the bumped `setup-python@v7` on every job that uses it — that run IS the functional validation. Risk note: setup-python v7 migrated to ESM and requires a node24 runner (ubuntu-latest provides it); no inputs we use were removed (we do not pass `pip-install`).

### Change B — PR #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1)

The `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` constraint has two consumers OUTSIDE pyproject.toml that PR #124's diff does not touch and this change must keep coherent:

* `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:105` installs `'mcp>=1.28.1,<2'` into a clean venv
  for the MCP-optionality job — on path 1 bump it to `,<3` in the same change (else CI
  exercises v1 while the package ships v2); on path 2 it stays `<2`, matching the kept
  pin.
* `docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md:28` records the `<2` pin and its
  rationale (DNS-rebinding fix GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f) — on path 1 amend the ADR text with
  a dated note that the ceiling moved to `<3` (the floor still covers the GHSA); on
  path 2 it stays accurate as written.

Apply `gh pr diff 124` (pyproject.toml + uv.lock) onto a fresh worktree, `uv sync --all-extras`, then decide on evidence:

1. **Compat shims hold** (expected path): the full test suite (`make test` — the MCP
   surface that imports the at-risk v1 paths is covered by
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp*.py` — nine modules incl. `test_mcp.py`,
   `test_mcp_http_transport.py`, and the five `test_mcp_auth*` modules — plus
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py`), `make
   lint` (now ruff 0.16.1), and `make typecheck` all pass — possibly after mechanical
   fixes (new ruff rules, import-path renames with 1:1 replacements, updated
   deprecation-warning filters). Mechanical fixes ride in the same change.
2. **Breakage is structural** (FastMCP/auth API gone or semantics changed): do NOT force
   the major through this ticket. Land the safe subset instead — ruff 0.16.1 bump +
   `uv.lock` refresh with mcp kept `<2` — comment the evidence (failing test names,
   import errors) on this ticket, and file a follow-up ticket for the mcp v2 migration
   linked `discovered_from` this one; PR #124 is then closed with a comment pointing at
   the landed subset + follow-up.

`ruff format --check` may newly fail on files 0.16.x formats differently; run `.venv/bin/ruff format src/ tests/ scripts/` and include the mechanical reformat in the change if so (it is what every subsequent commit's pre-commit hook will enforce).

### Closing the PRs

After each Gerrit change merges: `gh pr close <N> --comment "<landed as Gerrit change <url>; GitHub is a read-only mirror>"`. Dependabot sees the manifest change on the next mirror sync and stops re-opening.

## Scope

* IN: the two PR diffs, mechanical fixes needed to keep the gates green under the bumped
  ruff/mcp, closing PRs #123/#124 with provenance comments.
* OUT: any non-mechanical mcp v2 migration work (follow-up ticket if path 2 triggers);
  dependabot config changes; other open dependency updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0 (P0): a Gerrit change bumping click to >=8.3.3 in uv.lock is merged FIRST; its CI run's pip-audit step passes (PYSEC-2026-2132 cleared), unblocking all other changes.
- [ ] AC1: A Gerrit change with PR #123's diff (13 workflows + allowlist echo lines,
  byte-identical to `gh pr diff 123`) is merged with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`;
  the Verified run executed `actions/setup-python@v7` successfully.
- [ ] AC2: A Gerrit change for PR #124 is merged: either (path 1) the full diff with mcp
  2.0.0 + ruff 0.16.1 PLUS the two out-of-pyproject constraint consumers updated
  (`_optionality.yml:105` -> `,<3`; ADR 0050 amended with the ceiling-move note) and all
  of `make test`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` green, or (path 2) the documented safe
  subset (ruff bump, mcp kept `<2`, `_optionality.yml` and ADR 0050 untouched) plus a
  `discovered_from`-linked follow-up ticket for the mcp v2 migration.
- [ ] AC3: Both PRs #123 and #124 are closed on GitHub with a comment naming the Gerrit
  change(s) that landed the content.
- [ ] AC4: The decision evidence for Change B (test results under mcp 2.0) is recorded as a
  comment on this ticket.

## Verification commands

* `git diff <base>..HEAD -- .github/workflows | diff - /tmp/pr123.diff` (byte-fidelity, Change A)
* `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test && make lint && make typecheck` (Change B, in its worktree)
* `gh pr view 123 --json state`, `gh pr view 124 --json state` -> `CLOSED`
baseline.summary: Land dependabot PRs 123+124 through Gerrit (actions v7, mcp 2.0, ruff 0.16.1)

## Context / Problem
Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in tests are the proven CI flake class under runner contention (19d7, 5e94, edfe, 85c3). 15 sites scanned: 13 upper-bound in scope, 2 lower-bound out of scope; 11 currently unescaped. Detector prototype (regex + escapes) caught all, 0 FPs, and found one site manual scan missed (test_lock_stale_reclaim.py:127).

## Approach
DET BLOCKING code-review criterion scanning tests/** for upper-bound wall-clock asserts. Escapes: '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' line marker, or the existing perf-lane CI-exclusion guard '@pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("CI") == "true", ...)' on the test (the idiom the benchmark tests in tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py:245-249 already use — NOTE: the '@pytest.mark.benchmark' marker alone is NOT an escape — it is registered (pyproject.toml, informational) but no CI invocation filters it out (the suite runs -m 'not integration and not external'), so a benchmark-marked test still executes on CI; the skipif(CI) guard is what actually removes runner-contention flake risk). Migrations (proven by experiment): tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201 -> spy config._ordered_layers, the miss-path filesystem walk load_config only calls on a _RESULT_CACHE miss (reset_config_cache seam; regression sim caught 10/10); tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 -> exactly one pending_enrichment call + zero drain/spawn. Remaining 9 sites get markers with reasons. Optional follow-on: migrate reducer benchmarks to _api.replay_events spy to restore CI coverage (currently benchmark-skipped). Seed implementation from /tmp/exp4_detector.py; proxy rule: spy the MISS-PATH function, never tomllib (warm TOML cache evades parse spies). Self-exclusion: the detector's own unit-test file carries live upper-bound asserts as RED fixtures, so it is structurally excluded via the sibling guards' EXCLUDED_FILES idiom (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:57 — the exact failure b047 recorded when its fixtures self-tripped the comment-hygiene guard).

## Scope
- detector as DET code-review criterion (review-bot checkout) or CI lint per gate conventions
- tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201, tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 migrations
- markers on the 9 hang-guard sites

## Testing
Detector unit tests: unescaped upper-bound assert -> finding; hang-guard marker escape -> silent; skipif(CI) guard escape -> silent (bare '@pytest.mark.benchmark' without the skipif guard -> still a finding); lower-bound assert -> silent. Migrated tests: regression simulation goes RED (cache cleared per call / drain forced), warm path GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Detector blocks new unescaped upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests/** with a teaching message naming both escapes (hang-guard marker; skipif-CI perf-lane guard).
- [x] Both migration sites assert counting proxies (miss-path spies), proven RED under regression simulation.
- [x] All remaining in-scope sites carry reasoned markers; detector run on the tree is clean.
- [x] Detector has unit tests covering fire, both escapes (marker; skipif-CI guard — and bare benchmark marker NOT escaping), and lower-bound exclusion.
baseline.summary: Wall-clock upper-bound assert detector (DET blocking code-review criterion) + 2 site migrations

# Outsider onboarding: a warm "your first change" tutorial layered on CONTRIBUTING.md

## Why

CONTRIBUTING.md §1–§3 already documents the external Gerrit path (GitHub OAuth, clone-from-Gerrit-as-origin, hook, refs/for/main, the two votes, the §2e submit-authorization callout) — the gap is not information but SHAPE: it is a complete reference, not a first-contact narrative, and nothing on GitHub funnels an outsider into it. Every surveyed Gerrit-keeping project ships a dedicated first-change tutorial distinct from the reference (Go's contribute guide, LibreOffice GetInvolved, Wikimedia Gerrit/Tutorial); JGit proves a web-OAuth Gerrit needs only a short one. This story adds the tutorial layer and the funnel links; it does NOT restructure CONTRIBUTING.md's reference content.

## What

- New `docs/your-first-change.md`, 800–1500 words (one authoritative range; target ~1000), Go's two-layer structure (one-time setup vs per-change loop), LibreOffice-warm tone, consistent with CONTRIBUTING.md §1–§2 (same commands, same remote naming — the outsider clone uses `origin` = Gerrit, so pushes are `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main`; never the internal dual-remote `gerrit` name):
  1. How review works here (3 sentences): Gerrit not PRs; two bot votes gate submit; GitHub is a mirror. For vote semantics, link CONTRIBUTING.md §2c now; the review-policy story (which depends on this one) will retarget that link to `docs/review-policy.md` when it lands — this tutorial does NOT duplicate the vote table (epic single-source rule).
  2. One-time setup (~5 min): sign in at rebar.solutions.navateam.com with GitHub OAuth → generate HTTP password (Settings → HTTP Credentials) → clone via the authenticated `/a/` URL → install the commit-msg hook (one sentence demystifying Change-Id). Include the two common account-setup failure states (OAuth loop / hook curl failing) as gotcha rows.
  3. Your first change: branch from main → commit with `git commit -s` (DCO sign-off; brief, links CONTRIBUTING's DCO section once the DCO story lands — until then links developercertificate.org) AND the `rebar-ticket:` trailer. The outsider ticket flow, specified in-scope (no deferral): open a GitHub issue describing the work; the maintainer files the rebar ticket and replies with the id to put in the trailer; for tiny fixes the shepherded-patch path (CONTRIBUTING) skips Gerrit entirely. → `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main` with the magic ref demystified → reading a −1: link the authoritative vote-semantics doc; summarize only "finding = fix and re-push; coverage-gap = infra, not your code; Verified −1 = CI, comment `recheck` for flakes" without enumerating sub-reasons (the enum lives in one place) → `git commit --amend --no-edit` + re-push → final step: "a maintainer submits once both votes are green — you don't need (and won't see) a Submit button until you're added to Contributors" (mirrors CONTRIBUTING §2e; no false promise the outsider lands it themselves).
  4. Gotchas table: missing Change-Id; pushed to `main` instead of `refs/for/main`; new commit instead of amend; missing sign-off; missing/unresolvable rebar-ticket trailer; CI flake; OAuth/hook setup failures.
  5. See-also → CONTRIBUTING.md as the full reference.
- CONTRIBUTING.md: light edits only — add a prominent link to the tutorial near the top ("first time? start here"); no restructuring (the reference is already externally accurate).
- `docs/README.md` (audience-indexed docs ToC): add the tutorial under the Contributor section.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`: add the tutorial link alongside the existing CONTRIBUTING pointer (the PR template is an outsider's first contact until the lockdown bot lands).

## Scope

IN: `docs/your-first-change.md` (new), CONTRIBUTING.md top-link, `docs/README.md` index entry, PR-template link.
OUT: README.md front-door work (own story: README front door); restructuring CONTRIBUTING.md; the DCO section and shepherded-patch section (owned by the DCO and PR-posture stories, which add their own cross-links INTO this tutorial when they land — ownership-inversion rule); vote-semantics table (review-policy story); video/asciinema tutorials; changes to review gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/your-first-change.md` exists — prove: `wc -w docs/your-first-change.md` in [800, 1500]; covers the nine-beat sequence (account → credential → clone → hook → branch → signed commit w/ trailer → push refs/for → respond → amend/re-push) — prove: grep hits for `refs/for/main`, `commit-msg`, `--amend`, `commit -s`, `rebar-ticket:`.
- [ ] Zero Nava-internal references on the happy path — prove: `grep -cE "feature-branch-drivers|CLAUDE|dual-remote|push gerrit " docs/your-first-change.md` = 0 (the push remote is `origin`).
- [ ] The outsider ticket flow is actionable without sibling stories: the GitHub-issue → maintainer-files-ticket → trailer loop is fully described in this doc.
- [ ] Submit expectations match reality — prove: doc states a maintainer performs Submit for first-time contributors (no instruction that the outsider presses Submit).
- [ ] No duplicated vote table — prove: the doc links CONTRIBUTING §2c (or review-policy.md once retargeted) and does not enumerate coverage-gap sub-reasons.
- [ ] Funnel links present — prove, one grep PER FILE (multi-file grep -q passes if any one matches, so each is its own check): `grep -q "your-first-change" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "your-first-change" docs/README.md`; `grep -q "your-first-change" .github/pull_request_template.md`.
baseline.summary: Outsider onboarding: your-first-change tutorial, CONTRIBUTING restructure, README front door

# D — Correct the AGENTS.md rule so it is true (precondition for it being followed)

## Context / Problem

This story is **not** a rewording for emphasis; it is a correctness fix, and it is a precondition for stories A and B being trustworthy.

`AGENTS.md` currently says: "**Prefer its symbol tools over `grep`** when finding or following references … It resolves 'who calls / imports this?' reliably (definitions + references, not text matches)". That claim is **false in an important case**, verified in this repo against Serena/Pyright:

- `find_referencing_symbols` on `_anthropic_cache_settings` returned the import plus all five real call sites,
  but did **not** return `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:90`
  (`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_anthropic_cache_settings", ...)`). The symbol is named by a **string
  literal**, so there is nothing for the LSP to resolve.
- That exact class broke epic `061c` story S1: the identical monkeypatch pattern for
  `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` passed `tests/unit` and only surfaced in full-suite pre-flight. An agent
  following the current rule *exclusively* would have missed the site that failed.
- Separately, Serena's index can lag edits: it reported `runner.py:336` / `test_structured.py:175` when the
  current tree had `:341` / `:176`, after a commit in the same session rewrote 79 lines of `runner.py`.
- In the other direction, `grep` produced false positives Serena did not: two `output_mode()` matches that were
  **comments** (`runner.py:78`, `:160`).

A rule that is wrong some of the time trains agents to discount it all of the time — which is a plausible contributor to the original failure. Encoding the division of labour makes the rule safe to follow literally.

## Approach

Replace the bare preference with a short decision table, and keep it short — the aim is a rule an agent can apply correctly without re-deriving these findings.

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| who calls / imports a symbol | Serena `find_referencing_symbols` — semantic, no comment false positives |
| symbol named as a **string**: `monkeypatch.setattr`, `getattr`, `importlib` | `grep` — the LSP cannot resolve these |
| current line numbers after recent edits | `grep` on the working tree — the LSP index can lag |

Keep it lean per `AGENTS.md`'s own standing instruction (one-line pointers, not restated sections); the supporting evidence belongs in `docs/`, not inline.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md` §"Navigating the codebase (when editing rebar itself)" — the table replacing the bare preference.
- `docs/` — a short note recording the LSP string-literal blind spot and the stale-index caveat, with the
  verified examples, if a suitable doc home exists.

## Testing

Documentation change; verified by review rather than by test. The claims in the table are each backed by a reproducible check recorded on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` no longer states an unconditional preference; it states the three-row division of labour
- [ ] the string-literal blind spot is named explicitly with `monkeypatch.setattr` as the concrete example
- [ ] the stale-index caveat is named, with the guidance to trust the working tree for line numbers
- [ ] the section does not grow by more than a few lines (the file's own leanness rule), with detail in `docs/`
- [ ] the reminder text shipped in story A and this table do not contradict each other
baseline.summary: D — Correct the AGENTS.md rule so it is true (LSP string-literal blind spot)

## Summary
The completion-verification close gate's deterministic referencing-commit precondition (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `_completion_precheck` / `_referencing_commit_exists`) evaluates a ticket in isolation: it blocks the close of any ticket that records `file_impact` unless a commit references **that ticket's own id** via a `rebar-ticket:` trailer. A parent (epic/story) whose code is delivered by its children's commits therefore cannot close — even though every child landed a referencing commit and closed signed — forcing a `--force-close` that leaves the parent unsigned.

## Reproduction Steps
- [ ] Create an epic with `file_impact` set (a planning hint) and decompose it into children.
- [ ] Implement each child; each commit carries a `rebar-ticket: <child>` trailer (not the epic's id). Close each child (they close signed).
- [ ] `rebar transition <epic> in_progress closed`.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** The precondition credits the parent's entire descendant subtree — if the epic (or any descendant) has a referencing commit, the "work landed" precondition passes, the completion verifier runs on the epic's own criteria, and the epic can close **signed**.
- **Actual:** `Error: cannot close <epic>: it records file_impact (a code change) but no commit references it.` The gate never looks at descendant commits, so the only way to close is `--force-close` (unsigned).

## Design
Evaluate the referencing-commit precondition over the ticket **and its entire descendant subtree** (transitive — an epic is satisfied by grandchild task commits). Build the accepted-id set = `{ticket}` ∪ all descendants (via `rebar._engine_support.descendants.list_descendants`), resolve each, and pass the precondition if **any** commit trailer resolves into that set. `_referencing_commit_exists` takes a set of resolved ids and returns True on the first match.

Soundness: the open-children guard runs first, so a parent only reaches this precondition once all children are closed, and each child already passed this exact referencing-commit check at its own close — so crediting descendants cannot admit unlanded work. Stays deterministic (no LLM).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`: the referencing-commit precondition passes when a `rebar-ticket:` trailer references the ticket **or any of its descendants** (transitive subtree via `list_descendants`); a ticket with `file_impact` and no referencing commit anywhere in its subtree still fails closed.
- [ ] `_referencing_commit_exists` accepts a set of accepted resolved ids and returns True on the first commit whose extracted+resolved ref is in the set (behavior for the single-id case is unchanged).
- [ ] The block message names the subtree (e.g. "no commit references it (nor any of its descendants)").
- [ ] A leaf ticket (no descendants) with `file_impact` and its own referencing commit still closes; a leaf with `file_impact` and no referencing commit still fails closed (no regression).
- [ ] Tests cover: parent with file_impact + a grandchild referencing commit → precondition passes; parent with file_impact + no subtree commit → fails closed; leaf unchanged (both directions).
baseline.summary: close gate: credit descendant commits when checking a parent's referencing-commit precondition

# Repo-snapshot isolation for code-reading gates

## Context

The rebar MCP server is a long-lived process pinned to ONE working directory. Every operation
that reads PROJECT SOURCE CODE (the LLM gates) reads whatever branch + uncommitted changes
happen to be in that checkout at call time. This session hit it: a completion-verifier read
the wrong branch (a parallel task had switched the shared checkout) and produced a FALSE-
NEGATIVE on work correctly merged to main. Broader problem: an MCP server used by a DISTRIBUTED
TEAM concurrently cannot have all gates read one mutable working tree, and an HMAC-signed
verdict computed against a moving branch is not reproducible. Design grounded against Gitaly,
Sourcegraph gitserver/zoekt, GitHub tarball API, Bazel, ccache, Nix, in-toto.

## What

Every code-reading op accepts `ref` (branch|tag|SHA, default `origin/main`) + `source` mode:
- **attested** (default): fetch -> resolve ref to immutable SHA -> faithful lock-free
  materialization into a content-addressed snapshot -> run gate -> record `verified_at_sha`
  and bind it via the EXISTING SIGNED MANIFEST CHANNEL (a manifest step, NOT a payload-schema
  change — so no PAYLOAD_VERSION bump, no invalidation of prior signatures; see S4). Reproducible.
- **local** (opt-in): read the server's in-place checkout (possibly dirty); NEVER signs.

## Children (de-risking order)

Riskiest piece first — the lock-free portable snapshot primitive — then build outward:
1. S1 `hoot-glove-foyer` (6d56) — faithful, lock-free materialization core (the primitive).
2. S2 `clay-feast-strife` (70c7) — content-addressed snapshot cache: single-flight + reader-safety (depends on S1).
3. S2b `dodgy-luff-quasar` (b73c) — snapshot cache JANITOR: reclamation under disk pressure (depends on S2).
4. S3 `pale-peer-hawk` (fa49) — thread ref+source through the 5 gates (depends on S1).
5. S4 `ill-hazel-probe` (30b3) — attested signing: pin verified_at_sha via the manifest channel (depends on S3).
6. S4b `piney-gold-day` (e308) — claim-gate<->plan-review ref-resolution coherence + ADR 0002 (depends on S4).
7. S5 `harm-shove-gate` (b7fa) — CLI + MCP surfaces (depends on S3).
8. S6 `vain-weed-rave` (1ba5) — docs (depends on S4, S5).
Blocking edges encode this DAG. A thin vertical slice (S1 + the cache + one gate re-rooted
end-to-end) proves the snapshot primitive before the horizontal sweep.

## Out of scope

Sparse archiving; verdict memoization; auto ticket->commit provenance (REB-289); diff-base
(base+head) for code-review (single ref/snapshot like the others); serverless lifecycle (AWS
volume placement + EFS/NFS flock caveat tracked on alto-fruit-punch).

## Architecture decision record

The novel cross-cutting patterns (content-addressed snapshot layout, delete-on-last-close
reader safety, flock GC interlock, read-tree+checkout-index over `git archive`, dropping the
rejected PID+heartbeat lease, manifest-channel SHA binding) are captured in an ADR (authored
in S2/S4) so future maintainers see the decision + rejected alternatives.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No code-reading gate reads the server's working tree in attested mode; all read a
      faithful snapshot materialized at the pinned SHA.
- [ ] A signed verdict binds `verified_at_sha` via the signed manifest channel (no payload-
      schema/version change; prior signatures still verify) and is reproducible against that SHA.
- [ ] `local` source mode reads the in-place checkout and CANNOT produce a signed verdict;
      source=local is the documented back-out that restores the prior in-place read behavior.
- [ ] Concurrent gates on the same and different SHAs run without git-lock contention or
      cross-op corruption; the snapshot cache + janitor reclaim disk under a defined free-space
      watermark (S2) without disrupting in-flight reads.
- [ ] Private-repo fetch failures surface a descriptive, actionable credential error.
- [ ] Portable across macOS + Linux (no external tar; no hardcoded /tmp; flock+mkdir fallback).
- [ ] Operational tunables (free-space watermark, default ref, grace/age windows) are
      configurable with documented defaults (S2/S3).
- [ ] An ADR captures the architecture + rejected alternatives (PID-lease, payload-schema SHA binding).
- [ ] All EIGHT enumerated child stories (above) closed; `make lint` + full test suite green.
baseline.summary: Repo-snapshot isolation for code-reading gates (client ref, attested signing, concurrency-safe portable snapshots)

baseline.description:
## Why

The plan-review claim gate invalidates a signed attestation whenever the criteria-registry
stamp (`regver:`) differs from the current one. `regver` hashes the FULL effective routing
index — including every criterion's free-text `check` string — so any edit to
`criteria_routing.json`, however cosmetic, rotates the stamp and invalidates EVERY
outstanding plan-review attestation repo-wide at once.

Measured on this repo: renaming one phrase in a single `check` string rotates the stamp
(`b058e30f0de6a907` -> `23913c1f6987711b`) and would invalidate the attestations held by
632 tickets (~40 open/in_progress), forcing a full LLM re-review before any of them can be
claimed. That is a false invalidation: the attestation truthfully certifies that the plan
passed the criteria AS THEY STOOD AT SIGNING TIME, and a later wording change does not
falsify that statement.

ADR 0015 introduced the check to stop a project activating/editing/disabling a criterion and
then claiming against a review that never saw it. The concern is real but the remedy is too
blunt: it cannot distinguish a criterion being tightened from a typo fix, so it charges a
full re-review for both. The result is that criteria maintenance is effectively frozen.

## What

Grandfather plan-review attestations across criteria-registry drift: a `regver` mismatch (or
a missing `regver:` line on an older manifest) no longer blocks the claim. The drift is still
DETECTED and REPORTED — it becomes advisory metadata on the validity result instead of a
blocking verdict — so `review-plan --status` and the gate UX can still say "reviewed under an
older criteria registry".

Explicitly unchanged: `stale-code`, `stale-head`, `stale-material`, `stale-reopened` and the
signature check all keep blocking. Only the registry-version dimension is grandfathered.

Also unchanged: the drift-refresh eligibility path (`registry_unchanged` in
`attest._signature_branch_decision` / `_sidecar_branch_decision` / `drift_floor`). That flag
decides whether a cheap refresh may REUSE a prior verdict versus running a full review; it
never blocks a claim, and keeping it conservative is correct.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — the plan-review branch of `compute_validity`
  (the `stale-regver` early return): stop returning `valid: False`; annotate the result.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py` — the docstring listing possible verdicts.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — `registry_version` docstring, which currently
  states a rotation invalidates a prior attestation.
- `docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md` — new ADR, amends ADR 0015.
- `docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` — add an amended-by pointer.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the two verdict lists that name `stale-regver`.
- Tests listed under Testing.

OUT OF SCOPE: the Success-Criteria -> Acceptance-Criteria rename itself (separate ticket);
any config surface for forcing re-review on a material criteria change (recorded as future
work in the ADR).

## Approach

In `compute_validity`'s `kind == _MANIFEST_PREFIX` branch, replace the early
`return _result(False, ..., "stale-regver")` with a non-blocking capture: compare the signed
`regver` against `registry_version(repo_root)` and, on mismatch or absence, record
`registry_drift = {"signed": ..., "current": ...}`. Let control fall through to the remaining
freshness checks (`stale-code` / `stale-head` / `stale-material`) unchanged. Attach
`registry_drift` to the returned dict via the existing `_result` helper so every downstream
result carries it uniformly.

The signed `regver` continues to be read from the AUTHENTICATED manifest (`auth_manifest`),
never its plaintext mirror — the reporting path must not become a channel for unauthenticated
data (ADR 0049 / the opcert binding tests).

## Testing

- `tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py` — two cases currently asserting
  `verdict == "stale-regver"` invert to: valid, with `registry_drift` populated.
- `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` — same inversion for the overlay-change cases.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py` — the "no weakening" regver case becomes
  "grandfathered but reported"; the PLAINTEXT-corruption case must still prove the signed
  manifest is authoritative (unchanged assertion for `stale-code`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate_heldout.py` — drop `stale-regver` from the
  verdict->message mapping.
- NEW: a regression test proving a registry rotation alone leaves a claim UNBLOCKED while
  `stale-code` on the same attestation still blocks — pinning that only the registry
  dimension was grandfathered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plan-review attestation whose signed `regver` differs from the current
      `registry_version(repo_root)` returns `valid: True` from `compute_validity`, and the
      ticket can be claimed without a fresh `review-plan`.
- [ ] The same result carries `registry_drift` with the signed and current stamps, so the
      drift is reportable rather than silent.
- [ ] A manifest with NO `regver:` line is likewise grandfathered (valid), not rejected.
- [ ] `stale-code`, `stale-head`, `stale-material` and `stale-reopened` still return
      `valid: False` — proven by a test that rotates the registry AND drifts a dependency
      file on one attestation and asserts the verdict is `stale-code`.
- [ ] The signed `regver` is read from the authenticated manifest only; corrupting the
      plaintext mirror does not change the reported `registry_drift`.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md` exists, states the amendment to
      ADR 0015, and records the accepted consequence that a criteria TIGHTENING no longer
      retroactively forces re-review.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass, and the change carries Gerrit `Verified +1` (CI). Evidence for this criterion is a gate RUN, which leaves no artifact in the codebase; it is attested by the recorded CI vote and command output on this ticket.
baseline.summary: Grandfather plan-review attestations across criteria-registry (regver) drift

## Why / Summary

Outbound comment sync is non-idempotent: `get_comments()` fetches only the FIRST
PAGE of a Jira issue's comments, so the dedup in `_diff_comments` re-posts every
local comment outside that page on every reconcile pass. Over time this inflated 13
Jira issues to the 5000-comment hard cap (local truth: 22-76 comments each); once
capped, further comment adds fail `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — and because
acli returns exit 0 on that FAILURE, the failure is swallowed as a silent no-op.

## Root cause (proven)

`get_comments()` in BOTH `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_cli_ops.py:516`
and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli.py:653` invokes
`acli jira workitem comment list --key <k> --json` with NO `--paginate` and NO
`--limit`. acli defaults to `--limit 50`, `--order +created` (oldest first), so the
call returns only the 50 OLDEST comments — despite both docstrings claiming "Get all
comments." Runtime-verified against REB-155: response `{isLast:false, maxResults:50,
startAt:0, total:5000}`, 50 returned. `_diff_comments`
(`outbound_comments.py`) then compares each local comment against only those 50
bodies and re-emits any not present as an "add".

## Reproduction Steps

1. A Jira issue bound to a rebar ticket has > 50 comments, and the local ticket's
   comments are not all within the oldest-50 page.
2. Run a reconcile pass (or call `_diff_comments` with a live client whose
   `get_comments` returns page 1 only).
3. Observe: `_diff_comments` emits "add" mutations for local comments already present
   in Jira (beyond page 1) — Expected: 0 adds for an already-mirrored ticket.

- Expected: a steady-state pass emits **0** comment "add" mutations for a ticket
  whose comments are already mirrored to Jira, regardless of Jira comment count.
- Actual: it re-emits the comments not on Jira's oldest-50 page every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `get_comments()` returns the COMPLETE comment set for an issue (paginates all
      pages), in both `acli_cli_ops.py` and `acli.py`. Proving command:
      a unit test builds a fake acli that returns 3 pages (e.g. 50+50+20=120) and
      asserts `get_comments` returns all 120 — fails on the current single-page code.
- [ ] `_diff_comments` emits 0 "add" mutations when every local comment is already
      present in Jira but only beyond page 1. Proving command: unit test with a
      >50-comment Jira snapshot where the matching local comment is comment #75 —
      asserts empty mutation list; RED on current code.
- [ ] The full reconciler unit suite passes: `make test` (or
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler -q`).
- [ ] No new external dependency introduced; change is confined to the two
      `get_comments` call sites (+ tests).

## Notes

Fix = add `--paginate` (acli ignores `--limit` when paginating) OR loop startAt
until `isLast`. Prefer `--paginate` for parity with `acli`'s own pagination.
This is P1 of epic 58b0. The 13 capped Jira issues need a separate data cleanup
(sibling ticket) AFTER this fix deploys, else the buggy reconciler re-inflates them.
baseline.summary: get_comments fetches only page 1 -> non-idempotent comment re-posting inflates Jira to 5000-comment cap

## What
An OPTIONAL, isolated adapter that harvests coverage % and CI-health (run status, duration, red->green recovery, flake/recheck rate) from GitHub Actions run history and persists them as labeled snapshots into the going-forward store, so those trends stop depending on GHA's short log-retention window. The core command does not depend on this adapter.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/adapters/github_actions.py` — new isolated adapter: parse a GHA run's coverage (anchored word-boundary grep for the pytest-cov `TOTAL` line in the run-log tail) and CI-health from run-metadata JSON (status/conclusion, duration, and — across a fail->pass pair — a red->green recovery interval; recheck/flake rate from repeated runs on one commit).
- `scripts/harvest_gha.py` — new: pull recent `test.yml` run logs + run metadata (via `gh`/the Actions API), run them through the adapter, and append labeled snapshots to the snapshot store. This SCRIPT is the persistence path (run locally/by a maintainer), NOT the CI workflow.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_gha_adapter.py` — new.

## Snapshot store path & why NOT the CI workflow
Snapshots are written via `src/rebar/metrics/snapshot.py` to the git-tracked **`.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson`** (the established store path — `reports/` is gitignored; do NOT use it). **The `.github/workflows/test.yml` is deliberately NOT edited to commit snapshots**: the CI workflow runs with `permissions: contents: read` and CI checkouts are ephemeral, so it cannot commit a file back to the repo, and committing from CI is out of scope and fragile. Instead the harvester reads coverage/CI-health from the GHA API/run-logs after the fact and writes the tracked snapshots itself — which is exactly what removes the dependency on the retention window. (The coverage `TOTAL` line is already emitted to the run log by the existing pytest-cov step, so no workflow change is needed for the harvester to read it.)

## Approach
CI runs on GitHub Actions; coverage is in the run-log tail and CI-health in the run metadata, but only within a short retention window — so the harvester captures that window into the durable `.rebar` store. To keep the harness portable, the GHA source is an isolated adapter the core command never imports; a parallel adapter could target another CI. Log parsing is anchored (word-boundary grep for the coverage `TOTAL` line). Emitted snapshots carry `source="snapshot"` (or a CI-health-specific label) so they sit in the going-forward series. Additive and optional.

## Tests
- Unit (fixture log text + run-metadata JSON — no network): the adapter extracts the coverage % from a fixture log tail and computes a red->green recovery interval from two fixture runs; the emitted record carries the snapshot label. The core-command isolation is asserted by scanning the core module source for an adapter import.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_gha_adapter.py` passes: a fixture `test.yml` coverage log yields the parsed coverage % (`assert pct == 84.2`) and two fixture runs (fail then pass) yield the expected red->green recovery duration.
- [ ] `scripts/harvest_gha.py` writes the harvested coverage/CI-health as snapshots to `.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson` (the tracked store), verified by a test feeding it fixture run data (adapter output stubbed/injected) and reading the snapshots back via `read_snapshots` — proving the persistence path and the correct store path (NOT `reports/`).
- [ ] the portability guard holds: a unit test asserts the CORE metrics modules (`src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` and `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py`) do not import the GHA adapter (and the future `_commands/metrics.py` from 9a5a is held to the same rule).
baseline.summary: GitHub-Actions coverage + CI-health harvest adapter (optional, isolated)

content.text: # Add CI as a second Gerrit gate vote (`Verified`) via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions
## Context
The v1 code gate (epics d251 infra + b744 code-review, both closed) uses a SINGLE
deterministic vote: the Gerrit `LLM-Review` label, cast by the review-bot's four-pass
blocker. The intended end state requires BOTH (a) LLM review AND (b) CI (build / test /
lint / typecheck) to pass. This epic adds the second, independent vote — the Gerrit
`Verified` label — cast by CI.
**This runs against the LIVE Gerrit-gatekeeper topology** (Gerrit owns `main`; GitHub is a
locked, read-only mirror). It is a **proof-of-concept** that mechanically proves the
review/signing/gate flow with a real, independent CI vote — used by 1–2 developers on one
project, with agentic development producing frequent commits.
### Decision log (2026-07-01 brainstorm — grounded in prior art + verified)
- **Runner = GitHub Actions**, reusing the existing `.github/workflows/test.yml` checks. The
rebar GitHub repo is **public**, so Actions is free (incl. macOS) and the run page is a
**zero-auth, contributor-viewable log surface** — satisfies "clients can view logs" at no cost.
- **Integration = adopt `gerrit-to-platform` (g2p) WHOLESALE**, the LF RelEng Gerrit→GitHub-
Actions bridge, exactly as ONAP / O-RAN-SC / OpenDaylight / FD.io deploy it (~96 repos carry
a `gerrit-verify.yaml`) — the only mature, production-proven pattern for this integration. A
bespoke hybrid was **explicitly rejected** (Frankenstein). Jenkins+Checks and Zuul are
faithful but presuppose a standing CI fleet for multi-repo scale we don't have — rejected.
- **The CI `Verified` vote is an authenticated Gerrit label vote** (service account over SSH),
NOT a per-vote HMAC attestation.
- **Verified facts (no longer open):**
- `hooks` / `replication` / `webhooks` are Gerrit **core plugins** — bundled in `gerrit.war`,
enabled via `init --install-plugin` or copy-from-war; **NO external download / sha256 pin**
(that discipline is only for the non-core `events-log` / `oauth`).
- `lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action` `vote-type` vocabulary = `clear|success|failure|
cancelled`; `clear` → `--label Verified=0` (resets to 0; also zeroes `Code-Review`, harmless
as that label is disabled on this project). `success→+1`, `failure|cancelled→-1`.
- **Two entailed posture changes accepted** (g2p production standard; the ADRs are reconsiderable):
1. **Broaden replication to change refs** — **reversal of ADR-0010**. **NOT wildcard `refs/*`**
(that would replicate `refs/meta/config`, which embeds the webhook token — ADR-0010/0014
keep it off GitHub): use a **scoped** `refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` refspec alongside
existing lines, `replicatePermissions = false` retained, `refs/meta/*` excluded.
`checkout-gerrit-change-action`'s `gerrit-url` fallback covers replication lag.
2. **Inbound GitHub→Gerrit SSH vote path** — a Gerrit service account whose private key is a
GitHub Actions secret; the workflow SSHes into Gerrit (29418) to cast `Verified`.
- **Runtime placement (decided): g2p runs INSIDE the Gerrit container** via an extended image
(`FROM gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1` + Python ≥3.11 + `pip install gerrit-to-platform`).
Rationale: the `hooks` plugin execs `$site/hooks/*` **from inside the container**, so the hook
scripts' Python interpreter MUST live in the container — a host-side g2p (with hooks symlinked
into the bind-mounted `$site/hooks/`) is broken, because the container process cannot resolve a
host interpreter path. Consequence: the PAT flows via the **existing container-secret path**
(`fetch-secrets.sh` → compose `.env` → container env), NOT a host-side materialization hack.
## Locked design (the g2p production pattern)
- **Trigger:** g2p Gerrit `hooks` (`patchset-created` / `comment-added` / `change-merged`)
`workflow_dispatch` a `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` with the nine `GERRIT_*` inputs.
Single repo → no org `.github` "magic repo"; a local, non-`required` workflow.
- **Workflow = fixed 3-job shape**, all actions SHA-pinned:
1. `clear-vote` → `gerrit-review-action vote-type: clear` (Verified→0; GerriScary-safe reset),
then a short `sleep` for replication.
2. `build-and-test` → `checkout-gerrit-change-action` (fetch the exact `GERRIT_REFSPEC`) then
**our existing `test.yml` steps** (lint / typecheck / test matrix incl. macOS + module-size
/ prompt-index / criteria-routing gates + coverage floor).
3. `vote` (`if: always()`) → `im-open/workflow-conclusion` then `gerrit-review-action
vote-type: ${{ WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION }}` → `Verified` +1/-1, **run URL in the vote message**.
- **Gate:** new `[label "Verified"]` (NoBlock, ±1, `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`
mirroring `LLM-Review`) + `[submit-requirement "Verified"] submittableIf = label:Verified=MAX`;
voting restricted to Service Users. Final gate:
`label:LLM-Review=MAX AND label:Verified=MAX AND -has:unresolved`.
- **Re-run:** g2p `recheck` ChatOps (`comment-added` → `verify`); a new patchset auto-cancels the
prior run (`concurrency: cancel-in-progress`). The g2p hook should **retry** transient
`workflow_dispatch` failures; a persistent failure leaves `Verified=0` (fail-closed) AND alerts.
- **Fail-closed = surfaced block, not silence:** any dropped hook / failed run yields no `+1` ⇒
no submit, and raises the S6 alarm.
### GerriScary-safe non-negotiables (CVE-2025-1568)
Required together: patchset-scoped vote (tested refspec) + `copyCondition` reset on real code
change + `clear-vote` reset at run start + `Verified` votable only by the CI service account +
submit requirement keyed on the current patchset.
## Secrets & credentials (infra invariant — no plaintext)
New credentials: the **g2p GitHub PAT** (used by g2p in the Gerrit container) and the **CI
service-account SSH key** (a GitHub Actions secret used by the workflow to SSH back). Both MUST
follow the SSM-SecureString pattern, adding slots to **`infra/terraform/ssm.tf`**
(`rebar_secret_params`, `ignore_changes=value`). Because g2p now runs **in the container**, the
PAT materializes via the **existing** container-secret path — `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`
already writes `infra/compose/.env` (consumed as container env), so just add the PAT leaf to its
fetched set: no host-side materialization, no plaintext PAT in `gerrit_to_platform.ini` on disk.
The PAT MUST be **fine-grained, single-repo (`navapbc/rebar`)** (Actions r/w, Contents+Metadata r)
— NOT a classic org-wide PAT. Define **rotation + retire** for both (compromise + PoC decommission).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **S1 — Gate config** (`infra/gerrit/project.config`): add `[label "Verified"]` (NoBlock, ±1,
`copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`) + `[submit-requirement "Verified"] submittableIf
= label:Verified=MAX`; grant the CI service account's group `label-Verified -1..+1`.
**Activate the two-vote submit requirement LAST** (after S3–S5 prove the voter) to avoid
blocking all submits during rollout. Update `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` (gate section) and
write the ADR that supersedes/amends **ADR-0013** (gate is now two independent votes).
- [ ] **S2 — Replication broadening** + ADR: add the **scoped** `refs/changes/*` refspec (NOT
`refs/*`) to `infra/gerrit/replication.config`, keeping `replicatePermissions = false` and
excluding `refs/meta/*`; update the refspec table in `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`; write the ADR
superseding/amending **ADR-0010**; confirm the mirror-lock ruleset still bars non-replication
writes to `main`.
- [ ] **S3 — g2p install** in the Gerrit **container**: extend the image (`FROM
gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1` + Python ≥3.11 + `pip install gerrit-to-platform`) so the
in-container hook exec resolves its interpreter — host-side placement is rejected (the
`hooks` plugin execs `$site/hooks/*` inside the container); enable the `hooks` +
`replication` **core plugins** (from the war — no download/sha256; update
`infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md`); at container start, symlink the three console-script hooks
into the volume-mounted `$site/hooks/` pointing at the in-container g2p paths; write
`gerrit_to_platform.ini` (PAT via the container-env path from Secrets) + `replication.config`
symlink + `recheck → verify` mapping; write the ADR recording **g2p adoption** + the
in-container runtime decision. **Coexistence proof (concrete):** push a test patchset and
observe BOTH the review-bot webhook `LLM-Review` vote AND the g2p `workflow_dispatch` fire.
- [ ] **S4 — Service account + credentials:** provision the CI Gerrit service account via
`infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (account + group + `Verified` ACL); add the SSH key + PAT
slots to **`ssm.tf`** and add the PAT leaf to **`fetch-secrets.sh`** (container-env path, per
Secrets — no host-side materialization); set GitHub repo vars `GERRIT_SERVER` /
`GERRIT_SSH_USER` / `GERRIT_KNOWN_HOSTS` / `GERRIT_URL` and secret `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY`; write
the ADR recording the **inbound GitHub→Gerrit SSH vote path** (blast radius, key scope,
rotation/retire).
- [ ] **S5 — The workflow** `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`: the 3-job shape (`clear-vote`
→ `build-and-test` reusing `test.yml` steps via `checkout-gerrit-change-action` → `vote` off
`WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`), all actions **SHA-pinned**. `vote-type: clear` semantics are verified
(Verified→0). Decide test.yml convergence (recommend the `gerrit-verify-manual-dispatch.yaml`
hybrid so one file serves Gerrit dispatch + manual/branch runs).
- [ ] **S6 — Monitoring, back-out, E2E proof + docs:** add a **CloudWatch alarm** for g2p
hook-dispatch failures and `Verified`-vote failures — detection modelled on
`monitoring_s4b.tf` + `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (publish a metric from a journald log
pattern, as `voter_errors` does; name the log source + pattern + metric). Document + test a
**back-out** (disable the `Verified` submit requirement to restore single-vote gating). On the
live Gerrit, prove red CI blocks submit, `recheck` re-runs, a green change with both votes
submits + replicates; update `CONTRIBUTING.md` (two-vote flow + `recheck`); capture design
notes (cost / latency budget, flaky-test handling, `copyCondition` re-run behavior). Record
the change URL + votes.
## Deployment sequencing & risk
- **Ordering:** S2 (replication) + core plugins (S3) → S3/S4 (g2p + creds) → S5 (workflow) → prove
the voter green → **only then** S1 activates the two-vote submit requirement (S6 E2E). Closes the
"gate enforced but no voter exists" window (all submits blocked).
- **Failure surfacing:** g2p hook→`workflow_dispatch` failures (network / rate-limit / bad PAT)
retry, then alert (S6) — never silently leave a change unvotable.
- **New file consumers (name in the child stories):** `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`,
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`, `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, `infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md`,
`docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`.
## Decomposition
Six stories (S1–S6). S2 + core plugins are earliest; S3 depends on S2 + plugins; S4 pairs with S3;
S5 depends on S4 (creds); S6 (monitoring + back-out + E2E) gated on S1–S5; S1's submit-requirement
activation is deliberately last.
## Out of scope
- The `LLM-Review` vote itself (v1; epics d251 / b744).
- Per-vote HMAC signing of the CI verdict (decided: authenticated label vote only).
- Jenkins / Zuul self-hosted CI (rejected: over-weight for a single repo).
- GitLab support in g2p (not yet available upstream).
## Key references
- g2p: github.com/lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform (README mandates full mirroring of change refs);
docs.releng.linuxfoundation.org/projects/gerrit-to-platform.
- Real workflows: onap/.github + o-ran-sc/.github `gerrit-required-verify.yaml`; single-repo
template `lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform/examples/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- Actions (SHA-pin): `lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action`,
`lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action` (`vote-type` verified), `im-open/workflow-conclusion`.
- GerriScary / CVE-2025-1568 — the copyCondition + reset rationale.
- Gerrit core-plugins doc (hooks/replication/webhooks bundled in the war).
- Local: `infra/gerrit/{project.config,replication.config,install-plugins.sh,service-user.sh,plugins/README.md}`,
`infra/terraform/ssm.tf`, `infra/scripts/{fetch-secrets.sh,observability.sh}`, `monitoring_s4b.tf`,
`docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`, ADR-0007/0010/0013/0014, `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
