## Context / Problem

S1 [rebar:1934-63dd-4be9-4c48] lets a ticket explicitly assert `file_impact_scope: none`. The preceding implementation, merged on `main` as commit `6ec1ad21be8e4d359809a430e61607490a90af29`, gives that assertion real leverage: an authenticated `file-scope: none` attestation is not invalidated by unrelated HEAD movement. The existing S1 dependency is closed; the merged implementation is part of this story's base revision.

The assertion therefore needs a correctness check; otherwise a false declaration could silence drift protection. The check belongs in plan review, where the ticket plan, acceptance criteria, persisted scope, and `no_file_impact_reason` are available. It must be narrow: it runs only when the persisted scope is exactly `none`; `paths`, `undeclared`, missing, `None`, and unknown values must not incur an LLM call or finding.

## Approach

Add one advisory LLM criterion, `no-file-impact`, whose sole judgment is whether a ticket that declares no repository-file impact actually describes work that requires changing a repository file.

This extends the existing `applies_at` routing mechanism rather than adding a bespoke orchestration path: `require_parent_id` provides the structural precedent, deterministic routing isolates cost, and the existing advisory Pass-1 framework already owns LLM execution and fail-open behavior.

### Deterministic applicability

Follow the existing `require_parent_id` routing-axis pattern:

- Add `applies_at.require_file_impact_scope: ["none"]` to the packaged routing
  entry for `no-file-impact`.
- Extend the shared routing validator in
  `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` to accept a non-empty list of non-empty
  strings for the new key.
- Extend `registry.applies(...)` with a `file_impact_scope` keyword. When the
  routing entry declares required scopes, return false unless the supplied value
  is a string and is a member of that list. Missing/`None`/unknown values
  therefore fail closed by not selecting this criterion.
- Pass `ctx.state.get("file_impact_scope")` at the single orchestrator call site.

Existing criteria omit the key and retain their current behavior.

### Criterion judgment and prompt discovery

Create `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no_file_impact.md` with `category: plan-review-criterion`, `exec: 1-TURN`, facet `scope-intent`, advisory posture, and a 0.95 block threshold. Plan-review criterion prompts are auto-discovered from their front matter by the packaged prompt scan; do not edit the generated `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json`, which only indexes `category: review` prompts.

The prompt contains a co-located `CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local)` contract defining:

- `assertion_plausible: yes|no|insufficient`
- `reason_grounded: yes|no|insufficient`
- `repo_file_change_named: yes|no`

Its decision rules use every field:

- Set `assertion_plausible: no` when `repo_file_change_named: yes` or when a
  required deliverable otherwise entails a repository edit. Return an advisory
  contradiction finding citing that deliverable and coach declaring its paths.
- Set `assertion_plausible: yes` only when `reason_grounded: yes` and
  `repo_file_change_named: no`, with every deliverable outside the repository.
  Return PASS with no finding.
- Set `assertion_plausible: insufficient` when `reason_grounded` is `no`
  or `insufficient`, `repo_file_change_named: no`, and the plan is too vague to
  establish either outcome. Return non-blocking coaching that asks the author to
  name each deliverable and explain why none requires a repository-file edit.

Reading or analysing repository code without editing it remains compatible with `none`. A docs-only change is not compatible because documentation is still a repository file.

### Declared-reason data flow

Read `ctx.state.get("no_file_impact_reason", "")` in the orchestrator and carry it into Pass 1. The current `pass1.py` seam is an inline G5-only branch, not a generic per-criterion dispatcher. Replace the single `extra` assignment with compositional `extra_parts`: append `decomp_context` when the chunk contains G5, append the declared-reason block when it contains `no-file-impact`, then pass `"\n\n".join(extra_parts)` to `pass1_chunk`. A chunk containing both criteria must receive both blocks in stable order. The declared-reason block is:

```text
## Declared no-file-impact context
{"declared_reason":"<JSON-escaped persisted value>"}
```

Serialize the object with deterministic JSON (`sort_keys=True`, compact separators, UTF-8 preserved) so quotes, newlines, and Unicode in a persisted reason cannot change the prompt structure. A missing reason serializes as `{"declared_reason":""}` rather than omitting the field. The criterion prompt references this field alongside plan text. Do not add a dedicated `PlanContext` attribute.

### Registration and generated documentation

- Add `no-file-impact` to `CANONICAL_LLM`.
- Add its packaged routing entry, including
  `require_file_impact_scope: ["none"]`.
- Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with the repository generator;
  do not hand-edit the generated section.

## Test Design

Tests assert observable behavior and public contracts, never grep source text or depend on private implementation shape.

- Applicability contract: invoke the real criterion-selection path with
  persisted scopes `none`, `paths`, `undeclared`, missing/`None`, and an unknown
  future value. Assert `no-file-impact` is selected only for `none`; also assert
  existing criteria select identically across those inputs.
- Prompt-input contract: render the real Pass-1 request for `none` tickets and
  assert parsed structured context preserves (1) a non-empty reason containing
  quotes/newlines/Unicode and (2) a missing reason as the explicit empty string.
  Also render a chunk containing both G5 and `no-file-impact` and assert both
  public context blocks reach the LLM request in stable order. This verifies the
  LLM-boundary contract, not source text.
- Offline rubric behavior: exercise the criterion through the existing offline
  judge fixture with four cases: (1) an external operator action passes; (2) a
  plan requiring a new CLI flag produces advisory contradiction; (3) a
  docs-only plan produces advisory contradiction directing the author to
  declare documentation paths; and (4) a vague plan with an empty or
  ungrounded reason produces non-blocking `insufficient` coaching to strengthen
  `no_file_impact_reason`.
- Public explain contract: invoke `rebar explain no-file-impact` and assert a
  successful exit plus the criterion's semantic identity and applicability in
  output.
- Advisory gate contract: feed each contradiction/coaching outcome through the
  real verdict aggregation path and assert the ticket remains claimable.
- Generated-artifact contract: run the criteria-guide generator twice and assert
  the tracked guide is byte-identical after each run.

The held-out oracle includes legacy/missing scope, empty and escaped reasons, insufficient coaching, and advisory aggregation. A defect-seeded mutation of the routing predicate must make the held-out applicability test fail. Tests must remain green under behavior-preserving rename or extraction.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no_file_impact.md` — criterion rubric and
  criterion-local sub-answer schema.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — packaged routing entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` — shared routing-key validation.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — canonical membership and
  applicability predicate.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — persisted scope/reason input.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — structured declared-reason context.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — generated criterion documentation.
- Focused tests in the existing plan-review, routing, prompt, CLI, and gate test
  modules selected after the required coverage inventory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Persisted scope `none` routes `no-file-impact` into the Pass-1 finder set.
- [ ] Persisted scope `paths` does not route `no-file-impact`.
- [ ] Persisted scope `undeclared` does not route `no-file-impact`.
- [ ] Missing, `None`, or unknown persisted scope does not route
  `no-file-impact`.
- [ ] External-only deliverables produce PASS with no finding.
- [ ] A required source, configuration, or test-file change produces an advisory
  contradiction finding.
- [ ] A required documentation change produces an advisory contradiction
  finding directing the author to declare documentation paths.
- [ ] Insufficient evidence produces non-blocking coaching to strengthen
  `no_file_impact_reason`.
- [ ] The exact persisted reason round-trips through deterministic structured
  context in the production Pass-1 request.
- [ ] A missing reason reaches the production Pass-1 request as an explicit
  empty string.
- [ ] `no-file-impact` is present in the canonical criterion registry.
- [ ] The packaged routing entry passes shared validation.
- [ ] `rebar explain no-file-impact` succeeds with the generated criterion
  documentation.
- [ ] A fresh second criteria-guide regeneration produces no byte changes.
- [ ] A contradiction finding alone does not block claim.
- [ ] An insufficient coaching finding alone does not block claim.
- [ ] Reintroducing the prior always-selected routing behavior makes at least
  one held-out applicability test fail, and restoring the implementation makes
  that test pass.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The full test suite passes.
baseline.summary: Plan-review criterion no-file-impact: judge whether a no-file-impact assertion is correct

baseline.description:
## Why

Invariant I9 says compaction must stay safe against concurrent remote appends and must
never assume the per-clone lock excludes remote writers. The existing regression
(`test_sub_horizon_append_orphan_recovered_by_fsck_rebuild` in
`tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`) simulates the interleaving by
copying clone B's event file into clone A by hand plus a `--no-verify` commit — it never
does a real push/fetch/merge, so the actual publish/reconverge timing and retry logic
are unexercised. The report's suggested "either visible or fsck repairs it" oracle is
too permissive (a bug forcing every normal append through repair would still pass).

## What

- Add real push/fetch/merge interleaving tests with a tightened, scenario-specific
  oracle, keeping the existing manual-copy test as the fast deterministic regression.

Injection mechanics (committed, since `compact` holds one flock across an inline
critical section with no mid-flock hook): drive A's compaction with `--skip-sync` so the
test controls sync timing explicitly, rather than relying on compaction's own
`_sync_before_compact`. B's real push/fetch/merge is sequenced by the test around A's
`--skip-sync` compaction, not injected mid-flock.

## Scope

- `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` (or a sibling integration module)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scenario A (normal horizon, real push): A's foldable events are seeded with a
      FAR-PAST `REBAR_HLC_NOW` so they are older than the default horizon (fresh
      test-created events are all "young" and would make compaction a no-op —
      `_compact_locked` folds only `now - ts >= horizon`). A syncs, then compacts with
      `--skip-sync` and produces a real SNAPSHOT; B appends and PUSHES a current-time
      event during A's compaction window; after A fetches+reconverges, B's event is
      IMMEDIATELY visible, `fsck` is clean, and NO repair command is required.
- [ ] Scenario B (adversarial ordering, real push): force A's snapshot to carry a
      far-future timestamp by running A's `compact` subprocess with `REBAR_HLC_NOW` set
      to a far-future value, while B appends at a normal clock — so B's event filename
      prefix is guaranteed to sort BEFORE A's snapshot and is excluded from its
      `source_event_uuids`. **Sequencing (critical):** B must create+push its event at a
      normal clock BEFORE it fetches/witnesses A's far-future post-compact HEAD —
      otherwise B's HLC absorbs the far-future timestamp and B's subsequent event sorts
      AFTER the snapshot, defeating the adversarial ordering. Assert `fsck`
      deterministically flags the orphan,
      `--repair-snapshots` on A restores the exact event, THEN A pushes the repaired
      commit and B fetches+syncs. Because B never compacted, after fetch B holds BOTH its
      live `.json` orphan and A's rebuilt snapshot that already folded+retired it — so B
      must then run `fsck --repair` (mirroring the resurrection pattern in
      `test_two_clone_compaction_resurrection_no_data_loss_and_repairable`). Assert that
      after B's repair BOTH clones show identical ticket state with no UUID/content lost.
      Concrete oracle: `rebar show <id> --output json` on A and on B parse to equal
      objects (Python `==` on the parsed JSON), and the specific UUID of B's pre-push
      append is present in both — NOT merely that both processes exit 0.
- [ ] The existing manual-copy test is retained as a fast Scenario-B regression.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Add real remote-append-during-compaction interleaving tests

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The two weekly, canonical-repo-only GitHub Actions jobs that make **real, billable LLM
calls** surface **no retrievable record of token usage**:

- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` → `external` job (weekly `cron "0 6 * * 1"`),
  runs `pytest -m external tests/external` (`external-integration.yml:30-136`).
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` → `eval-live` job (weekly `cron "0 7 * * 1"`),
  runs `ev.run_eval(pid, max_cases=cap)` over the eval specs (`prompt-eval.yml:79-100`).

Per-call usage is *already captured in code* — `PydanticAIRunner.run` computes
`usage = _extract_usage(...)` (input/output/cache tokens + `requests`) at
`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:392,394`, logs one INFO line at `runner.py:452-470`, and attaches
it as a private `result["_usage"] = usage` at `runner.py:486`. But that record never reaches
either weekly job: the eval path (`ev.run_eval`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`) returns only
`passed`/`coverage`/`junit` and drops `_usage`; the external `pytest` tier surfaces nothing;
and the INFO log lines are swallowed because `src/rebar/__init__.py` attaches a `NullHandler`
to the `rebar` logger and neither job calls `logging.basicConfig`. The only usage-bearing
path, the `langfuse-trace` job, exports spans to an **ephemeral** Langfuse torn down with
`docker compose ... down -v` each run, so nothing is retrievable afterward.

There is **no token→USD price table anywhere** in the codebase, so this ticket records **token
usage** (input/output/cache tokens + request count), not a dollar figure.

Edit-set (all paths confirmed present unless marked *new*):
- *new* `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (720 LOC today; cap is 800 per `.github/module-size-limit.txt`)
- *new* `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`
- `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`
- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`

## Approach

Add one process-level usage sink at the **already-existing** `_usage` seam that is shared by
both jobs (both go through `PydanticAIRunner.run`), so a single hook covers both without any
per-test or per-eval plumbing.

1. New module `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py`:
   - `record(usage: dict, *, op: str) -> None` — when env var `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set to a
     path, append one JSON object per call (`op`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
     `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `requests`) as a line to that file (JSONL).
     No-op when the env var is unset. Best-effort: it wraps its file write in a `try/except`
     and never raises into the LLM call path (a telemetry sink must not break a run).
   - `summarize(path: str) -> str` — read the JSONL and return a Markdown summary: a totals
     row (summed tokens + total calls) plus a per-`op` breakdown table. A missing or empty
     file returns the single line `No LLM calls recorded.` (so a run with zero LLM calls still
     produces valid, honest summary output).
   - `__main__` CLI: `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize <path>` prints `summarize(path)`
     to stdout, for `>> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` in CI.
2. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — immediately after `result["_usage"] = usage` (`runner.py:486`),
   call `usage_log.record(usage, op=_call_label)` (module-level import). One statement; keeps
   `runner.py` well under the 800-LOC cap.
3. Both workflows (`prompt-eval.yml` `eval-live` job and `external-integration.yml` `external`
   job): set job env `REBAR_USAGE_LOG: ${{ runner.temp }}/usage.jsonl`; after the test/eval
   step (with `if: always()` so a test failure still reports spend), run
   `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize "$REBAR_USAGE_LOG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` and
   upload the raw JSONL via `actions/upload-artifact`. This gives both a human-glanceable job
   summary and a durable, machine-readable artifact.

Rejected alternatives: (a) persisting the `langfuse-trace` spans — requires standing up and
retaining a Langfuse backend + secrets, far heavier than the ask and off the eval job's path
entirely; (b) parsing the runner's INFO log lines out of pytest stdout — fragile and
suppressed by the `NullHandler` today. The `_usage` seam is the one chokepoint already common
to both jobs.

## Scope

- Recording is **token usage only** (input/output/cache tokens + request count). No dollar
  cost is computed — no price table exists in the repo, and adding one is out of scope.
- The sink is **opt-in via `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`**; default (env unset) behavior of the runner and
  of every existing caller is unchanged, so `make test` and normal library use are unaffected.
- Only the two weekly jobs set `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`; the PR/push and Verified lanes are untouched.
- No change to what tests/evals run, to gating, to `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES`, or to any provider
  credential handling.

## Testing

Offline unit tests only (no live LLM; consistent with the `not integration and not external`
default suite). New `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`:
- `record` appends one well-formed JSON line per call when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` points at a
  tmp_path file, and is a **no-op** when the env var is unset (assert no file created).
- `summarize` aggregates multiple recorded lines into correct totals and a per-`op` breakdown;
  a missing/empty file yields exactly `No LLM calls recorded.`
- Record-at-the-seam: drive `PydanticAIRunner.run` through the existing offline
  `FunctionModel` model-override path (with `pydantic_ai.models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`,
  as in `tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py`) with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` set to a tmp file, and
  assert a JSONL line is appended — proving the runner call site fires without a live call.
- CLI: invoking `summarize` via the module entry point returns/prints the Markdown summary.

Workflow YAML edits are validated by `python -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(f))"`
for each changed file (structural parse) in addition to the CI lint that already runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` exists exposing `record(usage, *, op)` and
      `summarize(path)` with the semantics above; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_usage_log.py` passing.
- [ ] With `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` unset, `record(...)` writes no file and the runner path is
      unchanged; verified by the no-op unit test.
- [ ] `PydanticAIRunner.run` appends a usage record when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set; verified by
      the FunctionModel-override unit test asserting a JSONL line was written.
- [ ] `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize <path>` prints the Markdown totals + per-op
      table (or `No LLM calls recorded.` for an empty/missing file); verified by the CLI test.
- [ ] The `eval-live` job (`prompt-eval.yml`) and the `external` job
      (`external-integration.yml`) each set `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`, append `summarize` output to
      `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (`if: always()`), and upload the JSONL as an artifact; verified by
      `yaml.safe_load` of each file and grep for the three additions.
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` remains ≤ 800 LOC; verified by `wc -l`.
- [ ] `make test`, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` all pass locally; the change lands via
      Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`.
baseline.summary: Record token usage from the two weekly live-LLM jobs (external + eval-live)

baseline.description:
# Give Cloud the resilience and config-validation coverage DC gained

## Context

Epic e369 hardened the DC adapter against a real instance and produced a tier of coverage Cloud never had. Cloud's tests grew from INCIDENTS THAT HAPPENED; DC's grew from CONFIGURATIONS THAT DIFFER. The second kind generalises, and Cloud does not have it.

This story is the Cloud half of the parity work. It is lower priority than [rebar:0fad-59f7-1605-4377] (Cloud's unpaginated whole-project readers) because Cloud is the mature, live-exercised path — but each item below is a real asymmetry, not a symmetry exercise.

## The gaps, with what DC has for comparison

**1. No per-member 429 sweep.** DC's `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` walks EVERY mutating transport member and asserts each fails on the first 429 — because retrying a mutation on an HTTP error is the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] fixed, and an enumeration is what stops a later-added mutation inheriting a retry by omission. Cloud has `test_retry_httperror.py` (5 tests) and one 429 path in `state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:352-368`, neither of which sweeps the member set.

**DC's property does NOT transfer uniformly, and assuming it does is the main risk in this item.** Cloud has no single choke point; its mutations traverse FOUR distinct 429 behaviours across two levels, all verified in the tree. Two are transport-level and DELIBERATELY OPPOSITE:

* **direct REST** (`AcliRestMixin._rest_urlopen_with_retry`) — "Does NOT retry on
  `urllib.error.HTTPError` (4xx / 5xx)" (`adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:50-52`). A 429 arrives as
  `urllib.error.HTTPError`. Here DC's property holds verbatim: exactly ONE attempt.
* **ACLI subprocess** (`acli_subprocess._run_acli`) — **already RETRIES a 429**, on purpose, via
  `_rate_limit_backoff` honouring `Retry-After`; `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff`
  (`state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) asserts the call SUCCEEDS on retry. A 429 here is an
  exit code plus `429` in stderr, not an HTTP exception.

…and ABOVE both sits the reconciler's dispatch level, which is the part most likely to be missed — and it is itself SPLIT IN TWO:

* **the retrying dispatch wrapper** — `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  (`dispatch_one.py:113-186`) catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and, when `exc.code == 429`, records
  `Retry-After` and RETRIES (`dispatch_one.py:151-160`). So a REST mutation that makes exactly one
  attempt when its transport method is called DIRECTLY is nevertheless retried when reached the way
  production reaches it.
* **the explicitly NON-retrying apply phases** — `dispatch_apply_phases`, whose module docstring
  states it owns "the phases that do NOT funnel their Jira writes through
  `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`". These include real mutations:
  `_update_one_apply_reporter` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:91`) and
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:142`, the single-attempt comment dispatch). A 429 here is a
  FOURTH behaviour — neither the subprocess backoff nor the dispatch-wrapper retry applies — and
  existing coverage (`test_comment_single_attempt.py`) pins attempt count for ONE member, not a
  sweep.

So "every mutating member fails on the first 429" is TRUE for a raw REST transport method called directly, TRUE again for the non-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` mutations, and FALSE for both the subprocess seam and anything routed through the retrying dispatch wrapper. **An attempt-count assertion is therefore meaningless unless it names the BOUNDARY it measures at.** Writing the DC assertion across all four would either fail immediately or pressure someone into deleting an intentional, tested backoff. This story must establish the split FIRST and assert a per-layer property — and it must not fold in a behaviour change (below).

**The two retries named above are KNOWN and DELIBERATE — they are not the bug trigger.** Both `_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff and `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch are already implemented, tested and documented, so "a mutation is retried on a 429" is not by itself a finding; the enumeration will hit them by construction. The bug-filing trigger is NARROWER: a mutating member retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already explicitly tested and documented — an UNDOCUMENTED or newly-discovered retry path. That is the [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] duplicate class. If one is found, file a linked bug with the evidence and do NOT "fix" it inside this test story. Separately, if the enumeration shows a KNOWN retry applying to a mutation in a way nobody has evaluated for duplicate-write safety, record that assessment on this ticket — as a finding, not as a code change.

**2. No config-validation tier.** DC asserts a non-HTTPS base URL is rejected, that the insecure override warns, that malformed config propagates, and that a missing credential fails loudly rather than going anonymous (`test_jira_dc_config_settings.py`, `test_dc_pat_required_heldout.py` — the latter exists because bug cd78 was exactly a silent fall-back to ANONYMOUS access). Cloud has no equivalent. Whether Cloud CAN go anonymous is itself unestablished and worth answering.

**3. The probe's resolved-status set is not runtime-configurable.** `adapters/jira/probe.py:39` pins `frozenset({"Resolved","Done","Cancelled"})`; DC threads `resolved_statuses` from settings and tests it. Cloud's `probe_remote` also re-resolves env itself rather than using the transport's configured session.

**"Is it deliberate?" is already answered — do NOT re-open it.** `probe.py`'s module docstring (`:20-25`) states that J2 moved the pure classifier to `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` taking the status set as a PARAMETER, and that `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` "is Cloud/DIG's *configured value* (a self-hosted Data Center workflow can name its resolved states anything), so it stays defined here". So it is documented as deliberate at the definition site, and an AC satisfied by "document it" would be satisfied by doing nothing. The remaining OPEN question is narrower and is the only one this item answers: **does a Cloud deployment whose workflow uses non-standard resolved-status names need a runtime config hook** (as DC has), or is the per-deployment constant genuinely sufficient? Record THAT decision with its rationale; if a hook is needed, file it as its own ticket.

**4. `search_user_by_email` degradation is unasserted on DC** (the mirror-image item, kept here so the pair is not split). `outbound_assignee.py:33-37` resolves the user-search method by NAME STRING across three aliases; DC provides none of them, so `_bootstrap_account_id_via_user_search` returns `None` and the path degrades to string matching. That degradation is probably correct — DC has no accountId concept — but nothing asserts it, so an accidental rename on the Cloud side would look like the same silence.

## Approach

Take these in the order above; 1 and 2 carry the risk, 3 is an investigation that may produce a ticket rather than a test, 4 is a one-test pin.

**Port the PROPERTY, not the test — and note the property is PER-LAYER.** Cloud's retry lives in a different place from DC's, so a copied test would assert the wrong seam. What must survive the port is the ENUMERATION — that every mutating member is named explicitly, because an ellipsis is how the next mutation inherits a retry.

**Step 0 for item 1, before any test is written:** enumerate every mutating member of Cloud's transport and classify each on BOTH axes, by reading bodies rather than inferring from names:

1. **transport seam** — one of THREE: ACLI subprocess (`_run_acli`); pooled direct REST
   (`_rest_urlopen_with_retry` / `_direct_rest_post_raw` / `_direct_rest_put_raw`); or **bare
   `urllib.request.urlopen`**, which bypasses `_rest_urlopen_with_retry` entirely and therefore does
   not even inherit its transient-fault retry — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
   (`acli_cli_ops.py:396`, urlopen at `:437`) is a confirmed instance, reached in production because
   `AcliClient.update_issue` delegates to the free function `update_issue` (`acli.py:374`), which
   calls `update_priority` when `priority` is among the changed fields (`acli.py:180`). A member with
   more than one leg (e.g. a REST leg and a subprocess leg) is called out as such.
2. **dispatch level** — which of THREE the reconciler uses: the retrying wrapper
   `dispatch_one._call_with_retry` (`dispatch_one.py:113-186`), which adds a 429 retry ON TOP of
   whatever the seam does; the explicitly non-retrying apply phases in `dispatch_apply_phases`
   (`_update_one_apply_reporter:91`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments:142`); or no dispatch wrapper at
   all. Determine this by reading the call site, since the module split is by RETRY POLICY, so the
   answer is not inferable from the member's own body.

**Completeness check for the table, run and recorded alongside it** — the table gates the whole item, so its coverage must be demonstrated, not asserted. Enumerate the candidate surface with a concrete command and account for EVERY name it returns:

    git grep -nE "^(    )?def [_a-z]" -- \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py \
      src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py

Three things about that pattern are deliberate, and each one is a way the table can look complete while omitting a writer:

* it matches BOTH indented class methods AND module-level free functions;
* it includes `_`-PREFIXED names — `acli_graph._add_label_impl:83` and `_remove_label_impl:143` are
  mutating, as are the `_direct_rest_*` helpers in `acli_rest.py`, and a `def [a-z]` pattern would
  emit none of them, so the "every name it returns is classified" rule would be satisfied vacuously;
* `acli_cli_ops.py` is in the file list, because `AcliClient` delegates real mutations to free
  functions there (`create_issue:147`, `update_priority:396`, `add_comment:469`).

Paste that raw output on the ticket next to the table. Every name in it is either classified in the table or explicitly marked NON-MUTATING with a one-line reason — no name may be silently absent. Cross-check the mutating set against DC's enumerated list in `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` and record any member DC sweeps that Cloud's table lacks, or vice versa, with the reason.

The table decides, per member, which property is asserted and at which boundary it is observed — and a member can legitimately have DIFFERENT correct answers at the two levels (one attempt raw, retried when dispatch-wrapped).

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — Cloud 429 sweep, Cloud config-validation tests, a DC
  user-search-degradation pin.
- an investigation note (or a linked bug) on the Cloud probe's hardcoded resolved statuses.
- the per-member seam classification table for item 1 (recorded on the ticket, not in code).
- No production change intended. Items 1 and 3 may each produce a linked BUG — item 1 only if a
  mutating member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
  documented (the two known deliberate retries do not count), item 3 if the hardcoded
  resolved-status set is an accident — and in both cases the fix is its own ticket, never folded in
  here.

## Testing

The 429 sweep must assert the ATTEMPT COUNT per member, not merely that an exception escaped — an implementation that retried and then re-raised satisfies a raises-only assertion having issued the write twice. This is the same correction being applied to DC's own sweep in [rebar:2944-dd3f-e982-4359]; do not copy that mistake forward.

**The instrument differs per seam, and a single patch point covers only half the members** — a sweep that patches `urllib.request.urlopen` is blind to subprocess mutations, and one that patches `acli_subprocess._run_acli` is blind to REST mutations, while either LOOKS complete because every member still raises. So:

* POOLED REST-seam members, called DIRECTLY on the transport (not through the dispatch wrapper) —
  observe attempts at the urlopen boundary; inject a 429 as `urllib.error.HTTPError`; assert EXACTLY
  ONE attempt (no retry), matching `acli_rest.py:50-52`.
* BARE-`urlopen` members — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority` (`:396`, urlopen at `:437`) bypasses
  `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`, so it has no retry of its own: assert EXACTLY ONE attempt there too.

  **One patch point covers both, and per-module patching is NOT a real isolation mechanism.** Both
  `acli_rest.py` (`:23`) and `acli_cli_ops.py` (`:24`) do `import urllib.request` — a MODULE-object
  binding — so both resolve `urlopen` at call time through the same shared `urllib.request` object.
  Patching it once affects both; `mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:160` already relies on
  exactly that, calling it "the process-wide `urllib.request.urlopen` (a shared singleton)". So
  patch it once and distinguish the seams by WHICH MEMBER was invoked and what the captured request
  looks like — not by which module the patch was applied through. Coverage of both seams must
  therefore be proven by ENUMERATION (every member in the table has a case) rather than by any
  assumed namespace separation.
* the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path — the same members reached through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
  DO retry a 429 by design (`dispatch_one.py:151-160`). Assert the retry is bounded and honours
  `Retry-After`; do NOT assert one attempt here. This is the layer where "is a MUTATION being
  retried on a 429?" is actually decided, so it is the layer the bug-filing trigger below applies to.
* subprocess-seam members — observe attempts at the `_run_acli`/`Popen` boundary; inject a 429 as
  the exit-code + `429`-in-stderr shape the existing test uses; assert the OBSERVED, INTENDED
  behaviour (a bounded retry honouring `Retry-After`, per
  `state/test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:369`) rather than one attempt — and record whether that
  retry applies to a MUTATION, which is the bug-filing trigger above.

Each seam's sweep must be MUTATION-CHECKED at its own instrument: make one member issue an extra attempt at that boundary and confirm THAT seam's sweep goes red — proving the sweep is not blind to the half it is supposed to cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every MUTATING Cloud transport member is enumerated explicitly — no ellipsis, no sampling —
      and classified on BOTH axes: transport seam (ACLI subprocess / pooled direct REST / bare
      `urllib.request.urlopen`) and dispatch
      level (retrying `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, the explicitly NON-retrying
      `dispatch_apply_phases` phases, or no wrapper). The table lands as a REPO ARTIFACT — the sweep
      test module's own enumeration plus a header comment carrying the per-member classification,
      which is where a reviewer will look — and is mirrored onto this ticket
- [ ] the table's COMPLETENESS is demonstrated, not asserted: the enumeration command from Step 0 is
      run, its raw output recorded beside the table, and every name it returns is either classified
      or marked NON-MUTATING with a reason — plus the DC cross-check for members present on one side
      and missing on the other
- [ ] each POOLED-REST and each BARE-`urlopen` mutating member, invoked DIRECTLY on the transport, is
      asserted to make EXACTLY ONE attempt under a 429, observed at the shared process-wide
      `urllib.request.urlopen`, with one case PER MEMBER from the table — `acli_cli_ops.update_priority`
      explicitly among them
- [ ] the DISPATCH-WRAPPED path is covered separately: reached through
      `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, a 429 IS retried by design (`dispatch_one.py:151-160`), so the
      assertion there is a BOUNDED retry honouring `Retry-After` — not one attempt
- [ ] each subprocess-seam mutating member is asserted against its ACTUAL intended 429 behaviour —
      the bounded `Retry-After` backoff in `_run_acli` — observed at the `_run_acli` boundary. This
      criterion is NOT satisfied by asserting one attempt there, because
      `test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff` proves the retry is deliberate
- [ ] mutations reached through the NON-retrying `dispatch_apply_phases` path
      (`_update_one_apply_reporter`, `_update_one_dispatch_comments`) are asserted to make exactly
      one attempt under a 429 — extending `test_comment_single_attempt.py`'s single-member pin to
      the sweep
- [ ] if a MUTATING member is retried on a 429 at a layer where that retry is NOT already tested and
      documented, a linked bug is filed with the evidence. The two KNOWN deliberate retries
      (`_run_acli`'s rate-limit backoff, `_call_with_retry`'s 429 branch) do NOT by themselves
      trigger a bug; where one applies to a mutation, the duplicate-write assessment is RECORDED
      here instead. This story changes NO retry behaviour either way
- [ ] Cloud rejects a non-HTTPS base URL, or the test records that it deliberately does not
- [ ] Cloud's behaviour on a MISSING credential is asserted: it must fail loudly, or the test pins
      that it does not and a bug is filed (this is bug cd78's shape on the other adapter)
- [ ] the OPEN question on the Cloud probe's resolved-status set is answered: whether a Cloud
      deployment using non-standard resolved-status names needs a runtime config hook as DC has, or
      whether the per-deployment constant suffices. The answer lands as a REPO ARTIFACT, not only a
      ticket comment — a comment at `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` in `adapters/jira/probe.py` recording the
      decision and citing this ticket id (plus the follow-up ticket id if a hook is needed) — so a
      reviewer can find it without the tracker. Re-documenting it as merely "deliberate" does NOT
      satisfy this: `probe.py:20-25` already says so, and an AC already true on an unmodified tree is
      not a criterion
- [ ] a test pins that DC exposes none of `_USER_SEARCH_METHODS` and that the bootstrap degrades to
      the string-match path rather than raising
- [ ] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED. "Mutation-checked" here means a CONCRETE MANUAL mutation,
      not a mutation-testing tool: for each new test, apply the named perturbation below, run that
      test module, record it RED with its pass/fail counts, revert, record it GREEN again. Both
      verdicts go in a REPO-VISIBLE place — the commit/Gerrit change description of the change that
      adds the tests, listing per test the mutation applied and the RED/GREEN pass-fail counts — as
      well as on this ticket, so the evidence is reviewable from the change itself and survives
      independently of the tracker. The named mutations are: for a REST-seam sweep, make one member retry
      once at the urlopen boundary (the `== 1` attempt assertion must go red); for a subprocess-seam
      sweep, SUPPRESS the retry outright — cap `_run_acli`'s attempt loop at one, or make it re-raise
      on a 429 exit without looping — so the ATTEMPT-COUNT assertion goes red. Note what does NOT
      work: making `_rate_limit_backoff` return `None` does not remove the retry at all, because
      `acli_subprocess.py:429` is
      `_backoff_sleep(rl_delay if rl_delay is not None else 2 ** (attempt + 1))` — a `None` merely
      swaps `Retry-After` for a uniform exponential delay and the call is still retried;
      for the non-HTTPS-URL test, FIRST establish whether Cloud has a scheme rejection at all —
      `_validate_reconciler_tls` (`_config_schema.py:78`) is invoked only from
      `ReconcilerConfig.__post_init__` (`:427`), and Cloud's `AcliClient` / settings resolution has
      no scheme check of its own, so the likely answer is that Cloud does NOT reject `http://`. If it
      DOES reject, disable that rejection and confirm the test goes RED. If it does NOT, the test is
      absence-documenting, and its mutation check is the inverse: ADD a scheme assertion to the
      production path, confirm the absence-documenting test goes RED, then revert — record which of
      the two cases applied. Do NOT hunt for a non-existent hook, and do NOT add one permanently
      (a production change, out of scope); for the missing-credential test, make
      the production path proceed WITHOUT raising when the credential is absent (the cd78
      anonymous-fallback shape) and confirm the test goes RED; for the `_USER_SEARCH_METHODS`
      degradation pin, add one of the three alias names to the DC stub and confirm the pin goes RED.
      Every  … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Cloud resilience + config-validation coverage, matching DC's

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A single Gerrit Verified run needs 21 concurrent job slots against a GitHub Free org-wide cap of 20 total / 5 macOS, shared with every other navapbc repo. `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` contributes 8 of those, and one of them does no unique work.

The `import-linter` job installs `-e .[dev]` — byte-identical to `_build-and-test.yml:230` — and runs `pytest tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py tests/unit/test_optional.py`. Those files carry NO pytest markers, and tests/conftest.py only auto-marks `external` under `tests/external/`, so all 9 tests already run in all four `test` matrix cells (3.11/3.12/3.13 + macOS) — strictly more coverage than this job single ubuntu/3.12 run.

The "import-leak test defeated by a polluted worker process" concern does NOT apply here, which is why the deletion is safe: `test_lean_workflow_runtime_pulls_no_heavy_stack` reads `sys.modules` inside a FRESHLY SPAWNED `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code])`; `test_no_core_module_imports_heavy_stack_at_module_scope` is a pure `ast.parse` walk over source; and `test_blocked_extra_degrades_friendly` uses the `block_extra` fixture, which EVICTS modules from `sys.modules` and is therefore STRONGER in a loaded worker, not weaker. There is no `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START`/`sitecustomize` in the repo, so even the coverage lane child is a bare interpreter.

## Approach
Delete the job — and repay, in the same change, the guard it was incidentally providing.

THE GAP THIS OPENS: nothing in the repo can see the deletion. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:131-162` asserts only caller-level WIRING strings (that gerrit-verify invokes the reusable, passes the refspec, that `vote.needs` contains `optionality`). `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:44-51` reads only caller job keys. NEITHER has any visibility into `_optionality.yml` inner jobs, so both pass unchanged after the deletion.

That means once the dedicated job is gone, the ONLY thing keeping those 9 tests running is the incidental fact that the two files carry no marker. A future contributor who adds `@pytest.mark.integration`, moves the files, or adds a `paths:` filter deletes the optionality guard with a fully GREEN build. Given this project already has a history of an optionality gap letting bugs reach main, shipping the deletion without a replacement guard is not acceptable.

So the deletion is paired with a durable, checked-in test asserting those two files are still collected by the default suite selection.

Rejected alternative: keep the job. It costs a slot against a cap the run already exceeds, for coverage the matrix strictly dominates. Rejected alternative: delete without the guard. That converts an explicit check into an implicit one with no alarm.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — remove the `import-linter` job only. No other job is touched.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — add the collection guard.

NOT in scope: the per-extra/union collapse (separate ticket ad63-17ad-d545-45d4), `clean-core-wheel`, `_build-and-test.yml`.

## Testing
The guard must be durable rather than a one-time check, because the risk is a future edit, not this change.

Add a test that runs pytest collection over the two files with the default suite selection (`-m "not integration and not external"`) and asserts 9 items are collected. Collecting by running the real selection — rather than grepping for marker text — is what makes it catch a marker added anywhere: file-level `pytestmark`, a decorator, or a conftest-applied mark.

The only real loss from the deletion is diagnostic latency: a heavy-import regression currently reddens a ~1 min job and afterwards surfaces inside a ~15 min matrix cell. That is accepted and recorded here deliberately.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `import-linter` job no longer exists in `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`.
- [ ] No other job in that file is modified.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` and `tests/unit/test_optional.py` collect 9 items under `-m "not integration and not external"`.
- [ ] That test FAILS if a marker excluding either file from the default selection is added.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` passes.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` passes (actionlint covers all workflows).
baseline.summary: Delete the redundant import-linter job and repay its guard with a collection test

baseline.description:
## Context

Auditors need to review, for one work ticket, what the automated LLM review gates decided: the
latest plan review, the completion-verification result, and the latest associated code review,
alongside the ticket's current details — with the ability to navigate the history of plan and code
reviews and to see each review's full four-pass breakdown (pass-1 findings, pass-2 verification,
pass-3 determination with thresholds, pass-4 coaching). The audit data is made lossless and readable
by the data-enrichment epic (a hard dependency; see the linked `depends_on` epic).

This epic delivers that as an OPTIONAL, disabled-by-default, read-only local web UI.

## Data contract (the named interface Epic 1 must expose)

This UI is a pure function of the enriched fields the data-enrichment epic (Epic 1) persists per
finding and per criterion. The two epics share THIS named interface — Epic 1 delivers it (via story
A's plan-review v2 `_slim`, story B's code-review v2 payload, and story C's completion `criteria[]`),
Epic 2 consumes it. The minimal enriched field set is:

| Consumer (UI region)          | Source (Epic 1)                        | Required fields                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Finding-provenance (per finding) | plan-review v2 (story A) / code-review v2 (story B) | `finding`, `criteria`, `location`, `evidence`, `scenarios`, `impact`, `suggested_fix`, `verification`, `validity`, `priority`, `decision`, `reason`, `block_threshold`, `blocking_enabled` |
| Round history + convergence   | plan-/code-review sidecar history      | full retained per-round sidecars (newest-first) + each round's `coaching[]` (`{move_id, finding_refs}`)                                        |
| Threshold meter (per finding) | plan-/code-review v2                    | the finding's resolved (per-finding) `block_threshold` + `blocking_enabled` + `priority` + `decision`                                          |
| Completion panel (per criterion) | completion `criteria[]` (story C)     | `criteria[]` of `{criterion, met, citation, kind}` where `kind ∈ {codebase-verifiable, operator-attested}`                                     |

`block_threshold` is the PER-FINDING resolved value each finding was judged against (persisted by
stories A/B), NOT a round-level scalar. The completion panel's per-criterion rows have NO source in
the pre-enrichment completion verdict (findings are failures-only); they are PRODUCED by story C's
`criteria[]`. This epic MUST NOT proceed to render a region until its Epic 1 field source has landed.

## Approach rationale

Server-rendered FastAPI + Jinja2, REUSING the `reviewbot` extra's already-shipped web stack rather
than adding a second web framework, bound to loopback only, with no client build step. This fits a
read-only, low-traffic, single-user audit view and reuses proven in-repo machinery (the reviewbot
FastAPI app is the established "thin, lazily-imported, never-required-by-core" precedent). The
alternative of a static HTML export was weighed and rejected for v1: the audit data is naturally
navigable (history rounds, drill-in) and replay is cheap, which a point-in-time static dump serves
poorly.

## Scope

- IN: the optional web-server surface (subcommand, config flag, `[ui]` extra, lazy import, loopback
  binding) and the per-ticket audit page rendering.
- OUT: any data-model/sidecar change (owned by the dependency epic — the Data-contract fields above
  are DELIVERED by Epic 1, not by this epic); network exposure / multi-user auth; write/edit actions
  (the UI is strictly read-only).

## Compatibility & rollback

The whole feature is default-off (`[ui] enabled = false`) and its web deps live in a new
`nava-rebar[ui]` extra, lazy-imported — so it is inert when disabled and when the extra is absent.
Rollback is turning the flag off / not installing the extra; no data or schema change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both child stories are closed.
- [ ] The page is navigable across the retained review history for BOTH plan review AND code review:
      an OLDER round (not just the latest) of EACH can be selected and its distinct content renders.
      Oracle: a live end-to-end test seeding ≥2 plan-review rounds AND ≥2 code-review rounds on one
      ticket, selecting the older round in each gate, and asserting each renders its (distinct from
      latest) content.
- [ ] With the feature enabled, `rebar audit serve` serves a ticket audit page showing the ticket
      details and the plan/completion/code panels with pass-1..4 detail, per-finding resolved
      thresholds, and the completion `criteria[]` rows. Oracle: a live end-to-end test that starts
      the server and asserts on the rendered response.
- [ ] With the feature disabled (default), no web dependency is imported and all existing commands
