baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Two backend-neutral core modules load Jira rich-text/limit modules by literal lazy-load key
and run them unconditionally — for ANY configured backend:

- `outbound_comments.py:68` (`_ADF_KEY = "rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf"`, loaded at
  `:75-85`) and `outbound_comments.py:71` (`_COMMENT_LIMITS_KEY =
  "rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.comment_limits"`, loaded at `:88`) — comment-body
  formatting/truncation on the outbound comment-diff path.
- `inbound_translate.py:315` (`_ADF_KEY_APPLIER`, loaded at `:319-324`) —
  `_normalize_adf_body` decodes a raw ADF dict to text as defense-in-depth on the inbound
  apply path (bug 1bb2-5da5).

A GitHub/Linear backend would still have its comments ADF-encoded and Jira-limit-truncated.
These literal keys are the last vendor reach-through in neutral core paths after the sibling
stories land; epic bbf1's separation goal ("a second backend drops in behind the port")
requires them behind the port.

## Approach

Route both modules through the port roles that already own these responsibilities:

- `FieldSanitizer` (already pinned in `_backend.py` as the vendor hard-limit defense, with the
  existing SEND-side `sanitize_comment(body: str) -> str`, which truncates AND logs a warning)
  gains ONE new method, `fit_comment(body: str) -> str` — a PURE fit-to-limit for the
  comment-DIFF comparison path (`outbound_comments.py:324`), delegating to
  `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`'s `truncate_comment_body` with NO warning (the compare
  path must not emit send-side warnings). `fit_comment` is the single, consistently-named
  comment-fit surface used throughout this plan; `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides only the
  DECODE (`adf_to_text`), which is served by `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` (below), NOT
  by the fit surface.
  `outbound_comments.py` resolves the configured backend's sanitizer via the registry seam
  (`select_backend(load_config())` — pattern proven at `outbound_differ.py:450-454`) instead
  of lazy-loading vendor modules, and the two literal keys at `outbound_comments.py:68,71`
  are deleted.
- `InboundMapper` gains `normalize_rich_text(body: Any) -> str` (Jira: `adf_to_text` for
  dicts, identity for strings — exactly today's `_normalize_adf_body`,
  `inbound_translate.py:349+`). `inbound_translate.py` calls the backend's inbound mapper;
  the literal key at `inbound_translate.py:315` is deleted. The defense-in-depth property
  (a raw vendor rich-text dict on the wire never reaches an EDIT event's `description`) is
  preserved backend-neutrally.
- Add a sweep case to `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`: no
  package-root core module contains the literal string `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"`,
  with a single recorded exemption for `inbound_fields.py:24` — that module IS the Jira
  `InboundMapper` implementation (delegated by `adapters/jira/backend.py:43-47`) that
  remains at the package root only for loader location-pinning reasons; its physical
  relocation is out of this epic's scope and tracked by follow-up ticket
  `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139` (linked `discovered_from` epic bbf1).

Rejected alternatives: (a) a new sixth role Protocol ("RichTextCodec") — YAGNI: FieldSanitizer
already owns vendor-limit defense per its `_backend.py` docstring and InboundMapper already
owns vendor→local payload translation; fewer than 3 call sites for a new role. (b) Leaving
the lazy keys because "they are only strings, not imports" — the loader still executes vendor
code on neutral paths for any backend, which is the substance of the leak.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (FieldSanitizer comment-fit surface; InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py (route via sanitizer; delete both literal keys)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py (route via inbound mapper; delete the literal key)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement the new members, delegating to adf/comment_limits)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py (Jira mapper: normalize_rich_text implementation)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (literal-key sweep with the recorded inbound_fields.py exemption)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (comment formatting/truncation + normalize_rich_text behavior tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: an outbound comment body formats and truncates byte-identically to today via
  the sanitizer route; a plain-string inbound description passes through
  `normalize_rich_text` unchanged.
- Failure/edge: an over-limit comment truncates with today's marker semantics; a raw ADF dict
  arriving on the inbound apply path is decoded to text and never written verbatim into an
  EDIT event (the bug 1bb2-5da5 regression case, now backend-neutral).
- Gate: the sweep case fails when any package-root core module (except the recorded
  `inbound_fields.py` exemption) contains the `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` literal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `outbound_comments.py` and `inbound_translate.py` contain neither `adapters.jira`
      imports nor `"rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira"` lazy-key literals — verified by the new
      sweep case in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] Comment formatting/truncation and inbound rich-text normalization behave identically
      for Jira — verified by the behavior tests in Testing (including the 1bb2-5da5
      regression case).
- [ ] The sweep gate documents the single `inbound_fields.py` exemption with its rationale
      and the follow-up ticket id — verified by reading the gate test.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Three under-scoped consumer surfaces are pinned here so no lazy-key deletion orphans a caller:

1. **Outbound-comment ADF DECODE (`outbound_comments.py:134`).** `_normalize_comment_body`
   calls `adf.adf_to_text(body)` to DECODE a remote Jira ADF comment dict to comparable text on
   the comment-DIFF path (bug 85a1) — a decode, not a send-side fit/truncate. It routes through
   the backend's `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text(body)` (the SAME decode surface as the
   inbound apply path: `adf_to_text` for dicts, identity for strings). `normalize_rich_text`
   therefore serves BOTH the inbound apply path AND this outbound comment-diff decode;
   `FieldSanitizer.fit_comment(body)` (a pure fit-to-limit, delegating to
   `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`, no send-side warning) serves the `:324` compare-body
   truncation. `outbound_comments.py` obtains BOTH the sanitizer and the inbound mapper from the
   one `select_backend(load_config())` it resolves, and BOTH literal keys at `:68,71` are deleted.

2. **`inbound_translate`'s PUBLIC decode surface (`_normalize_adf_body`).** This function is
   re-exported by `applier.py` (`__all__` lines 322/326/361/367) and imported + called at three
   sites by `apply_inbound_records.py` (lines 35, 145, 268, 308). It therefore STAYS as
   inbound_translate's public function, re-implemented to route through the backend's
   `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text(body)` (resolved via `select_backend(load_config())`), so
   BOTH consumers keep working unchanged and the bug-1bb2-5da5 defense (a raw ADF dict never
   reaches an EDIT event `description`) stays intact and backend-neutral. Only the vendor
   internals `_ADF_KEY_APPLIER` (the literal), `_AdfModule_Applier`, and `_load_adf_module` are
   deleted from `inbound_translate.py`. Because `applier.py` re-exports those three now-deleted
   names, `applier.py` drops them from its `inbound_translate` import list and from `__all__`
   (keeping `_normalize_adf_body`); `apply_inbound_records.py` is untouched.

3. **Scope additions:** `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` (drop the three dead
   re-exports; keep `_normalize_adf_body`).

**AC3 restated machine-executably:** the single-`inbound_fields.py`-exemption sweep is verified
by the test `test_no_root_core_module_carries_vendor_lazyload_literal` passing (green with
exactly that one exemption) plus a companion `test_sweep_exemption_is_still_needed` asserting
inbound_fields.py genuinely still carries the literal — both under `make test`, not by human
inspection.

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The outbound-comment ADF decode at `_normalize_comment_body:134` routes through
      `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` (NOT orphaned by the `_ADF_KEY` deletion); comment-diff
      dedup normalizes ADF-dict bodies to text byte-identically — verified by a comment-diff test
      with an ADF-dict remote body.
- [ ] `inbound_translate._normalize_adf_body` STAYS importable and routes through the port;
      `applier.py` no longer imports/re-exports `_ADF_KEY_APPLIER`/`_AdfModule_Applier`/
      `_load_adf_module`; `apply_inbound_records.py`'s three call sites behave identically
      (ADF dict -> text) — verified by the behavior tests plus a green import of both modules.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 936 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Rich-text codec and comment limits behind the port: delete the adapters.jira lazy-key literals from core

baseline.description:
# Committed store compatibility record with a fail-closed capability gate

Introduce a committed store-level compatibility record (`format_version` + `required_capabilities`) that a v1.0 binary reads before any mutating or externally-publishing operation, failing closed on an unknown version or required capability while keeping reads and diagnostics available. (Readiness Finding 2 — verified VALID against `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/{compact,fsck,init}.py`, `docs/migrations.md`.)

## Why

rebar's migration mechanism is an idempotent desired-state ensure-registry, not an ordered ledger: `run_ensures` runs every unit under the write lock, converts exceptions to `failed`, and **returns normally** (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` docstring "Never raises"; init/boot never abort). Event compatibility is preserve-and-ignore: unknown event types are skipped in replay (`reducer/_replay.py:195-196`) and omitted from the compaction fold but kept on disk (`_commands/compact.py:179-195`), and `fsck` emits an informational WARN that does not increment `issue_count` or stop operation (`_commands/fsck.py:229-252`, which itself notes "a reconcile host on an old binary may push stale state").

This forward-compat is correct for *optional additive* data — it prevents an old compactor from deleting new bytes. But there is **no committed store-format-version or required-capability record** (confirmed absent; `SCHEMA_VERSION` is a stamp, never compared to fail closed). So an old binary computes state that omits the unknown event and can then emit a new event, compact, evaluate close/verify policy, or push a stale field to Jira from that incomplete state. `docs/migrations.md` explicitly files the "A-tier ledger + committed store-format version that fails closed" under future work. **The reader must ship in v1.0**: an already-installed v1.0 binary cannot be taught later to inspect a record whose existence and semantics were not defined in v1.0 — so to ever mark a store as requiring a post-v1.0 capability, v1.0 must already know how to detect and refuse unknown required capabilities.

## What

Adopt git's repository-format-version pattern (`core.repositoryformatversion` + `extensions.*`: an implementation that does not understand the advertised format or a required extension must not operate, because continuing can produce incorrect results or lose data), and git's staged rollout (teach readers first, make writing opt-in, default later):

- **The record.** Add a committed store-level record, minimally
  `{"format_version": 1, "required_capabilities": []}`, at a fixed store path (e.g.
  `.store-compat.json`). It is **committed to the `tickets` branch** (not
  git-ignored) — it is the shared fact the gate reads. Write it with the store's
  standard write-to-tempfile-then-atomic-rename pattern so a partial/interrupted
  write never leaves a truncated file.
- **Recognised-capability vocabulary.** The new module exports
  `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()` — the set of capability strings
  **this** binary understands. The gate blocks when any entry in a record's
  `required_capabilities` is not in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. Future capabilities are
  added to this set only when the feature that consumes them ships (git
  `extensions.*` semantics).
- **The gate error.** The module exports `StoreIncompatibleError(Exception)`, raised
  by the gate; entry-point callers convert it to the existing `CommandError` /
  non-zero exit path (as other gate errors do), with a message naming the
  unsupported version/capability.
- **Four record states (explicit).** (1) **Absent** → implicit legacy format
  version 0, compatible / pass-through, NOT blocked. (2) **Present + compatible** →
  pass. (3) **Present + incompatible** (unknown `format_version` or a
  `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`) → **fail-closed**. (4)
  **Present + unreadable/corrupt** (JSON parse error, truncation, permission denied)
  → **fail-closed** with a diagnostic message naming the parse error and the record
  path (a corrupt record is NOT treated as absent — that would silently bypass the
  gate).
- **Expand phase (writing the record into pre-v1.0 stores).** Every store created by
  a pre-v1.0 build is state (1). An idempotent ensure unit (School B) writes the
  record at the current version when absent, at init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot.
  **Because `run_ensures` is fail-silent** (a `LockTimeout` silently skips the whole
  sweep; exceptions become `failed` and it returns normally), the covered-write path
  must not *depend* on the ensure sweep having run: the gate treats absent as
  pass-through regardless, and the record is written opportunistically. So a missed
  sweep never blocks writes — it only defers stamping the record to a later covered
  operation. **absent = legacy/needs-migration, not blocked; present-incompatible or
  corrupt = blocked.**
- **Gate at the true structural choke point, NOT by enumerating call-sites.** "No
  mutation without the gate" must not rest on a hand-maintained list a future path can
  bypass. The single convergence point for **all lock-based store mutations** is
  **`lock.acquire()` in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`** — both the `write_lock()` context
  manager AND the direct callers that bypass it (`txn.py`'s `_acquire_write_lock` for
  claim/transition, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`) call `acquire()`. Insert
  the `check_store_compat()` gate **inside `lock.acquire()`**, after `canonical_tracker()`
  resolves the path and before the fcntl/mkdir legs — so every lock-holding path
  (context-manager and raw-handle) is covered by one insertion point, with no
  enumeration. **Gate ALL `lock.acquire()` unconditionally — no `read_only` parameter
  needed.** The diagnostic exemption is already **structural**: `fsck`'s diagnostic
  path reads ticket data **without acquiring the lock at all**, so it is inherently
  ungated and stays available; only `fsck`'s **repair** path (which *does* call
  `lock.acquire()` at `fsck.py:419`), and `compact.py`/`txn.py`, hold the lock and are
  therefore gated. This is simpler and less error-prone than a read/write-intent flag.
- **`run_ensures` must NOT swallow the gate (fail-closed integrity).** `run_ensures`
  (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`) wraps its whole `with write_lock(...)` body in a broad
  `except Exception` that logs-and-returns (honouring its "Never raises" sweep contract).
  Because the gate raises `StoreIncompatibleError` **inside `lock.acquire()`** — which
  `write_lock()` calls — that broad handler would **catch and swallow it**, turning a
  fail-closed incompatibility into a silent sweep no-op for every caller that self-heals
  through `run_ensures` (init, MCP-boot's ensure sweep, `fsck --repair`). Remediate by
  adding an explicit `except StoreIncompatibleError: raise` **before** the broad
  `except Exception` in `run_ensures`, so the incompatibility propagates to the caller;
  the init / MCP-boot / fsck-repair entry points then surface it as a **non-zero exit /
  refused startup** (converting `StoreIncompatibleError` to their existing
  `CommandError` / error path). This keeps the gate un-swallowable on the ensure-sweep
  path. (Note: `StoreIncompatibleError` subclasses `Exception`, so this explicit re-raise
  is required — it is not skipped automatically the way a `BaseException` would be.)
- **Two paths do NOT go through `lock.acquire()` and each gets its own explicit gate:**
  1. **`fsck_recover.py`** performs raw `git cherry-pick`/`rebase --continue`/`merge
     --abort` via its `_git()` helper with **no locking at all** — so it is genuinely
     un-gated by the lock choke point. Add an explicit `check_store_compat(tracker_dir)`
     at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` before any mutation. (Wrapping the mutation block
     in `write_lock` too would additionally close a real pre-existing concurrency gap,
     but at minimum the explicit gate is required.)
  2. **Outbound Jira publish** — the push/reconcile side effect is a **remote API
     call**, not a lock-held write. Jira writes are scattered
     (`create_issue`/`update_issue`/`delete_issue`/`add_comment` across
     `apply_outbound.py` + `dispatch_one.py`), but they all funnel once per pass
     through **`reconcile._apply_mutations()`** (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py`,
     which calls `applier.apply(...)`). **Exact insertion point (no top-level `persist`
     guard exists in this function):** `_apply_mutations()` binds `persist = ctx.persist`
     near the top and threads it down into `applier.apply(...)`; it has **no**
     `if persist:` / `if not persist: return` branch of its own. So add the gate
     explicitly: immediately after `persist = ctx.persist` is bound (before the
     filter-narrowing / preflight block), insert
     `if persist: check_store_compat(repo_root / ".tickets-tracker")`. Because dry-run /
     reconcile-check / cap-0 passes run with `persist=False`, the `if persist:` guard
     excludes them; live (persisting) passes are gated before any `applier.apply(...)`
     Jira write. This mirrors the existing fail-closed cross-project guard precedent at
     `applier.py:637-652` ("refuse BEFORE issuing any Jira write … abort the whole pass,
     no partial writes"). **Use the reconciler's own tracker path**
     (`repo_root / ".tickets-tracker"`, hardcoded at `reconcile.py:133/670`), NOT
     `config.tracker_dir()`, since the reconciler resolves the store directly.
- **Completeness is CI-enforced.** A coverage test/lint greps the tree for **both**
  `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(` (and asserts each routes through the gate) plus
  asserts `fsck_recover_cli` calls `check_store_compat` — so a new un-gated write path,
  in any of the acquisition forms, fails CI rather than relying on this prose list.
- **Read/diagnostic allowance + the structured report shape (defined).** Under an
  incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only commands — `fsck` (diagnostic mode),
  `show`, `list`, `search` — stay available (exit 0). The incompatibility is surfaced in
  a **defined, machine-checkable shape**: `fsck`'s diagnostic JSON gains a top-level
  `compat_error` object
  `{"compat_error": {"kind": "unknown_format_version" | "unknown_capability" | "corrupt_record",
  "detail": "<human string naming the offending version / capability / parse-error + the
  record path>"}}` (and the same message on a stderr `WARNING` line). The `compat` module
  exports a **non-raising** `describe_store_compat(tracker) -> dict | None` that returns
  exactly this `{"kind", "detail"}` payload (or `None` when compatible/absent); the fsck
  diagnostic path calls it and, when non-`None`, attaches it as `compat_error` and emits
  the WARNING — without changing the exit code. AC6 asserts `.compat_error.kind` via
  `jq -e` so the check is deterministic. `fsck`'s **repair** mode (write-intent) is gated
  like any other mutation (non-zero exit).
- **Rollback safety (decided, then proven).** Post-rollback the committed
  `.store-compat.json` remains on the `tickets` branch unchanged, and a pre-v1.0 binary
  **ignores it** (ignored-unknown → rollback-safe): `.store-compat.json` is a *new*
  file at a path no pre-v1.0 code reads — pre-v1.0 replay/compaction/fsck open only
  event files and the known metadata files (`.env-id`, `.gitignore`, etc.), never this
  name — so there is no parse-and-error path. This is the committed design position
  (not a deferral), and the **hard rollback test below is its empirical proof** (git-
  stash the gate code, run `rebar fsck` against a store containing `.store-compat.json`,
  assert operable + file byte-unchanged). The delete-`.store-compat.json` recovery is
  documented as belt-and-suspenders only.
- **Scope boundary.** Keep the ensure-registry for convergent check-then-act repairs.
  Do **not** build the ordered ledger here — only the record + reader gate. Clarify
  the relationship to `SCHEMA_VERSION` in `reducer/_version.py` (it stays the
  event-schema discriminator; `format_version` is the new store-format gate — state
  whether they move together or independently).

## Scope

- New module under `src/rebar/_store/` for the compatibility record + gate, exporting
  `StoreIncompatibleError`, `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`, and `check_store_compat()`.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — insert the gate inside `lock.acquire()` (the single
  convergence point for `write_lock()` + all direct `lock.acquire()` callers:
  `txn.py`, `compact.py:167`/`:415`, `fsck.py:419`), gating every acquisition
  unconditionally (fsck diagnostic holds no lock → structurally exempt).
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py` — explicit `check_store_compat()` before its
  raw-git mutation (it holds no lock, so the `lock.acquire()` gate does not cover it).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — `if persist: check_store_compat(repo_root/".tickets-tracker")`
  inserted in `_apply_mutations()` immediately after `persist = ctx.persist` is bound
  (the function has no top-level `persist` guard; the `if persist:` wrapper is the single
  per-pass chokepoint for both write paths and excludes dry-run/cap-0 passes).
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` — add `except StoreIncompatibleError: raise` before
  `run_ensures`'s broad `except Exception` so the gate is not swallowed on the ensure
  sweep; add a `store-compat` ensure unit id.
- A coverage test/lint grepping `lock.acquire(` + `write_lock(` + `fsck_recover`'s check.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` — relate `format_version` to the existing
  preserve-and-ignore `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` machinery and to `SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (optional-additive events stay preserve-and-ignore; a required capability is the
  new fail-closed path).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — the ensure unit that writes the record when absent.
- `docs/migrations.md` — document the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  semantics, the absent-record upgrade path, and the concrete rollback state.
- Interface tests extending `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py`.
- Out of scope: the ordered migration ledger; changing any existing event-replay
  behaviour for currently-known types.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A committed store compatibility record (`format_version` +
  `required_capabilities`) is created at init at a fixed path, written atomically
  (tempfile + rename), and read by a gate function that raises
  `StoreIncompatibleError`; the module exports `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str]`.
- [ ] An **absent** record (pre-v1.0 store) is treated as legacy format version 0 /
  compatible (pass-through, not blocked), and the ensure unit idempotently writes the
  record on the next init / fsck-repair / MCP-boot — verified by a test that opens a
  record-less store with a v1.0 build, confirms it operates, and confirms the record
  is then present (upgrade-in-place, no manual step); the test also confirms a missed
  ensure sweep does not block writes — by monkeypatching `run_ensures` to raise
  `LockTimeout` (or return a `failed` outcome) and asserting a subsequent write still
  succeeds (the gate treats the still-absent record as pass-through).
- [ ] The gate is inserted inside `lock.acquire()` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, after
  path resolution, before fcntl/mkdir) and gates **every** acquisition unconditionally
  — `write_lock()` context-manager callers AND direct `lock.acquire()` callers
  (`txn.py`, `compact.py`, `fsck.py:419` repair) — by one insertion point; `fsck`
  diagnostic holds no lock so it is structurally exempt. Plus an explicit
  `check_store_compat()` at the top of `fsck_recover_cli` (raw-git, no-lock mutation)
  and in `reconcile._apply_mutations()` as `if persist: check_store_compat(repo_root/".tickets-tracker")`
  inserted immediately after `persist = ctx.persist` is bound (there is no top-level
  `persist` guard in that function; the `if persist:` wrapper is what excludes
  dry-run/reconcile-check/cap-0 passes), before `applier.apply()`, for the outbound
  Jira push. It raises `StoreIncompatibleError` (→ non-zero exit) before any side
  effect when the record is **present but incompatible**. Verified by (a) a test in
  `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py` writing a record
  with a `required_capabilities` entry ∉ `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` (e.g. `["unknown-v99"]`)
  and driving a lock-held mutation (store files byte-unchanged), an `fsck_recover`
  invocation, and a reconcile pass (mock Jira adapter records zero calls); and (b) a
  coverage test/lint that greps the tree for **both** `lock.acquire(` and `write_lock(`
  and for `fsck_recover_cli`'s + `_apply_mutations`'s `check_store_compat` call,
  asserting each routes through the
  gate — so a new un-gated write path in any acquisition form fails CI.
- [ ] A **corrupt/unreadable** record (truncated JSON / parse error) is treated as
  fail-closed (NOT as absent) with a diagnostic naming the parse error and path —
  verified by a test writing a truncated record and asserting a mutating entry point
  is blocked.
- [ ] A rollback **test** (hard requirement) simulates a pre-v1.0 binary by invoking
  the store layer with the gate patched out (monkeypatch `check_store_compat` to a
  no-op, emulating code that predates it) against a store carrying the committed
  `.store-compat.json`, and asserts **operable** = `rebar list`/`fsck` exit 0 AND a
  normal write (e.g. `comment`) succeeds, and the `.store-compat.json` file is
  byte-unchanged afterward (proving upgrade-in-place won't brick a pre-v1.0 clone). The
  ignored-unknown guarantee and the delete-`.store-compat.json` compensating path are
  also documented in `docs/migrations.md`.
- [ ] Under an incompatible/corrupt record, the read-only commands `fsck` (diagnostic
  mode), `show`, `list`, and `search` exit with the read-allowed code (0) and `fsck`'s
  diagnostic JSON carries a defined `compat_error` object
  `{"compat_error": {"kind": "unknown_format_version"|"unknown_capability"|"corrupt_record",
  "detail": "<...>"}}` (produced by the non-raising `describe_store_compat()`), with the
  same message on a stderr `WARNING` line — while `fsck` **repair** mode (write-intent)
  exits non-zero — verified by a test asserting `.compat_error.kind` via `jq -e` (a
  deterministic field check, not a substring grep) and the repair-mode non-zero exit.
- [ ] The gate is **un-swallowable on the ensure-sweep path**: `run_ensures`'s broad
  `except Exception` does not silently absorb `StoreIncompatibleError` (it has an explicit
  `except StoreIncompatibleError: raise` before it), so init / MCP-boot / `fsck --repair`
  against a present-but-incompatible store fail closed (non-zero exit / refused startup)
  rather than logging a sweep no-op — verified by a test that stamps an incompatible
  record and asserts `run_ensures` (or the init entry point that calls it) surfaces the
  error rather than returning a benign `failed` outcome.
- [ ] Optional additive (unknown-but-not-*required*) events retain today's
  preserve-and-ignore behaviour — the existing forward-compat contract tests still
  pass, and a new test proves a *required* capability fails closed while an *optional*
  additive event does not.
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents the record, the four states, the fail-closed
  gate, the deployment-order rationale (why the reader ships in v1.0), and the
  concrete rollback state. … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Committed store compatibility record with a fail-closed capability gate

## Why

Static wiring tests cannot prove that an LLM criterion distinguishes concrete breakage scenarios from harmless silence or valid project customization. A balanced, repeatable evaluation is needed before the blocking project criterion is considered ready.

## What

Add a project criterion evaluation corpus, add structural tests for that corpus, run the existing live evaluation runner, and tune only the project rubric if calibration exposes false positives or missed portability failures.

## Scope

In scope:

- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`, only for calibration-driven rubric adjustments
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py`
- live evaluation of `project.portability`

Out of scope:

- core registry, verifier, or disposition changes
- coaching move behavior
- existing portability debt
- adding requirements for client-agnostic wording

## Approach

Use the existing project eval override path proven by `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/README.plan-review.md`: `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` resolves for logical criterion `project.portability`. Author this exact top-level contract:

- `prompt: plan-review-project-portability`
- `model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`
- `epochs: 3`
- `gate: at_least(2)`
- `coverage_threshold: 1.0`
- one deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer
- a balanced `dataset` plus a non-empty `gold_set`

The dataset contains exactly eight ids. Each must-fire case uses `expect: finding`, includes an inline `input` plan, and uses the existing `note` metadata field. The note is one non-empty string containing the exact labels `Plan citation:`, `Alternate shape:`, `Causal mechanism:`, and `Observable breakage:` with non-whitespace text after every label:

- `PORT-F1`: reusable core adds `rebar landing` with a Gerrit-only push flow; alternate clients do not use this repository policy.
- `PORT-F2`: reusable core adds Python-only review criteria; Java, Next.js, .NET, Ruby, and Terraform projects cannot apply them.
- `PORT-F3`: reusable execution requires the macOS `security` binary; Windows, Linux, and BSD fail before work begins.
- `PORT-F4`: remote MCP derives the target repo from `Path.cwd()` plus unrestricted local filesystem access; a server outside the checkout cannot find or read the project.

Each must-not-fire case uses `expect: pass`:

- `PORT-N1`: the plan is silent about portability and contains no incompatible mechanism.
- `PORT-N2`: Gerrit-specific coaching remains in `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json` project configuration.
- `PORT-N3`: an additive terminal-color feature is explicitly limited to the CLI and leaves library plus MCP behavior unchanged.
- `PORT-N4`: workspace discovery accepts an explicit path and uses portable standard-library filesystem operations.

The `gold_set` contains all eight cases. Each gold entry carries a non-empty `input` scenario description plus a matching `finding` or `pass` `label`. The `finding_contract` test loads the YAML directly and asserts every `PORT-F*` note is a string whose four exact labels are each followed by non-whitespace text; it does not rely on `validate_eval_spec` to interpret note content. Run each dataset case three times through `rebar criteria eval`. The release threshold is recall `1.0`, false-accept rate `0.0`, `agreement: 1.0`, per-case `stability >= 0.6666666667`, and Cohen kappa `>= 0.70`. Kappa is specifically `calibrate_criterion` expected-vs-observed fire/no-fire agreement over the eight dataset cases; it is not `judge_alignment` and requires no LLM-judge scorer. If the threshold is missed, revise only `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` and rerun; do not change the generic registry, Pass 2, or Pass 3. If any model call times out, returns an API error, or produces a partial result, do not attest the partial output. Make at most three complete-command attempts: wait 30 seconds before attempt two and 120 seconds before attempt three. If attempt three fails, stop, leave the criterion uncalibrated, and record each UTC failure time plus error summary on the ticket; a later execution must start a fresh three-attempt sequence.

`tests/unit/test_criteria_eval.py` is the prior art for project prompt-id mapping, injected calibration, metric keys, and N-run stability. The new structural tests use the real eval loader plus `validate_eval_spec`; they use an injected solve function for deterministic metric assertions and never make a billable call.

## Dependencies

Depends on the criterion-integration child because calibration executes the activated project criterion and its authored rubric.

## Test Strategy

Validate corpus structure deterministically, then use the live criterion evaluation command for semantic calibration. Record the model, timestamp, run count, and aggregate metrics on this ticket so the external LLM result is auditable by the completion gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The project eval override resolves from `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k override_resolution`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `prompt: plan-review-project-portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `epochs: 3` plus `gate: at_least(2)`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares `coverage_threshold: 1.0`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The eval spec declares one deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k spec_contract`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly `PORT-F1` through `PORT-F4` with `expect: finding`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k balanced_corpus`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly `PORT-N1` through `PORT-N4` with `expect: pass`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k balanced_corpus`.
- [ ] Every must-fire case has a non-empty `note` whose four exact labels are followed by non-whitespace text. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k finding_contract`.
- [ ] The must-not-fire cases respectively cover silence, project configuration, explicit surface scoping, plus portable alternatives. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k negative_boundaries`.
- [ ] Every gold entry carries a non-empty `input` plus the expected `label`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k gold_set`.
- [ ] An injected perfect solve returns the exact metric mapping specified in the Approach. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py -k calibration_metrics`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] One complete CLI result satisfies the exact live threshold mapping in the Approach; a ticket comment records the command, model, UTC timestamp, run count, aggregate metrics, plus every case result. Prove with `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 3 --output json`.
- [ ] No calibration change touches generic implementation under `src/rebar/`. Prove with `test -z "$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src/rebar)"`.
- [ ] The final project rubric retains every structural marker specified by `immune-floury-toad`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py`.
baseline.summary: Calibrate the portability criterion

baseline.description:
# DC index lag makes a crashed create produce a DUPLICATE Jira issue

## Context / Problem

This is the only known defect where rebar writes WRONG DATA into Jira. Every other DC gap found so far causes rebar to read incomplete data or fail loudly; this one silently creates a SECOND Jira issue for the same local ticket — the exact outcome the write-ahead binding protocol exists to prevent.

**Jira DC's Lucene index is eventually consistent.** Nodes poll for index changes roughly once per second and replication can fall arbitrarily behind; Atlassian's KB and JRASERVER-70423 document a real-world lag of 2,991 seconds (~50 minutes). A JQL search cannot see an issue that is not yet indexed. Sound on Cloud, unsound on DC.

**There are TWO index-dependent sites, and an earlier draft of this ticket named only the first.** That matters, because fixing only the named one leaves the duplicate fully intact:

1. `binding_store.recover_pending`, keyless branch (`binding_store.py:521-531`) — searches for the
   `rebar-id:{local_id}` label and, on a miss, UNBINDS ("the create never reached Jira").
2. `dispatch_one.create_one`'s dedup (`dispatch_one.py:237-238`) —
   `hits = client.search_issues(f'labels = "rebar-id:{local_id}"')`, and on a miss it CREATES.

Site 2 writes the duplicate. Site 1 only removes the record that might have prevented reaching it.

**The chain, verified in source:**

    a. crash during create               -> keyless-pending entry (jira_key: None)
    b. next pass: recover_pending searches, misses (unindexed), UNBINDS
    c. outbound_differ.py:528-531 gates the create on get_jira_key(local_id) is None
    d. create_one dedup-searches, misses (unindexed), CREATES A DUPLICATE

**Why fixing site 1 alone is insufficient.** Suppose (b) leaves the entry PENDING instead of unbinding. `get_jira_key` returns `entry.get("jira_key")` (`binding_store.py:258-262`), which is `None` for a keyless-pending entry — so (c) still emits a create and (d) still misses. The duplicate happens anyway. The pending entry is invisible to the only gate that decides whether to create. `is_pending()` already exists (`binding_store.py:270`) and the differ does not consult it.

The authors already engineered this hazard away where a key was known: the KEYED-pending branch's docstring records "NO Jira search — deterministic, so a hard crash in the create->label window yields NO duplicate." The keyless branch falls back to search precisely because no key exists.

## Approach

**Suppress the CREATE while a keyless-pending binding is inside an index-lag grace window, and stop unbinding on a single negative search.** Both halves are required and they do different jobs: the create gate is what prevents the duplicate; leaving the binding pending is what gives the gate something to see.

1. **Record the evidence on the pending entry.** `recover_pending`'s keyless branch, on a negative
   search, increments a `search_miss_count` and leaves the entry PENDING rather than unbinding. The
   entry already carries `created_at` (`bind_pending`, `binding_store.py:289-297`), so its age is
   available without a schema change beyond the counter.
2. **Unbind only on corroborated absence.** Unbind when BOTH `search_miss_count >= 3` AND the entry is
   older than an index-lag grace period (default 3600s, chosen to exceed the ~2,991s lag documented in
   JRASERVER-70423). Until then the entry stays pending and the next pass retries. This converts a
   silent duplicate into a delayed-but-correct answer.
3. **Gate the create on pendingness, not just on the absent key.** The create branch is reached
   when `get_jira_key(local_id) is None`, which is ALSO true of a keyless-pending entry. The gate
   must additionally defer (not drop) the create when a keyless-pending binding for that local_id
   is younger than the grace period. This is the change that actually prevents the second issue.
   **The gate lives in `dispatch_one.create_one`, NOT in `outbound_differ`.** Two reasons, and
   the second is binding: (a) guarding at the WRITE rather than at plan time protects the actual
   create and reuses the deferred-create semantics `create_one` already has, so the mutation is
   deferred rather than dropped; (b) `outbound_differ.py` sits at EXACTLY the locked 800-LOC
   module-size cap, so nothing can be added to it.
4. `recover_pending` returns the count of RESOLVED bindings; an entry left pending is NOT resolved and
   must not be counted, or the caller reads "recovered" as "settled".

**Applied to BOTH vendors, not branched on DC.** Cloud's index is eventually consistent too — it is merely faster, so the window is narrower rather than absent. A vendor branch would mean the safe path is the one exercised least, and the correctness property (never conclude non-existence from one unindexed search) is not vendor-specific. The cost on Cloud is a create deferred by at most one pass in a rare crash-recovery path.

**Rejected: leaving the binding pending forever on repeated misses.** It is safer against duplicates but a genuinely-never-created ticket would then never sync at all — trading a rare duplicate for a permanent silent omission. The corroboration rule bounds the wait instead.

**Rejected: a non-indexed confirmation for the keyless branch.** There is none — JQL is the only way to find an issue by label, and the keyless state is by definition the one with no key to GET. That is why the keyed branch is already correct and this one cannot use the same trick.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — the keyless-branch miss counter, the
  corroborated-unbind rule, an accessor exposing "keyless-pending and within the grace window", and the
  resolved-count correction.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — `create_one` consults that accessor and
  defers the create while the binding is keyless-pending inside the grace window. (NOT `outbound_differ.py`:
  it is at the locked 800-LOC cap, and the write site is the better guard anyway.)
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests (new module).

## Testing

The oracle is a client that models the actual failure: the issue EXISTS but the search does not see it.

* **the whole path, which is the only test that proves the fix** — a lagging-index client where
  `create_issue` succeeds but `search_issues` returns empty. Drive crash -> recover -> differ -> create
  and assert EXACTLY ONE issue is created. A test asserting only "recover_pending did not unbind"
  passes today's code path while the duplicate is still written, which is the trap this closes.
* **the create is deferred, not dropped** — once the index catches up (search starts returning the
  issue), the next pass BINDS to the existing issue and still creates nothing.
* **corroborated unbind still works** — a genuinely-never-created ticket, after 3 misses AND past the
  grace window, unbinds and is then re-created, so the fix does not strand work forever.
* **the keyed branch is untouched** — its no-search determinism is asserted unchanged.
* **`recover_pending`'s return value** counts an entry left pending as NOT resolved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] under a lagging-index client (create succeeds, search returns empty), the full
      crash -> recover -> differ -> create path creates EXACTLY ONE issue, asserted by a test that
      FAILS against the current code
- [ ] the create gate consults keyless-pendingness, not only `get_jira_key(...) is None` — verified by
      reading `dispatch_one.create_one`; a fix confined to `recover_pending` does NOT satisfy this
- [ ] a single negative search never unbinds: unbinding requires >= 3 consecutive misses AND an entry
      older than the grace period, both asserted
- [ ] once the index catches up, the pending binding CONFIRMS against the existing issue and no second
      issue is created, asserted
- [ ] a genuinely-absent issue still unbinds after corroboration and is re-created, so no ticket is
      stranded permanently pending
- [ ] the KEYED-pending branch still performs NO search, asserted, since it is already correct
- [ ] `recover_pending` does not count a still-pending entry as resolved
- [ ] the Cloud path is asserted unaffected in behaviour beyond the deferral, since this changes shared
      code
- [ ] the reason (DC Lucene eventual consistency) is documented at both call sites so the next reader
      does not "simplify" the grace window away
baseline.summary: DC index lag makes recover_pending unbind a live create, producing DUPLICATE Jira issues

## Why
`_mkdir_lock_is_stale` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:169-188`) has branches for read errors
(`except OSError: return False`), missing separator, foreign host, non-int PID
(`except ValueError: return False`), and live/dead PID. Existing tests cover dead/live/
absent/foreign-host, but the **non-int PID, missing-`:`-separator, and owner-file read-error**
branches are untested (PARTIALLY-VALIDATED: a real partial-branch coverage gap). The safety
property is conservative — none of these may cause reclamation.

## What
Add a single table-driven test over the malformed/unreadable owner-stamp forms, asserting
`_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returns `False` (never reclaim) for each. Deterministic realizations of
the two racy cases:
- **unreadable owner file** → put a DIRECTORY at the owner-file path so `open()` raises
  `IsADirectoryError` (an `OSError`) → the `except OSError: return False` branch.
- **owner file replaced/observed mid-write** → a partial stamp with the colon not yet written
  (hostname only), i.e. the exact content a reader that caught the write in flight would see →
  the missing-separator branch → `False`.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` — one parametrized/table-driven test of the
  malformed-stamp forms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Table covers: empty owner file; missing colon; empty host; empty PID; non-numeric PID;
      negative PID; zero PID; extra delimiters (`host:1:2`); foreign host; a directory in place
      of the owner file (unreadable); and a partial mid-write stamp (colon not yet written).
- [ ] Every case asserts `_mkdir_lock_is_stale(...) is False` — conservative, no reclamation.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Add table-driven mkdir-lock malformed ownership-stamp tests

baseline.description:
## Why

Agents refining review criteria repeatedly blur the four-pass architecture by adding severity,
drop/block policy, or remediation instructions to Pass 1. Similar drift can make Pass 2 discover
new issues or prescribe fixes, make Pass 3 depend on model judgment, or make Pass 4 re-adjudicate
findings. Those changes erode the deliberate tension between a critical finder and a generous,
independent verifier.

## What

Dogfood rebar's project extension surface by authoring one code-review criterion,
`project.review-phase-boundaries`, with four co-located subrules:

- **Pass 1 — find:** discover grounded candidate findings only; never assess validity, impact,
  severity, confidence, drop/block posture, or remediation.
- **Pass 2 — verify:** independently answer atomic validity and impact questions only; never
  discover new findings, decide outcomes, or prescribe fixes.
- **Pass 3 — decide:** apply deterministic thresholds and partition findings without an LLM; never
  gather new evidence or coach.
- **Pass 4 — coach:** offer non-prescriptive next-move guidance for already-surfaced findings;
  never re-verify, alter the decision, or dictate an exact implementation.

The criterion itself is a Pass-1 finder: it emits grounded evidence only, carries no
severity/confidence, and always leaves `suggested_fix` empty.

## Scope

In scope:

- A committed project prompt at
  `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md`, routing/activation entry, and
  balanced eval spec at
  `.rebar/evals/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.eval.yaml`.
- Routing with `block_threshold: 0.90` and `blocking_enabled: false`; the threshold is recorded for
  pilot analysis but cannot block during this story.
- Use routing `exec: "1-TURN"` and prompt `execution_mode: single_turn` and `outputs: code_review_findings`. The finder receives the
  assembled diff, needs no repository tools or iterative calls, and returns one structured finding
  payload; single-turn keeps the pilot's runtime/cost proportional to one Pass-1 call.
- Guards that distinguish operative instructions from documentation or negative examples, require
  identifiable phase ownership, and abstain when ownership is unclear.
- Grandfather existing `suggested_fix` fields: unchanged debt is not a finding. Newly adding or
  expanding remediation instructions in Pass 1 is a finding. Removal of the field/contract is a
  separate cleanup when those core contracts are next modified.
- A balanced twelve-case corpus: `RP-F1..RP-F6` must fire and `RP-N1..RP-N6` must not fire.
- Record the live three-run eval on this ticket with model, UTC timestamp, all 36 executions, and
  the aggregate/stability metrics required below.
- Add a `Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries` subsection to `docs/llm-framework.md` explaining
  the project-owned placement, phase contract, advisory posture, and eval corpus.

Out of scope: the generic integration seam (dependency bug), live Gerrit rollout, changing the
kernel's impact model, removing grandfathered `suggested_fix`, or enabling blocking.

## Eval Contract

Each YAML case uses the `diff` key. `criteria eval` resolves the sanitized physical prompt id and
reuses eval_solver's existing `_run_code_review_case` per-prompt arm, which supplies the diff as
`ticket_context` and scores the native `{findings: [...]}` output. This calibrates the project
Pass-1 finder directly; it does not invoke plan-review `pass1_chunk` or run the full four-pass gate.

The existing `agreement` metric is the fraction of scored cases whose majority observed fire/no-fire verdict matches the expected verdict. Cross-run consistency is reported separately by each case's `stability` and the aggregate `stability_min`.

Must-fire cases cover: Pass-1 validity/impact grading; Pass-1 drop/block policy; Pass-1 remediation;
Pass-2 new-finding/decision/fix leakage; an LLM/discretionary Pass 3; and Pass-4 re-adjudication or
exact implementation prescription.

Must-not-fire cases cover: refining Pass-1 discovery scope; strengthening Pass-1 evidence rules;
refining Pass-2 atomic binary questions; changing deterministic Pass-3 threshold configuration;
adding non-prescriptive Pass-4 next-move coaching; and documenting a forbidden pattern or unchanged
grandfathered debt.

The corpus pins these concrete instructions:

- `RP-F1`: Pass 1 assigns candidate validity and impact; expect a Pass-1 assessment-leak finding.
- `RP-F2`: Pass 1 drops low-priority candidates or marks them blocking; expect a Pass-1 policy-leak
  finding.
- `RP-F3`: Pass 1 supplies an exact replacement/patch; expect a Pass-1 remediation-leak finding.
- `RP-F4`: Pass 2 may invent an additional issue, choose disposition, or direct a fix; expect a
  Pass-2 ownership finding.
- `RP-F5`: an LLM weighs evidence or chooses disposition in Pass 3; expect a deterministic-policy
  finding.
- `RP-F6`: Pass 4 overturns a finding or dictates an exact implementation; expect a coaching
  boundary finding.
- `RP-N1`: Pass 1 narrows the problem class it discovers; expect no finding.
- `RP-N2`: Pass 1 strengthens file/line/quote evidence requirements; expect no finding.
- `RP-N3`: Pass 2 asks atomic validity and impact yes/no questions; expect no finding.
- `RP-N4`: deterministic Pass-3 routing changes a numeric threshold or advisory posture; expect no
  finding.
- `RP-N5`: Pass 4 offers an investigative next move without selecting the implementation; expect no
  finding.
- `RP-N6`: documentation/eval text quotes a forbidden pattern, or a diff shows only unchanged
  grandfathered `suggested_fix` context; expect no finding.

Only added or modified normative instructions in prompt, workflow-op, or criterion content are
operative. Documentation, tests, eval expectations, explicitly labeled examples, and unchanged diff
context are descriptive. A candidate must identify the owning phase from the changed instruction;
otherwise the criterion abstains.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` activates `project.review-phase-boundaries` for `code_review`
  with `exec: "1-TURN"`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, and `blocking_enabled: false`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; d=json.load(open(".rebar/criteria_routing.json")); r=d["code_review"]["project.review-phase-boundaries"]; assert "project.review-phase-boundaries" in d["activate"] and r["exec"] == "1-TURN" and r["block_threshold"] == 0.90 and r["blocking_enabled"] is False'`.
- [ ] `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md` encodes all four
  allowed/prohibited boundaries plus the
  instruction-vs-description, unclear-phase abstention, negative-example, and grandfathered-debt
  guards and declares `execution_mode: single_turn` and `outputs: code_review_findings`. A runner-backed test inspects emitted findings
  and asserts grounded evidence is present, `severity`/`confidence` are absent, and
  `suggested_fix` is absent or empty; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path(".rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md").read_text(); assert "execution_mode: single_turn" in s' &&
  .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py`.
- [ ] The criterion emits one evidence-grounded finding for each `RP-F1..RP-F6`, emits none for
  `RP-N1..RP-N6`, never emits severity/confidence, and leaves `suggested_fix` empty. Across three
  runs, recall is `1.0`, false-accept is `0.0`, agreement is `1.0`, minimum per-case stability is at
  least `2/3`, and Cohen kappa is at least `0.70`; verify the committed corpus with
  `.venv/bin/rebar criteria eval project.review-phase-boundaries --runs 3 --output json |
  .venv/bin/python -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d["recall"] == 1.0 and
  d["false_accept"] == 0.0 and d["agreement"] == 1.0 and d["stability_min"] >= 2/3 and
  d["kappa"] >= 0.70, d'`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A complete three-run live eval is recorded on this ticket with model,
  timestamp, all 36 case executions, recall `1.0`, false-accept `0.0`, agreement `1.0`, minimum
  per-case stability at least `2/3`, and Cohen kappa at least `0.70`.
- [ ] The criterion is entirely project-owned: its implementation diff changes only committed
  `.rebar/` prompt/routing/eval assets, their `.gitignore` exceptions, criterion-specific tests,
  and the `Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries` subsection of `docs/llm-framework.md`; verify
  with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import subprocess; allowed={".rebar/criteria_routing.json", ".rebar/prompts/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.md", ".rebar/evals/code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries.eval.yaml", ".gitignore", "tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py", "docs/llm-framework.md"}; commits=subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "origin/main", "--format=%H", "--grep=rebar-ticket: 225a-323c-a9f6-436b"], text=True).split(); assert commits, "criterion commit is not on origin/main"; changed={p for commit in commits for p in subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", "--format=", "--name-only", commit], text=True).splitlines() if p}; extra=changed-allowed; assert not extra, f"non-project paths changed: {sorted(extra)}"' &&
  .venv/bin/python -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("docs/llm-framework.md").read_text(); assert "Project dogfood: review-phase-boundaries" in s' &&
  .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py && make lint`.
- [ ] The criterion change is landed on `main`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import subprocess; commits=subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "origin/main", "--format=%H", "--grep=rebar-ticket: 225a-323c-a9f6-436b"], text=True).split(); assert commits, "criterion commit is not on origin/main"'`.

## Dependency

Depends on the linked, closed, and landed CLI-admission story `41e2-a0a2-2db4-4847`, whose prerequisite seam stories supply code-review prompt-id resolution, Round-A fan-in, Pass-3 repository routing, and gate-aware calibration. This story uses those generic extension points and must not add a core special case for `project.review-phase-boundaries`.

No change is needed in src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py: its _degraded_plan_review_verdict outage path already passes ALL det_blocks (not just P8) into partition_findings, confirmed by reading that function. The existing workflow test test_p1_det_block_still_runs_llm_and_blocks (tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py:448) asserts the OLD behavior and is inverted by this change: it will be rewritten to assert finder.calls == 0 and a BLOCK verdict with coverage.llm_ran False. content.text: # S6 — Monitoring, back-out, and live E2E proof + docs
Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).
## Why
The PoC's success criterion is proving the two-vote gate end-to-end on the live Gerrit, with the
operability a real gate needs: failure alarms and a tested back-out. This story activates the gate
(after the voter is proven) and demonstrates the whole flow.
## What
Add a CloudWatch alarm for g2p dispatch + `Verified`-vote failures, a tested back-out, activate the
two-vote submit requirement, run the live end-to-end proof, and document the flow + design notes.
## Scope
- Monitoring (Terraform alarm + `infra/scripts/observability.sh` metric), back-out procedure,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, design notes. Gated on S1–S5.
- Out of scope: the individual component builds (S1–S5).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add a CloudWatch alarm for g2p hook-dispatch failures and `Verified`-vote failures — publish
the metric from a journald log pattern via `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (modeled on the
`voter_errors` metric behind `monitoring_s4b.tf`); name the log source, pattern, and metric.
- [ ] Document and TEST a back-out: disabling the `Verified` submit requirement restores
single-vote (`LLM-Review`-only) gating if g2p/CI is broken.
- [ ] Activate the two-vote submit requirement (authored in S1) now that the voter is proven.
- [ ] Live E2E on the Gerrit host: a red CI blocks submit; `recheck` re-runs; a green change with
BOTH votes submits and replicates to GitHub `main`. Record the change URL + both votes.
- [ ] Update `CONTRIBUTING.md` (two-vote flow + `recheck`) and capture design notes (cost / latency
budget, flaky-test handling, `copyCondition` re-run behavior).

content.text: ## Why
The plan-review attestation's freshness is currently bound to the exact code HEAD sha
(`attest.py` `claim_gate_check` step 3: `result.head_sha != head` → `stale-head`). This is
too coarse in BOTH directions:
- **Over-invalidation (child bug `worm-folly-barge`):** ANY commit — even an unrelated file or a
docs typo — invalidates a freshly-earned, still-correct attestation, forcing a slow (~3-5 min),
billable re-review for no semantic reason. Especially painful on multi-ticket branches and
shared-checkout test runs that move HEAD.
- **Under-invalidation (this epic's core goal):** the binding is to the WHOLE commit, not to the
code the review was actually grounded against, so the design also fails to model "the cited code
drifted" precisely.
Fix: scope attestation freshness to **what the review depended on, not who/what changed the rest of
the tree** — the content of the dependency files — using a content-addressed (Merkle) binding. This
matches the consensus of every sound incremental-staleness system (Gerrit `copyCondition`
`has:unchanged-files`, Bazel input-hashing, proof-caching dependency checksums). No per-commit
attribution, so the "sibling exemption" concern dissolves: a sibling's edit to a shared file is
treated exactly like any other edit.
## What
- **Dependency set** = union of the ticket's declared `file_impact` and the files cited in the
review's findings (whole-file granularity). The cited files are extracted **at sign time from the
in-memory verdict** — each finding's `citations[]` entries with `kind == "file"` (the
`CITATION_KINDS` vocabulary in `findings.py`) contribute their `path`. They are NOT read back from
the persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar, whose `_slim` form drops citation paths; and they are never
needed at claim time (the claim check reads the signed map, below).
- **Content-addressed binding:** at sign time, compute a `{path: content-hash}` map of the
dependency set and store it **inside the signed manifest** (`build_manifest` / `sign_plan_review`)
so drift detection is tamper-evident. (Today `head_sha` is recorded as audit metadata but is NOT
in the signed payload — this also closes that latent integrity gap.)
- **Hash algorithm/format:** SHA-256 over the **raw file bytes** (no newline/whitespace
normalization); binary and large files are hashed the same way (no special-casing). A path in the
set that does not exist on disk is recorded with a fixed `"absent"` sentinel hash, so a later
deletion (absent→present or present→absent) is a detectable change.
- **Content source:** the **working-tree, on-disk** file content (what `review-plan` actually reads
when it grounds the review), at BOTH sign time and claim time — NOT the committed git-blob at
HEAD. This is why the binding is HEAD-move/rebase immune: only the bytes the review saw matter.
- **Drift check at claim:** replace the whole-HEAD exact-match (`claim_gate_check` step 3) with a
per-file content-hash comparison. Any mismatch / deletion / unexpected-creation of a dependency
file = drift → block the claim (invalidate), prompting re-review. Content-addressing makes this
ancestry-independent (immune to rebases and shared-checkout HEAD moves — the specific
`worm-folly-barge` complaint).
- **Empty-set conservative fallback:** when the dependency set is empty (no `file_impact` AND no
citations — common; this very epic has `file_impact: []`), we cannot scope, so fall back to
invalidate-on-any-commit (today's safe behavior, but now ONLY for unscopable tickets).
- **New named DET-floor check (`P9` file-impact coverage):** `det_floor.py` currently has P1–P8; P4
checks only the file-impact UPPER bound (`fi > cap`), not empty. Add a new, explicitly named check
that, for **leaf tasks only** (`applies_at`), emits an **advisory finding (never blocks)** when
`file_impact` is empty, advising the caller to specify the `{path, reason}` files this work will
touch — so the attestation can be scoped to them (otherwise any commit invalidates it) and
`next_batch` can schedule it conflict-free. Register it in `CANONICAL_DET`, the completeness guard,
and the module docstring.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — `build_manifest` / `sign_plan_review` (embed the signed
`{path: content-hash}` map); `claim_gate_check` (replace step-3 whole-HEAD match with the per-file
drift check; `head_sha` / `signed_at` remain audit metadata only).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — new `p9_file_impact_coverage` advisory check, added to
the `DET_CHECKS` tuple + the module docstring.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — add `"P9"` to the `CANONICAL_DET` tuple and the
completeness guard (these live in `registry.py`, NOT `det_floor.py`).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — resolve the dependency set at sign time
(`file_impact` via `get_file_impact` ∪ the verdict findings' `kind=="file"` citation `path`s).
- Tests under the plan-review test suite.
Out of scope (Story 2): the narrowed delta-re-review on drift. This story always falls back to a
FULL re-review when drift invalidates.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The attestation binds a SIGNED `{path: content-hash}` map of the dependency set
(`file_impact` ∪ review-cited files); the whole-HEAD exact-match staleness check is removed.
- [ ] Claim SUCCEEDS when an unrelated file changed after signing (fixes `worm-folly-barge`); claim
is BLOCKED when a dependency file's content changed or was deleted (closes under-invalidation).
- [ ] Empty dependency set → conservative invalidate-on-any-commit fallback.
- [ ] New explicitly named DET check (`P9`) emits an advisory (non-blocking) warning on empty
`file_impact` at leaf tasks, with guidance text; registered in `CANONICAL_DET` + completeness
guard + module docstring. (Confirmed P4 does not already cover empty.)
- [ ] The drift check is content-addressed (rebase / HEAD-move immune) and cheap; a **test measures**
it (times `claim_gate_check`'s drift step over a representative dependency set, e.g. ~30 files,
and asserts it stays in low single-digit ms) and asserts the claim path makes no LLM/network
call — the perf claim is verified, not just asserted.
- [ ] The signed manifest serializes the dependency binding as a **per-path `{path: content-hash}`
map** (NOT a single rolled-up root hash), so Story 2 (`grace-thud-feint`) can attach a
per-finding code-hash vintage + reuse map on top of it. This payload shape is the contract
fixed in ADR `0002-code-drift-invalidation.md`.
- [ ] **Claim-path check reads the SIGNED map, not a re-derived set.** At claim time the drift check
iterates the `{path: hash}` entries IN the signed manifest and re-hashes exactly those paths —
it does NOT recompute `file_impact ∪ citations` from current ticket state. (Re-deriving would
let a post-sign `file_impact` shrink silently drop paths from the check and evade drift
detection; the signed map is the authoritative, tamper-evident set.)
- [ ] **Citation extraction is schema-correct.** The "cited files" half of the dependency set is
taken from the structured citation `path` (`kind == "file"`) on the **in-memory verdict's**
findings at sign time (the persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` `_slim` sidecar drops paths, so it is NOT
the source); a citation with no resolvable `path` is ignored (fall back to `file_impact`)
rather than guessed. Verify the actual findings/citation schema and
use the structured field; if none exists, that gap is part of this story's work.
- [ ] Tested: review at X, commit an unrelated file → claim succeeds; commit a dependency file →
claim blocked; delete a dependency file → blocked; empty-set ticket → any commit blocks; `P9`
fires on empty `file_impact` and is silent when populated.

baseline.summary: Code-drift detection + invalidation: content-addressed attestation freshness scoped to the review's dependency files (+ P9 empty-file-impact DET warning)

## Context

A live negative dogfood probe on Gerrit revision 8ac3d3c produced a built-in advisory but no project reviewer identity. Initial evidence showed the project prompt hash in the dependency snapshot, so repository asset capture occurred, but it did not prove that the project finder emitted a finding.

## Proven cause

Runtime experiments found that prompt metadata was read from the selected repository root while the prompt body was re-resolved without that root, producing an empty project-only prompt. Code review also computed an attested snapshot root and then discarded it for project-criterion discovery and validation. Direct ticket review and spec scan contained the same metadata/body split.

The historical revision is a limited canary: after the root repair it executes the full gate, but the unchanged project finder abstains in 5/5 isolated runs. Therefore it cannot produce project attribution. A strict FIRE fixture through the same production four-pass workflow proves that when the project finder emits, the finding retains its physical reviewer id, logical criterion id, and repository posture through Pass 3.

## Repair

- Resolve prompt metadata and bodies from one effective root.
- Use the attested snapshot for project-criterion discovery, validation, and execution; align explicit local runs to their live root.
- Apply the same repair to direct ticket review and spec scan.
- Preserve built-in and overlay-absent behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The precise changeable cause of the missing project reviewer and logical criterion identity is proven with runtime evidence from the real pipeline.
- [x] Automated coverage reproduces the root split before the fix and passes after it.
- [x] A project finding retains reviewer_id code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries and criteria project.review-phase-boundaries through clustering, Pass 2, Pass 3, and result emission.
- [x] Pass 3 applies block_threshold 0.90 and blocking_enabled false to the project finding, while overlay-absent and built-in attribution remain unchanged.
- [x] The repair lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments.
- [x] The unchanged historical probe is rerun and its limitation is quantified; a strict project FIRE fixture through the same full gate demonstrates the required identity and posture.
baseline.summary: Live project code-review finding loses criterion identity before Pass 3

# The Gerrit review bot cannot invoke Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change

Since the eb6e Bedrock cutover went live, the review bot's `base` step dies with a 403 and the bot casts a fail-closed `LLM-Review -1`. **Nothing can land through Gerrit** — the `LLM-Review +1` gate is one of the two required votes and only the bot can cast it.

## Evidence

Change 1331, patch set 1 (2026-08-04 00:45:54Z):

    [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (llm-unavailable)]
    step 'base' failed: status_code: 403, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    User: arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5
    is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel on resource:
    arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:896586841071:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    with an explicit deny in an identity-based policy

    Automatic retries exhausted (1 attempt(s)) — casting the fail-closed -1.

## It is a regression, and the window is tight

 * change 1330 got `LLM-Review +1` at **00:28:44Z** — the bot was healthy.
 * change 1331 got the 403 at **00:45:54Z**.

The cutover (`eb6e`, merged as `5892134975`) fills `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` with `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:186`. The review gate's `base` step is the `frontier` class, so it is the first thing the cutover re-points and the first thing to hit the deny.

## What I ruled out — the deny is NOT in the role

Read the instance role directly (`joe_frontier`, same account 896586841071):

 * inline `rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse` **ALLOWS** `bedrock:InvokeModel` on
   `arn:aws:bedrock:*:896586841071:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`, which matches the
   requested resource, and on `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*`.
 * the other two inline policies (`rebar-gerrit-cloudwatch-basic`, `rebar-gerrit-ssm-params-read`)
   contain no `Deny` and no bedrock action.
 * the only attached managed policy is `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`.
 * `PermissionsBoundary: None`.

So there is **no deny anywhere in this role's identity policies**. The explicit deny is being applied from outside the role — an org-level SCP or a similar account-wide guardrail — which is why it cannot be fixed by editing the role.

**CI's Bedrock access is unaffected**, which localises it further: the `external LLM (live bedrock)` arm of run 30857265932 succeeded at 22:04Z under the separate `rebar-external-ci-bedrock` role. Only the Gerrit instance role is denied.

## Two candidate fixes (needs an operator decision — I did not act on production infra)

 1. **Amend the org/SCP guardrail** to permit `bedrock:InvokeModel` on the opus-4-8 inference
    profile for `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`. Requires AWS admin.
 2. **Pull the documented kill switch** — `docker-compose.yml:160-163` records it as purely
    subtractive: delete the three `REBAR_LLM_*_MODEL` lines and recreate the container, and rebar
    resolves the classes back to the direct-Anthropic defaults. Restores reviews immediately;
    reverts the cutover's benefit. Needs SSM/SSH to the Gerrit host.

A third, narrower option if only opus is denied: re-point `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` at the sonnet profile that the standard class already uses — but that is unverified, because the deny's source is unknown and may cover every Claude profile for this role. Do not assume it is opus-only without testing.
## Acceptance criteria — VOID (operator ruling: maintenance window)

These were written on the assumption that the 403 was a permissions regression from the eb6e cutover. The operator has since confirmed the review bot was in a planned MAINTENANCE WINDOW, now resolved, so there is no deny to find and no fix to choose. The criteria are void rather than met, and are recorded struck through so the reasoning stays auditable.

- [x] ~~the source of the explicit deny is identified and named~~ [operator-attested] there is no
      explicit deny; the 403 was maintenance, not policy
- [x] ~~a change pushed to Gerrit receives a real LLM-Review verdict~~ [operator-attested] the bot
      is confirmed healthy again by the operator
- [x] ~~whichever fix is chosen, the outcome is recorded here~~ [operator-attested] no fix was
      required and no infrastructure was touched
baseline.summary: Gerrit review bot 403s on Bedrock: LLM-Review fail-closes on every change, nothing can land

## Summary

`rebar criteria eval <project.criterion>` (and the underlying
`calibrate_criterion`) cannot run the LIVE calibration of any project criterion
whose logical id contains the `project.` namespace dot, because the physical
prompt-id → criterion-id round-trip is lossy.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Activate a project criterion via `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (e.g.
   `project.portability`, `exec: 1-TURN`) with a rubric prompt and an eval fixture
   at `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`.
2. Run `rebar criteria eval project.portability --runs 1 --output json`.

Expected: the criterion runs live over the dataset and prints calibration metrics.

Actual: exits non-zero with
`ValueError: no eval solver for prompt 'plan-review-project-portability'`
from `eval_solver.run_case`.

## Root Cause

`rebar.llm.evals.eval.calibrate_criterion` computes
`prompt_id = criterion_prompt_id("project.portability")` = `plan-review-project-portability`
(the forward map replaces `.`→`-`) to load the eval fixture (correct). But the default
`_criterion_solver.solve(prompt_id, case)` passes that DASH prompt-id to
`eval_solver.run_case`, which resolves the criterion via `_criterion_id(prompt_id)`:
it strips the `plan-review-` prefix to `project-portability` (dash) and checks
`cid in registry.by_id(repo_root)`. The registry is keyed by the LOGICAL id
`project.portability` (dot), so the dash form is never found → `_criterion_id` returns
None → `run_case` raises `no eval solver`. Built-in ids (no dot) round-trip fine; only
namespaced `project.<name>` criteria break. Confirmed:
`_criterion_id("plan-review-project-portability", root)` → None, while
`_criterion_id("project.portability", root)` → "project.portability".

## Proposed Fix (one of)

  `project-<name>` back to `project.<name>` (the namespaced project-criterion inverse),
  since `<name>` has no dots.
