baseline.description:
## Why

Both link bugs were invisible in telemetry: the batch outcome reports mutation-level `error=None` and "applied N of N" but never the per-sub-op counts, so a link/comment/label that silently no-ops (or fails non-fatally, logged only to stderr) leaves the pass green. The inbound applier already returns `links_applied`; the outbound batch path does not. Make a silent no-op fail loudly — safely.

## What

- Surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied` in the **structured outbound batch outcome** (queryable, not only logged) and the `RECON:` line — parity with the inbound applier's existing `links_applied`.
- Add a **silent-no-op canary**: when a mutation carries N sub-ops of a kind but `applied == 0`, that is a failure condition (`computed > 0 && applied == 0`), surfaced in the outcome/telemetry and asserted by a test that would have caught the link drop.
- **Rollout safety:** the fail-loud invariant lands **warn-first** — emit telemetry + a `WARNING` behind a flag/canary — and is promoted to hard-fail only after a baseline pass that emits zero such warnings. Reverting to warn is a flag flip, no other code change. This avoids hard-failing production syncs on a false positive.
- Sequencing: depends on story D (the single consolidated applier) so the counts come from one path.
- Out of scope (justified): making the threshold itself configurable — the simple `computed > 0 && applied == 0` invariant IS the contract; only enforce-vs-warn is flagged. A configurable threshold is YAGNI.

## Scope

- In: outcome/telemetry plumbing in `batch_dispatch.py` / `applier.py` / `reconcile.py`; the canary test; the warn-first flag.
- Out: the probe wiring (story F); applier consolidation (story D).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The structured outbound batch outcome and the `RECON:` line surface `links_applied`, `comments_applied`, `labels_applied`.
- [ ] A test asserts that a mutation with computed sub-ops > 0 but applied == 0 fails (reproduces what the link drop would have triggered).
- [ ] The fail-loud invariant rolls out warn-first (telemetry + `WARNING`) behind a flag; promotion to hard-fail and reversion to warn are a flag flip with no other code change.
- [ ] Sync semantics are otherwise unchanged (telemetry + guard only); the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] The canary asserts the count invariant, not specific log strings (anti-change-detector).
baseline.summary: Surface outbound sub-op telemetry + silent-no-op canary

baseline.description:
## What

Generate `docs/mcp-reference.md` from the MCP server's OWN registrars, correctly
classified by gate, and gate it in CI. Mirrors the `gen_env_registry.py` generator +
drift-gate pattern.

## Source of truth (verified — registration-time vs call-time gating)
The server (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` `build_server()`) assembles THREE registrars:
- `register_read_tools` (`_mcp_reads.py`) — 23 tools, ALWAYS registered.
- `register_llm_tools` (`_mcp_llm.py`) — 6 tools, ALWAYS registered; gated at CALL time on
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`.
- `register_write_tools` (`_mcp_writes.py`) — 18 tools, CONDITIONALLY registered: returns
  early when `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` is truthy, so they are ABSENT from `list_tools()` in
  read-only mode. Totals verified: 47 tools (readonly off) / 29 (readonly on).

**Critical:** only `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` changes list membership. `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and
`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` are call-time only (tools always listed, refuse at call). So a
naive single `list_tools()` in ambient env silently produces a PARTIAL reference. The
generator MUST enumerate each registrar with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` so writes register.

## Classification rule (deterministic — registrar default + closed 3-entry special-case table)
There is NO per-tool gate attribute, and `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` do NOT map to the
env gate. Classify by which registrar registers the tool, then apply the closed override table:
| Group (registrar) | Default gate | Special-case overrides |
|---|---|---|
| READS | none (always available) | `reconcile` -> mutating modes blocked by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` FIRST, then require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` (BOTH gate live mode; dry-run always works); `fsck` -> recover path gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` |
| LLM | `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (call-time) | `sign_review` -> `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (HYBRID: in the LLM registrar but write-gated, makes no LLM call) |
| WRITES | `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` (registration-time; absent when readonly) | `run_workflow` -> write-gated by `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` AND, for a non-dry-run workflow that HAS LLM steps, additionally gated at call time by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (a second hybrid) |

This special-case table is CLOSED at FOUR entries (`reconcile`, `fsck`, `sign_review`,
`run_workflow`); the generator carries them explicitly and a drift check asserts these four
names still exist in their expected registrars, so a new hybrid is caught rather than
silently misclassified.
`sign_manifest` is a WRITE-registrar tool (not the LLM `sign_review` — do not conflate).
Gate descriptions come from the `MCP_ENV_VARS` constant (`mcp_server.py`), the same source
`rebar-mcp --help` uses, so the doc cannot drift from `--help`.

## Scope
- Add `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` (new): enumerate each registrar onto its own FastMCP
  with `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=0` (writes register); read each tool's name + first-line summary
  (from `.description`); classify via the table above; emit `docs/mcp-reference.md` with a
  generated header and exactly THREE clearly-labeled gate-tier sections:
  **Read-only (always)**, **LLM-gated (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`)**, and
  **Write-gated (`REBAR_MCP_READONLY`)**. The three special cases are inline ANNOTATIONS,
  NOT separate sections: `reconcile` under Read-only annotated "live/mutating modes blocked by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` and require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`"; `fsck` under Read-only annotated "recover path gated by
  `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`"; `sign_review` under Write-gated (NOT LLM-gated) annotated "hybrid: in the LLM registrar,
  write-gated"; `run_workflow` under Write-gated annotated "live LLM-step workflows also
  require `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`". Include the `MCP_ENV_VARS` gate descriptions.
- `--check` drift mode + CI gate in BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND
  `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (the actual Verified gate; a parity test
  `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` enforces every `scripts/*.py` in test.yml also
  appears in gerrit-verify.yaml — omitting it breaks `make test`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` is generated (marked generated) from the live registrars and
      lists all 47 tools (23 read + 6 llm + 18 write).
- [ ] Tools are structurally separated into labeled sections by gate tier (NOT prose) — a
      Read-only section, an LLM-gated section, and a Write-gated section each exist (verify,
      prints nothing):
      `for s in 'Read-only' 'LLM-gated' 'Write-gated'; do grep -qi "$s" docs/mcp-reference.md || echo "NO SECTION $s"; done`
- [ ] The three special cases are correctly placed — DETERMINISTIC section-bounded proof
      (all three sub-checks print nothing). `sign_review` is in the Write-gated section and
      NOT in the LLM-gated section; `reconcile` is annotated jira-gated; `fsck` annotated
      readonly-recover:
      `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`
      then a held-out unit test asserts, using section-bounded slicing of
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` (awk from a tier heading to the next `## `): `sign_review` row
      is inside the Write-gated section and absent from the LLM-gated section; the `reconcile`
      row text contains BOTH `REBAR_MCP_READONLY` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`; the
      `run_workflow` row (Write-gated) text contains `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`; the `fsck` row text contains
      `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`. (The section-bounded assertion is the independent oracle — it
      does not just re-run the generator's own classifier.)
- [ ] Count proof (deterministic, prints nothing):
      `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py && [ "$(grep -cE '^\| ?`?[a-z_]+`? ' docs/mcp-reference.md)" -ge 47 ] || echo "TOO FEW TOOLS"` (or an equivalent explicit count of listed tool rows >= 47).
- [ ] Drift gate works — adding/removing a tool changes output; a stale committed file fails
      `--check` (deterministic, prints `CAUGHT`):
      `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py; printf '\nstale\n' >> docs/mcp-reference.md; python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo MISS || echo CAUGHT; python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`
- [ ] The gate is wired in BOTH CI files (prints nothing):
      `for f in .github/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml; do grep -qF 'gen_mcp_reference.py' "$f" || echo "NOT WIRED: $f"; done`
      and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q` passes.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stay green.

Files: `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` (new), `docs/mcp-reference.md` (new/generated),
`tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py` (new — the held-out section-bounded placement +
enumeration tests, including the AC3 special-case placement assertions),
`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
baseline.summary: P1: Generate the MCP tool reference (generator + drift gate)

content.text: ## Why

Rec 2 (+ Rec 1 Tier A) of session-logs/2026-06-09-architecture-review.md (risk R5). CLI reads go bash ticket-show.sh/ticket-list.sh -> python3 heredoc -> ticket_reducer while library/MCP reads go _reads.py -> ticket_reducer in-process: arg parsing, id-resolution dispatch, and error-message STRINGS are written twice (_reads.py hand-replicates subprocess stderr text so parity tests pass). Freshness also diverges: bash-path commands run _ensure_initialized (fetch/merge <=1/min) but in-process reads do not — so MCP (the primary agent surface) has the STALEST reads despite real-time propagation being a first-order requirement. BREAKING-WINDOW: output text/freshness semantics may shift; land while there are no real consumers.
## What

- Point the dispatcher read arms (show/list/ready/search/deps) at the existing Python implementations in src/rebar/_reads.py; delete the bash read shims + their heredocs (src/rebar/_engine/ticket-show.sh, ticket-list.sh, ticket-ready.sh/.py read path).

- Make freshness an explicit interface-uniform policy: add the <=1/min best-effort fetch (with an env/--no-sync opt-out) to the native read path so all three interfaces share one freshness contract; document it in docs/concurrency.md + README.
- Delete tests/interfaces/test_native_read_parity.py once the second implementation is gone (a parity test outliving its second impl is dead weight).
## Scope
Read paths only; write paths untouched. Safety: test_native_read_parity.py + schema conformance suites pin shapes before the flip.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One read implementation serves CLI, library, and MCP (bash read shims deleted)
- [ ] Read-freshness policy uniform across interfaces; opt-out documented
- [ ] Schema conformance + interface parity suites green; native-read parity test retired
- [ ] No error-message strings hand-mirrored between Python and bash

baseline.summary: Collapse the dual read path: CLI reads via _reads.py + uniform read-freshness policy

baseline.description:
## The assertion cannot pass, even when the code is correct

`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:317-319`) creates an issue directly on the DC harness, runs a `bootstrap-strict` pass, then asserts:

    tickets = rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=str(dc_rebar_repo))
    matched = [t for t in tickets if remote_key in json.dumps(t)]
    assert matched, f"no local ticket was created from DC issue {remote_key}; ..."

`remote_key` is the RAW Jira key (`RBJNAZV-1`). Two facts make the match impossible:

1. **The local id is LOWERCASED.** `_jira_key_to_local_id` (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`) returns
   `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()`, so the created ticket's id is `jira-rbjnazv-1`. The `in` test is
   case-sensitive.
2. **The ticket payload carries NO raw Jira key.** `_inbound_create_write_create_event`
   (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) builds `create_data` from id / ticket_type / title /
   description / parent_id / tags / priority / assignee / creation_channel. The Jira key appears only
   as a TITLE FALLBACK (`fields.get("summary","") or jira_key`), so it is absent whenever the issue
   has a summary — as it does here ("J7 provenance oracle"). The binding is recorded separately, in
   the binding store (`_inbound_create_record_binding`), which `list_tickets` does not return.

Verified directly against the payload shape the inbound path writes:

    remote_key : RBJNAZV-1
    local_id   : jira-rbjnazv-1
    ticket json contains raw remote key? False

## Why this matters more than a broken test

Observed in GitHub Actions run 30651750699 (job "jira DC harness smoke"), where it is the ONLY failure — 1 failed, 14 passed — on the first run in which the harness got far enough to reach it (the PAT-cap fix [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] unblocked it).

The run reported `invariants: scanned=1` and `OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations`. The pass SAW the DC issue and applied a mutation. So the observable evidence is consistent with the inbound create having worked perfectly and the ORACLE being unable to see it.

**The consequence is that epic e369's headline acceptance criterion — "an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass" — is UNPROVEN, not disproven.** This test is the only thing currently asserting it, and it cannot distinguish "the ticket was created" from "the ticket was not created". Whichever the truth is, the oracle has to be fixed before the epic can make a claim either way. Do NOT read this failure as evidence that inbound is broken, and do NOT read a future green as evidence that it works until the assertion actually targets something the inbound path writes.

This is the THIRD oracle-that-cannot-pass found in this epic, after `_envelope()` being asserted on writing-mode passes (which emit no JSON — corrected under bda8). The pattern is consistent: the live tests were authored against an assumed output shape rather than the one the code emits, and the defects stayed invisible because an earlier failure aborted the run before the assertion was reached.

## Approach

Assert against what the inbound path ACTUALLY produces, and assert the binding too, so a pass is evidence of the round-trip rather than of a string appearing somewhere in a blob:

1. derive the expected local id with `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` and match on ticket `id`
   exactly — not a substring scan of `json.dumps`, which matches incidental occurrences and (as here)
   misses the real one;
2. additionally assert the BINDING maps that local id to `remote_key`, read from the binding store —
   this is where the DC↔local correspondence actually lives, and it is the property the headline AC
   is really about;
3. keep the existing `creation_channel == "jira"` assertion, which is correct and unaffected.

**Rejected: making the substring match case-insensitive.** It would make the test pass while leaving it a blob scan that could match on an unrelated field, and it would still not assert the binding — the thing that makes the local ticket genuinely correspond to the DC issue.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — the provenance test's assertions.

## Testing

The live DC harness job is the oracle. The fix is verified when that job reports the provenance test PASSING — and, because a green here would otherwise be indistinguishable from a weakened assertion, the new assertions must be shown to FAIL against a deliberately wrong local id (a unit-level check of the id derivation is enough for that half, since `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the provenance test matches the ticket by EXACT `id` equal to `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)`,
      not by a substring scan of `json.dumps(ticket)`
- [ ] the test additionally asserts the binding store maps that local id to `remote_key`
- [ ] a unit test asserts `_jira_key_to_local_id` lowercases and prefixes, so the derivation the live
      test depends on is pinned independently of the harness
- [ ] the live `jira DC harness smoke` job reports this test PASSING, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the epic's headline AC is only claimed after that green — and the ticket records that the prior
      failure was an oracle defect, so the run is not misread as a regression fix
baseline.summary: Live provenance oracle cannot pass: asserts the raw Jira key against a lowercased local id

baseline.description:
## Why
One combined-tree CI run must satisfy Gerrit's PER-CHANGE `Verified` gate. The bot casts `Verified` on the batch members from that single run — sound because ancestor-atomic submit means the untested intermediate states never reach `main`. This is the only gate-touching change in the epic and needs an explicit security audit.

## What
After the combined-tip CI passes, the bot (Service User `autolander-bot`) casts `Verified +1` on each batch member, then ancestor-atomic submits the whole batch. **S8 owns the cast-Verified → submit step** (S7 only assembled the chain and triggered the one CI run).

## Dependencies
Depends on **S7** (`arthrodial-skipping-gypsymoth`, 0128-9a17-79db-450e) — the assembled combined chain + the single combined-tip CI run: S8 casts per-member `Verified` from *that* run and then submits, so the assembly + one-run trigger must exist first.

## Scope
Phase 2. The Verified-casting mechanic, the atomic submit, + its security audit. Depends on the batching-assembly story.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **SHA-binding (new threat vector):** at assembly the `{change_id → patchset_SHA}` map is **written durably to the autolander state dir** (a file that survives crash/restart), not held only in memory; before casting `Verified +1` on a member the bot **reads it back** and asserts that member's stored SHA is exactly the one included in the combined-tip run that passed. On crash/restart the batch is re-validated against the stored map before any vote is cast. (GerriScary/copyCondition guards *carried* votes; SHA-binding guards *directly-cast* votes — a distinct vector.) Never a copied or stale vote.
- [ ] **Atomicity mechanism:** submit the whole batch atomically via `submitWholeTopic=true` (already deployed) — the bot sets a shared topic across all members of the single linear relation chain before submit; ancestor-atomic submit means intermediate states never reach `main`. (Parallel-sibling topologies are excluded from a batch; ADR-0040.)
- [ ] **Run-outcome confirmation:** the bot learns the combined-tip run outcome from the `Verified` vote the gerrit-to-platform bridge casts on the tip change (the existing per-patchset path) AND asserts the observed GHA `run_id` matches the one S7 dispatched for this batch (from the handoff record) — so it never fans out votes off a stale or mismatched run.
- [ ] **Fan-out protocol + mid-run failure:** only after the confirmed combined-tip run passes, **loop `ssh gerrit review --verified +1 <change>,<patchset>` over the members in chain order**, each targeting the post-assembly patchset; on **any** per-member vote failure, **abort — cast no submit** — and hand the batch back via S9. If the run itself fails, cast none and hand the batch to the re-batch path (S9).
- [ ] `Verified`-casting is restricted to the bot Service User ACL; documented that per-change `Verified` now means "tested as part of its landed batch," not "tested in isolation."
- [ ] **Security-invariants artifact:** the ADR-0042 (created by S6 `broken-checkered-tiger`) Security invariants section records the SHA-binding invariant (cast-Verified bound to the tested combined-tip SHA) and its concrete check — a test asserting the SHA-binding logic rejects a member whose SHA is not in the passed run — alongside the soundness argument (atomic submit ⇒ intermediate states never reach `main`), the no-copied-vote path, and the bot-only ACL; the two-vote gate is not weakened.
- [ ] The `submitWholeTopic` / runbook / CONTRIBUTING.md doc-drift from this semantic shift is handed to **S6's** docs sweep.
baseline.summary: S8 Bot-casts-Verified from combined run + security-invariant audit (Phase 2)

baseline.description: Deferred hardening (accepted limitation, ADR 0046). The commit-ancestry key-validity model (attest/authorship.py verify_authorship_at_commit) defeats the direct revoked-key-reuse case (a new event descends the revocation commit, so a revoked key's revoke-commit is an ancestor and the key is excluded). Its integrity rests on the tickets-branch commit graph being append-only, which today is a CONTROL (Gerrit-authenticated, controlled-environment write access), not a cryptographic guarantee. gittuf shipped the same log-position model and still needed a monotonic policy counter (CVE-2026-44544); TUF hard-codes N+1 root versioning. Future hardening: (a) a regression test asserting a revoked-then-re-introduced key at a LATER ancestry position FAILS; (b) documented threat analysis of tickets-branch force-push/rewrite and the controls that bound it; (c) evaluate an explicit monotonic anti-rollback guard as defense-in-depth. Not scheduled.
baseline.summary: Cryptographic anti-rollback for commit-ancestry key validity (monotonic guard + regression test + tickets-branch-rewrite analysis)

content.text: ## Why
Two repo-hygiene items from the 2026-07-08 audit OSS finding #6 cleanup bucket:

Decision: remove the tracked reports and ignore the directory **locally only** (`.git/info/exclude`, NOT the shared `.gitignore`), so the tooling keeps working on this machine without advertising the path in the public tree.

2. `.tokensave/` (code-graph MCP cache) is untracked but unignored — it pollutes `git status` on any machine running the tokensave server. Add it to the shared `.gitignore` alongside `.serena/` (both per-developer tool caches, so a shared ignore is correct here).

The marker is already correct (0.7.1) and can never go stale again. Removing the literal would BREAK that guard (the test hard-fails if the marker is absent). So there is nothing to do here; item 3 is dropped.

## AWS review-bot signing identity (Rebar Bot) via SSM

Configure the AWS **review-bot** container to attribute its ticket writes as the Rebar Bot
identity, materializing the signing key from SSM.

**Scope correction (ADR-0047):** the auto-lander was RETIRED and DELETED (`infra/autolander/`,
`Dockerfile.autolander`, `loop.py` are gone as of the ADR-0047 migration). So this task no
longer covers the auto-lander — only the review-bot remains as an AWS ticket-event writer. The
review-bot writes only EXEMPT types (`code_review` artifacts, `review_bot/voter.py`), so
signing here is for CLEAN ATTRIBUTION (the merge-gate does not require signatures on exempt
types), not a hard must-sign; still worth doing so AWS-authored events attribute to the bot.

- The SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` already exists (task bffe
  provisioned it + added it to `rebar_secret_params` in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`).
- Materialize it to a `0600` FILE at boot — a multi-line OpenSSH PEM key CANNOT go in the
  container `.env` (`fetch-secrets.sh` writes only single-line `KEY=VALUE`). Follow the
  `ci-gerrit-ssh-key` / `g2p-github-pat` materialize-to-file precedent (a dedicated boot step
  or `fetch-secrets.sh` extension writing to e.g. `/run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key`, 0600),
  NOT a `.env` line.
- Configure `identity.signing_key` = that file path and the bot git email
  (`joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`) in the reviewbot container (`infra/compose`,
  `infra/Dockerfile.reviewbot`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The reviewbot boot path materializes `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` to a `0600` standalone file (materialize-to-file precedent, NOT the `.env`); the secret is never baked into the image or committed.
- [ ] The reviewbot container sets `identity.signing_key` (or `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) to that path and its git `user.email` to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`, so its writes attribute to the Rebar Bot identity (`594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`).
- [ ] No auto-lander artifacts are referenced (they were deleted by ADR-0047); scope is the review-bot only.

content.text: # S4 — CI service account + credentials (SSM-backed)
Part of epic 1fa8 (CI as a second Gerrit gate vote via gerrit-to-platform → GitHub Actions).
## Why
The CI vote-back SSHes into Gerrit as a service account (the g2p production pattern); g2p (running
in the Gerrit container) also needs a GitHub PAT to `workflow_dispatch`. Both credentials must
follow the infra's no-plaintext invariant: SSM SecureString + materialize-at-boot (as with the bot
token, deploy key, OAuth secret).
## What
Provision the CI Gerrit service account (with the `Verified` ACL), and wire the PAT + SSH key
through SSM and the boot-time fetch, plus the GitHub-side vars/secret. Record the inbound
GitHub→Gerrit SSH trust path as an ADR.
## Scope
- `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (provision the account, as a template), `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`
(new SecureString slots), `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (host-side materialization).
- GitHub repo vars/secret; new ADR for the inbound SSH trust path. Pairs with S3.
- Out of scope: the workflow (S5), the gate (S1).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Provision the CI Gerrit service account via `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` (account + group +
the `Verified -1..+1` ACL from S1).
- [ ] Add the g2p PAT — **fine-grained, single-repo (`navapbc/rebar`)**, Actions read/write +
Contents/Metadata read (NOT a classic org-wide PAT) — and the service-account SSH key to
`infra/terraform/ssm.tf` (`rebar_secret_params`, `ignore_changes=value`); add the PAT leaf to
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (it already writes the container `.env` that g2p-in-container
reads — no host-side materialization needed).
- [ ] Set GitHub repo vars `GERRIT_SERVER` / `GERRIT_SSH_USER` / `GERRIT_KNOWN_HOSTS` /
`GERRIT_URL` and secret `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY`.
- [ ] Define a rotation + retire path for both the PAT and `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY` (compromise
response + PoC decommission).
- [ ] Write an ADR recording the inbound GitHub→Gerrit SSH vote path (blast radius, key scope).

baseline.summary: S4 — CI service account + credentials (SSM-backed)

## Why
Only PASSing completion verdicts leave a durable artifact (the signed attestation). FAIL verdicts vanish — .rebar/run_snapshots/ is empty and the 2026-07-12 calibration audit could only reconstruct FAILs from agents' voluntary session-log narration. The next completion-verifier calibration needs the actual verdicts: failing criterion, findings[], remediation text, timestamps.

## What
- On a completion-verifier FAIL in the close path (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py, verdict produced via src/rebar/llm/completion.py reconcile_verdict), persist the full verdict durably — mirror the plan-review REVIEW_RESULT sidecar pattern (an event/sidecar in the ticket store keyed to the ticket, not a git-ignored local file), so FAILs are queryable offline like plan-review runs are.
- Include a `schema` version string `"completion_verifier_fail_v1"` (mirroring the existing sidecars' `plan_review_result_v1` / `code_review_result_v1`, whose readers guard on `payload.get("schema")` — see plan_review/sidecar.py:157) so the new record type is identifiable and version-guarded, plus: verdict, findings[] (criterion, finding/detail, remediation), certifiable, model/runner, timestamp, and the ticket's material fingerprint at verify time.
- Keep the close path's behavior unchanged (persist-and-block; a persistence failure must not mask the FAIL). Implement the persist call inside a best-effort try/except in `_completion_precheck` (transition_close.py) BEFORE the FAIL is raised, mirroring plan_review/sidecar.emit's best-effort contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A FAILed close attempt leaves a durable, queryable record (a reducer-ignored sidecar event in the ticket store, mirroring REVIEW_RESULT) carrying `schema="completion_verifier_fail_v1"`, the failing criteria, and per-finding remediation text.
- [ ] A test drives a mocked FAIL through the close path (monkeypatch rebar.llm.verify_completion → FAIL stub, mirror tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py) and asserts the record exists with the expected fields (schema + criteria + remediation).
- [ ] A test exercises the PERSISTENCE-FAILURE branch: the sidecar write is mocked to raise, and the close path still blocks with the FAIL verdict unchanged (fail-closed preserved, persistence error swallowed) — asserting the exception does not mask or alter the FAIL.
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make typecheck passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.

content.text: ## Why
Fail-open is the IRONCLAD invariant of this epic — a false "absent"/false finding is the cardinal sin, and a
non-adopting client must pay nothing. That guarantee has to be verified uniformly across every backend on a
real polyglot corpus, not assumed per-component.
## What
- A **fail-open conformance suite**: for every backend (universal-ctags, deps/registries, OpenGrep/ast-grep,
scc/lizard) assert that unsupported-lang / missing-tool / parse-error / crash / timeout / version-skew /
invalid-detector each yields `abstain(reason)` + a coverage entry — never a raise, never a false `absent`/
false finding. Includes the IN-PROCESS cases (a hung/segfaulting tree-sitter parse under the worker boundary)
and the loader quarantining a schema-invalid project detector.
- A **refutation-yield + false-refute eval on an INDEPENDENT real corpus** (real repos with real references —
NOT a self-planted fixture; spike E3 = 88% yield / 0 false-refute on rebar's own source): measure the fraction
of real cross-file names the T1 floor resolves (`refuted`) and confirm ZERO false-refute — value MEASURED, not
asserted (a self-authored fixture would be self-fulfilling).
- A **polyglot fixture corpus** spanning several languages + ecosystems (unsupported-language, project-supplied-
language-extension, monorepo/workspace, import-vs-distribution-name) AND — critically — the false-refute HAZARD
class the design scopes out: a **common-name COLLISION** (a name with >1 definition) and a **MEMBER/dotted
reference** (`recv.attr`), each asserting the resolver **ABSTAINS** (spike E2: the guard restores 0 false-refute)
— exercising all three jobs.
- A **deps-lane eval** against the real registry oracle (seeded by spike2_deps.py): real→refute, hallucinated/
stdlib/slop→abstain, never a false-absent.
- A **non-adoption test**: with the optional extra absent, core imports cleanly and any oracle query fails open
to abstain/no-op with zero footprint.
## Scope
- `tests/grounding/`; depends on S2, S3, S4 (can develop alongside S5). Reuse the contract/harness from S1.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Conformance matrix: each backend × each failure mode (unsupported-lang / missing-tool / parse-error / crash / timeout / version-skew / invalid-detector, incl. in-process hang/segfault) → `abstain(reason)` + coverage; zero raises, zero false-refute.
- [ ] Refutation-yield + false-refute eval on an INDEPENDENT real corpus (real repos, NOT self-planted; spike E3 = 88% / 0-FP on rebar's own source): yield measured, false-refute = 0.

- [ ] Corpus covers the false-refute HAZARD class — common-name collision (>1 def) + member/dotted ref — each asserting ABSTAIN (spike E2 guard); plus a deps-lane eval (real→refute, hallucinated/stdlib/slop→abstain, no false-absent); plus unsupported-lang, lang-extension, monorepo/workspace, import-vs-dist.
- [ ] Non-adoption test: extra absent → core import-clean, queries fail open to abstain/no-op, zero footprint.
- [ ] Coverage reconstructable from recorded skips across a mixed-language run.

baseline.summary: Fail-open conformance suite + polyglot fixture corpus + non-adoption test

content.text: ## Why
The dependency half of job 1: refute "package X doesn't exist / is hallucinated" (slopsquatting is a real,
high-base-rate class). The load-bearing risk is FALSE positives — an internal/workspace package or an
import-vs-distribution-name mismatch must NEVER be called absent. So this lane is confirm-only with a strict
abstain gauntlet.
## What
- **Manifest + lockfile parsing** across purl ecosystems (npm/PyPI/crates/Go/Maven/RubyGems/NuGet) to enumerate
declared deps; **registry existence** probes (deps.dev as a direct oracle where available; per-registry
fallback) to disprove a hallucination claim.
- The **abstain gauntlet** (only emit `refuted`/`abstain`, never `absent`): per-ecosystem name normalization
(PEP 503, crates `-`≡`_`, Go `!`-escaping, npm scopes); workspace/monorepo membership (Cargo/pnpm/Go
`replace`/Maven reactor); stdlib/builtin; import-name-vs-distribution-name (`bs4`→`beautifulsoup4`); any
transient 429/5xx/timeout → `abstain`. Unknown ecosystem → `abstain`, never `absent`.
- **Validated against the real oracle (spike E4):** deps.dev resolved 5 real/normalized packages → `refute`
(incl. PEP-503 `scikit_learn`→`scikit-learn`) and abstained on hallucinated/slop/stdlib (`os`→`abstain(stdlib)`;
404→`abstain(not_on_public_registry)`, never `absent`) — the gauntlet structurally cannot emit a false-absent.
Repro: docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/spike2_deps.py.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/deps.py`; reuse `syft`/manifest parsers + registry HTTP (descriptive UA, throttle,
prefer index endpoints). Build on S1's contract + harness. Existence only — no vuln/CVE scanning here.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Manifest/lockfile enumeration across the purl ecosystems; registry existence via deps.dev + per-registry fallback.
- [ ] Abstain gauntlet enforced: normalization + workspace + stdlib + import/dist-name + transient-error → abstain, never absent.
- [ ] Unknown/unsupported ecosystem → abstain(reason); coverage recorded.
- [ ] Fail-open tested: offline / rate-limited / unknown-ecosystem / internal package → abstain, never a false "absent".
- [ ] Deps-lane eval against the real oracle (seeded by spike2_deps.py): real→refute, hallucinated/stdlib/slop→abstain, PEP503 normalization, zero false-absent.

# An on-demand CI job that MAPS the Jira DC image, so we can declare its contract instead of discovering it

## Why this is the right instrument

The DC image is **amd64-only and exists only inside CI** — the development host is arm64, which is why the previous AC verification pass recorded "no live cell was run during verification". Every question about that image is therefore currently answered the same way: ship a change, wait ~35 minutes, read the failure. Today that loop was spent three times on ONE question (does the project have an `Epic` type?), and the answer arrived as a SETUP FAILED at minute 35.

An on-demand GitHub Actions job that boots the pinned image and interrogates it collapses that loop to a single run, and its OUTPUT is the environment contract that [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e] needs written down.

## The load-bearing constraint: this is an AUTHORING tool, not a test-path component

**The deliverable is committed DATA, not a running agent.** If the agent ever executes on the normal harness path, we have reintroduced exactly the runtime discovery the operator just ruled against — with more non-determinism and an LLM in the loop. It must be:

 * **manually dispatched** (`workflow_dispatch`), never on push/PR/schedule;
 * **producing a committed artifact** — the declared capability contract plus the raw request/response
   evidence behind it — which a human reviews and lands;
 * **run again only when the image is re-pinned**, as the way we re-derive the contract for a new
   digest.

Its relationship to the harness is the same as a spike's to a story: it answers questions once so the answers can be written down.

## What it should answer — a CHECKLIST, not open-ended exploration

An unscoped "go explore" agent returns prose. This should answer specific questions and emit structured results:

**Inventory (what is there by default)**
 * exact image digest, Jira version, and licensed applications (Software present? — that determines
   whether `Epic` exists at all)
 * project templates the instance actually offers (`/rest/project-templates/latest/templates`)
 * for a project created from EACH candidate template: the issue types it yields
 * the full field inventory (`/rest/api/2/field`) — specifically the ids of `Epic Link` and
   `Epic Name`, which differ per instance
 * default screen configuration: is `Epic Link` on a standard issue's EDIT screen? is `Epic Name` on
   the Epic CREATE screen?

**Experiments (validate the configuration hooks BEFORE we depend on them)**
 * can the admin PAT create an issue type via `POST /rest/api/2/issuetype` and add it to a project's
   scheme? — the deterministic alternative to template roulette
 * can it add a field to a screen? Confirm by reading `editmeta` back
 * **the two falsifiers recorded on [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94]**: what operations does `parent`
   expose in a sub-task's `editmeta`, and does `{"update":{"parent":[{"set":null}]}}` behave
   differently from `{"fields":{"parent":null}}`? A difference overturns that ticket's
   NOT-RESOLVABLE verdict
 * **[rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] AC1**: does a sub-task `PUT fields.parent` return 2xx-and-ignore, or
   4xx? Raw REST, no rebar in the path
 * once an Epic exists: does writing `Epic Link` on a child actually take effect — the question
   change 1311 has now failed to reach three times

**Every answer must carry its raw request and response.** The contract must be traceable to evidence, not to an agent's summary — otherwise we have swapped "discovering from the instance" for "trusting a model", which is worse.

## Caveats worth designing against

 * **Pin by digest in this job too**, or the map describes an image we do not run.
 * **Boot time is minutes**; batch every question into one run rather than iterating.
 * The job holds an admin PAT on a throwaway instance — acceptable, but it must touch nothing
   outside it, and must not be reachable from a fork PR.
 * The agent must be told to REPORT rather than FIX. A mapping job that starts mutating the harness
   is how a spike turns into an unreviewed change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow boots the digest-pinned DC image and runs the checklist
      above, emitting a structured artifact (raw request/response per question)
- [ ] the artifact answers, unambiguously: which template yields `Epic`; the `Epic Link` /
      `Epic Name` field ids; whether those fields are on the needed screens by default; and whether
      creating an issue type + editing a screen via REST works with the harness's credentials
- [ ] the 37e7 and 1a9f falsifiers are executed and their raw responses recorded on those tickets
- [ ] the resulting environment contract is COMMITTED as data and consumed by the harness's setup
      assertion — it does NOT re-derive anything at test time
- [ ] the workflow cannot run on push, PR, or schedule, and this is asserted, not merely configured
- [ ] a short doc states when to re-run it (image re-pin) and that its output is authored, not live
baseline.summary: On-demand CI job that maps the Jira DC image, so its contract can be declared not discovered

# Advisory plan-review nudge: flag a leaf whose criteria count strains a single completion-verification run

## Context / Problem

Ticket `d59e-e042-2b94-4b70` fixes the load-bearing problem: the completion verifier's budgets were flat constants that did not scale, so a large ticket could not be verified at all. That fix is the real solution and this ticket must never become a prerequisite for it.

This is the **belt-and-suspenders** complement: reduce how often a ticket reaches the size where verification is strained in the first place, by coaching the author at plan time. Measured motivation from d59e: ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56` carries **14 acceptance criteria**, and the primary verifier had a FLAT 480-iteration budget for all of them (~34 tool calls per criterion), exhausting after ~780s. A verifier must produce one verdict record per criterion (`completion_recovery._validate_coverage`), so verification effort is linear in criteria count — a fact no plan-review criterion currently surfaces to the author.

## Approach

Add a new **advisory, never-blocking** criterion in the decomposition-shape family, modelled directly on the existing `decomp-shape` criterion (`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md:599`), which is already documented "Advisory — never blocks". It fires on a **leaf** ticket whose acceptance criteria count exceeds a configured threshold, and coaches the author to split the work into independently verifiable children rather than one ticket the verifier must cover in a single pass.

Make the check **deterministic** (a count of `- [ ]` entries in the `## Acceptance Criteria` block), so it runs in the existing deterministic floor with no LLM cost and no added latency — consistent with how the other cheap structural checks run.

**Explicitly non-load-bearing.** The criterion is advisory: it never blocks a claim, and d59e's budget scaling remains the mechanism that guarantees any ticket can be verified. If this criterion were ever promoted to blocking it would reintroduce exactly the failure mode d59e removes — an author unable to proceed because a ticket is large — so its advisory status is itself an acceptance criterion below.

**Threshold.** Default to firing above **12** criteria on a leaf, with the value config-overridable alongside the other plan-review tunables rather than hardcoded. 12 sits above the repo's typical leaf and below 9fd4's 14, so it would have coached the ticket that motivated this without firing on ordinary work. Assume this default unless measurement later says otherwise.

**Alternative rejected — make it blocking.** That would trade a verifier availability defect for a plan-time roadblock, and would stop an author writing a genuinely large-but-atomic ticket. The whole point of d59e is that size must not prevent progress.

**Alternative rejected — score description length instead of criteria count.** Length is a weak proxy: the verifier's work is driven by the number of verdict records it must produce, not by prose size, and a long Context section costs the verifier almost nothing. Criteria count is the signal that actually tracks verification effort.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — the deterministic count check and its threshold
  constant.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — register the criterion and route it to the
  leaf/decomposition scope, advisory tier.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — the generated per-criterion section.
- `tests/unit/` — a new test module for the criterion's fire/silence behaviour.

## Testing

Deterministic unit tests only — the check makes no LLM call, so no live tier is needed.

- fires on a leaf with more criteria than the threshold, and the finding names the count;
- stays SILENT at exactly the threshold (boundary), on a container (which delegates to children),
  and on the exempt ticket types;
- the finding is emitted in the advisory bucket, and a test asserts a plan carrying it still
  yields a PASS verdict that signs an attestation — the anti-regression guard against it ever
  becoming a roadblock;
- the threshold is read from config rather than a literal, asserted by overriding it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a new advisory criterion fires on a LEAF ticket whose `## Acceptance Criteria` block contains
      more than the configured threshold of `- [ ]` entries, and its finding text states the actual
      count and suggests splitting into independently verifiable children
- [ ] the criterion NEVER blocks: a test asserts a plan that triggers it still returns a PASS
      verdict and still signs a claim attestation
- [ ] the criterion is silent at exactly the threshold, on containers, and on the ticket types the
      criteria registry already exempts — one test per case
- [ ] the check is deterministic (no LLM call): a test asserts it produces its finding with the LLM
      runner unavailable
- [ ] the threshold is configuration-driven, not a hardcoded literal at the call site, asserted by
      a test that overrides it and observes the fire/silence boundary move
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` documents the criterion, including that it is advisory
      and never blocks, and states its relationship to `d59e` (this is a nudge, not the guarantee)
- [ ] running the new criterion against ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56` (14 criteria) produces the
      advisory finding, and against a 3-criterion leaf produces nothing — recorded as a comment
baseline.summary: Advisory plan-review nudge: flag a leaf whose criteria count strains one completion-verification run

content.text: # T4 — Import idempotency (skip by source_id) + deferred-push perf + large-import docs
## Context
P1.2 epic rule-swamp-pupil (ab74-b205-72af-4ce1). Hardens the T3 importer: re-runs /
resume-after-crash must never duplicate, and bulk import must not pay a network round-trip
per event. Depends on T3.
## What
- `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` — at import start, one streaming scan of the TARGET store
builds `{source_id → local_id}`; a line whose `source_id` is already present is SKIPPED
(never updated — updating existing tickets is sync = reconciler, out of scope).
- Deferred push: import runs with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` for its duration, then a single
explicit `push.push_tickets_branch(...)` at the end (eliminates per-event pushes).
Restore prior env state afterward.
- Docs: document the accepted KNOWN LIMITATION (one git commit + one lock cycle per event;
no batch-commit primitive — deferred to follow-up 39c5-d81a-aad6-4e21) and the guidance to
pre-compact the source + set `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` for large imports
(`docs/architecture.md` or `docs/concurrency.md`, plus `_cli/help/import.txt`).
## Scope
In: idempotency, deferred-push, docs. Out: a batch-commit primitive (separate follow-up).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Re-running an import (or resuming a killed one) produces ZERO duplicates (skip by
source_id via a streaming target scan).
- [ ] Existing tickets are never updated by import (skip-only on collision).
- [ ] Import defers push (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`) and pushes once at the end; prior env
restored.
- [ ] Large-import limitation + pre-compact/REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off guidance documented.
- [ ] Tests: idempotent re-run (0 dups), resume-after-partial, deferred-push behavior;
`pytest` green.

baseline.summary: T4 — Import idempotency + deferred-push perf + docs

## Context / Problem
Pass-1 submits every chunk and AGENT future at once into a 6-wide pool (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:438,462-464); with a cold cache the first ~6 concurrent calls each pay a full cache-WRITE for the byte-identical plan-bearing system prefix — measured shape ~7.9N effective plan-tokens versus an ideal 2.15N (~3.7x). The warm-then-fan-out pattern already exists, proven, for container bins (pass1.py:184-232, gated on CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS=4096 and >=2 pairings, with graceful degradation on a failed warm).

## Approach
Port the container warm gate to the main pool: when the estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and (chunks + agent criteria) >= 2, run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially (writing the cache prefix), then submit the remainder to the pool; a non-systemic warm failure degrades to direct fan-out exactly as the container path does (pass1.py:203-212). Verification uses the per-call cache metrics landed by the usage-instrumentation story. Alternative rejected: serializing the whole pool — forfeits 6-way parallelism to save only the redundant writes the single warm call already eliminates.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, tests/llm/test_pass1_warmup.py.

## Testing
Unit with a recording FakeRunner: with the gate met, exactly one call completes before any pool submission and the rest fan out; below the token gate or with a single call, behavior is unchanged; a warm-call exception falls back to direct fan-out and the review completes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With >= 2 Pass-1 calls and a large plan, the first call completes before the pool starts (checked: unit test asserting call-ordering via a recording runner).
- [ ] Small plans and single-call reviews bypass the warm-up (checked: unit test).
- [ ] A failing warm call degrades to today's direct fan-out and the review still completes (checked: unit test).
- [ ] In a stubbed-usage run, the shared prefix incurs one cache write and N-1 cache reads (checked: unit test over the per-call usage records from the instrumentation seam).
baseline.summary: Warm-then-fan-out for the Pass-1 chunk and agent pool

# v1.0 release-readiness hardening

Close the five validated readiness findings for `navapbc/rebar` before the v1.0
release, using well-established patterns from actively-maintained OSS projects
(uv, pydantic, pip for release integrity; git repository-format-version for the
store compatibility gate; nginx/OpenSSH for removed-input tombstones). Every
finding was independently verified against current `main` (see per-story
provenance); all five are valid.

## Context

rebar dogfoods a Gerrit-gated `main` (two independent votes: `LLM-Review` +
`Verified`) with GitHub as a read-only mirror, yet the **release and
store-compatibility surfaces sit outside that trust boundary**. The five findings
are independent but share one theme: a control that exists at the code-review
boundary is missing at the release / storage / configuration boundary.

- **Finding 1** — `release.yml` publishes on any human-pushed `v*` tag with no
  machine proof the tagged SHA is the reviewed-and-landed `main`; tags were
  deliberately left unprotected (`infra/terraform-github/main.tf:23-28`).
- **Finding 2** — there is no committed store-format-version / required-capability
  record, so a future release cannot make an already-installed v1.0 binary
  fail-closed on a store it cannot correctly interpret. This gate **must ship in
  v1.0 itself** — a v1.0 binary cannot retroactively learn to inspect a record
  whose semantics did not exist in v1.0. This is the most time-critical story.
  **Legacy-store (absent-record) policy is load-bearing:** every store created by
  a pre-v1.0 build has no record, so the gate must treat *absent* as the implicit
  legacy format (version 0, compatible / fail-**open**) and let the idempotent
  ensure-registry write the record on the next covered write — fail-**closed** only
  when the record is *present but incompatible*. Absent-means-blocked would break
  upgrade-in-place for every existing user; absent-means-silently-bypassed would
  defeat the gate. The expand-contract path and a safe rollback story are part of
  the child (see Finding 2's story).
- **Finding 3** — `python -m build`'s default wheel-from-sdist path bakes
  `COMMIT = None` into the published wheel, and CI installs the source tree
  (`pip install .`) rather than the artifact bundle, so the defect is uncaught
  until after PyPI immutability sets in.
- **Finding 4** — the release pipeline resolves actions, build tools, and a
  privileged OIDC-context binary from mutable references; the repo already
  SHA-pins actions in `gerrit-verify.yaml`, so `release.yml` is inconsistent with
  its own stricter convention.
- **Finding 5** — removed env vars are silently ignored and removed TOML keys get
  only a generic "typo?" warning, including surfaces that redirect the store
  (`TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR`), toggle write gates (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`),
  and change close policy (`verify.require_verdict_for_close`).

**Sequencing (encoded as dependency links).** Finding 2 first (must land in v1.0 to
be effective at all). Findings 1, 3, 4 all edit `release.yml`; they are serialised
by `depends_on` links in the order 4 → 3 → 1 (pin the toolchain, then restructure
build-once, then add the source-authorization gate) — so the Gerrit queue cannot
process them out of order — and file-impact is recorded so `next-batch` also
serialises them. Finding 5 is independent and can proceed in parallel; Finding 2 is
independent (highest priority). `docs/releasing.md` is edited by all three release
stories, so section ownership is assigned per-story (pinning → Finding 4;
build-once → Finding 3; authorization → Finding 1) to avoid overlap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All five child stories are closed.
- [ ] Each child story's change has landed on `main` through the Gerrit
  two-vote gate (`LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`).
- [ ] The store-compatibility gate (Finding 2) is present in the tree that ships
  as v1.0 (verified by the reader existing and being wired into the write paths),
  since it cannot be added retroactively.
- [ ] The Finding 2 story defines and documents the absent-record (pre-v1.0 store)
  policy — absent = legacy/compatible, record auto-written by the ensure-registry on
  next covered write, fail-closed only when present-but-incompatible — and a
  rollback-safe outcome for a pre-v1.0 binary encountering the record.
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` and `docs/migrations.md` are updated to describe the new
  release-authorization gate, the build-once artifact flow, and the store
  compatibility record (including the absent-record upgrade/rollback path).
- [ ] Each child story's plan-review advisory findings are recorded with an explicit
  Accept/Reject disposition and a one-line rationale (as a comment on the child
  ticket), and every Accepted finding is reflected in the child's description before
  that child's change receives its Gerrit `LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1` votes.
- [ ] Releases are initiated from the protected `main` branch via `workflow_dispatch`
- [ ] A v1.0 binary reads a committed store compatibility record and fails closed
- [ ] The exact wheel and sdist are installed and exercised before publication, the
- [ ] Every executable the release depends on is identified by an immutable reference
- [ ] Removed inputs that affect store location, write/sync gates, auth, security, or
baseline.summary: v1.0 release-readiness hardening

content.text: ## Context / Why
All code landing on `main` goes through Gerrit's two-vote gate (LLM-Review + Verified).
We want every such commit associated with a rebar ticket, enforced as part of the
**Verified (CI)** leg — the only enforcement point that both blocks submit AND can resolve
an ID against the live store. A `rebar-ticket:` commit trailer is introduced by this work as
the convention (no code parses one yet, so the first submitted commits must carry it). CI does
not apply to specialized branches (the `tickets` branch never goes through Gerrit), so this
gates only code changes to `main`. The mechanism is intended to be reusable, so it is documented as a
first-class rebar convention.
## What
Add a `rebar verify-commit-ticket` check that extracts a ticket reference from a commit
message and resolves it against the authoritative store via the standard config store logic
(`config.tracker_dir()` / `config.tickets_branch()`), then wire it as a fail-fast job in
`gerrit-verify.yaml` so a missing/unresolvable ticket drives Verified-1. Accept alias, full
ID, short ID, and Jira key (project prefix) — all handled by the existing `resolve_ticket_id`.
## Decisions
- **Location:** canonical is the `rebar-ticket: <id>` trailer; a leading `<id>:` subject token
is also accepted. First-element-ONLY enforcement is NOT adopted: no performance gain (a
single store lookup regardless of position) and no fragility gain (both are fixed-position
parses), while it would constrain every subject and eat the 50-char budget.
- **Single source of truth:** the expected-format wording lives in ONE Python constant
(`EXPECTED_FORMAT`). The CLI error and `--help` print it; the golden help capture and a
doc-drift test pin `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` to it, so they cannot diverge.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py`:
- `EXPECTED_FORMAT: str` — the shared expected-format/accepted-forms/example/fix text.
- `extract_ticket_refs(message) -> list[str]` — pull candidates from the `rebar-ticket:`
trailer (case-insensitive; value tokens split on whitespace and stripped of `()`,`,`)
and from a leading `<id>:` subject token. **SECURITY:** drop any candidate that is not a
single safe token — reject anything with `/`, `\`, `..`, whitespace, or control chars
(require `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`) BEFORE any store lookup, so a crafted
`rebar-ticket: ../../etc/passwd` can never reach the resolver's `os.path.isdir(tracker/
<cand>)` fast path. Shape-matching (full/short/alias/Jira/prefix) stays in
`resolve_ticket_id`; do NOT duplicate its `_FULL_ID_RE`/`_SHORT_ID_RE`/`_JIRA_KEY_RE`
(avoids drift — a plausible-but-wrong inline shape would silently diverge).
- `verify_commit_message(message, *, root=None) -> (ok: bool, tried: list[str], detail)` —
resolve each safe candidate via `resolve_ticket_id` against `config.tracker_dir(root)`;
ok if ANY resolves.
- [ ] CLI `rebar verify-commit-ticket` (intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, mirroring
the `review-plan` intercept). Input is ONE of `--rev <ref>` (reads via

`git show -s --format=%B`), `--message-file

`, or `--message ` (mutually exclusive;
default `--rev HEAD`). Behavior:
- `verify.require_ticket_for_commit` false → exit 0 (no-op / staged rollout).
- Merge commit (>1 parent, when `--rev` given) → exit 0 (exempt).
- A safe candidate resolves → exit 0.
- Else exit 1, printing `EXPECTED_FORMAT`: the `rebar-ticket: <id>` trailer format, the
leading `<id>:` alternative, the accepted ID forms (alias/full/short/Jira `<PREFIX>-<n>`),
a worked example, the candidate(s) tried (or `(none present)`) with "none resolved", and
the fix (add the trailer, `git commit --amend`, re-push).
- I/O robustness: a bad `--rev` / missing `--message-file` / unreadable-or-absent store
exits non-zero with a DISTINGUISHABLE error naming the cause (git failure, missing file,
store not found) — never conflated with the missing-ticket diagnostic (so CI infra errors
are told apart from a genuine ticket-less commit).
- [ ] Registration = PURE INTERCEPT (matching `review-plan` / `verify-completion`): the arm in
`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` `main()` fires before `_dispatch` and owns its OWN argparse
`--help` (which prints usage + `EXPECTED_FORMAT`). Intercepts carry NO `help/<sub>.txt`, NO
`overview.txt` line, NO `tests/golden/cli_help/` files, and are NOT in the coverage test's
`individual` set — they are invisible to the pinned-help parity contract
(`test_routable_set_matches_pinned_help_set`), so none of those touchpoints apply.
(Verified: review-plan/verify-completion/workflow follow exactly this pattern.)
- [ ] Config: `verify.require_ticket_for_commit: bool = False` in `VerifyConfig` +
`_SECTIONS['verify']` in `src/rebar/config.py` (env
`REBAR_VERIFY_REQUIRE_TICKET_FOR_COMMIT` via the generic env layer); enabled for THIS
project in `rebar.toml`.
- [ ] Store resolution uses the standard config helpers `config.tracker_dir()` /
`config.tickets_branch()` and is overridable via `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` (relocates the store,
highest precedence) / `tracker.dir` / `tracker.branch` — no bespoke store path. (Local
resolution reads the mounted store files; the CI job separately mounts that store — see
below.)
- [ ] CI: `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` gains a `require-ticket` job (needs
`clear-vote`; `build-and-test` + `vote` gain it in `needs` so a failure fails the run →
Verified-1, fail-fast before the matrix). Runners are GitHub-hosted + ephemeral (fresh
workspace per run); fetch+worktree is used (over per-file `git show tickets:path`) because
the standard resolver needs a real tracker dir to read. Steps:
- checkout the Gerrit change (`checkout-gerrit-change-action`) + `pip install -e .`;
- mount the authoritative tickets store from GitHub, **idempotently and with retry**:
`git worktree prune` + `rm -rf .tickets-tracker` first; then up to 3 attempts of
`timeout 60 git fetch --depth=1 https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}
'+tickets:refs/remotes/gh-tickets'` (short sleep-backoff between attempts); then
`git worktree add --detach .tickets-tracker gh-tickets`. On persistent fetch failure,
print a DISTINGUISHABLE infra-error (not a missing-ticket error) advising `recheck`, and
fail closed (two-vote fail-closed model);
- `export REBAR_TRACKER_DIR="$PWD/.tickets-tracker"` (pin the store explicitly rather than
rely on the default name) and run `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` (the CLI reads
the message itself from git; no untrusted commit text is interpolated onto a command line).
- [ ] Tests `tests/unit/test_verify_commit_ticket.py`:
- extraction: trailer with parenthetical, leading `<id>:`, multiple, none, AND a
path-traversal candidate is dropped (security);
- resolution against a fixture store for full / short / alias / prefix, and a Jira key via
a `.bridge_state/bindings.json` fixture;
- config-gate off → exit 0; enabled + no ticket → exit 1 AND the diagnostic contains the
trailer format + accepted forms + an example (asserted against `EXPECTED_FORMAT`);
- merge-commit exempt; the three input modes; a valid leading-`<id>:` commit → exit 0.
- [ ] Doc-drift test: a unit test imports `EXPECTED_FORMAT` and asserts
`docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` contains its text, so docs cannot silently drift.
- [ ] Docs (accurate + discoverable; a reusable, rebar-enforced convention for BOTH clients and
contributors):
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — every commit to `main` must carry a resolvable ticket ref; the
trailer format, the leading-`<id>:` alternative, accepted ID forms, CI enforcement.
- `CLAUDE.md` — in the `## Git workflow (code changes)` section, the same for agents.
- `docs/config.md` — the `verify.require_ticket_for_commit` flag.
- `docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md` (new) — the reusable mechanism: trailer convention +
`rebar verify-commit-ticket` + extraction/resolution + config; linked from the two above.
## Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/test_verify_commit_ticket.py -q`
- `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py -q` (intercept leaves parity intact)
- `rebar verify-commit-ticket --message "x: no ticket"; echo $?` → 1, printing EXPECTED_FORMAT
- `rebar verify-commit-ticket --message-file <(git show -s --format=%B HEAD); echo $?` → 0
- `grep -l 'rebar-ticket:' CONTRIBUTING.md CLAUDE.md docs/config.md docs/commit-ticket-trailer.md`
(all four document the trailer)
- CI-path (`require-ticket` job) is proved by an operator throwaway change, like the two-vote E2E.
## Out of scope
- Non-Gerrit paths (the `tickets` branch; direct GitHub pushes — already blocked by the ruleset).
- An advisory client-side `commit-msg` hook (optional future nicety).
- A `rebar-ticket: none` bypass sentinel (kept strict; merge commits are the only exemption).

baseline.summary: CI Verified gate: require a resolvable rebar ticket ID in every Gerrit commit to main

baseline.description:
## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Builds on **ddbe** (identity entity with `mappings: [{provider, external_id}]`),
committed on this branch, not yet on origin/main. Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
Resolve outbound Jira assignee/reporter by the provider's opaque **accountId**,
looked up through the identity entity's `{provider, external_id}` mappings, with
graceful degradation. Mappings key on the opaque id, NEVER email.

## Architectural constraint (drives every placement below)
`acli.py` is the reconciler ENGINE's Jira client: it imports only within the
`rebar_reconciler` package (its own `acli_*`/`adapters`/`adf` submodules) and must NOT
reach up into rebar's CORE library (`rebar._commands.*`) — that layering keeps the
engine separable from rebar core and avoids a circular import (rebar core → engine →
rebar core). (Its docstring's "stdlib only" line is stale re: intra-package imports,
but the core-library boundary holds.) Therefore ALL identity/mapping resolution lives
in the reconciler FLOW layer (`outbound_differ.py`, `dispatch_one.py`, which already
depend on rebar core); `acli.py`/`acli_rest.py` receive only a bool flag + resolved
accountId strings. (Resolution helpers take no `repo_root` at these sites — they
default to rebar core's `config.repo_root()` internally, per ddbe's identity module;
there is NO `repo_root()` in the reconciler's own `config.py`.)

## What
### 1. Provider-neutral seam (`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py`)
- `resolve_mapping(provider, external_id, *, repo_root=None) -> str | None` — id of the
  identity whose `mappings` contains `{"provider":provider,"external_id":external_id}`
  (exact match on the opaque id), else None. (AC1 seam; 2f13 also consumes it.) Never raises.
- `jira_account_id(local_assignee, *, repo_root=None) -> str | None` — resolve a LOCAL
  assignee string to a Jira accountId: an identity whose ticket id == `local_assignee`
  OR whose `email` == it (case-insensitive); return its `{provider:"jira"}`
  `external_id`, else None. Never raises.
- `identity_email(local_assignee, *, repo_root=None) -> str | None` — the matched
  identity's `email` (same id/email matching as `jira_account_id`), so the
  `/user/search` fallback can obtain an email to query. Never raises.

### 2. Assignee accountId fast-path (resolve in the DIFFER, skip flag through to acli)
- `_assignee_resolver` (`outbound_differ.py`, flow layer, may import rebar) tries
  `identity.jira_account_id(assignee)` FIRST. `_assignee_resolver`'s return is
  EXTENDED from `(accountId|None, authoritative)` to a 3-tuple `(accountId|None,
  authoritative, is_account_id: bool)` where `is_account_id` is True ONLY when the
  value came from the identity-mapping fast path (`jira_account_id`). `_diff_fields`
  (the caller) writes the accountId into `changed['assignee']` and sets
  `changed['_assignee_is_account_id'] = is_account_id`. All existing callers of
  `_assignee_resolver` must be updated to unpack the 3-tuple — notably
  `outbound_fields.py` (~line 435, currently `acct, authoritative = assignee_resolver(...)`)
  and any other unpack site — else `ValueError: too many values to unpack`. (`OutboundMutation`
  is a frozen dataclass — the sentinel rides INSIDE the `fields`/`changed` dict, not a
  new dataclass field.)
- `dispatch_one.update_one` POPS `_assignee_is_account_id` off `fields` (a small
  `_update_one_apply_*`-style step) and passes `assignee_is_account_id=<bool>` as a
  kwarg into `client.update_issue`.
- `AcliClient.update_issue` (stdlib-only) gains `assignee_is_account_id: bool = False`;
  it POPS this kwarg before delegating to the module-level `update_issue(**kwargs)` (so
  it is never forwarded to the ACLI subprocess as `--assignee_is_account_id`), and when
  True it submits `assignee` DIRECTLY (skips `validate_assignee_exists`). No rebar
  import enters acli.py — only a bool.
- Degradation UNCHANGED: no mapping → the existing `validate_assignee_exists`
  string-match → `AssigneeNotFoundError` → soft-fail → unassigned/project-default.
  264f never hard-fails on an unresolvable assignee.

### 3. `/user/search` bootstrap (best-effort, TRANSIENT, flow layer)
In `_assignee_resolver`'s fallback (flow layer), when `jira_account_id` misses, the differ obtains the
identity's email via `identity.identity_email(assignee)`
(falling back to `assignee` itself when it already looks like an email); if an email
is available it best-effort calls the client's `/rest/api/3/user/search?query=
<email>` (a helper in `acli_rest.py` that takes an email and returns an accountId or
None). The v3 endpoint returns a JSON LIST of user objects each with `accountId` +
`emailAddress`; extract the `accountId` of the entry whose `emailAddress` matches the
email EXACTLY (case-insensitive). Since Jira substring-matches, ZERO or ≥2 exact
matches → NO result (do not guess). The resolved accountId is used for THIS run only
(NOT written back to `mappings`; persistence out of scope). Any miss/ambiguity/hidden
email degrades to the string-match/unassigned path WITHOUT failing.

### 4. Reporter by accountId — dedicated REST sub-call, resolved in the flow layer
- `dispatch_one.update_one` gains `_update_one_apply_reporter(fields, issue_key,
  client)`, called BEFORE `_update_one_filter_fields` (mirroring
  `_update_one_apply_parent` at line 518→493): it POPS `reporter` off `fields`,
  resolves the local reporter string to an accountId via
  `identity.jira_account_id(reporter)`, and (when
  resolved) calls `client.set_reporter(issue_key, account_id)`. When
  `jira_account_id(reporter)` returns None (the reporter maps to no identity/
  accountId), reporter is SKIPPED (dropped — never sent as a raw string) and a
  soft-fail `alert_store.append(...)` of kind `outbound-reporter-unresolved`
  (`jira_key`, `field="reporter"`, `reason`) is recorded; the sync continues. Because reporter is
  popped BEFORE the allowlist filter, it is NOT added to `_OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST`
  and never reaches the scalar `client.update_issue(**fields)`. `reporter` IS added to
  `outbound_fields.py` so the differ emits it into `changed`.
- `acli_rest.set_reporter(jira_key, account_id)` uses `_direct_rest_put_raw`
  (NOT `_direct_rest_put`, which wraps as `{"value": ...}` for the properties API):
  `_direct_rest_put_raw(f"/rest/api/3/issue/{jira_key}", {"fields": {"reporter":
  {"accountId": account_id}}})`.
- `_update_one_apply_reporter` accesses `alert_store` by LAZY-LOAD (by file path,
  the same pattern `run_differs.py` / `fetcher.py` use) and obtains `repo_root` via
  `rebar.config.repo_root()` (flow layer may import rebar core) — `update_one`'s
  signature is NOT changed. Both soft-fail records below go through this.
- Failure is HTTP-ONLY (no subprocess): catch `urllib.error.HTTPError` (4xx =
  Modify-Reporter not granted) around ONLY the `set_reporter` call, record
  `alert_store.append(...)` kind `outbound-reporter-not-permitted` (fields `jira_key`,
  `field="reporter"`, `reason`), and let `update_one` continue (soft degradation) so
  OTHER fields still apply and the sync does not hard-fail.

## Scope
In: the `resolve_mapping`/`jira_account_id` seam, the assignee accountId fast-path
(differ → sentinel → acli bool), the transient `/user/search` bootstrap, and the
reporter REST sub-call with HTTP-only isolated degradation. Out: inbound ghost minting
(2f13), enforcement (3183), persisting bootstrapped accountIds. Tests use a fixture
identity + a stubbed client (no live Jira).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_mapping(provider, external_id)` returns the mapped identity id (keyed on
  the opaque id, not email) and None when absent; `jira_account_id` returns the jira
  accountId for a matching local assignee (and None otherwise) and `identity_email`
  returns that identity's email (and None when unmatched) — test all three.
- [ ] With a fixture identity mapping a local assignee to a stubbed accountId, the
  outbound mutation carries that accountId as the assignee and the stubbed client's
  `validate_assignee_exists`/assignable-search is NOT called — asserted by a spy whose
  call-count is 0 (measurable "no Jira search needed").
- [ ] An assignee with no identity mapping and a stubbed assignable-search miss
  degrades to unassigned/project-default WITHOUT raising or failing the sync (test).
- [ ] `/user/search` bootstrap: an identity with an email but no jira mapping resolves
  via a stubbed `/user/search` exact-email match to that accountId (transiently); a
  stubbed miss or ≥2-match degrades without failing (test both).
- [ ] Reporter is applied via `set_reporter` (REST) with the resolved accountId when
  the stub succeeds; when the stubbed `set_reporter` raises an HTTP 4xx, `update_one`
  records an `alert_store` entry of kind `outbound-reporter-not-permitted`, still
  applies other fields, and does not fail the sync (test asserts the alert, other
  fields applied, overall success).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (resolve_mapping + jira_account_id seam)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` (_assignee_resolver: identity fast-path + /user/search bootstrap + _assignee_is_account_id sentinel)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` (pop _assignee_is_account_id → assignee_is_account_id kwarg; _update_one_apply_reporter pop+resolve+set_reporter before the filter)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli.py` (update_issue: assignee_is_account_id bool param, popped before delegation, skips validate_assignee_exists)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_rest.py` (/user/search email→accountId helper + set_reporter via _direct_rest_put_raw)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_fields.py` (emit reporter into changed)
baseline.summary: identity: provider-neutral mapping + Jira adapter (outbound assignee/reporter)

baseline.description:
Jira reconciler silently fails to sync comments and inbound links while reporting
`converged` — three distinct defects, all hidden behind a pass that counts failed
sub-operations toward "applied N of N" and exits 0.

## Context

Investigation (/rebar-debug, 2026-07-17) established that status/existence sync is
healthy (0 drift across ~1200 tickets), but three field-level sync paths are broken
and invisible:

- **Comment sync (P1):** `get_comments()` returns only the first 50 of N comments
  (no `--paginate`), so outbound dedup re-posts the rest every pass. 13 tickets have
  been inflated to Jira's 5000-comment hard cap (local truth: 22-76 comments each);
  further adds fail `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and are swallowed.
- **Inbound link direction (P2):** `_diff_links_inbound` has its inward/outward
  branches swapped (`blocks`<->`depends_on`). Latent since 2026-06-15 (`f6687adf4`);
  UNMASKED when the outbound direction fix landed (`6b25dbead`/`43d154523`, 07-16/17)
