## Problem
The plan-review code-grounding finders (G1G2/E4/E6) ground assertions ONLY against the origin/main snapshot and never consider the ticket's prerequisites, so a plan that relies on a symbol/file a prerequisite ticket will create is flagged "missing/unverifiable" and BLOCKED. G1G2 already SAYS "a symbol created by a ticket this ticket depends_on is treated as EXISTING" (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G1G2.md:10`) but that rule is PROSE ONLY — unwired.

## Approach & rationale (G6/T1) — advisory det signal + LLM agent grounding; no new floor block
Introduce a machine-parseable inline citation `<subject> [rebar:<ticket-id>]` and honor it in two layers WITHOUT adding a blocking check to the DET floor (which is architecturally FAIL-OPEN per the det_floor docstring). No novel architecture (T1): reuses the `det_operator_attested` inline-tag PARSING approach (imported as a MODULE at `det_floor.py:452` via `from . import det_operator_attested`, called `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines(...)` — NOT a regex-constant import) and the existing `show_ticket` reviewer tool (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`).

### Layer 1 — deterministic, ADVISORY (genuinely mirrors det_operator_attested, which never blocks)
New `det_citation.py` parses `[rebar:<id>]` tokens and verifies each cited id is a DIRECT UPSTREAM prerequisite of the plan ticket P. "Upstream" has TWO encodings and BOTH count as verified:
- (a) P declares the dependency: P's own `ctx.state["deps"]` contains `{relation:"depends_on", target_id:<cited>}`; OR
- (b) the cited ticket declares the block: the CITED ticket C's deps contains `{relation:"blocks", target_id:P}` (a reverse lookup — C blocks P ⇒ C is upstream of P).
Note (per the D2 review's correct catch): in a ticket's own deps, a `blocks` entry means THAT ticket blocks its target (target is DOWNSTREAM), so P's own `blocks` entries do NOT verify — only P.depends_on(C) or C.blocks(P) do. `det_citation` therefore takes P's deps PLUS an injected `resolve_deps(ticket_id) -> list[dep]` callable (det_floor supplies one backed by `_reads.show_ticket`) to do the bounded reverse lookup (one read per distinct cited id). A citation matching NEITHER (a) nor (b) → an ADVISORY coaching finding ("add a depends_on edge to <id>, or ensure <id> blocks this ticket, or remove the citation"). Never blocks (respects fail-open floor). `accruing_since` for any emitted signal is a module-level constant matching the existing reader modules.

### Layer 2 — LLM agent grounding (deliberately non-deterministic; blocking stays where it already lives)
The coverage-check is INTENTIONALLY an LLM judgment, NOT a string/path match — an exact matching rule is impractical because relied-upon functionality is described in prose, not verbatim symbols. Protocol (fully specified even though the judgment is non-deterministic — this is the same LLM decision every Pass-1 finder already makes):
- TRIGGER: a grounding finder (G1G2/E4/E6) is about to flag a symbol/functionality as missing, and that symbol is cited `<subject> [rebar:<C>]` with an edge VERIFIED by Layer 1.
- PROCEDURE: the finder retrieves C via the `show_ticket(C)` tool and judges whether C's plan/file_impact establishes the SPECIFIC functionality this finding claims is missing.
- INPUTS: the cited ticket C's content (plan + file_impact) and the specific missing-functionality claim under evaluation.
- DECISION (FAIL-CLOSED): credit the citation — treat the symbol as EXISTING and DROP the finding — ONLY if the reviewer affirmatively confirms C provides that functionality. If C does not, or the reviewer is uncertain, the finding STANDS. An uncited citation, an edge-unbacked citation (Layer 1), or an unconfirmed-coverage citation is ground-as-normal → still fails closed. Determinism is neither required nor claimed; what is specified is the protocol contract (trigger, procedure, inputs, decision, default).

Anti-bypass WITHOUT a new floor block: crediting requires BOTH a Layer-1-verified edge AND affirmative LLM coverage; a fabricated or coverage-absent citation earns no credit, so the normal missing-symbol block applies.

## Grammar (vocabulary — T8)
`<subject> [rebar:<ticket-id>]`: `<subject>` is free text naming the relied-upon code element (file path, module, class, function, or config key); the TOKEN is the trailing `[rebar:<ticket-id>]`; `<ticket-id>` matches rebar's id/alias grammar. det_citation parses the bracket; the subject is the human/LLM-readable referent.

## Grounding (E4/G1G2 — verified via Grep/Read)
- CONFIRMED `det_floor.py:452` = `from . import det_operator_attested`; it is ADVISORY ("p6 never blocks", `det_floor.py:486`).
- CONFIRMED `PlanContext.state` carries the show_ticket state incl. `deps` (`det_floor.py:104-126`); dep entries are `{target_id, relation}` from the ticket's outgoing perspective (D2 review-confirmed).
- CONFIRMED `show_ticket` is always in the reviewer tool set (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`).
- Rubric SoT: `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_{G1G2,E4,E6}.md`. `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED (regenerate, never hand-edit).

## Scope
IN: `[rebar:<id>]` grammar; Layer-1 `det_citation.py` (advisory, both-direction edge verify via P.deps + resolve_deps reverse lookup) wired into det_floor's advisory lane; Layer-2 rubric edits (G1G2/E4/E6) specifying the LLM show_ticket coverage protocol; author guidance; regenerate the criteria guide.
OUT (separate): T8 overlay over-fire (bug 1a05-e3a8); snapshot-pinning; transitive-closure citations; deterministic coverage matching (explicitly rejected in favor of LLM judgment).

## Acceptance criteria (observable + proving command)
- [ ] `det_citation.parse_citations(plan_text)` returns `(subject, ticket_id)` per `[rebar:<id>]`. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py::test_parse`.
- [ ] Edge-check verifies BOTH directions and rejects downstream: `{depends_on->C}` in P.deps → verified; `{blocks->P}` in resolve_deps(C) → verified; a `{blocks->X}` in P.deps (downstream) or no edge → unbacked. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py::test_edge_both_directions`.
- [ ] The det check is ADVISORY — never flips the verdict to BLOCK. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py::test_advisory_never_blocks`.
- [ ] WIRING: det_floor invokes det_citation in its advisory lane — a PlanContext whose plan has an edge-unbacked `[rebar:<id>]` yields the advisory citation finding, verdict NOT BLOCK. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py::test_det_floor_wires_citation`.
- [ ] Rubrics G1G2/E4/E6 carry the `[rebar:<id>]` rule with the LLM show_ticket coverage PROTOCOL (trigger/procedure/inputs/fail-closed decision) AND the explicit "uncited / edge-unbacked / coverage-unconfirmed still fails closed" clause. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_citation_rubric_contract.py`.
- [ ] Author guidance added. PROVE: `grep -q "\[rebar:" docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md`.
- [ ] Criteria guide regenerated + plan-review suite green. PROVE: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide && pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review -k "citation or contract"`.

## Files likely touched
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_citation.py (new; advisory parse + both-direction edge verify via injected resolve_deps)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py (advisory-lane wiring; supply resolve_deps backed by _reads.show_ticket; small addition — det_floor is 746/800 LOC)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_{G1G2,E4,E6}.md (the LLM coverage protocol + fail-closed clause)
- docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md, docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md (regenerated)
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py (new), tests/unit/plan_review/test_citation_rubric_contract.py (new)

## Estimated scope: M

## Round-3 additions (clearing the INDETERMINATE no-verification findings)
- ERROR HANDLING (Layer 1, fail-closed): the reverse-lookup `resolve_deps(C)`/`show_ticket(C)` is wrapped so ANY exception (store/network/missing-ticket) is caught and the citation is treated as UNVERIFIED (advisory finding stands) — the exception NEVER propagates into the advisory lane. A failed reverse-lookup counts as 'unbacked' (safe), not 'abstain'.
- RATIONALE for the separate module + injected callable (G6): `det_floor.py` is 746/800 LOC (near the hard module-size cap), so the citation logic MUST live in a separate `det_citation.py` — this is the module-size policy, not gratuitous indirection. The `resolve_deps` callable is injected (not a hard `_reads` import inside det_citation) purely so the edge-check is unit-testable with a fake resolver.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] REVERSE-LOOKUP FAIL-CLOSED: when the injected `resolve_deps` raises, the citation is reported UNVERIFIED and NO exception escapes det_citation. PROVE: `pytest -q tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py::test_reverse_lookup_error_fails_closed`.
- [ ] RUBRIC BEHAVIORAL EVAL (runtime, not text-presence): a plan-review behavioral eval fixture under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/` exercises the Layer-2 coverage protocol on TWO plans — one citing a verified+covered prerequisite (expect: symbol credited, no missing-symbol finding) and one citing an edge-unbacked or coverage-absent prerequisite (expect: finding STANDS) — run over N samples against a predeclared threshold (mirrors the det_operator_attested lexicon-eval self-gating precedent). PROVE: the eval harness run recorded on the ticket. [operator-attested] — the behavioral-eval evidence (sample pass-rate vs threshold) is recorded on the ticket, as LLM-behavioral effects are validated by the eval harness rather than a single deterministic unit assertion.
baseline.summary: Plan-review: honor verified [rebar:<id>] cross-ticket citations so depends_on-created symbols ground instead of false-positive

# Split runner.py along a call-graph seam — it sits at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap

## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is **exactly 800 LOC** (`wc -l`), which is the repo hard cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`. The CI module-size gate compares with `$1 > lim` (strictly greater), so 800 PASSES today — but there is **zero headroom**: the next line added to this file fails `Verified` for everyone.

This is a pre-existing condition, not caused by one story: runner.py was 783 before `7468`, 787 before `dc0d`. `AGENTS.md` targets **200–500 LOC** per file, so it is well past target.

It is now a **hard blocker, not a nicety**. Both remaining code stories in epic `061c` must ADD lines to this file and cannot:

- `2932` (Bedrock) adds a `supports_temperature` capability check plus the cache-zero warning;
- `343b` (verdict provenance) adds provenance capture.

Both are strictly positive LOC, so there is no net-neutral way to write them. This task is recorded as `blocks` on both.

## Approach — the seam, chosen from measured data

`AGENTS.md`: split only along call-graph seams that already exist, never mechanically to hit a number, and never create a file under 100 LOC. Measured top-level symbol sizes in the current file:

| symbol | lines |
|---|---|
| `PydanticAIRunner` | 400 |
| `_pai_structured` | 76 |
| `RunRequest` | 47 |
| `FakeRunner` | 44 |
| `_extract_usage` | 34 |
| `_pai_check_config` | 29 |
| `_readonly_gate` | 21 |
| `get_runner` / `Runner` / `_check_tool_capability` | 19 / 17 / 17 |
| `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` | 16 |
| `_import_pydantic_ai` | 13 |
| `effective_max_tokens` / `effective_max_iterations` | 10 / 9 |
| `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS` | 3 |

**Extract the structured-output execution cluster** into a new leaf `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py`:

- `_pai_structured` (76) — the bounded structured-output retry driver
- `_extract_usage` (34) — which `_pai_structured` calls twice
- `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (16) — which interprets what `_extract_usage` returns
- `effective_max_iterations` (9) + `effective_max_tokens` (10) — the per-request budget sizing the retry loop
  and `run()` both enforce
- `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS` (3) — used only by `_pai_structured`

**= 148 lines moved.** `runner.py` lands at ~657 (under the 700 target below, with real headroom), and `structured_run.py` is ~165–175 LOC with its docstring and imports — comfortably over the 100-LOC floor.

**Why this is a genuine seam, with the dependency list enumerated by AST rather than by eye.** An earlier draft of this plan claimed the cluster references "exactly `_extract_usage`, `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS`, and `RunRequest`". That was produced by a hand-picked grep and was **incomplete** — it missed `usage_log`. Redone properly by walking the AST of each cluster member and intersecting its free names with runner.py's module-level names, the complete set each member needs is:

| cluster member | module-level names it needs |
|---|---|
| `_pai_structured` | `RunRequest`, `StructuredOutputError`, `UnretryableOutputError`, `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS`, `_extract_usage`, `usage_log` |
| `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` | `logger` |
| `_extract_usage`, `effective_max_iterations`, `effective_max_tokens` | none |

Which resolves cleanly, and only ONE item is a runner-defined dependency:

- `_extract_usage` and `_FAULTY_OUTPUT_SNIPPET_CHARS` **move with the cluster** — not external at all.
- `StructuredOutputError` / `UnretryableOutputError` come from `rebar.llm.errors` (verified: both defined there).
- `usage_log` is `from rebar.llm import usage_log` — a top-level import the new module must carry. Verified it
  pulls in NO heavy module, so the stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract holds.
- `logger` is a fresh `logging.getLogger(__name__)` in the new module.
- `RunRequest` is the only symbol still owned by `runner`, and it is used **only in an annotation** — see below.

The cohesion story holds: "drive a structured-output run and account its token usage". The members call each other, and nothing else in the file calls into the middle of them.

**The one snag, and its resolution.** `_pai_structured`'s signature annotates `req: RunRequest`, and `RunRequest` stays in `runner.py` (moving it would churn every `from rebar.llm.runner import RunRequest` site across the tests for no benefit). With `from __future__ import annotations` the annotation is a string at runtime, so `structured_run.py` imports `RunRequest` under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` only. There is therefore **no runtime import from `runner`**, which is what the leaf rule actually protects against — matching the convention already used by `anthropic_model.py`, `providers.py` and `capabilities.py`.

`runner.py` imports the five moved callables from `structured_run`. Direction is runner -> structured_run, never back.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Moving `_pai_check_config` (29) to `config.py` — the obvious quick win, but `config.py` is 768 LOC so it would land at ~796 and merely relocate the same landmine. (b) A tiny module holding only `_extract_usage` + `_warn_if_zeroed_usage` (50 lines) — violates the sub-100-LOC split rule. (c) Splitting `PydanticAIRunner.run()` itself (the real 400-line bulk) — a much larger behavioural risk, and not needed to clear the cap; worth its own story if runner.py trends up again.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` (**new leaf**) — the five moved symbols.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — the symbols removed and imported instead.
- Test import sites for the moved symbols. **Enumerate them with a symbol-reference query, not by eye**, and
  sweep separately for string-literal patch targets (`monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_pai_structured", ...)`)
  which an LSP cannot resolve — that exact class broke `7468` and `f184` in this epic. Known at time of writing:
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` patches `runner_mod._pai_structured` by string.

## Testing

**This is a pure relocation with no behaviour change, so it cannot be RED-first, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.** The oracle is the existing suite: 7517 tests currently pass, and they must still pass with no edits other than moved import sites and patch targets. A behaviour change here shows up as a failure in tests written for the behaviour, which is exactly the regression net this split needs.

The only genuinely new assertion is the structural one: that `structured_run.py` has no runtime import from `runner`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **`runner.py` is under 700 LOC** (projected ~657) — real headroom, not sitting on the cap — and
      `structured_run.py` is under 500 (the `AGENTS.md` target ceiling). Scoped to the two files this task
      touches: an earlier draft said "no file under `src/rebar` exceeds 700", which was unpassable, because
      `config.py` is 768 LOC and is deliberately NOT touched here (see rejected alternative (a)). `config.py`
      passes the real 800 gate with ~32 lines of headroom, so it is a known condition rather than this task's
      work; splitting it needs its own seam analysis if it ever trends up.
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` is >= 100 LOC (the `AGENTS.md` floor for a split)
- [ ] `structured_run.py` has NO runtime import from `runner`: `grep -n 'from rebar.llm.runner\|import runner'
      src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` shows only a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded line, if any
- [ ] `import rebar.llm` still pulls in NO heavy module (httpx / anthropic / pydantic_ai / openai / boto3),
      verified empirically — heavy imports stay function-local
- [ ] the FULL gating suite passes with **7517 passed** and zero test-logic edits: only import sites and
      string-literal patch targets may change, proving behaviour preservation
- [ ] every moved symbol's reference sites were found via a symbol-reference query PLUS a string-literal grep,
      and both were run (the string-literal sweep is what an LSP structurally cannot do)
- [ ] `structured_run.py` carries `from rebar.llm import usage_log` and imports its two error types from
      `rebar.llm.errors` — the AST-enumerated dependency set above, with nothing left implicit
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL `make test` pass, evidenced by the Gerrit
      change id and its `Verified +1` recorded in a comment on this ticket (this proof is external to the repo)
baseline.summary: Split runner.py along a call-graph seam — it sits at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap

## Context / Problem
`docs/plan-review-gate.md` and the `review_plan` docstring both state that a `bug`
short-circuits to a bare exempt PASS with `runner=exempt`. Probing on origin/main showed a
`bug` actually returns `runner='pydantic_ai'`, `coverage.llm_ran=True`, and a signature.

**Investigation result (2026-07-24): the CODE is correct; the DOCS are stale.**

`workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:160-175`)
short-circuits ONLY `session_log` / `code_review` / `identity`. Its inline comment records the
deliberate change:

    BUG REVIEW TIER (epic 6982 / R4): a bug no longer short-circuits to a bare exempt-PASS.
    It gets a LIGHT ADVISORY review — DET floor + necessity probe (registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA)
    — but is NEVER BLOCKED ... so a bug always PASSes.

`tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py` already pins exactly this, asserting `runner != "exempt"`
for a bug. So bugs being reviewed is an intentional feature, not a missing short-circuit.

**This ticket's original acceptance criteria were therefore wrong.** They asked to "make
exempt types short-circuit as documented", which would have REVERTED epic 6982. They have been
rewritten to the real defect: two stale statements in the documentation. Criteria are corrected
rather than closed-against-stale, per the remedy documented in 4636-432a-1871-4d74.

Note the two distinct exemption axes that made the original claim look right: a bug needs no
signed attestation to be CLAIMED (a CLI-side exemption in `rebar._commands.gates`, unchanged),
which is separate from whether the plan-review gate REVIEWS it. Conflating them is the trap.

## Expected Behavior
The documentation describes what the code does: `session_log` / `code_review` / `identity` are
gate-exempt (`runner=exempt`, no review); a `bug` is reviewed under the bug tier and can be
coached but never blocked.

## Scope
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (the `review_plan` docstring)

No behavior change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` no longer claims bugs are exempt from the gate, and names
      `session_log` / `code_review` / `identity` as the exempt types; verified by
      `grep -q 'A \*\*bug is NOT' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The never-signed passage no longer lists `bug` as an exempt runner; verified by
      `grep -q 'a\n\`bug\` is reviewed under the bug tier' docs/plan-review-gate.md` or by
      reading the section — it must say a bug is NOT exempt there.
- [ ] The `review_plan` docstring describes the bug review tier instead of claiming bugs are
      exempt; verified by
      `grep -q 'bug review tier' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`.
- [ ] The CLI claim-time bug exemption is called out as a separate axis, so the two are not
      conflated again.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py` still passes (no behavior change).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Docs wrongly claim bug tickets are gate-exempt (the bug review tier reviews them)

content.text: ## What
**Cut the reconciler over** to the self-healing ref-lock (C1+C2), behind an expand-contract switch
so the file backend is retained for rollback. No band-aids are removed here (that is C4).
delivered by C1/C2 and must be merged first.
- Add a `[reconciler] lock_backend = file | ref` config key (`_config_schema.py`) and register
`lock_lease_secs` (default 120, consumed by C2). Default `lock_backend` stays `file`; `ref` selects
the new path. This is the rollback lever.
- Rewire `acquire_pass_lock`/`release_pass_lock` and the phase-gate in `_advisory_lock.py` so that
under `lock_backend=ref` they use `_ref_lock` on `refs/reconciler/lock` and `refs/reconciler/gate`
instead of `_write_file_to_tickets_branch`. Fully specify the gate lifecycle (Design decision 2).
- **`acquire_pass_lock` failure contract:** when the create-only CAS is rejected (someone holds it),
raise `ReconcileLockError` (matching today's file-lock "already held" semantics) rather than an
opaque `CalledProcessError` (map `_ref_lock.RefLockHeldError` -> `ReconcileLockError`).
- Update `rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` (Steps 2a/2b/3) to acquire, start the C2 daemon-thread
heartbeat (`renew()` at `heartbeat_interval(lease)`), and release in a `finally`. **Concrete
lost-lease abort mechanism:** acquire creates a `threading.Event` (`lock_lost`); the heartbeat
daemon, on `LeaseLostError` from `renew()`, calls `lock_lost.set()` and exits (a daemon thread
cannot raise into the main thread). The pass **polls `lock_lost.is_set()` at per-ticket
checkpoints** and, if set, raises `ReconcileLockLost` to abort cleanly (the `finally` release then
no-ops — the lock is already gone). Idempotent -> safe re-run. Thread the acquire oid through
acquire -> renew -> release (Design decision 3).
- Under `lock_backend=ref`, stop writing `.reconciler-pass-lock`/`.reconciler-phase-gate` to the
tickets tree. Authoritative ref on `origin`; acquire/renew/release push via
`--force-with-lease=<ref>:<old>` (explicit lease ref form, never bare) — delivered by the C1
remote path (`remote="origin"`).
- **Edit set also includes the external consumers** that name the file locks:
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` (must fetch `refs/reconciler/*` before acquire),
`docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/concurrency.md` (update the I6 file-lock exception note). Update
the existing file-lock tests `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py` and
`test_advisory_lock_cas_race.py` to cover the ref backend.
Scope note: `merge=ours`/`.gitattributes`, the `b859` retry loop, and the file-lock code are LEFT IN
PLACE here (removed in C4) so this change is independently bisectable and reversible via the flag.
## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)
1. **Backend switch = one dispatch point per function.** `acquire_pass_lock` / `release_pass_lock` /
`check_phase_gate` each read `load_config().reconciler.lock_backend`; on `"file"` they run today's
`_write/_delete_file_to_tickets_branch` path verbatim (untouched — bisectable rollback), on
`"ref"` they call the ref-backend helpers below. The ref path passes `remote="origin"` (from
`sync.remote`) so the lock is authoritative on the shared remote. `acquire_pass_lock` maps
`_ref_lock.RefLockHeldError` -> `ReconcileLockError`; it returns the acquired **oid** so the
caller can thread it to `renew`/`release`. `release_pass_lock` takes that oid (idempotent no-op if
the ref is already gone/stolen).
2. **`refs/reconciler/gate` lifecycle — CAS-managed, own tiny schema.** The gate is a persistent
*phase-throttle marker*, not a lease-held lock, so it does NOT reuse the lock's
`{holder,lease_secs,heartbeat_ns,fence}` blob. It uses the SAME ref->blob CAS **mechanism** via
three thin helpers added to `_ref_lock.py` — `read_gate(repo, ref=GATE_REF, *, remote) ->
str|None`, `set_gate(repo, mode, *, remote)` (create-or-CAS-update), `clear_gate(repo, *,
remote)` (observed-oid delete) — over a blob `{"gated_mode": "<mode>"}`. **Creation:** whoever
throttles a phase calls `set_gate(mode)`; **transition:** `set_gate` CAS-updates the blob against
the observed oid (atomic); **clear:** `clear_gate`; **consumer:** `check_phase_gate(target_mode)`
reads the gated mode via `read_gate` and blocks iff `target_mode > gated_mode` (today's
`Mode`-ordering semantics, unchanged). Absent ref = no gate (open). A corrupt/unreadable gate blob
fails closed (treated as gated) consistent with the C1 read contract.
3. **Lost-lease abort thread-through (per-ticket).** `__main__` Step 3 creates `lock_lost =
threading.Event()`, acquires (capturing the oid), and starts a **daemon** heartbeat thread that
loops `renew(oid=<current>)` every `heartbeat_interval(lease)`; on `LeaseLostError` it
`lock_lost.set()` and exits. `run_pass` passes `abort_check=lock_lost.is_set` into
`reconcile_once`, which forwards it to `applier.apply`; applier calls `abort_check()` at the top of
its **per-mutation** loops (the `inbound_typed` dispatch loop and `_apply_batch`) and raises
`ReconcileLockLost` when set. So the file_impact expands to include `reconcile.py` and `applier.py`
(the callback thread-through) — a minimal `Callable[[], bool] | None` parameter defaulting to
`None` (no behavioural change when unset, so the file backend and all existing callers are
unaffected). `ReconcileLockLost` is a new exception (in `_advisory_lock.py`); the `finally` release
is a no-op after a lost lease (the ref already moved), so a re-run is safe/idempotent.
4. **`ReconcileLockLost` vs `ReconcileLockError`.** `ReconcileLockError` = "could not get the lock"
(acquire rejected / fail-closed). `ReconcileLockLost` = "held it, then lost it mid-pass" (heartbeat
detected a steal). Both abort the pass; the orchestrator returns a non-zero exit and the `finally`
release no-ops.
5. **Heartbeat thread lifecycle.** The daemon thread is started only after a successful acquire and
signalled to stop (a second `threading.Event`, `stop_heartbeat`) in the `finally` before release;
it is a daemon so a hard crash never wedges process exit. `renew` failures other than
`LeaseLostError` (e.g. transient) are logged and retried on the next tick; a `LeaseLostError` is
terminal (set `lock_lost`, exit).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `[reconciler] lock_backend` key selects `file` (default) or `ref`, and `lock_lease_secs`
(default 120) is registered; under `ref`, `acquire_pass_lock`/`release_pass_lock` + phase-gate
use `_ref_lock` over `refs/reconciler/*` and no `.reconciler-*` file is written to the tickets
branch; the `file` path is byte-for-byte unchanged (rollback lever).
- [ ] The `refs/reconciler/gate` lifecycle is fully specified and CAS-managed via `read_gate` /
`set_gate` / `clear_gate` over a `{"gated_mode": "<mode>"}` blob (creation, atomic CAS
transition, clear, consumer); `check_phase_gate` blocks iff `target_mode > gated_mode`;
`acquire_pass_lock` raises `ReconcileLockError` on a rejected CAS, not a raw subprocess error.
- [ ] `__main__.py` acquires, heartbeats at `heartbeat_interval(lease)` via the daemon thread,
releases in `finally`, and aborts the pass on a lost-lease signal; a crashed pass (no release)
is reclaimable after lease expiry (test with a short configured lease).
- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` fetches `refs/reconciler/*` before acquire; the
`refs/reconciler/*` push uses explicit `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<old>`; `docs/architecture.md`
+ `docs/concurrency.md` (I6) updated.
- [ ] Lost-lease abort is a `threading.Event` (`lock_lost`) set by the heartbeat daemon and polled
at per-mutation checkpoints (the `abort_check` callback threaded through `reconcile_once` ->
`applier.apply`); on set the pass raises `ReconcileLockLost` and the `finally` release no-ops
(test: heartbeat loses lease mid-pass -> pass aborts, no double-run). `abort_check` defaults to
`None` so existing callers/the file backend are unaffected.
- [ ] Idempotency asserted by a named double-acquire convergence test; existing file-lock tests
(`test_advisory_lock.py`, `test_advisory_lock_cas_race.py`) extended for the ref backend.
Non-integration suite green.

# DC segmenting MD→wiki renderer module (pure capability; codec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Data Center stores rich text as wiki markup (REST v2), a lossy text format. The `RichTextCodec` seam (epic `e369`, story J3 / `aac8`) routes DC rich text through **`WikiTextCodec`** (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:72`), today an **identity** codec: `fit_outbound` (`:82`), `normalize_outbound` (`:96`), `to_wire` (`:100`), `decode_inbound` (`:104`) all pass the plain string through. So DC ships rebar's raw Markdown as literal wiki source.

No library round-trips rebar's punctuation-dense prose: pandoc's jira reader misparses `->`, ASCII pipe-tables, and regex, and provably erodes them one character per pass (the ASCII-table body decays 9115→9110 monotonically). A whole-body all-or-nothing conversion is echo-safe but only ~15% rich. A **segmenting** one-way renderer that converts only structurally-safe units and passes dangerous ones through verbatim reaches ~68% of bodies / ~78% of chars rich, proven non-corrupting across 23 environments, 6 authors, and an out-of-distribution corpus.

**Why this story ships a pure module, not a codec change.** On DC — unlike Cloud — the live outbound wire flows THROUGH a codec op: the shared `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` composes the description as `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))` at `outbound_mapper.py:77`, and that string is what reaches `_issues.py:44 update_issue` → `issue.update(fields=…)`. The codec law (ticket a32a) further ties `normalize_outbound(t)` to `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` — parametrized over BOTH codecs at `test_rich_text_codec.py:163` — and the comment differ's dedup (`outbound_comments.py:48`) relies on it. Therefore **any change to `WikiTextCodec`'s `to_wire` or `normalize_outbound` is, on DC, an immediate live cutover** (a rendering `normalize_outbound` ships rendered wiki the instant it merges) **and breaks the pinned identity tests** (`test_wiki_normalize_is_identity:251`, `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string:244`, `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched:183`) **and the codec law**. To keep capability strictly separate from the hazardous cutover — which must land together with echo-safety in `3388` (which depends on this story) — **this story delivers only the pure renderer module and its tests, and leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity.** Nothing observable changes on merge.

## Prior art in this repo (the seam we build on — NOT greenfield)
- `WikiTextCodec` (DC) — `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:72`, identity today;
  constructed into the shared `OutboundFieldMapper` at `backend.py:84`. **Left
  unchanged by this story.**
- `RichTextCodec` Protocol — four ops; the wire op is `to_wire` (DC: a wiki `str`).
- **Codec law (ticket a32a):** `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
  at `test_rich_text_codec.py:163`; today `WikiTextCodec` satisfies it trivially
  (all ops identity). This story does not perturb it; `3388` re-establishes it for
  the rendering codec when it wires the renderer in.
- **Guard:** `backend.py:131 normalize_rich_text` is the **INBOUND** decode and
  delegates to the SHARED plain-text `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` (ticket
  21ca; also used by sibling repo `agentic-dev-platform`) — unchanged.
- **Import contract (ADR 0035):** `jira_family/` must not import `adapters/jira/`.
  pandoc/`pypandoc` is not a Cloud module, so the renderer lives in `jira_family/`.

## Approach (pure renderer module)
Add `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` exposing a pure function `render_markdown_to_wiki(md: str) -> str` (plus its internal segmenting helpers). It is **not referenced by any codec op or live send path in this story** — it is unit/corpus-tested in isolation, ready for `3388` to wire into `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`.

Pipeline: split the body into blocks and list-items; render structurally-safe units (headings, lists, code, quotes, safe paragraphs) to wiki via pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`); pass dangerous units (ASCII tables, arrow/regex/HTML-dense prose) through **verbatim**; reassemble in original order. Two lossless render rules: **code-aware arrow substitution** (`-> <- <-> =>` → `→ ← ↔ ⇒`, prose-only, skipping fenced/inline code) which MUST run on the **Markdown before pandoc**; and **verbatim-wrapping ASCII tables in `{noformat}`** to stop per-pass dash erosion.

**pandoc delivery (portability).** Pin **`pypandoc-binary`** (bundles a pandoc binary in the wheel) rather than bare `pypandoc` (which requires a system pandoc) so the DC path is self-contained in CI and prod. The renderer probes pandoc availability once; if pandoc is **absent or errors**, `render_markdown_to_wiki` **returns the input unchanged** (identity passthrough — echo-safe, never corrupting) and logs once. GPL/SBOM compliance for the bundled binary is handled by the robustness story `5c0e`.

## Corpus fixture (evaluability)
The ~68%/~78% coverage figures and the 179 code-arrow / 70 table-erosion regression counts are measured against a **vendored** fixture, `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` (a sanitized snapshot exported from the ticket corpus, committed into the repo — NOT fetched from a live environment at test time), so the tests are hermetic and the counts are reproducible in-session.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for this story (owned by `3388`)
- Wiring `render_markdown_to_wiki` into `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`, redefining
  `normalize_outbound` to the compare form, and updating the DC identity pin tests
  (`test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`, `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched`) + the codec-law test for the
  rendering codec.
- Applying the render on the live DC send (`outbound_mapper.py:77`) and CREATE
  path (`backend.py:70`); the second-pass convergence proof; the rollback path.
This story leaves every codec op and live send site untouched, so no observable DC behavior changes on merge.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (new) — segmenting renderer (split →
  per-unit safe-render/passthrough → reassemble; arrow substitution; table wrap;
  pandoc-availability probe + identity fallback). ADR-0035-clean. Pure module,
  not wired to any codec.
- `pyproject.toml` — pinned `pypandoc-binary` extra.
- `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` (new) — vendored, sanitized corpus fixture.
- **Guard (UNCHANGED):** `WikiTextCodec` and all its ops
  (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`); `backend.py:131 normalize_rich_text`; the
  live send sites `outbound_mapper.py:77` and `backend.py:70` (all wired by `3388`).
- `tests/` — segmenting/arrow/table/coverage tests over the vendored fixture.

## Testing (pure-module unit + fixture-corpus only)
- Happy path: headings + a checklist + a fenced code block render to wiki
  `h1.`/`*`-bullets/`{code}` via `render_markdown_to_wiki` and reassemble in order.
- Danger passthrough: an ASCII pipe-table, a prose `->`, and a `obj->method()`
  code arrow render with the table verbatim in `{noformat}`, prose `->`→`→`, and
  the code arrow untouched.
- pandoc-absent fallback: with pandoc unavailable, `render_markdown_to_wiki`
  returns the input unchanged and logs once (`test_dc_pandoc_absent_identity`).
- Codec untouched: `WikiTextCodec` stays identity — the existing
  `test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`,
  `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched`, and the codec-law test stay
  green unmodified.
- Corpus coverage/safety over `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`: rich for ~68% of
  bodies with 0 code-arrow rewrites and 0 prose corruptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki` segments a body and renders only
  structurally-safe units, passing dangerous units (tables/arrows/regex/HTML)
  verbatim; verified by `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough` on a mixed body.
- [ ] Code-aware arrow substitution runs on the Markdown before pandoc and touches
  0 code arrows; verified by a test asserting `obj->method()` is unchanged while a
  prose `->` becomes `→` (regression over the 179 known code-arrow bodies in
  `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/`: 0 rewrites).
- [ ] ASCII tables are verbatim-wrapped in `{noformat}` and do not erode across
  passes; verified by `test_dc_table_noformat_stable` over the 70 known erosion
  bodies in the fixture (70/70 stable).
- [ ] `pypandoc-binary` is pinned and, when pandoc is unavailable,
  `render_markdown_to_wiki` returns the input unchanged (echo-safe); verified by
  `test_dc_pandoc_absent_identity`.
- [ ] Over the vendored `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` the renderer produces rich
  output for ≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars with zero prose corruption; verified by
  `test_dc_corpus_coverage`.
- [ ] `WikiTextCodec` and all its ops remain identity and the live send sites are
  unchanged by this story; verified by the existing DC codec identity tests
  (`test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`,
  `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched`) and the codec-law test staying
  green unmodified (the observable cutover is `3388`).
baseline.summary: DC one-way segmenting wiki renderer

## Reproduction Steps
1. Land commit 10837ca88 (adds external volume gerrit_reviewbot_tickets to infra/compose/docker-compose.yml) WITHOUT updating the provisioning loops in infra/scripts/compose-up.sh.
2. Every rebar-autodeploy tick that sees a new main SHA rebuilds the review-bot image, then `docker compose up -d review-bot` aborts: external volume "gerrit_reviewbot_tickets" not found. Backoff resets on each new main SHA, so a busy push day compresses many multi-GB docker builds into a tight window.
3. Around 2026-07-10 03:15–03:52 UTC the 30G root disk transiently filled (pip Errno 28 in the autodeploy builds, journal); concurrent review clones then failed (VOTER_ERROR "No space left on device"), fail-closing changes 452/461/462 with [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)].

**Expected:** autodeploy converges after every main advance; reviews never veto for infra reasons.
**Actual:** deploys failed on every attempt for ~41h (fail #21 by Jul 10 00:00); transient ENOSPC fail-closed live reviews.

## Resolution (applied on-box 2026-07-10 ~04:45 UTC, supervised)
- Pruned builder/image caches (~3.5G), verified RED via `docker compose up -d --dry-run review-bot` (reproduced the volume error).
- Created the missing bind volume exactly matching sibling spec: `docker volume create --driver local --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets gerrit_reviewbot_tickets` (+ mkdir of host dir); dry-run then GREEN.
- One supervised autodeploy run: "review-bot redeployed + healthy", deployed-sha now d1e4cd5c; Gerrit container untouched; disk 20% used.
- The repo-side fix for infra/scripts/compose-up.sh (and hardening) is child/discovered work.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Autodeploy converges (deploy complete) after volume creation; no bot-build-failed since.
- [ ] Review-bot posts a real (non-coverage-gap) LLM-Review vote post-deploy (functional probe on change 461).
- [ ] Stale coverage-gap veto on change 452 cleared via /rerun.
- [ ] Discovered follow-up defects filed and linked discovered_from this ticket.
baseline.summary: incident: review-bot fail-closed LLM-Review vetoes — root disk exhaustion from a 41h autodeploy failure loop (missing gerrit_reviewbot_tickets volume)

content.text: ## Why
The reconciler concentrates the codebase's accidental complexity. This story
reduces it where the value clearly exceeds the regression risk — pure-refactor
changes to working, well-tested, high-blast-radius sync code must clear that bar.
## What
Two behavior-preserving wins (named REST budget; inbound scalar-field transform
table). Two further candidates (create_one DispatchContext; compute_mutations
flatten) were evaluated and deliberately deferred — see outcome.
## Scope
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/batch_dispatch.py` (named budget constant).
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` (`_apply_inbound_update` field table).
- Out of scope: `reconcile_once` (essential orchestration spine — untouched).
## Outcome (honest scoping)
- **Done — named budget:** `_REST_CALL_BUDGET = 200` replaces the bare literal in the
guard + docstring.
- **Done — inbound field-map table:** the scalar-field if-ladder
(description/priority/assignee/ticket_type/parent_id) is now a declarative
`{field: transform}` table; `title`/`summary` (fallback), `status` (2nd STATUS
event), and `labels` (tag read-modify-write) stay special-cased. Behavior-identical
(dict-merge order-independent); 346 inbound/apply tests pass.
- **Deferred — create_one DispatchContext:** ~30 test call sites pass the params BY
KEYWORD (self-documenting); a dataclass would churn all of them for zero functional
gain. Cost > benefit.
- **Deferred — compute_mutations flatten:** the plan-review confirmed `_emit` is ALREADY
centralized, so the remaining win is marginal; flattening the F(61) core diff risks
the central diff path for a cosmetic CC reduction.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The REST-call budget is a named constant (`_REST_CALL_BUDGET`), used in the guard;
no bare `200` literal remains in create_one.
- [x] `_apply_inbound_update` uses a transform table for the scalar fields, with `title`,
`status`, AND `labels` still special-cased; inbound apply tests pass.
- [x] `reconcile_once` is untouched.
- [x] The two deferred refactors (create_one DispatchContext, compute_mutations flatten)
have a recorded rationale (cost/risk > cosmetic benefit) rather than being silently
dropped.
- [x] ruff clean on the changed lines; the full reconciler apply/mutate/orchestrate
suites stay green; no behavioral diff.
</content>

# Settle 049e's one documentary claim with a live measurement

## Context

Bug `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` made the DC comment ceiling configurable (`[tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars`, default 32767) and DROPPED the idea of auto-discovering the ceiling from `/rest/api/2/application-properties`, on the grounds that the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is actually exposed requires the global "Administer Jira" permission, while rebar authenticates as an ordinary user's PAT.

**That conclusion is DOCUMENTARY, not measured.** 049e's agent tried to probe live and could not: the `tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and its README records three measured attempts where Jira never became usable within an hour on the arm64 workstation. So no 403 was ever captured. 049e's AC asked for an EMPIRICAL determination and got a documentary one; rather than tick that box on inference, the limitation was recorded and the probe deferred here.

## Why this is worth doing rather than dropping

The probe is genuinely runnable — just not on that host. The `jira-dc-harness` job in `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` runs the same harness on GitHub Actions' amd64 runners, where the image works. So this is a deferred measurement, not an impossible one.

## What it does NOT change

049e's remedy stands either way. Configuration is the correct fix whether or not the endpoint is readable: a readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery convenience on top of the config key, not invalidate it. So this ticket cannot regress 049e — it can only add an enhancement or confirm the drop. That independence is why 049e was closeable with this leg outstanding.

## Approach

Add a single cell to the live DC suite that requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` (and the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource) with the harness's ordinary non-admin PAT and RECORDS the outcome — status code and body shape — asserting only that the outcome is one of the two documented possibilities, so the cell reports a fact rather than pinning a guess.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a live DC cell requests `/rest/api/2/application-properties` with a NON-ADMIN PAT and records
      the observed status code, run id, and job name on this ticket
- [ ] the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource is probed separately, because that is where
      `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed and its permission requirement may differ
- [ ] the cell distinguishes 403 (permission, the documented expectation) from 404 (endpoint absent on
      8.17.1) from 200 (readable) — a bare non-200 assertion does NOT satisfy this
- [ ] the outcome is written back onto `049e-9fac-a821-4ea2` so its documentary claim is either
      confirmed or corrected in the record
- [ ] if the endpoint IS readable, a follow-up is filed for optional auto-discovery; 049e's config key
      remains the supported mechanism either way
baseline.summary: Probe empirically whether /rest/api/2/application-properties is readable by rebar's non-admin PAT on DC

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps
1. Push any commit to `main` (or open a PR).
2. The `verify-identity` GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`) runs the authenticated-authorship merge-gate.
3. The job fails.

**Expected:** the gate runs and does not block a landing when the project has not opted into enforcement.

**Actual (before fix):** the step exits 2 with `ticket store not found at '.../.tickets-tracker' (infrastructure issue — the tickets store is not mounted; not an authorship problem)`.

## Root Cause
Two compounding problems:
1. The workflow did a plain `actions/checkout@v5` and never mounted the `tickets` orphan branch (the store lives at the gitignored `.tickets-tracker/` worktree), so the gate exited 2.
2. The workflow forced `--require-authenticated` with no grandfather boundary, while the store holds **0 signed / 3504 unsigned** events (write-signing was scaffolded but never rolled out). So even with the store mounted the gate would fail every push by construction.

## Fix (delivered)
Enforcement posture is driven by project config, with all pre-rollout events grandfathered:
- Mount the `tickets` branch as `.tickets-tracker` before the gating step (mirrors `reconcile-bridge.yml`).
- Drop the forced `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags; the gate now honours `identity.require_authenticated` (kept OFF ⇒ advisory, exit 0) and `identity.enforce_since` (grandfather boundary) from `rebar.toml`.
- Set `identity.enforce_since` to the tracker HEAD at rollout-prep so, when signing is later enabled and the flag flipped, historical unsigned events are grandfathered and only new signed writes are enforced.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` mounts the `tickets` orphan branch as `.tickets-tracker` (full fetch + `git worktree add -B tickets .tickets-tracker origin/tickets`) before the `verify-identity (gating)` step, and the checkout uses `fetch-depth: 0`.
- [ ] The gating step invokes `rebar verify-identity` with **no** forced `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags, so posture follows config.
- [ ] `rebar.toml` has an `[identity]` block with `require_authenticated = false` and `enforce_since` pinned to a tracker-branch ref (grandfather boundary).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The `verify-identity` workflow run on `main` after this change lands shows a green (success) conclusion. Evidence: the GitHub Actions run URL + its `success` conclusion recorded as a comment.
baseline.summary: verify-identity CI gate fails on main: tickets store not mounted

# Remove the inert `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` / `bedrock_model_id` config knob

## Context / Problem

Story S3 [rebar:2932-8a98-6d70-4550] landed a `bedrock_model_id` field on `LLMConfig` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:521`), populated it from `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` and the `[tool.rebar.llm] bedrock_model_id` table key (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:633-638`), described it in the module docstring (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:21-22`), listed it in `docs/env-vars.md:55`, and duplicated its default literal into `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:38` behind a hand-sync comment.

**Nothing reads it.** A grep across `src/` and `tests/` finds no consumer other than the dataclass field declaration and the `from_env` assignment that populates it. The Bedrock model id is in fact carried by `cfg.model` as the provider-prefixed string `bedrock:<inference-profile-id>` — `providers.py` parses the provider from that prefix, and that is the path S3's own tests exercise.

So an operator who sets `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` gets **silence**: no model change, no warning, no error, and a documented env var that does nothing. This was found while checking whether the field could serve as a second model knob for the per-pass model requirement recorded on [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]; it cannot, because it is not wired at all.

**It has never shipped.** Change 1043 (which introduced it) is unsubmitted, so the defect exists only inside the in-flight epic stack and can mislead no operator until that stack lands. This ticket removes it before it ever does.

## Approach

**Delete the knob** — the field, the `from_env` wiring, the two docstring lines, the `docs/env-vars.md` row, and the duplicated literal in `bedrock_model.py` (which then needs no hand-sync comment, since the sole remaining definition is the one `bedrock_model.py` itself owns).

Deletion over wiring, for three reasons:

1. `cfg.model` ALREADY carries the Bedrock model id, and that is the tested, working path. Wiring a second
   knob means inventing precedence rules between two ways to express one value — a config ambiguity that
   would then need its own tests and documentation.
2. Nothing depends on it. Because it never shipped, removal is not a compatibility change: no configuration
   that works today stops working, since no configuration using it works today.
3. It does not serve the per-pass model work it was investigated for. That needs a per-pass MAPPING
   (Pass-1 vs Pass-2/Pass-4); a single scalar cannot express one, so keeping the field "in case" buys
   nothing concrete.

**Alternative rejected — wire it up so the documented knob works.** This adds a redundant second path to a value `cfg.model` already carries, requires precedence rules against the provider-prefixed form, and enlarges the config surface to satisfy documentation that is itself the thing in error. Fixing the docs by deleting the row is strictly smaller than fixing the code to match the docs.

**Alternative rejected — amend change 1043 so the field never appears in history.** Cleaner history, but 1043 already holds `LLM-Review +1`; amending resets that vote and forces a re-review, delaying S3's close on the epic's critical path. Because the whole stack submits together, main's landed state is identical either way.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — remove the `bedrock_model_id` field (`:521`), its `from_env` population
  (`:633-638`), and its module-docstring lines (`:21-22`).
- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — drop the "duplicated ... kept in sync by hand" rationale now that
  `config.py` no longer holds a second copy; `DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` itself STAYS (it is the live
  default this module documents as measured-working).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — remove the `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` row (`:55`).
- `tests/unit/` — the regression test below.

## Testing

Unit tier: the mechanism is config parsing, which is pure and in-process — no model call, no AWS.

- **regression (the actual defect):** setting `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` in the environment does not
  silently produce a config that claims a Bedrock model id — asserting `LLMConfig.from_env()` exposes no
  `bedrock_model_id` attribute, so a future reintroduction of an unread field fails this test.
- **collateral invariant:** the working path is untouched — a `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.
  claude-sonnet-4-6` config still resolves provider `bedrock` and that model id through `providers.py`.
- **docs/code agreement:** no `REBAR_LLM_*` name documented in `docs/env-vars.md` is absent from
  `config.py` (guards the general class of defect, not just this instance), if that check is cheap enough
  to be reliable; otherwise assert the specific name is gone from both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -r bedrock_model_id src/ docs/` returns only `bedrock_model.py`'s own
      `DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` definition and its docstring
- [ ] a test asserts `LLMConfig.from_env()` has no `bedrock_model_id` attribute when
      `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` is set in the environment
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<profile-id>` still resolves the bedrock provider and that
      model id (the working path is not collateral damage)
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` no longer lists `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`
baseline.summary: REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID is parsed and documented but read by nothing

## Context / Problem
At current origin/main commit 0f5dbc88b, Ruff ASYNC emits zero diagnostics across `src/rebar`. Ruff DTZ emits exactly three diagnostics: DTZ006 for `datetime.fromtimestamp()` and DTZ007 for `datetime.strptime()` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate_checks.py`, plus DTZ011 for `date.today()` in `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py`. The approved ratchet should land only after all three sites have explicit, tested timezone semantics.

## Dependencies and Ownership
This story has an ordering-only `depends_on` edge to `d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d` because both stories edit `pyproject.toml`; the Mypy strictness configuration lands first to avoid sibling merge conflicts. No runtime behavior in this story depends on the Mypy change. This story creates and owns `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`; `125d-ee6f-7af0-4200` depends on this story and extends that same file later.

## Approach
1. Create `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` as the owner of the shared Ruff configuration contract. This test separately asserts ASYNC selection, DTZ selection, absence of the exact Ruff security selector `S`, absence of `.semgrep.yml`, `.semgrep.yaml`, and `.semgrep/`, and absence of the literal `datetime.UTC` token from production Python files under `src/rebar`.
2. Define validation timestamp semantics as UTC. Change `validate_checks.py` to use the datetime module. Integer epoch seconds are converted with `datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(created, tz=datetime.timezone.utc)`. Persisted timestamp strings without an offset are interpreted as the event store's UTC wall time with `datetime.datetime.strptime(...).replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)`. Both paths produce the same UTC hourly cluster key.
3. Prove timezone invariance on supported POSIX/macOS platforms by running the validation behavior under at least two `TZ` values with `time.tzset()`. The test is explicitly skipped when `time.tzset` is unavailable; Windows is not a declared supported platform in `pyproject.toml`. Rejected: adding a production timezone-injection seam solely for this test, because the explicit timezone argument is directly testable and an extra API would add unused production complexity.
4. Preserve security-rule cadence as a host-local calendar-date decision. Obtain an aware current instant with an explicit `tz` argument, convert it to the host timezone, then extract its date. The implementation may use an equivalent helper or expression; the contract is the host-local date semantics plus DTZ005 compliance, not a particular line spelling. Boundary tests cover age equal to `cadence_days` and age greater than `cadence_days`.
5. Add ASYNC and DTZ to the gated Ruff selection after the tests fail against current configuration.
6. Run the focused, default, and integration pytest tiers.

The spelling `datetime.UTC` is prohibited because Ruff `target-version` remains `py310`; all production UTC construction uses `datetime.timezone.utc`. Rejected: blanket DTZ ignores.

## Scope
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` (required; created and owned by this story)
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/validate_checks.py`
- `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py`
- `tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py`
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`

## Testing / Verification
- Configuration and negative assertions: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py`
- Focused behavior: `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`
- Ruff families: `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests`
- Canonical lint: `make lint`
- Default tier: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`
- Integration tier: `pytest -m integration -q`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts ASYNC is selected by the global Ruff configuration.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts DTZ is selected by the global Ruff configuration.
- [ ] `ruff check --select ASYNC,DTZ src/rebar tests` exits 0.
- [ ] Tests prove integer epoch timestamps produce the same UTC hour cluster under at least two distinct process `TZ` settings on platforms providing `time.tzset`.
- [ ] Tests prove timezone-less persisted timestamp strings are assigned `datetime.timezone.utc` before clustering.
- [ ] A source-level AST assertion verifies the UTC-producing calls in `validate_checks.py` use `datetime.timezone.utc`; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py` executes that assertion.
- [ ] Behavioral validation tests prove the numeric and timezone-less timestamp paths produce the expected UTC cluster keys; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_validate_idea_exemptions.py` exits 0.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` recursively scans `src/rebar` Python files and fails if the literal `datetime.UTC` token is present.
- [ ] Security-pin tests prove the implementation obtains an aware current instant with an explicit timezone, converts it to the host timezone, and uses the resulting local date; `pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py` exits 0.
- [ ] `ruff check --select DTZ005 src/rebar/grounding/detectors/security_pin.py` exits 0.
- [ ] Security-pin tests prove `age_days == cadence_days` is not stale.
- [ ] Security-pin tests prove `age_days > cadence_days` is stale.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` exits 0.
- [ ] `pytest -m integration -q` exits 0.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts the exact Ruff security selector `S` is absent.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py` asserts `.semgrep.yml`, `.semgrep.yaml`, and `.semgrep/` are absent.
baseline.summary: Enable Ruff ASYNC and DTZ checks

## Context / Problem
FP verification over all 348 historical G7 findings (recorded on ticket 696a-82a4-47c5-4e54, research round 3 + operator decisions): at priority >= 0.85, 0 clearly-incorrect findings (22 CORRECT / 7 UNCLEAR across >= 0.75), with direct evidence authors revised plans in the demanded direction within minutes. The 0.80-0.85 band is empty (priorities quantize), so 0.85 selects the same historical set as 0.80 with less future exposure. G7 has never blocked because its routing entry carries default_posture "advisory" @ 0.95 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json, "G7") — a configuration artifact, the same shape the bfa8 T3/T10 enablement (commit e3962d21e) and the c97a T5c enablement (commit 623d68c4a) corrected. Two noise shapes must be fixed in the same change: an unresolvable parent is emitted as a finding instead of an abstain (observed on ticket 18f9), and same-issue duplicates stack (ticket 76d2 carried 3 findings for one contradicted parent clause). Only 3 historical findings carry plan-v4 kind grades yet — see the Monitoring note (deliberately not an AC).

## Approach
Follows the landed bfa8/c97a pattern exactly: a routing flip + rubric guidance, no pass3_decide changes, no new machinery.

(1) Routing (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json, "G7" entry): block_threshold 0.95 -> 0.85, default_posture "advisory" -> "blocking". Plan-review blocking derives ONLY from default_posture == "blocking" plus block_threshold — src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:73-77 (threshold_for, gate="plan_review"); the blocking_enabled field is the code-review gate's convention and is inert in plan review. A finding then blocks in Pass-3 when priority = validity x impact >= 0.85 (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:588, pass3_decide), threaded through the plan-review wrapper src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:756-771 (impact_fn=impact_plan).

(2) Kind scoping — provided by the EXISTING plan-v4 grading, stated exactly; no per-grade Pass-3 gate exists and none is added. G7 maps its severity onto the divergent_implementation axis (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md, kind-mapping paragraph), which impact_plan grades by DIVERGENCE KIND (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:350-357 DIVERGENCE_GRADE01/_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES; ADR 0054, commit 7d846e0c9): contradicts_reality and omits_required_site score 1.0 and hard-floor impact at 0.85 (decide.py:407-409); incomplete_enumeration contributes 0.55 (DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, pinned strictly below every blocking block_threshold by tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py:142 — note decide.py's inline comment misattributes this pin to test_impact_plan.py, which pins only UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB; the plan cites the real pin) and NEVER floors, so a cosmetic divergence cannot reach the 0.85 bar through this axis. Consequence, stated as the mechanism actually behaves: blocking @ 0.85 admits BOTH floor-grade kinds — contradicts_reality AND omits_required_site — at validity >= 0.85; an incomplete_enumeration-graded finding cannot block via the divergence axis. Restricting blocking to contradicts_reality alone (this ticket's original framing) would require per-grade gating that pass3_decide/threshold_for do not have; that machinery is REJECTED because (a) the landed precedents scope by guidance not machinery, (b) the FP evidence is kind-blind — 0 clearly-incorrect across ALL 348 historical findings at >= 0.85, so it supports blocking the whole band, and (c) ADR 0054 deliberately gives omits_required_site the floor (an omitted required site is the exact harm class the grading exists to catch), while the rubric fixes in (3) remove the known omission-side FP shapes (sibling handoff, closed parent). A one-sentence rubric guidance (the bfa8 T10 pattern) reinforces the kind mapping: only a genuine contract contradiction or a provably required omission is a floor kind; cosmetic/wording mismatches are incomplete_enumeration — coached, never auto-blocked.

(3) Rubric fixes (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md):
- FAIL-OPEN (abstain-with-coverage), the T13/T14 pattern (see src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T14.md FAIL-OPEN paragraph): a parent that cannot be resolved via show_ticket ABSTAINS with a covered-but-unverified note — never a finding.
- CLOSED parent: its contract is checked against its FINAL (as-closed) state, and scope the parent explicitly handed to sibling tickets is NOT a leaf violation (consistent narrowing remains a non-finding).
- DEDUP-AT-SOURCE, the c97a T5c pattern (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md "DEDUP-AT-SOURCE"): emit at most ONE finding per contradicted parent clause; additional manifestations fold into that finding's evidence. Rubric-only: the deterministic discovery-stage dedup (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:252-284, dedup_key/suppress_and_dedup) collapses only identical (criteria, location, body) triples and cannot recognize same-clause paraphrases, and no LLM-free same-clause detector is feasible — so decide.py is deliberately NOT touched (dropped from this ticket's earlier scope).

(4) Tests and pins: all THREE pinned blocking-set assertions gain G7 — tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py EXPECTED_ROUTING ("G7": (0.85, "blocking")) and the blocking-set assertion at test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking — G7 enters via a NEW `G7_BLOCKING = {"G7": 0.85}` constant added to the set-union expression (`... | set(PILOT_BLOCKING) | set(G7_BLOCKING) | ...`); G7 is deliberately NOT added to PILOT_BLOCKING because test_routing_posture_blocking_at_090 parametrizes over that dict asserting block_threshold == 0.90 — and tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING. Additionally tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py::test_g7_posture_is_advisory_at_0_95 hard-asserts the OLD posture (default_posture 'advisory', block_threshold 0.95) and is renamed/updated to test_g7_posture_is_blocking_at_085 asserting the new (0.85, 'blocking') pair. New tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py follows tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py: findings driven through the REAL orchestrator.pass3_over_findings wrapper with the REAL impact_plan (no impact monkeypatch — the kind grades themselves produce the impact).

(5) Regenerate docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md via `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` and commit the output.

Alternatives rejected: 0.80 threshold (admits future validity-0.80 findings with no historical quality evidence; the 0.80-0.85 band is empty so 0.85 loses nothing); per-grade Pass-3 gating (new cross-gate kernel machinery for a restriction the evidence does not demand — see (2)).

Monitoring note (explicitly NOT an acceptance criterion): re-run the FP classification once >= 20 kind-graded G7 findings have accumulated in the REVIEW_RESULT corpus; the zero-LLM criterion-effectiveness recorder already tracks blocking outcomes (same monitoring stance as the bfa8 pilot). Record the recheck on this ticket's close notes.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (G7 entry only), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md, tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py (new), tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py, tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py, tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py (posture pin updated), docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md (regenerated). NOT touched: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py, src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py, the verifier prompts.

## Testing
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/plan_review/test_g7_blocking.py tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py -v`, then the full `tests/unit` suite. Cases: threshold_for(["G7"], registry.by_id(), gate="plan_review") == (0.85, True); a G7 finding graded contradicts_reality with an all-yes graded binary BLOCKS (impact 1.0, priority 1.0); the same finding marked self_revealing floors to impact 0.85 -> priority 0.85 -> BLOCKS (exact-boundary case, priority >= block_threshold); omits_required_site all-yes BLOCKS (floor kind, pinned deliberately); incomplete_enumeration all-yes lands impact 0.55 / priority 0.55 -> ADVISORY; a floor-kind finding at validity 0.8889 with self-revealing impact 0.85 -> priority 0.7556 -> ADVISORY (the validity guard); rubric-text assertions for the abstain-with-coverage, closed-parent + sibling-handoff, one-per-clause dedup, and floor-kind guidance sentences.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] criteria_routing.json "G7" carries default_posture "blocking" with block_threshold 0.85 (checked: test_g7_blocking.py asserts threshold_for(["G7"], registry.by_id(), gate="plan_review") == (0.85, True)).
- [ ] Through the real plan-review Pass-3 wrapper with the real impact_plan, a contradicts_reality-graded G7 finding at validity 1.0 BLOCKS (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] Through the same wrapper, an omits_required_site-graded G7 finding at validity 1.0 BLOCKS (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] Through the same wrapper, an incomplete_enumeration-graded G7 finding stays ADVISORY at priority 0.55 (checked: test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] The G7 rubric contains each of the four new rule sentences: abstain-on-unresolvable-parent (never a finding); closed-parent-final-state + sibling-handoff; one-finding-per-contradicted-parent-clause; floor-kind guidance (checked: one rubric-text assertion per sentence in test_g7_blocking.py).
- [ ] The pinned routing table, the pinned blocking-set union (via the new G7_BLOCKING constant), the _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING set, and the test_plan_review_g7.py posture pin each reflect G7 at (0.85, "blocking") (checked: test_threshold_recalibration.py, test_impact_model_versioning.py, test_plan_review_g7.py all pass).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md is regenerated (checked: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` produces no diff on the committed tree).
baseline.summary: G7 floor-grade divergence blocking at 0.85 plus abstain and dedup fixes

content.text: ## Summary
REBAR_MCP_READONLY=TRUE (or True/YES) silently disables the readonly gate — the membership test is case-sensitive.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. REBAR_MCP_READONLY=TRUE; build_server().
2. list_tools() -> all 14 write tools exposed.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: common truthy spellings enable the gate; an operator setting TRUE believes the server is read-only.
- Actual: mcp_server.py:115-116 tests membership in ("1","true","yes") without .lower(); TRUE fails open (the dangerous direction).
## Source
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:115-116 (_readonly)
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:271-273 — REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE uses the same parse; its failure direction is safe (stricter) but fix both for consistency.
## Fix direction
.strip().lower() before the membership test in one tiny _env_truthy helper used by both checks.
## Suggested RED test
Parametrize TRUE/True/YES/Yes/1/yes/true -> all readonly (write tools hidden); ""/0/no -> not readonly.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Case-insensitive truthy parse for REBAR_MCP_READONLY and REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE
- [ ] RED parametrized test first
- [ ] Documented accepted values in README/CLAUDE.md

baseline.summary: REBAR_MCP_READONLY=TRUE (uppercase) silently disables the readonly gate

## Why

`verify.require_signature_for_close` (default False, OFF in this project) is the
"signature close gate" — it requires an HMAC signature BEFORE closing a work ticket.
It is documented as the ALTERNATIVE to `require_completion_verification_for_close`,
which is what THIS project actually uses (enabling both deadlocks a non-force close).
It has never been used here and is a retired alternative. Remove it and the close-gate
code reachable ONLY through it.

## What

Delete (reachable only via this gate):
- `resolve_signature_gate` — `_commands/gates.py:58-80` (whole function).
- `_signature_gate` — `_commands/txn.py:311-410` (whole function) + its two CommandErrors
  ("requires a certified signature (verdict: …)" and the "made at a different commit"
  HEAD-binding error).
- `transition_core` plumbing: the `sig_require`/`sig_config_error` locals + the
  `resolve_signature_gate` call (`txn.py:182-187`) and the story/epic close-gate block
  (`txn.py:250-260`).
- Config field + validator (`_config_schema.py:210`, `:485`).
- True-path tests: `test_signature.py:312`, `test_close_gate_story_epic.py:38,116`,
  `test_idea_close_bypass.py:27` (rewrite — bypass logic changes); trim flag-specific
  assertions in `test_config_typed.py`, `test_config_perf.py`, `test_config_backcompat.py`;
  regenerate golden CLI help (`transition__*help.out`).

## Scope — MUST PRESERVE

The entire shared HMAC signing/attestation substrate: `signing.py` (`signing_key`,
`verify_record`, `most_recent_attestation`, `head_sha`, `verify_signature`), the
`attestations` map, `sign_manifest`/`verify_signature` MCP tools, and the
completion-verifier close path (`transition_close.py`) + plan-review claim gate — all
share this machinery and must keep working. `--force-close` and `--verdict-hash` are
NOT owned by this gate — keep both. Docs handled by the doc-sweep story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `require_signature_for_close` removed from schema, parser, and any docs/help (coordinated with the doc-sweep story).
- [ ] `resolve_signature_gate` and `_signature_gate` deleted; the story/epic close path no longer references a signature gate.
- [ ] Shared signing machinery intact: plan-review claim gate and completion-verifier close gate both still function (prove with their existing tests green).
- [ ] `--force-close` / `--verdict-hash` unaffected; true-path tests removed/rewritten; golden help regenerated.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

content.text: Add an atomic `idea` command on all three surfaces (CLI, MCP, library) that creates
an `epic` in status `idea` in a single genesis CREATE event.
## Why
Capturing an idea must be one race-free operation. A create-then-transition path
would momentarily leave the ticket in `open` (claimable by a parallel agent, the
anti-pattern `claim` already forbids), so the idea must be born in `idea` via a
single CREATE event. The command is intentionally light: title plus an optional
description only.
## Prerequisite (depends on S1, 81b4-985e-b3e8-4026)
This story requires the status-vocabulary story to land FIRST: `idea` must be a
recognized status value (added to the `TicketStatus` literal and to
`_VALID_STATUSES`) before this command is coherent. Without S1, a created
idea-status ticket is inconsistent with the type surface, and the transitions
exercised by the end-to-end smoke test below (`transition idea open`,
`transition idea closed`) are rejected by the existing `_validate_status` guard.
A `depends_on` link to S1 is already recorded. This story's own deliverable — the
command emitting a single CREATE event carrying `status=idea` for an `epic` — does
not itself modify the status vocabulary; it consumes what S1 establishes.
## What
- Have `process_create` honor an optional `status` on the CREATE event, defaulting
to `open` when absent — completing the one CREATE field the reducer does not
currently read. The `idea` command is the sole producer of a non-`open` genesis
status; no general `create --status` flag is added.
- Add the CLI command `rebar idea "<title>" [--description=…]` creating an `epic`
in status `idea`.
- Add the MCP write tool `create_idea` with the same behavior.
- Add the library entry point `rebar.idea(...)` with the same behavior.
- Suppress the create-time "non-bug ticket lacks file_impact" stderr warning for
idea-created epics.
- Document `rebar idea` / `create_idea` / `rebar.idea` in the command/tool
references and note in `docs/event-schema.md` that a CREATE event may carry
`status`.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — `process_create` honors optional `status`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/idea.py` — new atomic CLI command.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — `rebar.idea(...)` library entry point.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — `create_idea` MCP write tool.
- `docs/event-schema.md` and command/tool reference docs.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `process_create` sets `status` from the CREATE event data when present.
- [ ] `process_create` defaults `status` to `open` when the CREATE event omits it.
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>"` creates a ticket of type `epic`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` has status `idea`.
- [ ] The ticket created by `rebar idea` is produced by a single CREATE event with
no intervening STATUS event (test inspects the event log).
- [ ] `rebar idea "<title>" --description=TEXT` records TEXT as the description.
- [ ] The MCP `create_idea` tool creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one CREATE
event.
- [ ] The library `rebar.idea(...)` creates an `epic` in status `idea` in one
CREATE event.
- [ ] No surface gains a general `create --status` flag.
- [ ] The create-time file_impact stderr warning does not fire for a ticket created
by `rebar idea`.
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` states that a CREATE event may carry `status`.
- [ ] The command/tool reference lists `rebar idea`, `create_idea`, and
`rebar.idea`.
- [ ] After S1 (status vocabulary) and S2 (close-bypass) have landed, an
end-to-end smoke test demonstrates the user-facing flow: `rebar idea`
creates a ticket absent from `ready`/`next-batch`; `transition idea open`
promotes it to claimable work; `transition idea closed` succeeds with no
completion-gate error. (This AC is gated on the S1/S2 prerequisite above.)
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.

baseline.summary: Add atomic 'idea' command (CLI/MCP/library) creating an epic in status idea
