# S3 — First-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching

## Context / Problem

rebar has no Bedrock path. Our clients will reach Claude through Bedrock more often than through the direct Anthropic API, and PR #121's answer — front Bedrock with an OpenAI-compatible gateway — forces every operator to stand up and accredit a proxy, and gives up prompt caching, the retrying transport, and native structured output in the process.

## Approach

Register a `bedrock` builder in the provider factory [rebar:7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1] that constructs pydantic-ai's native `BedrockConverseModel` with a `BedrockProvider`, authenticating through the ambient AWS credential chain (instance role in production, `AWS_PROFILE`/env locally) — no rebar-managed key. Prompt caching is already selected by the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` capability shipped in story f184, which sets **exactly two** keys — `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions`. An earlier draft of this plan named a third (`bedrock_cache_messages`); that is **rejected** for parity, because the direct-Anthropic path sets only the matching two and `AnthropicModelSettings.anthropic_cache_messages` is likewise left unset. Enabling message caching on Bedrock alone would make it cache MORE than Anthropic, which is a new behaviour with its own cost and TTL profile — a separate decision with its own measurement, not a third key smuggled in here. The parity bar in story 0d76 is measured against exactly these two keys. Ships as a new `[bedrock]` optional extra (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`) so boto3 stays out of the default `[agents]` install; the builder raises a clear missing-extra error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

**Caching HAS been measured (real AWS, us-east-2, account 5797…98).** The measurement is done; this section records the results and the decisions they force, so no implementer has to guess. Oracle: the same request twice with a `cachePoint` after a ~4000-token stable system prefix, reading `cacheReadInputTokens` / `cacheWriteInputTokens` off the real Converse response.

1. **On-demand model ids are not invokable at all** in this account/region — both
   `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` and the older `anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` return
   `ValidationException: Invocation of model ID … with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request
   with the ID or ARN of an inference profile.` So this story's original on-demand-vs-profile comparison is
   moot: **only inference profiles work**, and rebar's documented default must be one.
2. **A regional inference profile DOES cache.** `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`: attempt 1
   `cache_write=4017, cache_read=0`; attempt 2 `cache_write=0, cache_read=4017`; reproducible across runs (a
   later run hit a still-warm cache, 5-minute TTL). This **refutes the premise of pydantic-ai #4381** for this
   model/region — the issue this story was built around does not reproduce.
3. **Caching is MODEL-dependent and fails SILENTLY.** `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` and
   `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` both report `cache_read=0` AND `cache_write=0` on both
   attempts, billing the full 4029 input tokens every call — no error, no warning. A controlled same-model
   comparison (`us.` vs `global.`) showed BOTH fail, so the discriminator is the **model**, not the profile
   prefix. Silent full-price billing is the real hazard here.
4. `us.anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0` with a `cachePoint` hard-fails:
   `AccessDeniedException: You invoked an unsupported model or your request did not allow prompt caching.`

**Decision A — the default is `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`**, the verified-caching regional inference profile. Config accepts any profile id; this is what the docs recommend and what the parity story measures.

**Decision B — rebar must WARN when caching was requested but both counters are zero.** Because failure is silent, an operator otherwise pays full input price on every call forever with no signal.

**It cannot reuse `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, and that is the whole point of specifying it.** That guard fires on `requests > 0 AND input_tokens == 0 AND output_tokens == 0` — the zeroed-adapter case. The measured Bedrock failure is the opposite shape: `input_tokens=4029` (a perfectly healthy count) with `cache_read=0` and `cache_write=0`. The existing predicate never fires, so extending it would silently do nothing.

A SEPARATE helper is required, with this predicate:

    caching_requested AND usage.cache_read_tokens == 0 AND usage.cache_write_tokens == 0 AND usage.input_tokens > 0

- "caching_requested" is embodied by the existing local the runner already computes for the cache gate —
  `cache_settings is not None` (equivalently `caps.prompt_cache_style != "none"`). No new state is needed.
- It is invoked at the same seam as `_warn_if_zeroed_usage`, i.e. after `_extract_usage()` on the success path,
  and is gated on `self._model_override is None` for the same reason that guard is (test doubles report no usage).
- WARNING level, observability only, NEVER blocking — an ineffective cache is a cost problem, not a correctness
  one, and must not fail a gate run.
- The message must name the model id and both counters, so the operator can act (switch to a
  measured-caching model id) rather than merely learn that something is wrong.

### Decision C — `temperature` is FATAL on Bedrock for some models (found by measurement, not in the original plan)

`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` with `temperature=0` returns **400 `ValidationException: temperature is deprecated for this model`**; the identical call without it succeeds. Reproduced through pydantic-ai as well: `BedrockConverseModel` + `BedrockModelSettings(temperature=0.0)` → `ModelHTTPError` 400.

This breaks rebar's gates on Bedrock, not just a corner case: `runner.py` sets `model_settings["temperature"]` whenever `cfg.temperature`/`req.config.temperature` is set, and the plan-review **Pass-2 verifiers deliberately send `temperature=0`** so re-verifying a finding does not resample. Critically, `_drop_unsupported_sampling_settings` exists ONLY in pydantic-ai's `models/anthropic.py`, **not** in `models/bedrock.py` — so the direct-Anthropic path degrades gracefully (warning: "Sampling parameters ['temperature'] are not supported … will be ignored") and the Bedrock path hard-fails.

**Decision: carry it as a capability — but f184's override table must first learn the MODEL NAME.**

An earlier draft of this decision said "add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models". That is **not implementable as f184 shipped**, and the gap is worth stating precisely: f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates receive only the `ModelProfile`, and `BedrockModelProfile` carries **no per-model identifier** (verified: no model/name attribute on the profile object). So the only predicate expressible today is "is this Bedrock-hosted Claude", which would strip `temperature` from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` too — the measured-good default — destroying exactly the greedy Pass-2 determinism this decision exists to protect.

So this story adds a SEPARATE, additive table rather than changing f184's contract. f184 is **closed and its plan-review attestation is signed**, and it defines its override predicates as `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`; widening that signature would silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is that the parent wins, so f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` and its `_is_claude` predicate are left **exactly** as shipped.

1. Add `supports_temperature: bool = True` to `ModelCapabilities`.
2. Add a **second, distinct** override table, `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES: dict[str, Mapping[str, object]]`,
   keyed on the **exact** model id, applied AFTER the profile-shaped overrides. The two tables encode genuinely
   different things and are better apart than merged: f184's keys on *capability shape* (what kind of model is
   this), this one keys on *a specific model's API defect* (this exact id rejects a parameter).
3. Keys are **exact-set membership, never prefix matching**. That is both cleaner — only model ids whose
   behaviour has actually been MEASURED get an entry, so the table never speculates — and it preserves f184's
   attested criterion that `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is empty.
4. **`capabilities_for()`'s BODY changes; its public signature does not.** An earlier draft said "no signature
   change is needed anywhere", which misleadingly implied no change at all. To be exact — the shipped body reads
   only `getattr(model_or_model_string, "profile", None)` and, for strings, `partition(":")`; it never touches
   `model_name`. The required edit, stated as control flow so nothing is left to inference:

   - the private helper becomes `_capabilities_from_profile(profile, model_id: str | None)` — a PRIVATE helper,
     so this is not the signed `_REBAR_OVERRIDES`/`capabilities_for` contract f184 attested;
   - **path 1 (model object):** `model_id = getattr(model_or_model_string, "model_name", None)` (verified: a
     `BedrockConverseModel` returns e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), passed alongside the profile;
   - **path 2 (model string):** the id is the value `partition(":")` ALREADY produces — reuse it, do not re-parse;
   - **path 3 (conservative fallback):** no id is available, so no model-id override applies — the conservative
     record is returned unchanged, exactly as today;
   - **ordering inside the helper:** derive the fields from the profile, apply f184's profile-shaped
     `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` first (unchanged, first-match-wins), THEN apply
     `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES.get(model_id, {})` on top, so an exact-id entry wins over a shape-based one.
     A model id absent from the table changes nothing.

   `capabilities_for()`'s own parameter list, and f184's predicate signature, both stay as shipped.
5. `runner.py` omits `temperature` from `model_settings` when the capability is False, logging once at INFO that
   it did and why.

**This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate, not a relapse.** The epic's criterion forbids selecting *provider behaviour* by matching a *provider-name* string; recording a known per-model API defect is a different thing, and it is what pydantic-ai itself does — its profile functions dispatch on `model_name` (`anthropic_model_profile(model_name)`), and upstream's own `anthropic_disallows_sampling_settings` flag exists for exactly this class of quirk on the Anthropic side.

**Honest limitation: the list will drift** as AWS deprecates sampling parameters on more models, and an unlisted-but-affected model still hard-fails. A denylist is chosen over an allowlist because an unknown-but-affected model then fails LOUDLY, whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an unknown-but-fine model and let verdicts resample — a quiet correctness risk is worse than a loud configuration error.

#### The drift mitigation, specified (catch site, predicate, output)

An earlier draft promised to "translate a 400 naming a sampling parameter into an actionable error" without saying where or how, which is not implementable. Concretely:

**Catch site.** `runner.run()`'s existing `except Exception as exc` block (the one that wraps a systemic provider failure into `LLMUnavailableError`). The translation is attempted FIRST; only if it returns `None` does the existing `LLMUnavailableError` path run unchanged. Nothing else about that handler moves.

**Where the helper lives.** A new provider-AGNOSTIC function in the existing `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (already rebar's failure-classification seam):

    translate_sampling_parameter_rejection(exc, model_id: str) -> LLMConfigError | None

It must NOT live in the Bedrock leaf and must NOT introduce a provider-name branch in `runner.py` — the epic's criterion forbids that, and any provider could in principle reject a sampling parameter. It keys on the ERROR CONTENT, never on the provider name.

**Detection predicate**, grounded in the measured strings rather than invented. boto3 raises `ValidationException: The model returned the following errors: 'temperature' is deprecated for this model.`; through pydantic-ai the same failure surfaces as `ModelHTTPError: status_code: 400, model_name: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7, body: {'Error': {'Message': ...}}`. So the predicate is, on the exception or its `__cause__`:

- it looks like a client request rejection — `getattr(exc, "status_code", None) == 400` OR `"ValidationException"`
  appears in `str(exc)`; AND
- `str(exc)` mentions one of the sampling parameters rebar can send — `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`; AND
- it mentions a rejection word — `deprecated`, `not supported`, or `unsupported`.

All three conjuncts are required, so an unrelated 400 (a malformed request, a bad model id) is NOT swallowed and keeps its existing `LLMUnavailableError` classification.

**Output.** An `LLMConfigError` naming (a) the model id, (b) the offending parameter, and (c) BOTH remedies: add the id to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` with `supports_temperature=False`, or unset the temperature config. The whole point is that the operator learns what to change, not merely that something failed.

Rejected alternatives: dropping temperature on ALL Bedrock calls (loses Pass-2 greedy determinism on the measured-good default); catching the 400 and retrying without it (burns a billable, often multi-minute agentic call and keys on model-specific error text).

Note this also widens f184's signed capability record, which story 343b stamps into the verdict sidecar — doing it now is cheaper than after that payload shape is signed in the field. It directly de-risks story eb6e (the production review-bot cutover with no Anthropic fallback), which would otherwise hard-fail on such a model.

**Alternative rejected:** OpenAI-compatible gateway fronting Bedrock (PR #121). No proxy is needed for the native path, and the gateway path measurably loses caching and native structured output.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` (**new leaf**, mirroring `anthropic_model.py`) — the `bedrock` builder and
  its `BedrockProvider`/`BedrockConverseModel` construction. It does NOT go in `providers.py`: that file is at
  289 LOC against the **300-LOC cap that is an attested criterion of closed story 7468**, so the builder
  would breach a signed criterion. `providers.py` gains only the one-line registry entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — `supports_temperature` on the record plus a NEW exact-id
  `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` table (Decision C). f184's `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicate signature and
  `_is_claude` are left UNCHANGED — that contract is closed and signed. The profile override for Bedrock-hosted Claude and the `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"`
  cache-settings selection are **ALREADY SHIPPED by closed story f184** — verify, do not re-add.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — omit `temperature` when the capability withdraws it, and add the Decision B
  cache-zero warning. **BLOCKED ON task `2682-b015-4fe5-4066` (the runner.py split), which MUST land first.**
  Both additions are strictly positive LOC and `runner.py` is at EXACTLY the 800-LOC hard cap, so there is no
  net-neutral way to make them: an earlier draft said "net-neutral or the split lands first" without naming
  a dependency, which left an implementer facing a signed-criterion conflict with no resolution. The split is
  now a recorded blocking edge, not an aspiration. Story `343b` (verdict provenance) needs the same headroom.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — Bedrock region + model-id/inference-profile config keys.
- `pyproject.toml` — a `[bedrock]` optional extra (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`), AND that same extra added to
  the **`dev`** extra so this story's unit tests actually RUN in CI rather than skipping.

  The runtime posture is unchanged and that is the point: `[agents]` does not gain boto3, so
  `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still has no AWS dependency (an explicit AC below). But `BedrockConverseModel`
  and `BedrockModelSettings` are unimportable without it, so without the dev entry every builder-construction
  assertion would be `importorskip`-ed away in CI and the criteria would only ever be provable on a developer's
  machine. This is the SAME precedent story `dc0d` set for `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`, and the same one `mcp`
  already sets — an optional runtime extra that `dev` installs so its tests are real. Note most of this story's
  new logic (the `supports_temperature` override, the cache-zero warning, the 400 translation) is deliberately
  testable with profile STUBS and needs no boto3 at all; only construction does.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated.
- `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` (new); `tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py` (new, env-gated).

  **It MUST live under `tests/external/`, not a new `tests/live/`.** An earlier draft said `tests/live/`,
  which does not exist and would have been a live landmine: `tests/conftest.py` (a) auto-applies the
  `external` marker to every item under `tests/external/`, and (b) HARD-FAILS collection for any item marked
  `external` that lives outside it. A canary at `tests/live/` would therefore either be collected by the
  default CI selection (`-m "not integration and not external"`) and make billable AWS calls on every CI
  run, or — if marked `external` by hand — break collection for the WHOLE suite. Existing precedents to
  follow: `tests/external/test_completion_pass_live.py`, `tests/external/test_deps_live.py`.

## Testing

Two tiers, because the mechanism spans a pure construction path and a real external service.

- Unit (construction, mocked boto3 client): the builder produces a `BedrockConverseModel` whose settings carry
  **exactly the two** `bedrock_cache_*` keys the parity decision above fixes —
  `bedrock_cache_instructions` and `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions` — and NOT `bedrock_cache_messages`; a plain on-demand id and an inference-profile ARN both construct; a missing
  `[bedrock]` extra raises `LLMConfigError` naming the install command. Contrast case: an `anthropic` model
  still gets `anthropic_cache_*`, never `bedrock_cache_*`.
- Live canary (env-gated, `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK=1`, skipped in default CI): issue the same cached-prefix request
  twice and assert `usage.cache_read_tokens > 0` on the second — the observable oracle for "caching works".
  Run it for both the on-demand id and the inference-profile ARN and record both results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<claude-id> rebar review-plan <ticket>` completes with a valid structured verdict
      against real Bedrock, output attached as a comment on this ticket
- [x] **MEASURED** — the cache canary result is recorded on this ticket: on-demand ids are not invokable at all
      here; `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caches (`cache_write=4017` then `cache_read=4017`, reproducible);
      `us.`/`global.` opus-4-5 silently do not cache. rebar documents `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` as the
      default
- [ ] a test asserts rebar WARNS when caching was requested but both cache counters are zero (Decision B),
      since the failure is otherwise silent and bills full input every call
- [ ] a test asserts `temperature` is omitted for a model whose `supports_temperature` capability is False,
      and still sent for one where it is True (Decision C) — the contrast case
- [ ] unit tests pass with no AWS credentials present (boto3 client mocked), proving default CI is unaffected
- [ ] the live canary lives under `tests/external/` and is EXCLUDED by the default selection
      `-m "not integration and not external"` — verified by confirming the default suite's collected count is
      unchanged by its addition, so CI never makes a billable AWS call
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar[agents]` still installs without boto3 (`python -c "import boto3"` fails in that env)
- [ ] f184's shipped contract is untouched: `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` predicates still take a single `ModelProfile`
      argument and `grep -n 'startswith' src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` is still empty
- [ ] a test asserts a provider error matching the MEASURED shape (400 / ValidationException + a sampling
      parameter name + a rejection word) becomes an `LLMConfigError` naming the model id, the parameter, and
      both remedies — and a CONTRAST case asserts an unrelated 400 still becomes `LLMUnavailableError`, so the
      translation cannot swallow unrelated failures
- [ ] `grep -n 'bedrock\|anthropic' src/rebar/llm/failure.py` shows no provider-name branch — the translation
      keys on error CONTENT only
- [ ] a test asserts the conservative-fallback path still returns the unchanged conservative record when no
      model id is available (the third path above), so adding the second table cannot alter it
- [ ] a test asserts an exact-id override WINS over a profile-shaped one for the same model (ordering)
- [ ] a t … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: S3 — first-class AWS Bedrock provider (native, no gateway) with measured prompt caching

# Replace the tests that cannot fail

## Context

A parity audit found several tests in both suites whose assertions cannot fail. Each was verified by reading the body and the code under test — this list is evidence, not suspicion. They are worse than missing tests: a missing test is visible in a coverage gap, a vacuous one reports coverage it does not provide, and each of these carries a docstring promising a contract it never checks.

## The confirmed list

**1. `test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py` — `test_the_pat_never_appears_in_the_repr_of_the_transport`. A tautology.** Body: `t = JiraDataCenterTransport(client=object(), project="DC")` then `assert "pat-xyz" not in repr(t)`. The constructor takes `client`/`project`/`resolved_statuses` and **never receives a PAT at all**; and the class defines no `__repr__`, so `repr(t)` is `<...object at 0x...>`. The literal `"pat-xyz"` IS used elsewhere in the same module (`:59`, `:72`, `:87`, `:98`, `:100`) as the PAT fixture fed to `build_client_from_settings` — but it never reaches the `JiraDataCenterTransport(...)` this test constructs, which is exactly why the assertion is vacuous. It would pass unchanged if the transport stored and printed a credential. Its docstring — "a credential that leaks into logs via repr is a real disclosure path" — describes a real risk that is not tested.

**2. `test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — `test_the_structural_guard_fires_on_a_synthetic_unpaginated_caller`.** Docstring claims to be "TEETH for the guard itself", but the body RE-IMPLEMENTS the AST predicate inline (`:187-195`) instead of calling `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` — the module's own audit helper, defined at `:145` and used by the real guard at `:172`. (It is a TEST-module helper, not production code; the guard it backs is itself a test.) The teeth test never touches the predicate it claims to verify; if that predicate regressed, this stays green. It can only fail if `ast` itself breaks.

**The obvious fix does not work as-is, and that is part of this item's scope.** `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` takes NO arguments and hardcodes `ast.parse(_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text())` at `:152` — the LIVE transport file. Simply calling it from the teeth test would scan the real transport, which is currently clean, so the teeth test would pass regardless of whether the predicate works — the exact vacuity being fixed, reintroduced. The helper must first be parameterized — an optional source argument (e.g. `src: str | None = None`) falling back to `_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()` — so the real guard at `:172` keeps calling it with NO argument and unchanged behaviour, while the teeth test hands it the synthetic unpaginated source and asserts the predicate REPORTS the offender. Two things that look like fixes but preserve the defect: adding a SECOND standalone predicate for the synthetic case (that is the duplication-drift class sibling story bd9e exists to remove), and asserting only that the helper RUNS on the synthetic input, which `return []` already satisfies.

**3. `test_transport_port_completeness_heldout.py` — `test_validate_assignee_exists_returns_the_dc_username`.** The name and docstring promise the RETURN-VALUE contract ("returning `True`, or an accountId-shaped value, corrupts the identity"). The body is `assert hasattr(cls, "validate_assignee_exists")` — already asserted verbatim by the parametrized presence test in the same file. Zero incremental coverage, and **nothing anywhere asserts DC's `validate_assignee_exists` returns a username string rather than a bool.** This one is a real gap wearing a test's clothes.

**4. `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py` — the enumerated-mutations sweep. MINE, from this epic's S2, and the criticism is correct.** It asserts `total <= 1` client calls per member. `total == 0` satisfies that — so a member that raises BEFORE reaching the client (an `AttributeError`, a pre-flight `ValueError`) never exercises the 429 branch and still passes. `total == 1` is the assertion with teeth. The `pytest.raises(Exception)` also carries a comment claiming "the TYPE is asserted per-member below" when the code below only checks counts; the comment overstates what the test does.

**5. `test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py` — `test_an_unknown_backend_raises_the_registry_error_not_key_error`.** Never calls `select_backend`; asserts only `not issubclass(BackendRegistryError, KeyError)`. Real, but far narrower than its name — it pins a class relationship, not the raising behaviour.

## Approach

For each: decide whether the CONTRACT the docstring names is worth testing. Where it is (1, 3, 4), write the test the docstring already promises. Where the vacuity is structural (2), point the test at the shared audit helper it is supposed to be testing — parameterizing that helper first, since as written it cannot see the synthetic source. Where the name overreaches the assertion (5), either broaden the test or narrow the name — do not leave the two disagreeing.

**Do not simply delete them.** Each names a real property; deleting would lose the intent that the docstring captured. The intent is the valuable part and it should end up asserted.

## Scope

The five tests above. If the fix to (3) reveals that `validate_assignee_exists` does NOT return a username on some path, that is a bug ticket, not a silent expectation adjustment.

## Testing

Each rewritten test must be MUTATION-CHECKED against the property it now claims — that is the whole point of this story, and a rewrite that is merely longer has not improved anything.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the PAT-repr test constructs a transport that ACTUALLY carries a credential and asserts the
      credential's own value is absent from `repr` — mutation-checked by adding a `__repr__` that
      leaks it
- [ ] `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()`
      (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:145`) takes an optional source argument falling back
      to `_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()`, leaving the real guard's call at `:172` behaviourally
      unchanged — and there is still exactly ONE such predicate in the module
- [ ] the structural-guard teeth test calls that SHARED predicate with the SYNTHETIC unpaginated
      source instead of re-implementing the AST walk inline, and asserts it REPORTS the offender
      (not merely that it returns a list, which `return []` satisfies). MUTATION: break the
      PREDICATE — not the fixture — e.g. make `offenders` always empty, or drop `"max_results"` from
      the accepted keyword set, and confirm the teeth test goes RED. Mutating the fixture only
      proves the fixture is unpaginated, which nobody doubts
- [ ] `validate_assignee_exists` is asserted to return the USERNAME STRING for both backends, not
      merely to exist; if any path returns a bool or an accountId-shaped value, a bug is filed.
      MUTATION: make the stub return `True` (and separately an accountId-shaped
      `"5b10a2844c20165700ede21g"`) and confirm the assertion goes RED for each
- [ ] the rate-limit sweep asserts `total == 1` per member — NOT `total <= 1`, because `0` satisfies
      `<=` and means the 429 branch was never reached — AND replaces the blanket
      `pytest.raises(Exception)` at `test_dc_rate_limit_retry_heldout.py:138` with the specific
      escaping type, `pytest.raises(BackendHTTPError)`, asserting `.code == 429` per member. The
      `# noqa: B017` and the now-true "the TYPE is asserted per-member below" comment go away with
      it. Correcting the comment WITHOUT asserting the type does NOT satisfy this criterion.
      MUTATION: restore `total <= 1` and make one member raise before it reaches the client (e.g.
      a pre-flight `ValueError`), and confirm the `== 1` form goes RED where `<= 1` stayed green
- [ ] the unknown-backend test either exercises `select_backend` (preferred) or is renamed to what
      it actually pins, so name and assertion agree. MUTATION: if it was broadened, point it at a
      backend name that DOES resolve and confirm it goes RED; if it was renamed instead, record
      that no behavioural mutation applies because the test pins only a class relationship
- [ ] every rewritten test is mutation-checked with the mutation and verdict recorded on this ticket
baseline.summary: Replace the tests that cannot fail (both suites)

AND `identity.signing_key`/`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` points to that identity's OpenSSH
PRIVATE key (`_commands/_seam.py:264-325`). Gate-exempt types: session_log, code_review,
identity.

## What (delivered via child tasks)

   is empty; only an HMAC key + Gerrit deploy key exist). Generate an ed25519 keypair,
   create the identity ticket (email `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`), TOFU-register the
   public key. Shared by AWS + GitHub.
2. **Local dev** — per-developer identity + key + docs.

   work tickets (non-exempt) so it MUST sign; the review-bot writes only exempt types.

   stamps no author fields; route it through the seam (or stamp+sign) + inject the key.

content.text: ## Why

Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S2. The voter fail-closes with HTTP 409 on any merge commit today (`gerrit_client.get_patch` — "Revision has more than 1 parent"), blocking the pattern; and `patch?parent=1` would review the ENTIRE feature (violates R1). The bot needs a distinct merge-change path reviewing ONLY the auto-merge delta (conflict resolutions), fail-closed preserved.
## What

**FIRST (riskiest assumption):** capture a live fixture from the running Gerrit 3.14.1 proving `files/` with no `parent` returns the auto-merge-base file map for a merge commit (fixture committed to tests; cite rest-api-changes.html#list-files).

- `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`: merge detection (`revisions/{rev}/commit` parents >= 2) INSIDE `review_and_vote`, after the existing-vote check, BEFORE any diff fetch — identical for webhook, reconciler-backfill, and /rerun (reconcile.py needs NO change; a test routes a merge event through the backfill path). The extra commit GET per review is accepted overhead; errors on it fail closed.

- `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py`: new `get_commit`, `get_merge_files` (no parent), `get_file_diff` (auto-merge base), `get_mergelist`. NEVER bare `/patch` on merges (unit test asserts the 409 path stays fail-closed). ANY merge-path REST failure (commit/files/diff/mergelist) → fail-closed -1 with the existing coverage-gap (infra) tag.

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py`: `assemble_merge_change_context(merge_files, file_diffs, mergelist)` — the file list from `get_merge_files` IS an explicit input (finding fe192771). Format: `## Merge context` (integrated-commit subject lines; `MERGELIST_MAX_COMMITS = 100` is a COUNT pre-cap with truncation notice) then `## Auto-merge diff`; `DIFF_CHAR_CAP` governs the COMBINED string — mergelist section capped first, diff truncated last (f95ed0c3); per-file diffs fetched only until the combined cap is reached — bounds the sequential REST fan-out; note the latency budget (fc2fb799). Empty-auto-merge-diff (clean merge): review proceeds on mergelist-only context; robot comment states the conflict delta was empty.
- Data flow into the gate UNCHANGED: assembled string → `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text=…)` → `produce_code_review_verdict(cfg, diff_text=…)`.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`: `_TAG_SUFFIXES` reuses existing verdict keys, appending `(merge-change, N integrated commits)`.

- Observability: journald events `merge_change_review`, `merge_change_409_guard` (ERROR), `mergelist_fetch_error` (ERROR); CloudWatch metric `review_bot_merge_change_errors` (reason-tagged) via `infra/scripts/observability.sh` exactly as `voter_errors`, PLUS the `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` terraform resource modelled on `monitoring_s4b.tf` (f487d44b).

- Tests: extend `_FakeGerrit` in `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` with the four new methods (f0f74d65); fixture tests for context assembly, cap apportionment, empty diff, 409 guard, REST-failure fallbacks, backfill routing.
## Scope
Bot + assemble seam + monitoring + tests. No Gerrit config (S1), no g2p/CI (S3), runbook prose is S4 (this story only names the log signals).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Live 3.14.1 fixture proving the files/ auto-merge default is committed with the citing test
- [ ] Merge detection in review_and_vote covers webhook + backfill + /rerun paths (tests prove all three)
- [ ] 409-guard unit test: bare /patch on a merge stays fail-closed; every merge-path REST failure votes -1 with coverage-gap tag
- [ ] assemble_merge_change_context implements the documented format + cap apportionment (unit-tested incl. empty-diff + truncation cases)
- [ ] Robot comment carries the merge-change tag variant with integrated-commit count
- [ ] Metric + alarm applied; log events observable in journald
- [ ] make lint && make test green; live smoke: a merge change on the running Gerrit receives a vote with the merge-change tag

baseline.summary: S2: Review-bot merge-change review path — auto-merge base via files/ + per-file diff + mergelist

## Why

Every plan-review criterion that mentions the two headings POOLS them and applies ONE bar —
F1 reads "each acceptance/success criterion", G3 "each parent acceptance/success criterion",
G7 fetches "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract. The dual
vocabulary is therefore noise in the rubrics: it suggests to the reviewing model a distinction
the criteria do not implement, and it is the source the generated criteria guide is built from.
This story removes it at the source.

## What

Rename Success Criteria -> Acceptance Criteria throughout the reviewer prompts and the criteria
routing index, then REGENERATE the criteria guide from them.

## Scope

Reviewer prompts (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`):
- `plan_review_F1.md:10` — "each acceptance/success criterion" -> "each acceptance criterion"
- `plan_review_G3.md:10` and `:12` — line 12 carries BOTH bare-`SC` tokens in the repo:
  "THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'"
- `plan_review_G5.md:19` ("a set of unrelated success criteria" — the decomposition tell,
  which DOES mean the ticket's criteria), `plan_review_G7.md:12` and `:16`,
  `plan_review_COH.md:10`, `plan_review_container.md:14`
- `completion_verifier.md:59` — the Epic bullet naming `## Success Criteria`

Routing index `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `check` strings at
`:544` (COH), `:830` (G3), `:908` (G7).

Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with
`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` — it is GENERATED and
carries a do-not-hand-edit banner; all 11 of its SC hits are downstream of the files above.

EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED — `plan_review_T2.md:10`. Its phrase is "a pilot with success metrics ...
or stated success criteria for a trial": generic English for the metrics that define whether an
EXPERIMENT succeeded, not the ticket heading. Renaming it to "acceptance criteria for a trial"
would change T2's meaning. This is the same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`; the site is
recorded here so a later sweep does not "fix" it.

OUT OF SCOPE: the `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" wording in
`plan_review_verifier.md:81`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87` and
`review_kernel/verify_models.py:231` — a related but distinct concept, tracked separately.

## Approach

Textual substitution in the listed files only. Two forms appear and both are handled:
the phrase "acceptance/success criteria|criterion" collapses to "acceptance criteria|criterion"
(not "acceptance/acceptance"), and standalone "Success Criteria" becomes "Acceptance Criteria".
G3's two bare-`SC` tokens are edited by hand, not by pattern, because `\bSC\b` also matches
`O-RAN-SC` elsewhere in the repo. Their exact replacements are:
`THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS` -> `THREE AC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS`, and
`'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'` ->
`'the AC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'`.

Editing `criteria_routing.json` rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp, which on TODAY's
`main` invalidates every outstanding plan-review attestation (632 tickets, ~40
open/in_progress) as `stale-regver`. Ticket `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` (ADR 0053) grandfathers that
at the claim gate, and it HAS now merged — Gerrit change 962 landed as `095c4afef` and the
ticket is closed. This story's `depends_on 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` was a genuine MERGE-ORDER
constraint, not a preference: landing this rename first would have stranded ~40 in-flight
claims behind a full LLM re-review. That prerequisite is now SATISFIED, so the routing edit
is safe to make. (Status refreshed during implementation; the plan previously recorded 962
as still awaiting its votes.)

Once grandfathering has landed, the rotation is harmless at the claim gate (attestations stay
valid and report non-blocking `registry_drift`). It DOES still deny progressive drift-refresh
reuse, which is correct and expected.

## Testing

- Regenerate the guide and assert it is free of SC vocabulary (the regeneration is itself the
  check that the generator was run rather than the file hand-edited).
- `pytest tests/unit -k "criteria or routing or registry"` green.
- A test that captures `registry_version(None)` BEFORE applying the routing edit (from the
  pre-edit file content) and asserts it differs afterwards, so the rotation is proven by
  construction rather than compared against a literal that would rot the moment any other
  change touches `criteria_routing.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` returns matches ONLY at the three sites this
      story's Scope deliberately excludes, and no others — i.e. all 11 in-scope hits are gone.
      AMENDED during implementation: as originally written ("returns no matches") this criterion
      contradicted both this story's own Scope and its AC6. The three surviving hits are:
      `plan_review_T2.md:10` (generic English — "a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria
      for a trial"; renaming it would change T2's meaning, and AC6 REQUIRES it to survive), and
      `plan_review_verifier.md:81` + `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87`, which are the
      `dod_uncertifiable` "definition-of-done / success criterion" wording that Scope lists as
      OUT OF SCOPE (and that parent epic 1386 also excludes as a separate concept). Verify with
      `... | grep -v -e plan_review_T2.md -e plan_review_verifier.md -e plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`
      returning empty.
- [ ] `grep -noE "\bSCs?\b" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` returns no matches (both
      bare tokens renamed).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is regenerated by the documented command, still
      carries its GENERATED banner, and `grep -niE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)"` on it returns
      EXACTLY ONE match — the T2 criterion's embedded prompt ("...stated success criteria for a
      trial"). AMENDED during implementation: "is empty" was unsatisfiable alongside AC6. The
      guide is a GENERATED snapshot of the registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim,
      so T2's deliberately-excluded phrase necessarily echoes into it. Asserting exactly one
      match is strictly stronger than a bare exclusion: it also proves the phrase was carried
      through rather than silently dropped.
- [ ] Verified BEFORE the routing edit is made: `rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity`
      no longer returns a blocking `stale-regver` verdict on the branch point (i.e. ticket
      `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` has merged), asserted by a check against the current checkout rather
      than assumed.
- [ ] A test proves `registry_version(None)` computed from the PRE-edit routing content differs
      from `registry_version(None)` computed after the edit — capturing both values at run time,
      asserting inequality, and hard-coding neither.
- [ ] `grep -n "success criteria" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` still returns its
      one match, proving the deliberately excluded pilot-metrics phrase was left intact.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Rename Success Criteria to Acceptance Criteria in reviewer prompts and criteria routing

## Why

A valid portability finding needs a productive Pass 4 response, but the proposed generic core move was rejected. The coaching behavior therefore belongs in project configuration and must remain invisible to unrelated criteria.

## What

Add the project-specific `project-portability` coaching move and focused tests for loading, applicability, and deterministic rendering.

## Scope

In scope:

- `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py`
- Pass 4 coaching for `project.portability` findings

Out of scope:

- generic core coaching moves
- changes to built-in move definitions
- Pass 1, Pass 2, or Pass 3 behavior
- documentation and live criterion calibration

## Approach

Use the existing best-effort project move overlay proven by the fresh-worktree experiment. `.rebar/plan_review_moves.json` is a JSON object keyed by move id. Add exactly:

- key `project-portability`
- `name: restore rebar portability`
- `template: Rework {subject} so it remains portable across supported rebar client shapes; keep project-specific behavior in project configuration or an explicit extension boundary.`
- `applies_when: [project.portability]`

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py::load_move_registry` merges this file over a copy of the built-in registry with `strict=False`. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/coach.py::applicable_moves` admits the move only when its trigger intersects the surviving findings. `coach` then validates a bounded noun-phrase subject and renders the locked template deterministically. This project-owned composition is sufficient; no generic core move or kernel change is needed.

The established prior-art tests are `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_load_move_registry_merges_project_extensions` and `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_move_registry_matches_docs_table`. The parent epic experiment at `2026-07-16T00:50:08Z` proved the proposed id loads, remains excluded for trigger `F1`, becomes applicable for `project.portability`, and renders the locked sentence.

## Dependencies

Depends on the criterion-integration child because the move trigger must use the final activated criterion id.

## Test Strategy

Load the real project move registry, query applicability with representative trigger sets, and render the move through the normal coaching path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The project registry loads a move keyed `project-portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k move_id`.
- [ ] The loaded move name equals `restore rebar portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k move_name`.
- [ ] The loaded move template equals the exact sentence specified in this plan. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k move_template`.
- [ ] The loaded move declares only `project.portability` in `applies_when`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k move_trigger`.
- [ ] The move is applicable for the trigger set `{project.portability}`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k applies_to_portability`.
- [ ] The move is absent for an empty trigger set. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k ignores_empty_triggers`.
- [ ] The move is absent for the unrelated trigger set `{F1}`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k ignores_unrelated_findings`.
- [ ] Rendering the subject `the Gerrit landing workflow` produces the exact locked sentence. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k deterministic_render`.
- [ ] Loading the project move leaves the packaged `MOVE_REGISTRY` mapping unchanged. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py -k project_owned_only`.
- [ ] Existing project move loading plus the built-in documentation-table invariant remain green. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k move_registry`.
baseline.summary: Add scoped portability coaching

## Context / Problem

Discovered while diagnosing the 2026-07-31 `rebar-autodeploy-errors` alarm (root cause filed separately as 304e-9c0f-2068-4d0e). Two independent weaknesses in the deploy's health gate turned a recoverable stall into an hour of repeated rollbacks that could not be diagnosed from the deploy journal alone.

**1. The timeout is below the real worst case.** `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:50` sets `HEALTH_TIMEOUT="${HEALTH_TIMEOUT:-30}"` and :232 uses it as the readiness deadline. On 2026-07-31 the review-bot needed **~62s** to become ready, because `run_ensures()` burns a 60s lock budget (`_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2`) before giving up and continuing. The container was killed at +30s and rolled back to `:prev` seven consecutive times — and each rolled-back container then became healthy ~30s later, proving the image was fine and only the deadline was wrong.

Note the interaction: even after 304e is fixed, any future startup path that legitimately exceeds 30s will be rolled back rather than waited for. The deploy's deadline should exceed the application's own internal budgets, not sit below them.

**2. `bot-unhealthy` discards the evidence.** :235 emits `err bot-unhealthy "review-bot failed health check after deploy; ROLLING BACK to :prev"` and nothing else. The container's own stderr — which held the decisive signal (the missing `ensure ...` sweep lines and a 61s gap) — was only recoverable by going to the host and reading `docker logs` for a container that had already been replaced. The deploy journal alone could not distinguish "image is broken" from "image is fine but slow", which are opposite remediations.

## Approach

Raise `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` above the application's worst-case cold start, keeping it an env-overridable default. On a health-check failure, capture and log a bounded tail of the failing container's stderr into the deploy journal before rolling back, so the next occurrence is diagnosable without host access.

## Scope

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — the `HEALTH_TIMEOUT` default (:50), the readiness loop (:232), and
  the `bot-unhealthy` error path (:235).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `HEALTH_TIMEOUT`'s default exceeds the review-bot's worst-case cold start, with the chosen value
      justified against the application's own internal budgets (notably the ensure-sweep lock budget)
      rather than picked arbitrarily; still overridable by env.
- [ ] A `bot-unhealthy` failure records a bounded tail of the failing container's stderr in the deploy
      journal, so "broken image" and "slow start" are distinguishable from the journal alone.
- [ ] The rollback-to-`:prev` behaviour and the fail-safe guarantee (last-known-good stays live) are
      unchanged; verified by a test or a documented dry run.

# An issue link DELETED in Jira is never removed from the local ticket (inbound)

Found while writing the row-11 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table (story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism

The inbound link differ is ADD-ONLY, by construction and by its own docstring. `inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` opens with "Reflect Jira issuelinks into rebar relations. ADD-only." and closes with "ADD-only (no REMOVE mutations)" (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py:380 and :396). It iterates the CURRENT `fields.issuelinks` and emits an add per unseen link; nothing walks the local deps looking for one whose Jira counterpart has gone.

So the flow is asymmetric: the OUTBOUND direction does have a removal path (`outbound_links._diff_link_removals`, which emits `{"action": "remove", "type":..., "to_key":..., "relation":...}`, outbound_links.py:120-175, applied via `delete_issue_link`), while the inbound direction has no counterpart. A link a human deletes in Jira stays on the rebar ticket forever, and no pass ever reports it.

## Why this is a gap and not merely a documented design choice

Story 5200's acceptance criteria define a 14-row mutation table with an explicit oracle per direction. Row 11's INBOUND oracle is "that link is ABSENT" from the local ticket. That row cannot pass while the differ is add-only, so the epic's comprehensiveness claim is not reachable without either implementing the removal or amending the AC. This ticket IMPLEMENTS THE REMOVAL; the Approach below resolves the evidence question (how we know the peer deleted a link rather than that we failed to observe it), which is the part that made this more than a guard removal.

Note the add-only choice is not obviously safe either: the same docstring's idempotency logic already skips an emit when "the counterpart is absent from the ACTIVE local set", i.e. the differ is willing to reason about absence — just not about the absence of the LINK.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` asserts the local dep is gone after the Jira link is deleted. It should go RED on the harness until this is addressed.

## Approach

Mirror the outbound removal path, but gate it — an inbound removal is a WRITE that destroys local data, so the whole design problem is establishing that the peer really DELETED the link rather than that we merely failed to see it.

1. **A new `_diff_link_removals_inbound` in `inbound_differ.py`**, the mirror of
   `outbound_links._diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:120-175). It walks the local `deps` and
   emits `{"action": "remove", "target_id": <local id>, "relation": <local relation>}` — inbound
   records carry `target_id` (a local id), not `to_key`. Build the OBSERVED peer link set through
   `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link`, NOT from raw Jira keys, so both sides are compared in local
   relation vocabulary; comparing raw keys makes an `inwardIssue`/`Blocks` link read as `depends_on`
   while the local dep is `blocks`, producing a spurious removal of a link that is still there.

2. **`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` must branch on `action`.** It currently reads
   `if entry.get("action") != "add": continue` (apply_inbound_records.py:560-562) and only ever calls
   `rebar.link`, so a removal record is silently discarded — a differ-only fix would ship the exact
   silent-failure class this epic exists to end. Removal applies via `rebar.unlink`.

### The five guards, and why each is load-bearing

- **G1 OBSERVED.** Emit only when `"issuelinks" in jira_fields` — key PRESENT, empty list allowed.
  `fetcher.py:592-596` sets that key only for entries `get_issuelinks_map` returned a list for, and the
  base search omits issuelinks entirely (bug 3f04), so key-presence is a reliable "enrichment reached
  this issue" marker. Both readers make an empty list authoritative rather than dropping the key
  (Cloud `acli_graph.get_issuelinks_map` records `result[key] = links` for any list "including the
  empty list — an authoritative 'no links'"; DC `transport.py:391-394` builds `{key: list(... or [])}`).
  `_snapshot_schema.py` is `total=False` and never injects `[]`. So key-absent covers exactly the
  unsafe cases — enrichment failed, HTTP 410, a fail-open partial map, the issue fell outside a
  truncated page, a cross-project bound issue, or a client with no `get_issuelinks_map` — and every one
  of those fails safe to NO REMOVAL.
  **`_diff_links_inbound:397` opens `jira_fields.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses
  observed-empty into unobserved. That line must NOT be reused on the removal path.**
- **G2 TARGET BOUND.** Require `binding_store.get_jira_key(target_id)` non-None. An unbound target
  could never have had a Jira link, so its absence proves nothing.
- **G3 MANAGED.** `should_propagate_removal(relation, target_id, local_ticket)` from
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs` — the same predicate the outbound parent/link gates consume, so a
  peer-created dep rebar never owned is not clobbered. It also excludes
  `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`discovered_from` for free, because `MANAGED_REF_KINDS` omits relations
  with no reliable peer link type; do NOT add a redundant filter for them.
- **G4 ARBITRATION — REWRITTEN AFTER THE LIVE ORACLE REFUTED THE FIRST VERSION. READ THIS CAREFULLY.**
  The FIRST version of this guard said: "never mirror a removal for a target the outbound side is adding
  this pass", on the reasoning that an outbound ADD means "being pushed" rather than "peer deleted it".
  **That reasoning is WRONG, and its failure is total.** When the peer deletes a link, the local dep still
  exists and the peer lacks it — which is EXACTLY the condition under which the outbound differ emits a
  link ADD. So on any bidirectional pass a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that target,
  and the guard therefore always suppressed the inbound REMOVE: **the feature could never fire.** Proven by
  harness run 30784592232 against main @ `de2f1ed87` (which CONTAINS change 1276):
  `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` stayed RED with "the Jira link was DELETED … but the local dep …
  still targets 'jira-rbjflfv-2'". The mutation ledger was green throughout, because
  `test_g4_outbound_add_this_pass_suppresses_the_removal` asserted the behaviour the plan specified — **a
  mutation ledger cannot catch a wrong SPECIFICATION.**

  **THE CORRECTED RULE: `managed_refs` decides PRECEDENCE between the two directions. It is not a second
  AND-gate beside G3.** The two differs disagree about one fact — local dep present, peer link absent — and
  exactly one must win:
    * ref **IS managed** (rebar pushed it at some point) + peer lacks it → **the peer DELETED it** → the
      inbound REMOVE wins, **and the outbound ADD for that pair must be suppressed.**
    * ref is **NOT managed** (never pushed) + peer lacks it → **we simply have not pushed it yet** → the
      outbound ADD wins and the inbound REMOVE is suppressed. This is the ONLY case the old G4 should have
      covered.
  Suppressing only the inbound side is NOT sufficient and must not be shipped: both differs run against
  the same pre-pass snapshot and then both apply, so inbound unlinking locally while outbound re-adds in
  Jira leaves the pass DIVERGENT and the next pass re-adopts the link inbound — churn, not convergence.
  **So `outbound_links.py` (or the shared suppression context) is in scope: this is arbitration across BOTH
  differs.**
  An outbound REMOVE for the same pair still suppresses the inbound removal (the two directions must not
  both act on one pair in a pass; deferring re-evaluates next pass rather than double-removing).
- **G5 RELATION MATCH AT APPLY.** `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` takes NO relation
  argument, and that is deliberate — `_commands/unlink.py`'s usage text says "pair-scoped, NO relation
  arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and `_get_link_info` returns the most recent
  net-active link. So if a pair holds two active relations and the peer dropped only one, a naive
  unlink can remove THE WRONG ONE — a link the peer still has. The apply step must confirm the pair's
  net-active relation MATCHES the vanished relation, and skip + log otherwise.

### G3's blind spot, stated plainly rather than papered over

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the **LINK-event** processor (`reducer/_processors.py:411`), so a ref becomes "managed" the instant it is created LOCALLY — it does NOT mean "we pushed it to the peer". `seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for pre-feature tickets by seeding all current `deps` as managed. So G3 alone does not establish that the peer ever had the link. **Under the CORRECTED arbitration rule above, that is handled by precedence rather than by a second gate:** an UNMANAGED dep is never removed (the outbound ADD wins), so a brand-new local dep is safe by construction. What remains is the narrower case where `managed_refs` says managed but the ref was never actually pushed — chiefly `seed_managed_refs_from_current`, which marks a PRE-FEATURE ticket's CURRENT deps as managed. On such a ticket a never-pushed dep could be read as "the peer deleted it" and removed locally. That window is real and is recorded here deliberately; it is far narrower than the behaviour it replaces, which was that the feature never fired at all.

**The earlier text here claimed "G4 closes that in a healthy pass, because outbound emits a link ADD for exactly that dep and the suppression drops the removal." That sentence was the error** — it is precisely why the first implementation could never work, and it is retained in this form only so the mistake is legible rather than quietly overwritten.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer link set** (link present in the prior Jira snapshot, absent now = a real remote deletion). This is the textbook-correct signal and would retire G3's blind spot outright, but it is NOT available: as of `6cdd4b00d9` ("Narrow persisted Jira snapshot to key membership") `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set` persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership only, carrying no fields and therefore no issuelinks. Reaching for it means adding a new persisted artifact with its own migration and its own truncation semantics, which is a materially larger change than this defect warrants. Recorded so a future reader knows it was considered and why it was declined.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — the removal differ + G1/G2/G3, and making
  G4 deliberate. 718/800 LOC today; a ~50-line mirror lands ~770. If it would breach 800, shed weight
  into `link_direction.py` (59 LOC, already imported by both directions), never mechanically.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — action branch + `rebar.unlink` + G5.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py` (or the shared same-pass suppression context) —
  **ADDED after the live refutation:** the managed case must also suppress the OUTBOUND link ADD, or the
  pass ends divergent and churns. This is the arbitration half the original plan did not contemplate.
  579/800 LOC.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` — OPTIONAL, only to add a `should_mirror_peer_removal` sibling
  sharing the `managed_ref_set()` read path. Mechanically the identical predicate, so it buys naming
  and a place to document that inbound needs more than the managed check. Skip it if the guards read
  clearly without it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** any fetcher or adapter change (the observed/unobserved distinction already
  survives); `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`, which another ticket owns.

## Acceptance criteria

**AMENDED after an operator ruling — see the AC AMENDMENT comment on this ticket for the full reasoning and the ecosystem research with sources.** The ruling was: research the ecosystem, build if it is a parity gap, defer if it is not commonly handled. It is NOT commonly handled (Aha! refuses deletion propagation outright citing inadvertent-data-loss risk; Asana<->Jira and Workfront<->Jira leave the far item in place; Exalate makes link sync opt-in scripted config), and it is NOT a Cloud/DC parity gap (shared core; Cloud never mirrored a peer deletion and has no equivalent cell). So removal-mirroring is DEFERRED and the criteria written around "the removal IS emitted" no longer describe what this ticket ships.

The original criteria are preserved verbatim below under RETIRED rather than deleted, so the decision is auditable.

### What this ticket actually shipped — the criteria that stand

- [x] the apply-layer DROP is fixed. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` used to
      discard any non-`add` link record outright (`action != "add": continue`), so even a correct
      differ could not have worked. That branch + the `rebar.unlink` wiring landed in change 1276
      and is independently mutation-proven. This was a REAL defect and it is fixed
- [x] G1/G2/G3/G5 landed and are mutation-proven. They are dormant (nothing emits a removal for
      them to gate) but they are correct, and they are the guards a future implementation needs
- [x] the shipped semantics are STATED: local-wins-and-restore. A link deleted in Jira is re-added
      on the next pass — convergent, no local data destroyed, identical on both backends
- [x] the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is XFAIL with the full reason in the
      marker, `strict=False` so it fails LOUDLY as an xpass the moment a removal path starts
      working — NOT inverted and NOT deleted. Gerrit change 1303, MERGED as 29f9627128; verified on
      main: reason text present, strict=False, cell body unmodified
- [x] the ecosystem evidence is recorded, with sources, so this is not re-litigated from scratch
- [x] the refutation of the original design is recorded, with a probe — `managed_refs` cannot
      distinguish "a link we never pushed" from "a link the peer deleted"; the two states are
      IDENTICAL on every input the guards read. That finding stopped a second data-loss defect
      before it was written
- [x] the correct design is recorded WITH A WORKING TEMPLATE — change 1296 landed exactly this
      pattern for parents (a per-binding record of what the peer last had, advanced only on
      OBSERVATION), so whoever picks this up starts from shipped, reviewed code rather than from
      the refuted premise. `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs
- [x] `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap

### RETIRED — specify a feature deliberately NOT shipped

Recorded, not silently dropped. Every item below described emitting or gating a link REMOVAL, which this ticket no longer ships. The live cell still EXISTS and still RUNS (as an xfail); what changed is the product decision about what behaviour to ship, taken on ecosystem evidence plus a first-hand incident in which the identical inference destroyed 63 parent edges.

- ~~RETIRED~~ a link deleted in Jira is mirrored locally: the local dep is asserted POSITIVELY ABSENT after
      the pass, never "no exception was raised"
- ~~RETIRED~~ the removal record survives the apply layer end to end — differ emit → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → `rebar.unlink` → the dep is gone from the reduced ticket. A test that stops at
      the differ boundary does NOT satisfy this, because the record was silently dropped at
      `apply_inbound_records.py:560-562` and a differ-only oracle goes green while the store is untouched
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with the issue's `issuelinks` key ABSENT (unobserved — simulate the real truncation/fail-open
      shape, not a hand-deleted key if the real path differs), NO removal is emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with `issuelinks` present and EMPTY (authoritative "no links"), the removal IS emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G2: an unbound target emits no removal
- ~~RETIRED~~ G3: a dep that is not in `managed_refs` emits no removal, so a peer-created dep is never clobbered
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, MANAGED case: a MANAGED dep whose peer link is gone emits the removal **even
      though the outbound side is adding that target this pass**, and the outbound ADD for that pair is
      SUPPRESSED. Assert BOTH halves — inbound removal present AND outbound add absent — because
      suppressing only one leaves the pass divergent and churning
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, UNMANAGED case: an UNMANAGED dep whose peer link is absent emits NO removal and the
      outbound ADD proceeds, asserted against `link_add_keys`
- ~~RETIRED~~ a test pins that the two arbitration branches are decided by `managed_refs` and NOT by the mere
      presence of an outbound add — i.e. flipping only the managed-ness of the ref flips which direction
      wins. This is the assertion whose absence let the first version ship broken
- ~~RETIRED~~ the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is GREEN on a harness run, and the run id is
      recorded here. **A green unit suite is explicitly NOT sufficient for this ticket** — the first
      version had a fully green, mutation-checked unit suite and did not work at all
- ~~RETIRED~~ G5: when the pair's net-active relation differs from the vanished relation, no unlink is
      performed and the skip is logged
- ~~RETIRED~~ steady state does not churn: a managed dep still present on the peer emits NO removal on
      repeated passes
- ~~RETIRED~~ every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the removal unconditional — a fix that emits removals with no guard passes
      the happy-path oracle while being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that
      actually protect the product
- ~~RETIRED~~ `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is
      unmodified, and turns GREEN on the harness once this lands
- ~~RETIRED~~ `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap
baseline.summary: Inbound link removal is never mirrored (inbound link differ is ADD-only)

content.text: ## Why

Code inspection suggests Jira link/relation sync is scaffolded (client primitives in acli_graph.py: set_relationship/get_issue_links/delete_issue_link) but NOT wired into the diff/fetch/apply pipeline (OutboundMutation.links always []; fetcher/inbound have no link refs; no link MutationAction; no caller of the primitives). The user expects links SHOULD sync. Settle it EMPIRICALLY with tests + a live probe before re-scoping story 25ae.
## What

- Integration tests (in-process, real pipeline) that drive a rebar ticket carrying a link (blocks/depends_on) through the OUTBOUND differ and assert whether a link mutation is produced; and feed a Jira snapshot containing issuelinks through the INBOUND differ and assert whether a relation change is produced.

- A live probe (gated, authorized LIVE DIG): create two Jira issues + a rebar link between their tickets, run reconcile DRY-RUN, and observe whether the dry-run PLAN contains a link mutation (non-destructive); clean up any created issues.
- Report RAW results (do not assume outcome): does outbound emit links? does inbound reflect links? does the live dry-run plan include link ops?
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Integration tests exist exercising outbound + inbound link paths through the real differs
- [ ] A gated live probe runs reconcile dry-run with a real cross-issue rebar link and records whether links appear in the plan
- [ ] Empirical verdict recorded (works / partially / not wired) with evidence
- [ ] Suite green; ruff clean

## Why
Deferred from b550. gerrit-verify.yaml's monolithic build-and-test job HAND-COPIES the gate+suite command set that test.yml runs across its lint + pip-audit + test jobs. tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py polices that copy against drift. Factor the shared gate+suite into ONE reusable workflow_call file (the pattern _optionality.yml already proves) so drift is impossible by construction, and the copy-sync guard can be replaced by a delegation guard.

## What
Add .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml — a reusable (workflow_call) workflow, checkout parameterized by gerrit-refspec/gerrit-project/gerrit-url EXACTLY like _optionality.yml (branch-head via actions/checkout when gerrit-refspec=='' ; checkout-gerrit-change-action on the patchset when set), taking NO secrets. It defines THREE jobs mirroring test.yml's current decomposition (so test.yml keeps its job-graph parallelism):
- lint: make lint + pre-commit (SKIP no-commit-to-branch,lint,typecheck) + make typecheck + make config-check.
- pip-audit: the network-retried dependency-vuln scan (one ubuntu job).
- test: the os×py matrix (install .[dev] + git identity + Module-size + Prompt-index + Env-var + Docs-index + README-quickstart + CLI-ref + MCP-ref + Security-pin + Criteria-routing + server.json + Public-types gates + default suite + integration tier).
The union of these three == gerrit-verify.yaml's current build-and-test gate set, so nothing is dropped.

Rewire callers:
- test.yml: delete its inline lint/pip-audit/test jobs; call the reusable with NO inputs (branch-head). Keep golden-path, artifact-probe, and the secret-scoped external job (which the reusable, taking no secrets, must not absorb).
- gerrit-verify.yaml: replace the monolithic build-and-test job with a single reusable-call job STILL NAMED build-and-test (needs: [clear-vote, require-ticket]); this also splits gerrit's currently-inline lint/mypy/config-check/pre-commit out of the 4x matrix so they run once (a net improvement). clear-vote, require-ticket, optionality, golden-path, verify-identity, and vote are unchanged; vote still lists 'build-and-test, optionality' in needs, and im-open/workflow-conclusion still folds the reusable's job conclusions into the Verified vote (already proven for optionality).

golden-path remains duplicated between the two files for now (out of scope; smaller duplication, larger blast radius — noted as a follow-up).

## Correct premise: test_ci_workflow_parity.py enforces FIVE functions, not one
It is NOT 'solely a copy-sync policer'. Three of its five functions enforce independent safety invariants that MUST be preserved (relocated to scan the reusable), not dropped:
1. test_verified_gate_runs_every_shared_gate — the copy-sync check. REWRITE: assert each _SHARED_GATE_SIGNATURES value appears in _build-and-test.yml (the reusable), AND that BOTH test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml contain the delegation string './.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml'. (gate exists + both lanes run it via one source.)
2. test_no_drift_script_gate_is_verified_only_in_branch_ci — REWRITE: scan _build-and-test.yml for scripts/*.py (they now gate both lanes by construction); _INTENTIONAL_SCRIPT_ASYMMETRIES stays empty. The old test.yml-minus-gerrit diff is obsolete under a single source.
3. test_optionality_contract_gates_the_verified_path — SURVIVES UNCHANGED (independent invariant: optionality reusable wiring + GERRIT_REFSPEC + vote-needs-optionality). Not touched by this change.
4. test_branch_sensitive_precommit_hooks_skipped_in_ci — SURVIVES; retarget _precommit_all_files_steps at _build-and-test.yml (the reusable now owns the single pre-commit step) and assert no-commit-to-branch is in its SKIP.
5. test_ci_redundant_hooks_skipped_in_precommit — SURVIVES; same retarget: assert lint+typecheck are SKIPped in the reusable's pre-commit step AND that the direct 'make lint'/'make typecheck' steps still exist in the reusable (linter runs exactly once).
Also update tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py: add '_build-and-test.yml' -> 'Build and Test (reusable)' to the locked naming table so the naming gate covers it.

## Validation note
g2p dispatches gerrit-verify.yaml from main's ref, so THIS change's own Verified run uses the OLD inline gate; the refactored reusable path first runs post-merge via test.yml (branch-head), watched immediately after landing. actionlint (make lint) validates the reusable 'uses:' wiring + workflow_call input schema locally pre-merge; the rewritten parity + naming tests validate the structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml exists as a workflow_call reusable with lint + pip-audit + test(matrix) jobs, checkout parameterized by gerrit-refspec, taking no secrets.
- [ ] test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml BOTH delegate to ./.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml; gerrit-verify's reusable-call job is named build-and-test and vote still needs it; the Verified vote still works end-to-end (confirmed by the first post-merge run + the next change's Verified +1).
- [ ] All five test_ci_workflow_parity.py functions are updated per the enumeration above (three safety invariants preserved, retargeted to the reusable; two copy-sync checks rewritten as delegation+reusable-content checks); no safety guard silently dropped.
- [ ] test_workflow_names.py covers _build-and-test.yml.
- [ ] make lint (actionlint over all workflows) + the workflow tests pass; lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
baseline.summary: Consolidate test.yml + gerrit-verify build-and-test into a reusable workflow
