# Add the close-time plan-review gate

## Goal
Prevent an implemented ticket from closing after its own plan or a pinned upstream plan changed during execution, without running plan review inside close or invalidating every implementation because implementation files changed.

## Implementation
- This story is implemented only after its declared dependencies: 75de supplies `PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE`, `compute_validity(..., profile=...)`, pin health/enforcement, and additive validity results; 5967 supplies signed review phase/floor and phase compatibility. Those interfaces are feature-branch deliverables and are not present on current main before the predecessors land. Do not wire close until both predecessor implementations are available.
- Register `require_plan_review_for_close: bool = False` on `_config_schema.py::VerifyConfig`, add the bool coercer to `_SECTIONS["verify"]`, and update the config-surface golden. Default false preserves every existing close path and performs no signature or plan-material reads.
- Add `_commands/gates.py::close_plan_review_gate_check(ticket_id, ticket_state, *, repo_root) -> dict` as the sole close policy boundary. It calls `signing.verify_signature(kind="plan-review")`, then 75de's `compute_validity(..., kind="plan-review", profile=PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE)`. CLOSE intentionally disables only code freshness (verified HEAD and per-file dependency hashes) because implementation changes are expected during execution; signature, reopen, registry, current own material, 5967 phase compatibility, and configured pin enforcement remain active. This cannot reuse `claim_gate_check`, because DEFAULT intentionally blocks code drift while CLOSE must not.
- The helper runs only when `verify.require_plan_review_for_close=true` and the ticket is a task/story/epic taking the normal close path. It returns `{ok, verdict, reason}` and never invokes a model or network. `verify.enforce_plan_material_pins` controls only whether pin health invalidates; phase incompatibility, own-material drift, reopen, registry, signature, and malformed metadata always invalidate. Any unexpected local read/parser/signature exception is caught and returned fail-closed as verdict `unavailable`.
- In `transition_close.close_ticket`, after structural/exemption/force checks and before `_completion_precheck`, reduce current state and call `close_plan_review_gate_check`. Failure raises the normal command error before completion verification with exact message `plan-review close gate: <verdict>: <reason>. Run rebar review-plan <canonical-id> separately, then retry close.` The verdict is the exact `compute_validity` verdict (`unsigned`, `stale-reopened`, `stale-regver`, `stale-material`, `unverifiable-material`, `stale-pin-drift`, `stale-pin-missing`, `malformed-pin`, `incompatible-phase`, `malformed-phase`, or `unavailable`); reason is diagnostic only. Close never launches `review-plan` itself.
- Extend `txn.transition_core(..., *, pre_status_check: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], None] | None = None)` as a generic local pre-append hook; every existing caller defaults `None`. After acquiring the existing global write lock, re-reading state, verifying expected status, and applying structural close rules—but immediately before appending STATUS—invoke the callback with that freshly reduced state. A raised `RebarError` aborts the transaction and releases the lock without append/commit. `txn.py` imports no plan-review code.
- When close enforcement applies, `close_ticket` passes a closure as `pre_status_check`; the closure calls the same pure `close_plan_review_gate_check` on the locked fresh state and raises the same command error on failure. This is the second check, not pre-existing txn behavior. It runs inside the single existing critical section; `close_ticket` never acquires a second lock. A signature, ticket, phase, own-material, or related-pin change between precheck and lock is therefore caught before STATUS append.
- Preserve existing scope and bypass rules: bugs, session logs, code reviews, identities, and idea→closed remain exempt exactly as the claim gate; a non-empty force-close reason bypasses both completion verification and this plan-review gate and retains its audit event; structural child-closure rules are never bypassed. `close_ticket` remains the sole production task/story/epic close entry point, and all CLI/library/MCP surfaces inherit the behavior.
- Document the CLOSE profile policy, flag interaction, error/remediation vocabulary, locked callback, and force/exemption behavior in advanced `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `require_plan_review_for_close=false` or absent, normal close behavior is byte-for-byte equivalent and performs no plan-review reads.
- [ ] With enforcement enabled, task/story/epic close runs the plan gate before completion verification.
- [ ] CLOSE accepts certified, registry-current, material-current, phase-compatible reviews despite HEAD or file-dependency drift.
- [ ] Unsigned, reopened, stale-registry, own-material drift, malformed metadata, and phase incompatibility block even when pin enforcement is false.
- [ ] Pin drift/missing/malformed blocks only when `enforce_plan_material_pins=true`; disabled enforcement remains advisory.
- [ ] Every failure uses the exact verdict-prefixed message and separate `review-plan` remediation; unexpected exceptions fail closed as `unavailable` without traceback.
- [ ] Close performs zero plan-review LLM/model/network calls.
- [ ] The generic `pre_status_check` runs under the existing lock after fresh state/structural checks and before STATUS append.
- [ ] A failing locked callback appends and commits no STATUS event.
- [ ] A plan/signature/phase/material/pin change between precheck and lock is rejected by the locked recheck.
- [ ] Existing transition callers that omit `pre_status_check` are unchanged.
- [ ] Bugs, session logs, code reviews, identities, and idea→closed retain their existing exemptions.
- [ ] Non-empty force-close reason bypasses both gates with the existing audit trail but never bypasses structural child closure.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the CLOSE policy, both flags, callback ordering, error vocabulary, and bypass scope.

## Verification
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate.py` proves the full validity/verdict/config matrix, code-drift exclusion, fail-closed exceptions, and zero-model behavior.
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` proves precheck ordering, public close behavior, default-off compatibility, and remediation messages.
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_pre_status_check.py` proves inside-lock ordering, race rejection, and no-write callback failure.
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_idea_close_bypass.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py` updates existing exemption/force/signing ordering assertions.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_docs.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_config_surface.py` proves advanced documentation and config registration/golden coverage.
- Run `make check` and the full non-LLM test suite.

baseline.description:
## Symptom

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py` fails with

    AssertionError: assert False
      where False = isinstance(Mutation(direction=..., action=..., target='DSO-42', ...),
                               <class 'mutation.Mutation'>)

i.e. an object that IS a `Mutation` fails `isinstance` against `Mutation`. Observed on `macos-latest / py3.13` in CI while `ubuntu-latest / py3.13` — same Python version — passed, which is the signature of a collection-order dependency rather than a version or logic defect.

## Root cause (reproduced deterministically, not inferred)

Five test files load `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py` **by path** under the SHARED `sys.modules` key `"mutation"`:

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_quarantine_suppression.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_mutation.py`

Three of them shared this helper:

    def _load_module(name: str, path: Path) -> ModuleType:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)   # keeps an EARLIER registration
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
        return mod                          # ...but returns the NEW module

`setdefault` keeps whatever was registered first, yet the function returns the freshly-created module. So whenever another file has already registered `"mutation"`, the fixture hands back a module object that is **not** `sys.modules["mutation"]` — two live copies of the same source, with two distinct `Mutation` classes.

Meanwhile `differ._load_mutation()` resolves its `Mutation` cache-first out of `sys.modules` (checking `"mutation"`, `"rebar_reconciler.mutation"`, …). So the differ builds objects from copy A while the test asserts against copy B, and `isinstance` is correctly `False`.

Whichever file pytest collects first wins the `setdefault`, so the outcome depends on collection order — which differs between macOS and Linux.

**Deterministic reproduction** (fails before the fix, passes after):

    pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_conflict_resolution.py \
           tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py -q

The natural alphabetical order puts `test_differ.py` first, so it normally wins and the suite is green; that is why this sat latent.

## Fix (landed with story J4, `0a94-e104-7304-4d85`)

Make the helper cache-first, so the returned module always IS the registered one — mirroring what `differ._load_mutation()` already does:

    cached = sys.modules.get(name)
    if cached is not None and getattr(cached, "__file__", None) == str(path):
        return cached
    ...
    sys.modules[name] = mod

Applied to the three `setdefault`-based helpers. `test_differ_emits_probe.py` already assigned unconditionally (self-consistent) and `test_mutation.py` loads inline, so neither carried the defect.

## Why it was bundled with J4 rather than landed separately

J4 added two test files, which perturbed macOS collection order enough to make another registrant win the race — turning a latent landmine into a `Verified -1` that blocked J4's own change. The fix therefore had to sit at or below J4 in the review stack for J4 to go green. It is test-only, ~6 lines across three files, and the alternative (a separate change spliced beneath an already-pushed one, blocking on its own plan review) bought nothing. The bundling is disclosed in J4's commit message rather than smuggled.

## Remaining work this ticket tracks

- [ ] Consider a shared conftest helper so the by-path loader exists ONCE instead of being copy-pasted into
      five test modules — the duplication is what let three copies carry the same defect
- [ ] Audit the other shared by-path `sys.modules` keys (`differ`, `config`, `adf`, `outbound_fields`,
      `comment_limits`) for the same `setdefault`-then-return-new shape
- [ ] Consider making CI run the suite in a randomized order (e.g. `pytest-randomly`) so order-dependent
      coupling fails fast and locally rather than as a platform-specific surprise
baseline.summary: Test helpers return an unregistered copy of mutation.py, so isinstance fails on a collection-order flip

baseline.description:
## Why

Criterion authors configuring project-specific code-review rules currently see a valid overlay
merge but no criterion execution or eval path, a silent failure that is indistinguishable from a
rubric that found no issues.

ADR 0017 and `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` advertise one project-criteria extension surface across
plan review and code review, but the current code-review runtime only executes the static workflow
list and consults packaged decision/eval lookups. A project can therefore configure a net-new
LLM-backed code-review criterion that merges successfully yet never runs end to end.

## What

Complete the generic, project-id-agnostic code-review runtime seam. The child bug
`8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` owns the reproduced defect and implementation details. This story owns the
delivered capability and compatibility contract: activated project criteria run exactly once,
their repository prompt and eval assets resolve through the CLI, and deterministic Pass 3 uses
repository-effective routing.

## Scope

- Reuse plan review's runner-side dynamic fan-in pattern without adding a workflow DSL field or a
  hard-coded project criterion id. `CodeReviewBatchRunner` uses a named
  `PROJECT_FAN_IN_STEP_ID = "round_a"` constant as a stateless discriminator: activated project
  prompts are appended only for that step, deduplicated against included static physical ids, and
  never appended for `round_b`. No instance flag survives between reviews. A test submits both
  requests to one reusable runner and proves one project-prompt execution per review across the
  complete topology. This runner seam is chosen because it is the existing plan-review pattern and
  preserves the versioned workflow schema unchanged.
- Map a logical `project.<name>` criterion to physical prompt id
  `code-review-project-<name-with-dots-replaced-by-dashes>`; for this epic the physical prompt/eval
  basename is `code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries`. Routing JSON continues to use the
  logical id as its key; translation occurs only when prompt/eval assets are dispatched.
- Extend `criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id, *, gate_key="plan_review")` with
  `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "code-review-"`; the default preserves plan-review callers, while
  `gate_key="code_review"` produces the physical project id. Extend calibration as
  `calibrate_criterion(criterion_id, *, repo_root=None, runs=1, gate_key="plan_review")`; the CLI
  passes its resolved gate key, and calibration passes it to the same mapper. Existing
  criterion-preview/editor callers remain
  plan-review-only and retain the default; code-review project assets are manually authored through
  the documented `.rebar/` overlay surface in this epic.
- Resolve project prompt/eval assets from the reviewed repository snapshot. An activated missing or
  malformed asset is a fatal configuration failure: raise a located `LLMError` before model
  execution rather than emitting an empty-findings coverage gap or silently skipping the criterion.
- Extend `criteria eval` preflight to accept a logical id only when it is active in code review's
  repository-effective criteria. Compute plan-review and code-review membership: zero matches keeps
  the existing unknown-id error, one match selects that gate for `calibrate_criterion`, and two
  matches fail with an explicit ambiguous-gate error rather than silently choosing a prompt.
- Extend `_code_review_prompt_id(prompt_id, repo_root)` to recognize the sanitized physical id only
  when its logical inverse is active, then reuse the existing `_run_code_review_case` arm. Eval
  cases use the `diff` key and return the prompt's native `{findings: [...]}` output; they never run
  through the plan-review `_run_criterion_case` / `pass1_chunk` path and require no new solver arm.
- For every project prompt, retain the local physical-to-logical map built during fan-in. On each
  emitted project finding, overwrite `criteria` with `[logical_id]` and set `reviewer_id` to the
  physical prompt id. Pass 3 therefore consumes only logical routing keys regardless of model
  output; built-in finding attribution remains unchanged.
- Preserve the existing behavior and result shape for repositories without a code-review project
  overlay.
- In `code_review_decide`, compute `routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)` once. Bind
  the kernel's threshold callback to `registry.threshold_for(criterion, routing)`—which returns
  both `block_threshold` and `blocking_enabled`—and call
  `registry.nit_suppressed_criteria(routing)` so both deterministic decision inputs use the same
  repository-effective map; no YAML input or LLM step is added.
- Update `docs/llm-framework.md` to describe code-review project-criterion runtime resolution,
  configuration failures, and the eval entry point, completing rather than replacing ADR 0017.

Out of scope: authoring `project.review-phase-boundaries`, changing four-pass decision math,
modifying packaged built-in criteria, or deploying a Gerrit criterion.

## Sequencing and Rollback

The child bug is implemented and closed before this story closes. Downstream criterion authoring
depends on this story. Revert the fan-in, routing lookup, eval resolution, tests, and documentation
together if overlay-absent compatibility regresses; the additive seam has no data migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` is closed and its change is landed on `main`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/rebar show 8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` and
  `git log origin/main --oneline --grep='rebar-ticket: 8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8'`.
- [ ] A synthetic activated code-review `project.*` criterion runs exactly once in Pass 1, retains
  its logical id in every finding's `criteria`, and resolves validator-safe repository prompt/eval
  ids. The same reusable runner receives `round_a` and `round_b` requests for two review runs and
  records one project execution per review; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'fan_in or eval'`.
- [ ] Pass 3 applies repository-effective threshold, blocking posture, and nit-suppression routing
  for the synthetic id without invoking an LLM; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k routing`.
- [ ] Activated missing/malformed project assets raise a located `LLMError` before model execution,
  while an overlay-absent repository retains its pre-change result; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'missing or parity'`.
- [ ] `rebar criteria eval` accepts an activated logical code-review project id, maps it to the
  sanitized physical prompt id, dispatches `diff` cases through `_run_code_review_case`, and rejects
  unknown/inactive/dual-gate ambiguous ids; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k cli`.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` contains a `Code-review project criteria` section covering Round-A
  fan-in, logical/physical ids, fatal configuration errors, deterministic Pass-3 routing, and the
  `criteria eval` entry point; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("docs/llm-framework.md").read_text(); assert
  all(x in s for x in ("Code-review project criteria", "round_a", "criteria eval",
  "configuration error", "effective routing"))'`.
- [ ] Shared-overlay and four-pass regression suites pass; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_unified_criteria.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py
  tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_workflow.py && make lint`.
baseline.summary: Complete the generic code-review project-criterion runtime seam

content.text: ## Why
For an additive map the two signers must write distinct, self-identifying keys, and
completion validity needs a material fingerprint to detect post-signing edits.
## What
Both sign sites set an unsigned `data["kind"]` on the `SIGNATURE` event (`plan-review`,
`completion-verifier`) for robust routing (kind stays anchored via `manifest[0]`). The
completion signer ALSO records the plan-review material fingerprint
(description/AC/file_impact/children) as a manifest line, so completion validity-on-read can
recompute and compare (symmetric with plan-review). Drift-refresh re-sign preserves kind.
## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (`sign_plan_review`, `refresh_attestation`),
`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` (`_verdict_manifest` + completion signing),
`src/rebar/signing.py` (kind passthrough if needed).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Plan-review SIGNATURE events carry `data["kind"]=="plan-review"`.
- [ ] Completion SIGNATURE events carry `data["kind"]=="completion-verifier"`.
- [ ] Completion manifest records the material fingerprint (legacy completion sigs without it are treated as material-unknown by validity-on-read).
- [ ] `data["kind"]` and the fingerprint line do NOT alter the existing canonical payload in a way that breaks old signatures (no PAYLOAD_VERSION bump).
- [ ] Drift-refresh re-sign preserves the same kind.
## Added (review)
- The completion signer computes the material fingerprint via the SAME helper plan-review
uses (single source of the material field set); it does not redefine the field list.
## Clarification

- `data["kind"]` is only a ROUTING HINT; the SIGNED `manifest[0]` remains authoritative (114f uses the hint only iff it matches the manifest-derived kind). This story just sets the hint consistently; it does not change what is signed.
## Clarification (review): data[kind] is consumed, not dropped
- `process_signature` (114f) consumes `data["kind"]` at REDUCE-TIME via its
`attestation_kind(manifest, data)` routing (read directly from the event data, validated
against the authoritative `manifest[0]`) — it is NOT silently dropped. Additionally, 114f
stores the resolved/derived `kind` IN the signature record so the kind is self-describing
for consumers (incl. the legacy `signature` mirror).
- [ ] The signers set `data["kind"]`; the reducer routes by it (validated against manifest[0]) and records the resolved kind in the signature record.

baseline.summary: Signing call sites: stamp data[kind] on SIGNATURE events

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A plan edited mid-review still runs every remaining LLM pass and only fails at sign time — `generation.sign_manifest` re-collects the generation and raises `PlanReviewGenerationChanged` when `fresh.own_material != initial_generation.own_material` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:146-170). Everything billed after the edit is pure waste: Pass-1 checkpoints are keyed by the material fingerprint (`sizing._checkpoint_key`, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:495-517), so no completed chunk survives the edit either. The sign-time equality was deliberately narrowed to own material + pinned related material — `relation_snapshot` and `ticket_store_revision` are `compare=False` (generation.py:24-41; commit 7c3c08df8 / bug d70a: store-wide equality aborted signing on unrelated tickets' writes). The cancel predicate must be scoped the same way (OWN material only) or it reintroduces d70a as false mid-run cancels.

Since B-RETIRE the sole review driver is the v3 workflow `gates/plan-review.yaml` run by `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_tail.py (the cancelled-verdict builder _cancelled_plan_review_verdict lives here — gate_dispatch.py sat at the 800-LOC module-size cap, so the tail was split along the existing call seam; gate_dispatch re-exports the seam):111-241): precheck → assemble → finders (`batch` → `pass1.run_pass1`) → prerequisite verify → grounding → verify_branch{verify_inputs → verify → decide → coach_inputs → coach}. Two executor facts shape the mechanism: (a) a scripted-op exception is captured as a failed StepResult (src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py:498-499) and `rc.failed` short-circuits every remaining step (interpreter.py:319) — it does NOT propagate; (b) gate_dispatch then tries the coach/verify recovery reconstructions (gate_dispatch.py:218-232), so a cancel that looks like a mere step failure would be "recovered" into a findings verdict and flow on to the floors, signing, and `sidecar.emit` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:599-728) — and a sidecar write advances the store revision. The cancel signal must therefore be an out-of-band token that produce_plan_review_verdict checks BEFORE its recovery paths.

## Approach
(1) `generation.py` grows the run-scoped cancel token + probe (no new module):
- `PlanReviewCancelledStale(RuntimeError)`.
- a private `ContextVar` holding a `_CancelScope` dataclass `{ticket_id, baseline_own_material, repo_root, event: threading.Event}`, entered via `@contextmanager cancel_scope(...)`; `review_cancelled() -> bool` reads it None-safely.
- `own_material_changed(ticket_id, baseline, *, repo_root) -> bool`: under `ticket_reads.local_read_context()` (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:169-176 — makes `ensure_fresh` at reads.py:193-210 return before any fetch/reconverge or sync-lock acquisition) call `attest.current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:756-791 — a single-ticket light read: `show_ticket` + child ids, no store-wide reduction). Returns True only when baseline and current are both non-None and differ; unknown/None → False (fail-open; monotone — a missed cancel degrades to today's sign-time refusal).
- `probe_cancel(seam)`: no active scope → no-op; if the event is already set, or `own_material_changed(...)` is True → `event.set()` + raise `PlanReviewCancelledStale`. It NEVER compares tracker HEAD, the relation snapshot, or `related_material` (d70a scoping; dependency drift keeps its reusable checkpoints and is still caught at sign time).

(2) Probe placement — exactly the two between-pass seams, as one call at the top of the ops that already run there in BOTH `verify_branch` arms: `plan_review_verify_inputs` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:365 — after the finders batch, before the Pass-2 verify prompt step) and `plan_review_coach_inputs` (workflow_ops.py:414 — after decide, before the Pass-4 coach prompt step). No per-chunk polling, no new yaml steps, no whole-store reads.

(3) `pass1._chunk` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:479-498) first checks `generation.review_cancelled()` and returns `([], [])` without a runner call or checkpoint I/O — the ContextVar reaches pool workers because `_submit_ctx` submits under `copy_context()` (pass1.py:67-75). Defensive in the two-seam design (the event cannot be set mid-finders today) but it makes the funnel safe for any future seam at one Event-read of cost. In-flight `runner.run` calls are not interruptible — up to pool-width in-flight calls are accepted as sunk cost.

(4) `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict`: compute `baseline = orchestrator.material_fingerprint(ctx)` (the identical hash `initial_generation.own_material` carries — pass1.py:727-744) and add `generation.cancel_scope(...)` to the existing with-stack (gate_dispatch.py:179-184). Wrap `run_workflow` so a `PlanReviewCancelledStale` escaping the batch step is also caught (`_run_batch` calls `runner.run(req, rc.runner)` with no try — interpreter.py:399 — so batch exceptions propagate raw, unlike op exceptions). After the run, BEFORE the coach/verify recovery attempts: if the scope's event is set, return a cancelled verdict built with `claimability.indeterminate_verdict` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py:123-167) — finding id `plan-review-cancelled-stale`, `coverage_extra={"cancelled": {"seam": ..., "reason": ...}}`, `signature_reason="cancelled-stale"`, remediation "the ticket's own plan material changed mid-review; everything after the edit was skipped — rerun `rebar review-plan`".

(5) `__init__._run_plan_review`: immediately after the `produce_plan_review_verdict` call (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:599-607), if `verdict["coverage"].get("cancelled")` return the verdict verbatim — skipping the floors, `attest.sign_plan_review`, and `sidecar.emit`, mirroring the not-claimable early return (__init__.py:476-479). The verdict is unsigned INDETERMINATE with `sidecar_emitted: False`; the CLI maps INDETERMINATE to exit 2 (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:443,535). Monotone safety: the cancel path can only WITHHOLD an attestation (it returns before any signing code), never mint one.

Alternatives rejected: keying on tracker HEAD / the relation snapshot, or per-chunk `generation.collect()` polling — a store-wide reduction that can contend for the sync lock and false-cancels on unrelated writes (the exact d70a regression); cancelling on `related_material` drift — that discards reusable fingerprint-keyed checkpoints and sign-time already refuses it.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_cancel.py. Out of scope: the yaml (unchanged), the bespoke orchestrator (retired), verify-completion/code-review gates, any cancellation of in-flight runner calls.

## Testing
New tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_cancel.py on the existing offline harness (the `_patch_reads` / `_CountingFinder` / `_CannedAgent` pattern of tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py:49-183, driven through `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` as in tests/unit/test_gate_engine_cutover.py:90):
- post-finders cancel: `attest.current_material_fingerprint` patched to flip after the first finder call → the verify/coach prompt steps never run (agent-runner call recording), the verdict is INDETERMINATE carrying the `plan-review-cancelled-stale` finding, `signature.signed` is False, `sidecar_emitted` is False, and `review_plan`'s CLI disposition is exit 2.
- post-decide cancel: fingerprint flips after decide → coach never runs, same cancelled verdict shape.
- d70a guard: a mid-run write to a DIFFERENT ticket (the subject's own fingerprint unchanged) does NOT cancel — the run completes to the same PASS as an undisturbed run.
- freshness: the probe never fetches/reconverges — `ensure_fresh`'s sync machinery (patched to record) is not reached from a probe because the read runs under `local_read_context`.
- no-change byte-identity: with the cancel plumbing active and no mid-run edit, the produced verdict for fixed canned inputs equals the pre-change baseline verdict; the existing plan-review suites stay green.
- `_chunk` guard: with the scope's event pre-set, the pooled chunk funnel makes zero runner calls and serves no checkpoints.
- monotone/fail-open: a probe whose fingerprint read returns None (read error) does not cancel; the run proceeds to sign-time behavior.

Gates: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/workflow/` then the full `pytest tests/unit`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An own-material change observed at either seam cancels the review: INDETERMINATE, exit 2, no signature, no sidecar write, and the downstream verify/coach prompt steps are never invoked (checked: unit tests with call recording at both seams).
- [ ] A mid-run write to an unrelated ticket does NOT cancel, and related-material drift alone does NOT cancel (checked: d70a guard unit test comparing against an undisturbed run).
- [ ] The probe performs no fetch/reconverge and takes no sync lock (checked: unit test asserting the ensure_fresh sync path is never reached from a probe).
- [ ] With no mid-run change, review behavior and outputs are unchanged (checked: byte-identical verdict for fixed canned inputs in the offline harness + existing plan-review tests pass).
- [ ] The cancelled path can never sign or emit a sidecar: it returns before `attest.sign_plan_review` and `sidecar.emit` are reachable (checked: unit test asserting neither is called on a cancelled run).
baseline.summary: Cancel a plan review mid-run when the ticket's own material changes

# Usage-log pricing silently drops Anthropic and OpenAI rows: the provider-prefixed model_ref LookupErrors

## THIS IS A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THIS EPIC

Before the provider-seam work, the usage log recorded a BARE model id (`claude-opus-4-8`), which genai-prices resolves, so Anthropic prices displayed correctly. This epic made model strings PROVIDER-QUALIFIED, and `agent_call.py` records `model=ran_model` verbatim — so the stored id became `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, which genai-prices cannot resolve. `ran_model`'s history runs through this epic's own tickets: 747e149455 (2932, first-class Bedrock), cc33, e6bd, 8455, 5e75.

So the correct close class is `regression`, not `preexisting`, and this belongs INSIDE epic 061c rather than beside it.

## Mechanism

`usage_log._price_row` (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:412) passes the STORED `provider:model` string as `model_ref` to `genai_prices.calc_price`. When that id does not resolve, genai-prices raises `LookupError` — its unknown-model signal — which `_price_row` catches at :429 and turns into "unpriced". The catch is correct as a policy (pricing must never break `summarize`) but it makes the failure SILENT: the row is dropped from the cost total with no warning, because `LookupError` is swallowed before the `WARNING` branch.

## MEASURED against the installed genai-prices, using the same call shape as `_price_row`

    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6"            -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="anthropic", model_ref="claude-sonnet-4-6"                      -> OK  $0.004500
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4"                         -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4"                                -> OK  $0.004000
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="openai:gpt-5.4-mini"                    -> LookupError  (blank)
    provider_id="openai",    model_ref="gpt-5.4-mini"                           -> OK  $0.001200
    provider_id="bedrock",   model_ref="bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" -> OK  $0.004950
    control: provider_id="openai", model_ref="gpt-4o"                           -> OK  $0.003500

## The defect is ASYMMETRIC, and that is what makes it harmful rather than merely untidy

ONLY the `bedrock:` prefix form happens to resolve. Anthropic AND OpenAI both read blank. Every model involved is well known to genai-prices — the bare forms all price. So a provider cost comparison shows figures for Bedrock and nothing for the other two, which reads as "Bedrock is the expensive arm" when it is in fact the only arm being measured. That is a wrong-direction bias in exactly the comparison this epic exists to inform, and it is why the CI provider matrix's cost table [rebar:f124-f14a-fd62-4973] had to be computed BY HAND from logged token counts.

## Blast radius is not limited to CI

`summarize` renders the "est. cost" column for `rebar usage` output generally (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:444), so ordinary local and review-bot cost reporting is affected too, not only the external-integration job summary. The observable symptom is the `est. cost excludes N unpriced calls` line on runs where genai-prices demonstrably knows every model.

## Approach

Pass genai-prices an id it can resolve, keeping `provider_id` as the provider signal it already is.

The naive fix — strip everything before the first `:` — is WRONG for Bedrock, whose remainder (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) is not genai-prices' own AWS id shape either (its AWS ids look like `regional.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0`). So this needs a provider-aware translation, and per this epic's standing decision it must be decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP rather than prefix sniffing or a `split(":")` — the attested guard `test_capabilities_module_still_has_no_provider_name_prefix_matching` exists for exactly this class of shortcut.

Do NOT remove the `LookupError` -> unpriced policy; pricing must stay best-effort and must never break `summarize`. The fix is to stop feeding it an unresolvable id, and to make a genuinely-unknown model visibly unpriced rather than indistinguishable from a mis-formatted one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An Anthropic usage row PRICES rather than silently dropping to unpriced, proven by a test that
      FAILS before the fix on a realistic stored row (`provider="anthropic"`,
      `model="anthropic:claude-..."`).
- [x] An OpenAI usage row also prices — the fix covers ALL affected providers, not just Anthropic. A fix
      that handled only the `anthropic:` prefix would leave OpenAI blank and the comparison bias intact.
- [x] A Bedrock usage row still prices, and the Anthropic/Bedrock rate relationship is asserted so the
      asymmetry cannot silently return.
- [x] The id translation is decided by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, not by prefix matching or `split(":")`, and a
      test pins that — consistent with `capabilities.py`'s attested no-prefix-matching guard.
- [x] A model genuinely unknown to genai-prices is still tolerated as unpriced (pricing never breaks
      `summarize`) and is DISTINGUISHABLE in output from a row dropped because its id was mis-formatted.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: Usage-log pricing silently drops Anthropic rows: the provider-prefixed model_ref LookupErrors

Store only the SET of Jira keys seen last pass instead of the full ACLI payload. prev_snapshot is **228.1 MB / 4.5 MB per day** — the largest term after A1. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Measured effect
Over the newest **400 real revisions**: **218 of 399** consecutive pairs have an **identical key set** (so they become byte-identical and produce no commit at all), and when it changes the mean symmetric difference is **1.78 keys**. Key-set payload at HEAD is **19,960 bytes** vs a **27.1 MB** full payload.

## Why this is safe — gate G1 was cleared empirically, not by reasoning
A corpus mutation-diff ran the real differ plus the production `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` call-site filter over **four real snapshot pairs** with full prev vs key-set prev and found **zero difference in any observable mutation effect**. That filter is the load-bearing production guarantee: `run_differs.py` applies it before dispatch and drops both `(outbound, create, unbound_local)` and `(outbound, update, field_drift)` for either prev shape. Its removal note remains coupled to a future migration that passes real local state. Branch-3 also has defense in depth: `_mutation_to_batch_dict` reads `payload["changed_fields"]` for updates, which branch-3 never sets, so `fields` collapses to `{}` but the non-parent empty-fields path still invokes a no-op `update_issue(key)`; the load-bearing call-site filter remains the backstop that prevents this branch-3 mutation from reaching dispatch.

**It also removes wasted raw mutations.** With a full prev, keys in prev-but-not-curr make `compute_mutations` emit 973-998 `(outbound, create, unbound_local)` mutations when the fetch window shrinks or the project is re-targeted. The existing call-site filter already prevents those raw emissions from reaching `create_one` at HEAD. A key-set eliminates them at the source, reducing differ work and mutation-cap pressure without claiming a new Jira-facing behavior change.

Shape constraint: store a **dict** `{jira_key: {}}`, not a `set`. The prev-shape-sensitive consumers exercised here are `check_dual_identity_complete` and the differ's local-only / emit-both arms, whose `local_state[key] or {}` guards require mapping entries. The binding walk consumes `curr_snapshot` and a mutation-derived adopt-skip set, so it is unaffected. On the first pass after cutover the new reader tolerates an old full-payload prev; the same pass writes the key-set shape, and the committed full-vs-key-set corpus plus invariant tests cover that coexistence.

## Rollback (mandatory artifact)
The committed corpus runs both forward (full -> key-set) and backward (key-set -> full, the revert direction) comparisons. Deleting `prev_snapshot.json` is **not** a safe default escape hatch: an empty prev makes the differ re-derive inbound creates for curr-only keys unless a `rebar-id:` label suppresses them. If deletion is ever used, it MUST be followed by a cap-0/no-write pass proving zero unexpected inbound creates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Corpus mutation-diff (full prev vs key-set prev) over **>=4 real snapshot pairs** shows **zero
      difference** in any mutation reaching Jira with a non-empty effect. Tier: **repo-level corpus
      script** committed under the experiments path.
- [x] The **reverse-direction** diff (key-set -> full) is recorded on this ticket as the rollback
      artifact, showing the revert path emits no unexpected inbound creates. Tier: **repo-level
      corpus script**.
- [x] Branch-2 regression is gone: with a key-set prev and >=900 prev-only keys, **zero**
      `(outbound, create)` mutations are emitted. Tier: **unit** on `compute_mutations`.
- [x] `check_dual_identity_complete` behaves identically for full-payload and `{}` prev entries.
      Tier: **unit**.
- [x] The differ's local-only and emit-both arms preserve their intended outcomes with `{}` prev
      entries, including no field-bearing mutation reaching Jira unexpectedly. Tier: **unit**.
- [x] prev_snapshot at HEAD is <=64 KB after one pass. Verify: byte measurement.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` (prev persist), `run_differs.py`, `differ.py`, tests, corpus script

Scope: M. Depends on A4-1.
baseline.summary: A4-2: narrow prev_snapshot.json to a bare key-set {jira_key: {}}

## Context / Problem
The MCP `review_plan` tool (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) derives whether it signs a plan-review
attestation SOLELY from server read-only mode: it calls the library with
`sign=not ro, emit_sidecar=not ro`. There is no caller-facing `sign` parameter, so an MCP
client cannot request an explicit unsigned review the way a CLI caller can with `--no-sign`
or a library caller can with `sign=False`. Conversely, when read-only mode DOES suppress
signing, the returned verdict carries no machine-readable reason saying so — a client sees an
unsigned PASS and cannot distinguish "policy suppressed the signature" from "signing failed".

Split out of epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608 (uninformed-aspiring-rhino) on 2026-07-24: the CLI and
library boundaries of that epic are a test/help-hardening job, while this is a genuine public
API change to a different boundary with tool-schema and generated-reference consequences.

## Expected Behavior
- MCP `review_plan` accepts `sign: bool = True`, matching the library default.
- An explicit `sign=False` runs the review without signing, and the result names the caller's
  opt-out as the unsigned reason.
- Read-only server mode continues to suppress signing regardless of the requested value, and
  the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the read-only policy
  (distinct from the caller-opt-out reason and from a signing failure).
- The tool docstring states the sign-by-default contract and both unsigned exceptions.

## Approach
1. Add `sign: bool = True` to the MCP `review_plan` signature; pass `sign=sign and not ro`.
2. Introduce a machine-readable unsigned-reason field on the verdict distinguishing:
   `caller-opt-out`, `readonly-policy`, `not-signable` (BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/degraded/local),
   and `sign-failed`. Reuse the existing `signature.signed` boolean as the primary contract;
   the reason is additive, so existing consumers stay byte-compatible.
3. Update the tool docstring and regenerate `docs/mcp-reference.md`.

Rejected: inferring the reason client-side from the verdict shape — the read-only and
not-signable cases are indistinguishable without server knowledge, which is the bug.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (unsigned-reason plumbing, if the reason is
  produced at the finalization seam rather than the MCP boundary)
- MCP surface tests for plan review
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` (generated tool inventory / outputSchema)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MCP `review_plan` exposes `sign: bool = True`; a contract test proves the default
      persists an attestation and `sign=False` does not.
- [ ] With `sign=False`, the result carries a machine-readable unsigned reason identifying the
      caller opt-out; a test asserts the exact reason value.
- [ ] In read-only mode the result is unsigned regardless of the requested `sign` value and
      carries the read-only-policy reason, distinct from the caller-opt-out reason; a
      table-driven test covers (sign x readonly) combinations.
- [ ] A never-signable verdict (BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / degraded / local source) reports the
      not-signable reason rather than the opt-out or read-only reason.
- [ ] The MCP tool docstring states sign-by-default and names both unsigned exceptions;
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` regenerates cleanly and matches.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: MCP review_plan has no caller-facing sign opt-out and no machine-readable unsigned reason

# Persist ticket digest as a REVIEW_RESULT-style sidecar (shared cache)

## Why
The digest is a billable LLM artifact we never want to recompute (~$1.90 to enrich the whole 793-ticket store — see epic experiment comment). Storing it in the SHARED store (auto-pushed) makes one client's enrichment a cache-hit for everyone. rebar's exact precedent is `REVIEW_RESULT`: a reducer-IGNORED, preserved-and-ignored, per-ticket LLM-derived sidecar with a schema sentinel + a `prune` retention. We mirror it.

## What — payload schema (fully specified)
A `TICKET_DIGEST` sidecar event. Its `data` payload:
`{"schema": "ticket_digest_v1", "digest": {problem_keywords, component_or_area, key_entities, propositions}, "content_hash": "<hex>", "model": "<model-id>", "digest_hash_version": <int>}`.
The `schema` sentinel `"ticket_digest_v1"` guards reads (mirrors REVIEW_RESULT keying on `payload['schema'] == 'plan_review_result_v1'`) so a foreign/older payload is skipped, not mis-parsed. `content_hash`, `model`, `digest_hash_version` are the three freshness tags (named fields in the payload).

## Content hash — a LOCAL, self-consistent normalizer (no cross-layer import)
`content_hash = sha256(_normalize_text(state))` where `_normalize_text(state)` is a small
module-LOCAL function in `digest_sidecar.py` doing the canonical join (title + description +
comment bodies, `"\n".join`, empties skipped). It is deliberately LOCAL and NOT an import of
`rebar._engine_support.gates._ticket_text`: no `rebar.llm.*` module imports `_engine_support.gates`
(that would be a layering violation — the same reason S5/`ee3d` inlines its own join), and the
content hash is this story's OWN internal freshness key, so it need not be byte-identical to
any other module's normalizer. What matters is INTERNAL consistency: the SAME `_normalize_text`
is used both when writing (`emit`) and when checking freshness (read), so a hash computed at
write equals the hash recomputed at read for unchanged state. `DIGEST_HASH_VERSION` (module
constant in the sidecar) is bumped only if the hashed field-set ever changes, invalidating all
cached digests deterministically. (No dependency on S5's inline join — S5 does not hash; only
this story computes/consumes the content hash.)

## Freshness (computed on read, fail-closed)
The digest is CURRENT iff ALL of: stored `content_hash` == `sha256(_normalize_text(current))`
(via the SAME local `_normalize_text` used at write), stored `model` == active model, stored
`digest_hash_version` == current constant. Any mismatch → stale. If current state can't be read
(partial read) → NOT-current (fail-closed; never falsely fresh).

## Scope (exact edit targets — every registry a new event type touches)
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py`: the `_cmd_show` freshness render (detailed below). (No `gates.py` edit — the content-hash normalizer is local to `digest_sidecar.py`, see Content hash.)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: add `"TICKET_DIGEST"` to the `EVENT_TYPES` write allow-list AND its enumerated string in the StoreError message (lines ~97-103).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`: add `"TICKET_DIGEST"` to `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (NOT `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`) — preserved-and-ignored, never compacted into SNAPSHOT, no fsck WARN (mirrors REVIEW_RESULT).
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/__init__.py` (the package) + `src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py` with `emit(digest, ticket_id)` (appends + calls `prune`), `prune(ticket_id, keep=1)`, `latest_ticket_digest(ticket_id)` (guards on the `ticket_digest_v1` sentinel) — all modeled on `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`.
- `show` freshness render (CLI-show-ONLY — must NOT touch the library state shape):
  the parity invariant `test_show_list_search_share_one_shape`
  (`tests/interfaces/store/test_reducer_single_source.py:59`) asserts the **library** returns
  are identical — `set(rebar.show_ticket(id)) == set(list_tickets element) == set(search element)`
  and `show == lst == srch`. So `show_state`/`show_ticket` and `reducer/_present.py::public_state`
  (the SHARED key-stripping filter used by show/list/search/ready/MCP — NOT a show-only
  renderer) must be left untouched. The freshness flag ("present-fresh"|"present-stale"|"absent")
  is therefore added ONLY in the CLI show arm `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py::_cmd_show`
  (~line 144-171): after `state = show_state(...)`, `_cmd_show` computes freshness via
  `overlap.digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest(id)` + the freshness check and injects
  `digest_freshness` into the dict it prints (`json.dumps(state, ...)` and the `to_llm(state)`
  `--output llm` arm) — a CLI-presentation-only field that never enters the library
  `show_ticket`/`list`/`search` returns, so the parity invariant holds. No new field in
  `ticket_state.schema.json`; the digest stays a sidecar (like REVIEW_RESULT).
  `test_cmd_show_renders_freshness` asserts the CLI `show` stdout carries the flag;
  `test_library_shape_unchanged` asserts `show_ticket`/`list`/`search` still share one shape
  with a digest present (parity invariant held).
- Prune invocation: `emit` calls `prune(keep=1)` on every write — EXACTLY the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar pattern, nothing more. There is NO special archive/delete lazy-prune (that novel behavior is dropped: it has no `REVIEW_RESULT` prior art and `show_state` does not cleanly signal "gone" for archived tickets). An archived/deleted ticket's digest simply lingers as a harmless sidecar, bounded to ONE record per ticket by `keep=1`, and is never read into any hot path (like a stale REVIEW_RESULT). `latest_ticket_digest` does no existence check on the ticket.

## Dependencies
S1 (indecisive-callous-armyworm) — produces the `ticket_digest` payload. (The drain that decides to re-enrich lives in S4; this story owns only WRITE + READ + freshness of the sidecar, not the skip decision.)

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_ticket_digest_store.py`: `test_roundtrip`; `test_freshness_all_triggers` (stale on content-hash OR model OR digest_hash_version change); `test_hash_write_read_parity` (the content_hash written by `emit` equals the hash recomputed by the freshness check for UNCHANGED state — proving both paths call the SAME local `_normalize_text`; and an edit to title/description/comments flips it stale — proving the normalizer actually covers those fields); `test_fail_closed` (unreadable → not-current); `test_latest_wins` (two appends, latest-by-HLC); `test_older_binary_ignores` (fsck no WARN); `test_cmd_show_renders_freshness` (CLI `show` stdout carries the flag); `test_library_shape_unchanged` (show_ticket/list/search still share one shape with a digest present); `test_prune_keep1` (a second `emit` supersedes the first — exactly one `TICKET_DIGEST` retained per ticket).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `TICKET_DIGEST` write→`latest_ticket_digest` read roundtrip with the `ticket_digest_v1` sentinel guard; `pytest ...::test_roundtrip`.
- [ ] Freshness flips stale on ANY of content-hash / model / digest_hash_version mismatch; `::test_freshness_all_triggers`. The content_hash uses a LOCAL `_normalize_text` (no `gates` import); the write path and the freshness-check path use the SAME normalizer (write-hash == read-hash for unchanged state); `::test_hash_write_read_parity`.
- [ ] `TICKET_DIGEST` in `EVENT_TYPES` + `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (not `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES`); older binary preserves-and-ignores, no fsck WARN; `::test_older_binary_ignores`.
- [ ] Unreadable current state → NOT-current (fail-closed); `::test_fail_closed`.
- [ ] The CLI `show` stdout renders digest presence + freshness (not raw text) via `_cmd_show`; `::test_cmd_show_renders_freshness`. content.text: ## Summary
`rebar list --status=all` (or any invalid status value) silently returns an empty list instead of rejecting the value. An unrecognized filter value should be a loud error, not an empty result set.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar list --status=all` (all is not a valid status).
2. Observe: exit 0, output `[]`.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: non-zero exit + error naming the invalid status value and listing valid ones (open/in_progress/closed/blocked/deleted...).
- Actual: exit 0 with [] — indistinguishable from 'no tickets match'.
## Impact

Corrupted a real measurement during the 3006-e198 derisk experiments (an agent computed 614 false class-A drift candidates from the silently-empty list). Any agent or script filtering by a mistyped status silently operates on an empty world.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An invalid --status value exits non-zero with an error listing valid statuses.
- [ ] A test covers the invalid-status path (RED before fix).
- [ ] Valid statuses (and any 'all'-equivalent, if one is intended) are documented in `rebar list --help`.

baseline.summary: rebar list --status=<invalid> silently returns empty instead of erroring

# rebar's hardcoded Jira vocabularies disagree with a real DC instance in four places

## Provenance

Found by the capability-map job (run **30863672922**, ticket 259b) on its first execution — Jira DC 8.17.1, Server + Software licensed, a Scrum-template project. Every item below is a direct comparison of a rebar constant against what the instance actually offers, with the raw REST request/response recorded in that run's `evidence.json`.

None of these would surface as a test failure today. Three are silent by construction.

## The four defects

**1. Status `IDEA` does not exist.** `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA['idea'] = 'IDEA'` (`jira_family/value_maps.py`), but no status of that name exists in ANY workflow bound to ANY issue type on the instance. Every SCRUM type uses "Software Simplified Workflow for Project SCRUM", whose only statuses are To Do / In Progress / Done. **A local `idea` ticket can therefore never sync its status** — the mapped value matches nothing. Silent: the transition simply never resolves.

**2. Label limit is 254, not 255.** `JIRA_LABEL_MAX_CHARS = 255` (`value_maps.py:58`) is INCLUSIVE, but the instance REJECTS a 255-character label. The effective ceiling is 254. So a label of exactly 255 chars is fitted to the limit and then rejected by Jira — and per bug 6afc, ACLI exits 0 on that class of rejection, so it fails silently and re-emits. (`JIRA_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 254` was checked in the same pass and IS correct.)

**3. Two distinct issue types are both named `Task`** (ids 10003 and 10004). Any name-based type resolution is ambiguous and may bind to the wrong one, non-deterministically. rebar's `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` maps by NAME.

**4. Three link relations are unrepresentable on stock Jira** — `supersedes`, `discovered_from`, `caused_by` have no corresponding link type. `RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` maps only `blocks`, `depends_on` and `relates_to`, so those three silently do not sync. Whether that is intended is not recorded anywhere; it should be a documented decision rather than an accident.

## What the same pass CONFIRMED as correct, so it is not re-litigated

Issue types Bug/Story/Task/Epic all present; all five priorities (Highest..Lowest) present; link types Blocks and Relates present; **and the link DIRECTIONS verified end-to-end** — `blocks` and `depends_on` are true inverses of the single `Blocks` type, `relates_to` symmetric, all three confirmed by creating real links and reading both endpoints. That was the highest-risk vocabulary (a direction error inverts a dependency silently) and it is correct.

Transition names also equal their destination status names on this workflow, so bug 7f93's name-vs-destination hazard does not currently bite here — but that is a property of THIS workflow, not a guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] each of the four is triaged: fixed, or recorded as an accepted limitation with a reason
- [ ] the `idea` status gap has a decision — map it to an existing status, or state that `idea`
      tickets deliberately do not sync status
- [ ] the label limit is corrected to the enforced value, with a test that would catch an
      off-by-one against the instance rather than against a constant
- [ ] the duplicate `Task` name is handled by resolving types by ID where available, or the
      ambiguity is documented as harmless with evidence
- [ ] the three unmapped relations are documented as deliberate, or mapped
- [ ] the declared environment contract (3fe5) asserts these so a future instance change fails loudly
baseline.summary: rebar's hardcoded Jira vocabularies disagree with a real DC instance in four places

content.text: # Elevate trust-boundary crossing to an explicit framing in the T5c plan-review security overlay
## Context
Follow-up to a278 (container/leaf scrutiny + T10 endpoint-auth). Research on how mature
security / LLM-review projects avoid false positives converged on **trust-boundary crossing** as
the scope gate: a security concern is in scope only when a component is reachable by a LOWER-trust
actor (STRIDE Spoofing↔authn; OWASP ASVS 1.4.1 enforcement points; Semgrep/Anthropic
exploitability-over-category). Today T5c uses this idea only implicitly. Making it an explicit,
first-class framing (a) generalizes beyond auth to T5c's other dimensions and (b) sharpens the
reachability judgement — while keeping rebar's own local/in-process work false-positive-free.
Scope note: this is for **T5c only** — T10's `endpoint_access_contract` stays focused on infra
contract-completeness and must NOT be re-scoped to the general framing (approved: don't blur T10).
Files: `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` (rubric), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (T5c checklist if needed).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `plan_review_T5c.md` leads with an explicit TRUST-BOUNDARY scope gate: a security finding is in
scope only when the plan introduces/exposes a component reachable by a lower-trust actor
(public internet, another tenant, an untrusted network, an unauthenticated user); in-process /
local-CLI / loopback-only surfaces PASS as not-applicable.
- [ ] The framing GENERALIZES beyond auth: the same gate governs T5c's existing dimensions
(authn/authz, encryption-in-transit, least-privilege, secret lifecycle) — each fires only where
a boundary is actually crossed.
- [ ] Preserves the positive-pass carve-out (pure library / in-process module / single-user local CLI /
loopback-only → PASS, no auth demanded) so rebar's own local work stays FP-free.
- [ ] Zero-trust caveat encoded: a single-tenant / private network is LOWER severity, not exempt.
- [ ] T10 `endpoint_access_contract` is left unchanged (no blurring); a test/asserts T10 still fires
only on infra intent.
- [ ] Validation: recalibrated T5c run against `d251` (or an equivalent networked-service plan)
surfaces the security surface via the trust-boundary gate; run against a local no-network
negative (`8a1c`/`4702`) PASSes as not-applicable — old-vs-new documented.
- [ ] `validate-routing` + plan-review unit tests + `make lint` green.

baseline.summary: Trust-boundary framing for the T5c plan-review security overlay (generalize the scope gate; keep T10 focused)

content.text: ## Why

Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S3. R3 requires BOTH votes on every feature-branch change and on the merge change. The design EXPECTED g2p dispatch to be branch-agnostic; this story VERIFIES that and, per the verified finding below, REMEDIATES the gap it exposes. ASSUMES epic 1fa8 (smoky-flare-slug) is complete (g2p installed, gerrit-verify.yaml exists, two-vote submit active).
## VERIFIED FINDING (drives the revised scope)

g2p does NOT branch-filter dispatch (source: lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform@44d5d46 patchset_created.py / github.py / helpers.py — event->workflow mapping is filename-substring based, no branch keys in gerrit_to_platform.ini). BUT g2p dispatches via GitHub `workflow_dispatch(ref=refs/heads/{GERRIT_BRANCH})`, which REQUIRES that ref to EXIST on the GitHub mirror to resolve the workflow file. `replication.config` replicates only refs/heads/main + refs/tags/* + refs/changes/* — NOT refs/heads/feature/*. So a feature/* change's dispatch targets a non-existent GitHub ref -> 422/no-op -> the change gets LLM-Review but NEVER Verified and can never satisfy the two-vote gate. Proven live: change 198 on feature/s3-ci got LLM-Review+1 and zero CI. This is the exact failure the story exists to catch.
## What (REVISED — includes the remediation)
- **AC1 (verified statement):** record the g2p branch-filtering finding above (config or no-op) with source citation in the ini spec / a short g2p-dispatch note.

- **FIX (new, required for the story's CI-coverage evidence):** `infra/gerrit/replication.config` — add `push = refs/heads/feature/*:refs/heads/feature/*` to `[remote "github"]`, scoped to feature/* (NOT a wildcard, never refs/meta/*), so the workflow_dispatch ref resolves. Documented tradeoff: feature branches become transiently visible on the mirror (deleted after merge-back; teardown handled by S6 inventory + merge-back cleanup). **Deploy** to the running Gerrit via the gerrit_etc volume; `autoReload = true` in replication.config means the plugin re-reads on change with NO Gerrit restart (verified). Back-out: remove the line; a `.bak-s3` of the prior config is kept on the box.

- Verify `checkout-gerrit-change-action` fetches a MERGE refspec so CI builds the actual merge tree (get_change_refspec computes refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P identically for merge + normal commits — the patchset ref IS the merge tree; run-log evidence).

- Prove with run-log evidence: (a) a feature/* patchset-created triggers gerrit-verify.yaml and casts Verified (POST-FIX); (b) a merge change into main gets CI on the merge tree; (c) Verified RE-RUNS (does not carry) on a re-merge (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE); (d) `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` behaves sanely across concurrent branch + merge changes.
## Scope

g2p config + workflow verification + evidence, PLUS the replication.config feature/* fix + its live deployment (the prerequisite that makes feature/* CI possible — without it none of the run-log ACs can be produced). No label/ACL config (S1), no bot code (S2), no doc prose beyond the ini/dispatch spec (S4). The replication change is the minimal remediation, not new gate behavior.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verified statement on g2p branch filtering recorded (config or no-op), with source/doc citation, in the ini/dispatch spec
- [ ] replication.config replicates feature/* (committed) AND deployed live via autoReload (no restart); a newly-created feature branch auto-replicates to the GitHub mirror (proven)
- [ ] Run-log evidence: feature/* patchset triggers gerrit-verify.yaml and casts Verified (post-fix)
- [ ] Run-log evidence: merge change gets CI on the actual merge tree via the merge refspec
- [ ] Run-log evidence: Verified re-runs on a re-merge; no carry observed
- [ ] Concurrency behavior across branch + merge changes documented with a run example

baseline.summary: S3: CI (Verified) coverage on feature branches + merge changes — g2p dispatch verified
