baseline.description:
Wire the two-scope gate posture across the three gates, plumb resolution-class + sanitized diagnostic through the two verdict-returning gates, define the exit-11 contract, own the shared-file (runner.py) module-size reconciliation, enforce never-certify structurally, wrap the MCP failure surface, and document the model. Lands LAST (wave 3); INTEGRATION OWNER for the seams the other children touch.

## Why
The three gates must share a systemic *block-but-retryable* posture while PRESERVING per-criterion fail-open, carry `resolution_class` + `diagnostic` so routing and troubleshooting both work, expose a distinct-but-grounded exit code, never sign a degraded result, and tell the human exactly what to do.

## What

### Two-scope posture
A **systemic** failure → block-but-retryable (exit 11, unsigned) across the gates; a **per-criterion** failure → drop-and-continue fail-open (one flaky finder among N must NOT block a claim — PRESERVED, regression-tested). Make code-review match plan-review's existing systemic block; turn completion's fail-closed-as-FAIL into a distinct retryable exit (NOT a verification FAIL, which means "your work is wrong").

### The single source of retryability: `LLMOutcome`
mamba's `classify_llm_failure` returns an `LLMOutcome` with `resolution_class` (the closed 8-value enum) AND a pre-computed `retryable: bool`. Everything downstream reuses BOTH — the write-sites persist both into `coverage`; the CLIs read the persisted `retryable` bool directly and never re-derive retryability by string-comparing the class name.

### Two data-flow shapes
- **Shape A — plan-review + code-review return a DEGRADED VERDICT DICT.**
  - **Write-site:** `gate_dispatch._degraded_plan_review_verdict` / `_degraded_code_review_verdict` read `outcome = getattr(error, 'outcome', None)` off the caught `error` and, WHEN PRESENT, set `coverage['resolution_class'] = outcome.resolution_class.value`, `coverage['diagnostic'] = outcome.diagnostic`, and `coverage['retryable'] = outcome.retryable`.
  - **Reachability (verified):** `produce_plan_review_verdict` calls the helper three ways: `preflight` failure (`error=exc`), mid-run `LLMUnavailableError` (`error=exc`), and the finders-failed tail (`error=res.error`, a STRING). TODAY only mamba's run-seam attaches `.outcome`; `PydanticAIRunner.preflight` raises WITHOUT it. So this story ALSO attaches `.outcome` in `preflight` — `raise LLMUnavailableError(...)` becomes `exc.outcome = classify_llm_failure(exc, ClassifyContext(...)); raise exc` — so the common pre-call outage carries disposition too. The write-site reads `getattr(error,'outcome',None)`: present on the two exception paths (preflight now included), absent on the string finders-failed tail (→ plain INDETERMINATE, exit 2, correct — a finders-produced-nothing failure is not classified transient).
  - **code-review translation:** `rebar.llm.review_code` returns a `review_result` TRANSLATED from the gate `code_review_verdict` by `shim._verdict_to_review_result`. That translator is updated to COPY the gate verdict's `coverage` (with `resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic`) to the TOP-LEVEL `review_result['coverage']`, so `_review_code()` reads `result.get('coverage',{}).get('retryable')` directly (mirroring `_review_plan`).
- **Shape B — completion-verify FAILS by RAISING `LLMUnavailableError`** (no verdict dict). `transition_close._completion_precheck` (line ~174) has a broad `except Exception as exc: raise CommandError(...) from None` that TODAY discards the exception + its `.outcome`. Fix (SINGLE mechanism — no subclass, no new attribute): in `_completion_precheck`, before building the message, compute `_o = getattr(exc, 'outcome', None)` and `rc = 11 if (_o and _o.retryable) else 1`, then `raise CommandError(<class-specific message>, returncode=rc) from None`. `CommandError` already carries `returncode`, and `transition.py` already returns `exc.returncode` to the process — so exit 11 propagates with no plumbing change. There are TWO shape-B CLI surfaces with DISTINCT mechanisms: (a) the `rebar close`/transition path (`close_ticket`→`_completion_precheck`→`CommandError(returncode=11)`, above); (b) the standalone `rebar verify-completion` (`_verify_completion()`), whose OWN `except llm.LLMError as exc: return 1` arm (`_llm_commands.py` ~line 305) catches `LLMUnavailableError` directly — so THAT arm is updated to `_o=getattr(exc,'outcome',None); return 11 if (_o and _o.retryable) else 1`. Both shape-B arms also write the sanitized diagnostic to the session log (see below).

### Exit-code-11 contract
Retryable (`_o.retryable`, i.e. `WAIT_AND_RETRY`/`RETRY_NOW`) → exit **11** ("transient — retry", NEW). Any other non-null disposition → the gate's EXISTING INDETERMINATE exit. Null disposition → the existing PASS/BLOCK exit.
- **Exit 2 is NOT redefined.** `review-plan` ALREADY exits 2 for INDETERMINATE (pinned by arawana); UNCHANGED. Only the retryable subset is peeled to 11.
- **CLI sites (`_llm_commands.py`):** `_review_plan()` (shape A; tail currently `0/1/2` — extended to add 11) and `_review_code()` (shape A; TODAY always returns 0 on any verdict — updated to distinguish `0/1/2/11` off the preserved `coverage`). Shape B surfaces through TWO CLI entrypoints: `rebar verify-completion` (`_verify_completion()`) AND the `rebar close` / `rebar transition … closed` path (which reaches `close_ticket` → `_completion_precheck`; `transition.py` returns the `CommandError.returncode`, so exit 11 flows there too). `_review()` (the per-ticket `review_ticket` advisory reviewer) is NOT a site.
- **Message delivery:** the class-specific message (table below) is printed to STDERR as the line `llm-degrade: <resolution_class> — <message>` — shape B embeds it in the `CommandError` message; shape A renders it in `_review_plan`/`_review_code` from `coverage['resolution_class']` via a `_RESOLUTION_MESSAGES` lookup dict (the table below, keyed by class name).
- **Worked example:** a 429 degraded plan-review carries `coverage.retryable=True, resolution_class='WAIT_AND_RETRY'` → `_review_plan` exits 11; a 429 during `rebar close` raises `LLMUnavailableError`, `_completion_precheck` reads `.outcome.retryable` → `CommandError(returncode=11)` → the close exits 11 (fail-closed, unsigned).

### Per-class actionable messages (ResolutionClass → stderr text)
| ResolutionClass | Message |
|---|---|
| `WAIT_AND_RETRY` | Transient provider overload/rate-limit — wait for the backoff window, then retry. |
| `RETRY_NOW` | Transient connection blip — retry immediately. |
| `INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS` | Provider usage/quota ceiling hit — raise the provider limit or wait for the reset. |
| `CHANGE_SETTINGS` | The request exceeded a configured bound (tokens/steps/timeout) — adjust it and retry. |
| `CHANGE_INPUT` | The input was rejected (too large / malformed) — reduce or fix it and retry. |
| `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` | The model/provider is unavailable or refused — switch model/provider. |
| `FIX_AGENT_DESIGN` | An agent-construction bug (no tools / bad output contract) — fix the op wiring. |
| `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` | Unclassified failure — inspect the sanitized diagnostic. |

### Verdict-schema field (the two verdict-returning gates only)
Add OPTIONAL `coverage.resolution_class` (enum, 8 values), `coverage.retryable` (bool), `coverage.diagnostic` (sanitized object) to `plan_review_verdict.schema.json` and `code_review_verdict.schema.json` (their `coverage` is already `additionalProperties:true`, so this is documentary; readers tolerate unknown keys — forward/rollback-safe). **`completion_verdict.schema.json` is NOT changed** (shape B surfaces via the raised `.outcome`, no verdict dict — a field there would be dead). Sole writer of the schema edits.

### Session-log diagnostic write (calling convention, both shapes)
At each degrade site (shape A helpers AND the shape-B `_completion_precheck` arm), call `rebar.append_session_log(entry, summary=…, relates_to=<ticket_id>)` where `entry = json.dumps(sanitized_diagnostic, sort_keys=True)` (the sanitized dict, never the raw exception), `summary = f"llm-degrade {resolution_class} on <gate>"`, `relates_to` = the reviewed ticket id when available. Wrapped best-effort (`try/except Exception`): a session-log failure must NEVER fail the gate (regression-tested).

### Never-sign guard + pre-sign fingerprint recheck (at the CALLER, not generic `sign_manifest`)
`signing.sign_manifest(ticket_id, manifest)` is a generic multi-caller primitive with no verdict in scope, so the guards live at the SIGN-DECISION callers:
- **Never-sign guard:** at the plan-review sign path (`review_plan`) and the completion sign path (`close_ticket`), refuse to CALL `sign_manifest` when `verdict.get("verdict") != "PASS"` OR `verdict.get("coverage",{}).get("resolution_class")` is set. This makes the existing "degraded ⇒ unsigned" invariant STRUCTURAL (regression-tested). It introduces no new unsigned state (INDETERMINATE is already unsigned).
- **Pre-sign fingerprint recheck:** "material fingerprint" = the committed head SHA the verdict was verified against, which is ALREADY carried in the returned manifest as its `verified-at-sha:<sha>` step (`_verdict_manifest`). In `close_ticket`, INSIDE the write lock, immediately before calling `sign_manifest`, extract that sha from the manifest and compare it to a fresh `signing.head_sha(repo_root)` read; on mismatch (code drifted during the retry/timeout-widened verify→sign window) SKIP signing. The ticket STILL closes (the transition already committed) — this is the same closed-without-signature outcome as `--force-close`/`local`-source, so the close command EXITS 0 with a stderr warning "closed without a completion signature (code drifted between verify and sign)". Verify itself stays OUTSIDE the write lock (`transition_close` ordering preserved; asserted).

### MCP structured failure return (`_mcp_llm.py`)
The write-gated MCP tools (`review_plan`, `review_code`, `verify_completion`) in `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` today `return rebar.llm.X(...)` and let a raised `LLMError`/`LLMUnavailableError` propagate as a FastMCP tool ERROR (opaque to the agent). Wrap each body: on a raised `LLMError`, RETURN a structured result dict `{"error": str(exc), "resolution_class": <cls or None>, "retryable": <bool>, "diagnostic": <sanitized>}` (disposition read from `getattr(exc,'outcome',None)`), so the driving agent can branch on `retryable` instead of parsing an error string. (Shape-A tools already return a degraded verdict dict; this closes the shape-B/hard-error raise.)

### Integration ownership (shared files)
runner.py's module-size allowlisting (allowlist + ceilings 850 + `docs/architecture.md` remedy row) ALREADY LANDED with the anole commit in this stack (visible at `--ref HEAD`), so it is NOT a deliverable here. This story owns the final runner.py reconciliation (the `preflight` `.outcome` attachment above) and the taxonomy/retry/timeout docs, and lands LAST.

## Scope
- `gate_dispatch.py` degrade write-sites; `code_review/shim.py` (`_verdict_to_review_result` coverage preservation); `transition_close.py` (`_completion_precheck` returncode-11 + shape-B session-log; `close_ticket` never-sign guard + in-lock fingerprint recheck) preserving verify-outside-lock ordering; `_llm_commands.py` exit-11 mapping (`_review_plan`/`_review_code`/`_verify_completion`); `_mcp_llm.py` structured-failure wrap; `signing.py` (only if a caller-side helper is factored — the guard lives at the callers); the two verdict JSON schemas; `docs/exit-codes.md`; `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`; `docs/adr/`.
- NOT in scope: removing/weakening per-criterion fail-open; changing `completion_verdict.schema.json`; changing `sign_manifest`'s signature.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_review_plan()` exits 11 when the verdict's `coverage.retryable` is true.
- [ ] `_review_plan()` exits 2 (existing INDETERMINATE) when INDETERMINATE and `coverage.retryable` is false/absent.
- [ ] `_review_code()` distinguishes `0/1/2/11` off the preserved `coverage` (it currently always returns 0).
- [ ] `shim._verdict_to_review_result` preserves `coverage.resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic` onto the returned `review_result`.
- [ ] `_completion_precheck` raises `CommandError(returncode=11)` when the caught exception's `.outcome.retryable` is true, else `returncode=1`.
- [ ] `PydanticAIRunner.preflight` attaches `.outcome` (via `classify_llm_failure`) to its raised `LLMUnavailableError`, so preflight outages carry disposition.
- [ ] `_verify_completion()`'s `except llm.LLMError` arm returns 11 when `.outcome.retryable` is true, else 1.
- [ ] The `rebar close` / transition CLI path surfaces that returncode (exit 11) unchanged via `transition.py`.
- [ ] A degraded / INDETERMINATE verdict is emitted unsigned (never-sign guard at the caller refuses to call `sign_manifest`; regression test).
- [ ] The pre-sign head-SHA fingerprint (from the manifest's `verified-at-sha:` step) is re-checked inside the write lock immediately before signing; a mismatch closes unsigned and the close command exits 0 with a stderr warning (test for the mismatch path).
- [ ] Verify remains OUTSIDE the write lock (`transition_close` ordering asserted by a test).
- [ ] A degraded verdict/close prints the class-specific message (from the table) to stderr.
- [ ] The sanitized diagnostic is written to the session log at BOTH the shape-A and shape-B degrade sites via `append_session_log(json.dumps(diagnostic, sort_keys=True), summary=…, relates_to=…)`, best-effort (a session-log failure does not fail the gate; regression test).
- [ ] `coverage.resolution_class` (enum), `coverage.retryable` (bool), `coverage.diagnostic` (object) are optional properties on `plan_review_verdict.schema.json` and `code_review_verdict.schema.json`; `completion_verdict.schema.json` is unchanged.
- [ ] The shape-A write-site copies `resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic` from the caught error's `.outcome` when present (outage paths); the string-error finders-failed path yields a plain INDETERMINATE.
- [ ] Per-criterion fail-open preserved: a single flaky finder among N does not block (regression test).
- [ ] `_mcp_llm.py`'s `review_plan`/`review_code`/`verify_completion` return a structured failure dict `{error,resolution_class,retryable,diagnostic}` on a raised `LLMError` instead of propagating a FastMCP tool error (test for a degraded sub-path).
- [ ] `docs/exit-codes.md` gains a recorded-decision entry defining exit 11; `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py` pins 11.
- [ ] The exit-11 ADR (sections: Context, Decision — 11=block-but-retryable distinct from 2, Consumers+additive-safety, Rollback) enumerates consumers: the driving agent/human (docs/exit-codes.md), CI (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, `test.yml` — any-non-zero-is-failure, never invokes the gate CLIs so 11 is invisible to Verified), the review-bot (`src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` — votes off the verdict dict, tolerates open coverage keys); each additive-safe; rollback = retryable falls back to the existing INDETERMINATE exit (no data migration).
- [ ] The diagnostic-sanitization ADR (sections: Context, Allowlist + redaction rules, Threat model — keys/PII/hex/base64/email must never leak, Test coverage) is authored.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` are all green.

## Verified structural facts (experiment log — repo snapshot, offline)
```
Shape-B: transition_close.py::_completion_precheck (line ~174 broad except → CommandError from None discards .outcome; fix sets returncode from .outcome.retryable). CommandError (_commands/_seam.py) already carries returncode; transition.py returns exc.returncode (lines ~359/467).
Shape-A: gate_dispatch.py::_degraded_plan_review_verdict/_degraded_code_review_verdict. Called 3x: preflight (error=exc), mid-run (error=exc) → .outcome present; finders-failed (error=res.error STRING) → no .outcome → plain INDETERMINATE.
code-review CLI: rebar.llm.review_code → shim._verdict_to_review_result (translates verdict→review_result; must preserve coverage). _review_code currently returns 0 for any verdict.
CLI arms: _llm_commands.py::_review_plan (tail 0/1/2), _review_code, _verify_completion. rebar close/transition → close_ticket → _completion_precheck.
Schemas (coverage additionalProperties:true): plan_review_verdict.schema.json, code_review_verdict.schema.json (edited); completion_verdict.schema.json unchanged.
Signing: signing.py::sign_manifest(ticket_id, manifest) generic multi-caller; guard + head_sha recheck live at callers (review_plan sign path, close_ticket) — verify OUTSIDE write lock.
MCP: _mcp_llm.py review_plan/review_code/verify_completion return rebar.llm.X(...) (raise propagates as FastMCP error today).
Consumers: CI .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml + test.yml (make targets, not gate CLIs); review-bot src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py (verdict dict, not exit codes).
Exit contract: docs/exit-codes.md (0/1/2/10 frozen 2026-06-09) pinned by tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py; 11 additive.
```
Additive/rollback-safe: schema fields optional; exit 11 additive. Records the two NEW ADRs (exit-11, diagnostic-sanitization); transport-retry (0037) + async-watchdog (0038) already exist. Owns runner.py module-size reconciliation. Lands LAST.
baseline.summary: Two-scope gate wiring, verdict plumbing, never-sign guard, exit 11, docs

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Close a work ticket with the completion-verification gate enabled (verify.require_completion_verification_for_close=true).

2. For certain inputs (observed deterministically on ticket b593, a tiny pyproject metadata diff), the verify-step model emits its structured output as a top-level JSON **array** (a bare list of findings) rather than the completion_verdict **object**.

3. src/rebar/llm/structured.py validate_to() raises StructuredOutputError('structured output must be a JSON object, got list'); the workflow step 'decide@then/verify' fails and the close is blocked fail-closed.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: verifier tolerates/normalizes a single-verdict wrapped in a list (or the verify prompt/schema forces an object), producing a PASS/FAIL verdict.
- Actual: deterministic parse failure (5/5 attempts); the ticket cannot earn a signed completion attestation and must be --force-closed (left uncertified).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] tolerant_parse/validate_to in src/rebar/llm/structured.py robustly handles a top-level array carrying one verdict object (unwrap), OR the completion verify step constrains output to an object.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the 'got list' input and asserts a verdict is produced.
- [ ] Closing a previously-affected ticket earns a signed completion-verifier PASS.

baseline.summary: completion-verifier: top-level JSON array from verify model fails to parse (validate_to 'got list')

content.text: ## Why
The T2 semantic-resolution tier (epic `850f`) was deferred out of the v1 code-grounding floor as a
placeholder with three candidate backends and unresolved security/determinism tradeoffs. Before any
code lands, the selection and the confirm-only policy must be recorded as a durable decision, and the
IaC grounding lane (a different domain) must be split out so it is not silently folded into this epic.
This story produces that record; S2/S3 implement against it.
## What
- Add an ADR at `docs/adr/00NN-code-grounding-t2-semantic-resolution.md` (next free ADR number) that
records:
- **Decision:** v1 T2 backend = one-shot compiler/checker-CLI diagnostics, first language Python via
`pyright --outputjson`. LSP-client-library and containerized/hermetic tiers are **deferred** (with
their cost/security/determinism tradeoffs stated: LSP multiplies per-language server/runtime/config
surface; containerized needs an egress-locked single-tenant microVM sandbox because building
untrusted client repos is arbitrary code execution).
- **Confirm-only mapping:** a T2 `refuted` is emitted only when the checker ran to completion (file has no
import-resolution diagnostics = environment built) and there is no diagnostic at the reference;
every other case (tool-absent / unsupported-lang / no-file / parse-error / timeout / crash /
env-not-built / diagnostic-present) is `abstain` with a closed structured reason. T2 never asserts
an absence and never sits on a deterministic blocking path.
- **Minimal-seam decision (Rule-of-Three):** with one concrete backend, no `T2Backend` Protocol +
plugin registry — S2 ships a single `refute_semantic()` dispatch function selected by config. A
future backend adds a name + a branch.
- **Consumers unchanged:** T2 records reuse the existing three-valued contract and closed
vocabularies (`TIER_T2` already exists), so `5fd2`/`9da1` consumers need no edit.
- Reference the ADR from `docs/grounding.md` (a one-line pointer under the tiers section) so the design
is discoverable from the grounding doc.
- Create a **sibling epic** for the IaC grounding lane (`terraform validate` = IaC T1, Registry
provider/module existence = IaC T0, `terraform plan` = IaC T2) and `link <iac-epic> 850f relates_to`
so the split is recorded in the graph.
## Scope
In scope: the ADR document, the `docs/grounding.md` pointer, and the sibling IaC epic + link. Out of
scope: any `src/` change (that is S2/S3) — this is a design/doc-only story.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/0030-code-grounding-t2-semantic-resolution.md` exists and follows the repo's ADR
format (Status/Date/Context/Decision/Consequences headings, matching a sibling ADR's structure).
- [ ] The ADR records the backend-selection decision (pyright compiler-CLI diagnostics for v1).
- [ ] The ADR records the confirm-only mapping (`refuted` only on a completed run with no
import-resolution diagnostics and no diagnostic at the reference; every other case `abstain`).
- [ ] The ADR records the minimal-seam (no-registry) rationale and the LSP/containerized deferral with
their stated tradeoffs.
- [ ] `docs/grounding.md` links to the new ADR from its tiers/T2 section.
- [ ] A sibling epic for the IaC grounding lane exists, linked `relates_to` epic `850f`, with a
description scoping the IaC T0/T1/T2 tiers.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] The change touches only files under `docs/` (no `src/` edits).

## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Builds on **ddbe** (identity + mappings) and **264f** (`resolve_mapping`), committed
on this branch, not yet on origin/main. Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
An inbound external user (e.g. a Jira assignee/reporter with an `accountId` +
`displayName`) that has NO local identity mapping mints a PLACEHOLDER identity
storing the raw `(provider, external_id, display_name)`. Re-running resolution after
a real mapping appears UPGRADES the placeholder in place — idempotently, one identity
not two — keyed on the provider's stable opaque id (Gitea's OriginalAuthorID
discipline).

## Why
When rebar pulls a Jira ticket, its assignee/reporter/comment authors are external
Jira users we may not yet know. Minting a durable placeholder (keyed on the stable
accountId) preserves attribution without guessing an email, and lets a later real
mapping enrich the SAME identity rather than forking a duplicate.

## What
### 1. Resolve-or-mint seam (`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py`)
`ensure_identity_for(provider, external_id, display_name, *, repo_root=None) -> str`:
- IDEMPOTENT resolve-first: call `resolve_mapping(provider, external_id, repo_root=...)`
  (264f). If it returns an existing identity id, RETURN it (do NOT create a second) —
  this is what makes a re-run yield ONE identity. Optionally UPGRADE: if that identity
  is still a placeholder and `display_name` is non-empty and differs from its current
  title, update the title in place (`edit_ticket`) — the upgrade path.
- Else MINT a placeholder: `create_identity(name=display_name or external_id,
  email="", mappings=[{"provider":provider, "external_id":external_id}], ...)` marked
  as a placeholder via a `placeholder` tag set ATOMICALLY at mint: extend
  `create_identity_core` / `create_identity` with an optional `tags` list that is
  forwarded to `create_core(..., tags=...)` (create_core already accepts `tags`), so
  the CREATE event carries `tags=["placeholder"]` in one event (no separate tag() call,
  no tagless window). `is_placeholder` checks the `placeholder` tag in compiled state
  (the reducer surfaces CREATE tags). Return the new id.
- Never raises for a lookup problem (a resolve failure falls through to mint).
- `is_placeholder(identity_id, *, repo_root=None) -> bool` helper (the `placeholder`
  tag is present).
- The mapping key is ALWAYS the provider's opaque `external_id` (never email), so the
  resolve/upgrade is provider-neutral (works for jira/github/gitea alike).

### 2. Placeholder → real upgrade
When a real mapping/identity is later established for the same `(provider,
external_id)` — either a subsequent `ensure_identity_for` with a better
`display_name`, or an operator enriching the identity (email/keys) and removing the
`placeholder` tag — the SAME identity id is reused (resolve-first keys on
`external_id`). A test adds a real name/email to the placeholder, re-runs
`ensure_identity_for(same provider/external_id, ...)`, and asserts exactly ONE
identity exists for that mapping (not two) and it is the upgraded record.

### 3. Inbound reconciler wiring (`apply_inbound_records.py`)
Where the inbound apply reads the inbound Jira ASSIGNEE (the only inbound user field
today — `_extract_name(fields["assignee"])` at ~lines 113/258, which pulls the
`displayName`), ALSO resolve the inbound user through `ensure_identity_for("jira",
<accountId>, <displayName>)` so an unmapped inbound user mints/reuses a placeholder
identity and the local attribution references a stable identity. Keep the existing
name extraction as the human-readable fallback; the identity minting is additive and
best-effort (a missing accountId falls back to the name-only behavior without
failing the inbound apply).

## Scope
In: `ensure_identity_for` + `is_placeholder` (idempotent resolve-or-mint, keyed on
external_id, placeholder tag, in-place upgrade) and the inbound-apply wiring. Out:
outbound mapping (264f), enforcement (3183). Concurrency: minting is idempotent for
SEQUENTIAL re-runs (resolve-first); the reconciler applies inbound records single-
writer, so no concurrent double-mint of the same accountId is expected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensure_identity_for("jira", <accountId>, <displayName>)` on an accountId with
  no existing mapping creates a placeholder identity whose title is the displayName,
  whose `mappings` contains `{"provider":"jira","external_id":<accountId>}`, and which
  `is_placeholder` reports True (test).
- [ ] Re-running `ensure_identity_for` with the SAME `(provider, external_id)` returns
  the SAME identity id and does NOT create a second — a test asserts exactly ONE
  identity maps that accountId (list/search count == 1) after two calls, even when the
  second call supplies a different display_name (which upgrades the title in place).
- [ ] The mapping key is the provider's opaque `external_id` (not email), so an
  upgrade for a different provider/id is independent — a test with two different
  `external_id`s yields two distinct identities, and the same `external_id` under a
  different `display_name` still yields one.

- [ ] Inbound wiring (best-effort): given an inbound Jira assignee field with an
  `accountId` + `displayName` and no existing mapping, applying the inbound record
  mints/reuses a placeholder identity for that accountId (test drives the inbound
  apply path with a fixture record and asserts a placeholder identity exists for the
  accountId); a record missing an `accountId` falls back to name-only behavior WITHOUT
  failing the inbound apply.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (ensure_identity_for + is_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` + `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (export ensure_identity_for/is_placeholder)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` (resolve inbound Jira user via ensure_identity_for, additive/best-effort)
baseline.summary: identity: inbound ghost/placeholder + idempotent auto-upgrade

content.text: The plan-review gate's **Pass-2 verifier returns an empty `verifications` list**, so every Pass-1 finding reaches `pass3_decide` with no verification → `decision: indeterminate, reason: "no-verification"`. When ALL findings are no-verification (zero resolved), the verdict is forced INDETERMINATE, which is NOT signable → the plan-review claim gate blocks the ticket. This blocked epic 5ca8's children (clay-cake-act: 0 blocking, deterministic floor all PASS, 4 findings all no-verification → INDETERMINATE across multiple plan-hardening passes). It affects ANY `mode="structured"` prompted LLM op (the same json-repair path).
## Root cause (proven via joe-debug, runtime evidence)

The structured-output reliability stack (story 1268) has two paths in `_pai_structured` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`): a NATIVE path (`Agent(model, output_type=mode_obj)` — schema enforced) and an Anthropic PROMPTED path that generates FREE TEXT then tolerantly parses (json-repair). `structured.output_mode` returns `PromptedOutput(model_cls)` for Anthropic (which would inject the schema into the prompt), BUT the prompted branch built `Agent(model, **kwargs)` with `output_type=str` and **discarded `mode_obj`** — so the JSON schema was NEVER conveyed to the model. The model, knowing fields only from the verifier prompt's PROSE ("severity ATTRIBUTES", "BINARY sub-answers"), emitted plausible-but-divergent keys — captured live:
{"findings": [{"index": 0, "attributes": {...}, "sub_answers": {...}}]}

instead of the `plan_review_verification` contract shape `{"verifications": [{"index", "severity_attributes", "binary"}]}`. `VerificationOutput` ignores unknown keys, so tolerant parsing produced `VerificationOutput(verifications=[])` — a VALID, EMPTY object, no error raised. Instrumented run: `verify-step … verifs_per_chunk=[0] merged_verifs=0` → `decide: findings=4 raw_verifs=0` → all 4 no-verification.
## Reproduction Steps
1. `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 rebar review-plan <a-task-with-code-grounded-findings> -o json`.
2. Inspect `indeterminate` findings — all carry `reason: "no-verification"`; `blocking`/`advisory` empty; verdict INDETERMINATE despite the deterministic floor passing.
- **Expected:** the verifier emits schema-conforming `verifications` (keyed by 0-based `index`); `pass3_decide` resolves each finding to advisory/dropped; the verdict reaches PASS/BLOCK.
- **Actual:** the verifier emits a divergent JSON shape (schema never conveyed) → empty `verifications` → all findings no-verification → INDETERMINATE.
## Fix
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`: add `schema_directive(model_cls)` rendering the model's JSON Schema with a "use these EXACT keys; JSON only" directive.

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` `_pai_structured` PROMPTED path: append `schema_directive(model_cls)` to the initial prompt AND the bounded-retry prompt, so the model is told the exact output shape (restoring the schema-conveyance that `PromptedOutput` provides and the json-repair refactor dropped). NativeOutput path unchanged.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The prompted structured path conveys the output JSON schema to the model (a unit test with a schema-aware FunctionModel proves a `mode="structured"` run yields non-empty, correctly-keyed structured output only because the schema reached the prompt; mutation-checked).

- [ ] An OFFLINE unit test (a schema-aware `FunctionModel`, the repo's standard way to test LLM behavior without a billable call) proves the prompted structured path conveys the schema so a `mode="structured"` run yields non-empty, correctly-keyed output — RED before the fix, GREEN after, mutation-checked (`tests/unit/test_runner_structured_schema.py`). The end-to-end live `rebar review-plan` going INDETERMINATE → PASS (4 no-verification → 0 indeterminate, 2 resolved advisories) is recorded as the replication in PR #74 (not an in-repo test, since a real review-plan requires a live LLM).
- [ ] No regression: the runner-hardening / structured / pydantic-ai runner suites pass; `make check` clean.

baseline.summary: Plan-review verifier returns empty verifications (schema not conveyed in prompted structured path)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Bug 828a found that `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` told authors to name a rejected alternative, while the authoritative G6 criterion (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G6.md`) explicitly says NOT to require one because it primes implementers. The drift survived a month.

The packaged prose guides cite criterion ids inline as if authoritative — 15 distinct ids in the plan guide alone (`G6` on lines 77/130/289, `F1`, `E2`, `COH`, `ISF`, …), in both bare (`(G6)`) and backticked (`` (`G6`) ``) form — yet nothing couples them to the criteria registry. `validate_criteria_guide()` (`plan_review/registry.py:652`) is scoped by `_GUIDE_RELPATH` to the GENERATED `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` only. `tests/unit/test_guides.py` couples the guides to `coach_moves.MOVE_REGISTRY` only. So a criterion's rubric can be rewritten and every prose paraphrase of it silently becomes a lie.

## Approach — a citation PIN manifest (the prose is never regenerated)

A gate cannot mechanically judge whether prose accurately paraphrases a rubric; that is a semantic call. What it CAN do is refuse to let a cited criterion change **silently**. So the gate converts an invisible semantic drift into a visible, forced re-verification:

For every criterion id a packaged guide cites, pin a digest of that criterion's authoritative registry text. When the criterion's text changes, the pin no longer matches and the gate fails, naming the guide, the criterion, and the remedy: re-read the criterion, confirm the guide's claim about it still holds, then re-pin.

This reuses the existing **regenerate-in-place + parity-diff** contract exactly — but the regenerated artifact is a DERIVED PIN MANIFEST, not the guide body. The hand-authored prose is never rewritten by a generator, so the objection that prose guides "cannot be regenerated the way `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is" does not apply: nothing regenerates them here. `regenerate_guide_criterion_pins()` writes the manifest; `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` diffs it — the same shape as `regenerate_criteria_guide()` / `validate_criteria_guide()` and as the `reviewers/index.json` drift gate.

### The interface the checker depends on

The extractor keys ONLY on the registry's **closed criterion-id vocabulary** (`CANONICAL_LLM`), matched at word boundaries against the guide text. It depends on NO structure or markup in the guides — no heading convention, no section layout, no fence — so ordinary prose edits (rewording, reordering, adding sections) cannot break it, and a guide restructure is not a gate failure. Both citation forms are matched by construction, since backticks are not word characters. Digests are computed over `_guide_section_body(criterion)` — the same rendering `rebar explain <id>` serves — so scenario text, checklist, posture, exec tier, and facet are all inside the pin.

The manifest is generated over the PACKAGED built-ins only (`load_criteria(repo_root="")`, as `regenerate_criteria_guide` already does), so a project's `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay can never rotate the shipped pins.

### What the gate reports

1. **unknown citation** — a guide cites an id absent from the registry (renamed/removed
   criterion): the guide must be updated.
2. **stale pin** — a cited criterion's digest differs from its pin: its text changed, so the
   guide's claim about it must be re-verified and re-pinned.
3. **orphan pin** — a pin exists for an id no longer cited: prune it.
4. **missing manifest** — the pin file is absent: run the regenerator.

## Scope

- **NEW** `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/guide_parity.py` — extraction, digesting,
  `regenerate_guide_criterion_pins()`, `validate_guide_criterion_pins()`, and the
  `regenerate` / `validate` `_main`. It is a NEW module, not an append to
  `plan_review/registry.py`: that file is 755 LOC against the LOCKED hard cap of 800 in
  `.github/module-size-limit.txt`, so appending it would fail the CI module-size gate.
- **NEW** `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — the generated manifest, packaged
  alongside the guides it pins so it ships and is diffable in review.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — one line: fold
  `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` into the `validate-routing` composition at `:744`
  (`validate_packaged_routing() + validate_criteria_guide()`), which
  `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:386` already runs. No new CI step is needed.
- `tests/unit/test_guides.py` — the gate's tests.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — a short subsection telling guide authors and criterion authors what the
  gate enforces and how to clear a failure (`regenerate` after re-verifying the claim), so the
  new constraint is discoverable rather than only surfacing as a red build.

## Testing

- Mutating a cited criterion's registry text makes `validate_guide_criterion_pins()` report a
  stale pin naming that criterion and the guide that cites it (the 828a class).
- A citation of an id absent from `CANONICAL_LLM` is reported as an unknown citation.
- A pin whose id is no longer cited is reported as an orphan.
- An absent manifest is reported with the regenerator command.
- Regeneration is idempotent and canonical (byte-identical on a second run).
- The committed manifest is in sync with the registry (the drift gate itself).
- A prose-only edit that adds no new citation does NOT fail the gate (no false positive on
  ordinary guide edits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A criterion-text change that contradicts a claim in a packaged prose guide fails a gate;
      verified by mutating a criterion in a test and asserting the gate reports the divergence
      naming the criterion and the citing guide.
- [ ] The gate covers every guide in `AUTHOR_GUIDES`, not just the plan guide; verified by a
      parameterized test over `AUTHOR_GUIDES`.
- [ ] The gate runs in CI without a new workflow step, by composition into `validate-routing`;
      verified by a test asserting the composed `_main` surfaces a pin problem.
- [ ] Regeneration is idempotent and the committed manifest is in sync; verified by tests.
- [ ] A guide edit that changes prose without changing citations does not fail the gate;
      verified by a test.
- [ ] No `src/rebar` file exceeds the 800-LOC cap.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Gate parity between packaged prose guides and the criteria registry

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A 344-bug corpus analysis (session log 5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5) identified recurring escape channels: surface-parity gaps, contention semantics missed at authoring time, inert/miswired config, wall-clock flakes, unlocked store writes, auto-filer breakage, prose-only provenance rotting in code comments, and bug fixes landing without plan review. Each child was individually design-reviewed and approved by the operator (decision table in the session log; per-change experiments under /tmp/exp*.py referenced in child descriptions).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Bug provenance is observable at creation (detected-by) and trend-queryable (bug_trends metrics lens), without new required user input.
- [x] Deterministic pre-LLM gates exist for: raw git writes bypassing the store seam, unread config schema fields, upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests, unchecked AC checkboxes at close, historical-context rot in code comments, and oversized bug-fix diffs lacking a current plan-review attestation.
- [x] The reconciler transport is typed end-to-end, declared field asymmetries are pinned by property tests, and pagination loops are deduplicated into shared iterators.
- [x] Production shell logic (reconcile-bridge/canary workflow bodies, probe harness, vote normalizer) is migrated to Python per the strangler-fig policy.
- [x] Canary/automation bug filing follows the hardened dedup pattern and a documented bug-creation contract.
- [x] Engine-layer validation placement is advisory-enforced at plan review.
- [x] rebar-debug and rebar-implement skills (and the shared test-design standard) encode the approved discipline upgrades: ticket writebacks, two-axis invariant sweeps, surface census, config-effect contrast, case-(c) contention triggers, gate-finding oracle upgrades, and residual-gap disposition.
- [x] Explicit review-plan on a bug runs a real review, and the Gerrit backstop blocks oversized bug fixes lacking one.
- [x] Code comments citing dead SHAs/run-ids/dates are remediated to ticket citations, with a CI guard preventing regression.
baseline.summary: Bug-trend prevention program: observability, gates, migrations, and skill discipline from the 344-bug analysis

baseline.description:
## What
One-time backfill: run the conservative blame -> commit -> ticket resolver over existing closed bugs to draw `caused_by` links retroactively, seeding source-of-bugs history.

## Files
- `scripts/backfill_caused_by.py` — new: iterate closed bugs, reuse `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, draw `caused_by` on high-confidence single culprits; `--dry-run` default.
- `tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py` — new.

## Test tier
The test lives under `tests/scripts/` with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.scripts` (the scripts tier; `tests/unit/scripts/` does NOT exist). External tools are stubbed/mocked so the test is deterministic and needs no scc/lizard/jscpd installed.

## Approach
Reuse the same conservative single-culprit resolver as the live auto-derivation (no new heuristic) so backfilled links are deterministic and consistent with going-forward ones. Idempotent via an EXPLICIT existing-link check: because the low-level `rebar.graph._links._write_link_event` writer has NO built-in idempotency (a closed-bug backfill must write via it, bypassing `add_dependency`'s closed-source guard), the script guards the write itself — before writing it calls `rebar.graph._links._is_active_link(bug_id, culprit_id, "caused_by", tracker_dir)` and SKIPS the bug when an active `caused_by` edge to that culprit already exists. `--dry-run` by default so a run previews before writing; back-out is removing the additive links.

## Tests
- Unit (temp store + git): over a fixture of two closed bugs (one single-culprit, one ambiguous), the script proposes exactly one `caused_by` link; a second run is a no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py` passes: the script links the single-culprit bug and skips the ambiguous one (`assert links == 1`).
- [ ] re-running is idempotent — the test runs the script in WRITE mode (`--write`, NOT dry-run) twice: the first pass draws the caused_by link, and the second pass draws 0 new links because the bug already carries an active `caused_by` to its culprit (the script checks `_is_active_link` before writing). (`--dry-run` is the DEFAULT for safety; the idempotency AC explicitly opts into write mode.)
- [ ] the backfill actually executes end-to-end: the test invokes the script's entry point (write mode) over a fixture store of two closed bugs (one single-culprit, one ambiguous) and asserts exactly ONE caused_by link is drawn (to the single-culprit's resolved ticket) and the ambiguous bug gets none — proving the script runs the real resolver, not just that a helper exists.
baseline.summary: Backfill caused_by links over existing closed bugs (blame)

baseline.description:
# Asymmetric attestation foundation — DSSE envelope + SSHSIG scheme + pluggable-scheme substrate

## Context
rebar signs its attestations (plan-review, completion-verifier verdicts) with a **symmetric HMAC**
keyed on a per-environment secret (`src/rebar/signing.py`; `.signing-key` / `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY`).
Two upcoming capabilities — per-person **authorship** signing (the identity epic) and
third-party-verifiable **operation certificates** (the op-cert epic) — both need **asymmetric**
signatures (verify-by-anyone, forge-by-none) over attestation bytes, verified offline. Building
that signing layer twice would duplicate security-critical code and worsen the namespace collision
already forming on the `SIGNATURE` event type / `signature` / `key_id` fields. **Beneficiary:** the
two consumer epics (and their end users) — they get one hardened, standards-based signing substrate
instead of two divergent stacks.

## Approach (and why)
Reuse established standards rather than hand-roll crypto:
- **DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope)** as the envelope, signing `PAE(payloadType, body)` over
  exact opaque bytes. PAE eliminates the JSON re-serialization / canonicalization attack class (we
  never re-serialize parsed JSON to verify) and carries **no in-band `alg`** the verifier trusts —
  closing the JWT `alg`-confusion class (RFC 8725). DSSE is the Sigstore/in-toto/SLSA standard;
  ~30 lines, offline, scheme-agnostic.
- **SSHSIG via OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y`** (stdlib `subprocess`, **no new core dependency**) as the
  first asymmetric scheme — reuses the reference implementation and developers' existing SSH keys;
  verified offline against an `allowed_signers`-format trust input. Fail-closed was confirmed
  experimentally (wrong namespace / unknown principal / substituted key / tampered bytes / expired
  window all exit non-zero; `-Y check-novalidate` is structure-only and is never used for authz).
- **Pluggable scheme registry + per-kind policy table** (`kind → {scheme, namespace, trust-root}`),
  pinned out-of-band; the verifier **never** selects the scheme from record data. The existing
  **HMAC is registered as a legacy scheme** so current attestations keep verifying unchanged (this
  is the expand phase; the HMAC→asymmetric cutover for operation-certs is the op-cert epic's
  contract phase).

Alternative considered and rejected: `securesystemslib` for signing — it has **no SSH signer** (so
it would not cover the authorship path) and pulls `cryptography` (heavy) for Ed25519; core stays
stdlib-only.

## Scope
- **In:** a new attestation-substrate module (DSSE envelope + PAE; scheme registry; SSHSIG scheme
  via subprocess; per-kind policy table; verify-dispatch with domain separation); registration of
  the existing HMAC as a legacy scheme; an ADR; unit/behavioral tests.
- **Out:** any identity entity or authorship kind (identity epic); any change to operation-cert
  behavior / actor / enforcement (op-cert epic); **removing** HMAC (op-cert epic's contract phase).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new module (e.g. `src/rebar/attest/`) exposes `sign(kind, body_bytes) -> envelope` and
      `verify(kind, envelope, trust_root) -> verdict`, where `kind` selects `{scheme, namespace,
      trust-root}` from an out-of-band policy table (not from the envelope). A unit test asserts a
      record whose in-band scheme field is tampered still verifies under the policy-pinned scheme
      (no `alg` confusion).
- [ ] DSSE PAE is implemented per the v1.0.0 spec
      (`PAE(type,body)="DSSEv1" SP len(type) SP type SP len(body) SP body`), proven by a unit test
      against the spec's worked example; a test with duplicate/re-ordered JSON keys demonstrates
      verify operates on the exact stored bytes and does not re-serialize.
- [ ] The SSHSIG scheme signs and verifies via `ssh-keygen -Y` in a subprocess using argv arrays
      (no shell), branches only on exit code, and allowlist-validates namespace + principal. A test
      matrix asserts fail-closed on: tampered bytes, wrong namespace, unknown principal, substituted
      key, and expired validity window.
- [ ] The existing HMAC signer is registered as a legacy scheme; a plan-review/completion-verifier
      attestation created before this change still returns verdict `certified` (regression test).
- [ ] `ssh-keygen` availability/version (>= 8.9 for validity intervals) is detected; its absence
      fails closed with a clear error (test asserts no silent pass).
- [ ] An ADR under `docs/adr/` records the substrate: DSSE envelope, pluggable scheme, per-kind
      policy table, domain separation, HMAC-as-legacy.
- [ ] One signing substrate exists that both consumer epics import; no consumer needs its own crypto.
- [ ] Signatures are produced/verified over DSSE-PAE bytes; verification never re-serializes parsed JSON
- [ ] The SSHSIG scheme signs/verifies offline via `ssh-keygen` with **no new core runtime dependency**
- [ ] Existing plan-review / completion-verifier attestations still verify (HMAC as a registered legacy

## Intended decomposition (children)
1. DSSE envelope + PAE module (+ spec-example + duplicate-key tests).
2. Scheme registry + per-kind policy table + verify-dispatch (domain separation; alg-confusion test).
3. SSHSIG scheme via `ssh-keygen` (fail-closed subprocess contract + test matrix).
4. Register existing HMAC as a legacy scheme (regression test).
5. ADR + docs.

## Prior art / grounding
DSSE protocol v1.0.0 (secure-systems-lab/dsse); in-toto attestation; OpenSSH PROTOCOL.sshsig +
`allowed_signers`; git SSH commit signing (`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`); RFC 8725 (JWT BCP);
RFC 8785 (JCS, considered and rejected in favour of DSSE PAE). Fail-closed behavior of
`ssh-keygen -Y verify` confirmed by direct experiment in this environment (OpenSSH 10.2).
baseline.summary: Asymmetric attestation foundation — DSSE envelope + SSHSIG scheme + pluggable-scheme substrate

content.text: ## Why

Audit Reliability finding #1 (HIGH). Two clones can both claim the same open ticket (the write lock is per-clone). On merge the STATUS fork resolves deterministically (lower event UUID wins, `reducer/_processors.py` ~L145) and `assignee` resolves by HLC last-writer-wins, but **both agents were told CLAIMED** and proceed to duplicate work. The resolved fork is only a replay-time `logger.warning("PARENT_CHAIN_FORK_RESOLVED …")`, surfaced by no user-facing command. There is no two-clone concurrent-claim test (audit 7.1); `test_store_concurrency.py::test_claim_storm_one_winner` is single-clone.
## Design (two independent mechanisms)

- **Ownership is the authority for "who works this ticket": the `assignee` field** (HLC last-writer-wins). Claim-loss detection is based ONLY on assignee — it does NOT depend on the STATUS-fork tiebreak or on any `loser_env_id` (which is unreliable on reopened tickets). A successful `claim` keeps its existing contract; the new exit-10 is a best-effort signal that fires when a merged view already shows another clone owns the ticket.
- **The STATUS-fork resolution is surfaced separately** (for observability) via a pure derived-state record read by fsck/show.
## What / files

1. **Pure derived-state fork record** — `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, at the fork-resolution branch (right after the `PARENT_CHAIN_FORK_RESOLVED` warning), append a DICT (note: a dict literal with keys and values, NOT a set) to derived state:
`state.setdefault("status_fork_resolutions", []).append({"winner_uuid": winner_uuid, "dropped_uuid": loser_uuid})`

Pure/idempotent — rebuilt identically on each full replay; NO alert_store/repo_root/external I/O. (loser_env_id is intentionally NOT stored — it is unreliable across reopens and is not needed, since claim-loss uses `assignee`.)

2. **fsck finding** — `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py`: in the existing reduce loop, when a reduced ticket has a non-empty `status_fork_resolutions`, `lines.append(f"STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED: {ticket_id} — concurrent claim/status race resolved (dropped uuid=...)")` and `issue_count += 1`. ALSO add the kind `"status_fork_resolved"` to `_STRUCTURED_KINDS` (fsck.py:32) so the JSON transform parses out `ticket_id` into the structured `--output json` object (not just `{kind, detail}`).
3. **show surfacing** — `show <id> --output json` renders the full reduced ticket state, so the new `status_fork_resolutions` field appears automatically; no formatter change is needed.

4. **Best-effort claim-loss signal** — `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` `claim_compute`, after `push.push_after_commit(tracker)`: reduce the ticket from the LOCAL store; if its resolved `assignee` is set and `!= assignee` (this claimant) — i.e. a competing claim that was already on the remote won the merge that `push_after_commit` performed — raise `ConcurrencyMismatch` (**exit 10**) with a "claim lost on cross-clone merge (now assigned to <winner>)" message. If the assignee is still this claimant (no competing merge visible), return success unchanged.
5. **docs** — `docs/concurrency.md`: a short note under the fork-resolution invariant (I8) documenting the derived record → fsck/show and the best-effort assignee-based exit-10.
6. **Tests** (two):

- **(a) reducer replay-idempotency unit test** — `tests/unit/test_reducer_status_fork_record.py` (new): reduce an event log with two concurrent forking STATUS events; assert the reduced ticket has one `status_fork_resolutions` dict entry with the correct `winner_uuid`/`dropped_uuid`; reduce the same log again and assert the field is byte-identical (pure/idempotent, not a growing side effect).

- **(b) two-clone integration test** — `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` using `two_clones`, SEQUENTIAL ordering: clone A claims the ticket and pushes to the shared remote; clone B (ticket still open locally) then claims — B's `push_after_commit` fetches+merges A's winning claim, so B's post-push re-read sees `assignee == A`. Assert: (i) B's claim returns exit 10 / raises ConcurrencyMismatch (the exit-10 path EXERCISED explicitly); (ii) the converged `assignee` is A and identical across both clones after they sync; (iii) the merged ticket carries `status_fork_resolutions`, `fsck` emits `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`, and `show <id> --output json` includes the `status_fork_resolutions` field.
## Scope

In: `reducer/_processors.py`, `_commands/fsck.py` (finding + `_STRUCTURED_KINDS`), `_commands/claim.py`, `docs/concurrency.md`, the two tests. Out: changing the fork-resolution rule (lower-UUID-wins stays, I8); a bespoke text annotation for `show`; distributed locking; storing loser_env_id.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Resolved STATUS forks are recorded as DICT entries in PURE derived state by the reducer (no I/O/alert_store/repo_root), asserted by `tests/unit/test_reducer_status_fork_record.py` (entry correct AND byte-identical across two replays)

- [ ] `fsck` emits a `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` finding and `"status_fork_resolved"` is in `_STRUCTURED_KINDS`, so `fsck --output json` carries a structured `ticket_id` for it (asserted in the two-clone test); `show <id> --output json` includes `status_fork_resolutions`

- [ ] The best-effort claim-loss path returns exit 10 when the post-push re-read shows another clone is the `assignee`, and success otherwise; the two-clone integration test EXERCISES the exit-10 path explicitly (asserts exit 10 / ConcurrencyMismatch)
- [ ] The two-clone test asserts a deterministic converged assignee identical across both clones + the fork surfaced (fsck + show)
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the surfacing behaviour; `make test` green

baseline.summary: Surface lost cross-clone claims: post-claim verification, fsck/validate/show fork surfacing, two-clone claim test

baseline.description:
## Context

The Jira<->local reconciler (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`) has accumulated 23 hard-won parity lessons (L1-L23), each a reactive fix to an observed drift. Parity was claimed ENUMERATIVELY (fix the field, claim parity for it), so drift kept appearing in the un-enumerated states BETWEEN the point-fixes. A 2026-07 audit comparing Jira REB (606 issues) vs the local store (600 tickets, 606 bindings) found four un-healed drift classes that `bridge-fsck` reports as clean:

- **A (444d)** local archive/delete never propagated to the bound Jira issue.
- **B (5854)** Jira-native issues never adopted at steady state.
- **C (13eb)** confirmed bindings to deleted Jira issues never GC'd when the local ticket is archived.
- **D (8de5)** `bridge-fsck` blind to binding-level drift.

Unified root cause: the reconciler is EDGE-triggered and driven from the wrong index (the active local snapshot + `prev_snapshot`) instead of LEVEL-triggered from the binding store. The invariants this work must preserve are documented in ADRs 0026-0029.

## Scope (RE-SCOPED 2026-07-03)

This epic's acceptance is the **landed in-repo code deliverable**: the level-triggered classifier + per-binding baseline + convergence property tests + the four drift-class heals (A/B/C/D) + safety rails + the Phase-1 rollout derisk (dual-write shadow, breaker enforcement, rollback docs) — all merged to main through Gerrit and unit-tested. The **operational rollout tail** (every-mode decision census breadth, the high-risk Phase-3 prev_snapshot->baseline consumer-flag flip, and its gate of >= N clean live shadow passes + the capped live heal of the 7 known instances) requires live production Jira and the deployed 20-min workflow, so it is carved to follow-up **lofty-beech-twang (a118)**, owned by the deployed-workflow operator. The full rollout design (Phases 1-4, ADRs 0026-0029) is preserved there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pure classifier `classify(local, jira, binding, baseline) -> Decision` encodes the full state matrix (local x jira x binding); every cell defined and table-tested. — landed on main.
- [ ] A per-binding last-synced BASELINE replaces `prev_snapshot`'s merge role WITHOUT removing direction arbitration (preserves L1 / commit `16870dbec`; the corrected P4). The corrupt-baseline fail-closed abort is preserved. — baseline machinery landed; the live consumer-flag flip is carved to a118.
- [ ] Convergence property test: apply the classifier's Decisions, then re-reconcile -> ZERO actions, from randomized states (catches A/B/C). Plus no-orphan, conservation, and direction-preservation (a teammate's Jira-side edit is never clobbered) properties. — landed on main.
- [ ] Multi-pass stateful + fault-injection tests that faithfully persist the baseline between passes (the root of B) and assert self-heal on partial failure. — landed on main.
- [ ] One classifier, TWO consumers: the live pass acts; `bridge-fsck` (offline, reads `bindings.json`) + `reconcile_check` (online) report (heals D). — landed on main.
- [ ] Safety rails: GC/terminal only on confirmed-404 grace (never snapshot-absence, L13/L16/L17); circuit breaker refuses a pass mutating/retiring > N% of bindings; per-binding quarantine; per-pass metrics. — landed on main.
- [ ] All six children closed with their guardrails met; ADRs 0026-0029 landed. Execution order: FOUNDATION amiss-bun-wince (baf7) FIRST -> the four drift-class heals (A=port-jar-withe/444d, B=undo-grape-frost/5854, C=false-topaz-prong/13eb, D=hale-cameo-basin/8de5) -> ROLLOUT soar-quill-flare (7d23) LAST. — done: all six children closed (7d23 closed on its re-scoped code deliverable).
- [ ] Rollout behind the mode ladder (reconcile-check report -> dry-run -> bootstrap -> live) with a shadow phase; the workflow_dispatch mode input on .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml is the rollback brake. — mode ladder + shadow + rollback brake landed; live promotion is an operator action tracked on a118.
- [ ] FROZEN-ARTIFACT CENSUS REPLAY TEST (derisk 2026-07-03): a regression test replays the classifier over sanitized frozen production artifacts (614 bindings / 614 issues) and asserts EXACTLY the 7 known acting decisions (5x TERMINAL_TRANSITION REB-464/456/465/466/457, 1x PROBE/GC REB-530, 1x ADOPT REB-532) and nothing else, then asserts fixed-point on re-classify after simulated heal. — landed on main.
- [ ] OPERATIONAL TAIL carved to follow-up lofty-beech-twang (a118), owned by the deployed-workflow operator: every-mode decision-census breadth; the Phase-3 consumer-flag flip gated on >= N clean live shadow passes; the capped live heal of the 7 known drift instances with next-pass census = 0. Not in this epic's in-session scope. — carved out; provenance preserved via discovered_from 7d23.
- [ ] Reconciliation is expressed as a LEVEL-TRIGGERED controller with a per-binding baseline; CONVERGENCE to a fixed point is a TESTED PROPERTY, not a claim.
- [ ] All four drift classes (A/B/C/D) are healed and cannot recur (regression cells).
- [ ] Every existing lesson L1-L23 is preserved (no regression); the corrected P4 KEEPS the three-way-merge baseline (ADR 0026).
- [ ] Prior-art safety rails (confirm-before-destroy, circuit breaker, quarantine, metrics) are in place.

## Notes

Prior art surveyed: Kubernetes controllers / Flux / Argo CD / Terraform / Crossplane (level-triggered reconcile, prune-off-by-default, `allowEmpty` mass-delete guard) and Unito / Exalate (adopt-by-match, provenance echo suppression, per-field 3-way merge, quarantine). This epic converts enumerative parity CLAIMS into a tested convergence PROPERTY.

## Derisk evidence (2026-07-03, pre-implementation)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

An orphaned store write-lock froze the review-bot's startup on the Gerrit host for over an hour on 2026-07-31, causing seven consecutive autodeploy failures (CloudWatch alarm `rebar-autodeploy-errors`, 18:21 UTC onward). The lock could never be reclaimed, by design, and would not have self-healed.

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`:
- `_owner_stamp()` (:152-154) writes `f"{socket.gethostname()}:{os.getpid()}"` into the lock dir.
- `_mkdir_lock_is_stale()` (:171-190) returns `False` unless `host == socket.gethostname()` (:184).

Inside a container `socket.gethostname()` is the **container id**, and docker assigns a NEW one on every `compose up -d` recreate. So a lock orphaned by the SAME host's previous container is classified as a **foreign-host** lock — the shared-filesystem case the guard was written for — and is never reclaimed. There is no age-based ceiling, so the orphan is permanent.

The conservatism itself is deliberate and correct in its intended setting; the docstring says "never reclaim on anything short of proof (bug yaw-gravel-linen)". The defect is that **hostname is not host identity inside a container**, so the foreign-host branch misfires for what is actually the same host.

## Observed (production, 2026-07-31)

- Lock dir `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets/.ticket-write.lock.d/`, created 18:30:49, owner stamp
  `1e0fab75d5bd:3085`. Container `1e0fab75d5bd` ran 18:03:46-18:30:55 and was SIGKILLed mid-store-write
  when a deploy recreated it (it logged a completed code_review artifact link and `Shutting down` in
  the same second).
- Every later container has a different id, so `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returned False forever.
- `run_ensures()` (`_store/ensures.py:158`) calls `write_lock()` with the defaults
  `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2` = a 60s budget, then swallows `LockTimeout`. Startup
  therefore took ~62s instead of <4s, exceeding autodeploy's `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30`, so every deploy was
  rolled back to `:prev`.
- Journal evidence (spans 2026-07-03 -> 2026-07-31): 197 `is a writable rebar store` lines vs 183
  `ensure env-id` lines = 14 lock-timeout boots, ALL on 2026-07-31 from 18:30:49 onward, zero in the
  preceding four weeks. `.ensure-applied` remained stamped at the last successful sweep, 18:03.
- Cleared manually by removing the orphaned lock dir; this ticket is the durable fix.

## Approach

Make the owner stamp stable across container recreates on one host (e.g. boot_id + pid, or a start-time-qualified pid) so a same-host orphan is provably reclaimable, and/or add an age-based reclaim ceiling so a lock that cannot be proven live is reclaimable after a bounded interval. Keep the existing refusal-without-proof behaviour for the genuine shared-filesystem case.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — `_owner_stamp`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`, `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`.
- Tests for the container-recreate scenario and the shared-filesystem scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A lock orphaned by a dead process on the SAME host is reclaimable even when the recorded
      hostname differs because the process ran in a since-recreated container; verified by a test that
      simulates a changed `gethostname()` with a dead pid.
- [ ] A lock owned by a LIVE process is still never reclaimed, and a genuinely foreign-host lock is
      still not reclaimed on the strength of hostname alone; verified by tests (no regression of
      bug yaw-gravel-linen).
- [ ] An unprovable lock does not block indefinitely: either an age ceiling applies or the failure is
      surfaced rather than silently swallowed into a 60s stall.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Store mkdir lock is permanently unreclaimable inside a container: gethostname() is the container id, so a same-host orphan looks foreign-host

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Plan review LLM calls run at the flat DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS (16000, src/rebar/llm/config.py:269) with no output-budget raise anywhere in the plan-review call sites. A structured response that exceeds the ceiling raises UnretryableOutputError (src/rebar/llm/structured.py; runner.py:628-651 degrades to INDETERMINATE) — observed live on epic a492's container review: one bin over 17 children failed after 333s, and the S7-landed exhaustiveness directive (enumerate every independent defect in one run) deliberately increases per-call finding output, widening this exposure. Truncation here has only bad outcomes: a full-cost re-review or silent loss of critical findings. The completion verifier was remediated for the same family by RAISING the output token budget (completion_recovery.py raises max_tokens, :207/:222); plan review needs the comparable remediation. Operator goal: allow effectively unlimited output tokens for plan-review calls — output is naturally bounded by the model's actual findings, and unspent max_tokens costs nothing.

## Approach
Operator scope extension: the remediation covers ALL review workflows and ALL their LLM passes — plan review (Pass-1 chunks/AGENT/container/ISF/prerequisite, Pass-2 verify + novelty + completion sub-calls, Pass-4 coach, xchecks), the four-pass code review (base finder, Round-A/Round-B overlays, Pass-2 verify, Pass-4 coach — which the Gerrit review-bot inherits), the completion verifier's PRIMARY call (its recovery path already raises; the main call must get the same model-max floor), and review_ticket. scan_spec and the overlap judge are out of scope (not review gates; their outputs are small and schema-bounded). Raise every covered call's output budget to the RESOLVED MODEL'S MAXIMUM output capacity (the API requires a finite max_tokens, so model-max IS the unlimited setting). Mechanism: the runner already lets a request raise the config floor (runner.effective_max_tokens — a request may only raise, and req.output_token_limit still clamps down where bounded recovery needs it). Add a per-model max-output lookup — check first whether the just-landed ModelProfile capabilities seam (change 1014, f184: read capabilities from ModelProfile) exposes max output tokens and use it; otherwise a small table beside sizing.largest_window_tokens with a conservative fallback to the current default for unknown models. Apply it at the plan-review request builders: Pass-1 finder chunks and AGENT criteria, container bins, ISF finder/summarizer, prerequisite finder, and the verify/coach workflow steps (whichever do not already scale via output_tokens_per_item — the verify agentic arm's existing per-item scaling and 64000 ceiling may be replaced by or reconciled with model-max; state the final rule uniformly). Bounded-recovery paths that intentionally clamp via output_token_limit are untouched. Verify timeout interaction: larger max_tokens must not trip request timeouts (cfg.timeout_s; the SDK's streaming requirement for long requests is handled at the transport — confirm by reading anthropic_model.py). Alternative rejected: per-bin child-count scaling (this ticket's earlier draft) — still an arbitrary ceiling; any finite budget below model-max re-creates the truncation class the operator ruled out.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py (request builders), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py (or the ModelProfile seam: model max-output lookup, shared by all workflows), src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/completion-verification.yaml (step budgets reconciled to the one model-max rule), src/rebar/llm/completion.py (primary verifier call floor), src/rebar/llm/operations.py (review_ticket), code-review step builders under src/rebar/llm/code_review/ as needed, tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py (new, covering every workflow's request fields), tests updated where they pin request max_tokens.

## Testing
Unit with a recording FakeRunner: every plan-review request carries max_tokens equal to the resolved model's max output (per the lookup) and never below DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS; unknown model falls back to the default; output_token_limit clamps still apply where set; the verify arm's budget follows the stated final rule; existing plan-review workflow tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every LLM request in the plan-review, code-review, and completion-verification workflows plus review_ticket carries the resolved model's maximum output budget, floor-raised through the existing runner contract (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` asserting request fields per workflow and per pass, including code-review overlays and the completion verifier's primary call).
- [ ] Unknown/unmapped models fall back to the current default without error (checked: unit test).
- [ ] Bounded-recovery output_token_limit clamps are unaffected (checked: existing recovery tests pass).
- [ ] A synthetic oversized-findings container fixture that previously raised UnretryableOutputError at 16000 completes under the raised budget (checked: unit test with a FakeRunner that enforces the request ceiling).
baseline.summary: plan-review container bins have no output-token scaling (UnretryableOutputError on large child sets)

baseline.description:
# Attested signing: pin verified_at_sha via the signed manifest channel

## Why

A signed verdict is only worth anything if it is reproducible and bound to specific content.
Today the verdict signs a manifest and stores git `head_sha` as AUDIT METADATA ONLY
(signing.py) — nothing cryptographically pins WHAT code was verified. Attested mode must
resolve->pin->record->sign the immutable SHA. (Claim-gate ref-resolution coherence is a
sibling story; this slice is the attested-signing pin only.)

## What

- Bind the SHA through the EXISTING MANIFEST CHANNEL, NOT a new signed-payload field.
  `signing._canonical_payload` signs exactly `{v, algorithm, ticket_id, manifest}` and
  `sign_manifest`/`compute_signature` already sign the full `manifest: list[str]`. Carry the
  pin as a MANIFEST STEP (`verified-at-sha:<sha>`): it enters the signed bytes (bound +
  reproducible) WITHOUT touching `_canonical_payload` or bumping `PAYLOAD_VERSION` — so NO
  invalidation of prior certified closures. The manifest-vs-payload signing decision is
  recorded in the architecture ADR.
- Record `verified_at_sha` as a queryable ticket field (convenience metadata; the trust anchor
  is the manifest step). Keep the existing `head_sha` audit field AS IS (additive).
- Resolution boundary: resolve the client `ref` (default `origin/main`) to an immutable SHA;
  an UNRESOLVABLE ref in attested mode fails closed (no sign).
- Atomicity MECHANISM (named, not just asserted): the combined manifest pin + `verified_at_sha`
  ticket write is serialized through the ticket's existing event-append / optimistic-concurrency
  boundary (compare-and-set on the current SHA), so concurrent retries / races between two
  verifications against different SHAs cannot interleave (no check-then-act TOCTOU). Set-once
  per SHA; re-verifying a DIFFERENT SHA overwrites (no stale/double pin).
- verified_at_sha lifecycle: on REOPEN/abandon the pin is retired (cleared/invalidated) so a
  stale SHA never outlives its closure; local-mode runs never set it.
- Bar signing in `local` source mode: verify + report, NO signature.
- Shape the manifest pin so a future move to DSSE + asymmetric + transparency log is an envelope
  swap, not a rewrite (KEEP HMAC now; limits documented in S6).

## Scope

- In: manifest-channel SHA binding (no payload-version bump), `verified_at_sha` field +
  lifecycle, resolution boundary + fail-closed, atomic/idempotent/overwrite pin with a named
  serialization mechanism, local-mode signing bar, in-toto envelope shape.
- Out: claim-gate ref-resolution coherence (sibling story); snapshot/cache (S1/S2); HMAC-trust
  docs (S6, dependency).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An attested PASS adds a `verified-at-sha:<sha>` MANIFEST STEP covered by the signature;
      verifying certifies the SHA. No `_canonical_payload` change, NO `PAYLOAD_VERSION` bump
      (regression test: pre-existing signatures still verify). The decision is recorded in the ADR.
- [ ] `verified_at_sha` is a queryable ticket field; re-running against the same SHA reproduces
      a verdict + manifest over identical content; `head_sha` audit field preserved (additive).
- [ ] The pin + field write is serialized via the ticket's event-append/optimistic-concurrency
      (compare-and-set) — proven by a concurrency/retry test (two writers racing, and a re-verify
      against a different SHA overwrites with no stale/double pin); NOT verified by inspection.
- [ ] On reopen/abandon the `verified_at_sha` pin is retired (no stale SHA outlives the closure);
      a `local`-mode run (dirty allowed) never sets it and never emits a signature.
- [ ] An unresolvable ref in attested mode fails closed (no signature).
- [ ] The manifest pin is shaped as an in-toto-style statement so the HMAC envelope can be
      swapped for DSSE/asymmetric later without changing the pin's data shape (covered by a test/contract).
baseline.summary: Attested signing: pin SHA, record verified_at_sha, in-toto-shaped HMAC, claim-gate coherence

## What
