# P1.1 — Structured query: field predicates, OR, negation, --sort

## Context (problem + research)

rebar `search` is whitespace-split, case-insensitive **AND of substrings** with a
few fixed flags (`reducer/search.py:search_states(states, query, *, status,
ticket_type, has_tag)`, confirmed by EXP-R10). No OR, no field-scoped predicates
(`assignee:`, `priority:<2`), no caller-controlled sort, no saved queries. Agents
post-filter in their own code, fragmenting behavior. Comparable trackers expose
richer query: Fossil offers SQL report queries; git-bug a `status:open label:x
sort:` query language. This is a read-only, low-risk, high-daily-value upgrade
(I3-clean — no writes).

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP8: a ~40-line parser does field predicates + `OR` + negation + degrade-to-
  substring (unknown `field:` -> literal substring, no crash).
- EXP-R10 (real code): confirmed the real `search_states` and
  `apply_ticket_filters(results, *, type_filter, status_filter, parent_filter,
  tag_filter, priority_filter, without_*...)` signatures — the integration seams.

## What / Implementation detail

1. New `reducer/_query.py` parser: tokenize; recognize `field:value`
   (`status:`, `type:`, `priority:` incl. `<`/`>`, `assignee:`, `tag:`,
   `parent:`) with exact match (tag = set membership; parent accepts id OR alias,
   resolved to full id before matching), leading `-`/`not:` negation, and **comma-OR
   within a field** (`status:open,in_progress`) as the only OR mechanism in v1 — there
   is NO bare `OR` keyword (a literal `OR` degrades to a substring). `priority:` uses
   GitHub range operators `<`,`<=`,`>`,`>=`,`n..m`. Free text still matches the existing
   `_haystack`. Unknown `field:` -> literal substring.
2. Expose one `match_predicate(state, field, op, value)` in `reducer/_filters.py`
   shared by `_query.py` and `apply_ticket_filters` (one comparison vocabulary).
3. `--sort/-s` in `_engine_support/reads.py` + `_reads.py`: keys
   `priority|created|updated|id|status`, `-key` descending; default sort unchanged
   so goldens hold. **Do not** touch `reducer/_sort.py` (that is event replay order,
   not presentation sort).
4. Parity across CLI (`--sort`, help texts), library (`sort=` kwarg), MCP
   (`sort` + bumped inputSchema).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `reducer/_query.py` parser (predicates, comma-OR, negation, substring fallback) + unit tests
- [ ] `updated_at` computed during replay as running max(created_at, every replayed event ts); set on the reduced dict; `process_snapshot` re-seeds the max from the SNAPSHOT `compacted_at` (replay skips pre-snapshot events)
- [ ] `compact.py` strips `updated_at` from the reduced dict BEFORE serializing `compiled_state`; SNAPSHOT event bytes byte-identical with/without the change (canonical-bytes parity test holds) — no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no new event type
- [ ] latest-event-ts accumulator added to the replay loop; compacted-then-untouched ticket asserts `updated_at == compacted_at`
- [ ] None-last `(is_none, value)` tuple sort key applies to ALL sort keys incl `created`/`updated` (never `key or 0`)
- [ ] shared `match_predicate` in `_filters.py` used by both query and filters
- [ ] `--sort` on list/search/ready (CLI), `sort=` (library), `sort` (MCP inputSchema)
- [ ] parity test across all three interfaces + a sorted-list golden
- [ ] back-compat: plain substring search byte-identical to current output

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.1).
- [ ] `search "status:open,in_progress priority:<2 assignee:alice"` (comma-OR within a
- [ ] A plain `search "login"` returns byte-identical results to today (back-compat).
- [ ] No event-schema change; no SCHEMA_VERSION bump.
baseline.summary: P1.1 — Structured query: field predicates, OR, negation, --sort

content.text: ## Why
The epic's headline deliverable is a STABLE internal API both review gates consume — one implementation, not
two. This story integrates Engine A, T0, and Engine B behind the three query surfaces and pins the
consumer-facing contract so `5fd2` (DET floor P2/P3/P4) and `9da1` (Pass-2 grounding) can build against it.
## What
- The public **oracle API** exposing the three query surfaces over the engines:
`refute_absence(reference) -> evidence`, `applies(dimension, repo) -> evidence`, and
`scan(repo, *, detectors=None, dimensions=None, path_globs=None) -> [evidence]` (job-3 smell/metric scan;
`None` = all applicable) — each returning the normalized three-valued evidence model + coverage (shape fixed by spike E5).
- The **consumer integration contract**: the reference-in schema (DEFINED + validated in S2 — S5 EXPOSES and
documents it, never redefines it), and the **closed dimension-ID vocabulary OWNED HERE** (the registry of
applicability dimensions a consumer passes to `applies()` / a detector declares — initial set
`{web_frontend, has_iac, touches_auth, has_migrations, has_tests, …}`, versioned), plus the detector identifiers
and how coverage is surfaced — documented so `5fd2`/`9da1` wire up deterministically.
- **Docs**: how the oracle works; the fail-open behavior + the CLOSED reason enum + coverage semantics; the
detector envelope format + the `.rebar/detectors/` convention; the **`.rebar/` language-extensibility slot**
(project ctags optlib / tree-sitter custom grammar) and configurable metric thresholds; the loader's
pre-validate/quarantine behavior; and the CLI/library/MCP entry points (read-only; mirrors existing rebar
read-tool patterns).
## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/__init__.py` (public surface) + a thin CLI/MCP read-tool exposure + `docs/`.
- Depends on S2 (Engine A), S3 (T0), S4 (Engine B). Pure-evidence: no block/advisory logic.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Stable public API for the three query surfaces over the three engines, returning the evidence model + coverage.

- [ ] Typed signatures for all three surfaces (incl. `scan`'s); the closed dimension-ID vocabulary DEFINED + owned here (consumers/detectors draw from it); reference schema only EXPOSED (defined in S2); coverage surfacing; `5fd2`/`9da1` can build against it.

- [ ] Read-only CLI/library/MCP read-tool entry points consistent with existing rebar read tools — INCLUDING a canonical `.schema.json` in `src/rebar/schemas/`, registration in `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`, and a schema-conformance test (the typed-read-tool convention).

- [ ] Docs updated AND existing docs refreshed (T7): the new grounding read tools/schemas added to the CLAUDE.md MCP "Reads" list + docs/output-schemas.md, alongside API / fail-open + reason enum + coverage / detector format / `.rebar/detectors/` / language-extensibility slot / thresholds / loader-quarantine docs.

content.text: # Cluster 2 — unify the two `_advisory_lock` backoff functions into one parameterized helper
## What
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` contains two structurally identical
jittered-exponential-backoff functions — both compute `min(base * factor**i, cap) *
uniform(1 - jitter, 1 + jitter)` — that differ only in their constants:
- `_compute_backoff_seconds(retry_index)` — `_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS=0.2`, `_BACKOFF_FACTOR=2.0`,
`_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=5.0`, `_BACKOFF_JITTER_FRACTION=0.3` (used by `acquire_pass_lock`, budget
`_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT=5`).
- `_cas_backoff_seconds(retry_index)` — `_CAS_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS=0.05`, factor `_BACKOFF_FACTOR`
(=2.0, already shared), `_CAS_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=1.0`, `_CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER_FRACTION=0.3` (used by
`_cas_advance_with_retry`, budget `_CAS_RETRY_BUDGET=8`).
Collapse the shared math into ONE parameterized pure function `_jittered_backoff(retry_index, *,
base, factor, cap, jitter_fraction)` that performs exactly one `random.uniform` call (preserving the
RNG draw count/order, so a seeded sequence is identical). Keep `_compute_backoff_seconds` /
`_cas_backoff_seconds` as thin wrappers that bind their respective constants, so the two call sites
and the two retry **budgets** are unchanged. This is the single genuine in-file duplication
identified by the audit; the other retry sites solve different problems and are intentionally left
bespoke (see parent epic `civil-marlin-flare`).
## Why
One backoff formula in one place is observable and tunable; two hand-copied copies drift silently.
Behavior is preserved exactly — both budgets keep their constants and the formula is unchanged.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py` has a single parameterized backoff
function; `_compute_backoff_seconds` and `_cas_backoff_seconds` are removed (or become trivial
wrappers binding their constants), with no remaining duplicated `base*factor**i`/jitter math.
- [ ] Both call sites (`acquire_pass_lock`, `_cas_advance_with_retry`) produce the same backoff
schedule as before for their respective constants; the two retry budgets are unchanged.
- [ ] The existing jitter test
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_retry_jitter.py` still passes (extend it
if needed to cover both constant sets through the unified function).
- [ ] No universal `retry()` helper or new `_retry.py` module is introduced; the change stays inside
`_advisory_lock.py`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make test` pass; net LOC for the module does not increase.

baseline.summary: Cluster 2: unify the two _advisory_lock backoff functions into one parameterized helper

## What
The going-forward compact metrics snapshot: a small JSON record appended per CI run (and readable by the command) persisting point-in-time code-health numbers whose history is otherwise ephemeral — coverage %, complexity distribution, clone count — so their movement accrues.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/snapshot.py` — new: `write_snapshot(dict)` appends a timestamped record to a committed NDJSON file; `read_snapshots(since,until)` yields in-range records for the registry.
- `.gitignore` — add `!.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson` to surgically un-ignore the store. The repo gitignores ALL `.rebar/` contents via a blanket `.rebar/*` rule (line 20) and tracks specific files with per-file `!`-negations (e.g. `!.rebar/criteria_routing.json`); WITHOUT this negation line the snapshot file is silently gitignored and the series never persists.
- `.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson` — new committed artifact (one snapshot per line). **It lives under the tracked `.rebar/` store, NOT under `reports/`**: `/reports/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:74`), so a snapshot file there would never be committed and the trend series would silently never accumulate. `.rebar/` is already tracked in git (e.g. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`), so snapshots persist and sync.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_snapshot.py` — new.

## Approach
Coverage/complexity/clone are computed at a point in time; their trend needs a stored series, which does not exist today. An append-only NDJSON snapshot (not a new event type) is the lowest-friction durable store; it lives under the tracked `.rebar/` store so it is committed and synced (unlike the gitignored `reports/`, which holds only ephemeral CI artifacts). The command reads it for trend metrics, and until a snapshot exists a metric reports `unavailable`. Append-only and additive.

## Tests
- Unit: `write_snapshot` then `read_snapshots` round-trips; a range filter excludes out-of-range records; a malformed line is skipped without raising.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_snapshot.py` passes: a written snapshot is read back within its date range (`assert rec in read_snapshots(since,until)`) and excluded outside it.
- [ ] a corrupt/truncated NDJSON line is skipped and the reader still returns the valid records — unit test asserts count equals the valid-record count.
- [ ] the snapshot store path is `.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson` (a git-tracked path), verified by the test writing under `.rebar/` and asserting the file is not matched by the repo's `.gitignore` — so the going-forward series actually persists.
baseline.summary: Going-forward metrics snapshot writer/reader (NDJSON)

# Live DC harness (rendered HTML) + cross-repo contract test

## Context / Problem
The DC codec is validated offline against pandoc's jira reader as a proxy, but the real Jira DC wiki renderer and Jira's own storage canonicalization differ from pandoc and cannot be modeled offline — that gap is the residual risk this story closes. The repo already runs live DC testing with a Dockerized Jira 8.17.1 instance in GitHub Actions (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`), so this extends that harness rather than building a new one. Separately, the sibling repo `agentic-dev-platform` imports the `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` seam from this package, so changing its behavior must be guarded by a contract test.

This story is the LIVE proof of the state-based echo-safety and settled-conflict behavior that `5c0e` (DC render robustness) and `3388` (cutover + echo suppression + local-wins conflict) deliver; it depends on both.

## Approach
Extend the existing Docker DC harness with a rich-text test that:
- renders a representative body and pushes it via the real API
  (`rebar.edit_ticket(local_id, repo_root=repo, description=value)`, the pattern
  already used by `_out_description` in
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`), and asserts **rendered HTML**
  through `?expand=renderedFields` — not just the wiki source via `?fields=description`
  — so we verify what Jira actually interprets (`*foo*`→bold, `h1.`→heading,
  `{code}`→macro). No `renderedFields`/`expand=` assertion exists in the harness
  today, so this is a genuinely new fidelity check.
- runs a second reconcile pass to assert **state-based echo-safety end-to-end** (the
  landed rich body decodes to a value the differ recognizes as unchanged → no
  re-push), exercising `3388`'s once-only-upgrade-then-converge path against the real
  renderer.
- performs a **both-sides concurrent edit** to assert `3388`'s settled conflict
  behavior with the precondition that policy actually requires. The
  `outbound-field-conflict` alert fires ONLY on a both-sides divergence
  (`local != baseline` AND `remote != baseline`, `outbound_field_diff.py:354-362`); a
  bare Jira-side edit with local unchanged is instead suppressed by the
  directionality guard (`_suppressed_by_inbound`) and mirrored inbound (Jira-wins)
  with NO conflict alert. So the live scenario is: (1) push a body and let a pass
  converge so a baseline is recorded; (2) make a **rebar-side** edit to the
  description AND a **Jira-side** edit to the same field before the next pass;
  (3) assert the next pass emits rebar's body (**local-wins**) and records the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` bridge alert — the remote value
  is recorded, never silently destroyed (NOT a novel LWW clock; this is the a713 +
  `3388` policy proven live, mirroring `3388`'s `test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`
  precondition).

Gate it with the harness's existing skip markers (absent-harness / absent-extra) and the session-scoped PAT the harness already provisions. Add a contract test that pins the public shape/behavior of `normalize_rich_text` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py:134`, exposed as `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) so a change that would break the `agentic-dev-platform` import fails here first.

## Scope
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — new rich-text live test module (render+push,
  `?expand=renderedFields` HTML assertions, 2nd-pass echo, both-sides-concurrent-edit
  local-wins + conflict-alert assertion), reusing the existing conftest
  fixtures/skip markers.
- CI workflow for the DC harness job — ensure the new test runs in the existing
  amd64 Docker job (no new job).
- `tests/` — cross-repo `normalize_rich_text` contract test.

## Testing
- Live render fidelity: a pushed rich body's `renderedFields` HTML contains the
  expected bold/heading/code-macro markup (skipped when the harness/extra is absent).
- Live echo-safety: a second reconcile pass against the live instance pushes no
  description change (upgrade-then-converge holds against the real renderer).
- Live conflict: with a converged baseline, a **both-sides** edit (rebar-side AND
  Jira-side to the description) before the next pass keeps rebar's body and raises the
  deduped `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description` alert (remote value recorded,
  not clobbered); a bare Jira-only edit is NOT asserted as a conflict (it is
  Jira-wins inbound).
- Contract: `normalize_rich_text` accepts the documented inputs and returns the
  documented type/shape; a signature/behavior change fails
  `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The Docker DC harness has a rich-text test asserting rendered HTML via
  `?expand=renderedFields` (not just wiki source), covering bold/heading/code-macro;
  verified by the test running in the existing DC-harness CI job.
- [ ] The live test asserts state-based echo-safety across a second pass (no re-push)
  AND `3388`'s settled local-wins + `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert under the
  required **both-sides** precondition (converged baseline, then a rebar-side AND a
  Jira-side edit to the description → local-wins emit + deduped
  `outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description`, remote value recorded, not silently
  destroyed); verified by the same live test.
- [ ] A cross-repo contract test pins `normalize_rich_text`
  (`InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text`) back-compat so a breaking change fails here
  first; verified by `test_normalize_rich_text_contract`.
baseline.summary: Live DC harness (rendered HTML) + cross-repo contract test

## Context
433c requires AC boxes checked before close; but checking a box edits the description, and material_fingerprint (llm/plan_review/pass1.py) hashes the raw description — so the required box-flip trips stale-material in validate_attestation (attest.py) and forces a fresh LLM review before EVERY close. Observed on all four closes of d3ed/433c/9d07/a584. Checkbox STATE is progress metadata (verified independently by the completion verifier); the ITEM TEXT is the material.

## Approach
Normalize checkbox state before hashing in material_fingerprint: case-insensitive `- [x]`/`- [X]` → `- [ ]` (also `*` bullets), line-anchored, so flipping a box never changes the fingerprint while ANY text change still does. Single seam: both the plan-review close gate and the completion-verifier staleness check recompute through material_fingerprint via current_material_fingerprint.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py (material_fingerprint: normalize description basis)
- tests: unit on fingerprint invariance + a close-gate-level regression

## Testing
RED first: fingerprint(desc with [ ]) == fingerprint(desc with [x]) fails today; any non-checkbox text edit still changes the fingerprint; validate_attestation no longer returns stale-material after a pure box flip.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Flipping any AC box (either direction, x or X, - or * bullet) leaves the material fingerprint unchanged.
- [x] Any other description edit still changes the fingerprint (staleness preserved).
- [x] A signed plan-review attestation stays valid across a pure box-flip edit (no stale-material at close).
- [x] Existing attestations signed on unchecked descriptions remain valid for checked descriptions (normalization is backward-compatible by construction).
baseline.summary: AC checkbox flips invalidate plan-review attestation (stale-material on every close)

# Four-pass review KERNEL: extract the shared evidence → verify → decide → coach framework (plan-review as reference)

## Context

Industry practice and 2025–2026 research converge on a **multi-pass** LLM review: a finder
surfaces cited EVIDENCE against a locked rubric (no model-emitted severity/confidence); a
SEPARATE verifier validates each finding via atomic, independent binary sub-questions; a
DETERMINISTIC policy (not the model) decides severity and blocking; and an affirmative COACH
maps the surviving advisories to a locked move registry. That is **four passes** (the coach is
Pass-4, demonstrated by plan-review) — the framework's name is updated from three-pass to
four-pass.

The framework is no longer hypothetical. The **plan-review gate (epic `5fd2`)** realized the
full four-pass concretely and runs it in production as the *sole* plan-review gate on the v3
workflow engine: Pass-1 finder (evidence contract `{finding, criteria[], evidence[],
scenarios[], impact}`), Pass-2 verifier (severity attributes + a typed binary sub-answer set),
Pass-3 deterministic `pass3_decide`, Pass-4 coach (move registry, rendered deterministically).
Recent work hardened it further (a non-frontier verifier-model default, token-budget verify
chunking, the coach gated on surviving>0). BUT that implementation lives INSIDE
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — it is **not a shared kernel**. A second review surface (the
code-review capability, epic `b744`) would otherwise COPY the passes, forking the verification
vocabulary and the deterministic decision math — exactly the silent-drift class this repo
already paid for once (the retired bespoke vs workflow verify divergence).

This epic **extracts** the value-bearing, divergence-dangerous passes into a reusable kernel
that both gates consume, so the decision core and the binary vocabulary cannot fork.

## Supersedes the prior three-pass epic (`9da1`)

This replaces "Realign rebar reviews to three-pass; migrate existing reviewers" because the
scope changed on three counts:
1. It is **four** passes (the coach pass), not three.
2. "Migrate the existing reviewers" is dropped: `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py` is a throwaway
   DEMO, not a migration target — real code review is epic `b744`, which CONSUMES this kernel.
3. The framework is already built (in plan-review), so the work is **extraction + a clean
   consumer seam**, not a from-scratch build. The old epic's 10 overlay-catalog comments are
   inputs to `b744`, not to this epic's deliverable.

## What the kernel is — and is NOT

**SHARED (extract into the kernel — domain-agnostic, divergence-dangerous):**
- **Pass-2** finding-verifier: operates on a findings list + a domain context; emits per finding
  `{severity_attributes, binary}`. Owns the single `verification` output contract (the binary
  sub-question vocabulary + the severity-attribute enums) and the verify orchestration already
  built for plan-review (token-budget chunking, merge-by-global-index, the verifier-model
  default).
- **Pass-3** deterministic decision: the one `pass3_decide` (+ math: validity from the graded
  binary fraction; impact from the ordinal-mapped severity attributes; the conditional
  cited-reference veto; per-criterion thresholds, parameterized).
- **Pass-4** coach MECHANISM: move-selection → deterministic template render → the bounded
  noun-phrase subject validator → the no-free-prose discipline → gate-on-surviving>0; plus a
  pluggable move-registry SCHEMA.

**NOT shared (already reusable / engine-provided):**
- Pass-1 criteria→batch orchestration — the `ProductionBatchRunner` already does token/budget
  finder batching; the workflow `batch` step already aggregates. Not re-abstracted.
- The workflow shell (steps/branch/batch/`RunnerAgentStep`/`gate_dispatch`) — the v3 engine
  already provides it; each gate keeps a thin workflow.

**Per-gate PLUG-INS (the consumer seam):** criteria + routing, finder prompts, the
domain-context assembler (plan text vs diff), the verify-prompt preamble, and the move-catalog
CONTENT (planning moves vs code moves).

## Enforcement — keep reuse honest WITHOUT making the workflow system brittle

Enforce STRUCTURE mechanically and BEHAVIOR via evals; never enforce prompt *text* via a lint
(an anti-pattern — DSPy / Guardrails / Instructor / promptfoo all enforce typed contracts +
output/behavior, not prompt-string greps):
- **Vocabulary** → ONE registered `verification` schema. Validate via the existing TOLERANT
  stack (json-repair + bounded retry + pydantic-ai native outputs) and DEGRADE to INDETERMINATE
  on an unparseable turn — never hard-crash a gate. Keep the schema small/flat (the
  reliability cost of strict validation is the failure mode to avoid).
- **Decision interpretation** → ONE `pass3_decide` function (thresholds parameterized per
  criterion).
- **Soft prompt rules** (atomicity; independence — don't show the finding's own conclusion;
  allow "insufficient"; verdict-with-citation-NOT-fix) → a canonical RULES SCAFFOLD + kernel
  doc for discoverability, ENFORCED by BEHAVIORAL evals (deterministic FakeRunner assertions on
  the gate path in CI + a small GATED live eval kept OFF the blocking CI path). **No
  prompt-marker lint** (explicitly rejected as brittle/gameable).
- **Move registry** → registered schema + load-time validation, with a `triggers`/applies_when
  applicability field.
- **Drift** → reuse the existing contract / derived-prompt-index drift gate (it keys on the
  output CONTRACT, not on prompt wording).

## Out of scope (decisions recorded, not deliverables)

- **Completion verifier stays single-pass.** It is already binary-per-given-criterion; a full
  independent verify pass ≈2× the agentic cost for a small, unmeasured accuracy gain. The one
  cheap lever (the binary/independence discipline in-prompt) was applied separately, not here.
- The throwaway `code_review.py` demo reviewers (real code review = `b744`).
- Threshold/severity calibration (separately deferred; thresholds start high → mostly advisory).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A shared kernel module (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`) houses: Pass-2
      `verify_findings(findings, *, context, model, headroom)`, the registered `verification`
      contract, Pass-3 `pass3_decide` (+ math, per-criterion thresholds parameterized), and the
      Pass-4 coach mechanism + move-registry schema.
- [ ] The plan-review gate consumes the kernel for Pass-2/3/4; an offline (FakeRunner) test
      asserts the produced verdict is unchanged vs the pre-extraction behavior (reuse, not fork).
- [ ] The `verification` contract is the single source of the binary-question vocabulary +
      severity-attribute enums; validation uses json-repair + bounded retry and DEGRADES to
      INDETERMINATE (never crashes a gate) on an unparseable turn.
- [ ] The move-registry schema includes a `triggers`/applies_when field; coach move-selection
      applies a DETERMINISTIC applicability filter, then the LLM picks among the applicable moves
      (closing the prior wholly-LLM-delegated selection gap).
- [ ] A canonical verifier-rules scaffold + kernel doc record the soft prompt rules; a
      BEHAVIORAL eval (offline FakeRunner on the gate path; a small gated live eval off the
      blocking CI path) verifies the rules are obeyed. NO prompt-marker lint is added.
- [ ] A documented consumer seam enumerates the per-gate plug-points (criteria, finder prompts,
      domain-context assembler, verify preamble, move-catalog) that `b744` consumes; this epic
      `blocks` `b744`.
- [ ] Out-of-scope decisions are recorded (completion verifier single-pass + rationale;
      throwaway code_review.py not migrated; calibration deferred).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] A shared four-pass kernel module exists (Pass-2 verifier + `verification` contract; Pass-3
- [ ] The plan-review gate is rewired to CONSUME the kernel for Pass-2/3/4 with NO behavior change
- [ ] A documented consumer SEAM (the per-gate plug-points + the rules scaffold) that `b744` builds
- [ ] Enforcement is structural (schemas) + behavioral (evals), with no prompt-text lint;
baseline.summary: Four-pass review kernel: extract the shared evidence->verify->decide->coach framework (plan-review as reference)

# Live rich-text cutover + state echo suppression + concurrency conflict safety

## Context / Problem
This story **cuts the live Cloud and DC send paths over to the now-capable rich codecs** (delivered by `e59d` and `271c`, on which this story depends) and makes that cutover echo-safe. Because the DC codec is one-way and lossy, loop prevention cannot rely on `decode(encode(x))==x`. Both clients must suppress echo by **state**: compare the current Jira value against the last-synced baseline the reconciler already keeps (ADR 0026, `binding_store.py:102`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` at `:108`; `set_baseline` at `:459`). We must also not silently destroy either side's edits under concurrency — this story **reuses** the repo's settled concurrency policy (story a713: local-wins + a deduped `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert over the ADR-0026 baseline) rather than inventing a new arbitration — and any state we add must respect epic `0303`'s churn discipline (a per-pass timestamp there caused the tickets-store bloat this feature must not regress).

**Why the cutover lives HERE, not in the leaves.** `e59d`/`271c` deliver capable codecs but deliberately leave the live send sites on the plain/identity path, so that the observable format change and its echo-safety land **together** in one story (this one), never a hazard-before-safety window.

## Prior art in this repo (build on the existing convergence + conflict machinery, do NOT re-invent it)
- **Three-way baseline arbitration already exists (ADR 0026, story d6bd).** The
  outbound diff compares the LOCAL ticket against a per-binding **baseline**
  (`binding_store.get_baseline`, mapped through the `InboundMapper` at
  `outbound_field_diff.py:193-197`) so a field is emitted only when local diverged
  from the last-synced Jira ancestor; `description` is one of the
  `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (`outbound_field_diff.py:46`) and is already handled
  this way at `outbound_field_diff.py:273-293`. This story does NOT invent a new
  three-way merge — it makes that existing description compare rich-codec-aware.
- **Both-sides conflict detection + local-wins is ALREADY the settled policy
  (story a713).** When a mirrored field diverged on BOTH sides
  (`local != baseline` AND `remote != baseline`), `outbound_field_diff.py:354-362`
  appends `(jira_key, fname)` to the `conflict_sink`, which
  `run_differs.py:_emit_outbound_field_alerts` (`:97`) emits as a **deduped
  `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert** — resolution stays **local-wins** (rebar
  emits its value; the remote is never silently dropped, it is surfaced as the
  alert). This story REUSES that exact channel and policy for the body; it does not
  add a parallel LWW clock or a new conflict sink.
- **Once-only re-emit convergence already exists.** `outbound_field_diff.py:285-292`
  compares the fitted-local body to the RAW remote so a stale body re-emits exactly
  once, after which the landed body decodes to the normalized form and converges.
  For rich text this terminates iff the codec is idempotent under the compare —
  guaranteed by the codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
  (`test_rich_text_codec.py:163`, ticket a32a) plus the empirically-proven
  round-trip idempotence (marklas 99.65%). No observe-after-push GET is needed: a
  benign Jira re-canonicalization is absorbed by the decode-on-compare, then
  converges on the next pass.
- The rich-text COMPARE normalization is the codec's **`normalize_outbound`** op
  (`RichTextCodec`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`), already routed through by
  `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` (`outbound_mapper.py:77`),
  `outbound_fields.py:564`, and `inbound_differ.py:210`. This story makes those
  compares rich-aware; it does NOT add a second, parallel `norm()`.
- `binding_store.py` already persists the last-synced baseline via the always-on
  `_advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:519`, run at persist `:600` from
  `ctx.curr_snapshot`); this story reuses that single writer unchanged.
- The codec law and the comment dedup that depends on it (`outbound_comments.py:48`)
  are preserved by routing every compare through the codec op.

## The live cutover (both clients — this story's new scope)
Reroute the direct plain-encode call sites through the capable codecs so the wire actually carries rich text, and prove convergence:
- **Cloud:** repoint the four `AdfCodec` ops to the Markdown-aware `adf.py`
  functions (`to_wire→markdown_to_adf`, `decode_inbound→adf_to_markdown`,
  `normalize_outbound→adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf`,
  `fit_outbound→fit_markdown_to_adf_limit`) and install the whole-codec plain-text
  fallback, updating the pin test at `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`.
  Then reroute the live consumers to the Markdown-aware path: the encode at
  `adapters/jira/acli.py:205` and `acli_cli_ops.py:369`, the fit at
  `jira_fields.py:53`, and the direct `adf.normalize_description` /
  `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` compare sites at `outbound_fields.py:564` and
  `inbound_differ.py:210` — **paired so the send-fit and the compare-fit are the
  identical transform** (the once-only re-emit convergence invariant). Each
  already-synced description re-emits **exactly once** (the `outbound_fields.py:564`
  once-only re-emit mechanism) to upgrade to rich ADF, then converges.
- **DC:** wire the pure `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki` (from `271c`) into
  `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`, and **redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to the
  compare form `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`** so the codec law
  (`test_rich_text_codec.py:163`) is re-established for the rendering codec. Because
  DC's live send composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))` at
  `outbound_mapper.py:77`, this redefinition is exactly what makes
  `issue.update(fields=…)` begin shipping rendered wiki — the cutover — so it
  **must** land here with echo-safety, not in the leaf. **The DC CREATE path is a
  SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer:** `_map_local_to_dc_fields`
  (`backend.py:70`) constructs its OWN `WikiTextCodec()` and builds
  `"description": codec.fit_outbound(...)`, applying **only `fit_outbound`, never
  `to_wire`** — so redefining `to_wire`/`normalize_outbound` alone does NOT render
  on create. This story changes `_map_local_to_dc_fields` to render before the fit
  (compose the renderer/`to_wire` with `fit_outbound`) so a newly-created DC issue
  ships rendered wiki too. Update the DC identity pin tests
  (`test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`,
  `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched`) to the rendering behavior.
- **Rollback:** the cutover is gated behind a single switch (config/flag) that
  restores the plain/identity path for that client without reverting the codec
  capability, so a bad rollout is one revert, not a code rewrite. **The flag ships
  defaulting OFF** (opt-in, not a 100%-traffic flip): it is enabled per-client
  (Cloud first, then DC) only after a canary tenant validates convergence, so no
  single flip touches all traffic and the safe plain/identity path is the shipped
  default.

## Approach (echo-safety + concurrency — REUSE the existing baseline + conflict machinery)
Echo-safety and concurrency for the body are **already implemented** by the ADR 0026 three-way baseline diff and the story-a713 both-sides conflict channel (see Prior art). This story's job is to make that existing description path **rich-codec-aware and provably convergent**, not to build a new merge:

1. **Rich-aware compare.** The description compare at
   `outbound_field_diff.py:273-293` already fits the local body and compares it to
   the remote; after the cutover the fit/compare run through the Markdown-aware
   codec (`normalize_outbound` = `adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf` for Cloud,
   `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` for DC). Because the send-fit and the compare-fit
   are the **identical transform**, an already-synced body re-emits **exactly
   once** to upgrade to rich, then converges (the existing once-only re-emit
   mechanism, now codec-idempotent by the codec law).
2. **Baseline stays the single existing writer.** No observe-after-push GET and no
   second baseline writer are added: `_advance_baselines` continues to advance the
   per-binding baseline from `ctx.curr_snapshot` at persist. A benign Jira
   re-canonicalization of the rich body is absorbed by the decode-on-compare (step
   1) rather than by re-reading the pushed value, so the per-key
   succeeded-mutation plumbing the earlier draft required is unnecessary.
3. **Two DISTINCT compares, each in the correct space — a lossy codec must both
   upgrade a legacy body exactly ONCE and then converge; these are not the same
   predicate and must not be collapsed.**
   - **Emit compare (`outbound_field_diff.py:292`), local-vs-REMOTE — LEFT
     UNCHANGED.** `fitted = normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local))` (the full
     outbound round-trip, `outbound_mapper.py:77`) is compared to
     `canonical_remote["description"]`, which is ALREADY
     `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local(jira_fields)["description"]` =
     `decode_inbound(remote_wire)` (the InboundMapper decode at `:188`). Both
     operands are therefore already in the decoded/normalized space, so a lossy
     round-trip cancels on both sides and a no-edit body converges **without**
     re-normalizing the remote. The remote is deliberately kept as the plain
     inbound-decoded value and is **NOT** re-run through `normalize_outbound`: a body
     written by the pre-cutover plain/identity encoder decodes to a form that differs
     from the newly-rendered `fitted`, which is exactly what forces the **one-time
     upgrade re-emit**; routing the remote through the port too would make a stale
     legacy body compare equal and it would never upgrade (the load-bearing rationale
     already documented at `outbound_field_diff.py:287-291` and
     `outbound_fields.py:555-561`). This story leaves the emit compare's remote side
     as-is and relies on both operands already being decoded for lossy convergence.
   - **Baseline compares (`_suppressed_by_inbound:252`, `_local_matches_baseline:385`)
     — LOCAL side normalized.** These gate directionality/origin-gating and the
     both-sides conflict scan by comparing the **RAW local Markdown**
     (`ticket["description"]`) against `baseline`, which is
     `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local(raw_baseline)` = `decode(baseline_wire)`
     (`:197`). Here the two operands are in DIFFERENT spaces — raw local vs decoded
     baseline — so under a lossy codec `decode(baseline_wire) != raw_local` even with
     no rebar edit, reporting "local changed" every pass (re-emit forever +
     origin-gating misfire). This story routes the **local** side of these
     description compares through the codec `normalize_outbound` (`decode∘to_wire`,
     idempotent by the codec law) so both operands sit in the same decoded space and
     the lossy artifact cancels. `_remote_matches_baseline` (`:399`) already compares
     two decoded values (`canonical_remote` vs decoded `baseline`) and is LEFT
     UNCHANGED. An AC asserts a no-edit body is suppressed by the baseline
     directionality guard and matches its stored-then-decoded baseline across
     consecutive passes, a genuine rebar edit still shows as changed, and a legacy
     body upgrades exactly once.
4. **Concurrent both-sides edit → the EXISTING local-wins emit + conflict alert +
   additive inbound merge (all unchanged).** When `local != baseline` AND
   `remote != baseline` on the body, the outbound emit stays the settled
   **local-wins** (rebar's body is emitted) and the divergence is surfaced on the
   **existing `conflict_sink` → `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert**
   (`outbound_field_diff.py:354-362` → `run_differs.py:97`). The INBOUND apply
   keeps description in its existing **"additive"** conflict class
   (`conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES` / `_field_contract.FIELD_CONTRACT`,
   `resolve_additive` — "conflicts merge additively, never overwrite"), so neither
   side's content is destroyed and no registry reclassification (and no
   `_field_contract` parity break) is introduced. This story adds nothing to the
   conflict registries; it relies on description already being a mirrored field in
   that conflict scan and already being additive on inbound.
5. **Shared-codec-op side effects are enumerated.** Redefining
   `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` from identity to the rendering form is a
   change to a **shared** codec op, so its OTHER consumer — the DC comment-diff
   dedup key (`outbound_comments._diff_comments` via `_resolve_codec` `:123`, used
   `:286`; the `_IdentityCodec` docstring `:106-116` notes DC's identity
   `normalize_outbound` is what keeps that key on plain text today) — is explicitly
   enumerated. To avoid changing the comment dedup key as a description-cutover side
   effect, this story keeps the comment-diff path injecting the plain-text/identity
   normalizer UNCHANGED; comment rendering and its dedup-key migration are owned by
   `789c` (which depends on this story). An AC asserts DC comment-diff still
   converges (no duplicate re-post) after the description cutover.

**Origin-gating so Jira-native constructs survive (AC5).** Outbound is gated on rebar-origin: a description update fires only when `local` differs from `baseline` (a rebar-side edit). When a Jira author adds a native construct with no Markdown source (a panel/mention/date — constructs `adf.py` already decodes at `:164/219`) between passes and rebar made no edit, that pass sees `remote != baseline` but `local == baseline`, so origin-gating emits **no** outbound and the construct survives untouched. Only a genuine rebar-originated body change re-encodes (and a concurrent both-sides edit is surfaced as the local-wins conflict alert above, never a silent clobber). For the rich layer, store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the binding (proven 0.07 KB/version stable, identical to the baseline profile; a per-pass timestamp was proven to reproduce 0303's 12.62 KB anti-pattern) so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` — Cloud cutover: repoint the four `AdfCodec`
  ops to the Markdown-aware `adf.py` functions + install the whole-codec fallback.
- `adapters/jira/acli.py` (`:205`), `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` (`:369`),
  `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` (`:53`), `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`
  (`:564`), `inbound_differ.py` (`:210`) — Cloud live cutover through the
  Markdown-aware path (gated).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (`:198/205/207/208`) —
  update the Cloud pin test to the Markdown-aware delegation; update the DC identity
  pin tests + codec-law test for the now-rendering `WikiTextCodec`.
- `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` — DC cutover: `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`
  delegates to `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki`; `normalize_outbound` set to
  `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (re-establishes the codec law for the rendering
  codec) — this is what makes `outbound_mapper.py:77` ship rendered wiki.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (`:70`) — DC CREATE-path: change
  `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (today `codec.fit_outbound(...)` only) to render via the
  renderer/`to_wire` before the fit, so create ships rendered wiki (gated).
- `binding_store.py` — inline change-gated `rich_sha` beside the existing baseline
  (`_BASELINE_FIELDS`).
- `outbound_field_diff.py` (`:252`, `:385`) — normalize the **local** side of the
  description baseline compares in `_suppressed_by_inbound` and
  `_local_matches_baseline` through the codec `normalize_outbound` so it sits in the
  same decoded space as the already-decoded baseline (lossy artifacts cancel). The
  emit compare (`:292`) and `_remote_matches_baseline` (`:399`) are LEFT UNCHANGED:
  both already compare two decoded operands, and the emit compare's plain
  inbound-decoded remote is what forces the one-time legacy-body upgrade re-emit
  (rationale at `:287-291`). Reuse `_advance_baselines` unchanged (no
  observe-after-push GET, no `_apply_mutations` change).
- `outbound_comments.py` (`_resolve_codec:123`, used `:286`) — enumerated consumer
  of the redefined `normalize_outbound`; keep the comment-diff injecting the
  identity/plain normalizer UNCHANGED (comment rendering is `789c`'s), so the
  description cutover does not shift the comment dedup key.
- the existing description differ / compare path — reuse the ADR-0026 three-way
  baseline diff + the story-a713 local-wins + `conflict_sink` conflict channel + the
  existing additive inbound merge (no `FIELD_CLASSES`/`_field_contract` change), plus
  **origin-gating** (outbound only when `local != baseline`, so a Jira-native
  construct authored with no rebar edit survives); reuse the codec
  `normalize_outbound` (NOT a new `norm()`, NOT changing the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`).
- `tests/` — cutover, convergence, echo, conflict, and no-churn tests.

## Testing
- **Cloud convergence:** after the cutover, a converted ADF description posts once,
  and a second reconcile pass emits **zero** description updates (`test_cloud_cutover_converges`).
- **DC convergence:** a rendered-wiki description posts once and a second pass
  emits zero description updates (`test_dc_cutover_converges`).
- Self-echo: a rebar-originated body change propagates exactly once and a second
  pass pushes nothing (0 echo-back).
- Concurrent: both sides edit the same body; the pass keeps rebar's body
  (local-wins) and appends the divergence to the existing `conflict_sink` so an
  `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert fires — the remote value is recorded, not
  silently discarded (`test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`).
- Normalizer composition (lossy-safe): the emit compare keeps the plain
  inbound-decoded remote (both operands already decoded → the lossy round-trip
  cancels) so a pre-cutover legacy body upgrades exactly once and then converges;
  the baseline directionality/conflict compares normalize the LOCAL side so
  `decode(baseline_wire)` matches a no-edit local across two consecutive passes.
  Asserted by `test_legacy_body_upgrades_once`,
  `test_lossy_baseline_compare_local_normalized`, and
  `test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes`.
- Comment-diff unaffected: after the description cutover the DC comment-diff dedup
  key is unchanged (identity/plain) and comment-diff converges with no duplicate
  re-post (`test_dc_comment_diff_unchanged_by_cutover`).
- Origin-gating: a Jira author adds a native panel/mention to a synced description
  and rebar makes no edit; the next pass emits zero outbound and the construct
  survives verbatim (`test_jira_native_construct_survives`).
- No-churn: a pass with no body change updates 0 `rich_sha` entries and writes no
  timestamp; asserted by the git-delta cost harness (≤0.07 KB/version stable).
- Rollback: with the cutover flag off, the wire reverts to the plain/identity
  encode for that client (`test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`).

## Acceptance Criteria … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: State-based echo suppression + LWW conflict safety

baseline.description:
# Optional authentication for the rebar MCP server (OAuth 2.1 Resource-Server model)

## Context

`rebar-mcp` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP("rebar")`) is today
**stdio-only**: `build_server().run()` is called with no transport argument. It has **no HTTP
transport and no per-request/session plumbing**. Per the MCP authorization spec, authentication is
an **HTTP-transport concern** — stdio servers *should not* authenticate (credentials come from the
environment). rebar has deliberately kept MCP stdio-only and met every remote need with separate
FastAPI library-mode services (the Gerrit `review_bot`, the in-flight op-cert service), so
**nothing consumes rebar-mcp over the network today** (Gerrit and GitHub Actions use the rebar
library/CLI in-process, per ADR-0007).

This epic adds an **optional** capability: rebar-mcp can serve over HTTP and require
authentication, acting as an **OAuth 2.1 Resource Server** that validates inbound bearer tokens and
advertises RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata. The capability is generic (provider-agnostic) so
any organization can front it with its own identity provider — it is **not** coupled to this
project's dev auth model. Design-of-record: session log `emanatory-confounded-dodo` plus the
higher-effort coherence/peer/security review pass captured in the same log.

## Why (beneficiary + problem)

**Beneficiary:** an operator/organization (including rebar itself, as future follow-on) that wants
to expose rebar MCP tools to remote MCP clients (Claude Code / an IDE / a CI job) over the network
instead of a local stdio subprocess. **Problem today:** there is no HTTP transport and no
authentication, so a shared/hosted rebar store cannot be reached by a remote MCP client without
exposing it unauthenticated. This epic makes a remote rebar-mcp endpoint possible and safe to
require auth on, verified locally.

## Approach & rationale (positive)

Build rebar's **own** token verifiers against the **official `mcp` SDK's `TokenVerifier` seam**
(`mcp.server.auth.provider.TokenVerifier.verify_token(token) -> AccessToken | None`), wired via
`FastMCP(token_verifier=…, auth=AuthSettings(…))`, and serve the optional Streamable-HTTP transport
the SDK already provides. rebar is a **Resource Server only** — it validates tokens and advertises
discovery metadata; it is **not** an Authorization Server and does **not** implement Dynamic Client
Registration (identity is delegated to the deploying org's IdP).

**Why this fits:** (a) the official SDK — already a dependency — provides the `TokenVerifier` seam,
`AuthSettings`, RFC 9728 metadata routes, `TransportSecuritySettings`, and Streamable-HTTP transport
natively; the verifiers are small modules on a stable, blessed seam. (b) It is the mainstream
self-hosted path (GitHub, Grafana, Neon, GitLab, and the SDK's own `simple-auth` example build auth
on the official SDK; GitHub's remote server likewise delegates identity and does not do DCR). (c) It
avoids the standalone `fastmcp` framework, whose `server.auth` module is semver-exempt and has had
multiple CVEs. (d) It keeps every line under rebar's own tests/CI/version control.

**RS-only + no-DCR is defensible, not a usability gap.** Claude Code / Claude.ai do not *require*
DCR: they auto-discover via the RFC 9728 PRM rebar serves (pointing at the org IdP), and when the
IdP lacks anonymous DCR (Entra, Cognito, default Keycloak/Auth0/Okta) the user falls back to
first-class **manual `--client-id`/`--client-secret`** or a **static bearer `--header`** — both of
which rebar's PRM + static verifier serve directly. S7 documents these three connection paths.

## Security (this epic crosses a trust boundary — the core of the plan)

Enabling HTTP exposes rebar-mcp to **lower-trust network actors**. The posture is first-class and
propagated to every child:

- **Authentication is the deliverable.** With auth enabled, every request is admitted only on a
  validated bearer token; an unauthenticated request receives **401 + `WWW-Authenticate`** with the
  RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` URL. Identity is delegated to the org IdP; rebar mints no tokens.
- **The composite verifier is the single audience/fail-closed choke point.** The SDK does **not**
  validate token audience and `AccessToken.resource` defaults to `None`, so there is no SDK
  backstop. Therefore the **composite** re-validates every returned token: it rejects unless
  `AccessToken.resource` is present **and** equals the single configured `auth_resource_server_url`
  (RFC 8707). Every verifier — including static and trusted-proxy, which have no natural token
  audience — must populate `.resource` explicitly. A verifier cannot bypass the audience check.
- **One resource, one audience.** There is a single `auth_resource_server_url`; it is what the PRM
  advertises AND the audience every verifier validates against — they are never independent.
- **Fail-closed everywhere:** any verifier that raises is logged and treated as **non-acceptance**
  (never acceptance); if no verifier returns a valid, audience-matching token the request is denied
  (401). Misconfigured auth, an unknown `auth_strategies` entry, `auth_enabled=true` with an empty
  composite, or auth-enabled-over-HTTP with no verifier wired all **refuse to start**. An HTTP
  transport with auth disabled refuses to start unless `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` is set.
- **Transport hardening:** DNS-rebinding/`Origin` protection on by default with explicit loopback
  defaults; loopback bind by default; a non-loopback bind requires explicit host/origin allowlists
  AND an explicit TLS-at-edge acknowledgment (bearer tokens/secrets must never cross the network in
  cleartext). Discovery URLs derive from the configured `auth_resource_server_url` (validated https
  for non-loopback), not the request scheme — the behind-a-proxy correctness fix.
- **No token passthrough** to any upstream (confused-deputy prohibition); tokens/secrets never
  logged (a redaction layer is required and tested).
- **Authenticated ≠ authorized (named residual).** Any authenticated principal wields rebar's full
  ambient authority (writes auto-push; `reconcile live` uses rebar's own git/Jira creds) gated only
  by server-level `required_scopes` and the existing `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`/`ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`/
  `ALLOW_LLM` env gates — which now also gate remote actors. Per-tool scope→capability authorization
  is deferred and documented as a residual risk. Rate-limiting/brute-force protection is delegated
  to the edge proxy in v1, with mandated high-entropy static tokens; documented as a residual.

## Scope

**In scope:** an optional Streamable-HTTP transport; a provider-agnostic auth framework (composite
`TokenVerifier` that is the single audience/fail-closed choke point + config-driven selection)
shipping five verifiers (static bearer, JWKS/JWT, RFC 7662 introspection, trusted-proxy passthrough,
pluggable custom); RFC 9728 metadata + 401; the security/transport hardening above; local
verification (pytest); docs + an ADR; config/manifest updates (`McpConfig`, `MCP_ENV_VARS`,
`server.json`, regenerated `mcp-reference.md`/`env-vars.md`).

**Out of scope (explicit):** deploying an authenticated endpoint on AWS / `rebar.solutions.navateam.com`
and any Gerrit/CI reconfiguration (Gerrit and CI do not use MCP — deliberate follow-on); rebar
acting as an Authorization Server / DCR / token issuance; per-tool scope→capability authorization
(server-level `required_scopes` only); rate-limiting inside rebar (edge-proxy responsibility in v1);
GitHub-**user** and Gerrit authentication (neither is an OAuth token issuer — only a deploying org's
proxy/custom concern). stdio remains the default transport and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories (S1–S7) are closed.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp` serves over an optional Streamable-HTTP transport while stdio remains the default
      and default behavior is byte-unchanged when the new flat `mcp.*` keys are unset (observable:
      the existing `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` stdio suite still passes).
- [ ] With auth enabled, the local suite demonstrates 401-without-token (with a `WWW-Authenticate`
      header carrying the RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` URL), a served PRM document, 200-with-valid-
      token, 403-insufficient-scope, and rejection of a token whose `resource` ≠ `auth_resource_server_url`
      enforced at the composite.
- [ ] All five verifier modes (static, JWKS/JWT, introspection, trusted-proxy, custom) are
      selectable via the flat `mcp.auth_strategies` list / `REBAR_MCP_*` env vars, each has passing
      tests, and each populates `AccessToken.resource` so the composite audience check applies.
- [ ] Fail-closed startup is tested: unknown `auth_strategies` entry, `auth_enabled` with an empty
      composite, auth-enabled HTTP with no verifier wired, and HTTP with auth disabled and no
      `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` all refuse to start.
- [ ] New flat config keys and env vars are reflected in `MCP_ENV_VARS` and `server.json` (the CI
      manifest drift gate `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes) and in regenerated
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` / `docs/env-vars.md`.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-auth.md` and an ADR document the resource-server-only model, the composite audience
      choke point, the five verifier modes, the security posture (incl. the authenticated≠authorized
      residual and rate-limiting delegation), the behind-a-proxy deployment (TLS + allowlists +
      discovery URLs), and the three interactive-client connection paths.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the final integrated branch.
- [ ] A rebar-mcp operator can run the server over HTTP with authentication **required**, using any of
- [ ] The trust-boundary guarantees hold and are demonstrated locally: unauthenticated → 401 +
- [ ] Misconfiguration and downgrade are fail-closed: unknown strategy, empty composite with auth on,
- [ ] A third-party operator can connect an interactive Claude client (documented paths) and the design

## Testing strategy (children carry the tiers/oracles)

Verification is entirely local (no AWS). Each verifier is unit-tested against its own real logic
(valid/invalid/audience/expiry/algorithm-confusion/rotation/fail-closed/header-spoofing cases), and
the HTTP+auth surface is integration-tested by driving the SDK's Streamable-HTTP ASGI entrypoint
with an in-process `httpx` `ASGITransport` client (asserting HTTP status, the `WWW-Authenticate`
header, and the served PRM document). Each child story names its test tier and observable oracle.

## Compatibility & rollback

Purely **additive**: stdio stays the default, auth is off by default, all new behavior is gated
behind new, unset-by-default flat `mcp.*` keys, so existing stdio deployments and the existing MCP
tests are unaffected. The dependency changes are pinning `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` (the v2-alpha renames the
SDK surface; 1.28.1 is at/above the DNS-rebinding fix) and adding `pyjwt[crypto]` for the JWKS
verifier. Rollback is config-level: leave the new keys unset (or `mcp.transport=stdio`) for exactly
today's behavior.
baseline.summary: Optional authentication for the rebar MCP server (OAuth 2.1 Resource-Server model)

# 88d9's inbound parent-clear is unreachable in a bidirectional pass: outbound re-pushes the parent and inbound discards its own clear

A parent cleared on the Jira side is never cleared locally. The inbound clear that ticket 88d9 built is COMPUTED and then DISCARDED within the same pass, so `.parent_id` survives indefinitely on a child whose remote parent is gone.

## Proven RED-first, not inferred

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_parent_clear_bidirectional_37e7.py` wires the REAL outbound differ into the REAL inbound differ the way `run_differs` does — deliberately NOT a hand-built outbound entry, which is the flaw that hid this. Two cells, first run, no setup fighting:

    test_real_outbound_differ_emits_a_parent_write_for_the_deparented_child   PASSED
    test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass                     FAILED

      outbound fields for DC-1: {'parent': 'DC-2'}
      inbound fields for DC-1:  {}
      inbound items suppressed by outbound context: 1
      RECON: outbound_update key=DC-1 changed=[parent] comments=0 labels=0 links=0

`suppressed == 1` is the smoking gun: inbound computed exactly one item — the clear — and it was thrown away.

## Mechanism, both steps read from source

1. **Outbound re-pushes the parent.** `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent` resolves the
   bound epic parent; `canonical_remote["remote_parent_id"]` is now `None`; they differ, so the
   local-wins branch emits `changed["parent"] = <parent key>`. Crucially `parent` is NOT in
   `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`, so no baseline arbitration ever defers to inbound on this field.
2. **Inbound discards its own clear.** `inbound_differ` canonicalizes the outbound `parent` to
   `parent_id`, then the contradiction filter drops every key already present in the outbound
   entry — including the clear it just computed.

The clear's precondition (Jira has no parent, local does) is IDENTICAL to the outbound re-push's precondition. So for any parent rebar can resolve outbound — bound, and epic-typed per bug 8b25's guard — 88d9's clear can never fire in a bidirectional pass.

## Why the existing 88d9 suite is green

Every 88d9 acceptance cell passes `outbound_mutations=None`. The single cell that DOES supply outbound context — `test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear` — hand-builds a fake outbound entry and asserts the suppression as DESIRED behaviour. It never asks whether the real outbound differ produces that mutation in the clear scenario. It always does.

That is this epic's signature failure shape one level up: not a vacuous oracle, but a REAL oracle asserting the wrong thing because its input was fabricated rather than produced.

## Scope

Confirmed for the EPIC-parent case, which is the normal one on Data Center. For a non-epic local parent `_resolve_local_parent` omits the parent entirely, outbound emits nothing, and the suppression cannot fire — that is the separate situation [rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b] covers.

## Blast radius beyond DC

The suppression lives in the SHARED differ layer, not in a vendor adapter, so Jira Cloud is implicated on the same code path wherever a parent is cleared remotely while the local parent still resolves. Not yet observed there — recorded as a question, not a claim.

## Proposed fix (from the trace, not yet implemented)

Give the outbound parent branch the directionality guard the mirrored fields already have, reusing 88d9's own evidence channel: before emitting a parent SET, suppress when `local_parent` is truthy, `remote_parent` is falsy, AND `binding_store.get_peer_parent(local_id) == local_parent` — i.e. the peer de-parented since our last observation while local stood still, which is exactly the case `diff_inbound_parent` exists to handle. `get_peer_parent` must stay getattr-guarded, and its absence must fall through to today's local-wins push.

Guard 4 (`test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_suppresses_the_clear`) then needs restating as "an outbound push suppresses the clear ONLY when local re-set the parent", rather than unconditionally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `test_inbound_clear_survives_a_real_bidirectional_pass` is GREEN
- [x] a local parent that was genuinely re-set still wins outbound — the fix must not invert
      into "remote always wins", which would silently drop real local intent
- [x] `test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_round_trips` is GREEN on a live harness run,
      with the run id recorded
- [x] the reworded guard 4 asserts suppression only for the local-re-set case
baseline.summary: 88d9's inbound parent-clear is unreachable in a bidirectional pass: outbound re-pushes the parent and inbound discards its own clear

## Why

Outbound link sync broke because production routes outbound updates through the **batch** applier (`batch_dispatch.update_one` + `_mutation_to_batch_dict`), while the link/comment/label features and their tests lived in the **typed-leaf** applier `apply_outbound._apply_outbound_update` — which production does not execute. Capabilities had to be re-added to the batch path one bug at a time (parent 8b25, comments 87e4, links 3f04). Two parallel outbound appliers guarantee the next capability will drift the same way.

## What

- Collapse outbound application to **one** path. Either delete the dead typed leaf `_apply_outbound_update` (and its now-misleading tests), or make it the single production path and route the batch dispatch through it — chosen so there is no separately-tested parallel that production skips.
- Retarget the existing typed-leaf tests at the surviving production path.
- Add **one** test that drives a multi-sub-op outbound UPDATE — scalar fields + comments + labels + links + parent together — through the production path in a single mutation (the sub-ops were only ever tested in isolation, in separate files).
- **Safety (rollout):** verify behavioral parity BEFORE deleting the retired path — assert the surviving path applies every sub-op the retired path did (fields, comments, labels, links, parent), so the deletion cannot silently drop a capability.

## Scope

- In: applier consolidation in `apply_outbound.py` / `batch_dispatch.py` / `applier.py`; the combined multi-sub-op test; the parity check.
- Out: sub-op telemetry (story E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Exactly one outbound applier path remains in production; the retired path is deleted (no dead, separately-tested applier code).
- [ ] Behavioral parity is verified — the surviving path applies every sub-op the retired path did — before the retired path is deleted.
- [ ] A single test drives fields + comments + labels + links + parent through the production path in one UPDATE and asserts each sub-op took effect.
- [ ] No capability regresses; the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] The combined test asserts effects (sub-op outcomes), never interaction/mock-call-counts.
baseline.summary: Collapse the dual outbound applier paths to one production path

## Context
ADR 0051 / bug 88eb landed FOREGROUND auto-gc on the tickets worktree (fixes the
detached-maintenance corruption). Measured safe on the current 184k-object store
(~1-2s routine, ~8-9s worst-case). But the git `gc` maintenance task does a FULL
repack whose cost scales with TOTAL store size, so the worst-case foreground pause
grows as the store grows, eventually approaching the 60s write-lock budget.

## Idea — strictly-better posture: bound each foreground maintenance run to O(new objects)
Replace the size-scaling `gc` task with git's incremental maintenance tasks, kept
foreground (serialized under the write lock, preserving the ADR 0051 safety):

- Disable the `gc` task (`maintenance.gc.enabled=false` / keep `gc.auto=0` semantics).
- Enable **`loose-objects`** — packs NEW loose objects into a fresh `loose-*.pack`
  (default batch 50k), and does NOT rewrite existing packs or the multi-pack-index.
- Enable **`incremental-repack`** — geometric, auto-sized batch capped at 2 GB
  (git commit a13e3d0), so a run "never" repacks the whole store in one shot.
- Optional (Gitaly's further win): pack loose objects into a fresh pack WITHOUT
  updating the MIDX (the residual O(size) cost), consolidate geometrically only
  occasionally.

## Prior art (see bug 88eb research)
- Microsoft Scalar: `gc.auto=0` + background `loose-objects`/`incremental-repack` via
  `git maintenance` (docs/advanced.md).
- GitLab/Gitaly: geometric repacking + time-based full repack + loose-object packing
  that never updates the MIDX (13s -> 174ms).
- git's own `git maintenance` "incremental" strategy: runs loose-objects +
  incremental-repack, never the gc task, and sets maintenance.auto=false.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The tickets worktree runs incremental maintenance (loose-objects +
  geometric incremental-repack), foreground, with the full `gc` task disabled.
- [ ] Measured foreground-maintenance pause stays bounded (~1-2s) as the store grows
  well past ~500k objects (proving command: the gc-latency measurement harness).
- [ ] No regression to the 88eb corruption fix (concurrency test stays green on git 2.54).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated; ADR 0051's "escape hatch / scale-up" section points here.
baseline.summary: Bound foreground git-maintenance to O(new objects): disable the gc task, use loose-objects + geometric incremental-repack

# Concurrent review-plan silently drops the plan-review attestation: enrich_drain._prune_queue_events uses an unlocked whole-index git commit that races locked store writes

## Summary

Under `[agents]`, every `review-plan` finish triggers the opportunistic enrichment drain, whose
`rebar.llm.enrich_drain._prune_queue_events` (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:191-207`) stages and
commits with a **raw, unlocked, whole-index** `git rm` + `git commit` — taking neither the unified
store write lock nor a commit pathspec. Running in the detached drain child concurrently with a
review's locked `stage_and_commit` writes, it drops the concurrent writer's event, so a PASS
review leaves NO persisted attestation (and no observability sidecar).

This is the un-hardened twin of bug `malevolent-emigratory-umbrette`, whose fix routed the two
sibling prunes (`plan_review/sidecar.py:94`, `overlap/digest_sidecar.py:141`) through the locked,
pathspec-scoped `event_append.delete_events`; the enrich-queue prune was missed.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Concurrently run `rebar review-plan` on several DIFFERENT tickets (separate processes), with the
   `[agents]` extra + a real key (so the enrichment drain is live).
2. Some PASS reviews return `sidecar_emitted=False` and `verify-signature` → "unsigned — ticket has
   no signature", despite a PASS verdict. Serial runs persist fine.

Confirmed by an isolated-store experiment (remote OFF, so branch-divergence is excluded): 6 locked
`append_event` writers vs 4 processes calling the real `_prune_queue_events` produced 33/360 writes
raising `git commit failed while holding lock` ("nothing to commit" — the writer's staged blob was
swept into the prune's whole-index commit — and "cannot lock ref 'HEAD': is at X but expected Y"),
with all 33 blobs left IN HEAD but UNLINKED from the worktree (sweep-and-strand); worktree-listing
readers then report them absent.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** a concurrent write is serialized by the single store write lock (invariant I5); a
  committed event is durable and visible to readers. "A push failure never fails the write — the
  commit stays local" (CLAUDE.md). A PASS review persists a claimable attestation.
- **Actual:** the unlocked prune committer sweeps/orphans a concurrent locked write; the review's
  own commit fails (swallowed by `sidecar.emit` → `sidecar_emitted=False` and by
  `attest.sign_plan_review` → unsigned), and the swept blob is unlinked from the worktree.

## Root Cause

`_prune_queue_events` performs a store write OUTSIDE the unified write lock with a whole-index
commit, contrary to `event_append.delete_events`'s contract (`event_append.py:302-307`) and the I5
single-lock invariant (`_store/lock.py:1-24`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:_prune_queue_events` no longer runs a raw unlocked `git rm` /
  whole-index `git commit`; it routes through the locked, pathspec-scoped
  `event_append.delete_events` (mirroring `plan_review/sidecar.py:prune`).
  - Proving: `rg -n 'subprocess.run.*git' src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` shows no raw `git commit`
    in `_prune_queue_events`; `rg -n 'delete_events' src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` present.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the race (RED before the fix) and passes after: concurrent
  locked writes + the drain-queue prune leave zero dropped/stranded events.
  - Proving: the new test in `tests/` fails on `origin/main` and passes with the fix; `make test` green.
- [ ] A sibling sweep confirms no other unlocked `git commit` store-write remains outside the
  locked path.
  - Proving: `rg -n "git.*commit" src/rebar --glob '*.py'` reviewed; any raw store-commit routes
    through the locked path or is justified.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass — CI's `Verified` gate green on the landed change (external CI state; attested by a comment citing the change + vote + merge).
baseline.summary: Concurrent review-plan silently drops the plan-review attestation: enrich_drain._prune_queue_events uses an unlocked whole-index git commit that races locked store writes

# S5 — Signed verdicts stamp provider, endpoint, tier, and effective capabilities

## Context / Problem

A signed gate verdict records only a model string. THREE sites write it: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:629`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:206,223`, and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py:105` each write `"model": verdict.get("model")`. That string is the resolved `provider:model`, so a verdict produced behind an opaque gateway still claims it came from `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`. Once rebar supports two first-class providers and a best-effort tier, a consumer cannot tell a Bedrock-backed verdict from an Ollama-backed one, even though rebar signs both.

## Approach

Keep the existing `model` string field untouched and **add** a sibling `provider_provenance` object: `{provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities}`. `endpoint_host` records the host only (never a full URL, never credentials); `tier` is `first_class` or `best_effort`; `capabilities` is the effective record from S2 [rebar:f184-a5f1-f181-4700]. Verdicts still sign on every tier — a contributor running Ollama can still exercise the gates, which matters for the OSS on-ramp — but a consumer now has the lever to reject an off-tier verdict.

Additive-only is deliberate: it makes this a **backward-compatible** payload change, so an older reader ignores the new key and no store-compatibility capability gate or migration is required. Readers that want the provenance treat its absence as "unknown, legacy".

**Alternative rejected:** refusing to sign off-tier verdicts. It gives a stronger guarantee but breaks local development without a first-class provider key, which weakens exactly the contributor on-ramp `docs/plan-review-gate.md` depends on.

**Alternative rejected:** replacing the `model` string with the structured object. That is a breaking payload change requiring a compatibility gate and a migration for zero added information.

**Where the record is assembled, and why NOT in `providers.py`.** An earlier draft of this plan said `providers.py` would 'expose the provenance record from the factory'. That is impossible AND unnecessary:

- IMPOSSIBLE: `ProviderSession.provider_factory` is the `(str) -> Provider` hook handed to pydantic-ai's
  `infer_model`. Its return type is fixed by that contract, so it has no channel to hand anything else back to
  the caller. This is the SAME limitation the module already documents for the retrying httpx client (which is
  why builders append to `self._closeables` instead of returning it).
- UNNECESSARY: `runner.run()` ALREADY holds every field, in one scope — `resolved = _pai_model(cfg)`
  (`runner.py:273`) gives the provider-qualified model, `_provider_name` (`:294`) the provider,
  `caps = capabilities_for(...)` (`:357`) the effective capability record, and `cfg.base_url` the endpoint.
  Nothing needs to travel back from the factory at all.

So the runner assembles the record from data it already has, via a helper in `capabilities.py` (277 LOC, the roomiest candidate; `runner.py` is at 698 against the 800 cap, so the runner-side change stays a call, not an inline block). `providers.py` — at 299 against the <300 cap that is an ATTESTED criterion of closed story 7468 — is left untouched, which removes that constraint from this story entirely.

**Reuse the already-computed capability record, do not recompute it.** `runner.py:357` resolves `caps` ONCE per run, and the model-object-vs-string distinction there is load-bearing (it caused a prior regression). Provenance must stamp THAT record; calling `capabilities_for` a second time can silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run.

**`endpoint_host` uses `urlparse(base_url).hostname`, never `.netloc`.** `.hostname` strips userinfo; `.netloc` RETAINS `user:secret@`. Note `runner.py:650` uses `.netloc` — harmless there (a truthiness check) but the wrong accessor to copy here. This is the mechanism behind the security oracle below.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — assemble the provenance record. It takes PRIMITIVES
  (`provider: str`, `model: str`, `base_url: str | None`, `caps: ModelCapabilities`) and returns the record.
  It must NOT take `LLMConfig` or a provider object: this module is a declared LEAF whose docstring states it
  imports nothing from `runner`/`providers` and keeps `import rebar.llm` stdlib-only.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — call that assembler and thread the record alongside `ran_model`.
- **`src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is NOT modified** (see Approach).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — populate it alongside `ran_model`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` (`:629`), `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` (`:206,223`),
  and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (`:105`) — the CODE-REVIEW gate's verdict payload. It was
  missing from an earlier draft of this Scope and is the most consequential of the three for this epic:
  code review is the gate being cut over to Bedrock [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], so a consumer trying to
  tell a Bedrock-backed LLM-Review vote from an Anthropic-backed one reads THIS payload. Leaving it out
  would have shipped provenance to the two gates that need it least.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — document the additive field.
- `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract tier: the mechanism is a producer/consumer shape agreement across a signed, persisted payload, so the test feeds a real runner result into the real sidecar writer and reads the persisted record back.

- happy path: a Bedrock run persists `provider_provenance.tier == "first_class"` and `provider == "bedrock"`.
- best-effort path: a run with `REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL` persists `tier == "best_effort"` and the endpoint host.
- collateral invariant: the pre-existing `model` string field is byte-identical to what it was before this
  change, and the signature over the payload still verifies.
- security oracle (negative control): given a `base_url` containing credentials
  (`https://user:secret@host/v1`), the persisted `endpoint_host` is `host` and the persisted payload contains
  neither `secret` nor the api_key anywhere.
- backward compatibility: a sidecar payload written WITHOUT the new key still loads and verifies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts no credential material from `base_url` or `api_key` appears anywhere in the persisted
      sidecar payload
- [ ] a test asserts a legacy payload lacking `provider_provenance` still loads and its signature verifies
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar review-plan` on a real ticket writes a sidecar whose `provider_provenance.tier` matches the
      configured provider, shown in the ticket comment
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` documents the field as additive and optional
