content.text: # Live-store remediation: drive fsck to zero (safe, reversible, batched, committed)
## Why
`rebar fsck` on the live store = 2422 SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT + 11 ORPHAN_EVENT + 1 MISSING_CREATE. Fix #1 stopped
new corruption; this cleans the backlog. DESTRUCTIVE on a live, git-backed shared store — safety is first-class.
Consumes NEW sibling deliverables: A1 (tricolour-head-ratfish) ADDS the `.retired` rename + `RETIRED_SUFFIX` +
retire helper; A2 (glandulous-potent-waxwing) ADDS the `include_retired` rebuild path. depends_on A1+A2.
## Repair per fault class
- SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT (2422): a folded source file STILL PRESENT (listed in `source_event_uuids`, never deleted).
Repair = call A1's retire helper to rename each still-present listed source to `.retired`. NOT a rebuild.
- ORPHAN_EVENT (11): a pre-snapshot event absent from `source_event_uuids`. Routed BY EVENT TYPE (see policy):
AUTO-RECOVER types -> A2's `reduce_ticket(..., include_retired=True)` rebuild; HUMAN-TRIAGE types -> surfaced,
NOT auto-rebuilt (the rebuild would pick an order that may be wrong).
- MISSING_CREATE (1): `fsck --repair` logs it, no automatic write; human triage.
## Orphan disposition (a CODE constant, not just prose)
Define two sets in code (enumerating ALL KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES so none is unclassified):
- AUTO-RECOVER (additive/commutative): COMMENT, LINK, UNLINK, TAG_DELTA, COMMITS, BRIDGE_ALERT, REVERT.
- HUMAN-TRIAGE (order-sensitive): STATUS, EDIT, FILE_IMPACT, VERIFY_COMMANDS, SIGNATURE, WORKFLOW_RUN,
WORKFLOW_STEP, ARCHIVED. Decisions recorded in the PR / a linked ops doc.
## Safety
- GIT-AWARE writes: the tracker is a git worktree. Each batch commits+pushes:
`git -C <tracker> add -A && git -C <tracker> commit -m 'a3-remediation: batch N/M' && git -C <tracker> push`.
If a push FAILS (conflict/network/reject), ABORT the run and surface the error — do NOT continue; the pre-tag
enables rollback. BEFORE any write: `git -C <tracker> tag pre-a3-remediation <oid>`; rollback = `git reset --hard
pre-a3-remediation && git push --force-with-lease`.
- Dry-run FIRST: `fsck --repair --dry-run` prints per-ticket before/after diff + dispositions, writes NOTHING
(a test asserts zero file writes + zero commits); the live run is gated on human review.
- Reconciler pause: disable the `reconcile-bridge.yml` GHA schedule for the window via the GitHub API/CLI
(`gh workflow disable reconcile-bridge.yml`), verify no pass is mid-flight, and RE-ENABLE in a `finally`/failsafe
(auto re-enable after N minutes or on repair-process exit) so a crash never leaves it disabled. (The pass-lock
`refs/reconciler/lock` is a leased CAS lock and would expire, so it is NOT the pause mechanism.) Manual writers
hold off (documented); the batched+committed+pre-tagged design makes a stray write recoverable.
- Idempotent/resumable: fsck itself is the AUTHORITATIVE resumability check (re-run repairs only tickets fsck still
flags). A per-ticket `.a3-repaired` marker is a LOCAL, gitignored optimization only. Per-snapshot rewrite uses the
EXISTING `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` (not hand-rolled). The SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT rename + rebuild hold the
store write-lock for the per-ticket critical section (no TOCTOU with a concurrent writer). Per-ticket failure
logs+skips (no batch abort). Batched `--limit=200`, wait >=30s between.
## Scope
`_commands/fsck.py` ONLY (`--repair`/`--dry-run`/`--limit`, per-batch git commit+push, disposition constants,
per-snapshot `fsutil.atomic_write`, local marker, write-lock critical section; update the `fsck --help` golden files
`tests/golden/cli_help/fsck__help.out` + the `-h` variant). This ticket does NOT edit `compact.py` (A1 owns all
compact.py changes) — it CALLS A1's retire helper and A2's `include_retired` rebuild. Gated on RC1 fix #1.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fsck --repair --dry-run` prints per-ticket before/after + dispositions; a test asserts ZERO file writes and ZERO commits in dry-run.
- [ ] Live repair commits+pushes each batch; a push failure ABORTS + surfaces the error; pre-tag created; rollback rehearsed on a fixture (post-rollback store == pre-tag state).
- [ ] Reconciler paused by `gh workflow disable` (verified no in-flight pass), re-enabled in a failsafe `finally`.
- [ ] Orphan disposition is a code constant covering ALL KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES; AUTO-RECOVER rebuilt, HUMAN-TRIAGE surfaced (not auto-rebuilt); tested.
- [ ] Resumability via fsck re-check; `.a3-repaired` marker local/gitignored; per-snapshot rewrite uses `fsutil.atomic_write`; write-lock held per ticket; crash-before-marker is safe (test).
- [ ] Synthetic-fixture unit tests: SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT / ORPHAN_EVENT (both dispositions) / MISSING_CREATE (incl. `.retired`) repair correctly.
- [ ] Live store reaches 0 UNRESOLVED faults (triaged+documented orphans count as resolved); before/after counts recorded.

baseline.summary: Live-store corruption remediation: drive fsck to zero

baseline.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` recreates the `compose-review-bot-1` container whenever `main` advances and the bot's source changed. It does NOT drain in-flight reviews first, so recreation stops uvicorn and KILLS whatever code review is running. Because a full code review takes far longer than the gap between deploys during a landing burst, reviews can be killed before they ever vote — and the gate LIVE-LOCKS: no change gets an `LLM-Review` vote, so nothing can submit, which is indistinguishable from an outage.

## MEASURED, live, on 2026-08-03 (account 896586841071, instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5)

SEVEN recreations in 90 minutes, from `journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy`:
    16:23:05, 16:41:17, 16:48:22, 17:10:06, 17:14:46, 17:29:50, 17:49:28
    => gaps of 18, 7, 22, 4, 15, 20 minutes

A full code review, from the bot's own logs, is SEVEN passes and takes ~10 MINUTES:
    code-review-base 94.6s / 103.5s / 134.9s · code-review-tests 92.3s / 125.3s
    code-review-scope-intent 29.1s / 101.0s · code-review-api-compat 96.7s / 114.1s
    code-review-verify 80.9s / 137.6s · plus deletion-impact, phase-boundaries, coach
    >1,000,000 input tokens per change (LLM_TOKEN_USAGE: input 1,010,039, cache_read 883,980)

FOUR of the six gaps are SHORTER than one review. The interruption was observed directly in the log — passes running, then `INFO: Shutting down` / `Application shutdown complete` / `Finished server process [1]`, mid-review.

USER-VISIBLE IMPACT observed at the time: changes 1302 (`Verified +1` at 17:24) and 1303 (`Verified +1` at 17:32) both sat with `LLM-Review = 0` for 20-35 minutes, unsubmittable.

## Why NO ALARM FIRED — this is the part that matters

The bot is HEALTHY by every signal the monitoring has:
  - `docker inspect`: `running`, `restarts=0`
  - every deploy logged `{"event":"autodeploy","msg":"review-bot redeployed + healthy"}`
  - ZERO `VOTER_ERROR` lines, so `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` (monitoring_s4b.tf) stayed `OK`
  - all 11 CloudWatch alarms `OK` throughout
A killed review emits NO `VOTER_ERROR`, because nothing failed — the process was asked to stop. So the fail-closed voter path never runs and the alarm that eb6e's rollback plan depends on cannot see this failure mode AT ALL. **The gate can be fully live-locked while every health signal reads green.**

## Why this is not self-evidently benign

Interrupted reviews ARE retried by the reconciler, so the system self-heals ONCE deploys stop. The defect is that it cannot converge while deploys keep arriving faster than reviews complete — and a landing burst is exactly when the gate is most needed. Convergence depends on the burst ending, not on any bound in the deploy path.

## Relevance to the Bedrock cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]

eb6e removes the cross-provider fallback and names the `VOTER_ERROR` CloudWatch alarm as its safety net. This bug shows a live-lock the gate can enter that the alarm provably does not observe, so that safety net has a blind spot independent of provider. Worth resolving, or at least recording, before the cutover relies on it.

## Approach

Make recreation wait for in-flight work, rather than making reviews survive recreation. Options to weigh:
  (a) DRAIN: before `docker compose up -d`, poll a bot endpoint for in-flight review count and wait up to
      a bounded timeout; recreate immediately when idle. Needs an endpoint exposing that count.
  (b) DEFER: if the bot reports busy, skip this deploy cycle and retry on the next timer tick (~2 min).
      Simplest, and autodeploy is already an idempotent oneshot timer, so skipping is natural.
  (c) COALESCE: debounce — require N seconds of no new `main` commits before deploying, so a burst
      produces one deploy instead of seven.
(b) and (c) compose well and need no new bot surface. Whatever is chosen, bound the wait so a permanently busy bot cannot block deploys forever, and LOG the deferral so a skipped deploy is visible rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A deploy that would interrupt an in-flight review is DEFERRED or DRAINED rather than recreating the
      container mid-review, proven by a test or a scripted simulation of the busy case.
- [x] The deferral/drain is BOUNDED, so a permanently-busy bot cannot block deploys indefinitely, and the
      bound is stated with its rationale.
- [x] A deferred deploy is LOGGED and visible (journald + the autodeploy metric), so a skipped cycle can
      never be mistaken for no change having landed.
- [x] The interrupted-review failure mode becomes OBSERVABLE: either it emits a countable marker that an
      alarm can watch, or the gap is explicitly recorded as accepted with its reasoning — the current
      state, where a fully live-locked gate leaves every health signal green, is what this criterion
      exists to end.
- [x] A landing BURST is covered, not just a single deploy: a simulation with commits arriving faster than
      one review completes ends with the review voting rather than being killed repeatedly.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Autodeploy recreates the review-bot mid-review, so a landing burst live-locks the LLM-Review gate

## Why

The additive-attestations rollout (epic dark-acme-lumen) kept a legacy single-slot
`state['signature']` mirror alongside the authoritative kind-keyed `state['attestations']`
map — the *expand* half of an expand/contract. This ticket ships the *contract* half: stop
carrying the mirror in new SNAPSHOTs. Dropping it is a one-way door (a pre-attestations clone
reads `state['signature']` and has no map to fall back to), so it is gated on a readiness
condition, made fully reversible by config, and documented.

## What (ordered so no reader ever sees a stripped mirror)

1. **ADD a NEW helper** `signing.most_recent_attestation(state)` (does not exist today; this
   ticket creates it). Semantics: return the record with the greatest `signed_at` from
   `state['attestations']` (ties → last processed, matching the legacy mirror's
   last-writer-wins); fall back to `state['signature']` only when the map is absent/empty.
   This reproduces the mirror's "latest signature of any kind" from the authoritative map.
2. **Migrate all three in-tree mirror readers to call that helper** (so they no longer read
   `state['signature']` directly), done BEFORE step 3 so a stripped mirror is never observed:
   `signing._record_for_kind` (kind=None verify-latest path), `_engine_support/validate.py`
   (`signature_findings` — same "most-recent record, verify_record it" semantics, now
   map-sourced), and `_commands/txn.py:_signature_gate` (line 362, require_signature_for_close).
   Because `attestations` is always present on a post-feature snapshot (and old snapshots are
   folded into it on read), every migrated reader still finds the record after the drop.
3. **Only then drop the mirror on the write side:** `compact.py` strips the legacy `signature`
   key from a SNAPSHOT's compiled_state (normal-compaction AND fsck-rebuild paths), gated by a
   NEW `compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror` config flag (default `false` = drop).
4. Keep the read-side fold-in (`_processors.py`) so pre-map snapshots still upgrade on read.
5. Document the readiness gate, rollback, and target version.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`, `src/rebar/signing.py`,
`src/rebar/_engine_support/validate.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, `docs/migrations.md`,
tests under `tests/unit/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] Readiness gate satisfied before the mirror is dropped: no
  pre-attestations clone/reconcile-host that reads `state['signature']` remains live. Evidence:
  this fleet auto-updates hourly to origin/main (so no pre-attestations binary is live), and
  the gate + upgrade-first ordering is documented in docs/migrations.md "Legacy
  signature-mirror retirement". Recorded as a ticket attestation.
- [ ] Rollback + named target version: the drop is reversible with NO code downgrade — setting
  `compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror = true` (env `REBAR_COMPACT_EMIT_LEGACY_SIGNATURE_MIRROR`)
  re-emits the mirror on the next compaction. Named rollback target: that flag on the 0.7.x
  line (introduced after 0.7.1). Documented in docs/migrations.md; verified by a unit test that
  the rollback flag keeps `signature` in the snapshot.
- [ ] Contract: a new SNAPSHOT's compiled_state contains `attestations` but NOT the legacy
  `signature` mirror (default flag), and docs note the field retired. Verified by unit tests
  in `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py` covering: (a) the strip default drops
  `signature` and the rollback flag keeps it; (b) `most_recent_attestation` resolves the
  latest-by-signed_at record from the map (this is the SINGLE accessor all three migrated
  readers — `signing._record_for_kind` kind=None, `validate.py:signature_findings`,
  `txn.py:_signature_gate` — now call, so one accessor test covers all three call sites);
  (c) a mirror-less snapshot round-trips through `process_snapshot` and still resolves via the
  map; (d) the legacy-mirror fallback when the map is absent. docs/migrations.md documents the
  retirement.

## Verification

- `make lint && make typecheck` pass; `pytest tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py`
  and the signing/attestation suites (test_signing, test_attestations_reducer,
  test_attestation_verify, lifecycle/test_signature) pass with no regressions.
baseline.summary: Contract phase: drop the legacy signature SNAPSHOT mirror (post-upgrade)

## Context / Problem
The proposed deterministic clarity criteria need adversarial validation against this project ticket history. A rule that rejects a valid historical ticket is either unsound or requires a narrower applicability gate.

## Approach
Search completed and accepted tickets for the strongest counterexample to each proposed rule, then inspect the full ticket and relevant review/completion evidence. Historical accepted tickets are the right corpus because they expose legitimate plan shapes that synthetic examples can miss.

## Scope
Read-only analysis of the rebar ticket store; no repository files will be modified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each proposed deterministic criterion has a cited historical counterexample or an explicit statement that no counterexample was found; verified by ticket ids and quoted plan excerpts recorded in a ticket comment.
- [ ] Each counterexample explains why the ticket remained valid and what false-positive mechanism the rule would trigger; verified by the recorded status, review evidence, or delivered outcome.
- [ ] Each criterion is classified as retain, narrow, advisory-only, or reject based on the evidence; verified by a structured recommendation table in the recorded findings.
- [ ] Findings are recorded on this ticket; verified by the presence of the final analysis comment.
baseline.summary: Find historical false positives for proposed clarity criteria

## Why

Two regexes key on the `## Success Criteria` heading and one scope extractor lists it. They are
the only code that READS the heading to make a decision, so until they change the heading
remains load-bearing and the store migration cannot be verified. (One further site,
`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:308`, WRITES the heading into generated eval fixtures; that
is a producer, not a reader, and belongs to the eval-specs story — this story does not depend
on it and its AC greps deliberately do not cover it.) `_count_ac_items` already counts `- [ ]` items ONLY
under `## Acceptance Criteria`, so criteria written under SC never reach the P1 blocking floor
and can never carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — collapsing the two TIGHTENS the gate.

## What

Point the heading-reading code at `## Acceptance Criteria`, and update the test fixtures that
embed `## Success Criteria` in ticket descriptions.

## Scope

Code:
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:136` — the epic branch of `_clarity_score`, currently
  `+2` for `^##\s+Success Criteria`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227` — the deliberate copy of that heuristic used for
  P1 coverage (non-blocking); the two must stay in lockstep, which the module comments require.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py:253` — `_SCOPE_HEADINGS`, which lists
  `"## success criteria"` alongside `"## acceptance criteria"`; drop the SC entry.

Test fixtures embedding the heading:
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_rubric_consistency.py:4,36`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py:48`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree.py:28`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree_heldout.py:22`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_story_epic.py:29`
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py:219,293,356,407,425,465`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py:108`

OUT OF SCOPE: removing `clarity-check` entirely (separately planned). This story only stops it
keying on the SC heading.

## Approach

In both `_clarity_score` copies the epic branch REPOINTS its `+2` from `^##\s+Success Criteria`
to `^##\s+Acceptance Criteria`. Because AC is already a universal blocking floor, the bonus
becomes automatic and the epic branch stops discriminating. That is accepted deliberately:
clarity-check is a dead metric already slated for removal, and the alternative is worse.

The arithmetic, measured against the real `_clarity_score` rather than estimated. The epic
fixture in `test_gate_rubric_consistency.py` scores 6 today (heading +1, len>=200 +1,
len>=500 +1, bullet +1, SC +2 ... minus length, netting 6 at 440 chars). With the SC block

Dropping the bonus would also lower every real epic in the store by 2, risking a live
clarity-check regression across the 108 migrated tickets for the sake of a metric being deleted.

## Finding

Canonical contributor guidance hardcodes a specific maintainer/bot DCO identity even though project contribution policy requires contributors to sign with their own real configured identity.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:124-169` documents the Gerrit workflow and currently prescribes `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>`.
- `.agents/rules/rebar.md:28-34` repeats the same personal bot identity.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:198-214` requires a real contributor name and email for DCO sign-off.

## Remediation

Make the canonical guidance identity-neutral: contributors and agents use the real name and email configured for the actor performing the commit (`git config user.name` / `git config user.email`). Retain Joe Oakhart's bot identity only in narrowly scoped automation guidance for a workflow that actually runs as that bot.

Cascade flag: documentation-only contract change; verify all imported/copied agent guidance (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/*.md`, and any other contributor-facing guidance under `docs/`) so contradictory instructions do not remain. Automation-owned paths (`infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/fixtures/`) and experiment corpora (`docs/experiments/`) legitimately reference the bot identity and are explicitly out of scope for the sweep and for the consistency check below.

Add a deterministic consistency check: a `make lint`-integrated grep step (e.g. a target in the `Makefile`, or a script under `scripts/` invoked from `make lint`) that runs
`git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'`
(the `:(glob)` pathspec magic makes `**` recurse into subdirectories under `docs/`; the `:(exclude)` pathspec drops `docs/experiments/` from the scan) and fails the build if it finds any match. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and `tests/` are excluded by construction because they are not passed as pathspecs. Document, next to the check, which file owns it and that `infra/`/`.github/workflows/`/`tests/`/`docs/experiments/` are the intentional exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` tells contributors and agents to verify `git config user.name` and `git config user.email` and to sign off with that configured real identity. Verify: `grep -q 'git config user.name' AGENTS.md && grep -q 'git config user.email' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] `.agents/rules/rebar.md` and any derived guidance no longer instruct every actor to use Joe Oakhart's bot identity. Verify: `! git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- '.agents/rules/*.md' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Any retained Joe-specific identity is explicitly scoped to the automation that owns it (e.g. `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) and is not presented as general contributor guidance. Verify: `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart'` returns matches ONLY under `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/`, or `docs/experiments/`; any match outside those prefixes fails the check.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md`, canonical agent guidance, and generated/imported guidance describe one consistent DCO contract, defined concretely as: all three name "the committer's own configured git identity (`git config user.name`/`user.email`)" as the sign-off source, and none of them names a specific third party (Joe Oakhart or otherwise) as the required sign-off for general contributions. Verify: `for f in CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md .agents/rules/rebar.md; do grep -q "configured git identity" "$f" || exit 1; done` exits 0 (each file must contain the phrase, or the loop exits non-zero on the first miss), AND `git grep -l 'Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md'` returns no results.
- [ ] A deterministic consistency check exists and fails the build on a reintroduced hardcoded personal sign-off: implemented as a `make lint`-integrated grep step (script or Makefile target) running `git grep -nE 'joeoakhart\+bot@navapbc\.com|Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart' -- AGENTS.md '.agents/rules/*.md' CONTRIBUTING.md ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' ':(exclude)docs/experiments/**'` (the `:(glob)` magic recurses into `docs/adr/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/migrations/`, `docs/calibration/`, etc.; `:(exclude)` drops `docs/experiments/`; `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, `tests/` are excluded by not being passed as pathspecs) and fails the build (non-zero exit) if `git grep` finds any match. Verify: the new check's script/target exists, running it against the post-change guidance files exits 0, and running it against a scratch copy with the hardcoded string reinjected exits non-zero.
baseline.summary: Make contributor sign-off guidance identity-neutral

baseline.description:
## Summary

Sibling sweep of bug 5546 (rebar-debug Step 7). 5546's root cause is a repeatable pattern, not a one-off: **a bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` whose result is then consumed as `<remote>/<branch>`.** A bare fetch always writes FETCH_HEAD but only *opportunistically* writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` — and only when the remote's CONFIGURED refspec covers that branch. Under a narrow refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, which is what `git clone --single-branch` AND `actions/checkout` produce by default) the ref is never written, or — worse, when it already exists — never UPDATED, so the consumer silently reads a missing or STALE ref.

5546 fixed the `sync.py` instance. Two live instances remain; both were confirmed semantically (read in context), not by string match.

## Sibling 1 — `src/rebar/_store/push.py:182`

```python
_git(base_path, "fetch", remote, branch)          # :182  bare fetch
...
merge = _git(base_path, "merge", remote_ref, ...) # :202  consumes f"{remote}/{branch}"
```

This is the non-fast-forward retry loop. Under a narrow refspec the merge target is missing or stale, so the merge cannot absorb what actually rejected the push and **every retry re-pushes the same rejected history until the budget is exhausted.**

## Sibling 2 — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:286,309` (and the canary at :424,:436)

```sh
git fetch origin tickets || true                      # :286
ahead=$(git rev-list --count origin/tickets..HEAD ...) # :287  consumes origin/tickets
...
git fetch origin tickets 2>&1 || ...                  # :309  inside the retry loop
```

Note the SAME workflow already uses the correct explicit form at line 115 (`git fetch origin '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets'`), as does `verify-identity.yml:55` — so these sites are internally inconsistent, which is good evidence they are an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

**This is a strong candidate root cause for bug 449f-f9bf-be90-47fe** (and for the Reconcile Bridge push-rejection evidence recorded in 5546's own comment thread: 4 runs on 2026-07-30 exhausting a 5-retry budget with `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`). Because line 115 creates `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` earlier in the job, the later bare fetches at :286/:309 leave it STALE rather than absent — so `rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD` and the reconcile merge both operate on a snapshot that never advances, and the retry loop provably cannot converge no matter how large the budget. That mechanism has NOT yet been experimentally confirmed against a real runner; it is a cited hypothesis, and confirming or rejecting it is the first task here.

## Deliberately NOT siblings (checked and cleared)

- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:70,87` — bare fetch, then consumes
  `review/<branch>` / `tickets/<branch>`. Same shape, but the workspace is built by
  `git init` + `git remote add`, which installs the DEFAULT WILDCARD refspec, so the
  branch is always covered. Not reachable.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:347`, `review_bot/gerrit_client.py:335`,
  `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:115`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:86`,
  `verify-identity.yml:55` — already use an explicit refspec. Correct as written.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:375` — a genuine instance, but bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220
  already owns and fixes it. Excluded to avoid a conflicting edit.

## Why filed rather than folded into 5546

5546's authorized surface was `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` + its tests. `push.py` and the CI workflows are separate blast radii — the workflow change in particular needs a real runner to verify — so they get their own reviewable change rather than riding along.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 449f hypothesis above is experimentally confirmed or rejected against a real
      narrow-refspec checkout; if confirmed, 449f is linked to this ticket.
- [ ] `push.py`'s retry-loop fetch uses an explicit refspec, with a test proving the
      non-fast-forward retry loop converges under a narrow clone refspec (it currently
      cannot).
- [ ] The reconcile-bridge workflows' bare `git fetch origin tickets` sites use the
      explicit refspec already used at line 115 of the same file.
- [ ] A guard (lint rule, test, or reviewer-facing note) prevents the bare-fetch form
      from being reintroduced.
baseline.summary: sibling sweep of 5546: bare git fetch leaves <remote>/<branch> missing or stale in push.py and the reconcile-bridge workflows

# Gerrit change descriptions show line breaks at fixed-width intervals

## Context / Problem

Reported alongside bug 4e21 (Jira descriptions rendering a break at the end of every soft-wrapped line). The reporter observes a similar-looking line-break problem on Gerrit change descriptions.

## What has already been ruled out

Bug 4e21's fix does NOT address this. That fix changes `text_to_adf` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py`, which lives in the Jira adapter and is reachable only from the Jira REST v3 payload builders (`adapters/jira/acli.py:201`, `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:369`) plus the three description compare sites. Nothing under `src/rebar/review_bot/` or the Gerrit client imports it. A search of `src/rebar/review_bot/` and `src/rebar/llm/` for `textwrap` or any reflow helper found no matches, so rebar does not appear to be injecting these breaks in code.

## Working hypothesis (NOT yet confirmed — this is the work)

A Gerrit "change description" is the git commit message. Gerrit renders commit messages as preformatted fixed-width text and preserves the author's newlines verbatim. Commit-message bodies are conventionally hard-wrapped at ~72 columns (git's own norm), so the breaks may be authored rather than injected, which would make this intended behavior rather than a defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- Obtain a concrete example Gerrit change whose description renders wrongly, and record the change number.
- Determine whether the newlines are present in the commit message object itself (`git cat-file commit <sha>`) or introduced by a rebar/review-bot code path.
- Classify explicitly: defect vs intended-behavior vs authoring convention. If intended, close as not-a-bug with the citation and, if useful, document the commit-message wrapping convention instead.
- Only if it is a genuine injection defect: fix under RED->GREEN discipline.

## Notes

Filed at the reporter's request during the 4e21 session and deliberately scoped OUT of that session. Not yet reproduced or confirmed as a defect.
baseline.summary: Gerrit change descriptions show fixed-width line breaks (investigate; may be authoring convention)

baseline.description:
## Context
Operation certificates become asymmetric on the foundation substrate (namespace `rebar.opcert.v1`),
signed by an environment's Ed25519 key and verifiable by anyone against its public key, binding the
ticket/state so they cannot be replayed. New module `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`, mirroring
`attest/authorship.py`, registers `rebar.opcert.v1` in the `registry.py` `POLICY` table pinned to
the `sshsig` scheme, and is wired in `attest/__init__.py`.

**Environment-key era rotation (folded in from former task 5893) — explicit-SHA model.** Env keys
live **out-of-band** (`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, on the code branch, NOT the tickets
branch — see the epic's "Trust config & era-validity protocol"), so the identity epic's
tickets-branch resolver (`authorship.resolve_event_commit` / `_keyring_for`, which glob
`<ticket_dir>/<position>-*.json`) **cannot be reused verbatim**. Instead each key record carries
explicit `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit` **git SHAs on `main`**. What is reused is the
era-validity **rule** — the `git merge-base --is-ancestor` ancestry comparison and the shared
`key_not_valid_at_era` verdict — factored so authorship (position→commit) and op-cert
(explicit-commit) share one ancestry predicate.

**Two-phase verdict (matches `verify_authorship.py`).** Like authorship, the substrate's era check
returns a non-verified `Verdict` (`unknown_principal`) when no key is valid at the era; the
`key_not_valid_at_era` reclassification is done by the **op-cert verifier** (the analog of the
gate-layer two-phase check): first verify against ANY historical key for the env; if that passes
but the era-scoped check fails, emit `key_not_valid_at_era`; otherwise emit `mismatch` (all
verdicts are canonical `verify_signature_result.schema.json` enum members).

**Material fingerprint = the existing canonical gate fingerprint (opaque to the substrate).** The
`material_fingerprint` bound in the subject is exactly the string the gates already compute today
in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py::material_fingerprint`: the 16-hex-char truncation of
`sha256(json.dumps({ticket_id, description, file_impact, children}, sort_keys=True))` (tags /
comments / links / assignee are NOT material). The op-cert substrate (`opcert.py`) treats this
fingerprint as an **opaque string**: `sign_opcert`/`verify_opcert` bind and byte-compare it
exactly, and the caller (the plan-review / completion-verifier gate) supplies it — so the substrate
does not depend on `PlanContext`. Replay/mutation defense is therefore: the verifier is given the
ticket's CURRENT fingerprint and rejects any cert whose bound fingerprint differs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Op-certs are produced/verified via the foundation substrate (`src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`,
      `register_opcert_policy()` pinning `rebar.opcert.v1` → `sshsig` in `registry.POLICY`,
      registered in `attest/__init__.py`) with an Ed25519 environment key; a test asserts a cert
      signed by env E verifies against E's public key and fails against a different key.
- [ ] The certificate subject is an in-toto v1 Statement binding
      `{ticket id, material fingerprint, merged-log position (a `main` commit SHA)}`, where the
      material fingerprint is the existing canonical gate fingerprint
      (`plan_review.pass1.material_fingerprint`, 16-hex sha256 over
      `{ticket_id, description, file_impact, children}`) supplied by the caller and treated as an
      opaque bound string by the substrate; a test asserts a cert cannot be replayed onto a
      different ticket or onto a mutated material fingerprint.
- [ ] Environment-key rotation uses the **explicit-SHA** era model: a key is valid at the cert's
      bound `main` commit `P` iff `is-ancestor(added_at_commit, P)` and not
      `is-ancestor(revoked_at_commit, P)` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), reusing the shared
      ancestry *rule*, NOT `resolve_event_commit`. The op-cert verifier does the two-phase check
      (verify against any historical key; if that passes but the era check fails → the shared
      `key_not_valid_at_era` verdict; else `mismatch`). All three verdicts (`certified`,
      `key_not_valid_at_era`, `mismatch`) are in the canonical `verify_signature_result.schema.json`
      enum — no new verdict string is introduced. A test asserts a cert from a key valid
      at its era verifies while one past its rotation surfaces `key_not_valid_at_era`.
baseline.summary: op-cert: asymmetric environment-signed kind + subject binding

# Fail-loud tombstone registry for removed environment and config inputs

Add a runtime tombstone registry that turns a retired, still-set env var or TOML key into a targeted migration error (old name + replacement + removed-in version + nonzero exit) when it affects store location, write/sync gates, auth, security, or lifecycle policy — while genuinely-unknown keys keep the project's chosen forward-compatibility policy. (Readiness Finding 5 — verified VALID against `src/rebar/_deprecations.py`, `src/rebar/config.py`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `tests/unit/test_config_tracker_dir.py`.)

## Why

The deprecation registry (`_deprecations.py`) now holds **only permanent aliases**; every scheduled-removable surface was deleted in the pre-1.0 passes and survives only in a historical comment block, so a removed name has no runtime signal path. Consequently removed **env vars are fully silent** — not in `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`, so they fall through to defaults with no warning at all — and removed **TOML keys** get only the generic `_config_schema.py` "unknown key … (typo?)" warning-and-ignore (hard error only under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`), which neither names the replacement nor says the key was removed. This bites security/state-sensitive surfaces: `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` silently redirects the store to the default `.tickets-tracker` (proven by `tests/unit/test_config_tracker_dir.py:42-47`); `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` (→ `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`) silently reverts a live-sync write gate; `verify.require_verdict_for_close` (→ `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`) silently drops a close-gate policy; the legacy `rebar_id_guard_mode` id write-guard key is "no longer honored." An operator upgrading with a stale deployment manifest gets a process that reads a different store or a weaker policy than their configuration names.

## What

Adopt the nginx obsolete-directive + OpenSSH deprecated-keyword pattern (retain the retired name explicitly; either report it and name the replacement, or reject configuration when ignoring it could change effective behaviour — OpenSSH counts bad options and terminates config loading):

- Add a `RemovedInput` tombstone registry with explicitly-defined vocabularies
  (in one place in `_deprecations.py`): `_TOMBSTONE_KINDS = frozenset({"env", "cfg",
  "file"})` and `_TOMBSTONE_BEHAVIORS = frozenset({"error", "warn"})`. These are
  **separate** from the existing alias-registry `_KINDS = frozenset({"env", "cfg",
  "cli", "lib", "mcp"})` (which has no `"file"` and serves a different purpose) —
  do not overload it. A `RemovedInput` has (kind, name, replacement, removed_in,
  behavior), applied at config discovery / CLI startup **before defaults are selected**.
- **Distinct, un-swallowable error type — `class RemovedInputError(BaseException)`.**
  A retired error-class input raises a dedicated `RemovedInputError` that subclasses
  **`BaseException`** (NOT `Exception`, NOT `ConfigError`). This is the load-bearing
  choice, not stylistic: `tracker_dir()` wraps `load_config()` in `try/except
  ConfigError` (silent fallback to `.tickets-tracker`), and the MCP boot ensure-sweep
  wraps `_config.tracker_dir()` in broad `except Exception` blocks
  (`mcp_server.py:302-312` and `:311`). A `ConfigError`- or `Exception`-derived
  tombstone would be swallowed at one of those sites — re-creating the exact
  silent-redirect the gate must prevent. A `BaseException` subclass is caught by none
  of them and propagates to a top-level exit. (BaseException over `SystemExit` so it is
  an explicit rebar error type, not conflated with interpreter shutdown.)
- **Defensively re-raise at the MCP boot handlers.** Belt-and-suspenders: the
  `except Exception` blocks at `mcp_server.py:302-312`/`:311` are updated to
  `except RemovedInputError: raise` (before the broad catch) so the intent is explicit
  and survives any future change that widens them to `except BaseException`. Grep the
  config→CLI→MCP path to confirm no bare `except:` / `except BaseException` swallows it.
- **Top-level CLI handler (clean exit, not a traceback).** Because `RemovedInputError`
  is a `BaseException`, an *unhandled* one would print a raw Python traceback. In
  `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:main()` the handler must wrap the **entire body after the
  CLI-override parsing / help-check block through the return** — NOT just `_dispatch()`
  — because `main()` has ~15 early-return intercepts (reconcile, review, review-code,
  enrich, verify-commit-ticket, identity, config, …) that run *before* `_dispatch()`
  and any of which can touch config. So `try: <all intercepts + _dispatch()> except
  RemovedInputError as e: sys.stderr.write(str(e) + "\n"); return 1` — every command
  surfaces the targeted migration message (old name + replacement + removed-in) and a
  nonzero exit, not a traceback. This coexists with `config validate`/`doctor`, which
  does NOT go through the raising `load_config()` path at all — it calls a dedicated
  `scan_tombstones(env, toml_tables, file_paths) -> list[tuple[RemovedInput, str]]`
  that walks the registry and returns **all** matches without raising, so it can report
  every issue (the raising path would abort on the first).
- **MCP-server exit semantics (not just CLI).** The persistent `rebar-mcp` server must
  **fail startup / the write request hard** on a retired error-class input rather than
  downgrade it to a per-request error — verified by a test driving the MCP write path
  with the retired input set (warm cache) and asserting the operation is refused (the
  `BaseException` propagation guarantees this).
- **Cache-safe placement (important).** The env-var tombstone check must fire even
  on a warm `_RESULT_CACHE` hit — today `env_overrides()` runs only on a cache miss
  in `_resolve()`, so a check placed there would be skipped in the long-running MCP
  server. Place the env-var tombstone check at the **top of `load_config()`, before
  the cache lookup**, so it fires unconditionally; and add the tombstoned env-var
  names to `_env_signature()` (the same pattern already used for `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`)
  so a retired var appearing mid-process invalidates the cache. The **file-presence**
  tombstone (`.rebar/config.conf`) is likewise an **unconditional check at the top of
  `load_config()` before the cache-key computation** — `if (repo_root(root) / '.rebar'
  / 'config.conf').exists(): raise RemovedInputError(...)` — NOT added to
  `_config_probe_paths()` (which runs only on a cache **miss** via `_resolve()`, so it
  would never fire on a warm MCP cache hit). **TOML-key tombstones**
  (`verify.require_verdict_for_close`, `reconciler.*`) are checked **inside `_resolve()`**
  (where the TOML is already parsed) and raise there — and this is **inherently
  warm-cache-safe with no cache-structure change or marker**, by the existing
  invariant: `_resolve()` runs only on a cache **miss** and raises *before* populating
  `_RESULT_CACHE`, so a warm entry can only exist for a config that was **clean** at
  population time. For a tombstoned key to appear afterward the config file must change
  (or a new config file must appear) — which the warm-hit validation already detects
  (`_file_token` mismatch on a tracked file, or `_config_probe_paths()` catching a
  newly-appearing config) → cache miss → re-`_resolve()` → re-raise. So no non-file
  sentinel is added to the validation tuple and the `Path(tok[0])` loop stays
  homogeneous; env + file checks are the only pre-cache additions, and all three kinds
  (env, file, TOML) fire on both cold and warm cache.
- **`TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` is gated at the single env-read source, not only in
  `load_config()`.** The store-location env var is read by a **dedicated** function
  `tracker_dir_override()` (config.py:101-105, `os.environ.get("REBAR_TRACKER_DIR")`),
  called directly by `tracker_dir()` AND by
  `rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:_resolve_tracker_dir` (~line 171-182) — paths
  that do **not** flow through `load_config()`. A `load_config()`-only check would leave
  those callers reading the wrong store silently. So the `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` env-var
  tombstone check is placed **inside `tracker_dir_override()`** (the single source for
  that env read) so every resolution path fails closed; the top-of-`load_config()` scan
  still covers the other error-class env vars (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`, …). This
  is a placement refinement of the "top of `load_config()`" rule for the one input that
  has a bypassing dedicated reader.
- Hard-error (nonzero exit, message naming the old name, replacement, removed-in
  release, and a concise migration example) for retired inputs affecting store/data
  location, write targets, sync/reconcile, auth, security controls, verification /
  lifecycle policy, mutation enablement, or external publication.
- Warn-only for operationally inert retired inputs.
- Add a `rebar config validate` / `rebar doctor` command that inspects process env,
  project TOML, user TOML, and file-supplied config against the active aliases and
  tombstones.
- **Prevent future silent removals (anti-regression guard).** The registry is only as
  complete as today's audit; nothing stops a *future* removal from being silent again.
  Add a CI check that compares the set of recognised config keys / env vars against a
  committed golden list and **fails if a key is removed without a corresponding
  tombstone entry** — so the tombstone registry stays complete by construction.
- Do not change the forward-compat policy for genuinely-unknown keys (they keep the
  WARN / `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error` behaviour). The registry covers only
  known retired inputs that would otherwise be silently ignored or defaulted.

Seed the registry with the enumerated removed inputs (from the Finding 5 audit), each individually named and classified:

- **env, error** (store/security/policy/sync): `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR`→`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`
  (store location); `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`→`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`
  (live-sync write gate).
- **env, warn** (operationally inert): `REBAR_PUSH`→`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` (push timing);
  `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES` and `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET` (both
  removed, no replacement — the ref lock self-heals).
- **cfg, error**: `verify.require_verdict_for_close`→
  `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` (close-gate policy).
- **cfg, warn**: `reconciler.lock_backend` (ref lock is the only backend),
  `reconciler.lock_max_retries` (removed, ref lock self-heals).
- **file, error** (security): the legacy flat `.rebar/config.conf` file itself. Its
  reader was removed in DE7, so keys like `rebar_id_guard_mode` (the id write-guard —
  a security surface, replaced by env `REBAR_UNSAFE_ID_GUARD_BYPASS`) are silently
  inert if left in a stale file. Handle this as a **file-presence** tombstone at
  discovery (detect a leftover `.rebar/config.conf` and error, naming `rebar.toml` /
  `[tool.rebar]` as the replacement and the env var for the guard) — **not** as a
  `_config_schema.py` TOML-key tombstone, since the removed key never reaches the
  TOML parser (a TOML-routed tombstone for it would be permanently-unreachable dead
  code).
- **`REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS`→`REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`** lives in the optional `rebar.llm`
  layer (not `config.py`/`_config_schema.py`), so its tombstone is applied in the LLM
  config load path (see Scope), classified **warn** (LLM step budget).

### Implementation sequencing (thin vertical slice first)

Deliver as staged, independently-landable changes so the riskiest assumption is proven before the rest is built on it:

1. **Slice 1 — de-risk the propagation (land first).** The `RemovedInput` registry +
   `RemovedInputError(BaseException)` + the cache-safe env check at the top of
   `load_config()` + the rewritten `tracker_dir` test + the MCP re-raise. This proves
   `BaseException` propagates through the known MCP handlers (`mcp_server.py:302-312`/
   `:311`) without being swallowed — the single riskiest piece.
2. **Slice 2 — breadth on top.** The file-presence (`.rebar/config.conf`) tombstone,
   the `rebar.llm` `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone, the `config validate`/`doctor`
   command, the CI golden-file anti-regression guard, and docs.

Each slice is a stacked change closed only after its own CI is green.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — add the tombstone registry alongside the alias
  registry, defining `_TOMBSTONE_KINDS = frozenset({"env","cfg","file"})` and
  `_TOMBSTONE_BEHAVIORS = frozenset({"error","warn"})` (separate from the existing
  `_KINDS`); update `test_deprecation_registry` for the new vocabularies.
- `src/rebar/config.py` — apply the env-var and file-presence tombstone checks at the
  **top of `load_config()` (before the `_RESULT_CACHE` lookup)** so they fire on a warm
  cache hit, and add tombstoned env-var names to `_env_signature()`; the TOML-key
  tombstone check lives in `_resolve()` (inherently warm-safe — see What) with no
  cache-structure change.
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:main()` — wrap the whole body (all ~15 early-return
  intercepts + `_dispatch()`) in `except RemovedInputError as e: sys.stderr.write(...);
  return 1` (clean exit for every command, no traceback).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — route a known retired **TOML** key
  (`verify.require_verdict_for_close`, `reconciler.*`) to a targeted removed-key error
  rather than the generic "typo?" warning.
- `src/rebar/llm/` (`LLMConfig.from_env()`) — apply the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone
  there (it is not a core-`config.py` var).
- `tests/unit/test_config_tracker_dir.py` — **replace** `test_removed_legacy_alias_ignored`
  (which sets `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` and asserts `tracker_dir_override()` returns `None`
  — silent-ignore) with a new `test_removed_legacy_alias_errors` that asserts a
  `RemovedInputError` is raised instead. Also grep the test suite for any other test
  asserting silent-ignore of a now-tombstoned input and update it (the deliberate
  behavior change: silent-ignore → fail-loud).
- New CLI subcommand (`config validate` / `doctor`) + wiring (`show_config.py`), plus a
  `scan_tombstones(env, toml_tables, file_paths) -> list[tuple[RemovedInput, str]]`
  function it calls to walk the registry and collect **all** matches **without raising**
  (so it reports every issue); it does NOT call the raising `load_config()` path. Exits
  non-zero if any error-class match is present.
- MCP server entry path — the `except Exception` blocks at `mcp_server.py:302-312`/`:311`
  re-raise `RemovedInputError` explicitly; ensure a `RemovedInputError` raised during config load fails
  the write request / startup hard rather than being caught by the request-loop's
  top-level handler; audit that path for broad `except` handlers.
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json` (committed) + a pytest that imports the live
  allowed-key set (`_config_schema`) + env vars and the `_deprecations.py` registries,
  diffs against the golden file, and fails if a key is in neither the live set nor a
  tombstone/alias (anti-regression guard).
- `tests/unit/` — table-driven test over every seeded removed input: each retired
  input yields nonzero exit + old name + replacement + no store mutation; a
  genuinely-unknown key keeps the existing policy.
- `docs/config.md` — document the tombstone behaviour and the validate/doctor command.
- Out of scope: removed CLI flags already rejected by argument parsing and removed
  Python attributes that already raise — those are already fail-loud.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `RemovedInput` tombstone registry exists and is applied at config discovery
  and CLI startup before defaults are chosen, at the top of `load_config()` before
  the `_RESULT_CACHE` lookup (so it fires on a warm cache hit) — verified by a test
  that sets a retired env var, primes the cache with a prior `load_config()`, and
  confirms the tombstone still fires.
- [ ] Setting a store/security/policy/sync-affecting retired input (e.g.
  `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR`, `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`,
  `verify.require_verdict_for_close`) fails with a nonzero exit and a message naming
  the old name, the replacement, and the removed-in release, and does not mutate the
  store or reach the network — verified by a table-driven test that, for each seeded
  removed input, sets only that input, invokes config load / the smallest CLI command
  that initialises config, and asserts nonzero exit + old-name + replacement in the
  message + no store write (store files byte-unchanged) + no network call (enforced via
  `pytest-socket`, or a `unittest.mock.patch` on the lowest-level HTTP/socket primitive
  asserting `call_count == 0`).
- [ ] Operationally-inert retired inputs (`REBAR_PUSH`,
  `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES`, `reconciler.lock_backend`, …) warn rather than
  error — the warning is emitted via the existing deprecation-warning path
  (`logging.warning` on the `rebar` logger, the same channel `warn_deprecated` uses),
  naming old→replacement→removed-in. Verified by a second sub-table in the table-driven
  test that captures the logger (via `caplog`) and asserts exit code 0, the log record
  contains the old name + replacement, and the process continues to normal completion.
- [ ] The error-class tombstone raises a `RemovedInputError` (a `BaseException`
  subclass, not `ConfigError`/`Exception`) — verified by the **rewritten**
  `test_config_tracker_dir.py` test (formerly `test_removed_legacy_alias_ignored`,
  which asserted silent-ignore): setting `TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR` and calling
  `tracker_dir()` now raises rather than falling back to `.tickets-tracker` (its
  `except ConfigError` cannot swallow a `BaseException`).
- [ ] Setting `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` and calling `LLMConfig.from_env()` surfaces the
  tombstone (naming `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`) rather than silently ignoring it — verified
  by a dedicated test in the `rebar.llm` layer.
- [ ] The tombstone fails hard on the **MCP-server** path too (not only the CLI) —
  verified by an **in-process** test that primes the config cache, sets a retired
  error-class input, then calls an MCP write-tool handler function directly (e.g.
  `create_ticket`) and asserts `RemovedInputError` propagates out (not caught by the
  boot `except Exception` at `mcp_server.py:302-312`/`:311`, which are confirmed to
  re-raise it). Plus a pytest that reads `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` and asserts every
  line matching `except\s+(Exception|BaseException)` has a `RemovedInputError: raise`
  guard immediately above it (a reproducible check, not a hand grep).
- [ ] A CI/anti-regression check fails if a recognised config key / env var is removed
  without a corresponding tombstone entry — implemented as a pytest test that imports
  the live allowed-key set (`_config_schema`'s allowed keys) + env vars and the
  tombstone/alias registries (`_deprecations.py`), diffs against a committed
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json`, and fails with a diff if any key appears in
  neither the live set nor a tombstone/alias.
- [ ] A  … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Fail-loud tombstone registry for removed environment and config inputs

content.text: # RC2b: snapshot-horizon-safe replay (no silent sub-horizon drop)
## Why
When two clones write at once, one can compact and delete the events it folded before seeing the other's event.
After merge, that event sorts BEFORE the snapshot and replay's positional skip drops it regardless of
`source_event_uuids` -> silent data loss. Live store holds ~11 such orphans.
## Decision (ACCEPTED): Option 1 (rebuild-on-stray) + Option 3 (conservative horizon)
Option 2 (per-field LWW-by-timestamp) deferred.
## Concrete rules
- SETTLED (Option 3): compaction folds an event only if `hlc.physical_now() - event_ts >= COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS`.
`COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` is a NEW `CompactConfig` field (default `1_800_000_000_000` = 1800 s in HLC nanosecond
ticks — HLC uses `time.time_ns()`); ALSO add its coercer entry to `_SECTIONS['compact']` in `_config_schema.py`
and an env-var alias in `config.py` (the established pattern). Younger "hot-edge" events stay live `.json`.
- REBUILD (Option 1): fsck detects a merged-in pre-snapshot orphan (KNOWN-type `.json` sorting before the SNAPSHOT,
uuid absent from `source_event_uuids`) and rebuilds that ticket's snapshot from the full ordered log INCLUDING
`.retired`. This needs a NEW `include_retired: bool = False` param on `reduce_ticket` (`reducer/_api.py`) +
`prepare_event_files` (`reducer/_cache.py`, both listing paths ~97/~102) + `scan_for_latest_snapshot` seeing the
same set. CACHE (resolved): the rebuild path BYPASSES the `compute_dir_hash` cache and reads the full file set
directly (avoids a stale `*.json`-only hash ignoring `.retired`). Rebuild uses `fsutil.atomic_write` (the existing
helper — do not hand-roll tmp+rename); the old snapshot goes to `<snap>.bak`, deleted only after a clean replay
round-trip in the same run. `.bak` CRASH RECOVERY (resolved): if `<snap>.bak` exists at rebuild start, RE-REBUILD
from the full log (authoritative) and overwrite — do not "restore from .bak". Log (WARN) each detected orphan +
rebuild; a rebuild counter lives as a module-level metric in fsck. Concurrency: a single-writer guard (the store
write-lock) serializes fsck rebuild vs compaction on a ticket.
## Dependencies
- A1 (tricolour-head-ratfish) ADDS `RETIRED_SUFFIX`/`is_active_event`/the `.retired` rename (NOT in the codebase
today) — depends_on A1 landing first (wired). A3 (entitled-unsweet-nutria) REUSES this `include_retired` rebuild.
## Scope
`reducer/_processors.py` (process_snapshot + positional skip ~648-702), `reducer/_api.py` + `reducer/_cache.py`
(`include_retired` + cache bypass), `_commands/fsck.py` (orphan-detect + rebuild + counter), `_commands/compact.py`
(horizon fold guard), `_config_schema.py` (`CompactConfig.COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` + `_SECTIONS['compact']`),
`config.py` (env alias). `reducer/_sort.py` read-only. NOT the reconciler code.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `COMPACTION_HORIZON_NS` on `CompactConfig` (default 1_800_000_000_000 ns), coercer in `_SECTIONS['compact']`, env alias in `config.py`; ADR records the rule. Test: an event younger than the horizon is NOT folded.

- [ ] `reduce_ticket`/`prepare_event_files`/`scan_for_latest_snapshot` gain `include_retired`; default False preserves behavior; the rebuild path bypasses the cache. Test: rebuild does not return a stale cached state.

- [ ] Rebuild uses `fsutil.atomic_write`; `.bak` written + deleted only after a clean round-trip; if `.bak` exists at start, re-rebuild (test covers the interrupted-rebuild restart); rebuild counter incremented + WARN logged.
- [ ] A merged-in pre-horizon orphan is no longer silently dropped. Two-clone sub-horizon-append regression test: RED before, GREEN after.
- [ ] Determinism proof: `reduce_ticket` twice on the same file set (incl. shuffled `os.listdir` order) -> equal compiled_state. Proof: `python -m pytest tests/scripts/reducer/ -k determinism -q`.
- [ ] Decision + design recorded in an ADR.

baseline.summary: Snapshot-horizon-safe reconciliation (RC2b): no silent sub-horizon drop
