baseline.description:
## Context
Code review reviews each Gerrit patchset (and each local `rebar review-code` run) fresh, with no memory across runs. Plan review already has a novelty rising-floor convergence mechanism (ADR 0008): on a re-review it loads the prior run's SURFACED findings, an LLM novelty sub-call scores each current finding against those priors, and a deterministic predicate drops NOVEL + low-priority findings so the remediation loop converges instead of surfacing fresh trivia each pass. This epic brings a comparable, machinery-reusing novelty mechanism to code review, adapted for its one key difference: code findings carry source citations, so the floor is gated per-finding on whether the cited code REGION changed since the last review.

A durable, git-shared `code_review` artifact (per Gerrit change/revision) already persists findings as a write-only calibration corpus (limestone-unethical-zebrafinch). This epic adds the READER and the region gate that consume it, plus local-review persistence.

## Design (settled)
- REUSE boundary is the contract, not the prompt. Code review calls TWO pure kernel primitives UNCHANGED: the novelty SCORING contract (novelty_model / NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS in review_kernel/verify.py) and rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty) (review_kernel/decide.py). The novelty PROMPT is gate-specific and is NEW work: the existing plan_review_novelty.md uses the {{plan}} template var and is plan-scoped, so code review adds its own novelty reviewer prompt (code_review_novelty.md, oriented to a diff + a finding list) and a new reviewer id (code-novelty), exactly as the base/overlay reviewer prompts already differ per gate. Runner wiring mirrors plan-review's novelty sub-call: the novelty system prompt carries the diff as domain context, the surfaced prior findings are appended to the instructions as a context block, and the call binds output_schema='code_review_novelty' (the reused kernel contract). The cites_prior_location sub-question is adapted to source-file/line region semantics. Exact prompt front-matter, template-variable names, and reviewer-index registration are implementation details resolved by the child against the live reviewer index / runner conventions — the plan fixes the mechanism (diff-as-context + prior-findings-in-instructions + reused novelty contract), not an unwritten prompt's field names. A new region_gated_floor (code_review-specific) wraps rising_floor_drop with a third conjunct. The reused novelty contract is registered for code review at code_review/contracts.py::register_contracts() (importing novelty_model from review_kernel.verify), mirroring plan_review/passes.py::register_contracts(); without it a RunRequest(output_schema='code_review_novelty') fails at runtime. No shared novelty-engine abstraction spanning reader/eligibility/gating, since those genuinely differ per gate.
- Novelty is scored ONLY against findings returned to the client (surfaced block/advisory), never against dropped/hidden findings (surfaced-only; the plan-review side is old-frilly-plankton).
- Permanent drop of low-impact findings is the intended convergence compromise; the priority floor is the escape hatch that keeps surfacing higher-impact findings. Trust the priority score: no categorical exemption, and recalibration lives on the priority axis, not the novelty axis. No eval-gated activation flag.
- Region gate is content-addressed and resilient (survives rebase/force-push, needs no reachable commit): store a per-reviewed-file content-hash map {path: sha256} in the artifact. Reuse boundary: the private _hash_file primitive from plan-review attest.py is reused; dependency_hashes() itself is NOT (it is plan/ticket-coupled — pulls ticket file_impact, resolves plan-verdict citation buckets, and a pinned attested snapshot), so code review writes a thin dep collector over its changed_files that calls _hash_file per path; at the next run, re-hash the current files and compare. The region state is a DEFINED vocabulary, not prose: constants REGION_UNCHANGED / REGION_CHANGED / REGION_UNKNOWN (in code_review/region_gate.py), referenced by the predicate and the hash-compare. Only REGION_UNCHANGED enables a drop; REGION_UNKNOWN behaves as raise. Absence-evidence, multi-location, moved, and renamed-file findings all resolve to REGION_UNKNOWN. File-level for v1; line-level (reviewdog added semantics via git diff --no-index against a stored snapshot) is a later refinement.
- Fail-safe: region_gated_floor is wrapped in try/except. Any failure in the reader (artifact load), the current-file hashing, or the comparison resolves affected regions to REGION_UNKNOWN and returns the FULL unfiltered finding set (no drops) — mirroring plan-review's _maybe_apply_rising_floor / _score_floor_novelty fail-safes. A broken signal can only make the gate stricter, never suppress more. A prior artifact lacking the deps map (an older v1 payload) yields REGION_UNKNOWN for all findings -> no drops.
- Carryover findings carry an explicit schema field carried_from (the prior run/patchset key) and are OMITTED from coaching (not re-coached); they remain surfaced. Dropped novel-on-unchanged findings move to the verdict dropped bucket. drop_reason reuses the existing verdict field (plan-review uses the value "novelty"); code review ADDS the value "novelty-region" to that same vocabulary.
- Keying + addressing: local reviews are keyed on the session id (resolve_session_id(), with a per-invocation uuid fallback when it returns None); Gerrit reviews are keyed on the change_id, which SPANS revisions/patchsets: each patchset emits its own artifact titled "code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}", and the reader for patchset N+1 queries prior revisions of the SAME change_id (the change is the memory key; the revision only makes each artifact idempotent). Artifacts are addressed by title: Gerrit uses "code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}" (existing); local uses "code-review: session:{session_id}", and session_id is ALSO a top-level payload field. TYPED keyspaces (session:<id> vs change:<id>); each reader matches only its own title prefix / key, so a prior LOCAL review never seeds a change's FIRST Gerrit review.
- uuid-fallback rationale (conscious tradeoff, not a gap): a bare `rebar review-code` with no session lifecycle (resolve_session_id() -> None) mints a fresh uuid per invocation, so local convergence is intentionally INERT there — isolation is chosen over convergence to guarantee no cross-session contamination. Genuine per-session local convergence is delivered wherever a session lifecycle exists: any coding-agent harness (native session var, validated shared-across-subagents + unique-per-session) or a SessionStart shim exporting REBAR_SESSION_ID (docs/session-id-shims.md) for harnesses lacking a native var.
- Neutrality preserved: the Pass-1 finder never sees prior findings; only the post-find novelty seam does (ADR 0008 Invariant 1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reader loads prior SURFACED (decision in {block, advisory}) code-review findings by typed key (session/change).
- [ ] The reader returns the reviewed-file content-hash map from the resolved artifact.
- [ ] The code_review_result_v1 payload carries session_id as a top-level field.
- [ ] The code_review_result_v1 payload carries a {path: sha256} deps map.
- [ ] Local artifacts use the "code-review: session:{session_id}" title scheme.
- [ ] Local `rebar review-code` persists a code_review artifact (today only the Gerrit voter does).
- [ ] region_gated_floor reuses the novelty sub-call and rising_floor_drop unchanged (no fork).
- [ ] region_gated_floor drops a finding only when it is novel AND low-priority AND REGION_UNCHANGED.
- [ ] region_gated_floor never drops on REGION_CHANGED.
- [ ] region_gated_floor never drops on REGION_UNKNOWN.
- [ ] Carryover findings are stamped with the carried_from field.
- [ ] Carryover findings are omitted from coaching while remaining surfaced.
- [ ] A reader/hash/compare error returns the full unfiltered finding set (no drops).
- [ ] Local review memory is keyed on the session id (with a per-invocation uuid fallback).
- [ ] Gerrit review memory is keyed on the Gerrit change.
- [ ] A test verifies a prior local review does not change a change's first Gerrit review verdict.
- [ ] c639 makes the code-review reader surfaced-only.
- [ ] Bug old-frilly-plankton makes the plan-review novelty prior set surfaced-only.
- [ ] The ADR records the explicit decision that NO arbiter / relation-taxonomy / oscillation-loop machinery is added and why the lightweight novelty floor suffices (positively discharging the no-dso-cycle-machinery success criterion; this is the epic's original oscillation/convergence-signal decision, made by design rather than deferred).
- [ ] On a re-run of a review with NO code changes to the cited files, every prior low-priority SURFACED finding is stamped carried_from and NOT re-coached, and is not re-surfaced as novel — verifiable by the region_gated_floor test harness. (This is the observable proxy for "repeat-noise reduced".)
- [ ] Novel low-priority findings on UNCHANGED code are dropped for convergence; novel findings on CHANGED code, and all high-priority findings, are always raised at full strength.
- [ ] Local and Gerrit finding memory are isolated namespaces: a prior local review does not alter a change's first Gerrit review verdict.
- [ ] Achieved WITHOUT importing dso's heavy cycle machinery (arbiter, relation taxonomy, oscillation loop).
baseline.summary: Cross-patchset code-review finding memory (deferred from sure-foyer-aroma)

content.text: ## Summary
rebar reopen with no arguments crashes with a raw bash 'unbound variable' diagnostic instead of usage text.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. rebar reopen
2. Output: .../rebar: line 291: $1: unbound variable (exit 1). Compare: rebar claim / rebar archive with no args print proper Usage text.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: misuse prints the reopen usage line to stderr, exit 1, no shell diagnostics (the sibling-command contract).
- Actual: raw set -u failure from the dispatcher.
## Source
src/rebar/_engine/rebar:291 — reopen arm dereferences "$1" after _strip_output_flags/set -- with no arity check, under set -u.
## Fix direction
Arity guard before the dispatch: [ $# -ge 1 ] || { _print_subcommand_help reopen >&2; exit 1; } (match the pattern used by sibling arms). Validated diff in the implementation-notes comment.
## Suggested RED test
rebar reopen (no args) -> exit 1, stderr contains "Usage: rebar reopen", stderr does NOT contain "unbound variable"; rebar reopen <closed-id> still reopens.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No-arg reopen prints usage, exit 1, zero bash diagnostics (RED test first)
- [ ] Happy-path reopen unchanged
- [ ] Audit sibling arms for the same hole; fix any found in the same pass

baseline.summary: rebar reopen with no args crashes with raw bash 'unbound variable' instead of usage

baseline.description:
# A per-pass model configuration seam (one env var cannot express four passes)

## Problem

rebar's gates deliberately run different model classes per pass. On the direct-Anthropic path this works today and is MEASURED: a real `rebar review-plan` made 41 calls on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (Pass-1, which escalates up from the YAML `model_ladder`) and 1 on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` (the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier downgrade). The operator requirement is exactly that shape: Pass-1 on opus for most criteria, Pass-2/Pass-4 on sonnet.

There is no way to express that on any non-default provider, because the whole selection collapses onto ONE knob:

- ~~**The verifier downgrade inverts.**~~ **RESOLVED — retained only so the record shows what changed.**
  This bullet argued that `review_kernel/verify.py:269`'s `verifier_default if model == default_model
  else (model or verifier_default)` would read ANY Bedrock id as an explicit operator choice, so the
  sonnet downgrade would stop applying and Pass-2/Pass-4 would follow Pass-1 onto one model. That
  mechanism is now UNREACHABLE: `resolve_verifier_model` has ZERO callers under `src/rebar`, pinned by
  `test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers` (172e). The verifier paths resolve the
  `standard` CLASS instead, so the inversion cannot occur. What remains is narrower and is the real
  subject of this ticket: four code-review steps declare no class at all.
- ~~**Pass-1's ladder routes to the wrong provider.**~~ **RESOLVED — this problem no longer exists, and
  the claim is retained only so the record is honest about what changed.** This section originally read
  that `plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder: [claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6,
  claude-opus-4-8]` as BARE names, and that since `config.py` maps the `claude` prefix to provider
  `anthropic`, a Bedrock run would send its Pass-1 finders to DIRECT ANTHROPIC — a split brain. VERIFIED
  AT HEAD: that ladder now reads `[trivial, standard, frontier]`, i.e. CLASS terms (story 7761 landed
  it), so the bare-name provider inference no longer applies to plan-review's Pass-1. The split-brain
  risk this ticket was partly created to fix is already closed for plan-review; what REMAINS is the
  code-review gate, below.
- **Code review is only PARTLY split — this is the remaining problem and the reason this ticket is still
  needed.** CORRECTED against HEAD: an earlier version said `code-review.yaml` "declares no `model:` and
  no `model_ladder:` on any step", which is no longer true — `verify` (`:143`) declares `model: standard`
  at `:156` (story 172e landed it). The four steps that still inherit `cfg.model` implicitly are `base`
  (`:67`), `round_a` (`:77`), `round_b` (`:109`) and `coach` (`:182`). So the gate has a Pass-2 split and
  no Pass-1/Pass-4 split. Note the four undeclared steps do NOT fall back to `resolve_verifier_model` either — nothing under
  `src/rebar` calls it. They simply inherit the run's single resolved `cfg.model`, having declared no
  per-step model for the interpreter to override with.

## Why this blocks two stories

- **eb6e (production cutover)** scopes itself to "the bot service's `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`" — one env var
  for four passes. Both single-model outcomes are wrong: opus-everywhere hard-fails Pass-2, which
  pins `temperature=0` (MEASURED: `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` returns 400 `temperature is
  deprecated for this model`; see [rebar:1903-868c-b704-4a80]), and sonnet-everywhere silently
  downgrades Pass-1 with no test to catch it.
- **0d76 (parity bar)** compares v1=Anthropic against v2=Bedrock. Without per-pass control the arms
  differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), so any criterion failure is
  unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production. A full corpus run is ~3,200 model
  calls; spending that on an unattributable comparison is the expensive way to learn this.

## Approach (the mechanism EXISTS — this ticket is the CONSUMER)

**THE EXACT CLASS EACH STEP DECLARES — stated here so no executor has to guess.** A review round blocked twice on this being unspecified.

| step | `code-review.yaml` | pass | declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base`    | `:67`  | Pass-1 finder (single-shot) | `model: frontier` |
| `round_a` | `:77`  | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `round_b` | `:109` | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `verify`  | `:143` | Pass-2 verifier             | `model: standard` — ALREADY LANDED (172e) |
| `coach`   | `:182` | Pass-4 coach                | step-level `model: standard` |

This matches the criterion above — opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4 — because `frontier` and `standard` resolve to exactly those families via `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS`.

**WHY THE BATCH STEPS MUST USE A LADDER KEY, AND WHY IT HAS EXACTLY ONE RUNG.** A step-level `model:` on a `batch:` step is a SILENT NO-OP — `interpreter.py:384-395` builds `BatchRunRequest` from the `batch:` sub-dict only (`model_ladder=tuple(batch.get('model_ladder') or ())`) and never passes the enclosing step's `model:`, while `runners.py:128-130` computes `resolve_model_string(ladder[0]) if ladder else None` and comments that an empty ladder means "no per-step model, NOT a resolved class". Because `model` IS a legal step key (`schema.py` `_STEP_ORDER`), such a declaration VALIDATES and is then discarded — and a test asserting only that the YAML carries a class token would PASS while runtime behaviour was unchanged. An earlier version of this very table made that mistake. ONE RUNG, not plan-review's three: `plan-review.yaml:62-65` declares its finder batch as `model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]`, so copying that precedent here is the obvious move — and it is the WRONG one for this ticket. A ladder escalates per criterion, so the model that actually answers a given criterion is NOT determinate: a cheap criterion may be resolved at `trivial` and never reach `frontier`. This ticket's first criterion requires a TEST asserting "the RESOLVED model for each pass ... is the intended class", and that assertion is not writable against a non-deterministic resolution. Flat classes keep the criterion falsifiable. Adopting the ladder for cost reasons is a legitimate FOLLOW-UP optimisation, but it is a different change with a different oracle, and bundling it here would make the per-pass guarantee untestable — which is the whole point of the ticket.

**PASSES vs STEPS — two different counts, both correct, stated so they are not read as a contradiction.** "Four passes" is the plan-review PASS model (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verifier, Pass-3 decide, Pass-4 coach) and is what this ticket's title means. "Five LLM-calling steps" is the CODE-REVIEW gate's step count in `code-review.yaml`. One pass can be implemented by MORE THAN ONE step — which is precisely how the batch steps `round_a`/`round_b` escaped an earlier count. Neither number is wrong; they measure different things.

**REWRITTEN: an earlier draft called this a "candidate, not a decision" and sketched a mapping still to be designed. Stale — epic eb58 has since shipped it.** `model_classes.py` provides the trivial/standard/frontier slots, the nine `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_<FIELD>` overrides, per-class fallback chains and class-aware resolution; the batch runners and verifier paths already consume it; and `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is deprecated, fanning out to all three classes. This ticket does NOT design a mapping — it makes the remaining gate steps DECLARE their class.

Make the per-pass model resolvable per provider rather than inferred from one string. Sketch: express the mapping (Pass-1 finder ladder, Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier) as configuration keyed by provider, so a Bedrock run names Bedrock inference-profile ids for each pass instead of inheriting bare `claude-*` names. Note `bedrock_model_id` is NOT the answer — a single scalar cannot express a mapping, which is part of why it was deleted [rebar:281f-3336-c668-4979].

**STALENESS AUDIT of this section, run against source at HEAD 18ecd9709 rather than accepted wholesale from a review finding:**
* STALE, fixed: `plan-review.yaml` no longer names bare `claude-*` ids — `:62` declares a `model_ladder`
  in CLASS terms (7761).
* STALE, fixed: "no per-provider class mapping exists" — `model_classes.py` exists and is consumed.
* **RETRACTED — I DEFENDED THIS CLAIM AND IT WAS WRONG.** An earlier revision asserted that
  `review_kernel/verify.py:263-269`'s equality test (`verifier_default if model == default_model else
  ...`) is OPERATIVE, and that steps without a declared class "still inherit the equality rule". The
  function body does still contain that expression — which is all I actually checked — but it has
  **ZERO production call sites**: `resolve_verifier_model` appears under `src/rebar` only as its own
  definition, one docstring mention in `model_classes.py:279`, and two re-export lines in
  `review_kernel/__init__.py`. `tests/unit/test_code_review_verifier_class.py:171`
  (`test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers`, landed by 172e) ENFORCES that
  nothing calls it, and instructs "do not relax the assertion". So the rule is superseded and
  unreachable, not live. I verified EXISTENCE and inferred REACHABILITY, which is not the same thing.
* **THE REAL MECHANISM, corrected:** the four undeclared steps inherit the run's single resolved
  `cfg.model` because they declare no per-step model at all — the interpreter simply has nothing to
  override with. That single-knob inheritance is what this ticket removes. `resolve_verifier_model` is
  NOT part of the story and must not be cited as the defect; if anything, a NEW caller of it would
  reintroduce the 172e defect and break the guard test.

This ticket does NOT touch `verify.py:269`. An earlier revision said the chosen shape "must also fix" that equality test; that instruction rested on the retracted claim above. The helper is superseded and callerless, a guard test pins it that way, and ADDING a caller would reintroduce the defect 172e removed. Leave it alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts the RESOLVED model for each pass under a Bedrock configuration is the intended
      class (opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4)
- [ ] a test asserts no bare `claude-*` model id is resolved to provider `anthropic` during a run
      configured for another provider
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade still applies when the operator has NOT explicitly
      chosen a model, on a non-default provider
- [ ] the code-review gate expresses its per-pass models explicitly. RE-MEASURED against the shipped YAML — and this CORRECTS AN ERROR AN EARLIER PASS OF THIS PLAN
      INTRODUCED. That pass wrote "the gate has THREE prompt steps, not four", which is WRONG: it
      counted only the single-shot prompt steps and MISSED THE TWO BATCH STEPS. The gate has FIVE
      LLM-calling steps — `base` (:67), `round_a` (:77), `round_b` (:109), `verify` (:143) and `coach`
      (:182). Only `verify` declares `model: standard` (:156, landed by 172e). The remaining work is
      therefore FOUR steps — `base`, `round_a`, `round_b`, `coach` — all still inheriting `cfg.model`.
      Correcting "four" DOWN to "three" made this plan worse than its original wording, and would
      have shipped two batch steps silently unclassed
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real gate run on the non-default provider shows the per-pass model ids
      actually used, cited from the run's usage log in a comment
baseline.summary: Per-pass model configuration seam: one env var cannot express four passes

Sweep (rebar-debug, sibling of 0e15) found two non-CLI bug-close call sites that never got the ed13 --class requirement, so both now fail to close BUG tickets:

1. src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:117 — MCP tool transition_ticket() calls rebar.transition(id, current, target) with NO close_class. The library rebar.transition/_lib_writes.transition (line 337) DOES support close_class=. transition_core (txn.py:253) enforces --class unconditionally on any *->closed of a bug (unless current=='idea'), and force/force_close do NOT bypass it. => an agent over MCP CANNOT close any bug ticket (raises 'requires --class'). Regression: MCP could close bugs before ed13. (This is NOT the deliberate no-force policy; close_class is a required classification, not a bypass.)

2. src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py:356 — replay closes via transition_compute(local,'open','closed',force=True) with no close_class; force!=force_close and neither bypasses the class guard. Re-materializing a closed BUG from an NDJSON dump is rejected and the per-row fail-open (line 357) leaves the bug OPEN with a warning => import cannot restore closed bugs.

FIX: thread close_class through both. MCP: add a close_class parameter to transition_ticket and pass to rebar.transition (only needed for bug close; empty ok for non-bug). Import: carry the source close event's close_class if present, else default (e.g. 'undetermined'/'duplicate'). RED->GREEN each: MCP tool closes a bug with a valid class; import re-materializes a closed bug. CLI create/close and the canary (Gerrit 853) are handled; probe-rebar closes non-bugs (exempt).

content.text: ## Why

Audit OSS finding #5 (MEDIUM). The docs tree has exceptional depth (36 top-level docs + 30-plus ADRs) but no navigation: the Documentation URL in pyproject lands on a bare directory listing, and the content skews heavily toward LLM-agent operators (CLAUDE.md is the richest usage doc but is agent-facing). A human newcomer gets the README Quickstart and then a wall of internals (plan-review-gate.md, workflow-authoring-v2.md). Two artifacts are missing: an index, and a human-oriented "using rebar day-to-day" guide.
## What

1. docs/README.md: a short index grouping every doc by audience — user / operator / contributor / agent — with one-line descriptions; link it from the main README and point pyproject's Documentation URL at it.

2. docs/user-guide.md: a human-facing guide distilling the CLI workflow (create/claim/comment/link/transition, search/list/ready, session logs, the gates as a user experiences them) without agent-protocol framing; cross-link rather than duplicate the deep docs.
## Scope
In: the two new docs, README + pyproject link updates, one-line description sweep of existing docs for the index. Out: rewriting existing docs, restructuring docs/ directories, changes to CLAUDE.md.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] docs/README.md exists, lists every file in docs/ (and the adr/ + design/ dirs as groups) under an audience heading with a one-line description
- [ ] docs/user-guide.md covers the day-to-day CLI loop end-to-end for a human reader, with working commands verified against the current build
- [ ] Main README links the index; pyproject [project.urls] Documentation points at docs/README.md
- [ ] No orphan docs: everything in docs/ is reachable from the index

baseline.summary: Human-facing docs: docs/README.md index grouped by audience + a day-to-day user guide

baseline.description:
## Observability gap

`rebar audit show <id> --output json` surfaces the **completion** attestation/sidecar, but its
`plan_reviews[]` entries do **not** expose whether each plan-review was cryptographically
**signed**. The per-entry keys are: `coaching, coverage, findings, impact_model_version,
material_fingerprint, metrics, model, regver, runner, schema, ticket_id, ticket_type, verdict,
verified_at_sha` — there is no `signed` / `signature` / `signer` / `key_id` field.

Consequence: a PASS that was signed is **indistinguishable in the audit** from a PASS produced
with `--no-sign` (or one whose signing step failed to persist). The plan-review **claim gate**
depends on a valid signed attestation existing, yet the audit trail — the natural place to
confirm gate-readiness — cannot answer "is this plan-review signed, by whom, and at what SHA?".

To confirm signature persistence today you must bypass the audit and read the raw
`*-SIGNATURE.json` events on the `tickets` branch (`git show tickets:<id>/<...>-SIGNATURE.json`)
and check the latest SIGNATURE is newer than the latest EDIT. That is not a supported/ergonomic
verification path.

## Suggested fix

Add plan-review signature metadata to each `plan_reviews[]` entry in the audit projection —
e.g. `signed: bool`, `signer` (author id / email), `key_id`, and the attestation
`material_fingerprint` + `verified_at_sha` it covers — mirroring how the completion attestation
is already surfaced. Optionally a `signature_current: bool` (no EDIT newer than the SIGNATURE).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rebar audit show <id> --output json` `plan_reviews[]` entries include a signature block
  (signed flag + signer + key_id + covered fingerprint/sha) when a `SIGNATURE` event exists.
- [ ] A signed PASS and a `--no-sign` PASS are distinguishable in the audit output.
- [ ] Text output (`--output text`) notes signed/unsigned per plan-review.
baseline.summary: audit show does not surface plan-review signature status (signed PASS indistinguishable from --no-sign)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Agents and contributors struggle to discover *how to write a plan that passes the
plan-review gate*. The existing material is either gate-mechanics (`plan-review-gate.md`) or a
generated, reviewer-facing criterion registry (`plan-review-criteria-guide.md` / `rebar
explain <id>`) — there is no concise, author-facing on-ramp, and AGENTS.md mispoints authors
at the criterion registry for the "description template". The same discoverability gap exists
for the code-review (`LLM-Review` + `Verified`) gate.

## Approach

Add two hand-written, prose on-ramp docs — `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and
`docs/passing-code-review.md` — kept short and distinct from the generated registry (so the
registry stays the single source of truth for the reviewer). Make them discoverable from the
CLI/MCP by extending the existing `rebar explain` seam with author-guide names (`rebar explain
plan` / `rebar explain review`) via the one shared `registry` lookup that already backs the
CLI, the MCP `explain_criterion` tool, and the library. Fix the AGENTS.md pointers. Rejected
alternative: generating these from the registry (rejected — the on-ramp is prose, not a
per-criterion rubric, and would fight the parity gate).

## Scope

- docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md (new), docs/passing-code-review.md (new)
- docs/README.md (link both new docs — the docs-index CI gate requires every top-level
  docs/*.md to be linked from the index)
- AGENTS.md (fix pointers; add code-review on-ramp reference)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py (AUTHOR_GUIDES + explain_guide)
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py (_explain routes guide names)
- src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py (explain_criterion routes guide names)
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py (cover the guide path)

## Testing

Unit tests over the new `explain_guide` path across all three surfaces (library, CLI, MCP):
success for every registered guide, unknown-name → `unknown-id`, missing-file → `missing-file`.
Pure in-process logic (no live boundary), so offline unit coverage exercises the real path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` exists and states the description template + the
      blocking-criteria checklist; verified by reading the file and `rebar explain plan`
      printing it (exit 0).
- [ ] `docs/passing-code-review.md` exists covering the commit checklist, LLM-Review dimensions
      (blocking vs advisory), and vote responses; `rebar explain review` prints it (exit 0).
- [ ] `rebar explain <criterion-id>` still works unchanged; an unknown topic exits 1 with a
      structured `unknown-id` error.
- [ ] AGENTS.md points authors at both new docs; no pointer claims the template lives in the
      criterion registry.
- [ ] Both new docs are linked from `docs/README.md`, so the docs-index CI gate stays green;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_check_docs_index.py::test_current_repo_index_is_clean`.
- [ ] `make lint` and the explain unit tests pass.
baseline.summary: Author-facing plan-review & code-review on-ramp docs + rebar explain plan/review

baseline.description:
# S1 — Optional Streamable-HTTP transport for rebar-mcp + transport hardening

## Why
Authentication in MCP is an HTTP-transport concern; the spec says stdio servers must not
authenticate. rebar-mcp is stdio-only today (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`, `build_server().run()` with
no transport arg). Before any verifier can exist there must be an HTTP transport to authenticate
against. This story adds that transport and its network hardening — the foundation every auth story
builds on — with stdio unchanged as the default. It also owns the SDK version pin, because it is
the first story to construct the SDK's HTTP transport / `TransportSecuritySettings`.

## What
Add an **optional Streamable-HTTP transport** to rebar-mcp, selected by config, using the official
`mcp` SDK's native support:
- **Pin the SDK here:** set `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` in `pyproject.toml` — in BOTH places it appears: the
  `[project.optional-dependencies] mcp` extra AND the `[dev]` extra (both currently `mcp>=1.9`). The
  v2-alpha renames the surface; 1.28.1 is at/above the DNS-rebinding fix GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f. All
  later stories build on this pin.
- Extend the existing **flat** `McpConfig` dataclass and the flat `_SECTIONS['mcp']` key→coercer
  dict in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (the one-level `coerce_sparse` architecture — NO nested
  sub-tables) with flat scalar keys: `transport` (`stdio` default | `http`), `http_host` (default
  `127.0.0.1`), `http_port` (default `8000`), `http_path` (default `/mcp`), `http_allowed_hosts`
  (comma-separated), `http_allowed_origins` (comma-separated), and `allow_unauthenticated_http`
  (bool, default `false`). Each is one dataclass field + one flat coercer entry, auto-deriving its
  `REBAR_MCP_*` env var. This story registers these keys in `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` and
  regenerates `docs/mcp-reference.md`/`docs/env-vars.md` for its slice (the CI drift gate
  `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` must pass). NOTE — both doc generators currently miss
  dynamically-derived MCP env vars and must be adjusted (all later key-adding stories rely on these
  fixes): (a) `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` **hardcodes** the gate-env-var table (line ~208, the
  static tuple `("REBAR_MCP_READONLY","REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM","REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC")`) instead of
  iterating `MCP_ENV_VARS` → change it to iterate `MCP_ENV_VARS`; (b) `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
  (which generates `docs/env-vars.md`) AST-scans for literal `os.environ`/`os.getenv` calls, so it
  will NOT see the `REBAR_MCP_*` names the flat coercer derives dynamically → teach it to also ingest
  `MCP_ENV_VARS`. `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` (drift-gated by `scripts/check_server_manifest.py`)
  remain the authoritative registration; the two generators are made to reflect it.
- In `build_server`/`main`, when `transport=http` construct `FastMCP("rebar", host=…, port=…,
  transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(...))` and run via `run(transport="streamable-http")`;
  the stdio path is unchanged.
- **Explicit transport-security defaults:** DNS-rebinding/Origin protection **on**. For a loopback
  bind, set explicit loopback allowlists (`127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>`, `[::1]:<port>` and
  the matching `http://…` origins) rather than empty lists (empty + protection-on either 421s
  localhost or degrades protection). Construct `host`/`port`/`transport_security` at `FastMCP(...)`
  time, NOT via late attribute assignment (the documented "421" late-host bug).
- **Non-loopback bind fail-closed gates:** a non-loopback `http_host` requires BOTH
  `http_allowed_hosts` AND `http_allowed_origins` to be non-empty, AND an explicit TLS-at-edge
  acknowledgment `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_TLS_AT_EDGE` (a flat `http_tls_at_edge` bool key) — because bearer
  tokens and proxy secrets must never cross the network in cleartext; without it the server refuses
  to start.
- **Unauthenticated-HTTP guard:** `allow_unauthenticated_http` (env `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP`)
  read through the flat coercer (a resolved config field, NOT a bespoke `os.environ` read). Starting
  `transport=http` with auth disabled refuses to start unless `allow_unauthenticated_http` is true.
  (Auth config lands in S2; until then "auth enabled" is treated as false, so HTTP requires the ack.)

## Approach & rationale
Use the SDK's built-in Streamable-HTTP transport and `TransportSecuritySettings` rather than
hand-rolling an ASGI server — the SDK provides both, keeping this a thin wiring change on a blessed
seam, consistent with peer servers (GitHub/Grafana/Neon). Keep every config key flat to fit rebar's
existing `coerce_sparse` architecture (adding scalars alongside `readonly`/`allow_llm`/
`allow_jira_sync`).

## Scope
The transport + transport-security + the two fail-closed startup gates (non-loopback and
unauthenticated-HTTP) + the SDK pin only. It ships **no** token verifiers and validates **no** token
(that is S2+). A subset of the epic.

## Security
Crosses a trust boundary (opens a network listener). Mitigated here by: DNS-rebinding/Origin
allowlisting on by default with explicit loopback defaults; loopback-only bind by default; a
non-loopback bind requiring both allowlists AND the explicit TLS-at-edge ack; and the fail-closed
unauthenticated-HTTP refusal. TLS is terminated at an edge proxy (documented in S7); rebar binds
HTTP behind it and never advertises or serves bearer auth in cleartext.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` pins `mcp>=1.28.1,<2`; `make typecheck` resolves the SDK imports used here.
- [ ] `McpConfig` exposes the flat `transport`/`http_host`/`http_port`/`http_path`/
      `http_allowed_hosts`/`http_allowed_origins`/`http_tls_at_edge`/`allow_unauthenticated_http`
      keys as fields + `_SECTIONS['mcp']` coercer entries; unset → stdio, byte-identical to today
      (observable: existing `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` stdio suite passes).
- [ ] Integration test (tier: integration — an in-process ASGI HTTP client, e.g. httpx
      `ASGITransport`, driving the SDK's Streamable-HTTP ASGI entrypoint within its lifespan/session
      context; concrete entrypoint resolved against the pinned `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` at implementation
      time; a unit test cannot cross the Starlette transport/middleware seam) boots with
      `transport=http` (and `allow_unauthenticated_http=true` set for this auth-off boot) and asserts
      a baseline MCP request succeeds (observable oracle: HTTP 200 + valid `initialize` response).
- [ ] Integration test asserts a disallowed `Host` → **421** and a disallowed `Origin` → **403**,
      while an allowed loopback request passes (negative control in the same test), confirming the
      explicit loopback defaults work with protection ON.
- [ ] Unit/integration test asserts a non-loopback `http_host` refuses to start when either
      allowlist is empty OR `http_tls_at_edge` is unset, and starts when both allowlists AND the ack
      are supplied (observable oracle: process exits non-zero / raises a clear message vs boots).
- [ ] Unit/integration test asserts `transport=http` with auth off and no
      `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP` refuses to start, and starts when the ack is set.
- [ ] `MCP_ENV_VARS` + `server.json` include the new keys; `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` iterates
      `MCP_ENV_VARS` (not the hardcoded tuple) and `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` ingests `MCP_ENV_VARS`,
      so the regenerated `docs/mcp-reference.md` AND `docs/env-vars.md` include every new `REBAR_MCP_*`
      key; and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (observable oracle: both regenerated docs
      contain the new key names and the drift tests are green).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive: stdio remains default; all new keys default to today's behavior when unset. The only
cross-cutting change is the `mcp` pin, backward-compatible with existing installs. No change to the
existing 48 tools or the stdio path.
baseline.summary: S1 — Optional Streamable-HTTP transport for rebar-mcp + transport hardening

# Data Center refuses to null a sub-task's `fields.parent` (HTTP 400)

## Provenance

Filed to satisfy [rebar:88d9-fe42-e50f-4067]'s AC11, which pre-authorised this exact outcome:

> UNLESS it reports its explicit `SETUP FAILED` message, which means Data Center refused to null a
> sub-task's `fields.parent`. That is a PLATFORM finding, not this fix failing; record it and file
> it separately rather than weakening the cell.

Observed on harness run **30834117797** (job 91755000385, main @ `25ead49f3e`).

## Evidence — verbatim

> SETUP FAILED (not a rebar defect): Data Center REFUSED to clear the parent of sub-task RBJYRMS-2 —
> BackendHTTPError: HTTP Error 400: JiraError HTTP 400 url:
> http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/api/2/issue/10029

The message came from `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips`'s SETUP, not its assertion: the cell could not get Data Center into the precondition state it needed, so it never exercised the code under test. The cell was deliberately built to report this case DISTINCTLY rather than as an ambiguous red, and it did.

## What this does and does not establish

**Does:** DC 8.17.1 rejects a `PUT` that nulls a sub-task's `fields.parent`. A sub-task on DC must have a parent — the field is structurally required — so there is no "detached sub-task" state for the fixture to create.

**Does not:** say anything about whether rebar's inbound parent clear works. That path's evidence is the discriminating trio recorded on 88d9 (measured RED against both wrong states, GREEN against the fix) plus the full 2079-passing suite. The live cell simply cannot reach it on a sub-task.

## Consequence — the inbound clear has no live coverage on DC

This is the honest statement of the gap, and it should not be papered over: the ONLY live cell for the inbound parent clear is blocked by a platform constraint, so on Data Center that path is proven by unit evidence alone. Given that this epic has twice shipped mutation-proven code that was wrong in production (1276, 1288), unit-only coverage of a data-affecting path is a real risk, not a formality.

## Options for restoring live coverage, none yet chosen

 1. Use a NON-sub-task child whose parent is an Epic Link, and clear the epic link instead — a
    different write path (greenhopper sentinel epic `"none"`), so it tests the clear the production
    code would actually take for a non-sub-task.
 2. Assert the refusal itself as the contract: pin that DC rejects the null so a future DC version
    that starts accepting it fails loudly and tells us the coverage gap can be closed.
 3. Accept unit-only coverage for the sub-task clear and record it as a known limit.

Option 1 is the only one that yields real coverage, and it is closest to what a rebar deployment would actually do, since [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] casts doubt on the sub-task write path working at all on this version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the refusal is confirmed against the target DC version with the raw response body recorded
      (the current evidence is the status code and URL only)
- [x] one of the three options above is chosen, with the rejected ones and the reason recorded
- [x] if option 1 or 2: the cell lands and is GREEN on a live harness run, with the run id recorded
- [x] N/A — option 2 was chosen, not option 3. Condition never held. ~~if option 3: the limitation is documented where a DC operator will see it, not only on a ticket~~
baseline.summary: Data Center refuses to null a sub-task's fields.parent (HTTP 400): the inbound-clear live cell cannot reach its precondition

Stop forcing `gc.auto=0` on the tickets worktree so stock background `git gc`
can reclaim loose-object/pack growth. This is safe **only in conjunction with the
union-recovery work** (sibling WUs), but the gc-config change itself is isolated
and leaves the suite green on its own.
## Scope (files)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: delete `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` (lines ~74-84)
and its call site (~124).
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`: drop the two `git config gc.auto 0` writes (~217, ~413).
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`: drop the `gc.auto 0` write (~61).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`: drop the `gc.auto 0` write (~182); instead set
`git config gc.autoDetach true` at init so a forked background gc never serialises
a foreground write.
- Migration: idempotent `git config --unset gc.auto || true` run at init (and/or fsck)
so existing trackers shed the stale `gc.auto=0`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_ensure_gc_auto_zero` and its call removed from `event_append.py`
- [ ] All four `git config gc.auto 0` writes removed (`txn.py` x2, `compact.py`, `init.py`)
- [ ] `gc.autoDetach=true` set at init
- [ ] Idempotent `--unset gc.auto` migration runs at init (re-runnable, no error if absent)
- [ ] A `git gc --prune=now` on a populated tracker loses no reachable ticket data (test)
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green

## Why

The epic needs a project-owned Pass 1 finder that rejects concrete portability failures without demanding generic portability prose. The fresh-worktree experiment has already proven that the project overlay, prompt loader, and production fan-in mechanism support this extension shape.

## What

Add and activate `project.portability` in the project criteria overlay, author its Pass 1 rubric prompt, and add focused integration tests for prompt resolution, scope routing, and production finding fan-in.

## Scope

In scope:

- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py`
- Pass 1 discovery for both leaf and container tickets

Out of scope:

- Pass 2 validity or impact logic
- Pass 3 disposition logic
- coaching moves
- live semantic calibration
- remediation of existing portability debt

## Approach

Use the existing project overlay seam rather than adding a built-in criterion. This keeps rebar-specific policy in the rebar repository while exercising the same supported extension boundary available to clients. Configure `exec: 1-TURN`, `facet: project-invariants` (the established free-form project grouping used by `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py`), `applies_at.scope: [container, leaf]`, `default_posture: blocking`, and `block_threshold: 0.9`, then add the id to `activate`.

The prompt front matter is fixed as:

- `schema_version: 1`
- `title: Rebar portability`
- `description: Find concrete rebar portability failures across supported client shapes.`
- `execution_mode: single_turn`, the prompt-library counterpart of routing `exec: 1-TURN`
- `category: plan-review-criterion`
- `dimension: project-invariants`

The rubric body uses these exact second-level headings so tests have a mechanical oracle:

- `## Finding threshold`
- `## Required finding fields`
- `## Supported client-shape matrix`
- `## Non-findings`

Under `Finding threshold`, require all four counterexample elements before emitting a finding: cited plan mechanism, materially different supported client shape, causal failure mechanism, and observable breakage scenario.

Under `Required finding fields`, specify `location: str` for the plan citation, `finding: str` for the assumption plus causal mechanism, `scenarios: list[str]` for the alternate client shape plus observable breakage, `evidence: list[str]` for the plan quote plus grounding facts, and `criteria: list[str]` containing `project.portability`.

Under `Supported client-shape matrix`, include these exact labels and values:

- `Harness`: Python library, CLI, remote MCP; no Claude Code or Codex dependency.
- `Target project`: Ruby, Python, Java, Next.js, .NET, Terraform subprojects in a monorepo.
- `Platform and venue`: macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD, CI, servers, developer workstations.
- `Project location and access`: in-checkout current working directory, explicitly located workspace, server outside the checkout, no unrestricted-local-filesystem assumption.

Under `Non-findings`, require the literal rules `Silence about portability is not a finding` and `Project-specific behavior behind project configuration or an explicit extension boundary is allowed`.

## Grounding

Prior art is `tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py`, which proves the overlay and prompt contract, plus `tests/unit/workflow/test_production_batch_runner.py`, which covers the real fan-in runner. The parent epic `jira-reb-1003` records the completed experiment at `2026-07-16T00:50:08Z`: worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-reb-1003-portability`, branch `experiment/jira-reb-1003-portability`, base `b0ac25447203d864463408c933497f21bc1f8dbf`, result `experiment=PASS; routed_scopes={container:true,leaf:true}; project_fan_in=[project.portability]; surfaced_findings=1; move_loaded=project-portability; restricted_to=project.portability`.

## Test Strategy

Exercise the real overlay loader, prompt resolver, routing registry, and `ProductionBatchRunner` fan-in with deterministic fakes. Tests inspect the authored rubric contract; live LLM behavior belongs to the calibration child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The overlay activates `project.portability` with `exec: 1-TURN`, `facet: project-invariants`, and `applies_at.scope: [container, leaf]`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k criterion_activation`.
- [ ] The activated criterion uses `default_posture: blocking` plus `block_threshold: 0.9`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k criterion_activation`.
- [ ] The project rubric declares the exact six front-matter values specified in this plan. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k prompt_frontmatter`.
- [ ] The project rubric resolves through the production prompt loader for `project.portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k prompt_resolution`.
- [ ] A leaf plan routes `project.portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k leaf_routing`.
- [ ] A container plan routes `project.portability`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k container_routing`.
- [ ] Production project fan-in surfaces an injected `project.portability` finding. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k production_fan_in`.
- [ ] The rubric contains the exact `Finding threshold` heading plus all four counterexample elements. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k finding_threshold`.
- [ ] The rubric contains the exact `Required finding fields` heading plus the five typed field markers specified in this plan. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k finding_schema_markers`.
- [ ] The rubric contains every label-value pair specified under `Supported client-shape matrix`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k client_shape_matrix`.
- [ ] The rubric contains the exact rule `Silence about portability is not a finding`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k omission_guard`.
- [ ] The rubric contains the exact rule `Project-specific behavior behind project configuration or an explicit extension boundary is allowed`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py -k project_configuration_guard`.
- [ ] Existing behavior remains unchanged when the project overlay is absent. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_criteria_overlay.py tests/unit/workflow/test_production_batch_runner.py`.
baseline.summary: Activate the rebar portability finder

# A failed identity write DELETES the created Jira issue

## Context / Problem

`dispatch_one.create_one` writes identity markers immediately after `create_issue` succeeds, and on ANY failure in that block it deletes the freshly created issue (`dispatch_one.py:324-328`) and re-raises. Destroying a successfully-created issue to recover from a failure to LABEL it inverts the cost: a created-but-unlabelled issue is recoverable, a deleted one is not.

The trigger is not exotic. Jira rejects a field write with *"Field 'x' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown"* in at least three distinct situations, and the message is misleading in roughly half of them: the field genuinely is not on the project's Create/Edit screen; the workflow property `jira.permission.createclone.denied` is set (nothing to do with screens); or the value is MALFORMED on a field that IS on the screen. A self-hosted DC instance with a customised Create screen hits this on the first write.

**A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME BLOCK, found while tracing this one and not previously recorded.** The write-ahead records the key BEFORE the identity writes — `record_pending_key(local_id, jira_key)` + `save()` at `dispatch_one.py:307-308`, deliberately inside the try. The rollback then deletes the issue but **never unbinds**, so a KEYED-pending binding survives pointing at a DELETED Jira key. On every subsequent pass `recover_pending`'s keyed branch calls `client.add_label(keyed, …)` on that dead key, raises, is caught into the failure sink, and the entry stays pending — permanently. The ticket never syncs again and each pass re-attempts a doomed write. So the current behaviour does not merely lose an issue; it also strands the local ticket forever. Both symptoms have the same cause and the same fix, so they are handled here rather than split.

## Approach

**Stop deleting. Leave the keyed-pending binding in place and let retro-attach finish the job.**

The recovery path this needs already exists and is already correct: `recover_pending`'s KEYED branch retro-attaches the `rebar-id` label and the `local_id` entity property and then confirms, with **no Jira search** — deterministic, and explicitly documented as such because a crash in the create→label window must not yield a duplicate. A failed identity write leaves exactly the state that branch is built for. The rollback was solving a problem the write-ahead protocol had already solved, and destroying data to do it.

So the change is subtractive: remove the `delete_issue` call, keep the BRIDGE_ALERT (retitled to say the issue was RETAINED for retro-attach, not deleted), keep re-raising `write_err` unmasked so the item is still reported as failed, and leave the binding keyed-pending.

**The one case that is genuinely different: a `BindingPersistError`.** If `record_pending_key` fails to persist, no key was recorded and no label was written, so nothing local points at the issue. The issue is not lost, though — it is an unmarked issue in the project, which the INBOUND pass adopts as a new remote issue on the next run. That is a strictly better outcome than deletion and needs no special handling; it is called out here so the next reader does not add a delete back for that branch.

**Declare the screen requirement rather than solving it.** rebar requires `labels` on the project's Create and Edit screens. The mature precedent is explicit: Sentry's Jira integration states it does NOT support custom required fields — *"The only required fields supported are those that are pre-populated by Sentry"* — with "create the issue in Jira and link it" as the workaround. That is a deliberate scope boundary from the most mature integration in the comparison set.

**Rejected: createmeta-driven pre-flight field discovery.** It would mean implementing DC ≥ 9.0's split `createmeta/{proj}/issuetypes[/{id}]` endpoints with a different response envelope plus version-gating at 9.0 — substantial machinery to predict a failure that the retro-attach path already recovers from once we stop deleting. Explicitly out of scope.

**Rejected: unbinding on rollback.** It would fix the stranded-binding half while keeping the destructive half, and it would re-open the duplicate hazard: an unbound local ticket with a live unlabelled issue in Jira is exactly the state that produces a second issue on the next pass (see [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03]).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — remove the rollback delete; retitle the
  BRIDGE_ALERT; leave the binding keyed-pending; improve the error message.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — state the Create/Edit screen requirement for `labels`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests (new module).

## Testing

* **the issue survives** — with `add_label` raising, assert `delete_issue` is NEVER called and the
  created key still exists on the client.
* **the binding is left recoverable** — assert the entry is keyed-pending with the created key, then
  run `recover_pending` against a client whose label write now succeeds and assert it CONFIRMS to the
  same key. This is the property that makes not-deleting safe, so it is asserted end-to-end rather
  than by inspecting the entry alone.
* **no duplicate** — a subsequent create pass for the same local ticket creates NOTHING, since the
  binding is now confirmed.
* **the failure is still loud** — `write_err` is re-raised unmasked and the BRIDGE_ALERT is written;
  a retained issue must not read as success.
* **the error message** names the screen requirement AND the two other causes.
* **the persist-failure branch** does not delete either, asserted, since that is the case a future
  reader is most likely to "fix" by restoring the delete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a failed identity write NEVER calls `delete_issue`, asserted by a test that fails against the
      current code
- [ ] after a failed identity write the binding is KEYED-pending on the created key, and a subsequent
      `recover_pending` against a recovered client CONFIRMS it to that same key — asserted end-to-end,
      not by inspecting the entry alone
- [ ] a following create pass for that local ticket creates NO second issue
- [ ] the original `write_err` is still re-raised unmasked and a BRIDGE_ALERT is still written, so the
      item is reported failed rather than silently retained
- [ ] the BRIDGE_ALERT text says the issue was RETAINED for retro-attach — it currently claims "Jira
      issue deleted", which would be false after this change
- [ ] the operator-facing error names the Create/Edit screen requirement AND mentions the
      `jira.permission.createclone.denied` workflow property and the malformed-value case, since the
      Jira message is misleading about half the time
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` states that `labels` must be on the project's Create and Edit screens
- [ ] the `BindingPersistError` branch also does not delete, asserted
- [ ] createmeta pre-flight is explicitly recorded as OUT of scope with the Sentry precedent
baseline.summary: A failed identity write DELETES the created Jira issue; declare the screen requirement instead

baseline.description:
## Why
Keep the single-instance bot alive under hangs, controllable in an incident, and — critically — **crash-safe**: a restart must never double-submit or strand a stack. This is the reliability-fallback backbone. Split out of S5 (`perpetual-ultrasonic-raccoon`).

## Files
- `infra/autolander/loop.py` — EDIT: heartbeat write, emergency-stop sentinel check, SIGTERM drain + recovery-record write, restart-recovery reconciliation. (`loop.py` is created NEW by the **S2** core-loop tasks — S5d `depends_on` **S2a** so the file exists before these lifecycle hooks are added.)
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.autolander` — EDIT: add the `HEALTHCHECK` line (the file itself is created NEW by sibling **S5a**; this task `depends_on` S5a so the create precedes this edit).
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — EDIT: set `stop_grace_period: 120s` on the autolander service (so the SIGTERM drain can write `recovery.json`).
- `infra/autolander/tests/test_crash_recovery.py` — NEW: the crash-recovery/idempotency test suite (kill-at-each-phase + the drain⇄autoheal-race case).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Heartbeat (AC5):** the bot writes a timestamp file in the state volume once per its 15 s poll (S2 cadence); its age is served as `heartbeat_age_s` by S5c's status endpoint. Contract: freshness ≤ 15 s; `land`'s `lander_down` treats age **> 90 s** (6× poll) as down.
- [ ] **Liveness/restart (AC4):** a `HEALTHCHECK` marks the container `unhealthy` on a **hang** by stat-ing the **local heartbeat file** and failing if its age exceeds **90 s** (the `lander_down` bound) — it MUST NOT probe Gerrit (a Gerrit outage would flap restarts). **Concrete Docker parameters:** `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=2 CMD <stat-based check: unhealthy if heartbeat age > 90s>` (interval 30 s × retries 2 → ~90 s to trip, matching the bound; `start-period=60s` avoids boot false-positives). During the ≤120 s drain the bot keeps heartbeating each tick, so the age stays < 15 s and the container remains `healthy` — autoheal is not provoked. The `willfarrell/autoheal` sidecar (S5a) restarts the `autoheal=true`-labeled container on `unhealthy`.
- [ ] **Emergency-stop (prior art: Zuul `pause`):** an emergency-stop **sentinel file** in the state volume (presence = stop; operator creates to pause, removes to resume) transitions the bot to `paused` (the S2 `phase` value) — STOPS consuming new `Autosubmit` changes. Lives on the state volume so a redeploy does not silently un-pause.
- [ ] **Drain-on-shutdown + crash-safe recovery (RELIABILITY FALLBACK):** on SIGTERM the bot's **FIRST action is to write the recovery record** `recovery.json` to the state volume (the `wipChain` snapshot — `change_id`, `chain_member_ids`, `tested_shas`, `phase`, `re_drive_count`, and the S3 handback `acknowledged` flag) — written up-front so recovery is guaranteed no matter what interrupts the drain. It then attempts a graceful finish of an already-near-complete submit + S3 outcome write (prior art: Zuul `graceful`), time-bounded to **120 s**, with the compose service set to **`stop_grace_period: 120s`** so `docker compose stop/down` does not SIGKILL early.
- [ ] **Drain ⇄ autoheal race (must not fight each other):** during the drain the bot **keeps writing its heartbeat each tick** so the HEALTHCHECK stays healthy and autoheal is not provoked into a mid-drain `docker restart` (autoheal's `docker restart` does NOT honour `stop_grace_period`). And because `recovery.json` is written FIRST, even if autoheal *does* restart the bot mid-drain, recovery is still safe (the restart path below reconciles it). Belt-and-suspenders: no interruption can strand a stack.
- [ ] **Restart reconciliation** — on restart the bot reads `recovery.json` + reconciles against LIVE Gerrit and S3's markers BEFORE selecting new work, with a rule for every interruption point:
  - `phase=rebasing` — discard the in-memory `wipChain` and **re-select from scratch** (`Autosubmit` still set, Gerrit holds the current patchset). No submit happened; nothing to undo.
  - `phase=awaiting_verified` — discard in-memory state and **re-select**; the change is still `Autosubmit`+needs-fresh-`Verified`, so the loop re-enters `awaiting_verified` for the same patchset. Idempotent; no submit happened.
  - `phase=submitting` — check LIVE Gerrit: all members `MERGED` → write the `merged` outcome/ack; not merged → **re-drive**. Never blindly re-issue submit.
  - `phase=idle` — no in-flight work was captured; nothing to recover — proceed to normal selection.
  - `phase=paused` — recovery defers to the **emergency-stop sentinel file** (the source of truth, not the snapshot): if the sentinel is still present, stay `paused`; if it was removed, resume normal selection. (The `recovery.json` phase is advisory here; the sentinel decides.)
  - **an incomplete hand-back** (detected by an S3 marker with `acknowledged=false` — NOT a `wipChain` phase value) — complete the idempotent `Autosubmit`-removal across the stack, then set `acknowledged=true`.
  No double-submit; no stranded stack. (This covers all six `phase` values — `selecting` reduces to `idle`/re-select.)
- [ ] **Heartbeat-freshness proving test:** a test reads `heartbeat_age_s` from the S5c status endpoint (`GET /autolander/status`) while the bot runs and asserts it stays **< 15 s** (fresh); then it stops the heartbeat writer (simulating a hang) and asserts `heartbeat_age_s` crosses **90 s**, that the `HEALTHCHECK` flips the container to `unhealthy`, and that a concurrent `land` returns `lander_down` — bounds-checking the actual measured age, not just the prose contract.
- [ ] **Crash-recovery/idempotency test (the reliability guarantee):** an automated test kills the bot at each `wipChain` phase (`rebasing`, `awaiting_verified`, `submitting`) **and during an in-flight hand-back** (S3 marker `acknowledged=false`), and asserts the restarted instance neither double-submits nor strands a stack, and converges the S3 marker to `acknowledged=true`. A dedicated case asserts the **drain⇄autoheal race is benign**: a SIGTERM followed by an autoheal `docker restart` mid-drain still recovers cleanly (because `recovery.json` is written first).
baseline.summary: S5d Liveness/heartbeat/autoheal + emergency-stop + drain + crash-safe recovery

## Context
rebar records NO session identifier on a claim distinct from `assignee` and the event
`author`. A claim writes a `STATUS(open->in_progress)` (+ `EDIT(assignee)`); the envelope
carries `timestamp`, `uuid`, `event_type`, `author` (git user), and `env_id` — but
`env_id` is the tracker init-environment id (written once at `rebar init`, shared by ALL
events), NOT a per-session/per-agent id. So an `in_progress` state cannot be attributed to
the specific agent **session** that claimed it.

The design for this epic is complete (unknowns resolved, experiments run, OSS surveyed).
Full design doc lives with the driving session; the resolved decisions are below.

## What
When a coding-agent session id is present in the environment, automatically record it on
the `open->in_progress` transition so an in_progress ticket is attributable to the session
that started it — additively, without disturbing `assignee`/`author`, local-only,
compaction-safe, tolerated by older clones.

## Design decisions (resolved)
- **Env-var contract (ordered, data-driven list).** Explicit rebar var first, then native
  harness vars by popularity, ambient last: `REBAR_SESSION_ID` -> `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`
  -> `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` -> `SESSION_ID` -> None. (`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` captured
  as a secondary `remote_session` field.) **Design correction (story 7656):** Codex is NOT a
  native var in this list — it exposes no supported readable session env var, so it is covered
  by its SessionStart shim exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID` instead (there is no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`).
  Never fall back to git HEAD (changes per commit). One shared resolver replaces today's two
  divergent ones.
- **Storage.** Record on the claim `STATUS` event's `data["session"]`; fold to reducer
  state key `claimed_session` (mirrors `assignee`). No new event type, no envelope change.
- **Jira.** N/A — a local reducer-state key never enters the reconciler (outbound differ
  is an explicit allow-list).
- **Reliable capture.** `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is an env var only in the remote runner;
  the local CLI needs a SessionStart hook that exports `REBAR_SESSION_ID`.

## Context (gotchas to respect — from OSS prior art)
- Session ids are NOT stable across `--resume`/`--continue`/fork/subagents; treat the
  record as "the session that emitted this claim event", not a per-ticket lifetime id.
- A leaked/stale env var pollutes unrelated sessions (rebar bug 76e9 class) — prefer
  hook-injected, session-scoped values.
- Keep it local-only + opaque (consent/provenance sensitivity); read the var as a plain
  string, never interpolate/execute it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Decomposed into discrete-deliverable child stories parented to THIS epic (via each
      child's `parent_id`, confirmable with `rebar deps 38ec-5f12-fdf5-4340`): S1
      `6014-0863-2e36-41b3`, S2 `68ef-da4f-b64b-4903`, S3 `199b-f56f-5ba1-468b`, S5
      `c557-8f46-0c16-4bf5`, S4 `ec5c-bd06-aa49-42d0`, S6 `7656-0a67-e881-4131`, plus the
      module-size split refactor `458f-5b67-961e-4e80` — all closed.
- [x] Env-var contract implemented as the ordered, extensible resolver above
      (`REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`, with
      Codex covered by its `REBAR_SESSION_ID` shim rather than a native `CODEX_THREAD_ID` — see
      `src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py`).
- [x] Storage shape implemented (STATUS `data["session"]` -> `claimed_session` state).
- [x] Claim/transition records the id when present; no-op when absent.
- [x] Read surface exposes the claiming session id for a ticket.
- [x] Backward/forward compatible + compaction-safe (regression-tested).
- [x] Local-CLI capture shim ships (Claude Code), plus Codex/Cursor shims.
- [ ] A claim made while a recognized session env var is set durably records that session
- [ ] Absent the env var, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (fully backward compatible).
- [ ] The recorded id survives compaction and is preserved-and-ignored by older clones.
- [ ] Works in the LOCAL Claude Code CLI (not only the remote runner), via a capture shim.
- [ ] Session id is attributable across the popular OSS harnesses (Claude Code, OpenCode,
baseline.summary: Track a claim<->session relationship, auto-recorded from environment variables when present

# Tier-3: CI-scheduled enrichment drain (GitHub Actions)

## Context
Follow-on to the cross-ticket overlap epic (only-crave-art). Because the store is git-backed and already pushed to a remote, a scheduled GitHub Action (`on: schedule:`) can run `rebar enrich --drain` against the pushed store — zero LOCAL setup, the Renovate/Dependabot model. rebar already runs Actions for ticket→Jira sync, so the harness exists.

## Why deferred (product-owner decision)
We want to confirm the system works WITHOUT the CI job before implementing CI as a primary mechanism, because MANY CLIENTS WILL NOT HAVE dedicated CI configured. Tier 1 (opportunistic detached drain) must carry the feature on its own first.

## Known caveats to design around
- GitHub cron has a 5-min floor and 5-30+ min delays under load (best-effort cadence, not an SLA).
- Scheduled workflows auto-disable after ~60 days of repo inactivity.
- Pair `schedule:` with `workflow_dispatch:`; use a GitHub App token / OIDC (the bare GITHUB_TOKEN can't update workflows). The API key must be a CI secret.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A committed `.github/workflows/` drain runs `rebar enrich --drain` on a schedule and pushes results back.
- [ ] Manually triggerable via `workflow_dispatch`.
- [ ] Documented as best-effort (imprecise cadence, inactivity auto-disable) and optional — Tier 1 remains the primary mechanism.
baseline.summary: Tier-3: CI-scheduled enrichment drain (GitHub Actions)

# Outbound parent-set can never be carried by a reconcile pass on Data Center (two gates that do not compose)

## Provenance

Found while building story 5200's missing row-12-OUTBOUND live cell, by an agent instructed to establish the real contract before writing an oracle rather than assume a round-trip was supported. It is a PRODUCT gap, not a test gap.

## Mechanism — each gate is defensible alone; on DC they are DISJOINT

**The APPLY side wants a SUB-TASK child.** `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` `set_parent` (:668-712) reads the issue, checks `fields.issuetype.subtask` (:693-694), and for a sub-task writes `issue.update(fields={"parent": {"key": parent_key}})` (:711-712). For a NON-sub-task child it raises `NotImplementedError` (:695-710) naming the reason: epic membership on DC is the "Epic Link" CUSTOM FIELD written through the Agile API under `greenhopper`, not `fields.parent`. That decline is deliberate and correct — it stops `fields.parent` being written and silently no-op'd.

**The EMIT side wants an EPIC parent.** `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent:136-139` returns `(False, None)` — omitting the parent field ENTIRELY — for any parent whose local `ticket_type` is not `epic`. That is bug 8b25's hierarchy guard, built over `local_ticket_types` (`outbound_differ.py:475-477`) and already unit-covered by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` — verified UNEDITED: `git diff 7fc96b277 gerrit/main` on that path is EMPTY across the whole epic, and change 1302 adds only a new test file.

**A DC sub-task's parent is a STANDARD issue, which imports as local `ticket_type` `"task"`.** So the one child shape DC accepts (sub-task) can only have a parent shape the emit gate refuses (non-epic). The sets are disjoint: **no reconcile pass can ever emit an outbound parent-set that DC would accept.**

Both gates were written for Cloud's next-gen Epic-parent hierarchy, where they compose fine. Nobody composed them against DC's model.

## Why this is the FIFTH instance of a known class

"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — d067 (outbound status submitted as a field edit, never a transition), 8d68 (inbound UPDATE never minted an identity), 751e (empty assignee never unassigns), 2b16 / 88d9 (inbound link removal and parent clear never emitted). Every one was a SILENT success: no traceback, no alert, the pass reports OK. This is the same shape — a local parent/child relationship simply never reaches Data Center, and nothing reports that it did not.

`dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows `set_parent`'s exception (warn-and-continue, keyed at :546), so even the DECLINE is invisible; but on DC the decline is not even reached, because the emit gate dropped the field first.

## Scope note — deliberately NOT gating e369

Recorded rather than folded into epic e369, consistent with the operator's ruling on `e39f-5055-f5af-424a` (a DC write-path gap ruled follow-up, not gating). Two supporting reasons:
 * the fix is a HIERARCHY-MODEL change, not a patch — either the emit gate learns DC's sub-task shape or
   DC's `set_parent` learns the Epic Link field. Either is a design pass with a real blast radius.
 * closing e369 does not assert this works. Its operator-attested criterion is bidirectional reconcile
   (an issue created in DC appears locally; a local EDIT appears in DC), both proven live; no criterion
   claims outbound parent sync.

**I am flagging this as a BORDERLINE call.** The operator's earlier ruling on the three J11-surfaced defects took the strictest available option, and unlike e39f this one does NOT fail safe — it is a silent DIVERGENCE, not a safe refusal. If the operator prefers the strict reading, reparenting this under e369 is one command. The tension is recorded here on purpose rather than resolved quietly.

## What story 5200 does and does not now cover

5200's row-12-outbound cell (change 1283) asserts the PRIMITIVE at the transport level — `dc_transport.set_parent(child, B)` then a raw-REST read-back of `fields.parent` — following the same precedent row 14 outbound set for the same reason. It deliberately does NOT assert the pass-level suppression as correct behaviour, because that would freeze this gap into the suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a test asserts, at the pass level, that a local parent/child relationship syncable on Cloud is
      ALSO emitted for DC — i.e. the emit gate and DC's accepted child shape overlap for at least one
      real configuration
- [x] the chosen fix is stated explicitly: either the emit gate learns DC's sub-task shape, or DC's
      `set_parent` writes the Epic Link custom field through the Agile API — with the rejected option and
      the reason recorded. Option B (DC set_parent writes the Epic Link through the Agile API) CHOSEN with three reasons; option A (teach the emit gate DC's sub-task shape) REJECTED with three reasons — both recorded in the CLAIMED comment
- [x] the 8b25 hierarchy guard's Cloud behaviour is UNCHANGED, pinned by its existing tests in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` — verified UNEDITED: `git diff 7fc96b277 gerrit/main` on that path is EMPTY across the whole epic, and change 1302 adds only a new test file
- [x] a parent that genuinely cannot be represented on the deployment surfaces an OPERATOR-VISIBLE signal
      rather than being silently dropped — DONE in change 1305 (merged `364c4e8f5e`): a `bridge_alerts` entry on every set_parent failure arm, three distinct kinds (`outbound-parent-unrepresentable` / `-rejected` / `-failed`), fail-open, warn-and-continue preserved. the swallow at `dispatch_one.py:571-578` is why this class
      stayed invisible for five instances running
- [x] mutation-checked, with verdicts recorded here — 1305: 4 mutations, ALL killed, each by exactly one cell (M1 drop-the-alert, M2 collapse-the-kinds, M3 alert-unconditionally, M4 remove-the-fail-open)
baseline.summary: Outbound parent-set can never be emitted for DC: the epic-parent emit gate and DC's sub-task-child apply gate are disjoint
