# Batch-commit write primitive for bulk operations (import/migration scale)

## Context

Discovered from the export/import design brainstorm (`rule-swamp-pupil`, 2026-06-17). rebar's write path commits ONE git commit per event under a per-event lock acquire/release (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:82-146`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py:187-231`); no batch/bulk/transaction primitive exists. A bulk import of N tickets composes N×~3 events → thousands of commits + thousands of lock cycles (~3.3 min of lock overhead alone for ~2,000 events, before commit/push). `rule-swamp-pupil` already mitigates network amplification (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` + single final push), but the per-event commit/lock cost remains. This task is the real fix, deferred until real-world store sizes demand it.

## What / Implementation detail

Add `_store.batch_stage_and_commit(events)`: under ONE write lock, write/rename M event files, one `git add`, ONE commit. Crucially, **each event remains its own file** (unique name) — so cross-clone union-merge and SNAPSHOT compaction (which key off event UUIDs, not commit boundaries) are unaffected, and invariants I5 (single locked writer) and I2 (composed events) hold. Route the importer (and optionally the reconciler applier) through it in chunks (per-ticket or per-N). Atomicity: a single commit of M staged files is atomic at the git level; partial staging before commit is recoverable because import is idempotent (resume by `source_id`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_store.batch_stage_and_commit(events)`: one lock, M event files, one commit; each event its own file
- [ ] importer routes events through it in chunks; single-event path unchanged
- [ ] atomicity + crash-resume (idempotent) tests; union-merge + compaction regression tests
- [ ] benchmark: large-import wall-clock before vs after

Deferred optimization for `rule-swamp-pupil`; build if store sizes demand it.
- [ ] A bulk import of a large synthetic store completes in a fraction of the per-event wall-clock, with the same resulting logical state.
- [ ] Cross-clone convergence + compaction unaffected (regression tests).
- [ ] The single-event write path is unchanged.
baseline.summary: Batch-commit write primitive for bulk operations (import/migration scale)

content.text: ## What
The test repo-isolation guard `_no_repo_root_leaks` (`tests/conftest.py:157-181`)
only diffs the **top-level** entries of `REPO_ROOT` (`set(os.listdir(_REPO_ROOT))`
before vs after each test). It is therefore **blind to a test leaking state INTO a
pre-existing top-level directory** — most importantly `.rebar/` (this checkout
dogfoods rebar, so `.rebar/` always exists locally). A test that writes
`.rebar/run_snapshots/<sha>` adds no *new* top-level entry, so the guard passes
locally — while a fresh CI checkout (no `.rebar/`) sees the SAME write *create*
`.rebar` and flags it. This is a false-green/false-red split between local and CI.
## Why
This is the exact gap that hid the `test_sweep_removes_readonly_snapshot_tree` leak
(fixed in `fc792e4f`): the test snapshotted into `cwd = REPO_ROOT`'s `.rebar/`, which
was invisible to the top-level guard locally but failed CI's clean checkout. The
guard's job is to catch tests that escape their sandbox; right now it catches only
the subset that create a *new top-level* entry, giving false confidence locally.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Ensure `REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` exists (it does in any checkout that has run rebar).
2. Add a test that writes a file under `REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` (e.g. `(_REPO_ROOT /
".rebar" / "leaked.txt").write_text("x")`) without using `tmp_path`.
3. Run it **locally**: the `_no_repo_root_leaks` guard does NOT fail it (the new file
is inside the pre-existing `.rebar/`, so the top-level `os.listdir` diff is empty).
4. Run it on a **fresh checkout** (no `.rebar/`): the write creates `.rebar/` → the
top-level diff flags `['.rebar']` → the test fails.
**Expected:** a test that writes anywhere under `REPO_ROOT` it didn't create is flagged
**locally**, regardless of whether the containing dir pre-existed.
**Actual:** leaks into a pre-existing top-level dir (`.rebar/`, etc.) pass locally and
only surface (if at all) on a clean CI checkout.
## Proposed improvement
Extend the guard to detect new entries created **inside** the volatile pre-existing
dirs, not just at the top level — while staying cheap and not flagging dirs with
legitimate per-test churn:
- Snapshot a deeper path set for the known cache/state dirs that tests must NOT touch
in `REPO_ROOT` — at minimum `.rebar/` (one level: `{f".rebar/{e}" for e in
os.listdir(REPO_ROOT/'.rebar')}`), diffed before/after alongside the top-level set.
Optionally generalize to a bounded recursive walk that **excludes** the dirs with
legitimate churn (`.git/`, `.tickets-tracker/`, `.venv/`, caches) so it stays fast.
- Keep the existing best-effort cleanup of leaked paths, extended to the deeper set.
- (Belt-and-suspenders, optional) add a CI/local parity note or a `make` target that
runs a representative slice in a throwaway checkout, so the local↔CI environment gap
(pre-existing `.rebar`, installed extras, filesystem) is exercised before push.
The underlying test bug is already fixed; this ticket hardens the *guard* so the next
such leak fails locally instead of only in CI.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_no_repo_root_leaks` flags a test that creates a new entry under a pre-existing
`REPO_ROOT/.rebar/` (verified by a self-test that deliberately leaks into `.rebar/`
and asserts the guard fails it) — even when `.rebar/` pre-exists.
- [ ] The guard still passes the full existing suite (no false positives from dirs with
legitimate per-test churn — `.git/`, `.tickets-tracker/`, etc. remain excluded).
- [ ] The check stays inexpensive (no full-repo recursive walk of large dirs; scoped to
the known state dirs or a bounded/excluded walk).
- [ ] Leaked deeper paths are cleaned up (best-effort) as the top-level ones already are.
</content>

baseline.summary: test isolation guard _no_repo_root_leaks misses leaks into pre-existing top-level dirs (e.g. .rebar/)

content.text: ## Why
The `rebar.*` library facade returns plain `dict`/`list` shapes with no named,
documented return contract, so published-library consumers cannot tell which keys
are guaranteed or get type-checker support. The review flagged this as the main
library-API gap. rebar's public contract is *already* the canonical JSON Schemas
in `src/rebar/schemas/` (loaded via `rebar.schemas.load`/`names`/`OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`),
and it already has a derived-artifact + CI drift-gate pattern (the prompt-index
gate: regenerate-in-place then `git diff --exit-code`) to keep derived artifacts
in sync. Pydantic is deliberately NOT a core dependency (core is
`pyyaml`/`jsonschema`/`referencing`), so runtime models are off the table.
## What
Give the schema-backed subset of the `rebar.*` facade a typed return contract
**additively and statically**, via schema-derived `TypedDict`s generated from the
canonical JSON Schemas. **Zero runtime change** — returns stay plain dicts;
existing callers are untouched.
### Design decisions (resolving plan-review findings)
- **`additionalProperties: true` (BLOCKING G6).** Every public output schema is
*open* ("unknown properties allowed so the event-sourced shape can evolve").
TypedDict cannot express arbitrary extra keys, so we generate **closed
TypedDicts that name the documented/guaranteed contract**: schema-`required`
keys are normal fields; non-required keys are wrapped in `typing.NotRequired[…]`
(PEP 655, available in stdlib `typing` on our `requires-python = ">=3.11"`),
with `total=True`. This preserves the "required fields are present" guarantee
(unlike the blanket `total=False` used by the hand-authored
`_snapshot_schema.py` precedent) while marking optional keys. The runtime dicts
remain open; that openness is documented in the generated module docstring and
each class docstring — reading undocumented extra keys is outside the typed
contract by design.
- **Generator: a small custom in-repo generator, not an off-the-shelf tool
(T1/T2/T3/E2).** We write `src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py` (a `python -m
rebar.schemas.gen_types` entry-point, mirroring `regenerate_prompt_index`)
rather than adopting `datamodel-code-generator`, because (a) rebar avoids adding
dependencies, and (b) our schemas use cross-file `$ref` into
`common.schema.json#/$defs/*`, `["string","null"]` unions, and draft-2020-12 —
constructs off-the-shelf generators support only partially. A focused generator
handling exactly the constructs present (object `properties`/`required`,
`["T","null"]`→`T | None`, arrays, `$ref` to `common.schema.json#/$defs/*`
resolved to shared generated TypedDicts, enum `$ref`→`Literal[…]`) is simpler
and dependency-free. It resolves the `from` reserved-word key (transition_result)
via the functional `TypedDict("TransitionResult", {…})` form. Output is written
deterministically (stable key order + trailing newline) so the diff-gate is
stable.
- **Enum vocabulary only from formal `enum`/enum-`$ref` (T6/T8).** Where a value
vocabulary lives only in a schema `description` string (e.g. `workflow_run`
`status`), the generator emits `str`, not `Literal` — Literal comes only from a
formal `enum` constraint or a `$ref` to an enum def (`ticket_status`,
`ticket_type`, `priority`). This limitation is documented; we do not over-promise
Literal unions.
- **Scope = the schema-backed facade subset, enumerated (advisory 1/14).** We
generate + annotate for the public functions whose return shape has a canonical
entry in `rebar.schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`: `transition`/`reopen`
(`transition_result`), `claim` (`claim_result`), `create_ticket` dict form
(`create_result`), `clarity_check` (`clarity_result`), `check_ac`/`quality_check`
(`gate_result`), `validate` (`validate_report`), `get_file_impact`
(`file_impact`), `get_verify_commands` (`verify_commands`), `grounding_info`,
`sign_manifest` (`sign_result`), `verify_signature` (`verify_signature_result`),
`show_ticket`/`list_tickets`/`search`/`ready`/`recent_session_logs`
(`ticket_state`), `get_workflow_status`/`get_workflow_result` (`workflow_run`),
`deps` (`deps_graph`), `next_batch` (`next_batch`), `summary` (`summary`),
`list_epics` (`list_epics`), `bridge_fsck` (`bridge_fsck`). **Explicitly OUT of
the generated set** (no canonical output schema — annotated `dict[str, Any]`,
unchanged, and listed as out-of-scope): `append_session_log`,
`start_session_log`, `attach_commits`, `export_tickets`, `import_tickets`,
`reconcile`, and `run_workflow` (its `_result_dict` shape differs from the
`workflow_run` schema). `fsck` returns captured `str` (unchanged).
- **`create_ticket` polymorphism (advisory 2).** `create_ticket` returns `str`
(bare id) by default and a dict when `return_alias=True`. We add `@overload`s
keyed on the `return_alias` literal (`Literal[False] -> str`,
`Literal[True] -> CreateResult`) so existing `tid = rebar.create_ticket(...)`
callers keep `str` and no spurious mypy error is introduced.
- **Type-checker gate = mypy only (advisory 9).** The gated checker is `make
typecheck` (mypy over `src/rebar`); pyright is not a CI gate here, so AC claims
mypy only (the generated TypedDicts are pyright-compatible, but only mypy is
enforced).
- **Exceptions: promote exactly `RebarError` + `ConcurrencyError` (advisory
13/15).** These two (already in `rebar.__all__`, defined in `rebar/_errors.py`)
are the stable public exception surface; `SigningError` stays internal (wrapped
into `RebarError`). No others promoted. Documented in `docs/reuse-surface.md`
(or the README library section) with their `.returncode`/`.stderr` contract.
- **ADR + docs (advisory 8/16).** Add a short ADR under `docs/adr/` capturing the
static-only, schema-derived, custom-generator, no-Pydantic decision and its
trade-offs; add a README/usage note pointing consumers at `from rebar.types
import …` and the exception surface.
## Scope
Schema-derived TypedDicts (`src/rebar/types.py`, generated) + the generator
(`src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py`) + a CI drift-gate (in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`, mirroring the prompt-index gate) + facade return
annotations in `src/rebar/__init__.py` + exception docs + an ADR. Static-typing
only: NO Pydantic/dataclass runtime models, NO new core runtime dependency, NO
change to any return value. Pairs with the API-stability matrix story (830d, the
Python-facade row).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/types.py` holds `TypedDict`s generated from the canonical JSON
Schemas for the enumerated schema-backed facade subset (What/Scope above);
required keys are normal fields, non-required keys are `NotRequired[…]`, and the
file carries an "AUTO-GENERATED — run `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`" banner.
- [ ] `src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py` regenerates `src/rebar/types.py`
deterministically from `src/rebar/schemas/*.schema.json`, resolving cross-file
`$ref` into `common.schema.json#/$defs/*` and `["T","null"]` unions; running it
twice is a no-op (stable output).
- [ ] The enumerated facade functions in `src/rebar/__init__.py` are annotated
with these TypedDicts (with `@overload`s for `create_ticket`'s polymorphic
return); out-of-scope functions are left as `dict[str, Any]`; no runtime return
value changes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` (mypy over `src/rebar`) and `make lint` stay green; no new
core runtime dependency is introduced.
- [ ] A CI drift-gate in `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `python -m
rebar.schemas.gen_types` then `git diff --exit-code -- src/rebar/types.py` and
fails on stale committed types, with the regeneration command in the error
message (mirroring the prompt-index gate).
- [ ] `RebarError` and `ConcurrencyError` are documented as the stable public
exception surface (with their `.returncode`/`.stderr` contract) in a committed
doc; an ADR under `docs/adr/` records the schema-derived-TypedDict decision.

baseline.summary: Typed public library models: schema-derived TypedDicts for the rebar.* facade, drift-gated

## Problem
Run in a backgrounded shell whose cwd is reset away from the repo, 'rebar review-plan' can complete the review but resolve repo/tracker root from the transient cwd, then fail to persist an attestation WITHOUT surfacing an error to the caller — a workflow that backgrounds gate runs appears to succeed while signing nothing.

## Investigation target
Trace review-plan repo/tracker-root resolution and the sign step's error handling for a silently-swallowed failure when cwd != repo root. Reproduce at runtime before fixing.

## Fix (report ask)
Fail loudly when signing cannot persist, and resolve repo/tracker root independently of the transient cwd (or require an explicit root and error if unresolved).

## Acceptance criteria
- A review-plan sign that cannot persist surfaces a non-zero exit / explicit error to the caller (never a silent no-op success).
- Root resolution does not silently depend on a cwd that differs from the ticket's repo.

## Verification
Runtime repro of the cwd-reset scenario + a regression test asserting the loud failure.
baseline.summary: review-plan from a cwd-reset/background shell can sign nothing with no error surfaced

## Why

The task-decomposition SOTA report (epic 6982, §5 of docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md;
prior art T1: CodePlan's layer-cake antipattern, claude-task-master's DAG ordering, Kiro's
"waves") identifies two recurring **decomposition-SHAPE smells** in CONTAINER plans (a parent
split into children) that the existing container criteria G3 (child-coverage) and G4
(child-consistency) do NOT target:

- **layer-cake split** — children partitioned by ARCHITECTURAL LAYER (a "DB/schema" child, a
  "service/API" child, a "frontend/UI" child) instead of vertical, independently-shippable
  slices. Each child is un-demoable alone and the integration risk is deferred to the end.
  G3 (does the union cover the parent's ACs?) and G4 (7 cross-child interaction modes) both pass
  a layer-cake — coverage is complete and the layers are individually consistent; the DEFECT is
  the partition axis itself.
- **consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge** — a child NAMES/CONSUMES an artifact a SIBLING
  produces (its output file, schema, event, symbol), yet there is NO ordering dependency
  (depends_on/blocks) between them, so a parallel-agent scheduler can start the consumer before
  the producer exists. G4's "dependency gap"/"ordering violation" modes are broad and
  benign-filtered; this is the specific, high-signal producer→consumer-without-edge shape.

Both are SHAPE properties of the (parent, children) decomposition — not coverage, not code
grounding. This story ships one focused advisory container criterion for exactly that surface.

## What

Add one new **advisory, AGENT-tier, CONTAINER** plan-review criterion, id `decomp-shape`
(facet `container`, like G3/G4 — NOT codebase-grounding), that audits the (parent, children,
sibling-roster) decomposition for the two smells above. It runs on the EXISTING container
fan-out — no new pass, no new engine construct:

- **Mechanism seam (cited).** Container criteria are pulled out of the normal agent path and run
  via the dedicated per-child loop: `CONTAINER_CRITERIA = ("G3", "G4")` at
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:43` (partitioned at pass1.py:373-374), dispatched by
  `passes.pass1_container(...)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:357` — which builds the
  combined rubric from the `criteria` list (`rubric = "\n\n".join(_criterion_block(c) ...)`,
  passes.py:387), validates model self-reported attribution against `valid_ids`
  (passes.py:381, 428), and hands the finder parent + whole children + the complete sibling
  roster. Adding `decomp-shape` to `CONTAINER_CRITERIA` fans it out through that same seam with
  per-criterion + per-child attribution; nothing else changes.
- **Registration seam.** A packaged built-in LLM criterion must be added to
  `registry.CANONICAL_LLM` and `registry.AGENT_TIER` (like G3/G4; NOT `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` — its
  facet is `container`, not codebase-grounding), be given a routing entry in
  `criteria_routing.json` (`exec:AGENT`, `facet:container`, `applies_at.scope:["container"]`,
  `default_posture:"advisory"`, `block_threshold:0.95`), a rubric prompt at
  `reviewers/plan_review_decomp_shape.md` (front-matter `title`→guide name, body→scenario), and a
  regenerated `## decomp-shape` guide section — else `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` flags
  ORPHAN and CI fails (the bit that hit R2/b080), and `validate_criteria_guide()` flags the
  missing section.
- **Two criterion-local checklist sub-answers** (gated-then-detected): `has_container_decomposition`
  (GATE — parent has >=2 children forming a decomposition; `no` -> not-applicable -> PASS) and
  `decomposition_shape_sound` (`no` when a layer-cake partition OR a
  consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge is present — the finding).
- **Bounded sanity harness.** Container criteria are NOT runnable over the inline-text eval path
  today (`eval_solver._run_criterion_case` raises for `cid in CONTAINER_CRITERIA`,
  eval_solver.py:105). This story extends that arm to run a container criterion via
  `pass1_container` when the fixture carries a `children:` list — a small, contained enhancement
  that makes `decomp-shape` (and G3/G4) calibratable through `rebar criteria eval`, keeping the
  sanity run bounded to one live container call per fixture.

It ships **advisory posture (never blocks)** — its permanent posture per this epic's operator
direction. Promotion to blocking is a **future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change**,
DOUBLE-gated: (1) the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder (`criterion_effectiveness.py`)
must show it earns its blocks (high `detection_proxy`, low `blocking_fp_proxy`, sufficient
sample) AND (2) E6's judge order-stability must improve above floor — E6's order-shuffle
reliability FAILED (fleiss_kappa=0.55 < 0.6 floor, raw=0.7 < 0.8; e6_summary.json), which is a
declared R3 PREREQUISITE FAILURE (e6_judge_reliability.py:672): an order-sensitive judge makes a
BLOCKING container verdict untrustworthy, so blocking-promotion is deferred until order-stability
clears floor. Advisory shipping is unaffected — a non-blocking coaching nudge is safe under
judge instability.

## Scope

IN: the criterion + its routing/registry/rubric/guide, the eval_solver container-arm extension,
the bounded sanity fixtures + committed result, deterministic unit tests, and the promotion-gate
documentation note. OUT: any blocking promotion (future dogfood-gated), the E2/E3 mutant corpus
(permanently rejected on cost; sanity uses hand-authored fixtures), dogfood-accumulation waits.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `.../criteria_routing.json`, `.../pass1.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_decomp_shape.md`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`,
`docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`,
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml`,
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/decomp_shape_sanity.json`,
`tests/unit/test_decomp_shape_criterion.py`, `tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py`,
`docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `decomp-shape` is REGISTERED as an advisory, AGENT-tier CONTAINER criterion and is
  non-orphan. Proof: `python -c "import json; from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r;
  from rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1 import CONTAINER_CRITERIA; assert 'decomp-shape' in
  r.CANONICAL_LLM and 'decomp-shape' in r.AGENT_TIER and 'decomp-shape' not in r.CODEBASE_GROUNDED;
  assert r.validate_packaged_routing()==[]; assert 'decomp-shape' in CONTAINER_CRITERIA;
  e=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'))['decomp-shape']; assert
  e['exec']=='AGENT' and e['facet']=='container' and e['default_posture']=='advisory';
  print('OK')"` prints OK, and `rebar explain decomp-shape` exits 0 with a `## decomp-shape`
  section (`validate_criteria_guide()==[]`).
- [ ] Deterministic (no-LLM) unit tests for the non-LLM logic pass — registration invariants,
  routing/finding shape (advisory, container facet, scope), prompt-contract front-matter +
  sub-answer keys, the eval_solver container-arm (a fake runner threads through `pass1_container`),
  the eval-fixture shape, and zero-wiring auto-inclusion into the effectiveness recorder. Proof:
  `pytest tests/unit/test_decomp_shape_criterion.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] Bounded sanity check committed: hand-authored fixtures — one known layer-cake container
  plan + one known consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge plan (must-fire), plus vertical-slice
  and well-ordered containers (must-not-fire) — the criterion FIRES on both positives and is
  CLEAN on the negatives. Proof: `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/decomp_shape_sanity.json`
  preserves the raw per-case `rebar criteria eval decomp-shape --output json` output and records
  recall over the positives (target 1.0) and false-accept over the negatives; any negative fire
  is ADVISORY (never blocks), recorded as a promotion-gate FP signal. <=8 live single-criterion
  container runs total; NO E2/E3 corpus, NO batch eval.
- [ ] The criterion auto-flows into the standing recorder. Proof: a unit assertion feeds one
  synthetic firing row through `criterion_effectiveness.firings_from_review` /
  `compute_effectiveness` and asserts `decomp-shape` is auto-included with ZERO per-criterion
  wiring (the id appears in the `--report` metrics map).
- [ ] The advisory->blocking promotion gate is documented, citing d8a5's protocol in
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder + advisory->blocking
  promotion gate", and NOTING that E6's order-sensitivity (fleiss_kappa=0.55 < floor) defers
  blocking-promotion until order-stability clears floor (a second gate on top of dogfood
  effectiveness). Proof: the section names `decomp-shape` and the E6 order-stability prerequisite.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The change is landed on main: `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` and
  submitted (Gerrit), attested in-session.
baseline.summary: R3: decomposition-shape container criterion (advisory-only; blocking-promotion dogfood+E6-gated)

## Summary
The four LLM sidecar retention prunes bypass rebar's canonical locked event-write
path. Each `prune()` runs raw `git rm` + a whole-index `git commit` (no pathspec)
via `subprocess.run`, WITHOUT acquiring `write_lock`, WITHOUT rebase-guard, and
WITHOUT the shared index-lock retry/self-heal. This races normal ticket writes in
the shared tracker worktree.

Affected sites (near-identical copy-paste):
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` `prune`
- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py` `prune`

Contrast the canonical writer `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:stage_and_commit`,
which holds `write_lock`, checks rebase state, does a path-limited add, retries
index-lock failures, and cleans staged residue. event_append even warns (line
~263) that a whole-index commit "could sweep unrelated staged residue in under
THIS write's message" — the prunes reintroduce exactly that, outside the lock.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run an LLM gate (plan-review / completion-verify / code-review) whose sidecar
   emit triggers `prune()` on a ticket with > RETAIN_PER_TICKET sidecar events.
2. Concurrently run a normal ticket write (claim/transition/comment) on the same
   tracker so its `git add` (holding write_lock) overlaps the prune's lock-free
   `git commit`.

Expected: retention prune is serialized with every other store write; it commits
only its own deletions and never observes/writes another writer's staged state.

Actual: the prune's whole-index `git commit` can commit a concurrent writer's
staged event under a `prune:` message, causing the original writer's commit to
report a false failure (its `_unstage`+`_silent_unlink` then removes an
already-committed event from the worktree, diverging worktree from HEAD). Under
index.lock contention the prune instead fails outright (best-effort swallowed),
making retention unreliable in the multi-agent workload.

## Fix (Option B — narrow lock-respecting delete helper)
Add ONE `delete_events(tracker, relpaths, commit_msg)` primitive in
`event_append` that acquires `write_lock`, checks the rebase guard, `git rm`s the
given paths, commits PATHSPEC-SCOPED (`git commit -- <paths>`, not whole-index),
and routes git through the shared index-lock retry. Route all four prunes through
it. Keep the helper NARROW (delete-events-under-lock, not a general locked-git
facade) and preserve each caller's best-effort try/except so a failed prune never
fails the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single `delete_events`-style helper exists in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`
      that acquires `write_lock`, checks the rebase guard, and routes git through the
      shared index-lock retry.
- [ ] The helper's `git commit` is pathspec-scoped to the deleted paths (cannot
      sweep unrelated staged residue), and it cleans up on failure.
- [ ] All four sidecar `prune()`s (`plan_review/sidecar.py`, `code_review/sidecar.py`,
      `completion_sidecar.py`, `overlap/digest_sidecar.py`) call the helper instead of
      raw `subprocess.run(["git", ... "rm"/"commit"])`.
- [ ] Each caller retains its best-effort exception-swallowing posture (a failed
      prune never fails the gate).
- [ ] A unit/interface test covers the helper: it deletes only the named events,
      commits under the lock, and does not sweep an unrelated staged file in the index.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass; the change lands via Gerrit
      with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Sidecar retention prunes bypass the canonical locked write path (unlocked git rm+commit races store writes)

content.text: `rebar review-plan` reports `signature` present (the JSON `signature` field is non-null, and
batch tooling reads `signed=True`) even when the **verdict is BLOCK**. The documented contract
is that it "signs a plan-review attestation on a **non-blocking PASS**" — so a BLOCK verdict
should NOT carry a passing signed attestation. Either the signing-on-BLOCK is a bug, or the
`signature` field means something other than "passing attestation"; either way it is misleading,
because the signature is meant to be the trustworthy proof-of-PASS that downstream gates (the
claim gate) and CI rely on. A consumer that checks "is there a signature?" to decide
claimability would be misled by a signed BLOCK.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Author a ticket whose plan trips a blocking criterion (or use any ticket the four-pass gate
BLOCKs).
2. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` (default source = attested, signing on).
3. Inspect the result JSON: `verdict` and `signature`.
## Expected
- On `verdict == BLOCK`, no passing attestation is signed — `signature` is null/absent (or the
field is unambiguously labeled as a non-passing attestation), so "has signature" reliably
means "passed".
## Actual
- Observed repeatedly this session: tickets with `verdict=BLOCK` returned `signature` populated
(`signed=True`). Concretely, Round-2/3/4 runs on the S4/S6/S7 d251 children showed e.g.
`s6: BLOCK block=6 ... signed=True` and `s4: BLOCK block=2 ... signed=True` — a signature on a
BLOCK.
## Notes
- Inferred from the JSON `signature` field, not the signing internals — possible the field is
populated-but-not-a-passing-attestation; that distinction is exactly what's unclear and should
be made explicit. Surfaced while dogfooding the plan-review gate on epic d251 (alto-fruit-punch).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id>` on a BLOCK verdict does NOT emit a passing signed attestation
(either `signature` is null/absent on BLOCK, or the field/type is explicitly distinct from
a passing attestation and documented as such).
- [ ] `verify_signature` / the claim gate cannot be satisfied by an attestation produced on a
BLOCK verdict (a BLOCKed plan is never claimable on the strength of its signature).
- [ ] The behavior is documented (docs/plan-review-gate.md): exactly when a signature is emitted
and what its presence guarantees.
- [ ] A regression test asserts: BLOCK verdict -> no passing signature; PASS verdict -> signature present.

baseline.summary: plan-review: signed attestation emitted on BLOCK verdict (signature should mean PASS)

content.text: ## Why
The per-child plan-review flagged (T7, on nearly every child) that the new author-facing conventions have
no documentation artifact. Handle it ONCE here rather than per-child, so the conventions are discoverable.
## What
Author the workflow-authoring-v2 docs + ADRs covering: the prompt FRONT-MATTER format + closed key set;
the `execution_mode` divergence (an ADR — why fixed-on-prompt vs DSPy/BAML/pydantic-ai swappable strategy);
the step CONTRACT conventions (`inputs`/`outputs` ↔ `input_schema`/`output_schema` ↔ named registry schema);
the `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` OVERRIDE mechanism + write-back location detection; the derived-index LOCKFILE +
CI drift gate; and the 3-state VALIDATION semantics (OK/UNKNOWN/ERROR + abstain rules + runtime-against-consumer).
## Scope
In: docs/ + ADR(s) + CLAUDE.md pointers for the above. Out: the implementations themselves (their own stories).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A docs page documents the prompt front-matter format + closed key set + the override mechanism.
- [ ] An ADR records the `execution_mode`-fixed-on-prompt decision and the rejected swappable-strategy alternative.
- [ ] The contract conventions (prompt `inputs`/`outputs` vs op `input_schema`/`output_schema`, both → registry names) are documented.
- [ ] The derived-index lockfile + CI drift gate, and the 3-state validation semantics, are documented.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md / the agent guide points to the above so authors can find them.

# The attested `<700` headroom target no longer matches its baseline

## What happened

Rebasing the LLM-provider-seam stack onto current `origin/main` turned `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap` RED:

```
AssertionError: runner.py is 713 LOC; the split must bring it under 700 so
adding a line is not a build break
```

**This is not a regression in the split.** Measured on the rebased stack:

| | LOC |
|---|---|
| `runner.py` on `origin/main` (no split) | **798** |
| `runner.py` on the stack (2682's split applied) | **713** |
| 2682's attested target | **< 700** |

The split still removes 85 lines. What changed is the BASELINE: when 2682 was authored, main's `runner.py` was ~698 and the split produced 655. Main has since grown it by ~100 lines (server-side web search for bug ff64, usage-log provider stamping, and others), so replaying the same split now lands at 713.

## Why it cannot simply be forced under 700

Two candidate seams exist, and BOTH are pinned by the test suite as deliberate monkeypatch seams — moving either would require ~15 test edits across 9 files, which is precisely what 2682 was careful to avoid (its criterion was ZERO test edits):

- `_import_pydantic_ai` — `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_import_pydantic_ai", ...)` in `test_llm_temperature.py`, `test_llm_timeouts.py`, `test_llm_provider_factory.py`, `test_agent_build_invariants.py`, `test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` (x2), `test_bedrock_provider.py`, `test_web_tool_gating.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`.
- `_pai_check_config` — imported directly from `rebar.llm.runner` in `test_openai_compatible_provider.py` (x3).
- `_check_tool_capability` / `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` — 7 references in `test_agent_build_invariants.py`, including `runner_mod._TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED.clear()` as a MODULE ATTRIBUTE. Moving it saves only ~17 lines and would need a re-export shim to land at ~698 — a 2-line margin achieved mechanically, which the module-size policy explicitly forbids ("never mechanically to hit a number").

## The decision this needs

The test's STATED intent — "runner.py must stop sitting ON the 800 gate, not merely pass it" — is arguably satisfied at 713, which has 87 lines of headroom against the hard cap. But 700 is an ATTESTED acceptance criterion of CLOSED story 2682, so changing it is not a unilateral call.

Options, none of which should be taken silently:

1. **Do the seam work properly** — extract the preflight/import cluster (`_import_pydantic_ai` + `_pai_check_config`, ~40 LOC) into its own module and update the ~15 monkeypatch sites to target the new module. Real headroom (~676), but a genuine refactor with suite-wide reach.
2. **Re-derive the target from the current baseline** and record why, acknowledging that 2682's number was calibrated against a main that no longer exists. This changes a closed story's attested criterion and should be explicit, not incidental.
3. **Push back on main's growth of `runner.py`** — 798 LOC with a 800 cap means main itself is now one line from a build break, which is the deeper problem this surfaced.

Option 3 is worth noting independently: **`runner.py` on `origin/main` is at 798/800.** Whatever is decided here, main has two lines of headroom in its single busiest module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a decision is recorded on this ticket naming which option was taken and why
- [ ] `test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap` passes on a stack rebased onto current `origin/main`, without a re-export shim introduced solely to satisfy the count
- [ ] if the target is changed, the new number is justified against the CURRENT `origin/main` baseline and the change is cross-referenced from closed story 2682
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes on the rebased stack, evidenced by the pytest summary in a comment
baseline.summary: 2682's runner.py <700 target is unreachable after main grew runner.py to 798

content.text: ## Summary

The mirror-guard workflow fails on every evaluation: permissions declares 'administration: read', which is NOT a valid GITHUB_TOKEN workflow-permission scope, so the workflow fails schema validation and no jobs run (0-job 'startup failure'). Even if valid, its ruleset-drift check needs a GitHub token with administration:read (a fine-grained PAT), which org policy won't grant the default token.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Push to main (or trigger mirror-guard).
2. Observe: run created with 0 jobs, conclusion=failure, 'log not found'.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: mirror-guard runs and verifies Gerrit->GitHub replication using the default token.
- Actual: workflow fails validation (invalid permission key) and never runs.
## Fix

Scope the Actions workflow to the REPLICATION check only (rebar.mirror_guard --replication), which needs no admin token (fetch_github_main_sha treats the token as optional; Gerrit read is anonymous). Drop the ruleset-drift check from this workflow and remove the invalid administration:read permission, so it runs on the default GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: read) with no PAT.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] mirror-guard.yml permissions contains no invalid keys (drops administration:read; keeps contents: read).
- [ ] The workflow runs 'rebar.mirror_guard --replication' (no ruleset check), needing no fine-grained PAT.
- [ ] mirror-guard is green on main (replication in sync) without any new secret.

baseline.summary: mirror-guard CI red: invalid administration:read permission + PAT-only ruleset check

# PR posture on the GitHub mirror: welcome-bot redirect + shepherded-patch intake (with pre-flight experiments)

## Why

PRs opened against the mirror can never merge (today a repository ruleset rejects merges; PRs would sit open and unanswered — the posture universally condemned across peers: Gerrit's own mirror with rotting PRs, pre-archive AOSP). Peers split: Chromium/Qt/torvalds flipped GitHub's native Feb-2026 `has_pull_requests: false` setting (zero-cost but silent); LibreOffice/Wikimedia/OpenDev bot-close with a warm redirect. For a project that wants to convert drive-bys into repeat contributors, research recommends keeping PRs ENABLED as an intake channel: a bot answers instantly and the maintainer converts worthwhile patches to Gerrit (Wikimedia's "ask someone to convert" path).

## What

Decision (record as ADR `docs/adr/0037-oss-contribution-intake-posture.md`, covering: PR posture chosen + rejected alternatives incl. native disable and GerritBot-style auto-import; revisit trigger = PR volume exceeding solo-shepherd capacity): keep PRs ENABLED + auto-answer bot.

- Add `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` using dessant/repo-lockdown **SHA-pinned with a trailing version comment** (repo convention per gerrit-verify.yaml: "All third-party actions are SHA-pinned"; resolve the current v5.x release SHA at execution, e.g. `dessant/repo-lockdown@<sha> # v5.0.2`). Trigger: `pull_request_target: types: [opened, reopened]` (`reopened` closes Wikimedia's reopen loophole, T374157). Explicit least-privilege block: `permissions: { pull-requests: write }` (nothing else — `pull_request_target` runs with an elevated token on fork PRs; issues are real intake here, so the workflow must NOT touch issues: no `issues:` events, no issue inputs). `close-pr: true`, `lock-pr: false` (LibreOffice pattern — thread stays open). **Exempt `dependabot[bot]`** (job-level `if: github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'`): the release-hygiene story configures Dependabot whose PRs are advisory notifications that a maintainer converts to Gerrit changes — the bot must not close them. Verify the v5 input key names against the action's manifest (action.yml) at execution; a renamed input fails silently.
- Comment message per the convergent five-part skeleton: thank by name; "read-only mirror, PRs can't merge here — this close is automatic, nothing is wrong with your change"; deep-link Gerrit (GitHub OAuth sign-in) + `docs/your-first-change.md` (exists before this lands — this story depends_on the onboarding story); shepherded-patch escape hatch; warm tone.
- Publish the shepherded-patch policy in CONTRIBUTING.md (new section; Qt's voice — allowed, explicitly slower, best-effort): contributor runs `git commit -s` (their own DCO sign-off — required; see the DCO section) then attaches `git format-patch -1` output to a GitHub issue (plain diff acceptable with name/email to credit); maintainer applies with `git am` (author = contributor, committer = shepherd), adds their own `Signed-off-by` and the `rebar-ticket:` trailer via amend (message-only; authorship untouched), pushes `refs/for/main`, drives review; `Co-authored-by:` when substantially rewritten. If E2 (below) finds Forge Author NOT grantable, the policy text instead promises `Co-authored-by:` credit — the section is written after E2 resolves.
- Update the GitHub repo description: "Read-only mirror — code review at https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com".

Pre-flight experiments (complete BEFORE the workflow lands; record each outcome as a ticket comment AND fold consequences into the affected artifact):
- [E1] Scratch-repo test of `has_pull_requests: false` fork-side UX — documents the rejected alternative in the ADR.
- [E2] Admin read of Gerrit ACLs (JoeOakhartNava identity) on the live server + `infra/gerrit/project.config`: is Forge Author granted to Registered Users on the rebar project? If not, add the grant via the declarative config path or downgrade the authorship promise (go/no-go feeds the policy text above).
- [E3] Audit ALL `.github/workflows/*` for `pull_request`/`pull_request_target` event dependencies — known set today: test.yml, optionality.yml, eval.yml, eval-plan-review-container.yml (enumerate at execution with `grep -l "pull_request" .github/workflows/*`); confirm none is broken by bot-closed fork PRs (they run on PR events but fork PRs being closed quickly may cancel runs — acceptable; record). Any real breakage found is fixed in this story or ticketed via discovered_from.
- [E4] Confirm the `rebar-ticket:` trailer policy for shepherded patches (default: shepherd creates/uses a ticket and amends the trailer in) and cross-check it against the onboarding tutorial's outsider-ticket flow.

Note: maintainer-opened test PRs are NOT exempted from the bot — a closed test PR is precisely the verification (AC1); no exemption logic.

## Scope

IN: lockdown workflow + message text, CONTRIBUTING.md shepherded-patch section, repo description, ADR 0037, experiments E1–E4.
OUT: GerritBot-style automatic PR→Gerrit import — non-goal recorded in ADR 0037: only Go operates one; the gerrit github-pullrequest plugin is dormant; even at Go's scale bridged PRs merge at ~34% vs ~78% native (golang discussion #61182). Also OUT: issue lockdown (Issues are real intake), changes to the merge-blocking ruleset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test PR from a non-collaborator fork receives the comment and is closed (not locked) — prove: the test PR's timeline shows the bot comment + closed state; a REOPENED test PR is re-closed (covers the `reopened` type).
- [ ] Message content check — prove by grep of the workflow file: contains "read-only mirror", "nothing is wrong with your change", a link to `docs/your-first-change.md`, a link to https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com, and the patch-fallback offer; contains none of "rejected", "not accepted", "closed as invalid".
- [ ] Workflow hardening — prove: `lockdown.yml` has a `permissions:` block granting only `pull-requests: write`; the action ref matches `@[0-9a-f]{40} # v` (SHA-pinned); input keys verified against the pinned action.yml.
- [ ] Dependabot exemption present — prove: `grep -q "dependabot" .github/workflows/lockdown.yml`; a Dependabot-authored PR (or a simulated actor test) is NOT closed by the bot.
- [ ] E1–E4 outcomes recorded as ticket comments; E2's go/no-go reflected in the CONTRIBUTING policy text; E3 breakage (if any) fixed or ticketed.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md shepherded-patch section present with all four required elements — prove, each individually against the section: `grep -q "format-patch" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "Signed-off-by" CONTRIBUTING.md` (both-trailer DCO handling); `grep -qi "author" CONTRIBUTING.md` reflecting the E2 outcome (either `git am` authorship preservation or `Co-authored-by` fallback — whichever E2 selected); `grep -q "rebar-ticket" CONTRIBUTING.md` (trailer policy); `grep -qi "best-effort" CONTRIBUTING.md` (caveat).
- [ ] ADR 0037 committed covering posture decision, native-disable rejection (E1 evidence), GerritBot non-goal, revisit trigger. Repo description updated — prove: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar --jq .description` contains "read-only" or "mirror".
baseline.summary: PR posture on the GitHub mirror: welcome-bot redirect + shepherded-patch intake (pre-flight experiments)

# The `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain is a documented subsystem with no live producer

## Status

DISCOVERED while fixing d103-c3f8-2fbc-4c97 / 727f-b351-59ba-4b3b. Not a regression those fixes introduced - it predates them and neither changes it. Filed so it is not lost.

## What is unreachable

`differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` is the only producer of `(inbound, probe)` mutations. It iterates `local_state` looking for entries carrying a bound `jira_key` field. Its sole production caller, `run_differs`, passes `prev_snapshot` - a FETCHED Jira snapshot, whose entries never carry `jira_key` (`fetcher.py`, and the contract shape in `_snapshot_schema.py`). The loop therefore never emits, and everything downstream of it is dead in production:

* `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` in `run_differs.py`
* `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeResult`, `ProbeBranch`, the router)
* `backend.probe_remote` / the `SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability

Confirmed empirically: fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair, `compute_mutations` emits only `jira_new`, `unbound_local` and `field_drift`. The only fixture in the repo that supplies a `jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`.

## Why it matters

This is the mechanism ADR 0028 para 2 relies on to tell "deleted" from "aged out of the fetch window" - deletion is proven only by a bounded direct GET returning 404. With no live producer, that discrimination is never exercised in production. Ticket b9b8 already reworked the live DC cell `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` for exactly this reason: it "asserted an observable no production path emits".

## What is NOT the fix

Do NOT re-enable the arm by making `run_differs` pass a `jira_key`-bearing local_state without also removing `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` in the SAME change. That suppression exists only because the caller passes the legacy `(prev, curr)` pair; migrating the caller makes the suppressed emissions correct again, and leaving both in place would silently drop real work.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Establish whether the absence-probe path is still wanted, or whether ADR 0028 para 2's
   direct-GET confirmation has since been implemented elsewhere and this chain is genuinely dead
   code to delete. Record the answer with a citation either way.
2. If wanted: a RED-first test proving `(inbound, probe)` is produced from the real
   production call path, not from a hand-built `local_state` fixture.
3. If dead: remove the chain, and remove the fixture-only test with it.
baseline.summary: Inbound-probe dispatch chain has no live producer

## Summary
`AcliClient.set_relationship(from, to)` emitted `jira link create --out from --in to`, but
ACLI's `--out`/`--in` are INVERTED vs the naive reading: `--out X --in Y --type Blocks`
creates "Y blocks X" (the `--in` issue is the blocker). So every reconciler-written link was
reversed. This stayed hidden because (a) rebar reads links direction-agnostically, (b) most
links were adopted from Jira rather than written by us, and (c) the tests never asserted
absolute direction.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create Jira issues X, Y. Call `set_relationship(X, Y, "Blocks")`.
2. Observe Jira shows "Y blocks X" (expected "X blocks Y"). (Live-validated 2026-07-16.)
3. Consequence via the applier: `A blocks B` -> Jira "B blocks A" (reversed); `A depends_on B`
   -> after c8ed added the applier swap, Jira "A blocks B" (reversed).

**Expected:** `A blocks B` -> "A blocks B"; `A depends_on B` -> "B blocks A".
**Actual:** both reversed (blocks reversed since outbound link sync shipped; depends_on
reversed by c8ed, which added the correct applier swap but on top of the inverted primitive).

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_graph.py::set_relationship` maps `from_key`->`--out`,
`to_key`->`--in`, which is backwards. Fix: emit `--out to_key --in from_key` so the link reads
"from blocks to". With c8ed's applier swap + the relation map, BOTH relations then write the
correct direction. Live-validated end-to-end via the differ+applier (blocks->"A blocks B",
depends_on->"B blocks A").

## Why the tests missed it
The live E2E round-trip (`tests/external/test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`) checked only that a
Blocks link existed in EITHER direction and that outbound<->inbound AGREE (a consistency check
that holds even when reversed), and never covered `depends_on`. Unit tests stub
`set_relationship`, so they cannot see the flag order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `set_relationship(from, to)` emits `--out to --in from`; a unit test pins the flag order.
- [ ] A live E2E test asserts ABSOLUTE direction for BOTH `blocks` and `depends_on`.
- [ ] Live-validated: blocks->"A blocks B", depends_on->"B blocks A" through rebar's code paths.
- [ ] [operator-attested] the ~96 reversed `blocks` links (and any c8ed-reversed depends_on) are repaired in live Jira.
baseline.summary: Outbound Jira links written REVERSED: set_relationship passes ACLI --out/--in backwards

## Context

After landing code-review-only criterion `project.review-phase-boundaries`, fresh plan review for story 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d fails before LLM execution. `plan_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)` calls the shared overlay with `gate_key="plan_review"`; the global `activate` list contains the code-review-only criterion, and overlay validation raises `CriteriaError: activated criterion ... has no plan_review routing entry`. The deterministic layer catches and skips project criteria, leaving `review-plan` unsigned INDETERMINATE.

## Plan

- Define cross-gate activation semantics in the shared project-criteria overlay: an activated criterion routed exclusively to another known gate is ignored by the current gate, not treated as malformed.
- Preserve strict failure for an activated id absent from every supported gate and for malformed routing in the selected gate.
- Add regression coverage using a repository overlay with one plan-review criterion and one code-review-only criterion, exercising both registries and the real plan-review precheck path.
- Document the gate-scoped activation behavior in the project-criteria architecture documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `activate` containing a valid code-review-only project criterion, `effective_criteria(repo_root, gate_key="plan_review")` returns plan-review criteria without raising and does not include the code-review-only id.
- [ ] With `activate` containing a valid plan-review-only project criterion, `effective_criteria(repo_root, gate_key="code_review")` returns code-review criteria without raising and does not include the plan-review-only id.
- [ ] An activated criterion absent from every supported gate still raises `CriteriaError`; malformed routing for the selected gate still raises.
- [ ] A regression test proves `review-plan` can execute its deterministic project-criteria resolution on the landed mixed-gate overlay instead of becoming unsigned INDETERMINATE.
- [ ] The gate-scoped activation rule is documented and canonical lint, typecheck, and test gates pass.
- [ ] The change lands on `main` through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments.
baseline.summary: Scope project-criterion activation to its review gate

content.text: `rebar review-plan` (the four-pass plan-review gate) is **non-deterministic and mis-calibrated**
as a gate: the same ticket re-reviewed gives different PASS/BLOCK verdicts and a different finding
set each run, the advisory batch is a near-constant ~10 regardless of plan quality, and almost
every finding is tagged `severity=critical` while remaining non-blocking. The Pass-1 finder
recall is stochastic, so "PASS" is not reproducible for the same input — which undermines a gate
whose contract is "must PASS before you can claim." (The finding CONTENT is consistently high
quality; this bug is about stability/calibration, not correctness.)
## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` on a well-formed ticket; note `verdict` + the
`blocking`/`advisory` arrays.
2. Without changing the ticket (or after a change that only ADDS detail/hardening), re-run.
3. Compare verdicts, finding counts, and which findings appear.
## Expected
- The verdict is reproducible for the same input (same ticket -> same PASS/BLOCK), and finding
count/severity reflect actual plan quality (a strong plan yields fewer/lower-severity findings
than a weak one).
## Actual (observed across ~29 runs this session on epic d251 + its children)
- **Non-reproducible verdicts.** S4/S6/S7 went `PASS -> BLOCK` after remediations that only added
hardening, and each re-run surfaced DIFFERENT blocking findings; S6's block count was
non-monotonic across rounds: `0 -> 3 -> 1 -> 6`. The same plan can pass for one run and block
for the next.
- **Fixed-size advisory batch.** Almost every ticket, every round, returned ~10 advisories
(`P/10a` near-uniformly; one ticket once at 8) — reads as a target/cap, not a measurement, so
advisory volume does not discriminate plan quality.
- **Severity inflation.** Most advisories are `severity=critical` (e.g. epic 10/10, S3 10/10)
yet non-blocking (`reason: default-advisory`) — "critical but doesn't block" is incoherent and
makes severity useless for triage.
- **Weak cross-criterion dedup.** A single root issue surfaced as multiple findings under
different criteria (e.g. S1's `use_lockfile`/TF>=1.10 issue appeared 4x under T1/T3/E2/G6),
inflating the count.
## Impact
"Re-run until it passes" (the gate protocol) assumes convergence that doesn't hold: remediating
the cited block can surface new, unrelated blocks, so a good-faith author may not reach a stable
PASS. Two agents reviewing the same ticket can get different claimability.
## Notes
- Likely root: Pass-3 (decide) is deterministic GIVEN the findings, but Pass-1 (finder) recall is
stochastic, so determinism is only conditional on a non-deterministic input. The fixed-~10 and
all-critical patterns suggest finder prompt/threshold calibration. Surfaced dogfooding d251.
- Separate, more clear-cut bug filed for signed-on-BLOCK.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Re-running `review-plan` on an unchanged ticket yields a stable verdict (PASS stays PASS;
no spurious PASS<->BLOCK flips) — e.g. via seeding/caching the finder, lowered temperature,
or a deterministic finder pass, measured over N repeat runs.
- [ ] Advisory count reflects actual issues found (not a near-constant ~10); document/justify any
cap and surface when findings were truncated.
- [ ] Severity is calibrated so `critical` implies blocking (or the block thresholds are aligned
so a wall of "critical" advisories cannot coexist with a clean PASS); severity becomes
usable for triage.
- [ ] Cross-criterion dedup collapses one root issue reported under multiple criteria into a
single finding.
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the determinism guarantees and the calibration of
severity vs. blocking thresholds.

baseline.summary: plan-review: non-deterministic verdict + mis-calibrated findings (fixed ~10 advisories, all 'critical', PASS<->BLOCK flips)

content.text: ## Why
The README is a thorough ~31KB reference (Why / Requirements / Install / CLI /
Python / MCP / Config / Tests) but has **no short tutorial** — Install jumps
straight into reference-style command docs. A newcomer has no golden path from
zero to a working first flow. Meanwhile `rebar --help` already emits a full,
authoritative command index backed by 40 per-command help files, so a separate
"cheat sheet" would only duplicate it and invite drift.
## What
Add a single, single-sourced `## Quickstart` section near the top of `README.md`:
- Install (one canonical line) -> `rebar init` -> create a first ticket ->
`ready` / `claim` -> close, showing **expected output** at each step.
- A minimal "point an agent at it" example (the MCP one-liner) so the agent path
is visible.
- Uses only the ~6 core commands inline and **defers the full command list to
`rebar --help`** rather than re-listing commands.
## Scope
`README.md` only (one new section + a link to it from the top). Explicitly NOT a
separate cheat-sheet doc and NOT a duplicate command index — `rebar --help` +
the `_cli/help/*.txt` files remain the authoritative command reference. Keep it
short (a screenful).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `README.md` has a `## Quickstart` section near the top with an
install -> first-ticket -> first-agent-flow walkthrough and expected output.
- [ ] It shows only the core commands inline and points to `rebar --help` for the
full list (no re-listed command index, no separate cheat-sheet file).
- [ ] The commands shown are copy-pasteable and correct against the current CLI.
- [ ] A top-of-README link points to the Quickstart.

## Why
`rebar review-code` (the local/coding-agent path) reviews a diff but persists NOTHING — only the
Gerrit voter emits a `code_review` artifact. Without a local artifact there is no per-session memory
for the region-gated novelty floor (blameless-grindable-noctule) to converge against. This story
makes local `review-code` emit a session-keyed `code_review` artifact, reusing the payload/reader
shape from revenued-thickset-dassie.

## What
- **Resolve the local memory key.** Use the centralized
  `rebar._commands.session_id.resolve_session_id()` (precedence: `REBAR_SESSION_ID` →
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` → `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` → `SESSION_ID`; validated shared-across-subagents,
  unique-per-parallel-session).
  - **Fallback (approach A):** when it returns `None` (bare/headless, no SessionStart shim), mint a
    per-invocation `uuid4` (do NOT persist a shared file). This guarantees ISOLATION — no
    local→Gerrit bleed and no cross-session contamination — at the cost of making local convergence
    intentionally INERT for a bare invocation (each run gets a fresh key, so the reader finds no
    prior). Genuine per-session convergence arrives wherever a session lifecycle exists (native
    harness var or a SessionStart shim exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID`).
- **Set `session_id` on the verdict.** The local path sets `verdict["session_id"] = session_key` so
  the payload (revenued-thickset-dassie's `build_payload`, which reads `verdict.get("session_id")`)
  carries it top-level. The typed memory key for the reader is `session:<session_key>`.
- **Wire the local gate entry to emit + persist.** Thread the resolved key down the local call chain
  `_review_code → shim.review_code → gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` and emit a session-keyed
  artifact:
  - **Signature changes (in scope):** add `target_ticket: str | None = None` and
    `session_id: str | None = None` parameters to `code_review/shim.py::review_code(...)`, AND add a
    `session_id: str | None = None` field to the `CodeReviewRequest` dataclass in `gate_dispatch.py`
    (alongside the existing `target_ticket`). The shim forwards both onto
    `CodeReviewRequest(target_ticket=…, session_id=…, …)`. Without these the resolved key cannot
    reach the emit path.
  - **Create-or-reuse idempotency (session key = stable convergence point).** Before emitting, a
    local-emit helper resolves ONE artifact ticket per session key, mirroring
    `voter.emit_code_review_artifact` (voter.py ~199–220) EXACTLY:
    `title = f"code-review: session:{session_key}"`; scan
    `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review", repo_root=repo_root)` for a title match and REUSE
    that artifact id; else `rebar.create_ticket("code_review", title, …)`. Then `sidecar.emit(verdict,
    target_ticket=artifact_id, …)`. So two sequential local reviews under one session id append
    sidecar events to the SAME artifact (AC4) instead of duplicating.
  - **`relates_to` link (best-effort).** Link the artifact `relates_to` the work ticket resolved
    from the head commit's `rebar-ticket:` trailer (via the existing `extract_ticket_refs` +
    `resolve_ticket_id`, exactly as `voter.emit_code_review_artifact` does) for searchability. No new
    `--ticket` CLI flag is added (out of scope). A trailerless/unresolved/ticketless review STILL
    persists (memory is keyed by session, not by ticket) — the only degradation is no cross-run
    match when the key differs; a missing/unresolved link is logged, never fails the review.
  - **Best-effort throughout:** artifact create/reuse/emit/link failures are logged and swallowed —
    they must NEVER fail the review (mirrors the voter + sidecar posture).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` (`_review_code`: resolve key, thread it down),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` (`review_code`: add `target_ticket`/`session_id` params),
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (local-emit helper: create-or-reuse the session artifact
  + set `verdict["session_id"]`).
- Depends on the payload shape + reader (revenued-thickset-dassie) — specifically `build_payload`
  reading `verdict.get("session_id")`, which lands with c639; this story is reviewed/implemented
  AFTER c639 is committed on the stack, so that dependency exists in the tree.
- OUT of scope: the Gerrit voter path (already emits; inherits the payload extension); the
  region_gated_floor consumer (blameless-grindable-noctule).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Local `rebar review-code` emits a `code_review` artifact keyed `session:<id>` carrying the
      reviewed-file `deps` map and a top-level `session_id`.
- [ ] The session key = `resolve_session_id()`; when `None`, a per-invocation `uuid4` is used (no
      shared-file persistence), making bare-invocation local convergence intentionally inert.
- [ ] `shim.review_code` gains `target_ticket` + `session_id` parameters and `CodeReviewRequest`
      gains a `session_id` field, both forwarded, so the local path can supply the artifact anchor
      and session key.
- [ ] Create-or-reuse idempotency: two sequential local reviews under ONE session id append to the
      SAME artifact (title `code-review: session:{id}`), not duplicate tickets.
- [ ] The artifact `relates_to`-links the ticket resolved from the head commit's `rebar-ticket:`
      trailer when one resolves; a trailerless/unresolved review still persists (keyed by session)
      and never fails the review (no new `--ticket` flag).
- [ ] Tests: a local review with a set `REBAR_SESSION_ID` emits/reuses one session-keyed artifact
      across two runs; a bare review (no session var) mints a uuid key and still persists; artifact
      failures never fail the review.
baseline.summary: Persist a code_review artifact for local rebar review-code + session keying (uuid fallback)

baseline.description:
## What
Read-only derivations over the existing gate sidecars for gate-economics + env-diagnosis metrics: an LLM cost proxy (`llm_calls`, latency) from the plan/code-review sidecars, cost-per-accepted-change, first-pass verification, and env-diagnosis intervals (`gate_error_v1` ERROR → next PASS). All read-only; nothing is written.

## Data-access ground truth (the plan is built on this)
- **Only `REVIEW_RESULT` (`plan_review_result_v2`) carries a `metrics` block** — `{det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, claim_path}` (`plan_review/sidecar.py:496-497`). **`COMPLETION_VERDICT` carries NO metrics block** (verified in `completion_sidecar.py:182-219`; neither the pass nor fail branch has `llm_calls`). So all `llm_calls`/latency derivations read `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics` ONLY — the completion sidecar is used for the pass/fail *outcome*, never for cost.
- **"Accepted change"** is defined precisely: a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` record (`SCHEMA_PASS`, `completion_sidecar.py:29`) on a ticket — i.e. the completion (close) gate PASSED. This is NOT a plan-review PASS (`plan_review_result_v2` with `verdict=="PASS"`), which only clears the *claim* gate and does not mean the ticket closed. The reader distinguishes the two by schema.
- Sidecars are reducer-ignored. **This reader uses a single RAW ordered scan** of each ticket's `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` and `*-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json` event files (resolve dir via `tracker_dir`+`resolve_ticket_dir_name`; sort by the ns-epoch filename prefix / `event_sort_key`; `json.load`; read `event["data"]` + `event["timestamp"]`). The schema-guarded helpers are NOT used for counting, because `latest_pass_record` returns only the single most-recent PASS (`completion_sidecar.py:137`) and `all_review_results` hard-filters to `plan_review_result_v1/v2` — neither can COUNT completion passes nor surface `gate_error_v1`. A record's kind is read off `data.schema` / `data.verdict`: `plan_review_result_v2` (verdict PASS/BLOCK/FAIL) with a `metrics` block; `completion_verifier_pass_v1` / `_fail_v1`; and `gate_error_v1` (verdict ERROR, carries a `gate` field). The raw scan sees ALL of them on the stream in order.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py` — new: reader over the sidecars, registered into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py`.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_sidecar_metrics.py` — new.

## Metric definitions
- **llm_call_proxy / latency** — sum `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics.llm_calls` (and latency fields) over the range. `source="sidecar"`.
- **cost_per_accepted_change** — summed `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics.llm_calls` divided by the count of `completion_verifier_pass_v1` records (accepted closes) in range; returns `None` (→ `Unavailable`) when there are zero accepted closes (no division by zero).
- **first_pass_verification** — fraction of tickets whose FIRST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record is a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` (passed on the first verification attempt).
- **first_pass_verification** — fraction of tickets whose FIRST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record (oldest-first by filename order) is a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` (passed on the first close-verification attempt). Reads the raw COMPLETION_VERDICT files per ticket in chronological order and inspects the earliest one's schema.
- **env_diagnosis_interval** — pair each `gate_error_v1` ERROR record with the next PASS record **for the SAME gate** on that ticket's stream. Because plan-review and code-review both write to `REVIEW_RESULT`, pairing matches on the ERROR record's `gate` field (`plan_review`/`code_review`/`completion`) against the next same-gate PASS (a `plan_review_result_v2`/code-review PASS for those gates, a `completion_verifier_pass_v1` for completion) — NOT merely the next PASS on the stream. The interval = PASS `timestamp` − ERROR `timestamp`; an ERROR with no following same-gate PASS is an open (unclosed) diagnosis interval.

## Approach
Pure read-side derivations over sidecars that already persist per-run metrics, verdicts, and (via ticket 8bc5) the additive ERROR outcome. `confidence="high"`; `is_authoritative("sidecar")` is True. Nothing is written.

## Tests
- Unit (real sidecar fixtures written to a temp store): cost-per-accepted-change over 3 REVIEW_RESULT runs (llm_calls 2+3+4=9) with 1 `completion_verifier_pass_v1` returns 9; with 0 accepted returns `None`. An ERROR record paired with a later PASS on the same ticket yields an interval equal to the fixture timestamp delta; an ERROR with no PASS yields an open interval.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_sidecar_metrics.py` passes: a `gate_error_v1` ERROR row paired with a later PASS on the same ticket yields a diagnosis-interval duration equal to the fixture timestamp delta (`assert dur == expected`).
- [ ] cost_per_accepted_change over a fixture of 3 REVIEW_RESULT runs summing `llm_calls==9` with exactly 1 `completion_verifier_pass_v1` returns 9; a fixture with 0 accepted closes returns `None` (→ `Unavailable`, no ZeroDivisionError) — both asserted.
- [ ] the cost derivations read `llm_calls` ONLY from `REVIEW_RESULT.metrics` (never from COMPLETION_VERDICT, which has none) — asserted by a fixture whose COMPLETION_VERDICT records carry no metrics yet cost is still computed from the REVIEW_RESULT runs.
- [ ] `first_pass_verification` over a fixture of 3 tickets where 2 have their EARLIEST `COMPLETION_VERDICT` record as `completion_verifier_pass_v1` and 1 has an earliest `completion_verifier_fail_v1` returns 2/3 — asserted numerically (proves the oldest-first COMPLETION_VERDICT scan).
- [ ] `env_diagnosis_interval` pairs a `gate_error_v1` ERROR (gate=`plan_review`) with the next `plan_review` PASS and NOT with an interleaved `completion` PASS on the same REVIEW_RESULT/COMPLETION_VERDICT streams — asserted (proves the gate-field match).
- [ ] the metrics register into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` with `source="sidecar"` (authoritative) — asserted.
baseline.summary: Gate-sidecar reader (gate-economics + env-diagnosis metrics)

## Why
The auto-lander is a long-running service; it must deploy like the review-bot, log to its OWN service logs (never `session_log`), and — critically — fail LOUDLY and recover crash-safely, since a single-instance bot that wedges silently would reintroduce the manual toil this epic removes.

## What
Containerize the loop service (S2) and wire it into docker-compose (single instance) on the existing Gerrit box; provision its credential + Gerrit capability; make hangs/errors/stuck-states highly visible; and guarantee crash-safe restart. Decomposed into child tasks so each is loadable whole.

## Dependencies
Depends on **S2** (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`, 0ee8-08de-bf0f-45ec) — the core loop this story packages and deploys. Uses **S3**'s (`darksome-starry-sable`, 0525-6d71-8969-4512) outcome marker for drain/restart reconciliation.

## Design context (shared contracts the children implement)
- **Status model (prior art: Chromium CQ + Zuul/Tide):** per-change outcome is reported BACK onto the Gerrit change (comment + `Autosubmit` label state) which `land` reads via Gerrit; bot liveness + queue-status are served by a read-only HTTP status endpoint exposing **`heartbeat_age_s`** (the field `land`'s `lander_down` binds to).
- **Heartbeat contract (design-fixed):** a state-volume timestamp file, written once per the bot's 15 s poll; freshness ≤ 15 s; `lander_down` at age > 90 s.
- **Reliability posture:** single-writer (flock) + heartbeat + autoheal restart + loud error metric + stuck-state alarm + crash-safe recovery record. HA (external state store) is deferred to a future epic.
- **Stuck-state threshold (design-fixed):** the time-in-phase alarm fires when a `wipChain` sits in any non-`idle` phase for **> 45 min** (the 30-min CI-await bound + margin), configurable — published as the `autolander_time_in_phase_seconds` CloudWatch metric.
- **Autoheal socket:** the autoheal sidecar mounts the Docker socket **read-write** (it must issue `docker restart`); this socket-write privilege is the accepted, inherent cost of autoheal.

## Scope
Deploy + credentials + observability + liveness/recovery. NOT the core rebase/submit loop logic (S2); the heartbeat write, status endpoint, sentinel check, and drain are thin service-lifecycle hooks into `infra/autolander/loop.py` that this deploy story owns.

## Acceptance Criteria (story-level; children carry the implementation detail)
- [ ] **Package + single-instance** — child **S5a** (`08e1-5505-d898-4192`): Dockerfile + compose service + autoheal sidecar + flock guard + external state volume (+ `compose-up.sh SITE_SUBDIRS`).
- [ ] **Credentials + capability** — child **S5b** (`ea61-01c3-daea-4824`): SSM token (no IAM change), `AUTOLANDER_GERRIT_TOKEN`, and the bot's `Rebase` access right on the rebar project's `refs/heads/*` (submit already covered by Contributors membership).
- [ ] **Observability + status endpoint (LOUD failures)** — child **S5c** (`9a6f-065d-91c4-4e03`): `autolander_errors` (three feeders + alarm), the stuck-state time-in-phase alarm, the named `autolander_time_to_land_seconds` metric, and the read-only status endpoint.
- [ ] **Liveness + crash-safe recovery** — child **S5d** (`38be-a778-43f5-4a4e`): HEALTHCHECK + autoheal, heartbeat, emergency-stop sentinel, drain-on-SIGTERM with a concrete recovery record, and the crash-recovery/idempotency test.
- [ ] The service NEVER writes `session_log`; all failure modes (hang, error, stuck, `lander_down`) are visible via metric/alarm for troubleshooting.
baseline.summary: S5 Deploy (container + compose, single instance) + observability (service logs, not session_log)

content.text: ## Why
Nothing currently checks the DIFF against its ticket. plan-review checks the plan; completion-verifier
checks at close; a diff-time scope check is complementary and catches scope drift in the change itself.
## What
New scope-intent overlay, content-triggered when >=1 ticket resolves from the commit's rebar-ticket:
trailer. Grounded prerequisites from plan review:
- REGISTER `scope-intent` in the closed OVERLAY_IDS tuple in registry.py (unknown ids are dropped).
- assemble_diff (assemble.py) does NOT currently read the rebar-ticket: trailer; add trailer parsing via
extract_ticket_refs (supports multiple ids: multiple trailer lines AND whitespace-separated tokens) and
assemble the referenced tickets' scope/AC as this overlay's context.
- Ticket-blindness is NOT free: ticket_context is threaded into the shared reviewer_input, so keeping base
+ other overlays ticket-blind requires explicit plumbing (gate ticket context to the scope-intent
overlay only; do not leak it to the others). Verify with a test.
Checks the diff against the UNION of all referenced tickets so legitimate multi-ticket commits don't
produce false scope findings. Reuses plan-review's scope-intent criterion vocabulary. Advisory.
## Scope
reviewers/code-review-scope-intent.md, registry.py (OVERLAY_IDS + content trigger), assemble.py (trailer
read + ticket-context assembly), criteria_routing.json (SHARED — coordinate with C, F).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scope-intent` in OVERLAY_IDS; overlay fires only when a ticket resolves from the trailer.
- [ ] assemble_diff reads the trailer (all ids) and assembles union scope context.
- [ ] A test proves base + other overlays receive NO ticket context (ticket-blind).
- [ ] A multi-ticket commit naming all its tickets produces no false scope-drift finding (eval).
- [ ] Overlay is advisory.
## Data-flow: commit message -> scope-intent overlay (resolves plan-review G6)
The trailer lives in the COMMIT MESSAGE, which is not part of the diff text, so it must be plumbed
end-to-end (default "" everywhere → overlay simply does not fire when absent, per the AC):
- `assemble.py`: `assemble_diff_context(...)` gains `commit_message: str = ""`. It calls
`extract_ticket_refs(commit_message)`; for each resolved trailer ticket it loads that ticket's
scope/AC and assembles a UNION scope-context string, exposed as a SEPARATE context field consumed
ONLY by the scope-intent overlay (base + other overlays stay ticket-blind — assert this).
- `assemble_diff_input` schema: add optional `commit_message`.
- `gates/code-review.yaml`: thread `commit_message` into the `assemble_diff` step; the scope-intent
overlay's `ticket_context` includes the union scope-context.
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict(...)`: accept + forward `commit_message` (default "").
- Call sites (`shim.review_code`, `review_bot/voter.py`): pass the change's commit message when
available (Gerrit change commit body), default "" otherwise.
scope-intent is content-triggered (fires only when ≥1 trailer ticket resolves) and ADVISORY.
## Per-overlay context injection (resolves plan-review G6, batch-runner tension)
CodeReviewBatchRunner today injects one shared `_context` (the diff) into every overlay
(`batch_runner.py:58`). scope-intent needs a DIFFERENT ticket_context (the union ticket scope). Resolve
by extending the batch runner, not by polluting the shared context:
- `CodeReviewBatchRunner.__init__` gains `context_overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None` (prompt_id ->
ticket_context). In `run`, when an overlay's `prompt_id` is in `context_overrides`, inject that string
as its `ticket_context`; every other overlay keeps the shared diff `_context` (base + others stay
ticket-blind — assert it in a test).
- `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` builds `context_overrides={"code-review-scope-intent":
<union_scope_context>}` ONLY when the commit-message trailers resolve ≥1 ticket (else omit → overlay
inert), using the union-scope string assembled in assemble.py.
This is additive and default-None, so existing single-context behaviour is unchanged.

baseline.summary: Scope-intent overlay (diff vs union of trailer tickets)
