content.text: ## Why
Epic `850f` needs a place for a T2 semantic backend to plug in and be reported, without touching the
deterministic T1 lane or any consumer. Today `TIER_T2` exists in the closed tier vocabulary but is
never emitted, and member/dotted references abstain inline in `resolve.refute_absence`. This story
adds the opt-in, default-off seam and wiring; S3 adds the actual pyright backend behind it. Shipping
the seam separately keeps the seam change regression-safe and independently reviewable.
## What
- New module `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` (stdlib-only, import-clean) exposing:
- `T2_BACKENDS: tuple[str, ...] = ()` initially — the closed set of selectable backend names. (S3
adds `"pyright"`.) An unknown/empty selection fails open to disabled.
- `refute_semantic(reference, *, repo_root, config, timeout=None, cache=None) -> dict | None` —
returns a normalized `TIER_T2` evidence record (`refuted`/`abstain`) or `None` meaning "T2 declined
to run; keep the caller's T1 record". With no registered backend it returns `None` (default-off).
`cache` is a **caller-owned** optional mapping (mirrors T1's `index` param) for reusing one
backend invocation across many references in a single review — no module-global mutable state, so
no cross-thread concern.
- `available_backends() -> list[dict]` — `[{name, available, version}]` for each name in
`T2_BACKENDS`, each probed fail-open (empty while `T2_BACKENDS` is empty).
- Extend `GroundingConfig` + `load_config` in `resolve.py` with three `.rebar/grounding.toml`
`[grounding]` keys (all default-off / safe):
- `t2_enabled: bool = False`, `t2_backend: str | None = None`, `t2_timeout_seconds: float = 30.0`.
Invalid types/values fail open to the default (never a raise), consistent with the existing loader.
- Wire escalation in `oracle.refute_absence` (the single consumer entry): after the T1/deps lane
returns, if the record is an `abstain` on a `member`/dotted reference or a not-found bare
`symbol`/`import`, call `semantic.refute_semantic(...)`; a returned `refuted@T2` replaces the T1
abstain, otherwise the T1 record is returned unchanged. `resolve.refute_absence` is **not** modified
(T2 stays out of the deterministic T1 lane).
- Extend `oracle._backend_availability()` to append `*semantic.available_backends()` so
`grounding_info` reports T2 backends.
## Scope
In scope: `semantic.py`, the config keys, the `oracle` escalation + availability wiring, and unit
tests. Out of scope: the pyright backend itself and its extra/docs (S3). While `T2_BACKENDS` is empty
the seam is fully inert.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/grounding/semantic.py` exists exposing `refute_semantic`, `available_backends`, and
`T2_BACKENDS`.
- [ ] `semantic.py` is stdlib-only: `tests/unit/grounding/test_non_adoption.py` still passes
(the import-purity guarantee holds).
- [ ] `GroundingConfig`/`load_config` expose `t2_enabled` (bool, default False), `t2_backend`
(str|None, default None), and `t2_timeout_seconds` (float, default 30.0).
- [ ] Each new config key fails open to its default on malformed input (a test feeds a malformed
`.rebar/grounding.toml` and asserts the defaults, with no raise).
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` escalates member/dotted and not-found-symbol abstains to
`refute_semantic`.
- [ ] `oracle.refute_absence` returns `refute_semantic`'s `refuted@T2` when produced, otherwise the
unchanged T1 record.
- [ ] `resolve.refute_absence` is unmodified (verified by diff review — the T1 lane stays out of T2).
- [ ] `oracle._backend_availability()` includes the T2 backends reported by `available_backends()`.
- [ ] `grounding_info()` output validates against `grounding_info.schema.json` after the change.
- [ ] Default-off regression: a test in `tests/unit/grounding/` asserts that with `t2_enabled=False`
(empty `T2_BACKENDS`) `oracle.refute_absence` returns the pre-change evidence for a member/dotted
reference (still `abstain` at `TIER_T1`).
- [ ] A seam-dispatch test using an in-test fake backend (monkeypatched into `T2_BACKENDS` +
`refute_semantic`) shows a `refuted@T2` record replaces the T1 abstain.
- [ ] That `refuted@T2` record validates against `grounding.schema.json`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/grounding/` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.

baseline.summary: T2 grounding S2: pluggable semantic seam (refute_semantic + config + oracle escalation, default-off)

content.text: # WS6 — Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review
## Why
Epic `d251` (AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP) **shipped and merged** — including S4b's complete review-bot:
`src/rebar/review_bot/` (receiver `app.py`, `voter.py`, `gerrit_client.py`, `dedup.py`,
`reconcile.py`) plus the **verdict→label seam `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root,
ref) → {decision, message, findings}`**. That seam is currently implemented over the OLD
single-pass `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` + a blocking-severity heuristic — a deliberate "proven
pipe" placeholder. `adapter.py`'s own docstring says: *"b744-WS6 will REIMPLEMENT this same
signature over `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` — drop-in, with no caller change."*
WS6 is exactly that swap: make Gerrit's `LLM-Review` vote driven by **our new four-pass code
review** (the deterministic Pass-3 blocker), not the single-pass demo.
## Realignment (2026-06-30) — supersedes the earlier standalone-package plan
The pre-merge WS6 plan (a NEW `src/rebar/gerrit/` voter package + REST client + patchset handler)
is **retired as redundant**: d251 already ships all of that in `src/rebar/review_bot/`. WS6 must
NOT build a parallel package — it CONSUMES the shipped receiver and swaps only the decision engine
behind the existing seam. The live dogfood is split out to WS6-b (`0da5`); the GitHub cutover to
WS7.
## What
- **Rewrite `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision`** over
`gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` (the typed `PASS`/`BLOCK`/`INDETERMINATE` verdict):
- keep the signature + return shape (`{decision, message, findings}`, plus an additive
`coverage_gap` flag) so `voter.py` is unchanged;
- map the verdict fail-closed (below); the four-pass gate's own Pass-3 thresholds
(`criteria_routing.json`) decide PASS vs BLOCK, so the adapter no longer applies the
`blocking_severities` severity heuristic (it becomes vestigial for this path);
- review the receiver's cloned working tree by passing `repo_root` (the security detectors scan
the changed files there) + the fetched `diff_text`.
- **Add an `enabled: bool | None = None` override to `produce_code_review_verdict`** so the adapter
can pass `enabled=True` (force-enable): the code-review gate is OFF by default
(`verify.enable_code_review`), but voter activation is itself the authoritative gate, so the
per-repo flag would otherwise leave every change with the inert disabled verdict. (ADR 0015.)
- **Update `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`** adapter tests to drive the four-pass verdict (mock
`produce_code_review_verdict`) instead of `review_code`.
- **ADR 0015** records the seam reimplementation + the force-enable rationale + the fail-closed
vote mapping + the coverage-gap message distinction.
## Vote mapping (fail-closed; the gate's Pass-3 owns PASS/BLOCK)
`produce_code_review_verdict` emits three verdicts (PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE) plus an inert
disabled verdict. The adapter collapses them to the receiver's PASS/BLOCK (the voter then casts
`llm_review_max_value` / `llm_review_block_value` from `ReceiverConfig`):
| verdict / state | adapter decision | note |
| PASS + full coverage | PASS | advisory findings are surfaced in the message, non-blocking |
| BLOCK (blocking findings) | BLOCK | real finding (`coverage_gap=False`) |
| INDETERMINATE (LLM outage) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap |
| PASS but `coverage.enabled==false` (inert) | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`gate-disabled`) — defense-in-depth |
| fail-closed security-scanner abstain | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`scanner`) |
| ANY exception / bad shape | BLOCK | fail-closed coverage-gap (`review-error`) |
## Distinct coverage-gap message (infra vs code)
The vote comment (`ReviewInput.message`, posted by the receiver's `post_vote`) begins with a
machine-parseable tag so an INFRA `-1` is unmistakable from a real-finding `-1`:
`[LLM-Review: PASS]`, `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]`, and
`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (<gate-disabled|llm-unavailable|scanner|review-error>)]`. The
`coverage_gap` sub-reason is derived deterministically from `verdict.coverage`
(`enabled==false` → gate-disabled; `llm_unavailable` → llm-unavailable; a `security_detectors`
note with `reason=='fail-closed-abstain'` → scanner). A real secret MATCH
(`reason=='detector-finding'`) is a finding, NOT a coverage gap.
## Scope
- IN: the `adapter.py` reimplementation, the `produce_code_review_verdict` `enabled` override, the
updated `test_review_bot.py` adapter tests, ADR 0015.
- OUT: the receiver/voter/gerrit_client/reconciler (d251 shipped them — unchanged); the live
end-to-end dogfood (WS6-b, gated on the deployed env); the GitHub cutover (WS7).
## Dependencies
- CONSUMES d251's shipped `review_bot` package + the provisioned `LLM-Review` label / value
mapping (`ReceiverConfig`). depends_on WS4 (98ff, closed) for `produce_code_review_verdict`.
- No live env needed: the adapter is fully verifiable offline (mock the verdict; the receiver's
own tests already stub Gerrit).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `review_bot/adapter.py`'s `code_review_decision` is reimplemented over `produce_code_review_verdict` with `enabled=True`; the signature + `{decision, message, findings}` return shape are unchanged (the voter is not touched).

- [ ] Vote mapping is exhaustive + fail-closed over PASS / BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / inert-disabled / scanner-abstain / exception; a test asserts each → the correct decision, and that an inert-disabled verdict never yields PASS.

- [ ] `produce_code_review_verdict` gains an `enabled: bool | None = None` override (default None = read config); a test asserts `enabled=True` forces the gate to run even when `verify.enable_code_review=false`.

- [ ] The vote message distinguishes a coverage-gap `-1` (sub-reason gate-disabled / llm-unavailable / scanner / review-error) from a real-finding `-1`, via the documented first-line tag; a test asserts the PASS tag, the finding tag, and each coverage-gap sub-reason.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` adapter tests are updated to the four-pass verdict (mock `produce_code_review_verdict`); the full `pytest -k review_bot` suite passes; ruff + mypy clean.
- [ ] ADR 0015 records the seam reimplementation, the force-enable rationale, the fail-closed vote mapping, and the coverage-gap message vocabulary.

baseline.summary: WS6: Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review

# A — PreToolUse hook: re-surface Serena on every grep

## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` already says to prefer Serena's symbol tools over `grep`, and an agent with Serena configured still enumerated call sites by hand with `grep` for many turns (epic `061c` story S2). Launch-time guidance decays: by mid-task, one line of a long document has no salience. The fix is a reminder delivered **at the moment of the action**, executed by the harness rather than remembered by the agent.

## Approach

A `PreToolUse` hook on the `Bash` tool that emits a short reminder when the command invokes the grep family.

**The trigger must be as dumb as possible.** Match a grep-family invocation (`grep`, `rg`, `egrep`, `fgrep`) in the command string — nothing more. Deliberately do NOT try to classify whether the pattern "looks like a symbol", whether the target is under `src/`, or parse the command: a clever predicate is fragile, mis-fires, and a hook that mis-fires gets disabled, which is worse than a hook that occasionally reminds you of something you already knew. Accepting false positives is the design, because the cost of a false positive is three lines of text and the cost of a false negative is the behaviour this epic exists to fix.

**The message must be small and must not be wrong.** Two to three lines. It names the preferred path AND the one case where `grep` is genuinely correct, so an agent that reads it and continues with `grep` for a string-literal search has been *helped*, not overridden. Something of the shape:

```
Serena (LSP) is available: find_referencing_symbols / find_symbol resolve real references — prefer it for
"who calls/imports X". grep is still right for symbols named as STRINGS (monkeypatch.setattr, getattr) and
for current line numbers, which the LSP index can lag.
```

**Non-blocking, always.** The hook informs; it never denies the call.

## Scope

- `.claude/settings.json` — ADD a `hooks.PreToolUse` entry matching `Bash`. This file is **created and made
  trackable by story C** (`06ae-0d45-aff1-46f2`), which also adds the `.gitignore` negation without which
  nothing under `.claude/` can be committed at all (`.gitignore:38` ignores `.claude/`). This story therefore
  **depends on C** (`blocks` edge recorded) and must MERGE its `hooks` block into the existing tracked file
  rather than overwrite it — C's `env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` must survive.
- `scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py` — the hook body as a tracked, testable script rather than an inline
  shell one-liner buried in JSON, so the trigger and the message can be pinned by an automated test.
- `docs/` — one line pointing at the hook from the same doc home story C uses.

## Verified ground truth (probed 2026-07-29)

- `PreToolUse` surfaces text to the model via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`. **Plain non-JSON stdout is
  NOT shown to the model** (debug log only), so the hook must emit JSON — a bare `echo` reminder would be
  invisible and the story would silently under-deliver.
- The hook stays non-blocking by **omitting `permissionDecision` entirely** (normal permission flow applies).
  Emitting `"allow"` would also be non-blocking but would additionally SUPPRESS the permission prompt, changing
  this repo'''s security posture — out of scope, so do not do it. Exit code 2 blocks the call; the hook must never
  exit 2.
- Project settings resolve to the operator'''s MAIN checkout, shared across worktrees — so the hook cannot be
  observed firing from the authoring worktree session. Verification is by EXECUTING the hook script directly
  against the documented stdin envelope (which is exactly what CI can re-check), plus a post-land transcript.

## Testing

- The hook fires on a plain `grep -rn foo src/` and on `rg foo`.
- It does NOT block: the grep still runs and its output is unchanged.
- A command with no grep produces no reminder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash` emits the reminder for `grep`, `rg`, `egrep`, `fgrep`
- [ ] the trigger is a plain grep-family string match — no pattern classification, no path heuristics — and the
      hook config is small enough to read at a glance
- [ ] the message is <= 3 lines and names both `find_referencing_symbols` AND the string-literal/line-number
      grep exceptions, so it is never misleading
- [ ] the hook is non-blocking: a transcript shows the grep executing normally after the reminder
- [ ] an AUTOMATED TEST shows it firing on `grep -rn foo src/` and `rg foo`, and NOT firing on a non-grep
      command; the test executes the hook against the documented `PreToolUse` stdin envelope and asserts the
      emitted JSON carries `additionalContext` and NO `permissionDecision` (proving informative + non-blocking)
- [ ] the hook never exits non-zero and never emits `permissionDecision`, so it cannot deny a call or suppress a
      permission prompt even on malformed input (asserted for empty stdin / absent command / non-JSON stdin)
- [ ] C'''s `env.ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` setting is still present in `.claude/settings.json` after this change
baseline.summary: A — PreToolUse hook: re-surface Serena on every grep call

content.text: ## Why

The suite grew via characterize→port→parity during the migration and likely carries change-detector tests (tautological, assertion-light, or pinned-to-implementation rather than behavior) that resist refactoring without catching bugs.
## What
- Stand up mutation testing (e.g. mutmut or cosmic-ray) over src/rebar core modules; record baseline mutation score.
- Identify surviving mutants (untested behavior) AND change-detector tests (tests that pass under mutation / assert nothing meaningful / restate the implementation).
- Prune or rewrite change-detector tests to assert observable behavior; add tests to kill high-value surviving mutants.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Mutation testing wired (documented invocation) with a recorded baseline score
- [ ] Change-detector tests catalogued and pruned/rewritten to behavioral assertions
- [ ] High-value surviving mutants killed; mutation score improved and recorded
- [ ] Suite still green locally + CI

## Summary

The `langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)` job of the `external-integration`
workflow has been broken since the d6d1 cutover (2026-06-22) and tests behavior that no
longer exists. Two independent breakages:

1. **Readiness probe imports an uninstalled SDK.** `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml:128`
   runs `from langfuse import get_client; assert get_client().auth_check()`, but the `langfuse`
   Python SDK was dropped from `[agents]` in c282b2950. `pip install -e '.[dev]'` no longer
   installs it, so all 24 readiness iterations raise `ModuleNotFoundError` — hidden by
   `2>/dev/null`, masquerading as "Langfuse project did not initialize in time".

2. **Test asserts a removed trace_id round-trip.** `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py:100` asserts
   `result["trace_id"]` is truthy and fetches `GET /api/public/traces/{id}`. The runner now
   hardcodes `trace_id=None` (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:391); the SDK trace-id capture was deleted
   in 2e9bd4205 when tracing became write-only OTLP export (src/rebar/llm/tracing.py). Also the
   job never installs `[tracing]`, so `setup_tracing` no-ops and no spans are exported at all.

## Decision (user, 2026-07-09)

Rewrite the job to validate CURRENT behavior (write-only OTLP span export to Langfuse), not the
removed SDK trace_id round-trip.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the `external-integration` workflow (langfuse-trace job).
2. Observe "Wait for Langfuse to be ready" time out after 120s ("project did not initialize in time").

Expected: readiness passes; a review run's OTLP spans land in Langfuse and the test confirms it.
Actual: readiness fails on a hidden ModuleNotFoundError; the test would fail on the None trace_id anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Readiness probe no longer imports the langfuse SDK; uses a REST check (e.g. `curl -fsS -u pk:sk .../api/public/projects`) and does not mask stderr.
- [ ] The langfuse-trace job installs the `[tracing]` extra so OTLP export actually fires.
- [ ] `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py` asserts OTLP spans for a review run are ingested by Langfuse (fetched via REST), with no reliance on a runner-surfaced `trace_id`.
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: the rewritten test passes against the docker-compose.langfuse.yml stack with a real review call, and the external-integration GitHub Action's langfuse-trace job runs successfully.
baseline.summary: langfuse-trace job tests removed behavior + readiness probe imports uninstalled SDK

## Context

A documentation audit (final unified report, evaluated at commit `2272d68ca` =
`origin/main`) surfaced front-door defects and factual drift in rebar's docs. Every
finding was re-validated against `origin/main` before filing this epic; one audit
finding (that `docs/config.md` mis-describes the config-file format) was **REFUTED**
— the loader matches the doc exactly — and is deliberately excluded.

Our audiences are human clients, LLM clients, human contributors, and LLM
contributors. The two highest-leverage moves are (a) fixing the immediate defects
that break onboarding/trust, and (b) adding cheap **drift-proofing** so the same
class of staleness cannot silently return — the true lever on maintenance burden.

### Validated findings this epic remediates
- P0: README `session-log` syntax is invalid (missing subcommand); README quickstart
  is not actually one ticket end-to-end (hard-coded `reel-lot-tea`, separate Python
  ticket, MCP shows config only).
- P1: dependency count + `mcp` floor wrong in README and `docs/config.md` (truth: 3
  base deps, `mcp>=1.9`); `docs/output-schemas.md` points at a moved source path and
  describes a removed bash shell-out; stale bash-engine language in CI comments +
  `leaf.py`.
- P2: `docs/README.md` index is incomplete (4 unlinked living docs) and mixes living
  references with historical evidence.

### Reuse note (avoids duplicate work)
- `scripts/probe-rebar.sh` already implements the full install→…→close golden path;
  it just is not wired into CI.
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` + its CI drift gate is a proven **generator +
  drift-gate** pattern to template for new generated references.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets are closed (each with green CI / `Verified +1`).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass on the assembled stack. This
      aggregate integration check is owned at the EPIC level (not any single child):
      the executor runs it on the full assembled stack before landing, as the
      parent-level close gate.
- [ ] The refuted config-format finding is NOT acted on (no spurious change).
- [ ] Lower-value inventory work (Python-API / config-key) is captured as an `idea`,
      not shipped speculatively.
- [ ] The golden-path CI gate runs the **literal commands extracted from the README quickstart fenced block** (not merely an independent probe with its own syntax), so a wrong command *printed* in the README — e.g. the `session-log` missing its `append` verb — fails the build. This is the mechanism that makes command *text* rot (not just executability) a hard CI failure, and doubles as the end-to-end new-user onboarding validation (CI follows the README exactly as a cold reader would).
- [ ] Docs-index completeness/drift fails the build (docs-index CI gate `f088`): every
      living/normative `docs/*.md` is linked from the index, and the relative links
      the remediation touches (index entries + inbound links to docs relocated under
      `docs/archive/` by `9d81`) resolve. Scope is bounded to index completeness and
      the links this epic manages — it is the enforcement arm of the P2 finding, not a
      general site-wide linter.
- [ ] Generated CLI + MCP references drift-gate against their live registries.

### Drift-proofing mechanism — how command *text* rot fails the build (closes G6/F4)
The audit gap is that testing command *executability* (running `probe-rebar.sh`, which uses its own internally-correct syntax) does NOT catch a wrong command *printed in the README*. So the golden-path gate (ticket `contained-dendritic-angora`/0435) is scoped to **extract the fenced command block(s) from the README quickstart and execute those exact lines** in a throwaway repo. A stale/invalid README command then exits non-zero and fails CI. This is both the text-accuracy drift guard (G6) and the concrete end-to-end onboarding validation (F4): a new user copy-pasting the README is exactly what CI now does.

### Shared-file edit ordering (closes P5)
Several children edit `README.md` (session-log fix `a41f`, quickstart repair `b55f`, dep-count `319a`, catalog-trim `b5a4`). These are **serialized through the review stack in dependency order** — each change is built on the prior one (a41f → b55f → 319a → … → b5a4), so there is no concurrent same-file edit; `b5a4` additionally `depends_on` the generated-reference tickets (`e866`, `235a`) it links to. The stack order IS the observable ordering proxy: a later change rebases on the earlier landed change, never races it.

The SAME single-linear-stack serialization covers the other shared files: `.github/workflows/test.yml` (edited by `0435`, `e205`, `e866`, `235a`, `f088`) and `docs/README.md` (edited by `9d81`, `6755`) are each modified by exactly one change at a time in stack order — every change is built on the prior landed one, so there is never a concurrent same-file edit to reconcile. Execution is a single agent driving one relation-chain, so the dependency order and the stack order are the same total order.
- [ ] Every validated defect above is corrected against `origin/main`.
- [ ] New CI gates make quickstart-command rot and docs-index drift fail the build
- [ ] The docs index is complete and clearly separates living reference from historical
- [ ] Volatile command/tool surfaces move toward generated references so they cannot go
baseline.summary: Documentation remediation: fix front-door defects, drift-proof the docs, clarify taxonomy

## Context / Problem
usage-log rows (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py) record the four token fields but not model, provider, or timestamp, and the plan-review budget shedder prices work with hard-coded guesses (COST_SINGLE_TURN_USD=0.006, COST_AGENT_USD=0.12, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:107-109). No provider publishes a machine-readable price API; pydantic's genai-prices package bundles offline price data with cache read/write tiers, historical prices by timestamp, and a typed LookupError for unknown models. Operator approved it as an optional add-in with graceful fallback.

## Approach
(1) Extend usage_log.record to record(usage, *, op, model=None, provider=None) plus a UTC ISO timestamp written inside record(); update its single call site at runner.py:547 to pass model=ran_model and the provider inferred by the existing mapping at src/rebar/llm/config.py:321-327. (2) summarize reads plain JSONL dicts (not live usage objects), so pricing maps row fields explicitly: build genai_prices' usage input from the stored dict — input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens keyword-mapped one-to-one — and call calc_price with the row's model, provider, and parsed timestamp. No reliance on pydantic-ai objects at summarize time; the mapping is a pure dict-to-kwargs adapter function with its own unit test. (3) summarize keeps its existing grouping by op and adds cost: per-row cost from that row's own model/provider/timestamp (a multi-model op sums correctly row by row); the report prints per-op est. cost plus a per-model rollup table. (4) Pricing is attempted only when `import genai_prices` succeeds; each calc_price call is wrapped in `except Exception` (pricing must never break summarize): LookupError marks the row unpriced, any other exception logs at WARNING and marks the row unpriced; the summary reports "excludes N unpriced calls". When the package is absent, summarize prints token totals with the cost column reading "unavailable (install rebar[pricing])". (5) New optional extra `pricing = ["genai-prices"]` in pyproject.toml. Never a hard error, never a silently-wrong number; the column is labeled "est. cost". Alternative rejected: vendoring LiteLLM's ~2 MB price JSON — takes on key-normalization and schema-drift ownership that genai-prices maintains upstream.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py, src/rebar/llm/runner.py (record call site), pyproject.toml, tests/unit/test_usage_log.py (extend), docs/llm-framework.md (usage-log section).

## Testing
Unit: rows gain the three new fields via the updated record signature; the dict-to-kwargs adapter maps all four token fields and tolerates missing keys (defaults 0); summarize with a stubbed genai_prices prices known rows, marks unknown-model rows unpriced via LookupError, marks a malformed-row pricing crash unpriced via the broad handler with a WARNING log, and totals annotate the exclusion; summarize with the import failing prints the unavailable message and exits 0; old-format rows without the new fields still summarize.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New usage-log rows carry model, provider, and UTC timestamp, populated from the runner call site (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`).
- [ ] The dict-to-kwargs adapter converts a stored row into genai-prices usage input covering all four token fields, defaulting absent fields to 0 (checked: adapter unit test).
- [ ] With genai-prices importable, summarize prints per-op est. cost and a per-model rollup, marking unknown or crash rows unpriced without raising (checked: unit tests with a stubbed price module covering LookupError and a generic exception).
- [ ] Without genai-prices, summarize prints token totals and "unavailable (install rebar[pricing])" and exits 0 (checked: unit test with import blocked).
- [ ] Rows written by the previous format still summarize without error (checked: fixture test).
baseline.summary: Optional genai-prices cost accounting in usage-log summarize

## Context / Problem

The `criteria eval` CLI admits only plan-review ids: its preflight rejects anything not in `plan_review.registry.by_id(repo_root)` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:143-155`), so an activated project **code-review** criterion is refused as "unknown" before the gate-aware eval resolver is ever reached. Fifth of five seams (root cause on superseded bug 8a4b).

## Approach

Extend the preflight to admit code-review ids and to resolve the target gate deterministically:

- Look the id up in BOTH the plan-review effective registry and the code-review effective registry (`code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)`, `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:179-184`).
- Admit iff present in **exactly one** gate; dispatch to the gate-aware calibrate path that child 4 `[rebar:8153-e9b5-5706-49c8]` adds to `calibrate_criterion`.
- If the id is active in **both** gates, reject as **ambiguous** with a message telling the author which gates claim it; if in neither, keep the existing "unknown" error.
- Update the subparser help text to include the concrete project code-review example `project.foo` alongside the plan-review example.

**Rejected alternative.** Adding a `criteria eval --gate` flag — heavier UX for a rare case; the "active in exactly one gate ⇒ resolve there" rule covers the common path and only genuine cross-gate ambiguity needs operator input.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py` — dual-registry admission, one-gate resolution, ambiguity rejection, help text.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — append CLI cases to this shared test file, which was created by child 1 `[rebar:fc72-bf7e-7652-4228]`. This ticket depends on child 1 and child 4 `[rebar:8153-e9b5-5706-49c8]`; tests build a synthetic repo activating `project.foo` as a code-review criterion.

## Testing

- Happy path (CLI): `project.foo`, active in code-review only, is admitted and reaches the calibrate call with exit 0.
- Unknown edge: an id active in neither registry returns exit 1 and emits the existing "unknown" message.
- Ambiguity edge: `project.foo` active in both registries returns exit 1 and emits an "ambiguous" message naming `plan_review` and `code_review`.
- Help text: `criteria eval --help` contains the exact substring `project.foo` in the code-review example.

Tier: unit — invoke the command handler with a synthetic-repo `repo_root`, with calibration stubbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A one-gate project code-review id is admitted and dispatched to the code-review calibrate path; verified by `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k cli`.
- [ ] An unknown id is rejected with exit 1 and the existing distinct "unknown" message; verified by the same `-k cli` selector.
- [ ] An id active in both gates is rejected with exit 1 and an "ambiguous" message naming `plan_review` and `code_review`; verified by the same `-k cli` selector.
- [ ] `criteria eval --help` contains the exact code-review example substring `project.foo`; verified by the same `-k cli` selector.
baseline.summary: Admit one-gate project code-review ids in the criteria eval CLI

baseline.description:
## Context
The identity epic shipped the merge-gate as `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml`, which walks
the MERGED LOG (CLI `rebar verify-identity`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py`). Its
enforcement posture and grandfather boundary are read from **rebar.toml**
(`identity.require_authenticated`, `identity.enforce_since`) — the workflow step is a bare
`run: rebar verify-identity` with NO CI flags/vars. This story adds a **required-environment op-cert
verification lane** that mirrors that gate: same merged-log walk, config-driven posture/boundary,
reusing the shared verify-identity CI job rather than a parallel walker.

**Op-cert storage shape (delivered by keystone e4df).** An op-cert is stored on a ticket as an
`attestations[<kind>]` record carrying a DSSE `envelope` (`signing.sign_opcert_manifest` writes it;
`opcert.opcert_from_record` reads it back to `(envelope, {material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit})`).
This story READS that shape over the merged log; ee0b's trusted server and 8f1d's migration PRODUCE
it. A fixture synthesizes one via `sign_opcert_manifest`. **Which kind:** the lane targets the
**`completion-verifier`** attestation kind — it reads `attestations["completion-verifier"]` (the
close-gate op-cert; the `attestations` map is kind-keyed, so the key is fixed by the lane, not
guessed) and treats a ticket with no `completion-verifier` op-cert as "absent" for the enforcement
check below.

**Config-driven posture/boundary (mirror `identity.*`).** Add `verify.opcert_enforce_since`
(grandfather boundary, mirroring `identity.enforce_since`); `verify.require_environment` (which
environment must sign; already shipped in 42d1) is the posture. The workflow step is a bare
`run: rebar verify-opcert` — NO CI variable — reading both from rebar.toml, exactly as
`verify-identity` reads `identity.*`. The lane stays advisory until `verify.opcert_enforce_since`
covers op-cert-bearing commits and `verify.require_environment` is set, so adding it does not flip
the repo to blocking before producers (ee0b/8f1d) exist.

**Grandfathering the ABSENCE case (the missing-op-cert enforcement anchor).** `verify-identity`'s
`_is_enforced(commit_sha, since_ref)` tests the commit that introduced *an event*. A ticket that
carries NO op-cert has no such event/commit. Resolution: the enforcement anchor for a ticket
lacking a required-environment op-cert is the commit that introduced the ticket's **terminal
`STATUS` event** — the status-change event whose target status is `closed` (rebar has no separate
"CLOSE" event type; closure is a `STATUS` event, per `_store/event_append.py`). That event's
introducing commit is resolved with the same `authorship.resolve_event_commit` mechanism, then fed
to `_is_enforced` against `verify.opcert_enforce_since`: a ticket whose close-`STATUS` event
predates the boundary is grandfathered (advisory pass); one after it is enforced, so a
missing/foreign op-cert fails. A ticket with no close-`STATUS` event yet (not closed) is out of
scope for the completion-verifier lane.

**Per-ticket walk.** `verify_authorship.py`'s merged-log helpers (`_collect_all`/`_collect_range`,
`_ScopedEvent`) yield per-EVENT; op-cert enforcement is per-TICKET. `verify-opcert` reuses those
helpers to enumerate the in-scope event set, then **groups by `ticket_id`** and evaluates each
ticket once, rather than re-implementing the walk.

**Edit targets.** `src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py` (new CLI, mirroring `verify_authorship.py`);
`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (add a `verify-opcert` equality-test intercept arm alongside the
existing `verify-identity`/`verify-commit-ticket` arms); `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (add
`verify.opcert_enforce_since`); `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (add the op-cert step +
the CI-trigger audit comment).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A CLI entrypoint `rebar verify-opcert` (in `src/rebar/_commands/`, mirroring
      `verify_authorship.py`) reads `verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` from
      config (with optional `--require-environment` / `--since` overrides), walks the merged log's
      tickets (reusing the merged-log walk helper), groups by ticket, and for each in-scope ticket
      verifies its required-kind op-cert via `rebar.attest.trusted_env.verify_required_environment`
      (reading the stored op-cert with `opcert.opcert_from_record`). Exit 1 iff an ENFORCED in-scope
      ticket lacks a valid required-environment op-cert; else exit 0 (advisory). A unit test asserts
      the exit-code contract.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` gains an op-cert verification **step** (same job /
      same merged-log walk, config-driven posture/boundary — NOT a parallel job) that is a bare
      `run: rebar verify-opcert` (no CI variable). A test asserts the workflow file contains a
      `rebar verify-opcert` step.
- [ ] A fixture test proves the gate: a ticket carrying a valid op-cert (via `sign_opcert_manifest`,
      env key pinned in a fixture `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, `verify.require_environment`
      set, and `verify.opcert_enforce_since` before the ticket's close) PASSES; a ticket missing the
      op-cert, and one whose op-cert is signed by a foreign (non-pinned) key, both FAIL. Fixture in
      `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` or `tests/unit/test_verify_opcert.py`; the test names the
      command it runs.
- [ ] CI-trigger audit as a concrete artifact: a comment block in
      `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` enumerates its `on:` triggers and classifies each
      INCLUDED (op-cert lane runs under it) or NO_FILTER (no `paths`/`branches` filter excludes an
      op-cert-bearing change); a test asserts the audit comment is present and lists every trigger.

## Remediation: verify-side authoritative-input rule (findings #4 + #5, change 664 rejected)

Change 664's review surfaced two coupled security findings in the gate's verification inputs
(`src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py:163-204`). The rule (the epic's "Verify-side
authoritative-input rule" + "Authoritative era anchor" bullets): the verifier trusts only signed
envelope contents and state it fetched/computed/resolved itself — never the stored record's
self-reported values, and never a producer-chosen anchor for a trust decision.

**Finding #4 (material half — fixed in a prior patchset, keep):** the gate recomputes
`material_fingerprint` from the authoritative ticket state its own merged-log walk produced
(same fingerprint function as the producer) and requires the signed subject to bind THAT value;
the record's plaintext mirror is a display hint.

**Finding #4 (commit half — necessary but insufficient):** `merged_log_commit` is read only from
the signature-verified payload (verify-then-extract) and constrained to resolve to a real
ancestor of the gated `main` HEAD, plus the `verify.opcert_enforce_since` grandfathering floor.
This proves the commit is real — not that it is the right one.

**Finding #5 (era anchor — the rollback gap, this remediation):** the era key-validity check
must not run at the cert's self-chosen `merged_log_commit` (a revoked-key holder freshly signs a
cert binding a pre-revocation ancestor; revocation becomes unenforceable). Per the epic's
resolution (Option B, era-at-storage-anchor):
- Key validity is evaluated at the cert's **storage anchor `S`** — the introducing commit of the
  envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event, resolved by the gate from its own merged-log walk with the
  same fail-closed resolver as the close anchor; an unresolvable/compacted anchor fails closed
  (the key must then be currently valid).
- Era boundaries in `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` become **tickets-branch log positions**
  (`added_at_log_position` / `revoked_at_log_position`), operator-stamped at add/revoke time via
  a `rebar trusted-env` helper — the same DAG as `S`, plain ancestry comparison.
- Revocation without a grandfather pin fails ALL that key's certs (compromise kill-switch);
  with a pin, certs stored at/before the pin stay valid (routine rotation preserves history).
- `merged_log_commit` keeps only its code-state meaning (ancestor-of-gated-HEAD +
  enforce-since floors); it carries no key-validity semantics.

### Additional Acceptance Criteria (findings #4 + #5)
- [ ] The gate recomputes `material_fingerprint` from authoritative ticket state: a test stores a
      SELF-CONSISTENT cert+record whose bound material does not match the ticket's current
      authoritative material and asserts the gate FAILS it (`mismatch`), while the same cert
      passes when the ticket state matches.
- [ ] `merged_log_commit` is taken from the signature-verified payload and constrained: a test
      asserts a bound commit that is not an ancestor of the gated history FAILS closed, and that
      mutating the record's plaintext `material_fingerprint`/`merged_log_commit` fields
      (envelope untouched) does not change the verdict in either direction.
- [ ] Rollback regression (the CVE-2026-44544-style case): a cert signed by a REVOKED key,
      freshly stored (storage anchor `S` after the key's `revoked_at_log_position`), binding a
      valid-era ancestor `merged_log_commit`, FAILS as `key_not_valid_at_era`; the same cert
      stored at/before the pin PASSES; a revoked key with NO grandfather pin FAILS all its
      certs; an unresolvable storage anchor fails closed (current-validity required).
- [ ] `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` era fields are tickets-branch log positions with an
      operator helper (`rebar trusted-env add|revoke`) that stamps the current tickets tip; a
      test asserts the schema parses, the helper stamps correctly, and a malformed/legacy
      main-SHA era field surfaces the existing located-error behavior.
baseline.summary: op-cert: merge-gate verification CI job over the merged log

baseline.description:
## Motivation
Discovered from 4de6 (completion verify->sign TOCTOU) and 80af (--ref carrier). rebar's git-tree-reading GATES (completion verification, plan-review claim gate's code reads, code review, commit-ticket verify) resolve symbolic refs (HEAD / origin/main) LAZILY and sometimes MORE THAN ONCE within a single logical operation. Any re-resolution of a symbolic ref mid-operation is a TOCTOU seam: a concurrent commit (routine in the parallel-agent/shared-worktree model) splits the two reads. 4de6 is the concrete instance; the --ref carrier fix pins the completion close, but the pattern is broader.

## Pattern to adopt
"Resolve once, thread the concrete sha." A symbolic ref is resolved to an IMMUTABLE sha ONCE at an operation's entry; every tree read within that operation uses that sha (never re-resolves the symbol). rebar already has both halves: the _snapshot/gate_source cache (snapshots keyed by sha -> free consistency across reads at the same sha) and the --ref param carrier (80af). The remaining work is to route EVERY gate's tree reads through a per-operation resolved sha, and to audit for any remaining lazy re-resolution seams (e.g. completion close also re-reads via caused-by git-blame and the plan-review close-gate recheck).

## Optional: CLI-scoped 'pinned rev'
Mirroring config.set_cli_overrides (the -c layer set once at main() entry and read by all consumers) and the ad9f central mount gate, a contextvars pinned-rev could be set once at CLI entry (resolve_ref('HEAD')) and serve as the DEFAULT source of 'what HEAD means now' for gates that default to HEAD.

## Caveats (why NOT a single invocation-wide rev)
1. Different gates have different natural base refs: completion close verifies HEAD (the tree being closed); plan-review/code-review verify the ATTESTED base (origin/main via REBAR_GATE_REF/[snapshot].ref). One invocation-wide pin would force them onto one rev -> wrong for at least one. Correct granularity is resolve-once-PER-OPERATION (each op pins ITS ref), with any CLI pin acting only as the default HEAD-sha source, not a single global rev.
2. Library/MCP have no single 'invocation' boundary (long-lived processes call many ops over time) -> ambient pinning is a CLI concept only; library/MCP callers thread ref explicitly (or None for lazy). Same CLI-only split as the ad9f mount gate.

## Scope sketch (children, if promoted)
- Audit all gate tree-reads for lazy/multiple symbolic-ref resolution; enumerate seams.
- Per-operation resolve-once for each gate (completion already via 4de6; plan-review; code-review; commit-ticket).
- Optional CLI-scoped pinned-rev contextvar + default wiring (CLI only).
- Tests: for each gate, moving HEAD mid-operation must not split verify from its downstream (sign / hash / compare).
baseline.summary: Invocation-consistent git-rev pinning: resolve-once-per-operation + optional CLI-scoped pinned-rev for all tree-reading gates

baseline.description:
## Why
`origin/main` ALREADY has `rebar fsck --repair` (the A3 data-remediation verb: rebuild
snapshots, retire orphans; requires mutation; `--dry-run`/`--limit`). Rather than add a
colliding second mutation flag, fold the ensure-sweep into that existing "drive to healthy"
verb, and give plain read-only fsck an ensures report line. The server boot path should also
converge.

## What
WS1 landed `rebar._store.ensures` with `run_ensures(tracker) -> list[EnsureOutcome]`,
`registry_ids() -> frozenset[str]`, and `applied_ids(tracker) -> set[str]`. WS3 wires them into
three surfaces.

**Fold `run_ensures()` into `fsck --repair`.** In `fsck.py::fsck_cli`, the `if do_repair:` block
(~line 725) already calls `_repair_run()` (the A3 data phase) then re-scans. Add the ensure-sweep
there as a DISTINCT phase, only on a live (non-`--dry-run`) run: call
`ensures.run_ensures(tracker)` and append a short summary of the outcomes to the report
(`ensures: swept N unit(s); C changed, F failed`, plus a per-unit line for any non-`ok` unit).
`run_ensures` acquires AND RELEASES the store write lock INTERNALLY (per-sweep), so it does not
nest inside `_repair_run()`'s batch and is never held across anything else — no deadlock. The
ensure phase is log-and-continue and DISTINCT from data-repair: a failed unit (already caught by
`run_ensures` → `failed`) never aborts the data-repair and never rolls back committed ticket data.
NO new `--fix`/mutation flag is introduced. `--dry-run --repair` stays read-only (no sweep). This
means existing `fsck --repair` callers now ALSO converge config — an acknowledged behavioral change.

**Read-only `ensures: N/M applied` line.** In `_scan()` (the read-only path, shared by plain
`fsck` and the `--repair` re-scan), append one informational line (no `issue_count` change)
derived WITHOUT calling `run_ensures`: `M = len(ensures.registry_ids())`,
`N = len(ensures.applied_ids(tracker) & ensures.registry_ids())` (intersection so a stale marker
id can't inflate N). Print `ensures: N/M applied`; when `N < M` append ` — run `rebar fsck
--repair` to converge`. An absent/garbage marker yields `applied_ids == set()` → `ensures: 0/M
applied`. Because this lives in `_scan`, the library read-only surface (`rebar.fsck` /
`fsck_cli(..., no_mutate=True)`) prints the line but NEVER sweeps.

The line is INFORMATIONAL (lowercase `ensures:` tag), NOT a structural issue: like the existing
`a3-remediation:` repair lines and the `fsck complete` summary, it is INTENTIONALLY excluded from
`--output json` — `_transform_json` only lifts `^[A-Z_]+:`-tagged structural issues + `FIXED:`
lines into the JSON payload, so a lowercase `ensures:` line is (correctly) skipped there and never
inflates `issue_count` or flips the exit code. Uppercasing the tag would wrongly enroll a converged
store's report line as a JSON "issue"; text-only is the deliberate, precedent-matching choice. So
the `ensures: N/M` line appears in the human text surface only; it does NOT change the JSON schema.

**MCP server startup.** In `mcp_server.main`, AFTER the `--help` early-return and BEFORE
`build_server().run()`, best-effort converge the store: resolve the tracker
(`config.tracker_dir()`), and if it is an existing dir call `ensures.run_ensures(tracker, timeout=…, attempts=1)`
with a SHORT lock budget (a few seconds) so a contended lock skips rather than delaying boot.
`run_ensures` acquires and RELEASES its own write lock internally — it is NOT held across
`build_server().run()`, and the server boot itself runs under NO lock. Wrap the whole thing in a
`try/except` that log-and-continues: an ImportError, a missing store, or any sweep error must
never abort boot. (WS3 adds an optional `timeout`/`attempts` passthrough to `run_ensures` that
forwards to `write_lock`; default `None` keeps WS1's behavior unchanged.)

**Tests owned by WS3 (fsck + MCP surface).** There is NO existing byte-parity golden for the fsck
REPORT output — the only fsck goldens are the static `--help` text
(`tests/golden/cli_help/fsck__dashhelp.out` / `fsck__help.out`, exercised by
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli_argparse.py`), which the new report line does NOT change, and
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_library.py::test_fsck_runs` only asserts `"fsck"` is present. So no
golden/byte-parity file needs editing (verified: `python scripts/…` / rerun `test_cli_argparse`
stays green). WS3 adds a NEW `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py` asserting the surfaces
it owns — including the MCP startup: a test monkeypatches `mcp_server.build_server` to return a
stub whose `.run()` records that it was called, spies `ensures.run_ensures`, invokes
`mcp_server.main()` (argv without `--help`), and asserts `run_ensures` was called BEFORE
`build_server().run()`; a second case passes `--help` and asserts `run_ensures` is NOT called
(early return); a third patches `run_ensures` to raise and asserts `main()` still calls
`.run()` (boot never aborts).

## Scope
In: folding `run_ensures` into `--repair`, the read-only `ensures: N/M` line + its
marker/registry data-flow, `no_mutate` gating, MCP server-startup wiring (best-effort, short-lock,
never-under-boot-lock), the `run_ensures` timeout/attempts passthrough, and the new fsck test file.
Out: the registry/`run_ensures` (WS1), the write-path hint (WS2), the authoritative git-log
zero-commit / hot-path / concurrency / no_mutate-never-sweep behavioral suite (WS5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar fsck --repair` additionally runs `run_ensures()` as a distinct phase (folded into the existing A3 path; `run_ensures` takes + releases the store write lock internally); NO new mutation flag is introduced; `--dry-run --repair` does not sweep
- [ ] `rebar fsck --repair` on a pending store converges it (writes `.ensure-applied`) and reports the swept units; a second `--repair` reports no ensure changes (the fsck-level idempotency check; the authoritative git-log zero-commit assertion lives in WS5)
- [ ] Plain read-only `rebar fsck` prints `ensures: N/M applied` (M=`registry_ids()`, N=applied∩registry) WITHOUT calling `run_ensures`; an absent marker prints `0/M`; the library `no_mutate=True` surface prints the line but never sweeps
- [ ] The informational lowercase `ensures:` line is intentionally text-only: it is NOT emitted into `--output json` (consistent with `a3-remediation:`/`fsck complete`) and never inflates the JSON `issue_count` or changes the exit code; a test asserts `--output json` on a pending store still parses and reports the correct issue_count
- [ ] MCP server startup calls `run_ensures()` after the --help check and before `build_server().run()`, best-effort (log-and-continue, never aborts boot) with a SHORT lock budget; the lock is released before boot (never held across `build_server().run()`). Proven by a test that stubs `build_server` + spies `run_ensures` and asserts: (a) `main()` (no --help) calls `run_ensures` BEFORE `.run()`; (b) `main(["--help"])` does NOT call `run_ensures`; (c) when `run_ensures` raises, `main()` still calls `.run()`
- [ ] No existing fsck golden/byte-parity test changes (the report line is additive and the `--help` goldens are unaffected); WS3's new `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py` covers the N/M line, `--repair` sweep + fsck-level idempotency, and `no_mutate`-never-sweep
baseline.summary: WS3: fold ensure-sweep into existing rebar fsck --repair + read-only ensures: N/M line + MCP startup

content.text: ## Current state (do not regress)
`rebar delete <id> --user-approved` ALREADY EXISTS and performs an intentional
SOFT delete: it writes a `.tombstone.json` marker, cleans up inbound links
(UNLINK events), and guards against deleting a ticket with non-deleted children.
The ticket then drops out of default listings but its event history is retained
on the `tickets` branch — i.e. it is recoverable and remains replay/clone-
consistent (the merge-as-union model still converges). This soft delete is the
correct, safe default and MUST be preserved. (`--user-approved` is the existing
friction flag.)
## The work: add an EXPLICIT HARD delete to the command
Add an opt-in hard-delete mode (e.g. `rebar delete <id> --user-approved --hard`,
or a distinct verb) that PERMANENTLY removes the ticket's events from the store,
not just tombstones it. Hard delete must carry MORE friction than soft delete
and must reckon with the append-only, auto-pushed, multi-clone design.
### Hard part — convergence across clones (decide + document)
The store is append-only and merges as a union, and every write auto-pushes to
`origin/tickets`. Physically `rm`-ing event files in one clone does NOT converge:
another clone still holds those events and a later merge re-introduces them
("zombie" resurrection). So a real hard delete needs a PROPAGATING purge
mechanism, e.g. a dedicated `PURGE`/`HARD_DELETE` event (or tombstone variant)
that the reducer honors as "exclude AND suppress re-merge of these event UUIDs",
combined with a coordinated removal of the underlying files (like SNAPSHOT's
*.retired rename, under the write lock). Decide and document the exact semantics
and how it interacts with invariants I1 (append-only) and I8/I9 (fork/compaction).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Soft delete (current `delete --user-approved`, tombstone) is unchanged and remains the default

- [ ] A distinct, MORE-effortful hard-delete path exists (explicit intent beyond `--user-approved`, e.g. re-typing the id or an extra `--hard`/confirm token); a bare `delete <id>` and even `delete <id> --user-approved` never hard-delete

- [ ] Hard delete permanently removes the ticket's events and CONVERGES across clones (no resurrection after fetch/merge) — purge semantics decided & documented (PURGE/HARD_DELETE event vs physical removal; honored by the reducer)
- [ ] Dangling-reference handling defined (refuse, or warn + clean up inbound links) for hard delete
- [ ] fsck stays clean after a hard delete (no MISSING_CREATE/orphan-link noise for the purged id)
- [ ] Available + correctly gated across CLI, library, MCP (REBAR_MCP_READONLY blocks it; MCP exposure of hard delete especially guarded)
- [ ] Docs updated (README, CLAUDE.md, docs/event-schema.md if a new event type is added; clarify soft vs hard) + tests (incl. a cross-clone convergence test)
## Notes
- While here: the soft-delete children guard (`ticket_delete` in ticket-lib-api.sh)
reads parent_id from the CREATE event only, so a child REPARENTED via
`edit --parent` is missed — the same class of bug fixed for the transition
open-children guard (commit 535bee1). Fix the delete children guard to use the
effective parent_id too, or factor out the shared scan.

baseline.summary: delete: add an explicit hard-delete mode (current delete is an intentional soft delete)

content.text: # S4a — Review-bot Gerrit identity + event plumbing (plugins, SSM token, IAM)
## Why
Before the review-bot can vote (S4b), the Gerrit-side plumbing must exist: a service-account
identity the bot votes as, the event-delivery plugins that notify it, and the secrets/IAM to
reach them. Split out from the bot's review/vote LOGIC (S4b) because this is a distinct layer
(Gerrit account + plugin install + AWS IAM/SSM) with no application logic — keeping each story
single-layered (the S4 oversize the gate flagged was 4 layers in one ticket).
## What
- **Bot identity.** A dedicated Gerrit account in the built-in `Service Users` group (thread
isolation; SERVICE_USER accounts are excluded from the attention set except on a negative
vote). Its HTTP auth token (for the OUTBOUND REST vote in S4b) is GENERATED by
`infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` itself — after creating the account it calls
`PUT /a/accounts/<bot>/password.http` (the account HTTP-password / token endpoint), captures
the value returned in the response body, and stores it in SSM Parameter Store at a fixed path
(`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`). `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` is **idempotent**:
check-before-create (`GET /a/accounts/<bot>`) and `put-parameter --overwrite`, so
re-provisioning regenerates+restores the token without duplicating the account or orphaning it.
- **Least-privilege IAM.** The instance role grants `ssm:GetParameter` scoped to exactly the bot
parameter path (`arn:aws:ssm:<region>:<acct>:parameter/rebar/prod/*`), never `Resource:"*"`.
- **Event delivery — two integrated channels.**
- *Push (primary):* install the `webhooks` plugin to POST `patchset-created` to the review-bot
receiver (the HTTP endpoint stood up in S2, behavior wired in S4b).
- *Backfill (safety net):* install the `events-log` plugin, which STORES a queryable event log
(`GET /a/plugins/events-log/events?...`) — it does NOT auto-replay; the S4b reconciler polls
it. Plugin **provenance is a durable end-state, not a research note**: the exact arm64 jar
URLs + checksums + versions for Gerrit 3.14.1 are pinned in `infra/gerrit/` (recorded files),
so a rebuild installs byte-identical plugins.
- **Inbound webhook auth (peer-pattern correction — the `webhooks` plugin has NO HMAC).** The
Gerrit `webhooks` plugin offers no request signing/HMAC (only `sslVerify`, which defaults
false), and it reads its remote config EXCLUSIVELY from `refs/meta/config`. So inbound
authenticity is bolt-on and split across the boundary. `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` is a
**TEMPLATE** committed with a placeholder (e.g. `remote.<name>.url =
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/?token=__BOT_TOKEN__`) — NOT a static committed
secret. At config-push time `service-user.sh` reads the token from SSM, TEMPLATES the URL by
substituting the placeholder, and pushes the rendered config to `refs/meta/config`. Because the
`webhooks` plugin only reads `refs/meta/config`, a URL-embedded token NECESSARILY lands there —
so the URL-token is NOT "kept out of refs/meta/config." It is a SECONDARY, bounded-exposure
control: `refs/meta/config` is Gerrit-access-controlled and is NOT replicated to GitHub
(`replicatePermissions=false`), and the token is rotatable. The PRIMARY inbound control is the
**network ACL** — the `/review/` path on nginx is reachable only from the Gerrit host
(loopback/SG). S4b's receiver additionally validates the token + source.
## Scope
In: the Gerrit Service-Users bot account + SSM token + least-privilege IAM + install/pin the
`webhooks` and `events-log` plugins + the inbound webhook secret/ACL config. Out: the receiver's
parse/review/vote/reconcile LOGIC and observability (S4b); replication (S5). Depends on S3
(project + `LLM-Review` label/ACL exist so the bot's vote permission resolves) and S2 (the
receiver service + nginx `/review/` route exist).
## Files
- `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` — idempotent bot-account creation; GENERATES the bot HTTP token
via `PUT /a/accounts/<bot>/password.http`, captures it, and upserts it to SSM; at config-push
time renders `webhooks.config` from its template (token from SSM) and pushes to
`refs/meta/config`.
- `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` — `webhooks` plugin remote config TEMPLATE: a placeholder
secret-token URL (patchset-created -> the `/review/` receiver) + `allowedUrlPattern` if used;
rendered with the SSM token at push time (no committed secret).
- `infra/gerrit/plugins/` — pinned `webhooks` + `events-log` jar provenance (URLs + checksums +
versions for 3.14.1/arm64) and the install step.
- the least-privilege SSM IAM policy for the bot token path (in the infra Terraform).
> Record `set_file_impact` for these paths before claiming.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The bot account exists in `Service Users` (SERVICE_USER tag; excluded from the attention
set except on a negative vote); its REST auth token is GENERATED by `service-user.sh` via
`PUT /a/accounts/<bot>/password.http`, captured, and stored in SSM
(`/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`); re-running `service-user.sh` is idempotent (no duplicate
account / orphaned token).
- [ ] The instance role's SSM read is scoped to the bot token path only (no `Resource:"*"`),
verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] The `webhooks` and `events-log` plugins are installed on Gerrit 3.14.1 from pinned,
checksum-verified, arm64-compatible jars whose URLs/checksums/versions are recorded in
`infra/gerrit/` (a rebuild reinstalls byte-identical plugins).
- [ ] `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config` is committed as a TEMPLATE with a token placeholder (no
committed secret); `service-user.sh` renders it with the SSM token at config-push time and
pushes it to `refs/meta/config` (the only place the `webhooks` plugin reads remote config).
- [ ] The `webhooks` remote POSTs `patchset-created` to the `/review/` receiver via the rendered
secret-token URL, and — since the token necessarily resides in `refs/meta/config` and the
plugin provides no HMAC — the PRIMARY control is that `/review/` is reachable only from the
Gerrit host (network ACL / nginx): verified by a request without the token / from a
disallowed source being refused at the edge. (`refs/meta/config` is Gerrit-access-controlled
and not replicated to GitHub via `replicatePermissions=false`; the token is rotatable.)
- [ ] `events-log` is installed and queryable (the S4b reconciler depends on it); confirmed by a
sample `GET /a/plugins/events-log/events` returning recent events.
## Round-7 remediation

- **Non-clobbering refs/meta/config push (T4):** `service-user.sh` updates `refs/meta/config` via **read-modify-write** (fetch current ref -> update only the webhooks config -> commit -> push), NEVER a full-tree replacement (which would wipe S3's `LLM-Review` label / submit-requirement / ACL on `refs/meta/config`).
- [ ] The webhooks-config push is read-modify-write and preserves S3's existing `refs/meta/config` (verified: after S4a's push the `LLM-Review` label + submit requirement from S3 remain present).
## Round-8 remediation

- **HTTP-password generation body (G6):** the `PUT /a/accounts/<bot>/password.http` call MUST send a JSON body `{"generate": true}` (HttpPasswordInput) to trigger server-side generation; the generated password is returned in the response body and captured into SSM `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`.
## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)

- The bot's Gerrit HTTP token (SSM `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`) is the receiver's OUTBOUND READ credential for BOTH the REST `/a/` calls (diff fetch + vote) AND git-over-HTTPS clone of the change ref into `repo_root` (S4b's `resolve_gate_handle` context). Its scope must cover both; no separate read key is provisioned (the S5 deploy key is GitHub-write-only).
- `events-log` REST backfill query (`GET /a/plugins/events-log/events`) gets an explicit smoke-check here before S4b's reconciler depends on it (it was not in the named E1–E5 derisk set).
Added ACs:
- [ ] Documented + tested that the bot HTTP token authenticates BOTH Gerrit REST `/a/` and git-over-HTTPS clone of a change ref (the receiver's read path); scope covers both
- [ ] `events-log` query endpoint smoke-checked (returns recent events) as a precondition for S4b's backfill reconciler
## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30)

- **Blocking — ADR for inbound-webhook-auth (captured):** `docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md` records the decision: the Gerrit `webhooks` plugin has NO HMAC and reads remote config only from `refs/meta/config`, so (a) the PRIMARY inbound control is the network ACL (`/review/` reachable only from the Gerrit host via nginx/loopback + SG), (b) a URL-embedded secret token is a SECONDARY bounded-exposure control that necessarily resides in `refs/meta/config` (Gerrit-access-controlled, NOT replicated to GitHub via `replicatePermissions=false`, rotatable), and (c) S4b's receiver additionally validates the token + source. Added to Files + an AC.

- **`replicatePermissions=false` durability (advisory):** this is set in S5's replication config; S4a's ADR-0014 notes the dependency (the token's non-exposure to GitHub relies on S5 keeping `replicatePermissions=false`), and S5's AC asserts it.

- **Surgical RMW refs/meta/config push:** `service-user.sh` updates ONLY the `webhooks.config` file in the `refs/meta/config` tree (it writes/replaces that one file and commits), never touching `project.config`/`groups` (S3's label/submit-req/ACL). Verified post-push that S3's LLM-Review label + submit requirement remain.

- **Plugin install rollback:** plugin jars are dropped into the persistent `plugins/` dir; rollback = remove the jar + restart (or `gerrit plugin remove`). Pinned provenance (URL+sha256+version) lets a rebuild reinstall byte-identical; a destabilizing plugin is removed by deleting its jar and restarting Gerrit.

- **Token-generation mechanism (impl reality):** on this PoC's `DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` instance, cookie-auth REST mutations are refused, so the bot account + its HTTP token are created via the Gerrit SSH admin command (`gerrit create-account <bot> --group "Service Users" --http-password <generated>`), authenticated by the admin SSH key; the generated password is captured to SSM `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`. (Equivalent end-state to the `PUT password.http {"generate":true}` path; the AC's intent — a generated, SSM-stored bot token + idempotent re-provision — is preserved.)
Added ACs:
- [ ] `docs/adr/0014-inbound-webhook-auth.md` exists and records the no-HMAC / network-ACL-primary / URL-token-secondary / refs/meta/config-resident / not-replicated decision.
- [ ] The refs/meta/config push is surgical (only webhooks.config changes); S3's project.config (LLM-Review label + submit requirement + ACL) is preserved post-push.

baseline.description:
## Context
A project pins trusted-environment public keys out-of-band (never the tickets branch) and may
require a specific environment's certificate for a gate; the check verifies against the pinned key,
not the certificate's self-claimed keyid.

**Config location + schema (from the epic's "Trust config & era-validity protocol").** Keys are
pinned in a YAML file at **`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`** (repo-root, on the Gerrit-gated +
CODEOWNERS-protected code branch — NEVER the auto-pushed `tickets` branch). Schema:

```yaml
environments:
  - env_id: "<string>"            # logical environment name; MUST equal the DSSE principal (keyid)
    keys:
      - public_key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…"       # one OpenSSH ed25519 authorized-keys line
        added_at_commit: "<git-sha-on-main>"      # era start
        revoked_at_commit: "<git-sha-on-main>|null"  # era end (null = still valid)
```

A per-gate `require_environment` names one `env_id` that must produce the certificate. An absent
file (or no `require_environment`) is the low-security default: local certs are records, not
controls. This story owns the loader + the required-environment check; the era-validity *rule* over
`added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit` is implemented in child 368c and consumed here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A config loader reads trusted-environment public keys from `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`
      (the out-of-band, review-gated path — NOT the tickets branch), validating the schema above;
      an absent file yields "no required environment" (opt-in default off).
- [ ] A cert from an environment not in the pinned set fails the required-environment check (test),
      and a cert whose `env_id` is pinned but whose signature does not verify against the pinned key
      also fails (test).
- [ ] The check verifies against the **pinned** key for the required `env_id`, never the
      certificate's self-claimed `key_id`/keyid (test: a cert whose keyid claims a pinned env but
      whose signature is by a different key FAILS).
baseline.summary: op-cert: out-of-band trusted-environment key config + required-environment policy

baseline.description:
Cut the cost of obtaining the tickets store, and fix the fail-open bootstrap that silently produces an empty divergent store.

Measured facts and the corrected premises: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Sibling epic: **0303-692c** (censual-organic-mouflon). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

A fresh full clone of `tickets` costs **1.04 GiB / 59s wall / 319s CPU**. Measured against GitHub, `--filter=blob:none` costs **68.7 MiB / 14.3s** — a ~15x reduction. In CI the tickets objects arrive in the `actions/checkout` step, measured at **237 s** on run 30494781536, versus **2 s** for the manual worktree mount that follows.

Separately, P1 bug **01e8-302b** (bilingual-capitalist-caecilian) is open: in Claude Code's web environment the tickets fetch timed out through the agent git proxy and `rebar init` **silently bootstrapped a fresh empty store**, diverging from `origin/tickets` so every read returned `[]` and new writes landed on a branch that cannot fast-forward back.

## Approach and why this one

**rebar cannot filter a clone it does not perform.** `grep -rn 'git clone' src/` yields only a docstring; every rebar fetch is post-clone, and `init.py:375` runs only inside `if remote:` — i.e. only once `origin/tickets` already resolves, by which point the objects are local. So the size lever is the `actions/checkout` step (which has supported a `filter:` input since v4.1.0) plus documented clone guidance — not rebar-side fetch flags. This is a deliberate narrowing after two earlier designs were measured to be inert.

`blob:none` is safe for rebar's own access patterns: whole-store `verify-identity` in a blobless clone fetched **0 bytes** and ran *faster* than in a full clone (3.75s vs 3.98s), because its scan is a pure tree-level diff and event/keyring bodies are read from the **working tree** (`verify_authorship.py:371`, `authorship.py:119-128`). The accepted cost is stated rather than waved away: `git blame` over historical trees runs on the bug-close path (`metrics/blame.py:69` <- `derive_caused_by` <- `transition_close.py:513`).

And a faster fetch does **not** fix the P1 — it only lowers the probability. The mechanism is the fail-open fallthrough to `worktree add --orphan`, which is fixed directly.

## Scope (children)

1. **B3** set `merge.ours.driver=true` in the reconciler workflow (prerequisite for B1)
2. **B1** add `filter: blob:none` to the `actions/checkout` steps that mount tickets
3. **B2** fail closed instead of orphan-bootstrapping an empty store (fixes P1 01e8-302b)
4. **B4** clone guidance doc + make `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure
5. **B5** add `--no-renames` and `-c log.showSignature=false` to the two authorship resolvers
6. **B6** delete `.bridge_state.bak-retarget` (33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree at HEAD)

## Compatibility and rollback

Every child is independently revertible and none changes a persisted format. B3 must land **before** B1: `reconcile-bridge.yml` uses `fetch-depth: 0` precisely because shallow history breaks merge-base, and `blob:none` keeps commits but removes merge-base **blobs** which the reconverge path materializes — with `merge.ours.driver` undefined on the runner, `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` silently degrades to a 3-way text merge of an 18 MB JSON file. B6 must land before epic 0303-692c's reclaim so the strip does not retain those blobs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A controlled **before/after byte measurement** (pack size, or `GIT_TRACE_PACKET` received
      bytes) of a fresh CI checkout with and without the filter shows the expected reduction, **and**
      the subsequent manual tickets fetch is confirmed to inherit
      `remote.origin.partialclonefilter`. Must NOT be a config-presence assertion: git writes that
      key even when the server ignored the filter (reproduced). Tier: CI job measurement.
- [ ] A reconverge against a diverged remote succeeds on a blobless runner (proves B3 landed before
      B1 and the merge driver is defined).
- [ ] With a reachable remote advertising `tickets`, a simulated fetch failure causes a **non-zero
      exit** and **no orphan branch is created**. Tier: CLI subprocess against a real temporary
      remote. This is the RED case for P1 01e8-302b.
- [ ] `derive_caused_by` returns `None` when blame fails on **any** path, rather than tallying a
      partial path set and electing a culprit that would not have won over the full set (which would
      write a wrong `caused_by` link). Tier: unit test injecting a per-path failure, asserting no
      link event is written.
- [ ] With `log.showSignature=true` **and signed commits** in the fixture repo, `resolve_event_commit`
      and `resolve_position_commit` return a valid 40-hex SHA. The signing is load-bearing: with
      `--format=%H` over unsigned commits the setting emits no extra lines, so an unsigned fixture
      makes this vacuously green. Tier: unit against a real temporary git repo.
- [ ] `.bridge_state.bak-retarget` is absent from the tree at HEAD and working-tree size drops by
      >=33 MB.
- [ ] The clone-guidance doc exists and states the measured numbers (full 1.04 GiB / 59s vs
      blob:none 68.7 MiB / 14.3s) and the accepted `git blame` degradation.
baseline.summary: Cut tickets-store clone cost via CI partial clone + fail closed instead of bootstrapping an empty store

baseline.description:
Document how to clone this repo cheaply, state the one accepted degradation honestly, and fix the latent wrong-answer bug that degradation would otherwise cause. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Doc
Record `--filter=blob:none` guidance with the measured numbers (full **1.04 GiB / 59 s** vs blobless **68.7 MiB / 14.3 s**), and that `--filter=tree:0` must never be used here (measured **3.57 GiB**, 3.4x larger than full). Note that rebar itself cannot filter a clone it does not perform.

## The code fix (why it belongs with the doc)
`git blame` over historical trees runs on a real rebar path: `metrics/blame.py:69` <- `_blame_file_commits` <- `derive_caused_by` (`:94`) <- `transition_close.py:514`, i.e. **on every bug close without an explicit `--caused-by`**. Under a blobless promisor this faults blobs one at a time.

**Prerequisite the earlier draft missed (plan-review G6 remediation): failure and emptiness are currently indistinguishable.** `_blame_file_commits` (`blame.py:67-79`) returns `[]` BOTH when the git call fails (`if out is None: return []`) AND when a successful blame yields no SHAs. So "abort on any per-path failure" is **not implementable as stated** — there is nothing to detect. This ticket must therefore FIRST change `_blame_file_commits` to return `None` on git failure and `[]` on a successful-but-empty result, and only then have `derive_caused_by` abort on `None`. Treating a legitimately empty file as a failure would suppress correct derivations.

Total failure is benign (`blame.py:37` returns `None`). **Partial failure is not:** `derive_caused_by` loops per path and tallies across all of them, so if blame succeeds on some paths and fails on others — entirely plausible with a partly-warm object store — the strict-majority test runs over a **subset** and can elect a culprit that would not have won over the full set. That writes a **wrong `caused_by` link**, which is worse than writing none.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_blame_file_commits` returns **`None`** on git failure and **`[]`** on a successful-but-empty
      blame — the two are distinguishable. Tier: **unit** with both fixtures.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_blame.py -k distinguishes -v`.
- [ ] `derive_caused_by` returns `None` when `_blame_file_commits` returns `None` for **any** path,
      rather than tallying a partial set. Tier: **unit** injecting a per-path git failure.
      Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_blame.py -k partial_failure -v`.
- [ ] A path whose blame legitimately yields **zero** lines does **not** abort the derivation (the
      negative control that keeps correct derivations working). Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] No `caused_by` link event is written in that case. Tier: **integration** on the close path
      asserting the event set.
- [ ] With all paths succeeding, the derived culprit is unchanged from today — the negative control.
      Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [ ] The guidance doc exists, states the measured numbers, names the accepted `git blame`
      degradation, and is linked from the docs index. Tier: **doc-existence + content check**.

## Files
`src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `docs/` guidance page, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies.
