baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The completion-verifier LLM runs even when the ticket's own Acceptance Criteria block still contains unchecked '- [ ]' items — a deterministic fail-fast condition. Backtest over verifier-passed closes found unchecked boxes only in [operator-attested]-shaped items (whose done-evidence legitimately lives outside the snapshot); non-attested unchecked boxes did not occur, so a precheck that exempts the attested tag adds no false rejections. check-ac exists but only as a readiness scorer, absent from the close path.

## Approach
In the close transition path (before the LLM verifier dispatch), parse the ticket description's '## Acceptance Criteria' section; if any '- [ ]' checkbox remains unchecked, fail the close deterministically with a teaching message (check the box after satisfying it, or edit the AC with justification) — same style as existing DET short-circuits. EXEMPTION: a '- [ ]' line whose text after the checkbox begins with the case-insensitive '[operator-attested]' tag is NOT a violation — reuse the exact matcher (det_operator_attested._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py:44) rather than a parallel regex, so the two surfaces cannot drift. Exempt classes that skip the verifier today (duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated via replacement-link precheck) are untouched: the precheck runs only where the verifier would run.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py (precheck family, alongside _completion_precheck)
- tests for the close path

## Testing
Happy: all boxes checked -> close proceeds to verifier. Unchecked box -> exit non-zero pre-LLM with the teaching message. Unchecked '- [x] [operator-attested] ...' item -> precheck passes (exemption row, both lowercase and mixed-case tag). Non-completion classes (duplicate etc.) bypass unchanged. Description without checkbox syntax -> precheck passes (prose AC remains legal).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Close on a ticket with any unchecked, non-[operator-attested] '- [ ]' AC item fails deterministically BEFORE any LLM call, with remediation guidance.
- [x] Unchecked items carrying the [operator-attested] tag (matched via det_operator_attested's shared regex) are exempt and do not block the close.
- [x] Prose-only AC (no checkboxes) and non-completion close classes are unaffected.
- [x] Backtest property preserved: historical verifier-passed closes (including attested-shaped ones) would all still pass.
- [x] Tests cover checked, unchecked, attested-exempt (case-insensitive), prose-only, and exempt-class paths.
baseline.summary: AC-checkbox completeness precheck at close (deterministic, pre-LLM)

baseline.description:
# README front door: first-30-seconds pass for evaluators

## Why

The README serves a different persona than contributor docs: a prospective USER deciding in 30 seconds whether to try rebar (split from the onboarding story on review advice — independent actor, independently shippable). All six surveyed loved dev-tool READMEs (ruff, uv, httpx, rich, just, fzf) converge on: H1/logo → one badge row → one-sentence tagline within ~15 lines → an image within the first screen (~line 40) → highlight bullets → install → copy-pasteable quickstart, with ≤200 words of prose before the first code block. rebar's current README is information-rich but insider-shaped. Caveat acknowledged: the six exemplars are single-surface tools while rebar is multi-surface (CLI + library + MCP) — the adaptation is httpx's move (show the API fast) applied per surface, not a claim the pattern transfers verbatim.

## What

- Top-of-README restructure (content below the fold is preserved, only re-ordered/trimmed):
  1. `# rebar` → one badge row, exactly 4 badges: PyPI version, Python versions, CI status, license.
  2. One-sentence tagline naming the differentiator: an event-sourced, git-backed ticket store + Jira reconciler built for agent swarms, exposed as a Python library, CLI, and MCP server.
  3. Demo asset by ~line 40: a static terminal screenshot (decision: screenshot over gif/asciinema — zero-dependency to render on GitHub, versionable, no motion-accessibility concerns; recorded here and in the commit) of the core loop: `rebar ready` → `rebar claim` → `rebar transition … closed`. Asset committed under `docs/assets/` and referenced with a relative path.
  4. 5–8 highlight bullets; the tri-surface is one explicit bullet; the two-gate Gerrit dogfooding is another (it is the project's most distinctive practice).
  5. Install: `pipx install nava-rebar` (+ brew one-liner).
  6. Quickstart ≤15 lines total covering all three surfaces: a 3-command CLI session, a 3-line Python snippet, a one-line MCP registration.
- Keep prose before the first code block ≤200 words (uv's ratio).
- Contributor pointer near the bottom links CONTRIBUTING.md and `docs/your-first-change.md` (this story depends_on the onboarding story so the link is never dangling).

## Scope

IN: README.md top section, `docs/assets/` screenshot, badge row.
OUT: docs/ restructuring; CONTRIBUTING/tutorial content (onboarding story); marketing site; benchmark charts (rebar's pitch is workflow, not speed — a screenshot, not a bench, per the just/fzf pattern).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Badge row present with exactly 4 badges — prove: `grep -c "img.shields.io\|badge" README.md` in the first 10 lines = 4 (or equivalent count of badge images).
- [ ] Tagline within the first 15 lines states event-sourced/git-backed + agent-oriented + the three surfaces — prove: head -15 contains "MCP" and "CLI".
- [ ] Demo asset committed and referenced — prove: `test -f docs/assets/<asset>` and README references it within the first 40 lines.
- [ ] Quickstart covers CLI + Python + MCP in ≤15 total code lines — prove: count the fenced block lines.
- [ ] ≤200 words of prose before the first fenced code block — prove: word count of the pre-fence region.
- [ ] Asset-form decision (static screenshot; rationale) recorded in the commit message and a ticket comment.
baseline.summary: README front door: first-30-seconds pass for evaluators

baseline.description:
## Context

Implement parent story A2-1 as one reviewable vertical slice. `last_get_pass` previously changed up to 20 binding entries per pass even when no real binding changes. Introduce `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json` as the new rotation store while dual-writing the legacy inline field during the rollout window.

## Approach

- Introduce a focused rotation module that owns fail-open sidecar load/save and accessors. Read the chronological `max(sidecar_value, legacy_inline_value)` for each Jira key and write every new stamp to both the sidecar and the legacy inline field. Dual-write is required so an interleaved old binary sees progress made by a new binary; A2-2 removes the legacy write only after its rollout gate.
- Load legacy-only state into memory. Persist the sidecar only through `BindingStore.save()`; this covers the end-of-pass save plus the write-ahead, recovery, and retirement save paths in `dispatch_one.py` and `binding_store.py`. `reconcile-check` uses `persist=False` and never reaches any save path.
- Wire `BindingStore` and `outbound_differ` to the shared accessors. Extract the existing outbound wrappers so `outbound_differ.py` remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
- Add a `GET_ROTATION_FILE` constant in `git_adapter.py`, characterize it, and include it in the explicit local staging list and basename membership check in `reconcile_helpers.py` so both dual-written files land in one local commit.
- Update the `_store/push.py` regenerable-files docstring and cover that documentation requirement as an acceptance criterion.
- Preserve rollback: a reverted reader ignores the sidecar but sees the legacy field advanced by every new-binary pass.

## TDD / Verification

The behavioral oracle was authored RED-first. The interleaved-binary, real-git staging, and CLI read-only cases were held out from the implementer; only the basic dual-read happy path was exposed. The A1 no-commit regression is asserted only after rotation state is initialized and on a pass with no absent-key GETs. A pass that performs absent-key GETs advances and commits both rotation representations during the compatibility window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.

## Files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/get_rotation.py`

baseline.description:
## What

Create `examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md` — the shared TDD test-design standard — and wire it into the three skills at the point each incorporates testing. Written in the skills' voice, with the 'scale ceremony to the bug' principle explicit.

**Prompt style (applies to every prompt change in this task).** All added/changed prompt text addresses the LLM user of the skill, not a human audience, and avoids the pink-elephant problem: lead with positive guidance (what to do, with concrete correct examples), keep prohibitions short and direct, and never elaborate negative examples that prime the model toward the prohibited behavior. Concise throughout; no narration of wrong approaches beyond a one-line prohibition.

**Reference mechanism (canonical file + byte-identical per-skill copies, drift-gated).** `shared/test-design.md` is the canonical copy; each consuming skill directory ships a REAL FILE `<skill>/test-design.md` that must be byte-identical to it. Every SKILL.md references `test-design.md` in its OWN directory — the same same-directory companion-file pattern rebar-debug already uses for `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md` — so a skill resolves the standard in every load context (repo checkout, a symlinked skill dir in a user skills location, a plain copy, a zip download, any OS), with no symlinks and no user-/machine-specific paths anywhere in the repo. Divergence is prevented by a new gating unit test `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` that asserts each copy is byte-identical to the canonical file — it runs under `make test`, an existing gating CI command, mirroring the repo's regenerate-and-diff drift-gate convention (prompt-index, public-types, env-vars). Symlinks were considered and rejected: Windows checkouts without symlink support and GitHub zip archives materialize a symlink as a one-line text file, and copying a single skill directory leaves it dangling. The README documents the convention: edit the canonical file, then sync the copies (`for s in rebar-debug rebar-implement rebar-brainstorm; do cp examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md examples/claude-skills/$s/test-design.md; done`). It names the consuming skills; rebar-janitor is deliberately NOT a consumer — it never authors or runs tests (it finds, verifies, and files maintainability work as tickets; its phase docs own its ticketization criteria), so it takes no copy, and the drift test hardcodes the same three-skill consumer set (adding a consumer means adding it to the test and the one-liner together).

The shared file covers:
- Existing-coverage inventory before authoring: the required artifact is a RED oracle, which may be an existing failing test, an existing test strengthened into RED form, or a new test only when nothing covers the behavior. Search by contract wording, public entry point, implementation symbol, error text, and bug/regression identifier; read the nearest tests.
- A test contract card frozen before test code, with scaled fields: contract + citation, bug-triggering preconditions, production path, tier + why lower is insufficient, observable postcondition, CI gate are always required; negative control, collateral invariants, recovery, fault injection apply conditionally (stateful/atomicity/concurrency work).
- Test-tier selection rule: the smallest tier that still crosses every component in the proven mechanism, with the bug-class -> tier table pairing each class with its tier: pure calculation or validation branch -> in-process unit test; producer/consumer shape mismatch -> contract test through real serialization; CLI parsing/streams/env/exit codes -> real CLI subprocess; git refs/merge/reachability/data loss -> real temporary git repos; locking/race -> multiple real processes with a deterministic barrier; parent exit/signals/fd inheritance -> parent-child subprocess; crash recovery -> kill-and-restart at a failpoint; external-service mapping -> stateful verified fake; LLM instruction behavior -> behavioral eval. Work spanning several bug classes takes the tier per mechanism-component. At planning time the tier rule is a readiness check, never a deferral: acceptance criteria name both the observable oracle and the tier, and a plan whose mechanism is too unclear to pick a tier carries an unresolved design decision that must be resolved (research, a spike, a clarifying question) before the ticket is recorded.
- 'Trigger the mechanism, assert the contract': arrange conditions that force the mechanism through the smallest production path crossing the faulty seam; assert the public/contractual consequence, never mock call counts, private helpers, intermediate payloads, or source text.
- Minimum behavioral oracle: prove the fixture preconditions; assert an exact behavioral postcondition (not is-not-None / nonempty / no-exception); collateral invariants for stateful operations; a clean retry where the contract is atomicity/recoverability.
- Contrast case: default for input-class defects and stateful operations (nearest passing control / second representative input, parameterized where a family applies); justified omission allowed for trivially single-point bugs.
- Fault realism: the injected fault must occur inside the code whose recovery/cleanup is under test (fail the real second rename, not a top-level wrapper); race tests must synchronize with a barrier/pipe/marker/failpoint, never timing-only sleeps as the primary mechanism.
- Prove the test gates: the runner collects the node; it runs (not SKIP/XFAIL) in the supported CI environment; any temporary xfail is strict=True with a removal condition; the test runs under a gating CI command.
- Defect-seeded mutation: derive the mutation from the confirmed root cause (re-introduce the exact defect), not an arbitrary negation.
- LLM-surface evals: pinned model/settings, paired before/after prompts, multiple samples with a predeclared threshold and reported failure rates, plus a negative control — quantified rates, never one RED and one GREEN sample. One narrow carve-out: a single-sample RED/GREEN pair is acceptable ONLY when the assertion is deterministic under the pinned settings (e.g. schema/rule-based scoring at temperature 0) and the report states that determinism; cost or inconvenience is never grounds for skipping quantification.

Skill integration (each SKILL.md references `test-design.md` in its own directory, resolved by its committed byte-identical copy):
- `examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md`: Step 4 becomes 'Design and prove a RED oracle' — inventory first, contract card, tier rule, then RED with proven preconditions, loading the shared file at Phase 2 entry. Step 4's existing LLM-surface paragraph is updated to cite the shared file's quantified-eval requirements as the governing RED-artifact standard, superseding its current single-eval description. Step 5's mutation check becomes defect-seeded, and the fixer handoff list gains a fourth item — the frozen contract card (intended postcondition + invariants) — appended after 'confirmed root cause, evidence, original reproduction steps', while test fixture/assertions stay held out. `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md`'s Phase 2 (Repair) bullet — whose current wording defines RED as a single failing eval/behavioural assertion — is updated to cite `test-design.md`'s quantified-eval requirements (multiple samples, predeclared threshold, negative control) as the governing RED-artifact standard, so the two files cannot disagree.
- `examples/claude-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`: Phase 4a gains an explicit instruction sentence — before deriving the specification, work from `test-design.md` in this skill's directory for oracle design (coverage inventory, tier selection, oracle completeness, gating proof) — and Phase 4b's authoring text cites it for the oracle-minimum checks; the held-out structure (4c/4d/4e) is unchanged.
- `examples/claude-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md`: in the existing 'Before recording tickets, read the project's plan-review gate' section, add: before recording any ticket whose acceptance criteria will include or reference testing, verification, or behavioral oracles, read the shared file — when in doubt, read it (the cost is one file read; the benefit is correctly-shaped ACs that name the observable oracle).
- `examples/claude-skills/README.md`: document the shared/ + copies convention (canonical file, byte-identical copies, the sync one-liner, the gating drift test).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md` exists as a regular file and covers every bullet above (inventory, contract card, tier table + per-mechanism-component rule + planning-readiness (no tier deferral) rule, trigger/assert rule, oracle minimum, contrast default, fault realism, gating proof, defect-seeded mutation, LLM evals) with the scale-to-the-bug principle stated. Prove: `for t in 'RED oracle' 'contract card' 'tier' 'collateral' 'fault' 'gating' 'defect-seeded'; do grep -qi "$t" examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md || { echo "MISSING $t"; exit 1; }; done` plus a section-by-section read against the bullet list.
- [ ] For each of rebar-debug, rebar-implement, rebar-brainstorm: `examples/claude-skills/<skill>/test-design.md` is a regular file byte-identical to the canonical copy. Prove: `for s in rebar-debug rebar-implement rebar-brainstorm; do cmp examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md examples/claude-skills/$s/test-design.md; done` succeeds and `git ls-files -s examples/claude-skills | grep 120000` is empty.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` asserts byte-identity of every copy against the canonical file AND self-verifies its detection logic: a second test case builds a perturbed copy in `tmp_path` and asserts the same comparison detects the divergence (so the RED path is machine-verified on every CI run, not human-attested). Prove: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q` green, with both the identity case and the detection case collected.
- [ ] rebar-debug Step 4 is retitled to RED-oracle design. Prove: `grep -n '^## Step 4.*RED oracle' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` returns a match.
- [ ] rebar-debug Step 4's LLM-surface paragraph defers to the shared eval standard. Prove: `awk '/^## Step 4/,/^## Step 5/' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -q 'test-design.md' && awk '/^## Step 4/,/^## Step 5/' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -q 'LLM-surface'` (section-scoped, window-free).
- [ ] rebar-debug Step 5 hands the fixer the contract card as a fourth handoff item without exposing held-out test code. Prove: `awk '/^## Step 5/,/^## Step 6/' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -q 'contract card'` (section-scoped), and reading the handoff sentence confirms it enumerates root cause, evidence, reproduction steps, contract card — no test path/file.
- [ ] `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md`'s Phase 2 (Repair) bullet is QUALIFIED (not deleted or fully rephrased): it keeps its RED-artifact definition and adds a citation that quantification follows `test-design.md`. Prove: `awk '/Phase 2 \(Repair\)/,/^$/' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md | grep -q 'test-design.md'` (bullet-scoped).
- [ ] rebar-debug Step 5's mutation check is defect-seeded. Prove: `grep -n 'defect-seeded\|re-introduce' examples/claude-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` hits inside the mutation-check bullet.
- [ ] rebar-implement Phase 4a/4b cite the shared file inside those sections (content-level placement, not a footnote). Prove: `awk '/^### 4a/,/^### 4c/' examples/claude-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md | grep -q 'test-design.md'` succeeds and the cited sentence names the oracle-design duties (inventory, tier, oracle completeness, gating proof).
- [ ] rebar-brainstorm's 'Before recording tickets' section directs reading the shared file with the when-in-doubt trigger. Prove: `grep -n -C3 'test-design.md' examples/claude-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md` shows the hit inside that section.
- [ ] `examples/claude-skills/README.md` documents the convention — BOTH facts proven separately: `grep -q 'byte-identical' examples/claude-skills/README.md && grep -q 'cp examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md' examples/claude-skills/README.md`.
- [ ] No user-/machine-specific paths. Prove: `git grep -n '/Users/\|joeoakhart' -- examples/claude-skills tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` returns nothing.
- [ ] Style check, two parts. Deterministic: `! grep -nE '^(Bad|Wrong):' examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md` and `! grep -n 'do NOT assert' examples/claude-skills/shared/test-design.md` (no negative-example blocks or shouted negative enumerations in the shared file). Artifact: a comment on this ticket lists all six touched prompt files with a per-file affirmation of positive-first phrasing and short direct prohibitions; prove the comment exists via `rebar show 43c9-9aa5-290e-4900`.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass (the drift test gates via `make test`, CI's single source of truth; the targeted node `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q` is additionally run to show both its cases collected).

content.text: ## Summary

When a synced local ticket is archived or moved to status `deleted`, its bound Jira issue is left live (e.g. "To Do") indefinitely. The reconciler's outbound diff never sees these tickets, so no transition/close/unbind is ever emitted. Proven on REB-464/456/465/466/457 (bound to locally archived/deleted test tickets), all still "To Do" in Jira.
## Root Cause (two filter layers, an unintended gap)

- Layer 1 (archived): the reconciler builds its local snapshot via `rebar list --full` (`reconcile.py:455`) with no `--include-archived`; `reducer/_api.py:234` drops `archived=True`. Archived tickets never enter the diff.
- Layer 2 (deleted): deleted-status tickets survive the snapshot but are skipped in the differ loop (`outbound_differ.py:537-540`, `excluded_statuses={archived,deleted}`).

- Smoking gun: `outbound_fields.py:94` maps `"deleted" -> "Done"` (propagation is INTENDED) but the `:539` skip fires before that mapping runs (`:636`) — intended behaviour rendered dead code. `OutboundMutation` declares a `"delete"` action (`outbound_differ.py:245`) but nothing ever constructs one. Not a deliberate "never mutate Jira" policy: `closed -> Done` propagates normally.
- Runtime proof: `rebar list --full` returns 0 for the archived id vs 1 with `--include-archived`; a `reconcile --mode dry-run` (249 mutations over 606 issues) plans nothing for any of these keys.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Sync a local ticket to Jira (binding confirmed).
2. Archive it, or transition it to `deleted` locally.
3. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run`.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: local archival/deletion of a bound ticket drives its Jira issue to a terminal status (Done) and/or retires the binding, within one pass.
- Actual: no mutation is planned; the Jira issue is stranded live forever.
## Proposed design (perf-safe, binding-driven)

Drive terminal-transition detection from the BINDING STORE, not a full archived-ticket scan, so cost scales with the number of *synced* tickets (~606), never with the total number of archived tickets:
- Each pass compute `missing = bindings.keys() - active_snapshot_ids` (synced tickets that fell out of the active view = just archived/deleted). Cheap set-diff over ~606 bindings.
- For only those ids, do a targeted state read and emit the already-wired terminal transition (`deleted`/`archived -> Done`) via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` + `_diff_fields`.

- Idempotency: once Jira == Done the field-diff is empty (near-zero steady-state cost); optionally retire the binding after the terminal transition so it leaves the working set. Per-pass cost = O(newly-archived-since-last-pass), shrinking to zero — never O(all-archived). Do NOT switch the full snapshot to `--include-archived`.
- Unifies with the class-C binding GC (same binding-store iteration).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A locally archived or deleted ticket bound to a Jira issue drives that issue to a terminal Jira status (Done), or unbinds it, within one reconcile pass.
- [ ] Detection is bounded by #bindings / #newly-archived, not total archived-ticket count (no full `--include-archived` snapshot per pass); documented with a perf note/test.
- [ ] The dead `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS["deleted"]="Done"` mapping becomes reachable (or is replaced by an explicit terminal-transition path).
- [ ] A test binds a ticket, archives/deletes it locally, runs a pass, and asserts the Jira issue transitions to Done (RED before fix).
- [ ] The concrete drift (REB-464/456/465/466/457) reconciles after the fix.
## Notes

Discovered comparing Jira REB vs the local store. All current instances are "delete me" test tickets, but the mechanism affects any real archived (or closed-then-archived) ticket. `bridge_fsck` does not detect this (see the class-D ticket). Files: `outbound_differ.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `reconcile.py`, `reducer/_api.py`.
## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)
Approved policy: local archive/delete drives the Jira issue to a terminal status (Done). But:

- [ ] Drive the terminal transition from the per-binding BASELINE + binding-store walk, NOT from snapshot membership; act only on a CONFIRMED terminal/404 (grace-counted), never on snapshot-absence (L13/L16/L17).

- [ ] Close the bidir loop: add `archived` to the reverse status map AND the single-pass bidir suppression, so inbound reading Jira `Done` does not flip local `archived -> closed` (L21/L3; `inbound_translate.py:121`). Today `archived` maps nowhere on the reverse path.
- [ ] Gate the whole class behind the circuit breaker (refuse a pass that would terminal-transition/retire > N% of bindings) [prior art: Argo `allowEmpty`].
- [ ] Preserve `note_absent` grace + reversible retirement (L14/L15); a local-archive retirement must not corrupt the `absent_404_count` machinery.
- [ ] Unify with class C (13eb): one binding-store loop heals terminal transitions and GCs dead bindings.
- [ ] Parity is proven by the CONVERGENCE property (re-reconcile after the heal yields zero actions), not by an enumerated case.
## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)

DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): do NOT hand-roll a detection path. This bug is the `TERMINAL_TRANSITION` Decision cell of `classify()` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/classify.py) plus its apply handler.

1. Detection: the level-triggered binding-store walk (all_bindings()) classifies each bound pair; a pair whose LOCAL ticket is archived or status=deleted while ObservedJira=PRESENT with Jira status != Done yields `TERMINAL_TRANSITION`. Read the local ticket's true state with a targeted read (`rebar show`-equivalent library call), NOT by adding --include-archived to the snapshot (see the perf note: 120 archived tickets exist, only 6 are bound).

2. Apply: emit the already-mapped transition via `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` ("deleted"->"Done"; add "archived"->"Done") through the existing outbound mutation dispatch (typed_dispatch/apply_outbound) — construct a normal status-transition mutation; do NOT invent a new mutation type.

3. ADR 0029 #2 is a HARD PREREQUISITE in this ticket: add `archived` to the reverse status map (inbound_translate.py `_status_maps` region) so inbound Jira `Done` on a locally-archived ticket KEEPS local archived (never flips it to closed), and add the archived case to the L3 single-pass suppression map (inbound_differ.py). RED test first: archive locally -> 1 pass -> Jira Done -> next inbound pass -> local STILL archived; assert stability over 3 simulated passes.
4. Circuit breaker: TERMINAL_TRANSITION is an acting kind — it is automatically counted by check_blast_radius (foundation); no extra work beyond NOT bypassing the apply-path breaker.
5. Live acceptance cells: REB-464/456/465/466/457 (verified still 'To Do' on 2026-07-03) transition to Done; census on the following pass shows 0 acting for this class.

Files: classify.py (cell), outbound_fields.py (status map + reachability of the dead deleted->Done mapping), inbound_translate.py + inbound_differ.py (reverse map + L3), apply_outbound.py/typed_dispatch.py (handler), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + diffing/.

baseline.summary: Reconciler never propagates local archive/delete to the bound Jira issue (stranded live issues)

## Context / Problem
Ticket 699f replaced the per-test store build in `tests/interfaces/conftest.py` with a per-worker template that each test copies. Its acceptance criterion read: "The template fixture asserts it is virgin (no tickets, no `<repo>/.rebar/`)."

The landed change (Gerrit 1063, merged) satisfies only HALF of that. `_rebar_repo_template` asserts `not (repo / ".rebar").exists()` but never asserts the template carries no tickets. The no-tickets half is checked only by a separate test, `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_template_stays_virgin`. The completion verifier caught this and correctly refused to close 699f.

Why this matters rather than being a wording nit: the invariant is that the template must NEVER be pre-seeded. Several tests in the tier assert on emptiness (session-log counts in `tests/interfaces/queries/test_recent_session_logs.py` and `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_session_log_capture.py`) and hold only because nothing seeds the template. The obvious next optimisation -- pre-warming the template with tickets so tests skip setup -- would silently invert those assertions.

A fixture-level assertion fails at CONSTRUCTION, once per worker, before any test runs, and covers every consumer. A test-level assertion fires only when that one test is selected, so a narrowed run such as `pytest tests/interfaces/store` has no protection at all. Closing that gap is the reason to fix this properly rather than argue the criterion into compliance.

## Approach
Add the missing assertion to `_rebar_repo_template` in `tests/interfaces/conftest.py`, immediately after `rebar.init_repo()` and the root commit, INSIDE the existing `pytest.MonkeyPatch.context()` block. It must sit inside that block because the assertion needs `REBAR_ROOT` and cwd pinned at the template; the context exits before the current post-build assertions run, which is why the existing `.rebar` check is a plain filesystem test.

Keep the existing `.rebar` assertion where it is: it needs no environment and reads more clearly beside the other post-build checks.

Rejected alternative: leave the check in `test_template_stays_virgin` only and record evidence on 699f to satisfy the verifier. The criterion would then read as met while the narrowed-run gap above stays open. That is gaming the gate, not meeting it.

Rejected alternative: assert at the filesystem level (no ticket directories under `.tickets-tracker`) to avoid needing the pinned environment. That works, but it duplicates knowledge of the store layout that `rebar.list_tickets()` already owns, and would miss a ticket recorded anywhere the layout check does not look.

## Scope
- `tests/interfaces/conftest.py` -- one assertion inside the template fixture's MonkeyPatch context.

`test_template_stays_virgin` STAYS. It is not made redundant: it also asserts `.rebar` absence from a test context and documents the invariant where a reader of the sentinel file will look for it. This ticket adds enforcement at construction; it does not move the existing check.

## Testing
No new behavior -- this adds an assertion to existing test infrastructure, so no new test is warranted.

The assertion must be shown to be load-bearing rather than decorative: seed a ticket into the template right after the build, confirm the fixture raises, then remove the seed and confirm the tier passes. That is a temporary local check; the durable evidence is the tier passing with the assertion in place.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_rebar_repo_template` in `tests/interfaces/conftest.py` asserts the freshly built template has no tickets, inside the MonkeyPatch context where REBAR_ROOT and cwd are pinned.
- [ ] The existing `.rebar` absence assertion is retained.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_template_stays_virgin` is retained and passes.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/interfaces -q` passes with the same collected/passed counts as before this change.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
baseline.summary: Assert template has no tickets inside the fixture, not only in a test

baseline.description:
## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow fails in production on a recurring basis — **22 failed runs between 2026-07-23T20:29Z and 2026-07-30T22:14Z** — and **7 of those failures landed AFTER the most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix**, including two in the very `refs/reconciler/lock` subsystem that fix repaired.

Individual failures are self-healing (a later scheduled run succeeds), which is why they have never been ticketed: the heartbeat canary only files a ticket when staleness exceeds its 2h threshold (it did so once, `4b5c`). The remaining failures are invisible.

## Timing investigation vs commit history

**Most recent reconciler-bridge bug fix:** `7c763f1a7` — *"a4b2: prune an orphaned local pass-lock ref"*, authored 2026-07-27 23:20:41 -0700 = **2026-07-28T06:20:41Z**. Ticket `a4b2` (*Stranded local refs/reconciler/lock wedges every local reconcile pass permanently*) is a **bug** and its fix is specifically about the pass-lock ref lifecycle.

Every later commit touching `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` is J-series Jira Data Center *story* work (`62d9`, `0a94`, `aac8`, `9fd4`), not a bug fix. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge*.yml` has no commit since `5623a2496` (`0e15`, 2026-07-19); `src/rebar/_store/push.py` / `sync.py` have none since `27e1165cd` (2026-07-17).

**Failures after that fix (7):**

| When (UTC) | Run | Failing step |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29T15:27:11Z | 30465914822 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T00:45:55Z | 30503669644 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T03:06:34Z | 30510284129 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T05:02:44Z | 30515516036 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |
| 2026-07-30T19:46:26Z | 30576272914 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T20:29:25Z | 30579382013 | Run reconciler |
| 2026-07-30T22:03:07Z | 30585738860 | Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets |

**Rate before vs after the fix** (same workflow, contiguous windows):

```
PRE-FIX  2026-07-23T20:29 -> 2026-07-28T06:20 : 955 runs, 815 success,  15 failure, 124 cancelled  (1.57% fail)
POST-FIX 2026-07-28T06:20 -> 2026-07-30T22:14 : 549 runs, 460 success,   7 failure,  81 cancelled  (1.28% fail)
```

The failure rate is essentially unchanged, and the lock/lease failure mode recurs after a lock-specific fix. `a4b2` addressed a *local* stranded ref wedging local passes; it did not address CI-side lease loss under contention. **This bug is therefore NOT a regression of `a4b2` and not a claim that `a4b2` is wrong — it is the residual, separate problem `a4b2` did not cover.**

## Three distinct failure modes observed post-fix

**(1) Pass-lock lease lost mid-pass** — 2 runs (30576272914, 30579382013):

```
ref-lock renew: refs/reconciler/lock CAS rejected — lease lost/stolen
  (held 52b2181c53bacdfc7c6d4623afbd5d5ec6f6b0ff)
ERROR: reconcile heartbeat lost the lease (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting pass
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: pass lock lease lost mid-pass (pass_id='2026-07-30T19-50-55') — aborting
```

Aborting on lease loss is correct-by-design (`2711`: "heartbeat loses lease mid-pass -> pass aborts, no double-run"), but the abort surfaces as a hard workflow failure (exit 1) rather than a benign skip.

**(2) Push to `origin/tickets` rejected after 5 retries** — 4 runs:

```
Push rejected (attempt 4):
 ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have
Push failed after 5 retries. Last stderr: ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Concurrent writers keep advancing `origin/tickets` faster than the retry budget.

**(3) Unhandled `HTTP Error 404` from the reconcile pass** — 1 run (30465914822, 2026-07-29T15:34:55Z):

```
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
```

Preceded in the same run by repeated (non-fatal) warnings:

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records: _apply_inbound_update: rebar.link failed for
  761e-5af2-ed57-408a -> 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 (blocks): RebarError('rebar link failed (exit 1):
  Error: ERROR: redundant link — ... are in a direct parent-child relationship')
```

A bare 404 escaping as an unhandled exception is the least explained of the three and may be a genuine gap rather than contention.

## Adjacent signal: cancellation volume

124 pre-fix + 81 post-fix runs were **cancelled** (~15% of all runs), consistent with heavy schedule/dispatch overlap. High overlap is the plausible common driver behind both mode (1) and mode (2), so it is included here as evidence rather than as a separate ticket.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** contention between overlapping reconciler runs is absorbed
  (backoff, longer retry budget, or a clean no-op exit), so a run that loses a
  race does not turn the workflow red; genuinely unhandled errors (mode 3) fail
  loudly and distinguishably.
- **Actual:** ~1.3% of runs fail, in three different ways that are
  indistinguishable at the workflow level, none individually tracked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three modes is classified as either *benign contention*
      (should exit non-red / be absorbed) or *a real fault* (should stay red),
      with the decision recorded.
- [ ] Mode (1): losing the pass lock to a legitimate concurrent holder no longer
      produces a red run; a genuine lock fault still does.
- [ ] Mode (2): the `origin/tickets` push either succeeds under normal
      contention (adequate retry/backoff, or fetch-rebase-retry) or exits
      non-red when it has provably lost a benign race.
- [ ] Mode (3): the `HTTP Error 404` path is root-caused and either handled with
      a specific error or reported with enough context to identify the
      failing request.
- [x] Post-fix verification. The `>= 500 runs` population gate originally written
      here is **WAIVED by operator decision (2026-07-31)**: at ~215 Reconcile Bridge
      runs/day it is wall-clock-bound at ~2.3 days, and it adds no evidence about the
      MECHANISM beyond what the oracles already prove. Replaced by, and satisfied by:
      (a) each fixed mode proven RED-first against an oracle held out from the
          implementing agent, then mutation-checked by re-seeding the exact defect —
          mode 1 returns `assert 1 == 75`, mode 3's create/delete 404 escapes again;
      (b) the post-fix sample that actually exists at close, recorded plainly:
          **7 Reconcile Bridge runs** since the fix landed (6 success, 1 cancelled,
          0 failures). Seven runs is a small sample and is explicitly NOT claimed as
          proof the failure has stopped — it is on the record so the number is stated
          rather than implied. Sustained-absence evidence, if wanted, needs the
          wall-clock this waiver declines to spend.
- [ ] Cancellation rate is either explained as expected or reduced.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (pass lock / reconcile_once error
      handling).

## Investigation provenance

Found during a cross-source audit of AWS, Gerrit and GitHub Actions logs for errors not tracked as bugs (2026-07-30). Run inventory: 2,598 Actions runs over 2026-07-23 → 2026-07-30 pulled via the Actions API; failure classification from per-job step conclusions and job logs.
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge fails ~1.3% of runs in three modes (lock-lease loss, tickets push rejected, unhandled 404) — 7 recurrences after the a4b2 pass-lock fix

baseline.description:
## Why

The concurrency contract promises compaction is recoverable if the process dies after
the snapshot is written and partway through source retirement. Existing tests only
monkeypatch Python exceptions (which still run `except`/cleanup code) or construct
orphan states by hand — none kill an actual compactor process. `SIGKILL` runs none of
the rollback, lock-release, cache-cleanup, or git-staging code, so the real
process-death durability contract (including lock reclamation and a dirty tracker
worktree left between snapshot write and commit) is unproven.

## What

- Add a deterministic subprocess test that kills a real `rebar compact` process
  mid-retirement and verifies recovery from a fresh CLI process.
- Use a test-only failpoint / filesystem barrier to pause after the first source
  rename, rather than a timing-based race window.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` (new process-death test)
- Possibly a small test-only failpoint hook in `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`
  (guarded so it is inert in production).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test seeds foldable events, launches `rebar compact` in a subprocess, pauses after
      the first source rename via a barrier, and `SIGKILL`s it.
- [ ] From a fresh CLI process: the write lock is recoverable, the ticket reads at its
      exact pre-crash semantic state, no source UUID is lost, `fsck` returns the
      documented clean/repairable result, and re-running compaction is idempotent or
      performs the documented repair (after which `fsck` is clean).
- [ ] The test is deterministic (no reliance on a narrow timing window).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Add real compactor process-death (SIGKILL) recovery test

content.text: ## Why

Multi-backend reconcilers (ticket systems beyond Jira) are planned. Today the Jira/Atlassian assumption is threaded across ~24 reconciler files with no vendor-adapter seam, and the 55-module reconciler is a flat namespace. These are one design problem: the sub-package boundary IS the vendor-adapter seam. (O5 + S5 — verified; combined per maintainer.)

Citations: O5 — Jira coupling across `_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (`acli*`, `adf.py`, `jira_fields.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, differ/apply cluster; `outbound_fields.py` touched 2026-07-06 for one status mapping). S5 — 55 flat `.py` files, no sub-packaging.
## What

DESIGN/ADR FIRST (do this now): author an ADR mapping (a) the Jira-coupled modules, (b) the operations that must become vendor-neutral (issue CRUD, field mapping via outbound_fields/adf, the acli transport), (c) the target sub-package layout separating a backend-neutral core (differs/apply/dispatch/store) from an `adapters/jira/` vendor layer, and (d) the interface a second backend would implement. THEN execute the sub-packaging around that seam, preserving import paths. Do NOT build a speculative full adapter abstraction ahead of the ADR — the ADR decides the seam.
## Scope

Reconciler structure + vendor seam. Sequence the code move AFTER the reconciler function-extraction and git-adapter tickets so modules move once. This is the enabler for the future second-backend initiative.
## Plan-review remediation — preservation mechanism + phased execution
The naive "package `__init__` re-exports" mechanism is insufficient for two verified reasons; both are addressed by a **loader-safe, patch-safe, phased** execution:

1. **Module-qualified attribute access (e.g. `acli_subprocess._run_acli`, patched module-qualified in tests).** A package `__init__` re-export exposes a *symbol* but not the old *module path*, and re-exporting into a shim module creates a patch-binding pitfall (a test patching the old path would not affect the canonical module's binding). Therefore, per moved module, ALL references are migrated to the new canonical path in the same change — internal importers, every test patch target, and any `importlib`/string-qualified reference — so there is exactly one binding site. A module whose reference/patch surface is too broad to migrate safely in this change is NOT moved in Phase 1; it is inventoried in the ADR for Phase 2.

2. **The file-location dynamic loader (`_loader.lazy_load` / `__main__._load_sibling_keyed`) resolves siblings by `_PACKAGE_DIR / filename`.** It loads only backend-neutral machinery (`mode.py`, `_advisory_lock.py`, `_ref_lock.py`, `mutation.py`, `_errors.py`), which STAY at the package root in Phase 1, so the loader is untouched and unbroken. The Jira vendor modules (`acli*`, `adf.py`, `jira_fields.py`, `outbound_fields.py`) are imported normally (not dynamically loaded), so relocating them cannot break the loader. Any Phase-2 relocation of a dynamically-loaded module must also update the loader to discover the new sub-package dir.

**Phase 1 (this change):** author the ADR; create the `adapters/jira/` vendor package; physically relocate the vendor modules that can be migrated safely (all refs updated, full suite green); update `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` + `.github/module-size-ceilings.txt` PATHS for any moved over-cap file. **Phase 2 (follow-up ticket, linked `discovered_from`):** relocate the remaining vendor + core modules per the ADR layout, updating the loader and the broad test-reference surface, and retire any transitional shims.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR authored: Jira-coupling inventory + vendor-neutral operation list + target sub-package layout + second-backend interface sketch (design done NOW)

- [ ] `adapters/jira/` vendor package established as the seam; the safe subset of vendor modules relocated there, with import paths preserved (all internal/test/dynamic references resolve; full suite green)
- [ ] Module-size allowlist + ceilings PATHS updated for any relocated over-cap file
- [ ] Adding a second backend is documented in the ADR as "implement `adapters/<name>/` against the seam"
- [ ] Remaining full-reorg scope captured as a Phase-2 follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from`

baseline.summary: Reconciler vendor-adapter seam: ADR + sub-packaging for multi-backend (O5+S5)

## Why

The author-facing guides are the ONLY place the SC/AC split was ever described as a real
distinction — `rebar explain plan` currently tells container authors they need
`## Success Criteria` on top of the universal `## Acceptance Criteria` floor. That prose is the
source of the divergence this epic removes; leaving it in place after the gates change would
instruct authors to write a heading nothing reads.

## What

Rewrite the author guide and user docs for the collapsed vocabulary, including the leaf/container
section rule that motivated the split.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:58,76` — the leaf-vs-container section rule
  ("Container ... needs `## Success Criteria`" and "Containers additionally: `## Success
  Criteria` + the child decomposition"). Both must be restated so containers are described by
  what actually differs: they still need `## Acceptance Criteria`, plus a child decomposition
  that COVERS it (G3), and they defer testing to children.
- `docs/user-guide.md:219,230`
- `docs/llm-framework.md:407`

## Approach

Rewrite rather than substitute. A literal rename of line 58 would read "Container needs
`## Acceptance Criteria`", which is true of every ticket and so says nothing — the container
guidance has to be re-expressed as the decomposition/coverage requirement. This is the one place
in the epic where the edit is editorial rather than mechanical.

Note the guide is packaged and surfaced by `rebar explain plan`, so it is a shipped artifact,
not just documentation.

## Testing

- `rebar explain plan` renders the updated guide with no SC vocabulary.
- `pytest tests -k "guide or explain"` green.
- Manual read-through that the container guidance still tells an author what containers need
  DIFFERENTLY from leaves (coverage + decomposition), i.e. the section did not become vacuous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/_guides/ docs/user-guide.md docs/llm-framework.md` returns no matches.
- [ ] `rebar explain plan` exits 0 and its output contains no SC vocabulary.
- [ ] The guide's leaf-vs-container section still states a container-specific requirement
      (child decomposition covering the parent's acceptance criteria, testing deferred to
      children) rather than collapsing to "containers need Acceptance Criteria".
- [ ] `make lint` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Rewrite author guide and user docs for the collapsed criteria vocabulary

baseline.description:
## Context

Bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events breaks the event store's append-only union invariant. Independently valid stale clones can then produce delete/modify conflicts instead of reconverging without history loss.

Gerrit change 989, commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d, removed queue and digest pruning and added a real two-clone regression proving both histories survive and merge cleanly. That was the required correctness and recovery fix.

Removing pruning creates a deliberate long-term retention problem. Each successful enrichment cycle normally appends ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST events; retries or claim races can append more. At the 2026-07-27 measurement, the live tickets tree contained 1,198 such files totaling about 1.23 MB: roughly 5.5% of tracker files and 0.5% of tracker bytes.

Queue reduction reads accumulated per-ticket event history, pending-work discovery scans every ticket directory, and latest-digest lookup enumerates the ticket directory. Without retention, live file/inode counts and these O(history) scans grow linearly, increasing clone, checkout, index, merge-tree, and operational costs. The former deletion scheme bounded only the live tree; deleted blobs remained in earlier Git history, so it never truly bounded repository storage.

Existing follow-up task 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d records the initial retention design work. This epic preserves the broader architectural context and is intentionally out of scope for the current session.

## Long-term objective

Design and land merge-safe retention, compaction, or archival semantics that bound hot/live tracker cost while preserving cross-clone convergence, crash recovery, auditability, and every independently committed event or a lossless compacted representation. Physical deletion or rename of committed UUID events is not an acceptable solution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current queue and digest growth rates and read/clone/index costs are measured with deterministic benchmarks.
- [ ] The chosen design bounds hot/live event lookup and working-tree growth without rewriting or deleting independently committed UUID events.
- [ ] Real two-clone stale-history tests prove independent retention operations reconverge cleanly and preserve all logical state.
- [ ] Crash recovery, claim leasing, latest-digest selection, auditability, and migration/rollback behavior are documented and tested.
- [ ] Operational rollout includes monitoring and a safe migration for existing unbounded histories.
- [ ] The relationship between live-tree retention and Git object/history storage is documented so the design does not claim storage reclamation it does not provide.

## Related evidence

- Closed root-cause bug: 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282
- Existing retention-design task: 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d
- Correctness fix: Gerrit change 989 / commit be8a0c059571b340cd7705191769a4a64998643d
baseline.summary: Bound tracker growth without deleting committed event history

baseline.description:
# `binding_store.py` is at 787/800 — extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

Raised by the operator while reviewing change 1296 (ticket 88d9): "We're adding a lot to binding_store.py. Should we split that out to preemptively avoid the 800 LOC cap?" Measured rather than estimated: the file was **749** LOC, 1296 takes it to **787**, and the cap is **800**. Thirteen lines of headroom, and the CI module-size gate fails the build when ANY `src/rebar` file exceeds the cap — so the next contributor to touch this file breaks the build, having added nothing wrong.

Deliberately NOT done inside 1296: that change is a data-loss fix that needed to land promptly, and bundling a structural refactor into it would have made it slower to review and harder to reason about. The docstrings added there were tightened instead (795 -> 787) to buy immediate headroom.

## The seam, which already exists

`binding_store.py` holds two distinct concerns:

1. **binding lifecycle** — bind / confirm / unbind, absence + rekey handling, GC/retire grace, the
   immutable numeric Jira id (bug 7c26). This is the bulk of the file.
2. **last-synced PEER STATE** — the ADR-0026 three-way-merge baseline (`get_baseline`, `set_baseline`,
   `seed_baselines_from_snapshot`, `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) plus the peer-parent evidence channel added by
   1296 (`get_peer_parent`, `set_peer_parent`). Together ~130 LOC with docstrings — comfortably over
   the policy's 100-LOC floor for a new module, and a genuine cohesive concern: "what did the peer
   look like the last time we successfully looked".

Concern 2 has its own ADR, its own absence semantics ("an ABSENT baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins"), and its own advance site in the pass (`reconcile._advance_baselines` / `_advance_peer_parent`). Its consumers are `outbound_field_diff`, `binding_walk` and now `inbound_fields` — none of which touch binding lifecycle.

## What makes this non-trivial, stated honestly

These are METHODS on `BindingStore`, not free functions, so this is not a file move. Extraction means either module-level helpers taking the entry dict (the store keeps thin delegating methods, so no caller changes) or a mixin. The first is preferable — it keeps the public surface identical, so every existing call site and every test double stays valid, and it makes the peer-state functions directly unit-testable without constructing a store.

Per the module-size policy this must be split ALONG THE SEAM ABOVE and not mechanically to hit a number, and the new module must not fall under 100 LOC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `binding_store.py` is under 700 LOC, and the new module is over 100
- [ ] `BindingStore`'s public surface is UNCHANGED — no call site and no test double is edited to
      accommodate the split, asserted by the fact that the reconciler suites pass untouched
- [ ] the peer-state functions are directly unit-testable without constructing a `BindingStore`, and
      at least one new test does so (otherwise the extraction bought nothing)
- [ ] `_BASELINE_FIELDS` moves WITH the cluster, and `outbound_field_diff` / `binding_walk` /
      `inbound_fields` still resolve their reads (a grep-backed consumer list recorded on this ticket)
- [ ] the absence semantics survive the move verbatim: absent baseline degrades to local-wins, absent
      peer parent degrades to NO CLEAR. A test pins each, because these are the properties that make
      the cluster safe and a refactor is exactly when they get quietly dropped
- [ ] the module-size gate passes, and the full reconciler unit + integration suites pass
baseline.summary: binding_store.py is at 787/800: extract the last-synced-peer-state cluster

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Automated bug filers can spam duplicates, file on single flakes, or silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces). The audit surface is the THREE existing filers — no new filer is built; this ticket HARDENS what exists and documents the contract for future filers: the heartbeat-alert filer (scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:197) and the binding-drift-alert filer (cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:350) — canary_bridge.py has exactly these two create sites, verified by inventory —, plus `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:135, called at :522), which today files one bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup key, no template contract, and no empty-detail abort.

## Approach
Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager 'for:'): dedup via a stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day; templated body (check name, first-red time, run URL, failing-output tail, workflow path) with abort-if-empty-detail; recovery comment on green with close left to agents is documented in the CONTRACT as the default for future filers whose bugs carry investigation value; it is NOT retrofitted anywhere in this ticket. The two canary_bridge filers ALREADY auto-close their alert ticket on green via `rebar transition open closed --force-close` (cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:247-262, cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:398-410) — that existing recovery contract is KEPT AS-IS (pure state alerts, nothing to investigate once green); the audit records this divergence and its rationale in the table rather than retrofitting agent-close onto them. Pattern elements apply per-site by SEMANTIC FIT, recorded in the audit table: the N>=2 consecutive-red threshold applies only where a derivable red/green run signal exists: the HEARTBEAT filer only — its stale check fails the canary run (the 'Fail job on stale' step), so the workflow's previous run conclusion carries the signal. The BINDING-DRIFT filer gets NO threshold, with rationale recorded: its oracle never fails the run (conclusion carries no drift signal), and drift is PERSISTENT state, not a flake — it cannot self-heal between runs, so first-observation filing is correct and dedup + daily accumulation already bound spam; the conflict filer has no cycle semantics, so it gets dedup (stable tag derived from the conflict identity: local id + jira key), template, abort-if-empty, and detected_by — not the threshold. CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE: no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state. On red, the filer queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion (gh api repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs?status=completed&per_page=2, excluding the current run); previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red, no ticket. Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path regardless of threshold. ACCUMULATION DEDUP ('max one accumulation comment/day'): derived from the target ticket's OWN comment history — the accumulation comment opens with a stable marker line; the filer reads the ticket (rebar show --output json), finds the newest marker-bearing comment, and skips if it is <24h old. The ticket store IS the durable state; no new store, and the */20 cron cannot spam. First-red time in the template = the previous red run's timestamp. WORKFLOW THREADING (scope): the consuming alert steps in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml today pass only STALE/RUN_URL/DRIFT_* env; the heartbeat alert step's run-history query additionally needs GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (already used by other steps in that workflow), the repo (github.repository), and the workflow file id (the literal filename) threaded as step env — enumerated as workflow edits in scope, heartbeat step only. The contract doc records the same recipe for future filers with run-conclusion signals. LIFECYCLE: green with no open tagged ticket (single flake that never crossed the threshold) => recovery path no-ops on the empty has-tag search — stated as an invariant and unit-tested. USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit the fitting pattern elements; (b) document the bug-creation contract for automation — exact rebar create args, exit codes, dedup search command, REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create.

## Scope
- canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py `_file_conflict_bug_ticket`: dedup tag + template + abort-if-empty + detected_by (no threshold — no red/green cycle)
- docs: bug-creation contract page
- audit table of every auto-file site in the change description, with a per-site row: which pattern elements apply and why

## Testing
Heartbeat-filer unit tests: first red -> no ticket; second consecutive red -> one ticket with template fields; third red same day -> accumulation comment, not a new ticket; second accumulation within 24h -> skipped (marker-line dedup); green with open ticket -> existing auto-close path preserved (transition open closed --force-close, unchanged); green with NO open ticket -> no-op, exit 0; empty detail -> abort with loud log, no hollow ticket; previous-run query failure -> treated as first red (fail toward not filing, loud log). Binding-drift tests: first observed drift -> one ticket (no threshold, rationale in table); repeat drift -> accumulation not duplicate; green -> existing auto-close preserved. Conflict-filer tests: same conflict twice -> one ticket + one accumulation comment; distinct conflicts -> distinct tickets; empty conflict detail -> abort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All three audited auto-file sites use the fitting dedup+template pattern elements (audit table enumerates sites x elements with rationale, including the kept auto-close divergence and the binding-drift no-threshold rationale).
- [x] Heartbeat consecutive-red threshold implemented via workflow run-history query; no new state store introduced; single flake files nothing.
- [x] Bug-creation contract documented and referenced by every filer.
- [x] Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above, including the green-with-no-ticket no-op and the query-failure arm.
- [x] detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).
baseline.summary: Auto-bug-filer hardening: dedup pattern, all-site audit, contract doc

content.text: ## Summary
rebar's LLM runner inherits `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the environment, so when a local
Claude-Code payload-optimizing proxy (headroom, `http://127.0.0.1:8787`) is enabled, ALL
of rebar's agentic LLM calls are routed through it. That proxy corrupts rebar's **agentic
tool-loop** requests (Pass-2 plan-review verifier, completion-verifier), producing an empty
provider stream. The empty stream surfaces as `UnexpectedModelBehavior("Streamed response
ended without content or tool calls")`, is caught at `runner.py:333` as a terminal
`LLMUnavailableError` (no retry), and fail-closes the plan-review verdict to INDETERMINATE —
which writes no attestation, so **every code-grounded ticket becomes un-claimable**.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable headroom (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`).
2. `rebar review-plan <code-grounded-epic>` (e.g. ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f).
3. Observe `coverage.verify_failed=True`, `coverage.metrics.verify_requests=0`,
`coverage.verify_error` = "Streamed response ended without content or tool calls",
verdict INDETERMINATE.
Expected: verify completes; verdict PASS/BLOCK on the plan's merits.
Actual: verify makes 0 requests; verdict INDETERMINATE; claim refused ("attestation stale").
Discriminating proof: `env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL rebar review-plan <same>` → verify_requests=20,
verify_error=None, verdict PASS. Single-turn and simple/large tool-use streams pass through
headroom fine; only the multi-turn agentic tool-LOOP breaks. RTK (bash hook) is not involved.
## Fix
rebar's internal agent must not route through a local (loopback) Claude-Code payload optimizer.
When the resolved model is Anthropic and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a loopback host, build the
Anthropic model with a provider pinned to the direct public API (bypassing the local proxy).
Respect non-loopback gateways (untouched). Opt out with `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set to a loopback host, rebar's runner builds an Anthropic model
whose provider base_url is the direct public API (`https://api.anthropic.com`), not the loopback.
- [ ] A non-loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (a real gateway) is respected (passed through unchanged).
- [ ] `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY=1` opts back in (no bypass) for users who intend the local proxy.
- [ ] Non-Anthropic providers and the test model_override path are unaffected.
- [ ] Unit test covers loopback-bypass / non-loopback-passthrough / opt-out; existing runner tests pass.
- [ ] Replication: with headroom running, `rebar review-plan ac1b-cef3-35c8-415f` yields a determinate
verdict (verify_requests>0), not INDETERMINATE.

baseline.summary: runner routes agentic LLM calls through local headroom proxy -> empty stream -> INDETERMINATE

content.text: ## Why
The floor must key on VERIFIED delivery, never bare `closed` status — otherwise a force-closed or
abandoned child would launder un-validated work past scrutiny, and a stale closed ticket can hard-
block the epic review (observed in practice).
## What
Add a `delivered_now(child, epic, repo_root)` helper (in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`,

reusing the `compute_validity(sig, child_state, 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read check used INSIDE `_child_closure_findings` in `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` — note that fn is a DEFICIT detector (returns findings for children LACKING delivery), so we reuse its validity CALL applied to children whose status IS closed, NOT the fn itself) that returns True iff
the child is `closed` AND holds a completion-verifier attestation that is VALID on read
(`compute_validity(..., "completion-verifier")` — so drift-stale / force-closed / unsigned all read
false), OR child B is superseded by a SIBLING A (same parent; direction B superseded_by A) that is itself a live vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress, not force-closed/abandoned) (read the
`supersedes`/`duplicates` links via `src/rebar/__init__.py`; verify shared parent so work that left
the epic does not count as delivered). Recomputed each run. In-progress / abandoned / force-closed
children return False -> stay in scope.
## Scope
- IN: the `delivered_now` predicate + its sibling-supersede check + validity-on-read reuse.
- OUT: the Pass-3 wiring (separate story); the Pass-2 sub-call (separate story).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `delivered_now` is True for a closed child with a VALID completion attestation; False for force-closed, unsigned, drift-stale, in-progress, and abandoned children.

- [ ] `delivered_now` treats B as delivered-elsewhere ONLY when a SIBLING A (same parent) supersedes B (direction: B superseded_by A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR active open/in_progress); False when A is not a sibling or is itself force-closed/abandoned (closes the supersede-direction + replacement-not-done gap).

- [ ] The predicate reuses the `compute_validity(..., 'completion-verifier')` validity-on-read call (NOT the deficit-detector `_child_closure_findings` itself), applied to closed children, and is recomputed per run (no persisted state).
- [ ] Unit tests cover attested / force-closed / drift-stale / supersede-sibling / supersede-nonsibling / in-progress cases.
## Supersede mechanism (concrete artifact)
The supersede relationship is the structured `supersedes` LINK RELATION (one of rebar's six link
relations) — an auditable, event-sourced graph edge in the ticket's deps, NOT a free-text note,
tag, or naming convention. `delivered_now` reads it via `rebar.show`/`ticket_deps`: child B is
delivered-elsewhere iff a SIBLING A (same `parent_id`) has an `A supersedes B` edge (equivalently B
`superseded_by` A) AND A is a live in-epic vehicle (delivered-now OR open/in_progress). Because the
edge is a structured graph relation (not unsigned prose) AND the superseding sibling A stays in
review scope, this is NOT the unsigned/gameable suppression the Alternatives reject: no coverage is
removed (A is still reviewed), and the security/contract preserve-set (T5c/T10) is never dropped
regardless of supersede — so a manipulated edge cannot launder a security finding.
## Acceptance Criteria (mechanism)
- [ ] The supersede signal is the structured `supersedes` link relation read from the child's deps (named artifact), not a note/tag/convention.
- [ ] A test asserts the security/contract preserve-set is never dropped even when a supersede edge is present (no laundering).
## Acceptance Criteria (reopen semantics)

- [ ] A PARENT epic reopen does NOT un-deliver its closed children: ADR 0009 keys on each ticket's OWN `last_reopened_at`, so only a CHILD's own reopen invalidates that child's completion attestation. Closed children remain `delivered-now` across a parent reopen; a reopened child flips to not-delivered and its findings resurface.

baseline.summary: delivered-now predicate: reuse completion attestation (validity-on-read) + in-epic sibling supersede
