baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
When a ticket's acceptance criteria stop matching reality, the completion-verification close
gate blocks the close and there is no obvious sanctioned way forward. Agents reach for
`--force-close` (which closes WITHOUT verification, leaving an uncertified ticket) or for
`--ref <old-commit>` (which verifies against the tree where the criteria still held).

**Decision (2026-07-24): both of those are the WRONG answer for stale criteria.**

Closing against criteria that no longer describe the work leaves inaccurate state in the
ticket system. The ticket permanently claims something that is not true of the codebase — and
the ticket store is the shared, durable record other agents read. A close that "passed" by
pointing at an old commit is a close whose criteria still lie.

**The correct path is: EDIT the ticket so its criteria are accurate, re-pass the plan-review
gate, then close against the corrected criteria.** The criteria end up true, the close is
genuinely verified, and the record is accurate.

This ticket is therefore a DOCUMENTATION fix, not a feature. It was originally scoped toward
building an auditable "criterion disposition" record (moot / invalidated / superseded) with
cited evidence and provenance. That is deliberately REJECTED as overbuilt for a single bug
report: it adds a whole audited sub-system to avoid an edit that authors should be making
anyway.

## Worked example (the case that prompted this)
`86a5-9221-0037-4e38`'s criteria grepped `docs/passing-code-review.md`. A later commit
(c2bfbe217) moved that guide into the package, leaving the old path a stub — so the criteria
became false. It was closed with `--ref f90850861`, the commit where the work landed, which
PASSED verification but left the ticket asserting a file check that no longer holds. Under this
decision the right move was to edit the criteria to name
`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, re-pass plan review, and close.

## Out of scope (explicitly not building)
- An auditable criterion-disposition record (moot / invalidated-by-fix / superseded).
- An automation-owned closure path for bot-filed alert tickets.
- Any change to `--force-close`, which remains the escape hatch for a human operator's
  judgment call and correctly leaves the ticket unsigned.

## Known related gap (NOT fixed here)
Closing an epic whose plan review predates a criteria-registry change is blocked by the
plan-review close gate's `stale-regver` check, forcing a full billable re-review of an
already-executed plan. Hit twice on 2026-07-24 (86a5 and 58f2). Recorded here so it is not
lost; it needs its own ticket if it keeps costing.

## Scope
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — a short subsection under the completion close gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states that when acceptance criteria no longer match reality
      the fix is to EDIT the ticket, re-pass plan review, then close against the corrected
      criteria; verified by
      `grep -q 'criteria no longer match' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The same passage says explicitly that closing against stale criteria — whether via
      `--force-close` or by pointing `--ref` at an older commit — leaves inaccurate state in
      the ticket system and is not the remedy; verified by
      `grep -q 'inaccurate state' docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] The addition is SHORT (a single subsection, not a new document or a new mechanism).
- [ ] `make lint` and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier has no legitimate close path when acceptance criteria are invalidated by the fix or are auto-generated/unverifiable

baseline.description:
# Re-architect the DC transport along CAPABILITY seams, so it stops needing rescue splits

## Why now (operator-approved as a separate change)

`transport.py` is at **799/800**. The next parent-related change cannot land. This is the fourth time in one day the file has forced prose-trimming to fit: 756 → 780 (1302) → 794 → 781 (1305) → 799 (1311 + 9bb9). Each rescue bought a few lines and none addressed why growth keeps landing here.

## The diagnosis: the previous splits were REACTIVE, so they did not change where code goes

Two extractions already happened, both under cap pressure, both along whatever seam was nearest:

    retry.py        258 LOC   retry policy + error translation   (story S1 of b586)
    transitions.py  166 LOC   transition resolution + routing
    transport.py    799 LOC   EVERYTHING ELSE

`transport.py` re-exports the extracted names as a facade, so from a caller's view nothing moved. Critically, **neither split gave a NEW operation an obvious home**. A new capability still has exactly one plausible destination — the god file — so the file re-grows to the cap and the cycle repeats. b586's own lesson (S1 mechanical relocation passed plan review FIRST TRY where the combined ticket took ten rounds) was about splitting *a change*; it did not fix the module's shape.

## The insight: the right seam ALREADY EXISTS and is not being used

`_backend.py` defines the capability Protocols this class implements — `TicketTransport`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe`. Those ARE the module's natural boundaries, and the class already satisfies them. The file is organised by nothing; the contract is organised by capability. Aligning the two means every future operation has a determined home: *"which capability is this?"* answers *"which file does it go in?"*

## Proposed architecture — capability mixins composed by a thin transport

Reading the current method inventory, the clusters are clean and already disjoint:

    _base.py        ~120   shared plumbing: __init__, _client, _unwrap, _call_logged,
                           _user_attr, _paged_search  (the mixins' common substrate)
    _issues.py      ~180   create_issue, get_issue, get_issue_by_rest, update_issue,
                           delete_issue, search_issues
    _hierarchy.py   ~150   set_parent, _resolve_epic_link_field_id, get_parent_map
                           <- where 39c1 / 9bb9 / future parent work LANDS
    _links.py       ~120   set_relationship, get_issue_links, get_issuelinks_map,
                           delete_issue_link
    _comments.py    ~100   add_comment, get_comments, get_comment_map
    _people.py      ~130   _assign, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists
    _properties.py  ~110   _put_property, set_issue_property, set_entity_property
    transport.py    ~150   the composition root: class JiraDataCenterTransport(...mixins),
                           build_client_from_settings, _jira_client_class, __all__ facade
    (retry.py, transitions.py unchanged)

Every unit lands in the **200–500 target band or just under**, and none is a sub-100-LOC fragment — the two failure modes the module-size policy names.

**`JiraDataCenterTransport` remains ONE class**, composed from mixins, so `isinstance` against the Protocols, `assert_transport_conforms`, and every caller and test keep working with no edit. That is what makes this a *mechanical relocation* rather than a redesign — and, per b586's evidence, what makes it reviewable in one pass.

## Why mixins rather than delegation or free functions

Delegation (`self._issues.create_issue(...)`) would change the call shape at every site and break Protocol conformance. Free functions taking a client would lose the shared cache (`_epic_link_field_id`) and the `_call_logged` wrapper. Mixins keep one object, one cache, one `self`, and move only the *text*. The cost is that mypy needs the shared attributes declared on a base — hence `_base.py` rather than bare mixins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] behaviour is UNCHANGED: this is a relocation. No test assertion is edited, and the full
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` suite (2105 at time of filing) passes untouched
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport` remains a single class satisfying the same Protocols —
      `assert_transport_conforms` and the shape contract `tests/_jira_shape_contract.py` pass unedited
- [ ] the `transport.<name>` facade still resolves for every currently re-exported name, so
      `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` and friends pass UNEDITED (the reason `__all__` exists)
- [ ] every resulting module is between 100 and 500 LOC; none exceeds the 800 cap
- [ ] `_resolve_epic_link_field_id` has exactly ONE definition after the move — the duplication
      9bb9 deliberately avoided must not be reintroduced by the split
- [ ] a short note in the package docstring states the organising principle (one module per
      capability Protocol) so the NEXT operation has a determined home rather than defaulting here
- [ ] done as its own change, landing BEFORE further parent work, per the operator's approval

## Explicitly out of scope

Changing any behaviour, touching `retry.py`/`transitions.py`, or altering the Protocols themselves.
baseline.summary: Re-architect the DC transport along capability seams to stop chronic cap-driven splits

## Why
The reconcile-bridge outage (bug 8002-a92f-0999-45dd) was an *unparseable* workflow:
`f2bde8d3b5` put `${{ runner.temp }}` in a job-level `env:` of `reconcile-bridge.yml` (and
its canary) — a GitHub Actions startup failure (0 jobs) that stopped Jira sync for ~2 days.
**CI never caught it** because `make lint` (the gate the Gerrit `Verified` vote runs) scopes
actionlint to `release.yml` ONLY (`Makefile`, `RELEASE_WORKFLOW`; comment line 101: "Scoped
to release.yml — NOT repo-wide"). Every other workflow — including the bridge + canary — is
unvalidated, so an invalid-workflow change merges green and silently disables the workflow.

## What
Widen the CI **actionlint** coverage in `make lint` from `release.yml` to **all**
`.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}`, so a parse-error / bad-context change is blocked at the
`Verified` gate. Cost is zero today: `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml
.github/workflows/*.yaml` already exits 0 with 0 findings (post-8002-fix). **zizmor stays
scoped to `release.yml`** — widening the security audit is a separate concern, out of scope.

## Scope
- `Makefile` lint target: invoke actionlint over ALL workflows (actionlint auto-discovers
  `.github/workflows` when given no path arg), keeping `zizmor $(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)` unchanged
  and preserving the macOS-skip + pinned-binary install logic. Update the actionlint-scope
  comments (lines ~19, 97, 101, 107, 115) that say "release.yml only"/"NOT repo-wide" so they
  describe the widened actionlint scope (noting zizmor remains release.yml-scoped).
- `docs/releasing.md:129`: correct "zizmor + actionlint scoped to `release.yml`" →
  "zizmor scoped to `release.yml`; actionlint covers all workflows".
- `tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_scope.py` (new): assert the Makefile lint recipe runs
  actionlint over all workflows (not `$(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)`-only), guarding a silent re-narrow.

## How it is guarded (accurate — corrects the prior plan)
Both `gerrit-verify.yaml:303` (pre-merge Verified) and `test.yml:55` (post-merge branch CI)
run `make lint`, so widening the Makefile target covers both legs automatically; a
reintroduced bad workflow fails that `make lint` step. NOTE: the existing
`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` only asserts both legs invoke the *string* `make lint`
— it does NOT verify actionlint's scope, so it is NOT the guard for this change. The new
`test_ci_actionlint_scope.py` is that guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make lint` runs actionlint against every `.github/workflows/*.yml`/`*.yaml`, not just
  `release.yml`. Proof: `sed -n '/^lint:/,/^actionlint-bin:/p' Makefile` shows the actionlint
  invocation is not restricted to `$(RELEASE_WORKFLOW)`.
- [ ] `make lint` passes on the current tree. Proof: `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] Reintroducing a `${{ runner.temp }}` job-level env into any workflow makes `make lint`
  FAIL for the runner-context reason. Proof: add the line, run `make lint` → non-zero exit
  citing `runner`, then `git checkout` to revert.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the Makefile actionlints all workflows and fails if re-scoped
  to `release.yml` only. Proof: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_ci_actionlint_scope.py -q`.
- [ ] No stale "actionlint scoped to release.yml" wording remains. Proof:
  `grep -rniE 'actionlint[^.]*scoped to .?release\.yml|actionlint[^.]*release\.yml only' Makefile docs/`
  returns nothing (accurate zizmor-scoped references may remain).
baseline.summary: Harden CI: extend actionlint coverage to ALL workflows (not just release.yml) — the gap that let the reconcile-bridge startup failure merge

## Why

The enriched sidecars (stories 4e19/7c84/e7e0) and the existing attestations are reachable today
only via scattered internal helpers; there is no single call that returns a ticket's FULL retained
review history or resolves its associated code reviews. The follow-on audit UI epic and any script
need one documented read surface.

## What

A read layer that, for a ticket id, returns: (a) the full retained history (not just latest) of
plan-review sidecars; (b) the completion attestation plus any completion sidecar record; (c) the
associated code reviews, resolved via the ticket's inbound `relates_to` links from `code_review`
tickets, each with its full sidecar history. Exposed as a library function, a CLI command, and a
read-only MCP tool.

## Data contract (the returned typed dict)

`audit_trail(ticket_id)` returns a `TypedDict` with EXACT key names and nullability:

```python
class CompletionRecord(TypedDict):
    attestation: dict | None   # the ticket's completion-verifier attestation (from show/keyring); None if unsigned
    sidecar: dict | None       # the latest completion sidecar record — a PASS (completion_verifier_pass_v1)
                               # or FAIL (completion_verifier_fail_v1) record; None if no sidecar event

class AuditTrail(TypedDict):
    ticket: dict                    # the ticket's current details (from rebar.show)
    plan_reviews: list[dict]        # full retained plan-review sidecar history, newest-first; [] if none
    completion: CompletionRecord | None  # None ONLY when BOTH attestation AND sidecar are absent
    code_reviews: list[dict]        # each: {ticket_id, sidecars: list[dict]} — a linked code_review
                                    # ticket + its own newest-first sidecar history; [] if none
```

- `plan_reviews` is ALWAYS a list (empty `[]` when the ticket has no plan-review sidecars), newest first.
- `completion` is a `CompletionRecord` dict when EITHER a completion-verifier attestation OR a
  completion sidecar record exists; it is `None` ONLY when BOTH are absent. The two sub-fields come
  from two DISJOINT sources (the attestation lives on the ticket; the sidecar is a `COMPLETION_VERDICT`
  event), so each is independently nullable inside the record.
- `code_reviews` is ALWAYS a list (empty `[]` when no `code_review` ticket links to this ticket via
  `relates_to`); each entry carries its OWN sidecar history list.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` and `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — add
  `all_review_results(ticket)` history enumerators (walk the ticket's `REVIEW_RESULT` events
  newest→oldest, schema-tolerant, returning the list of payload dicts; `[]` on missing/error),
  complementing the existing `latest_*` readers.
- `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` — the completion sidecar reader for the `completion.sidecar`
  field: reuse `latest_pass_record` (PASS) and `latest_fail_verdict` (FAIL) — the aggregator returns
  whichever is newest/present (no new reader needed unless a "latest of either kind" helper is
  cleaner; if added, keep it schema-tolerant over both `completion_verifier_pass_v1` and `_fail_v1`).
- New `src/rebar/audit/read.py` — an `audit_trail(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None)` aggregator composing
  the plan / completion / code-review histories, resolving code reviews via the ticket's inbound
  `relates_to` links from `code_review` tickets (reusing `rebar.show` / `rebar.list_tickets`),
  returning the `AuditTrail` typed dict above. Also add `__init__.py` for the new `rebar.audit`
  package.
- CLI registration (owns-its-own-`--help` intercept pattern used by `_workflow`/`_llm`/`_criteria`):
  - add an `audit` intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py::main`, dispatching to an
    `audit_cli(rest)` handler in a new `src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py` (parses
    `show <ticket> [--output json]` and prints the `AuditTrail`).
  - **create `src/rebar/_cli/help/audit.txt`** (the usage text for `rebar audit show`). This is what
    makes `audit` a recognized subcommand: `known_subcommands()` is NOT a hardcoded set — it is
    DERIVED from the `.txt` files under `src/rebar/_cli/help/` (every `<name>.txt` except
    `overview.txt`). So adding the help file registers the subcommand; do NOT edit `known_subcommands`.
- MCP read-tool registration: add a read-only `audit_trail(ticket_id)` tool inside
  `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py::register_read_tools` (decorated with `@mcp.tool(annotations=_ANN
  ["READ_ONLY"])`, like the other read tools), so it is available even under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`.

## Approach rationale

A single aggregator over the existing readers + the existing `relates_to` links reuses the linkage
the reviewbot already writes (`emit_code_review_artifact` links each code-review artifact
`relates_to` its work ticket), so no new linking mechanism is introduced — the read layer only
traverses links that already exist. The MCP tool is read-only so it is available regardless of
`REBAR_MCP_READONLY`.

## Compatibility & rollback

Pure addition (new readers + new command + new read-only tool); no existing behavior changes.
Schema-tolerant readers accept both v1 and v2 records. Reverting removes the new surface (delete
`rebar.audit`, `_audit_commands.py`, `help/audit.txt`, the intercept, the MCP tool, the
`all_review_results` readers) with no data impact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `audit_trail(ticket_id)` returns a dict with EXACTLY the keys `ticket`, `plan_reviews`,
      `completion`, `code_reviews`; `plan_reviews` and `code_reviews` are lists (newest-first,
      `[]` when none), `completion` is `CompletionRecord | None` (`None` only when both attestation
      and sidecar are absent). Oracle: an integration test seeding a ticket with multiple plan-review
      sidecars, a completion record, and a `relates_to`-linked `code_review` ticket with its own
      sidecar, then asserting the exact key set, the newest-first ordering of `plan_reviews`, that
      `completion` is a dict, and that `code_reviews[0]` carries its own sidecar history; plus a
      companion assertion that a bare ticket yields `plan_reviews == []`, `completion is None`,
      `code_reviews == []`.
- [ ] `rebar audit show <ticket> --output json` prints the same structure. Oracle: a CLI subprocess
      test asserting on the emitted JSON's key set.
- [ ] The MCP `audit_trail` tool returns the structure and is read-only (available even with
      `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1`). Oracle: a test invoking the tool handler under that env.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: audit read layer (full-history readers + relates_to resolution + CLI/MCP)

# Generalize the example skills: rename claude-skills -> agent-skills and de-brand

## Why

The example skills already use the SKILL.md format, which is now a cross-provider OPEN standard
(Anthropic's Agent Skills, adopted by Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, JetBrains Junie, and
more) — so the format is the right portable bet and should be KEPT. What is Claude-locked is the
packaging: the directory name `examples/claude-skills/`, the README's "Claude Code" branding and
docs.claude.com link, some Claude-Code-specific phrasing ("the Task tool"), and internal
references to `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md`. Generalizing these makes the examples usable as
illustrative material for any harness.

## What

Rename `examples/claude-skills/` → `examples/agent-skills/`. Update the README to de-brand:
state that SKILL.md is a cross-provider standard, note which harnesses read skills and from
where (paths differ per tool), and drop the Claude-only framing. Generalize Claude-Code-specific
orchestration phrasing to provider-neutral wording ("subagent" is fine; replace "the Task tool"
and similar). Repoint internal references from `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md` to `AGENTS.md`.
Update the shared/ sync test (`tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py`) and any code/docs that
reference the old path, so `make test` stays green. Keep each SKILL.md's `name`/`description`
frontmatter (the portable core).

## Scope

In: `examples/agent-skills/**`, `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py`, and any references to
the old dir path. Out: rewriting the skills' substantive logic. Depends on: the AGENTS.md story
(so the `CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md` reference repoint targets the real new file).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Directory renamed to `examples/agent-skills/`; no stale path references remain.
  - Proving: `rg -l 'examples/claude-skills' . | wc -l` == 0.
- [ ] README de-branded: no "Claude Code"-only framing; states SKILL.md portability and where
  each harness looks for skills.
  - Proving: reviewer confirms; `rg -c 'Claude Code' examples/agent-skills/README.md` reduced to
    only accurate, non-exclusive mentions.
- [ ] Skill bodies use provider-neutral phrasing and reference `AGENTS.md` (not `CLAUDE.md`).
  - Proving: `rg -c 'the Task tool|CLAUDE\.local\.md' examples/agent-skills/` == 0.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass (shared-sync test updated to the new path).

## De-risking results (exact rename surface)

Renaming `examples/claude-skills` → `examples/agent-skills` is low-risk and CI-safe. Exact
surface confirmed by sweep: `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` (`SKILLS_DIR` line 25 +
docstring lines 3, 9-10) and `examples/claude-skills/README.md:44` (the cp example).
**No `.github/workflows` reference** — nothing in CI depends on the path. Skill-body `CLAUDE.md`
references to repoint to `AGENTS.md`: `rebar-implement/SKILL.md` and
`rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md`. SKILL.md is confirmed as the cross-provider open standard
(keep the format). The provider-neutral phrasing sweep still applies (drop "the Task tool", etc.).
baseline.summary: Generalize the example skills: rename claude-skills -> agent-skills and de-brand

baseline.description:
## Context
A work ticket carries a single attestation slot (`state["signature"]`), written
last-writer-wins by `process_signature` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`). The
plan-review attestation (claim time) and the completion verdict (close time) share that
slot, so closing destroys the plan-review attestation (bug grumpy-site-beard /
e6a0-ba9b-ae92-43d7). The two are independent proofs and must coexist; we also expect
further attestation kinds and per-ticket CI-gate consumption later.

## What
Add `state["attestations"]`, a map keyed by attestation kind (per-key LWW, mirroring
`process_workflow_run`): additive across kinds, latest within a kind. Kind is derived from
the already-signed `manifest[0]` (`plan-review` / `completion-verifier`), so no
`PAYLOAD_VERSION` bump and existing signatures still verify. Reuse the `SIGNATURE` event
(add an unsigned `data["kind"]` ONLY as a routing hint). Attestations are immutable signed
records; validity for a gate is computed on read via one
`compute_validity(attestation, ticket_state, kind)` dispatcher.

## Kind identity + routing
- The SIGNED `manifest[0]` is AUTHORITATIVE for kind. Parse: the substring before the first
  ":" (e.g. "plan-review: PASS" -> "plan-review").
- `data["kind"]` is only a hint; `process_signature` uses it ONLY if it equals the
  manifest-derived kind, else ignores it (never trust the unsigned envelope over the signed
  manifest). A SIGNATURE event whose manifest is empty/unkindable (e.g. a legacy retired
  blank event) is ignored for routing (cannot key it) — its staleness is now handled by
  validity-on-read, not by clobbering.

## Compiled-state shape + the legacy mirror
- `process_signature` writes BOTH `state["attestations"][kind] = record` AND keeps
  `state["signature"]` as a LIVE mirror of the MOST-RECENT attestation (last SIGNATURE
  event wins the mirror), in live compiled state — not only in SNAPSHOT output.
- Why the live mirror: four existing consumers read `state.get("signature")` directly
  (`signing.verify_signature`, the close-gate path, `fsck`/validate, and the
  soon-removed `retire_attested_pin`); the live mirror means they keep working unchanged
  while `attestations` is wired up, AND it makes the SNAPSHOT/rollback mirror automatic
  (compiled_state already carries `signature`). The record shape is unchanged
  (manifest, algorithm, signature, key_id, head_sha, signed_at, author).
- 114f owns the canonical per-record shape; 2c2d/cc1b/ed26 reference it.

## Migration (expand only; contract deferred) + rollback
- Events keep the UNCHANGED `SIGNATURE` shape (plus the optional hint `data["kind"]`),
  so old code replays them fine.
- Read fold-in: an OLD SNAPSHOT whose `compiled_state` carries only `signature` (no
  `attestations`) is folded into `attestations` on restore (kind from its manifest).
  Raw post-snapshot SIGNATURE events replay normally into the map.
- New SNAPSHOTs carry BOTH `attestations` and the `signature` mirror automatically (the
  reducer maintains the mirror), so a rolled-back / not-yet-upgraded clone still reads one
  attestation. ROLLBACK is therefore safe at any time.
- The "contract" phase (dropping the mirror) is OUT OF SCOPE here; tracked by follow-up
  352b-5097-9971-4dc1, gated on an all-clones-upgraded readiness check.

## Verification surface
- `verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review")` ALWAYS returns a SINGLE verdict dict;
  `verify_signature_result.schema.json` is UNCHANGED. `kind` defaults to `"plan-review"`,
  so every existing library/MCP/CLI caller that omits a kind keeps single-verdict
  back-compat. Internally it reads `state["attestations"][kind]`, falling back to the
  legacy `state["signature"]` when the map is absent.
- The verify-ALL map is a SEPARATE entry-point `verify_attestations(ticket_id) ->
  {kind: verdict}` (NOT a new return shape of `verify_signature`).
- CLI: `verify-signature <t> --kind K` = single-gate exit code (0 iff certified);
  `verify-signature <t>` (no `--kind`) = human-readable listing via `verify_attestations`
  (exit 0 iff all certified). MCP `verify_signature` stays single (kind defaults to
  plan-review); the full per-kind set is surfaced via `show`/ticket-state (ed26) — no MCP
  schema break.
- Callers migrated to pass an explicit kind: `claim_gate_check`, `drift_refresh_candidate`,
  `refresh_attestation` (attest.py) -> `plan-review`; `_child_closure_findings`
  (completion.py) -> `completion-verifier`.

## Validity model (computed on read; records never mutated)
- `compute_validity(attestation, ticket_state, kind)` centralizes per-kind rules; the
  MATERIAL-CHANGE field set reuses the EXISTING plan-review material fingerprint
  (`orchestrator.material_fingerprint`: description/AC/file_impact/children) as the single
  source — no new separately-owned constant. "Computed on read" means NOT stored/mutated;
  it MAY do I/O (plan-review still performs its filesystem code-drift re-hash).
- DATA SOURCE for "not reopened since": the reducer records `state["last_reopened_at"]` =
  the timestamp of the most recent `closed -> open` transition (detected in `process_status`
  from the pre-update status == "closed" and target == "open"); null if never reopened.
  `compute_validity` checks `signed_at >= last_reopened_at` (or null) purely from compiled
  state.
- completion-verifier valid iff: certified AND status=="closed" AND not-reopened-since AND
  material-fingerprint-unchanged-since `signed_at` (the completion signer records the
  material fingerprint in its manifest, symmetric with plan-review).
- plan-review valid iff: existing freshness (material + filesystem code drift) AND
  not-reopened-since.
- `retire_attested_pin` (the blank-`SIGNATURE`-on-reopen mutation, signing.py) is REMOVED
  with its reopen call (transition.py); reopen invalidation is validity-on-read for both
  kinds. No lifecycle transition mutates any attestation record.

## Presentation (no secret leak)
- `public_state()` (`_present.py`) gets a DEDICATED `attestations` branch (the flat
  `_INTERNAL_SUBKEYS` cannot express a wildcard kind level): if `out["attestations"]` is a
  dict, replace with `{kind: {k:v for k,v in rec.items() if k != "signature"} for kind, rec
  in out["attestations"].items() if isinstance(rec, dict)}`. The legacy single-`signature`
  one-level hex strip is retained. This is the canonical strip path for all present/future
  kinds.

## Validation
- Manual dogfood smoke-test: create a ticket, sign a plan-review PASS, sign a
  completion-verifier PASS, `rebar show` shows BOTH kinds (neither overwriting the other,
  no hex); reopen and confirm both read not-valid; `rebar verify-signature --kind K` per
  kind.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `state["attestations"]` (kind-keyed, per-key LWW) added; `process_signature` writes
      `attestations[kind]` AND maintains the live `state["signature"]` most-recent mirror;
      routing uses authoritative `manifest[0]` (data["kind"] only as a validated hint).
- [ ] Signed canonical payload unchanged; every pre-existing signature still certifies.
- [ ] Old-snapshot read fold-in (`signature` -> `attestations`); new SNAPSHOTs carry both
      `attestations` and the mirror; contract deferred to 352b.
- [ ] Reducer records `state["last_reopened_at"]` (most recent closed->open; null if never).
- [ ] `compute_validity(attestation, ticket_state, kind)` centralizes per-kind validity,
      reusing the existing material fingerprint; completion = certified AND closed AND
      not-reopened-since AND material-unchanged-since; plan-review = existing freshness AND
      not-reopened-since.
- [ ] `retire_attested_pin` removed; no transition mutates any attestation record.
- [ ] `verify_signature(ticket_id, kind="plan-review")` returns a single verdict (schema
      unchanged, back-compat default); `verify_attestations(ticket_id)` returns
      `{kind: verdict}`; CLI no-`--kind` lists all (exit 0 iff all certified); claim gate
      reads `plan-review`, close + child-closure read `completion-verifier`.
- [ ] `public_state()` dedicated `attestations` branch strips the `signature` subkey from
      every per-kind record (no hex in show/MCP for any kind); legacy strip retained.
- [ ] `show`/MCP render the `attestations` map (omitted when empty).
- [ ] Tests: coexistence; within-kind replace; compaction round-trip; legacy + new-snapshot
      cross-read; reopen invalidates completion + plan-review validity without mutation;
      material-change invalidates completion; concurrent different-kind signs both survive;
      no HMAC hex in public output.
- [ ] A ticket simultaneously holds plan-review AND completion attestations; signing one never
- [ ] Compaction/SNAPSHOT round-trips all kinds; legacy single-signature tickets and old-clone
- [ ] A reopened ticket stops reading as completion-valid AND plan-review-valid (via
- [ ] No HMAC hex appears in `show`/MCP output for any attestation kind.
## compute_validity contract (pinned)
`compute_validity(attestation, ticket_state, kind, *, repo_root=None) -> {"valid": bool,
"reason": str}`. It ASSUMES the attestation record is already HMAC-certified (the caller
runs `verify_signature` first); compute_validity adds ONLY the lifecycle/freshness layer on
top (per-kind: completion = closed AND not-reopened-since AND material-unchanged-since;
plan-review = material + filesystem code-drift AND not-reopened-since). `reason` is a
human-readable explanation when `valid` is False (empty/"certified ..." when True).
Consumers: `claim_gate_check` (plan-review), the close gate + `_child_closure_findings`
(completion-verifier) call it and branch on `.valid`.
## Acceptance Criteria (compute_validity)

## Context

Bug 8185 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events makes independently valid stale-clone histories conflict. The immediate repair restores append-only union merges by stopping those deletes. The tradeoff is unbounded per-ticket event accumulation and O(history) queue/digest scans.

## Plan

- Measure queue and digest read/gate cost against realistic repeated-enrichment histories.
- Design retention that preserves cross-clone union convergence and recovery invariants, using merge-safe compaction or an equivalent append-only representation rather than physical deletion.
- Prove the design with real two-clone stale-history tests and performance coverage before changing production behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A benchmark or deterministic performance test quantifies current per-ticket scan growth.
- [ ] The chosen retention design preserves every independently committed event or its lossless compacted representation across stale-clone merges.
- [ ] Real two-clone coverage proves clean reconvergence when retention runs independently in both clones.
- [ ] Queue and latest-digest reads have a documented and tested bound.
- [ ] The design introduces no physical delete/rename conflict for committed UUID events.
baseline.summary: Design merge-safe retention for enrichment queue and digest history

## Status: NOT A BUG — report withdrawn

This ticket was filed on a wrong root-cause analysis. Investigation under /rebar-debug proved the reported defect does not exist. No code change was made and none is warranted. The original claim and its proposed fix plan are withdrawn in full; the sections below record what was actually established, so the ticket stays useful as a negative result.

## Original claim (WITHDRAWN)

That `rebar link-audit --repair` can never run because `_reconciler_in_flight` (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:227`) fails closed on a `ModuleNotFoundError` for `rebar_reconciler`, and that `fsck --repair` is affected identically.

## Why it was wrong

I grepped for the import line, observed that the same import raises `ModuleNotFoundError` in a bare interpreter, and concluded the probe could never read the lock. I never read the four lines immediately above it, which already do exactly what I was proposing to add:

```
from rebar._engine import engine_dir
eng = str(engine_dir())
if eng not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, eng)  # so the top-level rebar_reconciler package resolves
from rebar_reconciler import _advisory_lock as advisory
```

The function resolves the engine directory before importing. Re-tested exactly as the function does it: `engine_dir()` resolves and exists, the import succeeds, and `check_pass_lock` returns a real answer. I asserted a mechanism from a partial read instead of observing it run.

## What was actually proven

Sampled `refs/reconciler/lock` every 10s for two minutes. The blob was byte-identical across all 12 samples — same oid `6e5b4468`, heartbeat frozen at `1785386477382441825` (04:41:17), `lease_secs` 120. A frozen heartbeat means the holder was not renewing, so the lease expired at 04:43:17.

Discriminating experiment, run at lease age 220s:

- H1 — `check_pass_lock` honors lease expiry → predicted `False`.
- H2 — it returns `True` whenever the ref exists, so a stale lock blocks repair forever → predicted `True`.

Result: `check_pass_lock` returned `False`. **H1 confirmed, H2 rejected.**

The guard is correct in both directions: it reports held while the lease is live and free once it expires. Every earlier refusal coincided with a genuinely live lease — the first attempt hit one at 117s of a 120s lease. There is no live-lock, no stale-holder defect, and no always-held condition. The correct action was to wait out the reconciler pass, which is precisely what the guard exists to enforce.

`defect_legitimacy`: **intended-behavior**. Authoritative source: the function's own documented fail-closed contract at `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py:227-234`, whose behaviour the experiment matched exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The reported defect is disproven by a discriminating runtime experiment, with the result recorded on this ticket; verified by the H1/H2 experiment above.
- [x] No code change is made and no fix is landed, per the not-a-bug guard; verified by this ticket recording no file impact and no referencing commit.
- [x] The withdrawn claim about `fsck --repair` is retracted in writing; verified by the "Original claim (WITHDRAWN)" section above.

## Follow-up (not this ticket)

`_reconciler_in_flight` has no test coverage — `grep -rn _reconciler_in_flight tests/` returns nothing. That is a genuine coverage gap but not a defect, and not what this ticket claimed.
baseline.summary: link-audit --repair can never run: the reconciler in-flight probe fails closed on ImportError

baseline.description:
## Problem
The `rebar-brainstorm` skill (examples/agent-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md) tells the
author to run the plan-review gate on *each* ticket immediately after creating them, before
any dependency links exist and regardless of blocked state. This contradicts the actual gate
behavior documented in AGENTS.md / docs/plan-review-gate.md: `rebar review-plan` fast-fails
with no LLM (unsigned INDETERMINATE, exit 2) on a ticket that is not yet claimable — one still
`open` but blocked by an unclosed dependency — and reviews are dependency-scoped so they must
run in dependency order (prerequisites/children before dependents), never in parallel.

## Approach
Rewrite the "Before recording tickets, read the project's plan-review gate" section of
rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md so that, after creating tickets, the author FIRST establishes the
dependency graph between children (link via blocks/depends_on), then runs plan-review ONLY on
unblocked tickets (identified by `rebar ready`), in dependency order, reviewing later tickets
as their dependencies close and they become unblocked. Include a fallback: if `rebar ready`
returns an empty set, the graph likely has a cycle/authoring error — inspect and resolve before
proceeding. Rationale: authoring to the real gate protocol avoids a guaranteed no-LLM
fast-fail and matches AGENTS.md's dependency-order review rule; it is far cheaper than
discovering the exit-2 at review time.

Also assess rebar-implement/SKILL.md: it is an executor of an already-decomposed epic and
already claims/reviews only the unblocked, dependency-ordered set via `rebar ready`/
`next-batch`, treating the dependency graph as a precondition — so it needs no change. This
assessment is part of the ticket's scope (documented outcome: no edit, rationale recorded).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md's plan-review section states plan-review is run only on
  unblocked tickets, after the child dependency graph (blocks/depends_on links) is established,
  in dependency order — verified by reading the edited section (grep shows "unblocked" and
  "dependency order" in the section).
- [ ] The section references the no-LLM fast-fail (exit 2 / INDETERMINATE) on still-blocked
  tickets and names `rebar ready` for identifying the unblocked set — verified by reading the
  section.
- [ ] The section specifies a fallback for when `rebar ready` returns an empty set (diagnose
  the dependency graph for a cycle/authoring error and resolve before proceeding) — verified by
  reading the section.
- [ ] rebar-implement/SKILL.md is left byte-for-byte unchanged (verified by
  `git diff --stat origin/main -- examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md` showing no
  change), and the no-edit assessment rationale is recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Change lands on main through Gerrit — proven by recording the Gerrit
  change number and the LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1 vote outcomes as a comment on this ticket
  before close.
baseline.summary: rebar-brainstorm: run plan-review only on unblocked tickets after dependency graph is established

content.text: ## Why

Tier C of the bash->Python strangler-fig (story adult-oxide-slave, docs/bash-migration.md §5). Tier B retired the leaf writes; Tier C ports the compute-heavy read-side bash that orchestrates the reducer/graph with formatting on top. These are read-only over replayed state, so no write-path risk — the parity surface is ORDERING and FORMATTING determinism.
## What

Port behind REBAR_COMPUTE (kill-switch already in rebar._switch): next-batch (ticket-next-batch.sh ~954 LOC, conflict-aware file-impact scheduling), validate (validate-issues.sh ~945, repo-wide health + finding buckets), list-epics (ticket-list-epics.sh ~453). Riders at the same shape: list-descendants, summary, clarity-check/check-ac/quality-check. Reuse the Tier A read plumbing (in-process replay, freshness, --no-sync) + rebar.reducer/rebar.graph.
## Scope

Read-side compute only. Known parity traps (pin with golden matrices): bash sort vs Python sorted (locale/stability), jq number/escape formatting vs json.dumps, validate finding bucketing/severity order, next-batch batch composition over crafted file-impact overlaps (agents' parallel dispatch depends on this determinism). Each command spawns a child; its bash suite is the characterization gate, dual-run byte-identical before the default flips.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] REBAR_COMPUTE wired at dispatcher + library/MCP; default bash until parity+soak
- [ ] next-batch, validate, list-epics ported to rebar._reads/_commands, reusing reducer/graph
- [ ] Golden ordering/formatting matrices pin the parity traps (sort/locale, jq vs json.dumps, validate buckets, next-batch composition)

content.text: ## Why
The model emits no holistic severity/confidence anywhere in the decision path; the decision is deterministic
code.
## What
- Cited-reference veto (ONLY when a code citation is present) -> a UNIFIED PRIORITY SCORE computed DETERMINISTICALLY
from the Pass-2 sub-answers. FORMULA (v1 default — per the epic's Pass-3 spec; the attribute weights are
calibration-tunable): validity ∈ [0,1] = graded fraction of the binary sub-answers (yes=1 / insufficient=.5 /
no=0); impact ∈ [0,1] = the deterministic mean of the five Pass-2 severity attributes, each ordinal mapped to
[0,1] (prod/debt_impact max; blast_radius; likelihood; reversibility); PRIORITY = validity × impact ∈ [0,1]
(both LLM-judged spectrums, so a low-validity/high-impact finding can outrank a high-validity/low-impact one).
decision = DROP if validity < .5; else BLOCK iff (not cited-reference-vetoed) AND priority ≥ the criterion's
`block_threshold` (default 0.95, criterion opted into blocking); else ADVISORY.
- ADVISORY SURFACING CAP: the surfaced advisory findings are the top-N by priority score, N = a CONFIG value
(default 10, owned by `55de`); advisory overflow beyond N -> `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (recorded, not surfaced).
BLOCKING findings are EXEMPT from the cap: never dropped; if blocking count > N, ALL blocking findings are
returned. The cap can never suppress a block.

- Pass-3's SURVIVING (advisory, not-dropped) findings feed the Pass-4 affirmative coach `75a9` (crusty-herb-stand), which primes the caller with a next move per finding and NEVER alters this pass's decision.
## Scope
- Pure code (no LLM). Defaults advisory-only in v1 (only the DET floor blocks); per-criterion blocking is
opt-in; thresholds project-overridable and start high.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Deterministic veto -> confidence -> severity -> decision; no model holistic severity/confidence in the path.
- [ ] Advisory-only default; per-criterion blocking opt-in; thresholds configurable.
- [ ] Unified priority score (deterministic: validity + impact combined) drives block-threshold + advisory ranking; no model holistic score in the path.
- [ ] Advisory surfacing cap = config top-N (default 10, owned by `55de`); overflow advisory -> sidecar; BLOCKING never capped (ALL blocking returned even if > N); cap is config-driven + tunable.
- [ ] Unit-tested aggregation (veto, confidence, severity buckets, decision).

baseline.summary: Pass-3 deterministic aggregator

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`models_at_or_above` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:319-327`) locates the ladder START rung by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names (`sizing.py:99-103`) against the primary model. A primary from any other family matches nothing, falls through to the `return list(names)` fallback at `sizing.py:327`, and the caller receives the WHOLE ladder from the trivial rung. `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) has the same shape and returns `MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]` at `sizing.py:146`.

Reproduced on this tree (HEAD `1052bc856f`, no model override, no class table):

    models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')
      -> ['claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-8']
    largest_window_tokens('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')
      -> 1000000

Contrast, a correctly located primary on the same tree:

    models_at_or_above('anthropic:claude-opus-4-8')                 -> ['claude-opus-4-8']
    models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0') -> ['claude-opus-4-8']

Two distinct harms:

1. **Escalation DOWNGRADES and jumps provider family.** The Pass-1 escalation loop at
   `sizing.py:378` assigns each returned name straight onto the run config
   (`replace(cfg, model=model)`, `sizing.py:380-386`), so the first "escalation" for a nova primary
   is `claude-haiku-4-5` — a SMALLER window and a different provider than the operator configured.
   The prerequisite-coverage escalation has the same defect through a different expression: it
   calls `sizing.models_at_or_above(model)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py:260`
   and then takes `ladder[0]` at `:261`, because an unlocated primary is not present in its own
   returned ladder.
2. **The window is overstated.** `ctx.largest_window_tokens` is set from
   `largest_window_tokens(cfg.model)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:242` and feeds
   the P8 size budget at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:622` and
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:388`. So P8 UNDER-blocks: material that will not fit is
   judged to fit, and the review truncates instead of telling the author to decompose.

Who has this, and why now: any operator running the plan-review gate on a non-Anthropic-family model. The shipped default is the ladder name `claude-opus-4-8` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:37` and `:498`), so the defect is invisible on the default configuration and lands exactly on the deployments that set `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to their own provider's model — which is the configuration epic 061c exists to make correct.

## Approach

Make "the ladder cannot locate this primary" an EXPLICIT outcome at both functions instead of a silent substitution of the whole ladder / the ladder maximum.

- **`models_at_or_above(model)`** — keep both existing branches byte-for-byte: a falsy `model`
  still returns the whole ladder (`sizing.py:327`), and a located family name still returns
  `names[i:]` (`sizing.py:326`). Change ONLY the truthy-but-unlocated case to return `[model]`.
  Worked example, after the change: `models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')` returns
  `['bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0']`. The one-criterion retry still runs, on the operator's own
  model, and there is no higher rung to climb onto.
- **`largest_window_tokens(model)`** — keep the located branch (`sizing.py:141-145`) and keep
  `None` -> `MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`: with no configured model the gate runs its own default, which
  IS a ladder model, so the ladder maximum is the right answer there. Change ONLY the
  truthy-but-unlocated case to `min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER)`. Worked example, after the change:
  `largest_window_tokens('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')` returns `200000`, not `1000000`.

**Why `[model]` and not `[]`.** `pass1_with_ladder` has two independent recovery steps: batch -> one-criterion-per-call (`sizing.py:371-377`), and only then rung climbing. Returning `[]` would make the `for model in models_at_or_above(...)` loop body never execute, so `produced` stays `False` and control jumps straight to the `_too_big` failure finding (`sizing.py:401-421`) — discarding the single-criterion retry, which is the step that most often succeeds because one criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch. `[model]` preserves that retry and stops before the first cross-family rung, so `_too_big` fires only when the criterion genuinely does not fit.

**Why the ladder MINIMUM for an unlocated window.** The two error directions are not symmetric. Under-blocking is silent: the review proceeds and truncates. Over-blocking is loud and actionable: P8 emits "reduce/decompose it" with a `_too_big` finding the author can act on. With no window entry for the operator's model, the honest default is the conservative one. It is also safe for the other three window consumers — `verify_request_chunks` (`sizing.py:189`), `pack_prerequisite_bins` (`sizing.py:206`) and `pack_prerequisite_verifier_bins` (`sizing.py:241`) all divide by this number, so a smaller value yields MORE, SMALLER chunks, never an overflow.

**Why not read the real window from the model profile.** `ModelCapabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:30-42`) exposes `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style`, `supports_thinking` and `supports_temperature` — there is no context-window field. The same absence is already recorded in-tree at `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:278-281` ("The ModelProfile capabilities seam ... does not expose max output tokens, so this table is the single source"). Adding a window to that seam is a larger change across every consumer of `capabilities_for` (`capabilities.py:221`); this ticket removes the silent WRONG answer using the machinery that exists, and a profile-sourced window remains available as a later enhancement on top of an honest fallback.

**Riskiest assumption, tested first.** The assumption most likely to sink this plan is that no in-tree caller depends on the ladder maximum / full ladder for a truthy unlocated model. Step 1, before either function is edited, is the cheapest falsifier: run `grep -rn "largest_window_tokens\|models_at_or_above" src tests` and read every hit. The one known hit that asserts the behaviour being removed is `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1168`; it is updated in this change (see Scope and Testing). If that grep turns up a production caller that needs the optimistic value, the fallback is to keep `largest_window_tokens` optimistic and ship only the `models_at_or_above` half — but the search has already been run once for this plan and found only the one test assertion.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `models_at_or_above` (lines 319-327) and
  `largest_window_tokens` (lines 137-146), plus both docstrings, which today say "Unknown/absent
  model -> the whole ladder" (line 321) and "Unknown/absent -> the ladder maximum" (line 140) and
  must state the new unlocated rule. No other function in this file changes, and `MODEL_LADDER`
  (lines 99-103) is not edited.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — `test_largest_window_uses_configured_model_window`
  (line 1163): the assertion at line 1168, `largest_window_tokens("some-unknown-model") ==
  sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`, pins the exact behaviour being removed and is rewritten to the
  ladder minimum. New regression cases are added beside it and beside
  `test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (line 1123), reusing the module's `_SeqRunner` stub
  (line 1102) and the `orchestrator._models_at_or_above` / `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens`
  re-exports (`orchestrator.py:79` and `:74`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py` — one new case pinning that the prerequisite
  escalation path stays on the operator's model (see Testing).

**Not edited: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py`.** Its escalation at line 260 consumes `models_at_or_above`, so this change fixes it without touching it: with a returned ladder of `[model]`, `model in ladder` is true, `ladder.index(model) + 1` is out of range, and the existing `except (ValueError, IndexError)` at line 262 already converts that into the explicit `input-too-large` indeterminate record at line 263. That is asserted by a test, not assumed.

**Not in scope: rung TARGET resolution.** Ticket 7de4 changes how a LOCATED rung is NAMED; this ticket changes only WHICH rung the walk starts from. 7de4 is not on `origin/main` — its symbol is absent from the tree (`git grep _rung_target origin/main -- src` returns nothing at HEAD `1052bc856f`) — so this plan is written entirely against main and names no symbol 7de4 introduces. 7de4's plan states it leaves the start-rung behaviour byte-for-byte as it is and adds a pinning test asserting the nova primary still returns the three bare Anthropic rungs. That pin encodes the defect this ticket removes, so whichever of the two lands SECOND updates that one assertion to the new expected value; nothing else in either change overlaps.

## Testing

- **Regression, the exact reported id.** `orchestrator._models_at_or_above(
  "bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` equals `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]`, and no element
  of the returned list contains `"claude-"`. Fails on the current tree, which returns the three
  Anthropic rungs.
- **Regression, the window.** `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")`
  equals `200_000` (`min(w for _, w in sizing.MODEL_LADDER)`) and is strictly less than
  `sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`. Fails on the current tree, which returns `1_000_000`.
- **Failure path, escalation reports instead of silently crossing families.** Drive
  `orchestrator._pass1_with_ladder` with a `_SeqRunner`-shaped stub (the class at `test_plan_review.py:1102`, extended to record

## Why

A reconcile pass with silently-failed sub-ops still reports `OK: applied N of N` / exit 0
("converged"). Two gaps make sync failures invisible: (1) the silent-no-op canary
(`apply_handlers.py` ~line 218) only hard-fails behind `RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP`
(default "0" = warn-only); (2) `comment_errors` (swallowed partial comment failures,
`apply_handlers.py:117-118,195-196`) are recorded NON-fatally and never counted in
`mutation_failures` (`reconcile.py` ~line 1051), so a partial comment drop yields exit 0.
Confirmed by the /rebar-debug (b) audit: acli exit-0-on-failure IS detected at the transport
floor (`acli_subprocess._check_mutation_failure`), then demoted to non-fatal `comment_errors`.

## What (gate fatality behind the existing flag; keep default OFF)

- `apply_handlers.py`: when `comment_errors` is present AND `_rebar_env("RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP")=="1"`,
  set `outcome["error"]` (so partial comment failures count), mirroring the existing total-no-op
  canary flag check. Default off ⇒ landing is behavior-neutral.
- Optional: a per-pass telemetry summary line (silent-no-op count + comment-error count) —
  always-on, non-fatal (pure visibility).

## Sequencing (CRITICAL)

Do NOT activate fail-loud before the Jira comment cleanup (sibling ticket). The 13 capped
tickets still have ~7 genuinely-unsynced comments each that bounce off Jira's 5000 cap until
cleanup; flipping fail-loud first makes the reconciler FAIL every pass on them. Land the
gated machinery NOW (safe); ACTIVATE (set `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1` in
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` env) only AFTER the cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the flag ON, an outcome carrying `comment_errors` counts toward `mutation_failures`
      and drives a non-zero pass exit. Proving command: a unit test in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/` (extend `test_silent_noop_canary.py` / add one) —
      RED before the change (comment_errors → exit 0).
- [ ] With the flag OFF (default), behavior is unchanged (comment_errors non-fatal). Regression
      test asserts this.
- [ ] The silent-no-op canary already covers TOTAL no-ops for links/comments/labels (verify + a
      test for comments/labels, not just links — the (b) audit noted links-only coverage).
- [ ] `make test` green; no new dependency.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Flag activated in reconcile-bridge.yml AFTER the Jira cleanup lands.
baseline.summary: Observability: fail-loud on silent sub-op no-ops + count comment_errors (gated; activate after cleanup)

content.text: ## Why
Jobs 2 + 3 are the same machine: run declarative patterns over the repo, emit matches. Job 2 = deterministic
overlay-applicability triggers (better than naive grep); job 3 = low-threshold smell/decay scans that flag
areas for an LLM. This is where rebar owns common detectors AND lets projects extend — the extension mechanism
is the product.
## What
- **Engine B = OpenGrep** (permissive LGPL-2.1 Semgrep fork; 30+ langs; JSON+SARIF) as the primary matcher and
its rule-loading as the registry substrate; ast-grep optional lighter secondary; scc/lizard as a metric
matcher type (size/complexity; feeds smell + plan-review P4). Do NOT invent a match DSL.
- **Detector registry, thin-envelope + verbatim native payload** (Trivy model): a detector =
`{id, metadata, languages/applicability, severity-hint, backend, evidence-mapping}` + a native matcher payload.
The envelope rides in the rule's `metadata.rebar_envelope` (spike-validated, preserved verbatim). **`evidence-mapping`
is concrete (spike E5):** a match → the normalized record `{outcome, detector_id, reason, provenance_tier, job,
location, coverage}` (namespace + envelope fields read from `rule.properties`); a skipped backend uses the SAME
shape with `outcome=abstain, coverage.status=skipped`.
- **Built-in (official) + project-local** detectors auto-discovered from `.rebar/detectors/`, unioned at load;
namespaced IDs; last-wins/explicit override; deltas-only project config; absent dir = no error. The registry is
**process-local, built-once-and-cached, keyed by the detector-dir mtime** (rebuild on change); read-only in-memory
state (not the shared git store), so concurrent scans share one immutable snapshot.
- **Loader PRE-VALIDATES (ENGINE-FAITHFULLY) + quarantines each detector** before the scan — spike E1: the engine
ABORTS the whole run on a schema-invalid rule (exit 7), and `opengrep/semgrep --validate` (good→0, bad→2, NO scan
target needed) is the engine's OWN checker, so the loader validates with `--validate` (+ ast-grep's own per-rule
check) — NOT a divergent rebar-side schema — and drops a bad detector with `abstain(invalid_detector)`.
- **Self-declared applicability + file-presence routing** (a detector's applicability IS the job-2 trigger). A
detector declares its `dimension` from the **closed dimension-ID vocabulary owned by S5** (e.g. `web_frontend`,
`has_iac`, `touches_auth`); S4 does not invent dimension IDs ad-hoc.
- **Configurable metric thresholds (R-6):** scc/lizard oversize/complexity cutoffs are fields on the metric
detector's envelope with shipped defaults, project-overridable via the same `.rebar/` delta mechanism — DISTINCT
from per-ID severity/enable deltas (the cutoff value itself is tunable per project / per consumer like P4).
- **Custom-language detectors (R-7):** a project tree-sitter custom grammar (ast-grep `customLanguages` style)
declared in the `.rebar/` slot is honored for structural detectors; unsupported language → skipped + coverage.
- Each backend in a recover boundary (prefer the CLI form; in-process bindings behind a worker subprocess);
output normalized to S1's evidence model; version pinned/recorded (mismatch → `abstain(version_skew)`).
**Per-backend invalid-detector (spike E1):** OpenGrep `--validate` + ast-grep's own per-rule check pre-validate;
scc/lizard are metric tools with NO rule schema → `invalid_detector` is N/A there (only missing-binary /
unparseable-file → abstain). The OpenGrep+quarantine path is the FIRST vertical slice; ast-grep + metric land after.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/grounding/detectors/` (registry + loader) + `engine_b.py` (OpenGrep/ast-grep/metric backends).
- Bundled built-ins authored by us / from permissive sources (NOT Semgrep registry rules — licensing).
- Discovery owned here; `.rebar/detectors/` file convention coordinated with `55de`. Not a dup of `3156`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OpenGrep integrated as primary matcher; ast-grep secondary; scc/lizard metric matcher; outputs normalized to the evidence model.
- [ ] Thin-envelope detector format + registry; built-in + project-local `.rebar/detectors/` discovery; namespaced IDs + override precedence.

- [ ] Loader pre-validates ENGINE-FAITHFULLY (`opengrep/semgrep --validate`; ast-grep's own check) + quarantines an invalid detector (`abstain(invalid_detector)`) BEFORE the scan — never aborts on a bad rule (spike E1).
- [ ] Self-declared applicability + file-presence routing; detector `dimension` drawn from S5's closed vocabulary; absent language/files → skipped + coverage recorded.

- [ ] `evidence-mapping` concretely defined (match & abstain share `{outcome,detector_id,reason,provenance_tier,job,location,coverage}`, spike E5; envelope read from `rule.properties`). Metric thresholds project-configurable (shipped defaults, distinct from per-ID severity deltas); project tree-sitter custom grammar honored.

- [ ] Fail-open tested per backend (missing binary / version skew / unsupported lang / crash → abstain; invalid-detector → abstain for OpenGrep+ast-grep, N/A for metric tools); registry build process-local + cached + mtime-invalidated; bundled built-ins permissively licensed.

baseline.summary: Engine B — detector registry + OpenGrep evaluator (+ast-grep/metrics) for applicability + smell scans

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Backtests over the 7-day population (153 tickets; 104 passed-plan FP set, 55 blocked-plan hit set) and a 200-ticket extended set support two deterministic floor additions. (R1) verification-presence: 1-4/104 marginal FPs, all 4 blocked-plan hits overlapped the real blocking findings. (R2) the P6 vague lexicon matches word prefixes with no trailing boundary (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:458-477), so `clean` fires on "cleanly"/"lint clean"; the fixed rule measured 0 FPs across 304 passed plans. Operator approved both for blocking.

## Approach
p6_ac_quality is monolithic and stays advisory, so both new blocking rules are implemented as SEPARATE DET checks with their own coverage entries rather than promotions inside P6: (R1) a new blocking check `p10_verification_presence`: a leaf plan passes if it has a `## Testing` or `## Verification` H2 section, OR >= 1 `- [ ]`/`- [x]` AC item that contains an inline code span (backtick-fenced token) or matches the verification-vocabulary regex `(?i)\b(pytest|test_[a-z0-9_]+|make\s+\w+|rebar\s+\w+|git\s+\w+|grep\b|assert\w*|checked:|verif(?:y|ied|ies|ication)|exit\s+code)\b`. This vocabulary is exhaustive for the check — nothing else qualifies. (R2) a new blocking check `p11_ac_vagueness`: the fixed lexicon (both word boundaries; `clean` dropped; `etc.` kept; all other current _VAGUE_LEXICON terms kept) scanned over AC item lines only (det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines). Code-span handling: inline code-span positions are recorded on the ORIGINAL line before spans are blanked for matching; a lexicon hit inside a recorded span never fires, and an `etc.` occurrence whose start lies within 30 characters after a recorded span's end is exempt (a non-exhaustive enumeration of already-concrete examples). P6's advisory lexicon is updated to the same fixed matching so the two surfaces agree. Existing tests asserting P6-family posture are updated in the same change: tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py, tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py, and tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py (line 108 asserts `r.blocking is False` on a p6_ac_quality result — unaffected in behavior since P6 stays advisory, re-run to confirm). Documentation: docs/plan-review-gate.md has no DET-gate table; its deterministic-floor prose section is extended with P10/P11 descriptions. The criteria guide is generated from the LLM registry and does not cover DET checks — no regeneration applies. Alternative rejected: spec-by-example/riskiest-assumption floors — backtests showed no discrimination (76%/71% and 86%/80% fire rates on good vs blocked plans).

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py, tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py (new), tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py, tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py, tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py (confirm/adjust posture assertion), docs/plan-review-gate.md.

## Testing
Unit for R1: a plan whose ACs carry no code span and no vocabulary match and no Testing section blocks; one backticked-command AC passes; a "checked:" AC passes. Unit for R2 over the enumerated FP fixture lines transcribed from the backtest (each must NOT fire): "`make lint` exits 0 (ruff + format check clean)"; "mypy --strict runs clean on the new module"; "the parser clean parses all fixture files"; "Clean preferred-schema responses round-trip"; "the close precheck sees a clean tickets-tracker HEAD"; "the core-wheel lane is clean after the split"; "the collector cleanly collects all retired events"; "stale worktrees are cleaned up by the janitor"; "run `git grep -n 'pattern' docs/ src/`, etc. and confirm no hits"; "Robustness: the simulated-stall test passes". Positive cases (must fire): "works properly"; "handles errors, etc." with no adjacent code span; "reasonable performance".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] p10_verification_presence blocks a leaf plan with no code-span AC, no vocabulary-matching AC, and no Testing/Verification section, and passes each of the three qualifying forms (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py`).
- [ ] p11_ac_vagueness produces zero matches on the ten enumerated fixture lines and fires on the three enumerated positive cases (checked: parameterized test over the lines listed in Testing).
- [ ] `clean` is absent from the blocking lexicon and the `etc.` span-proximity exemption uses original-line span positions (checked: unit tests).
- [ ] P6 remains advisory and its existing posture assertions still hold (checked: the three updated/confirmed test files pass).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md's deterministic-floor section documents P10 and P11 (checked: doc text assertion in the new test file).
baseline.summary: Clarity floor: blocking verification-presence check and boundary-fixed vague lexicon

content.text: ## Why
The original epic problem: the plan-review verify pass chunks findings token-naively. Bespoke used a
hard-coded `batch_size=12` (`range(0, len(findings), 12)`); the workflow does ONE aggregate call, which
a pathological huge-findings ticket could push past the model context window. Replace the magic count
with PRINCIPLED, token-based chunking — estimate the verify request vs the selected model's window
(reusing the `sizing.py` machinery), splitting only when needed. This depends on WS1 (single verify
path) and WS2 (the per-step `model:` whose window we size against).
## What
- Replace any count-based batching with a token estimate vs the verify step's resolved model window,
reusing `largest_window_tokens(model)` + the `est_tokens` (chars/4) estimator — no new magic constant,
no new tokenizer dependency.
- Budget formula: `budget = floor(largest_window_tokens(model) * HEADROOM)`, `HEADROOM` a named config
knob `verify.verify_window_headroom` (default 0.8). A chunk fits when
`est_tokens(system_prompt + verify_instructions(chunk)) + projected_output(chunk) <= budget`.
- Projected output: `projected_output(chunk) = len(chunk) * PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS`, a named
per-finding reserve sized from the `plan_review_verification` schema (~256 tok/finding, documented).
- `<= budget` → ONE aggregate verify call (unchanged). `> budget` → minimal principled splits that
preserve GLOBAL finding enumeration and re-merge by finding `index` (existing merge contract).
- Single-oversized-finding edge case: escalate from the RESOLVED verify model via
`models_at_or_above(resolved_verify_model)`; if still too large at the top of the ladder, mark the
finding INDETERMINATE (non-blocking, surfaced) — never silently drop.
## Scope
In scope: the token-budget chunking decision in the workflow verify path, the `verify.verify_window_headroom`
config key, the `PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS` reserve, the oversized-finding escalation/INDETERMINATE
path, and tests (via a deterministic window-shrink seam). Out of scope: WS1 migration, WS2 model/editor
work, WS4 coach nit. Depends on WS1 (single path) and WS2 (resolved per-step model). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`, `workflow_ops.py` (the verify-inputs op), and config.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A token estimate (no magic `batch_size` constant) decides verify chunking, reusing
`largest_window_tokens` + `est_tokens`.
- [ ] The fit test is `est_tokens(request) + projected_output <= floor(window * HEADROOM)`, where
`HEADROOM` is the config knob `verify.verify_window_headroom` (default 0.8) and
`projected_output = len(chunk) * PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS` (a named per-finding reserve).
- [ ] `<= budget` findings → one aggregate verify call (unchanged behavior).
- [ ] `> budget` findings → minimal principled splits that preserve global enumeration and re-merge
verifications by finding `index`; a test (via a deterministic window-shrink seam) asserts
principled splitting, NOT count-12.
- [ ] The `> budget` test also asserts the chars/4 estimate plus headroom keeps a real request under
the actual model window (the estimator safety margin is grounded, not assumed).
- [ ] A single finding larger than the budget escalates from the resolved verify model via
`models_at_or_above`; if still too large at the top of the ladder it is marked INDETERMINATE
(non-blocking, surfaced) — never silently dropped; a test covers this path.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS3: Principled token-based chunking for the workflow Pass-2 verify

baseline.description:
## Context

B-RETIRE removed bespoke orchestrator.run_review, the ONLY producer of the per-pass latency/cost metrics (db7b AC5: coverage['metrics'] = {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, claim_path}). The workflow plan-review path did not emit them, so coverage['metrics'] was absent on the workflow gate (the sidecar emitted {}). This is a passive-observability regression (the metrics fed passive latency/cost-target refinement from dogfood data).

## Approach (decided)

Capture the latency split from **recorder step timings**: the workflow interpreter records a per-step `duration_ms` (leaf steps + the batch finder), and `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` reconstructs coverage['metrics'] from rec.steps after the run, attaching it to the verdict. Source decision (resolving the AC's two candidates): step timings for the tier split; the finder step's `criteria_count` for the llm_calls cost proxy.

- **det_ms** = wall-clock of the deterministic floor (the `precheck` step).
- **llm_ms** = wall-clock of the billable LLM tier (steps of kind agent/batch: Pass-1 finders + Pass-2 verify + Pass-4 coach).
- **total_ms** = the whole run's wall-clock, measured around run_workflow.
- **llm_calls** = cost proxy: finder criteria_count + one per succeeded agent step (verify/coach).
- **claim_path** = the structural marker (the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify; LLM/network-free) — RETAINED, matching the db7b dict exactly.

Tolerant of partial/untimed records (a missing duration contributes 0) so it never raises inside the gate, and attached on BOTH the happy path and the coach-failure recovery path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The workflow interpreter records a per-step `duration_ms` on leaf + batch steps (the recorder step-timing source).
- [ ] The workflow plan-review path emits coverage['metrics'] = {det_ms, llm_ms, total_ms, llm_calls, claim_path} (incl. claim_path), reconstructed from the workflow run's recorder step timings + the finder criteria_count.
- [ ] The sidecar carries the metrics again on the workflow gate (lifted to the top level) — verified to equal coverage['metrics'].
- [ ] A test drives produce_plan_review_verdict end-to-end OFFLINE and asserts the metrics are produced AND plausible (all five keys present; det_ms/llm_ms >= 0; total_ms >= llm_ms; llm_calls > 0; claim_path is the structural marker).
baseline.summary: Reinstate per-pass latency/cost telemetry (coverage.metrics) on the workflow plan-review gate

content.text: ## Why

An external (live Jira, real API mutation + cost) test LEAKED into a default run: the filter `-m "not integration"` does NOT exclude `external`, and the live tests run whenever Jira creds are present (skipif only gates on creds). This caused live mutations + orphan issues during routine suite runs. Research (recorded below) shows the fix is structural + env-gating, NOT an in-process network blocker (our external calls go through the `acli` SUBPROCESS, which no Python socket-patcher can catch).
## What

1. Env opt-in: external tests are INERT by default — require `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` (truthy) IN ADDITION to creds; a default run (even with creds) must not execute them. (Autouse/skip in tests/external/conftest.py.)

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan f93a-b947-558b-469c --output json` (a story with a ~2.6KB plan).
2. Observe the returned coverage.metrics + verdict.
Observed across 3 consecutive runs (attempts 3/4/5 in this session; cache cleared before attempt 5):
Expected: Pass-2 verify dispatches over the Pass-1 findings (verify_requests > 0), findings are
verified/decided, verdict is PASS or BLOCK. (This is what attempt 1 on an earlier revision of the same
ticket did: verify_requests=43, llm_ms=553581, verdict BLOCK with a verified finding.)
Actual: verdict INDETERMINATE with verify_requests=0, llm_ms~=21ms despite llm_calls=26, total_ms~=16s,
0x HTTP 429, and a COMPLETELY EMPTY stderr (no warning/error/exception logged). All 17 Pass-1 findings
fall through to `indeterminate` with reason `no-verification` because Pass-2 never dispatched. The result
is deterministically reproducible on this ticket's current plan; clearing `.rebar/cache` (which had no
entry for this ticket anyway) did not change it.
## Why it matters
A silent Pass-2 non-dispatch means the gate can return INDETERMINATE (fail-closed / non-signing) for a
plan that has no blocking issue, with NO diagnostic in stderr — indistinguishable to an operator from a
healthy review. It also blocks earning a fresh attestation after a material edit. The llm_ms~=21ms /
llm_calls=26 mismatch suggests Pass-1 was served from a cache (Anthropic prompt cache or other) and a
fully-cached Pass-1 may be the trigger for Pass-2 being skipped — needs root-causing.
## Context
Surfaced while re-reviewing story f93a (eval-foundation, epic sure-foyer-aroma ac1b) after remediating a
legitimate BLOCK. Evidence JSONs: ~/.claude/jobs/19885ca3/tmp/planrev/f93a_rereview{,3,4,5}.json
(attempt 1 = healthy verify; 3/4/5 = degraded). rebar 0.5.2 (c12ad713b-dirty).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root-cause why Pass-2 verify reports verify_requests=0 (llm_ms~=21ms, llm_calls=26) reproducibly on
this plan while attempt 1 verified normally; confirm/deny the cached-Pass-1 trigger hypothesis.
- [ ] A degraded/skipped verify pass emits a diagnostic (stderr log + a coverage note) — never silent.
- [ ] Either the gate re-dispatches verify on a cached Pass-1, or documents+justifies skipping it.
- [ ] A regression test covers the cached-Pass-1 -> verify path so this cannot silently recur.
