## Summary

`_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:723` over-matches, so several push failures that are **not** compare-and-swap mismatches are classified as one — which the ref-lock reports as "lease lost/stolen". The same branch discards the git stderr, so a production occurrence cannot be diagnosed after the fact.

Found while root-causing bug `449f-f9bf-be90-47fe`. Filed separately because fixing it changes lock classification semantics, and (see below) the very logging gap it creates is why we cannot yet prove it has fired in production.

## The code

```python
# A rejected ``--force-with-lease`` prints "stale info" (the lease mismatch) or a
# "! [rejected]" / "cannot lock ref" line — distinct from a genuine transport
# failure ("Authentication failed", "Could not resolve host"), which we do NOT
# classify as a CAS mismatch (fail-closed).
_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS = ("stale info", "rejected", "cannot lock ref")
```

`_push_lease_cas` (`:726-747`) lowercases stderr, substring-matches those markers, and on a hit raises a synthetic `CalledProcessError(128, ["git","update-ref",ref])` that `_cas_once` reads as a CAS mismatch and `renew` (`:570-572`) converts to `LeaseLostError` -> heartbeat abort -> pass abort.

## Evidence — runtime, driving `_push_lease_cas` with real git stderr strings

```
genuine CAS mismatch (stale info)              CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- correct
server-side concurrent ref lock (NOT CAS)      CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
remote internal rejection (NOT CAS)            CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
pre-receive hook declined (NOT CAS)            CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
GitHub secondary rate limit (NOT CAS)          CLASSIFIED AS CAS MISMATCH   <- wrong
transport: auth failed                         fail-closed                  <- correct
transport: host unresolved                     fail-closed                  <- correct
```

The strings used are real git output shapes, e.g. `error: cannot lock ref 'refs/reconciler/lock': Unable to create '...lock': File exists.` and `! [remote rejected] refs/reconciler/lock (pre-receive hook declined)`.

`"rejected"` in particular matches `! [remote rejected]`, which git emits for hook declines, quota/rate-limit rejections, and server-side errors — none of which mean the lease moved.

## The contract this violates

The module's own comment at `_ref_lock.py:719-722` promises the opposite: a genuine transport failure "we do NOT classify as a CAS mismatch (fail-closed)". ADR 0031 (`docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md:66,92`) states the same in its "Three exit-128 outcomes, one classifier" section. ADR 0031:189-190 additionally asserts "a **live** holder is never stolen (regression-tested)".

## The compounding defect — the evidence is thrown away

The classified branch (`:743-745`) raises **without logging**. The fail-closed branch below it (`:746-752`) *does* log the stderr. So the one path that makes a consequential claim ("your lease was stolen") is the one that keeps no evidence for it.

Concrete cost: `Reconcile Bridge` runs 30576272914 and 30579382013 (2026-07-30) aborted on `LeaseLostError`. Both landed ~86s into the pass, on the **second** heartbeat tick (lease 120s, interval 40s), and `renew`'s pre-CAS `read()` — which force-fetches from origin — saw the ref still at our own oid immediately before the push CAS failed. No other run logged a steal, and the workflow's `concurrency: reconcile-bridge` group serializes passes. That pattern is suspicious but **unprovable either way**, because the stderr that would settle it was discarded.

## Why this is filed, not fixed inline

Narrowing the markers changes what the lock treats as contention versus fault, on `acquire` / `release` / `renew` / `steal` alike. That is a real blast radius, and the occurrence rate is currently unmeasurable. The right order is: restore the evidence first, then narrow once a real sample exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The CAS-mismatch branch logs the git stderr (and the ref + expected oid) before
      raising, at a level that survives into CI logs — so the next occurrence is
      diagnosable. This alone is low-risk and should land first.
- [ ] On `LeaseLostError`, the holder additionally records what the remote ref
      actually was (e.g. an `ls-remote` of the lock ref plus the holder recorded in
      the lock blob), so "stolen by whom" is answerable rather than inferred.
- [ ] The marker set no longer classifies non-CAS rejections (hook decline, server
      ref-lock contention, rate limit, internal error) as a lease mismatch, with a
      unit test driving the real stderr shapes above and asserting the split. RED
      first against the current list.
- [ ] Fail-closed behaviour for genuine transport failures (auth, DNS) is unchanged
      and still covered.
- [ ] With the logging in place, state whether the two 2026-07-30 lease losses were
      genuine takeovers or spurious classifications — or, if no new occurrence has
      been captured, say so explicitly rather than closing on inference.
- [ ] File paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (lines 715-752,
      and the `renew`/`LeaseLostError` path around 559-601).
baseline.summary: _PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS misclassifies non-CAS push failures as a stolen lease, and discards the stderr that would prove it

content.text: ## What
Running a workflow against a **non-existent target ticket id** silently creates a
phantom, CREATE-less ticket directory in the store. The workflow recorder appends
`WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` events to the target ticket's directory **without first
verifying the ticket exists**, and the store's commit path does
`os.makedirs(ticket_dir, exist_ok=True)` — so the events land in a brand-new directory
that has no `CREATE` event. The result is a "ghost" ticket that `fsck` flags as
`MISSING_CREATE` forever (it is excluded from `list` as an error-state, so it is easy to
miss until a store-health check trips on it).
This was discovered during the 0.5.2 release dogfood: an orphan dir
`31c6-d82c-44a5-4953` held a single `_fake: true` `WORKFLOW_STEP` (a FakeRunner run,
epic a88f) and no CREATE — it was the sole `MISSING_CREATE` fsck finding in the real
store (since cleaned up).
## Reproduction Steps
1. In an initialized store, run a workflow targeting a ticket id that does **not** exist,
e.g. library `rebar.run_workflow(<wf>, ticket_id="no-such-ticket")` (or the CLI/MCP
`run_workflow` equivalent), with the FakeRunner so no LLM is needed.
2. `rebar fsck`.
**Expected:** the run **fails fast** with a clear "ticket … not found / has no CREATE"
error and writes **no** event files — no directory is created for a bogus id (same
contract leaf writes already enforce).
**Actual:** the run proceeds and writes `WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` events into a new
`no-such-ticket/` directory with no CREATE; `fsck` then reports
`MISSING_CREATE: no-such-ticket — no CREATE event found` permanently.
## Root cause (citations)
- `rebar.llm.workflow.runs.run_workflow` (`runs.py:169-192`) takes `ticket_id`, calls
`record_run_location`, and passes `target_ticket=ticket_id` to the executor **without
validating the ticket resolves / is not a ghost**.
- `executor.TicketEventRecorder._append` (`executor.py:233`) writes each
`WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP` via `_seam.append_event(self.ticket, …)`.
- `_seam.append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py:151-187`) composes the envelope and commits
through `_store.event_append.write_and_push` — it does **not** call
`_seam.require_not_ghost`, and `stage_and_commit` does `os.makedirs(ticket_dir,
exist_ok=True)`, so a non-existent target id materializes a CREATE-less dir.
- Contrast: the leaf-write commands (comment/edit/tag/…) call
`_seam.require_not_ghost(ticket_id, tracker)` (`_seam.py:70-83`) BEFORE appending,
precisely to refuse writing onto a ticket that was never created. The workflow
recorder is missing that guard.
## Proposed fix
Validate the target ticket up front, before the first `WORKFLOW_RUN` write:
- In `run_workflow` (the entry point), when `ticket_id` is provided, resolve it and run
the ghost check (`_seam.require_id` + `_seam.require_not_ghost`, or the library
equivalent) and fail fast with a clear error if it does not exist — BEFORE
`record_run_location` / starting the run, so no partial state is written.
- Optionally add the same `require_not_ghost` guard in `TicketEventRecorder` (or its
first `_append`) as defense-in-depth for any other caller that constructs a recorder
with a bogus target.
- Do not auto-create the ticket; recording run-state onto a non-existent ticket is a
caller error, mirroring the leaf-write contract.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `run_workflow` (library + CLI + MCP) against a non-existent `ticket_id` fails fast
with a clear "ticket not found / has no CREATE" error and writes **zero** event files —
no phantom directory is created.
- [ ] `run_workflow` against a real, existing ticket records `WORKFLOW_RUN`/`WORKFLOW_STEP`
exactly as before (no regression to the happy path or to `dry_run`).
- [ ] `fsck` stays clean after running workflows (no new `MISSING_CREATE`).
- [ ] A regression test exercises the non-existent-ticket case (asserts the fail-fast
error AND that no `<bogus-id>/` directory was created).
</content>

baseline.summary: workflow engine records WORKFLOW_RUN/STEP to a non-existent target ticket -> phantom CREATE-less dir (fsck MISSING_CREATE)

# Rename `_anthropic_cache_settings` to `_anthropic_cache_options`

## Context / Problem

`_anthropic_cache_settings` in `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` returns a pydantic-ai `ModelSettings` mapping (or `None` for a non-Anthropic model), not a settings object. Readers have twice mistaken it for a config accessor. Renaming it to `_anthropic_cache_options` makes the return shape read correctly at every call site. Pure rename: no behaviour change, no signature change, no new capability.

## Approach

Rename the definition, then update every reference — including the ones that name the symbol as a string, which a rename refactor will not touch.

## Scope

I went through the tree with `grep` and these are the files that mention it:

- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — the definition (line 39) and the module docstring (line 10).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — the re-export import (line 28) and the call site (line 337).
- `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` — the import (line 17) and four direct call sites
  (lines 313, 317, 318, 319).
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` — line 90, where the symbol is named
  as a **string literal** inside `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "_anthropic_cache_settings", …)`.
  A rename refactor will not touch this; after the rename the patch would silently target a name
  that no longer exists.
- `docs/code-navigation.md` — four occurrences, where this symbol is the worked example.
- `docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md` — two occurrences, same reason.

## Testing

Every acceptance criterion is checked by a command that runs in-session and produces observable output:

- `git grep -n _anthropic_cache_settings` must print nothing and exit 1.
- `git grep -n _anthropic_cache_options` must print the definition, the re-export, the call site,
  the test call sites, the monkeypatch string, and the doc occurrences.
- `make test` must pass, exercising the renamed function through `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`
  and the monkeypatch through `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git grep -n _anthropic_cache_settings` prints nothing and exits 1 (the old name is gone
      from the whole tree, including docs and the string literal)
- [ ] `_anthropic_cache_options` is defined in `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, re-exported from
      `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, called at the cache-settings site, and used at all four
      `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` call sites, verified by `git grep -n _anthropic_cache_options`
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:90` patches the NEW name, verified by
      `git grep -n '"_anthropic_cache_options"' tests/`
- [ ] behaviour is unchanged: the function still returns the cache-control settings mapping for an
      `anthropic:` model and `None` for `openai:`/`google-gla:`/`""`
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` all pass
baseline.summary: DEMO — rename _anthropic_cache_settings (deliberately thin inventory)

content.text: ## Why
Make prompts contract-bearing palette citizens like scripted ops, and represent the single_turn
vs agentic distinction precisely so the runner can be written without inventing protocol.
## What
- `execution_mode` is a CLOSED enum `{single_turn, agentic}` on the PROMPT front-matter (NOT the
workflow IR; it is DISTINCT from the existing step `mode:[findings,structured,text]`, which controls
output shaping and is unchanged). Document the relationship between the two fields.
- Runner DISPATCH protocol (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` + `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py`
RunnerAgentStep): `agentic` = the current pydantic_ai tool-using path (unchanged). `single_turn` =
ONE `pydantic_ai` model call with NO tools; the resolved prompt is rendered with the step's `with:`
inputs marshaled as template variables; the model is asked for structured output validated against
the prompt's `outputs` contract (reuse the existing structured-output stack); no tool loop.
- Surface the resolved prompt's consumes/produces/description in the inspector (reuse S0's path).
- `outputs` contract change on an override/variant is BREAKING: `validate` flags override-vs-builtin drift.
## Scope
In: enum + runner dispatch (both modes) + prompt-contract surfacing + drift flag. Out: deep/runtime validation (S5).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `execution_mode` is a `{single_turn,agentic}` enum on prompt front-matter, documented as distinct from step `mode`.

- [ ] `single_turn` runs exactly one model call with zero tools and returns output validated against the prompt's `outputs` contract; `agentic` is the unchanged tool-using path; both covered by tests.
- [ ] An agent step surfaces its prompt's contract in the inspector.
- [ ] `validate` flags an override/variant that changes a prompt's `outputs` contract.
- [ ] A live `single_turn` prompt produces structured output validated against its `outputs` contract.

- [ ] A prompt that LACKS `execution_mode` defaults to `agentic` (back-compat) — tested; the field is otherwise the closed `{single_turn,agentic}` enum, and S3's migration stamps it explicitly on existing prompts.

baseline.summary: Prompt contracts in IR/runner + execution_mode + inspector surfacing

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Agents file bugs outside an epic's hierarchy during epic execution and deem them out-of-scope/pre-existing even when they are defects in the epic's own deliverable; the direct-children close gate cannot see them. Event-precise backtest over 56 analyzable epic closes: 2 real at-close escapes (30a2 token-bin scaling under the token-reduction epic a492; 5b09 artifact persistence under 119f), and legitimate deferrals that must NOT block (30d3 proven-pre-existing fsck diagnostics; e6a0 filed-49s-before-close architectural follow-up, later its own epic; c8ed bug supersedes an investigation epic). 'Open linked bug' alone is not the discriminator — causation is. Incentive risk: the check keys on voluntary links; blocking legitimate deferrals teaches agents to stop linking.

## Approach
Three stages at epic close (verify-completion, epic path only):
1. DET floor: any OPEN/IN_PROGRESS bug with caused_by -> epic or any descendant = deterministic block (like the direct-children gate, completion.py ~:90). Reverse-edge read primitive, concretely: caused_by is DIRECTIONAL, stored on the BUG's own compiled deps[] with no reciprocal on the epic side — so the floor (and the stage-2 filter) enumerate open/in_progress bugs via the list-tickets read and scan each bug's deps[] for edges whose target resolves into the epic-subtree id set; the epic's own deps[] cannot supply these edges. Semantically unambiguous; 0 historical FPs; teaches: fix it, re-parent it, or dispute the link. Known-limited standalone coverage (caused_by edges are mostly auto-derived at a bug's own close, so open orphans rarely carry one) — the floor is the cheap deterministic tier; coverage of unlinked orphans comes from stages 2-3.
2. DET candidate filter for the screen: status in {open,in_progress} AND type=bug AND (created after the epic's FIRST in_progress transition OR linked any-relation/any-depth to the epic subtree, both directions). Timing-anchor read primitive: the first open->in_progress STATUS event from the epic's event directory, read WITH retired tombstones (the event_metrics._event_files idiom, include_retired=True — snapshot compaction folds old events, so the compiled state alone cannot supply it). Fallback when NO in_progress event exists at all (epic closed straight from open, or predates the workflow): anchor on the epic's creation timestamp — wider window, safe direction (over-inclusion only feeds the cheap screen). Backtested fan-out: median 3, p90 11, max 24 (descriptive, not a bound). Enforced screen ceiling: at most 32 candidates are evaluated per close — linked-to-subtree candidates first, then by created timestamp descending — and any remainder is recorded in the sidecar tally as an unevaluated-overflow count (visible to the operator, never silently dropped). Commit-relation criterion evaluated and REJECTED: 0 unique catches, 2 FPs, 58% of bug-cited SHAs already unresolvable (Gerrit rebase rot), and comment-hygiene work drains SHA citations from bug bodies going forward.
3. Haiku relevance screen: single-turn per candidate, forced choice {A: describes a defect in something this epic changed/built or behavior its AC claims; B: same subsystem, pre-existing or adjacent; C: unrelated} + one-line citation. Epic material (title/description/AC/children titles) in the system prompt for prompt caching; one warm call then parallel fan-out, reusing the warm-then-fan-out orchestration pattern of plan_review/pass1.py (extract the shared helper only if it lifts cleanly; otherwise mirror the pattern with a citation comment — no speculative refactor of pass1). MUST ride the model-class config + shared cache settings (bug afeb-bc04: hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass model-class config — do not add another instance; bug 7a79: 4096-token cache floor means small epics may not cache — acceptable, haiku is cheap uncached).
Forward A-verdicts to the completion verifier as compact evidence: title + screen citation + ticket id (~40 tokens each), cap 8 with titles-only overflow count. Forwarding path, concretely: the compact candidate block is appended INSIDE the fenced context assembled by completion_precheck (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:45, via operations.assemble_context) as a clearly-delimited 'unresolved bug candidates' section — no completion_precheck_output schema change. The verifier's native read-only show_ticket tool retrieves detail on demand — no context squeeze, no new plumbing. Screen output contract follows the overlap_verdict idiom (contracts.py:175): a prompt file with `outputs:` naming a new epic_bug_screen_verdict schema registered in contracts.py — forced choice A/B/C + one-line citation — with a normalizing validator; no hand-rolled JSON parsing. The validator's normalization DEFAULT is C (unrelated): any out-of-vocabulary, malformed, or missing verdict coerces to the non-surfacing value, mirroring overlap_verdict's safe default (related_distinct) — a garbled screen output degrades open and never fabricates an A-candidate. Verifier directive (landed as an edit to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md, where the adjudication rule lives next to the context it reads): block only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition. A disposition SATISFIES via store-grounded signals the verifier checks through show_ticket — (a) a supersedes or duplicates link (either direction) connecting the bug to the epic subtree or to a named successor ticket, or (b) a reasoned pre-existence/deferral assertion in the bug's description or comments, judged for substance (a bare 'out of scope' does not qualify). close_class NEVER satisfies (it exists only on closed bugs; candidates are open/in_progress by construction). Fixture mapping: c8ed satisfies via (a) (carries a real supersedes link to the investigation epic); 30d3 via (b) (description proves pre-existence); e6a0 via (b) (its supersession exists ONLY as comment prose — 'Superseded by epic 4702-a55c-7aeb-445a…' — with no supersedes/duplicates link; store verified). Prose-only supersession is intentionally handled by (b), not (a): (a) is the link-shaped fast path, (b) is the substance-judged prose path, and e6a0 proves the common case where agents record supersession in prose without linking. This protects the linking incentive. Record the full screen tally (per-bug verdict + citation) in the completion sidecar for audit and live FN calibration. Screen failure degrades open (log + skip), never blocks the close by itself; the DET floor is the hard tier. --force-close remains the operator escape hatch.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py (DET floor beside the direct-children gate; candidate filter)
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py (completion_precheck: (i) the DET-floor ENFORCEMENT short-circuit, mirroring the unclosed-child gate at ~:63-74 — an open/in_progress caused_by bug returns run_verify=False + precheck_failed=True + a deterministic FAIL verdict (same shape as deterministic_child_failure), NO LLM call; (ii) append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md (adjudication directive + disposition rule)
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/epic_bug_screen.md (new prompt, `outputs: epic_bug_screen_verdict`) + the full three-file overlap_verdict registration idiom: src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (response model + normalizing validator), src/rebar/schemas/epic_bug_screen_verdict.schema.json (the JSON schema), and src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py (EPIC_BUG_SCREEN_VERDICT constant + __all__ + prompt->schema map entry, mirroring OVERLAP_VERDICT at ~:130/:318)
- new module for the screen (module-size policy: keep completion.py under cap), e.g. src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py (screen tally recording)
- docs/plan-review-gate.md (close-gate section) + docs/llm-framework.md
- tests: unit for filter + floor + forwarding cap; regression fixtures below

## Testing
Regression set from the event-precise backtest — must-block: 30a2-4f2a, 5b09-4f3d (real at-close deliverable defects). Must-pass: 30d3-eaf0 (description proves pre-existence), e6a0-ba9b (disposition trail: filed then superseded by epic 4702), c8ed-d52d (supersedes an investigation epic — investigate/file/close is correct). Documented-unreachable, assert NOT flagged: 5e94-3841 (created 13 days post-close), 22f5-5a48 (fixed during epic, 2h before close). DET floor unit tests: open caused_by bug blocks; closed caused_by bug passes; discovered_from alone does not trip the floor. Filter unit tests: timing window uses FIRST in_progress transition; any-depth link traversal both directions. Screen: fan-out cap, warm-then-parallel ordering, degrade-open on model failure, tally lands in sidecar. All regression/unit tests are LLM-free at BOTH tiers: the screen runs through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map, AND the verifier decision path is faked/stubbed — automated must-block fixtures assert the DET-floor short-circuit (caused_by cases) or assert UP TO the forwarded candidate block (content + cap + overflow in the assembled fenced context); automated must-pass fixtures assert no floor trip and correct candidate forwarding. The REAL verifier's store-grounded disposition adjudication (30a2+5b09 block; 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass) is proven exclusively in the [operator-attested] live calibration AC — matching the repo's LLM-test idiom; the live haiku path likewise runs only in that calibration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] DET caused_by floor blocks epic close with an open/in_progress caused_by bug in the subtree, with a teaching message (fix / re-parent / dispute link).
- [x] Candidate filter implements exactly: open|in_progress bugs AND (created-after-first-in_progress OR linked-any-relation-any-depth); commit-relation is NOT implemented.
- [x] Screen rides model-class config + shared cache settings (no hand-built client), forced-choice output with citation, parallel after cache warm.
- [x] Verifier receives at most 8 compact candidates (title+citation+id) + overflow count inside the precheck-assembled fenced context (verified by a forwarding unit test on the assembled string).
- [x] Verifier adjudicates via show_ticket on demand and blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects per the store-grounded disposition rule — (a) supersedes/duplicates link, or (b) reasoned pre-existence/supersession prose; never close_class (verified by the must-block/must-pass regression fixtures).
- [x] Screen verdict rides a registered output schema + normalizing validator (overlap_verdict idiom); verifier directive text lands in completion_verifier.md.
- [x] Screen tally recorded in the completion sidecar, including the unevaluated-overflow count when the 32-candidate screen ceiling truncates; screen failure degrades open with a logged reason.
- [x] Full regression set above encoded as tests (must-block, must-pass, not-flagged).
- [x] docs/plan-review-gate.md close-gate section documents the three-stage gate (DET floor, candidate filter, screen + disposition rule) and docs/llm-framework.md references the epic_bug_screen prompt/schema.
- [x] [operator-attested] One live calibration run over the regression fixtures recorded on this ticket: (i) per-bug haiku A/B/C tally with timestamp, proving the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path end-to-end, AND (ii) the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture through the REAL disposition rule (live run 2026-08-03: 30a2 block; 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass; 5b09 pass — original must-block adjudication corrected against snapshot evidence of pre-close production recovery, see calibration comment); automated tests stay on the fake verdict map.
baseline.summary: Epic-close bug gate: DET caused_by floor + filtered haiku relevance screen + verifier adjudication

content.text: ## Why
The base (Pass-1) and verifier (Pass-2) prompts are the shared spine of the gate. Two evidence-backed
calibration changes belong here, kept minimal so the architecture's separation of concerns holds.
## What
- Base prompt: add ONE positive-framed linter/CI-deference line ("automated tooling already enforces
style/format/imports/types; your value is substantive issues they cannot see"). Justified by the
in-repo experiment (recall 2.0->2.33 substantive with fewer nits, Sonnet tier). NOTE: the experiment
also found the pink-elephant priming fear NOT SUPPORTED at small scale (n=3 diffs, deterministic reps)
— treat this as DIRECTIONAL, not proven; the durable guard is the eval no-fire case, not the claim.
- Pass-2 verifier (code-review-verify.md ONLY, not the shared kernel): add domain-agnostic verification
discipline — evidence-contradiction rubric ("authoritative tone is not evidence"), caller verification
before crediting reachability, step-by-step arithmetic for computed claims, and absence-claim
active-search feeding the EXISTING sub-questions (no new axis, no contract change). Guidance prefers
AST/LSP/code-graph tools over grep when available, grep as fallback.
## Scope
Edits to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md and code-review-verify.md. No kernel/contract change;
plan-review's shared verifier untouched. Dropped from the original bundle: verbatim excerpt,
threshold-invariance language, fragility naming (compensating mechanisms rebar solves elsewhere).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Base prompt has exactly one positive-framed deference line; nit/recall eval passes.
- [ ] Verifier prompt adds contradiction rubric, caller verification, arithmetic gate, absence search.
- [ ] Verifier guidance prefers AST/LSP tools when available, falls back to grep.
- [ ] No change to the shared verification contract or plan-review verifier; plan-review evals green.

## Why / Summary

The inbound link differ maps Jira `Blocks` issuelinks to the INVERTED rebar relation
(`blocks`<->`depends_on`). Latent since f6687adf4 (2026-06-15); UNMASKED when the
outbound direction fix (6b25dbead/43d154523) corrected the write path — the two
inversions had been cancelling on round-trip. Result: ~815 inbound link applies/pass
are cycle-rejected by rebar's guard, and the reconciler never converges.

## Root cause (proven, LIVE-validated)

- `_diff_links_inbound` (inbound_differ.py:519-527) AND `_diff_link_removals`
  (outbound_links.py:198-203) both invert inward/outward -> relation.
- LIVE Jira ground truth: REB-458 ("0250 blocks ba7e") carries `outwardIssue: REB-461`
  with `type.outward == "blocks"`. So **outwardIssue+Blocks => rebar `blocks`;
  inwardIssue+Blocks => rebar `depends_on`.** The code does the OPPOSITE (verified by
  running the current `_diff_links_inbound` on real REB-461 JSON — it emits the
  cycle-causing inverse).

## Chronic-pattern guardrails (this fix MUST NOT repeat prior failures)

Prior link fixes (3f04, c8ed, 3b86) each corrected ONE seam and were validated by a
ROUND-TRIP / self-consistency oracle that is invariant under double inversion — so the
mirror stayed broken and every audit read through the inversion. This fix must:

- [ ] Fix BOTH mirror sites in lockstep (inbound add AND removal path).
- [ ] UNIFY the duplicated direction logic into ONE helper (the inward/outward->relation
      mapping is copy-pasted in inbound_differ.py and outbound_links.py; `_JIRA_LINK_TO_RELATION`
      is re-declared in acli_graph.py:53, inbound_differ.py:459). One source of truth so the
      next inversion cannot reappear on an untouched copy.
- [ ] Assert ABSOLUTE direction pinned to a captured LIVE-JIRA ground-truth fixture
      (real REB-458/461 issuelinks JSON), NOT round-trip agreement. A test that asserts
      "outbound<->inbound agree" is banned here — it passes on inverted code.

## The completeness requirement (a pure branch-swap is NOT sufficient)

Measured on 17 real tickets: a pure swap eliminates the 30 cycle-rejections but then
emits ~all MIRROR-adds (the counterpart already owns the edge; ~400 spurious deps
store-wide). The fix must add INVERSE-AWARE CROSS-TICKET dedup: emit an inbound link
only if the edge X<->Y is absent in rebar in EITHER equivalent form (X has (blocks,Y)
OR Y has (depends_on,X); and the relates_to symmetric case). `compute_inbound_mutations`
already receives `local_tickets_by_id`, so the counterpart's deps are available.

- [ ] The dedup map MUST include the FULL local set (incl. archived tickets) — a residual
      mirror to archived cf10 in the live prototype was ONLY a map-exclusion artifact;
      cf10 owns the inverse edge. Verify `local_tickets_by_id` completeness or the fix
      re-emits mirrors to archived counterparts.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Local ticket A has dep `A blocks B`; both bound to Jira; outbound has (correctly)
   written REB-A outward Blocks -> REB-B.
2. Run inbound diff (or a reconcile pass).
3. Observe: inbound emits `A depends_on B` (inverted) -> rebar cycle-guard rejects it
   ("would create a cycle"). Expected: 0 inbound emits (edge already synced).

- Expected: inbound emits 0 link mutations for an already-synced link (either direction).
- Actual: inbound emits the inverted relation, cycle-rejected every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `_diff_links_inbound` unit test on the CAPTURED LIVE REB-458 issuelinks JSON
      (outwardIssue Blocks) asserts relation == `blocks`; on REB-461 JSON (inwardIssue
      Blocks) asserts relation == `depends_on`. RED on current code. Proving command:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/ -k link_direction -q`.
- [ ] A `_diff_links_inbound` test with the counterpart owning the inverse edge asserts
      0 emitted mutations (inverse-aware dedup). RED on a pure-swap fix.
- [ ] The removal-path mirror (`_diff_link_removals`) has an equivalent absolute-direction
      test. RED on current code.
- [ ] Existing tests that encode the reversed convention (test_reconcile_roundtrip.py:522,
      test_link_dedup.py:198) are corrected to the live-Jira shape and pass.
- [ ] LIVE fix-verification (pre-land): the fixed inbound differ, run against real REB
      issuelinks for the ~815 affected pairs, emits 0 cycle-rejecting mutations and 0
      mirror-adds (prototype already validated: converges to 0 with the full local map).
- [ ] `make test` passes; no new external dependency.

## Notes
P2 of epic 58b0. Blocked-independent of P1. The observability promotion (separate child)
should land AFTER this so the reconciler isn't flipped to fail-loud while this noise exists.
baseline.summary: Inbound link differ inverts blocks<->depends_on (unmasked by outbound fix); needs inverse-aware cross-ticket dedup

## Dependencies (STACKED — review with --ref HEAD)
Documents the whole identity epic shipped by ddbe/4e9d/bde5/e165/264f/2f13/3183 (all
committed on this branch). Review with `--ref HEAD`.

## Context
Document the authenticated-identity model end-to-end so operators and agents can
adopt it, and record the load-bearing architectural decisions as an ADR.

## What
### 1. `docs/identity.md` — the identity model end-to-end
A new operator/agent guide covering, with concrete `rebar identity …` examples:
- **The `identity` entity** (`src/rebar/…`): a gate/graph/Jira-sync-exempt ticket-type
  (like `session_log`) holding name, email, `{provider, external_id}` mappings, and
  public keys; the `.rebar/current_identity` self-identity pointer.
- **Tiers**: real identities vs. `placeholder` ghosts (inbound-minted, idempotently
  upgraded) — how to tell them apart (`is_placeholder`) and how ghosts get promoted.
- **Event attribution**: every local event carries denormalized `author`/`author_email`
  + optional `author_id`; replay back-compat.
- **Authorship attestation** (`rebar.authorship.v1`): SSHSIG over the foundation attest
  substrate; trust root = the identity's in-band keys.
- **Key rotation / era-scoping**: TOFU genesis, signed add/revoke, epoch-scoped validity
  (`identity key add|revoke`), and WHY validity is merged-log-position (epoch) not
  wall-clock.
- **Provider-neutral Jira mapping**: outbound assignee/reporter by opaque accountId, the
  `/user/search` bootstrap, and the **Modify-Reporter** permission constraint +
  documented degradation.
- **Opt-in enforcement**: `identity.require_authenticated`, the write-gate, and the
  crucial **"the merge-gate is the control; the local write-gate is UX-only"** caveat;
  replay-never-rejects; `rebar verify-authorship`.

### 2. ADR `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md`
Records the load-bearing decisions and their rationale/alternatives:
- **git-bug-style entity**: identity as a first-class event-sourced ticket entity
  (reusing the exempt-type substrate) rather than a side table.
- **Opaque-id keying**: mappings keyed on the provider's stable opaque id, NEVER email.
- **In-band TOFU**: trust-on-first-use genesis keys carried in-band on the identity,
  with a signed rotation chain (filling git-bug's IsProtected), and era-scoped validity.

### 3. Docs index
Add `docs/identity.md` (and the ADR per the ADR-dir convention) to the docs index so
the docs-index completeness gate stays green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/identity.md` exists and covers ALL of: the identity model, tiers, opt-in
  enforcement + the merge-gate-is-the-control caveat, Jira accountId mapping +
  Modify-Reporter constraint, key-rotation/era-scoping, and the provider-neutral seam.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` exists and records the git-bug-entity,
  opaque-id-keying, and in-band-TOFU decisions (context / decision / consequences).
- [ ] The docs-index completeness gate passes (`python scripts/check_docs_index.py
  --check` exits 0) with the new docs indexed.

## file_impact
- `docs/identity.md` (new operator/agent guide)
- `docs/adr/0045-authenticated-identity.md` (new ADR)
- the docs index file (add the new docs so check_docs_index passes)

# Re-home the outbound parent-CLEAR live cell to the Epic Link path

`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is one of three permanent reds in the live DC suite. It clears a **sub-task's** `fields.parent`, which Data Center will not do. Its INBOUND twin was already re-homed to the Epic Link by ticket 37e7's approved ruling; the outbound twin never was.

## The three reds are three DIFFERENT problems, not one

That reframing is the finding — treating them as one platform limitation is what kept them together in red.

| cell | real blocker | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` | the cell picked a sub-task; the Epic Link path is reachable | **this ticket** |
| `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | rebar must do the write and DC accepts-and-ignores it — unreachable, and its coverage is already green elsewhere | `xfail(strict=True)` |
| `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` | the DC-side reparent is only SETUP; the subject is rebar's inbound pass | re-target to adoption |

The outbound-set behaviour rebar can actually deliver is already pinned green by `test_a_subtask_reparent_is_REFUSED_rather_than_silently_ignored`, so `xfail(strict=True)` there loses no coverage — and an xpass would FAIL the suite, a stronger signal than today's permanent red.

## Why the Epic Link clear is believed reachable (source-verified)

 * `_resolve_local_parent` returns `(True, None)` for a locally-detached ticket regardless of
   parent type — the epic-only guard suppresses *sets*, not *clears*.
 * `fetcher.merge_parent_map` overlays `client.get_parent_map()`, and 9bb9 taught DC's
   `get_parent_map` to fall back to the Epic Link — so a standard issue under an epic yields a
   truthy `remote_parent_id` and the clear is observable outbound.
 * `set_parent` for a non-sub-task writes `{epic_link_field_id: None}` — the same path as a set.

Two gates the cell must be built around, or it will fail for the wrong reason:
 1. `should_propagate_removal` requires the ref to be MANAGED — so the cell must have **rebar**
    set the Epic Link in a priming pass, not create it Jira-side.
 2. `_peer_removed_the_parent` (339a) short-circuits on a truthy remote parent, so it does not
    interfere.

## THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN

**Whether `{epic_link_field_id: None}` actually clears on DC 8.17.1 is UNTESTED.** The capability map measured that WRITING the Epic Link works (req-0040/0041); clearing it was never probed. Do not write the cell before this is answered — that is exactly how changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 each shipped merged, mutation-proven and wrong.

A targeted, deterministic probe is added by this ticket: `scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py` + `.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml`. It is NOT the capability map — no LLM, no agent, four predetermined REST calls — so it settles the question without re-running or churning the map's committed answers.

## A related gap this surfaced

`set_parent`'s **non-sub-task branch has no read-back verification**, unlike the sub-task branch that 1a9f added. If the Epic Link clear silently no-ops, that is invisible today. Worth closing regardless of the probe's answer, though the probe's result decides whether adding it makes `set_parent` start refusing epic-parent clears (correct, and the same move 1a9f made).

## Ruled out, with evidence — do not re-investigate

 * **screen provisioning for `parent`** — REFUTED. `OrderableField` is defined as "fields able to
   be placed on screens" and Jira Server 8.x has NO Parent implementation of it; `parent` is
   absent from `/rest/api/2/field` (JRASERVER-47377, closed unfixed). It cannot be screened. This
   does not contradict the map's screen-gating finding, which was about a field that EXISTS.
 * **sub-task ⟷ standard conversion via REST** — no such endpoint in the 8.17.0 reference
   (JRASERVER-27893 open since 2012; the adjacent issuetype-change request closed Won't Do).
 * **bulk edit / `/issue/move` / `overrideScreenSecurity`** — none exist on DC 8.x
   (`/subtask/move` is sibling REORDERING); `overrideScreenSecurity` occurs zero times in the
   8.17/8.22/9.4/9.12 references — Cloud-and-app-only.
 * **delete-and-recreate** — rejected: new key, lost history, and a broken binding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the probe runs in CI and its verdict on `{epic_link: null}` is recorded here
- [ ] if it CLEARS: `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is re-homed to the Epic Link path
      (rebar-set parent in a priming pass) and is GREEN on a live run, with the run id recorded
- [ ] if it does NOT clear: that is a product defect — file it, and add the missing read-back to
      `set_parent`'s non-sub-task branch so it stops reporting a no-op as success
- [ ] `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` is `xfail(strict=True)` with a reason citing
      the measured platform limitation
- [ ] no cell is weakened to pass — no skips, no deleted assertions, no round-trip loosened
baseline.summary: Re-home the outbound parent-CLEAR live cell to the Epic Link path (probe first)

content.text: ## Why
The signed result is the composable CI rigor / anti-vibe-coding signal.
## What
- HMAC-sign the review result under the MCP environment key (reuse the close-gate signing machinery); bind to
the latest MATERIAL event commit; invalidate on material edits (description/AC/file_impact/decomposition;
not tags/comments/links/assignee); record coverage.
## Scope
- Reuse the close-gate signing; no new key custody. Integrity/forgery/replay/staleness model inherited.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sign + material-commit bind + invalidation-on-material-edit; coverage recorded.

baseline.description:
## Summary
A vanished git object poisons the SHARED index and CASCADES: `git commit` (whole-index) fails
`error: invalid object <sha> for '<path>'` / `error: Error building trees`, and because the
failed commit leaves the poisoned entry staged, EVERY subsequent write's commit fails
identically until the index is reset. This is the residual behind the enrich-prune
concurrency flake after Mode A (4f8d) and Mode B (ac26) were fixed (CI: `lost=28..50
swallowed_write_raises=28..50`, all on ONE object). Genesis: a loose object that vanishes
between `git add` and `git commit` (a background gc repack, or a partial/interrupted object
write under CI FS/memory pressure).

## Reproduction Steps
1. Baseline commit so HEAD exists. 2. Stage an event file, then delete its loose object
   (`objects/xx/rest`) — a vanished object. 3. A NEW rebar write's whole-index commit builds a
   tree from the index and fails `invalid object … Error building trees`; the next write
   fails identically (proven cascade — `tests/.../test_event_append_transient_retry.py`).

**Expected:** a locked write self-heals and no write is lost.
**Actual (pre-fix):** the poison persists (the per-path `_unstage` clears the CURRENT write's
path, never the earlier poison's) and wedges every later commit.

## Root Cause
`git write-tree` verifies each index blob EXISTS; a missing one fails the tree build. The
failed commit leaves the poisoned entry in the index. rebar's existing recovery only unstages
the current write's path, so a cross-path poison is never cleared → cascade.

## Fix
`event_append._recover_from_invalid_object`: on the `invalid object`/`Error building trees`
signature, `git read-tree HEAD` (reset the WHOLE index to HEAD — drops the poison regardless
of path; worktree untouched), re-`git add` this write's file(s) — regenerating a missing
object from the intact worktree file — and retry the commit. Non-destructive on a false
positive; bounded (one recovery attempt); emits a WARNING naming any orphaned worktree path.
Verified accepted pattern (git-annex regenerates its index identically); vetted by an
adversarial code review (APPROVE) and a prior-art sweep (acceptable-with-caveats, all met).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A cross-path vanished-object poison self-heals instead of cascading; a subsequent write
  also succeeds (RED test `test_cross_path_poisoned_index_self_heals`, mutation-checked).
- [ ] A write whose OWN object vanished regenerates it and commits
  (`test_own_vanished_object_is_regenerated`).
- [ ] The heal logs a WARNING naming any orphaned worktree path (observability guardrail).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` pass; the enrich-prune concurrency test passes; no
  existing store test weakened.
baseline.summary: Vanished git object poisons the shared index and cascades all writes (enrich-prune Mode D)

baseline.description:
## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` "Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets" step exhausts its 5 retries and fails the workflow red under normal `tickets`-branch contention. Spun out of bug `449f-f9bf-be90-47fe` (mode 2), whose fix covered the other two failure modes; this one is separated because it changes retry semantics of a shared push path and needs a contention harness to test honestly.

Two distinct defects, plus a disposition question.

## Defect 1 — the backoff is anti-adaptive for this failure class

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:328`:

```sh
backoff=$(( (1 << attempt) + RANDOM % 3 ))
```

By the time this sleep runs, the loop has **already** fetched and merged `origin/tickets` (`:321`), so its HEAD is a valid fast-forward *at that instant*. The only thing that can invalidate it is another push landing first. Sleeping therefore monotonically increases the probability of losing the very race the retry exists to win — and the sleep **grows** (3 → 6 → 10 → 17s) exactly as the remaining attempt budget shrinks.

Exponential backoff is correct for load-shedding against an overloaded or rate-limited server. It is the wrong algorithm for an optimistic-concurrency CAS on a hot append-only ref, where the correct move after a successful merge is to re-push **immediately**.

## Evidence — full retry timeline recovered from run 30585738860

Every one of the five rejections is preceded by a *successful* merge and a *successful* remote-tracking advance. The merges converge; only the push loses.

```
22:13:23.7  pre-loop fetch                      60ccc6506..4d37b6925
22:13:24.2  attempt 1 rejected (non-fast-forward)
22:13:24.7  merge OK (ort), "Waiting 3s"
22:13:28.3  attempt 2 rejected                  4d37b6925..dd70be0d7
22:13:29.0  merge OK, "Waiting 6s"
22:13:35.5  attempt 3 rejected                  dd70be0d7..a46013f4c
22:13:36.2  merge OK, "Waiting 10s"
22:13:46.7  attempt 4 rejected                  a46013f4c..f3a1fe61f
22:13:47.5  merge OK, "Waiting 17s"
22:14:05.0  attempt 5 rejected                  f3a1fe61f..939e92676
22:14:05.7  merge OK — never pushed, loop exits, exit 1
```

Derived: five remote advances over 41.9s => mean competitor interval **~8.4s**. Backoff budget 30-38s of a ~42s loop. Each remote advance lands *inside* the corresponding sleep.

Modelled with Poisson competitors at lambda = 1/8.4s, the per-attempt loss probabilities are 35% / 54% / 72% / 88%, giving **P(all five fail) ~= 12% per run**. With no sleep (window ~0.6s) the same model gives **~1.7e-6**.

Observed rate is consistent: 4 failures on 2026-07-30 clustered in contention bursts.

## Defect 2 — the final merge is computed and then discarded

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:296-332`: the loop body is `push -> classify -> fetch -> merge -> (if attempt < max) sleep`. On attempt 5 it performs a full fetch+merge and then falls out of the `while` **without ever pushing that merge**. The log above shows it: `f3a1fe61f..939e92676` is merged at 22:14:05.7 and the next line is `Push failed after 5 retries`.

That discarded merge had, by construction, just produced a fast-forwardable HEAD — a free ~93%-likely attempt thrown away. Five pushes cost five merges and used four.

## The authority this violates

The workflow states its own intent at `:315-320`: the merge-not-rebase choice "mirrors the local client path (`_store/push.py`) and invariant I1 (`docs/concurrency.md`)". The path it claims to mirror has **no backoff at all** — `src/rebar/_store/push.py:167-210` re-pushes immediately on the next iteration after `merge.returncode == 0 -> continue`. The workflow deviates from its stated reference implementation in precisely the dimension that determines convergence.

## Open question — is red even the right disposition?

`docs/concurrency.md:297-300` states the contract for this operation: "Push is **best-effort**: a failed push (no network, unresolvable non-fast-forward, recovery state) **never fails the caller** — it warns, leaves local commits intact, and the branch stays diverged. `rebar fsck` surfaces that divergence as a `PUSH_PENDING` notice ... so it is not silent." `push.py:265` and `:286-291` implement exactly that: warn, return, raise nothing.

The workflow instead exits 1. It has no `PUSH_PENDING` equivalent, so the missing artifact may be the notice channel rather than the severity.

Counter-consideration that must be settled first, NOT assumed: the runner is ephemeral, so a lost push discards the merged local commits with the container, while the Jira-side mutations were already applied. Whether that is benign depends on whether the next pass re-derives the same events. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:151-154` suggests it does ("a pass that times out makes no durable progress and the next pass re-does the work"), but that is about a timed-out pass, not a lost push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and record whether an exhausted push race should be red or a
      `PUSH_PENDING`-style non-red notice, resolving it against
      `docs/concurrency.md:297-300` rather than by preference. Evidence required:
      confirm for the 4 failed runs (30503669644, 30510284129, 30515516036,
      30585738860) that the events they failed to push were re-derived by a later
      pass, and that no duplicate Jira issue was created for the same `local_id`.
- [ ] Retry-after-successful-merge no longer sleeps an increasing interval; the
      re-push after a clean merge is immediate (matching `_store/push.py`).
      Any retained delay is justified in a comment against a named failure mode.
- [ ] The final merge is either pushed or not computed — no iteration performs a
      merge whose result is provably discarded.
- [ ] A deterministic contention harness covers this: a scripted competitor that
      pushes before each attempt, asserting the loop converges rather than
      exhausting. RED against the current loop first.
- [x] Post-fix verification. The `>= 500 runs` population gate is **WAIVED by
      operator decision (2026-07-31)**, same rationale as the sibling criterion on
      449f: it is wall-clock-bound and adds nothing about the mechanism. Replaced by,
      and satisfied by, the deterministic harness — a scripted competitor that pushes
      before each of the 5 attempts and then stops, driving the workflow's own YAML
      block verbatim. Both halves are mutation-checked: removing the final push returns
      it to RED on convergence, and restoring the exponential sleep returns it to RED
      on wall-clock (~37s vs ~3s). Post-fix production sample at close: **0 runs** —
      the fix landed minutes before close, so there is NO population evidence here at
      all, and none is claimed. The mechanism proof is the whole of the evidence.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` (lines 294-335);
      `src/rebar/_store/push.py` if the budgets are reconciled (it uses 3, the
      workflow 5).
baseline.summary: Reconcile Bridge push retry: exponential backoff is anti-adaptive for a CAS race, and the final merge is computed then discarded

## Why

`fsck` Check 3 (`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:148-171`) reclaims a stale git `index.lock` with the SAME time-of-check-to-time-of-use race that story df83 (sundried-bonny-sloth) just hardened in `gitutil._reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`: it reads `os.path.getmtime(lock_file)`, judges stale, then unconditionally `os.remove(lock_file)`. A peer can remove the stale lock and drop a fresh LIVE lock at the same path in that window, and fsck then unlinks the peer's live lock — corrupting the peer's index.

## What

Mirror the df83 hardening: re-validate device+inode+age immediately before the unlink; abort on inode-change or refreshed mtime. Consider extracting the now-hardened reclaim helper from `gitutil` and reusing it here so the two paths cannot drift again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] fsck Check 3 re-checks file identity (device+inode) and age at the moment of removal; mismatch aborts the unlink.
- [ ] A deterministic inode-replacement-during-reclaim regression test covers the fsck path (or the shared helper it now calls).
- [ ] Existing fsck stale-lock behavior (stationary stale lock removed; young lock left) still passes.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: Harden fsck Check 3 stale index.lock reclaim against the same TOCTOU as df83

# S7 — Documentation, ADR, and regenerated references for MCP auth

## Why
The capability must be usable and auditable by a third-party operator, and the design decisions +
residual risks must be recorded for maintainers and the rigorous security review. This story writes
the operator guide and the ADR, and does the FINAL consistency check of the derived reference
artifacts (each key-adding story S1–S6 already registers ITS keys and regenerates its slice; S7
confirms the integrated whole is consistent).

## What
- New `docs/mcp-auth.md` — the operator guide:
  - How to enable the HTTP transport + auth; each of the five verifier modes (`static`, `jwt`,
    `introspection`, `proxy`, `custom`) with a flat-config example each, and the closed
    `auth_strategies` vocabulary. State the flat-schema limitation: **one instance per strategy type**
    (for multiple issuers, use the `custom` verifier).
  - The **security model:** resource-server-only (no AS/DCR); the composite as the single audience/
    fail-closed choke point (every token's `resource` == `auth_resource_server_url`, RFC 8707); no
    token passthrough; DNS-rebinding/Origin defaults; the non-loopback bind requirements (allowlists
    + TLS-at-edge ack); tokens/secrets never logged.
  - **Behind-a-proxy deployment:** TLS terminates at the edge (nginx/ALB) and rebar binds loopback;
    the external host must be in `http_allowed_hosts` and the external origin in `http_allowed_origins`;
    `auth_resource_server_url` MUST be the external https URL (it drives the served PRM `resource` and
    the `WWW-Authenticate: resource_metadata` URL — NOT the request scheme), and is validated https
    for non-loopback. Include a concrete nginx/ALB header + allowlist example.
  - **The three interactive-client connection paths** (so RS-only isn't experienced as "can't
    connect"): (1) static bearer via Claude Code `--header "Authorization: Bearer …"` / Claude.ai
    `static_headers` — pairs with the static verifier; (2) automatic OAuth when the org IdP supports
    DCR or CIMD (Keycloak/Auth0/Okta can); (3) pre-registered `--client-id`/`--client-secret` for
    IdPs without anonymous DCR (Entra, Cognito). Note rebar serves the PRM that drives discovery.
  - **Residual risks (documented, not fixed here):** authenticated ≠ authorized — any authenticated
    principal wields rebar's full ambient authority (writes auto-push; `reconcile live` uses rebar's
    own creds) gated only by server-level `required_scopes` and the existing `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`/
    `ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`/`ALLOW_LLM` env gates, which now also gate remote actors; per-tool
    scope→capability authorization is deferred; rate-limiting/brute-force is delegated to the edge
    proxy in v1, with mandated ≥128-bit static tokens (document the generator one-liner).
- A new ADR under `docs/adr/` recording: the resource-server-only decision (no AS / no DCR); building
  our own verifiers on the official SDK seam vs adopting standalone `fastmcp` (semver-exempt auth,
  CVE history); the composite audience choke point (motivated by the SDK having no `.resource`
  backstop + the audience-confusion precedent PVE-2026-93393); the five verifier modes; the transport
  hardening (citing GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f DNS-rebinding, oauth2-proxy CVE-2026-40575 forwarded-header,
  CVE-2026-27124 confused-deputy); and the explicitly deferred items (AS/DCR, per-tool authz,
  in-process rate-limiting, AWS deployment).
- **Final reference/manifest consistency check:** confirm `docs/mcp-reference.md`/`docs/env-vars.md`
  are fully regenerated for the integrated set of new keys and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` +
  the reference drift gates pass on the combined branch (S1–S6 each regenerated their slice; S7
  verifies the union).

## Approach & rationale
Documentation-and-ADR story sequenced last so it documents the *actually shipped* surface (S1–S6);
regeneration (not hand-editing) keeps the derived docs authoritative and drift-gated. A docs/mechanical
leaf — no runtime behavior.

## Scope
`docs/mcp-auth.md`, the ADR, and the final reference/manifest consistency verification only. No code
behavior. Subset of the epic. Depends on S1–S6 (documents them).

## Acceptance Criteria
The ADR filename is fixed at `docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md`; each criterion
below has a single, unambiguous shell proving command that exits 0.

- [ ] `docs/mcp-auth.md` exists and covers: enabling HTTP+auth; all five verifier modes with a
      flat-config example each + the `auth_strategies` vocabulary + the one-instance-per-type
      limitation; the security model (composite audience choke point, fail-closed, no passthrough);
      behind-a-proxy deployment (TLS + allowlists + `auth_resource_server_url` drives discovery URLs)
      with an nginx/ALB example; the three interactive-client connection paths; and the residual risks
      (per-tool authz deferral, rate-limiting delegation, static-token entropy). Proving command:
      `test -f docs/mcp-auth.md && for h in 'Enabling the HTTP transport' '### `static`' '### `jwt`' '### `introspection`' '### `proxy`' '### `custom`' 'single audience' 'Behind a proxy' 'interactive-client' 'out of scope'; do grep -Fq "$h" docs/mcp-auth.md || exit 1; done`
      (each required section string is present).
- [ ] `docs/mcp-auth.md` is linked from `docs/README.md`. Proving command:
      `grep -Fq 'mcp-auth.md' docs/README.md && python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check`
      (the docs-index completeness gate exits 0 with the new file linked).
- [ ] The ADR `docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md` exists and records: the
      resource-server-only + build-own-verifiers decision, the composite audience choke point, the five
      verifier modes, the transport-hardening vulnerability CLASSES it mitigates (DNS-rebinding,
      forwarded-header spoofing, confused-deputy, audience-confusion), and the deferred items. The
      advisory identifiers (GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f, CVE-2026-40575, CVE-2026-27124, PVE-2026-93393) are
      cited as upstream-tracked references for those classes, NOT asserted as independently
      NVD-verified facts. Proving command:
      `test -f docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md && for s in 'esource' 'composite' 'DNS-rebinding' 'forwarded-header' 'confused-deputy' 'audience' 'defer'; do grep -Fiq "$s" docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md || exit 1; done`.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-reference.md` and `docs/env-vars.md` are regenerated for the integrated new-key set and
      the drift gates for them and for `server.json` pass. Proving command (all three exit 0):
      `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py --check && python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check && python scripts/check_server_manifest.py`.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass (docs/mechanical leaf; no typecheck-relevant code added here).

## Compatibility
Docs only; no runtime or dependency change beyond what S1–S6 introduced.
baseline.summary: S7 — Documentation, ADR, and regenerated references for MCP auth

## Context
A full re-examination of the plan-review and code-review blocking gates (session logs under this
program; see ideas `neat-sooty-termite`/c34d and `revealable-voracious-groundhog`/8214) established,
with data from 681 plan-review sidecars + the Gerrit code-review corpus + Sonnet-scored simulations
and held-out adjudication, that: (a) plan-review's current blocking set is sound but its 0.70 bar is
too high for several load-bearing criteria and its blocking set should expand; (b) the shared
`impact = mean(severity attributes)` model dilutes high-severity findings below the bar and, for
code-review, structurally mis-measures maintainability/latent-regression findings; (c) verdict-flip
is a finder-recall problem, not a false-positive problem. This epic implements the converged fixes.

## Approved plan-review threshold / posture changes (pre-redesign; must be included)
- Lower `block_threshold` 0.70 -> 0.60 for the criteria with block-worthy findings stranded in the
  0.60-0.70 band: **COH, E2, F1, G5, G6, T5e**.
- Keep **T4 @ 0.70** (its band findings were fail-safe migrations).
- Promote to blocking (`default_posture: blocking`): **G1G2 @0.70, T1 @0.70, T8 @0.70** (100%
  block-worthy at the would-block slice) and **E4 @0.75** (0.75 excludes its one borderline).
- **E1, T3** stay advisory (no threshold reaches 100% block-worthy; revisit later); **A1** stays advisory.
- Ship the **deterministic G5 decomposition signal** and **Pass-1 finding-memory** (recall) — both approved.

## Both impact redesigns (must be included)
- **Plan-review impact** (idea c34d): replace the diluting mean with severity-first **MAX + hard
  override** (any of unverifiable-AC / uncertifiable-DoD / undecomposed / divergent-impl -> auto-high),
  plus a **detection amplifier** (silent-vs-self-revealing, DoD-uncertifiable). No new axes.
- **Code-review impact** (idea 8214): a code-review-specific, verifier-embedded model — two lanes
  (**prod/correctness x likelihood-of-firing** and **maintainability x change-frequency floor**),
  each lane = **MAX over tier-tagged binary consequence questions** (carved with charitable carve-outs),
  a **reversibility det/hybrid floor**, a **detection amplifier**, and a **re-anchored scale**;
  dispatched per-gate off the shared `decide.py` kernel (no added LLM calls; Pass-2 is one aggregate call).

## Scope (children — discrete deliverables)
1. Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (config + tests).
2. Deterministic G5 decomposition signal.
3. Plan-review Pass-1 finding-memory (recall).
4. Plan-review impact redesign (MAX + override + detection; per-gate impact dispatch).
5. Code-review impact model redesign (two-lane tier-tagged; re-anchoring; per-gate dispatch).
6. Code-review data capture to the ticket store (change-scoped code_review artifact; PAT + persistent store; emission).
7. Code-review near-term nit reduction + new-behavior-without-test landmine detector.
8. Permissive rollout + calibration harness (corpus accumulation; offline replay + diff-grounded A/B tuning).

## Out of scope
- "Deeper" impact-aggregation reworks beyond the specified models remain parked in ideas c34d/8214.
- Retention/pruning of code-review artifacts (deliberately unbounded for now; revisit if it bites).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The approved plan-review threshold/posture table above is applied in
      `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` with tests.
- [ ] Deterministic G5 signal + Pass-1 finding-memory landed.
- [ ] Plan-review impact redesign landed (mean replaced by MAX/override/detection).
- [ ] Code-review impact redesign landed (two-lane tier-tagged model, re-anchored, per-gate dispatch).
- [ ] Code-review data capture landed and confirmed writing to `tickets` from the reviewbot.
- [ ] Near-term nit reduction + landmine detector landed.
- [ ] Rollout + calibration harness landed; new models ship permissive.
- [ ] All children closed with passing plan-review + completion-verifier.
- [ ] All approved plan-review threshold/posture changes land (the pre-redesign recalibration).
- [ ] Both impact-model redesigns (plan-review AND code-review) implemented per the converged design.
- [ ] Code-review results are captured into the rebar ticket store (change-scoped, PAT-credentialed).
- [ ] New impact models ship at permissive thresholds with a calibration harness accumulating the
- [ ] Every child closes with plan-review + completion-verifier passing.

## Why

on field evidence, with their `false` value being only a "back-out": `progressive_drift_refresh`,

is config debt. Make all three always-on and delete the off switch.

## What

`if not <flag>: return/None` back-out branch, and hardcode the enabled path.

- `progressive_drift_refresh` (`_config_schema.py:251`): reader `_progressive_enabled`

## Why

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` already has the full key-materialize + job-level
signing wiring (story 9e76/cc0b): it reads the `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` secret, masks it
(`::add-mask::`), writes it to a `0600` file at `${RUNNER_TEMP}/rebar-bot-signing-key`, and
exports `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=<that path>` (`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:211-228`),
with the bot email defaulted to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (`:205`, `:267`) so reconciler
events resolve to identity `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`. The wiring is **secret-gated**: with the
secret empty it writes **unsigned/advisory** (`:220-222`). This story confirms CI signs in
steady state — provisioning + verification of existing wiring, not new plumbing. It does **not**
modify the workflow YAML.

## Precondition (verified, not created)

- Identity `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d` (Rebar Bot) already exists (one registered ed25519 key); CI
  resolves to it via the `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL` default. Same identity local signing (79da) uses.
- The canonical private key lives in AWS SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key`
  (ADR-0012); its public half is exactly the key registered on 594c (verified locally by
  `ssh-keygen -y` match during 79da).
- A `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` secret already exists (`gh secret list`, last set 2026-07-14), but a
  GitHub secret value cannot be read back, so its correctness is only *proven* by a run that
  signs — not by its presence.

## What

1. **Set the secret from the authoritative SSM source.** `gh secret set REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY
   --repo navapbc/rebar` fed the decrypted SSM value (piped, never echoed). This guarantees the
   secret holds the key whose public half is registered on 594c. **T4 (irreversible overwrite):
   this is safe and recoverable — SSM is the single source of truth (ADR-0012) and is left
   unchanged; the "rollback" for the write-only secret is simply to re-run `gh secret set` from
   the same SSM param.** Record the `gh secret list` timestamp.
2. **Prove CI signs.** Capture `C=$(git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse HEAD)`, trigger a
   `reconcile-bridge` run (`workflow_dispatch`), wait for it to land ticket writes (fetch
   `origin/tickets`), and verify the events it introduced are signed + verified.

## Scope

The GitHub Actions workflow that writes tickets (`reconcile-bridge`). Secret set from SSM +
one live signing proof. No enforcement flip (8d39); no workflow-YAML change; empty `file_impact`
(no tracked repo-file change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **The signing secret is set from SSM.** `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` on `navapbc/rebar` is set
      from `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` (whose public half is registered on 594c).
      Evidence recorded: the `gh secret set` success + the `gh secret list` timestamp line.
- [ ] **A CI run produces signed, verified bot events.** With `C` = the tickets-branch HEAD
      captured before a `reconcile-bridge` run, after the run lands its writes on `origin/tickets`:
      (a) **non-vacuous** — the run advanced the tickets branch with bot-authored commits:
      `git -C .tickets-tracker rev-list "$C"..origin/tickets --count` > 0 **and**
      `git -C .tickets-tracker log "$C"..origin/tickets --format='%ae' | sort -u` contains
      `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`; and (b) **every non-exempt event the run introduced verifies
      under enforcement**: `rebar verify-identity --all --require-authenticated --since "$C"`
      exits 0 (an unsigned in-scope bot write would make this non-zero — this is exactly the
      enforcement the flip applies). Record `C`, the run URL, and the new commit range.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The secret is set in GitHub settings and a real run proves signing.
      Evidence recorded as a comment: the workflow-run URL, `C`, the new tickets commit range,
      the `verify-identity --since C` exit-0 result, and the `gh secret list` timestamp.
baseline.summary: Populate REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY and confirm GitHub Actions produces signed ticket events

# purge-bridge commits on the tickets tracker with a raw, unlocked whole-index git commit (same class as the enrich-queue prune race)

## Summary

`rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py` (~lines 135-152) commits its ticket-directory deletions with a
raw `git -C <tracker> add -A` + `git -C <tracker> commit --no-verify` that takes **neither the
unified store write lock nor a commit pathspec** — the same defect class as bug
`eclectic-spotted-barb` (the enrich-queue prune), where an unlocked whole-index commit races
concurrent locked store writes and sweeps/strands them.

Discovered during the Step-7 sibling sweep for `eclectic-spotted-barb`. Lower exposure than the
enrich-queue prune (which fired opportunistically on every write via the `[agents]` drain child):
`purge-bridge` is a **manual operator command**, so it only races if an operator runs it while
agents are writing. Filed separately because (a) its blast radius is much smaller and (b) the fix
is not a drop-in `delete_events` swap — it removes whole ticket **directories** via `git add -A`,
so it needs the unified write lock wrapped around a pathspec-scoped or `-A` commit (or a locked
batch delete), not the enrich-queue prune's exact pattern.

## Reproduction Steps

1. While concurrent agents are performing normal locked store writes, run `rebar purge-bridge`.
2. Its unlocked `git add -A` + whole-index `git commit` can sweep a concurrent writer's staged
   event into the purge commit / advance HEAD under the writer's ref update, dropping/stranding
   that write (same sweep-and-strand as `eclectic-spotted-barb`).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** every store write serializes through the unified write lock (invariant I5); a
  concurrent write is never dropped by a maintenance command's commit.
- **Actual:** `purge-bridge`'s commit runs outside the lock and can race concurrent locked writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `purge_bridge.py`'s deletion commit routes through the unified store write lock (no raw
  unlocked `git add -A` + `git commit` on the tracker).
  - Proving: `rg -n 'subprocess.run.*git.*commit' src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py` shows no
    unlocked whole-index commit; the write path acquires the store write lock.
- [ ] A concurrency regression test (mirroring
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py`) shows `purge-bridge` racing
  concurrent locked writes loses nothing (RED before, GREEN after).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: purge-bridge commits on the tickets tracker with a raw, unlocked whole-index git commit (same class as the enrich-queue prune race)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Discovered from 80af. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` (with verify.require_completion_verification_for_close=true) does its work in TWO steps against the git tree — verify, then sign — reading HEAD INDEPENDENTLY each time. A commit landing in the verify→sign window splits them; rebar correctly refuses to attest a tree it didn't verify, but CLOSES THE TICKET ANYWAY without a completion attestation, and its suggested remedy ("re-close to certify") is a no-op because the ticket is already closed. Full report (evidence, repro, analysis): ~/.claude/jobs/e9e3a20d/tmp/rebar-completion-race-bug-report.md

## Evidence (observed)
Closing 4030-df44-540f-4ec0 from a worktree another agent was committing into:
  "Warning: closed ... WITHOUT a completion signature — the code drifted between verify (5d2b47f) and sign (70ca791); not attesting stale state. Re-close to certify against the current tree."
- 5d2b47f = the ticket's real merged work (verifier checked this).
- 70ca791 = an UNRELATED in-flight commit from another agent in the shared worktree (signer saw this).
Post: ticket closed, attestation kinds = ['plan-review'] (NO 'completion'). The suggested re-close is a no-op (already closed). Only "recovery" is --force-close (itself the 'did not validate' signal) or fabricating a manifest via `rebar sign` — not acceptable.

## Root cause (hypothesis)
TOCTOU in transition_close.py: verify_completion(ref="HEAD") resolves HEAD→A; the pre-sign drift guard reads head_sha() again→B; A!=B → refuse sign; the close transition proceeds regardless (verify→close→sign ordering). It treats "the working tree" as an ambient global instead of pinning one revision for the whole verify+sign+close unit. Note: 80af's --ref fix only made the NON-default (--ref) path coherent (verify and sign both pin the ref); the DEFAULT (no --ref) path STILL reads HEAD twice and still splits.

## Expected
Either (a) pin ONE revision for the whole verify+sign+close unit (verify+sign+close all bind that rev; a concurrent commit can't split them) — the attestation binds verified-at-sha:A which is immutable and WAS verified, so an unrelated HEAD move to B should not invalidate it (same 'unrelated movement must not invalidate' principle as 790c's plan-review fix); OR (b) on drift, do NOT close — abort and leave the ticket in_progress so the operator re-runs the close (the plan-review gate's retryable posture). Plus a first-class non-force recovery (e.g. `rebar reverify-completion <id>`, analogous to sign-review/resign_plan_review) for an already-closed-but-unsigned ticket. Immediate 80af-based workaround exists: reopen → transition in_progress closed --ref <verified-sha> re-verifies+signs the real commit coherently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A completion close whose HEAD moves to an UNRELATED commit between verify and sign does NOT produce a closed-without-signature ticket — either it pins the verified rev and signs it, or it aborts the close and leaves the ticket in_progress (retryable). Verified by a test that moves HEAD in the verify→sign window.
- [ ] There is a non-`--force`, non-fabrication recovery to obtain the completion attestation for a closed-but-unsigned ticket (or the close never lands unsigned on a benign race in the first place).
- [ ] The residual unsigned-close message (if any) names an ACTUALLY-WORKING recovery, not a no-op re-close.
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green.

## Possibly related (from the same report; separate triage)
- PlanReviewGenerationChanged raised with IDENTICAL before==after generation hashes (~19x); blind re-run signs. (Distinct from 790c's related-material case.)
- review-code silent-empty output when backgrounded (exits 0 with empty result).
baseline.summary: completion close: verify->sign TOCTOU race closes a ticket permanently unsigned, with no non-force recovery
