baseline.description:
## Why

rebar's `_store/lock.py` mkdir-lock reclamation (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale`) is deliberately conservative: every branch that cannot POSITIVELY prove the owner is a dead same-host process returns `False` (never reclaim) — the "refuse without proof" contract of bug yaw-gravel-linen. 304e (castoff-tigerseye-ammonite) fixed ONE instance of the resulting failure — a container recreate making a same-host orphan look foreign — but left the CLASS open: an absent/unreadable owner stamp, a malformed v2 stamp, a genuinely foreign-host stamp on a shared filesystem, or a cross-namespace stamp seen without the fcntl proof all still wedge the store PERMANENTLY, exactly as the 2026-07-31 production incident did (review-bot boot 62s vs a 30s health check).

The 9305 OSS research (rec #1, highest value, fully backed) prescribes the missing piece: a wall-clock AGE CEILING, following git gc's gc.pid 12h precedent (builtin/gc.c) — a stamp we cannot prove orphaned is respected UNTIL a generous ceiling, then reclaimed, so the store can never wedge forever. rebar holds the write lock only for a single event append (seconds), so the ceiling can be far tighter than git's 12h.

## What / Approach

Add `_MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S` (1 hour) and reclaim a contended mkdir lock, even without proof of death, once its lock-dir mtime (the acquisition time; the stamp is never refreshed) exceeds the ceiling — but ONLY on the branches that today refuse for LACK of a liveness signal: absent/unreadable stamp, malformed v2 stamp, foreign host identity, cross-namespace without the fcntl proof, and non-numeric pid.

The ceiling must NOT override a positive `pid alive` probe. Per the research's own rule — "if you ever break a lock, do it under a conservative fail-closed guard PLUS a wall-clock backstop, NEVER ON A TIMER ALONE" — a branch where `os.kill(pid,0)` says the owner is alive keeps returning `False` regardless of age. The macOS "pid alive but start-time unconfirmable" gap is a SEPARATE research recommendation (#6, start-time fallback) and is explicitly out of scope here.

Reclaiming an unprovable-but-aged lock is noteworthy, so `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` logs the holder stamp and the dir age at WARNING (research rec #8, "report the holder"), turning a silent 60s wedge into an observable, attributable reclaim.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — the ceiling constant, an age helper, the age backstop on the
  refuse-without-proof branches, and holder-disclosure logging on reclaim.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py` — new.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An aged-out mkdir lock with an ABSENT/unreadable owner stamp is reclaimed (was permanent):
      `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` returns True once the dir mtime exceeds the ceiling, and `acquire`
      succeeds promptly.
- [ ] An aged-out FOREIGN-host v2 stamp and an aged-out MALFORMED v2 stamp are likewise reclaimed,
      while the SAME stamps with a fresh mtime are still refused — proving only age, not identity,
      changed the decision.
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose stamped pid is a LIVE same-host, same-namespace, start-time-matching
      owner is NEVER reclaimed even when its mtime exceeds the ceiling (proof of life beats age).
- [ ] SAFETY: a lock whose pid probes ALIVE but whose start time is unconfirmable is NOT reclaimed
      by the ceiling (the "never on a timer alone" boundary; macOS start-time is rec #6, not here).
- [ ] `_reclaim_mkdir_lock` emits a WARNING naming the reclaimed owner stamp and the dir age.
- [ ] The existing lock suites (`test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, `test_lock_container_recreate.py`)
      still pass unchanged — fresh (non-aged) orphans keep their current behaviour.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Age ceiling on refuse-without-proof mkdir-lock branches: close the permanent-wedge class (9305 rec #1)

baseline.description:
## What
An OPTIONAL, isolated backfill adapter that mines this machine's Claude Code session transcripts to reconstruct the LOCAL env/integration-diagnosis history (and corroborate attempts/replanning/recovery), which no structural signal captures. Output is LLM-classified and clearly labeled low-confidence; the core command does not depend on this adapter.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/adapters/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/metrics/adapters/claude_transcripts.py` — new isolated adapter (imported only by the backfill script, never by the core command).
- `scripts/backfill_transcripts.py` — new: targeted extraction (grep error signatures) -> classify -> write labeled snapshots.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_transcript_adapter.py` — new.

## Approach
Because all development happened on one machine, the transcripts are a near-complete local record of env toil that leaves no structural trace. To keep the harness portable, the adapter is optional and quarantined behind the backfill script — a parallel adapter could target another harness. It is a targeted pass: an **error-signature grep** over the transcript JSONL (patterns such as `LLMUnavailableError`, `ConnectionError`/`connection refused`, `ModuleNotFoundError`, `command not found`, `No such file`, HTTP `429`, `timed out`) selects candidate lines, then a **deterministic keyword/regex classifier** (NOT an LLM — so the adapter and its test are self-contained and reproducible, with no model call or human-calibration gate) maps each signature to the classification enum. Every emitted value carries `source=backfill_classified, confidence=classified` — that label IS the honest low-confidence signal, and it segregates these values from authoritative structural series. The classification enum (`env_setup`, `dependency`, `integration`, `tooling`, `none`) and the JSON output schema are defined in the adapter module.

**Normative pattern→enum routing table** (first match wins; case-insensitive substring/regex over the transcript line):
- `env_setup` ← `ModuleNotFoundError`, `ImportError`, `No such file or directory`, `virtualenv`/`venv` activation errors, `command not found`.
- `dependency` ← `pip`/`uv` resolution errors, `version conflict`, `Could not find a version`, `incompatible`.
- `integration` ← `ConnectionError`, `connection refused`, `timed out`/`ReadTimeout`, HTTP `429`/`5xx`, `LLMUnavailableError`.
- `tooling` ← `git` errors, `ruff`/`mypy`/`pytest` invocation failures, `Permission denied`.
- `none` ← a candidate line matching no rule above (dropped, not emitted).

**Emitted record JSON schema** (one per classified interval): `{"kind": <one of the enum values>, "signature": <the matched pattern/string>, "ts": <ISO-8601 of the transcript entry>, "source": "backfill_classified", "confidence": "classified"}`. The AC assertions (`jq -e`) target `.kind` and `.source`/`.confidence`.

## Tests
- Unit (fixture JSONL transcripts): a transcript with a known env-failure signature is extracted and classified into an `env_setup` interval; a clean transcript yields none; output carries the classified label.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_transcript_adapter.py` passes: a fixture JSONL transcript containing a known env-failure signature (e.g. a `ModuleNotFoundError` line) is extracted and deterministically classified into at least one interval tagged `source=backfill_classified`, `confidence=classified` (`jq -e`); a clean transcript yields 0. No LLM/network call occurs (the classifier is deterministic).
- [ ] the portability guard holds: a unit test asserts the CORE metrics package does NOT import the adapter — specifically that `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` and `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py` (the modules that exist today) do not import `adapters.claude_transcripts` (assert by scanning each module's source for the adapter import). The `rebar metrics` command's own isolation from adapters is enforced by ticket 9a5a's portability-guard AC — this ticket does NOT assert against `_commands/metrics.py` (which 9a5a delivers), to avoid a vacuously-passing scan of a not-yet-existing file.
- [ ] `scripts/backfill_transcripts.py` is exercised: a test invokes its entry point over a fixture transcript dir and asserts it emits the labeled classified records (so the script — not just the adapter — is covered).
- [ ] the classification enum (`env_setup`, `dependency`, `integration`, `tooling`, `none`) and output schema are defined in the adapter module — test asserts the enum has exactly these values.
baseline.summary: Local Claude-Code-transcript mining adapter (optional, isolated backfill)

Add tests proving a fresh `rebar init` honors a custom `tracker.dir` and `tracker.branch`
end-to-end, plus a regression test that defaults reproduce today's behavior, and an `fsck`
WARN when the configured branch/dir does not match what is actually mounted.

orphan branch is created under the custom name, the worktree/symlink uses the custom dir,
it is gitignored, and create/list/show round-trip.
- regression: with no config, the branch is `tickets` and the dir is `.tickets-tracker`.
- `fsck` mismatch: configured-vs-mounted divergence emits a WARN (not a hard error).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] e2e test: custom dir + branch init creates + mounts + gitignores correctly and round-trips.
- [ ] Regression test pins default dir/branch behavior.
- [ ] `fsck` WARNs on configured-vs-mounted branch/dir mismatch.
- [ ] `pytest -m "not integration"` green.
## Files
- `tests/interfaces/` or `tests/unit/` (new init/config test module)
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` (mismatch WARN)
## Depends on
- Child 3 and Child 4 (the call sites must be migrated first).
## Review refinements (plan-review gate)
- E6/F1 (conf 0.86): the custom-branch e2e must exercise a **write+sync path on a non-default
branch** (create -> push/pull or reconcile dry-run -> read-back), not only create/list/show,
so the migrated push/sync/reconciler/advisory-lock paths are actually verified end-to-end.
- E5 (conf 1.0): branch/`dir` validator **accept/reject unit tests are owned by child 14b8** (the
config-level validators); this child does NOT duplicate them — it covers init/e2e/regression/fsck.
- E2/T9 (conf 1.0): pin the fsck mismatch mechanism — "configured" = the precedence-resolved
`tracker.dir`/`tracker.branch`; "mounted" = the actual worktree/symlink + checked-out branch
(`git worktree list` / symlink target). The WARN compares those two.
- COH (conf 1.0): the init e2e creates a real orphan branch + worktree, but the default suite
runs `pytest -m "not integration"` — the test must run there via a tmp-repo fixture (or be
explicitly integration-marked AND a non-integration variant added). State which.
- [ ] e2e exercises a non-default-branch write+sync round-trip (not just create/list/show).
- [ ] (Validator accept/reject unit tests are covered by child 14b8 — not duplicated here.)
- [ ] fsck "configured" (precedence-resolved) vs "mounted" (worktree/symlink) source-of-truth pinned.
- [ ] The init test runs under `pytest -m "not integration"` (tmp-repo fixture) — or is dual-tiered.

## Summary
The reconciler resolves a ticket's `assignee` to a Jira user on TWO divergent code paths, producing inconsistent results for the same input. An UPDATE strictly resolves the assignee (exact / unique-normalized accountId, else unassign); a CREATE sends the **raw** local string to ACLI/Jira with no resolution, so Jira fuzzy-matches or applies a project-default assignee. Same local value `"joe"` therefore yields different outcomes depending on path.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Local ticket with `assignee="joe"` (not a unique Jira identity — e.g. 3 "Joe"s exist).
2. **CREATE path** (new issue): reconcile creates the Jira issue. **Actual:** Jira assigns it to `joeoakhart@navapbc.com` (fuzzy/default fallback) — a *wrong* user.
3. **UPDATE path** (already-bound, Jira unassigned): reconcile diffs assignee. **Actual:** `"joe"` is unmappable → issue left unassigned (and inbound later clears the local value).

**Expected:** both paths apply the SAME resolution policy: resolve `"joe"` → unique accountId if one exists, otherwise leave unassigned — never silently mis-assign to a fuzzy/default user.

## Root Cause
- **CREATE does NOT validate.** `acli.py:297-298` extracts the raw assignee; `acli_cli_ops.py:241-243` (non-JSON) and `:367-368` (JSON) pass the raw string straight to ACLI. No `validate_assignee_exists` call. ACLI/Jira then fuzzy-resolves or defaults.
- **UPDATE DOES validate.** `acli.py:347-349` calls `validate_assignee_exists()` before mutating; the diff resolver `outbound_differ.py:506-535` + `outbound_fields.py:372-390` map unmappable → unassign (`""`). Strict matcher: `acli.py:517-606`.

## Proposed Unification
Add ONE shared resolver consumed by both paths:
- New `AcliClient.resolve_assignee_for_mutation(assignee, *, issue_key=None, project_key=None) -> (accountId|None, authoritative: bool)` that wraps `validate_assignee_exists` and classifies the outcome: resolved accountId; `AssigneeNotFoundError` → `(None, authoritative=True)` (definitively unmappable → unassign); transient/API error → `(None, authoritative=False)` (do NOT unassign — preserve, let next pass retry). Preserve the `(acct, authoritative)` tuple rather than collapsing to a bare string, so a transient REST failure never spuriously unassigns.
- **CREATE** (`create_issue`, no issue key yet) resolves with `project_key=<project>`: resolved accountId → include in payload; unmappable → omit (leave unassigned); transient → omit (avoid mis-assign).
- **UPDATE** (`update_issue`, has issue key) resolves with `issue_key=<key>` via the same method.
- The diff-side `_assignee_resolver` collapses to a thin wrapper over the shared method (single source of truth).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CREATE and UPDATE route assignee resolution through ONE shared method; identical input yields identical Jira outcome.
- [ ] An ambiguous/unmappable assignee (e.g. `"joe"`) is left UNASSIGNED on both paths — never fuzzy-matched or defaulted to an unrelated user.
- [ ] A uniquely-resolvable assignee (exact email/accountId/displayName, or unique normalized variant) is assigned identically on both paths.
- [ ] Transient resolution failures do NOT unassign (authoritative=False is preserved end-to-end); only authoritative AssigneeNotFoundError unassigns.
- [ ] CREATE uses project-scope resolution (no issue_key yet); `validate_assignee_exists` already accepts `project_key`.
- [ ] Tests: CREATE+UPDATE parity for ambiguous, exact, unique-normalized, and transient-error cases.

## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli.py` (`create_issue`, `update_issue`, new shared resolver, `validate_assignee_exists`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/acli_cli_ops.py` (CREATE raw-string call sites)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` / `outbound_fields.py` (diff resolver → wrapper)
baseline.summary: Unify assignee resolution across CREATE and UPDATE reconciler paths (CREATE bypasses validate_assignee_exists -> fuzzy/default mis-assignment)
Tier D: write/sync core -> rebar._store/ behind REBAR_WRITE_CORE (the crux)

## Why

The visual editor's batch-criteria work (story B-UX) must let a user SELECT criteria and prompts
from the library AND CREATE new ones ("full in-editor authoring"). The prompt/criteria library
today supports enumerate (`load_catalog`/`registry.load_criteria`), read (`get_prompt`), and a
committed derived index (`regenerate-index`) — but has NO programmatic WRITE path. In-editor
authoring needs to create/update a prompt-library entry (front-matter + rubric body) and keep the
committed prompt index + the drift CI gate green. This is the data-model layer the editor sits on;
per the epic's sequencing it lands BEFORE the UX.

## What

Add a library WRITE + structured-enumerate data model for prompts and criteria (criteria are
prompt-library entries; D5 — a criterion's id IS its prompt-library id):

- An enumerate API returning the authorable list (id, kind=prompt|criterion, description, inputs/
  outputs, is-overlay) for the editor's pickers — a superset of the read-only inspector data.
- A create/update API that writes a prompt-library `.md` (front-matter + body) to the correct home
  (`.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` for user prompts; the packaged reviewers dir is read-only at runtime),
  validates the front-matter, and regenerates the committed reviewers index so the drift gate stays
  green.
- Validation + conflict handling (id collision, malformed front-matter, reserved ids).

## Scope

- New library write/enumerate functions (likely in `rebar.llm.prompts` + a thin criteria view over
  `plan_review.registry`), stdlib-only at import.
- Index regeneration wired so a create/update leaves `reviewers/index.json` consistent.
- Unit tests for enumerate shape, create/update round-trip, index regen, and validation/conflict.
- NO editor/frontend code here (that is B-UX); this is the backend data model only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An enumerate API lists authorable prompts + criteria with the fields the editor pickers need
      (id, kind, description, inputs/outputs, is-overlay), covering both packaged and `.rebar/prompts` entries.
- [ ] A create/update API writes a validated prompt-library `.md` to `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` and
      regenerates the committed index so the prompt-drift CI gate stays green.
- [ ] Validation rejects id collisions, malformed front-matter, and reserved ids with clear errors.
- [ ] Unit tests cover enumerate, create/update round-trip, index regen, and the validation paths.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: B-DM: Prompt + criteria library write/enumerate/index data model (the editor's backend)

baseline.description:
## Summary

Discovered while fixing bug 01e8 (rebar-debug sibling sweep). CONFIRMED with a runtime experiment; deliberately NOT fixed under 01e8 because it is outside that ticket's acceptance criteria and the remedy is a data decision.

`_store/sync.py:170-173`:

```python
if not _ok(tracker, "fetch", remote_name, branch, "--quiet"):
    return
if not _ok(tracker, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{remote_name}/{branch}"):
    return
```

A bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` only writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` when the remote's configured refspec covers it. Under a narrow clone refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`) it writes only FETCH_HEAD, so the guard on line 173 returns and the `--allow-unrelated-histories` union merge at sync.py:96-97 is NEVER REACHED.

## Evidence (measured)

Fresh single-branch clone: three consecutive `rebar list` passes (sync throttle marker cleared between each) all returned 0 tickets. `git fetch origin tickets --quiet` returned rc=0 while `git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets` returned 128. Positive control: after manually creating the ref with an explicit refspec and clearing the throttle marker, the very next read healed and the tracker logged 'Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during sync)'.

This is why 01e8's reporter saw `[]` persist for a whole session despite `sync.pull = on`.

## Why this was not folded into 01e8

01e8's AC3 chose to REPORT divergence (`rebar fsck` now exits non-zero with DIVERGED) rather than auto-heal it. Making sync reach its union merge would cause an accidentally-created orphan store to silently merge into the shared tickets branch. That may well be the right recovery behaviour, but it is a deliberate data decision that deserves its own review rather than riding along on a bug fix.

## Options

1. Fetch with an explicit refspec (`+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`) so the existing, already-intended union merge becomes reachable. Smallest change; matches what 01e8 did in init.py and fsck.py.
2. Keep sync inert on divergence and rely on the new fsck DIVERGED report plus an explicit operator recovery command.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether a divergent tracker should self-heal or require explicit operator action.
- [ ] If self-heal: sync fetches with an explicit refspec, and a two-clone/narrow-refspec test proves an already-divergent store reconverges with no event loss.
- [ ] If not: the fsck DIVERGED report names the exact recovery command, and sync's inertness is documented as intentional at sync.py:170.
baseline.summary: sync self-heal is unreachable under a narrow clone refspec: an already-divergent tracker never reconverges

## What
On bug close, auto-draw a best-effort `caused_by` link to the culprit ticket via git-blame, with a `--caused-by <id>` param to augment/override, plus a bug-template blame-hunt advisory. Provenance is an externally verifiable factual claim (blame is checkable), not agent self-assessment, so it is safe to derive/accept — unlike a process self-report.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py` — new: single-culprit resolver.
  - **Fixing-commit discovery:** the `<fixing-commit>` is the most recent commit in `git log` whose message resolves to THIS bug ticket — reuse `rebar._commands.verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs(message)` (verify_commit.py:55) to parse `rebar-ticket:`/subject refs and match the bug id (the same trailer-resolution the close path's `_referencing_commit_exists`, transition_close.py:32, already relies on). If no such commit exists yet (the fix may not be committed at close time), auto-derivation is skipped (returns None).
  - **Blame target:** blame the **pre-fix** state — the parent of the fixing commit (`<fixing-commit>~1`) — over the bug's recorded `file_impact`, never post-fix HEAD (which would attribute the fixing commit itself).
  - **"Single-culprit" threshold (explicit):** the resolver returns a culprit commit ONLY when a strict **majority (> 50%)** of the blamed lines across the `file_impact` files point to ONE commit AND that commit resolves to a ticket via its `rebar-ticket:` trailer; otherwise it returns None. This concretely defines "dominant culprit" and "multi-commit spread ambiguity."
  - Returns None (no link) on ambiguity: no `file_impact`, no fixing commit found, no >50% dominant commit, or no resolvable trailer.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — best-effort auto-link `caused_by` after the bug is closed. **CRITICAL ordering/guard:** the auto-link runs after `txn.transition_core` has committed the STATUS event, so the bug (the link SOURCE) is already `closed`; `graph._links.add_dependency` rejects links from a closed source (the `source_status == "closed"` raise at `_links.py:253`). The auto-link therefore writes via `graph._links._write_link_event(bug, culprit, "caused_by", tracker_dir)` **directly**, bypassing the closed-source and cycle guards — which add nothing for a non-blocking, non-cycle-inducing relation on a closed source. Same direct-writer path is used for the explicit `--caused-by` override applied at close time. Failure to resolve never blocks the close.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — parse `--caused-by <id>` and thread it end-to-end (mirrors ed13's `--class` threading, which already made `_parse_flags` return a tuple with `close_class`): `_parse_flags` returns an additional `caused_by` element (now a 5-tuple: `reason, force, force_close, close_class, caused_by`); `transition_cli` unpacks it; `transition_compute` gains a `caused_by: str = ""` keyword and passes it to `close_ticket`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — `close_ticket` gains a `caused_by` parameter; on a bug close it applies the explicit `--caused-by <id>` override (and, absent that, the blame auto-derivation) via the `_write_link_event` direct-writer path described above.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — **CRITICAL (same gap ed13 hit):** the public library facade `transition()` (line 329) calls `transition_compute` with a fixed keyword set that does NOT include `caused_by`; add a `caused_by: str = ""` parameter to `transition()` and thread it into the `transition_compute` call, so library callers (not just the CLI) can set `caused_by` on close.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — bug-template blame-hunt advisory.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py` — new. **All test bug-closes MUST pass a `--class` value** (a bounded `--class` is REQUIRED on bug close after ticket ed13, which this ticket stacks on top of).

## Approach
The culprit commit is an externally verifiable factual claim (blame is checkable), not agent self-assessment, so it is safe to derive/accept — unlike a process self-report. Reuses git blame + the existing `rebar-ticket:` trailer resolution rather than a novel mechanism. Auto-derivation is conservative: it links only on a single dominant culprit resolving to a ticket; ambiguous cases (refactors, moves, multi-commit, no `file_impact`) are left to `--caused-by` or `rebar link ... caused_by`. Best-effort — a failed resolution never blocks close, and the edge is written via `_write_link_event` directly so the closed-source guard does not silently swallow it. **Confidence semantics:** the `caused_by` LINK event itself carries NO confidence field (it is an ordinary link — `_write_link_event` writes only `{target_id, relation}`); the "classified vs authoritative" distinction is applied by the *consuming* provenance metric (the registry/reader), which treats a blame-auto-derived `caused_by` edge as `classified`-confidence evidence, never as an authoritative structural fact. This ticket does not add a confidence field to the link; it only draws the edge.

## Tests
- Integration (real temp git repo + store): a bug whose fix edits lines last changed (pre-fix) by a single commit carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer auto-gets a `caused_by` link to that ticket (closing with `--class`); an ambiguous multi-commit blame draws no auto-link; `--caused-by <id>` always sets the link.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py` passes: closing a bug (`--class regression`) over a single-culprit fixture yields a `caused_by` link to the resolved ticket (`rebar show <bug> --output json | jq -e '.links[]|select(.relation=="caused_by")'`) — proving the direct-writer path defeats the closed-source guard.
- [ ] an ambiguous two-commit blame yields no auto `caused_by` link — integration test asserts absence.
- [ ] `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class regression --caused-by <id>` sets the link regardless of blame — test asserts presence.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` gains a blame-hunt advisory section (e.g. `## Blame-Hunt Advisory`) explaining when auto-derivation applies and when to use `--caused-by` — asserted by a test/grep that the section and the `--caused-by` guidance are present.
baseline.summary: Blame-based caused_by auto-derivation + --caused-by param + bug-template advisory

content.text: ## Why
Blocking is project-owned policy; rebar's job is to surface the same eval/calibration instruments
it uses on its built-ins so a maintainer can decide informed. Today `eval_solver.run_case` is a
**closed hardcoded dispatch** (only `completion-verifier` / `ticket-quality` / `spec-alignment`;
raises otherwise) and the CLI is validate-only — so a project criterion cannot be run through the
eval harness at all.
## What
- A criterion-aware runner extending `eval_solver.run_case` so an arbitrary (built-in or project)
criterion prompt_id is runnable — reconcile the invocation model (the criterion runs as its
Pass-1 finder against a fixture); resolve the T3 advisory (the existing solver's invocation model
vs a per-criterion prompt).
- `rebar criteria eval <id>` — a live CLI (not validate-only) that runs the criterion's
must-fire/must-not-fire + discrimination fixtures from `.rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml` (discovery
already exists) with N-run stability.
- A calibration view over the existing κ/parity primitives: per criterion print **recall**
(=fraction of must-fire fixtures it fires on), **false-accept** (=fraction of must-not-fire it
wrongly fires on), **Cohen's κ** and **agreement %** (verdict vs the fixture's labeled expect).
Reconcile the preview/eval `verdict` vocabulary with the fixture `expect` vocabulary.
## Scope
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/eval_solver.py` (criterion-aware dispatch), `src/rebar/llm/eval.py` /
`eval_scorers.py` (reuse discrimination scorers, κ, parity), `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`
(`rebar criteria eval`), calibration rendering.
- Depends on story `#1` (a criterion must be loadable/activatable to eval it).
- Out: REVIEW_RESULT FP-replay (F1) — gate-agnostic, deferred; project criteria inherit it later.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `eval_solver.run_case` runs an arbitrary criterion prompt_id (built-in or project), not the
closed 3-id set; the invocation model is documented.
- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <id>` runs must-fire/must-not-fire + discrimination fixtures live from
`.rebar/evals/` with N-run stability.
- [ ] The calibration view prints recall, false-accept, Cohen's κ, agreement % per criterion, with
each metric defined; the eval `verdict` vocabulary is reconciled with the fixture `expect`.
- [ ] FP-replay (F1) is explicitly out of scope.
## Invocation model & implementation contract (remediation, run 1)
### Criterion arm of `run_case` (clears G6/T1/T8 blocker)
The existing `run_case` branches (`case_store` + a disposable git repo + `create_ticket`) are the
AGENTIC store-reader ops — structurally inapplicable to a plan-review criterion, which is a
single-turn/agentic **finder over inline text**. The criterion arm therefore does NOT use
`case_store`. Concrete path:
- `run_case(prompt_id, case, *, runner, graph=False, repo_root=None)` gains a `repo_root=None`
param (default `config.repo_root()`; back-compat for existing callers). If `prompt_id` resolves to
a criterion — bare id or `plan-review-<id>`, present in `registry.by_id(repo_root)` — take the
criterion arm; else the existing 3-id dispatch (unknown non-criterion still raises `ValueError`).
- The arm: `desc = registry.by_id(repo_root)[cid]`; `cfg = resolve_gate_config(repo_root)`;
`findings = passes.pass1_chunk(runner, cfg, plan=case["input"], chunk=[desc],
agentic=registry.exec_tier(desc)=="AGENT")`; return `{"findings": findings}`. No store, no ticket.
(Container G3/G4 + ISF need a graph/log, not inline text — OUT of scope here; a criterion whose
fixtures require them errors with a clear message.)
### Verdict ↔ expect vocabulary reconciliation (clears T8/AC3)
`_fired(verdict) = len(verdict.get("findings") or []) > 0`. A case's expected fire is derived from
its `expect` via the EXISTING sets: `FIRE_EXPECTS = {"finding","fail"}` → expected-fire;
`NOFIRE_EXPECTS = {"pass"}` → expected-no-fire. Only fire/no-fire cases feed the calibration
(validity/impact/novelty axis cases are skipped, not miscounted). Two-category labels `"fire"` /
`"no_fire"` feed `cohens_kappa` + agreement.
### Calibration metrics (clears AC3 metric defs)
`calibrate_criterion(criterion_id, *, repo_root=None, runner=None, runs=1, solve=None)` in eval.py:
- `recall` = fired / total must-fire fixtures; `false_accept` = wrongly-fired / total must-not-fire
fixtures; `agreement` = fraction of cases where observed == expected; `kappa` =
`cohens_kappa(expected_labels, observed_labels)`.
- Injectable `solve` (mirrors `run_eval`) so tests compute metrics deterministically without a model.
### N-run stability (clears E2/T5e/G6 — N is configurable)
`runs` (CLI `--runs`, default **1**) is N. Each case runs N times; its observed verdict is the
MAJORITY fire/no-fire across the N runs, and per-case `stability` = fraction of the N runs agreeing
with that majority (1.0 = fully stable). The view prints the min/mean stability so a flaky criterion
is visible. N=1 ⇒ stability trivially 1.0.
### CLI error states + sequencing (clears T6/E5/G5)
`rebar criteria eval <id>` errors clearly (non-zero exit, no traceback) on: missing/empty id; a
criterion id absent from the registry (`unknown criterion`); an absent `.rebar/evals/<prompt_id>.eval.yaml`
fixture (`no eval fixtures for <id>`); a fixture with zero fire/no-fire cases (`empty calibration
dataset`). Thin-slice sequencing: (1) `run_case` criterion arm + a unit test with a fake runner;
(2) `calibrate_criterion` + a deterministic-`solve` test; (3) CLI wiring + error-path tests.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)
- [ ] The criterion arm of `run_case` calls `passes.pass1_chunk` directly (no `case_store`), with a
documented `repo_root` param; a fake-runner unit test asserts fire (non-empty findings) and
no-fire (empty) map correctly.
- [ ] `calibrate_criterion` computes recall / false-accept / κ / agreement / stability with an
injectable `solve`; a deterministic test asserts the metric math (no live model).
- [ ] `rebar criteria eval <id>` errors clearly (non-zero, no traceback) on unknown id / absent
fixture / empty dataset; each has a test.

baseline.summary: Per-criterion eval runner + calibration view (rebar criteria eval)

baseline.description:
## Context
Plan-review, code-review, and completion sidecar emit paths automatically prune older committed UUID-named event files through delete_events. This repeats the destructive-retention mechanism proven to wedge the review-bot tracker in bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282.

## Evidence
- The two-clone experiment for 8185 proved that deleting a shared base sidecar while each stale clone appends a replacement makes Git infer rename conflicts.
- plan_review/sidecar.py, code_review/sidecar.py, and completion_sidecar.py each call delete_events from automatic retention.
- The store concurrency contract requires independent UUID events to reconverge by append-only union.

## Plan
- Build real two-clone RED reproductions for each automatic emit/retention path.
- Remove or replace automatic physical deletion only where the runtime experiment proves conflict.
- Preserve latest-result readers, audit history, reducer behavior, and clean tracker state.
- Verify each path RED to GREEN with mutation checks and the full concurrency tier.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Real two-clone tests prove each affected automatic sidecar path reconverges cleanly.
- [ ] Automatic sidecar writes do not physically delete committed UUID event files.
- [ ] Latest-result readers still select the newest valid sidecar.
- [ ] Focused, default, integration, lint, and typecheck gates pass.
baseline.summary: Automatic LLM sidecar retention can diverge independent tracker clones

## Context
The review gates expose real configuration — risk posture, chunking, budget caps, per-criterion advisory-vs-
blocking, and a global enable/disable kill-switch. A project needs a coherent way to read, set, and validate
that config rather than hand-editing scattered keys. (Spun out of `5fd2` as a separate epic; was follow-on F5.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A validated config schema covering risk posture, chunking, budget caps, per-criterion blocking, the global enable/disable, and the ADVISORY SURFACING CAP (top-N advisory findings; default 10; NEVER applies to blocking findings).
- [ ] A CLI/MCP surface to read/set/validate the config with shipped defaults.
- [ ] Invalid config is a located error, not a silent no-op.

baseline.description:
## Summary
Ticket write operations fail hard on git `index.lock` contention and NEVER self-heal:
a single interrupted/crashed commit leaves a stale
`.git/worktrees/<tracker>/index.lock` that wedges **every** subsequent ticket write
(`comment`, `edit`, `create`, `link`, `tag`, …) until a human manually removes it. Even
*transient* contention (two clones committing at once) surfaces as a hard error with no
retry. Locks should be transient and ticket operations should retry + reclaim provably-stale
locks to be self-healing.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Drive any ticket write through `rebar._store.event_append.stage_and_commit` (e.g.
   `rebar comment <id> "..."`).
2. Simulate an interrupted commit by leaving a stale git index lock:
   `touch "$(git -C <tracker> rev-parse --git-dir)/index.lock"` (no git process holds it).
3. Run `rebar comment <id> "anything"` again.

Observed in the wild: after an interrupted `rebar comment`, a ~15-minute-old
`/Users/.../.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/index.lock` (0 bytes, no owning process per
`lsof`) blocked five consecutive `rebar comment` retries; the store only recovered after a
manual `rm` of the lock file.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a transient `index.lock` contention is retried with bounded backoff and
  succeeds once the peer releases; a *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git
  process / older than a threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically — mirroring the
  stale-lock reclamation rebar ALREADY does for its own mkdir write-lock
  (`_store/lock.py::_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`). Ticket writes are
  self-healing in the common case; only a genuinely-held lock (live peer) waits/fails.
- **Actual:** `stage_and_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:145-175`) shells out to
  `git add`/`git commit` and raises `StoreError("Error: git commit failed while holding
  lock: … Unable to create '<gitdir>/index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to
  be running …")` on the FIRST failure — no retry, no backoff, no stale detection. The
  rebar `_store/lock.py` write lock is held around this, but that lock only reclaims its OWN
  mkdir lock; the git-owned `index.lock` created transiently by `git add`/`git commit` is
  not covered by any retry or staleness check, so one dead commit wedges all writes.

## Context / root cause
Two lock layers exist and only one self-heals:
- `_store/lock.py` (rebar write lock: fcntl + mkdir) — ALREADY reclaims a provably-stale
  mkdir lock (owner stamp `<host>:<pid>`, dead-pid probe).
- git's `index.lock` (created per `git add`/`git commit` inside `stage_and_commit`) — NOT
  covered. Interrupted/killed commits (CI cancellation, `^C`, OOM, a crashed peer) strand it.

The `edf7`/`6818` history in the surrounding comments shows related git-race hardening
(surfacing stderr, healing UU/unmerged paths), but transient/stale `index.lock` itself is
still fatal-on-first-try.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `stage_and_commit` (and the sibling inline committers `txn.py::claim_core`/
      `transition_core`, `compact.py`) retry a git `index.lock` "File exists / Another git
      process seems to be running" failure with bounded exponential backoff (small, capped
      total wait) before surfacing an error
- [ ] A *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git process AND/OR older than a
      configurable threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically, reusing/mirroring the
      staleness logic in `_store/lock.py` (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`);
      a genuinely-held lock (live peer within the window) is NOT stolen
- [ ] A concurrency test: two processes committing to the same tracker serialize and BOTH
      succeed (no spurious hard failure from transient `index.lock` contention)
- [ ] A stale-lock test: a pre-created `index.lock` with no owning process is reclaimed and
      the ticket write succeeds without manual intervention
- [ ] The retry/reclaim is fail-safe: a lock genuinely held by a live peer still waits within
      budget then surfaces a clear, actionable error (never silently drops the write, never
      corrupts the index)
- [ ] No regression to the existing `edf7` stderr-surfacing and `6818` unmerged-path healing
      behavior
baseline.summary: Ticket writes fail hard on git index.lock — add retry + stale-lock reclamation (self-healing)

baseline.description:
## Why

Creation provenance stops being auditable if compaction retires the original CREATE and the replacement SNAPSHOT omits or reinterprets the channel. This story makes recorded, inferred, and unknown provenance durable across normal compaction, conservative-horizon compaction, SNAPSHOT-only replay, legacy snapshots, and snapshot rebuild/recovery.

## What

- Preserve creation_channel and the optional true-only creation_channel_inferred marker inside SNAPSHOT.data.compiled_state. Do not add them to the SNAPSHOT envelope, whose author/env_id identify the compactor.
- Confirm src/rebar/_commands/compact.py continues to copy the complete reduced state while stripping only updated_at and the legacy signature mirror. Add a contract test that calls _snapshot_strip_keys() and asserts its result is disjoint from {"creation_channel", "creation_channel_inferred"}. The guard is deliberately test-enforced rather than a production assertion because the strip set is static internal policy and CI is the enforcement boundary.
- Document the rollback schema-state matrix: an existing new-code SNAPSHOT retains unknown compiled_state keys if replayed by old code; a first old-code compaction of raw creation-bearing CREATE events omits the field from that SNAPSHOT but retains the CREATE permanently as .retired; a never-compacted ticket retains the active CREATE value while the old reader hides it. The MVP has no writer-only binary mode. Before a full binary downgrade, operators stop every scheduled or manual rebar compact invocation. If the pause is violated, they record the affected ticket IDs from downgrade-window compaction activity, re-deploy the new binary, and rebuild those snapshots from the full log; include_retired=True replays the retained CREATE and restores creation_channel.
- At the end of process_snapshot, after compiled_state restoration and alongside the existing managed_refs/attestations/keyring migration hooks, call _project_legacy_creation_channel(state). The helper is a no-op for concrete recorded channels or an already-inferred jira value; absent, None, or provisional unknown-without-marker state is re-evaluated from restored ticket_id/author/env_id. A snapshot carrying a recorded channel is restored verbatim, while legacy and partial-migration snapshots receive the deterministic jira/unknown projection.
- Materialize creation_channel_inferred=true into snapshots produced from inferred historical state so later SNAPSHOT-only replay retains the certainty marker without access to retired CREATE files.
- Cover rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log and partial-horizon compaction, including replay of live events after the snapshot.
- Update event/compaction documentation to state that ticket genesis provenance lives in compiled_state and is distinct from SNAPSHOT event authorship. Update docs/output-schemas.md to state that SNAPSHOT-only replay plus snapshot rebuild emit the same creation_channel and creation_channel_inferred values through show/list/search/export as full-log replay.

## Approach Rationale

The compactor already snapshots reducer output and process_snapshot restores every compiled-state key. Preserving the field through that established path avoids a second provenance representation and keeps normal replay and recovery identical. A small legacy migration hook after snapshot restore is necessary because pre-feature snapshots cannot contain the new keys. No event rewrite or snapshot format fork is required. The rollback guidance distinguishes safe carry-forward of keys already present in compiled_state from first-compaction omission. Because .retired sources are retained permanently and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log reduces with include_retired=True, the omission is recoverable after re-upgrade; a targeted regression proves the compensating-forward path instead of overstating it as irreversible loss.

## Scope

IN: normal and horizon compaction, SNAPSHOT-only replay, legacy SNAPSHOT fallback, snapshot rebuild/recovery from retained .retired CREATEs, field-retention guards, the full-downgrade schema-state/precondition matrix, and compaction documentation.

OUT: changing source_event_uuids semantics, changing SNAPSHOT envelope authorship, rewriting existing snapshots, changing compaction thresholds, or adding a store-format migration.

## Files

- src/rebar/_commands/compact.py: compiled-state retention and full-log rebuild path.
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py: detect an old-style SNAPSHOT missing recorded provenance when a retained CREATE carries it and route --repair-snapshots through the existing rebuild seam.
- src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py: post-SNAPSHOT legacy projection using the shared helper.
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py: end-to-end retirement and replay.
- tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_snapshot.py: direct recorded/inferred/unknown snapshot projection.
- tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py: rebuild and horizon regression where needed.
- docs/event-schema.md and docs/concurrency.md: SNAPSHOT placement and recovery semantics.
- docs/output-schemas.md: consumer-facing parity between full-log, SNAPSHOT-only, and rebuilt-SNAPSHOT replay.

## Dependencies

Depends on the Jira/import story because the shared field, inference helper, and marker semantics must exist before snapshot migration can preserve them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Compacting tickets recorded as cli, mcp, python, jira, and import writes the exact channel into SNAPSHOT.data.compiled_state, retires the source CREATE, and SNAPSHOT-only replay returns the same value without an inference marker. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py -k recorded.
- [ ] Compacting an inferred historical Jira ticket materializes creation_channel=jira and creation_channel_inferred=true in compiled_state; SNAPSHOT-only replay preserves both. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py -k inferred.
- [ ] A pre-feature SNAPSHOT with creation_channel absent, None, or provisional unknown-without-marker projects inferred Jira only for the exact three-signal predicate and otherwise unknown; concrete recorded channels plus already-inferred Jira bypass re-inference. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_snapshot.py -k creation_channel.
- [ ] creation_channel and creation_channel_inferred never appear on the SNAPSHOT envelope and are not removed by _snapshot_strip_keys. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py -k placement.
- [ ] rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log plus conservative-horizon compaction preserve the same provenance while later live events replay normally. A simulated old-style SNAPSHOT missing creation_channel is detected and repaired from its retained CREATE through the existing fsck --repair-snapshots seam. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_creation_channel_compaction.py -k "rebuild or horizon or rollback_recovery" && uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py.
- [ ] Existing snapshot consistency, rollback recovery, and forward-compat behavior remain green. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_rollback_recovery.py tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_snapshot_checks.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_event_schema_forward_compat.py.
- [ ] As final documentation integrator, verify docs/event-schema.md plus docs/output-schemas.md jointly cover the enum, Jira inference, import semantics, SNAPSHOT placement, actor/environment/source_* distinctions, plus the diagnostic trust boundary. docs/concurrency.md covers rollback states, the compact pause, affected-ID capture, plus full-log rebuild. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py && make lint.
baseline.summary: Preserve creation provenance through SNAPSHOT compaction

baseline.description:
## Context
The first **asymmetric** scheme for the attest substrate (epic brilliant-curly-songbird): sign/verify over attestation bytes via OpenSSH `ssh-keygen -Y` (stdlib `subprocess`, **no new core dependency**), verified offline against an `allowed_signers`-format trust input, reusing developers existing SSH keys. Plugs into the registry `Scheme` protocol (task 518b). The `src/rebar/attest/` package already exists with `__init__.py` (task 9fd5).

## Mechanism (each command below was run and its behavior confirmed in this env, OpenSSH 10.2)
- **Sign — stdin -> stdout (never a file operand).** `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <privkey> -n <namespace>` with the payload piped on **stdin** and **NO file operand** writes the armored SSHSIG to **stdout**. Confirmed: `printf ... | ssh-keygen -Y sign -f id -n ns > out.sig` produces a signature that `-Y verify` accepts. (The `<file>.sig` on-disk output the man page describes applies ONLY when a file operand is passed on argv; this code passes the payload on stdin and never a file operand, so the signature is always on stdout.) `sign(pae_bytes, key_path, namespace)` returns those stdout bytes.
- **Verify — sig file on disk, data on stdin.** `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f <allowed_signers_file> -I <principal> -n <namespace> -s <sig_file>` reads the payload on **stdin**; the signature must be a file (`-s`). The allowed_signers content and the signature bytes are written to temp files; the process branches **only on exit code** (0 = valid). Argv array, never a shell string.
- **Validity windows.** Enforced via `valid-before=`/`valid-after=` options on the `allowed_signers` line; `ssh-keygen -Y verify` honors them against current time (or `-Overify-time`). Confirmed: an `allowed_signers` line with `valid-before=20200101` makes verify exit non-zero. This support requires **OpenSSH >= 8.9** — the reason for the version floor (the `-Y sign/verify` subcommands exist since 8.0, but allowed_signers validity intervals landed in 8.9).
- **Never** use `-Y check-novalidate` (structure-only) for authorization.

## Files
- `src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py` — `ssh_keygen_version()`, `ensure_available()`, `sign()`, `SshsigScheme` (registry `Scheme`; `trust_root`=allowed_signers content, `signatures[0].keyid`=principal, `signatures[0].sig`=armored SSHSIG bytes), `register_sshsig_scheme()`.
- `src/rebar/attest/__init__.py` — call `register_sshsig_scheme()` at import.
- `tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `SshsigScheme.verify(pae_bytes, signatures, namespace, trust_root)` invokes `ssh-keygen -Y verify` via an **argv array** (no shell), feeds `pae_bytes` on stdin, writes `trust_root` (allowed_signers) and `signatures[0].sig` to temp files, allowlist-validates principal + namespace (non-empty, no control chars), and returns a `registry.Verdict` branching **only** on exit code (0 -> `certified`, non-zero -> `mismatch`).
- [ ] Fail-closed test matrix (real `ssh-keygen`): `verified is False` on **tampered bytes**, **wrong namespace**, **unknown principal**, **substituted key**, and **expired validity window** (`valid-before` in the past). Plus a happy round-trip: `sign()` then `verify()` -> `certified`.
- [ ] `ssh_keygen_version()` returns the OpenSSH `(major, minor)` (or `None` if absent/unparseable). `SshsigScheme.verify` **fails closed** (non-`certified` `Verdict`, never a silent pass) when version detection returns `None` — test monkeypatches it to `None` and asserts `verified is False`.
- [ ] `ensure_available()` raises `SshKeygenUnavailable` (clear message) when ssh-keygen is absent (`ssh_keygen_version()` is `None`) OR below `8.9` — a test monkeypatches version detection to `None` and to `(8, 1)` and asserts `SshKeygenUnavailable` is raised in both cases.
- [ ] `register_sshsig_scheme()` registers `SshsigScheme` into the registry (discoverable via `registry.get_scheme("sshsig")`); no POLICY kinds pinned here (authorship kinds are the identity epic).
baseline.summary: attest: SSHSIG scheme via ssh-keygen (fail-closed subprocess)

baseline.description:
# Workflow engine: conditional overlays (via if:) + delegating batch step

## Context

Split out of soupy-spool-revel (6f2d) per the brainstorm (session logs boom-demon-jug ad3f +
woody-meat-seize). The e6d9 engine (declarative IR + thin worklist interpreter, run-state on the
git event log; step kinds uses/prompt/branch/loop/map + bounded-concurrent map fan-out) is closed.
To express a reusable 4-pass LLM-review pipeline ON the engine (epic B migrates plan-review +
completion-verification), the engine needs support for (1) conditional criterion INCLUSION and (2)
budgeted BATCH orchestration. This epic adds ONLY that, engine-only (no plan-review coupling). A
prior-art survey (Argo/Step Functions/dbt/LangGraph/Airflow/Dagster/Temporal) + a code investigation
grounded the design.

## The two concepts (one already exists, one is genuinely new)

1. **Conditional overlay = the EXISTING `if:` skip-guard (do NOT add a new field).** Code investigation
   found the engine ALREADY does per-step conditional inclusion: the v1 `if:` skip-guard (retained in
   v2; interpreter.py _guard_scoped) evaluates a predicate over run-start-journaled inputs + recorded
   prior outputs, is replay-deterministic (no live-store access), records a durable `skipped` event,
   and fails closed. So overlays ADOPT `if:`. The deliberately-CLOSED expression grammar (lint_refs.py
   _ALLOWED_EXPR; pinned by the v2 schema `expression`  — no operators/regex/functions) is the only
   gap: it can branch on a boolean in scope but cannot COMPUTE one. The clean design (keeping the grammar
   tiny + injection-safe) is a DETERMINISTIC scripted PRECOMPUTE step that turns each overlay trigger
   (has-children, has-linked-session-log, keyword/trigger match over a text input) into a boolean output
   the criterion's `if:` references; plus optionally journaling the resolved included-set at run-start
   for coverage. NO new IR field is added.

2. **Batch orchestration = a THIN delegating step (genuinely new).** No surveyed engine makes adaptive
   cost-budgeted batching first-class — it is app code everywhere — and encoding it in the IR would break
   the replay invariant (batch composition depends on a runtime token estimate + which call hit a context
   limit, so its control state is a recorded DECISION-TREE, not a function of outputs). So the IR gains a
   thin `batch` step declaring only params (group, usd_budget, model_ladder); a batch-RUNNER (behind a
   seam) does the adaptive packing / token-estimation / context-limit fallback / model-escalation /
   shed-to-INDETERMINATE / fingerprint-checkpoint and JOURNALS its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events
   the interpreter stores but never interprets. Epic A ships the seam + a reference default runner; epic
   B supplies the production runner (extracting the gate's sizing.py) behind this seam.

## Scope (engine-only)

- Overlay-via-`if:`: a deterministic trigger-precompute scripted step + a documented precompute-then-`if:`
  pattern + optional run-start journaling of the resolved included-set. The expression grammar is UNCHANGED.
- The `batch` step kind: schema/JSON Schema + the batch-runner SEAM + a reference default runner + the
  journaled batch-plan/fallback event vocabulary + interpreter wiring (store the opaque plan, do not interpret).
- A THROWAWAY demo workflow exercising an `if:`-gated (overlay) step + a `batch` step end-to-end (dry-run
  via FakeAgentRunner), removed by epic B; retained meanwhile as the visual-editing refinement sample.
- VISUAL EDITING in the workflow editor for the batch step (NEW) and the `if:` overlay predicate (EXISTING
  — confirm/extend the editor renders + edits `if:` and supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Overlays adopt `if:` (no new IR field): a deterministic precompute scripted step computes overlay-
      trigger booleans (has-children, has-linked-session-log, text/keyword trigger match) as step outputs;
      a criterion gated by `if: ${{ steps.<triggers>.outputs.<name> }}` is included when truthy and skipped
      (durable event) when falsy; the expression grammar is NOT extended. (A1)
- [ ] Replay determinism for inclusion: a mid-run store edit does not change the included/skipped outcome
      (read from the run-start journal, not live state); the resolved included-set is observable for coverage
      (journaled at run-start OR documented as recovered from skip statuses — decide + record). (A1)
- [ ] A `batch` step kind exists with declarative params (group/usd_budget/model_ladder), a batch-runner
      SEAM + a reference default runner; the runner journals its batch-plan + fallback as OPAQUE events the
      interpreter STORES but never branches on (a test asserts this); replay reads the recorded plan. (A2)
- [ ] The Burr-tripwire stays green (no asyncio/threading leaks outside the confined fan-out). (A2)
- [ ] A throwaway demo workflow exercises an `if:`-gated overlay step + a `batch` step end-to-end under the
      FakeAgentRunner (offline, no live calls), with a test; it is clearly labeled disposable. (A3)
- [ ] The workflow visual editor renders/edits the `batch` step and the `if:` overlay predicate, and
      supports add/remove of a conditionally-included prompt. (A4)
- [ ] make lint + the full test suite pass.
- [ ] The engine expresses conditional criterion inclusion (via `if:` + a precompute pattern) and budgeted
- [ ] A demo proves both offline; the batch step + the `if:` overlay are visually editable.
baseline.summary: Workflow engine: first-class conditional overlays + delegating batch step (engine-only; + throwaway demo + visual editing)

content.text: ## Summary

The visual editor's Save was rejected after any edit (even a drag) with 'branch: then is a required property': branch then/else arms were encoded as sub-processes with ids <gateway>@then, and reconstruction looked them up by that literal id. But '@' is illegal in a BPMN id (NCName) — the real bpmn-io parser DROPS such elements, so the arms vanished on Save. The unit tests missed it because they round-trip through xml.etree, which preserves anything.
## Fix
- Emit arm ids with a legal '.' separator and stamp each arm with a <rebar:Config _role=then|else> marker.
- Reconstruct arms STRUCTURALLY (the gateway->arm sequence flow + role marker), never from the arm id — robust to bpmn-js regenerating ids.
(src/rebar/llm/workflow/bpmn.py; commit 19d3985d.)
## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No emitted BPMN id is an illegal NCName (no '@'/':') — guarded by test_emitted_ids_are_legal_bpmn_ncnames in tests/unit/workflow/test_bpmn.py.
- [x] Branch arms are reconstructed after a simulated bpmn-js id rewrite — test_branch_arms_recovered_after_simulated_bpmnjs_id_rewrite in tests/unit/workflow/test_bpmn.py.
- [x] A faithful round-trip through the REAL bpmn-moddle preserves both arms and the save is accepted — test_branch_arms_survive_real_editor_save in tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py.

- [x] The full comprehensive sample round-trips through the real serializer with zero errors — test_full_demo_round_trips_through_real_serializer in tests/e2e/test_editor_e2e.py (tracked fixture tests/e2e/fixtures/roundtrip-demo.yaml).
## Verification
src/rebar/llm/workflow/bpmn.py (_gateway_arms / _arm_ids / _ROLE_KEY); tests above all green.

content.text: ## Summary

A Jira issue created directly in Jira (no rebar binding) is never adopted into the local store at steady state. Proven: REB-532 ("EXPERIMENT (delete me): assignee clobber repro", Bug, To Do) is fetched every pass but has no binding and no local ticket.
## Root Cause (edge-triggered adoption + prev_snapshot as a false "handled" proxy)
- REB-532 IS fetched — the inbound JQL has no rebar-label filter (`fetcher.py:67-79`).

- The binding-aware `inbound_differ.compute_inbound_mutations` skips any unbound issue by design (`inbound_differ.py:719-722`, docstring `:4-6` "local is source of truth"); it only emits `update`, never `create`.

- Inbound-CREATE lives only in `differ.compute_mutations`, which production calls as `compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot)` — BOTH Jira snapshots (`reconcile.py:901-903`). Create fires only for a key in `curr` but NOT `prev` (`differ.py:457-469`) = "new since last pass".

- `prev_snapshot` means "seen in a prior fetch", used as a proxy for "already handled" — but it is NOT "bound to a local ticket". `reconcile.py:1407` advances prev via `shutil.copy2(curr, prev)` UNCONDITIONALLY, regardless of whether adoption actually landed. So once REB-532 is in prev it is in both snapshots -> present-in-both (field-drift) branch -> never re-adopted. There is NO level-triggered reconvergence that asks "fetched key has no binding -> adopt".
- Runtime proof: `compute_mutations(prev={}, curr={REB-532}) -> 1 inbound create`; `compute_mutations(prev={REB-532}, curr={REB-532}) -> 0`.
## Why the test suite misses it

- The differ unit tests model `compute_mutations(arg1, arg2)` as `(local_state, jira_state)` (`test_differ.py:1-13`), so an unbound issue is always absent from arg1 and create always fires — validating a contract production does NOT use.
- Every adoption test uses `local={}` (empty prev) incl. the closest-named `test_unbound_jira_issue_without_rebar_id_label_still_creates` (`test_differ.py:542`).

- The only two-pass integration test binds everything in pass 1 (`test_reconcile_idempotency.py:268,291`), so the "in prev but still unbound" state is never constructed; the unconditional `copy2` at `reconcile.py:1407` is untested.
- `inbound_differ` tests assert unbound issues are ignored (`test_inbound_differ.py:112`), entrenching the skip.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Create an issue directly in Jira REB (no rebar-id), e.g. REB-532.
2. Let >= 2 reconcile passes run (so it enters prev_snapshot).
3. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run` and search the plan for the issue.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: a Jira-native issue is adopted into the local store (a `jira-*` local ticket + confirmed binding) and stays converged.
- Actual: it is fetched but never adopted; permanently orphaned in Jira.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Jira-native issue with no binding is adopted into local within one pass, regardless of whether it is already in `prev_snapshot` (level-triggered, not just edge-triggered) — without re-deriving all historical creates every pass (respect the prev_snapshot perf optimisation).

- [ ] `prev_snapshot` advance (`reconcile.py:1407`) no longer marks an issue "handled" when adoption did not actually bind it (decouple prev-advance from adoption success), OR a binding-aware reconvergence adopts unbound fetched issues.
- [ ] A RED test constructs the failing state: the SAME key present in both `prev_snapshot` and `curr_snapshot` with NO binding, then asserts it is adopted.
- [ ] REB-532 is adopted (or explicitly excluded as a test artifact) after the fix.
## Notes

Discovered comparing Jira REB vs local. Files: `differ.py`, `inbound_differ.py`, `reconcile.py`, `fetcher.py`, `apply_inbound.py`; tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/`, `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/`.
## Guardrails (must-preserve — prior-art + archaeology; folds in the corrected plan)
Approved policy: ADOPT unbound Jira-native issues (test-ticket hygiene is the creator's responsibility). But adoption is gated:
- [ ] Adoption MUST consult `bindings-retired.json` (`is_retired`) so a locally-archived-then-retired issue is not resurrected into a delete/re-adopt loop (interacts with C's GC).

- [ ] Run the rebar-id label audit (L9) and the label-derived-binding suppression (L10, bug 4354) FIRST: an issue already carrying a `rebar-id:`/`rebar-id-` label is bound — adopting it double-writes identity and recreates the phantom `jira-dig-NNNN` + ghost-label defect and can trip the double-bind quarantine (L11).
- [ ] Seed the per-binding BASELINE from the adopted issue's fields on bind, so the first outbound diff is EMPTY (echo suppression, L2).

- [ ] Adoption `create + bind` is keyed on the external id (idempotency/dedup key) so two overlapping passes cannot create duplicate local items before the binding lands [prior art: K8s read-all-then-write].

- [ ] Level-triggered: `unbound = fetched_keys - bound_keys` each pass (replaces the `prev_snapshot` edge-trigger), so a failed adoption re-fires until it binds. Do NOT rely on `prev_snapshot` for the trigger.
- [ ] Proven by the convergence property with an issue present in BOTH prev/curr snapshots and unbound (the exact steady-state cell the current suite never constructs).
## Implementation contract (foundation-first — read before coding)

DEPENDS ON amiss-bun-wince (baf7): this bug is the `ADOPT` / `SKIP_RETIRED` Decision cells of `classify()` plus the gated adopt handler. The trigger is LEVEL-based: `unbound = fetched_keys - bound_jira_keys` computed EVERY pass from the binding store — prev_snapshot plays NO role in the trigger (its unconditional advance at pass end stays as-is for now; the rollout ticket owns its future).
Adoption handler ORDER (ADR 0027 #4 — each step has an existing helper; do not reimplement):
1. `BindingStore.is_retired(jira_key)` -> Decision SKIP_RETIRED (prevents the delete/re-adopt loop with the GC bug 13eb).

2. rebar-id label audit (rebar_id_audit.py, L9) + label-derived-binding suppression (differ.py L10 region): an issue already carrying rebar-id:/rebar-id- is BOUND — route to binding repair, never double-create (the phantom jira-dig-NNNN defect).

3. Create local ticket + bind keyed on the EXTERNAL id (idempotency: a second overlapping pass must no-op); use the existing bind_pending -> create -> marker -> bind_confirm write-ahead protocol (binding_store.py docstring).
4. Immediately `set_baseline(local_id, adopted_fields)` (foundation method) so the FIRST outbound diff is empty — echo suppression per ADR 0027 #4c / ADR 0029 #3.

RED test (the exact cell today's suite never constructs): SAME key in prev_snapshot AND curr_snapshot, no binding -> assert ADOPT fires. Plus: retired key -> SKIP_RETIRED; labeled key -> no double-bind (L11 quarantine NOT tripped).
Live acceptance cell: REB-532 adopted (or explicitly archived in Jira as a test artifact — decide and record in a closing comment).

Files: classify.py (cells), apply_inbound.py or a new adopt handler beside dispatch_one.py, binding_store.py (consume, don't modify), fetcher.py (no changes — JQL already fetches unbound), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/ + diffing/ + integration two-pass test.

baseline.summary: Reconciler never adopts a Jira-native issue at steady state (edge-triggered inbound-create + prev_snapshot proxy)

content.text: Workflow gate ops re-resolve `LLMConfig.from_env()` independently instead of receiving the caller's resolved config, producing a DOCUMENTED correctness divergence: a library caller passing an explicit non-default `config=` has it honored for the LLM calls but the workflow verdict's `model`/`runner` fields still reflect the env config (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:78-79`).
## Why

Config resolution is a cross-cutting concern that should resolve once per run, not once per op. The current scatter silently ignores part of a caller's explicit configuration — a reliability/correctness gap for library/MCP consumers.
## What / files

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:113,329`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:60,104`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:89` — stop calling `LLMConfig.from_env(...)` per op.

- Resolve `cfg` once at the run boundary (`gate_dispatch.produce_*` / `review_plan`) and pass the `runner`/`model` identity into the ops as workflow `inputs` (the pattern already used for `ticket_id`), so ops read it from `ctx.inputs` rather than re-deriving from env. Keep `StepContext` config-agnostic (`executor.py:107-120`).
## Scope
In: single-resolution + thread model/runner identity through inputs; remove the documented divergence note. Out: redesigning `StepContext` to carry the full `LLMConfig` type.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A caller passing an explicit `config=` sees that model/runner reflected in BOTH the LLM calls and the verdict's `model`/`runner` fields.
- [ ] No op calls `LLMConfig.from_env()` after the run boundary resolves it.
- [ ] The divergence caveat at `plan_review/__init__.py:78-79` is removed (no longer true).
- [ ] Existing plan-review/completion gate tests still pass.

baseline.summary: Honor caller's explicit LLMConfig in workflow gate ops

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Configure a Jira project whose workflow has a status with no entry in the reconciler's `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` map (e.g. a custom state like "In UAT").
2. Move a Jira issue bound to a **closed** local ticket into that unmapped status.
3. Run a reconcile pass with inbound sync enabled.
**Expected:** the unmapped status is skipped (local status left untouched) and the unmapped status is surfaced as a deduped bridge alert.

**Actual (before fix):** `inbound_differ._map_jira_to_local_fields` did `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS.get(status_raw, "open")` — the `"open"` default silently REOPENED the closed local ticket. This class of bug bit once before (ticket 929a). Audit Reliability finding #7 (MEDIUM).
## Why it matters
Reopening closed work corrupts board state, re-enters tickets into ready/next-batch dispatch, and invalidates the meaning of completion attestations — all with no operator signal.
## What / files

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py`: `_map_jira_to_local_fields` no longer defaults an unmapped status to `"open"` — it OMITS the status field from the mapped dict when the Jira status has no `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` entry and no `rebar-status:` label. `_diff_jira_vs_local` skips the status field when it is absent from the mapped dict, so no status change is emitted (no silent reopen).

- Observability reuses the EXISTING fetcher alert: `fetcher.py` already emits a deduped `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge alert (built from the same `config.jira_to_local_status` mapping) for any unmapped status seen in a snapshot — so no second, redundant alert is added in the differ (alert at fetch, skip at diff is the correct split).
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`: documents the skip + existing-alert behaviour for unmapped inbound statuses.
## Scope
In: inbound_differ.py skip logic, docs. Out: adding a redundant differ-side alert (the fetcher already alerts); changing any existing status mapping; the `idea↔IDEA` round-trip must stay unaffected.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An inbound Jira status with no mapping is skipped (no local status change) — a closed bound local ticket stays closed
- [ ] The unmapped status is surfaced via the existing deduped `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge alert (no silent handling)

- [ ] Regression test: an unmapped inbound status against a **closed** bound local ticket emits no status change (`"status" not in changed`); mapped statuses (incl. `IDEA→idea`, `Done→closed`) still flow
- [ ] `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents the skip + alert behaviour
- [ ] Existing reconciler/bridge suites stay green; `make test` green

baseline.summary: Unmapped inbound Jira status defaults to open — can silently reopen closed local tickets

content.text: ## Why

Entering beta is the cheapest window to retire deprecated user-facing surface before a larger user base depends on it. Beyond the 7 registry-catalogued aliases (handled by the sibling "Remove deprecated aliases pre-beta" story), the pre-beta sweep found additional user-facing deprecations that should retire in the same clean break. Pre-1.0, so semver-permissible; still breaking for external consumers.
Citations:

- lib+MCP+CLI `list_epics` family: `__init__.py:1056-1090` (lib, warns), `_mcp_reads.py:239-252` (MCP tool, suppresses warning), `_engine_support/reads_cli.py:506-516` (`list-epics` CLI subcommand, warns), `schemas/list_epics.schema.json` (deprecated output schema). Replacement: `list_tickets(ticket_type='epic'|'bug', …)`.
- CLI `--verdict-hash` accepted-but-ignored flag `_commands/transition.py:45,94-102`.
- env `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` → canonical `REBAR_LLM_*` `llm/config.py:15,363-371`.
- CLI `--no-sync` → `--no-pull` `_engine_support/reads_cli.py:624`.
- cfg value `reconciler.lock_backend="file"` (accept-and-ignore branch) `_config_schema.py:335-336`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:100-116`.
- flat-conf key `rebar_id_guard_mode` `config.py:289-300`.
## What

Migrate this repo off each (per the DE7 migrate-first rule), confirm no internal use, then remove the shims/flags/tool/subcommand/schema + update docs and the deprecation registry. Retire the whole `list_epics` family together. Sequence AFTER the registry-completeness ticket adds any missing warnings, so external users had at least one warning release where feasible.
## Scope
User-facing deprecated surface NOT in the DE7 registry seven. Breaking for external consumers (accepted, pre-1.0). Does NOT touch event-schema/on-disk-store back-compat (that is KEEP — see report).
cascade_flag: removes public CLI/MCP/lib entrypoints + a schema — sweep external references; update help text, README, docs, and MCP tool listing.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] This repo uses only canonical replacements; repo-wide grep confirms no internal use of the removed surfaces
- [ ] `list_epics` retired across lib + MCP tool + CLI subcommand + output schema
- [ ] `--verdict-hash`, `--no-sync`, `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS`, flat `rebar_id_guard_mode`, and `lock_backend="file"` removed
