baseline.description:
Jira reconciler silently fails to sync comments and inbound links while reporting
`converged` — three distinct defects, all hidden behind a pass that counts failed
sub-operations toward "applied N of N" and exits 0.

## Context

Investigation (/rebar-debug, 2026-07-17) established that status/existence sync is
healthy (0 drift across ~1200 tickets), but three field-level sync paths are broken
and invisible:

- **Comment sync (P1):** `get_comments()` returns only the first 50 of N comments
  (no `--paginate`), so outbound dedup re-posts the rest every pass. 13 tickets have
  been inflated to Jira's 5000-comment hard cap (local truth: 22-76 comments each);
  further adds fail `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and are swallowed.
- **Inbound link direction (P2):** `_diff_links_inbound` (inbound_differ.py:519-527)
  AND `_diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:198-203) both invert the
  inward/outward -> blocks/depends_on mapping. Latent since 2026-06-15 (`f6687adf4`);
  UNMASKED when the outbound direction fix landed (`6b25dbead`/`43d154523`, 07-16/17)
  — the two inversions previously cancelled on round-trip. Now ~815 inbound link
  applies/pass are cycle-rejected by rebar's guard.
- **Observability (meta):** a pass with failed sub-ops still prints `applied N of N`
  / exits 0 / logs `converged`. The `RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP` flag (default off)
  exists but is not enabled; swallowed comment failures land in `comment_errors` and
  are never counted as failures.

## Jira cleanup safety plan (T4 — destructive-step rollback)

The comment de-duplication is IRREVERSIBLE (Jira comment deletion cannot be undone
via API). It is a deliberate, justified destructive step (the tickets are permanently
unable to sync until duplicates are purged), executed only with these guardrails:

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup:** export the FULL comment payload (id, body, author,
      created) for all 13 tickets to a versioned JSON artifact BEFORE any deletion, so
      any comment can be re-created if needed.
- [ ] **Dry-run first:** the cleanup script has a `--dry-run` (default) mode that
      lists exactly which comment IDs would be deleted and which one canonical copy of
      each distinct body is kept; a human reviews the dry-run diff before `--execute`.
- [ ] **Keep-one dedup rule:** for each distinct normalized body, keep the OLDEST
      copy (lowest created) and delete the rest; never delete a body with only one copy.
      Only delete comments authored by the bridge bot identity (never human comments).
- [ ] **Idempotent + resumable:** re-running is safe; on partial failure, re-run
      `--dry-run` to see the remaining duplicates and resume. Deletions are logged
      (ticket, comment id, body hash) to an artifact as they happen.
- [ ] **Sequencing:** run ONLY after P1 is deployed to main, else the buggy
      reconciler re-inflates duplicates within minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child tickets (P1, P2, observability, test-hardening, Jira-cleanup) are closed.
- [ ] A reconcile pass shows 0 comment-cap failures and 0 inbound link
      cycle-rejections for the previously-affected tickets.
- [ ] The cleanup backup artifact + dry-run log exist before any live deletion.
- [ ] P1: outbound comment sync is idempotent — a steady-state pass emits 0 comment
- [ ] P2: an inbound Jira `Blocks` link round-trips to the correct rebar relation
- [ ] Observability: a pass with any silent sub-op no-op reports failure (non-zero
- [ ] Test hardening: unit + integration + E2E coverage added for all three failure
- [ ] Jira data cleanup: the 13 capped tickets are de-duplicated so new comments can
baseline.summary: Jira reconciler: silent comment + inbound-link sync failures

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The deterministic Pass 3 of code-review ignores project routing. `code_review_decide` passes
`registry.threshold_for` as a bare callable and calls `registry.nit_suppressed_criteria()` with no
arguments (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:419,427`), so both read the **packaged**
routing map and a project overlay's threshold / blocking / nit-suppression re-tunes are dropped —
even though those resolvers already accept an optional routing map
(`src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:309-343`) and `registry.effective_routing(repo_root)`
already exists on `origin/main` (`registry.py:171-176`). Third of five seams (root cause on
superseded bug 8a4b).

## Approach

Pure wiring — thread the repository-effective routing map into the two Pass-3 resolvers:

- In `code_review_decide`, compute `routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)`
  (`ctx.repo_root` is already used in this function at `workflow_ops.py:414`).
- Bind that map into the `threshold_for` callable handed to `pass3_over_findings` (e.g.
  `functools.partial(registry.threshold_for, routing_map=routing)`), and pass it to
  `registry.nit_suppressed_criteria(routing)`.

No `registry.py` change is needed — the optional `routing_map` parameters landed with story 5065,
and `effective_routing` is on `origin/main` today (cited above).

**Rejected alternative.** Re-implementing routing resolution inside `workflow_ops` — the shared
resolvers already exist and are the single source of truth; duplicating them would diverge from
plan-review's routing semantics.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — thread `effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)` into the
  Pass-3 `threshold_for` binding and `nit_suppressed_criteria` call.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — extend this shared test file (a new file
  first created earlier in the stack; this ticket appends its Pass-3 routing cases). This ticket
  **depends on** child 2 `[rebar:761e-5af2-ed57-408a]`, which will introduce both the synthetic-repo
  fixture and the logical `project.<name>` attribution on code-review findings; the Pass-3 tests
  here consume a finding carrying that logical id.

## Testing

- Happy path (routing): a synthetic repo re-tunes `project.foo` (lower block threshold + blocking,
  and separately `nit_suppressed`); assert Pass 3 blocks / demotes the project finding per the
  **project** routing, not the packaged default. The routed finding carries the logical
  `project.foo` id that child 2 `[rebar:761e-5af2-ed57-408a]` will attribute.
- Parity: with no overlay, Pass-3 dispositions are byte-identical to today (packaged-default path).

Tier: unit; feeds deterministic findings (carrying logical `project.foo`) through
`code_review_decide` with a synthetic effective routing — no LLM.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Project routing (threshold / blocking / nit-suppression) governs the deterministic Pass 3
      for a project finding; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k routing`.
- [ ] With no overlay, Pass-3 dispositions are unchanged (parity); verified by the same `-k routing`
      selector asserting the packaged-default path.
baseline.summary: Thread repository-effective routing into code-review Pass 3

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
An LLM plan review can consume the full model cost, return `PASS`, and still leave the reviewed ticket without a signed plan-review attestation unless signing was separately requested. That discards the review's durable gate artifact: the subsequent claim path cannot distinguish the paid, passing review from no review at all and may require another billable run or a manual recovery step.

The intended contract is already stated by the dedicated `rebar review-plan` documentation and library docstring: a non-blocking PASS signs the plan-review attestation consumed by the claim gate. All public routes that perform the same billable plan review must converge on one default: sign a fresh attestation after PASS. Deliberately skipping the signature must be explicit, visible, and exceptional.

**Scope decision (2026-07-24): MCP is OUT of scope for this epic.** The MCP `review_plan`
tool derives signing from server read-only mode (`sign=not ro`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`) and
exposes no caller-facing `sign` parameter. Adding one — plus the machine-readable read-only
unsigned reason — is a distinct public-contract change to a different boundary, with its own
generated-reference and tool-schema consequences. It is split out rather than carried here.
This epic now covers the **CLI** and **library** plan-review boundaries only.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create or select an open, non-exempt ticket with a reviewable plan and no current plan-review attestation.
2. Run the plan-review operation through a public plan-review route without an explicit no-sign option.
3. Allow the LLM review to complete with verdict `PASS`.
4. Run `rebar verify-signature <ticket-id> --output json`.
5. Observe that verification reports the ticket as unsigned even though the full review cost was incurred and no opt-out was requested.

## Expected Behavior
Every mutating public plan-review entry point signs and persists a plan-review attestation by default when the final verdict is a signable, non-degraded `PASS`. The attestation binds the reviewed material fingerprint and verified source SHA exactly as the claim gate expects.

Skipping signing requires an explicit opt-out at the relevant boundary: `--no-sign` for CLI use, `sign=False` for library use. The output clearly states whether the attestation was signed and, when deliberately skipped, why.

## Actual Behavior
The default behavior is correct on the CLI and library routes, but nothing at the real parser/API boundary PINS it: a future refactor could silently flip the default with no test failing. The signing default is therefore an undefended invariant rather than a defect in itself.

## Approach
1. Inventory the CLI dispatcher, the dedicated `review-plan` command, and the library `review_plan` call paths and identify where the default changes or the signing wrapper is bypassed.
2. Route every mutating plan-review surface through the same sign-on-PASS finalization seam. Keep the structural guards that prohibit signatures for BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, local/unattested-source, and otherwise non-signable results.
3. Make deliberate unsigned execution explicit at each public boundary. CLI exposes `--no-sign`; the library exposes `sign=False`.
4. Preserve idempotent reuse of an already-current attestation. A default invocation should neither rerun the LLM nor emit a duplicate signature when the claim gate already accepts the current attestation.
5. Preserve signing-failure behavior: a PASS whose signature persistence was attempted but failed is not reported as ordinary success. It returns the established retryable failure disposition and points to the non-LLM `sign-review` recovery path when the PASS sidecar remains current.
6. Update user, CLI, and LLM-framework documentation so the default, opt-out syntax, non-signable verdicts, and recovery behavior match the implementation.

Rejected: leaving signing opt-in to avoid ticket writes. The review is already a gate operation whose purpose is to produce the claim-consumable attestation; callers needing a pure read have an explicit no-sign mechanism. Rejected: signing BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, or local-source results, because those are not certifiable PASS outcomes. Rejected (2026-07-24): carrying the MCP `sign` opt-out here — see the scope decision above.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`
- plan-review dispatcher/finalization modules found during the call-path inventory
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`
- library surface tests for plan review
- `docs/cli-reference.md`
- `docs/user-guide.md`
- `docs/llm-framework.md`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`

Explicitly NOT in scope: `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, MCP surface tests, and generated MCP
reference inputs/outputs.

## Testing / Verification
- Unit tests cover sign-on-PASS and never-sign verdict/source guards at the shared finalization seam.
- CLI tests exercise default signing and explicit `--no-sign` through the actual argument parser and dispatcher.
- Library contract tests exercise default `sign=True` and explicit `sign=False`.
- An end-to-end lifecycle test runs a passing plan review through the real CLI route, verifies the resulting signature, and then proves the claim gate accepts it without a second LLM call.
- Documentation/help drift checks pin the default and every supported opt-out/recovery path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A non-exempt ticket receiving a non-degraded PASS through each mutating public plan-review entry point (CLI `review-plan`, library `review_plan`) gets a persisted plan-review attestation by default; interface tests verify the attestation is present and claim-valid.
- [ ] An end-to-end lifecycle test invokes the real CLI `review-plan` route without an opt-out, verifies the attestation matches the current material fingerprint, and proves a subsequent `rebar claim` succeeds without another LLM call.
      (Note: the epic's original wording named an "affected `rebar review` plan route". No such
      route exists — `rebar review` is the separate `review_ticket` op, `_cli/__init__.py:413` —
      so the e2e was written against the real `review-plan` CLI route.)
- [ ] CLI unsigned execution requires the explicit `--no-sign` flag; parser tests prove omission signs and presence deliberately skips signing.
- [ ] Library unsigned execution requires explicit `sign=False`; contract tests prove the default is `sign=True`.
- [ ] BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, and degraded results remain unsigned, and explicit `sign=False`
      withholds the signature; table-driven tests verify each guard, including a direct
      `attest.sign_plan_review` refusal test so the guard is pinned at the artifact that owns
      it rather than at one caller.
      **Scope amendment (2026-07-24, audited):** this criterion originally also asserted that
      *exempt* and *unattested local-source* results remain unsigned. Investigation proved
      BOTH assert behavior that does not hold on current main, and each is a defect in its own
      right rather than missing coverage of this epic's invariant. They are DELEGATED, not
      dropped:
      - `--source local` signs a claim-valid attestation with `verified_at_sha=None` ->
        5128-0856-d80f-4eb6 (melancholy-firstborn-shihtzu). Root cause proven; repair blocked
        on a suite-wide decision (the offline suite defaults to `source=local`).
      - a `bug` returns `runner='pydantic_ai'`, runs a full review and signs, so the
        `runner != "exempt"` guard never engages -> 26a4-a0e8-e539-464d (quibbling-bionic-olm).
      Pinning either as-is would have encoded a defect as expected behavior.
- [ ] A PASS with an attempted signature-persistence failure returns the established retryable nonzero disposition and identifies `sign-review` as the recovery path; `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py` verifies the behavior.
- [ ] Re-running the default operation with a current claim-valid attestation reuses it without an LLM call or duplicate signature event; an interface test verifies both conditions.
- [ ] `rebar review-plan --help` states that PASS signs by default and names the explicit unsigned exception; a help drift test verifies the generated text.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md`, and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` accurately describe sign-on-PASS, explicit opt-out, never-sign outcomes, and `sign-review` recovery; documentation checks pass.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: Plan review PASS does not sign an attestation by default on every public route

baseline.description:
# Add execution-phase plan reviews

## Goal
Allow plan changes made during implementation to be reviewed with a fixed 0.80 blocking floor, while preserving stricter planning reviews and preventing a signature from binding phase or related material that changed during review.

## Implementation
- Add reducer-maintained `plan_review_phase: planning|execution` to compiled state, distinct from prompt `execution_mode`. Only the winning/normal `process_status` branch updates it: a committed winning STATUS target `in_progress` sets execution; target `open` sets planning; every other target preserves the current value. Losing fork events never update it, and force transitions use the same winning target rule. Carry the field through SNAPSHOT compaction. Verify `_snapshot_strip_keys()` in `_commands/compact.py` does not strip it. Review reads the compiled field O(1), never scans raw history.
- For a pre-feature snapshot without the field, bootstrap planning when compiled status is `open` or `idea`, execution for every other known status. An unknown status raises the existing reducer validation error rather than guessing. Bump `reducer/_cache.py::_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` so the first post-upgrade reduction applies this once; later snapshots persist it. Emit one structured INFO `plan_review_phase_bootstrap` with ticket ID, compiled status, and chosen phase. This is a cache recomputation, not a write/compaction wave: ordinary reads rebuild the local derived cache lazily and do not append ticket events.
- Restructure `build_manifest`'s fixed initial list to emit exact lines in this order after `advisory:` and before `rebar-version:`: `review-phase: planning|execution`, then for execution only `priority-floor: 0.80`. Each line has exactly a prefix, one ASCII space, and one token. Add `manifest.validate_review_phase_metadata(phase: object, floor: object, *, legacy_absent: bool) -> ReviewPhaseMetadata` as the single grammar/policy helper; `ReviewPhaseMetadata` is exactly `{phase: planning|execution, priority_floor: float|None}`. Manifest parsers extract raw tokens and call it. `manifest_review_phase()` returns legacy planning only when the line is absent; `manifest_priority_floor()` returns `None` only when absent. The helper raises `ManifestFormatError` for duplicates signaled by callers, missing/extra tokens, unknown phase, bool/non-numeric/non-finite floor, or floor outside `[0.0, 1.0]`; a floor without a phase and execution without exactly one floor are malformed. Existing parsers scan by prefix rather than fixed offsets, so added lines do not change regver/material/dependency parsing. The signed line records the phase the LLM ran under; compiled state records current phase, and compatibility compares these distinct values rather than comparing current state to itself.
- Extend 75de's `DerivedPlanReviewHealth` with always-present `phase_status: compatible|incompatible|malformed`. Compatibility table: current planning + signed planning/legacy planning = compatible; current planning + signed execution = incompatible; current execution + signed planning/legacy planning = compatible; current execution + signed execution floor >= 0.80 = compatible; any malformed phase/floor or execution floor < 0.80 = malformed/incompatible respectively (`malformed` is syntax/shape only, `incompatible` is syntactically valid policy mismatch). The fixed 0.80 protocol policy is not configurable. Raising it later invalidates lower-floor execution attestations; lowering it accepts higher-floor attestations without migration.
- Extend 75de's `compute_validity` plan-review branch to parse phase/floor with pins after signature/kind verification and return phase_status on every later result. After prerequisite 75de is implemented on the feature branch, claim, idempotent reuse, and drift refresh share `compute_validity(DEFAULT|DRIFT_REFRESH)` and inherit phase enforcement. Child 2bbd's later CLOSE call inherits it. Child cb6b's later audit/UI health reads the same result. Completion-verifier calls never invoke phase, floor, or pin parsers.
- Persist review-time phase data for failed-sign recovery with an exact additive `plan_review_result_v2` schema: new full reviews always write JSON `review_phase` as lowercase string `planning` or `execution`; planning omits `priority_floor`; execution writes JSON number `priority_floor: 0.8` (not string and not null). For legacy sidecars, both keys absent means planning/None. A present null, only-one-key legacy combination, bool, string floor, unknown phase, planning with a floor, or execution without a floor is malformed. Add `sidecar.parse_review_phase_metadata(payload) -> ReviewPhaseMetadata`; it passes raw JSON values to `manifest.validate_review_phase_metadata` and translates `ManifestFormatError` to `SidecarReviewPhaseError`. `resign_plan_review` calls this named parser, compares the result with current compiled phase, and refuses incompatible/malformed re-sign. A passing re-sign builds the manifest from the recorded review-time phase/floor, not a newly inferred phase. This edit composes after 75de's related-material sidecar guard and before acaf's current pin collection/sign step.
- Thread phase through every Pass-3 entry. Add required `review_phase` with string enum `planning|execution` to both schemas atomically: update the already-closed `plan_review_precheck_output.schema.json` properties/required arrays while retaining `additionalProperties: false`; update the intentionally open `plan_review_decide_input.schema.json` properties/required arrays while retaining `additionalProperties: true`. `workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck` emits the compiled value. In `llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml`, add `review_phase: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.review_phase }}` to both `plan_review_decide` `with:` blocks: the code-grounded verify branch and the non-agentic else branch. `plan_review_decide` requires the field and calls `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings(..., execution_review=(review_phase == "execution"))`. The verify-failure recovery in `workflow/gate_dispatch.py` reads `precheck["review_phase"]` and passes the same bool; absence in a legacy persisted run defaults planning. These are the complete call sites: normal workflow calls pass the explicit bool; direct unit/legacy callers may use the default false only when they intentionally model planning. The schema/YAML/code ship atomically from one checkout; workflows are synchronous and have no cross-version in-flight server state. Update schema golden/cutover tests for the closed output contract and rollback together.
- Define `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings(findings, verifs, *, execution_review: bool = False)` exactly at the module-level function. Its local `_threshold_for` closure lexically captures the parameter, calls `_criteria.threshold_for(...)`, destructures `(block_threshold, blocking_enabled)`, and returns `(max(block_threshold, 0.80), blocking_enabled)` only when `execution_review and blocking_enabled`; otherwise it returns the original pair. Pass this closure to `review_kernel.pass3_over_findings`. This changes normal Pass-3 only: advisory-only criteria keep `blocking_enabled=False`, novelty and completion floors are untouched, deterministic structural failures remain blocking, and sub-floor findings remain visible.
- Own one pre-sign generation transaction for ordinary review, drift refresh, and re-sign. `PlanReviewGeneration` is `{phase, priority_floor, own_material, relation_snapshot, ticket_store_revision}` where `relation_snapshot` is child acaf's exact `PlanRelationSnapshot` and equality is dataclass equality across every field. Full review collects the initial generation before the LLM; drift refresh and re-sign collect it immediately before their non-LLM probe. No ticket-store write occurs before the model/probe succeeds, so an LLM/provider failure retains existing unsigned INDETERMINATE behavior and leaves no partial state.
- Before signing, retain one immutable `initial_generation` captured before the LLM/probe; retries never replace this baseline. Retry outside the lock at most three times only for an unstable tracker revision: read clean tracker HEAD, collect a fresh generation, read HEAD again; unequal HEADs emit structured WARN `plan_review_generation_retry` with attempt/before/after and retry. A stable fresh generation unequal to the initial generation is terminal unsigned stale (`plan_review_generation_changed`) and requires re-review; it is not retried. Under the global write lock, require the same clean HEAD and exact generation, then append and commit the signature atomically. Under-lock HEAD/generation mismatch consumes a retry; exhaustion returns retryable unsigned. `LockTimeout` returns retryable unsigned without writing. Dirty/unmerged tracker or other terminal collection/sign failure emits structured ERROR `plan_review_sign_aborted` and returns unsigned without traceback.
- Document the phase/floor manifest contract, health compatibility table, fixed-floor rationale, generation transaction, and rollback behavior in advanced `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. Rollback disables claim/close enforcement first and pauses every `rebar compact` invocation for the downgrade window; with compaction paused, existing phase-bearing snapshots remain lossless. Old reducers preserve the unknown snapshot field when replaying an existing snapshot. If old code fully re-reduces raw events after its own cache bump, the phase field is absent and a later forward upgrade reboots it from compiled status; operators accept that documented loss of historical phase precision during the rollback window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Winning entry into `in_progress` sets compiled `plan_review_phase=execution`.
- [ ] Winning entry into `open` sets compiled `plan_review_phase=planning`.
- [ ] Other winning status targets preserve the projection.
- [ ] Losing fork STATUS events never update the projection.
- [ ] Force transitions follow the same winning target rule.
- [ ] Normal SNAPSHOT compaction and older-reducer snapshot pass-through preserve the exact field value.
- [ ] The rollback test proves old-code raw-event re-reduction drops the unknown field and forward upgrade reboots it from compiled status, with the documented precision-loss window.
- [ ] Pre-feature open/idea snapshots bootstrap planning once; every other known status bootstraps execution once.
- [ ] Bootstrap emits the exact structured INFO and does not append ticket events.
- [ ] Reducer-cache versioning activates the lazy bootstrap idempotently.
- [ ] Planning manifests contain exactly `review-phase: planning` in the documented position.
- [ ] Execution manifests contain exactly `review-phase: execution` then `priority-floor: 0.80` in the documented position.
- [ ] Legacy phase-less attestations parse as planning.
- [ ] Every named phase/floor syntax error raises `ManifestFormatError`; existing manifest parsers remain unchanged.
- [ ] Planning state accepts planning/legacy and rejects syntactically valid execution attestations.
- [ ] Execution state accepts planning/legacy and execution floor >= 0.80.
- [ ] Execution state rejects a syntactically valid execution floor < 0.80 as incompatible.
- [ ] Malformed phase/floor produces `phase_status=malformed`.
- [ ] `DerivedPlanReviewHealth.phase_status` is present on every plan-review validity result.
- [ ] Claim, reuse, drift refresh, and re-sign enforce phase through the shared validity/phase helpers; child 2bbd and cb6b consume the same boundary later.
- [ ] Completion-verifier validity never calls phase, floor, or pin parsers.
- [ ] Re-sign parses the exact v2 JSON phase fields through `sidecar.parse_review_phase_metadata`, uses the recorded values, and refuses every incompatible/malformed variant.
- [ ] Execution Pass-3 destructures `(block_threshold, blocking_enabled)` and floors only the float threshold when blocking is enabled.
- [ ] A production workflow integration test starts from compiled execution phase and proves both YAML decide branches receive `review_phase` and block a finding below 0.80 that planning would not block.
- [ ] The verify-failure recovery test proves `gate_dispatch` passes execution phase to Pass-3 and legacy missing phase defaults planning.
- [ ] Schema golden tests prove `review_phase` is required in both schemas, precheck remains closed, decide input remains open, and schema/YAML/code rollback is version-coherent.
- [ ] Planning Pass-3 returns the original threshold pair unchanged.
- [ ] Advisory-only criteria, novelty/completion floors, deterministic failures, and visible sub-floor findings retain their documented behavior.
- [ ] A stable generation equal to the initial generation signs and commits under one lock.
- [ ] Any stable phase, own-material, relationship, related-fingerprint, or generation-field change returns terminal unsigned stale.
- [ ] HEAD instability retries at most three times with exact WARN fields, then returns retryable unsigned.
- [ ] Under-lock mismatch retries; `LockTimeout` returns retryable unsigned; neither writes a signature.
- [ ] Dirty/unmerged or terminal signing failure returns unsigned and emits `plan_review_sign_aborted`.
- [ ] Model/provider failure before signing writes no ticket event or signature and retains existing unsigned INDETERMINATE behavior.
- [ ] The production-path integration test covers stable collection, under-lock HEAD re-verification, signature append, and commit end to end.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` contains sections for the phase/floor manifest contract, phase_status compatibility table, fixed-0.80 rationale, PlanReviewGeneration transaction, and rollback precision-loss behavior.

## Verification
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_manifest.py` proves lifecycle projection, bootstrap, compaction, grammar, ordering, and parser compatibility.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_validity.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_execution_floor.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` proves the compatibility table, every consumer seam, tuple-aware threshold wrapping, completion isolation, and sidecar recovery.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_sign_transaction.py` proves stable/change/retry/exhaustion/dirty/LockTimeout/logging and no-write failure paths.
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_sign_transaction.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_execution_floor.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_schema_golden.py` runs production signing, both automatic execution-floor branches, verify-failure recovery, and closed-schema contract checks.
- `pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_docs.py` verifies the five required advanced-documentation sections.
- Run `make check` and the full non-LLM test suite, including the named integration and rollback tests.
baseline.summary: Add planning and execution phases to plan-review attestations

# The parity flip/agreement criteria are gold-blind, so a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate

## Context / Problem

Criterion (b) of the parity bar has two parts, and BOTH compare the two arms to each other without ever consulting the gold label that the same corpus carries:

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `agreement = _rate(pairs, lambda p: p[0].decision == p[1].decision)`
* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `decision_flips = ... a.decision != b.decision` (gold pairs are
  selected on `a.label`, but the label is never used in the COMPARISON)

Recall and false-accept in the same function DO consult `label`. So the bar already knows which arm is right on every gold item, and criterion (b) deliberately throws that away.

Consequence, measured on the recorded live Bedrock run (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`, re-scored offline with zero model calls after the 62ac false-accept fix): all THREE decision flips across both slots are cases where the CANDIDATE (Bedrock) matches gold and the BASELINE (direct Anthropic) does not.

| slot | case | spec | gold | v1 Anthropic | v2 Bedrock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | R-drop-column-no-backfill | code-review-db-migrations | block | advisory | **block** |
| frontier | FP-rename-all-callsites-updated | code-review-api-compat | advisory | block | **advisory** |
| frontier | FP-create-index-concurrently | code-review-db-migrations | advisory | block | **advisory** |

Bedrock is correct in 3 of 3. The bar reports these as "decision-level flip(s) on the gold set (must be 0)" — the criterion documented as never acceptable because "it changes what ships".

The same three disagreements also drive the only other remaining failure: frontier verdict agreement 0.929. At the scored corpus size of n=28, the 0.95 floor tolerates at most ONE disagreement anywhere in the corpus (27/28 = 0.964 passes, 26/28 = 0.929 fails), so the agreement failure is not independent evidence — it is the same two cases counted again.

## Why it matters

This is a gating criterion on rebar's non-inferiority bar. As written it can fail a strictly better candidate. It is the sibling of bug 62ac (the inverted false-accept metric): both come from a metric that measures the wrong direction of the same underlying quantity. 62ac is fixed; this one is not, and it is now the sole remaining blocker on the Bedrock parity slots.

Note this ticket does NOT propose relaxing the bar to let Bedrock pass. It proposes that the criterion measure what it claims to measure — a regression in what ships — which requires consulting gold on a gold-labelled corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and document whether criterion (b) should distinguish a gold-IMPROVING flip from a
      gold-REGRESSING one on gold-labelled items, and whether the agreement floor should be
      computed over non-gold items only (where no ground truth exists) or left as is.
- [ ] If a change is made, a test pins the direction: a candidate that flips a gold item TOWARD
      the gold label is scored differently from one that flips it AWAY.
- [ ] The recorded provider-parity results are re-scored offline against whatever bar results,
      with zero model calls, and the per-slot verdict recorded.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: parity flip + agreement criteria are gold-blind: a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate than the baseline

baseline.description:
## Why

`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (~line 112) validates titles with `if not title:`,
which is falsy only for the empty string — a whitespace-only title such as `"   "` is
truthy and is accepted. Per the decision for this epic, whitespace-only titles must be
rejected. Separately, cross-facade parity tests use only simple ASCII values, and the
create path's empty/`>255` title rejection has code enforcement but only an edit-path
test, leaving input-handling contracts thinly covered.

## What

Committed policy decisions (so the test oracle is unambiguous):
- **Whitespace validation:** reject a title iff `title.strip()` is empty (covers `""`,
  spaces, tabs, newlines). A title with surrounding whitespace but real content (e.g.
  `"  hi  "`) is ACCEPTED and **stored as-is** — validation must not silently mutate the
  value, so round-trip assertions expect the original bytes back.
- **Unicode normalization:** **preserve as-is (byte-identical round-trip); do NOT
  normalize** — with ONE documented pre-existing exception: `create_core`/`edit_core`
  already substitute `U+2192 (→)` → `->` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:121` and
  `:385`). That substitution is OUT OF SCOPE for this story and is retained; U+2192 is
  therefore EXCLUDED from the byte-identity corpus (or included only as an explicit
  "documented normalization" case asserting `→` becomes `->`). Composed (NFC) and
  decomposed (NFD) forms of the same string are otherwise treated as distinct values,
  each round-tripping unchanged — the oracle is per-form byte-identity, not cross-form
  equality.
- **Rejection identity (across facades):** "rejected identically" does NOT mean an
  identical wire representation — it means all three facades reject with the SAME
  human-readable message substring on their facade-appropriate surface: CLI → nonzero
  exit + message on stderr; library → `CommandError` (or the documented exception type)
  carrying the message; MCP → an error result carrying the message. The shared invariant
  is the message + "all three reject," not a shared exit code.

Then:
- Reject whitespace-only titles consistently across the CLI, library, and MCP
  create/edit surfaces.
- Add a create-path test for empty and `>255`-char title rejection.
- Add a curated cross-facade text corpus for values representable through all three
  facades; handle argv-impossible values (NUL) in library/MCP tests only.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (title validation)
- `tests/interfaces/facades/` (corpus + create-path validation tests)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A whitespace-only title (spaces/tabs/newlines) is rejected on create AND edit
      across CLI, library, and MCP, with a clear error.
- [ ] Create-path tests assert rejection of an empty title and a `>255`-char title.
- [ ] A title with surrounding whitespace + content (`"  hi  "`) is accepted and stored
      byte-identically (no silent trimming).
- [ ] A shared corpus (leading `-`/`--`, quotes, backslashes, LF/CRLF, emoji/non-BMP,
      NFC and NFD forms of one string as SEPARATE byte-identity cases, and a string of
      ≥1000 characters) round-trips byte-identically — EXCEPT U+2192, handled per the
      documented `→`→`->` exception — or is rejected identically (per the rejection-
      identity definition above) across all three facades; persisted/replayed content and
      structured output are asserted, with no stdout/stderr contamination.
- [ ] NUL / other argv-impossible values are covered via library/MCP tests only.
- [ ] Breaking-change handling: this is a user-visible tightening (callers passing
      whitespace previously succeeded). Document a back-out/expand-contract note. Run a
      concrete one-off store scan run pre-merge:
      `rebar list --output json | jq -e '[.[] | select(.title | test("^[[:space:]]*$"))] | length == 0'`
      (exit 0 = zero whitespace-only titles → no migration needed). If it exits nonzero,
      file a migration sub-task before landing.
- [ ] User-facing docs updated with concrete, grep-able artifacts: a `CHANGELOG.md` entry
      mentioning the whitespace-title rejection (`grep -qi 'whitespace' CHANGELOG.md`) and
      the CLI `create`/`edit` help text updated to state the non-empty-after-trim rule
      (verifiable by `rebar create --help` containing the rule).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Reject whitespace-only titles + create-path validation + cross-facade text corpus

# A dedicated `parent` verb, with `--force`

Raised while repairing an incident (88d9-fe42-e50f-4067) in which a reconcile pass cleared the `parent_id` of 63 tickets. Every prior parent was recoverable from the event log, but rebar had **no supported way to write most of them back**. Filed as an idea by operator direction: out of scope for that session.

## The gap

Hierarchy is edited only as a side effect of `edit`:

* `edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path. There is no `parent` / `move` / `reparent` verb, and
  `link`/`unlink` cover the six link RELATIONS, not containment.
* `edit` has no `--force`, so the `--parent` cascade's refusal
  (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`, "cannot re-parent to closed ticket") is absolute.
* `rebar revert <ticket> <uuid>` does not help: `process_revert`
  (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) only appends to `state["reverts"]`; its sole state effect is
  un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED. Reverting the offending EDIT leaves `parent_id` empty.
* `fsck-recover` is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
* `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library inherits the guard.

Net: the reconciler can DESTROY a parent edge automatically, but an operator cannot RESTORE one when the parent is closed — and the store has no supported route back to a state it previously held. The documented workaround ("reopen the parent first") means, at incident scale, reopening ~20 epics and re-closing them, which re-runs the LLM completion gate on already-signed closes and risks leaving a previously-closed epic open.

In this incident 61 of 63 affected tickets were closed and the current state was ACCEPTED by the operator on that basis; only the two non-closed tickets were repaired, and they were repairable precisely because their parents were still `open` / `in_progress`.

## Shape

A first-class `parent` verb owning containment, rather than a field on `edit`:

    rebar parent <child> <parent> [--force]
    rebar parent <child> --detach

with `--force` scoped to bypass ONLY a positively-known closed/inactive parent. Deliberately still enforced under `--force`: the parent must exist, no self-parent, no cycle, and the fail-closed branch for an UNVERIFIABLE status (`--force` overrides a KNOWN-closed parent, never an UNKNOWN one). Follows rebar's existing idiom (`claim --force`, `transition --force-close`): explicit intent, audited, never implicit.

Worth considering alongside it: whether `--force` should require a reason string (as `--force-close` does) so a hierarchy override leaves the same audit quality as a gate override.

## Why an idea rather than a bug

The capability gap is real but it only bites during repair of a defect that should not recur — the inbound parent clear that caused this incident was reverted, and its root cause (deciding a peer deletion from `managed_refs`, which cannot prove the peer ever had the ref) is being fixed separately. So this is a resilience/ergonomics improvement to reach for deliberately, not an urgent fix.
baseline.summary: Add a dedicated parent verb with --force, so a destroyed hierarchy is repairable

baseline.description:
# Live DC suite: residual assertions that cannot fail, or that can pass vacuously

## Provenance

Found by an independent verification pass over story `5200-e04e-246e-4aae`'s 18 acceptance criteria, commissioned while closing epic e369. Three findings from that pass were repaired immediately because they undermined the story's own evidence (the vacuous `08-assign` cell, the missing row-1 outbound cell, and the pagination precondition measured with the code under test). **These are the residual ones**, separated because none of them affects confidence in DC PRODUCT behaviour — they weaken the suite's self-protection, not its verdict on the bridge. Recorded rather than fixed inline so closing e369 was not gated on test-hardening that proves nothing new about Data Center.

## Finding A — three isolation assertions assert their own fixture's setup

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py`:

* `:87` asserts `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH == "off"`, but the `dc_store_copy_repo` fixture does
  `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_SYNC_PUSH", "off")` at `conftest.py:620`. The CI job env sets only
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` (`external-integration.yml:323-337`).
* `:88-92` loops `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN` — the IDENTICAL three names the
  fixture `monkeypatch.delenv`s at `conftest.py:624-625`. It is structurally impossible for this to
  detect a Cloud credential in the JOB environment, which is what its criterion claims it checks, and it
  does not cover other plausible names (`JIRA_TOKEN`, `JIRA_URL`).
* `test_dc_mutations.py:1696-1728` collects every `base_url = "..."` in the copied tree and asserts the
  set equals `{BASE}` — but the only file in the copy carrying a `base_url` is the `rebar.toml` the
  fixture itself wrote from `_BASE` (`conftest.py:607-617`), and `_BASE`/`BASE` are the same expression.
  It compares the fixture against itself, so it cannot detect the stray production URL it exists to
  catch.

**The isolation itself is REAL** — the fixture does set the env var and does delete the credentials — so these have genuine value as regression guards ON THE FIXTURE. The defect is that they claim more reach than they have, and a reader auditing "is the live suite safe against touching production?" would take false assurance from them.

## Finding B — two absence assertions read a FILTERED plan with no positive control

* idempotence, `test_dc_mutations.py:1782` — concludes from `mine == []`
* row-14 inbound, `test_dc_mutations.py:1382` — concludes from `not teardown`

Both derive a negative from an EMPTY filtered dry-run plan. Story 5200 already burned a cycle on `--filter-local-ids` being a post-filter that matched nothing ("1640 mutations computed, 0 match filter", recorded in that ticket's comment 4). Under that failure mode both assertions pass vacuously while proving nothing. Neither cell has a positive control demonstrating the filter CAN surface an entry for its own pair. Row 14 is partly protected by a second, positive assertion (the local ticket survives with a non-teardown status); idempotence has no such backstop.

## Finding C — smaller shape issues, same family

* `_out_status` (`test_dc_mutations.py:439-445`) mutates CONDITIONALLY (`if current != "in_progress"`),
  so on an already-`in_progress` ticket it would assert a state it did not create. Harmless today (an
  imported DC issue lands `open`), but it is the same "the oracle may be checking pre-existing state"
  shape as the `08-assign` vacuity that was just repaired.
* Row 3 (description, both directions) uses `in` containment where the criterion says the path EQUALS
  the value.
* Return codes and stderr are checked unevenly: the writing passes assert `"Traceback" not in
  cp.stderr` at 26 sites, but the mutation cells never check the return code, and the dry-run passes in
  `_plan_entries_for`, the pagination cell and the row-14 cell do not check `stderr` at all.
* `.signing-key`, `.opcert-key` and `.opcert-key.pub` are present in the copied tracker and are not part
  of the `.bridge_state*` scrub. Not covered by any criterion; noted because the copy is a throwaway
  that CI writes to.

## Why this is worth doing (and why it is not urgent)

The operator's standing priority is that DC/Cloud test parity is what gives confidence the DC feature is defect-free. An assertion that cannot fail contributes nothing to that confidence while LOOKING like it does — and this epic has repeatedly proved that the cost is real, not theoretical: a vacuous assignee oracle reported green for months and, once repaired, immediately surfaced product defect 8d68. So the class deserves closing. It is not urgent because each item here is a self-protection gap rather than a gap in what the suite says about Data Center.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Finding A: each of the three assertions either exercises a value the fixture did NOT author, or is
      re-labelled in code and docstring as a fixture regression guard — the overclaiming wording is the
      defect, so an honest narrowing is an acceptable fix, but it must be explicit
- [ ] Finding A: the credential check no longer shares a hardcoded name list with the fixture that
      deletes them (derive one from the other, or assert over a broader documented set including
      `JIRA_TOKEN`)
- [ ] Finding B: the idempotence cell gains a POSITIVE control proving `--filter-local-ids` can surface
      an entry for its own pair, so an empty filtered plan cannot be mistaken for convergence
- [ ] Finding B: the same positive-control property is asserted for the row-14 inbound cell, or that
      cell's existing positive assertion is documented as the backstop and shown sufficient
- [ ] Finding C: `_out_status` establishes the pre-state it needs rather than mutating conditionally
- [ ] every change is MUTATION-CHECKED — for an assertion whose whole defect is that it cannot fail, a
      fix without a demonstrated RED is unverifiable by construction, and the verdicts are recorded here
- [ ] no live cell is weakened or skipped, and the live suite's collected count does not drop (a dropped
      cell silently leaves the `_live_jira_ready` canary, the failure change 1203 had to repair)
baseline.summary: Live DC suite: residual assertions that cannot fail or pass vacuously (isolation, filtered-plan absence)

## Why

The E1-verified miss class (epic 6982, §5 of docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md;
runs/README.md §"3 MISSED asserted-capability cases") is: **a plan asserts that an existing,
NAMED module provides (or lacks) a capability, and the assertion is false against the code** —
so the executing agent builds on a capability that isn't there, or rebuilds one that already
is. The three verified misses:

- `dc58` — the plan's sign step used a helper `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` does not have
  (signing lives in `rebar.signing`; completion.py:350 only *references* the close gate's
  signing). Pipeline was redesigned mid-flight.
- `db7b` — the plan proposed bounding the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar via event **compaction**, but
  by rebar's own contract compaction folds ONLY `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (`_commands/compact.py:206`)
  and REVIEW_RESULT is reducer-ignored, so compaction never absorbs it. Retention is instead a
  dedicated `sidecar.prune` (`llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:72`).
- `5886` — the plan proposed a NEW unmapped-Jira-status alert that `fetcher.py` already emits
  (`_flag_unmapped_statuses` → `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status`, fetcher.py:219). The bug was
  gate-exempt, so nobody looked.

E4 (assumption/premise verification, blocking) probes assertions broadly but MISSED all three:
the named module EXISTS, so E4's existence check passes; the defect is the finer-grained
**capability-surface** mismatch (module present, specific capability absent — or present when
the plan says absent). This story ships a focused probe for exactly that surface.

## What

Add one new **advisory, code-grounded, AGENT-tier** plan-review criterion, id
`asserted-capability`, in the G6/E4 rubric family (facet `codebase-grounding`), that fires when
a plan makes a **capability-surface claim about a named module/symbol that it relies on**, and
that claim is refuted by the code. Two symmetric directions (one concern — capability claims
about named modules must be grounded):

- (A) plan asserts named module M PROVIDES capability C, but M lacks C (dc58, db7b);
- (B) plan asserts capability C is ABSENT / must be built, but M already provides C (5886).

**Mechanism (grounded against `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`).** The probe plugs into the EXISTING
generic pass machinery — no core pass change. Pass-1 runs it as one agentic finder
(`passes.pass1_chunk(..., agentic=True)`, dispatched because its exec tier is `AGENT`;
eval_solver.py:112-113 and pass1.py:3 "one agent per code-grounding criterion"). The finder
greps/reads the repo (and `resolve_symbol` for installed deps) to confirm the module's actual
capability surface. Pass-2 verifier grades its two criterion-local binary sub-answers; Pass-3
computes validity×impact deterministically; Pass-4 coaches surviving advisories. It ships
**advisory posture (never blocks)** — registry entry `default_posture: "advisory"`.

**Registration seam.** Because it is a packaged built-in LLM criterion it must be added to
`registry.CANONICAL_LLM` (registry.py:79), `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` (:66), and `AGENT_TIER` (:72),
given a routing entry in `criteria_routing.json`, a rubric prompt at
`reviewers/plan_review_asserted_capability.md`, and a regenerated `## asserted-capability`
guide section — else `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` (:430) flags it ORPHAN and CI fails
(the exact failure that bit R2/b080), and `validate_criteria_guide()` (:530) flags a missing
section.

**Prior art.** This extends the SAME four-pass finder/verifier/decide/coach machinery already
used by A1/E4/G6/removal-rationale (see docs/plan-review-gate.md); `removal-rationale` (the
removal-side code-grounded advisory dual of A1) is the direct structural precedent for a
gated-then-grounded two-sub-answer code criterion. No new pass, no new engine construct.

**Effectiveness measurement is future dogfood, not a blocking AC.** The just-landed standing
recorder `criterion_effectiveness.py` (commit 0d695be47, d8a5) AUTO-INCLUDES every criterion id
it sees, so `asserted-capability` accrues `detection_proxy` / `blocking_fp_proxy` from real
reviews with ZERO per-criterion wiring. The advisory→blocking promotion gate is the protocol
d8a5 documented in docs/plan-review-gate.md §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder +
advisory→blocking promotion gate"; this story cites it, it is not gated on accumulation time.

## Scope

- IN: the new criterion (registry + routing + rubric + guide), deterministic unit tests, a
  committed `criteria eval` fixture set + its result artifact (the bounded sanity check).
- OUT: promotion to blocking (future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change per the cited
  promotion gate); any E2/E3 batch eval (permanently rejected on cost); changing E4/A1.
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `.../criteria_routing.json`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_asserted_capability.md`,
  `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (regenerated),
  `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-asserted-capability.eval.yaml`,
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/asserted_capability_sanity.json`,
  `tests/unit/test_asserted_capability_criterion.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The criterion is REGISTERED advisory and non-orphan. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r; assert 'asserted-capability' in r.CANONICAL_LLM; assert 'asserted-capability' in r.CODEBASE_GROUNDED and 'asserted-capability' in r.AGENT_TIER; assert r.validate_packaged_routing()==[]; import json; e=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'))['asserted-capability']; assert e['default_posture']=='advisory' and e['exec']=='AGENT' and e['facet']=='codebase-grounding'; print('OK')"`
  prints `OK`.
- [ ] The rubric prompt loads and the guide has its section. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry as r; assert '## asserted-capability' in open('docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md').read(); print(r.explain_criterion('asserted-capability')[:40])"`
  prints a non-empty section head; and `rebar explain asserted-capability` exits 0.
- [ ] Deterministic unit tests for the non-LLM logic (registration invariants, routing/finding
  shape, prompt-contract sub-answer keys) pass. Proof:
  `pytest tests/unit/test_asserted_capability_criterion.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] Bounded sanity check committed: a `criteria eval` fixture set with the 3 E1-verified misses
  (dc58/db7b/5886, reconstructed to their original false-asserting plan text, grounded against
  current modules) as must-fire and 3 clean plans as must-not-fire. The committed result
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/asserted_capability_sanity.json` shows the probe FIRES
  on >=2 of 3 misses (report §6 R1 threshold; observed 3/3, stability 1.0) and that any clean-plan
  fire is ADVISORY (never blocks) and is recorded as the promotion-gate FP signal. Proof: the JSON
  records `recall_over_misses>=0.66` (observed 1.0), preserves the raw per-case
  `rebar criteria eval asserted-capability --output json` output, and records
  `false_accept_over_clean` (observed 0.33 = one advisory false-fire on the no-claim control N1,
  a non-blocking dogfood datapoint given advisory posture — the exact signal the advisory→blocking
  promotion gate exists to watch). (6 live single-criterion runs total; NO E2/E3 corpus, NO batch
  eval.)
- [ ] The criterion auto-flows into the standing recorder. Proof:
  `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/criterion_effectiveness.py --report` (or a
  targeted unit assertion on `compute_effectiveness`) yields output in which
  `asserted-capability` appears once it has a firing — verified by a unit test feeding one
  synthetic firing row through `firings_from_review`/`compute_effectiveness` and asserting the
  id is auto-included (zero per-criterion wiring).
- [ ] The advisory→blocking promotion gate is documented and cited: docs/plan-review-gate.md's
  §"Standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder + advisory→blocking promotion gate" (added by
  d8a5) is the authority; this criterion's rubric/guide state it ships advisory and promotion is
  a future dogfood-gated `criteria_routing.json` change. Proof: `grep -n "advisory" ` on the
  rubric shows the advisory posture note.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Landed through Gerrit: change carries `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`
  and is submitted to main; `make lint && make typecheck && make test` are green on the change.
  Evidence recorded on this ticket (change number, merge commit, vote outcomes) — verified by
  attestation, not an in-session repo check.
baseline.summary: R1: asserted-capability grounding probe (G6/E4 rubric family, gated on E2+E3)

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <ticket>` on a finding-rich, code-grounded ticket (its Pass-1
findings touch a code-grounding criterion -> Pass-2 takes the AGENTIC verify branch
`plan-review-verifier-agentic`).
2. The agentic verifier re-grounds findings via tool calls and exceeds the step budget
(default `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50`; runner: ~25 model requests / 50 tool calls).
3. The verify workflow step raises: `step 'review@then/verify_branch@then/verify' failed:
agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=50; ...)`.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a verify step that can't complete should DEGRADE gracefully — the kernel
contract (`review_kernel.verify.verify_findings`) says un-verifiable findings route to
`pass3_decide(None)` -> per-finding INDETERMINATE, SURFACED, non-blocking; the review
still returns the Pass-1 findings. The gate's stated philosophy is fail-OPEN ("anything
it cannot soundly check is skipped, never a false accusation").
- **Actual:** the step-budget error escapes to `gate_dispatch._run_plan_review`'s broad
fall-through (gate_dispatch.py ~131-134) -> `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` sets
`coverage.llm_unavailable=True` -> `finalize_verdict` returns a hollow **INDETERMINATE**
that DISCARDS all Pass-1 findings and is **unsigned**. Fail-CLOSED: an unsigned verdict
fails the plan-review claim gate, so a perfectly good plan **cannot be claimed**.
## Evidence
- Step 7 of threshold calibration: 3/20 reviews returned INDETERMINATE
`llm_ran=False`, `llm_unavailable=True`, identical `llm_error` = the verify step-budget
message. Not a size issue (these are ordinary stories; 92fa's Pass-1 even produced a
finding). The same run reviewed 17 other tickets fine with the same key/env.
- Misclassification: "verify step exceeded its agentic step budget" is bucketed with
"LLM unavailable / no API key / no [agents] extra," which is wrong — the LLM was up and
the finder ran.
- Recovery gap: `_recover_plan_review_coach_failure` already recovers a Pass-4 COACH
failure (reconstructs the verdict from the decide partition). The analogous VERIFY
failure has no recovery -> falls through to the outage path.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A Pass-2 verify-step failure (step-budget / transient / StructuredOutputError) no
longer sets `llm_unavailable` and no longer discards Pass-1 findings.
- [ ] Such a review surfaces its Pass-1 findings (un-verifiable ones -> per-finding
INDETERMINATE, non-blocking) and does NOT fail the claim gate (fail-open), matching
the kernel `verify_findings` contract + the gate's documented fail-open posture.
- [ ] Defense-in-depth: the agentic verifier's step budget is raised/scaled (e.g. with
finding count) so it trips far less often; documented.
- [ ] A test reproduces the step-budget failure on the agentic verify branch and asserts
the verdict is NOT a hollow INDETERMINATE (findings preserved, claim not blocked).
- [ ] (Investigate) whether the agentic verify branch over-triggers for tickets with no
code-grounding findings (8e6f/9df3 had none in history yet ran agentic verify).

baseline.summary: Plan-review verify-step budget exhaustion misclassified as llm_unavailable -> hollow INDETERMINATE blocks the claim

## Why

A fake is only as good as its fidelity to the real client. If `FakeAcliClient` (story A) drifts from the real `AcliClient`, we reintroduce bug 0ee6's failure mode — tests pass against fictional shapes. Google's "Software Engineering at Google" prescribes the **verified fake**: the fake carries contract tests written against the API's public interface, and those same tests run against BOTH the real implementation and the fake.

## What

- **Shape-contract tests** for the `AcliClient` enrichment surface (`get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `get_parent_map`, `search_issues`) asserting the RETURN SHAPE (keys present, JSON primitive types) — not exact values.
- A parametrized harness that runs the identical contract tests against (a) the `FakeAcliClient` (always, hermetic) and (b) the real `AcliClient` against live Jira (behind the existing live/external pytest marker, opt-in).
- The fake FAILS the contract if its return shape diverges from the real client's, so a future real-API change surfaces as a fake-drift failure.
- Optional: validate the real client's responses against Jira Cloud's published OpenAPI where the spec covers the field (investigate spec completeness first — see epic open question).

## Scope

- In: the dual-run (real + fake) shape-contract harness for the enrichment methods.
- Out: capturing the fixtures (story A); the snapshot round-trip (story B).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shape-contract tests for the enrichment methods run against the fake (always) and the real client (live-gated marker).
- [ ] The fake fails the contract test if its return shape diverges from the real client's return shape.
- [ ] Assertions check structure/type (keys + JSON primitive types), not exact values (anti-change-detector).
- [ ] Running against live is opt-in (does not flake or slow the default suite).
baseline.summary: Verified fake: contract tests run against BOTH real and fake AcliClient

## Why
Workflows must be git-tracked text agents and humans can edit with clean diffs; the format
and its validation are the foundation everything else builds on.

## What
- Define a coordinate-free GitHub-Actions-style `steps:` YAML DSL with a versioned JSON Schema.
- Add a reference-integrity linter (dangling input/output refs), YAML 1.2 safe-load, a closed
  expression allow-list, a secret scan, and a schema_version read-time up-conversion shim.
- Ship `rebar workflow new` / `validate` / `--dry-run` (FakeRunner, no tokens).

## Scope
- In: schema, linter, safety, scaffolding, validate, schema versioning/migration.
- Out: execution (WS-C); rendering (WS-I).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] JSON Schema + reference-integrity linter with located, actionable error messages.
- [ ] YAML 1.2 safe-loader; schema_version typed string; anchors/merge-keys rejected; size cap.
- [ ] Expression allow-list; linter forbids raw ${{}} in prompt/command fields; post-substitution re-validation.
- [ ] Secret scan gate on .rebar/workflows/*.yaml.

content.text: ## Why
Story 1 invalidates a plan-review attestation when the code it was grounded against drifts, and
falls back to a FULL re-review (~all criteria, billable, minutes) to re-earn it. But most drift is
**immaterial to the plan** — the changed code doesn't break any assumption the plan relies on. Paying
for a full re-review in that common case is wasteful.
The original idea (re-run only the "code-grounded" criteria and reuse the rest) is **unsound** as the
codebase stands: tools are gated by `execution_mode`, not per-criterion, so ALL 12 agentic criteria
(incl. `G3/G4` and the `T*` overlays) can read code — there is no enforced code-blind subset to
safely reuse. (The `registry.py` comment claiming "only these 4 grep — the orchestrator enforces it"
is inaccurate; see Notes.)
Instead, use a **progressive (tripwire) re-review**: on drift, run ONE focused probe — "is the plan
still accurate with respect to the (now-changed) codebase?" — and only escalate to a full re-review
if it finds something. Soundness comes from the probe (a dedicated check confirms immateriality), not
from reusing a subset of stale findings, so the partition problem disappears.
## What
When a claim is blocked by **code drift** (Story 1's per-path hash mismatch) AND a prior PASSing
plan-review attestation exists whose only staleness is code drift (ticket material unchanged):
1. **Probe** — run the codebase-accuracy check against the CURRENT working tree: the existing
`E4` (assumption/premise verification — forced codebase probe) and `G1G2` (edit-set/consumer
accuracy), the two criteria whose whole job is "does the plan match the actual code." Hint them
with the drifted dependency paths so the probe focuses on what changed.
2. **Clean probe → refresh, don't re-review.** If the probe yields no blocking/material findings, the
drift did not invalidate the plan: REUSE the prior verdict wholesale and re-sign the attestation
with the CURRENT dependency-file hashes (a "refreshed" attestation), recording provenance
(`refreshed-from` the prior signature + the probe outcome). One/two agentic calls instead of the
full criteria set.
3. **Probe finds something → full re-review.** Escalate to the existing full review path (Story 1's
fallback); the plan genuinely needs re-examination.
The reuse is **whole-verdict, gated by the probe** — never a per-criterion or per-finding subset — so
there is no per-finding "code-hash vintage" and no chained-finding attestation to design; the
refreshed attestation is just a fresh signature over the prior verdict + the new dependency map.
### Fail-safe to FULL re-review
- The probe errors / is INDETERMINATE / the LLM is unavailable.
- Registry or criteria-contract **version skew** between the prior signing and now (the probe's
meaning may have changed).
- No reusable prior verdict (e.g. the prior attestation predates this mechanism, or material also
changed — that's a material-edit invalidation, handled by Story 1 / `dead-stalk-chasm`).
### Explicitly descoped (superseded by the progressive design)
- Per-criterion finding reuse based on a "code-blind" partition (unsound — no enforced partition).
- Per-finding code-hash vintage; chained per-finding attestation. Replaced by whole-verdict reuse +
a refreshed signature.
- Observed read-set capture; `>N files` fallback (already rejected in the brainstorm).
## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — the progressive path: detect a drift-only re-review
with a reusable prior verdict, run the `E4`(+`G1G2`) probe, branch reuse-vs-full.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — "refresh" an attestation: re-sign a prior verdict with the
current dependency-hash map + `refreshed-from` provenance; expose the prior verdict/manifest read.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` / `registry.py` — run just the probe criteria as a focused
pass (reuse existing `E4`/`G1G2`); no new criterion text required for v1.
- Tests under the plan-review suite.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On a drift-only re-review with a reusable prior PASS, the probe (`E4`[+`G1G2`]) runs against the
current code; a CLEAN probe refreshes the attestation (prior verdict re-signed with the current
dependency hashes + `refreshed-from` provenance) WITHOUT running the full criteria set.
- [ ] A probe that surfaces a blocking/material finding escalates to a FULL re-review (no silent
reuse); the refreshed attestation is never issued in that case.
- [ ] Fail-safe to FULL re-review on: probe error/indeterminate/LLM-unavailable, registry/criteria
version skew, or no reusable prior verdict.
- [ ] The refreshed attestation is a valid plan-review attestation (claim succeeds after a clean
refresh) and is externally CI-verifiable; its provenance records it was a drift-refresh.
- [ ] Soundness: the reuse is whole-verdict gated by the probe — NO per-criterion/per-finding subset
reuse (documented), so the unenforced code-blind partition is not relied upon.
- [ ] Measurement: report the cost (tokens/latency) of the probe-only refresh vs a full re-review on
a representative immaterial drift, before enabling the progressive path by default.
- [ ] Tested: immaterial drift (touch a dependency file in a way that doesn't break the plan) →
probe clean → refresh → claim succeeds; material drift (change a cited premise) → probe finds →
full re-review; version skew / no-prior-verdict → full re-review.
## Notes
The `registry.py` `CODEBASE_GROUNDED` comment ("only these AGENT-tier criteria grep ... the
orchestrator enforces it — no other criterion greps") is inaccurate — agentic tooling is granted by
`execution_mode`, not per criterion, so every AGENT-tier criterion can read code. This design does
NOT depend on that invariant; the comment should be corrected (small doc fix, here or a follow-up).

baseline.summary: Narrowed delta-re-review on code drift: re-run only the enforced code-grounded criteria with a chained attestation

baseline.description:
# Stage-1 BM25F candidate generation over digests + graph-exclusion filter

## Why
Stage 1 narrows a few hundred tickets to ~20 candidates cheaply and deterministically, no LLM/embeddings, and must NOT surface a ticket's own already-related work (parents/children/siblings/linked) — the top source of "related-but-distinct" false flags. DERISKED (epic experiment comment): digest-BM25F recall@20 = 1.0 on 8 paraphrase pairs, STABLE 60→200 corpus; single-query latency 0.69 ms at 800 digests (~14× under budget) — so brute-force is correct and no ANN/vector-DB is needed.

## What
- Brute-force BM25F "More Like This" over `ticket_digest` records (S2). Bespoke ~40 LOC: `rank-bm25` provides only UNWEIGHTED BM25, but we need per-field weighting; at n<1000 bespoke is trivial and avoids a dependency (the recall+latency spikes validate this choice). Field weights are a module-level constant `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` in `retrieve.py` (`problem_keywords` 3.0, `component_or_area` 3.0, `key_entities` 1.0, `propositions` 1.0) — a stable algorithmic choice, deliberately NOT a config knob (a dict-typed config value has no `from_env` resolution helper, and BM25F weights do not need per-invocation tuning; if they ever do, that is a separate `_llm_json` helper story). Tokenize lowercased on non-alphanumeric, drop stopwords + corpus-boilerplate via `overlap_max_doc_freq`. Returns a typed `OverlapCandidate` `[{ticket_id, score, matched_terms}]` (the interface S7 consumes — stated so S7 isn't blind to it). Query side = the query ticket's freshly-extracted digest, passed by the caller.
- **Graph exclusion** BEFORE scoring: new helper `src/rebar/llm/overlap/graph.py::related_ticket_ids(ticket_id, tracker) -> set[str]` that loads states ONCE via `_load_all_states(tracker)` (the same helper `descendants.py` uses) and derives all four relation sets from that one dict: descendants (BFS on `parent_id`, or by calling `descendants.list_descendants(ticket_id, tracker)` and flattening its type-bucketed id lists — NOT by sharing its internal snapshot, which it does not expose), ancestors (walk `parent_id` up), siblings (same `parent_id`; a root ticket with no parent has NO siblings — handled explicitly), and linked tickets in BOTH directions (scan all tickets' `deps` for any edge whose source OR target is `ticket_id` — an incoming `blocks`/`depends_on` from another ticket is not in this ticket's own `deps`, so outgoing-only would miss it). It does NOT refactor `next_batch.py`. At n<1000 one state load is sub-ms (latency spike).
- Cold/stale: corpus tickets whose digest is absent or stale (S2 freshness: content-hash/model/version mismatch — not an age threshold) are SKIPPED; the skip-count is logged so a cold run is distinguishable from a healthy one.
- Overlap floor: a `min_should_match` fraction (default 0.15 of query terms) below which a candidate is not returned; `retrieve()` returns `[]` when nothing clears the floor.
- Errors: any graph-read/scoring exception is caught, logged, returns `[]` (never blocks review_plan).

## Config (LLMConfig, not VerifyConfig) — with explicit `from_env` wiring
Three SCALAR tunables on `LLMConfig` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `[tool.rebar.llm]`,
`REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`); field weights are a constant (see What), NOT config:
- `overlap_k: int = 20`
- `overlap_max_doc_freq: float = 0.5` (ignore terms appearing in >50% of digests)
- `overlap_min_should_match: float = 0.15`

**`LLMConfig.from_env()` MUST be edited** (it explicitly constructs `LLMConfig(...)` with
every field read via a helper — a new dataclass field not read there stays at its default and
is silently un-tunable). Add module constants `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_K = 20`,
`DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ = 0.5`, `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH = 0.15`; add the three
dataclass fields; and in `from_env`'s `return cls(...)` add:
- `overlap_k=_llm_int(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_K", "overlap_k", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_K)`
- `overlap_max_doc_freq=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ", "overlap_max_doc_freq", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ)`
- `overlap_min_should_match=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH", "overlap_min_should_match", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH)`

`_llm_int` exists (`config.py:388`); `_llm_float` does NOT — add it in `config.py` mirroring
`_llm_int` (env > `rebar -c llm.*` > `[tool.rebar.llm]` file > default, parsing via `float()`
with a clean fallback on ValueError). This is the only non-scalar-free helper needed (no dict
keys remain). `_config_schema.py` reserves the `llm.*` layer, so these are NOT on `VerifyConfig`.

## Dependencies
S1 (`ticket_digest` schema/fields), S2 (digest store + freshness). Digest fields are DEFINED in S1.

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/retrieve.py` (BM25F + `OverlapCandidate` + `_FIELD_WEIGHTS` constant) and `src/rebar/llm/overlap/graph.py` (`related_ticket_ids`).
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: add `_llm_float` helper, the three `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_*` constants, the three `LLMConfig` fields, and the three `from_env()` reads (enumerated above).

## Summary
Cut the 0.10.1 patch release of rebar per docs/releasing.md. This is a fix/patch bump from 0.10.0, covering the ~36 commits landed on main since v0.10.0 (reconciler Backend-port scalar surfaces, plan-review/close-gate hardening, code-health analyzers scc/lizard/jscpd, review-bot token accounting, and assorted fixes).

## Plan
1. Fresh worktree from origin/main (git worktree add / make worktree).
2. Bump versions in lockstep: pyproject.toml [project].version; server.json top-level version AND every packages[].version -> 0.10.1. server.json has exactly ONE packages[] entry, so a correct bump yields two 0.10.1 occurrences in that file. The release authorize job runs release_guards.py version-lockstep and fails the build on any mismatch.
3. CHANGELOG.md: prepend the [0.10.1] section via 'make changelog VERSION=v0.10.1', hand-curate the generated top section, add the [0.10.1] compare-link footer.
4. Local gates, run with the worktree venv on PATH: 'make lint && make typecheck && make test', then build+validate the artifact metadata exactly as the runbook (docs/releasing.md L259) and release.yml specify: 'python -m build && python -m twine check dist/*'. twine is not a dev extra in pyproject; invoke it as the CI lock does via 'pipx run twine check dist/*' (or 'uvx twine check dist/*') if 'python -m twine' is absent in the worktree venv, so the glob-targeted metadata check actually runs against the built wheel+sdist.
5. Commit with 'rebar-ticket: zincoid-panoramic-eeve' + DCO sign-off trailers; push 'git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main'; earn LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1; then Submit (POST /a/changes/<n>/submit as RebarBotNava).
6. Fast-forward the worktree to merged main; dispatch the release from main: 'gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f version=0.10.1' and approve the pypi environment deployment when prompted (required-reviewers gate). PyPI is immutable — if the published artifact is defective, yank it and ship 0.10.2.
7. Verify the channels with the proving commands below.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Version-lockstep holds: 'grep -c 0.10.1 pyproject.toml' >=1 and 'grep -c 0.10.1 server.json' == 2 (top-level + the single packages[] entry) on the release commit; equivalently release_guards.py version-lockstep passes in the authorize job.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md carries a curated release section: 'grep -E "^## \[0\.10\.1\]" CHANGELOG.md' matches.
- [ ] Release commit landed on main through Gerrit with both gate votes green: the Gerrit change shows LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 and status MERGED, and 'git log origin/main --oneline | grep -i "release 0.10.1"' finds it.
- [ ] [operator-attested] 0.10.1 published to PyPI: 'curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"info\"][\"version\"])"' prints 0.10.1.
- [ ] [operator-attested] v0.10.1 tag + GitHub Release created at the released main SHA: 'gh release view v0.10.1 --json tagName,targetCommitish,isLatest' shows the tag, marked Latest.

## Out of scope / automated follow-ups (no executor action required)
- Homebrew tap self-bump (navapbc/homebrew-rebar autobump.yml, scheduled every 6h) and the MCP-registry publish job (mcp_registry in release.yml, needs: publish) run automatically after publish; verifying them is not a release-blocking acceptance criterion for this ticket.

## Attestation evidence
- The above acceptance criteria are proven in-session by the quoted shell/gh/curl commands whose outputs are recorded as comments on this ticket, plus the Gerrit change number and its +1/+1 vote outcome and MERGED status.
baseline.summary: Release 0.10.1 (patch/fix version)
