# Bring provider configs under version control + repo-wide CLAUDE.md reference sweep

## Why

Once `AGENTS.md` is canonical, two things must happen so the migration ships to other providers
and clones: (1) the committed-tree references to `CLAUDE.md` must move to the new structure, and
(2) the provider-config scaffolding must be **committed** — a spike found that `.codex/config.toml`
and `.agents/rules/rebar.md` are **untracked, locally `.git/info/exclude`d files on one machine**
(`git ls-files` returns nothing for them), so today no other clone or provider sees them.

## What

A `git grep 'CLAUDE\.md'` over tracked files gives the complete surface (24 refs). Ownership is
split, and this story owns a defined subset:

- **This story updates** (CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md or the new docs home): `CONTRIBUTING.md:570`,
  `README.md:354`, `rebar.toml:3`, `docs/architecture.md:65,233`, `docs/api-stability.md:25`,
  `docs/exit-codes.md:43`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:484`, `docs/llm-framework.md:462`,
  `docs/releasing.md:250`, `docs/workflow-editor.md:160`, `docs/workflow-engine.md:29`,
  `docs/adr/0043-…:121`, `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md:462,467`,
  `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh:130`, and the plan-review criteria
  text in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:407`,
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5e.md:10`, plus the prose comment in
  `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:307`. (The rename breaks zero code — every `src/` hit is a
  prose comment; the unrelated `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var does not match `CLAUDE.md`.)
- **Owned by other stories (out of scope here):** `docs/event-schema.md:46` (S1 replaces that
  pointer) and `examples/claude-skills/{rebar-implement/SKILL.md,rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md}`
  (S5 repoints them).
- **Deliberately NOT changed:** `CHANGELOG.md` (3 hits) — a changelog is a historical record of
  past changes made when the file *was* `CLAUDE.md`; rewriting it would falsify history.
- **Commit the Codex config:** bring `.codex/config.toml` under version control (`git add -f`,
  it is currently locally excluded) pointing at `AGENTS.md`, comment updated to the completed state.
- **Commit the generic rules file:** bring `.agents/rules/rebar.md` under version control as a
  concise distillation that **references `AGENTS.md`** as the source of truth (Antigravity
  `.agents/rules/*` does not support `@`-imports, so a short reference-and-summary, not a symlink).
- **Per-tool pointers:** record the decision on optional `.github/copilot-instructions.md` /
  `.cursor/rules` / Gemini config. Default: **defer to a follow-up** (none added here).

## Scope

In: the ~17 owned files listed above, `.codex/config.toml`, `.agents/rules/rebar.md`. Out: files
owned by S1/S5, `CHANGELOG.md`, the root-file/template changes. **Depends on S1, S2, S3** (S1 and
S5 must land their reference updates for the global tree to be clean; S2 must create `AGENTS.md`).
Rollback: `git revert` — docs/config/text only, no data migration.

## Assumption (flag for override)

The epic's goal (guidance *available to* Codex/Cursor/Antigravity) is only met if the provider
configs are committed, so this story brings `.codex/` and `.agents/` into version control. If the
team wants provider configs to stay per-developer/local, drop those two bullets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] This story's 17 owned files carry no `CLAUDE.md` reference (verifiable on this story alone;
  the thin `CLAUDE.md` pointer, historical `CHANGELOG.md`, and the S1-/S5-owned files are excluded
  because they are out of this story's scope).
  - Proving: `[ "$(git grep -c 'CLAUDE\.md' -- ':!CLAUDE.md' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!docs/event-schema.md' ':!examples' ':!docs/experiments' | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s+0}')" = 0 ]`
- [ ] The plan-review criteria text (both the `src/rebar/llm` files and the
  `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` mirror) references `AGENTS.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`.
  - Proving: `[ "$(git grep -c 'CLAUDE\.md' -- src/rebar/llm docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s+0}')" = 0 ]`
- [ ] `.codex/config.toml` is git-tracked and points at `AGENTS.md`.
  - Proving: `[ -n "$(git ls-files .codex/config.toml)" ] && git grep -q 'AGENTS.md' -- .codex/config.toml`
- [ ] `.agents/rules/rebar.md` is git-tracked and references `AGENTS.md` as the source of truth.
  - Proving: `[ -n "$(git ls-files .agents/rules/rebar.md)" ] && git grep -q 'AGENTS.md' -- .agents/rules/rebar.md`
- [ ] [operator-attested] The per-tool-pointer decision (default: defer) is recorded as a comment
  on this ticket citing the choice.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` pass and the module-size CI gate is green.
  - Proving: `make lint && make test`
baseline.summary: Retarget provider shims to AGENTS.md + repo-wide reference sweep + optional per-tool pointers

## Context

The commit contains `rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d`. However, the best-effort Gerrit voter persistence seam did not produce the required durable artifact: after a ticket write reconciled the shared tracker, `rebar search` found neither the revision nor Change-Id and `rebar audit show 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d --output json | jq .code_reviews` remained empty.

## Plan

- Identify the precise changeable cause rather than treating best-effort swallowing as sufficient.
- Add a RED regression at the smallest real voter/tracker boundary, implement the fix, and retain fail-safe voting behavior plus actionable emission diagnostics.
- Land through Gerrit, allow deployment, and rerun the live change-986 dogfood revision to prove a `code_review_result_v2` artifact is persisted and linked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A live Gerrit review with a resolvable `rebar-ticket:` trailer persists one idempotent revision-scoped `code_review` artifact and links it `relates_to` the work ticket.

content.text: ## Why
Sharper detection content in criteria that already exist -- prompt work; findings get sharper, generic passes untouched.
## What (each edits reviewers/plan_review_*.md; all enums enumerated here so the ticket is self-contained)

- E6 verify-command defect taxonomy -- the NINE patterns (E6 currently has 6 checks a-f; add to reach nine): (1) substring false-positive -> require word-boundary/quoted-key anchors; (2) shell-expansion leakage ($VAR/$? inside grep patterns); (3) wrong helper-script argv (cross-check --help); (4) fixture invalidity; (5) missing cardinality assertion when the criterion names a count (jq '.x|length' -eq N); (6) prose-vs-structured assertion target (assert on the artifact with jq -e, not prose); (7) missing prerequisite-state ordering; (8) conflicting ACs (tests-pass vs test-fails-RED) needing a sequencing AC; (9) references sibling-ticket files with no dependency edge. Add corrected-command anchors (grep -E '"cycle_count"[[:space:]]*:' not grep cycle).

- T3 THREE empiricism axes: (a) per-command --help/flag-level empiricism; (b) endpoint granularity (a new endpoint on a used vendor is a new integration); (c) environment preconditions (e.g. HTTP-only env contradicts an OAuth-callback flow). FOUR evidence classes DEFINED: Verified (observed), Partially-verified (integration exists, surface unconfirmed), Unverified (could not probe), Contradicted (environment falsifies it). RECORDED in Pass-1 evidence[] ONLY for Pass-2 to read. CORRECTION (verified): sidecar _slim (sidecar.py:233) DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES evidence[] -- so the four-class is NOT persisted to the slim sidecar; persisting it for calibration is OUT OF SCOPE here (a WS9-style follow-on). No P1Finding schema change (evidence is already list[str]; this is prompt-only).

- G3: three-part coverage standard (same observable outcome / scope matching-or-exceeding / measurable-in-same-terms) + DEFINE three contradiction patterns: bypass-annotation (child annotates/excludes items from the parent metric instead of resolving), scope-narrowing (child covers a narrower condition set), partial-without-remainder (child covers part, does not name the uncovered remainder).

- T5c ambiguity-not-absence access framing; T11 post-rollback SCHEMA-STATE assertion + DATA LOSS RISK; E2 defaultable-gaps coaching; G4 consumer-enumeration precursor (recall->worklist over the existing consumer-impact mode).
Rejected in evaluation: T9 RETIRE-row rule (nit) -- intentionally not a deliverable (kept out of the AC list).
## Provenance

Symbols introduced by a SIBLING story (e.g. committed_work_relies_on_unbacked_claim from WS1) are target-state, not pre-existing; the dependency is recorded.
## Acceptance Criteria

## Why
The GitHub CodeQL "Security and quality" scan flags `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` in
`docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/runtime_pydanticai_poc.py` (code-scanning alerts 3 and 4).
That file is a hand-run proof-of-concept: it is not packaged (the wheel/sdist ship only `src/rebar` —
`pyproject.toml:213`), is on no `import rebar` path, and never runs in production. The findings are
false positives (they log public provider-name strings such as "anthropic"/"openai", not secrets). The
individual alerts have been dismissed, but any code under `docs/` keeps generating recurring scan noise
on every push. The advanced-setup CodeQL workflow (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) currently passes no
config, so nothing is excluded.

## What
Add a CodeQL config file that excludes `docs/**` from analysis and wire it into the workflow, so the
exclusion is durable (survives future `docs/experiments` additions) rather than relying on per-alert
dismissals.
- New file `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` with `paths-ignore: ["docs/**"]`.
- Edit `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: pass `config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` to the

content.text: # S1 — Terraform base: EC2 box, networking, DNS subdomain, IAM, SSM secrets, state/backups
## Why
The PoC needs one cost-conscious, reproducible AWS host for Gerrit + the rebar MCP.
Codifying it as IaC is runtime-free and delivers the freeze-and-restore RTO (rebuild
from Terraform) without adding cost — so it serves P3 (reusability) without touching
P2 (cost). Everything else in this epic lands on this substrate.
## What
- One-time bootstrap (`infra/bootstrap/`): an S3 state bucket (versioning + SSE) created
by a small standalone config applied ONCE manually — this breaks the state-backend
chicken-and-egg (TF can't store state in a bucket it hasn't created yet). Its bucket
name feeds the main config's backend block.
- `infra/terraform/` using roll-your-own raw resources (the ec2-instance module adds
indirection at N=1):
- `versions.tf`: `required_version = ">= 1.10"` (S3 native `use_lockfile` needs TF
>=1.10; older TF SILENTLY ignores it and runs with NO locking) + `required_providers`
- `t4g.large` (Graviton, ~8 GB) on AL2023 arm64 — AMI resolved via the SSM public param
`/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-arm64` (NOT a hardcoded
id); gp3 root + a separate gp3 data volume mounted at `/var/gerrit` with
`lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`; IMDSv2 required.
- Default VPC; security group inbound 443 (HTTPS) + 29418 (Gerrit SSH); admin access via
SSM Session Manager (no inbound 22). One Elastic IP, also `prevent_destroy = true`.
- Route 53 A record `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` -> EIP in the existing public zone
`Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ` (solutions.navateam.com).
- IAM instance role: attach `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` (REQUIRED for Session Manager
— the sole admin path) + SSM Parameter Store read (+ KMS decrypt) + CloudWatch basic.
- SSM Parameter Store SecureString params (placeholders) for the Gerrit secrets, the
GitHub replication deploy key, the rebar MCP HMAC signing key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
- `user_data.sh` (cloud-init): at first boot, fetch the SSM SecureString params via the
instance role and write them to a `chmod 600` `.env` (NO plaintext secrets in user_data
itself); IMDSv2 enforced.
- Terraform S3 backend with `use_lockfile=true` (no DynamoDB); DLM daily EBS snapshots of
the data volume with a bounded `retain_rule { count = 7 }`.
- Packaging: ensure `infra/` is excluded from ALL distribution channels.
## Scope
In: the bootstrap + TF base + DNS subdomain + IAM + SSM scaffolding + boot script +
state/backup config + the packaging exclusion. Out: Gerrit/MCP containers (S2), Gerrit
config (S3), replication (S5), GitHub lockdown (S6).
## Files
- `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` (one-time state bucket: versioning + SSE)
- `infra/terraform/{versions,main,network,iam,ssm,dns,backup}.tf`
- `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` (SSM-pull -> chmod 600 .env boot script)
- `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]` include is `["src/rebar","tests","README.md"]`
so `infra/` is excluded by default — add an explicit exclude + a build-artifact check)

- `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md` (ADR capturing the three novel decisions: the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg pattern, the no-DynamoDB S3-native locking choice gated on Terraform >=1.10, and the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM parameter naming contract — each with rationale)
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform validate` and `plan` succeed (TF >=1.10 enforced via
`required_version`); `apply` stands up a reachable `t4g.large` with EIP, gp3 root + data
volume mounted at `/var/gerrit`, IMDSv2 enforced.
- [ ] The state-bucket bootstrap (`infra/bootstrap/`) is documented as a one-time manual apply;
the main config's S3 backend uses `use_lockfile=true` (no DynamoDB), gated by `required_version >= 1.10`.
- [ ] The stateful data volume AND the EIP carry `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` (no silent
destroy/recreate of Gerrit data on apply/rename/AMI change).
- [ ] `rebar.solutions.navateam.com` resolves (Route 53 A -> EIP in zone Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ); SG
allows 443 + 29418; admin access via SSM Session Manager with the role granting
`AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` and no inbound 22.
- [ ] `user_data.sh` pulls the SSM SecureString params at boot to a `chmod 600` file; no plaintext
secrets appear in user_data.
- [ ] DLM creates daily snapshots of the data volume with bounded retention (e.g. `retain_rule count=7`).

- [ ] `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md` exists and records the three novel architectural decisions with rationale: (1) the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg pattern, (2) the no-DynamoDB S3-native `use_lockfile` locking choice gated on Terraform >=1.10, and (3) the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM parameter naming contract.
- [ ] A built sdist AND wheel contain NO `infra/` files (deterministic check: `python -m build` then
grep the artifacts for `infra/`). Homebrew + the MCP registry INHERIT this exclusion because both
package the same built artifact (the formula builds from the sdist/release; the registry ships the
wheel) — so the sdist/wheel check is the single source of truth, documented as such.
## Round-7 remediation

- **DLM service role (G6):** AWS Data Lifecycle Manager assumes its OWN IAM role (trust principal `dlm.amazonaws.com`, perms `ec2:CreateSnapshot`/`CreateTags`/`DescribeVolumes`/`DeleteSnapshot`). S1 creates this DLM service role and wires its ARN into the `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` `execution_role_arn` — without it DLM silently creates no snapshots.
- [ ] The DLM lifecycle policy references a created DLM service role (trust `dlm.amazonaws.com`) and is ENABLED (verified it would snapshot the data volume, not silently no-op).
## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)

- SSM SecureString scaffolding extended so no downstream lookup fails: ADD `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint` (consumed by S7 `monitoring.tf`) and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` (consumed by S4a) to the enumerated placeholder params.

- Ownership contracts: S1 CREATES the single EC2 instance role (S2/S4a only add separately-named scoped inline policies, never re-declare it). S1 OWNS the DLM service role + `aws_dlm_lifecycle_policy` (retain count=7); S7 only asserts/monitors it (no second DLM resource).
Added ACs:
- [ ] SSM placeholder set includes `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint` and `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token` (in addition to Gerrit secrets, deploy key, HMAC key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)

- [ ] The EC2 instance role and the DLM lifecycle policy + DLM service role are created HERE and only here; ADR-0012 records the single-owner contract (S2/S4a attach scoped policies; S7 only monitors DLM)
## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-29 — recalibrated gate BLOCK)
Two blocking findings fixed; advisories triaged and folded in.
**Blocking (resolved):**

- **B1 — bootstrap state-bucket destruction guard:** the `aws_s3_bucket` in `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` carries `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` (the state bucket is the third stateful resource alongside the data volume + EIP; without it a `terraform destroy` of the bootstrap stack deletes all TF state, defeating the rebuild-from-Terraform RTO). Destroying it requires an explicit state migration first; recorded in ADR-0012.

- **B2 — idempotent data-volume init:** `user_data.sh` MUST check-before-mkfs — `if ! blkid <device> >/dev/null 2>&1; then mkfs.xfs <device>; fi` — so an instance replacement (e.g. the SSM AMI pointer advancing) re-mounts the existing `/var/gerrit` volume WITHOUT reformatting. `prevent_destroy` guards the Terraform resource; the blkid guard guards the in-guest filesystem (mkfs is a runtime op TF cannot prevent).
**Advisories folded in:**

- **Enumerated SSM param names** (the `/rebar/prod/*` naming contract, recorded in ADR-0012): `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`, `/rebar/prod/github-replication-deploy-key`, `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key`, `/rebar/prod/anthropic-api-key`, `/rebar/prod/alert-endpoint`, `/rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token`.

- **Placeholder lifecycle + fail-fast:** params are created with a `CHANGEME` placeholder; the operator MUST populate real values before the S2 apply. `user_data.sh` exits non-zero (cloud-init marks the instance failed) if any fetched value still equals the placeholder sentinel — never silently writes broken config.
- **IAM least privilege:** the instance-role SSM read + `kms:Decrypt` is scoped to `arn:aws:ssm:<region>:<account>:parameter/rebar/prod/*` (no wildcard), referencing `data.aws_caller_identity`.
- **AMI drift:** `aws_instance` carries `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`; an AMI upgrade is a deliberate runbook step, not a side effect of a routine apply.
- **Explicit volume sizes:** gp3 root 30 GB, data 50 GB, surfaced as variables.
- **`infra/terraform/variables.tf`** surfaces `snapshot_retention_count` (default 7), `instance_type` (default `t4g.large`), and the volume sizes.
**Added / updated ACs:**
- [ ] `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` state bucket has `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.
- [ ] `user_data.sh` volume init is idempotent (blkid check before mkfs); a re-run on instance replacement does not reformat the data volume.
- [ ] Instance-role SSM/KMS policy is scoped to `parameter/rebar/prod/*` (no wildcard), verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] `aws_instance` has `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ami] }`; AMI upgrade is a documented runbook step.
- [ ] The SSM placeholder param set is enumerated by exact name and recorded in ADR-0012; `user_data.sh` fails fast on an unpopulated placeholder sentinel.
- [ ] gp3 volumes have explicit sizes (root 30 GB, data 50 GB) surfaced as Terraform variables in `variables.tf`.

- [ ] ADR-0012 records FOUR decisions: (1) the S3 state-bucket bootstrap chicken-and-egg, (2) no-DynamoDB S3-native `use_lockfile` gated on TF >=1.10, (3) the `/rebar/prod/*` SSM naming contract, (4) the single-owner contract for the EC2 instance role + DLM policy.
## Round-13 plan-review remediation (NVMe device naming on Nitro)

- **B2 refinement — NVMe-aware device resolution:** on t4g.large (Graviton/Nitro) AL2023 presents EBS volumes as NVMe devices (`/dev/nvme1n1`…), NOT the Xen `device_name` (`/dev/xvdf`) Terraform sets. `user_data.sh` therefore resolves the data volume's real device DYNAMICALLY by its EBS volume id rather than hardcoding a name: the volume id is passed into the script via `templatefile()`, and the script matches it against the NVMe controller serial (`for d in /dev/nvme*n1; do nvme id-ctrl -v "$d" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "$VOL_NODASH" && DATA_DEV=$d; done`, or equivalently the AL2023 `/dev/disk/by-id/nvme-Amazon_Elastic_Block_Store_vol...` symlink / `ebsnvme-id`). Only after resolving `DATA_DEV` does the blkid-before-mkfs guard run, so the guard targets the correct device on Nitro. Added AC.

- [ ] `user_data.sh` resolves the data volume's NVMe device path dynamically by EBS volume id (not a hardcoded `/dev/xvdf`); the blkid-before-mkfs guard then runs against the resolved device. Verified the resolved device matches the attached data volume on the live t4g.large.

baseline.description:
# DC renderer robustness & performance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field, which introduces three production hazards proven in the DC experiment: (1) a per-field subprocess tax — latency is a flat ~0.3s/field spawn cost independent of body size, and a serial reconcile pass over many fields blocked ~20 min of wall time on `fork+exec`; (2) a pathological-input hang — one corpus body drove pandoc's jira reader to spin 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc invokes pandoc with no timeout, so one field can stall the whole reconcile indefinitely; (3) pandoc is GPL and rides in the `pypandoc-binary` wheel, so its provenance and license must be pinned and recorded. These must be designed against before the DC codec ships live.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide what 271c already chose)
- **The renderer module and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` ships the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` and delivers pandoc via the
  **`pypandoc-binary` wheel** (the pandoc binary is BUNDLED IN THE WHEEL and pinned
  in `pyproject.toml`), specifically so the DC path is self-contained in CI and
  prod with no system pandoc install. This story hardens THAT module and pins THAT
  wheel; it does **not** introduce a separate system-level pandoc or an
  `acli`-style version+sha binary pin (acli is a symlink + `acli jira auth login`
  system prerequisite, not a pinned pip binary — there is no acli pin pattern to
  mirror).
- 271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity and delivers `wiki_render.py` as a
  **pure module not referenced by any codec op or live send path in that story**
  (271c's own words); all live wiring — the codec ops AND the live send sites — is
  deferred to the cutover story `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]` and is **out of scope
  here**. This story touches only the pure `wiki_render.py` module functions, never
  the codec or the live send.
- **The change-gated "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property is delivered by the
  cutover/echo story `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`**, which introduces the
  change-gated `rich_sha` render gate; that symbol does not yet exist on
  `origin/main` and is not this story's to add. THIS story owns only the cost,
  timeout, fallback, batching, and compliance of a render that IS performed.

## Approach
- **Bound the per-render subprocess cost by batching contiguous SAFE units:** 271c
  segments the body into units and classifies each safe or dangerous. This story
  groups each **maximal run of contiguous SAFE units** and feeds that run to pandoc
  as **one Markdown document → one wiki segment**, so a body of many safe blocks
  costs one spawn per safe-run instead of one per unit. Crucially there is **no
  per-unit re-splitting of a batch's output**: the safe-run's combined wiki is
  emitted as a single contiguous segment, and reassembly is at the segment (run)
  level, not the unit level. (pandoc 3.9 exposes no `--server`/daemon, confirmed, so
  a persistent server is out of scope; safe-run batching is the available lever.)
- **Dangerous units are spliced VERBATIM — pandoc is never invoked on them.** Per
  271c, a unit flagged dangerous corrupts pandoc's jira reader, so it is passed
  through as its original Markdown **without any pandoc call** and inserted at its
  original position between the rendered safe-run segments. Original order is
  restored by concatenating the ordered sequence of segments (rendered safe-run wiki
  chunks and verbatim dangerous units) — no delimiter/sentinel splitting is needed
  because each pandoc invocation renders exactly one contiguous safe run.
- **Hard timeout + process-group reaping + batch-level verbatim fallback:** a plain
  `subprocess.run(timeout=)` / pypandoc timeout only reaps the DIRECT child, so a
  pandoc jira-reader spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild) survives and
  keeps burning the core (repo bug d843, CPython bpo-30154). Therefore the renderer
  MUST NOT use pypandoc's high-level `convert_text`/`convert_file` API (which spawns
  pandoc internally and returns no handle); instead it locates the wheel-bundled
  pandoc executable via `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()` and builds its OWN
  `subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True)`, **enforces the
  wall-clock timeout caller-side via `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)`
  and, on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, passes that `Popen`** to the shared leaf
  **`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`** (`_proc.py:26`) —
  `killpg` SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain, the exact helper already reused by
  the ACLI transport and grounding harness — so the whole process group, not just
  the direct child, is killed on timeout. The reap helper only kills/drains AFTER a
  timeout is detected; it does not itself wait out the timeout, so the caller-side
  `communicate(timeout=…)`/`except TimeoutExpired` detection is required, exactly the
  pattern `acli_subprocess.py` uses. **The wall-clock timeout is a config key**
  (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default **10s**) chosen from the DC experiment:
  it is >30× the observed ~0.3s/field normal render (so it never trips healthy
  bodies) and ~80× below the 13.5-min pathological hang (so a spinning field is
  killed in seconds, not minutes); `grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller's existing
  constants. On a safe-run pandoc call's timeout or
  non-zero exit, degrade **that entire safe-run segment** to its original Markdown
  verbatim (plain Markdown is trivially echo-safe) and record a **segment-level
  fallback marker**; other safe-run segments and the verbatim dangerous units are
  unaffected. The fallback boundary is exactly the pandoc-invocation boundary (one
  contiguous safe run), so there is no partial-segment reassembly to reconcile.
- **Compliance:** pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel by version in `pyproject.toml`
  (271c's mechanism), record the wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL license in the project
  SBOM/notice, and verify the wheel pin in CI.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — the pure DC renderer module delivered by
  271c: locate the wheel-bundled pandoc via `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()` and drive
  it through the renderer's OWN `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)` (NOT
  pypandoc's high-level convert API), add the per-invocation timeout with
  process-group reaping via the shared `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`,
  contiguous-safe-run batching (one pandoc call per safe run → one wiki segment;
  dangerous units spliced verbatim with NO pandoc call), and segment-level verbatim
  fallback. No codec op and no live-send site is touched here.
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin;
  no separate system pandoc).
- config (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s) — the per-invocation
  wall-clock timeout, tunable without a code change. Because a `reconciler.*` key
  has a fixed multi-file config surface in this repo (mirrors the existing
  `reconciler.jira_cli_timeout`), ALL of the following are updated together for the
  key to be reachable and documented: `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add the
  field `dc_pandoc_timeout_s: float = 10.0` to `ReconcilerConfig` plus its validator
  entry `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0)` alongside `jira_cli_timeout`;
  `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — a canonical-env alias in `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES`
  only if a non-derived env name is wanted (otherwise the auto-derived
  `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S` applies and no entry is added);
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — deliberately REGENERATE the golden to add the
  `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s` entry (the golden guard
  `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` is removal-only — it will NOT flag a new
  live key's omission, so the surface is regenerated on purpose when the key is
  added); `docs/config.md` — document the key in the `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` block.
  A unit test mirrors the existing `test_config_file_wiring.py` four-consumer pattern
  for the new key.
- CI workflow config — verify the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pin (NOT an acli-style
  system-binary sha check).
- SBOM/licensing notice file — record the wheel-bundled pandoc GPL entry.
- `tests/` — timeout, batch-fallback, and batching tests over the vendored DC
  corpus fixture.

## Testing
- Timeout path: a synthetic input that exceeds the configured timeout is killed by
  process-group reaping (the CPU-spinning pandoc grandchild is gone, not just the
  direct child) and its safe-run segment falls back to verbatim Markdown while the
  render returns; asserted by `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` (spawns a
  child that forks a spinning grandchild; asserts the group PID is reaped).
- Failure path: a non-zero pandoc exit degrades that safe-run segment to plaintext
  without raising, and the segment fallback is recorded; `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- Batching + order: a body of N contiguous safe units renders in one pandoc
  invocation (spawn-count spy) and the output preserves original block order when
  interleaved with verbatim dangerous units; `test_dc_render_batches_safe_run`.
- Dangerous units never hit pandoc: a body containing a dangerous unit invokes
  pandoc only on the safe runs and passes the dangerous unit through verbatim (the
  spawn-count spy records zero pandoc calls for the dangerous unit);
  `test_dc_dangerous_unit_verbatim_no_pandoc`.
- Segment==fallback boundary: when one safe-run invocation times out, exactly that
  run's segment falls back to verbatim and other safe runs still render;
  `test_dc_segment_fallback_boundary`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every pandoc invocation runs under a wall-clock timeout enforced caller-side
  via `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` (config
  `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s — well above the ~0.3s normal render,
  well below the 13.5-min pathological hang) and, on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`,
  process-group reaping (`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, which kills/drains AFTER
  the caller detects the timeout, so a pipe-holding CPU-spinning grandchild is
  killed, not orphaned) and, on timeout or non-zero exit, degrades
  that safe-run segment to verbatim Markdown without raising; the render returns;
  verified by `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` (asserts the spawned group is
  reaped) and `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- [ ] A changed body of N contiguous safe units renders in one pandoc invocation
  (one wiki segment) with original block order preserved, dangerous units are
  spliced VERBATIM with no pandoc call, and a safe-run timeout degrades exactly that
  run's segment; verified by `test_dc_render_batches_safe_run`,
  `test_dc_dangerous_unit_verbatim_no_pandoc`, and `test_dc_segment_fallback_boundary`
  (segment boundary == fallback boundary).
- [ ] The pandoc binary is provided by the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by
  version in `pyproject.toml` (271c's mechanism, not a system pandoc), the wheel
  pin is verified in CI, and the wheel-bundled pandoc GPL license is recorded in
  the SBOM/notice; verified by the CI wheel-pin check and a notice-file test.
baseline.summary: DC renderer robustness & performance hardening

Tracks remediation of the joe-janitor audit `.joe-janitor/report-2026-06-27.md` (delta vs 2026-06-24). Overall health is strong: no temporal decay, most prior top findings already fixed, security re-verified (semgrep reports zero true positives), and the LLM-disabled isolation story verified empirically. This epic scopes ONLY the requested subset and is decomposed into the 11 child tickets enumerated below.

## Context
Audit headline: the LLM workflow can be disabled / its deps absent and all client-facing ticket workflows still function (verified by a `sys.meta_path` import-blocker experiment); both LLM gates fail closed with actionable errors. The remaining debt is structural; this epic does not attempt to fix every Medium finding.

Deliberately OUT OF SCOPE (left in the report for separate triage): the workflow->plan_review back-edge structural fix, the `review_ticket` legacy/workflow shadow runner, the `drift_refresh` bespoke pass-driver, the `orchestrator.py` re-export shim, the `graph<->_commands` lazy cycle, and the `_engine.py`/`_engine/` name collision.

## Child tickets (decomposition)
- Bucket 1 (low-effort/low-risk wins): `war-bed-plunk` (task) — doc & comment accuracy fixes.
- Bucket 2 (client UX / reliability): `clay-cake-act` (task) — library force_close parity; `veiny-trout-brink` (task) — honor caller LLMConfig in gate ops; `rancid-vane-wreak` (story) — eliminate redundant ticket-graph re-assembly.
- Bucket 3 (top-3 risks, one ticket per deliverable): `romp-swath-wince` (story) — Risk 1 reconciler exception-taxonomy unification (OSS-informed; the child states the `ReconcilerError` base + `RetryExhaustedError(ReconcilerError, RuntimeError)` design); `tarry-creep-range` (task) — Risk 1 prompt write-backend consolidation; `unfed-liner-arson` (story) — Risk 2 split `outbound_differ.py` at the comment-diff seam; `self-waltz-ace` (story) — Risk 2 split `applier.py` at the dispatch/handlers seam; `dazed-daisy-bur` (task) — Risk 2 split `prompts.py` at the front-matter seam; `hush-quail-holm` (story) — Risk 3 decompose `reconcile_once()` in-place.
- Bucket 4 (E2E config tests): `foamy-gem-skip` (story) — close the F1/F2/F3 gaps.

## Bucket 4 gap definitions (F1/F2/F3)
- F1: the completion close gate is fail-closed-tested only via the library, not driven over CLI/MCP.
- F2: the completion fail-closed path is only simulated (monkeypatched error), never run with the real `[agents]` extra absent in the lean-install lane.
- F3: the optionality per-extra CI matrix omits `mcp` and `grounding`.

## Backward-compatibility / reversibility (one-way-door review)
- Bucket 2 `force_close` is ADDITIVE (a new optional parameter) — non-breaking. Honoring the caller's LLMConfig fixes a documented divergence no consumer relies on; the change is forward-only and covered by the child's parity test.
- Risk 1 exception unification is designed backward-COMPATIBLE: the unified `RetryExhaustedError(ReconcilerError, RuntimeError)` is still caught by every existing `except RuntimeError` and `except Exception` site (zero call-site breakage), so no expand-contract migration is needed. The `romp-swath-wince` child ticket records that taxonomy contract and serves as the design record (ADR-equivalent) for the one-way-door decision.
- All file splits preserve public imports via re-export shims; a stale-reference sweep is required (see Success Criteria + AC).

## Sequencing (de-risking, MVP-first)
Land ONE risky Bucket-3 seam end-to-end first as the de-risking slice — recommended `dazed-daisy-bur` (prompts.py split: simplest, exercises the split -> re-export -> allowlist-drop -> green-CI loop) — before the larger `outbound_differ.py`/`applier.py` splits. Ordering edges are recorded for the two file-conflict pairs: `romp-swath-wince` precedes `self-waltz-ace` (both touch `applier.py`; the split must land on the unified exception type), and `rancid-vane-wreak` precedes `veiny-trout-brink` (both touch `workflow_ops.py`/`production_batch_runner.py`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bucket 1 `war-bed-plunk`: doc/comment accuracy fixes merged; no stale `ticket_reducer/`/`ticket_graph/` path remains (grep verifies).
- [ ] Bucket 2a `clay-cake-act`: library `force_close` reaches parity with the CLI (additive, non-breaking); a parity test asserts identical behavior.
- [ ] Bucket 2b `veiny-trout-brink`: the caller's explicit LLMConfig is reflected in the verdict's model/runner fields; the divergence note is removed.
- [ ] Bucket 2c `rancid-vane-wreak`: a single plan-review run assembles the ticket graph at most once (asserted by a read-counter spy); verdict bytes unchanged.

# AGENTS.md tells agents to override `default_assignee` with a bare handle, which reconcile then clears

## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` — the canonical, launch-loaded agent guidance — instructs agents to claim with an explicit assignee in **three** places:

- `AGENTS.md:75` — "`claim <id> --assignee <you>` … as the FIRST step of working a ticket"
- `AGENTS.md:106` — "**Grab work atomically** — `claim <id> --assignee <you>`"
- `AGENTS.md:238` (library quick reference) — `rebar.claim(tid["id"], assignee="me")`

Two problems compound:

1. **It instructs an override of a setting that exists precisely to get this right.**
   `rebar.toml:66` configures `default_assignee = "joeoakhart@navapbc.com"`, and
   `_commands/claim.py:124-125` applies it **only** when `--assignee` is omitted
   (`if assignee is None`). Because `AGENTS.md` says to always pass `--assignee`, the
   configured default is **never** reached on the agent path.
2. **"`<you>`" / `assignee="me"` invite a bare handle.** An agent substitutes its own
   identity — e.g. `RebarBotNava`, or literally `me` as the library example shows — and
   `AGENTS.md` gives no hint that the value must be Jira-resolvable.

The consequence is a silent revert. The reconciler cannot resolve a bare handle to a Jira user, treats the ticket as unassigned, and the inbound differ writes `assignee=""` back over the local value. Work ends up attributed to nobody.

`docs/config.md:397-400` already documents the requirement correctly — "Use a **Jira-resolvable identity** (email or accountId) … a bare, ambiguous handle (e.g. `joe`) is left unassigned rather than mis-assigned (bug 544e)" — so the two documents **contradict each other**, and the one agents actually read at launch is the wrong one. `AGENTS.md` never mentions `default_assignee` at all.

This is the documented failure mode of closed bug `544e-0a25-eabb-4220`, and story `c36c-357a-2900-4ed7` added `default_assignee` specifically to fix it — but `AGENTS.md` was never updated to stop overriding it, so the fix does not reach agents.

## Evidence (observed live, epic e369)

Claimed the epic and story J1 with `--assignee RebarBotNava`, following `AGENTS.md`. Both reported success (`CLAIMED: acb2-… (assignee: RebarBotNava)`) and both later read back `assignee = ''`.

The event log proves the store write was correct and that no event ever wrote the empty string:

```
ticket: CLAIM acb2-1823-2f0d-415b
  EDIT.json -> "data":{"fields":{"assignee":"RebarBotNava"}}
```

Every subsequent assignee-bearing EDIT also wrote `"RebarBotNava"`. The `''` therefore comes from a later reconciler-authored EDIT, exactly as session log `bb27-06bf-b868-42c7` recorded with a live reproduction:

> "Event log for 3d3d: claim wrote EDIT {assignee:\"joe\"}; ~143s later a reconciler-authored
> EDIT wrote {assignee:\"\"} — the clobber. Live API: validate_assignee_exists(\"joe\")
> REJECTED (\"3 Joes, ambiguous\"); \"joeoakhart@navapbc.com\" RESOLVED to accountId
> 712020:6471376f-…"

Control: throwaway probe tickets (not Jira-bound) **retained** `RebarBotNava` indefinitely, confirming the clear is reconcile-side and not a `claim` parsing or persistence defect.

Note `claimed_session` and `claim_harness` survive the clobber, so the claim is still attributable — but `assignee`, which `list`/`ready`/`next-batch` and every human reader use, is not.

## Approach

Fix the guidance, not the code — `claim`'s explicit-wins precedence is correct and `default_assignee` already works.

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — change the claim instruction to omit `--assignee` so the configured
   default applies: `claim <id>` (noting it auto-assigns `ticket.default_assignee`). Where an
   explicit assignee is genuinely needed, state that it MUST be a Jira-resolvable identity
   (email/accountId), never a bare handle, with a one-line pointer to
   `docs/config.md#ticketdefault_assignee`. Update all three sites (`:75`, `:106`, `:238` —
   the library example `assignee="me"` is the worst offender).
2. Consider a **warning at claim time** when an explicit assignee is a bare handle (no `@`,
   not an accountId shape) while a `default_assignee` is configured — turning a silent
   revert into a visible nudge. Optional; the doc fix is the blocking part.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md`'s claim guidance no longer instructs an unconditional `--assignee` override; it
      shows `claim <id>` and states that `ticket.default_assignee` is applied automatically
- [ ] all three sites (`AGENTS.md:75`, `:106`, and the `:238` library example) are updated
      consistently, and `assignee="me"` no longer appears as a recommended value
- [ ] where an explicit assignee is documented, `AGENTS.md` states it must be Jira-resolvable
      (email/accountId) and links to `docs/config.md#ticketdefault_assignee`
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` and `docs/config.md` no longer contradict each other on assignee identity
- [ ] a fresh agent following ONLY `AGENTS.md` produces a ticket whose assignee survives a
      reconcile pass (verifiable by claiming a scratch ticket and confirming the assignee is
      non-empty after one bridge cycle)
baseline.summary: AGENTS.md tells agents to override default_assignee with a bare handle, which reconcile clears

baseline.description:
## Why
Report §5.2 found 4/8 tickets with persisted reviews were CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED: the gate
raised the right advisory, but the author applied it only AFTER claim — advisory latency,
not blindness. Authors defer advisories because nothing ranks which surviving advisories are
worth applying *now* vs safe to defer. A deterministic triage of the round's surviving
advisories is pure coaching (the reviewer never writes the plan) and carries no detection
risk, so per the epic gate table it ships first with **no eval gate** — validated post-ship by
dogfooding via R7's advisory-application-latency metric.

## What
Add a **deterministic advisory-triage stage** to the Pass-4 coach path of the plan-review
gate. It runs AFTER Pass-3 has decided findings and split them into blocking vs surviving
(advisory), and it partitions the round's surviving **advisory** findings into two buckets —
`apply-now` and `defer` — using ONLY fields already recorded on each decided finding. It emits
NO new LLM judgment (no model call) and no free prose; it renders from a locked format, so the
same decided-finding set produces byte-identical output.

**Output shape (structured, returned — not persisted).** The stage produces a structured
`triage` array, one entry per surviving advisory finding:
`{"id": str, "criteria": list[str], "priority": float, "block_threshold": float,
"bucket": "apply-now"|"defer", "reason": str}` (`reason` is `""` for `apply-now`). This array
is attached to the returned verdict as a **top-level key `verdict["triage"]`** — the
`plan_review_verdict` output schema has `additionalProperties: true`, so it validates with no
schema change — so the agent sees it at review time. It is **NOT** added to the persisted
`REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar:
`sidecar.build_payload` enumerates coaching-note fields explicitly, and R7's dogfood metrics
derive advisory *application* from post-claim outcomes joined to findings by `criteria`, not
from a stored triage stamp — so persistence is unnecessary and `build_payload` stays unchanged.
No Markdown, no config flag.

**Mechanism choice (rationale).** It is NOT an entry in the Pass-4 `MOVE_REGISTRY` (in
`passes.py`, re-exported by `orchestrator.py`). The registry schema
(`review_kernel/coach.py` `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA`) is a *per-finding* `{subject}`-placeholder
template the LLM fills; a single `{subject}` substitution cannot express a ranked two-bucket
split across all surviving advisories. So the triage is a small pure function on the
plan-review Pass-4 path — blast radius stays inside plan-review; the shared kernel coach
mechanism and its notes are unchanged.

**The ranking rule (fully specified, grounded in real fields).** Every decided finding carries
`priority` (= `validity × impact`, float in [0,1], always present — `review_kernel/decide.py`,
and set to 0.4 for DET-tier advisories in `orchestrator.py`). `block_threshold` is present on
LLM-decided findings (resolved by `decide.py`; 0.60 via plan-review's `criteria_routing.json`
routing, not `decide.py`'s 0.95 `DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`); DET-tier advisories
stamped by `partition_findings` (`orchestrator.py`) do **not** carry it, so `triage_advisories`
reads it as `f.get("block_threshold", DEFAULT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD)` — the 0.95 default applies when
absent (already imported in `passes.py`), under which a DET advisory (priority 0.4) buckets
`defer`. No other field is used — there is NO "remediation-mode carryover status" field on
Pass-4 findings.

- **Bucketing.** An advisory is `apply-now` iff `priority >= block_threshold - APPLY_NOW_MARGIN`
  (it came within the margin of blocking → highest value to apply now); else `defer`.
  `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` is a named module constant, default **0.10**.
- **Ordering (total, deterministic → byte-identical).** The `triage` array is sorted by
  `priority` DESC, then by `criteria[0]` (the first element of the finding's `criteria` list;
  a finding with empty `criteria` sorts last via a fixed sentinel `"~"`) ASC, then by `id` ASC.
- **Defer reason.** Built only from the finding's own numbers, e.g.
  `deferred: priority 0.32 is 0.28 below its 0.60 block line` — fixed words + recorded numbers,
  no LLM prose, non-prescriptive.
- **Eligibility.** Only findings with `decision == "advisory"` are triaged. Blocking findings
  must be remediated regardless and are excluded (this is why R6 is advisory-only).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` — the deterministic `triage_advisories(surviving)` pure
  function (bucketing + ordering + defer-reason via a locked format) and the `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN`
  constant.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` — in the `plan_review_coach` step (the sole live
  verdict-assembly path; the older bespoke `_run_passes` path was retired in epic
  solid-timer-unison), invoke `triage_advisories` on the surviving advisory findings and set
  `verdict["triage"]` before the closing `validate_structured(verdict, _OUTPUT_SCHEMA)` return.
  The two `gate_dispatch.py` recovery paths (`_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`,
  `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`) assemble DEGRADED verdicts when a pass fails and have no
  decided advisories to triage, so they are out of scope — a recovered verdict simply omits
  `triage`. No other returned-result consumer changes.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py` — unit tests (see ACs).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — document the triage stage, ranking rule, and R7 dogfood
  expectation.
- NOT touched: `sidecar.py` / the `plan_review_result_v2` schema (triage is returned, not
  persisted) and `review_kernel/coach.py` (kernel mechanism unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `triage_advisories` returns byte-identical output across two runs on the same fixed
      advisory set, and every `reason` string matches the locked format (only fixed tokens +
      recorded numeric fields — no LLM/prescriptive prose). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k determinism -q`.
- [ ] Boundary bucketing: an advisory with `priority == block_threshold - APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` is
      `apply-now`; one epsilon below is `defer` (parametrized). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k boundary -q`.
- [ ] The `triage` array is ordered by `priority` DESC, then `criteria[0]` ASC (empty→`"~"`),
      then `id` ASC — a test with deliberate priority ties and a multi-element / empty
      `criteria` pins the exact order. Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k ordering -q`.
- [ ] Only `decision == "advisory"` findings appear in the array; blocking findings are
      excluded, and every surviving advisory appears exactly once (including advisories that
      mapped to no coach move). Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k advisory_only -q`.
- [ ] Integration: the returned plan-review verdict carries the `triage` array as top-level
      `verdict["triage"]`, equal to `triage_advisories(surviving)` for that run (a test drives the
      `plan_review_coach` step with fixture findings and asserts `verdict["triage"]`).
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_triage.py -k integration -q`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the triage stage, its ranking rule (the
      `APPLY_NOW_MARGIN` default, the ordering, and the defer-reason format), and the R7 dogfood
      expectation. Proving command:
      `grep -q "APPLY_NOW_MARGIN" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "apply-now" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "defer" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "R7" docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] Landed through Gerrit directly in the packaged Pass-4 coach path — no config flag;
      `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: R6: advisory-triage coaching move (pass-4 registry, ship-first)

undercounting the Pass-4 coach. Correct the gate-level descriptions to four-pass.
## Scope (gate-level descriptions — fix)

baseline.description:
## Summary

Re-running `rebar review-plan` on the **already-signed, unchanged** auto-lander epic
`f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af` (and its story S1 `843b-801f-9ef9-442d`) produced a stream of
**invalid blocking findings** and **non-convergent** behaviour: the plan had been signed
CLEAN (`blocking: 0, advisory: 2`) at HEAD `2272d68`, and re-review at a later HEAD
`6244666` — with **no change to the plan**, only `main` advancing — returned `BLOCK`
(`blocking: 1, advisory: 13`). Remediating the findings then *increased* the finding count
and *spawned new blocks*. The gate never converged; the epic could only be claimed via
`--force`.

This bug documents each invalid/problematic finding with full context, its triggering
criterion, its round-over-round progression, and — crucially — **which stage of the review
pipeline (finding discovery / validation assessment / impact assessment) should have caught
it and why.** It is the raw material for calibrating the plan-review gate so an already-signed
plan is not re-blocked by non-deterministic false positives at a drifted HEAD.

## The review pipeline (stage vocabulary used below)

`review-plan` produces a verdict through three conceptual stages. Each invalid finding below
is attributed to the stage that should have filtered it:

1. **Finding discovery** — generation of candidate findings from the plan + graph. A finding
   whose premise is *contradicted by text present in the plan* should never be emitted here.
2. **Validation assessment** — deciding whether a candidate is *real*. A candidate that is
   contradicted by (a) the plan itself, (b) a sibling finding in the same verdict, or (c) the
   ticket's own recorded comment trail should be dropped as not-real here.
3. **Impact assessment** — scoring severity and deriving block-vs-advisory. A finding whose
   remedy is deferred/operator-attested/implementation-stage should not score at the blocking
   tier here.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Take a plan that has a valid, signed `plan-review` attestation (`blocking: 0`).
2. Let `main` advance so the attestation reads *stale* (HEAD-relative staleness) without
   editing the ticket.
3. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` again. Observe a materially different verdict — new blocking
   findings that were not present in the signing review, including at least one whose fix is
   already in the plan text.
4. Remediate a flagged advisory (e.g. "name the missing edit target in Scope"). Re-run the
   review. Observe that the remediation *introduces new blocking findings* (it now demands an
   AC + proving command for the thing you just added to Scope).

**Expected:** re-reviewing an unchanged, previously-signed plan at a drifted HEAD yields a
substantively stable verdict (still a PASS, or at most the same findings). Findings whose
premise is present-and-contradicted in the plan are dropped in validation. Remediating an
advisory does not manufacture new blocks.

**Actual:** the verdict flips PASS→BLOCK with no plan change; a blocking finding re-appears
verbatim after its fix is demonstrably present; two findings in the same verdict contradict
each other; and advisory remediation cascades into new blocks. The gate does not converge.

---

## A. Invalid BLOCKING findings

### A1 — Epic: "pre-cutover snapshot never captured / not stored" (FALSE POSITIVE)
- **Criteria:** `E2`, `F1`. **Impact:** 0.85 (blocking). **Rounds:** raised r1 → remediated
  (AC added naming actor, artifact, location, timing) → **re-raised VERBATIM r2**.
- **Finding text:** *"The security-invariants AC requires 'a GET /projects/rebar/access diff
  vs the pre-cutover snapshot,' but the plan never tasks anyone with capturing the pre-cutover
  snapshot before the label is deployed, nor where it is stored."*
- **Why invalid:** after r1 the plan literally contained: *"Pre-cutover access baseline
  (captured by S1 843b, BEFORE the label is pushed): save the current `GET
  /a/projects/rebar/access` response to `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json`
  and commit it in the same change."* This names the **actor** (S1), the **artifact/location**
  (the JSON file), and the **timing** (before cutover, same change) — exactly the three things
  the finding claims are absent. The finding offered **no `checklist_item` fix** (it had
  nothing to suggest because the fix was already present).
- **Stage that should have caught it:** **Validation assessment.** A validation pass that
  re-reads the plan for the finding's own premise would find the contradicting text and drop
  the candidate. Secondarily **finding discovery** should not regenerate a finding whose
  subject string is present in the plan.
- **Damning corroboration:** the SAME r2 verdict contains advisory A-adv "the parent
  **explicitly assigns capture to S1**" (see B2 below). One verdict simultaneously asserts
  "no one is tasked with capture" (blocking) and "the parent explicitly assigns capture to S1"
  (advisory). A validation stage that cross-checked findings against each other would have
  killed one of them.

### A2 — S1: "setup-project.sh has no AC / no proving command" and "line-148 commit message not updated" (REMEDIATION-INDUCED)
- **Criteria:** `E6`/`F1` and `G1G2`. **Impact:** 0.85 each (blocking). **Rounds:** absent r1 →
  **created by remediating epic advisory A-#6** ("add `setup-project.sh` to the plan's edit
  targets"). I added a Scope sentence naming `setup-project.sh`; r2 then blocked because that
  Scope deliverable had no matching AC/proving command.
- **Why problematic:** this is the **remediation cascade** — acting on a low-impact advisory
  manufactured two *blocking* findings. A gate that turns "you should also mention X" into "X
  is now a blocking deliverable with no AC" cannot converge: every remediation widens the
  surface faster than it closes it. (These two were legitimately fixable and I fixed them with
  one AC + `grep -F 'Autosubmit' infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`; the DEFECT is that the gate
  created them from an advisory in the first place.)
- **Stage that should have caught it:** **Impact assessment.** A newly-named, secondary
  audit-trail touch (a commit-message string) is not a blocking-tier gap; it is advisory at
  most. Escalating it to `blocking` (0.85) is impact inflation.

---

## B. Invalid / non-material ADVISORY findings

### B1 — Epic A8: "sibling tickets touch the same file with no ordering edge"
- **Criteria:** `P5`. **Impact:** 0.4. **Fix offered:** none.
- **Why invalid:** `infra/autolander/loop.py` is co-edited by S2a/S2b/S2c **by deliberate
  decomposition** (S2 was split into three tasks precisely to keep each unit loadable — the
  module-size ethos), and real ordering edges DO exist (`38be depends_on 89f9` and `08e1`).
  The premise ("no ordering edge") is false, and the pattern it flags is the intended design.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** — a dependency-graph read disproves "no ordering edge."

### B2 — Epic A9 / S1 A7: "Acceptance-criteria / definition-of-done quality issues"
- **Criteria:** `P6`. **Impact:** 0.4. **Fix offered:** none. **Rounds:** present both rounds.
- **Why invalid:** contentless. No specific AC is named, no defect is described, no remediation
  is suggested. It is un-actionable by construction — the agent cannot act on "quality issues."
- **Stage:** **Finding discovery** should not emit a finding with an empty body and no
  `checklist_item`; a finding with no actionable content is noise, not signal.

### B3 — Epic A12: "`POST /changes/{id}/rebase:chain` endpoint unverified"
- **Criteria:** `T3`. **Impact:** 0.0. **Fix offered:** add a live API probe.
- **Why invalid:** this exact claim was **already litigated and rejected in the ticket's own
  comment trail** — the epic records: *"Verified against the Gerrit REST API docs: `POST
  /changes/{change-id}/rebase:chain` DOES exist (3.6+, so the 3.14.1 instance has it) — the
  review's own advisory T3 concedes this."* The gate re-surfaced a settled, fact-checked
  point that a prior review round had already conceded.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** — the ticket comment trail is in scope for the review
  and directly refutes the finding. Re-raising conceded fact is a validation miss.

### B4 — Epic A11 & A13: "`rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader` trailer-preservation unverified"
- **Criteria:** `T1`, `T3`. **Impact:** 0.0 (both). **Fix offered:** add a probe/smoke test.
- **Why non-material:** these ask for *implementation-stage verification* of a documented
  Gerrit flag. The plan already routes that verification into child ACs — S2a carries an
  "uploader/trailer-preservation test" and S5b carries a "synthetic scratch-ref smoke change."
  The plan does not need to re-prove a library capability at plan-review time.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment** correctly scored these 0.0 (non-blocking), but they were
  still surfaced as duplicated findings (A11 and A13 are the same claim). **Finding discovery**
  should de-duplicate; a 0.0-impact, already-covered concern is noise.

### B5 — Epic A14: "S5 should formally `depends_on` S3, not merely 'Uses S3'"
- **Criteria:** `G4`. **Impact:** 0.0.
- **Why non-material:** S5 already documents "Uses S3's outcome marker," S5 is gated behind S2,
  and S3 completes in the same topological tier. The distinction between a `Uses` note and a
  formal `depends_on` here is cosmetic and impact-0.0 by the reviewer's own scoring.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment** (correctly 0.0) — but flagging it at all, given it is
  cosmetic, is discovery noise.

### B6 — S1 A4/A5/A6/A8/A9/A11: "pin curl/auth/jq/rollback into the plan ACs"
- **Criteria:** `T3`, `E6`, `T5b`, `T5c`. **Impact:** 0.85 down to 0.0.
- **Why non-material:** these demand that the plan AC embed the exact `curl` command, auth
  mechanism, `jq` assertion, HTTP-200 check, and rollback procedure for the **operator cutover**
  (`GET /a/projects/rebar/labels/...`, `GET /a/projects/rebar/access`). That cutover is an
  **operator-attested** step (ADR-0043) whose evidence is a recorded attestation, not an
  in-session command. Mechanical proving-commands belong in the cutover script/runbook, not the
  plan AC.
- **Stage:** **Impact assessment.** The gate does not distinguish codebase-verifiable ACs from
  operator-attested ones (ADR-0043); it applies the "every AC needs an in-session proving
  command" rule uniformly, inflating operator-runbook granularity to 0.85 blocking-adjacent.

### B7 — S1 A12: "no RETIRE path for the Autosubmit label"
- **Criteria:** `T9`. **Impact:** 0.0.
- **Why invalid:** demanding a feature-retirement procedure for a label being *introduced* is
  YAGNI/scope creep. The label ships with a documented back-out note already; a full retire
  runbook is out of scope for the introduction story.
- **Stage:** **Validation assessment** (scope check) should recognise retire-path demands on an
  introduction ticket as out-of-scope, not a plan gap.

---

## C. Cross-cutting review-gate defects (the root causes)

1. **Non-determinism across HEAD drift (the core bug).** The epic was signed CLEAN
   (`blocking: 0`) at `2272d68`; the identical plan re-reviewed at `6244666` returned
   `blocking: 1, advisory: 13`. No plan change occurred — only `main` advanced. Re-review of an
   unchanged plan must be substantively stable; it is not. This is what forces the entire
   re-claim treadmill.
2. **Verbatim re-block after a demonstrated fix (A1).** Validation does not re-read the plan for
   a finding's own premise before re-emitting it.
3. **Intra-verdict self-contradiction (A1 blocking vs its advisory twin).** Findings within one
   verdict are not cross-checked for consistency.
4. **Remediation-induced finding cascade (A2).** Acting on a low-impact advisory manufactures
   new blocking findings, so the finding count rises with each remediation round and the gate
   never converges.
5. **Uniform proving-command demand ignores ADR-0043 (B6).** Operator-attested ACs are scored
   as if they need in-session mechanical commands.
6. **Contentless and duplicated findings (B2, B4).** Findings with empty bodies / no
   `checklist_item`, and duplicate findings, pass discovery.
7. **Hard-override mis-classification is the blocking amplifier (root cause of the 0.85s).**
   Per the impact model shipped in closed story `0858-facb-6901-4781` (under closed epic
   `4cc3-23c9-b062-41ac`), a finding tagged with any of {AC-unverifiable, DoD-uncertifiable,
   undecomposed, divergent-implementation} gets `impact_sev` **force-set to ≥ 0.85** (a hard
   override, bypassing the severity MAX). Nearly every invalid finding above lands at exactly
   **0.85** — i.e. the validation stage mis-tagged a false-positive/non-material finding into
   a hard-override axis (chiefly "AC-unverifiable"), which then mechanically escalated it to
   the blocking tier. The override is doing its job; the DEFECT is upstream — validation
   assigns the hard-override axis to findings that are not actually AC-unverifiable (the AC is
   present, or the "unverifiable" step is operator-attested per ADR-0043). **Fixing validation
   mis-tagging is higher-leverage than re-tuning the threshold**, because the override
   deliberately ignores the threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Finding discovery drops (or does not emit) any candidate finding whose subject text is
      **present and contradicted** in the plan body; a regression fixture reproduces epic A1
      (snapshot AC present) and asserts no such block is emitted.
- [ ] Validation assessment cross-checks findings **within a single verdict** for mutual
      contradiction and drops the weaker/contradicted one; a fixture reproduces the A1
      blocking-vs-advisory contradiction and asserts at most one survives.
- [ ] Validation assessment consults the ticket's **recorded comment trail** and drops a
      finding that re-litigates a point the trail already resolved; a fixture reproduces B3
      (`rebase:chain` conceded in-trail) and asserts it is dropped.
- [ ] Impact assessment distinguishes **operator-attested** criteria (ADR-0043) from
      codebase-verifiable ones and does NOT demand an in-session proving command for the former;
      a fixture reproduces B6 and asserts those findings are not scored at the blocking tier.
- [ ] Finding discovery **de-duplicates** findings and suppresses contentless findings (empty
      body / no `checklist_item`); a fixture reproduces B2/B4.
- [ ] **Re-review stability (the headline criterion):** re-running `review-plan` on an
      unchanged, previously-signed plan at a drifted HEAD yields a verdict with **no NEW
      blocking findings** relative to the signing review; a fixture (sign at HEAD-A, advance to
      HEAD-B with no ticket edit, re-review) asserts the block set does not grow.
- [ ] A short design note (or ADR) records the "remediation cascade" anti-pattern (acting on an
      advisory must not manufacture a block) and the re-review-stability contract.

## Notes / provenance

Surfaced while executing the auto-lander epic `f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af` under `/rebar-implement`:
every one of its 13 live tickets was signed at `2272d68` and went stale when `main` advanced,
so each claim required a fresh review, exposing the non-convergence. Full per-finding triage
and the force-claim justifications are recorded on session log `547b-4aca-0076-4a36`.

**Related prior work (both CLOSED):** epic `4cc3-23c9-b062-41ac` "Review-gate impact redesign
+ threshold re-tune (plan-review + code-review)" and its story `0858-facb-6901-4781`
"Plan-review impact redesign: severity-first MAX + hard override + detection amplifier" — this
bug is a follow-on defect against that same subsystem (see cross-cutting defect #7: the
hard-override from `0858` is what force-escalates the mis-validated findings to 0.85). Linked
`relates_to 4cc3` and `discovered_from f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af`.
baseline.summary: Plan-review gate: non-convergent re-review of an already-signed plan at drifted HEAD emits invalid blocking findings (auto-lander epic f1fa)

## Why
One plan defect currently mints up to N blocking findings via multi-criterion co-citation (ticket a879: two nonexistent symbols x five criteria = 10 blocking findings per round for 3 consecutive rounds; ticket c9d8 round 1: one underspecified escape-hatch surfaced as 4 blocking findings). Agents face an inflated block wall for a single fix-unit, and per-criterion block tallies are distorted for future calibration. Dedup must GROUP, never drop: the gate's strength is unchanged. NOTE: the existing `norm_id` in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py is criterion-SCOPED (its hash bakes in the sorted criteria list), so norm_id equality CANNOT group across criteria - a criteria-free key is required.

## What
- Add a `fix_unit_key(finding)` helper in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py, next to the norm_id machinery, with two NEW inline sub-helpers defined here (neither exists today): `_norm_location(f)` = the same significant-token normalization norm_id applies to text, applied to `f.get("location", "") or ""` (lowercase, `re.findall` token split, the existing stop-token filtering, sorted de-duplicated join) - token-set rather than exact-string because independent finder criteria format the same location differently (path:line vs prose section names); and `_norm_claim(f)` = norm_id's existing token-set normalization of the finding text, EXCLUDING the criteria list from the hash basis (norm_id bakes sorted criteria into its hash; that exclusion is the whole point). `fix_unit_key(f) = sha256(_norm_location(f) + "|" + _norm_claim(f))`. Same reword tolerance as norm_id, criteria-free.
- After verdict production and before the sidecar emit (the seam in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py where the rising/completion floors already run), group blocking findings sharing a fix_unit_key WITHOUT moving any finding out of verdict['blocking'] (build_payload at sidecar.py:421-427 concatenates the existing buckets; removing findings would silently drop them from the sidecar). Grouping only STAMPS fields: every grouped finding gains `group_id` (= the fix_unit_key) and `is_primary` (True on exactly one finding per group - highest priority, with deterministic tiebreak: missing priority sorts as 0.0; ties broken by alphabetically-first sorted criteria entry, then lowest finding id). The primary also gains `group_criteria` (the union of the group's criteria lists). All N findings keep decision=block - the gate's semantics, the verdict shape consumers see, and the sidecar's lossless capture are unchanged apart from the additive fields.
- Sidecar persistence: `build_payload`'s `_slim()` field-selection currently omits unknown fields - explicitly add `group_id`, `is_primary`, and `group_criteria` to the `_slim()` dict in sidecar.py so the stamps survive into the persisted payload (additive optional fields on the current plan-review sidecar schema).
- CLI: the renderer in src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py prints only primaries (suppressing findings with is_primary=False), each with a "(+N co-criteria: E4, G1G2, ...)" suffix where N = the group's folded-member count. Library/MCP consumers see the full stamped blocking list (no suppression outside the CLI renderer).
- Keep the change out of src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py: this is a pipeline-layer grouping, not a decision change.

## Scope
IN: fix_unit_key helper, grouping of BLOCKING findings only, group_id persistence through _slim()/build_payload, CLI rendering, tests. OUT: advisory grouping (the advisory cap already bounds volume), cross-round dedup (that is the rising floor's job), any threshold/posture change, any change to norm_id itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A synthetic verdict with 5 blocking findings citing the same location and same claim text across 5 different criteria: after grouping, verdict['blocking'] still contains all 5 findings, exactly 1 has is_primary=True, all share one group_id, and the primary's group_criteria is the 5-criteria union; the verdict remains BLOCK. Oracle: new unit test; `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "fix_unit or group" -x` green.
- [ ] Findings at different locations or with different claims are NOT grouped, and two findings with identical text but different criteria ARE grouped (the criteria-free key property). Oracle: unit tests over fix_unit_key asserting both directions.
- [ ] The CLI output for a grouped primary finding includes the suffix "(+N co-criteria: <union>)" where N is the number of folded findings. Oracle: unit test over the renderer in src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py; `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "group" -x` green.
- [ ] The emitted sidecar retains all 5 findings with decision=block, each carrying the same group_id and exactly one carrying is_primary=True. Oracle: unit test reads the build_payload output and asserts those three properties.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all pass.
baseline.summary: Cross-criterion fix-unit grouping for blocking findings (one defect, one block group)
