content.text: ## Why
Today rebar has TWO session resolvers with DIFFERENT precedence chains:
`session_log._resolve_session_fp` (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> REBAR_SESSION_ID ->
SESSION_ID -> None`) and `transition_close._resolve_session` (`REBAR_SESSION_ID ->
SESSION_ID -> git HEAD -> "unknown"`). The latter OMITS `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so in a
real Claude Code session the FORCE_CLOSE audit comment falls through to git HEAD — a value
that changes every commit and is not a session id. This is a latent bug, and the two must
converge onto ONE shared resolver before anything else in the epic builds on session
resolution.
## What
Introduce one shared `resolve_session_id()` helper in a NEW module
`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py`, implementing a single **data-driven, ordered** var
list so new harness vars are a one-line add:
_SESSION_ID_VARS = ["REBAR_SESSION_ID", "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "SESSION_ID"]
Precedence rationale: the explicit, rebar-owned `REBAR_SESSION_ID` wins first (an
operator/hook override is authoritative), then the native harness var
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, then the ambient `SESSION_ID`, else `None`.
- **Empty-string handling (DECISION):** a var whose value is empty / whitespace-only is
treated as ABSENT (skipped), matching the existing falsy-`or`-chain semantics. Only the
first *non-empty* var wins; all-empty / all-absent -> `None`.
- **Refactor both call sites onto it:**
- `session_log._resolve_session_fp()` -> `return resolve_session_id()`. This
**intentionally inverts** session_log's current precedence (today `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`
before `REBAR_SESSION_ID`; now `REBAR_SESSION_ID` first). Impact is limited to sessions
that set BOTH vars (rare); the unified explicit-rebar-first contract is deliberate and is
documented in `docs/config.md`.
- `transition_close._resolve_session(tracker)` -> `resolve_session_id() or
_short_head(tracker) or "unknown"`. The shared resolver returns `None` on absence; the
git-HEAD / `"unknown"` fallback stays LOCAL to this call site (a cosmetic non-empty
audit string). This FIXES THE BUG: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is now captured at the
FORCE_CLOSE audit site.
- **AC4 scope (DECISION):** "never returns git HEAD" constrains the **return value of
`resolve_session_id()` ONLY**. The FORCE_CLOSE audit comment MAY still render short HEAD
via the documented local cosmetic fallback — that is out of scope for the shared resolver.
- **Deferred to S5 (c557):** the OSS harness vars `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` / `CODEX_THREAD_ID`
are added to the list by story `privy-eloquent-nauplius`, which owns verifying their
canonical names + harness provenance. S1 ships the extensible list with the three vars
above only.
- Update the existing `_resolve_session` unit tests in
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` (~lines 477-504) that call the
private helper, so they reflect the delegation (and guard against an ambient
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` by `delenv`-ing it in the fallback cases).
- The enumerated consumer `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_session_log_capture.py` is
UNAFFECTED by the precedence inversion and needs NO code change: every fingerprinting case
sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` only after `delenv`-ing `REBAR_SESSION_ID`/`SESSION_ID`, so
no assertion depends on which of REBAR vs CLAUDE_CODE wins (they are never both set). It is
simply re-run to prove it stays green after the refactor.
## Scope
- IN: new `src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py` shared helper + ordered list; refactor of the
two existing resolvers; unit tests for precedence / empty-string / all-absent + a
call-site wiring test proving `transition_close` captures `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` + a
no-duplicate-chains source guard test; update of the `test_completion_gate.py` resolver
tests and a green re-run of the (unmodified) `test_session_log_capture.py` consumer;
rewrite of the existing `docs/config.md` "Session provenance" section.
- OUT: recording the id on claims (S2 / 68ef); `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`/`CODEX_THREAD_ID` +
harness provenance (S5 / c557); reducer / read / hook work (later stories).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_session_id()` returns the first NON-EMPTY var in order
`REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`, else `None`.
Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -q` (cases assert each var's precedence).
- [ ] An empty-string / whitespace-only value is skipped (treated as absent).
Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -k empty -q`.
- [ ] `resolve_session_id()` NEVER returns git HEAD (its var list contains no git call).
Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -k "all_absent or none" -q` asserts
`None` when all vars are unset (no HEAD value can appear).
- [ ] `session_log._resolve_session_fp` and `transition_close._resolve_session` BOTH
delegate to the shared helper AND the OLD duplicate env-lookup chains are REMOVED.
Proof: a source-guard test in `test_session_id.py` reads both source files and asserts
each contains `resolve_session_id` AND contains NO `os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`,
`os.environ.get("REBAR_SESSION_ID"`, or `os.environ.get("SESSION_ID"` literal (the only
session-var env reads live in `session_id.py`).
- [ ] FORCE_CLOSE audit captures `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` when set (the bug fix).
Proof: `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -k resolve_session -q`
includes a case that sets ONLY `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and asserts
`transition_close._resolve_session(tracker)` returns that value (not HEAD).
- [ ] Existing `_resolve_session` tests updated and green.
Proof: `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py -k resolve_session -q`.
- [ ] The unmodified `test_session_log_capture.py` consumer stays green after the refactor.
Proof: `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_session_log_capture.py -q`.
- [ ] The existing `docs/config.md` "Session provenance" section (currently documenting
`REBAR_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID -> short git HEAD -> "unknown"`) is rewritten to the
unified ordered contract, ADDING `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` in its correct position and a
one-line precedence-inversion note; the stale `SESSION_ID -> short git HEAD` chain (as
the resolver contract) no longer appears. Proof: a doc-content assertion in
`test_session_id.py` that reads `docs/config.md` and asserts the new ordered list string
is present AND the exact stale contract string is absent.
## Depends on
- (none — foundation story)

content.text: ## Why

`sign` and `verify-signature` (native signing commands, added in PR #4) advertise `[--output json]` in their help and emit structured JSON, but neither is registered in `rebar.schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`. This gap was masked by the old `tests/interfaces/test_schema_coverage.py::test_commands_advertising_output_have_a_schema`, which parsed the bash dispatcher's help arms (which predate the signing commands). Tier E7 rewired that test to the in-process help source of truth (`rebar._cli._help`), surfacing the gap; the two commands are currently in a documented exclusion set in that test referencing this ticket.
## What
- Author JSON Schemas under `src/rebar/schemas/` for the `sign` and `verify-signature` `--output json` payloads (matching the actual emitted shape).
- Register them in `rebar.schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS` (keys `sign`, `verify_signature`).
- Add output-schema validation tests (mirror `test_schema_outputs.py`).
- Remove the `sign`/`verify-signature` exclusion from `test_schema_coverage.py::test_commands_advertising_output_have_a_schema`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/schemas/` has schema files for sign and verify-signature --output json
- [ ] `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS` registers both; `test_every_schema_file_is_wired` + `test_every_registry_entry_resolves` pass
- [ ] `--output json` payloads validate against the new schemas (added tests)
- [ ] the exclusion set in test_schema_coverage.py is removed and the test passes with no exclusions

content.text: ## Why

rebar has ~40 distinct env vars across ~150 read sites; only ~half are REBAR_-prefixed. Catalog every env var + read site; decide per var keep/rename/remove (informed by the interactive env-var review in session); implement REBAR_ prefixing with back-compat aliases; route reads through the typed Config.

content.text: # Plan-review Pass-1 finding-memory (recall fix)
## Why
Verdict-flip on identical code is a RECALL problem: in flipping same-material review pairs the decisive
would-block findings had validity ~0.99 and 14/17 flips were because the other run simply MISSED the valid
finding. Improving finder recall closes the gap; tightening thresholds cannot.
## What (independence-preserving: a POST-Pass-1 recall step, NOT a Pass-1 finder injection)
Re-surface a ticket's prior-review findings that the fresh Pass-1 finder MISSED, then let the UNCHANGED
Pass-2 verifier decide whether they still hold — so a genuinely-resolved concern is dropped, not re-blocked.
- LOAD: read the most-recent REVIEW_RESULT sidecar via the EXISTING `sidecar.latest_review_result(ticket_id)`
reader; take prior findings that scored NEAR/ABOVE the bar. Concrete rule (named module constants, not bare
literals; config-tunable later): `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY` (=0.5) AND `decision in {"block",
"advisory"}` — the LOWERCASE decision strings pass3_decide emits, excluding "dropped"/"indeterminate" —
capped to the top `RECALL_CAP` (=12) by priority to bound cost. Best-effort: any failure in the reader
(missing/garbled sidecar, I/O error) degrades to an EMPTY concern list — recall is then a no-op and NEVER
fails the review (mirrors the sidecar's observability-only posture).
- RECALL (strictly AFTER Pass-1): compute the fresh findings' `norm_id` set using the EXISTING
`sidecar.norm_id(finding)` (no new fingerprinting); for each prior concern whose `norm_id` is NOT in that
set (the fresh finder MISSED it), add it as a RECALL CANDIDATE finding (its prior
`finding`/`suggested_fix`/`criteria`/`location`, tagged `_recall: true`). Dedup candidates by `norm_id`.
- VERIFY (unchanged): recall candidates flow through the SAME Pass-2 verifier + Pass-3 decision as any
finding — each judged INDEPENDENTLY against the CURRENT plan. A concern the current plan resolved fails
validity (< 0.5) and is DROPPED by Pass-2, so a stale recalled finding can NEVER block on memory alone.
## Structural-independence invariant (explicitly preserved — the reason for the post-Pass-1 design)
The codebase enforces finder independence "by construction, not by prompt assertion": the pinned test
`test_prior_findings_only_reach_the_novelty_seam` (tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py) asserts the
Pass-1 finder / `verify_instructions` NEVER carry prior findings — prior findings reach ONLY the Pass-2
novelty seam (`verify.prior_findings_block`). ADR 0008 Invariant 1 is the same rule.
This design does NOT inject prior findings into the Pass-1 finder: the finder runs byte-unchanged, so
`test_prior_findings_only_reach_the_novelty_seam` and ADR 0008 Invariant 1 stay green. Prior findings enter
ONLY as post-Pass-1 recall CANDIDATES that are verified on their own merits (never merged into the finder's
context; never blocking without independent Pass-2 confirmation). A NEW test pins that the finder
instructions remain prior-free while recall candidates are added strictly after Pass-1.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — a `prior_concerns(ticket_id, repo_root)` reader that reuses
`latest_review_result` + `norm_id` (no new fingerprinting algorithm) and the `RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY`/
`RECALL_CAP` constants; best-effort (never raises).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` (`run_pass1`) — the post-Pass-1 recall step (the fresh finder is
unchanged; `ctx` already carries `ticket_id` + `repo_root`). Cost is the recalled candidates' Pass-2
verification tokens, NOT an extra finder call.
- `tests/unit/` — recall + resolved-drop + independence-preserved tests.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Prior-review findings (filtered `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY` AND `decision in {"block",
"advisory"}`, capped to `RECALL_CAP`) that the fresh Pass-1 finder MISSED (by `norm_id`) are
re-surfaced as recall candidates AFTER Pass-1; they are NOT injected into the Pass-1 finder context and
are deduped by `norm_id`. A reader failure degrades to a no-op (never fails the review).
- [ ] The Pass-1 finder is byte-unchanged: the pinned `test_prior_findings_only_reach_the_novelty_seam`
still passes, and a NEW test asserts `run_pass1`'s finder instructions never contain prior-finding text
(independence by construction preserved; ADR 0008 Invariant 1 upheld).
- [ ] No additional LLM FINDER call beyond the existing Pass-1. Recall candidates DO incur their own Pass-2
verification (that is the FP backstop), bounded by the `RECALL_CAP` (<=12) cap; there is no extra
finder pass and no new prompt.
- [ ] Proving command `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_novelty.py -v`
(all green — the second file runs the pinned independence test), covering: (a) a prior finding the
fresh run MISSED is re-surfaced as a recall candidate; (b) a prior finding the fresh run ALSO found is
NOT double-surfaced (norm_id dedup); (c) a recalled candidate whose current-plan verification FAILS
validity is DROPPED by Pass-2, not re-blocked; (d) with no prior sidecar, recall is a no-op. Recall-lift
on same-`material_fingerprint` pairs is measured OFFLINE by the calibration child
(raptorial-galloping-dragon), not gated here.

baseline.summary: Plan-review Pass-1 finding-memory (recall fix)

baseline.description:
## Why

Calibration finding (2026-07-27/28), grounded in the persisted REVIEW_RESULT corpus (51,964 verified findings; 18,085 on plan-v3):

A G6 finding on epic c4ad-a93e-0613-408f (sec-semantic-layer-2026-challenge) described a mechanism that would NOT work — four sites branching on the literal `"s3vectors"` omitted from the plan's scope, which would have re-embedded the whole corpus on every container boot and routed a wipe to a LanceDB drop against Postgres. It scored `impact=0.0`, `severity=none`, and landed ADVISORY despite `validity=0.8889`, `blocking_enabled=true`, `block_threshold=0.60`.

Root cause is NOT the threshold (0.60 is already the most permissive blocking bar in the registry). `impact_plan` is a MAX over seven axes; the verifier graded all seven `none`, so `max(...)=0.0`. The axes that recorded the real harm (`prod_impact: medium`, `blast_radius: module`, `likelihood: medium`) are deliberately unread by `impact_plan` — they are the superseded mean model's inputs, retained only for sidecar continuity.

The axis that SHOULD have fired is `divergent_implementation` ("the plan diverges from the implementation/reality it claims to describe"). Corpus evidence that it is mis-calibrated:

- It fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings, and it is the ONLY hard-override axis never
  calibrated (born in d487060b5, one line of prose, never revisited). Its sibling
  `ac_unverifiable` got a closed `Literal` + worked examples in story
  large-sleepful-needlefish; this axis did not.
- Of 1,307 findings in the "omitted scope site / unenumerated consumer" class — the family the
  axis exists to describe — it is graded `none` **1,173 times (~90%)**. 770 of those have all
  seven axes `none`, i.e. impact exactly 0.0.
- 47.7% of ALL plan-v3 findings (8,632) have all seven axes `none` → impact 0.0. This is the
  single largest population in the corpus, not an outlier.

## What

Two changes, landing together under ONE impact-model version bump (plan-v4), because the bump closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort and we must not spend two.

### 1. Grade `divergent_implementation` by DIVERGENCE KIND (the approved fix)

Mirror the oracle-kind precedent exactly — replace the ordinal `none|low|medium|high` with a closed `Literal` set that separates a load-bearing divergence from a cosmetic one:

- `contradicts_reality` — the plan asserts something about the code/system that is FALSE
  (a named symbol/file/behavior does not exist as described, or exists differently).
  KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor.
- `omits_required_site` — the plan's scope/file list omits a site the change provably MUST
  touch, where omitting it changes runtime behavior or leaves the goal unmet. KEEPS the 0.85
  hard floor. (This is the class the G6 finding belongs to, and the ~90%-missed family.)
- `incomplete_enumeration` — a site is omitted but touching it is optional/cosmetic (docs,
  comments, a redundant mention); the goal still holds without it. Contributes
  DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, BELOW every blocking threshold, and NEVER floors — coached,
  not auto-blocked.
- `none` — does not apply.

`DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB` is pinned by test strictly below the lowest blocking `block_threshold` (0.60), exactly as `UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55` is.

**Required structural change in `impact_plan` (not merely implied by "mirror oracle-kind").** `impact_plan` today resolves every axis through `_SEV01`, which is keyed exclusively on `none|low|medium|high`. The new symbolic grades are absent from that map, so a schema-only change would silently score all three as `0.0` — the axis would stop firing entirely instead of flooring. The named changes, mirroring `ac_unverifiable` / `ORACLE_GRADE01` / `_ORACLE_FLOOR_GRADES` exactly:

1. Add `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01: dict[str | None, float]` mapping `none`→0.0,
   `incomplete_enumeration`→`DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB`, `contradicts_reality`→1.0,
   `omits_required_site`→1.0.
2. Add `_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES = ("contradicts_reality", "omits_required_site")`.
3. EXCLUDE `divergent_implementation` from the generic `_SEV01` contribution loop and append its
   `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` contribution instead — introduce `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES =
   ("ac_unverifiable", "divergent_implementation")` as the single name for "axes graded by a closed
   kind set", and drive both the contribution loop and the override loop off it so the two cannot
   drift apart.
4. EXCLUDE it from the `_PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES` `_SEV01.get(...) > 0.0` check, replacing that
   with a `_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES` membership test OR'd into `has_override`.

The hard floor stays applied LAST (after the detection amplifier), so a self-revealing divergence still lands at or above 0.85 rather than 0.85 x 0.8 = 0.68.

The three-way split is required, not cosmetic: the corpus shows a blunt widening would route 113 findings into the 0.85 floor at once (42 of 983 runs flipping PASS→BLOCK, 4.3%), and the LAST time this team widened a grade-blind hard floor it over-fired ~2x and had to be walked back (calibration 3: 35.5% of plan-v2 blocks were floor-driven, `ac_unverifiable` 48.9% of them, 56% mere specificity demands). `incomplete_enumeration` is the pressure-release valve that precedent proves is necessary.

### 2. ADR: reject high-cost LLM-based calibration assessments

ADR 0054. Records that calibration MUST be driven by the data the gate already produces during normal use (the version-tagged REVIEW_RESULT sidecar corpus) and explicitly REJECTS purpose-built LLM eval suites / bulk re-review runs as the calibration instrument, on cost grounds. Narrows ADR 0036's "A/B gate" to two permitted zero-marginal-LLM-cost forms: (a) offline replay of the existing corpus under the candidate value, and (b) dogfooding the candidate in normal use and observing field results. Supersedes ADR 0036's A/B clause only; the permissive-rollout invariant, version-tagging discipline, and no-pooling-across-versions rules all stand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0054-data-driven-calibration-no-costly-llm-assessments.md` exists, status
      Accepted, and states (a) the rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites + bulk re-review
      as calibration instruments, (b) the two permitted A/B forms (corpus replay, dogfood +
      observe), and (c) that it narrows ADR 0036's A/B clause while leaving the permissive
      invariant and version-segmentation intact. Verified: the file exists and
      `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" docs/adr/0054-*.md` returns >= 2.
- [ ] ADR 0036 carries a forward pointer to 0054 so a reader arriving at the older A/B clause
      is not misled. Verified:
      `grep -n "0054" docs/adr/0036-impact-model-rollout-and-calibration-cadence.md` matches.
- [ ] `PlanSeverityAttrs.divergent_implementation` is a closed `Literal["none",
      "contradicts_reality", "omits_required_site", "incomplete_enumeration"]` in
      `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`. Verified: a verification payload carrying
      `"low"` for that axis now FAILS to parse (pinned by test).
- [ ] `impact_plan` resolves the axis through the new `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01` map and NOT through
      `_SEV01` (per the four named structural changes above): it floors at 0.85 for
      `contradicts_reality` and `omits_required_site`, and returns
      `DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB` (never floors) for `incomplete_enumeration`.
      Verified: unit test asserting all three, plus a test pinning
      `DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB < 0.60` (the lowest blocking threshold in
      `criteria_routing.json`) so a future recalibration below it fails loudly.
- [ ] The target defect now BLOCKS: a regression test replays the exact recorded attributes of
      finding `fc347224733dccc6b` (validity 0.8889, G6 `block_threshold` 0.60) with
      `divergent_implementation="omits_required_site"` and asserts `pass3_decide` returns
      `decision == "block"` (priority 0.7556 >= 0.60).
- [ ] Both verifier prompts (`plan_review_verifier.md`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`)
      define all three grades with a worked example each, in the same shape as the
      `ac_unverifiable` oracle-kind block. Verified:
      `grep -c "omits_required_site" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md` returns
      at least 1 per file.
- [ ] The plan-review `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` is bumped to `plan-v4`, and legacy plan-v3/v2
      sidecars still read without error. Verified: `test_impact_model_versioning.py` pins
      updated and green.
- [ ] `enrich_operator_attested` handling is explicit and UNCONDITIONAL for the new grades: on a
      recorded operator attestation it MUST set `incomplete_enumeration` to `none` (automatic, not
      discretionary), and MUST NOT alter `contradicts_reality` or `omits_required_site` — they
      survive enrichment unchanged (mirroring the `broken_oracle` rule). Verified: a unit test
      asserting the exact post-attestation value of the axis for all three grades
      (`incomplete_enumeration` → `"none"`; each floor grade → itself).
- [ ] EVERY existing fixture that grades the axis on the retired ordinal ladder is migrated to
      the closed set — the Literal makes `"low"|"medium"|"high"` a parse error, so a missed
      fixture is a broken test, and one of them lives OUTSIDE tests/unit. Known sites:
      `tests/unit/test_a8e5_operator_attested_edge.py` (uses `"high"` as a surviving-other-axis
      fixture) and `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282` (uses `"high"` as
      the hard-override fixture that drives its negative-control BLOCK). Verified:
      `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/` returns no
      matches outside the grade-split suite's own rejection test, AND `pytest tests/unit
      tests/interfaces` is green.
- [ ] Every PROMPT-side consumer of the axis is updated, not just the two verifiers. The G7
      criterion prompt (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md`) explicitly "maps its severity
      onto the existing `divergent_implementation` plan axis" and must name WHICH grade a
      leaf/parent divergence maps to (outside-the-contract → `contradicts_reality`; omitted
      required part → `omits_required_site`; cosmetic → `incomplete_enumeration`) and state that
      low/medium/high are invalid. Verified:
      `grep -c "contradicts_reality" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md` >= 1. Its eval spec
      (`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml`) references the axis in PROSE only and
      asserts no grade value, so it needs no change — confirmed by
      `grep -n 'divergent' src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml` showing only comments.
- [ ] The verifier prompts' shared preamble no longer tells the LLM the axis uses the ordinal
      ladder (a pink-elephant that would fight the new grades): the "Grade each axis
      none|low|medium|high (EXCEPT ac_unverifiable...)" line names BOTH kind-graded axes.
      Verified: `grep -c "EXCEPT ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation"
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier*.md` returns 1 per file.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; every touched `src/rebar` file stays under the
      800-LOC module-size cap. Verified: `make lint typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` and the generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`
      describe the new grades. Verified: the guide is regenerated from the registry, not
      hand-edited.

## Out of scope (recorded, not done here)

- The `prod_impact` floor ("Fix 2") is REJECTED — it collides with the novelty convergence
  floor (`novelty_priority_floor = 0.4`). See the evaluation comment on this ticket.
- `undecomposed` fires on 0.07% of plan-v3 findings (12/18,085) while holding hard-override
  power — a likely dead axis. Filed separately.
baseline.summary: Grade divergent_implementation by divergence kind + ADR rejecting high-cost LLM calibration (plan-v4)

content.text: The plan-review Pass-1 thread fan-out loses the active gate session, so every agentic finder call dispatched to a worker thread fails before any LLM call and its findings are dropped — the agentic (tool-using) review tier is silently dead in the fan-out while the gate still returns PASS.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <epic-with-children>` (the gate wraps the run in a `gate_session()` on the main thread).
2. Observe stderr: `WARNING rebar.llm.plan_review.pass1: container bin [...] FAILED in 0.0s (RuntimeError)` on every run.
3. The container bin "fails" in 0.0s (before any LLM call); the agentic Pass-1 chunks fail the same way but are swallowed silently by `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` (`return []`).
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the agentic container/chunk finders run inside the gate session and produce findings.

- Actual: `assert_gated("agentic filesystem tools")` (runner.py:204, pre-LLM) raises `RuntimeError` in the worker because `_in_gate_session` (a `contextvars.ContextVar`) is NOT inherited by raw `ThreadPoolExecutor` threads (inherited by asyncio tasks only — documented in config.py). Findings are dropped; the gate degrades to single_turn + deterministic coverage and still returns PASS.
## Root Cause

`pass1.py` submits agentic `runner.run` work to a raw `ThreadPoolExecutor` at two sites (`_run_container` and `run_pass1`'s chunk pool) without propagating the calling thread's context. Proven by a no-LLM experiment + a RED test reproducing the exact warning.
## Fix

`_submit_ctx(ex, fn, *args)` submitting `ex.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, fn, *args)` (a FRESH context copy per task) at both fan-out sites. Regression test: `tests/interfaces/store/test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Agentic Pass-1 finder calls dispatched to fan-out worker threads observe the active gate session (no `assert_gated` RuntimeError).
- [ ] `rebar review-plan` on an epic logs no `container bin ... FAILED ... (RuntimeError)` and the container tier produces findings.
- [ ] Regression test `test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py` is RED before / GREEN after; existing gate-threading tests still pass.
- [ ] Fix lands via PR to main.

baseline.summary: plan-review Pass-1 thread fan-out loses gate session — agentic tier silently dead

baseline.description:
# Build-once artifact identity + fix the provenance hook's None-commit path

Restructure the release graph so the exact wheel and sdist are built once, tested
in a clean environment, and published byte-for-byte, and fix the Hatchling hook so
the wheel-from-sdist path never bakes `COMMIT = None`. (Readiness Finding 3 —
verified VALID against `release.yml`, `test.yml:455-477`, `hatch_build.py`,
`pyproject.toml`, `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py`.)

## Why

The release artifact and the CI-tested code are products of different build paths.
The `build` job runs `python -m build` + `twine check` (a static metadata check)
and uploads `dist/` with **no install or functional test** before `publish`
(`release.yml` build→publish). The clean-install CI job installs the source tree
with `pip install .` (`test.yml:470`) — which builds a wheel in place with `.git`
present — so it never exercises the sdist→wheel path. The only smoke test of the
real artifact is documented as **post-publication** (`docs/releasing.md`), by which
point PyPI immutability means recovery is yank + republish.

The provenance hook computes the commit via `git rev-parse` (`None` outside a git
tree) and `initialize` writes `_build_info.py` **unconditionally**
(`hatch_build.py`), with no preservation of an existing baked value and no failure
when the commit is absent. `python -m build`'s default builds an sdist first, then
builds the wheel **from the extracted sdist** — which has no `.git` — so the
published **wheel** carries `COMMIT = None` while only the sdist keeps the real SHA.
The one test that asserts a non-null baked SHA builds a `WheelBuilder` directly
against the checkout (`tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:202-227`), bypassing
the failing path, so the defect is uncaught by every existing gate.

## What

Adopt the pydantic / pip build-once pattern (build once → upload one artifact →
download it in a separate test job that installs with the index disabled and
exercises the public surface → download the same artifact in the publish job and
verify hashes before publishing, never rebuilding):

- **Build once**: produce wheel + sdist in one job, record SHA-256 for each, upload
  one named artifact bundle.
- **Test the exact wheel**: in a fresh job with no repo checkout on `PYTHONPATH`,
  install the wheel by filename and run concrete probes — `python -c "import rebar"`,
  `rebar --help`, `rebar-mcp --help`, load every packaged JSON schema
  (`python -c "import importlib.resources as r, json, rebar; [json.loads(f.read_text()) for f in r.files('rebar').rglob('*.json')]"`,
  asserting the count is non-zero and each parses), and
  `python -c "from rebar import _build_info; assert _build_info.COMMIT"` — asserting
  the embedded build info is present and non-null.
- **Test the exact sdist**: install from the downloaded sdist in a clean dir (no
  `.git`, `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` unset), run the same probes, and assert the installed
  package reports a **non-null** short SHA matching the release — this exercises the
  hook's preserve-existing path (step 2): the sdist shipped `_build_info.py` with the
  SHA baked during the release build, and the rebuild-from-sdist must keep it rather
  than overwrite with `None`. (This is exactly the real end-user `pip install <sdist>`
  path, so the test doubles as the provenance guarantee for sdist installs.)
- **Publish the same bytes**: `publish` `needs:` both test jobs, downloads the
  original bundle, recomputes and compares hashes against the recorded build hashes,
  and publishes without rebuilding.
- **Complete the F4 evidence handshake.** Finding 4 delegated the wheel/sdist digests
  to this story: the build-once job uploads an **`evidence-artifacts`** fragment
  (the wheel/sdist SHA-256 sums) that F4's consolidation step concatenates into
  `release-evidence.txt`, and this story **extends the `test_release_workflow_pins.py`
  test that Finding 4 introduces** (this story `depends_on` F4, so that file already
  exists by the time this lands) — adding to its check (f) an assertion that the
  `evidence-artifacts` fragment name + its wiring appear in `release.yml`.
- **Fix the hook — a four-step precedence (env var + preserve-existing + git).**
  `hatch_build.py`'s `initialize` resolves the commit in this order: (1)
  `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` env var if set (the release build sets it — see below); (2)
  else **preserve** an existing non-null `COMMIT` already in `_build_info.py` if one is
  present; (3) else `git rev-parse --short HEAD`; (4) else `None`. Step (2) is
  essential for **install-from-sdist**: `pip install <sdist>` rebuilds a wheel from the
  extracted tree (re-running this hook) with no `.git` and no env var, so without
  preserve-existing the SHA the sdist shipped would be overwritten with `None` — step
  (2) keeps it, so a published-sdist install retains provenance too (not just the
  release wheel). (Env-var injection alone — the earlier decision — fixes only the
  release-built wheel; preserve-existing is what carries the sdist's baked value
  through an install.)
- **Canonical commit format = SHORT SHA (existing convention).** `signing.py` is
  built around short SHAs throughout (`_gate_commit_sha` → `git rev-parse --short`;
  `gate_code_version` / `rebar_version_step` docstrings say `<short-sha>[-dirty]`), so
  to avoid a full-vs-short skew between the baked value and the live-git value in the
  same `rebar-version:` manifest line, the new code conforms to short SHAs rather than
  changing `signing.py`. The workflow sets `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` to the **short** SHA
  (`${GITHUB_SHA::7}`, matching git's default abbreviation); the git fallback stays
  `git rev-parse --short HEAD`; `signing.py` is unchanged. The existing provenance
  test's `[0-9a-f]{4,}` regex still matches.
- **Fail-fast scoped to the release context:** the hook raises (fails the build) only
  when `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` is set but empty/unresolvable — so a developer's plain
  `pip install .` (env var unset) still degrades gracefully to the git value and
  never breaks.
- **Verify env-var propagation (do not assume).** The fix depends on `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT`
  surviving from the workflow shell through `python -m build` into the Hatchling
  `initialize` hook when the wheel is built from the extracted sdist. (Env vars
  propagate to the build backend subprocess via inherited `os.environ` **regardless of
  PEP 517 isolation** — isolation governs build *dependencies*, not the environment —
  so this is not coupled to F4's `--no-isolation` choice.) The plan still **proves**
  it with a test that runs `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=<short-hex> python -m build` and asserts
  the resulting **wheel** (built from the extracted sdist) carries that exact short
  SHA — rather than asserting propagation as settled fact.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — build-once + two artifact-test jobs + hash-gated
  publish (coordinate with Findings 1 and 4, which also edit this file).
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — optionally add a wheel/sdist artifact probe to
  regular CI so the defect is caught pre-release, not only in the release run.
- `hatch_build.py` — four-step precedence: `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` env var (short SHA) →
  preserve an existing non-null `COMMIT` in `_build_info.py` (install-from-sdist) →
  `git rev-parse --short HEAD` → `None`; fail only when the env var is set but
  empty/unresolvable (release-context fail-fast; unset = graceful preserve/git fallback
  for sdist + dev installs).
- `src/rebar/signing.py` — **in scope to confirm only** (no change expected): its
  short-SHA `_gate_commit_sha` path already matches the chosen canonical short format,
  so the baked value and the live-git value stay consistent in `gate_code_version()`
  output regardless of install type.
- `hatch_build.py` (`initialize`) — add `src/rebar/_build_info.py` to
  `build_data['force_include']` so the generated (git-ignored) file is shipped in the
  **sdist** as well as the wheel. (Do NOT add `artifacts=` to the sdist pyproject
  target — Hatchling's sdist builder uses `include`/`exclude` only and silently ignores
  `artifacts`, a wheel-only key; the hook's `force_include` works for both targets.)
  Without this the sdist never contains the baked SHA and the preserve-existing path
  has nothing to preserve.
- `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py` — add coverage for the wheel-from-sdist
  path (the currently-untested `COMMIT = None` case).
- `docs/releasing.md` — **section ownership:** this story owns the "Build-once"
  section, AND rewrites the existing **"Post-release smoke test"** section, which F1's
  trigger change + this story's pre-publication artifact tests make obsolete (the
  smoke test moves from post-publication to the pre-publish wheel/sdist test jobs).
  (Finding 1 owns "Release-source authorization" + the existing tag→PyPI procedure /
  Hard-rules sections; Finding 4 owns "Pinning".)
- Out of scope: byte-for-byte reproducible builds (timestamps/backend determinism)
  beyond the SHA-256 identity check through the pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release builds artifacts once and uploads a single named bundle containing
  the wheel, the sdist, and a `SHA256SUMS` file recording their digests; `publish`
  downloads that same bundle and runs `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (failing on any
  mismatch) before publishing — no rebuild occurs in `publish`.
- [ ] A wheel-test job installs the exact wheel by filename with no source checkout
  on the path and runs concrete probes — `python -c "import rebar"`, `rebar --help`,
  `rebar-mcp --help`, load every packaged JSON schema via `importlib.resources`
  (count non-zero, each parses), and a non-null-`COMMIT` assert
  (the wheel install does not re-run the hook, so it keeps its baked SHA). An
  sdist-test job installs from the sdist in a clean dir (`REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` unset, no
  `.git`) and also asserts a non-null `COMMIT` — proving the hook's preserve-existing
  step keeps the sdist's shipped SHA through the rebuild rather than overwriting it
  with `None`.
- [ ] The shipped wheel carries a non-null **short** source commit matching the
  release SHA — the workflow sets `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=${GITHUB_SHA::7}` before
  `python -m build`, and a test (added to `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py`,
  which currently only covers the direct-`WheelBuilder` path) asserts the wheel built
  via the default sdist→wheel path contains `COMMIT` equal to that short SHA (today
  this path yields `COMMIT = None`). The baked value and `signing.py`'s live-git
  value share the short format, so `gate_code_version()` is consistent across install
  types. The hook fails the build only when `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` is set but
  unresolvable (release context); an unset env var falls back to git (dev
  `pip install .` unaffected). **Both branches are pinned by concrete tests** in
  `tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py`: (a) `test_hook_fails_when_rebar_build_commit_empty`
  runs `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT="" python -m build` (env var set-but-empty) in a temp copy of the
  tree and asserts the build exits non-zero (the release-context fail-fast); and (b)
  `test_hook_falls_back_to_git_when_env_unset` builds with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` unset in a
  git checkout and asserts the wheel carries the `git rev-parse --short HEAD` value (graceful
  dev fallback, no failure). These make the fail-fast/fallback contract codebase-verifiable,
  not merely asserted in prose.
- [ ] The build-once job uploads an `evidence-artifacts` fragment (wheel/sdist SHA-256
  sums) consumed by F4's evidence-consolidation step, and the `test_release_workflow_pins.py`
  test introduced by Finding 4 (available since this story `depends_on` F4) has its
  check (f) extended to assert that fragment's name + wiring appear in `release.yml`.
- [ ] **ACs 1 and 2 are made in-session-verifiable by static workflow checks** (so a
  missing hash-gate or a misspelled probe fails `make test`, not only a live release run).
  `test_release_workflow_pins.py` gains: **(g)** the `publish` job contains a
  `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` step AND does not rebuild (no `python -m build` in `publish`);
  **(h)** a wheel-test job and an sdist-test job exist, each `needs:` the build-once job,
  and each contains the named probe commands from AC 2 — the wheel-test job asserts
  `import rebar`, `rebar --help`, `rebar-mcp --help`, the packaged-JSON-schema load, and
  `from rebar import _build_info; assert _build_info.COMMIT`; the sdist-test job runs the
  same probes in a clean dir with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` unset and asserts a non-null
  `_build_info.COMMIT`. **(i)** the build-once job produces a single named bundle
  containing the wheel, the sdist, and a `SHA256SUMS` file. These are parsed/grep assertions
  over `release.yml` (a static YAML check, analogous to F4's checks (c)–(h)), so ACs 1 and 2
  are codebase-verifiable in-session.
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` describes the build-once → test → publish-same-bytes flow,
  and the existing "Post-release smoke test" section is rewritten to reflect that the
  smoke test now runs pre-publication (against the exact wheel/sdist) rather than
  post-publication.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass, and the change lands via the
  Gerrit two-vote gate.
baseline.summary: Build-once artifact identity + fix the provenance hook's None-commit path

content.text: Map the local `idea` status to the Jira `IDEA` status across all reconciler status
maps, with a parity test, and document the Jira-side prerequisites.
## Why
For `idea` to sync, the reconciler must translate it to Jira `IDEA` outbound and
back inbound. rebar keeps several hand-maintained status maps that must all agree;
missing one causes a preflight abort or a silent mistranslation. `idea ↔ IDEA` is a
unique (injective) mapping, so no `rebar-status:` annotation label is needed and no
terminal-set change is required.
## Operator prerequisite + deployment sequencing (LOAD-BEARING)
Jira statuses are workflow-gated: `IDEA` must exist as a status in the target Jira
project's workflow WITH transitions into it (from the initial status, so a synced
idea can converge) and out of it (to To Do for promote, to Done for reject). This
is a Jira-admin action outside the codebase.
Sequencing risk: today a status the Jira workflow cannot reach makes the reconciler
pass abort (preflight `StatusMappingError`, or a `RuntimeError` from
`transition_issue_by_name`) — so shipping `idea` code before `IDEA` is provisioned
in Jira would abort reconciler passes. Mitigate by EITHER (a) provisioning the Jira
`IDEA` workflow status + transitions before/atomically-with merging this story, OR
(b) landing the reconciler transition-failure isolation follow-up (linked
`discovered_from` this epic) first, so a missing `IDEA` transition degrades to a
reported per-mutation failure instead of aborting the whole pass. The
create-drops-status convergence quirk (a newly-synced idea is born in the Jira
default status and reaches `IDEA` on a later pass) is accepted and documented, not
code-fixed here.
## What
- Add `idea → "IDEA"` to `config.local_to_jira_status`.
- Add `"IDEA" → idea` to `config.jira_to_local_status`.
- Add `"IDEA" → idea` to `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` (kept in lock-step
with the config reverse map by the parity test).
- Add `idea → "IDEA"` to `jira_fields._LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`.
- Add `idea → "IDEA"` to `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`.
- Extend the parity test to assert the `idea ↔ IDEA` entries.
- Verify/update the local-status vocabulary reference in `inbound_translate.py`
(`_LOCAL_STATUS_VALUES` and the `_jira_status_to_local` default path) so `idea`
is a recognized local status there too.
- Document the operator prerequisite (the Jira workflow must have an `IDEA` status
with transitions into and out of it), the deployment-sequencing requirement
(Jira provisioned first, or the reconciler-isolation follow-up landed first), and
the create-drops-status convergence quirk, in a reconciler/Jira setup doc that
CLAUDE.md can cross-reference.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — both direction maps.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/jira_fields.py` — `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_fields.py` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` — local-status
vocabulary reference.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py` — parity assertion.
- The reconciler/Jira setup doc — prerequisite + sequencing + convergence-quirk.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `config.local_to_jira_status["idea"]` equals `"IDEA"`.
- [ ] `config.jira_to_local_status["IDEA"]` equals `"idea"`.
- [ ] `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS["IDEA"]` equals `"idea"`.
- [ ] `jira_fields._LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA["idea"]` equals `"IDEA"`.
- [ ] `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS["idea"]` equals `"IDEA"`.
- [ ] The parity test asserts `config.jira_to_local_status` matches
`inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` including the `IDEA` entry.
- [ ] An outbound status translation of a local `idea` ticket yields Jira `IDEA`
(test-verified).
- [ ] An inbound translation of Jira `IDEA` yields local `idea` (test-verified).
- [ ] The status-mapping preflight does not abort on a local `idea` status.
- [ ] `inbound_translate` recognizes `idea` as a local status (no fallback to
`open` for a Jira `IDEA` inbound).
- [ ] The reconciler/Jira setup doc records the Jira-admin prerequisite (add `IDEA`
status + transitions any→IDEA and IDEA→Done in the project workflow).
- [ ] The doc records the deployment-sequencing requirement (provision Jira `IDEA`
before merging, or land the reconciler-isolation follow-up first).
- [ ] The doc records the create-drops-status convergence quirk.
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.

baseline.summary: Map local 'idea' status to Jira IDEA across reconciler maps

# Bedrock has no rebar-configured retry or timeout envelope, so `llm_retry_max_attempts` and `timeout_s` silently do not apply

## Context / Problem

The epic's `first_class = full fidelity` premise implies equivalent retry and timeout behaviour per transport. On the Bedrock path that is an **unmet intention, not a landed property**, and the gap is silent: the two knobs an operator would reach for have no effect.

`src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:88` is `return BedrockProvider(region_name=region)`. Its own docstring says so explicitly: "No custom client/transport is opened here (unlike the retrying Anthropic path)." There is no `botocore.config.Config(retries=...)`, no `"adaptive"` retry mode, and no `aws_read_timeout` anywhere under `src/rebar/llm/`. The tenacity envelope and `RetryConfig` live only in `anthropic_model.py:114-150`.

Consequences, stated precisely:

* Bedrock's transient-fault handling is **botocore's stock client defaults**. Those DO retry
  throttling and transient 5xx, so this is not "no retries at all" — it is retries that rebar neither
  configures nor can observe.
* `llm_retry_max_attempts` and `timeout_s` do NOT reach the Bedrock transport. An operator tuning them
  against a Bedrock throttle is tuning a knob wired to nothing, with no error to tell them.
* The divergence is invisible in tests: the Anthropic path's retry envelope is what the existing
  retry tests exercise, so they pass while saying nothing about Bedrock.

Discovered while writing the production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], whose original plan claimed "the existing tenacity transport retry absorbs transient faults". That claim was false on this path and was corrected in the plan rather than carried forward. The cutover deliberately does NOT fix this — closing it means changing the provider builder, which belongs in a `src/` ticket rather than inside a production cutover — and instead writes the actual posture into the runbook so an operator debugging a throttle is not hunting a retry envelope that does not exist.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py` — the provider builder, where a `botocore.config.Config` would be
  threaded in.
- whatever config seam carries `llm_retry_max_attempts` / `timeout_s` to a transport, so the Bedrock
  path reads the same values as the Anthropic path rather than ignoring them.

## Approach (not yet designed — this ticket is FILED, not planned)

Deliberately left open. The obvious shape is to construct a `botocore.config.Config` from the same config values the Anthropic path consumes and pass it into `BedrockProvider`, but the mapping is not one-to-one and needs design: botocore's `retries={"max_attempts": N, "mode": ...}` counts attempts differently from tenacity's stop condition, and botocore exposes `connect_timeout`/`read_timeout` rather than a single `timeout_s`. Whether "parity" means identical numbers or identical observable behaviour is the design question, and picking the wrong one produces a false claim of fidelity — which is the exact failure this ticket exists to correct.

## Testing

The oracle must not be satisfiable by the Anthropic path. It has to assert that a Bedrock provider built through `build_bedrock_provider` carries the configured retry/timeout values — i.e. inspect the constructed client's config rather than the rebar-side setting — and must FAIL if the builder reverts to a bare `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_bedrock_provider` threads a `botocore.config.Config` carrying retry and timeout settings
      derived from the same config values the Anthropic path uses, so `llm_retry_max_attempts` and
      `timeout_s` are honoured on Bedrock rather than ignored.
- [ ] the retry-count and timeout SEMANTICS are documented where they are set, stating how the
      configured value maps onto botocore's attempt counting and onto connect vs read timeouts, so
      "parity" names a defined behaviour rather than a matching integer.
- [ ] a test asserts the constructed Bedrock client's config carries the configured values, and FAILS
      if the builder is reverted to `BedrockProvider(region_name=region)` with no config. Verify this
      by MUTATING the builder back and observing the test go RED.
- [ ] the runbook statement added by [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] — that botocore stock defaults apply
      and the two knobs do not reach Bedrock — is updated to describe the new behaviour, so the
      operator-facing text does not outlive the defect it describes.
baseline.summary: Bedrock ignores llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout_s: no botocore retry envelope

# S2 — Auth framework (composite audience choke point) + Resource-Server wiring + static verifier

## Why
This story delivers the authentication admission core — the provider-agnostic seam every verifier
plugs into, and the single audience/fail-closed choke point the whole security model rests on —
plus the first (dependency-free) verifier so the path is exercisable locally: the static bearer
token (the "PAT" half of the confirmed floor).

## What
- Extend the flat `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']` (from S1) with flat scalar auth keys:
  `auth_enabled` (bool, default false), `auth_strategies` (comma-separated → ordered list),
  `auth_issuer_url` (str), `auth_resource_server_url` (str — the SINGLE resource identifier),
  `auth_required_scopes` (comma-separated → list), and `auth_static_tokens_file` (str path). Each is
  one field + one flat coercer entry; register in `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json` and regenerate
  `docs/mcp-reference.md`/`docs/env-vars.md`. There is **one** `auth_resource_server_url` for the
  whole server: it is what the RFC 9728 PRM advertises AND the audience every verifier is checked
  against — never a separate per-verifier audience. Per-verifier params (S3–S6) are additional flat
  keys those stories add; the flat schema holds **one instance per strategy type** (for multiple
  issuers, use the custom verifier) — documented in S7.
- New module `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`:
  - A `CompositeTokenVerifier` that is the **single audience + fail-closed choke point**. It tries
    each active verifier in order; a verifier returning an `AccessToken` is a candidate; a verifier
    returning `None` means "not my token" → try next; a verifier that **raises** is logged and
    treated as **non-acceptance** (never acceptance) → try next. For any candidate token the
    composite then **rejects unless `token.resource` is present AND equals `auth_resource_server_url`**
    (RFC 8707) — this re-check is independent of the sub-verifier, so no verifier (including a buggy
    or malicious custom one that returns `resource=None`) can bypass audience validation. If no
    verifier yields a valid, audience-matching token, the request is denied (401). An exception never
    yields acceptance.
  - A config→verifier **factory** built from `auth_strategies`, whose value vocabulary is the CLOSED
    set `static | jwt | introspection | proxy | custom`. An unrecognized entry is a **hard startup
    error**; `auth_enabled=true` producing an **empty** composite is a hard startup error; and
    `auth_enabled` with `transport=http` where no verifier is wired **refuses to start** (never a
    silent open endpoint).
  - The **`StaticBearerVerifier`**: reads the secrets file (below), stores only SHA-256 digests,
    compares with `hmac.compare_digest`, assigns each token's `client_id`/`scopes`, and stamps every
    returned `AccessToken` with `resource=auth_resource_server_url` so it passes the composite check.
- Wire it in `build_server`: when `auth_enabled`, pass `token_verifier=CompositeTokenVerifier(…)` and
  `auth=AuthSettings(issuer_url=auth_issuer_url, resource_server_url=auth_resource_server_url,
  required_scopes=auth_required_scopes)` to `FastMCP`, so the SDK serves the RFC 9728 PRM (a SINGLE
  `authorization_servers` entry derived from `issuer_url`) and emits 401 + `WWW-Authenticate`.
  Resolve S1's unauthenticated-HTTP guard against the real `auth_enabled`.
- **No-log redaction:** add a redaction helper used on every auth error/log path (composite raise
  handler, verifier errors) so no token/secret substring is ever emitted.

**Static-token secrets format (parsed by the verifier, NOT the TOML coercer).** The per-token
records live in the JSON/TOML file named by `auth_static_tokens_file`, parsed by the
`StaticBearerVerifier` at load — outside the flat coercer (which cannot hold variable-length records).
Each record supplies `client_id`, `scopes` (list), and the secret as EXACTLY ONE of: `token_env`
(the NAME of an env var holding the plaintext — preferred; nothing secret in the file), or
`token_sha256` (a precomputed lowercase SHA-256 hex digest, safe ONLY for a high-entropy token). The
verifier resolves plaintext from `token_env` and stores only its SHA-256; a record embedding a
plaintext literal, or missing both fields, is rejected at startup. Static tokens MUST be ≥128-bit
random; provide a `rebar` helper/documented one-liner to generate one (S7 documents the entropy
requirement and that static tokens are non-expiring, so `token_env` is preferred).

## Approach & rationale
Model the framework on the SDK's own `TokenVerifier`/`AuthSettings` seam (the blessed extension
point the `simple-auth` example uses), and make the composite the ONE place audience + fail-closed
are enforced, because the SDK's `BearerAuthBackend` never inspects `.resource` (grounded against
mcp 1.28.1) — there is no backstop behind the verifier. Keep config flat to fit `coerce_sparse`. A
composite (not a single selected strategy) lets a deployment accept static PAT for CI AND OIDC JWTs
for humans at once (the GitHub model). Static bearer first because it needs no external IdP, making
the end-to-end 401/200/403 path locally verifiable.

## Scope
The auth framework (composite choke point + factory + flat config + PRM/401 wiring + redaction) and
the **static** verifier only. JWKS/JWT (S3), introspection (S4), trusted-proxy (S5), custom (S6)
register additional verifiers on this seam. Subset of the epic. Depends on S1.

## Security
Boundary-crossing. Enforced here: the composite audience re-check (every accepted token's
`resource` == `auth_resource_server_url`); fail-closed (raise = non-acceptance, misconfig/unknown-
strategy/empty-composite/no-verifier-over-HTTP = refuse start, no verifier accepting = 401);
constant-time static compare; only SHA-256 digests held (no plaintext, no plaintext in config);
tokens/secrets never logged (redaction + test); a positive `expires_at` is set where a token has one
(never 0, which the SDK treats as no-expiry). Static tokens are dev/internal-grade, ≥128-bit, and
non-expiring (documented in S7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The flat `auth_enabled`/`auth_strategies`/`auth_issuer_url`/`auth_resource_server_url`/
      `auth_required_scopes`/`auth_static_tokens_file` keys exist as `McpConfig` fields + flat
      coercer entries, appear in `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json`, and the regenerated reference docs +
      `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` pass (observable: manifest drift test green; a round-trip
      test reads each key from TOML and from its env var).
- [ ] Integration test (tier: integration — httpx `ASGITransport` against the SDK's Streamable-HTTP
      ASGI entrypoint) asserts, with static auth enabled: unauthenticated → **401** + a
      `WWW-Authenticate` header carrying the RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` URL (observable oracle:
      status + header value).
- [ ] Integration test asserts the PRM is served at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/…` with a
      single `authorization_servers` entry (observable oracle: HTTP 200 + JSON field).
- [ ] Integration test asserts: valid static token → **200**; unknown/invalid token → 401; a
      principal lacking a `required_scope` → **403**; and a token whose `resource` ≠
      `auth_resource_server_url` (injected via a stub verifier in the composite) → 401 at the
      composite regardless of the sub-verifier (negative controls included).
- [ ] Integration test asserts session-id replay cannot hijack a principal: an `Mcp-Session-Id`
      obtained by one authenticated client, replayed by a DIFFERENT client that presents no valid
      token of its own, is NEVER served in the first principal's authenticated context (single
      observable oracle: the replayed request does not return the original principal's authorized
      access — it is denied 401 / treated as unauthenticated).
- [ ] Unit test asserts the composite contract: `None` → try next; an `AccessToken` with matching
      `resource` → accept; a verifier that **raises** → logged, non-acceptance, request denied (no
      swallow-to-accept), with a control where a raising verifier ordered after an accepting one is
      never consulted.
- [ ] Unit test asserts fail-closed startup: an unknown `auth_strategies` entry, an empty composite
      with `auth_enabled=true`, and `auth_enabled` + `transport=http` with no verifier wired each
      refuse to start (observable oracle: startup raises a clear message).
- [ ] Unit test asserts `StaticBearerVerifier` holds only SHA-256 digests (not plaintext), uses a
      constant-time compare, stamps `resource=auth_resource_server_url`, and rejects a secrets-file
      record with a plaintext literal or missing both `token_env`/`token_sha256`.
- [ ] Unit test asserts no token/secret substring appears in emitted logs across the composite
      raise-handler and a verifier error path (observable oracle: captured logs contain neither the
      token nor the secret).
- [ ] With `auth_enabled=false`, an integration test (with `allow_unauthenticated_http=true`) asserts
      no auth middleware: a no-token HTTP request gets a normal MCP response (not 401), and the stdio
      suite `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` still passes unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive; auth off by default. Only ADDS flat scalar keys to the existing flat `McpConfig`/
`_SECTIONS['mcp']` — no change to the coercer architecture, stdio, or the existing tools. Depends on
S1's transport + SDK pin.
baseline.summary: S2 — Auth framework + Resource-Server wiring + static-bearer verifier

## Summary
Switch the rebar Gerrit project submit type from `merge if necessary` to **Fast Forward Only** so a change is submittable only when built on the current `main` tip. When main advances, the change goes non-submittable until rebased/re-merged onto the tip; that rebase drops the Verified vote (copyCondition excludes TRIVIAL_REBASE) and re-runs CI on the exact tree that lands — closing the stale-base-merge gap (R5). Path C from the merge-queue design; Zuul ruled out on cost.

## What
- `infra/gerrit/project.config`: `[submit] action = fast forward only` (+ corrected comment)
- `docs/adr/0040-main-fast-forward-only-submit.md` (amends ADR-0020/0025; corrects ADR-0025's FFO claim)
- Agent-facing landing semantics in CLAUDE.md + CONTRIBUTING.md (rebase-to-tip to submit)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Submit type is Fast Forward Only in project.config; config-check passes
- [ ] ADR-0040 documents R5 mechanism + corrects ADR-0025 + records R4 treadmill tradeoff
- [ ] CLAUDE.md/CONTRIBUTING.md tell agents a change must be on current main tip to submit
- [ ] Feature-branch --no-ff merge-back remains compatible (verified via Gerrit docs)
- [ ] Operator apply step (setup-project.sh) flagged; refs/meta/config is detect-only
baseline.summary: Adopt Fast Forward Only submit type on main (ADR-0040) — no stale/untested tree can land (R5)
