## What
The LLM runner sends no sampling temperature (`runner.py` model_settings carried only cache
flags, max_tokens, timeout), so every review call — including the Pass-2 finding VERIFIER — runs
at the provider default temperature with no seed. The verifier's narrow yes/no `binary` +
`severity_attributes` are the ONLY inputs to the kernel's `priority = validity x impact`, so
re-sampling them on an identical input flips impact/validity and therefore the block/advisory
decision. Proven from stored client sidecars: the same finding, same plan, no edits, scored
`impact 0.85 / priority 0.74 / BLOCK` on one run and `impact 0.0 / priority 0.0 / advisory` on
the next. Upstream review-code report §2.

## Approach
Add a `temperature` field to `LLMConfig` (default None = provider default, byte-unchanged; env
`REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE`). Apply it in the runner's `model_settings`, with a per-request
`RunRequest.config.temperature` override winning over the runner cfg (mirrors the existing
max_tokens seam). Add a per-step `with: temperature` input honored in `workflow/runs.py`
(the v3 step schema is closed; `with` is the open extension, exactly like `step_budget_per_item`).
Pin `temperature: 0` (greedy) on the Pass-2 verify steps: code-review.yaml verify, plan-review.yaml
BOTH verify-branch arms, and the hand-built plan-review Pass-2 novelty sub-call. This is a
REPRODUCIBILITY floor for gate integrity, not a correctness fix.

## Scope / files
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `temperature` field + from_env + widen `_llm_float` default to
  `float | None`.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — apply temperature to model_settings.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` — honor `with: temperature`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml`, `plan-review.yaml` — `temperature: 0` on verify.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — greedy on the Pass-2 novelty sub-call.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py` — new.

## Acceptance criteria
- `LLMConfig().temperature is None`; `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE=0` -> 0.0; unparseable -> None.
- Runner omits `temperature` from model_settings when None (unchanged default); sets it when
  configured; a per-request config.temperature overrides the runner cfg.
- A workflow step with `with: {temperature: 0}` builds its RunRequest under cfg.temperature == 0.
- lint, typecheck, and the workflow/config/verify suites stay green.

## Out of scope
The single-pass completion-verifier gate (not four-pass Pass-2) is a natural sibling but left for a
follow-up. Correctness of narrow verification questions (a temperature-sweep robustness eval) is a
separate improvement.
baseline.summary: Pass-2 verifier samples at provider-default temperature; re-runs flip block/advisory

content.text: ## Summary

The mkdir leg of the unified write lock (`.ticket-write.lock.d`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`) has **no stale-lock reclamation**. The fcntl leg (`.ticket-write.lock`) is kernel-backed and auto-released when the holder dies, but `_acquire_mkdir` only polls `os.mkdir` until the deadline — so a `.ticket-write.lock.d` orphaned by a writer/push that was SIGKILLed mid-commit persists forever and makes **every subsequent write block the full lock budget (~60s) and then fail** with `LockTimeout`.

Discovered while root-causing `slim-fetch-ledge` (rebar show empty-stdout-under-contention). That P1 was fixed on the READ side (the read-path reconverge now waits only ~2s for the lock, commit 9943f1e1), so reads are immune to a stale mkdir lock. WRITES remain affected and are tracked here separately.
## Reproduction Steps
1. In an initialized store, simulate an orphaned lock: `mkdir .tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d` (no live holder).
2. Run any write, e.g. `rebar comment <id> "x"`.
3. Observe it hangs ~60s (the write lock budget = timeout x attempts) then fails with `LockTimeout`, even though no process holds the lock.
- **Expected:** a provably-stale mkdir lock (no live owner) is reclaimed so writes proceed promptly.
- **Actual:** the orphaned dir blocks every write for the full budget, then the write fails.
## Notes on a safe fix
- The fcntl leg is the real mutual-exclusion primitive (acquired first in `acquire`). The mkdir leg is a secondary dual-window/bash-interop guard.

- Reclamation must be conservative — incorrectly removing a live lock breaks mutual exclusion and can corrupt the store. Options: record the owner PID (and host/boot id) inside the lock dir on acquire and reclaim only when that PID is provably dead; and/or gate reclamation on the fact that the caller already holds the fcntl leg (safe only once the bash write core / dual_window is fully retired — verify before relying on it).

- macOS lacks util-linux `flock(1)`, so historically bash could hold ONLY the mkdir leg there ("stiff-mop-lane" gap); confirm the bash write core is fully retired before treating "we hold fcntl" as proof the mkdir dir is stale.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A provably-stale `.ticket-write.lock.d` (no live owning process) is reclaimed so a write proceeds without waiting the full lock budget.
- [ ] A LIVE lock holder is never reclaimed — mutual exclusion is preserved (concurrency test under contention).
- [ ] A regression test: with an orphaned mkdir lock (dead/absent owner), a write completes promptly instead of hanging ~60s then failing.
- [ ] Reclamation is documented in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` alongside the dual-window rule.

baseline.summary: mkdir write-lock leg (.ticket-write.lock.d) has no stale-lock reclamation; orphaned dir blocks all writes

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The outbound differ is the last core module that *compares* in vendor shape.
`outbound_differ.py:39-41` imports `_diff_fields`, `_extract_jira_field`, `_assignee_matches`,
and `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` from `adapters.jira.outbound_fields`; the update path
(`_compute_outbound_update_mutation`, call at `outbound_differ.py:732`) delegates to
`_diff_fields` (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:369-618`), which maps local→Jira and then
reads raw vendor snapshot keys (`fields.status.name`, `assignee.accountId`,
`parent.key`, ADF `description`). These helpers have no ADR 0035 §(d)-legal home: on the
Backend port they would force every backend to consume Jira snapshot dicts (exactly what plan
review blocked on the prior attempt, ticket 97f2 / Gerrit change 920); left in core they keep
the core vendor-shaped. Meanwhile the *inbound* differ already diffs canonically — it maps the
vendor payload to local shape via the injected `InboundMapper` before comparing
(`inbound_differ.py:159`). This asymmetry is the design flaw blocking epic bbf1 AC3.

## Approach

Bring the outbound update path to parity with the inbound differ: **diff in canonical shape;
vendor shapes cross core only as opaque payloads produced/consumed by port calls at the
boundaries.**

1. `run_differs.py` additionally passes `inbound_mapper=backend.inbound` to
   `compute_outbound_mutations` (the backend object is already in scope there —
   `run_differs.py:481-495` currently passes `outbound_mapper=backend.outbound`).
2. `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` canonicalizes the snapshot entry with
   `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local(jira_snapshot[jira_key])` (mirroring
   `inbound_differ.py:159`) and compares the local ticket against the canonical remote using
   new **neutral** field-comparison helpers in core (local vocabulary only).
3. The changed-field set is computed in local field names; the vendor update payload is built
   at the emission boundary by a NEW `OutboundMapper` method
   `map_fields_to_remote(local_fields: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]`: it takes exactly
   the changed local-name→local-value subset and returns the vendor-shaped payload for those
   fields only (the Jira implementation delegates to the same
   `_map_local_to_jira_fields` machinery over the partial dict — a pure canonical→vendor
   translation, §(d)-legal). The create path keeps using the whole-ticket
   `map_local_to_remote` (`outbound_differ.py:632`). Rejected mechanisms: filtering a
   full `map_local_to_remote(ticket)` result by the changed fields' vendor names — that
   requires a local→vendor field-name map in core (the exact knowledge the seam forbids) and
   risks emitting mapper defaults for untouched fields; and a synthetic partial-ticket into
   `map_local_to_remote` — its contract expects a full ticket and may default absent fields.
   `OutboundMutation.fields` therefore stays vendor-shaped and the entire apply pipeline is
   untouched (`batch_dispatch.py:107-110`, `dispatch_one.py:442-514` and the unpacked
   `client.update_issue(issue_key, **fields)` at `dispatch_one.py:602`).
4. Widen the Jira `InboundMapper` output (translation only, implemented in the vendor mapper
   `inbound_fields.py:141-184` / delegate `adapters/jira/backend.py:43-47`) with three NEW,
   exactly-named canonical keys, documented on the `InboundMapper` Protocol docstring in
   `_backend.py` (the `map_remote_to_local` signature is unchanged — `dict[str, Any]` in/out;
   today's scalar `assignee` string stays for existing consumers):
   - `assignee_identity: dict` with fixed keys `{"display": str|None, "email": str|None,
     "account_id": str|None}` — `account_id` is the backend's stable account identifier
     (Jira: `accountId`; a GitHub backend would map its login/node id). Core replaces the
     vendor shape-tolerant `_assignee_matches` (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:237-261`)
     with neutral membership matching (local value ∈ the non-None identity values),
     preserving the both-empty match (`outbound_fields.py:251-252`).
   - `remote_parent_id: str|None` (Jira: `fields.parent.key`) — a bare remote id string,
     already port vocabulary per `RemoteRef`. Core compares the BindingStore-resolved
     expected remote key against it, replacing `outbound_fields.py:531-558`.
   - `reporter_identity: dict` (same fixed shape as `assignee_identity`) for the outbound
     one-way reporter diff (`outbound_fields.py:346-366` and `:617`).
4b. **The assignee resolver and the `_assignee_is_account_id` sentinel keep their exact
   payload contract, re-homed §(d)-legally.** Today `_diff_fields` runs the assignee
   resolver against the raw Jira assignee dict and injects
   `changed["_assignee_is_account_id"] = True` on the accountId fast-path
   (`outbound_fields.py:471-530`, sentinel at `:508-513`), which `dispatch_one.py:488` pops
   before submit. In the new flow, `OutboundMapper` gains
   `resolve_assignee(local_value: str, remote_identity: dict | None) ->
   tuple[Any, bool, bool]` — parameterized ONLY on the canonical `assignee_identity` shape
   above (never on `jira_fields`), returning `(payload_value, authoritative,
   is_account_id)`, the same 3-state contract as today's resolver: when
   `authoritative=False` (no client / transient resolution error) the neutral differ falls
   through to legacy string-match behavior exactly as `outbound_fields.py:488-491` does now.
   The neutral differ decides *whether* assignee changed by membership matching, then calls
   `resolve_assignee` at emission and sets the same `_assignee_is_account_id` sentinel key
   in the payload from the returned flag — so the 264f accountId fast-path, the 9b94
   unmappable→unassign soft-fail, the non-authoritative fallback, and `dispatch_one.py:488`
   are all byte-identical downstream.
4c. **Labels canonicalize here too.** `_diff_labels` (`outbound_differ.py:755`) today reads
   the raw `jira_fields.get("labels")`. The Jira `map_remote_to_local` output gains
   `labels: list[str]` (a pass-through translation of `fields.labels`), and `_diff_labels`
   consumes the canonical list; identity-label exclusion semantics are unchanged (the
   rebar-id back-pointer labels are already handled by the existing convention logic).
5. Description parity: compare the port-sanitized local text
   (`FieldSanitizer.sanitize_description`) against the mapper-decoded remote text, preserving
   the ADF-fit + rstrip semantics of `outbound_fields.py:566-583`.
6. Core policies stay in core, expressed on local field names: issuetype excluded on update
   (today `outbound_fields.py:449-459`; the inbound differ already excludes `ticket_type`)
   and inbound-directionality suppression (today `outbound_fields.py:467-470`).
7. **The arbitration baseline is canonicalized at read time, storage unchanged.** The
   per-binding baseline is *written* from raw remote snapshot entries and stored in vendor
   field names/shapes (`binding_store.py:374` filters to `_BASELINE_FIELDS`,
   `binding_store.py:71`; writers pass `prev_snapshot[jira_key]` / `curr_snapshot[jira_key]`
   at `binding_store.py:390`, `reconcile.py:520`, `apply_inbound_records.py:212`). Per the
   canonical-comparison principle it is a stored remote payload: it stays vendor-shaped at
   rest (opaque; NO data migration, writers untouched), and the outbound differ's
   suppression/conflict path applies `inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` to the baseline
   entry at the same ingestion boundary as the snapshot. The vendor suppression helpers
   (`_local_matches_prev`/`_jira_matches_prev`, which today call `_extract_jira_field` on
   vendor-nested values) are replaced by neutral canonical-name equivalents, and the
   outbound↔inbound field-name reconciliation (`summary` vs `title`) disappears because
   baseline, snapshot, and local ticket all compare in local names after mapping. The Jira
   `map_remote_to_local` must therefore tolerate a partial fields dict (the
   `_BASELINE_FIELDS` subset) — mapping only the keys present. Other baseline consumers
   (e.g. `binding_walk.py:192`) are out of scope and keep reading the stored vendor shape.
8. `_diff_fields` / `_extract_jira_field` / `_assignee_matches` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` become
   adapter-internal; the `outbound_differ.py:39-43` imports are deleted and the test-suite
   re-exports migrate to `adapters.jira.outbound_fields`. The bound-but-absent direct-GET path
   is unchanged: the `absent_alive_fields` return (`outbound_differ.py:432-443`, populated at
   `:730`) remains a raw vendor dict passed through core opaquely (core never reads into it).
9. Amend ADR 0035 §(d) (`docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`) to pin the
   principle: *core compares only canonical shapes; the outbound differ canonicalizes the
   snapshot via `InboundMapper` and emits vendor payloads only via `OutboundMapper`.* The
   amendment states its delivery precisely — this story canonicalizes the FIELD, LABEL, and
   BASELINE comparison paths; the LINK comparison path (`_diff_link_mutations` at
   `outbound_differ.py:767` via `outbound_links._existing_jira_links`) is canonicalized by
   the sibling story `eefd-49b1-995f-488d` under the same epic, and the ADR text marks it as
   delivered there — so the principle is not overclaimed while the epic is in flight.

Rejected alternatives: (a) putting the vendor-shaped comparison helpers on the port — already
BLOCKED by plan review as an §(d) violation (port methods parameterized on `jira_fields`
dicts); (b) re-shaping `OutboundMutation.fields` to canonical and mapping in the applier —
touches the whole dispatch pipeline (`batch_dispatch`/`dispatch_one`/`apply_handlers`/
`apply_outbound`) for no additional neutrality, since emission-boundary mapping in the differ
already keeps vendor shape out of core logic.

Behavior risk, named: the old differ compares in Jira value-space (mapped local vs raw
remote), the new one in local value-space (local vs inbound-mapped remote). Where the
local↔Jira status/priority value maps are not inverse-consistent, or the remote status does
not map (the inbound mapper emits `status` only when mapped, `inbound_fields.py:167-176` —
the neutral helper must treat canonical-status-absent + local-status-present as a diff, since
local wins), decisions could drift. The characterization suite below pins decision-for-
decision equivalence before the old helpers are demoted.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py (canonical comparison; neutral helpers; emission-boundary mapping)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py (pass inbound_mapper=backend.inbound)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (InboundMapper contract note: canonical output incl. identity aliases + parent remote id)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py (Jira mapper: aliases, parent remote id, reporter aliases)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (delegate surface)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py (helpers become adapter-internal)
- docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md (§(d) canonical-comparison amendment)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (AST gate extended to outbound_differ.py)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (new characterization suite; migrated re-export tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: a bound ticket with one changed field emits an update whose vendor payload
  equals today's (port-mapped); an unchanged ticket emits nothing.
- Characterization (old-vs-new decision equivalence): identical emit/no-emit decisions and
  payloads across the full local↔Jira status and priority value maps; assignee shapes
  (accountId / emailAddress / displayName / both-empty), including the accountId fast-path
  emitting the `_assignee_is_account_id` sentinel and the unmappable→unassign soft-fail
  (resolver re-homed as `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee`); absent parent and parent change;
  ADF description fit+rstrip; inbound-directionality suppression driven by a vendor-shaped
  stored baseline (suppression still fires after canonicalization — the regression the old
  shape mismatch would silently cause is unconditional local-wins); conflict detection via
  the canonicalized baseline; a partial `_BASELINE_FIELDS` subset dict through
  `map_remote_to_local`; label add/remove decisions via the canonical `labels` list
  (identity labels still excluded); the non-authoritative assignee-resolver fallback to
  legacy string-match; unmapped remote status.
- Runtime proof: the update path builds its payload exclusively via the injected
  `OutboundMapper` (mirroring `test_outbound_differ_uses_injected_mapper`,
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:189-213`).
- Edge: snapshot entry missing/deleted sentinels (`_DELETED`/`_TRANSPORT_ERROR`) behave as
  today; `absent_alive_fields` passthrough unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` contains NO `adapters.jira` import (module-level or
      function-nested) — verified by the extended AST case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] The update path canonicalizes the snapshot via the injected `InboundMapper` before any
      comparison (runtime proof: a spy `InboundMapper` on a `FakeBackend` observes the
      snapshot entry for every bound update candidate), and `outbound_differ.py` contains
      none of the vendor payload key literals `"accountId"`, `"emailAddress"`,
      `"displayName"`, `"issuetype"`, `"issuelinks"`, `"inwardIssue"`, `"outwardIssue"` —
      verified by a deterministic source-text denylist case added to
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` (the vendor-key reads live
      only under `adapters/jira/`).
- [ ] The characterization suite proving old-vs-new decision equivalence (cases enumerated in
      Testing) is green — verified by `pytest` on the new test file.
- [ ] ADR 0035 §(d) records the canonical-comparison principle — verified by the amended ADR
      text in the change.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Three executor-ambiguities are pinned here:

1. **Partial-baseline `map_remote_to_local` — exact absent-key semantics (Step 7).** The Jira
   `_map_jira_to_local_fields` today reads each field as `_extract_jira_field_value(f, k) or
   <default>`, which DEFAULTS absent keys. It is made partial-tolerant by guarding each field's
   emission on vendor-key PRESENCE (`if k in jira_fields`), NOT on truthiness:
   - A vendor key PRESENT (even with a null/empty value) maps exactly as today (null → today's
     default/empty), so a FULL remote snapshot is byte-for-byte unchanged.
   - A vendor key ABSENT from the input dict yields NO corresponding canonical key in the output
     (it is NOT defaulted). So a partial `_BASELINE_FIELDS` subset maps only the keys actually
     recorded.
   - Absent canonical key at comparison time == "no baseline ancestor for that field" == the
     existing per-field local-wins signal (ADR 0026 §2): the arbitration/suppression path skips
     a field with no baseline entry, exactly as a `None` whole-baseline does today. This
     preserves decision-for-decision equivalence and keeps stored remote payloads opaque at rest
     (canonicalize at read only).
   The three new canonical alias keys follow the same presence rule: `assignee_identity` emitted
   only when `"assignee"` is present, `remote_parent_id` only when `"parent"` is present,
   `reporter_identity` only when `"reporter"` is present.

2. **Naming fix (§9 / link path).** The outbound link comparison function is `_diff_links`
   (imported into `outbound_differ.py` from `outbound_links.py`), NOT `_diff_link_mutations`
   (which does not exist). Links are OUT of 625b's code scope — sibling story eefd owns the link
   path; 625b only notes in the ADR that LINK is delivered under eefd. 625b makes no change to
   `_diff_links`.

3. **`map_remote_to_local` signature is unchanged** (`dict[str, Any] -> dict[str, Any]`); the
   partial-tolerance is purely internal (per-field presence guard). Existing full-snapshot
   consumers (`inbound_differ.py:159`) are unaffected because a full snapshot has every key
   present.

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `map_remote_to_local` maps a partial `_BASELINE_FIELDS` subset by emitting ONLY the
      canonical keys whose vendor source key is PRESENT (absent vendor key -> absent canonical
      key, never a default), while a FULL snapshot maps byte-identically to today — verified by
      a partial-input test and a full-input equivalence test.
- [ ] A field absent from the canonicalized baseline is treated as "no ancestor" (per-field
      local-wins), matching today's whole-`None`-baseline arbitration — verified by a
      characterization case in the equivalence suite.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 931 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Canonical-shape outbound field diff: inbound-map the snapshot, diff local-vs-local, emit vendor payload via the port

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. A rebar store previously synced/bound to the **DIG** Jira project (bindings +
`dig-####` rebar-id labels baked into event history).
2. Re-point sync at a different project: `rebar.toml [jira] project = "REB"`.
3. `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run`.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** with `jira.project = REB`, the reconciler syncs against REB only
(or refuses, surfacing the project mismatch).
- **Actual:** the plan targets **DIG**: 1,018 / 1,415 planned mutations point at
`DIG-####` keys (977 outbound UPDATEs + DIG-keyed creates); `reconcile-check`
reports 978 unbound **DIG** issues on the inbound side even though REB is empty.
Verified on navasage: DIG is the live DSO project (e.g. DIG-5805 is DSO's own
canary bug) — a live pass would mutate real DSO issues.
## Root cause
`jira.project` only governs the CREATE project for *unbound* tickets. Tickets
already bound (binding store `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json`:
62 confirmed DIG bindings) or carrying `dig-####` labels keep targeting DIG. There
is no cross-project guard and no supported "re-target to a new project" migration.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The reconciler refuses (or loudly warns + skips) when a planned outbound
mutation targets a Jira key whose project ≠ configured `jira.project`
(cross-project safety guard, fail-closed).
- [ ] The inbound fetch is scoped to `jira.project` (REB), not the whole instance / DIG.
- [ ] A documented path to re-target an existing store to a new project (clear/rebind
bind-state + strip stale rebar-id labels), so a clean REB mirror can be built.
- [ ] Re-running the dry-run after migration shows 0 mutations targeting DIG.

baseline.summary: Reconciler targets DIG despite jira.project=REB — stale DIG bindings/labels + no cross-project guard

content.text: ## What

The 131-file flat reconciler test package -> 7 component buckets: apply (24), mutate (22), diffing (21), orchestrate (21), state (18), conflict (16), fetch (9). conftest.py (the _seed_dotted_namespace shadow) + __init__.py stay at the package root and compose down; each bucket is a subpackage (__init__.py).
## Key gotcha (documented for tangly-abbey-smelt)

Bucket dir names MUST NOT match an engine module name. The conftest extends rebar_reconciler.__path__ to the engine dir, so a test subpackage named e.g. rebar_reconciler.mutation SHADOWS the engine's mutation.py, breaking 'from rebar_reconciler.mutation import MutationDirection'. Used apply/diffing/mutate (not applier/differ/mutation) to avoid colliding with applier.py/differ.py/mutation.py.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] 131 files in 7 non-colliding component buckets; root keeps conftest+__init__
- [x] parents[N] engine anchors bumped one level deeper (incl. non-standard forms), source-logic parents[4] strings left intact
- [x] unit tier count-neutral (890), reconciler tier 870 green, 0 isolation-guard hits

baseline.summary: Subdivide tests/unit/rebar_reconciler into component subdirs

baseline.description:
## Context
Pass 3 of the GitHub Code Quality remediation. Of 230 'present' findings, 201 are dismissed as churn/intentional. This ticket remediates the reliability/maintainability subset in one change. Every symbol below was grep-verified before removal; symbols found to be USED were deliberately KEPT (listed under 'Retained').

## Scope
### Tier 1
- AI-1 (env-inheritance bug) in TWO sibling reconciler reads: reconcile_helpers.py:_read_local_tickets AND run_differs.py:_read_local_ticket_full. Both had `_env = dict(_os.environ, REBAR_SYNC_PULL="off") if no_sync else None`, so when no_sync=False (`_env=None`) the subprocess inherits the parent env — a caller's ambient REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off then silently suppresses the live sync pull. Fix both: build an explicit env, set REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off only when no_sync=True, and strip the key on the live path. A grep confirms no other site carries this pattern. ProductionBatchRunner already takes agent_runner optional (agent_runner=None, tested via a 1-arg call); to keep the override contract mypy-consistent, make agent_runner optional in the base BatchRunner, DefaultBatchRunner, and CodeReviewBatchRunner too.

# `parity._recall_false_accept` computes specificity but the gate fails when it RISES

## Context / Problem

`parity._recall_false_accept` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:70-82`) computes, over the gold items whose label is NOT `block`, the fraction the runner did NOT block:

    safe = [r for r in gold if r.label != "block"]
    false_accept = sum(1 for r in safe if r.decision != "block") / len(safe) if safe else 0.0

That is SPECIFICITY (the true-negative rate) — higher is better. It is then consumed at two sites as if it were an ERROR rate, lower-is-better:

* `parity.py:125` — `if (fa2 - fa1) > NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN + 1e-9:` reports "false-accept rose", so
  a candidate is FAILED for false-firing LESS than the baseline.
* `parity.py:252` — `if false_accept > max_false_accept + 1e-9:` against
  `max_false_accept: float = 0.10` (`parity.py:230`). Any competent gate has specificity far above
  0.10, so this comparison is effectively always-fail.

The docstring at `parity.py:71` ("false-accept = wrongly-shipped / safe") matches neither the computation nor either consumption site.

Measured impact (story 0d76): the frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run failed partly on `false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02`, v1 0.786 -> v2 0.929. Those 0.143 are exactly two gold-ADVISORY cases (2/14) that direct Anthropic FALSE-FIRED on and Bedrock did not. The strictly more accurate candidate was penalised. Recorded at `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`.

## Approach

Keep the NAME `false_accept` and correct the COMPUTATION to the actual false-positive rate over safe items — `sum(1 for r in safe if r.decision == "block") / len(safe)` — leaving both comparison directions at `parity.py:125` and `parity.py:252` unchanged, and rewriting the docstring to describe what is now computed.

Rationale for choosing this over renaming to `specificity` and inverting both comparisons: the lower-is-better reading is the one the rest of the repository already encodes, so correcting the computation makes four independent existing artifacts agree instead of requiring all of them to change.

* `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:399` documents rebar's `false_accept` as
  "wrongly-fired / total must-not-fire fixtures (`expect` == pass)", and `eval.py:491` computes it as
  `(fp / n_nofire)` where `fp` counts `expected == "no_fire" and observed == "fire"` (`eval.py:481`).
  That is exactly `decision == "block"` over safe items. The project already has one settled meaning
  for this metric name.
* `docs/plan-review-gate.md:382` states the release thresholds as `recall: 1.0`, `false_accept: 0.0`
  — a target of 0.0 is only coherent for a lower-is-better error rate.
* `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml:75` reads
  `false_accept_margin: 0.02  # candidate false-accept rises by <= 2pp vs baseline`.
* `parity.py:230`'s `max_false_accept: float = 0.10` default and the `baseline_false_accept`
  regression check at `parity.py:260` are both written as ceilings on an error rate.

Renaming to `specificity` would instead require changing the metrics key, the two comparison directions, the container eval tolerance, the gate doc, and the `prerequisite_fidelity_report` keyword arguments `max_false_accept` / `baseline_false_accept` — a wider blast radius that would also leave `parity`'s metric name disagreeing with `evals/eval.py`'s. The narrow computation fix is the one that converges the codebase on a single definition.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — correct the `false_accept` expression in `_recall_false_accept`
  (`:81`) and rewrite the docstring at `:71-72`. No comparison operator changes.
* `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py` — add direction-pinning tests.
* Existing assertions elsewhere that read a parity `false_accept` value are re-checked and updated
  where the corrected computation changes the expected number.

## Testing

* Happy/direction test: a candidate that false-fires on FEWER safe items than the baseline must NOT
  produce a "false-accept rose" gating failure.
* Failure-direction test: a candidate that false-fires on MORE safe items than the baseline by more
  than the 2pp margin MUST produce that gating failure.
* Boundary test: a perfect run (no safe item blocked) yields `false_accept == 0.0`, matching the
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md:382` release threshold, rather than the pre-fix `1.0`.
* `prerequisite_fidelity_report` test: a candidate blocking no safe item passes the
  `max_false_accept = 0.10` ceiling; one blocking a quarter of them fails it.
* Each new test is verified RED before the change and GREEN after, and mutation-checked in both
  directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_recall_false_accept` returns the fraction of safe gold items the runner DID block; verified by
      a unit test asserting an exact value on a hand-built record set.
- [x] The docstring at `parity.py:71` describes that quantity, with no reference to "wrongly-shipped";
      verified by reading the diff.
- [x] Both consumption sites (`parity.py:125`, `parity.py:252`) keep their existing greater-than
      direction and are now correct for the computed quantity; verified by the two direction tests
      above, each failing before the change.
- [x] A candidate that false-fires LESS than the baseline is not failed by this criterion, and one
      that false-fires more by >2pp is; verified by the two direction tests.
- [x] The recorded provider-parity results at
      `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` are re-scored offline against the
      corrected bar with zero model calls, and whether the frontier slot's verdict changes is recorded
      as a comment on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default test selection is green.
baseline.summary: parity false-accept criterion is inverted: it gates specificity as a failure rate

content.text: main's CI (`gerrit-verify`) is red on `tests/unit/test_import_cycles.py::test_committed_baseline_matches_current_tree`, blocking every change based on main. The import-cycle strangler guard produces a NON-DETERMINISTIC `largest_scc_size` under CI's random test order, and is being removed as too fragile to justify. This change also makes `test_execution_mode_dispatch` environment-independent.
## Reproduction Steps
1. On main (`6a28e9a5a`), run the default suite the way CI does — random order (no `-p no:randomly`): `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`.

2. Observe `test_committed_baseline_matches_current_tree` fail with `assert 36 == 35` — and on a later run `assert 37 == 35`. The number climbs run-to-run on byte-identical inputs (same commit, same grimp 3.15, same Python).
3. Run the same test in isolation OR with `-p no:randomly` (fixed order): it passes with the clean baseline (35).
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: an import-cycle guard, if kept, must be deterministic — the same source must yield the same result regardless of test order.

- Actual: the guard runs `grimp.build_graph("rebar")` IN-PROCESS inside the test, so an earlier test's in-memory package-path / `sys.modules` mutations leak into grimp's view and inflate the SCC count (35→36→37) depending on random test order. This red-ed main non-deterministically.
## Context

Discovered while landing the reconciler abort-isolation fix (Gerrit change 331): CI's `Verified-1` was NOT that change's fault — it was this pre-existing order-dependent guard flakiness on main. The `ModelHTTPError` ImportError seen locally is a separate, local-only artifact of the loopback-proxy bypass (commit 4b9e49a57) firing against the test's empty `pydantic_ai` stub; it never affected CI (no loopback there). Decision: the guard's fragility outweighs its benefit — remove it rather than add subprocess isolation. Bundle the small execution-mode test hardening in the same change.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scripts/check_import_cycles.py`, `tests/unit/test_import_cycles.py`, and
`.import-cycle-baseline.json` are removed.
- [ ] The now-orphan `grimp` dependency (used only by the guard) is removed from
`pyproject.toml`, along with the guard's per-file ruff ignore.
- [ ] The stale `scripts/check_import_cycles.py` reference in
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_server.py` is removed/reworded.
- [ ] `test_execution_mode_dispatch::test_single_turn_runner_builds_agent_with_no_tools`
passes even when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a loopback host (stubs the bypass).
- [ ] The default suite passes on py3.12 in random order (no import-cycle failure).
- [ ] `make lint` passes; no other test or source references the removed files.

# J2 — Extract the Jira-family shared layer out of the Cloud adapter

## Context / Problem

`adapters/jira/` currently owns units that are Jira-family-general, not Cloud-specific: the local↔Jira value maps and sanitizers (`jira_fields.py`), the `rebar-id` identity convention (`identity.py`), the link relation vocabulary (`jira_fields._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`), and the absence-probe classifier (`probe.py`). PR #120 consumed these from a second adapter as **private** cross-package imports, which ADR 0035 never sanctioned — its seam is one level deep, core ⇄ adapter, with `adapters/jira/` as one backend's concrete implementation.

## Approach

Create `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` and move the **non-location-pinned** units into it with **public** names, then re-point the Cloud adapter's imports. Behavior is unchanged and proven so by the characterization oracles pinned in J1 [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b], which must pass untouched across this change.

**The move is by SYMBOL, not by file** — and only symbols out of the three modules that carry no by-path load references. Verified at plan time with the ADR-prescribed grep (`lazy_load(|_load_sibling_keyed(|spec_from_file_location(`) plus a filename-string sweep over `src/` and `tests/`: `jira_fields.py`, `identity.py`, and `probe.py` appear in **no** by-path load site.

- `identity.py` → relocates whole (`JiraIdentityConvention`). Imports nothing from `adapters/jira/`.
- `probe.py` → `classify_probe_response` moves, **taking the resolved-status set as a parameter** instead of
  reading the module-level `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES`. Those names (`Resolved`/`Done`/`Cancelled`) are Cloud/DIG
  workflow states; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything, so baking them into the
  shared classifier would misclassify a resolved DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED`. Cloud passes today's exact
  frozenset (so J1's pin holds unchanged); DC passes its own configured set in J6/J7. The live `probe()` /
  `_resolve_env()` stay in `adapters/jira/`: they read Cloud's ACLI settings, which is Cloud-specific transport.
  **`RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` itself does NOT move.** It is Cloud's *configured value*, not shared logic, so the
  frozenset stays defined in `adapters/jira/probe.py` and Cloud's `probe()` passes it into the relocated
  classifier. This keeps J1's pin passing **unmodified** (`test_backend_characterization.py`'s
  `test_probe_resolved_status_names_pinned` imports the constant from `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.probe`),
  and it is not a shim: `probe.py` remains the definition site of a Cloud-specific constant, while the shared
  *classifier* has exactly one home in `jira_family/`. The injected set is a **required keyword-only
  parameter**, deliberately NOT defaulted to Cloud's frozenset — a default would let a DC caller silently
  inherit Cloud workflow names and misclassify a resolved DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED`, which is the precise
  failure this parameterization exists to prevent. That is why the parameter is added now, ahead of its second
  caller in J6/J7, rather than deferred until DC exists.
- `jira_fields.py` → **splits.** It cannot relocate wholesale, because it imports from two pinned modules:
  `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from `adapters/jira/adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
  `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` (used by
  `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the file would make `jira_family/` import `adapters/jira/`, inverting the
  dependency direction this story's own structural oracle forbids. So:
  - **Move to `jira_family/` outright:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
    `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, and the value-map literals (see de-duplication below). None touch ADF or comment
    limits — `_sanitize_summary` is a pure character truncation against `_JIRA_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS`.
  - **Move in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and `_sanitize_comment`. Their vendor
    dependency is injected rather than imported — `_sanitize_description` receives the `RichTextCodec` (its
    `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the rich-text seam that J3 [rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66] formalizes), and
    comment truncation receives the vendor comment-limit contract. Cloud builds both objects in
    `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC builds wiki-markup/plain-text
    equivalents in J6/J7. Observable behavior for Cloud is unchanged and pinned by J1's oracles.
  - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` therefore **remains as a thin Cloud-side module** that constructs the Cloud
    contract objects and re-exports nothing — its ACLI-facing callers (`acli.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`,
    `acli_graph.py`) are re-pointed at the `jira_family` symbols directly, so no shim remains.

  If J3's `RichTextCodec` shape is not yet settled when this story is implemented, inject a minimal
  `Callable[[str], str]` fit function and let J3 widen it to the full contract — do NOT import the pinned
  module from `jira_family/` as a stopgap.

**`outbound_fields.py`, `adf.py`, and `comment_limits.py` do NOT move** — they are location-pinned per ADR 0035 §(a), and the pin is live, not merely historical:

- `adapters/jira/adf.py` is loaded by path from `inbound_fields.py:36` and
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:69` (`lazy_load(_ADF_KEY, "adapters/jira/adf.py")`), plus ~13 test files.
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` is loaded by path from `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py:193`,
  `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_roundtrip.py:72`, and
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_commits_on_ticket.py:121`.
- `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` is loaded by path from ~9 test files.

So the units inside them — `_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, and the ADF encoder — are shared **by dependency inversion, not relocation**: the pinned module imports the `jira_family` contracts (never the reverse) and is parameterized by them, so DC reuses one implementation with no file moving and `_loader.py` untouched. Relocating them is ADR 0035 Phase 2's work and is out of scope; if this story appears to require *moving* a pinned file, stop and record the blocker rather than moving it.

**Pinned means "cannot change path", not "cannot be edited"** — replacing a dict literal inside `outbound_fields.py` with an import from `jira_family/` is safe, because the loader resolves the file by path and does not care about its contents.

**The new import MUST be absolute (`from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import …`), never relative.** The pinned modules are loaded via `spec_from_file_location` under synthetic module names with no package context (`__package__ == ''`) — e.g. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py:178-193` loads both `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` and `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` as `_parity_<file>`. A relative import (`from ..jira_family import …`) raises `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` under that load mode. An absolute import resolves correctly, because the package conftest puts the engine dir on `sys.path` — verified empirically in this checkout by loading `jira_fields.py` (which already uses absolute `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf import …`) under a synthetic name: it imports cleanly. A test in this story loads each edited pinned module by path, as those existing tests do, to prove the new import survives that mode.

**The by-path parity test in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py` is RE-POINTED, not shimmed.** That test (`test_idea_maps_to_jira_idea_across_all_status_maps`, the `_load_attr` assertion at ~line 192) loads `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` by path and reads `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` off the loaded module object. Once the literal moves, that attribute no longer exists there, so the assertion raises `AttributeError` — and re-adding a binding in `jira_fields.py` to satisfy it would BOTH violate the no-shim rule AND re-create the second copy this story exists to delete, failing the single-dict-literal AC. **Resolution: update that test in this same change** to load the relocated map module under `adapters/jira_family/` by path and read the map from its new sole definition site. This is an importer update — exactly the "every internal importer and every `mock.patch` string is updated in this same change" rule stated below — and NOT an exception to the no-shim rule. It also doubles as the by-path load proof, since it exercises the relocated module under `spec_from_file_location` with no package context. The test's *assertion* (the `idea` <-> `IDEA` parity that every status map must satisfy) is preserved verbatim; only the module path it loads changes.

### De-duplicating the value maps (the pre-existing violation this story must not preserve)

The local→Jira status/priority maps exist TODAY in two independently-referenced copies that have already drifted:

- `jira_fields.py`'s `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the ACLI transport.
  Precisely: `acli.py:69-70` imports BOTH maps (status consumed at `acli.py:143`, priority at `acli.py:171`),
  while `acli_cli_ops.py:34` imports **only** `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` (consumed at `acli_cli_ops.py:343,354`)
  — the status map is not referenced in `acli_cli_ops.py` at all. `acli_graph.py:22` imports only
  `_sanitize_label`. So re-pointing the status map touches one ACLI importer, and the priority map two.
- the pinned `outbound_fields.py`'s `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by the `Backend`
  port through `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
- The drift: the `outbound_fields` status map has a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the `jira_fields` copy lacks.

Moving only the `jira_fields` copy would leave Cloud's backend reading a second copy, so this story makes `adapters/jira_family/` the **sole definition site**: both existing dict literals are deleted and replaced by imports from `jira_family/`.

**The `deleted` key is decided here, not deferred — one unified dict cannot preserve two disagreeing callers.** The unified map adopts **`"deleted": "Done"`**, i.e. the `outbound_fields` value. Rationale: there are actually **three** copies of this map in the tree, and two of them already agree on `Done` — `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py`'s `local_to_jira_status` (line 37). Only `jira_fields`'s ACLI-side copy omits the key, where it falls through to `status.replace("_", " ").title()` and yields the string `"Deleted"` — **not a state in the live DIG workflow** (`{To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}`), so that transition would be rejected by Jira rather than applied. `"Deleted"` is therefore a latent bug, not behavior worth preserving, and `deleted` is a real `TicketStatus` (`src/rebar/types.py:21`), so the path is reachable.

**This is the one deliberate observable change in this otherwise behavior-preserving story**, and it is called out rather than smuggled: after this change, transitioning a `deleted` ticket through the ACLI path resolves to `Done` instead of the invalid `"Deleted"`. A test in this story pins the new value and references this paragraph.

The ACLI call site **keeps** its `.title()` fallback for keys the map does not contain — that fallback is independently load-bearing, because `transition_issue` accepts either a local status name OR an already-Jira name (`"In Progress"` passes through it unchanged). Only the `deleted` outcome changes.

Bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) remains open for the part this story does NOT do: the missing ACLI-side characterization pins, and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.

Per ADR 0035 decision 4, **no re-export shims** are left at the old paths: tests patch module-qualified, so a shim would create a patch-binding bug. Every importer and every `mock.patch` string is updated in this same change, and each moved module keeps exactly one canonical path.

`adapters/jira/`'s ACLI transport (`acli*.py`) is explicitly **not moved**, and its *logic* is not modified: it is the Cloud-specific, live-validated part. Its **import lines do change**, because `acli.py:69-70` and `acli_cli_ops.py:34` import the value maps and sanitizers that this story relocates — with no shims left behind, those imports must be re-pointed at `jira_family/`. So the invariant is "no behavioral change to the ACLI transport", verified as an import-only diff, NOT byte-identity.

**Back-out path.** The story lands as a single Gerrit change, so the whole extraction reverts with one `git revert` of that commit — the move is import-graph-only and touches no persisted data or store schema. The one deliberate behavioral change (`deleted` -> `"Done"`) is send-side and in-memory: it changes which Jira transition name the ACLI path emits and never writes to the local ticket store, so a revert restores the prior (invalid-`"Deleted"`) behavior with no data migration or cleanup pass. A stale `mock.patch` target discovered post-merge surfaces as a test error rather than a runtime fault, so it is fixable forward without a revert.

**The ADR for this new seam is J8's deliverable, not this story's.** J8 [rebar:8c35-1a5e-927b-4644] amends ADR 0035 to record the Jira-family sub-seam — its import rules, ownership, and lifecycle — so a future adapter author learns the "family-shared symbols live in `jira_family/`, not in the concrete backend" convention from a durable design document. This story ships the machine-checked import contract that *enforces* the convention; J8 ships the prose that *explains* it, reviewable against the seam as actually built.

**Alternative rejected:** promoting these into the backend-neutral core. They are Jira-specific — a GitHub backend would want none of them — so the neutral core is the wrong home and would re-create the coupling ADR 0035's Phase 2 removed.

**Alternative rejected:** leaving them in `adapters/jira/` and importing across adapters (PR #120's approach). It makes a concrete backend double as a shared library with no contract, and points a dependency edge sideways between siblings.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new package).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/` — `identity.py` relocated; `probe.py`'s pure classifier
  relocated (live probe stays); `jira_fields.py` split by symbol (file stays as the Cloud-side contract
  construction site); `backend.py` and `outbound_fields.py` imports updated; `acli*.py`, `adf.py`,
  `comment_limits.py` untouched in location.
- Every internal importer and every test `mock.patch` string naming the old paths.
- **Out of scope:** moving any location-pinned module, and any edit to `_loader.py`.

## Testing

Contract tier plus the pinned characterization oracles: the mechanism is a relocation, so the oracle is that observable behavior is identical and that no import or patch target dangles.

- happy path: the full existing suite passes, including J1's exact-value characterization assertions, with no
  edits to those assertions.
- structural oracle: a test asserts no module under `adapters/jira/` imports a name from a sibling adapter
  package, and that `adapters/jira_family/` imports from neither `adapters/jira/` nor
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/` — pinning the acyclic direction this epic exists to establish.
- negative control: `grep` confirms no re-export shim module remains at any old path.
- collateral invariant: the reconciler's dynamic loader still resolves every by-path module (the existing loader
  tests pass unchanged), and a test asserts each pinned filename (`adapters/jira/adf.py`,
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`) still exists at its pinned path —
  proving no location-pinned file moved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `make test` passes with J1's characterization assertions unmodified
- [ ] J1's oracle change is already merged, and its Gerrit change number is recorded on this ticket as a comment
      before this story is pushed for review — the epic's "oracles written before any code moved" proof (epic AC8)
- [ ] no module under `adapters/jira/` imports a name from a sibling adapter package, and no module under
      `adapters/jira_family/` imports from `adapters/jira/` or `adapters/jira_datacenter/` — verified by grep at
      this story's merge time (the reciprocal check on `adapters/jira_datacenter/` is J7's AC, since that
      package does not exist yet)
- [ ] no re-export shim exists at any pre-move path (verified by `grep` for the old module names)
- [ ] every `mock.patch(` string in `tests/` naming a moved module resolves to the new path (`make test` green
      is the check, since a stale patch target raises)
- [ ] `adapters/jira/acli*.py` change ONLY in their import lines: `git diff -U0 -- 'src/**/adapters/jira/acli*.py'`
      shows no added/removed line outside an `import`/`from … import` statement, so the transport's logic is
      provably untouched while its imports are re-pointed at `jira_family/`
- [ ] `adapters/jira/adf.py`, `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, and `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` still
      exist at those exact paths, and `_loader.py` is unchanged (`git diff --stat` shows neither a rename nor an
      edit to `_loader.py`)
- [ ] the import contract is installed as a PERSISTENT check, not a one-off grep inside a single test. Chosen
      mechanism, so the implementer does not have to decide: a **test in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` that
      walks the AST of every module under `adapters/` and asserts the permitted import graph**, because it runs
      inside the existing `make test` that CI's `Verified` gate already executes — no new CI job, no new dev
      dependency, and it matches how this repo already enforces structural rules (e.g.
      `test_backend_neutrality.py`). It fails when a module outside `adapters/jira/` or
      `adapters/jira_datacenter/` imports `adapters/jira_family/`, or when `jira_family/` imports either of
      them. Demonstrated by a deliberately violating branch failing locally before being reverted (epic AC7).
      An `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml` is an acceptable substitute ONLY if it is wired into
      `make lint`, since a config no CI target runs is not enforcement
- [ ] no module under `adapters/jira_family/` imports from `adapters/jira/` — specifically, `jira_family/`
      contains no import of `adf`, `comment_limits`, `outbound_fields`, or any `acli*` module; the
      ADF/comment-limit dependencies of `_sanitize_description` / `_sanitize_comment` arrive as injected
      contract objects (verified by grep over `adapters/jira_family/`)
- [ ] exactly one dict literal defines the local→Jira status map and one the priority map **within
      `adapters/`**: `grep -rn` for the map literals under
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/` finds them only in `adapters/jira_family/`, and both the
      ACLI transport and `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote` resolve to that single definition.
      `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status` is EXPECTED to still exist after this story
      (deferred to bug `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61`) — the grep must be scoped to `adapters/` so this AC and the
      story's stated scope agree
- [ ] a by-path load test proves the new absolute imports survive `spec_from_file_location` under a synthetic
      module name with no package context: for each module this story edits that is loaded by path — the
      pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` and the relocated value-map module under
      `adapters/jira_family/` — a test loads it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` (mirroring
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py`'s `_load_attr`) and reads the expected attribute, so a
      relative import would fail it with `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package`
- [ ] `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py`'s by-path parity test loads the status map from its
      new `adapters/jira_family/` location with its `idea` <-> `IDEA` assertion preserved verbatim, and NO
      binding for `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` is re-added to `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` to satisfy it
- [ ] `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` still resolves at `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.probe` so J1's
      `test_probe_resolved_status_names_pinned` passes unmodified, and the relocated `classify_probe_response`
      takes the resolved-status set as a REQUIRED keyword-only parameter with no Cloud-name default
- [ ] observable behavior is unchanged for both callers EXCEPT the one declared `deleted` fix: J1's backend
      characterization pins pass unmodified, and a test pins the ACLI path's resolved value for every status it
      previously handled — plus the new `deleted` → `"Done"` (was the invalid `"Deleted"`), and the retained
      `.title()` fallback still passing an already-Jira name like `"In Progress"` through unchanged

baseline.description:
The AWS review-bot holds a persistent tickets clone that a redeploy does not refresh, and it writes on every Gerrit vote. Make the clone self-converge after the epoch guard has landed, and fix the deploy path so later ensure-script changes reach the box automatically. Session log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** contains the measured facts.

## Why

The clone lives on the EBS-backed external volume declared in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`. The generated entrypoint in `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:127-149` clones only when `${REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_DIR}/.git` is absent, so a normal redeploy preserves any divergent history. The entrypoint invokes `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` outside the PAT block, so convergence must still run when `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` is unset.

`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:50-69` currently configures the repo-local identity and runs the ensure registry, but does not fetch, classify ancestry, or reset a divergent persistent clone. The bot uses `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`; its artifact writer runs after the Gerrit vote and catches store errors inside `src/rebar/review_bot/artifact_emit.py:56-166`, while the call site is `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:719`. Convergence failure must remain best-effort and must never undo or wedge an already-cast vote.

## Deployment bootstrap

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:90` omits `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` from `BOT_PATHS`. The deploy decision at `:276` and rsync at `:334` therefore cannot deliver a first commit that changes only these scripts. This ticket depends on A6-0a and lands **after A6-0a**, as its own independently reviewable Gerrit change.

After this scripts-only change merges, perform the documented one-time hand-deploy from `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`: update `/var/lib/rebar/mirror`, install the merged `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` into `/opt/rebar` while preserving owner `502:502`, and start `rebar-autodeploy.service`. The newly installed `BOT_PATHS` then detects the ensure-script change and performs the normal rsync/build/health workflow. Future ensure-script changes self-deploy without another bootstrap.

## What

1. Before fetching, record the exact local `tickets` tip and the previously observed `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` tip. Fetch with the load-bearing explicit refspec `+refs/heads/tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets`; the classifier reads that freshly advanced remote-tracking ref. If fetch fails because credentials are absent or the origin is unreachable, preserve the local tip, emit an operator-readable warning, and return success so `set -eu` cannot abort an already-cast vote.
2. Preserve the existing union safety invariant for compatible stores: use `rebar._store.sync.reconverge` for equal, behind, ahead, and same-epoch divergent histories. It keeps local-only commits rather than resetting them.
3. Add one narrow boot-time adoption path for the reclaim: reset the dedicated review-bot `tickets` branch to the pinned newly fetched commit only when the local record is pre-epoch, the remote record has a valid string epoch, the prior remote tip was readable, and the pre-fetch local tip is an ancestor of that prior remote tip. Those preconditions prove the clone has no local-only commit to lose. If the local tip was ahead/diverged from the prior remote, the prior remote is unreadable, either record is corrupt, or the mismatch is anything other than absent-to-present, preserve the local tip exactly, warn, and require operator intervention. No recovery ref pins the reclaimed object graph.
4. Add `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` to `autodeploy.sh` `BOT_PATHS`. Preserve ensure execution outside the PAT block and preserve best-effort vote safety.
5. Hand-bootstrap the first deployment after merge, then record the deployed main SHA or image digest, the successful autodeploy/health receipt, a deployed-runtime epoch-mismatch refusal probe, and the persistent-clone convergence result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] A successful fetch advances the exact `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` ref read by the classifier by using `+refs/heads/tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets`. Tier: shell integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A failed or credentialless explicit-refspec fetch exits best-effort success, preserves the exact local tip, and emits an operator-readable warning. Tier: shell integration with a failing remote.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A table-driven shell integration proves compatible equal, behind, and strictly-ahead clones preserve or converge to the exact expected tip through the existing reconverge path.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A compatible same-epoch divergent clone unions through the existing reconverge path and preserves both the local-only and remote-only event commits. Tier: real-clone integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A pre-epoch clone whose pre-fetch local tip is an ancestor of its readable prior remote tip adopts the pinned newly fetched epoch-bearing remote commit exactly. Tier: real-clone integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The reclaim adoption path never resolves the remote target a second time between validation and reset. Tier: integration with a moving remote-tracking ref.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Local-ahead and local-diverged pre-fetch states refuse reclaim adoption and preserve the exact local tip. Tier: table-driven real-clone integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A missing prior remote, a corrupt epoch record, or a mismatch other than pre-epoch-to-valid-epoch refuses reclaim adoption and preserves the exact local tip. Tier: table-driven integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Every refused adoption emits an operator-readable manual-intervention warning. Tier: integration with captured stderr.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Every convergence/adoption case leaves no merge or stash state. Tier: shell integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] With `REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` unset, the generated entrypoint still invokes ensure/convergence against an existing clone outside the PAT block. Tier: shell integration through the generated entrypoint.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` appears in `autodeploy.sh` `BOT_PATHS`.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A path-classifier test proves a change to `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` selects the review-bot deploy branch.
- [x] [code-verifiable] An injected rebar store write failure after `post_vote` leaves the Gerrit vote recorded and returns normally through the existing best-effort artifact path. Tier: unit at the artifact/caller boundary.
- [x] [operator-attested] The merged A6-0b SHA or image digest, one-time hand-bootstrap exits, successful autodeploy and review-bot health receipts, deployed-runtime epoch-mismatch refusal output, and persistent-clone old/new tips are recorded on this ticket before closure.

## Scope

`infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` tests only if required for generated-entrypoint coverage, and focused tests.

Scope: S. Depends on A6-0a; lands after A6-0a as its own change.
baseline.summary: A6-0b: make the review-bot's tickets clone self-converge, and fix its deploy trigger

Job dies at ImportError before validating any spec.

2. Observe the offline validate job: ImportError: cannot import name 'eval' from 'rebar.llm'.

- Actual: ImportError at eval.yml:64 (and :114) -> job fails.

- [ ] The offline validate job validates all packaged eval specs (verified: 9 specs) and the prompt-eval workflow is green on main.

## Context
rebar needs first-class, reliable LLM "agent operations": tool-using agents that
review tickets/code and emit structured, schema-validated findings, exposed over
the same three interfaces as everything else (library, CLI, MCP). The agent
loop is a solved problem, so we build on an existing runtime rather than
reinventing one, and we must support filesystem + MCP tools and configurable
Langflow/Langfuse across environments (some of which cannot run Langflow).

## What / Scope
- An optional `rebar.llm` framework: pluggable Runner protocol (default in-process
  LangChain/LangGraph; Langflow REST; Fake for tests), reviewer registry (Langfuse
  prompt management + packaged fallbacks), and a findings contract pinned to the
  `review_result` JSON Schema.
- A reference operation `review_ticket` wired across library / CLI (`rebar review`)
  / MCP (`review_ticket`, gated).
- Optionality is a hard rule: core rebar stays stdlib-only; the stack is behind
  `nava-rebar[agents]` and lazy-imported.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar.llm` framework + `review_ticket` shipped over library/CLI/MCP
- [x] `review_result` schema + finding/citation/severity shared $defs, wired into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS
- [x] Offline test coverage (FakeRunner) + import-cleanliness guard; no interfaces-tier regressions
- [x] Docs: docs/llm-framework.md + README/CLAUDE.md/architecture.md
- [ ] Follow-up child tickets (Langflow client, code-review/aggregation, batch scan, live validation) tracked
- [ ] The framework ships and dogfoods: agents can review rebar tickets via rebar.
- [ ] Adding a new operation or reviewer is a small, documented change.
- [ ] Works across providers (Anthropic default; OpenAI/Gemini/local) and degrades

baseline.description:
# parity `decision_flips` counts an errored pair as a decision flip

## Context / Problem

An errored side of a paired parity run is scored as a DECISION FLIP. Criterion (b) treats a flip as never acceptable ("it changes what ships"), so a single transient throttle fails a parity slot as a model-quality regression.

Proven by experiment through the real entry point (recorded in this ticket's existing comment): 20 gold pairs, both arms unanimous `block`, one v2 record replaced by the production errored record -> `flips=1, n_gold=20, passed=False`. Re-run end to end through the live driver `parallel_run_and_diff` (`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:286-302`) with a runner raising `ThrottlingException` exactly once: identical. One throttle trips four gating failures, including the never-acceptable criterion.

### The mechanism

`src/rebar/llm/parity.py:107`

    decision_flips = sum(1 for a, b in gold_pairs if a.decision != b.decision)

compares `decision` on both sides of every gold-labelled pair with NO `errored` guard, while an errored side carries a SYNTHETIC decision no model produced. `err1, err2` are computed at `parity.py:102` and are unused.

The sole production constructor of an errored record is `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:174`:

    return ItemRecord(valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True, label=label)

`parity.py:46` documents the contract this violates: `errored` is "a runtime error / timeout (not a model verdict)". Criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates runtime error rate separately, so scoring an error under (b) both contradicts `:46` and double-counts one event.

### Two things that look like the mechanism and are NOT

1. It is NOT that the pair survives because `dropped` is a member of `_DECISIONS`. The filter at
   `parity.py:105` is `if a.label in _DECISIONS` — it tests the GOLD LABEL, never `decision`.
   A discriminating experiment gave the errored side `decision="__error__"`, outside `_DECISIONS`,
   and the pair was still retained and counted. NO value of `decision` can exempt an errored pair.
2. It is therefore NOT fixable by changing what `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` emits; the defect survives
   any value it could pick. That file is out of scope.

The changeable artifact is the missing `errored` guard at `parity.py:107`.

### The silent case

The corroborating validity/error movement that might let a careful reader notice something is off exists ONLY because `fidelity_spot_eval.py:174` happens to couple `errored=True` with `valid=False`. Nothing in `ItemRecord` (`parity.py:40-56`) enforces that pairing. A record with `errored=True, valid=True` yields `flips=1, validity_v2=1.0` — a completely silent fabricated flip.

### The report cannot distinguish fabricated flips from real ones

Three v2 arms against the same v1, all reporting `decision_flips=3` — (A) 3 real / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error, (C) 0 real / 3 errors — produce a BYTE-IDENTICAL gating string. `metrics` has no per-pair detail and no excluded count.

## Approach

Add an `errored` guard to the flip computation at `parity.py:107`: a gold pair where EITHER side has `errored=True` is excluded from `decision_flips` and counted instead into a new metric `errored_pairs`, which is surfaced in `ParityReport.metrics` and appended to the flip gating-failure string so arms (A), (B) and (C) are no longer byte-identical.

The guard reads `a.errored or b.errored` — the field the `parity.py:46` contract already defines as "not a model verdict" — rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test, because the discriminating experiment above proved decision-vocabulary tests are a no-op here. Excluding rather than re-scoring is correct because criterion (d) at `parity.py:128` already gates the error rate: the event is not lost, it is attributed once to the criterion that owns it instead of twice.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — guard the `decision_flips` comprehension at `:107`, compute
  `errored_pairs`, add it to the `metrics` dict at `:139-153`, and include it in the flip failure
  string at `:121`. Update the module docstring's criterion (b) wording at `:10-11`.
* `tests/unit/test_parity_bar.py` — add the errored-pair exclusion tests.
* `tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py` — existing `decision_flips` assertions re-checked; updated only
  where the errored guard legitimately changes an expected value.

## Testing

* An errored pair (production shape `valid=False, decision="dropped", errored=True`) opposite a real
  `block` verdict is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported as errored; RED before the change.
* The silent variant `errored=True, valid=True` is covered specifically, since no other signal
  catches it.
* A genuine flip between two non-errored sides is STILL counted — the guard must not suppress real
  regressions.
* Arms (A) 3 real / 0 errors, (B) 2 real + 1 error and (C) 0 real / 3 errors produce three DIFFERENT
  report outputs, asserted by comparing their gating-failure strings and `errored_pairs` values
  pairwise.
* Each new test is mutation-checked in both directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An errored pair is excluded from `decision_flips` and reported separately, with the guard at
      `parity.py:107` reading `errored` rather than any decision-vocabulary membership test; verified
      by a unit test asserting `decision_flips == 0` and a non-zero errored count on a one-errored-pair
      run that previously reported `decision_flips == 1`.
- [x] A test constructs a paired run where exactly one side errored and asserts it is not counted as a
      flip; it fails before the fix, verified by running it against the unmodified source.
- [x] A test covers the `errored=True, valid=True` record specifically; it fails before the fix.
- [x] A test asserts a genuine flip between two non-errored sides is still counted, so the guard does
      not mask real regressions.
- [x] Arms (A), (B) and (C) above produce non-identical report output; verified by a test asserting
      pairwise inequality of their gating-failure strings.
- [x] Re-scoring the recorded run at `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` with this
      guard changes no metric, since that run has a 0.000 error rate on all four arms; verified by an
      offline re-score with zero model calls and recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, and the default test selection is green.
baseline.summary: parity decision_flips counts a transient error as a decision flip, so one throttle fails the Bedrock parity slot as a quality regression

content.text: ## Why

The epic 88ab feature-branch flow (S3) replicates refs/heads/feature/** (all nesting depths) to the GitHub mirror so g2p's workflow_dispatch(ref=refs/heads/feature/<name>) resolves. Side effect: test.yml, eval.yml, optionality.yml all trigger on push: branches: ['**'], so every replicated feature/* branch-head push fans out 3 extra CI runs on the mirror. These runs cast NO Verified vote (gerrit-verify workflow_dispatch is the sole Verified source), so they are pure cost/noise, not part of the gate.
## What

- Scope feature/** OUT of the push triggers of test.yml, eval.yml, optionality.yml (e.g. push: branches-ignore: ['feature/**'], preserving main + pull_request), so replicated feature branches do not trigger redundant mirror CI.
- Verify the gerrit-verify (Verified) path is unaffected.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] test/eval/optionality no longer run on pushes to refs/heads/feature/** (all nesting depths) on the mirror — evidence: after the change lands + replicates, push a test feature/<x> branch head and confirm the GitHub Actions run list shows zero push-triggered test/eval/optionality runs for it (gh run list --branch feature/<x>)
- [ ] main + PR triggers unchanged; gerrit-verify Verified path unaffected
- [ ] A feature/** branch push produces zero push-triggered mirror runs (evidence)

baseline.summary: Scope feature/** out of push-triggered mirror workflows (test/eval/optionality) — avoid CI fan-out from feature-branch replication

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The `rebar-implement` skill (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md`) dispatches an
implementation subagent in Phase 4d but never specifies a model tier. In both Claude Code and
Codex CLI an unset model inherits the orchestrator's (expensive) model, so the subagent silently
runs on the strongest tier — the anti-pattern that erases any token saving. The skill also lacks
guidance on which work is safe to delegate to a cheaper model and how to escalate when a cheap
implementer is insufficient.

## Approach

Add a `## Model tiering` operating principle and targeted amendments to Phases 3, 4a, 4d, plus a
new `### 4e-bis` escalation ladder. Frame tiers as *capabilities* (strong / standard / cheap)
with Claude Code and Codex CLI example mappings, rather than hardcoding product names — the skill
is cross-harness (`AGENTS.md`-class prose read by non-Claude harnesses) and model names drift
across releases. The held-out-TDD invariant is preserved: test-authoring (4b) and held-out
validation (4e, already in the file) stay strong-tier, and a *separate* implementer always
exists, so a green result still means the implementer could not tailor code to the full oracle.
The design was pressure-tested across five adversarial review rounds before this change.

Rejected alternative: naming Opus/Sonnet/Haiku directly — simpler but breaks portability to
Codex and rots as models are renamed.

## Scope

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md` — the only file changed; prose-only
  (~+111/-2 lines). No source code, no behavior, no tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `## Model tiering` section exists with a capability-tier table naming both a Claude Code
      and a Codex CLI example per tier — checked by `grep -n 'Model tiering' && grep -c '^| '`.
- [ ] Phase 4d states a standard-tier default, a cheap-tier-only-for-transcription rule, and a
      constraints-in-brief requirement — checked by reading section 4d.
- [ ] A `### 4e-bis` escalation ladder exists that distinguishes normal held-out iteration
      (no escalation) from the model-weakness escalation triggers — checked by reading it.
- [ ] No hardcoded module-size number is introduced; the brief cites
      `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (which contains `800`) as the source of truth — checked by
      grep for the filename in SKILL.md.
- [ ] Phase 3 dispatch-by-kind includes a seam note directing research/discovery/grep-shaped
      non-code leaves to the cheap/fast tier — checked by grep for "tier" within the Phase 3
      non-code-leaf bullet.
- [ ] Phase 4a carries an explicit annotation that the existing-coverage search is cheap-shaped
      but spec derivation stays strong-tier by choice — checked by reading Phase 4a.
- [ ] Change is docs-only and `make lint` passes — checked by `git diff --stat` showing only the
      SKILL.md path and a clean lint run.
