baseline.description:
## What
Adopt the B1 batch primitive (`_store.batch_stage_and_commit`, ticket 890d-4733-1c88-4976 —
**hard prerequisite; this ticket `depends_on` B1**) on the NDJSON importer's independent
passes so a bulk import commits far fewer commits than one-per-event.

## Why
`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` already has idempotency-by-`source_id` and deferred-push,
but each pass funnels through a per-event commit. Every write in the importer — CREATE
(`composer.create_core`), parent/edit (`composer.edit_core`), comments and file-impact/
verify (`_commands/leaf.py`), links (`graph._links.add_dependency`) — ultimately calls the
ONE sink `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py::append_event`, which composes the event and commits
it via `event_append.write_and_push`. That single sink is where the commit happens.

## Deferred-commit sink (mechanism — a contextvar at ONE boundary, NOT kwarg-threading)
Introduce the compose/commit split at the SINGLE `_seam.append_event` boundary via a
module-level `contextvars.ContextVar` `_batch_sink` (default `None`):
- **`_batch_sink is None` (default):** `append_event` composes AND commits per-event exactly
  as today. Every existing caller — interactive and library — is unchanged, with NO kwarg
  threaded through `create_core`/`edit_core`/`leaf.*`/`_lib_writes`/`_lib_gates`. This is why
  the edit surface is tiny and guardrail-1 (interactive writes stay one-commit-per-event) is
  structurally guaranteed: nothing sets the contextvar outside the importer.
- **`_batch_sink` set to a buffer (a `list[tuple[str, dict]]`):** `append_event` still lets
  the caller's state-reading guards run (they execute BEFORE it) and still composes the
  canonical event, but APPENDS the composed `(ticket_id, event_dict)` to the buffer instead
  of committing. The importer owns the buffer, sets the contextvar around one pass, then
  flushes via `batch_stage_and_commit` and resets the contextvar.

## Flush-boundary failure semantics
The existing importer wraps each per-row write in a `try/except` that `warn()`s and
continues (fail-open at row granularity). That is PRESERVED for row-level problems by
moving them earlier: a malformed row that fails to COMPOSE (bad field, validation) is
`warn()`-skipped at compose time and simply never enters the buffer — same observable
behavior as today. The batch FLUSH itself (`batch_stage_and_commit`) is all-or-nothing:
a git-level flush failure aborts the import with a clear error rather than silently
dropping a chunk. This is safe because the import already runs `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`,
is idempotent-by-`source_id`, and is crash-resumable — a failed/partial flush leaves
whole-commit-or-none and a re-run re-scans committed `source_id`s and resumes.

## Scope (edit surface)
- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` — add the `_batch_sink` contextvar + a small helper
  (`batch_sink(buffer)` contextmanager) and the "append to sink vs commit" branch in
  `append_event`. This is the ONLY write-path source file changed.
- `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` — for the independent, append-only passes **Pass 1
  (CREATE), Pass 2a (parents), Pass 2c (file-impact/verify-commands), Pass 2d (comments)**,
  wrap each pass in `batch_sink(buf)` and flush `buf` through `batch_stage_and_commit` in
  chunks (default 256, hard-coded — no new config key). Passes run sequentially and each
  pass's buffer is flushed (committed) before the next, so a later pass reads the prior
  pass's committed state.
- **Pass 2b (links) and Pass 2e (statuses) stay per-event (do NOT set the contextvar):**
  2b because `add_dependency` does read-after-write within the pass (it emits TWO
  `_write_link_event` calls for a reciprocal `relates_to` and calls `_is_active_link`, an
  idempotency check that READS committed link state — buffering would make a later link in
  the chunk unable to observe an earlier one, a TOCTOU); 2e because it is STATEFUL
  (children-before-parents, `cascade=False`).

## Commit-count math
Per-pass flush -> total NEW commits = `sum_over_batched_passes(ceil(pass_events/256))` +
(per-event commits from Pass 2b links and Pass 2e statuses). For a synthetic import of N=3000 tickets where each ticket has 1 CREATE + 1 comment and
**NO parents, file-impact, verify-commands, links, or status transitions** (so Pass 1 and
Pass 2d each carry 3000 events and Passes 2a/2b/2c/2e carry zero), that is
`ceil(3000/256) + ceil(3000/256) = 12 + 12 = 24` batch commits vs ~6000 per-event (>=10x
fewer). The benchmark asserts the DELTA (commits after − before; baseline `init_repo`
commits excluded). A synthetic file that also exercises parents/file-impact adds
`ceil(pass_2a/256) + ceil(pass_2c/256)` more batch commits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_batch_sink` contextvar + `batch_sink()` contextmanager in `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`; `append_event` appends the composed `(ticket_id, event_dict)` to the active sink and skips the commit when a sink is set, else commits per-event exactly as today (default path byte-for-byte unchanged)
- [ ] Guardrail 1 preserved: only the importer ever sets the contextvar; interactive writes (`create`/`edit`/`transition`/`claim`/`link`/`comment`) still commit one-event-per-commit (a unit test asserts a normal `create`/`comment` still makes one commit each)
- [ ] Importer Passes 1, 2a, 2c, 2d run under `batch_sink(buf)` and flush via `batch_stage_and_commit` in 256-event chunks; Pass 2b (links) and Pass 2e (statuses) remain per-event
- [ ] Equivalence PROVEN by a pytest that imports the same NDJSON into two trackers (per-event vs batched) and asserts equal replayed state via a concrete normalizer: for each ticket id, load `rebar.show_ticket(tid, repo_root=t)` (the reducer's replayed dict) from both stores, delete the volatile keys (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `env_id`, and every event/comment `uuid`+`timestamp`), and assert the two normalized dicts are equal for every ticket (a raw `git ls-tree` diff is NOT valid because event filenames embed per-run `uuid`/`timestamp`). Concretely: a test helper `_state(t) = {tid: _normalize(rebar.show_ticket(tid, repo_root=t)) for tid in rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=t)}` with `_normalize` deleting the volatile keys, and `assert _state(t_per_event) == _state(t_batched)`
- [ ] Benchmark: a synthetic N=3000 import where each ticket has only 1 CREATE + 1 comment (no parents/file-impact/verify/links/statuses, so only Pass 1 and Pass 2d carry events) makes the commit-count delta = `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24), >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits. Commit count is read via `int(subprocess.run(["git","-C",tracker,"rev-list","--count","HEAD"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)` before and after the import
- [ ] Idempotent re-import test: run the same NDJSON import twice into one tracker; assert the second run adds ZERO commits (`rev-list --count HEAD` unchanged) and `rebar.list_tickets` returns the same ids/count (source_id re-scan skips all already-imported events)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/ -k import -q` all green
baseline.summary: B2: route the NDJSON importer's independent passes through the batch primitive

baseline.description:
# A committed lock turns any future advisory on a transitive dep into a build-stopping CI failure

## Why this exists

Closing `e47e-a33d-b9cf-4421` surfaced a `caused_by` edge to `ce5d-d352-9511-47bc` ("go uv-canonical with a committed lock"), and the edge is accurate. It is NOT a defect in ce5d — committing a lock is the right call for reproducibility — but it has a consequence nobody has a standing answer for:

**Before the committed lock, each install floated and a fixed upstream version was picked up silently. Now a transitive dependency is frozen, so the moment an advisory is published against the pinned version, the GATING `pip-audit` job fails on every change in flight, with no code change and nothing the authors of those changes did wrong.**

That is exactly what happened with `click 8.2.1` / PYSEC-2026-2132: six changes from five different work streams all went red simultaneously, and each author independently began diagnosing it.

## Why it will recur

Nothing about the click case was special. The preconditions are structural:
* uv's universal resolution locks every extra jointly, so ONE capping dependency (there, `inspect-ai`)
  holds the whole project on a vulnerable version;
* `pip-audit` is gating and correctly refuses to distinguish "reachable in this project" from
  "present in the environment" — `click.edit()` was never called anywhere in rebar;
* the retry logic in the job only retries DB-UNREACHABLE failures, so a real finding is not
  recheckable — which is the single most time-wasting property, because `recheck` is the first thing
  everyone tries.

## The knowledge that must not be rediscovered under time pressure

This is the substance of the ticket. It took several wrong turns to establish, including one confidently-recorded wrong conclusion:
* `constraint-dependencies` can only NARROW an existing constraint set. Testing feasibility with it
  returns UNSATISFIABLE **as its expected output**, which reads as proof that the upgrade is
  impossible. It is not proof of anything. `override-dependencies` REPLACES the offending requirement
  and is the correct instrument.
* `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` is a NO-OP against an upstream cap for the same reason.
* Overriding a cap is only safe when the cap is STALE rather than a real incompatibility, and that
  needs evidence (upstream issue/PR showing the incompatibility was fixed; the capped package
  importing and running under the newer version).
* An override must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition, or it outlives its justification silently.
* `override-dependencies` is a workspace directive, NOT published in wheel metadata — so it changes
  this repo's lock only, and downstream consumers are unaffected.

## Out of scope

Changing the pip-audit job to be non-gating, or adding blanket suppressions. The gate did its job here — it found a real advisory in the shipped environment. The problem is response latency, not the gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a short runbook exists (in `docs/`, discoverable from the pip-audit job's own failure output or
      a comment beside it) covering: how to tell a real finding from a DB-unreachable flake, that
      `recheck` cannot clear a real finding, the `override-dependencies` vs `constraint-dependencies`
      distinction, and the evidence required before overriding an upstream cap
- [ ] the runbook states the verification set for any lock intervention: `uv lock --check` under the
      uv versions in use, `uv sync --locked --extra dev`, and `pip-audit` over the whole resulting
      environment to confirm the old pin was masking nothing else
- [ ] a mechanism exists to notice an override whose REMOVE-WHEN condition has been met, rather than
      relying on someone happening to re-test — either a periodic check or a documented review trigger
- [ ] the runbook is linked from the pip-audit step so a person hitting the failure finds it without
      knowing it exists
- [ ] [operator-attested] the runbook is validated by walking the click/PYSEC-2026-2132 case through
      it and confirming it would have led to `override-dependencies` without the detour, with that
      walkthrough recorded on this ticket
baseline.summary: Committed lock turns transitive-dep advisories into build stoppages

content.text: ## Why
A re-fired container review re-litigates delivered AC (false BLOCKs / stale coaching). We need a
deterministic gate that drops those findings without hiding anything live — mirroring the novelty
floor (ADR 0008) and drift-refresh (ADR 0002).
## What
Add a third Pass-3 floor in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (`pass3_decide`) that, using the
completion sub-answers (story: Pass-2 sub-call) and the delivered-now predicate (story:
delivered-now), DROPS a finding iff ALL hold: attribution = a delivered-now child AND
containment = limited-to-closed AND layer = plan-semantics AND priority (validity x impact) < floor

AND the criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set (config-backed `verify.completion_preserve_criteria`; default the registered security overlay T5c + contract criterion T10). Recompute every run (never persist a drop). Record each
drop to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`sidecar.py`) joinable by finding id. Gate behind a
`verify.completion_floor_active` evidence-gate flag + a `verify.completion_priority_floor` in
`src/rebar/config.py` (VerifyConfig), defaulting inert — the total back-out, exactly like the
novelty flags.
## Scope
- IN: the Pass-3 drop predicate; the config keys; sidecar `floored` recording; the deterministic
aggregation of the three sub-answers + priority + structural criterion class.
- OUT: the sub-questions themselves (separate story); the delivered-now predicate (separate story).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pass3_decide` drops iff attribution=delivered-now AND containment=limited-to-closed AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND the finding's criterion is NOT in the always-preserve set; all other combinations keep.
- [ ] Suppression is inert unless `verify.completion_floor_active` is true; `verify.completion_priority_floor` is configurable (mirrors `novelty_priority_floor`).
- [ ] Every drop is written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (joinable by finding id) and is recomputed each run (no persisted suppression).

- [ ] The always-preserve set is CONFIG-BACKED (`verify.completion_preserve_criteria`) referencing REGISTERED criterion IDs — default {T5c security overlay, T10 endpoint/interface contract}; adding privacy/compliance is a config change, not code (T8/T5e).
- [ ] Completion drops carry a distinct `drop_reason="completion"` in the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (vs novelty `"novelty"` / normal), so `plan_review_result_v1` offline joins never collide (G6).
- [ ] A finding on a preserve-set (T5c/T10) criterion is never dropped regardless of the other axes.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the truth table (each single-condition flip preserves the finding).
## Worked example (suppression boundary)
Epic mid-flight; child X = closed+attested, child Y = open.
- "X's AC wording for step 3 is ambiguous" -> attribution=X(delivered-now), containment=limited-to-closed, layer=plan-semantics, priority<floor, criterion=COH -> DROPPED (settled plan text).
- "X's step-3 mechanism conflicts with Y's planned approach" -> containment=spans-open -> KEPT.
- "X's delivered contract omits an error field consumers rely on" -> layer=delivered-functionality -> KEPT.
- "X's endpoint has no auth" (T5c) -> criterion in {security} veto -> KEPT regardless of the other axes.
- If X was force-closed (not attested) -> delivered-now=False -> every finding on X KEPT.
## Acceptance Criteria (durable record + invariants)

- [ ] A durable ADR `docs/adr/0024-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md` codifies the contracts: the three-field sub-answer schema + closed enums, the `delivered-now` predicate, the completion-floor drop rule + config knobs, and the sidecar `drop_reason` field (inline AC + session log are not the durable record).
- [ ] The Pass-3 floor consumes the exact enum value `containment=="limited-to-closed"` (no value drift vs the sub-call).
## Acceptance Criteria (sidecar schema + ADR cross-refs)

- [ ] `_slim()` in `sidecar.py` gains a `drop_reason` field (enum {`null`, `"completion"`, `"novelty"`}): `null` for surfaced/normal findings, `"completion"` for completion-floor drops, `"novelty"` for novelty-floor drops; it lives in the per-finding slim payload and is the join key that disambiguates the two floors offline.

- [ ] ADR 0008 (novelty floor) and ADR 0002 (drift-refresh path) are updated with a cross-reference to ADR 0024 so the three Pass-3 floors/paths are documented as one coherent set (no standalone/misleading floor reference).

baseline.summary: Pass-3 completion floor: deterministic drop of delivered re-litigation + config evidence-gate

content.text: ## Why
The "select prompts AND scripted ops / author in place" half of the vision: compose by selecting
from a typed palette, and author new prompts in the UI.
## What
- TYPED PALETTE / INSERTION: insert a new step by selecting EITHER a scripted op OR a prompt from a
typed palette (grouped by category/contract), surfaced via editor endpoints
(`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py`, `editor_assets/`). Selecting a scripted op sets `uses:`;
selecting a prompt sets `prompt:`. (This delivers the success-criterion's "scripted ops from a typed
palette", not only the prompt library.)
- PROMPT LIBRARY: dropdown listing built-in + project prompts (from the derived index + project dir).
- CREATE a new prompt and EDIT prompt text in the UI. On Save, write-back AUTO-DETECTS a writable
`nava-rebar` source checkout (pyproject `[project].name == nava-rebar` AND a writable
`src/rebar/llm/...` path -> edit the packaged `.md`) else writes a `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` project
override; SHOW the resolved target path before Save. Writes are ATOMIC (write-temp + rename) through
S2's canonical writer, and creating/editing a prompt REGENERATES the derived index.
- NON-HAPPY PATHS (explicit): refuse + clear error when NEITHER a writable source checkout NOR a
writable project dir exists; id COLLISION on create-new (refuse/confirm-overwrite); discarding
unsaved edits; an empty/invalid prompt id.
- Round-trip golden tests prove no corruption on authored/edited prompts.
## Scope
In: typed palette (op+prompt insertion) + library + create/edit + atomic write-back + non-happy-paths +
index regen + tests. Out: properties-panel structured fields (S8).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The typed palette inserts a scripted op (sets `uses:`) AND a prompt (sets `prompt:`); the prompt dropdown lists built-in + project prompts.
- [ ] Create-new + edit-text persist via S2's writer with an ATOMIC write; write-back target auto-detected and the resolved path shown; packaged write refused when read-only.
- [ ] Non-happy paths handled: neither-location-writable error, id collision, discard-unsaved, invalid id — each surfaces a clear error (no silent corruption); round-trip tests pass.
- [ ] Authoring/editing a prompt regenerates the derived index (no stale index).
- [ ] A browser e2e exercises palette insert (op + prompt) / create / edit / Save.

- [ ] The palette groups by the CLOSED category vocabulary from the prompt model (review/verifier/transform/code/exploration); the insertion mechanism is specified (a bpmn-js palette/context-pad entry or a custom insertion panel) and inserts a valid `uses:`/`prompt:` step.

baseline.summary: Editor prompt library + authoring/write-back (select + create + edit in place)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`outbound_field_diff.py:197-203` wires the live account-search resolver into the outbound mapper by **setting an attribute on it**:

    outbound_mapper._assignee_resolver = lambda lv: assignee_resolver(lv, jira_key)

wrapped in a `try/except (AttributeError, TypeError): pass`. The consumer, `adapters/jira/backend.py:122`, then **discovers** it with `getattr(self, "_assignee_resolver", None)` and silently falls back to a non-authoritative result when it is absent.

This is a collaborator passed by side-channel rather than by contract, and it has three concrete costs:

1. **It fails silently.** If the injection ever stops happening — a mapper that forbids attribute assignment
   hits the bare `except ...: pass` — every assignee resolution degrades to `authoritative=False`. That is not
   cosmetic: a permanently non-authoritative assignee makes the outbound diff re-emit an assignee change it can
   never converge, the churn class epic `ace2` exists to fix.
2. **It hid a real bug in review.** GitHub PR #120's proposed Data Center adapter copied the `getattr` line
   into a class where nothing ever set the attribute, so its ENTIRE authoritative branch was dead code and DC
   would have returned `authoritative=False` for every assignee. A typed constructor parameter makes that
   failure impossible to write.
3. **It is invisible to the type checker.** The assignment needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` because the
   attribute is on no Protocol, so mypy cannot see the dependency at all.

## Approach

Thread the resolver **explicitly** instead of by attribute:

- widen `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` in `_backend.py:130` to accept the resolver as an explicit
  (keyword-only, defaulted) parameter, so the dependency appears in the neutral port contract and is typechecked;
- pass it at the single call site, `outbound_field_diff.py:327`;
- delete the attribute-injection block at `outbound_field_diff.py:197-203` and the `getattr` discovery at
  `backend.py:122`;
- keep every observable resolution outcome identical — this is plumbing, and story J1's characterization
  oracles pin all six states of `resolve_assignee`, so they must pass unmodified.

Note `outbound_differ.py:500` also defines a LOCAL function named `_assignee_resolver`. It is unrelated to the attribute and is only caught by a bare name grep; decide whether to rename it for clarity or leave it.

## Why this is a separate ticket

Discovered while implementing story J4 [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], whose plan asserted the attribute was never set (true of PR #120, not of this tree) and whose AC4 asked for `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` to return nothing. Satisfying that literally means changing the **backend-neutral port signature**, which affects every backend — a materially wider blast radius than J4's three-file scope, and precisely the kind of core-risking change epic e369 deliberately sequenced away from the Data Center delivery path. J4 instead guarantees the property where it matters (the new identity models take the resolver as an explicit parameter and contain no `getattr` discovery at all) and defers this core cleanup here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn '_assignee_resolver' src/` matches nothing except (optionally) the unrelated local function in
      `outbound_differ.py`, and no `getattr(..., "_assignee_resolver", ...)` remains anywhere
- [ ] the resolver is a declared parameter on the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` contract in
      `_backend.py`, with no `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` needed at the wiring site
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes without that ignore
- [ ] J1's characterization assertions for all six `resolve_assignee` states pass UNMODIFIED
- [ ] a test proves the degradation path is gone: with the resolver absent, the behavior is the documented
      explicit default rather than a silent non-authoritative fallback
baseline.summary: Replace the outbound mapper's _assignee_resolver attribute-injection with explicit parameter passing

baseline.description:
## Context

Placeholder epic for R-4 from the DSO gap analysis (~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md, R-4), REFRAMED during design review from 'cite bug history in rubrics' into a first-class, extensible mechanism.

DSO anchors its reviewer prompts with concrete worked examples from its own bug history (e.g. the --label vs --labels flag-mismatch defect; a false-positive from a 20-ticket calibration record). Concrete failures calibrate an LLM reviewer far better than abstract instructions. rebar has a BETTER source than DSO for this: the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar accumulates real per-criterion findings and false-positive signal.

## The concept (converged reframe)
A CALIBRATION-EXAMPLE LIBRARY for plan review:
- A CORE set of examples ships with rebar (per criterion: a sharp good/bad worked example).
- Projects can add their OWN project-specific examples -- mirroring the existing extension seam (.rebar/criteria_routing.json overlay + .rebar/prompts/ overrides). An absent overlay fails open to the core set.
- This makes rebar LEARN OVER TIME: it increases its effectiveness based on accumulated experience in a SPECIFIC project (a false positive seen once becomes a calibration anchor that prevents its recurrence).

This is the natural evolution of R-4 + the sidecar's per-criterion FP record + the existing project-overlay architecture.

## Open design questions (for the brainstorm session)
- [ ] WHERE in the four-pass pipeline is example context injected? (Pass-1 finder rubrics? Pass-2 verifier? both? Injecting into the verifier risks anchoring the FP-filter; injecting into the finder shapes what gets surfaced. Decide deliberately.)
- [ ] HOW are examples CURATED to prevent unbounded growth? (A per-criterion cap? Relevance/recency scoring? Dedup by norm_id? Promotion from sidecar -> curated library needs a gate so the prompt doesn't bloat and bust the cache.)
- [ ] Sourcing: hand-authored core vs auto-mined from sidecar corpus vs human-curated promotion of sidecar findings.
- [ ] Interaction with the CI prompt/routing drift-parity gate and prompt-cache efficiency (examples are prompt weight).
- [ ] Format/contract: how examples attach to a criterion (prompt front-matter? a sibling examples file keyed by criterion id?).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] This epic holds the reframed concept + open design questions from the review discussion
- [ ] Sequenced AFTER the G-series rubric enrichments (no point anchoring rubrics about to be rewritten)
- [ ] Placeholder only pending a dedicated brainstorming session
- [ ] A decision on injection point(s) in the plan-review pipeline
- [ ] A curation mechanism with a bounded-growth guarantee
- [ ] A core example set + a project-extension seam consistent with the existing overlay architecture
- [ ] A promotion path from observed sidecar findings/FPs into curated examples
baseline.summary: Plan-review calibration-example library (core + project-extensible, learns over time) (R-4)

content.text: ## What

`transition <id> open in_progress` currently bypasses the plan-review claim gate that `claim` enforces. Starting work via a plain transition should apply the SAME validation (require a certified plan-review attestation, or `--force` with an audit note). The gate logic, today living in `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py::_plan_review_precheck`, must be consolidated into a single shared method that both the claim path and the transition path call — so the two cannot drift.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The plan-review gate validation lives in ONE method (consolidated out of `claim.py` into a shared home, e.g. `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py`).
- [ ] `claim_compute` calls the consolidated method (behavior unchanged; existing claim-gate tests still pass).

- [ ] `transition_compute` calls the consolidated method when transitioning `open -> in_progress`, blocking (fail-closed) on a missing/stale attestation when the gate is enabled, and exempting bug/session_log.
- [ ] `--force` (with audit comment) bypasses the gate on the transition path, mirroring claim.
- [ ] New tests cover the transition open->in_progress gate (blocked / force-bypass / bug-exempt / earned-attestation-succeeds).

# Create canonical AGENTS.md (rebar dev guide) + reduce CLAUDE.md to a thin @AGENTS.md pointer

## Why

`AGENTS.md` is read natively by Codex, Cursor, Copilot's coding agent, Zed, Windsurf, Amp,
Factory, Jules, Devin, RooCode, and Cline — so one canonical `AGENTS.md` covers the ecosystem,
and Claude Code is bridged by a one-line import. This also fixes the size/duplication
anti-pattern: sections that duplicate a `docs/` file become one-line pointers.

## What

Author a lean `AGENTS.md` at the repo root that keeps rebar-INTERNAL developer specifics inline
and replaces every already-documented topic with a one-line `docs/…md` pointer. Then reduce
`CLAUDE.md` to a single `@AGENTS.md` import plus an optional `## Claude Code` section.

- **INLINE (kept in full):** intro; the record-work/claim-before-you-work operating rules; the
  parallel-agent loop; env bootstrap (`make install`/`make hooks`); module-size policy; Serena
  navigation; a **condensed** Git/Gerrit section; a 6-line library snippet.
- **POINTER (one line each), to EXISTING docs:** gate protocols → `docs/plan-review-gate.md`;
  quality gates + ticket template + project criteria → `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`; MCP
  tool set → `docs/mcp-reference.md`; store-shares-writes + parent-first cascade →
  `docs/concurrency.md`; ticket model → `docs/ticket-model.md` (created by S1); session logs →
  `docs/event-schema.md` + `docs/user-guide.md`; library reference → `docs/reuse-surface.md`; the
  LLM agent-operations topic → `docs/llm-framework.md`; the completion close-gate →
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. These are POINTERS only — this story writes no content into those
  docs (their content already exists; the two "stowaway" topics currently mixed into CLAUDE.md's
  Session-logs heading are simply not carried into AGENTS.md).

## Scope

In: new `AGENTS.md`, rewritten `CLAUDE.md`. No writes to any `docs/*` file (pointers only). Out:
`CLAUDE.local.md` (S3), the shim/reference sweep (S6), and code. **Depends on S1** (already linked
`depends_on`): `docs/ticket-model.md` must exist before `AGENTS.md` points at it. Rollback is a
plain `git revert` (docs/text only).

## Design decisions (spike-validated)

- The `@AGENTS.md` import is PROVEN in Claude Code 2.1.211 (headless canary + official docs
  recommend exactly `@AGENTS.md` + `## Claude Code`); no symlink fallback.
- Imports "load at launch" and do not reduce context, so the token win comes from de-dup into docs
  and **AGENTS.md must itself be lean.** A grounded estimate puts a complete lean file at ~152
  lines and ≤ 200 only if the Git/Gerrit section is condensed to agent-actionable rules and defers
  the full recipe to `CONTRIBUTING.md` (verbatim Gerrit → ~215-230, which misses the target).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` exists at repo root and is ≤ 200 lines.
  - Proving: `test -f AGENTS.md && [ "$(wc -l < AGENTS.md)" -le 200 ]`
- [ ] The Git/Gerrit section is condensed (≤ ~55 lines) and defers the full recipe to
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
  - Proving: `rg -q 'CONTRIBUTING.md' AGENTS.md`; reviewer confirms the section ≤ 55 lines.
- [ ] Each already-documented topic is a one-line pointer, not a restated section.
  - Proving: `rg -n 'docs/plan-review-gate.md|docs/mcp-reference.md|docs/ticket-model.md|docs/concurrency.md|docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md|docs/llm-framework.md' AGENTS.md`
- [ ] Every `docs/…md` path that `AGENTS.md` points at resolves to a real file (no dangling
  pointer; targets created by S1 are in place by then).
  - Proving: `for p in $(rg -o 'docs/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md' AGENTS.md | sort -u); do test -f "$p" || { echo "MISSING $p"; exit 1; }; done`
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` is a single `@AGENTS.md` import + optional `## Claude Code` section, ≤ 30 lines.
  - Proving: `[ "$(rg -c '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md)" = 1 ] && [ "$(wc -l < CLAUDE.md)" -le 30 ]`
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
  - Proving: `make lint`
baseline.summary: Create canonical AGENTS.md (rebar dev guide) + reduce CLAUDE.md to a thin @AGENTS.md pointer

## Context / Problem

With the port defined (S2 [rebar:ce4d-c3ca-5412-4798]) and selection wired (S3
[rebar:94f9-a9a0-7475-4e75]), the backend-neutral core still named Jira concretely — both by
constructing the Jira transport inline AND by importing the vendor field mappers directly. This
story routes the **transport-construction** sites through the `Backend` port so the core stops
building an `AcliClient` inline, and de-hardcodes the provider-identity `"jira"` literals.

## Scope split (recorded at implementation time)

The original story bundled TWO kinds of rewiring. They were split because the second requires a
dependency-injection refactor that fights the standalone `spec_from_file_location` test-loader
convention and is independently reviewable:

- **Landed here (this change):** the four transport/construction sites, the provider-identity
  literals, and the `apply_handlers` exception-class import — a behaviour-preserving change proven
  by the full reconcile suite staying green.
- **Split to follow-up [rebar:4af8-2d88-719e-4478]:** routing the core *importer* sites
  (`outbound_differ`/`inbound_differ`/`apply_inbound`/`outbound_comments`/`inbound_translate`) off
  the vendor mappers via injection, and single-sourcing the leak-fix constants
  (`outbound_links._RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, ADF-sizing, value-maps) under `adapters/jira/`.

## Scope (landed)

Transport/construction sites routed through `select_backend(load_config()).transport`:
- `applier._load_acli` and `fetcher._load_acli` now return the backend transport directly.
- `run_differs.py`'s outbound-diff client and `_attestation.build_acli_client_from_env()`
  obtain the transport from the selected backend (fail-fast env behaviour preserved).
- The jira factory builds the `AcliClient` with `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")`

## Testing

- **Integration:** the full reconcile unit+integration suite stays green (behaviour-preserving).
- **Neutrality gate:** a new test asserts no direct `AcliClient(` construction remains in the four
  transport modules and `apply_inbound_records` carries exactly one `"jira"` token.
- **Teeth:** perturbing the outbound delegation makes the characterization tests RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

  by the selected backend's `vendor`; `grep -n '"jira"' apply_inbound_records.py` returns exactly

- [x] `apply_handlers.py` catches `AssigneeNotFoundError` via a direct import (no `ctx.acli.…`);

- [x] The full reconcile suite yields identical outcomes to pre-story `main`;
  `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green; the neutrality gate is green.
- [SPLIT → rebar:4af8-2d88-719e-4478] Core importer sites stop importing the vendor mappers

## Context

When the plan-review claim gate re-fires on a CONTAINER ticket (epic/story with children) that is
mid-execution, it reviews the plan as if FRESH — blind to which children are already delivered. It
then re-litigates acceptance criteria already shipped by closed+attested children: false BLOCKs and
coaching to tighten AC that is done, plus a slow whole-context review of settled work.

Re-fires are legitimate but infrequent — a paused epic reopened (ADR 0009 invalidates an
attestation signed before the reopen), or a material course-correction to the epic plan
(material-fingerprint invalidation). The claim CASCADE is not the driver (it only fires while the
parent is `open`). Code-drift invalidation is INTENTIONAL and unchanged (a container's plan is
reviewed against codebase state — G6 runs at container scope): this epic changes only what a
re-fired review DOES, not when it fires.

## What we build

A deterministic Pass-3 "completion floor" (third floor beside the novelty floor ADR 0008 and the
drift-refresh path ADR 0002), fed by a separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring
`plan_review_novelty`) that answers three atomic orthogonal sub-questions per finding: ATTRIBUTION
(which closed child), CONTAINMENT (limited vs spans open), LAYER (plan-semantics vs
delivered-functionality). Pass-1 stays completion-blind (full recall); the coach is unchanged.

## Scope

- IN: the Pass-2 completion sub-call + three sub-questions; the Pass-3 completion floor + config
  evidence-gate + priority floor; the delivered-now predicate (attestation reuse + in-epic sibling
  supersede); sidecar recording; calibration gold-set + tests.
- OUT (deferred, separate epics): partial-completion attestation for in-progress children; a
  structured `resolution` enum on `close`; the sidecar re-injection queue; an optional second LAYER
  binary. In-progress children stay FULLY in scope in v1.

## Alternatives considered

- (a) Exempt epics from the claim gate — REJECTED: discards the container security review ADR 0016
  added (a container epic that stands up infrastructure would go unreviewed).
- (b) Completion-aware container review — CHOSEN; hybrid = (b) + keying on VERIFIED delivery
  (completion attestation) + in-epic sibling supersede.
- Decomposition-drift-only freshness (never invalidate a container on code drift) — REJECTED:
  code-drift invalidation is intentional; a container's plan IS reviewed vs codebase state (G6 runs
  at container scope).
- A single composite predicate instead of three sub-questions — REJECTED: attribution / containment
  / layer are orthogonal (identity / spatial scope / artifact layer); folding them loses the
  distinctions and re-couples model category + severity error.
- Hide delivered children / review only open children — REJECTED: blinds coherence + security to
  delivered<->open interactions; we FREEZE delivered children as visible context, not hide them.
- Tag- or progress-note-based suppression — REJECTED: unsigned + gameable (prompt-injection surface
  into a security-sensitive gate); we key on the signed completion attestation.
- Run the completion-verifier to drive scoping — REJECTED: FAIL-by-construction mid-flight + signing
  ambiguity (needs a third attestation kind); we READ the attestation closed children already carry.
- Reuse the novelty sub-answer mechanism (add the three completion questions to NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS)
  instead of a parallel sub-call — REJECTED: completion keys on a DIFFERENT context input (the
  delivered-children manifest) than novelty (prior findings), so a separate sub-call preserves the
  Pass-1 independence invariant by construction; they share the kernel sub-answer machinery, not context.

## Acceptance Criteria

Decision (recorded, not a forward deliverable): option (b)/hybrid chosen — see the decision comment, '## Alternatives considered', and the completion session log.
- [ ] A separate `plan_review_completion` Pass-2 sub-call (mirroring `plan_review_novelty`) emits, per finding, {attribution, containment, layer} with fail-safe values (insufficient/n/a/spans-open/delivered-functionality all keep).
- [ ] Pass-3 completion floor drops a finding iff attribution=delivered-now-child AND containment=limited AND layer=plan-semantics AND priority<floor AND criterion not in {security,contract}; gated behind an evidence-gate flag + configurable priority floor (mirroring the novelty floor).
- [ ] `delivered-now` = valid completion attestation (validity-on-read, reusing the `_child_closure_findings` predicate) OR superseded by a sibling under the same parent; force-closed/abandoned/in-progress children are NOT delivered and stay in scope.
- [ ] Drops recorded to the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (joinable, observable) and recomputed every run (a reopened/un-delivered child auto-resurfaces its findings).
- [ ] A durable ADR (`docs/adr/0020-completion-aware-container-plan-review.md`) codifies the new contracts (sub-call schema + closed enums, delivered-now predicate, completion floor + config, sidecar drop_reason) — inline AC + session log are not the durable record.
- [ ] Tests: a partially-complete epic review drops delivered plan-semantics findings yet preserves (a) a delivered child's delivered-functionality/security finding, (b) a finding spanning an open sibling, (c) all findings on a force-closed child; plus a calibration gold-set of must-never-suppress cases.
- [ ] A re-fired container review does not re-litigate delivered AC: findings limited to a
- [ ] Suppression is deterministic in Pass-3, keyed on VERIFIED delivery (completion attestation or
- [ ] No change to WHEN a review is invalidated (code-drift stays), no `close`-op change, no new
baseline.summary: Completion-aware plan-review for container tickets (epics/stories with children)

# The shared webhook/rerun secret is written to journald in every access-log line

## Context / Problem

The review-bot receiver is a uvicorn app, and uvicorn's default access log records the full request line INCLUDING THE QUERY STRING. Both authenticated endpoints take their secret as a QUERY PARAMETER (`?token=...`), so every request writes the secret to stderr -> journald in clear text:

    INFO:  127.0.0.1:34184 - "POST /rerun?token=<the actual secret>&change=1323 HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted
    INFO:  172.21.0.4:33070 - "POST /webhook?token=<the actual secret> HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted

Observed directly in the production container's journal (`journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1`).

## Why it matters

* **The secret is the auth for both endpoints.** `config.py:239` is
  `webhook_token = os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_TOKEN", "").strip() or bot_token`, and this
  container sets no `WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, so the webhook token IS `GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN` — the
  review bot's Gerrit credential. Anything that can read the journal therefore learns a
  credential that can both drive reviews AND act as the bot against Gerrit.
* **The blast radius is wider than the box.** journald content flows into anything that reads
  it: `infra/scripts/observability.sh` greps the same journal, operators paste log excerpts into
  tickets and chat, and any future log-shipping would carry the secret off-host. It also means
  the secret cannot be treated as unexposed after any incident that involved sharing logs.
* **It is a fail-open exposure, not a fail-closed one:** nothing errors, nothing alarms, and the
  endpoint keeps working — so there is no signal that would ever surface it.

DISCOVERED the hard way: an agent grepping the journal for `/rerun` activity while working [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] surfaced the token into a session transcript. That is the failure mode — the secret is sitting in the most-grepped log on the box.

**This ticket does not fix the exposure that already happened.** The token in the journal (and anywhere journal excerpts have been shared) must be treated as compromised and ROTATED independently of the code fix. Rotation alone is also not sufficient: without the fix, the new token is logged the moment it is first used.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — the `/webhook` and `/rerun` handlers and/or the uvicorn
  logging configuration (`configure_logging`).
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` — the `uvicorn` invocation, if the access-log format or
  its disabling belongs there.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the `/rerun` recipe currently instructs the operator to
  put the token in a URL, which is what puts it in the log; and a rotation note.

## Approach (options, with the tradeoff stated)

1. **Move the secret out of the query string** — accept it as a header (e.g. `X-Rebar-Token`) or
   in the POST body. Cleanest: access logs record the request line, not headers. But
   `/webhook` is called BY GERRIT, so the Gerrit-side webhook configuration must be able to
   send it — check what the `webhook` plugin supports before assuming a header is expressible.
   `/rerun` is operator-driven and can move to a header immediately regardless.
2. **Scrub the access log** — install a uvicorn log filter that redacts `token=[^&]*`. Keeps the
   URL shape, protects the value, and covers BOTH endpoints even if Gerrit cannot send a header.
   Weaker in principle (the secret still transits a URL, so it can leak via any other component
   that logs URLs) but it is the only option that works without a Gerrit-side change.
3. Do both: header for `/rerun`, redaction filter as the backstop for `/webhook`.

Do NOT simply disable the access log — it is load-bearing for debugging and for the `observability.sh` greps.

## Testing

The oracle must assert on the EMITTED LOG LINE, not on the handler's behaviour, because the handler is already correct — it is the logging that leaks:

- drive a request carrying a known sentinel token through the app with `caplog` (or a captured
  uvicorn handler) and assert the sentinel does NOT appear in any emitted record, while the
  route and status DO;
- verify RED by reverting the fix and observing the sentinel reappear;
- if a header is adopted, a second test that a query-string token is REJECTED (or at least not
  logged), so the old path cannot quietly persist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the webhook/rerun secret no longer appears in any log record the receiver emits, proven by
      a test that asserts on the emitted log line with a sentinel value and is verified RED by
      reverting the fix.
- [ ] the mechanism is stated in the code where the choice is made (header vs redaction filter),
      including WHY — so a future change does not reintroduce the query-string form as a
      convenience.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`'s `/rerun` recipe no longer instructs the operator to
      put the token in a URL, and carries a note that the previous token must be treated as
      compromised and rotated.
- [ ] the access log still records route and status for both endpoints (the observability greps
      and debugging value are not sacrificed to fix this).
- [ ] ROTATION IS TRACKED SEPARATELY AND EXPLICITLY: the currently-logged token is rotated, and
      that rotation is recorded as done rather than assumed, since the code fix does not
      un-leak what is already in journald.
baseline.summary: Review-bot logs the webhook token in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request

## What
Prove the batch write reduces commit count and does not break crash-resume: a before/after
commit-count benchmark on a synthetic many-event import, plus rollback + crash-resume tests.
**Depends on B1 (890d) and B2 (6386)** — the primitive and the importer adoption must exist.

## Why
Batching changes commit granularity (N events per commit). We must demonstrate the win
(commit-count reduction) and prove the safety properties: all-or-nothing per commit, and
that a crash mid-batch plus the `source_id` re-scan resumes cleanly. NOTE: the importer's
existing LINE parsing is fail-open (a malformed NDJSON line is skipped); the whole-chunk
rollback proven here is a property of the BATCH PRIMITIVE (`batch_stage_and_commit`) — one
event that fails validation inside a chunk rolls back that chunk's already-staged events —
not of the importer's line parser.

## Scope
- Benchmark test: build a synthetic N=3000 NDJSON where each ticket has 1 CREATE + 1 comment
  and no parents/file-impact/verify/links/statuses (so only Pass 1 and Pass 2d carry events),
  run `import_tickets`, and assert the commit-count DELTA (`int(subprocess.run(["git","-C",
  tracker,"rev-list","--count","HEAD"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)` after − before)
  == `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24), >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits.
- Malformed-event-mid-chunk test (batch primitive level): a chunk containing one event that
  fails validation triggers whole-chunk rollback — assert index clean (`git diff --cached
  --name-only` empty) AND commit count unchanged (`git rev-list --count HEAD`), and no
  chunk event files left on disk.
- Crash-resume test: simulate a crash before a chunk's `git commit` (e.g. monkeypatch the
  commit to raise after staging); assert the store is left whole-commit-or-none, then re-run
  the import and assert the `source_id` re-scan skips committed events and re-emits the rest.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Benchmark test asserts the commit-count DELTA (`git rev-list --count HEAD` after − before; baseline `init_repo` commits excluded via the delta) == `2*ceil(3000/256)` (=24) for a synthetic N=3000 CREATE+comment import, >=10x fewer than the ~6000 per-event commits
- [ ] Malformed-event-mid-chunk test: a chunk containing an event dict that fails the primitive's validation (invalid `event_type` / missing `uuid`) rolls the whole chunk back — assert BOTH `git diff --cached --name-only` is empty (index clean, no phantom staged blob) AND `git rev-list --count HEAD` is unchanged from before the failed flush (proving no commit was written), and none of the chunk's event files exist on disk
- [ ] Crash-resume test on a CREATE-only synthetic file (N=1000 tickets, so Pass 1 is the only batched pass and committed-event count == committed-ticket count): monkeypatch `event_append.subprocess.run` so `git commit` succeeds for the first K=2 256-chunks then raises after staging on the 3rd chunk. Assert (i) whole-commit-or-none: `git diff --cached --name-only` empty (B1's rollback ran) and `rebar.list_tickets` count == exactly 512 (no partial chunk); undo the monkeypatch and re-run the same import and assert (ii) `rebar.list_tickets` returns all 1000 tickets exactly once (no duplicates/losses) and (iii) the re-run adds exactly `ceil(488/256)=2` chunks' worth of commits (`git rev-list --count HEAD` delta), proving the source_id re-scan skipped the 512 already-committed tickets
- [ ] Named regression suites green (verified paths): `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_reducer_single_source.py` + `tests/unit/test_reducer_status_fork_record.py` (replay), `tests/unit/test_sync_union_recovery.py` + `tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` (union-merge convergence), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py` + `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py` + `tests/unit/test_snapshot_cache.py` (SNAPSHOT compaction)
- [ ] `make test` green
baseline.summary: B4: commit-count benchmark + crash-resume/rollback tests for batched writes

## Context / Problem
Inert-config class (281f, 9d7a family): a typed schema field ships with zero cfg.<section>.<field> read sites outside schema/config plumbing, so the knob silently does nothing. Env vars are already covered by the docs/env-vars.md drift gate; schema fields have no equivalent.

## Approach
Deterministic AST-level check: for each field in _config_schema.py, require >=1 attribute-read site outside the schema/config plumbing modules.

Detection shape (decisive, receiver-agnostic): an ast.Attribute node in Load context whose terminal attribute name equals the field name — matching ONLY on the final `.field` segment, never on a receiver spelling. This deliberately matches every real read shape in src/: `load_config().mcp.readonly`, `config.load_config(root).verify.overlap_enabled`, a section object bound to a local (`mcp_cfg.auth_introspection_endpoint`), `self.config.<section>.<field>`, or any alias. Trade-off, stated openly: terminal-name matching is permissive — an unrelated object's same-named attribute also counts, silently keeping the gate quiet. That failure mode is fail-QUIET (a rare shadowed name suppresses a firing), never a false fire on a live field; zero-reference firing stays sound because a field with literally no `.field` attribute read anywhere cannot be read. Same-named-field collisions across sections are likewise fail-quiet and accepted. Dynamic reads (getattr dispatch) are invisible to the AST walk by design — that is exactly what the marker is for. Escape hatch: '# read-via: <path-or-reason>' comment on the field for indirect reads (getattr dispatch, client-project-only knobs) — pointer required, not a bare boolean. Fires ONLY on zero references (the bug condition), so refactors that move reads cannot FP. Failing message teaches the escape and cites in-file examples. Wire into CI alongside existing gates.

## Scope
- new check script (AST walk over src/rebar) + CI wiring
- '# read-via:' markers for any legitimately indirect current fields (enumerate at implementation; expected small)

## Testing
Unit: field with a read passes; field with zero reads fails naming the field; read-via marker with pointer passes; marker without pointer fails. Full-tree run clean at merge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] CI fails when any schema field has zero read sites and no read-via marker; message teaches remediation.
- [x] Marker requires a pointer/reason; bare markers rejected.
- [x] Zero-reference-only firing (no change-detector behavior on refactors).
- [x] Tree clean at landing with justified markers only.
baseline.summary: Config-is-read DET check: every _config_schema.py field must have a read site

baseline.description:
# S2 — honour `Retry-After` on 429, scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] (ten BLOCK rounds; full record on that ticket). S2 is the POLICY half; [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) was the mechanical relocation that made room for it. **S1 HAS LANDED** — Gerrit 1179, on `main` as commit `529e802da0`. `transport.py` is now 683 lines (117 of headroom under the locked 800 cap) and the retry cluster lives in `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`. **Every line citation in this plan was re-probed against that post-S1 tree**; the previous revision's citations were taken pre-S1 and were all stale, which is what a round of review correctly caught.

Jira Data Center has built-in rate limiting (8.6+, **DC only**, **OFF BY DEFAULT** — an admin enables it), a per-user token bucket. rebar's DC transport does not handle it: `_with_connection_retry` retries only connection-level faults and its docstring states that `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` — any HTTP 4xx/5xx — is NOT in the retry set, so a 429 propagates as a hard failure on the first occurrence, on an instance that was merely asking rebar to slow down.

Two constraints shape the whole fix:
1. **A static pacing policy is NOT implementable.** The limit is admin-configured and may be absent
   entirely (pre-8.6, Server, or simply disabled), so honour headers WHEN PRESENT and degrade
   gracefully when absent.
2. **Atlassian prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter**, which differs from ADR-0036's
   backoff curve (designed for transient connectivity, where the server offers no guidance).
   Jitter is not decoration: every rebar instance hitting the same bucket would otherwise retry in
   lockstep.

**VERIFY THE NUMBERS BEFORE BUILDING TO THEM** — "off by default", "8.6+" and "retry-after + 20% jitter" come from OSS research with Atlassian citations, not from testing, and that research retracted two of its other claims on a second pass.

## Approach

**Reuse what exists — do not build a third `Retry-After` implementation.** `_errors.parse_retry_after()` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` already exist, `dispatch_one.py:41` already imports both, and `dispatch_one.py:148-172` is ALREADY a 429-honouring retry path for the REST transport. Read that path first and mirror it; a second parser is the finding that opened round 1.

**MIRROR IT, BUT NOT EXACTLY — one deliberate divergence, stated so it is not read as a slip.** That existing path applies `min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, retry_after)` with **no jitter** on the `Retry-After` branch (it jitters only the ADR-0036 curve, `dispatch_one.py:167-169`). Atlassian prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter for the DC token bucket, so this story's 429 branch jitters where the existing one does not. Reuse the PARSER and the CONSTANT; do not copy the delay arithmetic verbatim.

**SCOPE THE RETRY TO IDEMPOTENT READS. This is the load-bearing constraint.** `_with_connection_retry` is the single choke point for ALL 15 transport call sites INCLUDING `create_issue`, `add_comment` and `add_label`, and its docstring already records why JIRAError is unretried: "retrying a mutation on an HTTP error risks duplicates". Retrying 429s there would **reintroduce the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] just fixed** — a 429 can arrive after the server began the write, and nothing in the response distinguishes that from rejection at the gate. So: per-CALL opt-in, **defaulting to OFF**, so a mutation added later cannot inherit the retry by omission.

**THE OPT-IN HAS TO REACH THE RETRY LAYER THROUGH TWO DISTINCT PATHS, NOT ONE.** A previous revision threaded the flag through `_call_logged` alone and was blocked for it; the correction is recorded here because the gap is invisible unless the call sites are read individually:

  * PATH A — `_paged_search` -> `_call_logged` -> `_with_connection_retry`. `_paged_search`
    (`transport.py:315`) issues its search through `_call_logged` (`transport.py:165`), which today
    calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with **no keyword argument at all**. So `_call_logged` is an
    EDIT TARGET, not merely a conduit: it must accept `rate_limit_retry` and forward it. Omitting
    it makes the flag a no-op that still type-checks.
  * PATH B — a DIRECT `_with_connection_retry` call that bypasses `_call_logged` entirely.
    `get_comment_map` fetches comments **one request per issue** at `transport.py:367`
    (`_with_connection_retry(lambda k=key: self._client.comments(k))`). That is the
    HIGHEST-VOLUME read in a pass and therefore the single most likely thing to trip a token
    bucket — and it is precisely the call PATH A does not reach. It opts in directly.

Getting only PATH A would ship a rate-limit fix that misses the read most likely to be rate limited, while every test written against `_paged_search` passed.

**WHAT ESCAPES WHEN THE CAP IS EXHAUSTED.** `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, never the raw `JIRAError`. This is not a preference: it is what the boundary already does. `_with_connection_retry` (now `retry.py:121`) catches the library error types and raises `_as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc`, which reads `.status_code` into `BackendHTTPError.code` using urllib's spelling SO THAT the core's existing `except urllib.error.HTTPError` branches classify a DC failure exactly as they classify a Cloud one. Leaking `JIRAError` past that boundary is the actual regression risk here, and J10 pinned the neutral exception contract precisely to stop it. (A library error with no usable status degrades to `code=0`, which no core branch mistakes for a 404 or a success.)

## Scope

Four files' worth of edits, and the opted-in read call sites are ENUMERATED HERE — this is the single enumeration in the document, and Testing and the ACs refer back to it rather than restating it. (The previous revision had Scope defer to Testing while Testing deferred to Scope, so neither listed anything; that circularity was a blocking finding.)

- `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — `_with_connection_retry` gains
  `rate_limit_retry: bool = False`; the 429 branch, `Retry-After` parsing, jitter-then-clamp.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`:
  - `_call_logged` (`:165`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and FORWARDS it. Without this
    edit the flag cannot reach the retry layer from `_paged_search` at all.
  - `_paged_search` (`:315`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and forwards it to
    `_call_logged`. It **accepts and forwards**; it does NOT pass `True` unconditionally.

**THE OPTED-IN READ CALL SITES — FOUR, exhaustively** (line numbers probed on `main` at `529e802da0`, i.e. post-S1):
  1. `get_issuelinks_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:349` — passes `True`.
  2. `get_comment_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:363` — passes `True`.
  3. `get_comment_map`'s inner PER-ISSUE comment fetch at `transport.py:367` — a direct
     `_with_connection_retry` call (PATH B above) — passes `True`.
  4. `get_parent_map` -> `self._paged_search(query, fields="parent")` at `transport.py:461` —
     passes `True`.

**NOT in scope:** any mutation call site; any change to ADR-0036's connectivity backoff curve; any read not in the list of four above (every other read keeps today's behaviour, which is what the default-OFF flag guarantees).

## Testing

* **the cap-exhaustion contract** — a client that returns 429 forever: assert the escaping
  exception is `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, AND assert `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` does
  NOT escape. A test that only checks "it raised" passes while the vendor type leaks.
* **`Retry-After` is honoured when present** — the sleep is driven by the header, not the ADR-0036
  curve; jitter is applied and the result is CLAMPED to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`.
* **absent header degrades gracefully** — no header (limiter off / pre-8.6 / Server) behaves exactly
  as today.
* **MUTATIONS DO NOT RETRY, enumerated rather than sampled** — assert one 429 fails immediately for
  EVERY non-opting mutation member of the transport. Enumerate them explicitly; an ellipsis is how
  a later-added mutation silently inherits the retry.
* **the opt-in defaults to OFF** — a call that does not pass the flag does not retry a 429.
* **BOTH PATHS carry the flag** — one test per path, because they fail independently: a
  `_paged_search`-driven read (PATH A, exercising the `_call_logged` forward) and
  `get_comment_map`'s per-issue fetch (PATH B, the direct call). A single test over
  `_paged_search` would pass while the highest-volume read remained unprotected.
* **`_call_logged` still forwards nothing by default** — its existing callers (every other
  transport member) must be unaffected, asserted rather than assumed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) has LANDED — Gerrit 1179, `main` commit `529e802da0`;
      `transport.py` 789 -> 683 lines, `retry.py` created at 162 lines
- [ ] a 429 with a `Retry-After` header is retried on an opted-in READ, with jitter applied and the
      delay clamped to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`, asserted numerically
- [ ] `_errors.parse_retry_after` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` are REUSED — a test or the diff shows
      no second parser and no second constant
- [ ] cap exhaustion raises `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, and a test asserts `JIRAError`
      does not escape the adapter boundary
- [ ] EVERY mutation call site still fails on the FIRST 429 — asserted per member over an explicit
      enumeration of the transport's mutation members, not a sample
- [ ] the opt-in parameter defaults to OFF on `_with_connection_retry`, on `_call_logged` and on
      `_paged_search`, asserted, so a future call inherits no retry by omission
- [ ] `_call_logged` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry`. This is an EDIT, not a pass-through
      that already works: today it calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with no keyword argument, so
      without this change the flag is a no-op that still type-checks
- [ ] `_paged_search` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` — it does NOT pass
      `True` unconditionally. The decision, not a requirement to decide: an unconditional `True`
      would silently grant retry to every FUTURE caller of the helper, the same "inherits by
      omission" hazard the per-call opt-in exists to prevent
- [ ] ALL FOUR opted-in read call sites listed in Scope pass `True`, asserted PER SITE — including
      `get_comment_map`'s inner per-issue fetch, which does NOT route through `_paged_search` or
      `_call_logged` and is the highest-volume read in a pass
- [ ] the three researched numbers (DC-only, 8.6+, off-by-default; retry-after + up to 20% jitter)
      are each either confirmed against the target DC version or explicitly marked unverified
baseline.summary: S2 — honour Retry-After on 429, scoped to idempotent reads

baseline.description:
## Finding

Future ChatGPT sessions may have the GitHub connector and repository visibility but lack a local clone, direct Gerrit access, shell network access, or a mounted Rebar tracker. Existing general agent guidance does not explain how to recognize this environment, what operations remain safe, or when ticket creation cannot be completed natively.

## Evidence

- `AGENTS.md:27-45` requires work to be found, created, claimed, and recorded in Rebar before implementation.
- `AGENTS.md:124-131` states that GitHub is a read-only mirror and all code changes land through Gerrit.
- `templates/rebar-usage.md:18-30` requires search-before-create and native Rebar create/claim/link commands.
- `docs/concurrency.md:21-26` defines the tracker as a dedicated orphan `tickets` branch with append-only event files.
- `docs/concurrency.md:171-176` requires all writes to use the lock-guarded append/commit path; raw hand-authored tracker mutations are unsafe.
- `docs/import-export.md:52-64` documents `rebar import` as the only sanctioned bulk-ingest path: it composes ordinary events through the normal locked write path (no raw-event injection), consumes NDJSON (`src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`), assigns fresh local ids/HLC timestamps, and is idempotent by `source_id` (the imported line's own `ticket_id` becomes the created ticket's `source_id`).
- `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s `required` array is `["schema_version", "ticket_id", "ticket_type", "title", "status"]`. **`rebar import` does not JSON-Schema-validate against this file** — `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` (lines 221-225) checks only `ticket_id`/`ticket_type` directly and, if either is missing, **silently skips the record with a logged warning** (`warn(f"skipping record without ticket_id/ticket_type: ...")`) via a bare `continue` — it does not raise, and does not check `schema_version`/`status`/`title` at all. The `skipped` counter (line 205, incremented at line 227) counts ONLY already-imported records (`sid in seen_source`) — a missing-`ticket_id`/`ticket_type` record is warned about but does **not** increment `skipped`; it is invisible to the return summary's counters and detectable only via the `warnings` list. A fallback payload missing a required field is therefore silently dropped on import (surfaced only in `warnings`, not in any counter), not rejected with an error.
- `docs/mcp-reference.md` documents the `create_ticket` MCP tool's input schema (title, ticket_type, description, parent_id, etc.).

## Remediation

Add concise ChatGPT-specific guidance that teaches sessions to detect connector-limited execution, prefer the installed native Rebar CLI/MCP when a valid tracker worktree exists, respect the GitHub-read-only/Gerrit workflow, and avoid inventing tracker state or substituting GitHub Issues. Define a safe fallback that prepares fully formed ticket content and reports the exact missing capability rather than claiming tickets were created. Document the exceptional import path for appending CLI-generated NDJSON without hand-authoring or mutating existing events.

**Capability check and decision rule (resolves T8 findings):** the environment capability check enumerates six dimensions — local checkout, native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` binary, tracker worktree (a directory containing a valid `tickets` branch checkout, confirmed via `rebar exists <known-id>` or equivalent), network/remote access, GitHub connector, and Gerrit availability. "Native ticket creation is impossible" is defined precisely as: **the tracker-worktree dimension fails** (no accessible `tickets` branch checkout) **AND** **the network/remote dimension fails or the native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` binary is unavailable** — i.e., the session cannot reach a real store through either the CLI, the MCP server, or a git-remote clone/fetch. Any other combination of capability failures does not trigger the fallback; the guidance must state this rule explicitly so an executor does not need to infer it.

**Fallback payload schema (resolves T8 finding on AC6, and round-2 findings G6/T1):** the
reviewable ticket payload MUST conform to `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s actual
`required` array — `schema_version`, `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status` — plus
`description` (including a `## Acceptance Criteria` block) and `parent_id` if applicable. This
resolves an apparent conflict: a never-yet-created ticket has no rebar-assigned id, but the
schema's `ticket_id` is **not** a rebar-assigned id here — it is a **provenance id the agent
generates itself** (a stable UUID4), which becomes the imported ticket's `source_id` on
`rebar import` (per `docs/import-export.md`'s idempotent-by-`source_id` behavior) — re-running
the same fallback payload through `rebar import` later is then a no-op, not a duplicate. The
guidance must state each field's fallback value precisely: `schema_version: 1`,
`ticket_id: <agent-generated UUID4, becomes source_id on import>`, `status: "open"`,
`ticket_type`/`title`/`description` from the ticket content, `parent_id` if applicable — the
same shape produced by `rebar export` and consumed by `rebar import`, so a maintainer can
review it and optionally ingest it via `rebar import` without hand-transcription.

**Exceptional import mechanism (resolves E4 and G6 findings on AC7):** the only sanctioned exceptional import path is `rebar import` (or the library's `rebar.import_tickets()`), which is the native locked write path already documented in `docs/import-export.md` — never raw event-file injection and never a GitHub Contents API write to the `tickets` branch. The guidance must state precisely what this path does, not assert unverified behavior: it accepts NDJSON compiled-state projections conforming to the fallback payload schema above (not raw event files), assigns fresh local ids and HLC timestamps to each ticket (source provenance preserved via `source_id`/`source_created_at`/`source_author`), and is idempotent by `source_id`. Before invoking it, the operator confirms the target branch is current (`git fetch` + `rebar exists <known-id>` against the intended tracker) and runs `rebar import --dry-run` first — but the guidance must state its actual, narrower guarantee precisely: in dry-run mode (`src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py` ~lines 144-161), a record missing `ticket_id`/`ticket_type` hits a bare `continue` with **no counter increment and no warning at all** (the `warnings` list is never populated in the dry-run branch); only already-imported records (a `source_id` already present in the target) increment `skipped`. So a malformed record is invisible to `would_create`/`skipped` individually, but **is** detectable by comparing `would_create + skipped` against the total NDJSON line/record count: any shortfall is exactly the count of malformed (missing `ticket_id`/`ticket_type`) records, since those are the only category dry-run drops without incrementing either counter. Afterward, the operator runs `rebar validate` (or `rebar fsck`) against the tracker to confirm store integrity.

Cascade flag: guidance must remain consistent with Rebar's append-only, optimistic-concurrency, and native-command invariants; it must not normalize direct contents-API writes as the ordinary workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ChatGPT-specific guidance file or clearly labeled section is discoverable from `AGENTS.md` without bloating the canonical startup context. Verify: `grep -qi 'chatgpt' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Guidance includes an environment capability check covering local checkout, native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp`, tracker worktree, network/remote access, GitHub connector, and Gerrit availability. Verify: `grep -qi 'tracker worktree' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'gerrit' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance states that the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror for code changes and that GitHub Issues are not a substitute for the Rebar tracker. Verify: `grep -qi 'read-only mirror' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance requires search-before-create and native parent/child creation whenever the live tracker is accessible. Verify: `grep -qi 'search-before-create' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance prohibits hand-authoring, modifying, or deleting event files and explains the append-only reason. Verify: `grep -qi 'append-only' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] Guidance defines precisely when native ticket creation counts as "impossible" (the tracker-worktree-and-network/binary decision rule above) and, in that case, requires producing a reviewable ticket payload conforming to `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s required fields (`schema_version: 1`, an agent-generated UUID4 `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status: "open"`, plus `description` with an Acceptance Criteria block and `parent_id` if applicable) plus a transparent capability-gap report, without claiming persistence occurred. Verify: `grep -qi 'export.schema.json' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'schema_version' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] The documented exceptional import mechanism names `rebar import` (or `rebar.import_tickets()`) as the only sanctioned path — never raw event-file injection or Contents API writes — states it accepts NDJSON (not raw events), assigns fresh local ids/HLC timestamps, correctly describes missing-`ticket_id`/`ticket_type` records as silently skipped with NO warning and NO counter increment in `--dry-run` mode specifically (only already-imported records increment `skipped` there), recommends detecting malformed records via a `would_create + skipped == total record count` comparison, requires confirming the target branch head before invocation, and requires running `rebar validate` or `rebar fsck` afterward. Verify: `grep -qi 'rebar import' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'rebar validate\|rebar fsck' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md && grep -qi 'dry-run' docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md`.
- [ ] A lightweight documentation test (`tests/unit/test_chatgpt_guide_links.py`) asserts each of the following specific invariants against `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` and `AGENTS.md`, and exits 0 only if ALL hold:
  1. `AGENTS.md` links to `docs/chatgpt-agent-guide.md` (discoverability).
  2. The guide does not recommend GitHub Issues as a substitute for the Rebar tracker (no phrase matching "github issues" co-occurring with "instead of"/"substitute for"/"in place of" the tracker).
  3. The guide does not describe a direct GitHub Contents-API write to the `tickets` branch as a sanctioned or normal path (no phrase pairing "contents api" with "tickets branch" in an affirmative/how-to context).
  4. The guide names `rebar import` (not a raw event-file write) as the only sanctioned exceptional ingest mechanism.
  5. The guide's fallback-payload field list matches `src/rebar/schemas/export.schema.json`'s actual `required` array (`schema_version`, `ticket_id`, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status`).
baseline.summary: Document safe ChatGPT workflows for connector-limited Rebar environments

content.text: ## Why
Workflow-vs-bespoke parity nit found in tepid-bus-pomp review: bespoke `pass4_coach` returns `[]` with
NO LLM call when there are 0 surviving advisories; the workflow ALWAYS runs the `coach_notes` prompt
step, so a clean PASS (0 advisories) still makes one wasted coach LLM call (and a coach listing over an
empty set). Pre-dates B5 — the coach step has always run since B2. Gate it to match bespoke.
## What
- Gate the workflow `coach_notes` prompt step on `surviving > 0` (a `when:` condition) so a PASS with 0
surviving advisories makes no coach LLM call.
- Keep the `coach_inputs` / `coach` ops behaving correctly (empty coaching list) when skipped.
## Scope
In scope: the `when:` gate on the `coach_notes` step in
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (both the agentic and single-turn branches) and a test
asserting the coach call count is 0 on a 0-surviving PASS. Out of scope: WS1 migration, WS2 model/editor,
WS3 chunking. This story is independent of the others and can land in parallel.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The workflow `coach_notes` step is gated on `surviving > 0` (in both the agentic and single-turn
branches).
- [ ] A PASS with 0 surviving advisories makes no coach LLM call; a test asserts the call count is 0.
- [ ] A PASS/BLOCK with ≥1 surviving advisory still runs the coach step (no regression).
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS4: Gate workflow coach_notes on surviving>0 (bespoke parity, no coach call on clean PASS)

## Context / Problem
Two comments describe optionality CI jobs that no longer exist, left behind by tickets 2132 (change 1065) and ad63 (change 1066):

- `docs/llm-framework.md:48-49` says the lean-runtime contract is enforced by "an AST import-linter + a clean-core-wheel job that asserts the heavy stack is *not* importable + per-extra and union jobs". The `import-linter` JOB was deleted in 1065 (its 9 tests already run in all four `test` matrix cells, and a collection guard in `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` now pins that), and the `per-extra` matrix + `union` job were replaced in 1066 by a single `optional-extras` job running one venv per extra plus a joint union venv.
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:134` describes the reusable it invokes as "the lean-runtime / clean-core-wheel / per-extra / union contract".

The reusable's actual jobs are now exactly `clean-core-wheel` and `optional-extras`.

These are comments and prose only -- no behavior depends on them -- which is precisely why they will rot silently. Both were flagged during the 1066 review and deliberately left out of that change's scope to keep its diff reviewable.

## Approach
Correct both passages to describe the jobs that exist, and say where the import-linter half went so a reader who remembers it is not left thinking the check was dropped. Nothing else in either file changes.

Rejected alternative: fold these into 1066. That change was already replacing a matrix with hand-written bash across three files; adding doc edits to it would have made the diff harder to review for the silent-failure modes that mattered there.

Rejected alternative: also correct the adjacent "The optional surface is three extras" claim in the same `docs/llm-framework.md` section. It IS stale -- `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` holds five (`agents`, `eval`, `grounding`, `metrics`, `tracing`) and the section bullets only three. But fixing it properly means writing new descriptive content for `grounding` and `metrics`, which is a different kind of edit from correcting a job list. Left for a separate ticket so this one stays a mechanical correction.

## Scope
- `docs/llm-framework.md` -- the CI-enforcement clause in the "Extras taxonomy" section.
- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` -- the `optionality` job's leading comment.

Explicitly NOT in scope: the "three extras" count above; `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl`, which contain captured historical AC text from plan-review experiments -- editing those would falsify the experiment record.

## Testing
No testable behavior: both edits are comments/prose. `make lint` runs actionlint over all workflows, which parses the edited YAML; `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` covers the workflow wiring the comment describes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` no longer claims a per-extra or union job exists, and names the jobs that do (`clean-core-wheel`, `optional-extras`).
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` records that the AST import-linter check now runs in the default test suite rather than a dedicated job.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `optionality` job comment names the current jobs.
- [ ] No reference to a `per-extra`, `union`, or `import-linter` JOB remains in `docs/` or `.github/`, excluding `docs/experiments/**` archival corpora.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes.
