baseline.description:
# S1 — One provider factory behind pydantic-ai's `infer_model(provider_factory=…)`

## Context / Problem

Provider construction is an inline special case. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:268` reads
`if self._model_override is None and resolved.startswith("anthropic"):` and builds the retrying Anthropic
client in the middle of `run()`. Any second provider (Bedrock, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) has to add
another branch in the same place, which is how PR #121 was written. There is no single place that answers
"how is a Provider constructed for provider X".

## Approach

Introduce `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` holding a **per-run `ProviderSession`**: an object constructed once per
`run()` from the `LLMConfig`, exposing `provider_factory` — a callable matching pydantic-ai's
`infer_model(model_str, provider_factory=…)` hook signature `(str) -> Provider` — plus a registry mapping
provider name to a builder. Upstream directs user-configurable-provider apps to exactly this hook
(pydantic-ai#1343) rather than patching `infer_provider`, so rebar depends on a supported contract.

**Client teardown is the reason this is a session object, not a bare function.** The hook's return type carries
a `Provider` only, with no channel for the retrying `httpx.AsyncClient` that
`anthropic_model._build_retrying_anthropic_model` currently returns as the second element of a tuple
(`runner.py:283`) and that `runner.py:446-452` closes in a `finally` block. `ProviderSession` owns that
lifecycle instead: each builder that constructs an `httpx.AsyncClient` appends it to the session's private
`_closeables` list, and `ProviderSession.close()` closes them all. `run()` wraps its body in the session as a
context manager, so the existing `finally`-block teardown becomes the session's `__exit__` and the ad-hoc
`_http_client` local disappears. One session per `run()` call, never shared across runs or threads, so the
list needs no locking.

The Anthropic construction moves verbatim into an `anthropic` builder that still calls
`_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, keeping the tenacity transport, the `max_retries=0` guard, the
loopback-proxy bypass (`anthropic_model.py:60`) and the per-request `httpx.Timeout` unchanged; the builder
unpacks the existing `(model, client)` tuple, registers the client with the session, and returns the provider.
`_build_retrying_anthropic_model`'s own signature is unchanged, so the two tests that import it directly
(`tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:33`, `tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py:28`) keep working — but they import
it via `rebar.llm.runner`, so those two import sites move to `rebar.llm.anthropic_model` in this change.
`_pai_model` (`anthropic_model.py:159`) remains the model-string resolver and is not touched.

This story is a **pure relocation with no behavior change** — it lands the seam before any new provider uses
it, so the Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible stories are additive registrations rather than surgery on `run()`.

**Alternative rejected:** a chain of `elif` branches in `run()` (PR #121's shape). It keeps provider knowledge
smeared across the runner, makes each new provider a diff to the hottest function in the module, and leaves no
place to attach the capability lookups S2 needs.

**Alternative rejected:** a bare `build_model(resolved, cfg) -> (Model, Closeable | None)` helper that bypasses
`infer_model` entirely. It solves teardown just as well but abandons the upstream hook, so rebar would own
provider-string resolution forever instead of inheriting it.

**Alternative rejected:** passing a mutable out-parameter (e.g. a one-element list) into the factory closure to
smuggle the client back. It works but is an unnamed side channel with no ownership story, and it would have to
be repeated for every future closeable resource.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` (new) — `ProviderSession`, the builder registry, the `anthropic` builder.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — replace the `:268` branch with the session's factory; the `:446-452` teardown
  becomes the session context manager's exit.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — unchanged behavior; imported by the new builder.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` (`:33`), `tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py` (`:28`) — update the import
  site of `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` from `rebar.llm.runner` to `rebar.llm.anthropic_model`.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract test tier (producer/consumer through the real seam): the factory is the producer and `run()` the
consumer, so a unit test on the registry alone is insufficient — the assertion must be that `run()` obtains its
provider through the session and that the session closes what it opened.

- happy path: with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, the model `run()` builds is an `AnthropicModel`
  whose httpx client carries an `AsyncTenacityTransport` and whose `AsyncAnthropic.max_retries == 0`.
- resource oracle (the defect this design exists to prevent): after `run()` returns, every `httpx.AsyncClient`
  the session constructed reports closed — asserted on the real client object, not on a call count. A second
  assertion covers the exception path: `run()` raising still closes the client.
- failure path: an unregistered provider name raises `LLMConfigError` naming the registered providers, not a
  `KeyError`.
- negative control: the `model_override` test path bypasses the factory entirely, constructs no client, and the
  session closes nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -n 'startswith("anthropic")' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returns nothing
- [ ] the full existing suite passes unchanged (`make test`), evidencing no behavior change
- [ ] a test asserts `run()` sources its provider from `ProviderSession.provider_factory`, and that an unknown
      provider raises `LLMConfigError` listing registered names
- [ ] a test asserts every client the session opened is closed after `run()` returns **and** after `run()`
      raises, checked on the real client object's closed state
- [ ] a test asserts the `model_override` path builds no client and the session closes nothing (negative control)
- [ ] `grep -rn '_build_retrying_anthropic_model' tests/` shows both import sites resolving to
      `rebar.llm.anthropic_model`, and `make test` passes
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is under 300 LOC and imports nothing from `runner` (leaf module, matching the
      `anthropic_model.py` convention)
baseline.summary: S1 — one provider factory behind pydantic-ai infer_model(provider_factory=…)

baseline.description: Found during the 72d9 CI-hang investigation (faulthandler-proven). Mechanism: _fetch_origin prefers a blobless partial fetch (--filter=blob:none, src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py fetch site). On a checkout that is itself shallow (CI: git init + fetch --depth=1), materialize_tickets/materialize can therefore resolve a ref whose blobs are absent, and _materialize_tree's git read-tree / git checkout-index --all (repo_snapshot.py:447-461) then triggers git's promisor lazy fetching — one HTTPS round trip per missing object batch — with no timeout anywhere (run_git's timeout parameter defaults to None and no caller passes one). Observed: a single checkout-index blocked >15 minutes per test and hours per CI lane. A production rebar MCP server running from a shallow or partial clone can hang the same way. Expected: local-looking materialization must fail fast (or fetch missing objects in ONE batched, bounded operation) instead of unbounded lazy fetching. Suggested directions: set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 (git >= 2.43) in _materialize_tree's env so a missing object errors immediately with an actionable message; and/or pass explicit timeouts on network-capable run_git call sites; and/or detect a shallow/promisor repo in acquire() and surface a descriptive SnapshotError. Acceptance criteria: (1) AMENDED by operator decision (2026-07-31), superseding the original fail-fast wording BEFORE implementation. Original text, for the record: 'materializing a tree whose blobs are absent from a partial clone fails within seconds with a descriptive error naming the remedy'. That was rejected on two grounds: research established the ecosystem rule is 'filter iff you will NOT materialize' (actions/checkout is the reference implementation), and fail-fast would convert a 2.1-hour hang into a HARD FAILURE of every attested gate run on any partial clone, CI included. AMENDED CRITERION: materializing a tree whose blobs are absent from a partial clone SUCCEEDS, refilling them in exactly ONE bounded fetch rather than N sequential per-object RPCs, pinned by a unit test using a --filter=blob:none clone fixture and by a regression assertion that materialization completes with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 set (i.e. the attested path no longer DEPENDS on lazy fetching); (2) no run_git call on the materialize path can block indefinitely (timeout or GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH), asserted by test; (3) make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: materialize/_materialize_tree can lazy-fetch unboundedly on a partial clone (no run_git timeout): local-looking git ops hang for hours

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Plan-review attestations currently have two effective code-freshness modes: a non-empty signed dependency map is re-hashed path by path, while an empty map falls back to whole-HEAD freshness. Story 1934-63dd-4be9-4c48 added an explicit `file_impact_scope: none` state. A ticket that truthfully declares no repository edits should keep its certified plan after an unrelated commit, without weakening the conservative behavior of legacy or undeclared empty-impact tickets.

## Approach

Add a signed manifest scope contract with three classifier results:

- non-empty dependency paths always classify as `paths`;
- empty dependency paths plus effective own scope `none` classify as `none`;
- every other empty dependency set classifies as `unscoped`.

The pure helper contract is `classify_file_scope(dependency_paths, own_scope, *, container_all_none=False)`. This story exercises the leaf path. The keyword is an intentional pre-seam for story 0b14-5c30-fe45-4fdf, which alone will pass `container_all_none=True` when every live child explicitly declares none.

The signing data flow is explicit. `sign_plan_review` keeps `dependency_hashes` focused on path hashing, reads the effective own scope with the existing public `rebar.get_file_impact_scope(verdict["ticket_id"], repo_root=...)`, calls `classify_file_scope(deps.keys(), own_scope)`, and passes the result through a new backward-compatible `file_scope="unscoped"` keyword on `build_manifest`. `manifest.py` remains dependency-light and performs no ticket-store read. `build_manifest` emits the additive exact line `file-scope: none` only when the classified result is `none`; `paths` and `unscoped` keep the previous serialized output byte-for-byte. `manifest_file_scope` reads only the authenticated manifest and returns `none` only for that exact signed declaration; an absent, unknown, or malformed declaration is treated as `unscoped`, preserving fail-closed whole-HEAD behavior.

`resign_plan_review` already calls `sign_plan_review`, so its recovery path obtains the current effective scope through the same signing boundary without a new branch or a change to `resign.py`. A public integration test will create a none-scoped ticket, recover its PASS through `rebar.llm.resign_plan_review`, verify the authenticated signature, and observe that the recovered manifest retains the none scope. The separate dependency drift-refresh path cannot receive a none-scoped record because it requires a non-empty dependency map; no new refresh branch is added.

In `compute_validity` under the DEFAULT profile, non-empty deps continue to re-hash as today. When deps are empty and `manifest_file_scope(auth_manifest) == "none"`, code freshness is not applicable and evaluation continues through material, phase, and relationship-pin checks. Empty deps with any other scope retain the existing whole-HEAD `stale-head` verdict. CLOSE and DRIFT_REFRESH profiles are unchanged. The ordinary review path also remains coherent with drift-floor logic: `_idempotent_reuse` consumes this same validity result before drift-floor selection, so a still-certified none-scoped attestation is reused and never enters the unscoped re-review floor. Explicit forced reviews remain outside this freshness optimization.

The material fingerprint preserves the exact legacy basis for `paths` and `unscoped`. Only `none` adds a canonical JSON basis member `"file_impact_scope": {"kind": "none", "reason": <no_file_impact_reason>}` before the existing sorted-key serialization. This makes none distinct from an undeclared empty impact and makes a reason-only edit stale, while leaving every existing fingerprint byte-compatible. A scope flip or reason change after signing therefore yields `stale-material`.

All new manifest helpers are re-exported from `attest`, matching the existing one-way `attest -> manifest` compatibility surface. The operational package `plan_review.__init__` does not re-export low-level manifest readers and is not changed. Because `attest.py` is already at the 800-line hard cap, the implementation must keep it at or below the cap by tightening adjacent comments or equivalent local simplification; it must not raise the limit or create a sub-100-line fragment.

Rollback is conservative. Old readers ignore the additive `file-scope: none` line and apply whole-HEAD freshness. A none-scoped attestation signed by new code also recomputes as `stale-material` after rollback because the old fingerprint omits the new declaration marker; forced re-review is expected, with no data loss or false certification. New readers treat an older manifest with no file-scope line as unscoped.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py` — scope classifier, backward-compatible `build_manifest` keyword, exact none declaration, and authenticated-manifest reader.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — signing-boundary scope lookup/classification, helper re-exports, and DEFAULT validity branch while preserving the 800-line cap.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — canonical none-only material-fingerprint basis member.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — public manifest serialization/classification and fingerprint contract coverage.
- `tests/unit/test_attestation_invalidation.py` — signed validity, legacy, moved-HEAD, tamper, and material-staleness behavior.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` — public recovery re-sign behavior for a none-scoped ticket.

Out of scope: container inheritance and P9 lint (story 0b14-5c30-fe45-4fdf), the `no-file-impact` review criterion (story 1fd4-cebe-87e9-4937), package-level operational exports, and changes to drift-floor policy.

## Testing

Tests assert public behavior and serialized contracts only; they do not grep source text, inspect private registries, or pin internal call structure.

- A table drives `build_manifest` and its public reader across `paths`, `none`, and `unscoped`. The none result contains exactly one authenticated declaration, while the other two outputs equal their pre-feature expected manifests byte-for-byte.
- A signed-attestation table moves HEAD and observes `compute_validity`: path-scoped records re-hash dependencies, none-scoped records remain `valid` with verdict `certified`, and unscoped or legacy records return `stale-head`.
- A tamper scenario adds a none declaration only to an unauthenticated plaintext mirror while the signed manifest lacks it; validity remains `stale-head`.
- Stateful ticket tests compare `current_material_fingerprint` for otherwise identical undeclared, none, and paths tickets. Changing only `no_file_impact_reason` changes the none fingerprint, while legacy paths/undeclared expected fingerprints remain unchanged.
- A public `resign_plan_review` recovery scenario verifies the resulting signature and observes none scope through the authenticated manifest reader.
- The full suite plus lint and typecheck prove compatibility, including the module-size gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After an unrelated commit moves HEAD, a signed none-scoped plan remains `valid` with verdict `certified`, while all non-code freshness dimensions still run (checked through the public `compute_validity` result).
- [ ] An unscoped or pre-feature empty-impact attestation still returns `stale-head` after HEAD moves (checked in the same signed-attestation behavior table).
- [ ] The authenticated manifest contract emits exactly one `file-scope: none` declaration only for a none scope; paths and unscoped manifest output is byte-identical to the pre-feature contract (checked through `build_manifest` return values, not source inspection).
- [ ] A none declaration present only in unauthenticated plaintext cannot suppress `stale-head` (checked by a signed-manifest tamper scenario).
- [ ] Flipping scope between none and paths, or changing only `no_file_impact_reason`, makes the signed record return `stale-material` (checked against stateful ticket material through public validity/fingerprint behavior).
- [ ] The public recovery re-sign operation preserves none scope in its authenticated manifest, and a legacy manifest with no file-scope declaration retains unscoped validity semantics (checked through `resign_plan_review`, signature verification, and the manifest reader).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full test suite pass; every edited `src/rebar` module remains at or below the locked 800-line cap.
baseline.summary: Attestation scoping: a declared-none file impact signs 'file-scope: none' and skips whole-HEAD drift

## Why
Ticket 3b4e's close FAILed twice with the unmet criteria surfaced piecemeal — round 1 named one coverage gap, round 2 a different one — costing two extra Gerrit/CI cycles (changes 526, 527). A FAIL verdict should be complete: every unmet criterion enumerated with its remediation in one pass, so one remediation round can clear the gate.

## What
- Update the completion-verifier rubric prompt (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md) to require exhaustive evaluation: assess EVERY acceptance/success/close criterion independently and, on FAIL, emit one finding per unmet criterion — never stop at the first failure. State explicitly that a verdict naming only a subset of unmet criteria is an incomplete verdict.
- This is a pass-4/prompt-level change: no verdict-reconciliation or threshold logic changes (rebar.llm.completion.reconcile_verdict stays byte-identical).
- Prove the behavior with an EVAL case, not a tautological FakeRunner test (a FakeRunner test only returns pre-loaded findings, so it cannot demonstrate the prompt achieves exhaustive evaluation). This spans TWO files that must stay mutually consistent (`validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` requires every deterministic scorer named in a spec to be registered in `eval_scorers.REGISTRY`):
  - `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py`: IMPLEMENT and REGISTER a new deterministic scorer `enumerates_all_unmet_criteria` in `REGISTRY` — given a case annotated with the set of independently-unmet criteria, it scores 1.0 iff the FAIL verdict emits a distinct finding for EACH (>= N findings, each naming a different unmet criterion), else 0.0.
  - `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/completion-verifier.eval.yaml`: reference that scorer AND add a dataset case `CV-two-unmet-criteria` (expect: fail) whose fixture ticket carries exactly two independent AC gaps (e.g. an unimplemented function AND an untested path). ANNOTATION SCHEMA (code-grounded — existing deterministic scorers read annotation fields DIRECTLY from the raw case dict; there is NO `scorer_args` field, do not invent one): the case dict carries a top-level key `expected_unmet_criteria: [<substr1>, <substr2>]` — a list of short substrings, one per criterion that must appear. The `enumerates_all_unmet_criteria` scorer reads `case["expected_unmet_criteria"]` directly (the same way existing scorers read their per-case fields from the case dict) and scores 1.0 iff there is a BIJECTIVE match — each expected substring is matched (case-insensitive substring test on a finding's `criterion` field) to a DISTINCT finding, no finding reused for two substrings — else 0.0. Missing/empty annotation → the scorer abstains (not applicable), consistent with the other deterministic scorers.
  CLOSE-GATE vs CONFIRMATORY (timing, explicit): the eval RUN is a LIVE-LLM eval that runs in the dedicated `[eval]` eval-CI pipeline (the `external`/eval tier, NOT the per-PR `make test` gate — it needs credentials + the [eval] extra and is not part of the Verified vote). So this ticket's CLOSE is gated by the OFFLINE evidence only — `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` passing (which requires the scorer registered) PLUS the FakeRunner plumbing unit test (both run in `make test`). The eval run is the CONFIRMATORY behavioral proof of the prompt behavior, recorded when the eval pipeline next runs; it is not a per-PR gate and does not block the close.
- Additionally add a FakeRunner unit test (mirror tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py) asserting the PLUMBING invariant: a multi-finding FAIL verdict survives reconcile_verdict and the close path with all findings intact (guards against regression in the pass-through, distinct from the prompt-behavior eval above).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The completion-verifier prompt (completion_verifier.md, Verdict & findings section) requires per-criterion exhaustive evaluation and one finding per unmet criterion on FAIL, and states that a verdict naming only a subset of unmet criteria is an incomplete verdict.
- [ ] The `enumerates_all_unmet_criteria` deterministic scorer is implemented AND registered in `eval_scorers.REGISTRY` (evals/eval_scorers.py), and completion-verifier.eval.yaml references it plus a `CV-two-unmet-criteria` case (two independently-unmet criteria). Offline proof: `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)` passes on the extended spec (which it can only do because the scorer is registered). Behavioral proof (confirmatory, in the [eval] eval-CI pipeline — NOT the per-PR close gate): the eval run shows the case's FAIL verdict emits a distinct finding for BOTH unmet criteria (scorer == 1.0). The close is gated by the offline validate + the plumbing unit test above, both in `make test`.
- [ ] A FakeRunner unit test asserts a two-finding FAIL verdict is preserved (all findings intact) through reconcile_verdict + the close path.
- [ ] reconcile_verdict and the close-path logic are byte-unchanged (no reconciliation/threshold edits).
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.
baseline.summary: Completion-verifier FAILs must enumerate ALL unmet criteria in one verdict (anti-ratchet)

# Outbound clear-assignee cannot unassign on Jira Data Center

Found while writing the row-9 outbound cell of the J11 mutation table (story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae). NOT fixed here — filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a product defect stops and reports.

## Mechanism (proven by code path, three links in a chain)

1. The differ's desired value for an EMPTY local assignee is the EMPTY STRING, not
   None: `outbound_differ._assignee_resolver` returns `("", True, False)` when
   `not assignee` (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:504-505).
   `assignee` is in `_OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST`
   (dispatch_apply_phases.py:46), so it reaches `client.update_issue(key,
   assignee="")`.

2. The DC transport forwards that empty string VERBATIM to the vendor library.
   `JiraDataCenterTransport.update_issue` pops `assignee` and calls
   `self._assign(remote_id, assignee)` whenever the key is present — there is no
   empty-value branch (adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:281-287, 290-303).
   `_assign` calls `self._client.assign_issue(remote_id, "")`.

3. pycontribs/jira treats ONLY None / -1 / "-1" as Unassigned. In jira 3.10.5,
   `JIRA._get_user_id` starts `if user in (None, -1, "-1"): return user` and
   otherwise runs `search_users(user="", maxResults=20)`, raising
   `JIRAError("No matching user found for: ''")` when that returns nothing — and
   when it returns something, it assigns THAT arbitrary user. So the empty string
   is not an unassign instruction on this path at all.

## Cloud already has the fix; DC never got its half

This is bug 85a1's defect class, unported. The Cloud transport routes an empty/None assignee through `unassign_issue` instead of passing it on, with the reason recorded inline: "Bug 85a1 (Fix D7): assignee=None/empty is routed through `unassign_issue` (REST PUT /assignee with `{"accountId": null}`) rather than passed to ACLI as `--assignee ""`, which ACLI silently no-ops" (adapters/jira/acli.py:342-345, guard at :357-359).

The shape is identical to bug d067 (the status-to-transition seam existed on Cloud and Data Center simply never got its half), which the DC `update_issue` docstring itself records at transport.py:265-275.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_outbound_unassign_round_trips` asserts `fields.assignee` is null on the DC issue after a local assignee clear converges. It should go RED on the harness until this is fixed.

## Suggested fix

Give the DC transport the same empty-assignee branch Cloud has: in `_assign`, map a falsy assignee to `None` before calling `assign_issue` (pycontribs then PUTs `{"name": null}`, which is DC's unassign), rather than letting `""` reach `_get_user_id`.
baseline.summary: DC outbound clear-assignee never unassigns (empty string reaches assign_issue)

content.text: ## What
Add **lease-based self-healing** on top of the C1 ref-lock primitive so a crashed pass-holder
never wedges the reconciler beyond one lease interval. Builds directly on C1.
**Depends on: 524d-00fa-66ef-4432 (C1).** C1 delivers the `_ref_lock.py` module, the blob schema
(`heartbeat_ns`, `fence`), the `acquire`/`release`/`read` API, and the CAS helpers. **This child
ADDS `renew()` plus the lease-expiry/steal logic to that module** — it is not standalone and C1
must be merged first. (`renew()` is introduced here, not in C1.)
- **Relative-duration, skew-proof lease (DynamoDB-lock-client pattern):** expiry is NOT a
cross-clone timestamp comparison. A contender records `(observed_oid, fence)`, waits one lease
interval measured on its **own** clock, re-reads; if `fence` and the ref oid are unchanged, the
holder made no progress for a full lease -> considered dead. This is why the stored `heartbeat_ns`
is only diagnostic and the design is skew-proof.
- **`renew()`** (heartbeat) CAS-updates the blob's `heartbeat_ns` and increments `fence`
(`fence += 1`) while the holder still owns the ref (old = observed oid). `fence` is a **monotonic
progress-witness / generation counter** — it is the signal the expiry rule reads; it is NOT a
full fencing token handed to the protected resource (no stale-writer rejection is claimed).
- **CAS-break-on-expiry:** a contender may steal **only** an expired lease, by CAS-replacing the
blob against the exact observed OID. Because the steal is a compare-and-swap on the observed oid,
a **double-break race resolves to exactly one winner** — the loser's CAS fails, it backs off and
does NOT also acquire.
- **Lease + cadence config:** default lease **120 s**, heartbeat interval **`max(1, lease // 3)`**
seconds (integer floor, not a vague `~lease/3`), read from a new `[reconciler]` key
`lock_lease_secs`. Registering that key is C3's job (the `_config_schema.py` wiring lands with the
`lock_backend` switch); here it is consumed with a safe default so C2 is testable standalone.
- **`renew()` failure contract:** a rejected renewal CAS means the lease was lost/stolen. `renew()`
raises a **named exception** (e.g. `LeaseLostError`) — it does NOT silently retry into another
holder's lock. The orchestrator (C3) turns that exception into a pass-abort.
- Structured log emission for lease-steal, renewal-failure, and expiry-detection events.
- Lives in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (extends C1); no reconciler
orchestration wiring (that is C3). Extend the C1 ADR with the lease/heartbeat/fence contract.
## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)
1. **API surface added to `_ref_lock.py`.** `renew(repo_root, ref, *, oid, remote=None) -> str`;
and the steal is split into a **testable core** `try_break_if_stale(repo_root, ref, *, first,
holder, remote=None) -> str | None` plus a convenience `steal(repo_root, ref, *, holder,
remote=None, sleep_fn=time.sleep) -> str | None` that does observe -> `sleep_fn(first.lease_secs)`
-> `try_break_if_stale`. The one-lease wait is injected via `sleep_fn` so unit tests exercise the
CAS/expiry logic **without real time**; a short configured lease also keeps any live test fast.
2. **`renew()` contract.** Reads the current state; if the ref is absent or no longer points at
`oid` -> `LeaseLostError` (no CAS attempted). Otherwise it CAS-updates the blob to
`{holder, lease_secs (unchanged), heartbeat_ns=time.time_ns(), fence+1}` against `oid` (via the
shared `_cas_once` seam / `--force-with-lease` on the remote path); a rejected CAS ->
`LeaseLostError`. Returns the new oid the caller threads into the next `renew`. It NEVER retries
into another holder's lock.
3. **Steal contract.** `try_break_if_stale` takes the `first` observation and re-reads: if the ref
is now free (`None`) or its `(oid, fence)` changed -> returns `None` (the holder released or made
progress = live, never stolen). Otherwise it CAS-replaces the blob against `first.oid` with
`{holder=<contender>, lease_secs=first.lease_secs, heartbeat_ns=now, fence=first.fence + 1}`; a
rejected CAS (lost the single-winner race) -> `None`. It never steals a **free** ref (that is
`acquire`) and never steals a **live/renewing** holder.
4. **Fail-closed during steal/renew.** A `RefLockCorruptError` / `RefLockTimeoutError` from any read
in the steal/renew path propagates (fail-closed = treat as HELD); a contender never steals on an
unreadable blob.
5. **Lease constants.** `DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS = 120` and `heartbeat_interval(lease) -> max(1,
int(lease // 3))` live in `_ref_lock.py`; C3 wires `[reconciler] lock_lease_secs` into the
`acquire` call. `lease_secs` is carried IN the blob, so a contender waits the **holder's** lease,
not its own — the skew-proof relative-duration rule.
6. **Structured logs.** Emit on lease-steal (won a break), expiry-detection (no `(oid, fence)`
progress across one lease), and renewal-failure (`LeaseLostError`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_ref_lock.py` gains `renew()` (owner-only CAS-update of `heartbeat_ns`, `fence += 1`, against
the held oid) and a lease-expiry evaluation using observed-no-progress-over-one-locally-measured
-lease, not an absolute cross-clone clock diff; `renew()` on a lost/stolen lease raises
`LeaseLostError` (no silent retry) and returns the new oid on success.
- [ ] A contender CAS-breaks only an expired lease (no `fence`/oid progress across one lease); a
live, heartbeating holder is never stolen from (regression test); a free ref is never "stolen"
(that path is `acquire`).
- [ ] Double-break race: two contenders race to steal one expired lock (both call
`try_break_if_stale` against the same `first`); exactly one wins, the other observes CAS
failure and returns `None` (does NOT acquire) — single-winner regression test.
- [ ] Lease = `[reconciler] lock_lease_secs` (default `DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS = 120`), heartbeat interval
`heartbeat_interval(lease) = max(1, lease // 3)`, not hardcoded at the call sites; the one-lease
wait is injectable (`sleep_fn`) so tests need no real sleep.
- [ ] A corrupt/unreadable blob encountered during steal/renew fails closed (treated as HELD), never
stolen.
- [ ] Lease-steal / renewal-failure / expiry-detection events emit structured logs; the C1 ADR is
extended with the lease/heartbeat/fence contract. Non-integration suite green.

baseline.summary: Lease + heartbeat + CAS-break-on-stale self-healing (single-winner)

## Why
The gate returns FINDINGS (what's wrong) but never coaches a productive MOVE (here's a play to address this
class) — so a caller's next revision isn't primed with best practice. This Pass-4 "coach" adds affirmative,
forward coaching over the surviving findings: it primes the caller toward a de-risking/clarifying move, without
handing a ready-made solution. It is ADVISORY (never blocks) and is the shared coaching layer for `9da1` too.

## What
- A **single-turn, structured-output LLM call (NOT an agent, no tooling)** — the same cheap shape as the Pass-2
  aggregate verifier — running AFTER Pass-3 over ONLY the surviving (advisory, not-dropped) findings.
- It does TWO things only: (a) map each finding to a `move_id` from the fixed MOVE REGISTRY, (b) extract a short
  `subject` noun-phrase (what the move targets, drawn from the finding) that is VALIDATED by a deterministic
  SUBJECT VALIDATOR (v1 default: bounded = ≤ 8 words / ≤ 60 chars; REJECT if it contains code tokens — backticks,
  parentheses, `;`/`=`, or an `import`/`def`/`class` keyword — or a leading imperative verb; on REJECT, emit NO
  coaching for that finding — best-effort drop, never a retry-into-prose loop). Output schema:
  `[{move_id, subject, finding_refs[]}]`, CLUSTERED by move. The LLM authors NO free prose.
- **Deterministic rendering:** the coaching note is rendered from the move's LOCKED template + `subject`; the
  "name-the-move-not-the-answer" property is baked into the human-authored template, not the LLM's judgment.
- **MOVE REGISTRY (declarative, project-extensible — same pattern as the criteria/detector registries):** each
  move = `{id, triggers (criteria/finding-class), template, source}`. v1 moves: 1 spike/tracer-bullet ·
  2 prior-art/OSS-research/build-vs-buy · 3 pre-mortem · 4 riskiest-assumption-test · 5 weigh-alternatives
  (set-based) · 6 specification-by-example (observable "done") · 7 thin-vertical-slice · 8 ADR/one-way-door ·
  9 plan-the-verification · 11 propagate-revisions-to-children (fires when the ticket has children) ·
  12 generalize-the-finding-across-the-work (fires per review). Templates are IMPERATIVE actionable guidance.
- **C1-C4 authoring guardrails (LLM-recipient, positive-by-construction):** C1 actionable GUIDANCE (a move to
  pursue), NOT executable code/commands or the solution — enforced by the SUBJECT VALIDATOR above (not merely the
  template), since `subject` is the one free-text field the template interpolates; C2 reference findings BY ID, never restated;
  C3 select-from-registry + fill-subject (template enforces); C4 cap/cluster/front-load.
- **Caller-visible finding `id` contract:** the stable per-finding `id` is MINTED by the orchestrator (`ca03`)
  at result assembly (the content fingerprint) — its SOLE owner; this coach CONSUMES it (`finding_refs` point at
  that id) and the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`db7b`) records the same id; findings + coaching ship in ONE result
  so the reference resolves locally (no circular alignment).

## Scope
- INPUT is the CAPPED surfaced advisory set (Pass-3 surfaces the top-N advisory by priority score, config
  default 10); BLOCKING findings are surfaced UNCAPPED and may also be coached. The coach never alters the cap or
  the block decision.
- `src/rebar/` (in the gate's review pipeline) + a move-registry prompt-library entry. Reuses the rebar.llm
  single-turn structured-output path. Advisory only — coaching never affects the block/advisory decision (Pass-3).
- Grounded in LLM-feedback research (external-grounded feedback > self-reflection — Huang/DeepMind; anti-
  sycophancy; lost-in-the-middle; specific-actionable > Socratic). NOT human-pedagogy (no productive-struggle).
- Project-extensible: a project may add its own moves to the registry. Convergence expected in ~2-3 revisions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single-turn structured-output call over the surviving (advisory) findings; emits `{move_id, subject, finding_refs}` clustered by move; the LLM authors no free prose.
- [ ] Move registry (declarative, project-extensible) with moves 1-9,11,12 and LOCKED imperative templates; rendering is deterministic from template + subject.
- [ ] C1-C4 guardrails enforced by construction — INCLUDING a SUBJECT VALIDATOR (bounded noun-phrase; code/imperative/solution rejected) so C1 holds mechanically, not just via the template; plus reference-by-id, select-from-registry, cap/cluster/front-load.
- [ ] Coaching `finding_refs` reference the stable per-finding `id` MINTED by the orchestrator (`ca03`) at assembly (this coach is a CONSUMER, not the owner); findings + coaching ship in one result so the reference resolves locally.
- [ ] Advisory only — coaching never blocks and never alters the Pass-3 decision. Shared with `9da1`.
- [ ] Tested: finding→move mapping on a labelled set; deterministic render; reference resolution; a finding matching no move yields no coaching (best-effort).
baseline.summary: Pass-4 affirmative coach: single-turn structured-output coaching pass + move registry

## Why
`test_completion_floor_e2e.py::test_non_regression_floor_is_review_only` (`:178-198`) asserts,
via `inspect.getsource` over the floor functions, that tokens like `sign_manifest`,
`transition`, `reopen(` are ABSENT from their source, and that `completion_floor` does not
appear in `rebar.llm.completion`. A pure change-detector: a rename / helper / indirect call
evades it, and it exercises no runtime behavior. VALIDATED.

Context on what is testable: the floor's DECISION logic (which findings drop / are preserved /
resurface on reopen) is ALREADY behaviorally covered by the sibling tests in this file
(`test_floor_drops_and_preserves_per_gold_labels`, `test_floor_inactive_is_byte_identical`,
`test_reopen_resurfaces_dropped_finding`). And `_apply_completion_floor_to_verdict` is a PURE
verdict→verdict transform (no `repo_root`, no store/LLM I/O), so "it doesn't sign/transition"
cannot be shown by a store snapshot or by spying a close-path function it structurally never
calls — those tests are vacuous. The genuine, non-vacuous, non-duplicative behavioral content
the old test was reaching for is the floor's **observable purity contract**: it only
re-partitions findings and never emits any signing/attestation side-output.

## What
Replace the source-token test with a behavioral **purity-contract** test that runs the real
floor over the existing gold fixture (a case that drops a finding) and asserts on OBSERVABLE
state:
1. **Findings conserved (no create/lose/rewrite):** the multiset of finding ids across
   `advisory ∪ dropped` after the floor equals the set before — the floor only moves findings
   between the two lists (this is the observable analogue of "never signs/transitions/reopens";
   a floor that fabricated or dropped-without-recording a finding would fail it).
2. **No signing/attestation side-output:** the returned/mutated verdict grows NO
   `signature` / `attestation` / `attestations` key, and no new attestation KIND — the floor's
   only additions are the `dropped` list and the `coverage` narrowing annotation. (Assert the
   set of top-level verdict keys added by the floor ⊆ {`dropped`, and coverage sub-keys}.)
3. **Inputs not mutated:** the `cmap` argument and each finding's own content dict are unchanged
   by identity/value — the floor re-partitions list membership only, it does not rewrite the
   caller's inputs. (Deep-copy the inputs before the call; assert equal after.)
4. Keep the genuine artifact-contract assertion `attest._MANIFEST_PREFIX == "plan-review"`
   (no NEW attestation kind exists) — a real invariant, not a source grep.

Delete the `inspect.getsource` token-absence assertions (for the floor functions and for
`rebar.llm.completion`). The confinement-of-the-floor-to-plan-review property is NOT asserted
behaviorally, because it is a negative over a pure, structurally-separated function (any such
test is vacuous against the current code); it is left to the module structure, and this ticket
converts the false-confidence source grep into the real, observable purity assertions above.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_completion_floor_e2e.py` — replace `test_non_regression_floor_is_review_only`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A behavioral test runs the floor over the gold fixture and asserts findings are CONSERVED
      (the id set across `advisory ∪ dropped` is identical before/after — nothing fabricated or
      silently lost).
- [ ] The test asserts the floor adds NO `signature`/`attestation`/`attestations` key to the
      verdict (its only additions are `dropped` + the coverage narrowing).
- [ ] The test asserts the floor does not mutate its `cmap` input or the finding content dicts
      (pure re-partition) — verified against deep copies taken before the call.
- [ ] No `inspect.getsource` token-absence assertion remains; the
      `attest._MANIFEST_PREFIX == "plan-review"` artifact contract is retained.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Replace completion-floor review-only source-token test with a spy-based side-effect test
