baseline.description:
Discovered by the Step-7 sibling sweep while fixing bug 747f (blobless snapshot materialization).

747f added `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` to `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, joining the existing precedent in `src/rebar/_store/push.py:57` and `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:58` (`_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30`). The sweep found the *timeout* half of that bug class still live at other network-capable git call sites, each of which can block indefinitely on a stuck remote or a hung credential helper. 747f proved this is not theoretical: an unbounded git call on the materialize path produced 40 sequential per-object fetch RPCs and a measured ~2.1-hour hang.

## Scope — deliberately narrowed by the operator; recorded here, not silently

The original sweep listed 8 call sites. This ticket now covers SIX of them, in three modules. The other two were SPLIT OUT, not dropped:

**Deferred to task 983f-ee85-1e06-428e (rainbow-interested-kusimanse), linked `discovered_from` this ticket:**
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `fetch <remote> <branch>`
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` — `push origin HEAD:tickets`

**Reason for the split:** bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220 is IN PROGRESS in another session covering store/init/sync divergence and has already modified `init.py` and the fsck path. 01e8 declares no `file_impact`, so the overlap cannot be verified precisely, and the operator chose not to guess rather than risk a conflicting edit. 983f carries a `depends_on` link to 01e8 and is blocked until it closes.

## The six in-scope sites, re-verified against origin/main @ ed9d5e28d

**A. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (2 sites) — ALREADY BOUNDED; the original sweep note is STALE.**

`_remote_ref_absent` -> `ls-remote --exit-code` and `_push_lease_cas` -> `push --force-with-lease` both already pass `timeout=_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` (30.0s). This is structurally guaranteed, not incidental: the module's single git seam `_git(repo_root, args, *, timeout: float, ...)` declares `timeout` as a REQUIRED keyword-only parameter with no default, and it holds the module's only `run_git` call, so an unbounded git call is unrepresentable there. A timeout already surfaces as `RefLockTimeoutError` naming the operation and the bound, fail-closed (treated as HELD). **No edit is required or made here** — which also honours the standing instruction not to touch `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` while a parallel session owns it.

**B. `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py::clone_change_ref` — UNBOUNDED, fixed by this ticket.**

Five `subprocess.run` calls, none passing a timeout: `git init`, `fetch --depth 2 <repo_url> <revision_ref>`, `checkout FETCH_HEAD`, `remote add origin`, `fetch --depth 1 origin refs/heads/tickets`. The two fetches are network-capable. Additionally `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` is neither an `OSError` nor a `CalledProcessError`, so it sits outside the existing `except` tuple — a timeout would escape the token-redacting handler entirely, and `TimeoutExpired.cmd` carries the `user:token@host` fetch URL, making an unredacted timeout a credential-leak path as well as a hang.

**C. `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` — UNBOUNDED, fixed by this ticket.**

The single `_git(cwd, *args)` helper calls `subprocess.run(...)` with no timeout, so EVERY git call in the module is unbounded, including the two network-capable ones: `fetch --quiet review <branch>` and `fetch --quiet tickets <branch>`. A `TimeoutExpired` would also bypass `_git_ok`'s `WorkspaceError` conversion.

## Value chosen: `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`, matching 747f rather than `_store`

Both live modules do a COLD fetch into a freshly created directory (`gerrit_client` runs `git init` on a new dest per change; `workspace` fetches into a fresh `mkdtemp`), and `workspace`'s fetches are not even shallow. That is 747f's profile — a legitimately large RPC, legitimately minutes on a cold clone — not the `_store` profile, which is an INCREMENTAL ref-sized push/fetch against an already-warm clone and so is correctly bound at 30s. Choosing 30s here would risk breaking a working cold-clone path; 300s converts an unbounded hang into a bounded, diagnosable failure without narrowing any legitimate one. One constant per module (not a per-call-site matrix) matches the existing `_GIT_TIMEOUT` precedent instead of inventing a new mechanism.

## Resolved: the `git archive` question (was flagged UNJUDGED)

`src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py` materializes via `git archive --format=tar <sha>`, and the sweep asked whether it degrades like the `read-tree`/`checkout-index` pair 747f fixed. **Measured read-only; answer NO.** On a 40-file `--filter=blob:none` fixture with `uploadpack.allowFilter` enabled (git 2.55.0), `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` `child_start` counting shows 40 missing blobs resolved by exactly ONE batched child `git fetch ... --filter=blob:none --stdin`, versus 40 separate sequential fetches for the primitive pair 747f fixed. `git archive` therefore DOES batch its promisor prefetch and is NOT an instance of the 747f bug class. No change made and no follow-up filed; the file is owned by a parallel session and was inspected read-only only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` defines a module-level `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and all five `clone_change_ref` subprocess calls pass it, with a comment justifying 300 against the cited 747f and `_store` precedents.
- [ ] `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` defines a module-level `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and its single `_git` helper passes it, so every git call in the module is bounded.
- [ ] A `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `clone_change_ref` is converted to a `GerritError` that names the timed-out git operation and the bound, and is routed through the EXISTING token-redaction path so the `user:token@host` URL never appears in the message.
- [ ] A `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `workspace._git` is converted to a `WorkspaceError` that names the timed-out git operation and the bound, never propagating the raw exception.
- [ ] The two `_ref_lock.py` sites are confirmed already bounded and left unedited, with that confirmation recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] The two deferred `_commands/` sites are recorded on task 983f-ee85-1e06-428e with their blocking reason, NOT silently dropped from scope.
- [ ] Verified by the commands in the Testing section below: the new held-out test passes, and lint, typecheck, and the default suite all exit zero.

## Testing

A new held-out test file `tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py` is written BEFORE the fix and proven RED first, then run GREEN against the implementation, and mutation-checked by reverting the timeout to confirm it returns to RED. It asserts, without any network access (the git call is monkeypatched to raise `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`):

1. Both modules expose a positive numeric `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, mirroring the `tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py` assertion shape.
2. Every `clone_change_ref` subprocess invocation receives a `timeout` kwarg.
3. A timing-out `clone_change_ref` raises `GerritError` (not `TimeoutExpired`), the message names the git operation and the bound, and the bot token does NOT appear in it.
4. A timing-out `workspace._git` raises `WorkspaceError` (not `TimeoutExpired`) naming the operation and the bound.

Proving commands, all run from the worktree with its venv first on `PATH`:

- `pytest tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py -q`
- `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py -q` (no regression in the two modules' existing coverage)
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- `make test`
baseline.summary: Bound the remaining network-capable git call sites with an explicit timeout

baseline.description:
# The pass that GENERATES blocking findings moves to the cheapest model the moment b690 lands

## Severity framing

This is not a cost or consistency issue. **Pass-1 of plan-review is the finder** — it produces the findings that become blocking and gate every `claim`. Moving it to a weaker model makes the gate QUIETLY MORE PERMISSIVE, and there is no alarm for "the review was weaker than it should have been". `b690`'s change is `LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1` and green on every offline test, because **none of this risk is test-detectable**: the offline suite substitutes `FunctionModel`/`FakeRunner` for exactly the thing that changes, which is WHICH MODEL a live gate calls.

## The mechanism, verified end to end

Under this repo's actual config there is **no `model_classes` table anywhere** (no `[llm]` in `rebar.toml`, no `[tool.rebar…]` LLM keys in `pyproject.toml`, no `.rebar/config.conf`, no `REBAR_LLM_*` in shell rc / LaunchAgents / CI), so classes take built-in defaults:

    trivial -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5   standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   LLMConfig.from_env().model -> claude-opus-4-8

**Crucially, plan-review's runner floor is NOT `cfg.model`.** `plan_review/__init__.py:609` calls `produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, _verifier_cfg(cfg), …)`, so the whole run's `runner._config.model` is `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. Then:

1. `gate_dispatch.py:163` builds `ProductionBatchRunner(runner=get_runner(_verifier_cfg(cfg)))`
   → floor = sonnet.
2. `production_batch_runner.run` does `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0]))`
   → `plan-review.yaml:62-65` rung 0 is `trivial` → **haiku**.
3. `pass1.py:484` → `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` → `passes.pass1_chunk` builds
   `RunRequest(..., config=cfg)` (`passes.py:319-330`).
4. **PRE-b690** the runner opened `cfg = self._config` and DISCARDED `req.config` → Pass-1 actually
   ran on **sonnet**. **POST-b690** it honours the declaration and runs on **haiku**.

Measured:

    gate runner floor model  : anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    Pass-1 batch cfg.model   : anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5
    PRE-b690  effective model: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    POST-b690 effective model: anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

**The smoking gun that this was never intended-and-tested:** `origin/main`'s own `_verifier_cfg` docstring asserts "The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML `model_ladder` via the ProductionBatchRunner, not `cfg.model`." **That comment is FALSE on main**, and `b690` is what makes it true. `git log -L62,66` on `plan-review.yaml` shows Pass-1 has declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was born (originally the literal `claude-haiku-4-5`) and has **never once actually run on it**.

## Why the ladder does not save it

`pass1_with_ladder` escalates on a **context-limit signal** — it is a SIZE ladder, not a quality ladder (its own docstring says so). A plan that fits haiku's 200k window stays on haiku forever. Some Pass-1 chunks also run `execution_mode="agentic"` (code-grounding with tool calls), where the drop from sonnet to haiku is a large capability change, not a marginal one.

Secondary effect on the prerequisite finder (`registry.py:361-367` gives it `"default_posture": "blocking"`): `pack_prerequisite_bins(..., model=cfg.model)` now packs for haiku's 200k instead of sonnet's 1M, so context-limit escalation genuinely fires where it previously could not. Escalation does work (`models_at_or_above('claude-haiku-4-5')` → `['claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-opus-4-8']`), but the first attempt is a real downgrade and every attempt burns tokens.

## Why it is silent rather than loud

The gates fail CLOSED on errors — `attest_gate.py:112-125` blocks a claim on a missing/stale attestation, and an LLM outage degrades to INDETERMINATE → no signature → claim blocked. That is the loud path and it is fine. **This is the other kind:** a haiku Pass-1 that surfaces fewer grounded findings yields a **PASS**, which gets signed, and the claim proceeds. The sidecar records only the VERIFIER's model (`data.model`), never Pass-1's, so it is invisible in the artifacts too.

## An asymmetry worth deciding on

Code-review's Pass-1 finder declares **`frontier`** (`code-review.yaml`, landed by 3768). Plan-review's Pass-1 declares **`trivial`**. Both are finders that generate blocking findings. That asymmetry may be deliberate, but it has never been effective, so it has never been evaluated.

## The decision, made by the operator and confirmed by archaeology

**Pass-1 (the finder) runs on `frontier`/opus. Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach run on `standard`/sonnet.** That split is what `_verifier_cfg` was written to express, and its own docstring already asserts it ("The Pass-1 finder is unaffected"). The docstring has simply been false since 2026-06-27.

This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference. The sidecar record shows 115 plan reviews generating findings on opus up to 2026-06-27, then zero ever since — a total changeover one day after `4beec08a4` introduced the verifier downgrade and accidentally applied it to the whole run. See the archaeology comment for the day-by-day table.

**b690 is the ENABLER.** Until it landed, `PydanticAIRunner.run` discarded `req.config`, so NO ladder rung could influence Pass-1 at all. With b690, the declaration is finally reachable — and it says `trivial`, which is why the regression would deepen rather than heal on its own.

**The change:** `plan-review.yaml`'s `model_ladder` entry rung `trivial` -> `frontier`. `standard` would freeze the regression; `trivial` would deepen it.

Note that with rung 0 at `frontier`, `models_at_or_above(opus)` returns just `[opus]`, so model escalation becomes a no-op. That costs nothing: sonnet and opus share the same 1M window, so the only size-meaningful step was ever haiku->sonnet, and the size handling that matters (batch -> one-criterion-per-call -> the P8 too-big finding) is independent of the model rungs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `plan-review.yaml`'s Pass-1 `model_ladder` entry rung is `frontier`, so findings generate on
      opus as they did before 2026-06-27
- [ ] Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach remain on the verifier model (`standard`/sonnet) — this ticket
      must not disturb the downgrade that `_verifier_cfg` correctly applies to them
- [ ] a test asserts the EFFECTIVE model of Pass-1 at the seam that decides it
      (`ProductionBatchRunner` -> `run_pass1` -> `pass1_chunk`, i.e. the model reaching the runner),
      so a future change cannot silently move the finder again. Asserting the YAML text is NOT
      sufficient — the YAML has said `trivial` for five weeks while sonnet actually ran
- [ ] a test asserts Pass-1 and Pass-2 resolve to DIFFERENT models under the default config, since
      the defect was precisely the two collapsing onto one
- [ ] `_verifier_cfg`'s docstring claim that "the Pass-1 finder is unaffected" is either true after
      this change or corrected — it must not remain a false assertion in the code
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real plan-review run after the change records opus for the Pass-1 finder,
      cited from `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` per-step attribution (which story b690 made possible)
- [ ] the prerequisite finder's bin packing is checked against opus's window, since
      `pack_prerequisite_bins` sizes to `cfg.model`

## Notes

Found by an independent landing-safety assessment of the epic stack, NOT by the offline suite — which is green at the stack tip and cannot see this. `b690` itself is closed and correct in its own terms: it made declarations effective. This ticket is about one declaration that turns out to be wrong.
baseline.summary: b690 silently downgrades the plan-review Pass-1 finder from sonnet to haiku, weakening the claim gate that generates blocking findings

content.text: ## What
DEPRECATE list-epics in favor of generic list/query, by first EXPANDING the generic list filters to cover what list-epics filters by, then making list-epics a deprecating alias.
list-epics' filters/criteria all derive from the same reducer+graph the generic reads use; only the FILTER EXPOSURE is missing from generic list. So:
1. Expand generic 'list' filters (reads.py list_states + ticket_reads CLI + library list_tickets + MCP list tool):
- --min-children=N : tickets with >= N non-deleted direct children (child count via parent_id over reduced state).
- --unblocked / --blocked : filter by blocking state (reuse rebar.graph find_ready_tickets / all_blockers_closed).
These are universal filters, useful beyond epics.

2. Deprecate list-epics: emit a deprecation warning at every surface (CLI stderr, library DeprecationWarning, MCP tool description) steering to 'rebar list --type=epic --status=open,in_progress [--unblocked] [--min-children=N]'.

3. FOR NOW keep list-epics' current behavior + output ({p0_bugs,epics} envelope, child counts) intact so the MCP outputSchema + consumers don't break; the bespoke ticket-list-epics.sh (453 LOC) is removed in a later step once consumers migrate.
p0_bugs is a separable bug metric ('list --type=bug --priority=0'); not part of the generic list expansion.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] generic 'list' gains --min-children + --unblocked/--blocked at CLI + library + MCP (parity with list-epics' filter criteria)
- [ ] new filters covered by tests (dual-impl where relevant)
- [ ] list-epics emits a deprecation warning at CLI (stderr) + library + MCP, steering to generic list; behavior/output otherwise unchanged
- [ ] existing list-epics suites still green (behavior preserved); deprecation warning does not pollute stdout/JSON

content.text: # S2 — Deploy Gerrit + review-bot receiver (docker-compose) behind nginx + TLS
## Why
Run Gerrit and the **review-bot webhook receiver** as the two containers on the box, reachable
over HTTPS at `rebar.solutions.navateam.com`. Gerrit needs a `%2F`-safe reverse proxy — the
community uses nginx/Apache, NOT Caddy (Caddy URL-decodes paths by default with no global
switch, which breaks Gerrit's change/project screens; no confirmed Caddy+Gerrit recipe exists).
This is the bottom layer of the d251 "proven pipe": Gerrit serving, the receiver reachable over
HTTP, TLS terminated, secrets from SSM. NOTE (peer-pattern correction): Gerrit POSTs webhook
JSON, not MCP protocol — so the right component is a thin HTTP **webhook receiver that IMPORTS
the review kernel as a library**, NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server exposed over HTTP (a FastMCP
HTTP transport would reject a Gerrit webhook by spec; `streamable-http` is a red herring here).
## What
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`:
- official `gerritcodereview/gerrit` pinned to a PATCH tag (e.g. `3.14.1`) with persistent
volumes (git/index/cache/etc/db on the data volume) + the two-step init. DERISK NOTE (E4):
bare minor tags `3.14`/`3.13` do NOT exist on Docker Hub; pin a published patch tag
(`3.14.1`/`3.13.7`/`3.12.8`), all of which publish arm64 manifests.
- the **review-bot container** (signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sourced from SSM into the boot
`.env` — see secrets bullet; write-gating as needed); both `restart: unless-stopped`, pinned
tags. The receiver calls the `rebar.llm` library functions DIRECTLY, so the LLM review path is
enabled simply by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` being present + the `[agents]` extra being installed —
there is NO separate allow-flag for direct library calls (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` gates only the
stdio MCP server's tool wrappers, which this receiver does not use, so it is intentionally not
set).
- the Gerrit data volume is declared **`external: true`** (created once, outside compose) so a
stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy git/NoteDb/index state. S2 only DECLARES this
external data volume; volume snapshotting + retention is owned by **S7's DLM daily-snapshot
policy** (see S7), and the restore procedure is in the runbook. Freeze-and-restore (the d251
recovery posture, no break-glass v1) operates against the snapshots S7 manages.
- **Review-bot webhook receiver (in-scope S2 deliverable).** The second container is a thin
**webhook->review->vote receiver** (an ASGI/FastAPI service under `src/rebar/review_bot/`)
that IMPORTS the review kernel as a library and exposes a plain HTTP endpoint Gerrit's
`webhooks` plugin POSTs to. This is deliberately NOT the stdio rebar-MCP server over HTTP
(Gerrit speaks webhooks, not MCP JSON-RPC; an MCP HTTP transport would reject the request).
The stdio MCP server is unchanged and remains for agent use only. The receiver binds
`0.0.0.0:<PORT>` (default `8000`); nginx routes
`location /review/ { proxy_pass http://review-bot:<PORT>/; }`. Decision recorded in
`docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.
- `gerrit.config`: `container.heapLimit=2g` with `core.packedGitLimit` budgeted INSIDE the heap
(~512m-1g), NoteDb, `canonicalWebUrl=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`, sshd/httpd thread
caps + `sshd.batchThreads` to avoid parallel-clone OOM.
- nginx + certbot (Let's Encrypt) terminating TLS on 443: route Gerrit (`%2F`-safe: `proxy_pass`
with no path) and the receiver (`location /review/`) behind the one cert; Gerrit SSH on 29418.
- **certbot renewal lifecycle.** Initial issuance AND renewal: a systemd timer (or cron) runs
`certbot renew` twice daily with a deploy-hook that reloads nginx; nginx serves an
`/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location (webroot) so HTTP-01 renewal succeeds. Installed by
the bootstrap script.
- **secrets bootstrap (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`).** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` runs
`aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` for the signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (via the
**instance role**, no static keys) and writes a root-only (`0600`) `.env` that compose reads,
BEFORE `docker compose up`. The `.env` is gitignored + ephemeral (regenerated each boot, never
committed); the script is idempotent and **aborts** if SSM is unreachable (never reuses a
stale `.env`). Recorded in `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`.
- **IAM instance role (least privilege).** Grants `ssm:GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to
the project parameter-path prefix only (e.g.
`arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1:896586841071:parameter/rebar/prod/*`) plus `kms:Decrypt` on the
SecureString key — no wildcard. Defined in the infra IaC.
- **observability (minimal).** Both containers log via `journald`; a health probe hits `/` and
the receiver `/review/` health path; a disk-usage alarm guards the Gerrit data volume.
## Scope
In: containers, the external Gerrit data volume DECLARATION, base `gerrit.config`,
nginx+TLS+certbot renewal, the review-bot receiver HTTP surface + hosting, SSM->.env secrets
bootstrap, the SSM IAM instance role, minimal logging/health/disk observability. Out: Gerrit
project/label/submit-req (S3); the bot identity + event wiring + the receiver's review/vote
LOGIC (S4 — S2 stands up the *service*, S4 wires its behavior); replication (S5); the data
volume's snapshot + retention policy (S7's DLM daily-snapshot policy owns it — S2 only declares
the volume).
## Files
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `infra/compose/gerrit.config`, `infra/nginx/*.conf`
(incl. the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location and the `location /review/` upstream)
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM -> ephemeral `.env`), bootstrap scripts under `infra/`
(install the certbot-renew timer, the health/disk checks)
- `src/rebar/review_bot/` (the webhook-receiver ASGI service — skeleton/health endpoint in S2;
review+vote behavior in S4)
- `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`, `docs/adr/0008-secrets-source-ssm.md`
- `.gitignore` (ensure `infra/compose/.env` is ignored)
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gerrit is reachable at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` with a valid Let's Encrypt cert.
- [ ] A Gerrit change screen / a project path containing `%2F` renders correctly (encoded-slash round-trip verified end-to-end through nginx).

- [ ] certbot renewal is automated: the timer/cron is installed + enabled, the nginx `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` location serves the HTTP-01 challenge, and `certbot renew --dry-run` succeeds and reloads nginx via the deploy-hook.
- [ ] Gerrit SSH clone works on 29418 and the admin account is bootstrapped.

- [ ] Gerrit data persists across `docker compose down/up` and an instance reboot; the data volume is `external: true` so `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it. (Snapshot + retention of this volume is owned by S7, not S2.)

- [ ] The review-bot webhook receiver (a plain HTTP service importing the review kernel as a library, NOT the stdio MCP over HTTP) is reachable through nginx at `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/` — a POST reaches the receiver process (not a 502); the decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0007-review-bot-receiver.md`.

- [ ] The review-bot container's signing key + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are sourced from SSM at boot by `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` into a `0600`, gitignored, ephemeral `.env` (never baked into the image/compose, never committed); the script authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable. The receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra alone (no `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` flag, which gates only the stdio MCP server, is set).
- [ ] The SSM IAM instance role grants `GetParameter`/`GetParameters` scoped to `parameter/rebar/prod/*` only (no wildcard), verified against the attached policy.
- [ ] Both containers log to `journald`; a health probe covers `/` and `/review/`, and a disk-usage alarm covers the Gerrit data volume.

- [ ] Gerrit runs a supported version at an EXISTING arm64 patch tag (e.g. `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`; a bare minor tag like `3.14` is NOT used — it doesn't exist), with `heapLimit=2g` and `packedGitLimit` budgeted within it.
## Round-12 plan-review remediation (2026-06-30 — recalibrated gate BLOCK + critical advisories)
**Blocking — internal sequencing (phased build, each phase verified before the next):**

- **Phase 1 (riskiest first):** Gerrit `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1` (arm64) container up with the external data volume + base `gerrit.config`; reachable over plain HTTP through nginx (no TLS yet); `%2F`-encoded path round-trips. Proves the arm64 image + the `%2F`-safe proxy before anything else is layered on.

- **Phase 2:** nginx TLS via certbot (Let's Encrypt) on 443 + the `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` webroot + the twice-daily `certbot renew` timer with the nginx-reload deploy-hook; `certbot renew --dry-run` green.
- **Phase 3:** `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (SSM->ephemeral 0600 `.env`) via the instance role + the scoped IAM policy attachment (S2's separately-named inline policy on the S1-owned role).
- **Phase 4:** the review-bot receiver container reachable through nginx at `/review/` (skeleton + health only — review/vote LOGIC is S4b).
- **Phase 5:** observability (journald, `/` + `/review/` health probes, data-volume disk alarm).
**Critical advisories folded in:**

- **`webhooks` plugin is NOT bundled in the official image (seam to S4a):** S2 stands up the *service* only. The Gerrit site's `plugins/` dir is a bind-mount/volume path so a version-matched (3.14.1) `webhooks` + `events-log` plugin jar can be dropped in; ACTUAL plugin install + wiring is **S4a**. S2 verifies only that the site supports dropping plugin jars (the plugins dir is writable + on the persistent volume). No S2 AC depends on webhooks delivering events.

- **Receiver framework dependency (was absent):** add a `reviewbot` optional extra to `pyproject.toml` = `fastapi` + `uvicorn[standard]`. The receiver container builds via `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` (`pip install .[agents,reviewbot]`). The stdio MCP server is untouched.
- **Dockerfile added** to Files: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`.

- **`core.packedGitLimit` is OFF-HEAP (correction):** JGit's `core.packedGitLimit` is the mmap'd packfile budget, sized against TOTAL RAM, NOT inside the Java heap. Config: `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) + `core.packedGitLimit` ~1g budgeted against the ~8 GB box RAM ALONGSIDE (not within) the heap, leaving headroom for the OS + the receiver container.

- **`fetch-secrets.sh` explicit SSM-leaf -> env mapping** (the 7 params S1 created): `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password`->`GERRIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key`->`GERRIT_SSH_HOST_ED25519_KEY`, `github-replication-deploy-key`->`GITHUB_REPLICATION_DEPLOY_KEY`, `mcp-hmac-signing-key`->`MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`, `anthropic-api-key`->`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `alert-endpoint`->`ALERT_ENDPOINT`, `gerrit-bot-token`->`GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN`. (Same contract as S1's user_data.sh; S2 sources only the subset the containers need.)

- **LLM path enablement:** the receiver's LLM review path is enabled by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + the `[agents]` extra ALONE — `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` (which gates only the stdio MCP server) is intentionally NOT set.

- **External volume creation step:** the Gerrit data volume is a Docker `external: true` volume backed by the `/var/gerrit` EBS mount; `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` (the boot orchestrator) runs `docker volume create --driver local --opt type=none --opt o=bind --opt device=/var/gerrit gerrit_data` (idempotent) BEFORE `docker compose up`, so a stray `docker compose down -v` cannot destroy it.

- **Port single-source:** the receiver port is one env var `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` (default 8000) in the `.env`; compose and the nginx upstream both read it (nginx via an envsubst-templated conf at boot), so the two can't drift.
**Added / updated ACs:**
- [ ] The build is phased (Phase 1 Gerrit+HTTP -> 2 TLS -> 3 secrets/IAM -> 4 receiver -> 5 observability); Phase 1 reachability is proven before TLS is layered on.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares a `reviewbot` extra (fastapi + uvicorn); `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot` builds the receiver via `.[agents,reviewbot]`.
- [ ] `gerrit.config` sets `container.heapLimit=2g` (on-heap) and `core.packedGitLimit` as a SEPARATE off-heap budget (~1g) sized against box RAM, NOT inside the heap.

- [ ] `fetch-secrets.sh` maps the enumerated `/rebar/prod/*` leaves to the documented env-var names, writes a 0600 ephemeral `.env`, authenticates via the instance role, is idempotent, and aborts if SSM is unreachable.
- [ ] The Gerrit data volume is created as an `external` bind volume on `/var/gerrit` by `compose-up.sh` before `docker compose up`; `docker compose down -v` does not destroy it.
- [ ] The receiver port is single-sourced (`REVIEW_BOT_PORT`) and consumed by both compose and the nginx `/review/` upstream.
- [ ] The Gerrit site `plugins/` dir is on the persistent volume + writable (so S4a can drop version-matched webhooks/events-log jars); no S2 AC depends on event delivery.

baseline.description:
# Comment sync (append-only) with persistent Jira-comment-ID map + rich rendering

## Context / Problem
Comment sync currently identifies comments by **body equality** (a normalized-text key computed in `outbound_comments._diff_comments`), which is fragile: two comments with the same text collide, and an edited body looks like a brand-new comment. The in-code note at `outbound_comments.py` (`"PR #402 … ID-based binding once available; this body-equality match is the baseline"`) already anticipates the fix. The team has settled comment semantics as **append-only** — mirror comment *creation* both ways, but do not sync edits or deletes — which keeps the design simple and matches the reconciler's existing inbound behavior of skipping already-known Jira comment IDs.

This story ALSO **owns the DC comment-diff dedup-key migration that `3388` deliberately deferred here.** `3388` redefines `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` from identity to the rendering form for descriptions, but keeps the comment-diff path injecting the plain/identity normalizer UNCHANGED (via the a32a `_resolve_codec` seam, defaulting to `_IdentityCodec`) so the description cutover does not shift the comment dedup key. Flipping the comment path to the real rendering codec — and keeping comment-diff convergent when it renders rich — is this story's job, not `3388`'s.

## Approach
Two coupled changes, both append-only and echo-safe:

1. **Stable identity by a local comment key + the returned Jira ID, not body.** Each
   rebar comment originates from a COMMENT event whose **HLC `timestamp`** (unique,
   monotonic; already threaded onto the compiled comment entry at
   `reducer/_processors.py:349`, alongside `author`) is the **stable local comment
   identity** — nothing else on the entry (`body`/`author`/`source_*`) is
   collision-proof once body-equality is abandoned. Maintain a **persistent map
   `local_comment_key (HLC) → Jira comment ID`** in the binding state. Outbound: when
   rebar has a comment whose local key has no mapped Jira ID, create it in Jira and
   record the returned Jira comment ID against that local key. Inbound: mirror Jira
   comments whose IDs are not already values in the map as new rebar comments (whose
   entries carry the existing `jira_comment_id`, bug 85a1 `_processors.py:354-356`,
   the inbound half of this identity). **Append-only**: never push rebar edits/deletes
   to Jira comments and never apply Jira comment edits/deletes to rebar — an
   already-mapped key/ID is never re-synced (the ID map is the PRIMARY durable echo
   guard for comments, with the body-key match RETAINED as a secondary crash-durability
   fallback, and complementing the existing
   `RECONCILER_MARKER` machine-comment guard, `outbound_comments.py:72/177-184`,
   which still excludes bridge-internal payloads). The ID map is change-gated and
   fixed-shape (one small entry per comment, added once) to respect epic `0303`'s
   churn discipline.
1a. **Capture the returned Jira comment ID at the enactment sites (the write-back
   data path), carrying the local key through the mutation.** The Jira comment ID is
   only obtainable as `SupportsComments.add_comment`'s return value — a
   `dict[str, Any]` carrying `{"id": …}` (`_backend.py:491`; both transports return
   this shape — `adapters/jira/backend.py:265` Cloud,
   `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:433` DC), but **both enacting sites currently
   DISCARD it**: `dispatch_one.py:418` (create path) and
   `dispatch_apply_phases.py:165` (update path). Two links make the capture possible
   and must be built:
   (i) **the local key must ride ON the mutation entry** — the outbound builders
   `_map_comments_for_create` (`outbound_comments.py:148`) and the `_diff_comments`
   append (`:147`) today emit `{"action":"add","body":…}` with no key; this story adds
   `"local_comment_key": <HLC>` so the enactment loop knows which local comment a
   returned id belongs to;
   (ii) **the binding-store handle must reach both loops — and the update loop needs
   the WHOLE call chain threaded, not just its leaf.** The create loop is already
   wired: `create_one` receives `binding_store` (`dispatch_one.py:154`), so it can
   call `binding_store.record_comment_id(local_comment_key, returned["id"])` directly.
   The update loop is NOT: `_update_one_dispatch_comments`
   (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:147`) has no handle, and neither does its caller
   `update_one` (`dispatch_one.py:448`) nor `update_one`'s two production callers.
   So this story threads `binding_store` down the full chain:
   `handle_update` (`apply_handlers.py:201`) — which ALREADY holds the handle as
   `ctx.binding_store` (`BatchApplyContext.binding_store`, `apply_handlers.py:81`,
   already passed to `handle_create` at `:150`) — passes it into a new optional
   `binding_store` parameter on `update_one` (`dispatch_one.py:448`), which forwards
   it to `_update_one_dispatch_comments`. Production outbound updates route through
   this BATCH path (`applier._apply_batch` builds the `BatchApplyContext`;
   `applier.py` comment: "outbound/untyped go to the legacy `_apply_batch`"). The
   second, typed-leaf caller `_apply_outbound_update` (`apply_outbound.py:159`, def
   `:126`) delegates to the same `update_one`; it is threaded for parity by adding an
   optional `binding_store` param forwarded from `_apply_typed`
   (`applier.py:447`, which already receives `binding_store`) and passed through to
   `update_one`. `update_one`'s param defaults to `None`, so every other caller and
   all existing tests are unaffected.
   The id-key extraction (`returned["id"]`) is confirmed uniform across the Cloud
   (acli) and DC transports. Failures stay non-fatal exactly as today (the existing
   `comment_errors` capture is unchanged); only a successful create records a mapping.
   **Crash-durability:** `record_comment_id` `save()`s the map entry IMMEDIATELY on the
   successful `add_comment` return — a write-ahead point mirroring the binding-store
   protocol (`binding_store.py:6-28`, e.g. `record_pending_key … save()` before the
   next Jira call) — so a process hard-killed after the Jira create but before the next
   step cannot lose the mapping. As a second layer, the demoted body-equality guard
   (§1b) still catches a comment already on Jira should any single map write be lost,
   so this migration cannot reopen the DIG-5301 duplicate-comment class.
1b. **Two identity stores, one authoritative per DIRECTION — disjoint, never
   consulted across directions.** The repo ALREADY stores inbound-origin identity as
   a per-comment `jira_comment_id` field on the compiled entry (bug 85a1,
   `reducer/_processors.py:354-356`, stamped when a Jira comment is mirrored inbound).
   This story does NOT move or duplicate that: the existing per-entry
   `jira_comment_id` stays authoritative for INBOUND-origin comments, and the new
   binding-state map `local_comment_key → jira_id` is authoritative for
   OUTBOUND-origin (rebar-created) comments. **The two never need to consult each
   other, because each direction already has its own loop-breaker:**
   - **Outbound direction** — the OUTBOUND differ (`outbound_comments.py`) skips a
     local comment when EITHER (a) its local HLC key is already a key in the outbound
     map (a rebar comment already created on Jira — never re-create), OR (b) the local
     comment carries a `jira_comment_id` field (it is INBOUND-origin — mirrored FROM
     Jira, so it must never be pushed back). (a) is the new ID map, and (b) preserves —
     via the local field instead of body comparison — the existing guarantee that
     inbound-mirrored comments are not echoed outbound. The existing normalized-body
     membership test (`outbound_comments.py:143`) is NOT removed; it is DEMOTED to a
     belt-and-suspenders SECONDARY skip so that a lost/unpersisted map entry (process
     hard-killed between a successful `add_comment` and the map `save()`) cannot
     re-post a comment already present on Jira. The outbound differ is the ONE consumer
     of the map; it also reads the local `jira_comment_id` field (which the reducer
     already stamps, `_processors.py:354-356`).
   - **Inbound direction** — the INBOUND differ `_diff_comments_inbound`
     (`inbound_differ.py:280`) is left UNCHANGED and does NOT receive the outbound map.
     It already refuses to re-import our own outbound comments two ways: (a) every
     outbound body is decorated with `RECONCILER_MARKER` (`outbound_comments.py:178`),
     and the inbound differ skips any Jira comment whose body contains that marker
     (`inbound_differ.py:337`, "outbound echo — do not pull our own comment back in");
     (b) it already skips any Jira id matching a local `jira_comment_id`
     (`inbound_differ.py:299,319-321`), which covers inbound-origin comments.
   So the map is authoritative for the OUTBOUND direction ONLY; the inbound path needs
   no handle to it, and there is no cross-direction competition. This makes ID identity
   the PRIMARY outbound guard while DEMOTING the body-equality membership test
   (`outbound_comments.py:143`) to a secondary crash-durability fallback, and leaves
   BOTH the inbound differ and the inbound `jira_comment_id` field as-is.
2. **Render comment bodies through the codec — adding the encode step the comment
   send path currently lacks — and migrate the dedup key.** Outbound comment bodies
   are rendered through the SAME `RichTextCodec.to_wire` seam the descriptions use
   (`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` — `AdfCodec.to_wire` for Cloud, the
   now-rendering `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` for DC after `3388`), applied in
   `_map_comments_for_create`/`_decorate_outbound_comment`. **The Cloud comment send
   path needs an explicit encode step that does not exist today:** unlike the
   description path, which serializes ADF on the wire at `acli.py:205`
   (`--description json.dumps(_text_to_adf(...))`), `acli_cli_ops.add_comment`
   (`acli_cli_ops.py:469`) sends `--body <str>` with NO ADF encoding. Because Cloud
   `to_wire` returns an ADF **dict**, this story adds the analogous serialize step on
   the comment create path (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))`, mirroring
   `acli.py:205`); DC's `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` returns a **str**, so the existing
   `--body <str>` path already carries rendered wiki unchanged. To keep the local
   comparison key aligned with the rendered wire, this story **flips the a32a codec
   injection** (`_diff_comments`'s `_resolve_codec` argument, `outbound_comments.py`)
   from the default `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`, so the local dedup
   key is `normalize_outbound`-consistent with what lands on Jira. Because identity
   is now the ID map, the dedup key is only a secondary guard, so the migration
   cannot reintroduce duplicate re-posts: an AC asserts DC comment-diff still
   converges (zero duplicate re-post) after the injection flip (the deliberate mirror
   of `3388`'s `test_dc_comment_diff_unchanged_by_cutover`, which pinned the key
   UNCHANGED under the description-only cutover). The wire shape is asserted against
   the REAL create surface, not only a fake.

Descriptions + the description cutover ship first (`e59d`/`271c`/`3388`, on which this story depends), so this builds on the codec-rendering + state-echo-suppression already in place.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — persistent per-binding
  comment-ID map `local_comment_key → jira_id` plus a `record_comment_id(...)` writer
  that **`save()`s the entry immediately on the successful `add_comment` return**
  (write-ahead, mirroring the binding-store protocol at `binding_store.py:6-28`), so a
  hard-kill after the Jira create cannot lose the mapping and re-post next pass
  (change-gated, append-only, fixed-shape entry).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py` — comment differ that
  makes the ID map + inbound-origin `jira_comment_id` the PRIMARY identity (keyed via
  the local comment key), **skipping a local comment when EITHER its local key is in
  the outbound map OR it carries an inbound-origin `jira_comment_id` field** (so
  inbound-mirrored comments are never re-pushed); the existing normalized-body
  membership test (`:143`) is **RETAINED as a belt-and-suspenders SECONDARY skip**
  (crash-durability: a lost/unpersisted map entry cannot re-post a comment already on
  Jira — guards the DIG-5301 duplicate-comment class); both builders
  (`_map_comments_for_create` `:148`, `_diff_comments` append `:147`) add
  `"local_comment_key": <HLC>` to the mutation entry; outbound create renders via
  `RichTextCodec.to_wire` in `_map_comments_for_create`/`_decorate_outbound_comment`;
  flip the `_diff_comments` a32a codec injection (`_resolve_codec`) from
  `_IdentityCodec` to the real `RichTextCodec`; preserve the `RECONCILER_MARKER`
  machine-comment exclusion.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — the SOLE caller of both
  comment builders (`compute_outbound_mutations`): thread the already-held
  `binding_store` (or the resolved comment-ID map) plus the resolved backend
  `RichTextCodec` into `_diff_comments` at `:741-743` (which today passes only
  `inbound_mapper` and relies on the default `_IdentityCodec`/no-map), so the
  outbound-map skip and the real-codec render are reachable; `_map_comments_for_create`
  (`:624`) reads the local key from the ticket entries and needs no new caller argument.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` (`:418`, create path) —
  capture `add_comment`'s returned `{"id": …}` and call
  `binding_store.record_comment_id(local_comment_key, id)` (binding_store already
  threaded here, `:154`); keep the non-fatal `comment_errors` behavior.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py` (`:165`, update
  path) — capture `add_comment`'s returned `{"id": …}` in
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`:147`) and record it via the threaded
  `binding_store`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` (`update_one`, `:448`) — add
  an optional `binding_store` parameter (default `None`) and forward it to
  `_update_one_dispatch_comments`, so the update loop can reach the map.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_handlers.py` (`handle_update`, `:201`) —
  pass the already-held `ctx.binding_store` (`BatchApplyContext.binding_store`, `:81`)
  into `update_one`; this is the production outbound-update (batch) path.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_outbound.py` (`_apply_outbound_update`,
  def `:126`, `update_one` call `:159`) — add an optional `binding_store` param
  forwarded from `_apply_typed` (`applier.py:447`, which already receives it) and pass
  it through to `update_one`, so the typed-leaf caller has parity with the batch path.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` (`add_comment`,
  `:469`) — add the Cloud comment-body encode step (`--body json.dumps(to_wire(body))`,
  mirroring the description ADF serialize at `acli.py:205`); DC's str `to_wire` needs
  no change.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — surface the COMMENT event's stable local key
  (the HLC `timestamp`, already on the entry at `:349`) so the differ can associate a
  returned Jira id with the originating comment; no new per-pass state. The existing
  inbound `jira_comment_id` field (`:354-356`) is left as-is (authoritative for
  inbound-origin comments).
- inbound comment mirror path (`inbound_differ._diff_comments_inbound`, `:280`) —
  **left UNCHANGED; NOT in the edit set.** It already refuses our own outbound echoes
  via the `RECONCILER_MARKER` body check (`:337`) and already skips Jira ids matching a
  local `jira_comment_id` (`:299,319-321`); it does not receive and does not need the
  outbound map. Listed here only to record that the inbound direction is deliberately
  untouched (no cross-direction handle).
- `tests/` — comment identity, id-capture data-path, append-only, rendering
  (Cloud ADF encode / DC wiki), and dedup-key-migration convergence tests.

## Testing
- Duplicate bodies: two rebar comments with identical text create two distinct Jira
  comments and map to two distinct IDs (no collision), keyed by ID not body.
- Idempotence: a second reconcile pass creates 0 duplicate comments (mapped IDs are
  skipped).
- Append-only: a rebar comment edit does not push to Jira and a Jira comment edit
  does not overwrite rebar; only genuinely new comments mirror.
- Rich rendering: an outbound comment body is rendered through `RichTextCodec.to_wire`
  (Cloud ADF / DC wiki), asserted by the wire shape a create receives.
- Dedup-key migration convergence: after flipping the comment `_resolve_codec`
  injection to the real rendering codec, DC comment-diff still converges with zero
  duplicate re-post (the deliberate counterpart to `3388`'s
  `test_dc_comment_diff_unchanged_by_cutover`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Comment identity is a persistent map from a stable local comment key (the
  COMMENT event HLC) to the Jira comment ID, not the normalized-body key; verified by
  `test_comment_duplicate_bodies_distinct_ids` (two identical-text comments map to
  two IDs).
- [ ] The returned `add_comment` `{"id": …}` dict is captured at both enactment sites
  and persisted against the originating comment's local key: the mutation entry
  carries `local_comment_key` (HLC), `binding_store` reaches both loops (already in
  `create_one`; threaded through `update_one` and its callers `handle_update`/
  `_apply_outbound_update` into `_update_one_dispatch_comments`), and
  `record_comment_id` writes `local_key → id` uniformly across the Cloud (acli) and
  DC transports; verified by `test_comment_id_captured_and_persisted` (fake client
  returns `{"id": "1", …}`; the map records it against the local key).
- [ ] Inbound-origin identity (the existing per-entry `jira_comment_id`, bug 85a1)
  and the new outbound `local_key → jira_id` map are each authoritative for their own
  direction and never compete — the inbound differ is unchanged and consults ONLY its
  own `RECONCILER_MARKER`/`jira_comment_id` loop-breakers, never the outbound map;
  and the outbound differ skips a local comment when EITHER its local key is in the
  map OR it carries a `jira_comment_id`: an inbound-origin comment is never re-pushed
  and an outbound-origin comment is never re-created; verified by
  `test_comment_bidirectional_identity_no_double_sync`, which asserts a local comment
  carrying `jira_comment_id` but NO outbound-map entry produces zero outbound
  mutation.
- [ ] Comment sync is append-only in both directions — new comments mirror once,
  edits/deletes are not synced; verified by `test_comment_append_only` (an
  edit/delete triggers no cross-side write).
- [ ] Outbound comment bodies are rendered through the shared `RichTextCodec.to_wire`
  seam with the Cloud comment-body ADF encode step added on the real create surface … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Comment sync (append-only) with persistent Jira-comment-ID map

The debug skill reads prior tickets but never writes back (reads from a well it never fills); Step 7 sweeps by construct only (parity siblings are ABSENCES invisible to grep); Reporting lets residual fragility evaporate. Approved changes 14+15+16 from the bug-trend review.

## Approach
(14) Writebacks: Phase-1-exit RCA comment (root cause + discriminating evidence); Reporting summary comment (cause/proof/test/fix/siblings/replication); not-a-bug classification comment + cited source; Step-7 siblings filed via create + discovered_from encoded DIRECTLY in the skill (no AGENTS.md reference — client projects may lack it). Tracker discriminator, stated inline in the skill: the tracker the debug session is already operating within — the one that produced or holds the ticket under debug — is "the project's own mandated tracker" and receives the prescribed writebacks un-gated; ANY other tracker is third-party and stays approval-gated. The existing approval-gate paragraph (SKILL.md "Seek explicit user approval… writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers") is explicitly amended in the same change with a carve-out sentence so the prescribed own-tracker writebacks do not contradict it; all other tracker mutations remain gated. (15) Step 7 second sweep axis (construct search unchanged), decomposed into 4 forced-artifact questions: NAME THE RULE (operation+property, must not name the fixed site); CHANNEL CENSUS (fixed 5-slot checklist: CLI / MCP-API / library-facade / automated-callers / dual-direction, plus caller-set derivation — a surface absent from the shared core's callers is the parity signature); PER-SURFACE PROBE (cite path:line or MISSING); DISPOSITION (RED-test fix or ticket + discovered_from). Step 7's entry trigger is amended to the OR of the two axis triggers: enter when the root cause is a repeatable construct pattern (axis 1, existing wording) OR when the fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces (axis 2 — a parity sibling is an absence, present even for one-off constructs); each axis then runs only under its own condition. (16) Reporting item 'Residual risk & prevention': per observed-with-citation fragility, forced disposition — ticket filed (may propose structural guard) / accepted with reason / fixed in scope; 'none observed' legitimate; prose only, no new ticket-system structures.

## Scope
- examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md (single real file; ~35-45 lines total). SKILL.md has no symlink or synced copy — only shared/test-design.md is cp-synced across skills, and that file is untouched here.

## Testing
Prose-only skill change: no code tests. Validation = the existing skill sync gate (tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py, which covers shared/test-design.md only) run as a regression check confirming this change does not perturb the synced set, and a dry-run read-through against the 4-question artifacts on one historical bug (4b59 link-direction class).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All four writebacks encoded at their lifecycle points, with the inline own-tracker-vs-third-party discriminator AND the approval-gate paragraph amended with the matching carve-out (no contradiction between the two sections).
- [x] Step 7 carries both axes with the 4-question decomposition and forced artifacts, and its entry trigger is the OR of the two axis conditions.
- [x] Reporting carries the residual-risk disposition item with 'none observed' legitimate.

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A PASS from `rebar review-plan` is supposed to end with a signed attestation (the guide: 'on a non-blocking PASS, signs an attestation'). In practice, under concurrent store activity, the review completes PASS but exits unsigned. Observed 5 times in one session (2026-07-23, session log 1b86-3286-bbf9-4a8f) while re-planning epic bbf1 with parallel reviews running: tickets 97f2-2d98-2eff-41c1, eefd-49b1-995f-488d, aff0-b0d9-e11c-4b6a, 625b-9cd1-1ce9-4e5f, and epic bbf1-82e1-cf9d-494a all printed 'plan review PASSED but the attestation could not be persisted: plan review generation changed; re-review required' (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:121) or logged 'attestation signing failed; verdict unsigned' (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:738). Only reviews with zero concurrent store movement (e.g. ad44-9f46-07aa-480c's re-run) self-signed.

## Mechanism (read from the tree)
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:146-154: at sign time the plan-relation generation snapshot `collect(ticket_id)` is compared against `initial_generation` captured at review START; if ANY tracked material moved during the (minutes-long) LLM review, it raises PlanReviewGenerationChanged('plan review generation changed; re-review required') and the verdict stays unsigned. But the sanctioned recovery, `rebar sign-review <id>`, then signs from the SAME REVIEW_RESULT sidecar against the CURRENT head with no LLM re-run — and the claim gate accepts it ('re-signed the plan-review attestation from the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar'). So the in-command fail-closed check is strictly harsher than the invariant the store actually enforces, and the message's 're-review required' is contradicted by the recovery path that needs no re-review. Under multi-agent load (many parallel review-plan/edit/comment auto-commits) the majority of passing reviews hit this and each needs a manual rescue.

## Expected
Either (a) review-plan self-heals: on PlanReviewGenerationChanged, if the ticket's own material fingerprint is unchanged (only unrelated store movement), retry the sign against the current head — i.e. run the sign-review path in-process before giving up; or (b) if a genuine material change to the ticket occurred, keep failing closed but say so specifically; and in the residual failure message, instruct 'rebar sign-review <id>' (the documented recovery) instead of 're-review required' (wrong — a re-review is not required and wastes a full LLM run).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A review-plan PASS during which only UNRELATED store writes land (another ticket's edits/comments/attestations) ends certified with no manual step — verified by a unit/integration test that commits an unrelated ticket event between review start and sign.
- [ ] A review-plan PASS during which the reviewed ticket's own material changes still fails closed, with a message naming the ticket-material change — verified by a companion test.
- [ ] The residual unsigned-PASS message points to 'rebar sign-review <id>', not 're-review required' — verified by asserting the CLI output text (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:121).
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green.
baseline.summary: review-plan: passing review frequently ends unsigned under concurrent store writes; error demands re-review although sign-review certifies from the same sidecar

baseline.description:
## What
Read-only derivations over git history + the working tree for the code-health metrics that are durably git-derivable **under the current module-size mechanism**: module-size distribution against the hard cap, cap-change events, short-term churn, and the refactor-to-addition ratio.

## Current mechanism (the plan is grounded in this, not the deleted ratchet)
The old per-file ceilings ratchet is **gone**: `.github/module-size-ceilings.txt` and `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` were deleted (epic 716f). Module size is now a **single, flat, admin-locked hard cap** in `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (currently `800`). So the metrics derive from (a) scanning `src/rebar/**/*.py` line counts against that single-sourced cap, and (b) `git log`. There is **no** "allowlisted-module count", "total ceiling LOC", or "new vs raised ceilings" to read.

## The raw metric functions (multi-arg; the implementation)
In `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py`, all read-only and deterministic:
- `module_size_distribution(repo_root, ref="HEAD") -> dict` → `{"count": <n .py modules>, "near_cap_count": <within 10% of the cap>, "over_cap_count": <exceeding the cap>, "max_loc": <largest module LOC>}`. The cap is read from `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (single-sourced, never hardcoded). Scans `src/rebar/**/*.py` at the ref.
- `cap_change_events(repo_root, since, until) -> list[dict]` → a list (possibly empty) of `{"commit", "old_limit", "new_limit"}` dicts from `git log` over `.github/module-size-limit.txt` in range. **Return type is always a `list[dict]`** — `[]` for a range with no cap change (a real "no events" result, distinct from the Unavailable path).
- `churn(repo_root, since, until) -> dict` → `{"insertions": <int>, "deletions": <int>}` summed from `git log --numstat` over the range.
- `refactor_to_addition_ratio(repo_root, since, until) -> float | None` → deletions/insertions from numstat. Returns **`None`** when total insertions over the range is `0` (no additions to divide by — no data / avoids ZeroDivisionError); a populated range with real deletions of 0 returns `0.0`.

## Registration into the c085 registry (the compute-adapter contract)
c085's `MetricSpec.compute` is a **`Callable[[context], value | None]`** invoked by `evaluate()` as `spec.compute(context)` (registry.py:103-111). The raw functions above are multi-arg, so each `MetricSpec.compute` is a **single-arg adapter** that pulls the range from the context and calls the raw function, e.g. `compute=lambda ctx: churn(ctx.repo_root, ctx.since, ctx.until)`. The context is the small object the `rebar metrics` command (9a5a) passes to every compute, carrying `repo_root`, `since`, `until` (a metric that ignores the range, like `module_size_distribution`, simply reads `ctx.repo_root`). Each of the four `MetricSpec` entries sets: `lens="code_health"`, `source="git"`, `confidence="high"`, `accruing_since="2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"` (git history predates the metrics work, so these are available immediately — not `unavailable`), and the wrapping `compute`. A compute that finds no data in range returns `None` so `evaluate()` reports `Unavailable`.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py` — new: the four functions above + their four `MetricSpec` registrations appended to `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py`'s `REGISTRY` (unique ids `module_size_distribution`, `cap_change_events`, `churn`, `refactor_to_addition_ratio`).
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py` — new.

## Approach
Everything is deterministic and read-only. Distribution scans the tree at a ref against the single-sourced cap (no deleted files parsed); churn/refactor come from `git log --numstat`; cap changes from the limit file's history. Registered into the c085 registry via context-adapter computes. `source="git"`, `confidence="high"` (authoritative). Nothing is written.

## Tests
- Unit (real temp git repo): a fixture tree with modules of known sizes yields the expected `module_size_distribution` (count/max_loc/over_cap_count against a fixture cap file); a `git log --numstat` fixture yields the expected `churn` totals and `refactor_to_addition_ratio`; a commit changing `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is surfaced by `cap_change_events`; an all-additions range yields a valid ratio while a zero-insertions range yields `None`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py` passes against a temp git repo: `module_size_distribution` over a fixture tree returns `max_loc` equal to the largest fixture module's line count, `count` equal to the number of `.py` modules, and `over_cap_count` equal to the number exceeding the fixture cap (exact-value asserts on all three).
- [ ] `churn` over a two-commit numstat fixture returns the exact summed `{"insertions", "deletions"}`; `refactor_to_addition_ratio` over the same fixture returns the exact deletions/insertions ratio, and returns `None` when total insertions is 0 (asserted).
- [ ] `cap_change_events` over a commit changing `.github/module-size-limit.txt` returns a `list[dict]` containing `{"old_limit","new_limit"}` with the old and new values; a range with no such commit returns `[]` (both asserted — the return type is a list in both cases).
- [ ] each of the four metric ids (`module_size_distribution`, `cap_change_events`, `churn`, `refactor_to_addition_ratio`) is present in `REGISTRY` with `lens="code_health"`, `source="git"`, `confidence="high"` — asserted by iterating `REGISTRY` and checking `.id`/`.lens`/`.source` (so the assertion fails if a metric is unregistered or mislabeled, not merely that `is_authoritative("git")` is trivially True).
baseline.summary: Git-derivation readers (code-health metrics from git history)

baseline.description:
# DC comment/description length convergence — and settle whether the comment limit is even right

## Context

Cloud has two convergence suites that exist because oversized text caused real incidents: `mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` and `mutate/test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py`. Each drives an oversized value through TWO passes and asserts the second plans nothing — i.e. the truncated value the adapter sent must compare equal to what it reads back, or the differ re-emits the change forever.

**DC has neither.** And DC's comment path is the one with a question mark over it.

## The specific doubt, verified in source

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:146-149`:

    def sanitize_comment(self, body: str) -> str:
        return _shared_sanitize_comment(
            body, truncate=self._codec.fit_outbound, max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT
        )

Two things are bound to the DESCRIPTION here: the limit (`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`, 32767) and the fitter (`fit_outbound`, the description fit). Cloud does not do this — it routes comments through a dedicated `adapters/jira/comment_limits` module.

**RESOLVED — and the original suspicion here was WRONG, so this section is corrected rather than left standing.** This story was written believing that whether 32767 is the correct DC comment ceiling was UNKNOWN, and that Cloud's separate `comment_limits` module existed "precisely because comment limits are not description limits". Both are now settled against primary sources:

* 32767 IS the correct DC comment ceiling for stock Jira >= 7.0 — it is the default of
  `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose own definition covers "Description, Environment,
  **Comments** and Text custom fields". Comments and text custom fields are ONE property, so DC
  binding both to one constant is faithful to DC, not a shortcut.
* Cloud's `comment_limits` module exists because the UNITS differ, NOT the numbers: Cloud comments
  are limited in PLAIN characters (32767) while Cloud descriptions are limited in ADF-SERIALIZED
  size (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000, fitted empirically because `text_to_adf` inflates — a
  32767-char description was measured serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars). DC has no ADF inflation,
  which is why one constant genuinely suffices there.

So the substance of this story is NOT "find out, then pin it". It is: add the two DC convergence suites DC lacks, and cite the ceiling's provenance at the binding so the constant stops reading as an assumption.

## Approach

1. THE CEILING IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED — do not re-measure it. Jira's own `jpm.xml` defines
   `jira.text.field.character.limit` with `default-value 32767` and a description covering
   "Description, Environment, **Comments** and Text custom fields", and JRASERVER-28519 records
   that 7.0.0 made 32767 the default. Comments and text custom fields are ONE property by design,
   so binding DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is faithful to DC.
   The task is therefore to CITE that provenance in the source at the binding, so the constant
   reads as a decision rather than an assumption. Full evidence is in the research comment on this
   ticket. (That the limit is admin-configurable, and so wrong on a reconfigured instance, is a
   real but separate defect tracked as [rebar:049e-9fac-a821-4ea2]; it does NOT gate this story.)
2. Add the DC convergence suites as **SEPARATE FILES** in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/`.
   DO NOT parametrize them alongside Cloud's. Cloud's two suites hardcode Cloud-only internals
   that have no DC equivalent — `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`
   (`test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py:154`), and `ADF_PATH` /
   `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000` (`test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py:31-34`) —
   whereas DC fits via `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`, a plain character truncation at
   `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`, with no ADF serialization step at all. Parametrizing would require
   restructuring those incident-hardened Cloud tests, which this epic's own acceptance criteria
   forbid ("Cloud's pre-existing assertions still pass UNEDITED"). This mirrors the split that
   `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e` names as its fallback; here the split is the DEFAULT, not the fallback,
   because the blocker is already known rather than something to discover by trying.
3. **INJECT THE DC BACKEND EXPLICITLY AT BOTH SEAMS. DO NOT DRIVE EITHER TEST THROUGH THE CONFIG
   FALLBACK — it silently resolves to CLOUD.** This is the single most important instruction in
   this plan and it was found by plan review, verified in source at 2ea5c3391d:
   * `compute_outbound_mutations` (`outbound_differ.py:382-391`) accepts `outbound_mapper`,
     `inbound_mapper` and `links` — but NO `sanitizer`. When any of the three is omitted it falls
     back to `select_backend(load_config())` (`outbound_differ.py:431-441`).
   * Worse for the COMMENT test: `outbound_differ.py:744-746` calls
     `_diff_comments(ticket, jira_key, comment_snapshot, client=client, inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)`
     — it forwards NO `sanitizer`, so `_diff_comments` resolves one itself via
     `_resolve_sanitizer(None)` -> `select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer`
     (`outbound_comments.py:66-74, 205`), INDEPENDENTLY of any mapper the test injects.
   So a DC comment-convergence test driven through `compute_outbound_mutations` would compare
   bodies using CLOUD's sanitizer and converge against the WRONG truncation function — passing
   while proving nothing about DC. That is exactly the vacuous-green this epic exists to eliminate.
   THE REQUIRED SHAPES:
   * COMMENT convergence: call `_diff_comments(...)` DIRECTLY with an explicit
     `sanitizer=<the DC sanitizer>`. That keyword already exists (`outbound_comments.py:167`, the
     ticket-21ca injection seam) — no production change is needed to reach DC's path.
   * DESCRIPTION convergence: drive `compute_outbound_mutations` with ALL THREE of
     `outbound_mapper=`, `inbound_mapper=` and `links=` bound to a DC backend. Injecting only
     `outbound_mapper` is NOT enough: the guard at `outbound_differ.py:431` is an OR —
     `if outbound_mapper is None or inbound_mapper is None or links is None:` — so leaving ANY of
     the three unset fires the fallback block, which resolves the backend from config and can
     overwrite the others with CLOUD's. Construct a minimal `JiraDataCenterBackend` over a stub
     transport and pass `outbound_mapper=b.outbound, inbound_mapper=b.inbound, links=b`.
   NO PRODUCTION CHANGE IS IN SCOPE HERE. If threading `sanitizer` through
   `compute_outbound_mutations` looks desirable, that is a separate ticket, not this one.
3. Only then decide whether `max_chars` needs changing. A limit change is a BEHAVIOUR change and,
   if needed, belongs in its own bug ticket linked from here — not folded into a test story.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/` — NEW, DC-specific convergence files for comment and
  description. Cloud's two existing convergence files must be left BYTE-UNCHANGED.
- the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — a
  provenance COMMENT only, citing `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519.
- NOT the limit change itself, and NOT making the limit configurable (that is
  [rebar:049e-9fac-a821-4ea2]).

## Testing

Convergence is a two-pass property, so a single-pass assertion cannot establish it: the test must run the pass twice and assert the SECOND plans nothing for that ticket. A first-pass-only test would pass against a bridge that re-sends the same truncated comment forever.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an oversized DC comment converges: pass 2 plans no further change for that ticket, asserted
      on the plan rather than on the absence of an exception
- [ ] an oversized DC description converges, same assertion shape
- [ ] the truncation suffix marker survives the round trip and is asserted, not just the length
- [ ] the DESCRIPTION test proves it exercised DC's fit by a VALUE-BASED discriminator: DC fits
      plain characters at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), while Cloud fits ADF-SERIALIZED size at
      `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32000). Those genuinely differ, so a length/ADF-shape assertion here
      would FAIL if the fallback supplied Cloud's mapper
- [ ] the COMMENT test proves it exercised DC's sanitizer by an IDENTITY or RECORDING check, NOT by
      value. **A value-based discriminator is impossible here and must not be attempted**: DC's
      `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` and Cloud's `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body` truncate at
      the SAME limit (32767 / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS`) and append a BYTE-IDENTICAL suffix
      (`" … [truncated by reconciler]"` — `rich_text.py:69` and `comment_limits.py:46`), computing
      `keep` the same way. Any assertion on the resulting string therefore passes under EITHER
      sanitizer and is a test that cannot fail. Instead capture the injected DC sanitizer and assert
      it is the one that ran — e.g. wrap it in a recorder and assert the recorder observed the call,
      or assert identity against `dc_backend.sanitizer`
- [ ] the comment test's mutation check targets the INJECTION, not the value: removing the explicit
      `sanitizer=` must turn the cell RED via the identity/recording check. (A value assertion could
      not detect that, which is precisely why the identity check is required.)
- [ ] the comment test injects `sanitizer=` into `_diff_comments` explicitly, and the description
      test injects ALL THREE of `outbound_mapper=`, `inbound_mapper=` and `links=`; neither relies
      on `select_backend(load_config())` for any of them
- [ ] mutation-checked for the injection itself: REMOVING the explicit injection (letting the
      config fallback resolve the backend) turns the DC cells RED rather than leaving them green —
      because a green-without-injection cell is testing Cloud while claiming to test DC
- [ ] the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding carries a source comment citing
      `jira.text.field.character.limit` and JRASERVER-28519, so a reader cannot mistake the 32767
      for an assumption — verified by reading the comment in the diff
- [ ] Cloud's two existing convergence files are BYTE-UNCHANGED (`git diff` shows no edit to
      `test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` or
      `test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py`), because the DC suites are separate files
- [ ] the limit itself is NOT changed and is NOT made configurable by this story; that work stays
      in [rebar:049e-9fac-a821-4ea2]
- [ ] mutation-checked: raising the limit above the real ceiling, or removing the fit, turns a
      convergence test red
baseline.summary: DC length convergence, and settle the comment ceiling

baseline.description:
## Why

New local shell/session/worktree writes on this machine are **attributed but unsigned**:
there is no persistent `[identity] signing_key`, no `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, and no
`.rebar/current_identity` pointer. The store currently holds **0 signed events out of ~5097
in-scope events** (`rebar verify-identity --all` reports 0 `verified`) — which agrees with the
committed `rebar.toml` rollout-prep note "the store currently holds 0 signed events". (An
earlier draft said "~4 demo signed events"; the measured count is 0, so this Why is corrected
to match the codebase artifact.) Until every local session signs in steady state, flipping
`identity.require_authenticated` would reject every local write (bug `27ae-8322-9278-4a7c`).

## Precondition — identity already exists (verified here, NOT created)

The Rebar Bot **identity ticket already exists** in the store: `594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`
("Rebar Bot"), `email = joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`, with **one registered ed25519 public
key** (`ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHe3p+OG3L79IIh99qRBEkAEXaU+VbeQcSfhIu4M2F8b`).
This machine's `git config user.email` is `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`, so
`resolve_current_identity` resolves to 594c by the **git-email fallback**
(`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:530-544` `resolve_current_identity`, which calls
`_match_by_email` at `:119-153`) — **no `.rebar/current_identity` pointer is required** (the
pointer only disambiguates when >1 identity shares an email; exactly one matches here). This story therefore **confirms/probes** the identity and its key; it creates
one only if the probe shows it absent. This machine operates *as* the bot (its git email is the
bot email), so it legitimately reuses the shared Rebar Bot key rather than minting a separate
per-clone identity.

## What

Provision a **persistent, machine-wide** signing key so every new shell/session/worktree on
this machine signs with no per-session setup:

- **Materialize** the Rebar Bot private key from AWS SSM SecureString
  `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` (ADR-0012) to a `0600` file **outside the repo** at
  `~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key`. Never commit it; never echo it to logs.
- **Configure** `[identity] signing_key = "~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key"` in the **XDG user
  config `~/.config/rebar/config.toml`** — the per-machine, git-ignored config the loader
  merges under `project` precedence (`config.py` `LAYER_ORDER = default,user,project,env,cli`;
  the project `rebar.toml` sets no `signing_key`, so the user value wins in **every** worktree).
  This file is the single chosen mechanism — preferred over exporting
  `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` from a shell profile because it is **worktree- and
  shell-profile-independent**: a fresh non-login shell in any worktree reads it with no
  re-export. (`.rebar/config.conf` is tombstoned — `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:193` — and must
  not be used; the shared, committed `rebar.toml` must not carry a per-machine key path.)
- **Confirm** the public key registered on identity 594c is the public half of the configured
  private key.

## Scope

This machine's local clones only. GitHub Actions signing (4dc0) and Gerrit-side signing (1a51)
are separate stories; the enforcement flip is 8d39. This story changes **no tracked repo
files** — it writes only `~/.config/rebar/config.toml` and `~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key`, both
outside the repo (hence an empty `file_impact` is correct). The provisioning steps are captured
in the local runbook (AC5); a shared CLAUDE.md/ADR record of the pattern is deferred to the
enforcement-flip story.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Identity precondition confirmed.** `rebar show 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d` is an `identity`
      with the bot email and ≥1 registered key. Proving command:
      `rebar show 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d | jq -e '.ticket_type=="identity" and (.email|ascii_downcase=="joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com") and ((.keys|length)>=1)'`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **Registered public key equals the configured private key's public half.** Proving
      command:
      `diff <(ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key | awk '{print $1,$2}') <(rebar show 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d | jq -r '.keys[0]' | awk '{print $1,$2}')`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **git email matches the identity email.** Proving command:
      `test "$(git config user.email)" = "joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com"`.
- [ ] **A fresh worktree signs with no per-session setup.** From a worktree/shell *other* than
      where the key was configured, create a fresh probe ticket
      `t=$(rebar create task "signing-probe" | tail -1)`, then
      `rebar show "$t" | jq -e '.authorship.signed >= 1'` exits 0 (the write carries a
      signature). The event **verifies**, proven by its **absence** from the non-verified
      report (verified events are excluded from the report — `verify_authorship.py:503-504`
      `continue`): for a fresh, all-signed ticket,
      `rebar verify-identity --all --format json | jq -e '[.[]|select(.ticket_id==$t and .verdict!="verified")]|length==0' --arg t "$t"`
      exits 0 (zero non-verified entries for the probe ticket ⇒ its events verified).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The private key file is mode `0600`, lives outside the repo at
      `~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key`, and the setup is captured in the local runbook. Evidence
      recorded on this ticket as a comment: the `ls -l ~/.ssh/rebar-bot-signing-key` mode line
      (proving `0600`), the SSM source param (`/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key`), and the
      identity id (`594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`).
baseline.summary: Provision persistent local write-signing on this machine (all worktrees/sessions)
