# Add focused prerequisite consistency review

## Goal
Evaluate whether a ticket plan remains consistent with each direct prerequisite without injecting prerequisite material into general reviewers or changing existing parent and child review behavior.

## Upstream contract
Execution precondition: do not claim or implement this story until direct dependencies `75de-02b0-d454-410b` and `5967-4476-7f9f-442d` are closed and their reviewed changes are merged into the feature branch. The dependency links enforce that order. This plan targets their certified planned contracts: `75de` must deliver the review-time `PlanRelationSnapshot` preload keyed by authoritative canonical ID with relation kind, readable state, pinned material, and plan text; `5967` must deliver the review-phase snapshot plus `pass3_over_findings(..., execution_review=...)`. At implementation start, verify both symbols and contract tests exist; if either differs, stop as upstream contract drift rather than defining a local stub or duplicating ownership. This story neither recollects relations nor changes parent and child context handling.

## Implementation
- Register one prerequisite-consistency criterion. It runs only when the shared `PlanRelationSnapshot` preload succeeded and contains readable direct `depends_on` or inverse `blocks` prerequisites. The same canonical ID reached through both relation forms is evaluated once.
- Define stable order as ascending lexicographic order of authoritative canonical ticket ID strings. Use it for prerequisite packing, local finding flattening, split halves, and tail-conflict fixtures.
- Add `PASS_PREREQUISITE_FINDER = "plan-review-prerequisite-finder"` and `PASS_PREREQUISITE_VERIFIER = "plan-review-prerequisite-verifier"` in `passes.py`. Extend the production Pass-1 batch runner with the prerequisite-only finder route. It receives the subject plan plus stable whole prerequisite blocks and invokes `plan_review_prerequisite_coverage`. General criterion requests retain their existing inputs.
- Define measurable isolation: capture every request and assert that each general finder, general verifier, and coach system prompt, user prompt, and instructions contain neither prerequisite canonical IDs nor prerequisite plan text. Assert exactly one relation preload supplies both pin creation and prerequisite routing. Only the two focused prerequisite prompts may receive prerequisite material.
- Define `_prerequisite_coverage_model()` in `passes.py` with `PrerequisiteFinderFinding`, a new Pydantic model matching existing Pass-1 fields exactly: `finding: str`, `criteria: list[str]` constrained to `prerequisite-consistency`, `location: str = ""`, `evidence: list[str] = []`, `scenarios: list[str] = []`, `impact: str = ""`, `checklist_item: str = ""`, `suggested_fix: str = ""`, and required `prerequisite_id: str`. Define outer `PrerequisiteCoverageOutput { records: list[PrerequisiteCoverageRecord] }`; each record is `{prerequisite_id: canonical string, disposition: consistent|finding|indeterminate, findings: list[PrerequisiteFinderFinding], reason_code?: evaluation-error|output-invalid|attribution-invalid, detail?: string}`. The nested finding ID must equal its enclosing record ID. Add `contracts.register_contract("plan_review_prerequisite_coverage", _prerequisite_coverage_model)` to the existing `passes.register_contracts()` function.
- Require exactly one record per readable pinned canonical ID. `consistent` requires no findings or reason code. `finding` requires findings carrying that canonical `prerequisite_id` and no reason code. `indeterminate` requires no findings and one closed-enum reason code. Missing, duplicate, unknown-ID, parse-invalid, or schema-invalid output maps unresolved IDs in the bin to `output-invalid`; provider failure maps them to `evaluation-error`. Indeterminate records never assert incompatibility.
- Keep batching semantically neutral. Each focused Pass-1 prompt asks for independent subject-to-one-prerequisite judgments and forbids cross-prerequisite findings. Stable bins contain whole blocks only. Neither subject nor prerequisite is split. A tail conflict means the only incompatible prerequisite is the lexicographically last canonical ID in a multi-prerequisite packed bin; it must be detected and attributed identically to the same prerequisite evaluated in a singleton call.
- Reuse the registered index-keyed `plan_review_verification` contract for focused Pass 2 and place `prerequisite_attribution_valid` inside its `binary` object. Change `_build_binary(forbid, *, extra_fields: dict[str, tuple[type, Any]] | None = None) -> type`; after building existing fields, merge `extra_fields or {}` into the `create_model` field mapping. Change `_build_verification_output(forbid, severity_cls, *, binary_extra_fields: dict[str, tuple[type, Any]] | None = None) -> type` to call `_build_binary(forbid, extra_fields=binary_extra_fields)`. Only `plan_review_verification_model` passes `binary_extra_fields={"prerequisite_attribution_valid": (str, Field(default="na", description="yes|no|na"))}`. Base and code-review callers omit the keyword and remain byte-identical. Do not add the field to `_BINARY_NA_DEFAULT` or `GRADED_BINARY`; the focused decide path reads `verif["binary"].get("prerequisite_attribution_valid", "na")` as a veto outside validity arithmetic.
- The focused verifier receives the subject plan and, for each local finding, its authoritative prerequisite ID and plan block from the preload. It emits the existing `{index, severity_attributes, binary}` entry. Set attribution `yes` only when the finding is supported by that exact pair, `no` for wrong or unprovable attribution, and never `na` for a focused finding. Multiple whole focused records may share a call within budget.
- Preserve two non-overlapping verification index domains. General arrays retain `0..G-1`. Flatten focused findings in stable `(prerequisite_id, finding_index)` order into local `0..P-1` and verify only that list. Never inject focused findings into general arrays.
- In `plan_review_decide`, reshape the general verification domain with its existing logic and reshape the focused local domain separately so neither domain can shift the other. For the focused domain, missing, duplicate, malformed, out-of-range, `no`, or `na` attribution converts that prerequisite record to `indeterminate/attribution-invalid` and removes its incompatibility findings. After both verification domains are validated, offset each surviving focused finding and verification index by `G`, concatenate aligned general and focused arrays, and call `pass3_over_findings(..., execution_review=execution_review)` exactly once. Determine `execution_review` once from the review-phase snapshot supplied by `5967`; this single shared Pass 3 applies the 0.8 execution floor to every finding. There is no parallel decide pipeline.
- Partition the one returned decided array with DET findings through the existing single `partition_findings` call. Upheld focused findings therefore surface in blocking or advisory arrays with canonical `prerequisite_id` without shifting general indices. Extend `mint_finding_id` to use the authoritative structured identity encoding defined in Binding implementation sequence step 5 whenever `prerequisite_id` is present; identical text from different prerequisites cannot deduplicate.
- Size the actual focused prompt topology, including system prompt, subject plan, prerequisite or finding blocks, output reserve, and headroom, through a prerequisite-specific adapter in `sizing.py`. On context-limit error, split a stable bin into contiguous halves recursively. Escalate a singleton through `models_at_or_above()`. Largest-window exhaustion emits `indeterminate/evaluation-error` with `detail=input-too-large`. Non-context provider failure emits that record for every unresolved ID.
- Add optional `has_prerequisites`, `prerequisite_coverage`, `prerequisite_findings`, and `prerequisite_verifications` properties to `plan_review_decide_input.schema.json`; do not use conditional schema requirements. Both YAML branches always pass false and empty arrays when the route does not apply. Python validation inside `plan_review_decide` requires complete arrays when `has_prerequisites=true`. Extend decide output and coach input schemas with final coverage records.
- Wire focused finder and verifier steps and arrays through both branches in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml`. All four `plan_review_decide` YAML `with:` blocks pass `has_prerequisites`, `${{ steps.finders.outputs.prerequisite_coverage }}`, focused findings, and focused verifications. `plan_review_decide_output.schema.json` returns the validated final `prerequisite_coverage`. All four `plan_review_coach_inputs` YAML `with:` blocks pass `${{ steps.decide.outputs.indeterminate }}` and `${{ steps.decide.outputs.prerequisite_coverage }}`; its output schema preserves that coverage, and all four `plan_review_coach` step `with:` blocks pass it as the direct `prerequisite_coverage` input. In `workflow_ops.plan_review_coach`, compute `prerequisite_indeterminate = any(record.get("disposition") == "indeterminate" for record in ctx.inputs.get("prerequisite_coverage", []))`, add that boolean to the existing local `coverage` dictionary, and pass the same dictionary through the existing `coverage=coverage` argument to `orchestrator.finalize_verdict`. No op rereads the store.
- This story explicitly modifies both decision assembly and terminal verdict while preserving the epic's precedence. In `plan_review_decide`, after the single `partition_findings` call, if any final prerequisite coverage record is indeterminate, retain every `tier == "DET"` entry in `parts["blocking"]` so known structural failures stay visible; move only non-DET blockers into `parts["indeterminate"]` with `decision=indeterminate` and `reason=prerequisite-coverage-indeterminate`. Return those normalized parts plus coverage. In `orchestrator.finalize_verdict`, evaluate `coverage.get("prerequisite_indeterminate")` before blocking: any indeterminate prerequisite produces top-level unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, even when retained DET blockers remain in the blocking array. The finalizer does not move arrays. This preserves complete diagnostic evidence without allowing incomplete prerequisite coverage to become BLOCK or signed PASS.
- Add optional `gold_prerequisite_id` and `pred_prerequisite_id` fields to `parity.ItemRecord`, both defaulting to `None`. Preserve existing fields and container behavior. Add `prerequisite_fidelity_report` for authoritative-ID attribution plus recall and false acceptance. Existing container corpus results remain unchanged.
- Add separate opt-in `prerequisite_packing_spot_eval` and a module CLI entry point `--prerequisite-packing` in `fidelity_spot_eval.py`; do not route prerequisite data through `packing_spot_eval` or `container_fidelity_report`. Add eight or more gold sets of at least three prerequisites: two all-consistent, two single-conflict, two tail-conflict, one attribution-confusion, and one multi-bin. Packed recall may not decrease, false acceptance may not increase, coverage must be complete, and attribution errors must be zero. Failure retains smaller bins or singleton calls.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] General finder, general verifier, and coach requests contain no prerequisite IDs or plan text.
- [ ] One relation preload supplies both material-pin creation and prerequisite routing.
- [ ] Batch `with:` expressions resolve into `BatchRunRequest.with_inputs`; old batch steps default to an empty mapping unchanged.
- [ ] Existing parent and child criteria retain existing container corpus results.
- [ ] Stable focused batching never splits the subject or a prerequisite block.
- [ ] Every readable pinned prerequisite receives exactly one closed-schema disposition.
- [ ] The plan-review-only Pass-2 veto uses `yes|no|na`; code-review schemas remain unchanged.
- [ ] General and focused index domains are independently reshaped and cannot shift each other.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect attribution cannot produce a blocking finding.
- [ ] Every upheld focused finding appears in the verdict with its authoritative prerequisite ID.
- [ ] Same-text findings from different prerequisite IDs retain distinct finding IDs.
- [ ] Every indeterminate record contains no incompatibility finding.
- [ ] Any indeterminate prerequisite forces top-level unsigned INDETERMINATE; concurrent DET blockers remain visibly retained in the blocking array and `coverage.prerequisite_indeterminate=true`.
- [ ] Largest-window exhaustion emits `indeterminate/evaluation-error` with `detail=input-too-large`.
- [ ] The opt-in prerequisite evaluation meets recall, false-acceptance, coverage, and attribution thresholds.

## Verification
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py tests/unit/workflow/test_batch_step.py tests/unit/workflow/test_production_batch_runner.py`.
- Named structural tests include `test_mint_finding_id_different_prerequisite_ids_produce_distinct_ids` and `test_indeterminate_coverage_records_have_no_findings`.
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_plan_review_prerequisite_isolation.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`.
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --singleton --write-baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`; require exit 0 and record the singleton metrics. Then run `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`; require exit 0 with no absolute or comparative regression failures and record the packed metrics.
- Run `make check` and `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m "not integration"`.

## Binding implementation sequence and evaluation contract
The following details replace the earlier shorthand about relative fidelity and define the delivery order:

1. Internal proof phase: implement the coverage contract, focused finder prompt, singleton runner, gold corpus, and opt-in CLI as test scaffolding. Run the singleton gold evaluation before batching or production workflow wiring. Do not continue until singleton recall is at least 0.90, singleton false-acceptance is at most 0.10, coverage completeness is 1.00, and prerequisite attribution error rate is 0.00; record the first green output as the pinned baseline. This checkpoint is deliberately non-releasable: it has no production route, user-facing behavior, supported public surface, or independently closable acceptance outcome, and the prompt/contract must not land orphaned from their sole workflow consumer.
2. Production completion phase: implement packed finder calls and require packed recall to be at least the pinned singleton recall and packed false-acceptance to be no greater than the pinned singleton value, while retaining the absolute 0.90 and 0.10 floors, 1.00 coverage, and 0.00 attribution error. Only after that gate passes implement focused Pass 2, the single shared Pass-3 integration, and terminal verdict enforcement. The story is one atomic delivery and is neither closed nor released until both phases, all acceptance criteria, and all verification commands pass; the phase boundary is a fail-fast implementation checkpoint, not a child-ticket delivery boundary.
3. Define `prerequisite_fidelity_report(baseline: Sequence[ItemRecord], candidate: Sequence[ItemRecord], *, min_recall: float = 0.90, max_false_accept: float = 0.10, min_gold: int = 20) -> ParityReport` in `src/rebar/llm/parity.py`. It calls `parity_report(baseline, candidate, min_gold=min_gold)`, reads candidate recall and false acceptance using `_recall_false_accept`, and adds failures when candidate recall is below `min_recall`, candidate false acceptance exceeds `max_false_accept`, any authoritative readable ID lacks exactly one record, or any caught finding has `pred_prerequisite_id != gold_prerequisite_id`. Its metrics add `coverage_completeness`, `prerequisite_attribution_error_rate`, and the four configured floors. `passed` is true only when the base report and every added check pass. The CLI prints those exact metric keys and exits 1 on failure.
4. Define `pack_prerequisite_bins(blocks: Sequence[PrerequisiteBlock], *, subject_plan: str, system_prompt: str, model: str | None, per_block_output_tokens: int = PER_FINDING_VERIFY_TOKENS, headroom: float = DEFAULT_VERIFY_WINDOW_HEADROOM) -> tuple[list[list[PrerequisiteBlock]], list[PrerequisiteBlock]]` in `sizing.py`. Order blocks lexicographically by canonical ID. Compute `limit = int(largest_window_tokens(model) * headroom)`. Compute fixed input as `est_tokens(system_prompt) + est_tokens(subject_plan) + VERIFY_SYSTEM_RESERVE_TOKENS`. Charge each whole block `est_tokens(block.rendered_text) + per_block_output_tokens`. Greedily append while fixed plus the sum of block charges is at most limit; return a block as oversized when fixed plus its charge exceeds limit alone. Runtime context-limit splitting and model escalation then apply to these bins.
5. For prerequisite-scoped findings, use the single canonical structured identity encoding defined in Binding signal-chain and identity tests; do not define another encoding here. Non-prerequisite findings retain the legacy identity path unchanged.

The first-slice proving command is `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --singleton --write-baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`. The second-slice proving command is `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`. Record both results on this ticket before proceeding.

## Binding signal-chain and identity tests
- The single canonical prerequisite-scoped identity encoding is exact: encode four fields as UTF-8, prefix each with a 4-byte big-endian unsigned byte length, and concatenate them in this order: fixed version string `prerequisite-finding-id-v1`, finding text, comma-joined sorted criteria, and authoritative prerequisite ID. Hash the concatenated bytes with SHA-256 and retain the existing ID truncation. This encoding is used only when `prerequisite_id` is present. Every non-prerequisite finding continues to use the existing pipe-delimited encoding byte-for-byte.
- Add `test_prerequisite_indeterminate_signal_chain_agentic` and `test_prerequisite_indeterminate_signal_chain_single_turn` to `tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py`. Each loads the production `plan-review.yaml`, supplies a fake focused decide result containing one indeterminate prerequisite record and no DET blocker, follows its respective verifier branch, asserts the coach input receives that exact record, asserts the coverage dictionary passed to `finalize_verdict` contains `prerequisite_indeterminate=True`, and asserts the terminal verdict is `INDETERMINATE` with `signature.signed=false`. Add `test_prerequisite_indeterminate_retains_det_blocker` with a DET blocker plus prerequisite indeterminacy and assert unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, the DET finding remains in blocking, and the coverage flag remains true.
- Acceptance criterion: both production-YAML signal-chain tests pass, proving neither workflow branch can silently drop prerequisite coverage before final verdict assembly.
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py -k prerequisite_indeterminate_signal_chain` and require two passing tests.

## Binding comparative baseline and compatibility behavior
- The first-slice command is `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --singleton --write-baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`. It exits nonzero unless the absolute floors pass, then atomically writes JSON keys `recall`, `false_accept`, `coverage_completeness`, `prerequisite_attribution_error_rate`, `model`, `corpus_digest`, and `recorded_at`. The generated baseline is committed and its four metrics are copied to the ticket comment.
- Extend `prerequisite_fidelity_report` with `baseline_recall: float | None = None` and `baseline_false_accept: float | None = None`. When supplied, add gating failures when candidate recall is below `baseline_recall` or candidate false acceptance exceeds `baseline_false_accept`, in addition to all absolute floors.
- The second-slice command is `.venv/bin/python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval --prerequisite-packing --baseline src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-prerequisite-packing.baseline.json`. It validates the baseline schema and corpus digest, passes both baseline metrics into `prerequisite_fidelity_report`, and exits nonzero on absolute or comparative regression. Acceptance criterion: this command exits 0 and its report contains no `recall regressed from singleton` or `false acceptance regressed from singleton` failure.
- Preserve `mint_finding_id` byte-for-byte for every finding without `prerequisite_id`; all existing stored IDs remain valid. New prerequisite-scoped findings use only the canonical four-field encoding defined in Binding signal-chain and identity tests. No migration or dual write is required because prerequisite-scoped findings do not exist before this feature.
- When prerequisite coverage is indeterminate, use only the normalized decision and finalizer behavior defined in the Implementation section; there is no second array-mutation site. The resulting verdict arrays and string remain consistent while retaining all findings for remediation and UI display.
- The P8 short-circuit and `drift_refresh` call sites pass no prerequisite coverage by design; `coverage.get("prerequisite_indeterminate")` is false on those paths and their existing verdicts remain unchanged.

## Binding operational behavior
- Focused finder and verifier calls use the existing runner retry classification and exponential-backoff policy for rate limits and retryable 5xx failures. Only exhausted retries map unresolved IDs to `indeterminate/evaluation-error`; context-limit failures continue through split and model escalation.
- Emit structured event `plan_review_prerequisite_indeterminate` with ticket ID, prerequisite ID, reason code, model, attempt count, and bin size for every evaluation-error, output-invalid, or attribution-invalid record. Increment counters partitioned by reason code; never include prerequisite plan text.
- Reusing `plan_review_verification` is deliberate because the certified epic requires the optional attribution field in the existing index-keyed Pass-2 contract and the same threshold pipeline. The field is added only by `plan_review_verification_model`; code-review and kernel verification contracts remain unchanged.

## Binding focused prompt and failure contracts
- Create `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_prerequisite_finder.md`, resolved by prompt ID `plan-review-prerequisite-finder`. Its YAML front matter is `schema_version: 1`, title `Plan-review prerequisite finder`, description of isolated prerequisite consistency Pass 1, `outputs: plan_review_prerequisite_coverage`, `execution_mode: single_turn`, and `category: plan-review-pass`, matching the prompt-library contract used by existing reviewers. Its system instructions say: compare the subject plan independently with each supplied prerequisite plan; report only a concrete incompatibility where the subject depends on an output, interface, ordering, invariant, acceptance condition, or file-impact assumption that the prerequisite plan contradicts or cannot deliver. Do not review either plan for general quality, infer transitive prerequisites, compare prerequisites with each other, or create a finding merely because details are absent. Use only supplied text and canonical IDs.
- The finder user input is framed as `SUBJECT_PLAN` followed by stable repeated blocks `PREREQUISITE id=<authoritative-id>` and `PLAN_TEXT`, with explicit begin/end delimiters. The prompt states that block position has no semantic meaning and each judgment must be independent of other blocks in the call.
- The prompt must return `PrerequisiteCoverageOutput` with exactly one record for every supplied canonical ID and no other IDs. `consistent` means no concrete incompatibility was found and has empty findings. `finding` means one or more concrete incompatibilities were found; each finding uses the existing Pass-1 finding fields `finding`, `criteria`, `location`, `evidence`, `scenarios`, `impact`, `checklist_item`, and `suggested_fix`, plus required `prerequisite_id` equal to the enclosing record ID. The only criterion ID is the registered prerequisite-consistency criterion. The model never emits `indeterminate`; runner and schema-validation failures create indeterminate records deterministically.
- Focused verifier context-limit recovery has one authoritative algorithm. Before packing, each focused finding carries required `original_index`, its position in the authoritative flat `0..P-1` focused domain. First split bins between whole `PrerequisiteVerificationBlock` records into stable contiguous halves. If one record alone is oversized, split only that record's `findings` tuple into stable contiguous halves while repeating the complete subject plan and complete prerequisite plan text in each call; never split either plan text. Every split-call prompt labels each entry with its unchanged `original_index` and requires the verifier to echo that value as output `index`; reassembly merges by echoed index before reshape and attribution validation, never by half-call position. Escalate a single-finding record through `models_at_or_above()`. If that single-finding record fails at the largest window, convert the whole prerequisite record to `indeterminate/evaluation-error` with `detail=input-too-large` and discard every partial verifier result for that prerequisite.
- Add `test_largest_window_exhaustion_emits_indeterminate` to `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py`; mock every model to return a context-limit error and assert the exact disposition, reason code, and detail for both finder and verifier paths.
- Add acceptance coverage for observability: tests assert each evaluation-error, output-invalid, and attribution-invalid record emits `plan_review_prerequisite_indeterminate` with ticket ID, prerequisite ID, reason code, model, attempt count, and bin size; counters are partitioned by reason; captured events contain no prerequisite plan text.
- Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py -k "largest_window_exhaustion or indeterminate_observability"` and require all selected tests to pass.

content.text: The LLM completion verifier is budget-impractical for code-heavy, multi-criteria tickets.
## Context

Discovered dogfooding the close gate on this feature's own epic + workstreams. On a faster, decisive model (sonnet) a FOCUSED ticket (≈2 small AC) converges in ~12s, but a code-heavy workstream whose AC reference large files (e.g. WS-3: ~4 AC across `_cli/__init__.py` ~1000 lines, `mcp_server.py`, test files) does NOT converge even at recursion_limit=500 / ~560s. The agent reads many large files / searches across criteria; there is no cheap shortcut to verifying implementation-completeness of a code-heavy ticket. With the gate enabled, such tickets currently can't be closed without a very high REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or `--force-close`.
## Candidate directions
- A lightweight repo-map / orientation (tree-sitter/PageRank à la Aider) so the agent reads less.
- Stronger budget steering (hard tool-call cap) and/or summarized-file reads.
- The framework-wide AutoStrategy/ProviderStrategy migration (separate follow-up) for cheaper structured output.
- Per-ticket file-impact hints (`set_file_impact`) to focus the agent on the relevant files.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A code-heavy multi-criteria workstream ticket verifies (PASS/FAIL) within a practical budget/latency on the default verifier model.
- [ ] Decision recorded: raise the gate's default budget, add a repo-map, or scope the gate to focused tickets.

baseline.summary: Completion verifier: efficiency for code-heavy tickets (budget limit)

content.text: ## Why
The coach's move catalog must offer the right remediation. Two dso lessons need moves: pre-existing issues
should become follow-on tickets (pairs with rebar's discovered_from), and change-detector tests must be
DELETED, not re-pinned to new source text.
## What
Add two Pass-4 coach moves to `MOVE_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (and thus
`.rebar/code_review_moves.json`-overridable): `file-follow-on-ticket` (subject = the pre-existing/
out-of-scope issue; template guidance to file a `discovered_from` follow-on ticket) and `delete-bad-test`
(subject = the change-detector/tautological test; template guidance to DELETE it, not re-pin it to the new
source text). Deterministic `{subject}` templates; the LLM only picks the move name + names the subject.
### applies_when gating — DATA-FLOW (resolves plan-review G6 block f6f98d71)
The `applies_when` vocabulary is the CLOSED set `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` (`review_kernel.validate_move_registry`),
and a move is offered by Pass-4 ONLY when its `applies_when` overlaps `active_triggers`, where
`active_triggers = {c for f in surfaced for c in f.get("criteria", [])}` (`workflow_ops.py`
`code_review_coach_inputs` / `code_review_coach`, ~line 342). Those `criteria` values are the overlay ids
the reviewers emit (OVERLAY_IDS). Therefore a NOVEL tag (e.g. `"pre-existing"` / `"change-detector"`) would
NEVER enter `active_triggers`, so a move keyed on it would register but never fire (dead move). We
DELIBERATELY DO NOT extend the vocabulary. Instead we key on EXISTING overlay ids already emitted as
`criteria`:
- `delete-bad-test` → `applies_when: ["tests"]`. A change-detector/tautological/over-mocking test finding
arrives under the `tests` overlay criterion, so the move is offered whenever a surviving `tests` finding
exists. Its `name`/`template` make it the obvious pick for a change-detector finding (vs re-pinning), and
it sits alongside the existing `add-regression-test` move so the LLM selects delete — not "improve the
test" — for a change-detector subject.
- `file-follow-on-ticket` → `applies_when: ["always"]`. A pre-existing/out-of-scope finding can surface
under ANY overlay criterion, so the move is always offered; the LLM picks it when the surviving finding
is about a pre-existing issue (subject = that issue), and the template instructs filing a
`discovered_from` ticket rather than fixing it in-scope.
No new `applies_when` vocabulary value is introduced; both moves key on values already in the closed set,
so both pass `validate_move_registry` subject-validation and actually enter `active_triggers`.
## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` (MOVE_REGISTRY entries) + a unit test. No verdict-path change; the
coach prompt (`code-review-coach.md`) already picks the single most useful applicable move, so no prompt
change is required beyond the moves being offered.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `file-follow-on-ticket` and `delete-bad-test` moves exist in `MOVE_REGISTRY` with deterministic
`{subject}` templates and pass `validate_move_registry` (built-in, strict).
- [ ] Each move's `applies_when` uses ONLY existing `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` values (`delete-bad-test` →
`["tests"]`, `file-follow-on-ticket` → `["always"]`), so the move actually enters `active_triggers`
and is OFFERED by `code_review_coach_inputs` for the intended criteria (proven by a unit test using
`review_kernel.applicable_moves`).
- [ ] For a surviving finding tagged `criteria: ["tests"]`, `delete-bad-test` is among the applicable moves
(the change-detector remediation), distinct from the "improve/add test" moves; a unit test pins this.

baseline.summary: Coach moves: file-follow-on-ticket + delete-bad-test

baseline.description:
## Why

The code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (`code_review_result_v1`) persists only the SURFACED
findings — the `blocking`, `advisory`, and `coaching` buckets — and omits the `dropped` and
`indeterminate` findings that Pass-3 produced. It also does not persist the numeric
`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` each finding was judged against. So "the complete Pass-1
finding list" is not recoverable for a code review, unlike plan review.

## Dependency

This story **depends on 4e19** (plan-review lossless v2), which lands first in the stack and makes
the SHARED review kernel stamp the resolved boundary on every decided finding: `pass3_decide`
returns `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` and `pass3_over_findings` merges them, so every
code-review finding (via `code_review_decide`) already carries them by the time this story runs.
4e19 also adds those two fields (plus `evidence`/`scenarios`) to the plan-review `_slim`, so the two
sidecars **converge** in shape — this story does not introduce a field plan-review lacks.

## What

Extend the code-review sidecar to `code_review_result_v2`, pooling the four buckets the code-review
gate actually produces — `blocking`, `advisory` (surfaced), `dropped`, `indeterminate` — with each
finding's full Pass-2 `verification` and Pass-3 determination (`decision`/`priority`/…), plus the
resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` (stamped by the 4e19 kernel change). There is **no
`overflow` bucket** in code review: unlike plan-review (which applies an advisory cap that spills to
`overflow`), `code_review_decide` partitions only into `{blocking, surfaced, dropped, indeterminate}`
and the code-review verdict schema has no `overflow` property.

## Scope

The `dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets are computed by `code_review_decide` but are **not** currently
forwarded to the terminal verdict — `code_review_coach` assembles only
`{verdict, blocking, advisory, coaching, coverage}`, and `apply_region_gated_floor` only appends its
own novelty-floor drops post-hoc. So the wiring must be extended:

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — in the `verdict` step's `with:` block, pass
  `dropped: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.dropped }}` and
  `indeterminate: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.indeterminate }}` (alongside the existing `blocking`
  and `surfaced`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — `code_review_coach` accepts `dropped`/
  `indeterminate` inputs and includes them in its returned verdict dict; update its
  `code_review_coach_input`/`_output` schemas to allow the two new (optional) arrays.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — bump `SCHEMA` to `code_review_result_v2`; in
  `build_payload`, add `dropped`/`indeterminate` (norm-id-stamped, like `blocking`/`advisory`), each
  finding retaining its `verification`/`decision`/`block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled`; KEEP the
  separate `blocking`/`advisory` lists (so the surfaced reader is unchanged) and the change metadata
  (`change_id`/`revision`/`change_fingerprint`) + `deps`. `_latest_payload_with_ts` and
  `latest_code_review_result` accept BOTH `code_review_result_v1` and `_v2` (replace the
  `== SCHEMA` guard with membership in `{v1, v2}`), so old records still read and the surfaced
  reader keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union.

Code-review findings carry no `evidence`/`scenarios` (those are plan-review Pass-1 fields); this
story does not persist them for code review.

## Enumerated consumers to update

- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws4.py:210` asserts `payload["schema"] == "code_review_result_v1"`
  on a fresh emit; update it to `_v2` (the schema bumped).
- `docs/experiments/derive_code_review_threshold.py` is a jq/offline consumer that filters on
  `code_review_result_v1`; note that it should accept `_v2` too (or is left as historical — out of
  this story's code scope, flagged for the reader).

## Compatibility & rollback

`v1` code-review sidecars remain readable (new buckets absent → default to `[]`). The novelty-floor
reader that consumes surfaced findings keeps returning the `blocking + advisory` union, so
region-gating is unaffected. No backfill. Reverting bumps `SCHEMA` back to `v1` and stops writing the
`dropped`/`indeterminate` buckets; already-written `v2` records stay readable because the reader
still accepts both schemas (the reader change is independently safe to keep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_payload` produces a `code_review_result_v2` payload that pools `blocking`, `advisory`,
      `dropped`, and `indeterminate`, each finding retaining its `verification`, Pass-3 `decision`,
      and resolved `block_threshold`/`blocking_enabled` plus a `norm_id`. Oracle: a unit test driving
      `build_payload` with a verdict containing all four buckets and asserting on the payload JSON.
- [ ] `code_review_coach` forwards `dropped`/`indeterminate` from the decide step into the terminal
      verdict dict. Oracle: a contract test calling the `code_review_coach` op with those inputs and
      asserting they appear in the returned verdict.
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result` reads both a `v1` and a `v2` code-review sidecar. Oracle: a unit
      test with one hand-written record of each schema.
- [ ] The novelty-floor surfaced-findings reader returns exactly the `blocking + advisory` union
      from a `v2` payload, unchanged vs an equivalent `v1` payload. Oracle: a unit test comparing the
      two.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: code-review sidecar -> lossless v2 (all buckets + thresholds)

# terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

## Context / proven root cause
The `terraform-drift` GitHub Actions check has failed on every run against
`origin/main` since opcert.tf landed (commit f78940a43, 2026-07-15). The check runs
`terraform plan` over `infra/terraform/` with NO variable inputs
(.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml:61). `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`'s
assume_role_policy derives its principals from `var.opcert_admin_principal_arns`
(opcert.tf:138), which defaults to `[]` (opcert.tf:29). The live role was applied with
the operator-supplied account-root principal (`arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root`, per the
documented deploy pattern opcert.tf:26 / opcert-plan-assertions.sh:22). So every plan
renders an EMPTY principal and diffs it against live's account-root principal:

    # aws_iam_role.opcert_admin will be updated in-place
      ~ Principal = { ~ AWS = "arn:aws:iam::896586841071:root" -> [] }
    Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.   -> exit 2 -> check FAILS

This is an un-reconcilable phantom (applying the committed default would remove the
principal), so it permanently reds the daily drift sweep and masks any real future drift.

## Defect
Asymmetry inside opcert.tf: the sibling operator-seeded SSM KEY param carries
`lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` (opcert.tf:57-59) precisely so plan/apply never
diff on an operator-owned value — but the equally operator-supplied trust principal was
not given the same guard.

## Plan (fix direction: ignore_changes — user-approved)
Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }` to `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin`.
Terraform still creates the role; the operator owns the trust list out-of-band (honors the
documented "operator supplies principals at deploy" intent and mirrors the key-param
precedent). This suppresses the phantom diff at PLAN time — no terraform apply required.

## Acceptance criteria (measurable)
1. `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin` in infra/terraform/opcert.tf declares
   `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy] }`.
2. A hermetic source-contract test in tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py asserts (1)
   and was seen RED before the fix, GREEN after (with a mutation check returning it to RED).
3. `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass on the edited module.
4. No existing opcert infra test is weakened; full unit suite for the file passes.

## Verify command
    cd /Users/joeoakhart/fix-opcert-drift-ignore-changes
    ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_deploy_infra.py -q
    cd infra/terraform && terraform fmt -check && terraform validate
baseline.summary: terraform-drift check permanently red: opcert_admin trust-policy phantom drift

# The global rebar build is 4 days stale, and it SILENTLY disables the LLM tier of plan review

## Context / Problem
This machine's global `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` is supposed to track `origin/main` HOURLY via a rollback-guarded LaunchAgent (documented in `docs/local-env-main-tracking.local.md`). IT HAS NOT RUN SINCE 2026-07-27 17:10 — measured from the mtime of `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar/lib/python3.14/site-packages/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py`, and corroborated by the venv directory's own mtime. Today is 2026-07-31, so the global build is ~4 days behind main.

**THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT DEGRADATION OF THE REVIEW GATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING.** `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` carries `activate` as a DICT (scoped per review type), which main's overlay parser accepts — `git show origin/main:src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py | grep "must be a list of ids"` returns NOTHING. The stale global build predates that: its overlay.py DOES contain that check and raises `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. Support landed in `f3dbe32b0b` (2026-07-27, "3ba4: Scope project criteria by review type") and `7f4c650114` (2026-07-28).

MEASURED consequence of running `rebar review-plan <id> --ref HEAD` with the global build in this repo:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay .../.rebar/criteria_routing.json:
                  'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command EXITS 2 and emits a sidecar. It does not present as a broken install; it presents as a plan that could not be reviewed. The DET tier still runs and reports pass/fail per criterion, so the output looks substantive. An operator or agent reading that verdict would reasonably conclude the TICKET is the problem. **No LLM review happened at all.**

The worktree build parses the same file fine — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns 44 effective criteria — so this is purely the stale global install, not a repo defect.

## Why this matters beyond one command
AGENTS.md already warns to run the repo checkout's build rather than a stale global install, and gives the reason as "silently ignores newer config keys". This incident shows the consequence is worse than ignoring a key: an unrelated-looking INDETERMINATE on the claim gate. Any agent that trusts `which rebar` gets it. The MCP server is affected the same way and, per the local docs, will not hot-reload.

## Approach
Two separable pieces:
 1. DIAGNOSE why the LaunchAgent stopped. Check `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
    for its last exit status, and the agent's own log, before forcing a sync. A rollback-guarded updater
    that silently gave up 4 days ago has its own failure to explain — forcing a sync hides the evidence.
    Force it only after capturing that state:
    `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`.
 2. MAKE THE STALENESS LOUD rather than silent. A gate run whose LLM tier dies on a CONFIG-PARSE error
    from the installed build is not the same as an LLM outage, and collapsing both into
    `llm_unavailable` + INDETERMINATE is what made this cost time. A `CriteriaError` while loading the
    overlay is a CONFIGURATION fault: it should surface distinctly (its own verdict reason or a loud
    warning naming the installed build's version), so the reader is pointed at the install rather than
    at the plan.

## Scope
- The LaunchAgent / updater: diagnosis first, then a sync.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — distinguish a config-parse failure from an LLM outage in the verdict's
  `llm_error` / reason surfacing.
- Possibly a startup or gate-time warning when the running build's commit is far behind the repo's.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion below is verifiable IN-SESSION by a probe, experiment, or test — no criterion defers to a future change.

ALL OF THEM ARE TAGGED [operator-attested], and that is a statement of fact rather than a way around the gate: the completion verifier reads REPOSITORY FILES ONLY, while every probe here observes machine-local operational state — a launchd exit code, a pipx venv's recorded backend, `command -v uv` under a given PATH, the contents of ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log. NO repository file can record any of it, because THE FIX ITSELF TOUCHES NO REPOSITORY FILE (it is one line of a script under ~/.local/bin plus recreating a venv). The observed outputs are pasted verbatim in the evidence comment on this ticket so the attestation is checkable rather than merely asserted. The code hardening that was previously bundled here (reporting an overlay `CriteriaError` distinctly from an LLM outage, and naming the installed build as the suspect) has been SPLIT OUT to its own ticket, because it is a repo change with its own review and must not hold this environment repair open.

- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE A, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: `~/.local/bin/uv` (0.7.18) shadowed `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`
      (0.12.0) on the updater's PATH. Probe: under the script's ORIGINAL PATH order,
      `command -v uv` resolves the 0.7.18 binary; under the fixed order it resolves 0.12.0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] ROOT CAUSE B, PROVEN AND REPAIRED: the pipx venv was pinned to the pip backend, which pipx
      will not override. Probe: `pipx_metadata.json` recorded `backend = pip` before and records
      `backend = uv` after; and `pipx install --force --backend uv` against the OLD venv was
      demonstrably IGNORED (same `resolution-too-deep`, metadata unchanged).
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE UPDATER COMPLETES: a run exits 0 and `last-good.sha` advances off the Jul-17 commit
      (`4dd9172b9`) to the current tip of `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IT WORKS UNDER LAUNCHD, NOT JUST BY HAND: `launchctl kickstart -k` the agent and then
      `launchctl print` reports `last exit code = 0`. This is the criterion that matters — every
      by-hand run inherits the operator's rich shell environment, whereas launchd supplies a minimal
      one, so a by-hand pass does not prove the scheduled job works.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE INSTALL PATH ITSELF IS EXERCISED UNDER LAUNCHD, not just the no-op branch: with
      `last-good.sha` temporarily rewound, a launchd-triggered run performs a real install and
      advances it again (restore the true sha afterwards). Without this, a green kickstart only
      proves the `no change` early-exit.
- [ ] [operator-attested] IDEMPOTENCE: an immediately following run is a no-op — it logs `no change (already on <sha>)`
      and exits 0 rather than reinstalling.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE MUTATION BITES: restoring the original PATH order reproduces the exact
      `pipx needs uv>=0.9.17` failure, proving the one-line fix is load-bearing and not incidental.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS GONE: the GLOBAL build parses the dict-shaped `activate` in
      `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — `registry.effective_criteria('.')` returns the full criteria
      set where it previously raised `CriteriaError`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE GATE ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE GLOBAL BUILD: a real `rebar review-plan` invoked with the GLOBAL
      build reaches the LLM tier (`llm_ran: true`), not merely a successful criteria parse. This is
      the end-to-end form of the reported failure, whose signature was `llm_ran: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE SMOKE-TEST/ROLLBACK GUARD IS INTACT: the script's post-install smoke test still gates
      `last-good.sha`, evidenced by the smoke commands exiting 0 against the freshly installed build.
- [ ] [operator-attested] THE KNOWLEDGE IS RECORDED where the next person will look: the local runbook documents that
      PATH order is load-bearing, that `uv` is a hard requirement (so `--backend pip` is NOT a valid
      workaround for this package), that an existing venv pins its backend, and that `update.log` —
      not the 0-byte launchd logs — is the diagnostic file.

baseline.description:
# P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

**Correctness backbone.** Closes the one architectural gap a distributed tracker
should not ship without; P2.3 rides its total order.

## Context (problem + research)

rebar orders replay by the `${timestamp_ns}` filename prefix; invariant I8 admits
EDIT/COMMENT interleaving is "best-effort" under clock skew (only STATUS forks are
skew-independent, UUID-keyed at `reducer/_processors.py:78-120`). Two agents on
skewed clocks editing the same field resolve by last *wall-clock* writer -> silent
clobber. **git-bug solves exactly this with a persisted Lamport clock**
(`util/lamport/*`, `clocks/<name>`): a single `uint64`, advanced monotonically,
**re-seeded by witnessing max over history**; the local file is a disposable
cache, the authoritative value rides in git. Replay orders by logical time then a
content-id tiebreak. Radicle uses the same family (causal DAG + actor-id tiebreak).

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP1: `time_ns()` is 19 digits until ~year 2286; equal-width ints sort identically
  as strings and ints; string sort only breaks across DIFFERING widths -> stay 19-digit.
- EXP4: 2400 concurrent flock'd `next_tick()` ticks — all unique/monotonic/19-digit.
- EXP4b: with **no cache file**, `next_tick_for_ticket()` still issues a tick >
  `max(prefix)`, 19-digit -> the cache is reconstructable (git-bug's model).
- EXP-jq: the prefix is >2^53; jq rounds it -> **no jq/arithmetic may ever touch it**
  (reinforces P1.0's one-Python-serializer rule).
- EXP-R2 (real code): `event_sort_key` ts segment is `str` today; int-order ==
  string-order on real filenames; malformed names take the fallback -> change is safe.

## What / Implementation detail

1. New `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` = single monotonic integer
   `max(hlc.state, max(prefix of TARGET TICKET's events after sync), time_ns()) + 1`,
   RMW under a **local** `.rebar/hlc.lock` (held only inside the call -> no ordering
   hazard with the write lock). `.rebar/hlc.state` is a **disposable cache**
   (gitignored, I3/I7); correctness is re-derived from the durable log, so a
   missing/stale/raced cache is still correct.
2. Thread it through the four live timestamp seams: `_commands/_seam.py:153`,
   `ticket_txn.py` (STATUS/claim), reconciler `inbound_translate`, and
   `ticket-compact.sh` (via `python3 -m rebar._store.hlc next`). Add an injectable
   `REBAR_HLC_NOW` for the skewed-clock test.
3. Change `reducer/_sort.py:event_sort_key` (line 21) to `int(ts_segment)` (malformed
   fallback), keeping the `(ts, type_order, name)` tuple + LINK<UNLINK tiebreak;
   align the other prefix sorts (`graph/_links.py:53`, `_commands/unlink.py:47`,
   bare `sorted()` STATUS scans at `ticket_txn.py:187/318`). Keep the UUID tiebreak
   (git-bug: logical-time then content-id).
4. Bump `reducer/_version.py:SCHEMA_VERSION` -> 2. Single-integer encoding keeps
   width at 19 digits, so older clones still string-compare correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar._store.hlc.next_tick()` (single-int, local-lock RMW, witness max(prefix), injectable clock)
- [ ] threaded through all four live timestamp seams (incl. bash via `python3 -m`)
- [ ] `event_sort_key` + the 3 other prefix sorts use integer comparison; UUID tiebreak kept
- [ ] SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2; event-schema.md updated
- [ ] NEW skewed-clock EDIT/COMMENT convergence regression (merged red-first), width-comparator + forward-compat tests
- [ ] staged behind `REBAR_HLC` with kill-switch for one release

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P2.1).
- [ ] A NEW skewed-clock regression (two clones, injected skew) shows EDIT/COMMENT
- [ ] Width-comparator test: legacy 19-digit and new names sort into one global order.
- [ ] v1-reducer replay of a v2 store still yields a valid state (forward-compat).
baseline.summary: P2.1 — Hybrid Logical Clock for event ordering (skew-immune replay)

baseline.description:
## Context

The plan-review gate's re-review of an *edited* plan does not converge: each remediation
round can surface new issues in previously-clean criteria, expanding scope every run and
creating a non-terminating loop that drives cost, wall-clock, and agent non-compliance.
This is distinct from run-over-run reproducibility on fixed input (the LLM-as-judge
self-consistency problem); the plan legitimately changed, so feedback *should* differ. The
problem we solve: a remediation re-review should confirm the surfaced issues were resolved
**without** introducing different, lower-stakes issues that restart the loop.

Prior conversation rejected three approaches: per-diff-region scoping (new section-diffing
machinery), skip-clean-criteria reuse (unsound — reuses absence-of-finding, freezes
high-stakes defects an edit introduces), and the whole-verdict probe (too coarse). This
epic captures the chosen approach. Relates to the plan-review epic `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa`.
It is decomposed into 6 child tasks (see "Decomposition" below).

## Terminology (canonical)

- **impact** — the verifier's coarse severity-attribute score in [0,1] (`decide.impact`).
- **validity** — the graded fraction of the Pass-2 binary sub-answers in [0,1].
- **priority** — `validity × impact` (the existing Pass-3 score; the drop axis).
- **novelty score** — a new [0,1] score derived deterministically from a new Pass-2
  novelty sub-answer set (see below); high = "not present in the prior review".
- **carryover finding** — a current finding matching a prior-review finding (low novelty).

## What (the chosen design)

A **rising-floor remediation re-review**: run the FULL criteria set every time (no skipped
criteria, no Pass-1 anchoring → full recall), and on a remediation re-review apply a
deterministic Pass-3 floor that drops only **novel, low-priority** findings.

- **Full Pass-1, unanchored.** Every applicable criterion runs; the finder never sees prior
  findings (avoids the sycophancy/anchoring the research documents). High-priority defects
  an edit introduces are still found — nothing is frozen.
- **Novelty as a narrow-question score, in a SEPARATE Pass-2 sub-call.** Novelty is scored
  by a DISTINCT structured sub-call that ALONE receives the prior findings and answers a
  small novelty sub-answer set ("does this finding correspond to a prior finding?"). The
  existing verification sub-call (severity attributes + the binary/validity sub-answers)
  receives **NO** prior findings, so the `verify.py` independence invariant
  (VERIFIER_RULES[0]) is enforced *structurally*, not by prompt assertion — mirroring the
  Pass-1 isolation. Pass-3 maps the novelty sub-answers to a deterministic novelty score,
  exactly as it maps the binary sub-answers to validity. The sub-answers are factual **matches-prior** questions (same defect / same location / same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0` map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match). Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never dropped). Full set + arithmetic on task 150b. The sub-answers are factual
  **matches-prior** questions (does this restate the same defect / cite the same location /
  suggest the same fix as a specific prior finding?) on the `yes=1.0/insufficient=0.5/no=0.0`
  map; **`novelty = 1 − mean(matches-prior sub-answers)`** (high novelty = no prior match).
  Fail-safe: a failed/malformed novelty sub-call defaults novelty to 0.0 (carryover → never
  dropped). Full set + arithmetic live on task 150b.
- **Deterministic rising floor (Pass-3).** A finding is dropped iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND
  `priority < floor`. Carryover findings (low novelty) use the normal threshold and must
  still be resolved. A novel high-priority finding (high impact × high validity) is
  preserved (and may block). The whole policy is deterministic — no LLM holistic severity.
- **Freshness window = remediation-mode gate.** The floor applies only when: config enabled,
  plan changed, code unchanged since baseline, registry unchanged, a prior sidecar (with
  finding text) is available, and the last review (full OR partial) is within the window
  (default 60 min). **Each review resets the window**, so the loop persists across a series
  of edits while the agent is actively iterating; it lapses to a normal full (un-floored)
  review only after the agent goes idle past the window. Code-changed / both-drifted → full
  review (`drift_refresh` untouched — out of scope). **Back-out:** setting the config key off
  restores byte-identical full-review behavior.

## Narrowed-verdict / sidecar schema

- The verdict's `coverage` records `narrowed: true`, `floored_criteria`, and the floored
  finding ids when the rising floor was applied (absent/false on a normal review).
- Dropped novel findings are written to the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar (not the surfaced
  verdict), joinable by `norm_id`, so suppression is always observable.

## Defaults & calibration (falsifiable)

- Starting defaults (tunable): `T_novel = 0.7`; `priority floor = the p40 impact percentile
  of the 245-event corpus × validity` (≈ the "below major" band). Both are *derived*, not
  guessed: `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` prints the percentile inputs.
- The novelty scorer must clear an **evidence gate** BEFORE the Pass-3 drop rule is activated.
  The bar is concrete and uses the framework's existing idiom (NOT an invented AUC/F1): a
  `discriminates_novelty` deterministic scorer (per-case, **0.5 midpoint** — `kind: novel`
  scores novelty ≥ 0.5, `kind: carryover` < 0.5, mirroring `discriminates_true_from_false` /
  `discriminates_impact_levels`) gated at the spec level by **`gate: at_least(2)` over
  `epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8`** on ≥ 3 labeled novel/carryover pairs (task 150b).
- **Three distinct numbers (do not conflate):** (a) the **runtime drop threshold
  `T_novel = 0.7`** — Pass-3 drops a finding only if novelty ≥ 0.7 (and priority < floor),
  config-overridable; (b) the **eval discrimination floor 0.5** — the per-case midpoint the
  `discriminates_novelty` scorer separates novel from carryover at; (c) the **eval bar** —
  the spec gate `at_least(2)/epochs:3` + `coverage_threshold:0.8` the scorer must clear before
  the drop rule activates. 0.7 is "how novel to be droppable"; 0.5/the gate is "did the scorer
  prove it can tell novel from carryover at all".

## Within-session suppression (deliberate, honest bound)

Because the window resets on each review, a novel low-priority finding can be re-floored
every round while the agent keeps iterating — within-session suppression is **intentionally
unbounded** (the chosen persistence behavior). It is bounded only by: the idle-lapse window,
carryover findings still being enforced at the normal bar, and every dropped finding being
recorded in the sidecar. Optional future safety valve: a `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds`
cap that forces a full un-floored review. (No unsound *coverage* accumulates — Pass-1 always
runs the full criteria set; only the surfacing of novel low-priority findings is suppressed.)

## Empirical grounding (established)

- 245 `REVIEW_RESULT` events / 2,571 findings: the verifier's impact axis already
  discriminates (15% critical, 40% none, mean impact 0.43; attributes spread sensibly) — so
  impact discrimination is not a blocker; the floor has real spread to act on.
- The impact prompt nonetheless gives the severity attributes zero anchoring (vs rich
  guidance for validity) → tightening it is a robustness item, not a blocker.

## Already landed (observability foundation)

- `scripts/plan_review_impact_distribution.py` — repeatable corpus distribution report.
- `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scorer + `high_impact`/`low_impact` dataset pairs on
  `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml`.

## Decomposition (6 child tasks)

1. Persist finding text in the sidecar + latest-sidecar reader (foundation).
2. Pass-2 novelty sub-answers in a SEPARATE sub-call + a `discriminates_novelty` eval gate.
3. Pass-3 novelty score + rising-floor drop rule (depends on 2; gated by the eval bar).
4. Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring (depends on 1).
5. Tighten the verifier impact prompt (robustness; verified by the impact eval).
6. Docs + ADR + offline convergence tests (depends on 3, 4).

## Scope

- IN: full-run + deterministic rising floor; separate-sub-call novelty scoring + its eval
  gate; freshness-window remediation-mode gating; sidecar finding-text persistence;
  impact-prompt tightening; config keys; docs + ADR.
- OUT: the code-drift `drift_refresh` path (unchanged); per-diff-region scoping;
  skip-clean-criteria reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Sidecar `_slim` persists `finding`, `suggested_fix`, `checklist_item` (sidecar event
      only; surfaced verdict shape byte-unchanged); a latest-sidecar reader exists; the
      `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` retention bound is respected.
- [ ] Pass-2 scores novelty in a SEPARATE structured sub-call that alone receives prior
      findings; the severity/validity sub-call receives none (independence enforced
      structurally). Pass-1 receives no prior findings.
- [ ] A `discriminates_novelty` eval scorer (per-case, 0.5 midpoint) + ≥ 3 labeled
      carryover/novel pairs land on a DEDICATED `plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml` (keyed to the
      `plan-review-novelty` prompt — NOT the verifier spec, where the scorer would grade the
      wrong artifact; this dedicated-spec correction was mandated by child 150b's plan review);
      its bar is
      `gate: at_least(2)`/`epochs: 3` + `coverage_threshold: 0.8` (NOT an AUC literal),
      distinct from the runtime `T_novel=0.7`; the scorer clears that bar before the Pass-3
      drop rule is activated (the evidence gate).
- [ ] Pass-3: deterministic novelty score; drop iff novelty ≥ `T_novel` AND priority < floor;
      carryover → normal threshold; novel high-priority → preserved; dropped → sidecar.
- [ ] Defaults committed: `T_novel = 0.7` and the priority floor at the stated corpus
      percentile (config-overridable); the distribution script prints the inputs.
- [ ] Remediation-mode gate: config key (**default-OFF** for v1, expand-contract rollout) +
      window minutes (default 60, measured from the last review of any kind and reset each
      review); code-unchanged precondition via `verified_at_sha` equality (prior manifest vs
      current run); both-drifted → full review; key off/absent restores byte-identical full review.
- [ ] Coverage on a narrowed verdict sets `narrowed: true` + `floored_criteria` + floored
      finding ids; dropped novel findings are written to the sidecar.
- [ ] Impact-prompt tightening is verified by the `discriminates_impact_levels` eval scoring
      at or above its threshold on the existing high/low pairs (not an effort claim).
- [ ] Offline FakeRunner tests: convergence on a remediation edit; each precondition fallback
      to a byte-identical full review; novel high-priority preserved; carryover enforced.
- [ ] Docs: a `docs/plan-review-gate.md` section AND an ADR under `docs/adr/` recording the
      chosen design, the three rejected alternatives, and the invariants (Pass-1 unanchored;
      novelty in a separate Pass-2 sub-call; drop decision deterministic in Pass-3).
- [ ] A remediation re-review (pure plan edit, code unchanged, within window) runs the full
- [ ] Severity/validity independence is enforced structurally (novelty in a separate Pass-2
- [ ] Any precondition failing → byte-identical full review; `drift_refresh` behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope / explicitly deferred

- Any change to the code-drift `drift_refresh` path.
- A `max_consecutive_narrowed_rounds` cap on within-session suppression (optional future
  safety valve; the chosen design accepts unbounded within-session suppression while the
  agent is actively iterating).
baseline.summary: Convergent plan-edit re-review: full-run + deterministic rising floor

content.text: ## Why
LangChain/LangGraph is heavy (~80-110 deps) and its sole original justification (native Langfuse tracing) is
obsolete. Pydantic AI is provider-agnostic (the cross-provider hard requirement) at ~half the deps. Validated by
docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/runtime_pydanticai_poc.py.
## What
Implement a PydanticAIRunner behind the existing Runner protocol: single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents
with filesystem + MCP (stdio/http) + custom rebar-operation tools; no per-provider code (provider chosen by
config/model string). Keep FakeRunner. Parallel-run-and-diff against LangGraphRunner on the corpuses before any
cutover.
## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py (PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam)
- pyproject.toml [agents] (add pydantic-ai-slim extras)
Out: dropping LangGraph (separate story); the structured-output stack (separate story).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner implements run/preflight behind the Runner seam; FakeRunner unaffected.
- [ ] Tools wired: filesystem, MCP (stdio + http), and custom rebar-op tools.
- [ ] No per-provider code; provider selected via config/model string (Anthropic primary).

- [ ] Parallel-run-and-diff vs LangGraphRunner meets the DEFINED PARITY BAR on the corpuses before any cutover. Parity = NON-INFERIORITY, not byte-identity (outputs are LLM-driven, so exact equality is incoherent). On the standing eval corpus (DSO + snap + rebar tickets), same model + decoding params, N>=3 repeats: (a) structured-output validity v2 >= v1 (target >=99% valid parses, no regression); (b) per-criterion verdict agreement >= 95% AND zero decision-level flips (block/advisory/dropped) on the gold set; (c) recall and false-accept each within +/-2pp of v1 (non-inferiority margin, paired test); (d) runtime error/timeout rate v2 <= v1; (e) cost/latency recorded (informational, non-gating). The LangGraph drop (d6d1) is blocked until this bar is met.

baseline.summary: Provider-agnostic Pydantic AI runtime behind the Runner seam

baseline.description:
## Why
The plan-v2 impact model floors four failure-mode axes at 0.85 (above every blocking threshold) whenever the axis is non-none at ANY grade - the floor is grade-blind. Calibration 3 (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly; evidence comment on this story, 2026-07-15) measured the consequence on the plan-v2 segment: 35.5% of ALL blocking findings (807/2271) are floor-driven (would not block without the override), ac_unverifiable alone is 48.9% of the floor-driven set, 52/100 of a classified sample fired at grade=low, and the oracle-kind classification split 56% underspecified_oracle / 37% broken-oracle-shaped / 7% missing_oracle. The dominant floor-driven class is "a check exists, the plan just doesn't spell out the exact command/file/value" - a refinement demand that today auto-blocks with the same force as a genuinely untestable criterion. This story splits the axis so severity follows the actual defect.

## What
Replace the binary-ish ac_unverifiable severity grading with a THREE-value oracle-kind grade in the plan-review verification model, assigned explicitly by the pass-2 verifier (the calibration-3 evidence motivates three, not two - a broken oracle is not a refinement):
- missing_oracle: no verification method exists or could exist as the criterion is phrased (7% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor.
- broken_oracle: a stated proving command/symbol/count is factually wrong - nonexistent path, wrong CLI, contradictory assertion - so the stated verification CANNOT pass (37% of sample) - KEEPS the 0.85 hard floor (the check is protective; these are real plan defects).
- underspecified_oracle: a check exists or is clearly constructible; the finding demands the exact command/file/expected value (56% of sample) - scores BELOW the lowest blocking threshold in force after calibration 3 (0.60), i.e. maps to an impact contribution <= 0.55, so it surfaces and is coached but never auto-blocks.
BOTH verifier prompts define the three grades with one worked example each drawn from the calibration-3 classified sample (the gate YAML routes to TWO prompt files: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md - both change in lockstep). SCORING MECHANICS (exact decide.py change): impact_plan currently scores all seven axes through the shared ordinal map _SEV01 ({none,low,medium,high}) in TWO generic loops - the contribs list comprehension over _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES and the has_override any() over _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES. ac_unverifiable is REMOVED from both generic loops and special-cased: (1) contribs = [_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) for a in _PLAN_SEVERITY_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable"] + [ORACLE_GRADE01.get(attrs.get("ac_unverifiable"), 0.0)]; (2) has_override = any(_SEV01.get(attrs.get(a), 0.0) > 0.0 for a in _PLAN_HARD_OVERRIDE_AXES if a != "ac_unverifiable") or attrs.get("ac_unverifiable") in ("broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"). ORACLE_GRADE01 = {"none": 0.0, "underspecified_oracle": UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB, "broken_oracle": 1.0, "missing_oracle": 1.0} with UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB = 0.55 defined as a named module constant whose comment states its invariant (strictly below the lowest blocking threshold in criteria_routing.json), and a unit test asserts UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(block_threshold over blocking-posture criteria) so a future threshold recalibration below 0.55 fails loudly instead of silently re-enabling blocks. An unknown/legacy grade string maps to 0.0 via .get() default in plan-v3 scoring - legacy records are never scored with plan-v3 code anyway (segmentation, below). The other six axes keep _SEV01 and the any-non-none override unchanged. WRITE-TIME ENFORCEMENT (the concrete mechanism): src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py owns PlanSeverityAttrs; its ac_unverifiable field changes from the ordinal type to Literal["none", "underspecified_oracle", "broken_oracle", "missing_oracle"], so Pydantic strict validation rejects out-of-vocabulary grades at verification-parse time - that field is the closed-set gate the ACs pin. OPERATOR-ATTESTED ENRICH: workflow_ops.enrich_operator_attested's guard changes from `not in (None, "", "none")` to the explicit clearable set `in ("missing_oracle", "underspecified_oracle")` (clears to "none" when attested evidence satisfies the criterion - the recorded attestation IS the oracle) while broken_oracle is never cleared (a factually wrong stated command is not cured by an attestation) - this file is in Scope and the asymmetry is pinned by test. BACK-COMPAT: the closed-set validation applies to NEW plan-v3 verifications at parse time; already-stored plan-v2 sidecars keep their legacy {low,medium,high} grades and are read as-is - every calibration/replay consumer segments by impact_model_version (ADR 0036), so old records are never scored with new semantics - and this is pinned by a TEST (a plan-v2 fixture sidecar with grade "low" round-trips unmodified through latest_review_result/all_review_results). The sidecar SCHEMA id stays plan_review_result_v2: the payload shape (keys, nesting) is unchanged - only the value vocabulary of one severity-attribute field changes - so the schema-string guard in the readers keeps matching; IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION (plan-v3) is the segmentation key for the semantics change. ROLLBACK: the version bump makes back-out clean - reverting the change restores plan-v2 semantics and the corpora stay segmented; no expand-contract migration is needed because sidecars are immutable records, not migrated state. IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bumps plan-v2 -> plan-v3 in the same change. The other three override axes (dod_uncertifiable, undecomposed, divergent_implementation) keep their ordinal vocabulary and any-non-none floor, untouched in this story (their grade mix is unmeasured; calibration 4 scope).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py: ORACLE_GRADE01 + UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB constants; ac_unverifiable excluded from both generic _SEV01 loops and special-cased per the exact change spec above.
- src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py: PlanSeverityAttrs.ac_unverifiable becomes the closed Literal grade type (the write-time enforcement mechanism).
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py: enrich_operator_attested vocabulary update (clears missing/underspecified on attestation, never broken_oracle).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md AND plan_review_verifier_agentic.md: three-grade definitions + one worked example each; the plan-review verification output schema accepts exactly {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for the axis and rejects anything else at write time.
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py: IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump to plan-v3; the grade persists in verification.severity_attributes as today (values change, key stays).
- Unit tests: tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py (replace old low/medium/high ac_unverifiable pins with the three-grade pins; keep other-axis pins), tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py (plan-v2 -> plan-v3 assertion), tests/unit/_audit_page_helpers.py (hardcoded plan-v2 string updated), new pins for: schema acceptance AND rejection of an invalid grade, sidecar persistence, the enrich asymmetry, the UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB < min(blocking thresholds) invariant, and the plan-v2 legacy-fixture read-as-is round-trip.
- docs/plan-review-gate.md: the floor description updated to the graded rule with the back-compat note.
- Coordination: story ea39 (R5 kernel sub-answer, epic pastoral-aquatic-viper) also plans a version bump and depends_on this story - if both land close together the bumps compose (v3 then v4), never merge into one ambiguous version.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The verification model accepts exactly the closed grade set {none, underspecified_oracle, broken_oracle, missing_oracle} for ac_unverifiable on new plan-v3 verifications - pinned by BOTH an acceptance test and a rejection test for an out-of-vocabulary grade - and both verifier prompts (single-turn + agentic) define each grade with one worked example.
- [ ] Impact scoring pinned by unit tests: missing_oracle and broken_oracle findings floor at >= 0.85; underspecified_oracle findings score <= 0.55 (below the 0.60 lowest blocking threshold) and never trigger the hard floor; the other three override axes floor unchanged.
- [ ] IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION is plan-v3 in the same change (test_impact_model_versioning.py updated), the grade persists per finding in the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar (pinned by test), legacy plan-v2 records are read as-is (segmentation by version is the back-compat mechanism, asserted in the doc note), and enrich_operator_attested clears missing/underspecified but never broken_oracle (pinned by test).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents the three-grade rule citing the calibration-3 evidence comment on this story, and the change is MERGED through Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Split ac_unverifiable hard-floor axis into oracle-kind grades: missing/broken keep the floor, underspecified demotes (plan-v3)

content.text: ## What
Add a tickets-branch `.gitattributes` declaring `merge=ours` for the per-pass
mutable shared-root files so the union merge introduced in WU-2 never wedges on
them. uuid-named ticket dirs never collide; only `.bridge_state/bindings.json`
and the reconciler lock/gate files are rewritten every pass and would conflict.
The loser is a derived cache the reconciler rebuilds next pass — never ticket
events. `merge=union` is WRONG here (it line-unions JSON into invalid JSON).
This formalises behaviour `push.py` already handles ad hoc today, so it is a safe
standalone change and lands before WU-2 so the merge is conflict-free by construction.
## Scope (files)
- Tickets-branch `.gitattributes` (written/ensured at init):
`.bridge_state/* merge=ours` and `.reconciler-* merge=ours`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`: ensure the `.gitattributes` is created/maintained
idempotently on the tickets branch.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tickets-branch `.gitattributes` ships `merge=ours` for `.bridge_state/*` and `.reconciler-*`
- [ ] `.gitattributes` is created idempotently at init (re-runnable)
- [ ] `merge=union` is NOT used (would corrupt JSON)
- [ ] Convergence test: two clones each rewriting `bindings.json` merge without a wedge
