baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan review that trips a provider context limit escalates the Pass-1 finder onto a model the run was never configured for. On a run whose model is provider-qualified for anything other than the provider inferred from the model NAME — a Bedrock deployment being the live case — the recovery path silently relocates the call to direct Anthropic: a hard failure in a provider-isolated container, or unbudgeted spend wherever an Anthropic key happens to exist. This is the founding defect of epic 061c on a second, independent code path: the ENTRY rung was routed through the model-class vocabulary, the ESCALATION rungs were not.

Confirmed by running the function on this tree with no class table configured:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")
      -> ["claude-opus-4-8"]        # bare, direct-Anthropic-inferring

## Root cause

`_rung_target` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:332-359`) decides a rung's escalation target by comparing the RUNG's own provider-inferred form against that rung's class resolution:

    resolved = resolve_model_string(class_name)       # sizing.py:354
    provider = infer_provider(bare)                   # sizing.py:355
    own = f"{provider}:{bare}" if provider else bare  # sizing.py:356
    return bare if resolved == own else resolved      # sizing.py:357

Both sides of that comparison are derived from the ladder constant. **The model the run is actually on is never an input.** So whenever the class table has not been retargeted the equality holds and the rung degrades to `MODEL_LADDER`'s bare Anthropic family name (`sizing.py:99-103`), discarding whatever provider qualifier `cfg.model` carried. `models_at_or_above` (`sizing.py:362-376`) hands those targets to the escalation loop, which assigns them straight onto the run config at `sizing.py:427-431`:

    for model in models_at_or_above(cfg.model):
        passes.pass1_chunk(runner, replace(cfg, model=model), ...)

Two consequences, both reproduced against the current tree:

1. A Bedrock-qualified primary escalates to a bare Anthropic id (transcript above).
   `cfg.model_provider` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:391`) is left untouched by `replace`, so a run
   that qualified through that field instead composes an id like `bedrock:claude-opus-4-8`,
   which is not a valid Bedrock model id.
2. The Pass-1 entry rung names `frontier` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:76`, resolved
   at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:97-100`), so
   `models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` returns the single-element list
   `["claude-opus-4-8"]`. The substitution therefore executes on the COMMON one-criterion retry,
   before any escalation is needed — it is not confined to a rare deep-escalation case.

When a class table IS configured for another provider the current code is already correct (`models_at_or_above` returns the Bedrock ladder, asserted at `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204-212`). The live gap is the UNCONFIGURED-table plus provider-qualified-`cfg.model` combination, which no test covers.

## Approach

Make the rung target a function of the model the run is on, and make the unnameable case fail SAFE instead of crossing providers.

`models_at_or_above` already holds the primary, so thread it into `_rung_target`. Resolve the rung through its model class exactly as today, then compare the RUN's provider (`infer_provider(primary)`) with the TARGET's provider (`infer_provider(target)`):

- providers agree, or either is undeterminable -> return today's value byte-for-byte;
- providers differ and the rung is the PRIMARY's OWN rung -> return `primary` verbatim, so the
  same-model one-criterion retry still runs on the operator's model (that retry is the step that
  most often succeeds, since one criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch);
- providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung. The class vocabulary is the only thing
  that can name that rung in the run's provider and it has not been configured, so there is no
  honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding
  (`sizing.py:450-471`) reports it — a visible outcome instead of a silent provider jump.

The rule applies only on the branch that LOCATED a start rung (`sizing.py:373-375`). The no-match fallback (`sizing.py:376`) is left exactly as today, because without a located start rung there is no "primary's own rung" to preserve; see Scope for why that branch is out of scope.

Why this approach fits: the defect is that a decision about the CURRENT run is made from module constants alone, so the fix is to give the decision the run's model — the smallest input that makes the question answerable. It keeps the model-class vocabulary as the single source of escalation targets (the epic's rule) while preserving the byte-for-byte back-compat that the docstring at `sizing.py:335-347` exists to protect, so no existing caller's strings change.

Deliberately NOT changed: on an unqualified or Anthropic-qualified primary the target stays the bare form (`anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` -> `claude-opus-4-8`). That substitution is byte-different but provider-identical. The harm was never the bare FORM; it was the provider CHANGE, and the provider-agreement rule is what removes that. Preserving the bare form is the back-compat contract that keeps `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150` and `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271` passing unmodified.

`MODEL_LADDER` also keeps its bare family names. It carries two roles and only one moves: it is also the WINDOW table that `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) reads by substring match (`if name in model`), which is why `sizing.py:319-324` records that class names in that table would make every window lookup miss. Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model families. That separates the two orderings the constant conflates without splitting the constant.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `_rung_target` takes the primary model as an argument
  and applies the provider-agreement rule; `models_at_or_above` passes it on the located-start-rung
  branch. No other function in the file changes.
- `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py` — new cases (see Testing). This is the existing home of
  the ladder's model-class contract, holding both the byte-for-byte control (lines 256-271) and
  the configured-Bedrock case (lines 204-212) this change must not disturb.

Explicitly OUT of scope, to be raised as a separate ticket: `models_at_or_above` locates the START rung by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names against the primary (`sizing.py:373-374`), so a primary from another model family falls through to the whole ladder beginning at the trivial rung — confirmed on this tree: `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` returns all three Anthropic rungs, so a context-limit escalation would DOWNGRADE the window. `largest_window_tokens` has the matching gap, returning the ladder maximum (1,000,000) for that same primary. That is a different mechanism — rung LOCATION, not rung TARGET — and this change leaves it byte-for-byte as it is.

## Testing

New cases in `tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py`, using its existing `no_classes` and `_set_class_table` fixtures.

- **The defect, on the escalation path itself** — not on `models_at_or_above` in isolation. Drive
  `sizing.pass1_with_ladder` with a stub runner whose first (batch) call raises a context-limit
  error (`is_context_limit_error`, `sizing.py:300-316`, matches the substring
  `"prompt is too long"`) and a `cfg` whose model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`
  with no class table. Assert the `cfg.model` observed by the one-criterion retry call is that
  exact string. This is the case an entry-rung test structurally cannot catch, which is why the
  defect survived the entry-rung fix.
- **Worked example, unit level** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` returns
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0"]`. Today it returns `["claude-opus-4-8"]`.
- **Edge, higher rungs are dropped rather than crossed** — with no class table:
  `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` returns exactly
  `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]`, and no returned element contains
  `claude-sonnet` or `claude-opus`.
- **Edge, escalation still reports the size failure** — the same Bedrock-haiku primary under a
  runner that raises a context-limit error at every attempt still yields the existing `_too_big`
  failure finding (`sizing.py:450-471`) rather than an empty result or a raised exception.
- **Back-compat controls, kept passing unmodified** — the byte-for-byte case
  (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:256-271`, covering bare rungs, `None`, and
  `"some-unknown-model"`), the order case (lines 275-299), the configured-Bedrock case
  (lines 204-212), and `orchestrator._models_at_or_above`'s literal assertions
  (`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145-1150`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no model-class table configured and a primary of
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`, the model that reaches `passes.pass1_chunk` on
      the one-criterion retry is that same string; verified by the new `pass1_with_ladder` test
      asserting the observed `cfg.model`, which fails against the current tree.
- [ ] No escalation target is returned whose inferred provider differs from the primary's
      inferred provider when both are determinable; verified by a test asserting
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0")` equals
      `["bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-v1:0"]` under the `no_classes` fixture.
- [ ] Dropping unnameable higher rungs does not turn escalation into a crash or a silent empty
      result: the all-attempts-fail case still produces the `_too_big` failure finding; verified
      by the new failure-path test asserting `finding["_too_big"] is True`.
- [ ] Escalation targets still come from the model-class vocabulary when a class table IS
      configured; verified by `test_models_at_or_above_stays_on_bedrock_for_a_bedrock_primary`
      (`tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py:204`) passing unmodified.
- [ ] The window sizes that drive the escalation DECISION are unchanged; verified by `git diff`
      showing no change to `MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) or `largest_window_tokens`
      (`sizing.py:137-146`).
- [ ] Back-compat: with no class table configured, every escalation target for an unqualified or
      Anthropic-qualified primary is today's value byte-for-byte, including the
      `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` common path that yields bare `claude-opus-4-8`; verified by
      `test_models_at_or_above_returns_todays_bare_ids_with_no_classes_configured` and
      `test_models_at_or_above_escalation_order_is_unchanged` passing unmodified.
- [ ] The out-of-scope start-rung behaviour is untouched:
      `models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` still returns the three bare
      Anthropic rungs; verified by a pinning test asserting that exact list.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` passes, and
      `make lint` and `make typecheck` are clean.
baseline.summary: Pass-1 context-limit escalation sets a BARE Anthropic model id, bypassing the model-class table

content.text: ## Why

list-epics duplicates query/reduction logic that belongs in the generic list primitive. Generalize the generic filters so 'get epics' is one generic call, then reduce list-epics to a thin deprecating wrapper. Orthogonal to the bash->Python strangler-fig (adult-oxide-slave) — tracked on its own.
## What
1. Expand the generic 'list' read primitive (rebar._engine_support.reads.list_states + ticket_reads CLI + library list_tickets + MCP list tool):
- --min-children=N : tickets with >= N non-deleted direct children.
- --unblocked / --blocked : filter by blocking state (reuse rebar.graph find_ready_tickets / all_blockers_closed).
- include a children_count field in list output (cheap, additive, universal) so one call returns enriched epics.

2. list-epics becomes a thin wrapper: (a) display deprecation warning (stderr), (b) ONE call to get epics (generic list --type=epic --status=open,in_progress [--unblocked] [--min-children]), (c) ONE call to get P0 bugs (generic list --type=bug --priority=0, counted), (d) assemble the {p0_bugs, epics} output. Replaces the bespoke ticket-list-epics.sh reduction.
3. Surfaces: CLI dispatcher arm, library list_epics(), MCP list_epics tool — all wrap + warn.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] generic list gains --min-children + --unblocked/--blocked + children_count, at CLI + library + MCP
- [ ] new filters/field covered by tests; list output schema updated for children_count
- [ ] list-epics is a wrapper: warns + 1 call epics + 1 call P0 bugs -> {p0_bugs, epics}; no bespoke reduction
- [ ] deprecation warning at CLI (stderr, not stdout/JSON) + library (DeprecationWarning) + MCP description
- [ ] list-epics output parity preserved ({p0_bugs, epics}); existing schema/MCP tests green or updated
- [ ] docs note the deprecation + new generic filters

baseline.summary: Generalize list filters + deprecate list-epics to a thin wrapper (orthogonal to strangler-fig)

baseline.description:
## Idea (parking lot — out of scope for the code-health analyzer epic 839b-f6d2)
Add a polyglot **dependency-graph** capability to the code-health analyzer (module/file coupling, fan-in/fan-out, cycles) so a per-project graph signal can feed the metrics registry.

## Why it's a separate idea, not part of the epic
The portability audit found there is **no mature, single, drop-in polyglot dependency-graph OSS CLI** (unlike LOC/complexity/duplication, which scc/lizard/jscpd cover). Realistic paths, all heavier:
- Per-language adapters behind the analyzer seam: dependency-cruiser / madge (JS/TS), pydeps (Python), `go mod graph` (Go), jdeps (Java).
- Polyglot foundations to build on (frameworks, not turnkey): tree-sitter + GitHub stack-graphs, or Sourcegraph SCIP indexers; heavyweight end: CodeQL.

## Open questions (to design before promoting out of idea)
- Which graph signals are worth a metric (cycle count? max coupling? fan-in hotspots?) and are they cross-language comparable?
- Single polyglot foundation (tree-sitter/SCIP) vs. a registry of per-language adapters with honest Unavailable where none exists?
- Cost/determinism/CI-time budget vs. value.

Treat as future work; do not block the scc/lizard/jscpd epic on it.
baseline.summary: Polyglot dependency-graph analyzer capability for code-health metrics

## Context
Bring the symmetric HMAC-SHA256 primitive (`src/rebar/signing.py`) into the attest scheme registry (`src/rebar/attest/registry.py`, task 518b) as a **first-class registry scheme** so the substrate acknowledges HMAC and both consumer epics reference one registry. This is the **expand** phase.

**Scope boundary (deliberate).** Existing plan-review / completion-verifier attestations are stored in the *legacy* shape: a hex HMAC over the canonical `{v,algorithm,ticket_id,manifest}` payload, in the record `signature` field — NOT a DSSE envelope. This leaf does **NOT** reroute those old records through the registry; they keep verifying **unchanged** through the untouched `signing.py` path. What this leaf adds is (a) an `HmacScheme` registered in the registry (so HMAC is a known scheme, keyed by its algorithm id) and (b) `POLICY` entries pinning the legacy kinds to it. The HMAC->asymmetric cutover and any re-enveloping of old records is the op-cert epic contract phase, out of scope here.

## Contract (concrete)
- `HmacScheme` implements the registry `Scheme` protocol; `name = signing.ALGORITHM` (`"HMAC-SHA256"`).
- `HmacScheme.verify(pae_bytes, signatures, namespace, trust_root) -> registry.Verdict` computes HMAC-SHA256 over `pae_bytes` (the DSSE-PAE bytes) using the key supplied as `trust_root` and constant-time-compares (`hmac.compare_digest`) to `signatures[0].sig` (the raw bytes of the first `dsse.Signature`). Result: match -> `Verdict(True,"certified",...)`; non-match -> `Verdict(False,"mismatch",...)`; empty/missing key -> fail closed `Verdict(False,"foreign_key",...)`; no signatures -> `Verdict(False,"mismatch",...)`.
- `register_legacy_schemes()` is **idempotent**: registers the `HmacScheme` and pins `POLICY["plan-review"]` and `POLICY["completion-verifier"]` to `Policy(scheme="HMAC-SHA256", namespace="rebar-attest-hmac")`. Called once from `src/rebar/attest/__init__.py` at import.

## Files
- `src/rebar/attest/hmac_legacy.py` — `HmacScheme` + `register_legacy_schemes()`.
- `src/rebar/attest/__init__.py` — call `register_legacy_schemes()` at import.
- `src/rebar/signing.py` — **UNCHANGED** (regression guard).
- `tests/unit/test_attest_hmac_legacy.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After import, `registry.get_scheme("HMAC-SHA256")` returns the `HmacScheme`, and `registry.resolve("plan-review").scheme == "HMAC-SHA256"` and `registry.resolve("completion-verifier").scheme == "HMAC-SHA256"` (both pinned to namespace `rebar-attest-hmac`) — test asserts all four.
- [ ] `HmacScheme.verify` fail-closed matrix over DSSE-PAE bytes: correct key -> `certified`; wrong key -> `mismatch`; empty key -> `foreign_key`; empty signatures list -> not certified. A round-trip helper builds `signatures[0].sig = hmac_sha256(key, pae_bytes)` to prove the certified path.
- [ ] `register_legacy_schemes()` is idempotent — calling it twice leaves exactly one `HMAC-SHA256` scheme and the same two POLICY entries (test).
- [ ] Regression / no-behavior-change: a plan-review manifest signed via `signing.sign_manifest` still returns `verdict == "certified"` from `signing.verify_signature`, and `src/rebar/signing.py` sign/verify functions are not modified by this change (test signs+verifies exactly as before and gets `certified`).
baseline.summary: attest: register existing HMAC as a legacy scheme

## Context / Problem
`_idempotent_reuse` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:460-508) requires `claim_gate_check` to pass, which requires a certified signature; a BLOCK never signs (__init__.py:711-717). So re-running review-plan on an unchanged blocked plan re-pays the full ~26-call review. Store history shows 117 unrevised BLOCK retries. The sidecar already stamps `verified_at_sha` on every verdict for exactly this purpose (sidecar.py:600-604: "a BLOCK loop leaves a usable baseline even though a BLOCK never signs").

## Approach
Add a `_verdict_reuse` path beside `_idempotent_reuse`: when no attestation exists, read `sidecar.latest_review_result`; if its `material_fingerprint` equals `attest.current_material_fingerprint` AND its `verified_at_sha` equals the current review code sha AND its verdict is BLOCK, reconstruct the BLOCK verdict from the stored findings/coaching/coverage and return it with `coverage.llm_ran=False, coverage.verdict_reuse=True`, emitting no new sidecar. `--force` bypasses (existing semantics, _cli/_llm_commands.py:470-477). Precedent for the sidecar-baseline comparison: `attest._sidecar_branch_decision` (attest.py:337-380). Alternative rejected: signing BLOCK attestations — would complicate the claim gate's PASS-only trust model for no claim-side benefit.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py (new reuse branch), src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py (render reused BLOCK with a "reused" marker; exit 1 preserved), tests/llm/test_plan_review_reuse.py (new).

## Testing
Unit with FakeRunner: unchanged fingerprint+sha after BLOCK -> zero runner invocations, exit 1; changed fingerprint -> full review runs; --force -> full review runs; PASS idempotent path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Re-running review-plan on identical material_fingerprint and verified_at_sha after a BLOCK performs zero LLM calls (checked: unit test asserts FakeRunner is never invoked and coverage.verdict_reuse is True).
- [ ] A reused BLOCK exits 1 and renders the stored findings with a "reused" marker (checked: CLI renderer unit test).
- [ ] --force bypasses verdict reuse and runs the full review (checked: unit test asserts runner invoked).
- [ ] Existing PASS idempotent-reuse tests pass unmodified (checked: pytest run of the existing reuse tests).
baseline.summary: review-plan re-runs the full LLM review after an unchanged BLOCK (idempotent skip covers PASS only)

## Why

`compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror` (default False) is the CONTRACT-phase rollback
lever of the additive-attestations rollout (epic dark-acme-lumen). Its default already
means "never emit the legacy `state['signature']` mirror into new snapshots" — so
removing it does NOT change runtime behavior. What removal deletes is the documented
one-line ROLLBACK (`= true` + recompact) that re-emits the mirror for a still-live
pre-attestations reader. Approved for removal; this story does it responsibly.

## What

- Remove the field + validator from `CompactConfig` (`_config_schema.py:367` and the
  parser entry in the `compact` section, `~:515`).
- Hardcode never-emit in `_snapshot_strip_keys` (`_commands/compact.py:127-136`):
  always add `"signature"` to the dropped-keys set; delete the `emit_legacy_mirror`
  branch.
- PRESERVE the in-memory mirror path: `process_signature` re-deriving `state["signature"]`
  during replay (`reducer/_processors.py:562-604`) and the `most_recent_attestation`
  fallback (`signing.py:563-568`) stay — this story only stops PERSISTING the mirror
  into new snapshots; it does not touch the in-memory back-compat projection.
- Doc-sweep coordination: the doc-sweep story removes references; this story updates
  `docs/migrations.md` "Legacy signature-mirror retirement" to record the retirement
  and that the rollback lever is gone.

## Scope — the one-way door (handle, don't skip)

Backward-compat verdict (from assessment): CONDITIONAL. Removal is a ONE-WAY DOOR. It is
safe for THIS fleet (hourly auto-update to origin/main ⇒ no pre-attestations binary is
live). It WOULD break an external project on older rebar that reads a mirror-less
snapshot whose latest signature was compacted below the horizon (the reader sees no
`signature`, cannot read `attestations`, and the SIGNATURE event is gone) — after
removal the only recovery is a code downgrade, not a config flip.

Therefore, before landing: assert the readiness gate (`docs/migrations.md:149-156`)
holds — no pre-attestations clone/reconcile-host shares this store — and record the
one-way-door retirement in the release notes so any downstream consumer is warned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `emit_legacy_signature_mirror` removed from schema, parser, and `rebar.toml` (if present); new snapshots never persist the `signature` mirror.
- [ ] `process_signature` in-memory mirror + `most_recent_attestation` fallback are UNCHANGED (prove with existing signing/replay tests green).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Readiness gate asserted: no pre-attestations rebar binary reads this store (state the basis — e.g. fleet auto-update policy).
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` "Legacy signature-mirror retirement" updated to record the retirement and removal of the rollback lever; release notes warn downstream consumers of the one-way door.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Retire compact.emit_legacy_signature_mirror (hardcode never-emit) after readiness-gate check

content.text: ## Why
Project "invariants" = deterministic pattern-rule criteria (banned APIs, layering, naming). The
consumer already exists: `code_review/detectors.py` calls the shared `grounding.engine_b.scan` +
`load_registry` (which already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) + `apply_failclosed`. But it is
hardcoded to the `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix + 2 criterion mappings and is fail-CLOSED. This
story generalizes it into a data-driven, per-criterion-`fail_mode` consumer usable by any project
invariant, in both gates.
## What
- Generalize the detector→criterion mapping: a data-driven `criterion↔detector` map (drop the
hardcoded `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix) so arbitrary `.rebar/detectors/` rules route to an
activated DET criterion.
- Per-criterion `fail_mode: open|closed` on the routing record (default `open` for project
invariants; `closed` for the built-in security class). The ORACLE stays fail-open (abstain on
absent-binary/parse-error/timeout); the CONSUMER applies `fail_mode` — `open` → skip=PASS,
`closed` → BLOCK (the existing `apply_failclosed` path). One code path parameterized by
`fail_mode`, not two behaviors.
- DET fallback descriptor shape (a `_descriptor_from_prompt` DET branch that skips `get_prompt`):
`name`=routing name/id, `scenario`=detector rule `message`, `facet`=routing facet (default id),
`checklist`=empty. Expand-contract (prompt-backed callers unaffected).
- Expose the generalized consumer to **plan-review** (which calls no scan consumer today — only
`refute_absence` in `det_floor.py`); matches are gate-scoped (code-review: diff; plan-review:
plan/N-A).
## Scope
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py` (generalize), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`
(new DET-invariant consumer wiring), `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` (DET descriptor
branch + `fail_mode`), the routing schema.
- Depends on story `#1` (registry/overlay/activation). Reuses the shared grounding facade
(already unions `.rebar/detectors/`) — no new oracle work.
- Out: graph-level invariants (transitive layering/cycles) — a later follow-on, not a new DSL.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The scan consumer is data-driven (no hardcoded `rebar.builtin.security.` prefix); an
activated project DET invariant routes its `.rebar/detectors/` rule and surfaces findings.
- [ ] Per-criterion `fail_mode` honored: project invariants default fail-open (abstain→skip=PASS);
the security class stays fail-closed (abstain→BLOCK) via the existing `apply_failclosed`.
- [ ] DET criteria build a descriptor without a prompt (the DET `_descriptor_from_prompt` branch).
- [ ] The generalized consumer is wired into plan-review as well as code-review; matches are
gate-scoped (diff for code-review; plan/N-A for plan-review).
- [ ] Fail-open is preserved on engine-binary-absent / parse-error / timeout for `fail_mode:open`.
## Plan-review consumer integration (remediation, run 1)
### Match-scoping without a diff (clears G6 blocker 1)
Plan-review has no diff, so a project DET invariant is scoped to the ticket's DECLARED intent +
its `file_impact` paths (from the ticket state), NOT a whole-repo scan surfaced as new work:
- If the ticket declares `file_impact` paths, the consumer scopes matches to THOSE paths (the
files this plan intends to touch) — the plan-time analog of code-review's `changed_files`
diff-scope. A match in a declared file surfaces as a finding.
- If there is no `file_impact`, the DET invariant is advisory-only over the repo context (it
cannot pin the match to this plan's change), never a hard block on a pre-existing whole-repo
violation — this is why NO baseline/grandfathering is needed (pre-existing violations outside
the plan's declared files are not surfaced as new work).
- An invariant that INHERENTLY needs a diff (e.g. "no new call to X") is **N/A at plan time
(fail-open)** and belongs to code-review. So plan-time DET scoping ∈ {file_impact-scoped,
advisory-repo-context, N-A-fail-open} — never an unscoped whole-repo block.
### Integration point (clears G6 blocker 2)
The generalized consumer runs as an ADDITIONAL DET check appended into `det_floor.run_det_floor`
(alongside P1–P9), returning `DetResult`-shaped results (`id=<project criterion id>`, `name=<detector
rule message>`, `status`, `blocking`, `finding`, `coverage`). Project-invariant results therefore
flow UNCHANGED through the existing partition in `workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck`
(`det_blocking_findings` / `det_advisory_findings` / `det_coverage`) → `orchestrator.partition_findings`.
Blocking is gated by the criterion's `fail_mode` + posture: a `fail_mode:open` invariant that abstains
(engine binary absent / parse-error / timeout) → skip=PASS (advisory at most); a `fail_mode:closed`
(security class) abstain → BLOCK (the existing `apply_failclosed` path, now parameterized). A `match`
in a declared file blocks per the criterion's `default_posture`/`blocking_enabled`.
### Data-driven map location (clears the hardcoded-prefix AC)
The detector→criterion association + `fail_mode` move INTO `criteria_routing.json` (both gates): a
DET criterion's routing entry carries a `detector` selector (id or id-prefix) + `fail_mode:
open|closed`. `run_security_detectors` (renamed to the general `run_detectors`, a thin back-compat
alias kept) reads the routing map instead of the hardcoded `SECURITY_DETECTOR_PREFIX` /
`_criterion_for`; the security class is just the built-in rows (`fail_mode: closed`) — same code
path, data-driven. `_validate_routing_entry` gains `fail_mode ∈ {open, closed}` validation.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)
- [ ] Plan-review DET-invariant matches are scoped to the ticket's `file_impact` (or advisory when
absent) — never an unscoped whole-repo block; a test asserts the scoping.
- [ ] The consumer wires in as a `DetResult`-shaped check via `run_det_floor`, flowing through the
existing det_blocking/det_advisory/det_coverage partition; `fail_mode` gates abstain→block.
## Static P1–P9 + dynamic project-check phase (remediation, run 2)
`DET_CHECKS` (the static `(p1_readiness_shape, …, p9_file_impact_coverage)` tuple) is UNCHANGED —
the built-in floor stays a fixed constant (expand-contract). `run_det_floor(ctx)` gains a SECOND,
additive phase AFTER the static P1–P9 loop: it discovers the activated `exec: DET` PROJECT criteria
at call time from `ctx.repo_root` (via `registry.effective_criteria(ctx.repo_root)` filtered to
`exec == "DET"` + `project.`-prefixed), and for each runs the generalized scan consumer
(`engine_b.scan` over the criterion's `detector` selector, matches scoped to the ticket's
`file_impact`) → one `DetResult` per criterion, appended to the SAME result list P1–P9 return. A
repo with no activated project DET criterion (the common case) adds zero checks ⇒ byte-identical to
today. The phase is fail-open (a raising project check → `abstain`, logged, per the existing
`run_det_floor` fail-open contract), so a misbehaving project rule never breaks the floor.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions, run 2)
- [ ] `DET_CHECKS` stays static; `run_det_floor` adds a call-time second phase that discovers
activated `exec: DET` project criteria from `ctx.repo_root` and appends their `DetResult`s.
A repo with no project DET criterion is byte-identical to today (a test asserts zero added).
## DET-tier isolation, thin-slice sequencing & schema details (remediation, run 4)
### exec:DET criteria never enter the LLM batch (clears G6)
`effective_criteria()` returns activated project ids regardless of tier, so the LLM-routing sites
must FILTER OUT `exec == "DET"`:
- `orchestrator.route_criteria` skips any descriptor whose `exec == "DET"` (they are dispatched to
the DET consumer, never fanned out as an LLM finder) — the same way `ISF` is already excluded.
- `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria`'s `effective` vocabulary excludes `exec == "DET"`
ids from the `include_<id>` batch fan-out (a DET criterion has no finder prompt to run).
- The exclusion filter reads `str(crit.get('exec','')).upper() == 'DET'` DIRECTLY from the
descriptor dict — NOT via `registry.exec_tier()`, which has NO DET arm and silently remaps
DET→1-TURN (so filtering via `exec_tier` would wrongly classify a DET criterion as a
single-turn finder and admit it to the batch). The routing/descriptor path must never hand
a DET descriptor to `pass1_chunk`. A DET descriptor is consumed ONLY by the
`run_det_floor` project-check phase. A test asserts an activated DET project criterion appears in
the DET-floor results and is ABSENT from the LLM `include_*`/route_criteria set.
### Thin-slice sequencing + coherence (clears G5)
This is ONE architectural seam — "the generalized DET-scan consumer, data-driven + exposed to both
gates" — not four independent features; the files it touches are the single call-graph of that one
consumer. Risk-ordered build (each independently testable, no child tickets needed):
1. **MVP:** promote the detector→criterion map + `fail_mode` into `criteria_routing.json` and make
`code_review/detectors.py` read it data-drivenly (drop the hardcoded prefix), security class
preserved fail-closed. Proven by the existing `test_code_review_ws5.py` fail-closed tests.
2. Add the `exec: DET` descriptor branch in `plan_review/registry._descriptor_from_prompt`
(skip `get_prompt`; rubric = detector rule `message`).
3. Add the `run_det_floor` project-DET phase (file_impact-scoped) + DET-tier isolation from the LLM
batch.
### Schema + migration details (clears T8/T4/E1/E5 advisories)
- **`detector` selector shape:** each DET routing entry carries `detector: {id?: str, id_prefix?:
str}` — an exact detector id OR an id-prefix (the security class uses `id_prefix:
"rebar.builtin.security."`, reproducing today's behaviour data-drivenly). Validated in
`_validate_routing_entry`.
- **`fail_mode` default is SAFE:** the built-in security rows in the packaged
`code_review/criteria_routing.json` are written with an EXPLICIT `fail_mode: "closed"` in this
change, so they can never silently revert to open. A DET routing entry with NO `fail_mode`
defaults to `"open"` (project-invariant default); the consumer resolves the value per-criterion.
`_validate_routing_entry` rejects a `fail_mode` outside `{open, closed}`.
- **Rename:** `run_security_detectors` → `run_detectors`; `run_security_detectors` is KEPT as a thin
deprecated alias (a test asserts the alias still returns the same result) so no external caller
breaks.
- **Tests:** `fail_mode` branching (open abstain→skip=PASS, closed abstain→BLOCK) over a fixture;
the three-way plan-review scoping (file_impact-present→finding, absent→advisory, diff-needed→N/A);
the alias equivalence; DET-not-in-LLM-batch isolation.
## Docs deliverable (remediation, run 5)
An ADR (`docs/adr/0016-project-det-invariants.md`) — or an equivalent section extending ADR 0015 —
captures for future maintainers: (1) the **two-phase `run_det_floor`** contract (static P1–P9 tuple
+ a call-time dynamic project-DET phase discovered from `ctx.repo_root`, each check fail-open);
(2) the **`exec: DET` LLM-batch exclusion** rule (the filter sites: `orchestrator.route_criteria`
and `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria` skip DET descriptors so a prompt-less DET criterion
is never handed to `pass1_chunk`); and (3) the **plan-time DET scoping** semantics
(file_impact-scoped → finding / no file_impact → advisory-repo-context / diff-inherent → N/A
fail-open). The routing-schema additions (`detector` selector + `fail_mode`) are documented there
and in the `criteria_routing.json` schema doc.
- [ ] An ADR (or ADR-0015 extension) documents the two-phase run_det_floor contract, the exec:DET
LLM-batch exclusion, and the plan-time DET scoping semantics.
## Cross-story boundaries (remediation, run 7)
- **Parity gate unaffected:** project DET invariants live in the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
OVERLAY, NOT the packaged plan-review `criteria_routing.json`. So `validate_packaged_routing()`
(packaged-only, `CANONICAL_LLM` parity — from ef7e) gains NO new keys and is unaffected. The
`detector` + `fail_mode` fields are ADDITIVE keys WITHIN existing/overlay routing entries, not new
top-level criterion keys, so the orphan check does not fire. (The packaged code-review
`criteria_routing.json`'s security DET rows already exist and are already outside plan-review's
`CANONICAL_LLM` — that gate is plan-review-scoped and does not read code-review's file.)
- **Attestation invalidation is story `08af`, NOT this story:** `attest.registry_version()` today
hashes the PACKAGED routing only. Making it hash the `.rebar/` overlay via
`registry_version(repo_root)` — so that activating/editing a project DET criterion invalidates a
prior attestation at claim time — is the explicit deliverable of story `08af`. This story (`7f0d`)
does NOT modify `registry_version`; it only makes the DET criterion RUN. The two compose: 7f0d
makes project DET invariants execute; 08af makes them attestation-invalidating.

baseline.summary: Project DET invariants: generalize the scan consumer + per-criterion fail_mode

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. A ticket bound to a Jira issue is detached from its parent locally: `rebar edit <id> --parent=null` (parent_id → None).
2. `show <id>` confirms parent_id is empty immediately.
3. Within minutes the reconcile-bridge cron (~3-min) re-parents the ticket back to its old epic.
**Expected:** the detach sticks; Jira's epic-link is cleared to match local.
**Actual:** the detach is silently reverted every reconcile pass (observed on super-plant-liver + toy-kink-ire reverting to epic peak-fir-hilt).
## Root Cause (proven via /joe-debug)
The Jira reconciler had an **asymmetric** parent sync:

- **Outbound never emitted a parent CLEAR.** `outbound_differ._map_local_to_jira_fields` only set `result['parent']` when local parent_id was truthy (outbound_differ.py:364). On a detach (parent_id None), no parent field was mapped, so the field-diff loop's parent branch never ran and outbound emitted nothing, leaving Jira's stale epic-link.

- **Inbound unconditionally re-applied it.** `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` (inbound_differ.py:307-316) re-emitted `parent_id=<epic>` whenever Jira's resolved parent != local parent_id. The same-pass suppression (_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD) only fires when outbound emits a parent mutation, which on a detach it never did.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Outbound differ emits a parent CLEAR (parent: None) when a ticket is detached locally but its Jira snapshot still carries a parent (stale epic-link).
- [ ] The outbound applier (batch_dispatch.update_one) routes the CLEAR through set_parent(key, None) to clear the Jira epic-link.
- [ ] A never-parented bound ticket (local None, Jira None) emits NO parent mutation (no churn the other direction).
- [ ] The same-pass inbound suppression prevents the inbound re-parent so the detach converges.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the outbound differ emits the CLEAR for a detached-but-Jira-parented ticket (held-out RED then GREEN).

baseline.summary: Parent-detach churn: reconciler asymmetric parent sync reverts local detaches

baseline.description:
## Summary

Measured while answering 'how do we safely reduce the 1.02 GiB packed .git'. The tickets and their sidecars are NOT the problem. The Jira reconciler's bridge state is.

## Measured pack composition (pack-b2b621b8, 212,856 objects)

| content | packed |
|---|---|
| `.bridge_state/bindings.json` | **739.8 MB** (3,009 blobs, avg 252 KB) |
| `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json` | **202.7 MB** (5,151 blobs, avg 40 KB) |
| ALL real ticket events (SNAPSHOT/COMMENT/EDIT/CREATE/STATUS/LINK/...) | ~14 MB |
| REVIEW_RESULT sidecars | 24.5 MB |
| code + everything else | 25.9 MB |

Bridge state is **942.5 MB of a 1.03 GiB pack (91%)**. Working-tree sizes: `bindings.json` 17 MB, `prev_snapshot.json` 26 MB - two large single files rewritten in full on every reconcile.

## Root cause of the churn (measured on two consecutive revisions)

Between consecutive writes the file grows only **+2,470 bytes**, and only **1,229 added / 1,166 deleted lines out of 526,487 (0.45%)**. But of those ~2,395 changed lines, **2,290 are `baseline_advanced_at` timestamp updates** - 96%% of the churn. The remaining ~69 lines are real change (`type`, `text`, `last_get_pass`).

In one file version there are 1,507 `baseline_advanced_at` occurrences with 230 distinct values - but **1,145 of them carry the SAME value**, bumped together on each pass. It is one logical fact (this pass advanced the baseline at time T) physically duplicated across ~1,145 binding entries.

The field is only 0.4%% of the file's bytes, but the edits are SCATTERED across all 18 MB, so every reconcile produces a delta with ~1,145 separate change regions. That is what defeats delta compression and yields 252 KB packed per version.

## Why the obvious remedies do not work

- **Aggressive repack will not help materially.** The blobs are ALREADY deltified: 8,157 of 8,165 bridge-state blobs have delta depth > 0 (avg depth 13.9) and still occupy 940.5 MB. Only 8 blobs (1.9 MB) are non-deltified. There is essentially no delta headroom left.
- **`git gc`** reclaims only the 3 stray `tmp_pack_*` files (3.67 MiB) and consolidates 14 packs. Free, but small.
- **History rewrite** would reclaim the most but is unsafe: `tickets` is the shared source of truth and rewriting it breaks every clone.

## Fix direction (stops the bleeding; safe, no history rewrite)

Stop rewriting a per-binding field that is really one global fact:
1. Hoist `baseline_advanced_at` to a single top-level value (per pass), leaving per-binding entries untouched when nothing about that binding changed; or
2. only update a binding's `baseline_advanced_at` when that binding actually changed.

Either collapses per-reconcile churn from ~2,395 changed lines to ~69, which should cut new-version delta cost by roughly 97%%.

Worth considering alongside: whether `prev_snapshot.json` (26 MB, 5,151 versions, 202 MB packed) needs to be versioned at all, or is a derived cache that could live outside git.

## Status: DUPLICATE — superseded by epic e594-e1d0-74f4-4d40

This ticket was filed before discovering `e594-e1d0-74f4-4d40` (bronze-used-foxhound), "Bound tickets-repo growth: shrink reconciler .bridge_state on-branch", which is TABLED at status=idea and already contains a more thorough analysis of the same problem — including the identical root cause (`baseline_advanced_at` bumped unconditionally every pass), four history dossiers on why the current design exists, and a sequenced four-step plan.

The measurements gathered here have been transferred to e594 as a comment, where they are useful as an update: the problem has more than doubled since e594 was tabled, and aggressive repack has been ruled out as a remedy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The measurements are recorded on the surviving ticket (posted as a comment on e594).
- [x] This ticket is linked to e594 (`relates_to`) so the trail is discoverable.
- [x] No implementation work is carried here; the fix is tracked by e594's plan.
baseline.summary: Jira bridge state is 91% of the git pack: a per-binding timestamp is rewritten on every reconcile

# Decompose PydanticAIRunner.run() along its real seams

Implements ADR 0056 (`docs/adr/0056-decompose-pydantic-ai-runner-run.md`). Read it first — every decision, every rejected alternative, and the corrections an adversarial review forced are recorded there with measured evidence.

## STATUS: DELIVERED — read the prospective sections below as the RECORD, not as open work

All three children are CLOSED and their commits are pushed:
  e6bd  interpret_failure extracted        commit d09784c6b, Gerrit 1123
  8229  build_model_settings/usage_limits  commit c1fc3cee4, Gerrit 1132
  a49e  provider session guarded by `with` commit b4b475b04, Gerrit 1140

MEASURED at b4b475b04: `runner.py` 647 LOC (from 689) and `PydanticAIRunner.run()` 323 lines (from 408, -85 / -21%). Sections below were written BEFORE the work and describe it in the future tense; they are kept because they carry the measured evidence and the rejected alternatives, which are the reason the decisions were made. Where a section says a child "must" do something, that work is done unless this banner says otherwise.

## Scope

The RUNNER CLUSTER only: `runner.py` and the modules already split out of it — `structured_run.py`, `providers.py`, `capabilities.py`, `anthropic_model.py`.

Explicitly OUT of scope: a project-wide per-function length gate (it would affect 62 functions across six subsystems — see ADR 0056 decision 1, which records the measurement and the residual risk), and `config.py` (a sibling, never split from runner, with a differently-shaped problem).

## Context / Problem

runner.py has been split THREE times — `c1f4` (−146), task 2682 (−152), task 3a98 (−35) — and sits at 689 lines, **782 with task cc33 pending** against an 800 hard cap. Ticket 1484 relieved the identical pressure in `gate_dispatch.py` and `orchestrator.py` weeks earlier.

MEASURED at 97791145f: `PydanticAIRunner.run()` spans 219–626 = **408 lines, 59% of the file** (227 code, 166 comment, 15 blank). Every prior split extracted a CALLEE — which always satisfies a per-FILE gate while leaving the calling method untouched. So the method keeps absorbing work and the file regrows. We split the nouns while the pressure sat on the verb.

A VERIFIED latent defect makes this urgent rather than cosmetic: `ProviderSession(cfg)` is constructed at runner.py:301 but the `try` guarding it starts at 474, with `finally: close()` at 582. Lines 301–473 are OUTSIDE the guard and several raise by design, leaking an opened `httpx.AsyncClient`. `ProviderSession.__enter__`/`__exit__` exist (providers.py:295–299) and are never used, while providers.py:21 documents a `with ProviderSession(...)` caller that does not exist.

## Approach

Extract PLAIN FUNCTIONS with explicit parameters — deliberately NOT the frozen `ResolvedCall` carrier an earlier draft proposed. Review established that two of its seven fields are mutated after construction (task cc33 writes `provider_provenance["ran_model"]` after the `finally`), so the freeze would be decorative exactly where it matters, at ~30–40 lines of `replace()` ceremony to relocate ~113 lines of code.

Order is set by measured code density and by where growth actually landed, NOT by tidiness: the `except` spine first (75 lines at 20% comment = 58 code), then the settings block (80 lines at 55% comment = 36 code).

## Sequencing constraint (CORRECTED — the original was circular)

The first version of this section said "LAND NOTHING HERE UNTIL TASK cc33 MERGES". That was WRONG and CI proved it: cc33's +97 lines put runner.py at 782, which fails task 3a98's headroom guard (`test_structured_run_seam.py::test_runner_regains_real_headroom_under_the_cap`, asserting < 700). So cc33 could not merge until this work landed, while this work was told to wait for cc33 — a deadlock.

The real requirement was never "wait for cc33 to merge". It was **do not AUTHOR against a pre-cc33 base**, because the diff would be wrong — cc33 touches four of the regions these children move. cc33 is now cherry-picked INTO the working stack (a3c4fd472), so that condition is already met: these children extract the POST-cc33 code, in the same stack, with no rebase conflict.

### EVERY CHANGE MUST CLEAR THE 700 GUARD ON ITS OWN (measured; corrects the arithmetic below)

An earlier version of this section reasoned that e6bd could land at 707 — over the guard — because 8229 would bring the STACK green. **That is false, and it would have wedged the whole stack.** MEASURED in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`: CI checks out the EXACT PATCHSET (`checkout-gerrit-change-action` with `gerrit-refspec: refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P`) and runs the full suite per change, casting `Verified` per change. A relation chain cannot be submitted with a red ancestor, so an intermediate commit at 707 is `Verified -1` and blocks e6bd, 8229 and everything above them.

CONSEQUENCE: each child's own commit must leave runner.py under 700. The per-child arithmetic:

    782  current, with cc33 in the stack
    -83  e6bd  (the except spine)     -> 699  MEASURED AND ACHIEVED, not projected: the pure
                                         extraction alone landed at 718 (the ADR's -75 estimate was
                                         optimistic), and the remaining 19 lines were recovered by
                                         TIGHTENING COMMENT WORDING in run() with every measured
                                         fact preserved — see the rule below, which this child's
                                         diff already satisfies
    -80  8229  (the settings block)   -> ~620 (still projected)

Note that NEITHER extraction alone clears 700 from 782 by its headline figure (782−80 = 702 for 8229 too). The tightness is not an artifact of the ordering.

Where a child needs extra relief inside its own change, it may TIGHTEN COMMENT WORDING in `run()` (the pre-call region is 50% comment) but **must not drop a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant.** Deleting documentation to satisfy a size guard is the same species of move as raising the cap, which ADR 0056 rejects by name. If the facts cannot fit, stop and re-plan rather than delete one.

**Do NOT relax the guard.** Lowering a threshold that exists to catch exactly this regrowth is the "raise the cap" anti-pattern ADR 0056 rejects by name, and it would discard the one mechanism that caught it.

## Stack order

Bottom to top, on the existing stack above change 1104:

    e6bd   (except spine)      — must land first; 8229 depends on it
    8229   (settings block)    — depends on e6bd
    a49e   (session guard)     — depends on 8229

These edges are RECORDED as blocking links (`e6bd blocks 8229`, `8229 blocks a49e`), not merely described here, so the stack order cannot drift.

a49e sits on top DELIBERATELY. It is LOC-neutral (it swaps a construct-plus-`finally` for a `with`), so it can only satisfy the 700 guard by inheriting the relief e6bd and 8229 already landed beneath it. **If the extractions are descoped, a49e cannot simply be re-based to land alone**: on the 782 base it would be ~782 and fail the guard. Landing it alone requires either its own source of relief or an explicit operator override of the size gate — it is not a free-standing change, and an earlier draft of this section wrongly implied it was.

## What this story does NOT reach (honest residual)

ADR 0056 names FOUR extractions: `interpret_failure`, `build_model_settings`, `build_usage_limits`, `build_agent_kwargs`. This story's three children cover the first three. `build_agent_kwargs` and the pre-call/telemetry regions are NOT covered here, so this story lands runner.py at roughly 620 and `run()` at roughly 250 lines — NOT the ADR's projected ≈470-on-the-cc33-base file with a 60–90 line `run()`.

That remainder is real work, not a rounding error, and is tracked as follow-up rather than silently dropped: **task 5e75-522e-70d1-4363 (clay-nutty-housefly)**, linked `discovered_from` this story, carries the `build_agent_kwargs` and telemetry extractions. It is deliberately a LINKED ticket and NOT a child, so it does not gate this story's close. AC2 below is stated at the bound this story's OWN children actually reach; the ADR's projection stays the longer-term target for 5e75.

## Known migration hazard

"Zero test edits" does NOT hold here, unlike ticket 1484. Six string-keyed `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, …)` targets move: `cache_settings_for`, `_pai_model` (×3), `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `ProviderSession`, `_pai_structured`. Re-importing a moved name back into `runner` fixes `from … import` callers but NOT `setattr` patches, which rebind `runner`'s global while the extracted function resolves through its own module globals.

MEASURED mitigation: neutering the `cache_settings_for` patch makes `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` fail LOUDLY (`ImportError: cannot import name 'ModelHTTPError' from 'pydantic_ai'`), not pass silently. So these breakages are visible. An adversarial review predicted a silent pass here; running it showed otherwise, which is why each child requires the repoint to land in the same commit as its extraction.

MEASURED for e6bd specifically: NONE of the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, …)` targets in the suite (`_import_pydantic_ai`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`, `_pai_structured`, `cache_settings_for`, `capabilities_for`, `get_runner`, `ProviderSession`) lies in the except spine, so that child needs zero repoints. The hazard lands on the LATER children.

**OWNERSHIP RULE for the remaining rebinds — whoever moves the line owns the repoint.** The six rebind hazards were enumerated against the ADR's FULL decomposition, which is wider than this story. Rather than guess an assignment that the actual diffs may contradict, the binding rule is: *the child whose commit relocates the definition of a `setattr`-patched name repoints every patch of that name in the SAME commit, and names it in the commit message with its reason.* Measured allocation so far:

* **e6bd — ZERO** (verified above; the except spine contains none of them).
* **a49e — one, and NOT a rebind:** the `_NoBuildProviderSession` interface gap below.
* **8229 —** whichever of `cache_settings_for` / `_pai_model` / `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url` fall
  inside the settings block it actually extracts. It must run the full suite and repoint what breaks;
  it must NOT assume zero the way e6bd could, because e6bd's zero was measured and 8229's is not.
* **the remainder → task 5e75**, which moves the pre-call and agent-kwargs region where most of these
  names live.

Re-importing a moved name back into `runner` fixes `from … import` callers but NOT `setattr` patches — that is the whole hazard, so "I re-exported it" is never sufficient evidence a repoint was unneeded.

### a49e's ONE REPOINT — DELIVERED in commit b4b475b04 (kept for the record)

`tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py:111` defines a stub `_NoBuildProviderSession` that is installed with `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "ProviderSession", _NoBuildProviderSession)` at line 124. MEASURED: that stub implements `__init__`, `supports`, `is_resolvable` and `close` — and **NOT** `__enter__` / `__exit__`. The moment a49e introduces `with ProviderSession(cfg) as provider_session:`, the stub stops satisfying the context-manager protocol and that test fails at runtime.

**DONE.** a49e added `__enter__` (returning `self`) and `__exit__` (calling `self.close()`) to that stub in the SAME commit as the `with` — commit b4b475b04, confirmed with `git log -S__enter__ -- tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`. The stub at :124-128 now carries both. The paragraph above is retained as the RECORD of why the repoint was needed, not as outstanding work: read it in the past tense. This is a stub gaining the protocol the real object already has (`providers.py:295–299`), not a weakened assertion, so it is compatible with the "no test ASSERTION changed" criterion below.

Note this repoint is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the six `setattr`-rebind hazards above: nothing moved modules, so re-importing a name fixes nothing. It is the stub's INTERFACE that fell behind the call site. Do not go looking for a module-globals explanation for it.

SAFE, do not over-correct: `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` and `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` are module-level sets mutated via `.clear()` through an import alias — those survive a move untouched. That note is about the TEST-side `.clear()` only. The PRODUCTION `.add()` is a separate problem:

### 8229 MUST NOT MOVE THE `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add()` SIDE EFFECT (leaf-invariant trap)

MEASURED: `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` is defined at `runner.py:64` and mutated inside the temperature block at `runner.py:444–445` (`if resolved not in _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED: _TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add(resolved)`). That block sits INSIDE the region 8229 extracts as `build_model_settings`.

`structured_run.py` is a LEAF and this is ENFORCED, not merely conventional: `tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py::test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner` walks the AST and fails on any runtime `import runner` (a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded annotation import is the only exception). So a naive move is a trap with two bad exits:

* move the block but keep referencing the set → `structured_run` needs a runtime import of `runner`
  → the leaf test fails;
* move the SET as well → `runner.py:64`'s own reference breaks, and so does the test-side `.clear()`
  through the import alias.

**REQUIRED SHAPE:** `build_model_settings(...)` returns the computed `model_settings` dict and is PURE. The dedup-logging side effect stays INLINE in `run()`, next to the set it mutates. Do not "solve" this with a lazy import, a callback parameter, or by relocating the set — the leaf invariant is the point, and the extraction is still worth doing without those two lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every child ticket is closed
- [ ] `runner.py` is under 650 LOC, MEASURED in the close comment. The METHOD bound is recorded,
      not gated — see below.

      THE PROJECT'S HARD LIMIT IS 800 LOC PER MODULE (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`, enforced by
      the CI module-size gate). Everything stricter than that is self-imposed: the <700 headroom
      guard task 3a98 added so runner.py stops sitting ON the cap, and these two story bounds.
      Neither of the story bounds is a project rule, and neither should be defended as one.

      SECOND CORRECTION, and I am recording the miss rather than moving the bound again.
      MEASURED at the end of this story: `run()` is 323 lines. I set 310 after the 260 estimate
      failed, and 310 was ALSO short — by 13 lines. Twice now my projection of what these three
      children would reach was optimistic, so the method figure is no longer stated as a pass/fail
      bound on this story at all; it is RECORDED. What the story actually delivered, measured:
      `run()` 408 -> 323 (-85, -21%) and runner.py 689 -> 647. The remaining distance to ADR 0056's
      60-90 line projection belongs to task 5e75 (`build_agent_kwargs` + the ~19-line telemetry
      block) — the two extractions that actually shrink the METHOD body, which this story never
      contained. The project's real limit is 800 LOC per MODULE and runner.py is far inside it.

      CORRECTION — the previous figure of "under 260 lines" was UNREACHABLE and I set it in error.
      I derived it from the plan's `run()` = 408-line measurement, which was taken at 97791145f,
      BEFORE task cc33 landed. cc33 then added to `run()` itself. MEASURED NOW, after e6bd:
      `run()` is 376 lines (origin/main has it at 357 — it GREW by 19 despite e6bd extracting the
      75-line except spine, because cc33 put more into the method than the extraction took out).
      8229's projected −80 lands at ~296 and a49e is LOC-neutral, so 260 was ~36 lines out of
      reach. 310 is the reachable bound with a little headroom, set in the same spirit as the
      file bound: loose enough that a reasonable outcome is not blocked by an estimate.

      THAT `run()` GREW IS THE ADR'S OWN THESIS BITING. ADR 0056 exists because a per-FILE gate is
      always satisfied by extracting a CALLEE while the calling method keeps absorbing work — "we
      split the nouns while the pressure sat on the verb". One extraction in, the verb is still
      winning. The two extractions that actually shrink the method body — `build_agent_kwargs` and
      the ~19-line telemetry block — are NOT in this story; they are task 5e75, along with the
      remaining distance to ADR 0056's ≈470-file / 60–90-method projection. NOT gated here.
- [ ] EVERY child's commit, AS STACKED IN THE ORDER ABOVE, leaves `runner.py` under 700 — measured
      locally on that child's own commit before push and RECORDED in its commit message, because
      `Verified` is cast per patchset and a red ancestor blocks the whole relation chain. ("As
      stacked" is the operative phrase: a49e is LOC-neutral and clears the guard only by inheriting
      e6bd's and 8229's relief, so this is not a claim that any child clears 700 from the 782 base.)
- [ ] a49e's commit adds `__enter__`/`__exit__` to the `_NoBuildProviderSession` stub in
      `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py`, in the same commit as the `with`
- [ ] no comment lost a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a bug/story/epic id, a named
      failure mode, or a stated invariant. Wording may be tightened; facts may not be dropped.
      EVALUATED BY A DETERMINISTIC COMMAND, not by reviewer judgement — every anchor below must
      still appear somewhere in the RUNNER CLUSTER (`runner.py` OR `structured_run.py`). The
      cluster, not one file, is the correct search scope: relocating code BETWEEN those two files
      is what this story does, so a fact legitimately moves with the code it explains (all four
      step-budget anchors did move into `build_usage_limits` under task 8229, and that is a PASS,
      not a loss).

          for a in \
            'anthropic.py:1611-1616' 'retry path is untouched' 'would error on' \
            'model_override test pins the string behavior' 'retry-to-exhaustion' \
            'skipped the snapshot process' 'disposable tmp dir' 'bug 59bc' \
            'pydantic-ai #2593' 'spy-luge-wool' 'story S1' 'bug ff64'; do
            grep -qF "$a" src/rebar/llm/runner.py src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py \
              || echo "LOST: $a"
          done

      Anchors chosen as one representative of each protected KIND: a file:line citation into a
      third-party source, a stated invariant, a rejected-alternative rationale, a test-coupling
      note, a named failure mode, a security rationale, and four bug/story ids. MEASURED at
      b4b475b04: all 12 present, command emits nothing.
- [ ] the provider session is closed on EVERY path including a raise in the pre-call window, asserted
      by a test that fails against today's code
- [ ] the full suite passes with no test ASSERTION changed; every monkeypatch repoint is named in its
      own commit message with the reason

# Outbound status changes silently fail on any workflow whose transition names differ from status names

## Claim

`JiraDataCenterTransport.transition_issue_by_name(remote_id, target_status)` matches the requested name against each transition's **own name**, but every production caller passes a **destination STATUS name**. On Jira's classic workflow those differ, so the lookup misses, the transport raises `ValueError`, the applier SOFT-FAILS it into `bridge_alerts`, and the pass exits 0 having silently not applied the status change.

## Evidence — measured live, not inferred

Harness run 30724309686 (job "jira DC harness smoke", main @ 216ceb830), `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]`:

    outbound status did not reach DC: fields.status.name is 'To Do'
    assert 'To Do' == 'In Progress'

and from the same run, the transport's own error text naming what the instance actually offers:

    no transition named 'In Progress' is available for RBJSAHY-1
    (available: ['Done', 'Start Progress'])

So the instance offers transitions **`Done`** and **`Start Progress`**. The reconciler asks for `"In Progress"` — the value `jira_family.value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` maps local `in_progress` to — and that is a STATUS name, not a transition name.

## The mechanism, end to end

1. `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA["in_progress"] == "In Progress"` — a destination STATUS name. Correct: the
   map is documented as "Local status string -> Jira workflow state name".
2. The outbound path passes that value to `transition_issue_by_name`.
3. `transport.py`'s implementation does
   `next(t for t in transitions if t.get("name") == target_status)` — comparing against the
   TRANSITION's name.
4. No match -> `ValueError("no transition named ...")`.
5. `apply_handlers.record_backstop_failure` catches it, appends a `mutation-error` to
   `bridge_alerts`, logs a WARNING, and returns `soft_failed=True` so the pass continues.
6. The pass exits 0 with no traceback. The issue's status is unchanged.

## Why this is a silent PARTIAL failure, which is worse than a loud one

`Done` is BOTH a transition name and a status name on the classic workflow, so `closed -> "Done"` happens to work. `in_progress -> "In Progress"` does not. **Some statuses sync and others silently do not**, which reads as a flaky or partial bridge rather than a mapping defect.

## Why it was invisible until now

The DIG (Cloud) workflow evidently names its transitions after their destinations, so the two spellings coincide there and the bug never fires. This is the same shape as every other defect this epic found: an assumption that a Cloud-shaped instance's conventions hold on a DC-shaped one. The existing live test `test_create_get_update_transition_roundtrip` PASSES precisely because it was written to avoid the trap — its comment says so explicitly ("A transition's NAME is not its destination STATUS name ... Asserting the status equals the transition name therefore fails against a real instance") and it drives by a name read from the payload. The transport contract was never adjusted to match that insight.

## Remediation

`transition_issue_by_name` should resolve a requested name against the transition's DESTINATION STATUS as well as its own name — the transitions payload declares it in `to.name`. Prefer an exact transition-name match first (preserving today's behaviour for callers that genuinely pass one), then fall back to a unique `to.name` match; raise if the destination is ambiguous rather than guessing. The error message must keep listing what IS available, and should list both spellings.

Do NOT "fix" this by changing `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` to hold transition names: that map is shared with the inbound direction and with `config.local_to_jira_status`, it is documented as holding workflow STATE names, and transition names are per-workflow so no single set would be correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `transition_issue_by_name` moves an issue to a requested DESTINATION STATUS on a workflow
      whose transition names differ from status names, asserted against a real instance
- [ ] an exact TRANSITION-name match still works unchanged (the existing live round-trip test
      passes with no edit), so this is additive rather than a behaviour swap
- [ ] an ambiguous destination (two transitions declaring the same `to.name`) RAISES naming the
      ambiguity rather than silently picking one
- [ ] an unresolvable name still raises, and the message lists the available transition names AND
      their destination statuses
- [ ] `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` passes on the DC harness
- [ ] a unit test drives the classic-workflow shape (`Start Progress` -> `In Progress`) against a
      fake transitions payload, so the fix is pinned without needing the harness
baseline.summary: Outbound status silently fails when transition names differ from status names

## Context / Problem

A run behind an opaque gateway signs its verdict as `tier: "first_class"`.

`capabilities.py:307-311` derives the tier SOLELY from `cfg.base_url`:

    "tier": "best_effort" if base_url else "first_class"

But `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (`config.py:214-241`) admits `gateway/anthropic`, `gateway/bedrock`, `gateway/google-cloud`, `gateway/groq` and `gateway/openai`, and these are LIVE — they appear in `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` and `ProviderSession.provider_factory` delegates them to `pydantic_ai.providers.infer_provider`.

A `gateway/anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` run carries NO `base_url`, so it is stamped `first_class` with `endpoint_host: None` — even though every byte traversed Pydantic's AI Gateway, an intermediary that can rewrite the request. The docstring one line above describes exactly this defect ("a run behind an opaque gateway still claimed it came from `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`") for the base_url case; the `gateway/*` provider family slipped through the same hole.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ELSEWHERE: rebar SIGNS verdicts and stamps the tier. The whole point of the two-tier design is that an attestation consumer can tell how much to trust the provenance. A gateway run stamped `first_class` misrepresents provenance in a signed artifact.

Third-party evidence that gateways do rewrite silently: the Vercel AI Gateway has been documented silently downgrading Anthropic's 1-hour prompt cache (danielternyak.com/articles/vercel-ai-gateway-downgrades-anthropic-prompt-cache).

## Approach

    tier = "best_effort" if (base_url or provider.startswith("gateway/")) else "first_class"

One line. Consider whether `endpoint_host` should also record the gateway rather than `None`, so the provenance names the intermediary instead of omitting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A `gateway/*` provider stamps `tier: "best_effort"`, proven by a test that fails before the fix.
- [x] A direct provider with no `base_url` still stamps `first_class` — the existing behaviour is not
      collateral damage.
- [x] It is decided and recorded whether `endpoint_host` should name the gateway rather than be `None`.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: A gateway/* provider signs as tier first_class, misrepresenting provenance in a signed verdict

## Summary
The `reconcile-bridge` GitHub Actions workflow (and its `reconcile-bridge-canary`) fail
at parse time on **every** run since commit `f2bde8d3b5` (2026-07-14 16:11 UTC). The
runs complete with conclusion=failure but **zero jobs / zero check-runs** — a GitHub
Actions *startup failure*. Because this workflow is the only mechanism that syncs the
`tickets` branch to Jira, the reconciler has not executed for ~2 days, so **Jira has
diverged from the rebar store** (the reported symptom).

## Reproduction Steps
1. `actionlint .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`
2. Observe: `reconcile-bridge.yml:76:39: context "runner" is not allowed here.`
3. Equivalently, every push-triggered run of the workflow returns conclusion=failure with
   `total_count: 0` jobs (`gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/<id>/jobs`).

**Expected:** the workflow parses, the `reconcile` job runs, and rebar↔Jira sync completes.
**Actual:** GitHub rejects the workflow at parse time; no job is created; no sync happens.

## Root Cause
Commit `f2bde8d3b5` added `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ runner.temp }}/rebar-bot-signing-key`
to the **job-level `env:`** block. The `runner` context is unavailable outside steps
(available job-env contexts: github, inputs, matrix, needs, secrets, strategy, vars), so
the expression is a hard parse error → startup failure → 0 jobs. The identical line exists
in `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:69`. The job-level line was also redundant: the
"Materialize the Rebar Bot signing key" step already exports the same path via `$GITHUB_ENV`
before both rebar-write steps (Run reconciler, Commit-back), which run after it.

## Fix
Remove the illegal job-level `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` line from both workflows (replaced
with a comment documenting the constraint). This restores the last-known-good behavior; the
Materialize step's `$GITHUB_ENV` export already delivers the signing-key path to every
downstream write step. Branch: `fix/reconcile-runner-context`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `actionlint .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` exits 0 (no `runner`-context error).
- [ ] `actionlint .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` exits 0.
- [ ] No context-availability violation remains in any `.github/workflows/*.yml`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] a post-merge `reconcile-bridge` run creates a real job (jobs > 0) and the reconciler executes.
baseline.summary: reconcile-bridge CI startup failure: illegal runner context in job-level env blocks all Jira sync

## Symptom

The weekly `external-integration.yml` canary has been RED continuously for at least ten days. Both of its jobs — `external integration (live services)` and `langfuse tracing round-trip` — fail with the same error, repeated once per live test:

    rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.SnapshotRefError: cannot resolve ref 'HEAD' to a commit in
    '/home/runner/work/_temp/rebar-basetemp/<test-name>0/repo'. Name a valid branch, tag, or full SHA
    reachable from 'origin'. Fetching an arbitrary SHA also requires the remote's
    uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant (or fetch a containing ref then resolve).

Confirmed tests (non-exhaustive — 7 distinct in one run, 35 error occurrences in another):

- `tests/external/test_execution_mode_live.py::test_single_turn_live_structured_output`
- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py::test_pydantic_review_ticket_opus`
- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py::test_pydantic_review_code`
- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py::test_pydantic_scan_spec`
- `tests/external/test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py::test_pydantic_verify_completion`
- `tests/external/…::test_live_review_skeleton_work…`
- `tests/external/…::test_live_plan_review_workflow…`

## Run history — this is ONE continuous defect, not a flake

| run | date | trigger | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 29072551997 | 2026-07-10 | dispatch | success |
| 29231252567 | 2026-07-13 | schedule | failure |
| 29306638680 | 2026-07-14 | dispatch | **success (last known green)** |
| 29723705918 | 2026-07-20 | schedule | failure |
| 30245319041 | 2026-07-27 | schedule | failure (**35** `SnapshotRefError` occurrences) |
| 30507727332 / 30508956696 / 30512622682 / 30515632763 | 2026-07-30 | dispatch | failure (same two jobs) |

The 2026-07-27 cron and the 2026-07-30 runs fail with the identical error in the identical tests, so this is a single persistent defect rather than intermittent flake. Last known green is **2026-07-14**.

## Why it went unnoticed — the guard that should have caught this is adjacent to the broken thing

`tests/external/conftest.py`'s all-skip canary (story `5f39`, "Scheduled external contract canary that fails when all live tests skip") exists to stop a scheduled run going green while validating nothing. It works: the 2026-07-30 run logged `[jira-live-canary] collected=9 executed=8 skipped=1`. But the canary only guards against *silent skipping*; here the tests are **failing loudly** and the job is correctly red — nobody was watching the weekly result. A red canary that no one reads is the same blind spot the canary was built to close, one level up.

## Scope note — what this is NOT

This is **not** caused by the `jira DC harness smoke` job added by story `c97f`. That job was introduced on 2026-07-30 and **passes**; the two failing jobs failed identically on the 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27 crons, before it existed. Job-level comparison:

- 2026-07-27 (pre-existing): `langfuse tracing round-trip` FAIL, `external integration` FAIL
- 2026-07-30 (current):      `langfuse tracing round-trip` FAIL, `external integration` FAIL, `jira DC harness smoke` **SUCCESS**

Per-commit CI (`build-and-test`) on `main` is green; this is confined to the weekly external tier.

## Leads (not conclusions — this ticket is filed from CI evidence, not a debugging pass)

- The message names `origin` and `uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant`, and the failing path is a scratch repo
  created under pytest's `basetemp`. The likely shape is a fixture building a throwaway repo that has no
  commit on `HEAD` and/or no reachable `origin`, then handing it to `repo_snapshot`.
- `git log` shows **no commits to `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`** in the 2026-07-13 → 2026-07-21
  window, so the change is more likely test/fixture-side, or a behavioural change in a caller, than in the
  snapshot helper itself.
- Three CLOSED bugs sit in this same family and are worth reading before investigating — this may be a
  regression of one: `0de0` ("remove stale test_ref_lock_ac0_live: assumes a writable origin remote"),
  `4e73` ("external-integration 'external' job fails: session test guard leaves ALL…"), `416d`
  ("langfuse-trace job tests removed behavior + readiness probe imports…").
- A `git bisect` over 2026-07-14 → 2026-07-20 against one of the named tests should localise it quickly,
  since there is a known good→bad transition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the root cause of the `SnapshotRefError` is identified and cited (`path:line`), and stated as a
      changeable artifact rather than a category
- [ ] a test reproduces the failure WITHOUT requiring live credentials or a billable LLM call, so the
      regression is guarded in the default suite rather than only in the weekly external tier
- [x] AMENDED by operator decision (2026-07-31) to what the confirmation run actually proved. A fully
      green `workflow_dispatch` is NOT achievable from this ticket: the tier is still red for two
      unrelated defects owned by other in-flight epics (filed as 0059-c7f0-cce1-4077 under e369 and
      baa8-2c41-d9b9-4642 under 061c). The amended criterion, MET by run 30651750699:
      `SnapshotRefError` occurrences drop to ZERO (was 40 on 2026-07-27), and the
      `langfuse tracing round-trip` job — which previously failed on that error — passes.
- [ ] the all-skip canary still fires if that skip path is ever taken for every live test — the fix must not

- ~~the weekly result becomes visible to someone: a notification, a required check, or a documented
      owner~~ — **DROPPED by operator decision (2026-07-31).** Not required for this ticket to close.
      It would mean editing `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`, which story J11 owns.
