## Context / Problem
`rebar review-code` runs the same four-pass reviewer the Gerrit bot casts `LLM-Review`
with, so an author can preview code-review findings locally before pushing — the exact
analog of `rebar review-plan` for the plan gate. But the code-review on-ramp never
mentions it: the plan-review author can discover their local self-check, the code-review
author cannot. This closes that discoverability asymmetry so both gates read symmetrically.

## Approach
Surface `rebar review-code` in the same three places plan review's local self-check is
surfaced: the author on-ramp (`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`, printed by `rebar explain
review`), the docs index (`docs/README.md`), and the canonical `AGENTS.md` pointer.
Rejected: adding a new `rebar explain` topic for local code review — the existing `review`
guide is the right home, and a second topic would fragment the on-ramp rather than fix
discoverability.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md  (new "Preview the review locally" section, intro cross-link, loop-diagram preview step)
- docs/README.md               (index entry mentions the local preview)
- AGENTS.md                    (code-review pointer names `rebar review-code`)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` has a "Preview the review locally" section teaching
      `rebar review-code`, incl. the `[agents]` extra and `REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW`
      enabling requirement; verified by
      `grep -q 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md && grep -q '## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] The loop diagram in `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` shows the optional local
      `rebar review-code` preview step; verified by
      `grep -q 'rebar review-code — optional local preview' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] The `docs/README.md` passing-code-review index entry names `rebar review-code`;
      verified by `grep -A2 'passing-code-review.md)\*\*' docs/README.md | grep -q 'rebar review-code'`.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` code-review pointer names `rebar review-code`; verified by
      `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] The intro anchor link resolves to the new section heading (GitHub-generated anchor
      `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push` matches the heading text); verified by
      `grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.

## Criteria correction (2026-07-24)
The criteria above originally named `docs/passing-code-review.md`. Commit c2bfbe217
("package author guides in-package so `rebar explain` works from any directory") later moved
the guide to `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` and left the old path a pointer stub,
which made every grep in this ticket false even though the work was delivered and is intact at
the new path.

This ticket was first closed with `--ref f90850861` (the commit the work landed in). That
verified, but it left the criteria asserting checks that no longer hold — inaccurate state in
the shared ticket store. Per the remedy now documented in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
("When the acceptance criteria no longer match reality", ticket 4636-432a-1871-4d74), the
criteria have been corrected to name the guide's real location and the ticket re-closed against
them. The delivered content is unchanged; only the paths in the criteria moved.
baseline.summary: Make local code review as discoverable as plan review

baseline.description:
## Context
rebar records a rich, durable, event-sourced history — ticket events on the `tickets` branch (compaction renames folded events to committed `.retired` files, so the raw history survives synced), gate sidecars (`REVIEW_RESULT`, `COMPLETION_VERDICT`), the two-file module-size ratchet, and git — but there is no aggregation layer and no way to ask "how is the agent-driven dev loop trending over time?". Several agent-lifecycle signals are blindspots today (env/integration-diagnosis time, "which change caused a bug", replanning/escalation classification), and code-health movement (coverage/complexity/clone) is computed ephemerally in CI and never persisted. This epic delivers a single dynamic date-range `rebar metrics` command surfacing every available metric across three lenses — is the agent loop working, is the codebase decaying, are the gates worth it — plus the minimal passive instrumentation to close the blindspots without any new agent-facing manual command.

**"Tier-C blindspots" (defined):** the three agent-lifecycle signal categories that leave no durable trace in the event store today and so cannot be derived structurally — (a) env/integration-diagnosis intervals (an infra failure starts a diagnosis, its next clean gate ends it), (b) bug provenance ("which prior change/ticket caused this bug"), and (c) bug outcome classification (regression vs plan-defect vs flaky vs …). Each is closed by a passive emission stamped by trustworthy code, never by agent self-report.

## Approach
Derive-structurally over the durable event store (including `.retired` events) for everything with a clean event signature; add the smallest possible passive emission only where a signal genuinely leaves no trace, always stamped by trustworthy code (gate error handlers, git blame) rather than agent self-report — the layered-hybrid design that dev-analytics (DevLake, Swarmia) and agent-observability practice converge on, and that fits rebar's event-sourced substrate. We reuse existing surfaces (gate sidecars, the `transition` command, the link-relation set) rather than introduce a new event type, keeping every change additive and back-compatible (old records stay valid; readers tolerate absence). The command and its structural sources are harness- and target-project-agnostic (a rebar CLI over the portable event store); harness/CI-specific backfills are isolated optional adapters the core command never depends on.

**Blame-derivation is best-effort and non-authoritative.** `caused_by` auto-derivation blames the **pre-fix** state — the parent of the fixing commit (`<fix>~1`) — over the bug's recorded `file_impact`, never the post-fix HEAD (which would attribute the fixing commit itself). When a bug has no `file_impact`, spans multiple files ambiguously, or blame cannot resolve a single commit, auto-derivation is **skipped** (no wrong edge is written); the explicit `--caused-by <id>` override always wins. Auto-derived `caused_by` edges feed only `classified`-confidence provenance metrics and are never treated as authoritative — accuracy is a labeled heuristic, not a guarantee.

**Auto-link vs the closed-source guard (555e ordering).** The auto-link runs *after* `txn.transition_core` commits the STATUS event, so the bug (the link SOURCE) is already `closed` when blame runs; `graph._links.add_dependency` rejects links from a closed source (`_links.py:242-247`). So 555e writes the edge via `graph._links._write_link_event(bug, culprit, "caused_by", ...)` **directly**, bypassing the closed-source and cycle guards — which add nothing for a non-blocking, non-cycle-inducing relation on a closed source. Without this, every auto-derived edge would be silently swallowed and the feature would be a dead letter.

**Snapshot store path.** The going-forward snapshot series (3275) is committed to `.rebar/metrics-snapshots.ndjson` — a **git-tracked** path in the rebar store — NOT under `reports/`, which is gitignored (`.gitignore:74`) and would silently drop every snapshot.

**Back-out / expand-contract for the bug-close CLI change (ed13):** the `--class` enum replaces the required `--reason` on the *bug-close* path only; old STATUS records without `close_class` still reduce cleanly (readers tolerate absence), and back-out is simply ceasing to require/write the field. Because `--class` becomes required on bug close, its error message must enumerate the allowed values so any existing caller that omitted it fails loudly with an actionable message rather than silently.

## Decomposition
Three tracks; each child is a single concern (detail lives in the children):
- Command: metric-registry + unavailable/label contract; event-derivation readers; git-derivation readers; gate-sidecar reader + `ERROR` path; going-forward snapshot writer/reader; the `rebar metrics` CLI.
- Instrumentation: the `caused_by` link relation (additive); the bug close `--class` enum (persisted, replacing the discarded reason); blame-based `caused_by` auto-derivation + `--caused-by` param + bug-template advisory.
- Backfill (one-time, labeled): `caused_by` over existing bugs; historical bug `--class` from structural signals; complexity/clone snapshots at sampled commits; local Claude-Code-transcript mining (optional adapter); GitHub-Actions coverage + CI-health harvest (optional adapter).

**Cross-ticket coordination (shared-file ordering the dep graph does not encode):**
- `ed13` (bug close `--class`) and `555e` (`--caused-by` + blame) both edit `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` and `transition_close.py`; land **ed13 before 555e** and stack 555e on top so the close-guard restructure exists first. Any `555e`/`2f8e` test that closes a bug MUST pass `--class` (it is required after ed13).
- `0b96` (`caused_by` relation) and `9a5a` (metrics command) both touch `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt` and regenerate `tests/golden/cli_help/__overview_help.out`; 0b96 lands first (Layer 0), and 9a5a re-regenerates the golden on top.
- Layer-1 reader children (`18e6`, `3c07`, `7931`) each register into `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py`; land them sequentially up the stack (or via an append-only registration seam) so registry edits do not collide.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets are closed (epic rollup), verified by `rebar list --epic <this> --status open` returning none.
- [ ] `rebar metrics --since 2026-01-01 --until 2026-07-01 --output json` exits 0 and emits JSON where every registered metric key is present with either a value or `{"unavailable":{"reason","accruing_since"}}` — an integration test asserts via `jq -e` that no registered metric key is absent (the capstone 9a5a AC asserts this exact no-missing-key check, not merely a non-empty map).
- [ ] Every metric entry carries `source` and `confidence`, and a `source=backfill_classified` value is never aggregated into an authoritative structural series — a unit test asserts `is_authoritative('backfill_classified')` is False and the segregation holds.
- [ ] Bug-close friction stays flat: the required free-text reason is replaced (not supplemented) by a bounded `--class` enum persisted on the STATUS event, verified by `rebar show <closed-bug> --output json | jq -e '.close_class'`, AND a `rebar transition --help` diff shows no net increase in required bug-close arguments.
- [ ] Backfill is validated: at least one backfilled `caused_by`/`close_class`/snapshot value exists carrying `source=backfill_classified` + `confidence=classified`, asserted by a test over the backfill output.
- [ ] `rebar metrics --since <date> --until <date>` emits a machine-readable artifact spanning agent-process, gate-economics, and code-health metrics, with real date-range trends for every metric that has a complete history.
- [ ] The command is built once against a complete metric registry: metrics whose signals have not yet accrued report a structured `unavailable` state and light up automatically as data arrives, with no future code change.
- [ ] Tier-C blindspots (defined above) are captured passively: env/integration-diagnosis via an `ERROR` outcome on the existing gate sidecars; bug provenance via a new `caused_by` link relation (best-effort auto-derived from blame, plus an explicit override param); bug classification via a persisted close `--class` enum replacing today's validated-then-discarded free-text reason.
- [ ] **Bug-close friction stays flat (operationalized):** `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed` requires exactly one bug-specific argument both before and after this epic — today a REQUIRED free-text `--reason`, afterward a REQUIRED bounded `--class` enum. The required-argument count for a bug close does not increase from 1 to 2; verified by diffing `rebar transition --help` against the pre-epic baseline (the change swaps one required arg for another, adds none). No non-bug transition gains a new required argument.
- [ ] Historical data is backfilled wherever a durable source exists; **every** backfilled/classified value is labeled `source=backfill_classified` and `confidence=classified` (the single backfill vocabulary — there is no `backfill_structural`), and `is_authoritative()` returns False for it so it is never aggregated into an authoritative structural series.
baseline.summary: Passive metrics + agent-lifecycle instrumentation (rebar metrics command)

## Why
Rec 1 + Rec 9 of session-logs/2026-06-09-architecture-review.md (risks R3/R4/R5/R8/R9). 14.9k LOC of bash with ~140 embedded python3 heredocs (27 in ticket-lib-api.sh, 20 in ticket-lib.sh) is the dominant maintenance liability for agent-driven development. The hard-won lessons live in the I1-I9 doctrine, the already-Python critical sections (ticket_txn.py, reducer, graph), and the 1,400+ test corpus — not in the bash itself. The regression-safe playbook is already proven in-repo: REBAR_NATIVE_READS (commits 7d53bc5 -> a93885e): port behind a kill-switch, pin parity, soak, remove the switch.

## What
Tiered strangler-fig port; each tier spawns its own child tickets when started; the relevant bash suite is the per-command characterization gate, run against BOTH impls until byte-identical before any default flips:
- Tier A: read shims (show/list/ready/search/deps) -> dispatcher calls _reads.py (story rich-glare-sake).
- Tier B: leaf writes (comment, tag/untag, set-file-impact, set-verify-commands, archive, scratch) -> rebar._commands; may temporarily shell to the bash write core.
- Tier C: compute-heavy bash (ticket-next-batch.sh 944 LOC, validate-issues.sh 945, ticket-list-epics.sh 449).
- Tier D: the write/sync core (_flock_stage_commit, _push_tickets_branch, _reconverge_tickets) LAST, behind REBAR_WRITE_CORE=bash|python, soaked one full release on this repo's own store.
- Tier E: delete the dispatcher; cli.py becomes a real argparse CLI over the same _commands functions as the library. Unpacked-disk constraint, jq prerequisite, and flock fallback all retire here.
Test consolidation rides along (Rec 9): each ported command's bash suite is translated to pytest and retired only after the default flips and soaks; parity tests are deleted as each duplication collapses.

## Scope
The full bash engine over multiple releases; one tier (and within tiers, one command) at a time. NOT in scope: any change to the store/locking design (ratified sound) or the event schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tier ordering + kill-switch discipline documented in docs/architecture.md and followed (default stays bash until parity green + dogfood soak)
- [ ] Each port ticket carries its bash suite as the characterization gate (byte-identical before flip)
- [ ] End state: one implementation + three facades; zero standalone shell test harness; no embedded heredocs
baseline.summary: Bash-to-Python strangler-fig migration (Tiers A-E, kill-switch per tier)

content.text: ## Why
A kernel is only reusable if a SECOND gate can plug in without copying, and only honest if reuse
is enforced by mechanisms that don't make the workflow system brittle. This story defines the
consumer SEAM (what a gate plugs in) and the ENFORCEMENT strategy — deliberately enforcing
STRUCTURE mechanically and BEHAVIOR via evals, and explicitly REJECTING a prompt-text lint
(an anti-pattern: mature projects — DSPy, Guardrails, Instructor, promptfoo — enforce typed
contracts + output/behavior, never prompt-string greps). This is the contract `b744` (code
review) builds on.
## What
- **Consumer seam (doc + API):** a kernel doc enumerating the per-gate plug-points — criteria +
routing, finder prompts, the domain-context assembler, the verify-prompt preamble, and the
move-catalog — and the kernel's public Pass-2/3/4 entry points. Plan-review is the worked
reference; `b744` is the named second consumer (this epic `blocks` b744).
- **Soft-rule discoverability:** a canonical verifier-rules SCAFFOLD/snippet (atomicity;
independence — don't show the finding's own conclusion; allow "insufficient";
verdict-with-citation-NOT-fix) that a gate's verify-prompt preamble embeds.
- **Behavioral enforcement (NOT a lint):** an eval that asserts the rules are OBEYED — a
deterministic FakeRunner assertion suite on the gate path (runs in CI) + a small GATED live
eval kept OFF the blocking CI path (multi-run, lenient threshold). Reuse the existing contract/
derived-prompt-index drift gate for vocabulary drift. Add NO prompt-marker lint.
- Record the enforcement rationale (structure-mechanical, behavior-via-evals, no text-lint) in the
doc so consumers don't reach for the rejected mechanism.
## Scope
In scope: the kernel consumer-seam doc + the rules scaffold + the behavioral-eval enforcement
(offline + gated-live) + reusing the contract-drift gate. Out of scope: the pass extractions
themselves (WS1/WS2/WS3, on which this depends), building b744's code-review gate, and any
prompt-marker lint (explicitly rejected). Touches the kernel module's public surface, docs
(a new kernel doc + `reuse-surface.md`), and the eval seam (Inspect-AI / FakeRunner suites).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A kernel doc enumerates the consumer seam (criteria, finder prompts, domain-context
assembler, verify preamble, move-catalog) + the public Pass-2/3/4 entry points, with
plan-review as the worked reference; the epic `blocks` b744.
- [ ] A canonical verifier-rules scaffold records the soft rules (atomicity, independence,
allow-insufficient, verdict-with-citation-not-fix) for a gate's verify preamble to embed.
- [ ] A BEHAVIORAL eval verifies the rules are obeyed: a deterministic FakeRunner suite on the
gate path runs in CI; a small live eval is GATED and kept off the blocking path (multi-run,
lenient threshold).
- [ ] Vocabulary/contract drift is caught by the existing contract / derived-prompt-index drift
gate; NO prompt-marker (text-grep) lint is added, and the rationale is recorded.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS4: Kernel consumer seam + behavior-based enforcement (evals, no prompt-text lint) + docs

## Why
The engine must execute workflows deterministically and survive crashes/concurrency on an
event-sourced, auto-pushing store, identically across library/CLI/MCP.

## What
- Thin linear executor (graphlib.static_order) running scripted + agent steps.
- Persist run-state as new WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP event types (per-key LWW map), read back
  via replay for the async status tools.
- Idempotency: WORKFLOW_STEP marker committed AFTER the effect; forward-only recovery;
  (run_id, step_id) handed to downstream APIs as their idempotency token.
- Async over MCP: run_workflow returns a run_id; add get_workflow_status / get_workflow_result.

## Scope
- In: executor, run-state events, idempotency, async MCP entrypoints, TTL orphan-tmpdir sweep.
- Out: agent-step internals + snapshot creation/teardown (WS-D); scripted steps (WS-E).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Linear executor; Burr-tripwire CI test scoped to executor.py ONLY (not the package) asserting none of asyncio/concurrent.futures/threading/multiprocessing/retry-libs is imported; carries the written Burr-adoption trigger list; executor state pre-shaped toward an immutable Burr-style State.
- [ ] WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP event types wired (KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES, EVENT_TYPES, per-key LWW processor, compaction preserve, replay read-back).
- [ ] Globally-unique run_id; marker-after-effect idempotency; forward-only recovery.
- [ ] now()/uuid4()/random()/live reads captured once and persisted in the WORKFLOW_STEP record for deterministic replay.
- [ ] WS-C owns the TTL orphan-tmpdir sweep (snapshot create + finally-teardown belong to WS-D).

baseline.description:
## Why

The reusable 4-pass review pipeline needs criteria conditionally INCLUDED based on the input (a
security criterion fires only on security triggers; intent-fidelity only when a session log is
linked; container criteria only for parents with children). INVESTIGATION FINDING (analyst, with
citations): the engine ALREADY has this mechanism — the per-step `if:` skip-guard (interpreter.py
`_guard_scoped`, v1, retained in v2). It does per-step conditional inclusion, evaluated over
run-start-journaled inputs + recorded prior outputs (frame scope), is replay-deterministic (no live
store access; a skipped step records a durable `skipped` WORKFLOW_STEP event), and fails closed.
So we must NOT add a redundant `when`/`enabled` field — `if:` IS the overlay mechanism.

## What (the real, narrow gap)

The closed expression grammar (`_ALLOWED_EXPR` in lint_refs.py; pinned by the v2 schema `expression`
) is a bare variable-reference language: NO operators, comparisons, functions, or regex — only
truthiness over `inputs.*` / `steps.*.outputs.*` / `loop.*` / `map.*`. So `if:` can branch on a
boolean already in scope but cannot COMPUTE one. The overlay triggers (has-children,
has-linked-session-log, security-keyword-in-plan) are computations. The clean design — keeping the
grammar deliberately tiny — is a DETERMINISTIC scripted pre-step that computes each trigger boolean
and emits it as an output; the criterion steps then carry `if: ${{ steps.triggers.outputs.<name> }}`.
This is the in-pattern shape (steps.py fetch_ticket/fetch_epic_graph). Plus, optionally, journal the
resolved INCLUDED-SET at run-start so coverage accounting reads one stable set (today inclusion is
implicit, inferable from per-step skip statuses).

## Scope

- A deterministic overlay-trigger precompute scripted-step (src/rebar/llm/workflow/steps.py) that
  turns overlay conditions (has-children, has-linked-session-log, keyword/trigger match over a text
  input) into boolean outputs an `if:` references. The expression grammar is UNCHANGED.
- Optionally: journal the resolved included-set into the run-start WORKFLOW_RUN event
  (executor.py run_started) so coverage reads a stable set; OR document that inclusion is recovered
  from per-step skip statuses if that is sufficient.
- Document `if:` as the overlay/criterion-inclusion mechanism (the precompute-then-guard pattern),
  and a test proving an input-determined criterion is included/excluded + a replay test that a
  mid-run store edit does not change inclusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic precompute scripted-step computes overlay-trigger booleans (has-children,
      has-linked-session-log, text/keyword trigger match) as step outputs; the expression grammar is
      NOT extended (closed-allow-list preserved).
- [ ] A criterion (prompt) step gated by `if: ${{ steps.<triggers>.outputs.<name> }}` is INCLUDED
      when the trigger is truthy and SKIPPED (durable `skipped` event) when falsy — covered by a test.
- [ ] REPLAY test: after resolution, mutating the underlying store does NOT change the
      included/skipped outcome (inputs/outputs are read from the run-start journal, not live state).
- [ ] The resolved included-set is observable for coverage — either journaled into the run-start
      WORKFLOW_RUN event, or documented as recovered from per-step skip statuses (decide + record which).
- [ ] The overlay/criterion-inclusion mechanism (precompute-then-`if:`) is documented; make lint +
      the workflow test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Overlay construct: a declarative when/enabled predicate on prompt steps (resolved set journaled at run-start)

content.text: ## Why
Attestation manifests must carry the rebar gate-code version+SHA for audit
provenance (epic jira-reb-596). This story adds the value where it is signed and
the parser to read it back — the core of the feature, with no build or display
surface yet.
## What
- Add a gate-code SHA/version resolver in `src/rebar/signing.py` (co-located with
and reusing the `head_sha()` idiom, line 337 — a `git -C … rev-parse` subprocess;
do NOT invent a new git wrapper). It returns `"<version> (<short-sha>[-dirty])"`,
or just `"<version>"` when no SHA is resolvable:
- Version: `rebar.__version__`.
- SHA: `git -C <dir of rebar.__file__> rev-parse --short HEAD` — the **rebar
source (gate code)** dir, NOT the target repo. Resolution is **live-git-first,
omit-last** (build-baked fallback = story 2).
- `-dirty` rule: append `-dirty` iff `git -C <dir of rebar.__file__> status
--porcelain` is non-empty (any staged / modified-tracked / untracked change in
the rebar source tree).
- Any git failure -> omit the SHA (version only) and emit a debug log
(silent-failure guard).
- Append one `rebar-version:` line to BOTH manifests:
- `build_manifest` — `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (plan-review).
- `_verdict_manifest` — `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:282`
(completion-verifier).
- Add `manifest_rebar_version(manifest)` in `attest.py` (mirroring
`manifest_regver`) returning the stamp, or `None` for pre-stamp manifests.
- `compute_validity` stays untouched and must never read the stamp.
## Scope
Signing + parsing only. Build-time baking = story 2; `show`/`verify_signature`
surfacing = story 3.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `build_manifest` and `_verdict_manifest` each emit exactly one `rebar-version:` line in their output.
- [ ] The resolver returns the live-git short SHA with a `-dirty` suffix when the rebar source checkout is dirty.
- [ ] The resolver returns a version-only string (SHA omitted) and emits a debug log when git is unavailable / the install is non-git.
- [ ] `manifest_rebar_version()` returns the stamp for a stamped manifest and `None` for a pre-stamp manifest.
- [ ] `compute_validity` output is byte-for-byte unchanged, and a pre-stamp manifest still validates (proven by a passing test).
- [ ] Existing tests asserting on `build_manifest` / `_verdict_manifest` output pass after being updated for the new line.
- [ ] All of the following unit tests exist and pass: both-manifests-carry-line, live-checkout-dirty-resolution, git-absent-omit, parser-round-trip, pre-stamp-None.

baseline.summary: Stamp gate-code version+SHA into attestation manifests + parser

content.text: # WS3 — Escalation scripted ops + the code-review workflow
## Why

This is the heart of the gate: wire WS1's base + WS2's overlays into the two-round overlay-escalation topology and feed all findings into the shipped kernel Pass-2/3/4. The mechanism was DERISKED on the real v3 engine (offline) — the agent's `recommend_overlays` drove a second batch's membership, bogus ids dropped, the cap bounded fan-out, one-hop held — so this is implementation of a proven design, with NO core-engine change.
## What

- Two deterministic scripted ops: `overlay_union` (compute (glob U base.recommend) - already-run, ONE-HOP, capped at N=3 configurable; emit per-overlay `include_<overlay>` flags + `to_run`) and `merge_findings` (concatenate base + Round-A + Round-B finding lists).

- The thin `gates/code-review.yaml`: assemble_diff -> triggers (overlay_triggers) -> base (agent) -> round_a (batch, when:=triggers) -> union -> round_b (batch, when:=union) -> merge -> verify (Pass-2) -> decide (Pass-3) -> coach_gate/coach (Pass-4).
## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` (or register in `workflow/steps.py`) — `overlay_union`, `merge_findings`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the gate workflow.
- OUT OF SCOPE: the `gate_dispatch` entry + source-separation (WS4); the secrets/security auto-block detectors (WS5).
## Specifics pinned (plan-review remediation 2026-06)

- **Escalation cannot affect the verdict (explicit invariant):** the offline test asserts that flipping `recommend_overlays` changes only WHICH advisory overlays run (Round-B membership), never the Pass-3 decision for an identical finding set — escalation lives on the recall/selection side; the precision/decision side is deterministic.

- **`overlay_union` config:** the cap N (default 3) is read from `gates/code-review.yaml`, not hard-coded; `merge_findings` preserves per-finding provenance (which reviewer/round emitted it) so Pass-2 can re-ground each.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `overlay_union` computes (glob U recommend) - already-run, ONE-HOP, capped at N=3 (configurable), enum-constrained; `merge_findings` concatenates the three finding sources.

- [ ] `gates/code-review.yaml` validates (`rebar workflow validate`) and runs on the v3 engine; Round-A overlays are glob-triggered, Round-B membership = the escalated union, all findings flow into kernel Pass-2/3/4.

- [ ] An OFFLINE (FakeRunner) test asserts: Round-B membership == the escalated set; the cap bounds fan-out; one-hop holds (overlays do not re-escalate); escalation can never change the deterministic verdict.
- [ ] The gate calls the kernel `verify_findings` / `pass3_over_findings` / `coach` directly (no forked passes).
## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)

- `merge_findings` CLUSTERS near-duplicate findings (reuse `aggregate.py` clustering by file-anchor + dimension + line-proximity) BEFORE Pass-2, so N+1 overlays reviewing the same location don't quadratically inflate the verifier token budget.
- `overlay_union` receives `already_run` EXPLICITLY via its `with:` block, sourced from the Round-A triggers step output — not reconstructed from internal state.
- `gates/code-review.yaml` operator-facing config (thresholds, cap N, escalation shape) gets a DOCUMENTED schema (fields/types/defaults/valid ranges).
- An ADR documents the base→overlay one-hop ESCALATION design (union op, cap rationale, recall-only/never-verdict-side) — not only the single-pass retirement ADR.
Added ACs:
- [ ] `merge_findings` dedups/clusters near-duplicate findings (file-anchor+dimension+line-proximity) before Pass-2; test asserts N overlays on one location collapse
- [ ] `overlay_union` reads `already_run` from an explicit `with:` input wired to the Round-A triggers output; test asserts the wiring
- [ ] `gates/code-review.yaml` config schema documented (fields/types/defaults/ranges)
- [ ] ADR records the one-hop base→overlay escalation design (union/cap/recall-only)

baseline.summary: WS3: overlay_union + merge_findings scripted ops + gates/code-review.yaml (two-round -> kernel Pass-2/3/4)

content.text: ## Why

The SDET review (8125) found that the reconciler reducer fork/union tie-break does NOT resolve by event UUID as documented. CLAUDE.md / the reducer docstring state the STATUS fork is "resolved deterministically by UUID". Empirically (test_concurrency_regression fork test), for the concurrent-transition case both competing STATUS siblings carry an empty parent_status_uuid, so the second-applied event forks against an empty existing_uuid and wins UNCONDITIONALLY — i.e. the winner is the later-in-replay-order event (filename = timestamp-then-uuid order), NOT the UUID-determined one. Clones still CONVERGE (identical union replayed in identical filename order -> same winner), so the cross-clone agreement guarantee holds; but the documented MECHANISM ("by UUID") is inaccurate.
## Impact

Not a convergence/correctness break (clones agree). It is a doctrine-vs-implementation discrepancy: anyone relying on "lower/higher UUID wins" would be wrong, and the tie-break is timestamp-order-sensitive. test_concurrency_regression now pins the ACTUAL behavior (max by filename) and documents the divergence inline.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide intended semantics: either (a) make the reducer tie-break the STATUS fork by event UUID (so the doc is true), or (b) correct the docs/CLAUDE.md to describe the actual filename/replay-order tie-break (and confirm convergence is still guaranteed for clones whose pre-union event orderings differ)
- [ ] Reconcile the reducer code, its docstring, and CLAUDE.md to ONE accurate description
- [ ] test_concurrency_regression asserts the (then-correct) documented winner; fails if the rule changes

baseline.summary: Reducer fork tie-break is filename/replay-order, not UUID as documented

# Feature-branch accumulation: multi-story features assemble off-main under per-story LLM+CI gates and land via a reviewed merge change

## Context
Validation (session log apt-otter-urn, 2026-07-01) proved the current chain/topic flow cannot satisfy the five core requirements for multi-agent feature work: (R1) never review a huge diff in one review; (R2) accumulate a whole feature off-main and land it at once; (R3) every change reaching main passed LLM review; (R4) no invalidation fragility from content comparison or merge/rebase instability; (R5) the pattern must be validated by popular, actively-maintained OSS projects. Chains fail R4 (any rebase wipes votes under copyCondition=NO_CODE_CHANGE; the alternative TRIVIAL_REBASE carry IS content comparison). The adopted pattern is the OpenDev-documented **server-side feature branch + reviewed merge change**: stories are small changes reviewed INTO refs/heads/feature/<name> as they pass (attestations are consumed immediately into branch history — no vote ever needs to survive a rebase; branch history is the durable accumulator), then one --no-ff merge commit of the branch into main is pushed to refs/for/main as its own reviewed change, gated identically, and submitted atomically. Feature branches live only in Gerrit (replication pushes main+tags), so nothing reaches GitHub until the merge change lands.

**ASSUMES epic 1fa8 (smoky-flare-slug) is completed and merged**: the `Verified` label exists, cast by GitHub Actions via gerrit-to-platform hooks (patchset-created / comment-added `recheck`), the `gerrit-verify.yaml` workflow exists, and the two-vote submit requirement `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND label:Verified=MAX AND -has:unresolved` is active. (References to g2p config and `gerrit-verify.yaml` below are to those 1fa8 deliverables; they intentionally do not exist yet.)

### Decision log (2026-07-01 validation + web research; citations in apt-otter-urn)
- **OSS validation (R5):** OpenDev Infra Manual documents this flow verbatim (server-side branch, pushMerge ACL, `git merge --no-ff` pushed to refs/for/master); live use: openstack/swift feature/mpu + feature/threaded through 2026 with story-sized reviewed changes + reviewed catch-up merges; Qt runs reviewed merge changes live (qt-creator, June 2026). Caveat adopted as policy: keep feature branches SHORT-LIVED (OpenDev: "specifically not for sustained long term development"; Qt retreated from routine long-lived-branch merges in 2020).
- **Merge-change review base = Gerrit auto-merge** (conflict resolutions + manual edits only — usually near-empty), NOT the whole feature diff (R1). REST: `files/` with no `parent` param and per-file `diff` default to the auto-merge base for merge commits (rest-api-changes.html#list-files: "If not specified, the response contains a map of the files different in the auto merge result"); `mergelist` lists integrated commits. **This default is the riskiest assumption in the plan — S2 verifies it against the running Gerrit 3.14.1 with a captured fixture BEFORE building on it.** **TRAP:** bare `GET .../revisions/{rev}/patch` on a merge commit returns HTTP 409 ("Revision has more than 1 parent", GetPatch.java) — today our voter would fail-closed -1 on any merge change (safe, but blocks the pattern); `patch?parent=1` silently yields the ENTIRE feature diff (violates R1). The bot needs a distinct merge-change path.
- **UI default diff base for merge commits is FIRST_PARENT** (whole feature) — fine for humans; never design assuming reviewers land on the conflicts-only view.
- **LLM-Review copyCondition gains `changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE`** — Gerrit-native, purpose-built ("useful if you don't want to trigger CI or human verification again if your target branch moved forward", config-labels.html). A re-merge because main advanced keeps the +1; a changed feature tip is a REWORK and correctly re-reviews. Not a content-comparison heuristic (R4). S1 proves the config push is accepted by the running 3.14.1; the carry behavior itself is proven live in S5 scenario 4.
- **Verified deliberately does NOT carry on re-merge** (stays NO_CODE_CHANGE only): CI re-runs on the new combined tree via patchset-created. This is the semantic-conflict mitigation — a textually-clean merge shows an EMPTY auto-merge diff even when semantically broken (Chromium's standing objection to merges), so the LLM cannot catch it; CI must. Deliberate label divergence mirroring roles: LLM reviews content (unchanged on a clean re-merge), CI validates the tree (changed).
- **Submit type pinned explicitly**: `[submit] action = merge if necessary` + `mergeContent = true` (currently unset/inherited — an unpinned gap flagged in validation; FF-only or cherry-pick/rebase-always on main would defeat the atomic-merge design). S1 records the CURRENT effective inherited value before pinning and applies the pin in a quiet window (no open changes targeting main), with its own back-out note (S6).
- `receive.rejectImplicitMerges` is unaffected — it explicitly exempts real merge commits (config-project-config.html).

## Locked design
- **Branch namespace** `refs/heads/feature/<name>`, created/deleted server-side (UI/REST); `Create Reference` + `Delete Reference` on `refs/heads/feature/*` AND `Push Merge Commit` on `refs/for/refs/heads/main` + `refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*` all granted to ONE named narrow group (`feature-branch-drivers`), membership policy recorded in the ADR (label gates remain the enforcement point; the ACL bounds attack surface + review-cost amplification). Branch deletion after merge-back is a scripted/manual step (Gerrit has no auto-cleanup).
- **Story loop:** small changes target `refs/for/refs/heads/feature/<name>`; the review-bot webhook is branch-agnostic per config (webhooks.config has no branch filter; proven live by S5 scenario 1) and the submit requirements have no branch clause; g2p dispatch for `feature/*` refs is EXPECTED branch-agnostic and is VERIFIED in S3 (its done-definition) before the design relies on it — so BOTH votes gate every feature-branch change (R3); submit into the branch as each passes. Parallel agents in separate worktrees both target the branch; MERGE_IF_NECESSARY merges siblings without any manual rebase (R4).
- **Catch-up merges** main→feature as reviewed merge changes on the branch (OpenDev recipe), on a documented cadence; branch-lifetime cap.
- **Merge-back:** in the merge worktree, FIRST install the Gerrit commit-msg hook (`curl -sLo .git/hooks/commit-msg https://<gerrit-host>/tools/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg` — a fresh worktree/clone does not have it, and without it the amend adds no Change-Id and the push is rejected); then `--no-ff` merge commit, Change-Id stamped via `GIT_EDITOR=/bin/true git commit --amend`, pushed to refs/for/main under pushMerge; bot reviews vs auto-merge + mergelist; CI builds/tests the merge tree; both labels gate; submit lands the feature atomically; replication advances GitHub main; branch deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **S1 — Gate + ACL config** (`infra/gerrit/project.config`, `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`, declarative): LLM-Review `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE` (push accepted by the running 3.14.1); Verified copyCondition UNCHANGED (re-run posture) with the rationale recorded; record the current effective inherited submit type (Gerrit REST/ssh query, noted on the ticket) THEN pin `[submit] action = merge if necessary` + `mergeContent = true` in a quiet window; ACLs: `Create Reference`/`Delete Reference` on `refs/heads/feature/*` + `Push Merge Commit` on `refs/for/refs/heads/main` and `refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*`, ALL bound to the named `feature-branch-drivers` group — including extending `setup-project.sh`'s managed-groups `want` dict (~line 57, currently only Administrators + Service Users) so the group is created/resolved declaratively; ADR amending ADR-0013 (+ 1fa8's Verified ADR) recording the merge-change gate, label-divergence rationale, and the group membership policy; `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` gate/ACL sections updated. Verified live on the running Gerrit.
- [ ] **S2 — Review-bot merge-change path.** FIRST (riskiest assumption): capture a live fixture from the running Gerrit 3.14.1 proving `files/` with no `parent` returns the auto-merge-base file map for a merge commit (record the fixture in tests + cite rest-api-changes.html#list-files); only then build on it. Explicit edit targets: `voter.py` — merge detection via `revisions/{rev}/commit` parent count (>=2) runs INSIDE `review_and_vote` immediately after the existing-vote check and BEFORE any diff fetch, so the merge path is taken identically for webhook, reconciler-backfill, and `/rerun` triggers (reconcile.py itself is expected to need NO change — asserted by a test routing a merge-change event through the backfill path; the one extra `commit` GET per review is an accepted overhead — negligible next to the LLM call, and an error on it fails closed); `gerrit_client.py` — new `get_commit`, `get_merge_files` (no parent), `get_file_diff` (auto-merge base), `get_mergelist` methods; NEVER bare `/patch` on merges (a unit test asserts the 409 path stays fail-closed if ever hit); ANY merge-path REST failure (commit / files / diff / mergelist) → fail-closed -1 carrying the existing coverage-gap (infra) message tag, mirroring the current posture. Merge-context contract: a new `assemble_merge_change_context(auto_merge_diff, mergelist)` co-located with `DiffContext` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py` (reusing `DIFF_CHAR_CAP`; mergelist section capped by a named constant `MERGELIST_MAX_COMMITS = 100` with truncation notice), producing a documented format: `## Merge context` (integrated-commit subject lines) then `## Auto-merge diff`; the COMBINED string is capped at DIFF_CHAR_CAP with the mergelist section capped first, and per-file diffs are fetched only until the combined cap is reached (remaining files listed undiffed with a truncation notice — bounds the per-file REST fan-out); the empty-auto-merge-diff case (clean merge) is explicitly defined — review proceeds on mergelist-only context and the robot comment states the conflict delta was empty. **Data flow into the gate is unchanged:** the assembled string is passed as `diff_text` through the existing seam — `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text=…)` → `produce_code_review_verdict(cfg, diff_text=…)` — no runner/gate-machinery changes. Robot comment: the merge-change variant REUSES the existing `_TAG_SUFFIXES` verdict keys in `adapter.py`, appending `(merge-change, N integrated commits)` to the existing suffix text (no new verdict vocabulary), e.g. `[LLM-Review: PASS (merge-change, 12 integrated commits)]`. Observability: structured journald log events `merge_change_review` (mode activation + integrated-commit count), `merge_change_409_guard` (ERROR), `mergelist_fetch_error` (ERROR), published as a CloudWatch metric `review_bot_merge_change_errors` (reason-tagged) via `infra/scripts/observability.sh` exactly as `voter_errors` is, plus a "signals to watch" entry in the runbook. Unit + fixture tests for all of the above.
- [ ] **S3 — CI coverage on feature branches + merge changes** (assumes 1fa8 live): determine from g2p source/docs whether `gerrit_to_platform.ini` filters dispatch by branch (replace the design's expectation with a verified statement: either the confirmed required `feature/*` config, or a confirmed no-config-needed no-op, recorded in the ini spec); done-definition: a `feature/*` patchset-created event triggers `gerrit-verify.yaml` AND a merge change into main gets CI on the actual merge tree (checkout-gerrit-change-action fetching the merge refspec), each proven with run-log evidence; Verified re-runs (not carries) on a re-merge; `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` behaves sanely across branch + merge changes.
- [ ] **S4 — Documentation sweep**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` gains a "Multi-story features (feature branches)" section (branch creation request path, story loop targeting the branch, catch-up merge recipe, merge-back recipe with the commit-msg hook install as an explicit prerequisite step + the Change-Id amend + merge-conflict resolution guidance + how to abandon a bad merge change and start over, pushMerge-refusal troubleshooting, a "missing Change-Id on merge push" troubleshooting entry, branch deletion); `CLAUDE.md` Git-workflow section (~line 410) gains the feature-branch flow + when-agents-should-use-it guidance (multi-agent parallel features vs single small changes), including the hook-install-in-fresh-worktree note; `README.md` + install docs (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, CONTRIBUTING one-time setup) verified current for the two-vote + feature-branch world; `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`; `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` (merge-change ops: 409 semantics, /rerun on merges, the new log signals, bot-code rollback = redeploy the prior review-bot image); repo-wide sweep for stale text implying the single-change amend loop is the ONLY flow or describing PR-era GitHub practices (grep "pull request", "gh pr", "PR merge", single-change-only phrasing) — the sweep's hit list is recorded on the ticket and every hit is fixed or has a recorded justification.
- [ ] **S5 — Live multi-agent E2E validation** on the running Gerrit (scripted alongside `infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; every scenario's change URLs + votes recorded on this ticket): (1) **parallel siblings** — two agents in separate worktrees push independent story changes to `feature/e2e-<date>`; both earn LLM-Review + Verified and submit WITHOUT either rebasing (second submit succeeds via MERGE_IF_NECESSARY with no manual rebase; this also live-proves webhook + g2p branch-agnostic dispatch); (2) **stacking** — a third agent pulls the branch (both stories in history) and pushes a change on top; the reviewed diff covers ONLY its delta; (3) **merge-back** — `--no-ff` merge change to main: bot reviews the auto-merge delta only (assert NOT the whole-feature diff), CI green on the merge tree, both votes present, submit lands atomically, replication advances GitHub main with all commits, branch deleted; (4) **vote-carry on re-merge** — land an unrelated change on main mid-flight, push a re-merge (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE): LLM-Review +1 CARRIES, Verified RE-RUNS; then change the feature tip: BOTH wiped (REWORK); (5) **textual conflict** — overlapping feature-vs-main edits resolved in the merge commit; bot reviews the non-empty auto-merge delta; (6) **semantic conflict** — textually-clean but semantically broken combination (e.g. rename on main + new call-site on feature): auto-merge diff empty, LLM-Review passes, CI red → Verified=-1 BLOCKS submit (proves two-vote complementarity); (7) **races + negatives** — concurrent submits into the branch behave (MERGE_IF_NECESSARY or clear conflict signal); a merge push WITHOUT pushMerge is refused; branch creation outside `feature-branch-drivers` is refused; the reconciler backfills a dropped webhook for a feature-branch change (including a merge change, exercising the transparent merge detection).
- [ ] **S6 — Process + back-out**: branch-lifetime cap + catch-up cadence documented; stale-branch policy — a scripted inventory check flags `feature/*` branches inactive beyond the cap (merged-back OR abandoned) for owner-confirmed deletion, recorded in the runbook; back-out documented + tested (revoke pushMerge + feature/* ACLs restores the single-change-only flow with NO label/gate changes; the submit-type pin back-out = remove the `[submit]` block and confirm the inherited value matches the S1-recorded prior state; bot code back-out = redeploy the prior review-bot image); cost/latency recorded as a "Cost & latency" section in the amending ADR with, from the S5 runs: median CI wall-clock per merge change, count of LLM re-reviews avoided via MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE carry vs CI re-runs incurred across the scenarios, and per-review LLM cost if surfaced by the runner.
- [ ] R1–R5 all hold end-to-end and are each demonstrated by at least one S5 scenario (R1: scenarios 2+3; R2: 3; R3: 1+3+6; R4: 1+4; R5: recorded OSS evidence in apt-otter-urn + ADR).
- [ ] The RED/BLUE/GREEN replay (scenarios 1–3) completes with zero vote wipes, zero manual rebases, zero re-reviews of already-attested stories, and a single atomic landing on main.
- [ ] The S4 sweep hit-list on the ticket shows zero unjustified stale-practice references remaining.

## Sequencing & risk
S1 (additive config) → S2 (bot merge path MUST precede any real merge change — today a merge change 409s to a fail-closed -1; S2 opens with the files/-default fixture verification, the plan's riskiest assumption) → S3 (needs 1fa8 live) → S4 (after semantics locked) → S5 (last; gates epic close) ; S6 folds into S4/S5 outputs. Risk: auto-merge review blindness to semantic conflicts is accepted and mitigated BY DESIGN via the Verified re-run posture (S3) + scenario 6 proof. Risk: long-lived branches rot — mitigated by lifetime cap + catch-up cadence + stale-branch inventory (S6). Risk: g2p branch filtering silently skipping feature/* (would break R3) — closed by S3's verified statement + run-log done-definition.

## Out of scope
- Cherry-pick-down release-branch model (Qt QUIP-16) — solves release maintenance, not feature accumulation.
- Automated feature-branch cleanup service (scripted/manual deletion only; the S6 inventory check is a script, not a service).
- Changes to relation-chain/topic behavior for SMALL work (a 2–3 change chain remains fine; feature branches are for multi-story features).
- Any GitHub-side workflow (the mirror stays read-only; PRs stay dead).
- Stacked-diff client tooling.

## Key references
- Validation + research record: session log apt-otter-urn (c905-a38c-0419-448e) — OSS citations, REST mechanics, corrections.
- OpenDev Infra Manual "Project Driver's Guide" (feature branches + merge-back recipe + pushMerge ACL); openstack/swift feature/mpu live changes; Qt Merge Guidelines + QUIP-16.
- Gerrit 3.x docs: config-labels.html (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE), rest-api-changes.html (files/diff parent semantics incl. #list-files auto-merge default, mergelist, GetPatch 409), access-control.html (pushMerge, Create/Delete Reference), user-review-ui.html (auto-merge base, Merge List), config-project-config.html (rejectImplicitMerges exempts real merges).
- Local: infra/gerrit/{project.config,setup-project.sh,reviewbot-e2e.sh}, src/rebar/review_bot/{voter.py,gerrit_client.py,adapter.py,reconcile.py}, src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py, infra/scripts/observability.sh, ADR-0010/0013, epic 1fa8 (smoky-flare-slug) + its ADRs, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md §Git workflow, docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md, infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md.
baseline.summary: Feature-branch accumulation: multi-story features off-main under per-story LLM+CI gates, landing via a reviewed merge change

# A parent REMOVED in Jira never clears the local parent_id (inbound)

Found while writing the row-13 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table (story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism — TWO independent layers each drop the signal

1. THE SNAPSHOT NEVER CARRIES "no parent". The fetcher's parent enrichment merges
   `client.get_parent_map()` into the snapshot and, when the mapped parent is None,
   deliberately leaves the field ABSENT: "When parent_jira_key is None, leave the
   field absent (top-level issue) - consistent with Jira REST shape"
   (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:508-511). So an issue whose parent
   was removed looks identical to an issue that never had one.

2. THE DIFFER REFUSES TO EMIT A CLEAR. `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` resolves
   the Jira parent to a local id and emits `changed["parent_id"]` ONLY when that
   resolution is non-None; the None case is explicitly skipped with the reason
   recorded inline: "We do NOT emit parent_id=None to avoid accidentally clearing a
   locally-set parent when we just can't resolve it yet"
   (inbound_differ.py:257-270, helper `_extract_parent_local_id` at :90-110).

The comment names the real design tension: "Jira has no parent" and "the parent key is not bound yet" are COLLAPSED into the same None, so the differ cannot clear without risking a spurious clear. The apply layer is already ready for the clear — `apply_inbound_records` maps `parent_id` through `lambda v: v or ""` and its comment says "an absent/empty parent maps to '' (clears the parent; ticket 8b25)" (apply_inbound_records.py:361-372). Only the differ never sends it.

## Why this is a gap

Story 5200's row 13 INBOUND oracle is "`.parent_id` is null". It is unreachable today: a de-parenting done in Jira is silently invisible to rebar, so the two systems diverge permanently with no report.

Fixing it needs the ambiguity resolved, not just the guard removed: the parent map must distinguish "queried and absent" from "not resolvable". The information is NOT missing at the source — the map already returns `{key -> parent_key | None}`; it is discarded at fetcher.py:509-511. **The Approach below resolves exactly this**, and it is the reason this is a two-layer change rather than a one-line guard removal.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` asserts `.parent_id` is empty after the DC parent is cleared. It should go RED on the harness until this is addressed. Note that cell asserts the DC-side clear as its own SETUP step, so "Data Center refused to null a sub-task's parent" is reported distinctly from this gap.

## Approach

Two layers each drop the signal, so both must change. The design problem is the same one `2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9` faces in the link direction and is solved the same way: an inbound CLEAR is a WRITE that destroys local data, so it may only fire on POSITIVE evidence that Jira was asked and answered "no parent" — never on the mere absence of data.

**This epic has already settled the predicate shape, in its own story 5200.** That story's first draft of the parent-cell wait helper took a predicate over `mapping[key]`, and `get_parent_map` has a degradation contract — any REST failure logs a warning and returns `{}` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:520-527`). So "no parent for this key" and "the parent-map read failed entirely" were indistinguishable, and the wait would have been satisfied by a broken read. It was fixed before landing to `lambda m: key in m and not m[key]` — **key PRESENT with a falsy value**. That is exactly the distinction both layers below need; the fix is to carry it into production code rather than only into the test helper.

### Layer 1 — the snapshot must record "queried, and there is no parent"

`fetcher.py:508-511` merges `client.get_parent_map()` and, when the mapped parent is None, deliberately leaves the field ABSENT ("consistent with Jira REST shape"). Make it explicit instead: `snapshot[snap_key]["parent"] = None` — key PRESENT, value None.

Why this is safe for every existing consumer: all of them read the field with `.get("parent")` and branch on falsiness, so an explicit None is indistinguishable from absent to them — `inbound_differ.py:104` (`if not parent_raw: return None`), `inbound_fields.py:229`, `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:519` (`isinstance(parent_raw, dict)`), `apply_inbound_records.py:186`, and `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:518`. Only the new removal path uses `"parent" in jira_fields`. **Verify this list against the tree before relying on it** — a consumer that used `"parent" in fields` or indexed `fields["parent"]` would change behaviour.

The loop only visits keys `get_parent_map` returned AND that are in the snapshot, so an issue the map never mentioned still gets NO key — which is the unobserved case, and a total read failure returns `{}` and therefore clears nothing. Both degrade safe.

### Layer 2 — the differ must distinguish THREE states, not two

`_diff_jira_vs_local` (inbound_differ.py:257-270) resolves through `_extract_parent_local_id` (:90-110), which returns None for three different situations collapsed into one, then refuses to emit. Replace the two-state read with a three-state one:

| snapshot state | meaning | action |
|---|---|---|
| `"parent"` NOT in `jira_fields` | never queried / read failed / truncated | **skip** — emit nothing |
| `"parent"` present and falsy | queried; Jira has NO parent | **emit the clear** (gated below) |
| `"parent"` present with a key that resolves | Jira parent known | set/compare as today |
| `"parent"` present with a key that does NOT resolve | parent not yet bound | **skip** — retry next pass |

The existing inline comment ("We do NOT emit parent_id=None to avoid accidentally clearing a locally-set parent when we just can't resolve it yet") is correct about the hazard and wrong only in that it treats one unresolvable case as if it covered all of them. Preserve its intent — the unresolvable case still skips — while letting the observed-absent case through.

### The gates on the clear

- **MANAGED.** Only clear a parent rebar MANAGED: `should_propagate_removal("parent", local_parent_id,
  local_ticket)` from `rebar.reducer._managed_refs`. The outbound direction already wraps this exact
  predicate as `_parent_clear_is_managed` (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:296`), whose docstring
  states the symmetric intent outright — "a parent a human set directly in Jira (one local never had)
  would be clobbered instead of ADOPTED inbound". Reuse the predicate; do not invent a second rule.
- **KNOWN BLIND SPOT, recorded not hidden.** `add_managed_ref` is folded by the LINK/parent-set event
  processors (`reducer/_processors.py:90,411,528`), so a ref is "managed" the instant it is set
  LOCALLY — it does NOT prove we pushed it to Jira. `seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for
  pre-feature tickets. So MANAGED alone does not establish Jira ever had the parent.
- **SAME-PASS SUPPRESSION closes that blind spot, and here it already works.** `inbound_differ.py:667`
  drops any inbound `changed` field the same pass's outbound is writing
  (`changed = {k: v for k, v in changed.items() if k not in ob_entry["fields"]}`), and the outbound→
  inbound name translation `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` at :495-498 **does** contain
  `"parent": "parent_id"` — verified, so the suppression genuinely fires for parent rather than missing
  on a name mismatch. A locally-set parent that outbound is pushing this pass is therefore not cleared
  inbound. **Pin this with a test**, because it is currently load-bearing by inheritance and a future
  edit to that map would silently remove the protection.
  Residual window, stated plainly: a degraded pass in which outbound does not write the parent (skipped,
  disabled, or failed) while inbound proceeds.

### The emit, end to end

Emit `changed["parent_id"] = None`. The apply layer is ALREADY ready: `apply_inbound_records.py:361-372` maps `parent_id` through `lambda v: v or ""` under `if _fname in fields`, and its comment says "an absent/empty parent maps to '' (clears the parent; ticket 8b25)". So no apply-layer change is expected — but **prove it**, do not assume it: the mutation must be followed differ → `InboundMutation.fields` → `run_differs` payload → `apply_inbound` → the reduced ticket's `parent_id` is empty. A `None` value is exactly the kind of thing an intermediate `if v` or a falsy-filtering dict comprehension drops silently, which is this epic's signature failure mode (this is how `2b16` turned out to need a second file). If something does strip it, that file joins the scope and the ticket records why.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer snapshot.** Present-before / absent-now is the textbook signal and would retire the MANAGED blind spot, but `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set` persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership only, no fields — as of `6cdd4b00d9`. Using it means adding a new persisted artifact with its own migration and truncation semantics, larger than this defect warrants.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — layer 1 (explicit None for a queried-absent parent).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — layer 2 + the MANAGED gate.
  **CRITICAL, CHANGED AFTER 2b16: this file is at 797/800 once change 1276 lands — THREE lines of
  headroom, not 82.** 2b16 grew it 718 → 817 (over the cap) and had to shed the observed-peer-link set
  into `link_direction.py` to reach 797. So layer 2 CANNOT be added inline; plan the seam up front.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` — **the seam for layer 2's extraction.** It is
  247 LOC (ample room) and ALREADY reads `jira_fields.get("parent")` at :229, so parent-field extraction
  is work it already owns: this is a real call-graph seam, not a mechanical split to beat a number.
  `link_direction.py` is NOT the right home — it owns link direction, and 2b16 already left it at 89 LOC.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_parent_clear_88d9.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py` (another ticket owns it);
  `apply_inbound_records.py` unless the end-to-end trace proves the `None` is dropped there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] a parent removed in Jira clears the local `parent_id`: asserted POSITIVELY EMPTY on the reduced
      ticket, never "no exception was raised"
- [x] the clear survives END TO END — differ emit → `InboundMutation.fields` → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → the reduced ticket's `parent_id` is empty. A differ-boundary-only oracle does
      NOT satisfy this
- [x] with the snapshot's `"parent"` key ABSENT (unobserved: read failure, `{}` degradation, or a
      truncated page), NO clear is emitted — simulate the real shape, including
      `get_parent_map` returning `{}`
- [x] with `"parent"` present and falsy (queried, genuinely no parent), the clear IS emitted
- [x] a Jira parent whose key does NOT resolve to a local id still emits NOTHING (the original guard's
      intent is preserved and independently tested)
- [x] a parent that is not in `managed_refs` is NOT cleared, so a parent a human set directly in Jira is
      adopted rather than clobbered
- [x] the same-pass suppression is pinned by a test: when outbound is writing `parent` in the same pass,
      the inbound clear is suppressed — asserted through `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` so a future edit
      to that map fails a test instead of silently removing the protection
- [x] steady state does not churn: an issue that never had a parent, and one whose parent is unchanged,
      emit NO clear on repeated passes
- [x] every existing consumer of the snapshot `parent` field is enumerated and shown unaffected by the
      explicit-None change (a grep-backed list recorded on this ticket, plus a test that a
      never-parented issue still produces no parent mutation)
- [x] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set MUST
      include making the clear unconditional — an unguarded clear passes the happy-path oracle while
      being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that protect the product
- [x] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` is
      unmodified and took the PLATFORM branch on harness run 30834117797 (SETUP FAILED: DC refused
      to null a sub-task fields.parent), filed separately as [rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94] as this AC
      requires. Cell unmodified and NOT weakened. Originally: turns GREEN on the harness once this lands — UNLESS it reports its explicit
      `SETUP FAILED` message, which means Data Center refused to null a sub-task's `fields.parent`. That
      is a PLATFORM finding, not this fix failing; record it and file it separately rather than
      weakening the cell
- [x] the parent enrichment merge in `fetcher.py` is EXTRACTED into a named, directly-callable helper
      and the unit test drives THAT helper — not a hand-mirrored copy of it. **This is a lesson bought
      by 2b16**, whose equivalent guard evidence rests on `_enrich_like_fetcher`, a byte-faithful hand
      copy of `fetcher.py:592-596` written only because that merge is inline in `fetch_snapshot` and
      cannot be called directly. That copy will silently drift, and it guards the boundary between a
      truncated read and deleted local data. Do not repeat it: layer 1 is being edited here anyway, so
      extracting it is cheap now and removes the weakest link from the evidence
- [x] `fetcher.py`, `inbound_differ.py` and `inbound_fields.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap —
      `inbound_differ.py` starts this change at 797, so its delta must be net-negative or near-zero
