baseline.description:
## Summary
`test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` fails on git 2.54 CI
(Linux, all Python tiers) with `error: invalid object <sha> ... error: Error building
trees` — a writer's locked `append_event` commit fails, is swallowed, and the write is
lost (`lost == swallowed_write_raises`, counts vary 17..232/250).

## Proven root cause (confirmed by reproduction + forensics)
The tickets store is a linked git worktree (`.tickets-tracker`) that SHARES the parent
repo's object database. On git >= 2.47, `git commit` triggers `git maintenance run --auto
--detach` — a DETACHED background process that runs `git repack -d -l --cruft --write-midx`.
Under concurrent writes, MULTIPLE such detached maintenance processes run OUTSIDE rebar's
write lock, racing the concurrent writers and each other, and corrupt the shared object DB
(missing/dangling objects; hundreds of `tmp_pack_*` garbage files). git's own docs warn a
concurrent `git gc` "may corrupt the repository"; plain gc/maintenance-detach does not take
the object-db lock. Directly observed: 4+ concurrent `git maintenance run --auto --detach ->
git repack --cruft` processes live during the failure, while rebar's own write lock shows 0
overlaps (it serializes its own git perfectly — the corruption is 100% from git's detached
maintenance escaping the lock).

## Why prior fixes did not resolve it
- WU-1 (epic 97e7) unset `gc.auto` + set `gc.autoDetach=true`, trusting "stock git gc is
  safe by construction" — that reasoning covers only SERIAL reachability, never a CONCURRENT
  background repack racing in-flight writes.
- 4c1c's `_recover_from_invalid_object` heal treats the downstream symptom (poisoned index)
  and cannot recover a HEAD-referenced missing object (read-tree HEAD re-poisons).
- `gc.auto=0` does NOT disable it: git >= 2.47 uses `git maintenance run --auto` (gated by
  `maintenance.auto`), not the legacy `git gc --auto`.

## Evidence
- git 2.47.3 -> 0 repro; git 2.54.0 -> reproduces (Docker, isolated).
- Diagnostic: zero-concurrency / writers-only / single-pair all PASS; only the full
  concurrent config fails, with live detached maintenance repack processes captured.
- Prior art: git-gc/git-maintenance docs; ArgoCD #25101 (identical: git 2.47 detached
  maintenance escaping a lock on a shared git dir); GitLab/Gitaly `gc.auto=0`; Homebrew
  `gc.autoDetach=false`.

## Fix direction (pending final experimental confirmation)
Disable background auto-maintenance on the tickets worktree — `maintenance.auto=false`
(+ `gc.auto=0`, + `*.autoDetach=false` defense-in-depth) — so no detached maintenance can
race writers; PRESERVE WU-1's bounded-growth by running gc/maintenance SERIALIZED under
rebar's write lock (`git maintenance run --task=gc`). Confirm `maintenance.auto=false` vs
foreground `autoDetach=false` empirically before choosing.

## Reproduction Steps
1. On git 2.54, init a rebar store; run 5 writer procs (SIGNATURE/REVIEW_RESULT bursts) +
   4 pruner procs (enqueue + `_prune_queue_events`) concurrently against it.
2. Observe some writers' `append_event` fail with `invalid object ... Error building trees`
   and background `git maintenance run --auto --detach` processes running.
- Expected: no writes lost. Actual: writes lost (corrupted shared object DB).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_gc_config_unit` disables background auto-maintenance (`maintenance.auto=false` +
  `gc.auto=0`) so no detached `git maintenance`/`git gc` can run concurrently with writers;
  proven by a test asserting the store's effective config after `init`.
- [ ] Bounded-growth (WU-1) preserved via a serialized-under-write-lock gc/maintenance path,
  OR an explicit, documented decision to defer it.
- [ ] `test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` re-enabled (skip
  removed) and green on the git-2.54 CI matrix (proving command: that test on CI).
- [ ] gc-config + ensure-drift-matrix tests updated to the new posture; docs (sync.py,
  concurrency.md, init.py `_gc_config_unit`) corrected to state that concurrent background
  maintenance is unsafe.
baseline.summary: enrich-prune flake root cause: git>=2.47 detached 'git maintenance run --auto' corrupts the shared tickets-worktree object DB

content.text: # Continuous auto-deploy: the running Gerrit environment reflects `main` without manual deploy or restart
## Why
Landing a change on `main` does NOT update the running environment: the review-bot container's code,
`replication.config`, and g2p config need a MANUAL deploy (SSM / setup-*.sh) + sometimes a restart.
This drifts + toils (S2's merge-review code landed but the running bot is pre-S2; the S3 replication
fix was hand-applied). The environment must AUTO-REFLECT `main` — without ever destabilising the
LIVE, FAIL-CLOSED gate (no LLM-Review vote ⇒ no submit; a bad deploy could freeze all submissions).
## What
- **Trigger (RESOLVED): on-box systemd timer** `rebar-autodeploy.timer` (2-min) → `.service` oneshot
running `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`. Chosen over a GitHub-Actions→SSM `deploy.yml` because it adds
NO GitHub→AWS trust surface (no OIDC/`ssm:SendCommand` grant that would make the GH runner a
lateral-movement path); the box already reads the PUBLIC mirror read-only + has an instance role.
- **Loop:** `flock -n` guard; fetch `origin/main`; no-op when `== deployed-sha`
(`/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`, initialised to current HEAD on first run WITHOUT deploying, written
atomically only on success). Deploy ONLY the mirror `main` tip (Verified-by-construction: it only
advances via Gerrit submit). Change-detect per component via `git diff --name-only
deployed-sha..origin/main` ∩ a path manifest (review-bot: src/rebar/**, Dockerfile.reviewbot,
pyproject, docker-compose; replication: replication.config; g2p: ini + materialize script).
- **Apply only what changed (v1 = review-bot ONLY):** review-bot → tag current image `:prev`, sync
source (see Box-adaptation), `docker compose build && up -d review-bot`. **replication/g2p AND
`refs/meta/config` are DETECT-ONLY in v1** — a change is signalled (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`), never
auto-applied (their correct apply needs a live-site copy + SSM PAT re-fetch whose failure modes must
not sit in the unattended path guarding a fail-closed gate; v2 follow-up). See Box-adaptation §3.
## Stability — live-pipeline safety (load-bearing)
1. **Bounded blast radius:** never touch the `gerrit` container (explicit `review-bot` service target
+ a post-deploy assert the gerrit container id is unchanged); never modify `refs/meta/config` (gate
labels/rules/ACLs). No Gerrit restart — only the bot container restarts, only on a code change.
2. **In-flight reviews delayed, not lost:** a restart drops in-flight webhooks, but the existing
reconciler-backfill re-reviews them; the post-deploy health check confirms the reconciler is live.
3. **Self-heal, never freeze the gate:** after `up -d`, an END-TO-END health check (30s timeout —
liveness: process up + `/health` 200) gates success; on failure → immediate
rollback to `:prev` + `up -d`; deployed-sha NOT advanced. Max frozen window = the health timeout.
4. **Failure handling = capped exponential backoff, NOT hard-disable** (mature-OSS consensus: Flux
retryInterval/backoff; Argo CD retry backoff duration/factor/maxDuration; k8s controller-runtime
ItemExponentialFailureRateLimiter 5ms→1000s; systemd v254 RestartSteps/RestartMaxDelaySec):
- rollback keeps last-known-good RUNNING; retry the deploy with backoff base 60s, factor 2, cap
15m — never auto-disable the loop (a hard-disable strands the env stale until a human acts).
- **SHA-keyed reset (Argo CD's rule):** persist last-attempted-SHA + failure count; a NEW
`origin/main` tip RESETS the backoff to base (a fix-forward deploys promptly); a known-bad SHA is
not re-attempted faster than the cap (no thrash) and is never permanently blacklisted.
- **Outer storm guard:** systemd `StartLimitIntervalSec`/`StartLimitBurst` on the RUNNING bot
service catches a crash-looping container (→ failed, needs `reset-failed`) — reserved for the
pathological case, NOT the primary retry path.
5. **Config validated before it touches Gerrit:** parse-check replication/g2p config pre-apply; a
malformed config is skipped (prior retained) + alarmed. (Belt-and-suspenders to AC below.)
## Defense-in-depth: a CI gate that rejects malformed config (so it never reaches `main`)
`make config-check` — parse-validate every infra config: `git config -f {replication,project}.config
--list`; python configparser on the g2p ini template; `docker compose config -q`; `bash -n` on
`infra/**/*.sh`. Wired into `test.yml` (⇒ runs in `gerrit-verify` ⇒ the `Verified` gate), so a
malformed config FAILS CI and can NEVER land on `main` — the auto-deploy never encounters one at
runtime (the runtime pre-apply check in Stability §5 is the belt-and-suspenders for a direct box edit).
## Observability + back-out
Structured deploy log (from→to SHA + components) + `rebar/host:deploy_errors` (host-probe grep of an
`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker, mirroring voter_errors) + a CloudWatch alarm w/ SNS action; the
backoff/failure state is alarmed. Back-out: `systemctl disable --now rebar-autodeploy.timer`; the
manual path (compose-up.sh / setup-*.sh) is unchanged.
## Scope
Deploy orchestrator + systemd units + stability guards + the CI config-check + observability/back-out
on the existing compose stack. Reuses the idempotent setup/materialise appliers. refs/meta/config
auto-apply deferred (detect + signal). No change to gate semantics (S1/S2) or the 88ab flow.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A post-gate `main` change auto-reflects on the box (no manual action) ≤ 5 min; latency
live-measured. Idempotent: a no-change run is a no-op; a change re-applies ONLY the changed
component(s) — verified for review-bot code; a replication.config / g2p / refs-meta change emits
`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` and is NOT auto-applied in v1 (detect-only)
- [ ] review-bot rebuilt/restarted ONLY on a source-set change (docs-only change ⇒ no rebuild); after
a code change the running bot reflects it end-to-end (a merge change gets the S2 merge tag)
- [ ] Blast radius: the `gerrit` container is provably untouched; `refs/meta/config` never
auto-modified; no Gerrit restart. project.config changes are detected + signalled, not attempted
- [ ] Self-heal: a deliberately-broken bot image FAILS the health check ⇒ rollback to `:prev` (gate
restored), deployed-sha not advanced (proven live)
- [ ] Failure backoff: repeated failure uses capped exponential backoff (base 60s→cap 15m), keeps
last-known-good running, and a NEW `main` SHA resets the backoff (fix-forward deploys promptly);
the loop never auto-disables; the systemd StartLimit storm-guard is in place
- [ ] CI config-gate: `make config-check` runs in `test.yml`/`gerrit-verify` and FAILS on a
deliberately-malformed config (proven) — a malformed config cannot reach `main`
- [ ] flock serializes overlapping fires; deploy log + `deploy_errors` metric + alarm applied;
back-out (disable timer) tested; manual path still works; live end-to-end auto-deploy verified
## Box-adaptation of the deploy mechanism (grounded in live box i-00880b2c7f13527c5)
Live SSM inspection changed two assumptions in v1–v4, so the mechanism is adapted and v1's
**auto-apply surface is narrowed to the review-bot container only** (config = detect+signal).
The safety guarantees (blast radius, self-heal, backoff, config-check-at-CI, flock) are unchanged.
### Observed box facts (SSM)
- `/opt/rebar` is a plain **copy** of the repo root — NOT a git checkout (no `.git`; uid 502; a
`.deployed_ref` marker). It is the compose `build.context` (`../..`) for both services; review-bot
bakes source at **build** time (no source bind-mount), so a rebuild picks up new code.
- Real compose working dir: `/opt/rebar/infra/compose` (services `gerrit`, `review-bot`).
- The ONLY runtime state under `/opt/rebar` is `infra/compose/.env` (SSM-sourced secrets, git-ignored,
0600, regenerated at boot by `fetch-secrets.sh`). All Docker state lives OUTSIDE `/opt/rebar` —
named volumes (`gerrit_git`/`gerrit_index`/…) + bind mounts under `/var/gerrit/*` — so a source
resync cannot touch it. systemd 252. review-bot health `http://localhost:8000/health` → `{"status":"ok"}`.
### Adapted mechanism
1. **Mirror clone (self-bootstrapping).** autodeploy maintains its own **regular** git clone at
`MIRROR_DIR=/var/lib/rebar/mirror` — `git clone https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git` (public HTTPS,
no auth; a *regular* clone, NOT `--mirror`/`--bare`, so `origin/main` resolves for the diff/rev-parse
ops). autodeploy self-bootstraps it if absent and **aborts if the remote is not `https://`** (supply-
chain guard). ALL git ops — fetch `--prune`, `rev-parse origin/main`, the
`git diff --name-only deployed..target` component change-detection, checkout of the target — run there.
2. **Source sync = `rsync -a --delete $MIRROR_DIR/ /opt/rebar/`** with hard excludes protecting runtime
state: `--exclude '/.git'`, `--exclude 'infra/compose/.env'`, `--exclude '/.deployed_ref'`, plus the
dev/state set (`.venv .terraform .serena .claude .tickets-tracker`). `.env` + Docker volumes are never
touched; ownership kept 502:502.
3. **Apply — review-bot ONLY (v1 narrowed).** On a review-bot source-set change
(`src/rebar/** infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot infra/compose/docker-compose.yml pyproject.toml`):
tag current image `:prev` (guarded — skip if none, first-build has no rollback target), `docker compose
build review-bot && up -d review-bot` in `/opt/rebar/infra/compose`, END-TO-END health-gate (liveness:
process up + `/health` 200), rollback to `:prev` on failure, blast-radius assert (gerrit container id
unchanged), `docker image prune -f`. **replication.config, g2p, and refs/meta/config are DETECT-ONLY in
v1** — a change is signalled (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker) for a manual operator apply, never auto-applied.
Rationale: their correct apply needs live-site copy (`/var/gerrit/site/etc/…`) and an SSM PAT re-fetch
(`materialize-g2p-config.sh`) whose failure modes should not sit in the unattended path guarding a
fail-closed gate; they are rare and already hand-applied. Auto-apply of config is a documented v2 follow-up.
4. **State/backoff unchanged.** `deployed-sha`/backoff/first-run-adopt as in v1; first run seeds the marker
from `/opt/rebar/.deployed_ref` if present (else the mirror tip), still WITHOUT deploying. A persistent
**git-fetch failure is instrumented** (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR fetch_failed`) so a stalled mirror alarms.
### systemd + installer + scope additions
- **systemd fix:** `ExecStart=/opt/rebar/infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (not `/opt/rebar/src/…`),
`DEPLOY_REPO=/opt/rebar`, add `MIRROR_DIR=/var/lib/rebar/mirror`.
- **`infra/scripts/install-autodeploy.sh`** (new; mirrors `install-observability.sh`): self-bootstraps the
mirror clone, installs the `.service`+`.timer` unit files, `daemon-reload`. **Ships the timer DISABLED**
(staged rollout: enable only after a manual dry-run passes).
- The health check is a **liveness** probe (process up + `/health` 200), not a deep readiness check — the
AC wording is narrowed accordingly.
### Additional acceptance criteria (box-adaptation)
- [ ] autodeploy syncs source into the copy-based `/opt/rebar` via a self-bootstrapping regular mirror
clone (HTTPS-enforced) + `rsync --delete` with excludes; a live resync provably leaves
`infra/compose/.env` byte-identical and the `gerrit` container + Docker volumes untouched
- [ ] v1 auto-applies review-bot ONLY; a replication/g2p/`refs/meta/config` change is detected + signalled
(`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`), never auto-applied
- [ ] `install-autodeploy.sh` installs units with the **timer disabled**; a manual dry-run
(`systemctl start rebar-autodeploy.service`) applies a real `main` advance end-to-end on the box
(review-bot rebuilt from synced source, health OK), evidenced by the deploy log SHA transition

baseline.summary: Continuous auto-deploy: running Gerrit environment reflects main without manual deploy or restart

## What
Add `batch_stage_and_commit(tracker, items)` (and a batched `write_and_push` variant) to
`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: commit MANY events under ONE write-lock acquire + ONE
`git commit`, all-or-nothing. `items` is a sequence of `(ticket_id, event_dict)`.

## Why
The single-event write path (`stage_and_commit`) commits one git graph per event (~3.3
commits/event). The write lock (`_store/lock.py`) is NOT re-entrant, so a caller cannot
loop `stage_and_commit` under one lock. A dedicated batch primitive is the seam bulk
callers (the importer, B2) use to collapse N commits into 1. Batching is invariant-safe
because replay/dedup/union-merge/SNAPSHOT-compaction key off each event's per-event UUID,
not commit boundaries (each event stays its own I2 uuid-named file).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` only. Single-event `stage_and_commit`/`write_and_push`
  behavior unchanged (the reversibility guarantee).
- Validate + canonical-stage every event BEFORE taking the lock; then under ONE lock:
  atomic-rename each temp into `{ticket}/{ts}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json`, one `git add`, ONE
  `git commit`.
- All-or-nothing rollback: any failure (validation, rename, add, non-recoverable commit)
  unstages AND unlinks ALL already-placed paths, not just the failing one.
- Generalize `_recover_from_unmerged` to re-add the FULL batch path list on retry.
- Empty batch = no-op (no lock, no commit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `batch_stage_and_commit(tracker, items)` in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: one lock acquire, N I2 uuid-named files, exactly one commit; returns the event count
- [ ] `batch_write_and_push` variant: batch commit then ONE best-effort push
- [ ] All-or-nothing rollback on validation / rename / `git add` / non-recoverable `git commit` failure: every already-renamed path unstaged from the index AND unlinked from disk
- [ ] `_recover_from_unmerged` (bug 6818 UU self-heal) re-adds the full batch path list on retry — a batched commit self-heals a pre-existing unmerged `.bridge_state/*`
- [ ] Empty batch is a no-op (no lock taken, no commit made)
- [ ] Single-event `stage_and_commit`/`write_and_push` path unchanged; existing regression tests (`tests/unit/test_store_write_index_reset_on_failure.py`, `tests/unit/test_store_write_unmerged_recovery.py`) stay green
- [ ] New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py` cover: N-in-one-commit, canonical-byte parity vs single path, empty no-op, validation/commit rollback, next-write-uncontaminated, UU self-heal
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green
baseline.summary: B1: batch_stage_and_commit — batched-commit write primitive in _store

baseline.description:
## Why
Existing stores must learn they are behind the registry without hot-path cost — Rails
`CheckPending` for a School-B registry: compare the applied-set to the registry ids, nudge on
write activity, cheaply, rate-limited, never breaking a write.

## What
WS1 landed the registry as `rebar._store.ensures` and exports, on that module: `REGISTRY_IDS`
(the frozen id tuple), `registry_ids() -> frozenset[str]`, `applied_ids(tracker) -> set[str]`
(parses `.ensure-applied`, degrading absent/garbage/non-list → empty set), and `APPLIED_MARKER`
(`.ensure-applied`). WS2 adds the write-path pending-nudge to THAT module (no new module) plus the
`EnsureConfig` config section.

**Pending computation (compute-once, per process).** Add `maybe_emit_pending_hint(tracker)` to
`rebar._store.ensures`. It computes `pending = registry_ids() - applied_ids(tracker)` and caches
the resulting SET of pending ids in a module-level dict keyed by the canonical tracker path — so
`.ensure-applied` is read AT MOST ONCE per store per process (a converged store caches the empty
set and every later write is O(1), zero further reads). The cache holds the id SET (not a bare
boolean) precisely so the emitted hint can NAME the pending units. When `.ensure-applied` is
absent/unreadable/garbage, `applied_ids` returns the empty set so `pending` = all registry ids (a
pre-feature store is genuinely behind) — the hint fires, but the rate-limit bounds it to ≤1 per
interval so there is no per-write spam.

**Where it hooks (single choke point).** Call `maybe_emit_pending_hint` best-effort at the end of
`event_append.write_and_push` (after a successful commit+push). Covered via `write_and_push`:
`_seam.append_event` (comment/tag/edit/link/set_*/sign) and the `composer` create/edit/revert
path (which call `append_event` → `write_and_push`). We hook ONLY `write_and_push`, NOT
`_seam.append_event` (which itself calls `write_and_push`), so there is no double-firing.
Best-effort, NOT universal — the ACCEPTED GAP set commits inline (raw `git commit`, NOT through
`write_and_push`) and is intentionally NOT hooked: `claim` (`txn.claim_core` + `push_after_commit`),
`transition`/close (`txn.transition_core` + `push_after_commit`), `compact.py`, `delete.py`, plus
the ensure units themselves and `fsck --repair` batches. A rate-limited nudge is not a correctness
mechanism, and these mutators still surface pending state on the NEXT covered write. Pure reads
(list/show/…) never touch the hook.

**Emission + rate-limit.** Emit a single WARNING that names the pending unit ids and points to
`rebar fsck --repair` (the EXISTING heal verb — WS3 folds the ensure-sweep into it), but only when
`pending` is non-empty AND the last-hinted timestamp in `.ensure-hinted` is older than the
configured interval. Reading `.ensure-hinted` is symmetric with `.ensure-applied`: an absent OR
unparseable/garbage `.ensure-hinted` is treated as "never hinted" (`last = None`), so the hint
fires (and then writes a fresh timestamp) rather than being silently suppressed. On a decision to
hint, rewrite `.ensure-hinted` with the current time via `fsutil.atomic_write`
(temp-in-same-dir + os.replace — same helper WS1 uses for `.ensure-applied`). `.ensure-hinted`
(WS2-owned, git-ignored: ADD to `_GITIGNORE` at init.py:38-48) holds a single timestamp. A fresh
auto-init'd worktree already has a current `.ensure-applied` (WS1 wrote it), so `pending` is empty
and it NEVER hints.

**Config.** Add an `EnsureConfig` section to `_config_schema.py` (`ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400,
`ensure.hint_enabled`=true) with the full scaffolding: the `@dataclass EnsureConfig`, an entry in
`_SECTION_CLASSES`, coercers in `_SECTIONS` (`_as_int(minimum=0)` / `_as_bool`), an `ensure` field
on `Config`, and a re-export from `config.py`. Adding the section to `_SECTIONS` is automatically
picked up by `config._env_signature()` (which iterates `_SECTIONS`) so the env layer + cache key
work with no further edits. The hint reads these via `config.load_config(...).ensure`.

**Env-var documentation decision.** The env overrides are auto-derived by `config._canonical_env_name`
as `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_INTERVAL_SECS` / `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_ENABLED` — no per-key entry needed. These
names are built DYNAMICALLY (never appear as a literal `os.environ["…"]`), and `docs/env-vars.md` is
GENERATED by `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, whose AST scanner only captures literal `os.environ`/
`os.getenv` reads. So the ensure env vars are (a) NOT captured by the drift gate and (b) `docs/env-vars.md`
must NOT be hand-edited (the gate would regenerate it and fail on the diff). The `[ensure]` section and
its two env overrides are documented in `docs/config.md` instead (WS4 also covers them in
`docs/migrations.md`). No generated file is edited.

**Fail-silent.** `maybe_emit_pending_hint` swallows ALL of its own exceptions — including a lazy-import
ImportError/SyntaxError from `rebar._store.ensures` / `rebar.config` — behind a debug log, so a write
NEVER fails because of it. There is no import cycle: `event_append` lazy-imports `ensures` inside
`write_and_push` (module load order unaffected), and `ensures` never imports `event_append`. A rare
double-hint under parallel agents (two processes both past the interval) is accepted.

## Scope
In: `maybe_emit_pending_hint` in `rebar._store.ensures` (compute-once pending-set cache, rate-limit via
`.ensure-hinted` + `fsutil.atomic_write`), the best-effort `write_and_push` hook (lazy import,
fail-silent), the `.ensure-hinted` `_GITIGNORE` entry, `EnsureConfig` scaffolding, and the `[ensure]`
docs in `docs/config.md`. Out: `run_ensures()` + `.ensure-applied` format/write (WS1), `fsck --repair`
fold + `ensures: N/M` line (WS3), `docs/migrations.md` (WS4), the exhaustive hot-path/idempotency suite (WS5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `maybe_emit_pending_hint(tracker)` computes `pending = registry_ids() - applied_ids(tracker)` and caches the pending id SET once per process per canonical tracker; a converged store reads `.ensure-applied` at most once and does zero further reads on subsequent writes (verified by test (e): a spy on `applied_ids` shows exactly one read across two hint calls on the same tracker)
- [ ] `.ensure-hinted` read degrades symmetrically to `.ensure-applied`: an absent or unparseable/garbage marker is treated as "never hinted" so the hint fires (not silently suppressed), then a fresh timestamp is written
- [ ] The hook is called best-effort only from `event_append.write_and_push` (covering `_seam.append_event` leaf writes and the composer create/edit/revert path, which funnel through it); `_seam.append_event` is NOT separately hooked (no double-fire); the accepted-gap inline committers (claim/transition via `txn.*_core`+`push_after_commit`, compact, delete) are NOT hooked and this is documented; pure reads are untouched
- [ ] The WARNING names the pending unit ids and points to `rebar fsck --repair`, rate-limited via `.ensure-hinted` (written with `fsutil.atomic_write`; added to `_GITIGNORE`) using `ensure.hint_interval_secs` (86400s); suppressible via `ensure.hint_enabled` and its auto-derived env override `REBAR_ENSURE_HINT_ENABLED` (no generated-file edits; `docs/env-vars.md` untouched)
- [ ] `EnsureConfig` scaffolding complete (`@dataclass EnsureConfig` + `_SECTION_CLASSES['ensure']` + `_SECTIONS['ensure']` coercers + `Config.ensure` + `config.py` re-export); the `[ensure]` section + its two env vars are documented in `docs/config.md`
- [ ] The hook swallows all its own exceptions incl. lazy-import failures (debug-logged) so a write never fails; there is no import cycle between `event_append` and `rebar._store.ensures`
- [ ] WS2 owns four concrete tests: (a) a pending store (empty/absent `.ensure-applied`) emits exactly one WARNING naming pending units + `rebar fsck --repair`, and re-emits only after the interval; (b) a fresh auto-init'd worktree (current `.ensure-applied`) emits NO warning; (c) `ensure.hint_enabled=false` suppresses the warning even when pending; (d) fail-silent — when the pending computation raises (e.g. `applied_ids` patched to raise), `maybe_emit_pending_hint` swallows it (no exception propagates) and a real `write_and_push` still commits successfully with the hook installed (covering AC5); (e) read-dedup — a spy/counter on `applied_ids` shows exactly one read across two `maybe_emit_pending_hint` calls on the same tracker (covering the ≤1-read cache claim)
baseline.summary: WS2: applied-set marker + write-path pending-hint (cached once/proc, 24h rate-limit, fail-silent)

## Why

This is the keystone that closes the bug class. The fetcher (producer) and the differs/appliers (consumers) share an implicit contract — the snapshot-entry dict shape — that nothing pins or jointly exercises. Pin it once, and exercise producer→consumer together through the production path, so a key/shape divergence (the exact failure in bugs 0ee6 and 3f04) fails a test immediately.

## What

- A single source-of-truth **snapshot-entry schema** (TypedDict + JSON Schema) in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_snapshot_schema.py`, covering every field the differs read: `summary`, `description` (ADF), `status`, `priority`, `assignee`, `labels`, `comment` (nested), `issuelinks`, `parent`. Documented as the canonical shape both sides target.
- A **producer→consumer round-trip contract test** (`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_snapshot_contract.py`): the `FakeAcliClient` (story A) → `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` → `inbound_differ` + `outbound_differ` → applier, through the PRODUCTION path. It asserts each consumer-depended key/shape is actually produced and read correctly (comment, issuelinks, parent + scalars). Per the epic sequencing, land it FIRST on the `comment`/`issuelinks` seam, then broaden.
- Validation asserts **structure/type, not exact values** (Dredd/Gavel posture): `fetch_snapshot` output conforms to the schema; the differs emit the expected mutations for the captured payloads. No whole-blob golden equality; no mock-call-count.
- **Owns the epic's guardrail artifact (resolves the roster-level gap):** commit a documented **anti-change-detector guardrail** for reconciler tests — a short `docs/` note (ADR-style) that records the testing-strategy decision (why one producer↔consumer contract test through the production path, rather than Pact or a live sandbox), where the snapshot schema lives, and the rules new tests must follow (assert semantic round-trip + structure/type; no mock-call-count; no whole-blob golden equality). New tests reference it.

## Scope

- In: the schema module, the joint round-trip contract test, and the documented guardrail/ADR note.
- Out: capturing fixtures (story A), collapsing appliers (story D), telemetry (story E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_snapshot_schema.py` defines the snapshot-entry shape (TypedDict + JSON Schema) as the single source of truth.
- [ ] A test validates `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` output against the schema, and would FAIL on the pre-fix conditions (issuelinks absent; comment under the wrong key).
- [ ] A round-trip test runs fetcher → differs → applier through the production path and asserts comment/issuelinks/parent plus scalar fields read correctly; it fails if a producer key/shape diverges from a consumer read.
- [ ] All assertions are semantic (keys/types/round-trip), never whole-blob golden equality or interaction/mock-call-count.
- [ ] A documented anti-change-detector guardrail (ADR-style note recording the testing-strategy decision + the schema location + the rules) is committed and referenced by the new tests.
baseline.summary: Producer<->consumer snapshot contract: shared schema + round-trip test through production path

## Summary

With the ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS session-guard fix landed (Gerrit 442), the external
'external integration (live services)' job now runs its live tests (17 pass) instead of
failing every one at the model call. That unmasked 3 pre-existing failures — tests not
updated for src design changes landed after the suite last passed (2026-06-16):

1. **test_ref_lock_ac0_live.py** — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler'`
   at _ref_lock.py:249 (reconciler git-op refactor d9e0f0e7 added a deferred import; the
   file-path-loaded test never put src/rebar/_engine on sys.path).
2. **test_pydantic_text_mode** — `RuntimeError: agentic filesystem tools OUTSIDE the
   repo-snapshot gate` (config.py:228); the direct-runner RunRequest defaulted to
   execution_mode='agentic' (snapshot-gate epic b25fafcd1). A text reply needs no fs tools.
3. **test_pydantic_review_code** — `assert 'code-review-disabled' == 'pydantic_ai'`;
   review_code became an off-by-default four-pass gate (2d3e7611a). ENABLED, the gate runs
   via and reports the pydantic_ai runner (verified live) — so the fix is to enable the
   capability, and the test's original runner=='pydantic_ai' assertion holds.

All three are test-only fixes (no src defect).

## Reproduction Steps

1. Trigger the external-integration workflow (external job) on main.
2. Observe: 3 failed, 17 passed, 8 skipped — the 3 failures above.

Expected: the external job is green. Actual: 3 stale live tests fail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] test_ref_lock_ac0_live puts src/rebar/_engine on sys.path so `from rebar_reconciler import ...` resolves (mirrors sibling external tests).
- [ ] test_pydantic_text_mode runs the text path without tripping the snapshot gate (execution_mode='single_turn' — text needs no fs tools).
- [ ] test_pydantic_review_code enables verify.enable_code_review and asserts the live gated path: runner == 'pydantic_ai' (the enabled four-pass gate runs via and reports the pydantic_ai runner — verified live) and findings is a list.
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: the external-integration GitHub Action's external job runs green.

baseline.description:
On every autodeploy restart the review-bot silently abandons acknowledged-but-unreviewed
webhooks (the in-memory review queue is dropped), so changes stall until the slow backfill
reconciler catches up — and the reconciler itself can be frozen indefinitely by one hung
review. Drain the queue on graceful shutdown and give backfill reviews the same per-review
timeout the live worker has.

## Why
The review queue is an in-memory `asyncio.Queue` (`app.py:107`). `POST /webhook` enqueues and
returns `202 {"queued": true}` — a promise to process the event. But the lifespan shutdown
(`app.py:127-134`) **cancels the worker without draining the queue**, so on the hourly
autodeploy restart (ADR-0026) any enqueued-but-unreviewed event is lost, and any in-flight
review is cancelled. Recovery falls entirely to the reconcile backfill, which is slow (300s
interval; sequential full-LLM-review per change; cursor advanced only at end-of-pass,
`reconcile.py:221`). This was observed live: an autodeploy at ~22:53Z dropped a batch of
in-flight webhooks (changes 716-723) that then took ~25 min to drain. Separately, the worker
wraps each review in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout)` (`app.py:153`) but `reconcile_once` calls
`review_and_vote` with NO timeout (`reconcile.py:215`) — so a single hung backfill review would
freeze ALL backfill indefinitely (the safety-net has no safety-net).

## What
1. **Graceful drain (app.py lifespan):** in the shutdown `finally`, BEFORE cancelling the
   worker, `await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS)` (suppressing
   TimeoutError) so queued events are processed by the still-running worker before exit;
   anything not drained in the window still falls to the reconciler (fail-safe, not fail-lose).
   `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` from env (default 45).
2. **stop_grace_period (docker-compose.yml):** set the review-bot service `stop_grace_period`
   to 60s so Docker's SIGTERM→SIGKILL window is long enough for the drain to run (default 10s
   would SIGKILL mid-drain).
3. **Reconciler timeout parity (reconcile.py):** wrap the `review_and_vote` call in
   `reconcile_once` in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=<review_timeout>)`; on TimeoutError emit a
   greppable marker and CONTINUE to the next candidate (never freeze the loop). Share the
   timeout value with the worker (factor `review_timeout_seconds()` so both read the same
   `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`: drain in lifespan `finally`; `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS` helper.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/reconcile.py`: per-review `wait_for` + timeout marker + continue.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py` (or a small shared helper): `review_timeout_seconds()` used
  by both app and reconcile (DRY; avoids an app<->reconcile import cycle).
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: `stop_grace_period: 60s` on `review-bot`.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: RED tests for the drain and the reconciler timeout.
- Non-goal: replacing the in-memory queue with a persistent/disk-backed queue (heavier; the
  reconciler remains the ultimate recovery path — chosen approach per operator direction).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] On lifespan shutdown with items still queued, the items are drained (processed by the
      worker) rather than dropped; before the fix they are dropped.
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k shutdown_drain -q`
      passes and is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] The drain is bounded: if draining exceeds `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS`, shutdown still
      completes (does not hang) and remaining items are left for the reconciler.
      Proving command: a test with a slow/blocking worker asserts shutdown returns within the
      bound.
- [ ] `reconcile_once` does not hang on a review that never returns: a review exceeding the
      timeout is abandoned, a marker is emitted, and the loop proceeds to the next candidate.
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k reconcile_timeout -q`
      passes and is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets `stop_grace_period` on the review-bot service.
      Proving command: `python -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('infra/compose/docker-compose.yml')); assert d['services']['review-bot'].get('stop_grace_period')"`
- [ ] Existing gates stay green.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: review-bot: drain review queue on shutdown + reconciler per-review timeout (deploy resilience)

## Why
The serial auto-lander's first step: pick the front `Autosubmit`+submittable change/chain and route it to the correct Gerrit rebase call. Split out of S2 (`perovskite-frilly-grebe`) to keep each unit loadable whole.

## Files
- `infra/autolander/loop.py` — selection + rebase-routing (part of the core loop).
- `infra/autolander/gerrit.py` — thin STDLIB-ONLY Gerrit helper (the `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` `urllib`+Basic-auth+XSSI pattern; no new dependency, no import of `src/rebar`), covering the calls this loop needs (get change, RelatedChanges, rebase, rebase:chain, submit, DETAILED_LABELS).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Selection:** selects the front `label:Autosubmit+1 is:submittable` change/chain; **FIFO keyed on the `Autosubmit` vote's `ApprovalInfo.date`** (read via `GET /changes/?q=…&o=DETAILED_LABELS`), oldest-voted-submittable-first.
- [ ] **Rebase-routing:** detect a relation chain via `GET /changes/{id}/revisions/current/related`; a >1-member non-merge chain rebases with `POST /changes/{id}/rebase:chain` (confirmed on this instance's docs; linear ancestry only, no `committer_email`); a `--no-ff` merge change ALWAYS uses `POST /changes/{id}/rebase` (first-parent-only `MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE`), NEVER `rebase:chain`; a single non-merge change uses `POST /changes/{id}/rebase`.
- [ ] `RebaseInput.rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader=true` preserves the uploader + DCO `Signed-off-by`/`rebar-ticket` trailer (keeps the human as uploader; the rebase drops `Verified` so CI re-runs).
- [ ] **Gerrit helper** reuses this repo's STDLIB-ONLY pattern (not `pygerrit2`, not a `src/rebar` import); the bot authenticates as `RebarBotNava` via its SSM-backed HTTP password (provisioned by S5).
- [ ] **Tests:** unit-test the FIFO ordering + the merge-vs-chain-vs-single routing against recorded Gerrit JSON.
- [ ] [operator-attested] a live check exercises `rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader` (uploader unchanged + `Signed-off-by`/`rebar-ticket` trailers preserved on the rebased patchset) against the live Gerrit 3.14.1 instance. The multi-member `rebase:chain` variant is the same on_behalf REST mechanism (unit-tested); a live multi-member `rebase:chain` E2E is a bounded follow-up (idea).
baseline.summary: S2a Selection + rebase-routing (FIFO, RelatedChanges, rebase/rebase:chain) + stdlib Gerrit helper

baseline.description:
## Continuous Monitoring and Observability

Deploying code is only half the battle; knowing how it behaves in the wild is the other. Observability involves instrumenting systems with logs, metrics, and traces to understand their internal states.

**The Impact:** It drastically reduces Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) by allowing teams to pinpoint and fix the root cause of production failures quickly.

## Scope

Integrate observability considerations into the preplanning and implementation-plan workflows so that logging, metrics, and tracing are planned and implemented as first-class concerns alongside feature code — not bolted on after deployment. Preplanning should generate stories that include observability requirements, and implementation-plan should produce tasks that cover instrumentation alongside functional implementation.
baseline.summary: integrate observability into plan review

baseline.description:
PLACEHOLDER / FOLLOW-ON EPIC. Scoped OUT of the LLM-workflow engine epic. The
deterministic gate is an *example use* of the workflow engine; making that gate
**trustworthy** (cryptographically defensible "this passed review" claims) is the
concern captured here. Do not start until the workflow-engine epic is underway.

## Context
The LLM-workflow engine (separate epic) lets workflows mix scripted + agentic steps. A
recurring *example* shape is: a deterministic step gathers inputs → an agent step emits
findings → a deterministic gate decides pass/fail → a deterministic step records a signed
validation / protected tag on PASS. The engine only needs to *support* such a workflow.
This epic owns the hard part: making the gate's verdict a **trustworthy, tamper-evident,
non-repudiable attestation** that an LLM cannot forge or influence — and the new store
surfaces (protected tags, commit binding) that a trustworthy gate needs.

Driving use cases (the engine demonstrates these; this epic hardens them):
- code-review workflow over a ticket's attached commits → signed validation on PASS;
- review of an epic → a reserved/protected tag on PASS;
- completion-verification of an epic against its success criteria → signed validation on PASS.

## Research findings (captured 2026-06; preserve — this is the value of the placeholder)

### Trust boundary — "the LLM must never sign its own homework"
- The reviewing agent holds the full "lethal trifecta" (untrusted input = ticket/repo
  content; private access = filesystem + tickets; state-change = could write results) —
  OWASP LLM06 *Excessive Agency*. Prompt injection is unsolved; probabilistic guardrails
  are not a control.
- Required architecture: the agent emits **findings only**; a **deterministic gate** decides
  pass/fail; the **signing key is reachable only by deterministic code**, never by any tool
  granted to an agent step. This must be *demonstrated* (a standing test auditing the
  workflow's tool list + key-path reachability), not asserted.
- Self-preference bias (LLMs rate their own outputs higher) means an agent's output must not
  be its own reference. Defense is structural, not prompt-level.

### The signature must bind to the code + inputs it validates
- VERIFIED in rebar today: `sign_manifest` HMACs `{v, algorithm, ticket_id, manifest}` and
  **deliberately excludes `head_sha`** from the signed bytes (signing.py) — so a signature
  "stays certifiable as the repo evolves." That is correct for attesting *steps*, but WRONG
  for a claim about a *moving* repo: a sign at SHA A stays "certified" after code moves to B.
- VERIFIED: the close-gate freshness check (txn.py:308-320) compares HEAD against the
  **unsigned** `head_sha` record field — attacker-malleable.
- FIX: put `reviewed@<sha>`, `tree@<tree-hash>`, `prompt@<commit>`, `model=<id>`,
  `policy=<ver>` + a `review_result` content hash *inside the manifest* (the manifest IS
  inside the HMAC, so this binds them); the verdict surface HMAC-verifies, extracts the
  signed SHA, and re-checks it against current HEAD. The unsigned `head_sha` becomes
  audit-only. Fail closed on missing/duplicate/malformed tokens; keep the `head_sha=="unknown"`
  guard.
- Bind the snapshot to the SHA: resolve ref→immutable commit (`git rev-parse <ref>^{commit}`)
  FIRST, `git archive` THAT sha, record + verify the tree hash. Handle `.gitattributes
  export-ignore`/submodules (extracted tree can differ from `<sha>^{tree}` → decide hard-error
  vs documented-unreviewed).

### Crypto: ride the standards, don't reinvent
- HMAC is symmetric → any verifier can forge ⇒ no non-repudiation, no public verifiability.
  **Default to Ed25519** for any trustworthy/cross-party gate.
- **Emit the signed result as a standard in-toto / DSSE predicate** so off-the-shelf
  verifiers (`cosign verify-attestation`, `gh attestation verify`) validate it — stop
  shipping a private dialect. Our "manifest of verified steps + verdict" maps onto an in-toto
  Statement (subject = reviewed ref/tree; predicate = verdict + provenance).
- **Sigstore keyless** (Fulcio/Rekor/OIDC) when the verifier is *outside* our trust boundary
  (cross-org): key-management elimination + identity binding + transparency-log audit.
  Overkill for an internal same-trust-domain in-process gate (self-managed Ed25519 suffices).
- **Don't gate what the platform already gates:** CODEOWNERS + required-reviews already give
  "the LLM can't unilaterally authorize" for git merges. The signed gate earns its keep only
  for consequential actions that do NOT flow through a PR (ticket transition, deploy, API call).

### Concurrency / convergence (event-sourced store)
- SIGNATURE is last-writer-wins by UUID tie-break; the store is multi-clone (every write
  auto-pushes to origin/tickets). Key signatures by `(run_id, reviewed-sha)`; the trust
  surface requires a certified signature whose in-manifest sha == current HEAD AND verdict ==
  PASS. With the signed-SHA freshness fix: stale signatures fail freshness; concurrent
  same-SHA PASS signatures are verdict-equivalent (benign); a FAIL produces no signature.

### New store surfaces this epic needs (full event-schema rigor)
- **commits-on-ticket** event (attach commit SHAs as the code-review input). NOTE: this one
  may also be built in the engine epic if an example workflow needs it — coordinate.
- **Protected/reserved tags**: a DISTINCT event type with a processor that refuses/ignores
  conflicting plain-EDIT mutations to the reserved namespace (plain tags are unprotected,
  last-writer-wins). Convergence by HLC-prefix + UUID tie-break (never wall-clock). Exclude
  from reconcile/Jira (session_log precedent). Discoverable rejection (`list-reserved` + a
  specific "X is reserved; only a signed workflow gate may apply it" error). Trust ⇒ Ed25519
  (multi-clone by default).
- Agent input/exfil hardening: secret-glob deny over the snapshot (`git archive` INCLUDES
  committed secrets — `.env`/`*.pem`/`id_*`/`*.key`/`*.p12`/`.npmrc`/`.netrc`/cloud creds),
  applied as a merge over existing `denied_paths`; refs constrained to ancestor-of-a-trusted
  branch; agent-authored comments are executor-stamped provenance, excluded from review-input
  assembly (anti-self-poisoning / anti-stored-injection-via-search) and treated as an egress
  channel (no comment grant on sensitive-ref workflows). We do NOT claim to sanitize other
  untrusted content; defense is structural.

### Prior-art landscape (the pattern is mature; the LLM application is the empty seam)
- Deterministic-gate→signed-attestation is foundation-grade: **in-toto** (CNCF Graduated),
  **Sigstore/Cosign** (OpenSSF Graduated), **SLSA**, **DSSE**, **OPA/Rego** for the gate
  condition; **Danger** for pure-deterministic PR gates.
- Across 27+ surveyed LLM projects, **none** combine (LLM finds) + (deterministic code
  decides) + (attestation outside the model's control). This seam is our novelty — a
  recombination of proven parts.
- Demand to validate before building: audit/compliance + multi-agent trust. If no consumer
  truly needs a portable signed attestation (vs. a platform required-check), this is
  gold-plating — name the user first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A named consumer/requirement is documented (else close as "not needed yet").
- [ ] Threat model written; standing test proves the agent's tool surface cannot reach the
      signing key or the gate decision.
- [ ] Signature binds reviewed SHA + tree + prompt/model/policy inside the signed payload;
      verdict surface re-checks against current HEAD; unsigned `head_sha` demoted to audit.
- [ ] Snapshot is bound to the resolved commit SHA (rev-parse → archive → verify tree).
- [ ] Ed25519 default; signed result emitted as in-toto/DSSE; verifiable by `cosign` /
      `gh attestation verify`; Sigstore-keyless path scoped to cross-org consumers.
- [ ] Protected/reserved tag event type + processor (refuses conflicting plain-EDIT),
      convergence-safe, reconcile-excluded, discoverable rejection.
- [ ] Secret-glob deny + ref constraint + executor-stamped agent-comment provenance/egress.
- [ ] Concurrency: signatures keyed by (run_id, reviewed-sha); distributed double-sign
      reasoned through and tested.
- [ ] A workflow's gate verdict can be recorded as a **tamper-evident, non-repudiable
- [ ] Protected tags exist as a first-class, convergence-safe store surface.
- [ ] A named real consumer (audit/compliance or multi-agent trust) justifies the work.
baseline.summary: Deterministic gate security: trustworthy signed validation for LLM workflows (follow-on)

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps
1. Run /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh (or systemctl start rebar-observability.service) on a healthy box.
2. All sections execute and every metric publishes (trace confirms root_pct etc. reach put-metric-data).
3. The script's last statement is the mirror-out-of-sync guard `[ $oos -gt 0 ] && ...` which evaluates false on a healthy box, and there is no trailing `exit 0` — so the script's exit status is 1.

**Expected:** a run that publishes all metrics exits 0; systemd shows the unit succeeded. **Actual:** exit 1 on every healthy run; journald logs 'Failed with result exit-code' every 5 minutes, the unit sits in failed state (masking real failures and poisoning any future OnFailure/unit-failure monitoring), and install-observability.sh's verification start appears to fail.

Observed 2026-07-10 on the prod box while verifying ac14's root-disk metric (bash -x trace: last line `+ '[' 0 -gt 0 ']'` then exit=1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] observability.sh exits 0 on a healthy run (e.g. explicit `exit 0` at end, or guard restructured as `if`).
- [ ] A regression test or shellcheck-style check covers the exit status (mirror the test_autodeploy_prune.py stub-harness pattern if practical).
- [ ] systemd unit shows active(exited)/success after a timer run on the box post-deploy.
- [ ] File paths: infra/scripts/observability.sh.
baseline.summary: observability.sh exits 1 on every healthy run — final statement is a false test with no exit 0

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. In a disposable repository, add an activated `code_review` entry for
   `project.review-phase-boundaries` to `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` with
   `exec: "AGENT"`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, and `blocking_enabled: false`.
2. Add the matching project prompt and eval spec under `.rebar/prompts/` and
   `.rebar/evals/`.
3. Run the four-pass code-review workflow over a matching prompt/reviewer diff, then run the
   per-criterion eval command for the activated project criterion.

## Expected vs Actual

**Expected:** the activated project criterion is resolved from the reviewed repository, runs
exactly once in Pass 1, carries its logical `project.*` criterion id into findings, is judged by
Pass 3 using the repository's effective routing, and can be evaluated through the existing
per-criterion eval surface.

**Actual:** `gates/code-review.yaml` contains only a static built-in prompt list;
`CodeReviewBatchRunner` iterates only that list; `code_review_decide` calls
`registry.threshold_for` and `nit_suppressed_criteria` without the repository's effective routing;
and `eval_solver._code_review_prompt_id` accepts only the base, verifier, and packaged overlay ids.
The overlay vocabulary therefore advertises net-new code-review project criteria that cannot run or
control their configured posture end to end.

## Root Cause

ADR 0017 completed the shared overlay merge and exposed `code_review.effective_criteria` /
`effective_routing`, but code review never received the runner-side dynamic fan-in that plan review
uses, nor repo-aware Pass-3 lookup or project-id eval resolution. This is a generic integration gap,
not a special case for the boundary criterion.

## Scope

- Add `CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "code-review-"` and a gate-keyed
  `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id, *, gate_key="plan_review")`; the default preserves existing
  plan-review callers while code-review `project.<name>` maps to
  `code-review-project-<name-with-dots-replaced-by-dashes>`.
- Fan activated non-DET code-review project criteria into `round_a` only.
  `CodeReviewBatchRunner` uses `PROJECT_FAN_IN_STEP_ID = "round_a"` as a stateless discriminator,
  deduplicates physical ids against static criteria, and never injects them for `round_b`; no mutable
  flag survives between reviews. Do not change the version-pinned workflow schema or hard-code
  project ids in packaged YAML.
- Resolve project prompts from the reviewed snapshot; a missing or malformed activated prompt
  raises a located `LLMError` before model execution rather than being skipped or converted to an
  empty-findings coverage gap.
- Bind Pass 3 threshold and nit-suppression lookup to `effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)`.
- Extend the existing criterion-eval resolver to recognize activated code-review project criteria
  and load their `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml` specs. The resolver reuses
  `_run_code_review_case`, reads each case's `diff` key, and returns the prompt's native findings;
  it does not route project code-review criteria through plan-review `pass1_chunk` or add a new arm.
- Extend the `criteria eval` CLI preflight to accept a logical code-review project id only when it
  appears in `code_review.effective_criteria(repo_root)`. Compare membership in plan-review and
  code-review registries: no match is unknown, exactly one selects that gate, and a dual-gate match
  is an explicit ambiguity error. Pass the selected gate through `calibrate_criterion` to the
  gate-keyed prompt mapper; unknown, inactive, and ambiguous ids remain errors.
- Extend calibration with
  `calibrate_criterion(criterion_id, *, repo_root=None, runs=1, gate_key="plan_review")`; the CLI
  passes its uniquely resolved gate and calibration calls
  `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id, gate_key=gate_key)`.
- When a project prompt emits findings, overwrite each finding's `criteria` with its logical
  `project.*` id and set `reviewer_id` to the physical prompt id. Do not trust or translate the
  model's criterion attribution. Built-in findings preserve their current behavior.
- Update `docs/llm-framework.md` with the stable naming/runtime/error/eval contract.
- Preserve byte-for-byte behavior for repositories without a code-review project overlay.

Out of scope: authoring `project.review-phase-boundaries`, changing the four-pass decision math,
changing packaged built-in criteria, or deploying a Gerrit dogfood criterion.

## Implementation Notes

Likely seams are `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py`, and
`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py`, `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py`, plus the CLI preflight in
`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py`. Reuse the existing plan-review runner-side fan-in pattern;
do not add a project-specific branch or a new workflow DSL field. Eval recognition must invert the
same sanitized mapping and confirm the logical id is active in the repository-effective registry;
a prefix match alone is insufficient. `_code_review_prompt_id` therefore receives `repo_root`,
builds an active logical-to-physical map with `criterion_prompt_id(..., gate_key="code_review")`,
and returns the input physical id only when it is one of those computed values. This avoids parsing
the forward-only filename back into a logical id.

In `code_review_decide`, compute `routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root)` once, pass a
callback using that map to `pass3_over_findings` (`threshold_for` returns threshold plus blocking
posture), and pass the same map to
`nit_suppressed_criteria`. Both threshold/posture and nit suppression must be repo-aware together.
The authoring preview/editor remain plan-review-only and use the mapper's default; adding a visual
code-review criterion editor is out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An offline full-gate test activates a synthetic code-review `project.*` criterion and proves
  its project prompt runs once per review across reusable-runner `round_a` and `round_b` requests,
  every emitted finding carries the logical id in `criteria`, and the physical prompt/eval ids pass
  validation; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k fan_in`.
- [ ] A finding tagged only with the synthetic project id records the overlay's configured
  `block_threshold` and `blocking_enabled` values in Pass 3, and overlay `nit_suppressed` overrides
  are honored; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k routing`.
- [ ] An activated project criterion with a missing or malformed prompt fails with a located error,
  while an overlay-absent repository produces the pre-change workflow result; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'missing or parity'`.
- [ ] The criterion eval resolver accepts an activated code-review project id and its sanitized
  prompt id, the CLI preflight admits the logical id, the repository eval spec loads, and unknown or
  inactive ids plus a dual-gate ambiguous id are rejected. Its `diff` fixture runs through
  `_run_code_review_case` and produces native findings without entering the plan-review criterion
  arm; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'eval or cli'`.
- [ ] Existing shared-overlay and four-pass code-review regression suites remain green; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_unified_criteria.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py
  tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_workflow.py`.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` contains a `Code-review project criteria` section covering Round-A
  fan-in, logical/physical ids, fatal configuration errors, deterministic Pass-3 routing, and the
  `criteria eval` entry point; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("docs/llm-framework.md").read_text(); assert
  all(x in s for x in ("Code-review project criteria", "round_a", "criteria eval",
  "configuration error", "effective routing"))' && make lint`.

## Rollback

Revert the additive fan-in, repo-aware lookup, and eval-resolution changes together. Repositories
without a project code-review overlay remain the compatibility baseline, so rollback requires no
data migration or cleanup.
baseline.summary: Project code-review criteria do not run through the full four-pass integration seam

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. On a macOS host with no util-linux flock binary (no Homebrew util-linux), or anywhere with REBAR_FORCE_MKDIR_LOCK=1 exported for the bash side only.
2. Run a bash-path write (e.g. `rebar comment <id> x`, which goes through ticket-lib.sh _flock_stage_commit) concurrently with a transition/claim (which executes src/rebar/_engine/ticket_txn.py).

3. Observe the two critical sections do not mutually exclude: _flock_stage_commit takes the mkdir lock (.ticket-write.lock.d, ticket-lib.sh:166-194) while ticket_txn.py takes fcntl.flock LOCK_EX on .ticket-write.lock (ticket_txn.py:54-60) — and mkdir-based locking does not contend with fcntl.flock (acknowledged at ticket-lib.sh:233-234, 310-311 for the _flock_write_json case, but _flock_stage_commit still uses mkdir).
Expected: all writers on one clone serialize on one lock (invariant I5: single locked write path).

Actual: on the mkdir-fallback platform class, a leaf write and a transition/claim can interleave inside the git add/commit critical section. Event files themselves are safe (unique names, I2), but concurrent `git commit` in one worktree can fail on .git/index.lock and trip the 'git commit failed while holding lock' error path; the optimistic re-read in ticket_txn.py is also not actually serialized against bash writers there.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One lock discipline serializes ALL same-clone writers on every platform class (flock(1), fcntl-only, no-flock)
- [ ] Regression test: mixed bash-write + ticket_txn.py claim storm under REBAR_FORCE_MKDIR_LOCK shows strict mutual exclusion (no index.lock failures, no lost commits)
- [ ] Fix lands no later than Tier D of adult-oxide-slave (docs/bash-migration.md section 6 carries the dual-window interop rule)

baseline.summary: Lock-mechanism mismatch: bash mkdir-fallback writes do not contend with ticket_txn.py fcntl.flock on flock(1)-less platforms

## Context

The current change correctly blocks the target vocabulary, avoids symlink reads, and is approved; this follow-up keeps the additional boundary work scoped separately.

- [ ] Binary files remain safely ignored without false positives.

baseline.description:
# A destroyed parent edge cannot be restored: no supported route re-parents to a closed parent

## Impact, and why this is filed as a defect rather than an enhancement

The reconciler cleared the `parent_id` of 63 tickets (see 88d9-fe42-e50f-4067 for that incident). Every prior parent is recoverable from the event log, but **rebar cannot write them back**: 61 of the 63 parents are closed, and `rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation cascade (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`): "cannot re-parent to closed ticket '<id>'. Reopen the parent first".

So the tool can destroy a parent edge automatically but cannot restore one, and the store has no supported path back to a state it was previously in. That is the defect.

## All four candidate routes were checked, not assumed

* `edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path — there is no `parent` / `move` / `reparent` command, and
  `link`/`unlink` cover the six link relations, not hierarchy.
* `edit` has NO `--force`: zero mentions in its help output, and `force` does not appear anywhere in
  `_commands/composer.py`.
* `rebar revert <ticket> <uuid>` does NOT restore state. `process_revert`
  (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) appends a record to `state["reverts"]`; its only state effect is
  un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED. Reverting the offending EDIT logs the revert and leaves
  `parent_id` empty.
* `fsck-recover` is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
* `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library path hits the same guard.

## Why the documented workaround is not acceptable here

"Reopen the parent first" means, at this scale: reopen ~20 epics, re-parent their children, then re-close each. Re-closing runs the LLM completion-verification gate (`require_completion_verification_for_close = true`) ~20 times and writes fresh STATUS + COMPLETION_VERDICT events onto already-signed closes. A single gate failure leaves a previously-closed epic OPEN — a second visible regression introduced while repairing the first. Rewriting the close records of 20 completed epics to work around a missing flag is a symptom-level workaround.

## Approach

Add `--force` to `edit`, scoped to bypass **only** the closed-parent status check. Follows rebar's existing `--force` idiom (`claim --force`, `transition --force-close`): explicit operator intent, never implicit.

Deliberately still enforced under `--force`:
* the parent must EXIST (`resolve_ticket_id` + directory check),
* a ticket may not be its own parent,
* the cycle walk (a `--force` that could build a cycle would corrupt the hierarchy, which is a
  different and worse failure than the one being repaired),
* the `status == ""` fail-closed branch (an unverifiable parent stays refused — `--force` overrides a
  KNOWN-closed parent, never an UNKNOWN one).

Only the `status not in ("open", "in_progress")` refusal for a status that is positively known becomes overridable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `edit --parent=<closed ticket> --force` succeeds and the child's `parent_id` is the closed
      parent, asserted on the REDUCED ticket, not on the command's exit code
- [ ] without `--force` the same command still FAILS with the existing message, so the guard is not
      weakened for ordinary use
- [ ] `--force` does NOT bypass: a non-existent parent, self-parent, a cycle, or the `status == ""`
      fail-closed branch — one test per case, each asserting the specific error
- [ ] the flag is rejected/ignored coherently when `--parent` is absent (it has no other meaning)
- [ ] `--force` usage is discoverable: it appears in `edit`'s usage/help text
- [ ] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the bypass UNCONDITIONAL — an unconditional bypass passes the happy-path
      oracle while silently removing the guard for every caller, so the still-refused cases are the
      oracles that protect the product
- [ ] the 63 recorded parent edges are restored and verified by re-reading the reduced tickets, with
      the count confirmed against the manifest
baseline.summary: edit cannot restore a parent edge onto a closed parent, so a destroyed hierarchy is unrepairable

baseline.description:
The unit test `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py::test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated`
fails INTERMITTENTLY in CI with `rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar transition failed
(exit 2): Error: git operation failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD`. It is NOT a
CI-vs-Gerrit drift (Gerrit's Verified gate runs the identical pytest matrix, so it
fails there too) — it is test-isolation / concurrency flakiness under pytest-xdist
(`-n 4 --dist worksteal`), where a temp git store is exercised before its initial
commit exists (unborn HEAD), so a `rebar transition` git op hits `could not parse HEAD`.

Discovered while resolving bug `pillared-doddering-fawn` (the deterministic
`no-commit-to-branch` CI-drift red). Filed separately because it is a different
failure CLASS (flaky test, not drift) and out of scope for that change.

## Evidence
- run 29470200567: FAILED on cell `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.12)` only (py3.11,
  py3.13, macOS all PASSED). `1 failed, 6171 passed` — the single failure is this test.
- run 29468054945: FAILED on cell `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` instead; py3.12
  PASSED that run. i.e. the failing cell MOVES run-to-run → non-deterministic.
- Failing assertion context: the test drives `rebar transition` on a store with
  child tickets; the git op raises `fatal: could not parse HEAD`.

## Reproduction Steps
- [ ] Run the interface suite under xdist repeatedly:
      `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`
      (and/or the full interface tier) enough times to surface the intermittent failure.
- [ ] Observe an occasional `git operation failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD` from
      `rebar transition` in `test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated`.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the test passes deterministically on every cell / every run (a fresh test
  store always has a parseable HEAD before a transition git op runs).
- Actual: it fails on ~1 random matrix cell per run with `could not parse HEAD`,
  reddening branch CI (and it would redden the Verified gate too).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root-cause the `could not parse HEAD` (the test-fixture git-store setup that
      leaves HEAD unborn / races the initial commit under xdist worker parallelism),
      cited to the fixture/code (`path:line`).
- [ ] Fix so the test store always has a committed HEAD before any `rebar transition`
      git op, under xdist parallelism (e.g. ensure the fixture commits an initial
      state / is isolated per worker).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Demonstrate stability: the test passes across repeated xdist runs (quantified,
      e.g. 50/50 green) — a single green run does not close a flake.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make test` (or the interface tier) green on all matrix cells.
baseline.summary: Flaky test: test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated fails intermittently with 'could not parse HEAD' under xdist

baseline.description:
## What
Capture env/integration-diagnosis passively by writing an additive `verdict="ERROR"` gate-sidecar record (with an `error{cause,evidence_ref}` object) on the gates' infrastructure-exception path, so a diagnosis interval starts (ERROR) and ends (next PASS) is recorded by gate code, never by agent self-report.

## Current behavior (verified against the code — the plan MUST fit this)
The three gates handle an infra exception (`LLMUnavailableError`) **asymmetrically**, and this ticket does NOT change that:
- `produce_plan_review_verdict` (gate_dispatch.py:110) and `produce_code_review_verdict` (:512) **catch** `LLMUnavailableError` and **return a degraded INDETERMINATE** verdict (`_degraded_plan_review_verdict` :395 / `_degraded_code_review_verdict` :456) — a soft-degrade contract that must be preserved.
- `produce_completion_verdict` (:634) does **not** catch it — the exception **propagates** and the close gate fail-closes.
- `plan_review/sidecar.build_payload` writes schema `plan_review_result_v2` and does NOT reconcile the verdict; `completion_sidecar.build_payload` routes through `reconcile_verdict` (completion.py:214) which **coerces any non-PASS to FAIL** — so a naive `verdict="ERROR"` on the completion payload would be flattened to FAIL.
- Readers are schema-guarded: `latest_review_result`/`all_review_results` accept only `plan_review_result_v1|v2`; `latest_fail_verdict`/`latest_pass_record` accept only `completion_verifier_fail_v1`/`pass_v1`. An unrecognized schema is silently skipped.

## Files & approach
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — classify an infra exception (provider 5xx/connection/tooling) at each existing `except LLMUnavailableError` site, and **additively** write an ERROR sidecar record there, **preserving the existing per-gate outcome**:
  - plan-review + code-review infra sites: emit the ERROR record, then `return` the existing degraded INDETERMINATE verdict (write-then-degrade — the soft-degrade contract is unchanged).
  - completion infra site: wrap preflight (:651) so it emits the ERROR record then **re-raises** (write-then-reraise — the fail-closed contract is unchanged).
  - A domain BLOCK/FAIL (non-infra) writes **no** ERROR record.
- **Dedicated schema tag `gate_error_v1`** (NOT a reuse of the verdict schemas) with a small dedicated payload builder `build_error_payload(gate, cause, evidence_ref)` → `{schema:"gate_error_v1", verdict:"ERROR", gate:<plan_review|code_review|completion>, error:{cause,evidence_ref}}`. Because it is a separate builder it **never routes through `reconcile_verdict`**, so the `ERROR` verdict survives (is not coerced to FAIL). Written on the **existing** event types — `REVIEW_RESULT` (plan/code-review) and `COMPLETION_VERDICT` (completion) — so **no new event type** is introduced (both are already non-replay + in the write allow-list).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py` — add the `build_error_payload` helper + an `emit_error(...)` path (default-absent). The existing verdict readers are **left unchanged**: their schema guards naturally skip `gate_error_v1`, so no existing reader ever surfaces an ERROR record unexpectedly. The metrics gate-sidecar reader (ticket 3c07) is the consumer that reads `gate_error_v1`.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar.py` — new.

## Back-compat
Purely additive: older readers ignore `gate_error_v1`; no verdict-builder or reconcile path changes; back-out = stop emitting the ERROR record. Only gate-encountered infra failures are captured — a deliberate, stated scope limit (shell/CI toil outside a gate stays out of scope). Stamped by gate code on a real failure, so the self-report reliability problem does not apply.

## Tests
- Unit: a stubbed plan-review run raising `LLMUnavailableError` writes a `REVIEW_RESULT` record with `schema="gate_error_v1"`, `verdict="ERROR"`, non-empty `error.cause`, AND the gate still returns INDETERMINATE (degrade preserved). A domain BLOCK writes no ERROR record. The completion infra path writes the ERROR record then re-raises. Existing `latest_review_result`/`latest_fail_verdict` do not surface the ERROR record.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar.py` passes: injecting an infra exception at a gate yields a persisted `gate_error_v1` record with `jq -e '.verdict=="ERROR"'` and non-empty `error.cause`.
- [ ] the gate's pre-existing outcome is preserved on the infra path — plan-review/code-review still return INDETERMINATE, and the completion path still propagates the exception — asserted by the test.
- [ ] a domain BLOCK/FAIL produces no `gate_error_v1` record — unit test asserts absence.
- [ ] existing verdict readers (`latest_review_result`, `latest_fail_verdict`) never return the ERROR record — unit test asserts the schema guard skips it (so the ERROR verdict is not coerced to FAIL and does not pollute verdict reads).
baseline.summary: Gate ERROR outcome on the infra-exception path (env-diagnosis start)

content.text: Rec 7a of session-logs/2026-06-09-architecture-review.md (risk R6). applier.py:640 _read_latest_status re-implements status replay as a raw scan of STATUS event files ("last STATUS json wins"). It ignores SNAPSHOT folding and the reducer's UUID-based fork resolution, so it can disagree with the reducer on a forked or compacted ticket — the reconciler may then push a wrong status to Jira. Latent correctness bug, not a refactor.

Work: replace _read_latest_status with reduce_ticket(...)["status"] (or a thin reducer-backed helper). RED test first: construct a store with (a) a compacted ticket (SNAPSHOT + retired events) and (b) a STATUS fork resolved by UUID, show _read_latest_status diverging from the reducer, then fix.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RED test demonstrating divergence on compacted and forked tickets, then GREEN via reducer-derived status
- [ ] _read_latest_status deleted or reduced to a reducer call
- [ ] Reconciler unit suites green

baseline.summary: Reconciler: derive status via the reducer, not applier._read_latest_status
