baseline.description:
# `rebar create` accepts a file path for the ticket description (contents inlined)

## Context

Today `rebar create <type> <title>` takes the description as an inline string via
`--description "<text>"` (CLI), `description=` (library `rebar.create_ticket`), and the
`create_ticket` MCP tool. Authoring a rich, gate-passing description (the template requires an
`## Acceptance Criteria` block plus per-type headings, ≥~200 chars, bullets) as a single shell-quoted
string is painful and error-prone: newlines, backticks, `$`, and quotes must be escaped, and large
plans are unwieldy on the command line. Agents already work around this by writing the body to a temp
file and `cat`-ing it into `--description "$(cat file)"`, which is exactly the friction this removes.

This epic adds a way to pass a **file path** whose **contents become the description**. Critically,
the file is read at create time and its **contents are stored as the description** — the ticket does
NOT store a reference/path to the file (the file can be deleted afterward with no effect on the
ticket). This mirrors how tools like `git commit -F <file>` and `gh pr create --body-file <file>`
behave.

## What / Scope

In scope:
- **CLI:** add `--description-file <path>` (and a short alias if consistent with existing flags) to
  `rebar create`. Reads the file (UTF-8), uses its contents as the description. `-` means read from
  **stdin** (consistent with `gh`/`git -F -`). Mutually exclusive with `--description` (error if both
  given). Path errors (missing/unreadable/not a file) produce a clear non-zero exit with a useful
  message, not a traceback.
- **Library:** `rebar.create_ticket(...)` gains a `description_file: str | os.PathLike | None`
  parameter (or accepts the existing `description` plus a new `description_path`); reading is done in
  the library so all surfaces share one implementation. Inline `description` and the file param are
  mutually exclusive.
- **MCP:** `create_ticket` tool gains an optional `description_file` argument with the same
  read-and-inline semantics and mutual-exclusion rule. (Consider security: the MCP server may run with
  a constrained CWD — document/validate that the path is resolved relative to the repo root or an
  explicitly allowed base, and reject path traversal, consistent with the LLM file-tool containment
  already used elsewhere.)
- Docs: README CLI block + `rebar create --help` + CLAUDE.md tool notes updated to describe the flag
  and the "contents are inlined, not referenced" semantics.
- Tests: CLI (file, stdin `-`, missing file, both-flags-error), library, and MCP paths.

Out of scope:
- Templating/interpolation of the file contents (store verbatim).
- A `--description-file` for `edit` (could be a fast-follow; note it but don't build here unless cheap
  to share the same helper).
- Any change to how descriptions are stored/rendered.

## Design notes

- Put the read-and-validate logic in ONE place (library `create_ticket` or a small shared helper) so
  CLI/MCP both delegate — do not reimplement file reading per surface (this repo already has a
  cross-session-duplication problem; don't add to it).
- Decide the precedence/exclusivity rule explicitly and test it: passing both `--description` and
  `--description-file` is a usage error (exit non-zero), not a silent winner.
- `-` (stdin) is valuable for agents/pipes; implement it unless it conflicts with existing stdin use
  on `create`.
- Preserve the file contents exactly (including trailing newline handling decision — document it);
  the gate checks (`clarity_check`/`check_ac`) run on the stored description unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar create <type> <title> --description-file <path>` creates a ticket whose stored
      description equals the file's contents; deleting the file afterward does not change the ticket
      (contents are inlined, not referenced).
- [ ] `--description-file -` reads the description from stdin.
- [ ] Passing both `--description` and `--description-file` exits non-zero with a clear error; a
      missing/unreadable path exits non-zero with a clear message (no traceback).
- [ ] `rebar.create_ticket(...)` exposes the file-path parameter with identical inline semantics and
      mutual-exclusion, and the CLI delegates to it (single implementation).
- [ ] The MCP `create_ticket` tool accepts the file-path argument with the same semantics and a
      documented path-safety rule (no traversal outside the allowed base).
- [ ] Docs (README CLI block, `create --help`, CLAUDE.md) describe the flag and the inlined-not-
      referenced behavior; tests cover file / stdin / missing-file / both-flags-error across CLI,
      library, and MCP.
- [ ] `make lint` + full test suite pass.
- [ ] Agents and users can author multi-line, gate-passing descriptions from a file (or stdin) without
baseline.summary: rebar create accepts a file path for the ticket description (contents inlined)

content.text: # WS1 — Diff context-assembler + base reviewer
## Why

The four-pass code-review gate (parent b744) consumes the shipped review kernel, which needs (a) a `context` string the Pass-2 verifier re-grounds against — for code review that is the DIFF, not plan text — and (b) a Pass-1 base reviewer that always runs and emits the bounded overlay-escalation signal. This story builds those two foundations everything else wires onto.
## What
- A diff context-assembler that turns a `(base, head)` range / unified diff + changed-files list into the kernel `context` string (parallel to plan-review's `assemble_context(...).plan_text`).

- The base code-reviewer finder prompt (front-matter contract) that emits Pass-1 evidence findings AND `recommend_overlays: [{overlay_id, reason}]`, with `overlay_id` constrained to the FIXED overlay-catalog enum (the model cannot invent an overlay; a concrete one-line reason is required).
- The `recommend_overlays` output contract (a registered output schema) so the workflow can read it as a named step output.
## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py` — the diff context assembler. It RE-IMPLEMENTS the minimal git diff-read (the small `_git` / `_changed_from_diff` / orientation / compose helpers) so it is SELF-CONTAINED and does NOT import from `code_review.py` (the to-be-retired single-pass demo). "Reuses the existing diff read" means it follows the same logic/shape, copied — not an import dependency. This keeps WS4's retirement of `code_review.py` from breaking `assemble.py`.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — the OWNED closed `OVERLAY_IDS` enum constant (see starter set below). WS2 adds catalog CONTENT keyed by this enum.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — base reviewer prompt (front-matter `inputs`/`outputs`/`execution_mode`/`dimension`).
- The base reviewer output schema (in `src/rebar/schemas/` + the prompt `outputs:` binding) — a SINGLE structured schema carrying both `findings` and `recommend_overlays` (see Output-wiring below).
- OUT OF SCOPE: the overlay catalog CONTENT itself (WS2), the union/dispatch (WS3).
## Overlay-id ENUM — starter set (WS1 OWNS this; resolves the WS2 cross-dependency + the E2/T8 blocking finding)

WS1 defines the closed `OVERLAY_IDS` enum as a small shared constant (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py`). WS2 authors the catalog CONTENT (overlay finder prompts + `applies_to` globs) keyed by these ids — it adds content, never new ids. The starter set is the 11 specialist overlays drafted on the parent epic:
OVERLAY_IDS = (
"security",        # authn/authz, secrets, injection, unsafe deserialization
"performance",     # hot paths, N+1, allocation, complexity regressions
"i18n",            # localization / encoding / locale-sensitive formatting
"a11y",            # accessibility (UI/markup/ARIA)
"db-migrations",   # schema/data migrations, backfills, expand-contract
"docs",            # user/operator/API docs that must track the change
"supply-chain",    # dependency / lockfile / vendoring / provenance changes
"api-compat",      # public API / wire / CLI / config backward-compatibility
"iac",             # infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/CDK/K8s/Helm/Ansible)
"tests",           # test sufficiency / regression coverage for the change
"llm-prompts",     # prompt/contract/output-schema changes to LLM surfaces

This is the closed vocabulary the base reviewer's `recommend_overlays.overlay_id` is validated against. AC3's drop-test asserts a valid id (e.g. `"security"`) survives and an invalid id (e.g. `"made-up"`) is dropped. The list lives in code (configurable/extensible by adding an id here + WS2 content); the schema enum is generated from it so the two cannot drift.
## Output-wiring — how ONE agent step exposes two named outputs (resolves T1/T3/T8 advisories)
The v3 engine flattens an agent step's structured output dict into `steps.<id>.outputs`, so the TWO named outputs are simply two TOP-LEVEL KEYS of one structured output schema:

- The base step runs with `mode=structured` and `output_schema=code_review_base_output` (a single registered schema) — NOT `mode='findings'` (that path runs `finalize_findings()`, which would discard everything except `findings`, dropping `recommend_overlays`). This is the load-bearing wiring detail.

- `code_review_base_output.schema.json` (registered in `src/rebar/schemas/`) shape: `{ findings: [common.finding], recommend_overlays: [{overlay_id: <OVERLAY_IDS enum>, reason: string REQUIRED maxLength 200}] }`. `findings` required; `recommend_overlays` optional (defaults to empty).

- Downstream the workflow reads `steps.base.outputs.findings` (flows into merge → Pass-2) and `steps.base.outputs.recommend_overlays` (flows into WS3's `overlay_union`). The batch runner aggregates only `findings`; the base reviewer is therefore a STANDALONE agent step (not a batch criterion) so its `recommend_overlays` survives.
## Context-string shape (resolves the E2/F1 advisory)

`assemble.py` produces the kernel `context` string as a structured-markdown composite (the same shape `code_review.py._compose_context` produces, re-implemented here): a `## Changed files (N)` list, a `## Orientation` directory grouping, and a `## Diff` fenced block with the unified diff (capped at a configured char budget with an explicit truncation notice). This string is what `verify_findings(..., context=...)` re-grounds Pass-2 against. The assembler exposes it via a `DiffContext` dataclass (parallel to `PlanContext`) with a property returning this string.
## Coverage-gap note shape (resolves the E1 advisory)

The "coverage-gap note" emitted on base-reviewer failure is a finding-shaped record `{dimension: "coverage-gap", severity: "low", detail: "<why>", reviewer_id: "code-review-base"}` carried in the base step's findings list (so it flows through merge → verify → the verdict's `coverage`/`coaching`, where WS3/WS4 surface it). It is advisory, never a synthetic BLOCK (the base reviewer is recall-side).
## Specifics pinned (plan-review remediation 2026-06)
- **Overlay-id ENUM ownership:** WS1 OWNS the closed enum (above); WS2 authors content keyed by it. AC3's enum validation is fully satisfied within WS1.

- **"CI drift gate" = the existing derived-prompt-index drift check.** Observable in-session: `rebar workflow validate` passes; `python -c "from rebar.llm.prompts import get_prompt; get_prompt('code-review-base')"` resolves; `python -m rebar.llm.prompts regenerate-index` yields no diff.
- **Stakeholder:** the rebar maintainers operating the Gerrit code-gate (and downstream contributors whose changes the gate reviews).

- **Thresholds/limits are config, not magic constants:** the `reason ≤200 chars` bound and the diff char-cap are schema/config values, adjustable without code-shape changes (noted for the T5e advisory).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A diff context-assembler produces the kernel `context` string (the structured-markdown composite above) from a `(base, head)` range or a unified-diff input + changed-files list; unit-tested on a sample diff.
- [ ] `OVERLAY_IDS` is defined as a closed enum constant in `code_review/registry.py` (the 11-value starter set above); the `recommend_overlays` schema enum is derived from it so they cannot drift.
- [ ] The base reviewer prompt is a contract-bearing front-matter prompt that resolves via the prompt library and passes the CI drift gate.
- [ ] The base reviewer's output carries `recommend_overlays`, each `overlay_id` validated against `OVERLAY_IDS`; out-of-enum ids are dropped (not errored), with a test asserting the drop.

- [ ] The base reviewer runs as a STANDALONE agent step with `mode=structured` + `output_schema=code_review_base_output`, so BOTH `findings` and `recommend_overlays` survive as named step outputs (a test reads both); it is NOT a batch criterion and NOT `mode='findings'`.

- [ ] Base-step failure fallback: error/timeout/empty structured output → empty base findings + NO base-driven escalations (Round-B membership = glob-triggered overlays only) + a `coverage-gap` finding note; never auto-BLOCK (the base reviewer is recall-side; deterministic Pass-2/3 still runs on the findings that exist). Offline test asserts it.
- [ ] `assemble.py` has no import from `code_review.py`; a test pins the import path survives the WS4 retirement.
## Plan-review remediation (Round-11, 2026-06-29)

- recommend_overlays output contract PINNED: `{overlay_id: <OVERLAY_IDS enum>, reason: str (REQUIRED, ≤200 chars)}`, carried as a top-level key of the single `code_review_base_output` schema alongside `findings` (see Output-wiring).
- Base-reviewer FAILURE fallback: empty base findings + glob-only Round-B + coverage-gap note; never fail-closed to BLOCK.
- Diff-assembler contract vs WS4: `assemble.py` is a NEW self-contained module under `src/rebar/llm/code_review/` and does NOT import from the to-be-retired `code_review.py`.

baseline.summary: WS1: Diff context-assembler + base code-reviewer (enum-constrained recommend_overlays)

content.text: # WS2 — Overlay catalog + code-review prompts + move-catalog
## Why

The base reviewer (WS1) escalates to SPECIALIST overlays; the gate also triggers some overlays deterministically by file globs. This story authors that catalog (the specialist reviewers keyed by WS1's `OVERLAY_IDS`) plus the per-gate kernel plug-ins (verify preamble + Pass-4 code moves + the `threshold_for` posture resolver) the consumer seam requires.
## What

- The overlay catalog: one finder prompt per `OVERLAY_IDS` member (WS1 owns the enum; WS2 adds CONTENT), each a contract-bearing front-matter prompt. Per-overlay `applies_to` globs live in `criteria_routing.json` (the single source), not the prompt front-matter.
- A code-review verify-prompt preamble that EMBEDS `VERIFIER_RULES_SCAFFOLD` and re-grounds against the diff.
- A code Pass-4 move-catalog: a `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA` instance (each move `{name, template, applies_when}`).
- Code-review criteria routing: EXTEND WS1's `code_review/registry.py` (modeled on `plan_review/registry.py`) with a `threshold_for(criteria)` resolver reading a committed `criteria_routing.json`.
- The `code-review-coach` Pass-4 prompt (selects applicable moves; the kernel renders them).
## OVERLAY_IDS (WS1 owns the enum; restated for self-containment)

`security, performance, i18n, a11y, db-migrations, docs, supply-chain, api-compat, iac, tests, llm-prompts` — the closed vocabulary from `code_review/registry.py`. WS2 adds one finder prompt + one `criteria_routing.json` entry per id; it never introduces a new id.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-<overlay>.md` (×11) + `code-review-verify.md` + `code-review-coach.md` — `category: code-review-pass` (NOT `review`).

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — EXTEND WS1's module (which already holds `OVERLAY_IDS`): add the criteria-routing reader + `threshold_for` resolver, MODELED ON `plan_review/registry.py` (same shape, code_review package). "Parallel to plan_review/registry.py" = same structure, not a separate file.

- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — a COMMITTED routing index (the analog of `plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, which is likewise hand-maintained + read by its registry; NOT auto-generated). A test VALIDATES it (every overlay id present, schema well-formed, secrets/security keys present with `blocking_enabled=False`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py` — the code move-catalog instance.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py` — EXTEND WS1's module: register the `code_review_coach` move-pick contract (alongside WS1's `code_review_base_output`).

- `docs/review-kernel.md` — EXTEND with a "code-review consumer (b744)" section documenting the criteria-routing reader + `threshold_for`, the committed `criteria_routing.json`, the move-catalog, and the `code-review-pass` category separation (captures the novel patterns — the ADR/design-doc the gate requires).
- OUT OF SCOPE: the escalation union + workflow wiring + `gates/code-review.yaml` (WS3); the secrets/security DETECTORS (WS5) — WS2 authors the security overlay PROMPT, not the scanner.
## Threshold-loading mechanism (resolves the G6 BLOCK + the T1/T3/E1 advisories)
Follows the SHIPPED plan-review precedent EXACTLY — thresholds are NOT in any gate YAML:

- Per-criterion ROUTING (`exec` / `applies_to` / `default_posture` / `block_threshold` / `blocking_enabled`) lives in the COMMITTED `code_review/criteria_routing.json` (analog of `plan_review/criteria_routing.json`).

- `threshold_for(criteria) -> (block_threshold, blocking_enabled)` READS that index (as `plan_review/registry.py` resolves `block_threshold`/`default_posture`). Default for an absent key/field: `(0.95, False)`.
- `gates/code-review.yaml` (WS3) holds NO threshold values — it only gates WHICH criteria run via `when:`, like plan-review.yaml's `include_<ID>`.
## Overlay `applies_to` globs (resolves E2/T8/T2 "vocabulary undefined" + the over-broad-glob advisory)

Per-overlay `applies_to` globs are authored ONLY in `criteria_routing.json` (the single source — the analog of plan-review's `applies_at` living in its routing index, NOT in prompt front-matter; this avoids the dual-source drift A5 flagged). Overlays with no precise file signal are ESCALATION-ONLY (empty `applies_to` — they run only when the base reviewer's `recommend_overlays` escalates to them, never deterministically), avoiding firing on every change:
- `security` → `**/auth*`, `**/*secret*`, `**/security/**`, `**/signing*`, `**/*cred*`
- `performance` → ESCALATION-ONLY (no glob — base reviewer escalates; a `**/*.py` glob would fire on nearly every change, A12)
- `i18n` → `**/locale/**`, `**/*i18n*`, `**/translations/**`
- `db-migrations` → `**/migrations/**`, `**/alembic/**`, `**/*schema*.sql`
- `docs` → `**/*.md`, `docs/**`, `**/README*`
- `supply-chain` → `**/requirements*.txt`, `**/pyproject.toml`, `**/package*.json`, `**/*.lock`, `**/Pipfile*`
- `api-compat` → `**/*api*`, `**/schemas/**`, `**/*.proto`, `**/cli*`, `**/mcp_server*`
- `tests` → `**/test_*.py`, `**/*_test.py`, `**/tests/**`
- `llm-prompts` → `**/reviewers/**`, `**/prompts*`, `**/*.prompt`, `**/schemas/*.schema.json`

Calibration of globs + thresholds is DEFERRED. WS2's deliverable is the glob DATA (in `criteria_routing.json`). The deterministic Round-A trigger LOGIC — matching the diff's changed files against these globs to emit `include_<overlay>` flags — is WS3's work (WS3 decides whether to extend the existing `overlay_triggers` op or add a code-review glob-matcher); WS2 does NOT assert that mechanism already exists.
## Relationship to the existing single-pass reviewers (resolves the T1 overlap advisory)

The new `code-review-security` / `code-review-tests` (etc.) overlays are DISTINCT from the single-pass `security.md` / `tests.md` reviewers: the new ones are `category: code-review-pass` Pass-1 KERNEL finders (claim/criteria/evidence/impact shape, fed to the kernel passes), whereas the legacy reviewers are `category: review` (review_result shape) selected by the single-pass route WS4 retires. They do not collide (different ids, different category, different output shape).
## Move-catalog — concrete starter moves + `applies_when` vocabulary (resolves T8/E2)

The move-catalog (`moves.py`) is a `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA` instance, `validate_move_registry`'d at load. `applies_when` tags are drawn from a CLOSED vocabulary = the `OVERLAY_IDS` plus the literal `"always"`. The gate passes `active_triggers` = the union of `criteria` carried by the SURVIVING findings (exactly as plan-review's `pass4_coach` computes `{c for f in surviving for c in f.get("criteria", [])}`); the kernel `coach()` then offers ONLY moves whose `applies_when` overlaps `active_triggers` (or is empty / `["always"]`), and the LLM picks among that applicable subset. Starter moves:
- `extract-helper` — `applies_when: ["always"]` — "Extract the duplicated logic in {subject} into a shared helper."
- `add-regression-test` — `applies_when: ["tests", "always"]` — "Add a regression test covering {subject}."
- `threat-model` — `applies_when: ["security"]` — "Threat-model the change to {subject} (trust boundary, input validation)."
- `add-migration-guard` — `applies_when: ["db-migrations"]` — "Guard the migration in {subject} (expand-contract; reversible; backfill-safe)."
- `bound-the-hot-path` — `applies_when: ["performance"]` — "Bound or memoize the hot path in {subject}."
## Coach prompt output contract + "deterministic render" (resolves T8/F1/E1/A14)

- `code-review-coach` SELECTS among applicable moves and emits move-picks `[{move_id, subject, finding_refs}]` — it authors NO prose. A registered `code_review_coach` structured-output contract (in `code_review/contracts.py`) pins that shape (mirrors `plan_review`'s `_pass4_model`).

- "Deterministic render via the kernel" = the kernel `coach(surviving, registry, *, pick, active_triggers)` substitutes `{subject}` into each picked move's `template`; the LLM only picks, the kernel renders.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One contract-bearing front-matter finder prompt per `OVERLAY_IDS` member; all resolve via `get_prompt(<id>)`. Per-overlay `applies_to` globs (the starter set above; `performance` escalation-only) live in `criteria_routing.json` (single source), not the prompt front-matter.
- [ ] A code verify preamble (`code-review-verify.md`) embeds `VERIFIER_RULES_SCAFFOLD` and re-grounds against the diff.

- [ ] A code move-catalog (`moves.py`) validates against `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA` at load (`validate_move_registry`), each move carrying `applies_when` from the closed `{OVERLAY_IDS ∪ "always"}` vocabulary.
- [ ] The code-review registry exposes `threshold_for(criteria) -> (block_threshold, blocking_enabled)` reading `criteria_routing.json` (modeled on `plan_review/registry.py`).

- [ ] `criteria_routing.json` is committed (per-criterion `exec`, `applies_to`, `default_posture`, `block_threshold`, `blocking_enabled`); a test validates every `OVERLAY_IDS` member has an entry and the schema is well-formed.
- [ ] `threshold_for` BEHAVIOR is tested: a default criterion → `(0.95, False)`; the secrets/security keys exist with `blocking_enabled=False`; an unknown criterion → the default.
- [ ] The `code-review-coach` prompt is authored with a registered `code_review_coach` move-pick contract; a test asserts the kernel `coach()` renders a picked move's template deterministically.

- [ ] `docs/review-kernel.md` gains a "code-review consumer (b744)" section documenting the criteria-routing reader + `threshold_for`, the committed `criteria_routing.json`, the move-catalog, and the `code-review-pass` category separation (captures the novel patterns).
## Plan-review remediation (Round-11 + Round-12)

- WS2→WS5 threshold handoff: WS2 OWNS `threshold_for` + ALL criterion keys, shipping the secrets + High-Critical-security keys with `blocking_enabled=False`; WS5 flips EXACTLY those two to `True`. Recorded in `criteria_routing.json`; a test asserts the keys exist with `blocking_enabled=False`. Neither story ships a value the other silently assumes.
- `criteria_routing.json` is a COMMITTED, hand-maintained routing index (the plan-review precedent), validated by a test — NOT auto-derived by a script (that overpromise is removed).

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Push a v* tag (v0.7.0) → release.yml runs.
2. Build + Publish to PyPI succeed.
3. The `github_release` job fails in ~6s.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** the job creates the GitHub Release for the tag.
- **Actual:** step fails with `failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` (exit 1). GitHub Actions run 28763401143, job "Create GitHub Release".
## Root cause

The `github_release` job only runs `actions/download-artifact` then `gh release …`. It never runs `actions/checkout`, and sets no `GH_REPO`, so the `gh` CLI has no repository context and tries to infer it from a local git repo that isn't there.
## Fix

Set `GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` in the step env (lighter than a full checkout; `gh release create/view/edit/upload` and `--generate-notes` all work against the API with GH_REPO set). Introduced by change 314 (ticket f112-6222-e236-4b09).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` `github_release` step sets `GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` (or checks out the repo) so `gh` has repo context.
- [ ] The next tag-triggered release creates the GitHub Release automatically without the git-repository error.
- [ ] v0.7.0 GitHub Release exists and is marked Latest (created as a one-off since PyPI 0.7.0 is immutable and the tag workflow cannot be safely re-run).

baseline.summary: release.yml github_release job fails: gh needs repo context (not a git repository)

# op-cert: remove the legacy HMAC scheme (contract phase) via expand-contract migration

## Why
Once the producer signing seam ships (the expand phase: producers mint Ed25519 op-certs, the read
path accepts both envelopes and legacy HMAC records), the HMAC scheme is dead weight for op-cert
kinds — and leaving it verifiable keeps a forgeable path alive (anyone holding a clone's symmetric
secret can mint a "certified" verdict). This contract phase removes HMAC signing AND verification
for the op-cert kinds (`plan-review`, `completion-verifier`), completing the migration begun in
the foundation epic. The producer-key fork this story previously carried is settled in the epic's
"Producer-signing & compute-runtime design resolution" (fork A: every environment signs locally
with its own Ed25519 key) — this story only removes the legacy path.

**Hard dependency (not yet on `main`):** the producer signing seam story (the expand phase) and
the op-cert stack (Gerrit changes 649/650/660, in review) must land first — the asymmetric
producer path this story contracts onto does not exist on current `origin/main`; enforced by the
`depends_on` link and the dependency-gate AC below.

## What
- Remove the HMAC registration for the op-cert kinds from `src/rebar/attest/hmac_legacy.py` /
  `attest/registry.py` `POLICY` so neither `plan-review` nor `completion-verifier` resolves the
  `HMAC-SHA256` scheme. Shared functions are enumerated explicitly — changed vs untouched:
  - **changed**: `signing.sign_manifest` (the expand phase's dual-shape window closes: the HMAC
    branch for op-cert kinds is deleted, envelope-only); `hmac_legacy` op-cert kind
    registrations (deleted); the op-cert read path (HMAC records for these kinds no longer
    verify); `sign_result.schema.json` tightened to envelope-only for these kinds.
  - **untouched**: `signing.compute_signature` (generic HMAC utility), the `.signing-key`
    genesis and its non-op-cert consumers (`rebar init` seeds it; generic manifest verify), and
    the authorship kind. `.signing-key` removal is explicitly OUT of scope.
- Read path post-contract: a pre-existing HMAC attestation reads as **not-certified** (validity is
  computed on read) — it is preserved in the event log, never rewritten. Re-issue = re-run the
  gate (`rebar review-plan` re-signs the current plan; re-closing re-earns the completion cert).
- MCP surface: `sign_manifest` / `verify_signature` operate exclusively on the op-cert seam for
  these kinds; their docs/help updated.
- **Migration artifact** `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md` (a named observable artifact):
  `## Expand` (the producer-seam story: write-new/read-both) and `## Contract` (this story)
  sections, the cutover procedure (upgrade order: reconcile hosts first, per the store rollout
  rule — older clones preserve-and-ignore envelope events and `fsck` WARNs), the re-issue
  procedure for still-live HMAC attestations, and the rollback posture (required-environment
  policy is opt-in and defaults off; absent `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` /
  `verify.require_environment` unset keeps low-security behavior).
- No flag-day break: tickets whose HMAC attestation goes stale simply re-earn certs on their next
  gate run; closed history is untouched.

## Scope
- In: HMAC removal for op-cert kinds, read-path contract behavior, the migration doc, MCP-surface
  updates, tests below.
- Out: the authorship kind (already asymmetric, identity epic); the DSSE/SSHSIG substrate; the
  trusted service (ee0b) and its IaC; any trusted-env policy change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dependency gate: the asymmetric producer path is verified present before any removal — an
      import check plus an end-to-end op-cert sign/verify smoke test pass on the branch this
      story builds on; recorded as the story's first verification step.
- [ ] A test asserts no code path signs an HMAC operation-cert: the `plan-review` /
      `completion-verifier` kinds no longer resolve the `HMAC-SHA256` scheme in
      `registry.POLICY`, and `signing.sign_manifest` has no HMAC branch reachable for these
      kinds (`compute_signature` and `.signing-key` remain for non-op-cert consumers).
- [ ] A test asserts no code path ACCEPTS an HMAC operation-cert: a pre-existing HMAC-signed
      attestation for either kind reads as not-certified post-contract (preserved in the log,
      never rewritten), and re-running the gate re-issues a valid Ed25519 op-cert on the same
      ticket.
- [ ] `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md` exists, is non-empty, and contains `## Expand` and
      `## Contract` sections plus the cutover (upgrade-order) and re-issue procedures; a test
      asserts existence, non-emptiness, and both section headings.
- [ ] The authorship kind (`rebar.authorship.v1`) and any non-op-cert HMAC consumer are untouched;
      a test asserts authorship verification still passes post-removal.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.
baseline.summary: op-cert: remove legacy HMAC scheme (contract phase) + expand-contract migration

## Why
`canonical_tracker` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:81-84`, `os.path.realpath`) is the lock-path
anchor that guarantees a symlinked-path caller and a real-path caller contend on the **same**
`.ticket-write.lock` / `.ticket-write.lock.d` (`acquire` canonicalizes at `lock.py:289`).
VALIDATED: zero test references `canonical_tracker`; the invariant is untested.

## What
Add a test proving that two independent acquirers — one addressing the tracker by its real
path, the other by a symlink to it — mutually exclude, in BOTH directions.

Determinism (no sleep race): the two acquirers are two independent `acquire()` calls, each
opening its OWN file descriptor (fcntl leg) and attempting its OWN `os.mkdir` (mkdir leg).
Per the Linux `flock(2)` contract, separate `open()` descriptions to the same file contend
even within one process, and `os.mkdir` fails `EEXIST` on an existing dir regardless of
process — so holding the lock via one path makes the second acquirer via the OTHER path
deterministically fail. The second acquirer uses `timeout=1, attempts=1` (a bounded 1s
budget); because the lock is genuinely held, it is GUARANTEED to exhaust that budget and
raise `LockTimeout` — a deterministic outcome, not a timing race that a slow runner could
flip. Teeth: were `canonical_tracker` not resolving the symlink, the two paths would key
different lock files, the second acquire would SUCCEED, and the `LockTimeout` assertion would
fail — so the test genuinely exercises the canonicalization invariant.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` — add the symlink/realpath lock-identity tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Holding the lock acquired via the REAL path, a second `acquire()` via a symlink to the
      tracker raises `LockTimeout` (blocked); after release, the symlink caller acquires.
- [ ] The reverse direction (hold via the symlink, contend via the real path) also raises
      `LockTimeout`, then succeeds after release.
- [ ] Both tests are deterministic (bounded `timeout=1, attempts=1`; the block is guaranteed
      by a genuinely-held lock, not by sleep timing).
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Add canonical_tracker symlink/realpath cross-process lock-identity test

baseline.description:
# Code-grounding evidence oracle (v1: T0+T1 floor) — polyglot, deterministic, fail-open, pure-evidence

## Context

Both the plan-review gate (`5fd2`) and the three-pass code reviewers (`9da1`) need to GROUND findings in the
actual code — deterministically, polyglot, and fail-open. This epic builds that shared capability ONCE as a
reusable internal library so the two review efforts don't implement it twice.

It is a **pure EVIDENCE oracle**: it returns evidence (outcome + structured reason + provenance/coverage) and
NEVER decides block/advisory — that policy lives entirely in the consuming code (out of scope here). Every
wrapper FAILS OPEN: unsupported language / missing tool / crash / timeout → an `abstain` with a recorded reason
(never a false accusation), so coverage is honest and a client who doesn't adopt it pays nothing.

Buy-vs-build was checked: **no reusable WHOLE exists** (the AI-review field is closed-SaaS, verdict-emitting,
fail-CLOSED, FP-minimizing — the opposite posture). The gap is benign: the underlying pieces are mature and
reusable, so this epic is a **thin integration over reused backends** plus the novel contract. We reuse
aggressively at the backend layer and build only the integration + the evidence/abstain contract.

## The contract (locked)

- **Three-valued, confirm-only.** Every probe returns `resolved` OR `abstained(reason)` — and on the resolution
  lane the resolved verdict is **`refuted`** (we found it → the agent's absence claim is a false positive),
  never an asserted absence. You can't prove an absence; you can only DISPROVE an asserted one. So the oracle
  reduces false positives; it never manufactures confirmations.
- **Structured abstention reason + coverage** (SMT `unknown`-with-reason model): `abstain(reason = unsupported_lang
  | no_tool | parse_error | timeout | ambiguous | private_or_internal_suspected | network_error | rate_limited
  | version_skew | invalid_detector | other)`. The enum is CLOSED on the load-bearing reasons (no open `…`):
  `version_skew` (the #1 real failure) and `invalid_detector` (a project detector failing validation) are
  first-class; `other` is the explicit catch-all. Skips are recorded so callers can report coverage. Fail-open
  is the IRONCLAD invariant.
- **One normalized evidence model; SARIF at the edges.** Internally one finding/evidence shape across all
  backends; SARIF 2.1.0 is used for interchange/ingest (OpenGrep emits it) but our three-valued model is a
  superset (SARIF has no native `refuted`/`abstain`/coverage), mapped to/from SARIF at the boundary.
- **Reference-in contract.** The oracle does NOT extract references from prose (non-deterministic → consumer's
  LLM job). It checks EXPLICIT, structured references the review agent emits; deterministic extraction FROM CODE
  (parse a diff/file) is an optional in-scope helper. Separate candidate-generation (recall, model-driven) from
  verification (precision, deterministic) — the oracle is strictly the verification side.

## Three jobs over a full repo checkout

1. **Refute an asserted absence** (resolution lane). Given a structured reference (import/symbol/dependency a
   reviewer claims is hallucinated/invalid), try to DISPROVE it against the repo + its declared deps.
   - **v1 = a deterministic T1 floor** = a **universal-ctags** repo-wide tags index (164 langs, no server, no
     build) for symbol/definition existence + plain file-path existence + manifest/registry dependency existence
     (T0). (grep-ast is NOT a repo-wide indexer — it is a per-file AST-context grep; the repo-map/tags machinery
     lives in *aider*, not the package — so grep-ast is at most an optional context-display helper, NOT the
     index. Spike: docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/.) LSP/SCIP semantic resolution is **T2 — deferred** to
     `850f` (servers/builds, non-deterministic).
   - **The T1 `refuted` verdict is SCOPED to name-existence** (bare symbol / import name / dependency name — the
     high-base-rate hallucination class). Member/attribute/signature resolution (`foo.bar` on a type) and
     common-name-collision cases are coarse at T1 and **abstain to T2** rather than risk a false-refute. (Spike
     on a 4-language fixture: 100% yield, 0 false-refute, clean fail-open — but only for distinct names; yield is
     re-measured on a real corpus in the eval, not asserted.)
   - There is NO single off-the-shelf polyglot fail-open resolver (GitHub stack-graphs is ARCHIVED; multilspy
     needs servers; SCIP needs builds) — so job 1 is a TIERED resolver we orchestrate; universal-ctags is the
     always-available floor that makes day-one fail-open achievable.
2. **Self-declared applicability detection** (Engine B). Deterministic "does review dimension X apply to this
   repo?" triggers (is-web-project / has-IaC / touches-auth), STRUCTURAL not naive-grep, more reliable. A
   detector's own applicability declaration IS the deterministic trigger (`5fd2`/`9da1` overlay routing).
3. **Smell / architectural-decay scans** (Engine B). LOW-threshold attention routers that FLAG AREAS for an LLM
   to inspect closely — recall-oriented, not blocking. (scc/lizard size/complexity feeds this + plan-review P4.)

Jobs 2 and 3 are the SAME machine (run declarative patterns over the repo, emit matches); the only difference
is what the consumer does with a match (consumer policy, out of scope).

## Reuse map (confirmed)

- **Engine B backend = OpenGrep** (the permissive LGPL-2.1 fork of Semgrep — engine AND rules, 30+ languages,
  JSON+SARIF). Its custom + project-local rule loading IS the registry substrate — reuse it; do NOT re-invent a
  match DSL. This also dissolves the Semgrep-rule licensing trap (Semgrep CE's Rules License is non-OSI). ast-grep
  is an optional lighter secondary matcher.
- **Detector format = thin envelope + verbatim native payload** (Trivy model), NOT a cross-compiler (Sigma's
  compiler half is overkill for our inverse case). A detector = `{id, metadata, languages/applicability,
  severity-hint, backend discriminator, evidence-mapping}` + a native matcher payload (OpenGrep rule | ast-grep
  block | manifest predicate | metric threshold) passed through unchanged.
- **Job 1 floor = universal-ctags** repo-wide tags index (deterministic, no server; 164 langs). tree-sitter (via
  tree-sitter-language-pack, ~306 grammars) backs structural/detector parsing. grep-ast is NOT an indexer
  (per-file context only) → optional display helper, not the floor. **Reject** MegaLinter/Super-Linter/pre-commit
  as Engine B (CI runners, fail-closed, not embeddable). **Avoid** stack-graphs (archived).
- **Metrics = scc / lizard** as a metric matcher type.
- **Interchange = SARIF 2.1.0**; our evidence model is the superset.

## Registry conventions (from prior-art convergence)

- Built-in (official, shipped) detectors + **project-local detectors auto-discovered from `.rebar/detectors/`**,
  unioned at load; **namespaced** built-in vs project IDs; **last-wins / explicit override**; project config
  expresses deltas only (enable/disable/severity per ID, per-path globs); absent dir = no error (fail-open).
- **Applicability = self-declared + file-presence routing** (Trivy/MegaLinter) — absent language/files → skipped
  silently+cheaply (the polyglot + optional property, for free).
- **Fail-open = each backend in a recover/timeout boundary** (golangci-lint `analyzeSafe`): crash/absent/
  version-skew → skip + RECORD it (the visible skip IS the coverage record; never a silent no-op).
- **The recover boundary is rebar's, NOT the engine's.** Spike finding: OpenGrep/semgrep ABORTS the whole run on
  a schema-invalid rule (exit 7) rather than skipping it — so rebar's loader must **pre-validate + quarantine**
  each detector (recorded `abstain(invalid_detector)`) BEFORE invoking the engine. (Target-file parse errors are
  different — the engine skips-and-continues those.)
- **Fail-open spans out-of-process AND in-process backends.** Out-of-process tools (ctags, ast-grep, OpenGrep,
  scc/lizard, registry HTTP) are reaped via the subprocess pattern (`acli_subprocess`: process-group,
  SIGTERM→SIGKILL, timeout). In-process bindings (tree-sitter) CANNOT be bounded that way — a thread/signal
  timeout can't interrupt a hung C-extension call and a segfault would kill the host — so **prefer the CLI form
  of every matcher** (all have one) and run any unavoidable in-process binding inside a **worker subprocess**.
- **Version skew is the #1 real failure** — pin/record each backend version; mismatch → `abstain(version_skew)`.
- v1 distribution = built-in + `.rebar/detectors/` only; a shareable rule-pack registry/lockfile is DEFERRED.
- Detector discovery/loading is owned HERE; the project-config file convention is COORDINATED with `55de`
  (config tool/UX), not blocked on it. This layer is NOT a duplicate of `3156` (project-supplied LLM criteria).

## Polyglot & optional (must-holds)

- Polyglot, not Python-indexed: tree-sitter tags across grammars (not Python `ast`); purl ecosystems for deps
  (npm/PyPI/crates/Go/Maven/RubyGems/NuGet); multi-framework web detection (React/Vue/Angular/Svelte + Rails/
  Django templates); detectors carry a `languages`/`applies_to` field so a rule never fires on the wrong stack.
- Optional & non-impacting: gated behind an optional extra; core stays import-clean (the existing optionality CI
  gate); a non-adopting client pays nothing — engines aren't imported, any query fails open to abstain/no-op.

## Language support — ownership (R-7: we own the common case; the user owns the long tail; fail-open under both)

- **We own the common case (user does nothing).** The bundled engines already cover the overwhelming majority:
  universal-ctags (164 langs) + tree-sitter-language-pack (~306 grammars) — e.g. a COBOL project resolves out of
  the box (ctags ships `Cobol`; the grammar pack ships `cobol`). OpenGrep covers ~30 langs natively + a `generic`
  text mode.
- **The user owns the genuine long tail — via the engines' NATIVE extension mechanisms, surfaced through a
  documented rebar slot we read.** We never go find or build a parser. For a language no bundled engine parses:
  (a) cheapest — a **ctags optlib** (regex-based `--langdef`/`--regex-<LANG>` in a `*.ctags` file or an
  `--optlib-dir`; no recompile) gives the symbol-existence floor; (b) richer — a **tree-sitter grammar**
  registered the way ast-grep's `customLanguages` does, for structural detectors. The project declares these in a
  rebar config slot (under the `.rebar/` convention, coordinated with `55de`) pointing at the optlib/grammar
  path; the loader passes them through to the engines.
- **Fail-open is the floor under all of it.** A language neither we nor the user configured → `abstain
  (unsupported_lang)` with the coverage gap recorded — never a wrong answer. An unconfigured exotic-language
  project simply abstains on those files; everything else still resolves.

## Plan-review dispositions (round 1 — self-review via the `5fd2` three-pass gate; log `straw-larva-vigor`)

The gate produced 6 advisory findings (0 blocks). Disposition:
- #1/#2 (unvalidated reuse/yield bets) — RESOLVED by an experimental spike (task `risk-leg-churn`;
  docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/): ctags floor = 100% yield / 0 false-refute polyglot; grep-ast corrected
  to universal-ctags (R-A); T1 refute scoped to name-existence (R-B).
- #3 in-process fail-open (R-3), #5 `version_skew` in the reason enum (R-5), #6 configurable metric thresholds
  (R-6), plus the loader-owns-recover-boundary correction (R-C), and the R-7 language-ownership model — all
  folded into this design + the affected children (S1/S2/S4/S6).
- #4 horizontal big-bang (no thin vertical slice before all engines): VALID but **ACCEPTED WITH OVERRIDE** for
  v1 — the engines share one small contract (S1) and the integration risk is judged acceptable here; revisit if
  S5 integration surfaces contract churn.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shared evidence contract (three-valued + structured reason + coverage) + fail-open recover/timeout harness
      + optional-extra scaffolding (import-clean core), implemented and the dependency root for the rest.
- [ ] Engine A refutation resolver (**universal-ctags** T1 floor: file-path + repo-wide symbol-NAME existence,
      confirm-only; member/signature/collision abstain to T2) + the explicit reference-in schema; refutation yield
      + false-refute measured on a real corpus (not asserted); LSP/SCIP + grep-ast-as-index explicitly out.
- [ ] T0 dependency/package-existence (manifest + purl-ecosystem registries) with the abstain gauntlet
      (normalize + workspace/monorepo + stdlib + import-vs-distribution + transient-error → abstain, never absent).
- [ ] Engine B detector registry + OpenGrep evaluator (+ ast-grep secondary, + scc/lizard metric matcher),
      thin-envelope format, project-local discovery, self-declared applicability, SARIF-normalized evidence.
- [ ] Stable public oracle API exposing the three query surfaces + the consumer integration/reference contract,
      consumed by `5fd2` and `9da1`; docs for the API, fail-open behavior, the detector format, and `.rebar/detectors/`.
- [ ] Fail-open conformance suite + polyglot fixture corpus: every backend tested for unsupported-lang / no-tool /
      crash / timeout / version-skew / invalid-detector → `abstain` with coverage recorded; in-process backends
      fail-open under a worker boundary; a non-adopting client is unaffected. PLUS a refutation-yield + false-refute
      eval on a real multi-language corpus (seeded by docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/) so yield is measured.
- [ ] Language extensibility verified: a project-supplied ctags optlib (and/or tree-sitter custom grammar) for an
      otherwise-unsupported language is read from the `.rebar/` slot and used; an unconfigured language fails open.
- [ ] A reusable internal API exposes the three jobs (refute-absence, applies?, smell-scan) over a full repo,
- [ ] Every wrapper fails open: unsupported lang / missing tool / crash / timeout → `abstain` with a recorded
- [ ] Detector registry supports built-in + project-local (`.rebar/detectors/`) detectors via the thin-envelope
- [ ] Consumed by `5fd2`'s DET floor (P2/P3/P4) and the `9da1` reviewers — one implementation, not two.
baseline.summary: Code-grounding evidence oracle (v1: T0+T1 floor) — polyglot, deterministic, fail-open, pure-evidence

baseline.description:
# Review-bot Gerrit comment truncates findings silently (no ellipsis, no "N more" note)

## Context / Problem

Found incidentally while investigating ticket 368a (Gerrit line breaks — closed as not_a_bug). NOT the reported bug there; filed separately.

`src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:117-125` builds the blocking-finding comment the review bot posts on a Gerrit `-1`. Two silent truncations:

1. `adapter.py:122` — `detail = str(f.get("finding", "")).strip().replace("\n", " ")[:240]`. A finding longer than 240 chars is clipped mid-sentence with NO ellipsis or marker, so the author cannot tell the text was cut. Verified by execution: a 690-char finding produced a 271-char line ending mid-token with no `…`.
2. `adapter.py:120` — `for f in blocking[:10]`. With more than 10 blocking findings the rest are dropped with no "N more" note, so the comment understates how much must be fixed.

This matters because the comment is the actionable artifact for a blocked change: a truncated finding can be unactionable, and a hidden overflow reads as "that's all of them".

## Why this is a defect

The codebase has its own convention for marking truncation: `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:440` emits an explicit `… n unchanged line(s) …` marker. The same module truncating without a marker is inconsistent with that established pattern. The rebar-debug protocol's own guidance is the general principle: a bounded output must not read as complete when it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- A finding clipped at the length cap ends with an explicit marker (e.g. ` …`) so the reader knows text was removed.
- When more than the per-comment cap of blocking findings exist, the comment states how many were omitted (e.g. "… and N more").
- The full detail remains discoverable (the cap stays — the point is disclosure, not raising the limit).
- Existing review-bot comment tests keep passing; the marker is asserted by a new test.

## Notes

Low priority / UX. Confirmed by reading `adapter.py:117-125` and by executing the formatter with an over-length finding. Real posted bot comments observed in the wild are short (<=63 chars), so this triggers only on verbose blocking findings.
baseline.summary: Review-bot Gerrit comment truncates findings with no ellipsis or overflow note

# Logging substrate: named loggers + NullHandler + stderr entrypoint handlers + stdout-purity test

Foundational, lands FIRST — you cannot log a swallowed exception into a handler that does not exist, and
the print->logging migration depends on this. No `except` changes in this ticket (zero behavior change to
error handling); this only stands up the logging plumbing and the contract guard.

## What
- Establish the named-logger convention: modules use `logging.getLogger(__name__)` under the `rebar` root.
- Add `logging.getLogger("rebar").addHandler(logging.NullHandler())` in `src/rebar/__init__.py` (library
  hygiene — quiet by default).
- Install a **stderr** `StreamHandler` at ALL THREE entrypoints: the CLI `main` (`src/rebar/cli.py` /
  `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`), the MCP `main` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:main`), AND the reconciler
  subprocess `main` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:main`). Never target stdout.
- **Reconciler logger namespace (plan-review G4):** the reconciler is a THIRD subprocess entrypoint and its
  modules use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, so its loggers resolve under the **sibling** root
  `rebar_reconciler.*`, NOT under `rebar`. A `NullHandler` on the `rebar` root does NOT cover it. So also add
  `logging.getLogger("rebar_reconciler").addHandler(logging.NullHandler())` in
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` and wire the stderr handler in that subprocess's `main`,
  or diagnostics migrated there (sweep `colder-bugle-rake`) are dropped/last-resort-formatted — inverting SC2.
- Add a stdout-purity contract test: `rebar list --full` stdout is pure parseable JSON and diagnostics go
  to stderr (guards the reconciler's `json.loads(subprocess stdout)` contract at `reconcile.py:472`).
- Document the convention in the logging module's docstring (this docstring IS the convention reference).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/__init__.py` adds a `NullHandler` to the `rebar` root logger.
- [ ] CLI entry (`src/rebar/cli.py` / `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`) installs a stderr `StreamHandler`.
- [ ] MCP entry (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` `main`) installs a stderr `StreamHandler` (never stdout).
- [ ] Reconciler subprocess entry (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` `main`) installs a stderr
      `StreamHandler`, and `_engine/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` adds a `NullHandler` on the
      `rebar_reconciler` root logger (it is a sibling of `rebar`, not under it).
- [ ] A new test asserts `rebar list --full` stdout parses as JSON and a forced diagnostic appears on stderr.
- [ ] No `except` body is changed; `make lint` + full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Logging substrate: named loggers + NullHandler + stderr entrypoint handlers + stdout-purity test

baseline.description:
Add plan-review criterion T15 "overlay-derisk" so plans prove risky runtime mechanisms via a fast out-of-loop experiment BEFORE committing them into a slow, codified delivery loop (CI/CD, IaC apply, provisioning pipeline). Motivation: on infra epics, basic failures (a service that won't boot, a credential that doesn't authorize, a dependency that won't connect, a readiness check that never passes) are discovered only at the END of a long delivery cycle. No existing criterion rewards front-loading those checks into a cheap local run or a manual probe against the real target. This is a CORE built-in change (not project-specific), stack-agnostic (no hardcoded Terraform/docker), routed by the self-gating Pass-1 finder like the other Txx overlays.

## The finalized T15 rubric (design of record)

OVERLAY — apply only when ALL of the following hold; else PASS not-applicable.
- S1 Codified loop? the mechanism is delivered/validated by pushing through an automated pipeline or an environment/infrastructure apply, not by running or unit-testing code directly.
- S2 Slow or costly pass? one pass through that loop is slow (minutes-to-hours) or otherwise costly to run.
- S3 Runtime-only correctness? the change introduces behavior whose correctness only resolves when it actually runs in a realistic environment (boots, authenticates, connects, is authorized, passes readiness) — unreachable by static/unit checks.

When applicable, report a finding for each check not satisfied:
- (a) RISK NAMED — the plan identifies the specific mechanism(s) confirmable only by completing the full loop.
- (b) FAST OUT-OF-LOOP PROOF — for each named risk, the plan commits to proving it via the fastest feedback path available for that mechanism, outside the slow loop: running the unit locally/emulated where feasible, OR a manual experiment directly against the real target (an interactive call, a one-off CLI/console action, a probe script, a throwaway resource) where local reproduction isn't possible. The experiment is concrete and returns a verdict in minutes, not a delivery cycle. An unnamed "we'll verify" / "we'll check after deploy" does not satisfy it.
- (c) PROVE-THEN-CODIFY — the cheap experiment comes before committing the mechanism into the slow loop, so the loop validates an already-proven mechanism.
- (d) SCOPED CLEANUP — throwaway experiments are cleaned up afterward, with teardown that removes ONLY the artifacts the experiment itself created (the records a probe inserted, the scratch resource it spun up) and touches nothing pre-existing, shared, or persistent; a cleanup step that could delete, reset, or truncate a resource the experiment did not create (e.g. dropping an existing table or wiping a bucket to "reset" it) fails this check.

ANTI-FP: a manual experiment against the real target is a fully valid proof — never penalize choosing it over local reproduction; many stacks cannot be reproduced locally. A mechanism already proven elsewhere in the codebase needn't be re-proven.

Facet ~ empirical / approach-soundness; exec AGENT (it ground-checks that the named mechanism and named experiment are real/plausible against the codebase). Posture (advisory vs blocking) and block_threshold are NOT decided here — set by the normal registry/review process.

## Required companion change: T10 boundary partition
The de-risk (transient experiment) phase and T10's production-hardening phase must not overlap; there is no runtime cross-criterion suppression by design. Fix by partitioning in T10's own rubric text — add a scope clause: "This overlay evaluates the DURABLE infrastructure — the IaC/config that persists. Transient, throwaway experiments used to de-risk a mechanism before committing it — their creation, isolation, and teardown — are out of scope here." (T10 does NOT name T15 or any other overlay.)

## Acceptance criteria (epic closes when)
- All child tickets are closed.
- `rebar explain T15` renders the criterion; `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` regenerates docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md with a T15 section and the criteria-guide/registry validators pass.
- The writing-a-passing-plan guide instructs authors to de-risk out-of-loop before slow delivery loops.
- The coach-move decision (add or reject the proposed out-of-loop-proof move) is recorded.
baseline.summary: Add plan-review criterion T15 (overlay-derisk): prove risky mechanisms out-of-loop before slow delivery loops

# Stage-2 bounded LLM pairwise overlap judge (advisory findings + suggested link commands)

## Why
Precision lives in stage 2, not in a similarity threshold. The recall spike (epic experiment comment) showed retrieval recall is excellent BUT flagged precision-at-scale as the residual risk (same model produces query+doc digests → vocabularies converge → near-duplicates converge too). This judge IS that precision mitigation: a bounded LLM pairwise classifier over the ~K stage-1 candidates.

## What — output schema (fully specified, DIRECTED)
Output `overlap_verdict` (register in `contracts.py`): `{relation: enum, shared_artifact: string|null, confidence: number, abstain: bool}`, `relation ∈ {duplicates, supersedes, depends_on, related_distinct, unrelated}` (CLOSED). The judge is prompted with an ORDERED pair (First, Second) and its `relation` is read DIRECTIONALLY as "First `relation` Second" (e.g. `supersedes` ⇒ "First supersedes Second"; `depends_on` ⇒ "First depends_on Second"). Only `duplicates|supersedes|depends_on` are surfaceable; the `rebar link` relation set is the 6 built-ins (`blocks, depends_on, relates_to, duplicates, supersedes, discovered_from`) — the judge only ever emits the three surfaceable ones.
- Both orderings run: ordering-1 = (Q=query, C=candidate) → r1 = "Q r1 C"; ordering-2 = (C, Q) → r2 = "C r2 Q". AGGREGATION (fail-safe toward "distinct"; each side must cite a non-null `shared_artifact` and both `confidence >= overlap_conf_threshold`, else downgrade to `related_distinct`, not surfaced; an `abstain:true` in EITHER ordering also downgrades and consumes no surface slot):
  - **`duplicates` (symmetric):** surface iff r1 == r2 == `duplicates`.
  - **`supersedes`/`depends_on` (DIRECTIONAL):** surface iff exactly ONE ordering asserts the directional relation and the other is DIRECTION-CONSISTENT (not the same label pointing the other way). Concretely, r1 ∈ {supersedes,depends_on} is surfaced as "Q r1 C" only if r2 does NOT assert the reciprocal "C r1 Q" (r2 ∈ {related_distinct, unrelated, or the inverse}). If BOTH orderings assert the same directional label with opposite subjects (r1="Q supersedes C" AND r2="C supersedes Q"), that is a self-contradiction → downgrade to `related_distinct` (not surfaced). This resolves the inverted-`link_command` ambiguity: the surfaced direction is taken from the single ordering that consistently asserts it.
- Surface ≤ `overlap_surface_cap` (default 3) highest-confidence results: `{source_id, target_id, relation, shared_artifact, confidence, link_command}`. The `link_command` uses the DIRECTED pair: for a directional relation, `rebar link <source_id> <target_id> <relation>` where (source→target) is the asserting ordering's (First→Second) — so "Q supersedes C" ⇒ `rebar link Q C supersedes` and "C supersedes Q" ⇒ `rebar link C Q supersedes` (never both). For symmetric `duplicates`, canonicalize the pair by sorted ticket-id so the command is deterministic: `rebar link <min(Q,C)> <max(Q,C)> duplicates`.
- K candidates → 2K judge calls (both orderings), flat in corpus size.
- Errors: LLM timeout/error/malformed output on a candidate → treated as `abstain` (dropped), logged; never raises to the caller.

## Config (LLMConfig, not VerifyConfig) — with explicit `from_env` wiring
`overlap_conf_threshold: float = 0.7`, `overlap_surface_cap: int = 3` on `LLMConfig`
(`src/rebar/llm/config.py`, `[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — LLM tunables;
`_config_schema.py` reserves `llm.*`, so NOT `VerifyConfig`. **`from_env()` MUST be edited**
(it constructs `LLMConfig(...)` reading every field via a helper): add module constants
`DEFAULT_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD = 0.7` / `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP = 3`, the two dataclass
fields, and in `from_env`'s `return cls(...)`:
- `overlap_conf_threshold=_llm_float(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD", "overlap_conf_threshold", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD)`
- `overlap_surface_cap=_llm_int(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP", "overlap_surface_cap", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP)`

(`_llm_float` is added by S2 wood-heedless-sheldrake, a sibling — if S2 has not landed in the
stack yet, this story adds it, mirroring `_llm_int`.)

## Dependencies
S5 (`OverlapCandidate` interface + query/corpus digests). Consumed by S7. (S5 is a sibling story; a codebase grep won't find `OverlapCandidate` until it lands.)

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py` + rubric prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md` (`execution_mode: single_turn`, `outputs: overlap_verdict`, `category: overlap`) whose body MUST encode: the CLOSED 5-value `relation` classification ({duplicates, supersedes, depends_on, related_distinct, unrelated} — only the first three surfaceable), the require-a-cited-shared-artifact gate, the both-orderings instruction, and the abstain-when-unsure criterion.
- `overlap_verdict` schema `src/rebar/schemas/overlap_verdict.schema.json` + `register_contract("overlap_verdict", <builder>)` at the bottom of `contracts.py` (co-located with `response_model_for`, guaranteeing registration before use). WIRE the schema in `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` (`OVERLAP_VERDICT = "overlap_verdict"`, `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["overlap_judge"] = OVERLAP_VERDICT`, add to `__all__`) so `test_every_schema_file_is_wired` passes.
- **Deliverable — labeled fixtures:** `tests/fixtures/overlap_pairs/` with ≥12 labeled pairs (each `{a_digest, b_digest, gold_relation}`), COMMITTED as part of this story (consumed by `test_judge_precision_recall`).
- Config field wiring in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (enumerated above).
- OUT: retrieval (S5), wiring (S7).

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` (FakeRunner): `test_agree` (both agree+artifact → surfaced); `test_disagree_downgrade`; `test_requires_artifact` (null artifact → not surfaced); `test_abstain_dropped` (no slot consumed); `test_cap` (≤ surface_cap); `test_link_command` (valid relation string); `test_directional_link_command` (for `supersedes`/`depends_on`, the emitted `link_command` uses the asserting ordering's source→target direction — `rebar link Q C supersedes` NOT `C Q`; and a both-orderings-same-directional-label contradiction downgrades to `related_distinct`); `test_duplicates_canonical` (`duplicates` command uses sorted-id pair, deterministic); `test_llm_error_abstain` (no raise); `test_config` (sets `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_SURFACE_CAP`, asserts `LLMConfig.from_env()` resolves both from the env — proving `from_env` wiring, not just defaults).
- Precision/recall check as a PYTEST FIXTURE test (NOT the prompt-eval harness — no registered scorer exists for the `overlap_verdict` shape): `test_judge_precision_recall` (a deterministic UNIT test: a FakeRunner returns canned per-pair `overlap_verdict`s over a LABELED fixture of ≥12 pairs at `tests/fixtures/overlap_pairs/`, no live LLM) computes precision AND recall and asserts precision ≥0.8 AND recall ≥0.6 (the recall floor stops an abstain-everything judge from trivially passing). Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py::test_judge_precision_recall`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Judges both orderings, aggregates by the stated rule; `pytest ...::{test_agree,test_disagree_downgrade}`.
- [ ] Surfaces only with a non-null `shared_artifact`, else `related_distinct`; `::test_requires_artifact`. Abstain drops without consuming a slot; `::test_abstain_dropped`.
- [ ] ≤ `overlap_surface_cap` (default 3) findings, each `{source_id, target_id, relation∈{duplicates,supersedes,depends_on}, shared_artifact, confidence, link_command}`; the `link_command` is DIRECTED correctly (directional relation uses the asserting ordering's source→target; `duplicates` uses sorted-id canonical pair); `::{test_cap,test_link_command,test_directional_link_command,test_duplicates_canonical}`.
- [ ] LLM error on a candidate → abstain, logged, no raise; `::test_llm_error_abstain`.
- [ ] Fixture test `test_judge_precision_recall` (≥12 labeled pairs) asserts precision ≥0.8 AND recall ≥0.6; `::test_judge_precision_recall`.
- [ ] `overlap_conf_threshold` (0.7) and `overlap_surface_cap` (3) are read from the env by `LLMConfig.from_env()` (explicit wiring, `_llm_float` for the threshold); `::test_config`.
baseline.summary: Stage-2 bounded LLM pairwise overlap judge (advisory findings + suggested link commands)

content.text: The plan-review gate's deterministic check **P2 ("resolution") abstained `no_repo_root`** on the normal `attested` CLI/library path, so the LLM plan-completeness findings could not be code-grounded and landed as `indeterminate / reason: no-verification` (validity 0, severity none) instead of being verified into advisory or dropped. The verdict still computed (PASS when 0 blocking), but the review was running effectively blind to the code.
## Root cause (proven via joe-debug, runtime evidence)

There is no single authoritative resolver for the gate's *code read-root*; it was threaded ad-hoc across five hops (`review_plan → produce_plan_review_verdict → run_workflow → StepContext → workflow op → assemble_context`) and dropped to `None` at the workflow boundary. The det-floor op `plan_review_precheck` called `assemble_context(tid, repo_root=None)` with no `cfg`, so `PlanContext.repo_root` was `None` and `det_floor.p2_resolution` abstained `no_repo_root` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227`). The degraded/step-budget-fail path ran the det floor on the *original* ctx (which had `repo_root`), which is why a step-budget-failed run showed P2 **pass** — the inconsistency fingerprint. Runtime evidence: `precheck(repo_root=None)` → abstain `no_repo_root`; `precheck(repo_root=<dir>)` → P2 ran (11 refs, 9 resolved).
## Reproduction Steps
1. From the repo venv: `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50 rebar review-plan <task-id> -o json`.
2. Inspect `coverage.det.P2` → before the fix: `{"status": "abstain", "ran": false, "reason": "no_repo_root"}`.
3. Observe the LLM findings come back as `indeterminate` with `reason: "no-verification"`.
- **Expected:** in a gate run an attested snapshot is active (origin/main HEAD by default), so P2 runs against it (`ran: true`) and findings are code-grounded.
- **Actual:** P2 abstains `no_repo_root`; findings are parked as `no-verification` indeterminate.
## Fix (class-level, not just the immediate bug)

Centralize code-read-root resolution into a single resolver and use it at the assembly seam, so the "None → silent degrade" class is eliminated and the snapshot defaults to origin/main HEAD cleanly when nothing is specified:

- `rebar.llm.config.resolve_code_root(repo_root=None, *, cfg_repo_path=None, allow_checkout_fallback=True)` — cascade: explicit `repo_root` > `cfg.repo_path` > active attested snapshot (`current_code_root`, origin/main HEAD by default) > live checkout. Default never returns None; `allow_checkout_fallback=False` yields snapshot-or-None for lightweight builders that must not force a checkout root (which would induce cache writes).

- `orchestrator.assemble_context` resolves the `PlanContext.repo_root` **field** via the resolver (`allow_checkout_fallback=False` → snapshot-or-None) — so EVERY workflow det-floor/grounding op picks up the active snapshot, while the op's `repo_root` ARG (the ticket-store read-root) is untouched.
### Key invariant: code read-root vs ticket-store read-root are DISTINCT

The workflow's `repo_root` is the **ticket-store** read-root (it reaches `assemble_context`'s `rebar.show_ticket(repo_root=…)` via `StepContext`) — NOT the code read-root, which is a separate snapshot (`cfg.repo_path`/`current_code_root`). Threading the *code* snapshot through the workflow `repo_root` breaks ticket reads ("Ticket not found"), because the ticket store is not under the .git-less code snapshot. `produce_plan_review_verdict` therefore passes its ticket-store `repo_root` through UNCHANGED (a NOTE documents this); the code root is resolved at the `assemble_context` seam, and the agentic verifier reads code via `cfg.repo_path`.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single `resolve_code_root` resolver exists with the documented cascade; never returns None by default; `allow_checkout_fallback=False` returns snapshot-or-None (unit test `test_resolve_code_root_cascade` covers all four levels + the None branch).
- [ ] `assemble_context` no longer yields `PlanContext.repo_root=None` when an attested snapshot is active; off-gate callers (no snapshot, no cfg) keep `None` (no checkout-write regression).

- [ ] The code read-root and the ticket-store read-root are kept distinct: `plan_review_precheck` grounds P2 against the active code snapshot WITHOUT hijacking the ticket-store root, and `produce_plan_review_verdict` passes the ticket-store `repo_root` through unchanged (never substitutes `cfg.repo_path`) — regression tests assert both, with a mutation check.

- [ ] A real `rebar review-plan` in attested mode reports `coverage.det.P2.ran == true` (not `no_repo_root`) and findings are grounded (the `no-verification` indeterminate set collapses). Verified: verdict PASS, P2 ran (11 refs, 9 resolved), indeterminate findings 6 → 1.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean; the plan_review/workflow/config unit suites pass with no repo-root leak-guard failures.

baseline.summary: Plan-review gate: P2 abstains no_repo_root on attested path; centralize code-root resolution

content.text: ## Summary

Epic dark-acme-lumen (#98) added the kind-keyed `state['attestations']` projection in `reducer/_processors.py:process_signature`, but did NOT bump `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` in `reducer/_cache.py` (still 3). A build WITHOUT the attestations projection (e.g. an older global `pipx` install) writes a version-3 `.cache.json` that lacks `attestations`; a newer build sharing the same `.tickets-tracker` then serves that stale cache (matching dir_hash) and reports NO attestations.
## Impact

The plan-review CLAIM gate (`require_plan_review_for_claim`) verifies STRICTLY from `state['attestations']['plan-review']` (signing.verify_signature(kind=...)). A stale cache makes a genuinely-certified attestation read as 'unsigned', so `rebar claim` is BLOCKED on a validly-reviewed ticket. Observed live on b744 (the legacy `signature` mirror + `verify-signature` certify fine; the kind-keyed map is absent until the cache is deleted and the ticket re-reduced). Affects any mixed-build environment (the dogfood checkout's local build + the global pipx build / MCP server / hooks).
## Reproduction Steps
1. Earn a plan-review attestation on a ticket with a build that has the attestations projection.
2. Have an older build (no attestations projection, same `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION=3`) read the ticket (writes a stale cache).
3. `rebar claim <id>` -> 'no certified plan-review attestation (signature: unsigned)' despite `verify-signature` certifying.
Expected: a projection change invalidates prior caches (claim succeeds on a certified ticket).
Actual: stale cache served; claim wrongly blocked.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` is bumped whenever the reduced-state projection changes (bump it for the attestations addition), so caches written by a build with different projection logic are never served.
- [ ] A test asserts that a ticket carrying a signed plan-review SIGNATURE event reduces to a populated `state['attestations']['plan-review']` even when a pre-projection `.cache.json` is present.
- [ ] Workaround documented for mixed-build checkouts (delete `.cache.json` / single-build env).
## Notes

Discovered while implementing the code-review epic (b744). Workaround in use: delete the ticket's `.cache.json` immediately before `rebar claim`. NOT fixed here (out of scope for the code-review capability).

baseline.summary: Reducer cache not invalidated by kind-keyed attestations projection (stale .cache.json hides state['attestations'])

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Two tickets A, B bound to Jira with a `blocks`/`relates_to`/`depends_on` link present BOTH locally and as a Jira issuelink.
2. Remove the link locally: `rebar unlink A B`.
3. Run a reconcile pass.
**Expected:** the Jira issuelink is removed to match local; the unlink sticks.
**Actual:** the local unlink is silently reverted every pass (outbound `_diff_links` is ADD-only -> Jira keeps the link -> inbound `_diff_links_inbound` re-adds it locally).
## Root Cause

Same asymmetric-clear class as parent-detach: both link differs are ADD-only (`outbound_differ.py:983-1040`, `inbound_differ.py:440-514`); the applier has no remove-link path (`batch_dispatch.py:554-595`) and acli has no delete-link method.
## Design (consumes the shared managed-ref gate from parent story safe-luge-nog)
Make link removal LOCAL-AUTHORITATIVE via the shared, compaction-surviving managed-ref provenance gate:

- Outbound `_diff_links` emits a REMOVE for a Jira link of a mapped type, absent locally, ONLY when the ref is in `managed_refs` (deliberate unlink) — a never-managed Jira link is left for inbound ADOPT, never clobbered.
- New acli `delete_relationship(from_key, to_key, link_type)` (treat 404-on-already-gone as success).
- `batch_dispatch.update_one` routes the REMOVE through it, guarding HTTP errors non-fatally.
- Same-pass suppression: when outbound emits a link REMOVE for to_key, suppress the inbound link-ADD for that target (remove-wins) so local wins.
- NO inbound-remove dual (keeps links local-authoritative, consistent with parent).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_diff_links` emits a managed-ref-gated REMOVE for a Jira link absent locally; a never-managed Jira link emits NO remove (adopted inbound instead).
- [ ] New acli delete-relationship method removes a Jira issuelink; 404-on-gone treated as success; unit-tested.
- [ ] `batch_dispatch.update_one` applies the link REMOVE, HTTP errors non-fatal.
- [ ] Same-pass suppression drops the inbound link-ADD echo of an outbound link REMOVE.

- [ ] Regression tests (RED->GREEN, mutation-checked): local-unlink of a managed link emits an outbound remove and is not re-added inbound; a never-managed Jira link is adopted not removed; survives a compaction boundary.

baseline.summary: Issue-link/dep REMOVAL churn: same asymmetric-clear pattern as parent-detach (both differs ADD-only)

content.text: Restrict Gerrit Submit (landing) to authorized contributors, and add RebarBotNava.
## Why

Previously the project.config only restricted label *voting* to bots+admins; the Submit permission was inherited from All-Projects, so any Registered User holding the inherited grant could land a change once the bots voted MAX. We want only authorized contributors (or admins) to land; non-contributors may still propose (push refs/for/*) but must not be able to submit regardless of gate status.

- Add an exclusive Submit ACL on refs/heads/* in infra/gerrit/project.config granting submit to Contributors + Administrators only (exclusiveGroupPermissions = submit), mirroring the pushMerge exclusive-override technique.

- Document the contributor-authorization requirement in CONTRIBUTING.md.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] RebarBotNava is in Contributors and NOT in Administrators
- [ ] A plain Registered User / Service User cannot submit; can still push refs/for/*
