## Context / Problem
The anthropic cache breakpoint sits on the WHOLE system block (`anthropic_cache_instructions=True`, src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:39-52), so only byte-identical full system prompts share a cache entry. The Pass-2 verifier currently places the plan in the USER message, so its system block gets no plan-bearing cache benefit at all; moving the plan into the verifier's system prompt enables (a) within-pass reuse across the verifier's chunked calls (every chunk of one verify step shares one identical system prompt → one cache entry, written once and read per chunk) and (b) cross-run reuse strictly within Anthropic's ephemeral cache TTL (~5 min) — a best-effort bonus for rapid re-verifies of an unchanged plan, not a reliability guarantee. Byte-identity of the shared leading prefix across Pass-1 and both verifier prompts is enforced as a SINGLE-SOURCE STRUCTURAL INVARIANT (one code seam emits the prefix) — it positions the prompts for provider-side prefix reuse and prevents drift, but the plan does NOT claim it creates a shared cache entry between finder and verifier within one run (those system prompts still differ past the prefix under the whole-block breakpoint). Today the two passes render through different paths with no shared plan-bearing prefix: Pass-1 finder builds its system prompt via `passes._resolve_system` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:276-292) = `_SHARED_PREAMBLE` (passes.py:264) + the rendered finder template, whose `{{plan}}` sits at the template END (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_finder.md:30-31, no volatile marker); Pass-2 verify runs via the workflow `RunnerAgentStep` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:245) → `prompts.resolve_prompt_cached` (src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:380-405), which splits at the `<!--volatile-->` marker (plan_review_verifier.md:173 / plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:181 — the agentic arm is the primary production path) and routes the rendered `{{plan}}` into the USER message; the per-run finding listing arrives separately as `base_instructions` (the `instructions` output of `plan_review_verify_inputs`, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:363-395). So the Pass-2 system prompt never contains the plan, and no plan-bearing prefix is shared across passes. The codebase's cache floor is `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:49 — the Opus 4.8 minimum used by the warmup logic at pass1.py:222,496), which this change adopts as its threshold (NOT the older 1024 figure). Separately, incremental-depth BLOCK loops need an exhaustiveness directive in the shared reviewing stance.

## Approach
Byte identity by construction, single-sourced in code — no template gains a variable that any renderer cannot supply. (1) **`prompts.py` gains the single source**: a module constant `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE` (the text of `passes._SHARED_PREAMBLE`, moved verbatim, PLUS one new bullet — the exhaustiveness directive: "When surfacing findings, enumerate EVERY independent defect you find in THIS run; do not defer deeper or additional findings to a later review round.") and `shared_plan_prefix(plan: str) -> str` returning `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE + "# Plan under review (verbatim, whole)\n" + plan + "\n\n"`. Placement rationale: passes.py is at 798/800 LOC (the hard cap) and cannot absorb the builder; prompts.py is the natural home because it already owns the `VOLATILE_MARKER`/`split_volatile`/`resolve_prompt_cached` cache-prefix seam that `shared_plan_prefix` extends (prompts.py:349-405), and it stays stdlib-only. (2) **Pass-1 rule, exact**: `passes._SHARED_PREAMBLE` is DELETED. `_resolve_system(prompt_id, plan, cfg)` renders the template with variables `{"plan": plan, "shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan)}` (strict rendering only requires USED variables — prompts.py:321-330 — so the superset is harmless to every template), then returns `prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan) + strip_volatile_marker(rendered)` when `prompt_id == PASS_FINDER`, else `prompts.SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE + strip_volatile_marker(rendered)` (byte-equal to today's behavior, modulo the added directive bullet, for EVERY else-branch caller, enumerated: container, ISF, completion, coach, novelty (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:153 and src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:157), contradiction (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py:200), and comment-trail (xcheck.py:338) — none of these templates is restructured, so the else branch handles them with no caller change; __init__.py, eval_solver.py, and xcheck.py are AUDITED, no change). `plan_review_finder.md` drops its trailing "# Plan under review …\n{{plan}}" block (stance-only template; no marker added — the prefix boundary is explicit in code). Container/ISF/completion/coach templates are NOT restructured (their `{{plan}}` stays at the template bottom; separate prompt_ids and cache entries). The directive lives in the preamble, so it reaches EVERY Pass-1 request (finder chunks, container, ISF) and, by byte-identity, the verifier prefix too, where its "when surfacing findings" phrasing is inert. (3) **Verifier templates**: both `plan_review_verifier.md` and `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` begin their body with a `{{shared_prefix}}` line followed by the existing stance text unchanged, and DELETE the trailing `<!--volatile-->` + "# Plan under review …\n{{plan}}" block entirely. With no marker left, `split_volatile` takes its no-marker path (prompts.py:361-363): the WHOLE rendered template is the stable system prompt and `instructions` = `base_instructions` (the per-chunk finding listing stays user-turn — unchanged mechanism). Neither verifier declares front-matter `variables:`, so the contract change is exactly "used var `plan` → used var `shared_prefix`" under the legacy strict path; no parity-gate front-matter edit is needed. (4) **How `shared_prefix` reaches the live variable map — the exact seam**: `plan_review_verify_inputs` (workflow_ops.py:363) returns `{"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix(pctx.plan_text), "instructions": [...]}` — its `plan` output key is REMOVED (its ONLY consumers are the two verify `with:` lines being replaced, plan-review.yaml:182 and :293; the prerequisite step at yaml:149 reads a DIFFERENT step, `plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs`, untouched); `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verify_inputs_output.schema.json` (`additionalProperties: false`) correspondingly drops the `plan` property, adds `shared_prefix` (string, required), and its top-level + per-property descriptions are rewritten to name `{{shared_prefix}}` (no stale `{{plan}}` text remains); and BOTH verify steps in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (the agentic arm's `verify` at line ~177 and the single-turn arm's at line ~288) replace `plan: ${{ steps.verify_inputs.outputs.plan }}` with `shared_prefix: ${{ steps.verify_inputs.outputs.shared_prefix }}` in their `with:` blocks. `runs.py` needs NO edit: `RunnerAgentStep` already merges every string-valued `with:` input into the render variables (runs.py:204-207), so `shared_prefix` flows to `resolve_prompt_cached` through the existing generic mechanism — runs.py is an AUDITED consumer with zero changes. (5) **Every renderer of the verifier templates, enumerated**: (a) `RunnerAgentStep` — covered by (4); (b) `fidelity_spot_eval.py` — `plan-review-verifier` is REMOVED from `RELOCATED_PROMPTS` (fidelity_spot_eval.py:46-54, comment updated): the verifiers no longer carry the split marker so they are no longer "relocated" prompts, `test_relocated_prompts_all_carry_the_split_marker` (tests/unit/test_fidelity_spot_eval.py) then passes over the remaining entries, and no committed corpus renders a verifier (`RELOCATED_PROMPTS`/`relocation_spot_eval` have no consumers outside the module + that test; the unit-test corpus uses `completion-verifier` only), so `_relocation_requests` never sees `{{shared_prefix}}` and needs no change; (c) `passes._resolve_system` — supplies both variables per (2) (live code never calls it with the verifier ids; the bespoke pass2 was retired in epic solid-timer-unison WS1); (d) direct test renderers, each updated to supply `shared_prefix` (or drop `plan`): tests/unit/test_prompt_cache_split.py (THREE updates: remove the two verifier ids from `_MARKED_PROMPTS`; rewrite `test_bespoke_plan_review_path_strips_marker_and_keeps_plan_in_system` to the finder prefix invariant with this exact contract — `sys_prompt = passes._resolve_system(passes.PASS_FINDER, "PLAN-XYZ-marker-test", cfg); assert sys_prompt.startswith(prompts.shared_plan_prefix("PLAN-XYZ-marker-test")); assert "PLAN-XYZ-marker-test" in sys_prompt; assert prompts.VOLATILE_MARKER not in sys_prompt`; and rewrite `test_verify_step_prefix_is_byte_stable_across_plans` (tests/unit/test_prompt_cache_split.py:177-196) to supply `"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix("PLAN-ALPHA-aaa")` (resp. BETA) in place of `"plan"` and INVERT its expectations to the new contract — each verifier system prompt now CONTAINS its plan (`"PLAN-ALPHA-aaa" in r1.system_prompt`), the two system prompts DIFFER (`r1.system_prompt != r2.system_prompt`), each starts with its own `shared_plan_prefix`, and `instructions` carries only the base_instructions since the volatile body is gone), tests/unit/test_reviewer_prompt_hygiene.py (`test_resolve_system_preamble`, tests/unit/test_reviewer_prompt_hygiene.py:80-97: REMOVE `passes.PASS_VERIFIER` from the loop — no live bespoke verifier caller exists post-solid-timer-unison WS1, and keeping it would render a doubled preamble (the `_resolve_system` prepend PLUS the preamble embedded in the template's `{{shared_prefix}}`); the remaining ids keep asserting the stance leads the plan body), tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_live_plumbing.py (`test_runner_agent_step_resolves_plan_for_verify`: the StepContext inputs replace `"plan": "..."` with `"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix("## Plan\nBuild X in src/x.py.")`; the coach variant of the test is unchanged — the coach template keeps `{{plan}}`), tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_verify_recovery.py (`_verify_ctx`, tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_verify_recovery.py:47-62: its hard-coded `"plan": "## Plan\nBuild X in src/x.py."` input becomes `"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix("## Plan\nBuild X in src/x.py.")`), tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py (the `plan-review-verifier` StepContext inputs: `"plan": "P"` becomes `"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix("P")`), tests/external/test_review_kernel_rules_live.py:74-79 (the render call becomes `prompts.resolve_prompt(prompt, {"shared_prefix": prompts.shared_plan_prefix(context)}, repo_root=cfg.repo_path)` — `plan` dropped from the variables dict; the adjacent `strip_volatile_marker` call becomes a harmless no-op and may stay). The `plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml` standing spec references the prompt id but never renders the template offline (tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py validates spec structure only). (e) CONTRIBUTING.md:620 names `_SHARED_PREAMBLE` — updated to `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE`/`shared_plan_prefix` in prompts.py, and the same paragraph gains two invariant sentences for future contributors: the preamble/prefix is single-sourced in prompts.py (never re-inline it in a template), and the verifier templates must not re-introduce a `{{plan}}` variable or a volatile marker (test_shared_prefix.py is the canary). (6) **Pass-1 warm gate measures the ACTUAL prefix**: the finder warm-then-fan-out gate currently tests `det_floor.est_tokens(plan) >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (pass1.py:494-498), but after this change the cached bytes are `shared_plan_prefix(plan)` (larger by the preamble + heading). pass1.py gains a tiny helper `def _prefix_tokens(plan: str) -> int: return det_floor.est_tokens(prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan))` and the gate condition becomes `_prefix_tokens(plan) >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` — consistent with the bytes actually sent. The CONTAINER warm gate (`parent_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, pass1.py:222) is deliberately untouched: the container prompt is not restructured in this change and `parent_tokens` also feeds bin-packing sizing (pass1.py:200-207), which must keep measuring the plan alone. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` itself (pass1.py:49) is unchanged. (7) **No verdict/TTL change**: verify stays per-chunk with merge-by-index; temperature/budget `with:` inputs untouched; no TTL change. Alternatives rejected: raising cache TTL to 1h (pass gaps of 50-100ms never approach the 5-minute refresh-on-hit window; revise loops change the prefix bytes, so the 2x write premium buys nothing); padding the preamble itself past the 4096-token floor without moving the plan (a >4096-token boilerplate preamble adds that many tokens of pure overhead to every call, while the plan bytes are ALREADY sent per pass — making them the cached prefix costs nothing extra).

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py (SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE + shared_plan_prefix), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py (delete _SHARED_PREAMBLE; _resolve_system branch + variables), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_finder.md (drop trailing plan block), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md and plan_review_verifier_agentic.md ({{shared_prefix}} head; delete volatile tail), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py (verify_inputs emits shared_prefix), src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verify_inputs_output.schema.json (add shared_prefix), src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml (both verify `with:` blocks), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py (finder warm gate measures shared_plan_prefix via _prefix_tokens), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py (RELOCATED_PROMPTS minus plan-review-verifier), CONTRIBUTING.md (stale symbol reference + invariant sentences), tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py (new), tests/unit/test_prompt_cache_split.py, tests/unit/test_reviewer_prompt_hygiene.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_live_plumbing.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_verify_recovery.py, tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py, tests/external/test_review_kernel_rules_live.py (updated renderers per Approach 5d). Audited, no change: src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py (generic string `with:`-merge at runs.py:204-207 already carries shared_prefix), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py, src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py (else-branch `_resolve_system` callers, no signature change).

## Testing
New tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py (offline, FakeRunner/no model), against a named in-file fixture plan `FIXTURE_PLAN` built programmatically to exceed the cache floor (the test_pass1_warmup.py:88 approach): (1) `passes._resolve_system(passes.PASS_FINDER, FIXTURE_PLAN, cfg)` and the `resolve_prompt_cached` stable segment of BOTH verifier prompts (rendered with `shared_prefix=prompts.shared_plan_prefix(FIXTURE_PLAN)`) each `startswith(prompts.shared_plan_prefix(FIXTURE_PLAN))` byte-for-byte, and that prefix contains the full plan text; (2) `det_floor.est_tokens(shared_plan_prefix(FIXTURE_PLAN)) >= pass1.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (the imported constant — currently 4096 — so a future floor change re-verifies automatically); (3) the exhaustiveness directive is in `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE` and hence in `_resolve_system` output for PASS_FINDER, PASS_CONTAINER, and PASS_ISF (every Pass-1 entry point); (4) a sentinel finding listing passed as `base_instructions` appears in the returned `instructions` and NOT in the stable system segment, for both verifiers; (5) `not hasattr(passes, "_SHARED_PREAMBLE")`; (6) rendering the verifier prompts through `RunnerAgentStep` with a StepContext whose inputs mirror the yaml `with:` (findings/instructions/shared_prefix) succeeds; (7) the warm gate boundary: a plan built so that `det_floor.est_tokens(plan) < CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS <= pass1._prefix_tokens(plan)` proves the gate measures the prefix actually sent (est_tokens is deterministic chars-based, so the boundary plan is constructible); (8) `_resolve_system` output for a non-restructured pass starts with `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE` exactly once (no doubled preamble). Updated existing tests as enumerated in Approach (5d); tests/external is the opt-in live suite (not a CI gate) — the ACs use offline structural proxies, consistent with the standing eval posture. Regression: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/` then the full `tests/unit` suite; tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py (full-yaml fixture runs) and tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_warmup.py pass UNMODIFIED — verdict and warm behavior unchanged for existing fixtures (the gate change only widens the warm condition by the constant-size preamble).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For the named fixture plan, the Pass-1 finder system prompt and the rendered stable segments of BOTH verifier prompts each begin byte-for-byte with `prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan)`, which contains the full plan material (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py`).
- [ ] `det_floor.est_tokens(shared_plan_prefix(FIXTURE_PLAN))` >= `pass1.CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` (asserted against the imported constant, currently 4096 — pass1.py:49) (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_shared_prefix.py`).
- [ ] The reviewing-stance preamble text exists ONCE, as `prompts.SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE`, and `passes._SHARED_PREAMBLE` is removed (checked: unit test asserting `not hasattr(passes, "_SHARED_PREAMBLE")` and that `_resolve_system` output for a non-restructured pass starts with `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE`).
- [ ] The exhaustiveness directive is a bullet of `SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE` and present in the `_resolve_system` system prompt of every Pass-1 entry point (PASS_FINDER, PASS_CONTAINER, PASS_ISF) (checked: unit test in test_shared_prefix.py).
- [ ] The per-run finding listing remains user-turn (`base_instructions` → `instructions`) and is absent from every rendered stable system segment (checked: unit test in test_shared_prefix.py).
- [ ] `plan-review-verifier` is removed from `RELOCATED_PROMPTS` and every remaining entry still carries the volatile marker (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_fidelity_spot_eval.py::test_relocated_prompts_all_carry_the_split_marker` with the updated tuple).
- [ ] Both plan-review.yaml verify steps supply `shared_prefix` from `verify_inputs` outputs and the live render path resolves without PromptError (checked: unit test rendering via RunnerAgentStep with yaml-shaped inputs; `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py` full-yaml runs).
- [ ] Review verdict behavior on the existing workflow fixtures is unchanged (checked: tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py passes unmodified).
- [ ] The Pass-1 finder warm gate measures the actual prefix: for a boundary plan with `est_tokens(plan) < CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS <= pass1._prefix_tokens(plan)` the warm condition holds (checked: unit test in test_shared_prefix.py), and existing warm behavior is unchanged (checked: tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_warmup.py passes unmodified).
- [ ] `plan_review_verify_inputs` no longer emits a `plan` output and its output schema names `shared_prefix` with no stale `{{plan}}` description text (checked: unit assertion on the step's returned keys + `grep -c '{{plan}}' src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verify_inputs_output.schema.json` returns 0).
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md no longer references `_SHARED_PREAMBLE` and names the new single source (checked: `grep -c _SHARED_PREAMBLE CONTRIBUTING.md` returns 0 and `grep -c SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE CONTRIBUTING.md` returns >= 1).

## Context / Problem
The accepted clarity analysis on ticket e759-c562-e233-4108 identified two structurally unambiguous plan defects that the current length-and-heading heuristic does not reject: empty parsed Acceptance Criteria items and unresolved sentinel assignments in active execution sections. Standalone clarity and deterministic P1 must enforce the same floor without changing ticket-type exemptions or the legacy compatibility score.

## Approach
- Add one pure shared plan-structure helper. Inside the exact `## Acceptance Criteria` section, recognize standard `- [ ]` and `- [x]` checklist items, join every continuation line until the next checklist item or H2 heading, and mark an item defective only when the joined body is whitespace-empty.
- In exact active `## Approach`, `## Scope`, `## Testing`, and `## Acceptance Criteria` sections, scan case-insensitively for the sentinel tokens `TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, and `???`. Ignore fenced code and inline backtick code. A sentinel fires only when it starts a line or bullet, follows `:` or `=`, or follows the word `is`, `remains`, or `left`.
- Suppress a sentinel match when its same line contains a removal or negation term from this exact case-insensitive list: `no`, `zero`, `remove`, `delete`, `reject`, `forbid`, `must not`, `without`. Thus `Backend: TBD`, `TODO — decide cache`, and `status remains ???` fail; `NO stale TODO`, `Remove TODO markers`, and ``mention `TODO` as an example`` pass.
- Wire the shared result into standalone `clarity_check_compute` and plan-review `p1_readiness_shape`, preserving the existing clarity score as compatibility coverage.
- Add focused behavior tests before implementation, including historical negative controls and agreement between the two gate surfaces.

## Scope
- Add `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py` for the shared structural parser and hard-floor result.
- Update `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py` to apply the result to standalone clarity.
- Update `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` to emit blocking P1 findings for the same defects.
- Add `tests/unit/test_clarity_floor.py` for focused unit and cross-surface regression tests.

## Testing
- Run the focused clarity-floor tests during the red-green cycle.
- Re-run existing direct-consumer coverage in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` and `tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py`.
- Run the repository lint, typecheck, and full test gates after the focused suite is green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A standard Acceptance Criteria checkbox whose fully joined body is whitespace-empty fails standalone clarity.
- [ ] A checkbox with a blank first line and a nonblank wrapped continuation passes the nonempty-item rule.
- [ ] Each specified sentinel-as-value form in an exact active execution section fails standalone clarity.
- [ ] Fenced code does not trigger the sentinel rule.
- [ ] Inline code does not trigger the sentinel rule.
- [ ] Ordinary prose mentions do not trigger the sentinel rule.
- [ ] Each specified same-line removal or negation assertion suppresses the sentinel rule.
- [ ] Plan-review P1 blocks on an empty joined checkbox body.
- [ ] Plan-review P1 blocks on an unresolved sentinel assignment.
- [ ] Plan-review P1 passes the historical `NO stale TODO` negative control.
- [ ] Focused tests, direct-consumer tests, lint, typecheck, and the full repository test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Enforce deterministic clarity floors for executable plans

## Why

The eval specs and gold-set expectations assert against criterion PROMPT text. Once the reviewer prompts drop SC vocabulary, any spec still phrased in SC terms is describing a rubric that no longer exists, and the eval solver actively MANUFACTURES the dual vocabulary into every fixture ticket it generates — reintroducing the heading the migration is removing.

## What

Update the eval specs, the eval solver's generated fixture descriptions, and the gold-set expectation strings to the collapsed vocabulary.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-container.eval.yaml:6,91,93,205`
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml:36`
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:317` — currently emits
  `"## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] {etext}\n\n## Success Criteria\n- {etext}"`, i.e. every
  generated fixture carries both headings with duplicated text.
- `tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py:101,382` — expectation strings
  ("del-b's success criteria could be sized into two tasks", "fc1's success criteria could be split").

## Approach

Specs and gold-set strings are straight vocabulary edits. `eval_solver.py:317` drops the trailing `## Success Criteria` block entirely rather than renaming it — the two blocks carried the SAME `{etext}`, so emitting both under one heading would duplicate every criterion.

The gold-set strings are EXPECTATIONS, not inputs: changing them changes what the gold set scores. They are edited only because the underlying rubric wording changed, and the story verifies the gold set still scores as before rather than assuming it.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py tests/unit -k "eval or gold"` green.
- Confirm the gold-set pass/fail tallies are UNCHANGED versus the pre-change baseline, proving
  the edits were vocabulary-only and did not move any expectation.
- Assert a solver-generated fixture description now contains exactly one criteria heading.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ src/rebar/llm/evals/` returns no matches.
- [ ] `grep -n "success criteria" tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py` returns no matches.
- [ ] A solver-generated fixture description contains `## Acceptance Criteria` exactly once and
      no `## Success Criteria`, asserted by a test over `eval_solver`'s output.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The gold-set score tally is identical to the pre-change baseline (recorded in a ticket
      comment before the edit, compared after).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
baseline.summary: Update eval specs, eval solver fixtures and gold-set expectations to the collapsed vocabulary

content.text: ## What
Switch ticket alias generation for NEW tickets from adjective-noun-noun to
adjective-adjective-animal, using a vendored OSS wordlist (gfycat lists from
a-type/adjective-adjective-animal, MIT). Existing tickets are untouched and keep
resolving by their legacy aliases.
## Scope / Design
- New generator `compute_genesis_alias` in `src/rebar/_alias.py`, backed by a new
bundled wordlist `src/rebar/_engine/resources/ticket-wordlist-v2.txt`
(adjectives, `# ANIMALS` marker, animals). The two adjectives are guaranteed
distinct; deterministic off the hex id.
- Wired into the create path only: `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` `_compute_alias`
now calls `compute_genesis_alias`. New tickets persist the alias onto the CREATE
event, locking in the format.
- Legacy `compute_alias` (adjective-noun-noun) + old wordlist are UNCHANGED, so the
read-time backfill for pre-existing tickets is byte-identical (no existing alias
changes).
- License vendored to `docs/licenses/adjective-adjective-animal-LICENSE.txt`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New tickets get a 3-word `adjective-adjective-animal` alias whose two
adjectives differ, deterministic from the ticket id.
- [ ] Legacy `compute_alias` output is unchanged (existing tickets resolve to the
same aliases; pinned literals `real-soil-anger` / `brawny-gill-inlay` still hold).
- [ ] Generator is total + deterministic; too-short (<12 hex) id → None; missing
wordlist falls back to a hex alias with a one-shot WARN.
- [ ] Wordlist sourced from OSS with license vendored; not hand-curated.
- [ ] Tests cover the new format, path independence, and the missing-wordlist fallback.

baseline.summary: Alias generation: adjective-adjective-animal for new tickets (legacy unchanged)

# Rename `verify.overlap_enabled` → `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`, with a permanent alias and a docs entry

## Context / Problem

`verify.overlap_enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:140`) turns on a store-wide, LLM-backed cross-ticket duplicate detector that runs during `review-plan`. The name says none of the four things an operator needs at the config line: overlap of *what*, that retrieval scans the *whole* tracker so the work scales with store size, that it is *advisory* and can never block, and that it rides on `review-plan`. Sitting under `verify.` next to genuinely blocking gates (`require_plan_review_for_claim`, `require_ticket_for_commit`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:133,144`) it actively reads as a gate.

**The documentation gap is the concrete half of the defect, and it is narrower than first reported.** Grepping the tree: `docs/config.md` contains **zero** occurrences of the string `overlap` — so the key has no entry in the config-key inventory that operators actually read. The single mention anywhere in `docs/` is one bullet in an architecture decision record, `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md:64`. For an opt-in feature that spends LLM tokens proportional to tracker size, that is the part most likely to cost someone money or confusion. This repo itself runs with it on (`rebar.toml:39`), so the rename must not break a live config.

## Approach

Rename the field to **`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`**, keep both the old TOML key and the old env var working forever as **permanent aliases**, and add the missing `docs/config.md` entry. The name states the *output* — link suggestions — which is the thing an operator is deciding whether they want, and the `suggest_` prefix carries the advisory nature that `_enabled` does not. It fits because the whole complaint is that the name describes an internal mechanism ("overlap") instead of a user-visible product, and the config inventory is read by operators, not by the retrieval code.

### Why permanent, not scheduled

The deprecation registry records the deciding rule in prose at `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:88-99`: the six `_permanent` entries above it are permanent **because they are RENAMES** — "the same knob under a better name, so removing them would buy nothing" — while `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is `_scheduled` because it is a **supersession by a different interface**. This change is a pure rename: same boolean, same default, same consumers, better name. So both new rows use `_permanent(...)` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:65`), which also picks the right message wording — `_message()` (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:299-306`) emits "is a permanent alias of …" and never claims "deprecated", the contradiction the registry docstring was written to resolve.

### Backward compatibility rides on machinery that already exists

Both alias paths are already built and already tested; this change supplies data, not mechanism.

**TOML key.** `_ALIASES` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:645`) is an **empty** `dict[str, dict[str, str]]` kept explicitly as "the extension point for any future config-key rename window". `coerce_sparse` consumes it at `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:689-695`: for each `old → new` pair present in a section it calls `warn_deprecated(f"cfg:{sect}.{old}")` and rewrites the key, and if the canonical key is *also* present the canonical wins and the legacy one is dropped. So the entire TOML back-compat is one line — `_ALIASES = {"verify": {"overlap_enabled": "suggest_duplicate_tickets"}}` — plus the registry row whose key must be exactly `cfg:verify.overlap_enabled`, because that is the string `coerce_sparse` builds and `warn_deprecated` raises `KeyError` on an unregistered key (`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:329`).

**Env var.** The canonical name is derived mechanically as `REBAR_<SECTION>_<KEY>`, so it changes from `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` to `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS`. `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:295-315`) maps `legacy → (section, key, canonical)`, and `env_overrides` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:340-343`) honours the legacy name **only when the canonical key is unset in that layer**, warning through `warn_deprecated(f"env:{legacy}")`. `_map_legacy_env` needs **no** change: it special-cases only `REBAR_NO_SYNC` and `REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` and returns the value unchanged otherwise (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:319-326`). The config-cache signature already iterates `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` (`src/rebar/config.py:279-280`), so a mid-process change to the legacy var correctly invalidates the cache with no extra work.

Worked example of the two contracts, the thing a reviewer should be able to check by eye:

```toml
# an existing project config — keeps working, emits one permanent-alias notice
[tool.rebar.verify]
overlap_enabled = true              # → resolves to verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets = True

# both set — the canonical key wins, the legacy one is dropped without a warning
overlap_enabled          = false
suggest_duplicate_tickets = true    # → resolves to True
```

```sh
REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1 rebar review-plan <id>          # honored, warns
REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1 \
  REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS=0 rebar review-plan <id>   # canonical wins → off
```

### The three call sites, and one correction to this ticket's own file-impact

Grepping `src/rebar` for `overlap_enabled` returns exactly four hits: the field declaration (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:140`), its `_SECTIONS` coercer (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:528`), and two readers — `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:233` (the opportunistic enrichment drain's feature gate on ticket-write paths) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:765` (the advisory step inside the plan review, with its explanatory comment at `:755-761`). **`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` does not reference the flag** — this ticket's previous file-impact list named it in error, and it is dropped. `src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py` is also **not** edited: `overlap_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py:23`) never reads the flag, it is merely what the flag guards.

### Scope boundary held deliberately

The `[tool.rebar.llm]` tunables `overlap_k` / `overlap_drain` / `overlap_conf_threshold` and friends (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:428-445`) keep their names. They live on `LLMConfig`, a different section with a different audience (they tune the algorithm, they do not decide whether the feature runs), and renaming eleven tunables would turn a one-key rename into a migration. The new `docs/config.md` entry cross-references them by their existing names instead.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — rename the field at line 140 and its explanatory comment at
  lines 134-139; rename the `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer key at line 528; populate `_ALIASES` at
  line 645 with the one `verify` entry.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — two `_permanent` rows in `_ENTRIES` (`:73`): `cfg:verify.overlap_enabled`
  and `env:REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED`.
- `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — one `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` entry (`:295-315`).
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — the read at line 233.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — the read at line 765 and the comment naming the flag at
  line 759.
- `rebar.toml` — this repo's own setting at line 39 and its comment block at lines 32-38.
- `docs/config.md` — the new inventory entry in the `[tool.rebar]` verify block (the block at
  lines 93-110), plus the new permanent env rename added to the Back-compat list at lines 409-419,
  which today enumerates the six permanent renames.
- `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md` — line 64 names the old key; it gains the new name so the
  record stays navigable. The ADR's decision text is otherwise left intact, because an ADR records
  what was decided at the time.
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — add `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (near line 45) and
  `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS` (near line 96); the existing `verify.overlap_enabled`
  (line 45) and `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` (line 96) entries **stay**, because the golden is an
  anti-regression record of surfaces that must remain accounted for.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py` — the four schema assertions at lines 58-60 and 262-265.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` — the attribute set at line 176 and the comment at line 58.
- `tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py` (new) — the alias behaviour.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py`:

- **Happy path (TOML alias)** — `coerce_sparse({"verify": {"overlap_enabled": "true"}})` returns
  `{"verify": {"suggest_duplicate_tickets": True}}`, so an untouched project config still turns the
  feature on.
- **Happy path (env alias)** — with `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1` and the canonical var unset,
  `env_overrides()` yields `{"verify": {"suggest_duplicate_tickets": "1"}}`.
- **Conflict / precedence edge** — with **both** the legacy and canonical TOML keys present the
  canonical value wins and no warning is emitted; with both env vars set the canonical wins. These
  are the two cases the `coerce_sparse` and `env_overrides` code paths branch on and the two a naive
  alias gets backwards.
- **Empty / absent edge** — with neither set, `Config` resolves `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`
  to `False`, proving the default did not move.
- **Message wording** — `warn_deprecated("cfg:verify.overlap_enabled")` returns a string containing
  "permanent alias" and **not** "scheduled for removal", pinning the `_permanent` classification
  rather than just asserting the row exists.

Regression suites this change can break, run explicitly: `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` (its alias accounting at lines 47-56 and 62-70 is what makes the golden tolerate the renamed key), `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py` (registry completeness plus the raw-emission source scan), `tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py`, `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`, and `tests/unit/test_config_show.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is the canonical boolean (default `False`) on
      `VerifyConfig` with its `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer, and `verify.overlap_enabled` is no
      longer a live key; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py` (whose assertions at lines 58-60 and 262-265
      pin exactly the field, the `_SECTIONS` membership and the coercer).
- [ ] An existing project config setting `overlap_enabled = true` still turns the feature on and
      emits a permanent-alias notice; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_toml_alias_resolves`.
- [ ] `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1` still turns the feature on when the canonical var is unset;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_env_alias_resolves`.
- [ ] When legacy and canonical are both set — in TOML or in the environment — the canonical value
      wins; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_canonical_wins_over_legacy`.
- [ ] Both alias rows exist in `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` with `permanent=True` and
      `remove_in is None`, and their message says "permanent alias" rather than "scheduled for
      removal"; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_rows_are_permanent` and by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py`, which additionally fails if any emission
      site bypasses `warn_deprecated`.
- [ ] The two in-source readers (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:233`,
      `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:765`) and this repo's own `rebar.toml:39` use the new
      name, and the only surviving occurrences of the old name are the four back-compat sites.
      The grep must be **case-insensitive**, because two of the four spell the name in upper case
      (the env var) and two in lower case (the TOML key) — a case-sensitive `grep "overlap_enabled"`
      would silently miss the env-alias sites and make this criterion pass while they were wrong.
      So: `grep -rni "overlap_enabled" src rebar.toml` returns exactly these four lines and nothing
      else —
      (1) the `_ALIASES` entry `"overlap_enabled": "suggest_duplicate_tickets"` in
      `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`;
      (2) the `_permanent("cfg", "verify.overlap_enabled", …)` row in `src/rebar/_deprecations.py`;
      (3) the `_permanent("env", "REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED", …)` row in the same file;
      (4) the `"REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED"` key of `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` in
      `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`.
      In particular `grep -rni "overlap_enabled" rebar.toml` returns **zero** lines. Verified by
      running those two greps and by `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` documents the setting: what it produces (up to three advisory
      `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`depends_on` link suggestions), its three stages — the query
      ticket's digest via `enrich`, BM25F retrieval over the whole tracker with the query's own
      graph excluded, then a bounded pairwise LLM judge (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py:41-56`) —
      that it is advisory and NEVER blocks a claim or close, that its cost scales with tracker size
      rather than with the reviewed ticket, and that the algorithm tunables are the
      `[tool.rebar.llm] overlap_*` keys. The entry deliberately does **not** pin a per-stage model
      class, since that routing is being changed by bug `afeb`. Verified by
      `grep -n "suggest_duplicate_tickets" docs/config.md` returning the new entry and by reading
      that the five listed facts are present.
- [ ] The new permanent env rename `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` →
      `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS` is listed in the Back-compat section of
      `docs/config.md` alongside the six existing permanent renames (lines 409-419); verified by
      `grep -n "REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS" docs/config.md`.
- [ ] No config surface is orphaned by the rename: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` carries both
      the old and new key and both env names, and the old ones are accounted for as aliases;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and no file in `src/rebar` exceeds the module-size cap;
      verified by the CI module-size gate.
baseline.summary: Rename verify.overlap_enabled to name what it produces, and document it (it is currently undocumented outside the config schema)

content.text: # ACLI subprocess 429 handling: bounded backoff, honor Retry-After if available
## Context
All ACLI calls go through `_run_acli` (`acli_subprocess.py`), which retries all non-zero exit codes (except
401/assignee) with a uniform 2s/4s sleep. `_call_with_retry` (`dispatch_one.py:100-144`) adds 429/5xx
classification and already raises the EXISTING `RetryExhaustedError` (`_errors.py`). `_call_with_backoff`
(`acli_subprocess.py:236-292`) is dead code (no production call sites; it wraps `urllib`, NOT the subprocess
`CalledProcessError` domain). ACLI is a subprocess, so Jira `Retry-After` availability is UNVERIFIED.
## What (minimal, contract-preserving — a plan, not an implementation)
1. PROBE FIRST: against a rate-limited/staged endpoint, record (a) whether `Retry-After` is parseable in stderr,
(b) the exit code ACLI returns on HTTP 429, (c) whether ACLI retries 429 internally. Record on the ticket.
2. Add 429-aware jittered exponential backoff with a BOUNDED max-retry/total ceiling to the LIVE `_run_acli` retry
loop (so continuous 429s cannot hang the subprocess). Honor `Retry-After` IFF the probe confirmed it; else
backoff without it. If ACLI retries 429 internally, no Python-layer change for 429 (documented).
CONTRACT-PRESERVING: the ceiling only BOUNDS attempts — on exhaustion `_run_acli` raises exactly what it raises
today (`CalledProcessError`). Do NOT introduce or surface a new exception type from `_run_acli`; the 9 call
sites' contract is unchanged. (`RetryExhaustedError` stays where it is, in the app-layer `_call_with_retry`.)
3. Retryable-code scope: ADD-ON (recommended) — the 429 branch REPLACES the uniform sleep for that attempt (no
double-sleep); all other exit codes keep their current retry behavior (zero caller impact). NARROW to
{429,502,503} would break other non-zero codes and is OUT OF SCOPE unless separately decided.
4. `_call_with_backoff` (dead) is OPTIONAL cleanup only, NOT required by this ticket. If a follow-up removes it,
that follow-up also drops its `acli.py:57` import, its `__all__` entry, and the `test_error_taxonomy.py`
reference — but this ticket leaves it untouched.
5. PRESERVE the non-idempotent-write guard (`AcliTimeoutError` is not a `TimeoutError`).
6. Observability: log rate-limit detection, backoff trigger, Retry-After honored-vs-unavailable, ceiling reached.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Probe recorded: Retry-After availability, the 429 exit code, whether ACLI retries 429 internally (+ the Python outcome for the internal case).

- [ ] Bounded jittered exp-backoff added to the live `_run_acli` loop; honors Retry-After IFF probe-confirmed; add-on mode does not double-sleep; on exhaustion the EXISTING `CalledProcessError` contract is unchanged (no new exception surfaced to the 9 callers).
- [ ] Other non-zero exit codes retain current retry behavior (ADD-ON); NARROW is explicitly out of scope.
- [ ] No-blind-retry-on-timeout guard preserved; new backoff covered by a case in `tests/.../test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py`.
- [ ] Rate-limit/backoff/Retry-After/ceiling events logged; the retry policy is captured in an ADR/design note.

baseline.summary: Align ACLI bulk-path 429 handling with the REST path (honor Retry-After)

baseline.description:
## Why

Offline fixtures can establish the rubric's discrimination, but the epic succeeds only when the deployed Gerrit review bot loads the criterion from the reviewed rebar repository and carries it through the real four-pass pipeline. The first rollout must collect evidence without blocking contributors.

A live Gerrit probe is required because only the deployed bot's webhook-to-checkout-to-prompt path can prove end-to-end project-criterion execution; an offline replay would mock or bypass the repository-resolution behavior this story is intended to dogfood.

## What

Run an advisory-only Gerrit dogfood probe after the seam repair and project criterion land. Use one Gerrit change with four sequential patchsets against the review-system prompt surface:

1. A positive control adds this exact discovery/evidence refinement: `Before emitting, isolate
   the shortest changed clause that directs a review phase to act. Name the instructed phase, the
   assigned action, and the phase that owns that action. If the changed text does not identify all
   three, abstain instead of inferring an ownership violation.` The boundary criterion emits no
   finding.
2. Preserve the historical severity-only probe unchanged: `For each candidate finding, assign
   severity as high, medium, or low.` Record that it abstains because it does not identify the
   instructed and owning phases; this is evidence about stimulus limits, not criterion execution.
3. Use the predeclared balanced-corpus FIRE control RP-F2: `Pass 1 sets severity, confidence,
   blocking status, and remediation for every finding.` Capture the project-attributed advisory
   finding and its Pass-2/Pass-3 data.
4. A final patchset removes the FIRE sentence, retains only the valid positive-control refinement,
   and is the sole revision submitted to `main`.

## Preconditions

Before the probe, an operator confirms the configured `gerrit` remote targets rebar's Gerrit and that the deployed review bot posts `LLM-Review` results for this repository. Record the remote URL, change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message on this ticket. If the bot is absent or misconfigured, do not substitute an offline run: create an operational bug linked `discovered_from`, mark this story blocked, and resume only after the live prerequisite is restored. Allow 60 minutes after each patchset upload for its `LLM-Review` message; after that window, follow the same operational-bug and blocked-story path.

For this story, an acceptable review trace is the `code_review_result_v2` payload from the ambient ticket-store artifact titled `code-review: <change-id> @ <revision>`, pasted into a ticket comment. It must contain the reviewed `revision`, `coverage.llm_ran: true`, and the `blocking`, `advisory`, `dropped`, and `indeterminate` lists. The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE probe provides direct project-criterion execution proof: its finding must carry `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`. The positive control is deliberately a comparative observation—same Gerrit change, unchanged routing/bot, LLM coverage present, and no project-criterion entry in any verdict list—not a claim about unavailable per-criterion forwarding counters.

## Scope

- Keep `blocking_enabled: false` for the entire probe. `block_threshold: 0.90` is recorded but
  inert; no change in this story enables blocking.
- Record Gerrit change id, each patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, vote/message, project criterion finding,
  Pass-2 validity/impact attributes, Pass-3 priority/decision/threshold/posture, and final amended
  patchset outcome as ticket comments.
- Confirm the project-only physical prompt id ran against the RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset SHA using
  its stamped `reviewer_id`; compare the positive and cleaned revisions using the same artifact
  schema without claiming a nonexistent execution-count field.
- Leave the repository with only valid review instructions. Threshold calibration and a future
  `blocking_enabled: true` decision require a separate ticket backed by accumulated real-review
  data; this story neither selects a lower threshold nor promotes the criterion.

This story is observational: it does not change the rubric in response to probe results. A rubric or seam defect discovered by the probe is captured as a new ticket linked `discovered_from` and is fixed only through that separately reviewed work.

If the historical severity-only directive abstains, preserve that patchset and trace unchanged. Use only the already-committed RP-F2 balanced-corpus FIRE case as the discriminating follow-up; do not tune or improvise a new probe. If RP-F2 does not produce the project-attributed finding, record the unexpected trace, create a rubric/seam bug linked `discovered_from`, and mark this story blocked.

After the final patchset, post a calibration handoff comment on this ticket with the exact labels `Priority distribution:` and `Blocking promotion: deferred`; the latter must name a future, separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket as the only path to enabling blocking.

Out of scope: changing the rubric, collecting multi-day adoption metrics, changing the impact model, or enabling blocking.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] The Gerrit remote and review-bot precondition is recorded with remote URL,
  change id, patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, and bot vote/message before either probe is evaluated.
- [ ] Before and after all probe patchsets, project routing remains `block_threshold: 0.90` and
  `blocking_enabled: false`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import json; r=json.load(open(".rebar/criteria_routing.json"))["code_review"]["project.review-phase-boundaries"]; assert r["block_threshold"] == 0.90 and r["blocking_enabled"] is False'`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A positive-control Gerrit patchset is recorded with change id, patchset
  SHA, UTC timestamp, and an acceptable artifact payload with `coverage.llm_ran: true`. Routing and
  bot deployment are unchanged across the four patchsets, and no entry in `blocking`, `advisory`,
  `dropped`, or `indeterminate` names `project.review-phase-boundaries` for this valid
  discovery/evidence refinement; entries from unrelated criteria do not affect the comparison.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The historical severity-only patchset is recorded unchanged with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, sentence, and acceptable artifact payload. Its repeated abstention
  and absence from every project-attributed verdict bucket are recorded as a stimulus limitation,
  not treated as proof.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The predeclared RP-F2 FIRE-control patchset is recorded with change id,
  patchset SHA, UTC timestamp, exact corpus sentence, and an acceptable artifact payload. Its
  grounded `advisory` finding carries `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries`
  and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the project-attributed advisory entry's
  observed Pass-2 `validity`, `impact`, and at least two named `verification.binary` answers from
  the persisted artifact. These are observations from the run, not predeclared invariant values.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The ticket comment records the entry's observed Pass-3 `priority` and
  the deterministic routing outcome `decision: advisory`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, and
  `blocking_enabled: false`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] All negative directives are absent from the final submitted patchset, the
  project criterion emits no phase-boundary finding on that revision, and the recorded final
  revision contains only phase-compliant instructions. This fourth patchset of the same Gerrit
  change is the only probe revision submitted to `main`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A ticket comment contains the exact labels `Priority distribution:` with
  the observed Pass-3 values and `Blocking promotion: deferred` with an explicit handoff to a future,
  separately reviewed, data-backed posture ticket.
- [ ] The final cleaned dogfood change is landed on `main`; verify with
  `.venv/bin/python -c 'import subprocess; commits=subprocess.check_output(["git", "log", "origin/main", "--format=%H", "--grep=rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d"], text=True).split(); assert commits, "dogfood commit is not on origin/main"'`.

## Dependencies

Depends on the landed repository-root seam repair `3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5` and the project-criterion authoring story `225a-323c-a9f6-436b`. The former umbrella `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02` and child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` were superseded and closed.
baseline.summary: Dogfood the review-phase-boundaries criterion in advisory Gerrit reviews

content.text: ## Summary

The reducer's strategy layer is dead code: reduce_ticket accepts/defaults LastTimestampWinsStrategy but never calls strategy.resolve, and replay performs NO UUID dedup — duplicate-UUID event files double-apply.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. Create a ticket; rebar comment <id> "only-once".
2. Copy the COMMENT event file to a new filename (same uuid in payload, ts+1s).
3. rebar show <id> -> comments == ["only-once","only-once"].
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected (documented at ticket_reducer/_api.py:31-44): "dedup by UUID (first occurrence wins), sort by timestamp".

- Actual: _processors.py:347-416 replays raw files in FILENAME order, no UUID dedup (only snapshot-source-uuids skipped), sorted by filename timestamp not event timestamp. MostStatusEventsWinsStrategy equally unreachable. Verified: no .resolve( call site in ticket_reducer/.
## Impact
Merge-as-union convergence leans on UUID-level determinism; duplicate-UUID files (recovery cherry-picks, manual copies, fsck-recover paths) silently double-apply comments/edits/links.
## Source
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_api.py:197-244 (unused strategy param/default)
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_processors.py:347-416 (replay loop)
## Fix direction

Decide: (a) wire the strategy into replay (load -> strategy.resolve -> process), or (b) delete the dead strategy classes/param and add a minimal seen-UUID skip in replay_events, documenting filename-order replay. See validation notes comment for measured blast radius of each (incl. test_ticket_reducer_conflict.py interactions) before choosing.
## Suggested RED test
Duplicate-UUID event under a second filename -> applied exactly once; existing conflict-resolution tests stay green.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded: wire-strategy vs minimal-dedup + dead-code deletion
- [ ] tests/scripts/test_ticket_reducer_conflict.py and reducer suites green

content.text: ## Summary

The single-locked write path uses an flock-based lock file `.ticket-write.lock` (and the mkdir lock `.ticket-write.lock.d`). Under flock, the lock file is intentionally NOT unlinked on release (deleting it would race other lockers), so it correctly persists in the tracker working tree after every write. The problem: the tracker `.gitignore` seeded by `rebar init` does not list these lock files, so they surface as untracked files in the `.tickets-tracker` working tree — noising up `git status` and tripping git-cleanliness checks / stop hooks.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Have a tracker worktree on the `tickets` branch (`.tickets-tracker/`).
2. Perform any write, e.g. `rebar comment <id> "..."`.
3. `cd .tickets-tracker && git status --porcelain`
- Expected: clean working tree (lock files ignored).
- Actual: `?? .ticket-write.lock` appears as an untracked file.
## Root cause
- Lock names are defined in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`: `WRITE_LOCK_NAME = ".ticket-write.lock"`, `MKDIR_LOCK_NAME = ".ticket-write.lock.d"`.

- The tracker `.gitignore` is seeded from the `_GITIGNORE` constant in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (~line 29), which lists `.env-id`, `.closure-key`, `.state-cache`, `.scratch/`, `.cache.json`, `*/.cache.json` — but NOT the write-lock files.
## Fix

- Add `.ticket-write.lock` and `.ticket-write.lock.d/` to `_GITIGNORE` in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`, ideally sourced from the `WRITE_LOCK_NAME` / `MKDIR_LOCK_NAME` constants in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` so the ignore list cannot drift from the lock names.

- Existing trackers won't pick up the new entry automatically (the committed tickets `.gitignore` is seeded once in `_commit_gitignore`); define a migration (append on upgrade / `fsck` repair, or a documented one-liner).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_GITIGNORE` in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` ignores `.ticket-write.lock` and `.ticket-write.lock.d/`.
- [ ] On a freshly `init`'d tracker, `git status --porcelain` in the tracker worktree shows no untracked lock files after any write.
- [ ] The ignore entries are kept consistent with the lock-name constants in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (no drifting duplicate literals).
- [ ] A migration path is defined for existing trackers.
- [ ] A test asserts the seeded tracker `.gitignore` ignores both lock files.

baseline.summary: Tracker .gitignore omits write-lock files (.ticket-write.lock[.d]); flock lock surfaces as untracked

# CLOSED — premise disproven by measurement: scaling the verifier's step budget does not help

This epic was filed on the premise that the completion verifier's flat budgets were too small for a large ticket and should scale with the acceptance-criteria count. **That premise was tested and is false.** The epic is closed as disproven rather than decomposed; a correctly premised successor will be filed once the mechanism is identified.

## The disproving measurement

Ticket `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`, closed twice against the same tree, changing only the budget:

| Step budget | Model requests | Wall clock | s/request | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 480 (default) | 240 — hit the ceiling | 780s | 3.25 | none |
| 960 (2x) | 480 — hit the ceiling | 4,492s (75 min) | 9.36 | none |

Doubling the budget bought **zero** progress toward a verdict and 5.75x the wall clock. A run that merely needed more headroom would have finished somewhere inside the doubled budget; instead it consumed the new ceiling exactly as it consumed the old one. Per-request time also nearly tripled, which points at accumulating tool history — each turn re-sends the whole conversation — matching the existing caveat in `docs/llm-framework.md` that raising `REBAR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS` "does not repair repeated tool-history growth".

The conclusion holds regardless of whether the non-convergence turns out to be a tool-level loop or a termination-awareness failure: neither is fixed by a larger budget.

## Findings that SURVIVE the disproof

These were measured while investigating and remain true. They are recorded here so the successor does not re-derive them:

1. A step-budget exhaustion raises `LLMRunnerError` (`runner.py:465`, `raise budget_err from
   exc`), not `UnretryableOutputError`, so it falls through recovery's
   `except UnretryableOutputError` (`completion_recovery.py:405`) and reaches no fallback.
2. The obvious runaway discriminator does not work: `request_limit = ceil(max_iter/2)` vs
   `tool_calls_limit = max(8, max_iter)` (`runner.py:414-417`), so a one-tool-call-per-turn
   loop trips the request ceiling FIRST — indistinguishable from careful sequential work.
3. `_EVIDENCE_CHARS` (12,000 per criterion) vs `_MAX_TOTAL_EVIDENCE_CHARS` (96,000 aggregate)
   is incoherent above 8 criteria, and the aggregate check runs INSIDE the loop AFTER each
   billable call, so a 14-criterion ticket pays for all 14 and then fails with no verdict.
4. Recovery's per-criterion re-send is uncached: the `cache_control` breakpoint is on
   `system_prompt` (`runner.py:330-338`) but the context travels in `instructions`.
5. Recovery is a WEAKER oracle than the aggregate path — its finalizer decides `met` from
   bounded evidence summaries, never raw source — so availability must not be bought by
   routing more traffic to it.
6. There is no wall-clock deadline anywhere in the LLM path; `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S` is
   per-request only. The 75-minute run above was not bounded by anything.
7. `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` has no upper bound and no validation — `999999999`, `0` and `-5` all
   resolve through `_llm_int` unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the premise "scaling the step budget lets a large ticket verify" is tested against the
      motivating ticket at two budgets, and the result recorded above
- [x] the surviving findings are captured on this ticket so a successor need not re-derive them
- [x] no work is decomposed from this epic, because the work it proposed would not have fixed
      the reported problem
baseline.summary: DISPROVEN: scaling the completion verifier's step budget does not make a large ticket verify

# S3 — OIDC / JWKS JWT verifier

## Why
JWKS-backed JWT validation is the "OAuth" half of the confirmed floor and the generic "plug into
any OIDC provider" path — one verifier covers AWS Cognito, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Okta,
Keycloak, WorkOS, Google ID tokens, and GitHub Actions OIDC (all publish a JWKS and issue standard
JWTs). It is the highest-leverage verifier for the "wide variety of environments" goal.

## What
Add a **`JWKSTokenVerifier`** to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, selected by the `jwt` token in
`mcp.auth_strategies`, with flat config keys it registers: `auth_jwt_jwks_uri`, `auth_jwt_issuer`,
`auth_jwt_algorithms` (default `RS256,ES256`), `auth_jwt_leeway` (seconds, default 60),
`auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown` (seconds, default 30), `auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (seconds, default
10), `auth_jwt_expected_typ` (default **unset**), and `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host` (bool,
default `false`). It does **not** take a per-verifier audience — it validates
`aud == auth_resource_server_url` (the single resource from S2). Implemented with PyJWT
(`jwt.PyJWKClient` + `jwt.decode`); add `pyjwt[crypto]` to the `[mcp]` extra (the SDK pin lives in
S1). It validates the signature (pinned algorithms), `iss`, `aud`, `exp`/`iat`/`nbf`, optionally the
header `typ` (when `auth_jwt_expected_typ` is set — see Security), maps `scope`/`scp`→scopes, sets
`expires_at` from `exp` (a real positive value), and stamps `resource=auth_resource_server_url` so
the composite audience check passes. This story registers its keys in `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json` +
regenerates the reference docs.

## Approach & rationale
Use PyJWT's `PyJWKClient` (JWKS fetch + in-process key cache + `kid` lookup) and `jwt.decode` with an
explicit pinned `algorithms` allowlist — PyJWT's documented JWKS path and the same shape FastMCP's
`JWTVerifier` uses, giving provider-generic OIDC validation in a small module on the SDK seam. PyJWT
is already a transitive of `mcp`; `pyjwt[crypto]` makes the `cryptography` backend explicit for RS/ES
verification. **PyJWKClient's `lifespan` is a cache TTL, not an unknown-`kid` flood guard**, so this
verifier implements the unknown-`kid` refetch cooldown itself (see the concurrency-safe design in
Security) rather than relying on the library for it.

**Async-safety of the blocking JWKS fetch.** `PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt()` (and its
underlying JWKS HTTP fetch) is **synchronous/blocking**, but the verifier's `verify_token` runs on
FastMCP's async event loop. The verifier therefore offloads every key lookup / JWKS fetch to a worker
thread via `asyncio.to_thread(...)` so it never blocks the event loop, and it serializes the
cooldown check-and-update with an `asyncio.Lock` (see Security) so the "at most one fetch per
cooldown window" guarantee holds under concurrent requests.

## Scope
The JWKS/JWT verifier only, on the S2 seam. Not introspection/proxy/custom. Subset of the epic.
Depends on S2.

## Security
Boundary-crossing. Hard requirements (RFC 8725 JWT BCP):
- **Algorithm pinning:** reject `alg:none`; never derive the algorithm from the token header. Also
  **refuse to start** if any **symmetric** algorithm is configured in `auth_jwt_algorithms` together
  with a JWKS source (asymmetric-only on the JWKS path) — this blocks the RS256↔HS256 confusion
  attack (signing HS256 with the public key as the HMAC secret). The symmetric set that triggers the
  startup refusal is the closed, explicitly-enumerated family **`{HS256, HS384, HS512}`** (case-
  insensitive); anything outside the asymmetric families `RS*/PS*/ES*/EdDSA` on a JWKS source is
  likewise refused.
- Mandatory `aud == auth_resource_server_url` (RFC 8707), `iss == auth_jwt_issuer`, and `exp`/`nbf`
  with bounded `leeway`.
- **Cross-JWT-confusion `typ` check (configurable, because OIDC providers vary):** when
  `auth_jwt_expected_typ` is set, the JWT header `typ` MUST equal it (RFC 8725 §3.11 — e.g.
  `at+JWT` per the RFC 9068 access-token profile), so an ID token or other same-issuer/same-aud JWT
  cannot be replayed as an access token. It defaults **unset** (check skipped, relying on
  `aud`+`iss`+`scope`) because many IdPs do not stamp `typ` on access tokens; S7 documents that
  operators SHOULD set `auth_jwt_expected_typ=at+JWT` for RFC 9068-compliant IdPs.
- **SSRF-safe JWKS fetch:** `jwks_uri` is fixed at construction from trusted config (never the token
  — no `jku`/`x5u`), **HTTPS-only** (an `http://` URI is rejected at construction), with a bounded
  HTTP timeout given by the named key **`auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (seconds, default `10`)**, passed as
  the `timeout=` argument to `PyJWKClient` so a slow/hung JWKS endpoint cannot stall the verifier.
  Private/link-local hosts (e.g. `169.254.169.254`, RFC 1918, loopback) are **rejected by default**;
  an operator with a legitimate internal IdP sets `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host=true` to opt out.
- **Key rotation without DoS (concurrency-safe):** the JWKS is cached with a bounded TTL; the verifier
  caps refetch on an unknown `kid` to **at most one refetch per `auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown`
  seconds (default 30)** (implemented by the verifier itself, not PyJWKClient's `lifespan`). Because
  `verify_token` runs concurrently on the async event loop, the cooldown's read-check-then-update of
  the last-refetch timestamp is a check-then-act (TOCTOU) hazard; it is therefore made **atomic under
  an `asyncio.Lock`** that serializes the check-and-update, so two coroutines seeing the same
  unknown `kid` cannot both trigger a refetch. Result: an attacker flooding random `kid`s cannot force
  more than one JWKS fetch per cooldown window even under concurrency, while a legitimate rotation
   still refetches after the cooldown.
  **Timestamp-on-failure policy:** the last-refetch timestamp is updated on every fetch *attempt* (success OR failure), not only on success, so a JWKS endpoint that errors cannot be used to bypass the flood guard by making fetches fail. The cost is bounded: a transient JWKS outage delays a legitimate refetch by at most one `auth_jwt_jwks_refetch_cooldown` window (default 30 s), and during that window a fetch failure raises → the composite denies (the request fails regardless), so no invalid token is admitted; operators seeing persistent outages lengthen the endpoint's availability, not this guard.
- A JWKS-fetch failure raises (composite treats as non-acceptance → deny); a definitively invalid
  token returns None. All verify-path errors go through the S2 redaction helper so no token/secret
  substring is ever logged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` adds `pyjwt[crypto]` to `[mcp]`; `make typecheck` resolves the imports.
- [ ] The `auth_jwt_*` flat keys (including `auth_jwt_jwks_timeout`) are registered in
      `MCP_ENV_VARS`/`server.json`, appear in the regenerated reference docs, and
      `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes.
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit against the real verifier; the irreducible boundary — the JWKS HTTP
      fetch — is a stateful fake serving a locally-generated key set) asserts: a JWT with correct
      `iss`/`aud`(=resource) → an `AccessToken` with the expected scopes AND
      `resource==auth_resource_server_url` and an `expires_at` **equal to the token's `exp` claim**
      (observable oracle: returned `AccessToken.expires_at` == the exact `exp` used to mint the JWT,
      not merely a positive value).
- [ ] Unit tests assert rejection for: wrong `iss`; `aud` ≠ `auth_resource_server_url`; expired
      `exp`; `nbf` in the future; `alg:none`; and an `HS256` token signed with the RSA public key as
      the HMAC secret — each a distinct negative control.
- [ ] Unit test asserts that with `auth_jwt_expected_typ=at+JWT` set, a token whose header `typ` is
      absent/mismatched is rejected while a matching one is accepted (observable oracle: accept vs
      reject); and that with `auth_jwt_expected_typ` unset the typ check is skipped.
- [ ] Unit test asserts the verifier **refuses to start** when `auth_jwt_algorithms` includes a
      symmetric algorithm (`HS256`/`HS384`/`HS512`) alongside a JWKS source (observable oracle:
      startup raises).
- [ ] Unit test asserts construction-time SSRF guards: an `http://` `jwks_uri` is rejected; a
      private/link-local host is rejected by default and accepted only with
      `auth_jwt_allow_private_jwks_host=true`; and the JWKS client is constructed with
      `timeout=auth_jwt_jwks_timeout` (default `10` s) (observable oracle: for the SSRF rejections,
      construction raises; for the timeout, the test patches `jwt.PyJWKClient` and asserts it was
      called with keyword `timeout=10` — the concrete default value — so the assertion is exact and
      unambiguous, not merely 'a timeout is passed').
- [ ] Unit test asserts a JWKS **fetch failure raises** (→ composite non-acceptance/deny), distinct
      from a definitively-invalid token which returns None.
- [ ] Unit test asserts unknown-`kid` cooldown is concurrency-safe: a burst of concurrent requests
      with distinct unknown `kid`s within one cooldown window triggers **exactly one** JWKS fetch
      (observable oracle: the stateful JWKS fake's request count == 1 for the burst — not 0, which
      would mean the lock wrongly blocks all fetches, and not >1, which would mean the TOCTOU
      double-fetch was not prevented), while a token signed by
      a rotated key validates after the cooldown elapses (a legitimate rotation still refetches).
- [ ] Integration test (httpx `ASGITransport`) asserts a valid JWKS-issued token → 200 and a
      garbage bearer → 401 end-to-end through the transport.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive verifier, opt-in via the `jwt` strategy. The `pyjwt[crypto]` add is backward-compatible;
the SDK pin already lives in S1.
baseline.summary: S3 — OIDC / JWKS JWT verifier
