baseline.description:
## Context
On 2026-07-27, closing bug `3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5` after both implementation commits had merged exposed a completion-gate reliability failure. The target was an ordinary bug ticket with a ~2.1 KB description and six acceptance criteria. The worktree was clean at landed `origin/main` commit `bc838aed27b6a03e93d80c46c74c27b532e45580`; both Gerrit changes had `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and zero unresolved comments.

## Exact reproduction
From `/Users/joeoakhart/implement-119f-project-review-criteria` using the worktree `.venv`:

```sh
rtk .venv/bin/rebar verify-completion 3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5 --ref origin/main --source attested --output json
```

The process remained active and emitted no progress or partial result for several minutes, then exited 1 with exactly:

```text
Error: completion verification workflow did not produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed: the model hit the token cap before finishing (finish_reason=length) — its output is TRUNCATED; raise max_tokens or split the step
```

## Observed outcome
- No PASS or FAIL verdict was produced.
- No completion attestation was written.
- The fully implemented bug remained `in_progress` and could not be closed through the required gate.
- The failure was output-budget exhaustion, not an acceptance-criterion failure.
- Repository default is `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 16000` in `src/rebar/llm/config.py`; the CLI supports the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS` override.
- A diagnostic retry was started with the supported cap raised to 32k (outcome will be appended when it returns):

```sh
rtk proxy env REBAR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS=32000 PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/rebar verify-completion 3ba4-c0d1-1813-44a5 --ref origin/main --source attested --output json
```

## Expected behavior
Completion verification for a normal leaf bug should reliably return a structured PASS or FAIL under default settings. The workflow should bound/compact evidence and tool output, scale the response budget when justified, or recover by splitting the decision step. It should not spend several minutes and terminate without any verdict solely because the model reached the default output cap.

## Impact
This is a fail-closed close-gate availability defect: correct, merged work cannot transition to `closed`, and the only immediate operator workaround is an undocumented per-run token-budget increase and complete rerun.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the `decide@then/verify` token-exhaustion path with bounded fixtures.
- [ ] The completion workflow returns a structured verdict for the reproduced case without requiring an operator environment override.
- [ ] Truncation recovery remains fail-closed and never converts an incomplete model response into PASS.
- [ ] The CLI reports actionable diagnostics and preserves trace metadata if all safe recovery attempts fail.
- [ ] Documentation states the supported token-budget/recovery behavior.
baseline.summary: Completion verifier exhausts output-token cap without a verdict

baseline.description:
## What
The `rebar metrics` subcommand: parses `--since/--until` and `--output json|text`, renders the full metric registry over the range, and is the single entry point wiring the readers. (Date bucketing is intentionally out of scope for this ticket — the command reports each metric over the whole `[since, until]` range; a per-bucket `--bucket` series can be a later additive enhancement and is NOT part of this ticket's contract.)

## Files
- `src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py` — new: arg parsing + a render loop that evaluates every `MetricSpec` in the registry.
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — wire the `metrics` READ subcommand with a single mechanism: add an explicit `if sub == "metrics":` arm in `_dispatch()` (mirroring `init`/`scratch`) that imports `rebar._commands.metrics` and calls its entry point, placed on the reads path that first ensures the store is initialized (as the other read commands are). This is ONE dispatch arm — not a frozenset-membership route (no existing frozenset carries it).
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/metrics.txt` — new help text.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt` — add the `metrics` line to the subcommand overview.
- `tests/golden/cli_help/*.out` — regenerate the overview snapshots (`__overview_help.out`, `__overview_dashhelp.out`, and the other overview goldens) and add `metrics__help.out`; the subcommand set is enumerated there.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — do NOT hand-edit: it is GENERATED by `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (with a CI drift gate). After adding the help/overview text, REGENERATE it (`python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`) and commit the result.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` — this drift guard checks that every routable subcommand is advertised in the overview and has pinned help text. Its `_routable_subcommands()` unions the dispatch frozensets PLUS an `individual` frozenset listing commands routed by an explicit `if sub == …` arm (`init`, `scratch`, `delete`, `fsck`, …). Because `metrics` is routed by such an explicit arm (not a frozenset), **add `"metrics"` to that `individual` frozenset** so `test_routable_set_matches_pinned_help_set` counts it routable; the new `help/metrics.txt` and the `overview.txt` `metrics` line satisfy the pinned-help and advertised-in-overview halves of the guard.
- `tests/interfaces/test_metrics_cli.py` — new CLI subprocess test.

## Approach
A thin CLI over the registry keeps the command complete-once: it builds a **context object** and calls `rebar.metrics.registry.evaluate(spec, context)` for every `MetricSpec`, emitting value-or-`unavailable` per metric, so new signals appear with no CLI change.

**REGISTRY hydration (import the PACKAGE, not just registry):** `REGISTRY` is only fully populated after the reader modules run their registration side-effects, and those imports live in `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py` (which imports `event_metrics`, `git_metrics`, `sidecar_metrics`). Importing `rebar.metrics.registry` ALONE does not trigger them. So `metrics.py` must `import rebar.metrics` (the package — running its `__init__`, which hydrates `REGISTRY`) and then read `rebar.metrics.registry.REGISTRY`. This does NOT breach adapter-isolation: `__init__.py` imports the reader modules but NOT `rebar.metrics.adapters.*`.

**The context object (the contract the readers already expect):** every reader's registered `compute` is a single-arg callable that reads `ctx.repo_root`, `ctx.since`, `ctx.until` (via `getattr(ctx, "repo_root", None)` etc.). So `metrics.py` constructs a small context (a dataclass or `SimpleNamespace`) carrying exactly `repo_root` (the resolved store root), `since`, and `until` (the parsed range), and passes it to `evaluate`.

**Adapter isolation (portability guard from 1f77/538c):** `metrics.py` must NOT import any `rebar.metrics.adapters` module. The guard is a **source-level scan**: the test reads `src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py` and asserts its source contains no `rebar.metrics.adapters` import (holds regardless of whether the adapters package exists). Adapter-backed data reaches the command only via `REGISTRY` / the snapshot store, never a direct import.

**Field sourcing (spec vs value).** `evaluate(spec, ctx)` returns either a `MetricValue` (carrying `.value`, `.source`, `.confidence` — but NOT `lens`) or an `Unavailable` (`.reason`, `.accruing_since`). The `lens` lives on the `MetricSpec`, so the render loop composes each entry from BOTH: `lens = spec.lens`, and value/source/confidence/reason from the `evaluate` result. (Do not read `.lens` off `MetricValue` — it has none.)

**Fault isolation.** `registry.evaluate()` does NOT catch exceptions raised inside a metric's `compute` (e.g. a reader hitting a git/IO error). So the render loop wraps each `evaluate(spec, ctx)` in `try/except`: on an exception it renders that metric as `unavailable` (reason = a short error string) rather than letting one failing metric crash the whole command. Every registered id therefore always appears in the output.

**Output formats.** JSON (default) is the machine contract: `{"since": <str>, "until": <str>, "metrics": {<id>: {"lens","source","confidence","value"} | {"unavailable": {"reason","accruing_since"}}, ...}}` where `lens` comes from the spec and `source`/`confidence`/`value` from the `MetricValue`. `--output text` is a deterministic human summary — one line per metric in registry order: `<id>  [<lens>/<source>]  <value-or-"unavailable: <reason>">` (a self-defined layout, NOT borrowed from `rebar audit`). Both formats include every registered metric id.

## Tests
- CLI (real subprocess against a temp store): `rebar metrics --since ... --until ... --output json` exits 0 and emits a `metrics` map containing every registered id; an unpopulated metric shows `unavailable`; `--output text` lists every metric id.
- **Test-side REGISTRY hydration:** the test module must `import rebar.metrics` (the package, running its `__init__` reader imports) BEFORE reading `REGISTRY`, and assert `len(REGISTRY) > 0` first — otherwise the `set(output) >= {s.id for s in REGISTRY}` comparison could be vacuously true against an unpopulated `REGISTRY` in the test process. (The subprocess-run command hydrates its own REGISTRY the same way via `metrics.py`.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/test_metrics_cli.py` passes: `rebar metrics --since 2026-01-01 --until 2026-07-01 --output json` exits 0 and the emitted `.metrics` map contains an entry for EVERY id in `rebar.metrics.registry.REGISTRY`. The test FIRST asserts `REGISTRY` is non-empty (`assert {s.id for s in REGISTRY}`), THEN `set(output["metrics"].keys()) >= {s.id for s in REGISTRY}` (so the `>=` is not vacuously true), each entry being either a value (with a `lens` from the spec plus `source`+`confidence`+`value`) or an `unavailable` object with a non-empty `reason`.
- [ ] `--output text` prints one line per registered metric id (a human summary) — CLI test asserts every id appears and an unavailable metric renders as `unavailable`.
- [ ] the portability guard holds: a test asserts `src/rebar/_commands/metrics.py`'s source does not import `rebar.metrics.adapters`.
- [ ] `rebar metrics --help` renders the help file and the command is listed by bare `rebar` — CLI test asserts exit 0 and help contains `--since`.
- [ ] the golden CLI-help snapshots are regenerated (and `docs/cli-reference.md` via `gen_cli_reference.py`), and the `tests/golden/cli_help` + help-overview-coverage suites pass with `metrics` listed.
baseline.summary: The rebar metrics CLI command (date-range, JSON/text, registry render)

baseline.description:
## Why
Make the long-running service observable and make every failure LOUD and troubleshootable — hangs, errors, and stuck states must be highly visible, per the operability requirement. Also serve the remote liveness/queue surface `land` reads. Split out of S5 (`perpetual-ultrasonic-raccoon`).

## Files
- `infra/autolander/loop.py` — EDIT: the read-only HTTP status endpoint + the marker emission + the time-to-land / time-in-phase metric emit.
- `infra/scripts/observability.sh` — EDIT: the `autolander_errors` + `autolander_time_to_land_seconds` + `autolander_time_in_phase_seconds` `PutMetricData` feeders.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autolander.tf` — NEW: the alarms.
- `infra/compose/nginx/rebar.conf.template` (or the active nginx config) — EDIT: add a read-only `location /autolander/status` proxying to the bot's status port (the existing template proxies only `/review/` and `/`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Read-only status endpoint (prior art: Zuul `zuul-web`, Tide `deck`):** a small read-only HTTP endpoint on the bot serving JSON — the current `wipChain` (change, `phase`, `tested_shas`, **time-in-phase**), the count of `Autosubmit`-set-and-waiting changes, and **`heartbeat_age_s`** (integer seconds since the last heartbeat write — the exact field `land`'s `lander_down` binds to). **Concrete network path:** the endpoint listens on an in-container port (e.g. `:8080`); the compose service publishes it, and nginx routes **`GET /autolander/status`** (a new read-only `location` in `rebar.conf.template`, alongside the existing `/review/`) to it — so `land` reaches it at `https://<gerrit-host>/autolander/status`. Read-only, non-secret (queue state, no credentials).
- [ ] **Error metric (LOUD by default):** `observability.sh` publishes `rebar/host:autolander_errors` (`PutMetricData`) from THREE feeders, each a concrete bot-emitted signal: (1) the `AUTOLANDER_ERROR` marker (the loop writes it on **any** unhandled error, then hands the current stack back rather than wedging silently); (2) an `AUTOLANDER_HANDBACK` marker (the loop writes it on every stack hand-back — since a hand-back, not the client-side `lander_down`, is what the bot itself can emit); (3) the container `unhealthy` Docker health-state (via `docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}'`, NOT a journald grep). **Marker format (shared emitter/parser contract):** each marker is a single stdout line = the bare token (`AUTOLANDER_ERROR` / `AUTOLANDER_HANDBACK`) followed by one space and a compact JSON object (e.g. `AUTOLANDER_ERROR {"change":"...","phase":"...","detail":"..."}`), matching the repo's existing `*_ERROR` marker convention; `observability.sh` greps the leading token to count occurrences. Alarm in `monitoring_autolander.tf`.
- [ ] **Stuck-state alarm (high visibility) — as a CloudWatch metric, not an HTTP field:** the loop publishes a `autolander_time_in_phase_seconds` metric (`PutMetricData`, the current `wipChain`'s seconds-in-phase, emitted each poll while non-`idle`); `monitoring_autolander.tf` defines a CloudWatch alarm on THAT metric (alarms watch metrics, not the status-endpoint JSON). This makes a wedged-but-alive bot (a hang autoheal doesn't catch) visible.
- [ ] **Time-to-land metric:** emit `autolander_time_to_land_seconds` (explicit metric name) as **individual `Value` datapoints** per landed change (NOT `StatisticValues` — CloudWatch computes extended-statistic percentiles only from raw `Value` datapoints); p50/p90/p99 come from CloudWatch extended statistics downstream (no hard-coded buckets). **In-session proof** (concrete): a unit test asserts the `PutMetricData` call is built with a single `Value` (not `StatisticValues`) and the `autolander_time_to_land_seconds` name; populated percentiles are an expected post-deploy outcome, not an in-sprint deliverable.
- [ ] The service logs to container stdout and NEVER writes `session_log`.
- [ ] **Tests:** the status endpoint returns the documented JSON shape (incl. `heartbeat_age_s`); a forced error produces an `AUTOLANDER_ERROR` marker + a metric datapoint, and a forced hand-back produces an `AUTOLANDER_HANDBACK` marker; the `autolander_time_in_phase_seconds` publisher and the `monitoring_autolander.tf` alarm-on-that-metric expression are unit-checked; the time-to-land `PutMetricData` call is asserted to use a single `Value` with the right metric name.
baseline.summary: S5c Observability (loud errors + stuck-state alarm) + read-only status endpoint

baseline.description:
Encode the agent-build invariants that guard against silently-disabled safeguards as tests plus a one-time construction check — not per-call runtime blocking. Every mechanism below is a CONCRETE, verified pydantic-ai 1.107.0 signal.

## Why
Several dangerous silent failures are static properties of rebar's OWN agent construction, not per-call events: tools silently stripped when a hook returns None (#5177), tools silently ignored on a non-tool-calling provider (#6186), `usage_limits` silently ignored if set on the `Agent(...)` constructor instead of `run*` (#1987), and usage silently zeroed on some provider adapters (#5360). Asserting these per-call wastes work and risks false-blocking a healthy run — they belong in tests + a one-time check.

## What (concrete mechanisms)
- **Construction-time provider tool-calling check.** VERIFIED signal: a pydantic-ai model exposes `model.profile.supports_tools` (a bool). The check is gated on `self._model_override is None` (the SAME guard as the anthropic model construction) — so the `model_override` test double is NEVER checked, concretely and by construction (no `.profile`-inspection heuristic to exclude it). It applies where rebar constructs an explicit model OBJECT (the anthropic path via `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, the primary path in practice). Guard: FOR A TOOL-USING op (`tools` non-empty) where `model` is a model OBJECT exposing the capability — read defensively as `supports = getattr(getattr(model, 'profile', None), 'supports_tools', None)` (so a missing/None profile is a safe skip, never an AttributeError) — assert that when `supports is False` it raises (a `True`/`None` value passes); else raise `LLMConfigError` (fail fast). It is a NO-OP for the string-model paths (OpenAI/Gemini pass a model STRING to `Agent`, which pydantic-ai builds + validates internally — rebar has no object to introspect there) and for `model_override` (a test double). So the check bounds the path rebar actually owns without false-positiving on provider-string paths. CACHE: a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` keyed by the resolved model string — the check runs ONCE per unique model per process (not per call), so a hot loop pays nothing.
- **Tests — tools actually offered.** rebar builds the agent's tools as `pai_tools.filesystem_tools(cfg.repo_path)` (callables `read_file`, `list_directory`, `search_files`) + `pai_tools.rebar_tools(cfg.repo_path, allow_comment=…)` (`show_ticket`, and `comment_ticket` when allowed). A test asserts these builders return callables whose `__name__`s are exactly the expected set (so a #5177 hook-returns-None regression that strips a tool is caught).
- **Tests — `usage_limits` on `run*`, not the constructor.** A spy on `Agent`/`run_sync` asserts (a) `run_sync` IS called with `usage_limits=`, and (b) the `Agent(...)` constructor kwargs do NOT include `usage_limits` (the #1987 mis-placement). Confirmed: `Agent.run_sync` accepts `usage_limits`; the constructor does not honor it.
- **Usage-plausibility telemetry WARNING (never a block).** After a successful REAL run (`self._model_override is None` — offline test doubles report zero usage and must never warn), if `_extract_usage` reports BOTH `input_tokens == 0` AND `output_tokens == 0` while `requests > 0` (a request was actually made), log a WARNING (`llm usage looks zeroed/implausible …`) — an observability signal for the #5360 zeroed-adapter cluster. It NEVER blocks a gate (usage is observability, not load-bearing); a genuinely tiny run is at worst a benign warning.

## Scope
- Tests + the construction-time capability check + the telemetry warning. NO per-call runtime blocking for these invariants.
- NOT in scope: changing the tool surface or provider adapters themselves; a per-call usage assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test: `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`/`rebar_tools` offer exactly the expected tool names — fails if a tool is stripped (`test_expected_tools_offered`).
- [ ] Test: `run_sync` is called with `usage_limits=` and the `Agent(...)` constructor is NOT — fails on the #1987 mis-placement (`test_usage_limits_on_run_not_constructor`).
- [ ] Construction-time check: a model OBJECT with `profile.supports_tools == False` used for a tool-using op raises `LLMConfigError`; a string-model path is a NO-OP (test asserts no raise); the check is cached in a module-level `set()` `_TOOL_CAPABILITY_CHECKED` (invoked once per model string; `test_capability_check_cached` spies on the `model.profile` access — or a counter in the check helper — asserting a repeated same-model run reads the profile only once) — `test_capability_check_fails_fast`, `test_capability_check_noop_for_string_model`, `test_capability_check_cached`.
- [ ] Usage-plausibility emits a WARNING (asserted via caplog) on an all-zero-usage successful run and NEVER blocks (`test_usage_plausibility_warns_never_blocks`).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (the cached construction-time capability check + the usage-plausibility warning), `tests/unit/test_agent_build_invariants.py` (new).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
FunctionModel.profile.supports_tools == True; AnthropicModel("claude-sonnet-4-6").profile.supports_tools == True (bool)
  -> VERIFIED on the ACTUAL AnthropicModel type rebar constructs (offline, no API call — just the model object)
model.profile also exposes: supports_json_schema_output, supports_json_object_output, supports_thinking, ...
Agent.__init__ has tools/toolsets: True         (tools offered via the constructor; introspectable)
Agent.run_sync accepts usage_limits: True       (#1987: usage_limits belongs on run*, NOT Agent(...))
rebar tool builders: pai_tools.filesystem_tools -> [read_file, list_directory, search_files];
                     pai_tools.rebar_tools -> [show_ticket, (comment_ticket when allow_comment)]
_extract_usage returns a dict with input_tokens/output_tokens (both 0 => the zeroed-adapter signal)
```
These are pydantic-ai LIBRARY symbols (`model.profile.supports_tools` etc.), not rebar symbols
(bug succinct-formable-kite: a code-grounding pass must not read repo-absence as non-existence).
baseline.summary: Agent-build invariants as tests + one-time capability check

content.text: ## What
G5 (decomposition) currently judges from ticket TEXT and false-flagged an epic that already had 6
children as a "flat, undecomposed list". The store already loads the real children — `ctx.children`
is populated by the N+1 read in `orchestrator.py:166-182` and counted in `pass1.py:427`. Make that
fact authoritative for G5 so the model never counts children itself.
## Scope / files
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — inject an authoritative `DECOMPOSITION STATE (from store):
N direct children: [alias - title (status)]` block into the G5 finder context from `ctx.children`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` (or the DET-invariant seam) — add a deterministic veto that
drops any G5 "flat/undecomposed" finding when `len(ctx.children) > 0`.
- `tests/unit/` — regression test for the previously-misfired case.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The G5 finder context includes the store-sourced authoritative child summary.
- [ ] A DET guard suppresses a G5 decomposition finding when the ticket has >=1 child (count from the
store, not the model); G5 still judges child-content/altitude.
- [ ] Regression test: an epic with children no longer yields a G5 "undecomposed" finding; a genuinely
monolithic childless ticket still does.

baseline.summary: Deterministic G5 decomposition signal (store-derived child count feeds the finder + DET veto)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

A `caplog` assertion whose records never arrive DOES NOT FAIL — it passes vacuously. `assert not [unexpected]` is trivially true against an empty list, and even a positive `assert any(...)` only fails if someone wrote it that way. So a test can lose 100% of its coverage and stay GREEN, permanently and silently, with nothing in the run output distinguishing it from a test that genuinely verified something.

This is not hypothetical. It is happening in this repository right now.

## The live instance

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:145-146` (`configure_logging()`) sets

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.propagate = False

process-globally, and never restores it. pytest's `caplog` captures through a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off NO `rebar.*` record can reach it again for the remainder of the process. Every later `caplog` assertion on a rebar logger silently sees zero records.

Proven on a clean tree by a two-test probe: identical assertion, passes before `configure_logging()` and fails after; `caplog.at_level()` does not help because it adjusts LEVELS, not propagation. Full mechanism, both entry points, and the reproduction are on ticket b718-fb7f-b1a4-4feb — including that `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls `configure_logging()` at MODULE IMPORT time, so merely importing the app poisons the process (inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

b718 fixes THE POISONER. This ticket is about the far larger problem it exposed: THE SUITE CANNOT TELL THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A PASSING ASSERTION AND AN UNREACHABLE ONE.

## Blast radius — measured, though the precise void count is unknown

    54 test files contain `caplog`
    255 total `caplog` occurrences

How many of those are currently void in a full run is NOT established, and establishing it is the first job of this ticket. The count depends on run order and on which logger each assertion targets, and `-n 6 --dist worksteal` distributes tests across workers nondeterministically — so the SAME assertion may be live in one run and void in the next, on the same commit. That non-determinism is itself part of the defect: coverage is not reproducible.

## Why this is severe rather than untidy

* IT FAILS OPEN. Every other gate in this repo fails closed. This one silently reports success.
* IT IS INVISIBLE. Nothing in the output marks a void assertion. Reviewers, CI and agents all see
  green.
* IT SURVIVED DETECTION. It was found only as a side effect of debugging an unrelated ticket, by an
  agent that noticed one victim test and traced it. Nobody was looking for it.
* IT IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, so a test can be genuinely verifying in isolation — which is how it was
  written and reviewed — and verify nothing in the suite that actually gates merges.
* THE VICTIM IS NEVER THE CULPRIT. The one test that DID go red pointed at
  `test_agent_call_seam.py`, nowhere near `review_bot/config.py`.

## Approach

Fixing the current poisoner (b718) removes today's instance but not the class — any future code that touches logger propagation, handlers or levels reintroduces it, with the same silence.

The durable fix is to make an unreachable log assertion FAIL LOUDLY instead of passing. Candidates to weigh, not yet decided:
  * an autouse fixture that asserts `logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate` is True at test setup, so
    the poisoning is caught at the point of damage rather than at a random later victim;
  * a `caplog` wrapper/fixture used by rebar tests that fails when zero records were captured for an
    assertion that expected some;
  * making `configure_logging()` scoped/restorable so no test can leak it in the first place (overlaps
    b718 — coordinate rather than duplicate).
The first is the smallest change that converts a silent fail-open into a loud fail-closed, and it protects against future reintroduction rather than just this instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The number of `caplog` assertions currently void in a full default-selection run is ESTABLISHED
      and recorded — not estimated. The 54-file / 255-occurrence figures above are the search space,
      not the answer.
- [x] An unreachable log assertion FAILS rather than passing vacuously, and a test proves it: with
      propagation deliberately disabled, a previously-green assertion must go RED.
- [x] The guard catches the poisoning AT ITS SOURCE, not at a random later victim — a test asserts the
      failure names the code that disabled propagation, not an unrelated downstream test.
- [x] Any assertion found to be void is either restored to working coverage or deleted; none is left
      passing vacuously. Deleting is acceptable where the assertion no longer earns its place, but
      leaving a green no-op is not.
- [x] Coordinated with b718 so the poisoner fix and the class guard do not implement overlapping
      mechanisms.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Unreachable caplog assertions pass vacuously: the suite cannot distinguish verified coverage from zero coverage

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Blocking links written before comparability became structural (ticket 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd) are still wrong on disk: a `LINK` event is durable and nothing re-resolves it on read, so an epic blocked by its own child — or a cousin edge that should now sit between the parent stories — keeps distorting `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade. Scanning this repository's own tracker found 18 such edges.

## Approach

A store-wide scan over net-active blocking edges that asks the CURRENT resolver what each edge should be, so the check cannot drift from the rule it audits. Three finding kinds: `ancestor-blocking` (an endpoint is an ancestor of the other), `mis-escalated` (the resolver returns a different pair than the one recorded), `unreadable` (an endpoint could not be reduced; reported, never repaired). Enumeration reuses the reducer's compiled `deps[]` rather than re-deriving LINK/UNLINK replay.

`--repair` writes the replacement link BEFORE removing the stale one, so an interruption leaves a superset the next run converges rather than losing a dependency. It declines a pair whose pair-scoped `UNLINK` would cancel a different relation (`ambiguous-pair`), since the event model offers no relation-scoped unlink. It force-writes a `pre-doctor-repair` tag at the pre-run OID as a rollback anchor, and refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight. It takes NO store-wide lock: every event write already takes the tracker write lock for itself and that lock is not re-entrant, so an outer hold made each inner acquisition block for its full 60s timeout and fail. Anything unrepairable is reported with the original left intact and the run continues.

Rejected: folding these checks into `rebar fsck` (that validates event/storage integrity, this validates graph semantics), and re-resolving on read (would put the resolver on every read path and mutate during nominally read-only commands).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — the scan, classifier, repair driver and CLI.
- `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — registration and a dedicated dispatcher arm (`init_only=True` unless `--repair`, so a read-only run never reconverges the store).
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/doctor.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`, `docs/cli-reference.md` (generated), `docs/ticket-model.md`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` + registration, and the two `tests/interfaces/contracts/` guards that enforce help/overview/schema agreement.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.

## Testing

Clean store reports nothing; the bug-1803 shape classifies `ancestor-blocking`; a cousin edge classifies `mis-escalated`; repair ordering (replacement written before the stale unlink, asserted by forcing the unlink to raise and checking BOTH edges survive); resumability from that superset; `ambiguous-pair` declined with both links intact; unreadable never repaired; cyclic and closed-ticket replacements reported `unrepairable` with the run continuing; `--repair --dry-run` writes no events while still reporting findings; JSON output field assertions; a read-only run does not reconverge; `run_repair` completes without contending with itself; and `--repair` refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight, writing nothing.

## Delivery note

Landed as changes 1028, 1039, 1040 and 1045. Renamed from `link-audit` to `doctor` at operator direction — a standalone verb was rejected for core, so this became `doctor`'s first check; see the doctor epics dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 and 18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb, which carry the current status and the re-parent follow-up. Detailed rationale, corrections and the live-run attestation live in this ticket's comments and in the merged commit messages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar doctor` with no flags writes no events; verified by comparing the tracker's event-file count before and after in `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.
- [ ] An epic holding `depends_on` on its own child is reported with `kind == "ancestor-blocking"`, and `--repair` removes it so a second scan reports zero findings; verified by the repair case in the same module.
- [ ] A cousin edge recorded directly is reported with `kind == "mis-escalated"` and replaced by `--repair` with the story-to-story edge; verified by the mis-escalation case.
- [ ] Repair writes the replacement before removing the stale edge; verified by the ordering test that forces the unlink step to raise and asserts BOTH edges are present afterwards — no dependency lost.
- [ ] An ordered pair carrying two net-active links is reported `unrepairable` with reason `ambiguous-pair` and both links survive `--repair`; verified by the ambiguous-pair case.
- [ ] An unrepairable finding (cyclic replacement) leaves its original edge on disk, does not stop the run, and yields exit code 1; verified by asserting the edge still exists, that a second finding was still repaired, and the exit status.
- [ ] A store whose only links are non-blocking reports zero findings and is unchanged by `--repair`; verified by comparing the tracker event-file listing before and after.
- [ ] `--repair --dry-run` leaves the event count unchanged while still reporting the findings it would fix; verified by the dry-run case.
- [ ] `rebar doctor --output json` emits an object whose findings each carry `kind`, `source`, `target` and `relation` — with `kind` in `{"ancestor-blocking", "mis-escalated", "unreadable"}` — and additionally `repair_status` after a `--repair` pass; verified by asserting on the parsed keys and values, not merely that the output parses.
- [ ] `--repair` force-writes the `pre-doctor-repair` tag at the tracker's pre-run OID before its first write, and a second `--repair` run re-points it rather than failing; verified by asserting the tag OID in the repair test and re-running repair.
- [ ] A plain `rebar doctor` does not trigger a store reconverge; verified by asserting `ensure_initialized` is called with `init_only=True` when `--repair` is absent and `init_only=False` when present.
- [ ] `rebar help` lists `doctor`; verified by `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` passing, which fails if the help file and overview line disagree.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md` documents `doctor` including `--repair` and `--dry-run`; verified by `grep -n '^### `doctor`' docs/cli-reference.md` matching and by reading the section.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar doctor` against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling; verified by running
  `rebar doctor --output json | jq -r '.findings[] | if .relation == "depends_on" then .source else .target end'` to list each residual edge's BLOCKED side, then `rebar show <id> --output json | jq -r .status` for each, and attesting on this ticket that every one is `closed`. A `closed` blocked-side can never appear in `ready` or `next-batch`, so the edge is inert. Attested rather than asserted in-repo because it is a statement about live tracker state at a point in time.

  Amended from the original "zero outstanding findings, exits 0". That criterion is unreachable without reopening closed tickets: `add_dependency` refuses a link whose source is closed (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:254`), which is correct — a closed ticket depending on something is meaningless — so a mis-escalated edge whose resolved source has since closed can never be rewritten. The amendment narrows the criterion to the property that actually matters rather than a count the guard makes unattainable; the residual edges stay recorded and evidenced on this ticket.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The pre-repair finding count for this repository's tracker is recorded on this ticket, with the tracker HEAD OID the scan ran against and the `pre-doctor-repair` tag OID; attested by a comment carrying those three values, since the pre-repair state cannot be reconstructed from the post-repair repo.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/graph/ tests/interfaces/contracts/`, `make lint` and `make typecheck` all pass in the worktree; verified by running each.
- [ ] `--repair` refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight and writes nothing — the refusal raises `CommandError` naming the in-flight pass, the tracker's event count is unchanged, and the offending edge is still active; verified by `test_repair_refuses_while_a_reconciler_pass_is_in_flight` in `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` is between 100 and 800 lines, per the module-size policy; verified by `wc -l`.
baseline.summary: rebar link-audit: detect and repair blocking edges written under the type-tier rule

## Summary

There is no ongoing per-test performance signal in CI: slow tests are invisible until
someone profiles by hand. Add lightweight, always-on per-test timing to the gate so the
slowest tests surface in every run, and (optionally) persist a durations file usable for
future cross-runner sharding (pytest-split). `--durations` and
`pytest-split --store-durations` are both verified working on this suite.

## What

- Add `--durations=25` to the default-suite pytest invocation in `gerrit-verify.yaml`
  and `test.yml` so every gate run prints its 25 slowest tests (setup/call/teardown).
  Confirmed compatible with `-q`, coverage, and xdist.
- OPTIONAL (behind this task): add a scheduled/post-merge step that runs
  `pytest --store-durations --durations-path .test_durations` and uploads `.test_durations`
  as an artifact, so timing data is tracked over time and available if the team later shards
  across runners with pytest-split. Verified: `--store-durations` writes a valid JSON map
  (`{"<nodeid>": <seconds>, …}`).
- `.test_durations` must be gitignored (or artifact-only) so it never leaks into the
  checkout and never trips the repo-leak guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

      `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` and `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Sync a rebar store to Jira (e.g. the REB cutover) where local tickets have
assignees that are not Jira users (agent names like `claude`, `claude-opus`).
2. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run` after the initial create pass.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** once a ticket is created+bound and its synced fields match, the
reconciler emits no further mutations for it (convergence).
- **Actual:** ~323 of 355 bound tickets emit an `assignee` update every pass. The
local assignee (e.g. `claude`) is not a Jira user, so the applier soft-fails the
assign (`assignee 'claude' cannot be assigned — retrying without assignee`),
Jira stays unassigned, and `_assignee_matches("claude", None)` is False — so the
differ re-emits the same assignee update on the next pass. Perpetual churn (passes
still succeed; the canary stays green — this is noise/inefficiency, not failure).
## Root cause
`outbound_differ._diff_fields` + `_assignee_matches`: a local assignee that cannot
be resolved to a Jira account never matches Jira's (unassigned) state, and there is
no "unresolvable assignee → don't re-emit" suppression after the applier soft-fails.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A bound ticket whose local assignee cannot be assigned in Jira does NOT
re-emit an assignee update every pass (converge or suppress-after-soft-fail).
- [ ] Decide the intended semantics: skip assignee sync for non-Jira-user
assignees, map agent identities to a service account, or record an
unresolvable-assignee marker so the differ stops re-emitting.
- [ ] A dry-run after convergence shows 0 perpetual assignee-only updates.

baseline.summary: Reconciler churns assignee updates for non-Jira-user assignees (never converges)

# The LLM-Review safety-net alarm has NO actions, so it fires into an empty room

## Context / Problem

`rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` is the alarm the review-bot's fail-closed path depends on: `voter.py`'s `_voter_error()` writes a greppable `VOTER_ERROR` marker, `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 publishes `rebar/host:voter_errors`, and `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` alarms on it. The chain is real and the metric genuinely publishes (`get-metric-statistics` returns ~22 datapoints over 2h, consistent with the 5-minute probe).

**But the alarm has no actions, so nothing tells a human when it fires.** Verified on both sides:

* `grep -nE "actions" infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` returns NOTHING — neither `alarm_actions`
  nor `ok_actions` is declared.
* live `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --alarm-names rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` returns
  `AlarmActions: []`, `OKActions: []`, `ActionsEnabled: true`.

So the alarm transitions `OK -> ALARM` correctly and silently. It is discoverable only by someone who already went looking in the CloudWatch console — which is precisely the person who does not need an alarm.

**This is a sibling-inconsistency, not a house style.** Every other alarm family in this repo wires the SNS topic: `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:57-58,128-129,180-181` and `infra/terraform/monitoring_1fa8.tf:74` all use `[aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`, with the topic declared in `monitoring.tf`. `monitoring_s4b.tf` is the outlier.

**Why it matters more than a normal missing-notification bug.** The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main`. When the voter fails closed, changes become unsubmittable — the failure is *silent to Gerrit by design* (no vote is cast rather than a wrong one), and now also silent to the operator. Discovered while working the Bedrock production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], whose ORDERING criterion treats this alarm as the safety net that must be proven before the model flip, on the stated rationale that "a recovery path must be proven before it can be needed". A recovery path nobody is told to walk is proven only in the weakest sense: the state change is observable, the notification does not exist. The criterion is still satisfiable (the transition can be recorded from `describe-alarms`), but the safety it implies is thinner than the plan's wording suggests, and that is worth fixing rather than re-wording.

An adjacent contrast that shows the fix is cheap: the alarm added by bug 34cd (`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts`) DOES wire both `alarm_actions` and `ok_actions` to `aws_sns_topic.alerts`. The pattern is one line each.

## Scope

- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` — the `voter_errors` alarm resource.
- audit the remaining alarm files for the same omission, since s4b proves it is not caught by review:
  `monitoring.tf`, `monitoring_s5.tf`, `monitoring_ws7.tf`, `monitoring_88ab.tf`.

Out of scope: `observability.sh` (the publisher is correct and working), and the alarm's thresholds (`period = 300`, `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0` are deliberate and fine).

## Approach

Add `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` and `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`. Wire OK as well as ALARM so a recovery is visible and the alarm does not read as stuck-firing.

Then audit the siblings. The interesting question is not this one resource but **why a silent alarm survived review in a repo that otherwise wires them consistently** — if the audit finds more, the fix is a convention that is checkable rather than four more one-line patches. Do not add a `terraform validate`-style lint for this unless the audit shows it is a pattern; one outlier is a bug, four is a missing rule.

REMEMBER THE APPLY. Committing this does not create it: applies are manual, and [rebar:1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38] records that the drift check does not gate a Gerrit change, so an un-applied landing turns `main` red after submit.

## Testing

CloudWatch alarm wiring cannot be unit-tested meaningfully, so the oracle is the live one, and it must be an OBSERVATION rather than an inspection of the HCL:

1. after apply, `describe-alarms` on `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` shows a non-empty `AlarmActions`
   naming the alerts topic;
2. `set-alarm-state --state-value ALARM` forces a transition and a notification is confirmed
   DELIVERED to the topic's subscriber — not merely that the action is listed. "The ARN is in the
   field" is exactly the level of proof that let this bug exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` declares `alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions` pointing at
      `aws_sns_topic.alerts`, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`.
- [ ] the change is APPLIED, and live `describe-alarms` shows non-empty `AlarmActions`/`OKActions` —
      recorded as observed output, since the HCL alone is what looked fine before.
- [ ] one FORCED notification is observed end-to-end (`set-alarm-state` -> the subscriber received it),
      proving delivery rather than configuration.
- [ ] the other alarm files are audited for the same omission and the result is recorded — either
      "no others" or the list, with a note on whether a checkable convention is warranted.
baseline.summary: The voter_errors alarm notifies nobody: rebar-gerrit-voter-errors has no alarm_actions

# DC parent sync is ONE-WAY: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound never reads it

## The asymmetry

After Gerrit **1311** (ticket 39c1), `JiraDataCenterTransport.set_parent` writes a non-sub-task's parent to the instance-discovered "Epic Link" custom field. Nothing reads it back.

`get_parent_map` (`transport.py:515-546`) — the ONLY inbound parent read — searches with `fields="parent"` and extracts `fields.parent` alone:

    for issue in self._paged_search(query, fields="parent", rate_limit_retry=True):
        parent = fields.get("parent") if isinstance(fields, dict) else None
        out[key] = parent.get("key") if isinstance(parent, dict) else None

Repo-wide, `Epic Link` / `_epic_link` appears ONLY in `transport.py`'s outbound path.

**So a parent rebar sets on Data Center is invisible to rebar on the next inbound pass.** On DC, inbound can only ever see a SUB-TASK's parent — and [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] gives reason to doubt even that path takes effect.

## Why this is the epic's signature class, again

"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — d067, 8d68, 751e, 2b16/88d9, 39c1. This is a fresh instance, created by the fix for the sixth one. Not a regression (nothing read the Epic Link before), and 1311 is not wrong — its scope was the outbound half, and the emit gate only ever emits an EPIC parent, so the Epic Link is the correct target. But the ROUND TRIP is open, and epic e369's headline criterion is BIDIRECTIONAL reconcile.

## The unproven risk that makes this more than cosmetic

If outbound writes a parent the next inbound pass cannot see, the differ may re-emit the SAME parent mutation every pass — the perpetual re-emission bug 8b25 was filed for (~230 steady-state `fields=['parent']` mutations on Cloud). **Explicitly NOT asserted here**: it depends on how the outbound differ decides a parent is already synced. The live cell that would show it is `test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing`, which is currently GREEN — so either the churn does not occur or that cell does not cover this shape. Settle it before assuming either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `get_parent_map` returns a non-sub-task's parent from the instance-discovered "Epic Link"
      field, in addition to `fields.parent` for sub-tasks — field id discovered BY NAME, never
      hardcoded, reusing the discovery+cache the outbound side already has rather than a second copy
- [x] the two shapes do not collide: a sub-task's `fields.parent` still wins where both exist, and a
      test pins which takes precedence
- [x] the round trip closes: a parent WRITTEN by outbound is SEEN by the next inbound read, asserted
      against a real DC instance on a harness run (run id recorded). A unit suite does NOT settle
      this — changes 1276, 1288 and 1302 were all mutation-proven and all wrong live
- [x] idempotence is proven, not assumed: repeated passes over a converged epic-parent pair emit NO
      further parent mutation — this is the churn risk above
- [x] `get_parent_map`'s degradation contract is preserved: a failure still logs a WARNING and
      returns `{}` so the inbound pass falls back to parentless rather than aborting
- [x] `transport.py` stays under the 800-LOC cap (it is ~781 after 1311; the discovery helper
      already exists, so this should reuse it rather than grow a parallel one)
baseline.summary: DC parent sync is one-way: outbound writes the Epic Link, inbound never reads it

## Context
rebar has no general mechanism to apply an idempotent setup/config change to an
ALREADY-EXISTING install. Init-time `_migrate_*`/`_ensure_*` functions (e.g.
`_migrate_gc_config`) run only at `init`/re-init, so a fix shipped after a store was
initialized never reaches it unless someone re-inits — the gap the `gc.auto=0` legacy-store
issue exposed. Discovered from the gc discussion (e3d0).

**School B (desired-state / convergent), not School A (ordered ledger).** Idempotent,
safe-to-re-run, drift-correcting (Ansible/Puppet/Chef check-then-act `changed`/`ok`; K8s
level-triggered reconcile). We do NOT build an ordered version ledger (Alembic/Flyway/Rails
are for irreversible, unsafe-to-rerun migrations). The A-tier ledger (committed store-format
version, ordered, fail-closed on too-new) is future work (docs/migrations.md + doctor idea dabb).

## Design (corrected against origin/main via two plan-review passes)
**Ensure-registry (`ensures.py`).** A registry of ensure units, each `{stable, immutable id,
callable(tracker) -> EnsureOutcome}` where the callable is check-then-act (no-op when
converged) and `EnsureOutcome` is a small dataclass `{id, status: Literal["ok","changed",
"failed"], detail}`. `run_ensures(tracker)` runs ALL units unconditionally under the STORE
write lock (`_store/lock.py` write_lock — init_core does NOT currently hold it), catches a
raising unit (skip-and-continue → `failed`), returns the outcome list, and rewrites
`.ensure-applied` to the ids of the NON-failed (ok/changed) units only.

**The exact 5 re-init idempotent steps migrated** (init.py:209-213 — the already-initialized
path that reaches existing stores): `env-id`, `gc-config`, `merge-ours driver`,
`gitattributes` (COMMIT), `gitignore` (COMMIT). **Two units commit** (gitattributes AND
gitignore) → check-then-act (tree-check before commit) required for BOTH. These same units
also appear on the fresh-init path (init.py:242-248) and `_ensure_env_id` is additionally
called from `_init_via_symlink` (init.py:564, 582); the migration wires `run_ensures()` at all
init entry points and removes the hand-listed calls from each, with no double-execution. The
fresh-init-only bootstrap (`_commit_precommit`, `_gen_local_files`, `_exclude_scratch_in_tracker`,
`_ensure_branch_user_config`) are NOT ensures and stay.

**Entry points (non-hot):** init/re-init/symlink-init (always), `rebar fsck --repair` (opt-in),
MCP server startup (best-effort — log-and-continue, never abort boot; under write lock). The
sweep never runs on the hot write path or on pure reads.

**fsck reconciliation (origin/main ALREADY has `fsck --repair`).** `fsck --repair` is the
existing A3 data-remediation verb (rebuild snapshots, retire orphans; requires mutation;
`--dry-run`/`--limit`). We do NOT add a new `--fix` flag — we FOLD the ensure-sweep into the
existing `--repair` path (one "drive to healthy" verb, both data + config). Plain read-only
`rebar fsck` gains an `ensures: N/M applied` line derived WITHOUT calling run_ensures: M =
count of registry ids, N = count present in `.ensure-applied`. The pending-hint points to
`rebar fsck --repair`.

**Concurrency.** run_ensures runs under the store write lock so concurrent sweeps serialize;
check-then-act makes the second sweep a no-op. gitattributes/gitignore use `merge=ours`.
`.ensure-applied` is a full atomic rewrite (temp+rename) of the current non-failed id set — no
read-modify-write.

**Applied-set marker + write-path pending-hint (Rails CheckPending, hardened).**
- `.ensure-applied` (WS1-owned: format+write) and `.ensure-hinted` (WS2-owned) — both git-ignored
  (ADD BOTH to `_GITIGNORE`, init.py:38-48), atomic; `.ensure-applied` = JSON array, absent/garbage
  → empty set; `.ensure-hinted` = last-hinted timestamp.
- Hook the COMMON mutation paths via `_seam.append_event` / `event_append.write_and_push`
  (create/edit/link/comment/tag/set_*/sign/transition/claim), lazy import. Best-effort, NOT
  universal: `compact.py`, `txn.py`/`transition_close.py`, `delete.py` commit inline and are
  intentionally NOT hooked (acceptable — a rate-limited nudge, not correctness).
- `pending = registry ids − parsed .ensure-applied`, computed ONCE per process (cached boolean;
  registry static in a process). Converged store adds ≤1 read/process; reads untouched.
- Emit a WARNING → `rebar fsck --repair` only when pending AND `.ensure-hinted` older than the
  interval; then atomically update it. Interval + suppression are typed config (`EnsureConfig`
  in `_config_schema.py`: `ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400, `ensure.hint_enabled`=true), Interval + suppression live in the `[ensure]` config section (`ensure.hint_interval_secs`=86400, `ensure.hint_enabled`=true); the env override is auto-derived per rebar's standard mechanism — no edits to any generated file.
- Hook swallows ALL its own exceptions incl. lazy-import ImportError/SyntaxError (debug log) — a
  write NEVER fails on the nag. Rare double-hint under concurrency accepted.
- Marker gates the HINT ONLY, never the repair. Fresh auto-init'd worktree converges at init → never hints.

**Accepted trade-offs:** long-lived MCP server converges at boot, does not re-sweep mid-life
(drift caught at next `fsck --repair`) — WS4 documents it; a permanently-failing unit stays out
of the set and is named in the rate-limited hint. Post-rollback: old code simply ignores the
git-ignored `.ensure-applied`/`.ensure-hinted` files (no schema coupling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensures.py` registry generalizes the 5 re-init units; each is check-then-act with a stable/immutable id + `EnsureOutcome` result; BOTH commit units (gitattributes, gitignore) tree-check (second run → zero commits)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` runs unconditionally under the store write lock at all init entry points, `fsck --repair`, and MCP startup (best-effort at startup); NEVER gated on the marker
- [ ] Migration removes the hand-listed calls from BOTH re-init and fresh-init paths (and handles `_ensure_env_id`'s `_init_via_symlink` callers) with no double-execution
- [ ] The ensure-sweep is folded into the EXISTING `fsck --repair` (no new flag); plain `fsck` prints `ensures: N/M applied` read-only (M=registry ids, N=in `.ensure-applied`, without calling run_ensures)
- [ ] `fsck --repair` heals and is git-level idempotent (twice → zero new commits); the pending-hint points to `rebar fsck --repair`
- [ ] Best-effort write-path pending-hint on the common mutation paths (inline committers acknowledged out); pure reads untouched; ≤1 read/process; never fails a write (incl. lazy-import errors)
- [ ] Hint rate-limited via `.ensure-hinted` + typed-config interval (86400s) + `[ensure]` config-section suppression (`ensure.hint_enabled`; env auto-derived); fresh auto-init'd worktree never hints
- [ ] `.ensure-applied` (JSON array, atomic full rewrite of non-failed ids) + `.ensure-hinted` are added to `_GITIGNORE`; absent/garbage → empty set (no crash)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` has a typed `EnsureOutcome` + partial-failure contract (skip-and-continue; init logs failures, never aborts)
- [ ] Hot-path regression test: mutation ops may hint but never invoke `run_ensures` (no git-config subprocess; ≤1 marker read/process)
- [ ] `docs/migrations.md` documents reuse, marker-gates-hint-never-repair, hot-path contract, long-lived-MCP trade-off, post-rollback file-ignore, and A-tier future; gc-config is the reference unit
baseline.summary: First-class migration pattern: idempotent per-environment ensure-registry (B tier)

content.text: ## Finding (S1 — verified)

The module-size CI gate fully EXEMPTS allowlisted files, so a grandfathered file can grow without bound. Evidence: `attest.py` 268->837 (+212%), `passes.py` 589->839, `det_floor.py` 733->849, `inbound_differ.py` 754->802 all grew AFTER being allowlisted.
Citations: `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` (bare filenames); gate in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (`awk '$1>800'` then `comm -23` vs allowlist).
## Remediation

Convert the allowlist from bare filenames to `path <max-lines>` rows (ceiling = current LOC at grandfathering). The gate compares each allowlisted file against ITS OWN recorded ceiling; exceeding it fails CI ("reduce it or bump the row — a reviewed act"). New non-allowlisted files keep the 800 rule. Also drop the `__init__.py` filename-pattern exemption (give it a pinned ceiling row instead) so it is gate-visible.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Allowlist rows carry a per-file LOC ceiling
- [ ] test.yml fails when an allowlisted file grows past its ceiling; shrinking is free
- [ ] `__init__.py` is gate-visible (pinned row, not filename-exempt)
- [ ] Current allowlisted files pass at their pinned ceilings

baseline.summary: Add a per-file growth ratchet to the module-size allowlist

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
normalize_ci_conclusion.sh is a pure function in shell — trivially portable, currently tested only via a subprocess-driving contract test. Its REAL contract is two-input: f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED) -> vote in {success, failure, cancelled} (never out-of-domain), consumed by .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml.

## Approach
Port to a small stdlib-only Python entry point with unit tests; the workflow call site swaps to the Python invocation. The existing contract test tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the SHELL script via subprocess — it is the porting oracle: first re-point its subprocess invocation at the Python entry point (proving CLI-level behavior parity env-var-for-env-var), keep its full case table, and add direct in-process unit tests of the function. The shell file is deleted in the same change, so no test ever references a missing script. The workflow currently fetches the script via sparse-checkout of exactly 'scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh' (gerrit-verify.yaml:323) and calls it at :340 — update the sparse-checkout path to the new .py file (cone-mode: false so a single-file pattern works) and keep the entry point dependency-free so the single-file checkout still runs without the package installed. Opportunistic priority (lowest tier).

## Scope
- scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh (deleted) -> new stdlib-only Python entry point
- tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py: subprocess target swapped to the Python entry point, case table preserved
- .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml: sparse-checkout path at :323 AND the run invocation at :340
- new direct unit tests for the function

## Testing
The ported subprocess contract test keeps its full table (env-driven CLI parity). Direct table-driven unit test over f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED):
- success -> success; failure -> failure; cancelled -> cancelled (FAILURE_OBSERVED irrelevant for these — assert both values)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=false -> success (benign im-open fallback)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=true -> failure (fail-closed)
- empty CONCLUSION -> failure; unrecognized value (e.g. 'timed_out') -> failure (fail-closed anomaly rows)
- FAILURE_OBSERVED unset defaults to false
Outputs asserted to always be in {success, failure, cancelled}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Python entry point reproduces the shell mapping exactly as f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED), including skipped-fallback rows and fail-closed empty/unknown rows.
- [x] tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the Python entry point via subprocess with its case table preserved (no orphaned reference to the deleted .sh), plus direct unit tests cover the full contract (both FAILURE_OBSERVED values for pass-through rows included).
- [x] gerrit-verify.yaml sparse-checkout fetches the new .py path (cone-mode: false) and the run step invokes it; entry point is stdlib-only so the single-file checkout works; shell file deleted.
baseline.summary: Shell-to-Python Tier 1: normalize_ci_conclusion.sh

content.text: Each plan-review workflow op independently re-assembles the entire ticket graph from the store, so one gate run does ~4×(1 + 1 + K children) `show_ticket`/`list_tickets` reads. On an epic with many children this is the latency the observability commit (`08cd4c325`) was added to explain — "a slow epic review looks like a hang" — a client-facing reliability/perceived-performance issue.
## Why

The B-RETIRE migration decomposed the review into pure `uses` ops but gave them no shared context, so each re-reads + re-derives the graph (`orchestrator.assemble_context` is itself an N+1 read: `show_ticket` + `list_tickets(parent=)` + one `show_ticket` per child).
## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:66,147,212,235` — the precheck/assemble/verify_inputs/coach_inputs ops each call `orchestrator.assemble_context(...)`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:85` and `__init__.py:108` — assemble again.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:77-110` — `assemble_context` (the N+1 read).

Approach: assemble `PlanContext` ONCE in `plan_review_precheck`, serialize its `state`/`children` into the precheck step outputs, and have downstream ops reconstruct `PlanContext` from those outputs (as `plan_review_coach` already does at `workflow_ops.py:342`). Alternatively memoize on `(run_id, ticket_id)`.
## Scope
In: eliminate the redundant re-reads within one gate run; preserve verdict bytes exactly. Out: changing the verdict/finding shape or the workflow YAML's op sequence.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single plan-review gate run assembles the ticket graph at most once (assert via the observability step counts / a read-counter spy).
- [ ] Verdict output is byte-identical to pre-change for a fixed fixture (characterization test).
- [ ] Measured store reads for an epic-with-K-children review drop from ~4×(2+K) to ~(2+K).
- [ ] Existing plan-review tests pass.

baseline.summary: Eliminate redundant ticket-graph re-assembly in plan-review gate

baseline.description:
## Context
The 2026-07-12 calibration analysis (session logs remarkable-hydrated-nightjar / tainted-continuing-queensnake / shaggy-linoleum-gavial) found: (1) code review is too loose — 0 'BLOCK — finding' votes across 162 post-recalibration changes while confirmed must-fix findings sailed through as advisories (change #529's untested-degradation advisory scored impact 0.0 and went red on main 57 minutes after merge; #518's importlib code-execution findings at 0.54; #539's correctness findings at 0.60 — against a 0.95 threshold no real finding ever reached); (2) plan-review advisory load is protocol-inflated — CLAUDE.md mandates remediating ALL valid advisories (~13/round, 95% of remediation edits mint new findings), and with the convergence floors now default-ON (change 562) we want to observe organic agent behavior instead of mandated remediation; (3) completion-verifier defects are structural, not admissibility: FAIL verdicts persist nowhere, FAILs ratchet piecemeal (3b4e took 2 extra CI cycles), and 'children closed (signed)' epic ACs defeat the certifiable:false escape hatch (bf50/5f39 contagion, bug 02a3); and (4) leaf plans DRIFT from their parent's plan as leaves are claimed and edited — by epic close a leaf's ACs can describe a materially different deliverable than the parent declared, and no plan-review criterion checks a leaf's scope against its PARENT (drift is caught only at epic-close completion verification, far too late). The review that gates the CLAIM is the right moment to catch drift ticket-by-ticket. This 4th finding motivates child d4cf (the new G7 leaf-plan parent-containment criterion).

## Definitions & Sequencing
- **"serious-tier" (Success Criterion 1):** the code-review criteria whose findings map to the SERIOUS (0.9) consequence binaries in `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` — prod-lane `data_loss_without_recovery`, `security_bypass_not_enforced_elsewhere`, `silent_wrong_feeding_a_decision`; maint-lane `unversioned_published_contract_break`, `safety_net_removal_without_replacement` — plus the `security` criterion. Child b9c0 enumerates the exact enabled set and pins it in a test; everything else stays advisory at 0.95.
- **code-v2 vs code-v3 cohort ordering (f32e vs 9f25/b9c0):** 9f25 derives, and b9c0 enables, a block threshold over the existing **code-v2** finding cohort — valid for code-v2 sidecars only. f32e adds a new maint binary and bumps `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` to **code-v3**, which per ADR-0036 starts a FRESH calibration cohort. Re-deriving/enabling any threshold over code-v3 is explicitly a FUTURE follow-up, NOT part of b9c0 — no threshold in this epic consumes code-v3. The two workstreams are independent by design; there is no ordering dependency between f32e and 9f25/b9c0, and b9c0's threshold governs code-v2 findings regardless of f32e's landing order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All child tickets (the epic's work items) are closed, each with its change landed on main.
- [ ] An in-session measurement-framework artifact is recorded as a comment on this epic: (a) the pre-change BASELINE from the 2026-07-12 analysis (0 finding-blocks / 162 changes; ~13 advisories/round), (b) the exact re-runnable queries/commands for post-change measurement — code-review block/false-block counts from the `REVIEW_RESULT` (code_review_result_v1) sidecars, and plan-review advisory-uptake via `norm_id` survival across rounds — and (c) a pointer to where the ACTUAL post-deployment field data will be recorded: the committed, CI-verifiable file `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/g7-promotion-path.md` (G7 fire-rate + promotion band) plus this AC2 comment's re-runnable queries. (This is created at merge time and IS verifiable in-session; the actual multi-day telemetry is explicitly deferred, below.)
- [ ] The deferred post-deployment measurement is DOCUMENTED (this epic's AC2 measurement-framework comment + the committed `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/g7-promotion-path.md`) and is picked up NATURALLY by the next calibration session — which re-runs those queries against post-deploy field data, exactly as the 2026-07-12 session analyzed the prior cohort. No standalone tracking ticket is retained: operator decision 2026-07-12, the interim idea ticket 72b6-b0d2-2f93-456d was closed as handled-by-process (the one substantive follow-up — b9c0's provisional 0.54 threshold needing a non-circular held-out adjudication — is preserved in b9c0's AC + the AC2 caveat). That telemetry is OUT of this epic's close path: this epic closes on the measurement FRAMEWORK being in place, not on multi-day field data existing.
- [ ] Code-review blocking is derived from adjudicated field data (the crossover threshold where a finding is more likely correctly-blocking than false-blocking), enabled for the serious-tier criteria (defined above), and passes the ADR-0036 A/B gate before flipping.
- [ ] Agent guidance no longer MANDATES advisory remediation (loosened to judgment, NOT reversed), so post-change review rounds measure organic advisory uptake.
- [ ] Completion-verifier FAILs are durably persisted and enumerate all unmet criteria in one verdict; the signed-children AC anti-pattern is documented.
- [ ] A plan-review criterion gates leaf-plan/parent-plan scope CONTAINMENT (a leaf's scope must be a subset of its parent's; the parent wins on conflict), firing on the claim-gating review so leaf drift is caught ticket-by-ticket instead of at epic close — shipped advisory per the ADR-0036 expand-contract pattern with fire-rate observable from day one (child d4cf).
baseline.summary: Review-gate calibration 2026-07-12: code-review blocking lane + advisory-guidance loosening + completion-verifier fixes

content.text: # BUG: config-file mcp.readonly not honored by the LLM runner's comment tool
## What

`runner.py:566-571` `_readonly_gate` reads only env `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`; `mcp_server.py:208-223` is config-aware. A server made read-only via `[mcp] readonly=true` (env unset) hides MCP write tools but a `source=local` gate run still grants the review agent `comment_ticket` (`runner.py:219`, `pai_tools.py`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both surfaces resolve read-only through one config-aware helper (env wins over file, fail-closed).
- [ ] Regression test: file-only readonly => the review agent's comment tool is withheld.
- [ ] Commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer.

baseline.summary: BUG: config-file mcp.readonly not honored by the LLM runner's comment tool

content.text: ## Summary

MCP reconcile tool runs Jira-MUTATING bootstrap modes with zero gating, even under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1. Verified LIVE (incident, remediated): a reconcile call with mode=bootstrap-strict from a sandboxed temp store, readonly server, executed against real Jira and created 19 real issues (DIG-5615..DIG-5633; all deleted, deletion verified by JQL).
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. Export REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 and build the MCP server (build_server()).
2. Call tool reconcile with {"mode": "bootstrap-strict"} (acli installed + credentialed).
3. Observe the pass runs and applies real Jira mutations (OK: applied 10 of 993).
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: any Jira-mutating mode requires REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE=1; a readonly server exposes at most reconcile-check/dry-run.
- Actual: bootstrap-strict/bootstrap-throttle mutate real Jira ungated under readonly; only mode=="live" is checked.
## Source
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:271-276 — gate checks only the literal string "live".
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py:106-112 — MODE_CAPS: BOOTSTRAP_STRICT=10, BOOTSTRAP_THROTTLE=100 APPLIED mutations/pass; only RECONCILE_CHECK/DRY_RUN are cap-0.
- Note dry-run is not a pure read either: it writes bridge_state/ and the invariants path files local bug tickets.
## Fix direction

Gate by capability, not string: parse the mode via the Mode enum and require the env var for any mode whose MODE_CAPS != 0; under _readonly(), restrict reconcile to cap-0 modes (or hide it). Correct docstrings + CLAUDE.md ("'live' mutates Jira" is dangerously incomplete — also __init__.py:404-409, tracked with bug frog-oryx-strut).
## Suggested RED test

Parametrize all five modes x {readonly, non-readonly} x {with, without REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE} with a fake acli on PATH that fails loudly if executed; assert only cap-0 modes pass without the env var and that readonly blocks mutating modes before any acli invocation. Never real credentials in tests.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] bootstrap-strict/bootstrap-throttle (and live) require REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE=1 over MCP
- [ ] Under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 no Jira-mutating reconcile mode is callable
- [ ] Invalid mode strings produce a clean tool error (not a crash)
- [ ] RED test matrix above lands first and goes GREEN with the fix
- [ ] Docstrings/CLAUDE.md updated to name all mutating modes

baseline.summary: MCP reconcile: bootstrap modes mutate real Jira ungated, even under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1

baseline.description:
## Reproduction Steps
The rebar review bot (compose-review-bot-1 on the rebar-gerrit EC2 host) clones each change into /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots to review it. These snapshots are never garbage-collected, so the 30G root disk fills to 100%.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: review workspace is bounded / cleaned per review.
- Actual: /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots grew to 14G; root fs hit 100%; clone_change_ref failed with 'No space left on device', which the voter surfaces as [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)] on EVERY change (observed on 452, 458, 461, 462). This fail-closed vetoes unrelated changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The review-bot's per-change clone/snapshot workspace is bounded or cleaned after each review (e.g. rm the snapshot on completion, or a periodic prune).
- [ ] A disk-usage guard/alarm so the host does not silently reach 100%.
- [ ] Document the manual recovery (docker builder prune + clear /tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots) in an infra runbook.

## Discovered
While landing epic breaded-ammonitic-elephant: change 458's LLM-Review persistently returned coverage-gap (review-error). Root cause via SSM was the full host disk, not the change.
baseline.summary: review-bot host disk fills up (rebar-gate-snapshots leak) -> coverage-gap review-errors

baseline.description:
## What

The central index `docs/README.md` is incomplete (4 living/normative docs unlinked) and
mixes living reference docs with historical evidence with no visual/structural
distinction. Complete the index and add a taxonomy — **in place, WITHOUT relocating any
files.**

Verified state (`origin/main`): exactly four `docs/*.md` are unlinked from the index —
`attest-substrate.md` (living developer API ref), `review-policy.md` (normative policy),
`session-id-shims.md` (living reference), and `dco-rollout-evidence.md` (historical). The
other historical docs (`88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md`, `bash-migration.md`) ARE already
linked, just not labeled as historical.

## Decision: label-in-place, NO git-mv (resolves the plan-review E2/T7/E4/G1G2 findings)
The audit floated "and/or move historical files under `docs/archive/`". **We deliberately
choose NOT to relocate any file.** Rationale: the inbound-link blast radius of moving these
files is large and cross-cutting — `bash-migration.md` alone is referenced by 8-10 `src/rebar/`
production docstrings, the root `README.md`, `docs/oss-comparison-and-remediation.md`, and
test files; `88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md` is referenced by
`infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh`. A `git-mv` would silently break all of these
for near-zero reader benefit. Instead, historical docs stay at their current paths and are
grouped under a clearly-labeled **"Historical evidence"** section in the index. No file
moves ⇒ no inbound link can break.

## Scope
- Add index entries for the 3 living/normative unlinked docs (`attest-substrate.md`,
  `review-policy.md`, `session-id-shims.md`) under the appropriate living-reference/policy
  buckets.
- Add a clearly-labeled **"Historical evidence"** section to the index and list the
  historical docs there (`dco-rollout-evidence.md` — currently unlinked, add it;
  `88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md` and `bash-migration.md` — move their LISTING into this
  section, files stay put).
- Add a short taxonomy note at the top of the index defining the buckets: **living
  reference / policy / design rationale / historical evidence** — so future docs land in
  the right place.
- Do NOT git-mv or move any file; do NOT edit any inbound links (nothing moves).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The 3 living/normative docs are each linked EXACTLY ONCE from the index
      (verify, prints nothing):
      `for b in attest-substrate.md review-policy.md session-id-shims.md; do [ "$(grep -cF "($b)" docs/README.md)" = 1 ] || echo "BAD $b"; done`
- [ ] The 3 historical docs are each linked EXACTLY ONCE (so the old Contributor
      entries for bash-migration.md / 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md were MOVED, not
      duplicated) AND appear under the "Historical evidence" heading (verify, prints
      nothing for both loops):
      `for b in dco-rollout-evidence.md 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md bash-migration.md; do [ "$(grep -cF "($b)" docs/README.md)" = 1 ] || echo "DUP/MISSING $b"; done`
      and
      `for b in dco-rollout-evidence.md 88ab-feature-branch-evidence.md bash-migration.md; do awk '/^## Historical evidence/{h=1;next} /^## /{h=0} h' docs/README.md | grep -qF "($b)" || echo "NOT-IN-SECTION $b"; done`
      (`grep -cF` is a LITERAL count — no regex/dot-escaping issues; `=1` catches both
      a missing link and a duplicate left behind in Contributor, closing the G6 gap.)
- [ ] A "Historical evidence" section heading exists and a brief taxonomy note defines
      the four buckets (verify, prints nothing):
      `grep -qi '^#\+ *Historical evidence' docs/README.md || echo "NO SECTION"; for t in 'living reference' 'policy' 'design rationale' 'historical evidence'; do grep -qi "$t" docs/README.md || echo "NO BUCKET: $t"; done`
- [ ] No file is relocated and no inbound link edited — only `docs/README.md` changes
      (verify): `git status --porcelain -- docs/` shows exactly one ` M docs/README.md`
      line and NO `R`/`D` (rename/delete) entries.

Files: `docs/README.md` (only).
