baseline.description:
# Realign rebar reviews to the three-pass (evidence -> binary-verify -> deterministic-gate) structure

## Context
Industry practice and 2025-2026 research converge: an LLM reviewer should surface cited evidence against a locked rubric; a SEPARATE agent should validate each finding via atomic binary sub-questions; and a DETERMINISTIC policy (not the model) should decide severity and blocking. LLMs are unreliable at holistic severity/confidence judgments, so neither is emitted by the model. This epic builds that shared three-pass framework and migrates rebar's existing reviewers onto it.

## Prerequisite foundations — current codebase state (2026-06)

Foundations shipped since this epic was written; the design is UNCHANGED, but the substrate is now CONCRETE for
parts and the reviewer migration is PARTLY done (the closed prerequisite epics are NOT reopened — this realigns
THIS epic to what they delivered):

- **Reviewer PROMPT migration DONE; three-pass STRUCTURE migration still pending (epic `da27`, closed).** The
  existing reviewers (`code_quality`/`security`/`tests`/`spec_alignment`/`ticket_quality`/`completion_verifier`)
  were migrated to the front-matter CONTRACT model — `inputs`/`outputs` schema-name contracts, `execution_mode`,
  `dimension`, `applies_to` globs, a derived index + CI drift gate (`src/rebar/llm/prompts.py`, `reviewers/*.md`).
  That is the PROMPT-STORAGE half of 'migrate existing reviewers'. They still emit the OLD pass-1 shape
  `{findings:[{severity, dimension, detail, citations}], summary}`, NOT this epic's pass-1 EVIDENCE contract
  `{finding, criteria[], evidence[], scenarios[], impact}` — migrating the pass-1 SHAPE + adding Pass-2/Pass-3 is
  THIS epic's remaining work, layered on the already-contracted prompts.
- **Pass-1 data substrate (partial) + single-pass `review_code`.** `src/rebar/llm/findings.py`
  (`normalize_finding`, citation coercion, schema validation) + `src/rebar/llm/aggregate.py` (cluster +
  severity×agreement rank) exist; `review_code` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`) runs reviewers + aggregates today
  as a SINGLE PASS. There is NO Pass-2 verifier agent and NO Pass-3 deterministic gate yet — both are NEW WORK here.
- **Provider-agnostic runner + workflow engine (epic `e6d9`, closed).** `PydanticAIRunner` (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py`)
  is the sole runtime (LangGraph cut over), honoring the `execution_mode` {single_turn|agentic} seam — the substrate
  Pass-1 and the separate-context Pass-2 verifier run on; the declarative workflow engine (`run_workflow`) + the
  Inspect-AI eval seam shipped alongside.
- **Code-grounding for Pass-2 (epic `8f6c`, closed).** `src/rebar/grounding/` (the `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan`
  facade, exported from `src/rebar/grounding/__init__.py`) is the substrate for Pass-2's RE-GROUNDING in the actual
  code + the cited-code-reference-accuracy VETO. The overlay catalogs' 'Scanner pre-pass (Semgrep/Gitleaks/Trivy)'
  maps to the oracle's EXTENSIBLE detector registry (`detectors/registry.py`; OpenGrep/ast-grep shipped) — but
  security/secrets/CVE detectors are NOT yet shipped (only `smell_generic` + applicability), so those remain new
  work (here or shared with the code-review capability epic `b744`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pass-1 finding contract: `{finding (free text), criteria[] (each in the prompt's locked rubric set), evidence[] (flexible free text: code citations, prose, OR absence rationale), scenarios[] (free text), impact (free text)}`. Criteria is an array. No model severity/confidence.
- [ ] Pass-2 verifier = a separate agent / independent context that re-grounds in the actual code (via the shipped 8f6c grounding-oracle facade `refute_absence`/`scan` for cited-reference + smell grounding) and emits per finding: (a) severity attributes `{prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility}` (coarse ordinals); (b) typed binary sub-answers `{verdict: yes|no|insufficient, evidence_span/reason}`.
- [ ] Binary sub-question set (typed): the ONLY veto is cited-code-reference-accuracy, applied ONLY when a code citation is present (no-op for absence findings / non-code reviews); all others GRADED: is-verifiable (signal), evidence-entails-finding, path-reachable, impact-follows-necessarily, no-viable-alternative-explanation, no-existing-mitigation, severity-claim-justified.
- [ ] Pass-3 deterministic aggregator: conditional veto gate -> graded confidence (weighted fraction / log-odds) -> severity-from-attributes -> `block | advisory` against per-criteria thresholds (project-overridable; defaults start high -> almost all findings advisory while calibration data is gathered). No interactive escalation path (autonomous).
- [ ] Verifier prompt obeys the research rules: atomicity (one proposition per question); independence (do not show the finding's own conclusion when answering each sub-question); verdict-with-citation, NOT verdict-with-proposed-fix; allow "insufficient".
- [ ] Existing code-review reviewers (review_ticket and the code-quality/security/tests reviewers) migrated to the pass-1 EVIDENCE contract + shared pass-2/pass-3 — these are ALREADY on the da27 front-matter CONTRACT model (inputs/outputs/execution_mode/dimension/applies_to + derived index), so this is the pass-1-SHAPE + Pass-2/Pass-3 migration ON TOP of that, NOT a from-scratch reviewer rewrite; findings schema extended (`src/rebar/llm/findings.py`); aggregation + citation-resolution + schema-pin tests updated. (completion_verifier is OUT OF SCOPE: not migrated, unchanged.)
- [ ] Rubric sourced from Google eng-practices + Anthropic security taxonomy (locked + versioned); Conventional Comments not adopted.
- [ ] Known limitations recorded: veto-brittleness mitigated by the single conditional veto; decomposition controls validity PRECISION not finding-type RECALL; threshold calibration is explicitly out of scope (separate future work).
- [ ] All rebar reviews emit the pass-1 evidence contract; a shared pass-2 verifier agent and pass-3 deterministic aggregator exist and are used.
- [ ] Severity is computed deterministically from structured attributes; validity/confidence from typed binary sub-answers. No model-emitted severity number, confidence number, or high/med/low rating in the decision path.
baseline.summary: Realign rebar reviews to three-pass (evidence -> binary-verify -> deterministic gate); migrate existing reviewers

baseline.description:
## Why

A review pipeline runs N criteria-prompts in budgeted BATCHES (one LLM call per batch), with runtime
fallback (split -> one-per-call -> escalate model) on a context-limit. No surveyed engine makes
adaptive cost-budgeted batching first-class — it is app code everywhere — and encoding it in the IR
would break replay determinism (batch composition depends on a runtime token estimate + which call
hit a context limit). So the IR gets a THIN step that delegates the adaptive work to a runner.

## What

Add a `batch` step kind whose IR surface is purely declarative parameters: `group` (the prompt set),
`usd_budget`, `model_ladder`. A batch-runner SEAM (protocol) performs the adaptive packing /
token-estimation / context-limit fallback / model-escalation / shed-to-INDETERMINATE / fingerprint-
checkpoint, and JOURNALS its batch-plan + fallback transitions as OPAQUE events. The interpreter
STORES the journaled plan as an output but NEVER branches on its internals (thin-interpreter / Burr-
tripwire preserved). Ship a reference/default batch-runner; epic B supplies the production runner
(extracted from the gate's sizing.py) behind this seam.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py + JSON Schema: the `batch` step kind + its params + validation.
- A batch-runner protocol/seam (alongside AgentStepRunner in executor.py) + a reference default runner.
- The journaled batch-plan / fallback event vocabulary (recorded decisions, not recomputed).
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py: invoke the batch-runner, store the opaque plan as the step
  output; the interpreter must not interpret batch internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `batch` step parses + schema-validates with `group`/`usd_budget`/`model_ladder`; bad params
      are validation errors.
- [ ] A batch-runner SEAM exists with a reference default runner; the runner journals its batch-plan
      + fallback transitions as opaque recorded events.
- [ ] The interpreter stores the journaled plan as the step output and NEVER branches on its
      internals (a test asserts this); replay reads the recorded plan rather than recomputing it.
- [ ] The Burr-tripwire stays green (no asyncio/threading/concurrent leaks outside the confined
      fan-out path).
- [ ] make lint + the workflow test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Batch step: a thin delegating step kind + batch-runner seam + reference runner (journaled batch-plan)

baseline.description:
## GHA reconcile-bridge: sign inbound writes inline + inject key

CRITICAL: the reconciler's inbound writer (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`
`_write_event_file`, ~214-259) calls the `rebar._store` primitives DIRECTLY, bypassing
`_seam.append_event`, and stamps only `author` (no `author_email`/`author_id`/`author_sig`).
So Jira-sourced events classify `unknown-author`/`unsigned` under `verify-identity`. Config
alone is insufficient — this needs a code fix.

### Chosen approach: stamp + sign INLINE (not via `_seam.append_event`)

Enrich the event dict in `_write_event_file` BEFORE it is serialized/written:
1. `event.update(_seam.attribution_fields(repo_root))` — adds `author_email` and (when a
   current identity resolves) `author_id`.
2. `_seam._apply_authorship(event, ticket_id, event_type, data, str(tracker_dir), repo_root)`
   — when `author_id` + `identity.signing_key` are present, signs the canonical event bytes
   and stores the DSSE envelope under `author_sig` (best-effort; a miss writes unsigned).

**Rationale (why inline, NOT `_seam.append_event`):** `append_event` calls `write_and_push()`,
which COMMITS + PUSHES per event; `_write_event_file` intentionally writes an uncommitted file
so the reconciler's own orchestration can batch-commit the pass. Routing through
`append_event` would break that batch-commit model and thread `repo_root`/`tracker` through
12+ call sites. Inline stamping reuses the exact seam helpers, preserves the uncommitted-file
model, and is minimal blast radius. The added author fields are additive (older readers ignore
unknown keys — no store-format break). `_write_event_file` will need `repo_root` available
(derive from `tracker_dir.parent` or `config.repo_root()`).

### Prerequisite (SATISFIED)

Signing resolves `author_id` only if a Rebar Bot identity ticket with
`email=joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` exists — it does (task bffe created identity
`594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d`, public key registered). So with `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL` = that address the
git-email resolver maps reconciler writes to the bot identity.

### Workflow wiring

In `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: write `secrets.REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` to a
job-local file (`mktemp`, `chmod 600`, `::add-mask::` the value), set `identity.signing_key`
(or `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`) to that path, and set `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL=joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com`
(currently `rebar-bridge@users.noreply.github.com`) so git-email resolution maps to the bot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_write_event_file` stamps `author_email`/`author_id` (via `_seam.attribution_fields`) and signs `author_sig` (via `_seam._apply_authorship`) inline before writing; a reconciler-authored event written with the bot identity + a signing key verifies as `verified` under `rebar verify-authorship` (proven by a unit test that configures a bot identity + signing key, drives `_write_event_file`, and asserts the written event carries `author_id`/`author_email`/`author_sig` and verifies).
- [ ] Additive-fields regression test: a unit test constructs an event WITHOUT the new author fields (older-format) and asserts the reducer / `rebar show` still round-trips it cleanly (unknown/absent keys ignored, no format break). The batch-commit orchestration is unchanged (no eager commit/push added to the inbound path).
- [ ] `reconcile-bridge.yml` writes the key to a `chmod 600` job-local file, `::add-mask::`s it, and sets `identity.signing_key`/`REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` to that path. For the committer email: the existing "Configure git identity" step reads `BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL || 'rebar-bridge@users.noreply.github.com' }}` — CHANGE that fallback default to `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` (so resolution maps to the bot identity without depending on a repo variable being set; the `vars.BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL` override still wins if present). The key is never logged or committed.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: GHA reconcile-bridge: route inbound writes through signing seam + inject key

baseline.description:
## Problem

The review-bot's shutdown drain covers only HALF of its review paths.

`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`'s lifespan does:

    await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=shutdown_drain_seconds())

then cancels every task, bounded by `shutdown_cancel_seconds()` (10s).

`queue.join()` waits for the webhook QUEUE to empty, so a webhook-queued review IS protected (1200s drain, and compose grants `stop_grace_period: 1320s` — both far exceed the ~10 min review).

But `reconcile.reconcile_once` awaits `review_and_vote` INLINE, not through the queue. When the queue is empty, `queue.join()` returns IMMEDIATELY and the `reconcile_loop` task is cancelled within ~10s — abandoning a backfill review that may be minutes in.

Found while implementing [rebar:34cd-1a7c-b9b1-4b05]; verified by reading origin/main d4095763e3.

## Why it matters independently of 34cd

34cd fixes this from the DEPLOY side: autodeploy now defers a container recreation while `/health` reports `in_flight > 0`, so the autodeploy path no longer kills reconciler reviews.

The underlying drain gap is untouched by that. ANY other container stop still kills a reconciler review with effectively no drain:
  - an operator `docker compose restart` / `up -d` run by hand
  - `compose-up.sh` during a manual deploy
  - a host reboot / systemd stop
  - the rollback path inside autodeploy itself (`docker compose up -d` after re-tagging `:prev`)

The reconciler is also the path that RETRIES a review killed by anything else, so the gap sits on the self-heal path. And it is silent for the same reason 34cd was: a cancelled review fails nothing, so no `VOTER_ERROR` is emitted and `restarts` stays 0.

## Suspected fix

Make the drain cover in-flight reconciler work, not just the queue — e.g. have the lifespan wait on the same in-flight review count that 34cd added (`voter.in_flight_reviews()`) under the existing `shutdown_drain_seconds()` budget, before cancelling tasks. The budget and `stop_grace_period` are already sized for a full review, so this likely needs no new tunables.

Note the ordering constraint: the wait must not let a reconcile pass START a NEW review while draining, or shutdown could be extended repeatedly. The reconciler probably needs a stop-accepting-new-work signal alongside the drain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reconciler review in flight at shutdown is drained (bounded by the existing
      `shutdown_drain_seconds()`), not cancelled within `shutdown_cancel_seconds()`.
- [ ] The drain does not extend indefinitely: no new review may start once shutdown has begun,
      proven by a test.
- [ ] The existing webhook-queue drain behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Shutdown drain misses the reconciler's in-flight review, so any container stop kills it

content.text: ## What
**Retire the band-aids** now that the ref-lock (C3) is proven, flip the default backend to `ref`,
and remove the dead file-lock machinery + `merge=ours` entry, with a migration for existing repos.
**Depends on: 2711-21bf-ab71-4136 (C3).** The ref backend must be wired and validated first;
removing the file backend / retry loop before C3 would leave the reconciler with no working lock.
- Flip `[reconciler] lock_backend` default to `ref` and remove the `file` backend path from
`_advisory_lock.py` once the ref backend has baked.
- **Remove the `b859-8fa1` retry loop** in `acquire_pass_lock` AND its now-dead helpers
(`_resolve_retry_budget`, `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, `_compute_backoff_seconds`, and the
b859-only backoff constants). Retire the config key `lock_max_retries` (`_config_schema.py`
`ReconcilerConfig` field + coercion entry) and its env aliases
(`REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES` + deprecated alias `REBAR_RECONCILER_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET` in
`config.py`). Delete/adjust the tests that exercise them:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock_retry_jitter.py`, and the retry-budget
assertions in `tests/.../test_config_file_wiring.py` + `test_ev3c_env_renames.py`.
- **Deprecation path for the retired config key.** `lock_max_retries` removal is operator-visible;
rather than a hard break, treat a still-present `lock_max_retries` as **deprecated** — emit a
one-time deprecation warning (config-load path) and ignore it — and note the removal in
`docs/config.md` + the changelog, so existing operator configs do not error on upgrade.
- **Remove `.reconciler-*` from `_GITATTRIBUTES`** in `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (leave
`.bridge_state/* merge=ours` untouched — that is WS-1 binding data, out of scope), and update
`tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` to assert `.reconciler-*` is absent and
`.bridge_state/*` still present.
- **Migration for already-initialized trackers:** `_commit_gitattributes` is create-if-absent only,
so editing the constant does not fix existing repos. Add an update-migration arm (mirroring the
`_commit_gitignore` line-migration) that strips the `.reconciler-* merge=ours` line from an
already-committed `.gitattributes`. Idempotent; on git failure, log-and-continue (do not abort).
- **One-time cleanup:** remove any pre-existing `.reconciler-pass-lock`/`.reconciler-phase-gate`
committed on the tickets branch from the old scheme (a single named helper, idempotent, invoked
from exactly one site — reconciler startup; state the site explicitly).
- Extend the ref-lock ADR to record that the b859 loop is superseded by the C3 self-healing lock.
## Design decisions (resolves plan-review ambiguities; binding on the implementation)
1. **Precise removal set (verified dead by grep, not by line number).** After the file backend is
gone, delete every symbol left with zero consumers: the file dispatch branches in
`acquire_pass_lock` / `release_pass_lock` / `check_phase_gate`; `_write_file_to_tickets_branch`,
`_delete_file_from_tickets_branch`, `_commit_in_detached_tickets_worktree`,
`_git_show_tickets_file`, the file-based `check_pass_lock`, the `_LOCK_FILE`/`_GATE_FILE`
constants; the b859 outer-retry loop + `_resolve_retry_budget` / `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT` /
`_compute_backoff_seconds`; and `_cas_advance_with_retry` / `_cas_backoff_seconds` /
`_jittered_backoff` / the backoff constants **iff** grep confirms no remaining consumer once the
file backend is deleted. **KEEP** `_cas_once` and `_is_cas_mismatch` — they are imported by
`_ref_lock.py` and are the shared CAS discriminator. Every deletion is justified by a
zero-consumer grep across `src/` and `tests/`.
2. **`lock_backend` post-removal.** Keep the key (default now `ref`); the acquire/release/gate
dispatch becomes unconditional ref. A still-configured `lock_backend=file` is
**deprecated-and-ignored**: a one-time warning is logged and the ref backend is used anyway
(rollback via `file` is intentionally gone — ref is proven). The `{file, ref}` choice validator
stays so the value still parses.
3. **`lock_max_retries` deprecation mechanics.** Removing the `ReconcilerConfig.lock_max_retries`
field means a config that still sets it hits `Config.from_mapping`'s existing **unknown-key
path**, which WARNs-and-ignores under the default non-strict load — exactly the required
"one-time warning, not a load error". Verify no reconciler config-load site passes `strict=True`
(which would reject it); if one does, add `lock_max_retries` to an explicit deprecated-and-ignored
set rather than letting it error. The env aliases are removed from `config.py`'s env map.
4. **Migrations — two distinct, idempotent, single-site helpers.**
(a) *gitattributes line-strip* lives in `init.py` (an update arm on `_commit_gitattributes`,
mirroring the `_commit_gitignore` line-migration): if the committed `.gitattributes` contains a
`.reconciler-*` line, rewrite without it and commit; on any git failure log-and-continue (never
abort init). (b) *committed-lock-file cleanup* is a single named helper (e.g.
`_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`) invoked from exactly one site — the reconciler startup in
`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:main()`, before the pass acquires — that deletes any
`.reconciler-pass-lock` / `.reconciler-phase-gate` still committed on the tickets branch (no-op if
absent → idempotent; git failure log-and-continue).
5. **Regression test.** A test asserts no `.reconciler-*` path is ever committed to the tickets
branch after a ref-backend pass (and that the cleanup helper removes a pre-seeded one).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lock_backend` defaults to `ref`; the file-lock backend + the `b859` retry loop are deleted,
along with `_resolve_retry_budget`, `_LOCK_RETRY_BUDGET_DEFAULT`, `_compute_backoff_seconds`,
any then-dead backoff/CAS-retry helpers (grep-verified), the `lock_max_retries` config field +
coercion + env aliases, and their tests. `_cas_once`/`_is_cas_mismatch` are kept (used by
`_ref_lock`). A configured `lock_backend=file` is deprecated-and-ignored (one-time warning).
- [ ] `.reconciler-*` is removed from `_GITATTRIBUTES`; `.bridge_state/*` is left in place;
`tests/interfaces/store/test_gitattributes_merge.py` updated accordingly.
- [ ] A `.gitattributes` update-migration (mirroring `_commit_gitignore`) strips
`.reconciler-* merge=ours` from already-committed trackers; idempotent; git failure logs and
continues rather than aborting.
- [ ] A single, named, idempotent startup migration (invoked from `__main__.main()` before acquire)
removes any pre-existing committed `.reconciler-*` files; a regression test asserts no
`.reconciler-*` path is ever committed to the tickets branch.
- [ ] `lock_max_retries` is handled as deprecated-and-ignored (one-time warning, not a load error)
and its removal is documented in `docs/config.md` + changelog.
- [ ] Full non-integration suite green.

baseline.summary: Retire merge=ours .gitattributes + b859 lock-retry band-aid; migrate committed locks

baseline.description:
## Problem

Several reconciler test helpers load engine modules by path with this pattern:

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    mod  = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)   # <-- does NOT replace an existing entry
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)        # <-- but execs into the NEW object
    return mod                          # <-- and returns the NEW object

When `sys.modules[name]` is already populated (another test file in the same worker loaded it first), `setdefault` keeps the OLD module object while the helper execs and returns a NEW one. Any engine module that then does `import mutation` resolves the OLD object, so the class the code constructs and the class the test asserts against are DIFFERENT objects with the same name.

Symptom, from CI (macos-latest, py3.13):

    tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ.py::test_new_key_in_local_produces_outbound_create_mutation
    >   assert isinstance(m, mutation_mod.Mutation)
    E   AssertionError: assert False
    E    +  where False = isinstance(Mutation(direction=..., action=..., target='DSO-42'...), <class 'mutation.Mutation'>)

## Why it surfaced now

It is latent and ORDER-DEPENDENT, so it only fires when a particular pair of files lands in the same xdist worker. Change 1043 (story 2932) added tests, which changed sharding: patchset 1 passed CI, patchset 2 failed twice deterministically, with the only delta being added tests in an unrelated subsystem. The reconciler code itself is untouched by that change.

Not reproducible on a py3.14 local venv even running the whole `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/` directory in one process; the failing CI job is py3.13 on macos-latest. Treat CI as the reproducer.

## Fix

Make the helper return the module that is ACTUALLY registered, so exactly one class object exists per name:

    existing = sys.modules.get(name)
    if existing is not None and getattr(existing, '__file__', None) == str(path):
        return existing
    ... module_from_spec ...
    sys.modules[name] = mod        # assign, do not setdefault
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

The path guard matters: these names (`mutation`, `differ`, `applier`) are generic, so blindly reusing any same-named module could bind to something unrelated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] no reconciler test helper uses `sys.modules.setdefault` for by-path module loading: `grep -rn 'sys.modules.setdefault' tests/` is empty
- [ ] a test asserts the helper returns the SAME object on a second call for the same name+path (one class object per name)
- [ ] a test asserts a same-name/different-path load does NOT silently reuse the wrong module
- [ ] [operator-attested] CI is green on macos-latest/py3.13 for a change that previously reproduced the failure, evidenced by the Gerrit change id and its Verified +1 recorded in a comment
baseline.summary: Reconciler test _load_module uses sys.modules.setdefault, yielding two class objects and order-dependent isinstance failures

baseline.description:
## Why
The code-review gate cast ZERO 'BLOCK — finding' votes across 162 changes since the code-v2 impact model landed, while 76% of changes carried advisories and at least three carried confirmed must-fix findings (#529 impact 0.0 — proved out on main within the hour; #518 importlib code-execution at 0.54; #539 correctness at 0.60). Observed impact distribution clusters at {0, 0.32, 0.36, 0.54, 0.60} with an apparent 0.60 ceiling — the 0.95 default threshold is unreachable. Before enabling blocking we need the empirically-correct threshold, not a guess: the operator's decision rule is the crossover point at which a finding is MORE LIKELY correctly-blocking than false-blocking (0.6 is the prior/starting hypothesis).

## What
- Assemble the post-2026-07-08 code-v2 corpus: the ~149 deduplicated code-review finding records in the ticket store (.tickets-tracker). NOTE on schema: code-review sidecars use `schema: code_review_result_v1` and store findings under `blocking`/`advisory`/`coaching` buckets (each with an `impact`), keyed by `target_ticket`/`change_fingerprint` — NOT the plan-review `plan_review_result_v1` shape (`findings`/`material_fingerprint`). Join to their Gerrit changes and post-merge history (follow-up fix commits, red-main incidents).
- Adjudicate each finding with impact >= 0.3 as block-worthy vs not (blind to its score where feasible), mirroring the b463 plan-review methodology (manual scoring of the would-block slice; Sonnet-scored simulation with held-out adjudication acceptable for scale).
- Compute precision over the SAME decision quantity the gate actually thresholds on — NOT raw impact. The code-review block decision (pass3_decide/decide.py) compares a finding's PRIORITY = validity × impact against `block_threshold`, so the derivation computes precision(block-worthy | priority >= t) across candidate t in {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.54, 0.6}; select the SMALLEST t where precision > 0.5, tie-broken toward fewer false blocks. (Recording raw-impact percentiles too is fine for transparency, but the derived threshold must be in priority units so b9c0 can consume it directly.) Explicitly analyze the 0.54 band (the #518 security findings) and whether the 0.60 ceiling means t=0.6 only ever catches max-priority findings.
- DERIVATION TOOLING (corrected): `calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py` reads the PLAN-review sidecar schema and CANNOT consume code-review sidecars — do NOT reuse it for this corpus. Instead commit a dedicated code-review derivation script under docs/experiments/ (e.g. `derive_code_review_threshold.py`) that loads the `code_review_result_v1` sidecars (blocking/advisory buckets), joins the adjudication labels, and computes precision(block-worthy | priority >= t) across the candidate thresholds — reading each finding's stored `priority` field straight from the sidecar (decide.py:336-338 writes it; the sidecar preserves it). TWO DISTINCT STEPS (do not conflate them): (1) `docs/experiments/ab_impact_model.py` is the impact-MODEL separation gate — it scores the STATIC `tests/unit/fixtures/code_review_impact_labels.jsonl` HIGH/NIT fixture and gates that the code-v2 impact model separates HIGH from NIT (the ADR-0036 model-quality prerequisite). It does NOT derive a threshold from the real corpus. (2) the THRESHOLD is derived by the new `derive_code_review_threshold.py` over the real `code_review_result_v1` sidecar corpus (precision-crossover). Run (1) to confirm the model is sound, then use (2) to pick the smallest t with precision > 0.5. If extending the existing calibrator is preferred over a new script, its loader must first be taught the code-review schema and that documented — but the default is the standalone code-review script.

## Scope
Analysis + a written threshold recommendation committed as a REPO ARTIFACT under docs/experiments/ (e.g. `derive_code_review_threshold.md` or the script's `--emit-recommendation` output file) recording the chosen threshold + the precision-crossover / 0.54-band / 0.60-ceiling analyses (a ticket comment may mirror it, but the committed file is the verifiable artifact); NO routing/config change here (that is the sibling enablement story).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The adjudicated corpus is committed under docs/experiments/ (e.g. `code_review_adjudication.jsonl`) with the derivation script/notebook. SCHEMA (define the value vocabulary): each row is `{finding_id: str, criterion: str, impact: float, validity: float, priority: float, adjudication: "block-worthy" | "not-block-worthy" | "ambiguous", evidence: str (the follow-up-fix commit / red-main incident / reviewer rationale grounding the call)}`. SOURCE of validity/impact/priority (code-grounded): each `code_review_result_v1` sidecar finding already carries `validity`, `impact`, AND `priority` — they are the pass-3 decision fields `pass3_decide` writes per finding (decide.py:336-338) and the sidecar preserves in its `blocking`/`advisory` arrays. So the corpus is a STRAIGHT PROJECTION of those stored fields (no reconstruction, no separate validity source needed); the derivation reads the stored `priority` directly and computes precision(block-worthy | priority >= t) over it — priority is exactly what the gate thresholds on. `adjudication` uses exactly that three-value closed vocabulary (block-worthy = a human would want this to block; not-block-worthy = advisory-appropriate; ambiguous = excluded from the precision computation, counted separately).
- [ ] The chosen threshold and its precision-crossover justification (with the 0.54-band and 0.60-ceiling analyses) are committed as a REPO ARTIFACT under docs/experiments/ — CI-verifiable that the file exists and names a numeric threshold (not only a ticket comment).
- [ ] The ADR-0036 A/B gate result (HIGH<->NIT separation vs baseline) is recorded and passes.
- [ ] The derivation logic is unit-tested UNDER `tests/` (not only in docs/experiments/, which `make lint`/`make test` do not traverse): add `tests/unit/test_derive_code_review_threshold.py` (or a `scripts`-marked test) that imports the derivation module and asserts the precision-over-priority computation on a tiny in-test fixture — so the logic is covered by `make test`. The script itself is additionally proven by a direct run: `.venv/bin/python docs/experiments/derive_code_review_threshold.py --corpus <path>` producing the recorded threshold.
- [ ] make lint passes repo-wide (ruff config governs whether docs/experiments/ is linted; the committed script conforms to whatever scope applies).
- [ ] make test passes repo-wide, including the new tests/ derivation-logic test.
baseline.summary: Derive the code-review block threshold from the adjudicated code-v2 finding distribution

# Code-review 'new-behavior-without-test' landmine detector

## Context (discovered from grusome-uncheerful-nematode)
Child #7 originally bundled two changes: (a) the docs/llm-prompts nit down-rank (shipped in #7)
and (b) a grounding-assisted detector that fires when a diff adds new public behavior with no
correlated test. Investigation during the epic established that (b) needs a BESPOKE seam that
does not exist yet, so it was split out here to keep #7 landable.

## Why it needs a bespoke seam (not an existing one)
- Code-review DET detectors are **Engine B** grounding rules (gitleaks/opengrep-style YAML
  pattern rules) selected by `exec: DET` routing `detector` selectors and run via
  `run_detectors` -> `engine_b.scan`. A 'new-behavior-without-test' check requires diff-parsing
  the added public definitions AND cross-file correlation to test files — that is NOT the
  pattern-matching model Engine B implements.
- `rebar.grounding.resolve.extract_references_from_diff` extracts **imports only** (Python), not
  added symbol DEFINITIONS, so it cannot supply the added-definition set the detector needs.

## Sketch of the required seam
A Python code-review detector (in `code_review/detectors.py` or a new module) invoked in the DET
phase that: (1) parses the unified diff for newly-added exported/public defs via ast-grep /
universal-ctags (language-aware); (2) correlates against added/updated test files; (3) FIRES
(advisory/permissive first) when a new public def has no correlated test; (4) ABSTAINS
fail-open on: unparseable/garbled diff, no grounding backend available, or docs/config-only
change. Coaching surfaces through the existing `code_review_coach` path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A grounding-assisted `new_behavior_without_test` detector exists and is wired into the
      code-review DET phase, using real ast-grep/ctags grounding (added-definition extraction,
      NOT imports-only), shipped advisory/permissive first.
- [ ] MUST-FIRE (new public def, no test) / MUST-NOT-FIRE (def with a correlated test) /
      ABSTAIN (docs-only, unparseable, no backend) unit tests.
- [ ] Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_new_behavior_detector.py -v`.
baseline.summary: Code-review 'new-behavior-without-test' landmine detector (bespoke diff-parse + cross-file test-correlation seam)

## Why

The core driver of the visual-editing goal is letting developers ADD / REMOVE / EDIT individual
CRITERIA. With the A2 shape, the batch step's `criteria` list is a static authored list of
prompt-library-backed entries — discrete nodes the editor can represent and modify. Proving the
add/remove-criterion round-trip end-to-end is the editability deliverable AND part of A's de-risking
of B (the criteria-library <-> prompt-library <-> editor wiring).

## What

Extend the workflow visual editor (docs/workflow-editor.md) to render and edit a `batch` step's
`criteria` list — each entry a prompt-library-backed criterion with its optional `when` overlay —
and support ADD / REMOVE / EDIT of a criterion. Also render/edit the `batch` params
(prompt/finder, usd_budget, model_ladder) and a prompt step's `if:` overlay predicate (the existing
field; confirm + extend only as needed). Preserve the engine invariants: clean git diffs +
schema-validated text round-trip (the e6d9 editor invariant). The demo workflow is the refinement sample.

## Scope

- The workflow editor surface (bpmn-js / editor assets + the Python render/round-trip; see
  docs/workflow-editor.md + tests/e2e/test_editor_* / tests/unit/workflow/test_bpmn.py).
- Render + edit the `batch` step (criteria list + params) and the `if:` overlay predicate;
  ADD/REMOVE/EDIT a prompt-backed criterion in the criteria list.
- Round-trip keeps clean git diffs + schema validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The editor renders a `batch` step's `criteria` list (each a prompt-library-backed entry + its
      `when`) and supports ADD / REMOVE / EDIT of a criterion; it also renders the batch params and a
      prompt step's `if:` overlay predicate.
- [ ] Editor round-trip preserves clean git diffs + schema-validated text (the e6d9 invariant) — an
      add/remove-criterion round-trips losslessly.
- [ ] An editor test covers rendering + add/remove/edit of a criterion in the batch criteria list.
- [ ] make lint + the relevant editor/workflow tests pass.
baseline.summary: Visual editing for the new constructs (overlay predicate + batch step) in the workflow editor

## Context

Adoption epic for the DSO vs rebar plan-review gap analysis (~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md). Each remediation was evaluated in a design session (2026-07) against rebar's architecture (four-pass find->verify->decide->coach, deterministic Pass-3, locked coach MOVE_REGISTRY, DET floor, REVIEW_RESULT sidecar) under one lens: does rebar already solve this better at a different level, and does the remediation work WITH rebar's grain?

Guiding principle preserved throughout: rebar's multi-pass separation is the reliable substrate (DSO's own bug history validates it). We adopt DSO's CONTENT (detection lexicons, named FP classes, calibration idioms) to upgrade pass *content* to match pass *structure* -- never importing DSO's weaker mechanisms (self-scored persona committees, hard-gate anti-rationalization prose, lexical word-match).

Scope note: WS1-WS10 are DSO-report-sourced adoptions. WS11 (removal-rationale / Chesterton's Fence) is a NET-NEW criterion gap surfaced during this evaluation -- NOT in the DSO report -- filed here as an 11th workstream per design decision, so the epic is "plan-review criteria gaps found in this evaluation" (DSO-sourced + one net-new).

## Context (evaluated but NOT in this epic)
- G-1+G-2 (conflict/oscillation) -> epic grumpy-gland-rose (dedicated brainstorm)
- G-6 (cross-ticket interaction) -> epic only-crave-art (store-wide, outside the gate)
- R-1 part 2 (blocking-tier context isolation) -> placeholder epic fort-wisp-wren (depends on R-1 part 1 cohort field, shipped here)
- R-4 (calibration-example library) -> placeholder epic spin-cub-usher
- REJECTED: R-2 (double-verify; distinct criteria already give perspective diversity), T9 RETIRE-row rule (nit), the persona-committee / hard-gate-prose / word-match items (Section 7)
- NOTED, separate track: E5/E6 proxy-validation & cutover-e2e are advisory, so bypass-the-real-path incomplete implementations can slip both gates -- a threshold-calibration question handled outside this epic.

## Workstreams (child stories)
- WS1 Pass-2 vocabulary expansion; WS2 E4/exec:DET detectors; WS3 enumeration-overlay; WS4 DET verify-command blacklist; WS5 rubric enrichments; WS6 self-calibration anchors; WS7 prompt-hardening pass; WS8 coach moves; WS9 sidecar cohort field; WS10 docs + authoring surface (all DSO-sourced).
- WS11 removal-rationale criterion (Chesterton's Fence, removal-side dual of A1) -- NET-NEW, not from the DSO report.

## Integration ordering (shared files -- land in this order to avoid clobbering)
- plan_review_verifier.md + _agentic.md are edited by WS1 (new sub-answers), WS6 (blast_radius ratchet), WS7 (shared preamble). Land WS1 -> WS6 -> WS7.
- docs/plan-review-gate.md is edited by WS8 (MOVE_REGISTRY table), WS10 (R-3 invariant + tuning checklist) -- disjoint sections; coordinate the two edits.
- criteria_routing.json is edited by WS2 (hedge 1-TURN + E4), WS3 (two overlay criteria) -- disjoint entries.
- passes.py is edited by WS7 (_resolve_system preamble), WS8 (MOVE_REGISTRY), WS9 (cohort stamps) -- disjoint functions.
- WS9 (cohort field) is the prerequisite for placeholder epic fort-wisp-wren.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 11 child stories created capturing the design decisions (WS1-WS10 DSO-sourced + WS11 net-new Chesterton's Fence)
- [ ] Related design/placeholder epics linked (grumpy-gland-rose, only-crave-art, fort-wisp-wren, spin-cub-usher)
- [ ] This epic is the durable home for the plan-review criteria-gap effort surfaced in this evaluation
- [ ] Each of the 11 adopted workstreams (child stories WS1-WS11) is implemented and eval-guarded where it changes reviewer behavior. "Eval-guarded" = a change that alters reviewer OUTPUT (finder/verifier/coach behavior) ships with a recall AND/OR precision case in the eval-spec harness (src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/*.eval.yaml); a change that does not alter reviewer output (docs, mechanical, sidecar plumbing) ships with a deterministic unit check instead.
- [ ] Generic passes (Pass 2 verify contract, Pass 4 coach) stay generic across findings -- criterion-specific logic lives in criterion rubrics/evidence, not in the shared passes (WS11's sub-answers are criterion-local, not GRADED_BINARY additions)
- [ ] No new blocking behavior ships without calibration evidence (advisory-by-default, consistent with existing gate posture)
- [ ] Prompt/routing CI drift-parity gate stays green after rubric edits
baseline.summary: Adopt DSO plan-review gap findings (content upgrades to rebar's four-pass gate)

# The `[eval]` extra / inspect-ai path has NO automated coverage, and structurally cannot get any from the normal suite

## Background

Discovered while fixing the gating pip-audit failure on `main` (ticket e47e: click 8.2.1 / PYSEC-2026-2132). That fix adds `[tool.uv] override-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` because inspect-ai caps `click!=8.2.0,<8.2.2,>=8.1.3` and pinned the universal resolution to the vulnerable click 8.2.1.

The override was justified on evidence that inspect-ai 0.3.251 tolerates click 8.4.2: `import inspect_ai` succeeds, and `inspect --help` / `inspect eval --help` both render and exit 0 (which exercises click Command/Option construction and group -> subcommand dispatch, where an 8.2.2+ API break would surface). Upstream agrees the cap is over-tight (UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai PR #4596 against issue #4594).

What was NOT verified is a real eval task running end-to-end. That needs live model credentials.

## The gap predates the click change

CI has never exercised inspect-ai. This is not an oversight introduced by e47e:

* inspect-ai is only in the `[eval]` extra; the pip-audit job installs `--extra dev` only.
* `[tool.uv] conflicts` declares `[{extra="eval"}, {extra="dev"}]` mutually conflicting
  (pyproject: "nothing installs dev+eval together"). The pytest suite runs off `dev`, so
  inspect-ai CANNOT be present in the tested set.
* rebar imports inspect_ai lazily behind `guard_import(..., extra="eval")`, so those code
  paths abstain silently when it is absent.

That conflict declaration is exactly why this needs its OWN job/lane rather than a test added to the main suite - a test in the normal run can never have inspect-ai installed.

## Proposed work

Add a separate CI lane (or an opt-in, credential-gated job) that installs the `[eval]` extra and drives ONE minimal inspect-ai task to completion, so a click/inspect-ai incompatibility becomes visible instead of invisible. A mock/stub model provider is preferable to burning live credentials if inspect-ai supports one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a CI lane or opt-in job exists that installs the `[eval]` extra and runs at least one
      inspect-ai task end-to-end (not merely importing inspect_ai or invoking `--help`)
- [ ] that lane runs against the committed `uv.lock`, so it exercises the click version the
      lock actually carries (currently 8.4.2 via the e47e override)
- [ ] the lane fails loudly on an inspect-ai runtime/API break rather than skipping silently
- [ ] it does not require live model credentials to be present on every run (stub/mock model,
      or clearly gated so its absence is reported rather than passing vacuously)
- [ ] the `eval`/`dev` extras conflict is respected - the lane uses its own environment and
      does not attempt to co-install `dev` + `eval`

## Out of scope

Removing the click override. That is tracked by the REMOVE-WHEN in pyproject.toml (drop it once inspect-ai ships a release admitting click >= 8.3.3).
baseline.summary: Smoke-test the inspect-ai eval path under the [eval] extra

# J6 — Data Center transport on `pycontribs/jira`, behind an opt-in extra

## Context / Problem

The DC backend needs a transport satisfying rebar's `TicketTransport` role plus `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` (`_backend.py:80-282`). The Cloud transport is an ACLI subprocess (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:31` shells out to the `acli` binary), which is Cloud-shaped and must not be disturbed. PR #120 hand-rolled a stdlib `urllib` REST v2 client for DC.

## Approach

Build the DC transport on **`pycontribs/jira`**, the maintained Python client that already handles Server/DC versus Cloud differences, PAT bearer auth, pagination, and payload quirks that a hand-rolled client would rediscover. It is confined to an opt-in `[jira-datacenter]` extra and imported **lazily inside the functions that need it**, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract holds and `import rebar` stays dependency-free; a missing extra raises a clear install-naming error, mirroring `runner._import_pydantic_ai`.

Auth is a Personal Access Token read env-only from `JIRA_PAT` (DC PATs, Jira 8.14+), passed as `token_auth`; `url` and `project` come from the typed config so a `[tool.rebar.jira]` value is honored. A malformed config **fails loudly** rather than degrading to env-only — PR #120 swallowed `ConfigError`, which is against rebar's fail-loud posture.

The library's object model is unwrapped at this boundary: every method returns the **raw payload shapes** rebar's existing mappers already consume (`{"key": …, "fields": {…}}`), so nothing downstream learns about `jira.Issue`. Retry, timeout, and error typing are mapped onto rebar's existing transport contract — transient connectivity faults retried with the same 2s/5s backoff as `adapters/jira/acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry`, HTTP errors never retried, and assignee failures raised as `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` (`_backend.py:48`).

This story also supplies the `NameIdentity` resolver's user-search lookup [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85].

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib client (PR #120).** Competent, but it re-owns Jira REST semantics that a widely-used library has already hardened, and confining the dependency to an extra means non-DC users pay nothing for it.

**Alternative rejected: reusing the ACLI transport for DC.** ACLI is the Cloud-validated path; pointing it at DC would risk the one transport we have live confidence in, which this epic explicitly must not do.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (new).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (new) — `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_PROJECT`
  from typed config, env-only `JIRA_PAT`, fail-loud on `ConfigError`.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/__init__.py`** — add the DC backend import beside the
  existing `from .jira import backend as _jira_backend` (line 15). That import is not decorative: importing an
  adapter's backend module is the SIDE EFFECT that calls `register()` into `_backend_registry`, which is how
  `select_backend()` finds it. Without the DC equivalent, `select_backend("jira-datacenter")` raises
  `BackendRegistryError` at runtime ("unknown reconciler backend ...; registered keys: [...]",
  `_backend_registry.py:71` — NOT `KeyError`, which an earlier draft of this note claimed) even with the extra
  installed and every other file correct — a failure that no unit test of the
  transport itself would catch.
- **`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`** — the DC connection settings this story's own ACs already claim (the
  TLS/`allow_insecure` validator, `ca_bundle`, and `resolved_statuses`), which the parent epic's Scope assigns
  here. It was named in the ACs but missing from this list.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_transport.py` (new).
- **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`** (new) — note the path: J5
  [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] landed the harness under `tests/external/`, and an earlier draft of this Scope
  said `tests/live_jira_dc/`, which does not exist. The distinction is not cosmetic: `tests/external/` is the
  only tier fenced off from per-commit CI, so a live test outside it is collected by the default suite AND by
  `_build-and-test.yml`'s dedicated `pytest -m integration` step, on runners with no Docker, no Jira and no
  egress — breaking CI for everyone. Landing under the right path also inherits three mechanisms this story
  must honour: `tests/external/conftest.py` auto-applies the `external` marker (and hard-fails collection if
  it appears elsewhere); the autouse `_require_external_opt_in` fixture skips everything without
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`; and a module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel is what enrols the module in the
  all-skip canary, so **`test_transport.py` MUST define one** or a silently-all-skipped run reads as green.
  Absent harness ⇒ SKIP with an actionable message, never a hard failure.

## Testing

Two tiers. A stateful fake for fast unit coverage of shape mapping, and the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] as the real oracle — the test-design standard's "stateful verified fake plus a live canary where justified", and DC semantics are exactly where a fake's assumptions are most likely to be wrong.

- unit (fake library client): each `TicketTransport` method returns rebar's raw payload shape, not a
  `jira.Issue`; `JIRA_PAT` is sent as bearer token auth; a missing `[jira-datacenter]` extra raises naming the
  install command; a malformed config raises rather than degrading.
- unit failure paths: an HTTP error is NOT retried (call count is exactly 1) while a connection timeout IS
  retried with the documented backoff; an unknown assignee raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`.
- live (J5 harness): create → read → update → transition-by-name → comment → link → probe a real issue and
  assert each observable postcondition on the server, including that a transition to a name the workflow does
  not offer raises rather than silently no-oping.
- live edge: the absence probe returns the classifier's not-found state for a deleted issue, and a distinct
  state for one that merely lost permission.
- collateral invariant: no Cloud test changes and `adapters/jira/acli*.py` are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] every `TicketTransport`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` method has a
      passing live test against the J5 harness, output summarized in a ticket comment
- [ ] a test asserts an HTTP error is attempted exactly once and a timeout is retried per the documented backoff
- [ ] `pip install nava-rebar` then `pip show jira` reports not-installed, and `import rebar` succeeds
- [ ] importing the DC transport without the extra raises an error naming `pip install nava-rebar[jira-datacenter]`
- [ ] a malformed `[tool.rebar.jira]` config raises `ConfigError` rather than falling back to env-only
- [ ] the `NameIdentity` user-search lookup this story supplies [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85] is covered: a test
      asserts the resolver returns an authoritative identity for a user that exists on the DC instance, and
      raises `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` for one that does not. J4 shipped `NameIdentity` taking its
      resolver as an explicit constructor parameter precisely so this story could supply a REAL lookup; leaving
      it unwired would restore the permanently-non-authoritative assignee (and the diff churn) that J4's
      anti-churn oracle exists to prevent
- [ ] `select_backend("jira-datacenter")` resolves after `import rebar_reconciler.adapters` — a test pins the
      registry lookup, so a missing self-registration import fails here rather than at an operator's first run.
      The negative half of that test expects `BackendRegistryError` (`_backend_registry.py:71`), NOT `KeyError`:
      a `pytest.raises(KeyError)` would never match and the guard would be worthless
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows no change under `adapters/jira/acli*`
- [ ] the DC backend REJECTS a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` with a `ConfigError` naming the cleartext
      risk, unless `allow_insecure = true` is set; a unit test covers the reject branch with a non-loopback
      `http://` URL, and a second test asserts the override path emits a warning naming the risk (epic AC13)
- [ ] every live test against the J5 harness sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly (the harness serves plain
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`), so the loopback path exercises the override rather than bypassing the
      validator
- [ ] the `[jira-datacenter]` extra pins a minimum `jira` version with a compatible-release bound (e.g.
      `jira>=3.8,<4`), and a comment records which DC-vs-Cloud auth behavior that floor guarantees
- [ ] this story owns the `_config_schema.py` DC connection settings: the TLS/`allow_insecure` validator, the
      `ca_bundle` key, and `resolved_statuses` (J7 owns only the `reconciler.backend` choice widening)
- [ ] TLS certificate verification is never disabled — asserted against the parameter form the library
      ACTUALLY reads. `pycontribs/jira` takes TLS config through its **options dict**, not a bare constructor
      kwarg: `verify` is a key of `JIRA.DEFAULT_OPTIONS` (defaulting to `True`) and is consumed as
      `self._options["verify"]` (verified in upstream `jira/client.py`). So the test asserts the effective
      `options["verify"]` the transport passes is never `False` — either left at its default or set to a CA
      bundle path. An earlier draft said "constructed WITHOUT `verify=False`", which would be VACUOUS: no such
      kwarg exists, so the assertion would pass unchanged even with verification disabled through the options
      dict. The test must also assert a verification failure raises an error naming the `ca_bundle` setting
      rather than silently proceeding. `allow_insecure` is asserted to affect the URL scheme check ONLY — a test
      confirms it does not relax certificate verification
- [ ] `reconciler.resolved_statuses` configures the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set, defaulting to
      `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset; a test covers both the default and a custom workflow's names

baseline.description:
## Problem
Running `rebar metrics` with NO `--since/--until` (the default invocation) silently breaks every ticket-derived (agent_process) metric. The CLI defaults the flags to empty strings and passes them into the readers; `metrics.event_metrics._bounds("")` calls `datetime.fromisoformat("")` which raises `ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: ''`. The CLI's per-metric fault isolation catches it and renders each metric as `unavailable` with reason="Invalid isoformat string: ''", so the failure is silent.

## Reproduced (in the rebar repo itself)
`rebar metrics --output json` -> attempts_per_ticket / first_pass_rate / revert_recovery / reopen_recovery / rework_within_7_days all report `{unavailable: {reason: "Invalid isoformat string: ''"}}`.
With explicit dates (`--since 2026-01-01 --until 2026-12-31`) they compute correctly (e.g. first_pass_rate -> 0.9984). The git readers guard the empty string (churn returns data); the event/sidecar readers do not — an inconsistency.

## Expected
With no `--since/--until`, default the window to the **last 30 days** (until=today, since=today-30d) rather than passing empty strings. Empty/whitespace date values should normalize to this default (or to `None` open bounds) at the CLI boundary so no reader ever receives an unparseable string.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `rebar metrics` with no date flags returns real values for the agent_process metrics over a last-30-days window (no 'Invalid isoformat' unavailable).
- [ ] Default window documented in `rebar metrics --help`, user-guide, and the help text file.
- [ ] Explicit `--since/--until` still override the default; explicit empty-string values are handled gracefully.
- [ ] Unit/interface test covering the no-flags invocation (regression: currently masked as unavailable).
baseline.summary: rebar metrics with no --since/--until fails ticket-derived metrics; default to last 30 days
