baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The edit-then-re-review loop is common and hazardous as two shell commands, and claim's recovery text (src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:213-215) tells the user to run review-plan then claim by hand. Operator approved both flags. OSS precedent favors embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb (cargo publish verifies by default; terraform apply consumes a staleness-checked plan artifact) over new fused commands.

## Approach
(1) `rebar edit <id> ... --review`: edit_cli's hand-rolled parser (src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:528-561) treats every --name as requiring a value, so `--review` is handled as an explicit valueless flag checked BEFORE the field loop (popped from argv, bypassing the --key=value pathway); after edit_core commits the EDIT event, invoke rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, sign=True) and map the returned verdict dict to the process exit status with the disposition mapping (0 PASS / 1 BLOCK / 2 INDETERMINATE / 11 retryable per ADR 0040). _disposition_exit_code stays in src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py; the flag handlers use a lazy in-function import (`from rebar._cli._llm_commands import _disposition_exit_code`) — the established pattern for a _commands module reaching a _cli helper, per the existing lazy `from rebar._cli import _help` inside reopen_cli at src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:562. No file moves. (2) `rebar claim <id> --review`: implemented as a new keyword parameter review: bool = False on claim_compute, threaded from claim_cli's parser; the logic sits inside claim_compute at the claim.py:133 seam: when --review is set and the gate applies, call llm.claim_gate_check(ticket_id); if it reports not-ok, run review_plan(sign=True). The review verdict then determines control flow exactly: on PASS, proceed into the normal plan_review_precheck path and claim (precheck re-checks and fails closed with the standard message if the attestation is somehow still stale); on BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, or a retryable degrade, the claim is NOT attempted — the command prints the review's finding summary and exits with the disposition mapping applied to the review result (1 / 2 / 11 respectively), leaving the ticket open for revision. When stage 1 says the gate does not apply (disabled or exempt type), --review prints a one-line notice "plan-review gate not enabled for this ticket; --review skipped" and the claim proceeds — never a silent no-op. The flag is NOT propagated through the parent-first cascade. (3) Help and docs: the real help sources are src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt and src/rebar/_cli/help/claim.txt; docs/cli-reference.md is generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py and is regenerated, not hand-edited. Both help texts state the flags are not atomic against concurrent store reconvergence and point at `review-plan --status`. Exception path: if review_plan RAISES (provider outage, config error) instead of returning a verdict dict, both flags let the exception propagate to the standard CLI error handler — for edit --review the EDIT remains committed (it landed before the review started) and the process exits via the normal error path; for claim --review the claim core is never invoked. A test covers a raising stub for each flag. Lock discipline: neither flag holds the store flock across the review — the edit/claim appends its own event under the normal short-lived lock, releases it, and only then invokes review_plan, which itself takes the lock only for the brief under-lock generation re-check at signing; the multi-minute LLM passes run with no lock held. Both flags are CLI-only (the MCP surface keeps its REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM fence). Alternative rejected: new fused verbs — no OSS precedent, larger surface.

## Scope
src/rebar/_commands/composer.py, src/rebar/_commands/claim.py, src/rebar/_commands/gates.py (extract _plan_review_gate_applies; precheck refactored to call it), src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt, src/rebar/_cli/help/claim.txt, docs/cli-reference.md (regenerated via scripts/gen_cli_reference.py), docs/exit-codes.md (document the --review exit codes for edit and claim — the new codes apply only when the flag is passed; the flagless contracts are unchanged), tests/unit/test_review_flags.py (new).

## Testing
Unit with a stubbed review_plan returning verdict dicts: bare `--review` parses without consuming a following token (an edit with `--review --priority 1` keeps both); edit --review runs review after the EDIT commit and maps PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE stubs to exits 0/1/2; a BLOCK leaves the edit committed; claim --review claims on a PASS stub, and on BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, and retryable-degrade stubs never calls the claim core and exits 1, 2, and 11 respectively; it prints the gate-disabled notice for a bug-type ticket and claims anyway; it fails closed when the post-review recheck still reports stale; the parent cascade never receives the flag; a review stub that itself acquires the store flock succeeds under both flags; a RAISING review stub leaves the edit committed (edit --review) and never invokes the claim core (claim --review), exiting through the standard CLI error path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bare --review parses as a valueless flag without swallowing the next token (checked: parser unit test).
- [ ] edit --review runs the review strictly after the EDIT commit and exits with _disposition_exit_code(result, indeterminate_code=2) (checked: unit test recording call order and exit codes for PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE stubs).
- [ ] claim --review claims only on PASS; on BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/retryable-degrade it never invokes the claim core and exits 1/2/11 with the review summary printed (checked: unit tests with stubbed verdicts, including a retryable stub, asserting the claim core is not called).
- [ ] Both flag handlers obtain _disposition_exit_code via the lazy in-function import and the review-plan CLI's own exit-code behavior is unchanged (checked: unit test asserting the mapped exit codes; existing review-plan CLI exit-code tests pass).
- [ ] claim --review senses applicability via the shared _plan_review_gate_applies helper (also used by precheck), reviews only when the gate applies AND claim_gate_check reports not-ok, prints the skip notice when the gate does not apply, and never propagates through the parent cascade (checked: unit tests, including a config-disabled case and an exempt-type case).
- [ ] Help sources document non-atomicity and reference review-plan --status, and docs/cli-reference.md is regenerated (checked: help-text assertions; regenerated file committed).
- [ ] docs/exit-codes.md documents the --review exit codes for edit and claim and states the flagless contracts are unchanged (checked: doc text assertion; existing exit-code conformance tests pass).
- [ ] The store lock is not held while the review runs: a review stub that acquires the store flock succeeds under both flags (checked: unit test).
- [ ] A raising review_plan propagates through the standard CLI error path with the edit still committed and the claim never attempted (checked: unit tests with a raising stub for each flag).
baseline.summary: edit --review and claim --review flags

content.text: # Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap + live shadow validation + capped live heal
## Summary
High-risk tail of the baseline convergence rollout (carved from soar-quill-flare / 7d23). This AGENT (with
ACLI access) performs the live validation directly, with GUARANTEED cleanup of test artifacts in both live Jira
and the local store. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` runs `rebar reconcile --mode live` every ~20 min.
## Already landed (7d23, on main)
- Phase-1 baseline dual-write SHADOW (`baseline_shadow.py`) behind `reconciler.baseline_dual_write`, with per-pass
`baseline_shadow_check` logging + `baseline_shadow_divergence` alert.
- Circuit breaker (`check_blast_radius`, default 0.10) before the first acting mutation.
## Key facts established (code-verified — the plan is built on these)
- **The swap is namespace-COMPATIBLE.** In `_diff_fields`, `field_name` iterates `local_mapped` (output of
`_map_local_to_jira_fields`), which emits **JIRA** names (`"summary"`, `outbound_fields.py:138,371-378`).
`prev_snapshot[jira_key]` is JIRA-keyed (`_snapshot_schema.py:135`), and `BindingStore.get_baseline` returns the
same JIRA-keyed shape (`_BASELINE_FIELDS = ("summary","description","priority","status","assignee")`,
`binding_store.py:46-54`). So feeding `get_baseline(local_id)` where `prev_jira_fields` is read today is
shape-for-shape compatible — no field-name translation is required for the swap.
- **`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (`{"title",...}`, LOCAL names) is a pre-existing partial no-op**, NOT part of this
swap. The guard `if field_name in _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (outbound_fields.py:405) never fires for the
title/summary field (`"summary" ∉ {"title",...}`); it only fires for the four coinciding names
(description/priority/status/assignee). This asymmetry is UNCHANGED by the swap. Document it; do NOT silently
"fix" `"title"→"summary"` as part of the swap (that changes behavior and is out of scope).
- **`get_baseline` cannot signal "corrupt".** It returns `None` for BOTH absent and non-dict baseline
(binding_store.py:314-318), and `None` is documented-VALID = "no ancestor → local-wins" (ADR 0026 §2). A corrupt
`bindings.json` (the baseline lives inside it as `entry["baseline"]`) fails **CLOSED at LOAD**: `BindingStore._load`
raises `ValueError` (binding_store.py:103-124) at pass start, before any `get_baseline`. So the fail-closed
invariant is preserved by the existing load guard — the consumer swap needs NO new corrupt-detection branch.
- **`classify()` is NOT wired into the field-differ path for active bindings.** `binding_walk` skips active
bindings (`binding_walk.py:169-170` "handled by the field differ") and only runs `classify()` on OFF-snapshot
pairs. So there is NO production code path where both `classify()`'s decision and the field-differ's action exist
for the SAME active binding — comparing them there would require a parallel engine (explicitly forbidden).
- **`decision_census` is documented-but-never-emitted.** Only `binding_walk_census` is logged
(`run_differs.py:652`); `decision_census` appears only in a docstring (`classify.py:351`) with no `.log()` call.
So there is no live expand-contract yet — the census task STARTS emitting `decision_census`.
## Remaining CODE
1. **Add the flag.** New `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` in `ReconcilerConfig` in the TOP-LEVEL
`src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (NOT under `rebar_reconciler/` — that path does not exist; it is where
`baseline_dual_write` already lives, ~line 355). **TWO edits, both required** (mirror `baseline_dual_write`
exactly): (a) the dataclass field `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` after line 355, AND (b) the coercer
entry `"baseline_consumer_swap": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k),` in `_SECTIONS["reconciler"]` (~line 464) — without
(b) the TOML key is silently dropped at parse. Read it ONCE at the orchestration layer
(mirror `reconcile.py:936`'s `bool(_load_config().reconciler.baseline_dual_write)`) and thread the bool down,
not per-field `_load_config()`. Document the flag + flip procedure in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
2. **Phase-3 consumer swap (two call-sites, both in `outbound_fields._diff_fields`).**
- Site A — direction-suppression: `outbound_fields.py:405-407` (`_local_matches_prev(field_name, local_val,
prev_jira_fields or {})`).
- Site B — conflict-sink: `outbound_fields.py:519-526` (`_local_matches_prev(fname, local_mapped.get(fname),
prev_jira_fields)`).
Plumbing: thread `local_id` (already in scope at `outbound_differ.py:622`) into the `_diff_fields` call
(`outbound_differ.py:699-708`) plus the `baseline_consumer_swap` bool. `_diff_fields` already receives
`binding_store`. When the flag is ON, compute `baseline = binding_store.get_baseline(local_id)` once and pass it
(JIRA-keyed, same shape) wherever `prev_jira_fields` is used by the two `_local_matches_prev` calls; when OFF,
behavior is byte-for-byte the current `prev_snapshot` path. `None` baseline → the EXISTING absent branch
(`_local_matches_prev` returns False → local-wins). Corrupt-store fail-closed is inherited from load time (above);
no new consumer branch.
3. **RED-first direction-preservation property test.** With the flag ON (swapped consumer), assert that for each of
the five mirrored fields, when local == baseline the outbound diff SUPPRESSES the field (inbound-wins), and when
local != baseline it emits the mutation — matching `direction_is_inbound` (`classify.py:258-273`). RED before the
swap wiring, GREEN after. Include the title/summary asymmetry as an explicit documented case (title is not
suppressed today — the test pins that unchanged behavior, it is not a regression).
4. **Census expand-contract.** Emit `decision_census` (the documented-but-missing key) from the same `census(...)`
record currently shipped under `binding_walk_census` (`run_differs.py:652`); migrate any consumer to
`decision_census`; then DROP `binding_walk_census`. Rollback path for the drop: re-add the `binding_walk_census`
emit (one line) — documented in the commit.
5. **Divergence signal = the EXISTING `baseline_shadow_check` (no new classifier-vs-legacy alert).** The
code-verified reality: there is NO production path where a `classify()` decision and a competing "legacy" action
coexist for the same binding — `binding_walk` runs `classify()` only on OFF-snapshot pairs (no legacy there),
and the field-differ owns ACTIVE bindings (no `classify()` there). Building a per-binding classifier-vs-legacy
comparison would require a parallel engine, which this ticket explicitly forbids. Therefore the rollout's
divergence gate is the ALREADY-LANDED `baseline_shadow_check` / `baseline_shadow_divergence` (baseline_shadow.py:
91-95), which compares the dual-write baseline against `prev_snapshot` arbitration for active bindings — exactly
the swap being validated. This item is a DOCUMENTATION step: record in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` that
`baseline_shadow_check` is the divergence gate and why a separate classifier-vs-legacy alert is not built (no
legacy engine). No new alert code.
## Remaining OPERATIONAL (agent-run with ACLI; guaranteed cleanup) — wall-clock-bound
- **≥10 CONSECUTIVE clean shadow passes** (`baseline_shadow_check` divergent==0) BEFORE flipping the flag.
**Streak source (design gap resolved, NO code):** `bridge_state/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:10`), so the
`sync-log-*.jsonl` SyncLogger output is EPHEMERAL — torn down with the GHA runner. But the reconcile-bridge run
already prints `baseline_shadow_check` (and `baseline_shadow_divergence`) to stdout, which GitHub Actions captures
durably in each run's logs. Derive the streak OPERATIONALLY (no new persistence code, no workflow edit) by
querying the last N reconcile-bridge runs and reading their emitted divergent counts:
`gh run list --workflow=reconcile-bridge.yml --limit N --json databaseId,createdAt,conclusion` then
`gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check`. A run with divergent>0, a failed/absent run, or a gap
> 2× the schedule interval RESETS the streak. This keeps the streak recomputable by any agent from durable GHA
history without touching the workflow or the gitignored sync-log. COORDINATION: A3's live remediation pauses the
reconciler and RESETS this streak — A3's live pass already ran this session, so the streak starts fresh AFTER it;
do not run another A3 pass during the window.
- **Capped live heal** under bootstrap-strict incl. the GC-after-grace deletion (f8b5-2f30 → REB-530). PRE-HEAL
BACKUP covers BOTH sides: export affected Jira issue state (JSON via Jira API) AND tag the tickets branch
(`git tag pre-heal-<date>`); if either backup fails, ABORT the heal. Store artifacts in the workflow run
artifacts (retention documented).
- **Flip the flag only after BOTH gates.** Rollback rehearsed: (a) revert the flag to false and confirm the
reconciler reverts to `prev_snapshot` arbitration with no divergence, AND (b) force one `--mode dry-run` pass
confirming zero mutations; record both workflow run-ids.
## Scope (files EDITED)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add `baseline_consumer_swap` (top-level rebar config, beside `baseline_dual_write`)

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — add `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` to the `OutboundDiffConfig` dataclass (outbound_differ.py:242-273 — the sole config conduit to `_diff_fields`); thread `local_id` + the flag into `_diff_fields`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_fields.py` — `_diff_fields` reads `get_baseline` behind the flag
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py` — census expand-contract; scoped divergence alert
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — read `baseline_consumer_swap` ONCE at the orchestration layer (mirror :936's `baseline_dual_write` read) and thread the bool down
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/baseline_shadow.py` — emit the `RECON: baseline_shadow_check` diagnostic line (Round-5 decision)
- `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` — flag + flip/rollback procedure
- new test file under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — RED-first direction-preservation property test
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [CODE] `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` flag added (distinct from `baseline_dual_write`) as BOTH the
dataclass field AND the `_SECTIONS["reconciler"]` coercer entry, + documented in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
Proof: a config-parse test asserts default False AND that a TOML `baseline_consumer_swap = true` round-trips
(proving the coercer entry exists, not silently dropped).
- [ ] [CODE] Both `_local_matches_prev` call-sites (outbound_fields.py:405, :519) read `get_baseline(local_id)`
behind the flag; flag OFF is byte-for-byte the `prev_snapshot` path; `None` baseline → local-wins; corrupt
`bindings.json` still fails closed at load (existing `_load` guard — a test asserts a corrupt store aborts the
pass). Proof: named property/unit tests.
- [ ] [CODE] RED-first direction-preservation property test over the five mapped fields: RED (fails) before the
swap wiring, GREEN after; the title/summary asymmetry is pinned as an explicit case.
- [ ] [CODE] Census emits `decision_census`; consumers migrated; `binding_walk_census` dropped WITH a documented
one-line rollback. Proof: a test asserts `decision_census` is emitted and `binding_walk_census` is not.
- [ ] [CODE/DOC] No new classifier-vs-legacy alert is built (no production path has both a `classify()` decision
and a legacy action for the same binding without a parallel engine). `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents that
the EXISTING `baseline_shadow_check` is the rollout divergence gate and why. Proof: a doc-grep AC —
`grep -q "baseline_shadow_check" docs/jira-sync-setup.md`.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] ≥10 consecutive clean shadow passes, with the streak derived from GHA reconcile-bridge run
logs (`gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check`; reset on divergent>0 / failed run / >2×-cadence
gap — no new persistence code), not overlapping A3's live pass; evidence (run-ids + divergent counts)
recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Capped live heal with a bilateral pre-heal backup (Jira JSON + tickets-branch tag); heal aborts
if either backup fails; artifacts stored + linked.
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] Flip only after both gates (>=10 clean shadow passes + clean flag-ON live pass).
## Round-5 resolved decision (2026-07-09, epic adept-hedge-stain continuation)
**Streak-source gap CLOSED with a small CODE emission (not merely an ops procedure).**
Code-verified: `baseline_shadow_check` is emitted ONLY via `sync_logger.log` (baseline_shadow.py:92),
which writes the gitignored `bridge_state/sync-log-*.jsonl` — it NEVER reaches stdout, so the OPERATIONAL
streak AC's `gh run view <id> --log | grep baseline_shadow_check` would find nothing. Resolution:
`baseline_shadow.py` additionally prints a `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=<N> equal=<M>` line to
**stderr** (`file=sys.stderr`, flush=True) — matching the VERIFIED existing `RECON:` convention (applier.py:488,799
all use `file=sys.stderr`); `gh run view <id> --log` captures stderr too — so the
reconcile-bridge GHA captures the divergent count durably in each run's logs and the >=10-clean-pass streak
is derivable via `gh run view --log`. This adds `baseline_shadow.py` to the edited-files set. It is the ONLY
new persistence-adjacent mechanism (no workflow edit, no store write, no gitignored file relied on).
## Acceptance Criteria (round-5 addition)
- [ ] [CODE] `baseline_shadow.py` prints a `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=<N> equal=<M>` line to
**stderr** (`file=sys.stderr`, flush=True) whenever the shadow check runs — matching the VERIFIED `RECON:` convention — so the
operational >=10-clean-pass streak is derivable from GHA reconcile-bridge run logs (making the existing
`gh run view --log | grep baseline_shadow_check` OPERATIONAL AC achievable). Proof: a unit test captures
stderr and asserts the `RECON: baseline_shadow_check divergent=` line is printed with the correct count.
## Round-5 clarifications (review round-1 remediation)
- **BLOCK-4 (Site B full guard swap).** At `outbound_fields.py:519` the outer guard is
`if conflict_sink is not None and prev_jira_fields and jira_key:` — `prev_jira_fields` is used as a
truthiness guard there too, not only inside the two `_local_matches_prev` calls. Under
`baseline_consumer_swap=True` the ENTIRE Site-B use of `prev_jira_fields` is replaced by `baseline`
(the `get_baseline(local_id)` result): both the outer `and prev_jira_fields` guard AND the inner
`_local_matches_prev(fname, local_mapped.get(fname), prev_jira_fields)` argument. Flag OFF: byte-for-byte
the `prev_jira_fields`/`prev_snapshot` path. A `None`/`{}` baseline makes the outer guard falsy (skip the
conflict-sink), which is the correct local-wins behavior (no ancestor → no conflict to record).
- **ADV-6 (live-heal partial-failure rollback).** If Jira-side GC-after-grace deletions complete for some
issues and then the heal aborts, the RESTORE re-imports the pre-heal JSON for EVERY affected issue (not
only the ones mutated before the abort) and `git reset --hard pre-heal-<date>` restores the tickets branch;
the heal records, per issue, whether restore re-created it — a restore that cannot re-create a
GC-deleted issue is a LOUD failure (alert + abort the epic tail), never a silent partial.
## Acceptance Criteria (round-1 remediation additions)
- [ ] [OPERATIONAL] After the flag is flipped ON (`baseline_consumer_swap = true`), at least one live
reconcile pass runs WITH the flag ON and is verified clean (baseline_shadow_check divergent==0, no
unexpected mutations) before the tail is considered complete — proving the swapped consumer behaves in
production, not only in shadow. Evidence (run-id + divergent count) recorded on this ticket.
## Round-5 clarification (review round-2 remediation) — flag flow via OutboundDiffConfig
The `baseline_consumer_swap` bool flows on the ESTABLISHED config channel, not ad-hoc kwargs:
`reconcile.py` reads `_load_config().reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` ONCE (mirroring :936's
`baseline_dual_write` read) and threads it to `run_differs.py`, which sets it on the `OutboundDiffConfig(...)`
it constructs; `compute_outbound_mutations` / `_diff_fields` read it off that config object (alongside
`prev_snapshot`/`client`/`local_label_intent`). `OutboundDiffConfig` gains
`baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False` so the default is off end-to-end.
## Acceptance Criteria (round-2 remediation addition)
- [ ] [CODE] `OutboundDiffConfig` (outbound_differ.py) carries `baseline_consumer_swap: bool = False`, set from
config in `run_differs.py`'s `OutboundDiffConfig(...)` construction and read by `_diff_fields`; flag OFF
is the default end-to-end. Proof: a unit test constructs `OutboundDiffConfig` with the flag ON and asserts
`_diff_fields` takes the `get_baseline` path (and OFF -> the `prev_snapshot` path).

baseline.summary: Convergence rollout tail: Phase-3 consumer swap flip + live shadow-pass validation + capped live heal

## Summary
tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py::test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss (integration tier, run under pytest-xdist -n4 on GitHub-hosted runners) intermittently fails when its 8 concurrent subprocess writers race the git object/tree build on the shared store. Two distinct symptoms observed, same root class:
- 'git commit failed while holding lock: error: invalid object 100644 <sha> for "<ticket>/...-COMMENT.json" ... error: Error building trees' (run 29300833741, main f542/560180461, ubuntu py3.12, 2026-07-14)
- 'git commit failed while holding lock: fatal: could not parse HEAD' (run 29296542560, main 5348d2adf, integration tier, 2026-07-13)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the integration tier under load: pytest -m integration -n 4 (as CI does) on a loaded runner.
2. Intermittently: all 8 writers in test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss fail with a git tree-build/HEAD-parse error while holding the store lock.
Expected: concurrent writers serialize cleanly (the test asserts no writer failures + no lost events).
Actual: under contention a writer builds a tree referencing a blob object not yet durable / reads an unborn-or-mid-update HEAD, and git aborts with 'invalid object ... Error building trees' or 'could not parse HEAD'.
Passes 5/5 locally on an unloaded machine — load-dependent.

## Notes
Not introduced by recent changes (observed on both 5348d2adf and f542). Distinct from the b228 timing flake and the 85c3 harness/acli flakes. Likely a git object-write vs tree-build ordering race in the store write path under the lock (concurrent processes sharing one git dir).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss no longer fails under CI-load parallelism (the git tree-build/HEAD race is closed — e.g. ensure blobs are durably written before tree-build, or serialize the object-write+commit under the lock, or retry on the transient object/ref error).
- [ ] It still asserts no lost events under a concurrent writer storm.
- [ ] Regression coverage runs in the gerrit-verify Verified gate (integration tier).
baseline.summary: Flaky integration test test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss — concurrent git tree-build race under CI load

baseline.description:
## Problem
A source citation [rebar:<id>] from a child requires a DIRECT verified edge from the citing ticket to the cited target; a transitive/inherited edge does not satisfy it. Combined with link's hierarchy promotion (blocking deps on a story are promoted to the parent epic by design), a child's citation to a prerequisite is left ungrounded with no obvious cause.

## Design (per maintainer)
Citation validation must honor INHERITED links. Epic A has Child B; Child B cites Epic C. Epics depend on Epics and Stories depend on Stories. So as long as Epic A (B's parent) depends_on Epic C, the citation in Child B to Epic C is valid via inheritance from the parent's edge.

## Fix
When validating a [rebar:<id>] citation from a ticket T to target X, treat the citation as grounded if EITHER (a) T has a direct verified edge to X (current behavior), OR (b) an ancestor of T (walk parent_id chain) has a direct verified depends_on/blocking edge to X (or to an ancestor of X at the matching hierarchy level). Preserve current direct-edge behavior; only ADD the inherited path.

## Acceptance criteria
- A citation from Child B to Epic C is VALID when B's parent Epic A depends_on Epic C, with no direct B->C edge.
- A citation with neither a direct nor an inherited edge remains INVALID (no over-grounding).
- Existing direct-edge citations remain valid (no regression).
- Tests cover: inherited-valid, direct-valid, neither-invalid.

## Verification
pytest citation-validation tests for the three cases above.
baseline.summary: [rebar:<id>] citation validation should honor inherited hierarchy links

baseline.description:
# P1.4 — rebar gc + maintenance doctrine (bounded growth, recovery-safe)

## Context (problem + research)

Every mutation is a committed file, and the write path sets `gc.auto=0`
(`_store/event_append.py:64 _ensure_gc_auto_zero`) so a background `git gc` can't
prune the reflog commits the reset-recovery net relies on (now in
`rebar._store.sync:54-77`, `reset --hard origin/tickets` for unrelated/diverged
histories, "recoverable via reflog"). The cost is **unbounded** loose-object/pack
growth on long-lived `tickets` branches. git-bug packs ops into fewer objects with
a cache; Fossil's SQLite sidesteps small-object blowup. rebar sells "built to
scale" but ships no safe reclaim path. Akka's distributed-data pruning teaches the
discipline: gate discard on dissemination + a TTL marker, never wall-clock alone.

## Evidence (experiments)

- EXP6: a discarded commit **survives** `git gc --prune=14.days.ago` but is
  **destroyed** by `--prune=now` -> a conservative window is mandatory.
- EXP-R6 (real code): the gc recipe on the **real `.tickets-tracker` orphan-branch
  worktree** packed 26 -> 0 loose objects and `rebar show` still read correctly.

## What / Implementation detail

Operator-only `rebar gc` (**not** over MCP, like `init`), under the write lock
(I5) and only when not mid-recovery (reuse
`rebar._store.lock.check_no_rebase_in_progress` — no leading underscore):
1. `git -C <tracker> reflog expire --expire=<window> --expire-unreachable=<window> --all`
   (BOTH flags — EXP6: unreachable objects are governed by `--expire-unreachable`/
   `--prune`).
2. `git -C <tracker> gc --prune=<window>.ago` (**never `--prune=now`**); conservative
   default `gc.reflog_window` = 14 days that must exceed the worst-case offline/
   un-pushed interval.
3. Report bytes reclaimed. A `--compact-first` flag runs per-ticket `compact`
   over eligible tickets first (I1/I9-safe: SNAPSHOT folds, `*.retired` renames
   union). Document the "compact then gc" cadence in `docs/concurrency.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] operator-only `rebar gc` (reflog expire --expire+--expire-unreachable, gc --prune=<window>.ago, never now)
- [ ] `--compact-first` runs per-ticket compaction before packing
- [ ] mid-recovery guard via `check_no_rebase_in_progress`; not exposed over MCP
- [ ] gc-then-recover regression test + bytes-reclaimed sanity on a synthetic many-event ticket
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the compact-then-gc cadence and window rationale

See `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md` (P1.4).
- [ ] `rebar gc` reclaims space and reports it; reads work afterward.
- [ ] A `gc`-then-recover regression proves `_store.sync` recovery still works after gc
- [ ] Refuses to run mid-recovery; absent from the MCP surface.
baseline.summary: P1.4 — rebar gc + maintenance doctrine (bounded growth, recovery-safe)

content.text: ## What
Epic completion-verification (`verify_completion` behind the close gate) is
**count-dependent and unreliable for the child-closure check**. Closing an epic with
8 closed+signed children either **exhausts the LLM step budget**
(`recursion_limit=120`) or returns a **false negative** that it "cannot confirm" some
children exist — because it tries to find children by searching the *codebase for
their aliases* instead of enumerating the epic's children deterministically.
The child-closure check should be a **minimal, deterministic, count-independent**
operation: list the epic's children via the `parent_id` hierarchy and confirm each is
`closed` with a valid completion signature. The number of children should be
irrelevant to whether verification can run.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Create an epic with N children; implement + close each child (each gets an
HMAC completion signature under the close gate).
2. `rebar transition <epic> in_progress closed` (gate on; `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1`).
**Expected:** the gate confirms each child has a signed close (a cheap hierarchy +
signature lookup), verifies the epic's OWN criteria, and signs — in time roughly
independent of child count.
**Actual (epic e59d-0ae4-e3c8-45e8, 8 children):**
- First attempt: `agent exceeded its step budget (recursion_limit=120)` → gate
could-not-run → fail-closed → blocked.
- With `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=400`: ran, but FAILED "Acceptance Criterion #1" stating it
"cannot be confirmed via show_ticket that [five] tickets exist as children" — it only
found the 3 children whose aliases happen to appear in the codebase, and "the ticket
store directory is hidden from listing." All 8 children DO have `parent_id` = the epic
and `status=closed` with `signature` present (verified directly), so this is a false
negative.
## Likely cause
The verifier prompt/toolset has no deterministic "list this epic's children + their
close-signature status" capability, so the agent improvises (searches code for
aliases, attempts `show_ticket` on guessed ids) — which is both expensive (drives the
step-budget blowup) and incomplete (misses children not referenced in code). The
intended design ("epic verification = own criteria + child-closure **trust**", commit
7b09ab5f) needs a concrete child-enumeration input/tool to realize the "trust" half.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Epic completion-verification enumerates children via the `parent_id` hierarchy
(e.g. a `list_tickets(parent=…)` / children query or a precomputed child-closure
summary injected into the verifier) rather than searching the codebase for aliases.
- [ ] For each child it checks `status == closed` AND a valid completion signature, and
reports any child lacking one — a deterministic check whose cost does not scale with
re-reading each child's full body.
- [ ] An epic with many (e.g. ≥8) closed+signed children verifies without exceeding the
default LLM step budget.
- [ ] A regression test: an epic with all children closed+signed PASSES; an epic with a
child that is open or closed-without-signature FAILS, citing that child.
</content>

baseline.summary: epic completion-verification is count-dependent: child-closure check should be a minimal deterministic hierarchy+signature lookup

## Why

`src/rebar/_store/push.py` async mode spawns a detached child (`start_new_session=True`,
`close_fds=True`, streams to `DEVNULL`, reconstructed `PYTHONPATH`) whose whole purpose
is to finish the push AFTER the calling process exits. The current E2E
(`tests/interfaces/store/test_push_policy_e2e.py`) writes in-process and polls origin
while the parent stays alive — proving "lands in background," not "survives parent
exit." Spawn-failure logging and generic `PUSH_PENDING` surfacing are already covered
elsewhere, so only the parent-exit survival contract is untested.

## What

- Add a forced-order test proving the detached push completes after the spawning CLI
  process has exited.
- Order the interaction with a controlled `git` wrapper on `PATH` that blocks at
  `git push` behind a release file, so the parent provably exits before the child's
  push completes.

## Scope

- `tests/interfaces/store/` (new parent-exit survival test)
- A test fixture `git` shim (passes non-push commands through; blocks on push).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `git` shim on `PATH` passes non-push commands through and, on `git push`, writes
      an "entered push" marker and blocks on a release file/pipe.
- [ ] Launch `rebar create` with async push in a subprocess; wait for the "entered push"

content.text: # Plan-review proportionate-scrutiny keys on ticket TYPE, not container/leaf — security overlay never fires on container epics
## Summary
Plan-review's proportionate-scrutiny routing decides which criteria run using ticket **type**
(epic/story/task), not the container(has_children)/leaf distinction. `PlanContext.level` is
literally derived from `ticket_type` (`det_floor.py:117`). Because the security overlay **T5c**
is routed `applies_at.levels: ["task"]`, it is filtered out for any `epic`/`story` — including
**container epics that stand up real infrastructure**. This let the AWS-hosted Gerrit epic
(`d251`) pass plan-review with **no authentication contract specified** for an internet-hosted
service (the `DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` default; now tracked as bug `f2d6`/WS8).
## Reproduction Steps
1. `applies(registry.by_id()["T5c"], level="epic")` → returns **False** (confirmed).
2. The Gerrit work `d251` is a container epic (children S1–S7) describing a networked service
("Gerrit HTTP 8080 + SSH 29418; reverse proxy on 443") with no user/admin auth model.
3. Its plan-review therefore never ran the security overlay against the epic's contents.
4. (Content layer) Even when T5c is forced to run against the epic, 3/3 live runs flag adjacent
issues (unencrypted token volume, token-in-logs) but never the missing endpoint auth — the
rubric's anti-false-positive text brands "declared access level"/"endpoint authn" as canonical
false positives (calibrated for rebar-the-local-tool), suppressing the needed finding.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** Proportionate scrutiny keys on container vs leaf; a criterion representing a
cross-cutting risk surface (security) runs wherever that surface is described — container or
leaf. A container epic that stands up a networked service is reviewed for its auth contract.
- **Actual:** Scrutiny keys on ticket type; T5c is `task`-only; container epics standing up
infrastructure are never security-reviewed at the epic altitude, and an under-specified auth
contract passes.
## Scope
- IN: the proportionate-scrutiny **routing axis** only — `registry.applies()` (drop the
type-derived `level`; key on has_children), `is_mechanical_leaf`, `size_factor`, `_ticket_size`,
`PlanContext.level`, the sole `applies()` call site (`orchestrator.route_criteria`), and all 32
criteria's `applies_at` (`levels`/`container_only` → a container/leaf `scope`). Fix the
mis-scoped security overlay so it fires on containers. Plus a concise, generic content fix so the
gate detects an under-specified endpoint auth contract (networked service, needs identity, no
auth plan) WITHOUT false-positiving local/no-network tools (rebar's own review certification).
- OUT: the Gerrit auth remediation itself (`f2d6`/WS8); `det_floor._clarity_score` per-type
headings and the bug/session_log gate exemption (separate type axes, documented follow-ups).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `registry.applies()` no longer takes/uses a type-derived `level`; proportionate scrutiny is
decided by container(has_children)/leaf. `PlanContext.level` and its type→level mapping are
removed (or no longer used by any routing path).
- [ ] `is_mechanical_leaf`, `size_factor`, `_ticket_size` no longer key on the `"task"`/`"epic"`
type strings; they key on container/leaf (has_children).
- [ ] All 32 `applies_at` blocks in `criteria_routing.json` express scope as container/leaf, not
epic/story/task levels; each criterion's scope is re-mapped faithfully (child-coverage
criteria G3/G4 → container; code-grounding/impl-detail → leaf; cross-cutting → both). The
security overlay T5c is no longer altitude-gated away from containers.
- [ ] A concise, generic criterion change (security and/or a non-security endpoint-contract
completeness check, chosen by experiment) makes the gate flag an under-specified auth
contract for a networked service, with a documented negative-control run proving no false
positive on local/no-auth work.
- [ ] Validation on `d251`: the OLD criteria did not flag the missing Gerrit auth; the NEW criteria
do. Negative controls (`8a1c`, `4702`) do not regress to false positives.
- [ ] `validate_packaged_routing()` passes; existing plan-review tests updated to the new
container/leaf routing; new test(s) covering container-scoped security + the endpoint-contract
check; `make lint` clean.

baseline.summary: Plan-review scrutiny keyed on ticket type not container/leaf — security overlay skips container epics

content.text: ## What
Add an `mcp_registry` job to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that publishes
`server.json` to the MCP Registry on a `v*` tag using **GitHub Actions OIDC**
(`mcp-publisher login github-oidc`) — eliminating the interactive
`mcp-publisher login github` device flow (whose cached Registry JWT expires and
was the one manual, friction-prone channel during the v0.7.0 release).
## Why
PyPI already publishes via OIDC Trusted Publishing and (change 314/316) GitHub
Releases are auto-created. The MCP Registry was the last channel still requiring a
human browser login. OIDC needs no stored secret: the runner's OIDC token proves the
`navapbc/rebar` repo identity, which authorizes the `io.github.navapbc/*` namespace.
## Implementation (per modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/github-actions)
- New job `mcp_registry`, `needs: publish` (runs after PyPI so the registry's
package-ownership check resolves against the live version), same
`if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` gate.
- `permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }`.
- Steps: `actions/checkout@v5` (server.json lives in the repo) -> install mcp-publisher
(curl the release binary, os/arch-detected) -> `./mcp-publisher login github-oidc`
-> `./mcp-publisher publish`.
- No version step needed: the `Release X.Y.Z` commit bumps server.json before the tag,
so the tag tree already carries the correct version.
- Update `docs/releasing.md` section 4 to mark MCP Registry as automated (OIDC in CI),
demoting the manual `mcp-publisher login/publish` to a fallback.
## Verification note (end-to-end)
Like the sibling `publish` and `github_release` jobs, this job runs ONLY on a real
`v*` tag push and cannot execute in Gerrit branch CI (no tag, no OIDC token). So the
live end-to-end path (login github-oidc -> publish -> registry updated) is verified
on the NEXT tagged release (v0.7.1+), not at merge time. Pre-merge verification is
necessarily static: YAML well-formedness + job wiring, and that the install/login/
publish commands match the canonical upstream recipe. This deferral is intentional
and mirrors how the existing OIDC PyPI publish job is verified.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` contains an `mcp_registry` job gated to `v*` tag push with `permissions.id-token: write`.
- [ ] That job checks out the repo, installs mcp-publisher, runs `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`, then `mcp-publisher publish`.
- [ ] The job declares `needs: publish` so it runs after the PyPI publish.
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` documents MCP Registry publishing as automated via OIDC, with the manual `mcp-publisher login github` path demoted to a fallback.
- [ ] The workflow YAML parses (validated with a YAML loader) and the commit lands on main through Gerrit (LLM-Review + Verified green).

baseline.description:
## Summary
The `verify-identity` job added to `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` in commit 5febe8274
("run verify-identity as a PRE-MERGE whole-store gate") more than DOUBLED gerrit-verify CI
runtime: runs jumped from ~12-27 min (through sha cb0f8ec3b) to 44-72 min, first spiking to
43.8 min on 5febe8274 itself. The `verify-identity` job is the sole long pole (66.2 min in a
66.6-min run); every other job is unchanged.

## Root cause (profiled against the real store: 2572 events in scope, 808 signed)
`rebar verify-identity` (the step) = 63.5 min; the git fetch is only 2.2 min. Phase timing:
- `_collect_all` (whole-store walk): 1.9s
- `build_introducing_commit_map` (batched git log, bug 1cc0): 2.3s
- classify UNSIGNED events: ~0ms each (short-circuits)
- classify SIGNED events: 1,780 ms EACH -> ~24 min local / ~63 min on slower CI runners

cProfile of one signed classify: ~100% of time in `subprocess.run`, via
`_verify_signed -> verify_authorship_at_commit -> keys_valid_at_anchor -> resolve_event_commit`
= a full-history `git log --diff-filter=A` PER keyring record, PER signed event (5 git spawns
/event). This is the exact O(events × keyring × history) cost bug 1cc0's
`build_introducing_commit_map` was built to kill, but the batched map was only wired into the
enforcement/grandfather decision (`_resolve_commit`), NOT the era-verify hot path — verified
events `continue` before reaching it.

Also: `_classify` runs UNCONDITIONALLY; `identity.require_authenticated` only gates the final
pass/fail verdict, never whether the per-event git work runs. So enforcement being off does
not avoid the cost.

## Config reality
require_authenticated = true (enforcement ON). enforce_since pinned to tracker HEAD at re-flip
time, so only events introduced AFTER it are enforced; all earlier events are grandfathered
(reported, never fail). The gate git-verifies all 808 signed events but only post-enforce_since
events can change the verdict.

## Fix plan (3 parts)
1. Gate the expensive per-event era-verify when NOT enforcing (require_authenticated off):
   classify signed events cheaply (signed vs unsigned) in advisory mode. VERIFIED: the era
   result feeds only (a) the exit code when enforcement is ON and (b) informational counts /
   --format json (consumed only by unit tests). Both CI workflows gate on exit code only,
   which is unconditionally 0 in advisory mode. Safe.
2. Skip ARCHIVED tickets in `_collect_all` (reuse the reduce already done in
   `_is_gate_exempt_ticket`; status == "archived"). Free and authoritative.
3. Wire `--base`/grandfather-boundary scoping into the gate so collection is bounded to
   `enforce_since..HEAD` (via existing `_collect_range`), eliminating the git-heavy
   re-verification of provably-grandfathered history. Behavior-preserving for the enforced
   verdict.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Advisory mode (require_authenticated=false) does NOT run per-event git era-verification;
      exit code stays 0; whole-store scan drops to seconds.
- [ ] Archived tickets are excluded from the scan (with a regression test).
- [ ] With enforcement ON, collection is scoped so only enforce_since..HEAD events are verified,
      AND the security invariant holds: an unsigned/forged event introduced AFTER enforce_since
      still FAILS the gate (held-out test), while pre-boundary events are not git-verified.
- [ ] gerrit-verify `verify-identity` job wall-time returns to the low-single-digit minutes.
- [ ] Full suite + lint + typecheck green; landed via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: verify-identity whole-store gate: 63-min CI runtime (O(events×keyring×history) git subprocesses)

# The comment dedup key is NOT normalized the way the description send value is

## Summary

The description path and the comment path have different convergence protections, and the missing piece is exactly the normalization half. Today this is LATENT — it costs nothing, because rebar does not currently model any content transformation on the comment send path. Any real Markdown/wiki converter activates it, and the symptom is duplicate Jira comments re-posted on every pass, forever.

Filed from a peer session's round-trip experiment over 5,568 real rebar bodies, verified here against the code rather than taken on report.

## The asymmetry, in code

**Descriptions are protected.** `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` composes

    normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))

so the value sent is already its own fixed point under the round trip. The ordering is deliberate and documented in a long comment there, and it is PINNED by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py::test_cloud_send_path_composition_is_unchanged`, which includes an explicitly soft-wrapped case.

**Comments are not.** `outbound_comments._diff_comments` builds its comparison key with

    compare_body = sanitizer.fit_comment(_normalize_comment_body(raw))

There is no `normalize_outbound` equivalent. And `_normalize_comment_body` does NOT normalize both sides the same way — it calls `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`, which is:

    if isinstance(body, dict):  return adf_to_text(body)     # the JIRA side: decoded
    return str(body) if body is not None else ""             # the LOCAL side: pass-through

So the Jira side is decoded and the local side is handed back verbatim. The two sides are compared after DIFFERENT transformations.

## Why the truncation guard proves the shape of the bug

The comment path already carries one guard of exactly this kind, added after it bit:

> the send path truncates an over-length body ... Apply the SAME shared truncation to the expected
> local body before the membership test; otherwise the full local body never matches the truncated
> Jira body and the diff re-emits forever.

That is the identical failure mode, patched for the ONE transformation the send path was known to apply. Nothing generalizes it. A content transformation gets no such treatment, and the machinery that would notice — a comparison against what Jira will actually store — does not exist.

The `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` canary exclusion is a second instance of the same class patched per-symptom: a volatile timestamp never matches a prior body, so the comment re-added every pass.

## Why it is latent RIGHT NOW (do not "fix" a bug that is not firing)

Cloud comments go out through ACLI as `jira workitem comment create --body <text>` (`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`). rebar never computes the ADF that Jira will store, so it applies no content transformation of its own, and the dedup key happens to match. DC's `WikiTextCodec` is pure identity in all four operations, so DC transforms nothing either.

I could not establish whether ACLI's own text→ADF conversion alters bodies (e.g. rejoining soft wraps) — that is a live question about a third-party binary and only a live pass settles it. If it DOES, this is already firing on Cloud today. Empirically, rebar's own `text_to_adf` DOES rejoin soft wraps, so the transformation is not hypothetical for that encoder.

## What I verified empirically (so the future work is not built on a wrong premise)

Probing today's `adf.normalize_description` directly: `**/*.py`, `__pycache__`, `**a** **b**`, pipe tables, backticks, fenced blocks, `-`/`*` bullets and `__bold__` all round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY and are fixed points. Today's ADF path does no Markdown parsing at all — it only rejoins soft wraps and strips trailing whitespace. So the peer session's 9-19% flap rate is a property of the PROPOSED converter, not of anything shipping.

## The good news: the seam is already in the right place

`map_fields_to_remote` is SHARED and composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(...))` for both backends, so a pandoc-backed `WikiTextCodec` slots in by implementing the codec — no differ change. The `RichTextCodec` four-operation split is what makes that possible. This ticket is about the comment path catching up to the description path, not about redesigning the seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the comment dedup key is computed from what the SEND PATH will produce, the same way the
      description value is — i.e. the local comparison key goes through the codec's outbound
      normalization, not just `fit_comment`
- [x] a test asserts the property directly: given a codec whose outbound transform is NOT the
      identity, a local comment already mirrored in Jira emits NO add. This is the cell that does
      not exist today — every current dedup test uses transformations applied to both sides
- [x] a corpus/property test over real rebar comment bodies asserts encode-then-decode is a fixed
      point for the comment path, not just unit examples
- [x] `RichTextCodec` implementations are pinned to `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`.
      `WikiTextCodec`'s identity satisfies this trivially TODAY, which is why a pandoc implementation
      that got it wrong would pass the existing suite
- [x] the dependency is DOCUMENTED: outbound has no origin-aware gate, and the reason it does not
      need one is that degradation is symmetric. If encode ever stops being decode's inverse, a body
      pulled from Jira starts being re-emitted and the human's Jira-native formatting is destroyed.
      That invariant is currently load-bearing and unwritten
baseline.summary: Comment dedup key is not normalized the way the description send value is

content.text: ## Summary

The designed un-archive seam — rebar revert <id> <archived-event-uuid> — is broken end to end: ticket-revert.sh removes the .archived marker and _is_net_archived (ARCHIVED minus REVERT) is implemented for the list fast-path, but the reducer's process_revert only appends a revert record; replay still applies the ARCHIVED event, so compiled state stays status=archived/archived=True and the ticket remains hidden.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified in sandbox against installed 0.4.0 == HEAD engine, temp store; discovered while validating the fix for bug bored-grain-wok / f803)
1. rebar archive <id>; note the ARCHIVED event uuid (event file in .tickets-tracker/<id>/).
2. rebar revert <id> <archived-uuid> -> exit 0; .archived marker removed.
3. rebar list -> [] (ticket still hidden); rebar show <id> -> status: archived.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: reverting the ARCHIVED event restores the pre-archive state (visible in list, status open).
- Actual: revert is recorded but the archived projection survives replay.
## Source
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reducer/_processors.py process_revert (~:255) — appends to reverts, never touches state["archived"]/state["status"].
- Working halves: ticket-revert.sh:180-196 (marker removal), ticket_reducer/_api.py _is_net_archived (+ :281 fast path).
## Fix direction
In process_revert, after the append:

if data.get("target_event_type") == "ARCHIVED" and state.get("archived"): state["archived"] = False; and if status is exactly "archived", restore "open" (preserves deleted semantics — process_archived keeps deleted status). Validated in sandbox. CAVEAT: .cache.json has no reducer-version key, so previously-cached reverted tickets stay hidden until cache invalidation — bump/add a cache version with this change (relates to bug fond-ulna-ball).
## Suggested RED test
Reducer-level: ARCHIVED then REVERT(target=ARCHIVED) replay -> archived=False, status=open, ticket present in reduce_all_tickets default projection. RED today.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] revert of an ARCHIVED event makes the ticket visible in default list with status open (RED test first)
- [ ] deleted tickets are NOT resurrected by reverting an ARCHIVED event
- [ ] Cache invalidation handled (version key or documented self-heal)
- [ ] test_ticket_reducer_marker.py and archive/revert suites green

baseline.summary: revert of an ARCHIVED event never un-archives: process_revert appends a record but leaves the archived projection intact

## Evidence — a REAL Jira DC instance, GitHub Actions run 30604756524

A writing reconcile pass (`--mode bootstrap-strict`) against the live J5 harness exits 1:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

Found by story J7's new live module (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`) on its FIRST real run. `--mode dry-run` passes; only the writing path crashes.

## Root cause — the PORT under-specifies what the CORE requires

`set_entity_property` is called from THREE core sites:

* `dispatch_one.py:321`     — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, jira_key, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `binding_store.py:517`    — `client.set_entity_property(keyed, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `apply_inbound_records.py:279` — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)`

It is implemented in exactly ONE place: `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:266` (Cloud).

And crucially it is **NOT a member of the `TicketTransport` Protocol** in `_backend.py`, which declares only create_issue / get_issue / update_issue / transition_issue_by_name / add_label / search_issues.

So the core depends on a transport method the PORT never declares. That is why every structural check passed while the real thing was broken: `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` is satisfied without it, the contract suite never calls it, and 1636 unit tests are green. The Protocol is not a faithful statement of the core's requirements, so conformance to it proves less than it appears to.

This is the SAME CLASS of defect as J6's `add_label` bug (a method called with a shape `jira.JIRA` never had). Both shipped because the only oracle was a fake that mirrored the author's assumption.

## Why it matters

Epic e369 exists to deliver Jira Server/Data Center support. With this defect a DC deployment cannot complete a writing reconcile pass at all — the headline capability does not work. `local_id` entity properties are the binding marker the reconciler plants to correlate remote issues with local tickets, so this is not cosmetic: without it, binding/correlation cannot be established on DC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport` implements `set_entity_property` against DC's REST v2 entity-property
      endpoint, asserted by a live test that FAILS before the fix
- [ ] a full writing reconcile pass (`bootstrap-strict`) against the J5 harness exits 0/75 with no
      unhandled exception — i.e. J7's `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` and
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` PASS
- [ ] **`set_entity_property` is added to the `TicketTransport` Protocol** so the port states what the
      core actually requires, and a backend missing it fails `isinstance` instead of failing at runtime
- [ ] an AUDIT of the remaining core call sites for other transport methods absent from the Protocol
      (same technique: grep `client.<method>` in core modules, diff against the Protocol's members),
      with anything found either added to the Protocol or explicitly justified — otherwise this exact
      bug recurs on the next backend
baseline.summary: DC writing reconcile pass crashes: transport lacks set_entity_property, which the port never declared

content.text: ## Context

The plan-review claim gate (verify.require_plan_review_for_claim) binds the attestation to the exact code HEAD sha and treats a HEAD mismatch as 'stale', blocking the claim. Because the binding is to the WHOLE commit (not the code the review was actually grounded against), ANY subsequent commit — even one in a completely unrelated file — invalidates a freshly-earned, still-correct attestation.

This is the over-invalidation / false-positive sibling of this epic's under-invalidation concern: 4fcd is about CODE drift NOT being detected (the attestation only binds ticket-material, so relevant code can drift undetected). This bug is the inverse: IRRELEVANT code changes DO invalidate, adding real friction. Both share the root cause — the code-binding is too coarse (whole-HEAD) rather than scoped to the review's resolved edit-set / cited files. The mechanism in this epic's AC1 ('detects material drift in the code ... e.g. the resolved edit-set / cited files') would fix both facets at once.
## Reproduction Steps
1. On a feature branch, run `rebar review-plan <ticketA>` at HEAD=X -> earns a signed attestation bound to X.
2. Commit unrelated work (e.g. another ticket's code, or even a docs typo) -> HEAD advances to Y.
3. Run `rebar claim <ticketA> --assignee me`.
## Expected
The claim succeeds: the attestation is still valid because none of the code ticketA's plan was grounded against changed.
## Actual

The claim is BLOCKED: `Error: cannot claim <ticketA>: attestation is stale (signed at X, HEAD is Y).` The only recovery is to re-run the heavy LLM `review-plan` (minutes + billable) purely because HEAD moved, even though nothing relevant drifted. Observed repeatedly while implementing epic ring-gun-jot: committing sweep N's code staled the already-earned attestation for sweep N+1, forcing a re-review.
## Impact / friction
- Forces serialization (review-plan -> claim must straddle zero intervening commits) and defeats pre-earning attestations in parallel.
- Re-review is slow (~3-5 min) and billable, incurred for no semantic reason.
- Especially painful on multi-ticket branches and shared-checkout test runs that move HEAD.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Claim freshness is scoped to the code the review was grounded against (resolved edit-set / cited files) rather than the whole HEAD sha, so an unrelated commit does NOT stale the attestation.
- [ ] A relevant change (to the cited/edit-set files) STILL invalidates (no regression of this epic's under-invalidation goal).
- [ ] Tested: review at X, commit an unrelated file, claim succeeds; review at X, commit a cited file, claim is blocked.
- [ ] Recovery guidance / friction is reduced (no full re-review required for an unrelated commit).

baseline.summary: Stale-attestation claim block: ANY new commit (even unrelated) invalidates a fresh plan-review attestation

baseline.description:
## Context

Split out of the code-grounding T2 epic (`850f-bf87-8600-4af6`, ADR 0030). Terraform is **not** a
code-build environment — it declares cloud infrastructure and provides no language server or dependency
resolution — so it is out of scope as a "build env for code resolution." But IaC findings have their
**own** tiered grounding that mirrors the T0/T1/T2 model in a different domain. The general lesson from
ADR 0030 is that the tiering **recurs per domain**; IaC is a distinct grounding **lane**, captured here
as its own epic rather than folded into `850f`.

## Context — the IaC tiering (to be designed)

- **IaC T0 — Registry existence.** Terraform Registry provider/module existence probe (the analogue of
  the code T0 deps-existence lane): a declared provider/module that does not exist in the Registry is a
  refutable reference.
- **IaC T1 — offline reference resolution.** `terraform validate` (no cloud creds, no network to a
  provider API): validates that references between resources/variables/outputs resolve within the
  configuration. Offline + deterministic-ish → the IaC analogue of the T1 syntactic floor.
- **IaC T2 — live plan.** `terraform plan` (needs cloud credentials + provider API access): the
  high-fidelity, non-deterministic, credential-bearing tier — the analogue of code T2, and subject to
  the same confirm-only + never-on-a-blocking-path constraints (plus a credential-handling/security
  design, since `plan` authenticates to a cloud account).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide the v1 IaC tier(s) to implement among Registry existence (T0), `terraform validate` (T1),
      and `terraform plan` (T2), with the determinism/credential/security tradeoffs recorded in an ADR.
- [ ] The chosen tier(s) emit the existing three-valued evidence contract at the correct provenance
      tier, with no change to the contract or its consumers.
- [ ] IaC resolution is self-contained + opt-in (gated behind config / an optional extra) and
      fail-open (missing `terraform` binary / no creds / timeout → `abstain` with a closed reason).
- [ ] `terraform plan` (if in v1 scope) never runs on a deterministic blocking path and never carries
      credentials into an untrusted context; otherwise it is explicitly deferred with rationale.
- [ ] Fail-open matrix tested per implemented tier.
- [ ] An IaC grounding lane exists that emits the same three-valued, fail-open evidence contract
- [ ] IaC resolution is confirm-only and off any deterministic blocking path unless a tier is proven
baseline.summary: IaC grounding lane: tiered terraform validate/Registry/plan resolution (T0/T1/T2), split from code-grounding T2

## Why
Bug 5e40 (chordal-quasilegal-pipit, auto-lander epic f1fa): when main advances, every signed plan-review attestation reads stale, and each re-review of the BYTE-IDENTICAL plan runs the full un-floored criteria set — exposed to the measured 32% same-material verdict instability. Verified from the store: f1fa passed 07-11 19:07 and blocked 07-12 11:25 at the SAME material fingerprint (0290197d) on an E2/F1 finding with a provably false absence premise. The convergence floors enabled by change 562 deliberately do NOT cover this scenario (their eligibility requires code-unchanged + plan-changed; this is the complement). The designed mitigation ALREADY EXISTS: progressive drift-refresh (ADR 0002, epic boil-golem-veto Story 2, commit 3c2d2c920, since migrated onto the workflow gate in 22572a72b/bd7d0d411) runs a cheap scoped E4+G1G2 grounding probe against the drifted code and REFRESHES the attestation when the plan still holds — new findings can then only come from drift-relevant grounding, never from re-sampling the full set. It shipped default OFF pending a token/latency measurement that was never taken. Operator has approved enabling it (2026-07-12).

## What
- Close the original opt-in condition: measure the token/latency saving of a drift-refresh probe vs a full re-review on a representative ticket (an f1fa-shaped fixture: signed PASS, plan unchanged, HEAD advanced) and record the numbers on this ticket.
- Flip `progressive_drift_refresh: bool = False` -> `True` in src/rebar/_config_schema.py (~line 250), rewriting the adjacent 'OFF by default — opt-in until measured' comment to default-ON framing with explicit false as the back-out (mirror the change-562 pattern, including the dated operator-authorization note).
- Rule-based stale-framing sweep at implementation time (the 70c8 pattern — grep for default-off/inert framing about drift-refresh across src/ tests/ docs/): src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:70/74/~490, docs/config.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md (the three-floors table), docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md (dated note; it already carries the 2026-07-11 novelty-floor note).
- Update default-pinning tests; keep the off-path (explicit False -> full re-review) covered.
- Behavioral regression test for the incident class: with default config, a drift-only-stale re-review runs the probe path (E4/G1G2 scope) and does NOT re-run the full criteria set; a probe that finds the plan still grounded refreshes the attestation without a new full verdict.
- NON-GOALS: no change to the probe's criteria scope (E4+G1G2 as shipped); no change to what STALES an attestation; Story B's Pass-2 grounding hardening is separate.

## Scope
src/rebar/_config_schema.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py (comments/docstrings), docs/config.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md, docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md, default-pinning tests, one new behavioral test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] VerifyConfig.progressive_drift_refresh defaults to True; explicit false restores the full-re-review path (tested).
- [ ] A behavioral test proves a drift-only-stale re-review under default config takes the scoped probe path and can refresh the attestation without a full re-review.
- [ ] The token/latency measurement (probe vs full review on a representative ticket) is recorded in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The stale-framing sweep leaves zero default-OFF claims about drift-refresh in src/, tests/, docs/ (dated ADR notes excepted).
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make typecheck passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.
baseline.summary: Enable progressive drift-refresh by default: drift-only-stale re-reviews run the scoped grounding probe, not a full re-review

## Why

The audit UI needs an optional, disabled-by-default, read-only local web surface that is fully inert
when off. Establishing that surface — the packaging extra, the config flag (with ALL its wiring), lazy
imports, the loopback binding, and a running server that renders one real page end-to-end — is the
riskiest architectural piece (gating + packaging + binding), so it ships first as a thin vertical
slice that proves the whole optional-surface mechanism.

## What

A `rebar audit serve` subcommand that, when enabled, starts a FastAPI server (reusing the `reviewbot`
web stack) bound to 127.0.0.1, serving a read-only INDEX page listing tickets that have audit data
(each linking to a per-ticket page that the sibling rendering story fills in). Gated by a new
default-false `[ui] enabled` config flag and a new `nava-rebar[ui]` optional extra; all web imports
are lazy so disabled / absent-extra = inert. Default port `8765` (overridable with `--port`).

## Dependencies (the read layer — ALREADY LANDED on `main`)

This story depends on the audit read layer delivered by the data-enrichment epic's story E
(`rebar.audit.read`), which is **already merged on `main`**. Pinned contract this story builds on:

- `rebar.audit.read.audit_trail(ticket_id: str, *, repo_root=None) -> dict` — best-effort, NEVER
  raises. Returns an `AuditTrail` dict:
  `{"ticket": dict, "plan_reviews": list[dict] (newest-first), "completion": {"attestation": dict|None,
  "sidecar": dict|None} | None, "code_reviews": list[dict] ({"ticket_id", "sidecars": list[dict]})}`.
- There is **no** `list_audited_tickets()` helper in the read layer. The index route therefore
  **enumerates audited tickets itself**: iterate `rebar.list_tickets()` (id + type) and include a
  ticket when its `audit_trail(id)` shows any audit data — i.e. non-empty `plan_reviews`, a non-`None`
  `completion`, or non-empty `code_reviews`. This enumeration lives in `server.py` (a small
  `_audited_ticket_ids()` / index helper), not in the read layer (which this story does not modify).

Because the read layer is landed, the live end-to-end AC is reachable **within this story alone** (no
stub needed): the E2E test seeds a ticket with a plan-review sidecar and asserts it appears on the
index.

## Endpoint access contract (human/admin auth)

The server binds 127.0.0.1 (loopback) ONLY and serves READ-ONLY content; there is no state-changing
endpoint. Human access control is the loopback boundary — no network principal can reach it — the
justified no-auth posture (matching datasette / mlflow / `git instaweb --local`). Binding a
non-loopback host requires an explicit `--host` flag that prints a warning to stderr; actually
exposing the service to a network (and any auth then required) is OUT of scope for this epic —
documented, not implemented. No machine credentials are involved.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — add `[project.optional-dependencies] ui = ["fastapi", "uvicorn[standard]",
  "jinja2"]` (reusing the reviewbot stack); document the extra with a comment matching the neighbouring
  `reviewbot`/`agents` extras.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — the FULL `UiConfig` wiring (a partial edit is silently dropped as an
  unknown section by `coerce_sparse`): (1) add a `UiConfig` dataclass with `enabled: bool = False`;
  (2) add `ui: UiConfig = field(default_factory=UiConfig)` to the top-level `Config` dataclass;
  (3) register `"ui": UiConfig` in `_SECTION_CLASSES`; (4) add `"ui": {"enabled": lambda v, k:
  _as_bool(v, k)}` to the `_SECTIONS` coercer map — yielding env override `REBAR_UI_ENABLED`.
- `src/rebar/config.py` — add an **explicit** per-class re-export line `from rebar._config_schema import
  UiConfig as UiConfig` (this module re-exports each `_config_schema` dataclass with an explicit
  `... as ...` line — lines 30–40; it does NOT wildcard-export, so a new class must be added by hand);
  document the key in `docs/config.md`.
- New `src/rebar/audit/server.py` (< 500 LOC) — the FastAPI app + a `serve(host, port)` entry,
  lazy-imported inside the CLI handler with a friendly "install nava-rebar[ui]" `SystemExit` on
  `ModuleNotFoundError`; binds 127.0.0.1 by default; one index route enumerating audited tickets (see
  Dependencies) and linking each to its per-ticket page. All `fastapi`/`jinja2` imports live inside
  `server.py` (module scope is fine — nothing in core imports `server.py`, and `import rebar` /
  `import rebar.audit` never pull it, keeping the disabled/absent-extra path inert).
- CLI — `audit` is **already** an intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py::main` dispatching to
  `rebar._cli._audit_commands.audit_cli` (story E landed `audit show` + `help/audit.txt`, and `audit`
  is already a known subcommand). This story **adds a `serve` subcommand** to the existing
  `audit_cli` dispatcher (which currently only handles `show`) and **updates `src/rebar/_cli/help/audit.txt`**
  to document `serve`. Do NOT re-register the intercept or touch `known_subcommands()` — both already
  exist. `serve` parses `--host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `--port` (default `8765`), and lazily imports
  `rebar.audit.server`.

## Approach rationale

Reuse the reviewbot FastAPI/uvicorn stack rather than adding Flask or a bespoke `http.server`, so the
repo carries one web framework; lazy-import it inside the command (never at package init) so
`import rebar` stays dependency-free — the pattern the reviewbot extra already proves. `audit` already
owns a nested command grammar (`show`) and its own help text; this story extends that grammar with
`serve`. Ship a thin vertical slice (server + one real index page) so the risky packaging/gating/binding
path is exercised end-to-end from the first story.

## Compatibility & rollback

Default-off and behind an extra; `import rebar` unchanged. The `[ui]` section is additive (absent
`[ui]` defaults to `enabled=False`). Rollback = flag off / extra not installed. No data/schema change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[ui] enabled` round-trips through config via `rebar.toml`, `REBAR_UI_ENABLED`, and
      `-c ui.enabled=...`, each yielding `Config.ui.enabled == True`, and is NOT reported as an unknown
      key. Oracle: a unit test loading config through all three paths and asserting the value + absence
      of the "unknown key ignored" warning.
- [ ] With `[ui] enabled = false` (default), `import rebar` imports no web dependency and
      `rebar audit serve` refuses to start with a message that **names the `[ui] enabled` flag** and
      exits non-zero. Oracle: a test asserting no fastapi module is imported by `import rebar`, and that
      the disabled `audit serve` path returns non-zero AND its stderr message contains the flag name
      (`ui.enabled` / `[ui] enabled`) and starts no server.
- [ ] With the `ui` extra absent, `rebar audit serve` (when enabled) exits with an actionable "install
      nava-rebar[ui]" message, not a traceback. Oracle: a unit test simulating `ModuleNotFoundError`
      on the lazy `rebar.audit.server` import and asserting the message names the extra + non-zero exit.
- [ ] `rebar audit serve --host 0.0.0.0` prints a non-loopback exposure warning to stderr before
      binding; `--host 127.0.0.1` (default) does not. Oracle: a CLI test asserting the warning's
      presence/absence per host (without actually serving on a public interface).
- [ ] `rebar audit serve --port <n>` binds the given port (default `8765`). Oracle: the live
      end-to-end test binds an ephemeral `--port` and reaches the index there.
- [ ] With the feature enabled, the server binds 127.0.0.1 and serves an index page listing tickets
      that have audit data. Oracle: a live end-to-end test starting the server on an ephemeral port and
      asserting the index returns HTTP 200 and lists a seeded audited ticket (test-design §3
      server/CLI).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: audit web server scaffolding (subcommand, [ui] extra, config flag, loopback)

## Why

The epic's Success Criteria require the `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar to capture the FULL four-pass
record, including **pass-4 coaching**. Stories 4e19 (plan) and 7c84 (code) enriched the per-finding
buckets but NEITHER touched the separate `coaching[]` array. The plan-review sidecar's `_slim`
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, the `"coaching"` block) persists each coaching note as only
`{move_id, finding_refs}` — it DROPS `move_name`, `subject`, and the rendered `coaching` prose. The
full verdict coaching shape (per `plan_review_verdict.schema.json`) is `{move_id, move_name, subject,
finding_refs[], coaching}`. Because the LLM-chosen `subject` and the rendered prose are not
persisted, a downstream audit UI cannot reconstruct or re-render the coaching note — it has only a
move id and finding refs. This defeats the epic's "lossless capture" goal for pass-4.

## What

Persist pass-4 coaching **losslessly** in the plan-review sidecar (`plan_review_result_v2`): store
the full coaching record `{move_id, move_name, subject, finding_refs, coaching}` instead of the
2-field slim. Confirm the code-review sidecar (`code_review_result_v2`) already persists coaching
losslessly (`build_payload` stores `verdict.get("coaching", [])` verbatim) and lock that in with a
regression test.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — in `build_payload`, change the `"coaching"` block to
  persist the full record per note: `{"move_id": c.get("move_id"), "move_name": c.get("move_name"),
  "subject": c.get("subject"), "finding_refs": c.get("finding_refs", []), "coaching":
  c.get("coaching")}` (keep it schema-tolerant — a note missing a field yields None, never
  KeyError). This is additive to the existing `plan_review_result_v2` payload (no schema bump); the
  reader is unchanged.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — NO code change (it already stores the full coaching
  array); add a regression test asserting the code-review sidecar payload's `coaching` carries the
  full record shape, so the lossless property cannot silently regress.

## Approach rationale

Pass-4 coaching is a separate `coaching[]` array (not per-finding), so it was outside 4e19/7c84's
per-finding enrichment. The fix is a minimal widening of the plan-review `_slim` coaching projection
to the full verdict shape — the same "stop dropping fields" pattern 4e19 applied to per-finding
evidence/scenarios. No schema version bump is needed (v2 already; the coaching array just gains
fields). Code-review already persists the full array, so it only needs a regression lock.

## Compatibility & rollback

Purely additive to the plan-review sidecar payload — existing readers ignore the extra coaching
fields; older `v1`/slim records stay readable. Reverting restores the 2-field slim with no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The plan-review sidecar payload persists each pass-4 coaching note with its full shape —
      `move_id`, `move_name`, `subject`, `finding_refs`, and the rendered `coaching` prose — not just
      `{move_id, finding_refs}`. Oracle: a unit test driving `build_payload` with a verdict whose
      `coaching[]` carries the full shape and asserting all five fields survive in the emitted
      payload.
- [ ] The code-review sidecar payload persists pass-4 coaching losslessly (full record shape).
      Oracle: a unit test driving `build_payload` with a full-shape coaching note and asserting the
      fields survive.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: pass-4 coaching lossless persistence (plan + code sidecars)
