## Reproduction Steps

1. Dispatch reconcile-bridge-canary.yml (dry_run=false) so it writes a heartbeat ticket event, or observe a scheduled reconcile-bridge run that writes inbound Jira events.
2. Fetch the tickets branch and inspect the created event JSON.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** the event carries author_sig (signed by the Rebar Bot identity 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d), verifiable via rebar verify-authorship.
- **Actual:** the event is ATTRIBUTED (author_id/author_email = bot) but has NO author_sig. No 'could not sign' warning appears, so signing was never attempted — the write step's rebar config never saw identity.signing_key.

## Root cause

Stories 1787 (canary) and 9e76 (bridge) materialize secrets.REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY to a 0600 $RUNNER_TEMP file and export REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY via $GITHUB_ENV in an early step. That cross-step $GITHUB_ENV value is not taking effect in the later rebar write steps (REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY appears 0 times in post-materialize step env in the run log). So attribution (git-email resolution) works but signing does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] reconcile-bridge.yml AND reconcile-bridge-canary.yml set REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY at the JOB-level env (static ${{ runner.temp }}/rebar-bot-signing-key path) so every write step sees it, instead of relying on cross-step $GITHUB_ENV propagation.
- [ ] A dispatched canary run (dry_run=false) produces a ticket event whose author_sig verifies as the bot identity via rebar verify-authorship.
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test pass.
baseline.summary: CI ticket writes attributed but UNSIGNED — job-level env for REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
A single Gerrit Verified run needs 21 concurrent job slots. The navapbc org is on GitHub Free: 20 total concurrent jobs and 5 concurrent macOS, enforced PER ORGANIZATION and shared with every other navapbc repo. So one run, in an otherwise idle org, cannot fully parallelize; under a 6-change burst later runs queued 6.7-8.4m for a macOS slot, which is what turns a ~21m run into the 41-47m seen from Gerrit.

`.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` fans out 5 `per-extra` matrix cells plus a `union` cell — 6 jobs, each doing 0.4-0.8m of real work while holding a slot for a full checkout + setup-python + install.

(The redundant `import-linter` job is handled separately in ticket 2132-e48f-425c-4f24; this ticket does not touch it.)

## Approach
Collapse the 5 `per-extra` cells + `union` into ONE job running a venv loop.

ITERATIONS. Five-plus-one is WRONG as originally drafted, because the current matrix list and `_optional.EXTRAS` are not the same set. Verified: `_optional.EXTRAS == {agents, eval, grounding, metrics, tracing}` while the matrix runs `{agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding}`. So:
- `mcp` is NOT in `_optional.EXTRAS` — it is the server transport, has no detection probe, and is validated by its boot check instead.
- `metrics` IS in `_optional.EXTRAS` and has NO per-extra CI today — a real pre-existing gap the loop closes for free.
The loop therefore runs over `_optional.EXTRAS` keys UNION `{mcp}` = six isolation iterations, PLUS one UNION iteration installing `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into a single venv. The union is not redundant with the isolation runs: it is the only thing exercising JOINT dependency resolution and can surface a `ResolutionImpossible` no single-extra install can.

PER-ITERATION WORK must reproduce everything the current cells do, not just the install:
- `import rebar` with the extra present;
- for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, assert `_optional.extra_installed(extra)` (the detection probe);
- `rebar-mcp --help` for the mcp iteration ONLY, reproducing today's `if: matrix.extra == 'mcp'`. Running it everywhere fails in venvs lacking the entry point; dropping it silently weakens the mcp boot check.

TWO ABSOLUTE RULES, each guarding a silent-failure mode:
- NEVER `source .../activate`. Activations STACK across iterations, so PATH decides which interpreter runs and every iteration can silently re-test extra #1.
- ALWAYS invoke by absolute path (`"$v/bin/python"`, `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"`). A bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` runs the AMBIENT interpreter and can pass while testing nothing. Today's `rebar-mcp --help` (_optionality.yml:178-180) is exactly such a bare console-script call and must be rewritten.

ERROR ISOLATION is explicit because Actions runs `run:` under `bash -e`: a naive loop dies on the first failure (losing today's `fail-fast: false` diagnostics), while `|| true`/`set +e` without aggregation makes the whole contract a no-op that ALWAYS PASSES. Use an `rc` accumulator — guard each iteration with `|| { rc=1; echo "::error::<extra> failed"; continue; }` and end the step with `exit $rc`.

VENV HYGIENE: `python -m venv` from a `setup-python` interpreter is already clean (user site-packages disabled, `include-system-site-packages=false`), and `PYTHONPATH`/`PIP_*` are unset in both workflows, so `--copies`/`PYTHONNOUSERSITE`/`--without-pip` are NOT needed. The pip HTTP cache shared across venvs is a speed benefit only (wheels are content-addressed). Run `pip install --upgrade pip` per venv (ensurepip ships an old pip).

KEEP `clean-core-wheel` byte-identical. It is the check this file header credits with catching "the module-scope-import class that escaped once", it builds a real wheel, and it is the ONLY lane where `agents_extra_installed()` is False — which is what makes its skipif-degradation tests actually execute.

Rejected: sequential `pip install .[agents]` then `.[eval]` into one shared python — after the first install the env is contaminated, so a missing dependency declaration in a later extra PASSES silently; that is the exact bug class this workflow exists to catch. Rejected: per-extra venvs with no union iteration (loses joint resolution). Rejected: collapsing `clean-core-wheel` in. Considered and not chosen: `strategy: {max-parallel: 1}` on the existing matrix (5->1 peak slots, zero new bash) — the loop was chosen deliberately for the larger slot saving.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — replace the `per-extra` matrix job and the `union` job with the single venv-loop job.
- `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — durable guards on the loop shape and extras coverage.
- `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` — it hard-codes the doomed check names (`extra "agents" installs`, `union [agents,eval,tracing] resolves`, ...). It is not the live ruleset (that is Terraform `gerrit-mirror-lock-main`, which declares no `required_status_checks`), but it IS POSTed back by `infra/github/rollback-mirror-lock.sh:75-88` — so leaving it stale means an emergency rollback would demand checks that cannot exist and would freeze `main`.

NOT in scope: `import-linter` (ticket 2132), `clean-core-wheel`, `_build-and-test.yml`, `gerrit-verify.yaml`.

## Testing
Durable checked-in guards, not one-time manual observations, because the risk is a later careless edit:
- assert the loop step text contains the `rc` accumulator shape (`continue` and `exit $rc`) and contains NO `activate`, so the swallowed-failure and stacked-activation footguns cannot be reintroduced silently;
- assert every key in `_optional.EXTRAS` appears in the looped extra list, so a newly declared extra cannot ship with zero CI.

Workflow-level validation: `optionality.yml` triggers on `push`, so pushing a scratch branch to the GitHub mirror exercises the modified reusable end-to-end. A PULL REQUEST does NOT work — `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` runs `dessant/repo-lockdown` on `pull_request_target` with `close-pr: true` (only dependabot exempt), so the mirror auto-closes PRs. `workflow_dispatch` on `optionality.yml` is the fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each isolation extra installs into its own freshly-created venv, never one that already had another extra installed.
- [ ] The isolation iteration set equals `_optional.EXTRAS` keys plus `mcp`, so `metrics` gains per-extra CI it does not have today.
- [ ] A UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into one venv.
- [ ] Each isolation iteration runs `import rebar` and, for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, asserts `_optional.extra_installed(extra)`.
- [ ] `rebar-mcp --help` runs for the mcp iteration only, invoked by absolute venv path.
- [ ] Every interpreter/console-script call in the loop uses an absolute `"$v/bin/..."` path, and the loop contains no `activate`.
- [ ] The loop uses an `rc` accumulator with `continue` and exits non-zero if any iteration failed.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the loop step contains `exit $rc` and `continue` and no `activate`.
- [ ] A checked-in test asserts the looped extra list covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`.
- [ ] `clean-core-wheel` is byte-identical to its current form.
- [ ] `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` no longer names removed checks.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pass.
- [ ] `make lint` passes (actionlint covers all workflows).
baseline.summary: Collapse the optionality per-extra fan-out into one venv-per-extra job

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Discovered from 80af: `rebar verify-commit-ticket` fails 'ticket store not found' in a fresh linked worktree because it is a PURE INTERCEPT (_cli/__init__.py:438) dispatched before the arms that call the centralized `ensure_initialized`, and it does not self-manage init — yet it resolves ids against the store. The mount step is replicated per dispatch-arm and skipped entirely by the intercepts, so the "command forgot to mount the store" bug is structurally possible.

## Design (agreed)
The MOUNT half of init (`ensure_initialized(init_only=True)` → `_create_tracker`: symlink a worktree to the main repo store / attach to an existing tickets branch; already a no-op under REBAR_TRACKER_DIR override) should run at ONE central CLI choke point, BEFORE both the pure intercepts and the set-based dispatch, for every store-touching command. The RECONVERGE half (`reads.ensure_fresh`) is already shared across CLI/library/MCP via the _reads facade and stays in the leaves (init_only vs full differ ONLY by reconverge). Per the tolerance we agreed: the per-arm `ensure_initialized` calls may remain (idempotent re-mount is cheap and non-fatal); the central gate's job is to guarantee no command skips mount. Commands that must NOT auto-mount (policy=none): `init` (is init), `scratch` (fs-only), `explain` (guides, no store), and pure no-store reads.

Scope: CLI surface only. Library (`import rebar`) and MCP intentionally do NOT auto-mount (they require explicit init_repo / assume a mounted store; embedders inject a tracker which no-ops the gate) — unchanged here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar verify-commit-ticket` in a fresh linked worktree (no .tickets-tracker) auto-mounts (symlink to main repo store) and resolves the id, instead of 'ticket store not found' — regression test.
- [ ] The mount runs at a single central CLI gate covering the pure intercepts; no store-touching command can skip it.
- [ ] `explain` (and init/scratch) are NOT force-mounted — they keep working with no store — guard test.
- [ ] REBAR_TRACKER_DIR override still short-circuits the gate (tests/embedding unaffected).
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green; docs/cli-reference regenerated if the CLI surface changed.
baseline.summary: Centralize CLI store-mount so no command (incl. pure intercepts like verify-commit-ticket) can skip it

baseline.description:
Register `session_log` as a first-class ticket type and enforce its write-path
rules: it can be created and edited/commented, but it is gate-exempt, cannot be
claimed or transitioned, and rejects blocking links while allowing non-blocking
ones.

## Why

This is the foundation the rest of the epic builds on. The type must exist and
behave correctly on the write path before performance isolation, the recent-logs
command, Jira exclusion, or capture tooling can be layered on.

## What

- Add `session_log` to the ticket-type enum in
  `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` and to `_TYPES` in
  `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` (and its error message).
- Give it a hierarchy placement in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` that keeps it
  out of blocking-link promotion (leaf / non-participating).
- Refuse `claim` and `transition` on a `session_log` with a clear message
  (lifecycle-exempt); keep `show` / `comment` / `edit` working as normal.
- In the link path, refuse `blocks` / `depends_on` for a `session_log` endpoint
  while allowing `relates_to` / `discovered_from`.
- Make `clarity_check` / `check_ac` / `quality_check` treat `session_log` as
  exempt (pass/skip) in `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py`.

## Scope

Write-path + type registration only. Read-path performance isolation, the recent
command, Jira exclusion, capture tooling, and docs are separate stories.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar create session_log "..."` succeeds across schema + `_TYPES`.
- [ ] `claim` and `transition` on a `session_log` are refused with a clear error.
- [ ] `blocks` / `depends_on` to/from a `session_log` are refused; `relates_to` /
      `discovered_from` succeed.
- [ ] `clarity_check` / `check_ac` / `quality_check` return exempt/pass for a
      `session_log` regardless of body shape.
- [ ] `show`, `comment`, and `edit` operate normally on a `session_log`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover create, the refusals, the link rules, and gate exemption.
baseline.summary: Register session_log type + write-path rules (gate/lifecycle exempt, non-blocking links)

baseline.description:
## What

Turn on the cross-ticket overlap detector (epic only-crave-art) for THIS project by
setting `verify.overlap_enabled = true` in the tracked project config `rebar.toml`.
The feature's code shipped and is tested but ships gated OFF by default; this flips the
flag on so plan-review runs the advisory store-wide overlap step and surfaces `overlap[]`
suggestions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.toml` `[verify]` section sets `overlap_enabled = true` with an explanatory comment.
- [ ] No OTHER config key changes: `git diff rebar.toml` shows only the added
      `overlap_enabled` line + its comment block.
- [ ] The file still parses:
      `python -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('rebar.toml','rb'))"` exits 0.
- [ ] The local build reads the flag as true (not stale-global):
      `python -c "from rebar.config import load_config; assert load_config('.').verify.overlap_enabled is True"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] The overlap step executes end-to-end, proven by a structured assertion on the verdict.
      `rebar review-plan` emits JSON by default (flag is `--output json` / `-o json`; there is
      no `--json` flag):
      `rebar review-plan ade2-8c73-e010-491d --output json | python -c "import sys,json; v=json.load(sys.stdin); assert 'overlap' in v, v"`
      exits 0 (an empty `overlap: []` is expected until digests are enriched — the point is the
      key is PRESENT, proving the step ran and the flag is wired, not stale-global).
- [ ] Commit references this ticket (rebar-ticket trailer) and passes `make lint`.
- [ ] Change lands on `main` through Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1).

## Scope

- **`rebar.toml` only — a one-key config flip, no code change.** It does not add, remove, or
  alter any source; it activates behavior in code paths that already shipped and are already
  covered by the epic's test suite (`tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`, etc.). `rebar.toml` is the tracked, git-committed project
  config (preferred by config discovery over the git-ignored `.rebar/config.conf`), so the flag
  is persistent and shared for all contributors without per-machine env-var setup. Rollback is
  setting it back to false.

## Behavioral activation — the flag gates TWO paths (both already tested)

Flipping `overlap_enabled` on is a config-only change but it ACTIVATES two independent,
already-shipped code paths. Naming both so the behavioral consequence and its controls are explicit:

1. **Plan-review overlap step** (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`): the advisory two-stage
   retrieve-then-rerank pass that populates `overlap[]` on the verdict. **Advisory only —
   never blocks a claim or close.**
2. **Opportunistic enrichment drain** (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py::maybe_drain`, gated on the
   same `verify.overlap_enabled` check, invoked from the ticket write paths in
   `_store/event_append.py` and `_store/push.py`): asynchronously builds the BM25F digests
   stage-1 retrieval needs. So an ordinary `rebar` ticket write MAY now opportunistically trigger
   LLM enrichment.

**Mitigation / bounding (why path #2 is safe to enable):** the drain is best-effort and
**can never fail a write** (`maybe_drain` swallows all exceptions); it only fires when there is
soaked + lease-eligible work, is bounded by the `[tool.rebar.llm] overlap_drain*` tunables
(soak-min, lease-ttl, drain-batch, gate-budget), and — crucially — is **independently
disableable**: set `overlap_drain = "off"` under `[tool.rebar.llm]` to get plan-review overlap
WITHOUT any write-path enrichment (default is `async`; `always` runs it inline for tests/CI).
Verification of path #2's bounding/never-fails behavior is the epic's existing
`tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` (an end-to-end drain-fire AC is intentionally NOT added here —
this ticket changes no code, only enables already-tested paths). Rollback
(`overlap_enabled = false`) disables BOTH paths together.
baseline.summary: Enable store-wide overlap detection in project rebar.toml

baseline.description:
The `test` GitHub Actions workflow's `lint + type-check` job fails on EVERY push to
`main` (the post-merge branch CI + the Gerrit `Verified` mirror both run
`pre-commit run --all-files`). Root cause: commit `703661409`
(`compliable-stretchy-bee`, ticket e72b) added the `no-commit-to-branch` pre-commit
hook with `args: [--branch, main, --branch, master]`. That hook is a LOCAL,
commit-time guardrail ("don't commit directly to main"), but CI legitimately checks
out and runs `pre-commit run --all-files` while HEAD is on `main`, so the hook fires
and fails the whole job. The real enforcement of "land through Gerrit" is
server-side (GitHub ruleset + the two Gerrit votes); the hook was never meant to gate
CI.

The reason it landed SILENTLY is a CI-vs-Gerrit DRIFT the existing parity guard could
not see: gerrit-verify.yaml (pre-merge Verified gate) and test.yml (post-merge branch
CI) run the IDENTICAL `pre-commit run --all-files`, but gerrit-verify checks the change
out at a detached `refs/changes/*` ref (hook silent → Verified +1 → lands) while
test.yml runs on the `main` branch (hook fires → red). test_ci_workflow_parity.py only
compared command SIGNATURES, so both files running the same command looked fine.

Evidence: run 29470200567 (branch `main`) fails at
`pre-commit ... don't commit to branch...Failed` → `Process completed with exit
code 1`; lint + type-check failed on 6/6 recent main runs. A green run (29464899221)
was on a FEATURE branch, where the hook passes because HEAD is not main/master.

## Reproduction Steps
- [ ] Check out `main` (as CI does on a push-to-main event).
- [ ] Run `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` (the exact CI step).
- [ ] Observe `no-commit-to-branch` reports `Failed` and the command exits 1.

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: on a legitimate CI checkout of `main`, `pre-commit run --all-files`
  runs the code-hygiene + lint/typecheck hooks and passes; the local-only
  `no-commit-to-branch` guardrail does not gate CI.
- Actual: `no-commit-to-branch` fires because HEAD is `main`, failing the
  `lint + type-check` job on every main push.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The CI `pre-commit run --all-files` step in `.github/workflows/test.yml`
      skips the `no-commit-to-branch` hook (via `SKIP: no-commit-to-branch` in the
      step `env:`), verifiable by inspecting the step's `env:` block in the file.
- [ ] The same skip is applied to the mirrored `pre-commit` step in
      `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (Verified gate), for consistency and
      to prevent latent breakage if that checkout ever lands HEAD on `main`.
- [ ] The `no-commit-to-branch` hook remains present and unchanged in
      `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (the local commit-time guardrail is preserved, not
      removed), verifiable by diff.
- [ ] Locally reproduce the skip working: `SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run
      no-commit-to-branch --all-files` reports the hook as `Skipped`.
- [ ] DRIFT GUARD (the incident owner's second ask): a new test
      `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_branch_sensitive_precommit_hooks_skipped_in_ci`
      fails the build unless every branch-sensitive pre-commit hook (derived from
      `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, currently `no-commit-to-branch`) is SKIPped in BOTH
      workflows' `pre-commit run --all-files` step — closing the context-drift gap the
      command-signature parity could not catch.
- [ ] The guard is proven to have teeth (RED→GREEN): with the SKIP reverted the guard
      FAILS naming the exact missing skip; with it present all parity tests pass.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` remain green (change is the two workflow YAMLs
      plus the one parity-test file).
baseline.summary: CI lint job fails on every main push: no-commit-to-branch hook fires in pre-commit run --all-files

content.text: `rebar session-logs` silently returns nothing when the limit is passed in the
space-separated form (`--limit 30`) instead of the equals form (`--limit=30`).
The read-side CLI commands only accept `--opt=value`, while write/composer
commands (and even `ready` in the same module) accept the `--opt value` space
form, so the option-value syntax is inconsistent across the CLI and the repo's
own docs use the space form (e.g. `claim <id> --assignee <you>`). An agent
following that convention runs `session-logs --limit N`, gets a 2-line error on
stderr, and — if stderr is discarded or the output is piped — sees an empty
result and wrongly concludes there are no session logs.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Ensure session logs exist (`rebar session-logs` with no args lists them).
2. Run `rebar session-logs --limit 5` (space-separated form).
3. Observe: `Error: unknown option '--limit'` + usage on stderr, exit code 2.
4. Run `rebar session-logs --limit=5` (equals form) → works, exit 0.
5. Same split elsewhere: `rebar list --status open` → exit 2; `--status=open` → 0.
## Expected
- `--limit 30` (space form) is accepted, OR option-value syntax is consistent
across all CLI commands and matches the documented `--opt <value>` convention.
- A flag-parsing error is never mistaken for "no results": the symptom that the
command "comes back empty" should not happen for a mere arg-form mismatch.
## Actual
- `_cmd_session_logs` (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:236-252) matches
only `arg.startswith("--limit=")`; the space form falls to the `else` →
`unknown option '--limit'`, exit 2.
- Inconsistency is intra-file: `_cmd_ready` (reads_cli.py:302-311) accepts BOTH
`--epic <id>` and `--epic=<id>`; `claim --assignee <you>` (composer parser,
src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:477-480) accepts the space form too.
## Notes
- Root cause is arg-form parsing, not the session-log store: data is present and
the equals form returns it correctly. Severity is low (workaround = use `=`),
but it is a recurring agent-facing footgun and a CLI-consistency defect.
- Fix should address the read-CLI option parser class (session-logs `--limit`,
list `--status`, and peers), not just session-logs, so the space form is
accepted uniformly. Decide deliberately whether to standardize on accept-both
(recommended, matches docs) or to reject space-form everywhere and fix the docs.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar session-logs --limit 30` (space form) returns the same result as
`rebar session-logs --limit=30` (no "unknown option" error).
- [ ] Option-value parsing is consistent across the read-CLI commands in
`reads_cli.py` (at minimum `session-logs --limit` and `list --status`
accept the same form(s) as `ready --epic`).
- [ ] The chosen convention (accept-both vs equals-only) matches the documented
usage in CLAUDE.md / `--help`; whichever is picked, docs and parser agree.
- [ ] A regression test covers both `--limit 30` and `--limit=30` for
`session-logs` (and the analogous `list --status` space/equals forms).

baseline.summary: CLI: 'session-logs --limit <n>' (space form) rejected as unknown option — read-command flags accept only --opt=value, inconsistent with write commands/docs

content.text: ## Why
Code review (M3) flagged `shallow_contract_check` living in `executor.py` but
re-exported from `lint_refs.py` via `__getattr__` to dodge an import cycle (forced by
the lint_refs size cap), and that it is not yet consumed by the linter.
## What / Scope
Decide + record the home of `shallow_contract_check`: either relocate it to a neutral
module both `executor` and `lint_refs` can import directly (removing the `__getattr__`
indirection), or document the indirection as an accepted tradeoff. Wire it into the
linter if/where the static check belongs.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `shallow_contract_check`'s placement is either cleaned up (no `__getattr__` re-export) or explicitly documented as intentional with the rationale.
- [ ] If it is meant to back a lint check, it is wired in with a test; if standalone, that is documented.

baseline.summary: Resolve shallow_contract_check module placement / lint_refs size

baseline.description:
Prepare the committed helper and a verified real rehearsal artifact needed by the reclaim window. This story performs no remote ref deletion and never pushes. A6-1 alone refreshes the bundle if `origin/tickets` moved, deletes identified pins, and publishes the rewrite after all writers are quiesced. Session log 1cb6-d553-6565-49b4 contains measured facts.

## Context

Remote tag `refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z` and host-local tag `refs/tags/pre-a3-remediation` retain pre-rewrite history. An in-repository backup ref would defeat reclamation, so rollback material must be a bundle outside every Git worktree and Git directory. Live ref OIDs are derived at execution time rather than from measured counts or hardcoded IDs.

## Plan

- Add `infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py`, a stock-Git CLI for a clean, unfiltered clone owned exclusively by one invocation. It accepts the old tickets tip, an off-repo bundle path, a JSON manifest path, and repeatable pin-ref names. Import A6-0c `run_git`, `ref_name`, `is_partial_clone`, and `ReclaimError` from `reclaim_bridge_history.py` so safety behavior cannot drift.
- Enumerate `git ls-remote --heads --tags origin` at run time, collapse annotated-tag `^{}` lines onto canonical refs, and record every head/tag with exact direct and peeled OIDs. For each commit tip, record one relationship to the old tip: same, old-tip-is-ancestor, ref-is-ancestor, diverged-with-merge-base, unrelated, or non-commit.
- Refuse a clone containing any pre-existing `refs/reclaim-backup/` ref and name the fresh-clone remedy. Create one run-unique namespace beneath that prefix. Normal success and caught failures remove only that invocation namespace in `finally`; abnormal termination recovery is to discard the clone and rerun in a fresh unfiltered clone. Separate concurrent clones share no local refs, cannot overwrite existing artifact paths, and perform no remote write.
- Resolve requested pins from live enumeration or the local clone and refuse missing/non-commit pins. Build the bundle from explicit temporary refs for the old tip and pins, then verify it.
- Refuse partial/promisor clones. Refuse bundle or manifest paths inside the repository, its Git directory, or another registered worktree. Create parent directories only outside those boundaries and never overwrite an artifact.
- Restore the bundle into a throwaway repository and compare the restored old-tip and pin-tip OIDs exactly. Snapshot origin heads/tags before and after; no push, delete, or remote mutation is permitted.
- Run against a fresh real unfiltered clone and store the rehearsal bundle/manifest outside the repository. Record paths, SHA-256 checksums, sizes, old tip, pin tips, and bundle verification. A6-1 creates a fresh final bundle after quiescence whenever its old tip differs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] The helper enumerates every live origin head/tag at run time without a hardcoded count. Tier: temporary real Git remotes.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The manifest collapses annotated-tag `^{}` lines while retaining exact direct and peeled OIDs. Tier: temporary real Git remotes.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Every enumerated commit ref receives exactly one old-tip relationship. Tier: real Git fixtures for same, ancestor, descendant, diverged, and unrelated histories.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A non-commit ref is recorded without an ancestry command on that object. Tier: real Git remote with a blob ref.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Partial/promisor clone refusal exits nonzero before creating refs or artifacts and names a fresh-unfiltered-clone remedy. Tier: CLI integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Any output destination inside a registered worktree or Git directory is refused. Tier: real worktree integration parameterized for bundle and manifest.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Any pre-existing output artifact is not overwritten. Tier: CLI integration parameterized for bundle and manifest.
- [x] [code-verifiable] The bundle named-ref map exactly matches the expected old-tip plus requested pin-tip OIDs. Tier: real Git bundle integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] `git bundle verify` succeeds for the completed bundle. Tier: real Git bundle integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Bundle restore reproduces the full expected old-tip plus pin-tip OID map. Tier: real Git restore integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A recording Git wrapper observes no push or remote-delete invocation. Tier: CLI integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Origin heads/tags output is byte-identical before and after success. Tier: real Git comparison.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A caught verification failure leaves no incomplete artifact or current-run helper ref. Tier: fault-injected real-repository integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A pre-existing helper ref causes a nonzero fresh-clone-remedy result without deleting that ref. Tier: real Git ref integration.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Retrying from a fresh clone after simulated abnormal termination succeeds with current requested OIDs. Tier: killed-process integration.
- [x] [operator-attested] A ticket comment records both rehearsal artifact absolute paths.

## Context / Problem
While closing ticket 86a5-9221-0037-4e38 on current origin/main, the landed-work precheck scanned all reachable commit messages and printed three unrelated resolver errors such as `Error: Ambiguous prefix 2f3c matches multiple tickets`. The target ticket used a full ID and closed successfully, so these diagnostics came from unrelated historical commit references. `_referencing_commit_exists` calls the shared resolver for every extracted reference; the resolver writes ambiguity errors to stderr even though the precheck only needs to know whether a reference matches the accepted target IDs.

## Approach
Make the close precheck resolve unrelated historical candidates silently while preserving normal resolver diagnostics for user-facing commands. Add a regression test with an ambiguous historical short prefix before a valid full-ID trailer and prove close scanning neither emits the unrelated error nor misses the valid commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The close landed-work precheck does not print ambiguity diagnostics for unrelated historical commit references.
- [ ] A later valid full-ID commit reference is still detected when earlier history contains an ambiguous short prefix.
- [ ] Target-ID ambiguity remains visible in commands where the user explicitly supplies an ambiguous prefix.
- [ ] Focused tests and `make lint` pass.
baseline.summary: Close precheck prints unrelated ambiguous-prefix resolver errors

# A stale installed build must fail LOUDLY, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

## Context / Problem
Split out of bug 7cbe, whose ENVIRONMENT repair is complete. This is the durable half: 7cbe cost two weeks of silent gate degradation, and the reason it went unnoticed is a REPORTING defect in this repository's code, not the broken install.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured. A stale global build could not parse the dict-shaped `activate` in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, so criteria assembly raised `CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. The gate collapsed that into the ordinary LLM-outage path:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay ...: 'activate' must be a
                  list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command exits 2 and still emits a sidecar. The DET tier runs and reports per-criterion pass/fail, so the output LOOKS substantive. A reader — human or agent — reasonably concludes the TICKET could not be reviewed. In fact no LLM review happened at all, and the fault was entirely in the installed build. This is a CONFIGURATION fault wearing an LLM-outage costume.

## Approach
Separate the two failure classes at the point where the verdict's reason is built. An LLM outage (provider unreachable, rate-limited, credential rejected) and a CONFIG-PARSE fault (the installed build cannot read this repository's config) are different conditions with different remedies, and collapsing them is what hid this.

A `CriteriaError` escaping criteria assembly should surface as its own reason — distinct from `llm_unavailable` — and the message should name the INSTALLED BUILD as the suspect, because that is where the fault lives. The reader must be pointed at the install, not at the plan.

Consider also a cheap staleness signal: when the running build's commit is far behind the repository's HEAD, say so at gate time. That is the generalisation — a stale build will find new ways to fail, and the specific `activate` shape is only the instance we hit.

REJECTED — making the parse failure fatal (exit non-zero with no verdict): the gate is fail-closed by design and callers depend on receiving a verdict. The fix is to make the reason ACCURATE, not to change the control flow.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — where `llm_unavailable` / `llm_error` are set for a failed assemble
  step; add the distinct config-fault reason.
- possibly `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` — so the raised error carries enough context to be
  classified without string-matching.
- `tests/unit/` — the discrimination tests.

## Testing
Inject a `CriteriaError` from criteria assembly (a malformed overlay fixture, or monkeypatching `effective_criteria` to raise) and assert on the resulting VERDICT PAYLOAD — the observable a reader actually sees — never on internal names. Pair it with a genuine LLM-outage case in the same test file so the two are pinned as distinct rather than merely one being tested in isolation. A negative control matters here: a real outage must STILL report `llm_unavailable`, or the fix has simply relabelled everything.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test injects a `CriteriaError` during criteria assembly and asserts the verdict payload
      reports a CONFIG-FAULT reason distinct from `llm_unavailable`. This criterion fails against the
      current implementation, which reports `llm_unavailable: true` for that input
- [ ] a NEGATIVE CONTROL test asserts a genuine LLM outage still reports `llm_unavailable`, so the
      change discriminates rather than relabelling every failure
- [ ] a test asserts the surfaced message for the config-fault case names the INSTALLED BUILD (or its
      resolved location/version) as the suspect, so a reader is pointed at the install and not at the
      ticket
- [ ] the DET tier's behaviour is unchanged for both cases — a config fault must not suppress the
      deterministic findings that already run
baseline.summary: A stale installed build must fail loudly, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

content.text: ## Why
Collapse the reviewer-centric model into the unified prompt model: reviewers become a SUBSET of
prompts; the catalog becomes a generated derived index. Validated by spike E5.
## What
- Migrate the 6 reviewers' `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/catalog.json` metadata into per-file front-matter
using S2's writer (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`).

- Introduce a NEW unified resolver `get_prompt(prompt_id: str) -> Prompt` in `src/rebar/llm/prompts.py` to replace `get_reviewer`. NAMESPACE (verified): `resolve_prompt(reviewer, variables, langfuse)` ALREADY EXISTS as the template-render step (RETAINED; adapted to accept the unified `Prompt`) and `load_prompt` ALREADY EXISTS — so the new resolver is `get_prompt`, NOT `resolve_prompt`/`load_prompt`. Signature:
`get_prompt(prompt_id: str) -> Prompt` where `Prompt` exposes `{id, text, inputs, outputs,
execution_mode, category, is_reviewer, dimension, applies_to}`; it raises `PromptNotFound` for an
unknown id. Resolution order: project `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override > built-in packaged. Reviewer
membership is EXPLICIT (`category: review` / reviewer flag), NEVER inferred from output-schema shape.
MIGRATE the sole consumer `runs.py:RunnerAgentStep.run()` (calls `get_reviewer` at ~line 130) to
`get_prompt` (then call the existing `resolve_prompt` render-step with the resulting `Prompt`); remove `get_reviewer`.
- Build the GENERATED + COMMITTED derived-index (scan front-matter -> index) enforcing invariants
(exactly-one default; no `dimension` collision; preserve `langfuse_prompt`/`fallback_file`/
`applies_to`). A RETIRE path: a removed prompt is dropped from the index on regeneration. Add a CI
drift gate (`regenerate + git diff --exit-code`) in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. `applies_to` keeps
stdlib `fnmatch`.
## Scope
In: migration + resolver(+removal) + index(+retire) + CI gate + regression-equivalence. Out: prompt
CONTRACTS in the runner (S4), editor library (S6).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The 6 reviewers carry front-matter; `get_prompt(id)` resolves project>built-in and returns the unified `Prompt`; reviewer flag explicit.
- [ ] `get_reviewer` is REMOVED, `catalog.json` is removed/fully-derived, and a grep confirms no remaining `get_reviewer` callers (caller migration complete).

- [ ] Derived index generated+committed; invariants enforced (two-default AND dimension-collision rejections both tested); a removed prompt is retired from the index; CI drift gate fails on a stale index.
- [ ] Existing reviewer behavior preserved (resolution/default/applies_to routing) — equivalence regression tests green.

- [ ] The new unified resolver is `get_prompt(prompt_id) -> Prompt` (NOT `resolve_prompt`/`load_prompt`, which already exist); the existing `resolve_prompt(reviewer,variables,langfuse)` render-step coexists with no name clash; `get_reviewer` is removed and grep-clean.
- [ ] Migration stamps `execution_mode` on EVERY migrated prompt (default `agentic`), so no migrated prompt relies on an implicit default.

baseline.summary: Reviewer->prompt migration + resolver generalization + derived-index lockfile

baseline.description:
# Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic

## Scope: FOUR sites, one root cause, THREE take the class fix

Each builds a `RunRequest` by hand with `config=cfg` and declares no model class, so it inherits `cfg.model` regardless of how the three model classes are configured. MEASURED, not inferred — see the comments for the full experiment:

    llm/overlap/judge.py:46              op=overlap-judge    18 calls   <-- 18 of 23 in a plan review
    llm/enrich.py:81                     op=ticket-digest     1 call    <-- runs on the STORE WRITE path
    llm/operations.py:177                op=ticket-quality    1 call
    llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:571  op=code-novelty      1 call    <-- the site originally filed

Everything else honours the configuration: all four plan-review passes, the completion verifier, and all seven code-review workflow steps.

## Why this matters beyond consistency

Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or contractual reasons. These calls send real content to direct Anthropic: the diff and prior findings (`code-novelty`), ticket text (`ticket-digest`, `ticket-quality`), and ticket digests for pairwise comparison (`overlap-judge`).

**`overlap-judge` dominates plan-review traffic** — 18 of 23 calls. An operator who cuts over by configuring the three classes (the documented mechanism, and the one story eb6e will use) leaves the MAJORITY of plan-review traffic on direct Anthropic.

**`ticket-digest` is the most insidious** because it is not in a gate at all: `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` is called from `_store/event_append.py:609` and `_store/push.py:295`, so it runs on the ticket STORE WRITE path — on ordinary `rebar comment` / `rebar create` calls, with no gate invocation and nothing in any verdict to reveal it.

## The two configurations, and why both are needed

* classes on Bedrock, `cfg.model` left bare-anthropic → PRE-FIX, all four sites above show `anthropic`: they
  bypass the class config. This is the defect.
* classes AND `cfg.model` on Bedrock → 15 calls, 0 on anthropic: nothing is HARDCODED past config.

The second configuration passes even with this bug unfixed, because a bypassing call inherits `cfg.model`. Any regression test must therefore pin the FIRST configuration, or it proves nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] with a model-class table configured to values that DIFFER from `cfg.model`, no hand-built
      SUB-CALL in review-plan, review-code or verify-completion resolves to `cfg.model` — verified
      IN-SESSION by `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`, which configures exactly such a
      table (the only configuration in which "honoured the class" and "fell through to cfg.model"
      are distinguishable strings — with no table configured both resolve to the same default and
      the observation carries no information) and asserts, per site, the model that reaches the
      runner. The two TOP-LEVEL one-call ops (`operations.py::review_ticket`,
      `spec_scan.py::_scan_epics_inner`) are EXCLUDED by design and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN`. Reframed from "asserted from a live run's usage log": the property is
      a durable invariant of the code, so it belongs in a test that fails the day a new bypassing
      sub-call is written, not in a one-off credentialed run that cannot be re-checked.
- [ ] each of the THREE hand-built sub-call sites selects its model from the class
      vocabulary, and the class chosen for each is stated in the code with its reason rather
      than left implicit: `enrich.py` (ticket-digest) -> trivial, `overlap/judge.py`
      (overlap-judge) -> standard, `code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty`
      (code-novelty) -> standard. The fourth site originally in scope,
      `operations.py::review_ticket`, is DELIBERATELY left on `cfg.model` and registered in
      `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` with that reason: it is a top-level op's single LLM call, so
      there are no passes to differentiate and the operator's configured model is the right
      knob. Narrowed from "four sites" after the operator decision that one-call top-level
      ops keep `cfg.model`; the code was already correct and the criterion was stale.
- [ ] `code-novelty`'s choice is consistent with plan-review's novelty sub-call, or the difference is
      documented as deliberate at both sites — `score_code_novelty`'s docstring currently claims it
      "mirrors" `_score_floor_novelty`, which uses `_verifier_cfg`, and that parity does not hold
- [ ] a test fails if ANY hand-built sub-call inherits `cfg.model` while a class table is configured
      — the general defect, so a future hand-built sub-call cannot silently reintroduce it. A test
      that enumerates today's four sites by name does NOT satisfy this
- [ ] the `overlap-judge` test constructs its trigger deliberately: `wire.py:overlap_findings` runs
      the judge only when BM25F retrieval returns candidates (`if not candidates: return []`, with
      the query's own graph excluded), so a test that merely runs a gate and hopes the judge fires
      will silently pass while testing nothing — both probes during the investigation hit exactly
      that and produced zero judge calls
- [ ] `ticket-digest`'s fix holds on the STORE WRITE path, not only inside a gate run
- [ ] fail-safe behaviour is preserved at every site: the novelty signal must still degrade to
      "keep more findings", and the overlap step must remain advisory and never block a review

## Not in scope

Sibling `03b0` (a configured Bedrock provider is dropped for colon-bearing model ids) is a different seam — that one breaks the configuration before it is read; this one ignores it after.
baseline.summary: Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic (4 sites; overlap-judge is 18 of 23 plan-review calls)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`inbound_probe.py` is wholly Jira-specific code living in the backend-neutral core: it builds
the Jira REST URL shape (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?fields=status,resolution`), sends a
basic-auth GET, resolves `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_USER`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN` via
`adapters.jira.acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings()` (`inbound_probe.py:65-77`), and
classifies by Jira status names (`RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = {"Resolved","Done","Cancelled"}`).
It is called from `run_differs.py:369`, and its result vocabulary is consumed *neutrally* by
`reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe` (`reconcile_helpers.py:291-355`). A second backend
would need an entirely different probe, but there is no seam. Epic bbf1 AC3 requires zero
`adapters.jira` imports in core.

## Approach

Split vocabulary from vendor mechanics:

- The neutral vocabulary — `ProbeBranch` (4 branches), `ProbeResult`, `ProbeConfigError` —
  stays in root `inbound_probe.py`. The file must remain at the package root: it is
  location-pinned (ADR 0035 context list) and loaded by filename at
  `reconcile_helpers.py:317` (`_load("inbound_probe", "inbound_probe.py")`).
- The Jira mechanics (URL construction, basic-auth GET, GET-only invariant, status-name
  classification, JIRA_* env resolution) move to a new `adapters/jira/probe.py`.
- A new `@runtime_checkable` capability Protocol `SupportsAbsenceProbe` in `_backend.py` with
  `probe_remote(remote_id: str) -> Any` (return documented as `inbound_probe.ProbeResult`;
  `_backend.py` stays a pure stdlib+typing interface module, consistent with its existing
  loosely-typed `dict[str, Any]` style, so it does not import the vocabulary module).
  `JiraBackend` implements it by delegating to `adapters/jira/probe.py`.
- `run_differs.py:369` routes through the backend: `isinstance(backend, SupportsAbsenceProbe)`
  guarded, matching the existing capability pattern (`SupportsLinks`/`SupportsComments`/
  `SupportsIncremental` in `_backend.py`). Wiring: today the backend is loaded at
  `run_differs.py:234` — AFTER the probe dispatch call at `:230` — so the
  `_load_reconcile_backend()` call (`run_differs.py:62-75`, a pure registry/config load with
  no remote side effects) is hoisted above the probe dispatch, and the backend object is
  passed into `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` as a new `backend` parameter, replacing
  that function's direct `probe_mod.probe(...)` call at `:369`. The later load site reuses
  the already-loaded instance. A backend without the capability yields
  `ProbeResult(UNREACHABLE)` — the conservative "do not classify, leave for retry" branch
  that `route_inbound_probe` already handles (`reconcile_helpers.py:351`).
- Extend the AST neutrality gate to assert zero `adapters.jira` imports in
  `inbound_probe.py`.

Rejected alternative: injecting url/user/token through scalar port accessors and keeping the
GET + classification in core — that leaves the vendor REST URL shape and Jira status-name
classification in neutral code, so a second backend still could not drop in; the port must
own the whole probe as a capability.

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (SupportsAbsenceProbe capability)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_probe.py (reduced to neutral vocabulary)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/probe.py (new: Jira GET + classification)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement probe_remote)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py (capability-guarded routing at the probe call site)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py (NEW adapter classification tests; the old test_inbound_probe.py is DELETED, its classification coverage migrated here)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py (new: the capability-routing tests — backend-with-capability runtime proof, capability-lacking UNREACHABLE degradation)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (AST gate extended to inbound_probe.py)

## Testing

- Happy path: 200 + resolved status → PRESENT_RESOLVED; 200 + other status →
  PRESENT_FILTERED (now exercised against `adapters/jira/probe.py`).
- Failure/edge: 404/410/403 → ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED; 5xx/401/timeout/URLError → UNREACHABLE;
  missing JIRA_* env → ProbeConfigError naming the missing vars; GET-only invariant asserted
  in the adapter.
- Capability routing (new file
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py`): with a FakeBackend
  implementing SupportsAbsenceProbe, run_differs uses the backend's probe (runtime proof);
  with a FakeBackend lacking it, the mutation is classified UNREACHABLE and left for retry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inbound_probe.py` contains NO `adapters.jira` import and no vendor REST code (URL
      shape, auth, status-name classification all live under `adapters/jira/probe.py`) —
      verified by the extended AST case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` plus code review.
- [ ] `run_differs` reaches the probe only through `SupportsAbsenceProbe`; a
      capability-lacking backend degrades to UNREACHABLE — verified by the routing tests in
      Testing.
- [ ] Probe classification behavior is byte-identical for Jira (all branches) — verified by
      the migrated probe tests.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 927 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Vendor absence probe behind a SupportsAbsenceProbe capability (relocate Jira REST probe into adapters/jira/)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`rebar link <a> <b> depends_on` can silently record a different edge than the one requested, and can produce an edge in which a ticket blocks its own subtree. Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 hit this while wiring epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864's dependency graph: an epic ended up `depends_on` its own child, the requested child-level dependency was never recorded at all, and the operator had to retype children and hand-unlink the bad edge. Self-blocking edges distort `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade, so parallel agents are handed a wrong work order.

The cause is a policy defect rather than a coding slip. `resolve_hierarchy_link` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98`) decides "comparable level" for blocking links from the ticket's TYPE TIER (`_TYPE_TIER`, `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:26`) instead of from its position in the parent hierarchy. Bug jira-reb-1582 names the correct rule directly: comparability is structural, and any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency. This story supersedes both bugs and replaces the policy.

## Approach

Replace type-tier comparability with structural (nearest-common-ancestor) comparability; add a resolved-pair invariant that makes ancestor-blocking edges unrepresentable regardless of how the edge was produced; then detect and repair the edges already written under the old rule.

Rejected alternative — keep the type tiers and special-case the failing shape by clamping promotion below the nearest common ancestor. That removes 1803's specific symptom but leaves comparability keyed on a ticket's *type*, so a task and a story that are genuine siblings still could not hold a direct dependency, and re-typing a ticket would silently rewrite the meaning of the dependency graph. jira-reb-1582 asks for the rule itself to change; patching the fallback at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:93` would leave the store's semantics wrong in the same way.

Rejected alternative — reject cross-subtree blocking links with an error instead of escalating them. Honest, but it breaks every caller relying on auto-escalation today, including the `link` MCP tool and the reconciler's inbound apply path (`rebar.link` at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`). Escalation is retained, and its existing machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) is kept unchanged. Note it is NOT uniformly visible: `add_dependency` prints it to stdout, which the CLI surfaces, but the library facade `rebar.link()` calls `composer.link_core(..., quiet=True)` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615`), and `quiet` redirects stdout/stderr into a `StringIO` sink (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:628`) — so library and MCP callers have the record DISCARDED and see a silent substitution. That predates this story and is not changed by it, but it is the same silence bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 complained about, still present on the MCP path; recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics rather than fixed here.

## Success Criteria

- The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the parent hierarchy alone; `_TYPE_TIER` no longer participates in that decision.
- No blocking edge can exist between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant, by any path into the resolver.
- Blocking edges already written under the type-tier rule are detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass.
- The escalation contract callers depend on — auto-escalate a cross-subtree link, emit the redirect record — is unchanged.

## Decomposition

Two children, in dependency order:

1. **Structural comparability and the ancestor invariant** (leaf) — rewrites the resolver in `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` and moves the redundancy guard in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` onto the resolved pair. This is the fix for both superseded bugs.
2. **`doctor` detection and repair** (leaf, shipped as the first check of `rebar doctor`) — a store-wide scan plus one-shot repair for edges written under the old rule. It declares `depends_on` child 1, because the repair re-resolves each existing edge through the new resolver and cannot be written before those semantics are final.

The split follows the deliverable seam: child 1 changes what a new link means, child 2 fixes data already on disk. Each lands as one reviewable change. Neither is large enough to split further, and combining them would put a store-wide data rewrite in the same change as the semantics that rewrite depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The repro from bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 (a task and a story that are both direct children of one epic) records the requested task-to-story edge unchanged and produces no epic-to-child edge; verified by the regression test added in child 1, run against the store fixture.
- [ ] The worked example from bug jira-reb-1582 resolves as that ticket specifies — Task D under Story C escalates to Story C when linked to Task B, while Task B to Story C records directly; verified by the regression test added in child 1.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar doctor` against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling; verified by listing each remaining finding's BLOCKED side (the source for `depends_on`, the target for `blocks`) and attesting on this ticket that every one is `closed`, since a closed blocked-side can never appear in `ready` or `next-batch`. Attested rather than asserted in-repo because it is a statement about live tracker state at a point in time, and the pre-repair count cannot be reconstructed from the post-repair store.
- [ ] Both children are closed, each with its Gerrit change at `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`; verified by the change status in Gerrit before each close.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/` all pass; verified by running them in the worktree.
baseline.summary: Resolve blocking-link comparability structurally, forbid ancestor self-blocks, and repair existing edges

baseline.description:
CI drift gate: every `external: true` volume declared in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` must be provisioned by `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh`, enforced in `make config-check` (already wired into test.yml AND gerrit-verify.yaml), so a compose-file edit that adds an external volume without a matching provisioning change can never reach `main`. Shift-left gate for incident 2731 (commit 10837ca88 added `gerrit_reviewbot_tickets: external: true` without updating compose-up.sh; every `compose up` then failed "external volume not found" for 41h).

## Dependencies / rollout
Gated on bug e991-e347-3444-427c (compose-up.sh provisioning fix) landing FIRST (declared `depends_on` edge): until that fix lands, this check correctly reports the live drift and would fail CI on main. Rollout = land as a stacked Gerrit change directly on top of e991's commit; both changes pass the Verified gate on the stacked tree, and submit order (bottom-first) guarantees main is never in a state where the gate fails.

## What (mechanism — single source of truth)
- `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh`: hoist the currently-duplicated hardcoded subdir list into ONE top-level variable (`SITE_SUBDIRS="git index cache db etc logs plugins reviewbot reviewbot-tickets"` — the 8 existing entries plus the missing one e991 adds), with volume-name derivation (`gerrit_` + subdir with `-` → `_`) in one shared helper function. The two provisioning loops AND the new `--print-volumes` mode all iterate that same variable through that same helper — there is no second copy of the list or of the derivation to drift.
- `--print-volumes` mode: when `${1:-} == --print-volumes` (defaulted access — the script runs under `set -u`, so a bare `$1` would abort the normal zero-arg boot path), print the derived external volume names (one per line) and `exit 0`. The branch is placed immediately after the variable/helper definitions and BEFORE any side-effecting section (dnf/systemctl/docker/fetch-secrets), so it is side-effect-free by construction.
- `infra/scripts/config-check.sh` check 5: extract `external: true` volume names from docker-compose.yml with `python3` + `yaml.safe_load` (the same interpreter+library dependency check 3 already uses — no grep/awk heuristics over multi-line YAML). Run `compose-up.sh --print-volumes` capturing output AND exit code; a non-zero exit or empty output is itself a FAIL ("could not enumerate provisioned volumes") — never treated as an empty provisioned set. Fail naming each missing volume and pointing at compose-up.sh as the fix site.
- Self-test (pattern-regression guard) embedded in check 5: run the same extraction+comparison against an inline synthetic compose snippet declaring `gerrit_notprovisioned: external: true`; assert the check DETECTS it (non-zero, message contains the volume name and `compose-up.sh`). A silent false-negative regression of the extraction logic fails CI.
- The `--print-volumes` contract is documented in both script headers (compose-up.sh: "consumed by config-check.sh check 5"; config-check.sh: "requires compose-up.sh --print-volumes").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 (red / self-test): the embedded synthetic fixture with `gerrit_notprovisioned` makes the drift check exit non-zero with a message naming `gerrit_notprovisioned` and containing `compose-up.sh` — proven automatically on every `make config-check` run.
- [ ] AC2 (green, in-session): `make config-check` exits 0 on this change's tree (stacked on e991, so `gerrit_reviewbot_tickets` is provisioned) — proven by running `make config-check` in the worktree before push and by the Verified vote on the stacked change.
- [ ] AC3 (no side effects, deterministic): running `bash infra/scripts/compose-up.sh --print-volumes` with `PATH` pointing at stub `docker`/`dnf`/`systemctl` executables that each write a canary file prints the expected volume list (including `gerrit_reviewbot_tickets`), exits 0, and leaves NO canary file — proving no side-effecting binary was invoked. Proving command recorded in verify_commands.
- [ ] AC4 (enumeration failure is loud, automated): check 5 embeds a second self-test that runs the same enumeration helper against a nonexistent script path and asserts it reports "could not enumerate provisioned volumes" (non-zero) rather than passing on an empty set — proven automatically on every `make config-check` run, same as AC1.


## Alternative considered (and why rejected)
Parsing compose-up.sh's provisioning loop textually from config-check.sh (no new mode) was rejected: a grep/awk heuristic over bash silently drifts out of sync with the script's format (the same failure class this gate exists to prevent). `--print-volumes` executes the real list through the real derivation helper, so the check can only report what the script would actually do. Single consumer is acceptable: the mode is 4 lines and sits beside the data it exposes.
- [ ] AC5 (contract documented): both script headers document the `--print-volumes` contract (compose-up.sh: "consumed by config-check.sh check 5"; config-check.sh: "requires compose-up.sh --print-volumes") — proven by grep in the change diff.
baseline.summary: CI drift gate: every external volume in docker-compose.yml must be provisioned by compose-up.sh

# `_llm_float` is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars

## Context / Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` generates `docs/env-vars.md` from env-var reads under `src/rebar`, and a CI drift gate fails the build when the committed doc disagrees (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:314`). The generator recognises a read only when the callee is a KNOWN helper AND the name argument is a STRING LITERAL (`gen_env_registry.py:117-124`); `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` at `:37-47` registers `"_llm_str": (2, "")` and `"_llm_int": (2, "")`.

**`_llm_float` is NOT registered.** So every env var read through it is silently absent from the generated registry. MEASURED by running the generator: `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE` (`llm/config.py:651`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ` (`:692`), `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` (`:699`) and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` (`:720`) are all real, settable, operator-facing knobs and NONE appears in `docs/env-vars.md`.

This is exactly the bug class the registry exists to prevent, and the gate is currently GREEN while incomplete — a clean `--check` is therefore not evidence of completeness. `_llm_float` is defined at `llm/config.py:459-476` alongside `_llm_str` (`:426-436`) and `_llm_int` (`:439-456`); the omission is an oversight, not a decision.

## Approach
Add `"_llm_float": (2, "")` to `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` and regenerate `docs/env-vars.md`.

Land this BEFORE any structural change to `config.py`, so the derived-doc diff caused by fixing the scanner is not tangled with the diff caused by moving code. That keeps both changes reviewable.

**Also close the hole that let this hide:** the existing test `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` asserts one specific var is statically visible to the generator. Generalize the idea — assert that the helper registry covers every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `llm/config.py`, so adding a fifth resolver without registering it fails a test rather than silently dropping knobs from the docs.

## Scope
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` — one entry in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `tests/unit/` — the completeness assertion.

## Testing
- a test asserts each of the four named vars appears in the generated registry (fails today).
- a test asserts every `_llm_*` helper defined in `llm/config.py` is present in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`,
  so the next resolver cannot be added unregistered.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MAX_DOC_FREQ`,
      `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_MIN_SHOULD_MATCH` and `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_CONF_THRESHOLD` are all present in
      the generated env registry. This criterion FAILS against the current implementation
- [ ] a test asserts every `_llm_*` resolver defined in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is registered in
      `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`, so an unregistered future resolver is caught
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean and `docs/env-vars.md` is committed
      as generated output
baseline.summary: _llm_float is invisible to the env-var registry scanner: 4 undocumented env vars
