## Context / Problem
Source comments carry commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot: 8 of 18 cited SHAs in the tree are ALREADY unresolvable (Gerrit rebase-on-submit guarantees pre-land SHA death), and run IDs die with retention windows. Policy: source is for current state + concise rationale; the ticket system owns historical detail. The detector is NET-NEW code (the prototype that produced the corpus numbers ran in the planning session and was not committed; its measured results — 0 FPs, 15 violating sites, 47 compliant blocks on the then-current tree — are recorded here as design evidence, and the corpus is re-derived by running the new detector at the implementation worktree's HEAD, which is authoritative; the ticket comment records census drift to 16 sites already).

## Approach
(1) Remediate every detector hit at HEAD (17 pinned above as-of-plan: the original 15 census sites, of which 2 were later found under src/ in the PR-375 bucket, plus 3 post-plan RUN-id sites minus overlap) — each maps to a specific replacement already adjudicated: delete.py:188 drop dead-SHA mechanism sentence; classify.py:310 + test_frozen_census.py:79 cite epic 3006-e198; reconcile.py:588 + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_commit_binding_store_failure.py:10 (module docstring's 'cf93b2b7ad failure class') describe the failure class in behavioral terms (story findable via git log -S); test_ci_actionlint_install.py cite bug 4e99-b2ae; test_plan_review_explain.py:308 (docstring narrates 'the class of bug `62933ff62` fixed for plan-review deep-links' — a raw dead SHA) drop the SHA and cite bug c7e3-dd16; test_execution_mode_dispatch.py cite 454a-9266; test_inbound_differ_field_contract.py point at the live CONTRACT block + story a130-2b7c; 7 PR-#375 sites keep 'PR #375 review' and drop raw thread ids (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py:63/69/210/310/451 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/typed_dispatch.py:128 + src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py:233); test_at_most_one_invariant.py:199 drop e04e0b289c; 3 RUN-id sites from the post-plan J11/5200 work (tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:163/1638-context + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_assignee_oracle_discriminates_5200.py:20-context, runs 30721408463/30763838558) get the same treatment — narrative to a ticket, cite the ticket. Line numbers are as-of-plan pins; the re-run detector census at HEAD is the authoritative remediation list and may add/retire sites (same adjudicated replacement rules apply). (2) CI guard (detector is NET-NEW per Context; prior art/reuse: it follows the repo's scripts/check_*.py guard convention — check()/main() shape, wired as a named step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml like check_verify_gate_parity.py — landing as scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py): block-level scan (comment blocks + AST docstrings); rot-prone = SHA-like hex >=7 with digits+letters (denylist ed25519/sha256 etc), run/job/thread id >=8 digits after keyword, date+evidence-verb — defined as: a date token (YYYY-MM-DD or 'Month DD, YYYY') in the same block as a past-tense incident verb from the ENUMERATED set {failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked} (the block narrates a dated incident); 'surfaced' is deliberately EXCLUDED from the verb set — the prototype's 'bug surfaced' FP introduces current-state explanation, not an incident date, and must not trigger. Acceptor interaction: triggers are evaluated first, then a triggered block is ACCEPTED iff it cites a qualifying id — the gotcha cases must not trigger at all (they never reach the acceptor); ACCEPTED when the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug/rec/ADR id — hex-grouped (4x4 like 3006-e198-…) or word-triple alias (three lowercase hyphen-joined dictionary words, e.g. robe-creek-zealot, the store's human alias form) — pointing history at the ticket system is the sanctioned pattern; escape hatch 'context: external' for vendor-pinned refs (changelogs, upstream issue SHAs). Self-exclusion (sibling-guard convention): the detector's own unit-test module (tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py, whose fixtures MUST contain live rot-prone tokens as RED/gotcha cases) is excluded from the tree scan by an EXCLUDED_FILES tuple in the script — the same mechanism check_criteria_vocabulary.py uses (scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:38); fixtures live only in that one excluded module, so 'zero suppressions' means zero IN-TREE escape-hatch uses, with the single structural exclusion visible at the top of the script.

## Scope
- the detector-hit sites listed above (src/ + tests/; authoritative list = detector re-run at HEAD)
- scripts/ or CI lint module implementing the detector + workflow wiring
- short policy note in CONTRIBUTING.md or docs (source=current state, tickets=history)

## Testing
Detector unit tests re-derived at HEAD (prototype-measured shape: ~15-17 pre-fix sites RED, ~47 compliant blocks green — exact counts pinned when the detector lands), the acceptor-arm gotchas ('bug surfaced', 'ticket dirs' must NOT accept; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases MUST accept), escape hatch honored. Post-remediation tree scans clean.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] All detector-hit sites at HEAD remediated, each in one of three sanctioned forms: (a) cites a ticket/epic/story/bug id that RESOLVES in the ticket system (spot-check via rebar show), (b) drops the rot-prone token leaving durable current-state prose (PR-#375 bucket keeps 'PR #375 review', drops raw thread ids), or (c) replaces a SHA narrative with a behavioral description findable via git log -S (the test_commit_binding_store_failure.py form).
- [x] CI guard fails on reintroduced rot-prone refs, passes the current remediated tree with zero suppressions.
- [x] Escape hatch documented; policy note landed.
- [x] Detector unit tests cover the FP gotchas measured in the planning prototype ('bug surfaced'/'ticket dirs' NOT accepted; grouped 4x4 ids and word-triple aliases accepted; escape hatch honored).
baseline.summary: Comment hygiene: remediate rot-prone historical refs in code + CI guard

baseline.description:
## Why

Two work tickets (115b, 8c4f) burned close-gate cycles: their acceptance
criteria had "done" evidence that lives OUTSIDE the codebase (live-store fsck
surgery, phantom-dir deletion, changes landed through Gerrit) but were NOT tagged
`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043), so the completion verifier failed looking for
code proof until the tag was added retroactively. A cheap DETERMINISTIC pass-1
lint that surfaces this at PLAN time — before claim — removes the whole
round-trip. Rule-based lexicon checks are the proven high-recall/cheap tier for
requirement-defect shape (AQUSA-grade prior art); this project already ships two
such lexicon lints in the same P6/P7 family (`p6_ac_quality`'s vague-term +
verify-command lint at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:686`, and
`p7_destructive` at `:762`), so this is a well-precedented extension, not a new
mechanism.

## What

Add an ADVISORY, prompt-less DETERMINISTIC lint (ADR-0016 `exec: DET`, the P6/AC
family) that flags AC checklist items whose text carries operational-evidence
markers (deploy / prod / live-run / IaC-apply / cloud-state / merge-gate /
human-action / drill / store-surgery / recorded-attestation) but which are NOT
tagged `[operator-attested]`. It NEVER blocks (advisory coaching only).

### Design decisions (grounded against the code)

- **It EXTENDS `p6_ac_quality`; it does NOT add a `P10` and does NOT touch
  `criteria_routing.json`.** The static DET floor (`DET_CHECKS`,
  `det_floor.py:880`) is hardcoded P1–P9 and enumerated in
  `registry.py:78 CANONICAL_DET`; DET checks are NOT routed through
  `criteria_routing.json`. `registry.validate_packaged_routing()`
  (`registry.py:445-446`) flags any routing key not in `CANONICAL_LLM` as an
  ORPHAN and fails CI, so a packaged DET routing entry is impossible without a
  larger, out-of-scope change. And `.rebar/`-overlay `exec:DET` criteria run
  through `det_invariants.run_project_det_checks` (`det_invariants.py:207`),
  which scans CODE with a grounding detector (`engine_b`) — structurally wrong
  for an AC-TEXT lexicon. The existing regression test
  `tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py:327` already pins "the lint EXTENDS p6 …
  DET_CHECKS stays exactly P1-P9", exactly matching how the verify-command lint
  (G-3a) was folded into p6. So the correct home is `p6_ac_quality`, keeping
  `DET_CHECKS` at 9 and `CANONICAL_DET` unchanged. The task's suggestion of a
  `criteria_routing.json` entry is refuted by the code and is deliberately NOT
  done; `p6_ac_quality` already ships in the packaged registry (no config flag),
  satisfying "advisory in packaged registry".

- **Single-source the tag matcher.** The canonical `[operator-attested]` matcher
  is `workflow_ops._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE` (`workflow_ops.py:61`), consumed by
  the completion-verifier enrichment path (`workflow_ops.py:80
  enrich_operator_attested`, `passes.py:769`). `det_floor` imports nothing from
  `workflow_ops`, and `workflow_ops` imports `det_floor` lazily
  (`workflow_ops.py:135`), so `det_floor` will OWN the regex as
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `workflow_ops` will import it — no import cycle,
  one source of truth, so the lint and the verifier agree on "tagged" by
  construction (guarded by a unit test).

- **Precision-first (advisory posture).** An advisory lint must not nag, so the
  lexicon is tuned for precision with a codebase-verifiable SUPPRESSION co-signal
  (drop items that name an in-repo proving command / test / doc / config-file
  deliverable, or carry a "… — landed on main" trailer) and a NEGATION guard
  ("no live", "read-only provisioning"). Recall is a reported figure, not a gate.

### Self-gate (DETERMINISTIC — no LLM anywhere)

Run the locked lexicon over the frozen historical AC corpus committed under
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/`. The corpus is the AC checklist items
of the 556 E1 outcome-corpus tickets that resolve in the store
(`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl` → 3091 AC items,
31 already tagged `[operator-attested]`). Ground-truth for precision is a frozen
per-item TP/FP adjudication of the full flagged set (a census ≥ the required
50-item sample); recall is measured against the 31 tagged items with their tag
stripped. Measured on this corpus: flag rate 2.07% (≤5%), recall 61% (19/31),
precision ~92% (census of 64 flagged items, 6 adjudicated false-positive), and
both known cases (115b, 8c4f) fire. NO LLM call runs in the eval or the lint.

### Landing order (pre-registration, git-ancestry)

Landed as a 2-commit Gerrit stack so the eval is committed BEFORE the lint is
active: commit 1 adds the frozen corpus + the harness + the committed `eval.json`
result and the detector helper `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps()` in `det_floor.py`
in DORMANT form (defined, used only by the harness, not yet called by
`p6_ac_quality`); commit 2 wires the helper into `p6_ac_quality` (activation),
adds the unit tests + the `workflow_ops` single-source import, and documents the
lint in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — the `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`,
  the operational-evidence lexicon (marker families + suppression + negation),
  the pure helper `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps(text) -> list[(ac_line, markers)]`,
  and its wiring into `p6_ac_quality` (append one advisory coaching issue per
  gap; never changes P6's non-blocking status).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` — import
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_floor` (drop the local duplicate).
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/operator_attested_eval.py` — the
  deterministic eval harness (imports the shipped helper; runs over the frozen
  corpus; computes flag rate / recall / known-case firing; loads frozen precision
  adjudications; asserts the gate).
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_ac_corpus.jsonl` —
  the frozen AC corpus.
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json` — the
  committed eval result (precision/recall/flag-rate/known-cases + adjudications +
  PASS verdict).
- `tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py` — table-driven unit tests over
  labeled AC strings (115b/8c4f fixtures fire; negative controls do not;
  already-tagged items do not; agreement with `workflow_ops`).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — document the lint (advisory P6-family DET,
  ADR-0016/0043).

## Out of scope

- Any `criteria_routing.json` change (refuted by the code, see above).
- A new `P10` DET check or any change to `CANONICAL_DET` / `DET_CHECKS`
  cardinality.
- Blocking posture, LLM rubric, or an `.rebar/` overlay entry.
- Any human-adjudicated gold set (parked as idea e59d).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The deterministic lexicon eval is committed under
  `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json` BEFORE the
  lint is activated (its commit is a git ancestor of the p6 activation commit),
  recording sampled precision ≥ 70% over a ≥ 50-item flagged sample AND overall
  flag rate ≤ 5% over the frozen corpus, plus the recall figure. Proof:
  `python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_eval.json')); assert d['precision']['precision_pct']>=70 and d['precision']['sample_size']>=50 and d['flag_rate_pct']<=5.0 and d['gate']['verdict']=='PASS', d"`
  and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <eval-commit> <activation-commit>` exits 0.
  (If the eval had failed the thresholds, the story closes deferred with the
  failing result recorded instead.)
- [ ] Both known cases fire on their historical (tag-stripped) AC text, pinned as
  unit-test fixtures, and an already-tagged item does NOT fire. Proof:
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py -q` passes,
  including `test_known_case_115b_fires`, `test_known_case_8c4f_fires`, and
  `test_tagged_item_not_flagged`.
- [ ] The lint ships ADVISORY and prompt-less in the packaged floor: it extends
  `p6_ac_quality` (which never blocks), `DET_CHECKS` stays exactly 9 and
  `CANONICAL_DET` is unchanged, and no `criteria_routing.json` entry is added.
  Proof: `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import DET_CHECKS; assert len(DET_CHECKS)==9"`;
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review import registry,det_floor; assert list(registry.CANONICAL_DET)==['P1','P2','P3','P4','P5','P6','P7','P8','P9']; assert registry.validate_packaged_routing()==[]"`;
  and a unit test asserting a `p6_ac_quality` result on an untagged operational
  AC has `status=='fail'` with `blocking is False`.
- [ ] The lint and the completion-verifier agree on "tagged": `det_floor` owns
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` and `workflow_ops` imports it. Proof:
  `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE as a; from rebar.llm.plan_review.workflow_ops import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE as b; assert a is b"`
  and a unit test asserting `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps` never flags a line that
  `workflow_ops.operator_attested_ac_texts` recognizes as tagged.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the new advisory P6-family DET lint

content.text: ## Summary

In a non-interactive environment, rebar cannot bootstrap its tracker even when `origin/tickets` already exists. Any read fails with: `Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'rebar init' first (auto-init requires an interactive terminal).` There is no documented non-interactive path to attach an existing `origin/tickets` to a fresh checkout. This makes rebar unusable out-of-the-box for the automated/agent/CI consumers it targets.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Fresh clone (no `.tickets-tracker/`), with `origin/tickets` present on the remote.
2. Call a read: `sys.argv=['rebar','search','plan review']; main()`.
- **Actual:** `Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'rebar init' first (auto-init requires an interactive terminal).`
- **Expected:** rebar attaches to the existing `origin/tickets` (or a non-interactive `init` exists) and the read succeeds with no TTY.
3. Workaround required: `git worktree add .tickets-tracker -B tickets origin/tickets` (and then seeding `.env-id` — see the related init-gate bug).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A non-interactive bootstrap exists (e.g. `rebar init --yes` / `--non-interactive`, or auto-attach to an existing `origin/tickets`) that works with no interactive terminal.
- [ ] Attaching to an existing `origin/tickets` does not require manual `git worktree` + `.env-id` steps.
- [ ] Documented for CI/agent environments.
## Environment

- **rebar:** NOT pip-installed (`pip show nava-rebar` -> "Package(s) not found"; `import rebar` fails without `PYTHONPATH`); `rebar.__version__` = `0+unknown`. Source checkout: branch `claude/llm-code-review-commits-m0flss`, HEAD `91fe853`.

- **How rebar was called** (not on PATH): `PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from rebar.cli import main; import sys; sys.argv=['rebar', <args>]; main()"`, run from `/home/user/rebar`, with `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR="$PWD/.tickets-tracker"`.
- **Python:** 3.11.15 (`/usr/local/bin/python`).
- **OS/kernel:** Linux 6.18.5 x86_64.
- **Shell:** `/bin/bash` (GNU bash 5.2.21(1)-release).

- **Context:** non-interactive container (Claude Code on the web); fresh clone; `origin/tickets` present but no local `.tickets-tracker` initially (created manually via `git worktree add .tickets-tracker -B tickets origin/tickets`).

baseline.summary: rebar cannot bootstrap a tracker non-interactively even when origin/tickets exists (auto-init requires interactive terminal)

baseline.description:
## Why
Every gate row and all post-ship dogfooding in this epic needs standing outcome
instrumentation: today nothing routinely ties plan-review verdicts to downstream outcomes
(post-claim edits, reopens, force-closes, verifier FAILs), so false-positive drift stays
invisible until it burns author trust (the Tricorder <10% blocking-FP cliff). E1 froze the
per-ticket **outcome corpus** (`runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl`, 628 rows) and the miner that
produces it; this ticket turns that one-shot artifact into a **re-runnable gate-eval job** that
classifies each reviewed ticket, emits trailing per-criterion FP-proxy metrics, and documents
the alarm/demotion playbook.

## What
Commit a re-runnable **gate-eval instrumentation job** at
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py`.

**Corpus acquisition (subprocess, not import).** The job refreshes the outcome corpus by
invoking `mine_outcome_corpus.py` **as a subprocess** (`python <harnesses>/mine_outcome_corpus.py`,
which atomically writes `runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl`), then reads that JSONL. It does NOT
`import` and call `build_corpus()`, because that entry calls `sys.exit()` on floor-check failure
(`mine_outcome_corpus.py:381`), which would terminate the caller; and the miner lives in a
non-package `harnesses/` dir, so subprocess-by-path is also the clean invocation. A
`--no-refresh` flag skips regeneration and reads the committed corpus (offline / CI use). It
then reads each reviewed ticket's persisted `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars via
`rebar.llm.plan_review.sidecar.all_review_results`.

**Outcome classifier (deterministic; the honest finding is that the sidecar findings do NOT
carry the separating signal).** Investigation against the 8 §5.2 cases proved a classifier over
the sidecar findings *alone* reaches only **4/8** — the CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED cases (c8cc, f5df)
have finding profiles at or *below* the MISSED cases, because "caught-but-ignored" is a fact
about the author's **post-claim edit**, not about what the gate saw. The separating signal lives
in two outcome-corpus fields plus one sidecar-derived strength predicate. The classifier is a
first-match cascade, applied ONLY to tickets with `had_persisted_review` AND a post-claim signal
(`post_claim_edit_class != "none"` OR `review_round_count >= 2`); all others are **N/A**:

```
C1  post_claim_edit_class == "operator-attested-retag"  → CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED
C2  review_round_count >= 2                              → CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED
C3  has_strong_finding                                   → UNKNOWABLE
C4  else                                                 → MISSED
```
- `review_round_count` is the **git-walk outcome-corpus** count (true count), not the pruned
  on-disk sidecar count.
- **`has_strong_finding`** (the exact "substantive advisory" predicate, evaluated over the
  ticket's deduplicated round union — see Multi-round handling): ∃ a finding with
  `decision ∈ {"block","advisory"}` AND `priority >= 0.5` AND `severity ∈ {"critical","major"}`.
  The 0.5 floor is the codebase's own `RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY`
  (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:299`); the severity conjunct excludes
  high-priority-but-procedural (P6/P9) findings.

This **core** cascade reproduces the 8 frozen labels at **7/8** (only c8cc, a lone
`substantive-unclassified` case, misclassifies as MISSED). A `substantive-unclassified → CAUGHT`
rule would reach 8/8 but rests on that single case, so it is **deliberately excluded** as
overfitting and documented as such. The README states plainly that the classifier separates via
outcome-corpus fields + a sidecar strength predicate, NOT via sidecar findings alone (which
achieve only 4/8) — the load-bearing methodological finding.

**adverse post-claim edit** (used by both the classifier gate and the metrics below) is defined
once: `post_claim_edit_class ∈ {"plan-authored-post-claim", "ac-strengthened",
"substantive-unclassified"}` (the substantive classes; `operator-attested-retag` is handled by
C1; `cosmetic`/`none` are not adverse).

**Multi-round handling (load-bearing — `all_review_results` returns every retained round).**
`sidecar.all_review_results(ticket_id)` returns ALL retained review payloads (newest→oldest, up
to the 50/ticket cap), not just the latest. For each ticket the harness forms the **deduplicated
union** of findings across all retained rounds, keyed by
`(tuple(sorted(finding["criteria"])), finding["finding"])` — so a finding that persists across
rounds counts exactly **once** (no denominator inflation for high-round tickets) and a finding
cleared in a later round is still counted (no omission of earlier blocks). `has_strong_finding`
is `∃ a strong finding in this union` (consistent with the §5.2 investigation — 8c4f's strong
finding lived in its earlier BLOCK round, cleared by round 2), and every per-criterion metric
denominator below counts C's findings in this union.

**Per-criterion trailing metrics (FINDING-level, matching the parent epic's definition).** Over
the trailing window (see `--window`), joining each ticket's deduplicated finding union to its
outcome row by `ticket_id`, for each criterion C:
- **blocking_fp_proxy(C)** = (# of C's **blocking** findings whose ticket was subsequently
  adjudicated not-block-worthy) / (total # of C's blocking findings). The automatic proxy for
  "adjudicated not-block-worthy" is **`force_close OR reopen_count > 0`** (an explicit gate
  bypass, or a post-close reopen). The earlier `(no adverse post-claim edit)` disjunct is
  **removed**: blocking findings are remediated *pre-claim* in the review loop, so ~95% of
  tickets legitimately have `post_claim_edit_class == "none"`, and that disjunct would fire on
  nearly every honored block and mislabel it FP. This proxy is therefore a deliberately
  conservative **lower bound** (force-close can also happen for orthogonal operator-attestation
  reasons, ADR 0043), so the >10% alarm **triggers human review** of that criterion's recent
  blocks rather than an automatic demotion. Per-FINDING, matching the parent's "fraction of that
  criterion's blocking findings … subsequently adjudicated not-block-worthy."
- **advisory_application_rate(C)** = (# of C's **advisory** findings whose ticket later shows an
  adverse post-claim edit) / (total # of C's advisory findings).
- **rounds_per_ticket** = the `review_round_count` distribution over the window.
- **sample_counts(C)** = `{"blocking_findings": int, "advisory_findings": int, "tickets": int}` —
  the denominators (count of C's blocking findings, C's advisory findings, and distinct tickets
  touching C, over the deduplicated union in the window). Emitted with each criterion so a rate
  computed from a tiny sample is visible rather than hidden behind a bare fraction.

**Empty / degenerate input.** On the live store (628 reviewed tickets) the corpus is always
non-empty; defensively, if the window resolves to zero tickets `--emit` exits non-zero with a
message (rather than writing a trivial `{}`), a criterion with zero findings is omitted, and
`--verify-repro` fails loudly if any of the 8 frozen case ids cannot be resolved.

**`--window N`** bounds the corpus to the last `N` rows in the miner's deterministic emission
order (the corpus has no timestamp field; emission order is the stable proxy, documented as
such — a strictly chronological window is future work needing a timestamp). Default N=200.

**Alarm / demotion rule (documented playbook).** When a criterion's trailing
**blocking_fp_proxy exceeds 10%**, demote it from blocking to advisory via an ordinary
`criteria_routing.json` edit (`default_posture: "advisory"`). Precedent for demotion on FP
evidence: **T5e**, demoted to advisory in calibration-3 (task relishable-ammonitic-hoverfly).
(T3/T10 are a *different* precedent — criteria kept non-blocking from the start; never demoted —
so they are NOT cited as demotion precedent.) Dogfood monitoring, not a config flag; no
gate/source behaviour change.

## Scope
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py` — the job: a pure
  top-level `classify(post_claim_edit_class, review_round_count, has_strong_finding) -> str`
  (unit-testable), the `has_strong_finding` sidecar extractor, the finding-level metrics
  computation, and CLI flags `--verify-repro`, `--emit`, `--window N`, `--no-refresh`.
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/README.md` — classifier rules, the 4/8-vs-7/8 finding, the
  metric definitions + join key, cadence, and the metrics output path.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the alarm/demotion playbook (>10% blocking-FP rule, T5e
  precedent, operator response). The ONLY change outside `docs/experiments/`; documentation only.
- `tests/unit/test_gate_eval_classifier.py` — a golden test importing the pure `classify` and
  asserting the 8 frozen `(cls, rounds, strong) → label` tuples reproduce ≥6/8, plus a
  non-triviality assertion on a metrics fixture and a `--window` subset check.
- No change to `src/rebar/` behaviour — no gate or source behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `--verify-repro` recomputes the classifier over the 8 frozen cases (MISSED: dc58-af7b,
      db7b-c8fd, 5886-d028; CAUGHT-BUT-IGNORED: c8cc-68b8, f5df-0069, 115b-ceea, 8c4f-b81c;
      UNKNOWABLE: 3006-e198), prints the confusion table, and asserts **≥6/8 agreement** (exits
      non-zero below 6/8). Proving command:
      `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py --verify-repro`.
- [ ] `--emit` writes per-criterion metrics to
      `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/gate_eval_metrics.json` — a non-trivial object with
      ≥1 criterion whose `blocking_fp_proxy` and `advisory_application_rate` are **numeric**
      (a float in [0,1], not null) and whose `sample_counts` is a non-empty dict with a
      **positive total** (so the AC is NOT satisfiable by `{}`, all-null values, or all-zero
      sample counts). Proving command:
      `python docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/gate_eval_instrumentation.py --emit && python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/gate_eval_metrics.json'));assert d and any(isinstance(v.get('blocking_fp_proxy'),(int,float)) and isinstance(v.get('advisory_application_rate'),(int,float)) and isinstance(v.get('sample_counts'),dict) and sum(v['sample_counts'].values())>0 for v in d.values())"`.
- [ ] The pure `classify` reproduces ≥6/8 on the 8 frozen input tuples in a CI-collected test,
      and `--window N` yields a subset for smaller N. Proving command:
      `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gate_eval_classifier.py -q`.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` gains a new **"Blocking-FP-proxy demotion"** section
      documenting the >10% `blocking_fp_proxy` alarm rule, the operator demotion response, and the
      correct T5e precedent (not T3/T10, cited inside that section); the harnesses README
      documents the `sidecar-findings-alone` 4/8-vs-7/8 finding. Proving command (both sentinels
      are new content — neither pre-exists in its file, verified by `grep -c`):
      `grep -q "Blocking-FP-proxy demotion" docs/plan-review-gate.md && grep -q "sidecar-findings-alone" docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/README.md`.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; landed through Gerrit (evidence: the Gerrit change id, merge commit, and CI Verified vote recorded in a ticket comment).
baseline.summary: R7: standing gate-eval outcome instrumentation + dogfood FP monitoring

baseline.description:
## Why
Three sources disagree on the write-lock lifecycle:
- `docs/concurrency.md` I5 (lines ~107-117) still documents the retired **bash**
  `_flock_stage_commit` (`ticket-lib.sh:270`, FD 200) as the ACTIVE write path.
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (docstring lines 7-23) frames the fcntl+mkdir dual acquisition as
  a **migration window** that "flips `dual_window` to `False` permanently after the bash core
  is retired" — yet still defaults `dual_window=True` (`lock.py:281`).
- `tests/integration/test_store_concurrency.py` states the bash core is ALREADY retired and
  that the durable single-impl mechanism is the unified dual-leg lock where "the mkdir leg is
  always taken, which is exactly what closed the gap."

So the lock module says the mkdir leg is going away, while the test says it is the permanent
mechanism it relies on. A test cannot reliably enforce a contract the docs contradict.
VALIDATED.

## Decision: dual_window is a PERMANENT, intentional contract (not migration residue)
Chosen because it is the zero-behavioral-risk reconciliation AND it is what the surviving
code already assumes:
- The integration writer-storm gate explicitly depends on "the mkdir leg is always taken";
  the fcntl+mkdir pair is the durable descendant of the stiff-mop-lane gate, not scaffolding.
- The mkdir leg is the portable second window — atomic on POSIX where util-linux `flock` is
  absent (default macOS) — and underpins the foreign-host/shared-filesystem handling already
  coded in `_mkdir_lock_is_stale`. Removing it would weaken portable exclusion.
- Keeping `dual_window=True` changes NO production behavior; only the stale
  "migration-window / flips-to-False" narrative and the bash-era doc are corrected.

## What
1. `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` docstring: replace the "Tier D migration window / after bash
   retired `dual_window` flips to `False`" language with an intentional-permanent-contract
   note — fcntl (fast local) + mkdir (portable second window, atomic on POSIX / no-flock
   hosts) is the standing write-lock contract; `dual_window=True` is the permanent default,
   `dual_window=False` remains an fcntl-only escape hatch. No code/default change.
2. `docs/concurrency.md` I5: stop describing the retired bash `_flock_stage_commit`/FD 200 as
   the active path; describe the current Python unified fcntl+mkdir dual-window lock
   (`rebar._store.lock.write_lock` / `event_append`) as the permanent contract, mkdir as the
   portable leg on no-flock platforms.
3. Add an enforcing test (in `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py`, fast + deterministic)
   that pins the permanent contract behaviorally: holding the DEFAULT write lock creates BOTH
   the `.ticket-write.lock` fcntl file AND the `.ticket-write.lock.d` mkdir dir; with
   `dual_window=False` only the fcntl file is taken (no mkdir dir). Align the
   `test_store_concurrency.py` module docstring to the permanent framing (drop any
   migration-window wording).

## Scope
- `docs/concurrency.md`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` (docstring only), `tests/unit/
  test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` (new enforcing test), `tests/integration/
  test_store_concurrency.py` (docstring wording).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single, consistent lifecycle statement across the doc, the lock module, and the
      integration test: the fcntl+mkdir dual-window lock is the permanent write-lock contract.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` no longer describes the retired bash `_flock_stage_commit` path as
      the active write mechanism.
- [ ] The lock module's "migration window / flips to False" language is replaced with an
      intentional-permanent-contract note (default `dual_window=True` unchanged).
- [ ] A test enforces the contract: the default lock takes BOTH legs; `dual_window=False`
      takes only the fcntl leg.
- [ ] `make lint && make test` green.
baseline.summary: Settle the dual_window lock-portability lifecycle across docs, lock module, and tests

## Finding

`PlanContext` assembly (`orchestrator._assemble_context_uncached`) swallows child-enumeration and per-child-fetch failures with a bare `except Exception`, silently continuing with an empty/partial `children` list. Because `PlanContext.has_children` is `bool(self.children)`, a total enumeration failure also flips `has_children` to `False`, which makes container-scoped DET checks (confirmed: `det_floor.p5_task_dag`) return a trivial `pass` instead of reporting incompleteness — so a container whose hierarchy failed to load can still reach an unqualified clean PASS. This violates parent epic `6eca-183e-1cd2-4fb9` AC #4: "Plan review cannot produce an ordinary clean pass when the ticket hierarchy was loaded incompletely, unless the omitted context is demonstrably irrelevant."

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:173-187` (`_assemble_context_uncached`): `list_tickets(parent=canonical, ...)` wrapped in `try/except Exception` -> `listed = []` on total failure (line 173-178); per-child `show_ticket` wrapped similarly (line 184-187), falling back to the list summary row on partial failure. Neither path records that anything was lost.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:104-138` (`PlanContext.has_children` property, line 133-138): `return bool(self.children)`. `p5_task_dag` (line 362-368): `if not ctx.has_children: return DetResult("P5", "task-dag", "pass", coverage={"ran": True, "children": 0})` — confirms a wiped `children` list produces a silent P5 pass, not an incompleteness signal. `p8_reviewability`'s container pairing check (~line 598-604) is likewise skipped when `has_children` is `False`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`: `plan_review_precheck` (def at line 135) calls `orchestrator.assemble_context` at line 140, giving it the REAL `pctx` in scope; its only `finalize_verdict` call is at line 209, **inside `plan_review_precheck`** (not `plan_review_coach`), with `coverage={"det": det_cov, "llm_ran": False}` (line 213). `plan_review_coach` (def at line 503) builds a **new, minimal** `PlanContext(ticket_id=..., ticket_type=..., title="", description="")` at line 540-545 (no `children`/hierarchy data) and calls `finalize_verdict` at line 557, with `coverage` built at line 546-550 from `ctx.inputs.get("det_coverage")` (line 547) — i.e. call site 2 has no live `pctx` and must source everything from the precheck step's dict output.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:503-541` (`finalize_verdict`): computes `verdict` from `coverage.get(...)` flags only (`llm_unavailable` line ~527, `verify_failed` line ~529); it does **not** read any attribute off its `ctx: PlanContext` argument today — confirming `coverage` (not the `ctx` object) is the correct, established plumbing point for a new flag.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` has **three additional** `finalize_verdict` call sites beyond workflow_ops.py's two, none in the original plan:
  - `_recover_plan_review_coach_failure` (def line 298), `coverage` built lines 324-329 from `precheck.get("det_coverage")` (line 325) where `precheck = succeeded.get(STEP_PRECHECK)` (a **dict**, the recorded step output) — same shape as `plan_review_precheck`'s return value.
  - `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure` (def line 342), `coverage` built lines 381-389, identical `precheck.get("det_coverage")` pattern (line 382).
  - `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` (def line 402), `coverage` built lines 420-426 from `det_floor.det_coverage(det_results)` (line 421) where `det_results = det_floor.run_det_floor(ctx)` (line 412) and `ctx` here **is** the caller's real `PlanContext` (passed straight through from `produce_plan_review_verdict`'s own `ctx` param, lines 145-147/185-187) — so this site, unlike the other two, has direct access to the real `pctx.hierarchy_incomplete` and doesn't need dict-threading.
- `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_precheck_output.schema.json`: `"additionalProperties": false` (line 17) and `"required": [...]` (line 16) list exactly `run_llm, verdict, canonical_id, ticket_type, det_blocking, det_advisory, det_coverage` — no room for new fields as written. `det_coverage` itself is declared as `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}` (line 14) and IS in `required`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py:445-450`: `props = schema.get("properties")`, `literals = frozenset(props.keys())` — an output-contract ref-checker built directly from this schema's `properties`; an unlisted field name used in a `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<name> }}` ref would lint as UNKNOWN.
- Retry precedent: `_call_with_retry` genuinely exists, but at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:113-139` (the **Jira reconciler**, not a generic helper), retrying on `JiraAPIError`/`urllib.error.HTTPError` (429/5xx only, 4xx fails fast) and `TimeoutError`, with `delays=[1,2,4]` seconds — an HTTP-transport-specific predicate that doesn't transfer to a local ticket-store read. `structured.py:294-297` / `runner.py:510-582` implement `OUTPUT_RETRIES=2`, a single bounded reask that feeds the model its own validation error back — also not applicable (LLM-output-validation-specific, not a plain read retry). `src/rebar/_reads.py:53-94`: `show_ticket` (line 53-62) wraps `ticket_reads.ReadError` into `RebarError`, but `list_tickets`'s sole implementation `list_by_query` (line 65-76) calls `ticket_reads.list_states(tracker, query)` with **no try/except at all** — its exceptions propagate unwrapped, not as `RebarError`. Both paths are still caught by `_assemble_context_uncached`'s existing broad `except Exception`, so the planned remediation (catch `Exception`, not `RebarError`) is unaffected by this distinction. No reusable predicate/backoff precedent applies to this call; a bespoke tiny retry is justified, specified concretely below.

## Remediation

1. In `_assemble_context_uncached` (`orchestrator.py:163-211`), wrap the `list_tickets` call (line 174) in a bounded retry: **2 attempts total** (1 retry), catching the same broad `Exception` it catches today, with a **fixed 50ms delay** between attempts. On exhaustion set `pctx.hierarchy_incomplete = True` and `pctx.hierarchy_incomplete_detail = ["enumeration"]`. Add both fields to `PlanContext` (`det_floor.py:104-131`) with defaults `False` / `field(default_factory=list)` — a bare `= []` default on a `@dataclass` list field raises `TypeError` ("mutable default <class 'list'> for field ... is not allowed: use default_factory") at class-definition time (matching the existing `children: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)` pattern at `det_floor.py:114`). Apply the same bounded-retry-then-flag treatment to the per-child `show_ticket` fetch (line 184-187); on a per-child failure, append that child's id (not `"enumeration"`) to `hierarchy_incomplete_detail` and set `hierarchy_incomplete = True`, continuing with the summary row for that child (existing fallback behavior unchanged).
2. Thread `hierarchy_incomplete`/`hierarchy_incomplete_detail` through **all five** `finalize_verdict` call sites via the `coverage` dict (the mechanism `finalize_verdict` already uses for `llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed`), sourced differently per site since only some have the real `pctx`:
   - `workflow_ops.py:135` `plan_review_precheck`, call site line 209: real `pctx` in scope -> `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete"] = pctx.hierarchy_incomplete`, `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete_detail"] = pctx.hierarchy_incomplete_detail`. Also add both fields to the `base` dict (line 141-147) returned by this step so they flow to `ctx.inputs` downstream.
   - `workflow_ops.py:503` `plan_review_coach`, call site line 557: no real `pctx` -> `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete"] = ctx.inputs.get("hierarchy_incomplete", False)`, `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete_detail"] = ctx.inputs.get("hierarchy_incomplete_detail", [])`, mirroring the existing `ctx.inputs.get("det_coverage")` at line 547. `ctx.inputs` is populated entirely from the step's YAML `with:` block, so this only works once the YAML itself passes the two new fields: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` has exactly four `uses: plan_review_coach` steps (confirmed at lines 205, 219, 285, 299 — one `then`/`else` pair per branch arm, both branch arms identical), each with a `with:` block ending in `ticket_type: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.ticket_type }}` that must gain two more lines: `hierarchy_incomplete: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.hierarchy_incomplete }}` and `hierarchy_incomplete_detail: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.hierarchy_incomplete_detail }}`. Without this YAML edit, `ctx.inputs.get("hierarchy_incomplete", False)` always returns `False` and the coach-path threading is silently defeated.
   - `gate_dispatch.py:298` `_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`, coverage built ~line 324: `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete"] = precheck.get("hierarchy_incomplete", False)`, `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete_detail"] = precheck.get("hierarchy_incomplete_detail", [])` (same `precheck` dict already used for `det_coverage`).
   - `gate_dispatch.py:342` `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`, coverage built ~line 381: identical `precheck.get(...)` pattern.
   - `gate_dispatch.py:402` `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`, coverage built ~line 420: real `ctx` (`PlanContext`) is passed straight through -> `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete"] = getattr(ctx, "hierarchy_incomplete", False)`, `coverage["hierarchy_incomplete_detail"] = getattr(ctx, "hierarchy_incomplete_detail", [])`.
3. In `finalize_verdict` (`orchestrator.py:503-541`), add `elif coverage.get("hierarchy_incomplete"): verdict = "INDETERMINATE"` alongside the existing `llm_unavailable`/`verify_failed` branches (same `elif` chain, checked before falling through to PASS). No relevance-exception carve-out — see item 6 below for why.
4. In `drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop` (`drift_floor.py:190-211`), add the identical `elif cov.get("hierarchy_incomplete"): verdict["verdict"] = "INDETERMINATE"` branch so a dropped BLOCK re-derives INDETERMINATE, not PASS, at all three call sites: `drift_floor.apply_to_verdict` (call at `drift_floor.py:272`), `xcheck.apply_contradiction_drops` (def `xcheck.py:126`, call at `xcheck.py:180`), `xcheck.apply_comment_trail_drops` (def `xcheck.py:258`, call at `xcheck.py:311`).
5. Update `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_precheck_output.schema.json`: add to `properties` — `"hierarchy_incomplete": {"type": "boolean", "description": "True iff child enumeration or a per-child fetch failed during context assembly."}` and `"hierarchy_incomplete_detail": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Failed child ids, or [\"enumeration\"] on total list_tickets failure."}`. Do **not** add either to `required` — a missing key reads as falsy/empty everywhere it's consumed (item 2's `.get(..., False)`/`.get(..., [])`), so existing recorded verdicts / older step outputs without the field stay schema-valid. Leave `additionalProperties: false` as-is (both new keys are now declared). Rollback direction: if this schema change is ever reverted, run records already written by the new code (containing `hierarchy_incomplete`/`hierarchy_incomplete_detail`) would fail the reverted schema's closed `additionalProperties: false` validation when read back by `gate_dispatch.py`'s recovery paths (`precheck = succeeded.get(STEP_PRECHECK)`). This is an accepted tradeoff, not a gap to remediate here: schema field additions in this codebase are forward-only (no prior art for a schema-rollback data migration), and reverting an additive schema change without also migrating or discarding the records it wrote is a pre-existing risk of any schema evolution, not one this ticket introduces or must solve.
6. Parent-epic AC #4 reconciliation: parent epic `6eca-183e-1cd2-4fb9` AC #4 reads verbatim: *"Plan review cannot produce an ordinary clean pass when the ticket hierarchy was loaded incompletely, unless the omitted context is demonstrably irrelevant."* This leaf intentionally implements the fail-closed half only, with no relevance-exception carve-out, because the exception's own trigger condition — "the criteria that needed the missing context were still decided" — cannot be stated safely here: confirmed via `det_floor.py:104-138`/`362-368` that a failed enumeration collapses `children` to `[]`, which flips `PlanContext.has_children` to `False`, which in turn makes exactly the container-scoped checks that would consume the missing hierarchy (`P5` confirmed; `P8`'s container pairing check similarly gated) return a trivial `pass` rather than running against absent data. So "every criterion was decided despite incomplete context" is never a real state to detect — the container-specific criteria are unconditionally the ones suppressed, meaning any relevance carve-out would be vacuous by construction. Always-INDETERMINATE is therefore the correct, narrower implementation of AC #4 for this context-assembly failure mode, not a deviation from it.
7. Test-case content assertions: add a total-enumeration-failure test asserting `hierarchy_incomplete_detail == ["enumeration"]` exactly (not just that `hierarchy_incomplete` is truthy), and a partial-failure test (one child's `show_ticket` raises) asserting `hierarchy_incomplete_detail` contains that specific child's ticket id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PlanContext` gains `hierarchy_incomplete: bool = False` and `hierarchy_incomplete_detail: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` (`det_floor.py`).
- [ ] `_assemble_context_uncached`'s `list_tickets` call retries once (2 attempts total, 50ms fixed delay, same broad `Exception` predicate as today) before setting `hierarchy_incomplete=True`, `hierarchy_incomplete_detail=["enumeration"]` on total failure.
- [ ] The per-child `show_ticket` fetch gets the same bounded-retry-then-flag treatment; on a per-child failure the child's id is appended to `hierarchy_incomplete_detail` and `hierarchy_incomplete=True` is set, with the existing summary-row fallback unchanged.
- [ ] `plan_review_precheck` (`workflow_ops.py:135`) reads `pctx.hierarchy_incomplete`/`pctx.hierarchy_incomplete_detail` directly (real `pctx` in scope) and threads both into its `base`/`coverage` dicts, used at its own `finalize_verdict` call (line 209).
- [ ] `plan_review_coach` (`workflow_ops.py:503`) reads both fields via `ctx.inputs.get(...)` (mirroring `det_coverage`), NOT via any `pctx` attribute (its `pctx` at line 540 is a minimal reconstruction with no hierarchy data) — no contradiction between AC language and code here.
- [ ] All three `gate_dispatch.py` recovery/degrade paths (`_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`, `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`, `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`) thread `hierarchy_incomplete`/`hierarchy_incomplete_detail` into the `coverage` dict they build, per Remediation item 2 — five `finalize_verdict` call sites total are covered, not two.
- [ ] `finalize_verdict` (`orchestrator.py`) and `drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop` (`drift_floor.py:190-211`) each gain an `elif coverage.get("hierarchy_incomplete"): verdict = "INDETERMINATE"` branch; the drift_floor branch is exercised through all three call sites (`drift_floor.apply_to_verdict`, `xcheck.apply_contradiction_drops`, `xcheck.apply_comment_trail_drops`).
- [ ] `plan_review_precheck_output.schema.json` declares `hierarchy_incomplete` (boolean) and `hierarchy_incomplete_detail` (string array) in `properties`, neither in `required`; `additionalProperties: false` is preserved.
- [ ] All four `uses: plan_review_coach` steps in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` (both branch arms' `then`/`else`) have their `with:` block extended with `hierarchy_incomplete: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.hierarchy_incomplete }}` and `hierarchy_incomplete_detail: ${{ steps.precheck.outputs.hierarchy_incomplete_detail }}`, so `ctx.inputs.get(...)` in `plan_review_coach` actually receives the flag instead of always defaulting to `False`.
- [ ] No relevance-exception carve-out is implemented; the ticket body documents why (Remediation item 6), citing parent epic `6eca-183e-1cd2-4fb9` AC #4 verbatim and the `has_children`/container-criteria-suppression mechanism that makes the carve-out's trigger condition unstatable.
- [ ] Test coverage includes: (a) total-enumeration-failure -> `hierarchy_incomplete_detail == ["enumeration"]` exactly; (b) partial per-child failure -> `hierarchy_incomplete_detail` contains the specific failed child id; (c) both cases -> verdict is `INDETERMINATE` at at least one of the five `finalize_verdict` sites and survives a drift-floor/xcheck drop without reverting to PASS.
baseline.summary: Prevent clean plan-review passes with incomplete hierarchy context

## Summary

The environment-aware `resolve_symbol` grounding tool (`pai_tools.grounding_tools`,
bug 406f) classifies a resolved symbol as `repo-local` vs `third-party/stdlib` by
root-containment alone (`_within_root(origin, root)` at `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`).
When the virtualenv lives INSIDE the repo (`<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/<pkg>`),
a third-party dependency's origin path is under the repo root, so it is wrongly
labelled `repo-local` — defeating the tool's whole purpose of separating first-party
symbols from installed dependencies.

The discovery tools already avoid this (their `skip_dir` prunes `.venv`/`venv` via
`_NOISE_DIRS`), but the `resolve_symbol` locality check had no equivalent exclusion.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Have a repo-nested virtualenv (`<repo>/.venv`) with a third-party dep installed
   (e.g. PyYAML).
2. Call `grounding_tools(".")`'s `resolve_symbol("yaml")`.

- Expected: `EXISTS: … [third-party/stdlib (site-packages), origin=…]`.
- Actual: `EXISTS: … [repo-local, origin=…]` — the in-tree `.venv` origin is under
  the root, so it is misclassified as first-party source.

## Root Cause

`resolve_symbol` computes locality as `_within_root(realpath(origin), root)` only.
A repo-nested `.venv`/site-packages path satisfies `_within_root`, so third-party
deps installed in-tree read as `repo-local`.

## Fix

- Add `_is_dependency_path()` (+ `_DEPENDENCY_PATH_PARTS`) to `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py`
  detecting `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- Gate the classification in `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`: `repo-local` requires
  under-root AND not a dependency path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `resolve_symbol` classifies a dependency installed in a repo-nested `.venv`
      (origin under `<repo>/.venv/.../site-packages/…`) as `third-party/stdlib`, not
      `repo-local`.
- [ ] Genuine first-party source under the root (e.g. `src/rebar/…`, not in a
      dependency root) still classifies as `repo-local` (no over-exclusion).
- [ ] `_is_dependency_path` in `src/rebar/llm/fs_tools.py` flags
      `site-packages`/`dist-packages`/`.venv`/`venv` path components.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the in-tree-`.venv` case and the first-party `src/` case.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected unit tests pass.
baseline.summary: resolve_symbol misclassifies repo-nested .venv deps as repo-local

content.text: The agent step-budget default is too low for the agentic plan-review VERIFIER, causing routine INDETERMINATE plan reviews on code-grounded tickets.
## Why

`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 25` (env `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS`, src/rebar/llm/config.py:237) is too low for the agentic verifier (`plan-review-verifier-agentic`), which re-grounds findings against real code with tools. On code-grounded tickets it routinely exceeds 25 steps mid-verify → the `verify` step fails → the gate degrades to INDETERMINATE (`llm_unavailable`) → no signed review → the claim is blocked. Observed this cycle on `tarry-creep-range` (c38b): default 25 → INDETERMINATE; `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=50` → PASS + signed. Doubling the default to 50 removes the routine flake while staying well under the review-op floors that still apply.
## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` 25 → 50, and refresh the env-doc comment ("25 ~= 12 tool calls" → "50 ~= 25 tool calls").

- `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`, `src/rebar/llm/code_review.py`, `src/rebar/llm/operations.py` — refresh the stale "REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=25 ≈ 12 tool calls" comments to the new default (the flooring to `_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS=120` / `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS=240` is unchanged; the "far too low for review" sentiment still holds since 50 < 120).
- `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` — the default assertion `(16000, 25, 600)` → `(16000, 50, 600)`.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_review_budget.py` — the `cfg.max_iterations == 25` preconditions → `== 50` (the `>= _FLOOR` assertions stay valid since 50 < 120).
## Scope
In: the default value + the stale doc/comment refresh + the two test updates. Out: the per-op floors (`_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS`/`_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS`), `max_tokens`, `timeout`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` is 50; `LLMConfig.from_env()` with no override yields `max_iterations == 50`.
- [ ] The `REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS` env override and the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` legacy alias still take precedence over the default (unchanged).
- [ ] No doc/comment still claims the framework default is 25 (the stale "=25 ≈ 12 tool calls" notes are refreshed).
- [ ] The review/verify op floors (`_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS=120`, `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS=240`) are unchanged and still applied above the new default.
- [ ] `make check` + the suite pass (`test_config_llm` + `test_review_budget` updated).

baseline.summary: Double the default LLM agent step budget (25 -> 50)

content.text: ## Summary
`rebar show` (and its JSON output) surfaces the internal `managed_refs` provenance
projection in a way that reads as a **live `relates_to` link**, even after that link
has been removed with `unlink`. This makes a correctly-removed link look like it is
still present, and makes `unlink` look broken when it is working correctly.
## Context / root cause
`managed_refs` (`src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py`) is a **strictly-monotonic**
projection of every logical reference a ticket has *ever* managed. Per its own module
docstring (lines 32-38) and `add_managed_ref` ("Never removes", lines 92-103) it is
**deliberately never pruned by UNLINK/detach** — it exists so a local link/parent
removal can be propagated to a peer system (Jira) without being resurrected by the
next inbound sync. That behavior is correct and intentional for reconciliation.
The problem is purely **presentation**: `show` renders `managed_refs` alongside the
live link data with a `relates_to <target>` shape indistinguishable from an active
relation, with nothing marking it as "removed / provenance-only." The live link set
(`deps`) is the source of truth for what links actually exist.
## Reproduction Steps
1. `rebar link A B relates_to`  (creates the link).
2. `rebar unlink A B`  (removes it; reciprocal side removed too for relates_to).
3. `rebar deps A`  → shows `deps: []` (link is genuinely gone).
4. `rebar show A`  → still shows `managed_refs: [["relates_to", "B"]]`.
5. `rebar unlink A B` again → `Error: no LINK event found …` (confirms nothing to remove).
- **Expected:** after unlink, `show` does not present B as a current `relates_to`
relation of A. Any provenance/ever-managed info is either hidden from the default
human view or clearly labeled as removed/provenance-only, distinct from live links.
- **Actual:** `show` presents `managed_refs` such that B looks like a current
`relates_to` link of A, contradicting `deps: []` and misleading the reader into
thinking `unlink` failed.
## Impact
- Users (and agents) reading `show` conclude an unlinked relation is still present,
and that `unlink` is broken — wasted debugging (this bug was filed after exactly
that confusion). It undermines trust in the unlink/link surface.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a successful `unlink`, the default human `rebar show` output does not
present the removed relation as a current/live link.
- [ ] If provenance (`managed_refs`) is shown at all in user-facing output, it is
clearly labeled as provenance/ever-managed (removed links distinguishable from
active ones) — not rendered identically to live `deps` relations.
- [ ] The live link source of truth (`deps`) and the monotonic `managed_refs`
projection are visually/structurally distinct in `show`/JSON so they can't be
conflated.
- [ ] `managed_refs` remains monotonic (this bug must NOT be "fixed" by pruning it on
UNLINK — that would reopen the Jira removal-resurrection window the field guards).
- [ ] A regression test asserts that `show` for a ticket with a removed relates_to
link does not present it as an active relation.

baseline.summary: rebar show surfaces monotonic managed_refs as a live link, making removed (unlinked) relations look present

# Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at 793 LOC against the absolute 800 cap, so SEVEN lines of headroom, and it is the most CENTRAL near-cap file in the repo (fan-in 93). Ticket d23e's entire scope is this file — a `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation alias, which must keep honouring the old name, warn, and prefer the new. MEASURED comparable: the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone (`3eb3e71337`) cost +8 lines, and an alias is strictly bigger than a tombstone, so realistically 10-16 lines. Per-knob cost in this file is MEASURED at 10-13 lines. d23e is genuinely blocked.

## Approach
**ADR 0056 §Decision 5 pre-diagnosed this file and its prescription does NOT hold. Do not follow it.** It said config.py's problem is "178 lines of FLAT independent env reads" wanting "a declarative field table". Verified against the tree:
 * The SPAN claim holds (`from_env` is `config.py:575-753` = 179 lines) but the characterisation does
   not. Only 125 of those lines are the flat `return cls(...)`; the other 53 are an ORDERING-COUPLED
   preamble (the tombstone raise at `:581-584` must precede everything; `table`/`cli` must precede
   every read; `current_code_root()` must beat the env var, `:617-625`). Of 29 kwargs, 22 are regular
   and SEVEN are irregular (a derived non-knob `runner`; `api_key` env-only by secret policy; a 3-way
   `repo_path` cascade rooted in a ContextVar; `tickets_path` with no env var at all; 20 lines of
   custom `mcp_servers` JSON parsing; a nested `LangfuseConfig`; an enum-validating `overlap_drain`),
   plus two field/env/file name mismatches a convention-driven table cannot derive.
 * **A TABLE WOULD BREAK THE ENV-VAR DRIFT GATE — this is the crux.** `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
   is a pure AST walk with no name resolution: it recognises a read only when the name argument is a
   STRING LITERAL (`:117-124`) and files anything else under "dynamically-constructed reads", where
   the variable DISAPPEARS from the table. A loop over spec rows makes that argument an
   `ast.Attribute`, so all 19 currently-resolved rows vanish from `docs/env-vars.md` and CI fails.
   `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` exists to catch this class and names the precedent
   ("exactly what happened on sibling task f844"); `llm/model_classes.py:112-130` spells out nine
   literal `os.environ.get` calls rather than one indirection for the same reason. **The repo has
   already tried the table shape here and rejected it.**
 * In-file, a table nets roughly ZERO lines anyway (~66 lines of rows replacing ~110, plus ~20 of
   dispatch). It relieves nothing.

**What the ADR missed, and what this ticket does instead: 219 of the 793 lines are not configuration at all.** `config.py:51-152` and `:190-269` are the gate read-root / snapshot-session domain — four ContextVars and eleven functions (`current_code_root`, `resolve_code_root`, `current_tickets_root`, `current_code_sha`, `in_gate_session`, `gate_session`, `assert_gated`, `use_code_root`, `use_tickets_root`). `assert_gated` (`:216-240`) raises about `rebar.llm.gate_source` — it is a RUNTIME FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY GUARD, not a config knob.

Three properties make this the right cut rather than a mechanical carve:
 1. **The seam already has a consumer proving it real.** `llm/gate_source.py:35` imports exactly
    `gate_session, use_code_root, use_tickets_root`, and its module docstring (`:1-18`) already
    documents the block being moved.
 2. **The domain is INERT.** All 154 lines of gate-context growth landed in five commits on or before
    2026-07-09; ZERO since. Every commit after that date landed in the knob region. So this moves
    cold mass out of the way of the hot region.
 3. **One-way dependency, no cycle.** `gate_context` needs only stdlib + `rebar.config` + a lazy
    `rebar.llm.errors`; it imports NOTHING from `llm.config`. `llm.config` imports it at module scope
    for `from_env`. This respects `model_classes.py:16-20`'s rule that config must never import back.

LEAVE `config.py:155-187` (`_active_gate_config`, `gate_config`, `resolve_gate_config`) IN PLACE — it is genuinely about `LLMConfig` and moving it buys a lazy import for no benefit.

**HONEST LIMIT, state it in the change and the ADR: this RELOCATES MASS, it does NOT REMOVE THE ABSORBER.** The absorber is the ~10-13 line per-knob cost in `from_env`, and the only structural fix for that is blocked by the scanner. This buys about 15 knobs of runway, not permanence. The durable follow-ups are (a) teach `gen_env_registry.py` to consume an exported spec list — precedent exists at `:150-160` where it already imports and unions `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` — and only THEN table-ify, or (b) domain-split the knobs per feature cluster (the 12 `overlap_*` fields are ~115 lines but change `cfg.overlap_k` to `cfg.overlap.k` at ~31 sites). Both are separate epics.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — remove `:51-152` and `:190-269`; add a re-export block.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` — NEW, ~202 LOC (clears the 100-LOC floor).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — one regenerated cell: `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` moves file (`config.py:227`).
- `tests/unit/` — the headroom guard.

## Testing
**The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.** THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT TRUE: re-export the moved names from `llm.config` and repoint NO consumer in `src/`. 13 monkeypatch targets name a moved symbol, and every consumer of `current_code_sha` / `assert_gated` uses a FUNCTION-LEVEL `from rebar.llm.config import ...` (verified at `attest.py:123`, `:251`, `:429`, `sidecar.py:404`, `runner.py:259`), so the name is resolved in `config`'s globals at call time — exactly what `monkeypatch.setattr` rebinds. Repointing a consumer while a test patches `rebar.llm.config.<name>` is the silent-break mode ADR 0056 warns about.

Loud canaries, which fail at COLLECTION if the re-export is wrong: `tests/interfaces/store/test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py:19` and `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py:27` both do a module-scope `from rebar.llm.config import <moved name>`. `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:173` patches `llm_config.assert_gated` and fails loudly if the rebind stops taking effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC and `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` is at least
      100 and under 800
- [ ] the seam guard for `llm/config.py` is TIGHTENED from the staged `<= 800` that sibling d8ef
      introduces to the `< 700` policy target, in this same change — the change that creates the
      headroom is the one that may assert it. (d8ef ships the staged bound because config.py is 793
      today; do not re-add a guard, tighten the existing one in
      `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py`.)
- [ ] the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file
- [ ] no module under `src/` imports the moved names from `gate_context` — every consumer still reaches
      them through `rebar.llm.config`, so the monkeypatch targets keep working
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean, with the moved
      `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` row regenerated rather than hand-edited
- [ ] the NEW module's docstring states, IN-REPO, that this relocates inert mass and does NOT remove
      the per-knob absorber in `from_env` — so the next reader sizing up config.py's growth curve
      meets that caveat in the code rather than in a ticket they will not read
- [ ] `assert_gated`'s hardcoded `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` (`config.py:230`) is
      re-pointed to the module that actually contains it after the move, and a test asserts the
      REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning is emitted on the `gate_context` logger rather than
      the `config` one. This is an AUDITED security-relevant warning — the message itself says the
      override is "audited" — so attributing it to a module that no longer holds the code sends
      whoever greps the logs to the wrong file. VERIFIED SAFE to change: `grep -rn '"rebar.llm.config"'
      src/ tests/` returns ONLY that one line, so no test filters on the name and no consumer keys
      off it. Swept the rest of the moved block for the same class: the only other identity literals
      are the three `ContextVar` debug names, which remain accurate under `rebar.llm` and need no
      change

- [ ] [operator-attested] the same caveat appears in the Gerrit commit message. Tagged because the
      completion verifier reads repository files ONLY and cannot read git history, so a criterion
      about a commit message is unconfirmable from the codebase and would burn a close cycle
baseline.summary: Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

content.text: # Compaction: rename folded events to `*.retired` (invariant I1)
## Why
Compaction hard-deletes the event files it folds (`compact.py:140-144` `os.remove`). A delete/add
reconciliation (a rebase — the RC1 class) can resurrect a folded source event -> `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`.
`docs/concurrency.md` I1 already SAYS compaction must rename folded files to `*.retired`; the code does not.
Prerequisite for A2 (glandulous-potent-waxwing) rebuild backstop and A3 (entitled-unsweet-nutria) remediation.
## What
- Add ONE shared contract: `RETIRED_SUFFIX = ".retired"` + `is_active_event(name)` helper (in
`reducer/_cache.py` or a small util), imported by compaction, the reducer, and fsck — single source of truth.
- `compact.py:140-144` — replace `os.remove(fp)` with `os.rename(fp, fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX)`.
- ORDERING/IDEMPOTENCY: write the SNAPSHOT atomically FIRST, then rename; a re-run after a mid-loop crash
skips files already `*.retired` (the SNAPSHOT-present short-circuit at compact.py:227-231 / _scan_snapshot_state
:266-268 makes a re-compact a no-op). Race guard: `if os.path.exists(fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX): continue`.
- ERROR HANDLING: do NOT silently swallow `OSError` — log WARNING per failure / INFO per success so a partial
rename is observable; on failure, reverse already-completed renames before re-raising (atomic).
- `reducer/_cache.py` — exclude `*.retired` in BOTH listing paths: the `event_filenames` list (~line 97) AND
the `*.json` glob (~line 102), via `is_active_event`.
- `fsck.py` — explicit `is_active_event` guard in the `_check_snapshot` loop; `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` must NOT
fire on a retired source file.
- `docs/concurrency.md` (I1) — align doc with code; ADD a `.retired` lifecycle note: retention permanent for
now (accepted storage tradeoff); branch-wide `.retired` GC is a documented FOLLOW-UP (new linked ticket),
safe only past causal stability. State that `.retired` files are benign under a code rollback (old `*.json`
glob ignores them).
## Scope
Compaction + reducer/fsck `.retired` exclusion + the shared constant/helper + the I1 doc. Does NOT change
replay ordering (A2) or remediate the live store (A3).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Step 0 (RED): write the two-clone merge+rebase resurrection test; record it FAILING on unpatched code.

- [ ] `RETIRED_SUFFIX` + `is_active_event` defined once and used by compaction, reducer (both listing paths), fsck. Proof: `grep -rn "\.retired" src/rebar | grep -v RETIRED_SUFFIX` shows only the constant def.
- [ ] `os.remove` gone from the fold loop. Proof: `grep -n "os.remove" src/rebar/_commands/compact.py` — no fold-loop match.
- [ ] SNAPSHOT written before renames; simulated mid-loop-crash re-run is a no-op (idempotent); rename failures logged (not swallowed) and reversed (atomic).
- [ ] Reducer replay + `fsck` on a store with a `*.retired` file exit clean (no `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`); fresh replay equals the pre-compaction snapshot.
- [ ] Two-clone merge+rebase resurrection regression test now GREEN.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` I1 matches code; `.retired` GC follow-up ticket created + linked.

baseline.summary: Compaction: non-destructive `*.retired` rename (invariant I1)

baseline.description:
## Summary
`rebar review-plan <id>` unconditionally re-runs the full (billable, multi-turn LLM)
plan review every time it is invoked, even when **nothing about the ticket has changed
since the last successful review**. When several agents act on stale ticket state — or a
single agent re-invokes after an unrelated `HEAD` advance — this burns tokens and wall-clock
re-deriving an identical verdict. Plan review should be **idempotent against an unchanged
ticket**: if the material the last review was computed over is unchanged, short-circuit and
reuse the existing attestation, emitting a clear feedback message that explains why it did
not re-run. A `--force` flag must let a client override and re-run unconditionally.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` on a ticket and let it produce a passing attestation.
2. Without editing the ticket's description/acceptance criteria/type (i.e. the reviewed
   material is byte-identical), run `rebar review-plan <id>` again.
3. Observe a second full LLM review is performed (new billable call, ~minutes of wall-clock),
   producing a verdict equivalent to the first.

**Expected:** the second invocation detects the material is unchanged since the last review,
**skips** the LLM call, and prints a feedback message (e.g. "plan review skipped: ticket
unchanged since last review at <sha>/<ts>; pass --force to re-run"). The existing attestation
is reused. `--force` bypasses the check and re-runs.
**Actual:** a full re-review runs unconditionally regardless of whether anything changed.

## Notes / design pointers
- The plan-review attestation already records a `material` fingerprint (see the signed
  manifest, e.g. `material: c2b48241ad85a805`) and a `verified-at-sha`. The idempotence
  check should key on the **reviewed material fingerprint** (ticket content), NOT bare `HEAD`
  — a `HEAD` advance that does not touch the ticket's material must not force a re-run. Note
  the current claim gate treats an attestation whose `head_sha != HEAD` as "stale" and demands
  a re-run; that staleness definition is over-broad and is the root of the wasted work here.
- Decide the precise change-detection basis (material fingerprint vs. cited-code drift) and
  document it, so "unchanged" has one authoritative definition shared with the claim gate.
- `--force` must be plumbed through the CLI (`_review_plan`) and any MCP `review_plan` surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id>` short-circuits (no LLM call) when the ticket's reviewed
      material is unchanged since the last successful review, reusing the prior attestation.
- [ ] The short-circuit prints a clear feedback message explaining the behavior and how to
      override (`--force`).
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id> --force` re-runs the review unconditionally.
- [ ] A `HEAD` advance that does not change the ticket's reviewed material does NOT by itself
      trigger a re-run (idempotence is keyed on material, not bare HEAD).
- [ ] The MCP `review_plan` surface exposes the same `force` override.
- [ ] Regression test: two back-to-back reviews with no ticket change ⇒ exactly one LLM call;
      with `--force` ⇒ two calls.
- [ ] Docs (plan-review-gate.md) document the idempotence behavior and the `--force` escape hatch.
baseline.summary: plan review re-runs on unchanged ticket; add idempotence short-circuit + --force override

content.text: ## Why
The engine needs a lean DECLARATIVE IR expressing steps + conditionals + loops + map as DATA — the git source
of truth, agent-editable, and projectable to a visual editor. v1 is a strict acyclic DAG whose only control
flow is an `if:` skip-guard, which cannot express branching, loops, or fan-out.
## What
Define a v2 schema extending the v1 GitHub-Actions-style YAML: route/conditional edges, loop frames (mandatory
max_iterations), and map/fan-out over a collection; stable step ids. Add a v1->v2 migration shim and update the
linter so cycles are legal ONLY via declared loop frames (raw `needs` cycles still rejected), with frame-scoped
reference integrity and map `as` binding checks.

- src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json (additionalProperties:false retained)
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/schema.py, lint.py, migrate.py
Out: the interpreter (separate story).

- [ ] v1->v2 migrate shim registered in migrate.py with a golden round-trip test.

- [ ] Registry/coverage guard passes.

content.text: # Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)
## Why
Adjudication of would-block/near-block plan-review findings showed the gate UNDER-blocks: 15/20 findings
in the 0.60-0.69 band on blocking criteria were block-worthy with ZERO false-positives, and four
currently-advisory criteria (G1G2, T1, T8, E4) scored 75-100% block-worthy at their would-block slice.
The 0.70 bar strands real blocks and the blocking set omits load-bearing criteria. (E1 and T3 also scored
~75% but are NOT promoted here — no threshold cleanly separates their borderline findings; deferred.)
## What
Apply the approved per-criterion thresholds/postures in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`:
- Lower `block_threshold` 0.70 -> 0.60 for exactly: COH, E2, F1, G5, G6, T5e.
- Keep T4 @ 0.70 (its band findings were fail-safe migrations).
- Promote to `default_posture: blocking`: G1G2 @0.70, T1 @0.70, T8 @0.70, and E4 @0.75.
- E1, T3, A1 remain advisory. No other criterion changes.
## Scope
- Edit only the routing JSON + the plan-review unit tests asserting per-criterion `block_threshold` /
`default_posture`. No engine or aggregation changes here (the impact redesign is a separate child).
- This is a deliberate BREAKING behavioral change: plans that passed before may now BLOCK. Rollout is
coupled to the permissive-rollout child (ship the wider set first, tune via the calibration harness);
rollback is reverting the JSON (single-commit, trivially reversible).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `criteria_routing.json` matches the table above EXACTLY (per-criterion `block_threshold` +
`default_posture`); a test asserts each of the SIX lowered (COH/E2/F1/G5/G6/T5e @ 0.60) + the FOUR
promoted (G1G2/T1/T8 blocking @ 0.70, E4 blocking @ 0.75) + T4 UNCHANGED (@ 0.70, blocking).
- [ ] Plan-review unit tests updated and green; `make lint` passes. Proving command:
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py -v`.
- [ ] DETERMINISTIC simulation (no live corpus): using the packaged routing + the shared
`threshold_for` / `pass3_decide`, a test asserts that for EACH of the six lowered criteria a synthetic
finding at priority 0.65 now BLOCKS (>= 0.60) whereas at the OLD 0.70 it would NOT have; and that for
EACH of the four promoted criteria the posture is now `blocking` and a finding blocks only at/above its
NEW threshold (0.70 or 0.75). (Live-corpus block-rate delta on the accumulated sidecar corpus is
measured by the calibration child raptorial-galloping-dragon, NOT gated here.)
- [ ] No criterion OUTSIDE the approved set {COH,E2,F1,G5,G6,T5e,T4,G1G2,T1,T8,E4} changes posture or
threshold. A test pins the COMPLETE expected routing as an INLINE fixture inside
`tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py` — a dict mapping EVERY criterion id to its expected
`(block_threshold, default_posture)` — and asserts the packaged `criteria_routing.json` matches it
exactly. Any unintended change to ANY criterion (approved or not) fails the assertion; the expectation
lives in the test (versioned with it), so there is NO separate baseline snapshot file to drift.

baseline.summary: Plan-review threshold + posture recalibration (approved pre-redesign changes)

content.text: ## Why
`server.json` is the MCP registry front-door contract, but it has drifted from
the real config surface. It lists only `REBAR_ROOT`, `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`, and
the **deprecated** `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE`, while the actual gates are
`mcp.allow_llm` (`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`) and `mcp.allow_jira_sync`
(`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`). Users see the LLM/reconcile tools appear but fail
at call time with no manifest hint, and new installs inherit deprecated
terminology. Nothing prevents this from re-drifting.
## What
- Update `server.json` `environmentVariables` to the current contract: add
`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` with accurate
descriptions; keep `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` only if explicitly labeled
a deprecated alias (prefer replacing it with the current name).
- Add a **CI drift-guard** that compares the manifest's advertised env-var set
against the canonical gate list in code (the `REBAR_MCP_*` env gates read in
`mcp_server.py` / the readonly+allow gates), failing the build on divergence —
mirroring the existing prompt-index / criteria-routing drift gates in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`.
## Scope
`server.json` + one CI gate (a small script under `scripts/` or a step in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Identify the single source of truth for the env
gates so the guard has an authoritative list to diff against. No behavior change
to the server itself.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `server.json` advertises `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM` and
`REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC` with correct descriptions.
- [ ] The deprecated `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_RECONCILE_LIVE` is removed or explicitly
marked as a deprecated alias.
- [ ] A CI gate fails when `server.json`'s env-var set diverges from the
canonical `REBAR_MCP_*` gate list in code.
- [ ] The gate passes on the corrected manifest; `make lint` stays green.
