baseline.description:
## Symptom

A full default-selection run (`make test`) fails with ONE test, which passes in isolation:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict
      - StopIteration
      at: line = next(r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records if "llm call [" in r.getMessage())

Isolated: `pytest tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py` -> 12 passed. Order-dependent, not a defect in the test's own subject.

## Proven mechanism (clean tree, no other changes applied)

`src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:120 configure_logging()` does, at lines 145-146:

    lg = logging.getLogger("rebar")
    lg.setLevel(level)
    lg.propagate = False

`propagate = False` on the shared `rebar` parent logger is PROCESS-GLOBAL and is never restored. pytest's `caplog` captures via a handler on the ROOT logger, so once propagation is off no `rebar.*` record can reach it again. Every subsequent caplog assertion silently sees zero records.

Reproduced directly on a CLEAN checkout (changes stashed), two tests in one file:

    def test_a_baseline(caplog):                 # PASSES
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

    def test_b_after_configure_logging(caplog):  # FAILS: assert False
        from rebar.review_bot.config import configure_logging
        configure_logging()
        with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO): _emit()
        assert any("llm call [" in r.getMessage() for r in caplog.records)

Result: `1 failed, 1 passed`. The only difference is the `configure_logging()` call. `caplog.at_level()` does not help - it adjusts levels, not propagation.

Two entry points reach it: `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1288` calls it directly, and `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:202` calls it at MODULE IMPORT time (so merely importing the app poisons the process; that path is inert in this checkout only because `fastapi` is absent).

## Why this matters beyond one red test

The failure is silent and non-local: it does not point at `configure_logging`, it points at an unrelated victim whose position in the run order falls after the poisoning. Any future caplog assertion on a `rebar.*` logger is one ordering change away from the same mystery, and the affected assertions provide NO coverage in a full run while appearing green in isolation.

## Suggested direction (not implemented)

`propagate = False` exists to stop double-logging through uvicorn/root in the container. Options: attach the handler without disabling propagation and rely on the existing marker guard to avoid duplicates; make the propagation change conditional on actually running under uvicorn; or add an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` that snapshots and restores the `rebar` logger's `level`/`propagate`/`handlers` around every test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A caplog-based assertion on a `rebar.*` logger still captures records after
      `configure_logging()` has run in the same process, pinned by a test that fails before the fix.
- [x] The double-logging that `propagate=False` was introduced to prevent is still prevented; the
      existing `test_configure_logging_emits_rebar_info_to_stdout` and
      `test_configure_logging_is_idempotent` stay green.
- [x] `make test` (default selection) is green by exit code with no order-dependent failure.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code.
baseline.summary: configure_logging() sets propagate=False on the shared 'rebar' logger, silently breaking every later caplog test in the process

# Snapshot cache janitor — reclamation under disk pressure

## Why

Reclaiming the content-addressed snapshot cache under disk pressure WITHOUT corrupting
concurrent readers is the riskiest piece ("the hard part"). The spike showed a PID+heartbeat
lease is unsound (N readers, PID reuse, crash-stale); mature systems (Gitaly, Sourcegraph
gitserver, Bazel, ccache) lean on kernel guarantees instead. Built ON TOP of the cache story
(single-flight populate + delete-on-last-close reads + touch-on-read mtime).

## What

- A SINGLE background janitor in the long-lived server, OFF the hot path (Bazel moved GC to idle).
- Trigger: primary = FREE-SPACE watermark (`shutil.disk_usage`), backstopped by an
  incrementally-maintained byte total (no hot-path `du`); secondary = max-age cold-trim.
- Victim selection: LRU by the cache's touch-on-read `mtime`, skipping any entry within a
  short grace window.
- Eviction mechanism: `rename(<sha>, trash/<uuid>)` (atomic disappearance from the canonical
  path) THEN `rmtree` the trash entry — never in-place `rmtree` (races readers); open fds survive.
- Cross-process interlock: exclusive `flock` on `<cache>/gc/lock` for each GC pass; population
  stays lock-free.
- Startup sweep: `rmtree tmp/* trash/*`; reconcile the byte total via one full walk.
- Trash straggler: an interrupted rename->rmtree is re-drained on a later janitor pass (not only at startup).
- Self-heal: read-error -> discard (rename-to-trash) -> re-materialize; optional periodic
  integrity re-verify (re-derive tree git-ids vs the dir name).
- Tunables CONFIGURABLE with documented defaults: free-space watermark, mtime grace window,
  max-age cutoff, integrity-reverify period.
- ADR: capture the cache/janitor architecture (content-addressed layout, delete-on-last-close,
  flock GC interlock) AND the rejected PID+heartbeat lease.

## Scope

- In: the janitor (trigger/policy/mechanism/interlock), startup sweep, trash drain, self-heal,
  configurable tunables, the ADR.
- Out: the cache read/populate path (sibling cache story); materialization (S1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The janitor reclaims under a free-space watermark using LRU by touch-on-read `mtime`
      (NOT atime), skipping entries within the grace window; runs off the hot path.
- [ ] A secondary max-age cold-trim evicts genuinely cold entries (own test).
- [ ] Startup sweep clears `tmp/*` and `trash/*` and reconciles the byte total via one full walk.
- [ ] The byte total stays consistent under CONCURRENT populate-vs-evict (interleaving or
      fault-injection test) — no TOCTOU drift; verified against the walk.
- [ ] An interrupted rename-to-trash/rmtree straggler is re-drained on a later janitor pass.
- [ ] Eviction is rename-to-trash THEN rmtree; no in-place recursive delete of a live entry.
- [ ] A second process cannot run a GC pass concurrently (exclusive `gc/lock`).
- [ ] A corrupt/truncated entry is detected and self-healed by re-materialization.
- [ ] Watermark, grace window, max-age, and reverify period are configurable with documented defaults.
- [ ] An ADR records the cache/janitor architecture and the rejected PID+heartbeat lease.
baseline.summary: Snapshot cache janitor — reclamation under disk pressure

# Agentic code-review capability for rebar (off by default, source-separated), dogfooded via the Gerrit LLM-Review gate

## ⚑ CURRENT STATE — 2026-07-01 (handoff; see session_log `risky-cherry-seal`/b009)
**MERGED to `main`** (PR #102, commit `2d3e7611`): the full four-pass code-review capability
(WS1–WS5) + the Gerrit review-bot rewired to it (WS6). The capability is off-by-default + source-
separated; Gerrit's `LLM-Review` vote now runs the four-pass review via `review_bot/adapter.py`.

**Children:** WS1–WS5 CLOSED · WS6 (4119) CLOSED · **WS8 (f2d6) OPEN** · **WS7 (1bd2) OPEN** ·
**WS6-b (0da5) OPEN**.

**Remaining work is LIVE-INFRA and must run IN THIS ORDER — each is gated on access this session
lacked (navapbc GitHub org-admin + working AWS/SSM to the Gerrit host):**
1. **WS8 — Harden Gerrit auth FIRST.** The live Gerrit runs `auth.type =
   DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` (dev-mode; anyone can impersonate anyone). Confirmed strategy:
   **GitHub OAuth via `gerrit-oauth-provider`**. Full procedure in
   `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` (PR #104). DO NOT skip — cutting `main` over to a
   dev-auth Gerrit is a security downgrade.
2. **WS7 — Make Gerrit the only path into GitHub `main`** (cutover; consumes d251/S6 mirror-lock)
   + write repo-root `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the Gerrit contribution flow incl. how new devs provision
   credentials) + a tested rollback. Only after WS8 verifies.
3. **WS6-b — Live dogfood:** land `CONTRIBUTING.md` THROUGH Gerrit (`refs/for/main` → LLM-Review
   vote → submit → replicate), recording the change URL + vote.

The epic CLOSES only when WS8→WS7→WS6-b complete. Everything below is the original plan (for
context); the workstream list + ACs at the bottom are current.

---


## Context
Build the agentic code-review capability as a SEPARATE, OFF-BY-DEFAULT rebar capability whose source is clearly isolated so it has no effect when disabled. It CONSUMES the shared **four-pass review kernel** (evidence -> verify -> decide -> coach) and is enforced through Gerrit's `LLM-Review` label on the AWS-hosted environment. Dogfooding on rebar itself is the success criterion.

## Realignment (2026-06) — this epic now CONSUMES a shipped kernel
This epic was written against a "three-pass framework being built in epic `9da1` (OPEN)". That is stale on two counts, corrected here (closed prerequisite epics are NOT reopened):

- **The framework grew a 4th pass and SHIPPED.** `9da1` ("three-pass; migrate existing reviewers") was SUPERSEDED by `3316`/vivid-gang-day — the **four-pass review KERNEL** (Pass-1 finder evidence; Pass-2 separate binary verifier; Pass-3 deterministic decide; Pass-4 affirmative coach) — which is **CLOSED** and shipped as `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/` (`verify.py` / `decide.py` / `coach.py`). `3316` explicitly `blocks` this epic and `docs/review-kernel.md` names b744 as "the second consumer". So b744 is no longer a from-scratch passes build — it is a **kernel CONSUMER**: supply the per-gate plug-ins and call `verify_findings` / `pass3_over_findings` / `coach` directly.
- **`code_review.py` is not a migration target — it is a throwaway single-pass demo to RETIRE.** Today it does select-by-glob -> parallel reviewers -> `aggregate_findings` -> `finalize_findings`, with NO Pass-2/3/4. The deliverable is the kernel-consuming gate; the single-pass `aggregate_findings`-only route is removed (no half-migration).

## Current substrate (shipped PRECONDITIONS vs this epic's NEW work)
SHIPPED (build on; do not rebuild):
- The **four-pass kernel** `review_kernel` (`3316`) + its documented consumer seam (`docs/review-kernel.md`): Pass-2 `verify_findings(findings, *, context, run_chunk, window_tokens, est_tokens, headroom)` + the single `verification` contract; Pass-3 `pass3_decide` / `pass3_over_findings(..., threshold_for)`; Pass-4 `coach(surviving, registry, *, pick, active_triggers)` + `MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA` / `validate_move_registry` (with the `applies_when` field) + `VERIFIER_RULES_SCAFFOLD`. Verified gate-agnostic (consumes a code move-catalog + code findings directly).
- The **provider-agnostic `PydanticAIRunner`** (`e6d9`) + the **v3 workflow engine** (steps/branch/batch/map/loop, `RunnerAgentStep`, `ProductionBatchRunner`, `gate_dispatch`).
- **Contract-bearing code reviewer prompts** (`da27`): `code_quality` / `security` / `tests` front-matter prompts with `applies_to` globs + a derived index + CI drift gate.
- The **grounding oracle + detector registry** (`8f6c`): the fail-open evidence oracle + an extensible detector registry (built-in + project `.rebar/detectors/`).

NEW work (this epic):
- The four-pass code-review GATE that consumes the kernel (diff context-assembler, finder/verify/coach prompts, code move-catalog, per-criterion thresholds) + the thin `gates/code-review.yaml` + `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`.
- The OVERLAY catalog (the ~11 specialist reviewers drafted in the catalog comments) + the base->overlay ESCALATION mechanism (below).
- Secrets / High-Critical-security DETECTORS behind the grounding oracle's detector envelope (or wrap gitleaks/semgrep), with FAIL-CLOSED posture for the hard auto-block.
- SOURCE-SEPARATION into an optional module preserving the MCP `review_code` tool + `rebar review-code` CLI via re-export.
- Rewire d251's SHIPPED `review_bot` adapter seam to the four-pass gate (d251's S4b shipped the receiver/voter/client + the single-pass `adapter.code_review_decision`; WS6 swaps only its decision engine), and make Gerrit the enforced GitHub gatekeeper (WS7).

## Design — four-pass consumer + base->overlay escalation (mechanism PROVEN on the v3 engine)
Workflow shape (the same shape plan-review runs, plus a second agent-driven finder round):

```
diff
 -> assemble_diff (uses)                  # diff + changed_files context        [NEW diff assembler]
 -> triggers      (uses: overlay_triggers)# Round-A glob/keyword overlay flags   [EXISTING op]
 -> base          (agent, standalone)     # base reviewer: findings + recommend_overlays
 -> round_a       (batch, when:=triggers) # deterministically-triggered overlays
 -> union         (uses: overlay_union)   # (glob U base.recommend) - already-run, capped, ONE-HOP  [NEW ~30-LOC op]
 -> round_b       (batch, when:=union)    # the ESCALATED overlays (agent-triggered)
 -> merge         (uses)                  # base + round_a + round_b findings
 -> verify (Pass-2) -> decide (Pass-3) -> coach (Pass-4)   # all kernel
```

Overlay activation = UNION of (a) overlays whose deterministic triggers (`applies_to` globs / content signatures) match the diff, and (b) overlays the BASE reviewer escalates to via a bounded `recommend_overlays: [{overlay_id, reason}]` signal, `overlay_id` constrained to the FIXED catalog enum. A DETERMINISTIC orchestrator takes the union (minus already-run), caps it (top-N), dispatches Round B, and ALL findings (base + Round-A + Round-B) flow into the SAME Pass-2 verifier + Pass-3 deterministic gate. Bounds: ONE HOP (overlays do not re-escalate); per-change CAP; escalation lives on the recall/selection side only (a false escalation costs one extra advisory pass, never a wrong verdict; the precision/decision side stays deterministic). The base reviewer is a STANDALONE agent step (not a batch criterion) so its `recommend_overlays` output survives (the batch runner aggregates only `findings`).

Engine fit: requires NO core-engine change. `batch` membership is a static authored list (the fixed overlay enum) gated per-item by `when: ${{ steps.union.outputs.include_<overlay> }}` — exactly how plan-review's finder batch toggles criteria. A `uses -> batch -> uses -> batch` chain is expressible. The only new engine-side code is two trivial deterministic scripted ops (`overlay_union`, `merge_findings`); the mechanism was proven end-to-end OFFLINE on the v3 engine (the agent's recommendation drove Round-B membership; bogus ids dropped by the enum; the cap bounded fan-out; one-hop held).

## Dependencies — what must be satisfied to implement successfully
- SATISFIED: four-pass kernel (`3316`, closed) + consumer seam; runner + v3 engine (`e6d9`, closed); contract reviewer prompts (`da27`, closed); grounding oracle + detector registry (`8f6c`, closed).
- INTERNAL NEW WORK (in this epic; no external blocker): secrets / High-Critical-security detectors (fail-closed) on the `8f6c` registry; the diff assembler; the overlay catalog + prompts; the two scripted ops; source separation.
- EXTERNAL, NOW CLOSED + MERGED: **`d251` (AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP provisioning)** — shipped `src/rebar/review_bot/` (receiver `app.py` + `voter.py` + `gerrit_client.py` + the `adapter.code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root, ref)` seam) AND the GitHub mirror-lock tooling (S6). WS6 now REWIRES that shipped adapter to the four-pass gate (an offline swap, no live env); WS7 executes the GitHub cutover. `1fa8` (CI second "Verified" vote) is `relates_to`, out of scope for v1.
- PROVENANCE: `9da1` (superseded by `3316`), `3316`, and `d251` are ALL now closed/merged — there is NO remaining OPEN blocker. The only gated items are the LIVE steps (WS6-b dogfood, WS7 apply), gated on deployed-env / GitHub-admin access, not on an open ticket.

## Why this epic is NOT split (and the alternative)
The code-review CAPABILITY (passes 1-4 + overlays + the deterministic verdict, exposed via the existing MCP `review_code` tool + `rebar review-code` CLI) delivers value and is FULLY TESTABLE on real diffs WITHOUT Gerrit — so it does not need `d251`. Bundling it with the Gerrit dogfood couples a software deliverable to AWS infra on a different timeline. Rather than split the epic, the ACs below are PARTITIONED into (A) Capability — buildable and verifiable NOW against the shipped kernel — and (B) Dogfood/Gerrit — gated on `d251`. This keeps one epic with one provenance trail while making the dependency boundary explicit; splitting remains an option only if the capability is to be released/closed independently of the infra.

## Decisions pinned during plan-review (2026-06)
These resolve advisory findings the four-pass plan-review gate raised against this plan (verdict PASS):
- **Overlay cap N = 3** to start (conservative; aligns with the orchestrator-worker "3-5 subagents" prior art). Calibration of N + the advisory/block thresholds is DEFERRED (shared stance with the kernel epic — thresholds start high, so v1 is mostly advisory); the cap/threshold values live in `gates/code-review.yaml` config, not hard-coded.
- **Secrets/security detector path (v1 default):** WRAP existing scanners behind the grounding-oracle detector envelope — **gitleaks** for secrets, **semgrep** for High-Critical security — as the deterministic ground-truth pre-pass (the LLM triages/prioritizes, never invents). Native first-party detectors are a follow-on, not v1. (Alternative weighed: author native detectors first — rejected for v1 because the scanners already encode high-precision rule sets; scanner-as-ground-truth is settled production practice.) **Integration shape pinned by derisk experiment (Round-11; session_log a7e2-381c-6dc6-4d0c):** semgrep IS the opengrep rule format (passes `metadata.rebar_envelope` through + emits SARIF 2.1.0) → High-Critical security ships as detector YAML on the existing `opengrep` backend (vendored pinned p/owasp-top-ten + p/cwe-top-25 subset, diff-scoped). gitleaks uses TOML + compiled-in rules (no YAML rule file) so it can't be a detector YAML, but emits SARIF 2.1.0 → integrated via a generic SARIF-ingest backend (`sarif.from_sarif(trust_rebar_bag=False)`) that also serves semgrep. Fail-CLOSED lives in THIS gate's Pass-3 consumer (abstain on a secrets/High-Critical detector → BLOCK + coverage-gap), NOT in Engine B (fail-open invariant, must stay so). Detail on WS5 (bba6).
  - **Integration shape pinned by derisk experiment (Round-11; session_log a7e2-381c-6dc6-4d0c):** semgrep IS the opengrep rule format and passes `metadata.rebar_envelope` through verbatim + emits SARIF 2.1.0 → High-Critical security ships as **detector YAML on the existing `opengrep` backend** (vendored pinned `p/owasp-top-ten`+`p/cwe-top-25` subset, diff-scoped). gitleaks uses TOML + compiled-in rules (no YAML rule file) so it CANNOT be a detector YAML, but it emits SARIF 2.1.0 → integrated via a **generic SARIF-ingest backend** (`sarif.from_sarif(trust_rebar_bag=False)`), which also serves semgrep and any future SARIF tool. **Fail-CLOSED lives in THIS gate's Pass-3 consumer** (an `abstain` on a secrets/High-Critical detector → BLOCK + coverage-gap note), NOT in Engine B, whose cardinal invariant is fail-OPEN and must stay so for other consumers. Details on WS5 (bba6).
- **Observable verdict artifact:** the gate returns a typed `code_review_verdict` dict (`{verdict: PASS|BLOCK, blocking[], advisory[], coaching[], coverage}`) + emits a review sidecar — exactly parallel to plan-review's verdict + sidecar, so the verdict is a checkable artifact (not just a Gerrit side effect).
- **Re-export shim contract:** the PUBLIC SURFACE is preserved unchanged — the `rebar.llm.review_code(...)` callable, the MCP `review_code` tool, and the `rebar review-code` CLI keep their names/signatures and continue to return a `review_result`. What changes is the IMPLEMENTATION behind that surface: the four-pass kernel-consuming gate REPLACES the single-pass `evidence + aggregate_findings`-only route, which becomes unreachable. `aggregate_findings`/`normalize_finding` may survive as internal Pass-1 helpers; the single-pass GATE PATH does not. The destructive removal of the demo path is recorded in an ADR (one-way door).

## Implementation sequencing (workstreams) — now child stories
The capability is decomposed into child stories (created 2026-06), sequenced via `depends_on` so each lands behind the previous one's contract. WS1 is the ready entry; WS6 is gated on `d251`.
1. **WS1 — diff context-assembler + base reviewer** (8e6f-3ad2-1f24-4b8b / low-cloud-wreck) — ready now.
2. **WS2 — overlay catalog + finder/verify/coach prompts + code move-catalog** (8e78-d515-3a98-4eba / make-rant-buoy) — depends_on WS1.
3. **WS3 — `overlay_union` + `merge_findings` ops + `gates/code-review.yaml`** (8855-e5f9-05b4-4a04 / crow-knelt-fiber) — depends_on WS2.
4. **WS4 — `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` + source-separation** (98ff-d3b8-d2f7-4a86 / side-haiku-dew) — depends_on WS3.
5. **WS5 — secrets/security detectors (fail-closed)** (bba6-69b9-b9d4-4ac0 / corn-pub-oat) — depends_on WS3.
6. **WS6 — Rewire the Gerrit review-bot to the four-pass code review** (4119-1a4f-19ff-4cfa / virid-trench-stone) — depends_on WS4. d251's `review_bot` is shipped, so this is an OFFLINE adapter swap (no live env).
7. **WS6-b — Gerrit `LLM-Review` dogfood proof (live)** (0da5-162a-b41f-413c / van-withe-folly) — depends_on WS6; gated on the deployed AWS/Gerrit env.
8. **WS7 — Make Gerrit the only path into GitHub `main` (cutover) + contributor guide** (1bd2-1401-3a18-4031 / weedy-lath-abbey) — consumes d251/S6; live apply gated on GitHub admin access.

## Specifics pinned (plan-review remediation 2026-06)
- **Back-out for the destructive single-pass retirement (WS4):** the capability is OFF by default, so the new four-pass gate is INERT until enabled; the preserved public surface (re-export shim) keeps existing callers working. **Correction (Round-11):** because the single-pass code is DELETED, reverting the flag default does NOT restore single-pass behavior — it makes the gate inert, with `review_code()` returning a valid EMPTY `review_result` (+ a 'disabled' note), never an error/stub. So the back-out = default-off + shim returning the inert result; the ADR records this as a genuine one-way door (not a reversible behavior swap). This resolves the prior contradiction between calling WS4 a one-way door AND claiming the flag-revert restores prior behavior.
- **WS6 staged rollout (Round-11):** the Gerrit voter activates behind a per-project/staged opt-in before fleet-wide enforcement, so a BLOCK from an under-tested voter cannot gate all committers on day one. Detail on WS6 (4119).
- **WS6 staged rollout (Round-11):** the Gerrit voter activates behind a per-project/staged opt-in before fleet-wide enforcement, so a BLOCK from an under-tested voter cannot gate all committers on day one (detail on WS6/4119).
- **WS6 sequencing risk (it is last by necessity, not choice):** WS1-WS5 deliver a capability fully testable via the `rebar review-code` CLI + MCP `review_code` tool WITHOUT Gerrit, so the only WS6-new surface is the Gerrit REST/event wiring — de-riskable against a STUB Gerrit before `d251` lands. WS6 cannot move earlier because it depends on `d251` infra.

## Acceptance Criteria
The internal new-work dependencies are captured here as workstream ACs; each is a CHILD STORY (detailed ACs + file-impact + verify-commands live on the child). The epic is DONE when all children are closed.

### A. Capability (buildable now against the shipped kernel — no external blocker)
- [ ] **WS1** (8e6f-3ad2-1f24-4b8b / low-cloud-wreck) — diff context-assembler + base reviewer emitting enum-constrained `recommend_overlays` (standalone agent step).
- [ ] **WS2** (8e78-d515-3a98-4eba / make-rant-buoy) — overlay catalog (specialist reviewers with `applies_to` globs/content triggers) + a code verify preamble embedding `VERIFIER_RULES_SCAFFOLD` + a code move-catalog (`MOVE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA` instance) + a `threshold_for` resolver.
- [ ] **WS3** (8855-e5f9-05b4-4a04 / crow-knelt-fiber) — `overlay_union` (glob U recommend − already-run, ONE-HOP, cap N=3) + `merge_findings` + the thin `gates/code-review.yaml` (two-round escalation → kernel Pass-2/3/4); offline FakeRunner test asserts escalation/cap/one-hop and that escalation can never change the verdict.
- [ ] **WS4** (98ff-d3b8-d2f7-4a86 / side-haiku-dew) — `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict` returning the typed `code_review_verdict` + sidecar; OFF by default + SOURCE-SEPARATED; public surface preserved via re-export/shim; single-pass route retired (ADR).
- [ ] **WS5** (bba6-69b9-b9d4-4ac0 / corn-pub-oat) — secrets/security detectors (wrap gitleaks + semgrep behind the grounding-oracle envelope) feeding the hard auto-block; FAIL-CLOSED with a RED-fixture test (unavailable/errored detector BLOCKS or flags a coverage gap, never silently passes).

baseline.description:
Reported by a rebar client (report archived at `~/rebar-archived-child-claim-bug.md` on the operator host) against `nava-rebar 0.10.1` (source build at `f0cf30a0e` + `bcb735630`) with `verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`. **The divergence is reproduced in current `main`**, so this is not fixed by upgrading.

## Symptom

When a container ticket has a child whose status is `archived`, `rebar review-plan <container>` signs a material fingerprint computed over a child set that **includes** the archived child, while the claim gate recomputes the fingerprint over a child set that **excludes** it. The two can never agree, so every `review-plan` → `claim` sequence fails with:

```
Error: cannot start work on <id>: the plan was materially edited since review
(description/AC/file_impact/children changed).
```

Re-running `review-plan` cannot break the loop: each new attestation re-signs the same larger basis the gate will again recompute smaller. The recovery the error itself prints ("run the plan review to earn an attestation, then start work") is non-terminating for this ticket shape.

## Impact

Any container that has ever had a child archived — a normal board outcome when a child is superseded or found to be a duplicate — becomes permanently unclaimable through the supported path. The only exits are `claim --force` (which discards the very gate the config exists to enforce) or mutating the board to detach/unarchive the child. The message is also actively misleading: it reports a plan edit that did not happen, sending the operator to hunt a phantom description change.

## Reproduction

1. Create an epic with N children, each with a `file_impact`.
2. Archive one child. It keeps `parent_id=<epic>`, gains `status=archived`.
3. `rebar review-plan <epic>` → `PASS`, signed.
4. `rebar claim <epic>` → fails with "the plan was materially edited since review".
5. Repeat 3–4 any number of times; identical failure, no edit in between.

## Reporter's evidence (measured, not inferred)

Epic `5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66` in the reporter's store: 12 live children plus archived child `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` (`parent_id=5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66`, `status=archived`). Both fingerprints were reproduced by re-implementing the basis from `material_fingerprint`:

| child set | fingerprint | computed by |
|---|---|---|
| 13 ids (incl. `fb45`) | `084b676f66849bab` | value embedded in the signed attestation |
| 12 ids (excl. `fb45`) | `236d5fa9f6944e87` | `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` at claim time |

- `rebar._reads.list_tickets(parent=<epic>)` returns 12 deterministically (three separate
  processes); `fb45` is absent.
- The stored attestation's `material:` manifest line is `084b676f66849bab`.
- The epic's *original* attestation (signed earlier, by a different operator) carries 13
  `plan-material-pin: child …` lines including `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` — the review side has been
  enumerating the archived child **consistently**, not intermittently.

## Root cause (confirmed in this checkout, current `main`)

The reporter narrowed the divergence to "somewhere below `list_tickets`" and named a relation snapshot as a likely candidate. That is correct — the two sides do not in fact share an enumeration:

- **Gate side** — `attest.current_material_fingerprint()`
  (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:771`) calls
  `_reads.list_tickets(parent=canonical)`, whose default is `include_archived=False`
  (`src/rebar/_reads.py:87`) → **archived children excluded**.
- **Signer side** — the signed generation's `own_material` is computed in
  `generation.from_snapshot()` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:84`) from
  `snapshot.child_ids`, which `collect_plan_relation_snapshot()` builds by scanning reduced
  states and admitting every candidate whose parent resolves to the subject and whose
  `status != "deleted"` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:283`) → **archived
  children included**.

So the divergence is the archived-vs-deleted predicate: the snapshot filters only `deleted`, while `list_tickets` filters `archived` too. `current_material_fingerprint`'s docstring claims it is "matching `orchestrator.material_fingerprint`" — that stated invariant is what is broken, and nothing enforces it because the child predicate is spelled independently at each site.

## Fix direction

Exclude non-live children (archived, deleted) from the material basis, and apply that policy in **one shared helper both the signer and the gate call** rather than independently at two sites. Material is meant to capture *the plan*, and an archived child is no longer part of the plan; this is also what the gate already does, so the gate becomes correct by definition and only the signer changes.

Deliberately **not** choosing the symmetric alternative (include archived on both sides): that would make archiving a child a *material edit*, invalidating a parent's attestation for a board action that changed no plan content — trading this bug for a subtler one. The reporter reached the same conclusion independently.

Note `relation_snapshot.child_ids` also feeds `related_material` and the per-child `plan-material-pin` manifest lines, so the change must keep those consistent with the new basis (archived children should stop being pinned), and existing attestations that pin an archived child must not be treated as forgeries — only as stale in the ordinary way.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single shared helper defines "children that count as plan material" (live only: excludes
   `archived` and `deleted`), and both `generation.from_snapshot()`/`collect_plan_relation_snapshot()`
   and `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` obtain their child set through it — no
   independently spelled status predicate remains at either site.
2. Regression test: archive a child of a container, then `review-plan` → `claim` succeeds.
   Currently fails.
3. ~~Regression test: archiving a child alone does **not** invalidate a container's existing
   valid attestation (material fingerprint unchanged across the archive).~~
   **AMENDED — the original AC3 was unsatisfiable together with AC1.** Once archived children
   are excluded from the material basis (AC1's "live only"), archiving a child necessarily
   removes it from that basis and so necessarily MOVES the fingerprint. The rationale above had
   this inverted: it is the *include-archived-on-both-sides* option that would leave the
   fingerprint untouched, not the exclude option that was chosen. Replacement AC3:

   **Regression test: the signer-side and gate-side fingerprints agree BOTH before and after a
   child is archived.** That is the invariant that actually cures the bug. The accepted residual
   cost is explicit: archiving a child invalidates the container's attestation and requires a
   fresh `review-plan`. That is recoverable, unlike the permanent unclaimable loop this bug
   caused, and it is the price of keeping "material" mean "the live plan".
4. Regression test asserting the docstring invariant directly: for a container with a mix of
   live, archived, and deleted children, the signer-side fingerprint and
   `current_material_fingerprint()` are equal.
5. `plan-material-pin` manifest lines for the container no longer include archived children,
   and an attestation signed *before* the fix (pinning an archived child) is handled as stale /
   re-reviewable, not as a signature failure.
6. Full suite, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` green.

## Workarounds until fixed

- Detach the archived child from the parent (`rebar edit <child> --parent=null`) so both sides
  enumerate the same set, then re-run `review-plan` and `claim`. The reporter applied this to
  `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d`, which is now unparented in their store.
- `rebar claim <id> --force="<reason>"` works but discards the gate.
baseline.summary: Archived child permanently blocks claim on its parent: signer includes it in the material basis, claim gate excludes it

# Surface the ref + source controls on the CLI and MCP tool schemas

## Why

The new `ref` + `source` controls must be reachable by both human (CLI) and agent (MCP)
clients, so a distributed team can target the exact code version a gate runs against.

## What

- Add `--ref <branch|tag|sha>` (default `origin/main`) and `--source {attested|local}` to the
  code-reading surfaces, with the CLI<->MCP mapping pinned explicitly (no "surfaces as they
  exist"):
  - MCP tools: `review_plan`, `verify_completion`, `review_ticket`, `review_code`, `scan_spec`.
  - CLI counterparts (the same five operations as exposed by the CLI); enumerate the exact
    command names in the implementation and keep the two surfaces in lockstep (resolve the
    review/review_plan and code-review/review_code naming so coverage matches one-to-one).
- Document defaults + surface `verified_at_sha` in attested results (outputSchema/text).
- Decouple the verified-code path from the MCP server's cwd/branch; document that `REBAR_ROOT`
  only locates the object DB to fetch from.
- **Validation / failure paths** (not just happy path): an unresolvable or absent `ref`, an
  invalid `--source` value, and an unreachable/missing object DB at `REBAR_ROOT` each produce
  a clear, actionable error (attested fails closed; cf. S1 descriptive fetch/auth errors).
- **De-risk by vertical slice:** land ONE CLI command + ONE MCP tool end-to-end first
  (default `origin/main` resolve + attested `verified_at_sha` + `local`=unsigned) before
  fanning the two controls out across all five surfaces.

## Scope

- In: CLI flags, MCP tool-schema args, the pinned CLI<->MCP mapping, default wiring, failure/
  validation handling, surfacing `verified_at_sha`, the vertical-slice-first sequencing.
- Out: the underlying behavior (S1-S4); prose docs (S6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every code-reading CLI command AND its MCP tool counterpart accept `--ref`/`ref` and
      `--source`/`source` with documented defaults; the CLI<->MCP mapping covers the same five
      operations one-to-one (no naming-drift coverage gap).
- [ ] Omitting `--ref` resolves `origin/main` -> SHA (attested) and still signs (pin recorded);
      `--source=local` is reachable from both surfaces and reflected as unsigned in the result.
- [ ] Attested results surface `verified_at_sha`.
- [ ] An unresolvable/absent ref, an invalid `--source` value, and an unreachable object DB at
      `REBAR_ROOT` each return a clear actionable error (attested fails closed) — covered by tests.
- [ ] An AC verifies the cwd/branch decoupling: the verified-code path does not depend on the
      MCP server's checked-out branch; `REBAR_ROOT` only locates the object DB.
- [ ] A thin vertical slice (one CLI cmd + one MCP tool, end-to-end) lands before the full fan-out.

## Additional notes + Acceptance Criteria (advisory remediation)

- Pinned CLI<->MCP names (mirror the MCP tool names, confirm against the command registry):
  `review-plan`<->`review_plan`, `verify-completion`<->`verify_completion`,
  `review-ticket`<->`review_ticket`, `review-code`<->`review_code`, `scan-spec`<->`scan_spec`.
- `--source` default is `attested` (stated explicitly); `--ref` default is `origin/main`.
- The cross-surface contract (one-to-one CLI<->MCP mapping) and the cwd/branch decoupling
  (`REBAR_ROOT` only locates the object DB) are captured in the architecture ADR (S2/S4), so
  future maintainers don't re-couple the verified-code path to the server's checkout.
- Error recovery: each actionable error names the remedy target — an unresolvable/absent ref
  -> how to name a valid ref; an invalid `--source` -> the allowed enum; an unreachable
  `REBAR_ROOT`/object DB or missing credentials -> the setup-docs section (S6).

- [ ] The five CLI commands and five MCP tools are the pinned one-to-one set above (no
      naming-drift gap); `--source` defaults to `attested`, `--ref` to `origin/main`.
- [ ] Each failure-path error names its recovery target (valid-ref guidance / allowed --source
      enum / REBAR_ROOT+credentials docs), consistent across both surfaces.
- [ ] The cwd/branch decoupling + CLI<->MCP mapping are recorded in the architecture ADR.
baseline.summary: Surface the ref + source controls on the CLI and MCP tool schemas

Add REBAR_PUSH=always|async|off with default ALWAYS (real-time propagation is a first-order requirement); async pushes after returning, still best-effort, fsck still reports PUSH_PENDING.

(b) The mkdir-lock fallback (no-flock platforms, ticket-lib.sh) has unmeasured starvation behavior under many concurrent local agents on macOS. Add a CI stress test (N concurrent writers, assert no lost events, bounded wait).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Convergence semantics unchanged (PUSH_PENDING reporting, pre-push merge retry) under async

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
344 closed bugs exist but no lens aggregates them: close_class distribution over time, detection channel, open-bug age, caused_by fan-in (which components spawn bugs), time-to-close. Trend questions are answered today by ad-hoc scripts.

## Approach
Add a bug_trends lens to the rebar metrics registry (same _spec() registration pattern as gate-economics sidecar metrics). Dimensions: close_class distribution bucketed by close month; detected_by distribution (populated as the detected-by sibling lands — lens must degrade gracefully while the field is sparse); open-bug age percentiles; caused_by link fan-in per target; time-to-close percentiles. Surface taxonomy-window skew INSIDE the computed value payload: the close_class distribution carries an explicit labeled MISSING bucket (the pre-convention era where close_class is absent for ~214 bugs) alongside the vocabulary classes, so eras are never silently mixed. (The registry source/confidence labels are closed spec-level vocabularies and cannot express per-cohort annotations; each spec registers as source=structural, confidence=high.)

Range semantics (stock vs flow): the FLOW dimensions — close_class-by-month and time-to-close — filter on the close TRANSITION timestamp within the ctx since/until range, exactly as sibling event/sidecar metrics filter on their ranges; with the CLI default 30-day window the historical cohorts only appear when the caller widens --since (documented in the user-guide section). The STOCK dimensions — open-bug age percentiles, detected_by distribution, caused_by fan-in — are point-in-time measures over the current store and deliberately ignore the range (an age percentile or fan-in count has no flow window); this deviation from range-filtering siblings is stated here and in the module docstring.

## Scope
- src/rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py (new lens module; register() appends specs idempotently on id)
- src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py (side-effect import of the new module alongside event_metrics/git_metrics/sidecar_metrics — without it REGISTRY never sees the lens)
- docs/user-guide.md metrics section

## Testing
Happy path: synthetic store with classed+unclassed bugs -> lens returns distributions with era-skew labels. Edge: zero bugs -> 'unavailable' state per registry convention, not a crash or empty-implies-healthy. detected_by absent everywhere -> dimension reports unavailable, other dimensions unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] 'rebar metrics' exposes a bug_trends lens with the five dimensions, registered via the standard registry pattern.
- [x] Pre-convention MISSING close_class is surfaced as a labeled cohort, never silently dropped or merged.
- [x] Sparse/absent detected_by degrades that dimension to unavailable without affecting others.
- [x] Unit tests cover populated, empty, and mixed-era stores.
baseline.summary: bug_trends metrics lens (close-class, detected-by, age, caused_by fan-in, time-to-close)

# Inbound title is reverted by outbound local-wins, so a Jira-side summary edit never reaches the local ticket

## Symptom

Live against the Jira Data Center harness (run 30724309686), `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[02-edit-summary]` fails: a DC summary edit, confirmed present in the JQL index, does not reach the bound local ticket's `.title` after a clean writing pass. The sibling `[03-edit-description]` PASSES on the same fixture and the same pass, as do add/remove-label, comment, assign and unassign. The failure is title-specific.

## Proven root cause

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:38-45` defined the arbitration set as `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS = frozenset({"description", "priority", "status", "assignee"})` and its comment declared `title` "deliberately absent", on the grounds that the pre-625b differ iterated Jira-shaped keys (whose title key is `summary`, never a member of the local-named set) so title was never suppressed, and that behaviour was preserved verbatim.

The guard `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`outbound_field_diff.py:247-256`) is membership-gated on that set, and the title comparison at `outbound_field_diff.py:265-268` sat OUTSIDE every guard. So when a teammate edits the Jira summary while local is unchanged since the baseline, the outbound differ emits `title = <stale local value>`. The inbound differ then DROPS its own correct title update as a contradiction of a just-emitted outbound change for the same target: `inbound_differ.py:483-486` maps outbound `summary` to inbound `title`, and `inbound_differ.py:653-656` filters it out (bidirectional suppression, bug 3bf8).

Two consequences, only the first of which the live cell observed:

1. the Jira-side title never reaches the local ticket; and
2. the stale local title is pushed back over the Jira edit.

## Why description passes and title does not

`description` IS in the set, the fixture's local description equals the baseline, so `_suppressed_by_inbound` returns True, no outbound description is emitted, and the inbound description flows. That is the whole asymmetry.

## Authority violated

`docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md:21-31` names the arbitrated set as "the five inbound-mirrored scalar fields (title/description/priority/status/assignee)" and mandates: local == baseline means the outbound push is SUPPRESSED so the inbound differ mirrors it; local != baseline means local-wins. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:269` documents Title as syncing Jira to Local. Not DC-specific: the module is vendor-neutral, so Cloud reverts a Jira-side summary edit identically.

## Runtime proof

Driving `diff_canonical_fields` directly with local title == baseline title and a differing remote title returned `{'title': 'OLD'}`; the same call with description varied instead returned `{}`. Feeding that outbound emission into `compute_inbound_mutations` returned `[]` with `suppression_count == 1`, versus `[{'title': 'NEW-from-jira'}]` with no outbound context.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a baseline carrying `title` and local `title` matching it, a differing remote title emits NO
  outbound `title`; the inbound differ mirrors it into the local ticket.
- local `title` != baseline `title` still emits local-wins outbound (unchanged).
- No baseline, or a baseline omitting `title`, still degrades to local-wins (unchanged).
- A unit test on the LIVE canonical path (`outbound_field_diff`), not on the production-dead
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields`.
baseline.summary: inbound title reverted by outbound local-wins

## Why
With the threshold empirically derived (sibling story), flip the serious-tier code-review criteria from advisory-in-everything-but-name to actually able to BLOCK. Today only the two DET criteria (secret-detection, high-critical-security) can block; all 13 non-DET LLM criteria ship blocking_enabled: false at 0.95 — locked as the permissive-rollout invariant by ADR 0036 and pinned by tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks. The field false-block risk is demonstrably near zero (0 finding-blocks in 162 changes).

- CRITICAL DISTINCTION (the reviewer's catch): `blocking_enabled` lives on CRITERIA (the routing keys in criteria_routing.json: `security`, `api-compat`, `db-migrations`, `deletion-impact`, `tests`, `scope-intent`, …) — NOT on the consequence-BINARIES (`data_loss_without_recovery`, etc.), which are decide.py severity attributes that set a finding's IMPACT, not routing entries. So the flip is: turn `blocking_enabled: true` on the CRITERIA whose Pass-1 findings carry the serious (0.9) binaries.

## What
- DEFINITE MINIMAL SET (not a provisional mapping): consequence-binaries are scored per-finding by the verify pass (content-based), NOT "owned" by a criterion, so there is no principled binary→criterion table to write. The empirical basis for WHICH criteria are block-worthy is sibling 9f25's adjudication. Therefore this ticket flips exactly ONE criterion now: set `blocking_enabled: true` + `block_threshold` = the EXACT numeric value 9f25 records as its derived priority-crossover threshold (b9c0 is stacked ABOVE 9f25, so that number exists at implementation time; b9c0 copies it verbatim — no independent guess) on **`security`** (the AGENT criterion under which the #518-class importlib code-execution finding lands — a security finding). Every other LLM criterion stays advisory at 0.95; the two DET criteria (secret-detection, high-critical-security) stay blocking as-is.
- Any EXPANSION of the blocking set beyond `security` (e.g. api-compat, db-migrations, deletion-impact, tests) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here and gated on 9f25's per-criterion adjudication showing those criteria's findings are block-worthy at the derived threshold — filed as a follow-up if 9f25's data supports it, NOT guessed here. (This is why #539-class correctness findings — which have no clean owning criterion in the overlay set — are not force-mapped.)
- Update ADR 0036 (dated note: permissive rollout concluded for `security`, evidence attached) and ALL THREE blocking-set pinning tests, each updated to the new approved set `{secret-detection, high-critical-security, security}` and each still asserting NO OTHER criterion blocks: `tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks`, `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py` — ALL THREE test functions that pin `security` as advisory/non-blocking break when `security` flips and must be updated: `test_threshold_for_default_overlay_is_advisory_at_095` (L39 `reg.threshold_for(["security"]) == (0.95, False)`), `test_threshold_for_takes_min_threshold_and_any_blocking` (L52 `reg.threshold_for(["security","performance"]) == (0.95, False)`), and `test_secrets_security_keys_are_the_ws5_blocking_handoff` (L64 `set(blocking)`), AND `tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` (lines ~102/104 pin `deletion-impact` blocking_enabled is False — which stays False under this minimal set, so that test's assertion is UNCHANGED but must be confirmed to still hold).
- Keep pass-3 separation intact: this is a threshold/posture CONFIG change only — no decide.py math changes.
- NOTE: this depends on 9f25's derived threshold; if 9f25's honest crossover comes out ABOVE 0.54/0.60, AC4's "#518-class findings now BLOCK" is revisited with 9f25's actual number (do not force a threshold to satisfy the AC — the epic's Definitions record this contingency).

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json, tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py, tests/unit/test_code_review_ws2.py + tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py (the second and third blocking-set pinning tests), docs/adr/0036-*.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md (the cross-gate posture note), tests/unit/test_code_review_blocking_replay.py (self-contained serious-vs-NIT blocking replay). Depends on the derivation story 9f25 (consumes its derived threshold + its code-review derivation/replay script).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `security` criterion has blocking_enabled: true at the derived block_threshold in criteria_routing.json; all other LLM criteria remain advisory at 0.95 (expansion beyond `security` is deferred to 9f25's data).
- [ ] ALL THREE blocking-set pinning tests assert the new approved set `{secret-detection, high-critical-security, security}` and each fails on any unapproved addition: test_impact_model_versioning.py::test_code_review_only_det_security_criteria_are_hard_blocks, test_code_review_ws2.py (all three security-pinning functions: test_threshold_for_default_overlay_is_advisory_at_095, test_threshold_for_takes_min_threshold_and_any_blocking, test_secrets_security_keys_are_the_ws5_blocking_handoff), and test_code_review_deletion_impact.py (confirm its `deletion-impact blocking_enabled is False` assertion still holds under the minimal set).
- [ ] ADR 0036 carries a dated enablement note citing derivation ticket 9f25.
- [ ] A SELF-CONTAINED replay proves #518-class (security) findings now BLOCK under the now-blocking `security` criterion while false-blocks stay 0 — WITHOUT depending on any sibling's not-yet-built script. Proving artifact (owned by this ticket): a unit test `tests/unit/test_code_review_blocking_replay.py` that (a) constructs a handful of finding decision-inputs — the per-finding {criterion:'security', validity, severity_attributes/impact} dicts that `pass3_decide`/`reg.threshold_for` actually consume (NOT the code_review_result_v1 sidecar bucket JSON, which is the persistence shape, not the decision input) — modelling a couple of #518-class (importlib code-execution) security findings at their real priority plus a set of low-priority NIT findings, and (b) runs them through `reg.threshold_for(['security'])` + the priority≥threshold block decision with the flipped config, asserting the security findings block (priority ≥ derived threshold, blocking=True) while the NIT set yields 0 blocks. Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_blocking_replay.py -q`. (9f25 owns the corpus-wide adjudication + derivation; this AC only proves the config change makes qualifying findings block.) If 9f25's honest threshold cannot make these findings block without false-blocks, this AC is renegotiated against 9f25's data rather than forced.
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make typecheck passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.
baseline.summary: Enable the code-review blocking lane for serious-tier criteria at the derived threshold

## Problem / context
A subagent recently fast-forwarded the SHARED main checkout (/Users/joeoakhart/rebar) to satisfy a `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed`, clobbering uncommitted operator WIP. Root cause: the close's completion precheck reads the CLOSING checkout's git history and needs the merged `rebar-ticket:` commit reachable from HEAD, and our contributor guidance never told authors to fast-forward THEIR OWN WORKTREE (only) after a Gerrit merge.

Grounded mechanism (verified): `_referencing_commit_exists` runs `git log` over `repo_root` (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:32-57), called at :153-161 with the "cannot confirm the work landed" error; the completion verifier is invoked with `ref="HEAD"` (:186).

## Scope
DOCUMENTATION ONLY. No `src/rebar` code changes; no new flag/parameter on transition/close. Edit only Markdown docs (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md). Docs-only is the intended fix here (operator-set constraint) — the mechanism is correct; only the human/agent-facing guidance was missing.

## Plan
1. AGENTS.md — in the "Git workflow — land changes THROUGH GERRIT" section, near the close-discipline bullet, add a bullet: after a change MERGES and BEFORE the ticket close, `git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main` from inside the worktree; NEVER fast-forward/reset/stash the shared main checkout (it may hold operator WIP) — advance your worktree or a throwaway worktree at origin/main instead.
2. CONTRIBUTING.md — insert a NEW subsection §2f ("After merge — fast-forward your worktree, THEN close the ticket") immediately after the existing §2e (Submit); there is no pre-existing §2f. It carries the same two-part guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: AGENTS.md carries the post-merge fast-forward-your-worktree guidance AND the "never touch the shared main checkout" warning. Verify (both must hit): `grep -nF 'merge --ff-only origin/main' AGENTS.md` and `grep -niF 'shared main checkout' AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] AC2: CONTRIBUTING.md's landing recipe carries the same two-part guidance in a new §2f. Verify (all must hit): `grep -nF 'merge --ff-only origin/main' CONTRIBUTING.md`, `grep -niF 'shared main checkout' CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `grep -nF '2f.' CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] AC3: ZERO code changes — the diff touches only Markdown. Verify: `git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD` lists only `*.md` paths (no `src/rebar` path present).
- [ ] AC4: The pre-commit gate passes on the change. Verify: `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] AC5 [operator-attested]: the change lands via Gerrit (`LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`, then Submit/MERGED) and the ticket is closed from the FAST-FORWARDED worktree, without the shared main checkout being touched. Attestation evidence recorded on the ticket: the Gerrit change number, the MERGED status, and a comment confirming the worktree-only close.
baseline.summary: docs: post-merge close discipline — fast-forward your worktree, never the main checkout

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Ticket T is locally parentless (parent_id None) and bound to Jira.
2. A human sets an epic/parent P on T directly in Jira.
3. Run a reconcile pass.
**Expected:** local ADOPTS P (the prior behavior), since rebar never managed a parent for T.

**Actual (after PR #54 / drum-ruler-suit):** outbound emits a parent CLEAR unconditionally (local detached + Jira has a parent), DELETING the human's parent and suppressing inbound adoption. The un-gated CLEAR inverts the old adopt behavior into a clobber.
## Root Cause

The parent CLEAR added in PR #54 (`outbound_differ._map_local_to_jira_fields`, the `emit_detach_clear` branch) fires whenever local is detached and Jira has a parent — with no provenance check. It cannot distinguish 'we deliberately detached a parent we managed' from 'a human just set a parent we never managed'.
## Design (consumes the shared managed-ref gate from parent story safe-luge-nog)

Gate the parent CLEAR through the SAME `should_propagate_removal` provenance gate as links: emit the CLEAR only when the Jira parent ref is in `managed_refs` (we managed it, user detached) — otherwise ADOPT it inbound (the restored prior behavior). One shared pattern across parent + links.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The parent CLEAR is emitted ONLY when the Jira parent is in the ticket's `managed_refs` (a parent we managed, then detached).
- [ ] A human-set Jira parent on a locally-parentless, never-managed ticket is ADOPTED inbound, not cleared (regression test).
- [ ] A genuinely-detached managed parent still emits the CLEAR and converges (the drum-ruler-suit behavior preserved), incl. across a compaction boundary.
- [ ] Parent + link removal share the same gate helper (no duplicated provenance logic).

baseline.summary: Parent CLEAR is un-gated: clobbers a human-set-in-Jira parent on a locally-parentless ticket

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar's three LLM review gates — plan-review, code-review, and completion-verification — each
produce a rich internal record, but only a fraction is durably captured today:

- Plan-review and code-review run a shared four-pass kernel (find → verify → decide → coach) and
  emit a reducer-ignored `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar. The plan-review sidecar drops the pass-1
  `evidence` and `scenarios` fields; the code-review sidecar persists only the *surfaced* findings
  (blocking + advisory + coaching) and omits the dropped / indeterminate / overflow buckets. Neither
  persists the numeric `block_threshold` a finding was judged against — it is resolved from the
  criteria registry at decision time and then discarded.
- Completion-verification is single-pass and emits a sidecar ONLY on FAIL; a PASS persists just
  signed counts, so a successful close leaves no per-criterion audit record.
- All review sidecars are pruned to the most recent 10 per ticket.

A downstream feature (the ticket audit-trail UI, a separate follow-on epic) needs a COMPLETE,
self-contained audit record. This epic makes the stored audit data lossless and readable; it builds
NO UI. The read layer it ships also makes the audit data scriptable via CLI/MCP — valuable on its own.

## Approach rationale

Enrich the existing observability sidecars in place (new schema versions) rather than introduce a
new persistence mechanism — the sidecar path is already the durable, reducer-ignored, retained
record every review writes, so extending its payload is the lowest-blast-radius way to capture the
missing data. The signed attestation manifest is deliberately left carrying counts only (its
integrity contract is out of scope); this epic enriches observability, not the signature.

## Scope

- IN: sidecar payload enrichment (plan + code), completion PASS-path capture + agent
  output-contract change, retention-cap change, the audit read layer.
- OUT: any web UI or rendering (the follow-on epic); asymmetric-key signing; changing what is
  SIGNED (attestations still carry counts only).

## Compatibility & rollback

Sidecar schemas are bumped (`plan_review_result_v2` / `code_review_result_v2` / a completion `_v2`);
readers accept BOTH the old `v1` (rendered with the new fields absent) and the new `v2` records, so
pre-existing reviews stay readable and no backfill is required. Each change is inert until it next
runs; reverting a story restores the prior payload shape with no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed.
- [ ] After this epic, a freshly-run plan-review and code-review each write a `*_v2` sidecar whose
      payload contains every pass-1 finding across all buckets with its pass-2 verification, its
      pass-3 validity/impact/priority/decision/reason, the resolved numeric `block_threshold`, and
      the pass-4 coaching. Oracle: an integration test runs a review and asserts on the emitted event
      JSON.
- [ ] A completion-verification PASS emits a per-criterion audit record. Oracle: a test asserting on
      the emitted completion event.
- [ ] The audit read layer returns the full retained history for a ticket and its `relates_to`-linked
      code reviews. Oracle: an integration test seeding a ticket's histories and asserting the
      aggregate contains all of them.
- [ ] Every new plan-review and code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar captures the full four-pass record:
- [ ] A completion-verification PASS persists a per-criterion audit record (not only counts).
- [ ] Review-sidecar retention is raised so a ticket's review history is deep enough to audit.
- [ ] A documented read API (library + CLI + MCP) returns the full retained audit history for a ticket
baseline.summary: Audit data enrichment — lossless capture of review passes

# Parallelize the container fan-out with warm-then-fan-out + fix the centrality budget cap

## Why
The container loop is sequential (`2*N` calls ≈ 27 min wall-clock). Parallelizing fixes latency. But caching
(S1) is write-once/read-many — a NAIVE concurrent fan-out makes all calls MISS+WRITE (≈20x input cost, no read
benefit). So parallelization must WARM the cache first. Separately, the per-plan budget cap scales UP with child
count (centrality), disabling shedding for exactly the large epics that need it.

## What
- Move the container pairings out of the sequential `for crit: for child:` loop into the existing
  `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`pass1.py`).
- WARM-THEN-FAN-OUT: run ONE warming call first, await its first streamed token (the cache becomes readable once
  the first response begins), THEN fan out the remaining pairings concurrently so they READ the cached prefix
  rather than all re-writing it. (Optional: a pre-warm call at gate start.)
- Fix the budget cap that scales with centrality (`sizing.py` `base*(1+centrality)`) so shedding engages for
  large epics instead of being disabled by the very signal (more children) that should trigger it.

## Scope
- In: container parallelization; the warm-then-fan-out sequencing; the budget-cap fix.
- Out: the caching mechanism (S1, dependency); merge (S4); bin-pack (S5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Container pairings run concurrently in the thread pool (not the sequential loop).
- [ ] Warm-then-fan-out: one call warms the cache before the fan-out; on anthropic the fanned-out calls show
      `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` (NOT all writes) — proven by a test/measurement.
- [ ] The per-plan budget cap no longer disables shedding as child count grows (a large epic sheds as intended).
- [ ] An 8-child epic review wall-clock drops to minutes; `make lint` + tests pass.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 4/5)
- The runner is NON-streaming (`run_sync` blocks). Warm = run ONE pairing TO COMPLETION, then fan out the rest —
  not "await first streamed token". The warm pairing is the FIRST REAL pairing; keep its findings; fan out the
  remaining N-1; aggregate must equal the sequential baseline (no dup/drop).
- There is NO open ThreadPoolExecutor at `_run_container` (the Pass-1 pool closed at pass1.py:336). Create a NEW
  pool inside `_run_container`.
- Gate warming on `est_tokens(plan) >= 4096` (cache floor; reuse det_floor.est_tokens) — else fan out directly
  (no warm), since a sub-floor prefix never caches and warming would just add a serialized call.
- Warm-call failure: systemic (LLMUnavailableError) -> abort like the Pass-1 tier (pass1.py:327-331); non-systemic
  -> degrade to a direct fan-out (accept all-miss), never hang.
- Budget cap: do NOT invert centrality — shedding marks G3/G4 INDETERMINATE, so the naive "fix" would DROP
  child-coverage/consistency on the most central epics (a fidelity regression the epic AC forbids). Instead:
  container criteria are NEVER shed; the cap bounds only overlay/agent spend; correct the COST MODEL
  (sizing.py:206 `len(cont)*n_children*COST_AGENT`) rather than the centrality scaling.
- [ ] Warm = first real pairing run to completion; aggregate finding set equals the sequential baseline (no dup/drop).
- [ ] A NEW thread pool runs the remaining pairings concurrently; on anthropic the fanned-out calls show cache_read>0.
- [ ] Warming is skipped when est_tokens(plan) < 4096 (fan out directly); warm-call systemic failure aborts,
      non-systemic failure degrades to direct fan-out.
- [ ] Container criteria are NEVER shed by the budget cap; the cap bounds only overlay/agent spend (numeric target stated).
baseline.summary: Parallelize the container fan-out with warm-then-fan-out + fix the centrality budget cap

## Reported by, not investigated by, an adjacent session

Surfaced while confirming the fix for bug 8070 (external-integration canary). Per operator instruction this was NOT investigated — epic 061c is actively held by another session and owns the LLM provider seam. Filing it here so the owning session sees it. **No root cause is claimed.**

## Observed (live CI, reproducible)

Run 30651750699 — `workflow_dispatch` of `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` on `main` at commit `b7e6ac963`, 2026-07-31. Job **"external integration (live services)"**, two distinct failures:

```
tests/external/test_execution_mode_live.py:44
  assert res["status"] == "succeeded"
  AssertionError: {'run_id': '1785519373801819646-69026a0039094ff98b649bf175f16356',
                   'ticket_id': None, 'workflow_name': 'live_single_turn', 'status': 'failed', ...}
  assert 'failed' == 'succeeded'
```

# CI: `cast Verified` casts NO vote when workflow-conclusion aggregation resolves to `skipped` — green CI leaves the change un-landable

## Summary

The `cast Verified` job in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (~lines 442-468) aggregates
this run's job conclusions via `im-open/workflow-conclusion@v3.0.0` into `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`,
then casts the Gerrit `Verified` label from it (`vote-type: ${{ env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION }}`,
success→+1, failure|cancelled→-1). When the aggregation resolves to **`skipped`** — even though
every real CI job SUCCEEDED — the cast step aborts with
`##[error]Unknown vote-type 'skipped': expected clear, success, failure or cancelled` (exit 1),
so **no `Verified` vote is posted at all**. The change then sits at `Verified = (none)` and is
un-submittable despite fully-green CI, until a human notices and comments `recheck`. Two defects
compound here:

1. **The aggregation can yield `skipped` spuriously.** The workflow's own comment (lines ~444-447)
   notes `im-open/workflow-conclusion` takes a REST list-jobs *snapshot* that depends on the
   needed jobs being terminal first; a timing/ordering race can fold a not-yet-finalized job in
   as `skipped`, producing an overall `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION=skipped` while the jobs are actually
   green.
2. **The cast step is not robust to an unexpected conclusion.** `skipped` (and any value outside
   `clear|success|failure|cancelled`) hard-errors the job instead of failing safe — so a transient
   aggregation glitch becomes a **silent no-vote block** (the change looks stuck, not failed),
   rather than a clear `-1` or an automatic retry.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Push a change to `refs/for/main` whose CI is fully green.
2. Observe (occasionally) that all CI matrix/optionality/golden-path jobs succeed, but the final
   `cast Verified` job FAILS with `Unknown vote-type 'skipped'`, and the Gerrit `Verified` label
   stays unset.
3. Comment `recheck`; the re-run casts `Verified +1` normally.

**Observed instance:** change 743 (`eclectic-spotted-barb`), GitHub Actions run 29540921742.
Jobs: `CI (ubuntu, py3.11/3.12/3.13)`, `CI (macos, py3.13)`, `golden-path`, all `optionality`,
`require resolvable rebar ticket` = **success**; only `cast Verified` = **failure**
(`WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION: skipped`, `VOTE_TYPE: skipped` → exit 1). No `Verified` vote posted.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** green CI casts `Verified +1` deterministically; a transient aggregation hiccup
  either resolves to the true conclusion or fails in a way that still lands a vote / auto-retries,
  never leaving a green change silently voteless.
- **Actual:** an aggregation that resolves to `skipped` aborts the cast job, posting no `Verified`
  vote; the change is stuck until a manual `recheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `cast Verified` step handles a `skipped`/unexpected `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION` without
  leaving the change voteless — e.g. it re-resolves the true conclusion (re-query after all needed
  jobs are terminal), or maps an unexpected value to a safe, actionable outcome (retry, or a clear
  `-1` with a diagnostic), never a bare exit-1 that posts nothing.
  - Proving: a run whose aggregation would resolve `skipped` still results in a posted `Verified`
    vote (or an explicit retry), verified against `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The aggregation is hardened against the terminal-ordering race (the needed jobs are
  guaranteed terminal before the snapshot, or the snapshot ignores `skipped` when successes exist),
  so `WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION` reflects the real conclusion.
- [ ] A regression guard (workflow unit/lint or a documented manual check) covers the
  `skipped`-conclusion path.

## Notes

Discovered while landing the enrich-queue prune race fix (`eclectic-spotted-barb`, change 743):
all CI green, but `Verified` never posted due to this. Not a defect in that change's code — a
pre-existing CI-orchestration flake. Worked around via `recheck`.
baseline.summary: CI: `cast Verified` casts NO vote when workflow-conclusion aggregation resolves to `skipped` — green CI leaves the change un-landable
