## Why
The plan-review claim gate consumes the SIGNED attestation `rebar review-plan` produces on a non-blocking PASS. An agent that hand-optimizes away the signing (or defers it to a guessed 'final round') can leave tickets without the attestation the claim gate needs. Local guidance was added to CLAUDE.local.md; this shares the same positive framing with all contributors via the committed CLAUDE.md.

## What
Append to the Plan-review protocol in CLAUDE.md a positive instruction: run `rebar review-plan <id>` as documented so it signs on every non-blocking PASS; sign on every round (signing is free; the last round is not knowable; remediation harmlessly staleness-invalidates the prior attestation on read).

## Scope
Docs only (CLAUDE.md). Positive framing — avoids priming the anti-pattern by naming it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLAUDE.md Plan-review protocol states plan review signs an attestation on every non-blocking PASS and to sign on every round.
- [ ] Framed as a positive instruction (does not tell agents which flag NOT to use).
- [ ] make lint / pre-commit pass; lands on main via Gerrit (Verified +1).
baseline.summary: Add plan-review always-signs guidance to committed CLAUDE.md (positive framing)

baseline.description:
## Why

13 Jira issues are pinned at Jira's 5000-comment HARD cap, inflated by the pre-P1
non-idempotent re-posting bug (local truth 22-76 distinct comments each; Jira holds ~65
copies of each until it hit 5000). P1 (landed a6cdad0e2) STOPS new duplication, but the caps
remain — so NEW comments on these 13 tickets still silently fail to sync
(`COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`) until the duplicates are purged.

13 issues (rebar-id -> Jira key, local-distinct / Jira-total): REB-155(5fd2, 76/5000),
REB-352(e0e2, 64), REB-428(8937, 31), REB-341(db7b, 30), REB-289(b744, 29), REB-427(822a, 27),
REB-183(7284, 25), REB-327(d251, 25), REB-424(2359, 25), REB-425(33d0, 25), REB-190(75a9, 22),
REB-426(59ef, 22), REB-453(b4d4, 22).

## Concrete mechanisms (resolve the plan-review blocks — code-grounded, reused not reinvented)

**Bot-authored identification (safety-critical filter).** Jira REST returns each comment `body`
as an Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict, NOT a plain string, so the marker must be detected on
the RENDERED text, never by substring-searching the raw ADF object. A comment is
bridge-bot-authored IFF `adf.adf_to_text(body)` contains the reconciler marker
`RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py:43`), appended to every outbound
comment by `_decorate_outbound_comment` (`:140-147`) as its own paragraph — which survives the
ADF round-trip and re-renders to the literal marker text (`outbound_comments.py:144-145`). Reuse
`adf.adf_to_text` (the same renderer `_normalize_comment_body` uses) to render before the marker
check; note `_normalize_comment_body` STRIPS the marker for the dedup key, so marker DETECTION
uses the pre-strip rendered text while the dedup GROUPING uses the marker-stripped normalized
text. This intrinsic marker is the PRIMARY and authoritative identifier — robust to accountId /
display-name changes, unlike an author field. A comment whose rendered text lacks the marker is
treated as human/foreign and is NEVER a deletion candidate.
Secondary cross-check: the backup captures every comment's `author.accountId`; the script
asserts that all marked (candidate) comments across the 13 tickets resolve to a single bot
`accountId` and records it — a divergent accountId on a marked comment aborts the run for
manual review (defense in depth; the marker still governs).

**Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization (parity guarantee).** Group candidate comments
by `outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body)` — imported and reused verbatim, NOT
re-implemented — which does ADF->text via `adf.adf_to_text` then strips the marker and
leading/trailing whitespace (`outbound_comments.py:116-137`). Using the identical function the
reconciler uses to decide "already mirrored" guarantees the cleanup's notion of "distinct body"
matches the reconciler's, so post-cleanup the reconciler sees exactly one copy per distinct body
and emits zero re-adds. Machine-canary comments (`_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES`:
"BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:", "Still stale as of") carry volatile timestamps -> each is a distinct
normalized body -> each is kept (never a "duplicate" to purge) — correct and safe.

**Pagination (fetch ALL 5000, not the first page).** Reuse the live-validated
`acli.py::get_comments(key)` with `--paginate` + `_parse_paginated_comments` (the P1 fix,
confirmed returning 5000/5000 for REB-155) to build the full comment set for backup + delete-list.
Do NOT hand-roll a single-page fetch. NOTE: `_parse_paginated_comments` returns only a flat
`list[dict]` and DISCARDS the response envelope, so it does NOT surface Jira's reported `total`.
The completeness check therefore obtains the total via a SEPARATE, dedicated metadata call —
`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?maxResults=0` returns `{total, maxResults, startAt,
comments: []}`; the script reads `total` from that envelope (new script-level work, not provided
by the reuse target) and reconciles `len(fetched) == total` per ticket, REFUSING to proceed if
they differ (guards a silently-truncated fetch producing an incomplete/dangerous delete list).

**Keep-one rule.** For each distinct normalized body among MARKED comments on a ticket: keep the
OLDEST copy (min `created` timestamp) and delete the rest via
`DELETE /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment/{id}`. A distinct body with only ONE marked copy is
NEVER deleted. Unmarked (human) comments are never touched.

**Rate limiting + transient-failure handling.** Jira Cloud enforces API rate limits over
~64k+ DELETEs (≈4900 × 13). Throttle to a conservative default (≤10 req/s, i.e. ≥100ms
inter-call sleep). IMPORTANT: the existing `_direct_rest_delete` -> `_rest_urlopen_with_retry`
path does NOT retry HTTP 429/5xx — it re-raises 4xx/5xx immediately as deterministic
(`acli_rest.py:62-64`). SINGLE chosen route (no alternatives): wrap each DELETE call through
`dispatch_one._call_with_retry`, which is the repo's one existing 429+Retry-After-aware retry
(honors `Retry-After`, exponential backoff). Do NOT hand-roll a second retry layer. Deletions
are logged (ticket, comment id, normalized-body hash, outcome) to an append-only artifact
`artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` (one JSON object per line) as they happen, so a
mid-run rate-limit stall is resumable.

**Idempotent + resumable.** Re-running is safe: a comment already deleted (404 on DELETE) is
treated as success. On partial failure, re-run `--dry-run` to see the remaining duplicates and
resume `--execute`; the keep-one grouping is recomputed from the live paginated set each run.

**Rollback (irreversible-op mitigation).** Jira comment deletion cannot be undone via API. The
pre-deletion backup JSON (id, body, author, created, per ticket) is the restore artifact.
Concrete restore procedure: a `--restore <backup.json> --ticket <key>` script mode re-POSTs each
DELETED comment's ADF body (`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment`, cross-referencing the
deletions-<ts>.jsonl log to restore only what THIS run deleted). Target state after restore: the
ticket again holds one instance of each restored distinct body (content-restore, NOT id-restore —
re-created comments get NEW ids/timestamps, and the reconciler marker is re-appended by the
normal outbound decorate path on the next sync). The backup MUST exist and pass its completeness
check before any DELETE fires. Because restore only re-creates content (not the exact 5000-copy
inflated state), rollback is a safety net for accidental over-deletion, not a bit-exact undo.

## What — irreversible; execute ONLY under this T4 safety plan (inlined)

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup:** export FULL comment payload (id, body, author.accountId,
      author.displayName, created) for all 13 tickets to a versioned JSON artifact under
      `artifacts/jira-cleanup/backup-<ts>.json` BEFORE any deletion. Proving command: the script
      asserts, per ticket, `len(backup[key]) == jira_reported_total` and that the artifact is
      non-empty and parses; deletion is refused if the assertion fails.
- [ ] **Dry-run default:** the script defaults to `--dry-run`; it prints, per ticket, the count
      of marked comments, the count of distinct normalized bodies, the kept (oldest) id per body,
      and the delete-id count — and a machine-readable diff artifact. `--execute` is required to
      delete and runs ONLY after explicit human approval of the dry-run diff.
- [ ] **Keep-one dedup:** oldest-`created` kept per distinct normalized body; marker-authored
      only; single-copy bodies and all unmarked comments excluded (per mechanisms above).
- [ ] **Operator flow / rejection:** dry-run -> human review -> approve|reject. On reject or
      abort, NO deletion occurs and the run exits cleanly (backup + dry-run artifacts retained).
- [ ] **Sequencing:** run ONLY after P1 is live in the reconciler (CONFIRMED: reconcile-bridge
      run 29625135085 on commit a6cdad0e2 = green) — else the reconciler re-inflates within
      minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Backup artifact exists and passes its per-ticket completeness check — `len(fetched)` from
      the paginated `get_comments` equals `total` read from the dedicated
      `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?maxResults=0` envelope — BEFORE any deletion. Proving
      command: `python -m json.tool artifacts/jira-cleanup/backup-<ts>.json >/dev/null` + the
      script's count-reconciliation log line per ticket.
- [ ] Dry-run diff (delete-id list + kept-oldest-id per distinct body, per ticket) is produced
      and human-approved before `--execute`. [operator-attested]
- [ ] Deletion filter provably respects: (a) marked-only (RECONCILER_MARKER present), (b)
      keep-oldest-per-distinct-body, (c) never single-copy, (d) never unmarked/human. A unit test
      over a synthetic comment set asserts the delete-list the planner computes matches (a)-(d);
      RED if the filter mislabels a human/unmarked or single-copy comment as deletable.
- [ ] Rate-limit safety: the DELETE loop routes through `dispatch_one._call_with_retry`
      (the single chosen 429/Retry-After route); a unit test asserts a 429 is retried (not
      dropped) and `Retry-After` is honored.
- [ ] Completeness-gate enforcement: a unit test asserts the script REFUSES to proceed (non-zero
      exit, no DELETE issued) when the paginated fetched-count != the `?maxResults=0` reported
      `total` for any ticket (guards a silently-truncated fetch).
- [ ] accountId cross-check: a unit test asserts (a) a marked comment whose `author.accountId`
      diverges from the single resolved bot accountId ABORTS the run for manual review (no DELETE),
      and (b) a homogeneous marked set records the bot accountId and proceeds.
- [ ] Approval-gate enforcement: a unit/integration test asserts `--dry-run` (default) issues
      ZERO DELETE calls, and that `--execute` is the ONLY path that issues DELETEs; on operator
      reject/abort no DELETE is issued and artifacts are retained.
- [ ] Reconciler quiescing during `--execute`: the run window is coordinated so the live
      reconciler does not write to the 13 tickets mid-deletion (either the pass cadence is paused,
      or the window is chosen between passes). [operator-attested]
- [ ] Post-execution, each of the 13 tickets is below the 5000 cap AND a reconcile pass emits 0
      comment re-adds for them (idempotent steady state). [operator-attested against a green
      reconcile-bridge run]
- [ ] The deletion-log artifact `artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` (one JSON object per
      line: ticket, comment id, normalized-body hash, outcome) exists for the executed run.
      Proving command: `wc -l artifacts/jira-cleanup/deletions-<ts>.jsonl` matches the reported
      delete count.
baseline.summary: Jira data cleanup: purge duplicate comments on the 13 capped tickets (after P1 deploys; dry-run+approval first)

baseline.description:
## Context
The plan-review gate (`5fd2`) reviews ONE ticket's plan in isolation. It deliberately does NOT detect SEMANTIC overlap, duplication, or undeclared dependencies BETWEEN SEPARATE tickets across the store. Existing coverage is partial and different in kind: `G4` checks consistency WITHIN one epic's children; `next_batch` schedules around DETERMINISTIC file-impact conflicts; `duplicates`/`supersedes` are MANUAL links. The residual — semantic overlap / duplication / hidden cross-ticket dependency across UNRELATED tickets — is uncovered.

## Scope
A store-wide overlap detector for the ticket UNDER PLAN REVIEW, comparing it against the whole store (cross-epic AND non-epic; any other ticket may overlap). It runs as a distinct STORE-WIDE step during the plan-review invocation window (before claim), NOT as a per-ticket `5fd2` criterion — a per-ticket reviewer cannot see the whole store, which is exactly why this is a separate step. It is ADVISORY ONLY and never affects the claim-gate verdict.

## Design (plan of record — full detail + research + experiment evidence in the comments)
Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank: (0) each ticket gets a cached, LLM-extracted Cupid digest (no embeddings, no vector DB); (1) brute-force BM25F over corpus digests narrows to ~20 candidates, excluding the query ticket's own graph; (2) a bounded LLM pairwise judge classifies each candidate and surfaces ≤3 advisory link suggestions for human confirmation. Enrichment is async via an event-sourced queue drained opportunistically (Tier 1). Child stories S1–S7 implement it; Tier-2/Tier-3 drain and a Jira-reconciler drain are spun out as linked ideas.

### Derisking experiments (run 2026-07-09 — see the experiment-results comment)
- **Recall (the load-bearing bet): VALIDATED.** digest-BM25F retrieved 8/8 heavy paraphrases at rank 1, recall@20 = 1.0, STABLE as corpus grew 60→200 (raw-BM25 baseline decayed 0.875→0.75). No embedding stage is needed for recall. Caveat: N=8 (≥0.8 demonstrated, not 1.0 guaranteed); the residual risk is PRECISION at scale, which the S6 judge is the mitigation for.
- **Latency: VALIDATED.** brute-force BM25F single-query top-20 = 0.69 ms at 800 digests (~14× under the 10 ms budget) → no ANN / vector DB.
- **Enrichment economics: VALIDATED.** ~$0.0024/ticket, ≈ $1.90 one-time for all 793 tickets, cached and re-run only on edit.
- **Store primitives: CONFIRMED.** the manual write-lock (`lock.acquire`/`LockHandle`, `txn.py` precedent) supports the queue's read-check-append AND atomic enqueue; `_ticket_text` is the canonical hash normalizer to reuse; Windows detach requires an `os.name` guard (API-derisked, not live-tested).

## Config placement (consistent across ALL children)
The single gate ENABLE flag `overlap_enabled` (bool) lives on `VerifyConfig` (`_config_schema.py` `[tool.rebar][verify]`, with its `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer). ALL other tunables (proposition bounds, BM25F weights, K, max_doc_freq, conf_threshold, surface_cap, soak, lease, drain mode/batch) are LLM-feature tunables and live on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — `_config_schema.py` reserves `llm.*` for that layer, so tunables must NOT go on `VerifyConfig`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Detects semantic overlap/duplication between separate tickets store-wide (cross-epic AND non-epic), beyond deterministic file-impact and manual links (delivered across S1–S7).
- [ ] Surfaces ≤3 candidate duplicate/supersede/dependency relations for human confirmation with copy-paste `rebar link` commands; does not auto-mutate links (S6, S7).
- [ ] Runs as a store-wide step during the plan-review window; advisory-only; does NOT run as a `5fd2` per-ticket criterion and does NOT affect the claim-gate verdict (S7).
- [ ] The architecture is captured in an ADR under docs/adr/ (owned by S7).
- [ ] For the ticket under review, overlap is detected against every non-graph-excluded ticket in the store (cross-epic AND non-epic), beyond deterministic file-impact and manual links — measured by the S6 labeled precision/recall fixture.
- [ ] Candidate `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`depends_on` relations are surfaced for HUMAN confirmation (each with a ready-to-run `rebar link` command); the tool NEVER auto-mutates links. Rationale for suggestion-only: link semantics require human judgment of intent, and a false auto-link corrupts the dependency graph that `ready`/`next_batch`/the completion gate depend on — a false suggestion costs one ignored line, a false auto-link costs silent graph corruption.
- [ ] Low false-flagging of legitimately-related-but-distinct work: precision is measured on a labeled fixture of ticket pairs (S6), and a related-but-distinct pair must not be surfaced. (This is the experiment-identified residual risk; S6 is its owner.)
- [ ] It is a store-wide step run during the plan-review window, advisory-only, never blocking or altering the claim-gate verdict.
- [ ] An ADR (docs/adr/) captures the architecture (Cupid-digest-without-embeddings, event-store-as-enrichment-queue, digest-as-REVIEW_RESULT-style-sidecar, overlap-at-review-time-not-as-a-5fd2-criterion) — DELIVERED in child S7 (precious-spy-hellbender).
baseline.summary: Cross-ticket overlap & dependency detection (store-wide: cross-epic + non-epic) — outside the plan-review gate

baseline.description:
# Single-source the ticket-type map and extend the one-literal guard to cover it

## Context

This is the SAME defect class as the just-closed bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61, still live in a third map — and the guard that was supposed to prevent recurrence does not cover it.

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` enforces "exactly one dict literal defines each value map within `adapters/`" for the STATUS map (`test_exactly_one_status_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:300`) and the PRIORITY map (`test_exactly_one_priority_map_literal_within_adapters`, the assert at `:308`). There is no such assertion for the TICKET-TYPE map, and it is duplicated:

* `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE: dict[str, str] = {...}`, read at
  `:129` for the Cloud create path.
* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": ...}`,
  read at `:61` for the DC create path.

Both were verified present in the tree. `config.py:11` also references a `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` in a comment, which is worth checking for a third copy while doing this.

### Every consumer of the symbol, enumerated

A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them:

1. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:88` — definition (Cloud). Moves.
2. `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:129` — Cloud create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
3. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:43` — definition (DC). Moves.
4. `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:61` — DC create-path read. Unchanged if the alias is kept.
5. `rebar_reconciler/config.py:11` — a COMMENT only, no literal. Confirms there is no third copy in
   config; the finding is recorded here so the check need not be repeated.
6. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:8` — a
   docstring mention. No code impact.
7. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py:87` —
   **a live external consumer**: `assert "session_log" not in _of._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`, where `_of`
   is the `outbound_fields` module. This reads the name as a MODULE-LEVEL ATTRIBUTE on
   `outbound_fields`. If the relocation leaves the canonical map bound only under a new name (e.g.
   `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`) or referenced inline, this test breaks with `AttributeError`.

**Required binding strategy (this is not optional):** in `outbound_fields.py`, import the canonical map under the historical private name, exactly as J2 did for the other two maps at `outbound_fields.py:35-36`:

```python
from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA as _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE
```

That keeps `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` resolvable, so site 7 and the create-path read at site 2 need no edit. The DC backend gets the same treatment for its own call site. If the implementer instead chooses to rename, then site 7 MUST be updated in the same change and the suite re-run to prove it — the choice is free, leaving site 7 broken is not.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The two copies are read by the two CREATE paths. A divergence means the same local ticket type becomes a different Jira issue type depending on deployment — silently, at creation, with no comparison anywhere that would notice. fe15's status map had already drifted by one key (`"deleted"`) before anyone looked; there is no reason to assume this one is luckier, and nothing would tell us.

## Approach

Follow the **J2** pattern (story 62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743), which is the established local idiom for a map that lives on BOTH sides of the `adapters/` boundary and was reviewed when it landed: relocate the single definition into `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` alongside `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` and `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`, have both create paths import it under an alias, then extend the boundary guard so a future third copy fails the build.

Note explicitly that fe15 is NOT the precedent to copy for the mechanism, only for the defect class. fe15 deliberately used a **parity test rather than a shared import**, because its third copy lived in `rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a zero-dependency core module that must not import a vendor adapter package. That constraint does not apply here: both copies of the TYPE map already live under `adapters/`, so the shared import J2 used is available and is the right move.

**Compare the two copies BEFORE unifying them.** If they have already drifted, the unification is a BEHAVIOUR change for one deployment and needs the divergence decided explicitly and recorded — the way J2 decided `"deleted" -> "Done"` — not silently resolved by whichever copy is moved.

## Scope

- `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` — the single definition (and its export from the package
  `__init__`, matching how the status/priority maps are exposed).
- `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — delete the literal, import under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`
  alias.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — delete the literal, import under the same alias.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — extend the one-literal guard
  to the type map.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` — touched ONLY
  if the alias strategy above is not followed; unchanged if it is.
- the characterization pins for the type mapping on both create paths (see Testing) — **this ticket
  owns them unconditionally**.

## Testing

* the guard must FAIL when a second literal is reintroduced. "Mutation-checked" here means a
  concrete manual mutation, not a mutation-testing tool: re-add a literal
  `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE = {"task": "Task", "story": "Story", "bug": "Bug", "epic": "Epic"}` to
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, run the boundary-guard module, record that the new test is
  RED (and note the pass/fail counts), revert the mutation, record that it is GREEN again.
* both create paths keep producing their current issue-type values, pinned BY VALUE — an assertion
  on the built `"issuetype"` field for each of `task`/`story`/`bug`/`epic` through the Cloud create
  path and through the DC create path, not an assertion on the map's shape.
* `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` still passes unmodified (the alias check).
* the full `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` suite is green after the relocation.

Ownership note: sibling story cedc (DC backend characterization suite) also touches DC create-path characterization. To remove the ambiguity, the type-mapping pins are **owned here**; cedc depends on this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the two existing copies are DIFFED and the result is recorded in a comment on this ticket
- [ ] if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly with its rationale recorded,
      not defaulted to whichever copy was moved
- [ ] exactly one `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`-equivalent literal exists under `adapters/`, and it lives in
      `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`
- [ ] both create paths (`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`)
      read that single definition, imported under the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` alias
- [ ] `outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` still resolves as a module attribute, proven by
      `test_outbound_differ_session_log_exclusion.py` passing UNMODIFIED — or, if the implementer
      renamed instead, that test is updated in the same change and passes
- [ ] the boundary guard covers the ticket-type map
- [ ] that guard is MUTATION-CHECKED by the concrete procedure in Testing, with the RED and GREEN
      verdicts recorded in a comment
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the Cloud create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the type mapping is pinned by value for the DC create path, for all four local types
- [ ] the `config.py:11` comment reference is checked for a backing third copy, and the finding is
      recorded either way
baseline.summary: Single-source the ticket-type map; guard it like the others

baseline.description:
# J9 — Make the DC transport actually drive a writing reconcile pass

## Context / Problem

Story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1] landed the DC backend's port conformance and made it reachable through config, then drove it against a REAL Jira Data Center instance for the first time (GitHub Actions run 30604756524). The writing path CRASHES:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

`--mode dry-run` passes; `--mode bootstrap-strict` exits 1. So epic e369's headline capability — Jira Server/Data Center support — does not work yet, and the epic cannot honestly close without this.

Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5]; this story is its implementation.

## The root cause is a PORT defect, and the gap is TWELVE members

An AST audit over `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` — collecting every method invoked on a `client`/`transport` receiver, diffed against `JiraDataCenterTransport`'s methods and against every Protocol in `_backend.py` — measured the real gap:

**Called by the core, ABSENT from the DC transport (12):** `delete_issue`, `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_by_rest`, `get_issue_links`, `get_parent_map`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `set_reporter`, `validate_assignee_exists`.

**Declared on NO Protocol in `_backend.py`: the same 12.**

**The dominant failure mode is SILENT DEGRADATION, not crashing** — which inverts the obvious framing of this story. Classifying every call site by whether an enclosing `try` swallows `Exception`:

| behaviour | count | members |
|---|---|---|
| propagates (crashes) | 1 | `get_issue_by_rest` (`set_reporter` was in this bucket in an earlier draft — it is not reached on DC at all today, see below) |
| swallowed at EVERY site | 7 | `delete_issue_link`, `get_comments`, `get_issue_links`, `set_issue_property`, `set_parent`, `validate_assignee_exists`, `get_parent_map` (the last via `hasattr`, `fetcher.py:448`) |
| MIXED — crashes at some sites, swallowed at others | 3 | `delete_issue`, `remove_label`, `set_entity_property` |

So a DC deployment does not mostly crash: it mostly **appears to converge while quietly not syncing comments, links, parents, issue properties, or validating assignees.** `set_entity_property` is swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites and crashes at the third — which is the ONLY reason any of this was discovered. The crash was the lucky case.

This has a direct consequence for the acceptance bar: "no `AttributeError`" is the WRONG criterion, because it is already true at most sites and true for the wrong reason. Fixing only the crash would produce a green live run with the silent gaps fully intact — a worse outcome than today, because the green run would be taken as proof the capability works.

### Per-method triage is required — a blanket rule is wrong

Three of the twelve need a decision that "implement it like Cloud does" actively gets WRONG. Each was verified in source, and they establish that this story is TRIAGE, not bulk translation:

* **`get_parent_map` — Cloud's implementation is NOT portable.** `acli_graph.py:180` uses
  `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with an opaque `nextPageToken` CURSOR, and its own docstring records
  (ticket 8b25, live-proven) that the legacy `/rest/api/3/search` is RETIRED with HTTP 410 and that
  **sending `startAt` is rejected with HTTP 400**. That endpoint and pagination model are Cloud-v3
  only. DC REST v2 has `POST /rest/api/2/search` with OFFSET paging (`startAt`/`maxResults`). So the
  Approach's "read each Cloud counterpart first" is actively misleading here: copying Cloud yields a
  404/400 against DC. This one needs a v2 offset-paged implementation written fresh.
* **`set_reporter` — RESOLVED by measurement, and the answer is three-part.** (a) The CALL SITE needs
  no change: `jira_account_id` returns whatever `external_id` the family stored, and since bug 5f48
  merged, DC identities are minted under provider `jira` keyed on the DC USERNAME. Measured —
  `jira_account_id('<identity-ticket-id>') -> 'dcuser'`, while bare username / display name / email
  all return `None`. So the seam is already vendor-neutral and hands back exactly what DC needs;
  `set_reporter` is CONDITIONALLY reachable (on tickets whose reporter is an identity id), not
  unreachable. (b) The TRANSPORT method is needed with a DC payload:
  `issue.update(fields={'reporter': {'name': …}})`. (c) **The defect neither the plan nor the review
  had:** `inbound_fields._identity_of` (:163) builds the canonical identity from `raw.get("accountId")`
  ONLY. Measured against both real shapes, a DC reporter yields `account_id=None` while display/email
  survive — so `_diff_reporter` (`outbound_field_diff.py:105-111`) re-emits `changed["reporter"]` on
  EVERY pass, even straight after a successful write, because the next snapshot still reads `None`.
  Implementing the transport method WITHOUT fixing `_identity_of` converts a silent no-op into visible
  infinite churn and fails this story's own idempotence AC.
* **`set_entity_property`** is the one with live evidence, and it is the story's spine — but note it
  is swallowed at 2 of its 3 sites, so fixing it does NOT make the other two observable.

### The exception model is SPLIT OUT to J10 — not this story's problem

The DC transport raises `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` while two CORE modules (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:119`, `outbound_differ.py:138-141`) catch only `urllib.error.HTTPError`. That is real and verified, and it is **[rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052] (J10)**, which BLOCKS this story.

It lived here for two review rounds and produced double-digit findings largely from one tension: an Approach saying "translate into types the core already handles" (implying no core edits) against a Scope listing two core files. Separating the exception CONTRACT from the member IMPLEMENTATION lets each be stated without contradicting the other. J10 lands first; this story then implements the members on a transport whose error contract is already settled.

### The triage, DECIDED — verdict per member

Recorded here so the executor implements rather than researches. Each verdict is backed by the call site and by DC REST **v2** (not Cloud v3). "IMPLEMENT" means a normal v2 call; the two hard cases are called out explicitly.

| member | verdict | basis |
|---|---|---|
| `set_entity_property` | IMPLEMENT | `client.add_issue_property(issue, key, data)`. VERIFIED PRESENT at RUNTIME in jira 3.10.5. Reproduce THREE independent ways — (i) `grep -n 'def add_issue_property' .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/jira/client.py` → **line 2961**; (ii) `python -c "import jira,inspect; print(inspect.signature(jira.JIRA.add_issue_property))"`; (iii) `pip show jira` → 3.10.5 → `(self, issue: str, key: str, data) -> Response` in `jira/client.py`; body is `self._session.put(self._get_url(f"issue/{issue}/properties/{key}"), …)`. **A STATIC symbol lookup will NOT find it** — it is wrapped in `@translate_resource_args`, so a resolver reading the AST sees the decorator, not the `def`. Two review rounds reported it absent for this reason; the same class of false-negative as [rebar:dbf9-3fc8-625d-4730]. Verify at runtime, not statically. (It is correctly absent from OUR codebase — that is what this story adds.) Value must reach the API **verbatim** (Cloud bug 0b27: wrapping in `{"value": …}` silently stored the wrong shape) |
| `set_issue_property` | IMPLEMENT | same endpoint — Cloud's `set_entity_property` is literally an alias of it (`acli_rest.py:266`) |
| `delete_issue` | IMPLEMENT | `client.issue(key).delete()` |
| `delete_issue_link` | IMPLEMENT — **plus a call-site caveat** | `client.delete_issue_link(id)`. But `dispatch_one.py:733` catches `subprocess.CalledProcessError` and treats it as IDEMPOTENT SUCCESS (`_links_applied += 1`); its comment says outright "delete_issue_link shells out via ACLI (raises CalledProcessError, NOT an HTTPError)" — a Cloud/ACLI-specific handler. DC raises `BackendHTTPError` (post-J10), which does NOT match, so a concurrent-removal 404 would escape and unwind the pass instead of being absorbed. The DC implementation must therefore treat a 404/409 as idempotent success ITSELF, inside the transport, rather than relying on a handler written for a different transport |
| `get_comments` | IMPLEMENT | `client.comments(key)` — the transport ALREADY calls this inside `get_comment_map` (transport.py:327), so this is missing SURFACE, not missing capability |
| `get_issue_by_rest` | IMPLEMENT | `client.issue(key)` — already used by `get_issue` (transport.py:234); return the RAW dict, never leak a `jira.Issue` |
| `get_issue_links` | IMPLEMENT | read `issuelinks` off the issue fields; `JiraDataCenterBackend.map_remote_links` already canonicalizes that exact shape |
| `remove_label` | IMPLEMENT | `issue.update(update={"labels": [{"remove": <label>}]})` via the LIBRARY. **NOT the same mechanism as `add_label`** — an earlier draft wrongly said it "mirrors" it. `add_label` uses `Issue.add_field_value("labels", label)`, which has no removal counterpart, so removal goes through `Issue.update`'s `update` verb. Both are `Issue`-resource methods, but they are different calls with different payload shapes |
| `validate_assignee_exists` | IMPLEMENT — **not** `NotImplementedError` | `outbound_assignee.py:107-115` branches on `type(exc).__name__ == "AssigneeNotFoundError"`: that exact type ALREADY EXISTS in the DC transport (`transport.py:43`, subclassing `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError`) and is already raised by `_assign`. A `NotImplementedError` would fall to the `(None, False, False)` non-authoritative branch on EVERY DC assignee resolution — a permanent silent degradation to string-matching. Implement via `client.search_users(...)` (already used by `backend._search_users_by_username`), raising the existing `AssigneeNotFoundError` on a definitive miss. **RETURN CONTRACT, specified because Cloud's differs:** `outbound_assignee.py:108-109` does `acct = client.validate_assignee_exists(...)` then `return (acct or None, True, False)`, so the return value flows on AS the resolved assignee identity. Cloud returns an `accountId`; DC has no accountId, so DC returns the **username** (`name`) — consistent with `NameIdentity` and with the provider/external_id that bug 5f48 now mints. Returning an accountId-shaped value, or `True`, would corrupt the resolved identity |
| `get_parent_map` | IMPLEMENT, v2 shape ONLY | `client.search_issues(jql, fields=['parent'], startAt=…, maxResults=…)` — the library's OFFSET paging is DC-native. Do **not** port Cloud's `/rest/api/3/search/jql` cursor loop; its own docstring records that `startAt` is rejected there with HTTP 400 |
| `set_parent` | **SPIKE-GATED** (a fourth verdict category, distinct from the other three) | On DC, a SUB-TASK's parent is `fields.parent`, but EPIC membership is the "Epic Link" **custom field** (`customfield_NNNNN`, instance-specific), not `parent`. rebar models epics as ordinary parents, so a naive `fields.parent` write may silently no-op for epic links. **CRITICAL PRECONDITION, verified in the installed library:** `add_issues_to_epic` POSTs to `{server}/rest/{agile_rest_path}/{version}/epic/{id}/issue`, and `AGILE_BASE_REST_PATH` defaults to **`agile`** (`jira/resources.py:1518`). Jira Server/DC serves the Agile API under **`greenhopper`**, so with default options this call hits a path that does not exist on DC. The DC client must therefore be constructed with `options={'agile_rest_path': 'greenhopper'}` — a documented pycontribs option — and the spike MUST test both. (A review round asserted the method 'unconditionally raises NotImplementedError' per upstream issue #1244; that is NOT true of jira 3.10.5 as installed — the only two `NotImplementedError` sites in `client.py` guard `group_members` and `rename_user` for Jira < 6.0. The concern is real, the mechanism is the REST PATH, not a guard clause.) SPIKE EXIT CRITERIA, all answerable in ONE CI harness run: (1) `GET /rest/api/2/field` lists a field named "Epic Link" → record its `customfield_NNNNN` id; (2) `client.add_issues_to_epic(<epic>, [<key>])` returns 2xx against the harness WITH `agile_rest_path='greenhopper'`, and its behaviour with the default `agile` path is recorded too; (3) whether it takes the epic's KEY or numeric id; (4) whether a subsequent inbound fetch reports the link, i.e. it round-trips. If (1) or (2) fails, the verdict becomes `NotImplementedError` naming the epic-link limitation. There is no open-ended research: four questions, one run, a pre-decided fallback |
| `set_reporter` | IMPLEMENT + fix `_identity_of`; NO call-site change | RESOLVED by measurement, see below. `issue.update(fields={'reporter': {'name': …}})` (DC has no accountId), AND `inbound_fields._identity_of` must read DC's `name` — without that the reporter re-emits on every pass and the idempotence AC fails |

**Collateral finding, worth its own note:** `outbound_assignee.py:113` classifies by `type(exc).__name__ == "AssigneeNotFoundError"` — a STRING comparison on a class name, not an `isinstance` against the vendor-neutral `BackendAssigneeNotFoundError` that both adapters already subclass. It works, but it silently breaks on any rename and bypasses the neutral base class that exists precisely for this. Flag it; fixing it is optional here and should not expand this story.

So each of the twelve needs a recorded verdict — IMPLEMENT (with the DC v2 shape, not Cloud's), NOT-APPLICABLE (`NotImplementedError` naming the limitation), or UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE (with the upstream decision named) — backed by the call-site evidence, not by symmetry with Cloud.

A METHODOLOGICAL NOTE, because it changed the answer twice: an audit that matches only `client.method(...)` CALL forms under-counts, because the reconciler frequently passes the method as a VALUE — `_call_with_retry(client.delete_issue_link, link_id)` (`dispatch_one.py:731`), `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)` (`dispatch_one.py:321`). The audit must collect every ATTRIBUTE ACCESS on a `client`/`transport` receiver. A first pass using the narrow pattern reported ten and missed `delete_issue_link` and `set_parent`; the corrected pass reports twelve.

All twelve ARE implemented for Cloud, spread across `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py`, `acli.py` and `acli_graph.py`.

So `set_entity_property` is not "the" missing method — it is the FIRST one a live writing pass happened to reach. Eleven more sit behind it. **Implementing only `set_entity_property` would move the crash one call deeper** and produce another red run, looking like progress while the capability stays broken.

`TicketTransport` declares six members (`create_issue`, `get_issue`, `update_issue`, `transition_issue_by_name`, `add_label`, `search_issues`); the core reaches for twenty-one distinct transport members. The port describes under a third of its own requirement. That is exactly why `isinstance` conformance, the backend contract suite, and 1636 reconciler unit tests were all green against a transport that cannot complete a writing pass. **Conformance to an incomplete port proves less than it appears to** — the same class as J6's `add_label` defect, where the only oracle was a fake mirroring the author's assumption.

## Approach

1. TRIAGE each of the twelve to one of IMPLEMENT / NOT-APPLICABLE / UNREACHABLE-BY-CALL-SITE, with
   evidence (see the triage section above — `get_parent_map` and `set_reporter` both break the naive
   rule). Then implement the IMPLEMENT set **through pycontribs/jira**, which the DC transport already uses
   exclusively (no hand-rolled REST anywhere in it; the only `requests` import is for exception
   TYPES). Every one of the twelve is reachable via the library — but its API is SPLIT across
   `jira.JIRA` and `jira.resources.Issue`, and scanning only the former is exactly how J6 shipped the
   `add_label` defect (`add_field_value` lives on Issue, not the client) and how this plan's own first
   triage wrongly concluded three members had 'no helper'. `Issue.update(fields=…, update=…)` covers
   parent, reporter and label-removal. Read each Cloud counterpart for its CONTRACT, but do not assume
   its endpoint or pagination is portable — `set_entity_property` is
   Cloud's alias for `set_issue_property`, which PUTs to
   `/rest/api/3/issue/{key}/properties/{prop}` with the value sent **verbatim as the body** — an
   earlier Cloud bug (0b27) wrapped it in `{"value": ...}` and silently stored the wrong shape, so
   copy the corrected contract, not the intuition. DC is REST **v2**.
2. Where a method is genuinely not applicable to DC, it must raise a clear `NotImplementedError`
   naming the DC limitation — never be left absent to fail as `AttributeError` mid-pass. Each such
   decision needs evidence, not assumption.
3. Make absence detectable AT CONSTRUCTION rather than at some call site months later. `TicketTransport`
   is currently `class TicketTransport(Protocol)` with **no `@runtime_checkable`**, so
   `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` raises `TypeError` rather than returning `False` — verified
   directly, and it means the naive "just isinstance it" mechanism does not work. So: add
   `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport` (matching `Backend` and the capability protocols, which
   already carry it), declare the required members on it, and assert conformance where a backend is
   BUILT — `_build_jira_datacenter_backend` in `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and the Cloud
   equivalent — so a missing member fails loudly at construction.
4. Make the failures OBSERVABLE, by a named mechanism. **`transport.py` currently has NO logging at
   all** (zero `logging`/`logger` references — verified), which is precisely why a failure in a
   swallowed member surfaces nothing. Add the module-level convention its sibling adapters already
   use — `import logging` + `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, exactly as
   `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:13,25` does — and have each newly-implemented member log at
   WARNING naming the MEMBER and the REMOTE ID before the error propagates (J10 has already
   translated it to `BackendHTTPError` by then).
   **Use the logger, not `alert_store`:** `alert_store.append(record, repo_root)` requires a
   `repo_root` the transport does not have and should not acquire — the transport is a vendor
   adapter, not a store client. Sibling adapters use `logger.warning` for exactly this class of
   event (`acli_cli_ops.py:415`, `acli_subprocess.py:135,140`, `jira_family/sanitizers.py:85`), so
   this follows the established convention rather than inventing a second one.
5. Add a STRUCTURAL TEST that every transport member the core reaches for is declared on the port.
   It must collect EVERY attribute access on a `client`/`transport` receiver, not just call forms:
   a call-form-only audit silently under-counts (see the methodological note below) and would let the
   thirteenth member slip in unnoticed. This is what stops the class of defect recurring on the next
   backend.

**Alternative rejected:** implement `set_entity_property` alone. It fixes one crash, leaves eleven, and leaves the port still misdescribing what the core needs.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — ALSO gains a
  module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (it has none today) so member failures are
  observable; see Approach step 4. And implement (or
  explicitly `NotImplementedError`) the ELEVEN unguarded absentees listed in the audit above, plus a
  deliberate decision on `get_parent_map`. **NOT just `set_entity_property`** — implementing one
  method moves the crash one call deeper and produces another red live run.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — add `@runtime_checkable` to `TicketTransport`
  (it currently lacks it, so `isinstance` against it raises `TypeError`) and declare the members the
  core actually requires.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py`** — `_identity_of` (:163) currently builds
  the canonical identity from `raw.get("accountId")` ONLY, so a DC reporter yields `account_id=None`
  and the reporter mutation re-emits on every pass.
  **THE KEY IS SPECIFIED, not left open:** the existing `account_id` key receives
  `raw.get("accountId") or raw.get("name")`. Not a new key — `_diff_reporter` reads `account_id`, so
  putting DC's `name` anywhere else leaves the comparison broken. PRIORITY IS LOAD-BEARING:
  `accountId` must win. Measured across all three payload shapes —
  `{accountId}` → `'557058:abc'` (Cloud unchanged); `{name}` → `'dcuser'` (DC fixed);
  `{accountId, name}` → `'557058:abc'` (Cloud does NOT regress). Reversing that order silently
  re-identifies every Cloud user, so a test must pin it.
  This is a CORE module both adapters feed, which is why the precedence is stated here rather than
  left to the implementer.
- **`outbound_field_diff.py` is NOT a patch site** — stated explicitly because it has been raised
  three times. `_diff_reporter` (:105) reads `reporter_identity.get("account_id")`; once `_identity_of`
  populates that key on DC, `desired` and `remote_acct` both become `'dcuser'` and the comparison
  converges with NO edit to this file. Do not confuse it with `outbound_differ.py` (a different file,
  and J10's concern).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` and
  `adapters/jira/backend.py` — assert transport conformance in the FACTORY, where the backend is
  built, so a missing member fails loudly at construction rather than at a call site later.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — `FakeTransport` gains whatever members the
  widened port declares, since it is the contract suite's stand-in and must satisfy it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — a structural test for the audit: every transport attribute the
  core reaches for is declared on the Protocol.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — already written by J7; it is the oracle and … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: J9 — implement set_entity_property on DC and make the transport port state what the core requires

baseline.description:
## Why
Workflows need to call **external MCP servers** (serena, github, Atlassian, …) as a
first-class, deterministic step kind — the capability rebar's scripted ops cannot provide
(rebar's own ticket ops stay as scripted ops; this is for third-party tools). This is the
"deterministic MCP step" pattern (Dify/Rivet): the workflow author picks the call, not an LLM.
It is carved out of the foundation epic because it is a separable subsystem with its own
security surface (allowlist/secrets/manifest), is env-gated, and depends on the contract model
the foundation establishes while nothing in the foundation depends on it.

## Depends on
The foundation epic (contract-bearing prompt/step model): this epic surfaces an MCP tool's
`inputSchema`/`outputSchema` through the SAME contract/inspector machinery the foundation builds.
Build only after the foundation's contract registry, validation, and editor inspector land.

## What (settled design — see foundation epic decision-log)
- **`mcp_call` leaf step kind.** Same shape as a scripted step (with-in, named-outputs-out);
  add to the v2 IR schema `oneOf`, the step-kind classifier, and executor dispatch. Reuse
  pydantic_ai's MCP client (on the official `mcp` SDK, already an optional dep) for stdio + http;
  drop to the SDK's `ClientSession` for manifest work. NO hand-rolled transport/handshake.
- **Two-tier allowlist + trust.** rebar SHIPS a default allowlist; projects ADD servers via
  their own `.rebar/` config; secrets live in PROJECT config via `${{ secrets.x }}` indirection
  (never inline). Resolution mirrors prompts (built-in ⊕ project) BUT projects may only ADD —
  they CANNOT shadow/redefine a built-in server name. The allowlist pins endpoint IDENTITY
  (not just name) and IS the trust boundary (Flowise RCE CVE-2025-59528 lesson). A workflow may
  call only an allow-listed `server.tool`; else lint/runtime refusal. Env-gated by a new
  `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_MCP_CALL`-style flag, default off. MCP tool annotations
  (readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint) refine UX/defaults but are
  UNTRUSTED hints (default worst-case when absent); the allowlist enforces.
- **Cached manifest + explicit refresh.** Introspect a server once (`tools/list`, following
  `nextCursor` pagination), cache tool list + `inputSchema`s to `.rebar/mcp-tools/<server>.json`;
  the editor palette reads the CACHE (offline-capable, git-reviewable, deterministic). Explicit
  `rebar mcp refresh <server>` re-introspects; invalidate on `notifications/tools/list_changed`;
  stamp the manifest with a version/TTL. Run-time re-validates args against the live `inputSchema`
  and reconciles the server endpoint against the trusted allowlist.
- **Output handling.** When a tool declares `outputSchema`, validate `structuredContent` against
  it and feed those fields to the expression validator. When absent (the common case — and
  observed even when outputSchema IS declared, per spike E3), treat the result `content[]` as
  opaque `any`; handle `isError: true`. Opaque `any` is NOT silently mappable into a typed
  downstream input contract without an author-acknowledged cast.
- **Auth.** stdio = env credentials; http = OAuth 2.1 — modeled SEPARATELY; lean on the client
  lib, don't store bare tokens.

## Relevant code
- IR + dispatch: `src/rebar/schemas/workflow.v2.schema.json`,
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/{schema,executor,lint_refs}.py`.
- MCP client: pydantic_ai (`[agents]`) + `mcp` SDK (`[mcp]`), both already present.
- Allowlist/secrets config: `.rebar/` (mirrors the prompt two-tier resolution).

## Context
Designed in the foundation epic's /joe-brainstorm and derisked by spike E3 (introspect → manifest
→ call against the real serena server via the already-present SDK: paginated `tools/list`, all
tools advertise `inputSchema`, both structuredContent and opaque `content[]` handled, `isError`
graceful, bad args don't crash the client). Zero new runtime dependencies.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_call` is a first-class v2 IR step kind (schema + classifier + executor dispatch) that
      calls an external MCP server's tool with `with:` inputs and produces named outputs.
- [ ] Two-tier allowlist (built-in ⊕ project-add-only, no shadowing) with endpoint-identity
      pinning; secrets via `${{ secrets.x }}`; calls outside the allowlist refused; env-gated.
- [ ] Cached tool manifest with `nextCursor` pagination, `list_changed` invalidation, explicit
      refresh; editor palette renders each tool's `inputSchema` as typed fields from the cache.
- [ ] Output handling: validate `structuredContent` vs `outputSchema` when present; opaque-`any`
      fallback otherwise (incl. when outputSchema is declared but absent in results); `isError` handled.
- [ ] stdio (env) and http (OAuth 2.1) auth modeled separately; no bare-token storage.
- [ ] A workflow author can add an allow-listed external MCP tool call as a deterministic step,
baseline.summary: Workflow authoring v2: external MCP-call step kind (allowlist, secrets, manifest)

baseline.description:
## Why
The compact/delete/init contended-lock tests plant a lock then start a
`threading.Timer(0.4, unlink)` and assert only `rc == 0` plus snapshot/tombstone presence
(`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_index_lock.py:71-85`,
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_delete_init_index_lock.py:83-119`). On a slow runner the
0.4s timer removes the lock before git's first attempt, so the test passes through the
ordinary success path without ever exercising `_with_index_lock_retry`
(`gitutil.py:110-129`). VALIDATED.

## What
1. Add an instrumented test seam to `_with_index_lock_retry` in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`,
   using the codebase's standard test-seam pattern (a module-level callable defaulting to
   `None`, set from tests via pytest `monkeypatch.setattr` which auto-restores it): a
   module-level `_retry_probe: Callable[[int, subprocess.CompletedProcess], None] | None = None`.
   - **Type of `result`:** the `subprocess.CompletedProcess` returned by `run_once()` — the
     SAME type `run_once` already returns (`Callable[[], subprocess.CompletedProcess]`). Tests
     inspect `result.returncode` and reuse the module's own `_is_index_lock_error(result.stderr
     or result.stdout or "")` to assert the first attempt was a genuine index.lock error.
   - **Where it fires (every attempt, incl. the pre-loop call):** invoked once immediately
     after the INITIAL `run_once()` at `gitutil.py:120` (as `attempt_number=1`), and again
     immediately after each in-loop `run_once()` at `gitutil.py:128`. `attempt_number` for the
     in-loop calls is `attempt + 1` where the loop variable `attempt` runs `1..
     _INDEX_LOCK_ATTEMPTS-1` — so the sequence observed is 1, 2, 3, … matching real attempts.
   - **Production is unaffected:** the default is `None`, so the invocation is guarded
     (`if _retry_probe is not None: _retry_probe(...)`) and skipped in production. Callers that
     import `_with_index_lock_retry` by name (e.g. `event_append.py:45,211,219`) see no behavior
     change because the seam stays `None` outside tests. The probe is invoked directly (not
     wrapped in try/except): in production it is never set, and a test owns its own probe's
     behavior, so a probe raising surfaces as that test's own failure — the desired contract.
   - **No teardown footgun:** tests set the seam via pytest `monkeypatch.setattr(gitutil,
     "_retry_probe", …)`, which auto-restores it to `None` at test teardown (no manual reset,
     no cross-test leakage) — the standard way module-level callables are patched in this suite.
2. Rewrite the three contended-lock tests to use the seam instead of `threading.Timer`: plant a
   fresh (young, not reclaimable-as-stale) lock; the probe, on observing the first attempt fail
   with an index.lock error, unlinks the planted lock so the NEXT attempt succeeds (deterministic
   synchronization — the lock is released strictly after the confirmed first failure, never
   before). Assert at least two attempts occurred and that attempt 1's result was a genuine
   index.lock error. The now-unused `threading.Timer`-based `_plant_fresh_lock` timer branch is
   removed/updated so no test still relies on timing.
3. Add a dedicated non-lock-failure test in each of the two files: using the same seam to count
   attempts, drive a NON-index.lock git failure (e.g. a commit that fails for an unrelated
   reason) and assert the probe saw exactly ONE attempt (the non-lock failure returns
   immediately, never retried).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — add the `_retry_probe` seam to `_with_index_lock_retry`
  (guarded, default None; fires on the pre-loop attempt and every in-loop attempt).
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_index_lock.py` — deterministic ride-out test +
  a non-lock-not-retried test; drop the `threading.Timer` reliance.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_delete_init_index_lock.py` — deterministic ride-out tests
  (delete + init) + a non-lock-not-retried test; update/remove the timer-based
  `_plant_fresh_lock` branch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] First attempt deterministically returns the real `index.lock` error before the lock is
      released (synchronized via the `_retry_probe` seam, not a timer).
- [ ] Each rewritten contended-lock test asserts at least two attempts occurred (retry path
      exercised) and that the first attempt was a genuine index.lock error.
- [ ] A dedicated test in each file asserts a non-lock git failure returns on the FIRST
      attempt and is never retried (probe observed exactly one attempt).
- [ ] The final event/commit (snapshot/tombstone) exists; `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Contended index.lock ride-out tests must assert first-failure + retry count

## Context
Add an `rebar.authorship.v1` attestation KIND on the foundation asymmetric
attest substrate (`src/rebar/attest/`), so an event can be cryptographically
signed by an author identity and verified against that identity's in-band public
keys. This is the signing/verifying MACHINERY (registration + sign/verify + trust
root); WIRING it into the write path and enforcement is a later leaf (3183). Builds
on ddbe (identity entity holds `keys`) and the foundation SSHSIG scheme.

## Why
Authorship certification needs a tamper-evident proof that a specific identity
authored an event, verifiable offline against public keys carried in-band on the
identity entity (no external PKI). Reusing the foundation `attest` substrate gives
policy-pinned scheme selection (closes the alg-confusion class) for free.

## What
### 1. New module `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`
Constants: `AUTHORSHIP_KIND = "rebar.authorship.v1"`,
`AUTHORSHIP_NAMESPACE = "rebar.authorship.v1"`,
`PAYLOAD_TYPE = "application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json"`.

- `register_authorship_policy() -> None` (idempotent): pins
  `registry.POLICY[AUTHORSHIP_KIND] = registry.Policy(scheme="sshsig",
  namespace=AUTHORSHIP_NAMESPACE)`. (The `sshsig` SCHEME is already registered by
  `sshsig.register_sshsig_scheme()`; this pins the KIND→scheme policy so
  `registry.verify` selects the scheme from source-pinned policy, never from the
  envelope.) Wire the call into `src/rebar/attest/__init__.py` right after the
  existing `sshsig.register_sshsig_scheme()` line, so it is live at import.
- `sign_authorship(payload: bytes, key_path: str, principal: str) -> dsse.Envelope`:
  FIRST call `sshsig.ensure_available()` (raises `sshsig.SshKeygenUnavailable`
  when ssh-keygen is missing/too old — the honest precondition; without this
  `sshsig.sign`'s `subprocess.run(check=True)` would instead raise
  `FileNotFoundError`/`CalledProcessError`). Then `pae = dsse.pae(PAYLOAD_TYPE, payload)`; `sig = sshsig.sign(pae, key_path,
  AUTHORSHIP_NAMESPACE)`; return `dsse.Envelope(PAYLOAD_TYPE, payload,
  [dsse.Signature(keyid=principal, sig=sig)])`. `principal` is the author identity's
  id (it becomes the SSHSIG `-I` principal — `SshsigScheme.verify` reads
  `signatures[0].keyid` as the principal). Raises `sshsig.SshKeygenUnavailable` if
  ssh-keygen is missing/too old (do not swallow — signing must be honest).
- `allowed_signers_from_keys(keys: list[str], principal: str) -> str`: build SSHSIG
  allowed_signers content — one line per key, `"<principal> <authorized-keys-line>"`
  (the identity's `keys` are OpenSSH authorized-keys lines like
  `"ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."`; prefixing the principal yields a valid allowed_signers
  entry). Join with `"\n"`. Skip blank/malformed key entries.
- `resolve_trust_root(identity_id: str, *, repo_root=None) -> str | None`: load the
  identity via `rebar.show_ticket(identity_id, repo_root=...)`; if it is an
  `identity` ticket with a non-empty `keys` list, return
  `allowed_signers_from_keys(keys, principal=identity_id)`; else `None` (unknown
  identity or no keys → nothing to trust).
- `verify_authorship(envelope: dsse.Envelope, identity_id: str, *, repo_root=None)
  -> registry.Verdict`: `trust_root = resolve_trust_root(identity_id, ...)`; if
  `None`, return a non-verified `registry.Verdict(False, "unknown_principal",
  reason=...)`; else return `registry.verify(AUTHORSHIP_KIND, envelope,
  trust_root)`. The envelope's signature `keyid` MUST equal `identity_id` (the
  principal) or SSHSIG verification fails — this is what makes "signed by A does not
  verify against B" hold: verifying A's envelope against B builds B's allowed_signers
  (B's keys, principal=B_id), and neither the key nor the principal matches.

### 2. Determinism / trust-root selection
Trust root is ALWAYS resolved from the identity entity's in-band `keys` (never from
the envelope), and the scheme is ALWAYS selected from source-pinned
`POLICY[AUTHORSHIP_KIND]`. A caller cannot smuggle a scheme or a trust anchor
through the envelope.

## Scope
In: the authorship module (constants, policy registration, sign, verify, trust-root
resolution, allowed_signers builder) and its registration in `attest/__init__.py`.
Out: signing real events at the write seam / storing the envelope on events
(3183 enforcement), key lifecycle & rotation (e165). `payload` here is arbitrary
bytes supplied by the caller (later the event's canonical bytes); bde5 does not
decide what bytes an event contributes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `register_authorship_policy()` pins `POLICY["rebar.authorship.v1"]` to
  `Policy(scheme="sshsig", namespace="rebar.authorship.v1")` and is invoked at
  `attest` package import; a test asserts `registry.resolve("rebar.authorship.v1")`
  returns that policy.
- [ ] Round-trip: given an ssh keypair whose PUBLIC key is stored on identity A's
  `keys`, `sign_authorship(payload, privkey, principal=A_id)` produces an envelope
  that `verify_authorship(envelope, A_id)` reports `verified=True`
  (test skips if `ssh-keygen` unavailable via `sshsig.ensure_available`).
- [ ] Cross-identity rejection: the SAME envelope verified against a DIFFERENT
  identity B (different keypair) reports `verified=False` (B's in-band keys are the
  trust root, and neither key nor principal matches).
- [ ] Tamper rejection: mutating the envelope `payload` (or a signature byte) makes
  `verify_authorship(..., A_id)` report `verified=False`.
- [ ] Unknown/keyless identity: `verify_authorship` against an id that is not an
  `identity` ticket, or one with empty `keys`, returns a non-verified Verdict
  (never raises).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (new: constants, register_authorship_policy, sign_authorship, allowed_signers_from_keys, resolve_trust_root, verify_authorship)
- `src/rebar/attest/__init__.py` (call register_authorship_policy() at import, after sshsig registration)
baseline.summary: identity: authorship attestation kind on the foundation substrate

# GitHub Issues sync — provider parity with the Jira reconciler (de-Jira-ify the bridge)

## Context

Discovered from the export/import design brainstorm (`rule-swamp-pupil`, 2026-06-17). We want GitHub Issues sync at parity with the existing Jira sync: bidirectional, incremental, idempotent, dry-run by default.

**Critical design conclusion from that brainstorm:** GitHub sync must ride the EXISTING reconciler framework (binding store + outbound/inbound differs + applier), NOT the one-shot export/import path. Import is stateless / additive / lossy and would have to rebuild the entire binding/diff/conflict/convergence layer to do sync — the wrong substrate. git-bug's bridges confirm sync is bidirectional + incremental, distinct from bulk import. The one thing export/import leaves behind for this epic is the provider-neutral `--strip-external` association notion shipped by `rule-swamp-pupil`.

## What / Scope

The spine of this work is **generalizing the reconciler**, which is hardcoded to Jira in 6+ places:

- `jira_key` in the binding store (`rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`) → a `{provider, external_key}` abstraction.
- `jira-` local-id prefix (`inbound_translate.py:105`).
- ADF (Atlassian Document Format) rich-text codec (`adf.py`) → a GitHub Markdown codec.
- per-type/status/priority maps (`outbound_differ.py`, `inbound_translate.py`) → per-provider registries.
- `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` loop-breaker marker (`inbound_differ.py`).
- `rebar-id:` Jira labels / entity properties used for binding recovery → a GitHub equivalent.

Then add a **GitHub provider**: REST/GraphQL client, auth (token / `gh`), pagination + rate-limit handling, field mapping (state↔status, labels↔tags, assignees, milestone↔?, comments with external-id dedup), and inbound/outbound apply leaves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] reconciler binding/translate/differ/codec layers generalized to a provider abstraction; Jira migrated onto it with no regression (existing tests green)
- [ ] GitHub provider client: auth, pagination, rate-limit handling (read + write)
- [ ] field mapping GH↔rebar (state/labels/assignees/comments/external-id dedup) + Markdown codec
- [ ] bidirectional incremental sync + conflict resolution + loop-breaker; idempotent across passes
- [ ] dry-run default; live writes env-gated; `session_log` excluded
- [ ] tests against recorded GitHub fixtures + integration marker for live

Non-trivial; sized as a standalone epic. Builds on the provider-neutral external-association seam from `rule-swamp-pupil`.
- [ ] A `{provider, external_key}` binding abstraction replaces hardcoded `jira_key`, with Jira refactored onto it and NO behavior regression (existing Jira reconciler tests stay green).
- [ ] GitHub provider does bidirectional incremental sync of issues (create/update/status/comments/labels), idempotent across passes, dry-run default, live writes gated by an env flag mirroring `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`.
- [ ] Conflict resolution + loop-breaker parity with Jira; `session_log` excluded (parity with `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`).
baseline.summary: GitHub Issues sync — provider parity with the Jira reconciler

## Problem
`rebar explain plan` / `explain review` (and `explain <criterion-id>`) read their guide
markdown from `config.repo_root(...)/docs/...`. `repo_root` resolves to the *consuming
project's* git toplevel (or cwd), never the rebar install. So when rebar is installed as a
library/CLI/MCP and run against another project, the `docs/` tree is absent and every
`explain` guide lookup fails with missing-file. A client hit exactly this ("the author guide
lives in the rebar source repo, not this project").

## Goal
Make the plan-authoring guide (writing-a-passing-plan.md) and code-authoring guide
(passing-code-review.md) accessible through rebar's CLI, MCP, and Python library surfaces from
any installation, matching the established OSS convention for runtime-needed data files:
the canonical copy lives *inside* the import package, read via `importlib.resources` (the same
pattern rebar already uses for `criteria_routing.json`).

## Approach
1. Move the two prose guides to `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and
   `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` (canonical, in-package) and add
   `src/rebar/_guides/__init__.py`. Hatchling ships all files under `src/rebar`, so they land
   in the wheel automatically.
2. Change `AUTHOR_GUIDES` from `dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]` (path components under `docs/`) to
   `dict[str, str]` mapping guide name -> bare filename, e.g.
   `{"plan": "writing-a-passing-plan.md", "review": "passing-code-review.md"}`.
   `explain_guide(name)` resolves via `resources.files("rebar._guides") / AUTHOR_GUIDES[name]`
   and drops the `repo_root_path` parameter (resolution is repo-root independent). Unknown name
   still raises `ExplainError("unknown-id", ...)`; a genuinely absent packaged resource raises
   `ExplainError("missing-file", ...)`.
3. `explain_criterion(id)` renders the section directly from the packaged registry via the
   existing `_guide_section_body(criterion)` (the same content `regenerate_criteria_guide`
   builds the doc from) instead of reading `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`. Overlay
   project criteria still resolve via `load_criteria(repo_root=repo_root_path)`; unknown-id and
   malformed-registry states are preserved; the repo-root missing-file state is removed.
4. Leave `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `docs/passing-code-review.md` as thin pointer
   files to the in-package canonical source so existing links (docs/README.md, AGENTS.md)
   resolve.
5. Keep the dev/CI machinery unchanged: `regenerate_criteria_guide`, `validate_criteria_guide`,
   `_guide_path`, and the Pass-4 coach deep-links to the docs anchor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `REBAR_ROOT` set to a directory containing no `docs/`, `rebar explain plan`,
      `rebar explain review`, and `rebar explain <criterion-id>` (e.g. F1) each exit 0 and print
      the guide/section (installability guarantee).
- [ ] The library calls `registry.explain_guide("plan"|"review")` and
      `registry.explain_criterion("F1", repo_root_path=<dir-without-docs>)` return the content
      without raising (no dependency on repo-root `docs/`).
- [ ] The MCP `explain_criterion` tool returns `{criterion_id, section}` for a guide name and a
      criterion id under the same repo-root-independent condition.
- [ ] Both guides are present as packaged resources: `resources.files("rebar._guides")` contains
      `writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `passing-code-review.md`.
- [ ] `docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `docs/passing-code-review.md` still exist as pointer
      files (existing links do not 404).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; `tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py` passes,
      updated to assert repo-root independence instead of the old "missing-file when the repo
      has no docs" behavior, plus a test that both guides are packaged.
baseline.summary: explain guides accessible from any install (package the author guides)

## Resolution discovered during plan review

No production change is warranted. A4-1 already solved the operational defect at the correct boundary and deliberately preserved the raw differ contract.

The raw `compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state)` API must treat its first argument as real local state. For `local_state = {"RB-8": {}}` and `jira_state = {"RB-8": {"summary": "remote"}}`, it emits a `field_drift` update. That behavior is a load-bearing positive control for callers that honor the API contract.

The sole production snapshot caller does not honor that contract: it passes `prev_snapshot` and `curr_snapshot`, both remote Jira state. A4-1, merged as Gerrit 1256 / `6cdd4b00d9ee` with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, filters differ-owned `field_drift` and `unbound_local` emissions immediately at that call site. The source and tests explicitly require the filter to remain there so a future migration to real local state can remove it without weakening the pure differ.

Changing `_compute_mutations_emit_both` as originally proposed would contradict that decision and break the raw-differ positive control. This ticket therefore verifies the already-landed behavior and records the no-change decision.

## Verification plan

- Run `test_key_set_prev_field_drift_never_survives_the_production_filter`; it proves the raw positive control emits and the production call-site result contains zero outbound updates.
- Run `test_a_genuinely_new_remote_key_still_plans_its_inbound_create` and `test_seed_mutations_survive_the_suppression`; they prove the filter does not swallow genuine work or invariant repairs.
- Run the converged `reconcile_once` and real-repository idempotency tests; they prove persisted `mutation_count == 0`.
- Execute an in-session counting probe around the real production path with a key-set previous snapshot. Prove the counter observes a representative `git rev-parse` call in its positive control, then assert zero per-mutation calls after the A4-1 filter.
- Record exact commands and outcomes on this ticket and the epic session log. No source, test, or documentation file is changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [code-verifiable] The raw differ emits its documented field-drift positive control while the production snapshot call-site result contains zero outbound updates for the same key-set entry.
- [x] [code-verifiable] Genuine inbound-create and invariant-seed mutations survive the call-site filter.
- [x] [code-verifiable] A converged pass records `mutation_count == 0`.
- [x] [code-verifiable] An instrumented production-path probe records exactly zero per-mutation `git rev-parse` calls and its positive control proves the counter is live.
- [x] [operator-attested] The no-change decision, A4-1 Gerrit evidence, commands, and results are recorded on this ticket.

## File impact

None. A4-1 already contains the production filter and load-bearing characterization tests.
baseline.summary: A4-3 verification: accept A4-1 call-site suppression and make no differ change

# Remediate validated findings from the behavioral/contractual test-coverage audit

An external test-coverage audit (static, pinned to commit `2d1524ad8`) identified a
cluster of tests that assert against **source text / private structure / mere
existence** rather than behavior ("change-detector" tests), plus several documented
contracts with **no behavioral regression test**, and two documentation-vs-code
drifts. We re-verified every finding against the actual codebase with five
independent review passes: **all findings validated** (two downgraded to
"partial — the mechanism is partly tested but the specific gap is real"), and the
grep-against-source inventory surfaced **additional** anti-pattern tests beyond the
report's list.

This epic converts the false-confidence regressions into real behavioral coverage,
adds the missing data-safety/concurrency tests, hardens two thin production paths the
audit exposed, and reconciles the stale docs.

## Context

- The audit's core thesis is correct: the largest residual risk is **not** broad
  lack of testing — core coverage (CRUD parity, deterministic replay, two-clone
  reconvergence, no-loss writer storms, claim contention, detector verdict
  semantics) is strong — but **false confidence** in narrowly-targeted regressions
  whose tests inspect source structure instead of exercising the promised behavior.
- Verification method: five parallel read-only audit passes over production source,
  existing tests, docs, and CI config. Findings that were already covered were
  dropped; only genuinely-missing/miswired coverage is ticketed here.
- Grep-against-source is **not** universally an anti-pattern here: 59 of 77
  source-inspecting tests are JUSTIFIED (the source text *is* the observable
  contract — exact git argv an adapter builds, layering/import invariants via
  `ast.parse`, prompt/YAML/Terraform/CI "config-as-artifact" drift guards,
  runtime-produced artifacts). This epic only touches the ~9 ANTI-PATTERN and the
  handful of BORDERLINE cases where a behavioral test is feasible and stronger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories are closed (signed), each landing through the Gerrit gate
      (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1).
- [ ] No test in the changed set asserts only `hasattr(...)`, an exact private
      constant value, or a source substring where the underlying behavior is
      executable and was previously untested.
- [ ] Newly-added concurrency/race tests are deterministic (barrier/instrumented
      seams, not sleep-timing races that can pass on a slow runner).
- [ ] Every P0 finding (index.lock stale-reclaim TOCTOU; detached-HEAD local-ahead
- [ ] Each "change-detector" regression test named by the audit is either replaced
- [ ] The two documentation drifts (Jira link-sync inventory; dual-lock portability
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` stays green; no net loss of
baseline.summary: Remediate validated findings from the test-coverage audit
