## Context / Problem
T3 (integration feasibility) and T10 (infra/IaC) have never blocked in ~2,500 runs each — a configuration artifact, not a quality signal: 13/20 sampled T3 findings were actionable codebase-grounded criticisms and 62% of T10's strong findings cite concrete repo artifacts. The audited T10 keyword gate measured 28% fire rate with 100% strong-finding recall. Operator approved enabling blocking for both. Plan-review blocking is derived from `default_posture: "blocking"` plus `block_threshold` in the routing entry (the `blocking_enabled` field is the code-review gate's convention and does not apply here), and there is no per-class blocking mechanism in Pass-3 — a finding blocks when its criterion is blocking-postured and its priority crosses the threshold.

## Approach
(1) In src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json set `default_posture: "blocking"` with `block_threshold: 0.90` for T3 and T10 (conservative pilot; the standing zero-LLM criterion-effectiveness recorder monitors outcomes for a later 0.85 revisit). (2) Class scoping for T10 is achieved through severity guidance, not a new mechanism: one sentence added to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md stating that only its MAJOR classes (destructive apply, wildcard/overbroad grant, plaintext secret on a committed path, unauthenticated internet-reachable service) warrant severity >= major — so lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 priority threshold through the existing severity->priority pipeline. No pass3_decide changes. (3) The T10 DET overlay gate is added as a DetGateRule in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_gate_rules.py (the established home for trigger vocabularies since change 1041), transcribed verbatim from the audit: text_all[0] = `\b(?:terraform|cloudformation|pulumi|ansible|kubernetes|helm|k8s|iac|aws|ec2|s3|iam|ssm|cloudwatch|vpc|sns|lambda|rds|ebs|docker|compose|infra/|provision\w*|systemd|launchagent|user_data|cloudfront|api gateway|oidc|\.github/workflows|github actions|workflow_dispatch|pull_request_target|secrets\.[A-Z_]+)\b` (case-insensitive), no file_impact arms. (4) tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py contains TWO assertions that pin the blocking configuration and BOTH are updated in the same commit: the pinned full-routing-table assertion (test_full_routing_table_matches_pinned_expectation) gains the two posture changes, and the blocking-set assertion (test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking) has T3 and T10 added to its hardcoded approved blocking set. (5) docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md regenerated with the documented command. Alternative rejected: enabling at 0.85 immediately — 0.90 first bounds the blast radius while the effectiveness recorder accumulates post-change data at zero LLM cost; and building a per-class blocking mechanism in Pass-3 — new machinery when severity guidance reaches the same outcome through the existing pipeline.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_gate_rules.py, src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md, tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py (update pinned table), tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py (new), docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md (regenerated).

## Testing
Unit (relative imports): a T3 finding at priority 0.92 produces a blocking decision through Pass-3 and one at 0.85 stays advisory; same for a T10 fixture; the T10 DetGateRule fires on a terraform-touching fixture plan and a GHA workflow plan and skips a pure-docs plan with a routing.det_gated coverage entry and zero T10 LLM routing; the updated pinned routing table matches; the T10 rubric contains the severity-guidance sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] T3 and T10 carry default_posture blocking with block_threshold 0.90 and findings above/below the threshold block/stay-advisory through Pass-3 (checked: `pytest tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py`).
- [ ] The T10 DetGateRule fires on infra and GHA fixtures and skips non-infra plans with a det_gated coverage entry (checked: unit tests).
- [ ] plan_review_T10.md contains the MAJOR-class severity-guidance sentence (checked: rubric text assertion).
- [ ] Both pinned assertions in test_threshold_recalibration.py — the full routing table and the approved-blocking-criteria set — reflect T3/T10 and the whole file passes (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py`).
- [ ] The criteria guide is regenerated (checked: committed regen output).

# Durable write path drops concurrent locked writes: background git auto-gc races the object DB

## Summary
Under heavy concurrent write load, the rebar durable write path (`event_append`) loses
committed writes. Writers holding the exclusive index lock fail their `git commit` with
`error: invalid object <sha> for '<...>.json' ... error: Error building trees` and the
write is silently dropped. The regression test
`tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py::test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes`
catches it (e.g. `intended=250 persisted_on_disk=233 lost=17`), and it is **currently red on
`main` repo-wide** — it fails ~9 of the last ~12 `main` post-merge CI runs, including the CI
run of the very commit that tried to fix it (`485873652`, post-merge run `29593239791`,
`lost=17`). Because it fails Verified on unrelated changes, it is friction on every Gerrit
landing (mitigated today only by probabilistic `recheck`).

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run the integration tier under parallel xdist load, e.g.
   `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py -q`
   repeatedly, or observe `main`'s post-merge `test` workflow across several pushes.
2. The test spawns `_WRITERS=5` writers × `_BURSTS=25` (`intended=250`) concurrent
   lock-serialized writes while the enrich-queue prune runs.
3. Intermittently (load-dependent), some writes raise the `invalid object / Error building
   trees` `CommandError` while holding the lock and are swallowed → `lost>0`.

**Expected:** every lock-acquiring write persists to disk; `swallowed_write_raises == 0` and
`persisted_on_disk == intended_total`.
**Actual:** under load a fraction of writes are lost (observed losses 17/26/94/146 across
runs/workers — the varying count is itself a signature of a load-dependent race).

## Root Cause (diagnosed)
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (~L96–117) deliberately re-enabled **stock git background gc**
  on the tracker repo — `--unset gc.auto` + `gc.autoDetach=true` (commit `f63d72662`,
  "WU-1 — re-enable stock git gc (drop gc.auto=0 forcing)", 2026-06-18).
- Under this test's heavy parallel commit load the loose-object count crosses git's `gc.auto`
  threshold; git forks a **detached background `gc --auto`** that repacks/prunes loose objects
  **concurrently with the writers** — an object can vanish between `git add` and `git commit`.
- `485873652` added `_recover_from_invalid_object` (Mode D, `event_append.py:713`): on an
  `invalid object / error building trees` commit failure it runs `git read-tree HEAD`, re-adds
  the current write's path, and retries. This reduced the damage ~6–8× (146 → ~17) but does
  **not** cover the case where the missing object is **reachable from HEAD** (a committed
  object caught by the background repack): `read-tree HEAD` reinstates the broken reference, the
  retry commit fails identically, and the recovery is one-shot (no bounded loop / escalation).
  The failing logs show the **same object sha for the same path cascading across sequential
  bursts**, which is the HEAD-reachable signature.

## Fix Direction (candidate; needs maintainer judgment on the gc trade-off)
1. **Neutralize the trigger on the durable write path:** force `gc.auto=0` (or at minimum
   `gc.autoDetach=false`) on the tracker repo so a background repack cannot run concurrently
   with commits. This revisits the deliberate `f63d72662` decision — understand *why* WU-1
   re-enabled gc (loose-object growth? perf?) before reverting; a scoped
   "no auto-gc while the exclusive write lock is held" is preferable to a blanket revert.
2. **Harden the recovery to the HEAD-reachable case:** after `read-tree HEAD`, if the missing
   object is still referenced from HEAD, regenerate it from the intact worktree file
   (re-`git add` the committed path from disk) before retry; make `_recover_from_invalid_object`
   a **bounded loop** rather than one-shot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause confirmed: a targeted repro demonstrates a background `gc --auto` (or manual
      `git gc` under load) is what prunes the object referenced by the failing commit.
- [ ] The durable write path no longer loses writes under the test's load: 
      `test_enrich_queue_prune_never_drops_concurrent_locked_writes` passes **50/50 consecutive
      runs locally** under xdist parallelism (currently flakes).
- [ ] `main` post-merge CI passes this test across **10 consecutive** pushes after the fix lands
      (was failing ~9/12).
- [ ] The chosen gc trade-off is documented (a code comment + the ticket) explaining the
      interaction between WU-1's gc re-enablement and the write path, so it is not silently
      re-reverted.
- [ ] No regression in the durable-write / enrich-drain unit + integration tiers
      (`make test` green).

## Notes / Provenance
Discovered while landing epic 6982's R6 change (`5dac`, Gerrit #760): #760 touches nothing in
`src/rebar/_store/*` yet failed this test on CI, while sibling #761 (superset runtime tree)
passed — i.e. a probabilistic store-layer race, not a defect in the plan-review changes. Full
diagnosis captured here so a maintainer can pick it up; not in epic 6982's plan-review scope.
baseline.summary: Durable write path drops concurrent locked writes: background git auto-gc races object DB

## Why
Epic AC7 specifies the enforcement merge-gate as `rebar verify-identity
--require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>` that (a) exits non-zero when any
enforced event is not `certified`, (b) emits one structured report entry
`{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict, display}` per non-certified event, (c)
**grandfathers** pre-cutover events, and (d) runs as a CI merge-gate workflow. The delivered
gate (3183 / change 580) meets the SPIRIT (`rebar verify-authorship`, opt-in via config,
non-zero exit, replay-never-rejects, fsck/show grouping) but not the LETTER: wrong command
name, no `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags, text-only output (no JSON report), no
`enforce_since` grandfathering, and no CI workflow file. The epic completion-verifier flagged
AC7 unmet. This story builds AC7 in full. (Remediation of epic gnu-whale-ichor; user chose
"build it".)

## What
Build the AC7 enforcement surface on top of the delivered merge-gate, in
`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (+ config + a report schema + a CI workflow):

- **`rebar verify-identity` command.** Make `verify-identity` the canonical command name
  (add it to the CLI intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`), keeping `verify-authorship`
  as a back-compat alias routing to the same `cli()`. Regenerate the CLI reference
  (`docs/cli-reference.md`) + INTERCEPT_COMMANDS/_LADDER so the drift gate stays green.
- **`--require-authenticated` flag.** Forces enforcement ON for the run regardless of
  `identity.require_authenticated` config (the CI job passes it explicitly). Without it,
  config governs (unchanged).
- **`--since <ref>` grandfathering.** Default from a new `identity.enforce_since` config
  key (env `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE`). An event is ENFORCED iff its introducing commit
  is `<ref>` or a descendant of `<ref>` (at/after cutover, via `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor <ref> <event_commit>`); an event whose commit does NOT descend `<ref>` is
  **grandfathered** — its verdict is still computed and reported, but it never fails the
  gate. With no `--since`/`enforce_since`, all events are enforced (current behavior).
- **`--format json` report.** Emit a JSON array of entries
  `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict, display}` — one per NON-`verified`
  in-scope event (with a `grandfathered: bool`), validated against a new
  `src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json`. `display` is the grouping
  (`verified`/`unverified`/`unsigned`); `verdict` is the raw verdict. Default output stays
  the existing human text.
- **CI merge-gate workflow.** Add `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (or a gated step)
  that runs `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>`
  over the merged log and fails the build on a non-zero exit.
- Exit semantics: non-zero iff an ENFORCED (non-grandfathered) event is not `verified`
  (`certified`), under `--require-authenticated` (or config). Grandfathered/advisory → 0.

## Scope
In: the `verify-identity` command name + alias, `--require-authenticated`/`--since` flags,
`enforce_since` config + env, the JSON report + its schema, grandfathering by commit
ancestry, and the CI workflow. Out: the per-event classification itself (delivered +
TS2/TS3, unchanged) and the schema verdict enum (AC10). Folds into the 3183 commit (change
580); the CI workflow + report schema are new files in that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity --all` behaves as the merge-gate (same classification), and
  `rebar verify-authorship --all` still works as an alias (test both dispatch).
- [ ] `--require-authenticated` forces enforcement: with config off, `rebar verify-identity
  --require-authenticated --all` still exits non-zero on an unsigned/non-verified enforced
  event (test asserts exit code).
- [ ] `--since <ref>` grandfathers pre-cutover events: with an unsigned event introduced
  BEFORE the cutover ref and another AFTER, `--require-authenticated --since <ref>` fails
  ONLY for the post-cutover one; the pre-cutover event is reported `grandfathered` and does
  NOT fail the gate (test asserts exit code + that the pre-cutover event is grandfathered).
- [ ] `--format json` emits an array of `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author, verdict,
  display, grandfathered}` entries for the non-verified events, validating against
  `verify_identity_report.schema.json`; a test asserts an entry's field set + that `display`
  is the grouping value and `verdict` the raw verdict.
- [ ] A CI workflow file exists under `.github/workflows/` that invokes `rebar
  verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <…>` as a gating job (test/asserts the
  file exists and references the command).
- [ ] The CLI-reference drift gate passes (verify-identity documented; alias noted).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` (verify-identity name + --require-authenticated/--since flags + JSON report + grandfathering)
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (intercept verify-identity + alias verify-authorship)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` (identity.enforce_since + env REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE)
- `src/rebar/schemas/verify_identity_report.schema.json` (new report schema)
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yaml` (new CI merge-gate workflow)
- `docs/cli-reference.md` (regenerated: verify-identity)
baseline.summary: identity: verify-identity enforcement CLI + --since grandfathering + JSON report + CI gate (epic AC7)

## Bootstrap the shared Rebar Bot signing identity

No identity ticket or SSH authorship key exists yet. Create the one the AWS + GitHub bot
environments will share, and provision its private key into both secret stores.

- Generate an ed25519 keypair for the bot (private key never committed to the repo).
- Create the identity: `rebar identity create --name "Rebar Bot" --email joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com --key "ssh-ed25519 …"` (the `identity` type is gate-exempt, so this bootstrap write is not blocked even under enforcement).
- Declare the SSM parameter in IaC: add `"/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key"` to the
  `rebar_secret_params` list in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` (so Terraform owns the parameter's
  existence + SecureString type, matching every other `/rebar/prod/*` secret; the resource is
  created as a `CHANGEME` placeholder with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`, and the
  real value is populated out-of-band). This is the one code change in this task (→ Gerrit).
- Provision the PRIVATE key VALUE into both secret stores (operator has AWS + GH CLI access):
  - AWS SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` (`aws ssm put-parameter --type SecureString`;
    bootstrapped now so the AWS bots can use it — Terraform adopts it on the next apply via the
    `ignore_changes = [value]` lifecycle, `terraform import` if a create-conflict arises, an operator/deploy step).
  - GitHub Actions secret `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` on `navapbc/rebar` (`gh secret set`).
  The per-env consumption wiring (fetch-secrets.sh materialization + container config in 245e; workflow env injection in 9e76/1787) references these already-provisioned secrets.
- Verify TOFU registration and that a `git config user.email = joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` resolves to this identity via the seam's resolver.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Rebar Bot identity ticket exists with its ed25519 PUBLIC key registered; `rebar list --type identity` (JSON) includes it with the key present.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Git-email resolution verified (runtime resolution, attested by recorded command output): with the store repo's `git config user.email = joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` and no overriding `.rebar/current_identity` pointer, `python3 -c "from rebar._commands.identity import resolve_current_identity; print(resolve_current_identity())"` returns the Rebar Bot identity ticket id (the resolver does a case-insensitive git-email match against identity tickets).
- [ ] `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` is added to `rebar_secret_params` in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` so the parameter is IaC-tracked (not created purely out-of-band).
- [ ] [operator-attested] The PRIVATE key is provisioned (out-of-band infra state, attested by recorded aws/gh output) as an SSM SecureString `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` AND a GitHub Actions secret `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` (both verifiable: `aws ssm get-parameter --name /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key --with-decryption` succeeds; `gh secret list --repo navapbc/rebar` shows `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY`). Nothing secret is committed to the repo; the private-key file used for provisioning lives only outside the repo tree and is discarded after.

# `sign-review` aborts on stray UNTRACKED tracker files — a missed site of already-fixed bug d7cb

## Symptom

`rebar review-plan <id>` returns **PASS** but cannot sign, and the documented recovery `rebar sign-review <id>` fails **deterministically** (3/3, not contention):

```
{"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "PASS",
 "reason": "plan review generation could not be collected: store-read-failure"}
```

Net effect: a plan that PASSED cannot be signed, so `claim` and the plan-review CLOSE gate stay blocked on a clean PASS. The billable LLM review runs and passes, and only then can the result not be persisted — the work is paid for and discarded.

## CORRECTION to this ticket's original filing

This ticket originally named `attest.py:406` as the cause. That was a **lead, and it is refuted** as the source of this symptom: the message text is emitted only at `resign.py:153`, wrapping `generation.collect`, and `attest.py` is not on that path. `attest.py` is a *sibling* (below), not the cause.

## PROVEN root cause

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:146` calls

```python
initial_generation = generation.collect(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)
```

omitting `ignore_untracked`, which defaults to `False` (`generation.collect(..., ignore_untracked: bool = False)`). That reaches `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(ignore_untracked=False)` → `tracker_head_sha(tracker)` strict, which runs

```python
("status", "--porcelain")            # untracked INCLUDED
```

instead of `("status","--porcelain","--untracked-files=no")`. Any untracked file makes the output non-empty → `_store_error` → `store-read-failure` → resign's wrapper reports "plan review generation could not be collected".

## Experimental proof (runtime, isolated temp git repo)

| condition | strict (`ignore_untracked=False`) | lenient (`True`) |
|---|---|---|
| clean tree | OK (control) | OK |
| untracked `.tmp-event-*` (partial JSON) | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| untracked file, UNRELATED name + content | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| TRACKED dirty (modified file) | RAISE | **RAISE** |

Row 3 **refutes** the competing "partial-JSON parse failure" hypothesis: the failure is entirely content- and name-agnostic, purely the `git status` check. Row 4 shows the flag does NOT weaken the real guarantee — tracked dirty state still fails, as it must.

Field observation that opened the case: two orphaned `.tmp-event-*` files (~16h stale, 0 tracked-dirty / 2 untracked) in the shared tracker; moving them out made the identical `sign-review` succeed with nothing else changed.

## Why it is a DEFECT (cited authority, not the reporter's expectation)

This is a **missed site of an already-fixed bug class**. Bug `d7cb-22ae` (commit `1475e2868`, "d7cb: plan-review tolerates unrelated untracked shared-tracker files") fixed exactly this in two places and landed two regression tests that state the contract:

- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_review_plan_preflight_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_sign_manifest_fence_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
  — labelled "**sibling on the SIGNING path**", and stating that otherwise a stray artifact
  "aborts signing (`store-read-failure`), so no durable attestation is persisted and the plan-review
  claim gate cannot pass even for a clean plan".

That fix touched `__init__.py` and `generation.py` but **never `resign.py`**. The intended behaviour is therefore already established and this site violates it.

## Blast radius

`.tickets-tracker` is symlinked into every session, so ONE crashed writer anywhere blocks signing for every concurrent session on the machine — the same machine-wide collapse d7cb was raised to prevent.

## SIBLINGS found by sweeping every untracked-sensitive call site

| site | call | symptom when an untracked file exists |
|---|---|---|
| `resign.py:146` | `generation.collect(...)` | HARD FAIL — `sign-review` refuses (this ticket's confirmed cause) |
| `orchestrator.py:650` | `generation.collect(...)` | SILENT COST — wrapped in `except Exception: return None` ("unstable generation falls back to a full review"), so a stray file forces a full multi-pass LLM re-review instead of the cheap drift-refresh probe |
| `attest.py:139` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | aborts signing on the fallback path (when no `initial_generation`/snapshot is supplied) |
| `attest.py:406` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | same, in `refresh_attestation` |

Already correct (fixed by d7cb): `__init__.py:495`, `generation.py:131/133/173`.

`orchestrator.py:650` is the most insidious: it fails INVISIBLY and the only symptom is money and latency — a full LLM review where a cheap probe was intended.

## Approach

Pass `ignore_untracked=True` at each of the four sites. These are all READS that fingerprint the COMMITTED head, which untracked files cannot change; the authoritative under-lock re-check (`generation.py:173`) already tolerates them, so this makes the class consistent.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — the confirmed defect.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — siblings.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py` — regression tests beside the two existing d7cb siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `resign_plan_review` still signs a valid PASS when an UNRELATED untracked file
      exists in the tracker, and fails RED before the fix
- [ ] a test asserts TRACKED dirty state still blocks these paths — the flag must not weaken the
      real guarantee
- [ ] the orchestrator drift-refresh path does not silently fall back to a full review because of an
      untracked file
- [ ] every `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` / `generation.collect` call site in `src/rebar` either
      passes `ignore_untracked=True` or carries a comment saying why strictness is intended
baseline.summary: sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files: attest.py omits ignore_untracked

## What
The single source of truth for every metric the command surfaces: a declarative registry mapping each metric id to its lens, data source, and compute, plus the graceful `unavailable{reason,accruing_since}` state and the `source`+`confidence` labels — so the command is written once and never modified as new signals accrue, and a classified/backfilled value is never aggregated into an authoritative structural series.

## Files
- `src/rebar/metrics/__init__.py` — new package.
- `src/rebar/metrics/registry.py` — new: `MetricSpec` (id, lens, source, confidence, compute), the `REGISTRY`, `MetricValue`/`Unavailable` result types, and an `is_authoritative(source)` segregation helper.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_registry.py` — new.

## Approach
A declarative registry (not per-metric scattered code) is what makes the command complete-once: rendering iterates the registry, and a metric with no data yet returns `Unavailable(reason, accruing_since)` rather than being absent, so a new signal lights up by populating its source with no CLI change. `source` in {structural, git, sidecar, snapshot, backfill_classified} and `confidence` in {high, classified} ride on every value so downstream aggregation can keep high-confidence structural series apart from fuzzy backfills. Additive and standalone — no existing behavior changes.

## Tests
- Unit (in-process, real registry): a metric whose compute returns no data yields `Unavailable` with populated `reason` + `accruing_since`; `is_authoritative('backfill_classified')` is False and a classified value is excluded from an authoritative rollup helper.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/unit/metrics/test_registry.py` passes: every `REGISTRY` entry has a unique id, a `lens`, a `source`, and a `confidence` — asserted by collecting the registry and checking `len(ids) == len(set(ids))`.
- [ ] A metric with no data returns `Unavailable` carrying a non-empty `reason` and an ISO `accruing_since` — unit test asserts both fields present.
- [ ] `is_authoritative('backfill_classified')` is False and an authoritative aggregation excludes classified values — unit test asserts a mixed input yields a series containing only `source in {structural,git,sidecar,snapshot}`.
baseline.summary: Metric registry + unavailable-state & source/confidence label contract

baseline.description:
The review-bot's structured operational logs (the `_emit()` INFO events —
`voter_voted`, `voter_skip`, `merge_detection`, and all `reconcile_*`) are silently
dropped in production, so operators are blind to what the bot decides. Configure a
logging handler for rebar's loggers so these reach stdout/journald.

## Why
`src/rebar/review_bot/` contains NO logging setup (`grep` for `basicConfig`/`dictConfig`
in `src/rebar/` returns nothing). The container runs `uvicorn rebar.review_bot.app:app`;
uvicorn configures only its own `uvicorn.*` loggers and never the root or `rebar.*`
loggers. So a `logging.getLogger("rebar.review_bot.voter").info(...)` record has no
handler and falls through to Python's `logging.lastResort`, which emits **WARNING and
above only** — every INFO `_emit` line is discarded. This was directly observed during
incident triage: `journalctl` showed uvicorn's own access lines and the `print()`-to-stderr
markers (`VOTER_ERROR`, `ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR`) but ZERO `voter_voted`/`reconcile_*` lines,
making a healthy-but-slow reconciler look dead. The `_emit` docstrings call these
"observability markers" — dropping them violates that documented intent.

## What
Add a `_configure_logging()` to `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`, called once at module import
(before `app = FastAPI(...)`), that attaches a `StreamHandler(sys.stdout)` to the `rebar`
logger at level `INFO` (overridable via a `REVIEW_BOT_LOG_LEVEL` env var), with a bare
`"%(message)s"` formatter (the `_emit` payload is already JSON), an idempotency marker on the
handler (so repeated imports/reloads don't stack handlers), and `propagate=False` (so records
do NOT double-log through uvicorn/root). Targeting the `rebar` logger specifically — not root
— avoids duplicating uvicorn's access logs.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py`: add `_configure_logging()` + `import sys`; call at import.
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`: add a test asserting a `rebar.review_bot.*` INFO record
  reaches stdout after the app module configures logging (RED before the fix).
- Non-goal (separate follow-up): shipping logs to a shared service (CloudWatch Logs group).
  This change makes the logs *emitted*; centralizing them is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `logging.getLogger("rebar.review_bot.voter").info(...)` record is written to stdout
      once the review-bot app module has configured logging; before the fix the same record
      produces no stdout output (proving the drop).
      Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k configure_logging -q`
      passes, and the test is confirmed RED on the pre-fix tree.
- [ ] The handler is idempotent: importing/configuring twice does not attach a second handler
      (no duplicate log lines).
      Proving command: assert `len([h for h in logging.getLogger("rebar").handlers if marker])
      == 1` after two `_configure_logging()` calls (in the test).
- [ ] `REVIEW_BOT_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` lowers the effective level (env override honored); an
      absent/invalid value falls back to INFO.
      Proving command: covered by a parametrized assertion in the test.
- [ ] Existing gates stay green.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -q` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: review-bot: configure logging so structured _emit INFO events reach stdout/journald

Bug d843 bounds the ACLI subprocess. But the GIT network ops have the same unbounded-hang exposure and are OUTSIDE the acli path: _store/sync.py:116 `git fetch origin tickets` and _store/push.py `git push` (and _attestation.py:107 `git verify-commit`, which can hang on gpg-agent/keyserver) all call subprocess.run with NO timeout. A stuck remote or gpg-agent freezes the write/sync/attestation path.
## What

- Add bounded `timeout=` to the network git subprocesses: _store/sync.py `_ok`/fetch path, _store/push.py `_run`/push path. Treat timeout as best-effort failure (these are already best-effort) — never hang.
- Add a timeout to _attestation.py:107/118 git verify-commit (gpg-agent hang).
- These are local/simple git calls (no pipe-holding grandchildren), so a plain subprocess.run(timeout=) suffices — NOT the acli process-group treatment.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] git fetch (sync.py) + git push (push.py) have a bounded timeout; a stuck remote does not hang the caller (best-effort failure preserved)
- [ ] git verify-commit (_attestation) bounded against gpg-agent hang
- [ ] Unit test: a stubbed slow git command surfaces a bounded timeout
- [ ] Suite green; ruff clean

# Tier-1 opportunistic detached drain + `rebar enrich` CLI

## Why
The feature must run async across server/PC/Mac/cloud with ZERO client setup — no daemon, broker, or scheduler. The proven pattern (git gc --auto, npm update-notifier) piggybacks a cheap, detached drain on ordinary invocations. rebar ships the POSIX half of this already for async push (`src/rebar/_store/push.py:108`).

## What
- A `maybe_drain()` gate on ordinary invocations: a cheap "is anything soaked+unclaimed?" check that no-ops in the common case, else DETACHES the enrichment to a child that outlives the command.
- **Detach, POSIX in v1 (Windows drain is a documented no-op):** POSIX reuses push.py's approach (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`) + its PYTHONPATH bootstrap. **Windows drain is explicitly a NO-OP in v1** and `maybe_drain` returns early on `os.name == "nt"` (logging "windows drain deferred"), for a concrete reason the reviewer surfaced: the store's write lock `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` imports `fcntl` UNCONDITIONALLY at module top, so a detached drain child on Windows would crash at import the moment it touched the write path (`append_event` → `stage_and_commit` → `lock`). Rather than spawn a doomed child, v1 gates the detach to POSIX. The Windows `creationflags=subprocess.DETACHED_PROCESS | subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW` branch is still AUTHORED (API-derisked; these constants exist only on Windows — referenced ONLY inside the `os.name == "nt"` branch so the POSIX import never AttributeErrors) and unit-tested by kwargs selection, but is not reached by `maybe_drain` in v1. Making `lock.py` Windows-safe (conditional `fcntl` import) is spun out as a follow-up idea — Tier-1 targets server/PC/Mac; Windows drain is deferred, not blocking.
- **Observability:** the child configures a `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler` (maxBytes+backupCount bounded) writing to `.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log` (git-ignored) and redirects its own stderr there; stdout/stdin are DEVNULL — drain failures stay diagnosable.
- **Drainer loop (owns DONE + self-healing + growth-bound, moved here from S3):** from `pending_enrichment(now)` PLUS the fallback scan (tickets certified but with absent/stale digest — the defense-in-depth), claim one via the queue's OPTIMISTIC `queue.claim(ticket_id, drainer_id, …)` (append + earliest-live-lease arbitration — NOT a held `lock.acquire`, because `append_event` self-serializes writes under the store write lock and a claim cannot hold that lock across its own append; "one drainer lands, losers retry" is realized by post-append arbitration, per S4), run `enrich` (S1), write `TICKET_DIGEST` (S2), append `DONE_ENRICH`, then `prune` the ticket's queue events so log growth is bounded. **Prune rule (concrete, no "cycle" ambiguity):** keep=1 — retain ONLY the single latest queue event per ticket by HLC (the `DONE_ENRICH` tombstone just written), and drop ALL superseded queue events for that ticket (every prior `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`, `CLAIM_ENRICH`, and older `DONE_ENRICH`). The retained `DONE_ENRICH` means "not pending" to the reducer until a later `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` (a re-certification) supersedes it. This bounds each ticket's queue footprint to one event (mirrors the digest-sidecar `prune(keep=1)`). Process UP TO `DRAIN_BATCH` per run, then exit.
- **The drain's OWN lenient advisory lock (distinct from the store write lock AND from the optimistic queue-claim):** to stop two concurrent drain PROCESSES from doing redundant work, the drain takes a best-effort advisory lock file `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` (a non-blocking `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` create, or an equivalent flock with immediate timeout). If it is already held, the drain exits SILENTLY with code 0 (logged to the drain log) — it does NOT block/wait. This is a separate, drain-level lock: it is NOT the store write lock (`_store/lock.py`, held only briefly inside each `append_event`) and NOT the queue claim (which is optimistic append + arbitration, holding no lock). `test_lock_held_skip` exercises THIS advisory lock: a second drain invocation with the lock already held returns 0 without processing. Per-item error handling: an `enrich` exception (LLM timeout/rate-limit) releases the claim (lease expiry) and is logged; the batch continues to the next ticket; the failed ticket is re-picked on a later drain.
- **CLI `rebar enrich`:** `--drain` (bounded drain, the detached target), `--once` (claim+process one entry, in-process, tests), `status` (prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` from the queue reducer). **Bucket predicates (co-located with the CLI spec, computed by `queue.reduce_ticket(now)` per ticket, mutually exclusive):** `soaking` = has a latest `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` with `not_before_ns > now` and no later `DONE_ENRICH` (still in the soak window); `claimed` = past soak with a latest `CLAIM_ENRICH` (after the latest enqueue) whose `lease_expires_ns > now` and no later `DONE_ENRICH` (a live lease); `pending` = past soak, unclaimed-or-lease-expired, and no `DONE_ENRICH` after the latest enqueue (exactly what `queue.pending_enrichment` returns). A ticket with a `DONE_ENRICH` after its latest enqueue is in NONE of the three buckets. `overlap_drain ∈ {off, async, always}`, DEFAULT `async` (`async` = the opportunistic detached drain of this design; `always` = synchronous inline drain for tests/CI; `off` = no drain). Opt-out is `overlap_drain = "off"` on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`), env `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN` (the ONE canonical name — used in What, Scope, and ACs identically). `overlap_drain` is a STRING enum (`off|async|always`) so it lives on `LLMConfig` (read via `from_env`), NOT `VerifyConfig` (which is bool-only via `_as_bool`).

## Constants (defaults stated)
`DRAIN_BATCH = 5`, `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS = 20` — both on `LLMConfig`.

## maybe_drain injection point (decided)
`maybe_drain()` is invoked from `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py::write_and_push` immediately
after `push.push_tickets_branch` — the HIGH-FREQUENCY write path taken by
create/edit/comment/link/tag/sign/set_* (the bulk of ordinary invocations), behind a cheap
soaked?-check that no-ops on the common event. NOTE (reviewer-surfaced): the status-only
writes `transition`/`reopen`/`claim`/`compact`/`delete` use a SEPARATE push path
(`push.push_after_commit`, `push.py:267-286`), so a `maybe_drain` in `write_and_push` does NOT
fire for those. That is ACCEPTABLE and deliberate: the drain is OPPORTUNISTIC and
SELF-HEALING — a soaked ticket does not need every write to trigger a drain; it WILL be drained
on the next create/edit/comment anywhere in the store (and the fallback scan re-picks any
cert-without-fresh-digest ticket regardless). To avoid a rare cold-store gap where ONLY
status-only writes occur, `maybe_drain()` is ALSO called at the end of
`push.push_after_commit` (the same one-line cheap-gated call), so both push paths carry it.
`test_gate_latency` asserts the cheap gate no-ops within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` and spawns
nothing when nothing is soaked.

## Dependencies
S1 (enrich op), S2 (digest store), S3/S4 (queue + claim primitive + event types). This story
WIRES them; they are prerequisite sibling stories, not existing code.

**Event-type ownership (resolves the "DONE_ENRICH unregistered" concern):** the three queue
event types — `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`, `CLAIM_ENRICH`, `DONE_ENRICH` — are added to
`event_append.EVENT_TYPES` (write allow-list) and `reducer._version._NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES`
by the QUEUE story S4 (`vegan-forgetful-tiger`, `e1f4`), which this story `depends_on`. This
story only **emits** `DONE_ENRICH` (and appends `CLAIM_ENRICH`) via the drainer loop — it does
NOT re-register the types. Because S4 lands below S6 in the stack, the types exist before this
story's writes run; `test_done_enrich_registered` asserts `DONE_ENRICH in event_append.EVENT_TYPES`
as a guard so a missing prerequisite fails loudly rather than raising a StoreError at drain time.

## Scope
- New `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py`; CLI arm in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` (`rebar enrich` with `--drain`/`--once`/`status`); **CLI dispatch intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`** — add `if argv and argv[0] == "enrich": return _llm_commands.cmd_enrich(argv[1:], tracker)` alongside the existing `review`/`review-plan`/`verify-completion` intercepts (~line 375-400); without it `rebar enrich` is unroutable. The `maybe_drain` hook called from `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py::write_and_push` (after `push_tickets_branch`) AND from `src/rebar/_store/push.py::push_after_commit`, so BOTH write push paths carry the opportunistic drain; plus the drain's advisory lock file `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock`.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: add `overlap_drain` (str enum `off|async|always`, default `async`), `overlap_drain_batch` (int, default 5), `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms` (int, default 20) as `LLMConfig` fields AND wire them in `from_env()`: `overlap_drain=_llm_str(table, cli, "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN", "overlap_drain", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN)` (validate the value is in `{off,async,always}`, else fall back to default), `overlap_drain_batch=_llm_int(..., "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH", "overlap_drain_batch", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH)`, `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms=_llm_int(..., "REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS", "overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms", DEFAULT_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS)`, with the three `DEFAULT_*` module constants.
- OUT: native scheduler (idea Tier-2), CI drain (idea Tier-3).

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`: `test_once` (one entry end-to-end, FakeRunner); `test_batch_cap` (`DRAIN_BATCH` bound, backlog drains over runs); `test_gate_latency` (maybe_drain no-op < `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS`, no spawn when nothing soaked); `test_lock_held_skip` (silent exit 0, logged); `test_enrich_error_continues` (one enrich() raises → claim released, batch continues); `test_no_key_noop` ([agents]/key absent → clean no-op); `test_opt_out` (`REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off`); `test_self_heal` (certified-but-stale-digest ticket picked up by fallback scan); `test_windows_detach_kwargs` (the authored os.name=="nt" branch selects the DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW creationflags — mocked, not spawned); `test_windows_noop` (with `os.name` mocked to "nt", `maybe_drain` returns early WITHOUT spawning any child — the documented v1 Windows no-op, since lock.py's fcntl import would crash a Windows drain child); `test_status` (`rebar enrich status` prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` derived from the queue reducer over a seeded store — exact counts asserted); `test_done_enrich_registered` (`DONE_ENRICH in event_append.EVENT_TYPES` — the S4-prerequisite guard); `test_always_mode` (with `overlap_drain="always"`, a write-path `maybe_drain` runs the drain SYNCHRONOUSLY inline — no detached child — and the entry is processed before the call returns; the CI/test mode); `test_cli_dispatch` (`rebar enrich status` routes through the `_cli/__init__.py` intercept and returns 0); `test_config` (sets `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS`; `LLMConfig.from_env()` resolves them; an invalid `overlap_drain` value falls back to the default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar enrich --drain` processes up to `DRAIN_BATCH` (default 5) soaked+unclaimed entries then exits; backlog drains over successive runs; `pytest ...::test_batch_cap`.
- [ ] `maybe_drain` no-ops with no spawn when nothing soaked, within `DRAIN_GATE_BUDGET_MS` (20 ms); detaches a surviving child otherwise; `::{test_gate_latency}`.
- [ ] A single `enrich` failure releases the claim, logs, and the batch continues; the ticket re-drains later; `::test_enrich_error_continues`. Self-healing fallback picks up cert-without-fresh-digest tickets; `::test_self_heal`.
- [ ] `[agents]`/key absent → clean no-op; `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off` disables the opportunistic drain (single canonical env name); `::{test_no_key_noop,test_opt_out}`.
- [ ] Detach is `os.name`-branched and POSIX-only in v1: POSIX `start_new_session`; the Windows `DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW` branch is authored (referenced only in the nt branch) but `maybe_drain` no-ops on Windows — no child is spawned, because `lock.py`'s unconditional `fcntl` import would crash a Windows drain child; `::{test_windows_detach_kwargs,test_windows_noop}`. Each processed ticket gets a `DONE_ENRICH` append + a `prune` of its queue events (bounding growth); verified by `::test_batch_cap` observing DONE + a post-drain pending count of 0.
- [ ] `rebar enrich status` prints JSON `{"pending":int,"claimed":int,"soaking":int}` with the mutually-exclusive bucket predicates defined above (soaking = not-yet-past-soak; claimed = live lease; pending = past-soak unclaimed-or-expired) computed from `queue.reduce_ticket`; `::test_status`.
- [ ] Concurrent drain PROCESSES don't double-work: a second drain with the advisory `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` held exits 0 silently (logged), without waiting or processing — distinct from the store write lock and the optimistic queue-claim; `::test_lock_held_skip`.
- [ ] `overlap_drain` (`off|async|always`), `overlap_drain_batch`, `overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms` are read from the env by `LLMConfig.from_env()` (invalid `overlap_drain` → default); `DONE_ENRICH` is registered (by S4) before drain writes; `::{test_config,test_done_enrich_registered}`.
- [ ] `overlap_drain="always"` runs the drain synchronously inline (no detached child), processing the entry before the write returns; `::test_always_mode`. `rebar enrich` is routed via the `_cli/__init__.py` dispatch intercept; `::test_cli_dispatch`.
- [ ] The prune step retains exactly the latest queue event per ticket (the `DONE_ENRICH` tombstone), dropping superseded `ENQUEUE_ENRICH`/`CLAIM_ENRICH`/older `DONE_ENRICH` (keep=1, bounded growth); verified by `::test_batch_cap` (post-drain per-ticket queue-event count == 1).
baseline.summary: Tier-1 opportunistic detached drain + `rebar enrich` CLI

## Why

`src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is grandfathered over the 800-LOC module-size soft cap (currently 849 LOC by `wc -l`; pinned at ceiling 850 in `.github/module-size-ceilings.txt`, listed in `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`, with a remedy row in the `docs/architecture.md` offenders table). This story graduates it off the gate by extracting a cohesive leaf module along an existing call-graph seam.

## Seam

`docs/architecture.md`'s remedy row for `llm/runner.py` names this exact seam: "extract the anthropic-model construction cluster (`_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, the httpx timeout/transport wiring) into a sibling `anthropic_model.py`". This plan follows that row and **widens it plainly**: the named construction cluster alone is close to the 100-LOC floor, so the extraction also pulls the co-resident provider/model-resolution + cache helpers that the same construction path calls (`_pai_model` + its `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` map, `_anthropic_cache_settings`, and the `_DIRECT_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS` / `_RETRY_STATUSES` constants). The result is a single "provider/model resolution + Anthropic model construction" leaf, and this ticket updates/removes the arch.md row accordingly.

## What moves (locate by NAME on current origin/main)

New leaf `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`: `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX`, `_anthropic_cache_settings`, `_DIRECT_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_RETRY_STATUSES`, `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, `_pai_model`. Heavy libraries (httpx, anthropic, pydantic_ai, tenacity, urllib) stay LAZY in-function imports in the new module, preserving the stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract. The leaf imports nothing back from `runner.py`.

## Back-compat

`runner.py` re-imports and re-exports the 5 externally referenced names (`_DIRECT_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `_anthropic_cache_settings`, `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`) with `# noqa: F401`, so `rebar.llm.runner.<symbol>` attribute access keeps resolving for the importing/monkeypatching tests. `PydanticAIRunner.run()` keeps calling these by BARE re-exported name so the `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_module, "_pai_model", ...)` (and `_anthropic_cache_settings` / `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url` / `_build_retrying_anthropic_model`) seam still works. `import os` becomes unused in `runner.py` after the move and is deleted (ruff F401).

## Nature of change / testing plan

This is a pure/mechanical refactor: no signature or logic change, symbols moved verbatim. E5 testing-plan is not-applicable — the existing tests are the oracle (`tests/unit/test_transport_retry.py`, `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py`, `tests/unit/test_runner_local_proxy_bypass.py`, `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py`, plus `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` and `test_llm_framework.py` which access/monkeypatch the re-exported names).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` exists and is in [100, 800] LOC (verify: `wc -l src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`)
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` is <=800 LOC (verify: `wc -l src/rebar/llm/runner.py`)

content.text: # Finish Jira hard-delete -> outbound re-create (replaces lost epic-3e36)
## Why
On a Jira hard-delete the reconciler preserves local content (ADR 0027/0028) BUT never re-creates the Jira
issue. The path is broken at two joints:
- **Key mismatch**: `route_inbound_probe` (reconcile.py:316-324, ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED branch) builds the
inbound-delete Mutation with `payload={"reason": "hard_delete", ...}`, but `_apply_inbound_delete`
(apply_inbound.py:184) reads `payload.get("probe_outcome", "out_of_window")` — so the hard_delete branch is
UNREACHABLE (always defaults to out_of_window).
- **Dropped follow-on**: even when the branch is reached it builds a `follow_on`
(apply_inbound.py:202-210, keys `direction/action/target/local_id`, `action="create_after_hard_delete"`, NO
`fields`), but the applier consumer (applier.py:467-468) only handles `follow_on.get("kind")=="suppress_pair"`
— the `create_after_hard_delete` follow-on (which sets `action`, not `kind`) is silently ignored. This is the
`epic-3e36` TODO (apply_inbound.py:209-210).
## What (one coherent path: inbound detect -> standard outbound CREATE mutation)
1. **Canonical key = `reason`.** Change `_apply_inbound_delete` (apply_inbound.py:184) to read
`payload.get("reason") or payload.get("probe_outcome", "out_of_window")` (accept `reason`, keep back-compat).
Update ALL `probe_outcome` fixture sites in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py`
— verified there are exactly TWO: line 281 (`payload = {"probe_outcome": outcome}`, the parametrized test
covering all four outcomes incl. hard_delete) and line 332 (`payload={"probe_outcome": "redirect", ...}`).
Both must carry `reason` (parametrize both keys, or switch to `reason`). (The review's guess of line 289 is
stale — no `probe_outcome` there on current main.)
2. **Reconstruct `fields`.** The follow-on carries `local_id` but not `fields`, and `create_one`
(dispatch_one.py:147-156, 168) REQUIRES a `mutation["fields"]`. Fetch the still-present LOCAL ticket by
`local_id` and map it via `_map_local_to_jira_fields(ticket, binding_store=binding_store,
local_ticket_types=local_ticket_types, emit_detach_clear=False)` (outbound_fields.py:112-117) — the SAME mapper
the outbound differ uses (returns summary/description/issuetype/priority/status/assignee, and `parent` only when
the parent is bound). Pass the SAME `local_ticket_types` map the outbound path builds (local_id -> ticket_type,
from the loaded local tickets) so the non-epic-parent suppression guard behaves identically to a normal
outbound create; if it is not readily in scope, build a minimal one from the single fetched ticket (its own
type) — an unbound/absent parent is simply omitted and reconciled on a later pass (create_one is
parent-tolerant).
- **Lookup mechanism (explicit):** the applier inbound loop (applier.py:455-474) has NO `local_tickets` in
scope, and there is no by-id helper. `repo_root` IS in scope; read `<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker/<local_id>/
.cache.json` `state` directly (single-ticket, cheap), falling back to `reconcile_check.load_local_tickets`
only if the cache is absent.
- **Failure path:** wrap the `.cache.json` read in `try/except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError)`. If the local
ticket is absent, the cache is malformed, or `_map_local_to_jira_fields` yields empty/no-summary, do NOT emit
a create — log + skip (a hard-deleted ticket with no local content is not re-creatable). Tested.
3. **Wiring (dedicated pre-batch side-channel — must flow THROUGH `_apply_batch`).** Introduce a new
`pending_hard_delete_creates: list[dict]` local in `apply()` (declared next to `pending_bug_tickets` at
applier.py:453). In the inbound loop (L455-474), when `follow_on.get("action")=="create_after_hard_delete"`,
build a batch-dict CREATE entry (a **dict**, NOT a typed `Mutation`, because `outbound_list` is already a
`list[dict]`) shaped like a normal outbound create — `{"action":"create","key":<jira-target-or-"">,
"local_id":local_id,"fields":<mapped fields>}` (match the dict keys `_apply_batch`/`create_one` read: `fields`
+ `local_id`; use `_mutation_to_batch_dict` if you build a Mutation first) — and append it to
`pending_hard_delete_creates`.
Then, AFTER `outbound_list` is materialised + suppression-filtered (applier.py:486-490) and BEFORE the
`_apply_batch(outbound_list, …)` dispatch (L495), do `outbound_list.extend(pending_hard_delete_creates)`.
**This is DELIBERATELY unlike `pending_bug_tickets`**, which drains in the `finally` AFTER `_apply_batch`
(L503-521) via a separate `in_process_cli` call and thus BYPASSES `create_one`. The re-create MUST go through
`_apply_batch` -> `create_one` so it gets JQL dedup + `bind_confirm`. It shares only the *collection* idea
(a side-channel list populated in the inbound loop), not the drain site. No mid-loop `create_one`, no
typed-dispatch bypass.
### Follow-on dict schema (both discriminants coexist)
The applier's inbound-loop follow-on routing keys off TWO independent discriminants, kept as-is:
- `follow_on["kind"] == "suppress_pair"` -> `suppression.record(...)` (existing).
- `follow_on["action"] == "create_after_hard_delete"` -> the new re-create path (this ticket). Keys:
`direction, action, target, local_id` (no `fields` — reconstructed in step 2).
A given follow-on carries exactly one of `kind`/`action`; the routing checks both independently.
4. **Idempotency + deferral.** `create_one`'s JQL dedup (`labels = "rebar-id:<local_id>"`, dispatch_one.py:
194-219) prevents double-create on retry. If `rest_calls >= _REST_CALL_BUDGET` (=200, dispatch_one.py:97,
188-192) `create_one` issues zero REST calls, appends to `deferred_creates`, returns None -> the re-create
DEFERS to the next pass (same as the normal create path). Test BOTH partial-failure directions:
(a) create ok but a following rebind/confirm fails; (b) create deferred by budget exhaustion.
5. **Stale reverse-index cleanup.** `bind_confirm(local_id, jira_key)` (binding_store.py:276-288) overwrites
`bindings[local_id]["jira_key"]` and sets `reverse[jira_key]=local_id` but never removes the OLD key's reverse
entry (no `rebind` method exists; only `unbind` pops reverse). Fix: at the TOP of `bind_confirm`, read
`old_key = entry.get("jira_key")` BEFORE overwriting; if `old_key and old_key != jira_key`, `reverse.pop(old_key,
None)` in the SAME save. Edits `binding_store.py`.
6. **Guard + housekeeping.** Guard the re-create so ONLY a genuine `reason=="hard_delete"` triggers it (redirect/
out_of_window/trash never re-create). Repoint/remove the `TODO(epic-3e36)` at apply_inbound.py:209-210. Update
ADR 0027/0028 to document the now-completed re-create behavior (inbound consumer injects an outbound CREATE
into the same pass). Clear the `.joe-janitor/report` flag if present.
## Scope (files EDITED)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` — key fix (read `reason`) + TODO repoint
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — consume `create_after_hard_delete`; NEW import
`from .outbound_fields import _map_local_to_jira_fields` (the new cross-module coupling lives HERE — applier ->
outbound_fields); local-ticket lookup; `pending_hard_delete_creates` injection into `outbound_list`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — stale `reverse[old_key]` cleanup in `bind_confirm`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py` — fixture key updates (L281, L332)
- new test file `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_hard_delete_recreate.py` — consumer + rebind + failure + guard
- `docs/adr/0027*.md` / `0028*.md` — document completed behavior
**Read-only (NOT edited), noted for the coupling:** `outbound_fields.py` (`_map_local_to_jira_fields` is
imported/called by applier.py, not modified); `dispatch_one.py` (`create_one` behavior relied on, not changed).
## Acceptance Criteria
Each AC names its proving test (all under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`; run with
`pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ -q`).
- [ ] `_apply_inbound_delete` reads `reason` (canonical) with `probe_outcome` fallback; the hard_delete branch is
reachable from EITHER key. Both fixture sites (test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py L281, L332) updated. Proof:
`test_hard_delete_recreate.py::test_reason_key_enters_hard_delete_branch` AND
`::test_probe_outcome_key_still_enters_hard_delete_branch` (both keys asserted; the fallback is NOT dead).
- [ ] The applier consumes `action=="create_after_hard_delete"`: fetches the local ticket by `local_id`,
reconstructs `fields` via `_map_local_to_jira_fields`, and injects a batch-dict CREATE into `outbound_list`
before `_apply_batch`. Proof: `test_hard_delete_recreate.py::test_recreate_injected_into_outbound_batch`
asserts the fake acli client records a `create_issue` for the local_id (i.e. it flowed through `create_one`,
not a post-batch bypass).
- [ ] Consumer failure path: local ticket absent / `.cache.json` malformed / no mappable summary -> log + skip,
no create emitted. Proof: `::test_recreate_skips_when_local_ticket_absent` and
`::test_recreate_skips_on_malformed_cache`.
- [ ] Idempotency + deferral: JQL dedup prevents a double-create on retry; REST-budget exhaustion defers to the
next pass. Proof: `::test_recreate_jql_dedup_no_double_create` (create-ok, second pass dedups) and
`::test_recreate_deferred_when_budget_exhausted`.
- [ ] `bind_confirm` deletes the stale `reverse[old_key]` (read BEFORE overwrite) in the same save. Proof:
`test_binding_store.py::test_bind_confirm_rebind_drops_stale_reverse_key` asserts `reverse` has no dangling
old-key entry after a rebind.
- [ ] Guard: only `reason=="hard_delete"` re-creates (redirect/out_of_window/trash do not). Proof:
`::test_non_hard_delete_branches_do_not_recreate` (parametrized over the other outcomes).
- [ ] Housekeeping (each with a concrete check):
(a) `grep -rn "epic-3e36" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound.py` returns NO stale TODO (either
removed, or repointed to `c244`);
(b) `grep -rl "re-create" docs/adr/0027*.md docs/adr/0028*.md` (or the equivalent updated-behavior phrase)
matches — the ADR now documents that a hard-delete re-creates the Jira issue via a same-pass outbound CREATE;
(c) `test -e .joe-janitor/report && grep -L "hard-delete" .joe-janitor/report` — the stale janitor flag for
this item is cleared (or the file is absent).
- [ ] End-to-end test: a single reconcile pass driven from an inbound hard-delete probe result produces an
outbound CREATE for the still-present local ticket, asserted via the fake acli client's recorded create
call. Proof: `::test_hard_delete_recreate_end_to_end_one_pass` — distinct from the unit branch/consumer
tests (it drives the full `apply()` pass, not `_apply_inbound_delete` in isolation).

baseline.summary: Finish Jira hard-delete -> outbound re-create (replaces lost epic-3e36)

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

Discovered while fixing 1a47-61a4-a981-4398 (the review-bot stop_grace_period). That ticket raised the grace period so an in-flight store write has room to finish, but two unbounded residues remain that make any grace-period constant unprovable. Both are in the review path, not in compose, so they were left out of scope there.

**1. The store write runs ON the asyncio event loop, so the declared bounds cannot fire.** `voter.py` calls the synchronous `emit_code_review_artifact` (a plain `def`) directly from the `review_and_vote` coroutine — no `await`, no `asyncio.to_thread`. Every store write it performs (`create_ticket`, `sidecar.emit`, one `link` per trailer ref) therefore blocks the loop thread.

Proven locally with two experiments:
  * Entering/exiting `app.lifespan` with `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS=0.2` and a worker doing a
    3.0s SYNCHRONOUS block took **3.00s** to shut down — the declared bound did not bound it.
  * A heartbeat task ticking every 0.1s showed a single **2.01s gap** across a 2.0s synchronous
    review — the loop is blocked for the whole write.

Because the loop is blocked, `asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=_shutdown_drain_seconds())` cannot fire, `task.cancel()` cannot be delivered, and the following `await task` is bounded by nothing. The same applies to `_worker`s `asyncio.wait_for(review_and_vote(...), timeout= review_timeout_seconds())` for the on-loop region, and to `/health`, which cannot answer while a write is running.

This falsifies three stated invariants: the `app.py` module docstring on the bounded drain, the `docker-compose.yml` comment that the grace period need only exceed `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS`, and the docstring of `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_lifespan_drain_is_bounded` ("a review that never returns must not hang shutdown"). That existing test passes only because it blocks the worker at `await asyncio.sleep(3600)` — an await point, where cancellation lands instantly.

**2. The lock-held git calls have no subprocess timeout.** `_store/event_append.py` runs `git add` / `git commit` via bare `subprocess.run(...)` with no `timeout=`, INSIDE `with lock.write_lock(...)`. `_store/push.py` passes `timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT` for the same class of call, so this is an inconsistency rather than a deliberate choice. A slow or contended tracker volume can hold the mkdir write lock indefinitely.

Together these mean the worst-case in-flight store write is not computable, so no `stop_grace_period` can be shown sufficient — only made generously large, which is what 1a47 did.

## Approach

Bound the shutdown path so a worst case exists, then re-derive the grace period from it. Likely shape: move the blocking emission off the event loop so the existing `wait_for` bounds become enforceable, bound the lifespan cancel/await, and give the lock-held git calls the same `_GIT_TIMEOUT` treatment `push.py` already uses. Note that moving work to a thread does not by itself make it cancellable, so the lifespan bound is required too.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` — the on-loop `emit_code_review_artifact` call.
- `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` — the lifespan cancel/await bound.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` — subprocess timeouts on the lock-held git calls.
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — re-derive `stop_grace_period` once a worst case exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A worker blocked in SYNCHRONOUS code no longer prevents the drain bound from firing;
      regression-tested with a synchronous (not await-based) worker, which the existing
      `test_lifespan_drain_is_bounded` does not cover.
- [ ] The lifespan cancel + await path is bounded end to end, so total shutdown has an upper
      bound that can be stated.
- [ ] The lock-held git calls in `event_append.py` carry a timeout, matching `push.py`.
- [ ] `stop_grace_period` is re-derived from the now-computable worst case, and the honest-limit
      note in `docker-compose.yml` is removed or updated.
baseline.summary: review-bot shutdown and per-review timeouts are unenforceable: the store write runs synchronously on the event loop, and its lock-held git calls have no timeout

baseline.description:
## Finding

`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`'s `verify_findings()` is the shared Pass-2 kernel
entry point that chunks findings, runs each chunk via an injected `run_chunk` LLM callable, and
tallies `outcome_counts` (`clean`/`recovered`/`empty_outcomes`/`unrecoverable`) plus
`contract_violations`. It is fully implemented and unit-tested
(`tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py`, `tests/unit/test_review_kernel_rules.py`), but neither live
consumer pipeline calls it, and — per plan-review feedback on an earlier draft of this ticket —
neither CAN call it as-is: both pipelines run their Pass-2 model call as a declarative workflow
prompt step (one YAML step per token-budgeted chunk, merged by the executor), not as a
procedural loop with a `run_chunk` callback in scope. `verify_findings()`'s per-chunk
`outcome_counts` tally (which chunk was clean vs empty vs a `StructuredOutputError`) depends on
being IN that per-chunk loop; by the time `plan_review_decide`/`code_review_decide` see the
input, the workflow engine has already merged every chunk's output into one flat
`verifications` list, and per-chunk boundaries (which chunk contributed what) are gone. So
`empty_outcomes`/`unrecoverable` (chunk-level execution signals) are **not reconstructable** at
the `*_decide` step boundary without a separate architecture change (the verify prompt step
itself emitting per-chunk metadata as a named workflow output before the merge) — that is
explicitly deferred as follow-on work, not this ticket's scope.

What IS shared today, and inconsistently, between the two pipelines:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`'s `plan_review_decide` (~line 425) calls
  `review_kernel.reshape_verifications(...)` on the merged `verifications` list, and on
  `reshape.has_violations` (malformed/duplicate/unexpected indices) calls
  `orchestrator.record_contract_violation(reshape.summary())` — a run-scoped ContextVar sink
  (`plan_review/orchestrator.py:321-357`: `collect_contract_violations`/
  `record_contract_violation`/`drain_contract_violations`) activated in
  `gate_dispatch.produce_plan_review_verdict` (~line 171) and drained into
  `coverage["verification_contract_violations"]` in `plan_review_coach` (~line 563).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py`'s `code_review_decide` (~line 395) does the exact
  same `reshape_verifications(...)` call and `has_violations` check, but only
  `logger.error(...)`s — no sink exists for code-review, so the violation data never reaches
  `finalize_code_review_verdict`'s coverage, and there is no `outcome_counts` telemetry there at
  all.

## Scope note

`c2c5-53a7-2ce0-4d98` is a child of epic `6eca-183e-1cd2-4fb9` (Janitor Cleanup 2026-07-19),
discovered mid-run (`discovered_from` -> `1aa8-cdde-4ff6-40d0`) after the epic's other 5 leaves
had already been decomposed and were not in the epic's original plan/file_impact. It was left
open and unworked when the other 5 leaves closed, per an explicit scoping decision recorded on
the epic. It is now being completed under direct operator instruction ("Complete this story"),
which supersedes that earlier deferral.

## Remediation

Two concrete, single-path changes (no `run_chunk`/`verify_findings()` involvement — that
kernel entry point stays reserved for callers that own the procedural chunk loop, e.g. a
future non-workflow consumer):

1. **Shared contract-violation sink.** Move the existing ContextVar-backed sink
   (`collect_contract_violations`/`record_contract_violation`/`drain_contract_violations`,
   currently private to `plan_review/orchestrator.py`) into `review_kernel` (e.g.
   `review_kernel/verify.py` or a new `review_kernel/telemetry.py`) as the ONE implementation
   both pipelines import — not a duplicate. Update `plan_review/orchestrator.py`'s and
   `plan_review/workflow_ops.py`'s existing call sites to import it from its new home (a
   mechanical rename, no behavior change for plan-review). Wire the equivalent into
   `code_review`: activate `collect_contract_violations()` around the workflow run in
   `gate_dispatch._run_code_review_gate` (mirroring `produce_plan_review_verdict`'s
   `with assemble_context_cache(), collect_contract_violations(), gate_config(cfg):`), call
   `record_contract_violation(reshape.summary())` in `code_review_decide` when
   `reshape.has_violations` (replacing the bare `logger.error`, keeping the log too), and drain
   it into `finalize_code_review_verdict`'s verdict coverage as
   `coverage["verification_contract_violations"]`, mirroring plan-review's
   `coverage["verification_contract_violations"]` write in `plan_review_coach`.

2. **`outcome_counts` at the `*_decide` boundary (whole-run tally, not per-chunk).** Add a
   small shared helper in `review_kernel` — e.g.
   `decide_outcome_counts(raw_verifs: list, findings: list, reshape: VerificationReshape) ->
   dict[str, int]` — that derives a single-run `{"clean": int, "recovered": int,
   "empty_outcomes": int, "unrecoverable": int}` from data already available at the merged
   `*_decide` boundary:
   - `empty_outcomes = 1` if `findings` is non-empty but `raw_verifs` came back completely
     empty, else `0`.
   - `unrecoverable` is **always `0`** in this leaf — a `StructuredOutputError` inside one
     chunk is swallowed by the workflow engine's own repair/retry layer before the merged
     output ever reaches `*_decide`; a total verify-step failure already surfaces via the
     existing `coverage["verify_failed"]` signal (ticket 59bc/b24d), which this ticket does not
     touch. Tracking true per-chunk `unrecoverable` counts requires the verify prompt step
     itself to emit per-chunk metadata as a named workflow output before the merge — an
     explicitly deferred follow-on, not this ticket.
   - Otherwise (findings present and at least one verification came back):
     `recovered = 1, clean = 0` if `reshape.has_violations` (some entries were malformed/
     duplicate/unexpected but the run still produced usable verifications), else
     `clean = 1, recovered = 0`.
   Call this helper from both `plan_review_decide` and `code_review_decide` and add
   `outcome_counts` to each step's output dict (additive — no existing output key removed).
   Thread it into each pipeline's verdict coverage the same way `hierarchy_incomplete` was
   threaded in ticket b24d: `coverage["outcome_counts"]` set by `*_decide`'s output. No
   downstream INDETERMINATE/PASS logic changes — this is additive observability, exactly like
   the drop-in for `verification_contract_violations` above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan_review_decide` and `code_review_decide` both emit an `outcome_counts` field (a
      single-run `{clean, recovered, empty_outcomes, unrecoverable}` tally, `unrecoverable`
      always `0` per the documented boundary limitation above) computed by ONE shared
      `review_kernel` helper — no duplicated tallying logic between the two pipelines.
- [ ] `code_review_decide` records contract violations via the SAME shared
      `collect_contract_violations`/`record_contract_violation`/`drain_contract_violations`
      sink `plan_review_decide` uses (moved into `review_kernel`), activated in
      `gate_dispatch._run_code_review_gate` and drained into
      `finalize_code_review_verdict`'s `coverage["verification_contract_violations"]`.
- [ ] Existing plan-review and code-review test suites continue to pass unmodified (the sink
      move is a mechanical relocation — plan-review's behavior is byte-identical); new tests
      cover code-review's `outcome_counts`/contract-violation propagation specifically, and at
      least one test covers the moved sink from its new shared location for both pipelines.
- [ ] No change to either pipeline's decision thresholds, impact functions, or verdict shape
      (`outcome_counts` and `verification_contract_violations` are additive coverage keys only).

## Verify commands

- `pytest tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel_rules.py -q`
- `pytest tests/unit/plan_review -q`
- `pytest tests/unit/code_review -q`
- `pytest tests -q`
baseline.summary: Wire shared verify_findings outcome_counts telemetry into plan_review and code_review consumer pipelines

baseline.description:
## Context
During review-threshold re-tuning (2026-07) we found that genuinely high-severity plan-review AND code-review findings systematically score priority 0.60-0.69 and fall just under the 0.70 block bar. Root cause: `priority = validity x impact`, and `impact` is the unweighted MEAN of 5 severity attributes (prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility). A finding that is critical on one axis but 'easy'/'local' on others gets averaged down (e.g. critical prod-impact + easy reversibility + module blast -> impact ~= 0.67), so real blocks land below the bar and ship as advisory.

We worked around it by lowering per-criterion block_thresholds to 0.60, but the aggregation itself is the deeper lever.

## Why revisit
- Threshold-lowering is a blunt fix; it also admits any finding that happens to average ~0.60.
- The mean conflates 'severe on the dimension that matters' with 'mild overall'. A max, weighted, or severity-gated aggregation (e.g. a critical prod_impact should floor impact regardless of reversibility) would let high-severity findings clear the bar on merit without lowering thresholds globally.
- Same mechanism affects code-review (findings cap ~0.67).

## Possible directions (to design later)
- Weighted aggregation (prod_impact / blast_radius weighted higher than reversibility).
- max-of-attributes or a severity-gated floor for critical/major.
- Decouple 'is it block-worthy' from 'validity x mean-impact' entirely (a learned/ruled block-worthiness signal).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Not scheduled — parking-lot idea. Revisit after the 0.60 threshold change has run in production and we can measure block-rate/precision under it.
baseline.summary: Rework review impact aggregation — mean-of-5-attributes dilutes high-severity findings below the block bar

`verify.completion_floor_active` was assessed as fully implemented (no stubs; wired live
into `review_plan` at `llm/plan_review/__init__.py:536`) AND already calibrated: its
gold-set story 77cf is CLOSED, and `docs/calibration/completion_floor.md` records 30/30
floor decisions correct (κ=1.0) with zero must-never-suppress anchors dropped — stated
verbatim as "the evidence the operator needs before flipping the flag on". It has only
never been switched on. Enable it in THIS project to dogfood it on live reviews.

## What

- Set `verify.completion_floor_active = true` in this project's `rebar.toml` (schema
  default in `_config_schema.py:303` STAYS False for clients). Keep the companion tunables
  at their defaults (`completion_priority_floor = 0.4`, `completion_preserve_criteria =
  T5c,T10`) unless dogfooding evidence says otherwise.
- Identify + document the monitoring surface: every suppression is persisted to the
  plan-review SIDECAR `dropped[]` tagged `drop_reason="completion"` with full completion
  answers + `coverage.completion_floored_finding_ids` (`llm/plan_review/__init__.py:263,
  272-275`; `sidecar.py:342,358`). Document how to tail/audit it so a wrongly-suppressed
  finding is recoverable.
- OPTIONAL (judgment call, capture as a follow-up if declined): add a per-drop
  `logger.info` line at the drop site so live suppressions are visible without opening the
  sidecar — the successful-drop path currently logs nothing (only failures warn).

## Scope

Config activation + monitoring only — NO logic change to the floor. Risk is bounded:
advisory-only, container-only, 5-condition conjunction, fail-safe-to-keep everywhere. A
wrong suppression cannot change a PASS/BLOCK verdict and is always recoverable from the
sidecar. Rollback = set the key back to false.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `verify.completion_floor_active = true` present in this project's `rebar.toml`; schema default remains False.
- [ ] A short operator note (in `docs/calibration/completion_floor.md` or the plan-review-gate doc) explains how to audit completion-floor suppressions via the sidecar `dropped[]` / `drop_reason="completion"`.
- [ ] The completion floor is live and enabled on real plan-reviews in this project, and it never changes a PASS/BLOCK verdict. Demonstrated: a live container plan-review (epic 8d27, run from the worktree where `load_config(repo_root).verify.completion_floor_active` is True) executed the floor entry `_maybe_apply_completion_floor` with the flag on and delivered/closed children present; the verdict stayed PASS and zero findings were floored (the documented "none qualified" case — the epic's remediated plan surfaces no low-priority delivered-child findings for the floor to drop, so it correctly no-ops, fail-safe-to-keep). The floor's DROP behavior (that it does drop qualifying findings) is proven by the calibration gold-set (30/30 floor decisions correct, κ=1.0, zero must-never-suppress drops — docs/calibration/completion_floor.md) and the e2e test `tests/unit/test_completion_floor_e2e.py`.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass (the floor's existing unit/e2e tests stay green).
