## Why
Claiming with no `--assignee` (or with a non-Jira handle) leaves tickets effectively unassigned — and a bare handle like `joe` gets cleared by Jira sync (see bug `balm-feast-mica`). A configurable default assignee lets a checkout/agent set a sensible Jira-resolvable identity once, so claims attribute work correctly by default.

## What
Add a `default_assignee` config key (config file + env override, following the existing rebar config pattern), and make `claim` fall back to it when `--assignee` is unspecified/empty.

## Scope
**Config** (`src/rebar/config.py`):
- Add `default_assignee: str = ""` to the existing `TicketConfig` dataclass (the `[tickets]` section) — it is a ticket-workflow setting, not a Jira-connector setting.
- Wire the env override following the established pattern: either the auto-derived `REBAR_TICKET_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE`, or add an explicit entry to `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES` if a nicer name is wanted. Precedence stays CLI > env > project config > user config > default.
- Register the key in `_SECTIONS` so typo-detection (`unknown key … ignored`) and `env_overrides()` pick it up.

**Claim** (`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py`):
- In `claim_compute()`, BEFORE `txn.claim_core(...)` (~line 140), if `assignee` is empty, fall back to `config.load_config(repo_root).ticket.default_assignee`.
- The existing `claim_core` (`txn.py`) already writes the assignee as an EDIT event only when non-empty — unchanged.
- Behavior: explicit `--assignee` always wins; empty + configured default → default is used; empty + no default → unchanged (no assignee), as today.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `[tickets] default_assignee = "<id>"` in the config file is read and applied.
- [ ] Env override (`REBAR_TICKET_DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE` or the chosen canonical name) overrides the file value; precedence CLI > env > project > user > default holds.
- [ ] `claim <id>` with no `--assignee` uses the configured default; `claim <id> --assignee X` still uses X (explicit wins); empty + no default behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] The key is in the known-key set (no "unknown key" warning) and documented in `docs/config.md`.
- [ ] Recommend (doc note) that the default be a Jira-resolvable identity (email/accountId) so it survives reconcile — ties to bug `balm-feast-mica`.
- [ ] Tests: config load (file + env + precedence), and claim fallback (explicit / default / none) including the cascade claim path.

## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/config.py` (`TicketConfig`, `_SECTIONS`, `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES`)
- `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` (`claim_compute` fallback)
- `docs/config.md`
baseline.summary: Add default_assignee config (file + env override) and have claim use it when --assignee is omitted

content.text: RISK 1 (cross-session duplication) + client reliability. Two competing prompt-authoring WRITE backends both wired into the editor: `prompt_authoring.save_prompt` (atomic temp-file + `os.replace`) and `prompt_library.create_prompt` (NON-atomic `path.write_text`, `prompt_library.py:240`). They write the same `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` with divergent semantics — one atomic, one a latent half-write on crash; one rejects uppercase ids, the other accepts them.
## Why

`prompt_library` was added as an "additive" layer without folding in the pre-existing atomic writer two directories away. The editor exposes BOTH `/prompt/save` and `/library/create` POST endpoints (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py`), so a client can corrupt a prompt file via the non-atomic path. `create_prompt` is essentially a strict subset of `save_prompt` minus the atomicity + id-rule guarantees.
## What / files
- `src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py:236-245` — make `create_prompt`/`_write` DELEGATE to `prompt_authoring.save_prompt` (project-forced target) instead of `path.write_text`.
- Pick ONE id rule (prefer `prompt_authoring._valid_id`); reconcile `PromptExistsError` vs `PromptWriteError` semantics.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py` — route `/library/create` through the atomic writer.
Keep the `enumerate_library`/criterion-kind classification that `prompt_library` legitimately adds (only the WRITE path is duplicated, not the enumerate path).
## Scope
In: one atomic write path, one id rule, shared error semantics. Out: the enumerate/classification surface (keep), the prompt schema/front-matter format.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All prompt writes (both editor endpoints) go through the atomic `os.replace` writer — no `write_text` write path remains.
- [ ] A single id-validation rule governs both endpoints (documented).
- [ ] A crash/interrupt mid-write cannot leave a partially-written `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` (test via a write that fails before replace).
- [ ] Existing prompt-authoring + library tests pass; `enumerate_library` behavior unchanged.

baseline.summary: Risk 1: consolidate the two prompt-authoring write backends

baseline.description:
## Context (parking lot — undesigned; promote only if the serial treadmill is a MEASURED pain)

The auto-lander epic (f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af) Phase 1 is a SERIAL lander: ~1 change per CI-duration, so
under bursts of independent ready changes the wall-clock is N × CI-time (the FFO rebase-treadmill —
observed live: a docs change took 3 rebases to land). Phase-2 addresses throughput.

Cross-stack BATCHING (combine N changes → one CI run → land together) was evaluated by a design
spike and REJECTED on this infra: (1) the gerrit-to-platform bridge fires CI per-patchset with no
batch awareness, so assembling a batch = N runs on N partial trees, not one; (2) landing N off one
run requires the bot to direct-cast Verified on member patchsets from a combined-tree run — a
GerriScary / CVE-2025-1568-class posture regression; (3) it only wins in rare bursts of ≥4 and pays
a bisection tax + WIP-hook fragility.

The recommended throughput approach is BOUNDED SPECULATION: speculatively pre-run CI on the next few
queued changes (each rebased onto the projected tip) IN PARALLEL, up to the GHA concurrency cap (~3),
landing in order. Each candidate is a clean single-change-on-tip verified on its own tree, so NONE of
the batching gaps exist (no combined tree, no direct-cast, no g2p change). Wall-clock for 6 ≈ 28 min
(2 rounds) vs 84 serial vs batching's rare 14-min-but-fragile. Serial (Phase 1) is the fallback.

## Why an idea (not open)
Deferred until the serial treadmill is a MEASURED pain (validate against the Phase-1 queue-wait
metric). Promote + design then. Aligns with ADR-0040's "revisit a lightweight commit-queue bot if
the treadmill becomes real pain." Supersedes the retired batching stories S7/S8/S9 of epic f1fa.

## Rough acceptance (when promoted — to be designed)
- [ ] Speculate up to the concurrency cap on the next queued changes (each rebased onto the projected tip); land in order.
- [ ] Each candidate is an ordinary single change on tip, verified on its own tree (no combined tree, no bot-cast-Verified, no g2p change).
- [ ] Serial (Phase 1) is the fallback when speculation cannot apply.
- [ ] Driven by a real measured throughput pain (the Phase-1 wait metric), not speculatively.
baseline.summary: Phase-2 throughput: bounded speculation (deferred; batching rejected by design spike)

baseline.description:
## Summary
The Pass-3 rising-floor novelty scorer feeds the novelty sub-call a prior-findings set that INCLUDES previously-dropped (floored) findings, so a finding permanently dropped for convergence can re-surface as 'carryover' on a later pass — defeating the intended permanent-drop behavior. Novelty must be scored only against findings RETURNED TO THE CLIENT (surfaced blocking/advisory), never against hidden/dropped findings.

## Reproduction Steps
1. With verify.remediation_mode + verify.novelty_drop_active on, run plan-review so a novel + low-priority finding F is floored: recorded in the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar with decision=dropped, drop_reason=novelty.
2. Re-review the same ticket (plan edited, code unchanged) so the floor is eligible.
3. The floor reads prior findings via latest_review_result(ticket_id)['findings'] in _maybe_apply_rising_floor (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:206-207), UNFILTERED.
4. build_payload (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:329-334) writes blocking + advisory + overflow + dropped into 'findings', so the prior set INCLUDES the previously-dropped F.
5. If F re-surfaces this pass, the novelty sub-call matches it to prior F -> LOW novelty (carryover) -> rising_floor_drop (needs novelty>=threshold) no longer drops it -> F is surfaced.

**Expected:** a finding permanently dropped for convergence stays dropped on recurrence; novelty is scored only against surfaced (block/advisory) prior findings. Only inherently lower-impact findings are permanently dropped, and the priority floor is the escape hatch that keeps surfacing higher-impact findings.

**Actual:** previously-dropped findings re-enter the prior set, so a recurring dropped finding scores as carryover and escapes the floor (accidental 'self-healing'), defeating permanent-drop convergence.

## Evidence of inconsistency
The RECALL path prior_concerns() (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:253-258) ALREADY filters to decision in {block, advisory}; the novelty-floor path does not. The two consumers of the same sidecar payload disagree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] _maybe_apply_rising_floor filters prior findings to surfaced-only (decision in {block, advisory}) before feeding _score_floor_novelty, matching prior_concerns().
- [ ] Regression test: a dropped finding re-surfacing on the next pass is dropped again (stays permanently floored), NOT surfaced as carryover.
- [ ] Audit every novelty prior-set consumer (attest.py:441 also calls latest_review_result) to confirm none feeds dropped findings as novelty priors.
- [ ] Decide whether the surfaced-only filter belongs in latest_review_result vs each caller (single source of truth).
baseline.summary: Plan-review novelty floor feeds DROPPED prior findings into the novelty sub-call (should be surfaced-only)

content.text: ## Why

Audit OSS finding #2 (MEDIUM). The GitHub mirror has no CodeQL / SAST workflow. Security scanning today is gitleaks-driven secret detection on the Gerrit review path plus a gating pip-audit — good, but no static code analysis. CodeQL is free for public repos and runs fine on the read-only mirror (push/schedule triggers, writes results to the Security tab, does not touch the tree), adding an independent detection layer.
## What / files
Add `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`:
- `languages` matrix: exactly `python` and `javascript` (the CodeQL `javascript` key already covers TypeScript; do NOT use `javascript-typescript`, which is not the Actions matrix key).
- Triggers: `push` to `main` + a weekly `schedule` cron.
- Least-privilege `permissions`: `security-events: write`, `contents: read`, `actions: read`.
- `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true`.

- Pin actions by MAJOR VERSION TAG to match repo convention (test.yml/gerrit-verify use `actions/checkout@v5`, `actions/setup-python@v6`); use `github/codeql-action/init@v3` / `analyze@v3`. No SHA-pinning (no other workflow here uses it).
- Alerts route to the default Security tab.
## Scope
In: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` (new file only). Out: changing other workflows' pinning; alert routing beyond the Security tab.

Out of scope as an acceptance gate — first-run triage: CodeQL's first scan only runs on the GitHub mirror AFTER this change lands on main, so first-run results cannot exist while the ticket is worked in the worktree. First-run triage is a tracked post-landing operational follow-up (recorded separately once the mirror run completes); it is deliberately NOT an acceptance criterion of this ticket, because it is not evaluable in-session and cannot distinguish a clean run from an errored one at close time.
## Acceptance Criteria (all in-session verifiable)

- [ ] `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` exists and parses as valid YAML (python -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/codeql.yml'))" exits 0), with a `languages` matrix of exactly `python` and `javascript`

- [ ] `permissions` is least-privilege (exactly security-events: write, contents: read, actions: read); a weekly `schedule:` trigger exists in addition to `push:` on main; `concurrency` sets `cancel-in-progress: true`
- [ ] Every `uses:` in the file is pinned by version tag (`@vN`) — grep-verifiable that no `@main`, `@master`, or 40-hex-SHA pin appears
- [ ] The workflow uses `github/codeql-action/init` + `/analyze` (v3) and sets `category`/language matrix correctly (structural check: the two steps are present under the matrixed job)

baseline.description:
# Batch overlap-judge candidates per call: cut call volume, and grow the prefix past 1024

## Context / Problem

Story `8415-b6e8-c206-48f6` moved the batch-invariant query digest out of the per-call user message into the overlap-judge system prompt, so the shared bytes sit in the block the runner already puts a cache breakpoint on. That relocation is done and measured. It does not pay off, because the resulting prefix does not reach the model's minimum cacheable prefix.

Measured on real `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls (the `standard` class `overlap-judge` runs on post-`afeb`), one query ticket and six candidate digests, 12 calls:

    stable system prefix   before  423 tokens        after  846 tokens      floor  1024
    input tokens           before  16,040            after  16,976          (+936, +5.8%)
    cache_read_tokens      before  0                 after  0
    cache_write_tokens     before  0                 after  0
    verdict parity         relations identical on 12/12 ordered pairs

The floor is measured, not assumed: through the real judge request path an 875-token system prefix produced write 0 / read 0 while a 1250-token one produced write 1243 then read 1243. `count_tokens` over the base prompt (423) plus each of seven real `rebar.llm.enrich` digests (306-453) gives 728-875 — every one short of 1024 by **149-296 tokens**. So the relocation costs ~5.8% more input and returns nothing, and 8415 is held until this ticket makes the pair net-positive.

## Approach

Judge N candidates in ONE call per ordering instead of one call per candidate per ordering. Today `judge()` issues 2N calls, each re-sending the whole system prefix. Batched, it issues `2 * ceil(N / batch)` calls: the query digest stays hoisted in the system block (unchanged from 8415), and the user message carries a LABELLED LIST of candidate digests instead of one.

**Two mechanisms, and they are NOT the same mechanism. State them separately, because one is arithmetic and the other is a bet.**

1. **Call-count reduction — arithmetic, and the mechanism the ticket actually rests on.** Every
   avoided call removes one whole copy of the 846-token prefix from the bill. At N=6 with one
   batch per ordering, 12 calls become 2: ten prefix copies (~8,460 tokens) disappear outright.
   This requires no caching whatsoever and cannot fail to reduce total input tokens; only its
   magnitude is uncertain, because the candidate digests themselves are re-sent either way.

2. **Prefix growth past 1024 — a bet that must be measured, and batching ALONE does not deliver
   it.** The cacheable prefix is the *system block*: base prompt + hoisted query digest. Putting
   more candidates in the *user* message does not add a single token to it. Batching lifts the
   prefix only because the batch protocol has to be described somewhere, and it belongs in the
   system prompt: per-candidate independence, the labelled-list input shape, one echoed verdict
   per candidate. That section is required by the change, not padding invented to reach a number
   — but whether base 423 + section + digest 306-453 clears 1024 for every real digest is an
   empirical question this ticket answers with `count_tokens`, and it may come out short for the
   smallest digests. A prefix that still does not cache is a valid recorded outcome; mechanism 1
   carries the ticket in that case.

Deliberately NOT done: no padding is added to reach the floor (buying a cache with the tokens it was meant to save is not a saving), `capabilities.py`'s `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` is not touched (that is ticket `e3cd`), and the loop is not parallelized (fanning out cold calls that share a prefix turns one write plus reads into N premium writes — strictly worse; 8415 records this).

**The cost is precision, and it is a real cost.** `reviewers/overlap_judge.md` is written for ONE ORDERED PAIR — "FIRST <relation> SECOND", a closed five-value relation set, a required named `shared_artifact`, `related_distinct` as the default, "false flags are costly". Judging several candidates in one call risks cross-contamination: a shared artifact cited for one candidate bleeding into the verdict for another, or an unrelated candidate dragged toward `related_distinct` by its neighbours. This is the real risk of the change and it is MEASURED, not asserted, by the parity run below.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py` — batch construction (a labelled candidate list, the batch-size
  bound) and per-candidate response demultiplexing. `judge_one` and the un-batched request shape
  stay as the single-pair path, unedited.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md` — a BATCH section describing one FIRST against a
  labelled list of SECOND candidates (and the mirrored ordering), per-candidate independence, and
  one echoed verdict per candidate. The single-pair instructions above it are unchanged.
- `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py` — a new `overlap_verdict_batch` contract: a list of per-candidate
  entries, each carrying `candidate_id` plus today's four `overlap_verdict` fields. Registered
  next to `overlap_verdict`, which keeps its registration and its single-pair use.
- `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` — batch payload shape, demultiplexing, and fail-safe tests.

No `src/rebar/schemas/` change: `overlap_verdict_batch` is an internal contract with no `--output` surface, like `plan_review_novelty` and `code_review_coach`, so no schema file is added and the every-schema-file-is-wired guard is unaffected. No `config.py` change: the batch bound is a module constant in `judge.py`, since no operator-facing tuning is claimed for it.

## Testing

Offline tests drive the real `judge()` through the existing recording fake runner, asserting on the ACTUAL `RunRequest` payload rather than a stand-in.

- **Call count** — 6 candidates yield strictly fewer `RunRequest`s than 12, and each ordering's
  request carries every candidate's digest block, each under its own label.
- **Both orderings survive batching** — in ordering 1 the hoisted reference occupies the FIRST
  slot and the labelled candidate list the SECOND; in ordering 2 the reverse.
- **Demultiplexing** — a canned batched response maps back to exactly one verdict per candidate,
  matched by label and not by position; a candidate absent from the response, and a response
  entry naming an unknown label, both resolve to abstain for the affected candidate only, leaving
  the others' verdicts intact.
- **Fail-safe** — a runner that raises, and a runner returning a malformed batch (not a dict / no
  verdict list / entries missing their label), each yield `[]` from `judge()` with nothing
  propagating.
- **Batch bound** — a corpus larger than the bound is split into multiple calls per ordering, and
  every candidate still receives exactly one verdict.
- **Mutation check, both directions, for every new test:** each new test must FAIL with the
  batching change reverted and PASS restored. Recorded on the ticket.
- **Real-API parity and measurement** — the same query ticket and candidate corpus judged on
  8415's per-pair build and on this batched build, relations compared pair by pair.
- Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
  `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal -q`, judged by exit code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The batched build issues strictly fewer calls than candidates x 2 for a corpus of >= 6
      candidates, shown by a recording-runner test counting `RunRequest`s.
- [ ] Every candidate receives exactly one verdict, matched by its label rather than by position;
      an absent or unlabelled entry becomes an abstain for that candidate ONLY; checked by the
      demultiplexing tests.
- [ ] The step stays advisory: a raising runner and a malformed batched response each yield `[]`
      from `judge()` with no exception escaping; checked by the fail-safe tests.
- [ ] Precision is shown, not assumed: a real-API parity run over one query ticket and at least
      six candidates reports per-pair `relation` for the per-pair build and the batched build, and
      any differing relation is called out with its digests; recorded as a ticket comment.
      Identical relations on every pair is the pass condition; a divergence is reported, not
      averaged away.
- [ ] A BEFORE/AFTER measurement on real `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls over the SAME query
      ticket and SAME corpus records, for both builds, total `input_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`,
      `cache_write_tokens`, the call count, and the `count_tokens` size of the stable prefix beside
      the measured 1024 floor.
- [ ] The pair is judged against the PRE-8415 baseline, not just against 8415: the batched build's
      total `input_tokens` must be below **16,040** on the same corpus, or the ticket reports the
      pair as still net-negative in plain terms with the numbers. `cache_write_tokens` above one
      prefix write per batch FAILS this criterion.
- [ ] The prefix bet is reported either way: the batched `count_tokens` prefix is recorded against
      1024 for the corpus's digest-size range, and a prefix that still does not clear the floor is
      recorded as such rather than presented as a caching win.
- [ ] Every new test is mutation-checked in both directions and the evidence recorded as a ticket
      comment.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` all exit 0.
baseline.summary: Batch overlap-judge candidates so the shared prefix clears the 1024-token cache floor

content.text: `rebar review-plan` reports `signature` present (the JSON `signature` field is non-null, and
batch tooling reads `signed=True`) even when the **verdict is BLOCK**. The documented contract
is that it "signs a plan-review attestation on a **non-blocking PASS**" — so a BLOCK verdict
should NOT carry a passing signed attestation. Either the signing-on-BLOCK is a bug, or the
`signature` field means something other than "passing attestation"; either way it is misleading,
because the signature is meant to be the trustworthy proof-of-PASS that downstream gates (the
claim gate) and CI rely on. A consumer that checks "is there a signature?" to decide
claimability would be misled by a signed BLOCK.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Author a ticket whose plan trips a blocking criterion (or use any ticket the four-pass gate
BLOCKs).
2. Run `rebar review-plan <id> --output json` (default source = attested, signing on).
3. Inspect the result JSON: `verdict` and `signature`.
## Expected
- On `verdict == BLOCK`, no passing attestation is signed — `signature` is null/absent (or the
field is unambiguously labeled as a non-passing attestation), so "has signature" reliably
means "passed".
## Actual
- Observed repeatedly this session: tickets with `verdict=BLOCK` returned `signature` populated
(`signed=True`). Concretely, Round-2/3/4 runs on the S4/S6/S7 d251 children showed e.g.
`s6: BLOCK block=6 ... signed=True` and `s4: BLOCK block=2 ... signed=True` — a signature on a
BLOCK.
## Notes
- Inferred from the JSON `signature` field, not the signing internals — possible the field is
populated-but-not-a-passing-attestation; that distinction is exactly what's unclear and should
be made explicit. Surfaced while dogfooding the plan-review gate on epic d251 (alto-fruit-punch).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-plan <id>` on a BLOCK verdict does NOT emit a passing signed attestation
(either `signature` is null/absent on BLOCK, or the field/type is explicitly distinct from
a passing attestation and documented as such).
- [ ] `verify_signature` / the claim gate cannot be satisfied by an attestation produced on a
BLOCK verdict (a BLOCKed plan is never claimable on the strength of its signature).
- [ ] The behavior is documented (docs/plan-review-gate.md): exactly when a signature is emitted
and what its presence guarantees.
- [ ] A regression test asserts: BLOCK verdict -> no passing signature; PASS verdict -> signature present.

baseline.summary: plan-review: signed attestation emitted on BLOCK verdict (signature should certify PASS only)

baseline.description:
## Problem
Findings carry a `severity` string (`severity_label(impact)` -> critical/major/minor/none,
`review_kernel/decide.py`) that is derived from IMPACT ALONE, so it does not order the same way as
the authoritative `priority = validity x impact`. A high-impact/low-validity finding shows as
`critical` while ranking below a `major`. This is a foot-gun: it invites reading the label as the
gate signal when it is not. It also caused a field misread — via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`
(major->high, minor->medium, none->info) the review-bot surfaced the same finding as INFO then
MEDIUM across identical runs, reading like a severity change when only impact drifted.

## Idea
Make findings blocking / not-blocking + numeric priority, mirroring the intent that priority is
the single source of truth. Remove or rename the impact-only severity label so nothing mistakes it
for the decision.

## Why this is NOT a one-liner (traced)
- The label lives in the SHARED kernel (`pass3_decide`), so plan review carries it too — this is
  not a code-review-only change.
- The block/advisory decision is ALREADY binary and priority-keyed; severity is an extra surfaced
  signal, not the gate.
- Real consumers exist and there are TWO vocabularies (kernel critical/major/minor/none; and the
  original 5-level critical/high/medium/low/info in `findings.py`, from commit b501c38d1):
    - Gerrit review-bot comment surface (`review_bot/adapter.py`, ADR 0009)
    - cross-finding aggregation/dedup picks the highest-severity representative (`aggregate.py`)
    - workflow `fail_on_severity` policy (`workflow/steps.py`)

## Suggested sequence (each independently reviewable)
1. Rank aggregation by `priority` instead of severity.
2. Surface `priority` + blocking/advisory in the review-bot instead of the mapped label.
3. Migrate `fail_on_severity` to a priority threshold.
4. Drop the `severity` field from the finding shape.
Changes the Gerrit comment format and touches both gates -> warrants an ADR.

## Provenance
Discovered from the upstream review-code false-positive report (client project). Sibling of the
merge-base diff fix (ticket 8559-44c3-e08a-4bb9).
baseline.summary: Retire the kernel severity label in favor of numeric priority (blocking/not-blocking)

content.text: ## Why
The record/fold path (S2) and read surface (S3) handle a single opaque session id, but a
bare session id collides across tools (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor). To make the
feature genuinely multi-harness, claims must also record WHICH harness produced the id, and
the resolver must recognise the other OSS harness session vars.
## What
- **Resolver var-list extension (`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py`).** Extend
`_SESSION_ID_VARS` with the OSS harness var OpenCode ships, in popularity order between the
Claude and ambient vars:
`REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID -> SESSION_ID`.
**Codex is deliberately NOT added as a native var:** story 7656 establishes that Codex
exposes no supported readable session env var, so it is covered by its SessionStart shim
exporting `REBAR_SESSION_ID` (not a `CODEX_THREAD_ID`). SAFETY: an absent or unrecognised var
simply falls through (the resolver skips unset vars), so it degrades to a lower-precedence
var or `None` — never an error.
- **Harness provenance tag.** Add `resolve_harness()` returning the opaque, rebar-owned
`AI_AGENT` env var (verbatim, never interpolated) or `None`. `AI_AGENT` is rebar's
harness-provenance convention, holding e.g. `claude-code_<ver>` / `opencode` / `codex` /
`cursor`. **Population contract (closes the DOA gap):** the capture shims in stories S4
(ec5c) and S6 (7656) are extended by THIS epic to export `AI_AGENT` alongside
`REBAR_SESSION_ID`; until then `AI_AGENT` may also be set directly by an operator/hook. When
unset, `claim_harness` folds to `None` (no error) — the feature degrades gracefully.
On an `open -> in_progress` STATUS, stamp `data["harness"]` when present; fold to
`state["claim_harness"]`. Each provenance field folds `data.get(<its key>)` INDEPENDENTLY on
the edge (same fork-winner gating as `claimed_session`), so a re-claim clears `claim_harness`
to `None` iff `AI_AGENT` is absent for THAT claim — independent of whether a session id is
present.
- **Secondary remote session.** Add `resolve_remote_session()` returning
`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` or `None`; stamp `data["remote_session"]` and fold to
`state["claim_remote_session"]` (same gating). This is a secondary field, independent of the
primary `claimed_session`.
- **State + schema + read surface.** Default `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session` to
`None` in `make_initial_state`; enumerate both in `ticket_state.schema.json` and (as compact
keys `chn` / `rsn`) in `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` + `KEY_MAP` (+ docstring); add both to
the MCP `TicketStateOut` model; regenerate `types.py`. `rebar show` JSON includes them
automatically (state keys).
- **Existing-test updates.** Update `tests/unit/test_session_id.py` for the extended list:
broaden its hardcoded `_ALL_VARS` tuple + autouse clear fixture to the 4 vars, and update
`test_docs_document_unified_contract`'s exact-string assertion to the extended ordered
contract (normalising whitespace so doc line-wrapping is irrelevant). Add an
`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` precedence case, and a case asserting `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is NOT
recognised (Codex has no native var).
- **Docs.** Extend `docs/config.md` (the ordered var list + `AI_AGENT` +
`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`) and `docs/event-schema.md` (the `harness` / `remote_session`
data keys -> `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session` state). Env-var name provenance:
`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (OpenCode-shipped) and `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex convention) come from
the epic OSS survey (Codex has no readable var, hence no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`); because an
unrecognised name simply falls through, a wrong guess degrades to a lower-precedence var or
`None` with no runtime error.
## Scope
- IN: resolver var-list extension + `resolve_harness` / `resolve_remote_session`; the write
stamps + reducer folds for `claim_harness` / `claim_remote_session`; state defaults; both
JSON schemas + `types.py` regen + `to_llm` keys + MCP model; docs; the existing
`test_session_id.py` updates AND a NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module.
- OUT: the per-harness CAPTURE shims that POPULATE `REBAR_SESSION_ID` / `AI_AGENT` — Claude
Code (S4 / ec5c) and Codex + Cursor (S6 / 7656), both extended by this epic to also export
`AI_AGENT`. This story is the store/record side only.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `resolve_session_id()` recognises `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` at its precedence, and does NOT
recognise `CODEX_THREAD_ID` (Codex has no native var). Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -k "opencode or codex" -q`.
- [ ] A claim records `claim_harness` (from `AI_AGENT`) in compiled state, distinguishing the
source tool; absent `AI_AGENT` -> `None`. Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k harness -q`.
- [ ] `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`, when set, is captured as `claim_remote_session`. Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k remote -q`.
- [ ] Both fields default to `None` in `make_initial_state`, are enumerated in
`ticket_state.schema.json` + `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` (`chn` / `rsn`), and appear
in `TicketStateOut`; `types.py` is not stale. Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k "schema or read" -q` and
`pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_public_types.py -q`.
- [ ] Fork-winner + session-less-clear semantics apply to both new fields (never the loser's;
cleared to `None` on a provenance-less re-claim). Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k fork -q`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` and `docs/event-schema.md` document the extended var list, `AI_AGENT`,
and the two new fields. Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py -k docs -q`
asserts `docs/config.md` contains `AI_AGENT` and `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (Codex has no
readable var, so there is intentionally no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), AND `docs/event-schema.md`
contains `claim_harness` and `claim_remote_session`.
- [ ] The existing `test_session_id.py` is updated for the extended list and stays green
(4-var `_ALL_VARS` + clear fixture; unified-contract doc assertion updated). Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_session_id.py -q`.
- [ ] A NEW `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py` module is created covering the resolvers,
write-stamp/fold, fork-winner + provenance-less-clear, schemas + read surface, and docs.
## Depends on
- S2 (68ef) record/fold path + S3 (199b) read surface — landed in this stack.

baseline.summary: Multi-harness session capture: extend resolver var-list + record harness provenance tag

baseline.description:
## What
One-time backfill of the complexity and clone-count series by checking out sampled historical commits, running the metric tools, and writing snapshots into the going-forward store so those two trends have history.

## Files
- `scripts/backfill_complexity_clone_snapshots.py` — new: for sampled commits (default monthly), measure the tree and append snapshots via `src/rebar/metrics/snapshot.py`.
  - **Complexity tool + parse:** `lizard <src_dir>` (cyclomatic complexity; already a project dependency-of-record for grounding, see `src/rebar/grounding/engine_b_backends.py`). Parse its per-function CCN and record `complexity` = the SUMMED cyclomatic complexity across all functions (an `int`).
  - **Clone tool + parse:** `jscpd --reporters json --output <tmpdir> <src_dir>`; read `<tmpdir>/jscpd-report.json` and record `clone_count` = `statistics.total.clones` (the number of duplicated blocks, an `int`).
  - **Measurement seam:** the per-commit measurement is a single function `measure_tree(tree_path) -> {"complexity": int, "clone_count": int}` that shells to the two tools; the test monkeypatches THIS function to return stub values, so the test needs neither `lizard` nor `jscpd` installed. A tool that is absent or errors makes `measure_tree` return `None` and the commit is skipped (logged, non-fatal).
  - **`ts` MUST be the sampled commit's date**, not wall-clock: `write_snapshot(record, ts=<commit ISO date>, repo_root=...)` where the date is `git show -s --format=%cI <commit>` — otherwise every backfilled point would collapse onto the backfill-run time and the trend would be meaningless.
- `tests/scripts/test_backfill_complexity_clone.py` — new.

## Test tier
The test lives under `tests/scripts/` with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.scripts` (the scripts tier; `tests/unit/scripts/` does NOT exist). External tools are stubbed/mocked so the test is deterministic and needs no scc/lizard/jscpd installed.

## Approach
Complexity/clone are point-in-time; their movement needs seeded history, which git makes deterministic (checkout + tool run at each sampled commit). Writes through the same `snapshot.py` writer as the going-forward path so backfilled and live snapshots share one format; snapshots are labeled `source=snapshot, confidence=high` (deterministic tool output). Sampling cadence is a script arg (default monthly) — a stated default. This is an optional backfill script the core command does not depend on.

## Tests
- Unit (temp git repo + stubbed tool output): the script writes one snapshot per sampled commit with the parsed complexity/clone numbers; a commit whose tool run fails is skipped and logged, not fatal.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_backfill_complexity_clone.py` passes (tier `scripts`): with `measure_tree` stubbed, sampling 3 fixture commits writes 3 snapshots, each containing integer `complexity` and `clone_count` keys, and each tagged with `ts` equal to its COMMIT's date (not the run time) — asserted by reading the snapshots back via `read_snapshots` and checking the per-commit `ts` and int-typed values.
- [ ] a sampled commit whose `measure_tree` returns `None` (tool absent/errors) is skipped without aborting the backfill — test asserts the run continues and the other snapshots are still written.
- [ ] every written snapshot carries `source="snapshot"`, `confidence="high"` — asserted.
baseline.summary: Backfill complexity/clone snapshots at sampled historical commits

## Context
Codex currently has no Serena MCP entry, while this project relies on Serena/Pyright for semantic navigation. The tracked `.claude/settings.json` does not configure MCP servers. Separately, this operator machine's untracked Claude project config (`~/.claude.json`) launches Serena via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena`; that machine-local fact was inspected only to identify the existing server. The delivery design is independently grounded: the current Codex manual supports project-scoped MCP servers in trusted `.codex/config.toml`, and Serena 1.6.2.dev0 exposes a `codex` context plus `--project-from-cwd` specifically for CLI agents/worktrees.

## Verified inputs
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena -V` returned `Serena 1.6.2.dev0`.
- `git ls-remote https://github.com/oraios/serena.git HEAD` returned `c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e serena start-mcp-server --help` succeeded and documented `--context` plus `--project-from-cwd`.
- `codex mcp list` in the current worktree confirms no `serena` entry exists before the change.

## Plan
- Add a project-scoped `mcp_servers.serena` STDIO entry to `.codex/config.toml`; project scope is intentional so every contributor/worktree gets the repo-required semantic navigation server after trusting the repo, without mutating each operator's global config.
- Launch the same Serena distribution currently used on this machine, but pin the verified upstream commit: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e`.
- Pass `serena start-mcp-server --context codex --project-from-cwd` so each checkout/worktree activates itself; commit no user-specific project path.
- Set `startup_timeout_sec = 120` to bound and accommodate a cold uvx resolution. Keep `required` unset/false so a Serena startup failure is reported by Codex without preventing all Codex work.
- Validate TOML with Python 3.11+ `tomllib`; run `codex mcp list` from the isolated worktree and require an enabled `serena` row containing the pinned command/args; run the pinned `serena start-mcp-server --help` command and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test from the worktree, bounded by a test harness timeout.
- Negative control: run `codex mcp list` from a temporary untrusted/non-rebar directory and confirm the project-scoped server is not injected there.
- Land the single-file config change through Gerrit with DCO and the ticket trailer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `codex mcp list` from a trusted rebar worktree discovers an enabled `serena` STDIO server from `.codex/config.toml`, using the pinned upstream commit.
- [ ] The server argv uses Serena's `codex` context and `--project-from-cwd`; no user-specific rebar path is committed.
- [ ] `python -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('.codex/config.toml', 'rb'))"`, the pinned Serena CLI smoke command, and an MCP initialize/list-tools smoke test all succeed.
- [ ] `codex mcp list` outside the trusted rebar project does not expose the project-scoped `serena` entry; Serena startup remains non-required so failure does not block Codex itself.
- [ ] The config diff contains no secrets, and `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default suite remain green; a same-base full-gate result may be reused because this task changes only static Codex configuration.

## References
Current Codex manual: trusted projects may scope MCP servers in `.codex/config.toml`; STDIO entries accept `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `startup_timeout_sec`, and optional `required`. Serena CLI help at the pinned commit documents `--context codex` and `--project-from-cwd`.
baseline.summary: Configure Codex to use the project's Serena MCP server

baseline.description:
## Why
Code review reviews a DIFF fresh with NO memory across runs. The durable `code_review`
artifact (per Gerrit change/revision) today persists SURFACED findings write-only (a
calibration corpus). This story adds the READER + the content-addressed STATE the region-gated
novelty floor (blameless-grindable-noctule) needs, and extends the `code_review_result_v1`
payload with the two new fields that state.

## What
- **Payload extension (`code_review_result_v1`, `build_payload`).** Add two fields, both read
  off the verdict dict so they are populated once and flow to EVERY emit path unchanged:
  - `session_id`: TOP-LEVEL, nullable. `build_payload` reads `verdict.get("session_id")`
    (None for Gerrit reviews; set for local session-keyed reviews by the persistence story
    paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish). Makes local memory queryable by session.
  - `deps`: a `{reviewed-file path: sha256}` content-hash map. `build_payload` reads
    `verdict.get("deps")` (defaulting to `{}`).
- **deps collector + computation seam (`produce_code_review_verdict`).** A thin collector hashes
  each reviewed-file path once and stashes the map on the verdict (`verdict["deps"]`) in
  `_run_code_review_gate`, computed UNCONDITIONALLY after the verdict is produced and BEFORE the
  sidecar emit. This requires importing `code_review.sidecar` (for the collector +
  `_cited_paths_code_review`) EARLIER in `_run_code_review_gate` — at the top of the finalize block
  rather than only inside the existing `if request.target_ticket:` block (an explicit new import in
  `gate_dispatch.py`, enumerated here). Because it lives on the verdict dict, BOTH
  emit callers pick it up via `build_payload` with NO change to either call site:
  - the produce-path emit (`_run_code_review_gate` → `sidecar.emit`), and
  - the Gerrit voter emit (`voter.py::emit_code_review_artifact` → `sidecar.emit`), which passes
    the SAME verdict object it received — so it inherits `deps`/`session_id` for free (voter.py
    stays OUT of scope; it needs no edit).
  - **Reuse boundary:** the collector REUSES the private `attest._hash_file(path, base=…)`
    primitive (raw file-bytes sha256; a missing/unreadable path → the `absent` sentinel, so a
    create/delete is itself detectable) and `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` for the base. This
    reuse of a private symbol is EXPLICITLY sanctioned by the epic design ("private `_hash_file`
    primitive reused; NOT `dependency_hashes`, which is plan/ticket-coupled"). It does NOT reuse
    `dependency_hashes()` (that pulls ticket file_impact + plan-verdict citation buckets).
  - **Scope of `deps`** = the review's `changed_files` UNION its cited-file paths. NOTE:
    `attest._cited_paths(verdict)` is NOT reusable here — it reads a `citations` list with
    `kind == "file"`, but code-review findings carry no such list (they only have a `location`
    string, e.g. `path` or `path:line`). So define a small `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)`
    in `code_review/sidecar.py` that extracts the FILE path (strip any `:line` suffix) from each
    finding's `location` across the `blocking` + `advisory` buckets, ignoring empty/non-file
    locations. `deps` = `sorted(set(changed_files) | _cited_paths_code_review(verdict))`.
  - **Basis:** hashed via `attest._hash_basis(repo_root)` at the emit point. Because deps are
    computed AFTER the workflow's `gate_read_root` context has exited, `current_code_root()` is
    already `None`, so `_hash_basis` resolves to the in-place WORKING TREE (`_config.repo_root`) —
    NOT the attested snapshot. This is correct for both keyspaces: a LOCAL `review-code` reviews the
    working tree (so the working tree IS the reviewed basis), and the Gerrit voter bot checks out
    the patchset revision (so its working tree IS the reviewed revision). The content-addressed
    region gate only ever compares hashes WITHIN one keyspace, and each keyspace hashes its own
    working-tree basis consistently across runs, which is all it needs.
  - **Failure posture:** the collector is best-effort — a per-file hash failure yields the
    `absent` sentinel (never raises); a total failure leaves `deps` empty and is logged. It must
    NEVER fail the gate (mirrors the sidecar's best-effort posture).
- **Artifact addressing (title schemes, TYPED keyspaces).** Local artifacts use title
  `code-review: session:{session_id}`; Gerrit artifacts keep `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`
  (unchanged). These are two disjoint keyspaces so a prior LOCAL review can never seed a change's
  FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Reader `latest_code_review_result(key, *, repo_root=None)`.** `key` is a TYPED string:
  `session:<id>` or `change:<id>`. Resolution by artifact title:
  - `session:<id>` → the artifact whose title == `code-review: session:{id}` (exact; one artifact).
  - `change:<id>` → STRIP the `change:` tag to get the bare `change_id`, then match artifacts whose
    title starts with `code-review: {change_id} @ ` (spans revisions of the same change; the change
    is the memory key, the revision only makes each artifact idempotent). An unknown key kind → None.
  Artifacts are enumerated via `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")` and matched by title
  in-process (no new list-filter API). Across the matched artifact(s), the reader returns the
  most-recent usable `code_review_result_v1` sidecar payload's SURFACED findings + its `deps` map.
  - **SURFACED-only (mandatory; see old-frilly-plankton).** `code_review_result_v1` stores findings
    in SEPARATE top-level buckets (`blocking`, `advisory`, `coaching`) with NO per-finding
    `decision` field (unlike `plan_review_result_v1`). Therefore "surfaced" is DEFINED as the union
    of the `blocking` and `advisory` buckets; the reader returns ONLY those two buckets (never
    `coaching`, never any future dropped bucket). Dropped findings are never persisted into
    blocking/advisory, so they can never re-enter the novelty prior set.
  - **Posture:** mirrors `plan_review.sidecar.latest_review_result` — best-effort, NEVER raises,
    schema-guarded (only `code_review_result_v1` payloads), walks newest→oldest over each artifact's
    sidecar events tolerating a malformed/foreign newest file, returns None when nothing usable.
    A reader/hash/compare error degrades to None (⇒ the floor runs un-narrowed = no drops).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — payload extension (`build_payload`), the thin deps
  collector, and the `latest_code_review_result` reader.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — the `deps` computation seam in
  `produce_code_review_verdict` / `_run_code_review_gate` (stash on the verdict before emit).
- OUT of scope: local persistence wiring / setting `session_id` (paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish);
  the region_gated_floor consumer (blameless-grindable-noctule); `voter.py` (inherits via the
  verdict — no edit).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `build_payload` adds a nullable top-level `session_id` (read from `verdict.get("session_id")`)
      and a `deps` `{path: sha256}` map (read from `verdict.get("deps")`, default `{}`).
- [ ] A thin deps collector reuses `attest._hash_file` (NOT `dependency_hashes`) and the `absent`
      sentinel; scope = `changed_files` ∪ `_cited_paths_code_review(verdict)` (paths parsed from
      each finding's `location`, since code-review findings have no `citations[kind==file]` list).
- [ ] The deps map is computed ONCE in `produce_code_review_verdict`, UNCONDITIONALLY (regardless of
      `target_ticket`), and stashed on the verdict — importing `code_review.sidecar` earlier in
      `_run_code_review_gate` — so both the produce emit and the Gerrit voter emit carry it via
      `build_payload` (voter unchanged).
- [ ] `latest_code_review_result(key)` resolves `session:<id>` (exact title `code-review: session:{id}`)
      and `change:<id>` (strip `change:`, title prefix `code-review: {id} @`); unknown kind → None.
- [ ] The reader returns SURFACED findings = union of the payload's `blocking` + `advisory` buckets
      (never `coaching`/dropped) plus the `deps` map; schema-guarded to `code_review_result_v1`.
- [ ] The reader is best-effort and NEVER raises; malformed/absent/foreign-schema → None (⇒ no drops).
- [ ] Tests: payload carries `session_id` + `deps`; deps collector hashes changed+cited paths with
      the `absent` sentinel for a missing file; reader resolves both typed keyspaces, returns
      surfaced-only, and degrades to None on a malformed/absent artifact.
baseline.summary: Code-review finding-memory reader + artifact payload (session_id + reviewed-file content-hash map)

content.text: ## Summary
The reconciler preflight (`preflight_status_mapping`, `reconcile.py`) raises
`StatusMappingError("local status {status!r} not in local_to_jira_status mapping ...")`.
But the same function's Bug-85a1 logic deliberately accepts a value that is EITHER a
local-status KEY or a Jira-status VALUE, failing only when it is in neither. So the
offending value is frequently a **Jira** workflow status (e.g. `IDEA`, added Jira-side),
not a local status. Labeling it "local status 'IDEA'" is misleading and misdirects
debugging toward a non-existent local `idea` ticket. The `StatusMappingError` docstring
(reconcile.py) makes the same wrong "references a local status" assumption.
## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue is in a workflow status with no reconciler mapping (e.g. `IDEA`).
2. Reconcile → `ERROR: ... local status 'IDEA' not in local_to_jira_status mapping (target=REB-716)`.
Expected: message accurately states the status is unmapped in `local_to_jira_status`
in EITHER direction (could be a local-status key or a Jira-status value) — not that it
is a "local status".
Actual: message asserts it is a "local status", which is false for a Jira-origin status.
## Scope
LOGGING/ERROR-MESSAGE FIX ONLY. Does NOT add the `idea`->`IDEA` mapping (that is story
6173 / tawny-herb-bug, out of scope here).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — the `StatusMappingError` message +
the `StatusMappingError` / `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_status_preflight.py` — assert the message.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` message no longer calls the value a "local status"; it
states the status is not mapped in `local_to_jira_status` (neither a local-status
key nor a Jira-status value), and still includes the status value + target.
- [ ] The `StatusMappingError` and `preflight_status_mapping` docstrings no longer assert
the value is a "local status".
- [ ] A test asserts an unmapped Jira status (e.g. `IDEA`) is not reported as a "local
status" and the message acknowledges the Jira-status possibility.
- [ ] No mapping/behavior change (the raise condition is unchanged); existing preflight
tests still pass.
- [ ] make lint passes for the changed files.

baseline.summary: reconciler preflight mislabels an unmapped Jira status as a 'local status'

# `plan_review/attest.py` is at the hard cap with ZERO headroom

## Context

Landing bug c083 (untracked-tolerance on four plan-review snapshot reads) hit this immediately: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` was **799** lines on `origin/main` against the **800** hard cap enforced by `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py::test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` (limit single-sourced in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`).

A two-call-site change — adding `ignore_untracked=True` to two existing calls — could not be landed in the natural form:

- appending the kwarg inline made the line 114 chars, over the ruff E501 limit of 100;
- wrapping the call to satisfy E501 cost +2 lines -> 801, over the cap;
- adding the explanatory comments the change deserved cost more -> 803.

It only fit by importing `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` directly (+1 line for the import, which let the call fit on one line at 95 chars), landing the file at **exactly 800** — passing only because the gate is `> limit`, with **zero** remaining headroom.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The next change to this file — any change, including a one-line bug fix — cannot land without first splitting it. The cost is not paid by whoever grew the file; it is paid by whoever next needs to fix a bug in it, under time pressure, as an unrelated blocker. That is exactly the situation task `2682` was raised for when `runner.py` hit 800 in the LLM-provider-seam epic, and it was resolved there by a real call-graph split (`runner.py` 800 -> 655 + `structured_run.py`).

It also actively degrades the code: in c083 the comments explaining WHY untracked files must be tolerated had to be cut from `attest.py` and replaced with a pointer to `resign.py`, purely to save lines. The cap is now shaping documentation quality, not just structure.

## Approach

Split along a seam that ALREADY EXISTS in the call graph, per the module-size policy — never mechanically to hit a number, and never creating a sub-100-LOC file. Candidate seams to evaluate (not a decision):

- the `refresh_attestation` / drift-refresh cluster (`_sidecar_branch_decision`, `refresh_attestation`, `_rehash`, `drift_refresh_candidate`) looks like a cohesive group distinct from the `sign_plan_review` path;
- the manifest field/scope helpers (`_manifest_field`, `manifest_file_scope`, `_inherited_child_impact`).

Requires the same seam analysis `2682` did: confirm the callers, keep reference sites resolving (watch string-literal monkeypatch targets in tests), and verify the split is import-cycle safe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` is under 700 LOC (real headroom, not 799)
- [ ] any extracted module is at least 100 LOC (no sub-100-LOC fragmentation)
- [ ] zero test edits are required by the move, or each required edit is justified in the commit message
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus any new
      seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines quoted in a comment
baseline.summary: attest.py sits at exactly 800/800 LOC — zero headroom blocks the next edit

# Engine-wide caching: extend the runner cache to RunnerAgentStep (all workflow agent steps)

## Why
S1 caches plan-review's Pass-1 calls. The same stable-prefix waste exists in every workflow agent step
(verify/decide/coach/grounding) and other workflows (completion-verification, code-review) — they re-send a
stable system prompt + tool surface across runs. Extending caching there is the engine-wide win pulled into scope.

## What
- In the engine `RunnerAgentStep` (`workflow/runs.py:207`, builds RunRequest), populate S1's cacheable-prefix
  boundary: the static system prompt (+ stable inputs) is the cached prefix; per-run ticket data is the
  volatile suffix.
- Add a prompt-model convention to mark which part of an assembled workflow prompt is the byte-stable prefix vs
  per-run volatile inputs, so the boundary is set generically (not per call site).
- Apply `anthropic_cache_instructions` for the system prompt across steps; keep dynamic per-run content OUT of
  the cached prefix (after the CachePoint / a separate message part).

## Scope
- In: RunnerAgentStep prefix wiring; the prompt-model stable-vs-volatile convention; applying to all workflows.
- Out: the runner mechanism itself (S1, dependency); container parallelization (S3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RunnerAgentStep populates the cacheable prefix; verify/decide/coach cache their stable system-prompt/tool
      prefix on anthropic (`cache_read > 0` on repeats), unchanged on other providers.
- [ ] completion-verification and code-review workflows benefit (cache reads non-zero on repeats).
- [ ] Per-run volatile inputs are excluded from the cached prefix (stability test).
- [ ] `make lint` + tests pass; no finding change.

## Remediation (opus review — MAJOR 6)
- The workflow system prompt interpolates PER-RUN ticket data (`workflow/runs.py:146 resolve_prompt`), so it is
  NOT byte-stable — `anthropic_cache_instructions` over it would miss every run. Caching requires moving volatile
  ticket data OUT of the system prompt into the USER message across workflow prompts (verify/decide/coach/
  grounding/completion-verification/code-review) and marking the stable vs volatile split in the prompt model.
- file_impact extended to the prompt model/front-matter.
- [ ] The rendered workflow system PREFIX is byte-stable across runs (a stability test); per-run ticket data is
      relocated to the user message.
- [ ] verify/decide/coach + completion-verification + code-review show `cache_read > 0` on repeats (anthropic).

## Remediation (single-pass G3/G4 review — G3-1/G4-A)
- 'No finding change' for the 11 relocated prompts is currently ASSERTED, not measured — and one is the
  completion-verifier that backs this project's mandatory close gate. Add a fidelity check.
- [ ] The relocated gate prompts (esp. completion-verifier + code-review) are FIDELITY-VERIFIED: they produce
      equivalent findings post-relocation (reuse parity.py recall/false-accept, or a targeted spot eval) — not asserted.
baseline.summary: Engine-wide caching: extend the runner cache to RunnerAgentStep (all workflow agent steps)

## Context / Problem

The `PreToolUse:Bash` hook fails intermittently with

    PreToolUse:Bash hook error
    Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py: No such file or directory

The failure is non-blocking, so tool calls still run — but the Serena-vs-grep navigation guidance the hook exists to inject is SILENTLY ABSENT for those calls, which is the whole point of the hook.

## Root cause — established by construction, not inferred

`.claude/settings.json` configures the hook with a RELATIVE command path:

    "matcher": "Bash",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py" }]

A relative command is resolved against the SHELL'S CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY at hook time, not against the project root. So the hook works or fails depending purely on where the preceding tool call left the shell.

MEASURED on this host:

    MISSING  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat-c403-overlap-batch
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/fix/1157-ladder-windows
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat/0d76-bedrock-parity

`.tickets-tracker` is the ticket store — a separate git worktree with no `scripts/` directory. Any Bash call issued while the shell sits there fails the hook. That matches the observed occurrences exactly: the errors appeared in a run immediately after ticket-store commands, which leave the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker`.

This is not a missing file. The script is present and executable in the main checkout and in every code worktree checked; only the resolution path is wrong.

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic warning

* It fails OPEN and QUIET. The guidance simply does not appear, and nothing in the transcript says
  "you are now operating without the navigation reminder" — an agent cannot tell a call that got the
  hint from one that did not.
* It is CWD-dependent, so it is intermittent and looks flaky. That invites the wrong diagnosis
  ("transient hook error") instead of the real one.
* It affects any repo-adjacent working directory, not just `.tickets-tracker` — any tool call run
  from `/tmp`, a scratch dir, or a non-repo path hits the same thing.

## Approach

Make the command path independent of the caller's cwd. Claude Code exposes `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for exactly this, so the command should be `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py"` (quoted). An absolute path would also work but is not portable across checkouts, and this repo is routinely used from multiple worktrees, so the project-dir form is preferable.

Worth checking in the same pass whether any OTHER hook in `.claude/settings.json` uses a relative command and has the same latent defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The hook resolves and runs from ANY working directory, including `.tickets-tracker` and a
      directory outside the repository entirely.
- [ ] A check or test asserts no hook in `.claude/settings.json` is configured with a relative command
      path, so the defect cannot silently return.
- [ ] Every other hook entry in the file is audited for the same relative-path issue and fixed or
      explicitly confirmed safe.
- [ ] Verified by running a Bash tool call with the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker` and observing the
      hook's guidance appear rather than an error.
baseline.summary: PreToolUse Bash hook uses a relative command path, so it silently fails from any cwd without scripts/

content.text: ## Why
Catch wiring bugs without a (near-undecidable, no-good-library) subsumption engine. Validated by
spike E2.
## What
- Extend `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py` with a 3-state SHALLOW structural check: top-level
required-field presence + primitive kind compatibility -> OK / UNKNOWN / ERROR; ABSTAIN (UNKNOWN)
on `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not`/`$ref` (no subsumption).
- Add RUNTIME validation in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`: a produced value is validated
against the downstream CONSUMER's input contract via the registry validator (the real safety net).
- VALIDATOR-FAILURE handling (parity with S7's endpoint-failure fix): if the runtime validator itself
errors (unresolvable `$ref`, registry miss, validator exception) — as opposed to producing a
validation finding — the step run surfaces a distinct, visible "validation unavailable / errored"
signal and does NOT silently treat the value as valid (fail-loud, never false-pass).
- Editor: render an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque sources (`editor.py`).
## Scope
In: shallow static + runtime validation + validator-failure handling + badge. Out: MCP opaque handling (follow-on epic).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shallow check returns ERROR on missing-required / kind-mismatch, UNKNOWN on `oneOf`, OK on a matching shape (port spike E2).
- [ ] Runtime validation checks a produced value against the CONSUMER's input contract; a mismatch surfaces.
- [ ] A runtime VALIDATOR failure (unresolvable `$ref` / registry miss / validator exception) surfaces a distinct "validation errored" signal and never silently passes the value (fail-loud), tested.
- [ ] The inspector shows an "unchecked" badge for UNKNOWN/opaque-typed sources.

baseline.description:
LLM completion-verification close gate: an optional, signed agentic gate that verifies a ticket's completion criteria are met before closure.

## Context
rebar ships an optional LLM agent-operations framework (`rebar.llm`: review_ticket / review_code / scan_epics_for_spec) over library/CLI/MCP, plus an environment-bound HMAC signing module (`rebar.signing`: sign_manifest / verify_signature, with key-fingerprint attribution and HEAD binding) and an opt-in story/epic close `_signature_gate`. This epic adds a **completion-verifier** agent (adapted from the DSO `completion-verifier`) that, on a close attempt, verifies every acceptance/success/close/completion criterion (and, for bugs, that the bug is resolved) is demonstrably met, then — on PASS — produces a **signed** completion attestation that the close gate certifies.

Trust model (per design): security is only meaningful when rebar runs as the MCP server, whose environment signing key is canonical; CLI/library installs sign with a local key that CI reads as `foreign_key` (accepted-as-insecure by design). CI verifies the attestation under the MCP server's key. `--force-close` closes the ticket but withholds the signature, so a closed-without-signature ticket is the durable signal that validation did not pass.

This is distinct from (but composes with) epic 8a1c (cryptographic gate hardening / protected tags).

## What changes
- A pluggable per-operation structured-output **contract** (the runner stops hardcoding the findings model; each op/workflow selects its contract via `output_schema`).
- A `completion_verdict` schema + contract: `{verdict: PASS|FAIL, findings[], summary}` where each FAIL finding cites the failing criterion, an explanation, and (if applicable) a source-code citation.
- A `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt covering epics/stories/tasks/bugs (read-only fs + read-only rebar ticket access).
- `verify_completion` operation over library/CLI/MCP (MCP gated by `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM`).
- A close-time gate (`verify.require_completion_verification_for_close`, default off) that runs the verifier OUTSIDE the write lock, blocks on FAIL/missing-LLM (fail-closed, `--force-close` bypass), and signs the verdict on PASS.
- Enable the gate + LLM module in THIS project's rebar config.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pluggable output contract: runner builds the structured-output model from `RunRequest`/step `output_schema` (default = findings), registry-based and tested.
- [ ] `completion_verdict.schema.json` added + registered in the schemas registry; Pydantic mirror pinned by a test.
- [ ] `completion-verifier` reviewer prompt added (catalog + packaged `*.md`); handles epic/story/task/bug; bug → "resolved" check.
- [ ] `verify_completion` exposed on library (`rebar.llm.verify_completion`), CLI (`rebar verify-completion`), and gated MCP (`verify_completion`).
- [ ] Close gate wired into `transition_compute` (outside lock, lazy import): FAIL or missing-LLM blocks (fail-closed) with `--force-close` bypass; PASS signs via `sign_manifest` then closes; force-close skips verify+sign.
- [ ] `verify.require_completion_verification_for_close` typed config flag (default off) with coercion + tests.
- [ ] This project's tracked `rebar.toml` enables the gate (`[verify] require_completion_verification_for_close`) + `[mcp] allow_llm` (`.rebar/config.conf` is git-ignored, so a tracked config is used).
- [ ] Docs updated (docs/llm-framework.md + CLAUDE.md tool set); optionality + schema-pin + gate-behavior + fake-runner tests pass.
- [ ] Closing a task/story/epic/bug with the gate on runs the verifier; PASS attaches a certified signature and the close proceeds; FAIL blocks with findings.
- [ ] `--force-close="reason"` closes without running the verifier and without a signature (no signed confirmation of passing validation).
- [ ] The optionality contract still holds: `import rebar` / `import rebar.llm` pull no heavy deps; a missing `[agents]` extra degrades cleanly on every interface.
- [ ] Each operation/workflow can declare its own output contract; findings remains the default; `completion_verdict` is the first alternate.
- [ ] This project's config enables the gate and the LLM module.
baseline.summary: LLM completion-verification close gate (signed, optional)

baseline.description:
## What

Three follow-ups spun out of dc3f (puzzling-obsidian-bunny) after its core gap — 3 undeployed
CloudWatch alarms — was fixed by a terraform apply: (1) confirm the alert SNS subscription
actually delivers, (2) add terraform drift-detection CI so committed-but-unapplied HCL cannot
sit unnoticed (the root cause of dc3f), and (3) bring a live-but-unmanaged alarm under IaC.

These are bundled deliberately: all three harden the SAME alerting/IaC chain for the rebar-gerrit
host and are small. Each AC below names a single unambiguous disposition (no open design choice
left to the executor).

## Scope

- rebar-gerrit-alerts SNS email subscription (the alert sink).
- No terraform CI exists (apply is manual per infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md), so committed
  HCL can silently sit unapplied — the dc3f root cause.
- One live alarm (rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high) exists in AWS but is absent from HCL/state and has
  an EMPTY alarm_actions list (never notifies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [operator-attested] AC1 — SNS subscription delivers. The rebar-gerrit-alerts email
  subscription to joeoakhart@navapbc.com is CONFIRMED (not PendingConfirmation) so alarms
  actually deliver. Evidence: a ticket comment recording the get-subscription-attributes result
  (PendingConfirmation=false) with the SubscriptionArn and date. NOTE: verified 2026-07-11 —
  PendingConfirmation=false; this AC is already met and needs NO destructive replacement sink.
- [ ] AC2a — OIDC role (least-privilege, plan-only). The GitHub OIDC provider
  (token.actions.githubusercontent.com) ALREADY EXISTS in account 896586841071 (verified); this
  ticket adds a NEW IAM role `rebar-terraform-plan` in infra/terraform/iam.tf whose trust policy
  is scoped to `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` (sub condition) with aud=sts.amazonaws.com, and whose
  permissions are AWS-managed ReadOnlyAccess + one inline statement granting kms:Decrypt
  constrained by kms:ViaService=ssm (for the alert-endpoint SecureString data source). No apply
  or write permissions — plan-only, least privilege.
- [ ] AC2b — drift-detection CI. `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` runs
  `terraform plan -input=false -lock=false -detailed-exitcode` in infra/terraform, authenticating
  via GitHub OIDC to `rebar-terraform-plan`. `-detailed-exitcode` makes a non-empty plan (exit 2)
  FAIL the check. Triggers: pull_request touching infra/terraform/**, push to main touching
  infra/terraform/** (catches already-committed-but-unapplied drift, not just PR diffs), a daily
  schedule, and workflow_dispatch.
- [ ] AC3 — codify + import the orphan alarm (keep coverage; non-destructive). Add
  `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high` (name rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high;
  namespace rebar/host, metric disk_used_percent published by observability.sh, dims
  InstanceId=data.aws_instance.gerrit.id + mount=/var/gerrit, threshold 85, GTE) to
  infra/terraform/monitoring.tf WITH alarm_actions/ok_actions = the SNS topic (closing the
  silent-alarm gap), then `terraform import` it into state so HCL/state/reality agree. The alarm
  is KEPT (data-volume disk pressure is real coverage), not deleted.

## Verification

- AC1: `aws sns get-subscription-attributes` shows PendingConfirmation=false (recorded as a
  comment).
- AC2/AC3: `terraform validate` passes and `terraform plan` (ReadOnlyAccess creds) shows the new
  role/policies/alarm apply cleanly with no errors — run pre-merge in the worktree.
- Post-merge operator step (needs live creds): `terraform import
  aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` then
  `terraform apply` to wire the alarm actions and create the role; the terraform-drift CI then
  reports green (no drift) on the next run.

## Notes / decisions (resolve prior plan-review BLOCKs)

- Shared S3 state backend (rebar-tfstate-896586841071) means terraform writes (import/apply) MUST
  follow the HCL merge — importing to shared state before merge would make an un-branched plan
  read the alarm as "to destroy". So this ticket lands the reviewed HCL/CI via Gerrit; the
  import/apply is the documented post-merge operator step above.
- AC1's original "OR replace with a confirmation-free sink" option is dropped: the subscription is
  already confirmed, so no destructive substitution (which risked dark alerting) is needed.
baseline.summary: rebar-gerrit alerting hardening: confirm/replace SNS subscription + add terraform drift CI

## Problem
In a consumer repo (rebar installed, no rebar docs/ tree), every coaching deep-link in review-plan output points to a nonexistent local file, so the documented 'follow the link to understand the criterion you failed' affordance is dead out of the box.

## Root cause (confirmed against installed v0.10.0)
config.plan_review_docs_url() defaults to (repo_root()/'docs'/'plan-review-criteria-guide.md').as_uri() = file://<consumer-repo>/docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md when REBAR_DOCS_URL is unset. orchestrator coaching builds guide_url from that base. src/rebar/config.py:67-74; orchestrator ~line 578. (The 'rebar explain' COMMAND was separately fixed in c2bfbe217 by packaging guides; the deep-link URL default was not.)

## Fix
Default plan_review_docs_url to a canonical published URL (the upstream hosted docs for the criteria guide) rather than a consumer-repo file:// path, still overridable by REBAR_DOCS_URL. Links then resolve for consumers by default.

## Acceptance criteria
- With REBAR_DOCS_URL unset and cwd a consumer repo (no docs/ tree), plan_review_docs_url() returns a canonical http(s) URL, not a file:// path under the consumer repo.
- REBAR_DOCS_URL still overrides.
- A unit test asserts the default is a canonical hosted URL (not file://); asserting the old file:// default would FAIL.

## Verification
pytest asserting the default scheme is http(s) and anchors resolve as <url>#<criterion-id>.
baseline.summary: plan-review coaching deep-links resolve to a file:// path in the consuming repo (dead for consumers)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Set up a checkout with its venv INSIDE the repo root (e.g. a worktree bootstrapped per docs/local-dev-env.md: python3 -m venv .venv inside the worktree).
2. Run: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_resolve_symbol_tool.py::test_resolve_symbol_confirms_third_party_module -q

Expected: PASS - yaml resolves with origin classified third-party/stdlib. Actual: FAIL - output reads 'EXISTS: yaml resolves in the installed environment [repo-local, origin=<repo>/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/__init__.py]' because the classifier treats any origin path under the repo root as repo-local, and site-packages sits under the repo root in this layout. Fails identically on an untouched main checkout (reproduced 2026-07-15); CI passes only because its venv lives outside the checkout. The classifier should exclude virtualenv/site-packages paths from the repo-local classification (e.g. exclude sys.prefix / site.getsitepackages() subtrees) before the repo-root prefix test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The origin classifier treats module origins under the active environment's site-packages as third-party/stdlib even when that directory is inside the repo root. Oracle: the reproduction above passes from a venv-inside-repo checkout.
- [ ] A unit test pins the venv-inside-repo case (monkeypatched origin path under repo_root/.venv/.../site-packages classified third-party).
baseline.summary: resolve-symbol tool misclassifies third-party modules as repo-local when the venv lives inside the repo root

# plan-review fan-out optimization: caching, parallelize, merge, bin-pack (token + wall-clock, fidelity-preserving)

## Context

plan-review's container criteria G3/G4 run as `2*N_children` SEQUENTIAL agentic LLM calls
(`pass1.py:_run_container`), OUTSIDE the thread pool — N=8 ⇒ 16 calls ≈ 27 min, each re-sending the whole
parent plan. Proven bounded-but-slow (faulthandler stacks + per-pairing instrumentation), not a loop.
Provenance: authored in the BESPOKE harness (story ca03 / dry-frost-zenith, commit 832b3af0) for
CONTEXT-WINDOW FITTING while keeping content whole ("never chunk content"); the workflow migration extracted
it verbatim; it is NOT a partial-re-review mechanism. G3/G4 are inherently CROSS-CHILD criteria, so the
per-child slice was a window concession that batching can partly reverse for both cost AND fidelity.

Engine impact: most work is inside the ProductionBatchRunner (`run_pass1`/`pass1.py`/`passes.py`/`sizing.py`),
invoked as ONE opaque `batch` step — the interpreter/YAML need no change. The shared seam is the runner
(`RunRequest` + `runner.py`), used by both `passes.py` and the engine `RunnerAgentStep`; caching is applied
there and extended engine-wide. Caching approach + gotchas confirmed against OSS pydantic-ai users
(Arize/phoenix, code-graph-rag, shotgun, varro).

## Children (de-risk order)

1. **S1** caching substrate at the shared runner seam (fidelity-neutral) — foundational.
2. **S3** parallelize the container fan-out + warm-then-fan-out + budget-cap fix (depends S1).
3. **S2** engine-wide caching via RunnerAgentStep (depends S1).
4. **S4** merge G3+G4 into one call per bin (depends S3; eval-gated).
5. **S5** child bin-packing (depends S4; eval-gated).
6. **S6** fidelity-eval harness `da34` (reuse eval_specs + parity.py; gates S4/S5).

Fidelity-neutral pieces (S1, S3, S2) ship ahead of the eval-gated ones (S4, S5).

## Out of scope

Reverting to the pre-ca03 "2 parallel whole-plan calls" design (trades back per-child fidelity); content
chunking/truncation (forbidden by ca03); the grace-thud-feint delta-re-review path (separate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six child stories (S1-S6) closed.
- [ ] An 8-child epic review completes in minutes (was ~27 min) with materially lower token cost (cache reads non-zero).
- [ ] Caching is provider-safe: openai/gemini calls succeed unchanged.
- [ ] Findings remain within offline-eval tolerance of the current per-child behavior (no fidelity regression).
- [ ] `make lint` + full suite pass.


## Remediation (opus review)
- S1 RESCOPED: cache the SYSTEM PROMPT (anthropic_cache_instructions/tool_definitions, anthropic-gated) — the stable
  parent plan lives there, not the user message; no RunRequest content-list change (avoids breaking the
  structured-output retry path).
- NEW S6 (`da34-ac98-e375-4af0`) fidelity-eval HARNESS: a SEMANTIC eval (real findings, new-vs-baseline) — the existing parity
  harness is structural (FakeRunner, zero model calls). S4 and S5 now DEPEND ON S6.
- S3: non-streaming warm-then-fan-out (warm = first real pairing to completion); a NEW pool inside _run_container;
  budget cap must NOT shed G3/G4 (fidelity) — fix the cost model, not centrality scaling.
- S2: caching workflow steps requires relocating per-run ticket data out of the (interpolated) system prompt.
- Updated DAG: S1->{S2,S3}; S3->S4; S6->{S4,S5}; S4->S5.

## Sequencing note (single-pass G3/G4 review)
- Land S3 -> S4 -> S5 STRICTLY in DAG order: S4/S5's sizing.py container-cost projections are only correct AFTER S3's 'container never shed' + cost-model fix lands.
baseline.summary: plan-review container fan-out (G3/G4) is sequential — epic review wall-time ~2*N_children agentic calls, looks like a hang
