## Reproduction Steps
1. Run an attested-mode LLM gate from any checkout, e.g. `rebar review-plan <id>` (default source=attested).
2. Observe `Error: cannot list '<code-snapshot>/.tickets-tracker'` on stderr; the linked-session-log ISF context + prior REVIEW_RESULT recall are silently dropped.

## Root cause
In attested mode the ticket store is materialized SEPARATELY (`current_tickets_root()` / `cfg.tickets_path`) because it lives on the orphan `tickets` branch, absent from the code snapshot. `plan_review/pass1.py` passed `ctx.repo_root` (the CODE snapshot) as `repo_root` for TICKET reads: `_reads.show_ticket(tgt, repo_root=ctx.repo_root)` (line 319) and `sidecar.prior_concerns(..., repo_root=ctx.repo_root)` (line 504). `tracker_dir(<code-snapshot>)` = `<code-snapshot>/.tickets-tracker` which doesn't exist -> `_scan_alias` prints 'cannot list' and the reads degrade. PlanContext had no ticket-root field, so pass1 reused the code root.

## Fix
Add `tickets_root` to `PlanContext`, populated from `current_tickets_root()` at assemble time (assembling thread -> survives the pass1 worker-thread fan-out a ContextVar would not be inherited by); route the two reads through `ctx.tickets_root` (None -> live checkout store).

## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: attested ticket reads resolve against the pinned tickets snapshot; no spurious errors; ISF + recall preserved.
- Actual: reads target the code snapshot -> 'cannot list' + silently dropped context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PlanContext` carries `tickets_root` from `current_tickets_root()` at assemble time.
- [ ] `pass1.py` session-log + prior-concerns reads use `ctx.tickets_root`, not `ctx.repo_root`.
- [ ] Regression test asserts both reads target the tickets root (mutation-checked RED->GREEN).
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green.
baseline.summary: Attested LLM gate reads the ticket store from the code snapshot (silent context loss + 'cannot list' noise)

content.text: ## Why

CI keeps two ratchets advisory/non-gating (test.yml): full-tree mypy and the full-set ruff. The clean core (reducer/graph/_store) is mypy-gated, but the rest of src/rebar carries 158 mypy errors so gating it would red every build; and BLE001 (blind-except) is relaxed for tests/**. This let a type error reach CI on #56 (the local hook only runs ruff). Goal: drive the debt to zero and make both fully gating, so type/blind-except regressions fail at commit + CI, not after merge.
## What

- Drive `mypy src/rebar` to ZERO (158 errors / 37 files): llm (56), _engine_support (47), _engine (46), _io (6), _commands (3). Fix properly — real annotations / guards / TypeGuards; a justified `# type: ignore[code]` ONLY for genuine external-untyped / false-positive cases, never blanket silencing.

- Tighten BLE001: remove `BLE001` from the `tests/**` per-file-ignore and resolve the 20 blind-excepts (specific exception types or inline-justified `# noqa: BLE001`). KEEP the T201 CLI-print ignores (intentional operator output — out of scope).

- Flip CI to gating: expand `make typecheck` to the full `src/rebar`; make the test.yml mypy step gating (drop the advisory `|| true`); remove the now-redundant advisory full-set ruff step (the gating `make lint` already covers E,F,W,I,UP,B). Add a `typecheck` pre-commit hook so type errors fail at commit time.
## Scope

In scope: the mypy + BLE001 remediation + the CI/Makefile/hook gating flip. Out of scope (separate efforts, flagged): the module-size allowlist (file-splitting refactor), coverage fail_under=50 (needs new tests), the intentional T201 CLI-print ignores.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `mypy src/rebar` reports zero errors (was 158); fixes are real type corrections, with any `# type: ignore` carrying a code + one-line justification.
- [ ] `ruff check src tests` passes with BLE001 removed from the tests/** ignore (the 20 blind-excepts resolved); the T201 ignores are retained.
- [ ] `make typecheck` covers the full `src/rebar`; the CI mypy step is gating (no `|| true`); the redundant advisory ruff step is removed.
- [ ] A `typecheck` pre-commit hook runs `make typecheck` (check-only, never mutates), consistent with the existing lint hook.
- [ ] The full non-integration test suite stays green; no behavior change (type/lint-only edits).

baseline.summary: Enable full mypy + ruff(BLE001) gating in CI — remove the advisory ratchets

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar forked from navapbc/digital-service-orchestra (DSO) and inherits DSO's
Jira-reconciler design, but rebar currently has **no CI that runs the reconciler** —
Jira sync only happens when a human runs `rebar reconcile` locally. We want the
Jira <-> rebar sync to run automatically and observably, modeled on DSO's two
GitHub Actions workflows (`reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`),
translated to rebar's diverged surface, and documented so client projects can adopt
it from templates we ship.

### Confirmed divergences from DSO (drive the translation)
- Invocation: `rebar reconcile --mode live` (== `python -m rebar_reconciler`).
  Exit 75 = reschedule (re-run, NOT failure); exit 3 = another pass in flight.
- **Reconciler does NOT push its event writes.** It writes inbound events as
  uncommitted files into the `.tickets-tracker` worktree and bypasses the CLI
  auto-push path, so a CI **commit-back + push to `origin/tickets`** step is
  REQUIRED (DSO's loop is necessary, not redundant). `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH` does not
  cover this.
- No `BRIDGE_ENV_ID`; optional `REBAR_ENV_ID` (default author stamp "reconciler").
- Env names are the new `REBAR_*` set; Jira creds stay `JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/
  JIRA_PROJECT` (vars) + `JIRA_API_TOKEN` (secret, env-only).
- Canary ticket ops -> `rebar list --has-tag --output json`, `rebar create bug
  ... --priority --tags --description`, `rebar comment`, `rebar transition <id>
  open closed --reason "Fixed: ..."` (bug-close reason prefix enforced).
- Do NOT wire `scripts/jira-pressure-test/` e2e probes into CI (explicitly manual,
  live-mutating). Prefer `rebar bridge-probe` / `--mode reconcile-check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: schedule (~*/20) + workflow_dispatch
      (mode choice incl. dry-run/reconcile-check/live); mounts the `tickets` orphan
      branch as `.tickets-tracker` worktree; installs rebar + pinned acli (checksum
      verified) and authenticates; runs `rebar reconcile --mode <mode>`; treats exit
      75 as reschedule and 3 as benign "pass in flight"; commits reconciler events
      back and pushes to `origin/tickets` via a fetch-rebase-push retry loop; single-
      flight `concurrency`; failure surfaced to the run summary.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`: hourly schedule; checks the
      last successful `reconcile-bridge.yml` run via the Actions API; when stale
      beyond the window, opens (or comments on) a `heartbeat-alert`-tagged bug via
      the `rebar` CLI and auto-closes it on recovery; treats API errors as transient
      (no false alarms); commits ticket changes back to `origin/tickets`.
- [ ] Necessary+sufficient validation written up: each workflow step justified
      against rebar's actual reconciler surface (commit-back required, exit codes,
      lock semantics, creds), with anything intentionally omitted called out.
- [ ] `rebar.toml` carries the `[jira]` sync target (url/user/project=REB); the
      `JIRA_API_TOKEN` secret stays env-only.
- [ ] A setup doc (e.g. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`) documents, for a CLIENT project,
      exactly which repo **variables** (JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_PROJECT, ACLI_VERSION/
      ACLI_SHA256, bridge-bot identity) and **secrets** (JIRA_API_TOKEN) to set, how
      to mount the tickets branch, and how to copy the workflow templates; the two
      workflow files double as the copy-paste templates.
- [ ] Workflows lint/parse (actionlint or equivalent) and a dry-run/`reconcile-check`
      dispatch path is described for safe first validation before enabling `live`.
- [ ] A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow keeps the REB Jira project and the rebar
- [ ] A heartbeat canary detects when the reconciler goes stale and files/auto-closes a
- [ ] The set of workflows + repo vars/secrets is validated as NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT
- [ ] Client projects can stand up the same sync by copying templates and following a

## Plan-review remediations (advisory findings triaged — all valid)

- **Canary staleness threshold (fd3a, E2).** Pin the window: alert when no
  successful `reconcile-bridge.yml` run completed in the **last 60 minutes**
  (3x the 20-min cadence); exposed as a `workflow_dispatch` override
  (`alert_window_hours`, default 2 to match DSO) and validated as a positive int.
- **Necessary+sufficient write-up location (f67d/T7, F1).** It lives as a
  **`## Necessary & sufficient` section inside `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`** — ONE
  doc, not a separate design doc (resolves the navigation-ambiguity finding). The
  section maps each workflow step to the rebar reconciler fact that requires it.
- **Rollback / disable path (f8f1, T4).** Document: disable via Actions UI (toggle
  the workflow) or remove the `schedule:` trigger; an erroneous `origin/tickets`
  push is revertable via normal git history on the orphan branch; the
  `dry-run` / `reconcile-check` dispatch mode is the mandatory safe-first-validation
  gate before enabling `live`.
- **Least-privilege token + identity (f638, T10).** Each workflow pins an explicit
  minimal `permissions:` block — reconcile-bridge: `contents: write`; canary:
  `contents: write` + `actions: read`. The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` is sufficient for
  both the `origin/tickets` push and the Actions API read (no PAT needed); the
  commit identity is a configurable bridge-bot (`BRIDGE_BOT_NAME`/`_EMAIL` repo vars).
- **AC-quality / observable outcomes (f607, P6).** "Sufficient" is operationalized:
  the necessary+sufficient claim is checkable as the `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`
  section that justifies every step against a cited reconciler fact (commit-back
  required, exit 75/3 handling, lock semantics, env/creds), with omissions listed.
baseline.summary: Automated Jira<->rebar sync via GitHub Actions (reconcile-bridge + heartbeat canary) + client setup docs

## Summary
Outbound Jira link sync writes `depends_on` dependencies with **inverted endpoints**, because
the apply seam drops the `swap_endpoints` flag. This produces backwards "Blocks" links in Jira
and perpetual, non-fatal `rebar.link … "would create a cycle"` WARNINGs on every inbound pass.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create rebar tickets A, B with `A depends_on B` (B blocks A).
2. Reconcile outbound to Jira; observe Jira records **"A Blocks B"** (WRONG — should be "B Blocks A").
3. Reconcile inbound; the reconciler reads the inverted link and tries `add_dependency(A, B, blocks)`,
   which collides with the existing `A depends_on B` edge → `check_would_create_cycle` rejects it.
   Observed live for the 6 closed sibling stories under epic `jira-reb-687` (30ff/a879/95a5/978d/9a82/fd1d).

**Expected:** `A depends_on B` → Jira "B Blocks A"; inbound re-read is idempotent (no cycle).
**Actual:** Jira "A Blocks B" (inverted); inbound re-read cycle-rejects on every pass forever.

## Root Cause (verified, runtime-reproduced)
`depends_on` maps to `("Blocks", swap=True)` — "A depends_on B" must be written as "B Blocks A".
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py:121`: `jira_type, _swap = mapped` — **`_swap`
  is discarded**; the emitted mutation carries `type`/`to_key`/`relation` but no direction correction.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:831`: applies `set_relationship(issue_key,
  to_key, link_type)` — always making `issue_key` the outward/blocker side; **`relation` is never read,
  no swap anywhere in the apply path.** This violates the module's own documented contract
  (`outbound_links.py:105`: "swap_endpoints is handled by the applier when issuing the directional
  Jira call") and the intent of bug 3f04 (`f57cdcd2d`, "sync issue-link relationships in both directions").
- Pre-existing since 3f04 (2026-06-26); unrelated to the reconcile-bridge outage fix.

## Impact
- **rebar store:** no divergence/data loss — the acyclic DAG is correct; the rejected inbound links are
  the inverse edges that *should not* exist. The WARNINGs are cosmetic noise to rebar.
- **Jira:** real, persistent, SILENT data-fidelity divergence — every `depends_on`-derived link points the
  wrong way and never self-heals (outbound + inbound are both ADD-only and dedup "either direction").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Outbound apply honors `swap_endpoints`: a `depends_on` dep emits Jira "B Blocks A" (swap `--out`/`--in`),
  while `blocks` is unchanged. Proof: unit test on the applier for both relations.
- [ ] `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_link_sync.py` gains a `depends_on` (swap=True) case (currently
  only the `blocks`/swap=False path is tested — the gap that let this ship).
- [ ] After the fix, an inbound pass over an A depends_on B pair applies idempotently (no cycle WARNING).
- [ ] [operator-attested] one-time repair of the already-inverted Jira links (neither diff self-corrects them).
baseline.summary: Outbound Jira link sync inverts depends_on direction (drops swap_endpoints) — backwards Jira links + perpetual cycle-warning noise

baseline.description:
## Summary

In LIVE mode — the only mode production runs — `mutation_failures` is structurally always 0, so the reconciler's "fail loud at the end" exit is dead code. A pass that records per-mutation failures exits 0 and prints `applied N of N`.

Found by a regression audit of bug 449f's fix. The hole is PRE-EXISTING and old, but 449f's change routes two more actions (outbound create and delete) into it, converting what used to be a loud crash into a silent green pass.

## Mechanism

1. `_apply_batch` writes a manifest containing every mutation outcome, including
   `outcome["error"]` for soft-failed ones.
2. `apply_planning._emit_mode_manifest`, LIVE branch: **unlinks that manifest** and
   returns `("RETURN", None)` — "LIVE: no manifest file per contract".
3. `applier.apply()` therefore returns `None` in LIVE.
4. `reconcile.py` tally:
   ```
   mutations_applied = len(mutations)
   mutation_failures = 0
   if nowrite_plan is not None: ...
   elif manifest_path is not None:      # <-- never true in LIVE
       ... mutation_failures = sum(1 for o in outcomes if o.get("error"))
   ```
   With `manifest_path=None` the whole block is skipped. Its comment calls this
   "rare paths"; in LIVE it is the ONLY path.
5. `__main__.py` — `if failures > 0: return 1` can never fire in LIVE.

The dict-return seam does not save it either: `reconcile.py` only captures a dict return as `nowrite_plan` when `not persist`, and LIVE has `persist=True`.

## Blast radius — three contracts silently defeated in production

- **e534-5154-2401-40fb** ("isolate + fail loud at end"): the isolate half works; the
  fail-loud half has never worked in LIVE.
- **48c8-5375-f883-462d**: `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1` is ON in the live
  workflow (`reconcile-bridge.yml`). Its stated purpose is to make swallowed comment
  failures "count toward mutation_failures and drive a non-zero pass exit". It cannot.
  The flag has never had its intended effect in production.
- **85a1** (truthful tally): `mutations_applied = len(mutations)` counts FAILED
  mutations as applied, so stdout prints `OK: applied N of N mutations` while
  mutations failed — the exact structural lie 85a1 was filed to kill.

## Regression introduced by 449f (bcd888352)

| | before 449f | after 449f |
|---|---|---|
| outbound create/delete 404 | `HTTPError` escapes -> exit 1, RED, 29 of 30 mutations skipped | isolated, 29 applied, failure recorded — but exit **0**, GREEN, prints `applied 30 of 30` |

449f is directionally right (the 29 mutations now land) but it traded a loud failure for a silent one. Both halves of e534 must hold.

## Why no test caught it

Every fail-loud / truthful-tally test stubs `reconcile_once` to RETURN a `mutation_failures` value directly (e.g. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_fail_loud_exit_and_preflight.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_truthful_tally.py`). Nothing exercises `reconcile.py`'s real manifest tally in LIVE mode. 449f's own new test asserts batch-continuation at the `_apply_one` level and stops short of the exit code — the untested seam is exactly between them.

## Candidate fixes (decision required)

- **A. Surface the tally out-of-band from LIVE.** `_emit_mode_manifest`'s LIVE branch
  returns counts instead of `None`; `apply()` propagates; `reconcile.py` consumes them
  when `persist` is true. Preserves the "no manifest file in LIVE" contract. Changes
  `apply()`'s return contract, so every caller/stub must be checked.
- **B. Compute the tally before unlinking.** LIVE reads `applied_count`/`failed_count`
  out of the manifest it is about to delete and returns those. Smaller blast radius
  than A, same effect.
- **C. Keep the manifest in LIVE.** Simplest, but reverses a deliberate contract —
  needs the original rationale (size? PII?) before considering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In LIVE mode, a pass with >= 1 per-mutation failure exits NON-ZERO.
- [ ] In LIVE mode, `mutations_applied` excludes failed mutations, so the stdout line
      cannot claim `applied N of N` when a mutation failed (85a1 restored in LIVE).
- [ ] `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1` demonstrably drives a non-zero exit in
      LIVE (48c8's stated purpose actually achieved).
- [ ] A test drives the REAL `reconcile.py` LIVE tally path end-to-end to the exit
      code — not a stubbed `reconcile_once` return. RED before the fix.
- [ ] The "no manifest file in LIVE" contract is either preserved, or its removal is
      justified against the original rationale.
- [ ] File paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_planning.py`,
      `applier.py`, `reconcile.py`, `__main__.py`.
baseline.summary: LIVE mode never counts mutation failures: fail-loud exit is dead code, failed mutations reported as applied

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. AWS account 896586841071, us-east-1: inspect the `voter_errors` metric in CloudWatch namespace `rebar/host` (instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5) over 2026-07-05..07.
2. Review the `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm history (`aws cloudwatch describe-alarm-history --alarm-name rebar-gerrit-voter-errors`).
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the review-bot (the 'voter') casts the Gerrit LLM-Review vote with zero errors; `voter_errors` stays at 0.

- Actual: 52 `voter_errors` in recurring bursts across 07-05 17:27 PT -> 07-06 21:27 PT (2-5/period, peak Sum=10 in the 09:27 PT hour). The `rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` alarm (fires on any datapoint>0) flapped OK<->ALARM repeatedly on 07-06 evening; last recovered ALARM->OK at 07-06 22:17 PT. Clean and OK for ~19h since.
- Impact: the voter casts the Gerrit LLM-Review gate vote — intermittent failures risk stalling the review gate (currently recovered).
## Investigation blocker

The Gerrit host ships NO logs to CloudWatch Logs (only snap-demo groups exist), so the voter-service error text lives only in the EC2 instance journald and is not retrievable read-only via CloudWatch. Root-causing needs on-host access.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Identify the voter/review-bot failure cause from the host's journald (voter service logs) for the 07-05/06 window.
- [ ] Decide whether to ship voter/review-bot logs to a CloudWatch log group so future occurrences are diagnosable remotely.
- [ ] Confirm no LLM-Review votes were actually dropped during the window (or re-cast any that were).

baseline.summary: Gerrit review-bot voter errors: 52 intermittent LLM-Review voting failures over 48h (2026-07-05/06)

## Why
The delivered epic (Gerrit stack 558/560/561/563/576/579/580/581, NOT landed) diverged
from the APPROVED epic design on the authorship-payload format. bde5 (change 561,
commit c31fc7eb5) signs the event's RAW canonical bytes; the approved epic AC requires an
**in-toto Statement** payload whose `subject` binds `{event_uuid, content_hash}`. This
story transitions the authorship *machinery* to the approved design. (User rejected the
delivered design; full divergence record in session_log d7c0.)

## Stack scoping (why this story is authorship.py ONLY)
This story AMENDS Gerrit change 561 = commit c31fc7eb5 (bde5), which touches
`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` and NOTHING else. At that commit the authorship
functions have **no consumers yet**: the write-time signing call site (`_seam.py`), the
merge-gate content-binding (`verify_authorship.py`), and the SNAPSHOT ledger
(`compact.py`) are all introduced later in commit 721702e91 (3183). Therefore the
consumer cutover to the in-toto payload — and the epic-AC-named `create_placeholder`
alias (which wraps `ensure_identity_for`, introduced in commit ec3aff507 / 2f13) — is
handled in **TS3 (117b, change 580)**, the story that reworks that commit. Keeping the
edits in the commit where the symbols actually exist is what keeps every intermediate
patchset internally green.

## What (authorship.py machinery)
Add the in-toto Statement layer as NEW functions, and PRESERVE the existing low-level
primitive so KEY-op signing (`identity.py._verify_keyop_signature`, which signs
`keyop_payload` bytes, not events) and any other caller keep compiling unchanged:

- KEEP `sign_authorship(payload, key_path, principal)` and `verify_authorship(envelope,
  identity_id)` as the low-level SSHSIG-over-DSSE primitive (used by KEY-op signatures).
- `authorship_content_hash(event: dict) -> str`: **SHA-256, lowercase hex** over the
  event's canonical JSON with the `author_sig` key EXCLUDED (the signature never covers
  itself).
- `build_authorship_statement(event_uuid, content_hash) -> dict`: an in-toto Statement:
  - `_type`: `"https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1"`
  - `subject`: `[{ "name": "<event_uuid>", "digest": { "sha256": "<content_hash>" } }]`
  - `predicateType`: `"application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json"`
  - `predicate`: `{}`
- `sign_event_authorship(event: dict, key_path, principal) -> dsse.Envelope`: computes the
  content_hash, builds the Statement, and signs its canonical JSON bytes via the primitive
  (DSSE payloadType `application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json`, PAE-signed under the pinned
  authorship namespace). The Statement JSON is the DSSE payload.
- `verify_event_authorship(event: dict, envelope, identity_id, *, repo_root=None) ->
  Verdict`: (1) parse the DSSE payload as an in-toto Statement, (2) check
  `subject[0].name == event['uuid']` AND `subject[0].digest.sha256 ==
  authorship_content_hash(event)`, (3) THEN verify the DSSE signature against the identity's
  in-band keys (reusing `resolve_trust_root`). Any parse/shape failure or subject/hash
  mismatch yields a non-verified Verdict; it NEVER raises on a lookup problem (mirrors the
  existing fail-closed contract).

## Scope
In: the in-toto Statement authorship machinery in `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`
(content_hash + Statement build + `sign_event_authorship` + `verify_event_authorship`),
with the low-level `sign_authorship`/`verify_authorship` primitive preserved for KEY-ops.
Out: the write-seam stamping + merge-gate content-binding + SNAPSHOT ledger cutover to the
new payload AND the `create_placeholder` alias (all TS3/3183, commit 721702e91); the
era/validity model (TS2/e165); docs/ADR (TS4/b134).

## Landing / sequencing
TS1–TS4 land as ONE ATOMIC Gerrit stack submit (relation chain), so there is no runtime
window where a reworked commit is live without the others. Write-time signing is opt-in
and the stack is unlanded, so no persisted event carries an old-format `author_sig` — no
migration/backfill. Docs/ADR for this pivot are rewritten in TS4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sign_event_authorship` produces a DSSE envelope whose payload is an in-toto
  Statement (`_type` https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1, `predicateType`
  application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json) with `subject[0] = {name: event_uuid,
  digest: {sha256: content_hash}}`; a test asserts the structure + payloadType.
- [ ] `authorship_content_hash` is SHA-256 hex over the canonical event with `author_sig`
  EXCLUDED; a test proves adding/removing an `author_sig` key does not change the hash,
  and mutating any other field DOES change it.
- [ ] `verify_event_authorship` returns verified for an event signed by identity A against
  A's in-band keys; a test asserts it does NOT verify against identity B, FAILS on a
  tampered event body (content_hash mismatch), and FAILS on a tampered signature.
- [ ] `verify_event_authorship` returns a non-verified Verdict (never raises) when the
  envelope payload is not a valid in-toto Statement (malformed / missing subject) and when
  the identity is unknown/keyless (test).
- [ ] The low-level `sign_authorship(payload,...)` primitive is unchanged: a KEY-op-style
  signature over `keyop_payload(...)` bytes still verifies via the primitive path (test),
  proving the Statement layer did not break KEY-op signing.

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (in-toto Statement build/parse + content_hash + event sign/verify; primitive preserved)
baseline.summary: transition: authorship payload -> in-toto Statement (subject binds {event_uuid, content_hash})

## Context / Problem
T5c (the security overlay, exec AGENT) reviews plans under the gate-wide reviewing stance in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:264-274` (`_SHARED_PREAMBLE`), whose line "Evaluate the spec AS WRITTEN, not the current codebase" (passes.py:269) is prepended to EVERY plan-review pass prompt by `_resolve_system` (passes.py:276-292). The T5c rubric file itself (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md`) contains NO as-written text — the stance arrives via the shared preamble. For a security criterion that stance is out of step with surveyed LLM security-review tools (exploitability is a property of the system, not of the text): 46% of T5c's strong findings already cite repo artifacts despite it. Separately, 30% of T5c advisories are pure "does not declare X" template shape that Pass-2 cannot drop (the statement is literally true, so it verifies); 99 reviews carried >= 2 same-shape findings; and T5c advisories displaced other criteria in 103 advisory-cap-limited reviews. The existing SAME-ROUND DEDUP rule in the rubric body (plan_review_T5c.md line 19) dedupes per (surface, defect) PAIR, so a plan with N undeclared surfaces still yields N findings — the new rule is strictly tighter for this one template class. The operator approved: the grounded rewrite, blocking at 0.90, and dedup-at-source plus severity demotion instead of hard citation suppression.

Prior art / supersession: ticket d156-7eb5-b4f0-40c3 (closed) hardened this same rubric explicitly "without changing its posture (advisory @ 0.95)"; this story is the operator-approved follow-on that DOES change the posture — it deliberately supersedes that earlier constraint. Ticket 9374 (S7) is concurrently relocating `_SHARED_PREAMBLE` into prompts.py, so this story must NOT edit passes.py or prompts.py: the grounding change is a criterion-LOCAL override inside the T5c rubric only, which stays correct wherever the preamble lives.

## Approach
All three behavior changes are rubric text — instructions to the Pass-1 finder — following the T10 precedent bfa8 (commit e3962d21e) just landed: "severity guidance, not new machinery". The only non-test config change is two fields in the T5c routing entry. No changes to pass3_decide, orchestrator.py, passes.py, prompts.py, or det_gate_rules.py.

1. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` — four rubric-body edits, preserving every phrase pinned by tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:502-543 (trust-boundary gate first, loopback/not-applicable carve-out, mixed-scope rule, zero-trust caveat, T10 "no blurring" scope note):
   - GROUNDING OVERRIDE sentence: "GROUNDING OVERRIDE (this criterion only): unlike the shared reviewing stance's evaluate-the-spec-AS-WRITTEN default, ground the plan's security implications in the CURRENT codebase and configuration via the read tools — a control defined elsewhere (existing auth middleware, an existing config guard, an ignore rule) FLIPS a finding; verify before you flag." This works as a criterion-local override because the rubric is rendered into the SAME request as the preamble (`_resolve_system` compiles rubric + preamble together, passes.py:276-292) and the criterion-specific instruction is the more specific directive.
   - DEDUP-AT-SOURCE (tightens the existing SAME-ROUND DEDUP sentence for the one template class): emit at most ONE undeclared-access-posture finding per plan; when several surfaces lack a declared access posture, fold the additional surfaces into that single finding's evidence rather than emitting one finding per surface.
   - DEMOTION, not suppression (extends the existing "SEVERITY priors ... these bias how hard you press" sentence in its own idiom): a candidate finding that cites neither a repo artifact you actually read with the tools nor a quoted plan sentence must be pressed at MINOR — demoted, never suppressed (the grounded 46% keep their strength; the ungrounded lose blocking reach).
   - HIGH-class scoping sentence (structural mirror of T10's bfa8 sentence): "ONLY these two HIGH classes warrant severity >= major — a plaintext secret on a boundary-crossing path; an undeclared internet-reachable sensitive surface; every other finding is at most minor." This is consistent with the rubric's existing SEVERITY priors line, which already names exactly these two shapes as HIGH.
   Mechanism (why rubric text is the right lever): the Pass-1 finder emits NO severity field (passes.py:7 — `{finding, criteria[], evidence[], scenarios[], impact}` — severity/priority are computed deterministically in Pass 3 from Pass-2 graded attributes); rubric severity language shapes how the finder frames and presses evidence, which is exactly how bfa8 scoped T10's 0.90 blocking to its four MAJOR classes with zero pass3_decide changes — "so lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 bar through the existing severity->priority pipeline". Blocking itself stays criterion-wide (there is NO per-class blocking mechanism in Pass-3, and this plan does not invent one); the HIGH-class sentence is what keeps non-HIGH findings below the bar.
2. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` T5c entry (lines 385-386): `"block_threshold": 0.95 -> 0.9` and `"default_posture": "advisory" -> "blocking"`. These are the plan-review gate's ONLY blocking controls: `threshold_for` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:45-81) blocks for gate="plan_review" iff `default_posture == "blocking"`. The `blocking_enabled` field is the code-review gate's convention, INERT for plan-review, and is NOT added (convention pinned by tests/unit/test_project_symbol_reference_completeness.py::test_routing_entry_carries_no_inert_blocking_enabled_key). The checklist array in the entry is unchanged.
3. Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` via `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` (the command the guide's own header names; registry.py:604).

Execution stays AGENT; NO DET keyword gate for T5c — the audit showed the best candidate gate fires on 66% of plans while missing real findings (security findings live in plans without security words), unlike T10's 28%/100% rule. Alternative rejected: 1-TURN demotion of the whole criterion — forfeits the repo grounding that produces T5c's best findings. Rollback: a one-commit git revert of the two routing lines restores advisory @ 0.95 (rubric text can stay; it is strictly FP-reducing) — no data or schema migration. The blocking path reuses the existing pass3 machinery end-to-end, so no new failure modes or fail-open/fail-closed policy are introduced; block events land in the signed REVIEW_RESULT sidecars, and post-land behavioral outcomes (grounding rate, template-shape rate) are monitored by the same zero-LLM criterion-effectiveness recorder the bfa8 pilot uses — unit tests pin rubric text and Pass-3 mechanics, deliberately not LLM behavior.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md — rubric rewrite (four sentences).
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json — T5c posture/threshold only.
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py — extend the three `["T3", "T10"]` parametrizations (lines 91, 102, 111) with "T5c".
- tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py — EXPECTED_ROUTING line 68 `"T5c": (0.95, "advisory") -> (0.9, "blocking")`; add T5c to the pilot-blocking set consumed by test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking (lines 152-158).
- tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py — add "T5c" to _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING (line 111).
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py — NEW rubric-text pin module (tests/llm/ does not exist; tests/unit/plan_review/ is the home of the analogous bfa8 tests).
- docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md — regenerated output.
Out of scope: passes.py / prompts.py (ticket 9374 owns the preamble), orchestrator.py, review_kernel/decide.py, det_gate_rules.py.

## Testing
All tests under tests/unit/ (there is no tests/llm/ directory). Exact AC-to-test mapping:
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_criteria_blocking.py (extended parametrizations): the T5c routing entry carries default_posture "blocking" @ 0.9 and `threshold_for(["T5c"], ..., gate="plan_review")` resolves (0.9, True); a T5c finding pinned at priority 0.92 gets decision "block" and one at 0.85 stays "advisory" through the REAL `pass3_over_findings` wrapper (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:737) — covers AC3.
- tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py (new; same pattern as that file's test_t10_rubric_contains_major_class_severity_guidance — read the .md, assert exact phrases): (a) the grounding-override sentence (read tools + current codebase + a-control-defined-elsewhere-flips-a-finding), (b) the one-undeclared-access-posture-finding-per-plan cap, (c) the ungrounded-pressed-at-minor demotion wording ("demoted, never suppressed"), (d) the two-HIGH-class severity sentence with both class phrases — covers AC1/AC2.
- Updated pins: test_threshold_recalibration.py (full pinned routing table + exact blocking set) and test_impact_model_versioning.py (approved plan-review blocking set) — all THREE pinned blocking-set assertions gain T5c in the same commit, so no pin is left contradicting the routing change.
- Regression: tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_t5c_leads_with_trust_boundary_scope_gate and ::test_t10_not_reframed_by_trust_boundary_generalisation pass UNMODIFIED (the rewrite preserves the pinned trust-boundary body phrases).
- Guide currency oracle: after the commit, re-running `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` leaves `git diff -- docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` empty.
- Gates: `make lint && make typecheck`, targeted pytest on the four test modules, then the full `pytest tests/unit`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] plan_review_T5c.md carries the criterion-local GROUNDING OVERRIDE (tool-grounded evaluation against the current codebase/configuration; a control defined elsewhere flips a finding) and the two-HIGH-class severity-scoping sentence, with all previously pinned trust-boundary phrases intact (checked: tests/unit/plan_review/test_t5c_grounding.py string assertions + existing test_plan_review.py T5c pins green unmodified).
- [ ] The rubric caps undeclared-access-posture findings at ONE per plan (extra surfaces folded into that finding's evidence) and demotes candidate findings citing neither a read repo artifact nor a quoted plan sentence to minor — demoted, not suppressed (checked: test_t5c_grounding.py string assertions).
- [ ] criteria_routing.json T5c has default_posture "blocking", block_threshold 0.9, and NO blocking_enabled key; a T5c finding at priority 0.92 blocks and at 0.85 stays advisory through pass3_over_findings (checked: extended test_criteria_blocking.py parametrizations).
- [ ] All three pinned blocking-set assertions (test_threshold_recalibration.py EXPECTED_ROUTING + blocking-set test, test_impact_model_versioning.py approved set) include T5c and the full tests/unit suite is green (checked: CI Verified gate).
- [ ] docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md is regenerated and current (checked: re-running the regenerate-criteria-guide command yields an empty git diff for the guide).
baseline.summary: T5c grounded-security rewrite with dedup-at-source and HIGH-class blocking

# J5 — A Dockerized Jira harness as the Data Center verification oracle

## Context / Problem

There is no way to buy a Jira Data Center license to test against: Atlassian ended new DC purchases on 30 March 2026 and no longer issues DC trial licenses. There is also **no official OpenAPI/Swagger spec for Jira DC** — Atlassian publishes only WADL, and the long-standing requests for one (JRASERVER-65954, JRASERVER-68539) remain open — so spec-driven contract testing is unavailable. Cloud's v3 swagger is not a substitute: different auth, ADF vs wiki markup, accountId vs name. Without an oracle, a DC adapter is unverifiable except against fakes that encode our own assumptions.

## Approach

Use the **purpose-built test image the pycontribs/jira project uses for exactly this problem** — a thin wrapper over `addono/jira-software-standalone` that stands up a real Jira 8.17.1 at `http://localhost:2990/jira` with default credentials `admin`/`admin`. It is unaffected by the DC trial shutdown, and it is the substrate the most widely used Python Jira client validates itself against. Jira 8.17.1 is **≥ 8.14**, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so the PAT bearer auth the DC transport uses is exercised for real.

**The image must be BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry, not assumed.** An earlier draft of this plan said to `docker run pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it "a pinned, pullable image". That is false and was verified false before this plan was rewritten:

- `docker pull pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` → `pull access denied ... repository does not exist`.
- The Docker Hub API for `pycontribs/jira-test-image` returns `{"message": "object not found"}`. The
  `pycontribs` Hub namespace contains exactly seven repositories, all OS base images (centos, fedora, ubuntu,
  debian, alpine, opensuse, voidlinux). There is no `jira-test-image`.
- That tag is a **local build name**. `pycontribs/jira` carries `docker/jira-test-image/{Dockerfile,README.md}`,
  and the upstream README's own instruction is
  `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. It is published to no registry.
- Its base, `addono/jira-software-standalone`, **is** pullable, and the exact digest pycontribs pins
  (`sha256:04326628dc4ac36b2bfc1d0f2ebe5ba3807c1ec9cf9b18307d3c2ad7222537e9`) resolves.

Feasibility was proven before this rewrite: the upstream Dockerfile was fetched and built on the target host (879 MB image, container starts and stays up). So the oracle is real; only the acquisition mechanism changes.

**Decision: vendor a ~15-line Dockerfile in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** that `FROM`s the addono base **by digest** and reproduces the two things the upstream wrapper adds, with attribution to pycontribs/jira in a comment. Rationale: building from a third-party repo at test time would make the harness depend on another project's directory layout and default branch staying put; vendoring the few lines is self-documenting and pins our own supply chain. The alternative — a `git clone` of pycontribs/jira in the fixture — is rejected for that reason.

**Three details are load-bearing and must survive into the vendored file as comments**, because each looks like removable noise and each breaks the harness if removed:

1. **`-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` ENTRYPOINT is MANDATORY.** Atlassian shut down the Marketplace
   v1 REST endpoint that AMPS hardcodes for its SDK update check, so without this flag **every cold container
   start** fails with `FileNotFoundException` on `https://marketplace.atlassian.com/rest/1.0/plugins/...`. The
   failure looks like a transient network fault, so a maintainer "tidying" the flag away would produce a
   confusing, seemingly-flaky breakage.
2. **`-dit` (equivalently compose's `tty: true` + `stdin_open: true`) is REQUIRED** — AMPS exits without a
   controlling TTY. A plain compose service block is not sufficient.
3. **Only Jira 8.x is supported.** `JIRA_VERSION` is overridable across 8.x patch versions, but 9+/11+ fail
   Maven resolution because the upstream pom is anchored to the 8.x dependency graph. The README must say so,
   or a future reader will assume the harness can track a client's newer Jira by bumping a variable.

**The image does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it at runtime.** Verified by running it: the container log shows `Configured Artifact: com.atlassian.jira.plugins:jira-plugin-test-resources:8.17.1:zip` followed by ~917 `Downloading from atlassian-public: https://maven.atlassian.com/...` lines before Tomcat and H2 come up. Four consequences the harness must design around:

- **Egress to `maven.atlassian.com` is a hard RUNTIME dependency**, not a one-time image pull. An
  egress-restricted CI runner cannot start this harness at all.
- **`pinning the image digest does NOT pin Jira itself`.** If Atlassian withdraws the 8.17.1 artifacts from
  their public Maven repo, the harness stops working despite our pinned base digest. That, not the image, is
  the real fragility, and the README must say so — it also strengthens the case for the separately-tracked
  real-instance validation (`9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
- First start is dominated by that download, so the readiness budget must cover a large artifact fetch, not
  just JVM boot.
- The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (`~/.m2`) as a volume, or every fresh container
  re-downloads ~900 artifacts.

**No licensing claim is made.** An earlier draft said the image "carries its own license". That is a legal characterization this story has not verified, so it is replaced by the observed behaviour: no license key is supplied to build or start the instance, and the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run` provisions a local developer instance. The README states it that way.

**Local runs on Apple Silicon are the constrained path, and were measured.** Three attempts on an arm64 workstation failed: two killed by Cargo's default 600000 ms deploy ceiling, and a third — with `-Dproduct.start.timeout` correctly lifting that ceiling — still never reached Jira startup in 55 minutes. Two compounding causes, both recorded so a future reader does not repeat the runs: (a) the amd64 base under arm64 **emulation**, and (b) **resource starvation** — the colima VM was 2 vCPU / 4 GiB with seven other containers already resident, against a Jira that wants ~2 GB of heap by itself. A local run therefore needs BOTH a larger, Rosetta-backed VM (e.g. `colima start --cpu 6 --memory 12 --vm-type vz --vz-rosetta`) AND spare capacity; since that restarts the VM and evicts every running container, it is an operator decision, not something the harness can assume. Prefer the CI job.

**Platform is a real variable, not a footnote.** The base image is `linux/amd64`. On an `arm64` host (Apple Silicon, ARM CI runners) it runs under emulation, and the upstream README's "first responsive request within ~3-5 minutes" does not hold — observed startup on an emulated arm64 host is materially slower. So the compose file sets `platform: linux/amd64` **explicitly** (making behaviour deterministic instead of dependent on the host's default resolution), and the readiness probe's timeout is generous and overridable by env var rather than a hardcoded few minutes. The README records that a native-amd64 runner is strongly preferred.

**Stated limitation, deliberately accepted:** 8.17.1 is older than the version a client such as CMS is likely running, so this harness proves REST v2 protocol semantics, not deployment-specific behavior (workflow names, custom fields, permission schemes, user directories). Closing that gap requires access to the real instance and is tracked separately as ticket `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`; this story's README records the exact image tag so that comparison has a baseline.

Add the harness under **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/`** with a compose file, a readiness probe that polls until the instance answers REST, and a fixture that provisions a scratch project and tears down everything it created.

**The tier is `external`, NOT `integration` — corrected against the CI workflow.** An earlier draft marked these `integration`, reasoning that `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (**`Makefile:178`** — verified; an earlier draft cited 154, which is inside the `actionlint-bin` recipe) and so would exclude them. That reasoning is wrong, and dangerously so: `_build-and-test.yml` runs **`pytest -m integration` as its own dedicated CI step on every commit** ("Run the integration tier (concurrency + reconciler; network-guarded)"), explicitly because those tests "need no live services (mocked acli / local git)". So the `integration` marker is an **INCLUSION into CI**, not an exclusion — Docker-requiring tests marked that way would be collected and run on every commit against a runner with no container, no Jira and no egress, breaking CI for everyone.

The `external` tier is the one genuinely fenced off, and it is enforced structurally rather than by convention: `tests/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` (a) **auto-applies** the `external` marker to every item under `tests/external/`, so no per-file marker is needed, and (b) **hard-fails collection** if any item carries `external` while living outside `tests/external/` — so a live test cannot hide elsewhere in the tree. `external` runs only from `external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron), never on a commit. Living under `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` therefore satisfies the gating requirement AND supplies the structural backstop for free.

**Living under `tests/external/` means INHERITING that tier's contract — three mechanisms, all enumerated here because each silently changes how this suite behaves:**

1. **`_require_external_opt_in` (autouse, `tests/external/conftest.py`) SKIPS every test under
   `tests/external/` unless `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`.** It is a deliberate leak-guard (bug
   `4a48-6dd5-aef3-4c8e`): external tests must stay inert on a default invocation even when credentials happen
   to be present. Consequence for this story: `make jira-dc-up && pytest tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **skips
   everything** without the env var. The README must lead with the full invocation, and the readiness probe's
   error message is only reachable in an opted-in run.
2. **The `_live_jira_ready` sentinel drives the `jira_live` auto-marker and the all-skip canary.**
   `tests/external/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` applies `jira_live` to any module defining a
   module-level `_live_jira_ready`, and `pytest_sessionfinish` **fails the session** when at least one
   `jira_live` test was collected but none executed — the guard against a scheduled run that validated nothing.
   Every existing live-Jira module defines it (`test_reconcile_live.py`, `test_link_sync_live.py`,
   `test_link_sync_roundtrip_live.py`, `test_verified_fake_contract_live.py`). **`test_harness_smoke.py` MUST
   define `_live_jira_ready` too**, or it opts out of the canary and a silently-all-skipped harness run would
   look green.
3. **`_allow_live_model_requests`** re-enables pydantic-ai's global kill-switch for this tier. Irrelevant to
   this harness (it makes no model calls) but noted so the inherited fixture set is fully accounted for.

**Skip-vs-fail is settled here, because the tier forces it.** An earlier draft's "failure path" said the suite should FAIL with a "harness not running" message when the instance is down. That is wrong for this tier and would break the existing `external-integration.yml` job, which already runs `pytest -m external tests/external` with no Docker anywhere. The correct contract: **absent harness ⇒ SKIP with a clear, actionable message** (naming `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1`), and the **canary** — not a hard failure — is what prevents a vacuous green, because a run that collected `jira_live` tests and executed none fails the session. That gives both properties: no CI breakage when Docker is absent, and no silent nothing-ran success.

Teardown follows **`docs/adr/0037-reconciler-live-validation-harness.md` §3** (named in full because FIVE ADRs share the `0037-` prefix — code-review-novelty-convergence, cross-ticket-overlap, oss-contribution-intake-posture, reconciler-live-validation-harness, transport-retry — so a bare "ADR 0037" is unresolvable), which **prohibits post-deletion search-index assertions** because Jira's index lags creates and deletes by an unbounded interval and can return stale results either way. So the teardown oracle is not "query the project and find it empty": it asserts each delete call's HTTP status and then polls each issue's **direct REST endpoint** (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}`) until it returns 404, which is index-independent.

**Alternative rejected: fixtures and a stateful fake alone.** rebar's test-design standard allows a verified fake for external-service mapping, but a fake verified only against fixtures we recorded cannot falsify assumptions we never thought to record — transitions, permission errors, link direction. The fake is still built (J6 uses it for fast unit tests); this story gives it something real to be verified against.

**Alternative rejected: reusing pycontribs/jira's test assertions as the oracle.** Their tests assert their client's behavior, not rebar's field mapping. The reusable asset is the image and harness pattern, which is what this story takes.

**Alternative rejected: the Atlassian SDK's `atlas-run-standalone`.** It also yields a licensed local Jira, but it needs the full SDK toolchain and its licenses are short-lived (3-day timebombs requiring `atlas-mvn clean` recycling), which is hostile to repeatable CI. A pinned Docker image has neither problem.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile` (new) — the vendored wrapper: `FROM` the addono base **by digest**, the
  `-DskipAllPrompts=true` entrypoint, and the three rationale comments above plus attribution to
  pycontribs/jira.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/docker-compose.yml`, `conftest.py`, `README.md` (new) — compose `build`s the local
  Dockerfile (it does NOT reference an unpullable image), sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true`,
  `stdin_open: true`, mounts a persistent Maven cache volume, and publishes
  **`127.0.0.1:2990:2990`** — loopback-scoped, NOT the bare `2990:2990` an earlier draft said, which Docker
  binds on `0.0.0.0` and would expose a well-known-`admin`/`admin` Jira to the whole network.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_harness_smoke.py` (new).
- **`.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` — a NEW, SEPARATE job, modelled on the `langfuse-trace` job
  that already exists in this same file.** This is the key practical finding: the workflow ALREADY implements
  this exact shape at lines ~159-251 for an ephemeral self-hosted Langfuse — `docker compose ... up -d`, poll
  until healthy with an `::error::` + `logs --tail` on timeout, run the tests, dump logs `if: failure()`, and
  `docker compose ... down -v` under `if: always()`. So the Jira job is a direct adaptation of a working
  in-repo precedent rather than novel CI engineering; copy its structure and swap the compose file, the health
  URL (`/jira/rest/api/2/serverInfo`) and the test path.

  **`ubuntu-latest` resolves the platform problem entirely.** GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners are native
  **x86_64**, so the amd64 base image runs WITHOUT emulation — which was the sole reason this harness could not
  be verified on an Apple-Silicon workstation. rebar is a PUBLIC repo, so the standard runner is 4 vCPU /
  16 GB, comfortably above Jira 8.17.1's needs. And because this workflow triggers only on
  `workflow_dispatch` + a weekly cron, a 10-20 minute harness never touches per-commit CI.
  **CI — specifically a new job in this workflow — is therefore the PRIMARY intended home for this harness's
  acceptance evidence**, and a local run is the optional convenience path, not the reverse. This workflow is an unenumerated
  consumer in earlier drafts: at line 141 it already runs `pytest -m external tests/external -q`, so the new
  directory is collected by it the moment the files land, and it has **no** docker build/up/down steps. It also
  gates its existing job on an LLM API key, which this harness does not need. So the harness gets its **own
  job** (not an extension of the LLM-keyed one) that: builds the vendored Dockerfile, brings the instance up,
  waits on the readiness probe, runs ONLY `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down in an `if: always()`
  step. It must run on a **native amd64 runner** (see the platform note above). The pre-existing job is left
  alone, and because the harness tests skip cleanly without `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` plus a reachable instance,
  its collection of them stays harmless.
- `Makefile` — a `jira-dc-up` target only; the `test:` target is NOT modified (the `integration` marker is
  already excluded by its existing `-m` expression at **`Makefile:178`**), and `jira-dc-up` is added to the
  `.PHONY` list at `Makefile:30` — without that, a file or directory named `jira-dc-up` would make the target
  silently no-op.

## Testing

Real-external-service tier by construction — this story *is* the harness. Its own oracle is that the harness starts, is usable, and provably cleans up.

- happy path: the harness starts, the readiness probe reports REST answering, and a smoke test creates and
  reads back one issue through raw REST v2.
- auth path: a Personal Access Token minted on the 8.17.1 instance authenticates a request via
  `Authorization: Bearer`, proving the DC auth mode the transport will use is exercised, not assumed.
- teardown oracle (index-independent, per ADR 0037 §3): after a deliberately failing test, every issue the
  fixture created returns 404 from its direct `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}` endpoint, and each delete call's HTTP
  status was 2xx. Search is never consulted.
- gating oracle: `pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external"` collects zero tests from
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — and, separately, the `external` marker is auto-applied by
  `tests/external/conftest.py` rather than written per-file, with misplacement hard-failing collection.
- canary participation: `test_harness_smoke.py` defines `_live_jira_ready`, so its tests carry `jira_live` and
  an opted-in run in which every one of them skipped **fails the session** instead of reporting a vacuous pass.
- failure path (absent harness): with the instance down, the suite **SKIPS** with a message naming
  `make jira-dc-up` and `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` — not a raw connection traceback, and not a hard failure, which
  would break the pre-existing `external` CI job that has no Docker.

**The `allow_insecure` obligation is NOT this story's — it belongs to J6/J7.** A draft of this plan added an AC requiring every live test here to set `allow_insecure = true` and assert the cleartext warning. That was wrong on two counts, recorded so nobody restores it: (a) the `allow_insecure` config key and its warning-emitting validator DO NOT EXIST yet — they are **J6's** deliverable ([rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56], which already carries exactly that AC), so J5 could not satisfy it while J6 is open, contradicting this story's whole point of being independently claimable; and (b) it does not even apply here — J5's smoke tests speak **raw REST v2** to the instance and never construct rebar's DC backend or read rebar's config, so no validator is on their path. The epic's step-7 obligation attaches to the stories whose live tests drive rebar's DC transport against this harness (J6/J7), which is where it is already recorded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the harness **builds from the vendored `tests/external/live_jira_dc/Dockerfile`** and starts (via the compose
      file or the `jira-dc-up` target), and the readiness probe reports REST v2 answering at
      `http://localhost:2990/jira`. The criterion is explicitly BUILD-and-start, not pull-and-start: no
      acceptance step may depend on `pycontribs/jira-test-image` being pullable, because it is not published
- [ ] the vendored `Dockerfile` pins the addono base **by digest** (not by tag), keeps
      `-DskipAllPrompts=true` on the `atlas-run` entrypoint, and carries a comment explaining that removing
      that flag breaks every cold start via the retired Marketplace v1 endpoint
- [ ] the compose service sets `platform: linux/amd64`, `tty: true` and `stdin_open: true`, and the readiness
      timeout is env-overridable — so an emulated arm64 host is slow rather than spuriously failing
- [ ] a smoke test creates and reads back an issue via REST v2, and a PAT-authenticated request succeeds
- [ ] `test_harness_smoke.py` defines a module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel, so its tests receive the
      `jira_live` marker from `tests/external/conftest.py` and participate in the all-skip canary — an opted-in
      run where every harness test skipped must FAIL the session rather than report a vacuous pass
- [ ] with no instance running, the suite SKIPS with a message naming BOTH `make jira-dc-up` and
      `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` (the tier's autouse opt-in guard), and does NOT fail — verified by running the
      directory with the harness down, which must not break the pre-existing `external` CI job
- [ ] `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gains a SEPARATE amd64 job that builds the Dockerfile,
      waits on the readiness probe, runs only `tests/external/live_jira_dc/`, and tears down under
      `if: always()`. The pre-existing LLM-keyed job keeps its steps, secrets and gating untouched with
      exactly ONE deliberate exception: `--ignore=tests/external/live_jira_dc` is added to its pytest
      invocation. That exception is required and was decided during execution (recorded in this ticket's
      comments): `tests/external/conftest.py`'s all-skip canary counts `jira_live` items GLOBALLY, and that
      job runs `pytest -m external tests/external` over the whole tree with live Cloud creds. Without the
      flag the DC tests are collected there, skip for want of a harness, and their all-skip is MASKED by the … [truncated by reconciler]

content.text: ## Finding (DE5 / F14 — verified; dormant machinery)

`verify_attested_commit` shells out to `git verify-commit`/`git log` inheriting the caller CWD, so verification fails-closed when run from a sibling worktree rather than the attestation repo. Investigation: the function has NO production callers today (only tests) — it is part of an unwired band-attestation gate. So fixing in isolation adds an untestable param, but the maintainer approved a minimal, back-compat-safe fix now.
Citations: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py:91-135` (TODO(bug TBD — F14) at :94).
## Reproduction Steps
1. Attest a commit; run `verify_attested_commit(sha)` from a sibling worktree (different CWD).
2. Expected: verifies against the attestation repo. Actual: git subprocess can't find the sha -> returns False (fail-closed) spuriously.
## Remediation

Add an optional `repo_root: Path | None = None` param; when set, pass `-C <repo_root>` to both git subprocesses. Default preserves today's behavior (no callers to break). Fold into the git-adapter ticket's explicit-repo_root seam if that lands first.
cascade_flag: adds an optional param to `verify_attested_commit` — check the 4 test call sites.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `verify_attested_commit` accepts an explicit repo root and passes `-C` to git
- [ ] Default (no arg) behavior unchanged
- [ ] A test exercises the sibling-worktree/CWD case

baseline.description:
# S4 — RFC 7662 token-introspection verifier

## Why
Introspection completes the "validate against an external Authorization Server" story for providers
that issue **opaque** access tokens (or where instant revocation matters) — Keycloak, Okta, Auth0,
WorkOS all expose a standard `/introspect` endpoint. It is the pattern the SDK's own `simple-auth`
example demonstrates.

## What
Add an **`IntrospectionTokenVerifier`** to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, activated by including
`introspection` in the `mcp.auth_strategies` list (the strategy-selection config key **introduced by
S2**, this story's dependency — not a pre-existing seam), with flat config keys THIS story registers: `auth_introspection_endpoint`,
`auth_introspection_client_id`, `auth_introspection_client_secret_env` (NAME of an env var holding
the client secret — no plaintext secret in config), `auth_introspection_allow_private_host` (bool, default `false`), and
`auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud` (bool, default `false`). It does not take a per-verifier
audience — it validates against the single `auth_resource_server_url` (S2). It POSTs the token
(RFC 7662) with client authentication, accepts only `active: true`, and maps the response into an
`AccessToken` (all RFC 7662 response fields are OPTIONAL, so each has a defined fallback): `scope`
(a space-delimited string per §2.2) is split into the scopes list (absent → empty list),
`exp`→`expires_at` (absent → `None`, per Expiry below), `sub`→`subject` (absent → `None`), and
`client_id`→`client_id` (absent → falls back to `sub`, else `"unknown"`); and stamps `resource=auth_resource_server_url` so the composite
check passes. NOTE: the SDK's `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` is an **example, not an exported/hardened
class** — this story WRITES its own (adapting the example), it does not import it. Adds the `auth_introspection_*` fields to the `McpConfig` dataclass + the `_SECTIONS['mcp']` coercer
in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`; these auto-derive the `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_*` **env-var
names**, which are added to `MCP_ENV_VARS` (in `src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) and `server.json`;
`scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes. (The generated `mcp-reference.md`/`env-vars.md` are
regenerated for the full key set by S7; S1 fixes the generators to iterate `MCP_ENV_VARS`.)

## Approach & rationale
Adapt the SDK `simple-auth` example (the blessed reference) and add the production hardening its
docstring says it lacks: client authentication on the introspection call, strict audience handling, and fail-closed transport errors. Reuse the
already-present `httpx`.

## Scope
The introspection verifier only, on the S2 seam. Subset of the epic. Depends on S2. Independent of
S3/S5/S6.

## Security
Boundary-crossing. Requirements:
- Call the introspection endpoint over authenticated TLS (`client_secret_basic`, secret from
  `auth_introspection_client_secret_env`, which MUST be present and non-empty at startup or the
  verifier refuses to start — fail-closed), **HTTPS-only** (an `http://` endpoint is rejected at
  construction), a **bounded HTTP timeout (default connect 5s / read 10s)**. Private/link-local
endpoint hosts (RFC 1918, loopback,
  `169.254.0.0/16`) are **rejected by default**; an operator with a legitimate internal AS sets
  `auth_introspection_allow_private_host=true` to opt out.
- Accept only `active:true`. **Audience:** RFC 7662 §2.2 permits `aud` to be a JSON string OR an
  array of strings — the check passes if `auth_resource_server_url` equals the string form or is a
  member of the array form. If the AS omits `aud` (many do), the default is to **reject**
  (fail-closed); an operator whose AS scopes tokens to this resource by other means sets
  `auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud=true` to accept aud-absent tokens (documented risk in S7).
- **Fail-closed transport:** a non-200 status, a timeout, or a **malformed response** — a 200 whose
  body is not valid JSON, or valid JSON lacking a boolean `active` field — **raises** (composite
  treats as non-acceptance → deny); it never yields acceptance.
- **No caching in v1:** every request re-introspects the token with the AS, giving instant
  revocation. A positive-response cache (hashed key, bounded TTL) is a documented follow-on
  optimization, deliberately out of scope here to avoid the revocation-delay tradeoff.
- **Expiry:** when the response includes `exp`, set `AccessToken.expires_at` from it (a real
  positive value). When `active:true` but `exp` is absent (RFC 7662 permits it), set
  `expires_at=None` — validity is then bounded by re-introspection (every request re-checks the AS in v1). Never emit
  `expires_at=0` (the SDK reads a falsy value as no-expiry while looking like a set value).
- Tokens/secrets never logged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `auth_introspection_*` config fields exist in `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']`
      (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`); their derived `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_INTROSPECTION_*` env-var names are
      present in `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) and `server.json`; and
      `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (observable oracle: the manifest drift test is green
      and both files contain the new env-var names).
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit against the real verifier; the irreducible boundary — the introspection
      HTTP call — is a stateful fake fed production-shaped RFC 7662 responses) asserts an `active:true`
      response with a matching `aud` and an `exp` → an `AccessToken` with expected scopes,
      `resource==auth_resource_server_url`, and a positive `expires_at`; and that an `active:true`
      response OMITTING `exp` yields `expires_at=None` (never 0), with validity bounded by
      re-introspection (observable oracle: `expires_at is None`).
- [ ] Unit tests assert rejection for: `active:false` (returns None); a response OMITTING `aud` when
      `auth_introspection_allow_missing_aud=false` (fail-closed reject) — and acceptance of the same
      response when the key is `true`; a mismatched `aud`; and an `aud` supplied as an ARRAY that
      does/does not contain `auth_resource_server_url` (accept/reject respectively) — each a distinct
      negative control. Also assert `scope` given as a space-delimited string is split into the
      expected scopes list.
- [ ] Unit test asserts a non-200 status, a timeout, and a malformed response (200 body that is not
      valid JSON; and valid JSON lacking a boolean `active` field) each **raise** (→ composite
      non-acceptance/deny) and never yield acceptance, and that every request re-introspects with no
      caching in v1 (observable oracle: the stateful fake's request count increments once per request
      — two identical requests hit the fake twice).
- [ ] Unit test asserts construction-time guards: the introspection request carries
      `client_secret_basic` (secret sourced from `auth_introspection_client_secret_env`); an `http://`
      endpoint is rejected; and a private/link-local host is rejected by default and accepted only
      with `auth_introspection_allow_private_host=true` (observable oracle: the fake receives Basic
      auth; rejection at construction for the http/private cases). Also assert the verifier refuses
      to start when the env var named by `auth_introspection_client_secret_env` is absent or empty
      (observable oracle: startup raises a clear message).
- [ ] Component test (tier: component — the `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` inside a
      `CompositeTokenVerifier`, invoked through the composite's verify path, with the external
      `/introspect` endpoint as the SAME stateful fake) asserts an active, matching-audience token
      → an accepted `AccessToken`, and an `active:false`/absent token → None (→ composite deny).
      End-to-end HTTP behavior (401/200 through the ASGI transport) is exercised once for all
      verifiers by S2's transport harness, not re-tested here.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive verifier, opt-in via the `introspection` strategy. No change to other verifiers or stdio.
baseline.summary: S4 — RFC 7662 token-introspection verifier
