## Context / Current Gap

Stories 1934, 749c, 1fd4, and 0b14 landed authenticated `undeclared`, `paths`, and `none` behavior. The current packaged author guide mentions only the paths form at `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:96-100`; `docs/event-schema.md:52` still describes FILE_IMPACT only as a path/reason array. The standalone gate and ticket-model docs likewise lack one complete author-facing tri-state contract. This ticket creates that missing documentation. Because it edits repository files, its own scope is `paths`, never `none`.

## Approach

Document one already-landed contract at four reader-facing locations and behavior-test the only location exposed through a runtime public entry point: `rebar explain plan`. Verify the three standalone docs with a durable, auditable semantic checklist rather than source-grep or snapshot tests. The runtime test intentionally cannot prove, or make pass, any standalone-doc criterion; completion requires both the green public behavior test and the separate evidence-bearing checklist. Rejected alternative: tests that open documentation source files and search for mandated wording, because those are change detectors coupled to text placement rather than public behavior.

## Authoritative Landed Semantics

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:527-543` is the implementation evidence. Every later FILE_IMPACT event replaces all three derived fields:

- `paths`: a non-empty `file_impact` list, `file_impact_scope="paths"`, and `no_file_impact_reason=""`.
- `none`: `file_impact=[]`, `file_impact_scope="none"`, and the supplied substantive `no_file_impact_reason`.
- `undeclared`: `file_impact=[]`, `file_impact_scope="undeclared"`, and `no_file_impact_reason=""`.

Thus transition to paths clears any none reason; transition to none clears prior paths; transition to undeclared clears both paths and reason.

## Authoritative Review Criterion

The advisory `no-file-impact` plan-review criterion is registered at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:171-173`, specified at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:286-309`, and prompted by `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no-file-impact.md`. It applies only when `file_impact_scope == "none"`, has advisory default posture and a 0.95 block threshold, and asks three sub-answers: whether the declaration is plausible for the deliverable, whether the reason concretely explains why no repository artifact is needed, and whether the plan itself names a repository edit. The author guide will describe this as advisory LLM review, not as a guaranteed claim blocker. The story additionally requires a useful reason to say where non-repository output or evidence lives.

## Execution Steps

1. Update `docs/plan-review-gate.md` with an explicit tri-state section: state freshness, live-child neutral/poison roll-up, closed-child exclusion, material-fingerprint effects, and a mixed paths-plus-none example.
2. Update `docs/ticket-model.md` beside file impact with the three persisted states and the rule that docs-only/test-only repository changes declare paths.
3. Update `docs/event-schema.md` FILE_IMPACT wording with the three event fields and the exact replacement/clearing semantics above.
4. Update `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`, packaged source for public `rebar explain plan`. Give a separable author contract: the three choices; `rebar set-file-impact <id> --none "<reason>"`; no repository file changes; docs-only/test-only use paths; the advisory LLM criterion; and a reason explaining both `Why no repository files change` and `Where output or evidence lives`. Include one valid worked reason.
5. RED-first, add `test_explain_plan_file_impact_tristate_contract` in `tests/unit/test_plan_review_explain.py`. Invoke public `main(["explain", "plan"])`, assert exit code 0, and capture stdout. Case-normalized presence assertions check these stable public markers without order or layout dependence: `undeclared`, `paths`, `none`, `set-file-impact`, `--none`, `no repository file`, `docs-only`, `test-only`, `advisory`, `no-file-impact`, `why no repository files change`, and `where output or evidence lives`. Also assert the pre-existing `rebar review-plan` marker remains as a negative control against replacing the guide wholesale. This test must not open or grep source files, inspect private implementation shape, snapshot exact prose, or assert formatting/order.
6. Before the guide edit, run the new test and confirm it fails because the current public command omits the none command and author guidance, proving the discoverability gap through the real entry point. After the guide edit, rerun green. For the teeth check, temporarily remove the newly documented public tri-state block, confirm the same public test fails, restore it, and confirm green. Moving or reheading unchanged guidance must leave the test green.
7. Manually verify standalone criteria GATE-1 through EVENT-2 below. Record one Markdown table as a ticket comment with columns `criterion`, `PASS/FAIL`, `path:line`, and `semantic evidence`, plus reviewer identity, UTC timestamp, and tested git commit SHA. Each row quotes or faithfully paraphrases the passage. Use this template: `| GATE-1 | PASS | docs/plan-review-gate.md:line | undeclared binds whole HEAD |`. Audit with `rebar show cf33-642c-4984-4a87 --output llm` and `git show <recorded-sha>:<recorded-path>`. Any missing or FAIL row blocks completion.
8. Add a CONSISTENCY row to the same comment with path:line evidence from all four sources. Mark PASS only when the meanings of undeclared, paths, and none agree. This reconciliation is separate from the CLI test.
9. Run `make lint`, the project typecheck gate, and the full test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Standalone documentation

- [ ] GATE-1: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` defines undeclared as whole-HEAD freshness; verified by its PASS checklist row with path:line semantic evidence.
- [ ] GATE-2: the gate doc defines paths as dependency-scoped freshness; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-3: the gate doc defines authenticated none as contributing no file dependencies; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-4: the gate doc states a live none child is neutral in container roll-up; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-5: the gate doc states a live undeclared child poisons inheritance; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-6: the gate doc states a closed child is excluded from roll-up; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-7: the gate doc states changing a declaration changes the material fingerprint; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] GATE-8: the gate doc gives a mixed example where a paths child contributes dependencies and a none child does not; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] MODEL-1: `docs/ticket-model.md` documents all three persisted states beside file impact; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] MODEL-2: the ticket-model doc states docs-only work uses paths; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] MODEL-3: the ticket-model doc states test-only work uses paths; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] EVENT-1: `docs/event-schema.md` documents `file_impact`, `file_impact_scope`, and `no_file_impact_reason`; verified by its PASS checklist row.
- [ ] EVENT-2: the event-schema doc documents replacement and clearing semantics for every target state; verified by its PASS checklist row.

### Public CLI behavior

- [ ] CLI-1: public `rebar explain plan` succeeds and communicates undeclared, paths, and none; verified by `test_explain_plan_file_impact_tristate_contract`.
- [ ] CLI-2: public output communicates the none command; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-3: public output communicates that none means no repository file is touched; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-4: public output communicates that docs-only work uses paths; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-5: public output communicates that test-only work uses paths; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-6: public output identifies the no-file-impact check as advisory LLM review; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-7: public output separately communicates why no repository files change; verified by the public CLI test.
- [ ] CLI-8: public output separately communicates where output or evidence lives; verified by the public CLI test.

### Completion evidence

- [ ] EVIDENCE-1: the ticket comment contains PASS rows for every GATE, MODEL, EVENT, and CONSISTENCY item with path:line evidence, reviewer, UTC timestamp, and commit SHA; audited with the commands in step 7.
- [ ] EVIDENCE-2: RED, GREEN, defect-seeded mutation RED, and restored GREEN results for the public CLI behavior test are recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] QUALITY-1: no automated test reads or greps documentation source, asserts private shape, snapshots exact prose, or depends on formatting/order; verified by code review of the test diff.
- [ ] SCOPE-1: no production logic or schema file changes; under `src/rebar`, only `_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` changes; verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`.
- [ ] GATE-LINT: `make lint` passes.
- [ ] GATE-TYPE: the project typecheck gate passes.
- [ ] GATE-TEST: the full test suite passes.

# Consolidate/harden the duplicated `git rev-list --count` test helpers (flake class)

## Context (discovered by rebar-debug on efb7-09de)
efb7 fixed ONE copy of a fragile helper (test_import_batch_resume.py::_commit_count) that
crashed with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''` when
`git rev-list --count HEAD` transiently returned empty stdout. A Step-7 sibling sweep found the
SAME unchecked-subprocess + `int(stdout.strip())` pattern duplicated across other test helpers.

## Confirmed live siblings (same opaque int('') crash on a transient empty rev-list)
- tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batching.py:38-42
- tests/interfaces/io/test_import_idempotency.py:21-25
- tests/interfaces/store/test_ensure_drift_matrix.py:56-61  (counts the `tickets` ref)

## Lesser variants (flake risk but NOT the opaque crash — lower priority)
- tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py:28-30,60  — `_git` uses check=True, so a transient fails
  LOUDLY (CalledProcessError), not masked as int('') — but still not retry-resilient.
- tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py:60 — `int(out.stdout.strip() or "0")` already
  guards empty, but silently returns 0 (masks a transient as a wrong count).

## Already safe (no change needed) — recorded for completeness
- src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:539 — product code already guards:
  `int((cp.stdout or "0").strip() or "0")` inside try/except ValueError.

## Suggested approach
Extract ONE shared robust helper (check rc + non-empty stdout, bounded retry on transient, clear
error carrying git's stderr on persistent) into a test util and switch the duplicated helpers to
it — rather than copy-pasting retry logic. Mirror efb7's fix + regression test.

## Acceptance criteria
- The 3 confirmed siblings no longer raise int('') on an empty/failed rev-list (retry a transient,
  clear diagnostic on persistent), proven RED->GREEN per site or via the shared helper's test.

content.text: ## Why
Pass-4 coaching splits cleanly: the MECHANISM (map surviving advisories → a move from a locked
registry → deterministic template render; the LLM only picks `move_id` + a bounded noun-phrase
`subject`; no free prose; skip the LLM call when surviving==0) is generic; the move CATALOG
(plan-review's planning moves — spike, pre-mortem, ADR, thin-vertical-slice…) is domain-specific
(code review needs code moves). So the kernel should own the mechanism + a pluggable registry
SCHEMA, and each gate supplies its own catalog. This is also the right place to close the gap a
prior self-review flagged on the old epic: the registry is `{id, name, template}` with NO
applicability field, so move selection is wholly LLM-delegated — add a `triggers`/applies_when
field + a deterministic applicability filter.
## What
- Move the Pass-4 coach mechanism into the kernel: `coach(surviving, registry) -> notes` — the
applicability filter → LLM picks among applicable moves (move_id + bounded subject) →
deterministic render from the move template → the subject validator → the gate-on-surviving>0
behavior.
- Define a registered move-registry SCHEMA `{id, name, template, triggers/applies_when}`; validate
registries at load. Selection = deterministic filter on `triggers` THEN LLM choice among the
applicable (not free LLM choice over the whole catalog).
- Make plan-review's existing move catalog a registry INSTANCE the kernel consumes; rewire the
plan-review coach to call the kernel. No behavior change for the existing moves (their
`applies_when` defaults to always-applicable unless they already had a stated trigger).
## Scope
In scope: the coach mechanism + subject validator + render + surviving>0 gate, moved to the
kernel; the move-registry schema with the applicability field; plan-review's catalog becomes an
instance. Out of scope: authoring a code-review move catalog (that is `b744`), Pass-2/3 (WS1/WS2),
the seam doc + evals (WS4). Touches `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` (coach +
MOVE_REGISTRY + `_validate_subject`), `workflow_ops.py` (coach ops), the kernel module, and the
move-registry schema.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The kernel exposes a Pass-4 `coach(surviving, registry)` that selects moves, renders
deterministically from the template, validates the subject, and makes no LLM call when there
are 0 surviving advisories.
- [ ] A registered move-registry schema includes a `triggers`/applies_when field; move selection
applies a deterministic applicability filter before the LLM picks among applicable moves; a
test covers an applicability-filtered selection.
- [ ] Plan-review's move catalog is a registry instance consumed by the kernel; an offline test
asserts the rendered coaching is unchanged for the existing (always-applicable) moves.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS3: Extract Pass-4 coach mechanism + pluggable move-registry (triggers/applicability)

## Context

Placeholder epic from the 2026-07-08 audit follow-up (OSS finding #1: no automated dependency updates; see epic heedless-caloric-pikeperch for the rest of the audit remediation). Stock Dependabot cannot merge here — GitHub is a read-only mirror and code lands only through Gerrit. Research into Gerrit-gated OSS projects (Chromium AutoRoll, Wikimedia LibUp, OpenStack proposal bot, wmde's Dependabot->Gerrit bridge) converged on self-hosted **Renovate with `platform: gerrit`** (native since 37.112.0, still experimental) as the purpose-built option: it pushes each update to refs/for/main, manages Change-Ids via Renovate-Branch commit footers (re-pushes become patchsets, not duplicates), and needs only Contributor push rights — the existing LLM-Review + Verified gates apply unchanged, no autoApprove.

## What (rough shape — to be designed before promotion)

- **Hosting:** run Renovate CLI on a schedule (systemd timer or cron) on the **same AWS server that hosts Gerrit and the Rebar MCP server** — it already holds Gerrit credentials, network adjacency, and a rebar install with the environment signing key.
- **Identity:** a dedicated Gerrit bot account (or RebarBotNava) with HTTP token auth (RENOVATE_PASSWORD), Contributors group, push-for-review only — no self-approve, no vote rights; every bump passes both gates like any change.
- **Commit-ticket trailer integration (the rebar-specific piece):** CI's Verified gate rejects commits whose message doesn't reference a resolving rebar ticket, and Renovate owns the commit-footer area (custom trailers via commitBody don't work on the Gerrit platform). Decision per audit follow-up: a wrapper step around each Renovate run (or a per-update hook) uses the **rebar install on the same server** to `rebar create` a tracking ticket for the dependency change and **immediately force-close it** (`--force-close` — the goal is tracking/provenance, not gate validation; force-closed = deliberately unsigned), then injects that ticket id into the commit via the accepted `<id>:` subject-prefix form (e.g. commitMessagePrefix), since the trailer footer is unavailable. The ticket description records package, from->to versions, and the Renovate change URL.
- **Complementary signal:** keep GitHub Dependabot **security alerts** enabled on the mirror as an independent CVE feed (alerts only, no PRs).
- **Fallback:** if the experimental Gerrit platform proves too rough, replace with a small scheduled bump-and-push job (uv lock --upgrade + push to refs/for/main) reusing the same ticket-creation wrapper.

## Open design questions (resolve before promoting idea -> open)

- One standing ticket per run vs one ticket per dependency change (leaning per-change for provenance granularity)
- Whether the subject-prefix `<id>:` form satisfies verify.require_ticket_for_commit as-is for Renovate-authored subjects, or the config needs a bot exemption
- Renovate config scope: pip (pyproject core + extras), github-actions manager for the workflow pins (pairs with the audit's SHA-pinning recommendation), grouping/schedule/noise budget
- Secret handling for the bot HTTP token on the server (align with the SSM/ephemeral-secrets pattern, ADR-0008)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Renovate runs on a schedule on the Gerrit/MCP AWS server with platform: gerrit against this repo
- [ ] Each dependency update lands as a normal Gerrit change that passes LLM-Review + Verified with no human-side ceremony beyond review
- [ ] Every Renovate change carries a resolving rebar ticket id (created + force-closed automatically on the server) satisfying the commit-ticket gate
- [ ] Dependabot security alerts remain enabled on the mirror as an independent signal
- [ ] Runbook documented (docs/) covering the bot account, token rotation, pausing the roller, and the fallback path
baseline.summary: Stand up self-hosted Renovate (platform: gerrit) on the Gerrit/MCP AWS server, with rebar-ticket trailer integration

content.text: ## Why
The module-size policy (`docs/architecture.md:145-186`) exists so the over-cap set
is "tracked … visible, not silently growing." That intent is currently violated:
**8** files are over the 800-LOC soft cap but the documented offenders table lists
only **4**, and the one accurate check (the CI size report) is a warn-only `echo`
that never fails and runs only on Linux. So the inventory nobody is forced to read
is the only correct one, and the human-facing table has drifted.
## What
(1) Refresh the offenders table in `docs/architecture.md` to match reality
(8 files, correct LOC, correct remedies), and (2) give the CI size report teeth so
*new* over-cap files (or significant growth of existing ones) fail the build,
while grandfathering the existing set.
## Scope
- In scope: `docs/architecture.md` (the offenders table + the 500–800 watch-band
prose), `.github/workflows/test.yml` (the module-size report step).
- Out of scope: actually splitting any over-cap file (that is separate,
per-file work — the soft cap is deliberately soft; do not split preemptively).
## Context (citations)
- **Actual over-cap set (verified `wc -l`, 2026-06-18):** `reconcile.py` 1308,
`outbound_differ.py` 1277, `_cli/__init__.py` **1100 (undocumented)**,
`__init__.py` 1036, `reads.py` 930, `config.py` **909 (undocumented)**,
`mcp_server.py` 848, `applier.py` 801.
- **The stale table:** `docs/architecture.md:166-171` documents only 4
(`reconcile.py`, `outbound_differ.py`, `__init__.py`, `reads.py`).
`outbound_differ.py` is listed at `~1114` (actual 1277, +163 drift);
`__init__.py` at `~1019` (actual 1036).
- **Active mislisting:** `docs/architecture.md:180-186` places `mcp_server.py`
(848) and `applier.py` (801) in the "500–800 band … at the ceiling, not over
it" — both are *over* the cap.
- **The toothless CI step:** `.github/workflows/test.yml:109-120` (step name at
≈112) — an `echo`/`find`/`awk '$1 > 800'` whose terminating
`if [ -n "$over" ]; …; fi` always exits 0, gated `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`. The policy claims this is how
"new offenders surface in PRs" (`architecture.md:164`) — but a buried,
non-failing, Linux-only echo is weak surfacing.
- **Metric:** the report and the table both use raw `wc -l`; keep that metric.
## Implementation plan
1. **Refresh the table** (`architecture.md:166-171`): list all 8 over-cap files
with current LOC and a one-line remedy each (the two undocumented ones:
`_cli/__init__.py` — split the argv-routing/`_dispatch` arms from the lazy
command-delegation seam; `config.py` — split the dataclass/schema from the
env/CLI-override + cache machinery along the existing seam). Move
`mcp_server.py` and `applier.py` out of the watch-band prose (180-185) into the
table.
2. **Add a checked-in baseline allowlist** for the size gate — e.g.
`.github/module-size-allowlist.txt` listing the 8 grandfathered paths (one per
line), with a comment that it must match the architecture.md table.
3. **Make the CI step gate on regressions** (`test.yml`): rewrite the step so it
(a) computes the set of files with `wc -l > 800`, (b) subtracts the allowlist,
and (c) **exits non-zero** if any file is over-cap and not allow-listed (a new
offender). Optionally also fail if an allow-listed file grows by more than a
tolerance (e.g. >10% over its recorded baseline) — start with the simpler
"new-file-only" gate to avoid churn.
4. Remove the `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` restriction (the check is pure
`wc`/shell, portable) OR keep it but document why; preferred: make it run on
the primary lane unconditionally.
5. Add a short contributor note (in `architecture.md` near the table) that the
allowlist and the table must be updated together, and that adding to the
allowlist requires a remedy line in the table.
6. Test: add a throwaway 900-LOC file locally, run the gate logic, confirm it
fails; remove it; confirm green with the real tree.
## Tradeoffs
- **Benefit:** "not silently growing" becomes self-enforcing; the table and the
automated inventory can no longer disagree (CI fails if they do).
- **Cost/risk:** a hard gate on a deliberately *soft* cap could block a
legitimately-cohesive large module. Mitigation: gate only on **new** over-cap
files (allowlist grandfathers the existing 8), so existing work is unaffected and
authors of a genuinely-needed large new unit add one allowlist line + one table
row (a deliberate, reviewed act). The growth-tolerance check is optional — defer
if it proves noisy.
- **Alternative considered:** keep it warn-only and just refresh the table —
rejected; the table already drifted under exactly that regime.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md`'s offenders table lists all 8 current over-cap files
with accurate LOC and a remedy each; `mcp_server.py` and `applier.py` are no
longer in the "under the cap" watch-band prose.
- [ ] A checked-in allowlist enumerates the grandfathered over-cap files.
- [ ] The CI size step exits non-zero when a non-allow-listed file exceeds 800 LOC
(verified with a temporary oversized file), and passes on the current tree.
- [ ] The size check is not silently Linux-only (runs on the primary lane).
- [ ] A contributor note explains that the allowlist and the table change together.
</content>

baseline.summary: Refresh the module-size offenders table + give the CI size report teeth

# Comprehensive live reconciler validation + guaranteed bilateral cleanup

## Why
Prove the reconciler correct end-to-end against live Jira. An agent with ACLI access runs the full bidirectional
matrix and GUARANTEES cleanup in both systems. Validates POST-FIX behavior, so it runs AFTER the C-band lands
(several signals are the TARGET behavior those tickets create). Ordering captured here, not as hard depends_on
edges (avoids blocking-link promotion across mixed-type siblings); harness build may start early.

## Signal definitions (each an observable pass criterion)
- C1 (conflict signal): assert against the exact conflict record C1 (feline-wandering-dassierat) lands — reference
  C1's implemented signal at validation time (C1 is pre-manifest; do NOT hard-code an unverified field).
- C2 (hard-delete -> re-create): after a Jira hard-delete, a NEW issue with the same `rebar-id:<local_id>` label +
  entity property is created and bound; no false comment (lowerclass-creased-fruitbat).
- C3 (field-allowlist-drop alert): the deduped BRIDGE_ALERT C3 (nonglacial-tense-vulture) ADDS fires on a dropped
  outbound field (today only stderr — assert the post-C3 alert).
- C4 (429/backoff): monkey-patch the LIVE retry path C4 (lambswool-shaded-eider) implements — the `_run_acli`
  subprocess retry loop and/or `_call_with_retry` (dispatch_one.py) — NOT the dead `_call_with_backoff`. Because a
  subprocess `Retry-After` may be unavailable (per C4's probe), assert the JITTERED-BACKOFF behavior C4 lands (a
  simulated 429 exit -> backoff -> success), and Retry-After honoring only IF C4 confirmed availability.
- Echo suppression: outbound comments carry `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->`; field/status writes are baseline-seeded
  via the `ProvenanceLedger` (defined in `conflict_resolver.py`) — verify `mutation_count==0` on the next pass over
  just-written data (harness pre-seeds the baseline as a real pass would).
- Status round-trip incl. LOSSY labels: local `blocked` -> Jira nearest live status + `rebar-status:blocked` label
  -> inbound restores `blocked`; `idea<->IDEA` round-trips; assert no oscillation over N=3 passes.
- TOMBSTONE/GRACE: local archive -> Jira Done (not deleted); a Jira 404 on N=`RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE`
  (default 3) consecutive passes -> binding soft-retired to `bindings-retired.json`; a single 404 does NOT retire.
- Blast-radius breaker: with >=11 synthetic bindings, one acting decision (fraction 0.09) does NOT trip; a synthetic
  mass-change trips it. Assert via the breaker API in `classify.py`: `census()['breaker']['allowed'] == False`
  (`BreakerVerdict.allowed`; both live in `classify.py`, NOT binding_walk.py). NOTE `census()` adds the `'breaker'`
  key only when the breaker is evaluated on an acting pass — the mass-change scenario provides that.

## Harness (guaranteed bilateral teardown)
- Build on the existing `e2e_validation_probe.sh` if suitable; else a pytest autouse fixture `yield`+`finally`
  (or bash `trap cleanup EXIT`) that hard-deletes Jira test issues AND discards the local throwaway env — runs even
  on assertion failure/exception, and tracks WHICH of N synthetic artifacts were created (partial-setup) so teardown
  removes exactly those.
- Teardown-failure fallback: each cleanup call retries 3x with exponential backoff; on exhaustion append the id to
  `leaked-artifacts.log` (a CI artifact) and exit non-zero.
- Setup probe: create one throwaway issue and assert `client.delete_issue` returns `{"status":"deleted"}`; NOTE
  `acli.py:721-723` RAISES PermissionError on missing delete perm (fails loud), so a scope misconfig surfaces here.

## Isolation, credentials
- Dedicated Jira TEST project; a service account with "Delete Issues" scoped to that project only; token via a
  secret, never logged/committed. Local side: an ISOLATED throwaway tickets env/branch discarded post-run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Harness with GUARANTEED bilateral teardown (tracks partial-setup); a teardown-under-failure test injects a RuntimeError after create and asserts BOTH artifacts cleaned.
- [ ] One observable pass criterion per matrix scenario (C1-C4, echo, status-round-trip incl. lossy labels, tombstone/grace, idempotency mutation_count==0, blast-radius via `classify.census()['breaker']['allowed']==False`); harness exits 0 all-green and writes a JSON/JUnit report to a named path attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Teardown-failure fallback (3x exp-backoff, `leaked-artifacts.log` CI artifact, non-zero exit); ZERO surviving artifacts on success.
- [ ] Delete-permission probe passes (delete_issue returns deleted; raises loud if unscoped); credential scoped to the test project + injected via secret.
- [ ] Isolation documented; production REB + tickets branch untouched; N (oscillation passes) = 3.
- [ ] Runs after the C-band lands; re-runnable (idempotent teardown); harness pattern recorded in an ADR/design note.


## Round-6 corrections (from plan review)
- BREAKER ASSERTION: `classify.census()` only adds the `'breaker'` key when called WITH both `max_acting_fraction`
  AND `total_bindings` kwargs (classify.py:368) — a bare `census()['breaker']` KeyErrors on a non-acting pass. So
  assert the trip via `check_blast_radius(...)` returning a `BreakerVerdict` with `.allowed == False` (classify.py),
  or call `census(max_acting_fraction=..., total_bindings=...)` explicitly; do NOT index `['breaker']` unguarded.
- TEARDOWN RETRY: reuse an existing backoff helper (e.g. the app-layer retry in `dispatch_one`/`batch_dispatch`)
  rather than a bespoke 3x loop, where practical.
- C4 TARGET: patch the SINGLE live path C4 lands (per lambswool-shaded-eider) — the `_run_acli` subprocess retry
  loop; a subprocess `Retry-After` may be unavailable, so assert the bounded-backoff behavior (simulated 429 exit ->
  backoff -> success), with Retry-After honoring only if C4's probe confirmed it. Do not name two incompatible targets.
- C3 BASELINE: assert the post-C3 deduped BRIDGE_ALERT (C3 adds it); today the allowlist drop is only logged, not alerted.
baseline.summary: Comprehensive live reconciler validation + guaranteed bilateral cleanup

`rebar.cli:main` so it delegates to `rebar._cli.main(sys.argv[1:])` (and `sys.exit`s its return code)
instead of subprocessing the bash dispatcher. The dispatcher still EXISTS — category-B arms inside

content.text: ## Why
`docs/import-export.md` honestly notes that bulk import takes one git commit and
one lock per event, so multi-thousand-ticket imports serialize the write lock and
can take minutes. But there is no consolidated **scale envelope** telling
adopters what the tool can take: how many tickets/events/clones, expected
list/search latency, git object growth, and the maintenance commands that keep a
long-lived store healthy. Popularity changes the load profile (Jira imports,
bulk migrations, many agents, multi-year stores), and adopters need honest
numbers to plan.
## What
Add `docs/scale-envelope.md` documenting, with **representative measured
numbers** produced by a quick local benchmark run during implementation:
- Ticket / event / clone counts the design comfortably supports.
- Import throughput (events/sec) and the per-event commit+lock cost.
- `list` / `search` / replay latency at a few representative store sizes.
- Git object / pack growth expectations on a long-lived `tickets` branch, and
why `gc.auto=0` is set.
- Compaction thresholds and the recommended maintenance commands
(`compact` / `compact-all` / `fsck`).
## Scope
One doc (`docs/scale-envelope.md`) + a short reproducible measurement method.
Docs-only: no batched-commit import and no CI benchmark harness (both OUT per the
epic). Cross-link from README and `docs/import-export.md`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/scale-envelope.md` exists with representative measured numbers for
counts, import throughput, and list/search latency.
- [ ] It documents git-growth expectations and the compaction/maintenance
commands.
- [ ] The measurement method is reproducible (documented commands/store sizes).
- [ ] README and `docs/import-export.md` link to it; no benchmark harness is
wired into CI.

baseline.summary: Publish a scale-envelope doc with representative measured numbers

# Outbound status never transitions on Data Center — `update_issue` has no status routing

## Symptom

Live J11 cell `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` fails against the Dockerized Jira Data Center harness with:

    outbound status did not reach DC: fields.status.name is 'To Do'

The pass exits 0 with no traceback. A local `open -> in_progress` transition is reconciled as "applied" and the DC issue's status never changes.

## This is NOT covered by 7f93

Bug 7f93 taught `JiraDataCenterTransport.transition_issue_by_name` to resolve a destination STATUS name (`"In Progress"`) to the transition that reaches it (`Start Progress`). That fixed the INBOUND cell, whose setup helper `_in_status` calls `transition_issue_by_name` DIRECTLY.

**The outbound apply path never calls `transition_issue_by_name` at all.** 7f93 cannot fix it.

## Root cause, traced end to end

1. `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:81-82` maps local `in_progress` to the Jira
   workflow-state name via `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, emitting `fields["status"] = "In Progress"`.
2. `dispatch_apply_phases.py:41` — `_OUTBOUND_BATCH_ALLOWLIST` CONTAINS `"status"`, so
   `_update_one_filter_fields` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:130-139`) keeps it.
3. `dispatch_one.py:665` (`_update_one_scalar_update`) forwards the whole allowlisted dict as
   `client.update_issue(issue_key, **fields)`.
4. `client` is the configured backend's transport — `applier.py:591` calls `_load_acli()`, which
   is `select_backend(load_config()).transport` (`applier.py:221-231`). On this deployment that
   is `JiraDataCenterTransport`.
5. **On Cloud**, `adapters/jira/acli.py:170` pops `status` out of the kwargs and
   `acli.py:182-183` routes it to `transition_issue` -> `transition_issue_by_name`. The
   status→transition translation lives IN THE ACLI TRANSPORT, not in the shared dispatch path.
6. **On Data Center**, `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:248-255` pops ONLY `assignee` and
   puts everything else into `issue.update(fields=kwargs)` — a REST field EDIT
   (`PUT /rest/api/2/issue/<key>`). `status` is not an editable field in Jira; it is reachable
   only through a transition. Jira rejects it, the error is soft-failed, and the status stays put.

So the DC transport is MISSING the status→transition routing its Cloud sibling has. The translation was implemented once, per-transport, and the second transport did not get it — the same shape as bug 3f04 (outbound links re-added to one path only).

## Reproduction (no live Jira)

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_outbound_status_routing_5200.py`

* `test_the_dc_transport_edits_status_as_a_field_instead_of_transitioning` — GREEN today, pins
  the defect: `update_issue("DIG-1", status="In Progress")` produces
  `edited_fields == [{"status": "In Progress"}]`, `transitions_probed == []`,
  `transitioned == []`. No transitions probe happens at all.
* `test_an_outbound_status_should_dispatch_the_transition_that_reaches_it` — `xfail(strict=True)`,
  asserts the required behaviour (`transitioned == [("DIG-1", "11")]`, i.e. `Start Progress`).
  Verified with `--runxfail` that it fails naming the property:
  `AssertionError: the outbound status 'In Progress' must resolve to transition 'Start Progress'
  (id 11) and be dispatched; got transitioned=[] and edited_fields=[{'status': 'In Progress'}]`.
  `strict=True` so the build fails when the bug is fixed, forcing the marker off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport.update_issue` pops `status` out of its kwargs and routes it through
      `self.transition_issue_by_name(remote_id, status)` — which since 7f93 already resolves either
      a transition name or a destination status name — and NEVER submits `status` through
      `issue.update(fields=...)`
- [ ] the remaining allowlisted fields still go through the field edit in the SAME call, and the
      existing `assignee` routing is unchanged — proven by a test asserting both a status and a
      non-status field in one `update_issue` call
- [ ] the `xfail(strict=True)` marker on
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_outbound_status_routing_5200.py::test_an_outbound_status_should_dispatch_the_transition_that_reaches_it`
      is REMOVED and the test passes, asserting `transitioned == [("DIG-1", "11")]`
- [ ] the characterization test that currently pins the defect
      (`test_the_dc_transport_edits_status_as_a_field_instead_of_transitioning`) is INVERTED with the
      reason recorded in its docstring — not silently deleted and not relaxed, because its docstring
      states an intent worth keeping
- [ ] a transition Jira rejects as illegal from the current workflow state stays NON-FATAL, matching
      the existing `_is_illegal_transition_400` comment-fallback contract, and is OBSERVABLE as a
      bridge alert rather than silent — asserted by a test, since silent soft-failure is what let
      this defect survive
- [ ] [operator-attested] live evidence: the J11 cell
      `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` is GREEN on a real DC harness run,
      with the GitHub Actions run id and job name recorded as a comment on this ticket. Attested
      because it requires a Dockerized DC instance that ordinary CI on a PR diff does not stand up
- [ ] [operator-attested] mutation-checked: reverting the status routing in `update_issue` returns
      the un-xfailed test to RED with a message naming the missing transition dispatch (not an

content.text: ## Summary

The inline-commit write paths — `transition`/`reopen`/`claim` (txn.py), `compact` (compact.py), and `delete` (delete.py) — commit their events to the local `tickets` branch but **never call the auto-push**. Only the `append_event` family (`create`/`comment`/`edit`/`tag`/`untag`/`set_*` via `write_and_push`) and `link` (graph/_links.py) push. Because a push sends the whole `HEAD:tickets`, transition/compact/claim commits are normally *carried* to origin by the next push-capable write — so the gap is invisible until such a write is the **last** operation of a session (e.g. closing an epic), which strands its commits as `PUSH_PENDING`.
This contradicts the documented contract in CLAUDE.md: 'Every write (create/edit/transition/claim/link/…) auto-commits its event to the tickets branch AND auto-pushes to origin/tickets.'
## Reproduction Steps
In a fresh rebar repo with an `origin` remote:
1. `create` a ticket  → origin advances (push fires). ahead=0
2. `claim` it          → origin unchanged. ahead=1
3. `transition` closed → origin unchanged. ahead=3 (claim+status+compact)
4. `comment`           → origin advances, carrying all 4. ahead=0
Empirically reproduced deterministically in a clean repo (no concurrency, healthy origin), so it is a push **absence**, not a push **failure**.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: every write (incl. transition/claim/reopen/compact/delete) auto-pushes `HEAD:tickets` best-effort, per the CLAUDE.md contract.
- Actual: transition/claim/reopen/compact/delete commit but do not push; they rely on a later append_event write to carry them. A trailing status/compact strands commits (fsck → PUSH_PENDING).
## Root cause

The bash `write_commit_event` auto-pushed on EVERY write. The tier-E bash→Python migration (commits e6e645ae 'relocate transition/claim write core into rebar._commands.txn', 41217cc7 'port transition/reopen', 9f7bd246 'port compact/compact-all', ~2026-06-13) gave these paths their own inline rename+commit but omitted the push that write_and_push performs. NOT caused by 0b32 (1dbe5e7e, canonical bytes) or 7d1d (cee1fe98, HLC) — those threaded canonical-bytes/HLC through txn/compact on 2026-06-17 but preserved the (already-missing) push wiring; pickaxe -S'push' on txn.py/compact.py/transition.py shows no push call was ever present or removed.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `transition`/`reopen`/`claim`/`compact`/`delete` trigger a best-effort push of `HEAD:tickets` after their locked commit (after lock release), honoring the `sync.push` policy (always/async/off).
- [ ] A transition/compact that is the LAST op of a session leaves origin/tickets current (no PUSH_PENDING in fsck).
- [ ] Push remains best-effort: a push failure never fails the write.
- [ ] No double-push regression for the append_event/link paths that already push.
- [ ] Test: in a repo with an origin, a lone `transition`/`claim`/`compact` (no following append_event write) leaves ahead=0.

baseline.summary: Status/compact/claim/delete writes commit to tickets branch but never push (PUSH_PENDING when last op)

baseline.description:
# A bound key that leaves the fetch window is planned as an outbound CREATE, resurrecting it

## Status

DISCOVERED, NOT FIXED. Surfaced while triaging J11's inbound-probe cell (`5200-e04e-246e-4aae`). The static chain is complete but the live-path confirmation experiment has NOT been run, so this is filed for its own RED-first investigation rather than patched blind. Confidence ~0.7.

## What was observed

Deleting a bound DC issue and running a scoped DRY-RUN produced exactly one plan entry for the pair, quoted from harness run 30724309686:

    {'direction': 'outbound', 'action': 'create', 'target': 'RBJWUOX-1', 'local_id': 'RBJWUOX-1'}

An outbound CREATE, targeted at the Jira key of the issue that was just deleted, built from the STALE previous snapshot. Reproduced with no Jira at all by calling `differ.compute_mutations({'RBJWUOX-1': <snapshot entry>}, {})`, which emits that entry byte-for-byte including the `local_id == target` fallback (`differ.py:121-131`).

## Mechanism

`run_differs.py:222` calls `compute_mutations(ctx.prev_snapshot, ctx.curr_snapshot, ...)`, so the parameter named `local_state` is in fact the PREVIOUS JIRA SNAPSHOT. A key present in prev and absent from curr therefore takes the "local only" arm and emits an outbound create (`differ.py:421-441`). The dd-4 short-circuit that would suppress it (`differ.py:377-380`) cannot fire, because `bound_local_ids` is built from a `local_id` field that a fetched snapshot entry never carries (`differ.py:213-224` vs `fetcher.py:479` and the contract shape at `_snapshot_schema.py:96-135`).

Downstream, two guards fail to catch it:

- `applier.py:253-278` (`_cross_project_targets`) skips `action == "create"` entirely, on the
  stated assumption that a create's key is a local-id placeholder — false here, it is a real
  Jira key.
- `create_one`'s JQL dedup keys on `mutation["local_id"]`, which is empty because
  `EXCLUDED_FIELDS` strips `local_id` from the payload (`config.py:5`), degenerating the query
  to `labels = "rebar-id:"` (`dispatch_one.py:236-256`).

`apply_planning.py:62-63` even prioritises outbound creates into the cap window.

## Why this matters beyond hard deletes

The same trigger fires for any key that merely AGES OUT of the fetch window — a `status = Done` issue beyond `_DONE_RECENT_CAP` — not only for a deleted one. That makes this a violation of ADR 0028 Decision §1: "no destructive or terminal action may be driven by a key's absence from the fetched snapshot." A resurrect-create is as much a terminal action as a retire.

Vendor-neutral code throughout, so Cloud is affected identically.

## Also recorded: the differ's local_state contract was never migrated

`differ.py:7-11` states that this module REPLACED the legacy `compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, next_snapshot)` contract with `compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state)`. Its sole production caller (`run_differs.py:222`) was never migrated. Every local_state-shaped feature is therefore inert: `bound_local_ids` always empty, the duplicate-local-id and ambiguous-local-binding arms never fire, `_derive_provenance` always falls back to `local_id = target`, and `_compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` (`differ.py:610-650`) is unreachable — which also makes the entire `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain (`run_differs.py:349-395`, `inbound_probe.py`, `backend.probe_remote`) a documented subsystem with no live producer. The only fixture that supplies a `jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py:38-39`.

## The experiment that must run first

Fake-client `reconcile_once` in LIVE mode (harness: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py`) with `prev_snapshot = {"DIG-9": {...}}`, `curr_snapshot = {}`, an in-project target so `_cross_project_targets` cannot mask the result, and a recording fake client.

- Predicted TRUE: `client.create_issue` is called once, with fields derived from the stale
  prev summary.
- Predicted FALSE: no create call, meaning a guard not yet found drops it, and this ticket
  closes as not-a-defect.

Repeat with an out-of-project key to show the guard's create exemption.

## Acceptance criteria

- The experiment above is run and recorded on this ticket before any code change.
- If TRUE: a key absent from the current snapshot but present in the previous one never
  reaches `create_issue`, proven by a RED-first unit test at the differ or applier boundary.
- Whichever way it resolves, `differ.py:7-11` and `run_differs.py:205` are corrected so the
  module docstring stops describing a contract the caller does not honour.
baseline.summary: snapshot-absent key planned as an outbound create

## Status — RESCOPED + CLOSED (operator-approved 2026-07-18)

This story is closed against a **rescoped** acceptance set. It had two separable halves:

1. **A DETERMINISTIC half — DESIGNED AND BUILT.** The seeded-defect **mutant corpus**, the
   **mutation-assembly + benchmark-driver harness**, the **pure counting helpers**, the
   **pre-registered thresholds**, and their **golden tests**. This lives as WIP in the `cal-e2`
   worktree on branch `calib/6982-e2` (`assemble_e2_mutants.py`, `run_e2_benchmark.py`,
   `e2_counting.py`, `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl`, `runs/e2_thresholds.json`,
   `tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py`, `test_e2_benchmark.py`). It is **not landed on
   main** — the harness's only runtime purpose is to drive the rejected batch (below), so landing
   it would ship a moot LLM-spend entry point. It is recorded here as documented WIP.

2. **An EXPENSIVE LLM BATCH BASELINE — PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost, and SUPERSEDED.** The
   ~100-run live scoring of the mutant/control corpus by the current gate (`run_e2_benchmark.py`'s
   `review_plan` sweep, and the `e2_baseline.json` / `e2_run_validity.json` / `e2_verdicts.jsonl`
   it would emit) is **dropped**. It is superseded by story **d8a5** (change **#798, MERGED**):
   the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, on main),
   which accumulates the SAME detection / blocking-FP signal from real production reviews at **$0
   marginal LLM cost**. Baseline **mining** from history is also dead: only ~4 `plan-v3` sidecar
   baselines exist against the ~200 needed — the `impact_model_version` bump stranded the history.

The design record below (Why / classes / mechanism) is retained as the account of what was built;
the Acceptance Criteria are rescoped to the delivered deterministic WIP only.

## Why

R1 (asserted-capability probe), R3 (decomposition-shape), and R4 (necessity gate) all gate on
DETECTION POWER, which can only be measured against plans whose defects are KNOWN. This story
builds that ground truth by CONSTRUCTION: take real cleanly-closed plans, seed exactly one defect
per class, and the mutation itself is the label — no fresh LLM adjudication (which would duplicate
the gate's own sidecar and be circular; that is why E1's finding-level LLM labeling was
invalidated). The unmutated originals are the controls that bound blocking false positives.

Named verbatim in `docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` §6 R3: "Seeded-flaw eval: take
10 real historical epics that closed cleanly; generate mutated variants ... Pass condition: ≥7/10
mutants flagged, ≤1/10 originals flagged." E2 generalizes that to all five defect classes.

**Five defect classes** (each mutated mechanically from a real cleanly-closed base plan):

1. **absent asserted capability** — plan asserts a named module provides a capability it lacks.
2. **layer-cake split** — children re-partitioned by architectural layer so no single child
   yields an end-to-end observable outcome.
3. **consumed-artifact-without-ordering-edge** — a child names an artifact a sibling creates with
   no `depends_on`/`blocks` edge.
4. **unnecessary mechanism** — one over-action line injects a NAMED mechanism the plan does not
   need (FixedBench over-action), selected deterministically by `hash(base_id) % len(templates)`.
5. **untagged operational AC** — mutation strips the `[operator-attested]` tag from an AC whose
   completion evidence lives outside the codebase.

The corpus was built from `runs/outcome_corpus.jsonl` under a codebase-grounded "cleanly-closed"
filter (`post_claim_edit_class=="none"` AND `reopen_count==0` AND `force_close==false` AND live
`closed` status AND, for container classes 2 & 3, ≥2 children). Counting rule pinned in the pure,
golden-tested `e2_counting.py` (`classify_pair`, `run_validity`) which handles the gate's
PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE verdicts and the ≥0.20 INDETERMINATE run-validity cap. Store isolation is
by construction: the harness runs the gate against a standalone `git clone --local --branch tickets`
of the store (its own `.git` directory), so mutation commits never touch the real `.tickets-tracker`.

**Why the batch was never worth its cost.** The corpus + harness + counting helpers are complete
and construct-valid, but the ONLY thing running them adds is a one-shot snapshot of today's gate's
detection/FP numbers — which d8a5's standing recorder now produces continuously from real reviews
for free, and which mining cannot reconstruct (stranded history). The operator therefore rejected
the ~100-run batch permanently and accepted the deterministic build as the deliverable.

## Scope (delivered as WIP on `calib/6982-e2`; NOT landed on main)

- `harnesses/assemble_e2_mutants.py` — mutation-assembly script (deterministic, no LLM).
- `harnesses/e2_counting.py` — pure `classify_pair` / `run_validity` counting helpers (no LLM).
- `harnesses/run_e2_benchmark.py` — benchmark driver. Its store-clone/isolation and `emit_baseline`
  run-validity-guard SEAMS are built and unit-tested offline; its live `review_plan` sweep is the
  rejected batch and is NOT to be executed.
- `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl`, `runs/e2_thresholds.json` — corpus + pre-registered thresholds.
- `tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py`, `test_e2_benchmark.py` — golden/synthetic tests
  (offline; no LLM).
- README section documenting the design as WIP + the batch deferral.
- NO `src/rebar` gate/source changes (E2 was measurement, not a gate change).

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped — delivered deterministic WIP only)

- [ ] **Mutant corpus BUILT.** `runs/e2_mutant_corpus.jsonl` holds ≥10 mutant rows for each of
  defect classes 1–4 (class 5 degrades to N≥5 with the shortfall recorded per the class-5 ladder),
  each paired with exactly one control row; every row carries `pair_id`, `defect_class`, `role`,
  `source_ticket_id`, `plan_text`, `children`, and (mutants) `mutation_op` + `mutation_diff`; each
  class-5 control's `plan_text` retains an `[operator-attested]` AC line the mutant strips. Built
  and verifiable in the `calib/6982-e2` worktree; deterministic (no LLM).
- [ ] **Thresholds pre-registered.** `runs/e2_thresholds.json` pins per-class detection /
  blocking-FP targets for all 5 classes plus the INDETERMINATE run-validity cap. Built as WIP;
  deterministic.
- [ ] **Counting helpers BUILT + golden-tested.** `e2_counting.py`'s pure `classify_pair`
  (INDETERMINATE→FN not FP; multi-criteria set-intersection attribution) and `run_validity`
  (≥0.20 INDETERMINATE-cap) pass `pytest tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_counting.py` offline (no
  LLM). Built as WIP on `calib/6982-e2`.
- [ ] **Baseline-emit guard BUILT + tested.** `run_e2_benchmark.emit_baseline` enforces (not merely
  computes) the run-validity guard — returns non-zero and writes no `out_path` when any class
  exceeds the INDETERMINATE cap — proven by the synthetic-fixture integration test
  `pytest tests/unit/experiments/test_e2_benchmark.py` (offline; imports the seam only, no LLM).
  Built as WIP.
- [ ] **Store-isolation implemented BY CONSTRUCTION.** The harness sources its mutant store as a
  standalone `git clone --local --branch tickets` (own `.git` DIRECTORY, not a linked-worktree
  pointer) and asserts standalone-ness before any injection, so the real `.tickets-tracker` cannot
  be contaminated. Implemented in `run_e2_benchmark.py`; verified by code inspection (the
  live `--self-check-isolation` run is part of the deferred batch and is NOT executed).
- [ ] **[operator-attested] Batch baseline DEFERRED — permanently rejected on cost, superseded by
  d8a5.** The live ~100-run `run_e2_benchmark.py` gate sweep and its `e2_baseline.json` /
  `e2_run_validity.json` / `e2_verdicts.jsonl` outputs are intentionally NOT produced. The
  detection / blocking-FP signal they would have measured is now accumulated at $0 marginal LLM
  cost by d8a5's standing `criterion_effectiveness.py` recorder (change #798, MERGED, on main), and
  history-mining is dead (~4 `plan-v3` baselines vs ~200 needed). Evidence lives outside this
  codebase: operator decision 2026-07-18 + d8a5 / change #798. This AC is closed by operator
  attestation, not machine check.
- [ ] **Design documented as WIP.** The README section records the seeded-defect design, the
  counting/run-validity rules, the store-isolation mechanism, and the batch deferral +
  d8a5-supersession, so the WIP status and the drop rationale are auditable.
baseline.summary: E2: seeded-defect benchmark from real closed plans (5 defect classes + controls)

content.text: ## Why

Audit OSS finding #6 bucket (versioning honesty): Python 3.13 has been the current stable for over a year, but the project tests/advertises only 3.11 and 3.12 — test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml matrices stop at 3.12, and pyproject classifiers list 3.11/3.12 only. For a published PyPI package that leaves 3.13 (the default interpreter in many new environments) untested/unadvertised.
## Current matrix (exact, both workflows)
`os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, `python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]`, with

`exclude: (macos-latest, "3.11")`. Net effect today: **Linux runs 3.11 + 3.12; macOS runs 3.12 only** (the newest — the exclude drops the lower rev). macOS's value is platform-compat coverage (flock/mkdir lock, gtimeout), not the Python rev, so it stays single-interpreter for runner cost.
## What / files
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` and `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`:

- to KEEP macOS single-interpreter on the newest rev (preserving the existing pattern where the exclude drops all but the highest on macOS), CHANGE the exclude block to drop BOTH lower revs on macOS: `(macos-latest, "3.11")` AND `(macos-latest, "3.12")`. Net after change: Linux runs 3.11/3.12/3.13; macOS runs 3.13 only. (Simply adding "3.13" without a matching exclude would wrongly give macOS two jobs — 3.12 and 3.13.)
- update the matrix comment to say macOS runs 3.13.
- `pyproject.toml`: add `"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13"` classifier (after L35) once the matrix is green. `requires-python = ">=3.11"` already admits 3.13; unchanged.

- README supported-version wording: README states "Python ≥ 3.11" (floor) — already satisfied by 3.13, so no correction required (optional "(3.11–3.13 tested in CI)" clarifier). docs/api-stability.md is NOT edited — it has no Python-version wording.
## Local-interpreter note

The local dev interpreter here is Python 3.14, not 3.13, so the authoritative 3.13 green signal is the CI matrix job (Gerrit Verified). Local `make lint && make typecheck && make test` on 3.14 is additional evidence; if a real 3.13-specific blocker surfaces in CI, the fallback remedy is to document 3.13 as excluded and withhold the classifier.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml `python-version` include "3.13"; the macOS `exclude` drops 3.11 AND 3.12 (macOS stays single-interpreter on 3.13); the 3.13 Linux jobs run green in CI
- [ ] pyproject classifiers include `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13`; build/`twine check` passes
- [ ] README supported-version statements remain consistent with the matrix (floor "≥ 3.11" retained)
- [ ] `make lint` green locally; CI 3.13 job green (authoritative) — or a real 3.13 blocker documented and the classifier withheld

baseline.summary: Add Python 3.13 to the CI matrix, classifiers, and supported-version docs

Harden the T5c security-overlay rubric prompt against out-of-scope and duplicate advisory findings, without changing its posture (advisory @ 0.95) or its recall on genuinely in-scope security gaps.

Evidence: T5c produced 288 advisory findings in the last 7 days with zero blocks ever; observed failure shapes include (a) findings about credentials/assets the plan does not touch (e.g. demanding rotation of a Gerrit HTTP password on a plan that only destroys an SSM copy), and (b) same-round near-duplicates (ticket 9e76: two findings both demanding temp-key-file deletion). ADR 0018's trust-boundary scope gate already bounds WHEN T5c fires; this task bounds WHAT it may claim once fired.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md gains an explicit in-plan-asset scope rule: a finding must name the plan section/step that creates, modifies, or transmits the asset at issue; assets merely adjacent to the plan (existing credentials, services, or stores the plan does not touch) are out of scope and must not be findings. Oracle: `grep -ni "does not touch\|in-plan" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` returns at least one hit.
- [ ] The prompt gains a same-round dedup rule: one finding per (surface, defect) pair; additional criteria angles on the same pair are folded into that finding's text, not emitted separately. Oracle: `grep -ni "one finding per" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T5c.md` returns a hit.

Parked design idea (Option E from the api-stability version-marker analysis). Investigate
adopting **VCS-tag-derived versioning** so the version is computed from the git tag at build
time and is NOT hard-coded anywhere — not in `pyproject.toml`, not in `server.json`, not in
docs. `git tag vX.Y.Z` would become the entire version-bump action, eliminating the
multi-file lockstep bump the release currently performs by hand.

## Context

rebar currently hard-codes the version in `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` and mirrors
it into `server.json` (top-level + `packages[].version`), kept in lockstep manually and
asserted by the release workflow's `authorize` version-lockstep guard. rebar builds with
**Hatchling** and already bakes `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance via `hatch_build.py`. The
mainstream zero-touch pattern is `hatch-vcs` (a thin wrapper over `setuptools-scm`) which
derives `project.version` from the latest git tag.

## Why this is an idea, not ready-to-implement

Several open design questions must be resolved before committing:
- **server.json is not covered.** `hatch-vcs` sets the Python package version, but the MCP
  `server.json` version (top-level + packages) still needs to be produced/synced from the
  same source — how? (generate it at build time, a small sync step, or a check).
- **Interaction with the new release-authorization workflow.** The `authorize` job asserts
  `version_input == pyproject == server.json`. With a VCS-derived version there is no static
  `pyproject.version` to compare — the lockstep guard's contract changes. And the release is
  dispatched-from-`main` with a `version` input BEFORE any tag exists (the tag is created
  post-publish), which is the opposite ordering from tag-derived versioning. Reconcile these.
- **CI must fetch tags** (`fetch-depth: 0` / `fetch-tags: true`) everywhere the version is
  needed, or the version resolves to a dev/`0.0.0` string (a known setuptools-scm failure
  mode). rebar's build-once/test jobs run without full history in places.
- **Interaction with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` baking** and the build-once artifact-identity flow
  (story 6168) must be checked so provenance stamping still works.
- **Blast radius vs. payoff.** This is a large change to fix what is otherwise a small
  lockstep bump; weigh against simply keeping the current manual bump (now that the drift-prone
  docs marker is removed under Option A).

## Acceptance Criteria (for promoting this idea to designed work)

- [ ] A short design note that resolves: how `server.json` versions are produced/synced from
  the VCS-derived version; how the dispatch-from-`main` `version` input + post-publish tag
  ordering reconciles with tag-derived versioning; and the CI `fetch-tags` requirements.
- [ ] A prototype or spike showing `hatch-vcs` deriving `project.version` from a tag without
  breaking the build-once / `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance flow.
- [ ] A go/no-go recommendation with the tradeoff vs. the status quo (manual lockstep bump).

Discovered from the api-stability version-marker design discussion; sibling of the
version-agnostic-marker change (Option A).
baseline.summary: Explore VCS-derived versioning (hatch-vcs/setuptools-scm) as the single source of version truth

content.text: Sibling of the ready --json fix (23d2-e0f3 follow-up, commit c6a67e7), found auditing the read arms.
## Antipattern

A read arm accepts and silently ignores unknown/removed options instead of rejecting them, so a user passing a removed legacy flag (or a typo) gets silently wrong/ignored behavior. ready was fixed to reject; list and show already reject; search and deps still tolerate.
## Locations
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_reads.py _cmd_search: explicit `elif arg.startswith("--"): continue  # tolerate unknown flags (matches the old shim)`.
- _cmd_deps: only reads positional + --include-archived; any other --flag is silently dropped.
## Experiment (confirmed)
On a real repo:
- `rebar search probe --json` -> rc=0, silently accepted (--json ignored; json is default so it "works by accident").
- `rebar deps <id> --json` -> rc=0, silently accepted.
- `rebar deps <id> --bogus-flag` -> rc=0, silently accepted.
Compare: `rebar list --json` / `list --bogus-flag` -> rc=1 "unknown option"; `ready --json` -> rc=2 (fixed).
## Fix

Reject unknown --options in _cmd_search and _cmd_deps (exit non-zero + usage), matching list/show/ready. Keep known flags (search: --status/--type/--has-tag/--include-archived; deps: --include-archived). Decide whether the search "old shim" tolerance is still desired (likely not, post-collapse).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] search/deps reject unknown options (RED test first)
- [ ] known flags still work; output unchanged
- [ ] guard consistent across all read arms

baseline.summary: read arms search/deps silently ignore unknown options (e.g. removed legacy --json) — same as the ready --json fix

1. Let Dockerfile.reviewbot's entrypoint materialize the persistent tickets worktree (git clone --single-branch of the tickets branch) with REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT set.
2. Any store WRITE from the container (emit_code_review_artifact -> rebar.create_ticket, repo_root=None -> tracker /var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets) fails: first with 'ticket system not initialized' (.env-id is GITIGNORED so no clone ever has it; only rebar init / the ensure-registry generates it), and after ensures with 'Author identity unknown' (container has no git user.name/email).
3. emit_code_review_artifact swallows the exception (best-effort by design), so every prod review silently emits nothing — the code_review data-capture feature (story limestone-unethical-zebrafinch) has never produced a real artifact (the only code_review tickets in the store are test fixtures).

**Expected:** a fresh container + volume yields a writable ambient store; artifacts are emitted+pushed per review. **Actual:** write-dead store; silent no-op emission.

Proven on prod 2026-07-10 (f600 verification): in-container probe reproduced both failures; after run_ensures(tracker) + repo-local git identity (RebarBotNava / joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com) a probe create succeeded AND auto-pushed to origin/tickets (d3ee-c7b6-061e-4a66). The prod worktree volume is now manually converged, but any FRESH volume/clone regresses — the entrypoint must do this.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Entrypoint (or app startup) runs the ensure-registry (rebar._store.ensures.run_ensures) and sets a repo-local git identity on the tickets worktree after clone — idempotent on restart.
- [ ] A container test (or stub harness) proves a write against a fresh single-branch clone succeeds.
