baseline.description:
## Why
A significant epic failure showed leaf plans DRIFT as leaf tickets are claimed and edited: by epic close, the leaf ACs described a very different plan than what the epic said would be delivered, and nothing caught the divergence until the epic's completion verification. No current criterion checks a leaf plan against its PARENT'S plan — G1G2/E4 ground against the codebase, COH checks internal coherence. IMPORTANT CORRECTION (verified against the code): there is NO existing "ancestor carve-out" that injects a parent's PLAN TEXT — `pass1._ticket_graph_blob` (pass1.py:281) injects only the parent's ticket ID string into context. So the leaf-vs-parent comparison is NEW behavior this ticket adds — implemented by having G7's AGENT read the parent via its show_ticket tool at runtime (no new context-plumbing), not by mirroring a (non-existent) injection carve-out. The review that gates the CLAIM is the right moment to catch drift, ticket by ticket, instead of at epic close.

## What
- Add a new plan-review criterion (working id `G7`, facet parent-containment) to src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json + the registry: `exec: AGENT` (it must read the parent ticket from the store, like the other codebase-grounded criteria), with a rubric prompt at src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ following the existing G-series prompt conventions.
- ROUTING — fires ONLY on leaf tickets WITH a parent: the gate is (ticket has a parent_id) AND (ticket has no children). MECHANISM (the existing schema can't express "has_parent_id" — `applies()` in registry.py:311-339 gates only on `scope` (container/leaf), `suppress_types`, `suppress_when`): add a new boolean axis `require_parent_id` to the `applies_at` schema and to `applies()`, and thread the ticket's `has_parent_id` fact through `route_criteria()` (orchestrator.py:337-375, which calls `registry.applies()`) from the assembled PlanContext (which already knows the parent chain). So G7's routing = `applies_at: {scope: ["leaf"], require_parent_id: true, suppress_types: ["bug","session_log"]}`. The `scope:["leaf"]` gives "no children"; `require_parent_id` gives "has a parent"; bugs/session_logs stay exempt as today; parentless tickets and containers never run it. The `require_parent_id` axis: `_validate_routing_entry` (overlay.py:190-212) currently does NOT reject unknown applies_at keys (so the key would pass unvalidated) — this ticket ADDS an explicit `require_parent_id` boolean-type check there (non-bool raises), and `registry.validate_packaged_routing()` stays green on the packaged G7 entry.
- SEMANTICS: the leaf's What/Scope/ACs must be a SUBSET of the parent's declared scope — a finding fires when the leaf (a) delivers something the parent's plan does not contain or implies is out of scope, (b) contradicts a parent AC/success criterion, or (c) redefines a deliverable the parent specifies differently. Consistent narrowing (a leaf doing PART of the parent) is NOT a finding.
- CONFLICT RULE (the operator's directive, encoded in the rubric AND the Pass-4 coaching move): the PARENT WINS — it holds the full delivery context. Coaching directs the agent to realign the leaf to the parent; if the agent believes the parent is genuinely wrong, the productive move is to update the PARENT first (which stales the parent's own attestation and forces its re-review) and only then re-review the leaf — never to silently diverge the leaf.
- CONTEXT ASSEMBLY — NO new context plumbing (the ticket's original intent, verified against the code): G7 is `exec: AGENT`, and the pydantic_ai runner provides the read-only `show_ticket` tool to EVERY AGENT criterion (src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py — "`show_ticket` always"; the completion verifier reads tickets the same way, completion.py:18). So G7's agent FETCHES the parent at runtime: its rubric instructs it to call `show_ticket(<parent_id>)` (and optionally the grandparent) and compare the leaf's scope against the parent's plan text. The parent_id is ALREADY in the agent's context: `pass1._ticket_graph_blob` (pass1.py:281) emits a `parent: <parent_id>` line from `ctx.state['parent_id']` (pass1.py:288). So G7's agent reads that parent_id from its ticket-graph context and calls `show_ticket(parent_id)` ONCE for the parent's plan text (and optionally the grandparent) — one hop, via the always-available `show_ticket` tool, nothing else pre-injected. This means NO `parent_plan` field on PlanContext, NO `_assemble_context_uncached` change, NO `plan_review_verify_inputs`/verifier-prompt slot, NO pass1 finder-context change — the agent reads the parent on demand through its existing tool. To bound cost, the rubric directs the agent to read only the parent (and one grandparent), not the whole subtree.
- Pass-2/3 stay untouched: findings flow through the standard verify -> decide pipeline; severity maps onto the existing plan axes (divergent_implementation is the natural home — a leaf diverging from its parent is exactly a divergent-implementation signal).
- POSTURE: ship `default_posture: advisory` at 0.95 per the ADR-0036 expand-contract house pattern, BUT record fire-rate + adjudication from day one. IN-SESSION deliverable (the promotion-decision PATH, not the decision itself), as a COMMITTED REPO ARTIFACT (CI-verifiable that the file exists, not a one-time ticket comment): a new committed file `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/g7-promotion-path.md` documenting (a) the exact query — a **jq** query over the `plan_review_result_v1` REVIEW_RESULT sidecars (`.schema == "plan_review_result_v1"`), computing G7 fire-rate = (count of sidecars whose `.findings[]` has "G7" in `.criteria` and `.decision` != "dropped") / (count of G7-eligible reviews), and validity from those findings' `.validity` field — (b) the promotion trigger — blocking at the plan-review 0.6–0.7 band once the observation window shows an acceptable false-fire rate — and (c) where the actual promotion decision will be recorded. The actual promotion decision depends on post-deployment field data and is explicitly DEFERRED (out of this ticket's close path; it belongs with the epic's deferred measurement follow-up 72b6-b0d2-2f93-456d).
- NOTE (explicit non-goal here, candidate follow-up): a material PARENT edit does not currently stale the CHILDREN'S plan-review attestations, so drift introduced by editing the epic after leaves are reviewed is only caught on the leaf's next re-review. If the observation window shows parent-edit drift, file a follow-up for parent-edit-propagating staleness in attest.compute_validity.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (G7 routing entry), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py (register G7 in CANONICAL_LLM + AGENT_TIER (NOT CODEBASE_GROUNDED — that set is for criteria whose VERIFY re-grounds against CODE; G7 grounds against the parent TICKET via the store. Per registry.py:62-65 the tool capability — filesystem + rebar `show_ticket` — is granted by the prompt's agentic `execution_mode`, i.e. AGENT_TIER membership, NOT by CODEBASE_GROUNDED); add the `require_parent_id` axis to `applies()`), src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py (`_validate_routing_entry` at 190-212 currently ignores unknown applies_at keys — add an EXPLICIT `require_parent_id` bool-type validation block so a non-boolean value raises, rather than silently passing), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py (`route_criteria()` threads the ticket's has_parent_id fact into `applies()`), src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml (add G7 to the static `criteria:` batch list — criteria ARE enumerated there, so this edit is required), a new reviewers/plan_review_G7.md rubric prompt (instructs the agent to `show_ticket(parent_id)` and apply the parent-wins containment check), the coach MOVE_REGISTRY (one parent-realign move in passes.py), the regenerated docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md, and tests (routing: fires on leaf-with-parent only, skipped for parentless/container/bug/session_log; semantics: fixture parent/leaf pairs — contained/exceeding/contradicting; posture pin; validate_packaged_routing()==[]; a test asserting docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/g7-promotion-path.md exists AND contains the fire-rate query + the literal '0.6'/'0.7' band). NO new context-assembly plumbing (G7 reads the parent via its `show_ticket` tool at runtime) and NO kernel decide.py/verify.py math changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The criterion runs ONLY on tickets that have a parent_id and no children; a routing test proves it is skipped for parentless tickets, containers, bugs, and session_logs.
- [ ] Fixture-driven tests: a leaf narrowing its parent PASSES; a leaf adding out-of-parent-scope deliverables fires; a leaf contradicting a parent AC fires.
- [ ] The rubric and the Pass-4 coaching move state the parent-wins rule. Proving command: `grep -iE 'parent wins|show_ticket' src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md` returns the parent-wins directive + the show_ticket instruction, and the new parent-realign move appears in passes.py MOVE_REGISTRY (asserted by the MOVE_REGISTRY test).
- [ ] The criterion ships advisory (0.95) with fire-rate observable in REVIEW_RESULT sidecars. In-session proof (a COMMITTED repo file, CI-verifiable): the committed file `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/g7-promotion-path.md` exists AND contains the promotion-decision PATH — the fire-rate/validity jq query (referencing the `plan_review_result_v1` schema and the `.criteria`/`.decision`/`.validity` fields), the literal '0.6' and '0.7' band bounds, and the recording location — proven by a unit test (tests/) that asserts the file exists AND greps it for those anchors (content check, not mere existence). The actual promotion decision is explicitly deferred (see 72b6), not required to close this ticket.
- [ ] G7's rubric instructs the AGENT to read the parent (and optionally one grandparent) via its `show_ticket` tool and compare scope — no new context-assembly plumbing is added; a test confirms G7 is registered in AGENT_TIER (NOT CODEBASE_GROUNDED) — AGENT_TIER membership is what grants the show_ticket tool (registry.py:62-65) — and the rubric references reading the parent ticket via show_ticket.
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make typecheck passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.
baseline.summary: Plan-review criterion: leaf-plan parent-containment (leaf scope must be a subset of its parent; parent wins on conflict)

baseline.description:
## Context

Cost-driven POC simplification, decided 2026-07-13 after the auto-lander (epic f1fa) generated a sustained bug spiral (dc33 annotation-store [4 layers], 15a1 FF-string-match drive loop, 0d3e Autosubmit-dropped-on-rebase, plus the FFO rebase-treadmill re-CI cost). Root cause: the auto-lander is a stateful, polling, client-side bridge that re-implements Gerrit/git integration to reconcile Gerrit's synchronous submit gate with GitHub Actions' async CI **across a mandatory rebase** — and that mandatory rebase exists ONLY because of the Fast-Forward-Only submit type (ADR 0040). Gerrit's own submit types make the server do the integration: **Rebase-If-Necessary** rebases-and-submits server-side, atomically, under Gerrit's lock + ACL.

Decision (owner): (1) RELAX the pre-merge requirement to re-run full integration CI after a non-conflicted rebase — accept the bounded, rare semantic-conflict risk; (2) switch main FFO -> Rebase-If-Necessary so Gerrit integrates server-side; (3) DROP the auto-lander bot ENTIRELY (too expensive to maintain for too little value) — agents Submit directly when both votes are green; (4) rely on the EXISTING (free) post-merge main CI as the semantic-conflict detector, with MANUAL revert on the rare red (no auto-revert infra — cost constraint). Own CI infra (Zuul) is out (3x hosting cost, cannot use GitHub Actions runner). LUCI-CV-style batching only pays off at far larger scale.

Net effect: process becomes cheaper (no re-CI on rebases, no lander container/infra) AND more reliable (Gerrit owns the atomic rebase-submit; deletes the entire client-side bug surface: string-parsing, label-as-queue, polling TOCTOU, crash-recovery, container ticket-store). Supersedes the lander portions of ADR 0040 (FFO) and ADR 0042 (auto-lander).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR 0047 records the decision + supersedes lander parts of 0040/0042 (child: ADR story).
- [ ] main submit type is Rebase-If-Necessary on refs/meta/config; Autosubmit label + rebase-on-behalf ACL retired (child: cutover).
- [ ] All infra/autolander/ code, tests, the land/land-status command, and land-contract.md are deleted (child: retire-code).
- [ ] Deployed auto-lander infra decommissioned: container, compose service + gerrit_autolander* volumes, autodeploy hooks, fetch-secrets autolander token, terraform (ssm.tf autolander param + monitoring_autolander.tf), nginx /autolander/status route, SSM /rebar/prod/autolander-gerrit-token, CloudWatch rebar-autolander-errors alarm (child: decommission-infra).
- [ ] Landing docs (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/your-first-change.md, README.md) rewritten: 'Submit via Gerrit when LLM-Review+1 and Verified+1; Gerrit rebases server-side; on a textual conflict rebase manually; post-merge main CI + manual revert is the safety net' (child: docs).
- [ ] Post-merge safety net documented: existing main-branch CI as detector + a manual-revert runbook (child: safety-net).
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green after code/infra deletion.

## Context / resumability
Every workstream is a child story/task below with its own AC. Auto-lander bugs dc33/15a1/0d3e are OBSOLETED by retire-code (deleting the code IS their resolution) — linked here; close them when retire-code lands. 85c3 (CI flakes) is INDEPENDENT and still valuable (agents' own Submits still need a reliable Verified) — NOT superseded. Prior epic f1fa is superseded (commented there). Sequencing: ADR first (design record) -> retire-code + decommission-infra + docs (can parallelize) -> cutover (the pivotal refs/meta/config flip, operator apply in a quiet window, done LAST so nothing depends on the removed bits mid-flight; back-out is a one-line submit-type revert). Landing is manual Gerrit Submit throughout (the bot is paused/being removed).
baseline.summary: Retire the auto-lander; land via Gerrit Rebase-If-Necessary + agent Submit

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The runner attaches per-call usage to every result (`result["_usage"]`, src/rebar/llm/runner.py:543) but Pass-1 discards it: passes.pass1_chunk, passes.pass1_container, and passes.pass1_isf return findings lists only, so BatchRunResult.outputs (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:167-176) carries no usage key and plan-review coverage.metrics has call counts but no token totals for the most expensive pass (the gap is documented at src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:139-149; _attach_plan_review_metrics currently reconstructs only det_ms/llm_ms/llm_calls timing proxies). Per-criterion request counts are extracted (runner.py:_extract_usage) but never persisted, blocking data-driven criterion demotion decisions.

## Approach
run_pass1 does not call runner.run directly — calls flow through _chunk -> sizing.pass1_with_ladder -> passes.pass1_chunk (and the container/ISF variants). The usage is threaded through that chain as a coordinated API change with EVERY caller updated atomically in this one change. The three pass functions have consumers outside the plan_review package, all enumerated and updated here: the in-package chain (sizing.pass1_with_ladder chunk path, pass1._chunk, pass1's container fan-out via _timed_pairing, pass1's ISF invocation) plus src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py (pass1_container at line 120, pass1_chunk at line 137), src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py (pass1_chunk at line 345), and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py (pass1 calls and the run_focused_finder 2-tuple destructure at line 344) — the eval/preview call sites unpack and discard the new usage element (`findings, _usage = ...`). Specifics: (1) passes.pass1_chunk, passes.pass1_container, and passes.pass1_isf change return type from list[dict] to (list[dict], dict) — findings plus the call's _usage dict; _timed_pairing keeps its existing (findings, pairing_record, exc) triple — the container call's usage is embedded as pairing_record["usage"] so the observability record and the accumulator read one field. summarize_for_isf (passes.py:525-541) is a mode="text" single-turn call returning a plain string (str(runner.run(req).get("text", ""))) — it cannot return a pair without breaking its string contract, so it is handled differently: it changes to capture the full runner result internally and return (text, usage_dict), and its sole caller (the ISF oversized-log path in pass1.py) unpacks the pair and appends a call record attributed to the ISF criterion with criteria=["ISF"]. sizing.pass1_with_ladder's two pass1_chunk call sites (the direct-return path at sizing.py:316 and the out.extend escalation path at sizing.py:333) both unpack the new pair and merge usage records. The concurrent-futures collector at pass1.py:490 changes from findings.extend(fu.result() or []) to unpacking: each future resolves to (findings_list, usage_records); the collector extends findings and appends the records. (2) Checkpoint fast-path: when sizing.load_checkpoint serves a chunk from cache, no LLM call happened — the chunk contributes NO call record and zero usage (a test asserts a checkpoint-resumed chunk adds nothing to the aggregate). Aggregation protocol: usage is recorded per CALL as {criteria: [ids the call covered], requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens} — no llm_calls field on a per-call record (one record IS one call); the per-criterion llm_calls value is DERIVED as the count of call records covering that criterion. Ladder retries: every COMPLETED attempt pass1_with_ladder makes for a chunk appends its own call record, all carrying the same criteria list. An attempt that RAISES (e.g. the context-limit error that triggers escalation) returns no result dict, so its usage is not recoverable from the current runner API — such attempts contribute nothing, and this limitation is documented in the accumulator's docstring; recovering usage from raising calls is explicitly out of scope. run_pass1 derives (a) the aggregate sum over all call records and (b) a per-criterion map using this attribution rule: an AGENT call (single criterion) attributes wholly to that criterion; a multi-criterion single-turn chunk attributes its token fields divided equally across its covered criteria (a documented approximation — the sidecar retains the raw per-call records, so exact attribution is always reconstructable), while the derived per-criterion llm_calls and the requests field count in full for each covered criterion. (3) The prerequisite finder runs in ProductionBatchRunner.run() via prerequisites.run_focused_finder, which returns (records, findings) with no usage — it is extended to return (records, findings, usage) where usage is the SUM over every runner.run call its internal run_bin closure makes (run_bin is recursive and multi-call; each call's _usage is accumulated inside run_focused_finder), its callers updated in the same change — ProductionBatchRunner.run and the fidelity_spot_eval.py destructure (scope includes src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py), and that usage is merged into the aggregate before emitting BatchRunResult.outputs["_usage"]. (4) _attach_plan_review_metrics (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:249+) is EXTENDED to fold the new token totals from the batch step output into coverage.metrics alongside its existing timing fields. (5) The sidecar payload (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py build_payload) gains coverage.usage = {"per_call": [call records], "per_criterion": {id: map}} — these exact key names are what the tests assert. Alternative rejected: post-hoc parsing of the REBAR_USAGE_LOG JSONL — opt-in, not always present, and not keyed by criterion.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py, src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py (new, beside tests/unit/workflow/test_production_batch_runner.py).

## Testing
FakeRunner.run does not emit _usage (runner.py:134-151), so tests use a thin test-local wrapper runner that delegates to FakeRunner and attaches deterministic stub _usage dicts to each result — no change to FakeRunner itself. Unit with that wrapper: aggregate totals equal the sum over chunk, agent, container, ISF, and prerequisite call records; a two-criterion chunk with 100 input tokens attributes 50 to each criterion while counting one llm_call for each; a simulated ladder escalation whose first attempt completes yields two call records both counted, while a first attempt that raises contributes no record; coverage.usage.per_call and coverage.usage.per_criterion appear in the sidecar payload with the documented key names; coverage.metrics gains the token totals through the extended _attach_plan_review_metrics; a runner result without _usage degrades to zeros; the full existing pass1/batch-runner suites pass with the new return shapes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a review, coverage.metrics contains input/output/cache token totals that include Pass-1 and prerequisite calls (checked: `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py` summing FakeRunner stub usage).
- [ ] The sidecar payload carries coverage.usage.per_call (raw call records with criteria lists) and coverage.usage.per_criterion under exactly those keys (checked: sidecar payload unit test).
- [ ] A multi-criterion chunk divides token fields equally across its criteria and counts llm_calls in full per criterion; ladder-retry attempts each contribute a call record (checked: dedicated unit tests for both rules).
- [ ] Missing _usage on any call degrades to zero contribution (checked: unit test).
- [ ] Every caller of the three changed pass functions and of run_focused_finder — including eval_solver.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, and criterion_preview.py — is updated in this change and the existing pass1, batch-runner, eval, and finalize test suites pass unmodified in behavior (checked: full `pytest tests/unit/` run).
- [ ] A checkpoint-resumed chunk contributes no usage and run_focused_finder's usage equals the sum over its internal run_bin calls (checked: dedicated unit tests).
baseline.summary: Thread Pass-1 per-call usage and per-criterion request counts into batch outputs and the sidecar

# Rekey live cell derives a colliding project key ~1 run in 26

## Symptom

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py::test_a_rekeyed_issue_resolves_by_id_and_records_what_the_stale_key_returns` failed on harness run 30772461871 (job 91561874505, main @ bd3de0f864) with its OWN setup assertion:

    >   assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project
    E   AssertionError: assert 'RBJDRDZ' != 'RBJDRDZ'

48 passed / 1 failed, canary `collected=49 executed=49 skipped=0`.

## Mechanism — a self-collision, not a product defect

`test_transport.py:515-516` derives the rename target by replacing the last character with a literal `"Z"`:

    new_project_key = (jira_dc_project[:-1] if len(jira_dc_project) >= 4 else jira_dc_project) + "Z"
    assert new_project_key != jira_dc_project

Harness project keys are `RBJ` + 4 random letters (`conftest.py:154,185` — `_PROJECT_KEY_PREFIX` plus `_random_project_key`). **When the drawn key already ends in `Z`, the derived "new" key is byte-identical to the original.** This run drew `RBJDRDZ`, so `RBJDRD` + `Z` == `RBJDRDZ`.

So the cell is flaky by construction at roughly **1 run in 26** (uniform final letter). It passed on runs 30765232591 and 30767546938 purely because those draws did not end in `Z`.

## This is NOT a regression, and that matters for reading the run

The failure is unrelated to anything merged in that tree. Nothing in 1231/1232/1233/1234/1235 touches `test_transport.py`, project-key generation, or the rename path; the collision depends only on a random draw. The two cells that DID depend on this session's work both PASSED on the same run: `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` and `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity`.

**Credit where due: the cell FAILED SAFE.** Its setup assertion is what caught the collision. Without it the test would have issued `PUT /rest/api/2/project/<key>` renaming the project to the key it already has, and then asserted things about a "stale" key that was never stale — a green or a confusing red that would have taught us nothing about the actual contract (7c26's operator-attested question about what a stale key returns). The assertion is doing exactly its job; only the derivation is wrong.

## Fix

Derive a target that cannot collide, rather than asserting after the fact. Options, cheapest first:
* pick a replacement character that differs from the current final character (e.g. `"Z"` unless the key
  already ends in `Z`, in which case `"Y"`); or
* append/rotate rather than substitute, keeping within Jira's project-key constraints (uppercase letters,
  length limits); or
* derive the new key from the same `_random_project_key` generator and retry on equality, which reuses the
  existing validity guarantees instead of hand-rolling a mutation.
KEEP the `!=` setup assertion whichever is chosen — it is the thing that turned a silent nothing-happened rename into a legible failure, and it should stay as the guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the rename target cannot equal the source key for ANY key the harness can generate, proven by a
      repo-only unit test over the derivation that includes a key ending in the replacement character
- [ ] the `new_project_key != jira_dc_project` setup assertion is RETAINED, not deleted as redundant
- [ ] the derived key still satisfies Jira's project-key rules (uppercase, length), asserted rather than
      assumed
- [ ] [operator-attested] the cell passes on a harness run whose project key ends in the replacement
      character — either by forcing that key for one run or by recording that the derivation test covers
      it, with the reasoning recorded here
baseline.summary: Rekey live cell can derive a colliding project key (1-in-26 flake)

# Raise the completion-recovery context bound and stop misreporting the cause

Retyped from `bug` to `task`: the original report ("the close gate blames a missing `agents` extra") was a real defect whose messaging half landed in change 1027. This ticket carries the remaining, deliberately NARROW slice. The larger redesign — budgets that scale with criteria count — is epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8], and an advisory plan-time nudge is [rebar:259c-0f29-e920-4fab]; neither is a prerequisite for this.

## Context / Problem

A ticket whose text merely grew large could not be closed. Bounded recovery refused any context over 24,000 chars before doing any work, so correct, merged work had no path to `closed` except `--force-close`. Ticket 9a08, which created this module, calls that outcome "a fail-closed close-gate availability defect: correct, merged work cannot transition to `closed`". Reported independently as [rebar:db1c-2a74-ffe1-4f90] on ticket 2932.

## What is PROVEN (measured, not inferred)

1. **The advertised remedy could not be carried out.** Measured on `9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56`
   (34,282 chars, reproducing its live failure byte-for-byte): description 10,281 + 9 comments
   23,617 (comments = 69%). Deleting the ENTIRE description still leaves **24,001 chars — one over
   the old limit**; comments are the only sufficient lever and the store is append-only
   (`_lib_writes` exposes `comment()` with no delete/redact). Shipped ticket 19b1 makes comments the
   sanctioned completion-evidence channel, so following the system's own guidance drove tickets
   irreversibly over the bound.
2. **The bounds were mutually incoherent.** Criteria ⊂ description ⊂ context, yet
   `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` (32,000) > `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` (24,000); a criteria set of
   26,000–31,900 chars passed every criteria bound and was then refused on context.
3. **The step-budget failure path emitted a FALSE remedy.** `transition_close.py` selected the
   remedy as `recovery_failure_cause(exc) or <install-the-extra literal>`, and
   `recovery_failure_cause` returns `None` for anything that is not a `CompletionRecoveryError`. A
   step-budget exhaustion therefore got "install the `agents` extra" after the verifier had just
   spent 804s making real model calls. Change 1027 fixed this for the recovery path only.

## Approach

Raise the context cap to **100,000 chars** and elide NOTHING. That covers both real tickets this blocked (34,282 and 41,595) with ~2.4× headroom while still bounding the per-criterion re-send, since recovery sends the whole context once per criterion (worst case `_MAX_CRITERIA` 32 × the cap). Keep the cap at or above the criteria budget, pinned by an invariant test, so the incoherence in (2) cannot return. Select the close-gate remedy by CAUSE rather than exception type, so a failure that demonstrably ran the model stops blaming a missing dependency.

**Alternative rejected — compact an over-cap context instead of refusing it.** Implemented, then WITHDRAWN after adversarial review proved it a signed-false-PASS vector: on an epic the gate assembles one block per ticket (`assemble_context(graph=True)`), each with its own `#### Comments` heading, so "drop the oldest comment history" silently deleted whole CHILD tickets — including their unmet acceptance criteria — while reporting only that comments were removed. Reproduced directly. Elision is unsafe in both directions: dropping evidence a criterion IS met causes a false FAIL, dropping evidence it is NOT causes a false PASS. A refusal is a visible false-block; a bad elision is an invisible signed false PASS, and this gate SIGNS its verdict.

**Alternative rejected — derive the cap from the model window.** `sizing.container_budget` returns TOKENS, not characters, and `sizing.largest_window_tokens` returns the same ceiling for every model including unknown ones, so the derivation would be both a unit error and insensitive to the configured model. A stated constant with a recorded rationale is honest; a fake derivation is not.

**Alternative rejected — tell authors to prune tickets.** No such policy exists in this repo predating this bug's own error string, and (1) shows pruning cannot work for a comment-dominated ticket.

**Explicitly NOT in scope.** This does not close 9fd4: its live blocker is the primary verifier's flat step budget, which does not scale with criteria count. That work, and the equally incoherent evidence bounds, are epic [rebar:94b4-059e-a74a-4cf8].

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py` — raise `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` to 100,000 with its
  rationale recorded; no compaction.
- `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — remedy selected by cause.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` §"Bounded completion recovery" — the cap, why nothing is elided, and the
  withdrawn-compaction rationale.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py` (new),
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_step_budget_message_d59e.py` (new). The latter does not duplicate the
  sibling `test_close_gate_bound_message_d59e.py`, which already pins the bounded-recovery remedy
  and its negative control.

## Testing

Unit tier with an injected fake runner (no billable calls). Each new test is mutation-verified by re-introducing the exact mechanism it pins — reverting the cap, re-introducing elision, and breaking the criteria-vs-context invariant must each turn the suite red.

Failure and edge paths: an over-cap payload must still fail fast with zero billable recovery calls; a genuine unavailability must still receive the install-the-extra remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] both tickets this defect blocked — 9fd4 (34,282 chars) and 2932 (41,595 chars) — reach a
      verdict rather than a context-bound refusal, asserted by a test parameterized on those two
      measured sizes
- [ ] the context reaching the model is byte-identical to the assembled context — a test asserts
      every per-criterion call carries it verbatim, so a future reintroduction of elision fails
- [ ] `_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS` can never exceed the context cap, pinned as an invariant test
- [ ] an over-cap payload still fails fast with ZERO billable recovery calls, asserted by call
      count, so raising the cap did not delete the cost guard
- [ ] a completion-verifier failure that demonstrably ran the model (a step-budget exhaustion) does
      not tell the operator to install the `agents` extra, and does surface the remedy the
      exception itself carries; a genuine unavailability STILL gets the install-the-extra guidance
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` states the cap, that nothing is elided, and why compaction was
      withdrawn
- [ ] [operator-attested] the change lands with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`
- [ ] [operator-attested] the superseded compaction revision is abandoned in Gerrit so it cannot
      be submitted — the elision it introduced is a signed-false-PASS vector (on an epic the gate
      assembles one block PER TICKET, so dropping "oldest comments" silently deleted WHOLE CHILD
      TICKETS and their unmet criteria), so leaving it submittable is itself the risk
baseline.summary: Raise the completion-recovery context bound and stop misreporting the cause

baseline.description:
## Problem

A plan-review run on current `main` emitted, from `rebar.llm.plan_review.workflow_ops`:

    plan-review Pass-2 verification contract violation ... {'unexpected': [0, 1, 2, 3]}

EVERY verification index was rejected as unexpected, so all four findings degraded to INDETERMINATE. Observed during a real `review-plan` run at HEAD `1052bc856f`, not in a test.

## Why this matters more than the verdict suggests

The run's VERDICT was unchanged, which is exactly what makes this dangerous: Pass-2 is the verification pass that decides whether a Pass-1 finding is real. If every index is rejected, the gate is not verifying anything — it is degrading the whole set to INDETERMINATE and continuing. A reviewer reading only PASS/BLOCK sees a healthy gate.

Consequences to establish in the investigation:
* Does an INDETERMINATE finding still count toward the blocking decision, or is it silently
  dropped? If dropped, a run in this state cannot BLOCK on a Pass-2-verified criterion at all.
* How long has this been live? Every plan review taken as authoritative while it persists is
  suspect, including several signed during this epic.

## What is known

* Reproduced at HEAD `1052bc856f` (plain `origin/main`, not the provider-seam stack).
* The rejected index set was `[0, 1, 2, 3]` — a contiguous run from zero, i.e. ALL of them, which
  points at an index-BASIS mismatch (chunk-local vs global numbering, or a re-chunk between
  request and response) rather than at individual bad indices.
* The emitting site is in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`; the verify kernel that
  assigns the global `index` is `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py`.

## Approach

Investigate with /rebar-debug discipline: capture the ACTUAL request and response at the Pass-2 boundary — the indices sent and the indices returned — rather than reasoning from the code. Choose the capture point one layer BELOW the contract check, since the check only reports the mismatch and cannot show which side is wrong.

Do NOT assume the model returned bad data. An index-basis mismatch on rebar's side produces exactly this signature, and the contiguous-from-zero set is more consistent with a basis error than with a model fault.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The root cause is proven by a captured request/response pair at the Pass-2 boundary showing
  which side's indices are wrong, not by code reading alone.
- AC2: A regression test reproduces the mismatch and fails before the fix.
- AC3: After the fix, a real plan-review run emits no contract violation and findings retain their
  verified severity rather than degrading to INDETERMINATE.
- AC4: It is stated explicitly whether INDETERMINATE findings can block, and if they cannot, whether
  any gate decision made while this was live needs revisiting.
- AC5: make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Plan-review Pass-2 rejects every verification index and degrades all findings to INDETERMINATE, live on main

content.text: # Code-review near-term nit reduction: suppress docs + llm-prompts advisory noise
## Why
Code-review advisory volume is ~5 findings/review, dominated by `docs` and `llm-prompts` nits
(0/9 high-value in the dogfooded adjudication). That noise buries the findings that matter and
trains reviewers to skim. We want less nit friction on the two lowest-value advisory surfaces
without touching the blocking posture (everything ships advisory in v1).
## Scope note — the landmine detector is split out
This story ORIGINALLY also bundled a grounding-assisted "new-behavior-without-test" detector.
Investigation established that detector needs a BESPOKE seam that does not exist yet (code-review
DET detectors are Engine-B pattern rules that scan code, not diff-parse + cross-file test
correlation; `resolve.extract_references_from_diff` is imports-only, not added-definition
extraction). Building that seam is disproportionate to this near-term nit-reduction change, so it
is SPLIT OUT to the follow-up idea `acoustic-coveting-turaco` (linked `discovered_from` this
story). This story now scopes to the feasible, self-contained down-rank half only.
## What
Introduce a `nit_suppressed` routing flag on the `docs` and `llm-prompts` code-review overlays in
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`, and honour it in the deterministic Pass-3
decide (`code_review_decide`): AFTER `pass3_over_findings` returns the decided findings, the
partition loop re-buckets any finding whose `decision == "advisory"` and whose criteria are ALL
nit-suppressed into `dropped` INSTEAD of `surfaced`, overwriting its `reason` field with the
canonical string `"nit-suppressed"` (a NEW value in `code_review_decide`'s partition, alongside
the kernel `decide.py` reason vocabulary `no-verification` / `veto:cited-reference-inaccurate` /
`low-validity` / `default-advisory` — the kernel is NOT modified; the tag is applied gate-side).
The demotion is POST-pass3 (it changes only the surfaced/dropped partition, never validity/impact/
priority or the block decision). Blocking posture is untouched — the flag only affects advisory
surfacing — and a finding that ALSO maps to a non-suppressed dimension still surfaces (all-criteria
rule). Because the demotion runs before the decide op emits `surfaced`, the downstream
`code_review_coach_inputs` / `code_review_coach` steps (which consume `surfaced`) naturally receive
the reduced set — no coach change is needed.
## Scope / files
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — add `"nit_suppressed": true` to the `docs`
and `llm-prompts` entries (both stay `blocking_enabled: false`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — a `nit_suppressed_criteria(routing_map=None)` helper
returning the set of criteria flagged `nit_suppressed` (overlay-aware, mirroring
`threshold_for` / `effective_routing`).
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` — in `code_review_decide`, demote an advisory
finding whose criteria are ALL nit-suppressed to `dropped`.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_nit_routing.py` — the routing + decide-partition tests below.
No LLM-priority-threshold or blocking change here (blocking calibration is the rollout child
`raptorial-galloping-dragon`); this is advisory-surfacing only.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The packaged `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` marks BOTH `docs` and
`llm-prompts` with `"nit_suppressed": true` AND keeps them `"blocking_enabled": false`; no
other advisory overlay (e.g. `security`, `tests`, `performance`) is `nit_suppressed`. A unit
test asserts this over the packaged routing.
- [ ] `code_review_decide` DEMOTES an advisory finding whose criteria are ALL nit-suppressed from
`surfaced` to `dropped`, setting its `reason` to the canonical `"nit-suppressed"`; a finding
mapping to a nit-suppressed AND a non-suppressed criterion still surfaces; a non-suppressed
advisory finding still surfaces; and a BLOCK is never demoted. Unit-tested.
- [ ] The `nit_suppressed_criteria` registry helper reads the flag from the routing index
(overlay-aware) and returns `{docs, llm-prompts}` for the packaged routing.
- [ ] Proving command: `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_nit_routing.py -v`.
- [ ] NO detector code ships in this story: the diff touches only `criteria_routing.json`,
`registry.py` (the helper), `workflow_ops.py` (the partition demotion), and the test — no
`detectors.py` change and no `new_behavior_without_test` symbol anywhere. Verifiable:
`grep -rn new_behavior_without_test src/ tests/` returns NOTHING. (The detector itself is
split to the `discovered_from` follow-up `acoustic-coveting-turaco`, per the Scope note.)

baseline.summary: Code-review near-term nit reduction: suppress docs + llm-prompts advisory noise

content.text: # WU-4 — Forward-compat detection (fsck) + docs + deployment gate
Make the no-dual-write rollout window *visible* instead of silent, and document
the new event + grammar + deployment ordering. Depends on WU-1 (the
`TAG_DELTA` type must exist to reason about). Can run in parallel with WU-2/WU-3.
## What / Scope
- `fsck` / `bridge_fsck` (`src/rebar/_engine/` fsck path): add a generic check
that WARNS when the store contains event-type files whose type is NOT in the
running binary's `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` ("store contains event types newer than
this binary understands — upgrade required"). This converts the silent
old-clone divergence (an un-upgraded reconcile host ignoring `TAG_DELTA` and
pushing a stale tag set to Jira) into a detectable signal. Generic, not
TAG_DELTA-specific.
- `docs/event-schema.md`: add a `TAG_DELTA {added[],removed[]}` row; bump the
documented `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3; note this is the first body-changing type
addition that engages the unknown-type forward-compat path.
- `CLAUDE.md` (tool set / tag commands) + CLI `--help`: document the new
`--add-tag`/`--remove-tag`/`--set-tags` grammar and the `--set-tags=""`
"clears OBSERVED tags only" warning.
- Release note / docs: elevate "upgrade reconciler-running clones FIRST" from a
note to an enforced operational gate for this rollout.
## Delivery / green state
`fsck` flags an unknown-newer event type with an upgrade warning; docs and CLI

baseline.description:
## Context

The 2026-07-08 principal-architect audit (security / reliability / maintainability / OSS best practices; four deep-dive reviews plus bandit, semgrep, pip-audit, gitleaks, zizmor, radon) found no critical security issues but a cluster of high-leverage reliability seams and hygiene gaps. Reconciler-internal findings were routed to epic adept-hedge-stain (including the dead-safety-machinery story nonmystic-archetypic-gibbon); everything else lands here. Each child cites the audit finding it remediates.

Reliability deliverables in one place (so the AC terms below are defined):
- **claim-race surfacing** (child 3003): a lost cross-clone claim becomes observable to the loser (retroactive signal once the merge is visible) and via fsck/validate/show.
- **push-merge lock** (child e699): the push-retry fetch+merge runs under the store write lock so it can't race a concurrent locked write.
- **staged-event reset on write failure** (child 0e59): the event-append failure path resets the git index (`git reset -- <relpath>`), not just the worktree file, so a failed write's staged blob can't be swept into the next successful commit; the git-add return code is also checked before commit.
- **LLM timeout wiring** (child 02cd): the operator's REBAR_LLM_TIMEOUT / cfg.timeout_s actually bounds LLM calls.
- **unmapped-status guard** (child 5886): an inbound Jira status with no mapping is skipped + alerted instead of silently defaulting to open.

## Sequencing & rollout note

Children land as a single ordered Gerrit stack (bottom→top), so files touched by multiple children compose in commit order rather than conflicting: docs/concurrency.md (3e8b then 3003), README.md (09d8 badges, 3775 index link, d13e supported-versions), pyproject.toml (3775 urls, d13e classifier, d2fa mypy), test.yml (0f21 drift gate, d13e 3.13 matrix).

Rollout/rollback: every runtime change here is additive or hardens an existing best-effort path (no new user-facing surface, no data migration), each is an independently-gated Gerrit change, and rollback is a per-change `git revert` — no feature flag is warranted for this scope. CodeQL (c3f8) is intrinsically post-landing: its first mirror run only executes after the workflow file reaches main, so first-run finding triage is tracked as a post-landing follow-up, not a pre-merge close blocker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All child stories/tasks closed with green CI (Gerrit Verified +1 per change)
- [ ] Reliability children landed with regression tests: claim-race surfacing (3003), push-merge lock (e699), staged-event reset on write failure (0e59), LLM timeout wiring (02cd), unmapped-status guard (5886)
- [ ] Maintainability children (mypy ratchet start d2fa, env-var registry + drift gate 0f21) landed
- [ ] Docs children (stale shell-test citations + architecture remedy row 3e8b, docs index + user guide 3775) landed
- [ ] OSS/CI children (CodeQL workflow c3f8 — file valid & landed, first-run triage tracked post-landing; README badges 09d8; Python 3.13 matrix d13e; .joe-janitor/.tokensave hygiene 2440) landed
- [ ] A cross-clone claim that loses the merge race is surfaced to the losing claimant and pinned by a two-clone regression test
- [ ] No git-store write path can commit another write's leftovers, and the push-retry merge cannot race a concurrent locked write
- [ ] The operator-configured LLM timeout demonstrably bounds LLM calls, and is never silently lowered below the SDK default when unset. NOTE: the exact pydantic-ai API surface that receives the timeout (model HTTP-client settings vs. model_settings vs. a run_sync kwarg vs. an asyncio wrapper) is a child-02cd implementation decision — 02cd selects the surface for the installed pydantic-ai version, proves it with a test that asserts the value reaches the client, and records the choice; the epic asserts only the observable outcome.
- [ ] Inbound Jira statuses that have no mapping can no longer silently reopen local tickets (skipped + alerted + tallied)
- [ ] Typing and config-surface ratchets are in place (mypy strictness ratchet started; env-var registry with a CI drift gate)
- [ ] Docs drift called out by the audit is fixed; CodeQL runs on the mirror; docs are navigable by humans; repo hygiene items closed
baseline.summary: 2026-07-08 principal-architect audit remediation: reliability seams, gate hardening, maintainability ratchets, OSS hygiene

## Why

`reconciler.baseline_dual_write` and `reconciler.baseline_consumer_swap` are the
shadow/consume phase flags of the convergence rollout (epic 3006-e198 / story a118).
Both are now flipped ON in this project and have run clean in production, so the
phased switches have served their purpose. Retire them and hardcode always-on
(baseline always dual-written AND always consumed as the outbound field-differ's
arbitration ancestor).

## What

- Remove both fields + validators from `ReconcilerConfig` (`_config_schema.py:399,403`
  and parser `:533,534`).
- Hardcode always-consume: `outbound_fields.py:418-419` unconditionally reads
  `binding_store.get_baseline(local_id)` as `arbitration_prev`; collapse the boolean
  threading through `run_differs.py:458/473`, `outbound_differ.py:374/626/731/805`.
- Hardcode always-dual-write at `reconcile.py:938-954`. **`baseline_shadow.py` does TWO
  things — do NOT delete it wholesale.** `run_dual_write_shadow` (1) ADVANCES per-binding
  baselines via `binding_store.set_baseline(local_id, curr_snapshot[jira_key])`
  (baseline_shadow.py:84) — STILL NEEDED after hardcoding always-on — and (2) runs the
  equivalence check (`_mirrored_equal`, divergent counting, the
  `RECON: baseline_shadow_check` stderr line) — the rollout gate, now permanently
  satisfied and dead. First EXTRACT the `set_baseline` advancement loop into a standalone
  helper (e.g. `reconcile._advance_baselines`) called UNCONDITIONALLY before `save()`; then
  delete ONLY the equivalence-check portions (`_mirrored_equal`, divergence counting, the
  `baseline_shadow_check`/`baseline_shadow_divergence` diagnostics). If that leaves
  `baseline_shadow.py` empty, remove the file; otherwise keep the advancement helper.
- Remove the two lines from `rebar.toml` (`:65`, `:70`).
- Do NOT delete `prev_snapshot`/`prev_jira_fields` — still needed to advance/seed baselines.

## Scope

Backward-compat verdict: SAFE. Baseline is persisted additively into `bindings.json`
(no store-version bump; older binaries ignore the extra keys, per ADR-0026), the
reconciler is a single advisory-locked GHA host process (no old-clone race), and
neither flag changes the shape of anything written to Jira or the tickets branch.
Out of scope: the KEEP decisions (signature mirror, completion floor).

## Cold-start note (address, don't skip)

`seed_baselines_from_snapshot()` exists but is never called, so a repo upgrading from
a version that never dual-wrote gets `get_baseline()==None` → "local-wins" until
baselines populate lazily (could silently revert a concurrent Jira edit on first
passes). Chosen resolution (lower-risk than wiring seeding into the hot path):
**document the one-pass warm-up window AND make it observable** — the reconciler
emits a `RECON: baseline_cold_start local_id=<id>` line to stderr whenever
`get_baseline()==None` for a confirmed binding, so operators can identify the window
from GHA run logs, and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` describes the warm-up window and how
baselines populate lazily on the first always-on passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `baseline_dual_write` + `baseline_consumer_swap` removed from schema, parser, and `rebar.toml`; each is now an unknown key (a `[reconciler]` config setting either name is warned-and-ignored, per the removed-key backcompat test).
- [ ] Baseline dual-write and consume are unconditional; the boolean threading through `run_differs.py` / `outbound_differ.py` / `outbound_fields.py` is collapsed; no dead back-out branch remains.
- [ ] Dead shadow machinery (`baseline_shadow.py`) removed if fully unreachable, or a comment records why it stays.
- [ ] Cold-start local-wins window is made observable and documented: the reconciler emits a `RECON: baseline_cold_start local_id=<id>` stderr line whenever `get_baseline()==None` for a confirmed binding, and `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents the one-pass warm-up window. (A unit test asserts the log line fires on a cold-start binding.)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
- [ ] Reconcile dry-run behavior is proven unchanged by a NEW test that pins the one arbitration decision the removed flags controlled and would FLIP if that behavior regressed (not a pre-existing test merely staying green). Because the flags were already `true` in prod, the hardcoded behavior must equal the flags-true behavior; and since the flags are now removed, the flags-true tree can no longer be run to capture a literal stdout baseline — so the proof is a targeted decision-pin rather than a full-stdout diff (equivalent invariant, non-flaky): with a baseline present that DIFFERS from a STALE `prev_jira_fields`, the outbound dry-run must SUPPRESS the field (baseline consulted as `arbitration_prev`); reverting to prev_snapshot arbitration flips the decision and fails the test. Delivered by `test_dryrun_arbitration_pinned_to_baseline` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py` (verified to flip on revert).
baseline.summary: Retire the two reconciler baseline rollout configs -> hardcode always-on

content.text: # Make the pre-commit lint/typecheck hooks venv-independent
## What

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `make lint`/`make typecheck` as `language: system`, so when the venv is not activated the hook resolves a wrong `ruff` (newer, F811-strict) from PATH and cannot find `mypy` — the local commit gate fails and forces `--no-verify` (which also skips the Gerrit Change-Id hook). Make the Makefile targets invoke the venv-pinned tools explicitly (e.g. `python -m ruff`/`python -m mypy` or `.venv/bin/…`) so the hook works regardless of activation. No real code defect exists (pinned ruff 0.15.19 = CI is clean).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `make lint` + `make typecheck` (and the pre-commit hook) resolve the pinned venv tools without requiring `source .venv/bin/activate`.
- [ ] A commit in a fresh shell (venv not pre-activated) runs the hook to completion (no wrong-ruff/no-mypy failure).
- [ ] Commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer.

baseline.description:
## Problem
Under concurrent multi-agent work, review-plan completes its (billed) LLM review but fails to persist the signature, raising PlanReviewGenerationChanged with before==after head sha. Reproduces whenever ANY other ticket in the store is written (comment/claim/transition) during the review window. Makes require_plan_review_for_claim unreliable in exactly the parallel epic/child decomposition rebar promotes.

## Root cause (confirmed by reading)
generation.sign_manifest aborts when fresh != initial_generation (generation.py:133). PlanReviewGeneration is a frozen dataclass whose equality compares ALL fields, including (a) ticket_store_revision (the STORE-WIDE tracker HEAD sha) and (b) relation_snapshot, whose type PlanRelationSnapshot (relation_snapshot.py:56) compares ticket_states_by_id — the full state of EVERY ticket in the store. initial_generation is captured at review START; fresh at sign time (minutes later). Any commit to any ticket in the window changes both fields, forcing PlanReviewGenerationChanged even when before==after within the attempt.

## Why it is a defect (not fail-closed by design)
The SIGNED manifest binds only own material + deps (file hashes) + related_material pins; the claim-time re-check compute_validity re-validates only those same subject/related scopes. The store-wide sign-time equality is therefore stricter than both what gets signed and what gets re-validated — it invalidates on differences that produce no change in the signed artifact.

## Fix
Scope the generation equality to the subject's own material + direct related material (+ phase/floor) — the same scope the manifest binds. Exclude ticket_store_revision and ticket_states_by_id from PlanReviewGeneration identity (e.g. field(compare=False) or a scoped __eq__). Keep the within-attempt before/after head fence (it correctly guards a concurrent COMMIT during collection) but stop comparing the minutes-old store-wide baseline.

## Acceptance criteria
- Signing SUCCEEDS when an UNRELATED ticket is committed to the tracker between review-start (initial_generation) and sign time, provided the subject's own material and its direct related material are unchanged.
- Signing still FAILS (PlanReviewGenerationChanged) when the SUBJECT's own material OR a direct child/prerequisite's material changed during the window.
- The within-attempt before/after head fence is preserved.
- A test simulates an unrelated concurrent tracker write during the window and asserts a signature is persisted; the pre-fix code path would raise PlanReviewGenerationChanged.

## Verification
pytest concurrency test: unrelated write during window -> signed; subject/related write during window -> PlanReviewGenerationChanged.
baseline.summary: plan-review signing spuriously fails (PlanReviewGenerationChanged) under unrelated concurrent tracker writes

baseline.description:
## Summary
The plan-review gate emits false-positive **"X does not exist in the codebase" / "missing / hallucinated edit target"** findings when a ticket references a symbol/file/artifact that one of its **upstream (`depends_on`) dependencies** creates. Because the referenced artifact is a *deliverable of a blocking dependency* that hasn't been built yet, the code-grounded criteria grep the live tree, find it absent, and BLOCK. On a greenfield epic (where most artifacts are net-new deliverables of sibling stories), this floods every consumer story with BLOCK findings — and since a BLOCK verdict blocks the plan-review **claim gate** (`verify.require_plan_review_for_claim`), a well-designed greenfield epic becomes effectively **un-claimable**.

## How it surfaced
Discovered while decomposing + plan-reviewing the parallel-agent auto-lander epic (`f1fa-57d8-07cb-44af`) and its Phase-1 stories S1–S6. Across review rounds, dozens of BLOCK findings were variants of: "`Autosubmit` label does not exist", "`wipChain` has zero matches in src/", "`/rebase:chain` has no implementation", "`on_behalf_of_uploader` appears nowhere", "`infra/autolander/failure.py` does not exist", "`show_ticket S2` returns not found". Fixing every *meaningful* finding, wiring resolvable dependency links, and adding a greenfield note did NOT clear them — the forward-reference BLOCKs persisted structurally.

## Root-cause investigation
Traced to two **code-grounded criteria** (`registry.py: CODEBASE_GROUNDED / AGENT_TIER`), both blocking, neither aware of the ticket dependency graph:
- **`G1G2`** (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G1G2.md`, blocking, block_threshold 0.7) — *"Verify (via Glob/Grep) that every file/symbol the plan names actually exists; flag hallucinated/missing edit targets; CREATION=new behavior→out-of-scope."* This is the PRIMARY source of the "named-artifact doesn't exist" findings. It greps per-reference with no notion that a dependency will create the artifact.
- **`E4`** (`plan_review_E4.md`, blocking, 0.75) — *"Scan the plan for assertions about the codebase ... FORCE a Grep/Read probe per assertion ... Fail-closed on absent evidence."* A milder, secondary contributor.
- Contrast **`F1`**, which does NOT misfire because it carries the carve-out the others lack: *"ANTI-FP: evaluate the spec AS WRITTEN, not the current codebase."*

Classification of the observed findings (15 existence-findings, one review round) confirmed the precise pattern:
- The findings fire on the **CONSUMER** referencing a **dependency's** deliverable (e.g. S4 → S1's `Autosubmit` label, S4 → S3's outcome record — S1/S3 are in S4's `depends_on` closure).
- The **CREATOR** ticket is **never self-flagged** for its own artifact (S2 defines `wipChain` and is NOT told "wipChain doesn't exist" — it gets under-specification findings instead). So this is NOT a blanket "greenfield" problem; it is specifically the **cross-ticket, dependency-directional** reference.
- **Forward references (to DOWNSTREAM/sibling deliverables) are correctly a VALID finding and must stay flagged.** Example: S1/S4 reference `ADR-0042`, which is authored by S6 — a *downstream* ticket (S6 `depends_on` S1/S4). Referencing an artifact a later ticket creates blurs the dependency graph and breaks hermetic closure. The gate SHOULD flag this; the fix must NOT silence it.

## Design intent (the invariant this restores)
Forward references are **intentionally unsupported** — they blur the dependency graph, block hermetic closure of the ticket, and are often indistinguishable from the hallucinations/deficiencies the gate exists to catch. The gate should consult **upstream** dependencies before flagging a missing artifact: a symbol delivered by a `depends_on` ancestor is legitimately usable; a reference to anything else that is absent (downstream/sibling deliverable, or nothing) is a genuine finding.

## Fix (this ticket)
A minimal carve-out appended after the existing rubric (does NOT reorder or reframe the criterion; coaching stays out of scope — the criteria only generate findings):
1. `plan_review_G1G2.md` — append: *"Any symbol created by a ticket this ticket depends_on (evaluated recursively) is treated as if it EXISTS and is NOT MISSING."*
2. `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` (Pass-2 validator, second line of defense on evidence validity) — the same sentence appended to the ABSENCE/'missing X' higher-bar paragraph.
3. `plan-review-finder.eval.yaml` — two eval cases: a **false-fire (`expect: pass`)** where a plan references a symbol its declared dependency creates (G1G2 must NOT fire), and a **recall (`expect: finding`)** where a plan makes a forward reference no upstream dependency provides — the ADR-0042 shape — (G1G2 MUST still fire); plus a `gold_set` label.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Create an epic with child stories where a consumer story `depends_on` a producer story, and the consumer references a symbol/file the producer will create (net-new, not yet in the tree).
2. Run `rebar review-plan <consumer-story>`.
3. Observe a BLOCK "X does not exist in the codebase / missing edit target" finding for the dependency-provided artifact (from G1G2).

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a symbol delivered by a `depends_on` ancestor is treated as existing (no missing/hallucinated finding); only references with no upstream producer (forward refs / hallucinations) are flagged.
- **Actual:** every reference to a dependency-provided-but-not-yet-built artifact is flagged as missing, BLOCKing the consumer story and rendering greenfield epics un-claimable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `plan_review_G1G2.md` and `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` carry the single upstream-dependency carve-out sentence (appended after the current rubric, not reordered).
- [ ] The prompt-index regenerates with no drift; `make lint` / config-check pass.
- [ ] `plan-review-finder.eval.yaml` has the false-fire case (dependency-provided symbol → no G1G2 fire) and the recall case (forward reference with no upstream producer → G1G2 fires), plus a gold_set label; the eval spec parses.
- [ ] A dependency-provided reference no longer produces a G1G2 "missing" BLOCK; a forward reference (downstream/no-producer, e.g. ADR-0042) still does.
baseline.summary: Plan-review over-flags upstream-dependency artifacts as 'does not exist' (greenfield epics un-claimable) — G1G2/E4 lack ticket-graph awareness

baseline.description:
## Observed

While executing epic 6eca-183e-1cd2-4fb9 this session, `rebar review-plan <id>` began
returning INDETERMINATE / store-read-failure for a ticket whose plan had nothing wrong with
it. Root cause: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py`'s `tracker_head_sha()`
requires the SHARED `.tickets-tracker` worktree (checked out on the orphan `tickets` branch,
symlinked into every worktree on the machine) to have a perfectly clean `git status
--porcelain` (zero untracked/modified files) and `git ls-files -u` (no unmerged) before it
will return a usable HEAD sha for ANY ticket.

In this case, two untracked files (`*-REVIEW_RESULT.json`, `*-SIGNATURE.json`) had been left
by what was almost certainly a crashed/incomplete `rebar` process working on a COMPLETELY
UNRELATED ticket (`6673-7636-a116-4f90`). Those two orphaned files collapsed plan-review to
INDETERMINATE for every other ticket on the machine — including ones with clean, fully
plan-review-passable descriptions — with no diagnostic that pointed at the actual dirty
path(s). The only way to discover the cause was to manually `git -C .tickets-tracker status
--porcelain` and reason about it.

## Why this matters

`.tickets-tracker` is explicitly a resource SHARED across every concurrent agent session on
a machine (each epic/worktree gets a symlink to the same tracker checkout). Any agent's
crashed or slow-to-commit write anywhere in the tracker blocks `review-plan` — and therefore
`claim` — for every OTHER ticket and every OTHER agent, with a generic INDETERMINATE verdict
that gives no hint the failure is environmental rather than about the ticket's own plan.

## Suggested remediation (not investigated in depth — a starting point)

- Have `tracker_head_sha()` / the `store-read-failure` path surface the actual dirty/unmerged
  paths in its error (or the review verdict's diagnostic), not just a generic
  store-read-failure, so an agent hitting this doesn't have to reverse-engineer the cause via
  manual `git status`.
- Consider whether the clean-check truly needs to span the WHOLE tracker checkout, or could
  be scoped more narrowly (e.g. only paths touched by the review being run), to shrink the
  blast radius of one agent's crash/slow-commit onto every other concurrent reviewer.

## Non-destructive resolution used this session

Confirmed via `ps aux | grep rebar` that no process was still writing those files, confirmed
via file timestamps they were the newest artifacts in an otherwise fully-committed series for
that ticket, then committed them (matching the prior commit-message convention for that
ticket path) and pushed to `origin/tickets` — this unblocked `review-plan` for the whole
shared tracker without discarding anything.
