# Adopt the DCO: declarative Gerrit enforcement, contributor docs, agent sign-off policy

## Why

rebar has no inbound-IP mechanism (no DCO, no CLA). Both external reports and peer convergence recommend DCO over CLA: Qt's CLA is the stated reason it cannot accept PRs, and OpenStack replaced its CLA with the DCO for all contributions (TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html) explicitly to lower the barrier, directing enforcement into Gerrit itself — the server rejects an unsigned push at `refs/for/*` time, zero new infrastructure. Gerrit documents `receive.requireSignedOffBy` as a per-project `project.config` key (https://gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-project-config.html#receive.requireSignedOffBy — inheritable, NOT site-only); live verification below guards against placement surprises anyway.

Sequencing note (resolves the file-existence review findings): `docs/your-first-change.md` does not exist at plan time — it is created by story **fat-leaflike-canary**, which this story `depends_on` (edge recorded in the store). Every edit this story makes to that file executes only after that story lands; in dependency order the target exists.

## What

- **Declarative config path (never a manual push):** add `requireSignedOffBy = true` to the `[receive]` section of `infra/gerrit/project.config` and roll out via the existing `setup-project.sh` flow to `refs/meta/config` (JoeOakhartNava admin identity). Rationale: `setup-project.sh` overwrites `project.config` on every run; a one-off manual push would be silently reverted. **Rollback:** revert the line, re-run `setup-project.sh` — documented in a comment beside the key.
- **Two distinct sign-off rules (resolves the identity-mismatch finding):**
  1. **Agent commits (RebarBotNava / `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` committer):** trailer is exactly `Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>` — the responsible human's real name with his registered plus-addressed mailbox (routes to the human; kernel practice accepts plus-addresses; the certifier is the human, satisfying DCO 1.1). Documented in CLAUDE.md's commit guidance verbatim.
  2. **e2e test scripts** (`infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh`, `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` — all push to `refs/for/*` and would be rejected post-flip): each script adds `-s` to its `git commit` invocations so the sign-off is the script's OWN configured test identity (a hardcoded human trailer would mismatch the test committer). No other trailer engineering.
- **Automation inventory (decision rule):** enumerate commit-creating automation with `rg -l "git commit" infra/ scripts/ .github/ Makefile` at execution; the three e2e scripts above are the known set; anything newly found is updated the same way (add `-s`) or ticketed via discovered_from.
- CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work (DCO)" section, moby/Docker template (https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md "Sign your work"): link developercertificate.org, show the trailer, `git commit -s`, real-name requirement, push-time rejection note, Envoy-style "fixing DCO" note (amend/rebase re-signing), the shepherded-patch two-trailer rule (contributor's own sign-off required in the patch; shepherd adds theirs on amend — coordinated with the PR-posture story), **and a one-line CLA decision record: "rebar uses the DCO, not a CLA; a CLA would be adopted only if Nava counsel requires rights beyond Apache-2.0 §5 + DCO"** (the durable in-repo record of that decision).
- Cross-link retarget INTO `docs/your-first-change.md` (after fat-leaflike-canary lands — see sequencing note): point the tutorial's interim developercertificate.org link at the new CONTRIBUTING DCO section.
- **Migration order (strict, and provable from git history, not tracker artifacts):** commits land in this order — (1) docs (CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md/tutorial retarget); (2) e2e-script `-s` fixes; (3) the `infra/gerrit/project.config` flag + `setup-project.sh` rollout. Because all three are commits in this repo, the order is verifiable post-hoc: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` must be a descendant of the commits touching the e2e scripts and docs (`git log --oneline -- <path>` comparison). No window where agent/bot pushes fail.
- **Post-flip failure runbook** (one paragraph in the CONTRIBUTING DCO section): rejected push → `git commit --amend -s --no-edit`, re-push; agent-tooling regression → roll back the flag while fixing.
- Flip GitHub's "require sign-off on web-based commits" on the mirror (one settings toggle; belt-and-braces).
- Peer-norm citation for the human-signs policy: Kubernetes AI-review governance (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/github-management/ai-code-review-tools.md) — cited as supporting practice, not load-bearing authority (the policy stands on DCO 1.1's own terms).

## Scope

IN: `infra/gerrit/project.config` + setup-project.sh rollout, rollback note, CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section (incl. CLA record + failure runbook), CLAUDE.md agent-trailer guidance, e2e-script `-s` fixes, tutorial cross-link retarget (post-dependency), GitHub web-signoff toggle, live verification.
OUT: CLA machinery; the probot/dco GitHub app (acts on PR checks; PRs here are answered/closed by the lockdown workflow the PR-posture story lands); retrofitting existing history (DCO applies to new commits only — kernel/OpenStack precedent); CLAUDE.local.md (gitignored, not a reviewable artifact).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Config flag present and rolled out — prove: `grep -A5 "\[receive\]" infra/gerrit/project.config | grep -q "requireSignedOffBy = true"`; the rollback note exists — prove: `grep -qi "rollback" infra/gerrit/project.config`.
- [ ] Live verification: an unsigned push to `refs/for/main` is rejected (server message captured in the commit message or a `docs/` note) and the same commit re-pushed after `git commit --amend -s` is accepted.
- [ ] e2e scripts sign their commits — prove, per file: `grep -q "commit .*-s\b\|commit -s" infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh`; same grep for `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e.sh` and `infra/gerrit/feature-branch-e2e-scenarios.sh` (three separate checks); one e2e suite run passes post-flip.
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md DCO section — prove: `grep -q "developercertificate.org" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -q "commit -s" CONTRIBUTING.md`; `grep -qi "not a CLA" CONTRIBUTING.md` (the CLA decision record); `grep -qi "amend" CONTRIBUTING.md` (fix-up/runbook).
- [ ] CLAUDE.md names the exact agent trailer — prove: `grep -q "Signed-off-by: Joe Oakhart <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>" CLAUDE.md`.
- [ ] Migration order provable from history — prove: the commit touching `infra/gerrit/project.config` is a descendant of the latest commits touching the three e2e scripts and the CONTRIBUTING DCO section (compare `git log` for the paths).
- [ ] Tutorial retarget done after dependency — prove: `grep -q "Sign your work\|DCO" docs/your-first-change.md` links the CONTRIBUTING section (executes post fat-leaflike-canary).
- [ ] GitHub web-signoff on — prove: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar --jq .web_commit_signoff_required` = true.
baseline.summary: Adopt the DCO: Gerrit server-side enforcement, contributor docs, agent sign-off policy

baseline.description:
## Why
rebar records cross-cutting review-gate design in ADRs (plan-review's novelty rising floor is
ADR 0008). The code-review novelty convergence mechanism — its divergence from plan-review
(per-citation region gate; typed local/Gerrit keyspaces; content-addressed resilient region
detection), the reuse boundary (shared kernel primitives vs gate-specific orchestration), and the
deliberate NON-additions — needs a durable ADR + docs so future work does not re-litigate or
accidentally fork the novelty definition.

## What
Write **`docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md`** (status Accepted — it documents
DECISIONS that are IMPLEMENTED on this epic's stack) and cross-link the docs. The ADR documents,
each citing its backing implementation module so a reader can verify it:

- **Reuse the novelty sub-call + `rising_floor_drop`** — the shared kernel primitives
  (`review_kernel.verify.novelty_model` / `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` / `reshape_novelties`,
  `review_kernel.decide.novelty` / `rising_floor_drop`) reused UNCHANGED. Code-review-specific
  orchestration: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty` +
  `apply_region_gated_floor`, the `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md` prompt + the
  `code-novelty` reviewer id, and the `code_review_novelty` contract registered in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py`.
- **The new `region_gated_floor` conjunct + its tri-state fail-safe (UNKNOWN == raise)** —
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py` (constants `REGION_UNCHANGED` / `REGION_CHANGED` /
  `REGION_UNKNOWN` + the detector); the floor drops iff `rising_floor_drop(...)` AND region is
  `REGION_UNCHANGED`, and CHANGED/UNKNOWN always raise (fail-safe direction).
- **Surfaced-only prior set** — the reader `latest_code_review_result`
  (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py`) returns only the persisted `blocking` + `advisory`
  buckets, so a dropped finding never re-enters the novelty prior set (the code-review counterpart
  of child c3e4 / bug old-frilly-plankton).
- **Permanent low-impact drop = the intended compromise; the priority floor is the escape hatch.**
  Define "permanent" PRECISELY: the drop persists across RE-REVIEWS FOR THE SAME KEY (session or
  change) — it does NOT reset per review the way plan-review's floor re-scores each run — because
  the surfaced-only reader excludes a dropped finding from the prior set, so on recurrence it scores
  as NOVEL and is dropped again (as long as it stays low-priority + region-unchanged). Permanence is
  WITHIN one keyspace, not cross-key. The priority floor (`verify.novelty_priority_floor`) is the
  escape hatch: a higher-impact finding is never eligible, so it keeps surfacing. Trust the priority
  score — no categorical criterion exemption.
- **Typed session/change keyspaces, and why local must NOT seed a change's first Gerrit review** —
  `session:<id>` (local, `code-review: session:{id}`) vs `change:<id>` (Gerrit,
  `code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}`); the reader (`latest_code_review_result`) matches only
  its own title scheme, so the keyspaces are disjoint and a prior LOCAL review can never seed a
  change's FIRST Gerrit review.
- **Content-addressed region detection and its resilience to rebase/force-push** — the artifact
  stores `{path: sha256}` (reusing `plan_review.attest._hash_file`, computed in
  `code_review/sidecar.py::reviewed_file_hashes`); comparison keys on CONTENT, not a reachable
  commit, so it survives a rebase/force-push. File-level in v1; line-level deferred.
- **Explicit NON-additions (AC2).** Record the decision to add NO "dso-style
  arbiter/relation-taxonomy/oscillation-loop", DEFINING those terms inline so the rejection is
  evaluable: a **DSO-style arbiter** = a standalone decision/signal orchestrator that ADJUDICATES
  between competing findings/signals; a **relation-taxonomy** = a typed model of relationships
  BETWEEN findings (duplicates/supersedes/refines/…); an **oscillation-loop** = a detector that
  tracks a finding surfacing→dropping→resurfacing across runs to break cycles. The ADR records WHY
  the lightweight novelty floor suffices instead: a permanent, priority-gated drop of novel
  low-impact findings on unchanged regions monotonically narrows the surfaced set across
  patchsets without modeling oscillation or inter-finding relationships — so the heavier machinery
  buys no demonstrated benefit for added failure modes. This positively discharges the epic's
  original oscillation/convergence-signal criterion as a DESIGN decision, not a deferral.

Also update the docs to cross-link: **`docs/review-kernel.md`** (its "Code-review consumer"
section — documenting the novelty convergence behavior: carryover labeling, region-gated drop,
keying, resilience) and **`docs/reuse-surface.md`** (pointing the shared kernel primitives at the
code-review-specific region-gate seam).

## Scope
- `docs/adr/0037-code-review-novelty-convergence.md` (NEW), `docs/review-kernel.md` (the
  "Code-review consumer" section — the code-review gate doc), and `docs/reuse-surface.md`.
- Documents the IMPLEMENTED behavior landed by c639 / 3bff / e51b + the c3e4 surfaced-only fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR 0037 captures the design decisions above, INCLUDING the deliberate divergence from
      plan-review's whole-artifact floor (the per-citation region gate), each element citing its
      backing implementation module.
- [ ] ADR 0037 records the explicit decision to add NO dso-style arbiter / relation-taxonomy /
      oscillation-loop (terms DEFINED inline) and why the lightweight novelty floor suffices.
- [ ] ADR 0037 defines "permanent" drop precisely (within-key, via the surfaced-only prior set) and
      how it diverges from plan-review's per-review re-scoring.
- [ ] `docs/review-kernel.md` (Code-review consumer section) documents the novelty convergence
      behavior (carryover labeling, region-gated drop, keying, resilience).

baseline.description:
## Evidence — reproduced, not inferred

`fetcher._iter_pages` (the pager behind `fetcher.collect`, which builds the INBOUND SNAPSHOT the entire inbound differ runs on) terminates on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED page size:

    src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:324-326
        if len(page) < page_size:
            return
        start_at += page_size

Jira Data Center silently truncates `maxResults` when it exceeds `jira.search.views.default.max` — a common hardening, and the same server behaviour already established for this codebase when the identical defect was fixed in `get_parent_map` (change 1105). A truncated FIRST page therefore reads as "that is all there is".

Measured against a client that serves 250 issues but caps every page at 20 (default `page_size=100`):

    issues recovered: 20 of 250
    CONFIRMED DEFECT: 230 issues (92%) silently lost from the inbound snapshot

## Why this is more serious than its two siblings

This is the THIRD instance of one defect class. The first was `get_parent_map` (fixed, change 1105). The second is [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` / `get_comment_map`, which lose links and comments. This one loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES.

`collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so a truncated read is not a missing attribute on a present issue — it is an issue the pass never sees at all. Every unseen bound issue is a candidate for the absence/deletion path, and every unseen unbound issue simply fails to reconcile. A run in that state reports success: it raises nothing, and "converged" is true of the 8% it looked at.

## Blast radius — wider than the DC adapter, which is why this is NOT folded into 9263

9263 is confined to `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`. This is CORE `fetcher.py`, on the shared inbound path, so a change here reaches the live Cloud bridge as well as DC. That is a different risk profile and deserves its own review and its own live verification rather than riding along on an adapter-local fix.

Cloud reaches the same lines but is not known to be affected in practice: its ceiling and `same-token-twice` cursor-stall guards target a different truncation mode, and no short-page truncation has been observed there. The fix must therefore be verified as SAFE FOR CLOUD, not merely correct for DC.

## Approach

Advance by `len(page)` and terminate only on an EMPTY page — the same correction already applied to `get_parent_map`, whose docstring records the reasoning.

One thing the `get_parent_map` fix did not have to handle and this one does: `_iter_pages` must not spin forever if a server ignores `startAt` and returns the same non-empty page indefinitely. The existing `same-token-twice` guard covers the Cloud CURSOR stall, not an OFFSET stall. Add an offset-stall guard that raises `SilentTruncationError` (the type this function already raises for truncation it refuses to hide) rather than looping.

`cap` and ceiling semantics are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — the pager's advance/terminate conditions, plus the
  offset-stall guard.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.

## Testing

- a client serving N issues while capping every page below the requested size yields ALL N (the
  reproduction above, which currently returns 20 of 250)
- an exactly-full final page followed by an empty page terminates without an extra spurious request
- a server that ignores `startAt` raises `SilentTruncationError` rather than looping forever
- `cap` still clips, and the ACLI ceiling still raises — asserted so the Cloud contract is pinned
  unchanged by this fix

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the 250-issue/20-cap reproduction recovers 250, asserted by a held-out unit test that FAILS on
      the current code
- [ ] termination is on an EMPTY page only, and the advance is by `len(page)` — read from the source
- [ ] a `startAt`-ignoring server raises `SilentTruncationError` instead of looping, asserted by test
      with a bounded-time guarantee
- [ ] the existing `cap`, ACLI-ceiling and `same-token-twice` behaviours are unchanged, each asserted
      by a test that exercises them — this touches the shared Cloud path, so "DC is fixed" is not
      sufficient evidence
- [ ] the full unit suite passes, and the live DC harness job stays green
baseline.summary: fetcher._iter_pages truncates the inbound snapshot on a short page: 92% of issues silently lost

content.text: ## Summary

_has_rebar_id_label (binding_walk.py) matches ANY label with the rebar-id:/rebar-id- PREFIX, including a malformed empty 'rebar-id:' (no local id). The L10 adopt guard then stands down (treats it as identity-bound) and defers to binding-recovery — but with an empty id there is nothing to re-link, so the key is never adopted AND never bound, and bridge-fsck reports it as unbound_jira on every run. Surfaced by REB-659 (a manual 'assignee clobber' experiment carrying label 'rebar-id:'), which produced a perpetual bare-forge-tapir drift alert.
## Reproduction Steps
1. A Jira issue has label 'rebar-id:' (empty value) and no binding-store entry.
2. Run the binding walk / bridge-fsck.
3. The issue is neither adopted (L10 stands down) nor bound → perpetual unbound_jira drift.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: an empty/malformed rebar-id: marker is treated as UNMARKED (adoptable), so the key adopts (create+bind) normally.
- Actual: the empty marker counts as a binding marker → adoption stands down → the key is stranded.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] _has_rebar_id_label returns True only for a WELL-FORMED marker (non-empty id after the prefix).
- [ ] A key with an empty 'rebar-id:' label is adopted (inbound create); a well-formed 'rebar-id:<id>' still stands down (no double-bind).
- [ ] Regression test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_binding_walk.py; reconciler suite green.

baseline.summary: reconciler: malformed empty rebar-id: marker traps a Jira issue in unbound-drift limbo

baseline.description:
## Context
ADR 0043 defines exactly two completion-evidence kinds: untagged acceptance criteria are codebase-verifiable, while criteria whose evidence inherently lives outside the repository must use the exact `[operator-attested]` tag. The current P6 deterministic lexicon only coaches on a subset of untagged operational phrases and cannot semantically inspect every criterion or detect an incorrectly applied tag. A1 `f7ee-572b-1eb0-4af8` demonstrated the gap: plan review passed a repo-level benchmark criterion without the required tag, then completion verification failed after the work was already merged.

## Approach
- Add an explicit plan-review criterion that evaluates every acceptance-criterion checkbox independently and classifies where its completion evidence can truthfully be verified.
- Preserve ADR 0043 fail-safe semantics: untagged and malformed tags remain codebase-verifiable; only the exact case-insensitive `[operator-attested]` token selects ticket-attestation evidence.
- Find both error directions: externally verifiable criteria missing the exact tag, and codebase-verifiable criteria incorrectly tagged operator-attested (which would weaken completion proof to a comment).
- Require evidence specific to the criterion, not keyword-only classification. Reuse the existing deterministic detector as candidate/coverage input where useful, but keep semantic judgment in the new criterion and leave the P6 lexicon fail-open/advisory.
- Route and document the criterion through the canonical registry, reviewer prompt/contract, criteria routing, generated criteria guide, and frozen evaluation corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The new plan-review criterion visits every `- [ ]` / `- [x]` acceptance item and returns one of two evidence kinds, `codebase-verifiable` or `operator-attested`, with criterion-specific evidence for the classification. Tier: reviewer contract/unit test plus behavioral eval.
- [ ] An inherently external criterion with no tag or a malformed near-miss produces a finding whose remediation names the exact `- [ ] [operator-attested] …` syntax; an exact tag on an external criterion is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [ ] A codebase-verifiable criterion carrying `[operator-attested]` produces a finding explaining that ticket comments cannot substitute for repository proof; the same criterion untagged is accepted. Tier: prompt-contract fixtures and behavioral eval.
- [ ] A criterion that bundles repository proof and outside-world proof is not silently assigned one evidence kind: review tells the author to split it into independently certifiable criteria. Tier: behavioral eval with a mixed-evidence fixture.
- [ ] High-confidence misclassification findings participate in the normal validity × impact blocking policy, while deterministic keyword detection remains advisory/fail-open and records abstentions. Tier: policy/registry unit tests.
- [ ] Registry completeness, criteria routing, reviewer resources, generated `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, and author guidance describe the new check and ADR 0043 exact-tag semantics without drift. Verify with the repository generation/drift gates.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A pinned multi-sample before/after evaluation over a frozen corpus that includes A1, the historical 115b/8c4f cases, codebase negatives, malformed tags, over-tagged code criteria, and mixed-evidence items meets predeclared precision/recall and regression thresholds; record model/config, sample counts, per-class results, and the run artifact on this ticket.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass, including focused tests proving the completion verifier still treats untagged criteria as codebase-verifiable and exact-tag criteria as operator-attested.

## Scope
Plan-review criterion and its tests/eval/documentation only. Do not broaden the completion verifier’s trust boundary or add external-service access.
baseline.summary: Validate acceptance-criteria evidence classification in plan review

## Status — RESCOPED + CLOSED (operator-approved 2026-07-18)

This story is closed against a **rescoped** acceptance set. It had two separable halves:

1. **A DETERMINISTIC half — DESIGNED AND BUILT.** The stratified **sample**, the frozen
   **baseline**, the **FP-control pool**, the **replay driver** (clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip +
   manifest seams), the **pure LLM-free metrics library**, and its **golden tests**. This lives as
   WIP in the `cal-e3` worktree on branch `calib/6982-e3` (`replay_candidate.py`, `e3_metrics.py`,
   `runs/e3/sample.jsonl`, `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl`, `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl`,
   `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py`). It is **not landed on main** — the driver's only runtime
   purpose is to drive the rejected batch (below), so landing it would ship a moot LLM-spend entry
   point. It is recorded here as documented WIP.

2. **An EXPENSIVE LLM BATCH REPLAY — PERMANENTLY REJECTED on cost, and SUPERSEDED.** The
   ~450-run live gate replay (the coarse ~200-ticket single sweep PLUS the precise ~50-ticket ×3
   candidate + ×3 current fresh runs, and the `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` /
   `criterion_deltas.jsonl` / `fp_control.json` they would emit) is **dropped**. It is superseded
   by story **d8a5** (change **#798, MERGED**): the standing per-criterion effectiveness recorder
   (`criterion_effectiveness.py`, on main), which accumulates the SAME detection / blocking-FP
   perturbation signal from real production reviews at **$0 marginal LLM cost**. Baseline **mining**
   is also dead: only ~4 `plan-v3` sidecar baselines exist against the ~200 needed — the
   `impact_model_version` bump stranded the history (which is exactly why a live replay, not a
   sidecar re-score, would have been required, and why the cost was unjustifiable).

The design record below (Why / definitions / mechanism) is retained as the account of what was
built; the Acceptance Criteria are rescoped to the delivered deterministic WIP only.

## Why

R1 (asserted-capability grounding probe) edits the Pass-1 finder rubric, so it changes what EVERY
plan review surfaces. Before any gate candidate is exposed to production, we must measure how much
it perturbs the verdicts of plans that already passed and closed cleanly. E3 was the counterfactual
replay that would produce that measurement; with E2 it was the evidence R1 is gated on.

The gate has a hard false-positive bar (`docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` §5 / R1):
R1 FAILs if, on 30 sampled historical plans that PASSed and closed with zero post-claim edits,
>3/30 gain a new blocking finding, or the median new-advisory count rises by >1 per review; the
epic also reports a PASS→BLOCK flip rate ≤2% on the wider cleanly-closed sample.

**The design removes two confounds** (both verified in code): recall contamination (`review_plan`
re-surfaces a ticket's own prior findings via `prior_concerns`, which `emit_sidecar=False` does
not disable) and baseline drift + LLM nondeterminism. It does so with a **recall-stripped clone**
(copy the store, delete every `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` under sampled tickets, run over the clone),
a **material-fingerprint drift guard**, and a **two-tier** structure: a coarse descriptive ~200
sweep, plus a precise 30-plan FP-control that replays BOTH the candidate and the current gate fresh
(N=3, two-level median, current-vs-current null floor) to isolate the candidate's true effect.

The deterministic pieces — the reproducible stratified sample, the frozen `plan-v3` baseline, the
over-sampled 50-ticket FP-control pool, the clone/strip/manifest driver seams, and the entire pure
`e3_metrics` library (`build_matrix`, `criterion_deltas`, `tkey`, `pass_to_block_flip_rate`,
`fp_control_eval`, `fp_control_valid`) — were completed and golden-tested offline.

**Why the batch was never worth its cost.** The only thing the ~450 live gate runs add is a
one-shot snapshot of one candidate's verdict perturbation — a signal d8a5's standing recorder now
produces continuously from real reviews for free, and which mining cannot reconstruct (the
`plan-v3` bump stranded the sidecar history to ~4 rows). The operator therefore rejected the batch
replay permanently and accepted the deterministic build as the deliverable.

## Scope (delivered as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`; NOT landed on main)

- `harnesses/replay_candidate.py` — driver (`sample` / `run` / `analyze` / `--verify`), incl. the
  clone + REVIEW_RESULT-strip + manifest seams. Its `sample`/`analyze`/metrics paths are offline;
  its live `run` gate replay is the rejected batch and is NOT to be executed.
- `harnesses/e3_metrics.py` — pure, LLM-free metrics library (golden-tested).
- `runs/e3/{sample.jsonl, baseline.jsonl, fp_control_pool.jsonl}` — deterministic sample + frozen
  baseline + over-sampled FP-control pool.
- `tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` — CI-collectable golden tests over synthetic fixtures (no LLM).
- README (E3 section) documenting the design as WIP + the batch deferral.
- NO `src/rebar` behavior change (E3 was measurement).

## Acceptance Criteria (rescoped — delivered deterministic WIP only)

- [ ] **Sample + frozen baseline BUILT and reproducible.** `runs/e3/sample.jsonl` (stratified,
  deterministic `random.Random(1729)`) satisfies the cleanly-closed filter on every row
  (`post_claim_edit_class=="none"` AND `reopen_count==0` AND `force_close==false`);
  `runs/e3/baseline.jsonl` carries a `plan-v3` `baseline_verdict ∈ {PASS,BLOCK}` +
  `material_fingerprint` per ticket; `runs/e3/fp_control_pool.jsonl` is the 50-ticket over-sampled
  FP-control pool. Built and verifiable in the `calib/6982-e3` worktree; deterministic (no LLM).
- [ ] **Pure metrics library BUILT + golden-tested.** `e3_metrics.py`'s `criterion_deltas`
  (COMPUTED `sidecar.norm_id` join), `tkey` (criteria-independent text key), `build_matrix`,
  `pass_to_block_flip_rate`, `fp_control_eval` (two-level-median candidate↔current pairing;
  `null_floor` current-vs-current; `r1_pass = new_blocking_median <= max(3, null_floor) AND
  new_advisory_median_delta <= 1`), and `fp_control_valid` (usable≥30 boundary) pass
  `pytest tests/unit/test_e3_metrics.py` offline (no LLM). Built as WIP on `calib/6982-e3`.
- [ ] **Replay driver seams BUILT.** `replay_candidate.py` implements the recall-stripped clone
  (copy store + delete `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json`), the material-fingerprint drift guard, the
  over-sampling ticket-drop rule, and the manifest/candidate-build-verification write. These seams
  are present and offline-exercisable (`sample`, `analyze --verify`); the live `run` gate replay is
  the deferred batch and is NOT executed. Verified by code inspection.
- [ ] **[operator-attested] Batch replay DEFERRED — permanently rejected on cost, superseded by
  d8a5.** The live ~450-run gate replay (coarse ~200 sweep + precise ~50×3 candidate + ~50×3
  current) and its `raw_verdicts.jsonl` / `transition_matrix.json` / `criterion_deltas.jsonl` /
  `fp_control.json` outputs are intentionally NOT produced. The verdict-perturbation signal they
  would have measured is now accumulated at $0 marginal LLM cost by d8a5's standing
  `criterion_effectiveness.py` recorder (change #798, MERGED, on main), and history-mining is dead
  (~4 `plan-v3` baselines vs ~200 needed). Evidence lives outside this codebase: operator decision
  2026-07-18 + d8a5 / change #798. This AC is closed by operator attestation, not machine check.
- [ ] **Design documented as WIP.** The README E3 section records the baseline source + chosen
  round, the cleanly-closed filter, the recall-strip + fresh-both-gates design, the
  material-fingerprint drift control, the two-tier nondeterminism/cost story, and the batch
  deferral + d8a5-supersession, so the WIP status and drop rationale are auditable.

baseline.description:
# Proven root cause: a transient GitHub `git fetch` hang becomes a durable `LLM-Review -1` that suppresses its own backfill recovery

## Context / Problem

Gerrit changes 1189 PS1, 1193 PS1 and 1208 PS1 (7 in journald since 2026-07-31) carry `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)]`. The `-1` is spurious: 1189 and 1193 flipped to `+1` on re-review against effectively identical code. Because the review bot's backfill reconciler only re-drives changes that have NO `LLM-Review` vote, the spurious `-1` removes the change from its own safety net, so a several-second network blip permanently wedges a contributor's change until a maintainer re-triggers by hand.

## Proven mechanism (reproduced; each step cited)

1. Per review the bot makes a throwaway clone (`voter.py:603` `TemporaryDirectory`;
   `gerrit_client.py:314 clone_change_ref`) whose `origin` is the **GitHub mirror**
   (`gerrit_client.py:359`).
2. The attested gate calls `materialize_tickets` -> `resolve_ref(..., blobless=False)` ->
   `_fetch_origin` -> `git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin`
   (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:337-393`).
3. **That fetch intermittently hangs.** Reproduced inside `compose-review-bot-1`: 25
   consecutive runs of the exact command, **2 hung past 320s (rc=124)**, the other 23
   finished in 1-3s. Median 2s; the repo is 80 MB / 54k objects — a connection stall, not a
   large transfer and not load.
4. git has no `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`lowSpeedTime` configured, so the stall burns the whole
   `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` (`repo_snapshot.py:295`) and `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` is converted
   to `SnapshotFetchError` at `repo_snapshot.py:376-380`. **Verified in this session** by
   forcing `subprocess.run` inside `repo_snapshot` to raise `TimeoutExpired`:
   `_fetch_origin` raised `SnapshotFetchError: git fetch from 'origin' timed out after 300s
   (attested mode fails closed)`.
5. `adapter.code_review_decision`'s blanket `except Exception` (`adapter.py:207-211`) cannot
   tell an *infrastructure* fault from a *review* fault, so it returns
   `_block("review-error", {})`. **Verified in this session**: raising `SnapshotFetchError`
   out of `produce_code_review_verdict` yields
   `decision=BLOCK, coverage_gap=True, message="[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)]"`.
6. The voter maps that BLOCK to `cfg.llm_review_block_value` and POSTs it
   (`voter.py:673-680`). **Verified in this session**: `review_and_vote` returned
   `status="voted"` with a `-1` POSTed to the fake Gerrit, and recorded the dedup row.
7. **The vote suppresses the designed safety net.** `reconcile.py:205-211` pre-filters on
   `store.already_voted(...)` and `gc.has_llm_review_vote(...)` and `continue`s, so backfill
   only re-reviews *vote-less* changes. Posting the `-1` therefore removes the change from
   backfill permanently.

Every timeout timestamp in journald is EXACTLY a vote timestamp (23:39:03 ch1189, 00:22:11 ch1193, 04:46:53, 16:41:48 ch1208). Normal review setup is 14-19s; the failures are a step-function to 300s.

The inner `_GIT_TIMEOUT` (300s) always fires before the outer `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1200s, `review_bot/config.py:30`), so an infra stall is structurally guaranteed to take the vote-bearing path and never the benign no-vote path that `app.py:161-176` and `reconcile.py:222-226` already implement for a hung review.

## Alternatives ruled out by evidence

* **"transfer too large"** (the error string's own guess) — REFUTED: 80 MB repo, median 2s.
* **Auto-deploy restarting the bot mid-review** — REFUTED. `compose-review-bot-1` recreation
  times were 23:25:04, 00:00:22, 03:59:28, 05:37:03 UTC; each of the four timeouts falls
  strictly inside a single container's lifetime (1208's container had been up 12h). A SIGTERM
  would not emit this log line, and the same container kept reviewing afterwards.
* **CPU / credit starvation** — REFUTED: `CPUCreditBalance` flat at ~864.
* **Disk pressure** — REFUTED: root 61% used, /var/gerrit 9%.
* **Diff-dependent** — REFUTED: reproduced with no review running.

## Approach

Make the review bot distinguish a *retryable infrastructure fault* from a *review conclusion*, and route only the former to the existing, already-tested no-vote path. This fits because the system already has the correct behaviour for this class one layer up (`app.py:161-176`, `reconcile.py:222-226`: abandon without voting, let backfill retry) — the defect is that the inner layer is inconsistent with it, not that a new mechanism is needed. Fixing the inner layer to match the outer one is the smallest change that restores self-healing, and it adds no new subsystem, config key, or abstraction.

Two edits:

1. **`src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py`** — add a narrow classifier
   `_is_retryable_infra(exc)` that matches `rebar._snapshot.SnapshotFetchError`,
   `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, builtin `TimeoutError` (which `asyncio.TimeoutError` and
   `socket.timeout` alias), and builtin `ConnectionError`, walking a bounded `__cause__`
   chain so a wrapped transport fault is still recognised. When
   `produce_code_review_verdict` raises such an exception, return a new
   `{"decision": "ABSTAIN", ...}` result instead of `_block("review-error", {})`. Every other
   exception, the gate-import failure, and every genuine verdict path are untouched.
2. **`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`** — immediately before the decision→vote mapping at
   `voter.py:673-680`, handle `decision == "ABSTAIN"`: emit the greppable `_voter_error(...)`
   marker (so `rebar/host:voter_errors` still counts the fault), POST no vote, write no
   dedup row, and return `{"status": "error", "stage": "review_infra"}`. This mirrors the
   existing `review_setup` early return at `voter.py:663-672`.

`reconcile.py` needs no change: it counts only `status == "voted"`, and a change left vote-less is re-picked by the `has_llm_review_vote` pre-filter on the next pass. The merge-path `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` (`voter.py:243`) is deliberately left voting as today — it is a Gerrit REST fault on a change the bot could still reach, and its current fail-closed behaviour is pinned by `test_voter_merge_path_rest_failure_votes_block_coverage_gap`.

Acceptance criterion 5 (configure `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`lowSpeedTime` so the stall aborts in seconds) is out of scope here and is filed as a separate child ticket; this ticket removes the durable damage, that one shortens the stall.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` — the classifier, the `ABSTAIN` result, and the branch in
  the `except` at `adapter.py:207-211`.
* `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` — the `ABSTAIN` early return before the vote mapping.
* `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py` — the unit tests below (the existing home of every
  `adapter` / `voter` / `reconcile` unit test).

No other file changes. No config key, no new module, no dependency.

## Testing

Added to `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`, using the existing `FakeGerrit` / `DedupStore` / `_cfg` / `_event` / `ReconcileGerrit` harness (no network):

* **Happy path (the bug):** `produce_code_review_verdict` raises `SnapshotFetchError` ->
  `adapter.code_review_decision` returns `decision == "ABSTAIN"`, and
  `voter.review_and_vote` POSTs **no** vote (`FakeGerrit.votes == []`) and writes **no**
  dedup row.
* **Failure/contrast path (no silent-pass hole):** an ordinary `RuntimeError` from
  `produce_code_review_verdict` still returns `BLOCK` and the voter still POSTs the `-1`;
  a genuine blocking finding still POSTs the `-1`. An `ABSTAIN` never POSTs a `+1`.
* **Backfill re-eligibility:** after an abstained review, `reconcile.once` with a
  `has_llm_review_vote`-honest fake re-drives the same change on the next pass (it is a
  candidate again), whereas the pre-fix `-1` made it skip.
* **Degraded-mode safety:** with the events-log erroring (`RECONCILE_DEGRADED`), an
  abstained change stays unvoted, so it is unsubmittable — "don't vote" cannot create a pass.
* **Mutation check:** the new tests are run against the reverted fix to confirm they go RED,
  and against the fix to confirm GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A retryable infrastructure failure raised out of `produce_code_review_verdict` — at
      minimum `SnapshotFetchError`, plus `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, `TimeoutError` and
      `ConnectionError` — results in **no `LLM-Review` vote** and **no dedup row**. Checked
      by a unit test asserting `FakeGerrit.votes == []` and
      `DedupStore.already_voted(...) is False`.
- [ ] A `VOTER_ERROR` marker is still emitted on that path so `rebar/host:voter_errors`
      counts it. Checked by a unit test asserting the `VOTER_ERROR` line reaches stderr
      (`capsys`) with the change id.
- [ ] A genuine review conclusion still votes fail-closed exactly as today: a real blocking
      finding, an INDETERMINATE, a scanner abstain, a gate-disabled verdict and a
      non-retryable exception all still POST the block value. Checked by the existing
      adapter/voter tests continuing to pass unmodified plus one new contrast test for the
      non-retryable exception.
- [ ] Nothing provisional is posted on an abstained change (no `+1`, no `-1`, no message), so
      backfill is not re-suppressed. Checked by the same `votes == []` assertion.
- [ ] An abstained change is re-picked by the backfill reconciler on a later pass. Checked by
      a `reconcile.once` unit test that reviews the change again once no vote is present.
- [ ] Degraded mode is safe: with the events-log unavailable an unvoted change stays unvoted
      and therefore unsubmittable. Checked by a unit test asserting no vote is cast in the
      degraded path.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` all exit 0.

## Relationship to other tickets

* `bb9b-608f-0183-4ca5` (contributor-triggerable re-review) — this root cause is the dominant
  *source* of the fail-closed `-1`s that story exists to let contributors clear. Fixing this
  shrinks that story's load; it does not replace it.
* `0347-b2cc-e6e9-4f6b` — filed on the auto-deploy hypothesis, which this bug REFUTES with
  on-box container-lifetime evidence. Its second half ("fail-NO-VOTE instead of fail-closed
  for retryable conditions") is the correct fix and is subsumed here.
* NOT related to bug `d5c7-0d57-c3ab-4e93` (plan-review Pass-2 verification-index rejection):
  that is a deterministic LLM output-validation fault with no network involved. This fault
  makes zero LLM calls — it dies in git before the first prompt.
baseline.summary: review-bot: a transient GitHub git-fetch hang becomes an LLM-Review -1 that suppresses backfill recovery

baseline.description:
Enhance the completion verifier to distinguish between task completion and goal achievement, and ensure planning workflows produce verifiable goal declarations.

## Reference: get-shit-done must_haves

get-shit-done (47k stars) separates verification into three distinct categories:
- **truths** — observable user-facing behaviors (not task completion). "The user can log in with email and password" not "Login endpoint was created."
- **artifacts** — files with real implementation (not stubs, not TODOs)
- **key_links** — critical connections between artifacts (the login form submits to the auth endpoint, the auth endpoint writes to the session store)

This separation catches the gap where all tasks ran successfully but the feature doesn't actually work end-to-end.

## Problem

DSO's completion verifier currently checks that acceptance criteria are met and tests pass. But acceptance criteria are often written at the task level ("create the endpoint", "add the migration"), not at the goal level ("the user can complete the workflow end-to-end"). A story can close with all tasks green but the feature broken because the pieces don't connect.

## Changes Required

### 1. Planning Workflows (brainstorm → preplanning → implementation-plan)

- **Brainstorm** — epic success criteria should be written as observable user-facing truths, not implementation milestones. The gap analysis should flag criteria that describe implementation actions rather than user outcomes.
- **Preplanning** — each story's done definition should include at least one truth (user-observable outcome), the key artifacts expected, and any key_links between components.
- **Implementation-plan** — task acceptance criteria remain implementation-level (they should be), but the plan must also declare story-level must_haves that the completion verifier will check after all tasks complete.

### 2. Completion Verifier (dso:completion-verifier)

At story closure, the verifier should check three layers:
1. **Task completion** (existing) — all tasks done, tests pass
2. **Truths verification** (new) — each declared truth is demonstrably true. Not "the endpoint exists" but "a request to /login with valid credentials returns a session token"
3. **Key_links verification** (new) — declared connections between artifacts are functional. The form actually submits to the endpoint. The endpoint actually writes to the database.

At epic closure, the verifier should additionally check:
- All story-level truths roll up to epic-level success criteria
- No epic success criterion is unaddressed by story truths
baseline.summary: completion verifier enhancement

baseline.description:
## Why
`_acquire_fcntl` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py:127-140`) catches EVERY `OSError` from
`fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` identically: it sleeps and ultimately returns the timeout
sentinel `-1`. So a genuine system fault (ENOLCK/EIO/EBADF) is indistinguishable from real
contention (EAGAIN/EACCES) and gets masked as a spurious 30-60s `LockTimeout`. The mkdir leg
already branches on `errno` (`lock.py:222-230`). VALIDATED: no direct test of
`_acquire_fcntl`.

Note on EINTR: under PEP 475 (CPython ≥3.5) the interpreter retries a syscall interrupted by
a signal (including `fcntl.flock`) at the C level before returning to Python, so
`OSError(EINTR)` does not surface in user code — there is deliberately NO EINTR branch here
(it would be unreachable dead code).

## Caller-impact analysis
`_acquire_fcntl` has one caller — `acquire` (`lock.py:288`), which maps `fd < 0 → raise
LockTimeout`. `LockTimeout` is caught at ~12 sites (inbound_translate, sync, event_append×2,
ensures, push, compact×2, txn, fsck, _seam) — but every one handles it as **contention** (a
lock not acquired within the budget). This change leaves the contention path UNCHANGED
(EAGAIN/EACCES still → `-1` → `LockTimeout`), so all 12 handlers behave exactly as before.
The only behavioral change: a genuine unexpected fault (ENOLCK/EIO/EBADF) now propagates as
`OSError` (with its errno) instead of being masked as a spurious `LockTimeout` — which is the
bug being fixed. No handler wants to swallow a real EIO/ENOLCK as a lock timeout; failing
loud on a true fault is strictly more correct.

## What
Branch `_acquire_fcntl` on `errno`:
- **EAGAIN / EACCES (contention):** retry until `deadline`, then close the fd and return
  `-1` (unchanged).
- **Any other errno (ENOLCK/EIO/EBADF/…):** close the fd and re-raise the `OSError`
  immediately, preserving its errno/identity.
The fd opened at the top is closed on EVERY non-success exit (the timeout return AND the
re-raise path); on success the caller owns and closes it (unchanged).

Add direct tests of `_acquire_fcntl` that inject specific errnos by monkeypatching the
module's `fcntl.flock`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — errno branching in `_acquire_fcntl`; close fd on all paths.
- `tests/unit/test_lock_stale_reclaim.py` — new direct `_acquire_fcntl` errno tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EAGAIN/EACCES: retries until the deadline, then returns `-1` (contention behavior
      unchanged) — asserted with `flock` always raising EAGAIN and a near-immediate deadline.
- [ ] A non-contention errno (e.g. ENOLCK) is re-raised immediately as `OSError` with that
      errno (not masked as `-1`/`LockTimeout`) — asserted with `flock` raising ENOLCK, and
      confirming it raises promptly (before the deadline), not after waiting.
- [ ] The fd is closed on every failure path (the `-1` timeout return AND the re-raise) —
      asserted by spying on the module's `os.close` and confirming the opened fd was closed.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Discriminate contention from unexpected errors in _acquire_fcntl

baseline.description:
## Why
`_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock` reads the lock's mtime, judges it stale, then later
`os.remove`s the same pathname **without re-confirming it is the same file**
(`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:88-107`; mtime read at ~:100, unconditional remove at
~:103-105). A peer can remove the stale lock and create a fresh **live** `index.lock`
between the stat and the unlink, and rebar then unlinks the peer's new lock. VALIDATED:
no test replaces the inode during reclamation (existing tests cover only a stationary
stale lock and a young lock released later).

## What
Add a production hardening that re-validates identity+age immediately before removal
(compare `st_dev`/`st_ino` and mtime from a single `os.stat`/`os.open` handle, or an
equivalent safe-revalidation), and a deterministic regression test.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock`.
- Test: pause reclamation after the stale file is statted (injected seam, not sleep),
  replace it with a fresh file, resume; assert the replacement survives.
- Do not change the stale threshold constant or the retry loop's public behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A deterministic test reproduces inode-replacement-during-reclaim and asserts the
      freshly-created lock is NOT unlinked.
- [ ] The reclaim path re-checks file identity (device+inode) and age at the moment of
      removal; a mismatch aborts the unlink.
- [ ] Existing stationary-stale and young-lock ride-out tests still pass.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Harden index.lock stale-reclaim TOCTOU + deterministic replacement test

content.text: Make every rebar command emit structured JSON, and make every JSON output shape
authoritatively documented by a JSON Schema validated in tests across all three
interfaces (CLI, library, MCP). Scope below is the result of a full codebase audit.
## Motivation
The output surface is inconsistent: some commands emit JSON, others ad-hoc text/
TSV/id-list, with no machine-readable contract. A prototype exists (canonical
TicketState schema + cross-interface test + MCP outputSchema for show_ticket).
This epic generalizes it. The schema arm is tracked in the child story
fe3e-346e-e5eb-42db (Roll out JSON Schemas + typed MCP returns + 2 bug fixes).
## Output inventory (audit result)
### Already JSON — no --json work (schema only, via the story)
show, list, search (TicketState[]), deps, list-descendants, get-file-impact,
get-verify-commands, clarity-check, scratch get/set/clear. Behind a flag:
next-batch (--json), validate (--json), bridge-status (--format=json).
### Needs a structured/--json form ADDED (epic work; each then needs a schema)
Primary data outputs with NO JSON path today:
- list-epics (TSV) -> {p0_bugs[],epics[{id,alias,priority,title,children_count,blocking,blocked,blockers[]}]}; preserve exit 0/1/2
- ready (id-list default) -> JSON array of ids (or ticket summaries); note --format=llm NDJSON already exists
- summary (text line) -> [{ticket_id,status,title,blocking_summary}]
- check-ac (AC_CHECK: ...) -> {verdict,criteria_count,reason}
- quality-check (QUALITY: ...) -> {verdict,line_count,keyword_count,ac_items,file_impact,reason}
- fsck (line-tagged text) -> {issues:[{kind,ticket_id?,filename?,detail}],fixed[],issue_count}
- bridge-fsck (text; findings dict already exists) -> {orphaned[],duplicates[],stale[]}
- transition / reopen (UNBLOCKED: ...) -> {ticket_id,from,to,newly_unblocked[]}; keep exit 10
- claim (CLAIMED: ...) -> {ticket_id,status,assignee}; keep exit 10
- create (human line + bare id) -> {id,alias,title} (removes the `| tail -1` id-scrape convention)
- delete (Deleted + UNBLOCKED:) -> {ticket_id,deleted,newly_unblocked[]}
### Side-effect / exit-code only — NO --json needed
comment, edit, tag, untag, set-file-impact, set-verify-commands, link (non-dry-run),
unlink, exists (boolean by exit code), init (operator bootstrap, stderr only).
### Borderline (convert only for 100% coverage; low value)
compact, compact-all, fsck-recover, purge-bridge, revert, archive, link --dry-run,
resolve, format. `format` is a display helper and should likely stay text.
## Cross-cutting requirements
1. FLAG STANDARDIZATION: today there are three conventions — `--json` (next-batch,
validate), `--format=json` (bridge-status), `--format=llm` (show/list/ready).
Pick ONE canonical structured-output flag and apply it everywhere (alias the
others for back-compat). Decide & document.
2. SCHEMA-COVERAGE GUARD (key DoD): a test that enumerates every command's
structured output and asserts (a) it validates against a schema and (b) no
structured output lacks a schema — coverage is enforced, not aspirational.
3. MCP read tools advertise outputSchema (typed returns) consistent with the
canonical schemas (delegated to the story).
4. stderr/stdout discipline: keep human/progress/WARNING lines on stderr so JSON
stdout stays clean (audit noted show/list bridge-alert warnings, next-batch
conflict matrix, validate human output, list-epics "no epics" all already on stderr).
## Suggested child-task breakdown (to be filed under this epic)
- T1: schema rollout + typed MCP returns + 2 bug fixes  (== story fe3e-346e-e5eb-42db)
- T2: choose & apply the canonical structured-output flag (standardization + back-comat aliases)
- T3: add --json to the lifecycle/result commands (create/claim/transition/reopen/delete)
- T4: add --json to the read/report commands (list-epics/ready/summary/check-ac/quality-check/fsck/bridge-fsck)
- T5: schema-coverage guard test + docs of the per-command output contract
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inventory above is validated and turned into child tasks (T1-T5)
- [ ] Canonical structured-output flag chosen, applied everywhere, back-compat aliases kept
- [ ] Every data-returning command offers structured JSON (the "Needs --json" list above)
- [ ] A JSON Schema exists under src/rebar/schemas/ for every distinct JSON output shape
- [ ] Coverage-guard test: every structured output validates against its schema AND no structured output lacks a schema
- [ ] MCP read tools advertise outputSchema matching the canonical schemas
- [ ] Docs describe/link the per-command output contract (README/CLAUDE/docs)

baseline.summary: --json everywhere: structured output for every command, each backed by a JSON Schema

## Context / Problem

The final Jira modules still sit at the package root: `acli.py`, `acli_cli_ops.py`,
`acli_graph.py`, `acli_rest.py`, `acli_subprocess.py`, `adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, and
`comment_limits.py`. Per ADR 0035 §(c) the seam is `adapters/jira/`, so these belong under it.
This is the **last** story and it is atomic by necessity (ADR §1/§2): the three location-pinned
modules (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `comment_limits.py`) break the file-location loader
unless the loader is taught their new dir in the same change, and every surviving reference must
move together with no re-export shim (ADR Decision 4).

**Prerequisite state.** S4 [rebar:6673-7636-a116-4f90] (a `depends_on` prerequisite of this
story) removes the *backend-neutral core's* direct imports of these modules by routing it
through the `Backend` port. This story **assumes that landed state** and moves the now
adapter-only files; the exact surviving reference set is re-confirmed by grep at implementation
time (it must not include any core module once S4 has landed).

Edit-set (the references that survive S4 — verified against current `main`, to be re-confirmed
after S4 lands):
- Physically move the eight modules into `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/`.
- **Loader**, taught the new dir *without* breaking the ~30 other root modules it also loads:
  `_loader.lazy_load(key, filename)` resolves `path = _PACKAGE_DIR / filename`
  (`_loader.py:39,56`), so pass a **relative subpath** for the three moved location-pinned
  modules. The exact by-path load sites for these three (grep-confirmed on current `main`, each a
  module-local lazy-loader singleton — there is **no** `__main__.py` load site for them; `__main__.
  _load_sibling_keyed` only loads `mode.py`/`_advisory_lock.py` and is untouched) are:
  - `lazy_load(_ADF_KEY, "adf.py")` → `"adapters/jira/adf.py"` at **three** sites:
    `outbound_fields.py:69`, `outbound_comments.py:84`, and `inbound_translate.py:323`
    (`_ADF_KEY_APPLIER`).
  - `lazy_load(_COMMENT_LIMITS_KEY, "comment_limits.py")` → `"adapters/jira/comment_limits.py"` at
    `outbound_comments.py:100`.
  - the `spec_from_file_location` site that loads `adf` by sibling path —
    `inbound_fields.py:36–37` (`adf_path = Path(__file__).parent / "adf.py"`) → point at
    `adapters/jira/adf.py` (also listed under the sibling-reference set below).
  Each resolves correctly under the relative subpath and leaves all other root lookups untouched.
  (`outbound_fields.py`, being itself one of the moved modules, moves with its `_ADF_KEY` loader
  intact — its `lazy_load` call is repointed like the others.)
- **Surviving intra-adapter / non-core references to repoint** (dotted + sibling-filename):
  - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py:18–24` — **two** dotted imports of moved modules, both
    repointed: `from rebar_reconciler.adf import fit_text_to_adf_limit` (line `:18`) →
    `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf import fit_text_to_adf_limit`, **and** the
    `from rebar_reconciler.comment_limits import _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (lines `:19–21`) /
    `from rebar_reconciler.comment_limits import truncate_comment_body` (lines `:22–24`) →
    `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.comment_limits import …` (all three targets now
    co-located under `adapters/jira/`). Missing the `comment_limits` lines fails the module
    import after the move.
  - `inbound_fields.py:36` — `adf_path = Path(__file__).parent / "adf.py"` (the InboundMapper
    impl stays at root; adf moved) → point at `adapters/jira/adf.py`.
  - `acli.py:76` — `from rebar_reconciler.adf import text_to_adf as _text_to_adf` (moves with the
    `acli*` cluster; becomes an intra-adapter import
    `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf import text_to_adf as _text_to_adf`). Omitting it
    leaves a dangling root-path import that fails at runtime after the move.
  - `acli_cli_ops.py:36` — `from rebar_reconciler.adf import …` (moves with the `acli*` cluster;
    becomes an intra-adapter import).
  - Any `outbound_comments.py` / `inbound_translate.py` / `reconcile_check.py` adf/comment_limits
    loader refs **not already eliminated by S4** — grep-confirmed at S5 time; repoint or drop.
- **Test surface** (characterized correctly — the first draft's "~29 `mock.patch` strings" was
  wrong; there are **zero** `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.acli…")` string patches). Three
  distinct categories:
  1. ~23 files use `patch.object(applier|fetcher, "_load_acli", …)` — **object-level,
     path-agnostic**; unaffected by the physical move (they inject a fake transport).
  2. ~18 files hardcode `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(…, "<moved>.py")` /
     `SCRIPTS_DIR/… "acli.py"`-style **path constants** naming a moved module → must be rewritten
     to the `adapters/jira/` path.
  3. ~18 files use direct dotted imports `from rebar_reconciler.acli… / .adf / .outbound_fields`
     → must be rewritten to `adapters.jira.*`.
  Categories 2+3 (their deduped union) are the atomic migration set; category 1 is verified
  still-green, not edited.

## Approach

One atomic change (the constraints forbid a partial move). Re-run the grep sweep to enumerate
every surviving reference (categories above), move the files, teach the loader via relative
subpaths, repoint every dotted/sibling reference, and rewrite the category-2/3 test targets —
then run the full suite. The change is complete when a grep for the old root paths of the moved
modules returns zero hits in `src/` **and** `tests/` (excluding the path-agnostic `_load_acli`
patches) and the suite is green. No behavior changes — a pure relocation + rebind.

## Scope

- Move the eight remaining Jira modules into `adapters/jira/`.
- Relative-subpath loader updates for the three location-pinned modules.
- Repoint every surviving dotted/sibling reference (incl. `jira_fields.py:18`,
  `inbound_fields.py:36`, `acli_cli_ops.py:36`) and rewrite the category-2/3 test targets,
  atomically, with no re-export shims.
- **Out of scope:** any behavior change; the core rewire (S4, prerequisite); new backends
  (epic `be74`). `jira_fields.py` already relocated in Phase 1 — only its `adf` import changes.

## Testing

- **Tier:** integration (full suite) + a structural gate.
- **Full suite green** after the move is the primary oracle — the category-1 `_load_acli` tests
  and the rewritten category-2/3 tests all exercise the moved modules at their new paths.
- **Loader test:** dynamically loading `adf`/`outbound_fields`/`comment_limits` through the
  reconciler entry point succeeds at the new location (staging the move without the loader edit
  fails RED).
- **Non-moved-consumer regression:** exercising `inbound_fields.py` (which loads `adf` by sibling
  path) resolves the moved file, and the ~30 other root modules the loader serves are unaffected
  (a root-module dynamic load still succeeds) — proving the relative-subpath change is scoped.
- **Structural gate:** `grep` finds **zero** references to the old root paths of the moved
  modules in `src/` and `tests/` (excluding the path-agnostic `_load_acli` `patch.object`
  sites), and **no** re-export shim remains at any old path.
- **Teeth:** leave one category-2 path constant at the old path and confirm that test errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The eight modules physically reside under `adapters/jira/`; no source file remains at
  their old root paths and no re-export shim exists there — verified by `ls`/`grep`.
- [ ] The loader resolves `adf` / `outbound_fields` / `comment_limits` at the new sub-package
  path via relative subpaths, and a root-module dynamic load still succeeds (loader test +
  non-moved-consumer regression).
- [ ] Every surviving dotted/sibling reference is repointed (`jira_fields.py:18`,
  `inbound_fields.py:36`, `acli_cli_ops.py:36`, and any S4-residual loader refs); the deduped
  category-2/3 test targets reference the new `adapters.jira.*` paths — verified by `grep` for
  the old targets returning zero hits (excluding the path-agnostic `_load_acli` patches).
- [ ] Every `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/*.py` stays within the 800-LOC module-size cap
  (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`) after the move — verified by the module-size gate.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` all green.
baseline.summary: Relocate acli*/adf/outbound_fields/comment_limits into adapters/jira/ + teach loader; migrate ~29 patch strings atomically

## Context

A 5-way triage (per-rule, cross-checked against ruff) classified them: 374 dismiss (false-positive/non-shipping/intentional), 230 low-priority 'present' (style/uniformity, deferred), and 27 genuine low-risk/low-effort fixes. Plus 4 mechanical AI test-cleanups. This ticket lands ONLY the 31 mechanical, no-behavior-change fixes as a single change.

## Out of scope

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 31 fixes applied; each is a mechanical transform with no behavior change.

- [ ] Affected test modules pass (targeted pytest run) + no import/collection errors.

content.text: ## Why
Complete the contract vocabulary the prompt model reuses. Lowest-risk, built right after the
skeleton so the contract surface is fully exercised before prompts adopt it.
## What
- Add input/output schema names + description to the 7 remaining ops in

baseline.description:
# Consolidate cross-session duplicated primitives (canonical-JSON/hash + retry/backoff)

## Context

A codebase-health audit (joe-janitor, 2026-06-24; report at `.joe-janitor/report-2026-06-24.md`)
found a **cross-session duplication** pattern — many independent agent sessions each solving the
same sub-problem locally instead of reaching for a shared primitive — in two determinism-adjacent
clusters: canonical-JSON/content-hash (6+ sites) and retry/backoff (7+ sites).

## Revised scope (2026-06-25, post-brainstorm — supersedes the original framing below)

A grounded brainstorm + adversarial digest trace (recorded as comments on this epic) **revised the
original premise**: there is **no live cross-clone determinism bug**. Each digest is produced by a
single encoder for a single purpose and is never compared against a *different* encoder's output;
sign/verify and plan/apply both run the same code version, so every domain is self-consistent. The
one persisted-and-recompared site (`signing.py`) already uses the proposed canonical kwargs, so it
migrates **byte-identically**. Therefore this epic is a **pure DRY / maintainability consolidation**,
and the governing rule is **freeze every site's output bytes** (changing any digest is the only way
to introduce a regression). Two original citations were also corrected: `_store/canonical.py` is the
live serialization home (6 importers + a byte-parity contract), **not** "imported by nobody"; and
`orchestrator.py:688-689` contains **no** canonical-JSON code (stale citation, dropped).

The retry cluster is **right-sized rather than universally consolidated**: only the one genuine
in-file duplication is unified; sites that solve genuinely different problems are left bespoke (no
universal `retry()` framework — that was judged over-generalization).

## Scope

In scope:
- **Cluster 1 (canonical-JSON/hash):** make `_store/canonical.py` the single seam — extend it with
  backward-compatible `canonical_str(doc, *, ascii_only=False, default=None)` + `content_hash(...)`,
  migrate the real digest/serialization sites (`signing.py`, `llm/workflow/schema.py`,
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/conflict_resolver.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/mutation.py`) onto it,
  delete the local copies, and **preserve each site's exact output bytes** (every retained variant is
  an explicit, justified parameter — `ascii_only=True` for `mutation.py`, `default=str` for
  `conflict_resolver.py` — with a cited consumer).
- **Cluster 2 (retry/backoff), right-sized:** unify only the two near-identical `_advisory_lock`
  backoff functions (`_compute_backoff_seconds` + `_cas_backoff_seconds` — same `base·factor^n`
  capped + ±jitter formula, differing only in constants) into one parameterized pure function,
  preserving both budgets' constants and behavior.
- Characterization tests that **prove output bytes are unchanged** across the migrated canonical
  sites (incl. non-ASCII / nested / unicode-key inputs) and that signing verify round-trips
  unchanged; the existing advisory-lock jitter test continues to pin the unified backoff.

Out of scope (intentionally left bespoke / deferred):
- A universal `retry(...)` helper or a new `src/rebar/_retry.py` leaf module — **rejected** as
  over-generalization of genuinely different problems.
- The other retry sites stay as-is, each with a one-line rationale: `push.py` (git merge-CAS loop,
  no sleep-backoff), `jira-capability-probe.py` (polls on an *empty result* — eventual consistency,
  not exception retry), `runner.py`/`structured.py` (stateful prompt-feedback retry), and the
  intentionally distinct `acli_subprocess` / `acli_rest` transient-fault *policies*.
- Any change to the wire format / value of any existing signature or digest (this is behavior-
  preserving; `mutation.py`'s `ensure_ascii=True` is **preserved**, not "fixed").
- A third-party retry lib (`tenacity`) — keep core deps tiny.
- The other audit findings (jsonschema dep, file-size splits) — tracked separately.

## Plan (child tickets)

- **Child 1 — Cluster 1 (canonical-JSON/hash consolidation).** Extend `_store/canonical.py` with the
  documented one-true-encoding + `content_hash`; migrate the 4 real sites byte-identically; add the
  characterization + signing-round-trip tests.
- **Child 2 — Cluster 2 (advisory-lock backoff unify).** Collapse the two `_advisory_lock` backoff
  functions into one parameterized pure function; keep the two retry budgets as config; preserve
  behavior under the existing jitter test.

## Child tickets (delivered)

Both child tickets were created, **parented to this epic** (via `parent_id`, the containment
hierarchy — not a `deps` edge, so this epic's `deps` is correctly empty), and each passed the
plan-review and completion-verification gates with an HMAC-signed PASS verdict:

- **Cluster 1** — `blunt-tramp-kale` (`1c66-6644-4dfb-4afa`): consolidate canonical-JSON/content-hash
  onto the `_store/canonical.py` seam (byte-preserving). Status: **closed**; completion-verifier:
  **PASS** (signed @ commit `756a88a2`). Has its own AC + file-impact + verify-commands.
- **Cluster 2** — `snag-reek-ember` (`325a-8036-2069-4ed4`): unify the two `_advisory_lock` backoff
  functions into one parameterized helper. Status: **closed**; completion-verifier: **PASS** (signed
  @ commit `1e701b46`). Has its own AC + file-impact + verify-commands.

Both shipped in PR #21 (navapbc/rebar), merged to `main` 2026-06-25.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_store/canonical.py` is the single seam for "sorted-key compact JSON (+ sha256)": it exposes
      `canonical_str`/`canonical_bytes` (extended with `ascii_only` / `default` keyword params,
      defaults reproducing today's bytes) and `content_hash`; the real sites (`signing.py`,
      `llm/workflow/schema.py`, `conflict_resolver.py`, `mutation.py`) import it and their local
      reimplementations are deleted. (`schema.py`'s public `canonical_json`/`content_hash` names are
      preserved as re-exports/delegators.)
- [ ] The one true encoding (`ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":")`) is
      documented, and every retained variant is an explicit, justified parameter with a cited
      consumer: `ascii_only=True` for `mutation.py`, `default=str` for `conflict_resolver.py`. No
      silent divergence remains.
- [ ] A characterization test proves every migrated caller's **output bytes are unchanged** vs the
      pre-refactor snapshot for a fixed input set incl. non-ASCII, nested, and unicode-key payloads;
      and signing sign→verify round-trips are unchanged. (No digest value changes — behavior-
      preserving DRY, per the no-live-bug analysis on this epic.)
- [ ] The two `_advisory_lock` backoff functions are unified into one parameterized pure function
      that preserves both budgets' constants and behavior (pinned by the existing jitter test). The
      other retry sites are left bespoke, each carrying a one-line documented rationale; **no**
      universal `retry()` helper or `_retry.py` module is introduced.
- [ ] `make lint` + the full test suite pass; no new module exceeds the 800-LOC soft cap; no new
      sub-100-LOC leaf module is created (the canonical seam stays in `_store/canonical.py`; the
      backoff unify stays in `_advisory_lock.py`).
- [ ] Two child tickets (Cluster 1; Cluster 2 backoff-unify) are created and parented to this epic,
      each with its own AC + file-impact, and each passes the plan-review and completion-verification
      gates.
- [ ] One tested home each for canonical-JSON/hash and the advisory-lock backoff formula; a future audit
- [ ] Behavior is provably preserved: a byte-equality characterization test guarantees no migrated
- [ ] Net LOC decreases (duplication removed) with zero wire-format/digest changes.

## Original framing (superseded — retained for provenance)

The original description asserted a live cross-clone determinism hazard and a full retry-helper
consolidation (child tickets A1–A4 + B1–B4, a new `src/rebar/_retry.py`, and a `mutation.py`
`ensure_ascii` drift "fix"). The post-brainstorm analysis above supersedes that: no live bug exists,
the encoding is frozen rather than normalized, and the retry work is narrowed to the single genuine
duplication. See the epic comments for the digest-by-digest BENIGN/HAZARD trace.
baseline.summary: Consolidate cross-session duplicated primitives (canonical-JSON/hash + retry/backoff)

content.text: ## Why
The MCP `run_workflow` docstring in `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` claims the run
"executes in the background so it survives client timeouts" and "Run-state
persists durably ... (resumable on crash)". The implementation is a
`threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True)` (around `_mcp_writes.py:297`). A
daemon thread does NOT survive process exit, and there is no reaper or
`workflow resume` entrypoint that re-drives an orphaned run — so if the MCP host
exits, the run is stranded at `running` forever. The docstring oversells a
durability guarantee the code does not provide. Since MCP tools are
model-controlled, that inaccuracy can mislead an agent into relying on
non-existent crash-durability.
## What
Correct the honesty of the durability wording (documentation only — the durable
runner itself is explicitly OUT of scope):
- Rewrite the `run_workflow` docstring to state true semantics: the background
work runs on a **daemon thread that does not survive MCP-process exit**; there
is **no automatic reaper**; step records are persisted with idempotency keys so
a run **can be resumed only if re-invoked**, but nothing auto-resumes it.
- Align any adjacent claims that imply automatic crash-resumption
(e.g. `llm/workflow/runs.py` "durable; resumable" phrasing) so they describe
the persistence substrate, not an automatic guarantee.
## Files
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` (the `run_workflow` docstring)
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` (align wording if it overstates)
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `run_workflow` docstring no longer implies the daemon thread survives
process exit or that runs auto-resume after a crash.
- [ ] It accurately states: daemon thread, no reaper, resume requires
re-invocation, step records are idempotent.
- [ ] Any adjacent "resumable on crash" wording is aligned to describe the
persistence substrate, not an automatic guarantee.
- [ ] No runtime/behavior change; `make lint` stays green.

baseline.summary: Fix run_workflow durability docstring to state true crash semantics
