## Summary

`tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py::test_push_loop_converges_under_contention` (added one commit ago by 4c4f, `f7aa0d5b5`) failed in CI on a change that provably cannot affect it, then the same test passed 18/18 locally on that same patch set.

Observed once so far: GitHub Actions run **30665788197** (Gerrit change 1134, patch set 1, `gerrit-verify`), worker `popen-gw1`, ubuntu-latest, py3.13, git 2.54.0.

## Evidence

Failure output:

```
rc=1
competitor pushes fired=1
stdout:
Local tickets branch is ahead by 1 commit(s) — pushing.
stderr:
Push failed (non-retryable, exit 1): To .../origin.git
 ! [rejected]        HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
```

That message is emitted at `reconcile-bridge.yml:321`, the ELSE arm of the classifier at `:314`:

```sh
if echo "$push_stderr" | grep -qiE 'non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first'; then
```

The stderr shown contains BOTH `rejected` and `fetch first`, so the classifier should have matched and taken the retry arm. It did not. On attempt 1 the competitor had already pushed (`competitor pushes fired=1`), so this is the ordinary benign-contention path the test exists to cover.

## What has been ruled out

- **Not caused by change 1134.** Its only in-loop edit is `:319`, inside the THEN arm —
  unreachable in a run that took the ELSE arm. Its other edit (the pre-loop fetch)
  demonstrably worked, since `:299` printed an ahead-count that requires `origin/tickets`
  to have resolved.
- **Not the classifier's pattern.** 20,000 iterations of the exact `grep -qiE` against the
  exact stderr text from the failing run, under `set -euo pipefail`, produced 0
  misclassifications — so a `pipefail`/SIGPIPE interaction on that pipeline is not
  reproducible at this payload size.
- **Not reproducible locally.** 18/18 passes on the failing patch set (10 serial, 8 under
  parallel load), macOS, git 2.55.0.

## Leads not yet tested

- Whether `push_stderr` was actually EMPTY at classification time and the text in the
  `:321` message came from a later expansion — i.e. `push_stderr=$(git push ... 2>&1)`
  losing its capture under load. This is the leading hypothesis and is untested.
- git 2.54.0 (CI) vs 2.55.0 (local) behavioural difference in what `git push` writes to
  stderr vs stdout under `2>&1` capture.
- CPU starvation on a loaded runner perturbing the competitor shim's 6-subprocess sequence.

## Why this matters

The test gates every change through `gerrit-verify`, so a flake here costs a full CI cycle per occurrence and trains reviewers to `recheck` reflexively. It also guards a real convergence property (bug 4c4f), so weakening or skipping it is not the answer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism is reproduced deterministically (e.g. under enforced CPU contention or
      git 2.54.0) rather than inferred.
- [ ] Root cause named at a specific changeable artifact — the workflow's stderr capture,
      the classifier, or the test harness's shim.
- [ ] Fixed without weakening the convergence assertions the test exists to make.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`.
baseline.summary: test_push_loop_converges_under_contention flakes in CI: push classified non-retryable on attempt 1

baseline.description:
## Dependencies (STACKED — read against the stack tip, not origin/main)
e165 builds directly on two ANCESTOR changes in this review stack that are NOT yet
merged to origin/main: **ddbe** (identity entity + the `rebar identity` `main()`
intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`) and **bde5** (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`
with `sign_authorship`/`verify_authorship`/`resolve_trust_root`). Both exist at
e165's implementation base (the stack tip). Review this plan with `--source local`
so those ancestors are visible; against origin/main alone they will (correctly)
appear absent.

## Context
Give an `identity`'s public keys a LIFECYCLE with cryptographic continuity:
a trust-on-first-use (TOFU) genesis key, and subsequent key add/rotate/revoke
changes that must each be signed by a currently-valid key of that identity (fills
git-bug's unimplemented `IsProtected`). A key's validity is scoped to its ERA —
its position in the authoritative MERGED event log — never to an attacker-set
event timestamp. Builds on ddbe (identity + `keys`) and bde5 (authorship
sign/verify via `rebar.authorship.v1`).

## Why
Without a signed rotation chain, anyone who can append a KEY event to an identity
could inject their own key and forge authorship. Anchoring validity to merged-log
position (not wall-clock) stops an attacker from backdating a forged event into a
revoked key's window.

## What
### 1. KEY lifecycle events on the identity (TAG_DELTA precedent)
Add key-management event types folded by the reducer into an era-scoped keyring:
- Event types (new constants in `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`, added to the
  known-event-type set; bump the reducer version so older clones
  preserve-and-ignore — see the TAG_DELTA v3 note): `KEY_ADD` and `KEY_REVOKE`
  (a rotate = a `KEY_REVOKE` of the old key + a `KEY_ADD` of the new, or a single
  `KEY_ADD` that supersedes; keep the two primitive events, model rotate as their
  composition).
- `KEY_ADD` data: `{public_key: <authorized-keys line>, signature: <DSSE envelope
  or null for genesis>}`. `KEY_REVOKE` data: `{public_key: <line>, signature:
  <DSSE envelope>}`.
- New reducer processor `process_key_event` (in `_processors.py`, dispatched from
  `_replay.py`) folds these into `state["keyring"]`: a list of
  `{public_key, added_epoch, revoked_epoch|null}` records, where `epoch` is the ordinal
  position (see §2). `state["keys"]` (from ddbe) becomes the DERIVED set of keys
  whose validity window contains the CURRENT (latest) epoch — i.e. currently-valid
  keys — so existing readers keep working.

  SEEDING + MIGRATION (required): (a) `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py`'s
  `make_initial_state()` must seed `keyring = []` and `keyring_epoch = 0` (as it
  seeds `managed_refs`/`claimed_session`), so a ticket that never had a KEY event
  has canonical zero-values, not absent keys. (b) BOOTSTRAP for identities created
  by ddbe: `process_create` for an `identity` whose CREATE carried a static `keys`
  list seeds an implicit GENESIS keyring — one `{public_key, added_epoch:0,
  revoked_epoch:null}` record per CREATE key (all genesis keys share epoch 0 — the
  genesis is ONE lifecycle step regardless of key count), and sets the cursor
  `keyring_epoch = 1` (epoch 0 consumed by genesis; the next real KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE
  gets epoch 1). So a pre-existing identity's `keys` are all valid from epoch 0 and
  `resolve_trust_root`/`verify_authorship` work with no explicit KEY event. An
  identity created with NO keys has an empty keyring and `keyring_epoch = 0` (genesis
  happens later, at the first KEY_ADD, which is then the TOFU epoch-0 step).

### 2. Era = a snapshot-safe keyring EPOCH counter (NOT event timestamp, NOT the raw replay loop index)
Maintain a monotonic `state["keyring_epoch"]` integer = the NEXT epoch to assign
(a cursor, not a per-key id). Each key-lifecycle STEP consumes one epoch: the
reducer records the change at the CURRENT `keyring_epoch`, THEN increments it by 1.
MULTIPLE keys may be valid at the same epoch (a keyring legitimately holds several
concurrently-valid keys); an epoch does not uniquely own one key — it is only a
validity-window boundary. A key added at epoch `a` and
revoked at epoch `r` is VALID for epochs in `[a, r)` (open at `r`: a key cannot
sign at/after its own revocation); a never-revoked key has `revoked_epoch = None`.

CRITICAL — snapshot safety (the raw replay loop index is WRONG): `replay_events()`
starts from the latest SNAPSHOT and skips pre-snapshot events, so the loop index is
NOT the absolute ordinal. Therefore: (a) `process_snapshot` FREEZES `keyring_epoch`
(and the full `keyring`) into the SNAPSHOT `compiled_state` and RESTORES them on
replay; (b) `process_key_event` increments the RESTORED `keyring_epoch` counter, not
any loop index. This keeps epochs stable across compaction.

Epoch is derived purely from the canonical fold ORDER (the reducer's HLC-filename
replay order — identical on every clone after sync, see reducer/_cache.py,
_processors.py:538), NEVER from the attacker-controllable `data`-level timestamp.

Canonical signed content of a KEY op (what the authorship signature covers): the
epoch is NOT signed (it is assigned at fold time). The signature covers
`canonical.canonical_str({"op": "KEY_ADD" | "KEY_REVOKE", "identity_id": <id>,
"public_key": <authorized-keys line>}).encode("utf-8")` (sorted-keys canonical
form from `rebar._store.canonical`). This binds a specific key operation to a
specific identity; the write-gate checks it was authorized by a currently-valid key
(the trust root at the latest epoch BEFORE this op).

### 3. Write-time refusal of unsigned/invalidly-signed KEY changes
A `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` after genesis is REFUSED (the write raises, no event is
appended) unless its `signature` is a valid `rebar.authorship.v1` authorship
envelope (bde5 `verify_authorship`) over the KEY event's canonical content,
produced by a key that is CURRENTLY valid for this identity (valid at the era
immediately preceding this change). The GENESIS `KEY_ADD` (the first key event for
an identity that has no keys yet) is TOFU: accepted WITHOUT a signature (nothing to
chain to). Surface this via a new command/library seam
`add_identity_key` / `revoke_identity_key` (CLI `rebar identity key add/revoke`)
that performs the signature check before appending.

### 4. Epoch-scoped authorship verification (extends bde5)
Add `verify_authorship_at_epoch(envelope, identity_id, epoch, *, repo_root=None) ->
Verdict`: resolve the identity's keyring, build the trust root from ONLY the keys
whose `[added_epoch, revoked_epoch)` window contains `epoch`, and verify. An event whose
signing key was revoked before the event's epoch fails; one within the key's valid
epoch passes. (`verify_authorship` from bde5 stays as the "current-era"
convenience.)

Epoch derivation for an arbitrary (non-KEY) event: the epoch that GOVERNS an
event's authorship is the number of the identity's KEY lifecycle events whose
canonical fold position precedes that event. Provide a helper
`epoch_for_position(identity_id, event_position, *, repo_root=None) -> int`.
It must be SNAPSHOT-AWARE (KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE are KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES and are folded
into the identity's SNAPSHOT by compact.py, whose files are then retired — so a
naive file scan under-counts). Compute it by folding the identity's keyring the same
way the reducer does — start from the latest SNAPSHOT's restored `keyring_epoch`
(the epoch as of compaction) and add only the POST-snapshot KEY events whose
canonical `{HLC-ts}-{uuid}` position precedes `event_position`. Equivalently: reduce
the identity's KEY history (SNAPSHOT base + live KEY events) truncated at
`event_position` and read the resulting `keyring_epoch`. Reuse the reducer's
snapshot-start logic (do not re-scan raw files independently). e165 defines this derivation + the
`verify_authorship_at_epoch` primitive (which takes the resolved epoch); WIRING it
into live event verification at the write/merge path is 3183's job. The AC tests
call `verify_authorship_at_epoch` with explicit epochs on a constructed keyring, so
the primitive is exercised independent of the derivation helper.

### 5. Write-path allowlist + CLI wiring (grounded consumer list)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`: `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` MUST be added to the
  hardcoded `EVENT_TYPES` frozenset (~line 50) or `_validate_event` raises
  a `StoreError` (invalid event_type; ~line 120) and the write seam fails before any
  event lands. Separate from the reducer known-type set in `_version.py` — BOTH need
  the new types (the TAG_DELTA precedent touched both).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py`: bump `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` so stale `.cache.json`
  files (which lack `keyring`/`keyring_epoch`) are invalidated.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py`: `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` must be placed in one of
  its orphan-type frozensets (`_AUTO_RECOVER_ORPHAN_TYPES` or
  `_HUMAN_TRIAGE_ORPHAN_TYPES`) — a test asserts these together cover every
  KNOWN_EVENT_TYPE except CREATE/SNAPSHOT. KEY events onto an identity are not
  orphans in the graph sense; classify them under human-triage (or a dedicated
  exempt path) so the coverage assertion holds.
- CLI `rebar identity key add|revoke`: extend the identity subcommand `main()`
  intercept in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (the seam ddbe used) — NOT the
  `_ARGV_REGISTRY`/`_WRITES_FULL` golden-file path (which would touch `tests/golden`).

## Scope
In: the KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE events + reducer keyring fold + epoch computation, the
signed-rotation write gate (add/revoke seam), TOFU genesis, and
`verify_authorship_at_epoch`. Out: auto-signing every normal event / the merge-gate
enforcement (3183), Jira mapping (264f/2f13). Key material lives in `keys` as
before; private keys are operator-held (signatures are produced out-of-band via the
bde5 signing seam).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE` on an identity that already has a genesis key is
  REFUSED unless accompanied by a valid authorship signature from a currently-valid
  key of that identity; a test asserts an UNSIGNED key-add is refused (raises / no
  event appended) while the genesis key-add (first key) is accepted TOFU.
- [ ] An event whose authorship envelope was produced by a key REVOKED at an
  earlier era fails `verify_authorship_at_epoch` for that event's epoch, while an event
  signed within the key's valid era PASSES (test builds a keyring with an add then
  a revoke and checks both sides of the boundary).
- [ ] Validity is computed from the keyring EPOCH (fold order), NOT the event's
  `data` timestamp: a test with a misleading/backdated `data` timestamp does NOT
  change which epoch (key set) governs it.
- [ ] Snapshot safety: an identity whose keyring events are COMPACTED into a
  SNAPSHOT reduces to the SAME keyring + `keyring_epoch` as the uncompacted log,
  and a KEY event ADDED AFTER the snapshot gets the correct next epoch (a test
  compacts then adds a key and asserts the epoch is contiguous, not reset).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` (KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE constants + version bump + known-type set)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (process_key_event: fold keyring + epoch counter + derive current keys; process_snapshot freezes/restores keyring+keyring_epoch)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` (dispatch KEY events)
- `src/rebar/attest/authorship.py` (verify_authorship_at_epoch + era-scoped trust root)
- `src/rebar/_commands/identity.py` (add_identity_key/revoke_identity_key seam with the signed-rotation write gate; CLI wiring)
baseline.summary: identity: TOFU genesis + G2 signed key-rotation chain + era-scoped validity

## Why
CLAUDE.md's 'Gate protocols (MANDATORY)' section (CLAUDE.md:112-121) instructs agents that even on a PASS they 'must remediate all valid advisory findings before continuing'. Field data: ~13 advisories/round, 95% of remediation edits mint new findings, and the mandated loop drove the 4+-round tail that consumed 60% of gate compute. With the convergence floors now default-ON (change 562) the operator wants to LOOSEN this guidance — NOT replace it with guidance to ignore advisories — and observe whether agents implement advisories properly on their own judgment.

## What
- Edit CLAUDE.md's plan-review protocol paragraph (~lines 118-120): remove the MUST-remediate-all-valid-advisories mandate. Replace with neutral judgment framing, e.g.: review the advisory findings and coaching notes; apply the ones that genuinely improve the plan; a blocking verdict must still be remediated and re-reviewed. Do NOT add language discouraging advisory uptake.
- Sweep for echoes of the mandate across ALL agent-facing docs — `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, AND `examples/` (the committed skill copies). There are TWO genuine echoes, both softened to the same judgment framing ('apply the advisory findings that genuinely improve the plan') while KEEPING their BLOCK-must-remediate / re-run-until-pass instruction: (1) `examples/claude-skills/rebar-implement/SKILL.md:136` ('remediate every valid finding'); (2) `examples/claude-skills/rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md:135` ('remediate findings before claiming' — an unqualified all-findings mandate). EXPLICIT non-echoes left untouched: the `rebar-janitor` skill's 'Remediation Plan' phase (a different concept — proposing code-debt fixes, not advisory-finding remediation), and `rebar-implement/SKILL.md:254` ('on FAIL, remediate and retry') which is the COMPLETION-verifier close gate (stays mandatory). The completion-verifier protocol paragraph stays UNCHANGED. The 'Sign on every round' and BLOCK-must-remediate guidance stays verbatim.
- The observation plan (compare advisory-uptake rate and rounds-to-pass before/after via REVIEW_RESULT sidecars — `norm_id` survival across rounds = an advisory was addressed) is recorded on the parent epic's measurement-framework AC (epic 9d50 AC2), not duplicated here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The mandate is GONE and the replacement framing is judgment-based. Two-sided proof: (negative) `grep -niE "remediate all valid advisory|must remediate all valid" CLAUDE.md` returns NOTHING; (positive) `grep -n "apply the ones that genuinely improve the plan" CLAUDE.md` returns the new sentence AND `grep -n "not a mandate to remediate every advisory" CLAUDE.md` returns the clause that explicitly frames uptake as a judgment call (not discouragement).
- [ ] BLOCK-remediation and sign-every-round guidance are unchanged (present-phrase proof): `grep -n "you must \*\*remediate the failure" CLAUDE.md` still shows the blocking-verdict-must-be-remediated clause, and `grep -n "Sign on every round" CLAUDE.md` still returns the verbatim paragraph.
- [ ] No other agent-facing doc still states the mandatory-advisory-remediation rule, and BOTH known echoes are softened to judgment framing. Two-sided proof over `CLAUDE.md docs/ CONTRIBUTING.md examples/`: (negative) `grep -rniE "remediate every valid finding|remediate all valid advisor|remediate findings before claiming" <those paths>` returns NOTHING; (positive) `grep -rn "apply the advisory findings that genuinely improve the plan" examples/claude-skills/` returns the softened lines in BOTH rebar-implement/SKILL.md and rebar-brainstorm/SKILL.md, each still retaining its BLOCK-remediation instruction. (The `rebar-janitor` 'Remediation Plan' phase and rebar-implement's completion-verifier line 254 are deliberately untouched.)
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.
- [ ] make test passes on the change.
baseline.summary: Loosen the mandatory advisory-remediation guidance in CLAUDE.md (observe organic advisory uptake)

baseline.description:
# Event-sourced enrichment queue: cert-triggered enqueue, 60-min soak, latest-wins, lock-guarded claim

## Why
Enrichment must be async and off the hot write path. rebar's event store is already a durable, shared, serialized-write queue substrate — better than a bolted-on SQLite/broker (which cannot live on a shared path nor be visible to all clients). Modeling the queue as sidecar events makes "a new certification replaces the old entry" the natural latest-wins reduce.

## What
Three sidecar events keyed by `ticket_id`, reduced to queue state:
- `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` `{ticket_id, not_before_ns}` appended on plan-review CERTIFICATION, `not_before_ns = cert + SOAK` (SOAK default 60 min). A re-cert appends a new one that supersedes the prior (latest-wins by HLC) and bumps `not_before_ns` — the soak/debounce as a stored timestamp filtered at drain, NOT an in-process timer.
- `CLAIM_ENRICH` `{ticket_id, drainer_id, lease_expires_ns}`, `DONE_ENRICH` `{ticket_id}`.
- Reducer `pending_enrichment(now_ns)` → entries past soak, unclaimed-or-lease-expired, with no later DONE.

## Atomicity + claim (accurate to the store's ACTUAL locking model — DERISKED)
`append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py`) SELF-SERIALIZES every write: it goes through
`stage_and_commit`, which acquires the store write lock (`_store/lock.py::write_lock`) for its
own append. So a claim CANNOT hold `lock.acquire` across its own `append_event` — the
non-reentrant mkdir leg of the lock would deadlock/timeout. The claim primitive is therefore
OPTIMISTIC (the epic's stated model: "one drainer lands, losers retry"), not a held-lock
read-check-append.
- **Enqueue placement (no false atomicity):** `sign_plan_review` writes the SIGNATURE via `sign_manifest`→`append_event`, which takes its OWN per-event lock; there is no shared held-lock spanning cert+enqueue, and refactoring the signing path to provide one is out of scope. So `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` is a SEPARATE append immediately after `sign_plan_review` returns. Correctness does NOT depend on atomicity: the S4 drain's self-healing fallback treats any certified ticket with an absent/stale digest as enqueable, so a crash between cert and ENQUEUE cannot permanently miss it.
- **Race-free claim (OPTIMISTIC append + arbitration):** the drainer re-reduces the ticket's queue state and, only if still pending (unclaimed or lease-expired), appends `CLAIM_ENRICH` (with a fresh `lease_expires_ns`) via `append_event` (which self-serializes under the store write lock). It then ARBITRATES: among the `CLAIM_ENRICH` events after the latest `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` whose lease is STILL LIVE, the earliest `(timestamp, uuid)` wins. THIS drainer won iff it is that earliest live claim; losers re-read and pick another. Filtering contenders by live lease is what makes lease expiry self-healing (an expired prior claim is not a contender). Exactly one drainer lands per soak window.
Lease `LEASE_TTL` (default 15 min); a claim with `lease_expires_ns < now` is treated as unclaimed on the next drain (self-healing, no separate reaper process). Defense-in-depth fallback (owned/implemented by the S4 drain, see below): the drain ALSO treats a ticket that is certified but whose digest is absent/stale as implicitly enqueable, so even a crash between cert and ENQUEUE cannot permanently miss it.

## Scope (exact edit targets)
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` `EVENT_TYPES` (+ StoreError message): add the three types. `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py`: add to `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` (sidecar; like REVIEW_RESULT/TICKET_DIGEST).
- Enqueue hook in the `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` certification path (`attest.sign_plan_review`, best-effort after the SIGNATURE append), using the HLC clock (`hlc.physical_now()`) for `not_before_ns`. No held-lock cert-critical-section (the enqueue is a separate append; correctness rests on the self-healing fallback, not atomicity).
- Config field target `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: `overlap_soak_min` (60), `overlap_lease_ttl_min` (15) on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`, `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_*`) — LLM-feature tunables, not `VerifyConfig`.
- This story owns ENQUEUE + CLAIM + the reducer. It does NOT own DONE-emission, the growth-bound retention, or the self-healing scan — those require the drain runner and are OWNED BY S4 (leggy-heedless-mosquito).

## Dependencies
S2 (wispy-cheerless-tick) for the digest freshness the enqueue/drain consult. S4 owns the drain that appends DONE + runs the fallback scan.

## Testing
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py`: `test_enqueue_and_recert` (not_before = cert+SOAK; re-cert supersedes+bumps); `test_soak_and_latest_wins` (pending honors soak + ≤1/ticket); `test_claim_race` (two claimers in one critical section → exactly one CLAIM lands); `test_lease_reclaim` (expired lease reclaimable, idempotent).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Certifying appends `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` with `not_before_ns = cert + SOAK` (a separate append after `sign_plan_review`); re-cert supersedes+bumps; `pytest ...::test_enqueue_and_recert`. A crash between cert and enqueue is recovered by the S4 self-healing scan (no permanent miss).
- [ ] `pending_enrichment(now)` returns only past-soak, unclaimed-or-expired, ≤1/ticket; `::test_soak_and_latest_wins`.
- [ ] Two concurrent claimers → exactly one wins via optimistic append + earliest-live-lease arbitration; the loser re-reads and picks another; `::test_claim_one_winner`.
- [ ] Lease-expired claim reclaimable on next drain (self-healing); re-processing idempotent; `::test_lease_reclaim`.
- [ ] The three event types are in `EVENT_TYPES` + `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES`. (DONE-emission, growth-bound, and the self-healing scan are S4's ACs, not this story's.)
baseline.summary: Event-sourced enrichment queue: cert-triggered enqueue, 60-min soak, latest-wins, optimistic claim

Benchmark config resolution and prove it is fast + bounded + cached.

content.text: # T3 — NDJSON import core: rebar import / rebar.import_tickets() (two-pass, composed events)
## Context
P1.2 epic rule-swamp-pupil (ab74-b205-72af-4ce1). Consume our own NDJSON and reproduce the
same logical state in a fresh repo via the NORMAL locked write path (no raw-event
injection). Depends on T1 (provenance plumbing) and T2 (NDJSON format + schema to consume).
Idempotency + deferred-push perf are split into T4; this ticket delivers a correct working
importer (re-runs may duplicate — that gap is closed by T4 and documented here).
## What
- New `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`, `src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py`.
- `rebar.import_tickets(...)` library fn + `rebar import` CLI (dispatch in
`_cli/__init__.py`, help `_cli/help/import.txt`, `--dry-run`, `--output`).
- Two-pass:
- Pass 1: `create_ticket(type, title, description, priority, tags, assignee)` for every
line (do NOT set parent in CREATE — parent must be open/in_progress); capture
`{source_id → new local_id}` id-map. Pass source_* (T1) into the CREATE.
- Pass 2 (per ticket): `edit_ticket(parent=…)`; `link(…)` (dedup by
`(source,target,relation)`); `transition(open→in_progress|closed)` to reproduce non-open
STATUS; `comment(…)` with per-comment source fields; `set_file_impact`/`set_verify_commands`.
- Dangling parent/link target not in the import set → skip + warn (never fail the run).
- `_provenance.py` maps export line → create/comment kwargs (source_* extraction).
## Scope
In: correct two-pass importer + STATUS reproduction + dry-run + dangling skip. Out:
idempotent skip-by-source_id, deferred-push perf, large-import docs (all T4).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Round-trip: `export` a store then `import` into a fresh repo reproduces the same
logical state (status, assignee, parent, links, tags, comments, file_impact,
verify_commands) modulo fresh ids, with original date/author preserved as `source_*`.
- [ ] Non-open statuses (closed/in_progress) reproduced via STATUS events.
- [ ] Provenance surfaced on imported tickets/comments (source_id/created_at/author/env).
- [ ] Dangling parent/link target → skipped with a warning; run still succeeds.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports create counts without writing.
- [ ] Tests: round-trip ≡ logical state, status reproduction, provenance surfacing,
dangling-link skip, dry-run; `pytest` green.

baseline.description:
Harden `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` against disk exhaustion from repeated failed rebuilds (incident 2731: 41h of per-main-advance rebuild attempts accumulated multi-GB buildkit cache + dangling layers on the 30G root disk until pip/clone ENOSPC fail-closed the LLM-Review gate). Today `docker image prune -f` runs ONLY on the success path (line 166) and nothing ever prunes the buildkit build cache on either path — a failing deploy loop is exactly when garbage accumulates fastest and is exactly the path with no reclamation.

## What (pinned design — no alternatives left to the executor)
- Add one helper `prune_docker_caches()` in autodeploy.sh that runs, best-effort:
  1. `docker builder prune -f --keep-storage "${BUILD_CACHE_KEEP:-5GB}"` — a HARD storage cap on the buildkit cache (quantified bound; `--filter until=…` was rejected as time-based and unbounded under a tight failure loop). `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP` joins the existing tunables block (overridable via /etc/rebar/autodeploy.env).
  2. `docker image prune -f` — dangling images from failed/superseded builds.
  Both invocations discard stdout and `|| true`: a prune failure must NEVER mask the deploy-failure exit code or alter control flow (same idiom as the existing success-path prune). But it is not fully silent: on a prune non-zero exit the helper emits one `log "prune_docker_caches: ... failed (non-fatal)"` journald line, so a persistently failing prune is visible in the unit journal rather than invisibly leaving the disk-pressure defect live.
- Flag verification (DONE, pre-plan): probed the deploy box via SSM on 2026-07-10 — `docker builder prune --help` on Docker 25.0.14 (build 0bab007) documents `--keep-storage bytes   Amount of disk space to keep for cache`. The flag is confirmed on the exact engine that runs this script.
- Each prune invocation is wrapped in `timeout 120` (a slow/wedged daemon under the very disk pressure this targets must not hold the deploy lock indefinitely; 120s is generous for a prune).
- Call `prune_docker_caches` from `record_backoff_failure()` — the single seam every failure exit already goes through (build fail, health-check rollback, checkout/rsync fail) — so every failed attempt reclaims before backing off.
- Replace the success path's bare `docker image prune -f` with the same helper, so the buildkit cache is also capped on success (the incident's cache accumulated across BOTH outcomes; keeping ≤5GB warm cache preserves rebuild speed).
- Note: on the health-check-rollback path the freshly built image is TAGGED (`:latest` re-tagged from `:prev` after rollback leaves the bad build's layers referenced by nothing after the next successful build); the `--keep-storage` builder cap plus dangling-image prune is the bounded, safe reclamation — we deliberately do NOT delete tagged images (`:prev` is the rollback lifeline).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 (failure path prunes): with `docker` stubbed by a PATH-front shim that logs argv and exits per-scenario, driving `record_backoff_failure` records exactly one `builder prune -f --keep-storage 5GB` and one `image prune -f` invocation, and the function still writes the backoff file with the original fail count. Harness: a NEW CI-run pytest module `tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` that sources the helper functions from autodeploy.sh in a bash subprocess with a tmp-dir PATH-front `docker` (and `timeout`) shim logging argv; invocation: `pytest tests/unit/test_autodeploy_prune.py` (runs in `make test`, so CI itself is the proof).
- [ ] AC2 (prune failure is inert): with the stub forcing both prune commands to exit 1, `record_backoff_failure` still records the backoff and the helper returns 0 (prune can never mask the deploy failure), AND the helper emits the `prune_docker_caches: … failed (non-fatal)` log line (asserted on captured output) — same pytest module as AC1.
- [ ] AC3 (bounded growth, quantified): the buildkit cache bound is the `--keep-storage` value (default 5GB, tunable via `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP`); proving commands (both must pass): `grep -q 'docker builder prune' infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (the capped prune exists) AND `! grep 'docker builder prune' infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh | grep -qv 'keep-storage'` (no uncapped builder prune exists) — asserted inside the AC1 pytest module so an absent call cannot false-pass.
- [ ] AC4 (syntax + config-check): `bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` passes and `make config-check` stays green (check 4 covers script syntax).
- [ ] AC5 (success path uses the helper): the success path calls `prune_docker_caches` and contains no remaining bare `docker image prune` outside the helper; proving command: `grep -c 'docker image prune' infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` returns 1 (the helper's single occurrence) and the AC1 stub harness driven through the success path records the same two prune invocations.
baseline.summary: autodeploy: prune docker build cache on the failure path (disk-pressure hardening)

Add a "last N session logs" capability reachable identically from the library,
the CLI, and an MCP tool, ordered by creation time.

## Why

Agents need a fast way to pull up recent session logs without scanning the whole
store. The requirement is "list the last 5 session logs" from all three
interfaces; rebar's shared read impl means one library function auto-flows to CLI
and MCP.

## What

  `limit` (default 5).
- Add the library wrapper in `src/rebar/_reads.py` and export it from
  `src/rebar/__init__.py`.
- Add the CLI subcommand `rebar session-logs [--limit N]` (register in

- Add the MCP tool (e.g. `recent_session_logs`) in `src/rebar/mcp_server.py` with a
  documented `outputSchema` under `src/rebar/schemas/`.

## Scope

The recent-logs read surface only. Depends on the type existing (foundation) and
on visibility rules (performance isolation).

      tickets, newest first.

baseline.description:
# Claim-gate <-> plan-review ref-resolution coherence (shared boundary, ADR 0002)

## Why

Plan-review binds the `file_impact` `{path:hash}` map AT the pinned SHA (ADR 0002); the
claim-gate freshness re-check must hash those paths at the SAME ref basis. If the two gates
resolve the ref independently (two hash sites), they can diverge (whole-HEAD vs pinned-SHA),
re-introducing the staleness false-positive ADR 0002 set out to prevent. Split from the
attested-signing pin so each is a thin, independently-reviewable slice.

## What

- Introduce ONE shared ref-resolution boundary consumed by BOTH the signing/plan-review gate
  and the claim-gate freshness re-check — not two independently-coded resolution sites.
- Update ADR 0002 to record the consolidation (and the manifest-channel binding cross-ref).
- Rule-of-Three / YAGNI check: there are exactly two consumers today (plan-review hashing +
  claim-gate re-check); the consolidation is justified by the divergence risk above and is
  de-risked by an explicit back-out.
- Back-out: the shared boundary is reversible to the prior per-site resolution (a flag/revert),
  stated explicitly.

## Scope

- In: the shared ref-resolution boundary, the claim-gate freshness re-check wired through it,
  ADR 0002 update, the back-out path.
- Out: the attested-signing manifest pin (sibling story); snapshot/cache (S1/S2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Plan-review `file_impact` hashing and the claim-gate freshness re-check resolve the ref
      through ONE shared boundary (same pinned-SHA basis) — not two hash sites.
- [ ] A negative test asserts both gates hash at the SAME ref (guards whole-HEAD divergence),
      asserting the behavioral contract rather than snapshotting current output.
- [ ] ADR 0002 is updated to record the shared-resolution consolidation.
- [ ] The consolidation has a documented back-out to the prior per-site resolution (reversible).
baseline.summary: Claim-gate <-> plan-review ref-resolution coherence (shared boundary, ADR 0002)

baseline.description:
# Jira Server / Data Center support via a Jira-family seam (not a forked second adapter)

## Context / Problem

CMS and similar federal clients run **self-hosted Jira Data Center**, which rebar cannot reconcile against. DC differs from Cloud on three axes: REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF, Personal Access Token bearer auth instead of the ACLI subprocess, and name-based user identity instead of `accountId`.

GitHub PR #120 proposed a second adapter package for this. It rides ADR 0035's `Backend` port correctly, but it reaches into `adapters/jira/` privates (`_map_local_to_jira_fields`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS`, `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY`, `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `classify_probe_response`) and forks `map_fields_to_remote` as a verbatim copy of `adapters/jira/backend.py:42-72` with one line changed. That creates a de facto "Jira family" layer with no contract: `adapters/jira/` becomes simultaneously a concrete backend and a shared library, with nothing pinning what is shared and nothing stopping a Cloud change from breaking DC.

## Approach

Make the Jira family an **explicit sub-seam** rather than an accident, in an order that never puts the live-validated Cloud path at risk.

1. **Freeze Cloud first.** Extend the existing held-out characterization tests
   (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`) to pin the current outputs of every unit
   about to move, so any behavior change during extraction fails a pinned oracle.
2. **Extract a `adapters/jira_family/` shared layer** — and re-point the Cloud adapter at it. Cloud's ACLI
   transport is not touched at all.

   **Only non-location-pinned symbols may physically move.** ADR 0035 §(a) pins `adf.py`,
   `outbound_fields.py`, and `comment_limits.py` as **Jira-coupled *and* location-pinned**: they are loaded by
   filename relative to `_PACKAGE_DIR` (via `_loader.lazy_load(` / `_load_sibling_keyed(` /
   `spec_from_file_location(`), so physically moving them breaks the dynamic loader unless the loader is taught
   the new sub-package in the same change — deferred to ADR 0035's Phase 2, explicitly **out of scope here**.
   **Location-pinned means "cannot change path" — NOT "cannot be edited."** Editing a pinned module's
   *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe and is how the pinned units get
   single-sourced; only *relocating* the file breaks the loader.

   **Move by SYMBOL, not by file.** `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` cannot relocate wholesale: it imports
   `fit_text_to_adf_limit` from the pinned `adf.py` (used by `_sanitize_description`) and
   `truncate_comment_body` / `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` from the pinned `comment_limits.py` (used by
   `_sanitize_comment`). Moving the whole file would point `jira_family/` at `adapters/jira/` — the exact
   dependency inversion the import contract in §6 forbids. So the file is split by symbol, and the two coupled
   sanitizers are **parameterized by the contracts this epic already introduces** rather than importing a
   vendor module: `_sanitize_description` takes the `RichTextCodec` (its `fit_text_to_adf_limit` call *is* the
   rich-text seam), and comment truncation takes the vendor's comment-limit/truncation contract. Cloud
   constructs those contract objects in `adapters/jira/` from its pinned `adf.py` / `comment_limits.py`; DC
   constructs wiki-markup/plain-text equivalents. `jira_family/` imports neither.

   Concretely, of the six symbols PR #120 reached for:
   - **Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic:** `_sanitize_label`, `_sanitize_summary`, `InvalidLabelError`,
     and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` (all in `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`, not location-pinned and not
     ADF/limit-coupled), `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned), and the new
     `RichTextCodec` / `UserIdentityModel` contract objects.
   - **Moves to `jira_family/` only in contract-parameterized form:** `_sanitize_description` and
     `_sanitize_comment` — same observable behavior, but the ADF/limit dependency arrives as an injected
     contract instead of a direct import of a pinned module.

   - **Stays put (path-wise):** `_map_local_to_jira_fields` in the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`,
     and the ADF encoder in the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. These are shared **by dependency-inverting
     instead of moving**: the pinned module is parameterized by the `jira_family` contracts (it imports *from*
     `jira_family/`, never the reverse), so DC reuses one implementation without any file relocating and
     without the loader changing. Any story that would *move* a pinned file must instead stop and record the
     blocker.

   One more unit needs parameterizing rather than sharing verbatim: `classify_probe_response` hardcodes
   `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`. Those are Cloud/DIG workflow state
   names; a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything. So the classifier moves to
   `jira_family/` taking the resolved-status set **as a parameter**, with Cloud passing today's frozenset
   (pinned unchanged by J1's oracle) and DC passing its own configured set. Sharing it with the Cloud names
   baked in would silently misclassify a DC issue as `PRESENT_FILTERED` when it is in fact resolved.
   The DC set is **operator-configured** via a `reconciler.resolved_statuses` config key (a list of workflow
   state names), defaulting to the same `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` when unset so an operator whose workflow
   uses the conventional names configures nothing. Cloud continues to pass its own frozenset, so Cloud is not
   made configurable by this change.

   **The value maps are a special case — they are ALREADY duplicated, and this epic must not preserve the
   duplication.** There are today **three** independently-referenced copies of the local→Jira status map (and
   two of the priority map):
   - `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py`: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` / `_LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` — read **only** by the
     ACLI transport (`acli.py:69-70,143,171`; `acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354`).
   - `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (pinned): `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` / `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_PRIORITY` — read by
     the `Backend` port via `backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote`.
   - `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`: `local_to_jira_status` — the engine-level config copy.

   They have **already drifted**: `outbound_fields` and `config.py` both carry a `"deleted": "Done"` entry the
   `jira_fields` copy lacks. So simply moving the `jira_fields` copy to `jira_family/` would leave Cloud's
   backend still reading a second copy — the exact "two places" the epic exists to eliminate. This epic
   consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15` (its call sites are
   engine-level config, a wider blast radius than this epic's seam).

   **Resolution: `adapters/jira_family/` holds the ONE definition of each value map. Both current copies are
   deleted and replaced by imports from it** — `jira_fields.py` (whose map literals move out, the file itself
   staying put for its ADF/limit-coupled sanitizers) and `outbound_fields.py` (pinned, so it stays at its path
   but its dict literals become an import). After this,
   grep finds exactly one dict literal per map, reachable from the ACLI transport, the Cloud backend port, and
   the DC backend alike.

   The `deleted`-key drift **must be decided in J2**, because a single unified dict cannot preserve two
   callers that currently disagree. J2 adopts `"deleted": "Done"` — the value **two of the three** existing
   copies already use (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`).
   The ACLI-side omission produces `"Deleted"` via a `.title()` fallback, which is not a state in the live DIG
   workflow, so Jira would reject that transition: a latent bug, not behavior to preserve. This is the one
   declared observable change in an otherwise behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by its own test. Bug
   `fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61` (`controlled-ornate-honeybee`) keeps the remainder: the missing ACLI-side
   characterization pins and folding `config.py`'s third copy into the single definition.
3. **Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts**: a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for
   DC) and a `UserIdentityModel` (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing
   behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.
4. **DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library**, gated behind a `[jira-datacenter]`
   extra and imported lazily, so the engine's `dependencies = []` contract and the battle-tested Cloud path are
   both untouched.
5. **Verify against a real Jira.** Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026, so the oracle
   is the Jira 8.17.1 test instance the pycontribs/jira project uses, reachable at
   `http://localhost:2990/jira` — the same substrate that project validates itself against.

   **It is BUILT, not pulled — corrected against the registry.** An earlier version of this step said to
   `docker run -dit -p 2990:2990 pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1` and called it a pinned *pullable* image.
   That is false: `docker pull` returns "repository does not exist", the Docker Hub API returns
   `object not found`, and the `pycontribs` namespace publishes only seven OS base images. The tag is a LOCAL
   BUILD NAME — pycontribs/jira ships `docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile` and its README's own instruction is
   `docker build -t pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 docker/jira-test-image`. Its base,
   `addono/jira-software-standalone`, IS pullable and the digest pycontribs pins resolves. J5
   [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] therefore vendors a small Dockerfile pinned to that base digest; the mechanism
   and its three load-bearing details (`-DskipAllPrompts=true`, the TTY requirement, 8.x-only) live there.

   Two consequences worth recording at epic level because they shape what this oracle can promise: the image
   does NOT contain Jira — `atlas-run` downloads it from `maven.atlassian.com` at first start, so egress to
   Atlassian is a hard runtime dependency and **pinning the image digest does not pin Jira itself** — and the
   base is `linux/amd64`, so an arm64 runner emulates it and starts far slower than upstream's quoted 3-5
   minutes. Jira 8.17.1 is ≥ 8.14, the release that introduced Personal Access Tokens, so PAT
   bearer auth is exercised for real. J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] owns the harness and records the
   version-drift limitation (8.17.1 is older than a client such as CMS is likely running, so it proves REST v2
   protocol semantics, not deployment-specific workflow/field/permission behavior — tracked separately as
   `9895-ac7d-4276-4f08`).
6. **Keep the new boundary structurally enforced, not conventional.** The drift this epic exists to prevent can
   recur the moment a contributor adds Cloud-specific logic to the shared layer. So the seam ships with a
   machine-checked import contract (an `import-linter` contract in `pyproject.toml`, or an equivalent CI grep
   check): only `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` may import `adapters/jira_family/`, and
   `jira_family/` may import neither of them.
7. **Security posture for the DC connection.** Self-hosted DC is frequently served over plain HTTP inside
   corporate networks, which would put ticket bodies and the PAT on the wire in cleartext. The DC backend
   therefore **requires `https`** for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit
   `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning). Operator docs state the least-privilege
   expectation: a **dedicated service account** whose PAT is scoped to only the projects rebar reconciles
   (Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues on those projects), never an
   admin-level token.

   **The PAT is env-only, never file-config.** Like Cloud's `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, the DC PAT is read from a
   `JIRA_PAT` environment variable and is NOT accepted from `[tool.rebar.jira]` in a committed config file, so
   the credential cannot be checked into a repo by accident. The DC transport never logs the token, and a
   missing `JIRA_PAT` raises a config error naming the variable rather than falling back to anonymous access.

   **Certificate verification stays ON.** Self-hosted DC commonly presents a self-signed or internal-CA
   certificate, and the tempting fix — disabling verification — turns the `https` requirement into theatre. So
   the DC transport never sets `verify=False`: an operator with an internal CA points rebar at their CA bundle
   (a `ca_bundle` config key / the standard `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var honoured by the underlying client), and
   a verification failure surfaces as a clear error naming the CA-bundle setting rather than being silently
   downgraded. `allow_insecure` governs the URL *scheme* only; it does NOT relax certificate checking.

   **The J5 harness is the intended `allow_insecure` case, not an exception to it.** The Dockerized Jira serves
   plain `http://localhost:2990/jira`, so every live test against it sets `allow_insecure = true` explicitly and
   asserts the warning is emitted. That is deliberate: it means the loopback-only test path exercises the
   override rather than bypassing the validator, and the validator's reject-by-default branch is covered by a
   unit test with a non-loopback `http://` URL. The override is **not** narrowed to loopback — an operator on a
   private network is a real use case — but the warning text names the cleartext risk.

**Provenance decision.** DC and Cloud share the single `jira` creation channel, `jira-` local-id prefix, and `jira_key` binding; deployments are disambiguated by the `RemoteRef.instance` field that ADR 0035 §(d) already defines for exactly this. They are the same vendor. Generalizing the store vocabulary is epic `be74`'s work, where a genuinely different vendor (GitHub) makes it necessary; doing it here would mean a store migration for no user-visible benefit.

**Alternative rejected: PR #120's separate adapter package.** Two copies of the field maps and sanitizers drift, and cross-adapter private imports are a dependency direction ADR 0035 never sanctioned.

**Alternative rejected: a hand-rolled stdlib REST client.** PR #120's client is competent, but pycontribs/jira already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks that thousands of users have found. Confining it to an opt-in extra keeps the cost off every rebar install.

**Alternative rejected: `atlassian-python-api`.** It was surveyed in ADR 0004 and does support DC with PAT auth, but `pycontribs/jira` is the better fit here for two reasons: it ships the Dockerized-Jira-SDK test harness pattern this epic adopts as its verification oracle (its own `tests/conftest.py`), and its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object. Either would work; picking one and confining it to an opt-in extra is what matters.

**Alternative rejected: generalizing `jira_key` / the `jira-` prefix / the channel vocabulary now.** That is epic `be74`'s spine and touches 50+ binding-store sites; pulling it forward delays the CMS delivery for no behavioral gain.

**Alternative rejected: moving the location-pinned modules now.** Relocating `outbound_fields.py` / `adf.py` into `jira_family/` would be the tidier file layout, but it requires teaching the dynamic loader the new sub-package and re-targeting every `mock.patch("rebar_reconciler.<mod>.<attr>")` site in the suite (ADR 0035 §(a)–(b)). That is ADR 0035's Phase 2; doing it here would couple a live-Cloud-risking refactor to a delivery epic for no DC-visible benefit. Dependency inversion gets the same single-implementation guarantee at a fraction of the risk.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/` (new), `adapters/jira/`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (new).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen `reconciler.backend` (**owned by J7**), add the TLS/`allow_insecure`
  validator and the `ca_bundle` + `resolved_statuses` keys (**owned by J6**). Split deliberately: J6 lands the
  DC connection settings with the transport that consumes them; J7 lands the backend-choice widening with the
  assembly that makes the choice valid.
- `pyproject.toml` — `[jira-datacenter]` extra, and the import contract.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`, `test_backend_contract.py`.
- A new ADR amending ADR 0035.
- **Out of scope:** relocating any location-pinned module (`adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`,
  `comment_limits.py`) or touching `_loader.py` — ADR 0035 Phase 2 owns that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit
- [x] `test_backend_contract.py`'s backend fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes for it
- [x] an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared `jira` provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon
- [ ] [operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at
      `localhost:2990`, selected by `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` with `reconciler.base_url`
      pointing at that instance: at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound
      pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions
      in the reconcile log
- [x] No SHARED mapping logic exists in two places, and each VARYING unit has exactly one shared CONTRACT:
      (a) the field/value maps, the label sanitizer, the link-relation vocabulary, and the probe classifier
      each have exactly one implementation in `adapters/jira_family/`, imported by both backends (or, for
      the location-pinned modules, consumed parameterized by a `jira_family` contract); and (b) the
      rich-text codec and the user-identity model each have exactly one shared CONTRACT in
      `adapters/jira_family/` with one implementation PER DEPLOYMENT. `adapters/jira_datacenter/` defines no
      copy of any unit in (a). Cross-imports between `adapters/jira/` and `adapters/jira_datacenter/` are
      forbidden and machine-checked, failing CI on a violation.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required "exactly one implementation reachable by both backends" for
      ALL SIX units including the codec and the identity model. That prescribes an outcome that would be
      WRONG if achieved:** Cloud is ADF and DC is wiki/plain text; Cloud identifies users by `accountId`
      and DC by `name`. Two implementations of one pinned contract IS the correct design
      (`jira_family/rich_text.py:36 RichTextCodec` → `WikiTextCodec` / `AdfCodec`;
      `jira_family/identity_model.py:42 UserIdentityModel` → `NameIdentity` / `AccountIdIdentity`). Two
      further corrections folded in, both recorded in this epic's AC-verification comment: the create-path
      field map legitimately exists twice (`jira_datacenter/backend.py:53 _map_local_to_dc_fields`, because
      Cloud's version lazy-loads the location-pinned `adf.py` BY FILE PATH — a coupling DC must not carry),
      so the "defines none of its own" clause is scoped to the units in (a); and the enforcement clause is
      narrowed to what the checker actually does — it forbids cross-IMPORTS and pins one dict literal per

baseline.description:
# An inbound peer link-removal never converges when a pair holds two relations

## Mechanism, established in source

`rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` takes **no `relation`** argument, and that is deliberate: `_commands/unlink.py`'s usage text says "pair-scoped, NO relation arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and `_get_link_info` returns "the most recent net-active link for target".

But links are STORED per relation: `graph/_links.add_dependency`'s docstring states it is idempotent "if a net-active LINK with the same **(target_id, relation)** already exists". So a pair CAN hold two differently-related deps (e.g. `blocks` and `relates_to`) simultaneously.

That asymmetry — write keyed on `(target, relation)`, remove keyed on `target` alone — is the defect.

## The consequence, introduced knowingly by 2b16

Change 1276 (bug `2b16-9be0-a8f5-41d9`) added the inbound link-removal path with guard **G5**: before unlinking, it confirms the pair's net-active relation MATCHES the relation whose peer link vanished, and **declines + logs** when it does not. That is the correct, safe direction — the alternative is removing a link the peer still has, i.e. destroying local data.

The cost is that the decline is **permanent**: the removal is re-emitted and re-declined on every subsequent pass, so the two systems never converge, and **there is no alert** — only a log line. This is the "silently non-convergent" shape rather than the "silently wrong" shape, which is the better failure, but it is still invisible.

2b16's implementing agent flagged the API asymmetry but could not establish whether two relations can actually coexist for one pair; that question is settled above, so this is LIVE, not theoretical, and G5 is not dead code.

## Options (deliberately not pre-decided)

1. A relation-scoped removal — the honest fix, but it changes a public library signature
   (`rebar.unlink`) or needs a lower-level seam, so it wants its own design pass.
2. Keep the decline and make it OBSERVABLE — a bridge alert or a non-convergence counter, so an operator
   sees a pair that will never settle instead of a log line nobody reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test proves a pair CAN hold two differently-related net-active deps (or proves it cannot, which
      would close this ticket as not_a_bug and make G5 dead code — establish which before designing)
- [ ] a peer deletion of ONE relation in a two-relation pair reaches a defined end state: either the
      correct link is removed, or the non-convergence is surfaced through an operator-visible channel
      rather than a log line
- [ ] whichever path is chosen, G5 never removes a link the peer still carries — assert that positively
- [ ] mutation-checked, with verdicts recorded here
baseline.summary: Inbound link removal never converges when a pair holds two relations (unlink is pair-scoped)

content.text: ## Why
`docs/architecture.md:49-55` states the core invariant: **all mutations go through
ONE locked append+commit path in `rebar._store`** (`event_append.py`, `push.py`,
`sync.py`, `lock.py`). `graph/_links.py` violates this — it hand-rolls a second,
divergent write path for LINK events. This is the single confirmed *structural*
finding of the 2026-06-18 audit (HIGH; the adversarial validator searched for a
justifying reason and found none). The risk is concrete: push policy, HLC
semantics, lock semantics, and commit shaping now live in two places, so any
change to `_store` silently fails to propagate to link writes, and the hand-rolled
copy already carries defects (wrong author, zero env_id, weaker lock).
## What
Route link-event writes in `graph/_links.py` through the canonical
`_store` write path (the same path `_commands/_seam.append_event` →
`_store.event_append.write_and_push` uses), eliminating the duplicate
lock+commit+push logic while preserving the pre-write cycle-check semantics.
## Scope
- In scope: `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` (`_write_link_event` / `add_dependency`),
reusing `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`.
- Out of scope: changing link *semantics* (cycle rules, hierarchy promotion),
the reconciler's grandfathered advisory lock, any non-link write.
## Context (citations)
- **The duplicate path:** `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:108-255` (`_write_link_event`).
It builds the LINK envelope by hand, opens `.ticket-write.lock` with bare
`fcntl.flock` (≈ lines 148-149), shells `git add` + `git commit --no-verify`,
and runs its own retry/push/rebase/merge loop. It hardcodes
- **The canonical path it should use:** `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:143`
(`write_and_push`) → `:77` (`stage_and_commit`), which writes via atomic
temp+rename, locks through `_store.lock.write_lock(tracker, dual_window=True)`
(the unified **dual-leg fcntl+mkdir** lock, `_store/lock.py:1-29`), and runs the
rebase guard (`check_no_rebase_in_progress`).
- **How other writers do it correctly:** `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:151-187`
(`append_event`) composes the envelope (real `author(...)`, real
`env_id(tracker)`) and routes through the store path; `_commands/delete.py`
writes UNLINK events this way.
- **Validator note:** the cycle checks (`_links.py:317-345`) run *before*
`_write_link_event`, which already acquires its lock *internally* — so "check
then write" is *already* non-atomic. A separate write path buys no atomicity;
the differences are pure defects.
## Implementation plan
1. Read `_seam.append_event` (`_commands/_seam.py:151-187`) and
`event_append.write_and_push` to confirm the envelope fields and return
contract (exit code / event id).
2. **PREFER `_seam.append_event` over `write_and_push` directly.** The review
confirmed `write_and_push(tracker, ticket_id, event)` takes a **pre-composed**
event and does **NOT** tick HLC — so calling it directly would force `_links.py`
to keep composing the envelope *and* ticking itself (the error-prone status quo).
`_seam.append_event(source_id, "LINK", {"target_id":…, "relation":…}, tracker)`
composes the envelope with real `author()`/`env_id(tracker)` **and** ticks HLC
internally (`_seam.py:174`) — strictly cleaner. Replace `_write_link_event`'s
body to call it, and **delete the existing `hlc.next_tick` call** (`_links.py:125`)
so there is no double-tick.
3. Delete the now-dead inline `fcntl.flock` block, the `git add`/`commit`
subprocess calls, and the bespoke push/rebase/merge retry loop.
4. Preserve the existing pre-call cycle-check / idempotency ordering in
`add_dependency` exactly (do not move the check inside the lock — it is
currently outside, and changing that is a separate design decision).
5. Verify the HLC tick source: `_links.py` currently calls
`hlc.next_tick(...)`; confirm `write_and_push`/`stage_and_commit` performs the
tick (or pass it through) so timestamps stay monotonic and no double-tick
occurs.
6. Run the link/graph test suites (`tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_links.py`,
`tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`, any `tests/**/`*link* and
`*graph*`), plus a two-clone convergence test if one exists, to confirm event
shape and merge behavior are unchanged.
## Tradeoffs
- **Benefit:** one write path; push/HLC/lock policy evolves in exactly one place;
the author/env_id/rebase-guard defects vanish for free.
- **Cost/risk:** the extraction must preserve the "cycle-check (outside lock) →
append (inside lock)" ordering and idempotency, so it is *not* a mechanical
move — review the atomicity assumptions in `add_dependency` carefully. If
`write_and_push` ticks HLC internally, ensure the old explicit `hlc.next_tick`
call is removed to avoid a double tick.
- **Behavioral change to note:** LINK events will now carry the real `author` and
`env_id` instead of the sentinel values. This applies to **both** writes —
the primary link AND the `relates_to` reciprocal (both go through
`_write_link_event`, e.g. `_links.py:369`). Confirm no test asserts on
`author == "ticket-graph"` or the zero-UUID env_id; update any that do (they
were asserting on a defect).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `graph/_links.py` no longer opens `.ticket-write.lock` directly, no longer
shells `git add`/`commit`, and no longer implements its own push loop; it routes
LINK writes through `_store.event_append.write_and_push` (or the `_seam`).
- [ ] LINK events carry a real `author` and a real `env_id(tracker)` (no
`"ticket-graph"` / zero-UUID sentinels).
- [ ] HLC timestamps remain monotonic (no double-tick) — verified by a reducer/HLC test.
- [ ] All existing link/graph/unblock tests pass; two-clone link convergence (if a
test exists) is unchanged.
- [ ] `ruff check src tests` and the scoped mypy gate stay green.
</content>

baseline.summary: Route graph/_links.py link writes through the canonical _store write path

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

`capabilities.py:330` defines a SINGLE global constant

    CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096

commented as the Opus floor, and applies it to every model. Anthropic's minimum cacheable prefix is MODEL-DEPENDENT, and two independent investigations in this epic measured real floors that the constant misdescribes.

## Measured evidence — two agents, two paths, neither trusting the other

MEASUREMENT A (via the overlap-judge path, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`), bracketed two ways:
    bare API            922 tok -> no cache      1042 tok -> write 1035, read 1035
    real judge request  875 tok -> nothing       1250 tok -> write 1243, read 1243
  => sonnet-4-6 floor is ~1024, NOT 4096.

MEASUREMENT B (via a wrapped httpx transport, live A/B with identical marker and payload):
    haiku-4-5   1193 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   2748 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   4749 tok -> CACHED (w=4742 r=4742)
    sonnet-4-5   253 tok -> not cached
    sonnet-4-5  7930 tok -> CACHED (w=7923)
  => haiku-4-5's floor lies between 2748 and 4749; the sonnet-4-5 bracket is consistent with ~1024.

The two are not in conflict: they show the floor VARIES BY MODEL, which is exactly what a single global constant cannot express. A floor of 4096 is roughly right for haiku and roughly 4x too high for sonnet.

## Two distinct harms, both observed

1. FALSE NEGATIVE IN THE WARNING. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` gates `warn_if_cache_ineffective`
   (`structured_run.py:417-422`). A genuine caching failure on a sonnet call site with a 900-3000
   token prefix is silently below the global floor and never warns — the exact blind spot bug 7a79
   introduced the floor to avoid over-warning about, now over-corrected in the other direction.
2. IT MISLEADS SIZING DECISIONS. Work on ticket 8415 hoisted a shared prefix to make it cacheable and
   landed at 846 tokens. Against the real 1024 floor that is a near miss (+5.8% input tokens, zero
   cache); against the documented 4096 it looks hopeless. The constant materially changes what an
   engineer concludes is worth doing.

## A second, separable defect in the same predicate

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares total `input_tokens` against the floor, but what governs caching is the size of the MARKED PREFIX, not the total request. A call with a 150-token marked prefix and a 7000-token unmarked user message clears the floor on totals and is uncacheable in fact. Bug f81d carries the detail; noted here because any fix to the constant should fix the compared quantity too, or the floor will still be measured against the wrong number.

## What is NOT established

The exact floor per model, from a documented source rather than bracketing. The measurements above are empirical brackets on three models on one date; Anthropic publishes per-model minimums and those should be the source of truth, with the measurements used to VERIFY rather than to define.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The cache floor is model-dependent rather than one global constant, sourced from documented
      per-model minimums and carried on the capability record alongside `prompt_cache_style`.
- [x] `warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares the MARKED PREFIX size against that model's floor, not the
      total `input_tokens`.
- [x] A test pins that a sub-floor prefix on a LOW-floor model (sonnet) now warns where it previously
      did not, and fails before the fix.
- [x] A test pins that the haiku floor is not lowered to sonnet's, so the fix does not reintroduce the
      over-warning bug 7a79 removed.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS is a model-blind global: 4x too high for sonnet, so real caching failures never warn

baseline.description:
## Why

Plan-review Pass-4 coaching is rendered per finding, so when several findings share one root cause the author receives N instance-level fixes and no signal that the *method* is at fault. A downstream project reported one story costing 7 review passes and ~35 blocking findings, where the criterion distribution (`G1G2` blocking in 3 distinct passes, `E4` in 4, `G6` in 4) traced to a single enumeration-method failure: the author kept adding the specific file the reviewer named instead of enumerating the population that file was drawn from, so the next pass surfaced the next unenumerated member.

The move registry's nearest existing move is `12` ("Generalize {subject} across the rest of the work."). It is always-applicable and carries no proof obligation, so satisfying it is still an unverifiable claim — three passes running the author asserted the enumeration was complete when it was not. What ended the loop was an acceptance criterion in the form of a `grep` expecting zero matches, which an incomplete enumeration cannot satisfy.

## What

Add one built-in Pass-4 coaching move that reframes a named instance as a sample from a population and requires a machine-checkable completeness proof, scoped via `applies_when` to the criteria where a population actually exists.

## Scope

In scope:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` — one new entry in `MOVE_REGISTRY`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — the mirroring row in the move table
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — one focused test for the new move

Out of scope:

- changes to any existing move's id, name, template, or `applies_when`
- the review kernel (`src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/coach.py`) — mechanism is unchanged
- the code-review move registry (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/moves.py`)
- cross-pass recurrence detection, criterion-concentration coaching, and structured
  incompleteness flags — the other upstream proposals, which need new machinery
- Pass 1, Pass 2, Pass 3 behavior; criterion text; `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`

## Approach

`MOVE_REGISTRY` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py` is the plan-review gate's catalog for the shared kernel coach mechanism. Ids `1`–`14` are taken, so add exactly:

- key `15`
- `name`: `sample, not the population`
- `template`: `Treat {subject} as one sample from a population, not a single item to fix — enumerate the whole population by the distinct ways the pattern occurs, then add a machine-checkable acceptance criterion that fails while any instance remains.`
- `applies_when`: `["G1G2", "E4", "G6", "A1"]`

The template carries exactly one `{subject}` placeholder, which `rebar.llm.review_kernel.coach.validate_move_registry` requires at load time, and the LLM never authors prose — `render_coach_notes` formats the locked template with a validated bounded noun-phrase subject.

The four triggers are real criterion ids in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` and are the criteria where a finding names a member of a population: `G1G2` and `E4` (facet `codebase-grounding` — unenumerated consumers, unprobed assertions), `A1` (facet `codebase-grounding` — call sites behind the rule of three), and `G6` (facet `approach-soundness`, checklist key `mechanism_correctness` — unhandled edge/empty cases). Verifiability criteria (`E6`, `F1`) are deliberately excluded: a missing proving command is not a population.

Scoping via `applies_when` — rather than sharpening move `12` — keeps the change additive: `rebar.llm.review_kernel.coach.applicable_moves` admits move `15` only when a surviving finding's `criteria[]` intersects those four ids, so no unrelated review sees it, and move `12` stays available for generalization findings that have no machine-checkable population. Prior art for a scoped built-in move is move `10` (`applies_when: ["G5", "A1", "T2"]`) and move `13` (`applies_when: ["G7"]`); prior art for a scoped coaching move added for a specific review failure is ticket `truthful-specified-silverfish`, which used the project overlay because its criterion was project-specific — this move's triggers are core criteria, so it belongs in the built-in registry.

`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_move_registry_matches_docs_table` asserts the doc move table and `MOVE_REGISTRY` have identical id sets and templates, so the new row in `docs/plan-review-gate.md` must be added in the same change or that existing test fails. `tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py` (the always-applicable-except-scoped assertion) already covers move `15` generically once it declares `applies_when`.

## Dependencies

None.

## Test Strategy

Assert the new registry entry's id, name, exact template, and exact trigger set directly on `MOVE_REGISTRY`, and assert its applicability is off with no triggers and on for each of its four triggers via the kernel's `move_applies`. The docs-table mirror and the scoped-applicability invariant are covered by the two existing tests named above, which run in the same suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MOVE_REGISTRY` contains key `15` whose `name` is `sample, not the population`, whose
      `template` is the exact sentence specified in the Approach section. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k population_move_template` —
      expected: exit 0, 1 passed.
- [ ] Move `15` declares exactly `["G1G2", "E4", "G6", "A1"]` in `applies_when`. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k population_move_triggers` —
      expected: exit 0, 1 passed.
- [ ] Move `15` is inapplicable for an empty trigger set, applicable for each of its four
      triggers individually. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k population_move_applicability` —
      expected: exit 0, 1 passed.
- [ ] The move table in `docs/plan-review-gate.md` mirrors the new entry. Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py -k move_registry_matches_docs_table` —
      expected: exit 0, 1 passed.
- [ ] No existing move id, name, template, or `applies_when` changed — the registry diff is
      addition-only. Prove with
      `test "$(git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py | grep -c '^-[^-]')" -eq 0` —
      expected: exit 0.
- [ ] The plan-review, review-kernel, G7, and project-portability coaching suites are green.
      Prove with
      `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_g7.py tests/unit/test_project_portability_coaching.py` —
      expected: exit 0, 0 failed.
- [ ] Lint passes. Prove with `make lint` — expected: exit 0.
- [ ] Typecheck passes. Prove with `make typecheck` — expected: exit 0.
baseline.summary: Pass-4 coaching move: treat a named instance as a sample from a population

content.text: ## Why
rebar is event-per-file-per-commit: every mutation = one git commit (closer to
git-issue, the documented high-bloat counterexample). Re-enabling stock gc (epic
minor-haste-ogle) fixes *reclaim* of object bloat, but the growth *rate* is set at
write time. The durable way to bound growth is to create fewer objects at the
source — exactly what git-bug does.
## What
Batch multiple mutations into a single git blob/commit per logical operation, the
git-bug `operationPack` pattern (multiple ops serialized into one blob -> one
commit per Commit()), instead of one commit per event. Must preserve the
append-only / merge-as-union (CRDT) convergence the store relies on, and the
globally-unique event identity used by replay/dedup.
Prior art (verifiable):
- git-bug operationPack: https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/operation_pack.go
- git-bug entity commit/merge: https://github.com/git-bug/git-bug/blob/master/entity/dag/entity.go
## Scope
In: a batched-write primitive + adoption on the highest-churn write paths (import,
reconciler apply, multi-event transactions). Out: changing the per-ticket event
schema or the union/replay semantics.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A batch-commit primitive writes N events in one commit, preserving per-event identity, replay, and union-merge convergence
- [ ] Adopted on at least the bulk paths (import; reconciler batch apply)
- [ ] Object-count reduction demonstrated on a synthetic many-event run (before/after)
- [ ] No regression: replay, dedup, and cross-clone convergence tests green

baseline.summary: Write-time op batching: fewer commits per mutation (git-bug operationPack pattern)
