## Context / Problem

Split out of bug 304e-9c0f-2068-4d0e (castoff-tigerseye-ammonite) to avoid widening that fix's scope; filed rather than fixed there.

`run_ensures()` (`src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:158`) calls `write_lock()` with the module defaults `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=30` x `_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS=2` = a **60 second** acquisition budget, then treats a `LockTimeout` as a whole-sweep no-op (it does log a WARNING — it is not silent — but it has already burned the 60s by then).

304e fixed the *reclaimability* defect that made one particular lock unprovable forever, so that specific 60s stall is gone. The budget itself is untouched and is a standing fragility: ANY genuinely contended lock — a concurrent writer, a slow push, a genuinely foreign-host lock on a shared filesystem (which is correctly never reclaimed) — still stalls the ensure sweep for a full minute on a path that runs at boot. The review-bot's autodeploy health check is `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30`, so a 60s budget on the boot path can fail a deploy on its own, with no orphaned lock involved.

`run_ensures`'s own docstring already anticipates this: "A caller that must not block (e.g. MCP boot) passes a SHORT budget so a contended lock skips the sweep rather than delaying it." The MCP boot path does; the review-bot startup path evidently does not.

## Approach

Audit `run_ensures` callers on startup paths and give the boot-time ones a short bounded budget (the sweep is idempotent and re-runs, so skipping it under contention is cheap and safe), or make a short budget the default for the ensure sweep and let the long budget be opt-in. Consider whether the boot path should surface the skip more loudly than a WARNING.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No startup/boot path can spend more than a few seconds acquiring the write lock for the ensure
      sweep; verified by a test that holds the lock and asserts the boot path returns promptly.
- [ ] A skipped sweep is still visible (logged) and still re-runs on the next boot.
- [ ] The fail-closed StoreIncompatibleError re-raise is unaffected.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
baseline.summary: run_ensures uses the full 60s write-lock budget on the boot path, so any contended lock alone can blow a 30s deploy health timeout

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
Discovered while closing tickets this session. The completion-verification gate's LLM verifier (rebar verify-completion / the close-gate _completion_precheck) returns NON-DETERMINISTIC verdicts for IDENTICAL inputs — same ticket, same code at HEAD, same acceptance criteria, same ticket comments — within minutes and with no changes between runs.

## Evidence (ticket ad9f-45f1-339f-4346, code at origin/main HEAD, unchanged between runs)
- `rebar verify-completion ad9f --output json` standalone -> verdict PASS, 0 findings.
- `rebar transition ad9f in_progress closed` (same gate, moments later) -> "completion verification FAILED — 2 unmet criteria; not closing".
- Immediate retry `rebar transition ad9f in_progress closed` -> PASS, ticket closed.
Three runs, three effectively different outcomes (PASS / FAIL-2 / PASS) with no intervening change.

## Impact
- The close gate is unreliable in BOTH directions: it can spuriously BLOCK a legitimately-complete ticket (wasting an LLM run and forcing retries) and — the more dangerous direction — spuriously PASS a genuinely-incomplete ticket on a lucky run. A gate whose verdict flips on identical input cannot be trusted to certify completion.
- Interacts badly with the completion close mechanics (see 4de6): flaky FAILs during a close are expensive (billed LLM) and confusing; flaky PASSes undermine the whole attestation.

## Root-cause hypothesis
LLM sampling non-determinism: the verifier runs the model without pinned/deterministic decoding (temperature/seed) and/or without multi-sample aggregation, so per-run sampling variance flips borderline criteria between upheld/unmet. Model: pydantic_ai/claude-* per config.

## Suggested fixes
- Pin decoding for the verifier (temperature 0 and/or a fixed seed where the provider supports it) so identical inputs are reproducible.
- Multi-sample majority/quorum vote per criterion with a declared threshold (the plan-review gate already uses a multi-pass verify structure; mirror it).
- Distinguish a genuine FAIL from a flaky one: on a non-PASS close, allow a bounded retry/quorum before failing closed, and surface a 'low-confidence / non-reproducible' signal rather than a hard FAIL.
- Add a determinism regression check (run the verifier N times on a fixed fixture; require identical verdicts).

## Relation to our changes
UNRELATED to the 790c/80af/ad9f/4de6 code changes — this is the LLM-verifier layer (verify_completion), not the git-tree/ref plumbing those touched.

## Possibly related (same session / same subsystem)
- review-code silent-empty output when invoked non-interactively/backgrounded (exits 0 with an empty result — indistinguishable from a clean 0-findings pass). (From the 4de6 report.)
- PlanReviewGenerationChanged raised with IDENTICAL before==after generation hashes; a blind re-run signs. Also a currency/consistency check that fails against itself.

## Scope of THIS ticket (agreed) + Acceptance Criteria
Resolve e458 with two concrete, testable changes; the residual multi-sample quorum / deeper determinism hardening is a separate follow-up (see idea 4217 family).
- [ ] The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar payload (BOTH the PASS `completion_verifier_pass_v1` and FAIL `completion_verifier_fail_v1` schemas, via build_payload) records `verified_at_sha` (the immutable commit the verifier ran against; None in local mode) and `trace_id` (the model-run id), so two sidecars can be compared for input-identity from stored data alone — verified by a unit test on build_payload for both PASS and FAIL.
- [ ] The completion verifier pins model sampling temperature to 0 (greedy) by default — cfg.temperature is set to 0.0 in _verify_completion_inner UNLESS the operator explicitly set REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE (an explicit value wins), mirroring the model/step-floor tuning already there and the plan-review Pass-2 verifier's greedy pin — verified by a test that the tuned cfg.temperature is 0.0 by default and preserves an explicit non-None value.
- [ ] make lint && make typecheck && make test green.
Note: temperature 0 is a MITIGATION (reduces sampling variance), not a proof of determinism; combined with the recorded verified_at_sha it makes any residual drift observable (identical input, identical decoding) rather than ambiguous.
baseline.summary: completion verifier is non-deterministic: identical inputs yield PASS vs N-unmet-criteria across runs, making the close gate unreliable

# The gating pip-audit job fails on EVERY Gerrit patchset, blocking all Verified +1 votes

## Symptom

`build-and-test / pip-audit (dependency vulnerabilities)` fails on every patchset run observed today, so no change can reach `Verified +1`. Confirmed across five independent runs on different agents' patchsets: 30770494611, 30770603146, 30770604307, 30770971365, 30771122330, 30771131391. All share head sha 4214516f95 (`origin/main`), and the failures are identical, so this is a property of `main`, not of any one change.

## Root cause — a real advisory, NOT a network flake

From run 30770494611's job log (the audit step's own output):

    pip-audit attempt 1/3
    click 8.2.1   PYSEC-2026-2132   8.3.3   Pallets Click, versions 8.3.2 and below,
      contain a command injection vulnerability in the click.edit() function, allowing
      attackers to pass arbitrary OS commands from an unprivileged account.
    ##[error]pip-audit found dependency vulnerabilities (see output). Bump the pinned
      version, or add --ignore-vuln <ID> with justification if accepted.

It succeeded on attempt 1 — it REACHED the advisory DB and found a vulnerability. So the workflow's documented infra escape hatch does NOT apply: `_build-and-test.yml`'s failure policy reserves `recheck` for the case where all three attempts fail to reach the DB. Commenting `recheck` will not clear this.

`click` is a TRANSITIVE dependency pinned at 8.2.1 in the committed `uv.lock` (line 711); it is not pinned in `pyproject.toml`. The advisory appears to have been published after `ce5d: go uv-canonical with a committed lock` landed the lock, which is why a previously green gate went red with no code change.

## Remediation (one of)

1. Refresh the lock so `click` resolves to >= 8.3.3 (the fix version pip-audit names).
   Preferred: it removes the vulnerability rather than accepting it.
2. If 8.3.3 is not resolvable under the current constraint set, `--ignore-vuln
   PYSEC-2026-2132` with a written justification, per the failure policy's explicit
   provision for that (`_build-and-test.yml`, "Failure policy"). Note rebar does not call
   `click.edit()`, so the exploit path is plausibly not reachable — but that argument
   belongs IN the justification comment, reviewed, not assumed here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip-audit` is green on a fresh patchset against `main`
- [ ] the fix is a lock/pin change or a justified, greppable `--ignore-vuln`, not a
      blanket skip of the job
- [ ] if option 2 is taken, the justification names why the vulnerable code path is
      unreachable from rebar

## Why this is filed separately

Discovered while landing story 79d5 (DC length convergence), whose diff is two new test files plus a source comment and touches no dependency pin. A lock refresh is a different change with a different blast radius, and `uv.lock` is outside that story's declared file impact.
baseline.summary: pip-audit gate is red on main: click 8.2.1 PYSEC-2026-2132

## Why
The diff-scope filter keeps a detector match only when `location.file` is EXACTLY equal to an
entry in `changed_files` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:74`, `if loc and loc in
changed:`), with neither side normalized. A location and a changed-file entry that denote the
SAME file with different spellings (`./app.py`, an absolute path under repo_root, `a//b.py`
repeated separators, a unicode NFC/NFD variant) compare unequal, so a real high-severity
security match is silently dropped. VALIDATED.

## Decision: normalize BOTH sides at this boundary
Add a small canonicalizer applied to `location.file` AND each `changed_files` entry before the
membership test — a pure textual canonical form (no filesystem access, since diff-scope paths
need not exist on disk):
1. If the path is absolute AND under `repo_root`, make it relative to `repo_root` (both sides
   then live in the same relative space; the upstream contract already intends repo-relative).
2. `os.path.normpath` — collapses `./`, repeated separators (`a//b` → `a/b`), and `..`.
3. `unicodedata.normalize("NFC", …)` — so a composed/decomposed unicode filename matches.
Symlink resolution (realpath) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: it requires the file to exist on
disk, which a diff-scope path need not; this ticket canonicalizes spelling, not inode identity
(noted in a code comment).

## What
1. `detectors.py`: add `_canonical_path(p, repo_root)` (relativize-under-repo_root → normpath →
   NFC) and apply it to both `loc` and every `changed_files` entry (build the `changed` set from
   canonicalized entries; canonicalize `loc` before the `in` test).
2. `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py`: variant-path matching tests (RED-first — they fail
   against the current exact-match code, pass after canonicalization).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py` — canonicalize both sides of the diff-scope filter.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py` — variant-path-form tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `location.file` and `changed_files` are both canonicalized (relativize-under-repo_root +
      normpath + NFC) before the membership test.
- [ ] Tests: a match whose `location.file` is `./app.py`, an absolute path under repo_root,
      `a//b.py` (repeated separators), and an NFC/NFD unicode variant each STILL matches its
      changed-file entry `app.py` / `a/b.py` / the unicode name — the high-severity match is
      retained.
- [ ] A genuinely-different file (e.g. `other.py` not in `changed_files`) still does NOT match.
- [ ] `make test` green.
baseline.summary: Define and test the security-detector diff-scope path contract

baseline.description:
## Context
Discovered while implementing epic sonic-columned-sturgeon (op-certs). Children 4214 (merge-gate
verify), ee0b (trusted-server producer), and 8f1d (HMAC→opcert migration) all depend on a shared
primitive: **how an asymmetric op-cert (a DSSE envelope) is stored on a ticket and produced.** The
epic decomposition treated this as implicit; it is a core event-sourcing change, so it gets its
own ticket.

Today attestations are HMAC records. `reducer/_processors.py::process_signature` builds the
`attestations[kind]` record from a FIXED field set (manifest/algorithm/signature/key_id/head_sha/
signed_at/author/kind) — it does NOT preserve an added `envelope`. Storing an op-cert DSSE envelope
therefore requires a reducer change (runs on every ticket replay; the SNAPSHOT/compaction fold at
`_processors.py:763` restores `attestations` verbatim, so op-cert fields survive compaction for
free) plus a producer in `signing.py`.

## Selected design — Option A (DECIDED 2026-07-13 by Joe Oakhart; no further confirmation needed)
Extend the existing `SIGNATURE` event record — do NOT introduce a new event type. The *structural*
choice (carry the new signature inside the existing event/record rather than a new event type)
mirrors git signed commits (a `gpgsig` header on the existing commit object) and additive
Protobuf/Avro schema evolution.

**Cross-version behavior (accurate — NOT tolerant-reader-transparent).** An op-cert `SIGNATURE`
event carries the DSSE `envelope` and OMITS the HMAC `signature`/`algorithm`. So an OLD clone does
not "ignore an unknown field and keep verifying": it reduces the event into a record with no HMAC
and reads it as **UNSIGNED** — it cannot verify an op-cert because it lacks the asymmetric verifier.
This is exactly the identity epic's SSHSIG-authorship rollout posture (older clones preserve the
event append-only but cannot verify it) and the `TAG_DELTA` precedent: **op-cert events are
preserved-but-unverifiable on pre-upgrade clones; upgrade the verify/reconcile hosts first.** What
IS additive-transparent is the record *schema*: the new `envelope`/bound fields are present-only, so
legacy HMAC `sign_manifest` records are byte-unchanged and existing HMAC verification is untouched.

Concretely:

- **Producer** (`signing.sign_opcert_manifest`, parallel to `sign_manifest`): builds a DSSE
  envelope via `opcert.sign_opcert(ticket_id, material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit,
  key_path=…, principal=…)`, then appends a `SIGNATURE` event whose record carries the signed
  `manifest` (first line `"<kind>: …"` so the reducer derives the kind), the encoded `envelope`
  (`dsse.encode`), the bound `material_fingerprint` + `merged_log_commit`, and `algorithm="sshsig"`
  — NO HMAC signature.
- **Reducer** (`process_signature`): additionally preserve `envelope`, `material_fingerprint`,
  `merged_log_commit` into the `attestations[kind]` record (read via `data.get(...)`, present-only).
  No change needed to the compaction fold (it restores `attestations` verbatim).
- **Read helper** (`opcert.opcert_from_record`): returns `(dsse.Envelope, {material_fingerprint,
  merged_log_commit})` when the record carries an `envelope`, else `None` (distinguishes an op-cert
  record from a legacy HMAC record).
- **Rollout:** op-cert events are preserved append-only by older clones but read as UNSIGNED
  there (no asymmetric verifier) — upgrade verify/reconcile hosts first, exactly as the SSHSIG
  authorship rollout and `TAG_DELTA` require. The record-schema extension itself is additive
  (legacy HMAC records unchanged).

(Considered and rejected: Option B — a new `OPCERT` event type + separate `opcerts` map — cleaner
separation but larger change and its separation is moot once 8f1d removes HMAC.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `signing.sign_opcert_manifest(...)` writes an envelope-bearing `SIGNATURE` event; a test
      asserts the ticket's reduced `attestations[<kind>]` record then carries the encoded
      `envelope` + bound `material_fingerprint`/`merged_log_commit`, and NO HMAC `signature`.
- [ ] `process_signature` preserves those fields through a full reduce AND through a
      compact-then-replay round-trip; a test asserts an op-cert survives compaction unchanged.
- [ ] `opcert.opcert_from_record(record)` returns `(envelope, bound_fields)` for an op-cert record
      and `None` for a legacy HMAC record (test both); the returned envelope, fed to
      `opcert.verify_opcert` with a pinned keyring, certifies (end-to-end test).
- [ ] The record-schema extension is additive (present-only): a test asserts a legacy HMAC
      `sign_manifest` record is byte-unchanged (no `envelope`/bound keys) and still HMAC-verifies,
      so existing HMAC attestations are untouched. Rollout note documented: op-cert events are
      preserved-but-unverifiable on pre-upgrade clones (read as unsigned) — upgrade verify/reconcile
      hosts first (as with SSHSIG authorship / `TAG_DELTA`).
- [ ] 4214 can read a stored op-cert to verify it over the merged log; ee0b/8f1d can produce op-certs
baseline.summary: op-cert storage + producer primitive (DSSE envelope on a ticket) — shared keystone for 4214/ee0b/8f1d

# A shell-expanded comment body wrote live credentials into the ticket store; only GitHub push protection caught it

## What happened

An agent posted a ticket comment whose body quoted an upstream error message containing backtick-delimited text. The body was passed to `rebar comment` inside a DOUBLE-QUOTED shell argument, so zsh performed COMMAND SUBSTITUTION on the backticks. The backticked token happened to be `local`, a zsh builtin, which with no arguments prints every shell and environment variable. That dump was interpolated into the comment body and committed to the tickets store.

The resulting COMMENT event was 17,821 characters where the intended text was a few thousand, and contained live secrets read straight out of the environment:

* an Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-`, 108 chars)
* TWO GitHub personal access tokens (`ghp_`, 40 chars each)
* an OpenAI-style service key (`sk-svc-`, 167 chars)
* a Google-style API key and several base64 blobs

## Blast radius — nothing reached a remote, and the reason matters

GitHub secret-scanning PUSH PROTECTION rejected the push: "push declined due to repository rule violations ... To push, remove secret from commit(s)". Verified afterwards: the offending commit is on NO remote branch and is NOT an ancestor of origin/tickets. Every unpushed commit was scanned and exactly ONE commit / ONE file is affected.

So the credentials never left the machine. **The only control that stopped this was a third-party scanner on the far side of the push.** rebar itself accepted the body, signed it, committed it, and would have pushed it to a mirror of a real repository. That is the finding: there is no rebar-side control at all, and the one that saved us is outside the project.

A second consequence worth noting: because push protection blocks the whole ref update, the poisoned commit wedged 108 unrelated commits of legitimate ticket history behind it. A single bad body therefore also becomes an availability problem for the store's durability.

## Why this is rebar's problem and not merely operator error

The proximate cause is a quoting mistake by the caller, and callers will keep making it: agents routinely paste provider error text, log lines and code snippets into comments, and that text frequently contains backticks. The store's job is to persist what it is given, but it currently persists a credential dump silently and irreversibly (event files are append-only and signed), and the damage is only discoverable at push time, far from the cause.

Note also the asymmetry: rebar ALREADY understands that secrets must not be logged in some places, and the review-bot's own token exposure is tracked separately. There is no equivalent guard on the one surface that writes attacker-useful text to a git history.

## Scope

- the comment/description write path (whatever validates an event body before it is committed
  and signed) — a pre-write secret screen.
- optionally the CLI argument surface, so a body arriving with a shell-expanded variable dump is
  recognisable.
- documentation for agents on passing untrusted text to `rebar comment` safely.

## Approach

Two independent layers, and the first is the one that matters:

1. **Screen event bodies for high-confidence secret shapes before committing** — the same
   prefix families GitHub's scanner uses are cheap, low-false-positive anchors (an
   Anthropic/OpenAI key prefix, a GitHub token prefix, an AWS access-key id). On a hit, REFUSE
   the write with a clear error naming the matched family and offset. Refusing is correct rather
   than redacting: a body containing a live credential is almost never the body the author meant
   to write, so silently truncating it would hide the mistake that produced it.
2. **Make the shell hazard hard to hit** — document the safe invocation (write the body to a
   file and pass it via a form the shell does not re-scan) and prefer a stdin/file-based body
   argument over a positional string for long bodies.

Deliberately NOT proposed: scanning the whole store retroactively, or weakening the append-only event model. The guard belongs at the write boundary.

## Testing

- a body containing a synthetic token of each screened family is REFUSED, with the family named,
  and NO event file is written and NO commit is created. Verify RED by removing the screen.
- a body containing look-alike-but-harmless text (a hex string, the literal word 'sk-ant' with no
  key material, a base64 blob under the length floor) is ACCEPTED, so the screen does not become
  a nuisance that agents learn to work around.
- a body legitimately quoting backticked text is stored VERBATIM when passed by the documented
  safe path, proving the fix does not merely forbid the content that triggered the incident.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] an event body containing a high-confidence secret shape is refused at the write boundary,
      before any event file is written, signed, or committed — proven by a test verified RED.
- [ ] the refusal names the matched secret family and does not echo the secret value.
- [ ] look-alike benign text is not refused, evidenced by explicit negative cases, so the screen
      does not train agents to route around it.
- [ ] the safe way to pass untrusted or quoted text as a comment body is documented where agents
      will read it, with the failure mode named (shell command substitution on backticks).
- [ ] the incident is recorded with its blast radius, including that the only control which
      stopped it was outside the project.
baseline.summary: Ticket store persists shell-expanded credential dumps; only GitHub push protection caught a live PAT leak

## Summary

`tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py::test_force_bypasses_verdict_reuse` and `::test_code_change_reruns_full_review` fail on `main`'s tree, blocking unrelated changes from earning `Verified +1`. Both assert `runner.calls > first_calls` and get `assert 0 > 0` — the fake LLM runner is never invoked at all.

Observed on Gerrit changes 1039 and 1040 (both `Verified -1`, both otherwise unrelated to plan review). Reproduces locally.

## Blame

**Primary: 228b-… (`c781127a2` "228b: short-circuit plan review on any DET block"), surfaced by a rebase-without-re-verify on 7e77-cbe5-5bcf-4096 (`517e0470a`, Gerrit change 1035).**

The two tests are built, per their own module docstring, on "a DET-floor BLOCK (missing Acceptance Criteria fails P1 unconditionally) with a schema-aware counting fake runner". They assert the LLM passes still RUN in that state. 228b changed exactly that contract — it short-circuits plan review on any DET block, so the runner is never called and `calls` stays 0.

The two changes never met in CI:
- 7e77's patchset was based on `36411da47` ("4143: remind about Serena…"), which PREDATES `c781127a2`. Its CI run 30524084670 was green (7659 passed) against that base — a base without the short-circuit.
- Gerrit then rebased it on submit. Its own message: "Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 517e0470ab…".
- The rebased commit was submitted WITHOUT re-running CI, so nothing ever tested 7e77's tests against 228b's behaviour.

This is the Rebase-If-Necessary semantic-conflict hazard: two changes each green in isolation, red once combined, with no gate on the combination.

## Confidence and what is NOT yet proven

Confirmed: the commit ordering, the two bases, the green CI on 7e77's pre-228b base, the rebase-on-submit message, and the failing assertions.

NOT confirmed: reverting only `c781127a2`'s `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` on top of `517e0470a` did NOT restore green. So the short-circuit path as it exists on main is not solely that file — 7e77 also rewrote `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` (-52 lines) and added `reuse.py`, and the effective routing is likely the combination. Whoever picks this up should treat "228b's contract change vs 7e77's test assumption" as the lead, not as a finished diagnosis.

## Second, independent defect in the same tests

These tests are NOT self-contained. Run their file alone they fail identically — at 7e77's original pre-rebase patchset, at merged `main`, and on an unrelated feature branch:

    pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py    ->  2 failed, 5 passed

They only pass as part of a full-suite run, so they depend on state established by some other test. CI runs `pytest -n 4 --dist worksteal`, which distributes tests across workers DYNAMICALLY, so which worker they land on — and whether their unnamed dependency ran there — shifts whenever the suite changes. That makes them latently flaky regardless of the 228b conflict, and it is why adding unrelated tests can flip them red.

## Expected

1. Reconcile 228b's short-circuit contract with what 7e77's tests assert — either the tests encode a stale contract and should be updated, or the short-circuit is too aggressive for the `--force` / code-drift paths. That is a call for the owners of those two tickets, not a mechanical fix.
2. Make the two tests self-contained so they pass in isolation and cannot be flipped by worker distribution.
3. Consider whether Gerrit submitting a rebased commit without re-running CI needs a guard, since that is what let this land.

## Impact

`main`'s tree is failing these tests, so every unrelated change picking them up gets `Verified -1` and cannot land. Currently blocking Gerrit changes 1039 and 1040.
baseline.summary: test_plan_review_reuse fails on main: 228b DET short-circuit vs 7e77 test assumption, landed via rebase-without-re-verify

baseline.description:
## Why
This is the convergence mechanism itself: reuse plan-review's novelty machinery to stop code review
re-nagging carryover findings and to drop novel low-impact findings on UNCHANGED code, while ALWAYS
raising novel findings on newly-changed code (the per-citation region gate is the deliberate
divergence from plan-review's whole-artifact floor).

## What
- **Consume the reader.** Call `latest_code_review_result(key)` (revenued-thickset-dassie) for the
  current review's typed key to obtain prior SURFACED findings + the prior `deps` map. Key selection:
  `session:<id>` for local reviews (set on the verdict by paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish),
  `change:<id>` for Gerrit.
- **REUSE unchanged kernel primitives (no fork):** the novelty SCORING CONTRACT
  (`review_kernel.verify.novelty_model` / `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS`), the reshaper
  `review_kernel.verify.reshape_novelties`, the per-finding novelty math
  `review_kernel.decide.novelty`, and the drop predicate
  `review_kernel.decide.rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, *, t_novel, floor)` — all verbatim. A
  thin `score_code_novelty` (mirroring plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` runner wiring) drives
  the sub-call and, from `reshape_novelties`, surfaces BOTH the novelty float (for the drop) AND the
  `matched_prior_id` (for `carried_from`). NOTE: it does NOT reuse the kernel `score_novelty`
  wrapper verbatim — that returns only `{index: float}` and DISCARDS `matched_prior_id`, which the
  carryover-labeling AC needs; `score_code_novelty` reuses the same underlying primitives
  (reshape + decide.novelty) so the scoring is identical, just also returning the matched id.
- **NEW code-review novelty PROMPT + reviewer id.** Add `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md`
  (`outputs: code_review_novelty`, `execution_mode: single_turn`, `category: code-review-pass`) and a
  `code-novelty` reviewer id used in the sub-call's `RunRequest(reviewers=["code-novelty"])`. Wiring
  mirrors plan-review's `_score_floor_novelty` runner: the diff is the domain context and the prior
  SURFACED findings are appended to the instructions as a context block (NOT a `{{plan}}`/template
  var). Register the reused contract at `code_review/contracts.py::register_contracts()`
  (`contracts.register_contract("code_review_novelty", novelty_model)`, importing `novelty_model`
  from `review_kernel.verify`) — mirroring `plan_review/passes.py`; without it a
  `RunRequest(output_schema="code_review_novelty")` fails at runtime.
  - **cites_prior_location REDEFINED for code (critical).** `NOVELTY_SUBANSWERS` shares the field
    name `cites_prior_location`, whose kernel/plan meaning is "same PLAN location/section/AC line".
    The code prompt MUST firmly redefine it so the model does not anchor on the plan meaning:
    `cites_prior_location — does this finding point at the SAME source file AND approximately the
    same line region (within ~10 lines) as the prior finding? (not merely the same file — the same
    localized area)`. (This closes the epic-review advisory T1.)
- **NEW `region_gate.py`** (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py`) defining the region-state
  vocabulary + detector:
  - Constants: `REGION_UNCHANGED = "unchanged"`, `REGION_CHANGED = "changed"`, `REGION_UNKNOWN = "unknown"`.
  - **Citation basis:** a finding's cited region is derived from its `location` field (a `path` or
    `path:line`). The detector takes the finding's cited FILE path, hashes the current file
    (`attest._hash_file`), and compares to `prior_deps[path]`: equal → `UNCHANGED`; differ → `CHANGED`;
    path absent from `prior_deps`, OR the finding is multi-location / absence-evidence (no concrete
    file) / moved / renamed / any error → `UNKNOWN`. File-level in v1 (line-level deferred).
- **NEW `region_gated_floor`** (in `code_review/workflow_ops.py`, applied over the decided advisory
  set in the produce path before the sidecar emit — the code-review analogue of plan-review's
  `_maybe_apply_rising_floor`, which sits after the verdict and before emit):
  - A finding is DROPPED iff `rising_floor_drop(priority, novelty, t_novel, floor)` is true AND its
    region is `REGION_UNCHANGED`. `REGION_CHANGED` and `REGION_UNKNOWN` NEVER drop (both raise).
  - **Thresholds/activation (decided):** reuse the EXISTING config — `verify.novelty_drop_threshold`
    (t_novel), `verify.novelty_priority_floor` (floor), AND `verify.novelty_drop_active` as the
    activation/evidence gate. This introduces NO NEW config key (the epic's "no eval-gated
    activation flag" = no NEW flag): the code-review floor reuses plan-review's SAME three keys, so
    it is OFF by default and an operator opts in with evidence exactly as plan-review requires
    (preserving the opt-in-with-evidence discipline the reviewer flagged). On top of the flag, the
    floor also SELF-GATES: inert whenever there is no prior memory for the current key (first review,
    or a reader error → empty prior set). Both gates must be open to drop anything.
  - Dropped findings carry `drop_reason = "novelty-region"`.
  - **Carryover labeling:** a finding that matches a prior surfaced finding (low novelty) but is NOT
    dropped is stamped `carried_from` = the `matched_prior_id` returned by `score_code_novelty` for
    that finding (the prior finding's id; empty ⇒ not stamped). Data model: by the time the floor runs (post-decide, in the produce path), findings
    are plain dicts in the verdict's `advisory`/`blocking` lists — `carried_from` is added as a KEY
    on that dict (no Pydantic model change needed; the coach already ran in-workflow, so the floor
    strips coaching notes whose `finding_refs` point at a `carried_from`-stamped finding from the
    verdict's `coaching` list). The finding remains surfaced.
  - **FAIL-SAFE (full mirror of plan-review):** the whole floor is wrapped in try/except; any
    reader/hash/compare/novelty error returns the FULL unfiltered finding set (no drops). A finding
    with no novelty entry defaults to novelty 0.0 (carryover = kept).
- **Neutrality (ADR 0008 Invariant 1):** the Pass-1 finder NEVER receives prior findings; only the
  post-find novelty seam does.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py` (region_gated_floor + novelty sub-call wiring),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/region_gate.py` (NEW: vocab + detector),
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/contracts.py` (register `code_review_novelty`),
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code_review_novelty.md` (NEW prompt),
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` (invoke the floor before emit).
- Depends on the reader/payload (revenued-thickset-dassie) and, for end-to-end LOCAL integration, on
  local persistence (paradoxal-balsamic-bubblefish). This story is reviewed/implemented AFTER c639
  (+3bff) are committed on the stack, so the reader (`latest_code_review_result`) + `deps` map exist
  in the tree; region_gated_floor UNIT tests run against a mocked reader.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `code-novelty` reviewer prompt (`code_review_novelty.md`) + reviewer id exist, binding the
      reused novelty contract, with diff context + prior findings in the instructions block and
      `cites_prior_location` redefined for source-file/line regions.
- [ ] The `code_review_novelty` contract is registered in `contracts.register_contracts()`;
      `rising_floor_drop`, `reshape_novelties`, and `decide.novelty` are reused UNCHANGED (the thin
      `score_code_novelty` surfaces `matched_prior_id` for carryover; it does not reuse the
      `score_novelty` wrapper, which discards it).
- [ ] `region_gate.py` defines `REGION_UNCHANGED`/`REGION_CHANGED`/`REGION_UNKNOWN` used by the
      detector, which compares a cited file's current sha256 to the prior `deps` map.
- [ ] `region_gated_floor` drops a finding ONLY when novel AND low-priority AND `REGION_UNCHANGED`;
      `REGION_CHANGED` and `REGION_UNKNOWN` both raise; dropped findings carry
      `drop_reason = "novelty-region"`.
- [ ] Thresholds/activation reuse the EXISTING `verify.novelty_drop_threshold`,
      `verify.novelty_priority_floor`, and `verify.novelty_drop_active` (no NEW config key); the
      floor is OFF by default and additionally self-gates inert with no prior memory.
- [ ] Carryover findings are stamped `carried_from` = the matched prior finding's id (string, added
      as a dict key), have their coaching notes stripped from the verdict, but remain surfaced.
- [ ] Any reader/hash/compare/novelty error returns the full unfiltered finding set (no drops).
- [ ] The Pass-1 finder receives no prior findings; only the novelty seam does — asserted by a test
      that the finder/verifier pass inputs contain no prior-findings context (ADR 0008 Invariant 1).
- [ ] Tests (mocked reader): unchanged-region low-priority novel → dropped; changed-region novel →
      raised; absence/multi-location → UNKNOWN → raised; carryover → `carried_from` = matched id +
      coaching stripped; forced reader error → no drops; and a neutrality test that the Pass-1
      finder step receives no prior findings.
baseline.summary: region_gated_floor: content-addressed novelty convergence for code review

content.text: A single failed Jira mutation (e.g. an unreachable workflow transition) aborts the
entire reconciler pass mid-way, silently skipping all later mutations. The
reconciler should isolate per-mutation failures: apply everything it can, then fail
loud at the END with a non-zero exit and a report of what failed.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Have a local ticket whose mapped Jira status is not reachable via any available
workflow transition on its Jira issue (e.g. a local `idea` before the Jira
`IDEA` status/transitions are provisioned).
2. Run a reconcile pass that includes that ticket plus other tickets with valid
mutations.
3. Observe the pass abort when it reaches the unreachable transition.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: the reconciler applies every other (valid) mutation in the pass,
records the failed one, and at the END exits non-zero with a report naming the
failed mutation(s) — no valid mutation is silently skipped.
- Actual: `transition_issue_by_name` raises an uncaught `RuntimeError` (no
transition reaches the target), or the preflight raises `StatusMappingError`,
aborting the whole pass mid-way; mutations for all subsequent tickets are skipped
until the next scheduled run.
## Context
This is independent of the `idea` feature (it affects every transition), but it is
the mechanism that makes the `idea → IDEA` create-drops-status convergence and the
"Jira not yet configured" window tolerable instead of pass-aborting — see the
`idea` epic and its "Jira `idea ↔ IDEA` mapping" story. Relevant code: the abort
sites are the preflight in `reconcile.py` (`StatusMappingError`), the per-mutation
error handling in `dispatch_one.py` (only HTTP-400 "illegal transition" currently
degrades to a comment-fallback), and the `RuntimeError` in
`acli.py::transition_issue_by_name` when no transition reaches the target.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reconcile pass containing one unreachable-transition mutation still applies
every other valid mutation in that pass (test-verified).
- [ ] The failed mutation is recorded and surfaced in the pass's end-of-run report.
- [ ] The pass exits non-zero when any mutation failed (fail loud), rather than
exiting 0 or aborting mid-pass.
- [ ] A `RuntimeError` from `transition_issue_by_name` (no transition reaches the
target) is caught per-mutation and does not abort the pass.
- [ ] The status-mapping preflight does not abort the whole pass for a single
unmapped/unreachable status.
- [ ] `make lint` and the reconciler test suite pass.

baseline.summary: Reconciler aborts whole pass on one failed Jira transition; should isolate + fail loud at end

STATUS: TABLED — a sensitive reconciler-CORE change, deferred by decision. This idea is a resume pointer; the FULL raw record (measured facts, verified findings, 4 history dossiers on WHY the current design exists, options, open gates) is in session_log **bdc7-9256-ff48-4520** (felicific-hardheaded-elephant). Prior measured facts + cited prior-art research: session_log **b96a-15a5-1c0a-47c5**. Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Problem
The rebar tickets git store (.tickets-tracker, `tickets` branch) grows UNBOUNDEDLY: ~443 MB / ~178k objects for ~15k tickets, of which ~85% (~375 MB) is the reconciler's `.bridge_state/` Jira-sync cache — bindings.json (219 MB / ~987 versions) + prev_snapshot.json (155 MB / ~4450 versions). By packed size the repo is 95.7% blobs, so tree/sharding/active-archive splits are the WRONG lever. Every ephemeral CI job and local clone pays the full history on clone.

## Key findings (verified this session)
1. Nothing reads the git HISTORY of .bridge_state — only the current worktree copy. Its history's sole value is debugging.
2. prev_snapshot is NOT redundant (an earlier "delete it" hypothesis was disproven): its direction-arbitration role IS superseded by the per-binding baseline in bindings.json, but it remains the load-bearing EDGE-TRIGGER ancestor (run_differs.py:198 -> differ.py:299 inbound-create). It is, however, grossly OVER-PROVISIONED: its live consumers need only the SET of Jira keys, not the full ACLI payload -> can shrink 24 MB -> ~25 KB and stop churning every pass.
3. bindings.json's dominant growth driver is `baseline_advanced_at`, a WRITE-ONLY timestamp bumped unconditionally on ~92% of entries every pass (never read) — so the file rewrites a scattered delta every pass (~987 versions ~= ~987 passes). Content is 97% baseline, 86% of which is the description stored as full ADF dict.
4. Storage posture is settled (epic 6c9c): .bridge_state stays committed on-branch as a merge=ours derived cache; event-sourcing/re-homing it (WS-1) was explicitly dropped. Trust verification is ancestry-based (survives a consistent history rewrite) EXCEPT the absolute-SHA enforce_since pin (rebar.toml:105).

## Plan (tabled; implement in order)
1. prev_snapshot -> bare KEY-SET (dict {jira_key:{}}), after clearing the open gate G1. + dead-code cleanup of the fixture-only prev plumbing.
2. bindings.json: CHURN GUARD (drop/guard baseline_advanced_at + write-when-changed in set_baseline; collapses version count) THEN TEXT NORMALIZE (adf_to_text + .name, -66%, no migration). DIGEST (-92%) optional, higher-risk, only behind a dual-write-shadow rollout, and EXCLUDE assignee (one-to-many match = REB-532 risk).
3. DEBUG TRAIL: a separate bounded full-Jira-snapshot artifact, max 1/day, 15-day retention, on a dated disjoint path, never fail-closed.
4. ONE-TIME coordinated history reclaim (filter-repo strip old .bridge_state blobs): a reconciler-paused, all-clones-converged 8-step flag-day with lockstep enforce_since re-pin. Do LAST.

## Open gates (resolve before implementing) — see session log [10]
- G1 (blocks step 1): resolve whether differ._compute_mutations_emit_both reaches Jira with a key-set prev (null-ancestor field-clear risk) via a corpus mutation-diff. THE critical fence.
- G2 (blocks digest): normalization parity + extend direction-preservation property suite first.
- G3: coordinate with the ACTIVE reconciler session (epic 58b0 sync-correctness) — shared differ/field contract; ride the proven dual-write-shadow -> N-divergent=0 -> flip rollout template.
- G4: enforce_since re-pin + converge ALL auto-pushing clones or --allow-unrelated-histories drags the stripped blobs back.

## Decisions already made
Debug trail = 1/day x 15-day; existing 337 MB = one-time coordinated reclaim; bindings.json investigated now (folded in). .bridge_state stays committed (required for ephemeral CI + local consistency).
baseline.summary: Bound tickets-repo growth: shrink reconciler .bridge_state on-branch (prev->key-set + bindings churn-guard/normalize) + one-time history reclaim

## Context

This epic tracks remediation of findings from the 2026-06-18 principal-engineer
maintenance audit of rebar (code debt, smells, architectural decay, separation
of concerns, doc accuracy, unit/dir size). The audit ran deterministic scans
(ruff/radon/vulture/ast-grep/jscpd/Serena) feeding seven single-perspective
subagents, then an **adversarial validation pass** (four subagents that read
every citation first-hand and tried to refute each finding). The re-run recipe
and tool list live in `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md`.

**Overall state: the codebase is healthy.** 0 mutable default args, 0 real bare
`except:`, only 2 high-confidence dead-code items, 2 TODO markers, no `__all__`
drift, no orphan modules, no unreachable code, the tree is clean for its own ruff
gate, and test investment tracks risk. The two load-bearing boundaries (the
engine `sys.path` seam and the LLM optionality/lazy-import contract) are intact
and runtime-verified. The debt is **localized and nameable**, captured in the
child stories below.

Severities below are the **validation-corrected** ones (several initial findings
were overstated and were downgraded after first-hand refutation; one was struck
entirely — see `docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md` for the methodology lesson).

## Children (in recommended execution order)

1. **[HIGH] Route `graph/_links.py` link writes through the canonical `_store` write path** — the one confirmed structural violation: a second write path bypassing the mandated single locked core.
2. **[HIGH] Run the LLM-optionality degradation tests in a no-extras CI lane** — the optionality safety-net (10 always-skipped test instances) currently runs in zero CI lanes.
3. **[MED] Documentation-truth sweep** — README still documents a deleted bash engine; event-schema version + event-type drift; one actively-false source comment; archive completed planning docs.
4. **[MED-HIGH] Refresh the module-size offenders table + give the CI size report teeth** — table is 50% stale; CI check is a warn-only `echo`.
5. **[MED] Fix the unresolved-alias blocker edge that can mis-report a ticket as ready** — the one validated wrong-answer broad-except; harden the answer-affecting sites.
6. **[MED] DRY the validated duplication clusters (F9/F4/F5/F2-F3/F7)**.
7. **[MED] Reduce accidental complexity in the reconciler differ/applier**.
8. **[LOW] Dead-code removal + low-severity hygiene cleanups**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 8 child stories exist as children (`parent_id`) of this epic with detailed implementation plans and citations.
- [ ] The two HIGH stories (graph write-path unification; optionality CI wiring) are completed first.
- [ ] Each story's own acceptance criteria are met and verified before it is closed.
- [ ] This epic is closed only after all children are closed or deferred-with-reason.
</content>

# Cloud Markdown↔ADF functions (pure capability; AdfCodec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Cloud stores rich text as ADF (structured JSON). The `RichTextCodec` seam (epic `e369`, story J3 / `aac8`) routes Cloud rich text through `AdfCodec` (`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`), a pass-through wrapper over the pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. **`adf.py`'s encode is plain-text-structured, not Markdown-aware:** `text_to_adf` (`adf.py:275`) splits the body on blank lines and emits each block as one `paragraph` node, so Markdown block syntax (headings, list markers, fenced code) and inline syntax (bold/strike/link) is carried as **literal characters** and Cloud renders raw source. Its `adf_to_text` (`adf.py:26`) already emits Markdown-ish text on decode; the missing half is a Markdown-aware **encode**.

**Why this story ships pure functions, not a codec change.** On Cloud, codec ops are reachable on the LIVE send path: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` fits the description that is posted, via `jira_fields.py:53` (`_shared_sanitize_description(..., fit=AdfCodec().fit_outbound)`) → `backend._JiraSanitizer.sanitize_description` → `acli.py:205` (`_text_to_adf(_sanitize_description(value))`). The description-compare sites also call `adf.py` directly (`outbound_fields.py:564`, `inbound_differ.py:210`). So **repointing `AdfCodec` ops in this story would change live Cloud truncation and comparison** — a cutover that must land together with echo-safety in `3388` (which depends on this story), never before it. To keep capability strictly separate from the hazardous cutover, **this story delivers only the new Markdown↔ADF functions in `adf.py` and their tests, and leaves `AdfCodec` a plain pass-through.** Nothing observable changes on merge.

## Prior art in this repo (the seam we build on — NOT greenfield)
- `RichTextCodec` Protocol — `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (four ops).
- `AdfCodec` (Cloud) — `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`; pass-through over
  `adf.py`, pinned by `test_rich_text_codec.py:198`
  (`test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module`), asserting
  `fit_outbound == adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`:205`),
  `to_wire == adf.text_to_adf` (`:207`), `decode_inbound == adf.adf_to_text(...)`
  (`:208`). **Left unchanged by this story;** `3388` updates these when it repoints.
- `adf.py` — `text_to_adf` (`:275`), `adf_to_text` (`:26`),
  `normalize_description` (`:310`), `fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`:341`). New functions
  are ADDED here; the existing plain ones stay for the live path + fallback.
- Live Cloud consumers of the codec/`adf.py` (rerouted later by `3388`):
  `jira_fields.py:53` (fit), `acli.py:205` / `acli_cli_ops.py:369` (encode),
  `outbound_fields.py:564` / `inbound_differ.py:210` (compare).

## Engine decision: vendored `marklas` (committed, not a spike)
Use **`marklas`** (pure-Python, mistune-based, MIT) for Markdown↔ADF, **vendored under `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` with its upstream provenance recorded**:
- Upstream: `https://github.com/byExist/marklas`; PyPI distribution `marklas`.
- Pin the exact upstream **version + commit sha in `pyproject.toml`**, and copy the
  upstream **MIT `LICENSE`** into `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/LICENSE` (single-
  maintainer bus-factor is mitigated by vendoring a pinned copy).

This is a **committed decision backed by a completed experiment**, not an open spike: a direct head-to-head against `adf.py` over a 5,730-body corpus (see the fixture below) measured marklas at **99.65% idempotent round-trip** (echo-safe under the reconciler's normalize-both-sides model) while producing **structurally-rich ADF for 56.7%** of bodies (56.3% both rich AND idempotent). The ≥99.6% AC below locks that measured bar in as a regression. Scripts + raw counts: session log `5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5`; `files/parity_*.py`, `files/parity-results.md`.

### Rejected alternative — extend `adf.py`'s handlers in-house
Weighed and **rejected on empirical grounds** (recorded here so the review sees the rationale). The appeal was that `adf.py`'s *decode* already emits Markdown-ish text, suggesting a symmetric *encode* is small. The corpus head-to-head refutes this for the half that matters — the **encode**:
- `adf.py`'s `text_to_adf` produces **0%** structurally-rich ADF over the 5,730
  bodies: it flattens **every** construct to paragraph text and emits **zero** ADF
  marks. Of the bodies marklas renders as structured ADF, `adf.py` renders **0**:
  headings (1,924), bullet lists (2,538), task lists (1,780), ordered lists (795),
  code blocks (280), tables (60), blockquotes (33), rules (72); inline marks strong
  (1,396), inline-code (2,569), em (439), strike (7), link (12) — all 0.
- `adf.py`'s 100% round-trip fidelity is therefore **trivial**: it translates no
  rich structure, so there is nothing to lose. It is a plain-text→paragraph
  encoder, not a Markdown↔ADF codec.
- Reaching marklas parity in-house means building a **full GFM→ADF parser + ADF→GFM
  serializer** — i.e. re-implementing marklas/mistune. The prior hand-rolled
  attempt stalled at **90.7%** fixed point, its residual tail being exactly the
  emphasis/mark serialization a bespoke engine gets wrong. Only the *decode* half
  overlaps; the *encode* is greenfield.

## Approach (pure functions in `adf.py`)
Add three functions to `adf.py`, wrappers over vendored marklas, **not referenced by any `AdfCodec` op or live send path in this story**:
1. `markdown_to_adf(md: str) -> dict` — Markdown-aware ADF encode.
2. `adf_to_markdown(doc: dict) -> str` — ADF→Markdown decode, applying a
   deterministic **mark-order canonicalizer** so co-located `strong`+`strikethrough`
   (`**~~x~~**` ⇄ `~~**x~~**`) has one canonical form (the one true 2-cycle
   oscillator; without this the pair never converges).
3. `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit(md: str, *, limit=…) -> str` — length-fit that
   measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization (so a future markdown-aware wire is
   bounded correctly).
Ship a helper that composes an idempotent round-trip `adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(t))` for the corpus test, and a **whole-codec plain-text fallback** helper (returns the plain `adf.py` functions as a set) that `3388` will install on conversion error — defined and unit-tested here, wired there.

## Corpus fixture (evaluability)
The 99.65% idempotence and the rich-coverage counts are measured against a **vendored** fixture, `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (a sanitized snapshot of the 5,730 ticket bodies, committed into the repo — NOT re-exported from a live store at test time), so `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence` is hermetic and reproducible in-session. The test asserts BOTH the ≥99.6% idempotent ratio AND the body count (5,730) so the fixture cardinality is guarded.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for this story (owned by `3388`)
- Repointing the four `AdfCodec` ops to the Markdown-aware functions + installing
  the whole-codec fallback, and updating the pin test at
  `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`.
- Rerouting the live Cloud consumers — `jira_fields.py:53` fit,
  `acli.py:205`/`acli_cli_ops.py:369` encode, `outbound_fields.py:564` /
  `inbound_differ.py:210` compare — to the Markdown-aware functions (paired so the
  send-fit and compare-fit stay the identical transform), the once-only re-emit
  migration, the second-pass convergence proof, and rollback.
This story changes no `AdfCodec` op and no live send site, so no observable Cloud behavior changes on merge.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/adf.py` — add `markdown_to_adf` / `adf_to_markdown`
  (+ mark-order canonicalizer) / `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` + the plain-fallback
  helper; existing plain functions untouched.
- `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` — vendored, sha-pinned copy + upstream `LICENSE`.
- `pyproject.toml` — record the vendored upstream version + sha.
- `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (new) — vendored, sanitized 5,730-body corpus.
- **Guard (UNCHANGED):** `AdfCodec` and its four ops
  (`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`); the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` (ticket 21ca; also used by sibling repo
  `agentic-dev-platform`); the live sites `jira_fields.py:53`, `acli.py:205`,
  `acli_cli_ops.py:369`, `outbound_fields.py:564`, `inbound_differ.py:210` (all
  rerouted by `3388`).
- `tests/` — unit tests for the new functions + the corpus idempotence test.

## Testing (pure-function unit + fixture-corpus only — no live send)
- **Structured round trip:** heading+checklist+inline-code+link round-trips
  MD→ADF→MD to a fixed point via `markdown_to_adf`/`adf_to_markdown`, asserting ADF
  node types (`test_cloud_adf_roundtrip`).
- **Mark-order oscillation:** the two known combined strong+strikethrough bodies
  converge in ≤1 pass under `adf_to_markdown`; a permutation property test asserts
  100% convergence.
- **Fit measures the real wire:** `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` bounds the
  `markdown_to_adf` serialization, not the plain encode
  (`test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`).
- **Corpus idempotence:** over the vendored `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/`, the
  round-trip is idempotent (normalize-both-sides stable, `r(r(x))==r(x)`) for
  ≥99.6% of the bodies AND the fixture holds 5,730 bodies
  (`test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`; measured 99.65%).
- **Codec untouched:** `AdfCodec` stays a plain pass-through — the existing
  `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` stays green unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `marklas` is vendored under `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` with its upstream
  `github.com/byExist/marklas` version + commit sha recorded in `pyproject.toml`
  and its MIT `LICENSE` copied alongside; verified by an import/provenance test
  asserting the pinned sha and the presence of the MIT license text.
- [ ] `adf.markdown_to_adf` emits Markdown-aware ADF (heading/list/code/emphasis
  nodes, not literal `#`/`-`/`**`) and `adf.adf_to_markdown` returns the source
  Markdown; verified by `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting node types and decoded
  equality.
- [ ] The combined strong+strikethrough oscillation is eliminated by the mark-order
  canonicalizer in `adf_to_markdown`; verified by the regression + permutation
  property test (100% convergence).
- [ ] `adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization;
  verified by `test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`.
- [ ] Over the vendored `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` the MD→ADF→MD round-trip
  is idempotent for ≥99.6% of bodies and the fixture holds 5,730 bodies; verified
  by `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`.
- [ ] `AdfCodec` and its four ops remain a plain pass-through and the live send
  sites are unchanged by this story; verified by the existing
  `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` staying green
  unmodified (the observable cutover is `3388`).
baseline.summary: Cloud ADF codec (marklas), truly bidirectional

baseline.description:
## Why
The plan-review calibration epic (6982) can cheaply measure DETECTION on KNOWN-seeded defects (E2) and
judge RELIABILITY via self-consistency (E6), and it can lean on the gate's own persisted sidecar
validity/impact. What it CANNOT currently produce is an **independent finding-level TP/FP gold set** — a
verdict on the gate's surface/drop decisions from a standard OTHER than the gate itself. That gold set is
the missing ingredient for measuring the gate's PRECISION on REAL plans (false-positive rate) and for
calibrating Pass-2's sub-question / impact-axis thresholds against ground truth rather than the gate's own
opinion. This idea parks that work, DESIGNED ENOUGH to resume, once human adjudication time is budgeted.

## Context — why the first attempt (E1's adjudication corpus) was invalidated
The E1 finding-adjudication corpus was labeled by a process WEAKER than the gate it judged and is invalid
(79% of labels contaminated). Two root causes, both to AVOID here:
1. The LLM rater saw a TRUNCATED plan (PLAN_CAP=6000 chars); production reviews the WHOLE plan + children.
2. The LLM rater ran single-pass with NO tools; production runs 16 criteria as AGENTIC finders that grep
   the codebase. The human adjudication inherited the flaw (dispute set selected by the faulty process,
   anchored on faulty rationales, not independently code-grounded). Re-running the gate's OWN grounded
   verifier to label is CIRCULAR (it just reproduces the sidecar). So the gold set MUST come from
   independent HUMAN judgment, made efficient by grounded evidence.

## What (design — hard-won constraints)
Build a stratified, review-time-faithful, human-adjudicated finding-level TP/FP gold set:
- **Sample:** reuse the surviving E1 finding SAMPLE (300 surfaced + 100 dropped, text-bearing, positionally
  bucketed by coverage.counts, stratified by criterion). Over-weight the code-grounded criteria
  (E4/G1G2/G3/G4/G6/G7/T1/T3/T5c/T8/T10/T11/T13/T14/A1/removal-rationale) and the surfaced/dropped boundary,
  where the gate is hardest to judge.
- **Adjudicator capability floor (non-negotiable):** the human must judge each finding with (a) the WHOLE
  plan + children (never truncated), and (b) the finding's cited code. Provide GROUNDED EVIDENCE via the
  already-prototyped reuse pipeline (harnesses/grounded_batch_adjudicate.py + verify_single_finding.yaml):
  it reruns production's plan-review-verifier-agentic (assemble_context + get_runner agentic + pai_tools
  codebase tools) to surface the cited code, the binary sub-answers, and the impact axes — so the human
  adjudicates efficiently, NOT from raw text. The human JUDGMENT stays independent of the gate (do not adopt
  the verifier's label as truth — use its evidence).
- **Review-time grounding (required):** ground each finding at the commit its review ran against. Recover it
  from the ticket's REVIEW_RESULT event timestamps -> the contemporaneous origin/main SHA (git rev-list -1
  --before). Current-HEAD grounding is biased (drift flips verdicts: e165 moved dropped->advisory).
- **Plan-version fidelity (required):** restrict to plan_matches_review=True tickets (~85%/165 of 195 in the
  E1 sample; compare the review round's material_fingerprint to the current one). Exclude drifted-plan
  tickets (the finding is about a plan that no longer exists) unless old-plan reconstruction is added.
- **Reliability:** double-adjudicate a stratified subset by a second human; report a prevalence-robust
  agreement (Gwet AC1 / raw agreement), NOT bare Cohen's kappa (TP-skew triggers the kappa paradox).
- **Deliverable:** a frozen gold JSONL {finding_id, ticket_id, review_sha, plan_matches_review, human_label
  (TP/FP), adjudicator, grounded_evidence_ref}, plus the gate's own sidecar call per finding, so the
  human-vs-gate DELTA localizes which Pass-2 sub-questions/axes miscalibrate.

## How it enriches epic 6982
- Gives E2/E3/R1 a real FP/TP standard to calibrate blocking thresholds + measure precision on REAL plans
  (complements E2's construct-valid seeded-defect detection ground truth).
- Turns E6 from self-consistency-only into self-consistency-vs-truth (does a stable judge also agree with the
  human gold?).
- The human-vs-verifier deltas are the direct refinement backlog for the Pass-2 verification questions.

## Cost / prerequisite
The BINDING constraint is human adjudication TIME (this is why it is deferred, not the LLM cost — the grounded
evidence pipeline is ~$0.30/finding). Budget/staff the human adjudication before promoting idea->open. The
machinery (sample, grounded evidence harness, review-time resolver) already exists from the E1 session.

## Acceptance Criteria (for when promoted idea -> open)
- [ ] A stratified human-adjudicated gold set of >= N findings (choose N by human budget) is committed, each
      row grounded at its review-time SHA with plan_matches_review=True and grounded evidence attached.
- [ ] A double-adjudicated subset reports prevalence-robust inter-adjudicator agreement (Gwet AC1 + raw).
- [ ] The gate's sidecar call is recorded beside each human label; the human-vs-gate delta table is produced
      and handed to the Pass-2-refinement stories.
- [ ] The adjudication protocol (whole-plan + code-grounded + review-time + independent human judgment) is
      documented so the gold set is reproducible and defensibly independent of the gate.
baseline.summary: Human-adjudicated finding-level TP/FP gold corpus (independent, grounded, review-time-faithful) — future enrichment for the plan-review calibration epic

# Release build fails: check_build_env_locked doesn't PEP 503-normalize package names

The hash-locked `--no-isolation` release build aborts because
`scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` compares package names WITHOUT PEP 503
canonicalization, so a package whose `pip freeze` name uses `.`/`_` but whose lock
entry uses `-` is falsely reported "installed but ABSENT from the lock", failing the
build job and blocking every release.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Dispatch `release.yml` from `main` (v0.8.0 attempt, run 29467136412).
2. The `Build distributions (build-once)` job runs
   `python scripts/check_build_env_locked.py --lock .github/release-requirements.txt --freeze <(pip freeze)`.
3. It exits 1 with: `jaraco.classes==3.4.0: installed but ABSENT from the lock` (also
   `jaraco.context`, `jaraco.functools`, `pyproject_hooks`, `readme_renderer`).

Local repro:
`python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import check_build_env_locked as m;print(set(m._parse_pins('jaraco-classes==3.4.0'))==set(m._parse_pins('jaraco.classes==3.4.0')))"`
prints `False`.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** `jaraco.classes` (from `pip freeze`) and `jaraco-classes` (in the
  pip-compile lock) are recognized as the SAME package (PEP 503: runs of `[-_.]`
  collapse to a single `-`), so the subset check passes and the build proceeds.
- **Actual:** the two spellings hash to different keys, so the installed package is
  judged absent from the lock and the build FAILS — even though it is pinned.

## Root cause

`_parse_pins` lowercases the name and strips an `[extra]` suffix but does not apply PEP
503 name normalization. `build`/`twine`'s transitive deps (`jaraco-classes/-context/
-functools`, `readme-renderer`, `pyproject-hooks`) are pinned in the lock with hyphens
but reported by `pip freeze` with dots/underscores, so they never match. This is the
first release through the new pinned build-once pipeline (08a8/6168 landed after v0.7.1),
so the mismatch was never exercised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_build_env_locked.py` canonicalizes every package name with PEP 503
  normalization (`re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()`) on BOTH the lock and freeze
  sides before comparing (verify: the two spellings map to one key —
  `python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import check_build_env_locked as m;assert set(m._parse_pins('jaraco-classes==3.4.0'))==set(m._parse_pins('jaraco.classes==3.4.0'))"`).
- [ ] A regression test in `tests/unit/test_check_build_env_locked.py` fails before the
  fix and passes after: a lock with `jaraco-classes==3.4.0` and a freeze with
  `jaraco.classes==3.4.0` (and an `_`/`.` variant) is accepted as lock-consistent
  (`main([...]) == 0`), and a genuine version mismatch on a normalized name still fails.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass, and re-dispatching `release.yml`
  from `main` with `version=0.8.0` gets past the build's env-lock guard.
baseline.summary: Release build fails: check_build_env_locked missing PEP 503 name normalization

## Context / Problem
The reconcile-bridge-canary workflow carries ~200 lines of production logic in YAML run-blocks — staleness classification, two alert-ticket lifecycle state machines (heartbeat + binding-drift), each with find/open/comment/close steps. This is the highest-defect shell surface (449f: 7 recommendations), untestable and unlintable by ruff. The companion reconcile-bridge.yml push-back loop was ALSO a defect source (4c4f), but that loop's fix deliberately kept it in YAML under a verbatim-execution test — see Alternatives below.

## Alternatives / prior art
tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (ticket 4c4f) established that CAS push loops on the hot tickets ref stay in workflow YAML and are tested VERBATIM (extracting them creates an untested-glue drift seam; the block contains zero ${{ }} expressions so the YAML itself is executable under test). This plan honors that decision: BOTH CAS push loops — reconcile-bridge.yml "Commit reconciler events back and push" (93L) and the canary's "Flush any unpushed ticket changes" (35L) — are OUT of scope and stay in YAML. What migrates is classification/alert-lifecycle logic, which differs from the push loops in kind: it has branchy decision logic (API-error vs zero-state vs stale; dedup-find vs open vs comment vs close), no git-ref CAS races, and it currently interleaves ${{ }} expressions with logic — exactly the shape that benefits from extraction + unit tests. The drift-seam risk the 4c4f rationale warns about is mitigated the same way the probe port (f1eb) mitigated it: an anti-rot unit test pins the thin YAML invocations (workflow parses, step invokes the canonical Python entry point with the expected env/args), and the extracted functions carry their own unit tests.

Deployment note: the f1eb executes-from-main trap does NOT apply here — gerrit-verify.yaml never runs the canary, and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml executes from main on schedule/workflow_dispatch only AFTER this change merges, so workflow edits and the new script deploy atomically; no transitional shim is needed.

The reconcile-bridge raw git write (the 93L commit-back loop) is NOT routed through the library write seam: it is workflow-only orchestration on a dedicated CI worktree, and the seam's own code warns a whole-index commit there races normal store writes. Instead, the raw-git-write lint child (d37e) allowlists the two verbatim-tested YAML loops as documented exceptions; this ticket records that contract in the migrated module's docstring.

## Approach
Strangler-fig on reconcile-bridge-canary.yml only: move the four logic families into one Python module invoked by thin YAML steps.
1. scripts/canary_bridge.py (new, single module, ~250-400 LOC): subcommands
   - check-heartbeat: GitHub API query (gh api via subprocess, injected runner seam) + classification {api-error->transient/no-alert, no-success-runs->stale(never), older-than-window->stale, fresh->ok}; emits GITHUB_OUTPUT keys (stale, last_run_ago, status_msg) exactly as today.
   - heartbeat-alert: the find/open/comment/close lifecycle against rebar CLI (find existing open alert by marker tag, open when stale+none, comment when still stale, close on recovery) — one function per transition, dedup pattern preserved. Error handling — PRESERVE each step's existing failure disposition (verified against the YAML), not a blanket rule: (a) alert-lifecycle WRITES (create/comment/transition close) have NO fallback in YAML today -> stay FAIL LOUD (non-zero exit -> red canary run; a silently swallowed alert-write failure would defeat the canary); (b) the dedup FINDs (`rebar list ... || echo ''`, YAML lines 218-219/341-342) deliberately degrade to empty -> the subcommand preserves fail-soft-to-not-found (treat CLI failure as 'no existing alert'); (c) check-binding-drift: `rebar bridge-fsck` exits 1 BY DESIGN when it finds drift (the signal the canary exists to detect; YAML line 316 `|| true`) -> the subcommand captures stdout regardless of exit code, parses JSON, and treats unparseable/empty output as empty drift data exactly as the YAML python block does today — exit 1 with valid JSON is DRIFT (alert path), never an error; unit tests cover each disposition: fsck-exit-1-with-drift-JSON -> drift reported; fsck-garbage-output -> empty drift; alert-write failure -> non-zero exit. DRY_RUN: the step-level `if: env.DRY_RUN == 'false'` gates stay in YAML, AND the subcommands re-check DRY_RUN from env and short-circuit all rebar writes when 'true' (defense in depth against a dropped `if:`).
   - check-binding-drift + binding-drift-alert: same two shapes for the second alert family.
2. Thin YAML: each replaced step becomes env + `python scripts/canary_bridge.py <subcommand>`; ${{ }} values pass via env, keeping logic expression-free.
3. Anti-rot test pins the wiring (canary workflow invokes scripts/canary_bridge.py subcommands; no logic-bearing run-blocks reappear beyond the allowlisted flush loop).
4. reconcile-bridge.yml is untouched except NO changes needed — its 13L exit-code case on "Run reconciler" is workflow-native annotation glue (::notice/::error) and stays.

## Scope
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml: 10 logic steps -> thin invocations (Check last successful run; Log canary result; Find/Open/Comment/Close heartbeat alert; Check binding-drift; Find/Open/Comment/Close drift alert). The flush loop and plumbing steps (mount, install, identity, signing key, seed, fail-on-stale) stay.
- scripts/canary_bridge.py: new module with the four subcommands.
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py: unit tests for classification + lifecycle transitions.
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py or a sibling anti-rot test: pin the canary wiring.
- tests/unit/test_reconcile_bridge_canary_class.py: RE-POINT — it asserts every `rebar transition ... closed` in the canary YAML carries --class (bug 0e15/ed13 guard); the close-on-recovery commands move to Python, so the guard becomes an assertion on scripts/canary_bridge.py's close calls (the protection survives, relocated).
- Verified-unaffected consumers (enumerated; assertions target steps that STAY): tests/interfaces/store/test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py (parametrizes over reconcile-bridge-canary.yml; asserts fetch-depth:0 + merge-not-rebase invariants — the checkout/merge plumbing stays in YAML untouched); tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py (mount->init->first-merge ordering + no manual ours-driver — plumbing and flush stay in YAML), tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py (checkout `with:` inputs — checkout untouched), tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py (workflow `name:` — unchanged), tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py (bridge file untouched).
- pyproject.toml: T201 per-file-ignore for the new operational script — matching the LANDED legitimate-print entries (scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py, scripts/retarget_jira_project.py, scripts/check_server_manifest.py); f1eb's probe_rebar.py entry additionally lands before this via change 1275, stacked earlier in this epic.

## Testing
- Unit: classification matrix (api-error, never-succeeded, stale, fresh, malformed window input), each lifecycle transition (open-when-none, dedup-when-open, comment-when-still-stale, close-on-recovery, no-op paths), GITHUB_OUTPUT emission format, the rebar-error path (runner raises -> subcommand exits non-zero, loud), and a DRY_RUN=true case asserting ZERO rebar mutations. Runner seam injected (no live gh/rebar in unit tier).
- Anti-rot: workflow YAML parses; each replaced step invokes the module subcommand; flush loop still present verbatim (guard against accidental migration).
- Parity: trigger reconcile-bridge-canary.yml via workflow_dispatch in-session after merge; compare step outcomes/annotations to the last pre-migration scheduled run.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Canary logic steps reduced to env + single-command invocations; classification/lifecycle logic lives in scripts/canary_bridge.py with unit tests.
- [x] Both CAS push loops (bridge commit-back, canary flush) remain in YAML byte-identical to pre-change; test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py still passes.
- [x] Anti-rot test pins the canary wiring (invocations + no new logic-bearing run-blocks).
- [x] tests/scripts suite green; lint/typecheck green.
- [x] [operator-attested] One workflow_dispatch canary run post-merge shows parity (same stale/fresh classification and alert behavior as the preceding scheduled run); run id + outcome recorded in a ticket comment before close.

## File impact
- .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml (edit)
- scripts/canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge.py (new)
- tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py (edit, or sibling anti-rot module)
- pyproject.toml (edit: T201 ignore)
