## Why

External creation paths have different semantics from local facades. A Jira issue materialized locally is a jira creation, while an existing local ticket later pushed to Jira keeps its original channel. NDJSON import creates a fresh local record through import while source_* continues to describe the prior store. Historical Jira records need a conservative answer without rewriting shared event history.

## What

- Add creation_channel=jira to the CREATE data assembled only by the inbound Jira materialization path in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py. That direct writer calls validate_creation_channel("jira") from reducer/_version.py before writing because it bypasses create_core. For placeholder identities, _ensure_inbound_assignee_identity passes creation_channel="jira" through rebar.ensure_identity_for -> identity.ensure_identity_for -> create_identity_core -> create_core. The dependency story owns these signatures with python defaults; this story owns only the Jira argument at the inbound boundary.
- Preserve the original cli, mcp, or python channel when a local ticket is later bound or pushed outbound to Jira; sync direction must not rewrite genesis provenance.
- Have src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py invoke the shared library creation path with the internal import channel. The newly created local ticket reports import even when the exported source record contains another creation_channel. Existing source_id/source_created_at/source_author/source_env behavior remains unchanged.
- Add _project_legacy_creation_channel(state: dict) -> None in reducer/_processors.py. It is a no-op only when state has a concrete recorded value (cli, mcp, python, jira, or import) or creation_channel_inferred=true. An absent, None, or provisional unknown value without the marker is unresolved legacy input: the helper reads state["ticket_id"], state.get("author"), plus state.get("env_id"), then sets either jira with creation_channel_inferred=true or unknown with the marker absent. Call it at the end of process_create after ticket_id/author/env_id and recorded CREATE data have folded. This state-shaped interface is shared unchanged by process_snapshot in child 568c. Define LEGACY_JIRA_AUTHOR="reconciler" plus LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID="reconciler" in reducer/_version.py. inbound_translate._event_meta performs the absolute package import from rebar.reducer._version inside the function body for its default author/env values, following the existing late-import pattern, and the reducer helper imports the same constants normally. The absolute rebar.* import is compatible with the existing isolated spec loader and does not rely on sibling rebar_reconciler package context; extend the spec-load contract test to pin it. When creation_channel is missing, infer jira only if ticket_id starts with "jira-", author equals LEGACY_JIRA_AUTHOR, and env_id equals LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID. Missing/None or env-overridden historical signals are mismatches. On a match set creation_channel=jira plus creation_channel_inferred=true; on every mismatch set creation_channel=unknown and omit the marker.
- Base inference only on creation-stable state. Do not inspect current tags, current Jira bindings, source_* fields, comments, or mutable reconciler state.
- Add positive and one-signal-at-a-time negative tests so a locally crafted title/tag/binding cannot trigger inference.
- Document recorded versus inferred Jira provenance, the import/source_* distinction, and the diagnostic trust boundary: creation_channel_inferred is heuristic audit metadata, not a security attestation. Extend test_schema_coverage.py to pin that statement.

## Approach Rationale

New external writers declare their channel because they know it exactly. Historical inference is limited to the deterministic ID/author/environment conjunction already produced by the legacy reconciler: inbound_translate._jira_key_to_local_id generates jira-* IDs; _event_meta uses the shared LEGACY_JIRA_AUTHOR and LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID constants, each exactly "reconciler", as defaults. A function-local absolute import from rebar.reducer._version is the chosen sharing seam because spec-loaded reconciler modules already resolve installed rebar.* package imports through established late-import paths; a contract test loads inbound_translate through the isolated loader, calls _event_meta, and asserts both defaults, preventing either resolution failure or duplicated-literal drift. Requiring all three signals prioritizes zero false positives; overridden, missing, or incomplete legacy metadata intentionally returns unknown.

## Scope

IN: Jira inbound CREATE, Jira-side-effect identity creation, outbound non-rewrite behavior, NDJSON import, full-log legacy Jira inference, negative controls, export/import semantics, and documentation.

OUT: guessing historical local channels, mutating old events, treating Jira binding as creation, executing SNAPSHOT-only legacy inference (the helper interface intentionally supports it; child 568c owns the call and tests), compaction, and new filtering/reporting surfaces.

## Files

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py and inbound_translate.py call sites: recorded Jira channel and side-effect identities.
- src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py and _io/_provenance.py: recorded import channel while preserving source_*.
- src/rebar/reducer/_version.py and src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py: shared exact legacy Jira constants used through an absolute package import by producer defaults and reducer inference.
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_env_aliasing.py: isolated spec-load coverage for the shared constants and exact defaults.
- src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py: shared deterministic legacy projection helper.
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_creation_channel_jira.py: Jira inbound/outbound and inference controls.
- tests/interfaces/io/test_creation_channel_import.py and test_export_ndjson.py: import/export behavior.
- docs/event-schema.md, docs/cli-reference.md, and docs/output-schemas.md: Jira/import channel semantics in event, CLI, and public output contracts.

## Dependencies

Depends on the local-contract story because it supplies the enum, writer validation, reducer field, and public output contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A newly materialized inbound Jira issue and any placeholder identity created by that path persist validated creation_channel=jira, independent of reconciler author/env overrides; the direct writer rejects an off-vocabulary injected value. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_creation_channel_jira.py -k inbound_recorded.
- [ ] Binding or pushing an existing cli/mcp/python ticket to Jira never changes its stored or projected creation_channel. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_creation_channel_jira.py -k outbound.
- [ ] NDJSON import persists creation_channel=import on the new local CREATE, preserves source_* provenance, and does not copy the exported source ticket channel into the new local channel. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/io/test_creation_channel_import.py -k import.
- [ ] NDJSON export includes creation_channel plus creation_channel_inferred when present, using the TicketState output contract without a parallel serializer rule, and the full export suite remains green. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson.py.
- [ ] A legacy full-log ticket with no recorded channel projects jira plus creation_channel_inferred=true only when jira-* ID, reconciler author, and reconciler env_id all match exactly. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_creation_channel_jira.py -k legacy_positive.
- [ ] Removing or changing each inference signal independently produces creation_channel=unknown with no inference marker; tags, bindings, source_* metadata, and titles never affect the decision. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_creation_channel_jira.py -k legacy_negative.
- [ ] Existing import idempotency and reconciler inbound behavior remain green. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/interfaces/io/test_import_idempotency.py tests/interfaces/io/test_import_ndjson.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py.
- [ ] Isolated spec-loading of inbound_translate resolves the shared legacy constants plus exact defaults without sibling-package context. TicketState output regression remains green. docs/output-schemas.md states that creation_channel_inferred is diagnostic metadata rather than a security attestation. Prove with uv run pytest -q tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_env_aliasing.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py && make lint.

baseline.description:
# Authenticated identity — entity + authorship certification + provider-neutral user mapping

## Context
rebar has no real concept of **who** performed an operation: `author` is `git config user.name`, an
unauthenticated free string anyone with push access to `origin/tickets` can forge. Two needs follow:
(1) attribute ticket events to a **real person** so activity is auditable and non-repudiable, and
(2) map that person to **external ticket-system users** (Jira now; GitHub Issues / Linear later) so
sync assigns work to the right person. **Beneficiary:** projects syncing to external trackers (correct
assignee/reporter attribution, wrong or lost today) and anyone auditing "who did this." This epic
depends on the **asymmetric attestation foundation** for its signing substrate.

## Approach (and why)
Adopt **git-bug's** identity model on rebar's existing event machinery, filling its gaps:
- **Identity = a first-class entity** whose event log IS its version chain (rebar already has
  event-sourcing / replay / snapshot). Stable **opaque rebar id** as the handle — **not**
  self-certifying; the signing key provides tamper-evidence, not the id. Attributes: `name`, `email`,
  `{provider, external_id}` external mappings, and **public** keys only.
- **Attribution always** (name+email denormalized on every event, git-style) + an optional
  `author_id` reference + an optional **authorship signature** — a new attestation kind on the
  foundation's substrate (namespace `rebar.authorship.v1`).
- **Trust root = the identity's in-band public keys**, TOFU on the genesis key + **G2** (key add/
  rotate/revoke must be signed by a currently-valid key). Safe for authorship: low authority, cannot
  forge another person's signatures; the worst case from a bad TOFU binding is a display-name dispute.
- **Provider-neutral mapping.** `{provider, external_id}` keys on the provider's **opaque stable id**,
  never email. Jira is the **first adapter** behind a provider seam; an unmapped inbound user mints a
  **placeholder** that idempotently auto-upgrades.
- **Deliberate creation.** A normal write never auto-mints an identity **entity**; identities are
  created explicitly or as a mapping target (see the default-install invariant below).

## Mechanisms (concrete definitions — these resolve the load-bearing terms)
- **Private key material.** Authorship signing uses the developer's **existing SSH private key** via
  `ssh-agent` / `~/.ssh`; it is **never** stored in the repo or on the `tickets` branch. The identity
  entity stores only **public** keys, and a write-time guard rejects any attempt to place private-key
  material into an identity event.
- **Era (key-validity window) = position in the `tickets`-branch commit graph, refined by intra-commit
  index.** rebar's HLC is **per-ticket** (`hlc.next_tick(tracker, ticket_id)` in
  `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py`), so it gives no global cross-ticket sequence. Events reach the
  `tickets` branch either singly (`event_append.stage_and_commit`, one event per commit) or in bulk
  (`event_append.batch_stage_and_commit`, **N events in one commit**), so commit **ancestry** is the
  global merged order, **refined by a stable `intra_idx`** (an event's 0-based rank
  within its commit when that commit's event files are sorted by `(timestamp, uuid)` — a deterministic,
  insertion-independent order computed from the committed events themselves, not git's lexicographic
  tree order; 0 for single-event commits; nothing extra is stored). Each event therefore has a position `(commit, intra_idx)`, and
  the same commit-graph is what git-bug uses for `ValidKeysAtTime`. Each key record binds
  `{pubkey, added_at:(commit,intra_idx), revoked_at:(commit,intra_idx)?}`. Key K is **valid for** an
  event E iff E's position is **>= added_at and < revoked_at** (when set), where positions compare by
  commit ancestry first (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) and, when two positions share a commit, by
  `intra_idx` — no wall-clock, no fabricated global sequence. Multi-clone reconcile yields one merged
  graph, so validity is deterministic once merged; the authoritative check runs on that merged branch.
- **Verification state — reuse the existing `verdict` enum (do not invent a parallel one).** The
  authorship result reuses the 4-value verdict enum already defined in
  `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` — `certified`, `unsigned`, `foreign_key`,
  `mismatch` — **extended** with one new value `key_not_valid_at_era` (added to that same schema). The
  human-facing `show`/`fsck` display collapses these into a trichotomy: **verified** = `certified`;
  **unsigned** = `unsigned`; **unverified** = `foreign_key` | `mismatch` | `key_not_valid_at_era`.
  There is **no** separate reason field — the `verdict` value IS the reason.
- **The "merge gate" (the real control).** rebar's `tickets` branch auto-pushes to `origin/tickets`
  with no GitHub pre-receive hook, so enforcement is a **CI verification job** — a GitHub Actions
  workflow on the `tickets` branch that runs `rebar verify-identity` / `fsck` over the **merged** log
  and **fails the check** (non-zero exit + a structured per-event report → red commit status / alert)
  on any `unsigned`/`unverified` event **when** the project sets `identity.require_authenticated=true`.
  This is **detect-and-fail-on-the-merged-log**, not pre-receive rejection (the honest limitation of a
  hookless remote); the local write-gate is only a fast-fail UX affordance. Enforcement is scoped by a
  **cutover ref** `identity.enforce_since` (a `tickets`-branch commit recorded when the project first
  enables enforcement): the CI job runs `verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <enforce_since>`,
  so only events at/after the cutover can fail — pre-cutover events are **grandfathered** (reported,
  not failed). Deployment prerequisite: enable the workflow, set `identity.require_authenticated=true`,
  and record `identity.enforce_since` at the enabling commit.
- **Authorship attestation shape.** The DSSE envelope is `{payload, payloadType, signatures}` — DSSE
  has **no `subject` field** (that is an in-toto concept). The **payload** is an in-toto-style Statement
  whose `subject` binds the signed event as `{event_uuid, content_hash}`, with
  `payloadType = "application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json"`; the signature covers
  `PAE(payloadType, payload)`. Because the binding lives in the Statement `subject`, a signature cannot
  be lifted to another event. If the signing key is unavailable at write time, the event is authored
  **unsigned** (Tier 0) — the write never blocks.
- **Placeholder create-path.** The identity create path supports **system-minted placeholders** (no
  user present, no keys, partial data): `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)`,
  owned by the entity child and consumed by the inbound-ghost child.
- **Modify-Reporter constraint.** Setting the Jira `reporter` field via REST requires the project's
  Jira role to hold the **"Modify Reporter"** permission; without it, reporter sync degrades to
  assignee-only (documented), never hard-fails.
- **Default-install invariant.** With zero identity configuration, behavior is byte-identical to
  pre-feature: a write succeeds with the denormalized git author (name+email — this is the git commit
  author, already public in commit metadata, so it is **not** new email exposure; the "no broadcast"
  property is specifically that **no identity entity with keys/mappings is auto-minted** by a normal
  write), and `list`/`ready`/gates behave identically.

- **`verify-identity` CLI (the enforcement tool).** `rebar verify-identity [--require-authenticated]
  [--since <ref>] [--format text|json]` scans events on the merged `tickets` log (optionally since a
  ref), computes each event's verification state, and emits one **report entry** per event (all events
  in `--format json`; only non-`verified` in text). **Exit code:** non-zero iff any `unsigned`/
  `unverified` event is found under `--require-authenticated`; `0` otherwise (advisory without the
  flag). The CI merge-gate job runs it with `--require-authenticated`.
- **Report-entry schema.** `{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit (tickets-branch SHA), author (name+email),
  author_id?, verdict: <a verify_signature_result verdict, incl. the new key_not_valid_at_era>,
  display: "verified"|"unverified"|"unsigned"}`. `fsck` embeds the same entries; the `verdict` is the
  single source of the failure reason (no separate reason field).
- **Compaction survival (concrete).** A SNAPSHOT records, per folded signed event, a verification tuple
  `{event_uuid, content_hash, signature, signer_pubkey, position:(commit,intra_idx)}`, so a compacted signed event
  re-verifies (signature checked against the recorded `content_hash`; era resolved by comparing the
  recorded event `position` against the signer key's `added_at`/`revoked_at`) without the original event
  object. `process_snapshot` surfaces these tuples; a
  round-trip test asserts a compacted signed event still returns `verified`.
- **TOFU genesis base case.** The genesis key-add is **self-signed** — signed by the very key it
  introduces — and its `added_at_commit` is the identity's genesis commit; it is valid for every event
  whose commit is a descendant of (or equal to) that genesis commit. This is the base case of the G2
  "signed by a currently-valid key" rule (the recursion bottoms out at the self-signed genesis = TOFU);
  every later key change must be signed by an already-valid key.
- **Jira bootstrap availability + fallback.** Seeding `accountId` from email via
  `GET /rest/api/3/user/search` requires the integration's Jira role to hold **"Browse users and
  groups"** and returns nothing when the target's email is privacy-hidden — so it is best-effort with
  an explicit fallback chain: (1) an operator-provided mapping (a config/CSV of `identity → accountId`);
  (2) resolve `accountId` from existing Jira data where the user is already assignee/reporter on synced
  issues; (3) else degrade to project-default assignee (`-1`)/unassigned and leave the mapping unset for
  later repair. Never hard-fail, never block a sync.

## Scope
- **In:** the `identity` entity (a new ticket-type on the `session_log` exemption pattern); event
  attribution fields; the authorship attestation kind on the foundation's substrate; the TOFU + G2 key
  chain with era-scoped validity; the provider-neutral mapping + Jira adapter + placeholder/auto-upgrade;
  reconciler outbound assignee/reporter + inbound ghost; opt-in enforcement (local write-gate + the CI
  merge-gate verify job + fsck marking); snapshot/compaction carrying folded identities + signatures;
  docs + ADR.
- **Out:** the signing substrate itself (foundation epic); operation-cert behavior (op-cert epic);
  DSSE transparency-log / keyless follow-ons; **actual** GitHub Issues / Linear sync (the adapter seam
  must not preclude them, but wiring them is separate).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new `identity` ticket-type exists and is exempt from lifecycle / gates / graph / Jira-sync
      (mirrors `session_log`); a create path mints one carrying name, email, `{provider,external_id}`
      mappings, and **public** keys, and a `create_placeholder(provider, external_id, display_name)`
      path mints a keyless partial-data placeholder. Verified by creating both, asserting `show`
      renders the fields, and asserting exclusion from `ready`/`next_batch`/default `list`.
- [ ] Every mutating event carries a denormalized `author` name + email; an optional `author_id`
      references an identity. Regression test: existing events without `author_id`/email still replay
      to the same state.
- [ ] An `authorship` kind wraps an in-toto Statement payload (its `subject` binds `{event_uuid,
      content_hash}`) in a DSSE envelope (`payloadType application/vnd.rebar.authorship.v1+json`), signed
      via the foundation substrate over `PAE(payloadType, payload)`, and
      verifies offline against the identity's in-band keys; a test asserts an event signed by identity A
      does not verify against B, a tampered event fails, and an unavailable signing key yields an
      `unsigned` (Tier-0) write, never a blocked write.
- [ ] Each identity key record binds `{pubkey, added_at_commit, revoked_at_commit?}` (`tickets`-branch
      commit SHAs); key add/rotate/revoke is refused unless signed by a currently-valid key (G2). Using
      two fixture commits on the `tickets` branch, a test asserts the genesis key-add is accepted only when self-signed (TOFU base
      case), an unsigned non-genesis key-add is refused, an event whose commit is NOT a descendant of the key's `added_at_commit` (or IS a descendant of its
      `revoked_at_commit`) fails verification, and one that is a descendant of `added_at_commit` and not
      of `revoked_at_commit` passes.
- [ ] `{provider, external_id}` mappings key on the provider's opaque id; the reconciler resolves an
      outbound Jira assignee by `accountId`, bootstraps via `/user/search` best-effort (which needs the
      "Browse users and groups" permission and may return nothing), then falls back to an
      operator-provided mapping, then to existing Jira assignee/reporter data, and finally degrades to
      project-default (`-1`)/unassigned without hard-failing; reporter is set by `accountId` only when
      the Modify-Reporter permission is held, else assignee-only. Test with a
      fixture identity + stubbed `accountId`.
- [ ] An inbound Jira user with no mapping creates a placeholder via `create_placeholder`; re-running
      resolution after a real mapping is added idempotently upgrades it — a test asserts one identity
      results, not two.
- [ ] Enforcement is opt-in (`identity.require_authenticated`): with it on, a CI merge-gate job runs
      `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <identity.enforce_since>` over the merged
      log and **exits non-zero**, emitting one report entry (`{event_uuid, ticket_id, commit, author,
      verdict, display}`) per non-`certified` event at/after the cutover, while pre-cutover events are
      grandfathered (test asserts exit code, a report entry's fields, and grandfathering); the local write-gate fails fast but is documented UX-only. Replay never rejects
      (test: a bad-signature event still folds into state); `show`/`fsck` surface the display grouping (`verified`/`unverified`/`unsigned`) over the raw `verdict`.
- [ ] Default-install regression: with zero identity configuration, an integration test asserts a
      normal write succeeds unsigned, **no identity entity is minted**, and `list`/`ready`/gates behave
      identically to pre-feature (proves SC "default install unchanged").
- [ ] Snapshots (compaction) record the per-signed-event verification tuple `{event_uuid, content_hash,
      signature, signer_pubkey, position}` so compacted signed events still return `verified`
      without the original event object (round-trip test).
- [ ] Docs + ADR: identity model; the verdict enum (existing `verify_signature_result` verdicts + new `key_not_valid_at_era`) and its `verified/unverified/unsigned` display grouping; opt-in enforcement + the
      CI-merge-gate-is-the-control caveat + its detect-vs-reject limitation; Jira `accountId` mapping +
      the Modify-Reporter permission requirement; key-rotation / era (commit-ancestry: `added_at_commit`/`revoked_at_commit`);
      private-key storage (ssh-agent/`~/.ssh`, never committed); the provider-neutral seam.
- [ ] A person running rebar has a modeled identity; events attribute it (name+email always; an authorship
- [ ] An opt-in project can REQUIRE authenticated authorship: `unsigned`/`unverified` events are flagged by
- [ ] The identity provides a stable local↔`accountId` map the reconciler uses to set the Jira assignee
- [ ] Key rotation works: events verify against the keys whose validity-ancestry contains them (added_at_commit ancestor, revoked_at_commit not); a revoked key
- [ ] Default install is byte-identical to pre-feature; signing and enforcement are fully opt-in.

## Intended decomposition (children)
1. `identity` ticket-type + entity (attributes, **public**-key-only storage + private-key guard,
   exemptions, normal + `create_placeholder` paths, config pointer, default-install invariant).
2. Event attribution (name+email + `author_id`) + replay back-compat + default-install regression test.
3. Authorship attestation kind on the foundation substrate (DSSE subject binding; unsigned fallback).
4. TOFU genesis + G2 signed key-rotation chain + era (commit-ancestry) validity.
5. Provider-neutral mapping + Jira adapter (outbound assignee/reporter, Modify-Reporter degrade).
6. Inbound ghost/placeholder + idempotent auto-upgrade.
7. Opt-in enforcement: local write-gate + **CI merge-gate verify job** + fsck `verified/unverified/unsigned`
   marking + replay-never-rejects + snapshot carries identities/sigs.
8. Docs + ADR.

## Prior art / grounding
git-bug identity entity + `ValidKeysAtTime` (log-position key validity) + bridge metadata; SCIM
`externalId`; OIDC `(iss,sub)` (email disqualified as key); Jira Cloud GDPR `accountId` (email
null/hidden) + Modify-Reporter permission; Gitea/GitLab placeholder-user + auto-upgrade; git `.mailmap`
(email as adopt-heuristic only). Depends on the asymmetric attestation foundation.
baseline.summary: Authenticated identity — entity + authorship certification + provider-neutral user mapping

content.text: ## Why

Audit Reliability finding #2 (HIGH). In `src/rebar/_store/push.py`, `push_tickets_branch` performs a fetch + non-fast-forward `git merge` + stash mutation on the push-retry path that runs **unlocked**, by documented design (push runs after the write lock is released). The same fetch+merge on the sync path (`src/rebar/_store/sync.py` `reconverge` / `_do_reconverge`) is correctly guarded by the write lock. A concurrent writer that already passed its rebase guard can have its `git commit` fail against transient MERGE_HEAD/index activity from the push-retry merge, spuriously failing the user's write. In `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=async` mode this is routine: a detached background process merges while the foreground batch keeps writing. Related (audit 3.2): the async detached spawn in `push_tickets_branch` swallows its own `OSError` (`except OSError: pass`).
## What / files

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — in `push_tickets_branch`'s non-fast-forward retry/merge block: keep the `git fetch` OUTSIDE the lock (it only moves remote-tracking refs), then wrap the merge/stash mutation in `with _lock.write_lock(base_path, timeout=<short>, attempts=1, dual_window=True):`, mirroring `sync.py::reconverge` (fetch outside, `with write_lock(...): _do_reconverge(...)`). **Re-check `_lock.check_no_rebase_in_progress(base_path)` INSIDE the locked critical section** (as `_do_reconverge` does) — not only before acquiring the lock — to close the TOCTOU where a concurrent reconverge/push could create MERGE_HEAD between a pre-lock check and lock entry. On `_lock.LockTimeout`, skip the merge and leave the push pending (best-effort) rather than racing; never fail the user's write.
- Log the async-push detached-spawn `OSError` at WARNING (via the module logger) instead of `except OSError: pass`.
## Scope

In: `push.py` (lock around the merge portion with an inner rebase re-check; spawn-failure logging); one concurrency regression test. Out: `sync.py` (already correct); changing push best-effort semantics; stash-drop hardening (separate low finding).
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The non-fast-forward reconcile merge in `push_tickets_branch` runs under `_lock.write_lock`, with `check_no_rebase_in_progress` re-checked INSIDE the lock; a lock timeout means the merge is skipped (push stays pending), verified by a regression test using the `two_clones` fixture in `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`

- [ ] The async-push detached-spawn failure path logs at WARNING — verified by a unit test that forces the spawn (`subprocess.Popen`) to raise `OSError` and asserts a WARNING record via `caplog` (no silent `except OSError: pass`)
- [ ] New test: a concurrent locked write during a push-retry merge — the write succeeds (no spurious StoreError) and no event is lost
- [ ] Push remains best-effort: no code path lets a push failure fail a write (existing push/sync tests stay green)
- [ ] `make test` green

baseline.summary: Take the write lock around the push-retry reconcile merge

content.text: ## Summary

A work ticket carries a single cryptographic attestation slot (`state["signature"]`). Both the **plan-review attestation** (earned at claim time via `rebar review-plan`) and the **completion verdict** (signed at close by the completion verifier) are written as `SIGNATURE` events into that one slot. The reducer applies `SIGNATURE` as last-writer-wins, so the completion verdict signed on close **overwrites and destroys** the plan-review attestation. These two attestations are independent proofs of two different gates and should be **additive** — a closed ticket should retain BOTH.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Take a non-bug work ticket (e.g. a `story`) and earn a plan-review attestation: `rebar review-plan <id>` (PASS). `rebar show <id>` now shows `signature.manifest[0] == "plan-review: PASS"`.
2. Claim and complete the work, then close: `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed`. The completion verifier runs and signs a completion verdict.
3. `rebar show <id>` again.
**Expected:** the ticket retains both attestations — the plan-review PASS *and* the completion-verifier PASS (queryable independently).

**Actual:** the `signature` field now shows only `manifest[0] == "completion-verifier: PASS"`; the plan-review attestation is gone from compiled state. Observed live on story `3d3d-da49-c3f3-4298` (REB-522): `signature` was `["plan-review: PASS", ...]` while in_progress and became `["completion-verifier: PASS", ...]` after close.
## Root Cause

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:376` `process_signature()` does `state["signature"] = {…}` — a single slot, last-writer-wins (see its own docstring, line 377). The compactor builds the SNAPSHOT `compiled_state` via this same reducer, so after compaction the earlier attestation is permanently lost from compiled state (the raw append-only SIGNATURE events still exist in the log, but `show`/MCP/`verify-signature`/the gates read the single compiled field). Both verdict kinds are already distinguishable by `manifest[0]` (`"plan-review: …"` vs `"completion-verifier: …"`), so they can be keyed.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ticket can simultaneously hold a plan-review attestation AND a completion verdict; signing one does not clobber the other (additive, not last-writer-wins across kinds).
- [ ] Within a single kind, last-writer-wins still applies (re-running plan-review replaces the prior plan-review attestation; re-closing replaces the prior completion verdict).
- [ ] `process_signature` (and the SNAPSHOT/compaction path that replays it) preserves all kinds across compaction.

- [ ] `verify-signature` can certify each attestation kind; the claim gate reads the plan-review attestation and the close gate reads/writes the completion verdict, each unaffected by the presence of the other.
- [ ] Backward compatible: tickets with a single legacy `signature` still verify; the change is forward/back-compat for older clones (new shape preserved-and-ignored, per the rollout convention).
- [ ] Tests cover: plan-review then close retains both; re-sign same kind replaces in place; round-trip through compaction; legacy single-signature ticket still reads/verifies.
## Affected Files (initial)
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (`process_signature`)
- `src/rebar/signing.py` (`sign_manifest`, verify)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` (signing call sites)
- relevant SIGNATURE schema under `src/rebar/schemas/` and reducer/compaction tests

baseline.summary: Completion verdict signature clobbers the plan-review attestation (single signature slot is last-writer-wins; should be additive)

baseline.description:
# Extract interpret_failure() -- run()'s except spine

ADR 0056 decision 3, FIRST extraction. The ordering is deliberate and was corrected by adversarial review.

## Why this one first

An earlier draft ordered resolution first, claiming "every" recent commit touching runner.py was a pre-call resolution concern. Review disproved it -- at least five were not: 8e4d6a46d and 5144a9009 (usage/cost, post-call), 4291b9a56 (disposition classifier, in the except arm), 3938c7ed2 (gate posture, in preflight), c8aa1ecdd (refusal fail-closed, in the call section). The real figure is ~70%.

The except spine is also the DENSEST code region in the file: 75 lines at only 20% comment (58 code), versus the pre-call region's 50% comment (113 code across 254 lines). Per line extracted it returns the most headroom, and it is where several of the most recent growth commits actually landed.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:555-629` -> `interpret_failure(...)`.
  MEASURED on the cc33 base (commit ad5ced165): line 555 is the first `except UsageLimitExceeded as
  exc:` and line 629 is `raise provider_err from exc`, the last statement of the last arm. An earlier
  draft of this bullet said "507-581", which was wrong at BOTH ends: 507 is the `_call_label`
  observability setup that sits BEFORE the `try:`, and 581 stops inside the middle arm, omitting the
  entire broad `except Exception` arm (582-629) — the one carrying the load-bearing
  sampling-rejection ordering. Re-locate by content, not by these offsets, if the base moves.
- Destination: `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — the run-execution cluster already split from
  runner.py (task 2682/3a98). NOT `failure.py`, which stays pure classification, and NOT a new file
  (AGENTS.md forbids creating one under 100 LOC by splitting).
- The `finally:` block at 630 STAYS in `run()`. It is teardown, not interpretation.
- tests/unit/

### Parameters the arms genuinely read (name them explicitly; no carrier unless >~6)

`exc`, `run_messages`, `req_limit`, `eff_max_iter`, `ran_model`, `_call_label`, `req.execution_mode`, and `_t0` (for the elapsed-time log). `ran_model` is required by BOTH the `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` call and the `ClassifyContext`, so it is not optional. ADR 0056 permits a carrier above ~6 parameters; a small frozen context object holding the logging and counter fields is in-bounds here, since none of its fields is mutated after construction (the ADR's objection to `ResolvedCall` was that two of ITS fields were).

## Preserve the arm ORDER — it is the whole contract

Keep `UsageLimitExceeded`, then `LLMError`, then broad `Exception`; and within the broad arm try `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` FIRST. Python's type lattice hides a regression here: `UsageLimitExceeded` and every `LLMError` are plain `Exception` subclasses, so a broad-first spine silently reclassifies a step-budget stop or a typed failure as a provider OUTAGE. And `LLMConfigError` is a SUBCLASS of `LLMUnavailableError`, so an `isinstance` assertion CANNOT distinguish a correctly-translated sampling rejection from the broad fallback — arm-ordering tests must assert `type(x) is`, never `isinstance`.

NOTE for the implementer: translate_sampling_parameter_rejection performs NO retry -- it inspects and reclassifies. An earlier architecture draft wrongly described it as rebuilding settings and retrying. It does not break the resolve-then-execute shape.

## Monkeypatch repoints: MEASURED ZERO for this child

None of the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "...")` targets in the suite (`_import_pydantic_ai`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, `_pai_model`, `_pai_structured`, `cache_settings_for`, `capabilities_for`, `get_runner`, `ProviderSession`) lies in the except spine, so this extraction needs no repoints. That zero was MEASURED for this region and does NOT transfer to the sibling children.

## Pre-existing decay this ticket should tidy, not be blamed for

`tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py` carries 23 descriptive labels of the form `"CURRENT(runner.py:NNN): ..."` (e.g. `runner.py:346`, `runner.py:365`). They are the third element of test-case tuples — human-readable descriptions, NOT assertions, which is why the suite passes regardless. They were ALREADY WRONG before this ticket: they cite 346/365 while the spine actually sits at 555-629, so they date from a layout two splits ago. Since this extraction moves the code they describe, retarget them to name `structured_run.interpret_failure` WITHOUT a line number, so they cannot rot again. This is label text only — no assertion changes.

## Testing

Unit tier: pure given an exception and the counters. Plus one end-to-end assertion through the real `PydanticAIRunner.run()`, because a `run()` that stopped calling the seam would still pass every isolated unit test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts a sampling-parameter rejection is reclassified to the typed config error and NOT
      to LLMUnavailableError -- the arm-ordering property; it fails if the broad classification runs
      first. MUST assert `type(err) is LLMConfigError`, because LLMConfigError subclasses
      LLMUnavailableError and an isinstance check would pass vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the raised TYPE is unchanged for each of the three arms, so every existing
      `except LLMUnavailableError` caller keeps working
- [ ] the classified disposition is still attached as METADATA without changing the raised type,
      asserted as: the raised error's `.outcome` is not None AND `type(err) is LLMUnavailableError`
- [ ] an end-to-end test drives the real `run()` with a failing model and asserts the sampling
      rejection still surfaces as the typed config error -- proving run() still routes through the seam
- [ ] runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message, AND the resulting file is under
      the 700 headroom guard on THIS commit (parent 7f86 AC3: `Verified` is cast per patchset, so a
      red ancestor blocks the whole relation chain)
- [ ] any monkeypatch target that moved is repointed IN THE SAME COMMIT and named in the message with
      its reason (expected: none — see "MEASURED ZERO" above)
- [ ] no comment moved or rewritten in `run()` lost a measured number, a `file:line` citation, a
      bug/story/epic id, a named failure mode, or a stated invariant
baseline.summary: Extract interpret_failure() from run()'s except spine

baseline.description:
Bring `resolve_event_commit` and `resolve_position_commit` in line with the bulk map builders, which already carry both flags. This is an authorship-correctness fix, unrelated to repo size. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`authorship.py:152-168` (`resolve_event_commit`) and `:194-209` (`resolve_position_commit`) omit `--no-renames` and `-c log.showSignature=false`; the bulk builders at `:313-331` and `:383-401` carry both, and `:298-300` documents why. The missing `log.showSignature=false` is a **live latent bug**: on a host with `log.showSignature=true`, `gpg:` lines interleave into stdout and `lines[-1]` (`:172`, `:213`) returns a non-SHA.

`--no-renames` is behaviour-preserving: it can only convert `R` into `A`+`D`; both pathspecs match at most one path (positions are globally unique `{ts}-{uuid}`); and the only event-file renames are `.json` -> `.json.retired`, which no `*.json` pathspec matches. **Do not add `--no-merges`** — `authorship.py:294` documents that the fallback exists precisely to catch files added only inside merge commits.

Note: an earlier framing justified this as a partial-clone performance fix. That motivation is **not** established — pathspec limiting runs before diffcore rename detection, so these single-path resolvers likely never fault blobs. The correctness argument stands on its own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With `log.showSignature=true` **and signed commits** in the fixture repo (a `gpg.program` /
      `gpg.format` shim suffices), both resolvers return a valid **40-hex SHA**. Tier: **unit**
      against a real temporary git repo. The signing is load-bearing: with `--format=%H` over
      *unsigned* commits the setting emits no extra lines, so an unsigned fixture makes this
      **vacuously green**.
- [ ] Both flags appear in the argv of both resolvers, and `--no-merges` does **not**. Tier: **unit**
      pinning the constructed command.
- [ ] Resolver output matches the bulk map builders' output over a sample of >=100 real events — the
      cross-check that the flags did not change semantics. Tier: **integration** against the store.

## Files
`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`, tests

Scope: XS-S. No dependencies.
baseline.summary: B5: add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers

baseline.description:
# Workflow engine v2: declarative IR + thin interpreter + provider-agnostic runtime + visual editing

## Context

Split out of the remediation epic 6f2d (soupy-spool-revel) per the deep-design brainstorm (session log
ad3f-2d99-6d41-40e6 "boom-demon-jug"). The brainstorm established that "remediation" is really a
re-architecture of the workflow engine; THIS epic owns the BUILD. 6f2d retains remediation-on-top (docs,
migrating existing reviewers onto this engine, prompts, eval coverage, cleanup, visual+eval review,
intent-alignment) and depends_on this epic. Every decision is grounded in 4 deep-research rounds + codebase
spikes + 3 passing de-risk POCs under docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/ (REFERENCE, not deliverables).

## What we are building (4 parts)

- **Declarative IR (git source of truth):** one YAML/JSON file per workflow; steps are deterministic
  (`uses:` an INTERNAL registered op) or agentic (`prompt:` an LLM step); control flow (conditional
  branches, bounded loops, map/fan-out) expressed as DATA; stable step ids. Evolves v1 GitHub-Actions YAML.
- **Thin synchronous interpreter (engine):** run-state on rebar's EVENT LOG (genuine reuse —
  WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP events on the target ticket, same reducer/commit/push); iteration-keyed
  idempotency markers; mandatory max_iterations; control-flow state derived from recorded outputs
  (replay-correctness discipline the engine POC proved). BOUNDED-CONCURRENT fan-out: parallel LLM calls,
  serialized commits (decision: included in v1).
- **Provider-agnostic agent runtime behind the existing Runner seam:** Pydantic AI, REPLACING
  LangChain/LangGraph (sole justification — native Langfuse tracing — is obsolete; Langfuse is OTel-native).
  Runs single-turn LLM calls AND tool-using agents (filesystem + MCP + custom rebar-op tools). Tracing via
  OTel -> Langfuse, dev/maintenance only (clients pay nothing).
- **Ephemeral visual editor:** bpmn-js (constrained BPMN metamodel — NOT draw.io's free-form canvas, which
  would allow edits that don't map back). A thin IR<->BPMN serializer (bpmn-moddle + a registered `rebar`
  moddle descriptor) projects the IR for editing and round-trips back; the visual format is NEVER committed
  (auto-layout on open).

## Structured-output reliability (output feeds deterministic steps — reliability is key)

Retire the second-interpreter LLM (a recognized anti-pattern). Layered stack (research-grounded):
1. Provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported (OpenAI strict ~100% vs <40%;
   Gemini responseSchema; **Anthropic native structured outputs now GA**) via Pydantic AI NativeOutput; else
   PromptedOutput cross-provider.
2. Deterministic tolerant parse of near-miss output (json-repair) — no LLM.
3. Pydantic validation + normalizing validators (numeric/length bounds HERE, not in the JSON Schema, to stay
   inside Anthropic's strict-grammar subset).
4. Bounded SAME-model retry feeding the validation error back (Pydantic AI retries={'output': 2}; raise the
   default budget of 1).
Handle Anthropic stop_reason in {refusal, max_tokens}; for steps needing extended thinking, SPLIT reasoning
and structured extraction into two steps (thinking is a tradeoff vs forced structured output).

## Dependencies

- Reuse: event-sourced git store (run-state), git-canonical prompt library, Inspect AI eval seam, Runner seam.
- Add (runtime, light): pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,...] (~41 pkgs vs LangGraph ~80-110); provider SDKs;
  json-repair; OTel exporter ([tracing]) -> Langfuse.
- Drop: langchain, langgraph, langchain-mcp-adapters.
- Add (edit-time ONLY, out-of-process): bpmn-js (browser editor) + bpmn-moddle (MIT serializer). NOT runtime.
- Build (the only custom code): IR schema+linter (low risk); interpreter (moderate, justified by
  event-sourcing); Pydantic-AI Runner adapter (low); IR<->BPMN serializer (moderate, bounded — bpmn-moddle +
  one descriptor + round-trip fixtures; POC-validated).

## How it meets the invariants
- I1 human visual edit incl. loops/conditionals: bpmn-js (constrained metamodel) + round-trip serializer.
- I2 LLM edit+validate: lean schema'd IR; atomic id-keyed edit ops + schema + linter validation.
- I3 git-stored, clean diff NOT required: only the IR is committed; visual format ephemeral.
- I4 light runtime / heavy edit-deps OK: interpreter is stdlib; agent runtime lazy-loaded for agent steps;
  visual editor out-of-process.
- Cross-provider (hard req): Pydantic AI provider-agnostic, NO per-provider code; Anthropic-only rejected.
- Tool-using agents (FS+MCP+rebar ops): native to Pydantic AI (validated).
- Deterministic step logic INTERNAL-only (registry not exposed via CLI/MCP).
- Don't-build-unique-engine is EARNED: every off-the-shelf engine (DBOS/Restate/Spiff) owns its run-state and
  conflicts with event-sourcing; standard formats (BPMN/ASL) carry impedance > a lean IR.

## De-risk POCs (all PASS; docs/experiments/workflow-remediation-pocs/)
- engine_interpreter_poc.py: replay exactly-once across ALL crash points (deepest risk retired).
- runtime_pydanticai_poc.py: cross-provider integration validated; Claude thinking+structured-output 400
  reproduced AND mitigated (PromptedOutput); dep weight 41.
- visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs: IR<->BPMN round-trip preserves ids / multi-instance / agent metadata.

## Known limitations
- We own/maintain the interpreter (replay correctness is subtle — POC found+fixed one bug; contained by the
  state-discipline rule + tests).
- IR<->BPMN serializer is bespoke and bounded by BPMN's vocabulary (our IR must map onto BPMN).
- Agent-step config richness in the canvas is limited (edit flow visually, prompts in text).
- Pydantic AI is young (2.0 beta incoming) — contained by the strict swappable Runner seam.
- OTel->Langfuse token/cost attribute mapping is a known soft spot (analytics, not span structure).
- Cross-provider COMPLETION proven on Anthropic; OpenAI/Google billing-blocked (integration validated).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] v2 IR JSON Schema + v1->v2 migrate shim + linter (cycles legal only via declared loop frames); coverage guard.
- [ ] Interpreter: conditionals/loops/map; iteration-keyed (run_id,step_id,iteration) markers; mandatory
      max_iterations; replay tests (kill mid-run -> replay from events -> no double effects).
- [ ] Bounded-concurrent fan-out: parallel agent calls + serialized event commits; deterministic replay
      preserved; Burr tripwire relaxed NARROWLY for the map path only (recorded).
- [ ] PydanticAIRunner behind the Runner seam; FS+MCP+custom tools; structured output via NativeOutput/
      PromptedOutput (NOT forced-tool ToolOutput); validate + bounded retry; parallel-run-and-diff vs the old
      LangGraph path to the DEFINED PARITY BAR (child 7d58: non-inferiority on the eval corpus — validity >= v1,
      per-criterion verdict-agreement >= 95% + zero decision flips, recall/false-accept within +/-2pp) before
      cutover; the bar gates the LangGraph drop.
- [ ] LangChain/LangGraph/langchain-mcp-adapters removed; tracing via [tracing] OTel->Langfuse, optional.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability layers 1-4 implemented; thinking+extraction split where needed;
      stop_reason handling; second-interpreter LLM removed.
- [ ] bpmn-js editor + IR<->BPMN serializer with a registered `rebar` moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures
      (ids, agent metadata, multi-instance survive); visual format never committed.
- [ ] docs reference the 3 de-risk POCs.
- [ ] v2 declarative IR (steps + conditionals + loops + map) with a JSON Schema + linter, agent-editable.
- [ ] Thin interpreter executing it with run-state on the event log, deterministic resume/replay, and
- [ ] Agent runtime swapped to provider-agnostic Pydantic AI behind the Runner seam; LangGraph dropped.
- [ ] Structured-output reliability stack (native/strict + tolerant parse + validators + bounded retry); the
- [ ] Human visual view+edit via bpmn-js over an ephemeral IR<->BPMN projection.
baseline.summary: Workflow engine v2: declarative IR + thin interpreter + provider-agnostic runtime + visual editing

# rebar bug-trend analysis (2026-08-01, reviewed)

Data baseline: 344 bug tickets (77 Jun, 260 Jul, 7 Aug 1); 333 closed. Bug-close `--class` enum (regression | plan_defect | env_integration | flaky | preexisting | not_a_bug | duplicate | escalated | undetermined) became required ~07-19 (ed13); 214 closed bugs carry no class — ~207 predate the requirement, ~7 post-date it via then-unenforced close surfaces (the 376d class: MCP transition / NDJSON import). Of the 119 classified: preexisting 57, plan_defect 15, env_integration 14, duplicate 12, regression 12, not_a_bug 4, flaky 4, undetermined 1. Caveat: every classified close is a July/Aug-created bug (the June cohort closed pre-taxonomy), and the class is closer-self-reported, unaudited. Tags: 237/344 untagged, ad-hoc vocab. creation_channel: unknown 209 / cli 126 / jira 5 / python 4. file_impact set on 100/344. `rebar metrics` registry lenses: agent_process (attempts_per_ticket, first_pass_rate, reopen_recovery, revert_recovery, rework_within_7_days), code_health (churn, refactor_to_addition_ratio), gate_economics (cost_per_accepted_change, first_pass_verification, env_diagnosis_intervals); module-size metrics show `unavailable`. No bug lens exists.

Title-keyword clustering (overlapping, 261/344 matched): reconciler/Jira sync 77; concurrency/locking/git-store races 76; plan-review/attestation gate defects 55; CI/test flakiness+isolation 41; silent-failure/fail-open 39; infra/deploy 27; code-review gate 24; completion-verifier/close gate 22; config/env-var 19; truncation/pagination/limits 15; direction-inversion/asymmetry ~7.

Recurring same-class families (explicit in titles): unlocked raw git commits bypassing the canonical locked write seam (3a33, 3435, 4dd2, 3b4e); pagination truncation (9263, 1f3d, deac); link-direction inversion (3b86 → 4b59 → 32cc); asymmetric ADD-only differs (7f42, 908c); lock wedges/reclamation (620c, a4b2, 304e, ac26, 1a47, 9305, 449f — 449f documents 7 post-fix recurrences as residual, not regression); mtime-less cache staleness (1d76, e995, 908b); wall-clock perf assertions in tests (edfe, b228, 19d7, 5e94, 85c3); missing subprocess timeouts (c16f, d843, 747f); "exists on CLI only, not lib/MCP" parity (6e88, 1598, 5199, d21b; close --class rollout misses 0e15, 376d); unread config/env keys (281f, 9d7a; b00f is the adjacent scanner-blind-spot case).

---

## Q1 — Additional observability/traceability? YES, three low/zero-friction gaps.

What already exists and costs users nothing extra: bug-close `--class` (bounded enum, enforced); the **blame-hunt subsystem** — every bug close best-effort auto-derives a `caused_by` link to the culprit ticket (`src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `transition_close.py:490`, ticket 555e) with retroactive backfills (`scripts/backfill_caused_by.py`, `scripts/backfill_bug_class.py` — structural, no-LLM close_class backfill from reverts/REVIEW_RESULT/gate_error signals, ticket 5062); `discovered_from` links; tags; session logs; auto-filed canary tickets (binding-drift, heartbeat) with a find-existing-then-comment dedup pattern; the code-review FP ledger (`fp:code-review` bug tickets with a `root-cause:` enum, compiled into NO-FIRE eval cases); `rebar metrics` lenses.

Gaps:
1. **The close taxonomy captures relationship-to-work, not mechanism or escape channel.**
   `preexisting` (57/119) tells you it wasn't a regression; it does not tell you it was a
   concurrency bug that escaped because no gate looks at raw git writes. Recommendation:
   a **batch auto-classifier** extending the 5062 backfill pattern — structural signals
   where they suffice, the `rebar.llm` framework for the rest — writing bounded
   `mechanism:*` / `detected-by:*` tags to closed bugs on a schedule, spot-checked. Zero
   author burden. Do NOT add a second *required* close flag: the `--class` rollout itself
   broke every automated close surface (0e15 red main; 376d MCP/NDJSON gaps; the canary
   closes bugs programmatically — reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:300), and automation would
   stamp a constant value anyway, polluting the data.
2. **Nothing aggregates.** Answering "top bug mechanism this month" required re-mining 344
   titles by hand; the registry has agent_process/code_health/gate_economics lenses but no
   bug lens. Recommendation: a `bug_trends` metrics lens over data already in the store —
   close_class distribution over time, mechanism-tag distribution, open-bug age,
   `caused_by` fan-in (shared culprits), canary time-to-detect. Read-only; zero burden.
3. **Class-level recurrence is prose; only culprit-level links are structured.**
   `caused_by` gives queryable bug→culprit-ticket links, but "same class as the
   enrich-queue prune race", "sibling sweep of 5546", "9305 rec #1" live in titles —
   recurrence-of-a-mechanism across channels is unqueryable. Recommendation: a link/tag
   convention (`relates_to` to the anchor bug + a `class:<anchor>` tag) written by the
   debug skill automatically (see Q4), so recurrence rate per class becomes a query.
Also: extend the FP-ledger pattern (proven for code review) to plan-review false positives — a large fraction of the 55 plan-review bugs are FP/noise reports; making each a NO-FIRE eval case compounds precision. Anti-recommendation: no new mandatory fields at bug **create** time (canaries and agents must file cheaply), and no mandatory prose root-cause field (comments already carry it).

## Q2 — Fragility/decay trends? Mostly surface-expansion + latent-defect discovery, with four real structural weaknesses.

The July spike tracks new subsystem activation (review-bot, auto-lander, Bedrock cutover, Jira DC, live tiers); the June baseline was itself audit-driven (audit-2026-06-09 filed ~17 on 06-10; antipattern-audit). In the classified (July-created, self-reported) subsample, `preexisting` outnumbers `regression` 57:12 — consistent with latent-defect discovery rather than decay, though that subsample excludes the June cohort and is unaudited. Four structural fragility patterns are real and mitigable regardless:
1. **A bespoke concurrent database on git** (~76 bugs). Many writers (CLI, MCP, review-bot,
   reconcile-bridge, enrich queue, janitors, retention) re-discover the locking contract;
   failures: unlocked whole-index commits, auto-gc/maintenance corrupting the shared object
   DB, unreclaimable locks in containers. Mitigation: one canonical locked write seam
   (`run_git_write` exists; delete/txn/compact/init already route through it), **enforced
   deterministically in CI** — forbid raw `git commit`/index mutation outside an
   allowlisted seam, scoped to store-touching code AND workflows/scripts:
   reconcile-bridge.yml:283 does a raw `git commit` of ticket events in CI and is the live
   instance behind 449f's dominant failure mode; a src/rebar-only lint would miss it.
   Allowlist the seam files and test-fixture repos (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py).
   Plus the contention policy 9305 asks for.
2. **Hand-written per-field, per-direction reconciler differs** (~77). Asymmetric ADD-only
   differs, direction inversions, silent pagination truncation, untyped transport (cc77
   names the type gap as the root cause of a357's class). Mitigation: typed transport
   protocol (mypy-enforced port completeness — cc77), roundtrip/property invariants
   (inbound∘outbound identity, direction preservation), pagination-by-construction (one
   paged iterator, no raw page calls).
3. **The gates are themselves a top bug surface** (~100 across plan-review/code-review/
   verifier): attestation staleness/races, verdict non-determinism (620b, e458), token-cap
   INDETERMINATEs, FP classes. Meta-fragility: guardrail bugs erode trust and consume the
   bug budget. Mitigation: treat gate reliability as a product area (it is trending that
   way), keep the FP-ledger/eval loop growing, prefer deterministic pre-checks before LLM
   passes.
4. **Silent-failure default** (~39): fail-open checks, exit-0-on-error, unread env keys,
   integrations broken for weeks unnoticed (1630: 4119 mail errors since 06-30; 8070:
   canary red since 07-14). Mitigation: fail-loud policy for gate/infra code paths +
   auto-file tickets on canary red transitions (pattern already exists for binding-drift/
   heartbeat).

## Q3 — Gate levers, precision-first. Yes: mostly deterministic, narrowly-scoped ones.

Current posture is good: code review blocks only on security + secret/high-critical detectors; the rest is advisory; plan-review criteria carry applicability gates and ANTI-FP clauses; an FP ledger polices code-review noise. Levers, ranked by signal-to-noise:
1. **Deterministic CI lint: no raw git writes outside the canonical store seam** (catches
   the 3a33/3435/4dd2 class; low-FP *with* an allowlist for the seam itself and
   test-fixture repos, and scoped to include workflows/scripts — see Q2 §1 for why).
2. **Engine-layer enforcement rule as a code-review project criterion** (narrow): new
   validation/gates must live in the engine, not the CLI layer — catches the 0e15/376d and
   "CLI-only flag" parity class. Deterministic alternative: a parity test template.
3. **"Config key must be observably read" check** — for each new config/env key, require a
   test or a registry entry proving a behavioral effect; the env-registry drift gate
   already exists but checks documentation only (`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`), and b00f
   shows scanner blind spots.
4. **Auto-file P1 tickets on external/live canary red transitions** (8070 sat red for two
   weeks) — observability, but it closes the "merged broken, nobody looked" channel.
   Reuse the reconcile-bridge canary's find-existing-open-ticket→comment dedup pattern
   (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:259-267) so it cannot spam; external-integration.yml has
   no such path today.
5. **Narrow advisory code-review criterion: absolute wall-clock assertions in tests**
   (edfe/b228/19d7/5e94/85c3 class) — textually detectable, low FP as a scoped rule.
6. **Extend the FP-ledger pattern to plan review** — precision lever for existing criteria
   rather than a new detector; build on the adjudication corpus + FP-proxy harness already
   in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/.
7. Candidate only — needs a security design first: completion verifier executing a
   ticket's recorded `verify_commands` deterministically before the LLM pass would turn
   "AC satisfied" from pure judgment into judgment + executed evidence and catch
   proxy-validation escapes at close. But verify_commands are agent-authored arbitrary
   shell run in whichever environment closes the ticket: it needs sandboxing/allowlisting
   and a staleness story (plan-time commands vs post-merge tree) before it is a lever, not
   a liability.
Anti-levers: no new blocking LLM dimensions (T9/T5b stay advisory — concurrency/reliability review by LLM is FP-prone); no mutation-testing gate in CI (keep manual/scoped); no mandatory local review-code preflight (cost without vote).

## Q4 — rebar-debug: strong on single-bug rigor; four gaps for class-level closure.

The two-phase protocol, falsifiability, dynamic-proof rule, parsimony/exit gate, not-a-bug guard, and Step 7 sibling sweep are all present and good. Gaps vs "sibling issues, recurrence through different channels, residual fragility":
1. **No ticket-store writeback.** The skill never claims the bug ticket, records the proven
   root cause + experiment log as a comment, closes with the right `--class`, or files
   sibling/residual tickets with links. Note this is partly deliberate: the skill's
   Approval gate (SKILL.md:94-106) requires user approval before writing to "Jira or other
   trackers". So the fix must reconcile with that gate, not bypass it: add a "Record the
   outcome" section that treats the project's own rebar store as the sanctioned write
   surface when project guidance (AGENTS.md) mandates recording work there, keeping the
   approval gate for external trackers (Jira). Content: root-cause comment (mechanism,
   citations, experiments), close with the taxonomy class, siblings → tickets linked to
   the anchor bug, residual risks → tickets. This is also what makes Q1's recurrence
   observability free.
2. **Step 7 sweeps constructs, not channels.** It greps for the same code construct; the
   observed recurrences are the same *invariant* violated via a different surface (CLI vs
   MCP vs import; local vs CI — a4b2 fixed the local wedge, 449f documents the CI-side
   residue). Add: derive the sweep from the violated invariant, and enumerate parallel
   surfaces (CLI/lib/MCP/workflow/import/CI scripts) and other writers of the same state —
   "who else enforces or relies on this invariant?"
3. **Residual-fragility disposition.** Reporting covers bounded sweeps, but confirmed
   adjacent weaknesses from Phase 1 (dossier leads that weren't the root cause but are real)
   and known-uncovered residue of the fix have no required disposition. Add: a "residual
   risk" line in Reporting + file tickets for confirmed adjacent defects instead of
   dropping them (449f is the exemplar of why).
4. **No class-prevention hook.** When the cause is a repeatable pattern, Step 7 fixes live
   instances but never asks "can this class be made impossible or detectable?" (lint, type,
   constructor, CI gate, FP-ledger entry when a gate mis-fired). Add one paragraph: propose
   the structural guard as a ticket (not inline scope-creep).
Keep additions conditional (writeback only where a rebar store exists — the skill is cross-project) and short; the skill already warns against ceremony inflation.

## Q5 — rebar-implement: five escape-rate additions that don't duplicate gates.

Held-out TDD, RED-first, mutation/refactoring litmus, preflight, stacked landing are all in place; plan review owns plan quality, code review owns security/tests/scope advisories, the verifier owns AC satisfaction, CI owns lint/type/module-size/suite. Escaped classes that none of those own, addressable in the skill:
1. **Surface-parity enumeration in 4a.** When the behavior exists on multiple surfaces
   (CLI/lib/MCP), the spec must enumerate them and either cover each or explicitly file a
   follow-up ticket (create + link discovered_from). Targets the proven parity class
   (6e88/1598/5199/0e15/376d). No gate checks this today.
2. **"New config is read" oracle rule in 4b.** Any new config key/env var/flag gets one
   test proving behavior differs when it is set (kills 281f/b00f "parsed but read by
   nothing"). The CI env-registry gate checks documentation, not effect.
3. **Contention edge case in tier selection.** If a leaf mutates the ticket store or other
   shared state, the held-out edge set includes one second-writer/contention case —
   authored to test-design §7's deterministic-barrier discipline (multiple real processes,
   barrier/failpoint, no sleeps), else waived. The discipline matters: the repo's newest
   flaky-test close (08-01) is itself a contention test, and an undisciplined mandate here
   would feed the ~41-bug CI-flakiness cluster. Scoped to the store's dominant bug class,
   not a general mandate.
4. **Gate-finding → oracle upgrade loop in 4g.** On any post-push Verified -1 or LLM
   finding that is real, record in the session log which held-out test should have caught
   it and add that case before amending — converts every escape into a permanent oracle
   member.
5. **Residual-gap disposition at close.** If an edge/E2E case was deliberately descoped,
   file the ticket before closing the leaf (extends the existing discovered_from rule from
   "missing dependency" to "known untested residue").
Anti-additions: no mandatory local `review-code` preflight, no mutation-testing runs per leaf, no re-statement of module-size/lint (already in the 4d brief and CI).

baseline.description:
Block direct commits to `main`/`master` at commit time by enabling the pre-commit
framework's built-in `no-commit-to-branch` hook, so the "never commit to main"
rule this repo already enforces server-side (GitHub ruleset + Gerrit gates) also
fails fast locally — at `git commit` instead of only at push/review.

## Why
CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md mandate that no change land on `main` except through
Gerrit's two gates. Today nothing stops a local `git commit` while `HEAD` is on
`main`; the mistake is only caught later at push. Catching it at commit time is
cheaper and matches the repo's "errors happen early" posture.

## What
Add the packaged `no-commit-to-branch` hook (id from `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks`,
already pinned at `rev: v6.0.0` in this repo) to the existing hooks list in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, with an EXPLICIT `args: [--branch, main, --branch, master]`.

Rationale for explicit args (chosen over relying on the hook default): the tool
default at v6.0.0 is `frozenset(args.branch or ('master', 'main'))` — verified by
inspecting the installed hook source `pre_commit_hooks/no_commit_to_branch.py` — so a
bare entry already protects `main`. But passing the branches explicitly (a) documents
intent inline for the next reader, and (b) is robust to any future change of the
upstream default. The cost is two lines; the robustness/clarity gain is worth it.
Because the repo already depends on that pinned repo, this adds no new dependency and
requires no `rev` bump.

## Scope
- One file: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- Add a single `- id: no-commit-to-branch` entry (with the explicit `args`) under the
  existing `- repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` block (the one
  holding `check-yaml`, `check-toml`, etc.).
- No change to the `local` lint/typecheck hooks; no Makefile change (the hook is
  activated by the existing `pre-commit install` in `make hooks`).
- Non-goal: server-side enforcement (already covered by the GitHub ruleset + Gerrit);
  this is a local fail-fast convenience only, and remains bypassable with
  `git commit --no-verify` by design.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.pre-commit-config.yaml` contains a `no-commit-to-branch` hook id with an
      explicit `args` listing both `main` and `master`, under the
      `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` repo block.
      Proving command: `grep -q 'no-commit-to-branch' .pre-commit-config.yaml && python -c "import yaml,sys; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.pre-commit-config.yaml')); hs=[h for r in d['repos'] for h in r['hooks'] if h['id']=='no-commit-to-branch']; a=hs[0].get('args',[]); sys.exit(0 if hs and 'main' in a and 'master' in a else 1)" && echo OK`
- [ ] The config still parses and the hook is registered; running it on the current
      (non-protected) working branch passes.
      Proving command: `pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files` prints
      `Passed` and exits 0 while `HEAD` is on the feature branch.
- [ ] A `git commit` attempted while `HEAD` is on a protected branch is rejected.
      Proving command (negative path, exit code asserted):
      `git switch -c __scratch_main main 2>/dev/null; git branch -f main; git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main; pre-commit run no-commit-to-branch --all-files; test $? -ne 0 && echo BLOCKED-OK` — i.e. the hook exits non-zero (prints `Failed`) when HEAD is `main`. Restore HEAD to the feature branch afterward. (Run manually in a scratch checkout; not a CI step.)
- [ ] Existing gates are unaffected: `make lint && make typecheck` stay green and the
      YAML hygiene hooks still pass.
      Proving command: `make lint && make typecheck && pre-commit run check-yaml --all-files`
      all exit 0.
baseline.summary: Block direct commits to main via pre-commit no-commit-to-branch hook

## Why

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` is a grandfathered over-cap module (currently 971 LOC; soft cap 800). It carries a row in `.github/module-size-allowlist.txt`, `.github/module-size-ceilings.txt` (975), and a remedy row in docs/architecture.md. This story graduates it off the module-size gate by extracting a cohesive leaf of pure helpers.

## What

Create a new pure leaf module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py` (DetResult-free, re-only deterministic text/graph helpers), mirroring the existing sibling `det_operator_attested.py`. MOVE three cohesive islands out of det_floor:

1. Verify-command lint (G-3a / WS4): `_VERIFY_*`, `_GREP_*`, `_SHELL_VAR_RE`, `_lint_verify_command`, `_verify_command_strings`.
2. G5 decomposition-veto cluster: `decomposition_state_block`, `_G5_UNDECOMPOSED_RE`, `_is_undecomposed_claim`, `veto_undecomposed_g5`.
3. Pure task-DAG graph helpers: `_find_cycle`, `_file_interference`.

The `DET_CHECKS` registry and all p1-p9 check functions STAY in det_floor. `p5_task_dag` real-imports `_find_cycle`/`_file_interference`; `p6_ac_quality` real-imports `_lint_verify_command`/`_verify_command_strings`; det_floor re-exports `decomposition_state_block`/`veto_undecomposed_g5` (# noqa: F401) for pass1.py + test_g5_decomp_det.py. The leaf references `PlanContext` only as a type annotation, imported under `if TYPE_CHECKING` with `from __future__ import annotations` first, so it is a true runtime leaf (no runtime import of det_floor).

## DEVIATION from docs/architecture.md remedy row

The arch.md offenders row proposes extracting ONLY the verify-command-lint cluster into `det_verify_lint.py`. That row is superseded: the verify-lint cluster alone is SUB-FLOOR (<100 LOC) AND would leave det_floor still over the 800 cap. This ticket therefore WIDENS the seam — it moves the verify-lint island, the G5 decomposition-veto island, and the pure graph helpers (`_find_cycle`/`_file_interference`) into one `det_lint.py` leaf. The stale arch.md row is deleted by this ticket. ## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py passes (verify: python -m pytest that file -q)
- [ ] Back-compat: det_floor still exposes decomposition_state_block and veto_undecomposed_g5 (re-exported); pass1.py and test_g5_decomp_det.py unchanged
- [ ] Named suites green: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_g5_decomp_det.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py -q

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem
The first proposal mixed forward validity with historical convention. Revise it to a small deterministic floor intended to have no false positives, then use accepted history only as an adversarial counterexample corpus.

## Approach
Test failure patterns rather than preferred prose style. A rule qualifies for the floor only when the detected state is structurally incompatible with an executable plan; otherwise it remains advisory. Search closed tickets carrying signed plan-review and completion evidence, inspect every matching candidate in context, and narrow or remove any rule with a legitimate match.

## Criteria Under Review
1. An Acceptance Criteria checkbox must contain non-whitespace text after the checkbox marker.
2. Two Acceptance Criteria items must not be exact duplicates after joining continuations and normalizing whitespace/case.
3. Active execution prose must not contain a bare unresolved sentinel (`TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, or `???`) in Approach, Scope, Testing, or Acceptance Criteria; ignore fenced code, inline code, quotations, examples, explicit removal/prohibition assertions, and superseded/history sections.
4. Structured file-impact entries, when present, must have a nonempty path and nonempty reason; absence of file impact is allowed.
5. A `[rebar:<id>]` prerequisite citation used as plan evidence must resolve to a direct verified upstream dependency; ignore literal examples in code spans/fences.

## Scope
Read-only ticket-store analysis. The only mutation is the final findings comment on this ticket; no repository files or other ticket material will be changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every criterion under review has a documented historical search and cited matching tickets, verified by the final findings comment.
- [ ] Every legitimate matching ticket is treated as a counterexample and causes the rule to be narrowed or rejected, verified by before/after detection wording in the final findings.
- [ ] The final recommendation clearly separates hard-floor rules from advisory signals, verified by a structured classification table in the final findings.
- [ ] If a rule has no historical match, the finding says that explicitly without claiming proof of soundness, verified by the final findings comment.
baseline.summary: Adversarially validate a revised deterministic clarity floor

baseline.description:
# Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes

## Summary

At 2026-08-03 19:13 an agent session posted a comment on ticket 129e containing a full zsh environment dump. The dump embedded SEVEN live credentials (Anthropic, 2x GitHub PAT, Gemini/Google, Jira/Atlassian, OpenAI service-account, PyPI). GitHub push protection then rejected refs/heads/tickets (GH013) on the Anthropic key, so EVERY session's store writes queued local-only (153 commits at diagnosis) — a full store-sharing outage triggered by one comment.

rebar has no write-time secret guard: `comment`/`edit`/event append accept arbitrary bodies, and the auto-push seam surfaces the rejection only as `WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries`, which names neither the offending commit nor the reason, so the outage looks like transient contention.

## Root cause

1. No secret-pattern screening at the event-write seam (comment/description/session-log bodies).
2. The push-retry path swallows the git error detail (GH013 + secret location were only visible via a manual `git push`).

## Fix plan

1. Add a deterministic secret screen at the event-append seam (single choke point all writers share): reject or redact bodies matching high-confidence credential patterns (sk-ant-*, ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_, github_pat_, AIza…, ATATT…, xox?-, AKIA…, pypi-AgE…, sk-proj-/sk-svcacct-, PEM private-key headers) BEFORE the event file is written. Reject with a teaching message (what matched, why, how to redact); `--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` style override deliberately NOT provided over MCP.
2. Surface push-rejection detail: when the store push fails, include the git stderr tail (first GH013 violation line + path) in the warning so the failure self-identifies.
3. Unit tests: each pattern fires; placeholder/regex-text forms (e.g. `sk-ant-api03-...`, `sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) do NOT fire (word-boundary + length guards — the store already contains such benign strings in jira-reb-687 REVIEW_RESULT events); redaction path preserves event schema; push-failure warning carries the reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Event-append rejects (or redacts, per config) bodies matching the high-confidence credential patterns, with a teaching message naming the matched pattern class.
- [ ] Placeholder/truncated forms and pattern-literals in review payloads do not trip the screen (regression fixtures from jira-reb-687 events).
- [ ] Store push failures log the git rejection reason (GH013 line + offending path) instead of a bare retry count.
- [ ] Unit tests cover fire/no-fire per pattern and the enriched push warning.

## File impact

- src/rebar (event-append seam; store push module) — exact modules to be pinned during planning with Serena/grep.
- tests/unit (new secret-screen suite; push-warning test).
baseline.summary: Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes
