## Problem

`main` (origin/main HEAD 94e605a29) is red: `tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_hierarchy_incomplete.py::test_precheck_output_schema_accepts_old_and_new_shapes` fails deterministically with `agent output failed schema 'plan_review_precheck_output': 'review_phase' is a required property`.

## Root cause

Change 889 ("Add phased plan-review attestations") made `review_phase` a **required** property of `plan_review_precheck_output.schema.json` — correctly, since the precheck now always emits it (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:561,690,720`). The test's `old_shape` fixture, which predates that change and omits `review_phase`, was never updated. Change 889 earned `Verified +1` on a patch set based on a pre-test base; Rebase-If-Necessary merged it at submit without re-running CI, so the semantically-broken combination landed green (ADR 0047 hazard).

## Fix

Add `"review_phase": "planning"` to the `old_shape` dict in `test_precheck_output_schema_accepts_old_and_new_shapes`. The field is now always emitted, so the fixture was simply stale; `new_shape` (built via `**old_shape`) inherits it. No production code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `old_shape` in `test_precheck_output_schema_accepts_old_and_new_shapes` includes `"review_phase": "planning"`, matching the now-required schema property.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_hierarchy_incomplete.py` passes against origin/main src (all 12 tests green).
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- [ ] No production/schema files are changed — the fix is test-only (the schema requirement is intentional).
- [ ] [operator-attested] Change lands through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
baseline.summary: Fix red main: stale old_shape fixture omits now-required review_phase

baseline.description:
## Why
Init-time `_migrate_*`/`_ensure_*` steps run only at init/re-init, so config fixes never reach
already-existing stores. A first-class idempotent ensure-registry generalizes them (School B
desired-state) so every non-hot entry point converges an existing install.

## What
Create `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`: a registry of ensure units, each `{stable, immutable id,
callable(tracker: str) -> EnsureOutcome}` where `EnsureOutcome` is a small dataclass
`{id, status: Literal["ok","changed","failed"], detail: str}` and the callable is
check-then-act (no-op when converged). `run_ensures(tracker)` runs ALL units unconditionally
under the STORE write lock (`_store/lock.py` write_lock — init_core does NOT currently hold it;
this is a new dependency), catches a raising unit (skip-and-continue → `failed`), returns the
outcome list, and atomically rewrites `.ensure-applied` to contain ONLY the ids of non-failed
(ok/changed) units via the existing `fsutil.atomic_write` helper (temp-in-SAME-dir + os.replace,
so it is never a cross-device rename; a full rewrite, not an incremental append; absent/garbage/
non-list JSON on read → empty set). Add `.ensure-applied` to `_GITIGNORE`
(init.py:38-48).

`run_ensures()` NEVER raises: besides catching per-unit exceptions, a `write_lock` acquisition
failure (LockTimeout) is caught and treated like a whole-sweep no-op (logged; the caller — init
or MCP boot — continues, never aborts), and a failure to write the `.ensure-applied` marker
itself (OSError, e.g. disk-full/permission) is swallowed best-effort (the sweep's git-level
convergence already happened; the marker is only a hint) — it never fails the sweep or the caller.

Migrate exactly the 5 re-init idempotent units (init.py:209-213): `env-id`, `gc-config`,
`merge-ours driver`, `gitattributes` (COMMIT), `gitignore` (COMMIT). BOTH commit units
tree-check before committing. Wire `run_ensures()` at ALL init entry points and remove the
hand-listed calls: the re-init arm (209-213), the fresh-init arm (eight calls at init.py:241-248:
the migrated units are gitignore(242), gitattributes(245), gc(247), merge(248); the bootstrap
_ensure_branch_user_config(241)/_exclude_scratch_in_tracker(243)/_commit_precommit(244)/
_gen_local_files(246) stay — note `.env-id` is created by _gen_local_files(246) on fresh-init, so
the env-id unit no-ops there and `_ensure_env_id` is NOT among these calls), placing
`run_ensures()` AFTER the fresh-init bootstrap so ordering is preserved.

In `_init_via_symlink`, the two `_ensure_env_id` call sites sit in structurally distinct
branches and each gets its OWN independent `run_ensures(tracker)` call (the function is NOT
restructured to a single unified return): replace `_ensure_env_id(tracker)` at line 564 with
`run_ensures(tracker)` immediately before that branch's `return 0` (the already-symlinked
early-return guard), and replace `_ensure_env_id(tracker)` at line 582 with `run_ensures(tracker)`
immediately before the final `return 0` (the fresh-symlink-creation path); control flow is
otherwise unchanged. Confirm no OTHER callers of the 5 helpers remain after removal (no
double-execution).

The fresh-init-only bootstrap (`_commit_precommit`, `_gen_local_files`,
`_exclude_scratch_in_tracker`, `_ensure_branch_user_config`) is NOT part of the registry and
stays. init_core logs any `failed` units (warning) and NEVER aborts on an ensure failure.
Post-rollback: old code ignores the git-ignored `.ensure-applied` file; committed
`.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` content stays on the tickets branch (harmless/idempotent — old code
tree-checks before committing, so it neither re-commits nor errors on the extra committed content).
Update the stale docstring refs to `_migrate_gc_config` in BOTH `sync.py:17` and the init.py
module docstring (line 8) to point at the ensure registry.

## Scope
In: `ensures.py`, registry + 5 check-then-act units (EnsureOutcome), `run_ensures()` under the
store write lock, `.ensure-applied` format+write + `_GITIGNORE` entry, init wiring at all entry
points (replace + remove old calls incl. symlink-init). Out: pending-hint + `.ensure-hinted`
(WS2), fsck/server wiring (WS3), docs (WS4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ensures.py` registry: each unit has a stable/immutable id + `callable(tracker) -> EnsureOutcome`; a test asserts the registry's id set equals a frozen expected set (so a rename/typo is caught and applied units can't silently reappear as pending)
- [ ] `run_ensures()` runs all units under the store write lock and returns typed `EnsureOutcome`s; a raising unit is caught (skip-and-continue → `failed`) and excluded from `.ensure-applied`; init logs failures and never aborts
- [ ] `run_ensures()` never propagates an exception to its caller: a `write_lock` acquisition failure (LockTimeout) is caught and logged as a whole-sweep no-op, and an OSError writing `.ensure-applied` is swallowed best-effort; a test asserts init/boot continues (returns 0) when the write lock cannot be acquired
- [ ] All 5 units migrated; BOTH gitattributes and gitignore tree-check before committing; a second `run_ensures()` on a converged store makes zero changes and zero git commits (git-log assertion)
- [ ] Hand-listed calls removed from the re-init arm and the fresh-init arm; in `_init_via_symlink` each of the two `_ensure_env_id` sites (564, 582) is independently replaced by `run_ensures(tracker)` before its own `return 0` (structure otherwise unchanged); no double-execution; no other callers of the 5 helpers remain
- [ ] `.ensure-applied` written atomically via `fsutil.atomic_write` (temp-in-same-dir + os.replace, no cross-device rename) as a JSON array of ONLY non-failed unit ids; it is added to `_GITIGNORE`; absent/garbage/non-list degrades to empty set without crashing
- [ ] An end-to-end test drives `init_core` AND `_init_via_symlink` after the cutover and asserts the store converges (all 5 units applied, `.ensure-applied` written) — not just `run_ensures()` in isolation
- [ ] Stale docstring refs to `_migrate_gc_config` are updated in both `sync.py:17` and the init.py module docstring (line 8)
- [ ] Fresh-init bootstrap steps (_commit_precommit/_gen_local_files/_exclude_scratch/_ensure_branch_user_config) remain and are NOT in the registry
baseline.summary: WS1: ensure-registry (ensures.py) + migrate 5 check-then-act steps + init wiring

content.text: ## Why
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is exposed as an env var ONLY in the remote/cloud runner; the LOCAL
Claude Code CLI does not export it. Without a shim the session-provenance feature silently
no-ops for local-CLI users — the most common case. The robust, harness-agnostic capture is a
Claude Code SessionStart hook that reads the hook's `session_id` from stdin and exports it as
the portable `REBAR_SESSION_ID`, plus the harness tag `AI_AGENT=claude-code`.
## What
- **Hook script (`scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh`).** Reads the
SessionStart JSON envelope from stdin (field `session_id`) and, when `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is
set, APPENDS `export REBAR_SESSION_ID=<id>` and `export AI_AGENT=claude-code` to it. These
are the Claude Code hook-contract facts — the SessionStart stdin `session_id` field and the
`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` env-injection file — per the **Claude Code hooks reference**
(https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), cited in the script header + docs page. GRACEFUL
DEGRADATION: this is the only external-API coupling, and if a future Claude Code renames the
field/var or changes the mechanism, the shim simply no-ops (no `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` / unparsed
`session_id` → exit 0) — it never errors or blocks the session, so a wrong assumption fails
safe. To make that fail-safe OBSERVABLE (not silently inert), the docs ship a **manual
verification procedure** (`echo "$REBAR_SESSION_ID"` in a fresh session; claim + `show` and
check `claimed_session`/`claim_harness`) so an operator can confirm the hook is actually
wired and diagnose an env-mechanism mismatch. This external-integration coupling is
irreducible — a shim MUST name the harness's env-injection var — and is grounded in the
cited official reference plus that verification step. The harness tag is the base name
`claude-code` (the `AI_AGENT` vocabulary permits an optional `_<version>` suffix, but the
local hook has no reliable version source, so it emits the bare base name). Uses `python3`
(the interpreter rebar itself runs on — a system prerequisite, `requires-python >= 3.11`, not
a packaged dependency; if it is somehow absent on PATH the parse yields empty and the hook
no-ops) to parse the JSON
robustly — any parse failure, a missing/blank `session_id`, or an absent `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is
a silent no-op with exit 0 (fire-and-forget; NEVER blocks the session). Idempotent: re-firing
on resume/clear/compact first STRIPS this hook's own prior `REBAR_SESSION_ID`/`AI_AGENT`
exports from the env file (preserving other hooks' lines) then re-writes the current values,
so the file never accumulates duplicate/stale lines and always reflects the CURRENT session
(whose id may differ across resume per gotcha G1 — not "the same value").
- **Vocabulary alignment.** Update the `claude-code_<ver>` examples in `docs/config.md`,
`docs/event-schema.md`, and the `session_id.py` comment to present the harness tag as a base
name with an OPTIONAL `_<version>` suffix, so bare `claude-code` is consistent with the
documented vocabulary.
- **Docs (`docs/session-id-shims.md`).** A new install guide: the `settings.json`
`hooks.SessionStart` snippet pointing at the script, the caveat that the id is NOT stable
across `--resume`/`--continue`/fork/subagents (epic gotcha G1 — treat it as "the session
that emitted the claim event"), and guidance to keep it session-scoped (do NOT export
`REBAR_SESSION_ID` from a shell profile — gotcha G3). Cross-links `docs/config.md`.
## Scope
- IN: the Claude Code SessionStart hook script; the `docs/session-id-shims.md` install page;
the small vocabulary-alignment edits (`docs/config.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`,
`session_id.py`); and a NEW `tests/unit/test_session_shims.py` validating the script (valid
shell + env-file output for mock stdin, malformed JSON, idempotent re-fire, unwritable-file,
and no-op cases) AND asserting the base-name vocabulary form across all three doc/comment
targets.
- OUT: Codex/Cursor shims (S6 / 7656, which extend the same docs page); the record/read core
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh` exists and is valid shell. Proof:
`bash -n scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh` (asserted in
`tests/unit/test_session_shims.py`).
- [ ] Given stdin `{"session_id":"abc123"}` and a `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` temp path, the script
writes `export REBAR_SESSION_ID=abc123` AND `export AI_AGENT=claude-code` to that file.
Proof: `pytest tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -k claude_code_exports -q`.
- [ ] Robust no-op (exit 0, never blocks the session) for each of: a blank/missing
`session_id`, MALFORMED/unparseable JSON on stdin, an unset `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, AND an
UNWRITABLE `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` (path under a non-existent dir). Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -k "noop or malformed or unwritable" -q`.
- [ ] `docs/session-id-shims.md` includes a "Verifying the hook is wired" section (the
`echo "$REBAR_SESSION_ID"` + claim/`show` procedure), so the fail-safe design is
operator-observable. Proof: a doc-content assert that the "Verifying the hook" heading is
present AND the section carries the literal `echo "$REBAR_SESSION_ID"` step and the
`claimed_session`/`claim_harness` check — not merely the heading.
- [ ] Idempotent re-fire: firing twice with DIFFERENT `session_id`s leaves exactly ONE
`REBAR_SESSION_ID` export (the latest), one `AI_AGENT` export, and preserves a pre-existing
unrelated `export OTHER_HOOK_VAR=…` line (no accumulation, no stale id). Proof:
`pytest tests/unit/test_session_shims.py -k idempotent -q`.
- [ ] `docs/session-id-shims.md` documents the hook script path + the `settings.json` install
snippet, and the two caveats by their specific phrasing. Proof: a doc-content assert in
`test_session_shims.py` checking `SessionStart`,
`scripts/session-shims/claude-code-session-start.sh`, the `"hooks"`/`"SessionStart"` JSON
snippet, and (whitespace-normalised) the exact G1 phrase "NOT stable across `--resume` /
`--continue` / fork / subagents" and the exact G3 phrase "do NOT `export REBAR_SESSION_ID=…`
from a shell profile".
- [ ] The `claude-code_<ver>` vocabulary examples in ALL THREE of `docs/config.md`,
`docs/event-schema.md`, and the `session_id.py` comment are updated to a base-name +
optional `_<version>` form. Proof: a NEW test
`tests/unit/test_session_shims.py::test_harness_vocabulary_is_base_name_form` reads all
three files and asserts each NO longer contains the old always-versioned example string
(the literal `` claude-code_<ver>` / `opencode `` fragment that S5 wrote) AND DOES contain
the base-name phrase (`` base name `claude-code` `` in the docs,
`base name "claude-code"` in the source comment).
## Depends on
- S1 (the `REBAR_SESSION_ID` contract) and S5 (the `AI_AGENT` -> `claim_harness` contract).

baseline.summary: Claude Code SessionStart hook shim to populate REBAR_SESSION_ID in the local CLI

content.text: Own the **remediation-mode GATE**: the freshness-window + precondition check that decides
whether a re-review runs in floored (remediation) mode or as a normal full review, and wire
it parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`. (This is the task-4 candidate-check; the
Pass-3 drop math it gates is task cc5b. Body/title were previously swapped with task 3689 —
this restores the epic's 6-task decomposition.)
## Preconditions (ALL required, else byte-identical full review)
- config enabled (`remediation_mode` key; see rollout note below)
- plan changed since the prior review
- **code UNCHANGED since baseline** — detected deterministically by comparing the gate's
attested `verified_at_sha` (the origin/main snapshot SHA the gate signs into the prior
review's manifest) against the current run's `verified_at_sha`. Equal ⇒ code unchanged;
differ ⇒ code drifted. This reuses the already-signed snapshot ref — no new diff machinery.
- registry unchanged (criteria-routing material fingerprint equal to the prior review's)
- a prior `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar WITH finding text is available (task e344)
- the last review of ANY kind (full or partial) is within the window (default 60 min),
measured from that last review and **reset on each review** so the loop persists across a
series of edits and lapses to a normal full review only after the agent goes idle.
Code-changed / both-drifted → full review (`drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged, out of scope).
## Rollout (resolves the default-on advisory)
The `remediation_mode` config key ships **default-OFF** for one release (expand-contract:
ship off → validate on the dogfood corpus → flip the default on in a follow-up), so existing
consumers do not silently get a narrowed verdict on upgrade. Setting the key off (or absent)
restores byte-identical full-review behavior at any time — the back-out.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Candidate check enforces ALL preconditions; any failure → full review (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `attest.py`)
- [ ] `remediation_mode` config key (default-OFF for v1) + window minutes (default 60) in `src/rebar/config.py`; key off/absent → byte-identical full review
- [ ] "code unchanged" is the `verified_at_sha` equality check (prior manifest vs current run); registry-unchanged is the routing material-fingerprint equality check
- [ ] Window measured from the last review of any kind, reset on each review
- [ ] both-drifted → full review; `drift_refresh` path byte-unchanged
- [ ] Wiring is parallel to `drift_refresh` in `_run_plan_review`; the Pass-3 drop math itself lives in cc5b (this task only decides remediation-mode eligibility)

baseline.summary: Remediation-mode gate: freshness window + preconditions + wiring

baseline.description:
## Why

Audit Maintainability finding #1: `reconcile.py:697` (and the reconciler's `_loader` helper) loads sibling modules by file path (`_load("reconcile_run_differs", "run_differs.py")`) instead of normal package imports. This defeats every static tool the repo relies on — Pyright/Serena reference resolution, import-linter layering checks, IDE navigation, and the grounding oracle — in the repo's largest and most change-heavy subsystem (~40 modules, 5 of the 10 biggest files). The audit rated the reconciler the highest-onboarding-cost area partly because of this. The mechanism predates the reconciler shipping as a proper package; it is now pure legacy.

## What

Convert the `_engine/rebar_reconciler` path-based `_load()` calls to ordinary `from . import …` / `import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.…` package imports, delete the `_load()` helper once callerless, and let the existing lazy-import pattern (module-level function-local imports with rationale comments) handle any genuine circular-import seams the conversion surfaces.

## Scope

In: all `_load()` call sites under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, the loader helper itself, and any import-cycle untangling the conversion forces. Out: any behavioral change to reconciliation, module splits/renames (janitor epics own refactors — this story changes only *how modules are referenced*, which is why it rides this epic despite the scope boundary; flagged at creation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zero path-based `_load(` call sites remain under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (grep-verifiable)
- [ ] The `_load` helper is deleted outright — the file-path loader (`spec_from_file_location`-based `_load()` and the `_loader.py` `lazy_load` bootstrap) is removed once callerless, with no deprecation stub left behind (deletion is final; there is no future migration path to preserve)
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; reconciler test suites (`tests/scripts/bridge/`, reconciler units) pass unchanged
- [ ] Pyright/Serena can resolve references into the converted modules (spot-check: find-references on a converted symbol returns its call sites)
- [ ] No new import cycles: `python -c "import rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler"` and the optionality guard stay green
baseline.summary: Reconciler: replace path-based _load() module loading with package imports

content.text: ## Finding (DE3 — verified)

`_dispatch_mutation` is dead in production (self-documented as "no longer called from reconcile_once") but kept alive only for a coverage test, and it pins a lazily-built dispatch table — giving false coverage confidence and drift risk vs the real applier path.

Citations: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:83` (`_dispatch_mutation`), self-doc at `reconcile.py:944-946`; dispatch table at `reconcile.py:25`; only caller `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_dispatch_coverage.py`.
## Remediation

Delete `_dispatch_mutation` and its coverage-only dispatch table; rewrite/delete `test_dispatch_coverage.py` so coverage reflects the live dispatch path only. If the table is needed at a live site, inline it there.
cascade_flag: symbol deletion — confirm no non-test caller remains.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_dispatch_mutation` and its dead dispatch table are removed
- [ ] `test_dispatch_coverage.py` exercises the real dispatch path (or is removed)
- [ ] Coverage no longer counts the fossil path

content.text: Make `idea → closed` a reject/drop transition that bypasses the
completion/attestation close gates, keyed on the from-status being `idea`.
## Why
Closing a ticket that is in `idea` means "reject/drop this undesigned idea," not
"this work is complete." Running the completion/attestation gates on it is
nonsensical — there is nothing built to verify or attest — and would block the
reject. Only the from-status `idea` is exempted; every other close path is
unchanged.
## What
- Place the bypass in `close_ticket()` (transition_close.py) as a guard **after**
the open-children guard block and **before** the `_completion_precheck` call:
when the from-status (`current_status`) is `idea`, skip the precheck and return
a normal close result. `_completion_precheck` does not receive `current_status`,
so the check belongs at the call site — this keeps the open-children guard
unconditional and threads no new parameter into `_completion_precheck`. Skipping
the precheck covers the completion verifier, the file-impact→referencing-commit
precheck, and the reason-guard copy inside the precheck.
- In `transition_core` (txn.py), skip the bug-close-reason guard and the
story/epic signature gate when the from-status is `idea`.
- Keep the structural open-children guard active for `idea → closed` (integrity,
not completion): a parent in `idea` with non-closed children is still refused.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — `close_ticket()` from-status guard
placed after the open-children guard and before `_completion_precheck`; the
open-children guard itself is left in place.
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — `transition_core` skips the bug-reason guard and
signature gate when from-status is `idea`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Closing a ticket from `idea` does not invoke the completion verifier
(test-verified, e.g. via a spy/no-LLM assertion).
- [ ] Closing a ticket from `idea` does not run the file-impact→referencing-commit
precheck.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` bug does not require a `Fixed:`/`Escalated:` close reason.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` story does not require a certified signature under the
signature gate.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` epic does not require a certified signature under the
signature gate.
- [ ] Closing an `idea` parent that has a non-closed child is still refused by the
structural open-children guard (test-verified).
- [ ] A normal (non-`idea`) close path still runs the completion verifier
unchanged (regression test-verified).
- [ ] `make lint` passes for the changed files.

baseline.summary: Bypass completion/attestation close gates for idea-to-closed

baseline.description:
## What
Persist a bounded bug-classification enum at close, replacing today's validated-then-discarded free-text `--reason`. Adds a REQUIRED `--class` param to `transition` for bug closes and folds `close_class` into reduced ticket state so it survives and is queryable, with the vocabulary that feeds the classification metrics.

## Files
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — parse a new `--class <value>` flag in `_parse_flags` (alongside `--reason`).
- `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — validate the enum for bug closes (replacing `bug_close_reason_ok` at the transition_core guard, ~line 221-232) and write `close_class` into `status_data`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — CRITICAL: the `_completion_precheck` guard at line ~121 also calls `txn.bug_close_reason_ok(reason)`; update it to accept a valid `close_class` (or skip the reason pre-check when `close_class` is supplied). Thread `close_class` through the close path.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — CRITICAL: `process_status` only folds a fixed set of keys; add a `_fold_close_class(state, data)` helper (mirroring `_fold_claimed_session`) that sets `state['close_class'] = data['close_class']` on a `*->closed` edge, called in BOTH the fork-winner and normal-update branches — otherwise `close_class` never surfaces into reduced state and `rebar show` cannot see it.
- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json` — add optional `close_class`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt`, `docs/ticket-model.md`, `docs/user-guide.md` — document the enum.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_bug_close_class.py` — new.

## Approach
The bug-close reason is required today but never persisted (`txn.py` validates then drops it), so replacing it with a bounded, folded enum is friction-neutral-to-negative and turns wasted input into a hard signal. `--class` is REQUIRED on bug close (mirrors the old required `--reason`): omitting it exits nonzero with a message listing the allowed values. Because `status_data` keys are not auto-surfaced, the enum only reaches `rebar show` via an explicit `_fold_close_class` fold — the exact-parallel of `_fold_claimed_session`. The guard lives at two sites (`txn.py` transition_core AND `transition_close.py` `_completion_precheck`), both updated. Closed MECE vocabulary with an escape + hygiene values: `regression`, `plan_defect`, `env_integration`, `flaky`, `preexisting`, `not_a_bug`, `duplicate`, `escalated`, `undetermined`. `escalated` preserves today's Escalated branch; the rest refine Fixed. Additive/optional schema field (readers tolerate absence); back-out = stop requiring/writing it.

## Tests
- CLI (real subprocess): closing a bug with `--class regression` persists and surfaces `close_class=regression`; omitting `--class` exits nonzero; an invalid class is rejected; `undetermined` is accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_bug_close_class.py` passes: `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class regression` exits 0 and `rebar show <bug> --output json | jq -e '.close_class==\"regression\"'` matches (proving the fold reaches reduced state).

content.text: ## Summary
`rebar show <id>` intermittently returns EMPTY stdout with an apparently-successful (zero) exit instead of the
ticket JSON. Downstream consumers that pipe/redirect `show` into a parser receive empty input and crash. The
store itself is intact — the same ticket `show`s correctly moments later, and `fsck` is clean — so this is a
read-output bug, not data loss.
## Circumstances under which we observed it
Seen repeatedly during a session doing scripted read→transform→write loops on tickets (fetch a description with
`rebar show`, edit it, push with `rebar edit --description`):
- It manifests during a BURST of rapid back-to-back rebar invocations — several `rebar edit` (writes) immediately
followed by `rebar show` (reads) — with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (the default), so each write spawns a
background push to `origin/tickets`.
- The empty return correlates with those in-flight background pushes/git activity on the `tickets` worktree
(`.tickets-tracker/`): a tight retry loop of `rebar show <id> > file` can fail on EVERY attempt (8/8) during the
contention window, while a single `rebar show` after a multi-second quiet period succeeds.
- DECISIVE SIGNAL: setting `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` for the read/write burst made `rebar show` succeed reliably every
time (single piped call) — strongly implicating background-push / git-lock contention as the cause.
- During the same window, `rebar clarity-check <id>` and `rebar check-ac <id>` on the SAME id SUCCEED (a different
read path), and `rebar fsck` reports "no issues found" — so the data is present; only `show`'s stdout comes back
empty.
- Environment: macOS (darwin) / zsh; rebar over the `tickets` orphan branch (worktree `.tickets-tracker/`); an
`origin` remote present; default `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.
## Reproduction Steps
1. With `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` (default) and an `origin` remote, run a burst: `rebar edit` on several tickets,
then immediately `rebar show <id> > out.json` (or `rebar show <id> | python3 -c "import sys,json;json.load(sys.stdin)"`).
2. Repeat in a tight loop.
3. Observe `out.json` intermittently empty / the parser failing with `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`,
despite a success-looking exit.
4. Set `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and repeat → `rebar show` succeeds every time.
## Expected vs Actual
- EXPECTED: `rebar show` is read-consistent under concurrent background push — it returns the full ticket JSON,
or on genuine failure exits NON-ZERO with a diagnostic on stderr. It must NEVER emit empty stdout with exit 0.
- ACTUAL: intermittently emits empty stdout with a success exit during background-push contention, silently
breaking read→transform→write pipelines.
## Impact
- Silently breaks scripted pipelines that consume `rebar show`. It is also a latent DATA-LOSS vector in
combination with `edit --description`: an empty `show` feeding an unguarded `edit --description "$(...)"` would
erase content — the edit-side empty-value guard (bug `e78f-9f79`) mitigates the clobber, but the empty `show`
is the upstream root cause and should be fixed directly.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar show` never returns empty stdout on a zero exit; under read/push contention it returns the complete
record or exits non-zero with a clear error to stderr.
- [ ] `show` reads a consistent snapshot (or retries internally) so a concurrent background push to
`origin/tickets` cannot truncate its output; reproduced + fixed under `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the burst-of-writes-then-`show` pattern and asserts `show` output is always
complete-or-erroring (never empty+exit0).
- [ ] Audit the other read paths (clarity-check/check-ac/fsck observed unaffected) for the same race; fix
uniformly or document why only `show` is affected.

baseline.summary: rebar show intermittently returns empty stdout (exit 0) under concurrent background auto-push

# CHANGELOG.md: git-cliff, prepend-scoped generate-then-curate from conventional commits

## Why

No user-facing changelog exists: `docs/release-notes.md` is the agent-facing contract-change log, and GitHub Releases notes are auto-generated. Across nine surveyed Python tools, towncrier (pip/pytest) solves a many-contributor merge-conflict problem rebar doesn't have; ruff/uv generate from PR labels (needs a PR workflow rebar doesn't have); git-cliff converts the conventional-commit discipline rebar already pays for into a changelog. Keep-a-Changelog is the convergent shape (rich's CHANGELOG.md is the exemplar). Rejected alternatives — towncrier (double-entry ceremony), PR-label generation (no PRs), GitHub-Releases-only (no in-repo artifact) — recorded in cliff.toml header comments.

## What

- Add `cliff.toml`. Keys under their proper sections (a top-level key is silently ignored): `[git] conventional_commits = true`, `filter_unconventional = false`, plus a catch-all commit parser so mixed-history commits are kept. The normative `commit_parsers` mapping (each line individually grep-provable in the AC): `feat` → "Added"; `fix` → "Fixed"; breaking (`!`/BREAKING CHANGE) → "Breaking" (own group, listed first); `perf` → "Changed"; `refactor` → "Changed"; `docs` → "Documentation"; skipped: `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `test`.
- **Pin the tool with an explicit version variable:** Makefile gains `GIT_CLIFF_VERSION := <exact 2.x pin chosen at execution>` and a `make changelog` target that (a) errors clearly if `git-cliff` is missing or its `--version` mismatches the pin, and (b) errors if `VERSION` is not supplied. Install path documented in docs/releasing.md as `pipx install git-cliff==<pin>` (standalone Rust binary; NOT a pyproject dev extra).
- **Invocation interface (resolves the missing-parameter finding):** `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z` → runs exactly `git cliff --unreleased --tag $(VERSION) --prepend CHANGELOG.md`. Full-file regeneration is forbidden after initial generation: the initial run (once, back through v0.1.0; ledger quality accepted for history) is executed manually and documented as one-time; thereafter only the prepend-scoped target is sanctioned, so committed hand-curated sections are never touched. The maintainer hand-curates the newly prepended section before tagging.
- Include `## [Unreleased]` and the compare-link block (rich pattern).
- `docs/releasing.md` gains the step: `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z` → curate the top section (~5 min) → commit → tag; plus the pin + install line. Dial position recorded there: generate-then-edit (pure-generated rejected as ledger-like; mypy-style prose rejected as unsustainable solo).
- **Repoint `[project.urls]` Changelog** (required edit; currently `docs/release-notes.md`, pyproject.toml:78) → `https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md`.
- Pointer line at the top of `docs/release-notes.md`: "User-facing changelog: CHANGELOG.md; this file tracks agent-visible contract changes" (the epic's cross-link AC, owned here).
- Known consumer, acknowledged: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:310` classifies CHANGELOG-touching diffs as a hard-to-reverse surface, so curation commits score higher review impact — accepted; no code change.

## Scope

IN: `cliff.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, Makefile (`GIT_CLIFF_VERSION` + `changelog` target), `docs/releasing.md` step, pyproject urls repoint, release-notes pointer line.
OUT: towncrier/news fragments; changing commit conventions; back-editing published GitHub Releases; the auto-generated GitHub Releases notes (complementary, unchanged); any change to workflow_ops.py.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` exists — prove: `grep -c "^## \[" CHANGELOG.md` ≥ 8 and `grep -q "\[Unreleased\]" CHANGELOG.md` and a compare-link block at the bottom (`grep -q "compare/" CHANGELOG.md`).
- [ ] `cliff.toml` normative mapping — prove, each individually: `grep -q "feat" cliff.toml && grep -q "Added" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "fix" cliff.toml && grep -q "Fixed" cliff.toml`; `grep -qi "breaking" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "refactor" cliff.toml`; `grep -q "Documentation" cliff.toml`; skips present: `grep -q "chore" cliff.toml`; structure: `grep -A3 "\[git\]" cliff.toml | grep -q "filter_unconventional = false"`; catch-all parser present (a trailing `message = ".*"`-style rule) — prove: `grep -q '"\.\*"' cliff.toml`; header comments record the rejected alternatives — prove: `grep -qi "towncrier" cliff.toml`.
- [ ] Makefile interface — prove: `grep -q "GIT_CLIFF_VERSION" Makefile`; `grep -q -- "--unreleased" Makefile`; `grep -q -- "--prepend" Makefile`; `grep -q "VERSION" Makefile` with a guard that errors when unset (`grep -qi "VERSION is required\|VERSION not set" Makefile`); no bare full-regen invocation in the target.
- [ ] Idempotence of the sanctioned path: running `make changelog VERSION=<current>` twice with no new commits produces no second diff.
- [ ] docs/releasing.md — prove: `grep -q "git-cliff==" docs/releasing.md` (the literal pinned install spec) and `grep -q "make changelog" docs/releasing.md`.
- [ ] URL repoint + pointer — prove: `grep "^Changelog" pyproject.toml | grep -q "CHANGELOG.md"`; `head -5 docs/release-notes.md | grep -q "CHANGELOG.md"`.
baseline.summary: CHANGELOG.md: git-cliff generate-then-curate from conventional commits

## Problem

The provider-parity corpus includes the `code-review-verify` spec, whose output carries NO decision polarity, so the two-bucket parity mapping cannot score it. Every verify case is therefore scored `advisory` regardless of its gold label, which makes the gold-block case `V-real-defect` a GUARANTEED recall miss on BOTH arms.

Confirmed empirically in the committed artifact `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`: `V-real-defect` has `label: "block"` with `v1.decision == v2.decision == "advisory"`, `valid: true`, `errored: false`, on BOTH the standard and frontier slots. Both verify cases sit inside the scored gold set (30 records, `n_gold` 28; the two excluded are the `G3-*` container fixtures).

Mechanism: `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` (imported by `provider_parity.py:52` so the two cannot drift) keys only on `verdict == "FAIL"` or a non-empty `findings`. The verifier emits neither — its output vocabulary is `{verifications: [...]}` — so it falls through to `advisory`.

## Why the obvious fix is WRONG

"Treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block`" looks right and is not. `code-review-verify.eval.yaml` states the contract twice:
  - header: "Per the T8-advisory contract it is scored on PRESENCE of verifications, NOT a FAIL/BLOCK
    verdict ... either way the verifier must emit a graded answer set."
  - dataset: "the gating scorer is presence-based, so the verifier must emit verifications for both."
BOTH cases — `V-real-defect` (gold block) and `V-clean-rename` (gold advisory) — are REQUIRED to emit a non-empty list. Mapping presence to `block` would fix the recall miss and simultaneously score the clean case as a block, manufacturing a FALSE ACCEPT. The arm has no polarity to read; no adapter can invent one.

## Approach

EXCLUDE `code-review-verify` from the parity corpus, for a reason DISTINCT from the existing `AGENTIC_SOLVERS` exclusion (that one excludes agentic ops; this one excludes a polarity-free scorer). Keep the two reasons separately named so a future reader does not collapse them.

## Impact on the recorded run

Excluding both verify cases takes `n_gold` 28 -> 26, still above `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20`. It removes one guaranteed miss from each arm, so recall rises on both. The miss was SYMMETRIC, so no gating verdict flips — the v2-vs-v1 noninferiority comparison is unaffected and false-accept is untouched (the affected case is a gold-block case, not a safe one). This corrects measurement ACCURACY, not a pass/fail outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `code-review-verify` is excluded from the parity corpus by a named, separate mechanism from
      `AGENTIC_SOLVERS`, with the reason (no decision polarity) stated at the definition.
- [x] A test asserts NO case from a polarity-free spec is eligible, and that the exclusion reason is
      distinct from the agentic exclusion — i.e. removing the agentic set does not silently cover this.
- [x] A test pins the SPECIFIC failure this fixes: a `{verifications: [...]}` output does NOT map to
      `block`, AND a gold-block verify case is no longer scored as a live miss because it is excluded
      rather than mis-scored. It must fail before the fix.
- [x] The recorded artifact is RE-SCORED OFFLINE with zero model calls; the new `n_gold` and recall are
      recorded, and it is stated explicitly whether any GATING verdict changed (expected: none).
- [x] The gold floor still holds after exclusion (`n_gold >= MIN_GOLD_ITEMS`), asserted by a test so a
      future corpus shrink cannot silently drop below it.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code, the default selection is green, and the
      config-read and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: Parity corpus scores the polarity-free code-review-verify arm, guaranteeing a recall miss

## Summary
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_transition_open_children.py::test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated`
is FLAKY in CI: it passes locally and on re-run, but intermittently fails with a git-state race
in its temporary rebar-store fixture. Observed repeatedly while landing epic sure-foyer-aroma's
13-change Gerrit stack — different changes' CI runs failed on this one test, each cleared by a
`recheck`, and it passes deterministically when run locally in isolation.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Push a stack of changes to Gerrit (or otherwise trigger the full default CI suite repeatedly).
2. Observe that on some runs this single test fails during its temp-store setup, while 4500+ other
   tests pass; a `recheck` (same patchset, no code change) then passes.
Two distinct failure signatures observed (both git races in the fixture's temp repo):
- Run 28825842708 (change 325, ps2): `rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar transition failed (exit 2):
  Error: git operation failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD`
- Run 28828139721 (change 339): `rebar._errors.RebarError: rebar create failed (exit 1):
  Error: git commit failed while holding lock`

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** the test is deterministic — it passes on every run given identical code (it passes
  locally 100% of the time and on CI rechecks).
- **Actual:** it fails intermittently in CI (~1 in N runs) with a git error (`could not parse HEAD`
  / `git commit failed while holding lock`) originating in the temp rebar-store setup, not in the
  behavior under test (the direct-children guard count). The failure is environment/timing-driven.

## Likely Root Cause (hypothesis — confirm before fixing)
The test's fixture builds a temp rebar store and performs `create`/`transition` against it. The two
signatures suggest either (a) an operation running before the store's git HEAD/initial commit is
fully established (`could not parse HEAD`), or (b) `index.lock` contention — a prior git op's lock
not yet released, or concurrent access under xdist/parallel CI. Investigate the fixture's
store-init ordering and any lock-release/retry gap in the `git commit`/`create` path used under
test. This is a TEST/fixture-reliability bug, not a defect in the transition-guard behavior itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause of the intermittent git race in the fixture is identified (HEAD-not-ready vs
      index.lock contention) and documented.
- [ ] The fixture (or the store-init/commit path it exercises) is made deterministic — e.g. ensure
      the initial commit/HEAD exists before ops, and/or the lock acquisition retries/serializes —
      so the test cannot fail on this race.
- [ ] The test passes reliably under repeated/parallel CI runs (no `recheck`-only greens); ideally
      add a stress/repeat guard or a regression note so the flake does not silently return.
baseline.summary: Flaky test_guard_counts_only_direct_children_not_unrelated: intermittent git-race (could not parse HEAD / index.lock) in temp-store fixture

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. Open a PR; CI runs the default pytest suite across the matrix (ubuntu/macos × py3.11/3.12).
2. On a loaded runner (observed on `macos-latest, py3.12`), `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_perf.py` fails on absolute wall-clock assertions even though the code is unchanged.
Observed failures (PR #108 run 28505746020):
- `test_graph_perf.py:59` — `build_dep_graph took 3.192s for 1,000-ticket chain (limit: 2.0s)`
- `test_graph_perf.py:327` — `9 cross-tier add_dependency calls took 8.65s (limit: 5.0s)`
Both passed on all ubuntu runners in the same PR; a manual re-run of the macOS job passed. So the failures are runner-load-dependent, not a code regression.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** perf tests gate against genuine algorithmic regressions and are stable across CI runners.

- **Actual:** they assert against fixed absolute-time thresholds (`< 2.0s`, `< 5.0s`) that a slow/loaded shared runner (esp. macOS) blows past, producing false-failure PR blocks that require manual re-runs.
## Impact
Flaky red on unrelated PRs → wasted re-runs + eroded trust in the gate (a green PR gets blocked by an infra hiccup). This blocked epic 3156's final merge (PR #108) until a manual re-run.
## Root cause

Absolute wall-clock budgets are sensitive to shared-runner contention. A perf test should measure a *relative* signal (scaling / ratio vs a baseline op on the same machine) or run in an isolated, non-gating, retried context — not a raw seconds ceiling.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_perf.py` no longer false-fails under runner load: either (a) assert on a RELATIVE metric (e.g. per-op time scaled to a same-machine baseline, or big-O scaling ratio between N and 2N) instead of an absolute seconds ceiling, or (b) mark the wall-clock assertions with a bounded retry (e.g. `flaky`/rerun) AND widen the ceilings with generous headroom, or (c) move the raw-timing assertions to a dedicated NON-gating perf job (still run, reported, not merge-blocking) while keeping a correctness-only assertion in the gating suite.
- [ ] The chosen approach still catches a real >2x algorithmic regression (a deliberately O(n^2) reintroduction fails the test) — documented in the test.
- [ ] No absolute single-run wall-clock ceiling remains in the gating path for these two tests.

baseline.summary: Flaky graph perf tests (absolute wall-clock limits) fail on loaded CI runners

# op-cert: trusted gate service — authoritative-state fetch, per-kind dispatch, async job API (+ client command)

## Why
For high assurance, a developer routes a gate run to a trusted environment that fetches
authoritative state ITSELF (ticket state from the tickets branch; code at the review remote's
`main` tip), runs the gate, and returns an Ed25519-signed `rebar.opcert.v1` cert — so
client-supplied inputs cannot forge a pass (the SLSA non-falsifiable-provenance principle). This
story builds the **service and its client half only**; AWS IaC + the real deploy are the sibling
"AWS IaC + deploy" story, and the signing behavior itself ships in the "producer signing seam"
story this depends on. All design forks are settled in the epic's "Producer-signing &
compute-runtime design resolution" section — this story implements, it does not decide.

**Hard dependencies (not yet on `main`):** the op-cert substrate consumed here
(`signing.sign_opcert_manifest`, `src/rebar/attest/opcert.py`, `trusted_env.py`, `sshsig.sign` —
Gerrit changes 649/650/660, in review), the merge-gate consumer `rebar verify-opcert` (story 4214,
Gerrit change 664, in review — referenced by the client ACs below), and the producer signing seam
story must land first;
mentions of them below are forward references to that stack, enforced by this ticket's
`depends_on` links. `src/rebar/review_bot/app.py` (the pattern mirrored) IS on `main` today.

## What
**Service** (`src/rebar/opcert_service/`, library-mode: rebar imported behind a thin FastAPI app —
the `review_bot/app.py` software pattern; NOT the stdio `rebar-mcp`):
- **Async job API** (gate runs take 30s–minutes; no sync request can hold): `POST /opcert/jobs`
  validates, enqueues on an in-process `asyncio.Queue`, returns **202 `{job_id}`**;
  `GET /opcert/jobs/{job_id}` returns the job record. Single background worker drains serially
  under a bounded per-run timeout: default **900 s** (gate runs take 30s–minutes; the ceiling is
  generous), configurable via `REBAR_OPCERT_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Job state is in-memory (a restart loses queued jobs; clients
  re-submit — cert minting is idempotent).
- **Request schema**: `{"ticket_id": str, "kind": "completion-verifier"|"plan-review"}` — ONLY
  identifiers. Any other client field (a `material_fingerprint`, a `commit`, an `env_id`) is
  IGNORED; the server derives every authoritative value itself.
- **Authoritative fetch**: the worker fetches the tickets branch (ticket state) and the review
  remote's `main` tip (code) with its own read-only credentials — sources named by env config:
  `REBAR_OPCERT_REVIEW_REMOTE_URL` (code) and `REBAR_OPCERT_TICKETS_REMOTE_URL` (tickets
  branch), credentials from the service env. It sets `merged_log_commit = <fetched main HEAD
  sha>` and computes the material fingerprint itself. Each job runs in an **ephemeral
  workspace clone** discarded after the job.
- **Per-kind dispatch + native verdicts (no unified enum)**: `plan-review` →
  `rebar.llm.review_plan(...)` (verdict `PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE`); `completion-verifier` →
  `rebar.llm.verify_completion(...)` (verdict `PASS|FAIL`). Error handling is per-kind and
  ASYMMETRIC, matching the live code: `verify_completion` RAISES
  `LLMError`/`LLMUnavailableError` → the job ends `status: "error"` with the enum mapping
  below; `review_plan` does NOT raise on an LLM outage — it degrades IN-BAND to
  `verdict: "INDETERMINATE"` (unsigned), so the job COMPLETES with that verdict and
  `envelope: null`; only an unexpected exception maps a plan-review job to
  `status: "error", class: "internal"`. Never a fabricated verdict. Response/job schema:
  `{status: "queued"|"running"|"completed"|"error", kind, verdict: <native enum>|null,
  envelope: <encoded DSSE>|null, material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit, error: {class, message}|null}`
  — `envelope` present ONLY on a `PASS` verdict. `error.class` is a CLOSED enum mapped from the
  raised exception type: `"llm_unavailable"` (`LLMUnavailableError`), `"llm_error"` (other
  `LLMError`), `"timeout"` (per-run timeout exceeded), `"internal"` (anything else).
- **Signing = the producer seam, once; the service only PROVISIONS the key.** The gate
  producers mint the op-cert via the signing seam (producer-seam story); the handler itself
  never signs bespokely and never passes `sign=False`. Per-kind producer step: `review_plan`
  signs internally (`sign=True` default). `verify_completion` has NO `sign` parameter — the
  completion producer step lives in the close gate today (`transition_close.py`'s
  `_verdict_manifest` + seam call) — so this story EXTRACTS that pair into a reusable
  `sign_completion_verdict(result, ticket_id, repo_root)` used by BOTH `transition_close.py`
  (behavior unchanged) and this worker on a PASS verdict: the worker invokes the same producer
  function, not a bespoke signer. The hand-off protocol: this story
  adds one override to the seam's key resolution — `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` (an explicit key
  file path) takes precedence over the `<tracker>/.opcert-key` genesis. Before dispatching a
  job, the worker fetches the SSM SecureString (`/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key`),
  **materializes it to a 0600 `mkstemp` temp file** (SSHSIG signing shells
  `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <path>` and needs a file path), sets `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` to that
  path and `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` as the principal for the gate run (the principal is the
  environment's logical id string — it MUST exactly equal the environment's `env_id` entry in
  the consuming project's `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`, since it becomes the DSSE keyid
  the merge gate pins on; a non-empty printable token, e.g. `nava-opcert-prod-1`), and **deletes the file in a
  `finally`** — never persisted, and the seam signs exactly once with the provisioned key. The
  key MUST be passphrase-free (`ssh-keygen -Y sign` is non-interactive). The legacy HMAC
  environment key is never provisioned in the server.
- **Stateless / store-read-only — reconciled with the seam's `sign=True`.** Running a gate with
  signing on appends a `SIGNATURE` event to the store it runs against; on the server that store
  is the job's ephemeral workspace clone, with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and NO tickets-branch
  write credential — so the event lands only in the discarded workspace, never on the shared
  branch. The worker reads back the freshly-appended record by the NAMED mechanism —
  `show_ticket(ticket_id)["attestations"][kind]` in the ephemeral workspace (the reduced record
  of the just-written `SIGNATURE` event; `opcert.opcert_from_record` decodes its `envelope` +
  bound fields) — and returns the envelope in the response; the CLIENT persists it to the shared tickets branch. Nothing is
  ever pushed by the server (asserted by a test on the workspace remote config). Endpoint authn
  (SigV4) is terminated at API Gateway (the IaC story); the app additionally requires a shared
  secret as defense in depth — same posture as `review_bot`'s check (which uses a `?token=`
  query parameter, `review_bot/app.py`); the opcert app checks an `X-Opcert-Guard` **header**
  instead (value from the `REBAR_OPCERT_GUARD` env var, materialized from SSM by the deploy
  story), because API Gateway injects static request headers on the integration.
- **Container image**: `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert` (build context = repo root, per the
  review_bot Dockerfile pattern) installing **OpenSSH ≥ 8.9** and running
  `uvicorn rebar.opcert_service.app:app`.

**Client** (`src/rebar/_commands/remote_cert.py`, CLI `rebar remote-cert <ticket-id> <kind>`).
Wiring is enumerated (the drift gates that bit change 664 before): the `argv[0] ==` intercept
ladder in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` gains the `remote-cert` arm; a help file is added under
`src/rebar/_cli/help/`; `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`'s curated `INTERCEPT_COMMANDS` dict is
updated in the same change (its set-equality test fails otherwise); and every new
`REBAR_OPCERT_*` env var is regenerated into `docs/env-vars.md` (`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
scans `src/rebar`; the CI env-var drift gate fails otherwise).
- Reads `verify.opcert_remote_url` (new `VerifyConfig` key, `str | None = None`; unset → clear
  error; nothing remote is ever required for local operation). SigV4-signs the request with
  ambient AWS credentials, submits the job, polls to a terminal status, and on `PASS` **persists
  the returned envelope + bound fields as the `SIGNATURE` event** (the same event shape
  `sign_opcert_manifest` appends; auto-pushed with the tickets branch). Safe because the envelope
  is self-authenticating — tampering with the bound values breaks the signature the merge gate
  (`rebar verify-opcert`) verifies. Non-PASS / error → non-zero exit with the job's error class.

## Scope
- In: the FastAPI service, dispatch/verdict mapping, authoritative fetch, SSM-parameter key
  materialization + the `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` seam override, Dockerfile, the `remote-cert` client command, `verify.opcert_remote_url`.
- Out: Terraform/API Gateway/SSM resources + the real deploy + live round-trip
  (the "AWS IaC + deploy" story); the producer signing seam itself (dependency); HMAC removal
  (8f1d).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `POST /opcert/jobs` ACKs 202 `{job_id}` and `GET /opcert/jobs/{id}` reaches a terminal
      status via the background worker; a test drives the round-trip against a fake authoritative
      source with the request/response schemas above.
- [ ] Integrity test (the load-bearing one): a request carrying a **doctored
      `material_fingerprint`** and a doctored `commit` is accepted, the extra fields are ignored,
      and the signed op-cert's bound `material_fingerprint`/`merged_log_commit` equal the values
      the server derived from its own fetch — a client cannot influence any bound value.
- [ ] Per-kind verdict mapping: tests assert `plan-review` jobs surface
      `PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE` natively, `completion-verifier` jobs surface `PASS|FAIL`, a
      raised `LLMError` yields `status="error"` with `verdict=null`, and `envelope` is non-null
      ONLY on `PASS` (BLOCK/FAIL/INDETERMINATE/error all return `envelope: null`).
- [ ] Key materialization: a test asserts the SSM SecureString value is written to a 0600
      `mkstemp` file for the `ssh-keygen -Y sign` invocation and that NO key file remains after
      signing (including on a raised exception — the `finally` path).
- [ ] The server appends no tickets-branch event: a test asserts the store is unchanged after a
      completed job; `rebar remote-cert` persists the returned envelope as a `SIGNATURE` event
      that `verify_signature`/`rebar verify-opcert` then certify, and a tampered envelope is
      rejected (`mismatch`).
- [ ] Offline default preserved: a test asserts every local op-cert sign/verify path works with
      `verify.opcert_remote_url` unset and no network — the remote path is opt-in and its absence
      never blocks a local operation.
- [ ] `infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert` installs OpenSSH ≥ 8.9 and starts the service; a test
      asserts the Dockerfile declares both.
- [ ] Origin guard: tests assert a request missing the `X-Opcert-Guard` header, or carrying a
      value that does not match `REBAR_OPCERT_GUARD`, is rejected (403) before any work is
      enqueued; a matching header is accepted.
- [ ] Server never pushes: a test asserts the job workspace runs with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and
      no push remote/credential, and that the shared store is byte-identical after a completed
      PASS job (the SIGNATURE event exists only in the discarded workspace).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

baseline.description:
# New-gate CI steps fail pre-gate changes: workflow from target branch, tree from change

## Summary

Gerrit's verify job takes the **workflow definition from the target branch** but **checks out the change's tree**. A newly landed gate step that runs a repo script (`python scripts/check_X.py`) therefore hard-fails every open change whose base predates the gate-introducing commit: the step runs, but the script does not exist in the checked-out tree.

Observed in production: changes 1332/1333 (based before d37e's 6739ea54fa landed) failed Verified with `python: can't open file '.../scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`. The just-merged wall-clock-assert gate (1e95, 9af88c3ada, scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py) has the identical window. Immediate recovery for 1332/1333 was a server-side rebase:chain — but every future gate-script landing re-opens this window for all in-flight changes.

## Root cause

The two new gate steps in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml invoke their script unconditionally. The workflow definition and the checked-out tree can legitimately diverge (definition-from-target-branch is Gerrit CI's model), so a gate step must tolerate a tree that predates its script.

## Fix plan

Guard both new gate steps with an existence check that SKIPS (with an explanatory log line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree:

    - name: raw-git-write gate
      run: |
        if [ -f scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py ]; then
          python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py
        else
          echo "scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping"
        fi

Same shape for the wall-clock-assert gate step. Include an inline workflow comment stating the idiom and WHY (definition-from-target-branch vs change tree skew), so future gate authors copy the guard along with the step. Deleting a gate script in a change silently skips that gate for that change — acceptable: such a deletion is itself visible in review, and the gate re-enforces on every post-merge change.

Older gate steps (comment-hygiene, module-size, commit wrap) predate all open changes; leave them unguarded to keep the diff minimal — the documented idiom covers any future script.

## Verification

- actionlint via make lint passes on the edited workflow.
- Shell logic locally exercised both branches: script present -> runs detector (exit propagates); script absent (temp dir) -> skip message, exit 0.
- CI on the change itself (which HAS both scripts) still runs both gates — Verified +1 proves the present-branch path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both new gate steps (raw-git-write, wall-clock-assert) skip with an explanatory message when their script is absent from the checked-out tree, and run it when present.
- [x] The skew rationale + copy-me idiom is documented inline in the workflow at the gate steps.
- [x] make lint (actionlint) passes; both branches of the guard exercised locally.

## File impact

- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml (edit)

baseline.description:
Cupid enrichment op: LLM ticket-digest extractor + digest schema.

## Why
Semantic overlap detection needs a compact, normalized per-ticket representation that
catches paraphrase ("login broken" vs "users can't authenticate") WITHOUT embeddings,
keeping rebar on its Anthropic-only, no-heavy-ML grain. The Cupid pattern
(arXiv:2308.10022) uses an LLM as a one-time feature extractor. DERISKED: the recall
experiment (see epic experiment comment) showed digest-BM25F retrieves 8/8 heavy
paraphrases at rank 1 (recall@20 = 1.0); the digest is the load-bearing artifact for the
whole feature.

## What
A new LLM operation `rebar.llm.enrich(ticket_id)` returning a validated dedup-digest
wrapper, plus its output schema and prompt. It is a **structured single-turn** op:
assemble the ticket's canonical text -> load the prompt ->
`RunRequest(mode="structured", output_schema="ticket_digest", execution_mode="single_turn")`
-> `get_runner(cfg, override=runner).run(req)` (the runner validates the structured
response against the `ticket_digest` schema via `finalize_outcome`/`validate_structured`)
-> the op post-processes the proposition count and returns the wrapper.

Modeled on the structured single-turn pattern in
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py::pass1_chunk` (which builds
`RunRequest(mode="structured", execution_mode="single_turn")`) — **NOT** on
`src/rebar/llm/completion.py` (that is a *gate* op that resolves a read-root and delegates
verdict production to the workflow engine; it contains no `RunRequest`), and **NOT** on
`operations.py::review_ticket` (which uses `mode="findings"`/`execution_mode="agentic"`,
the opposite of what we want). Because `enrich` is single-turn with no file/repo tools it
does **NOT** need `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` / `gate_read_root` or snapshot
materialization; it builds cfg via `LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=...)` (or an explicit
`config=`), assembles the ticket text, and runs.

The digest schema (`ticket_digest`):
`{problem_keywords: string[], component_or_area: string, key_entities: string[], propositions: string[]}`;
`propositions` = 2-6 atomic problem/repro statements; logs/stack-traces/code are discarded
by the prompt. The payload is deterministic (no timestamps/uuids) so the stored record is
stable modulo LLM wording.

### Op signature (with a body-injection escape hatch for offline tests)
`enrich(ticket_id=None, *, text=None, repo_root=None, config=None, runner=None)`. Exactly
one of `ticket_id` / `text` must be given (else `ValueError`):
- `ticket_id` given -> the op reads the ticket via the established `rebar.llm` facade
  `from rebar import _reads; state = _reads.show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` (the
  same layering-correct pattern used by `completion.py:294`, `operations.py:82`,
  `plan_review/orchestrator.py:168`), then assembles the source text with a TRIVIAL INLINE
  join of `state["title"]` + `state["description"]` + each `state["comments"][*]["body"]`
  ("\n"-joined, skipping empties) directly in `enrich.py`. It does NOT import
  `rebar._engine_support.gates._ticket_text` — no `rebar.llm.*` module imports
  `_engine_support.gates`, and doing so would be the first layering violation in the package;
  the join is a couple of lines and needs no private helper. (S1/`2d0f`, which computes a
  content-hash, owns its OWN local normalizer for hashing; enrich's inline join only feeds the
  LLM prompt and need not be byte-identical to it.)
- `text` given -> the op uses that string directly as the source, bypassing the store read
  entirely. This is the injection seam the offline `test_enrich_quality` and other unit
  tests use to feed a fixture `body` without a live ticket store. (It is a real API on the
  op, not a test-only monkeypatch.)

### System prompt + instructions assembly (query context)
- **system_prompt** is resolved from the packaged prompt FILE `reviewers/ticket_digest.md`
  (file stem `ticket_digest` -> prompt id `ticket-digest`, underscores normalized to dashes
  exactly as `ticket_quality.md` -> `ticket-quality`) via the da27 prompt machinery —
  `prompts.get_prompt("ticket-digest", repo_root=cfg.repo_path)` then
  `prompts.resolve_prompt(prompt, {...}, repo_root=cfg.repo_path)` — mirroring
  `plan_review/passes.py::_resolve_system`. No inline prompt string constants; a project
  `.rebar/prompts/ticket-digest.md` override wins.
- **instructions** are the source text resolved above (from `ticket_id` or the injected
  `text`), rendered as plain text. No graph, no file contents. The PROMPT (not the op)
  instructs the model to discard any logs/stack-traces/code that appear in the body — so log
  exclusion is a prompt-encoded guarantee, verified statically by `test_prompt_excludes_logs`.

## Return shape & processing order (grounded in `findings.finalize_outcome`)
`get_runner(cfg, override=runner).run(req)` returns, for `mode="structured"`, the dict
`{**payload, "runner": <str>, "model": <str|None>, "trace_id": <str|None>}` where `payload`
is the model's structured output already validated against the `ticket_digest` schema
(`findings.finalize_outcome` -> `validate_structured`, `findings.py:321`). So the run result
carries the four digest fields PLUS three provenance keys — it is NOT itself a bare digest.
The op therefore:
1. Selects the digest by field name:
   `digest = {k: run_result[k] for k in ("problem_keywords", "component_or_area", "key_entities", "propositions")}`
   (dropping the `runner`/`model`/`trace_id` provenance keys).
2. Post-processes the `propositions` list ONLY: if `len > overlap_propositions_max`, truncate
   to max; if `len < overlap_propositions_min`, keep them all and set
   `low_proposition_count=True`; it never raises on count.
3. Returns the wrapper
   `{"digest": <ticket_digest dict, exactly the four fields>, "low_proposition_count": bool}`.
   `low_proposition_count` lives on the op's RETURN object only — never a fifth field of the
   persisted `ticket_digest`. The `digest` value validates against `ticket_digest`.

## Error contract (resolves AC "clean error, no partial write")
- A shape-invalid structured payload (valid JSON, wrong shape — e.g. `propositions` missing
  or non-string) raises `FindingsError` from `validate_structured` (`findings.py`) INSIDE
  the runner's `run()`, before the op sees any result; the op never catch-and-partial-writes,
  so no record is persisted. This is the path `test_bad_shape` exercises with a FakeRunner
  seeded with a schema-invalid `structured=` dict.
- An absent structured response at runtime (the live model emits no parseable structured
  object) is raised as `rebar.llm.errors.StructuredOutputError` by `finalize_outcome`
  (`findings.py:305`, `structured is None` branch) — a framework guarantee on the live path
  (FakeRunner cannot reproduce it: `FakeRunner(structured=None)` falls through to the
  findings branch, `runner.py:120-137`), so it is asserted at the `finalize_outcome` unit
  level, not fabricated through FakeRunner.
- Absent LLM (no `[agents]` extra / no API key) raises `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError`
  (subclasses of `LLMError`) cleanly via the runner preflight/config path; `test_absent_llm`.
- The op defines NO new exception type — it reuses the framework's (`FindingsError`,
  `StructuredOutputError`, `LLMUnavailableError`).

## Config-bound threading (resolves the zero-arg-builder gap)
The proposition bound is NOT enforced through the `register_contract` schema builder (the
zero-arg `Callable[[], type]` cannot see config). Instead: (a) the prompt instructs the
model to emit MIN..MAX propositions, and (b) the op post-validates the parsed count
(truncate to max if more; keep + flag `low_proposition_count` if fewer; never raise). The
MIN/MAX bounds are LLM-feature tunables on `LLMConfig` (`[tool.rebar.llm]`, env
`REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_PROPOSITIONS_MIN` / `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_PROPOSITIONS_MAX`, read in
`LLMConfig.from_env` via the `_llm_int` helper) — `_config_schema.py` reserves the `llm.*`
layer, so these must NOT go on `VerifyConfig`.

## Scope (exact edit targets)
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`: add module constants `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_PROPOSITIONS_MIN = 2` /
  `DEFAULT_OVERLAP_PROPOSITIONS_MAX = 6`, dataclass fields
  `LLMConfig.overlap_propositions_min` / `overlap_propositions_max`, and two `_llm_int(...)`
  lines in `from_env` (env `REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_PROPOSITIONS_MIN/MAX`, file keys
  `overlap_propositions_min/max`).
- New op module `src/rebar/llm/enrich.py` defining
  `enrich(ticket_id=None, *, text=None, repo_root=None, config=None, runner=None)` (exactly
  one of `ticket_id`/`text`; `text` bypasses the store read — see Op signature above).
- Export: add `from rebar.llm.enrich import enrich` to `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py` and add
  `"enrich"` to the `# operations` group of its `__all__` (NOT `src/rebar/__init__.py`; the
  core package must not import `rebar.llm`).
- Prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ticket_digest.md` (stem `ticket_digest` -> id
  `ticket-digest`), front-matter `schema_version: 1`, `execution_mode: single_turn`,
  `outputs: ticket_digest`, `category: enrich` (NOT `review`, so it is not indexed/selected
  as a reviewer — `reviewers/index.json` lists only `category=="review"`), and a body that
  explicitly instructs the model to discard logs/stack-traces/code and emit MIN..MAX atomic
  propositions. The valid `execution_mode` enum is `single_turn|agentic`
  (`prompting/prompts.py:74`); `1-TURN` is invalid. If a new packaged prompt must be
  enumerated in a `_packaged_prompt_files()`/catalog manifest, add `ticket_digest.md` there.
- Output schema `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_digest.schema.json` (all four fields required;
  `problem_keywords`/`key_entities`/`propositions` = arrays of non-empty strings;
  `component_or_area` a non-empty string; `propositions` `minItems: 1`). WIRE IT: in
  `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py` add `TICKET_DIGEST = "ticket_digest"`, register
  `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["enrich"] = TICKET_DIGEST`, and add `TICKET_DIGEST` to `__all__` — this
  satisfies `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py::test_every_schema_file_is_wired`
  (every schema file must appear in `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS.values() | exempt`). The synthetic
  `"enrich"` key has no CLI `--output` arm (like `"verify_completion"`), so the CLI-coverage
  invariants do not drive it.
- Contract registration + bootstrap: define the builder `ticket_digest_response_model()`
  **inside `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py`** (co-located with `completion_verdict_response_model`,
  pydantic imported inside the body), and register it at the BOTTOM of `contracts.py` with
  `register_contract("ticket_digest", ticket_digest_response_model)` next to the two built-ins
  (`review_result`, `completion_verdict`). Registration is guaranteed-before-use by
  **co-location**: `response_model_for` is defined in `contracts.py`, so any code path that
  calls `response_model_for("ticket_digest")` has necessarily imported `contracts.py`, which
  executes the module body — including the bottom `register_contract(...)` line — first. (This
  is the correct mechanism; `rebar.llm.__init__` does NOT import `contracts` at module top —
  the runner imports it lazily — so the guarantee is co-location, not startup import.) Defining
  the builder in `contracts.py` (not `enrich.py`) also avoids a `contracts -> enrich` import
  cycle. `enrich.py` merely references the schema by the string name `"ticket_digest"`.

## Dependencies
None (leaf). S1/S2/S7 consume the op + the `ticket_digest` schema as sibling stories.

## Testing
- Unit `tests/unit/test_enrich.py` (all use `FakeRunner(structured=...)` — NO live LLM):
  - `test_schema_valid` — `enrich()` with a FakeRunner seeded with a valid digest returns
    `{digest, low_proposition_count}` and `digest` validates against `ticket_digest`.
  - `test_no_nondeterministic_fields` — the returned `digest` has exactly the four schema
    fields (no timestamps/uuids/provenance keys leaked from the run result).
  - `test_propositions_bounded` — FakeRunner returning >max propositions => truncated to max;
    <min => kept with `low_proposition_count=True`, no raise.
  - `test_bad_shape` — FakeRunner seeded with a schema-invalid `structured=` dict (e.g.
    `propositions` omitted) => `FindingsError` raised inside the run, and nothing is returned/
    written (no partial write).
  - `test_absent_llm` — with the real (pydantic_ai) runner and no `[agents]`/key, preflight/run
    raises `LLMUnavailableError`/`LLMConfigError` cleanly.
  - `test_enrich_exported` — `from rebar.llm import enrich` succeeds AND
    `rebar.llm.contracts.response_model_for("ticket_digest")` returns the registered
    ticket_digest model (not the default findings model) — covers the export + contract-
    registration Scope items.
  - `test_prompt_excludes_logs` — STATIC assertion that the packaged
    `reviewers/ticket_digest.md` prompt text contains the explicit "discard
    logs/stack-traces/code" directive (the honest place the exclusion guarantee lives — a
    FakeRunner cannot prove model behaviour).
  - `test_prompt_frontmatter` — loads the prompt via `prompts.get_prompt("ticket-digest")`
    and asserts `execution_mode == "single_turn"`, `outputs == "ticket_digest"`, and that it
    is NOT a reviewer (`category != "review"`, absent from `reviewers/index.json`) — so the
    enrich prompt is never selected as a plan/ticket reviewer.
  - `test_finalize_absent_structured` — a `finalize_outcome`-level unit asserting that a
    `structured_response=None` outcome raises `StructuredOutputError` (the live-path guarantee
    FakeRunner cannot reproduce).
- Quality fixture test `test_enrich_quality` — **offline + deterministic, exercises the real
  `enrich()` op path** (assembly -> run -> select -> post-process -> wrap). Fixtures live at
  `tests/fixtures/enrich_quality/*.json`, >=6 files COMMITTED as deliverables of this story,
  each shaped
  `{"ticket_id": str, "body": str (one is a ~4000-token body), "digest": {<pre-generated ticket_digest, four fields, captured once from a real enrich run>}, "gold": [<expected entity/keyword strings>]}`.
  The test FIRST asserts cardinality — `assert len(fixtures) >= 6` (so an empty/missing
  fixture dir fails loudly rather than passing vacuously). Then for each fixture it builds a
  `FakeRunner(structured=fixture["digest"])` and calls `enrich(text=fixture["body"], runner=<fake>)`
  (the `text=` injection seam — no store read), and asserts deterministic string-set
  membership on the RESULT: >=1 `gold` string appears (case-insensitive) in
  `result["digest"]["key_entities"]` union `result["digest"]["problem_keywords"]`. This both
  exercises `enrich()` and stays deterministic (the canned digests are real captured model
  outputs; regenerate only when the prompt changes).
- Gated live regenerator `test_enrich_quality_live` — `@pytest.mark.skipif` unless
  `REBAR_RUN_LLM_EVAL=1`; calls the real model over the fixture bodies and re-asserts gold
  membership (the path that regenerates the canned `digest` blocks). NEVER runs in CI.
- Proving command: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py -q` (self-contained;
  fixtures committed, live test skipped, so it never needs a generation step first).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar.llm.enrich(ticket_id)` returns `{digest, low_proposition_count}`, and the
  `digest` field (exactly the four schema fields) validates against `ticket_digest`;
  `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_schema_valid` and `::test_no_nondeterministic_fields`.
- [ ] `from rebar.llm import enrich` succeeds and `contracts.response_model_for("ticket_digest")`
  returns the registered model (not the default findings model);
  `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_enrich_exported`.
- [ ] The packaged `reviewers/ticket_digest.md` prompt encodes the logs/stack-traces/code exclusion
  directive; `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_prompt_excludes_logs`.
- [ ] The `propositions` count is enforced in the op (>max truncate to max; <min keep + flag,
  no raise); `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_propositions_bounded`.
- [ ] A shape-invalid structured payload raises `FindingsError` with no partial write
  (`::test_bad_shape`); an absent structured response raises `StructuredOutputError`
  (`::test_finalize_absent_structured`); absent-LLM raises `LLMUnavailableError`
  (`::test_absent_llm`).
- [ ] The quality fixture test asserts `len(fixtures) >= 6` (fails loudly if the committed
  fixture dir is empty/missing) and, for each, calls `enrich(text=fixture["body"], runner=<fake>)`
  with a FakeRunner seeded with that fixture's captured digest, asserting >=1 gold
  entity/keyword appears in `key_entities` union `problem_keywords` (deterministic; exercises
  the op path via the `text=` injection seam); `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_enrich_quality`.
- [ ] The packaged prompt loads as `ticket-digest` with `execution_mode: single_turn`,
  `outputs: ticket_digest`, and is NOT a reviewer (`category != review`);
  `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich.py::test_prompt_frontmatter`.
baseline.summary: Cupid enrichment op: LLM ticket-digest extractor + digest schema

content.text: ## What
Port exists + resolve + format (resolution/display arms) to in-process Python in one cohesive
rebar._engine_support.lookups module.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] exists/resolve/format dispatch in-process via rebar._cli (_LOOKUPS set, full auto-init)
