baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The outbound link differ compares in vendor shape. `outbound_links.py:30` imports
`_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` from `adapters.jira.jira_fields`; `_existing_jira_links`
(`outbound_links.py:38-63`) reads the raw vendor `fields.issuelinks` list
(`{type:{name}, inwardIssue:{key}, outwardIssue:{key}}`) into a `(type_name, other_key)` set;
and `_diff_links` translates relation→`(jira_type, swap)` inline at `outbound_links.py:105`.
Epic bbf1 AC3 requires zero `adapters.jira` imports in core, and ADR 0035 §(d) requires that
core compare only canonical shapes (vendor payloads cross core opaquely, produced/consumed by
port calls at the boundaries — the same principle the sibling canonical field-diff story pins
for fields).

## Approach

Move both link translations onto the `SupportsLinks` capability (adapter-side, translation
only — neither member is parameterized on a shape a non-Jira backend lacks):

- `map_remote_links(remote_fields)` → the canonical link set: entries of
  `(relation, remote_key, opaque_vendor_type)`. The Jira implementation absorbs today's
  `_existing_jira_links` (`outbound_links.py:38-63`) including its direction-agnostic dedup
  (`:57-62`), translating vendor link-type names back to canonical relations via the adapter's
  own map; remote link types with no canonical relation are returned with `relation=None` so
  core continues to ignore them for matching and never removes them (today's semantics).
  The `opaque_vendor_type` passenger is carried untouched by core solely for the REMOVE
  payload's `type` key.
- `link_payload_for_relation(relation)` → `(vendor_type, swap)` — the emission translation,
  replacing the inline `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK.get(relation)` at `outbound_links.py:105`.

Core `_diff_links`/`_diff_link_removals` (`outbound_links.py:66-135` and `:138-199`) then
compare local `ticket["deps"]` (`{target_id, relation, link_uuid}`) against the canonical set
in relation vocabulary. Emitted ADD/REMOVE payload keys are unchanged (ADD
`outbound_links.py:119-128`, REMOVE `:196-197`), so the link apply path is untouched.
`_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` becomes adapter-internal. The AST neutrality gate in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` is extended to assert zero
`adapters.jira` imports in `outbound_links.py`.

Rejected alternatives: (a) keeping the vendor link diff in core (violates §(d) and AC3);
(b) a port method that accepts the vendor issuelinks dict *and* the local deps and returns
the diff — that moves diffing onto the port, the exact violation class plan review blocked
on ticket 97f2's prior attempt (core owns diff; the port only translates).

## Scope

- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py (SupportsLinks: map_remote_links + link_payload_for_relation)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py (canonical comparison; drop vendor import)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py (implement the two members)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/jira_fields.py (_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK becomes adapter-internal; reverse map)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py (AST gate extended to outbound_links.py)
- tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ (link-diff behavior tests)

## Testing

- Happy path: a local dep missing remotely emits an ADD with today's exact payload keys and
  values (`type`, `to_key`, `relation`, `swap`, `link_uuid`); a dep present remotely (either
  direction) emits nothing.
- Edge/failure: unknown remote link types are ignored for matching and never removed;
  removals remain managed-ref gated (`outbound_links.py:138-199` semantics); REMOVE payload
  carries the original vendor type name via the opaque passenger.
- Gate: the extended AST case fails if `outbound_links.py` re-grows an `adapters.jira`
  import.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `outbound_links.py` contains NO `adapters.jira` import (module-level or
      function-nested) — verified by the extended AST case in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`.
- [ ] Link diffing compares canonical relations only; vendor link-type names appear in core
      solely as opaque payload passengers — verified by code review + the behavior tests in
      Testing (identical ADD/REMOVE payloads to today).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green; whole test tree collects with 0 errors.

## Plan-review remediation (drift re-review, G1G2 findings)

Two gaps are pinned here:

1. **`outbound_differ.py` is in scope.** `compute_outbound_mutations` (in `outbound_differ.py`)
   calls `_diff_links(ticket, jira_fields, binding_store)` at the update path. That call site
   must additionally pass the configured backend's `SupportsLinks` capability so `_diff_links`
   / `_diff_link_removals` can translate via `map_remote_links` / `link_payload_for_relation`.
   The backend is already in scope there (threaded for the field diff). So:
   `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` is ADDED to Scope — it passes the
   `SupportsLinks` capability as the new 4th argument to `_diff_links`.

2. **The ADD dedup stays DIRECTION-AGNOSTIC.** Today `_existing_jira_links` inserts
   `(jira_type_name, other_key)` for the key present on EITHER `inwardIssue` OR `outwardIssue`,
   so a Jira link of a given type between the local issue and key K dedups a local dep to K
   REGARDLESS of which side K is on (verified: a local `blocks`→K dep against an INWARD Blocks
   link from K emits nothing today). The canonical set from `map_remote_links` carries the
   `opaque_vendor_type` passenger precisely so this is preserved: the core ADD dedup matches a
   local dep against a canonical entry on **`(opaque_vendor_type, remote_key)`** — the
   direction-agnostic pair equal to today's `(type_name, other_key)` — NOT on `(relation,
   remote_key)`. `link_payload_for_relation(relation)` yields the local dep's `(vendor_type,
   swap)`, and the dedup compares that `vendor_type` + target key against the canonical
   entries' `(opaque_vendor_type, remote_key)`. The `relation` field of a canonical entry
   drives ONLY the direction-SPECIFIC REMOVE managed-gate matching (mirroring today's
   `resolve_inbound_link`-based REMOVE). `map_remote_links` still applies today's
   direction-agnostic dedup internally (it may return one canonical entry per
   `(vendor_type, remote_key)`).

**Added acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The ADD dedup is direction-agnostic: a local dep to K dedups against a remote link of the
      mapped vendor type between the local issue and K whether K is the inward or the outward
      side — verified by a held-out test (inward remote link vs outward local dep -> no ADD),
      matching today's behavior byte-for-byte.
- [ ] `outbound_differ.py` passes the `SupportsLinks` capability into `_diff_links`; the AST
      neutrality gate still passes for `outbound_differ.py` (the capability is the injected
      backend, not an `adapters.jira` import).

## Landed

Implemented and merged to `main` as Gerrit change 935 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).

## Context / Problem
T11's POST-ROLLBACK SCHEMA STATE paragraph is a stock-finding generator: 8 of 21 sampled findings were near-identical "plan does not assert post-rollback state" advisories that are tautologies against an append-only store (median priority ~0.1), drowning its rare real catches (e.g. the 114f fold-in overwrite data-loss bug). The operator approved a constraint and rejected a per-plan cap; the constraint must be portable across stacks (no store technology named).

## Approach
Replace the post-rollback paragraph in src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T11.md with a four-condition applicability rule: raise post-rollback-state findings ONLY when the plan (a) changes how existing persisted records are interpreted, (b) rewrites or migrates records in place, (c) removes or narrows a read path, or (d) performs a one-way transformation with no back-out. Add the explicit anti-false-positive line: purely additive, backward-compatible persistence changes that existing readers ignore (new record/event types, optional fields, new tables or columns with defaults) do not qualify — residual data after rollback is the norm in append-only and backward-compatible systems, not a risk. No store technology is named in the applicability rule itself, so it applies equally to SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats. Posture stays advisory. Alternative rejected: a one-finding-per-plan cap — operator rejected it; the applicability rule removes the tautology class at the source instead.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T11.md, tests/unit/test_plan_review_t11_rubric.py (new, beside the other plan-review rubric contract tests in tests/unit/), docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md (regenerated).

## Testing
Rubric text assertions in tests/unit/test_plan_review_t11_rubric.py: the four conditions and the anti-FP line are present; the old unconditional post-rollback wording is gone; the applicability rule names no store technology (the illustrative anti-FP examples are exempt from that assertion).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The rubric raises post-rollback findings only under the four named conditions (checked: `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_t11_rubric.py` asserting the conditions and absence of the old wording).
- [ ] The anti-FP line for additive backward-compatible changes is present (checked: same test file).
- [ ] The criteria guide is regenerated (checked: committed regen output).
baseline.summary: Portable persistence-safety constraint for the T11 migration rubric

## Context / Problem

ADR 0035 §(d) ("Adding a second backend") was only a prose sketch, so the concrete backend
interface for Phase 2 (epic `bbf1-82e1-cf9d-494a`) was unspecified. That blocks decomposition
and plan-review of the implementation stories (S2–S5), which must cite concrete Protocol
names. This story lands the §(d) revision that pins the interface.

Edit-set (docs only): `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`.

## Approach

Rewrite §(d) to pin four decisions, each grounded in the current coupling:

- **rebar's local ticket is the canonical model** — no separate `CanonicalTicket`. The seam
  speaks local-field vocabulary; adapters translate vendor⇄local via the mappers that already
  exist (`outbound_fields.py`, `inbound_fields.py`/`inbound_translate.py`). No parallel schema
  kept in lock-step, no redundant `rebar⇄canonical` hop.
- **Core owns diff/apply; adapters only read + enact.**
- **Role Protocols behind one `Backend` facade** — `TicketTransport`, `OutboundMapper`,
  `InboundMapper`, `FieldSanitizer`, `IdentityConvention`, plus opt-in capability Protocols
  (`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`).
- **One new type `RemoteRef{vendor, instance, remote_id}`** (identity tuple), replacing the
  hardcoded `"jira"` literal in `apply_inbound_records.py` and the bare `jira_key`.

Also update the Status line, Decision points 5–6, and Consequences to reference the pinned
design and scope the first real second backend to epic `be74-7832-03a8-48ac`.

## Scope

- Revised §(d): the role-Protocol table, the `Backend` facade, `RemoteRef`, the registry
  keyed on `config.reconciler.backend`, the three leak-fixes, and the proof-of-seam
  (contract suite + test-only `FakeBackend`; the real GitHub adapter deferred to epic
  `be74`).
- Status/Decision/Consequences edits for consistency.
- No code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §(d) names all five role Protocols, the `Backend` facade, `RemoteRef`, and the registry
  keyed on `config.reconciler.backend` — verified by reading the rendered section.
- [ ] The ADR states the canonical model is rebar's own ticket (no separate model) and lists
  the three leak-fixes (ADF-sizing out of the differ, lossy-status/parent rules into the Jira
  adapter, duplicated value-maps/link-constants single-sourced) — verified by `grep` for those
  terms in the file.
- [ ] The Status line references epic `bbf1`; the proof-of-seam scopes the first real second
  backend to epic `be74` — verified by reading.
- [ ] `make lint` passes on the branch (docs-only change introduces no lint error).

content.text: ## Summary

clarity_check returns a schema-violating {"output",...} dict on a missing ticket; sibling gates degrade with proper shapes; over MCP it surfaces as a pydantic ValidationError instead of a clean error.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar.clarity_check("deadbeefdeadbeef") -> {"output": "ERROR: failed to retrieve ticket ...", "passed": false}
2. rebar.check_ac("deadbeefdeadbeef") -> {"verdict":"fail","criteria_count":0,"reason":"could not load ...","passed":false}
3. Over MCP: call_tool("clarity_check", ...) -> ToolError: 3 validation errors for ClarityResultOut (score/verdict/threshold missing).
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: one consistent missing-ticket contract across all three gates and across library/MCP (either RebarError like show_ticket, or a schema-conforming fail result).
- Actual: clarity_check alone violates clarity_result.schema.json and explodes the MCP output model.
## Source
- src/rebar/__init__.py:178-183 — fallback dict shape {"output", "passed"}.
- src/rebar/mcp_server.py:211-214 — ClarityResultOut rejects it.
## Fix direction

On engine exit 2 raise RebarError (consistent with show_ticket), or return {"score":0,"verdict":"fail","threshold":N} — pick ONE contract and apply to all three gates. See validation notes comment for the recommended option.
## Suggested RED test
All three gates on a nonexistent id, via library AND MCP; assert the single chosen contract.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] clarity_check missing-ticket result validates against clarity_result.schema.json OR raises RebarError — consistent with check_ac/quality_check after the change
- [ ] MCP clarity_check on missing id returns a clean ToolError or valid payload (no pydantic stack)
- [ ] RED test first; parity asserted across library + MCP

content.text: # Code-review data capture: a change-scoped `code_review` artifact type + reviewbot emit
## Why
Code review persists NOTHING to the shared store today: the reviewbot only writes ephemeral
`/tmp` gate snapshots — no `origin` remote, no push credential. So there is no durable record and
no corpus to calibrate the new impact model (`impact_code`, sibling `albite-lazy-barb`) from. We
want every review to leave a durable, searchable, ticket-linked artifact on the shared `tickets`
branch.
## Why a new ticket TYPE (not a sidecar-only record)
The artifact must be (a) SEARCHABLE by keyword and (b) LINKABLE (`relates_to`) to the work tickets
its change cites — in the SAME store, so a corpus query can join reviews to tickets. A per-ticket
sidecar event cannot stand alone as a change-scoped record (a diff has no ticket), and a separate
store would not be searchable/linkable alongside work. So we mirror `session_log`: a first-class
ticket type that is out of the dependency graph, gate/lifecycle-exempt, excluded from Jira sync,
and hidden from default `list` but searchable — exactly the properties a bulk artifact needs.
## What
Emit a change-scoped `code_review` artifact ticket keyed by `(gerrit change-id, revision)`,
carrying the code-review verdict (impact + tier-tagged sub-answers) as a sidecar on the artifact,
plus a diff-scoped `change_fingerprint` join key and per-finding `norm_id`s; and `relates_to`-link
it to EVERY rebar ticket cited by the change's commit `rebar-ticket:` trailers (many-to-one).
### A. The `code_review` ticket type (mirror `session_log` at EVERY guard site)
Add `code_review` to the type system and replicate `session_log`'s exemptions. Concrete sites
(verified present in the tree):
- Enum/source-of-truth: `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json` (`ticket_type` enum), then
regenerate `src/rebar/types.py` via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` (do NOT hand-edit).
- Runtime validation: `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` `_TYPES` tuple (+ the hardcoded
"Must be one of" error strings and `_USAGE`); add to `_FILE_IMPACT_EXEMPT_TYPES`.
- Store/graph exclusion: broaden the single reducer predicate at `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`
(`exclude_session_logs` KEEPS its name for back-compat; its predicate becomes `ticket_type not
in _NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, a new shared module constant). Callers that pass the flag INHERIT
the broadened exclusion with NO edit: `graph/_graph.py`, `graph/_blockers.py`,
`graph/_unblock.py` (never an open-child blocker), `graph/_ready.py`,
`_engine_support/next_batch.py`. `graph/_hierarchy.py` is edited EXPLICITLY (NOT via the flag):
its `_TYPE_TIER` gains `code_review: 0` and its blocking-link refusal reads the constant
directly.
- Gate exemption: `_engine_support/gates.py` (check-ac / clarity / quality → gate-exempt pass);
plan-review exemption axis `llm/plan_review/{orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py,__init__.py,
orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py}` (the `("bug","session_log")` short-circuit → add `code_review`);
and the plan-review CLAIM gate short-circuit in `_commands/gates.py`. (`__init__.py` / `det_floor.py` /
`registry.py` are NOT edited — they carry no such type short-circuit.)
close gate `_commands/transition_close.py` (skip the billable verifier); the lifecycle
guards in `_commands/transition.py` + `_commands/txn.py` (transition AND claim refusal) and the
plan-review claim-gate exemption in `_commands/gates.py`.
- Jira exclusion: add `code_review` to `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES` in
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`; leave the two local→Jira type maps —
`_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (`outbound_fields.py`) and `_TYPE_LOCAL_TO_JIRA` (`reconcile_check.py`) —
untouched so any leak surfaces.
- Export: broaden the hardcoded `session_log` guard in `_io/export_ndjson.py` so default NDJSON
exports exclude `code_review` too (opt in via `include_session_logs`).
- Visibility: `_engine_support/reads.py` — hidden from default `list`, present in `search`/`show`
(generalize the `exclude_session_logs=(ticket_type != …)` predicate).
- Lifecycle: like `session_log`, the artifact is NOT claimed/transitioned (the emit path CREATEs
it directly; it is never dispatched).
### B. Join keys (what is reused vs what is genuinely new)
- `norm_id` IS reused verbatim: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:210` `norm_id(finding)`
takes a finding dict (`finding`, `criteria`) — code-review findings share that shape, so
per-finding identity reuses it with NO new algorithm.
- `material_fingerprint` is NOT reusable: `plan_review/pass1.py:551` `material_fingerprint(ctx:
PlanContext)` is ticket-scoped (ticket_id/description/file_impact/children) and a diff has no
PlanContext. So we add ONE small NEW diff-scoped analogue `change_fingerprint(change_id,
revision, changed_files, diff_text)` in the code-review sidecar module — same construction as
`material_fingerprint` (sha256 over a sorted-key JSON basis, 16-hex prefix), applied to the
change instead of a ticket. This is the honest correction to the earlier "no new algorithm"
claim: finding identity reuses `norm_id`; the change-scoped key is a small documented new
function mirroring the existing one.
### C. Reviewbot emit + trailer linking (`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`)
In `review_and_vote`, AFTER the successful `store.record_vote` (voter.py ~496), where
`decision`, `commit_message`, `change_id`, `revision` are in scope:
0. COMPUTE `change_fingerprint(change_id, revision, changed_from_diff(diff_text), diff_text)` from
the reviewed diff (the voter binds `diff_text` in the review block; it is "" on a review-error).
1. CREATE the `code_review` artifact ticket (`rebar.create_ticket("code_review", <title keyed by
change-id+revision>, …)`); title carries the change-id + revision.
2. Emit the verdict sidecar onto the artifact by calling `code_review.sidecar.emit(...)` DIRECTLY. This
requires EXTENDING the existing `code_review/sidecar.py` `emit(verdict, *, target_ticket,
repo_root=None)` and `build_payload(verdict, *, target_ticket)` signatures with THREE NEW
keyword params — `change_id=""`, `revision=""`, `change_fp=""` (all defaulting empty so existing
callers, e.g. the gate's `target_ticket` emit, are unaffected). `build_payload` is also extended
to stamp per-finding `norm_id` (reused from plan-review) onto its blocking/advisory lists. The
FULL verdict is threaded up from `adapter.code_review_decision` (a NEW `verdict` key ADDED to
its return dict), so the voter does NOT re-invoke `produce_code_review_verdict`.
3. TRAILER RESOLUTION: `verify_commit.extract_ticket_refs(commit_message)` over the change's commit message (voter.py's `commit_message`, the
fetched commit body; for a merge patchset that is the merge commit's message — merge-parent
trailer union is best-effort, out of scope here). For each ref, resolve via the store:
- RESOLVABLE (a ticket with that alias/full/short id exists) → `rebar.link(artifact, ticket,
"relates_to")`.
- UNRESOLVED (well-formed ref, no such ticket) or FOREIGN (a Jira-key-shaped ref absent from
the store) → log, non-fatal, continue.
A decision that carries NO `verdict` key (e.g. the merge coverage-gap path via
`_merge_coverage_gap_decision`, or a fail-closed review-error) emits NO artifact — the voter reads
`decision.get("verdict")` and returns early when it is absent/empty. All emit/link/push failures
are caught and logged; they NEVER fail the review vote (the vote is already cast). Idempotency: the artifact is keyed by `(change-id, revision)` — a re-review of
the SAME revision reuses/updates the same artifact (look up by the change-key title before
creating) so retries do not duplicate.
- LOG FORMAT (measurable): a single WARNING-level line per unresolved/foreign ref via the
reviewbot logger — `logger.warning("code_review artifact %s: unresolved rebar-ticket trailer
%r (change %s/%s)", artifact_id, ref, change_id, revision)` — and one INFO summary line
`logger.info("code_review artifact %s: linked %d/%d trailer refs", artifact_id, linked, total)`.
### D. Infra (config in-repo; the on-box push is a DEPLOY-STEP canary, un-verifiable in-session)
- SSM slot: add the leaf `reviewbot-tickets-pat` to `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`'s `rebar_secret_params`
(a SecureString the operator populates with the RebarBotNava contents:write PAT — a DEPLOY
prerequisite).
- Materialization: add the `reviewbot-tickets-pat → REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` leaf→env mapping to
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (writes `infra/compose/.env`, 0600).
- Container: `infra/compose/{docker-compose.yml,Dockerfile.reviewbot}` — set
`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` AND `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` (so rebar's
ambient `config.tracker_dir` — read by the reviewbot's `repo_root=None` create/link/emit calls —
resolves to the persistent worktree, NOT the container `/app` cwd); on startup materialize that
PERSISTENT tickets worktree once (clone of the `tickets` branch onto the mounted volume) and
configure a URL-SCOPED (origin only, NOT global) git credential
helper that echoes `username=x-access-token` / `password=$REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` so the token
never lands on disk or in a remote URL. Concurrency: voter.py holds a per-(change_id, revision) `asyncio.Lock`, so two reviews of the SAME
revision cannot race the idempotent lookup-then-create; DIFFERENT changes write DISTINCT artifact
tickets (distinct event files) into the append-only, auto-committing store, so they need no extra
lock either.
- The actual on-box PAT push is a DEPLOY-STEP CANARY (requires SSM + the live container) and is
therefore NOT verifiable in this session; the completion-verifier judges the IMPLEMENTATION
(the artifact-build + trailer-resolution code + the infra config), not the live push.
## Scope / files
- Lifecycle/export guards: `src/rebar/_commands/{transition.py,txn.py,transition_close.py,gates.py}`,
`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py` (mirror the session_log guards).
- Type: `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py` (regen),
`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`, `src/rebar/graph/*.py`,
`src/rebar/_engine_support/{gates.py,next_batch.py,reads.py}`,
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/{orchestrator.py,workflow_ops.py,__init__.py,det_floor.py,registry.py}`,
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`.
- Emit + keys: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (`change_fingerprint`, augment payload),
`src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` (thread the full `verdict` up on `code_review_decision`'s
return), `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py` (create artifact + trailer-link).
- Infra: `infra/compose/{docker-compose.yml,Dockerfile.reviewbot}`,
`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`, `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `code_review` is a valid ticket type (in `common.schema.json` + regenerated `types.py` +
`composer._TYPES`) and is mirror-exempt like `session_log` at every guard site: excluded from
the reducer/dependency-graph/`ready`/`next_batch`, gate-exempt (check-ac/clarity/quality +
plan-review + close), excluded from Jira sync (`EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`, both Jira maps
untouched), and hidden from default `list` but returned by `search`. Proving command:
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] `change_fingerprint(change_id, revision, changed_files, diff_text)` exists in the code-review
sidecar module and returns a stable 16-hex fingerprint (same construction as
`material_fingerprint`); per-finding identity reuses `plan_review.sidecar.norm_id` verbatim.
Unit-tested (stability + sensitivity to each input). Proving command:
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] The reviewbot emit path builds a `code_review` artifact payload for a review verdict and
resolves `rebar-ticket:` trailers into `relates_to` links: RESOLVABLE refs are linked;
UNRESOLVED/FOREIGN refs are logged at WARNING (with the specified format) and are NON-FATAL;
the artifact is idempotent per `(change-id, revision)`. Unit-tested with a fake store
(resolvable ref → link; unresolved ref → logged, not raised). Proving command:
`.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py -v`.
- [ ] Infra config lands in-repo: `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` + a persistent tickets-worktree volume
in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, a PER-URL (not global) git credential helper +
one-time tickets-worktree materialization in `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`, the
`reviewbot-tickets-pat → REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` mapping in `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh`,
and the `/rebar/prod/reviewbot-tickets-pat` SSM slot in `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`. Proving
command (presence of all four in-repo edits): `grep -q 'REBAR_SYNC_PUSH' infra/compose/docker-compose.yml
&& grep -q 'REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT' infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh && grep -q 'reviewbot-tickets-pat'
infra/terraform/ssm.tf && grep -qE 'credential\.[^ ]+\.helper|x-access-token' infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`. The live
on-box PAT push is a DEPLOY-STEP canary (needs SSM + a running container) and is explicitly
OUT of in-session verification — the completion-verifier judges the IMPLEMENTATION, not the push.
- [ ] No retention cap / prune path is added for the `code_review` artifact set (deliberate — it
IS the calibration corpus). Observable: no code prunes/caps `code_review` tickets. Proving
command: `! grep -rniE 'prune|retention|cap|evict' src/rebar/ --include='*.py' | grep -i code_review`
(no prune/retention/cap logic mentions code_review anywhere under src/rebar).
## Implementation precision (grounds the acceptance criteria)
- `reads.py` list-visibility uses EXACTLY `exclude_session_logs=(ticket_type not in
_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES)` (the shared `("session_log","code_review")` set) so default `list`
hides BOTH artifact types while `list --type=code_review` shows them; the downstream
`apply_ticket_filters(type_filter=...)` narrows to the exact type.
- The `reducer/_api.py` `exclude_session_logs` boolean KEEPS its name (back-compat — NO caller
migration) but its predicate broadens to `ticket_type not in _NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES`, so every
existing `exclude_session_logs=True` caller (ready/next_batch/deps/validate/list) transparently
excludes `code_review` too. The new set is a single module constant.
- Idempotency lookup uses `rebar.list_tickets(ticket_type="code_review")` and matches on the
`title` field == `f"code-review: {change_id} @ {revision}"`; on any lookup failure the fallback
is to CREATE a fresh artifact (accepting a rare duplicate over dropping the record).
- The git credential helper is URL-SCOPED via the `credential.<tickets-url>.helper` config key
(set by the Dockerfile entrypoint before the worktree clone), echoing `username=x-access-token` /
`password=$REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_PAT` so the token never lands on disk or in a remote URL. rebar
resolves its store via `config.tracker_dir` — which reads `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` (canonical env) —
so the compose `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` points the ambient store at
the persistent worktree (the emit runs OUTSIDE the temp code-clone `with` block, so it MUST NOT
use that deleted tmpdir — it passes `repo_root=None` and relies on this env). Both the helper
wiring and store resolution are exercised only by the DEPLOY-STEP canary (un-verifiable in-session).

baseline.summary: Code-review data capture to the rebar ticket store (change-scoped, PAT-credentialed)

content.text: ## Why
Today a plan-review criterion is inert unless it is in the hardcoded `CANONICAL_LLM` frozenset
(`plan_review/registry.py:70`) AND the packaged `criteria_routing.json`; `_routing_index()` /
`load_criteria()` are `@lru_cache`d with no `repo_root` key. So a project cannot add a criterion at
all. This story opens the vocabulary and adds the project overlay — the **dependency root + MVP
slice** for the whole epic (`3156`). It is NOT blocked on `b744` (extends plan-review directly).
## What
- `effective_criteria(repo_root)` = `CANONICAL_LLM` ∪ activated project ids; route it through
**every** plan-review vocabulary site: `load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the
workflow Pass-1 batch vocab in `workflow_ops` (`plan_review_assemble_criteria`). The
`include_<id>` output key must sanitize the `project.<name>` id (`.`→`_`) at BOTH the assemble
and consume sites (keep the rule co-located).
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay: gate-keyed (`{plan_review: {...}, activate: [...]}`),
reusing the packaged routing schema; `project.<name>` namespace; an un-prefixed built-in id =
re-tune/disable; a `project.`-id colliding with a built-in, or a duplicate, is **rejected at
load** (located error). A criterion runs only if in `activate`.
- Cache isolation: keep `_routing_index()` cached for the packaged index; add
`effective_routing(repo_root)` (uncached, or keyed by `(repo_root, overlay mtime)` — note mtime
granularity, prefer content hash if flaky); extend `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()`.
- Routing validation: load-time (invalid routing = located error, not silent skip) + a CI
drift/parity gate mirroring `reviewers/index.json`.
## Scope
- Files: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py`,
`src/rebar/llm/prompt_library.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` (schema doc).
- MVP end-to-end: activate ONE project LLM criterion from the overlay → it runs in plan-review
Pass-1 → surfaces a finding. (Attestation invalidation is story `#4`; unify is story `#6`.)
- Out: code-review side (story `#6`, b744-blocked); DET consumer (story `#2`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `effective_criteria(repo_root)` loads activated project criteria and is routed through
`load_criteria`, `check_registry_coverage`, and the workflow Pass-1 batch vocab; an activated
project LLM criterion fans out and runs in plan-review Pass-1.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay per schema: gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace,
explicit `activate` list, load-time collision/rebind rejection (located error).
- [ ] `include_<id>` key sanitization (`.`→`_`) applied at both assemble + consume sites.
- [ ] Overlay merge is cache-isolated per repo (packaged index stays cached; overlay is not);
a RED test proves no cross-repo routing leakage in the long-lived MCP server.
- [ ] Routing validation: invalid overlay routing is a located error + a CI drift/parity gate.
- [ ] An ADR documents the unified-registry + overlay merge/activation contract.
- [ ] MVP slice demonstrated end-to-end (activate one criterion → runs → surfaces a finding).
## Backward-compatibility, fan-out mechanism & cache strategy (remediation, run 1)
### Expand-contract / backward-compatibility (clears T4)
Every signature change is **additive** with a `repo_root=None` default that preserves
today's behaviour, so no existing caller breaks:
- `registry.load_criteria(repo_root=None)`, `registry.by_id(repo_root=None)`,
`registry.check_registry_coverage(repo_root=None)`, `registry._descriptor_from_prompt(cid,
*, repo_root=None, routing_index=None)`, and the NEW `effective_criteria(repo_root=None)` /
`effective_routing(repo_root=None)` all default `repo_root=None`.
- `repo_root=None` resolves to `config.repo_root()` (the same root `get_prompt` already
resolves `.rebar/prompts/` overrides against) — so an **overlay-absent** repo yields
**exactly** today's packaged-only vocabulary/routing (no behaviour change, no churn).
- **Call sites updated** (enumerated): `orchestrator.route_criteria` (passes the ctx
repo_root), `workflow_ops.plan_review_assemble_criteria` (uses `ctx.repo_root`),
`attest.registry_version`/`plan_review.__init__` coverage (story #4 threads repo_root;
this story keeps the no-arg default working), and the tests. Bare `load_criteria()` /
`check_registry_coverage()` keep working unchanged.
- **Rollback:** delete `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (overlay-absent ⇒ packaged behaviour),
or revert the additive params (all default `None`).
### Dynamic Pass-1 fan-out mechanism (clears G6/T1/T3 — schema-safe, NO v3 change)
The v3 `batch` step schema (`workflow.v3.schema.json`) is IMMUTABLE + version-pinned with
`additionalProperties:false` on `$defs/batch`, and the gate validates its OWN document at run
time — so a new `batch` field (e.g. `extra_criteria`) is impossible without a v4 schema+shim
(out of MVP scope). Instead, project criteria fan out through the **rebar-specific
`ProductionBatchRunner`** (`production_batch_runner.py`), NOT a new doc field:
- built-in criteria keep fanning out via the STATIC `criteria:` list in `gates/plan-review.yaml`
(each gated by its `include_<ID>` key — byte-identical to today);
- the runner, after `assemble_context`, calls `route_criteria(ctx)` (which now returns the FULL
effective set) and appends ONLY the `project.<name>`-prefixed descriptors — already past the
SAME `applies()`/overlay filter the built-ins use — to the finder's tier-split set, deduped
against the built-ins. `assemble` still emits sanitized `include_project_<name>` booleans
(`.`→`_`) as the coverage/routing record. `gates/plan-review.yaml` and the immutable schema
are UNTOUCHED. (Probe-mode caveat: route_criteria has no probe notion, so a project criterion
is also evaluated during a drift probe — harmless, documented follow-up.)
### Cache strategy — content-hash, not mtime (clears E2/G6/T8/T9)
`effective_routing`/`load_criteria` are memoized in repo-keyed module dicts keyed by
`(repo_root, sha256(overlay-bytes))` — a **content signature**, NOT mtime (mtime
granularity is coarse/flaky), so editing the overlay auto-invalidates the memo. The
packaged `_routing_index()` stays `@lru_cache`d (immutable per binary). Stale-entry
growth is bounded: `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears both memos + the lru_caches
(the RED cross-repo-leak test proves repo A's routing never serves repo B).
### Sanitization inverse & missing-prompt fallback (clears T8)
The `.`→`_` map is one-directional at the workflow-key layer only; the criterion id and
prompt id retain the dotted form, so no inverse un-sanitization is needed (the
`project_criteria` entry carries the real dotted `prompt` id directly). An activated
project id whose prompt file is absent/malformed surfaces as a **located `RegistryError`**
from `load_criteria` (same as a missing built-in prompt) — fail-loud at load, never a
silent skip.
### ADR contents (clears E1/AC6)
`docs/adr/0015-project-supplied-criteria.md` documents: the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
overlay schema (gate-keyed, `project.<name>` namespace, `activate` list); the merge +
collision/rebind rules; `effective_criteria`/`effective_routing` as the vocabulary seam;
the content-hash cache-isolation contract; and the runner-side (schema-free) project fan-out.
### Scope clarification (clears E5/T8/G5)

Files also touched: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py` (project fan-in) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` (`route_criteria` threads repo_root). MVP end-to-end exercises ONE activated project **LLM** criterion (`exec: 1-TURN`). Project
`exec: DET` criteria (the prompt-less descriptor branch) are story #2; the shared
`rebar.llm.criteria` unification is story #6. The CI drift/parity gate here is a
**validation** gate (the packaged `criteria_routing.json` stays schema-valid and in parity
with `CANONICAL_LLM` + the prompt files), not a generator, since the routing is
hand-authored judgement (thresholds/applies_at) with no derivation source.
## Acceptance Criteria (remediation additions)
- [ ] All new/changed registry signatures are additive with a `repo_root=None` default that
preserves packaged-only behaviour (overlay-absent repo == today); rollback = delete the
overlay.
- [ ] The dynamic Pass-1 fan-out for a project criterion is runner-side (`ProductionBatchRunner`
appends the `project.` subset of `route_criteria`), leaving the immutable v3 `batch` schema
and `gates/plan-review.yaml` UNCHANGED.
- [ ] An activated project criterion with a missing/malformed prompt file raises a LOCATED
`RegistryError` from `load_criteria` (fail-loud, no silent skip); a test asserts it.
- [ ] Overlay mis-authoring is covered by named tests: collision/rebind rejection, un-namespaced
net-new id, activated-without-routing, invalid routing schema, malformed JSON — each a
located `RegistryError`.
- [ ] `prompt_library._invalidate_caches()` clears the new overlay-merged caches (proven: an
overlay edit is picked up for the same repo_root without a process restart).

baseline.summary: Criteria registry: open the vocabulary + .rebar/ routing overlay + activation + cache isolation (plan-review MVP root)

content.text: ## Summary
rebar.__version__ reports 0.3.0 while the installed package metadata is 0.4.0.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD)
1. python -c "import rebar, importlib.metadata as m; print(rebar.__version__, m.version('nava-rebar'))"
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: module attr matches package version.
- Actual: src/rebar/__init__.py:22 hardcodes 0.3.0; pyproject.toml:10 is 0.4.0 (Release 0.4.0 commit 2a06570 did not bump the attr).
## Fix direction
Derive __version__ from importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar") with a dev-checkout fallback; add a release-check test asserting module attr == package metadata so this cannot recur.
## Suggested RED test
test asserting rebar.__version__ == importlib.metadata.version("nava-rebar") — RED today, GREEN after.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] __version__ derived from package metadata (single source of truth: pyproject)
- [ ] Guard test prevents recurrence
- [ ] Works in editable installs (pip install -e) without crashing

# Flaky: test_import_batch_resume._commit_count crashes on empty `git rev-list` output

## Context (discovered during CI for bug 7c91-0488)
On gerrit-verify run 29620766631 (ubuntu py3.12 only; py3.11/py3.13/macos all passed), the
integration tier failed:

    FAILED tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py::test_benchmark_commit_count_is_ceil_per_pass
    E   ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''   (test_import_batch_resume.py:51)

## Root cause (suspected — not yet proven)
`_commit_count` (tests/interfaces/io/test_import_batch_resume.py:45-51) runs
`git rev-list --count HEAD` via subprocess.run WITHOUT check=True and WITHOUT guarding empty
stdout, then `int(r.stdout.strip())`. In the concurrency/integration tier a timing race (tracker
HEAD not yet present / transient git error) yields empty stdout -> int('') -> ValueError. Single-
cell matrix failure = flake signature.

## Suggested fix
Assert the subprocess return code and non-empty stdout (or retry) before int(); fail with the
git stderr rather than an opaque int('') ValueError. Out of scope for the terraform-drift fix.

## Acceptance criteria
- _commit_count no longer raises int('') on empty/failed `git rev-list`; it either retries to a
  ready HEAD or fails with a clear diagnostic including git's stderr.
- The test passes deterministically across the py3.11/3.12/3.13 matrix.
baseline.summary: Flaky: test_import_batch_resume._commit_count int('') on empty git rev-list output

content.text: `rebar show`/`get-file-impact` (jq reducer in ticket-lib-api.sh) and
`list`/`search`/native (Python ticket_reducer) are two hand-written reducers that
have drifted. Confirmed by code + experiment. Resolve by making the Python reducer
the SINGLE source of truth.
## Reviewed plan (3 opus reviews: accuracy+prototype, maintainability, performance)
Performance reversal: the jq reducer is the SLOW path (O(events × jq fork); ~910ms
@121 events). Python reduce_ticket is ~31-35ms flat. So we DROP the bash cache
fast-path (saves only ~12ms, adds a drift hazard) and adopt the simpler fallback:
delete jq, route show/get-file-impact through reduce_ticket (which already has its
own .cache.json fast-path). Faster than today on every input; no degradation.
Confirmed: a VERIFY_COMMANDS processor mirroring jq's last-write-wins semantics is
correct AND fixes a latent bug (verify_commands is silently dropped on compaction
today). Drift inventory was incomplete: the jq->python swap also surfaces internal
keys jq never emitted — `parent_status_uuid`, `last_status_env_id`, and
`preconditions_summary.source_count` — so an interface-boundary presentation filter
must strip them uniformly across show/list/search/llm (to_llm leaks them too).
Deleting jq breaks tests/scripts/test_ticket_reducer_schema_parity.py (asserts >=2
jq programs) — must be retired and replaced by a golden full-key parity test.
## Ordered child tasks (T1-T5)
- T1 VERIFY_COMMANDS processor in ticket_reducer (+ make_initial_state/make_error_dict) + unit test; fixes compaction drop.
- T2 Interface presentation filter: strip internal keys (parent_status_uuid, last_status_env_id, preconditions_summary.source_count) from show/list/search/llm; fix to_llm.

- T3 Delete both jq reducer copies (ticket-lib-api.sh:340,1409) + the separate jq preconditions scan; route show + get-file-impact through reduce_ticket; preserve not-found envelope, stderr bridge-alert warning, exit codes, --format=llm, multi-id, []-on-miss.
- T4 Golden cross-reducer parity test (full key-set + value equality across show/list/search/native + llm over all event types); retire test_ticket_reducer_schema_parity.py.
- T5 Update ticket_state.schema.json (verify_commands optional; internal keys excluded); optional follow-ons: writes refresh cache; library/MCP call reduce_ticket in-process.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] show, list, search, native reduce_ticket (and --format=llm) return identical, internal-marker-free top-level shapes for the same ticket (incl. verify_commands when set)
- [ ] verify_commands survives compaction (SNAPSHOT carries it)
- [ ] jq reducer fully removed; single Python reducer is the only state producer
- [ ] golden full-key parity test guards against future drift; old jq-asserting test retired
- [ ] no performance degradation (reduce_ticket path is faster than the old jq path)
- [ ] schema updated; no regression in existing reducer/show/list/get-file-impact tests

baseline.summary: show vs list/search return divergent ticket-state shapes (two reducers drifted: verify_commands vs parent_status_uuid)

## What

Add a lightweight CI gate that keeps the docs index honest: every living top-level
`docs/*.md` page must be linked from the central index (`docs/README.md`), with an
explicit allowlist for intentionally-unindexed files (git-ignored `*.local.md`,
historical/archive docs). This drift-proofs the P2 index-completeness finding so it
cannot silently recur. It ALSO validates that relative markdown links within `docs/`
resolve — any relative markdown link within `docs/` that points at a nonexistent
`docs/…` target fails the gate, so a broken relative link cannot slip past the
index-only completeness check. (Sibling `9d81` keeps historical docs in place rather
than moving them, so there are no archive relocations to chase; this general
relative-link check is the durable guard regardless.)

Template the established pattern: `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` + its CI drift gate
show the shape (a small script invoked from `.github/workflows/test.yml` that fails on
divergence).

- Add `scripts/check_docs_index.py` (new): (a) enumerate `docs/*.md`, parse links out
  of `docs/README.md`, diff against an allowlist, exit non-zero on unindexed living
  docs; (b) scan ALL `docs/*.md` for relative markdown links to `docs/…` targets and
  exit non-zero on any that do not resolve to an existing file (general broken-relative-
  link guard within docs/).
- Wire it into BOTH `.github/workflows/test.yml` AND `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`
  (the latter is the actual Gerrit `Verified` gate; it mirrors test.yml's drift gates).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A new script fails when a living top-level `docs/*.md` is not linked from
      `docs/README.md` and not on the allowlist.
- [ ] The allowlist covers `*.local.md` and designated historical/archive docs.
- [ ] The check is wired into CI and passes on the (now-completed) index.
- [ ] Adding a new unindexed doc is caught — DETERMINISTIC proof (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `touch docs/_gate_probe.md; python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "MISS" || echo "CAUGHT"; rm -f docs/_gate_probe.md`
      (a fresh unindexed, non-allowlisted `docs/*.md` makes `--check` exit non-zero).
- [ ] A relative link in any `docs/*.md` pointing at a nonexistent `docs/…` target
      fails the gate — DETERMINISTIC proof (prints `CAUGHT`):
      `printf '[x](./_nope_$$.md)\n' >> docs/README.md; python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo MISS || echo CAUGHT; git checkout -- docs/README.md`

Files: `scripts/check_docs_index.py` (new), `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
baseline.summary: P1: Add docs index-completeness / dead-link CI gate

baseline.description:
## What
Add agent-facing documentation to stop a recurring confusion: agents scoping "batch writes to the local ticket store" wander into the Jira reconciler (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`) and mistake its internals for the local store write API.

## Why
The reconciler is a CLIENT of the same git-backed store — it shares the low-level lock (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, invariant I5) and the canonical-bytes contract — so a grep for "batch"/"commit" lands there. Two specific false friends: `applier._apply_batch` is an OUTBOUND Jira REST sequencer (not a local commit-batcher), and inbound events are written by `inbound_translate._write_event_file` (one file per call under the lock, via `os.replace`, with no `git add`/`commit` — it does NOT go through `stage_and_commit`). The stale epic cold-stall-chalk compounded this with its "WS-B3: batch-apply" wording. This has already misled at least one agent. Fix lands where an agent greps (module docstrings) plus one authoritative section.

## Scope
- Add a "Two writers, one store" section to `docs/architecture.md` (inserted immediately before the "### Python package layout & the engine import boundary" subsection) distinguishing the local store write path (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`; citing — not editing — the inline cores in `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`) from the Jira reconciler (a CLIENT of the store), stating what they share, clearing up the two false friends above, and listing the overloaded vocabulary.
- Add docstring signposts pointing to that section in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`, `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`, and `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`.
- No code behavior changes (docs + docstrings only).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` has a "Two writers, one store" section naming the two writers (the local `rebar._store` write path vs. the Jira reconciler as a client of the store).
- [ ] The section states the two writers share ONLY `rebar._store.lock` + the canonical-bytes contract, with no shared write API.
- [ ] The section clears up `applier._apply_batch` as an OUTBOUND Jira REST sequencer, not a local commit-batcher.
- [ ] The section clears up `inbound_translate._write_event_file` as writing one event file per call with no `git add`/`commit` (not via `stage_and_commit`).
- [ ] The section lists the overloaded vocabulary: reconcile / apply / batch / sync.
- [ ] A docstring cross-ref to the section is added in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`.
- [ ] A docstring cross-ref to the section is added in `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`.
- [ ] A docstring cross-ref to the section is added in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py`.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.

## Notes
- The `__main__.py` signpost from the original plan was intentionally dropped: the only `commit_tree`/`update_ref` there is the legacy-lock-file purge, not an event-file batch commit — anchoring a batch-write note there would misattribute.
- The `applier.py` docstring signpost was intentionally DESCOPED: applier.py was at exactly the 800-LOC soft cap, and adding lines tripped the module-size CI gate. The information is not lost — `docs/architecture.md` 'Two writers, one store' explicitly names `applier._apply_batch` as the outbound-Jira false friend.
- The stale `cold-stall-chalk` WS-B3 "batch-apply" wording is being corrected concurrently by the epic-decomposition work (tracked under that epic), so it is out of scope here.
baseline.summary: docs: disambiguate local ticket-store write path vs. Jira reconciler ('Two writers, one store')

content.text: ## What

`rebar list` (and the MCP `list_tickets` tool) currently return full ticket dicts including `description` and `comments`, producing very large output (148KB for `list --type=epic`). Make these agent-facing list surfaces lean by default.
## Scope

- `list_states(..., include_body: bool = True)` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py`: when False, strip `description` and `comments` from each public_state dict. Default True keeps internal callers (`validate`, `next_batch`, `list-epics`) unchanged.
- CLI `_cmd_list` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py`: lean by default; add `--full` flag to include bodies. Update usage/help text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar list --full` includes `description` and `comments`

content.text: ## Why
The deterministic decision math (Pass-3) is the most divergence-dangerous part of the four-pass
framework: if two gates compute "what blocks" differently, the gate guarantee silently forks.
`pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` already live in `plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`
and are *already* shared across the (former) bespoke and workflow paths — this lifts them into a
named shared kernel module as the framework's single decision core, with per-criterion thresholds
parameterized so a consuming gate can set its own posture without forking the math.
## What
- Create the kernel package (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`) and move the deterministic
Pass-3 core into it: `pass3_decide` (validity = graded fraction of the binary sub-answers;
impact = mean of ordinal-mapped severity attributes; priority = validity×impact; the
conditional cited-reference veto; block/advisory against per-criterion thresholds) +
`pass3_over_findings`.
- Parameterize the per-criterion `block_threshold` / posture so consumers pass their own
thresholds; keep plan-review's current defaults intact.
- Rewire the plan-review workflow's `plan_review_decide` op to call the kernel (no behavior
change). Keep a thin re-export from `plan_review` if needed for back-compat.
## Scope
In scope: the Pass-3 decision function + math + the binary→validity / attrs→impact maps, moved to
the kernel; plan-review consumes it. Out of scope: Pass-2 verify (WS2), the coach (WS3), the seam
doc + evals (WS4), and threshold *calibration* (deferred). Touches
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`/`passes.py`, the new kernel module, and
`workflow_ops.py` (the decide op).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A kernel module exists and houses `pass3_decide` + `pass3_over_findings` + the
validity/impact/veto math; per-criterion thresholds are a parameter, not hardcoded.
- [ ] The plan-review `plan_review_decide` op consumes the kernel; an offline test asserts the
decided partition (blocking/advisory/dropped/indeterminate) is unchanged vs before.
- [ ] No second copy of the decision math remains; any `plan_review` references are thin
re-exports, not duplicated logic.
- [ ] `make lint` + `make check` + the full test suite pass.

baseline.summary: WS1: Extract Pass-3 deterministic decision into the shared review kernel

content.text: ## What

The release workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes `nava-rebar` to PyPI on a `vX.Y.Z` tag but never creates a **GitHub Release**. The v0.2.0/v0.3.0 GitHub Releases were created by hand and that manual step lapsed, so github.com/navapbc/rebar shows **v0.3.0 as Latest** while tags and all three channels (PyPI, Homebrew, MCP Registry) advanced to **v0.6.0**. `docs/releasing.md` does not mention the GitHub Release channel at all.
## Why
GitHub's Releases page is the human-facing "what's the latest version" surface. It being 3 versions stale is misleading to users and contributors.
## Fix (two parts)
- **Backfill (ops):** create GitHub Releases for the missing tags `v0.4.0`, `v0.5.0`, `v0.5.1`, `v0.5.2`, `v0.6.0` with auto-generated notes so `Latest` points at v0.6.0 now.

- **Process (code, via Gerrit):** add a job/step to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that creates a GitHub Release on every `v*` tag push (auto-generated notes, marked latest), and document the channel in `docs/releasing.md`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GitHub Releases exist for v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.6.0 and `gh release list` shows v0.6.0 as `Latest`.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` creates a GitHub Release automatically on a `v*` tag push (with `contents: write` on that job and auto-generated notes).
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` documents the GitHub Release channel/step.
- [ ] Change lands on main through Gerrit (both LLM-Review and Verified votes green).

# S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers

## Context / Problem

The external integration suite is the only place rebar exercises a REAL provider end to end, and it runs on ONE provider. `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gates every live job on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (lines 46, 124, 185, 247; the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback appears only in the guard message, not as a matrix arm), and `prompt-eval.yml` likewise. So the provider seam this epic built — first-class Anthropic AND Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible — has exactly one arm under live test. A Bedrock-only regression (throttling shape, a `cachePoint` envelope change, an inference-profile id that stops resolving, structured output degrading) cannot be caught by CI today. It can only be caught by a human running the gates locally, which is what S7b makes possible and is NOT a substitute for automation.

This is the THIRD of the three permanent provider switches, the other two being the repo config / local environment [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] and the AWS review bot [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]. It is deliberately NOT "flip CI to Bedrock": the goal is live-grounded confidence across every provider we hold credentials for, so a MATRIX, not a switch. Flipping the single arm from Anthropic to Bedrock would trade one blind spot for another.

## Approach

Make provider a MATRIX DIMENSION of the external suite rather than an ambient default. Run the live jobs once per credentialed provider — Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI where a key exists — and have each arm SKIP LOUDLY when its credential is absent, so a missing secret is visible as a skip rather than indistinguishable from a green run.

SELECT THE PROVIDER THROUGH `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the layered config-file pointer, rather than bespoke per-arm CI wiring. Each matrix arm writes a small config file setting only `[llm.model_classes]` and points the env var at it. This is the right instrument for three reasons: it is the mechanism rebar already documents for exactly this purpose (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, landed by S7b), it DEEP-MERGES over the discovered config instead of replacing it so the arm overrides provider and model and nothing else, and it means CI DOGFOODS the same override path a developer uses — so the pointer itself gets live coverage on every run instead of being exercised only by hand. The deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is explicitly not the instrument: it cannot express per-class models.

Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain, not an API key, so the matrix cannot key on "an API key secret exists"; the Bedrock arm needs its own credential presence check.

THE S7 PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and an earlier draft of this plan wrongly said it did. S7 [rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67] grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reached via IMDS from inside `compose-review-bot-1` (caller identity `assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/<instance-id>`). The external suite runs on `ubuntu-latest` (`external-integration.yml:32`) — a GitHub-hosted runner with no instance role and no IMDS path to that host. So the CI arm needs its OWN credential mechanism, named explicitly: OIDC federation — `permissions: id-token: write` plus `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path). Static long-lived keys in a secret are the rejected alternative: they would put a durable AWS credential in CI to save a one-time role setup.

REGION MUST BE SET EXPLICITLY, and the `[llm.model_classes]` file cannot carry it. Bug [rebar:a574] established by measurement that IMDS does NOT supply a region and that Bedrock hard-fails with `NoRegionError` at client construction when none resolves — and that rebar's own `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` alone was insufficient, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` was also required. The Bedrock arm therefore sets BOTH as job env. This is a real trap, not a hypothetical: it already broke a Bedrock cutover once.

Cost is the real constraint: N providers multiplies the live spend of a suite that already runs weekly. Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The external suite runs its live jobs for MORE THAN ONE provider, with provider as an explicit
      matrix dimension rather than an ambient default read from whichever key happens to be set.
- [x] Anthropic and Bedrock are both covered. OpenAI is covered where a credential exists, or its
      absence is recorded as a deliberate decision with the reason.
- [x] Each arm selects its provider via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointing at a config file that sets
      ONLY `[llm.model_classes]`, NOT via the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`. A test or CI assertion
      pins that the override changes provider/model and leaves the rest of the discovered config intact.
- [x] An arm whose credential is ABSENT skips LOUDLY and is distinguishable in the run output from an arm
      that ran and passed — a missing secret must never read as green.
- [x] The Bedrock arm obtains credentials by a NAMED mechanism valid on a GitHub-hosted runner — OIDC
      role assumption via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to a dedicated scoped role (the S7 EC2
      instance-role path is NOT reachable from `ubuntu-latest`) — and a test or CI assertion pins that it
      does not silently fall back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [x] The Bedrock arm resolves an AWS region explicitly, setting BOTH `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` and
      `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as job env, and FAILS LOUDLY with the typed configuration error (per
      [rebar:a574]) when no region resolves — it must never skip silently or read as green.
- [x] The per-trigger COST of the matrix is measured and recorded, and the cadence decision (every
      trigger vs reduced cadence/subset per provider) is stated with its rationale.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
baseline.summary: S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers, not just Anthropic

## Why

Once planned-trace parity holds (B4), the gates can be switched from the bespoke orchestrator /
direct-agent path to the engine workflow path — converging on one substrate — WITHOUT regressing
the claim/close gate behaviour or the signed verdicts/attestations CI depends on.

## What

Cut the claim gate (plan-review) and the close gate (completion-verification) over to the engine
workflow path behind a config flag, defaulting to the workflow path once parity is proven. The
signing/attestation surfaces (`attest.py` plan-review signatures; the `completion_verdict` HMAC
signing) must keep producing byte-compatible signed artifacts so existing closed/claimed tickets
verify and CI's signature checks still pass. The bespoke path stays reachable behind the flag as a
fallback until removed.

## Scope

- Wire `_commands/claim.py` (plan-review precheck) and `_commands/transition.py` (close verify) +
  the library entrypoints (`review_plan` / `verify_completion`) to dispatch through the workflow
  engine, behind a config flag.
- Preserve the signed-verdict / attestation formats (material fingerprint binding, manifest
  prefixes) so verification is unchanged.
- Integration tests: claim gate + close gate still pass/fail correctly via the workflow path; signed
  artifacts verify.
- Depends on B4 (parity must hold first).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The claim (plan-review) and close (completion-verification) gates dispatch through the engine
      workflow path behind a config flag, defaulting to the workflow path.
- [ ] Signed verdicts/attestations remain byte-compatible (material binding + manifest prefixes
      unchanged); previously signed tickets still verify and CI signature checks pass.

to apply it convergently. No interface emits it yet — this unit only makes the
store *understand* the event, so it ships green and unblocks the writer units.
## What / Scope
- Define `TAG_DELTA = "TAG_DELTA"` in `src/rebar/reducer/_version.py` and
reference the constant INSIDE `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` (same file) and inside
`EVENT_TYPES` in `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` (import the constant) so the
literal cannot drift between the two sets.

exists yet (`process_edit` tags handling untouched). Full suite green.
## Acceptance Criteria

# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the **measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]` criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote / timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor, consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag "the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10) already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans** instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — a `det_`-style deterministic presence/shape check for the provenance fields,
  alongside the existing `det_operator_attested.py`.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — extend the three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements with the
  provenance requirement, and add the new advisory criterion.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR amending or superseding ADR-0043's evidence contract (it is the ADR that established
  the current shape).
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — route the new criterion, advisory posture (see story B's overlay work; this
  story should use the same mechanism rather than inventing a second one).
- Corpus/replay fixtures for the calibration required by ADR-0054.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` is flagged by
      a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no judgement about correctness — only
      presence and non-placeholder shape
- [ ] a test asserts the wrong-account escape is now catchable: a plan declaring one account against a repo
      whose Terraform backend names another produces a finding, built from the real `579718921998` vs
      `896586841071` case
- [ ] a CONTRAST test asserts a correctly-declared plan produces NO finding, so the criterion does not fire on
      every well-formed ticket
- [ ] a test asserts a scoped-permission criterion declaring `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged, and that
      `production-equivalent` is not — the `bedrock:*` case
- [ ] the new criterion ships **advisory**, never blocking on first landing (ADR-0054), and the ticket records
      the corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promotion
- [ ] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn '<criterion-id>' src/rebar/` is empty — other rebar clients are unaffected
- [ ] an ADR records the amended evidence contract and cites ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [ ] `grep -rn 'completion' <the new check>` shows no attempt to re-run a world measurement in the verifier —
      the rejected alternative stays rejected
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite pass, evidenced by the Gerrit
      change id and its `Verified +1` recorded in a comment on this ticket — and, dogfooding this story's own
      rule, that comment states the environment, principal and privilege posture of the run
baseline.summary: E1 — Force measurement provenance into attested evidence
