# S2 — Capability decisions read `ModelProfile`, not provider-name strings

## Context / Problem

Two capability decisions are made by string-matching a provider name. `src/rebar/llm/structured.py:63` `output_mode()` picks `NativeOutput` only when the prefix is in `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` (`structured.py:46`, a frozenset of four literal names), and `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:341` attaches prompt-cache settings only when the resolved string starts with `anthropic` (via `anthropic_model._anthropic_cache_settings`, `anthropic_model.py:39`). Both are wrong for Bedrock-hosted Claude, whose capability flags differ from the direct Anthropic API — the model string would say `bedrock`, so caching would silently switch off and structured output would silently take the prompted path. PR #121 hit exactly this and patched it with a `force_prompted: bool` threaded through four call sites.

## Approach

pydantic-ai exposes a per-vendor capability record at `model.profile` (`ModelProfile`). Replace both string matches with profile reads, and add a rebar-side override layer for cases upstream gets wrong or does not cover — using `ModelProfile` overrides for Bedrock-hosted Anthropic is the documented upstream guidance precisely because those flags diverge from the direct API.

### Where the code lives (resolves the S1 `providers.py` size conflict)

`capabilities_for()` and the override table go in a **new leaf module `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py`**, NOT in `providers.py`. Reason: S1 (`7468-25e5-ae4f-43d1`, closed) carries an **attested** acceptance criterion that `providers.py` stays under 300 LOC, and it is already 225 LOC — adding the record, the override table and the cache-settings selector would breach a criterion that has been signed. Capability *interpretation* is also a distinct concern from provider *construction*, and the repo's module-size policy targets 200–500 LOC units split along existing seams. `capabilities.py` is a leaf on the same footing as `anthropic_model.py`: it imports nothing from `runner` or `providers`, and heavy libraries are imported inside functions.

### The capability record

`capabilities_for(model) -> ModelCapabilities` returns a small frozen dataclass with **three** fields:

- `native_structured_output: bool`
- `prompt_cache_style: str` — one of `"none"` / `"anthropic"` / `"bedrock"`
- `supports_thinking: bool`

**The exact `ModelProfile` fields read** (verified against the pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1):

- `native_structured_output` is derived from `ModelProfile.supports_json_schema_output` (the strict
  json_schema capability `NativeOutput` requires). `ModelProfile.supports_json_object_output` and
  `ModelProfile.default_structured_output_mode` also exist and are NOT used — named here so a reader knows the
  choice was made, not missed.
- `prompt_cache_style` is derived from the profile's **capability FIELDS**, not from a name string and — for
  the Bedrock arm — not from its concrete type either: a profile exposing `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`
  yields `"bedrock"`; an `AnthropicModelProfile` yields `"anthropic"`; anything else yields `"none"`.

  **Why field presence rather than `isinstance(profile, BedrockModelProfile)`** — this is a hard constraint, not
  a style choice. `BedrockModelProfile` is exported ONLY from `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock`, which imports
  `botocore` at module top; there is no SDK-free `pydantic_ai.profiles.bedrock` (verified: the `profiles`
  package has no `bedrock` submodule). `boto3` appears in `pyproject.toml` only under the `reviewbot` extra, so
  the CI env that runs `make test` does NOT have it. An `isinstance` check would therefore (a) break the
  stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract and (b) fail in CI. Field presence needs no vendor import.
  `AnthropicModelProfile` is safe to `isinstance` against because `pydantic_ai.profiles.anthropic` is SDK-free.

  **S2 must add NO new runtime dependency** — in particular it must not add `boto3`/the `[bedrock]` extra, which
  is S3's scope.
- `supports_thinking` is derived from `ModelProfile.supports_thinking`. (`ModelProfile.thinking_always_enabled`
  and `thinking_tags` also exist and are not read here — the record answers "can this model reason at all",
  not how its reasoning is delimited.)

### How the profile is obtained — the lazy-model-string problem S1 created

`capabilities_for()` cannot simply read `model.profile`, because after S1 (`7468`, closed) **`run()` does not always hold a model OBJECT.** S1 deliberately leaves a provider that pydantic-ai recognizes but rebar does not build (openai, google) as a lazy model **string**, because eagerly resolving it would force that vendor's optional SDK to be importable — `pydantic_ai.providers.openai` raises `ImportError: Please install the openai package` and rebar's `[agents]` extra deliberately does not install it (verified: the `openai`, `google` and `groq` SDKs are all absent from the venv).

So `getattr(model, "profile", None)` on a `str` returns `None`, which would hit the conservative fallback and set `native_structured_output=False` for OpenAI and Google — silently destroying their `NativeOutput` path. `tests/unit/test_structured.py:177` asserts against exactly that, so it would surface as a regression.

`capabilities_for(model_or_model_string)` therefore accepts **either** form:

1. an object exposing `.profile` (the rebar-built providers: Anthropic, and Bedrock in S3) -> read it directly;
2. a provider-qualified model **string** -> resolve the vendor's profile WITHOUT constructing a provider, via
   a single `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` map from provider name to the matching function in **`pydantic_ai.profiles.*`**;
3. anything else -> the conservative record + one WARNING.

The critical verified fact that makes (2) work: **`pydantic_ai.profiles.*` are pure capability records and import cleanly WITHOUT the vendor SDK** — `from pydantic_ai.profiles.openai import openai_model_profile` succeeds and returns `supports_json_schema_output=True` with no `openai` package present, unlike `pydantic_ai.providers.openai`. So rebar reads capabilities for a provider it cannot construct, which is exactly the asymmetry S1's lazy-string path needs.

`_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` is a **single registry table**, and it is the one place a provider name maps to anything. The epic's criterion forbids *scattered* provider-selection branches and requires name->behaviour mapping to live in one registry; this is that registry, not a reintroduction of `startswith("anthropic")` decision-making.

**The required key set, enumerated.** A missing key silently falls back to the conservative record, which is a behavior change, so the keys are specified here rather than left to the implementer. Every row below was resolved against pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1:

| key | resolver | `supports_json_schema_output` | why the key is needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `profiles.anthropic.anthropic_model_profile` | True (overridden to False) | direct Claude |
| `openai` | `profiles.openai.openai_model_profile` | True | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |
| `openai-chat` | `profiles.openai.openai_model_profile` | True | upstream also exposes this prefix |
| `google-gla` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | **the prefix rebar itself emits** — `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` maps `google`/`google_genai` -> `google-gla` |
| `google-vertex` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |
| `vertexai` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | deprecated alias upstream still accepts |
| `google` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | upstream's CURRENT name |
| `google-cloud` | `profiles.google.google_model_profile` | True | upstream's current name for Vertex |
| `groq` | `profiles.groq.groq_model_profile` | **False** | in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` |

Two things this table settles:

- **`google-vertex` does NOT change behavior.** It is enumerated explicitly, and `google_model_profile` reports
  `supports_json_schema_output=True` for it, so it keeps `NativeOutput`. (Note `google-gla`/`google-vertex`/
  `vertexai` are *deprecated aliases* in 1.107.1 — upstream's live prefixes are `google`/`google-cloud` — but
  rebar's own `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` still emits `google-gla`, so omitting the aliases would break rebar's own
  output. S1's `providers._DEPRECATED_PROVIDER_ALIASES` exists for the same reason.)
- **groq remains the ONLY disclosed behavior change**, and it is a property of its profile, not of a missing key.

`bedrock` is deliberately absent: it is a rebar-BUILT provider (S3), so it arrives as a model object and takes the `.profile` path. Adding a string resolver for it would need `boto3` importable, reintroducing exactly the optional-SDK coupling this design avoids.

### `supports_thinking`'s processing protocol — who reads it, and who does not

This field's consumer is **provenance, not control flow**, and that distinction is the whole protocol:

- **`output_mode()` does NOT read it.** It keeps taking the caller-supplied `thinking: bool`, because pairing
  extended thinking with a native/forced output constraint is a documented Anthropic **400 on the request** —
  a property of the *call being made*, not of the model's capability. Reading the profile here would answer the
  wrong question.
- **S5 (`343b-4fdc-6722-469b`) reads it**, and reads it as part of the whole record: S5's signed provenance
  payload is `{provider, model, endpoint_host, tier, capabilities}` where `capabilities` **is this record**. So
  every field on this dataclass becomes part of a *signed, non-repudiable* verdict artifact.

That last point is why `supports_thinking` belongs on the record now rather than being deferred to the story that first branches on it. rebar does **not** currently persist the model's chain of thought, so a verdict's reasoning is not recoverable after the fact. If chain-of-thought retention becomes a requirement — a plausible auditability ask for a gate that blocks merges — the signed record must already state whether the model that produced each historical verdict was *capable* of thinking, because that fact cannot be reconstructed later from the sidecar. Adding the field after S5 ships is also strictly more expensive: it changes the shape of an already-signed payload rather than being present from the first signature. The field is therefore load-bearing for audit, and it is a deliberate, documented exception to "no field without a consumer" — the consumer is S5, one story away in this same epic, and it is named here.

### The rebar override table — schema, lookup, precedence, and its one entry

The override layer is **load-bearing, not speculative**, and the reason is concrete. Verified against pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1: `anthropic_model_profile("claude-opus-4-8").supports_json_schema_output` is **`True`**, and so is Bedrock-hosted Claude's. A naive profile read would therefore set `native_structured_output=True` for Claude and flip `output_mode()` to `NativeOutput` — silently changing rebar's PRIMARY provider away from the `PromptedOutput` path that `structured.py:40-46` deliberately chose (pydantic-ai may still route strict json_schema through ToolOutput per profile, and PromptedOutput plus rebar's tolerant parse is the reliable combination). `tests/unit/test_structured.py:179` already asserts Claude gets `PromptedOutput`. The override table is what keeps that contract.

**Schema.** An ordered tuple of `(predicate, overrides)` pairs — deliberately NOT a dict keyed by provider name, for two reasons: a name key would reintroduce exactly the string matching this story exists to remove, and it could not express the single rule below, which must span two different *hosts* of the same model family.

```python
_REBAR_OVERRIDES: tuple[tuple[Callable[[ModelProfile], bool], Mapping[str, object]], ...] = (
    (_is_claude, {"native_structured_output": False}),
)
```

- **Predicate**: `Callable[[ModelProfile], bool]`, reading the profile's **type** and/or its **capability
  fields**. It never inspects the model string or the provider name.
- **Value**: a partial mapping of `ModelCapabilities` field name -> value. Only the named fields are replaced;
  unnamed fields keep their profile-derived value.
- **Lookup**: iterate in declaration order; the **first** matching predicate wins and iteration stops. No
  merging across multiple matches, so there is no precedence ambiguity to reason about.
- **Precedence vs the profile**: overrides are applied **after** profile derivation (including after the
  `prompt_cache_style` type-dispatch), so an override always wins over the upstream flag.

**The one initial entry** identifies Claude on either host:

```python
def _is_claude(profile: ModelProfile) -> bool:
    """Direct-Anthropic OR Bedrock-hosted Anthropic."""
    return isinstance(profile, AnthropicModelProfile) or (
        getattr(profile, "bedrock_thinking_variant", None) == "anthropic"
    )
```

Both arms are required and neither is redundant: **Bedrock-hosted Claude's profile is a `BedrockModelProfile`, NOT an `AnthropicModelProfile`** (verified — they are sibling `ModelProfile` subclasses), so an `isinstance(AnthropicModelProfile)` test alone would miss the very models this epic exists to support, and Bedrock Claude would wrongly get `NativeOutput`. The second arm reads pydantic-ai's own `BedrockModelProfile.bedrock_thinking_variant` field, which is `'anthropic'` for Bedrock Claude, `'openai'` for Bedrock-hosted OpenAI, and absent/`None` for Meta and Amazon models (all verified). Note this is a **capability field read whose value happens to be a string enum** — materially different from `resolved.startswith("anthropic")` on a model string, which is the pattern this story removes.

**A rule derived purely from flags was tried and rejected.** `supports_json_schema_output and not supports_thinking` looks elegant and reproduces Anthropic and OpenAI correctly, but it was tested against every provider in today's `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` and **breaks two**: `gemini-2.5-flash` has `supports_thinking=True` (would lose `NativeOutput`) and `groq` has `supports_json_schema_output=False` (same). So `native_structured_output` is derived from `supports_json_schema_output` alone, plus this table.

**One disclosed behavior change: groq.** `groq_model_profile(...).supports_json_schema_output` is `False`, yet today's hardcoded `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` includes `groq`, so groq currently gets `NativeOutput` and after this change gets `PromptedOutput`. This is accepted deliberately rather than papered over with a second override entry: the profile is the authoritative capability source (the entire premise of this story), groq is not reachable through rebar's own provider map (`_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` covers anthropic/openai/google only), no test asserts it, and the direction is the safe one — `PromptedOutput` works everywhere. A test pins the new behavior so it is deliberate rather than incidental.

### Cache-settings selection — ONE function, one shape

`_anthropic_cache_settings(resolved: str)` is **deleted** from `anthropic_model.py` and replaced by a single `cache_settings_for(caps: ModelCapabilities)` in `capabilities.py`, which dispatches on `caps.prompt_cache_style`. This is a definite decision, not a choice left to the implementer: one function with one calling convention, so `runner.py`'s call site has exactly one shape.

**The exact settings keys** (verified against pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1 — note `BedrockConverseModelSettings` does **not** exist; the class is `BedrockModelSettings`):

| `prompt_cache_style` | class | keys set |
|---|---|---|
| `"anthropic"` | `pydantic_ai.models.anthropic.AnthropicModelSettings` | `anthropic_cache_instructions=True`, `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions=True` |
| `"bedrock"` | `pydantic_ai.models.bedrock.BedrockModelSettings` | `bedrock_cache_instructions=True`, `bedrock_cache_tool_definitions=True` |
| `"none"` | — | returns `None` (no cache keys sent) |

`AnthropicModelSettings` additionally has `anthropic_cache_messages` / `anthropic_cache` and `BedrockModelSettings` has `bedrock_cache_messages`; none of them are set here, preserving today's behavior exactly (only the instructions + tool-definitions breakpoints).

### Degradation contract

A model whose `.profile` is missing, `None`, or of an unrecognized type degrades to the **conservative** record (`native_structured_output=False`, `prompt_cache_style="none"`) and logs **exactly one** WARNING naming the model type. Conservative because both fallbacks are the safe direction: `PromptedOutput` works everywhere, and sending no cache keys is always valid. It never raises — an unknown provider must not break a run.

**Alternative rejected:** PR #121's `force_prompted` boolean. It is a per-call-site patch that grows one argument per capability per provider, and it encodes the answer at the caller rather than at the model — the next provider needs another boolean threaded through the same four signatures.

**Rollback.** The change is behavior-preserving for both currently-shipping providers, so backing out is a revert of this single change; there is no data migration and no config flag to unwind. If a profile read misbehaves in production the conservative fallback is already the safe state (prompted output, no cache keys), which degrades cost/latency but never correctness.

## Scope

Production:

- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` (**new** leaf) — `ModelCapabilities`, `capabilities_for()` (accepting a
  model object OR a model string), the `_PROFILE_RESOLVERS` registry, the rebar override table, and
  `cache_settings_for()`.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured.py` — `output_mode()` (`:51`) takes a `ModelCapabilities` instead of a model
  string; delete `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` (`:46`) and its use (`:63`).
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — **three** edit targets:
  - `:28` — the module-level `from rebar.llm.anthropic_model import (...)` block currently pulls in
    `_anthropic_cache_settings`. Since that helper is deleted, this import must drop it and instead import
    `cache_settings_for` (and `capabilities_for`) from `rebar.llm.capabilities`. Leaving it would be a hard
    ImportError at module load, not a subtle failure.
  - `:341` — the cache gate (the plan previously mis-cited `:316`, which is the toolset-filter line) reads
    `prompt_cache_style` via `cache_settings_for()`.
  - `:599` — the `output_mode()` call site passes the capability record instead of the model string.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — **delete** `_anthropic_cache_settings` (`:39`) and its docstring
  reference (`:10`).

Tests — **all four** affected files (S1 shipped with an under-enumerated test scope; this is the complete set, established by grepping every call site):

- `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` (**new**) — the mapping + degradation + cache-settings selection +
  `supports_thinking` derivation and its non-consumption by `output_mode()`.
- `tests/unit/test_structured.py` (`:176`, `:177`, `:179`, `:189`) — four `output_mode()` calls using the old
  string signature; must move to capability records.
- `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` — **both** cache tests, not just one:
  `test_cache_settings_enabled_only_for_anthropic` (`:310`, plus the direct `_anthropic_cache_settings` import
  at `:17` and its four calls at `:313`–`:319`) and
  `test_cache_model_settings_attached_only_for_anthropic` (`:358`).
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_execution_mode_dispatch.py` (`:90`) — monkeypatches
  `runner_mod._anthropic_cache_settings`; that patch target disappears, so it must move to the new seam. (This
  fourth site is the same file whose `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` patch S1 had to fix — it stubs
  `pydantic_ai` empty, so its replacement must not force a real settings-class import.)

## Testing

Unit tier for the mapping (a pure function over a profile) plus contract tier for the two consumers, since the defect class is a consumer reading the wrong signal.

- happy path: an Anthropic model yields `prompt_cache_style == "anthropic"` and `output_mode` returns
  `PromptedOutput`; an OpenAI model yields `native_structured_output=True` and `NativeOutput`.
- **Bedrock case (the motivating defect), in two layers so it runs without `boto3`:**
  1. **Always-run:** a profile stub carrying the Bedrock capability fields (`bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`,
     `bedrock_thinking_variant="anthropic"`) yields `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` AND
     `native_structured_output=False` (the Claude override reaching its Bedrock arm). No AWS, no credentials,
     no optional SDK.
  2. **`boto3`-gated pin (the verified-fake guard):** a test skipped via `importorskip("boto3")` asserts the
     REAL `BedrockProvider.model_profile("us.anthropic.claude-haiku- … [truncated by reconciler]

content.text: ## Summary
Two related gaps in the workflow reference-linter (`workflow/lint_refs.py`), surfaced reviewing the code-review gate (epic b744 / WS3):

1. `check_string` is routed over a step's `with:` values + the `if:` guard, but NOT over a `batch:` step's `criteria[].when` expressions (lint_refs.py ~378-407). So a typo'd `${{ steps.X.outputs.include_typo }}` in a batch criterion's `when:` is NEVER name-checked — it only surfaces at runtime.

2. `_output_fields_map` (lint_refs.py ~547) reads only `schema.properties.keys()`, ignoring `patternProperties`. So an output whose dynamic keys live in `patternProperties` (e.g. `overlay_union_output`'s `include_<overlay>` keys, or `plan_review_assemble_criteria_output`'s `include_<ID>`) is invisible to the reference check.
## Impact

The code-review gate (gates/code-review.yaml) leans on 22 `${{ steps.triggers/union.outputs.include_<overlay> }}` refs in batch `when:` clauses; none are linted. A typo would pass `rebar workflow validate` and only fail/misbehave at runtime (silently skipping an overlay). Pre-existing (plan-review's include_<ID> refs have the same blind spot); not introduced by b744.
## Reproduction Steps
1. In a v3 workflow, add a batch criterion `{prompt: X, when: '${{ steps.s.outputs.nonexistent_key }}'}`.
2. `rebar workflow validate <file>` → passes (no 'output not produced' finding), despite the bogus ref.
Expected: the linter flags the unknown output ref (as it does for `with:`/`if:`).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lint_refs` walks `batch.criteria[].when` expressions through `check_string` (same as `if:`/`with:`).
- [ ] `_output_fields_map` consults `patternProperties` (a ref matching a pattern is considered produced), so dynamic-keyed outputs aren't falsely flagged AND a non-matching typo IS flagged.
- [ ] A test: a typo'd batch `when:` ref fails `workflow validate`; a valid `include_<overlay>` ref passes.
## Notes

Discovered reviewing WS3 (8855) of the code-review epic (b744). Not fixed there (linter is shared infra; out of scope for the gate). Workaround: the code-review gate's offline test exercises the real `when:` resolution, catching typos at test time.

baseline.summary: Workflow linter doesn't name-check batch.criteria[].when refs + is patternProperties-blind

content.text: # BUG: Concurrent access to the ticket store produces corruption (inconsistent compaction snapshots + orphan events)
## Summary
Concurrent writers to the shared `tickets` branch are producing a **corrupted /
internally-inconsistent store**, which should not be possible. The store's design —
per-store `flock` serialization plus an append-only JSONL event log with
last-writer-append semantics and merge-on-push reconciliation — is supposed to make
concurrency safe: writes serialize under the lock, events only append, and divergent
clones converge on replay. Observed behavior contradicts that guarantee.
## Reproduction Steps
Observed live on 2026-07-05 while closing epic REB-601 (`9322-f84a-e047-4471`) with a
second agent session concurrently active on the same store (its commits show
`CREATE/CLAIM/FILE_IMPACT/REVIEW_RESULT/SIGNATURE/COMPACT` on ticket
`4563-d974-5166-419b`, plus `chore: sync events from rebar reconciler` and
`Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)` commits).
1. Two sessions write to the same store (`tickets` branch), auto-committing + auto-pushing.
2. Session A closes `seedy-edema-groan` (`b043-9490-32ca-4548`) through the completion
verifier: the event log records `STATUS(closed)` then `SIGNATURE(completion-verifier)`.
A `COMPACT b043-9490-32ca-4548` event lands afterward (compaction rewrites history into a
snapshot).
3. Read the ticket back (`rebar show b043-9490-32ca-4548` / `rebar list --parent 9322…`).
4. Run `rebar fsck`.
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** Reads reflect the last committed events. `b043` replays to
`status=closed` (its only status/signature events are the close + completion-verifier
sign; there is **no** `REOPEN`/`STATUS(open)` event after them). `fsck` reports a clean
(or near-clean) store. Concurrent writers converge without corruption.
- **Actual:**
- `rebar show b043` and `rebar list` report `status: open` **while the same ticket
still carries its `completion-verifier` signature** (a signature only produced at
close) — an impossible pair. Its event log contains **no reopen event** after the
close, so the `open` state is a bad **compaction snapshot**, not a real transition.
- `rebar fsck` reports **2920 issues**, including many `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`
(snapshot references a source UUID that still exists as a separate EDIT event) and
`ORPHAN_EVENT` (pre-snapshot event not captured in `source_event_uuids`).
- Reads flip-flop between invocations (same ticket read as `closed` then `open`),
indicating nondeterministic replay against an inconsistent snapshot set.
- Net: a `closed` epic (REB-601) with a child that reads `open` — a graph-integrity
violation the completion gate is supposed to prevent.
## Suspected Area
The corruption clusters around **compaction/snapshot generation** and the
**merge-during-push reconciliation** path, not the base append path:
- Compaction may snapshot a stale/partial event set when events arrive (or are merged from
`origin/tickets`) concurrently with the compaction — `source_event_uuids` then omits
events that still exist independently (`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` / `ORPHAN_EVENT`), and the
snapshot's materialized status can predate later events (the `open`-vs-signed
contradiction).
- The `Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during push retry)` path may interleave a
remote compaction with local un-compacted events (or vice versa) such that replay is no
longer deterministic across clones.
- Investigate whether `flock` actually covers the compaction + push/merge critical section
(vs only individual event appends), and whether it holds across the read-modify-write of a
snapshot. Note: the running binary also emits `unknown key 'verify.require_ticket_for_commit'
ignored` — confirm the compaction code path under test is the current build, not a stale one.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified and documented: the precise interleaving (compaction vs
concurrent append / origin merge) that yields `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT` /
`ORPHAN_EVENT` and a snapshot status that contradicts later events.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the corruption deterministically: concurrent
writers + a compaction (and/or a merge-during-push) drive at least one
`SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`/`ORPHAN_EVENT` or a status/signature contradiction,
failing before the fix.
- [ ] Fix ensures compaction + push/merge reconciliation is serialized (or otherwise
made atomic) with event appends so a snapshot's `source_event_uuids` always
captures every superseded event and replay is deterministic across clones.
- [ ] `flock` (or the equivalent guard) is verified to cover the full
compaction/snapshot read-modify-write and the merge-during-push critical section.
- [ ] After the fix, replaying the store yields a single consistent status/signature per
ticket (no `open`-with-completion-signature); `b043-9490-32ca-4548` and REB-601's
children read consistently across repeated `show`/`list` calls.
- [ ] A remediation/repair path exists for the already-corrupted store: `fsck` on the
current store no longer reports `SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT`/`ORPHAN_EVENT` (either a
`fsck --repair`-style rebuild of snapshots from the event log, or documented manual
steps), driving the current 2920-issue count to zero for these classes.

baseline.summary: Concurrent access to ticket store produces corruption (inconsistent compaction snapshots + orphan events)

baseline.description:
## Why
AGENTS.md is the canonical, cross-vendor agent guidance. CLAUDE.md bridges Claude Code to it via an @AGENTS.md import, and .codex/config.toml points Codex's project_doc_fallback at it. GitHub Copilot's coding agent already reads AGENTS.md natively, but other Copilot surfaces (Copilot Chat, Copilot CLI) look at .github/copilot-instructions.md first and had no pointer back to AGENTS.md, so they could silently drift from the canonical guidance.

## What
Add .github/copilot-instructions.md as a thin bridge file (mirroring CLAUDE.md's role): it declares AGENTS.md authoritative, summarizes the key sections (ticket workflow, Gerrit git flow, module-size policy, code-navigation tooling), and explicitly says not to duplicate content that could drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/copilot-instructions.md` exists in the tracked tree and states that `AGENTS.md`
      is canonical/authoritative for this repo.
- [ ] The new file summarizes rather than restates `AGENTS.md` (ticket workflow, Gerrit git
      flow, module-size policy, code-navigation tooling) and says `AGENTS.md` wins on conflict.
- [ ] No local-only Copilot state is added to the tracked tree (mirrors the posture where
      `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.codex/worktrees` stay untracked/local-only).
- [ ] Change lands through Gerrit per CONTRIBUTING.md: commit carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer
      and DCO sign-off, pushed to `refs/for/main`, and reaches `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.

## Context / Problem
probe-rebar.sh accumulated stale assertions (08ce: 3 stale asserts against removed flags/keysets). Its missing 'set -e' is DELIBERATE harness design (continue past failures, report all) — a naive port or hardening pass would break it.

## Approach
Port to a Python probe harness (scripts/probe_rebar.py) preserving the continue-on-failure design (collect results, report all, exit non-zero if any failed — the same contract, now explicit). Assertion-parity review required: every current assertion enumerated and carried over or retired with a reason (the 08ce class came from silent drift). Do NOT add set -e semantics.

Shell deletion and consumer re-pointing happen in the SAME change, after the side-by-side parity run: every consumer that hard-wires the shell path is re-pointed to the Python entry point in this change, so CI and the anti-rot gate track the new harness atomically.

## Scope
- scripts/probe-rebar.sh -> scripts/probe_rebar.py (port; the shell path is retained as a 7-line transitional exec shim because gerrit-verify.yaml executes from MAIN's workflow definition, whose golden-path step still invokes the shell path until this change lands — discovered on patchset 1, Verified-1 exit 127; deletion is follow-up d772-6007-5d04-4101)
- Consumers re-pointed in the same change (enumerated by grep for 'probe-rebar'):
  - .github/workflows/test.yml:128 — 'bash scripts/probe-rebar.sh </dev/null' -> python invocation

baseline.description:
## Context

Parallel agent sessions race to land changes on the Fast-Forward-Only `main` (ADR-0040).
The loser of each race must manually rebase-to-tip and retry, and with a large feature
**stack** this update-and-retry causes many CI re-runs on non-conflicting changes — burning
**wall-clock** (GitHub Actions minutes are free for this OSS repo, but concurrency is capped)
and **agent tokens/attention** (sessions hand-roll the rebase + poll for submittability).

This epic builds the **auto-lander**: agents set an opt-in intent and walk away; changes land
autonomously (or are handed back with a single actionable outcome), while the strong two-vote
gate is never weakened.

> **Terminology.** "stack" (the agent's view of a related series) and "chain" (a Gerrit
> relation chain) are used synonymously throughout this epic and its children.

**Separation-of-concerns scope (the load-bearing decision):** landing/merge-queueing is
**platform-specific and maintainer-owned**, NOT part of rebar's platform-agnostic
ticket/workflow/gate/reconcile mission. So everything here is **THIS project's infrastructure**
(Gerrit + GitHub Actions), living in `infra/` + a project CLI/script — it MAY `import rebar` for
ticket ops (e.g. close a ticket on merge) but adds **no Gerrit-specific landing logic to
`src/rebar` core**. The platform-agnostic generalization is deliberately deferred to a separate
`idea` (the landing provider-seam, `1701-8bc1-e3b7-4984`).

**Design settled in the brainstorm (all grounded in OSS prior art):**
- **Phase 1 = serial lander (this epic's committed scope).** Land the front `Autosubmit`
  change/chain: rebase to tip → await fresh Verified → ancestor-atomic submit.
- **Phase 2 = throughput, DEFERRED.** Cross-stack batching was evaluated by a design spike and
  **rejected** on this infra (the gerrit-to-platform bridge fires CI per-patchset → N runs not one;
  landing N off one run needs a GerriScary-class Verified direct-cast; wins only in rare bursts of
  ≥4 + a bisection tax + WIP-hook fragility). The recommended throughput approach — **bounded
  speculation** (speculate ≤ the GHA concurrency cap; each candidate a clean single-change-on-tip
  verified on its own tree) — is deferred to idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`, promoted only if the serial
  treadmill becomes a MEASURED pain.
- **Gate substrate stays:** FFO as the R5 backstop; strict `Verified` copyCondition
  (drops on rebase → CI re-runs); LLM-Review carries `TRIVIAL_REBASE` (ADR-0041) so a
  conflict-free rebase re-runs ONLY CI, not the LLM review.
- **`Autosubmit` opt-in label = a lease the agent hands the bot;** coexists with manual submit.
- **The stack is the atomic unit for landing AND failure:** never partial-land, never evict a
  change from *within* a stack; on failure the **whole stack is handed back to its owning agent**
  to remediate (Goal-2 exception: agent is pulled in only when code must change).
- **Agent contract = one command → one typed outcome** (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed |
  review_failed`); the `land` command is the single point that *returns* the outcome, so agents
  never correlate votes/labels/status themselves. Delivered as project tooling reading Gerrit
  primitives. **Outcome provenance (the deliberate split model — NOT co-located; this is the
  authoritative statement, superseding any looser "single source of truth" phrasing elsewhere):**
  the one outcome the bot must *decide and persist* — `needs_rebase` (a rebase conflict /
  FFO-not-landable state, which is NOT a native Gerrit vote and so has no live signal) — is
  **recorded by the lander into its own state (S3)** and read back by `land`; the three outcomes
  that ARE native Gerrit facts — `merged` (change status MERGED), `ci_failed` (a post-rebase
  `Verified -1` on the current patchset) and `review_failed` (an `LLM-Review -1`) — are **derived
  live by the `land` command from Gerrit primitives (S3/S4)**, not stored by the bot. (This
  matches S3 AC3 + S4 AC5, which own the code: only `needs_rebase` is persisted; `ci_failed` is
  read live from the current `Verified` vote.) So `land` is the single *reporter* of a unified
  typed outcome, composed from one bot-state read (`needs_rebase`) + live Gerrit reads.

## Greenfield note

This epic is greenfield: the `Autosubmit` label, the autolander service + its `wipChain` and state dir, the `land`/`land-status` command + outcome enum, the outcome-record schema, and ADR-0042 are all NEW artifacts created by this epic's stories. Cross-story references to them are forward-references to sibling deliverables (see each story's `## Dependencies`), not references to existing code.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Phase 1 — serial auto-lander (first deliverable)
- [ ] `Autosubmit` Gerrit label authored in `infra/gerrit/project.config` / pushed to
      `refs/meta/config`: **requester-votable ACL** (vote granted to group `Contributors`, so an
      agent sets the label under its OWN identity via the land command — the bot casts no votes;
      the grant is tightly scoped, not a bot-only or open grant), **non-gating** (informational;
      gating is redundant under FFO),
      **non-sticky** (empty copyCondition).
- [ ] Serial auto-lander service (project infra; deploys like the review-bot —
      `infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` + compose): for the front `Autosubmit`+submittable change/chain
      it rebases to the current tip (`POST /changes/{id}/rebase` / `/rebase:chain`,
      `RebaseInput.rebase_on_behalf_of_uploader=true` to preserve author/DCO/`rebar-ticket` trailers) → awaits a fresh
      `Verified +1` → ancestor-atomic submits the exact tested SHA. Single `wipChain` (serialized,
      one instance).
- [ ] **No gate-semantics change** — the serial lander reads existing `Verified` votes and casts
      NO votes (the bot never casts Verified in this epic's committed scope).
- [ ] Failure handling: CI-fail → remove `Autosubmit`, rely on the native `Verified -1` + run
      logs; rebase-conflict (`409`) → remove `Autosubmit` and record a conflict outcome. **Never
      partial-land; never evict a change from within a stack** — the whole stack is handed back to
      its owning agent.
- [ ] **Agent landing contract (the lead story):** a single **project** command that requests a
      land and returns ONE typed terminal outcome (`merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed |
      review_failed`) + distinct exit code; blocking (`--wait`) and single-shot status variants.
      `land` is the single **reporter** of the outcome, composing it per the split-provenance
      model above (one bot-state read for `needs_rebase`; live Gerrit reads for
      `ci_failed`/`merged`/`review_failed`) so the agent never correlates primitives itself. The command
      lives in **project tooling** (repo CLI/script), NOT `rebar` core; it may `import rebar` for
      ticket ops.
- [ ] Observability: the bot logs to **its own service logs** (container stdout → existing
      CloudWatch monitoring), NOT `session_log` (which is for agentic sessions only).
- [ ] Docs: rewrite this repo's landing section (`CLAUDE.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md`) to the new
      contract — "set `Autosubmit` / run the land command; act on the single typed outcome; do
      NOT watch votes or treat two green votes as 'it will land'." ADR-0042 (created by S6
      `broken-checkered-tiger`) records the auto-lander + agent contract.
- [ ] **Pre-cutover access baseline (captured by S1 `843b`, BEFORE the `Autosubmit` label is
      pushed to `refs/meta/config`):** save the current `GET /a/projects/rebar/access` response to
      `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json` and **commit it in the same change that
      adds the label to `project.config`**, so the ADR-0042 security-invariants diff below has a
      committed baseline to diff against. Without this baseline captured before cutover, the
      access-diff check is unperformable. (S1 owns the capture; S6/ADR-0042 owns the diff.)
- [ ] **Security-invariants artifact:** an ADR-0042 **Security invariants** section enumerating
      each invariant — non-gating `Autosubmit`; requester-votable (`Contributors`) vote ACL, tightly scoped; re-verify `is:submittable` on
      the exact tested SHA immediately before submit; two-vote gate unweakened — and, per
      invariant, the concrete check that proves it (a `grep` of `infra/gerrit/project.config`, a
      `GET /a/projects/rebar/access` diff vs the committed
      `infra/gerrit/access-snapshot-pre-autolander.json` baseline, and/or a test asserting the
      re-verify logic) (CVE-2025-1568 / GerriScary posture).

### Phase 2 — throughput (DEFERRED to idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`)
- [ ] No Phase-2 work is in this epic's committed scope. Cross-stack batching was evaluated and
      **rejected** by the design spike (stories S7-S9 archived); the throughput follow-on is
      **bounded speculation**, promoted from the idea only on a measured serial-treadmill pain.
- [ ] An agent sets the landing intent and walks away; in the common (non-conflicting) case the
- [ ] On any failure the agent receives **one typed, actionable outcome** — it never watches votes or
- [ ] **Nothing lands whose to-be-merged tree wasn't CI-tested** (FFO + strict Verified preserved;
- [ ] Redundant CI runs from the parallel-landing race are eliminated (each change/stack is CI'd only
- [ ] **No Gerrit-specific landing logic in `src/rebar` core** — rebar stays platform-agnostic.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (separate tickets)

- **Cross-stack batching** — evaluated by the Phase-2 design spike and **rejected** on this infra
  (per-patchset CI dispatch → N runs not one; a GerriScary-class `Verified` direct-cast; rare wins +
  bisection tax + WIP-hook fragility). S7-S9 archived; throughput deferred to **bounded speculation**
  (idea `c3a9-5f4c-bdc6-4e27`) — the correctly-shaped follow-on, not "speculation ruled out."
- **Platform-agnostic landing provider-seam in `rebar` core** (Gerrit/GitHub/GitLab adapters +
  portable outcome enum) — deferred to a separate `idea` (`1701-8bc1-e3b7-4984`; YAGNI until a
  second platform needs to land; consistent with rebar's provider-neutral identity/reconciler
  direction).
baseline.summary: Parallel-agent auto-lander for main — serial lander (project infrastructure)

content.text: ## Why
PyPI/wheel installs have no rebar git checkout, so live-git SHA resolution
(story 1) yields version-only there. Baking the release commit SHA at build time
gives consistent gate-code provenance across dev/editable and PyPI installs
(epic jira-reb-596).
## What
- Add `hatch_build.py` at the **repo root** implementing `BuildHookInterface`; it
runs `git rev-parse --short HEAD` at wheel/sdist build and writes a generated,
git-ignored `src/rebar/_build_info.py` (`COMMIT = "<sha>"`, or `COMMIT = None`
when built outside a git tree).
- Register it in `pyproject.toml` with a `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` stanza
(WITHOUT this, hatchling silently skips the hook and the baked SHA never ships).
- Add `src/rebar/_build_info.py` to `.gitignore` AND to the `artifacts` glob under
`[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` (git-based source discovery drops git-ignored
files from the wheel otherwise — the baked SHA would never reach PyPI).
- Extend the story-1 resolver fallback to **live-git-first, build-baked-second,
omit-last**: with no live checkout, import `_build_info.COMMIT`.
- Keep package version STATIC (`pyproject.toml` `version`); do NOT adopt hatch-vcs.
## Scope
Build-time SHA capture + fallback wiring only. Depends on story 1's resolver.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `hatch_build.py` writes `src/rebar/_build_info.py` with the build-time short
SHA; a non-git build writes `COMMIT = None` (graceful).
- [ ] `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` is registered AND `_build_info.py` is in
the wheel `artifacts` glob and `.gitignore`.
- [ ] Resolver falls back to the baked SHA on a non-git install, still preferring
the live checkout SHA when one exists.
- [ ] Package version remains static (no hatch-vcs).
- [ ] Tests: baked-fallback resolves the SHA when live git is absent; version-only
when both absent; a built wheel actually contains `_build_info.py` with a SHA.

baseline.summary: Bake release commit SHA at build time for non-git installs

# WS8 — Harden Gerrit auth (replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT with GitHub OAuth)

## Why
The live Gerrit (`rebar.solutions.navateam.com`, 3.14) runs `auth.type =
DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT` — a dev-only mode where anyone can impersonate any account (no
real IdP). It CANNOT be the sole gate on production GitHub `main` (WS7) until real auth is in
place. **Confirmed strategy (2026-07-01): GitHub OAuth via the `gerrit-oauth-provider` plugin
(GitHub backend), no reverse-proxy org gate** — access curated via a short account roster + Gerrit
ACLs. Precedent: GerritHub authenticates its whole user base this way; the plugin is actively
maintained (3.13.x, tracks the Gerrit release train). Blocks WS7.

## Config (the target state)
`infra/compose/gerrit.config`:
```ini
[auth]
    type = OAUTH
    gitBasicAuthPolicy = HTTP        # bots + git-over-HTTP keep working via HTTP passwords
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    root-url = "https://github.com/"
    client-id = "<GitHub OAuth App client id>"     # non-secret; from SSM
```
`etc/secure.config` (secrets, NOT committed — materialized from SSM like the S5 deploy key):
```ini
[plugin "gerrit-oauth-provider-github-oauth"]
    client-secret = "<GitHub OAuth App client secret>"
```
Plus: install the pinned `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar into `$GERRIT_SITE/plugins`, and remove ALL
`DEVELOPMENT_*` auth.

## Deliverables — split by access boundary
### In-repo (committed; applied on a fresh redeploy) — DELIVERABLE THIS SESSION
- A runbook `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md`: the full procedure (OAuth App, plugin,
  gerrit.config/secure.config, SSM params, redeploy, bot HTTP-password provisioning, account
  migration, verification, rollback).
- `gerrit-oauth-provider` pinned-jar provenance in `infra/gerrit/plugins/README.md` +
  install-plugins scaffolding.
- The `[auth]` block comment in `infra/compose/gerrit.config` points at the runbook + WS8 (the
  live flip to `type = OAUTH` lands with the plugin+secrets chain, per the runbook — flipping it
  in isolation would break a fresh Gerrit boot).

### Access-gated (needs org admin + working AWS) — HANDOFF
- Create the **GitHub OAuth App** on `navapbc` (callback `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/oauth`)
  → client-id/secret. (Needs GitHub org admin via the web UI; this session's token lacks `admin:org`.)
- Put client-id/secret in **SSM** under the Gerrit secret prefix; add the params to `infra/terraform/ssm.tf`.
- **Apply to the live host** (AWS SSM/SSH — this session's AWS session is EXPIRED): install the
  plugin, seed the OAuth config into the live `site/etc/gerrit.config` + `secure.config`, remove
  become-any-account, restart Gerrit.
- **Provision bot credentials BEFORE cutover**: give the `rebar-review-bot` service account an HTTP
  password (dev-mode required none), so its git/REST access survives the auth change.

## Acceptance Criteria
### In-repo (this session)
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/gerrit-auth-hardening.md` documents the complete GitHub-OAuth hardening procedure (OAuth App → plugin → gerrit.config/secure.config → SSM → redeploy → bot passwords → account migration → verify → rollback).
- [ ] The `gerrit-oauth-provider` jar is pinned + provenance-documented (plugins/README.md) and wired into the plugin install path.
- [ ] `infra/compose/gerrit.config` `[auth]` comment points at the runbook + WS8 (records that the live flip to OAUTH lands with the plugin+secrets chain).
### Live (access-gated)
- [ ] GitHub OAuth App created; client-id/secret in SSM; `ssm.tf` params added.
- [ ] Live Gerrit switched to `auth.type = OAUTH` (become-any-account removed); Gerrit restarts healthy; a human logs in via GitHub OAuth.
- [ ] `rebar-review-bot` has an HTTP password; its REST/git access verified post-cutover.

## Dependencies
- Blocks WS7 (the Gerrit-only cutover must not precede real auth).
- Live steps need `navapbc` GitHub org admin + working AWS access to the Gerrit host (d251 infra).
baseline.summary: WS8: Harden Gerrit auth (GitHub OAuth, replace DEVELOPMENT_BECOME_ANY_ACCOUNT)

# S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of `transport.py` (behaviour-preserving)

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260], whose plan hit BLOCK ten times. The round-by-round record is on that ticket; the structural finding is that it carried TWO independent changes — a mechanical relocation and a new 429 policy — and every round found new surface because a fix to one re-opened the other. Rounds 6-7 were about THIS half's mechanics; rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 were about the policy half (now S2). Splitting is the same move that turned J9's eight BLOCKs into a first-try PASS as J10.

This story is the mechanical half and is **forced by the module-size cap, not by taste**: `transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`** against the LOCKED 800-line cap (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so there are ELEVEN lines of headroom and the 429 policy cannot be added in place. (Recording the measurement because this file's LOC has been misquoted twice in epic e369: the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263 base difference, and now that 9263 is merged both readings agree at 789.)

## Approach

**Relocate, do not redesign.** Move the retry/error cluster from `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` into a new `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`, changing no behaviour. The cluster is `_connection_retry_exceptions`, `_jira_http_error_types`, `_as_backend_http_error`, `TlsVerificationError`, `_tls_verification_error`, and `_with_connection_retry`.

**`TlsVerificationError` MUST move with the rest.** `_tls_verification_error` returns it, so leaving the class behind in `transport.py` makes `retry.py` import from `transport.py` while `transport.py` imports `_with_connection_retry` from `retry.py` — a circular import. The class and its factory are one unit.

**Re-export from `transport.py` so existing importers keep working.** `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` imports `TlsVerificationError` from the transport module; that test must pass UNEDITED, because editing it to chase the move would convert a regression signal into a rubber stamp.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — NEW; the moved cluster.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — cluster deleted,
  cluster imported, names re-exported.

**NOT in scope:** any behaviour change, and specifically any 429 / `Retry-After` handling — that is S2. If this story changes what any call does, it has failed.

## Testing

The oracle for a pure relocation is that the EXISTING suite passes unedited — a new test asserting the code moved would only restate the diff.

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` DC transport tests pass with NO edits.
* `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes with NO edits (proves the re-export works).
* The module-size gate passes, and `transport.py` is measurably smaller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry.py` exists and contains all six named members, and `transport.py` no longer defines
      them
- [ ] `TlsVerificationError` lives in `retry.py` WITH `_tls_verification_error`, and a test or a
      clean `python -c "import ..."` proves there is no circular import between the two modules
- [ ] `transport.py` re-exports the moved names, and `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes
      **with zero edits to that file** — asserted by `git diff --exit-code` on it
- [ ] the full DC transport unit suite passes with zero test edits; if any test needed an edit,
      this story is not behaviour-preserving and must be reworked rather than the test adjusted
- [ ] `transport.py` is under the 800-line cap with headroom for S2, and the measured before/after
      line counts are recorded on this ticket
- [ ] NO diff hunk changes control flow, retry counts, backoff values, or exception types — a
      reviewer can confirm the change is a move by reading the diff alone
baseline.summary: S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of transport.py (behaviour-preserving)

## Why
Change #529's sole advisory — 'the new degrade behavior has no test; all classifier tests importorskip pydantic_ai so a core-only env never exercises it' — scored severity none / impact 0.0, then proved out as a red-main incident 57 minutes after merge (fix #530). No threshold can catch a finding scored 0.0: this is a pass-2/impact-model vocabulary gap in impact_code (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py:230-267), whose maint lane has safety_net_removal_without_replacement but nothing for 'change introduces/unmasks a reachable path with NO automated coverage'. Distinct from the blocking-lane stories: those tune pass-3 thresholds; this fixes what pass 2 can express.

## What

It is True when the change introduces or unmasks a reachable code path with NO automated test coverage. Named edit sites:
  - `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py`: add `reachable_path_without_automated_coverage` to `_CODE_MAINT_BINARIES` (decide.py:198-205) at **tier moderate (0.6)** — abstain-safe (absent/False → contributes 0, never inflates, per `_code_truthy`).

- Per ADR 0036 a formula/vocabulary change REQUIRES an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump: `code-v2 → code-v3` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` (L26). Update the version-pinning test `tests/unit/test_impact_model_versioning.py` (the `== "code-v2"` assertion at line ~34 → `code-v3`). A fresh version-segmented cohort is required before any threshold consumes code-v3 (out of scope here — 9f25/b9c0 stay on code-v2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION is bumped to code-v3 in sidecar.py, sidecars carry it, and `test_impact_model_versioning.py`'s version assertion is updated to `code-v3` (from `code-v2`).
- [ ] `tests/unit/fixtures/code_review_impact_labels.jsonl` gains a HIGH-labeled row exercising the new binary, and a unit test in `test_impact_code.py` replays a #529-shaped finding asserting impact > 0 under code-v3 while the code-v2 impact of old (binary-absent) sidecars is byte-unchanged (0 contribution when absent).
- [ ] make lint passes on the change.

- [ ] make test passes on the change.

content.text: # BUG: code-review vote renders a fail-closed DET detector match as "BLOCK — finding / 0 blocking issues"
## Reproduction Steps
1. Push a change touching a file that a fail-closed DET detector (gitleaks secret-detection) matches on.
2. The 4-pass LLM gate returns PASS (no LLM blocking findings), but apply_failclosed forces BLOCK.
3. The Gerrit vote is LLM-Review-1 tagged "[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]" with message "rebar code review found 0 blocking issue(s):" — and NO robot comment names the match.
Root cause: src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:123-151 apply_failclosed sets
verdict["verdict"]="BLOCK" on a match but never appends the match to verdict["blocking"]
(it only records it under coverage.security_detectors). review_bot/adapter.py then counts
len(verdict["blocking"])==0 and renders "found 0 blocking issue(s)"; adapter.py:183-191 tags
it "finding". voter.py posts only the message. So a genuine detector block is unnamed and
non-actionable — and a REAL leaked secret is hidden from the author identically.
Expected: a fail-closed detector match is surfaced as a named, counted blocking finding.
## Acceptance Criteria

## Why

Surfaced by the plan-v4 divergence-grading calibration (story doggish-nonorganic-tsetsefly), from the same plan-v3 sidecar corpus (18,085 verified findings).

`undecomposed` fires on **12 of 18,085 findings (0.07%)** — two orders of magnitude below every other axis — while holding full HARD-OVERRIDE power (any non-none grade floors impact at 0.85 and auto-blocks). Comparison across the seven axes on plan-v3:

| axis | non-none |
|---|---|
| vague_directive | 31.03% |
| ac_unverifiable | 15.79% |
| internal_conflict | 10.17% |
| divergent_implementation | 7.72% (fixed in plan-v4) |
| dod_uncertifiable | 5.36% |
| irreversible_without_rationale | 1.97% |
| **undecomposed** | **0.07%** |

Two candidate explanations, both worth confirming before touching anything:

1. **Working as intended / correctly suppressed.** The axis's own prompt text says a deterministic
   signal (G5) already suppresses false 'flat plan' findings on tickets that HAVE children, and
   most reviewed tickets do have children. If so, 0.07% is the correct residual and the axis
   simply has a narrow true population — no change needed, just documentation.
2. **Mis-specified / unreachable.** The grading instruction may be so hedged ('Grade ONLY a
   genuine gap') that verifiers never assign it, in which case a real class of flat-plan defects
   is scoring 0.0 the same way the divergence class did before plan-v4.

## What

Investigate, do not pre-commit to a fix:

- Pull the 12 firing findings from the corpus and read them — are they genuine flat-plan defects,
  and did they block?
- Determine how often the G5 deterministic suppressor fires, to separate 'correctly suppressed'
  from 'never assigned'.
- Look for the inverse population: findings whose TEXT describes an undecomposed/flat plan but
  which scored the axis `none` (the same ~90%-missed analysis that motivated plan-v4's
  divergence grading).
- Only if (2) is confirmed, propose a change — and note that any impact-model shape change costs
  an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump that closes the plan-v4 cohort, so batch it per ADR 0054 §4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A comment on this ticket reports the 12 firing findings (criteria, decision, whether the
      floor was load-bearing) and the measured G5 suppression rate. Verified: the comment exists
      and cites per-finding ids from the corpus.
- [ ] The comment states which explanation the evidence supports (correct-residual vs
      mis-specified) with the counts backing it, and either (a) records 'no change needed' with the
      rationale, or (b) links a follow-up story scoped to the fix. Verified: one of the two
      outcomes is explicitly recorded.
- [ ] Method is ADR-0054-compliant: driven off the persisted sidecar corpus at zero marginal LLM
      cost — no purpose-built eval suite and no bulk re-review sweep. Verified: the comment names
      the corpus + replay as its instrument.

## Notes

Analysis-only ticket; it may legitimately close with 'the axis is fine, here is why'.
baseline.summary: Investigate the near-dead 'undecomposed' hard-override axis (12/18,085 fires on plan-v3)

baseline.description:
# live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap

## Context / Problem

The live Jira DC harness tier dies at SETUP, so no live acceptance evidence can be produced at all — and every remaining story in epic e369 (notably J11, the epic's headline live proof) runs on this harness. Reproduced across two independent CI runs (30604756524, 30623000498), same signature:

    ERROR at setup of test_add_label_and_the_links_surface_against_a_real_instance
    AssertionError: PAT creation failed: 403
      {'exception': 'com.atlassian.pats.exception.UserTokenLimitExceededException',
       'error': "You can't create more than 10 tokens."}

`jira_dc_pat` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:355`) is declared `@pytest.fixture` with NO scope, so it is FUNCTION-scoped: every test that requests it mints a brand new Personal Access Token via `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` and never deletes it. Jira Data Center caps a user at 10 PATs. Consumption therefore grows as O(tests) while the budget is fixed at 10.

Two properties make this expensive to diagnose, and both are reasons to fix it properly rather than by trimming test count:

* **It mis-attributes.** The ERROR surfaces at setup of a test in `test_transport.py` — a module
  nobody touched — because that is merely the test that happened to run once the budget was
  spent. The cause is session-wide.
* **It looks flaky but is deterministic.** The fixture mints with `expirationDuration=1`, so
  tokens self-clear after a day. Whether a run fails depends on how recently the instance was
  used, not on chance.

## Approach

**Make `jira_dc_pat` SESSION-scoped**, turning PAT consumption from O(tests) into O(1).

This is the fix that scales, and scaling is the actual requirement: J11 adds substantially more live tests to this tier, so any fix whose budget is still proportional to test count merely moves the cliff. Every consumer needs only *a* valid PAT — no test in this tier asserts per-token behaviour (verified: the fixture's only assertions are on `rawToken`, and its sole consumers use it as a bearer credential) — so one token per run is behaviourally identical to one per test.

**Rejected: per-test teardown via `DELETE /rest/pat/latest/tokens/{id}`.** It preserves per-test isolation that nothing here needs, costs an API call per test, and — decisively — it is not verified to be implementable: the creation response is only asserted to carry `rawToken`, and whether it also returns an `id` has NOT been confirmed against a live instance. Choosing it would make the fix depend on an unverified response field. Session scope depends on nothing new.

**Complementary: sweep leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` tokens at session start**, mirroring `_leaked_scratch_projects()` (`conftest.py:181`), which already does exactly this for scratch PROJECTS left by interrupted runs. Session scope alone fixes consumption WITHIN a run; it does not help a run that starts against an instance already holding 10 tokens from a crashed predecessor. Both layers are required for the ACs below, and they address different failures.

The sweep uses the same defensive posture the project fixture already establishes: read the token list from its direct REST endpoint and, if it cannot be enumerated, **return empty rather than invent a failure** — a sweep that cannot see is not evidence of cleanliness, and the harness-readiness assertion remains authoritative for usability. Deleting a leftover token is likewise best-effort: a failed delete is reported, not fatal, because the session-scoped mint that follows is the real test of whether headroom exists.

**Raw `urllib` REST is correct here and is not a divergence from "never hand-roll REST".** That rule governs the DC *transport*, which must go through `pycontribs/jira`. This conftest deliberately speaks raw REST v2 with stdlib `urllib` only (see its module docstring) so the harness does not depend on the client library the harness exists to validate. The sweep reuses the existing `_request` helper.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` — change `jira_dc_pat` to `scope="session"`,
  document the 10-token cap in its docstring, and add a `_leaked_harness_tokens()` helper plus
  its invocation from the existing session-scoped `_jira_dc_harness_ready` autouse fixture.
- `tests/unit/` — unit coverage for the sweep helper's parsing and its
  cannot-enumerate/failed-delete degradation, exercised against a stubbed `_request` so it runs
  in the normal (non-live) tier.

No production `src/rebar` code changes: this is a test-harness defect.

## Testing

The live tier cannot run on this workstation (its base image is linux/amd64 only and this is Apple Silicon — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:54-73`), so the split is deliberate:

* **Unit (runs everywhere, in CI on every change):** the sweep helper returns the leftover
  token names/ids from a well-formed list response; returns EMPTY when the endpoint errors or
  returns a non-list (the cannot-enumerate path); ignores tokens not carrying the
  `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix (so it never deletes a human's unrelated PAT — the failure mode
  that would make this fix worse than the bug); and does not raise when a DELETE fails.
* **Live (GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job):** the acceptance evidence. The full
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite completes with no `UserTokenLimitExceededException`.
  Because session scope makes consumption O(1), one token is consumed regardless of test count,
  which is what supplies headroom rather than a coincidence of the current count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `jira_dc_pat` is `scope="session"`, verified by reading the fixture declaration, so a run
      mints exactly ONE PAT no matter how many tests request it
- [ ] the full `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite runs in the GitHub Actions
      `jira DC harness smoke` job with ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`, confirmed by
      reading that job's log — not the overall run status
- [ ] headroom is structural, not coincidental: because consumption is O(1) in test count, the
      run above passes with MORE live tests present than the count that first triggered the cap
- [ ] a leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` token from a crashed run is deleted at session start, so
      it does not break the next run — covered by a unit test against a stubbed `_request`
- [ ] the sweep never deletes a token lacking the `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix, asserted by unit
      test
- [ ] the sweep degrades safely: a non-200/non-list list response yields an empty result rather
      than an exception, and a failed DELETE does not abort the session — both unit-tested
- [ ] the 10-token cap and the session-scope decision are documented in the `jira_dc_pat`
      docstring, since the cap is a non-obvious Jira DC limit
baseline.summary: live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap; jira_dc_pat is function-scoped

## Context / Problem
The Gerrit Verified gate takes 21-47 minutes end-to-end. Measured on run #1823 (id 30569775555), the critical path is a SINGLE job: `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` at 18.6m. Every other job is <=8m; if macOS vanished the run would finish in ~8m.

Worse, macOS runner concurrency is capped (peak 4 concurrent macOS jobs observed across 25 sampled jobs from the last 30 runs). When 6 changes were dispatched within 10 seconds, the later ones queued 6.7-8.4m for a macOS runner. That queue is what turns a 21m run into the 41-47m the operator observes. So macOS job DURATION is doubly valuable: it is both the critical path and the thing holding a scarce runner slot other changes wait on.

Within that job, the `--cov` default-suite step is 15.4m of the 18.6m. The macOS cells pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, so coverage.py traces the entire run — but NOTHING consumes the macOS coverage number. The `fail_under = 70` floor in `[tool.coverage.report]` is enforced identically by the three ubuntu cells running the exact same test selection.

## Approach
Make the coverage flags conditional on the matrix OS in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: ubuntu cells keep `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, macOS cells run without them. This is pure duplicate-work removal — the identical 7856 tests still execute on macOS, and the coverage floor is still gated three times over on ubuntu.

Rejected alternative: dropping the macOS cell entirely. That is the obvious 2x win and it removes exactly the platform-compat coverage (flock/mkdir lock, gtimeout) the cell exists for. Out of bounds — the requirement is no coverage loss.

Rejected alternative: keep `--cov` on macOS but add `--cov-fail-under=0`. Pointless: it retains the tracing cost, which IS the cost, and only removes an assertion that already passes.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — the `test` job default-suite step only. The integration-tier step already passes no `--cov` and is untouched. The `-n` worker counts, `--dist` modes, `--basetemp`, and every drift gate are untouched.
- `docs/coverage.md` — record that coverage is collected on the ubuntu cells only, and why.

Explicitly NOT in scope: sharding the macOS job, changing `-n`, and the verify-identity partial-clone fix (recorded on epic 42eb-5789-c798-4dfc). Those are separate changes with their own risk profiles.

## Testing
No new testable behavior — this is a CI workflow configuration change, so no new unit test is warranted. `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the substring `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (line 67), which this change preserves; that suite must stay green. Verification is observational on the next Verified run: the macOS default-suite step gets faster with an unchanged pass count, and the ubuntu cells still print the coverage report.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The macOS matrix cells run the default suite with no `--cov` or `--cov-report` flags.
- [ ] The ubuntu matrix cells still pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`.
- [ ] The `-m "not integration and not external"` selection is byte-identical on both platforms, so the set of tests executed on macOS is unchanged.
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `docs/coverage.md` states that CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only.
baseline.summary: Drop coverage collection from the macOS pytest cells (CI wall-clock)

content.text: ## What
Add proactive detection in the reconciler fetcher: when `_build_snapshot`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`) encounters a Jira workflow
status absent from `config.jira_to_local_status`, emit a stderr WARNING and an
observable `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` bridge_alert (deduped per 24h) naming
the offending status and an example issue.
## Why
A Jira-side workflow status with no reconciler mapping (e.g. an `IDEA` status
added to the Jira workflow) is otherwise discovered only downstream, when it
reaches an outbound mutation and trips `reconcile.preflight_status_mapping`. A
stale such status in `prev_snapshot.json` once stalled the entire bridge. The
per-mutation isolation fix already makes an unmapped status non-fatal; this adds
early, proactive visibility at snapshot-build time so the missing mapping is
flagged and can be added before it causes churn.
## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py`: add `_known_jira_statuses()`
and `_flag_unmapped_statuses()`; call the latter from `_build_snapshot`
(fail-open — detection must never break the fetch).
- Fires once per distinct unmapped status per pass; alert is deduped across
passes via `alert_store.is_deduped` (24h window).
- Out of scope: adding the `idea`/`IDEA` mapping itself (owned by the in-flight
idea-status epic).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_build_snapshot` emits a `fetcher-unmapped-jira-status` alert via
`alert_store.append` naming any Jira status not in `config.jira_to_local_status`.

- [ ] Detection is fail-open — an error during detection never breaks the fetch.

baseline.description:
## Why

The parent-first claim/transition cascade is thoroughly covered for the sequential,
single-process case (parent-first, multi-level, already-progressed/blocked parent,
parent-failure-aborts-child, child-failure-after-parent, cycle termination, exit-code
propagation). There is no test for a cross-process / two-clone race where two agents
work different children of the same open parent. The report is right that the expected
semantics must be written down before a test can assert them (e.g. may children be
claimed independently once the parent is in progress? does a losing parent claim after
merge invalidate the corresponding child claim?).

## What

Committed policy (to be documented, then tested) for two same-parent/different-child
sub-cases:
- **(a) Same-tracker, serialized:** agent A claims the parent (cascade) then child A.
  Agent B, seeing the parent already `in_progress`, does NOT cascade and may claim
  child B independently under its own assignee. Parent ownership does NOT constrain
  sibling child assignees. This is fail-fast: if B's parent-claim were attempted while
  the parent is `open` and lost, B's child is never attempted.
- **(b) Two offline clones:** both independently claim the (open) parent + a child. On
  merge, forks are resolved **independently per ticket** by the reducer's UUID tie-break:
  - The PARENT's STATUS fork resolves to one winner (surfaced as `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`
    on the parent); the losing agent's parent ownership is thereby signaled.
  - If both clones claimed the SAME child, the CHILD also has a concurrent STATUS fork,
    resolved by the same tie-break INDEPENDENTLY of the parent — so the child's winner may
    differ from the parent's winner. If they claimed DIFFERENT children, each child simply
    carries its own single claim.
  - In all cases the losing agent's already-written claim (parent and/or child) is **left
    in place (orphaned under the losing assignee); it is NOT retroactively rolled back or
    tombstoned.** The signal is `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED` on the affected ticket(s).

Document this in `docs/concurrency.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, then encode it in two tests.

## Scope

- `docs/concurrency.md` and/or `CLAUDE.md` (policy statement)
- `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` (or sibling) — new race tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ownership policy for BOTH sub-cases above is written down in
      `docs/concurrency.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, including the explicit rule that a losing parent
      claim leaves the losing agent's child claim in place (orphaned), detected via the
      parent's `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`.
- [ ] Same-tracker process race test (sub-case a): two real processes race on one
      tracker; confirms lock serialization, that B does not cascade a parent already
      `in_progress`, and both children end claimed under their respective assignees.
- [ ] Two-clone offline race test (sub-case b): both clones claim parent+child offline,
      then merge; confirms deterministic convergence, the parent `STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED`
      signal, that a SAME-child claim produces an independently-resolved child STATUS fork
      (child winner may differ from parent winner), and that the losing agent's claim(s)
      remain in place (not rolled back).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: Define parent-cascade race policy + cross-clone race tests

## Why
ADR 0047 relaxes pre-merge re-CI on a clean rebase, so the detector for a rare semantic conflict between two individually-green changes is the EXISTING post-merge `main` CI, with a MANUAL revert as the remedy (no auto-revert — deliberate cost/scope choice). ADR 0047 promised this runbook ("runbook to follow"); this task delivers it.

## What
- [ ] Create `infra/runbooks/main-red-post-merge.md`: document (a) the detector — `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs the full suite on every `push` to `main` (branches-ignore feature/**) after Gerrit replicates the submit to the GitHub mirror; where to watch it; that it is a post-merge *detector*, not a pre-merge gate; (b) the manual-revert procedure — confirm-not-flake, identify the culprit change, revert THROUGH Gerrit (revert change → two-vote gate → Submit), confirm green, re-land correctly; (c) that auto-revert is deliberately NOT built (revisit only if red-main recurs).
- [ ] Cross-link the runbook from ADR 0047 (replace its "runbook to follow" placeholder) and from CONTRIBUTING.md's post-merge safety-net note.

# Make the API-stability version references version-agnostic (remove drift-prone markers)

Adopt the mainstream OSS pattern (FastAPI/attrs/httpx): state the stability **policy**
without naming a current version in prose, and point readers to the CHANGELOG / GitHub
Releases for live numbers. This removes the duplicated `currently X.Y.Z` package-version
marker in `docs/api-stability.md` — and with it the drift it caused and the guard that
policed it (`tests/unit/test_version_sync.py`) — so no version must be hand-bumped in the
doc each release. (Design Option A from the api-stability version-marker analysis; Option E
— VCS-derived versioning — is parked separately as idea deficient-eastmost-hoopoe.)

## Why

`docs/api-stability.md` hard-codes `(currently 0.8.0)`, duplicating `pyproject.toml`'s
version. That duplication silently drifted before (the doc once read 0.6.0 while the package
was 0.7.1), which is why `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` exists to fail CI on a mismatch.
The specific number adds nothing over the "0.x ⇒ any minor may break" statement that carries
the real meaning; the live version belongs in the CHANGELOG / Releases, which the release
flow already maintains. Removing the marker eliminates the duplication at its source, so the
consistency test is correctly removed WITH it (removing the test while keeping the marker
would reopen the drift bug). The same anti-pattern already bit the same file a second time:
the Event-schema row reads `SCHEMA_VERSION (currently **3**)` while the code is at **5** — a
live, wrong literal — so this change de-literals those parentheticals too. Popular
actively-maintained projects write pre-1.0 stability policy this way: FastAPI's "About
FastAPI versions" and attrs' "Backward Compatibility" name no current version and defer to
the changelog.

## What / Scope

- `docs/api-stability.md`:
  - Reword the opening so it states the 0.x SemVer policy WITHOUT a `currently X.Y.Z` version
    literal, and links to the CHANGELOG and GitHub Releases for the current version.
  - De-literal the Event-schema row: replace `SCHEMA_VERSION (currently **3**, in
    rebar/reducer/_version.py)` and `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1)` with references to
    those constants in their source files WITHOUT a hard-coded number (fixes the stale `3`,
    which is actually 5, and removes the same drift-prone anti-pattern).
  - Keep the rest of the page (the per-surface stability matrix content) unchanged.
- `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` — DELETE. Its sole purpose was to keep the now-removed
  package-version marker in sync; with no marker there is nothing to check.
- `docs/releasing.md` — remove ONLY the two dangling references added when cutting v0.8.0:
  drop `docs/api-stability.md` from the step-1 `git add` bump command, and delete the
  `test_version_sync.py` / `(currently X.Y.Z)` mentions in that step. **Preserve** the
  unrelated 1.0-declaration section's reference to `docs/api-stability.md` (the "remove the
  Pre-1.0 caveat" instruction near line 434) — it is not about the version marker.
- Out of scope: any change to `pyproject.toml`/`server.json` version handling (that is
  Option E, parked as idea deficient-eastmost-hoopoe).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/api-stability.md` contains NO `currently <number>` literal of any kind — neither
  the package version nor the schema versions (verify:
  `! grep -Eiq 'currently[* _]*[0-9]' docs/api-stability.md`) — and DOES link to the
  changelog/releases for the version (verify: `grep -Eiq 'CHANGELOG|releases' docs/api-stability.md`).
- [ ] The Event-schema row still names `SCHEMA_VERSION` and its source file but with no
  hard-coded number (verify: `grep -q 'SCHEMA_VERSION' docs/api-stability.md && grep -q '_version.py' docs/api-stability.md`).
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` no longer exists (verify:
  `test ! -e tests/unit/test_version_sync.py`).
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md`: no `test_version_sync` reference remains, its step-1 `git add`
  command no longer stages `docs/api-stability.md`, and no `currently X.Y.Z` literal remains;
  BUT the 1.0-declaration reference to api-stability.md is preserved (verify:
  `! grep -q 'test_version_sync' docs/releasing.md && ! grep -Eq 'git add[^\n]*api-stability' docs/releasing.md && ! grep -Eq 'currently [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' docs/releasing.md && grep -q 'api-stability' docs/releasing.md`).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass (the deleted test is gone; a repo-wide
  `grep -rl 'test_version_sync' --include='*.py'` over `src`/`tests` returns nothing), and the
  change lands on `main` through the Gerrit two-vote gate (`LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`).
baseline.summary: Make API-stability version reference version-agnostic (remove drift-prone marker + test)
