## Why
`rebar review-plan` runs a billable multi-pass LLM review whose only product is a
plan-review claim attestation. Running it on a ticket that cannot be claimed yet — a
terminal/paused status, or an `open` ticket still blocked by an unclosed dependency —
spends the LLM call for nothing (the attestation is unusable) and assesses the plan
against an environment that will change once the blocker lands, forcing a re-review
anyway. Delaying the review until the ticket is claimable is both cheaper and more
correct.

## What
Fast-fail `review-plan` BEFORE any context assembly or LLM pass when the ticket is not
claimable, returning an unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict with no LLM call. `--force`
(library `force=True`, MCP `force`) bypasses the check to review a non-claimable ticket
anyway. `in_progress` tickets are never fast-failed (drift/execution re-reviews stay
legitimate); `bug`/`session_log` stay gate-exempt.

## Scope
- New `rebar.llm.plan_review.claimability` module: a cheap, fail-open claimability
  check (one dep-graph read) plus a shared `indeterminate_verdict` builder that the
  existing plan-relation-snapshot early return also adopts (keeps the package `__init__`
  under the module-size cap).
- Wire the check at the top of `_run_plan_review`, guarded by `force`.
- Surface each indeterminate finding's reason + remediation in the CLI text renderer.
- Documentation for the new behavior across the gate/workflow/exit-code guides.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `review-plan` on an `open` ticket blocked by an unclosed `depends_on`/`blocks`
      prerequisite returns INDETERMINATE with `coverage.llm_ran=false`, a
      `ticket-not-claimable` finding, signs no attestation, and exits 2.
- [ ] `review-plan` on a `closed`/`idea`/`blocked` ticket fast-fails identically.
- [ ] An `in_progress` ticket (even with an open blocker) is NOT fast-failed; the LLM
      review runs.
- [ ] `--force` / `force=True` bypasses the fast-fail and runs the full review.
- [ ] `bug`/`session_log` tickets remain exempt (behavior unchanged).
- [ ] The fast-fail performs no LLM or network call (proven by a runner that raises if
      invoked).

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/claimability.py (new)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py
- src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py
- tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py
- docs/plan-review-gate.md, docs/user-guide.md, docs/workflow-engine.md, docs/exit-codes.md, docs/concurrency.md, AGENTS.md, src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md
baseline.summary: review-plan: fast-fail non-claimable tickets before running the LLM

content.text: ## Why

Chesterton's Fence: "don't remove a fence until you know why it was put up." The plan-review gate has strong ADDITION-side discipline (A1: rule-of-three / YAGNI / NIH / anti-premature-optimization) but NO symmetric REMOVAL-side discipline. An autonomous agent under scope pressure is biased toward "simplifying" by deleting guardrails it does not understand -- exactly the early-trajectory defect this gate exists to catch. This criterion is the removal-side DUAL of A1.

Coverage gap confirmed against current criteria: T4 covers removal's CONSEQUENCES (consumer breakage, reversibility, destructiveness) and E5 partly covers test sync -- but none asks whether the plan UNDERSTANDS why the removed thing existed. You can knowingly tear down a fence with a rollback plan and still not know why it was built, and that passes T4. Net-new gap; NOT in the DSO report (adjacent to but distinct from residual-references / current-vs-future-state).

WS1/WS2 (committed_work_relies_on_unbacked_claim + E4 exclusion scan) verify a removal-justifying CLAIM ("X is unused") -- necessary but NOT sufficient: a fence's purpose is often invisible to a caller-grep. This criterion demands the deeper grounded demonstration.
## What -- new advisory criterion `removal-rationale`

A code-grounded, LLM-routed, ADVISORY criterion (applies_at leaf; err-toward-surfacing, coach-not-block). Two bright-line triggers (a disjunction -- NO subjective "is this incidental?" judgment). Registered in criteria_routing.json with a new reviewers/plan_review_removal_rationale.md prompt.
### Trigger / GATE (else not-applicable -> PASS). Fires if ANY holds:

1. The plan REMOVES or WEAKENS an externally-observable behavior or contract on ANY path -- including failure / timeout / invalid / boundary / exception semantics. CRITICAL: "internal" is defined by observable-behavior PRESERVATION, not file locality. A refactor that changes how errors/failures/timeouts are handled (swallows an error, changes an exception type, retry->fail-fast, shrinks a timeout) is NOT exempt -- failure-mode behavior is outward-facing.

2. The plan removes/weakens a check / test / validation that GUARDS such a behavior. (Tests IN SCOPE; overlap with E5.changed_behavior_tests is resolved by the Pass-4 coaching pass grouping, not by partitioning the criteria.)

3. The plan removes an artifact carrying an EXPLICIT INTENT MARKER: an explanatory comment, a `# do not remove`, a referenced bug/ticket, or a test named after a bug. (Bright, grep-able -- objective, not a vibe.)

### EXEMPT (PASS / not-applicable): dead-code removal, pure internal simplification that preserves ALL observable behavior incl. error/failure semantics, mechanical/config/doc changes with no behavioral delta. rebar values legitimate simplification -- this criterion must never nag it.
### PASS demonstration (the intent: "show we understand what we're changing," NOT "poke holes"):

The plan must supply a concrete TRIGGERING SCENARIO -- the input/condition under which the removed behavior/guard mattered -- GROUNDED in evidence (the explanatory comment / a pinning test / git-blame / linked ticket / a spec-named input class), NOT invented -- plus evidence the reason no longer applies (handled elsewhere / precondition now guaranteed / contract intentionally changed and updated). The scenario is a specification-by-example of the fence (reuses coach move 6).
### Checklist sub-answers (criterion-local -- NOT generic Pass-2 GRADED_BINARY additions, so genericity is preserved):
- gate: `removes_external_behavior_or_guarded_fence` {yes|no|insufficient} (the disjunction above; no -> not-applicable).

- rationale (only meaningful when gated in): `removal_scenario_grounded` {yes|no|insufficient}: "Does the plan give a concrete scenario where the removed behavior/guard mattered, GROUNDED in a comment/test/blame/linked-ticket (not invented), plus evidence the reason no longer applies?"

### FP guards: two bright-line triggers (no incidental-judgment); grounded-scenario requirement blocks fabricated-scenario false-PASS (thoroughness-theater / self-oracle); explicit exemption preserves refactor/cleanup/dead-code.

### Accepted limitation (LOG in coverage, do not hide -- R-3 / no-silent-caps): a purely-latent guard whose removal changes behavior only for inputs never exercised today AND which carries no intent marker will NOT fire -- it is indistinguishable from dead code without external signal, and chasing it is the un-scalable nag we are avoiding.
## Provenance

Labels like A1 / E5 / T4 / R-3 and "WS-N" are provenance tags from the DSO gap-report evaluation + session log brief-bride-rash (95f1-1b3b-a867-4020); Chesterton's Fence itself is a net-new gap surfaced in this session (NOT from ~/dso_rebar_plan_review_gap_report.md). Concrete code targets are in this ticket's file_impact.
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New advisory criterion `removal-rationale` registered in criteria_routing.json (exec 1-TURN or agentic, facet, applies_at leaf, default_posture advisory) + a reviewers/plan_review_removal_rationale.md prompt. Proof: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry validate-routing` exits 0.

- [ ] Gate EXEMPTS dead-code / behavior-preserving internal refactor. Proof: recall case in tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py where such a plan yields not-applicable; `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_evals.py -k removal_rationale_exempt`.
- [ ] Gate FIRES on an internals change that alters error/failure handling (e.g. swallows an exception / retry->fail-fast). Proof: recall case; `pytest ... -k removal_rationale_error_path`.
- [ ] Gate FIRES on removal of an artifact with an explicit intent marker (commented workaround) even with no happy-path delta. Proof: recall case.

- [ ] Rationale sub-answer requires a GROUNDED scenario: a fabricated/ungrounded justification scores low validity. Proof: recall case with an invented scenario asserting low `removal_scenario_grounded`.
- [ ] Advisory posture confirmed (does not block a claim). Proof: verdict on a triggering ticket is advisory, not block.
- [ ] Coaching reuses move 6 (specification-by-example) to ask for the grounded scenario; E5 test-removal overlap is grouped by the coaching pass (recall case where both fire and coach groups them).
- [ ] The latent-guard limitation is documented in docs/plan-review-gate.md and recorded in the criterion's coverage.
- [ ] docs/plan-review-gate.md documents removal-rationale as the removal-side dual of A1.

baseline.summary: WS11: removal-rationale criterion (Chesterton's Fence, removal-side dual of A1)

content.text: ## Why
While implementing the plan-review gate (epic 5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa) we reuse three load-bearing
subsystems — the HMAC signing/attestation surface (`rebar.signing`), the LLM workflow runtime
(`rebar.llm.runner` / `rebar.llm.workflow` executor), and the prompt/contract model
(`rebar.llm.prompts`). These are documented at the FRAMEWORK / USAGE / EVENT level
(`docs/llm-framework.md`, `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/workflow-authoring-v2.md`) but there is
no single developer-facing API REFERENCE describing the reuse surface itself — the exact
function signatures, return shapes, invariants, and extension seams — for the next agent that
needs to build ON this machinery (as the plan-review gate does). This ticket creates that
reference, for both human and LLM audiences.
## What / Scope
A new doc (or docs) that FULLY describe, as a reuse/extension reference:
1. **The signing surface (`src/rebar/signing.py`)** — `sign_manifest`, `verify_signature`,
`verify_record`, `signing_key`, `key_fingerprint`, `compute_signature`, `parse_manifest`,
`head_sha`; the manifest format, the HMAC-SHA256 + PAYLOAD_VERSION canonicalisation, the
environment-key custody model (`REBAR_SIGNING_KEY` / `.signing-key`), the
certified|mismatch|foreign_key|unsigned verdict vocabulary, the SIGNATURE event +
last-writer-wins replay, and the head_sha staleness binding. Document the close-gate
consumption pattern AND how a NEW gate (e.g. plan-review at claim) reuses it.
2. **The LLM workflow runtime (`rebar.llm.runner`, `rebar.llm.workflow` executor)** — the
`Runner` protocol (`run`/`preflight`), `RunRequest` (every field incl. `mode`,
`execution_mode`, `output_schema`, `extra_tools`), `get_runner`, the PydanticAI runner, the
structured-output stack (`structured.py`), and `run_workflow` (the declarative-IR executor:
inputs/run_id/dry_run, RunResult, step kinds). Cover BOTH single-call operations (like
`verify_completion`) AND declarative workflows — even parts not used by plan review.
3. **The prompt/contract model (`rebar.llm.prompts`)** — `get_prompt`, `resolve_prompt`, the
front-matter closed-key contract (inputs/outputs schema-names, execution_mode, category),
`.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override resolution, the derived prompt index + CI drift gate, and
how to add a new reviewer/prompt with a structured output contract.
4. **The output-schema/contract seam (`rebar.llm.findings`, packaged JSON Schemas)** — how an
operation declares its own `output_schema`, where schemas live, validation
(`validate_structured`), citation resolution, and finding normalization.
Audience: both human developers and LLM agents. Cross-link from `docs/llm-framework.md` and
`CLAUDE.md`. This is documentation only — no behavior changes.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A developer-facing API reference exists (new doc under `docs/`, e.g. `docs/reuse-surface.md`,
or focused additions to existing docs) covering the signing surface, the LLM workflow
RUNTIME api (runner + workflow executor), the prompt/contract model, and the output-schema
seam — each with exact function signatures and return shapes.
- [ ] The signing section documents the manifest format, HMAC/PAYLOAD_VERSION canonicalisation,
the environment-key custody model, the verdict vocabulary
(certified|mismatch|foreign_key|unsigned), the head_sha staleness binding, and a worked
example of a NEW gate reusing `sign_manifest`/`verify_signature` (not just the close gate).
- [ ] The LLM-runtime section documents the `Runner` protocol, every `RunRequest` field, the
structured-output contract path, and `run_workflow` declarative execution — including parts
not used by the plan-review epic.
- [ ] The prompt/contract section documents `get_prompt`/`resolve_prompt`, the front-matter
closed-key contract, `.rebar/prompts/` override resolution, and adding a new reviewer/prompt.
- [ ] Written for BOTH human and LLM audiences (concrete signatures + copy-pasteable examples).
- [ ] Cross-linked from `docs/llm-framework.md` and listed in `CLAUDE.md`'s docs pointers.
- [ ] Each documented signature/return shape is verified against the current source by an
AUTOMATED drift-check test (`tests/unit/test_reuse_surface_doc.py`, run in CI) that
introspects each documented callable — not manual inspection.
- [ ] The output-schema/contract seam section (scope item 4) documents `validate_structured`,
`contracts.register_contract`/`response_model_for`, where the packaged JSON Schemas live,
and citation resolution + finding normalization (`rebar.llm.findings`).

baseline.summary: Document reusable machinery API reference: signing surface, LLM workflow runtime, prompt/contract model

## Why
Incident 2731's trigger commit (10837ca88) shipped the code_review artifact feature, but it was inert in prod: the box's .env had no REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_* vars. autodeploy.sh rsync-excludes infra/compose/.env (line 88) and never re-runs fetch-secrets.sh, so NO newly-added SSM-backed env key can reach the box on deploy without a manual boot — a half-updated-deploy-path defect.

## Status
AC1 (artifacts emitted from prod reviews) is DONE and proven in prod (see comments: SSM slot populated, terraform state reconciled, fetch-secrets re-run by hand, end-to-end artifact 8e68 emitted on change 492, 2026-07-10). The SSM/terraform work was OPERATIONAL and is already complete; note the slot /rebar/prod/reviewbot-tickets-pat already exists in infra/terraform/ssm.tf (rebar_secret_params, ~line 49) with lifecycle{ignore_changes=[value]}, so 'terraform apply' is a NO-OP for its value — the operative provisioning step was 'aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite --name /rebar/prod/reviewbot-tickets-pat --type SecureString --value <PAT>', NOT terraform. This is recorded for accuracy; no terraform/SSM work remains.

## Remaining work (AC2 — the only code change)
Make autodeploy re-run fetch-secrets.sh before 'docker compose up' so new/rotated SSM-backed env keys reach the review-bot container on deploy without a manual boot.

Precise design (in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh):
- Add a dedicated trigger SECRETS_PATHS='infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh infra/terraform/ssm.tf'. Rationale: a new env key requires editing fetch-secrets.sh (to emit the leaf) and/or ssm.tf (to declare the param); NEITHER is in BOT_PATHS, so keying the refresh only off BOT_PATHS would miss exactly the env-only-change scenario AC2 names. (Pure SSM VALUE rotation with no git change is out of scope: main does not advance, so autodeploy no-ops — that path is operator-triggered, not deploy-triggered.)
- Guard the existing review-bot redeploy block on: changed BOT_PATHS OR changed SECRETS_PATHS (so a secrets-only change still recreates the container to pick up the new .env).
- Placement: AFTER the rsync+chown (so $DEPLOY_REPO holds the TARGET fetch-secrets.sh) and BEFORE the ':prev' tag / 'docker compose build && up'. Invoke ENV_FILE="$COMPOSE_DIR/.env" bash "$DEPLOY_REPO/infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh"; then re-assert the preserved .env owner.
- Error contract (preserves autodeploy's fail-safe, never-half-updated guarantee): fetch-secrets is fail-fast — on any SSM error it exits 1 WITHOUT touching .env. On that failure, emit an err 'secrets-fetch-failed' marker, record_backoff_failure, and exit 1 — abort the deploy BEFORE tagging :prev or building, so the running bot stays on its current image (:latest untouched, nothing to roll back). Never build/up against a stale or half-written secrets file. Runs only on an actual bot/secrets redeploy (not every 2-min tick), so no SSM quota regression.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] code_review artifacts are written + pushed from prod reviews (no 'emission failed' warnings). [DONE in prod — change 492 / artifact 8e68]
- [ ] autodeploy.sh re-runs fetch-secrets.sh before 'docker compose up' on a BOT_PATHS OR SECRETS_PATHS change; a new SSM-backed env key reaches the box on deploy without a manual boot.
- [ ] On fetch-secrets failure the deploy aborts fail-safe (err marker + backoff, .env intact, running bot untouched, no rollback needed).
- [ ] Tests cover: (a) fetch-secrets runs before compose up on a secrets-only change; (b) fetch-secrets failure aborts the deploy without building.
- [ ] File paths: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (the code change); infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh, infra/terraform/ssm.tf (referenced/triggering, unchanged).

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- Least-privilege PAT swap (broad classic repo-scope -> fine-grained contents:write only): human-mintable only; recommended, tracked separately.
- Bug d220 (entrypoint clone write-dead on a FRESH volume): separate ticket; prod volume already converged.

## Why

The project-specific criterion and coaching move are intended to be a concrete client example of the supported extension boundary. Documentation must show the composition accurately without making project moves appear to be packaged built-ins.

## What

Document the rebar portability guard in a separate project-extension subsection, add a structural documentation test, and run the complete repository regression gates after all implementation children land.

## Scope

In scope:

- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
- `tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py`
- final repository lint, typecheck, and test verification

Out of scope:

- changing criterion, move, verifier, or disposition behavior
- documenting the project move inside the parsed built-in move table
- remediating pre-existing portability debt

## Approach

First update the existing `**Project-extensible:**` paragraph so its schema reads `{move_id: {name, template, applies_when?}}` and states that absent or empty `applies_when` is always applicable while a non-empty list intersects active criterion triggers. Then add `### Dogfooding a project portability guard` immediately after that paragraph and before `### The advisory cap`. The structural placement anchor is the end of the existing sentence `never hand over a solution.`; this location is deliberately outside the built-in move table parsed by `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_move_registry_matches_docs_table`.

The subsection is the client-facing composition example and contains:

- the exact `project.portability` `plan_review` routing entry with `exec: 1-TURN`, `facet: project-invariants`, `applies_at.scope: [container, leaf]`, `default_posture: blocking`, `block_threshold: 0.9`, plus `activate: [project.portability]`;
- the prompt path `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`, `execution_mode: single_turn`, the four exact rubric headings, plus the typed field mapping from `immune-floury-toad`;
- the four supported shape dimensions with all values specified by the finder child;
- the exact rules `Silence about portability is not a finding` plus `Project-specific behavior behind project configuration or an explicit extension boundary is allowed`;
- the exact `project-portability` move id, name, `applies_when`, plus locked template from `truthful-specified-silverfish`;
- the balanced eight-case eval path with exact release thresholds `recall: 1.0`, `false_accept: 0.0`, `agreement: 1.0`, per-case `stability >= 0.6666666667`, plus expected-vs-observed fire/no-fire `kappa >= 0.70`;
- the responsibility split: Pass 1 discovers a cited concrete counterexample, unchanged Pass 2 verifies validity/impact, unchanged Pass 3 decides disposition, Pass 4 consumes the project move for surviving findings.

This one subsection is the durable dogfood example requested by the epic; it does not restate generic architecture in a new ADR. The structural test reads the real document, locates the subsection by its exact heading, verifies all literals, then proves its byte range begins after the end of `never hand over a solution.` and ends before `### The advisory cap`.

## Grounding

`docs/plan-review-gate.md` already documents the built-in Pass-4 table at `### The Pass-4 move registry` plus the project extension paragraph immediately after it. `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_move_registry_matches_docs_table` extracts only numeric-id table rows and requires exact parity with packaged `MOVE_REGISTRY`; placing a hyphenated project id in a separate subsection preserves that parser contract. The parent experiment explicitly confirmed this placement decision.

## Dependencies

Depends on the criterion, coaching, and calibration children so the documentation describes the final validated behavior rather than an intermediate design.

## Test Strategy

Use a focused structural documentation test for required examples and placement, then run all repository gates from the fresh worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The existing project-extension paragraph documents `{move_id: {name, template, applies_when?}}`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py -k project_move_schema`.
- [ ] The existing project-extension paragraph defines absent, empty, plus non-empty `applies_when` behavior. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py -k project_move_schema`.
- [ ] The guide contains the exact heading `### Dogfooding a project portability guard`. Prove with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_project_portability_docs.py -k subsection_heading`.

baseline.description:
# Cut the v0.8.0 release (minor bump)

Cut the next release of `nava-rebar`, incrementing the **minor** version `0.7.1 -> 0.8.0`,
using the new dispatch-from-`main` release-authorization workflow (story fd84). Bump every
version manifest + enforced doc marker in lockstep, promote the curated CHANGELOG
`[Unreleased]` section to `[0.8.0]`, correct the release runbook to the Gerrit landing flow,
land the change on `main` through the Gerrit two-vote gate, then dispatch `release.yml` from
`main` with `version=0.8.0` and drive it to a completed publish.

## Why

`main` is at `0.7.1`; the accumulated user-facing changes in `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`
warrant a release. Pre-1.0 SemVer permits breaking changes in a minor bump, so `0.8.0` is
correct. The new `release.yml` only publishes from a `workflow_dispatch`-on-`main` run whose
`authorize` job asserts version-lockstep, so the manifests must equal the dispatch `version`
input on `main` before the run. Separately, `docs/releasing.md` step 1 still documents the
**old** `git push origin main` flow, which contradicts this repo's Gerrit-only landing rule
(direct pushes to `main` are rejected) — the runbook must be corrected as part of cutting a
release correctly.

## What / Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — `[project].version` `0.7.1` -> `0.8.0`.
- `server.json` — top-level `version` and `packages[0].version` -> `0.8.0`.
- `docs/api-stability.md` — the prose marker `currently 0.7.1` -> `currently 0.8.0`. This is
  **enforced**: `tests/unit/test_version_sync.py` asserts the doc marker equals
  `pyproject.toml`'s version, so a missed bump fails `make test` and blocks the Gerrit
  `Verified` vote.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — retitle `## [Unreleased]` to `## [0.8.0] - <landing date>` and open a fresh
  empty `## [Unreleased]` above it; update the footer reference links (add
  `[0.8.0]: .../compare/v0.7.1...v0.8.0`, retarget `[unreleased]` to `.../compare/v0.8.0...HEAD`).
  The section is already hand-curated so no `git-cliff` regeneration is needed. The date is
  set from the actual commit date at commit time (`git log -1 --format=%as`), not hardcoded.
- `docs/releasing.md` — correct the release runbook to the Gerrit flow: step 1 must **not**
  say `git push origin main`; instead bump + commit with the `rebar-ticket:`/DCO trailers and
  land through Gerrit (`git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`, earn `LLM-Review +1` AND
  `Verified +1`, then Submit), consistent with the "Release-source authorization" section and
  CONTRIBUTING.md. Fix any other step that implies a direct push to `main`.
- Land the one commit on `main` via Gerrit, then dispatch `release.yml --ref main -f
  version=0.8.0`, approve the `pypi` required-reviewer gate, and monitor to completion. No
  workflow/product-code logic changes — this is a release cut plus a runbook correction.

## Failure recovery (release is partly irreversible)

PyPI is immutable: a published `0.8.0` can only be **yanked**, never replaced — a bad release
is fixed by yanking + cutting `0.8.1`. If a run publishes to PyPI but a later job
(`github_release`/`mcp_registry`) fails, do **not** re-dispatch the whole workflow (it would
re-attempt the already-done PyPI publish); re-run only the failed job, or complete it manually
(`gh release create v0.8.0 …` / re-run the mcp publish step), since PyPI/MCP versions are
idempotent-by-existence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pyproject.toml` `[project].version == "0.8.0"` (verify:
  `python -c "import tomllib;assert tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['project']['version']=='0.8.0'"`).
- [ ] `server.json` top-level `version` and every `packages[].version` == `"0.8.0"` (verify:
  `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('server.json'));assert d['version']=='0.8.0' and all(p['version']=='0.8.0' for p in d['packages'])"`).
- [ ] `docs/api-stability.md` prose marker reads `currently 0.8.0` (verify:
  `grep -q 'currently 0.8.0' docs/api-stability.md`).
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## [0.8.0]` section AND a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` above it
  AND a `[0.8.0]:` footer link (verify:
  `awk '/^## \[Unreleased\]/{u=NR}/^## \[0\.8\.0\]/{v=NR}END{exit !(u>0 && v>u)}' CHANGELOG.md && grep -q '^\[0.8.0\]:' CHANGELOG.md`).
- [ ] `docs/releasing.md` no longer instructs a direct push to `main` for a release and
  documents the Gerrit landing flow (verify:
  `! grep -q 'git push origin main' docs/releasing.md && grep -q 'refs/for/main' docs/releasing.md`).
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass locally (incl. `test_version_sync`), and
  `python -m build && python -m twine check dist/*` succeed on the bumped tree.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The commit lands on `main` through the Gerrit two-vote gate
  (`LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`) — attested by recording the Gerrit change URL + both
  vote outcomes/timestamps as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `release.yml` is dispatched from `main` with `version=0.8.0`; the
  `authorize` job passes all four guards and the run completes with `publish`,
  `github_release`, and `mcp_registry` all successful — attested by the workflow run URL + job
  conclusions recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] PyPI serves `nava-rebar 0.8.0` (verify:
  `test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/0.8.0/json)" = 200`).
- [ ] [operator-attested] A GitHub Release `v0.8.0` (Latest, sdist+wheel attached) + tag exist
  (`gh release view v0.8.0 --repo navapbc/rebar`) and the MCP registry lists `0.8.0` — the
  outcomes recorded as a comment on this ticket.

## Outcome
Landed as Gerrit change 1217 at merged commit `750a56b3b004f3c3f4cc1b456d3c56bd7809b87d`. `BindingStore.set_baseline` now filters the five mirrored fields, preserves keys whose value is `None`, returns early when the stored baseline is equal, and never reads the clock or writes `baseline_advanced_at`. This execution-state record supersedes planning-time line references while preserving the original rationale and acceptance contract.

## Planning-time root cause and measured value
Before A1, `set_baseline` unconditionally replaced `entry["baseline"]` and stamped `baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso()`. The stamp had no production reader. Across the original 40-revision study, baseline values changed 0 entries while the stamp changed 1,144 entries in a sort-ordered ~18 MB file, producing pathological git delta churn. The write-when-changed guard is byte-neutral for that historical corpus; the measured packed-cost win is from retiring the volatile stamp. Planning evidence lives in session log `1cb6-d553-6565-49b4`.

## Implemented behavior and call sites
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py:451-466` owns filtering, equality comparison, early return, and changed-value assignment.
- `BindingStore.seed_baselines_from_snapshot` begins at `binding_store.py:468` and delegates through the same guarded method.
- `reconcile._advance_baselines` begins at `reconcile.py:520` and needs no caller edit because the guard is centralized.
- The inbound-adopt dynamic call is at `apply_inbound_records.py:257-260` and receives the same centralized behavior.
- Historical serialized stamp keys are inert; cleanup of cache history/current cache artifacts belongs to the parent epic rollout and rewrite, not to a new production reader or migration in A1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state preserve byte-identical `bindings.json`. Proved by `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head`.
- [x] The same integration test preserves the tracker HEAD, proving the unchanged second pass creates no commit. Run with `pytest tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head`.
- [x] Exact identifier search finds no production reference: `grep -Rnw baseline_advanced_at src/rebar` returns no match.
- [x] Every new baseline written by `set_baseline` omits `baseline_advanced_at`; unit tests fail fast if baseline writes read the clock. Proved in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`.
- [x] A present-but-null baseline field round-trips as present. Proved by `test_present_null_baseline_field_round_trips`.
- [x] A changed baseline persists the new value and changes serialized bytes, so the guard cannot degenerate into never-write. Proved by `test_changed_baseline_updates_serialized_bytes`.
- [x] Repeated `seed_baselines_from_snapshot` input preserves serialized bytes, and the inbound-adopt path retains its existing focused coverage.
- [x] The complete repository suite is green: `make test` passed with 8,519 passed, 39 skipped, and 175 deselected; `make lint` and `make typecheck` passed.
- [x] [operator-attested] Marginal packed cost over the frozen 40-SHA corpus is at most 25% of baseline. Operator evidence on this ticket records the exact corpus, transformation, serializer, repack flags, pack byte counts, formula, and result: 13.84 KiB/version before versus 2.33 KiB/version after (16.8%).
- [x] [operator-attested] Gerrit change 1217 received `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`, then merged without unresolved comments.

## Files
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — implementation.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — read-only caller context.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — read-only dynamic caller context.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py` — unit/serialization oracle.
- `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py` — stateful-fake git-backed E2E oracle.

Scope: completed A1 only; standalone follow-up story `deeb-89c1-1080-4690` owns plan-review evidence-kind classification.

content.text: ## Summary
archived is an inescapable status: reopen/transition/claim all fail, and the engine's own recovery hint is a command its own validator rejects.
## Reproduction Steps
(verified on installed 0.4.0 == HEAD, temp store)
1. rebar archive <id>
2. rebar reopen <id> -> exit 10, hint: "Re-run: ticket transition <id> archived open"
3. rebar transition <id> archived open -> exit 1: invalid current_status 'archived'. Must be one of: open, in_progress, closed, blocked
4. rebar transition <id> open (auto-detect) -> exit 1 (auto-detect feeds 'archived' into the same validator)
5. rebar claim <id> -> exit 10. grep -rni unarchive src/ -> nothing.
## Expected vs Actual
- Expected: a working unarchive path, or at minimum a recovery hint that succeeds when executed verbatim.
- Actual: no CLI path out of archived; the suggested command always fails.
## Source
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket_txn.py:76 — hint built from actual_status verbatim even when it is not a legal current_status.
- src/rebar/_engine/ticket-transition.sh:121-146 — _validate_status whitelist open|in_progress|closed|blocked.
## Fix direction

Add an unarchive path (and/or accept archived as current_status for archived->open). NOTE: archive mechanics involve a marker (.archived) in addition to status — the validated mechanism details (event vs marker, list reappearance, claimability) are in the implementation-notes comment; follow it.
## Suggested RED test
archive -> reopen (or the emitted hint, executed verbatim) succeeds; ticket reappears in default list and is claimable. Hint text always names an executable command.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A documented CLI path returns an archived ticket to open (RED test first)
- [ ] After unarchive: visible in default list, claimable, fsck clean
- [ ] ticket_txn hint never suggests a command the validator rejects
- [ ] transition/archive suites green

baseline.description:
## Root cause — PROVEN by captured request + live A/B, not inferred

The only `cache_control` breakpoint rebar places is on the SYSTEM-prompt block (plus tool definitions). At both failing call sites that block is tiny and the real payload rides in the USER message, AFTER the breakpoint, unmarked. Anthropic silently declines to cache a sub-minimum marked prefix: no error, `cache_creation=0`, `cache_read=0`.

`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:333-355` — `cache_settings_for` sets only `anthropic_cache_instructions` and `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions`; its own docstring states "neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched". In pydantic-ai those flags mark only the last system block and the last tool.

CAPTURED OUTBOUND REQUESTS (httpx transport wrapped at the `anthropic_model.py:95-161` seam, real config/runner/prompts, body dumped before it left the process):

    coach_notes            system[0]  ~150 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6928 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0
    enrich/ticket-digest   system[0]  ~477 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6326 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0

LIVE A/B isolating prefix SIZE from every other variable — identical marker, identical large user message, only the marked-prefix size varies:

    haiku-4-5    1193 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    2748 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    4749 tok -> w=4742 r=4742    CACHED
    sonnet-4-5    253 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    sonnet-4-5   7930 tok -> w=7923           CACHED

Empirical floor sits between 2748 and 4749 for BOTH models. rebar marks 150 and 477.

WHY THE PASS-1 FINDERS CACHE FINE in the same process: `plan_review/passes.py` returns `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + body` for `PASS_FINDER`, putting a multi-thousand-token prefix in the SYSTEM slot — those are the 5781-9385 cache_write rows in the same run.

Contributing detail for coach_notes: `reviewers/plan_review_coach.md:20` places `<!--volatile-->` two lines from the end, so `resolve_prompt_cached` leaves only ~9 lines of stance prose in the system slot and routes `{{plan}}` to the user message.

## Rejected hypotheses

* "No breakpoint is placed" — REJECTED: the captured request shows `cache_control` on `system[0]` in
  both cases.
* "The prefix is unstable between calls" — REJECTED twice: `cache_write=0` means no write was ever
  ATTEMPTED, and an unstable-but-marked prefix still writes on every call; separately the marked block
  is byte-stable by construction.
* "Provider-side caching unavailable" — REJECTED: finders cached in the same process, same provider.

## The two sites are NOT the same problem

* `coach_notes` is genuine RECOVERABLE bleed. The plan is ALREADY in the cache, written by the Pass-1
  finders that carry it in the system prefix. The coach re-sends the same plan in a different slot, so
  it cannot hit that entry and re-pays full price every run.
* `enrich`/ticket-digest is different in kind. Its ~6.3k user payload is one ticket's text, unique per
  call, so even a message-level breakpoint would only ever WRITE, never READ. There is no reusable
  prefix at that site at all — a naive fix there ADDS cost.

## A separate, sharper defect this exposed in the warning itself

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) compares total `input_tokens` against `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, but what actually governs caching is the MARKED PREFIX size. The two warnings observed were true positives only by coincidence of the totals clearing 4096. The same predicate applied to the marked prefix (150 / 477) would have named the cause directly instead of merely flagging a symptom. Note also that 4096 is roughly right for sonnet-4-5 and haiku-4-5 too, so the "OPUS floor" comment understates its generality.

## The obvious fix is DISPROVEN — do not retry it

The earlier remedy in this ticket (place the breakpoint at the `cache_settings_for` seam via `anthropic_cache_messages` or `anthropic_cache`, with a guard excluding no-reusable-prefix sites) was implemented up to the point of disproof and REJECTED on evidence:

* BOTH mechanisms mark AFTER THE ENTIRE MESSAGE LIST. `anthropic_cache_messages` routes to
  `_apply_message_cache_control`, which marks "the last content block of the LAST MESSAGE";
  `anthropic_cache` reaches the same function on the Bedrock/Vertex fallback path. So the marked span
  always ENDS with per-call-unique bytes — for `coach_notes` the run's surviving-findings list appended
  after `{{plan}}` by `resolve_prompt_cached`, for `enrich` the ticket text.
* That makes both sites WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The guard would therefore have to exclude BOTH,
  making the change inert rather than narrow.
* THE RECOVERY PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG. This ticket previously asserted `coach_notes` could hit the
  cache entry the Pass-1 finders write. It cannot: the finders' entry is keyed on a system block of
  `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body`, while the coach's system block is its own stance prose. The
  two requests diverge at the FIRST SYSTEM BYTE, so no coach request in any slot can read that entry.
* `coach_notes` is a SINGLE step behind `branch: coach_gate` — one call per gate run, not a loop. So
  even a correct breakpoint only ever reads if a PREVIOUS gate run wrote the same prefix within the
  5-minute TTL.

## What a real fix would require

A read needs a breakpoint BEFORE the volatile tail — `pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint`, which is a `RunRequest` content-list change the current design deliberately avoids — PLUS a plan-review-wide shared-prefix redesign so the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with the finders. Both are larger than this ticket as originally scoped, and the second changes a precision-sensitive prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] FIRST, AND GATING THE REST: the recoverable saving is QUANTIFIED before any redesign is
      committed to. Measure what a correct breakpoint would actually recover for `coach_notes` given
      that it fires once per gate run and the cache TTL is 5 minutes — i.e. the realistic cross-run hit
      rate, not the per-call token count. `enrich`/ticket-digest is excluded from this measurement (see
      below).
- [x] REWORDED to be verifiable — the original was self-referential and could never pass; see the
      comment "THE ORIGINAL WORDING OF THIS CRITERION DEADLOCKED THE CLOSE GATE". The verifiable
      requirement: the measurement is RECORDED on this ticket, and the won't-fix decision is
      DOCUMENTED with its rationale, so a reader can see why the fix was not pursued. The act of
      closing is the OUTCOME this criterion authorises, not a condition to be verified before it.
      ORIGINAL WORDING: "If the measured saving does NOT justify a `CachePoint` migration plus a
      shared-prefix redesign, the correct outcome is to CLOSE THIS AS WON'T-FIX with the measurement
      recorded. That is an acceptable and expected result, not a failure — the cheap fix is
      disproven and the expensive one may not earn its cost."
- [x] `enrich`/ticket-digest is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for caching and recorded as such: its payload
      is one ticket's unique text per call, so it can only ever WRITE, never READ. Adding a breakpoint
      there would ADD cost. This is written down so a future reader does not "complete" the fix by
      including it.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: the breakpoint is placed BEFORE the per-call-volatile tail, and a test
      asserts the MARKED SPAN ENDS BEFORE the first per-call-unique byte. A test that merely asserts
      "a cache breakpoint exists" passes for the wrong reason — that was already true when the bug was
      filed.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with whatever writes the entry it is
      meant to read, demonstrated by a captured request pair showing a common marked prefix — because
      without that a write is never read and the change is inert.
- [x] SATISFIED BY ticket e3cd (commit 25f5146dc0): `warn_if_cache_ineffective` now measures the MARKED
      PREFIX against that model's floor rather than total `input_tokens`, and names the cause. Do not
      re-implement this here — that is the duplicate-mechanism trap.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: [operator-attested] a real run after the fix shows nonzero cache_READ (not
      merely cache_write) for `coach_notes`, cited from REBAR_USAGE_LOG with run sha and timestamp. A
      write alone proves nothing here, since write-only is the defect.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
baseline.summary: Two plan-review sub-calls request prompt caching and receive none, paying full input price on every run

# Class config schema and resolver

## Context / Problem
rebar has no way to express "which model for which capability tier". `cfg.model` is a single scalar, so every per-pass decision is inferred (see the parent's problem statement). Nothing can be wired to classes until the classes exist and can be resolved.

## Approach
Add three config slots — `trivial`, `standard`, `frontier` — parsed from the EXISTING layered config (`config.py:388-398`: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > config file > default). Each slot accepts `model`, `provider`, `endpoint`, and an optional `fallback` array; the array is PARSED and carried now but not yet consumed (its runtime wiring is a sibling ticket), so the schema does not need a second migration later.

Expose one resolver: class name -> provider-qualified model string. It reuses `infer_provider` (`config.py:344`) when `provider` is omitted, so a slot naming only `model = "claude-opus-4-8"` keeps working exactly as a bare id does today.

Secrets stay env-only: a slot MUST NOT accept an `api_key`, mirroring the existing rule that secrets are not config-file keys.

**Per-class defaults, when a slot is unset.** The defaults ARE today's values, so an operator who configures nothing gets byte-identical behaviour to the current release — which is also this work's rollback story:

| class | default | where it comes from today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frontier` | `claude-opus-4-8` | `config.py:39` `DEFAULT_MODEL` |
| `standard` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `config.py:45` `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`, documented as "the decisive NON-FRONTIER model" |
| `trivial` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `plan-review.yaml:62-65`, the `model_ladder` entry rung |

Each default is a BARE id, so it resolves through `infer_provider` exactly as it does today. No default names a provider, so configuring nothing cannot silently pin an operator to one.

**How the flat env layer addresses a structured slot.** `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` is scalar by construction, so a nested slot is addressed by FIELD, one env var per field: `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_ENDPOINT`, and the same for `STANDARD_` and `TRIVIAL_`. This keeps the existing precedence rule intact per key (CLI > env > config file > default) rather than inventing a merge rule for whole objects.

**The `fallback` sub-object schema.** A fallback entry is a PROVIDER TARGET carrying exactly the same fields as a class slot, minus `fallback` itself:

| field | required | type | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | YES | string | a bare id or a provider-qualified one, same as a slot's `model` |
| `provider` | no | string | omitted -> `infer_provider`, identical to slot behaviour |
| `endpoint` | no | string | omitted -> the provider's default endpoint |
| `api_key` | FORBIDDEN | — | rejected loudly, same secrets boundary as the slot |

**It is NON-RECURSIVE**: a fallback entry MUST NOT itself carry a `fallback` key, and one that does is a typed config error. The chain is already an ordered list, so nesting adds no expressiveness while introducing cycle risk and an unbounded resolution depth. A slot with no `fallback` key and a slot with `fallback = []` are the same thing: no fallbacks.

This ticket PARSES and VALIDATES that shape and carries it on the resolved record; CONSUMING it at runtime is task cc33.

`fallback` is deliberately CONFIG-FILE-ONLY and has no env form, because encoding an array of objects in a scalar env var would mean inventing a serialization format. An environment needing a fallback chain uses `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` — which **does NOT exist yet**; it is delivered by sibling task cb6f. Until cb6f lands there is no environment-only way to set a fallback chain, and that is accepted: this ticket's job is the schema, not the delivery mechanism.

**Alternative rejected — a new config file/discovery path.** Forks the precedence chain and duplicates the loader; the `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointer that cb6f will add is the escape hatch instead.

**THE INTEGRATION POINT — who calls the parser.** `parse_class_slots` takes an already-loaded mapping, which leaves open who hands it the real config. That entry point is `model_classes.load_class_slots(repo_root=None)`, in the SAME new module:

    def load_class_slots(repo_root=None) -> dict[str, ClassSlot]:
        from rebar.llm.config import _read_llm_file_table
        return parse_class_slots(_read_llm_file_table(repo_root).get("model_classes"))

`_read_llm_file_table` (`config.py:401`) already returns the merged `[tool.rebar.llm]` table (user < project) and already degrades to `{}` on a malformed core config, so a broken pyproject cannot break an LLM op — that failure mode is inherited, not re-invented.

It lives in `model_classes.py`, NOT in `config.py`, for two reasons: config.py has 23 lines of headroom, and `LLMConfig` does not need to carry the slots — consumers (tasks 172e, 7761, cc33) call `load_class_slots()` directly. Putting it here also keeps the config import edge one-way.

Without this named entry point the schema would be unreachable from real configuration — a parser nothing calls. That is what the second plan review correctly blocked on after the scope was narrowed to keep config.py under its cap.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` — NEW leaf module: the three slots, the `fallback` entry schema,
  their validation, the resolver, AND the `load_class_slots()` entry point that reads the real
  config table. **Not `config.py`**: that file is at 777 of the 800-LOC hard
  cap (23 lines of headroom) and this schema is far larger than that, so putting it there is not
  landable — the same saturation ticket 1484 just relieved elsewhere. The new module imports
  `infer_provider` / `DEFAULT_MODEL` / `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` FROM `config.py` and `config.py` does
  NOT import it back, so the edge is one-way and no cycle is possible.
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — only the env-var docstring block for the nine new vars, if the
  generator reads it. Any larger change here means the split above was not respected.
- `tests/unit/` — new tests for parsing and resolution.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — REGENERATED in this change. The nine new per-field env vars
  (`REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}`) necessarily appear in the
  generator's output, so the committed file must be updated here or the drift gate fails.

## Testing
Unit tier: pure config parsing and string resolution, no model calls, no network.
- happy path: a slot with model+provider resolves to `provider:model`.
- omitted provider: resolves via `infer_provider`, matching today's bare-id behaviour.
- unset slot: resolves to the documented default for that class.
- a slot carrying `api_key` is REJECTED loudly (the secrets boundary).
- a `fallback` array parses and is carried on the record without being consumed.
- a `fallback` entry is validated to the slot-minus-fallback schema: `api_key` rejected, a nested
  `fallback` rejected, an omitted `provider` inferred.
- `fallback = []` and an absent `fallback` key produce the same resolved record (no fallbacks).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts each of the three class names resolves to a provider-qualified model string
- [ ] a test asserts that with NO class configured, `frontier`/`standard`/`trivial` resolve to
      `claude-opus-4-8`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`/`claude-haiku-4-5` respectively — i.e. today's behaviour
      is preserved bit-for-bit when nothing is configured
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL` overrides the config-file value for that slot's
      `model` field only, leaving the slot's other fields intact
- [ ] a test asserts a slot omitting `provider` resolves identically to today's bare-id behaviour
- [ ] a test asserts a slot containing `api_key` raises a typed rebar config error naming the secrets rule
- [ ] a test asserts a parsed `fallback` array is carried on the resolved record
- [ ] a test asserts `load_class_slots()` reads the `model_classes` sub-table from the merged
      `[tool.rebar.llm]` config and returns resolved slots — proving the parser is REACHABLE from
      real configuration and not an orphan
- [ ] a test asserts `load_class_slots()` returns the documented defaults when the config file has
      no `model_classes` table at all (the inherited degrade-to-empty path)
- [ ] a test asserts a `fallback` entry carrying `api_key` raises a typed rebar config error (the
      secrets boundary applies to ENTRIES, not only to slots)
- [ ] a test asserts a NESTED `fallback` (an entry itself carrying a `fallback` key) raises a typed
      rebar config error naming the non-recursive rule
- [ ] a test asserts a `fallback` entry omitting `provider` resolves via `infer_provider`, identically
      to a slot that omits it
- [ ] `docs/env-vars.md` is REGENERATED AND COMMITTED in this change, and the regenerated file lists
      all nine `REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}` vars; re-running the
      generator afterwards then produces no diff, which is what the drift gate actually checks
baseline.summary: Class config schema and resolver

baseline.description:
## Context

Three production Jira-sync bugs escaped our tests this cycle, all the same CLASS — a gap at a *seam* that no test or probe spanned:

- **Inbound comments (bug 0ee6):** the inbound differ read snapshot key `comments`, but the fetcher writes the nested Jira-REST key `comment` — producer and consumer were unit-tested in isolation, so their shared shape was never jointly exercised.
- **Issue-links both directions (bug 3f04):** outbound link dispatch existed only in a *typed-leaf* applier that production does not use (production routes through the *batch* applier, which dropped links); inbound links were invisible because the snapshot never carried `issuelinks`.
- **A live e2e probe encoded the inbound-comment bug as EXPECTED** (`Phase3.verify-inbound-comments-gap … NOT-SYNCED`), so the defect could never be detected.

Root causes: (1) no producer↔consumer contract — differs are unit-tested against hand-built snapshot dicts in shapes the real fetcher never emits; (2) two outbound applier paths drift (tests cover the dead typed leaf; production uses the batch path; capabilities were re-added one bug at a time — parent 8b25, comments 87e4, links 3f04); (3) sub-op success is silent (the batch outcome reports mutation-level `error=None`, never `links_applied`/`comments_applied`); (4) live probes are manual, not in CI, do not round-trip relationships, and can encode bugs as expected.

Deep research (Pact consumer-driven contracts; vcrpy semantic matchers; Schemathesis + Dredd/Gavel structure-not-value validation; Google SWE-book "verified fakes" and its change-detector warning; and how real Jira clients test — `jira-python` uses a live Dockerized/Cloud sandbox, while `jira-cli` serves on-disk fixtures *captured from real Jira* THROUGH its production serialization via an in-process mock) converges on a layered strategy right-sized for a single team: **one producer↔consumer snapshot contract test, fed by hermetic-but-honest fixtures derived from real Jira payloads, exercised through the PRODUCTION code path** — explicitly avoiding change-detector bloat. Full live-sandbox e2e and cross-team Pact are out of scope (overkill for a single team).

## Child stories

This epic decomposes into six stories (sized for one PR each):

- **A — Hermetic-but-honest Jira fixtures + verified fake client** (`fe57-7712-1e3f-45f4`): the foundation — fixtures captured from real Jira, served through the production path.
- **B — Producer↔consumer snapshot contract: shared schema + round-trip test** (`8937-eed3-c881-4ea1`): the keystone; also owns the documented anti-change-detector guardrail artifact.
- **C — Verified fake: contract tests against BOTH real and fake client** (`59ef-ff3e-5aea-47b1`): keeps the fake honest.
- **D — Collapse the dual outbound applier paths to one** (`33d0-1e2c-e059-4181`).
- **E — Sub-op telemetry + silent-no-op canary** (`2359-ac1a-7c76-4f56`): depends on D.
- **F — Honest bidirectional round-trip probe; de-encode "expected-bug" guards** (`822a-2bad-fe48-43e0`).

## Sequencing (MVP-first thin vertical slice)

The epic ships incrementally, not as a big-bang:

1. **A → B scoped FIRST to the known seam** — capture the inbound-comment (`comment`) and `issuelinks` shapes (bugs 0ee6/3f04) and land the single round-trip contract test on exactly those, before broadening the schema to all fields. This thin vertical slice de-risks the whole contract approach against the canonical failure.
2. **C** once the fake exists (keep it honest).
3. **D then E** — telemetry builds on the single consolidated applier.
4. **F** reuses A's fixtures for the hermetic round-trip and de-encodes the probe guards.

Each story is independently shippable behind its own PR.

## Rollout & rollback

- The **fail-loud sub-op invariant** (story E) lands **warn-first** (telemetry + `WARNING`) behind a flag/canary, and is promoted to hard-fail only after a baseline pass that emits zero such warnings; revert = drop back to warn (no other code change).
- The **applier collapse** (story D) verifies behavioral parity — the surviving path applies every sub-op the retired path did — **before** the retired path is deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single-source-of-truth snapshot-entry schema module exists as the canonical shape.
- [ ] A test validates the fetcher's snapshot output against that schema.
- [ ] A test validates each differ's snapshot reads against that schema.
- [ ] One round-trip contract test exercises fetcher → snapshot → differs → applier through the production path, using fixtures derived from real Jira payloads.
- [ ] Outbound application is collapsed to a single production path (no parallel applier remains).
- [ ] The retired outbound applier path is deleted.
- [ ] Outbound sub-op telemetry (`links_applied`/`comments_applied`/`labels_applied`) is surfaced in the structured batch outcome.
- [ ] A `computed > 0 && applied == 0` sub-op condition fails loudly, after the warn-first rollout in Rollout & rollback.
- [ ] Bidirectional comment/link/parent round-trip is asserted hermetically through the production path.
- [ ] Every probe assertion that encodes a current bug as expected is converted to fail-when-the-gap-closes.
- [ ] A documented anti-change-detector guardrail for reconciler tests is committed and referenced by new tests (owned by story B).
- [ ] All six child stories are closed; the full reconciler suite is green.
- [ ] Producer (fetcher + enrichment) and consumers (differs/appliers) cannot drift on snapshot shape without a test failing.
- [ ] Outbound sync is exercised through the production code path, not a parallel dead path.
- [ ] A silent sub-op no-op (e.g. links computed but never applied) fails a test/canary instead of passing green.
- [ ] Bidirectional round-trips (comments, links, parent) for the real Jira shapes are asserted; no probe encodes a bug as expected.
- [ ] New tests assert behavior/contract (semantic round-trip, structure/type); the suite stays lean; zero change-detector tests added.
baseline.summary: Close the Jira-sync producer<->consumer & tested-vs-shipped test-coverage gap class

content.text: ## Reproduction Steps
1. On a CLEAN checkout (no pre-existing .tickets-tracker), run `pytest -m "not integration"` (as CI does).
2. The bash-suite collector runs test-ticket-{list-descendants,next-batch,purge-bridge}-dispatcher.sh.
## Expected
All suites pass; no entries leaked into REPO_ROOT.
## Actual
Two distinct CI failures (run 27437641565, both runners, on origin/main):
1. REAL: `Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT: ['.tickets-tracker']`. The no-args/arity tests in 3
dispatcher suites invoke an auto-initing command (list-descendants/next-batch/purge-bridge) WITHOUT a
sandboxed TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR, so _ensure_initialized auto-inits .tickets-tracker INTO the checkout,
tripping the conftest leak guard. Masked locally because the dev checkout already has a .tickets-tracker
(dogfood store) — the guard sees no NEW entry. Gate-command arity tests (check-ac/clarity/quality/summary)
do NOT leak (those arms intentionally skip _ensure_initialized).
2. SPURIOUS: ~909 FileNotFoundError errors — the macOS tmp-cleaner reaps pytest's default /tmp/pytest-of-*
basetemp mid-run (10-16 min). The CI pytest step passed no fixed --basetemp.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The 3 no-args arity tests sandbox TICKETS_TRACKER_DIR so auto-init cannot land in the checkout
- [ ] Fix is behavior-preserving (same usage output + exit; proved no-leak in a clean-checkout simulation)
- [ ] CI pytest step pins a fixed --basetemp (under runner.temp, not /tmp) + -p no:cacheprovider
- [ ] The 3 patched suites pass via the collector

content.text: ## Why
Every prompt/detector change in this epic must be measured, or we repeat dso's mistake of uncalibrated
drift. This is the gating foundation: no prompt story merges without a passing eval.
## What
FIRST extend the eval harness to support code-review prompts, THEN author specs:
- Harness prerequisite (grounded gap from plan review): eval_solver.run_case() has NO execution arm for
code-review prompt ids (code-review-base, code-review-verify, overlay ids), and eval_scorers.py REGISTRY
has no scorer validating a code_review_* output. Add a run_case arm + register code-review gating scorers
BEFORE specs can run.
- OUTPUT-SHAPE CONTRACT (pin this to avoid a vacuous-pass bug): the code-review arm runs INDIVIDUAL prompts
(base/overlays return {findings:[...]}; verify returns {verifications:[...]}) — the per-prompt calibration
granularity, NOT the full gate. Code-review scorers therefore score on FINDINGS presence/absence (recall =
the target defect's finding is present; no-fire = absent), NOT on the completion-verifier FAIL vocabulary.
eval_scorers._fired() currently matches only verdict=='FAIL'; do NOT route code-review cases through it.
If (and only if) a case exercises the full-gate verdict, extend _fired to also match verdict=='BLOCK' and
add 'block' to FIRE_EXPECTS so dataset validation accepts it.
- Then build eval specs for base/overlays/verify with two families seeded from dso's corpus:
NO-FIRE (must not flag): sourced-bash functions, subdirectory scripts, list-form subprocess, Rule-5
structural greps, moved-code renames with callers updated, already-public config reads, valid
observable-postcondition tests.
SEEDED-DEFECT recall (must flag): tautological test, dangling deletion, asymmetric signature change,
hallucinated API, VCS conflict marker, ticket scope drift.
- A deterministic scorer GATES; an llm-judge only REPORTS.
## Scope
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py (new code-review arm, findings-based output), eval_scorers.py (new
findings-based code-review scorers), src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ (specs + fixtures). No gate behavior change.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] eval_solver.run_case executes code-review prompt ids (base, verify, overlays) returning the prompt's
native structured output ({findings}/{verifications}), NOT the full-gate verdict.
- [ ] >=1 code_review_* gating scorer registered that scores on findings presence/absence (not FAIL/BLOCK
verdict); code-review recall cases cannot vacuously pass through the FAIL-only _fired.
- [ ] Eval specs exist for base, verify, and at least the tests + security overlays.
- [ ] No-fire and recall case families seeded from the dso incidents above.
- [ ] The nit-framing experiment is encoded as a committed eval case (fixture + scorer assertion); its
no-fire/recall expectations pass on the current gate as baseline.

baseline.summary: Eval foundation for the four-pass code-review prompts

baseline.description:
# S6 — Pluggable custom verifier

## Why
No fixed set of verifiers covers every organization's identity system (bespoke internal token
services, non-standard introspection like GitHub's, mTLS-header trust). A pluggable seam keeps the
capability open-ended — an operator drops in their own verifier without patching rebar — which is
core to the "generic, wide variety of environments" goal.

## What
Add a **custom-verifier** mode to `src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py`, activated by including `custom` in the `mcp.auth_strategies` list (the strategy-selection
config key **introduced by S2**, this story's dependency — not a pre-existing seam), with one flat config key it registers: `auth_custom_import` (a `module:factory`
import string resolving to a factory that returns an object implementing the official SDK
`mcp.server.auth.provider.TokenVerifier` protocol). The factory's returned verifier is placed in the
composite and treated like any built-in — crucially, **the composite's audience re-check still
applies**: a custom verifier that returns an `AccessToken` with `resource=None` or a wrong `resource`
is rejected by the composite (S2), so a buggy/hostile custom verifier cannot bypass RFC 8707. Loading
validates the resolved object satisfies the protocol and fails closed otherwise. Adds the `auth_custom_import`
field to `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`); its derived
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_CUSTOM_IMPORT` env-var name goes in `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py`) +
`server.json`; `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes (docs regenerated by S7).

## Approach & rationale
Expose the SAME `TokenVerifier` seam the built-ins use, loaded via a config-named import path (the
established Python import-string convention, e.g. how uvicorn/Starlette resolve app factories). This
keeps custom verifiers ecosystem-compatible and adds no new abstraction. The composite audience
re-check (S2) is what makes an untrusted-in-code-quality custom verifier still safe on the audience
axis.

## Scope
The custom-verifier loader + protocol validation only, on the S2 seam. Subset of the epic. Depends on
S2. Independent of S3/S4/S5.

## Security
Boundary-crossing AND it loads operator-configured code (arbitrary import executes at load):
- The import path is an **operator-supplied trusted config value** and is treated as a documented
  trust boundary. It is read ONLY from resolved config (`auth_custom_import`), **never** from a
  request or any untrusted source — enforced structurally (the value is consumed only at startup from
  the config object), not merely documented.
- Import resolution uses `importlib.import_module` on the configured dotted path and does **not**
  insert the current working directory (`""`) into `sys.path`, so a module resolvable ONLY from the
  cwd is not loaded (avoids cwd shadowing/hijack). Resolution/validation failure, or a resolved
  object lacking `verify_token`, is a **fail-closed startup error** (never run with partial/no auth).
- The composite's mandatory audience re-check (S2) still applies to whatever the custom verifier
  returns — it cannot mint an accepted token for a wrong/absent audience.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The `auth_custom_import` config field exists in `McpConfig`/`_SECTIONS['mcp']`
      (`_config_schema.py`); its derived `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_CUSTOM_IMPORT` env-var name is in
      `MCP_ENV_VARS` (`mcp_server.py`) + `server.json`; and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` passes
      (observable oracle: manifest drift test green; both files contain the new env-var name). Docs
      regenerated by S7.
- [ ] Unit test (tier: unit) asserts a valid `module:factory` resolves (via `importlib`) to a working
      verifier whose accepted token (with `resource=auth_resource_server_url`) is honored by the
      composite (observable oracle: the composite accepts the token).
- [ ] Unit test asserts cwd is NOT consulted: a `module:factory` whose module exists ONLY in the
      current working directory (not installed / not on the configured import path) FAILS to load
      (observable oracle: loading raises a fail-closed error and the cwd module is not imported),
      proving the loader does not add cwd to `sys.path`.
- [ ] Unit test asserts fail-closed startup for: an unresolvable import path, and a resolved object
      that does not implement `verify_token` (observable oracle: startup raises a clear message) —
      two negative controls.
- [ ] Unit test asserts a custom verifier returning an `AccessToken` with `resource=None` or a wrong
      `resource` is **rejected by the composite** (the custom seam cannot bypass the audience check).
- [ ] Component test asserts a token accepted by a configured custom verifier (returning
      `resource=auth_resource_server_url`), invoked through the `CompositeTokenVerifier`'s verify path,
      is accepted; end-to-end HTTP behavior is exercised once for all verifiers by S2's transport
      harness, not re-tested here.
- [ ] `docs/mcp-auth.md` (S7) documents that `auth_custom_import` is a trusted operator config value
      that executes code at load.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.

## Compatibility
Additive, opt-in via the `custom` strategy. No change to other verifiers or stdio.
baseline.summary: S6 — Pluggable custom verifier

content.text: ## Why
Deletion/asymmetric-change review is a positive analysis task the reviewer won't do unless prompted, but
it doesn't belong in the always-on base prompt. rebar's grounding oracle has no reverse-reference lookup,
so a purely deterministic version is imprecise new work. The aligned design is a specialist LLM overlay
gated by a deterministic diff-content trigger.
## What
- New capability: content-triggered overlays — a deterministic diff-content predicate that activates an
overlay, alongside today's path-glob triggers (registry.glob_triggered_overlays seam).
- REGISTER the overlay id: add `deletion-impact` to the closed OVERLAY_IDS tuple in registry.py (grounded
prerequisite — every dispatch path validates against OVERLAY_IDS and silently DROPS an unknown id, so a
criteria_routing.json entry alone would never dispatch).
- deletion-impact overlay (agentic, findings-only, one-hop): triggered when the diff removes a
def/class/signature (polyglot regex over '-' lines; the regex is expected to evolve per language).
Caller-search mechanism (specified): the overlay uses its read-only tools (search_files / read_file;
AST/LSP when available) to find surviving references to the removed/renamed symbol in UNCHANGED files
and flags dangling ones. Advisory/coach-not-block; claims flow through Pass-2 verify + Pass-3 decide.
Over-firing the trigger costs one advisory pass, never a wrong verdict.
## Scope
registry.py (trigger seam + OVERLAY_IDS), gates/code-review.yaml wiring,
reviewers/code-review-deletion-impact.md, criteria_routing.json entry (SHARED FILE — coordinate with
stories E and F which also edit it; file_impact declared so next_batch serializes them).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `deletion-impact` added to the OVERLAY_IDS closed tuple; dispatch reaches the overlay.
- [ ] Content-trigger seam added and unit-tested; path-glob triggers unaffected.
- [ ] Overlay fires on removed def/class/signature lines, not on unrelated diffs.
- [ ] Caller-search mechanism documented (tools, one-hop scope); dangling-deletion recall eval passes; a
valid rename-with-callers-updated does not fire.
- [ ] Overlay is advisory (no new BLOCK source).
## Data-flow: content trigger -> overlay_union (resolves plan-review G6)
The diff-content predicate must be plumbed into the union step (today `overlay_union` receives only
`changed_files` paths via `glob_triggered_overlays`):
- Add `registry.content_triggered_overlays(diff_text) -> list[overlay_id]` (analog of
`glob_triggered_overlays`) that runs the polyglot removed-def/class/signature regex over the `-`
lines of `diff_text` and returns `['deletion-impact']` when it matches.
- Add a `diff_text` (or precomputed `content_triggered`) input to the `overlay_union` op; extend its
formula to `selected = set(glob_set) | set(content_set) | set(recommend_ids)` (Round-A) and keep the
`- already_run` subtraction for Round-B.
- Wire `diff_text: ${{ steps.assemble_diff.outputs.context }}` into BOTH the `triggers` and `union`
steps in `gates/code-review.yaml`.
This keeps path-glob triggers unaffected (content set is unioned in, not replacing glob).

baseline.summary: Content-triggered overlay capability + deletion-impact overlay

## Why
The design has sharp edges (hot-path cost, concurrency on the shared branch, rate-limit,
no_mutate, absent marker). Only tests lock the invariants so future ensures can be added
safely.

## What
The code under test is provided by this ticket's DEPENDENCIES (WS1 `ec29`, WS2 `891c`, WS3 `424c`),
all in the same feature stack: `rebar._store.ensures` exports `run_ensures(tracker)`,
`REGISTRY_IDS`/`registry_ids()`, `applied_ids(tracker)`, `maybe_emit_pending_hint(tracker)`,
`APPLIED_MARKER` (`.ensure-applied`). Add behavioral tests covering: git-level idempotency (`run_ensures` twice on a converged store
→ zero new commits); hot-path regression: a common mutation never invokes `rebar._store.ensures.run_ensures` and reads `.ensure-applied`
at most once per process; AND the write-path nudge `rebar._store.ensures.maybe_emit_pending_hint` itself spawns NO
subprocess at all (it only reads a marker file — unlike the old init-time git-config migration),
asserted by spying subprocess around a direct call to it; concurrency (two real OS processes running the sweep on the same checkout both complete —
serialized by the store write lock — and the store converges to a VALID, COMPLETE `.ensure-applied`
(parseable JSON containing exactly the registry ids), demonstrating the atomic temp+rename write
leaves no partial/invalid marker); no_mutate (library read-only fsck mutates nothing);
absent/garbage `.ensure-applied` (→ empty set → converges, no re-commit storm). The fsck byte-parity/help-golden tests are owned by WS3, and the pending-hint unit tests by WS2 — NOT here.

## Scope
In: the behavioral test suite for WS1-2 invariants.
Out: fsck byte-parity/help goldens (WS3), the feature code itself (WS1-3), docs (WS4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Idempotency test: `run_ensures()` twice on a converged store makes zero new commits/pushes (git-log assertion)
- [ ] Hot-path regression test: (a) a ticket mutation (create/comment) never calls `run_ensures`; (b) it reads `.ensure-applied` at most once per process (the cached pending set); (c) the write-path nudge `rebar._store.ensures.maybe_emit_pending_hint` spawns NO subprocess — verified by spying `subprocess` (run/Popen/check_call/check_output/call) around a direct call to `rebar._store.ensures.maybe_emit_pending_hint` — so the hot path never shells out (contrast the old init-time git-config migration)
- [ ] Concurrency test: two real OS processes sweeping the same checkout both exit 0 (serialized by the store write lock, `_store/lock.py`) and the store converges to a VALID, COMPLETE `.ensure-applied` (parses as JSON == `set(rebar._store.ensures.REGISTRY_IDS)`) — the observable outcome of the atomic temp+rename write; the test asserts this positive convergence, not the (structurally-impossible-to-observe) absence of a torn write
- [ ] no_mutate test: a library read-only fsck surface (no_mutate=True) mutates nothing and never runs the sweep
- [ ] absent/garbage-marker test: a missing or garbage `.ensure-applied` degrades to empty-set (pending=all) without crashing
baseline.summary: WS5: tests — idempotency, hot-path regression, concurrency, no_mutate, absent-marker

# Thread ref + source mode through the code-reading gates

## Why

Today the gates derive their code root from the MCP process cwd / `repo_root` and read its
mutable working tree (`cfg.repo_path`). They must instead read the snapshot materialized at
the client-specified ref, with a uniform single-`ref` interface across every operation.

## What

- Add `ref` (branch|tag|SHA, default `origin/main`) and `source` (`attested` default |
  `local`) parameters to: `review_plan`, `verify_completion`, `review_ticket`, `review_code`,
  `scan_spec`. Every operation takes ONE ref and gets ONE snapshot (code-review included; no
  base+head pair in this epic).
- Attested: call S1/S2 to obtain a snapshot dir at the pinned SHA; point the gate's file
  tools (`pai_tools` root / `cfg.repo_path`) at the snapshot dir instead of the server cwd.
- Local: read the server's in-place checkout directly (no materialization, no cache); mark
  the run as unsigned (S4 bars signing). In local mode `repo_root` IS the read root (the
  checkout); in attested mode `repo_root` only locates the object DB and the snapshot is the
  read root.
- Replace the implicit `repo_root`-derived code root with the snapshot handle across all three
  dispatch touchpoints: `gate_ops`, `completion.py`, `operations._assemble_context`.
- **Back-compat / expand-contract:** existing callers that pass neither param get the
  documented defaults (ref=`origin/main`, source=`attested`), so the change is additive; state
  this back-out path (defaults preserve today's "verify latest" intent without the wrong-branch bug).
- **Consumer tolerance:** a gate whose snapshot dir is absent/being retired (S2 GC) treats it
  as a miss and re-materializes (ENOENT -> re-acquire), never reads a partial tree.
- **Defaults configurable:** the `ref`/`source` defaults are overridable per deployment, not
  hardcoded constants.

## Scope

- In: parameter threading, gate file-tool re-rooting to the snapshot, local-mode in-place read,
  back-compat defaults, consumer absent/stale tolerance.
- Out: signing rules (S4); CLI/MCP surface schemas (S5); snapshot/cache internals (S1/S2);
  the architecture ADR (authored in S2, cross-referenced here).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the five gates accepts `ref` + `source`; attested reads the snapshot dir, never
      the server's working tree.
- [ ] Omitting the params applies the documented defaults (ref=`origin/main`, source=`attested`);
      the defaults are configurable, not hardcoded.
- [ ] All three dispatch touchpoints (`gate_ops`, `completion.py`,
      `operations._assemble_context`) consume the snapshot handle — not just the interface signature.
- [ ] `local` mode reads the in-place checkout (dirty allowed), is flagged unsigned, and uses
      `repo_root` as the read root; attested uses `repo_root` only to locate the object DB.
- [ ] code-review uses a single snapshot at a single ref (no base+head pair) like the others.
- [ ] A gate tolerates an absent/being-GC'd snapshot dir by re-materializing (ENOENT -> miss),
      never reading a partial tree.
- [ ] Regression test asserts the attested verdict is IDENTICAL regardless of the server's
      checked-out branch (the behavioral contract — NOT an output snapshot / change-detector),
      reproducing this session's wrong-branch false-negative.

## Additional notes + Acceptance Criteria (advisory remediation)

- Terminology: "snapshot dir" and "snapshot handle" refer to the SAME entity (the handle wraps
  the dir + SHA + cleanup); used interchangeably.
- Defaults config mechanism: `ref`/`source` defaults are read through the EXISTING rebar config
  precedence (rebar.toml `[llm]`/gate table + `REBAR_*` env override), consistent with how
  other LLM/gate settings resolve — not a bespoke new mechanism.
- Rollback: `source=local` is the explicit back-out that restores the prior in-place working-
  tree read if the default snapshot read ever regresses a deployment.

- [ ] The `ref`/`source` defaults resolve via the standard rebar config + `REBAR_*` env
      precedence (named, not a deferred mechanism choice).
- [ ] A test covers the ENOENT/absent-snapshot path (gate re-materializes, never reads a partial tree).
- [ ] A test covers local-mode unsigned flagging (a local run is reflected unsigned in the result).
- [ ] `source=local` is documented as the rollback to in-place reads.
baseline.summary: Thread ref + source mode through the code-reading gates
