baseline.description:
# Coaching move: when a plan stops CONVERGING, propose a decomposition instead of another finding list

## The observation

Twice in epic e369 a plan absorbed round after round of review findings, and both times the remedy was not a better answer to the findings — it was **splitting the ticket**:

* **J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]** blocked EIGHT times. Extracting the exception contract into
  J10 [rebar:bb8c...] produced a first-try PASS.
* **b586 [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260]** has now taken TEN rounds and is still BLOCK. Its findings
  partition cleanly into two concerns that alternate: the POLICY (rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 — helper
  reuse, duplicate-risk scoping, citation precision, the per-call read/mutation boundary, what
  exception escapes at cap exhaustion) and the MECHANICS of the module extraction the 800-LOC cap
  forces (rounds 6, 7 — what moves, what routes through what, which tree the LOC is measured on).
  Each fix in one concern re-opened surface in the other.

The gate is doing its job in both cases — the findings were real and several were serious. What it cannot currently say is the thing a senior reviewer would say on round four: *"stop answering these one at a time; this is two tickets."*

## Why the obvious trigger is WRONG

"After N rounds, suggest splitting" would have fired on b586 at round 3 and been wrong. Rounds 1 through 9 CONVERGED — 20 advisory + 1 blocking, down to 1 blocking. That is a plan being iterated well, and telling its author to restructure would have been noise that trains people to ignore the gate.

**The signal is not the round count. It is the loss of convergence**, and it has a specific shape:

1. **Non-monotonicity** — the blocking count RISES after having fallen (b586: 1 blocking at round 9,
   7+ at round 10). That is the fingerprint of "fixing one thing re-opened another."
2. **Alternating clusters** — findings partition into >= 2 groups by criteria code and cited
   location, and consecutive rounds hit DIFFERENT groups rather than drilling into one.
3. **Disjoint citation sets** — the groups cite non-overlapping files/sections (b586: the extraction
   findings cite `transport.py` structure; the policy findings cite `_errors` / `dispatch_one`
   semantics).

Requiring all three is what keeps it from firing on a plan that is simply deep.

## The move itself

When those conditions hold, the gate stops emitting an (N+1)th finding list and instead emits a **structural verdict**: the cluster partition it actually computed, round-by-round, plus a proposed decomposition — "these 10 rounds' findings fall into 2 groups that alternate; here are the 2 candidate tickets, and here is which findings belong to each."

Design constraints that matter:

* **Advisory, not a new blocking verdict.** Keeping one ticket is a legitimate authorial choice; the
  gate should make the structural claim VISIBLE, not enforce it. It also must not become a way to
  dodge findings — the findings still stand and still block.
* **It must show its work.** The value is in the partition, not the recommendation. An author who
  disagrees needs the round-by-round cluster assignment to argue with, exactly as they would with a
  finding's evidence.
* **No new storage.** `rebar audit show <id>`'s `plan_reviews` array already retains the per-round
  `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars — verified: b586 currently carries 10 retained rounds. The trend is
  computable from what is already there.
* **Prefer deterministic clustering first.** Findings already carry structured `criteria` and
  `location` fields, so grouping may not need an LLM call at all. Reach for a model only if the
  deterministic partition proves too coarse.

## The confound to handle honestly

b586's description grew from ~8.8 KB to ~28 KB across the ten rounds. **More plan is more surface, so some of the rising finding count is the plan getting longer, not worse.** Any trend metric should normalize by plan size (or at minimum surface the size delta alongside the count) — otherwise the move will fire on thorough authors, which is precisely the population it should leave alone.

## Open questions (this is an idea, not a design)

* Do the retained `plan_reviews` sidecars expose per-round BLOCKING COUNTS? The projection checked
  here showed the verdicts but not the counts, so the trend's raw input needs confirming before any
  of this is buildable.
* Where should it surface — in the `review-plan` output, in `review-plan --status`, or only in
  `rebar audit show`? The first is loudest and the most likely to be resented.
* Should it ever fire at round 1 on a plan that is obviously two tickets (e.g. one whose Scope lists
  two unrelated modules and whose ACs partition with them)? That is a different, cheaper detector
  and possibly the better first version.
* J9's split was authored by a human noticing the pattern. Is one automated nudge enough to change
  behaviour, or does the coaching only work when it names the CANDIDATE SPLIT concretely?

## PRIOR ART — this is a MOVE in an existing registry, not a new mechanism

Checked before leaving this as an idea, and it substantially shrinks the scope. rebar already has a **Pass-4 coach with a pluggable move-registry**:

* [rebar:cf40-f372-47a1-44a3] (closed) extracted the coach MECHANISM into the kernel and defined a
  registered move-registry SCHEMA `{id, name, template, triggers/applies_when}`, with selection as a
  DETERMINISTIC filter on `triggers` and only then an LLM choice among the applicable moves. Each
  gate supplies its own catalog.
* [rebar:315d-b4ba-6c9e-482d], [rebar:75a9-01c2-304d-4532], [rebar:5dac-c177-56ff-4af4] and
  [rebar:e3cf-3afc-e80d-4d19] are prior moves shipped through that machinery.

So the deliverable is most likely **one registry entry plus its `triggers` predicate**, not new plumbing — and the "prefer deterministic clustering first" note above is already the house pattern rather than a novel suggestion.

**THE ONE REAL MECHANISM GAP, and it is the crux of this idea.** The existing coach operates on the SURVIVING ADVISORIES OF A SINGLE PASS. This move's trigger is inherently CROSS-ROUND — it needs the previous rounds' blocking counts and cluster assignments, which a per-pass coach does not have in hand. So the honest scoping is:

* if the coach can be given read access to the retained `plan_reviews` sidecars, this is a normal
  registry entry with an unusual `triggers` predicate;
* if it cannot, the mechanism needs a cross-round input FIRST, and that — not the move — is the
  actual piece of work. Settle this before estimating.

## RELATIONSHIP TO [rebar:259c-0f29-e920-4fab] — adjacent, NOT a duplicate

259c is an advisory nudge that fires on a LEAF WHOSE ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA COUNT is high, because completion-verification effort is linear in criteria count. Both coach "this ticket may be too big", so they should be read together and their messages must not collide. They differ in the signal:

* 259c is STATIC and fires on ROUND ONE from the plan's own shape (criteria count).
* this one is DYNAMIC and cannot fire before round three, because it needs a TREND.

259c is the cheaper detector and probably the better first version of the family — which is also the answer to one of the open questions above. If only one of the two is built, build 259c.

## Provenance

Both instances are recorded in session log [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9] (handoff #4 lesson 3, and handoff #7). The b586 round-by-round breakdown that this generalises from is a comment on [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260].
baseline.summary: Plan-review coaching move: when findings stop converging, propose a decomposition

## Context / Problem
ed2b (`rebar show` intermittently returned EMPTY stdout with exit 0 under concurrent background auto-push) was fixed by bounding the read-path reconverge lock wait (`_RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 2` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py`) and landed with a show-only regression test (`tests/interfaces/store/test_show_no_stall.py`). But read-output integrity under sync contention is a GENERIC property of every read surface that routes through `ensure_fresh` — list, search, ready, next-batch share the same reconverge path as show and would regress silently (bug-trend review change 20: one-time machinery, no bespoke per-surface copies).

## Approach
Generalize the existing ed2b harness rather than inventing a new storm: reuse/hoist `repo_with_origin_tickets` + the `_rebar_cli` helper from `test_show_no_stall.py` into a sibling property module. One property-style test parameterized over the CLI read surfaces (`show`, `list`, `search`, `ready` at minimum): under the same burst-of-writes contention (each `rebar edit` spawning a background push via `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`), every ZERO-exit read invocation must produce PARSEABLE output for its format. Use each surface's JSON spelling — `--output json` where the flag exists (show/list/ready); `search` takes no output flag and already emits a JSON array by default — and pin: exit 0 implies stdout parses as JSON of the surface's documented shape (list/object). This sidesteps legitimately-empty text output — e.g. `rebar ready` in default text mode prints nothing when no tickets are unblocked — because valid-empty serializes as `[]`, distinguishable from truncated-empty stdout. A LOUD nonzero exit is acceptable — empty-success is the bug. Explicitly NOT pagination invariants: rebar's read CLI has no cursor/offset pagination; the property is output-integrity-or-loud-error.

Throttle handling (decisive): `ensure_fresh` reconverges at most 1/min per store via the `/tmp/.ticket-sync-<md5(tracker)>` marker, so only the first read in a window can stall. The harness must call the existing `_clear_sync_throttle(tracker)` helper (already in `test_show_no_stall.py:69`) BEFORE EACH parameterized read invocation so every surface actually exercises the reconverge path rather than short-circuiting to the local snapshot.

## Scope
- tests/interfaces/store/ — new sibling module + minimal fixture/helper hoist (no production code)

## Testing
The test IS the deliverable. RED demonstration: temporarily revert the ed2b ledge locally (raise `_RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` back to the 15s writer default so reads stall on the held lock) and observe the property fail on at least one surface; restore and confirm green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] One parameterized property covers show/list/search/ready via the real CLI under the ed2b write-burst + background-push harness; no bespoke per-surface copies.
- [x] Invariant pinned: exit 0 implies stdout parses as the surface's JSON shape (valid-empty `[]` passes; truncated/empty stdout fails); nonzero exits pass (loud failure allowed).
- [x] Throttle marker cleared before each read so every invocation exercises the reconverge path.
- [x] RED demonstrated by locally reverting the reads.py lock-timeout ledge; green on the fixed tree.
- [x] ed2b harness reused (hoisted or imported), not duplicated.
baseline.summary: Concurrency suite: generic reads-under-writer-storm property

## Problem
tracker_head_sha intentionally rejects any git status output, but initialized ticket stores do not ignore reducer-owned per-ticket .archived and .write.lock runtime markers. A normal store with archived tickets is therefore permanently dirty and every plan review returns unsigned INDETERMINATE store-read-failure. The live store also has two old orphan review/signature events that fsck recovery must reconcile separately.

## Plan
- Add the two reducer runtime marker patterns to the canonical tickets-branch gitignore ensure.
- Add migration and clean-store regression coverage proving existing stores converge and strict tracker_head_sha succeeds with runtime markers present.
- Use the supported fsck recovery path for genuinely orphaned event files; do not weaken strict dirty/unmerged detection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-ticket .archived and .write.lock runtime markers are ignored in new and migrated ticket stores.
- [ ] tracker_head_sha succeeds on an otherwise-clean store containing those markers.
- [ ] Genuine untracked event files remain visible to git status and still produce store-read-failure.
- [ ] Existing gitignore ensure tests and focused relation snapshot tests pass.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The live store is clean after supported recovery and 75de plan review advances past store-read-failure to its next validation gate.
baseline.summary: Plan relation snapshots reject rebar runtime marker files

content.text: ## Finding (A1 — verified)

The workflow visual editor interpolates repo-sourced content into an inline `<script>` block via `json.dumps`, which does not escape `/`. Content containing a literal `</script>` breaks out of the script context and injects markup that runs with the in-page `window.REBAR_TOKEN` guarding the `/save` write endpoint.

Citations: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:292-298` (json.dumps of bpmn_xml, prompts, contracts, library, descriptor, overlay_triggers) -> `:366-373` (interpolated into `<script>window.REBAR_* = {...}`). Untrusted inputs on a cloned/shared repo: `editor_server.py:159,162` (prompts via `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md`), `:188` (enumerate_library), and the edited workflow YAML.
## Reproduction Steps
1. In a cloned repo, put `</script><script>fetch('/save',{method:'POST',body:...})</script>` inside a `.rebar/prompts/*.md` or workflow YAML.
2. Open the visual editor on that repo.
3. Expected: content rendered inert. Actual: injected script executes with REBAR_TOKEN, forging authenticated /save writes.
## Remediation

Add a `_js_embed(obj)` helper: `json.dumps(...)` then escape `<` (e.g. `</`->`<\/`, and `<!--`/`-->` defensively); route all interpolated payloads through it. (Alternative: move data into `<script type="application/json">` read via textContent.)
End state: repo-sourced strings cannot terminate the script element; REBAR_TOKEN no longer exfiltratable via crafted content.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All `json.dumps` payloads embedded into inline `<script>` in editor.py are escaped against `</script>` breakout
- [ ] A test asserts a payload containing `</script>` renders inert
- [ ] No behavior change to legitimate editor content

baseline.summary: Fix editor XSS: escape </script> breakout in inline-script interpolation

## Context / Problem
The automated-quality audit found approved maintainability ratchets that cannot be enabled wholesale without first accounting for existing diagnostics. This epic stages blocking enforcement for function complexity, four safe Mypy settings, Ruff ASYNC/DTZ, and Ruff RUF hygiene. It explicitly defers disallow_any_generics, disallow_untyped_defs, Ruff security-family S rules, and Semgrep expansion.

## Approach
Deliver independently reviewed stories into a short-lived Gerrit feature branch, then merge the completed branch atomically to main. Stories that edit pyproject.toml execute in this order: d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d, then 28cd-d8f8-4456-482c, then 125d-ee6f-7af0-4200. The 28cd story creates and owns tests/unit/test_ruff_ratchet.py; 125d depends on 28cd and extends that file. The complexity story does not share pyproject.toml and may proceed independently when next-batch reports no file-impact conflict.

Rejected: one large cleanup change, because it would mix distinct tools, obscure regressions, and make rollback difficult.

## Child Decomposition
- c9f7-d6df-bce0-4b77: add a symbol-level shrink-only C901 baseline at threshold 15 and wire it into the canonical lint gate.
- d9f5-baa5-9fc3-451d: enable no_implicit_optional, strict_equality, warn_redundant_casts, and warn_unused_ignores after revalidating the measured diagnostics.
- 28cd-d8f8-4456-482c: make the three DTZ sites timezone-explicit, enable ASYNC/DTZ, create the shared Ruff ratchet test, and run the integration pytest tier.
- 125d-ee6f-7af0-4200: clear RUF100 and other approved RUF diagnostics, extend the shared Ruff ratchet test, and continue to defer RUF001, RUF002, and RUF003.

## Verification Checkpoints
After each story, its focused commands and Gerrit labels are recorded on that child ticket. After all children merge to the server-side feature branch, the integration worktree runs each command in the Acceptance Criteria independently.

content.text: ## Summary
The integration test
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`
**fails (does not skip)** in an environment where `acli` is on PATH but no live Jira project is
configured for the test's fixture repo. Observed while running the full unit+integration suite
locally during the commit-ticket-gate work (ticket `263d-e96c-80b4-4c84`). NOT caused by that
change (which does not touch reconcile / Jira), and it is excluded from the default CI gate
(`-m "not integration and not external"`), so the Gerrit `Verified` gate is unaffected.
## Reproduction Steps
1. Have `acli` on PATH (so the test's `shutil.which("acli") is None` skip guard does NOT fire).
2. Do NOT configure a live Jira project for the fixture (`JIRA_PROJECT` unset; the fresh
`rebar_repo` fixture has no `[jira] project`).
3. Run: `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`
(or the whole integration tier: `pytest -m integration`).
## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** the test skips (no live Jira env) or asserts a routed, non-mutating dry-run.
- **Actual:** `rebar reconcile` raises and exits non-zero; the assertion
`'"mode": "dry-run"' in out or '"no_write": true' in out or returncode == 0` fails:
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: inbound fetch requires a valid jira.project key
(JIRA_PROJECT / [jira] project); got ''. Refusing to search Jira unscoped.
## Analysis
The reconciler's inbound-fetch guard (refuse an unscoped Jira search when `jira.project` is
empty) is correct, pre-existing behaviour. The bug is in the TEST's precondition: its skip
guard checks only for `acli` on PATH, not for a configured Jira project — so on a machine where
`acli` is installed but the fixture repo has no `jira.project`, the test runs and trips the
guard. Test brittleness / missing precondition, not a reconciler regression.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The test SKIPS (not fails) when a live Jira project is not configured — e.g. also gate on
`os.environ.get("JIRA_PROJECT")` (or a configured `[jira] project`), or set `jira.project`
in the fixture repo before invoking `rebar reconcile`.
- [ ] With `acli` present AND a valid Jira project, the test still exercises the dry-run path.
- [ ] `pytest -m integration tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` passes or skips cleanly in
both configurations (project set / unset).

baseline.summary: test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira fails (not skips) when acli is present but fixture has no jira.project

## Context / Problem
Plan-review findings can tell a client to comply with rebar-internal identifiers such as "ADR 0043." Those ADRs live in the rebar source repository, are not part of a client project's architecture record, and are not meaningful or necessarily accessible to the plan author. The defect is currently grounded in bundled reviewer instructions including src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md, plan_review_E6.md, plan_review_F1.md, plan_review_T13.md, plan_review_T14.md, and plan_review_hedge.md, plus deterministic operator-attested coaching in src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Initialize or open a client repository that uses rebar but does not contain rebar's docs/adr files.
2. Create a work ticket whose acceptance criteria require ticket-recorded operational evidence without the [operator-attested] tag.
3. Run rebar review-plan for that ticket with the bundled plan-review criteria.
4. Observe a finding or suggested fix that justifies the required tag by citing "ADR 0043" or "ADR-0043."

## Expected Behavior
The finding explains the applicable rule in self-contained language: operational evidence recorded on the ticket requires the exact [operator-attested] tag and concrete specifics. It does not require the client to know or locate a rebar-internal ADR.

## Actual Behavior
Reviewer prompt text and deterministic coaching can emit rebar-internal ADR identifiers in client-facing findings, impacts, suggested fixes, remediation, or coaching.

## Approach
Replace rebar-internal ADR citations in reviewer-facing prompt instructions and deterministic finding/coaching templates with self-contained plain-language rules. Preserve the underlying behavior, such as requiring the exact [operator-attested] tag and concrete ticket evidence, but explain it without assuming knowledge of rebar's design history.

Add a portability regression that runs plan review against a fixture client repository with no rebar docs/adr tree and asserts that reviewer-authored finding, impact, suggested-fix, remediation, and coaching text contains no rebar-internal ADR identifier. Add a source-level contract test covering bundled plan-review prompt text and deterministic user-facing message templates so future internal provenance references cannot leak into client output. Internal Python comments, rebar's own ADR documents, and client-authored/cited ADRs that exist in the target repository remain allowed.

Rejected: shipping or linking rebar's ADR corpus to every client. That would expose implementation history instead of making findings self-contained and would still couple client guidance to rebar internals.

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T13.md
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T14.md
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_hedge.md
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py
- tests/unit/test_plan_review_portability.py

## Testing
- Deterministic path: an untagged operational-evidence AC still produces actionable coaching, but no rebar ADR identifier.
- LLM prompt path: the fixture client has no rebar ADR files; generated finding fields state the applicable rule in plain language.
- Source contract: bundled plan-review prompt bodies and deterministic client-facing templates reject rebar-internal ADR tokens while permitting internal code comments and an ADR citation grounded in a client fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An operator-attested plan-review fixture produces the same criterion decision before and after the wording change; verified by pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_portability.py.
- [ ] Reviewer-authored finding, impact, suggested_fix, remediation, and coaching fields for a client fixture with no rebar ADR files contain no rebar-internal ADR identifier; verified by pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_portability.py.
- [ ] Bundled plan-review prompt bodies and deterministic user-facing message templates contain no rebar-internal ADR citation; verified by pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_portability.py.
- [ ] A client-authored ADR citation backed by a file in the target repository remains eligible as grounded evidence; verified by pytest -q tests/unit/test_plan_review_portability.py.
- [ ] Internal implementation comments and docs/adr files remain outside the portability restriction; verified by the source-contract test's explicit scan scope.
- [ ] The default non-integration suite exits zero; verified by pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q.
baseline.summary: Plan-review findings leak rebar-internal ADR references

# OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts

## Context

rebar is technically near-1.0 (PyPI Trusted Publishing + PEP 740 attestations, immutable releases, `docs/api-stability.md` stability matrix, event-schema forward-compat) but the public contribution funnel is closed: GitHub (navapbc/rebar) is a read-only mirror with Issues and Discussions disabled (verified via API 2026-07-09: `has_issues: false`), and while CONTRIBUTING.md already documents an external Gerrit path (§1–§3), there is no GitHub-side intake, no governance/DCO/review-policy artifacts, and no user-facing changelog. Three converging assessments (internal repo audit; an external deep-research report; peer research across Go, Chromium, Qt, LibreOffice, Wikimedia, OpenStack, Eclipse) identify public intake + written governance as the only blockers to a credible v1.0.0.

Peer convergence establishes the design: KEEP Gerrit — Wikimedia reversed its GitLab migration in June 2024 over the review model (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/GitLab/Migration_status), JGit/EGit migrated TO GerritHub rather than accept PRs (https://gitenterprise.me/2023/11/21/14-years-of-jgit-egit-code-reviews-migrated-to-gerrithub/) — and pair the wall with a ramp: bot-answered PRs (LibreOffice/Wikimedia pattern), a first-change tutorial, a shepherded-patch fallback, GitHub Issues as zero-friction intake (Go's model), DCO enforced at the Gerrit server (OpenStack TC resolution 2025-05-20, https://governance.openstack.org/tc/resolutions/20250520-replace-the-cla-with-dco-for-all-contributions.html), and skipped non-convergent ceremony (CODEOWNERS, GPG-signed tags, RC trains — each a recorded non-goal with rationale in a child).

Stars/forks/contributor counts are explicitly OUT of scope; success is artifact completeness and funnel quality.

Cross-child protocols (binding on all children):
- **Vote-semantics single source:** `docs/review-policy.md` (child wrathful-preregal-blobfish) is the sole authoritative DOCUMENT for Gerrit vote semantics; its table's content is transcribed from the code enums (`_TAG_SUFFIXES` in adapter.py + the merge-path tags in voter.py) — document-of-record and source-of-truth are distinct and both are named. Every other doc links to it rather than duplicating the table. Until it lands, CONTRIBUTING.md §2c remains the interim authority.
- **Ownership inversion for cross-links:** a child that CREATES a doc never forward-links to a sibling's not-yet-existing doc; the sibling that creates the later doc owns adding links into earlier docs. Dependency edges: PR-posture and review-policy each depend_on the onboarding tutorial (their artifacts link it).
- **Decisions live in the repo**, not only on tickets: design decisions are recorded as ADRs under `docs/adr/` or in the owning doc (e.g. `docs/releasing.md`), with a ticket comment pointing at the artifact.
- **Shepherded-patch DCO interplay:** a shepherded contribution needs the ORIGINAL author's `Signed-off-by` (contributor runs `git commit -s` before `git format-patch`) plus the shepherd's own sign-off added on amend — the OpenStack two-trailer convention; documented in both the DCO and PR-posture children.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All nine child stories closed: GitHub intake; PR posture; onboarding tutorial + CONTRIBUTING; README front door; DCO; governance docs; review policy; CHANGELOG; release hygiene / 1.0 declaration.
- [ ] The four pre-flight experiments (E1 fork-side UX with has_pull_requests=false; E2 Gerrit Forge Author ACL; E3 PR-event dependency audit; E4 rebar-ticket trailer policy for shepherded patches) are executed AND each dependent child's design is updated or explicitly confirmed against the outcome (outcome-framed: an experiment that invalidates an assumption must change the affected child before that child is worked). E3-discovered breakage is fixed (or ticketed via discovered_from) by the PR-posture child.
- [ ] The `docs/api-stability.md` pre-1.0 caveat flip and the Development Status classifier bump are staged for the v1.0.0 release change (release-hygiene child names the landing vehicle).
- [ ] Final consistency audit (epic-level, before epic close, owned by the epic executor): re-read CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, SUPPORT.md, README.md, and all new docs as one set; verify no artifact contradicts the Gerrit-primary workflow or another artifact (including the vote-semantics single-source rule); record the audit result as an epic comment.
- [ ] Cross-link completeness: `docs/release-notes.md` carries a pointer to CHANGELOG.md (owned by the changelog child); every new doc is reachable from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md.
- [ ] GitHub intake works and is self-explanatory: Issues enabled with structured forms; an issue can be filed with no Gerrit account, no local checkout, and no knowledge beyond the form itself (verifiable from the rendered chooser, not a timing claim).
- [ ] The path from GitHub to a merged Gerrit change is documented end-to-end in one tutorial an outsider can follow with zero Nava-internal knowledge (measured by concrete checks in the onboarding child, e.g. no references to internal-only groups/layouts on the happy path).
- [ ] A no-Gerrit patch fallback is published. Authorship preservation via `git am` is promised only if experiment E2 confirms Gerrit's Forge Author permission is (or can be) granted; if E2 fails, the documented fallback is `Co-authored-by:` credit and the policy text says so (go/no-go, not an unconditional promise).
- [ ] Governance, review policy, DCO, and maintainer info are published, each grounded in a named peer convention (curl/CNCF, Chromium-CQ/Zuul, OpenStack/moby — URLs in the children).
- [ ] Release artifacts (CHANGELOG, dependabot, README front door, 1.0 declaration mechanics) match documented 2026 Python-tool convergence.
baseline.summary: OSS v1.0.0 community front door — contribution intake, governance, and release artifacts

## Context / Problem

`criterion_prompt_id` — the single logical→physical criterion-id map both review gates
delegate to — hardcodes the plan-review prompt prefix (`PLAN_REVIEW_PROMPT_PREFIX = "plan-review-"`
at `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:31`, applied unconditionally at `ids.py:42`). So a project
**code-review** criterion resolves into the plan-review prompt namespace, the first of five seams
that drop project code-review criteria (root cause on superseded bug 8a4b). This is the shared
abstraction the other four seams consume, so it lands first.

## Approach

Make the resolver gate-aware, additively:

- Add a keyword-only `gate_key: str = "plan_review"` parameter to
  `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id, *, gate_key="plan_review")`.
- Introduce a `_PROMPT_PREFIX = {"plan_review": "plan-review-", "code_review": "code-review-"}`
  map in `ids.py`; select the prefix by `gate_key`; an unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`
  (imported from `rebar.llm.criteria.model`, confirmed present at
  `src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py`).
- The `.`→`-` namespace rewrite is unchanged, so `project.foo` + `code_review` →
  `code-review-project-foo` and stays filesystem-safe and injective per the existing charset
  invariant documented in the module docstring.

The default `"plan_review"` preserves today's behavior byte-for-byte, so the two existing callers
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:302`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:487`)
need **no** change and plan-review parity is guaranteed by construction. Code-review call sites
(introduced by the fan-in and eval children) pass `gate_key="code_review"` explicitly.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Making `gate_key` *required* — it would force editing
`eval.py:419`'s existing call, colliding with the eval-admission child's file set and breaking the
disjoint-file decomposition; the default is the historically-correct value, not a silent bug. (b)
Registering the prefix on the gate via `criteria.overlay.register_gate` — adds import-order
coupling to gate registration for no caller benefit; the forward-only map is the pattern the
module docstring already commits to.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py` — add `gate_key` param + `_PROMPT_PREFIX` map.
- `tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py` — NEW file; the shared test file later
  children extend. This child adds the resolver unit tests only.

## Testing

- Happy path: `criterion_prompt_id("project.foo", gate_key="code_review") == "code-review-project-foo"`;
  `criterion_prompt_id("F1", gate_key="plan_review") == "plan-review-F1"`.
- Parity/default: `criterion_prompt_id("F1") == "plan-review-F1"` (no `gate_key` given) — existing
  plan-review behavior unchanged.
- Edge: an unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`; cross-gate injectivity — no code-review
  project id collides with any plan-review physical id.

Tier: unit (pure function, no I/O).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id("project.foo", gate_key="code_review")` returns
      `"code-review-project-foo"`; verified by
      `rtk .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k resolver`.
- [ ] `criterion_prompt_id("F1")` (no gate_key) still returns `"plan-review-F1"`, proving
      plan-review parity; verified by the same `-k resolver` selector.
- [ ] An unknown `gate_key` raises `CriteriaError`; verified by the same `-k resolver` selector.
baseline.summary: Gate-key the criterion-id resolver (criterion_prompt_id)

# 1.0 release hygiene: dependabot, classifier bump, stability-promise flip, RC skip (tag signing: explicit skip)

## Why

Final mechanical artifacts for the 1.0 declaration, sized to what 2026 peers actually do — which REVERSES two earlier assumptions. (1) Signed git tags are no longer convergent: of CPython/pip/ruff/uv/pytest/httpx, zero sign new release tags in 2026 (CPython dropped GPG at 3.14 per PEP 761; ruff/uv/httpx use lightweight tags); the baseline is annotated tags + GitHub immutable releases + PEP 740 attestations — all already in place here. (2) RC trains are not convergent: pydantic v2 shipped beta→final in 13 days with zero rcs; attrs/structlog skipped 1.0 entirely; the load-bearing artifact is the written compatibility policy, which `docs/api-stability.md` already is.

## What

- `.github/dependabot.yml`: `github-actions` ecosystem ONLY, `interval: monthly`, one catch-all group. The `cooldown` key is **intentionally omitted** — it is in production use in pip's own config (https://github.com/pypa/pip/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml), but its schema status was disputed in review and its value here is marginal (it only delays update PRs a few days); omitting it removes any dependence on a contested feature. Revisit trigger: update-PR noise. Record this omission decision as one line in the file header.
- **Mirror-interaction decision (recorded in the file header + docs/releasing.md):** this config shape is the pip/pydantic GitHub-native pattern — NOT what Gerrit peers do (they run bespoke bots pushing bumps as Gerrit changes: Wikimedia LibraryUpgrader, OpenStack requirements automation). Since Dependabot's output is a GitHub PR and PRs cannot merge here, Dependabot PRs are ADVISORY NOTIFICATIONS: the maintainer reads the diff, lands the equivalent bump via a Gerrit change, and closes the PR — Dependabot is another shepherded patch author under the PR-as-intake posture. The lockdown workflow exempts `dependabot[bot]` — owned by story **nonsecular-arthritic-sidewinder** (artifact: `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml`, job-level actor guard); this file's header names that workflow file explicitly. Rejected alternatives, one line each in the header: bespoke Gerrit-pushing bot (peer pattern; overkill for a monthly actions-only stream — captured as idea misogynic-cerulean-goldfish); alerts-only with no version-update PRs (loses the ready-made diff; security alerts fire regardless and remain on). No `pip` ecosystem entry — version updates act on pins/lockfiles; rebar's unpinned `>=` core deps give them nothing but noise (rationale in header). Add a `uv` block only if a `uv.lock` is ever committed.
- Staged for the v1.0.0 release change: bump `Development Status :: 4 - Beta` → `5 - Production/Stable` (pyproject classifier) and flip the pre-1.0 caveat in `docs/api-stability.md` so the stability matrix becomes the operative SemVer promise. **Durable staging record (in-repo, not a ticket promise):** `docs/releasing.md` gains a "1.0 declaration" subsection stating exactly these two edits land in the v1.0.0 release change itself, so the requirement survives independent of any tracker.
- `docs/releasing.md` decision records:
  - Tag signing: SKIPPED, with rationale (2026 peer baseline; attestations cover artifact provenance) and revisit triggers (workflow compromise entering the threat model, or a downstream consumer asking to verify tags). Confirm annotated tags remain the practice and immutable releases stay on.
  - RC: SKIPPED (the recorded decision). Rationale: an RC only yields data if someone runs it; with no external adopters, `--pre` installs ≈ 0 and `1.0.1` is the de-facto rc. Revisit trigger: an external adopter volunteering to test. Conditional constraint recorded alongside (today's automation is RC-unsafe): `release.yml` fires on ALL `v*` tags, passes `--latest` unconditionally to `gh release create`, and runs the MCP-registry publish job — a hypothetical `v1.0.0rc1` tag would be marked Latest AND published to the MCP registry. The note must state: no rc-form tag may be pushed unless release.yml first gains a prerelease guard (detect `rc` in the tag → `--prerelease`, not `--latest`; skip the MCP-registry job). PEP 440 spelling (`1.0.0rc1`, not `-rc.1`) used in the constraint text. This story does NOT modify release.yml.
  - Deferral list as non-goals: SBOM/license-scan tooling beyond GitHub's dependency-graph export; Renovate (see idea misogynic-cerulean-goldfish); a lockfile for optional extras (revisit post-1.0).
- Verify at execution: `git tag -l 'v*'` shows no pre-existing rc-form tags contradicting the note.

## Scope

IN: `.github/dependabot.yml`; docs/releasing.md decision records (tag signing, RC skip + guard constraint, 1.0-declaration staging subsection, deferrals).
OUT: modifying release.yml; executing the release (the classifier bump + api-stability flip are EXECUTED in the 1.0 release change, not here — here they are only recorded as staged); contract-freeze code work (exit codes / error envelope / MCP schema pin — tracked elsewhere); SBOM tooling; CI matrix changes (Windows explicitly out — classifiers claim POSIX/macOS, consistent today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dependabot.yml` committed — prove: `test -f .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -c "package-ecosystem" .github/dependabot.yml` = 1; `grep -q "github-actions" .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -q "interval: monthly" .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -q 'patterns' .github/dependabot.yml`; `grep -qv "cooldown" .github/dependabot.yml` (key omitted) and the header comment records the omission decision — prove: `grep -qi "cooldown" .github/dependabot.yml` matches only in a comment line.
- [ ] Advisory-PR flow documented — prove: `grep -qi "advisory" .github/dependabot.yml` and `grep -q "lockdown.yml" .github/dependabot.yml` (header names the exemption artifact); `grep -qi "gerrit" .github/dependabot.yml`.
- [ ] Dependabot accepts the config — prove: after push, the Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot view shows the update job scheduled with no config-parse error.
- [ ] docs/releasing.md decisions present — prove: `grep -qi "tag signing" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -q "1.0.0rc1" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -q -- "--latest" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -qi "SBOM" docs/releasing.md`; `grep -qi "renovate" docs/releasing.md`.
- [ ] 1.0-declaration staging subsection present — prove: `grep -qi "Production/Stable" docs/releasing.md` and `grep -q "api-stability" docs/releasing.md` (the subsection names both staged edits and their landing vehicle).
- [ ] No rc-form tags exist — prove: `git tag -l | grep -c rc` = 0.
baseline.summary: 1.0 release hygiene: dependabot, classifier bump, stability-promise flip, RC decision

content.text: ## Context
rebar hard-codes the git remote name `origin` at every ticket-branch network site,
so the shared ticket store MUST be reachable as `origin`. In our split-residency
setup (code reviewed via a `gerrit` remote; the `tickets` branch's source of truth
on GitHub for the GitHub Actions -> Jira sync) this forces `origin`=GitHub and
leaves no config seam. Parallels the earlier `tickets_branch()` migration (closed
task `rich-gravel-twain`) which centralized the *branch* name; this does the same
for the *remote* name.
## What
Add a `sync.remote` config key (default `"origin"`), resolved through the normal
precedence (config-file `[sync] remote` + `REBAR_SYNC_REMOTE` env, the same generic
mechanism as `sync.push`), exposed via a `tickets_remote()` helper mirroring
`tickets_branch()`, and thread it through every currently-hardcoded site.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `SyncConfig` gains `remote: str = "origin"` and `_SECTIONS["sync"]` coerces it
in `src/rebar/config.py`; `REBAR_SYNC_REMOTE` works via the existing generic
env layer (no bespoke env wiring) and participates in the config-cache signature.
- [ ] New `config.tickets_remote(root)` helper mirrors `config.tickets_branch(root)`.
- [ ] Every hard-coded `"origin"` network site uses the resolved remote:
`src/rebar/_store/push.py` (presence guard + push/fetch/ref),
`src/rebar/_store/sync.py` (`reconverge` fetch/verify + `_do_reconverge`),
`src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` (`_push_pending`),
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` (`_mount_or_create_branch` and
`pending_init_attaches_to_existing`).
- [ ] Default behavior is unchanged when unset (still `origin`); the existing suite passes.
- [ ] New unit tests cover: default resolves to `origin`; `[sync] remote` config and

content.text: ## Why

Epic 88ab (elfish-chair-lug) S1. The feature-branch pattern needs Gerrit-side changes: vote-carry for re-merges after main advances (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE), an explicitly pinned submit type (currently unset/inherited — FF-only or cherry-pick would defeat atomic merge-back), and a bounded write path for merge commits + feature branches.
## What

- `infra/gerrit/project.config`: LLM-Review `copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE`; Verified copyCondition UNCHANGED (re-run posture — rationale in the ADR).

- Record the CURRENT effective inherited submit type (ssh/REST query, noted on this ticket) BEFORE pinning `[submit] action = merge if necessary` + `mergeContent = true`; apply in a quiet window (no open changes targeting main).

- ACLs: `Create Reference` + `Delete Reference` on `refs/heads/feature/*`; `Push Merge Commit` on `refs/for/refs/heads/main` + `refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*`; ALL bound to a new named group `feature-branch-drivers`.
- `infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh`: extend the managed-groups `want` dict (~line 57, currently Administrators + Service Users only) so the group is created/resolved declaratively and idempotently.
- ADR amending ADR-0013 (+ the 1fa8 Verified ADR): merge-change gate design, label-divergence rationale, group membership policy.
- `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` gate/ACL sections.

Inherited plan-review findings (run 3): membership policy must be constrained in the ADR — initial members = repo admins + named operating agents; changes via admin-approved setup-project.sh edit (f8e6233f). Back-out wording: "no label/gate changes REQUIRED" — the copyCondition addition is inert absent merge changes (MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE cannot match a non-merge patchset) and may be left or reverted (f51eb171/f90d5449).
## Scope
Gerrit config + setup script + ADR + setup docs only. No bot code (S2), no CI/g2p (S3), no contributor docs (S4).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] copyCondition change applied declaratively (refs/meta/config) and accepted by the running Gerrit 3.14.1
- [ ] Current inherited submit type recorded on this ticket BEFORE the [submit] pin lands; pin applied in a quiet window
- [ ] `feature-branch-drivers` group exists holding exactly the three ACLs; `setup-project.sh` converges it idempotently on re-run
- [ ] ADR merged: gate design, Verified/LLM-Review divergence rationale, membership policy (initial members + change process), copyCondition back-out note

content.text: ## Why
MCP tools carry no behavior annotations, so clients cannot present safe UI or
confirmation flows. rebar already has the semantic information internally —
reads are separate from writes, writes are hidden under `REBAR_MCP_READONLY`,
Jira-live and LLM tools are call-gated — but none of it is exposed as the MCP
`ToolAnnotations` hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`,
`openWorldHint`) that the spec defines for exactly this purpose.
## What
Annotate every registered tool via `FastMCP.tool(annotations=ToolAnnotations(...))`
across the three registrars (`register_read_tools` in `_mcp_reads.py`,
`register_llm_tools` in `_mcp_llm.py`, `register_write_tools` in `_mcp_writes.py`).
Confirmed feasible: `mcp` 1.28.1 exposes `ToolAnnotations` with all four hint
fields and `FastMCP.tool` accepts `annotations`.
Mapping policy:
- **Read tools** -> `readOnlyHint: true`.
- **Additive writes** (create/comment/tag/link/edit/claim/transition/set_*) ->
`readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`; `idempotentHint: true` where
the op is idempotent (e.g. tag/untag).
- **Destructive/irreversible** (archive/delete/compact, reconcile-live) ->
`destructiveHint: true`.
- **Outward-reaching** (LLM review/verify, Jira reconcile, `run_workflow`) ->
`openWorldHint: true`.
## Scope
`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`, `_mcp_llm.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`. Annotations are hints
only — no behavior change. Add/adjust a parity test if the interface suite pins
tool metadata.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every `@mcp.tool()` in the three registrars carries a `ToolAnnotations`
consistent with the mapping policy above.
- [ ] Read tools are `readOnlyHint: true`; delete/archive/reconcile-live are
`destructiveHint: true`; LLM/Jira/workflow tools are `openWorldHint: true`.
- [ ] The server still builds and starts; existing MCP/interface tests pass.
- [ ] No functional behavior of any tool changes.

baseline.summary: Annotate MCP tools with behavior hints (read-only/destructive/idempotent/open-world)

baseline.description:
Activity-based liveness for LLM gate ops using `agent.run_sync()`-compatible mechanisms: a per-request READ timeout (bounds a hung MODEL, at the HTTP layer) + a per-TOOL timeout (bounds a hung ASYNC/MCP tool), layered on the step caps the runner ALREADY derives. NO total-runtime timeout, NO async stream-event watchdog (deferred).

## Why
A single hard total-runtime timeout truncates healthy multi-minute / large-context (1M-token) runs; liveness must be gauged by ACTIVITY, not total elapsed time. But the runner uses `agent.run_sync()` exclusively — a blocking synchronous call with no concurrent stream-event hooks. The async idle-watchdog pattern (LangGraph/Claude-SDK) needs `agent.run()`/`run_stream_events` + an event loop this runner does not have. So liveness is achieved at request+tool granularity WITHOUT asyncio.

## What
- **Per-request READ timeout (both execution modes — `single_turn` structured calls AND `agentic` tool-using runs) — the PRIMARY, verified mechanism.** Set `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` (a total of `cfg.timeout_s` with a tight connect) on the shared `httpx.AsyncClient` story arcticduck constructs, passed in via the EXISTING seam `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(..., http_timeout=<httpx.Timeout>)` (arcticduck committed that param in `runner.py` — review this story with `--ref` at the stack HEAD). This REUSES `cfg.timeout_s` (already the per-request budget, today wired only to `model_settings['timeout']`) — NO new `llm_request_timeout_s` key (would duplicate it). Bounds a HUNG MODEL (no bytes) — the real, common failure. VERIFIED under `run_sync` by arcticduck's spike (an httpx read/timeout fires at the transport). It is Anthropic-path-only (OpenAI/Google build their own httpx clients — acceptable; the gates run on Anthropic). NO duplication with `model_settings['timeout']`: on the ANTHROPIC path rebar uses arcticduck's CUSTOM `httpx.AsyncClient`, so THIS client's `httpx.Timeout` is the authoritative per-request bound; the pre-existing `model_settings['timeout'] = float(cfg.timeout_s)` (runner.py:288-289) governs the OTHER providers (OpenAI/Google), which use pydantic-ai's internally-built client, not ours. Same value, different provider paths — one authoritative mechanism per path, not two competing on one path. Interaction with the retry transport (correct, not a bug): a per-ATTEMPT read timeout raises `httpx.TimeoutException`, which is in arcticduck's retry set — so a transiently-slow model is retried; a PERSISTENTLY hung model times out each attempt, exhausts `llm_retry_max_attempts`, and surfaces `LLMUnavailableError` (classified WAIT_AND_RETRY by mamba). Bounded either way, no total-runtime cap.
- **Per-TOOL timeout — bounds ASYNC/MCP tools (an honest, verified scope).** Add `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` to the shared `Agent(...)` construction kwargs (flows to all three `Agent(model, **kwargs)` sites; a no-op on `single_turn` where `tools=[]`). VERIFIED offline: `Agent(tool_timeout=0.3)` CANCELS an ASYNC tool (`await asyncio.sleep(3)`) at ~0.3s — but is a NO-OP for a SYNC blocking tool (`time.sleep(3)` waited the full 3s), because pydantic-ai uses async cancellation which cannot interrupt sync code that blocks the loop. rebar's in-process tools (`filesystem_tools`, `rebar_tools`) are SYNC, so `tool_timeout` primarily protects MCP/network toolsets (async); the sync in-process tools are fast (file/ticket reads) and a looping/slow one is bounded instead by the step caps. When `tool_timeout` fires it CANCELS the tool and feeds a soft timeout error back to the MODEL (which adapts / can finish) — it is a liveness BOUND, not a run-aborting classified failure — it raises NO exception into the runner (so NO new classification arm is needed); the model simply receives a tool error and proceeds. This honest scope (async-tool bound + sync-tool caveat) is the correction over an earlier over-claim.
- **Step caps: ALREADY PRESENT — reused, not re-added.** The runner already derives `request_limit = max(1, ceil(max_iterations/2))` and `tool_calls_limit = max(8, max_iterations)` from `cfg.max_iterations` and applies them via `UsageLimits` on `run_sync` (pinned by arawana). Those DERIVED caps ARE the runaway-loop bound and the backstop for a repeatedly-slow sync tool; this story adds NO duplicate limit config knobs.
- **Deferred (ADR content only, NOT built):** the sub-event stream-idle-watchdog needs the async `agent.run()` migration, conflicting with the exclusive `run_sync` design. This story authors the ADR CONTENT at `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (placeholder number; blackbear, sole ADR owner, records/numbers it) with Context/Decision/Consequences on why it is deferred.

## Verification (probes that actually cross the mechanism)
- **Read timeout:** a MockTransport whose handler sleeps past a small `read` timeout trips `httpx.ReadTimeout` UNDER `agent.run_sync()` (the arcticduck seam), proving it fires in the synchronous runner; a MockTransport that responds JUST UNDER the read timeout completes normally (healthy-long-run not aborted).
- **Tool timeout:** an `Agent(tool_timeout=<small>)` with a deliberately-sleeping ASYNC tool is CANCELLED at ~the timeout (asserted by elapsed << tool sleep); the run continues (soft error to the model). A companion assertion documents that a SYNC blocking tool is NOT interrupted (the known caveat) — so the test pins reality, not an over-claim.
- **No total-runtime / no-asyncio:** a test greps the gate path to assert no total-runtime timer and no new event loop / `asyncio.run` in the agentic run path beyond the existing teardown.

## Scope
- ONE new `LLMConfig` key: `llm_tool_timeout_s` (default 120), read via `_llm_int` from `[llm]` + `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`. The per-request read timeout REUSES `cfg.timeout_s` (no new key). Regenerate `docs/env-vars.md`; add `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S` to `test_config_llm.py`'s `_clean` fixture; document both in `docs/config.md`.
- Wire `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` into arcticduck's `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(http_timeout=...)`; add `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` to the shared `Agent(...)` kwargs.
- NOT in scope: any total-runtime cap (rejected); the async stream-event watchdog (deferred, ADR content only); new step-cap config knobs (derived caps already exist); making rebar's sync tools async or thread-cancellable (a follow-on if sync-tool bounding is ever needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `LLMConfig.llm_tool_timeout_s` (120) exists, read from `[llm]` + `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S`; the per-request read timeout reuses `cfg.timeout_s` (no duplicate key). `docs/env-vars.md` regenerated (drift gate passes); `REBAR_LLM_TOOL_TIMEOUT_S` in `test_config_llm.py`'s `_clean` fixture.
- [ ] `httpx.Timeout(read=cfg.timeout_s, connect=10.0, write=30.0, pool=10.0)` is passed into `_build_retrying_anthropic_model(http_timeout=...)` for both execution modes (single_turn + agentic); a sleeping MockTransport trips `httpx.ReadTimeout` under `run_sync` (probe), and a just-under-timeout MockTransport completes normally (healthy run not aborted).
- [ ] `tool_timeout=cfg.llm_tool_timeout_s` is on the shared `Agent(...)` kwargs; a sleeping ASYNC tool is cancelled at ~the timeout (probe), with a companion assertion documenting the sync-tool no-op caveat.
- [ ] No total-runtime timeout and no new asyncio event loop are introduced in the gate path (asserted by a grep/structural test); the existing derived step caps (arawana) are unchanged.
- [ ] The deferred-async-watchdog ADR CONTENT exists at `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (Context/Decision/Consequences; numbered/recorded by blackbear).
- [ ] `make test`/`make lint`/`make typecheck` green.

Files: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` (build+pass `httpx.Timeout`; add `tool_timeout` to the shared Agent kwargs), `src/rebar/llm/config.py` (one LLMConfig key + `from_env`), `docs/config.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` (regenerated), `docs/adr/00XX-async-liveness-watchdog.md` (content), `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py` (`_clean`), `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py` (new — read-timeout + async-tool-timeout + sync-caveat + no-total-runtime probes).

## Verified library behavior (experiment log — pydantic-ai 1.107.0, httpx 0.28.1, offline)
ACTUAL captured output (no billable call):
```
Agent.__init__ has tool_timeout: True;  Agent.run_sync has usage_limits: True
httpx.Timeout(600.0, read=300.0, connect=10.0).read == 300.0   (per-request read timeout settable)
UsageLimits fields include total_tokens_limit
Agent(tool_timeout=0.3) + ASYNC tool (await asyncio.sleep(3)) -> CANCELLED at 0.31s, run continues ('done')
Agent(tool_timeout=0.3) + SYNC  tool (time.sleep(3))        -> NOT interrupted, waited 3.02s (async cancel can't stop sync)
rebar tools (filesystem_tools/rebar_tools) are SYNC defs    -> tool_timeout bounds MCP/async tools, not these
arcticduck committed _build_retrying_anthropic_model(..., http_timeout=) in runner.py (the wiring seam)
```
These are pydantic-ai/httpx LIBRARY facts (not rebar symbols; bug succinct-formable-kite). The read
timeout on the shared client is the primary hung-MODEL bound (verified via arcticduck's spike); the
tool timeout is an honest async/MCP-tool bound with a documented sync no-op caveat.
baseline.summary: Activity-based liveness: per-request timeout + step caps + idle-watchdog (no total-runtime timeout)

content.text: # T1 — Provenance plumbing: carry source_* through the write path + surface in ticket_state
## Context
Foundation for P1.2 rebar→rebar migration (epic rule-swamp-pupil / ab74-b205-72af-4ce1).
Import must preserve original id/date/author/env as provenance WITHOUT injecting foreign
HLC timestamps. CREATE and COMMENT event payloads must be able to carry optional
`source_*` fields; the reducer must read them and surface them in `ticket_state`.
Public write APIs build event `data` internally (`_commands/composer.py:132-144`,
`_commands/leaf.py:57`), so the plumbing spans BOTH the composer/leaf write layer and
the reducer processors. Additive + forward-compatible (no new event types).
## What
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` — `create_core` accepts optional `source_id`,
`source_created_at`, `source_author`, `source_env`; when present, write them into the
CREATE event `data`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py` — the COMMENT leaf accepts optional `source_comment_id`,
`source_author`, `source_created_at`; write into COMMENT `data` when present.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_state.py` — initial state seeds `source_*` keys (default None).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` — `process_create` reads the four `source_*` from
`data`; `process_comment` reads per-comment source fields onto the comment entry.
- `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json` + `common.schema.json` — document the new
optional fields (ticket-level `source_*`; per-comment `source_*`).
- `src/rebar/reducer/_present.py` — ensure `public_state()` does NOT strip the new fields.
## Scope
In: the optional pass-through + surfacing only. Out: export/import modules (T2/T3),
any CLI surface. No behavior change when source_* are absent.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CREATE event with `source_id`/`source_created_at`/`source_author`/`source_env` in
`data` round-trips: `reduce_ticket` surfaces all four in `ticket_state`.
- [ ] COMMENT with per-comment source fields surfaces them on the comment entry.
- [ ] Absent source_* → fields are None/omitted; existing `ticket_state` output unchanged
(no regression in the full test suite).
- [ ] `ticket_state.schema.json` / `common.schema.json` validate the new optional fields.
- [ ] New reducer test exercises CREATE+COMMENT provenance surfacing; `pytest` green.

baseline.summary: T1 — Provenance plumbing: source_* through write path + ticket_state

baseline.description:
## Context / Problem

The AWS Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot (`src/rebar/review_bot/`) makes billable LLM calls on
every patchset review but records **no token usage** in any retrievable form. Per-call token
usage is computed by the runner (`_extract_usage` → `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`,
`cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `requests`; `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`) and attached
as `result["_usage"]`, but the review path discards the token fields: the code-review metrics
assembler reads `_usage` only for the verifier **request count**
(`src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:157`, `verify_requests`), and the voter never reads
usage at all. The bot already publishes CloudWatch *error* counts via a best-effort boto3
pattern (`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:88-102`, `:145-165`), so there is an established seam
to emit token counts the same way — it is simply not wired for usage.

Goal: have the bot read `_usage` and emit token counts to CloudWatch.

**Coverage scope (explicit).** This ticket captures the token usage that is already surfaced
on the review's **agent** step outputs — Pass-2 `verify` and Pass-3 `decide`
(`finalize.py:143-162` already iterates these and reads their `_usage`). The Pass-1 **finder
batch** does NOT surface per-finder `_usage` on its step output
(`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py:168-177` emits `findings`/`criteria_count`
but no `_usage`; the shared `run_pass1` returns only `findings`,
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:548`), and threading finder usage through that shared
plan-review path is a larger, riskier change. So the emitted totals are the review's
agent-step token usage, labelled as such, and a follow-up ticket is filed (linked
`discovered_from`) to surface Pass-1 finder usage for a complete total. This is strictly
better than today's zero token visibility and does not misrepresent the number.

Edit-set:
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py`
- `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`
- *new* `tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_metrics.py`

## Approach

1. `finalize.py` `_attach_code_review_metrics`: in the existing `rec.steps` loop that already
   reads `outputs["_usage"]`, aggregate the token fields across **every succeeded step that
   exposes `_usage`** (not just the verify request count). Add to `coverage["metrics"]`:
   `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and
   `total_tokens` (= input + output). Keep `verify_requests` unchanged. This also enriches the
   persisted `code_review` artifact (which serializes `coverage.metrics`), so the data is
   retrievable both in CloudWatch and in the artifact. The addition is additive and tolerant of
   steps without `_usage` (contributes 0).
2. `voter.py`: add `_publish_token_usage_metrics(metrics: dict)` — best-effort boto3
   `put_metric_data` to `Namespace="rebar/host"`, one `MetricData` entry per token field
   (`review_bot_llm_input_tokens`, `review_bot_llm_output_tokens`,
   `review_bot_llm_cache_read_tokens`, `review_bot_llm_cache_write_tokens`,
   `review_bot_llm_total_tokens`; `Unit: "Count"`), swallowing any ImportError/boto/credential
   error exactly like `_publish_voter_error_metric` (`voter.py:88-102`). Also emit a greppable
   `LLM_TOKEN_USAGE ` JSON line to stderr/journald for the reliable host-probe fallback,
   mirroring the error markers. Call it after a **successful** vote (in `review_and_vote`, right
   after the `voter_voted` emit, ~`voter.py:644-657`), reading the totals from
   `decision["verdict"]["coverage"]["metrics"]` (the verdict is threaded up at
   `src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:219`). Best-effort: the vote is already cast, so emission
   never fails the review (wrapped, swallowed, logged) — same contract as artifact emission.

Rejected: threading Pass-1 finder `_usage` through `run_pass1` now (shared plan-review path,
signature change, thread-pool aggregation) — deferred to the linked follow-up. Rejected a
process-global `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`/accumulator to capture all calls — the bot reviews changes
concurrently, so a process-global sink would interleave usage across reviews.

## Scope

- Emits **token counts only** (input/output/cache/total tokens + the existing request count).
  No dollar cost (no token→USD price table exists in the repo).
- CloudWatch emission is **best-effort** and swallowed on any failure — identical fail-open
  contract to the existing error-metric publishers; a metric failure never affects the vote.
- Covers Pass-2 verify + Pass-3 decide agent-step usage (see Coverage scope above); Pass-1
  finder usage is a linked follow-up.
- No change to voting logic, thresholds, dedup, or the artifact schema beyond the additive
  `coverage.metrics` token keys.

## Testing

New `tests/unit/test_review_bot_token_metrics.py` (offline; no live LLM, no real AWS):
- `finalize`: build a fake step-recorder (`rec.steps`) with agent steps carrying `_usage`
  dicts and assert `_attach_code_review_metrics` sums `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/
  `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens`/`total_tokens` into `coverage["metrics"]`, and that a
  record with no `_usage` yields zeros (tolerant). Mirrors the metrics assertions in
  `tests/unit/test_code_review_fp_ledger.py` / `tests/unit/test_findings_finalize.py`.
- `voter`: monkeypatch a fake `boto3` module capturing `put_metric_data` calls and assert
  `_publish_token_usage_metrics({...})` emits the five named metrics with the right values to
  `Namespace="rebar/host"`; assert that when `boto3` import/credentials fail the call swallows
  the error (returns without raising). Mirrors the boto3-absence tolerance the existing
  publishers document (`voter.py:101`).
- Optionally assert (via the existing `review_and_vote` test harness in
  `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`) that a successful vote invokes the token publisher with the
  verdict's `coverage.metrics`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_attach_code_review_metrics` adds `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`,
      `cache_write_tokens`, and `total_tokens` to `coverage["metrics"]`, summed across all
      `_usage`-bearing succeeded steps; verified by the finalize unit test asserting exact sums.
- [ ] A step record with no `_usage` contributes 0 and never raises; verified by the tolerance
      unit test.
- [ ] `voter._publish_token_usage_metrics` emits exactly the five `review_bot_llm_*_tokens`
      metrics to `Namespace="rebar/host"` with `Unit="Count"` and values from the passed
      metrics dict; verified by the fake-boto3 unit test capturing `put_metric_data`.
- [ ] `_publish_token_usage_metrics` swallows a boto3 import/credential/network failure without
      raising; verified by the boto3-absence unit test.
- [ ] `review_and_vote` calls the token publisher after a successful vote using
      `decision["verdict"]["coverage"]["metrics"]`; verified by the voter harness test (or an
      equivalent direct assertion).
- [ ] A follow-up ticket for Pass-1 finder token capture is created and linked
      `discovered_from` this ticket.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass; `finalize.py` and `voter.py` stay
      ≤ 800 LOC; the change lands via Gerrit with `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`.
baseline.summary: Review bot: read _usage and emit token counts to CloudWatch
