# Sweep: CLI surface (_cli/, _commands/) — diagnostics to stderr, KEEP stdout data prints

The CLI surface is where stdout `print(json.dumps(...))` data output legitimately lives — that is a
machine contract and MUST stay on stdout (the reconciler `json.loads` it). Only migrate *diagnostic*
stderr prints. Most excepts here re-raise `CommandError` (low risk).

## What
- Audit prints in `src/rebar/_cli/` and `src/rebar/_commands/`: classify each as stdout DATA (keep as
  `print`) vs stderr DIAGNOSTIC (migrate to the named logger). Do not move data output off stdout.
- Bring broad-excepts in these packages to the observability floor (log `exc_info` or justified noqa).
- Confirm the T201 per-file-ignore for the CLI presentation layer is correct (data prints allowed here).
- Remove these packages from the BLE001 allowlist as they become conformant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Stdout data `print(json.dumps(...))` output in `_cli/`/`_commands/` is unchanged (contract intact).
- [ ] Diagnostic stderr prints migrate to the logger; broad-excepts meet the observability floor.
- [ ] The T201 per-file-ignore covers the CLI presentation layer; library/core/MCP stay print-free.
- [ ] These packages removed from the BLE001 allowlist; `make lint` + full test suite pass.
baseline.summary: Sweep: CLI surface (_cli, _commands) — diagnostics to stderr, keep stdout data prints

baseline.description:
# Enforce release-source authorization + version lockstep before publication

Re-anchor the release to the proven OSS pattern (uv model): a single `workflow_dispatch`-from-`main` workflow that asserts version-lockstep + ancestry, then **builds and publishes directly** via PyPA Trusted Publishing (OIDC — no long-lived secret, no tag relay), gated on a required-reviewers `pypi` environment re-keyed from "v* tags only" to "`main` via dispatch". The source is reviewed-and- landed `main` **by construction**. (Readiness Finding 1 — verified VALID against `release.yml:17-21`, `infra/terraform-github/main.tf:23-101`, `docs/releasing.md`.)

## Why

`main` is constrained to the Gerrit replication deploy key, but `refs/tags/v*` was deliberately left open (`infra/terraform-github/main.tf:23-28`) so a human can push a `v*` tag to drive PyPI + MCP-registry + GitHub-Release publication (`release.yml:17-21`, jobs `build`/`publish`/`github_release`/`mcp_registry`). The only gate anywhere is `if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` (release.yml:53/81/116) — nothing checks that the tagged SHA is an ancestor of (or equal to) reviewed `main`, verifies any Gerrit/CI result for that exact SHA, or asserts version consistency. A PEP 740 attestation would correctly name this repo's workflow but cannot distinguish a tag on reviewed `main` from a tag on any other commit. Separately, the three version values (`pyproject.toml:10`, `server.json` top-level and `packages[].version`) are kept in lockstep only by a manual runbook (`docs/releasing.md`), so a future mismatch would publish disagreeing versions across the PyPI / GitHub-Release / MCP channels with no machine check.

## What

Adopt uv's proven release process and pydantic's pre-build version check, in this order of control strength:

- **Primary control — initiate from `main` via `workflow_dispatch` (source reviewed
  by construction).** Make `workflow_dispatch` the sanctioned release trigger, run
  from the `main` ref. Because the GitHub mirror's `main` is exactly the
  Gerrit-reviewed-and-landed history, releasing from `main` guarantees the source is
  reviewed **by construction** — the same guarantee the wider OSS world gets from
  "release only from the protected branch." This replaces "accept whatever commit an
  arbitrary pushed tag points at," which was the actual divergence from consensus.
- **Version-lockstep, before build (pydantic pattern).** A first job parses the
  intended version and every manifest and asserts exact equality **before build**:
  `version_input == project.version == server.json.version ==
  each server.json.packages[].version`; mismatch fails before build.
- **Ancestry assertion (belt-and-suspenders).** In the same dispatch job, assert the
  checked-out `main` HEAD is reachable from `origin/main` via
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main` (checkout with
  `fetch-depth: 0` + `git fetch origin main`, since a shallow clone defeats ancestry —
  the repo documents this at `reconcile-bridge.yml:83-88` and `verify-identity.yaml`
  already uses `fetch-depth: 0`). With dispatch-from-`main` this is redundant with the
  ref guard, kept as defense-in-depth.
- **Build, then publish DIRECTLY via PyPA Trusted Publishing — no tag relay.** The
  same workflow builds and then publishes using OIDC (`id-token: write`, the existing
  `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` trusted-publishing flow). There is **no** intermediate
  tag push: a tag pushed by the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` would not trigger a downstream
  workflow anyway (GitHub's anti-recursion rule), so a two-phase relay is avoided
  entirely, and no PAT / GitHub App secret is introduced.
- **Compose with — do not regress — F3 and F4 (this story lands last).** Per the
  dependency chain (F4 → F3 → F1), this story edits `release.yml` on top of F4's and
  F3's changes. The dispatch trigger must **retain** F3's build-once → test-wheel /
  test-sdist → hash-gated-`publish` job graph and F4's `mcp_verify`/`mcp_registry`
  split + evidence-consolidation job — the trigger change swaps only *how the run
  starts and is authorized*, not the internal job structure. Concretely, **re-key
  every downstream version source and job guard from `github.ref_name` / the
  tag-context `if:` to the `workflow_dispatch` input** (the `github_release` and
  `mcp_registry` jobs derive their version from the input, and their
  `if: github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')` guards —
  which go always-false once the tag trigger is removed — are updated to the dispatch
  condition).
- **Human authorization — re-key the `pypi` environment + a fail-closed preflight
  (uv release-gate + PyPA Trusted Publishing).** The `publish` job runs in the `pypi`
  deployment environment with **required reviewers**, so publication needs a second
  human's approval. Because the job now runs in the dispatch (`refs/heads/main`)
  context rather than a tag context, the environment's deployment-ref policy is
  **re-keyed from "v* tags only" to "`main` via `workflow_dispatch`"** with required
  reviewers — **no new secret**. This is the single most security-critical gate
  (anyone with `actions:write` can start a dispatch; only the environment's reviewers +
  branch policy enforce "a second human approves each publish"), so it must not live
  as an un-versioned console setting that could be silently cleared. Rather than couple
  to the AWS-authed `terraform-drift.yml` (a different provider/auth model), enforce it
  **at release time**: a **preflight step queries the GitHub REST API
  (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/pypi`) and FAILS the release closed** if the
  environment lacks required reviewers or its deployment-branch policy is not
  `main`-only. This detects drift exactly when it matters (it blocks the actual
  publish, stronger than a periodic plan), is codebase-verifiable (the step exists in
  `release.yml`), and needs only the workflow's own read token. Net effect: "only `v*`
  tags may publish" becomes the stronger, self-enforced "only a dispatch-from-`main`,
  reviewer-approved run may publish — and a release aborts if that protection is
  missing".
- **Tag + GitHub Release created AFTER a successful publish (record only).** Once
  publish succeeds, the workflow creates the `v*` tag and the GitHub Release for the
  record/mirror; the tag is an **output**, never a trigger. Concretely, the `github_release`
  job (which holds `contents: write`) **drops `--verify-tag`** and calls
  `gh release create "v<version>" --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --generate-notes --latest dist/*`,
  which **creates the lightweight tag at the release SHA** when it does not pre-exist — so no
  intermediate tag push / PAT is needed, and the version comes from the dispatch input, not a
  pre-pushed tag. (An existing-release run stays idempotent via the `gh release view` path.) The MCP job derives the
  version from the dispatch input (not from a tag).
- **No raw-tag publish path.** With the environment keyed to dispatch-from-`main`, a
  hand-pushed `v*` tag cannot reach the `pypi` environment and therefore cannot
  publish — this eliminates the "arbitrary pushed tag publishes" surface that was the
  original finding, rather than merely gating it.
- **OIDC subject stays environment-scoped — the PyPI trusted-publisher entry is
  unaffected by the trigger change.** The `publish` job keeps running in the `pypi`
  deployment environment, so the OIDC token's `sub` claim stays
  `repo:navapbc/rebar:environment:pypi` — **environment-scoped and ref-independent**.
  PyPA Trusted Publishing matches on owner/repo + **workflow filename (`release.yml`)
  + environment name (`pypi`)** and does **not** constrain on the git ref/tag, so the
  tag→dispatch trigger change alters none of the matched fields and the existing
  trusted-publisher entry continues to accept the dispatch-context token with no
  reconfiguration. (Were the entry ever ref-constrained, the mismatch would fail
  **loudly** at the `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` step on the first dispatch run —
  never silently — surfacing rather than corrupting a release.)
- **Verify the guard LOGIC with unit tests (no live staging needed).** Extract the
  three guards into small testable units — the version-lockstep comparison, the
  ancestry check, and the env-preflight response parsing — and unit-test them with
  fixtures (matching/mismatching versions; ancestor/non-ancestor SHAs; env-protection
  present/absent JSON). This makes the negative paths codebase-verifiable without any
  live publish. The guard *steps existing* in `release.yml` is likewise
  codebase-verifiable.
- **Guard-firing is verified AUTONOMOUSLY on the real workflow — no staging fork.** The
  three abort guards precede every publishing job, so they can be demonstrated to fire
  WITHOUT any real publish: after this story lands, the agent triggers `release.yml` via
  `gh workflow run` with a non-`main` ref and a mismatched version input, and confirms via
  `gh run view --log` that each run aborts at its guard step before build/publish. This
  needs only the environment's `workflow` scope (present) and produces no PyPI/registry
  side effect. A staging fork + a TestPyPI trusted-publisher would only be needed to
  exercise the *positive* real-publish path, which is deliberately NOT part of verifying
  this story (publishing a real release is not a story deliverable); that positive path is
  covered by the unit-tested guard helpers + the codebase-verifiable dispatch-from-`main`
  wiring. **Live `pypi` environment config is also autonomous:** the agent reads and, if
  drifted, configures the environment's required reviewers + `main`-only branch policy via
  the admin GitHub API (the environment holds a `repo`-scoped admin token), then confirms
  — escalating to request access only if the API write is denied.
- **`main.tf` / tag-push restriction stays OUT of scope (unchanged, deliberate).**
  `main.tf:23-28` documents the `tag_lock` was removed (no viable GitHub tag bypass
  actor in this mirror topology) and the contract test
  `tests/unit/test_mirror_lock_terraform.py::test_module_is_main_only_no_tag_lock`
  codifies "no tag lock". We do not restrict *who* can push a tag; publication safety
  now comes entirely from dispatch-from-`main` + the re-keyed reviewer-gated environment.
- Record the approved SHA, version, manifest versions, and artifact hashes in release
  evidence.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — switch the trigger to `workflow_dispatch` (version
  input, run from `main`); enforce `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`; add the
  version-lockstep + ancestry checks before build; build then publish directly via the
  OIDC trusted-publishing flow gated on the re-keyed `pypi` environment; create the
  `v*` tag + GitHub Release after a successful publish (record only). Remove the
  `push: tags: v*` publish trigger (it can no longer reach the re-keyed environment).
- **Autonomous post-landing verification (no operator fork):** after this story lands,
  the agent (a) triggers `release.yml` via `gh workflow run` with invalid inputs and
  confirms via `gh run view` that each guard aborts before publish (needs only the
  `workflow` scope), and (b) reads/configures/verifies the live `pypi` environment's
  required reviewers + `main`-only branch policy via the admin GitHub API (`repo` scope).
  Both record their evidence as comments on this ticket. No staging fork or TestPyPI
  publisher is required; escalation is a fallback only if the needed GitHub scope is
  denied.
- Unit tests for the extracted guard helpers (version-lockstep, ancestry, env-preflight
  parsing) — the codebase-verifiable proof the guards behave correctly.
- `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py` — **extend** with fd84's structural checks
  (dispatch-only trigger with a `version` input; the `authorize` job's four guards precede
  build via `needs`; no stale tag-context `if:`/`github.ref_name` remains; the
  `github_release` job needs `publish`). The existing 08a8/6168 invariants are
  **preserved unbroken** by this story's edits: the `authorize` job holds only
  `contents: read` (no `id-token: write`), so `test_single_annotated_zizmor_suppression`
  (exactly one suppression) still holds; the publish job's hash-gate/no-rebuild body
  (`test_g_publish_hash_gated_no_rebuild`) and the mcp_verify/mcp_registry split
  (`test_mcp_verify_registry_split`) are untouched except for the tag→dispatch `if:` re-key,
  which those tests do not assert on — so they stay green (re-run the full module to confirm).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — a **preflight step** in the dispatch flow that
  calls `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/pypi` and fails the release if the
  environment lacks required reviewers or a `main`-only deployment-branch policy
  (fail-closed drift detection at release time). **Preflight schema (the exact
  field paths the fail-closed parser inspects and the unit-test fixtures replicate):**
  from `GET .../environments/pypi`, require `protection_rules[]` to contain an entry with
  `type == "required_reviewers"` **and** a non-empty `reviewers` list; and require
  `deployment_branch_policy` to be non-null with `custom_branch_policies == true`. From
  `GET .../environments/pypi/deployment-branch-policies`, require `branch_policies[].name`
  to be **exactly** `{"main"}` (any other/extra branch fails). These live in
  `scripts/release_guards.py::check_env_protection`. No `infra/terraform-github/`,
  `terraform-drift.yml`, or terraform-contract-test changes (the GitHub provider's
  AWS-vs-GitHub auth split made drift-workflow coupling disproportionate; the
  preflight is the stronger, self-contained control). `infra/terraform-github/main.tf`
  and its no-tag-lock contract test remain **unchanged**.
- `docs/releasing.md` — document the dispatch-from-`main` process, the version-lockstep
  invariant, and the required environment reviewers. **Section ownership:** this story
  owns the "Release-source authorization" section **and rewrites the now-obsolete
  existing sections it invalidates** — the "Tag → PyPI publishes automatically"
  procedure (replaced by dispatch-from-`main`) and the "Hard rules" manual-lockstep
  framing (now machine-enforced). (Finding 3 owns "Build-once" + rewriting the
  "Post-release smoke test" section; Finding 4 owns "Pinning" — so the three concurrent
  release stories do not overlap-edit the same headings.)
- Out of scope: the build-once / pinning work (Findings 3 and 4 — separate stories
  that also touch `release.yml`; coordinate ordering per the epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC 0 (dependency gate — verify before starting).** This story composes on top of
  F3 (build-once) and F4 (pinning), which land first per the epic chain (F4 → F3 → F1).
  Before implementation, confirm by grep that `release.yml` on the working base already
  contains F3's `wheel_test` / `sdist_test` jobs and its hash-gated `publish` (no rebuild),
  AND F4's `mcp_verify` / `mcp_registry` split + the evidence-consolidation job. If they are
  absent (F3/F4 not yet landed/merged into this branch's base), STOP and rebase onto the
  landed F3/F4 first — this story only re-keys *how the run starts and is authorized* and must
  not re-introduce or fork those job graphs. (This makes the cross-story dependency an
  explicit, checkable precondition rather than an assumed baseline.)
- [ ] The workflow **retains** F3's build-once → wheel_test/sdist_test → hash-gated `publish`
  job graph and F4's `mcp_verify`/`mcp_registry` split + evidence-consolidation job unchanged
  in structure (verified by grep: those job names still present after this story's trigger
  re-key), so the authorization change is additive, not a rewrite.
- [ ] `release.yml` is triggered by `workflow_dispatch` (version input), contains a
  guard step failing when `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'`, a version-lockstep step,
  and an ancestry step (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, checkout `fetch-depth: 0` +
  `git fetch origin main`), all before build; and it has **no** `push: tags` publish
  trigger — all codebase-verifiable from the workflow definition.
- [ ] The workflow **retains** F3's build-once → wheel_test/sdist_test →
  hash-gated-`publish` job graph and F4's `mcp_verify`/`mcp_registry` split +
  evidence-consolidation job, and re-keys the `github_release`/`mcp_registry` version
  sources + guards from the tag context to the `workflow_dispatch` input — verified by
  the workflow definition still containing those jobs and no `github.ref_name`/tag-`if:`
  version derivation remaining.
- [ ] The workflow publishes directly via the OIDC trusted-publishing flow (no
  intermediate tag push / no relay / no PAT) and creates the `v*` tag + GitHub Release
  only **after** a successful publish (tag is an output, not a trigger) — codebase-
  verifiable from the job graph.
- [ ] A release-time preflight step calls `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/pypi`
  and fails the release closed when required reviewers are absent or the
  deployment-branch policy is not `main`-only — codebase-verifiable (the step exists in
  `release.yml`); the actual live environment configuration is set + verified
  **autonomously** via the admin GitHub API (see the environment-config AC below). So a
  cleared environment protection aborts the release instead of silently enabling
  single-actor publishing.
- [ ] Unit tests for the extracted guard helpers pass: version-lockstep flags a
  deliberate mismatch, the ancestry check rejects a non-ancestor SHA (and accepts a
  non-tip ancestor), and the env-preflight parser fails on env-protection-absent JSON —
  all codebase-verifiable without a live publish.
- [ ] The guards are demonstrated to **fire in a real `workflow_dispatch` run**,
  completed **autonomously** by the agent (no operator fork/TestPyPI needed): after this
  story lands, the agent triggers `release.yml` on `navapbc/rebar` via `gh workflow run`
  with (i) a **non-`main` ref** and (ii) a **mismatched version input**, and confirms via
  `gh run view --log` that each run **ABORTS at its guard step before any
  build/publish/tag job** — so NO PyPI / MCP-registry / GitHub-Release side effect occurs
  (the ref guard, version-lockstep, and ancestry checks all precede every publishing job).
  The run URLs + the aborting guard-step log lines are recorded as a comment on this
  ticket. The **positive** clean-dispatch → real-PyPI publish is deliberately NOT
  triggered (publishing a real release is out of scope for verifying the story; the
  guard-PASS path is covered by the unit-tested helpers + the codebase-verifiable
  dispatch-from-`main` wiring). Escalate only if `gh workflow run` / `actions:write` is
  unavailable in the environment.
- [ ] The live `pypi` GitHub environment is **configured to the codified policy —
  required reviewers enabled AND a `main`-only deployment-branch policy — and verified,
  autonomously** by the agent using the environment's admin GitHub token: it reads
  `GET /repos/navapbc/rebar/environments/pypi`; if required reviewers are absent or the
  branch policy is not `main`-only, it **configures** the environment via
  `PUT /repos/navapbc/rebar/environments/pypi` with a `reviewers` body of the shape … [truncated by reconciler]
baseline.summary: Enforce release-source authorization + version lockstep before publication

baseline.description:
## Why

Review-result sidecars (plan- and code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` events) are pruned to the most
recent `RETAIN_PER_TICKET = 10` per ticket. Drift-refresh re-reviews on a single ticket can
exceed 10 rounds, so an auditor loses the earlier rounds. Raise the retention bound to 50 — well
above the observed single-digit remediation-loop depth — while still capping unbounded growth of
`REVIEW_RESULT` events on the `tickets` branch (the hot path of every write). It is a deliberate
bound, not unlimited retention.

## Current state (the plan review's correction)

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` HAS a `prune()` function and a `RETAIN_PER_TICKET = 10`
constant, and its `emit()` calls `prune()`. **`src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` has NEITHER
a `prune()` function NOR a `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` constant, and its `emit()` does not prune** —
code-review `REVIEW_RESULT` events currently grow unbounded. So this story does two things: it
RAISES the plan-review bound to 50, AND it ADDS an equivalent prune path to code-review governed
by the SAME shared constant, so both paths retain identically.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — raise `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` from `10` to `50`. Keep the
  prune newest-first (ordering unchanged); only the retained count changes.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py` — ADD retention governed by the SAME constant:
  - reference the shared bound (import `RETAIN_PER_TICKET` from `rebar.llm.plan_review.sidecar`,
    so there is ONE named constant governing both paths — no second literal to drift);
  - add a `prune(ticket_id, *, keep=RETAIN_PER_TICKET, repo_root=None)` function mirroring
    `plan_review.sidecar.prune` (list the ticket's `-REVIEW_RESULT.json` events by filename
    timestamp, `git rm` all but the newest `keep`, commit with `--no-verify`; best-effort and
    exception-swallowing — a failed prune never fails the gate);
  - call `prune(target_ticket, repo_root=repo_root)` from `emit()` after `append_event`, matching
    plan-review's emit → prune sequence.

## Approach rationale

A single shared constant (imported, not duplicated) keeps the change minimal and makes "governs
both paths" literally true — no new config key (YAGNI: no consumer has asked for a per-repo
override; a config key can be added later if a real need appears). The code-review prune reuses
the exact newest-first-by-filename-timestamp strategy plan-review already uses, so both paths
behave identically.

## Compatibility & rollback

Purely a bound increase plus a new (previously absent) code-review prune. No schema/format change.
Already-pruned plan-review history is not recovered (already deleted); going forward more is
retained. Code-review sidecars that already grew unbounded will be pruned to 50 on the next emit.
Reverting sets the constant back to 10 (prunes more aggressively) and/or removes the code-review
prune (code-review growth becomes unbounded again); no migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After 50+ reviews on one ticket, up to 50 `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars are retained and a write
      past 50 prunes the oldest — for BOTH the plan-review and the code-review sidecar. Oracle: a
      unit test appending N>50 synthetic events on each path (via each module's `prune`) and
      asserting the retained count is exactly 50 and the newest are the ones kept.
- [ ] The retention cap is a SINGLE definition, not duplicated: `plan_review.sidecar` defines
      `RETAIN_PER_TICKET = 50` and `code_review.sidecar` obtains the SAME value by importing it
      (no second `= <literal>` in code_review). Oracle: a test asserting
      `code_review.sidecar.RETAIN_PER_TICKET == plan_review.sidecar.RETAIN_PER_TICKET == 50`, and
      that each module's `prune` defaults its `keep` to that constant.
- [ ] `code_review.sidecar.emit` prunes after appending (the previously-absent path now exists).
      Oracle: a test that emitting more than the cap on a code-review target ticket leaves exactly
      50 events.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: raise review-sidecar retention cap (10 -> 50, shared constant)

# Pin `config.local_to_jira_status` against the canonical Jira-family map

## Context / Problem

**This ticket's original scope is already delivered; what remains is one specific residue, and this plan has been rewritten to that residue.** Filed during J1 as "the local->Jira maps exist in two drifted copies inside `adapters/jira/`". Story J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] consolidated those two into a single definition and resolved the drift. Verified against the tree, not assumed:

* `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` now holds the SOLE adapter-side definition
  (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`).
* The ACLI transport reads it (`acli.py:73,75`; `acli_cli_ops.py:35`) and so does the Backend port
  (`outbound_fields.py:35-36`), both via an alias to the old private names.
* The `deleted` drift is decided: the unified map adopts `"deleted": "Done"`, and
  `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py` pins it
  (`test_deleted_now_resolves_to_done_instead_of_the_invalid_deleted`).

So original ACs 1-3 are met. The residue is the **THIRD copy**, which J2 deliberately left out of its scope and named this ticket for, in `value_maps.py`'s own module docstring: "``rebar_reconciler/ config.py``'s separate third copy is deliberately out of this story's scope — see bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61."

## Evidence — the residue is a REAL unpinned gap, measured

`config.local_to_jira_status` (`config.py:24-38`) is a key-for-key **independent literal**. Today it is content-identical to `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` (compared programmatically: `==` is True), so there is no drift *yet* — but nothing prevents one.

MUTATION EXPERIMENT (the same method that originally exposed this bug class): setting `config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"] = "Archived-MUTANT"` — a value that is NOT a state in the live DIG workflow ({To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}) — left **59 passed, 0 failed** across `state/test_config.py`, `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py`, and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py`. Nothing catches divergence. That is precisely the failure mode this ticket reported, surviving in the one copy J2 did not touch.

Note the partial existing cover, so this plan does not re-add it: `test_config.py`'s `test_idea_maps_to_jira_idea_across_all_status_maps` already pins the `idea -> IDEA` entry across all three maps. It is ONE key. The other six are unpinned, which is why the mutation above went unseen.

## Approach — a parity test, NOT a shared import

**Do not make `config.py` import the canonical map.** `config.py` currently imports nothing but `__future__` — it is a deliberately zero-dependency core module — and `adapters/jira_family/` is a VENDOR package whose `__init__` states its dependency direction is one-way ("Concrete backends import this package; it never imports them back"). Having core `config` import a Jira adapter would invert that layering. It would also put the operator-override surface and the documented empty-dict kill-switch (`test_config.py:91-98`) behind an adapter import.

**Use the idiom this file already established for exactly this problem.** `config.jira_to_local_status` is a second literal of `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, and the codebase keeps the two honest with a PARITY TEST plus a lock-step comment — see the comment at `config.py:50-51` ("Must stay in lock-step with inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS (parity is enforced by tests/.../test_config.py)") and `test_jira_to_local_status_parity_with_inbound_differ`. Mirror that, one layer over.

`test_config.py` already has the mechanism: `_load_attr(module_file, attr)` loads a constant **from a file path** via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, so the test reads the adapter's map WITHOUT importing the adapter package into core's test context — and it is already called with `"adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py"` today. No new machinery is needed.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py` — ONE new parity test.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a lock-step COMMENT above
  `local_to_jira_status`, mirroring the one already above `jira_to_local_status`. No code change.

**NOT in scope:** any change to a map's VALUES (they already agree; changing one would be a behaviour change this ticket does not need); any production import between core and the adapter layer; the priority map (`config.py` has NO priority copy — verified: no priority attribute exists on the module, so there is no third priority literal to pin).

## Testing

The oracle is the parity test itself, and it must be shown to have teeth rather than asserted to: re-run the mutation above and confirm the new test goes RED, then revert and confirm GREEN. A parity test that passes against a divergent map is worse than none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test in `state/test_config.py` asserts `config.local_to_jira_status` equals
      `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` loaded from `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` via the existing
      `_load_attr` helper — full-dict equality, not a per-key spot check

content.text: Generalize the JSON-Schema prototype into authoritative schemas for rebar's
CURRENT JSON outputs, used as a cross-interface drift oracle and as MCP
outputSchemas. (Child of the "--json everywhere" epic.) Scope below is the
result of a full codebase audit.
## Already in place (prototype — extend, don't redo)
- src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json + schemas/__init__.py loader
- tests/interfaces/test_schema_ticket_state.py (validates show via lib/CLI/MCP)
- MCP show_ticket returns typed TicketStateOut -> advertises outputSchema
- jsonschema in [dev] extra
## Distinct JSON shapes today (each needs a schema)
1. TicketState (object) — show; also array items of list, search. (DONE: schema exists)
2. TicketState-LLM (renamed short keys) — show/list/ready --format=llm
3. DepsGraph — deps: {ticket_id,deps[],blockers[],children[],ready_to_work}
4. NextBatch — next-batch --json: {epic_id,epic_title,batch_size,available_pool,batch[{id,title,priority,type,files[],files_likely_read[]}],skipped_*[]}
5. ListDescendants — {epics[],stories[],tasks[],bugs[],parents_with_children[]}
6. ClarityResult — clarity-check: {score,verdict,threshold(,passed)}
7. ValidateReport — validate --json: {score,critical_issues[],major_issues[],minor_issues[],warnings[],suggestions[]}
8. BridgeStatus — bridge-status --format=json (raw .bridge-status.json + unresolved_alerts_count)
9. FileImpact[] — get-file-impact: [{path,reason}]
10. VerifyCommands[] — get-verify-commands: [{dd_id,dd_text,command}]
11. Scratch envelopes — scratch get/set/clear: {status:"ok"|"hit"|"miss"|"error",...}
12. ErrorEnvelope (show not-found) — {error,input,message}
13. BridgeFsck findings (currently text-only; dict exists) — {orphaned[],duplicates[],stale[]}
## Consolidation (use shared $ref sub-schemas — author once, reference everywhere)
- TicketState is the keystone: list/search are {type:array,items:{$ref:TicketState}} (byte-identical reducer output).

- Promote reused sub-objects to named $refs: comment {body,author,timestamp}; dep {target_id,relation,link_uuid} (ALSO used by DepsGraph.deps[] — same entry); file_impact_entry {path,reason} (shared by get-file-impact AND TicketState.file_impact[]); verify_command_entry {dd_id,dd_text,command} (shared by get-verify-commands AND TicketState.verify_commands[]); bridge_alert; revert.
- next-batch batch/skipped_* items all share a BatchItem base {id,title} (+ variant fields conflict_file/conflict_with, blocked_story) -> 3 variants, all $ref.
- Unify result envelopes: CheckResult/GateResult {verdict|passed, score?, threshold?, metrics?, reason?} shared by clarity-check + (json-ified) check-ac + quality-check. ClarityResult is a subset.
- Unify issue reports: IssueReport {score?, issues:[{severity,kind,ticket_id?,detail}], counts} shared by validate (collapse the 5 severity arrays), fsck, bridge-fsck.
- Unify ErrorEnvelope: show not-found {error,input,message} vs scratch {status:"error",code,reason} -> one {status:"error",code,message} referenced wherever a structured error is emitted on stdout.
## MCP typed returns (advertise outputSchema; ~12 models, several shared)
Follow the show_ticket/TicketStateOut pattern for every read tool returning bare
dict/list/object. One model per shape; reuse across tools:
- TicketStateOut -> list_tickets, search (DONE for show_ticket)
- DepsGraphOut -> ticket_deps;  NextBatchOut -> next_batch;  ReadyOut -> ready_tickets (after Bug 2)
- ClarityResultOut -> clarity_check;  GateResultOut(passed,output) -> check_ac + quality_check
- ValidateReportOut -> validate (after Bug 1);  FileImpactItemOut -> get_file_impact (+ types set_file_impact input)
- VerifyCommandItemOut -> get_verify_commands (+ types set_verify_commands input)
- StatusResultOut(id,status,assignee?) -> transition_ticket + claim_ticket + reopen_ticket
- CreateResultOut(id,alias) -> create_ticket (resolve Mismatch C);  AckOut (optional) for the 10 "ok" writers
## Prerequisite bug fixes (these tools can't be typed until they return correct data)

- BUG 1 (validate arg): MCP validate (mcp_server.py:154) AND library validate (__init__.py:197) pass ticket_id, but engine validate is repo-wide (validate-issues.sh:80-83 rejects positionals). Confirmed: returns {output:"Unknown option: <id>",exit_code:1}. Fix: drop ticket_id in both layers; call ["validate","--json"].

- BUG 2 (ready --json): library ready() (__init__.py:316) calls ["ready","--json"], but engine ready only has --format {ids,llm}/--epic. Confirmed: rebar.ready() raises RebarError(exit 2) -> MCP ready_tickets ALWAYS errors. Fix: call `ready --format llm` (or add --json to the engine) and define ReadyOut.
## Other interface mismatches to reconcile
- C: create_ticket — MCP returns bare id; library can return {id,alias}; agent workflow favors {id,alias}. Standardize.
- D: edit_ticket — MCP lacks `ticket_type` param (library/CLI have it). Add it.
- E: set_file_impact/set_verify_commands — MCP params typed bare `list` (no inputSchema); pair with item models.
- F: fsck(recover:bool) maps to two CLI subcommands (fsck / fsck-recover) — cosmetic; document.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A JSON Schema authored under src/rebar/schemas/ for each shape #2-#13 (incl. shared $ref sub-schemas in a common file)
- [ ] Cross-interface conformance test per schema (lib/CLI/MCP as applicable), reusing the prototype pattern
- [ ] All read MCP tools advertise outputSchema via typed returns (grouped models above)
- [ ] BUG 1 fixed: validate takes no ticket_id (lib+MCP), matches repo-wide engine; test
- [ ] BUG 2 fixed: ready works end-to-end (lib+MCP return data, not an error); test
- [ ] Mismatches C/D/E reconciled across CLI/library/MCP (parity); F documented
- [ ] Schema source-of-truth decision documented (hand-authored vs generated from models) + drift guard if both coexist
- [ ] Docs link schemas from README/CLAUDE/docs/event-schema.md

baseline.summary: Roll out JSON Schemas for all current JSON outputs (+ fix MCP validate signature)

## Finding

The public Python transition documentation says `force` can waive the unresolved-children close restriction, while the CLI and implementation enforce that restriction unconditionally.

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:20-24` describes `force` as waiving the unresolved-children guard.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:33-49` states that `--force` does not bypass the unresolved-child rule.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:5-25` rejects closing a parent with open children regardless of `force` or `force_close`.
- `docs/concurrency.md:117-135` distinguishes the close invariant from gate bypass and documents force propagation through claim gates.

## Remediation

Document the stable abstraction rather than enumerating today's gates: force bypasses all gates, including gates added in the future. The prohibition on closing a ticket with open children is a ticket-system invariant, not a gate, and therefore cannot be bypassed by force.

Cascade flag: public API contract wording affects library, CLI, MCP, user guide, and agent-facing guidance; update all surfaces that define force semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Public Python, CLI, MCP, user, and agent guidance consistently states that force bypasses all gates.
- [ ] Guidance explicitly classifies the open-children close prohibition as a ticket-system invariant rather than a gate.
- [ ] Guidance states that force does not bypass ticket-system invariants.
- [ ] Documentation does not hardcode a closed list of current gates as the definition of force behavior.
- [ ] Contract tests demonstrate that force bypasses enabled gates but cannot close a parent while any child remains non-closed.
baseline.summary: Clarify that force bypasses gates, not ticket invariants

content.text: ## Why

The escaped bugs all began with unit tests feeding the differs hand-built `jira_snapshot` dicts in shapes the real fetcher never produces (flat `comments` instead of nested `comment`; `issuelinks` the snapshot never carried). The converged fix (per `jira-cli`'s pattern) is **fixtures captured from real Jira payloads, served through the production serialization path** — never hand-massaged. This is the foundation every other story in the epic builds on.
## What

- Capture **scrubbed real Jira REST payloads** for the exact responses the fetcher consumes: the paged `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql`, plus the enrichment maps `get_comment_map` (`{"comment":{"comments":[…]}}`), `get_issuelinks_map` (`{"issuelinks":[…]}`), and `get_parent_map` (`{"parent":{"key":…}}`). Store under `tests/fixtures/jira/`.

- A `FakeAcliClient` (in `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/_fakes.py`) that returns those fixtures from the real method signatures (`search_issues`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map`, `get_parent_map`) so they flow through the production `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` enrichment — the fake adds NO shape massaging.
- Secret-scrubbing on capture (strip API tokens, emails, accountIds) via layered redaction (vcrpy-style), so committed fixtures carry no secrets.
- A `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` (live-gated) + documented re-capture procedure so fixtures stay honest and do not rot into change-detectors.
## Scope
- In: captured fixtures + the fake client + capture/scrub script + re-capture doc.
- Out: the contract test that consumes them (separate story), the verified-fake honesty check (separate story).
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/fixtures/jira/*.json` hold scrubbed real Jira payloads for search + comment + issuelinks + parent (verified: no tokens/emails/accountIds present).
- [ ] `FakeAcliClient` serves the fixtures through the production fetcher enrichment path with no shape transformation.
- [ ] `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` captures + scrubs from a live Jira (gated) and the re-capture cadence is documented.
- [ ] Fixtures are consumed only via the production code path (no test reads them and hand-reshapes).

baseline.description:
## Summary

A cross-subtree blocking link is silently substituted for library and MCP callers. `rebar link a b depends_on` may record a DIFFERENT edge than the one requested — escalating each endpoint to the nearest common ancestor's children — and the caller is told only `"ok"`.

This is the "Silent" impact bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 reported ("the user believes T1->S was recorded; it was not"). Story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 fixed *which* edge escalation produces, but not whether the caller is told. It remains unfixed on the path agents actually use.

## Root cause

`add_dependency` composes a machine-readable redirect record (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`) and prints it to stdout via `_emit_redirect` (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:213`, called at `:269` and `:282`). stdout is the ONLY channel — the record is never returned.

The CLI sees it. Nothing else does:

- `rebar.link()` calls `composer.link_core(..., quiet=True)` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615`);
- `quiet` wraps the call in `contextlib.redirect_stdout(sink), contextlib.redirect_stderr(sink)` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:629`), discarding both the record and the `REDIRECT:` warning;
- the MCP tool `link_tickets` calls `rebar.link(...)` and returns the literal `"ok"` (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:213-214`).

So an agent linking two tickets over MCP is told the operation succeeded, with no indication that different endpoints were recorded.

## Approach

Make the redirect record a RETURN VALUE, and leave `quiet=True` alone.

Removing `quiet` is the obvious-looking fix and is wrong: `rebar-mcp` speaks MCP-over-stdio (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:668`), so an unsuppressed `print()` inside a tool call would inject a bare JSON object into the JSON-RPC stream and corrupt the protocol. The same suppression protects the other in-process callers that must not emit stray stdout — the reconciler's inbound apply (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502`), `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py:106`, and `src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:343`. Separately, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py:191` calls `add_dependency` DIRECTLY, bypassing the facade entirely; it ignores the return value, so widening that signature is a no-op for it, but it is listed so the call-site inventory is complete. `quiet` is load-bearing; the defect is that stdout is the only channel, not that it is suppressed.

The propagation chain has FIVE links, and three of them currently drop the value on the floor. Each is named here because the fix silently no-ops if any one is missed:

1. `add_dependency` (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:152`) returns the redirect record, or `None` when nothing was escalated. Its existing stdout print stays exactly as-is, so the CLI contract pinned by `test_add_dependency_cross_story_emits_redirect_json_to_stdout` (`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py:109`) is untouched.
2. `link_core` (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:602`) returns what `add_dependency` returned, still from inside the `quiet` sink.
3. **DROP POINT** — the `_link` inner closure in `rebar.link()` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:614-615`) calls `composer.link_core(...)` with no `return`. Add one.
4. **DROP POINT** — `_python_leaf` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:483`) is annotated `-> None` and calls `fn(*args, repo_root=repo_root, **kwargs)` at `:495` with no `return`. It must return the inner call's value, and its annotation must widen accordingly.
5. **DROP POINT** — `rebar.link()` itself (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:606`) is annotated `-> None`; it must return `_python_leaf`'s value.

Then `link_tickets` returns `"ok"` unchanged when nothing was escalated, and when something was, this exact template:

    ok (escalated: {source}->{target} recorded as {resolved_source}->{resolved_target})

Fixed template rather than free prose, so a consumer can match on it and the test can assert it exactly.

`_python_leaf` is SHARED by every Tier B leaf write (comment, tag, edit, archive, …), so widening it is the one part of this change with reach beyond `link`. It is still safe: those callers ignore the return, so returning a value instead of `None` cannot change their behaviour, and the alternative — bypassing `_python_leaf` for `link` alone — would duplicate its `CommandError -> RebarError` mapping, which is the single thing keeping the library's exit-code contract uniform. Widen the annotation rather than fork the helper.

Rejected: change `link_tickets` to return a structured dict. Better for machine consumption, but it changes the tool's declared return type from `str`, which moves its MCP `outputSchema` and drags in the schema-drift gate (`scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`) and the `tests/interfaces/contracts/` schema guards — a contract change disproportionate to making a substitution visible. Every sibling MUTATE tool (`unlink_tickets`, `edit_ticket`) also returns `"ok"`, so a string keeps the surface consistent. The string is the minimum that removes the silence; a structured payload can follow if a consumer needs to parse it.

Rejected: log a warning instead of returning. `logger.warning` already fires at `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:201` and is swallowed by the same `quiet` sink, so it reaches no one; and a log line is not available to the caller as a value.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — `add_dependency` returns the redirect record (or `None`); the stdout print and its ordering after the durable write are unchanged.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` — `link_core` returns what `add_dependency` returned; the `quiet` sink stays.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — THREE edits: the `_link` closure (`:614-615`) returns `link_core`'s value; `_python_leaf` (`:483`) returns its inner `fn(...)` call (`:495`) and widens its `-> None` annotation; `rebar.link()` (`:606`) returns that value and widens its own annotation.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — `link_tickets` reports the substitution in its return string when one occurred.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py` — cover the new return value alongside the existing stdout assertion.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` — cover the MCP tool's two return shapes. If that module does not exist, create it.

## Testing

- Happy path: a sibling link (no escalation) returns `None` from `add_dependency` and `rebar.link()`, and `link_tickets` returns exactly `"ok"` — the unchanged shape.
- Escalation: a cross-subtree link returns a record carrying the original and resolved endpoints, and `link_tickets`' string contains both the requested pair and the recorded pair.
- Regression: the existing stdout assertion still passes, proving the CLI channel was not moved or removed.
- Regression: `quiet=True` still suppresses stdout — asserted by capturing stdout around a `rebar.link()` call that escalates and confirming it is empty, which is the property protecting the MCP stdio stream.
- Edge: a rejected link (redundant / cyclic / closed endpoint) still raises rather than returning a record, so the return value can never be mistaken for success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `add_dependency` returns the redirect record for an escalated link and `None` for an unescalated one; verified by the new cases in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py`.
- [ ] `rebar.link()` returns that same record to library callers; verified by a case asserting the resolved endpoints differ from the requested ones.
- [ ] The MCP `link_tickets` tool returns exactly `"ok"` when nothing was escalated, and exactly `ok (escalated: {source}->{target} recorded as {resolved_source}->{resolved_target})` when something was; verified by the two cases in `tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` asserting the full string, not a substring.
- [ ] `_python_leaf` returns its inner call's value rather than discarding it, and no existing leaf-write caller changes behaviour; verified by a case asserting a non-link leaf write (e.g. `rebar.comment`) still succeeds and by the existing library tests passing unmodified.
- [ ] `rebar.link()` still writes nothing to stdout even when it escalates; verified by capturing stdout around the call and asserting it is empty — the property that keeps the MCP stdio stream intact.
- [ ] `test_add_dependency_cross_story_emits_redirect_json_to_stdout` passes unmodified; verified by `git diff` showing that test body unchanged.
- [ ] The MCP tool's declared return type is still `str`, so `docs/mcp-reference.md` needs no regeneration; verified by `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` leaving the file unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/scripts/graph/ tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py` all pass; verified by running each.
baseline.summary: Cross-subtree link escalation is silent for library and MCP callers

## Context / Problem
plan_review_T1.md instructs "Tool-grounded where possible (web/codebase)", but the agent toolset (src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py, wired at src/rebar/llm/runner.py:257) provides only read_file, list_directory, search_files, resolve_symbol, show_ticket — no web access. Empirically only 3/14 recent T1 findings were tool-grounded; the rubric's primary grounding channel is dead weight. Operator ruled this a bug.

## Approach
Enable Anthropic's server-side web-search tool for AGENT criteria that declare it: add an optional `"web": true` key to a criterion's routing entry (T1 only, initially); when set and the resolved provider is anthropic, the runner adds the server-side web_search tool to that request's model settings (seam: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py settings assembly, alongside the existing cache settings at anthropic_model.py:39-52). Non-anthropic providers and offline runs get today's behavior; the T1 rubric is updated to say web grounding applies when the tool is offered and to fall back to codebase/plan reasoning otherwise. Alternative rejected: a homegrown HTTP fetch tool in pai_tools — network policy, sanitization, and result-quality burdens for one criterion when the provider offers a managed tool.

## Scope
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py, src/rebar/llm/runner.py (thread the per-request web flag), src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json (T1 entry), src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T1.md, tests/llm/test_web_tool_gating.py.

## Testing
Unit: a request flagged web=true on an anthropic-resolved model carries the web tool in settings; openai/gemini-resolved models do not; unflagged criteria never carry it. No live web call in tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A T1 pass-1 request against an anthropic-resolved model includes the server-side web-search tool in its model settings (checked: unit test on settings assembly).
- [ ] Non-anthropic providers and non-web criteria produce byte-identical settings to today (checked: unit test comparison).
- [ ] plan_review_T1.md describes the conditional availability and the fallback (checked: test asserts rubric text).

baseline.description:
## Why

With the gated server surface in place (this epic's server-scaffolding story, on `depends_on`), the
per-ticket audit page must let a human answer, fast: "did this ticket pass its gates, and if not why —
and can I trust how the machine decided that?" Primary users are BOTH a spot-checking auditor (verdict
+ real problems at a glance) and a gate-debugger (full per-finding provenance). Design goal:
verdict-first, findings-second, provenance-on-demand. This design is the product of two rounds of HCD
critique (finding-centric IA + a neutral threshold meter).

## Dependencies (all consumed from the LANDED read layer — this story modifies NO data model)

This story is a pure function of the audit read layer already merged on `main`
(`rebar.audit.read.audit_trail(ticket_id) -> dict`). It consumes ONLY what that contract exposes and
does **not** modify any sidecar, read helper, or schema (data-model changes are epic-1's scope, OUT of
scope here). Fields available per the landed contract:

- `trail["ticket"]` = `rebar.show_ticket(...)` — title, status, assignee, and `description`. There is
  **no** separate `acceptance_criteria` field: the acceptance-criteria block lives INSIDE the
  `description` markdown, so the header renders the `description` (which contains the AC block) behind a
  toggle — it does not read a distinct AC field.
- `trail["plan_reviews"]` = newest-first list of `plan_review_result_v2` payloads. Each carries:
  `verdict`, `model`, `impact_model_version` (the gate/model version shown as a trust caption),
  `material_fingerprint`, `coverage`, `coaching[]` (`{move_id, finding_refs, move_name, subject,
  coaching}`), and `findings[]` (the FULL pooled set). Each finding carries `finding`, `criteria`,
  `location`, `evidence`, `scenarios`, `impact`, `suggested_fix`, `verification`, `validity`,
  `priority`, `decision`, `reason`, `block_threshold`, `blocking_enabled`, `norm_id`. The per-finding
  `decision` field (set by `pass3_decide`) is one of **`block | advisory | dropped | indeterminate`**
  ONLY — there is no `overflow` decision value. `overflow` is a payload-level BUCKET holding
  advisory-`decision` findings beyond a display cap; for both grouping and the convergence series they
  fold into ADVISORY (see the four series below). **No per-round timestamp and no per-round
  signature are exposed** by `all_review_results` (it returns only the inner payload) — so the page
  MUST NOT claim a per-round timestamp or a per-round "certified" badge.
- `trail["code_reviews"]` = list of `{ticket_id, sidecars[]}`; each sidecar is a code-review payload
  (the reader accepts BOTH `code_review_result_v1` and `code_review_result_v2`) with SEPARATE buckets
  `blocking/advisory` (+ `dropped/indeterminate/coaching` on v2). Code-review findings are NOT the
  plan-review four-pass shape — they carry the fields THEY have (typically `finding`, `location`,
  `suggested_fix`, `norm_id`, and possibly `verification`), with NO per-finding `decision` (the bucket
  IS the decision). The page renders whichever of these fields are present and degrades gracefully when
  one is absent (v1 sidecar, or a field a given review didn't populate).
- `trail["completion"]` = `{attestation, sidecar} | None`. The `sidecar` is EITHER a
  `completion_verifier_pass_v1` record carrying `criteria[]` (`{criterion, met, citation, kind}`, `kind
  ∈ {codebase-verifiable, operator-attested}`) OR a `completion_verifier_fail_v1` verdict that carries
  **failures-only `findings[]` and NO `criteria[]`**. The completion panel MUST handle both.

### The decision series (convergence viz + finding grouping)

Plan-review pools findings into up to five `decision` buckets: `blocking`, `advisory`, `overflow`,
`indeterminate`, `dropped`. For BOTH the finding grouping and the convergence visualization the page
renders **four canonical series**, merging `overflow` into `advisory` (both are non-blocking surfaced
findings): **BLOCKING · ADVISORY (incl. overflow) · DROPPED · INDETERMINATE**. Code-review's native
buckets map to the same four series (its `advisory` already includes overflow-equivalents).

## What

A read-only, single-column, finding-centric page at `/ticket/<id>`, built from native
`<details>/<summary>` (no JS — keyboard + screen-reader support come free), one consistent chevron
affordance, and a real `h2`/`h3` heading outline.

- **Ticket header (compact, collapsible):** title, status, assignee; the `description` (which contains
  the full acceptance-criteria block) behind a "details" toggle (not a persistent side rail). No
  certification badge is rendered — signing status is the gate's own output, not surfaced on this
  read-only page.
- **Gate-status strip (sticky):** all three gate verdicts shown AT ONCE, each with a magnitude count
  (`PLAN ✗ FAIL · 3 blocking` / `COMPLETION ✓ PASS · 8/8 met` / `CODE ⦸ not run`). Each chip is an
  in-page anchor that JUMPS to that gate's detail section. Answers pass/fail (and roughly how bad) in
  zero clicks. Each gate's strip state is DERIVED from the read layer: PLAN from the latest
  `plan_reviews[0]` (`verdict` + its blocking count); COMPLETION from `completion.sidecar` (PASS with
  met/total from `criteria[]`, or FAIL); CODE from the latest sidecar of the code-review artifact in
  `code_reviews` (its `verdict` + blocking count) — showing "not run" when `code_reviews` is empty or
  carries no sidecar. Each absent/empty gate shows the "not run" chip, never a hidden one.
- **Detail sections in FIXED canonical order** (plan → completion → code) — the order never changes as
  verdicts change (preserves spatial memory); severity is carried by the strip + a colored heading
  treatment on a failing section, NOT by reordering.
- **Plan-review and code-review sections** (each with round history):
  - Round navigation via a server-rendered `◂ round n of N ▸` selector. No JS: the selector items are
    anchor links to the SAME page with a query string `?<gate>_round=<n>`, where `n` is a **1-based
    index into the newest-first `plan_reviews` / code-review sidecar list** — so `n=1` is the latest
    round (the default when the param is absent), `n=2` the previous one, up to `n=N` the oldest. The
    server clamps an out-of-range or non-integer `n` to the latest round. The two gates use independent
    params (`plan_round`, `code_round`) so one can be stepped without disturbing the other.
  - Per-round **convergence visualization** adapts to round count with a STABLE per-form DOM marker:
    **≤3 rounds → `<div class="conv-bars">`** with one `<div class="conv-bar">` per round (small
    multiples); **≥4 rounds → `<svg class="conv-line">`** with one `<polyline>` per **non-empty
    decision series** (of the four canonical series above — so at most 4 polylines, one per series that
    has data across the rounds, NOT one per round). Either form is accompanied by a visually-hidden
    `<table>` giving the per-round per-series counts for screen readers (WCAG 1.1.1).
  - A round headline verdict, and findings **grouped by decision series**: BLOCKING (expanded, fully
    legible) → ADVISORY / DROPPED / INDETERMINATE (each a quiet one-line collapsed group with a count),
    sorted by `priority` within a group. No "collapse all" control (that needs JS); each group is an
    independent native `<details>` (blocking open, the rest closed).
  - **The finding is the atomic unit.** A finding row (chevron = expandable) opens IN PLACE to the
    provenance read as ONE narrative under human labels. For **plan-review** findings this is the full
    four-pass read — Finding (pass-1 `finding`, mapped `criteria`, `location`, `evidence`, `scenarios`,
    `impact`, `suggested_fix`) → Verification (pass-2 `verification` sub-answers + severity attributes)
    → Decision (pass-3 `decision` + `reason`) → Coaching (pass-4 matched `coaching` move + note). For
    **code-review** findings (which do not carry the identical four-pass shape) the row renders the
    fields that ARE present — `finding`, `location`, `suggested_fix`, optional `verification`, and the
    round's matched `coaching` — under the same labels, omitting a pass whose field is absent rather
    than assuming it. Each is contained in a subtle indented block that reads as one unit; `norm_id` is
    a demoted small metadata line.
  - **Threshold meter = a neutral per-finding meter:** a 0–1 bar filled to `priority` with a tick mark
    at the finding's OWN resolved `block_threshold` (the per-finding value pass-3 used, persisted on the
    finding — the server reads it straight off the record, doing NO runtime `criteria_routing` lookup).
    Whether the fill crosses the tick IS the decision, read spatially. The fill color inherits the
    decision-series color (blocking = alert hue; advisory/dropped/indeterminate = neutral). **v1
    fallback:** a legacy `plan_review_result_v1` finding lacks `block_threshold`/`priority`; when either
    is absent the meter is omitted and replaced by a quiet "threshold not recorded (v1)" caption, so the
    row still renders.
- **Completion panel** (criterion-centric, single-pass, NO chevron — the honest grammar difference from
  finding rows):
  - **PASS sidecar (`completion_verifier_pass_v1`, has `criteria[]`):** one row per criterion from
    `criteria[]` — met glyph (from the criterion's `met` boolean) + `kind` badge
    (`codebase-verifiable` / `operator-attested`) + `citation`. The "lacking attestation" flag is read
    straight off the criterion record: an `operator-attested` criterion is flagged as lacking
    attestation exactly when its `met` is `False` (the verifier records `met=False` for an
    operator-attested criterion when it finds no recorded attestation) — no separate lookup, no
    cross-referencing another data source.
  - **FAIL sidecar (`completion_verifier_fail_v1`, NO `criteria[]`) or absent `criteria[]`:** a fallback
    path renders the failure `findings[]` (one row per unmet criterion the verdict cites) under an
    explicit "verdict FAIL — criteria unmet" heading, so the panel never silently breaks.
- **Empty/partial states:** each absent gate shows a quiet, text-only "not yet run" panel with a real
  `h2`/`h3` heading — never hidden.
- **Trust signals** in each round header (a quiet caption): the gate/model version (`model` +
  `impact_model_version`) and the round `verdict`. (NO per-round timestamp and NO certified badge —
  neither has a landed source in the read layer; certification is the gate's own output and is not
  surfaced on this read-only page.)
- **Visual system:** a strict 3-level type scale; saturated color reserved for verdict + decision-series
  chips only (everything else neutral grey); severity is always encoded by glyph + label + color (never
  color-only); scores shown to one decimal.

## Approach rationale

Finding-centric IA (finding = row; four passes = its in-place provenance) was chosen over
pass-as-navigation after HCD critique: passes are a pipeline artifact, but auditors reason in findings;
co-locating a finding's story answers "why this finding" in one expand and serves both audiences without
a second view. The neutral threshold meter replaces a signed green/red delta whose green=cleared-bar
reading collided with the traffic-light convention (green blocking findings on a failed review read as
"healthy"); inheriting the decision-series color makes strength and severity one coherent signal. The
tick is the finding's OWN resolved threshold (the per-finding value pass-3 used, read straight off the
record — no re-derivation, no round-level scalar, which does not exist). Everything is server-rendered
from the read layer over native no-JS `<details>` + jump-linked anchors + query-param round selection;
single-column stacking survives narrow width at 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/audit/server.py` — add a `/ticket/<id>` route consuming `rebar.audit.read.audit_trail`,
  plus a tiny per-gate round selector reading `?<gate>_round=<n>` and the four-series mapping helper.
- New `src/rebar/audit/templates/*.html` (Jinja2) — the page + sticky gate-strip + gate-section +
  finding-provenance + completion-panel + empty-state partials; inline CSS; the convergence
  visualization + threshold meter as inline SVG/CSS (no external JS/asset); each collapsible is a native
  `<details>`. The threshold meter reads each finding's persisted `block_threshold`/`priority`/`decision`
  (with the v1 fallback); the completion panel reads the read layer's completion record (PASS `criteria[]`
  or the FAIL fallback). Each file within module-size policy (< 500 LOC; split partials along real seams,
  none < 100 LOC).

## Compatibility & rollback

Additive on top of the server-scaffolding story's gated surface; still default-off, loopback-only,
read-only. Rollback = the epic's flag / extra. No data or schema change (this story reads the landed
contract only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sticky gate-status strip shows all three gate verdicts with magnitude counts simultaneously,
      each chip anchoring to its detail section. Oracle: an E2E test on a ticket passing plan review
      (blocking=0), failing completion (k/n met), and with no code review, asserting the rendered HTML
      shows all three states + counts + anchor hrefs.
- [ ] Detail sections render in the fixed order plan → completion → code regardless of which gate
      failed. Oracle: an E2E test comparing section order across two tickets with different failing
      gates.
- [ ] A PLAN-review finding row expands in place to the four-pass provenance (Finding / Verification /
      Decision / Coaching). Oracle: an E2E test seeding a finding with known, distinct field VALUES and
      asserting the expanded HTML contains the SPECIFIC values — the pass-1 `evidence` string, the
      pass-2 `verification` value, and the pass-3 `decision` + `reason` string (not merely the four
      section headings). A code-review finding row renders its available fields (`finding`,
      `location`, `suggested_fix`) without asserting an absent pass.
- [ ] The threshold meter renders a bar filled to `priority` with a tick at the finding's OWN resolved
      `block_threshold` (a per-finding value, not a round-level scalar), with a decision-series-derived
      fill color class. Oracle: an E2E test on a round with two findings whose persisted
      `block_threshold` values DIFFER, asserting the two tick positions differ and each fill has its
      decision-derived color class. A v1 finding (no `block_threshold`) instead renders the
      "threshold not recorded" caption.
- [ ] Findings are grouped by decision series with BLOCKING expanded and ADVISORY / DROPPED /
      INDETERMINATE collapsed-and-counted, sorted by `priority` within each group. Oracle: an E2E test
      asserting group order, expanded blocking rows, and correct collapsed counts.
- [ ] The convergence visualization renders stacked per-round bars (`<div class="conv-bars">` with one
      `.conv-bar` per round) for a ≤3-round ticket, and a line graph (`<svg class="conv-line">` with one
      `<polyline>` per non-empty decision series — NOT per round) for a ≥4-round ticket, each with an
      accompanying visually-hidden screen-reader data table. Oracle: two E2E tests — a 2-round ticket
      asserts `<div class="conv-bars">` with exactly 2 `.conv-bar` rows and NO `.conv-line` svg; a
      4-round ticket whose fixture populates K non-empty series asserts `<svg class="conv-line">` with
      exactly K `<polyline>` elements (one per series) and NO `.conv-bars`; and the visually-hidden
      `<table>` has exactly N data rows (one per round) and one data column per canonical series, each
      cell being that round's count for that series (matching the fixture's per-round per-series
      counts).
- [ ] The `◂ round n of N ▸` selector lists the retained plan- and code-review rounds newest-first,
      defaults to the latest, and selecting an OLDER round (via `?<gate>_round=<n>`) server-renders that
      round's distinct content (findings + convergence). Oracle: an E2E test seeding ≥2 rounds,
      asserting the selector shows N, defaults to latest, and requesting an older round renders its
      (distinct-from-latest) findings.
- [ ] The completion panel renders one chevron-less row per criterion from a PASS verdict's `criteria[]`
      (met glyph + kind badge + citation) and flags an `operator-attested` criterion lacking an
      attestation; for a FAIL verdict (no `criteria[]`) it renders the failure findings under an explicit
      FAIL heading. Oracle: one E2E test on a PASS completion whose `criteria[]` mixes
      `codebase-verifiable` and `operator-attested` kinds (including one operator-attested criterion with
      no recorded attestation), asserting the met glyph, kind badge, citation, and missing-attestation
      flag; and a second E2E test on a FAIL completion asserting the failure-findings fallback renders.
- [ ] A ticket with no code review and no completion verdict shows an explicit plan-review-only page
      with real `h2`/`h3` "not yet run" panels for the absent gates. Oracle: an E2E test asserting the
      empty-state panels render with headings.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` pass.
baseline.summary: audit per-ticket page (finding-centric IA, gate strip, neutral threshold meter, convergence viz)

content.text: RISK 1 (cross-session duplication). Two independently-authored modules each define their OWN `RetryExhaustedError` with a DIFFERENT base class, each raised by a separate retry loop and re-exported from a different public surface. A caller writing `except RetryExhaustedError` against one import silently MISSES the one raised by the other path — exception identity drives control flow, so this is a latent reliability bug, not cosmetic.
## Why

Verified ground truth: `acli_subprocess.py:124` → `class RetryExhaustedError(RuntimeError)` (re-exported via `acli.py`); `batch_dispatch.py:39` → `class RetryExhaustedError(Exception)` (re-exported via `applier.py`). So `acli.RetryExhaustedError is not applier.RetryExhaustedError`. `JiraAPIError` has ONE body (`batch_dispatch.py:31`) re-exported through both surfaces — only the re-export, not the class, is duplicated. The `acli` raise site chains (`raise ... from last_error`); the `batch_dispatch` site does NOT (`raise RetryExhaustedError(str(last_exc))` — drops the cause).
## What — OSS-informed design (requests/urllib3/httpx/tenacity + PEP 3134)

Consensus: one package-level base in a dedicated errors module; subclass `Exception` (or the single most-derived stdlib type a caller already catches); carry the last failure; chain the cause. `_errors.py` already exists (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_errors.py`, ~67 LOC) — ADD the unified types there:
- `class ReconcilerError(Exception)` — the catch-all base seam (per requests `RequestException` / urllib3 `HTTPError`).

- `class RetryExhaustedError(ReconcilerError, RuntimeError)` — MRO `RetryExhaustedError→ReconcilerError→RuntimeError→Exception` is consistent and is caught by BOTH existing `except RuntimeError` (acli path) AND `except Exception` (batch path) sites, so NO call-site breaks. `__init__(self, message="", *, last_exception=None, attempts=None)` — message-first keeps both current `RetryExhaustedError("…")` call sites working; the optional fields mirror tenacity `RetryError.last_attempt` / urllib3 `MaxRetryError.reason`. Do NOT list `(RuntimeError, Exception)` literally (redundant/duplicate base — pylint E0241).
- `class JiraAPIError(ReconcilerError)` — move the single body from `batch_dispatch.py:31` here, keeping `__init__(self, message, status_code)` verbatim.

Then delete both `RetryExhaustedError` bodies and `import` the canonical one (`from rebar_reconciler._errors import RetryExhaustedError`); leave the `acli.py`/`applier.py` `__all__` re-exports (they now re-export the SAME object). Fix the chaining gap at `batch_dispatch.py:137`: `raise RetryExhaustedError("…", last_exception=last_exc, attempts=max_retries+1) from last_exc`.
## Scope

In: unify the two exception types in `_errors.py`, repoint both modules, fix the missing `from` chain. FOLLOW-ON (separate, not this ticket): consolidate the 5 HTTP/subprocess retry LOOPS (push/batch_dispatch/acli_subprocess×2/acli_rest) onto one `retry(fn, *, attempts, backoff, retry_on)` helper — linked as discovered_from.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler.acli import RetryExhaustedError` and `from ...applier import RetryExhaustedError` resolve to the SAME object (`is` identity test).
- [ ] A `RetryExhaustedError` raised by either retry loop is caught by `except RuntimeError`, `except Exception`, AND `except ReconcilerError`.
- [ ] Both raise sites chain the cause (`__cause__` is the last underlying exception); `last_exception`/`attempts` populated.
- [ ] `JiraAPIError` defined once in `_errors.py`, `__init__(message, status_code)` unchanged; both surfaces import it.
- [ ] Tests cover the cross-path `except` identity + chaining; existing reconciler tests pass.

baseline.summary: Risk 1: unify reconciler exception taxonomy + chaining (OSS-informed)

baseline.description:
## Context

rebar's reusable review system intentionally separates four concerns: a critical finder discovers
candidate issues, a generous verifier independently assesses those candidates, deterministic policy
decides their disposition, and a coach helps the client respond without taking over remediation.
Criteria calibration regularly erodes those boundaries by moving severity, disposition, or fix
instructions into the finder; similar drift can make the verifier invent issues, the decision phase
depend on an LLM, or the coach re-adjudicate results.

This epic dogfoods the existing project-criteria extension described by ADRs 0015, 0016, and 0017.
The boundary policy remains a project-owned criterion rather than a packaged rebar-core criterion.
One generic core bug is included because inspection of `origin/main` found that the advertised
code-review extension seam is incomplete: project routing can merge, but a net-new LLM-backed
project criterion is not dynamically fanned into Pass 1, resolved by the eval surface, or consulted
through repository-aware routing in Pass 3.

## Why

Separation creates productive tension: Pass 1 is intentionally critical while Pass 2 is
intentionally generous, and Pass 4 separates the reviewer from the client who owns remediation.
Letting one phase perform another phase's job collapses that tension, makes review outcomes harder
to reason about, and turns rubric edits into hidden policy changes.

The chosen approach adds one co-located project criterion, `project.review-phase-boundaries`, rather
than one criterion per phase. This gives the code-review gate one architectural invariant to invoke
and one balanced eval corpus to calibrate while preserving precise phase-specific subrules.

## Four-Phase Contract

- **Pass 1 — discover:** emit evidence-grounded candidate findings only. Refining which problems a
  criterion discovers, or the evidence required for discovery, is valid. Assessing validity,
  impact, severity, confidence, drop/block posture, or remediation is a boundary violation.
- **Pass 2 — assess:** answer atomic binary validity and impact questions for an existing candidate
  only. It does not discover new findings, decide disposition, or prescribe a fix.
- **Pass 3 — decide:** apply configured thresholds and deterministic rules to drop, block, or retain
  findings. No LLM participates and no new evidence or coaching is introduced.
- **Pass 4 — coach:** provide non-prescriptive next-move guidance for already-decided blocking and
  non-blocking findings. It does not re-verify, change disposition, or dictate an exact
  implementation.

Existing `suggested_fix` support is grandfathered debt: unchanged occurrences are not findings, new
or expanded Pass-1 remediation directives are findings, and the field is removed the next time its
core contract is otherwise touched rather than expanding this epic into an unrelated migration.

## Scope

1. **Complete the generic integration seam — `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`:** deliver dynamic fan-in,
   repository-effective Pass-3 routing, project eval/CLI resolution, compatibility coverage, and
   runtime documentation. Its child bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` owns the reproduced defect and fix.
   The repair maps logical `project.<name>` ids to validator-safe physical
   `code-review-project-<name>` ids and adds no `project.review-phase-boundaries` special case.
   Routing JSON remains keyed by the logical id; physical ids exist only at prompt/eval dispatch.
2. **Author the project criterion — `225a-323c-a9f6-436b`:** add project routing, prompt, tests, and a
   balanced `RP-F1..RP-F6` / `RP-N1..RP-N6` eval corpus. Configure `block_threshold: 0.90` but keep
   `blocking_enabled: false`.
3. **Dogfood in Gerrit — `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d`:** capture a valid positive control and an invalid
   cross-phase directive in real advisory-only reviews, including Pass-2 and Pass-3 evidence; amend
   the invalid directive out before submission.

Work is sequential: the seam story and nested bug precede criterion authoring, and both precede
live Gerrit dogfooding. The dogfood story also directly depends on the seam story so the runtime
prerequisite is visible even if the criterion story is later reorganized.

Out of scope: enabling blocking, tuning the `0.90` threshold without real-review data, changing the
kernel's impact model or deterministic decision math, modifying packaged built-in criteria, or
removing untouched `suggested_fix` debt. Any future promotion to `blocking_enabled: true` requires a
separate ticket whose plan cites accumulated Gerrit evidence.

## Risks and Rollout

- **False positives from policy prose or examples:** require an operative instruction, identifiable
  phase ownership, negative-example suppression, and abstention when ownership is unclear; prove the
  distinction with the balanced eval corpus before live rollout.
- **Extension seam changes regress repositories without overlays:** preserve the overlay-absent path
  and pin it with compatibility tests in the seam bug.
- **Premature contributor blocking:** ship and dogfood with `blocking_enabled: false`; the configured
  `0.90` threshold is observational until a separately reviewed, data-backed posture change.
- **A known-bad probe lands:** use a real intermediate Gerrit patchset for evidence, then remove the
  directive and record the final phase-compliant revision before submission.

Rollback is additive: revert the project routing/prompt/eval assets to disable the criterion, and
revert the generic fan-in/routing/eval repair as one unit if its compatibility suite regresses. No
ticket-store or user-data migration is involved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three direct child stories `2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, `225a-323c-a9f6-436b`, and
  `9447-b31c-e0b7-446d` plus nested seam bug `8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8` are closed; verify hierarchy and
  status with
  `.venv/bin/rebar list --parent jira-reb-1001 --output llm`,
  `.venv/bin/rebar list --parent 2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02 --output llm`.
- [ ] The bug, criterion, and dogfood changes are landed on `main`; verify commits with
  `git log origin/main --oneline --grep='rebar-ticket: \(8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8\|225a-323c-a9f6-436b\|9447-b31c-e0b7-446d\)'`.
- [ ] The generic seam accepts a synthetic activated code-review `project.*` criterion, runs its
  physical prompt exactly once in Pass 1, resolves its diff-based eval spec through the existing
  code-review solver arm, and rejects unknown/inactive ids at the CLI; verify with
  `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py`.
- [ ] Pass 3 uses repository-effective threshold, posture, and nit-suppression values for the
  synthetic logical id while an overlay-absent repository preserves its pre-change result; verify
  with `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py -k 'routing or parity'`.
- [ ] `project.review-phase-boundaries` remains project-owned with `block_threshold: 0.90` and
  `blocking_enabled: false`; verify with
